english_meaning: A dishonest, unreliable, or troublesome person. Someone who behaves badly or causes problems for others. A person with a bad character within an otherwise good group. An individual whose actions harm others or damage trust. An informal term for a rogue or wrongdoer.
example_sentence: Every class has one bad egg who spoils things for others. Be careful of him, he’s a bad egg. The team suffered because of one bad egg. She turned out to be a bad egg in the company.

word: A bad workman always quarrels with his tools
english_meaning: An incompetent person always blames his tools or external factors instead of accepting his own lack of skill. Skilled people can work well even with poor resources, but unskilled people always find excuses.
example_sentence: When Ali failed to fix the car, he said the tools were useless but really, a bad workman always quarrels with his tools. Instead of blaming the computer for the mistakes, she should improve her typing skills, a bad workman always quarrels with his tools. He couldn’t bake the cake properly and said the oven was old, a bad workman always quarrels with his tools. The artist said the brushes were bad when his painting looked rough, truly, a bad workman always quarrels with his tools.

english_meaning: An approximate number or rough estimate. A number that is not exact but is close enough to give a general idea. It is used when precision is not necessary or when only an estimate is available.
example_sentence: Can you give me a ballpark figure for the total expenses?. The contractor provided a ballpark figure before starting the project. I do not need the exact amount, just a ballpark figure will do. The company estimated a ballpark figure for next year’s budget.

english_meaning: It means being obsessed with a specific idea or thought that you cannot stop talking about. It refers to a persistent preoccupation or fixation on a particular subject. It describes a state of agitation or restlessness caused by a certain issue. It indicates that someone is constantly bothered or excited by a singular notion.
example_sentence: She has a bee in her bonnet about recycling and talks about it constantly. My boss has a bee in his bonnet regarding punctuality this week. He won't stop complaining because he has a bee in his bonnet about the new policy. You clearly have a bee in your bonnet about this issue, so let us discuss it.

english_meaning: A general or overall view of something. To see or understand something from a high, broad, or general perspective, rather than looking at small details. It means having an overview of a situation, place, or subject.
example_sentence: From the tower, we got a bird’s eye view of the city. From the plane, we got a bird’s eye view of the entire city. The report gives a bird’s eye view of the education system in Sindh. During the meeting, the manager presented a bird’s eye view of the company’s progress. This map provides a bird’s eye view of the disaster-affected areas.

english_meaning: Something that seems bad or unlucky at first but later turns out to be good. Hidden advantage in a difficult situation. Unexpected benefit from a problem. Good outcome from a bad beginning
synonyms: ["Hidden blessing","Silver lining","Unexpected benefit","Good fortune in adversity"]
example_sentence: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise because I found a better one later. His illness was a blessing in disguise as it made him change his unhealthy lifestyle. Missing the flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise when the plane had technical issues. The failure in business was a blessing in disguise that taught her valuable lessons.

english_meaning: A question that is unclear, confusing, or not easily understood.
example_sentence: His explanation was so fast that it turned into a blur question for the students. When she spoke softly, her question sounded like a blur question to everyone. The interviewer’s blur question left the candidate unsure about how to answer. It is hard to respond correctly when the question itself is a blur question.

english_meaning: An extra or deciding vote given by a chairperson to break a tie. The single vote that settles a matter when both sides have equal votes. A special right of a presiding officer to decide a deadlocked decision. The final vote that determines the outcome of an equally divided ballot.
example_sentence: The chairman used his casting vote to approve the proposal. When the committee was equally divided, the speaker exercised a casting vote. The bill was passed only because of the president’s casting vote. She rarely needs to use her casting vote in board meetings.

english_meaning: A small weakness in a person’s character, plan, or defense. It means a hidden flaw that can cause problems or make them vulnerable.
example_sentence: His arrogance is the only chink in his armour. The plan had a small chink in its armour. Every hero has a chink in his armour. That mistake showed a chink in his armour.

english_meaning: An unbelievable and exaggerated story told as an excuse. A far-fetched tale invented to deceive someone. A ridiculous explanation that nobody is likely to believe. A foolish or absurd account of events made up to avoid blame.
example_sentence: He told his boss a cock-and-bull story about a flat tyre. Nobody believed her cock-and-bull story about losing the money. Don't give me a cock-and-bull story; just tell me the truth. The witness came up with a cock-and-bull story to protect his friend.

english_meaning: A person who is just a small part of big organization or system. An unimportant or minor member of a large organization, system, or process, easily replaceable.
example_sentence:
He felt like just a cog in the machine, doing the same work every day without recognition.
In a huge corporation, many employees see themselves as cogs in the machine. Though she’s a cog in the machine, her role is essential for the project’s success.

english_meaning: Something that is extremely unlikely or almost impossible to happen. An event that is highly improbable or something that is not expected to happen. Since July is typically one of the hottest months in many places, a cold day during July is considered unusual. Therefore, the expression refers to something that is very unlikely to occur.
synonyms: ["Never","When pigs fly","Not in a million years","Impossible"]
example_sentence: He will apologize on a cold day in July. Winning that championship without practice will happen on a cold day in July. She said she would lend him the money on a cold day in July. They'll finish the project without any effort on a cold day in July.

english_meaning: A person whose abilities or plans are hidden and who surprises others by succeeding. A person who is not well known or expected to win or succeed, but later surprises everyone with unexpected success. It is often used in competitions, politics, or any situation where someone quietly performs better than expected.
example_sentence: He was a dark horse in the election and ended up winning easily. Nobody expected her to top the class, but she turned out to be a dark horse. The small team was a dark horse in the tournament and defeated stronger opponents. That quiet employee is a dark horse with amazing skills.

english_meaning: A completely different matter or situation from the one being discussed. Something that is not related to or comparable with what has just been mentioned. An entirely separate issue that must be handled differently.
synonyms: ["Another matter","Separate issue","Different story","Unrelated topic","Whole new ballgame"]
example_sentence: Managing a small shop is one thing, but running a company is a different kettle of fish. Playing football is fun, but coaching is a different kettle of fish. Writing a poem is easy for her, but writing a novel is a different kettle of fish. I can cook simple meals, but baking cakes is a different kettle of fish.

english_meaning: Very common and of little value because of abundance. Something so ordinary that it is easy to find anywhere. Not special or rare in any way. Available in large quantities and therefore cheap.
example_sentence: Ideas like that are a dime a dozen; execution matters. In this city, cheap souvenirs are a dime a dozen. Talented singers are a dime a dozen on social media. Job seekers with basic skills are a dime a dozen.

english_meaning: A person who stops others from using something they do not need themselves. This idiom refers to someone who selfishly prevents others from benefiting from something even though they have no use for it themselves.
example_sentence: He never uses the old computer but refuses to let anyone else have it. He is a dog in the manger. She kept the files locked even though she had no work to do with them, acting like a dog in the manger. The manager would not approve the plan nor allow others to improve it. A real dog in the manger. Keeping unused land idle while others need it is the behavior of a dog in the manger.

english_meaning: Something that has been done very badly or is in a state of complete confusion. A messy, untidy, or badly organised situation. A poorly executed piece of work. A muddle or disorderly arrangement of things.
example_sentence: He made a dog's breakfast of the whole report. The kitchen was a dog's breakfast after the party. Their attempt to fix the website was a dog's breakfast. The new rules are a complete dog's breakfast.

english_meaning: Something done very badly or left in a complete mess. A situation or piece of work that is badly organised. Used in the phrase dressed up like a dog's dinner, meaning dressed in a showy or ridiculous way. A confused or untidy result of poor effort.
example_sentence: They made a dog's dinner of the building work. The report was a dog's dinner from start to finish. She turned up dressed up like a dog's dinner. Our travel plans ended up a complete dog's dinner.

english_meaning: A small problem that spoils an otherwise good situation. A minor flaw that reduces overall enjoyment or success. Something unpleasant that disturbs an otherwise pleasant experience. A drawback that stands out in a positive setting. An irritating detail that ruins the whole.
example_sentence: The trip was perfect, but the bad weather was a fly in the ointment. His rude comment was a fly in the ointment at the party. The only fly in the ointment is the high price. Everything went smoothly except one fly in the ointment.

english_meaning: A person with enormous energy, drive, and presence. Someone whose personality is powerful and impossible to ignore. A natural power such as wind, fire, or an earthquake. An unstoppable influence that shapes events. Something whose strength cannot be resisted or controlled.
example_sentence: As a teacher, she was a force of nature. He is a force of nature on the football field. The storm proved to be a force of nature no one could stop. Their new leader is quite simply a force of nature.

english_meaning: With even stronger reason. All the more certainly because a stated fact or conclusion provides a stronger case. By an argument showing that if one proposition is true, another more obvious or compelling proposition must also be true. A Latin expression used in logic, law, and formal writing.
synonyms: ["With stronger reason","All the more","Even more certainly","By greater force","Necessarily"]
example_sentence: If a child cannot enter, a fortiori an unaccompanied infant cannot enter. The law protects private letters and, a fortiori, confidential medical records. A minor error requires correction; a fortiori, a serious falsehood does. If the cheaper option is unaffordable, a fortiori the luxury model is beyond our budget.

word: A friend in need is a friend indeed
english_meaning: A true friend is one who helps you in difficult times. Real friendship shows during hardships, not in good times. A person who supports you when you need it most is a real friend. Difficult times reveal genuine relationships. Loyalty is proven through help during crises.
example_sentence: When I was ill, he stayed by my side; a friend in need is a friend indeed. She helped me pay my bills, proving that a friend in need is a friend indeed. My cousin supported me during the tough time; truly a friend in need is a friend indeed. Only real friends stay in bad times, as a friend in need is a friend indeed.

english_meaning: A comfortable but restrictive situation. A life of luxury that lacks true freedom. A pleasant environment where one still feels trapped. Wealth or privilege that comes with hidden limitations. A beautiful yet confining condition.
example_sentence: She lived in a gilded cage as a princess. His job pays well but feels like a gilded cage. Many celebrities describe fame as a gilded cage. The mansion was beautiful but felt like a gilded cage to her.

english_meaning: A business or an activity that is making a profit and is expected to continue to do well. It can also be used generally to describe anything that is active, running, or functional.
example_sentence: He sold the cafe as a going concern. They knew that, as a going concern, the cafe would command a higher price with prospective buyers. The factory is a going concern and is making steady profits. Their partnership is still a going concern after 10 years.

english_meaning: A kind, trustworthy, and reliable person. Someone with a pleasant and honest character. A person who can be counted on for support and decency. An informal expression praising someone as thoroughly likeable. A description used for a genuinely nice human being.
example_sentence: Don’t worry about John, he’s a good egg. She’s a good egg who always helps her neighbors. You can trust him with the keys, he’s a good egg. My grandfather was a good egg loved by everyone.

english_meaning: A reasonable and practical balance between two opposite choices or opinions. It suggests avoiding excess on either side and choosing a middle path that combines the good aspects of both sides.
example_sentence: Let’s find a happy medium between work and rest. She always seeks a happy medium in arguments. We need a happy medium between freedom and order. The happy medium was a compromise both accepted.

english_meaning: A person who is difficult to deal with, persuade, or get to know. A problem or task that is difficult to solve or accomplish. Something that requires great effort or skill to handle.
example_sentence: The new client turned out to be a hard nut who resisted every proposal. She is a hard nut to crack but earns great respect once you get through to her. The final question on the exam was a real hard nut that stumped most students. He was known as a hard nut in negotiations, never conceding easily.

english_meaning: Something or someone that is very difficult to understand, solve, or deal with. A tough problem, a difficult task, or a person who is not easy to influence, convince, or understand. It is often used in situations where effort, skill, or patience is required.
example_sentence: Solving this puzzle is a hard nut to crack. The new software bug turned out to be a hard nut to crack for the developers. He is a hard nut to crack when it comes to negotiations. Climate change is a hard nut to crack for global leaders.

english_meaning: A person or problem that is difficult to deal with, solve, or understand. Someone who is tough, stubborn, or not easily influenced, or a situation that requires effort, skill, and patience to handle successfully.
example_sentence: The new manager is a hard nut to cut and does not accept excuses. This puzzle is a hard nut to cut, even for experts. He proved to be a hard nut to cut during negotiations. Learning this language can be a hard nut to cut for beginners.

word: A leopard does not change its spots
english_meaning: One cannot change their innate character. A person’s basic nature does not change. No matter how hard someone tries to appear different, their true character stays the same.
example_sentence: Don’t trust him, a leopard does not change its spots. A leopard does not change its spots, so beware. She said a leopard does not change its spots. History shows a leopard does not change its spots.

english_meaning: A quick and careless piece of work, especially cleaning. Something done hastily and without proper care. A superficial effort made in a hurry.
example_sentence: She gave the kitchen a lick and a promise before the guests arrived. The room got only a lick and a promise this morning. He cleaned the car with a lick and a promise. A lick and a promise is not enough for such a big job.

word: A morsel is enough for the grateful heart
english_meaning: A grateful person is satisfied with very little. Contentment makes even the smallest amount feel like an abundance. It signifies that true satisfaction comes from within, and a thankful attitude does not require great wealth or quantity to feel blessed.
synonyms: ["Contentment Is Great Wealth","Enough Is As Good As A Feast","A Contented Mind Is A Continual Feast","Gratitude Turns What We Have Into Enough"]
antonyms: ["Greed Has No Limits","Much Would Have More","A Greedy Man Is Always Poor","A Covetous Man Is Never Satisfied"]
example_sentence: Even when times were tough, they shared their meager meal, knowing that a morsel is enough for the grateful heart. He didn't ask for a large reward, demonstrating the truth that a morsel is enough for the grateful heart. She accepted the small gift with tears of joy, proving that a morsel is enough for the grateful heart. Rather than demanding more, true believers understand that a morsel is enough for the grateful heart. They had very little to offer, but her glowing smile showed that a morsel is enough for the grateful heart.

english_meaning: A very small amount of comfort, consolation, or hope in an otherwise bad, distressing, or sad situation. It refers to something minor that makes a difficult time slightly easier to bear, even if it does not solve the overall problem. A tiny piece of reassurance or relief experienced during a challenging period.
synonyms: ["A crumb of comfort","A little consolation","A sliver of hope","A bit of solace","Small comfort","Minor relief","A grain of solace"]
antonyms: ["Complete despair","Total distress","Overwhelming grief","Utter devastation","Deep sorrow","Profound agony"]
example_sentence: Winning the final match of the series was a morsel of comfort for the otherwise defeated team. The doctor's reassuring words offered her a morsel of comfort during the anxious wait. He found a morsel of comfort in knowing that he had tried his absolute best. Receiving a short letter from home was a morsel of comfort for the lonely soldier. The modest decrease in overall inflation provided a morsel of comfort to struggling families.

english_meaning: A very small piece or amount of information. A tiny detail, a snippet of news, or a small fragment of knowledge. It refers to a minor but often useful or intriguing fact that is discovered, shared, or gathered during an inquiry.
synonyms: ["Snippet Of Information","Piece Of News","Fragment Of Knowledge","Tidbit","Scrap Of Information","Morsel Of News","Grain Of Truth","Small Detail","Clue"]
antonyms: ["Wealth Of Information","Abundance Of Knowledge","Comprehensive Data","Complete Picture","Full Story","Detailed Account","Mountain Of Information"]
example_sentence: Every morsel of information is crucial for solving this complex case. She managed to gather a precious morsel of information about the company's new project. Even a single morsel of information can completely change the direction of the investigation. He refused to share even a morsel of information with the press. The spy risked his life to smuggle out just one morsel of information to his headquarters.

word: A morsel today is better than a feast in imagination
english_meaning: A small but actual benefit enjoyed in the present is much more valuable than a huge but imaginary or uncertain benefit in the future. It emphasizes the importance of reality and present possessions over unrealistic dreams, fantasies, or uncertain future promises.
synonyms: ["A Bird In The Hand Is Worth Two In The Bush","Half A Loaf Is Better Than None","Better An Egg Today Than A Hen Tomorrow","Something Is Better Than Nothing","Reality Is Better Than Fantasy"]
antonyms: ["Build Castles In The Air","Live In A Fool's Paradise","Pie In The Sky","Count Your Chickens Before They Hatch","Chase Rainbows"]
example_sentence: He accepted the low-paying job immediately, knowing that a morsel today is better than a feast in imagination. Don't reject this small offer while waiting for a perfect one, because a morsel today is better than a feast in imagination. Investors preferred the small, guaranteed return, proving that a morsel today is better than a feast in imagination. She stopped dreaming about winning the lottery and started saving what little she earned, realizing a morsel today is better than a feast in imagination.

english_meaning: Something unpleasant that must be accepted because it brings a greater benefit. An undesirable thing that cannot be avoided in a given situation. A harmful or annoying element tolerated for practical reasons. Something disliked but regarded as unavoidable.
example_sentence: For many people, paying taxes is a necessary evil. Long meetings are a necessary evil in large organisations. He sees advertising as a necessary evil of free media. Antibiotics can be a necessary evil despite their side effects.

english_meaning: A person or thing that generates a lot of interest or excitement for a very short time but is soon forgotten. An event that attracts short-lived attention and fades away quickly. A brief and passing sensation that leaves no lasting impact.
synonyms: ["Flash In The Pan","Passing Fad","Short-lived Sensation","Fleeting Trend","Temporary Craze","Momentary Marvel","Transient Phenomenon","Bubble","Novelty","Gimmick"]
antonyms: ["Lasting Legacy","Timeless Classic","Permanent Fixture","Enduring Success","Lifelong Fame","Immortal Legend","Constant Phenomenon","Unfading Memory","Eternal Tradition"]
example_sentence: The scandalous news was just a nine days wonder and people soon stopped talking about it. His sudden rise to fame proved to be a nine days wonder. Don't worry about the rumors because they are just a nine days wonder. The viral video was a classic nine days wonder that everyone forgot by next month.

english_meaning: An essential, regular item in a place. A person or thing that has been present in a place for so long that people hardly notice them anymore. Someone so familiar and common in a setting that they almost become invisible or unremarkable.
example_sentence: He has been teaching in this school for 40 years, he’s almost a part of the furniture now. She has been working in the same office for so long that people see her as part of the furniture. The old security guard at the bank is just like part of the furniture, everyone is used to him being there. He attends every meeting but never speaks; he’s just part of the furniture.

english_meaning: Something that gives a person the opportunity or access to achieve success or gain entry to something. A guarantee of entry into a field or profession. A strong advantage that improves social or professional status. A stepping stone toward higher achievement. A qualification that increases acceptance or recognition.
synonyms: ["Key to","Gateway to","Ticket to","Stepping stone to","Pathway to"]
example_sentence: A good education is a passport to a successful career. Strong communication skills can be a passport to leadership roles. Hard work is often a passport to achievement. Networking can serve as a passport to new business opportunities.

english_meaning: A polite way to ask someone what they are thinking. Asking gently about someone's thoughts. Encouraging someone to speak. Showing curiosity about silence. Friendly conversational opener. Used when someone appears quiet, thoughtful, or distracted. The speaker is inviting them to share their thoughts or feelings. It is friendly and informal.
synonyms: ["What are you thinking","Care to share your thoughts","What is on your mind","Tell me what you are thinking","Share your thoughts"]
antonyms: ["Never mind","Keep it to yourself","I do not want to know","Say no more"]
example_sentence: You have been quiet for a while, a penny for your thoughts. She looked out the window silently, and he said, a penny for your thoughts. A penny for your thoughts, you seem worried today. He smiled and asked, a penny for your thoughts, when she stopped talking.

english_meaning: A single image can convey complex ideas, emotions, or stories better than a long description. Visuals often communicate more effectively than words.
example_sentence: The chart explained everything, a picture is worth 1000 words. In a meeting, charts and infographics make the data easy to understand, proving that a picture is worth a thousand words. Instead of describing the beauty of the mountains, showing a photo of the snow-covered peaks makes the experience clear, a picture is worth a thousand words.

word: A poor workman who blames his tools
english_meaning: An incompetent person always blames his tools or external factors instead of accepting his own lack of skill. Skilled people can work well even with poor resources, but unskilled people always find excuses.
example_sentence: He lost the match but blamed the bat — a poor workman who blames his tools.

english_meaning: A person who behaves in a strange or unusual way. An odd or eccentric individual. Someone difficult to understand because of odd habits. A peculiar character who does not fit in.
example_sentence: Our new neighbour is rather a queer fish. He is a queer fish but a brilliant scientist. People call him a queer fish because he never speaks. That queer fish collects broken clocks.

english_meaning: A very great and unmistakable success. An achievement that is clear, complete, and widely recognised. An outcome far better than expected and praised by many.
example_sentence: The charity concert was a resounding success. Their new product proved a resounding success in the market. The exhibition was a resounding success with over ten thousand visitors. What began as an experiment became a resounding success.

word: A rolling stone gathers no moss
english_meaning: Someone who keeps moving from one thing to another instead of staying committed. Such a person may avoid responsibilities and may not collect experience, property, respect, or strong relationships over time. In some modern situations, the proverb can also have a positive meaning. A person who keeps moving and changing may stay active, fresh, skilled, and free from boredom or unhealthy habits.
antonyms: ["Stable person","Settled person","Consistent worker","Loyal employee","Committed person","Steady individual"]
example_sentence: Ahmed changed four jobs in two years because a rolling stone gathers no moss. Sara never stayed in one city long enough to build close friendships because a rolling stone gathers no moss. My grandfather advised me to focus on one business because a rolling stone gathers no moss. Ali kept changing his study plans and failed to master any subject because a rolling stone gathers no moss.

english_meaning: A practical method or guideline based on experience rather than exact measurement. A rough principle that is generally correct but not precise. A simple guide that helps in making quick decisions. An approximate standard used in everyday practice.
example_sentence: As a rule of thumb, drink eight glasses of water a day. A good rule of thumb is to save ten percent of your income. He follows the rule of thumb that simple designs work best. As a rule of thumb, arrive fifteen minutes early.

english_meaning: The feeling that an event is special, important, and memorable. An awareness of the dignity and significance of a particular event. The quality in a ceremony that makes it feel grand and meaningful.
example_sentence: The music and lighting gave the ceremony a real sense of occasion. There was a great sense of occasion as the guests arrived. She dressed formally to mark the sense of occasion. The stadium was filled with a sense of occasion before the final.

word: A shared morsel tastes sweeter than a full meal alone
english_meaning: A small amount of food shared with others brings more happiness than eating a large amount by oneself. The joy of companionship and sharing makes even the smallest thing feel greatly satisfying and meaningful. It highlights the importance of generosity, community, and togetherness over selfishness and solitary indulgence.
synonyms: ["Joy Shared Is Joy Doubled","Sharing Is Caring","Companionship Sweetens The Fare","Shared Happiness Is Multiplied","Fellowship Makes The Feast"]
example_sentence: They barely had enough bread to go around, but as they laughed together, they realized a shared morsel tastes sweeter than a full meal alone. He preferred to eat his meager lunch with his colleagues rather than dine lavishly in solitude, knowing that a shared morsel tastes sweeter than a full meal alone. Though the feast was small, the family enjoyed every bite, proving the old adage that a shared morsel tastes sweeter than a full meal alone. She always brought extra snacks to the study group because she believed a shared morsel tastes sweeter than a full meal alone.

english_meaning: A wild guess without certainty. A guess. Something you do without knowing what the result will be.
example_sentence: It was just a shot in the dark, but I was right. The figure he came up with was really just a shot in the dark. It was only a stab in the dark, but I hoped I could learn something.

english_meaning: A person or thing that one is extremely pleased or relieved to see. Someone whose presence brings joy after a long absence. A very welcome sight. Something pleasing to look at after difficulty or waiting. An expression of delight upon seeing someone.
example_sentence: After the long journey home, my family was a sight for sore eyes. The green fields were a sight for sore eyes after the desert trip. You are a sight for sore eyes, my old friend! A hot cup of tea in winter is a sight for sore eyes.

english_meaning: A clever, intelligent, or quick-thinking person. Someone who is resourceful and able to deal with difficult situations.
example_sentence: Don’t underestimate her—she’s a smart cookie and knows how to negotiate deals. He solved the problem in minutes; that boy is a really smart cookie. You have to be a smart cookie to survive in such a competitive industry. She may look quiet, but she’s a smart cookie when it comes to business.

english_meaning: Having no real chance of success. It describes a situation where success is almost impossible because the conditions are completely against it.
example_sentence: He has a snowball’s chance in hell of winning. They had a snowball’s chance in hell against that team. There’s not a snowball’s chance in hell she’ll agree. Without funds, we’ve got a snowball’s chance in hell.

english_meaning: A betrayal by someone trusted. An act that harms somebody, done by a person they thought was a friend.
example_sentence: Losing his friend’s trust was like a stab in the back. Her refusal to support his campaign was a real stab in the back.

english_meaning: An attempt made without knowledge or certainty. A guess. Something you do without knowing what the result will be.
example_sentence: His answer was just a stab in the dark. The figure he came up with was really just a shot in the dark. It was only a stab in the dark, but I hoped I could learn something. I didn’t know the answer, so my guess was just a stab in the dark.

english_meaning: An unpleasant ending. A surprising and often unpleasant detail or consequence that appears at the end of a situation, story, decision, or event, reducing its overall positive effect
example_sentence: The movie was entertaining, but there was a sting in the tail when the hero betrayed his friend. The job offer looked perfect, but the long unpaid probation was a sting in the tail. His speech was inspiring, with a sting in the tail that criticized the audience sharply. The agreement seemed fair, yet the hidden fee at the end was a real sting in the tail.

word: A stitch in time saves nine
english_meaning: Solving a problem immediately prevents it from becoming worse later. Taking timely action saves a lot of work in the future.
synonyms: ["Prevention Is Better Than Cure","Nip It In The Bud","Procrastination Is The Thief Of Time","Timely Action","An Ounce Of Prevention Is Worth A Pound Of Cure","Forewarned Is Forearmed","Act Early","Early Bird Catches The Worm","Precaution","Promptness","Proactiveness"]
antonyms: ["Procrastination","Delay","Let It Ride","Kick The Can Down The Road","Better Late Than Never","Ignorance","Negligence","Put Off","Avoidance"]
example_sentence: I noticed a small leak in the roof and fixed it before the rainy season because a stitch in time saves nine. You should pay off that credit card debt now, as a stitch in time saves nine. The mechanic replaced the worn belt before it broke entirely, proving that a stitch in time saves nine. We resolved the customer's complaint early on since a stitch in time saves nine.

english_meaning: A sudden and unexpected piece of good fortune. A fortunate event that happens by chance rather than by effort. An unplanned occurrence that brings a favourable result. A lucky break that improves someone's situation.
example_sentence: Finding that job was a real stroke of luck. By a stroke of luck, they caught the last train. It was a stroke of luck that the rain stopped before the match. He met his business partner by a stroke of luck.

english_meaning: An unexpected gain of money or benefit that arrives by chance. A sudden piece of good fortune bringing profit or advantage. An unearned benefit received without planning or effort. A surprising financial gift or gain.
example_sentence: The inheritance came as a stroke of windfall for the family. A stroke of windfall allowed him to pay off his debts. The company enjoyed a stroke of windfall after the new contract. Her lottery win was a genuine stroke of windfall.

english_meaning: The final performance, work, or achievement of someone before retirement or death. A last appearance or effort before ending a career. A farewell act regarded as the finest of its kind.
example_sentence: This concert was the singer's swan song after forty years on stage. The novel proved to be the author's swan song. He scored a century in what became his swan song. The exhibition was the painter's swan song before retirement.

english_meaning: A small but highly attractive piece of food. Something very appealing, enticing, or desirable, often offered in a small amount or presented as a tease. A very attractive offer, opportunity, piece of gossip, or prize that is difficult to resist.
example_sentence: The bonus offered to the employees was a tempting morsel they could not refuse. To a hungry traveler, even a piece of dry bread looks like a tempting morsel. The latest celebrity gossip was a tempting morsel for the tabloids. The investor saw the struggling startup's low valuation as a tempting morsel. She dropped a tempting morsel of information to keep everyone curious and engaged.

english_meaning: A sign of approval or agreement, to express that something is good or accepted.
example_sentence: The boss gave the project a thumbs up. He gave me a thumbs up before the presentation. Everyone gave a thumbs up to the new policy. That’s a thumbs up from the team.

word: A tiger doesn't change its stripes

Their relationship became stronger during long distance, as absence makes the heart grow fonder. He missed his best friend so much that he understood absence makes the heart grow fonder.

english_meaning: Complete and without any conditions or restrictions. Not qualified or diminished in any way. Viewed or existing independently and not in relation to other things. A value or principle which is regarded as universally valid or which may be viewed without relation to other things. Having unlimited power or authority, typically over a nation or territory.
example_sentence: He demanded absolute silence while he was concentrating on the puzzle. The dictator ruled the country with absolute power for over three decades. I have absolute confidence in her ability to lead the team to victory. There is no absolute proof that the suspect committed the crime.

english_meaning: Temperature measured from absolute zero on the Kelvin scale. A scale in which zero represents the complete absence of thermal energy. The thermodynamic temperature used in scientific calculations. A measurement expressed in kelvins rather than degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.
example_sentence: Gas laws are usually written in terms of absolute temperature. The absolute temperature of the sample was recorded in kelvins. At absolute zero the absolute temperature equals zero. Scientists converted the readings into absolute temperature before plotting the graph.

english_meaning: The lowest possible temperature, at which particles have minimum thermal motion. The point equal to zero kelvin, or about minus 273.15 degrees Celsius. A theoretical limit that can be approached but never fully reached in practice.
example_sentence: Absolute zero is defined as zero kelvin. No substance can be cooled below absolute zero. The experiment brought the gas close to absolute zero. At absolute zero, molecular motion is at its minimum.

english_meaning: Formal release from guilt, obligation, or punishment. The act of forgiving someone for their sins, especially the religious forgiveness pronounced by a priest. Freedom from blame or responsibility. A declaration that a person is forgiven and free from the consequences of wrongdoing. The state of being pardoned or cleared of sin.
example_sentence: The priest granted absolution to the repentant man. She sought absolution for the mistakes of her past. He felt a sense of absolution after confessing the truth. The court's decision gave him absolution from all charges. Many people seek spiritual absolution through prayer.

english_meaning: A political system in which one ruler holds complete and unrestricted power. The principle or practice of government without constitutional limits. The belief that there are unchanging, universal standards of truth or morality. A rigid insistence on fixed principles without allowing exceptions.
example_sentence: The revolution brought an end to royal absolutism. Moral absolutism leaves little room for compromise. Historians have long debated the roots of absolutism in Europe. Critics warned that the new law smelled of political absolutism.

english_meaning: A person who supports or believes in absolute rule by one authority. Someone who holds that certain principles are universally true and admit no exceptions. Relating to or characteristic of absolutism. Unwilling to accept compromise or shades of opinion.
example_sentence: The king ruled as a true absolutist for over forty years. She takes an absolutist view on questions of honesty. His absolutist attitude made negotiation impossible. Absolutist regimes rarely tolerate criticism.

english_meaning: To officially declare a person free from guilt, blame, or the consequences of wrongdoing. To formally release someone from a moral, religious, or legal obligation. To pardon or excuse someone for an offense or failure. To clear someone of all responsibility through a formal declaration or judgment. To set someone free from the burden of sin, accusation, or punishment through authority.
example_sentence: The priest absolved him of his sins after confession. The court absolved her of all charges due to lack of evidence. He was absolved of blame for the accident. The confession helped absolve the suspect in the eyes of the public. Her sincere apology did not automatically absolve her of responsibility.

english_meaning: To take in or soak up a substance such as liquid, heat, or light. To assimilate or integrate information, ideas, or experiences fully. To engage someone's complete attention and interest. To take in and make part of oneself through learning or exposure. To incorporate a smaller organization or group into a larger one. To bear or endure a cost, impact, or shock without being overwhelmed.
example_sentence: A sponge can absorb large amounts of water quickly. The student worked hard to absorb the new concepts. Dark colors absorb more heat than light ones. She was so absorbed in her book that she missed dinner. The country struggled to absorb the large influx of refugees.

english_meaning: Able to be soaked up or taken in by a substance or the body. Describing a nutrient or medicine that can pass into the bloodstream. In surgery, describing stitches or materials that dissolve naturally inside the body. Capable of being absorbed or assimilated.
example_sentence: Vitamin C is easily absorbable by the body. The surgeon used absorbable stitches on the wound. Iron is more absorbable when taken with citrus juice. The material is soft, light, and highly absorbable.

english_meaning: A measure of how much light a substance absorbs at a given wavelength. In chemistry, the logarithm of the ratio of incident light to transmitted light through a sample. A value obtained with a spectrophotometer and used to determine the concentration of a solution.
example_sentence: The absorbance of the sample was measured at 540 nanometres. A higher absorbance indicates a more concentrated solution. They plotted absorbance against concentration to draw the calibration curve. The instrument records absorbance automatically.

english_meaning: Taken in or soaked up by a substance, surface, or the body. Deeply interested and fully occupied with something. Having had one's attention completely held. Incorporated or merged into a larger body or organisation.
example_sentence: Most of the water was absorbed by the dry soil. She was absorbed in her book and did not hear the bell. The small firm was absorbed into a larger company. He looked completely absorbed in his work.

english_meaning: The ability of a material to soak up and hold liquid. The degree or capacity to which something absorbs moisture. A measurement of how much fluid a substance can take in relative to its own weight.
example_sentence: Cotton towels are valued for their high absorbency. The test measured the absorbency of each paper sample. Low absorbency makes the fabric unsuitable for cleaning. Absorbency decreases once the material is coated.

english_meaning: Able to soak up liquid or moisture easily. Describing a material designed to take in and hold fluids. A substance used to absorb liquid, gas, or heat. Capable of taking in energy, sound, or shock.
example_sentence: Use an absorbent cloth to wipe up the spill. Absorbent paper is placed under the sample during the test. The company produces highly absorbent packing material. Sand is a cheap absorbent for oil spills.

english_meaning: Extremely interesting and holding one's full attention. Taking in liquid, heat, sound, or energy. Engaging the mind so completely that time passes unnoticed. The action or process of soaking something up.
example_sentence: The documentary was absorbing from start to finish. Thick curtains act as a sound-absorbing layer. She found the lecture unusually absorbing. Absorbing the shock, the suspension kept the ride smooth.

english_meaning: The process by which one substance takes in and incorporates another substance. Complete and deep mental engagement with a task, idea, or subject. The process by which nutrients, liquids, or light are taken into the body or a surface. The merging or incorporation of one organization, culture, or group into a larger one. The state of being entirely engrossed in an activity or thought. The capacity of a material to take in and retain a substance.
example_sentence: The absorption of nutrients takes place in the small intestine. Her absorption in the task meant she ignored all distractions. The absorption of the smaller company took six months. Light absorption differs between various surface types. The absorption of new information is easier when interest is high.

english_meaning: To choose not to do something, especially something you could do. To deliberately avoid or refrain from an action, habit, or practice. To hold oneself back voluntarily. To stay away from something by choice. To decline participation. To avoid indulgence.
example_sentence: He decided to abstain from smoking for health reasons. She abstained from voting during the meeting. Many athletes abstain from junk food before competitions. They chose to abstain from commenting on the issue.

english_meaning: Not self-indulgent, especially when eating and drinking; moderate and restrained in one's appetites. Choosing to consume little food or alcohol.
example_sentence: He was abstemious in his diet, eating only plain food. Her abstemious lifestyle contributed to her long life. Being abstemious during Ramadan is a spiritual practice. The abstemious monk survived on very little food and water.

english_meaning: The act of refraining from doing something, especially voting in an election or debate. A deliberate choice not to participate in a particular action or indulgence. The practice of voluntarily withholding one's vote or involvement in a decision. A disciplined refusal to take part in a habit, activity, or substance. A formal decision to neither support nor oppose a measure by not casting a vote.
example_sentence: Three members chose abstention rather than voting against the proposal. His abstention from alcohol improved his health significantly. The bill passed despite the abstention of several key delegates. She practiced abstention from social media for a month. Their abstention from the vote was seen as a silent protest.

english_meaning: The act of choosing not to do or have something, especially something enjoyable such as alcohol, food, or sex. The voluntary decision to avoid or restrain oneself from certain pleasures, habits, or activities.
example_sentence: Fasting is one of the fundamental of Islam that means abstinence. He practiced abstinence from alcohol for health reasons. Many religions encourage abstinence before marriage. Her abstinence from sweets helped her control her diabetes. The doctor recommended abstinence from smoking after surgery.

english_meaning: Relating to ideas or concepts rather than concrete, physical things. Existing only in thought or as a mental concept with no physical reality. A brief written summary of a longer document, article, or research paper. Difficult to understand due to being theoretical or non-specific. In art, characterized by non-representational shapes, colors, and forms rather than depictions of real objects. To remove or separate something from a larger whole.
example_sentence: Love and justice are abstract concepts that differ across cultures. The scientist presented an abstract of her research findings. Abstract art challenges viewers to interpret shapes and colors freely. His argument was too abstract to be practically useful. She submitted an abstract of her thesis to the conference committee.

english_meaning: Difficult to understand because of being complex, obscure, or highly intellectual. Hard to comprehend, especially due to being expressed in an overly complicated or technical manner. Used to describe ideas, texts, or subjects that are deep, esoteric, and not easily grasped by ordinary readers. Profound and abstract to the point of obscurity.
example_sentence: The professor's lecture on quantum mechanics was far too abstruse for most first-year students.  His writing style is often criticized for being needlessly abstruse.  The legal document was filled with abstruse terminology that confused even experienced lawyers.  She struggled to follow the abstruse arguments presented in the philosophy seminar.  The abstruse theory took years for other scientists to fully understand.

english_meaning: The quality of being difficult to understand or obscure. Something that is complex, hard to comprehend, or obscure, often due to deep or complicated reasoning, abstract ideas, or technical language.
example_sentence: The abstrusity of the philosopher's argument confused many students. The book’s abstrusity made it hard for casual readers to follow. He enjoyed discussing abstrusity in quantum mechanics. Critics complained about the abstrusity of the legal document.

english_meaning: Completely unreasonable or illogical. So unreasonable, illogical, or contrary to common sense that it seems ridiculous or laughable. It describes ideas, actions, or situations that do not make practical sense.
example_sentence: It is absurd to believe that the sun revolves around the earth. His excuse for being late sounded completely absurd. The price they asked for such a small item was absurd. She laughed at the absurd idea of walking in the storm without an umbrella.

english_meaning: Something that is completely unreasonable or ridiculous. The quality or state of being illogical, unreasonable, or nonsensical. It can describe ideas, actions, or situations that lack sense or reason.
example_sentence: The idea that humans can live forever is pure absurdity. It is an absurdity to think money can buy happiness. His claim that the earth is flat is full of absurdity. The novel explores the absurdity of war through dark humor.

english_meaning: A Latin word meaning “absurd” or “that which is unreasonable”. It is most commonly encountered in the expression reductio ad absurdum, a method of reasoning in which an argument is shown to lead to an absurd or contradictory conclusion. Something that is absurd, illogical, irrational, or impossible to accept through reasonable thinking. It is associated with ideas or conclusions that contradict common sense, established facts, or logical principles. In logic and philosophy, it appears in the expression reductio ad absurdum, which means demonstrating that a claim or assumption leads to an absurd or contradictory result.
synonyms: ["Reduction to the absurd","Ad absurdum argument","Logical absurdity","Disproof by contradiction"]
example_sentence: The philosopher used reductio ad absurdum to disprove the theory. By reducing the claim to absurdum, she showed its logical flaws. The argument collapses into absurdum under close examination. Students learned to test ideas by pushing them to absurdum.

english_meaning: A very large quantity of something. Plenty. More than enough. A plentiful or overflowing amount of something. It is used when there is more than enough of a thing, such as food, wealth, opportunities, happiness, or natural resources.
example_sentence: The garden produced an abundance of flowers this spring. There is an abundance of information available on the internet. The region is known for its abundance of natural resources. She lived a life of abundance and happiness.

english_meaning: Existing in large quantities, more than enough. Existing or occurring in large amounts. It refers to more than what is needed or expected. It can be used for food, resources, opportunities, happiness, knowledge, or anything available in plenty.
example_sentence:
Fish are abundant in the lake.
We have abundant evidence to prove his guilt. The region has abundant natural resources. Fresh water is abundant in this valley. She has abundant energy even after a long day. The garden produced abundant vegetables this year.

english_meaning: To use something in the wrong way or for an improper purpose. To treat a person or animal in a cruel, violent, or harmful manner. Offensive, insulting, or hurtful language directed at someone. The misuse of power, authority, or a substance such as drugs or alcohol. Unjust, corrupt, or harmful practices carried out by those in authority. Physical, emotional, sexual, or verbal mistreatment of another person.
example_sentence: Abuse of power can destroy trust in any institution. She reported the abuse to the authorities immediately. Children who suffer abuse need professional care and support. The manager was dismissed for verbal abuse of his staff. Drug abuse remains a serious public health concern worldwide.

english_meaning: Characterized by cruel, violent, or deeply offensive behavior toward others. Using harsh, insulting, and degrading language regularly. Involving unjust, harmful, or exploitative treatment of a person. Prone to causing physical, emotional, or verbal harm. Describing a relationship, environment, or individual that causes repeated injury or distress. Showing a pattern of dominance and mistreatment of vulnerable individuals.
example_sentence: Abusive behavior in the workplace must be reported immediately. She left the relationship because her partner was abusive. Abusive language on online platforms is subject to penalties. The abusive comments left her feeling deeply hurt. Children raised in abusive homes often struggle in adulthood.

english_meaning: Describes a situation, place, or group where people are actively talking, reacting, or feeling excited, often because of news, an event, or anticipation. Full of excitement, activity, or talk.
example_sentence: The office was abuzz with news of the promotion. Social media is abuzz after the movie trailer was released. The market was abuzz with shoppers before the festival. The classroom became abuzz when the teacher announced a surprise test.

english_meaning: Extremely bad, terrible, or appalling in quality or character. Of very poor standard; failing completely to meet any reasonable expectation. Described as deeply inadequate or disastrously low in performance or merit. So bad as to seem immeasurably or bottomlessly poor. Causing disappointment or dismay through profound failure or deficiency.
example_sentence: The team's performance in the final match was abysmal. The living conditions in the camp were abysmal. His abysmal grades shocked his parents and teachers. The food at that restaurant was abysmal and overpriced. Abysmal customer service drove many clients away.

english_meaning: In an extremely bad, poor, or inadequate manner. To a terribly low standard that causes disappointment or dismay. In a way that represents total failure or a profound fall short of expectations. At a level so low as to seem bottomless or immeasurable. With disastrous inadequacy or remarkably poor execution.
example_sentence: The plan was abysmally executed from start to finish. She performed abysmally in her first professional appearance. The project was abysmally underfunded from the beginning. He abysmally failed to meet the basic expectations. The reforms abysmally failed to address the root causes of poverty.

english_meaning: An extremely deep, vast, and seemingly bottomless pit or gorge. A great void or emptiness, physical or metaphorical, that appears to have no end. A state of profound despair, ignorance, or moral corruption. A deep, dark chasm in the earth or ocean floor. A metaphorical condition of hopelessness, chaos, or complete darkness. An immeasurable depth of space, sea, or human suffering.
example_sentence: The explorers looked down into the dark abyss of the canyon. She felt as if she were staring into an emotional abyss. The economy teetered on the edge of a financial abyss. The submarine descended into the abyss of the ocean. He was slowly pulled into the abyss of addiction and despair.

english_meaning: A place of study or training in a special field. A society of learned persons organized to advance art or science. A secondary school, especially a private one. An institution for higher learning. A prestigious organization recognizing achievements.
example_sentence: She was admitted to a prestigious music academy. The military academy trains future officers. He received an award from the Academy of Sciences. The film won several Academy Awards.

english_meaning: To agree, to give consent, or to accept a request or demand. To agree to something after initially resisting or considering it. It is often used in formal situations such as accepting a proposal, request, treaty, or authority. It can also mean to take on a position or office.
example_sentence: After hours of discussion, he finally acceded to their request. The government acceded to the demands of the protesters. She acceded to the position of chairperson last year. He was reluctant at first but later acceded to the plan.

english_meaning: To increase in speed or rate of movement. To cause a process, development, or change to happen more quickly. To gain momentum or pace over time. To bring forward the timing of an event or process. To grow faster in rate, especially in economic, biological, or technological contexts. To stimulate faster progress or development in an activity or condition.
example_sentence: The car began to accelerate smoothly onto the highway. Technology has helped accelerate economic growth worldwide. The doctor advised against anything that could accelerate the illness. Climate change may accelerate the melting of Arctic ice. The new investment will accelerate the development of the project.

english_meaning: To emphasize or highlight something. To stress, highlight, or make something more noticeable. It is often used in writing, speech, design, and decoration. A particular way of pronouncing words, or special importance given to something.
example_sentence: The speaker accented the key points in his speech. She accented her eyes with makeup. The report accents the need for disaster preparedness. Her accent shows she is from Karachi. The accent in this word falls on the first syllable. The program places special accent on climate awareness.

english_meaning: To make something more noticeable, stronger, or clearer. To emphasize or highlight a feature, quality, feeling, or difference so that it becomes more noticeable or important. It often refers to making something stand out clearly in speech, writing, appearance, or behavior.
example_sentence: The designer used bright colors to accentuate the beauty of the dress. Good lighting can accentuate the details of a painting. His speech accentuated the importance of education in society. The makeup was applied carefully to accentuate her eyes.

english_meaning: To agree to receive or take something offered. To consent to or agree with a proposal, idea, or situation. To admit someone into a group, place, or position. To acknowledge something as true, valid, or unavoidable.
example_sentence: She accepted the gift with a warm smile. He accepted the job offer without hesitation. The university accepted him into the engineering programme. We must accept that mistakes sometimes happen.

english_meaning: The means or opportunity to approach or enter a place. The right or opportunity to use or benefit from something.
example_sentence: You need a password to gain access to the secure computer files. The only access to the island is by a small ferry boat. Students have free access to the university library resources. He was denied access to the building because he lacked a permit.

english_meaning: The quality of being able to be reached or entered. The quality of being easy to obtain or understand.
example_sentence: The government is working to improve accessibility for disabled citizens. The accessibility of information online has changed how students study. Modern apps prioritize accessibility to ensure everyone can use them easily. The new ramp greatly increased the accessibility of the public library.

english_meaning: Able to be reached or entered. Easy to understand, obtain, or influence.
example_sentence: The remote village is only accessible by a narrow dirt road. Her writing style is very accessible to a broad range of readers. The manager makes sure he is accessible to his staff at all times. All public buildings must be accessible to people in wheelchairs.

english_meaning: The attainment or acquisition of a position of rank or power. A new item added to a collection. Formal acceptance or agreement to a treaty. The act of joining an organization or country. An increase or addition to something.
example_sentence: The queen's accession to the throne was celebrated nationwide. The library announced several new accessions this month. The country signed the accession to the trade agreement. His accession to power surprised everyone.

english_meaning: To add fashion accessories to an outfit. To provide a machine or room with extra functional or decorative items.
example_sentence: She decided to accessorize her black dress with a pearl necklace. You can accessorize your new car with various high-tech gadgets. The stylist showed the models how to accessorize for the summer season. He loves to accessorize his desk with unique stationery and plants.

english_meaning: A supplementary item that adds to, completes, or enhances the primary thing. A decorative item worn or carried to complement an outfit or appearance. A person who knowingly assists in a crime without directly committing it. An additional attachment or component that adds functionality to a main device. Something secondary in importance that nonetheless contributes to the whole.
example_sentence: She bought a matching accessory for her new outfit. He was charged as an accessory to the robbery. A good belt can serve as the perfect accessory for any look. Accessories such as earrings and bracelets complete the ensemble. The police arrested both the main suspect and the accessory.

english_meaning: Enthusiastic public praise, recognition, or approval given to someone or something. To greet or welcome someone with strong approval or admiration. An expression of great admiration or applause by a group of people. To publicly announce, recognize, or proclaim someone as outstanding or excellent. Strong, enthusiastic, and widespread positive reception of a work, performance, or person.
example_sentence: Her debut novel received widespread critical acclaim. The artist's performance won her international acclaim. He was acclaimed as one of the greatest scientists of his generation. The film received acclaim at every major film festival. She smiled modestly despite the unanimous acclaim from the audience.

english_meaning: To adjust to a new environment situation or climate. To gradually become used to new surroundings, conditions or climate so that your body or mind can function comfortably.
example_sentence: It took days to acclimate to the heat. She acclimated to her new job quickly. The team acclimated to the altitude. Plants acclimate slowly.

english_meaning: An award, honor, or expression of praise for achievement. Recognition or praise given to someone for their accomplishments, excellence, or merit. It can be formal, like an award, or informal, like verbal praise. Historically, a touch on the shoulder with a sword to confer knighthood.
example_sentence: She received the highest accolade for her research in medicine. The film won multiple accolades at the international festival. He earned accolades from his colleagues for his dedication. The author’s work was met with critical accolades. The teacher’s encouragement was an accolade in itself. (praise or approval)

english_meaning: To provide adequate space, lodging, or facilities for someone. To adjust, adapt, or modify to meet someone's needs or preferences. To make room for or fulfill a request in a cooperative manner. To reconcile or bring into agreement different opinions or interests. To oblige or do a favor for someone without inconvenience. To contain or hold a certain number of people or things.
example_sentence: The hotel can accommodate up to three hundred guests. They tried to accommodate all dietary requirements at the event. The school was willing to accommodate students with special needs. He was kind enough to accommodate her last-minute request. The conference room can accommodate up to fifty people.

english_meaning: Someone who knowingly assists, supports, or takes part in a crime or illegal act carried out by another person. The accomplice may help plan the act, provide tools, give information, or help after the act such as hiding evidence or protecting the offender.
example_sentence: The robber and his accomplice escaped on a motorcycle. Investigators searched for an accomplice who helped hide the stolen money. He did not want to be an accomplice in a dishonest plan. The detective believed the criminal had at least one accomplice inside

english_meaning: To successfully achieve or complete a task, goal, or purpose. To manage to do something difficult or impressive. To bring something to a successful conclusion.
example_sentence: She was determined to accomplish every goal she had set herself before the year was out. He accomplished the seemingly impossible task in less time than anyone expected. The team accomplished more in one week than most groups manage in a month. Without the right support, it is very difficult to accomplish anything meaningful. She was proud of everything she had accomplished in her long and distinguished career.

english_meaning: To grant, bestow, or reconcile, to be in harmony with. A formal or informal agreement between people, groups, or countries, a state of harmony where opinions or actions match.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a peace accord to end the conflict. His actions were in accord with his words. The committee accorded her the highest honor. There was a natural accord between the team members, which improved their performance.

english_meaning: A written or spoken report describing an event or experience. A record of money received and paid out. An arrangement with a bank or business for financial transactions. Importance, value, or consideration given to something. To consider or regard in a particular way.
example_sentence: She gave a detailed account of the accident to the police. He opened a new bank account last week. The teacher took every student's opinion into account. All employees must account for the funds they use.

english_meaning: A spoken or written description of what happened. A report giving the details of an incident in order. A narrative of occurrences as observed or remembered by someone. A record used as evidence of how something took place.
example_sentence: The witness gave a clear account of events to the police. Her account of events differed from his in several details. The book offers a detailed account of events during the war. Reporters pieced together an account of events from many sources.

english_meaning: The fact or condition of being responsible for one's actions and decisions. The obligation to explain, justify, and take responsibility for what one does. A willingness to accept blame or credit for outcomes. The quality of being answerable to someone for a duty or task. A system in which people are required to report on their work and accept its consequences.
example_sentence: Public officials must act with honesty and accountability. There is a growing demand for greater accountability in government. The manager takes full accountability for the team's performance. Teachers share accountability for their students' progress.

english_meaning: Required or expected to justify one's actions or decisions. Responsible for something and obligated to explain it. Answerable to someone in a position of authority. Able to be explained or understood. Held liable for the outcome of one's conduct.
example_sentence: Every employee is accountable for the quality of their work. Ministers are accountable to parliament for their decisions. The company must be held accountable for the pollution it caused. Parents are accountable for the safety of their children.

english_meaning: To officially recognize and certify an organization, institution, or person as meeting required standards. To give credit or assign responsibility to someone for an achievement or action. To send or appoint an official representative with recognized credentials. To provide formal authorization or approval to operate in an official capacity. To validate or endorse the quality and legitimacy of a program or professional.
example_sentence: The board voted to accredit the university's new medical program. The government accredited her as an official representative. Several organizations accredit teachers before they enter classrooms. He was accredited with discovering a new species of insect. The institution was accredited after a thorough review process.

english_meaning: Officially recognised or approved as meeting a required standard. Given official authority or sanction to act on behalf of an organisation or country. Certified as qualified by an authorised body. Widely accepted or believed to be true.
example_sentence: She studied at an accredited nursing college. Only accredited journalists were allowed inside the hall. The laboratory is accredited by the national testing authority. He served as the accredited representative of his government.

english_meaning: To grow or increase gradually by the addition of new layers or parts. To become attached or joined together by growth. To accumulate slowly over time.
example_sentence: Sediment accretes on the ocean floor over centuries. Small planets accrete matter from surrounding dust. Interest continues to accrete on the unpaid amount. The reef has accreted slowly over thousands of years.

english_meaning: Gradual growth or increase by the addition of new layers or parts. The process of things being added or joined to something over time. A thing formed or added in this way. In law, an increase of property by natural addition, such as land added by a river.
example_sentence: The delta grows by the slow accretion of silt. Coral reefs form through the accretion of tiny organisms. The library expanded by gradual accretion over a century. Lawyers argued about the accretion of land along the riverbank.

english_meaning: The gradual accumulation or increase of something over time. An amount of money, interest, or benefit that builds up and becomes due. In accounting, the recording of income or expenses when they are earned or incurred rather than when cash is exchanged.
example_sentence: The accrual of interest begins from the date of deposit. Employees can check the accrual of their annual leave. The company follows the accrual method of accounting. Late payment led to a steady accrual of penalties.

english_meaning: To accumulate or receive gradually over time, especially something beneficial like interest, benefits, or advantages. It can also mean to grow or increase naturally as a result of an action or process.
example_sentence: Interest will accrue on your savings account every month. Over the years, she accrued a lot of knowledge about art. Benefits accrue to employees after five years of service. Legal fees may accrue if the case continues for a long time.

english_meaning: To adopt the customs, values, and behaviour of another culture. To help or cause a person or group to adjust to a different culture. To modify a culture through prolonged contact with another culture.
example_sentence: Immigrant families often acculturate within a generation. Schools help newcomers acculturate more easily. He struggled to acculturate after moving abroad. The tribe slowly acculturated to life in the city.

english_meaning: To gather or collect over time. To gradually gather or increase in quantity, number, or value over a period. It can refer to tangible things like money, objects, or intangible things like knowledge or experience.
example_sentence: She managed to accumulate a large collection of books over the years. Debt can quickly accumulate if you are not careful with your spending. The snow accumulated on the roof during the night. Over time, he accumulated a lot of experience in disaster management.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being correct, precise, and free from error. Conformity with truth, fact, or an established standard. The degree to which a measurement, calculation, or statement reflects the actual value. Precision and reliability in the performance of a task or communication of information. Exactness and faithfulness to the true nature of something.
example_sentence: The accuracy of the data was confirmed by multiple experts. She prided herself on the accuracy of her financial reports. Accuracy is essential in medical diagnoses to avoid errors. The map's accuracy impressed all who used it for navigation. The survey's accuracy was questioned due to sampling errors.

english_meaning: Correct in all details and free from errors. Precise and exact in measurement or description. Careful and truthful in reporting or reflecting facts. Hitting the intended target or mark.
example_sentence: The report gives an accurate account of the incident. Her watch is very accurate. We need accurate measurements before cutting the wood. The archer's aim was accurate.

english_meaning: In a way that is correct and true in every detail. With precision and exactness. Without any errors or mistakes. In a manner faithful to the facts or original. Done carefully and reliably.
example_sentence: The witness accurately described the suspect to the police. The scientist accurately measured the temperature of the sample. She accurately predicted the outcome of the election. The map shows the borders accurately.

english_meaning: A charge or claim that someone has done something wrong or illegal. A statement blaming a person for a fault, crime, or offense. The act of accusing or being accused. An assertion that a person is guilty of misconduct, often made formally.
example_sentence: The accusation against him was never proven in court. She denied the accusation of cheating in the exam. Making a serious accusation requires solid evidence. The accusations damaged his political career. He responded calmly to the false accusation.

english_meaning: To charge someone with an offence or crime. To claim that someone has done something wrong. To blame someone for a fault or wrongdoing.
example_sentence: The police accused him of theft. She was accused of lying to the committee. Do not accuse anyone without evidence. He accused his brother of breaking the vase.

english_meaning: A person or people charged with or on trial for a crime. Blamed or held responsible for a fault or offence. Formally charged with wrongdoing in a court of law.
example_sentence: The accused stood silently before the judge. The accused denied all the charges against him. Two of the accused were released on bail. The lawyer defended the accused with strong arguments.

english_meaning: To make someone or oneself familiar with something through regular experience. To cause to accept as usual or normal. To adapt to a new condition, place, or way of life. To habituate through repeated exposure. To train oneself to something.
example_sentence: It took her time to accustom herself to the cold weather. Soldiers are accustomed to a strict routine. He soon accustomed himself to living alone. Parents should accustom children to early sleeping habits.

english_meaning: A secret advantage, plan, or resource kept hidden until it is needed. A hidden strength or clever trick that can be used to win or gain the upper hand. Something powerful held in reserve and revealed at the right moment. An unexpected resource that gives a person an edge over others.
example_sentence: She stayed calm because she had an ace up her sleeve. The lawyer kept one strong witness as an ace up his sleeve. Our team has an ace up its sleeve for the final match. He smiled quietly, clearly holding an ace up his sleeve.

english_meaning: Sharp and bitter in taste. Harsh, severe, or biting in speech, manner, or tone. Cutting or sarcastic in expression.
example_sentence: The critic gave an acerb review of the play. Her acerb remarks silenced the whole room. He had an acerb wit that few people appreciated. The lemon had an unpleasantly acerb taste.

english_meaning: To convert or be converted into vinegar or acetic acid. To make sour or acidic in taste or nature.
example_sentence: Wine can acetify if the bottle is left open. Bacteria acetify the liquid during fermentation. Warm temperatures may acetify unfinished wine. The chemist explained how alcohol begins to acetify.

english_meaning: Vinegar, especially as used in pharmacy or chemistry. A dilute solution of acetic acid used as a solvent for medicinal substances.
example_sentence: The pharmacist prepared the tincture using acetum. Acetum has been used in medicine since ancient times. The recipe called for a small quantity of acetum. Acetum is a common solvent in traditional preparations.

english_meaning: A continuous or prolonged dull pain in a part of the body. To suffer from a continuous dull pain. To feel intense sadness or longing. A strong emotional desire or yearning.
example_sentence: I have a terrible ache in my back. My legs ached after the long walk. Her heart ached for her lost friend. He ached to see his family again.

english_meaning: To reach a desired result after planning or effort. To accomplish something difficult. To complete a task successfully. To gain success in exams, career, or life goals. To bring a planned idea into reality.
example_sentence: She worked hard to achieve her dream of becoming a doctor. The team achieved great success in the tournament. He achieved his target before the deadline. They achieved better results after improving their strategy.

english_meaning: The successful completion of a task or goal through effort and skill. A great or heroic deed or exploit. The act of attaining something desired or significant. An accomplishment that confers honor or distinction. A heraldic device or a complete display of armorial bearings.
example_sentence: Winning the Nobel Prize is a remarkable scientific achievement. The team celebrated the achievement of their sales targets after months of hard work. We should focus on personal growth and individual achievement rather than just status. The knight's shield displayed his heraldic achievement with pride.

english_meaning: A small but serious weakness in someone or something that is otherwise strong. A vulnerable point that could lead to failure or downfall. In anatomy, informally, the Achilles tendon area.
example_sentence: Poor defence has always been the team's Achilles heel. His temper is his Achilles heel in business. The company's Achilles heel was its dependence on a single supplier. Chocolate is my Achilles heel when I try to diet.

english_meaning: A chemical substance that neutralises alkalis, turns litmus red, and has a sour taste. Having a sour or sharp taste. Sharp, bitter, or critical in tone or manner. A powerful hallucinogenic drug (informal).
example_sentence: Lemon juice contains a mild acid. The chemist mixed the acid with water carefully. She made an acid comment about his behaviour. Acid rain is harmful to plants and buildings.

english_meaning: The industrial or metallurgical process of converting iron into steel by adding carbon. A cementation technique used to produce steel from wrought iron by introducing carbon at high temperatures. The process of hardening and strengthening iron by infusing it with carbon to create a durable alloy. A historical method of producing carburized or case-hardened iron surfaces. A procedure used in metalworking to improve the structural integrity of iron.
example_sentence: Acieration was a key industrial process during the Industrial Revolution. The factory specialized in the acieration of raw iron.
