Modern techniques have significantly improved the acieration process. Acieration produces steel that is stronger than ordinary iron. Engineers studied acieration to develop better building materials.

english_meaning: Lacking cilia or hair-like projections on the surface of a cell or organism.  A scientific term used mainly in biology and zoology to describe a cell, tissue, or organism that does not have cilia, which are tiny hair-like structures used for movement or for moving fluids across a surface.
antonyms: ["Ciliated","Hairy","Flagellated (in some biological contexts","though flagella and cilia are different structures) Bearing cilia"]
example_sentence: The researcher identified an aciliate cell under the microscope. Some microorganisms are naturally aciliate and rely on other methods of movement. The specimen appeared aciliate, showing no visible hair-like structures. Scientists compared the aciliate organism with closely related ciliated species.

english_meaning: The highest point of achievement, development, or excellence. The peak or summit of something. The most perfect example of a particular quality or type.
example_sentence: That performance was the acme of her long career. The building is considered the acme of modern design. He reached the acme of political power at forty. Their craftsmanship is the acme of patience and skill.

english_meaning: Fear of sounds or noises. An extreme or irrational fear of certain sounds or noises. People with this phobia may experience anxiety, panic attacks, or avoidance behavior when exposed to loud, unexpected, or particular types of sounds.
example_sentence: Her acoustic phobia made it difficult for her to attend concerts. Children with acoustic phobia may cover their ears during thunderstorms. The sudden alarms triggered his acoustic phobia. Acoustic phobia can interfere with daily life if left untreated.

english_meaning: Fear of sounds or noises. An extreme or irrational fear of certain sounds or noises. People with this phobia may experience anxiety, panic attacks, or avoidance behavior when exposed to loud, unexpected, or particular types of sounds.
example_sentence: Her acousticophobia made it difficult for her to attend concerts. Children with acousticophobia may cover their ears during thunderstorms. The sudden alarms triggered his acousticophobia. Acousticophobia can interfere with daily life if left untreated.

english_meaning: To make someone aware of or familiar with something or someone. To introduce a person to someone or something so that they know them or are familiar with the facts, skills, or ideas. It involves providing knowledge or information to someone, or becoming familiar with someone or something.
example_sentence: She wanted to acquaint herself with the new software before the meeting. I would like to acquaint you with our team members. The guide acquainted the tourists with the history of the city. He was quickly acquainted with the rules of the game.

english_meaning: A person you know but who is not a close friend. Someone you have met or know slightly through work, school, social contact, or community interaction. The relationship is polite or casual rather than deep or personal. It can also refer to general knowledge or familiarity with something.
example_sentence: She is only an acquaintance from my college days. I met an old acquaintance at the conference yesterday. His acquaintance with climate science helped him understand environmental risks better. We became friends after starting as simple acquaintances at work.

english_meaning: To accept or comply with something without voicing objection or protest. To give silent or reluctant consent to a proposal, decision, or demand. To go along with something passively even when one disagrees. To yield or submit to a situation or authority without resistance. To tacitly agree by not challenging or opposing what is happening. To tolerate a situation by choosing not to fight against it.
example_sentence: He reluctantly acquiesced to the decision made by the committee. She had no choice but to acquiesce to the demands of her superiors. The government eventually acquiesced to the public's demands. Though unhappy, he acquiesced to the new working conditions. She acquiesced to the proposal after long and careful consideration.

english_meaning: To gain, obtain, or come into possession of something through effort or experience. To buy or procure something through commerce or exchange. To develop or build up a skill, knowledge, or habit over time. To come to have or possess something previously lacking. To secure ownership of property, assets, or resources. To absorb or learn through practice, exposure, or experience.
example_sentence: She worked hard to acquire the necessary skills for the job. The company plans to acquire several smaller businesses next year. He managed to acquire a rare collection of vintage books. Children naturally acquire language through exposure and interaction. She acquired a taste for classical music after years of listening.

english_meaning: The process of gaining possession, knowledge, skill, property, or control over something. It can be used in business when one company purchases another, in learning when a person gains knowledge or language, or generally when something valuable is obtained.
example_sentence: The company made a major acquisition by purchasing a smaller technology firm. Language acquisition in children usually happens naturally through interaction. The museum announced the acquisition of several ancient paintings. Hard work led to the acquisition of valuable skills.

english_meaning: To declare someone not guilty of a crime. To formally decide in a court of law that a person is not guilty of the crime they were accused of. To behave or perform in a particular way during a situation or task.
example_sentence: The jury decided to acquit the man due to lack of evidence. After reviewing the facts, the judge acquitted her of all charges. The officer acquitted himself well during the difficult investigation. She acquitted her duties with honesty and dedication.

english_meaning: A decision by a court that a person accused of a crime is not guilty. The formal judgment given by a judge or jury stating that the accused person is not guilty of the charges. It ends the criminal case and releases the person from legal blame for that charge. It may occur when evidence is insufficient or when the court finds the accused innocent.
example_sentence: The jury announced the acquittal of the accused after reviewing all the evidence. His acquittal brought relief to his family and supporters. The court ordered an acquittal because the prosecution failed to prove the charge. After a long trial, the defendant finally received an acquittal.

english_meaning: A unit of land area measurement used in the imperial and U·S. customary systems. An area equal to 43,560 square feet or approximately 4,047 square meters. Historically, the amount of land a yoke of oxen could plow in one day. One-six-hundred-and-fortieth of a square mile. A plot of land commonly used for agricultural or real estate assessment. A broad extent or large quantity of land in general. A measurement equal to 4,840 square yards.
example_sentence: The farmer purchased a ten acre plot to expand his wheat production. Each acre of the estate was meticulously landscaped with native flowers. The price of an acre has risen significantly due to urban development. It takes a considerable amount of time to mow an entire acre of grass.

english_meaning: Angry and bitter in tone or manner, especially in speech or argument. Marked by sharp resentment and harsh words. Full of ill feeling and hostility. Characterised by bitter disagreement.
example_sentence: The meeting ended in an acrimonious dispute. They went through a long and acrimonious divorce. His acrimonious remarks upset the whole team. Relations between the two neighbours grew acrimonious.

english_meaning: Bitter anger or harshness in speech or behavior. A strong feeling of bitterness, resentment, or sharp anger that appears in a person's words, tone, or actions, especially during arguments, criticism, or long standing conflicts. It often shows hostility and lack of goodwill between people or groups.
example_sentence: The debate ended with a lot of acrimony between the two leaders. Years of legal disputes created deep acrimony between the families. The meeting was supposed to be calm, but it quickly turned into acrimony and accusations. Despite the earlier acrimony, they later agreed to work together.

english_meaning: A person who performs difficult physical movements such as jumping, balancing, bending, and flipping, often in a circus, gymnastic show, or stage performance. It also refers to someone who shows great skill and flexibility in body movement or sometimes in handling difficult situations cleverly.
example_sentence: The acrobat amazed the audience by walking across the rope without losing balance. A young acrobat flipped through the air during the circus show. The acrobat trained for years to perfect his balance and strength. She moved like an acrobat, bending and turning with great control and grace.

english_meaning: A word formed from the initial letters of other words. A type of abbreviation created by combining the first letters of a series of words to form a new word, which is usually easier to say or remember.
example_sentence: NASA is an acronym for National Aeronautics and Space Administration. AIDS is an acronym for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. ASAP is an acronym for As Soon As Possible. PIN is an acronym for Personal Identification Number.

english_meaning: An intense or extreme fear of heights. It is a type of specific phobia where a person feels anxiety, panic, or dread when they are at a high place or even thinking about heights.
example_sentence: She could not go on the Ferris wheel because of her acrophobia. His acrophobia made climbing the ladder nearly impossible. Even standing on a balcony triggered his acrophobia. People with acrophobia often avoid tall buildings or mountain trips.

english_meaning: A fortified elevated city or citadel built on a hill in ancient Greek civilization. The rocky hilltop on which major temples and public buildings of ancient Greek city-states were constructed. A historically significant elevated platform serving as the religious and civic center of a Greek city. A protected highland settlement used for defense and worship in ancient times. The highest point of a city, particularly referring to the famous Acropolis of Athens, Greece.
example_sentence: Tourists from around the world visit the Acropolis in Athens. The Acropolis houses the famous Parthenon temple. The ancient Acropolis was once the religious center of the city. Scholars have studied the architecture of the Acropolis for centuries. The view from the Acropolis offers a stunning panorama of Athens.

english_meaning: An action, rule, change, or effect that applies to all members of a group, all areas, or every part of something without exception. It indicates uniform treatment or impact rather than selective application.
example_sentence: The company announced a five percent salary increase across the board. The government reduced taxes across the board to support businesses. The new safety rules apply across the board to every department. Prices were raised across the board due to rising production costs.

english_meaning: A poem, word puzzle, or text in which the first letters of each line or sentence spell out a word or message. A literary device in which specific letters, typically the first of each line, combine to form a hidden word or name. A form of wordplay used in poetry where initials create a concealed pattern or meaning. A type of written composition used as a code, puzzle, or decorative literary form. A creative writing technique where each line begins with a letter that collectively spells a name, word, or phrase.
example_sentence: She wrote an acrostic poem spelling her mother's name. The teacher asked the class to create an acrostic using the word SCIENCE. An acrostic is a clever way to embed a hidden message in writing. The children enjoyed making acrostics with their own names. The puzzle book included several fun acrostics for readers to solve.

english_meaning: To represent someone, take action on their behalf, or perform duties for another person or organization. It is used when a person or organization performs duties, makes decisions, or represents another person, usually in a formal, legal, or professional context. It often appears in business, law, or official matters.
example_sentence: The lawyer acts for several international clients. He was asked to act for the chairman during the meeting. She acted for her sister in signing the documents. The firm acts for many large companies.

english_meaning: To take action based on advice, information, or feelings. To do something because you have been advised or told to do it. Carry further or advance.
example_sentence: She acted on the doctor’s advice. The police were acting on a tip from an informer and caught the gang red-handed. Why didn't you act on her suggestion? There have been concerns as to why the Board didn't act on a recommended pay raise.

english_meaning: To express emotions or behavior, often in a dramatic way. Perform something with actions and gestures. To represent in action. To translate into action. To perform a ceremony or show how something happened, as if performing a play.
example_sentence: The children acted out their favourite poem. The ritual of the party conference is acted out in the same way every year. Children's negative feelings often get acted out in bad behaviour. The child acted out in class. She acted out her frustrations.

english_meaning: To behave badly or malfunction. To not work as it should. To act in a way different from that which is normal or expected.
example_sentence: My computer’s ACTING UP; I think I might have a virus. The kids started acting up. How long has your ankle been acting up? Sophie got bored and started acting up. My car always acts up in cold weather. The child acted up in class. The computer is acting up again.

english_meaning: What you do is more important than what you say. What people do is more important than what they say. Real intentions and character are shown through actions, not promises or words. Deeds are more powerful and truthful than speech.
example_sentence: He promised to help the poor, but never did anything, actions speak louder than words. She never talks much about kindness, but always helps others, actions speak louder than words. A true leader shows commitment through work, not speeches, actions speak louder than words. Instead of saying sorry, he changed his behavior, actions speak louder than words.

english_meaning: To make something start working or to cause a device or system to begin operating. To make a person or thing more active or lively. To start a process or reaction. To bring into effect or use.
example_sentence: Press this button to activate the machine. She activated her new SIM card this morning. Exercise helps to activate the muscles. The alarm is automatically activated at night.

english_meaning: A person who works actively and energetically to bring about political, social, environmental, or other kinds of change. Someone who campaigns for or against a particular cause, often through protests, organizing, speeches, or writing. Relating to or characteristic of activism. A person who supports vigorous action rather than passive acceptance.
example_sentence: She is a well-known human rights activist in the country. The environmental activist led a peaceful protest against pollution. Many young activists are using social media to spread awareness. He was an activist for women's education throughout his life. The journalist interviewed several activists working in rural areas.

english_meaning: The state of existing in fact or reality. Actual existence as opposed to what is imagined or supposed. The true situation or real state of affairs. Something that actually exists or happens.
example_sentence: The plan became an actuality after years of work. In actuality, the situation was worse than reported. The dream transformed into actuality. We must deal with actualities, not theories.

english_meaning: Sharp ability to understand and judge situations quickly. Keen insight, sharp intelligence, and the ability to make good judgments quickly, especially in practical matters such as business, politics, leadership, or problem solving. A person with acumen can notice details, understand complex situations, and make wise decisions.
example_sentence: Her business acumen helped the company grow rapidly. The leader showed great political acumen during the crisis. His financial acumen allowed him to make smart investments. Teachers admired her academic acumen and analytical thinking.

english_meaning: To taper gradually to a sharp, fine point at the tip. To make or become increasingly pointed toward the end. Describing a shape, structure, or biological feature that narrows to a distinct fine point. To sharpen or make more acute at one end. Characterized by a gradual and elegant narrowing to a pointed tip, especially in botanical or anatomical contexts.
example_sentence: The leaf had an acuminate tip that narrowed to a fine point. The craftsman worked to acuminate the wooden stake for the fence. Many tropical plants have acuminate leaves adapted to shedding rain. The tool was acuminated to allow precise cutting. The pencil was sharpened to an acuminate point.

english_meaning: The process or result of tapering to a sharp or fine point. The state or quality of ending in a pointed tip. The gradual narrowing of a structure, leaf, crystal, or shape to a distinct sharp end. The act of making something more acute or pointed. The condition of being pointed or having a sharpened extremity in natural or manufactured objects.
example_sentence: The acumination of the blade improved its cutting precision. The botanist described the acumination of the leaf tip. The gradual acumination of the crystal structure was remarkable. The acumination of the tool required careful grinding. Acumination is a common feature among many species of tropical plants.

english_meaning: Very serious, severe, or intense. Sharp and quick in perception or understanding. Having a keen sense or intelligence. Sudden and short but severe in effect, especially of an illness. Forming an angle less than ninety degrees.
example_sentence: The patient is suffering from acute pain in the chest. She has an acute sense of hearing. There is an acute shortage of clean water in the area. His acute analysis impressed the entire committee.

english_meaning: An angle that measures less than 90 degrees. A sharp, narrow angle formed by two lines meeting closely. Any angle greater than zero but smaller than a right angle. A common term in geometry used to classify angles by size.
example_sentence: An acute angle is always less than a right angle. The two roads meet at an acute angle. He measured an acute angle of fifty degrees. Each angle of this triangle is an acute angle.

english_meaning: A triangle in which all three interior angles are less than 90 degrees. A triangle with three acute angles. A sharp-cornered triangle without any right or obtuse angle. One of the three main types of triangle classified by angle.
example_sentence: An equilateral triangle is always an acute-angled triangle. Each angle of an acute-angled triangle is less than ninety degrees. The teacher drew an acute-angled triangle on the board. They identified the shape as an acute-angled triangle.

english_meaning: To a very intense, severe, or extreme degree. With great perception, intelligence, or sensitivity. In a manner that is sharp, penetrating, and clear. So strongly felt or experienced as to be almost overwhelming. To a painfully high or critical degree. In a way that demands immediate attention due to intensity or urgency.
example_sentence: She was acutely aware of the tension in the room. He felt acutely embarrassed when he forgot his speech. The patients suffered acutely from the lack of medical care. She was acutely conscious of every sound in the silent house. He acutely analyzed every angle of the problem before responding.

english_meaning: The quality of being sharp, keen, or intense. Sharpness of mind, perception, or judgement. The severity or intensity of a pain, illness, or crisis. Keenness of a sense such as hearing or sight.
example_sentence: The acuteness of his hearing surprised the doctor. She solved the puzzle with remarkable acuteness. The acuteness of the crisis forced quick action. Age gradually reduced the acuteness of her vision.

english_meaning: Not cyclic; not arranged in or forming a closed ring or cycle. In chemistry, describing a compound whose atoms form an open chain rather than a ring. In mathematics, describing a graph that contains no cycles. Not occurring in regular repeated cycles.
example_sentence: Butane is an acyclic hydrocarbon. The algorithm works only on a directed acyclic graph. Her symptoms followed an acyclic pattern. Acyclic compounds are also called open-chain compounds.

english_meaning: An antiviral medicine used to treat infections caused by herpes viruses. A drug prescribed for cold sores, genital herpes, chickenpox, and shingles. A synthetic nucleoside analogue that stops viral DNA from replicating. A widely used medication available as tablets, cream, or injection.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed acyclovir for the cold sores. Acyclovir works best when taken early in the infection. She applied acyclovir cream twice a day. Acyclovir is included in the list of essential medicines.

english_meaning: Made or done for a particular purpose or situation, not planned in advance. Something created or done specifically for a single, immediate problem or purpose. It is not part of a long-term plan or system. It is often temporary and used only when needed.
example_sentence: The company formed an ad hoc committee to solve the crisis. We made an ad hoc arrangement for the meeting. The decision was ad hoc and not part of the official policy. They built an ad hoc shelter during the storm.

english_meaning: Endlessly. Again and again in the same way; without limit or end.
example_sentence: The debate continued ad infinitum without reaching any conclusion. He repeated the same excuse ad infinitum until no one believed him anymore. The committee argued the point ad infinitum, wasting hours of everyone's time. She joked that the meeting could go on ad infinitum if no one called it to a close.

english_meaning: To a boring or annoying degree. Continuing something for too long until it becomes tiresome. Repeating something excessively. Doing or discussing something to the point of disgust. Beyond the limit of endurance or interest.
example_sentence: He repeated the same story ad nauseam. The politicians debated the issue ad nauseam. She complained ad nauseam about the noisy neighbors. The topic was discussed ad nauseam in every meeting.

english_meaning: To speak, perform, or act without preparation, improvise. Something improvised or made up on the spot. Done spontaneously without preparation
example_sentence: The actor had to ad-lib when he forgot his lines. She ad-libbed a reply to the unexpected question.  His ad-lib saved the presentation. His ad-lib saved the presentation. She gave an ad-lib performance. He made an ad-lib comment during the meeting.

english_meaning: A short, widely known saying that expresses a general truth or piece of wisdom. A traditional, well-accepted proverb passed down through generations. A brief, memorable phrase that encapsulates a common human experience or moral truth. A time-honored expression of wisdom found in many languages and cultures. A pithy statement that conveys a universal truth in a concise and memorable form.
example_sentence: The adage 'actions speak louder than words' is still very relevant today. He often cited the old adage that patience is a virtue. There is an old adage that says you reap what you sow. The teacher used the adage to illustrate the day's moral lesson. His grandmother lived by the adage that honesty is the best policy.

english_meaning: The lump at the front of the throat formed by the thyroid cartilage, usually more visible in men. The projecting part of the larynx that moves up and down during swallowing or speaking. A visible bulge in the neck that becomes prominent during male puberty.
example_sentence: His Adam's apple moved as he swallowed nervously. Boys develop a visible Adam's apple during puberty. The doctor examined the area around his Adam's apple. You can feel your Adam's apple by touching your throat.

english_meaning: Very firm in opinion or decision. Not willing to change. A person who refuses to change an opinion, decision, or attitude even when others try to persuade them. It also refers to something extremely hard or unbreakable in older usage.
example_sentence: She was adamant that the project must finish on time. The teacher remained adamant about maintaining discipline in the classroom. Despite many requests, he stayed adamant and refused to change his decision. The manager was adamant about following the company rules.

english_meaning: Extremely hard, unyielding, or impenetrable in physical or figurative sense. Having the hardness and brilliance of a diamond. Unbreakable and resistant to any force or pressure. Showing a firm and inflexible character that cannot be bent or worn down. Describing a material or will that is impossibly strong or resistant to any external influence.
example_sentence: Her adamantine will impressed everyone around her. The knight's adamantine armor protected him in every battle. He held an adamantine grip on his principles despite criticism. The general's adamantine determination inspired his soldiers. The contract was written with adamantine terms that could not be altered.

english_meaning: To change or adjust oneself or something else to suit new or different conditions. To modify a piece of work to fit a new purpose, medium, or audience. To become accustomed to or fit in with a new environment or situation. To alter behavior, habits, or structure in response to changed circumstances. To rework or adjust a plan, system, or idea to improve its suitability.
example_sentence: Animals must adapt to survive in changing environments. She had to adapt her teaching style for online classes. He quickly adapted to life in a new country. The novel was adapted into a successful film. Companies that fail to adapt often fall behind their competitors.

english_meaning: The process of changing something so that it suits a new situation or purpose. A film, play or book based on a work in another form. In biology, a feature or change that helps a living thing survive in its environment. The act of becoming accustomed to new conditions.
example_sentence: The film is an adaptation of a famous novel. Adaptation to desert life takes many generations. The building required some adaptation for wheelchair users. Their quick adaptation to the new system impressed everyone.

english_meaning: To begin a completely new phase in one's life or history. To introduce a significant new development or era into an ongoing situation. To bring a fresh perspective or completely different turn of events to a narrative. To experience a major change that alters the course of existence or a specific field.
synonyms: ["Turn Over A New Leaf","Start Fresh","Open A New Phase","Begin A New Era","Make A Fresh Start","Chart A New Course","Enter A New Stage","Break New Ground","Turn A Corner","Usher In A New Epoch"]
antonyms: ["Maintain The Status Quo","Keep Things The Same","Stay In A Rut","Dwell In The Past","Continue The Old Ways","End The Story","Close The Book","Halt Progress","Stagnate","Remain Unchanged"]
example_sentence: Winning the championship will add a new chapter to the team's legacy. Her decision to move abroad is going to add a new chapter to her personal journey. The discovery of this artifact will add a new chapter to ancient history. We are ready to add a new chapter to our business by expanding internationally.

english_meaning: To make a bad or difficult situation worse by saying or doing something that increases anger, tension, or conflict. To intensify a problem or emotion rather than calm it down.
example_sentence: His rude comments only added fuel to the fire during the argument. When she laughed at his mistake, it added fuel to the fire. Blaming others at this point will just add fuel to the fire. Spreading rumors about them added fuel to the fire of misunderstanding.:

english_meaning: To make a bad situation worse. To say or do something that increases anger, tension, or problems.
example_sentence: His words added fuel to the fire. When he insulted her in front of everyone, it only added fuel to the fire. Bringing up old arguments during the meeting will just add fuel to the fire. His rude comment on social media added fuel to the fire of the ongoing controversy. Instead of calming his friend down, he shouted back and added fuel to the fire.

english_meaning: To include something extra or attach something additional. To attach or include something extra to what already exists. To add extra cost or fee. To include more information or detail. To install additional digital items or features.
example_sentence: We can add on a storage room if you need more space. They added on extra charges at the end of the bill. You can add on new features to the software anytime. She added on two more tasks before finishing the report.

english_meaning: To make a total when counted. To seem reasonable or make sense. To calculate the total of several items. To gradually form a noticeable amount. To seem believable or consistent with known facts.
example_sentence: These expenses do not add up. When you add up all the costs, the project becomes expensive. His story does not add up, so I doubt it. Small savings add up over time.

english_meaning: Something extra that is added to improve, extend, or complete something. An extra feature, service, item, or component that is attached to a product, plan, software, building, or system to increase its usefulness, capacity, or value. It is not part of the original basic structure but is included later to improve performance or convenience.
example_sentence: The customer purchased an add on for extra cloud storage. The hotel offers breakfast as an add on to the room package. The developer installed a browser add on to block ads. The new room is an add on to the original house.

english_meaning: A person who is physically or psychologically dependent on a substance or behavior. Someone who has developed an uncontrollable and compulsive need for something harmful. A person unable to stop a habit or behavior despite knowing its negative consequences. To cause someone to become dependent on something through repeated exposure. An enthusiast or devotee deeply committed to a particular interest or activity.
example_sentence: He became an addict after years of recreational drug use. The program was designed to help recovering addicts rebuild their lives. She is a self-confessed addict when it comes to reading mystery novels. The addict sought treatment at a rehabilitation center. Being a social media addict can negatively impact mental health.

english_meaning: A chronic, compulsive physical or psychological dependence on a substance or behavior. A condition characterized by an inability to stop using a substance despite harmful consequences. A strong habitual attachment to a behavior or activity that disrupts normal life. A medical disorder involving uncontrollable craving, seeking, and use of a substance. The state of being enslaved to a habit, practice, or substance that is harmful to the individual.
example_sentence: Addiction to gambling can destroy families and finances. She overcame her addiction to alcohol through years of therapy. Addiction is a medical condition that requires professional treatment. Social media addiction is a growing concern among teenagers. The government launched a campaign against drug addiction.

english_meaning: The process of adding something to something else. A person or thing added to an existing group. The mathematical operation of combining numbers to find their sum. An extra part built onto a building. An increase resulting from being added.
example_sentence: The new player is a valuable addition to the team. Children learn addition in their early classes. They built an addition to their house last summer. In addition to English, she speaks three other languages.

english_meaning: A substance added to something in small amounts to improve or preserve it. Any ingredient introduced to a product to enhance its quality, flavor, texture, or shelf life. Something that adds to or increases a total when combined. A chemical or natural substance mixed into food, fuel, or materials for a specific purpose. Relating to or characterized by the process of addition rather than subtraction.
example_sentence: Food additives are used to extend the shelf life of products. The paint additive improved its resistance to moisture. Artificial additives in processed food can be harmful to health. The chemical additive enhanced the concrete's strength. She preferred to buy food products with no artificial additives.

english_meaning: To bring forward facts, evidence, examples, or arguments in support of a claim or position. To cite or refer to specific information to prove or support a point. To present concrete evidence during a debate, trial, or argument. To offer logical or factual support for an assertion or theory. To introduce relevant data or examples as evidence during a discussion or legal proceeding.
example_sentence: The lawyer adduced several pieces of evidence during the trial. She adduced historical examples to support her argument. He adduced statistics to prove the effectiveness of the program. The scientist adduced data from three separate studies. The teacher asked students to adduce reasons for their opinions.

english_meaning: Highly skilled or very good at something. A person who has strong ability, practice, or expertise in a particular activity, task, or field. Someone who performs an action with great competence and confidence.
example_sentence: She is adept at solving complex problems quickly. The teacher is adept in explaining difficult ideas in simple words. He became adept at using computer software after years of practice. The diplomat was adept at handling sensitive negotiations.

english_meaning: Enough for a particular purpose or need. Something that is sufficient, acceptable, or satisfactory in quantity, quality, or ability to meet a requirement
example_sentence: The food supply was adequate for the entire group. She has adequate knowledge of computer programming. The hospital does not have adequate medical equipment. His explanation was adequate but not very detailed.

english_meaning: To physically stick to a surface. To follow closely, maintain loyalty, or support a rule, belief, or agreement. To be consistent with something, such as rules, plans, or standards. To hold together physically or figuratively.
example_sentence: The stamp will adhere to the envelope if moistened. She adheres to a strict diet every day. All employees must adhere to the company’s code of conduct. The new paint will adhere better after cleaning the wall.

english_meaning: The act of following or sticking to a rule, plan, or belief. The faithful observance or support of a law, rule, guideline, belief, or commitment. It implies consistency and dedication in maintaining certain standards or practices.
example_sentence: Her strict adherence to the schedule impressed her colleagues. Patients showed better recovery with adherence to the prescribed medication. The company promotes adherence to ethical business practices. Teachers emphasize adherence to classroom rules.

english_meaning: A person who follows, supports, or believes strongly in a particular idea, organization, religion, or leader. Sticking firmly to a surface or closely attached. Also loyal or devoted.
example_sentence: She is an adherent of traditional education methods. Many adherents attended the leader's speech. The label remained adherent to the bottle. He remained adherent to his principles throughout his life.

english_meaning: The quality of sticking firmly. Strong support or loyalty to an idea, group, or policy. Abnormal band of tissue that forms between organs after injury or surgery. Attraction between different substances that causes them to stick together
example_sentence: The strong adhesion between the tape and the wall kept the poster in place. Scientists studied the adhesion of water molecules to glass. After surgery, the patient developed internal adhesions that caused pain. His adhesion to the organization remained strong for many years.

english_meaning: A substance used to join two surfaces together by sticking them. Something that sticks firmly to a surface.  It can be glue, paste, resin, cement, or other bonding material used in household, medical, or industrial work.
example_sentence: The carpenter used a strong adhesive to fix the wooden pieces. This tape has a powerful adhesive on one side. Doctors used a medical adhesive to close the small wound. The label fell off because the adhesive was weak.

english_meaning: Goodbye, especially a formal, emotional, or final farewell. An expression used when parting.
example_sentence: She bid adieu to her friends before boarding the plane. With a heavy heart, he said his final adieu to the old house. They exchanged a tearful adieu at the train station. He waved adieu as the ship slowly left the harbor.

english_meaning: Relating to, consisting of, or containing animal fat. Fatty connective tissue that stores energy, insulates the body, and cushions organs.
example_sentence: Adipose tissue helps insulate the body and store energy for later use. The scan showed excess adipose tissue around the abdomen. Researchers studied how adipose cells respond to insulin. The fish has a small adipose fin near its tail.

english_meaning: A type of connective tissue in the body that stores energy in the form of fat. The layer of fatty tissue found under the skin and around internal organs. Body tissue that provides insulation, cushioning, and protection for organs. A tissue that also acts as an endocrine organ by releasing certain hormones.
example_sentence: Adipose tissue stores extra energy as fat. A layer of adipose tissue keeps the body warm in cold weather. Excess adipose tissue around the waist increases health risks. Adipose tissue also cushions the kidneys and other organs.

english_meaning: Next to or adjoining something else. Directly beside or very close in position. Sharing a common border or side. Near without necessarily touching.
example_sentence: Their house is adjacent to the park. She sat in the chair adjacent to mine. The two fields lie adjacent to each other. His office is adjacent to the reception.

english_meaning: To be next to and joined with something. To share a common boundary or wall with another place. To attach or add one thing to another. To lie side by side and touch.
example_sentence: Our garden adjoins the neighbour's field. The kitchen adjoins the dining room. Two small offices adjoin the main hall. Their land adjoins the river on the eastern side.

english_meaning: To stop a meeting, discussion, or activity for a time, usually to continue later. To officially stop a meeting, court session, assembly, discussion, or activity for a period of time, with the idea that it may continue later or on another day. It can also mean to move to another place after a formal activity.
example_sentence: The judge decided to adjourn the hearing until Monday. We will adjourn the meeting for lunch and continue at 2 pm. The chairman adjourned the session after all agenda items were discussed. After the conference, the members adjourned to the dining hall for tea.

english_meaning: To make an official judgment or ruling in a legal case or dispute. To act as a judge or arbitrator and settle a conflict through formal legal process. To decide between competing claims or parties in a fair and authoritative manner. To preside over a competition or contest and declare a winner. To resolve a disagreement through a recognized official process.
example_sentence: The panel was asked to adjudicate the dispute between the two companies. A senior judge was appointed to adjudicate the complex case. He was asked to adjudicate the annual poetry competition. The arbiter will adjudicate the contract disagreement next week. The international court agreed to adjudicate the territorial dispute.

english_meaning: The formal legal process of resolving a dispute or reaching a decision through a judge or arbitrator. An official ruling or judgment issued to settle a conflict between two parties. The act of hearing and deciding a case in a court of law or administrative tribunal. The outcome or verdict of a formal judicial or arbitration process. A binding decision made by an authorized authority after a review of evidence and arguments.
example_sentence: The adjudication of the case took several months to complete. Both parties agreed to submit to formal adjudication. The adjudication resulted in a settlement favorable to the plaintiff. The dispute went through a formal adjudication process. The committee's adjudication was final and binding on both parties.

english_meaning: A thing added to something else as a supplementary rather than an essential part. A person associated with an organisation in an auxiliary capacity. Something joined or added to another thing but not an essential part of it.
example_sentence: Exercise is a useful adjunct to a healthy diet. She works as an adjunct professor at the university. The new software is an adjunct to the main system. Good sleep is an important adjunct to recovery.

english_meaning: To manage, direct, or oversee the affairs of an organization, department, or institution. To carry out administrative duties such as organizing, planning, and controlling resources. To govern or run a system, program, or office efficiently. To apply or enforce laws, policies, or procedures within an organization. To supervise and coordinate the activities of a staff or group to achieve goals.
example_sentence: She was appointed to administrate the regional education department. The manager's job is to administrate daily operations efficiently. It takes skill and experience to properly administrate a large hospital. He was asked to administrate the distribution of relief funds. The council was restructured to better administrate the city's services.

english_meaning: Relating to the management or operation of an organization. Connected with office duties, rules, records, or official procedures.
example_sentence: She handles administrative tasks. The administrative office is on the second floor. New administrative rules were announced. The project needs administrative approval.

english_meaning: In a way related to management, official procedures, or organizational control. From an administrative point of view. By official office action.
example_sentence: The departments were administratively combined. Administratively, the change is simple. The case was closed administratively. The school is administratively responsible for the program.

english_meaning: A person who manages an organization, office, system, or program. Someone responsible for rules, records, and operations. A person who administers an estate or official process.
example_sentence: The school administrator answered parents' questions. A system administrator fixed the server. The court appointed an administrator for the estate. Good administrators keep records clear.

english_meaning: Deserving respect, approval, and praise. Worthy of being admired for good qualities or achievements. Excellent or of very high quality.
example_sentence: Her honesty is truly admirable. He showed admirable courage during the crisis. The teacher did an admirable job with the students. Their patience under pressure was admirable.

english_meaning: In a way that deserves admiration or respect. In an excellent or praiseworthy manner. To a degree that inspires approval and respect. In a manner showing skill, courage, or good qualities. Very well; commendably.
example_sentence: She handled the difficult situation admirably. The team performed admirably under great pressure. He behaved admirably despite the harsh criticism. The new teacher managed her class admirably.

english_meaning: A senior naval officer of very high rank. An officer who commands a fleet of warships. A high-ranking commander responsible for major naval operations. A title or rank used for senior officers in a navy. In some countries, "Admiral" is one of the highest ranks in the naval forces.
example_sentence: The admiral inspected the fleet. She became the first female admiral in the navy. The admiral ordered the ships to return. A red admiral butterfly landed on the flower.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of respect, appreciation, and warm approval for someone or something. A sense of wonder and pleasure felt toward someone who is considered excellent or impressive. Respectful appreciation for qualities such as courage, talent, beauty, or achievement. A positive emotional response triggered by the perceived superiority or excellence of a person or object. An attitude of high regard and esteem directed toward an admired individual or thing.
example_sentence: She looked at the painting with genuine admiration. His admiration for her dedication was evident in everything he said. The crowd expressed their admiration with thunderous applause. He earned the admiration of his colleagues through hard work. Her admiration for the natural world inspired her career in ecology.

english_meaning: To regard with respect, warm approval, or pleasure. To look at something with pleasure or appreciation. To have a high opinion of someone or something.
example_sentence: I really admire her dedication to work. Tourists stopped to admire the beautiful view. He admired his father more than anyone else. She admired the painting for a long time.

english_meaning: A person who greatly respects or approves of someone or something. A person who is romantically attracted to another. A follower or supporter of a person's work or achievements.
example_sentence: He has always been a great admirer of her poetry. She received flowers from a secret admirer. The painter had many admirers across Europe. As an admirer of his work, I attended every lecture.

english_meaning: To confess or acknowledge that something is true, often reluctantly. To allow someone to enter a place. To accept someone into an institution, school, or organisation. To take a patient into hospital for treatment. To have room for something.
example_sentence: He admitted that he had made a serious mistake. Only ticket holders will be admitted to the hall. She was admitted to the university on merit. The patient was admitted to hospital late last night.

english_meaning: To mix or blend one substance with another. To combine ingredients or elements together.
example_sentence: The pharmacist admixed two liquids to prepare the medicine. Please admix the powder with warm water. The chef admixed spices into the sauce. Small amounts of colour were admixed with the paint.

english_meaning: To warn or gently correct someone about their behavior. To reprimand mildly. To advise seriously. To caution against danger or mistake. To urge someone to act responsibly.
example_sentence: The teacher admonished the student for talking during the lecture. He was admonished to be careful while driving. The manager admonished the staff to follow company rules. She gently admonished her child for being rude.

english_meaning: A firm warning, scolding, or piece of advice given to correct a person's behaviour. A gentle but serious reproof. A caution against doing something wrong or dangerous. Counsel intended to remind someone of their duty. Mild rebuke combined with guidance for improvement.
example_sentence: The teacher's admonition helped the student to improve his behaviour. He ignored his father's admonition and faced serious trouble. The judge delivered a stern admonition to the young offender. Her gentle admonition was enough to stop the children from quarrelling. The book is full of moral admonitions for young readers.

english_meaning: Making a big issue out of something unimportant. Unnecessary trouble, fuss, delay, or excessive activity about something simple. It is often used to criticize overreaction or pointless effort.
example_sentence: There is no need to make so much ado about a small mistake. He finished the task without any ado. Why all this ado over a simple meeting. She accepted the offer without ado.

english_meaning: A type of building material made from sun-dried earth and straw, also a type of house made from this material. A natural building material, often in the form of bricks, made from a mixture of earth, water, and organic materials like straw. An adobe house is typically thick-walled, providing insulation against heat and cold. The software company Adobe known for Photoshop, Acrobat, and other creative tools.
example_sentence: The floors were bare adobe and the walls painted blue. Adobe houses were common in the Southwest. No adobe, just white columns and wrap-around porches. The one-story adobe structure was built in 1905 to house miners. After a while they make adobe bricks and build their houses by stages, one room followed by another.

english_meaning: The time in a person’s life when they develop from a child into an adult. The transitional period of physical and psychological development between childhood and maturity. The time period between the beginning of puberty and adulthood.
example_sentence: Adolescence brings about major changes in a young person’s body. He had survived a difficult adolescence. During adolescence, the body and mind go through many complex changes, some of which are difficult to deal with.

english_meaning: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult. Between the ages of a child and an adult. A juvenile between the onset of puberty and maturity. Being of the age 13 through 19.
example_sentence: Adolescents between the ages of 13 and 18 and the problems they face. Stop acting like an adolescent!. I'm looking after six adolescents for a week. She doesn't understand the emotional problems of adolescents. The two adolescent boys made their mother very tired.

english_meaning: An extremely handsome young man. A man whose physical beauty attracts admiration. In Greek mythology, a beautiful youth loved by the goddess Aphrodite. A symbol of male beauty and youthful charm. Sometimes used humorously for a man who is overly proud of his looks.
example_sentence: He looked like an Adonis in his wedding photographs. The actor is regarded as the Adonis of the film industry. She admired the young Adonis sitting in the cafe. The painting depicts Adonis surrounded by goddesses. Not every handsome man can be called an Adonis.

english_meaning: To legally take another person's child and raise it as one's own. To take up, embrace, or begin using a new idea, method, habit, or practice. To accept or follow a particular approach, attitude, or lifestyle. To formally approve and put into effect a plan, law, or policy. To take on the identity, name, or characteristic of another. To choose and follow a particular course of action or way of living.
example_sentence: The couple decided to adopt a child from an orphanage. Many countries have adopted new environmental policies this year. She adopted a healthier lifestyle after her diagnosis. The school adopted a new reading curriculum for all grades. He adopted a more patient approach when dealing with difficult clients.

english_meaning: Legally taken into a family as one's own child. Chosen and put into use, as a method, policy, or idea. Formally accepted or approved by vote. Taken as one's own although not native or original, such as an adopted homeland.
example_sentence: Their adopted son is now a doctor. The committee reviewed the newly adopted rules. The resolution was adopted by a large majority. She speaks proudly of her adopted city.

english_meaning: A person, especially a child, who has been legally adopted by another family. Someone taken into a family through the legal process of adoption. An adopted child or adult in relation to their adoptive parents. Sometimes used for an animal taken from a shelter.
example_sentence: The adoptee later searched for her birth family. Many adoptees describe similar feelings of curiosity. The agency offers counselling for adoptees. As an adoptee, he grew up in two cultures.

english_meaning: A person who legally takes another person's child into their family as their own. A person or organization that begins to use a new product, idea, or technology. Someone who accepts and follows a new method or practice. A person who takes in an animal from a shelter to care for it.
example_sentence: The adopters were interviewed carefully by the agency. Early adopters of the app gave useful feedback. Many adopters of the new software reported better results. The shelter thanked the adopters of the rescued puppies.

english_meaning: The legal act of taking another person's child into one's own family as one's own. The act of choosing and starting to use a new method, idea, or policy. Formal acceptance or approval of a proposal, law, or report. The process of taking in and caring for an animal from a shelter.
example_sentence: They completed the adoption after a long legal process. The adoption of the new policy improved efficiency. Adoption of the report was approved unanimously. Pet adoption has become popular in the city.

english_meaning: Relating to a family relationship created by adoption rather than by birth. Describing a parent or family that has legally adopted a child. Chosen or taken as one's own, though not originally belonging to one. Relating to a country or place that someone has made their home.
example_sentence: His adoptive parents raised him with great love. She met her adoptive family for the first time last year. He always speaks warmly about his adoptive country. Adoptive families receive support from the agency.

english_meaning: Deep love, admiration, worship, or respect for someone or something. An intense feeling of love, admiration, devotion, or respect toward a person, deity, object, or idea. It can describe both religious worship and strong personal affection.
example_sentence: The child looked at his mother with complete adoration. Fans showed their adoration for the singer by cheering loudly. She spoke about her grandfather with great adoration and respect. The temple was filled with people offering prayers in adoration.

english_meaning: To love, admire, or like someone or something very much. To love someone deeply, admire them greatly, or be extremely fond of something. It can also mean to worship or revere someone or something with great respect and devotion.
example_sentence: She adores her grandmother and visits her every weekend. Many children adore animals and enjoy spending time with them. I absolutely adore classical music because it helps me relax. The fans adore the singer for his talent and kindness.

english_meaning: A person who loves, admires, worships, or is devoted to someone or something. A person who has deep love, admiration, affection, respect, or devotion for someone, something, or a deity. The word is often used for a devoted admirer, fan, lover, or worshipper.
example_sentence: She was an adorer of classical music and attended every concert she could. The actor was surrounded by admirers, but one loyal adorer had followed his career for decades. He remained an adorer of nature throughout his life. As an adorer of the poet's work, she collected all of his books.

english_meaning: To make something more beautiful or attractive by adding decorations. To enhance the appearance of someone or something by adding ornaments, accessories, or decorative elements. It often implies adding beauty, elegance, or charm to an object, place, or person.
example_sentence: The walls were adorned with paintings. She adorned her room with fresh flowers. The bride adorned herself with gold jewelry. The walls were adorned with beautiful paintings. The festival adorned the city with colorful lights. He adorned his speech with clever anecdotes.

english_meaning: One of a pair of small glands sitting on top of each kidney. A gland that produces adrenaline and prepares the body for stress. An endocrine gland that secretes cortisol and aldosterone. A gland consisting of an outer cortex and an inner medulla.
example_sentence: The adrenal gland releases adrenaline when we are frightened. Cortisol from the adrenal gland helps the body handle stress. A tumour on the adrenal gland can raise blood pressure. Each adrenal gland sits like a cap on top of a kidney.

english_meaning: Floating without being fastened or steered, especially on water. Without purpose, guidance, or direction in life. Loose from a fastening or moorings.
example_sentence: The small boat was left adrift in the ocean. After losing his job he felt completely adrift. The ship broke free and drifted adrift in the storm. Without her mentor she was adrift in the new city.

english_meaning: Clever and skilful, especially in handling difficult situations. Skilled. Dexterous. Expert. Quick and able in thought or action. Showing great ability in using the hands or the mind. Used for people who manage tasks, problems, or challenges with intelligence and ease.
example_sentence: She is an adroit negotiator who always finds a fair solution. The politician gave an adroit reply to the journalist's tough question. He is adroit at handling complex business deals. The surgeon's adroit hands saved the patient's life. With adroit footwork, the player dribbled past two defenders.

english_meaning: To praise someone excessively or in a way that is not sincere. To flatter greatly. To admire and worship beyond what is reasonable. To show extreme devotion. Used when a person gives exaggerated compliments or attention, often to win favour or out of blind admiration.
example_sentence: The courtiers used to adulate the king to gain his favour. Fans often adulate their favourite movie stars without knowing them personally. He hates people who adulate him just to get promotions. The media tends to adulate successful businessmen and politicians. It is unwise to adulate someone simply because of their wealth.

english_meaning: Excessive admiration or praise. Flattery. Worshipful attention. Extreme respect or devotion shown to a person. The act of praising someone too much, often insincerely. Used to describe the kind of attention given to celebrities, leaders, or heroes by their admirers or followers.
example_sentence: The young actor received great adulation after his first successful film. The leader's adulation by the crowd made him feel proud. She tries to avoid the constant adulation of her fans. The book describes how power and adulation changed the king's personality. Excessive adulation can sometimes spoil even a humble person.

english_meaning: A fully grown and developed person, animal, or plant. Having reached the age of maturity as defined by law. Suitable for or characteristic of mature people. Emotionally and mentally mature.
example_sentence: Only adults are allowed to enter this section. She handled the situation in a very adult manner. An adult ticket costs twice the price of a child's. The film is intended for an adult audience.

english_meaning: To make something impure by adding inferior or harmful substances. To contaminate or pollute something. To weaken purity or strength. To mix something with inferior material. To corrupt morally or physically. To reduce the quality or purity of something by mixing it with another substance, often something cheaper, harmful, or unnecessary. It is commonly used for food, drinks, medicines, or products.
example_sentence: Some traders adulterate milk by adding water. The spices were adulterated with cheap fillers. Adulterated food can harm human health. Unscrupulous companies sometimes adulterate medicines to reduce costs.

english_meaning: The act of making something impure by adding harmful or inferior substances. Contamination of food or products. Reduction in purity or quality. Mixing of inferior materials. Corruption or degradation of something pure.
example_sentence: The adulteration of milk with water is a common problem in some areas. The government has strict laws against food adulteration. Adulteration of medicines can be dangerous for human health. The shopkeeper was fined for adulteration of spices.

english_meaning: Sex between a married person and somebody who is not their husband or wife. Voluntary sexual intercourse between a married person and someone other than that person's current spouse or partner. Extramarital sex that willfully and maliciously interferes with marriage relations.
example_sentence: He was accused of committing adultery. She is going to divorce him on the grounds of adultery. Many people in public life have committed adultery. Adultery is often cited as grounds for divorce. He found out that his wife had committed adultery. She accused her husband of adultery.

english_meaning: The state or period of being fully grown and legally considered an adult. The stage in human development that follows adolescence, typically from age eighteen onward. The phase of life marked by full physical, emotional, and intellectual maturity. The time in life when a person is responsible for their own decisions and actions. A life stage associated with independence, work, family, and civic responsibility.
example_sentence: Adulthood brings both freedom and a sense of responsibility. The transition to adulthood can be both exciting and challenging. She entered adulthood with great ambitions and determination. Legal adulthood in most countries begins at eighteen years of age. He looked back fondly on childhood, knowing adulthood brought its own burdens.

english_meaning: The process of moving forward or making progress. Promotion to a higher position, rank, or level in a job. Development or improvement in knowledge, science, or technology. The act of helping something to grow or succeed. Payment of money before it is due.
example_sentence: There are good opportunities for advancement in this company. The advancement of medical science has saved countless lives. She was rewarded with rapid advancement in her career. The charity works for the advancement of women's education.

english_meaning: Coming from an external or accidental source rather than from a natural or inherent origin. Occurring unexpectedly or in an unusual position; not naturally belonging to the place. Added or appearing accidentally rather than as part of the original design. In biology, growing from an unusual or unexpected part of a plant. Not arising from a regular cause but rather from outside circumstances.
example_sentence: The plant developed adventitious roots along its stem. The discovery of the treasure was entirely adventitious. Adventitious shoots grew from the base of the old tree. The success of the campaign was partly adventitious and partly planned. He acknowledged that much of his fame had been adventitious.

english_meaning: An unusual and exciting, typically hazardous, experience or activity. The engaging in hazardous and exciting activity, especially the exploration of unknown territory. A commercial speculation, often one involving considerable risk. To engage in daring or hazardous activity. To put one's money or life at risk in a daring enterprise.
example_sentence: She traveled across the world in search of a great adventure. The hikers set off on an exciting adventure through the dense Amazon rainforest. He decided to adventure into the unknown territories of the deep ocean. Their latest business adventure proved to be highly profitable despite the initial risks.

english_meaning: A willingness to take risks in business or politics. The tendency to engage in reckless or hazardous activities, often for personal or political gain. Reckless military or political intervention in the affairs of another country. Behavior that values daring and taking chances over careful planning and safety.
example_sentence: The nation's military adventurism led to a devastating and prolonged war. Critics accused the CEO of corporate adventurism that endangered the company's future. Political adventurism often results in unforeseen and disastrous consequences. He warned against the dangers of adventurism in foreign policy decisions.

english_meaning: An opponent or enemy in a conflict or competition. A person or group that opposes or attacks. Someone who actively resists or fights against another. A rival or antagonist.
example_sentence: He defeated his adversary in the debate. The two nations were long-time adversaries. She faced a formidable adversary in court. The chess player studied his adversary's strategy.

english_meaning: Negative & unpleasant, Not likely to produce a good result. Opposed to one's interests. Acting against or in a contrary direction
example_sentence: The drug is known to have adverse side affects. Lack of money will have adverse affect on research program.

english_meaning: In a way that prevents success or development. In an unfavorable or harmful manner. In a way that is contrary to one's interests or welfare. Positioned in a direction that is opposite or hostile. Acting in a manner that results in a negative outcome.
example_sentence: The high interest rates affected the small business adversely. His health was adversely impacted by the stressful environment. The crops were adversely affected by the sudden heavy frost. New regulations might adversely change the company's profit margins.

english_meaning: A condition of difficult or challenging circumstances that test one's strength and resolve. Misfortune, hardship, or trouble experienced over a period of time. A state of distress, suffering, or unfavorable conditions. Difficult experiences that shape character and build resilience. The opposite of prosperity; a period marked by struggle, loss, or hardship.
example_sentence: She grew stronger through every moment of adversity she faced. True character is revealed in times of adversity. The nation stood united in the face of great adversity. He learned to remain hopeful despite years of adversity. Adversity, when faced bravely, can be a powerful teacher.

english_meaning: A published statement informing the public of a matter of general interest. To turn the mind or attention. To call attention in the course of speaking or writing.
example_sentence: The speaker adverted to the recent changes in policy during his speech. She briefly adverted to her childhood experiences in her memoir. The report adverts to the risks involved in the project. He did not advert to the financial difficulties facing the company.

english_meaning: A state of being aware. The process of being heedful. The quality of being advertent, heedfulness, regard, consideration. The act of adverting, of the quality of being advertent, attention, notice, regard, heedfulness
example_sentence: A history textbook that has been widely criticized for its lack of advertency to the contributions of minorities.

english_meaning: Paying careful attention, mindful. A person who is attentive, watchful, and consciously aware of what is happening around them. It refers to being mentally alert and carefully noticing details.
example_sentence: Marcia listened to everything I said with an advertent expression on her face. Damages may be payable if there is advertent wrongdoing. Reside said the firms have pledged to institute measures intended to prevent the advertent trade with Iran

english_meaning: In a careful deliberate manner. Formed as the antonym of inadvertently, intentionally, on purpose, purposely.
example_sentence: He advertently avoided mentioning her mistake. She advertently read the instructions before starting the experiment. The manager advertently listened to every employee’s concern. He advertently chose words that would not hurt anyone.

english_meaning: To promote a product, service, event, job, or business publicly in order to attract customers, applicants, or attention. To announce or make a fact, need, or opportunity publicly known. To describe or present something as having particular qualities. To reveal or draw attention to something, sometimes unintentionally.
example_sentence: The company plans to advertise its new service online. They advertised the vacant position in two newspapers. The hotel is advertised as a peaceful family retreat. He avoided wearing expensive jewelry because he did not want to advertise his wealth.

english_meaning: A public notice, message, image, video, or announcement that promotes a product, service, event, job, or idea. Paid material placed in print, broadcast, outdoor, or digital media to attract attention or encourage action. A person or thing that demonstrates the value or quality of something. The act or practice of making something publicly known.
example_sentence: The company released a television advertisement for its new phone. She found the vacancy through an online advertisement. The colorful advertisement attracted many customers. His excellent work is a good advertisement for the training program.

english_meaning: Public support or recommendation for a cause or policy. If refers to actively supporting, promoting, or arguing in favor of a cause, idea, policy, or group. It often involves raising awareness, influencing decisions, and working toward positive change in society, law, or community.
example_sentence: She is known for her advocacy of women's rights. The organization focuses on environmental advocacy. His advocacy helped bring changes in the law. Advocacy for education is essential in developing countries.

english_meaning: A person who publicly supports or recommends a particular cause or policy. A lawyer who pleads a case in a court of law. To speak or write in favour of something. Someone who speaks on behalf of another person or group.
example_sentence: She is a lifelong advocate of children's rights. The advocate presented the case clearly before the judge. Many doctors advocate regular exercise and a balanced diet. He advocated for cleaner public transport in the city.

english_meaning: Protection or support. Guidance, sponsorship, or backing provided by someone or an organization, often in a formal or authoritative way. It originally refers to the shield of Zeus in Greek mythology, symbolizing powerful protection.
example_sentence: The new environmental project was launched under the aegis of the UN. The conference was held under the aegis of the Ministry of Education. The charity operates under the aegis of a local community group. The museum exhibition was organized under the aegis of a famous historian.

english_meaning: Relating to, involving, or requiring oxygen. Something that requires oxygen for its process or activity. Commonly used in biology for organisms that need oxygen and in exercise for activities that increase heart and lung efficiency.
example_sentence: Running and swimming are aerobic exercises. Aerobic bacteria need oxygen to survive. Cycling is an effective aerobic activity. She joined an aerobic dance class to improve her stamina.

english_meaning: Fear of flying or air travel. An intense and persistent fear of flying in airplanes or being in the air. People with this fear may feel anxiety, panic, sweating, or rapid heartbeat when thinking about or experiencing air travel. It can limit travel and affect personal or professional life.
antonyms: ["Confidence in flying","Fearlessness of air travel","Love of flying"]
example_sentence: Because of aerophobia, she prefers traveling by train instead of flying. His aerophobia began after experiencing strong turbulence on a flight. Therapy helped him manage his aerophobia and travel abroad. Aerophobia can cause panic even before reaching the airport.

english_meaning: A person who has or affects to have a special appreciation of art and beauty. One who cultivates a high sensitivity to aesthetic pleasures. An individual who prioritizes artistic appearance and sensory experiences above practical considerations. A follower of the aesthetic movement in art and literature. A connoisseur who is deeply responsive to the sublime and beautiful.
example_sentence: As a true aesthete, he could spend hours contemplating a single painting in the gallery. The interior designer was an aesthete who refused to use any furniture that was not visually perfect. She lived her life as an aesthete, surrounding herself with classical music and rare orchids. Critics often dismissed him as a mere aesthete who cared more for style than for substance.

english_meaning: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty. Relating to the perception of beauty or artistic taste. It can describe objects, experiences, or styles that are visually or sensorially pleasing. In philosophy, it also refers to the study of art and beauty.
example_sentence: The new building has a very modern aesthetic that appeals to young professionals. She has an aesthetic sense that helps her design beautiful interiors. The painting’s aesthetic value is recognized worldwide. Minimalist aesthetics are popular in contemporary architecture.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to beauty or the appreciation of beauty. From a visual or artistic point of view. In a manner that is pleasing to the senses, especially the sight. Concerning the principles of good taste and artistic expression. With regard to aesthetic principles rather than functional or practical ones.
example_sentence: The building is aesthetically pleasing but lacks functional space. The software was redesigned to be more aesthetically modern. She arranged the flowers aesthetically in a tall crystal vase. The film was praised for being aesthetically stunning despite a weak plot.

english_meaning: The approach to art and culture that emphasizes beauty and visual appearance over moral, social, or practical narratives. A 19th-century intellectual movement in Britain that advocated 'art for art's sake' and the pursuit of refined taste. The quality or state of being aesthetic or having a high appreciation for beauty. The doctrine that aesthetic value is the primary standard for judging artistic or literary worth. A style or philosophy characterized by intense devotion to beauty in nature and the arts.
example_sentence: The artist's devotion to aestheticism meant he ignored the political implications of his work. Victorian aestheticism was often criticized for being superficial and detached from reality. Her home decor is a perfect reflection of modern aestheticism and minimalist design. The principles of aestheticism suggest that beauty alone justifies the existence of a masterpiece.

english_meaning: Related to summer or occurring in summer. Belonging to summer climate. Happening or appearing in warm season. Adapted to hot weather conditions.
example_sentence: Many animals show aestival behavior by becoming more active in summer. The region experiences heavy aestival rainfall every year. Farmers prepare for aestival crops as the temperature rises. Certain flowers bloom only during the aestival season.

english_meaning: To spend the hot or dry summer season in a dormant or inactive state. To remain in a prolonged sleep or torpor during periods of extreme heat or drought. The summer equivalent of hibernation observed in certain animals and insects. To conserve energy and moisture by entering an inactive state during dry seasons. A biological survival mechanism used by certain organisms to withstand harsh summer conditions.
example_sentence: Lungfish aestivate during dry seasons by burrowing into the mud. Some snails aestivate during summer to conserve moisture. The snail aestivated for weeks until the rain returned. Certain insects aestivate when temperatures rise too high. The tortoise aestivated in a cool burrow during the hot summer months.

english_meaning: At a great distance. From a distance. Far away in space. Emotionally distant in some contexts. Something located or happening at a long distance in space or time. It is often used in literary or formal contexts to describe physical distance or emotional separation.
example_sentence: She watched the mountains from afar. The sound of music came from afar. He admired her talent from afar without speaking to her. The village looked beautiful from afar.

english_meaning: The quality of being friendly, polite, and easy to talk to. Warmth in manner. Pleasantness. Approachability. Good-natured behaviour towards others. The trait of being kind, courteous, and welcoming, which makes other people feel comfortable in one's company.
example_sentence: His affability made him popular among colleagues and friends. The manager's affability put new employees at ease immediately. She is known for her natural affability and warm smile. The teacher's affability encouraged shy students to participate. People often praise his affability and willingness to help others.

english_meaning: Friendly, approachable, and easy to talk to in all social situations. Showing warmth, kindness, and a willingness to engage pleasantly with others. Characterized by a pleasant manner and an open, welcoming attitude. Easy to get along with; sociable, courteous, and cheerful in interactions. Displaying good-natured ease and charm in speaking and dealing with others.
example_sentence: The affable teacher made every student feel welcome. She was naturally affable and could befriend anyone easily. His affable nature made him very popular in the office. The hotel manager greeted every guest in an affable manner. Despite being famous, she remained genuinely affable and humble.

english_meaning: A feeling of love, fondness, care, or warmth toward someone or something. A gentle and positive feeling of love, care, fondness, or attachment toward a person, animal, place, or thing. It is usually expressed through kindness, concern, warmth, and emotional closeness.
example_sentence: She showed great affection for her younger brother. The dog followed its owner with affection and loyalty. Children need affection and support from their parents. He spoke about his hometown with deep affection.

english_meaning: Showing love, care, and warmth toward someone. A person or behavior that shows fondness, tenderness, and emotional warmth. It is used for someone who openly expresses love, care, or gentle feelings toward others, such as family members, friends, or pets.
example_sentence: She is very affectionate toward her younger brother. The dog became more affectionate after being adopted. He wrote an affectionate letter to his mother. They shared an affectionate hug after a long time apart.

english_meaning: In a way that shows love, care, warmth, or fond feelings toward someone. An action done with emotional warmth, tenderness, or deep liking.
