It is often used when someone speaks, looks at, or treats another person in a loving or caring manner. It shows positive emotional attachment, such as between family members, close friends, or loved ones.
example_sentence: She smiled affectionately at her little brother. He spoke affectionately about his childhood memories. The teacher looked affectionately at her students after their success. The old couple held hands and looked affectionately at each other.

english_meaning: Affectionateness means the quality of being warm, loving, and showing care or tenderness toward others.  A personality trait or behavior where a person naturally expresses love, care, emotional warmth, and gentle feelings toward family, friends, children, or even animals. It reflects kindness in actions, soft behavior in relationships, and emotional closeness.
example_sentence: Her affectionateness toward children makes her a great teacher. The dog showed great affectionateness to its owner. His affectionateness was visible in the way he cared for his parents. Affectionateness in a family creates a strong emotional bond.

english_meaning: To promise formally to marry someone. To engage or betroth a person in marriage. To pledge one's faith or trust to another. A formal promise of marriage or a pledge of trust.
example_sentence: He was affianced to his cousin at a young age. The families affianced their children in a small ceremony. She wore the ring given to her by her affianced husband. Their affiance was announced in the local newspaper.

english_meaning: Close relationship between two people or things having similar qualities, structures, features. A natural liking, connection, or similarity between people or things.  It can describe shared interests, strong bonds, or structural resemblance. It is also used in science to describe a natural relationship between substances.
example_sentence: There is close affinity between Italian & Spanish. She has a strong affinity for classical music. There is a natural affinity between the two friends. His affinity with nature is reflected in his paintings. Certain chemicals show a strong affinity for water.

english_meaning: To attach or fasten one thing to another. To add a signature, stamp, or seal to a document. A letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word. In grammar, a prefix or suffix that changes a word's meaning.
example_sentence: Please affix a recent photograph to the form. He affixed his signature at the bottom of the page. The prefix 'un' is a common affix in English. Students learned how affixes change word meanings.

english_meaning:
To cause pain, suffering, or distress to someone. To cause suffering or trouble. 
To distress or burden someone with pain, disease, or hardship. To make someone suffer physically, mentally, or emotionally. It is often used for illness, problems, disasters, or difficult situations that trouble people over a period of time.
example_sentence: The disease afflicts an estimated two million people every year. The village was afflicted by a severe drought. She was afflicted with a rare disease. Poverty continues to afflict many families. He was deeply afflicted by the loss of his friend.

english_meaning:
A condition of pain, suffering, or distress. A cause of pain or suffering
A serious illness or disorder. Emotional hardship or sorrow. A burden that troubles someone for a long time. Something that causes continuous pain, suffering, or trouble. It may be physical, emotional, or mental. It is often used for illness, hardship, or a serious problem that affects a person deeply.
example_sentence: The disease was a terrible affliction that affected the entire village. Poverty remains a major affliction in many parts of the world. She faced her affliction with courage and patience. His hearing loss was an affliction he learned to live with.

english_meaning: Wealth, abundance of money, possessions, or resources. The state of having a large amount of money, property, or other material goods. A condition of prosperity and plentiful resources. Often used to describe individuals, families, or nations enjoying high economic status.
example_sentence: The 1950s were an age of affluence in America. Her affluence allowed her to travel around the world in luxury. The region’s affluence comes from its rich natural resources. He displayed his affluence through his large mansion and expensive cars. Despite his affluence, he lived a modest life.

english_meaning: Having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value. Having a lot of money and a good standard of living. A branch that flows into the main stream. Somebody who is wealthy. A stream or river flowing into a larger river or into a lake, a tributary stream.
example_sentence:
We live in an affluent neighborhood. The store will benefit from its base of affluent customers to whom various other products will be sold in due course.
Some have argued that ethical food is a sign of an affluent society with a lot of time.

english_meaning: In a financially successful and comfortable way. In a manner that reflects abundance of money or resources. With the benefits of high social and economic status. In a style associated with luxury and ease. In a way that shows economic security and independence.
example_sentence: They lived affluently in a large house by the sea. She was raised affluently and attended the best schools. The family dined affluently at five star restaurants. He invested wisely and now lives affluently in retirement.

english_meaning: An action or remark that causes outrage or offense. To intentionally insult, offend, or disrespect someone, especially in an open or public manner. It refers to a deliberate act, statement, or behavior that hurts someone's pride, modesty, or dignity. To face in defiance or confront with an intentional insult.
example_sentence: His careless speech was a deliberate affront to modern decency. She considered his rude remarks to be a personal affront. I did not mean to affront you by leaving the meeting early. The poorly designed new building is an affront to the historical architecture of the city. He took the sudden cancellation of his project as a personal affront.

english_meaning: A person who is very enthusiastic about a particular activity or subject. Someone with deep knowledge and love for a hobby, sport, or art form. A devoted fan or follower of something. An expert admirer who follows a field closely.
example_sentence: He is a well-known aficionado of classical music. Cricket aficionados filled the stadium hours before the match. As a coffee aficionado, she roasts her own beans. The gallery attracts art aficionados from across the country.

english_meaning: Far away from home or from a usual place. To or at a distance, especially when travelling or searching. Out in the fields or open countryside. Away from the correct subject or intended point.
example_sentence: Students came from as far afield as Karachi and Peshawar. We had to look further afield for a suitable house. The hunters went afield before sunrise. His answer wandered rather far afield from the question.

english_meaning: Mentioned or referred to previously in a text or speech.
example_sentence: The aforementioned witness confirmed the details of the incident to the police. Please refer to the aforementioned document for further clarification. The aforementioned rules apply to all employees without exception. As stated in the aforementioned paragraph, the contract will expire next month.

english_meaning: It refers to something or someone mentioned previously in a text or conversation. It is commonly used in legal documents to designate a person, item, or clause named before. It serves to identify a subject without repeating all previously stated details.
example_sentence: The aforesaid property shall be handed over to the rightful heir. All terms stated in the aforesaid agreement remain binding on both parties. The aforesaid witness failed to appear in court today. Pursuant to the aforesaid regulations, the permit was granted.

english_meaning: Thought, intention, or planning formed in advance, especially before committing an act. Premeditation, chiefly in the legal phrase ‘malice aforethought’.
example_sentence: The prosecutor argued that the murder was committed with malice aforethought. The evidence suggested aforethought rather than a sudden impulse. Courts distinguish between an impulsive act and one committed with aforethought. His careful preparations showed clear aforethought.

english_meaning: Into conflict or difficulty with. In violation of rules, customs, or the law, especially in the phrase ‘run afoul of’.
example_sentence: The company ran afoul of environmental regulations and faced heavy fines. He ran afoul of the law after failing to pay his taxes. Their new policy ran afoul of local customs and caused public outrage. She was careful not to run afoul of her strict manager.

english_meaning: Feeling fear or anxiety. Worried that something bad might happen. Reluctant to do something due to fear. Regretful about giving unwelcome information. Concerned about a possible consequence.
example_sentence: She is afraid of dogs. He was afraid to speak in public. I'm afraid I cannot help you today. They were afraid of losing the match.

english_meaning: In the end, anyway. Used to give a reason that explains what you just said (showing justification or reminder). Used to emphasize something that is obvious or already known. Used to introduce a final fact or argument that supports a conclusion.
example_sentence: You should forgive him, after all, he’s your brother. We decided to stay home; after all, it was raining heavily. She can’t be blamed — after all, she wasn’t even there. He won the competition, after all, he practiced every day.

english_meaning: An effect that continues after its cause has ended. A delayed consequence of an event, illness, treatment, or experience. A physical or emotional condition remaining afterward.
example_sentence: Fatigue can be an after-effect of the infection. The town still feels the after-effects of the flood. Drowsiness is a common after-effect of this medicine. Anxiety was a lasting after-effect of the accident.

english_meaning: Occurring after the usual closing time or regular working hours. Relating to activities done outside official business hours. In finance, taking place after a market has formally closed.
example_sentence: Call the after-hours number if the problem is urgent. Staff attended an after-hours training session. The clinic provides after-hours medical care. The company’s shares rose in after-hours trading.

english_meaning: The market for spare parts, accessories, and services for a product after its original sale. Trade in replacement parts supplied by companies other than the original manufacturer. Relating to goods sold after the initial purchase of a vehicle or machine. In finance, the market in which shares are traded after their initial issue.
synonyms: ["Secondary market","Resale market","Spare-parts trade","Replacement market","Post-sale market","Accessory market"]
example_sentence: He bought aftermarket wheels for his old car. The aftermarket for smartphone accessories is growing rapidly. Aftermarket parts are often cheaper than original ones. The shares rose sharply in the aftermarket.

english_meaning: The emotional effects that remain after a shocking or painful experience. Changes in society or community life following a major event. Effects that continue for a long period after the event has ended. Major changes in leadership, laws, or policies that follow an important event.
example_sentence: People in Pakistan are still coping with the aftermath of the recent floods. A lot of rebuilding took place in the aftermath of the war. How does a country cope with the aftermath of war? The president visited the region in the immediate aftermath of the disaster. Many more people died in the aftermath of the explosion. New reforms were introduced in the aftermath of the revolution.

english_meaning: Situated nearest to the back or rear. Furthest behind in position or order. In nautical use, closest to the stern of a ship. The last in a line or sequence.
example_sentence: The aftermost cabin was reserved for the crew. Passengers were asked to move to the aftermost seats. Damage was limited to the aftermost part of the vessel. He sat in the aftermost row of the small aircraft.

english_meaning: The period of the day between noon and evening. The time from about 12 p.m. until sunset. Relating to or happening during this part of the day. A particular afternoon regarded as an occasion or event.
example_sentence: We usually go for a walk in the afternoon. She has a meeting on Monday afternoon. The children played in the garden all afternoon. It rained heavily yesterday afternoon.

english_meaning: At a later or subsequent time. After the event or time mentioned. Later on. Following something that has happened.
example_sentence: We had dinner and went for a walk afterward. She apologized to him afterward. He felt very tired afterward. They discussed the matter and left afterward.

english_meaning: Wide open, especially describing the mouth because of surprise, shock, wonder, or admiration. Someone whose mouth is wide open because they are extremely surprised, amazed, shocked, frightened, or filled with admiration. It can also describe staring in complete astonishment.
example_sentence: The children stood agape as the magician made the elephant disappear. She looked agape when she heard that she had won the scholarship. The audience sat agape, watching the breathtaking fireworks. He remained agape after seeing the massive waterfall for the first time.

english_meaning: A business or organisation that provides a particular service on behalf of others. A department or body of government responsible for a specific area of work. The capacity of a person to act independently and make their own choices. The means or process by which something is achieved or caused. An office or branch that represents a larger company.
example_sentence: She found the job through a recruitment agency. The agency is responsible for monitoring air quality. Students should be given more agency over their own learning. The change was brought about through the agency of local volunteers.

english_meaning: A list of items to be discussed at a formal meeting. An underlying often ideological plan or program. A set of things that need to be done or are considered important. The program of matters to be dealt with by a group or individual.
example_sentence: The board of directors added three new items to the meeting's agenda. She has a hidden agenda when it comes to the new company policy. Education reform is at the top of the politician's agenda. We need to stick to the agenda to finish the meeting on time.

english_meaning: Having the capacity or quality of an agent; able to act independently and make choices. Exercising control over one's own actions and decisions. In modern usage, describes artificial intelligence systems that can plan and act toward goals autonomously.
example_sentence: The research focuses on building more agentic AI systems. Children become more agentic as they learn to make their own choices. An agentic approach gives employees real control over their work. The new framework supports agentic behavior in language models.

english_meaning: To collect, gather, or form into a mass, cluster, or large group. To bring together different things into one combined whole. As a noun, a mass or collection of various items grouped together. In geology, a coarse rock made up of volcanic fragments.
example_sentence: Several small companies agglomerated to form a large corporation. The dust agglomerated into thick clumps on the shelves. The geologist studied the agglomerate rocks formed by the volcano. Tiny particles agglomerated together to make a solid mass. The city is an agglomerate of many cultures and traditions.

english_meaning: The act or process of gathering things together into a mass or group. A collection of many different items, people, or elements grouped into one. A large cluster or accumulation, often without a clear order. In urban studies, a continuous area formed by several towns joined together.
example_sentence: Karachi is a huge agglomeration of people from different regions. The agglomeration of dust caused breathing problems for many residents. The exhibition displayed an agglomeration of art from various countries. There was an agglomeration of cars at the busy junction. The urban agglomeration has expanded rapidly over the last decade.

english_meaning: Tending to stick or join things together into a single mass. In linguistics, describing a language in which words are formed by joining separate elements, each with one clear meaning.
example_sentence: Turkish is an agglutinative language with long suffix chains. The glue has a strongly agglutinative effect on paper. Agglutinative forms make the grammar easier to analyse. Students often find agglutinative word building unfamiliar.

english_meaning: To increase the power, wealth, or status of a person, often in an undeserved or exaggerated way. To make oneself or another appear greater or more important than the reality justifies. To enlarge or exalt the importance or reputation of something beyond its true merit. To inflate one's own significance through self-promotion or propaganda. To pursue personal power or prestige at the expense of accuracy or fairness.
example_sentence: The dictator used propaganda to aggrandise his personal image. She was accused of trying to aggrandise her own role in the project. The politician sought to aggrandise his power at the expense of others. The media often aggrandise celebrities beyond their true achievements. His speeches were designed to aggrandise the ruling party's legacy.

english_meaning: To increase the power, status, or wealth of. To make something appear greater than it really is. To enhance the reputation of beyond what is justified by the facts. To exaggerate. To make greater in size or importance. It is often used in a negative sense for people who try to make themselves look more important, powerful, or wealthy than they actually are.
example_sentence: He used the position only to aggrandize himself and his family. The king sought to aggrandize his empire through constant wars. Politicians often aggrandize their achievements before elections. She told the story in a way that aggrandized her own role. The new wing was built to aggrandize the palace.

english_meaning: The act of increasing one's own power, wealth, status, or reputation. The process of making something appear greater or more important than it really is.
example_sentence: The war was fought purely for territorial aggrandizement. He accused the minister of personal aggrandizement. The project served the aggrandizement of the ruling family. Her speech was free of self-praise or aggrandizement.

english_meaning: To make something worse or more severe. To intensify pain or difficulty. To worsen a situation. To irritate or annoy someone. To make a problem, situation, or condition worse or more serious. It is often used for illness, pain, or conflicts. It can also mean to annoy someone.
example_sentence: Loud noise can aggravate his headache. His rude behavior aggravated the situation. Scratching the wound will aggravate it. She was aggravated by constant interruptions.

english_meaning: Made worse, more serious, or more severe than before. Feeling annoyed or irritated by someone or something. In law, describing a crime committed with additional serious circumstances, such as violence. Increased in intensity or degree.
example_sentence: The dust aggravated her asthma badly. He was charged with aggravated assault. She felt aggravated by the constant interruptions. Poor drainage aggravated the flooding in the town.

english_meaning: Making a problem, illness, or situation worse than before. Causing annoyance or irritation to someone. In law, describing a factor that makes an offence more serious. Extremely irritating in behavior or manner.
example_sentence: The noise outside was truly aggravating. Smoking is an aggravating factor in heart disease. The judge listed several aggravating circumstances. His aggravating habit of interrupting spoiled the discussion.

english_meaning: The act of making a bad situation, problem, or illness worse. A feeling of annoyance or irritation. Something that causes trouble, annoyance, or extra difficulty. In law, a circumstance that makes an offence more serious.
example_sentence: The delay caused further aggravation for the passengers. Stress led to an aggravation of his condition. She left the meeting in sheer aggravation. The court noted the aggravation of the offence by the use of a weapon.

english_meaning: A person or thing that makes a bad situation worse. Someone who annoys or provokes others. A factor that increases the severity of a problem.
example_sentence: Loud noise was a major aggravator of his headache. The delay proved to be an aggravator in the negotiations. He was known as an aggravator among his classmates. Stress can act as an aggravator of many diseases.

english_meaning: A total or whole formed by combining several separate parts or amounts. Formed or calculated by adding units together. To gather or combine into a single group or total. In construction, crushed stone, sand, or gravel mixed with cement to make concrete. In sport, the combined score of two matches.
example_sentence: The aggregate cost of the project exceeded one million rupees. Their aggregate score put them at the top of the table. The software aggregates data from many sources. Fine aggregate is mixed with cement to make strong concrete.

english_meaning: Hostile or violent behavior or attitudes toward another, an act of attacking or being assertive in a forceful way. Actions, behaviors, or attitudes that are forceful, hostile, or attacking in nature. It can manifest physically, verbally, or psychologically. It can be personal, social, or political. In psychology, it also describes an innate or learned tendency to confront, dominate, or harm others.
example_sentence: The research shows that computer games may cause aggression. The country’s military aggression alarmed its neighbors. His aggression during the argument made everyone uncomfortable. Aggression in sports can sometimes lead to penalties. Psychologists study how childhood experiences influence adult aggression.

english_meaning: Ready to attack or confront, assertive in a forceful way. Showing strong determination, initiative, or energy. Can refer to hostile or combative behavior, or highly competitive and proactive actions.
example_sentence: The dog became aggressive when strangers approached. She took an aggressive approach to complete the project on time. His aggressive marketing strategy increased sales significantly. The politician made an aggressive speech against corruption

english_meaning: To cause someone to feel distressed or resentful. To treat unfairly and cause hurt. To inflict injury or hardship on someone. To make someone feel wronged. To offend or trouble emotionally.
example_sentence: The unfair decision aggrieved many employees. He felt aggrieved by his friend's harsh remarks. The community was aggrieved by the loss of their park. She wrote to the authorities as an aggrieved citizen.

english_meaning: Feeling resentment at having been unfairly treated. Suffering from an injustice or grievance. Having a complaint or sense of wrong. Treated unjustly and feeling hurt or angry.
example_sentence: The aggrieved employees filed a complaint. She felt aggrieved by the unfair decision. The aggrieved party sought legal remedy. He spoke as an aggrieved victim.

english_meaning: Struck with sudden shock, horror, or disbelief at something unexpected or terrible. Showing intense and visible dismay, fear, or astonishment in response to a shocking event. Filled with a sense of horror or revulsion at something witnessed or heard. Overcome with emotional disturbance caused by something disturbing or upsetting. Standing rooted in stunned disbelief or terror at an unexpected revelation.
example_sentence: She stood aghast when she discovered the extent of the damage. The audience was aghast at the unexpected twist in the play. He was aghast at the news of the sudden tragedy. The team was aghast when they learned their project had been cancelled. They looked aghast as the fire spread to the neighboring buildings.

english_meaning: Able to move quickly and easily. Quick, smart, and clever. Able to think quickly and in an intelligent way. Able to deal with new situations or changes quickly and successfully.
example_sentence: Years of ballet and modern dance had made her strong and agile. For a man of 80, he has a remarkably agile mind. Monkeys are very agile climbers. You need to have agile fingers to do this kind of work.

english_meaning: The ability to move quickly and easily. The ability to think quickly and in an intelligent way. The gracefulness of a person or animal that is quick and nimble.
example_sentence: As a player, she combines strength and agility. This job requires considerable mental agility. Airlines want the agility and flexibility to push things the way they do on their website and sell more content.

english_meaning: To argue strongly for something you want, especially for changes in a law, in social conditions, etc. To make somebody feel angry, anxious or nervous. To make something, especially a liquid, move around by mixing or shaking it. To move or force into violent.
example_sentence: Political groups agitating for social change. Some militant groups have been agitating for autonomy for the region. Her family are agitating to have her transferred to a prison in the UK. This remark seemed to agitate her guest. Richard felt agitated by a mixture of anger, fear and pleasure. Agitate the mixture to dissolve the powder.

english_meaning: A state of anxiety or nervous excitement. The action of campaigning to arouse public concern about an issue. The action of briskly stirring or disturbing something.
example_sentence: There was visible agitation among the protesters who had gathered outside the parliament building. She concealed her inner agitation behind a composed and professional exterior. The agitation for political reform grew stronger as the economic situation worsened. He masked his agitation with a forced smile and a steady voice. The milk was placed in a machine for gentle agitation to prevent separation during storage.

english_meaning: A small plastic or metal tip at the end of a shoelace or cord that prevents it from fraying and makes it easier to pass through eyelets.
example_sentence: The aglet on my shoelace broke, so I cannot tie my shoes properly. He used a lighter to seal the aglet of the rope. Without an aglet, the shoelace becomes hard to insert into the shoe holes. The new hoodie has metal aglets on its drawstrings.

english_meaning: A person who believes that nothing can be known about God or the existence of a higher power. Someone who is unsure or non-committal about the existence of God or any divine reality. It can also describe a general attitude of skepticism or doubt toward knowledge claims, especially in religion.
example_sentence: She describes herself as an agnostic and does not follow any religion. The agnostic philosopher questioned the certainty of spiritual knowledge. He remained agnostic on the topic of life after death. Being agnostic, he avoids debates on religious doctrines.

english_meaning: Combative or argumentative. Relating to competition, struggle, or conflict. In biology and animal behavior, involving threat, aggression, defense, avoidance, submission, or fighting between individuals. Relating to an agonist that activates a receptor or produces a biological response.
example_sentence: The debate became increasingly agonistic as neither speaker would compromise. The deer displayed agonistic behavior during the breeding season. Researchers recorded both aggressive and submissive agonistic signals. The drug has an agonistic effect on the receptor. An agonistic political culture can make cooperation difficult.

english_meaning: To suffer great mental or physical pain. To worry or struggle for a long time over a difficult decision. To cause someone severe distress or torment. To think about something anxiously and at length.
example_sentence: She agonized for weeks over whether to accept the job. He agonized about the mistake he had made. Do not agonize over things you cannot control. The long wait for results agonized the whole family.

english_meaning: Extreme physical or mental pain. The struggle that precedes death. Intense feelings of suffering, acute mental or physical pain.
example_sentence:
She lay there screaming in agony.
I was in an agony of suspense.
We've both suffered agonies of guilt over what happened.
It must be agony for them to say goodbye.

english_meaning: An agony aunt is an advice columnist who answers letters from readers about their personal problems. She provides guidance on relationships and emotional dilemmas in a magazine or newspaper. The term refers to a person who listens to and offers advice on personal issues. It acts as a sympathetic listener for those seeking help with their private troubles.
example_sentence: She wrote a letter to the local agony aunt seeking advice about her failing marriage. The magazine's agony aunt receives hundreds of emails every week from troubled teenagers. He realized he was acting like an agony aunt for all his friends' relationship problems. Being an agony aunt requires a great deal of empathy and psychological insight.

english_meaning: A public open space used for assemblies and markets in ancient Greek cities. The central marketplace of an ancient Greek town. A gathering or assembly of citizens in such a place.
example_sentence: The ruins of the ancient agora still attract tourists. Citizens gathered in the agora to debate public affairs. Traders sold olives and pottery in the agora. The temple stood at the northern edge of the agora.

english_meaning: Fear of being in situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable, often leading to avoidance of open or crowded spaces. A type of anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear and anxiety about being in places or situations where they feel trapped, helpless, or embarrassed.
synonyms: ["Fear of open spaces","Space anxiety","Panic disorder-related phobia","Avoidance disorder"]
example_sentence: She developed agoraphobia after being trapped in an elevator. His agoraphobia makes it difficult for him to attend crowded events. Therapy helped him slowly overcome his agoraphobia. People with agoraphobia often feel anxious even in familiar open spaces.

english_meaning: Suffering from an abnormal fear of open or public places. Relating to agoraphobia, the fear of crowded or unfamiliar spaces. A person who suffers from agoraphobia.
example_sentence: He became agoraphobic after the accident and rarely left home. Agoraphobic patients often avoid crowded markets. Therapy helped her overcome her agoraphobic fears. The agoraphobic refused to attend the ceremony.

english_meaning: Relating to farming, agriculture, or cultivated land. Concerning the ownership and division of farmland. Relating to rural areas and people who live by farming. A person who supports the fair distribution of agricultural land.
example_sentence: The country still has a largely agrarian economy. Agrarian reforms gave land to poor farmers. He studied agrarian societies of South Asia. Agrarian communities depend heavily on seasonal rainfall.

english_meaning: To have the same opinion as someone else. To say yes to a proposal, request, or suggestion. To reach a decision together after discussion. To match or be consistent with something. To be suitable or good for someone, especially food or climate.
example_sentence: I agree with everything you have said. They agreed to meet again on Monday. The two witnesses' statements do not agree. The mild climate agrees with her health.

english_meaning: To have the same opinion; to be suitable for health.
example_sentence: I feel terrible- that food didn’t agree with my stomach. Do you agree with capital punishment?

english_meaning: Pleasant and enjoyable to experience. Willing to accept or agree to something. Friendly and easy to get along with. Acceptable or suitable to all parties concerned.
example_sentence: We spent an agreeable evening by the river. He was agreeable to the changes in the contract. Her agreeable manner made everyone feel welcome. The terms were agreeable to both companies.

english_meaning: In a pleasant and enjoyable manner. In a friendly and willing way. In a way that is acceptable and satisfying, often pleasantly surprising.
example_sentence: I was agreeably surprised by the quality of the food. He nodded agreeably when we suggested the plan. The afternoon passed agreeably in the shade of the trees. She spoke agreeably to every guest at the table.

english_meaning: An arrangement accepted by two or more people or groups. A formal contract or treaty setting out shared terms. Harmony of opinion or feeling between people. In grammar, the correct matching of words in number, gender, or person.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a trade agreement last month. There was general agreement that the plan should go ahead. Please read the rental agreement carefully before signing. Subject verb agreement is an important grammar rule.

english_meaning: Smiling broadly, with a wide grin on the face. In a state of grinning or showing pleasure through the face. Expressing amusement or satisfaction visibly. Wearing a joyful or mischievous smile. Displaying happiness or teasing with a full smile.
example_sentence: He stood there agrin, proud of his achievement. She came out of the room agrin with joy. The child looked agrin after receiving the gift. He was agrin from ear to ear.

english_meaning: With the bottom of a vessel touching and resting on the sea floor or riverbed. Describing a boat or ship that has become stranded in shallow water and cannot move freely. Unable to float due to contact between the hull and the bottom. In a position of being stuck on or touching the ground beneath water. Applied to vessels that have run onto a sandbank, reef, or shallow area.
example_sentence: The tanker ran aground in the shallow waters near the coast. The ship went aground during the storm and could not be moved. A small fishing boat was found aground on the sandbank. The rescue team worked to float the vessel that had run aground. The cargo ship ran aground and caused an environmental concern.

english_meaning: A person who helps or assists someone, especially in an official or professional capacity. Someone who provides support, assistance, or advice to a person, often someone in a position of authority. This can include administrative help, personal assistance, or professional guidance.
example_sentence: The senator’s aide prepared all the documents for the meeting. She works as a teaching aide in the local school. His aide advised him on the best way to handle the crisis. The president’s aide organized the schedule for the official visit.

english_meaning: Ailurophilia means a strong love or fondness for cats. An emotional attraction or deep affection toward cats. A person who has ailurophilia enjoys being around cats, caring for them, and often feels comforted or happy in their presence. It is not just liking cats, but a stronger emotional preference or passion for them.
antonyms: ["Ailurophobia","Fear of cats","Cat aversion","Dislike of cats","Feline dislike"]
example_sentence: Her ailurophilia is clear from the dozens of cats she has adopted. Due to his ailurophilia, he volunteers at an animal shelter every weekend. Ailurophilia often leads people to become passionate cat rescuers. She jokes that her ailurophilia is stronger than her love for anything else.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of cats. A person suffering from ailurophobia experiences extreme anxiety or panic in the presence of cats.
example_sentence: Her ailurophobia made it impossible to visit her friend who owned cats. Napoleon Bonaparte reportedly suffered from ailurophobia. His ailurophobia was so severe he could not enter a house with a cat. She sought therapy to overcome her ailurophobia.

english_meaning: To direct or focus toward a goal. To direct an action or effort toward a specific goal or objective. To intend or plan to achieve something. To target someone or something, physically or figuratively.
example_sentence: The campaign aims at reducing plastic waste in cities. He aimed at improving his English skills through daily practice. The archer aimed at the target carefully before releasing the arrow. The program is aimed at helping young entrepreneurs start their businesses.

english_meaning: To reveal private problems, arguments, disagreements, secrets, or embarrassing matters in public. The expression is often used when someone talks openly about personal or family problems that would normally be kept private.
synonyms: ["Reveal private matters","Expose personal problems","Make private matters public","Publicize personal affairs","Reveal secrets","Expose embarrassing information","Disclose personal problems","Spill personal secrets"]
antonyms: ["Keep private matters private","Keep something confidential","Keep personal affairs to oneself","Maintain privacy","Keep a secret","Conceal personal problems","Keep things under wraps"]
example_sentence: The couple decided not to air their dirty laundry in public. She aired her dirty laundry on social media after the argument. There is no need to air our dirty laundry in front of the neighbors. The manager warned the employees not to air the company's dirty laundry during the meeting.

english_meaning: To talk publicly about private, personal, or family problems, especially those that are embarrassing or unpleasant.
synonyms: ["Expose personal matters","Reveal private issues","Make personal problems public"]
antonyms: ["Keep things private","Maintain discretion","Protect one’s reputation","Handle issues in private"]
example_sentence: You shouldn’t air your dirty laundry on social media. They keep arguing in public, always airing their dirty laundry. Let’s solve this privately instead of airing our dirty laundry at the office. He regretted airing his dirty laundry during the interview.

english_meaning: Delivery of supplies or digital files through air or wireless transfer. To send supplies, packages, or aid from an aircraft without landing. It is also used for wirelessly sharing files between devices such as phones or computers. Military supply delivery from aircraft. Cryptocurrency free token distribution. Promotional giveaway sent digitally
example_sentence: The army performed an airdrop of food to the remote village. She used Airdrop to send photos to her friend. The company announced a cryptocurrency airdrop for users. Relief agencies planned an airdrop after the flood.

english_meaning: Feeling sick or nauseous while traveling in an airplane. Experiencing discomfort, nausea, or vomiting due to motion during air travel. This is a type of motion sickness specifically occurring on airplanes.
example_sentence: She felt airsick after the turbulent flight. He always gets airsick on long journeys. The child became airsick during takeoff. They offered him medicine because he was airsick.

english_meaning: A passage between rows of seats in a building such as a church, theater, or airplane. A narrow walkway between shelves in a shop. A path or corridor separating sections. The space people walk through in seated arrangements. An aisle is typically a long, narrow passage that allows movement between rows of seats or shelves and is commonly found in places of worship, public venues, stores, and transport vehicles.
example_sentence: The bride walked slowly down the aisle toward the altar. Please keep the aisle clear during the flight for safety reasons. You will find the cereal in aisle five of the supermarket. He stood up from his seat and moved into the aisle. The theater staff guided latecomers along the aisle to their seats.

english_meaning: Slightly open, not fully closed. Partly open, as of a door or window. In a position that leaves a small gap. Left open just a little, often on purpose.
example_sentence: She left the door ajar so the cat could come in. The window was ajar and cold air filled the room. He noticed the gate standing ajar late at night. Please keep the door ajar while the paint dries.

english_meaning: Similar in nature, character, or quality; closely related. Something that is very similar to another thing or closely connected by nature, qualities, origin, or relationship. It is commonly followed by the preposition to.
example_sentence: Her writing style is akin to that of a famous novelist. The feeling of excitement was akin to winning a championship. His ideas are akin to those presented in the research paper. Learning a new language is often akin to opening a door to another culture.

english_meaning: Taking place or done in the open air. Referring to outdoor dining or activities. Describing paintings done on fresh plaster outdoors. Enjoyed in a natural, open setting. Relating to fresh, outdoor experiences.
example_sentence: We enjoyed an al fresco lunch in the garden. The restaurant offers al fresco dining in summer. They held the wedding reception al fresco. Al fresco painting requires special techniques.

english_meaning: Brisk and cheerful readiness to do something. Eagerness. Promptness. Willingness combined with quick action. Liveliness in responding to a task. Used to describe the speed and enthusiasm with which a person accepts or performs a duty, request, or opportunity.
example_sentence: She accepted the new responsibility with great alacrity. The children jumped up with alacrity when their father called them. He responded to the emergency call with surprising alacrity. The employees showed alacrity in completing the project before the deadline. The dog wagged its tail with alacrity at the sight of its owner.

english_meaning: Causing fear, worry, concern, or a feeling that something dangerous or unpleasant may happen. Something that makes people feel afraid, worried, shocked, or concerned because it suggests a possible danger, problem, or unpleasant situation.
example_sentence: The doctor reported an alarming increase in the number of patients. The firefighters responded quickly to the alarming situation. There was an alarming drop in the company's sales last month. The news of the storm's approach was alarming to local residents.

english_meaning: In a way that causes fear, concern, or anxiety about potential danger. To a degree that signals a serious or urgent problem requiring immediate attention. In a manner that is troubling, worrying, or frightening to observe or experience. With a rate or degree that suggests a dangerous trend or escalating crisis. In a way that triggers alarm or a strong feeling of unease.
example_sentence: The number of infections rose alarmingly within days. The temperature in the region has been alarmingly high this summer. The crime rate in the neighborhood increased alarmingly. Her health deteriorated alarmingly fast after the surgery. The pollution levels in the city have risen alarmingly in recent years.

english_meaning: An exclamation used to express grief, pity, or regret. A word said when something sad or disappointing happens. Used to introduce an unfortunate fact.
example_sentence: Alas, the old library was demolished last year. Alas, he arrived too late to say goodbye. The harvest failed again, alas, for the third season. Alas, we cannot change what has already happened.

english_meaning: Although, even though. Used to introduce a contrast or limitation in a statement. It connects two clauses, showing that the second clause modifies or reduces the force of the first clause. It is formal and mostly used in writing.
example_sentence: He finally agreed to join the project, albeit reluctantly. The movie was enjoyable, albeit a bit too long. She accepted the offer, albeit with some hesitation. The journey was exciting, albeit tiring.

english_meaning: A colorless volatile liquid that is the intoxicating ingredient in drinks like beer and wine. Any organic compound containing a hydroxyl group. Beverages containing ethanol that can cause intoxication. A substance that acts as a depressant on the central nervous system.
example_sentence: Excessive alcohol consumption damages the liver. The solution contains 70% alcohol. He decided to quit drinking alcohol. Rubbing alcohol is used as a disinfectant.

english_meaning: A person who suffers from alcoholism or addiction to alcohol. Relating to or containing alcohol. Caused by or associated with alcohol consumption. Someone who cannot control their drinking.
example_sentence: He joined Alcoholics Anonymous to overcome his addiction. This beverage is alcoholic and contains 5% alcohol. She comes from a family with an alcoholic parent. Alcoholic drinks should be consumed responsibly.

english_meaning: Algophobia is an extreme, morbid, or irrational fear of experiencing physical pain. It is a psychological condition where an individual suffers from intense anxiety at the mere prospect of pain. The phobia often causes people to excessively avoid medical procedures or daily activities due to overwhelming dread. It represents an abnormal hypersensitivity and psychological distress related to the anticipation of painful sensations.
synonyms: ["Fear of pain","Odynophobia","Agliophobia","Dread of pain","Pain phobia","Extreme pain anxiety","Morbid dread of pain","Hypersensitivity to pain","Pain apprehension"]
example_sentence: Persons with algophobia may refuse essential medical care out of sheer terror. Her algophobia caused her to panic before taking a simple blood test. Cognitive behavioral therapy is often effective in treating severe algophobia. The physician noticed that his patient's extreme distress stemmed from algophobia.

english_meaning: A false or alternative name used instead of a real name. Another name that a person uses instead of their real name. It is often used for privacy, safety, writing, acting, or sometimes to hide identity. In legal or criminal cases, it may refer to a false name used to avoid recognition. In technology, it can also mean an alternative name for a file or email address.
example_sentence: He checked into the hotel under an alias. The writer published the novel under an alias. The criminal was arrested while using an alias. She created an email alias for professional work. The actor worked under an alias before becoming famous.

english_meaning: Evidence that a person was somewhere else when a crime was committed. A claim or proof of being elsewhere at the time of an event. An excuse used to avoid blame or responsibility. To provide an excuse or defence for someone.
example_sentence: The suspect had a solid alibi for the night of the robbery. Her colleagues confirmed his alibi. He always has an alibi for arriving late. The lawyer alibied his client with security footage.

english_meaning: A person who is from a different country and is not a naturalized citizen. A hypothetical being from another planet or outside the Earth's atmosphere. Relating to a foreign country or a different group. Belonging to a place or world other than the one currently being discussed. To be strange, unfamiliar, or repugnant to a person's nature or character. To transfer ownership or property to another person.
example_sentence: The government granted temporary work permits to every legal alien living in the state. Science fiction movies often portray an alien invasion as a threat to humanity. His cold and calculated behavior was completely alien to his normally kind personality. Scientists are scanning the deep reaches of space for any signs of alien life.

english_meaning: To make someone feel isolated or estranged. To cause someone to feel detached, unfriendly, or withdrawn, often by one’s actions, behavior, or attitude. To transfer ownership or rights of property to another person.
example_sentence: His constant criticism alienated his coworkers. The new law alienated many citizens. She alienated her family by refusing to attend gatherings. Ignoring his friends alienated him from the group. Harsh government policies alienate minority communities. He alienated his land to his nephew.

english_meaning: Feeling of isolation or separation. The state of being estranged, isolated, or detached from others, oneself, or society. It can occur emotionally, socially, legally, or culturally. It includes feelings of disconnection, lack of belonging, or loss of rights. The transfer of ownership, rights, or interest in property from one person to another, usually permanently.
example_sentence: The new employee experienced alienation in the office because no one talked to him. Alienation from family can cause emotional stress. Many youths feel alienation from traditional social values. Political alienation often leads to low voter turnout. Legal alienation occurs when property rights are transferred to another person.

english_meaning: To place or arrange things in a straight line or in correct positions. To bring into agreement, cooperation, or association with something else. To adjust parts of a machine so that they work together properly. To join or side with a particular group, cause, or opinion. To make one thing consistent or in accord with another.
example_sentence: Please align the text to the left of the page. The country decided to align itself with its neighbors on trade issues. The mechanic aligned the wheels of the car perfectly. We must align our goals with the company's long-term vision.

english_meaning: Placed or arranged in a straight line or correct position. Positioned so that parts fit or work together properly. In agreement or support with a particular group, idea, or goal. Allied or associated with a side or party.
example_sentence: Make sure the shelves are properly aligned before drilling. The team's efforts are aligned with the company's goals. The two countries were closely aligned during the war. Her values are aligned with those of the charity.

english_meaning: The arrangement of things in a straight line or in correct relative positions. The state of being adjusted so that different parts work together properly. Agreement, support, or association with a particular group, cause, or policy. The correct positioning of the wheels of a vehicle. A grouping or forming of a united political, social, or economic order.
example_sentence: The alignment of the stars was studied by the astronomers. The car needs a wheel alignment after the accident. Her political alignment has always been with progressive parties. Proper alignment of the machine parts is essential for smooth operation.

english_meaning: Similar to one another in appearance, character or manner. In the same way or to the same degree. Equally, without distinction between the parties concerned.
example_sentence: The twins look very much alike. The new rules apply to teachers and students alike. No two fingerprints are exactly alike. They dressed alike for the family photograph.

english_meaning: The whole passage through which food travels in the body, from the mouth to the anus. The digestive tract in which food is broken down, absorbed and expelled. The tube-like system of organs responsible for digestion.
example_sentence: The teacher drew the alimentary canal on the whiteboard. Food is absorbed as it passes along the alimentary canal. Infections can affect any part of the alimentary canal. The alimentary canal of an adult is several metres long.

english_meaning: Money that a court orders one spouse to pay the other after divorce or separation. A regular allowance for the maintenance of a former husband or wife. Financial support provided for a spouse's living expenses after marriage ends.
example_sentence: The court ordered him to pay monthly alimony. She receives alimony until she remarries. He fell behind on his alimony payments. Their lawyers argued for weeks over the amount of alimony.

english_meaning: A portion of a larger whole, especially a measured sample taken for analysis. A quantity that divides into another an exact number of times without a remainder. To divide a sample into equal measured parts.
example_sentence: The technician removed an aliquot of blood for testing. Five is an aliquot part of twenty. Each aliquot was stored in a separate tube. Please aliquot the solution into ten equal samples.

english_meaning: A person who talks angrily or threatens others but does not take real action. Someone who appears aggressive, loud, or threatening, but is actually harmless and unwilling to act. It often describes people who boast, argue loudly, or try to scare others without taking serious action.
synonyms: ["Empty threats","Big talker","Harmless bluster","Loud but harmless","Boastful person"]
antonyms: ["Man of action","Fearsome person","Serious threat","Strong and decisive person"]
example_sentence: The manager sounds strict, but he is all bark and no bite. Don’t be afraid of his threats because he is all bark and no bite. My neighbor keeps complaining loudly, yet he is all bark and no bite. The coach shouted at the players, but everyone knew he was all bark and no bite.

english_meaning: A radio call addressed to every patrol vehicle of a police force. A general alert broadcast to all units on duty. An instruction meant for everyone in a fleet or group rather than one person.
example_sentence: All cars, proceed immediately to the central market. The dispatcher repeated the message to all cars on duty. An all cars alert was issued after the robbery. All cars in the northern zone reported back within minutes.

english_meaning: To do something with full energy, force, enthusiasm, or determination. To approach a task or situation aggressively and with maximum effort.
example_sentence: The team entered the final match all guns blazing, determined to win the championship. She started her new business all guns blazing, with full confidence and energy. The politician came to the debate all guns blazing, attacking every weak point of his opponent. He faced the challenges all guns blazing, refusing to give up.

english_meaning: A person who talks big but acts little. Someone who talks big but does nothing or cannot prove their claims.
example_sentence: He keeps saying he will start a business, but he is all hat and no cattle. The politician made many promises, but turned out to be all hat and no cattle. She talks about helping the poor, yet does nothing; she is all hat and no cattle. Everyone thought he was successful, but he was all hat and no cattle.

english_meaning: Considering everything or overall. It is used to sum up or give a final opinion after looking at all aspects of something. It can also mean a person or thing that is most important or central in someone’s life, “everything to someone.”
example_sentence: He is all in all in the office. All in all, it was a successful event despite a few small issues. He is my friend, guide, and support, my all in all. All in all, the trip was enjoyable and worth the time. She handled the project very well; all in all, she did an excellent job.

word: All is well that ends well
english_meaning: If something has a good ending or successful result, the earlier problems, difficulties, or mistakes are forgiven or forgotten. A successful ending covers earlier troubles. Final success matters more than temporary difficulties. Good results make painful experiences easier to accept. Happiness at the end removes disappointment from the journey.
synonyms: ["Every cloud has a silver lining","The end justifies the means","All's fair in the end","A happy ending makes up for everything","Better late than never"]
antonyms: ["A bad ending ruins everything","Too little","Too late","Failure at the end overshadows success","Ending badly destroys earlier efforts"]
example_sentence: Our trip had many problems, but we reached safely home, All is well that ends well. The project was delayed several times, yet the client loved the final work, All is well that ends well. She struggled throughout the semester, but passed the exam with excellent marks, All is well that ends well. The wedding arrangements were chaotic at first, but the ceremony became beautiful in the end, All is well that ends well.

english_meaning: Having full mental capacity or sanity. Being mentally sound and sharp. In full possession of one's senses. Able to think and reason clearly. Not confused or mentally impaired.
example_sentence: Despite his age, he still has all his marbles. She has all her marbles and manages her business well. You need all your marbles to solve this puzzle. He seems to have lost some, but grandma has all her marbles.

english_meaning: To reduce or calm a fear, worry, or doubt. To make a painful or unpleasant feeling less severe. To relieve or satisfy hunger, thirst, or pain. To put someone's mind at ease.
example_sentence: The minister tried to allay public fears about the new tax. A glass of cold water allayed his thirst. Her calm explanation allayed my doubts. The medicine allayed the pain within minutes.

english_meaning: A claim that someone has done something wrong, without proof yet. A statement or accusation saying that a person committed a crime or improper act. It is not confirmed and may or may not be true until investigated or proven.
example_sentence: The allegation against the official was investigated by the court. She denied the allegation made by her coworkers. There was no evidence to support the allegation. Allegations of corruption can damage public trust.

english_meaning: To state that someone has done something wrong or illegal, often without providing conclusive evidence. It is usually used in legal, formal, or news contexts.
example_sentence: He is alleged to have mistreated the prisoner. The prosecution alleges she was driving carelessly. The company alleges that the competitor copied its product design. He alleged that the journalist misquoted his statement.

english_meaning:
To state something as a fact without giving proof. 
Accused but not proven or convicted. Claimed or said to be true, but not yet proven.
example_sentence: He is alleged to have mistreated the prisoner. The prosecution alleges she was driving carelessly. The alleged thief was caught near the market. She denied all the alleged accusations against her. The alleged corruption case is still under investigation. The company denied involvement in the alleged fraud.

english_meaning: Said to be true but not proven. Used when something is claimed or reported as true, but there is no confirmed proof yet. It is often used in news, legal cases, and formal reports to show uncertainty or caution.
example_sentence: He allegedly stole confidential documents from the office. The company allegedly violated environmental laws. She was allegedly involved in the fraud case. The suspect allegedly escaped before the police arrived.

english_meaning: Loyalty and support for a ruler, country, group, or belief. The act of binding yourself (intellectually or emotionally) to a course of action. A person’s continued support for a political party, religion, leader, etc.
example_sentence: Soldiers have to swear allegiance to the Crown, The King. People of various party allegiances joined the campaign. He affirmed his allegiance to the president. She proudly recited the Oath of Allegiance. The students pledge allegiance (to the flag) at the beginning of the school day.

english_meaning: Fully loyal and devoted to a person, country, cause, or institution. Showing steadfast faithfulness and commitment through actions and words. True to one's obligations and pledges in times of difficulty or temptation. Reliably devoted and supportive regardless of changing circumstances. Characterized by deep-rooted loyalty that does not waver under pressure.
example_sentence: The soldier remained allegiant to his country until his last breath. She was allegiant to her principles even under intense pressure. All citizens are expected to be allegiant to the laws of the land. He proved himself allegiant to his team during the most difficult times. The knight swore to be allegiant to the king and his cause.

english_meaning: Containing or relating to allegory, in which characters and events symbolically represent broader truths. Using symbolic figures, stories, or actions to convey a deeper moral, political, or spiritual meaning. Describing a text, artwork, or narrative that operates on two levels — literal and symbolic. Characterized by the use of extended metaphor to communicate complex ideas indirectly. Belonging to or typical of the allegorical tradition in literature or art.
example_sentence: The allegorical painting depicted the triumph of good over evil. Orwell's Animal Farm is widely recognized as an allegorical novel. The poet used allegorical figures to illustrate his political message. Many ancient myths are allegorical representations of natural forces. The film's allegorical content invited viewers to think beyond the surface story.

english_meaning: In a manner that uses allegory or symbolism rather than direct, literal expression. By means of symbolic representation to convey a deeper or hidden message. Through the use of extended metaphors or symbolic narrative. In the style of allegorical writing or interpretation that operates on two levels. Through indirect storytelling that encodes a moral, spiritual, or political message.
example_sentence: The poem is allegorically about the loss of innocence. She interpreted the dream allegorically as a sign of inner conflict. The director approached the subject allegorically to avoid censorship. The teacher explained the story allegorically to the students. The film speaks allegorically about political repression and resistance.

english_meaning: Having an allergy; reacting badly to a particular substance. Caused by or relating to an allergy. Strongly disliking someone or something, used informally. Sensitive in a harmful way to food, dust, medicine, or other substances.
example_sentence: He is allergic to peanuts and must read every label. She developed an allergic reaction after taking the medicine. Many children are allergic to dust and pollen. He jokes that he is allergic to hard work.

english_meaning: A harmful reaction of the body's immune system to a normally harmless substance. A medical condition causing sneezing, rashes, or swelling after exposure to something. Hypersensitivity to food, dust, pollen, or medicine. Informally, a strong dislike of something or someone.
example_sentence: She has a serious allergy to peanuts. Dust allergy keeps him sneezing all through the spring. The doctor prescribed tablets for his skin allergy. He has an allergy to long, pointless meetings.

english_meaning: To make pain, suffering, or difficulty less severe. To reduce the intensity of something unpleasant such as pain, stress, hardship, or problems. It does not completely remove the issue but makes it easier to tolerate or manage.
example_sentence: The medicine helped alleviate his headache. Good sleep can alleviate stress and anxiety. The government took steps to alleviate poverty. Warm tea may alleviate a sore throat.

english_meaning: A small, narrow lane or passage often found between or behind buildings. It can serve as a pedestrian path, service road, or shortcut. Some alleys may be quiet and residential, while others may be dark and commercial.
example_sentence: Children often play hide and seek in the narrow alley behind the school. The small alley led to a hidden garden. Trash bins were lined up along the alley. He got lost while walking through the maze-like alleys of the old city.

english_meaning: A relationship formed between two or more parties to cooperate for specific purposes, such as political, economic, military, or social goals. It often involves trust and shared interests.
example_sentence: The two countries formed a military alliance to strengthen their defense. Several companies entered an alliance to develop new technology. She sought an alliance with local organizations to support her project. The political parties formed an alliance before the elections.

english_meaning: People, groups, or countries that cooperate with each other for a common purpose. Nations joined together by a formal agreement, especially in war. Supporters who help or assist in a struggle or cause. Friends who provide help and back up during difficulties.
example_sentence: Britain and the United States were close allies during the war. She found strong allies among her colleagues at work. The two nations remained allies for decades. Political allies helped him win the election.

english_meaning: To repeat the same starting sound in nearby words. To use the same initial consonant sound in a group of words, usually for style, rhythm, or emphasis in speech or writing.
example_sentence: The poet chose to alliterate to give the line a musical sound. She alliterated words carefully in her speech to make it memorable. Many slogans alliterate to catch attention quickly. Writers often alliterate to strengthen imagery and rhythm.

english_meaning: Repetition of the same starting sound in nearby words. A literary device in which the same consonant sound is repeated at the beginning of two or more closely placed words to create rhythm, emphasis, or musical effect in speech or writing.
example_sentence: For alliteration it ought to be Pablo or Picauo. What a wonderful way to teach alliteration. Poets as we know have always a made great use of alliteration. She sells seashells by the seashore. Big brown bears roam the forest. Peter picked a peck of pickled peppers. Silent snakes slide slowly.

english_meaning: To give or set aside something for a particular purpose or person. To distribute resources such as money, time, or space officially. To assign a duty, place, or share to someone. To divide something among different uses according to a plan.
example_sentence: The government will allocate more funds to rural schools. We must allocate enough time for revision before the exam. Rooms were allocated to guests on arrival. She allocated each student a separate task.

english_meaning: The act of giving out or distributing something for a particular purpose. An amount of money, time, or resources set aside for someone or something. The process of deciding officially how resources will be shared. A share or portion assigned to a person, group, or project.
example_sentence: The allocation of funds for education has been increased. Each department received a fair allocation of resources. The allocation of seats will be announced next week. Poor allocation of time caused the project to fail.

english_meaning: Originating in a place other than where it is now found. In geology, describing rocks or sediments that have been moved from their place of formation. In biology or ecology, referring to material or organisms brought in from outside a system. Not native or indigenous to the area in question.
example_sentence: The valley contains allochthonous rocks carried by ancient glaciers. Allochthonous material enters the lake through the river. Geologists identified an allochthonous block in the mountain range. The study compared allochthonous and native plant species.

english_meaning: In linguistics, one of the different forms of a morpheme that have the same meaning. A variant pronunciation or spelling of a grammatical unit, such as the plural endings in cats, dogs, and horses. In chemistry or mineralogy, a different crystalline form of a substance. Any variant shape of a basic unit.
example_sentence: The plural morpheme has three common allomorphs in English. Students were asked to identify the allomorphs in the passage. The past tense marker appears as a different allomorph after certain sounds. Allomorphs vary according to the sounds around them.

english_meaning: Include something in a plan or calculation. To take into consideration. Make provision for something in planning.
example_sentence: You should allow for delays when planning a journey. We must allow for delays. The budget allows for extra expenses. The new design allows for easier repairs. Engineers had to allow for strong winds when building the bridge.

english_meaning: To permit, admit, or make possible something. To be capable of something. A situation, condition, or statement accepts or permits a certain interpretation, action, or result.
example_sentence: The rules don’t allow off any exceptions. The rules allow of no exceptions. The job allows of flexibility. The situation allows of only one interpretation. Her plan allows of some improvement. Such behavior does not allow of forgiveness.

english_meaning: To refer to something indirectly or mention it without stating it clearly. To make an indirect reference to a person, event, idea, or situation without explaining it openly. The speaker hints at something rather than saying it directly.
example_sentence: During the meeting, the manager alluded to possible changes in the company policy. The writer alluded to historical events in his novel. She alluded to a personal problem but did not give details. The teacher alluded to an important topic that would appear in the exam.

english_meaning: To attract or delight as if by magic. To lead away from a usual or proper course by offering some pleasure or advantage. To entice by charm or attraction. Power of attraction or fascination. The power of irresistible attraction.
example_sentence:
The country has lost its allure as a destination for foreign investment.
The film has all the nostalgic allure of fifties Paris. The allure of the stage drew him back to acting.

english_meaning: An indirect or passing reference to a person, event, place, or work without directly naming it. A brief and often unexplained hint embedded in speech or writing. A literary device used to evoke a cultural, historical, or artistic reference. A subtle reference that relies on the reader's existing knowledge to interpret correctly. An implicit comparison or reference that enriches meaning without full explanation.
example_sentence: The speech contained a clear allusion to the famous Shakespearean play. Her comment was an allusion to the political crisis of the previous decade. The poet's allusion to Greek mythology enriched the poem's meaning. The author's allusion to historical events gave the novel depth. His allusion to the earlier argument was not lost on the audience.

english_meaning: A country that has agreed to help and support another country, especially in case of a war. A person who helps and supports somebody who is in a difficult situation, especially a politician. To join (yourself) with another person, group, etc. in order to get or give support. To unite or form a connection or relation between.
example_sentence: He allied himself with a wealthy family by marriage. He allied himself with the Communists. There may be occasions when America can ally with some of those states, as we did during the Gulf War.

english_meaning: Money, food, or other donations given to poor and needy people as an act of charity. Charitable giving as a religious or moral duty. Help or relief given out of compassion to those in need. Voluntary donations made to support the poor, often associated with religious practice.
example_sentence: He gave alms to the beggars outside the mosque. Giving alms to the poor is an important act of charity in Islam. The wealthy man distributed alms during the festival. She always keeps some coins to give as alms. Collecting alms for the needy was part of their religious duty.

english_meaning: Next to or by the side of someone or something. Together with another person or thing. At the same time as something else. In cooperation or comparison with someone or something.
synonyms: ["Beside","Next to","By","Near","Along with","Together with","Adjacent to","Parallel to","With","Beside by side"]
example_sentence: The boat came alongside the dock. She worked alongside experienced nurses during training. The new policy was introduced alongside other reforms. Place the chart alongside the explanation for clarity.

english_meaning: A person who stays distant emotionally or socially and does not show warmth or involvement with people around them.
example_sentence: She remained aloof during the meeting and spoke very little. The new teacher seemed aloof, but later students realized he was simply shy. He stood aloof from the crowd and observed the event quietly. Her aloof attitude made others think she was unfriendly.

english_meaning: To argue, quarrel, or dispute noisily with another person. To have a heated verbal exchange or angry discussion. To engage in a loud or bitter argument, usually in public.
example_sentence: The two neighbours began to altercate over the boundary wall. He altercated with the shopkeeper about the price of the item. They altercated for nearly an hour without any result. It is not wise to altercate in public places. The brothers altercated bitterly over their late father's property.

english_meaning: A noisy argument, quarrel, or angry dispute, especially in public. A heated exchange of words between two or more people. A short but intense disagreement that may sometimes lead to a fight.
example_sentence: There was a loud altercation between the driver and the passenger. The meeting ended in a bitter altercation between the two members. Police arrived quickly to stop the altercation in the market. A small misunderstanding led to a serious altercation. He was injured during an altercation outside the restaurant.

english_meaning: To happen, appear, or cause things to occur one after another in a repeated pattern. To switch regularly between two states, actions, or choices. Every other one in a series. Serving or available as a substitute. A person chosen to act in another’s place.
example_sentence: Alternate layers of fruit and cream in the dish. The weather alternated between rain and sunshine. Meetings are held on alternate Fridays. An alternate will attend if the main delegate is unavailable.

english_meaning: Pairs of angles formed on opposite sides of a transversal crossing two lines. Interior alternate angles lie between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal. Exterior alternate angles lie outside the two lines on opposite sides. When the crossed lines are parallel, each pair of alternate angles is equal.
example_sentence: The teacher asked us to identify the alternate angles. Alternate interior angles are equal when the lines are parallel. Draw a transversal to create two pairs of alternate exterior angles. She used alternate angles to prove that the lines were parallel.

english_meaning: One after another in a repeated sequence. By turns between two states, actions, or people. Sometimes one way and sometimes another. A less common form of alternatively, meaning as another possibility.
example_sentence: The lights flashed alternately red and green. The baby laughed and cried alternately. The two nurses watched the patient alternately. Add the flour and milk alternately to the mixture.

english_meaning: One of two or more available possibilities. A choice or course of action used instead of another. Different from the usual, traditional, or mainstream option. In some contexts, relating to nonconventional lifestyles, medicine, music, or energy.
example_sentence: We need an alternative to plastic packaging. Cycling is a healthy alternative means of transport. She listens to alternative music. The doctor discussed alternative treatments with the patient.

english_meaning: As another possibility or choice. In a way that offers a different method or course of action. Used to introduce a contrasting or substitute suggestion.
example_sentence: You can take the bus or, alternatively, walk to the station. Alternatively, we could meet on Friday. Pay online; alternatively, send a cheque by mail. The sauce can be served hot or alternatively chilled.

english_meaning: In spite of the fact that. Even though. Used to introduce a contrast between two statements. But; however, when used to add a qualifying remark.
example_sentence: Although it was raining, we continued the walk. She smiled, although she was clearly tired. Although the film was long, nobody left early. He agreed to help, although he had little time.

english_meaning: An intense or irrational fear of heights. Individuals with altophobia may experience dizziness, sweating, rapid heartbeat, or panic when exposed to high places.
example_sentence: She avoided the balcony because her altophobia made her anxious. Climbing ladders is nearly impossible for him due to altophobia. The tall building made him nervous because of his altophobia. Altophobia can interfere with normal activities like hiking or sightseeing.

english_meaning: The selfless concern for the well-being and happiness of others. It involves acting out of a desire to help people, often at one's own expense. This moral practice emphasizes kindness, generosity, and compassion without expecting anything in return.
example_sentence: Her entire life was a testament to selfless altruism. Many charitable organizations rely on the altruism of their donors. True altruism means helping others without wanting anything in return. The millionaire showed great altruism by giving away his fortune. Animals sometimes exhibit altruism toward members of their group.

english_meaning: A person who is selflessly concerned for the well-being of others. Someone who prioritizes the needs and happiness of others over their own, often performing acts of kindness, charity, or generosity without expecting anything in return.
example_sentence: The altruist donated a large sum to the orphanage without revealing his identity. She is an altruist, always putting others’ needs before her own. Volunteers at the shelter are true altruists, giving their time freely. His altruist nature inspired the whole community to help the needy.

english_meaning: Showing unselfish concern for the well-being of others. Acting for the benefit of others without expecting anything in return. Characterised by or arising from a devotion to the welfare of others.
example_sentence: Her altruistic decision to donate her entire salary to charity inspired everyone who knew her. He was motivated by entirely altruistic reasons and expected nothing in return for his help. The organisation was founded on altruistic principles by people who wanted to make a genuine difference. She questioned whether truly altruistic behaviour was even possible in a competitive society. His altruistic efforts on behalf of the community earned him widespread respect and admiration.

english_meaning: One of the tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged. A small hollow cavity in the body. The bony socket in the jaw that holds a tooth.
example_sentence: Oxygen passes into the blood through each alveolus. An alveolus is surrounded by tiny blood vessels. Smoking destroys the walls of the alveolus. The dentist examined the alveolus after removing the tooth.
