english_meaning: Amiable, lovable, pleasant, sweet-natured. Lovable, friendly, kind, pleasant, or gracious in nature. It describes a person who is warm-hearted and easy to like. It is also used in music to indicate that a passage should be played in a gentle, pleasing, and affectionate manner.
example_sentence: She had an amabile personality that attracted everyone around her. The teacher spoke in an amabile tone to calm the nervous students. His amabile behavior made him popular among his colleagues. The musician played the melody in an amabile style, creating a soothing atmosphere.

english_meaning: A mixture of different elements. A combination of parts that create a complete whole.
example_sentence:
The show was a wonderful amalgam of dance, music, and drama.
Nearly every new parent feels an amalgam of joy and terror. The film script is an amalgam of all three books.

english_meaning: To combine or unite things into one whole. To mix, merge, or join two or more things such as organizations, ideas, groups, or substances so that they become a single unit. It often refers to forming a stronger or more effective whole by bringing parts together.
example_sentence: The two companies decided to amalgamate to improve their market strength. Different cultural traditions gradually amalgamated in the city. The organization plans to amalgamate several small programs into one large project. His research amalgamates ideas from sociology and economics.

english_meaning: The act of joining or mixing different things to form one whole. The process in which two or more organizations, ideas, substances, or groups combine to create a single unified entity. It is often used in business, science, culture, and social contexts where separate elements become integrated into one system.
example_sentence: The amalgamation of the two banks created a stronger financial institution. The city culture is an amalgamation of many traditions and languages. The company announced the amalgamation of its regional offices. Modern music is often an amalgamation of different musical styles.

english_meaning: A leafy green plant whose leaves and seeds are both edible. A nutritious vegetable widely grown in South Asia and Africa. A grain-like seed considered a healthy alternative to rice and wheat. A plant valued for its high protein, iron, and calcium content. A traditional crop used for centuries in local cooking and medicine.
example_sentence: Amaranth leaves are cooked like spinach in many households. Amaranth seeds are a healthy alternative to regular grains. She prepared a warm soup using fresh amaranth leaves. Amaranth is often recommended for people with low iron levels.

english_meaning: To accumulate or gather a large quantity of resources, money, knowledge, or objects. The focus is on collecting over time, often with effort and planning.
example_sentence: She managed to amass a fortune through smart investments. Over the years, he amassed a large collection of rare books. The company has amassed significant experience in renewable energy projects. Scientists have amassed data from hundreds of experiments.

english_meaning: Gathered together a large quantity of something over time. Collected. Accumulated. Built up. Heaped up. Brought together in great amount. Used especially when someone has gradually collected wealth, possessions, information, or supporters in large numbers through effort or time.
example_sentence: He amassed a huge fortune through hard work and wise investments. The library has amassed thousands of rare books over the centuries. Over the years, she amassed a remarkable collection of antique coins. The general amassed a powerful army before launching the attack. The scientist amassed enough evidence to support his groundbreaking theory.

english_meaning: A person who engages in an activity for personal enjoyment rather than as a profession. Someone without formal training, qualifications, or professional experience in a given field. A hobbyist who pursues a skill or interest without financial compensation. A person with less than professional-level skill, experience, or polish. One who participates in a sport, art, or craft out of love rather than livelihood.
example_sentence: He started as an amateur photographer before turning professional. The film festival included entries from both amateur and professional filmmakers. She painted as an amateur but her work was of professional quality. The amateur team surprised everyone by reaching the finals. As an amateur, he lacked the technical skills of experienced players.

english_meaning: A powerful feeling of great surprise, wonder, or astonishment. An emotional state triggered by encountering something extraordinary or unexpected. The intense pleasure or shock experienced when something impressive or impossible occurs. A condition of being dazzled, awed, or speechless in the face of something remarkable. An overwhelming sense of wonder or disbelief at something surprising or miraculous.
example_sentence: The children stared in amazement at the colorful fireworks. She watched in amazement as the magician performed impossible tricks. His rapid recovery left the doctors in amazement. The audience sat in amazement throughout the entire performance. She gasped in amazement at the breathtaking mountain view.

english_meaning: A hard translucent fossilised resin produced by extinct coniferous trees, typically yellowish in colour and used in jewellery. A yellowish-orange colour resembling this resin. In traffic signals, the yellow-orange light that indicates caution.
example_sentence: The ancient insect was perfectly preserved inside a piece of amber millions of years old. She wore an amber necklace that contrasted beautifully with her dark skin. The traffic lights changed to amber, signalling that the green would soon follow. The amber glow of the streetlights gave the old city a warm and atmospheric quality. Scientists extracted DNA from an insect trapped in amber and made a remarkable discovery.

english_meaning: A person who can perform tasks such as writing, throwing, or using tools with both the right hand and the left hand with equal skill. It can also describe someone who adapts easily in different situations or uses different methods effectively.
antonyms: ["One handed","Inflexible","Clumsy","Unskilled with the left hand or right hand"]
example_sentence: She is ambidextrous and can write with either hand. The surgeon is ambidextrous, which helps during complex operations. Being ambidextrous allowed the athlete to throw from both sides. His ambidextrous skills made him very efficient at many manual tasks.

english_meaning: The character, feeling, or mood of a place or environment. The atmosphere or overall feeling of a place, including its surroundings, lighting, sound, and general mood that affect people’s experiences or emotions.
example_sentence: The restaurant's soft music and candlelight gave it a romantic ambience. The restaurant has a cozy ambience that makes you feel at home. The peaceful ambience of the library helped me concentrate. Soft music added to the romantic ambience of the evening. The hotel lobby’s elegant ambience impressed the guests.

english_meaning: Surrounding or existing in the environment. Relating to the atmosphere or conditions around something. Often used to describe sound, light, or general environmental conditions that are present but not dominant.
example_sentence: The ambient light in the room created a relaxing mood. She enjoys listening to ambient music while studying. Ambient temperatures were unusually high this summer. The ambient noise of the city made it hard to concentrate.

english_meaning: The state of having more than one possible meaning. The state of being difficult understand, explain due to involvement of many aspects.
example_sentence: You must understand the ambiguity of my position. Write clear definition to avoid ambiguities. There were several inconsistencies & ambiguities in her speech.

english_meaning: Having more than one possible meaning. Not clear or uncertain. Used for a word, sentence, idea, or situation that can be understood in different ways. It creates confusion because the exact meaning is not clearly expressed.
example_sentence: The teacher said the question was ambiguous, so many students answered it differently. His reply was ambiguous, and nobody understood his real opinion. The law contains ambiguous language that lawyers interpret in different ways. Her facial expression was ambiguous, so it was hard to tell if she was happy or upset.

english_meaning: In a way that is unclear or open to more than one interpretation. Something expressed so that its exact meaning is uncertain or confusing.
example_sentence: The witness answered the question ambiguously, which confused the court. The instructions were written ambiguously, so many people misunderstood them. He spoke ambiguously about his future plans. The politician responded ambiguously to avoid giving a direct answer.

english_meaning: Attracted to both men and women. A person who feels romantic or sexual attraction toward people of both sexes or genders. It can also describe someone whose feelings or behavior show attraction to both males and females.
example_sentence: The character in the novel is described as ambisexual, showing attraction to both men and women. Some researchers use the word ambisexual when discussing human sexuality. He openly talked about being ambisexual during the interview. The film explores the life of an ambisexual artist and the relationships he forms.

english_meaning: Something that you want to do or achieve very much. The desire or strength of mind to be successful, rich, powerful, etc. A strong wish to achieve something.
example_sentence:
He has already achieved his main ambition in life - to become wealthy. She was intelligent but suffered from a lack of ambition.
 Her ambition is to start her own business. We are looking for someone with drive and ambition.

english_meaning: A person who strongly wants to accomplish something important in life. Such a person usually works hard, sets clear goals, and tries to improve their position, skills, or achievements. The word can also describe plans or projects that require great effort and determination.
example_sentence: She is an ambitious student who wants to become a scientist. The company launched an ambitious project to expand internationally. His ambitious nature helped him achieve great success in business. They set ambitious goals for improving education in rural areas.

english_meaning: In a way that requires a lot of effort, money or time. In a way that shows you are determined to be successful, rich, powerful, etc. In a way that needs great skill and effort to be successful or be achieved.
example_sentence:
she pursued her goals ambitiously. ‘Time's Arrow’ is Amis's most ambitiously structured novel. Rosalie marries ambitiously and unhappily. I ambitiously embroidered a mountain scene on a jacket when I was only 13.
The museum unveiled the ambitiously designed exhibit on Tuesday.

english_meaning: Having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something or someone. It means you are unsure or have two opposing feelings at the same time. A person may like and dislike something simultaneously, making it difficult to decide or take a clear position.
example_sentence: She felt ambivalent about moving to a new city because she liked her current job but wanted a change. He was ambivalent about the proposal, unsure whether it was a good opportunity or a risk. Many people feel ambivalent about technology, appreciating its benefits but worrying about its impact. I am ambivalent about the movie; some parts were great, but others were boring.

english_meaning: To walk at a slow, relaxed, and unhurried pace, usually for pleasure. To stroll gently without any particular destination or urgency. A leisurely walk taken to enjoy surroundings or for light exercise. To move with ease and without rushing, taking in the environment. A comfortable and pleasant walk, often in a natural or scenic setting.
example_sentence: They decided to amble through the park on a sunny Sunday morning. She ambled along the beach, enjoying the sound of the waves. After dinner, the family took an amble around the neighborhood. He ambled across the garden, lost in his own thoughts. The old man ambled slowly down the quiet village road.

english_meaning: Extremely pleasing in taste or smell. Something that tastes or smells wonderfully delicious and sweet, often linked to food, fragrance, or an experience that feels heavenly.
example_sentence: The ambrosial aroma of fresh coffee filled the room. She prepared an ambrosial dessert for the guests. The garden was full of ambrosial scents after the rain. He described the dish as ambrosial and unforgettable.

english_meaning: To make a surprise attack on somebody or something from a hidden position. To suddenly attack someone after hiding and waiting for them. The act of hiding and waiting for somebody and then making a surprise attack on them.
example_sentence: The guerrillas ambushed them near the bridge. She was ambushed by reporters. Five soldiers died after their bus was ambushed on a country road. He was ambushed by gunmen on his way to work. Several passers-by were killed in the ambush. Fear of ambush prevents the police from going to high-risk areas. The soldiers lay in ambush, their guns loaded. Two soldiers were killed in a terrorist ambush.

english_meaning: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better. To improve. To enhance. To relieve. To make a difficult situation more tolerable. Used in formal contexts to refer to actions that reduce suffering, hardship, or problems and bring about a better condition.
example_sentence: The new policies are designed to ameliorate the living conditions of the poor. Doctors prescribed medicine to ameliorate the patient's pain. The government took several steps to ameliorate the economic crisis. The teacher tried to ameliorate the student's anxiety before the exam. Modern technology has helped to ameliorate many problems in agriculture.

english_meaning: The act of making something better or improving a bad condition. A gradual improvement in quality, comfort, or circumstances. In language study, the change of a word's meaning to a more favourable sense.
example_sentence: The scheme aims at the amelioration of rural poverty. Slow amelioration of the soil increased the yield. Doctors reported an amelioration in his condition. Amelioration has turned many once-negative words into praise.

english_meaning: Open and willing to suggestion, guidance, or persuasion. Responsive to reason, direction, or another's wishes without resistance. Easy to manage, work with, or influence in a positive way. Capable of being brought into agreement or compliance. Willing to submit to a rule, authority, or request without objection. Disposed to accept control, correction, or instruction without difficulty.
example_sentence: She was amenable to changing the plan if it improved outcomes. The team was amenable to the manager's new approach. He was amenable to any suggestions that could help solve the problem. The suspect was amenable to answering the investigator's questions. Children are often more amenable when they feel heard and respected.

english_meaning: A minor change or improvement made to a document, law, or agreement. A formal alteration to a constitution, contract, or bill. The act of correcting or improving something. A revision made to make a text more accurate or effective. A change proposed or made to a motion during a meeting.
example_sentence: The parliament passed an important amendment to the law. She suggested an amendment to the draft contract. The First Amendment protects freedom of speech. A small amendment made the policy much clearer.

english_meaning: A feature or service that makes a place pleasant, comfortable or easy to live in. Something, such as a swimming pool or shopping center, that is intended to make life more pleasant or comfortable for the people in a town, hotel, or other place. Any feature that provides comfort, convenience, or pleasure.
example_sentence: The campsite is close to all local amenities. Many of the houses lacked even basic amenities (= baths, showers, hot water, etc). The council has some spare cash, which it proposes to spend on public amenities. The 200-year-old jail is overcrowded, understaffed, and lacking in basic amenities. Straus established employee amenities such as restrooms, medical care, and a lunchroom. The hotel's rooms are functional, incorporating all the basic amenities but no more.

english_meaning: A violet or purple variety of quartz used as a precious or semi-precious gemstone. A gemstone prized for its beautiful purple hue, ranging from pale lilac to deep violet. Historically associated with sobriety and clarity of thought in ancient cultures. February's birthstone, valued both ornamentally and for its supposed healing properties. A crystalline mineral used extensively in jewelry and decorative objects.
example_sentence: She wore a beautiful amethyst pendant at the ceremony. Amethyst is the birthstone for the month of February. The jeweler displayed a stunning collection of amethyst rings. Ancient Greeks believed amethyst could prevent drunkenness. The amethyst crystal caught the light and glowed with purple brilliance.

english_meaning: Pleasant, friendly and easy to like. Having or showing pleasant, good-natured personal qualities. Having an easygoing and pleasing manner especially in social situations.
example_sentence: The owner of the inn is an amiable, talkative widow who treats guests like family. Her parents seemed very amiable. So amiable was the mood of the meeting that a decision was soon reached. He was amiable and charming, and he possessed an ability to make people feel comfortable in his presence.

english_meaning: Friendly, peaceable, or showing goodwill. Behavior, relationships, or interactions characterized by friendliness, cooperation, or absence of conflict. Often used to describe settlements, discussions, or agreements where parties are polite and cooperative.
example_sentence: They reached an amicable agreement after long negotiations. Despite the disagreement, their divorce was amicable. The meeting ended on an amicable note.  We had an amicable discussion about the project challenges.

english_meaning: In a friendly or peaceful manner. Acting or resolving a situation in a way that is friendly, cooperative, and without conflict or hostility. Often used in the context of agreements, discussions, or separations.
example_sentence: They settled the dispute amicably without going to court. The neighbors resolved their differences amicably. The two companies parted amicably after the contract ended. We discussed the issue amicably and reached a solution.

english_meaning: In the middle of something. Surrounded by something. Used to show that something happens in the center of a situation, place, or group of things. It often describes being surrounded by events, people, noise, problems, or conditions.
example_sentence: The village remained calm amid heavy rainfall. She found her friend amid a large crowd at the market. The meeting continued amid loud protests outside the building. The flowers grew beautifully amid the green grass.

english_meaning: In the midst or middle of, surrounded or encompassed by
example_sentence: The Trump administration is formulating its North Korea policy amidst accelerating threats and deteriorating relations in the region.

english_meaning: Friendly relationship. A peaceful and friendly relationship between people, groups, or countries where there is goodwill, harmony, and mutual respect. It often describes cooperation and absence of conflict.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a treaty to promote amity and cooperation. The community festival helped build amity among people from different cultures. Years of honest dialogue created amity between the neighboring villages. Leaders encouraged amity so that social tensions could be reduced.

english_meaning: An instrument that measures electric current in amperes, normally connected in series with the circuit being measured.
example_sentence: The technician connected the ammeter to measure the current in the wire. A faulty ammeter can give inaccurate readings. The dashboard ammeter showed that the battery was charging. Students used an ammeter in the physics lab to test a simple circuit.

english_meaning: An informal shortened form of ammunition. Bullets, shells, cartridges, or other material fired from weapons. Information, evidence, or arguments that can be used to criticize someone or strengthen a position.
example_sentence: The soldiers checked their ammo before leaving the base. The hunter stored his ammo in a locked cabinet. Her research gave her plenty of ammo for the debate. The leaked documents provided critics with fresh ammo.

english_meaning: A colourless gas with a strong, sharp smell, made of nitrogen and hydrogen (NH3). A solution of this gas in water, used as a household cleaner. A chemical widely used to make fertilisers, plastics, and explosives.
example_sentence: The strong smell of ammonia filled the cleaning cupboard. Ammonia is an important raw material for making fertiliser. Never mix ammonia with bleach, as it releases toxic fumes. The factory was closed after a small ammonia leak.

english_meaning: An extinct marine mollusk with a coiled, chambered shell, common as a fossil in rocks from the Mesozoic Era. The fossilized shell or remains of this animal. A member of an ancient Semitic people whose kingdom lay east of the Jordan River.
example_sentence: The museum displayed a large ammonite fossil from the Jurassic Period. We found the imprint of an ammonite in the limestone. The ammonite's spiral shell fascinated the young geologist. The ancient Ammonites lived east of the Jordan River.

english_meaning: A positively charged ion formed from ammonia by adding a hydrogen ion (NH4+). A group found in many salts and chemical compounds used in fertilisers, medicines, and cleaning products.
example_sentence: Ammonium nitrate is widely used as an agricultural fertiliser. The teacher explained how ammonium ions form in water. Some cough syrups contain ammonium chloride. Farmers applied ammonium sulphate to improve the soil.

english_meaning: Bullets, shells, bombs, or other materials used in weapons. Also information or ideas used to support an argument.
example_sentence: The soldiers checked their ammunition before the mission. The hunter ran out of ammunition during the trip. The journalist gathered facts as ammunition for the debate. His research gave him strong ammunition against criticism.

english_meaning: Loss of memory, either partially or completely. Forgetfulness due to shock or trauma. Inability to recall information. A medical condition in which a person loses the ability to remember past events, facts, or even personal identity. It can be temporary or permanent and may result from injury, illness, stress, or trauma.
example_sentence: After the accident, he suffered from amnesia and could not recognize his family. The patient experienced temporary amnesia after the surgery. Emotional trauma can sometimes lead to amnesia. She woke up with amnesia and had no memory of her past life.

english_meaning: A person who suffers from memory loss. A person unable to recall important personal information. Someone with partial or complete memory loss. Used figuratively for someone who forgets things easily. A person affected by amnesia, a condition in which someone loses the ability to remember past events, information, or even personal identity. It can be temporary or permanent and is often caused by injury, illness, or psychological trauma. As an adjective, it describes anything related to memory loss.
example_sentence: After the accident, he became an amnesiac and could not recognize his family. The movie tells the story of an amnesiac trying to recover his past. The doctor treated the amnesiac with specialized therapy. She acted like an amnesiac when asked about the incident.

english_meaning: A general pardon granted to offenders, especially political prisoners. A period during which people can admit an offense without punishment, such as tax amnesty. Forgiveness granted to a group rather than an individual.
example_sentence: The government declared amnesty for political prisoners after the peace agreement. Thousands of immigrants applied for amnesty to legalize their status. The king granted amnesty to rebels who agreed to lay down their weapons. The tax department announced a short amnesty period for people to pay unpaid taxes.

english_meaning: In a frenzied, uncontrolled, or wildly destructive manner. Running wildly with little or no regard for others' safety. Acting in a violently out-of-control way due to extreme emotion or mental disturbance. In a state of chaos, confusion, or reckless action. A term borrowed from Malay describing a sudden violent, murderous frenzy.
example_sentence: The frightened bull ran amok through the crowded market. Rumors ran amok after the announcement was made. A rioter ran amok and destroyed several cars. The escaped elephant ran amok in the village causing widespread panic. He went amok when he discovered his belongings had been stolen.

english_meaning: Lacking any moral principles or standards of right and wrong. Not concerned with or governed by moral considerations. Having no ethical judgment or moral code to guide behavior. Indifferent to whether actions are morally right or wrong. Existing outside or beyond the framework of moral reasoning. Not to be confused with immoral; amoral means without morality rather than against it.
example_sentence: The corporation made amoral decisions motivated purely by profit. His amoral attitude toward others alarmed many of his friends. She grew up in an environment that promoted an amoral worldview. The documentary explored the amoral nature of war. An amoral person does not consider right or wrong in their actions.

english_meaning: Showing or expressing love or sexual desire. Feelings, actions, or expressions of romantic or sexual affection. Often used to describe someone who is fond of love or inclined toward romantic relationships.
example_sentence: He wrote an amorous letter to his beloved. The couple exchanged amorous glances at the party. She smiled in an amorous way, showing her affection. The poem was filled with amorous imagery.

english_meaning: To gradually pay off a debt or cost over a period of time. To gradually reduce or extinguish a debt by regular payments. To write off an intangible asset’s cost over its useful life in accounting. To spread an expense over a period to match revenue or financial planning. To lessen the impact of a financial obligation gradually.
example_sentence: The company plans to amortize its equipment purchase over five years. Homeowners often amortize their mortgage to make payments manageable. The software cost was amortized over its expected five-year lifespan. Businesses amortize startup costs gradually to reduce tax burden.

english_meaning: To increase, intensify. To excite, energize, or stimulate people. To strengthen or enhance something.
example_sentence: They amped up the volume at the party. The coach gave a speech to amp up the team. We need to amp up our marketing efforts. The coach amped up the team before the match. They amped up the sound system for the concert. The campaign amped up their efforts to win.

english_meaning: A character or symbol representing the conjunction word and. The specific typographic glyph '&' used in writing and printing. A logogram that originated as a ligature of the letters in the Latin word et. A punctuation mark often used in business names and titles to save space.
example_sentence: The logo of the law firm prominently featured a stylish ampersand between the partners' names. In many programming languages, the ampersand serves as a bitwise operator or a reference indicator. You should use a full word in formal essays instead of an ampersand. The graphic designer adjusted the kerning around the ampersand to improve the layout's balance.

english_meaning: An animal that can live both on land and in water, relating to creatures that can survive in both environments. Cold-blooded vertebrates that typically begin life in water with gills and undergo metamorphosis to develop lungs for breathing on land. Common examples include frogs, toads, and salamanders. The term can also describe vehicles or objects capable of operating on both land and water.
example_sentence: The frog is a well-known amphibian. Salamanders are fascinating amphibians that can regenerate limbs. Some military vehicles are amphibians and can move on land and water. The pond is home to several types of amphibians.

english_meaning: More than enough in quantity, scope, or capacity; generously sufficient. Large, wide, or spacious in size or extent. Plentiful and more than adequate for the purpose. Describing a situation, resource, or space that satisfies a need without scarcity. Having a generous or abundant quality that exceeds minimal requirements.
example_sentence: There was ample time to prepare for the presentation. The room provided ample space for all the guests. She had ample evidence to support her claims. The organization had ample funds to carry out its mission. The recipe calls for ample amounts of garlic and herbs.

english_meaning: An electronic device that increases the strength of a signal or sound. A piece of audio equipment used to make music or speech louder. Anything that increases the intensity or effect of something.
example_sentence: He plugged his guitar into the amplifier. The old amplifier began to hum during the concert. Social media can act as an amplifier of rumours. They bought a powerful amplifier for the hall.

english_meaning: To increase the volume, strength, or intensity of a sound, signal, or effect. To make something larger, greater, or more noticeable than it originally was. To expand on a statement or idea by adding more detail or explanation. Used in electronics to describe increasing the power of an electrical signal.
example_sentence: The speakers were used to amplify the singer's voice across the stadium.  Social media has the power to amplify both positive and negative messages quickly.  The professor asked the student to amplify her argument with more examples.  The device amplifies weak radio signals so they can be clearly received.  Her concerns were amplified by the lack of communication from management.

english_meaning: To cut off a limb or part of the body, usually by surgery. To remove a damaged or diseased body part for medical reasons. Figuratively, to cut off or remove a part of something.
example_sentence: Surgeons had to amputate his left leg below the knee. The infection spread so fast that doctors amputated the finger. He learned to walk again after the amputated limb healed. Editors amputated the final chapter from the book.

english_meaning: A small object, charm, or piece of jewelry worn, usually around the neck because people believe it will protect them from evil, harm, illness, or bad luck.
example_sentence: She wore an amulet around her neck to protect herself from evil spirits. In many cultures, a baby is given an amulet for good luck and safety. The soldier carried an amulet in his pocket as a sign of faith. The ancient Egyptians believed that amulets brought health and prosperity.

english_meaning: To have a personal reason, hidden motive, or selfish interest behind one’s actions or opinions. Having a personal motive or selfish reason.
example_sentence: He supported the plan because he had an axe to grind. He supported the new policy because he had an axe to grind. Don’t trust his advice; he has an axe to grind. She joined the committee with an axe to grind, hoping for a promotion. It seemed like the journalist had an axe to grind against the mayor.

english_meaning: To have a very strong memory, someone who never forgets things, even after a long time.
example_sentence: She never forgets dates; she has an elephant memory. My grandmother has an elephant memory she remembers stories from her childhood in detail. He has an elephant memory for names; he never forgets anyone he meets. Teachers say she has an elephant memory because she recalls every lesson perfectly. Be careful what you say, he has an elephant memory and won’t forget it!.

english_meaning: A thing that is itself important and not just a part of something more important. Something valued for its own sake, not as a way to achieve something else.
synonyms: ["Goal in itself","Self sufficient purpose","Intrinsic goal","Purpose in its own right"]
antonyms: ["Means to an end","Instrumental goal","Stepping stone","Tool for something else"]
example_sentence:
For her, shopping had become an end in itself.
For him, travelling had become an end in itself rather than a means of seeing new places. For her, learning music is an end in itself, not a way to earn money. He believes education should be an end in itself, not just job training. Exercise became an end in itself rather than a means to lose weight. The artist paints as an end in itself, not to gain fame or profit.

word: An idle brain is the devil's workshop
english_meaning: When a person stays idle without useful work, negative, harmful, or foolish thoughts often enter the mind. Idleness often causes negative thinking. Staying busy helps avoid bad habits. Productive activities keep the mind healthy. Free time without purpose may lead to trouble
synonyms: ["Laziness leads to trouble","Idleness breeds mischief","Busy hands keep the mind clean"]
antonyms: ["Hard work leads to success","Keep yourself busy in useful activities","Productivity brings positivity"]
example_sentence: My parents always encourage me to stay busy because an idle brain is the devil's workshop. During the holidays, Ali started getting into trouble since an idle brain is the devil's workshop. Teachers give students creative assignments because an idle brain is the devil's workshop. He began learning computer skills to avoid wasting time, knowing that an idle brain is the devil's workshop.

english_meaning: An idiom meaning a strong desire for money. Greed or eagerness to accept bribes. A grasping, money-loving nature. Used to describe someone easily tempted by financial gain.
example_sentence: Shakespeare accuses Cassius of having an itching palm. The clerk has an itching palm and delays every file. Officials with an itching palm damage public trust. Do not deal with a man who has an itching palm.

english_meaning: Someone who speaks very smoothly, politely, or flatteringly, often to deceive, manipulate, or gain favor. It refers to a person who uses sweet or flattering words to achieve their purpose rather than being sincere.
example_sentence: He got the promotion because of his oily tongue, not his hard work. Don’t trust his oily tongue, he says what people want to hear. With an oily tongue, he convinced everyone to support his plan. Her oily tongue hides her true intentions.

english_meaning: Belonging to or resembling a period other than the one in which it exists. Historically misplaced or inconsistent with a particular time. Outdated and no longer suitable for present conditions.
example_sentence: The film's wristwatch was an anachronistic detail in a medieval scene. Some people consider the rule anachronistic today. Using a typewriter in that modern office felt anachronistic. The play deliberately included anachronistic references for comic effect.

english_meaning: A rhetorical device in which the last word of one clause is repeated at the beginning of the next. Repetition that links one phrase or sentence to another. A technique used to create emphasis and continuity. A chain-like form of verbal repetition.
example_sentence: Fear leads to anger, anger leads to hate is an example of anadiplosis. The speaker used anadiplosis to connect each idea. Anadiplosis gives a sentence a rolling rhythm. The class found anadiplosis in the political speech.

english_meaning: A medical condition characterized by a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin in the blood. It results in reduced oxygen flow to the body's organs, causing symptoms like fatigue, paleness, and weakness. It is often caused by an iron deficiency.
example_sentence: Her constant fatigue and paleness were eventually diagnosed as severe anaemia. Eating iron-rich foods like spinach and liver can help prevent anaemia. The doctor prescribed a daily iron supplement to treat his anaemia. Heavy blood loss during the surgery resulted in temporary anaemia. Pregnant women are routinely checked and tested for signs of anaemia.

english_meaning: Occurring or living without oxygen. A process, organism, or condition that does not require oxygen to function or survive. It is commonly used in biology, chemistry, and exercise science
example_sentence: Some bacteria can only live in anaerobic conditions. Beneficial anaerobic filter bacteria require oxygen to oxidise nitrites to safer nitrates. Like anaerobic digestion, the aerobic processing of waste material produces methane which can be used as a biogas fuel.

english_meaning: The loss of feeling or sensation in the body, especially loss of pain, caused by drugs before surgery. The medical practice of making a patient insensitive to pain during an operation. A condition in which a person cannot feel touch, pain, or temperature in part or all of the body.
example_sentence: The patient was given anaesthesia before the operation began. Modern anaesthesia has made surgery far safer than before. She felt no pain because the anaesthesia was working well. The doctor explained the risks of general anaesthesia to the family.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specialises in giving anaesthesia and caring for patients before, during, and after surgery. A physician trained in pain management and in monitoring a patient's vital functions during an operation.
example_sentence: The anaesthesiologist explained the procedure before the surgery. A skilled anaesthesiologist monitored the patient throughout the operation. She trained for years to become an anaesthesiologist. The anaesthesiologist adjusted the dose according to the patient's weight.

english_meaning: A drug or substance that causes loss of feeling or awareness, used before surgery or painful treatment. Relating to or producing a loss of sensation. Something that dulls pain or numbs the senses.
example_sentence: The dentist used a local anaesthetic before removing the tooth. He was still drowsy from the anaesthetic. The anaesthetic effect wore off after about an hour. She was given a general anaesthetic for the operation.

english_meaning: A doctor or trained medical professional who administers anaesthetics to patients. A specialist responsible for keeping a patient free of pain and stable during surgery.
example_sentence: The anaesthetist gave the injection a few minutes before surgery. A senior anaesthetist supervised the entire procedure. The anaesthetist asked whether he had any allergies. Hospitals in the district are short of trained anaesthetists.

english_meaning: A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase. A word puzzle based on rearranging letters. The result of shuffling letters to create a new meaningful word.
example_sentence: The word 'listen' is an anagram of 'silent'. He enjoys solving anagrams in the weekend newspaper. Her pen name is an anagram of her real name. The teacher used anagrams to make spelling practice fun.

english_meaning: Relating to or based on analogy, that is, on similarity between two different things. Explaining or reasoning by comparing one situation with another that resembles it. Involving a comparison that helps make an idea easier to understand. In linguistics, describing a change in word form produced by the influence of similar words.
example_sentence: He used an analogical argument to explain the theory. Analogical reasoning is common in legal judgments. The professor drew an analogical comparison between cells and factories. Children often learn grammar through analogical patterns.

english_meaning: Having similar features to another thing and therefore able to be compared with it. Similar in some way to another thing or situation and therefore able to be compared with it.
example_sentence: Sleep has often been thought of as being in some way analogous to death. The two processes are not analogous. The national debt is analogous with private debt. The two situations are roughly analogous. The experience of mystic trance is in a sense analogous to sleep or drunkenness. The emergency vehicle for the International Space Station is analogous to a lifeboat.

english_meaning: A comparison of one thing with another thing that has similar features, a feature that is similar. The process of comparing one thing with another thing that has similar features in order to explain it. A way of describing or explaining one thing by means of describing another with which it shares certain points or qualities.
example_sentence: The teacher drew an analogy between the human heart and a pump. There are no analogies with any previous legal cases. We can understand this theory by analogy with human beings.

english_meaning: To examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it. To treat or study somebody using psychoanalysis. To study or examine something in detail in order to discover or understand more about it. To separate (a thing, idea, etc) into its parts so as to find out their nature, proportion, function, interrelationship, etc
example_sentence:
The job involves collecting and analysing data.
Researchers have analysed the results in detail using specialist software. Learn to step back and critically analyse situations. He tried to analyse his feelings. The first step is to define and analyse the problem. The water samples will be analysed for the presence of polluting chemicals. We need to analyse what went wrong.

english_meaning: The detailed study or examination of something in order to understand more about it, the result of the study. A careful examination of a substance in order to find out what it consists of. The act of examining a substance, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to discover what it is or contains.
example_sentence: Further analysis revealed significant regional variations in the results. We made the decision based on our analysis of the situation. The blood samples are sent to the laboratory for analysis. You can ask for a chemical analysis of your tap water. In analysis the individual resolves difficult emotional conflicts. The forensic lab carried out a second analysis of the DNA sample Analysis is also a short form of psychoanalysis. What's your analysis of the current economic crisis?

english_meaning: A person who studies or examines information carefully to understand it or make decisions. Someone skilled in examining data, trends, situations, or problems, often providing insights, interpretations, or recommendations based on systematic evaluation. Analysts are found in fields like finance, science, politics, sports, and technology.
example_sentence: He's a senior research analyst at Deutsche Bank. City analysts forecast huge profits this year. According to music industry analysts, music downloads are set to decline by as much as 30 per cent this year. Most financial analysts have been surprised by the persistence of the recession. Many analysts are predicting an upswing in the economy.

english_meaning: A method or ability to study a subject by separating it into components in order to understand its structure, causes, or relationships. Often used in science, mathematics, research, and critical thinking.
example_sentence: She has an analytic mind that helps her solve complex problems. The researcher used an analytic approach to study climate data. His analytic skills are valuable in policy planning. Mathematics often requires analytic thinking to understand formulas.

english_meaning: Relating to careful examination of something by breaking it into parts. A person or method that studies facts, data, ideas, or problems step by step in order to understand how they work and to reach logical conclusions.
example_sentence: She has an analytical mind and solves complex problems quickly. The researcher used an analytical approach to study climate data. His analytical skills helped the team understand the cause of the failure. Teachers encourage students to develop analytical thinking in science classes.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to analysis or logical examination. Doing something by carefully examining the components, understanding the structure, and evaluating relationships to reach a logical conclusion. Often used in thinking, problem-solving, or studying data.
example_sentence: Equations of motion for the water atoms were solved analytically. Tests that measure children’s ability to think analytically are being introduced in a number of schools. The research is analytically rigorous sloppy. Some people are better than others at thinking analytically.

part_of_speech: Specialist, Expert, Evaluator, Examiner, Commentator, Researcher
english_meaning: The study of data to understand patterns, trends, and insights. The systematic computational analysis of information or data. It involves examining raw data to draw conclusions, make decisions, and predict outcomes. Often used in business, science, and technology to optimize processes and strategies.
example_sentence: Web analytics tracks and reports visitors’ behaviour when they click into a website. The company concentrates on customer analytics, analyzing data on customers to understand their wants and needs. ‘More lenders will participate on the sites and the analytics will continue to improve,’ he says. This technology provides detailed analytics about campaign reach. Analytics on a restaurant's and user's profiles show many meals have been donated.

english_meaning: To examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it. To treat or study somebody using psychoanalysis. To study or examine something in detail in order to discover or understand more about it. To separate (a thing, idea, etc) into its parts so as to find out their nature, proportion, function, interrelationship, etc
example_sentence: In the article, several experienced diplomats analyzed the president’s foreign policy. Joe had never tried to analyze their relationship. We should learn to discern and analyze the essentials of complicated questions.

english_meaning: Repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses or sentences. A literary device in which a word or phrase is repeated at the start of consecutive sentences, clauses, or lines to create emphasis or rhythm in speech or writing.
antonyms: ["None directly","But lack of repetition or variation could be considered opposite in effect"]
example_sentence: Anaphora is one of the most striking features of texts. Every day, every night, in every way, I am getting better. We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields. With malice toward none, with charity for all, with firmness in the right. I have a dream that one day… I have a dream that my four little children….

english_meaning: A state of disorder due to absence of authority or government. A situation in which there is no effective government, law, or order, leading to chaos, confusion, and lack of control.
example_sentence: The overthrow of the military regime was followed by a period of anarchy. There was complete anarchy in the classroom when their usual teacher was away. Anarchy can emerge when social institutions fail to function properly. The collapse of the regime led to complete anarchy in the city.

english_meaning: Something or someone that is strongly disliked or hated. A formal curse or ban imposed by a church. A person or thing regarded as cursed or detested. An idea or practice that one completely opposes.
example_sentence: Cruelty to animals is anathema to her gentle nature. The corrupt leader became anathema to the whole nation. The church declared the practice anathema centuries ago. Dishonesty is anathema to his character.

english_meaning: Relating to the physical structure of the body or an organism. Pertaining to the science of anatomy or the arrangement of bodily parts. Connected with the study of how the organs, bones, and tissues of living creatures are organized. Describing features or characteristics defined by the body's structural organization. Of or relating to the internal structure of a living thing as studied scientifically.
example_sentence: The medical student studied the anatomical structure of the human brain. Anatomical models helped students visualize the skeletal system. The surgeon required precise anatomical knowledge to perform the operation. The anatomical differences between species were studied in detail. He drew anatomical sketches of the human body for his art class.

english_meaning: The scientific study of the structure and arrangement of the parts of living organisms. The branch of biology dealing with the form and structure of the body. The physical structure of an organism as revealed through dissection and examination. A detailed analysis or breakdown of something complex, used metaphorically. The subject area concerned with bones, muscles, organs, and their relationships within living bodies.
example_sentence: Students of medicine study anatomy in their first year. The anatomy of a frog and a human share some surprising similarities. She passed her anatomy examination with excellent marks. The professor used detailed diagrams to teach the anatomy of the heart. Understanding anatomy is essential for any healthcare professional.

english_meaning: A person in family who lived a long time ago. Animal in the past which a modern has developed from. An early form of machine later become more developed.
example_sentence: His ancestors had come to America from Ireland. A reptile that was the common ancestor of lizards & turtles. The ancestor of modern bicycle was called a penny-farthing

english_meaning: The lineage or descent of a person tracing back through family history. One's family background and the series of ancestors from whom one is descended. The ethnic, national, or social heritage passed down through generations. A person's family tree and its historical, cultural, and biological roots. The collective history of a family line that shapes identity and heritage.
example_sentence: She took great pride in her mixed ancestry. DNA tests can reveal surprising details about one's ancestry. He researched his ancestry and discovered links to several countries. Her ancestry on her father's side traced back to West Africa. Understanding your ancestry can deepen your sense of identity.

english_meaning: A heavy metal attached to a rope, chain & dropped over the side of ship to keep in one place. To fix firmly in position, to secure, or to serve as a mainstay. To be person who reads news on TV or Radio.
example_sentence: The ship dropped its anchor near the harbor. She is the anchor of our family, always keeping us grounded. The journalist anchored the live broadcast from the studio. He anchored the tent firmly into the ground.

english_meaning: History that is 1000 years in the past. Dating or surviving from the distant past. Having had an existence of many years
example_sentence: The area where market was anciently held. Rome's ancient ruins remain carefully preserved even in the midst of the bustle of the modern city

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of men. A person with androphobia experiences extreme anxiety, discomfort, or panic in the presence of or when thinking about men.
example_sentence: She developed androphobia after years of abuse. Her androphobia made it difficult to work in a male-dominated office. Androphobia is often linked to past trauma or violence. With therapy, she gradually overcame her androphobia.

english_meaning: A condition in which the blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells. A deficiency in hemoglobin causing reduced oxygen delivery to tissues. A blood disorder characterized by fatigue, weakness, and pale skin. A medical condition resulting from insufficient iron, vitamins, or chronic disease.
synonyms: ["Blood deficiency","Low hemoglobin","Iron deficiency","Red blood cell deficiency"]
antonyms: ["Normal blood count","Healthy hemoglobin","Adequate red blood cells"]
example_sentence: Iron deficiency anemia is the most common type. She was diagnosed with severe anemia. Anemia can cause extreme fatigue. Eating iron-rich foods helps prevent anemia.

english_meaning: A condition in which the body fails to react to an antigen. Lack of energy. Reduction or lack of an immune response to a specific antigen. A condition in which the body's immune system fails to react to an antigen.
example_sentence: The patient showed anergy to the standard vaccine. After working all night, he felt anergy throughout the day. Some immune cells may enter a state of anergy to prevent overreaction. The long meeting left everyone in a state of anergy.

english_meaning: A temporary state of controlled unconsciousness or insensitivity to pain. The medical procedure of administering drugs to dull or remove physical sensation. A loss of feeling or awareness caused by injury or illness. A state of numbness or lack of sensation in a specific part of the body. The branch of medicine concerned with the administration of anesthetic agents.
example_sentence: The patient was placed under general anesthesia before the operation began. Local anesthesia was used to numb the area around the tooth extraction. Modern anesthesia has made complex surgical procedures much safer for patients. She experienced a strange sense of anesthesia in her fingers after the accident.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specializes in anesthesia and pain management during surgery. A physician who administers medications to prevent pain and monitors patients during operations. A specialist in perioperative care and critical care medicine.
example_sentence: The anesthesiologist put the patient to sleep before surgery. She works as an anesthesiologist in the operating room. The anesthesiologist monitored vital signs during the procedure. Anesthesiologists ensure patient safety during operations.

english_meaning: To make a person or animal unable to feel pain by giving them a drug. To administer an anesthetic before a medical or surgical procedure. To deaden feeling or sensation in a part of the body. To make someone emotionally numb or insensitive to something.
example_sentence: The surgeon decided to anesthetize the patient before the operation. The dentist anesthetized her gum before removing the tooth. Vets must anesthetize large animals with great care. Years of bad news had anesthetized the public to such tragedies.

english_meaning: A spiritual being believed to act as an attendant, agent, or messenger of God. A person of exceptional goodness, purity, or selflessness. A financial backer or investor, especially one who supports a startup or theatrical production. A representation of a heavenly being in art, often shown with wings and a halo. A guardian spirit or protector assigned to a person or place.
example_sentence: She has the voice of an angel and performs with incredible grace. The charity was saved at the last minute by a generous angel investor. Many religions describe Gabriel as a powerful angel who delivers divine messages. My grandmother was an absolute angel who dedicated her life to helping the poor.

english_meaning: A medical imaging technique used to visualize the inside of blood vessels and organs. An X-ray photograph of blood vessels made by injecting a radiopaque contrast agent into the bloodstream. A diagnostic procedure that helps doctors identify blockages or narrowing in the arteries. A clinical record or image produced by angiography to assess heart health or circulation. A specialized test typically performed in a catheterization laboratory to detect cardiovascular diseases.
antonyms: ["Physical Exam","External Palpation","Visual Inspection","Surface Observation","Non-diagnostic Procedure","Blind Assessment"]
example_sentence: The cardiologist recommended an angiogram to check for blockages in the patient's coronary arteries. After the angiogram was completed, the doctor explained the results to the family. The procedure involves inserting a catheter to perform the angiogram safely. Modern technology has made the process of getting an angiogram much less invasive than before.

english_meaning: A medical imaging technique used to visualize the inside of blood vessels and organs. An X-ray examination of the blood or lymph vessels, carried out after introduction of a radiopaque substance. A diagnostic procedure to detect blockages, narrowing, or abnormalities in the circulatory system. The process of producing a radiograph of blood vessels. A clinical method to evaluate the health of arteries and veins using contrast media.
example_sentence: The doctor recommended a coronary angiography to check for heart blockages. The patient was prepped for the angiography procedure early in the morning. Angiography provides a clear map of the blood vessels for the surgeons. After the angiography, the results showed a significant narrowing of the artery.

english_meaning: A surgical procedure to widen a narrowed or blocked blood vessel, usually using a small balloon. A treatment that restores normal blood flow, often followed by placing a stent in the artery.
example_sentence: The doctor recommended angioplasty to open the blocked artery. He recovered quickly after a successful angioplasty. Angioplasty is often preferred to open-heart surgery. The hospital performs several angioplasty procedures every day.

english_meaning: To try to get something by hinting, scheming, or using indirect methods, not asking directly, but trying to get it cleverly.
example_sentence: He was angling for a promotion by praising the boss all the time. She kept asking about the project, clearly angling for more information. The journalist was angling for an exclusive interview. I think he’s angling for an invitation to the party. The politician was clearly angling for public sympathy.

english_meaning: Extreme pain, distress, or anxiety. Severe physical or mental pain, difficulty or unhappiness.
example_sentence:
Tears of anguish filled her eyes.
 He suffered the anguish of watching his son go to prison.

english_meaning: Having sharp angles or corners. Lean and bony, with prominent features. Measured by angles rather than distance. Stiff or awkward in movement.
example_sentence: The building has a very angular modern design. He had an angular face with sharp cheekbones. Physics students learn about angular velocity. Her movements were stiff and angular on stage.

english_meaning: Without history or lacking historical record. Something that has no recorded history, no connection to past events, or lacks historical development. It may refer to ideas, cultures, statements, or objects that appear without any traceable background or historical context.
example_sentence: The claim was considered anhistous because no evidence supported it. His view of the culture seemed anhistous and ignored its rich past. The report gave an anhistous perspective on the issue. An anhistous narrative often misleads readers about real events.

english_meaning: Characteristic of or resembling an animal. Driven by basic physical urges rather than reason. Wild. Primitive. Instinctive. Used to describe behaviour, sounds, or feelings that are seen as belonging more to animals than to civilized humans, often involving aggression, passion, fear, or raw physical desire.
example_sentence: He let out an animalistic roar when he won the match. The crowd was driven by an almost animalistic excitement. There was something animalistic in the way he attacked his food. The film shows the animalistic side of human nature. Their fight was savage and animalistic.

english_meaning: To bring something to life or make it lively and active. To produce a film or sequence in which drawings or objects appear to move. To encourage or inspire someone with energy and enthusiasm. Alive or having life, as opposed to inanimate.
example_sentence: A warm smile animated her tired face. The team will animate the characters next month. His speech animated the whole audience. Biology studies both animate and inanimate matter.

english_meaning: Full of life, energy, and enthusiasm. Made using animation techniques so that images appear to move. Lively and expressive in speech or manner. Brought to life or made active.
example_sentence: They had an animated discussion about politics. The children love animated films. Her animated face showed real interest. The animated map explains the journey clearly.

english_meaning: The technique of making drawings or models appear to move on screen. A film or video created by this technique. Liveliness, energy, and enthusiasm in a person's manner. The act of bringing something to life or making it active.
example_sentence: The studio is famous for its hand-drawn animation. Children watched the animation with great excitement. She spoke with animation about her travels. The animation of the logo lasts only two seconds.

english_meaning: Strong feeling of dislike, hatred, or hostility towards someone. Bitter enmity. Active opposition. Deep-rooted resentment. A feeling of anger or hatred between people or groups that can lead to conflict. Used to describe long-lasting and intense negative feelings rather than passing irritation.
example_sentence: There has been deep animosity between the two families for many years. The political rivals showed open animosity during the debate. He felt no animosity towards the man who had once cheated him. The match was played in an atmosphere of mutual animosity. Such old animosity between the tribes is difficult to remove easily.

english_meaning: Strong hostility, hatred, resentment, or ill will toward someone or something. Deep-seated hostility, resentment, hatred, or ill feelings directed toward a person, group, idea, or institution. It often describes a lasting emotional dislike rather than a temporary feeling of anger. The word can also refer to prejudice or bias that influences a person's actions or decisions.
example_sentence: The manager's decision appeared to be driven by personal animus rather than fairness. Despite years of disagreement, she showed no animus toward her former colleague. Political animus often prevents people from working together effectively. His comments revealed deep animus against the new policy.

english_meaning: The joint connecting the foot with the lower leg. The narrow part of the leg just above the foot. The bony area on either side of this joint. The part of a sock, shoe, or trouser that reaches this joint.
example_sentence: She twisted her ankle while running downhill. The doctor wrapped a bandage around his swollen ankle. The water was only ankle deep near the shore. He wore boots that covered his ankles.

english_meaning: A person who writes annals, that is, a record of events arranged year by year. A historian who records events in chronological order without much interpretation. A chronicler of the yearly happenings of a country or institution.
example_sentence: The annalist recorded every important event of the king's reign. Modern historians still rely on the work of that medieval annalist. As the college annalist, she kept a careful record of each session. The annalist wrote plainly, leaving judgement to later readers.

english_meaning: To officially add or attach a territory, building, or room to a larger existing one. To incorporate land or property into a bigger unit by legal or forceful means. An additional structure or section attached to a main building. To seize control of another country or territory and make it part of one's own state.
example_sentence: The government moved to annex the disputed territory after years of negotiation. The hotel built an annex to accommodate more guests during the busy season. The country attempted to annex the neighboring region, which caused international outrage. The library's annex housed a rare book collection not available in the main building. The new annex was used as additional office space for the expanding company.

english_meaning: The formal or forcible incorporation of one territory into another political state. The act of taking control of an area and making it part of another country. A political or military action that extends the boundaries of a state into another region. The process of officially bringing a region under the jurisdiction of an existing government.
example_sentence: The annexation of the region triggered widespread international protests. Historical annexation often resulted in the suppression of local culture and language. The annexation was condemned by several world leaders and international bodies. The legal status of the annexation remains disputed to this day. Forced annexation is a clear violation of international law and human rights.

english_meaning: An additional document attached to a main report, contract, or official paper. A supplement appended to a formal document to provide supporting details or evidence. A separate piece of information added to the end of an official or legal document. An exhibit or attachment referenced within the body of a formal agreement.
example_sentence: Please refer to the annexure at the end of the report for full details. The contract included an annexure clearly outlining the payment terms and conditions. The annexure contained supporting evidence for the claims made in the main document. The legal team reviewed every annexure carefully before signing. All annexures must be signed and initialled before the agreement is considered finalized.

english_meaning: To destroy somebody, something, yourself completely. To defeat somebody, something completely. To destroy something completely so that nothing is left. To defeat completely. To reduce to nothing, to destroy, to eradicate.
example_sentence: The human race has enough weapons to annihilate itself. She annihilated her opponent, who failed to win a single game. A city annihilated by an atomic bomb. The enemy troops were annihilated.

english_meaning: The act of somebody, something being completely destroyed. The complete defeat of somebody, something. The state or fact of being rendered nonexistent, physically unsound, or useless.
example_sentence: The Brazilian needed just 82 minutes to complete the annihilation of his opponent. Humanity is just one misunderstanding, one miscalculation away from nuclear annihilation. They were to surrender immediately or face total annihilation. Annihilation can create gamma - rays or even new particle - antiparticle pairs.

english_meaning: The yearly return of the date of an important past event. A celebration held on the date when something notable happened in an earlier year. The date on which a couple was married, marked each year. A yearly commemoration of a death, founding, or historic occasion.
example_sentence: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in the mountains. The school marked the fiftieth anniversary of its founding. A special ceremony was held on the anniversary of the disaster. She sends him flowers every year on their anniversary.

english_meaning: To add notes, comments, explanations, or marks to a text, document, image, or book for clarification or study. To explain, comment on, highlight, or add informative notes to written material, images, maps, diagrams, or digital content. It is commonly used in education, research, editing, programming, and document review.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the students to annotate the poem with important notes. Researchers annotate scientific articles to explain difficult terms. She annotated the document before sending it to her manager. The editor annotated the manuscript with correction marks and comments.

english_meaning: Having been provided with critical or explanatory notes. A text that includes additional comments, definitions, or explanations added by an editor or scholar.
example_sentence: She studied an annotated version of the novel for her exam. The annotated bibliography listed all sources with brief descriptions. He submitted an annotated copy of the contract to his lawyer. The annotated manuscript revealed new insights into the author's intentions.

english_meaning: A note, comment, explanation, or remark added to a text, image, document, or diagram to give extra information or clarification. An additional note or comment attached to written material, books, articles, images, maps, or digital documents for explanation, interpretation, clarification, or analysis. Annotations are commonly used in education, research, literature, programming, and document editing.
example_sentence: The teacher added annotations to the student's essay to explain the mistakes. Researchers often use annotations in academic articles for clarification. The map contained annotations showing important historical locations. She wrote annotations in the margins of her favorite novel while studying it.

english_meaning: A person who adds explanatory notes, comments, or critical remarks to a text or document. Someone who annotates written material to provide additional context or clarity.
example_sentence: The annotator added footnotes to explain the historical references. She worked as an annotator for a medical research database. A skilled annotator can greatly improve the usability of old manuscripts. The annotator highlighted all the key passages in the legal text.

english_meaning: To make somebody slightly angry or upset. To make somebody uncomfortable or unable to relax. To disturb the peace of mind of (someone) especially by repeated disagreeable acts.
example_sentence: His constant joking was beginning to annoy her. It really annoys me when people forget to say thank you. It annoys me to see him getting ahead of me. I know you’re doing this only to annoy me.

english_meaning: To officially declare something legally void, null, or without effect. To formally cancel a legal contract, marriage, or official document. To reverse or undo the legal validity of an action or agreement. To make something legally unenforceable or as though it never existed, through proper legal authority.
example_sentence: The court agreed to annul the marriage after hearing the evidence presented by both parties. The contract was annulled because it had been signed under duress and without proper consent. The new government moved to annul several decrees passed by the previous administration. Their union was annulled due to procedural irregularities discovered during the review. The judge decided to annul the fraudulent agreement and ordered compensation for the victims.

english_meaning: The legal act of declaring a contract, law, or marriage void and of no legal effect. An official declaration that something never had legal validity from the very beginning. The formal and binding cancellation of a marriage or legal agreement by a court of law. A judicial or administrative action that reverses the legitimacy of a prior decision.
example_sentence: She applied for an annulment of the marriage on the grounds of fraud. The annulment of the contract saved the company from significant financial loss. The court granted an annulment based on the clear lack of informed consent. The annulment process required both parties to appear personally before the judge. After the annulment was finalized, she was free to begin a new chapter in her life.

english_meaning: A device that gives visual or audible signals indicating the status or condition of equipment. An indicator panel showing warnings or alerts. A signaling system that announces events or conditions. An electronic display showing system status.
example_sentence: The fire alarm annunciator shows which zone is affected. The annunciator panel displays system warnings. Check the annunciator for fault indicators. The aircraft annunciator alerted the pilot.

english_meaning: To apply oil or another substance to someone as part of a religious or ceremonial act. To consecrate or make sacred through the application of oil, typically during a formal ceremony. To formally designate or choose someone for a special role or high honor. To pour or spread oil on someone as a blessing or as a sign of divine favor.
example_sentence: The priest anointed the sick with holy oil during the special prayer service. Kings were anointed before their formal coronation ceremonies in ancient traditions. She anointed her dry hands with warm coconut oil before going to bed. The bishop anointed the newborn child during the baptism ceremony. The coach was informally anointed as the successor long before the announcement was made.

english_meaning: Different from what is normal or expected. Irregular or unusual in a way that is difficult to explain. Not fitting the usual rule, pattern, or classification. Abnormal or inconsistent with surrounding facts.
example_sentence: The lab reported an anomalous result in one sample. Scientists studied the anomalous weather pattern carefully. His behavior seemed anomalous for such a quiet student. The accountant found an anomalous entry in the records.

english_meaning: Something that is different from what is normal or expected. An unusual condition that does not fit the general rule. A deviation from the standard pattern in data or results. A person or thing that is difficult to classify because it is odd. An irregularity that may point to an error or a rare event.
example_sentence: The scientists noticed an anomaly in the temperature readings. Such heavy rain in June is an anomaly for this region. The audit revealed a small anomaly in the accounts. His calm behaviour during the crisis was an anomaly among the staff.

english_meaning: The act of making something anonymous by removing identifying information. The process of removing or changing personal information from data so that an individual cannot be identified. It is commonly used to protect privacy in research, medical records, surveys, and digital platforms.
example_sentence: The hospital used anonymisation to protect patient records before sharing them with researchers. Proper anonymisation helps companies comply with privacy laws. The survey data went through anonymisation to remove all personal details. Anonymisation reduces the risk of identity theft in online databases.

english_meaning: To remove personal or identifying details from something such as data, documents, or records so that the person it refers to cannot be recognized or identified. To make something anonymous.
example_sentence: We anonymise the data so researchers cannot identify any individual subjects. The research team anonymised the participants’ names before publishing the report. Hospitals anonymise patient records to protect privacy. The company anonymised user data before sharing it with analysts. Students’ exam papers were anonymised to ensure fair marking.

english_meaning: The state of remaining unknown to most other people. The quality or state of being mostly or completely unknown.
example_sentence: Names of people in the book were changed to preserve anonymity. The anonymity of the city (= where people do not know each other). The person donating the money insisted on complete anonymity. Some people prefer the anonymity of life in a big city.

english_meaning: The act of making something anonymous by removing identifying information. The process of removing or changing personal information from data so that an individual cannot be identified. It is commonly used to protect privacy in research, medical records, surveys, and digital platforms.
example_sentence: The hospital uses anonymization to protect patient records. Social media platforms often perform anonymization on user data before sharing with advertisers. Researchers applied anonymization to the survey results to ensure participants’ privacy. Anonymization of emails prevented tracing back to the original sender.

english_meaning: To remove personal or identifying details from something such as data, documents, or records so that the person it refers to cannot be recognized or identified. To make something anonymous.
example_sentence: We anonymize the data so researchers cannot identify any individual subjects. The company anonymized all customer records before sharing them for research. Journalists often anonymize their sources to protect their identities. The survey data was anonymized to ensure participants' ants’ privacy. He anonymized the file so no one could trace it back to him.

english_meaning: A person whose name is not known or not made public. Something done without revealing the identity of the doer. A work such as a book or letter published without the writer’s name. Lacking unique features, ordinary or not distinctive.
example_sentence: The money was donated by an anonymous benefactor. Police said an anonymous caller warned that a bomb was about to go off. I'm not prepared to give credence to anonymous complaints.

english_meaning: In a way that keeps a person's name or identity unknown. Doing something without revealing one's name, identity, or personal details. It is used when a person wishes to remain unknown while giving information, making a donation, posting a message, or expressing an opinion.
example_sentence: The house was donated anonymously to the Spanish Colonial Arts Society in 1998. It is impossible for somebody who blogs anonymously to guarantee that his or her identity cannot be discovered. She wrote these letters anonymously. They made the donation anonymously.

english_meaning: An eating disorder characterized by an abnormally low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted perception of weight. People with this condition often severely restrict their food intake. It requires medical and psychological treatment for recovery.
example_sentence: Anorexia is a dangerous eating disorder that primarily affects young women. She successfully recovered from anorexia after months of intense psychological therapy. People suffering from anorexia often have a completely distorted image of their bodies. The clinic specializes in treating eating disorders like bulimia and anorexia. Extreme weight loss and a refusal to eat are main symptoms of anorexia.

english_meaning: An additional skill, qualification, or way of earning money that increases your options. An extra ability that can be useful in different situations.
example_sentence: Learning coding would add another string to your bow. Her teaching certificate is another string to her bow. Speaking Spanish gave him another string to his bow at work. The course offers another string to your bow when jobs are competitive.

english_meaning: To reply rudely to someone in authority. To reply rudely or defend oneself against criticism.
