example_sentence: Her mother was shocked when she started answering her back and refusing to help. The student answered back to the teacher. Don’t answer back to elders. She has a habit of answering back whenever someone corrects her.

english_meaning: A small social insect that lives in large organized colonies. A hardworking insect known for carrying loads much heavier than itself. A member of a colony that has queens, workers, and soldiers.
example_sentence: An ant carried a crumb back to its nest. Ants work together in a highly organized way. We found a long line of ants in the kitchen. The ant colony was built under the old tree.

english_meaning: A person or force that strongly opposes another, especially the main character in a story. A person, group, idea, or force that actively resists or conflicts with another, often the protagonist. In literature, the antagonist creates obstacles and tension. In real life, it can refer to anyone who opposes a policy, action, or viewpoint.
example_sentence: In the novel, the antagonist constantly tries to stop the hero from succeeding. Fear can act as an antagonist to personal growth. The main antagonist in the film was more powerful than expected. He became an antagonist of the reform due to his strong opposition.

english_meaning: Actively opposing or showing strong hostility toward someone or something. Characterized by conflict, resistance, or aggression in attitude or behavior. Having properties or effects that are directly opposite or contradictory to each other. Tending to create friction, disagreement, or opposition in a relationship or situation.
example_sentence: The two rivals maintained an antagonistic relationship throughout the entire season. He adopted an antagonistic tone during the negotiations, which made progress difficult. The union's antagonistic stance made it very hard to reach a workable agreement. She felt the antagonistic energy in the room as soon as she walked through the door. Their antagonistic behavior disrupted the entire team's morale and overall performance.

english_meaning: The point in the sky directly opposite to the direction in which the sun is currently moving through space. The celestial direction from which the solar system appears to be receding. A term used in astronomy to describe the counter-direction of the sun's motion through interstellar space. The counterpoint to the solar apex in the study of stellar astronomy.
example_sentence: Astronomers calculate the antapex to better understand the sun's motion through interstellar space. The antapex of the sun's motion lies in the direction of the constellation Columba. The direction of the antapex was first identified using detailed stellar velocity data. Studies of the antapex help scientists map the overall movement of the solar system. The antapex is defined as the exact opposite point of the solar apex in astronomy.

english_meaning: Before midday or before 12 noon. It is used in the 12 hour clock system to indicate the time between midnight 12:00 and just before noon 11:59. It appears after the time to show that the hour falls in the morning period.
example_sentence: The meeting will start at 9:00 AM. I usually wake up at 6:30 AM. The flight departs at 5:15 AM tomorrow. She sent the email at 11:45 AM before leaving for work.

english_meaning: A thing or event that comes before another and may have caused it. A person's ancestors or family background. In grammar, the word or phrase to which a pronoun refers. Coming before something in time or order.
example_sentence: Poverty was an antecedent of the unrest in the region. She was proud of her distinguished antecedents. In this sentence the pronoun has no clear antecedent. Antecedent conditions made the flooding far worse.

english_meaning: A small room leading into a larger, main room. A waiting area placed before an important chamber or hall.
example_sentence: Guests waited in the antechamber before the ceremony began. The antechamber was lined with old portraits. He paced the antechamber, rehearsing his speech. A guard stood at the door of the antechamber.

english_meaning: To come before something else in time. To assign or mark a document with a date earlier than the actual one.
example_sentence: These ruins antedate the arrival of the empire. His appointment antedates the new policy by a year. The clerk was accused of antedating the contract. Cave paintings antedate written records by millennia.

english_meaning: A person or thing from a very old time, something antiquated. Extremely old or outdated, belonging to a time long before the flood described in the Bible.
example_sentence: The museum displayed antediluvian tools from prehistoric times. His antediluvian views on education shocked the young teachers. They drove an antediluvian car that barely started. The antediluvian laws were finally abolished after decades. My grandfather is an antediluvian who refuses to use a smartphone. That typewriter is an antediluvian in today’s office.

english_meaning: A swift, slender, horned mammal of Africa and Asia belonging to the family Bovidae. The leather or meat obtained from such an animal.
example_sentence: A herd of antelope grazed near the waterhole. The antelope outran the cheetah by a narrow margin. Tourists photographed antelope on the open plain. He wore gloves made of soft antelope.

english_meaning: Occurring or existing before birth. Relating to the medical care of a woman during pregnancy.
example_sentence: She attended her antenatal appointment on Thursday. The clinic offers free antenatal classes. Good antenatal care reduces many risks. Antenatal tests detected the condition early.

english_meaning: A collection of selected writings, poems, or stories by different authors or from different works, usually gathered in one book. A published collection of literary pieces such as poems, short stories, essays, or songs chosen from different writers or sources. It is often organized around a theme, time period, or genre.
example_sentence: The teacher gave us an anthology of modern English poetry. I enjoy reading a short story anthology before sleeping. The library has a new anthology of African writers. She published an anthology of her favorite essays.

english_meaning: A person or organism that loves or is attracted to flowers. It can describe both humans who adore flowers and insects like bees that are naturally drawn to them.
example_sentence: As an anthophile, she filled every room with fresh flowers. Bees are natural anthophiles that help in pollination. The anthophile spent weekends at botanical gardens. He was known as an anthophile who grew over fifty rose varieties.

english_meaning: The scientific study of human beings, their societies, and their cultures. The study of human origins, behaviour, and physical development. The comparative study of human customs, beliefs, and social relations.
example_sentence: She studied anthropology at a well-known university. Anthropology helps us understand how different cultures develop. His research in anthropology focused on rural communities. Modern anthropology combines fieldwork with genetic evidence.

english_meaning: Designed to attack, defend against, detect, or destroy enemy aircraft. Used for weapons, guns, missiles, defenses, or systems aimed at aircraft. Opposing or protecting against air attacks.
example_sentence: The army installed anti-aircraft guns near the base. Anti-aircraft missiles protected the city from air attacks. The old fort still has anti-aircraft positions. Soldiers trained on an anti-aircraft defense system. The aircraft avoided the anti-aircraft fire.

english_meaning: Designed to stop or defend against ballistic missiles or projectiles. Opposing ballistic weapons. Relating to systems that intercept fast-moving missiles.
example_sentence: The country tested an anti-ballistic missile system. Anti-ballistic shields protect against incoming rockets. Engineers improved the anti-ballistic radar. The treaty limited anti-ballistic defenses.

english_meaning: The prevention of terrorist attacks and activities. Government and security measures taken to identify and stop terrorism. Laws, policies, and strategies designed to combat terrorist organizations. Intelligence and security operations aimed at detecting terrorist threats. International cooperation to prevent terrorism and terrorist financing. Measures taken to protect civilians and important places from terrorist attacks. The organized effort to reduce or eliminate the threat of terrorism. Activities designed to disrupt terrorist networks and prevent them from carrying out attacks.
example_sentence: An anti-terrorism court heard the case this week. The province set up a special anti-terrorism force. New anti-terrorism rules apply at all major airports. Officials reviewed the anti-terrorism strategy after the incident.

english_meaning: Able to kill bacteria or stop their growth. Used against bacteria. Relating to substances, treatments, or products that reduce bacterial contamination.
example_sentence: Use antibacterial soap when required by hospital rules. The cream has antibacterial properties. Antibacterial medicines should be used carefully. The surface was cleaned with an antibacterial spray. Some antibacterial products are not needed for everyday use.

english_meaning: A medicine or substance that kills bacteria or stops their growth. Relating to antibiotics. Used to treat bacterial infections, not viral infections.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed an antibiotic for the infection. Antibiotic resistance is a serious health problem. Do not take an antibiotic without medical advice. The antibiotic helped clear the bacterial infection. Antibiotic treatment does not cure a common cold.

english_meaning: A protein made by the immune system to recognize, bind to, and help neutralize foreign substances such as bacteria, viruses, or toxins. A defensive substance in blood and body fluids that responds to antigens.
example_sentence: The blood test checks for antibodies. An antibody can attach to a specific virus. Vaccines help the body produce protective antibodies. Scientists developed an antibody treatment for the disease. Antibodies are important parts of the immune response.

english_meaning: To expect or look forward to something before it happens. To think about or predict something before it happens. It can mean expecting an event, preparing in advance, imagining a future situation, or reacting before something actually occurs.
example_sentence: We assess glaciers, landslides, glacial lakes and other remote hazards to anticipate the risk of floods and other climate-induced hazards. We don't anticipate any major problems. The eagerly anticipated movie will be released next month. We need someone who can anticipate and respond to changes in the fashion industry. We eagerly anticipated the day we would leave school. When Scott reached the South Pole he found that Amundsen had anticipated him.

english_meaning: A feeling of expecting something to happen. The act of expecting or predicting something before it happens. It can describe an emotional feeling of excitement, hope, fear, or anxiety about a future event. It also means preparing for something in advance.
example_sentence: He bought extra food in anticipation of more people coming than he'd invited. The courtroom was filled with anticipation. There is growing anticipation that the chairman will have to resign. Parents visit the school in anticipation that action will be taken. There was widespread anticipation of further expansion.

english_meaning: Expecting or preparing for something that is likely to happen. Relating to an action, feeling, or response that happens in advance because something is expected. It describes preparation, prediction, or reaction before an event actually occurs.
example_sentence: Previously you'd see much more anticipatory hiring. Hence anticipatory governments have been forced to change the incentives that drive their leaders. An anticipatory story is a trap to the teller.

english_meaning: Moving or rotating in a direction opposite to that of the hands of a clock. Describing a path that curves to the left from a fixed starting point. Used specifically in British English to denote a counter-rotational movement. In mathematics it refers to a positive rotation in a standard coordinate system. In sports it describes a race run in a direction favoring the inside rail on the left. In navigation it indicates a turn that decreases degrees in a specific azimuthal context. In circular mechanics it refers to a torque or force applied against the clockwise norm. In everyday language it refers to any process reversed from the standard chronological rotation.
example_sentence: The runner circled the track in an anticlockwise direction to warm up. Please turn the valve anticlockwise to release the internal pressure. Most modern racetracks in the UK are designed to be run anticlockwise. The dancers performed a complex routine rotating anticlockwise around the center pole.

english_meaning: Relating to the study or collection of antiques and ancient objects. A person who collects, studies, or deals in rare old books and artefacts. Concerned with the history and remains of the past. Describing a shop or trade dealing in old and rare items. Having an interest in things valued for their age rather than their use.
example_sentence: He spent the afternoon in an antiquarian bookshop. The museum bought the manuscript from a well-known antiquarian. She has an antiquarian interest in old maps. Antiquarian collections often reveal forgotten local history.

english_meaning: To make something old-fashioned, obsolete, or no longer relevant to current times. To render a technology, method, or idea outdated by the introduction of something newer and better. To cause something to appear no longer useful by replacing it with a more modern alternative. To bring about the end of relevance or usefulness of an older system or practice.
example_sentence: Modern smartphones have largely helped to antiquate traditional landline phones. Rapid advances in technology tend to antiquate older methods of communication. The rise of the internet has begun to antiquate many traditional business models. Industrial growth can quickly antiquate traditional craft skills passed down through generations. The arrival of digital cameras served to antiquate film photography almost overnight.

english_meaning: An object that is old, rare, and valued for its age, craftsmanship, or historical significance. Something belonging to or made in a former period of history, especially prized for its rarity and beauty. Of great age and historical interest, reminiscent of or belonging to ancient times. A collectible item whose value increases with its age, origin, and uniqueness.
example_sentence: She collected antique furniture from the Victorian era with great care and passion. The antique vase was valued at several thousand dollars at the auction house. He spent his weekends hunting for antiques at local fairs and flea markets. The museum showcased a remarkable collection of ancient Greek antiques. Her grandmother left her a beautiful antique brooch that had been in the family for generations.

english_meaning: Hostility, prejudice, or discrimination against Jewish people as a religious, ethnic, or cultural group. A set of beliefs, attitudes, or actions that target Jewish individuals or communities with hatred or bias. Historically rooted prejudice that has manifested in social exclusion, violence, and systemic discrimination against Jews. Hatred or intolerance directed specifically at Jewish people or Judaism.
example_sentence: The museum's exhibition documented the history of antisemitism across Europe.  Antisemitism led to widespread persecution of Jewish communities throughout history.  The organization works to combat antisemitism and promote tolerance.  Education plays a key role in addressing the roots of antisemitism.  The report highlighted a worrying rise in antisemitism in several countries.

english_meaning: A substance that prevents the growth of germs, especially on the skin or wounds. Used to stop infection in living tissue. Extremely clean and free from germs. Lacking warmth, character, or personality; coldly impersonal.
example_sentence: Apply an antiseptic cream to the cut twice a day. The nurse cleaned the wound with an antiseptic solution. This soap has strong antiseptic properties. The waiting room had a cold, antiseptic atmosphere.

english_meaning: Not wanting to spend time with other people, or behaving in a way that is harmful to society and social rules. A person who avoids social interaction and prefers to be alone. Behavior that is harmful, disruptive, or against the interests of society.
example_sentence: His antisocial behavior led to his expulsion from school. She became antisocial after her traumatic experience. Vandalism is an antisocial act that affects the whole community. He spent weekends alone, preferring antisocial solitude.

english_meaning: Measures, policies, or actions taken to prevent and defend against acts of terrorism. Relating to efforts designed to protect people and property from terrorist attacks. The defensive side of security work aimed at reducing vulnerability to terrorism. A general term for laws, forces, and strategies created to stop terrorist activity.
example_sentence: The government introduced new antiterrorism laws last year. Airport staff receive regular antiterrorism training. The city increased antiterrorism measures before the festival. Both countries signed an antiterrorism cooperation agreement.

english_meaning: Direct opposite. A contrast or opposition between two things, the exact opposite of an idea, concept, or quality. It is often used in literature or speech to highlight differences.
example_sentence: Love is the antithesis of hate. His calm demeanor was the antithesis of her fiery temperament. The new policy is the antithesis of fairness. Freedom is the antithesis of oppression.

english_meaning: Directly and completely opposed or contrary to something in nature or principle. Being the exact opposite in character, meaning, or effect. Standing in sharp or irreconcilable contrast to another idea or belief. Fundamentally incompatible or in strong logical or moral conflict with something else.
example_sentence: Corruption is completely antithetical to justice and good governance in any society. His actions were antithetical to the very values he publicly claimed to hold dear. Lying is antithetical to the fundamental principle of honest and open communication. The new policy seemed antithetical to the organization's original mission and founding goals. Kindness and cruelty are antithetical qualities that cannot genuinely coexist in one character.

english_meaning: A word that has the opposite meaning to another word in the same language. A term used in linguistics to describe words with contrary meanings. The opposite of a synonym.
example_sentence: The antonym of hot is cold, just as the antonym of happy is sad. Students were asked to write the antonym of each adjective listed in the exercise. Understanding antonyms helps learners develop a richer and more nuanced vocabulary. Dark is an antonym of light, and fast is an antonym of slow. The teacher explained the difference between synonyms and antonyms at the start of the lesson.

english_meaning: To be restless or unable to sit still due to excitement or nervousness. Very excited.
example_sentence: The kids had ants in their pants before the trip. He had ants in his pants before his first flight. The children had ants in their pants waiting for the party to start. She can’t sit still, must have ants in her pants today!. He had ants in his pants during the meeting, thinking about the big game.

english_meaning: The opening at the end of the digestive system through which solid waste (feces) leaves the body. It is a part of human and animal anatomy, located at the end of the rectum.
synonyms: ["Rectal opening","Back passage","Anal opening","Terminal opening of the digestive tract"]
example_sentence: The doctor examined the anus for any signs of infection. Waste leaves the body through the anus. The anus is an essential part of the digestive system. Pain near the anus can be a symptom of a medical condition.

english_meaning: The state of feeling nervous or worried that something bad is going to happen. A mental health problem that causes somebody to worry so much that it has a very negative effect on their daily life. A worry or fear about something.
example_sentence: She felt anxiety before her final exam. His anxiety about the interview kept him awake all night. Parents often experience anxiety when their children are sick. Too much anxiety can affect both mental and physical health.

english_meaning: Feeling worried, nervous, or uneasy about something with an uncertain outcome. Having a strong desire or eagerness for something. Experiencing mental tension or concern. A state of mind where a person feels worry, fear, or uneasiness, often about what might happen in the future. It can also describe a strong eagerness or excitement to achieve or receive something.
example_sentence: She felt anxious before her exam. He is anxious about his health. They were anxious to hear the results. The mother felt anxious when her child was late. He became anxious when the phone kept ringing. The parents were anxious about their child’s safety.

english_meaning: Feeling worry, nervousness, or strong eagerness about something. In a worried or nervous way. With fear about what may happen. With strong desire or eagerness. Restlessly expecting something.
example_sentence: She waited anxiously for the exam results. The mother looked anxiously at her sick child. He anxiously checked his phone for messages. Students listened anxiously to the announcement.

english_meaning: The largest artery in the body, which carries blood away from the heart. The main vessel that begins at the left ventricle and supplies the whole body. The great artery from which all other systemic arteries branch.
example_sentence: The aorta carries blood from the heart to the body. A tear in the aorta is life threatening. The aorta arches over the heart before descending. Surgeons repaired the weakened wall of the aorta.

english_meaning: A group of culturally related Native American tribes from the southwestern United States, including states like Arizona and New Mexico (known for their warrior traditions and resistance during the 19th century). A powerful American attack helicopter used in modern warfare. An organization that develops open source software such as the Apache HTTP Server. A fierce or rebellious person.
example_sentence: The Apache lived in the deserts of the American Southwest. Geronimo became famous for his resistance against American troops. The army deployed a Boeing AH-64 Apache during the mission. The company relies on software supported by the Apache Software Foundation.

english_meaning: Separate or at a distance from someone or something. A state in which people or things are separated, not together, or placed at a distance. It can also describe something that is different from others or emotionally distant.
example_sentence: The two houses stand apart from each other. They decided to live apart after many arguments. Her talent sets her apart from the rest of the team. The old chair fell apart after years of use.

english_meaning: Showing no interest, enthusiasm, or concern. Feeling or showing little or no emotion, concern, or interest in things that usually matter to others. Often describes someone indifferent to events, feelings, or responsibilities.
example_sentence: She was apathetic about the election results and did not vote. His apathetic attitude towards his studies worried his parents. The students seemed apathetic during the long lecture. He remained apathetic even when his friend needed help.

english_meaning: A lack of interest, enthusiasm, concern, emotion, or motivation about something. A state in which a person does not care about things that would normally be important, interesting, or emotional. An apathetic person may show little motivation, concern, excitement, or emotional response toward events, people, work, or social issues.
example_sentence: The public's apathy toward voting worried the community leaders. His apathy toward his studies resulted in poor grades. The manager was frustrated by the team's apathy during the project. Apathy toward environmental issues can lead to serious problems.

english_meaning: An opening, gap, hole, or slit through which light or air can pass. In photography, the adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls the amount of light entering the camera. Any small or narrow gap in a wall, surface, or other material. An orifice or passageway through which something can enter or exit.
example_sentence: The camera's aperture was adjusted carefully to allow more light into the lens. The aperture in the stone wall allowed a thin beam of golden sunlight to enter the room. She peered through the small aperture in the wooden fence to see what was happening outside. A wide aperture produces a beautifully blurred background in portrait photography. The technician carefully checked the aperture of the telescope before beginning observations.

english_meaning: To become extremely angry, excited, or out of control.
example_sentence: He went apeshit when he found out someone scratched his new car. The fans went apeshit when the singer appeared on stage. My boss went apeshit after the report got delayed again. She went apeshit with joy when she heard the good news.

english_meaning: The highest or uppermost point of something. The tip, peak, or summit of a structure, mountain, or geometric figure. The most successful, powerful, or important point in a person's career or an organization's history. The culminating point of any sequence, process, or development.
example_sentence: She reached the apex of her career at the impressive age of thirty-five. The apex of the pyramid can be clearly seen from several miles away. The lion is widely regarded as the apex predator of the African savanna. He stood at the apex of his profession after many years of dedicated hard work. The company reached its apex during the economic boom of the nineteen nineties.

english_meaning: A very small soft-bodied insect that sucks sap from plants. A common garden pest that weakens plants and spreads plant diseases.
example_sentence: Aphids covered the underside of the rose leaves. The farmer sprayed the crop to control aphids. Ladybirds feed on aphids in the garden. An aphid attack can quickly weaken young plants.

english_meaning: A short, wise saying that expresses a general truth. A concise statement that conveys a deep idea, moral lesson, or universal truth. It is often memorable and thought provoking, commonly used in literature, philosophy, and everyday speech.
example_sentence: "Actions speak louder than words" is a well known aphorism. His speech was filled with aphorisms about life and success. "Time is money" is a classic aphorism used in business. The book contains many aphorisms that teach valuable lessons.

english_meaning: The destruction of the world. The end of the world, as described in the Bible. The final book of the Bible, also known as Revelation, which describes events leading up to the final destruction of the world. A situation causing very serious damage and destruction.
example_sentence: The book offers a vision of the future in which there is a great nuclear apocalypse. Nobody was artistically better prepared to deal with the watery apocalypse that followed Hurricane Katrina than this 75-year-old man. A large part of this secret literature was the apocalypses. Apocalypse's blood can heal other mutants, but is fatal for humans.

english_meaning: Describing very serious damage and destruction in past or future events. Like the end of the world.
example_sentence: Before them was an apocalyptic landscape of burnt villages and bomb craters. But some take a more apocalyptic view. His speeches conveyed an oppressively apocalyptic vision. The apocalyptic view must be rejected. The reason is, I'm fascinated by the apocalyptic recovery.

english_meaning: Of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true. Not genuine or verified. Used for stories, accounts, or writings that are popularly told but not based on real evidence.
example_sentence: Many apocryphal stories are told about the life of the famous poet. The tale of the buried treasure turned out to be apocryphal. Several apocryphal quotes are wrongly attributed to great leaders. The historian dismissed the account as apocryphal. There are apocryphal anecdotes about his childhood adventures.

english_meaning: In a way that shows regret or asks for forgiveness. With a tone or manner expressing that one is sorry. In a humble and remorseful manner. While admitting fault or expressing embarrassment. In a way that seeks to excuse or explain a mistake politely.
example_sentence: He smiled apologetically after arriving late to the meeting. She apologetically explained that the item was out of stock. The child looked apologetically at his mother after breaking the vase. He coughed apologetically before interrupting the conversation.

english_meaning: A formal written defense or justification of one's beliefs, opinions, or actions. A reasoned argument presented to explain or defend a controversial position or decision. An official explanation or formal written account used to counter criticism or accusations. A response to attacks on one's character, faith, or professional conduct.
example_sentence: He wrote a detailed apologia explaining his controversial and widely criticized decision. The politician's apologia failed to convince his critics or restore public confidence. She published an apologia to address the serious accusations that had been made against her. The philosopher's apologia has been carefully studied and debated for many centuries. His apologia was both remarkably eloquent and deeply sincere in its reasoning.

english_meaning: British spelling of apologize; to express regret or say sorry for a mistake or offense. To admit a fault and ask for forgiveness. To offer an explanation or defense.
example_sentence: He apologised for interrupting the speaker. She apologised to her teacher for missing class. The airline apologised for the long delay. You should apologise for what you said.

english_meaning: A person who offers arguments in defense of something controversial. A speaker or writer who defends a belief, doctrine, or institution. One who justifies or explains an idea, often against criticism.
example_sentence: He is a well-known apologist for free market economics. The writer became an apologist for the government's policies. She is an apologist of modern art. Many apologists have defended the ancient traditions.

english_meaning: To express regret or say sorry for a fault, mistake, or offense. To acknowledge one's wrongdoing and ask forgiveness. To make an excuse or offer a defense for something.
example_sentence: He apologized for being late to the meeting. She apologized to her friend after the argument. The company apologized for the poor service. I must apologize for my rude behavior yesterday.

english_meaning: An expression of remorse or regret for a wrong done to someone. A formal statement acknowledging fault and offering sincere sorrow for an offense or failure. A verbal or written acknowledgment of responsibility and genuine regret for causing harm. The act of asking forgiveness for a mistake, misunderstanding, or harmful action.
example_sentence: She offered a sincere and heartfelt apology for arriving late to the important meeting. His apology was graciously accepted by all those he had hurt. A genuine apology requires honest acknowledgment of the mistake and a real change in behavior. He wrote a thoughtful apology letter to his old friend after their long misunderstanding. The company issued a formal public apology for the serious data breach that had affected its customers.

english_meaning: Overcome with extreme anger and unable to control it. Furious to the point of being nearly speechless or physically shaking. Relating to or suffering from apoplexy, an old medical term for a stroke. Showing signs of intense rage such as a flushed face and raised voice. Extremely enraged or incensed in a way that seems almost uncontrollable.
example_sentence: He was apoplectic when he saw the damage to his car. The manager became apoplectic after hearing the excuse. She turned apoplectic with rage at the unfair decision. The old doctor described the patient's condition as apoplectic.

english_meaning: An old-fashioned medical term for a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain. Sudden loss of consciousness and paralysis due to a ruptured blood vessel. A state of extreme anger or excitement that seems to overwhelm a person. Great rage or shock that leaves someone almost incapacitated. Any condition marked by sudden collapse or violent emotion.
example_sentence: The old man died of apoplexy in his sleep. His face turned red as if he were about to have apoplexy. She nearly had apoplexy when she saw the phone bill. Doctors once called every sudden collapse apoplexy.

english_meaning: A sudden breaking off in the middle of a sentence, leaving it unfinished. A rhetorical device where the speaker stops abruptly for effect. An unfinished statement that suggests strong emotion.
example_sentence: His angry speech ended in aposiopesis. The poet used aposiopesis to create suspense. Aposiopesis often reveals more than words could. She stopped mid-sentence in a moment of aposiopesis.

english_meaning: The act of rejecting your former religious or political beliefs. The act of giving up your religious or political beliefs and leaving a religion or a political party. The renunciation of one's religion or faith.
example_sentence: Apostasy was punishable by death under the country's strict religious laws. In those days apostasy was punishable by death.

english_meaning: A person who has rejected their religious or political beliefs. Someone who has given up their religion or left a political party. A disloyal person who betrays or deserts his cause or religion or political party or friend etc.
example_sentence: The most furious anarchist become the most barefaced apostate. He is an apostate from Christianity. We must punish this apostate priest.

english_meaning: A person who strongly believes in a policy or an idea and tries to make other people believe in it. Someone who strongly supports a particular belief or political movement. One of the original 12 disciples chosen by Christ to preach his gospel.
example_sentence: An apostle of world peace, liberty. I shall not pursue my inquiries as to which schools the apostles of that policy emerged from. He seemed to take the view that it was all the responsibility of the apostles of class warfare.

english_meaning: A punctuation mark used to show possession or the omission of letters. A mark written as a raised comma in words such as don't and John's. In literature, a rhetorical device in which a speaker addresses an absent person or an abstract idea.
example_sentence: Add an apostrophe to show that the book belongs to Ali. Many students misuse the apostrophe in plurals. In 'can't', the apostrophe replaces the missing letters. The poet uses apostrophe to address death directly.

english_meaning: The highest point in the development of something; a perfect example. The elevation of a person to the rank of a god. Glorification of someone or something as ideal. The culmination or climax of a process or career.
example_sentence: The novel is the apotheosis of his writing career. That performance was the apotheosis of modern dance. The emperor's apotheosis was celebrated across the empire. This building is often called the apotheosis of Mughal architecture.

english_meaning: To shock and horrify someone deeply. To fill a person with dismay or disgust. To cause strong feelings of dread or moral outrage.
example_sentence: The living conditions in the camp appalled the visitors. I was appalled by his rude behaviour towards the staff. The photographs of the disaster appalled the entire nation. It appalls me that such waste is still allowed.

english_meaning: Shocking, horrifying, or very bad. Extremely unpleasant or terrible. Causing dismay or horror. Very poor in quality.
example_sentence: The conditions in the prison were appalling. She was shocked by the appalling behavior of the crowd. The food at the restaurant was appalling. They witnessed an appalling act of cruelty.

english_meaning: In a way that causes shock, horror, or dismay. Extremely badly or in a shocking manner. To a degree that is dreadful or terrible. In a manner that inspires disgust or alarm. Very poorly; shockingly.
example_sentence: The prisoners were treated appallingly by the guards. He drove appallingly during the storm. The building was appallingly designed and dangerous. She sang appallingly in front of the whole audience.

english_meaning: Clothing, garments, and accessories worn on the body. The collective term for all forms of dress or attire. Formal or specialized clothing appropriate for a particular purpose, occasion, or profession. Outward dress that reflects cultural identity, personal style, or social role.
example_sentence: The store specializes in outdoor apparel designed for hikers and serious climbers. She wore elegant and tasteful apparel to the prestigious award ceremony. The fashion designer launched a widely praised new line of casual apparel this season. Traditional apparel varies widely and beautifully across different cultures around the world. The entire team was dressed in matching branded apparel for the championship event.

english_meaning: Clearly visible or obvious to the eye or mind. Seeming real or true but not necessarily so upon closer or more careful examination. Readily perceived or understood without difficulty or ambiguity. Appearing to be true based on external observation even if not yet confirmed by deeper investigation.
example_sentence: It was apparent to everyone in the room that she had not slept properly in days. The serious damage to the building was apparent from a considerable distance. The simple solution was perfectly apparent to everyone who looked at the problem carefully. His discomfort was clearly apparent despite his repeated attempts to smile and appear at ease. It soon became apparent that important information had been deliberately withheld from the team.

english_meaning: As far as one can judge or see based on available evidence. According to what seems to be true or real. Seemingly or outwardly on the surface.
example_sentence: Apparently, the train has been delayed due to technical issues. She was apparently unaware of the changes made to the schedule. The market is apparently recovering after a long slump. He is apparently the most qualified candidate for the job.

english_meaning: To make an earnest and urgent request for help, support, or mercy. To apply to a higher court or authority to reconsider a decision made at a lower level. The power or ability to attract, interest, or charm someone. A call to emotions, reason, or authority in an attempt to persuade. A formal petition or request addressed to an authority or the general public.
example_sentence: She filed a formal appeal against the court's original ruling on the matter. The charity's fundraising appeal raised over a million dollars in just one week. He appealed directly to the manager for a second chance to prove himself. The stunning mountain scenery had an irresistible appeal for tourists visiting the region. The lawyer carefully prepared and submitted an appeal on behalf of her client.

english_meaning: The way someone or something looks. The act of arriving or becoming visible. A public performance or attendance at an event. The outward impression given, which may differ from reality.
example_sentence: He cares a great deal about his appearance. Her sudden appearance surprised everyone. The singer made a brief appearance on stage. Despite appearances, the plan was well prepared.

english_meaning: To calm, satisfy, or pacify someone by meeting their demands, reducing anger, or giving comfort. It can also mean to bring peace by doing something to please someone who is upset.
example_sentence: The manager tried to appease the angry customer by offering a refund. She spoke softly to appease the crying child. The government took steps to appease the protester. He apologized to appease his friend after the misunderstanding.

english_meaning: The act of calming someone or satisfying their demands to avoid conflict and maintain peace, often by giving in or making concessions.
example_sentence: The government’s policy of appeasement failed to stop the conflict. She offered an apology as an act of appeasement. Appeasement is not always the right way to deal with aggression. He gave gifts to his angry friend as a gesture of appeasement.

english_meaning: A person who makes an appeal to a higher court against a decision made by a lower court. Someone who disagrees with a judgment or decision made by a court, tribunal, or authority and formally requests a higher authority or court to review and change that decision.
example_sentence: The appellant filed a petition challenging the verdict of the lower court. The court heard arguments from both the appellant and the respondent. The appellant hopes the higher court will overturn the previous ruling. Legal counsel advised the appellant on the merits of the appeal

english_meaning: Relating to a court that reviews decisions made by lower courts. Concerned with appeals and the reconsideration of legal judgments.
example_sentence: The appellate court upheld the lower court’s decision. She works in appellate litigation. The lawyer filed an appellate brief. Appellate judges reviewed the evidence and legal arguments.

english_meaning: A name or title by which someone or something is known. A name, title, designation, or label given to a person, place, thing, or group. It is often used for formal names, descriptive titles, or identifying terms. A word or phrase used to identify, describe, or call someone or something. It may show respect, profession, status, quality, or origin. It is commonly used in literature, geography, social titles, and official naming systems.
example_sentence: The king earned the appellation "The Brave" after winning many battles. Karachi is often given the appellation "City of Lights". Her friendly nature made the appellation "Angel of the Office" very suitable. The scientist disliked the appellation that the media gave him.

english_meaning: A name, title, or descriptive word used for a person, place, or thing. It means relating to naming or giving a title. A name, label, designation, or title by which someone or something is called or known. It can also describe a word used as a common name instead of a proper name.
example_sentence: “Doctor” is an appellative used for medical professionals. The king was proud of the appellative “Defender of the Nation”. “Teacher” is a common appellative in schools. She disliked the appellative people gave her during childhood.

english_meaning: To add something at the end. To attach, add, or join something to the end of a document, list, text, or other item.
example_sentence: Please append your signature to the document. The report was incomplete, so he appended extra data. She appended a note at the end of the email. The program appends new records automatically.

english_meaning: The small finger-shaped pouch attached to the cecum of the large intestine. A section of extra information added at the end of a book or document. Any additional part attached to something larger.
example_sentence: The doctor removed his inflamed appendix. Pain from the appendix is usually felt on the right side. The full data is given in the appendix of the report. She added an appendix listing all the sources.

english_meaning: To consciously perceive and understand a new experience in relation to previous knowledge. To interpret a new sensation by actively relating it to existing mental frameworks or past understanding. To become fully aware of something through active mental processing rather than passive sensation. To grasp something meaningfully through the deliberate use of prior knowledge and experience.
example_sentence: Children naturally apperceive new information by linking it to what they already know from experience. The psychologist studied carefully how patients apperceive emotional cues in social situations. She was able to apperceive the subtle shifts in tone during the conversation. He apperceived the danger in the situation very quickly and acted without hesitation. Learning to apperceive one's surroundings more accurately improves situational awareness significantly.

english_meaning: The process of understanding or interpreting new information by relating it to previous knowledge. The mental process by which new ideas are assimilated and understood in the context of existing knowledge, experience, or awareness. It emphasizes conscious perception and reflection.
example_sentence: The teacher encouraged students to use apperception to connect history lessons with current events. His apperception of the painting revealed details that others missed. Apperception plays a key role in learning languages efficiently. Through apperception, she could understand the scientific concept better.

english_meaning: Desire to eat food. A natural feeling of hunger or desire for food. It can also mean a strong desire or interest for something such as success, knowledge, or adventure.
example_sentence: After playing football, he had a huge appetite for dinner. The long walk in the mountains increased our appetite. She has a strong appetite for learning new languages. Success in business increased his appetite for bigger goals.

english_meaning: A small dish or something that stimulates appetite before the main meal. A starter dish. A light snack before meals. Something that increases desire or interest. An introduction to something larger. A small portion of food served before the main course to stimulate the appetite. Anything that creates interest or desire for something more.
example_sentence: She ordered a soup as an appetizer before the main course. These small snacks work well as appetizers at parties. The trailer served as an appetizer for the upcoming movie. Fresh salad can be a healthy appetizer.

english_meaning: To show your approval of somebody, something by clapping your hands (= hitting your open hands together several times). To express praise for somebody, something because you approve of them or it. To declare enthusiastic approval of.
example_sentence: He started to applaud and the others joined in. She was applauded as she came on stage. The audience applauded loudly. His efforts to improve the situation are to be applauded.

english_meaning: The act of clapping hands to show appreciation, approval, or enjoyment. Public praise or strong approval for a performance, speech, achievement, or action. Expression of admiration from an audience or group of people.
example_sentence: The singer received loud applause after her performance. His speech was welcomed with great applause from the audience. The students gave applause to their teacher for the inspiring lecture. The actor smiled proudly as the crowd burst into applause.

english_meaning: A round fruit with firm, juicy flesh and red, green, or yellow skin. The edible fruit of the apple tree, widely eaten fresh or used in cooking. A common orchard fruit valued for its sweet or slightly tart taste. Something regarded as precious or dearly loved, as in the phrase the apple of one's eye.
example_sentence: She packed a red apple in her lunch box every morning. The apple trees in the valley bloom beautifully in spring. He sliced an apple and shared it with his younger sister. My grandmother bakes a delicious apple pie on weekends.

english_meaning: A small, round, green vegetable that looks like a small apple in shape. A summer squash commonly used in South Asian cooking. A vegetable of the cucurbit family, valued for its light and easily digestible nature. A soft-textured gourd often cooked with lentils, meat, or spices. A nutritious vegetable frequently recommended for a healthy diet.
example_sentence: My mother often cooks apple gourd with minced meat. Apple gourd is considered light and healthy for the stomach. He bought fresh apple gourds from the vegetable market. Doctors often recommend apple gourd for patients recovering from illness.

english_meaning: A cause of disagreement or conflict. Something that creates argument, rivalry, or tension among people or groups, often leading to long lasting disputes.
synonyms: ["Cause of conflict","Bone of contention","Source of dispute","Point of disagreement"]
antonyms: ["Cause of harmony","Source of peace","Unifying factor","Bond of agreement"]
example_sentence: The division of land became the apple of discord between the two families. Money is often the apple of discord in business partnerships. The new policy turned into an apple of discord among the staff. Political power has long been the apple of discord in the region.

english_meaning: Someone who is loved very much. A person who is extremely dear, precious, or loved more than others, often a child or someone very close
example_sentence: Her youngest son is the apple of her eye. The teacher treats that student like the apple of her eye. For his grandparents, he has always been the apple of their eye. She is clearly the apple of her father’s eye.

english_meaning: Used when comparing unlike things. Two things that are completely different and cannot be fairly compared because they belong to different categories or have different qualities. Used when someone compares two things that are too different to be judged together fairly. For example, comparing a bicycle with an airplane or comparing poetry with mathematics would be considered comparing apples and oranges. People often use this idiom in discussions, debates, business, education, and daily conversation to point out that the comparison is unreasonable.
synonyms: ["Completely different things","Incomparable things","Different as night and day","Mismatched comparison","Unlike things"]
example_sentence: Comparing online classes with outdoor sports is like comparing apples and oranges. You cannot compare a beginner singer with a professional artist because that would be apples and oranges. Their lifestyles are apples and oranges since one prefers city life and the other loves village life. Comparing Android phones with laptop computers is apples and oranges.

english_meaning: A small application designed to run within another program or a web browser. A specialized utility program that performs a limited and specific task. A component of a graphical user interface that provides a narrow set of controls or information. A compact software component that is often downloaded automatically to enhance the functionality of a parent application.
example_sentence: The webpage used a Java applet to display the interactive stock market chart. You can adjust the sound settings through the control panel applet. Many early web games were built as a simple applet that loaded in the browser. Developers often use an applet to handle secure file uploads without refreshing the entire page.

english_meaning: A device or piece of equipment designed to perform a specific task, typically a domestic one. A specialized tool or instrument used for a particular purpose or job. An electrical machine used in the household to assist with cooking, cleaning, or food preservation. The act of applying something, though this sense is archaic compared to the physical object. A medical or dental device designed to be worn to correct a deformity or assist a function.
example_sentence: The new kitchen appliance makes brewing coffee much faster. She went to the store to buy a major appliance like a refrigerator. The dentist fitted a corrective appliance to straighten his teeth. Every electrical appliance in the house should be unplugged during a storm.

english_meaning: The quality of being relevant or appropriate to a particular situation or purpose. The extent to which a rule, law, or theory can be applied in practice. The state of being capable of being put to use or service. The practical relevance of a concept to a specific set of circumstances. The condition of having a valid connection to a subject.
example_sentence: The legal team debated the applicability of the new law to cases involving international waters. Students often question the practical applicability of theoretical physics in everyday life. We need to evaluate the applicability of these safety regulations to smaller businesses. The researcher demonstrated the broad applicability of the new algorithm across various fields of study.

english_meaning: Capable of being applied or relevant to a particular situation. Having a valid connection or relation to the matter at hand. Legally binding or valid in a specific context or jurisdiction. Suitable or appropriate for a specific use or purpose. Being in force or currently effective in a given scenario.
example_sentence: The new safety regulations are applicable to all construction sites starting next month. Please provide all applicable documents when submitting your visa application. The discount is only applicable to full-priced items and cannot be combined with other offers. This legal clause is no longer applicable under the revised state statutes.

english_meaning: A person who formally applies for a job, place, permit, or benefit. Someone who submits a written request for consideration. A candidate seeking admission, employment, or membership. In official terms, the party making a request under a scheme or law.
example_sentence: Every applicant must attach a copy of the degree. The company interviewed twelve applicants for the post. The applicant was informed of the decision by email. Each applicant should submit the form before Friday.

english_meaning: A formal request to an authority for something. The action of putting something into operation or practical use. A computer program designed to fulfill a particular purpose. Sustained effort or hard work.
example_sentence: Please submit your application by Friday. The application of new rules caused some confusion. This application helps you track your daily expenses. His application to his studies yielded great results.

english_meaning: An arrangement to meet someone at a particular time and place. The act of choosing someone for a job or position. A job or position to which someone has been appointed. A scheduled meeting, especially with a professional.
example_sentence: I have an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock. Her appointment as head of the department was announced today. Please call the office to make an appointment. He accepted the appointment with great pride.

english_meaning: To divide something among people. To give a share of something to somebody. To give as a share or portion. To give out (something) to appropriate individuals.
example_sentence: Apportion the expenses between the parties involved. The programme gives the facts but does not apportion blame. They apportioned the land among members of the family.

english_meaning: The ongoing act of dividing and distributing resources, tasks, or responsibilities among people or groups. The process of assigning shares or allocations to different parties in a fair or calculated manner. The activity of splitting something into portions assigned to specific individuals or groups. Actively engaging in the fair or calculated distribution of something between competing parties or needs.
example_sentence: Apportioning the annual budget fairly among all departments was a genuinely challenging task. The committee spent many hours apportioning responsibilities carefully among its members. Apportioning resources effectively and efficiently is the key to successful project management. The government focused on apportioning aid as quickly as possible to the most severely affected regions. Apportioning blame after a failure rarely leads to productive or constructive outcomes.

english_meaning: Very suitable or appropriate to the particular situation. Well chosen and directly relevant to what is being discussed. Fitting neatly with the subject or occasion.
example_sentence: She made an apposite remark that summed up the debate. The speaker quoted an apposite line of poetry. His example was apposite to the problem under discussion. The title of the book is remarkably apposite.

english_meaning: A formal assessment or evaluation of the quality, value, or condition of something. An expert judgment made after careful examination of a person's performance or an asset's worth. A structured review used to measure the progress, quality, or effectiveness of a person, plan, or property. A professional estimate of the monetary value of a property or item.
example_sentence: The annual performance appraisal helped the team identify clear areas for improvement. She received a very positive appraisal from her manager at the end of the quarter. The property appraisal came in significantly higher than the owners had originally expected. He requested a professional appraisal of the antique jewelry before putting it up for sale. A thorough appraisal of the situation was essential before any major decisions could be made.

english_meaning: To recognize the value or worth of something. To be grateful or thankful for something. To understand fully the meaning or importance of something. To enjoy or value qualities in a person or thing. To increase in value over time.
example_sentence: I really appreciate your help with the project. She appreciates good music and art. The value of the property has appreciated over the years. We appreciate the effort you put into this work.

english_meaning: Recognition and enjoyment of the good qualities of someone or something. A feeling of gratitude or thankfulness. A full understanding of a situation or problem. An increase in the value of an asset or currency. A written review or assessment of a person's work.
example_sentence: She expressed her appreciation for their kind help. He has a deep appreciation of classical music. There is little appreciation of the difficulties involved. Property in this area has seen strong appreciation.

english_meaning: To arrest or capture a person suspected of a crime. To understand or grasp an idea mentally. To feel fear or worry about something that may happen. To anticipate with fear or anxiety. To become aware of something through perception or thought.
example_sentence: The police managed to apprehend the thief after a long chase. She quickly apprehended the main idea of the lecture. He apprehended danger when he heard the strange noise outside. Students sometimes apprehend complex theories after careful study.

english_meaning: A feeling of worry, fear, or anxiety about a future event or situation. The act of legally arresting or capturing someone accused of a crime. The mental act of understanding, grasping, or making sense of an idea or concept. A vague or persistent unease about something that might go wrong.
example_sentence: She felt a deep and growing sense of apprehension in the hours before the final exam. His apprehension grew steadily as the court date drew closer. The police ensured the swift apprehension of the suspect within a few hours of the incident. There was a general apprehension among the public about the safety of the newly released product. Her remarkably quick apprehension of complex ideas consistently impressed her university professors.

english_meaning: Anxious, uneasy, or fearful about something that may happen in the future. Showing or feeling worry or nervousness about an anticipated event or its outcome. Anticipating negative consequences or difficulties with a sense of dread or caution. Characterized by a worried or cautious state of mind in the face of uncertainty.
example_sentence: She felt deeply apprehensive about speaking in front of such a large and unfamiliar audience. He was noticeably apprehensive about starting his very first day at the new job. Many local residents were apprehensive about the scale of the upcoming changes to their neighborhood. The student was extremely apprehensive about the results of the final examination. She cast an apprehensive glance at the dark storm clouds that were rapidly gathering overhead.

english_meaning: A young person who works for an employer for a fixed period of time in order to learn the particular skills needed in their job. Someone who works for an expert to learn a particular skill or job.
example_sentence: I'm not even an apprentice in the snooping game, compared to you and Fred. He was apprenticed to his uncle as a carpenter. He worked for two years as a plumber’s apprentice

english_meaning: A period of training in which a person learns a skill or trade from an experienced worker. A formal agreement under which someone works while learning a craft. The position or status of an apprentice. A time of learning through practical experience.
example_sentence: He served a four-year apprenticeship as an electrician. The company offers apprenticeships to school leavers. She completed her apprenticeship with a master carpenter. Many young people prefer an apprenticeship to a university degree.

english_meaning: To tell or inform somebody of something. To give information, notify, or make someone aware of a fact, event, or situation.
example_sentence: He was apprised of the logistics of the situation. Let me apprise you of the current situation. We were fully apprised of the situation. He saw no reason to apprise the committee of what had happened.

english_meaning: An informal short form of the word approval, used mainly in British English in business. The arrangement of taking goods on approval, with the right to return them. Used in the phrase 'on appro', meaning goods supplied for inspection before purchase.
example_sentence: The shopkeeper let us take the books on appro. These curtains were sent on appro last week. You can order the samples on appro and return them free of charge. Goods supplied on appro must be paid for within thirty days.

english_meaning: To come near to someone or something, to move toward a place, or a method of dealing with a situation or problem. To move closer to a person, place, or object. To ask, consult, or communicate with someone. A particular way of dealing with a task, problem, or situation. To be close to a particular time or event. A road, path, or means of reaching a place.
example_sentence: The airplane slowly approached the runway for landing. She approached the manager with a new business idea. We need a different approach to solve this problem. The examination period is approaching quickly.

english_meaning: Friendly and easy to talk to. Willing to listen and open to conversation. Able to be reached or accessed physically. Easy to understand or deal with.
example_sentence: Our new manager is very approachable and helpful. Students find her approachable whenever they have problems. The village is approachable only by a narrow road. He explains difficult ideas in an approachable way.

english_meaning: Formal approval or official agreement. Praise or warm approval expressed towards someone or something. Acceptance of an action or decision as good and right.
example_sentence: The proposal received the approbation of the entire committee. Her performance won the approbation of the critics. He nodded in silent approbation. The plan was carried out with the approbation of the board.

english_meaning: The quality of being appropriate, especially in the use of language in a particular situation. Suitability of words, style, or behaviour for a given context. The extent to which something matches accepted norms of a situation.
example_sentence: Teachers should explain the appropriacy of formal and informal language. The essay was marked down for lack of appropriacy in tone. Appropriacy matters as much as grammatical accuracy. Learners often struggle with the appropriacy of polite requests.

english_meaning: Suitable, proper, or correct for a particular situation. To take something for one's own use, often without permission. To set aside money or resources for a specific purpose.
example_sentence: Please wear appropriate clothing for the interview. His remarks were not appropriate for a formal meeting. The government appropriated the land for a new road. Parliament appropriated funds for flood relief.

english_meaning: In a way that is suitable or proper for the circumstances. Correctly and in keeping with accepted standards. In a manner that fits the occasion or purpose.
example_sentence: Please dress appropriately for the ceremony. The staff responded appropriately to the emergency. Funds must be spent appropriately and transparently. She appropriately thanked everyone who had helped her.

english_meaning: The act of taking something for one's own use, often without permission. The setting aside of money by a government or organization for a specific purpose. The adoption of elements of one culture by members of another. The act of allocating funds officially.
example_sentence: The committee approved the appropriation of funds for education. He was accused of the appropriation of company money. Cultural appropriation is a widely debated topic. The budget included an appropriation for new hospitals.

english_meaning: The act of officially agreeing to something. Formal permission or authorisation. A favourable opinion or positive feeling about someone or something. Acceptance or praise given to a person's actions.
example_sentence: The project cannot begin without the manager's approval. She smiled with approval when she saw the results. The plan won the approval of the entire board. He looked at his son with obvious approval.

english_meaning: To officially agree to or accept something. To think that something is good, right, or acceptable. To give formal permission or authorisation. To confirm a plan, decision, or request.
example_sentence: The committee approved the new budget without changes. My parents approve of my decision to study abroad. The council has approved plans for a new hospital. She did not approve of his careless attitude.

english_meaning: In a way that shows agreement or satisfaction. With a favourable or positive attitude. In a manner expressing praise or support. Showing that one likes what has been done.
example_sentence: He nodded approvingly at her answer. The teacher smiled approvingly at the students' work. She looked approvingly around the newly painted room. The audience murmured approvingly after the speech.

english_meaning: A speech sound produced by bringing articulators close together without creating turbulence. A consonant sound where the vocal tract is narrowed but not enough to cause friction. A type of phonetic sound like 'w' or 'y' in linguistics. A sound intermediate between a vowel and a fricative.
example_sentence: The sound 'r' is an approximant in English. Approximants are produced with less constriction than fricatives. The linguist studied approximant sounds. 'W' and 'y' are common approximants.

english_meaning: Almost correct or exact but not completely so. Close to the real number, amount, or level. To come close to something in quality, amount, or nature. To estimate something roughly rather than precisely.
example_sentence: The approximate cost of the repairs is fifty thousand rupees. Please give me an approximate time of arrival. His account of the incident approximates the truth. We approximated the distance using a simple map.

english_meaning: Close to a particular number, time, or amount but not exactly. Used to show that something is almost but not completely accurate or exact. Roughly or about. Nearly or around a certain value.
synonyms: ["About","Around","Roughly","Nearly","Close to","More or less","In the region of","Circa"]
example_sentence: The building is approximately one hundred years old. It takes approximately two hours to drive there. There were approximately fifty people at the meeting. The cost will be approximately five hundred dollars.

english_meaning: The pleasant warmth of the sun in winter. It refers to the gentle and comforting warmth felt from sunlight during cold weather, especially in winter. It describes a quiet, soothing natural warmth rather than heat.
example_sentence: We sat quietly in the garden enjoying the apricity of the winter sun. The apricity made the cold afternoon feel calm and comfortable. She opened the window to let the apricity fill the room. Hikers paused on the hilltop to feel the apricity after a chilly walk.

english_meaning: A small, soft, orange-yellow fruit with a single stone inside. A stone fruit closely related to the peach but smaller and less juicy. The tree that produces this fruit. A pale orange-yellow colour resembling the fruit.
example_sentence: We bought a basket of fresh apricots from the roadside stall. Dried apricots are a healthy snack during long journeys. The apricot tree in our garden bore fruit for the first time. She chose an apricot shade for the living room curtains.

english_meaning: Difficult or unpleasant times often lead to better outcomes. Early struggles, hardships or problems can produce growth, success and good results later, just as spring rain helps flowers bloom.
example_sentence: Don’t worry, April showers bring May flowers. Hard work now means success later. Pain today can bring joy tomorrow. It’s a reminder that struggle leads to growth.

english_meaning: A protective garment worn over the front of one's clothes. A hard-surfaced area on an airfield for parking aircraft.
example_sentence: She tied her apron before starting to cook dinner. The blacksmith wore a heavy leather apron for protection. The plane taxied toward the apron to unload passengers. He wiped his floury hands on his apron.

english_meaning: A natural or innate ability to learn or perform a particular task well. A person's inherent talent or capacity to excel in a specific area of work or study. A readiness or quickness of mind for acquiring new skills or knowledge. The natural potential to succeed in a particular discipline, activity, or field.
example_sentence: She showed a remarkable natural aptitude for mathematics from a very early age. His strong aptitude for languages helped him learn three new ones in rapid succession. The test was specifically designed to measure natural aptitude rather than acquired academic knowledge. A clear aptitude for leadership became apparent in her during group activities at school. He had an undeniable natural aptitude for music and progressed much faster than his peers.

english_meaning: In a way that is suitable or appropriate for a particular situation. Fittingly. Suitably. Appropriately. In a manner that exactly matches the meaning or purpose. Used when describing how something is said, named, or done in a way that fits perfectly with the context.
example_sentence: The book is aptly titled 'Lessons from a Long Life'. He aptly described the situation as a complete disaster. She aptly summarized the entire meeting in just two minutes. The town, aptly known as the 'City of Lights', is famous for its festivals. The teacher aptly compared learning a language to building a house.

english_meaning: A light bluish-green colour, similar to the colour of clear sea water. Water, especially as used in scientific or pharmaceutical terms. A Latin word for water often used in names and compounds. Relating to water or having a water-like blue-green shade.
example_sentence: She painted the bedroom walls a soft aqua. The water in the lagoon was a bright aqua. The label used the Latin word aqua for distilled water. He wore an aqua shirt with white trousers.

english_meaning: A bluish-green color like that of seawater. A precious bluish-green gemstone, a variety of beryl. Having a light blue-green color. A semi-precious stone used in jewelry.
example_sentence: Her eyes were a striking aquamarine color. She wore an aquamarine necklace to the party. The sea looked aquamarine in the morning light. The ring was set with a large aquamarine stone.

english_meaning: Love or strong attraction to water. A strong fondness, fascination, or attraction toward water bodies, aquatic activities, or water-related environments. It can include swimming, boating, or simply enjoying being near water.
example_sentence: Her aquaphilia made her spend every weekend at the lake. People with aquaphilia often enjoy sailing and diving. He developed aquaphilia after years of swimming lessons. The resort attracts guests with a strong aquaphilia.

english_meaning: Fear of water. An intense and irrational fear of water that can affect a person's daily life, often causing anxiety around swimming pools, lakes, oceans, or even bathing.
example_sentence: Her aquaphobia prevented her from learning to swim. He felt anxious near the beach due to his aquaphobia. Aquaphobia can make even a short bath stressful. Therapists often help patients overcome aquaphobia gradually.

english_meaning: A person born under the zodiac sign of Aquarius. Relating to the sign Aquarius or to those born under it. Describing qualities such as independence and originality linked to Aquarius. A member of an early Christian group that used water instead of wine, in historical use.
example_sentence: As an Aquarian, she values her freedom greatly. The magazine printed the Aquarian horoscope for the week. He shows many typical Aquarian traits. Aquarian friends often enjoy unusual ideas.

english_meaning: A transparent tank or container filled with water in which fish, aquatic plants, and other water animals are kept for display, study, or as pets. A public place or building where many kinds of sea creatures are kept and shown to visitors.
example_sentence: We bought a new aquarium for our living room and filled it with colorful fish. Children love to visit the city aquarium to see sharks and jellyfish. The aquarium needs to be cleaned regularly to keep the fish healthy. He decorated his aquarium with plants, stones, and lights.

english_meaning: Living or growing in water. Relating to water or taking place in water. Connected with water sports or water habitats.
example_sentence: Fish and frogs are aquatic creatures. The lake supports many aquatic plants. She won a medal in an aquatic event. Pollution is destroying aquatic life in the river.

english_meaning: Relating to or containing water. Dissolved in water, especially in chemistry. Watery in appearance or consistency. Formed by the action of water, used of certain rocks and deposits.
example_sentence: The chemist prepared an aqueous solution of salt. Aqueous liquids conduct electricity when they contain ions. The eye contains a clear aqueous fluid. These rocks are aqueous in origin.

english_meaning: Suitable for growing crops. Capable of being ploughed and used to produce food. Relating to land that can be farmed. Fit for cultivation. Used to describe soil, land, or fields where crops can be grown successfully. Arable land is essential for agriculture and food production.
example_sentence: Much of the country's arable land is used to grow wheat. The farmer purchased a large piece of arable land near the river. Climate change is reducing the amount of arable soil worldwide. Only a small portion of the mountainous region is arable. The government is encouraging farmers to protect arable areas from urban development.

english_meaning: The delicate, web-like middle layer of the three meninges. A thin membrane lying between the dura mater and the pia mater. The layer beneath which cerebrospinal fluid circulates around the brain and spinal cord.
example_sentence: The arachnoid mater looks like a fine spider's web. Cerebrospinal fluid flows below the arachnoid mater. The arachnoid mater has no blood vessels of its own. Bleeding under the arachnoid mater is a medical emergency.

english_meaning: Extreme fear of spiders. A psychological condition in which a person experiences intense and irrational fear of spiders. This fear can cause anxiety, panic attacks, avoidance behavior, and discomfort even when seeing pictures or thinking about spiders.
example_sentence: She avoided the basement because of her arachnophobia. His arachnophobia made it impossible for him to enter a room with spiders. Even a tiny spider triggers his arachnophobia. Therapy helped her manage her arachnophobia over time.

english_meaning: In a way that uses personal power unfairly and without considering people's rights and wishes. In a way that does not seem to be based on a reason, system or plan and sometimes seems unfair.
example_sentence: The leaders of groups were chosen arbitrarily. The political frontiers in Africa were often arbitrarily drawn up by the old colonial powers. He arbitrarily decided to take the part.

english_meaning: Not seeming to be based on a reason, system or plan and sometimes seeming unfair. Using power without limits and without considering other people. Based on chance rather than being planned or based on reason. Using unlimited personal power without considering other people's rights or wishes
example_sentence: The choice of players for the team seemed completely arbitrary. He makes unpredictable, arbitrary decisions. The refugees were found during an arbitrary vehicle check at the ferry port. The company has been the subject of an arbitrary take-over.

english_meaning: To officially settle an argument or a disagreement between two people or groups. To make a judgment in an argument, usually because asked to do so by those involved.
example_sentence: The committee was created to arbitrate between management & unions. A referee was hired to arbitrate the dispute. An outside adviser has been brought in to arbitrate the dispute between the management and the union. I've been asked to arbitrate between the opposing sides.

english_meaning: The process of settling a dispute between two parties by referring it to a neutral third person or panel whose decision is usually binding. A formal method of resolving disagreements outside the court system. It is commonly used in labour disputes, business conflicts, and international issues.
example_sentence: The two countries agreed to settle the dispute through arbitration. The labour union demanded arbitration in the wage dispute. The contract included a clause for compulsory arbitration. International arbitration helped end the long conflict. The arbitration ruling was accepted by both companies.

english_meaning: An independent person or body officially appointed to settle a dispute. A person who has the power to make decisions and judge a situation. Someone chosen to resolve a disagreement between two parties. An authoritative person who acts as a referee in a conflict. A neutral party who facilitates a compromise.
example_sentence: The arbitrator ruled in favor of the union after long deliberations. Both sides agreed to accept the decision of the impartial arbitrator. An experienced arbitrator can prevent a case from going to court. The dispute was finally settled by a private arbitrator.
