english_meaning: A place where different kinds of trees and woody plants are grown, studied, and displayed for scientific, educational, or recreational purposes. A specialized botanical garden devoted mainly to trees, shrubs, and other woody plants. It is used for conservation, scientific research, education, and public enjoyment. Arboretums often contain rare, native, and exotic tree species arranged and labeled for visitors and researchers.
example_sentence: The university maintains an arboretum for botanical research and education. Visitors enjoyed walking through the arboretum and observing rare tree species. The arboretum contains hundreds of native and exotic trees from around the world. Students visited the arboretum to learn about plant conservation.

english_meaning: A specialist trained in the care and maintenance of trees. A professional who plants, prunes, diagnoses, and treats trees and woody plants. An expert in tree safety and management.
example_sentence: An arborist inspected the damaged oak tree. We hired a certified arborist to prune the branches safely. The arborist diagnosed a fungal disease in the tree. She trained as an arborist after studying forestry.

english_meaning: A curved line that forms part of the circumference of a circle. Any smooth curve joining two points. A luminous electrical discharge between two electrodes. The curved path followed by a projectile.
example_sentence: The arc of the rainbow spanned the entire sky. An arc is measured in degrees. The basketball followed a perfect arc into the hoop. The welder created an electric arc to join the metals.

english_meaning: Known or understood by very few people. Mysterious. Secret. Obscure. Hidden from general knowledge. Difficult to understand. Used to describe knowledge, practices, or information that is specialized, unusual, or accessible only to a small group of experts or initiated people.
example_sentence: The professor specialized in the arcane rituals of ancient civilizations. Only a few scholars understand the arcane symbols carved on the stone. The book explores the arcane knowledge of medieval alchemists. He explained the arcane rules of the old game with great patience. Many arcane traditions are slowly disappearing in the modern world.

english_meaning: A curved structure spanning an opening and supporting weight above it. A curved shape resembling an arc. To form or cause to form a curved shape. Chief or principal in rank or importance.
example_sentence: The stone arch has stood for centuries. The cat arched its back when frightened. The bridge features several beautiful arches. He is the arch rival of the champion.

english_meaning: A main or strongest rival. A person, group, or organization that is a long-standing and intense opponent, often competing repeatedly in the same field or for the same goal.
example_sentence: India and Pakistan are often described as arch-rivals in cricket. The two companies became arch-rivals after competing for the same market. Sherlock Holmes faced his arch-rival Professor Moriarty. The debate turned intense when she confronted her arch-rival.

english_meaning: The scientific study of human history and prehistory through the systematic excavation of sites and the analysis of physical artifacts. The discipline that uncovers, examines, and interprets material remains of past civilizations. A field combining science, history, and fieldwork to reconstruct how ancient human beings lived. The systematic investigation of cultural remains, including tools, buildings, and texts from earlier periods of history.
example_sentence: Archaeology has revealed a great deal about the daily life of ancient Egyptian civilization. She pursued a university degree in archaeology because of her deep fascination with ancient cultures. The archaeology team uncovered ruins confidently dating back more than two thousand years. Archaeology is a discipline that skillfully combines science, history, and careful detective work. Their latest archaeology project unearthed beautiful pottery dating from the Bronze Age.

english_meaning: An extinct bird-like dinosaur from the Late Jurassic period. A fossil creature showing features of both reptiles and birds. An important evolutionary link between dinosaurs and modern birds. A feathered animal with teeth, claws, and a long bony tail.
example_sentence: The museum displays a rare fossil of an Archaeopteryx. Archaeopteryx had feathers but also sharp teeth. Scientists study Archaeopteryx to understand how birds evolved. The first Archaeopteryx specimen was found in Germany.

english_meaning: Something very old and no longer commonly used in language, style, or ideas. Very old or from an earlier historical period. Outdated in language or style. No longer commonly understood or used. Belonging to an ancient stage of development
example_sentence: The word “thou” is an archaic form of “you”. Some archaic laws are still found in old legal books. He used archaic expressions in his poetry. The museum displayed archaic tools used by early humans.

english_meaning: A word, phrase, or style that is no longer in common use. The use of old-fashioned language or customs. Something surviving from an earlier time that now seems outdated.
example_sentence: The poem is full of archaisms that puzzle modern readers. Using 'thou' today is a clear archaism. The lawyer's language was weighed down by legal archaisms. Some archaisms survive only in religious texts.

english_meaning: An angel of the highest rank in religious tradition. A chief or principal messenger of God, such as Gabriel or Michael. Figuratively, a person regarded as exceptionally noble or protective. A leading spiritual being placed above ordinary angels.
example_sentence: The painting shows an archangel with a flaming sword. According to tradition, the archangel Gabriel brought the revelation. Children listened closely to the story of the archangel. He guarded the family like a watchful archangel.

english_meaning: The study of human history through the excavation of sites and analysis of artefacts. The scientific examination of ancient remains, buildings, and objects. The discipline concerned with recovering and interpreting material traces of past societies.
example_sentence: Archeology has revealed much about the ancient city of Mohenjo-daro. He devoted his life to the archeology of the Indus Valley. Students of archeology spend weeks at excavation sites. New technology has transformed modern archeology.

english_meaning: A very typical or perfect example of a particular kind of person or thing. An original model or pattern from which all others of the same type are copied or developed. A recurring symbol, character type, or narrative pattern that appears consistently across different cultures and time periods. A universal image or theme that exists in the collective human unconscious, as described in Jungian psychology.
example_sentence: The heroic warrior is a classic archetype found in stories and legends around the world. She became the archetype of the selfless and dedicated nurse in the minds of the public. The villain in the story closely followed the archetype of the corrupt and power-hungry politician. Jung identified several universal archetypes that recur throughout the depths of the human psyche. The wise and guiding mentor remains one of the most beloved archetypes in world literature and film.

english_meaning: A small but serious weakness in a person or thing that is otherwise strong. A single vulnerable point that can cause complete failure. A hidden flaw that makes someone easy to defeat. In Greek mythology, the only part of the hero Achilles' body where he could be wounded.
example_sentence: Overconfidence has always been his Achilles' heel. Poor defence is the Achilles' heel of this otherwise strong team. Her impatience proved to be the Achilles' heel of an excellent plan. The weak battery is the Achilles' heel of this smartphone.

english_meaning: A senior priest or monk in some Eastern Christian churches. The head of a monastery or group of monasteries. An honorary title given to an important monastic leader. A church official ranking above an ordinary abbot in certain traditions.
example_sentence: The archimandrite led the prayers in the monastery chapel. Visitors asked the archimandrite about the history of the community. The title of archimandrite is respected in many Eastern churches. An archimandrite supervised several monks and novices.

english_meaning: An ancient Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, and inventor from Syracuse in Sicily, widely regarded as one of the greatest scientists of antiquity. He is credited with discovering fundamental principles of levers, buoyancy, and approximating the value of pi. The inventor of the Archimedes screw and designer of ingenious war machines used to defend Syracuse against Rome. Known for his famous exclamation of Eureka upon discovering the principle of water displacement.
example_sentence: Archimedes discovered the principle of buoyancy while stepping into his bathtub, and reportedly cried Eureka. Archimedes is universally credited with the famous and joyful exclamation of Eureka upon his great discovery. Archimedes designed highly effective war machines to defend the city of Syracuse from Roman attacks. The foundational works of Archimedes continued to influence mathematics and engineering for many centuries. Students of physics still study the lever principle and the law of buoyancy credited to Archimedes.

english_meaning: An old Russian unit of linear measurement equal to approximately 28 inches or 71 centimeters. A traditional unit used in Russia, Turkey, and parts of Central Asia before the widespread adoption of the metric system. A historical measurement standard used in trade, construction, and fabric measurement across the Russian Empire. A pre-metric unit commonly encountered in historical Russian documents, blueprints, and records.
synonyms: ["Arshin","Russian yard","Traditional unit of length","Historical measure","Imperial unit"]
example_sentence: The old architectural blueprint measured the dimensions of the room in archins. Fabric was traditionally sold and measured by the archin in nineteenth-century Russian markets. The archin was officially replaced by the metric system in Russia in the early twentieth century. Historical property records from the Russian Empire often list all dimensions in archins. The tailor used archins to calculate precisely how much fabric would be needed for the garment.

english_meaning: A large group or chain of islands. A sea or stretch of water containing many islands. A cluster of scattered islands lying close together. Something spread out in a scattered, island-like pattern.
example_sentence: Indonesia is the largest archipelago in the world. We sailed through a beautiful archipelago at sunrise. The archipelago is home to rare birds and plants. Fishermen from the archipelago sell their catch on the mainland.

english_meaning: A place or collection where records, documents, or data are stored for long-term keeping. A collection of historical documents or records kept for reference. A place where digital files are stored but not actively used. To store information safely for future access.
example_sentence: The company keeps old files in an archive. She searched the archive for historical photos. Please archive these emails for future use. The newspaper archive contains articles from 1950.

english_meaning: Very passionate, enthusiastic, or deeply devoted. Showing strong feelings, enthusiasm, or intense passion toward something or someone. It can describe love, support, belief, or interest.
example_sentence: She is an ardent supporter of education for girls. He gave an ardent speech about climate change. They are ardent fans of classical music. The teacher showed ardent dedication to her students.

english_meaning: Requiring or involving great effort, endurance, or difficulty to complete or achieve. Hard to accomplish because of the very high level of exertion or perseverance required. Testing one's physical or mental strength to the fullest extent over a sustained period. Demanding sustained determination, considerable labor, and strong willpower to see through to the end.
example_sentence: The long trek to the mountain summit was both physically and mentally arduous. She completed the arduous task with remarkable quiet determination and without complaint. The process of writing and defending a doctoral thesis is truly arduous and deeply demanding. Training for the championship was an arduous but ultimately very rewarding experience. The arduous journey across the desert tested the endurance and willpower of every single traveler.

english_meaning: A place where events, sports, or competitions happen. It also means a field of activity or area of life. A large open space or enclosed area designed for sports, entertainment, or public events. It can also mean any field of action, conflict, or public activity such as politics, business, or debate.
example_sentence: After 30 years in the political arena, our local member of parliament is retiring next year. She entered the political arena as a young woman. He said he hoped to join the entrepreneurial business arena. The boxing match was held in a large arena. She entered the political arena at a young age. The new stadium is the biggest arena in the city.

english_meaning: To exchange opposing views with someone, often in an angry way. To give reasons in support of an idea or against it. To try to persuade others by presenting evidence and logic. To suggest strongly that something is true.
example_sentence: They often argue about money and household chores. She argued that the policy would harm small farmers. He argued his case calmly before the committee. The evidence argues strongly in favour of an early release.

english_meaning: To defeat someone in an argument by reasoning better or proving them wrong. To persuade someone to lower a price or demand through discussion.
example_sentence: The teacher tried to argue the girl down, but she couldn’t. She argue him down ten percent. She argued him down in court. He was argued down by his opponent. He managed to argue the shopkeeper down to a lower price. No one could argue her down once she made up her mind.

english_meaning: To discuss something thoroughly, especially to reach a conclusion, agreement, or solution. To settle a matter by reasoning or debate. It’s a constructive discussion, not just a quarrel.
example_sentence: If we can’t argue our differences out, we’ll have to take them to court. They argued out the proposal. The matter was argued out in the meeting. They argued out the differences and finally reached an agreement. Let’s argue out this issue before making a final decision. The team argued out the plan until everyone was satisfied. We can argue it out later instead of fighting now.

english_meaning: An angry exchange of opposing views between people. A reason or set of reasons given to support or oppose an idea. A discussion in which people express different opinions. A summary of the main theme or line of reasoning in a text.
example_sentence: They had a bitter argument over the property. His argument in favour of reform was very convincing. The book opens with a clear statement of its argument. There is a strong argument for reducing working hours.

english_meaning: The process of forming reasons and drawing conclusions in support of a claim. A systematic discourse or set of reasons presented to persuade someone. The action or technique of debating or arguing a point. A collective series of statements intended to establish a proposition. The study of how conclusions can be reached through logical reasoning.
example_sentence: His complex argumentation failed to convince the jury of his innocence. The professor focused on the formal rules of logical argumentation in the seminar. Effective argumentation requires both sound evidence and clear reasoning. The book provides a brilliant piece of argumentation against the new economic policy.

english_meaning: A form of government in which power is held by the nobility or a privileged upper class. Also refers to the highest social class in a country, often with hereditary titles and wealth.
example_sentence: The ancient Greeks debated whether aristocracy or democracy was better. Many members of the aristocracy owned large estates. The novel portrayed life within the English aristocracy. In theory, aristocracy means rule by the best-qualified citizens.

english_meaning: A member of the highest social class, usually holding a hereditary title. A person of noble birth or high rank. Someone who behaves with the elegance or superiority associated with nobility. A person regarded as the finest example of a particular group or class.
example_sentence: The aristocrat lived in a grand country house. Many aristocrats lost their estates after the revolution. She carried herself like a true aristocrat. He was an aristocrat among modern painters.

english_meaning: A person belonging to the highest social class. A member of the aristocracy, usually someone from a noble family who traditionally holds social, political, or economic power. The status is often inherited and linked with wealth, land ownership, or royal connections.
example_sentence: The aristocrate lived in a grand mansion outside the city. Many aristocrates played key roles in early European politics. Despite being an aristocrate, he supported social reforms. The novel describes the life of an aristocrate during wartime.

english_meaning: Belonging to or typical of the aristocracy or nobility. Having the characteristics of upper-class elegance and refinement. Relating to a ruling class of hereditary privilege. Exhibiting sophisticated or superior manners.
example_sentence: She has aristocratic features and bearing. The aristocratic family owned vast estates. His aristocratic manners impressed everyone. The mansion reflects aristocratic taste.

english_meaning: Relating to the philosophy or teachings of the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle. Following the logical and empirical methods of Aristotle. Concerning Aristotelian logic, ethics, or metaphysics. Based on observation and systematic reasoning.
example_sentence: The Aristotelian approach emphasizes observation. Aristotelian logic influenced Western philosophy. His reasoning follows Aristotelian principles. The Aristotelian worldview dominated medieval thought.

english_meaning: A Greek philosopher and polymath during the Classical period in Ancient Greece. A student of Plato, he was the founder of the Lyceum and the Peripatetic school of philosophy and the Aristotelian tradition.
example_sentence: Aristotle's writings cover many subjects including physics, biology, and ethics. He studied the works of Aristotle in college. The teacher quoted Aristotle to explain the concept of logic. Aristotle is considered one of the fathers of Western philosophy.

english_meaning: The branch of mathematics dealing with basic operations of numbers. The study of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Basic mathematical calculation and computation. The foundational operations with numbers.
example_sentence: Children learn arithmetic in elementary school. Basic arithmetic skills are essential for daily life. The problem requires simple arithmetic. Mental arithmetic helps improve calculation speed.

english_meaning: The averages calculated by adding numbers and dividing by the count. Simple averages found by summing values and dividing by how many there are. The most common type of average used in statistics. Central values calculated through addition and division.
example_sentence: Calculate the arithmetic means of these data sets. The arithmetic means provide a simple measure of central tendency. Arithmetic means are easy to understand and compute. We compared the arithmetic means of both groups.

english_meaning: A sequence of numbers where each term after the first is obtained by adding a constant. A number series with a common difference between consecutive terms. A progression like 2, 4, 6, 8 where each increases by the same amount. A linear sequence with regular intervals.
example_sentence: The sequence 3, 7, 11, 15 is an arithmetic progression. Find the 10th term of this arithmetic progression. Arithmetic progressions have a constant common difference. The formula helps calculate any term in an arithmetic progression.

english_meaning: The sum of terms in an arithmetic sequence. A series where each term increases by a constant difference. The total obtained by adding all numbers in an arithmetic progression. A sequence sum with a common difference between consecutive terms.
synonyms: ["Sum of arithmetic sequence","Arithmetic progression sum","Sequential sum with constant difference"]
example_sentence: The arithmetic series 1+2+3+4+5 equals 15. Calculate the sum of this arithmetic series. Arithmetic series have a constant difference between terms. The formula helps find the sum of an arithmetic series quickly.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving arithmetic. Concerning mathematical calculations with numbers. Based on or using numerical operations. Of or pertaining to computation.
example_sentence: The solution requires arithmetical operations. Her arithmetical skills are excellent. The problem involves simple arithmetical reasoning. Arithmetical accuracy is important in accounting.

english_meaning: Fear of numbers or mathematics. A strong and persistent fear of numbers, calculations, or dealing with mathematics, which may cause anxiety, avoidance, or distress.
example_sentence: His arithmophobia made it hard for him to manage his finances. She avoids math classes due to her arithmophobia. Arithmophobia can interfere with everyday tasks like shopping or budgeting. Therapy helped him gradually overcome his arithmophobia.

english_meaning: Either of the two upper limbs of the human body from the shoulder to the hand. A part of something shaped like or working like an arm, such as the arm of a chair or a record player. A branch or division of an organization or military force. To supply someone with weapons or equipment. To prepare something for action, such as arming an alarm.
example_sentence: He broke his arm while playing cricket. She carried the baby in her arms. The research arm of the company is based in Lahore. The guards were armed with modern rifles.

english_meaning: A large fleet of ships. An organized group of warships or a large number of vehicles, aircraft, or other things moving together, often for military or strategic purposes.
example_sentence: The navy sent an armada to protect the coastline. The company launched an armada of new products this year. The Spanish Armada tried to invade England in 1588. An armada of drones monitored the forest fire.

english_meaning: The last battle between good and evil before the Day of Judgment. The site or time of a final and conclusive battle between the forces of good and evil. A dramatic and catastrophic conflict, especially one seen as likely to destroy the world or human race.
example_sentence: The movie depicted a nuclear Armageddon. Some religious texts prophesy an Armageddon. The two superpowers seemed on the brink of Armageddon. It felt like we were witnessing the financial Armageddon of the global markets.

english_meaning: A person who gives opinions, advice, or criticism about something they have not experienced or are not actively involved in. Someone who comments on or judges a situation, profession, or activity from a distance without practical knowledge, experience, or responsibility. The term suggests easy criticism from comfort, often without understanding real challenges.
example_sentence: He is just an armchair critic who has never managed a real business. Armchair critics often underestimate how difficult fieldwork can be. Instead of helping, he became an armchair critic of the project. The team ignored armchair critics and focused on real feedback from experts.

english_meaning: A person who believes in the theological system of Jacobus Arminius, emphasizing human free will in salvation rather than predestination. Describing something based on or influenced by Arminian theology, stressing human free will.
example_sentence: He is an Arminian who values free will. Many Arminians attend this church. Arminians disagree with strict Calvinist doctrines. An Arminian view of salvation emphasizes choice. The sermon offered an Arminian perspective. Their Arminian beliefs reject predestination.

english_meaning: A theological system within Protestant Christianity based on the teachings of Jacobus Arminius. It teaches that human beings have free will to respond to God's grace. It rejects the idea that God has unconditionally chosen certain people for salvation. It supports conditional election, universal atonement, and the possibility that believers may fall from grace.
synonyms: ["In theological context","Free will theology","Remonstrant theology","Wesleyan theology"]
example_sentence: Arminianism teaches that people have the freedom to choose salvation. Many Methodists follow Arminianism in their theology. Arminianism opposes the idea of unconditional predestination. The debate between Arminianism and Calvinism shaped Protestant history.

english_meaning: The metal coverings formerly worn by knights or warriors to protect the body in battle. Protective layer on a vehicle or ship.
example_sentence: The knight polished his armour before heading into the tournament. Modern tanks are protected by heavy steel and ceramic armour. He wore a suit of armour as part of his historical costume. The turtle's thick shell acts as a natural form of armour.

english_meaning: Part of body under arm where joins the shoulder. The hollow beneath the junction of the arm and shoulder.   A very dirty, unpleasant, or undesirable place (Informal meaning).
example_sentence: The area on the body where people apply deodorant is an example of an armpit. The city has been called the armpit of America. He felt pain in his armpit after lifting heavy boxes. The doctor checked the swelling under her armpit. Sweat stains appeared around the armpit area of his shirt.

english_meaning: A pleasant smell. A distinctive, usually pleasant fragrance especially from food, flowers, or substances.
example_sentence: The aroma of fresh coffee filled the room. I love the aroma of baked bread. The kitchen was full of the aroma of spices. The aroma of roses spread in the garden.

english_meaning: Having a pleasant and strong smell or fragrance. Something that has a sweet, pleasant, spicy, or noticeable smell. It is often used for food, flowers, spices, perfumes, oils, herbs, and plants. In chemistry, it also refers to compounds containing a special ring structure like benzene.
example_sentence: The kitchen was filled with aromatic spices. She bought an aromatic perfume from the market. Fresh aromatic herbs improved the taste of the soup. The garden became aromatic after the rain.

english_meaning: The action or fact of arousing or being aroused. A state of physiological alertness, wakefulness, and readiness to respond to stimuli. The act of stimulating sexual excitement.
example_sentence: The sound of the alarm caused a sudden arousal from sleep. Emotional arousal can affect performance. The novel described scenes of intense sexual arousal. The coffee produced a state of mental arousal.

english_meaning: A person who organises or plans something so that it happens smoothly. A musician who adapts a composition for particular voices or instruments. Someone who puts things in a proper or pleasing order. A person who settles the details of an agreement or event.
example_sentence: The wedding arranger handled every detail of the ceremony. He worked as an arranger for several film songs. A skilled flower arranger prepared the hall. The arranger of the tour booked all the hotels.

english_meaning: The act of coming to or reaching a place. A person or thing that has come or been brought to a place. The moment when someone or something begins to exist or be used. The appearance of something new in a particular field. The reaching of a conclusion or decision.
example_sentence: We are waiting for the arrival of the train. Her arrival brought great joy to the family. The arrival of the internet changed our lives. A new arrival in the neighborhood was warmly welcomed.

english_meaning: Having an exaggerated sense of one’s own importance or abilities. Overbearing, prideful, or haughty. Proud in a way that shows you think you are better than others.
example_sentence: He was so arrogant that he refused to listen to anyone’s advice. The manager’s arrogant attitude made the team feel undervalued. She answered the question in an arrogant tone, ignoring the teacher’s guidance. His arrogant behavior at the party offended many guests.

english_meaning: A building or place where weapons, ammunition, and military equipment are stored or made. A collection or supply of resources or tools used for a particular purpose
example_sentence: The army stored all its weapons in a secure arsenal. The new arsenal included advanced missiles and tanks. Knowledge and education are powerful tools in your arsenal for success. The police discovered an illegal arsenal of guns and explosives in the basement.

english_meaning: The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property. The malicious burning of another's house or property, or in some statutes, the burning of one's own property to collect insurance.
example_sentence: The police are treating the fire as a case of arson. He was convicted of arson and sentenced to ten years in prison. The warehouse was destroyed in an arson attack. Arson is a serious felony.

english_meaning: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart to the body. A thick-walled, muscular vessel that withstands high blood pressure. An important route or channel of communication or transport.
example_sentence: An artery carries oxygen-rich blood to the tissues. A blocked artery can lead to a heart attack. The nurse felt the pulse in his wrist artery. This highway is the main artery of the city.

english_meaning: Painful inflammation and stiffness of the joints. A medical condition affecting joints, causing pain, swelling, and reduced motion.
example_sentence: My grandmother suffers from severe arthritis in her hands. He takes medication to manage his arthritis pain. Early diagnosis of arthritis is important. The cold weather makes my arthritis worse.

english_meaning: Relating to the legendary King Arthur and his knights. Describing the medieval stories, romances, and legends connected with Arthur's court. Characteristic of the chivalric world of Camelot and the Round Table. Belonging to the body of literature based on these legends.
example_sentence: The museum holds a fine collection of Arthurian manuscripts. She is writing a thesis on Arthurian legend. The film draws heavily on Arthurian themes of honour and loyalty. Merlin is one of the best known Arthurian characters.

english_meaning: A vegetable made up of thick green leaves around a tender edible heart. A flower bud eaten boiled, grilled, or preserved in oil. The tall thistle-like plant that produces this bud. A delicacy served in Mediterranean cooking.
example_sentence: She boiled the artichoke and served it with butter. Artichoke hearts are delicious in a salad. The artichoke plant grows quite tall. He learned how to trim an artichoke properly.

english_meaning: A piece of writing on a particular subject published in a newspaper, magazine, or website. A separate item or object, especially one of a set. A clause or section in a legal document or agreement. In grammar, a word such as a, an, or the used before a noun.
example_sentence: She wrote an article about climate change for the magazine. Every article in the shop is on sale this week. Article five of the agreement deals with payment terms. Students often struggle with the correct use of the definite article.

english_meaning: To express or explain your thoughts or feelings clearly in words. To speak, pronounce or play something in a clear way. To be related to something so that together the two parts form a whole, To be joined to something else by a joint, so that movement is possible, to join something in this way. Good at expressing ideas or feelings clearly in words. Clearly expressed or pronounced.
example_sentence: She gave a witty, entertaining, and articulate speech. He found it difficult to articulate his feelings. The bones articulate with each other at the joint. A good leader must be able to articulate a clear vision. They need an articulate spokesperson for their cause.

english_meaning: The formation of clear and distinct sounds in speech. The action of putting into words an idea or feeling. The state of being jointed; a joint or juncture between bones or cartilages in the skeleton of a vertebrate.
example_sentence: The speech therapist worked on the child's articulation. His articulation of the company's goals was very clear. The elbow allows for articulation between the upper and lower arm. Her clear articulation made her easy to understand.

english_meaning: An object made or shaped by humans, especially one that has historical, cultural, scientific, or archaeological importance. A historical object made by humans, such as tools, pottery, weapons, or jewelry. An object showing evidence of human culture or civilization. In science or medicine, a false or misleading result caused by an external factor during observation or testing. In technology or digital media, an unwanted distortion or error in sound, image, or data.
example_sentence: The museum displayed ancient artifacts from the Indus Valley Civilization. Archaeologists discovered several gold artifacts during the excavation. The strange mark on the X-ray was only an imaging artifact. Poor internet connection created digital artifacts in the video.

english_meaning: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially to trick or deceive. Skilled or artistic workmanship. Trickery or deception through clever means. An ingenious device or technique. Craft or ingenuity in making something.
example_sentence: His success was achieved through artifice rather than merit. The painting showed great artifice in technique. She used artifice to manipulate the situation. The scheme was full of artifice and deception.

english_meaning: The quality of being made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally. The quality of being not natural or sincere. Lack of naturalness or spontaneity.
example_sentence: I was struck by the artificiality of her smile. The artificiality of the flavors in the candy was obvious. There's a certain artificiality to the dialogue in the play. He disliked the artificiality of Hollywood.

english_meaning: A skilled worker who makes useful or decorative objects by hand. A craftsperson trained in a particular traditional trade. A person or small producer whose goods are made carefully in limited quantities using specialized skill.
example_sentence: The artisan carved a delicate pattern into the wooden door. Local artisans sell handmade pottery at the weekend market. Each loaf is prepared by an artisan baker. The village supports artisans who preserve traditional crafts.

english_meaning: A person who creates paintings, drawings, sculptures, or other visual art. A person who practices a creative art such as music, dance, theater, writing, or filmmaking. A performer or entertainer. A person who displays exceptional imagination or skill in an activity.
example_sentence: The artist displayed her paintings in a city gallery. He works as a makeup artist for film productions. The young artist wrote and performed her own songs. That chef is a true artist in the kitchen.

english_meaning: Relating to art, artists, or the creation of art. Having natural creative ability or skill. Showing imagination, sensitivity, taste, or a strong awareness of beauty. Designed or performed with creative intention rather than only practical purpose.
example_sentence: She has an artistic talent for painting landscapes. The building is admired for its artistic design. He took an artistic approach to arranging the exhibition. The director defended the unusual ending as an artistic choice.

english_meaning: The freedom to alter facts, reality, language, or conventional rules for a creative purpose. Permission accepted in art or literature to depart from strict accuracy. A deliberate creative deviation used to improve expression, drama, or effect.
example_sentence: The film used artistic license to simplify the historical timeline. Through artistic license, the painter gave the landscape brighter colors. The novelist took artistic license with several real events. A little artistic license made the stage adaptation more dramatic.

english_meaning: In a way that shows artistic skill, creativity, imagination, or sensitivity to beauty. In relation to art, artistic quality, or creative achievement. In a visually graceful, tasteful, or expressive manner.
example_sentence: The hall was artistically decorated with flowers and lanterns. The film is artistically ambitious but easy to understand. She arranged the photographs artistically on the wall. He has developed artistically since joining the theater group.

english_meaning: A leafy salad green with slender leaves and a peppery, slightly bitter taste. A herb-like vegetable eaten raw in salads or scattered over cooked dishes. The plant grown for these edible leaves. A green widely used in Mediterranean cooking.
example_sentence: She topped the pizza with fresh arugula. Arugula has a sharp, peppery flavour. The salad mixed arugula with cherry tomatoes. Arugula grows quickly in cool weather.

english_meaning: Used to strongly affirm that something is true. The speaker calls God as proof of honesty. I swear it is true. I am completely honest. I promise sincerely. I strongly affirm the truth. I truly mean what I say.
synonyms: ["I swear","I promise","Honestly","Truly","I give you my word","On my honor","I solemnly swear"]
antonyms: ["I doubt it","Maybe","I am not sure","Possibly","I guess"]
example_sentence: As God is my witness, I never told anyone your secret. As God is my witness, I will always stand by you. As God is my witness, I didn’t take that money. As God is my witness, I’ll make sure justice is done.

english_meaning: Extremely dry, with no moisture at all. Completely lacking water or wetness. Very parched or arid. Totally dehydrated. Without a trace of liquid.
example_sentence: The ground is as dry as a bone after weeks without rain. My throat feels as dry as a bone. The old well is as dry as a bone now. These leaves are as dry as a bone and will burn quickly.

word: As far as I am concerned
english_meaning: In my opinion. According to my thinking. From my point of view. Personally speaking. As I see the matter. Regarding my feelings or decision. In my judgment. So far as my interest or opinion is involved.
antonyms: ["Objectively speaking","Generally speaking","According to others","From everyone’s perspective","Public opinion says"]
example_sentence: As far as I am concerned, honesty is the best policy. As far as I am concerned, the meeting should start on time. As far as I am concerned, education is very important for success. As far as I am concerned, this plan is better than the previous one.

english_meaning: Very healthy, strong, and full of energy. In perfect physical condition.
example_sentence: At 70, he is still as fit as a fiddle. After a week of rest, he is now as fit as a fiddle and ready to work again. Even at the age of seventy, my grandfather is as fit as a fiddle. She exercises every day, eats healthy food, and stays as fit as a fiddle. Don’t worry about me, I’m as fit as a fiddle after the check-up.

english_meaning: Occurring or happening in the recent past. It describes a trend or behavior that has developed recently. It is used to indicate that something has been the case over the last few days or weeks. It points to a shift from older patterns to newer ones in recent times.
example_sentence: He has been working extremely long hours as of late. The weather has been surprisingly warm as of late. She has shown a lot of interest in painting as of late. Their performance on the field has improved significantly as of late.

english_meaning: From this current moment forward. It refers to the present time and circumstances. It indicates the status of something at the exact time of speaking. It suggests that a situation is true right now but might change in the future.
synonyms: ["Currently","Presently","At Present","For The Time Being","Right Now","At This Moment","Up To Now","For Now","At This Time"]
antonyms: ["In The Past","Previously","Formerly","Before","Long Ago","In The Future","Eventually","Ultimately","Down The Line"]
example_sentence: As of now, we have not received any updates from the management. The project is fully funded as of now. As of now, she intends to accept the job offer in London. There are no plans to change the schedule as of now.

english_meaning: It refers to something that has not happened or been done up to the present moment. It indicates a state of affairs continuing until now. It means so far or up until the current time. It is often used in negative statements to show that an expected event has not occurred.
synonyms: ["So Far","Up To Now","Until Now","Hitherto","Thus Far","To Date","Yet","Up To The Present","Up Till Now","Heretofore","As Yet"]
antonyms: ["Already","Previously","Formerly","Before","Earlier","In The Past","Long Ago","Then","At That Time","Long Since"]
example_sentence: We have not received any official confirmation as of yet. The results of the medical tests are unknown as of yet. As of yet, no one has claimed responsibility for the incident. She has not decided which college to attend as of yet.

english_meaning: It refers to something in the exact sense of the word or strict definition. It means exactly that or by that name. It is used to describe someone or something in its current capacity or role. It indicates that a preceding statement is the reason for what follows.
synonyms: ["Strictly Speaking","Exactly","In Itself","Per Se","By Itself","Intrinsically","By Definition","Fundamentally","Essentially","In Essence","In Its Own Right"]
example_sentence: I am not a qualified mechanic as such, but I can fix basic car problems. The money was not a loan as such, but rather a generous gift. He is the manager of the department and, as such, makes the final decisions. There are no fixed rules as such, only general guidelines to follow.

english_meaning: In a straight line between two places, without following roads or natural obstacles. Used to describe the shortest geographical distance.
synonyms: ["In a straight line","Directly","By the shortest route","Geographically"]
example_sentence: The village is only five miles away as the crow flies. As the crow flies, the airport is close, but the road takes much longer. The two towns are ten kilometers apart as the crow flies. Our houses are near each other as the crow flies, although a hill lies between them.

word: As the king, so are the subjects
english_meaning: People usually follow the behavior, character, and habits of their leader. Good leaders create good followers, while bad leaders influence people negatively. Leadership influences society. Example is stronger than words. People imitate authority figures. Moral behavior spreads from the top. Culture of a group depends on its leader
synonyms: ["Like leader","Like followers","A fish rots from the head","People follow their leader","Like father","Like son","Leadership shapes behavior"]
antonyms: ["Good people can resist bad leadership","Independent minds do not blindly follow leaders","Character comes from within","Followers may differ from leaders"]
example_sentence: The company employees became disciplined after the new manager arrived because as the king, so are the subjects. In a family where parents speak politely, children often behave respectfully too. As the king, so are the subjects. The citizens started ignoring rules because their leaders were also careless. As the king, so are the subjects. The school developed a culture of honesty under its sincere principal. As the king, so are the subjects.

word: As you sow so shall you reap
english_meaning: Your actions decide results, Your actions determine your results. Whatever you do, good or bad, will come back to you in the same way.
synonyms: ["What goes around comes around","You reap what you sow","Every action has a consequence","Cause and effect"]
antonyms: ["Luck decides everything","Fate is unavoidable","Things happen without reason"]
example_sentence: If you study hard, you’ll pass the exam, as you sow, so shall you reap. He mistreated others for years, and now no one helps him, as you sow, so shall you reap. Those who help people in need are always blessed, as you sow, so shall you reap. She was kind to everyone, and now everyone supports her, as you sow, so shall you reap.

english_meaning: To go up or rise to a higher place or position. To gain a higher position in society, career, authority, or importance. To grow stronger, louder, or more intense. Often used for sounds, emotions, prices, or temperature. To rise to a higher spiritual, moral, or emotional state. To move upward in numerical order or increase in value.
example_sentence: They slowly ascended the steep path up the mountain. He eventually ascended to the position of chief executive. A long flight of steps ascends (= leads up) to the door of the museum. She ascended the throne when her mother abdicated. The hikers plan to ascend the mountain early in the morning. Smoke began to ascend into the sky after the fire started.

english_meaning: The state of rising in power, influence, or importance. The condition or period during which someone or something gains dominance, authority, or superiority over others. It often implies a rising trend in status, control, or influence.
example_sentence: The politician's ascendance in the party was rapid. Technology’s ascendance has transformed modern life. During the medieval era, the king enjoyed complete ascendance over his subjects. The company’s ascendance in the market was due to innovative strategies.

english_meaning: Dominance, control, or influence over others. A position of power, influence, or superiority in which someone or something has the ability to control, guide, or dominate others. It can refer to social, political, or personal influence.
example_sentence: The ascendancy of technology in daily life is undeniable. The political party gained ascendancy after winning the election. Her ascendancy in the company came from years of hard work and dedication. Cultural ascendancy often influences fashion, language, and art.

english_meaning: Rising in power or influence. Dominant. A position of dominance or controlling influence.
example_sentence: The modernist movement was in the ascendant. His party is in the ascendant. The star's career is in the ascendant. They hold an ascendant position in the market. She is an ascendant figure in national politics.

english_meaning: A climb or walk to the summit of a mountain or hill. The action of rising or climbing up. An upward slope or path. An instance of rising or moving up through the air.
example_sentence: The first ascent of Everest was in 1953. The path steepened for the final ascent. The plane began its ascent to 30,000 feet. His ascent to power was swift.

english_meaning: To find out the true or correct information. To come upon after searching, study, or effort. To find out or learn with certainty. To come to an awareness of.
example_sentence: It can't be difficult to ascertain the facts. I ascertained that the driver was not badly hurt. The police have so far been unable to ascertain the cause of the explosion. It should be ascertained that the plans comply with the law.

english_meaning: A person who practices severe self-discipline and avoids all forms of indulgence, often for religious or spiritual reasons. Practicing severe self-discipline and abstention from indulgence.
example_sentence: The monk lived an ascetic life, owning nothing but his robe and bowl. The monk lived an ascetic life in the mountains, far from worldly pleasures. Many saints are known for their ascetic lifestyles and devotion to prayer. His ascetic habits impressed everyone at the monastery. She adopted an ascetic routine to gain mental clarity and peace.

english_meaning: Severe self-discipline and avoidance of all forms of indulgence, typically for religious reasons. The practice of a strict and self-denying lifestyle, characterized by abstaining from worldly pleasures and comforts, often with the goal of pursuing spiritual goals.
example_sentence: He practiced a life of extreme asceticism, eating only what was necessary and sleeping on a hard floor. Many ancient philosophies praise asceticism as a path to spiritual enlightenment. The monk's asceticism was a source of inspiration for his followers. Her journey into asceticism began after a profound personal loss. Despite the wealth around him, he chose a path of asceticism.

english_meaning: Free from bacteria, germs, or other harmful microorganisms. Relating to methods used to prevent infection during medical procedures. Thoroughly clean and sterile in a medical sense. Lacking warmth, emotion, or individuality; coldly detached.
example_sentence: The wound was cleaned using aseptic techniques. Surgeons must maintain aseptic conditions in the operating theatre. All instruments were kept in an aseptic environment. His aseptic manner made the interview feel cold.

english_meaning: Not involving sexual activity or sexual attraction. Also refers to reproduction that does not require two sexes. In biology, it describes reproduction from a single organism without fertilization, such as cell division or budding. In human context, it describes a person who does not feel sexual attraction to others or has very little interest in sexual activity.
example_sentence: Some plants reproduce through asexual reproduction. The amoeba multiplies by asexual cell division. She identifies as asexual and does not feel sexual attraction to others. Many simple organisms rely on asexual reproduction for survival.

english_meaning: A person does not experience sexual attraction toward anyone. It is not the same as abstinence, it is about innate lack of sexual desire.
example_sentence: Asexuality is a valid sexual orientation. He realized his asexuality in his early twenties. Asexuality does not prevent forming emotional relationships.

english_meaning: To or on the shore or land from the direction of the sea. On land as opposed to at sea.
example_sentence: The sailors were glad to be ashore after a long voyage. We swam ashore. The goods were brought ashore by boat. The storm washed the wreckage ashore.

english_meaning: Extremely foolish, stupid, senseless, or lacking good judgment. A person, idea, action, decision, comment, or behavior that is remarkably foolish or unreasonable. It often implies a level of stupidity that is difficult to understand or justify.
example_sentence: It was an asinine decision to ignore all the safety warnings. His asinine comments offended many people in the meeting. The company lost money because of an asinine management strategy. Everyone laughed at the asinine excuse he gave for being late.

english_meaning: To inquire or seek information regarding someone or something. To show interest by questioning.
example_sentence: He asked about my father. She asked about your health. He asked about the new project. He called to ask about your health. Students often ask about the exam schedule. She asked about job opportunities in the new company. Visitors frequently ask about the history of this place.

english_meaning: To inquire about someone’s health, well-being, or situation, especially when they are not present. It shows care, concern, or interest about a person.
example_sentence: Jenny rang earlier and asked after you, so I told her you were fine. He asked after your mother. She asked after me when I was sick. When I called the office, my boss asked after my health. He asked after all his old friends from college.

english_meaning: To seek information by asking several people. Ask a number of people for information of help.
example_sentence: I have no idea, but I’ll ask around at work and see if anyone can help. I asked around for a good mechanic. She asked around about the event. I don’t know the answer, but I’ll ask around and let you know. She’s been asking around to find a good doctor in the city. We asked around, but nobody had seen the missing dog. If you’re looking for a job, ask around, someone might know of an opening.

english_meaning: To request, seek, or demand something from someone. To express a desire to obtain or receive something.
example_sentence: He asked for help. She asked for directions. He asked her out to dinner. She asked him out to the movies. She went to the manager to ask for help. If you need anything, don’t hesitate to ask for it. He asked for a glass of water. By ignoring the rules, you are asking for trouble.

english_meaning: To invite someone to come inside (usually into your house, room, or office). It is used when you let someone enter your home or a place, often as an act of politeness or hospitality.
example_sentence: Jon’s at the door.’ ‘ask him in.’. She asked me in for tea. They asked the neighbors in. It was raining, so she asked me in for a cup of tea. He knocked at the door, and they asked him in warmly. The teacher asked the parents in to discuss their child’s progress. When guests arrived, she smiled and asked them in.

english_meaning: To invite someone (especially someone you are attracted to) to go out with you, usually on a date or social outing. To invite someone to go somewhere together in a friendly or social way.
example_sentence: He wanted to ask her out but was too shy. They asked us over for lunch. She asked her friend over. He finally got the courage to ask her out on a date. She asked him out for dinner after the meeting. Tom wanted to ask Jenny out, but he was too shy. If you like her, you should just ask her out and see what happens.

english_meaning: To invite someone to your house or place for a visit, meal, or event. It is an informal phrase used especially for inviting friends or guests.
example_sentence: They have asked us over for drinks on Friday. We asked our neighbors round for tea. She asked her colleagues round. We asked our neighbors over for dinner last night. She asked me over to see her new house. He asked his colleagues over for tea after work. I’ll ask you over sometime next week to discuss the project.

english_meaning: To invite someone to visit your home. To ask several people for information or help.
example_sentence: I’ll ask some friends round for dinner tonight. She asked round to see if anyone had seen her lost dog. They asked their neighbors round for tea last weekend. If you need advice, ask round, someone might know the answer.

english_meaning: Not in a straight or level position. Crookedly, awry. Wrong; amiss.
example_sentence: The picture on the wall was slightly askew. Her hat was knocked askew. His tie was askew. All our plans have gone askew.

english_meaning: A tall green vegetable with tender spears eaten as a delicacy. A spring vegetable cooked by steaming, grilling, or roasting. The perennial plant that produces these shoots. A vegetable prized for its delicate flavour.
example_sentence: Grilled asparagus was served beside the fish. Asparagus appears in the markets each spring. She tied the asparagus spears in a neat bundle. Fresh asparagus should snap easily when bent.

english_meaning: A specific part, feature, angle, or characteristic of a situation, object, or idea. The way something appears or is viewed. Shows how an action relates to time, such as completed or ongoing. The way something looks or appears. The position or relationship of planets.
example_sentence: One important aspect of education is critical thinking. The financial aspect of the project needs careful planning. She considered every aspect of the problem before deciding. The cultural aspect of the festival attracts many tourists.

english_meaning: The proportional relationship between the width and the height of an image, screen, or shape. A measurement expressing how wide a picture or display is compared with how tall it is. In engineering, the ratio of the length of a wing or body to its width. A standard format used to describe screen or video dimensions.
synonyms: ["Proportion","Dimension ratio","Screen ratio","Format","Width-to-height ratio","Scale","Frame proportion","Display ratio","Image proportion","Geometry"]
example_sentence: Most modern televisions use a sixteen-by-nine aspect ratio. The photograph was cropped, which changed its aspect ratio. Choose the correct aspect ratio before exporting the video. Older films were shot in a squarer aspect ratio than today's movies.

english_meaning: Harshness or severity, especially in tone, manner, or conditions. Roughness, sharpness, or severity in behavior, speech, or environment. It can describe difficult circumstances or the sharpness of a surface.
example_sentence: The teacher addressed the students with unexpected asperity. Life in the desert is known for its asperity. His speech was full of asperity and criticism. The mountain trail tested their patience with its asperity.

english_meaning: To attack the reputation of someone by making false or damaging statements. To spread harmful rumours or accusations about a person. To slander, defame, or speak ill of someone. To sprinkle, especially with holy water in a religious ceremony. To criticize unfairly with the aim of harming honour.
example_sentence: It is wrong to asperse someone without solid evidence. The politician tried to asperse his rival before the elections. She refused to asperse her former colleagues in the interview. Critics aspersed the writer for his controversial novel. The priest aspersed the congregation with holy water.

english_meaning: A person who strongly desires or tries to achieve a particular position, goal, or honor. Having ambitions to achieve something, especially a high position or distinction. Someone who hopes or works hard to become something, for example, a job seeker, a student aiming for success, or a candidate for a position.
example_sentence: Many aspirants applied for the position of manager. He is an aspirant for the national football team. Every aspirant must work hard to achieve success. The scholarship attracted hundreds of young aspirants. It is to inform that all aspirant candidates of forthcoming MDCAT must bring their original CNIC.

english_meaning: To pronounce a sound with a breath of air, as the letter ‘h’ in “hat”. To draw in air or another substance into the lungs or a tube (used medically or technically). A sound that is produced with an audible breath, such as ‘h’ in English.
example_sentence: In English, the letter ‘h’ is aspirated in words like “house” and “happy”. The doctor had to aspirate fluid from the patient’s lungs. In some accents, people do not aspirate the ‘h’ sound. The teacher explained that “pin” has an aspirated p, while “spin” does not.

english_meaning: A strong desire, hope, or ambition to achieve something. The act of aiming for a high goal or ideal. The action of drawing breath or removing fluid.
example_sentence: Her aspiration is to become a successful social worker. Education fulfills the aspirations of young minds. He worked hard to achieve his lifelong aspiration. Their collective aspiration is to build a better future.

english_meaning: To have a strong desire or ambition to achieve something high or great. To aim for success, excellence, or a particular goal in life.
example_sentence: He aspires to become a successful engineer one day. Many young people aspire to work for international organizations. She aspires to bring positive change to her community. We should all aspire to live a meaningful and honest life.

english_meaning: To attack someone physically or strongly criticize someone with words. To trouble the mind or senses such as fear, doubts, or noise. To confront aggressively, to bombard with questions or criticism, to disturb strongly, to strike repeatedly.
example_sentence: The soldiers were ready to assail the enemy fortress at dawn. Reporters began to assail the minister with difficult questions. Dark thoughts continued to assail his mind during the night. A strong smell of smoke assailed our senses as we entered the building.

english_meaning: Open to being attacked physically or verbally. Vulnerable to criticism or argument due to flaws. Not adequately defended or protected from harm. Susceptible to being questioned or doubted. Lacking the necessary strength to resist an offensive force.
example_sentence: The fortress was strategically weak and remained highly assailable from the north. Her legal argument was assailable because she lacked physical evidence to support her claims. Without a proper firewall, the company's private data is assailable by hackers. The politician found his reputation assailable after the scandal broke in the local news.

english_meaning: A person who attacks someone physically or verbally. An individual who initiates an attack, either physically, such as hitting or assaulting someone, or verbally, by aggressively confronting or criticizing.
example_sentence: The police quickly apprehended the assailant who attacked the pedestrian. The assailant shouted threats before fleeing the scene. She bravely defended herself against the assailant. Witnesses described the assailant as wearing a dark hoodie.

english_meaning: To murder someone, usually an important person, often for political or religious reasons. To deliberately kill a prominent or important person, typically for political, ideological, or financial reasons. This act is usually planned and carried out in secret.
example_sentence: The rebel group planned to assassinate the visiting diplomat. History books recount leaders who were assassinated for their reforms. The spy was caught before he could assassinate the target. He was accused of trying to assassinate the mayor. Many novels depict plots to assassinate royalty or heads of state.

english_meaning: To attack someone physically or verbally. To attack a place forcefully, strongly criticize someone, or overwhelm someone emotionally or physically. A physical or verbal attack. A threat of harm, a strong military attack, or severe verbal criticism.
example_sentence: The man was arrested for assaulting a guard. The army assaulted the enemy base at dawn. He claimed that someone assaulted him in the street. The assault left him seriously injured. The soldiers prepared for the final assault. She filed a complaint after the assault.

english_meaning: To test or analyze a substance to find its quality or composition. A laboratory examination of metal, ore, chemicals, or medicine. An attempt or trial. To evaluate or measure something carefully.
example_sentence: The lab will assay the ore for gold content. Scientists performed an assay on the new medicine. His first assay at public speaking was nervous but sincere. The company assayed samples from the mine.

english_meaning: To gather people or things together in one place for a common purpose. To fit or put the parts of something together to form a complete whole. To come together as a group. Used both for gathering people and for constructing or building something from separate components.
example_sentence: The students assembled in the school hall for the morning assembly. The engineer assembled all the parts of the machine carefully. The general assembled his troops before the battle. It took him two hours to assemble the new bookshelf. Thousands of people assembled in the square to hear the speech.

english_meaning: A person or machine that fits parts together to make a finished product. A worker employed on a production line to put components together. A program that converts assembly language into machine code. Someone who brings people or things together in one place.
example_sentence: The assembler fitted the engine parts with great care. Robots have replaced many assemblers in the factory. The assembler translates the code before it runs. She works as an assembler in a furniture workshop.

english_meaning: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully. To cause others to recognize (one's authority or a right) by confident and forceful behavior. To defend, maintain, or insist on.
example_sentence: He continued to assert that he was innocent. You need to assert yourself more in meetings. The company asserted its right to the property. She asserted her independence from her parents.

english_meaning: To confidently and firmly claim, demand, or stand up for one’s legal, moral, or personal rights. It means you declare your rights clearly and refuse to let them be ignored.
example_sentence: The workers were asserting their rights during the protest. She asserted her right to equal pay. She asserted her right to speak freely during the meeting. He asserted his right to appeal against the decision. Citizens should assert their right to vote in every election.

english_meaning: A confident statement that something is true. A claim made without necessarily giving proof. The act of stating or defending a right, belief, or opinion. A firm expression of authority or confidence.
example_sentence: Her assertion was challenged by several experts. The lawyer repeated his assertion that the witness was reliable. The essay begins with a bold assertion about freedom. His calm assertion of authority ended the argument.

english_meaning: Having or showing a confident and forceful personality. Disposed to or characterized by bold or confident statements and behavior.
example_sentence: You need to be more assertive to succeed in this business. She has an assertive and confident manner. The course helps people to become more assertive. An assertive person can state their needs clearly.

english_meaning: To evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, or quality of something. To set the value of (a tax, fine, etc.) for a person or property at a specified level.
example_sentence: The committee was asked to assess the suitability of the candidates. We need to assess the impact on the environment. The damage was assessed at $5,000. It's difficult to assess the effects of the new law so soon.

english_meaning: The action of assessing someone or something. An evaluation. The evaluation of the worth, significance, or extent of something. An amount that is fixed as a tax.
example_sentence: His assessment of the situation was accurate. The final assessment will be based on your coursework and exams. A detailed assessment of the risks is required. The city conducted a property tax assessment.

english_meaning: Showing great care, attention, and effort. Working hard and persistently. Diligent and devoted in performing tasks. Constantly attentive to duties or responsibilities. Used to praise someone who applies themselves steadily and thoroughly to study, work, or any task requiring perseverance.
example_sentence: She is an assiduous student who never misses a lecture. His assiduous research led to a major scientific discovery. The assiduous efforts of the team produced excellent results. He was assiduous in his attention to the smallest details. The nurse provided assiduous care to the elderly patient.

english_meaning: To give a task or duty to someone. To allocate something for a particular purpose. To appoint a person to a position or place. To transfer a legal right or property to another.
example_sentence: The manager assigned the report to her. Two rooms were assigned for the training. He was assigned to the northern office. She assigned her share of the property to her brother.

english_meaning: A task or piece of work given to someone. A duty or job allocated as part of study or employment. The act of assigning something to a person. In law, the transfer of a right or property to another person.
example_sentence: The teacher gave us a written assignment. He accepted an overseas assignment for two years. Her first assignment was to interview the mayor. The assignment of the lease was completed last week.

english_meaning: Capable of being assimilated. Able to be absorbed and incorporated, either by the body or into a culture. Easily understood and integrated.
example_sentence: The nutrients in this food are easily assimilable. New ideas are not always immediately assimilable. The book presents complex theories in an assimilable form. The culture found the new migrants to be assimilable.

english_meaning: To fully understand an idea or some information so that you are able to use it yourself. To become, or cause somebody to become, a part of a country or community rather than remaining in a separate group. To make an idea, a person’s attitude, etc fit into something or be acceptable. To absorb food or a substance into the tissue of a living organism.
example_sentence: The committee will need time to assimilate this report. Some people can only assimilate change gradually. New arrivals feel the pressure to assimilate. As a Chinese teen I tried to assimilate into Canadian culture. Over time different groups were assimilated into the community. These changes were gradually assimilated into everyday life. In this form vitamins can be easily assimilated by the body.

english_meaning: The process of taking in and fully understanding information or ideas, or becoming similar to a group or culture. The process by which a person or group absorbs information, ideas, or cultural traits and becomes integrated into a different environment or society. It is also used in biology for the absorption of nutrients, and in language for sound changes influenced by nearby sounds.
example_sentence: The dog's rapid assimilation of new tricks pleased his owners. The assimilation of ethnic Germans in the US was accelerated by the two world wars. Poor assimilation of vitamins and nutrients can cause health problems. The assimilation of immigrants into American culture has been a constant feature of US history.

english_meaning: To connect one thing with another in the mind. To spend time with someone as a friend or colleague. A partner, colleague, or fellow worker. Joined or connected with another, often in a lower rank. To be involved with a group or organization.
example_sentence: Most people associate the color red with love. He does not associate with dishonest people. She works as an associate in a law firm. The company hired several new associates this year.

english_meaning: Connected with something or someone in the mind. Joined or linked together with something. Related or connected in some way. Working together with others in a partnership or organization.
example_sentence: Smoking is associated with lung cancer. The problems associated with poverty are numerous. She is an associate professor at the university. He associated the smell with childhood memories.

english_meaning: A connection or relationship between things or people. An organized group of people with a common purpose or interest. The mental connection between ideas or experiences. The act of joining or connecting with others.
example_sentence: There is a strong association between diet and health. She is a member of the teachers' association. The association meets monthly to discuss issues. Free association is a technique used in psychotherapy.

english_meaning: Repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words to create rhythm, musical effect, or emphasis in speech or writing. It usually occurs in poetry but is also used in prose and everyday language.
example_sentence: There is a recurrence of the e-a assonance at the ends of lines, but in no definable pattern. Alliteration and assonance is not only a language phenomenon, but also an artistic one in poems. The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain. Go slow over the road. Hear the mellow wedding bells. Try to light the fire.

english_meaning: To sort or classify into groups of a similar kind. To group things together by type. To suit or be in harmony with.
example_sentence: The shop assistant began to assort the books by genre. The socks were assorted by color and size. The collection includes assorted chocolates. We assorted the documents into different files.

english_meaning: A collection or mixture of different kinds of things. A group or collection that contains a variety of different items. These items may differ in type, size, color, or purpose but are gathered together in one place or set.
example_sentence: The shop offers an assortment of chocolates and candies. She bought an assortment of fruits for the picnic. The toolbox contains an assortment of screws and nails. The library has an assortment of books on history and science.

english_meaning: To make an unpleasant feeling less intense or severe. To soothe, calm, or relieve pain, anger, grief, fear, or worry. To satisfy hunger, thirst, or desire. To ease or lessen distress. It is often used in formal contexts when emotions or physical discomfort are reduced or softened.
example_sentence: He tried to assuage her grief with kind words. The government took steps to assuage public anger over the new law. A cold drink helped assuage his thirst. Nothing could assuage the mother's sorrow. The manager attempted to assuage the concerns of the worried employees.

english_meaning: A positive declaration intended to give confidence. A promise or guarantee that something will happen. Self-confidence and certainty in one's own abilities. Freedom from doubt or skepticism. A type of insurance policy, especially life insurance.
example_sentence: He gave me his personal assurance that the project would be completed on time. The athlete spoke with great assurance during the press conference. Despite the difficulties, she faced the challenge with calm assurance. The insurance company offers a variety of life assurance policies.

english_meaning: To tell someone something positively to dispel any doubts. To make something certain to happen. To give confidence or a feeling of security. To confirm or promise with confidence. To guarantee against loss or provide insurance for something.
example_sentence: I can assure you that your secret is safe with me. The captain spoke calmly to assure the passengers during the storm. Regular maintenance will help assure the long life of your vehicle. She wanted to assure herself that the doors were locked before sleeping.

english_meaning: A chronic respiratory condition that causes the airways to narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus. It leads to difficulty in breathing, wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath. The severity of the condition can vary greatly from person to person.
example_sentence: His severe asthma prevents him from playing intense sports in winter. The pollution in the city triggered a sudden asthma attack. She always carries an inhaler to manage her childhood asthma. Children with asthma need to strictly avoid dusty environments. Cold weather can severely worsen the symptoms of asthma.

english_meaning: A sweet, sparkling Italian white wine made from Moscato Bianco grapes, produced in the Asti region of Piedmont, Italy. It is known for its light, fruity, and sweet flavour.
example_sentence: They toasted the new year with a bottle of Asti Spumante. Asti Spumante is a popular choice at Italian celebrations. The dessert was perfectly paired with a glass of Asti Spumante. She preferred Asti Spumante over drier sparkling wines.

english_meaning: A common eye condition in which the cornea or lens has an irregular shape, causing blurred or distorted vision at various distances. It is easily corrected with glasses or lenses.
example_sentence: The optician diagnosed him with astigmatism during the eye test. She needed special lenses to correct her astigmatism. Astigmatism is one of the most common refractive errors worldwide. His headaches were caused by untreated astigmatism.

english_meaning: In a state of excited movement. Up and about; out of bed. Being in motion.
example_sentence: The whole town was astir with the news. She was astir early in the morning. The slightest noise set the dogs astir. Rumors were astir about the king's health. The city was astir with festival preparations.

english_meaning: To surprise or impress (someone) greatly. To fill with sudden and overpowering surprise or wonder. To amaze.
example_sentence: Her reply astonished me. The magicians' tricks never fail to astonish the audience. It would astonish you to know how much he earns. The sheer size of the building will astonish you.

english_meaning: To surprise or shock somebody very much. To surprise or shock someone very much. To fill with bewilderment or wonder.
example_sentence:
His arrogance astounded her. The magician will astound you with his latest tricks.
 What astounds me is that they never apologized.

english_meaning: So surprising that it is difficult to believe. Causing great amazement or shock. Remarkably impressive in scale or quality. Overwhelming the mind with wonder.
example_sentence: The team showed astounding courage in the final match. Her progress in six months has been astounding. He told us an astounding story about his journey. The results were astounding to everyone involved.

english_meaning: Fear of thunder and lightning. An intense and irrational fear of thunder and lightning. People with this phobia may feel extreme anxiety, panic, or discomfort during storms, even when there is no real danger. It is a type of specific phobia related to weather conditions, especially thunderstorms.
example_sentence: The child suffers from astraphobia and hides under the bed during storms. Her astraphobia makes her extremely nervous whenever thunder is heard. People with astraphobia often avoid going outside when it rains heavily. He installed special soundproof windows to reduce his astraphobia anxiety during thunderstorms.

english_meaning: Become lost. To be stolen. Away from the correct path or correct way of doing something. Away from the right path or direction.
example_sentence:
The argument is so complex, a reader might easily go astray. The letter must have gone astray in the post.
I was led astray by an out-of-date map.

english_meaning: The scientific study of the possibility of life beyond the Earth. The branch of science dealing with the origin, evolution, and distribution of life in the universe. The study of how living things might survive in space environments.
example_sentence: She is studying astrobiology at a leading university. Astrobiology combines biology, chemistry, and astronomy. Mars missions have greatly advanced astrobiology. The lecture on astrobiology attracted a large audience.

english_meaning: An ancient instrument used to measure the position of stars and planets. A device once used by astronomers and navigators to determine latitude and time. A historical scientific tool for observing the sky.
example_sentence: The museum displays a brass astrolabe from the tenth century. Muslim astronomers greatly improved the astrolabe. Sailors used an astrolabe to find their latitude at sea. He explained how an astrolabe measures the altitude of stars.
