english_meaning: A person who studies the supposed influence of stars and planets on human affairs. Someone who makes predictions based on the positions of heavenly bodies. A practitioner of astrology who prepares horoscopes.
example_sentence: The astrologer predicted a difficult year ahead. Many kings once kept an astrologer at court. She consulted an astrologer before the wedding date. The astrologer studied his birth chart carefully.

english_meaning: Relating to astrology. Pertaining to the study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world.
example_sentence: He went to an expert for an astrological reading. She checks her astrological forecast every day. The book contains astrological charts and predictions. Astrological signs are based on your birth date.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to astrology. According to beliefs about the influence of stars, planets, zodiac signs, or horoscopes on human life and events.
example_sentence: Astrologically, she considered the date favorable. The prediction was explained astrologically, not scientifically. He reads events astrologically through zodiac signs. Astrologically speaking, Mars was said to influence the decision. Many people enjoy discussing relationships astrologically.

english_meaning: The study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world. A pseudoscience claiming divination by the positions of the planets and stars.
example_sentence: Many people believe in astrology and read their horoscopes daily. Astrology is not considered a true science. She developed an interest in astrology. He consulted a book on Chinese astrology.

english_meaning: The branch of astronomy that measures the positions and movements of stars. The precise measurement of the location, distance, and motion of celestial bodies. A scientific method used to map the sky accurately.
example_sentence: Astrometry helps scientists calculate the distance to nearby stars. Modern satellites have made astrometry far more precise. He specialises in astrometry and star cataloguing. Astrometry data revealed the slow motion of the galaxy.

english_meaning: A person trained to travel and work in a spacecraft. Someone who journeys beyond the Earth's atmosphere. A member of a space mission crew.
example_sentence: The astronaut spent six months on the space station. She dreamed of becoming an astronaut as a child. Astronauts must undergo years of rigorous training. The astronaut waved to the crowd before boarding the rocket.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies stars, planets, and other objects in space. An expert in astronomy who observes and researches the universe. A person who uses telescopes and data to explain celestial phenomena.
example_sentence: The astronomer discovered a new comet last night. Astronomers use powerful telescopes to study distant galaxies. She became a famous astronomer after her research on black holes. Ancient astronomers mapped the stars without modern tools.

english_meaning: Relating to astronomy or the study of celestial bodies. Extremely large in amount, size, or cost. Involving numbers or distances so great that they are hard to imagine.
example_sentence: The observatory carries out astronomical research all year. The cost of the project was astronomical. Astronomical distances are measured in light years. House prices in the city have reached astronomical levels.

english_meaning: A unit of length equal to the average distance between the earth and the sun, about 149·6 million kilometers. A standard measure used in astronomy for distances within the solar system. A unit written as AU or au.
example_sentence: Mars orbits at about 1.5 astronomical units from the sun. One astronomical unit is roughly 150 million kilometers. Distances inside the solar system are given in astronomical units. Jupiter lies more than five astronomical units away.

english_meaning: A person who loves or is fascinated by stars, astronomy, or celestial objects. Someone who has a deep interest in stars, planets, and space. This person often studies, observes, or collects information about celestial phenomena and enjoys activities like stargazing or learning about astronomy.
antonyms: ["Astrophobia","Disinterested in astronomy","Ignorant of stars","Apathetic to space"]
example_sentence: As an astronophile, she spends every night observing the sky with her telescope. He became an astronophile after visiting a planetarium as a child. The club is full of astronophiles who share tips on stargazing. Astronophiles often track meteor showers and celestial events

english_meaning: A person who loves stars, planets, and the study of the sky. Someone fascinated by astronomy and celestial phenomena. A stargazer who admires the night sky. An enthusiast of the cosmos and space exploration.
example_sentence: The astrophile spent every clear night with her telescope. As an astrophile, he memorized every constellation. Astrophiles often gather during meteor showers. The astrophile club meets on weekends.

english_meaning: Fear of stars or celestial space, often related to fear of storms. An intense, irrational fear of celestial phenomena, such as stars, space, or outer space, sometimes extending to fear of thunderstorms or night sky. It may cause anxiety, panic attacks, or avoidance behavior.
example_sentence: She suffers from astrophobia and avoids going out at night. His astrophobia made him nervous during the meteor shower. Children with astrophobia may refuse to look at the night sky. Therapy helped him cope with his astrophobia.

english_meaning: Having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage. Shrewd, clever, and crafty.
example_sentence: He was an astute businessman. She made some astute comments on the situation. It was an astute move to buy the shares then. He is an astute observer of the political scene. An astute investor can make a lot of money.

english_meaning: Separated into pieces, apart, divided, or broken into parts. Into separate parts. Apart from each other. Broken, torn, or split into pieces. Divided physically or emotionally. Completely separated after being joined together.
example_sentence: The earthquake rent the ground asunder. Their family was torn asunder by the war. The lightning split the tree asunder. What God has joined together, let no man put asunder.

english_meaning: A safe place or protection for someone in danger, especially from political persecution. Protection granted by a government to someone who has left their country to escape danger or persecution. An institution providing shelter and care for people who are mentally ill or in need. Any place offering safety, refuge, or sanctuary.
example_sentence: The refugees sought asylum in a neighboring country. He was granted political asylum after fleeing persecution. The old monastery served as an asylum for the lost travelers. Many mental health patients were cared for in the asylum.

english_meaning: Not identical on both sides, uneven or irregular in shape, size, or arrangement. So something that lacks symmetry. This could be in physical shapes, designs, patterns, or even abstract contexts like balance in systems, strategies, or relationships.
example_sentence: The painting had an asymmetric composition that drew the eye to the center. The new building design is intentionally asymmetric to stand out. The molecule has an asymmetric structure, giving it unique chemical properties. In fashion, asymmetric hems are trendy this season.

english_meaning: An object, design, or structure that is uneven or not balanced on either side. It can be used in physical, artistic, or abstract contexts.
example_sentence: The building has an asymmetrical design that draws attention. She wore an asymmetrical dress with one sleeve longer than the other. The artist created an asymmetrical sculpture that looks different from every angle. The garden layout is intentionally asymmetrical to appear natural.

english_meaning: Something that lacks symmetry, balance, or proportion in its shape, structure, or arrangement. It describes situations, objects, or designs where parts do not mirror each other evenly.
example_sentence: The painting was hung asymmetrically on the wall. His socks were asymmetrically mismatched. The building’s windows are arranged asymmetrically. The data distribution was asymmetrically skewed to the right.

english_meaning: Lack of equality or balance between parts, not symmetrical. A situation, shape, or arrangement where the two sides are not identical or evenly balanced. It can apply to objects, patterns, or even situations.
example_sentence: The painting has intentional asymmetry to create visual interest. Her face shows slight asymmetry when she smiles. The building design uses asymmetry to stand out in the cityscape. Asymmetry in the data suggested an error in measurement.

english_meaning: To operate or happen at different times, not simultaneously. To arrange, perform, or function in a way that does not occur at the same time as something else. Often used in technology, communication, or processes where activities are not synchronized.
example_sentence: The software allows users to asynchronise their tasks so they can work offline. The lecture was asynchronised with the online materials to allow flexibility. We had to asynchronise the video feed because of network delays. The team decided to asynchronise their schedules to avoid overlap.

english_meaning: To cause something to happen at different times rather than at the same time. To arrange events, processes, or activities so that they do not occur simultaneously. Often used in technology, communications, or coordination contexts.
example_sentence: The software can asynchronize data transfers to improve speed. Teachers try to asynchronize online lessons for students in different time zones. The production lines were asynchronized to avoid congestion. He chose to asynchronize his meetings so he could attend more without overlap.

english_meaning: Not occurring at the same time or not coordinated in time. Something that happens independently, without requiring simultaneous timing or coordination with other events or processes. Often used in technology, communication, and education.
example_sentence: Online courses can be asynchronous, allowing students to learn at their own pace. Email is an asynchronous form of communication compared to instant messaging. The system processes data asynchronously to improve efficiency. Asynchronous meetings let teams collaborate across different time zones.

english_meaning: A figure of speech in which conjunctions such as and, or, or but are deliberately omitted from a series of words, phrases, or clauses to create emphasis, speed, or dramatic effect. A rhetorical and literary device where conjunctions are intentionally omitted between words, phrases, or clauses. This makes the sentence shorter, faster, more forceful, and often more memorable. Writers and speakers use asyndeton to increase dramatic effect, express urgency, emphasize each item equally, or create a powerful rhythm.
example_sentence: The phrase I came, I saw, I conquered is a famous example of asyndeton. The writer used asyndeton to make the sentence faster. Asyndeton can create urgency in a speech. Students identified asyndeton in the opening paragraph.

english_meaning: Having nothing to do and not knowing what you want to do. A situation where someone has free time and does not know how to occupy it, often leading to boredom or restlessness.
example_sentence: Come and see us, if you're at a loose end. After finishing all his assignments, he was at a loose end for the afternoon. She felt at a loose end during the long holiday with nothing planned. He wandered around the city at a loose end, looking for something to do. When the team canceled the meeting, I was at a loose end with no work to complete.

english_meaning: Extremely slowly. Moving or progressing far more slowly than expected. Making very little advance over a long period.
example_sentence: Traffic moved at a snail's pace during the rain. The construction work is going on at a snail's pace. He types at a snail's pace. Reforms progressed at a snail's pace for years.

english_meaning: Continuously or without stopping for a certain period of time, doing something in one go without rest.
example_sentence: He worked for eight hours at a stretch to finish the project The children watched television for three hours at a stretch. She can stand and teach the class for two hours at a stretch. The soldiers marched for miles at a stretch without taking a break.

english_meaning: In severe conflict or hostility. To be in a state of hostility or open conflict. A situation where two people or groups are so angry and bitter toward each other that they seem ready to fight at any moment. It shows deep tension, distrust, and open disagreement.
example_sentence: They have been at daggers drawn since the dispute. The two countries are at daggers drawn. The rivals are at daggers drawn again. He’s at daggers drawn with his boss.

english_meaning: A long, detailed explanation without leaving anything out. In great detail very thoroughly. With many words. Speaking or writing for a long time, covering every part or aspect.
example_sentence: The professor explained the theory at great length during the lecture. She described her journey at great length, including every small incident. The report discusses climate change impacts at great length. He spoke at great length about his plans for the future.

english_meaning: Close by, within easy reach. Available or ready for use when needed. About to happen very soon. Near in time or place.
example_sentence: Keep your phone at hand in case of emergency. The examination is at hand, so study seriously. Help was at hand when the accident occurred. All the tools you need are at hand.

english_meaning: Not captured or free, especially referring to a criminal or dangerous animal. In a general way or as a whole. Representing an entire state or area rather than a specific district.
example_sentence: The escaped suspect remains at large, and police are urging vigilance. Society at large must address the root causes of economic inequality. He was elected as a representative at large for the region. Dangerous wildlife should not be left roaming at large.

english_meaning: Free or permitted to take an action. Someone has the freedom, permission, or authority to take an action or make a choice without restriction. It can apply to formal situations (like official permission) or general freedom to act.
example_sentence: You are at liberty to leave anytime. He’s at liberty to make his own decisions. The citizens are at liberty to vote. Employees are not at liberty to share company secrets.

english_meaning: Allowed or free to reveal information. Someone has permission, freedom, or the right to express an opinion, make a statement, or share information without restriction. It often implies that the speaker is not bound by secrecy or authority in this context.
example_sentence: I’m not at liberty to say anything yet. She was at liberty to share the news. The officer isn’t at liberty to comment. Are you at liberty to discuss it now?

english_meaning: To be in strong disagreement or serious conflict with someone. It means two people or groups are arguing strongly and cannot agree on something. It shows a state of serious conflict where both sides hold opposite opinions and refuse to compromise. Often used in politics, workplaces, or personal relationships where disagreement becomes intense and ongoing. It suggests not just a small argument, but a deep and persistent conflict.
synonyms: ["To be in conflict","To disagree strongly","To be at odds","To clash","To quarrel"]
antonyms: ["To agree","To be in harmony","To get along","To cooperate","To reconcile"]
example_sentence: The two departments are at loggerheads over the new budget plan. The teacher and student were at loggerheads about the assignment deadline. The neighbors have been at loggerheads for years over the property wall. The company owners are at loggerheads regarding future investments.

english_meaning: In disagreement or conflict with someone. Not matching or consistent with something else. In a state of dispute or opposition.
example_sentence: The two ministers have been at odds for months. His statement is at odds with the official report. She found herself at odds with her own family over the sale. The colours of the room are at odds with the furniture.

english_meaning: Always available to follow requests. Always ready to obey someone’s orders or requests immediately.
example_sentence: The servants were always at the king’s beck and call. He keeps his employees at his beck and call. The manager expects his staff to be at his beck and call even after office hours. She doesn’t want to be at anyone’s beck and call; she values her independence.

english_meaning: Extremely worried, confused, or frustrated; not knowing what to do. When someone is at a point where they have exhausted all their ideas, patience, or resources and do not know what action to take next. It describes a state of desperation or mental strain.
example_sentence: After trying everything to fix the computer, she was at her wits’ end. He was at his wits’ end trying to quiet the crying baby. They were at their wits’ end when the negotiations failed. I am at my wits’ end with this complicated paperwork.

english_meaning: To be extremely happy, joyful, or delighted. (as in a perfect or heavenly state of joy).
example_sentence: She was at seventh heaven when she received her job offer. After the birth of his daughter, he felt at seventh heaven. When the team won the final match, everyone was at seventh heaven. He was at seventh heaven after hearing the good news about his promotion.

english_meaning: In a state of confusion, disorder, or disorganization when things are not in their proper place or when people are uncertain what to do.
example_sentence: When we moved to the new house, everything was at sixes and sevens. After the sudden resignation of the manager, the whole office was at sixes and sevens. The students were at sixes and sevens before the exam started. Since the flood, the village has been at sixes and sevens.

word: At the drop of a hat
english_meaning: To do something immediately, without hesitation, or without any delay or preparation. Showing readiness to act quickly and willingly.
example_sentence: He is always ready to help his friends at the drop of a hat. She’ll start singing at the drop of a hat, she just loves performing. If you need him, he’ll come at the drop of a hat. They change their plans at the drop of a hat without thinking twice.

english_meaning: It means doing something immediately without any hesitation or delay. The phrase describes an action taken instantly and often without much forethought. It refers to being ready and willing to respond to a situation at the slightest signal. The expression denotes a sudden change in behavior or plans triggered by a minor event. It signifies acting promptly with eager anticipation and zero reluctance.
example_sentence: He is ready to start a fight at the drop of hat. She would pack her bags and travel the world at the drop of hat. We cannot just change our entire business strategy at the drop of hat. He expects everyone to rush to his aid at the drop of hat.

english_meaning: At the last possible moment before it’s too late. Doing something just in time or at the final moment.
example_sentence: He submitted the work at the eleventh hour. He submitted his assignment at the eleventh hour, just before the deadline. The team scored a goal at the eleventh hour and won the match. She changed her decision at the eleventh hour and decided not to travel. They saved the company at the eleventh hour by arranging urgent funds.

word: At the end of the day
english_meaning: Ultimately; when everything is considered; in the final analysis. Used to emphasize the most important fact or conclusion after considering everything else. It often signals a final judgment, decision, or perspective.
synonyms: ["Ultimately","In the end","When all is said and done","After all","In conclusion"]
antonyms: ["Initially","At the beginning","At the start","In the first instance"]
example_sentence: At the end of the day, he'll still have to make his own decision. At the end of the day, hard work pays off. We can discuss details, but at the end of the day, safety comes first. At the end of the day, it’s your decision to make. At the end of the day, the results matter more than the process.

english_meaning: Completely unable to think of what to do next. Frustrated because no solution is left. Feeling helpless in a difficult situation. Exhausted mentally and emotionally. Having tried everything with no result.
example_sentence: I'm at my wit's end trying to solve this problem. She was at her wit's end with her crying baby. He is at his wit's end after failing three times. The teacher was at her wit's end with the noisy class.

english_meaning: The fear of imperfection or of not being good enough. A person with atelophobia is constantly afraid of making mistakes or failing to meet their own high standards.
example_sentence: Her atelophobia caused her to rewrite every email several times. Atelophobia often goes hand in hand with perfectionism. His atelophobia prevented him from submitting his work. She sought counselling to manage her atelophobia.

english_meaning: A person who does not believe in the existence of a god or any gods. Someone who rejects the belief in any deity, often relying on science, reason, or philosophy rather than religious faith. An atheist may question or deny the existence of God or any divine being.
example_sentence: She grew up as an atheist and never attended religious services. The book was written by a famous atheist philosopher. He proudly identifies as an atheist in discussions about religion. Many atheists argue for morality without relying on God.

english_meaning: Relating to or characterized by atheism. Believing that no god or gods exist. Not believing in the existence of any deity. Expressing or showing disbelief in God. Connected with the rejection of religious belief. The term describes ideas, people, philosophies, or societies that deny the existence of a supreme being or divine power and reject all forms of religious faith.
example_sentence: He grew up in an atheistic household where religion was never discussed. The professor's atheistic views often sparked debate in his philosophy class. Their atheistic outlook shaped the way they raised their children. Some atheistic philosophies still emphasize strong moral values. The novel presents an atheistic interpretation of human existence.

english_meaning:
The layer of gases surrounding the Earth.
The air in a specific place.
The mood, feeling, or emotional environment of a place or event.
A surrounding influence or condition affecting people or things. The air surrounding the Earth or a particular place. It also means the feeling, mood, or environment of a place, event, or situation.
example_sentence: The Earth's atmosphere protects us from harmful rays. The restaurant had a calm and friendly atmosphere. The classroom atmosphere was perfect for learning. Smoke polluted the atmosphere of the city.

english_meaning: The basic unit of a chemical element. The smallest particle of a substance that can exist, consisting of a nucleus of protons and neutrons and a surrounding cloud of electrons. A very small amount of a thing.
example_sentence: An atom consists of a nucleus and electrons. The splitting of the atom releases enormous energy. There is not an atom of truth in his story. Water is composed of hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

english_meaning: To make amends or repair a wrong or mistake. To take responsibility for a wrongdoing and try to correct it. It often involves apology, compensation, or actions that show regret and a desire to make things right. It is commonly used in moral, religious, and personal contexts.
example_sentence: He tried to atone for his mistake by helping those he had hurt. She wanted to atone for her harsh words by apologizing sincerely. The company attempted to atone for its errors by compensating the customers. He spent years trying to atone for his past actions.

english_meaning: On the top of, upon, or at the highest point of something. It is used to show that a person, object, or thing is positioned on the highest part of something else. It can also mean being in a leading or dominant position.
example_sentence: The cherry atop the cake was perfect. The eagle perched atop the highest peak. He stood atop the hill, looking down at the valley. There was a flag atop the building.

english_meaning: Refers to something that is very unpleasant, cruel, or of very poor quality. It can describe actions, conditions, behavior, or situations that are shocking or horrifying.
example_sentence: The movie received atrocious reviews from critics. The weather conditions were atrocious during the storm. He was punished for his atrocious behavior. The food at that restaurant was absolutely atrocious.

english_meaning: In a very bad or cruel way. Used to describe an action or behavior that is extremely bad, cruel, or unpleasant
example_sentence: The house was atrociously messy after the party. He treated his opponents atrociously during the debate. The movie was atrociously boring and long. The workers were paid atrociously low wages.

english_meaning: A cruel and violent act, especially in a war. An extremely cruel, violent, or shocking act.
example_sentence: In the war, both sides committed atrocities. They are on trial for committing atrocities against the civilian population. Any atrocity, at any time, was expected from them. Atrocity and terror are not political weapons.

english_meaning: To make an effort to achieve or complete something difficult. An act of trying to do something, especially something requiring effort. An effort to surpass a record or achieve a specific athletic goal. An effort to harm or kill someone in a violent manner. To undertake or seek to perform a task.
example_sentence: She will attempt to climb the mountain this weekend. His first attempt at baking a cake was a complete disaster. The athletes made a brave attempt to break the world record. Any attempt to escape will be met with immediate punishment.

english_meaning: To give attention to a task, problem, person, or responsibility. It can also mean to take care of someone, handle a matter, or deal with something that needs action.
synonyms: ["Take care of","Deal with","Look after","Handle","Pay attention to"]
example_sentence: The nurse will attend to the patient shortly. Please attend to your homework before going outside. The manager attended to the customer’s complaint immediately. I need to attend to some urgent matters at work.

english_meaning: To serve someone, look after them, or remain with them to provide help or care.
example_sentence: Nurses attended upon the injured soldiers throughout the night. The servants attended upon the king during the ceremony. She attended upon her grandmother during her illness. Personal assistants attend upon the director during official visits.

english_meaning: The act of being present at a place or event. The number of people present. A record of whether people are present or absent. Regular presence at school, work, meetings, or events. The act of accompanying, serving, or caring for someone. Attention or service given to a person, especially in older usage.
example_sentence: Attendance at the concert exceeded all expectations. The teacher checks attendance at the start of each class. Regular attendance is essential for success in this course. A nurse remained in attendance throughout the night.

english_meaning: A person employed to provide a service or look after a place or another person. Someone who accompanies an important person. A person present at an event or gathering. Happening at the same time as, or as a result of, something else. Connected with or accompanying a particular condition. Giving attention, care, or service, in older usage.
example_sentence: The flight attendant helped us find our seats. A parking attendant directed the cars toward the exit. The policy created delays and attendant costs. The queen entered with two attendants beside her.

english_meaning: A person who is present at an event, meeting, class, or ceremony. Someone who has registered for and takes part in a conference. A member of an audience or gathering. A participant considered in relation to their presence rather than their role. A person who regularly goes to a particular place or event.
example_sentence: Each attendee received a name badge at the entrance. The workshop attracted attendees from several countries. An attendee asked a thoughtful question after the lecture. Conference attendees can download the schedule online.

english_meaning: To dress or clothe someone in a particular way. To dress, clothe, or decorate someone in particular clothes, especially formal, elegant, traditional, or special clothing. Clothing, dress, or what a person is wearing, especially when speaking in a formal, elegant, traditional, or noticeable way.
example_sentence: She arrived at the wedding in elegant traditional attire. Office attire should be neat and professional. The dancers wore colorful attire during the cultural show. The bride was attired in a beautiful red gown. The actor was attired as a king for the play. The children were attired in warm clothes for winter. She was richly attired for the royal event.

english_meaning: A settled way of thinking or feeling about someone or something, typically reflected in a person's behavior. A personal view, opinion, or mental position toward a particular subject. The posture or position of the body, especially one assumed for a specific purpose. A confident or arrogant manner that someone displays.
example_sentence: She has a positive attitude towards her studies. His rude attitude annoyed everyone in the meeting. The teacher praised the children for their helpful attitude. The dancer struck a graceful attitude on the stage. You need to change your attitude if you want to succeed.

english_meaning: Relating to a person’s attitude, opinions, beliefs, or feelings. Concerned with measuring or explaining attitudes. Caused by or reflected in a particular way of thinking rather than by practical conditions.
example_sentence: The survey revealed significant attitudinal differences between the two groups. Lasting reform requires both legal and attitudinal change. Researchers used an attitudinal scale to measure public trust. The main barrier to inclusion was attitudinal rather than financial.

english_meaning: To adopt or display an affected or artificial attitude or pose, especially to impress others. To behave in a self-conscious or theatrical manner. To strike a pose or speak in a way that is not natural in order to attract attention.
example_sentence: He tends to attitudinize whenever the cameras are around. Stop attitudinizing and speak honestly for once. Politicians often attitudinize to please their voters. She attitudinized in front of her friends to seem important. The actor attitudinized on stage to capture the audience's attention.

english_meaning: A lawyer who is legally qualified to advise or represent people. A person appointed to act for another in legal or business matters. An official authorized to conduct legal proceedings on behalf of a government or organization.
example_sentence: The attorney reviewed the contract before her client signed it. He hired an attorney to represent him in court. Please send all legal documents to my attorney. The attorney presented new evidence during the trial.

english_meaning: The chief legal officer of a country, state, or other jurisdiction. A government official who advises the government on law and may oversee public prosecutions or legal affairs.
synonyms: ["Chief law officer","Justice minister","Government counsel","Chief legal adviser"]
example_sentence: The attorney general announced a review of the law. Parliament asked the attorney general for legal advice. The state attorney general filed a case against the company. She served as attorney general for four years.

english_meaning: Able to be regarded as being caused by or belonging to a particular person, thing, or cause. Capable of being assigned, credited, or ascribed to a specific source or reason. Said of something whose origin or responsibility can be traced.
example_sentence: The accident is attributable to poor weather conditions. His success is largely attributable to hard work. The decline in sales is attributable to the new competitor. Many health problems are attributable to a poor diet. The painting is attributable to a famous Renaissance artist.

english_meaning: To say or believe that something is the result of a particular thing. To say or believe that somebody is responsible for doing something, especially for saying, writing or painting something. To regard a quality or feature as belonging to somebody, something. A quality or feature of somebody, something.
example_sentence: She attributes her success to hard work and a little luck. The power failure was attributed to the recent storms and high winds. This play is usually attributed to Shakespeare. The committee refused to attribute blame without further information. Patience is one of the most important attributes in a teacher. The most basic attribute of all animals is consciousness.

english_meaning: The gradual reduction in strength or numbers due to constant stress or pressure. The process of gradually wearing down or weakening. The loss of employees through resignation or retirement rather than termination. Erosion or grinding down through friction.
example_sentence: The army was weakened through attrition. The company reduced staff through natural attrition. Years of war led to attrition of resources. Employee attrition increased during the recession.

english_meaning: Not typical; unusual or uncommon. Something that does not conform to the usual type, pattern, or expectation; irregular or abnormal in nature.
example_sentence: His reaction to the news was atypical for him. The weather this month is atypical for the region. Atypical symptoms can make diagnosis difficult. She wore an atypical outfit for the formal event.

english_meaning: A reddish-brown color, especially of hair. Having a rich brown color with a reddish tint. A shade between brown and red commonly seen in hair.
example_sentence: She had long auburn hair that shone in the sunlight. The auburn leaves of autumn covered the ground. He admired her auburn locks. The horse had a beautiful auburn coat.

english_meaning: To sell something to the highest bidder. To sell an item or property publicly, where people bid and the highest offer wins.
example_sentence: They auctioned off their property as they were heavily in debt. He backed away from the dog. She backed away slowly. They auctioned off the old furniture. The painting was auctioned off for charity. The government decided to auction off the land. He auctioned off his collection of stamps.

english_meaning: Bold, daring, and willing to take risks. Showing a confident lack of fear. Too bold in a way that may seem rude or shocking. Original and adventurous in an impressive way.
example_sentence: Her audacious plan surprised the whole team. The thief made an audacious escape in daylight. It was audacious of him to challenge the champion. The designer presented an audacious new building concept.

english_meaning: Able to be heard. That can be heard clearly by the ear. It is used when a sound is strong enough to be detected or understood by listening.
example_sentence: The teacher spoke in an audible voice so all students could hear. His heartbeat was barely audible in the silent room. The alarm became audible after the door was closed. She made sure her instructions were audible to everyone in the hall.

english_meaning: The assembled spectators or listeners at a public event such as a play or concert. The people who watch a particular television or radio program. A formal interview or meeting with a person of high rank or authority. A group of readers or consumers of a specific piece of media or literature. The act of hearing or attending to someone's words or performance.
example_sentence: The theater audience erupted into applause at the end of the spectacular play. The popular podcast has reached a massive global audience. The ambassador requested a formal audience with the king to discuss the treaty. The author writes books specifically tailored for a young adult audience.

english_meaning: Relating to the sense of hearing or the organs involved in hearing. Connected with the ears and the perception of sound. Pertaining to what is heard rather than seen or read.
example_sentence: The doctor checked his auditory nerves carefully. Music can have a strong auditory effect on the mind. Some children are auditory learners and grasp things by listening. The auditory canal connects the outer ear to the eardrum. She suffers from a mild auditory problem since childhood.

english_meaning: Showing a willingness to take bold risks. Extremely daring or fearless in behavior. Confidently unafraid of danger, difficulty, or authority. Shockingly bold, sometimes to the point of rudeness. Displaying courage combined with originality or defiance.
example_sentence: The audacious climber scaled the mountain in a single day. Her audacious plan surprised the board members. He made an audacious escape from the prison. The company launched an audacious new marketing campaign.

english_meaning: A tool with a spiral blade used for boring holes in wood, soil, or ice. A large screw-shaped device used to move loose material such as grain or snow. A drilling implement turned by hand or by machine to make deep holes. The rotating helical part of a machine that conveys material along a tube.
example_sentence: The carpenter used an auger to bore holes for the bolts. Farmers loaded the grain into the truck with a mechanical auger. He drilled through the thick ice with a hand auger. The auger jammed when it struck a hidden stone in the soil.

english_meaning: To make something greater by adding to it. To increase, enlarge, or improve something in size, value, strength, or amount by adding more to it. It is often used when something already exists and is being enhanced further.
example_sentence: He augmented his income with a part-time job. The company plans to augment its staff during the busy season. He augmented his income by doing freelance work. The teacher used videos to augment the lesson. Regular exercise can augment your overall health.

english_meaning: The act of making something larger, greater, or stronger. An increase in amount, size, or degree. Something added to improve or enlarge an existing thing. The process of supplementing or enhancing.
example_sentence: The augmentation of the water supply took two years. He asked for an augmentation of his monthly salary. The hospital announced the augmentation of its emergency staff. Data augmentation helped improve the model's accuracy.

english_meaning: To predict or foretell a future event, especially from signs or omens. To be a sign of a particular outcome, whether good or bad. To serve as an indication of how something is likely to turn out. In ancient Rome, a religious official who interpreted omens to guide public decisions. A person who claims to foresee the future through signs.
example_sentence: The strong opening sales augur well for the new business. Dark clouds on the horizon augured a difficult journey ahead. The ancient augur studied the flight of birds before the battle. Her confident performance in training augurs a successful season.

english_meaning: An invisible quality or energy that seems to surround someone or something and strongly influences how others feel about it. It can suggest mood, character, or presence.
example_sentence: The teacher had an aura of confidence that calmed the students. The old library carried an aura of mystery and wisdom. Her kindness gave her an aura that people trusted instantly. The leader entered the room with an aura of authority.

english_meaning: Golden in color or appearance. Made of gold or covered with gold. Brilliant or splendid like gold. In literature, using flowery or grand language.
example_sentence: The aureate glow of the sunset filled the sky. The crown had an aureate shine under the lights. The poet was known for his aureate style of writing. An aureate frame surrounded the old painting.

english_meaning: The visible, shell-shaped outer flap of the ear made of skin-covered cartilage. The part of the ear that collects sound waves and funnels them into the ear canal. A small ear-shaped pouch attached to each atrium of the heart.
example_sentence: The auricle helps us judge the direction of a sound. He wore a small ring on the edge of his auricle. The auricle is shaped by flexible cartilage. In the heart, each auricle sits above a ventricle.

english_meaning: The act of listening to sounds inside the body, usually with a stethoscope. A medical examination of the heart, lungs, or other organs by listening. The clinical technique used to detect abnormal internal sounds.
example_sentence: The doctor performed auscultation of the patient's chest. Auscultation revealed an irregular heartbeat. Medical students practise auscultation from the first year. Careful auscultation can detect early lung problems.

english_meaning: Support, protection, or patronage given by a person or organisation. Signs believed to indicate future success. The guidance or sponsorship under which something is done.
example_sentence: The conference was held under the auspices of the university. They travelled under the auspices of a charity. The talks began under favourable auspices. The programme runs under government auspices.

english_meaning: Giving signs of future success or good fortune. Favorable or promising. Marked by hope and good conditions. Lucky or encouraging at the beginning of something.
example_sentence: The clear sky was an auspicious sign for the wedding. She made an auspicious start to her career. The agreement came at an auspicious moment. Their first meeting proved auspicious for the project.

english_meaning: In a way that suggests future success. With favourable signs or promising conditions. In a manner that seems lucky or fortunate.
example_sentence: The project began auspiciously with strong public support. Their partnership started auspiciously last spring. The season opened auspiciously with an easy win. Everything seemed to begin auspiciously that morning.

english_meaning: Simple and plain, without any decorations. Strict and serious in appearance and behaviour. Allowing nothing that gives pleasure, not comfortable.
example_sentence: The monk lived an austere life in the mountains. Her austere personality made her seem unapproachable. The room had an austere design with no decorations. The school follows austere rules to maintain discipline.

english_meaning: A strict and simple way of living. It refers to reducing comforts, spending less, and avoiding unnecessary things. In economics it describes government policies that cut expenses to control debt.
example_sentence: The family adopted austerity after facing financial trouble. The government introduced austerity to reduce national debt. His room showed austerity with only the basic furniture. After overspending for years they decided to live with more austerity.

english_meaning: Self-government or the state of being politically or economically independent, especially by relying on one's own resources rather than depending on others. A condition in which a country, state, or political community governs itself independently or seeks to meet its own needs without relying on foreign countries or external sources.
example_sentence: The nation suffered under decades of autarchy. Historians described his rule as an autarchy rather than a democracy. Autarchy concentrates all state power in a single ruler. The revolution ended the old system of autarchy.

english_meaning: A film director whose individual style, vision, and creative control are so strong that they are regarded as the primary author of the film. An artist with a distinctive personal signature across their body of work.
example_sentence: The festival honored him as a great auteur of modern cinema. Critics study her films as the work of a true auteur. Auteur theory argues that the director is the main creative force behind a film. Many consider him the most influential auteur of his generation.

english_meaning: Of undisputed origin and not a copy, genuine. True to one's own personality, spirit, or character. Reliable, trustworthy, or based on fact. Made or done in the traditional or original way.
example_sentence: This is an authentic painting by Picasso. She told an authentic story of her struggles. The restaurant serves authentic Italian food. Make sure the documents are authentic before signing them. His authentic style of writing impressed the readers.

english_meaning: In a genuine, real, and true manner. In a way that faithfully represents the original or actual source. Sincerely and honestly, without pretending or copying.
example_sentence: The restaurant serves authentically prepared regional dishes. She spoke authentically about her struggles. The museum displays artifacts authentically restored to their original condition. He lived authentically, never pretending to be someone else.

english_meaning: To prove or confirm that something is genuine, real, and not a forgery or copy. To verify the identity or origin of a person, document, or object. To establish the authority or validity of something officially.
example_sentence: Experts were called in to authenticate the ancient painting. The system uses passwords to authenticate users before granting access. Notaries authenticate documents with their official seal. Scientists worked to authenticate the origin of the rare manuscript.

english_meaning: The quality of being genuine, real, or true. The condition of being trustworthy, reliable, or based on facts. The state of being made or performed in the original or traditional way. Truthfulness of origin, attributions, or claims.
example_sentence: Experts confirmed the authenticity of the ancient manuscript. The authenticity of his story was questioned by many. She values authenticity in her relationships. The museum guarantees the authenticity of every artifact displayed. The chef is known for the authenticity of his recipes.

english_meaning: A person who writes a book, article, play or other written work. The creator or originator of an idea, plan or event. To write or create a piece of written material. The person legally recognised as the writer of a work.
example_sentence: The author signed copies of her new novel. He is the author of the peace plan. She authored three books before the age of thirty. The author explained his ideas during the interview.

english_meaning: Favoring or enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom. A person who demands complete obedience and exercises absolute power. Relating to a system of government in which the ruler has total control.
example_sentence: The country suffered under an authoritarian regime for decades. His authoritarian style of teaching made students uncomfortable. The manager's authoritarian behavior caused many employees to resign. Authoritarian governments often suppress free speech. She refused to work under such an authoritarian boss.

english_meaning: Able to be trusted as being accurate or true, reliable. Commanding and self-confident, likely to be respected and obeyed. Based on competent authority or expert knowledge. Proceeding from an official source and requiring compliance.
example_sentence: She gave an authoritative speech on climate change. This is the most authoritative book on the subject. He spoke in an authoritative tone that silenced the crowd. The teacher gave an authoritative explanation of the topic. We need an authoritative source to confirm this news.

english_meaning: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience. A person or organization having such power. Expert knowledge or a recognized expert in a field. Official permission or approval to do something. Confidence and influence resulting from expertise or position.
example_sentence: The manager has the authority to hire new staff. Local authorities are investigating the incident. She is a leading authority on ancient history. The book was written with great authority.

english_meaning: A system of government by one person with absolute power. A country, state, or society governed by one person with unrestricted authority. Domineering rule or control by a single individual without any checks.
example_sentence: The country was ruled as an autocracy for many years. People rose up against the cruel autocracy of the king. Autocracy often leads to corruption and injustice. He criticized the government for turning into an autocracy. History has shown that autocracy rarely brings lasting peace.

english_meaning: A ruler with absolute power over a country or organization. A person who governs alone, without any checks or balances, often making decisions unilaterally and demanding complete obedience.
example_sentence: The king acted as an autocrat, ignoring the council’s advice. In the company, the CEO was an autocrat who made all decisions alone. History often remembers autocrats for their harsh rule. She refused to become an autocrat, preferring to consult her team.

english_meaning: Taking no account of other people's wishes or opinions, domineering. Relating to a ruler who has absolute power. Acting in a dictatorial or commanding manner without consulting others.
example_sentence: His autocratic leadership style upset many employees. The autocratic ruler ignored the people's demands. She made an autocratic decision without consulting the team. Autocratic governments rarely tolerate opposition. The teacher's autocratic behavior discouraged class participation.

english_meaning: In an autocratic manner, with absolute power and without considering others. In a dictatorial way that demands obedience. With domineering authority and no room for discussion.
example_sentence: He ruled autocratically for nearly two decades. The manager autocratically rejected every suggestion. She behaves autocratically with her subordinates. The committee was led autocratically by its chairman. Decisions made autocratically often lack public support.

english_meaning: A person who learns by themselves without a formal teacher. Someone who gains knowledge and skills through self-study, personal effort, books, online resources, or practical experience instead of attending formal classes or having a teacher.
synonyms: ["Self learner","Self taught person","Independent learner","Self educated person"]
example_sentence: He became a successful programmer as an autodidact. She is an autodidact who learned painting at home. Many famous writers were autodidacts. As an autodidact, he studied mathematics using online courses.

english_meaning: Relating to the practice of somebody getting sexual excitement from their own body. Sexually satisfying yourself (as by masturbation).
example_sentence:
I like thinking, which is autoerotic, the mind being part of the body and thoughts.
Masturbation is a common autoerotic practice.
Experts concluded the man’s death likely was not due to autoerotic asphyxiation, but a murder.

english_meaning: The practice of stimulating oneself sexually to achieve pleasure or orgasm, without involving another person. It can include behaviors such as masturbation or sexual fantasies. It is a concept studied in psychology and human sexuality.
example_sentence: Autoeroticism is a natural part of adolescent sexual development. Psychologists study autoeroticism to understand human sexuality. Some literature discusses the role of autoeroticism in sexual identity. The film explored themes of loneliness and autoeroticism.

english_meaning: Relating to diseases where the immune system attacks the body's own tissues. Involving an immune response directed against the body itself. Caused by antibodies or immune cells targeting one's own organs or tissues.
example_sentence: Lupus is an autoimmune disease. Her autoimmune condition requires ongoing treatment. Autoimmune disorders affect millions of people worldwide. The doctor specializes in autoimmune diseases.

english_meaning: Not under external control, independent in decision-making. Able to organize and manage one’s own activities or tasks. Operating automatically or without human intervention (used in technology or robotics). A region or entity with its own governing authority within a larger system. Thinking or acting based on one’s own reasoning rather than influence.
example_sentence: The autonomous council manages local affairs without interference. Scientists are developing autonomous robots for space exploration. The autonomous province enacted laws suited to its population. He became more autonomous in managing his finances.

english_meaning: Independence to make your own decisions or control your own affairs. The condition of having self rule or the freedom to govern yourself. It can refer to personal independence, an institution or region managing its own matters, or the ability to act without external control.
example_sentence: The region demanded greater autonomy from the central government. Children need some autonomy to build confidence and decision making skills. The university was granted autonomy to design its own curriculum. Employees feel more motivated when they are given autonomy in their work.

english_meaning: An autophile is a person who loves solitude or being alone. It refers to someone who feels happiest, most comfortable, and spiritually fulfilled in their own company. It can also describe a person who has an intense passion or admiration for automobiles.
example_sentence: As an autophile, Sarah spends her weekends reading quietly in her cabin. Being an autophile does not mean one is antisocial or depressed. He realized he was an autophile when he enjoyed traveling alone more than in groups. The autophile spent hours admiring the vintage sports cars at the exhibition.

english_meaning: A person who fears loneliness or being alone; someone who has an irrational dread of being by themselves or isolated from others.
example_sentence: As an autophobe, she could not spend even an hour alone. His autophobe tendencies made relationships very difficult. The autophobe panicked whenever left alone at home. She sought help for her autophobe condition through therapy.

english_meaning: An intense fear of being alone or feeling abandoned. It is more than simple loneliness and often causes anxiety, panic, or emotional distress when a person is by themselves.
synonyms: ["Fear of being alone","Fear of abandonment","Monophobia","Isolation anxiety"]
antonyms: ["Love of solitude","Comfort with loneliness","Independence","Emotional self reliance"]
example_sentence: She avoids staying home alone because her autophobia triggers panic attacks. His autophobia makes long periods of isolation very difficult. Therapy helped her manage the anxiety caused by autophobia. Autophobia is not about disliking solitude but fearing abandonment.

english_meaning: A medical examination of a dead body to find the cause of death. Postmortem examination. Medical investigation after death. A detailed analysis of a failure or event to understand what went wrong.
example_sentence: The doctor performed an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death. The police ordered an autopsy in the suspicious case. The autopsy report revealed no signs of poisoning. After the project failed, the team conducted an autopsy of their mistakes.

english_meaning: The season between summer and winter when temperatures fall and leaves change color. A period of maturity or gradual decline late in a person’s life or in the development of something.
example_sentence: The leaves turn red and gold in autumn. We usually visit the mountains in early autumn. Autumn brought cooler evenings and shorter days. The poet wrote about the autumn of his life.

english_meaning: A formal statement in which the United Kingdom government presents economic forecasts and proposed financial measures, usually in autumn. A seasonal government update on taxation, spending, and the economy.
example_sentence: The chancellor announced new tax measures in the Autumn Statement. Businesses waited for the Autumn Statement before making plans. The Autumn Statement included updated growth forecasts. Parliament debated the proposals in the Autumn Statement.

english_meaning: Relating to or characteristic of autumn. Having colors, weather, or qualities associated with autumn. Suggesting maturity, decline, or the later part of life.
example_sentence: The garden was filled with autumnal colors. A cool autumnal breeze moved through the trees. She decorated the table with autumnal leaves. The novel has a quiet and autumnal mood.

english_meaning: Providing additional help or support. Something or someone that functions in a supportive or supplementary role, assisting the main function or operation. In grammar, an auxiliary verb helps the main verb to form tenses, moods, or voices.
example_sentence: The hospital has an auxiliary power generator in case of outages. She works as an auxiliary nurse in the community clinic. In the sentence "She has gone," "has" is an auxiliary verb. The army called in auxiliary forces to support the main battalion.

english_meaning: A mass of snow, ice, and rocks falling rapidly down a mountainside. A sudden arrival or occurrence of something in overwhelming quantities. To descend or rush down like a mass of snow.
example_sentence: An avalanche buried several climbers on the mountain. The actress received an avalanche of fan mail. The village was destroyed by a sudden avalanche. He faced an avalanche of criticism after his speech. The team was hit by an avalanche of injuries this season.

english_meaning: Extreme desire for wealth or material gain. A strong, selfish desire to acquire and hoard wealth or possessions, often at the expense of ethics or concern for others. It implies greed that is excessive and morally negative.
example_sentence: His avarice led him to cheat his business partners. The king’s avarice made him ignore the needs of his people. Avarice can destroy friendships and trust. She avoided people driven by avarice.

english_meaning: Having or showing an extreme greed for wealth or material gain. Excessively acquisitive and unwilling to share resources. Being driven by a desire to hoard riches at any cost. Characterized by a miserly or grasping nature.
example_sentence: The avaricious landlord increased the rent despite the building's poor condition. Avaricious corporations often prioritize profits over environmental safety. His avaricious nature led him to betray his closest friends for a bribe. It is difficult to satisfy an avaricious person who always wants more.

english_meaning: A nautical command to stop or desist from a particular action immediately. A call to hold fast or stay still, used primarily by sailors. An exclamation meaning 'stop' or 'cease'. Used to get someone's attention or to halt progress.
example_sentence: Avast, ye swabs, and listen to the captain's orders! The sailor shouted 'Avast!' when he saw the rope about to snap. Avast hauling the line before it becomes entangled in the winch. The boatswain yelled 'Avast' to signal the end of the shift.

english_meaning: An incarnation, embodiment, or manifestation of a person or idea. In Hindu mythology, the descent of a deity to earth in an incarnate form. An icon or figure representing a particular person in a video game, internet forum, or online platform.
example_sentence: Lord Krishna is considered an avatar of Vishnu. She chose a cartoon character as her avatar. He is regarded as the avatar of kindness and compassion. You can change your avatar in the game settings. The leader was seen as the avatar of justice by his followers.

english_meaning: To punish or harm someone in return for an injury or wrong. To obtain justice or satisfaction on behalf of oneself or another person. To retaliate for a defeat, insult, or injustice.
example_sentence: She vowed to avenge her brother's death. The team avenged last year's defeat with a decisive victory. He wanted to avenge the insult but chose to remain calm. The hero returns to avenge the villagers who were attacked. Justice, not anger, should guide anyone seeking to avenge a wrong.

english_meaning: A person who inflicts harm in return for an injury or wrong done to themselves or another. One who takes vengeance on behalf of a victim. A figure, often in mythology or fiction, who seeks justice through retribution. A retaliator who rights a perceived wrong through punishment.
example_sentence: He saw himself as an avenger of his family's lost honor. The dark knight returned to the city as a silent avenger against crime. Legends speak of a supernatural avenger who punishes the wicked. She acted as an avenger for those who were too weak to fight for themselves.

english_meaning: The imagined ability to see one's memories in advance, as if remembering the future. A longing to know how life will unfold before living it. The wish that time flowed backward so we could learn before choosing. A poetic term for the desire to view life in reverse.
example_sentence: He felt a strange avenoir as he watched the children play. The poet described avenoir as a bittersweet ache. Avenoir haunts anyone who wishes they had known sooner. She wrote about avenoir in her latest essay.

english_meaning: Having a strong dislike or opposition to something. Unwilling or reluctant to do a particular thing. Feeling distaste towards an idea or activity. Not favourably inclined.
example_sentence: He is averse to taking financial risks. She seemed averse to any change in the routine. Many investors are averse to uncertainty. I am not averse to a short walk after dinner.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of dislike or disinclination toward something. A settled or firm dislike for a person, activity, or thing. A feeling of repugnance combined with a desire to avoid something.
example_sentence: She has always had a strong aversion to any form of dishonesty or deception. His aversion to early mornings was well known among his colleagues. The patient developed an aversion to the smell of the medication after prolonged use. Her aversion to public speaking made it difficult for her to present her research. He overcame his aversion to spicy food after years of living abroad.

english_meaning: Showing great enthusiasm for or interest in something. Having or showing a keen interest in or enthusiasm for something. Extremely eager or greedy in pursuit of something.
example_sentence: She is an avid reader of historical novels. He is an avid supporter of his local football team. They were avid travelers and visited many countries. My father is an avid collector of old coins. The boy showed an avid interest in painting from a young age.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving avionics or aircraft electronics. Concerning electronic systems in aviation. Associated with flight control and navigation electronics. Of or pertaining to aerospace electronic equipment.
example_sentence: The avionic equipment needs maintenance. Avionic systems are critical for flight safety. He works on avionic design projects. Avionic technology has advanced significantly.

english_meaning: The electronic systems used in aircraft, spacecraft, and satellites. The technology combining aviation and electronics. Systems for communication, navigation, and flight control in aircraft. The science of electronic equipment for aerospace applications.
example_sentence: Modern aircraft rely heavily on avionics. Avionics systems include radar and GPS. The avionics upgrade improved flight safety. He specializes in avionics engineering.

english_meaning: A deep interest, affection, or emotional attachment to birds. It often includes bird watching, bird keeping, studying bird behavior, or supporting bird conservation.
example_sentence: Her aviophilia began when she started observing migratory birds as a child. Aviophilia often leads people to support wildlife and habitat conservation. Because of his aviophilia, he spends weekends photographing birds. The book explores aviophilia as both a hobby and a scientific interest.

english_meaning: Fear of flying in an aircraft. An anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear or panic when flying or even thinking about air travel. This fear may be linked to heights, loss of control, turbulence, or past negative experiences.
example_sentence: Because of her aviophobia, she always chooses to travel by train instead of plane. His aviophobia became worse after experiencing severe turbulence. Therapy helped her manage aviophobia and fly again with confidence. Many people with aviophobia feel anxious days before their flight.

english_meaning: A pear-shaped fruit with dark green skin, creamy pale-green flesh, and a large seed. A tropical fruit rich in healthy fats, often used in salads and spreads. The tree on which this fruit grows. A soft green colour similar to the flesh of the fruit.
example_sentence: He spread mashed avocado on his morning toast. Avocados grow best in warm, frost-free climates. The salad tasted better with slices of ripe avocado. She painted the kitchen wall a soft avocado green.

english_meaning: Showing kindness, friendliness, or generosity in a way that resembles a caring uncle. Often implies a supportive, warm, and guiding demeanor. Characteristic of an uncle; kind and indulgent. Supportive, mentoring, and protective behavior toward younger people. Gentle, approachable, and trustworthy in demeanor.
example_sentence: His avuncular smile made the new students feel instantly at ease. The professor had an avuncular approach, always encouraging students to ask questions. She enjoyed the avuncular advice of her elder colleague. His avuncular gestures made everyone in the office trust him naturally.

english_meaning: Knowing about something or realising that it exists. Having knowledge or understanding of a particular situation or fact. Noticing something through the senses or feelings. Well informed about current events, issues, or social concerns.
example_sentence: I was not aware that the office would be closed today. She is fully aware of the risks involved in the plan. He became aware of a strange noise behind him. Young people today are far more environmentally aware.

english_meaning: Very bad or unpleasant. Causing fear, shock, or distress. Extremely serious or severe. Very great in amount or degree. In older usage, inspiring awe or deep respect.
example_sentence: The weather was awful all weekend. She felt awful about missing the meeting. There was an awful silence after the announcement. The accident caused awful damage to the bridge.

english_meaning: Causing difficulty or discomfort; hard to deal with. Lacking grace or skill in movement or manner. Creating or feeling embarrassment or inconvenience. Not convenient or well-designed for use.
example_sentence: There was an awkward silence after his comment. The package is awkward to carry. She felt awkward at the formal dinner. The tool has an awkward design.

english_meaning: In a clumsy or ungraceful manner. In a way that causes embarrassment or discomfort. Without skill or coordination. In an uncomfortable or difficult way.
example_sentence: He awkwardly apologized for his mistake. She moved awkwardly in the high heels. The conversation ended awkwardly. He awkwardly reached for the door handle.

english_meaning: Lack of grace or skill in movement or handling. Social discomfort or embarrassment in a situation. The quality of being difficult to deal with or inconvenient. Clumsiness in speech, manner, or design.
example_sentence: There was an obvious awkwardness between the two old friends. He apologised for the awkwardness of the arrangements. The awkwardness of the tool made the job harder. Her awkwardness on stage disappeared after a few minutes.

english_meaning: A tool with a heavy bladed head mounted across a handle, used for chopping wood. To end, cancel, or dismiss something or someone, often suddenly. To reduce drastically, especially by cutting jobs, budgets, or services.
example_sentence: He used an axe to chop the wood for the fire. The company decided to axe several projects to cut costs. Hundreds of workers were axed during the recession. The government plans to axe the unnecessary departments. She swung the axe and split the log in one stroke.

english_meaning: A jump in figure skating involving one and a half rotations in the air. A skating move named after Norwegian skater Axel Paulsen. A difficult maneuver in ice skating. A forward-entry jump with rotation.
synonyms: ["Figure skating jump","Skating maneuver","Ice skating jump","Rotation jump"]
example_sentence: She landed a perfect triple axel. The axel is one of the most difficult jumps in skating. He is practicing his double axel for the competition. The skater fell while attempting the axel.

english_meaning: A person who uses an axe, especially to cut down trees. A woodcutter or lumberjack. Someone skilled in wielding an axe. A person who performs drastic cost-cutting in business.
example_sentence: The axeman skillfully felled the large tree. He worked as an axeman in the logging industry. The company brought in an axeman to reduce costs. The axeman's precision was impressive.

english_meaning: Relating to or forming an axis. Situated around or along a central line. Concerning the central or main part of something. In the direction of an axis.
example_sentence: The earth rotates on its axial line. Axial symmetry means symmetry around an axis. The axial skeleton includes the skull and spine. Axial forces act along the length of a structural member.

english_meaning: The armpit. The hollow space under the shoulder where the arm joins the body. In plants, axilla also means the angle between the upper side of a leaf or branch and the stem from which it grows.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the patient's axilla for swollen lymph nodes. Sweat glands in the axilla help regulate body temperature. She felt a small lump in her left axilla and decided to see a doctor. The injury extended from his shoulder down to the axilla.

english_meaning: A statement or proposition regarded as being established, accepted, or self-evidently true. A widely accepted principle or rule. In mathematics or logic, a basic truth that does not require proof.
example_sentence: It is an axiom that honesty is the best policy. The teacher explained the axioms of geometry. Hard work brings success is a well-known axiom. He often quotes axioms from ancient philosophers. The whole theory is built upon a few simple axioms.

english_meaning: Self-evidently true without requiring proof. Based on or involving axioms or accepted principles. So obvious as to be beyond dispute or doubt. Relating to statements accepted as true without demonstration.
example_sentence: It is axiomatic that all humans need water to survive. The principle is axiomatic in mathematics. His honesty is axiomatic among his colleagues. The statement is considered axiomatic and needs no proof.

english_meaning: In a self-evident or obvious manner. By means of axioms or accepted principles. In a way that requires no proof or demonstration. Obviously or undeniably.
example_sentence: The conclusion follows axiomatically from the premises. This principle is axiomatically true in all cases. Axiomatically, the whole is greater than any of its parts. The result can be derived axiomatically.

english_meaning: A hypothetical elementary particle in particle physics. A theoretical particle proposed to explain certain phenomena in quantum mechanics. A subatomic particle that may constitute dark matter. A particle predicted by theory but not yet observed experimentally.
example_sentence: Scientists are searching for evidence of axions. The axion is a candidate for dark matter. Axion detection experiments are ongoing. The existence of axions remains theoretical.

english_meaning: An imaginary straight line around which an object rotates. A fixed reference line used for measuring coordinates on a graph. A central line that divides something into equal parts. An alliance between countries or groups with a common purpose.
example_sentence: The earth rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours. Label the horizontal axis with the years. Fold the paper along its central axis. The two nations formed a powerful political axis.

english_meaning: A rod or spindle, either fixed or rotating, passing through the center of a wheel or group of wheels. The central shaft on which wheels turn, especially in vehicles. A bar connecting two opposite wheels of a vehicle.
example_sentence: The truck's axle broke on the rough road. Mechanics replaced the rear axle of the car. The cart's wooden axle creaked under the heavy load. A bent axle can cause the wheels to wobble. The driver checked the axle before the long journey.

english_meaning: Yes, an expression of agreement, affirmation, or approval. Used to express agreement or consent, especially in formal or nautical contexts. Can be a positive response to a question or proposal. Used in parliamentary or official voting to indicate support.
example_sentence: Aye, captain, I understand the orders. All in favor, say aye. She answered aye when asked if she agreed. Aye, that is exactly what I meant. All those who this proposal say aye. Although the arguments have remained the same, the balance has swug in favour of the ayes.

english_meaning: Bright blue color like the sky on a clear day. A vivid, bright shade of blue that resembles the color of a clear daytime sky. It is often used in poetry, art, and design to describe something pure, calm, and open like the sky or sea.
example_sentence: The sky turned a deep azure after the storm passed. She wore a dress of soft azure silk. The azure sea stretched endlessly toward the horizon. Artists often use azure to represent peace and freedom.

english_meaning: An infant, A very young baby who is still carried in the arms. A person who is very inexperienced, immature, or naïve.
example_sentence: When he joined the company, he was just a babe in arms compared to the senior managers. She’s no babe in arms when it comes to politics, she knows exactly what she’s doing. The young mother looked tired while holding her babe in arms.

english_meaning: A very pale, soft shade of blue. A light blue color often associated with baby boys. A gentle pastel blue used in clothing and decoration.
example_sentence: The baby's room was painted baby blue. She wore a baby blue sweater on the cool evening. He bought a baby blue blanket for the newborn. The sky turned a soft baby blue at dawn.

english_meaning: A person born during a period of high birth rates after World War Two. Baby boomers are people born roughly between 1946 and 1964, when many countries experienced a rapid increase in births due to economic recovery and social stability after the war.
example_sentence: My parents are baby boomers who grew up during a time of economic growth. Many baby boomers are now retiring from full time jobs. Baby boomers experienced major social and cultural changes. The baby boomer generation values job security and stability.

english_meaning: An unmarried man. A person who holds a first university degree. A young knight serving under another's banner in medieval times. A man of any age who has never married. In some contexts, an independent single male living alone.
example_sentence: He remained a bachelor throughout his life. She earned a bachelor's degree in economics. The bachelor lived alone in a small apartment. Many of his friends were still bachelors in their thirties.

english_meaning: A young, unmarried woman who lives an independent life. A woman who has never been married. A female participant on a reality television dating show seeking a husband. A woman attending a social party held before her wedding. An independent female who is single by choice or circumstance.
example_sentence: She is enjoying her life as a successful bachelorette in the city. The bachelorette and her friends went to Las Vegas for a weekend celebration. She was chosen as the lead bachelorette for the upcoming season of the show. Many modern women prefer the bachelorette lifestyle before settling down.

english_meaning: The rear surface of the human body from the shoulders to the hips. The part of something that is opposite the front. The spine and the muscles supporting it. To support someone or something, especially with money or approval. To move in a backward direction. Located at or near the rear.
example_sentence: He hurt his back while lifting heavy furniture. The garden is at the back of the house. Several investors backed the new project. She backed the car slowly out of the garage.

english_meaning: To move backward from something or someone. To retreat or withdraw. To sell an item or property publicly, where people bid and the highest offer wins.
example_sentence: She backed away from the barking dog. He backed away from the argument. The crowd backed away as the fire spread. Don’t back away from your responsibilities.

english_meaning: To withdraw from a position, claim, or demand after resistance. To stop arguing or fighting when opposed. To yield, surrender, or accept defeat.
example_sentence: She refused to back down and was fired. He refused to back down, even when everyone disagreed with him. After a long argument, she finally backed down and accepted their proposal. The company backed down in the face of public pressure. He never backs down from a challenge.

english_meaning: To move backward and collide with something. To move backward into a space. To get involved in something again (often unintentionally). To re-enter a situation or condition.
example_sentence: He prefers to BACK his car INTO the garage. He accidentally backed into a parked car. She backed into the garage slowly. He backed into his old job after leaving the company. She backed into her old habits after some time.

english_meaning: Retreat, make space. To move away from someone or something. To stop criticizing, interfering, or being aggressive. To reduce pressure or intensity in an argument or situation.
example_sentence: You better back off a little if you want me to start serving this crown again. The dog barked, so he quickly backed off. You should back off and let her handle the problem herself. The manager told the staff to back off when the client got angry. He refused to back off even when he knew he was wrong.

english_meaning: Recovered from a problem, illness, or difficulty and functioning normally again.
