A situation where a person has gone through hardship such as illness, financial trouble, emotional stress, or failure, and has now recovered enough to return to normal life or activity. It often implies strength, resilience, and improvement after a setback.
example_sentence: After months of treatment, she is finally back on her feet. The small business was back on its feet after the crisis. He struggled for years but is now back on his feet financially. With support from friends, she got back on her feet again.

english_meaning: To reverse onto something. To have something directly behind it. To move or maneuver something backwards onto something.
example_sentence: The vehicle backed onto my father’s toe. Our house backs onto a beautiful park. The school playground backs onto a busy road. The restaurant backs onto the river, giving it a lovely view. The library backs onto the main street, so it can get noisy sometimes.

english_meaning: Fail to keep an arrangement or promise. To withdraw from an agreement, commitment, or promise. To decide not to do something you had earlier agreed to do.
example_sentence: He backed out two days before the holiday so we gave the ticket to his sister. He promised to help me with the project, but he backed out at the last minute. They agreed to sign the contract, but later backed out. She never backs out of her commitments. The company backed out of the deal after reviewing the risks.

english_meaning: Fail to keep an agreement, arrangement. To withdraw from an agreement, promise, or responsibility that one had previously accepted. To fail to keep a commitment or plan.
example_sentence: She backed out of the agreement at the last minute. He backed out of the deal at the last minute. She promised to help us, but then she backed out of her commitment. The company backed out of the contract due to financial problems.

english_meaning: To be forced to start again from the very beginning after a failure or setback. When all the effort is wasted, and you must return to the starting point.
example_sentence: After months of planning, the project was rejected, so we are back to square one. He failed the exam, which means he is back to square one with his studies. When the negotiations collapsed, both sides were back to square one. We lost all our data in the system crash, and now we are back to square one.

english_meaning: To start again from the beginning because the previous attempt failed. When a plan or idea does not succeed, and you have to go back and make a new one. Start over with a new plan.
example_sentence: The design failed, so it’s back to the drawing board. The plan didn’t work, so we’re back to the drawing board. Our first design didn’t work, so it’s back to the drawing board. The project failed due to technical issues, time to go back to the drawing board. After the client rejected our proposal, we went back to the drawing board.

english_meaning: Returning to work or routine duties, often something difficult, tiring, or unpleasant.
example_sentence: Vacation is over, time to go back to the salt mines. After lunch, everyone went back to the salt mines to finish the report. Monday morning again; I guess it’s back to the salt mines. He sighed and said, “Well, back to the salt mines,” as he opened his laptop.

english_meaning: To support someone or something. To make a copy of data for safety. To move backward. To accumulate or cause a delay (traffic, work, etc).
example_sentence:
My friends always back me up when I’m in trouble. You should back up your computer files regularly.
The car backed up to let the truck pass. Traffic was backed up for miles after the accident.

english_meaning: A secret or unofficial means of communication, especially in politics or diplomacy. A way of passing information or holding discussions outside official channels. Used for confidential talks between governments or organisations.
example_sentence: The two countries used a back-channel to resolve the dispute quietly. Diplomats often rely on back-channel talks before any official agreement. A back-channel message helped end the crisis. The deal was reached through secret back-channel negotiations. Intelligence agencies maintain back-channel links with their counterparts.

english_meaning: To speak badly about someone when they are not present. To criticize, insult, or spread negative comments about a person when that person is not there to hear or defend themselves. It usually reflects jealousy, resentment, or dishonesty and can damage relationships and trust.
example_sentence: Some people smile in front of you but backbite when you leave the room. It is unfair to backbite your colleagues instead of discussing problems openly. A true friend will never backbite you in your absence. Office politics often begin when employees start to backbite each other.

english_meaning: The column of bones running down the middle of the back, also called the spine. The main support or most important part of a system or organisation. Strength of character, courage, and determination. The main high-capacity route of a communications network.
example_sentence: He injured his backbone in the accident. Small farmers are the backbone of the rural economy. She had the backbone to speak against the decision. Fibre-optic cables form the backbone of the network.

english_meaning: To produce a result opposite to the one intended, usually with harmful effect. Of an engine, to make a loud bang because of premature or delayed combustion. A fire deliberately started to stop an advancing fire by removing fuel. A sudden explosive noise from a vehicle's exhaust.
example_sentence: The plan backfired and cost the company millions. His attempt to embarrass the minister backfired badly. The old truck backfired loudly as it climbed the hill. Firefighters lit a backfire to protect the village.

english_meaning: A strong negative reaction by a large number of people, for example to something that has recently changed in society. A strong feeling among a group of people in reaction to a change or recent events in society or politics. A sudden violent backward movement or reaction. A strong public response against something.
example_sentence: The government is facing an angry backlash from voters over the new tax. They face a backlash from shareholders. There was a conservative backlash against the feminism of the 80s. The mayor foresaw no political backlash against his proposal. There was swift backlash to the senator's controversial comments.

english_meaning: A passenger who gives unwanted advice to the driver. A person who interferes in matters that are not their responsibility. Someone who criticizes without doing the work themselves. An observer who tells others how to act. A person offering unsolicited direction.
example_sentence: My aunt is a real backseat driver during long trips. Nobody likes a backseat driver in the office. Stop being a backseat driver and let me focus. He acts like a backseat driver in every meeting.

english_meaning: A yard or garden at the back of a house. An area considered to be in one's immediate neighborhood or sphere of interest. A nearby area where one feels a sense of ownership or familiarity.
example_sentence: The children were playing in the backyard. We grow vegetables in our backyard. He built a small swimming pool in the backyard. The factory was set up right in their backyard. Politicians often ignore the problems in their own backyard.

english_meaning: Salted and cured meat from a pig, usually eaten fried. Bacon is meat taken from the back or sides of a pig. It is preserved using salt, and sometimes smoked, before cooking. It is commonly used in breakfasts, sandwiches, and many dishes for flavor.
example_sentence: He cooked bacon and eggs for breakfast. The sandwich was filled with crispy bacon. Bacon adds a rich flavor to the dish. She prefers her bacon well-cooked and crunchy.

english_meaning: The plural form of bacterium referring to multiple unicellular microorganisms. A group of microscopic organisms that live in soil, water, and the bodies of plants and animals.
example_sentence: Washing your hands with soap helps eliminate harmful bacteria. The human gut contains trillions of beneficial bacteria. These bacteria multiply rapidly in warm environments. Antibiotics are prescribed to treat infections caused by bacteria.

english_meaning: A member of a large group of unicellular microorganisms which have cell walls but lack organelles and an organized nucleus. A single microscopic organism that can cause disease or be beneficial.
example_sentence: The scientist isolated a single bacterium under the microscope. A specific bacterium is responsible for causing this type of infection. Not every bacterium is harmful to the human body. The structure of this bacterium makes it resistant to certain antibiotics.

english_meaning: A person who negatively influences others; a troublemaker in a group. Someone whose behavior or attitude is harmful, unethical, or disruptive, often spoiling the reputation or morale of a group. It comes from the saying "one bad apple spoils the whole barrel".
example_sentence: He is considered a bad apple in the company because of his dishonest practices. One bad apple can ruin the morale of an entire team. Don’t let a bad apple in your circle lead you astray. She avoided him, knowing he was a bad apple who caused problems wherever he went.

english_meaning: Hostility, resentment, or ill-feeling between people or groups, often caused by past conflicts or disagreements.
example_sentence: There has been bad blood between the two families for decades. Despite the reconciliation, some bad blood remained from their previous argument. The rivalry created bad blood among the employees. He tried to patch things up, but the bad blood was too deep.

english_meaning: An event or phenomenon believed to portend bad luck or evil in the future. A warning or sign indicating that a disastrous situation or failure is imminent. A negative foreboding or intuition experienced by an individual regarding upcoming events.
example_sentence: Seeing a black cat cross the street was considered a bad omen by the superstitious travelers. The sudden drop in stock prices served as a bad omen for the economic future. Dark storm clouds gathering overhead felt like a bad omen before the outdoor wedding. He ignored the bad omen and decided to continue his journey despite the warnings.

english_meaning: A person or thing that keeps coming back, usually unwelcome or troublesome. Someone who returns repeatedly despite attempts to avoid them.
example_sentence: That bad penny always turns up at the worst possible time. He’s like a bad penny, no matter what we do, he keeps coming back. The old problems are a bad penny; they just won’t go away. Every time there’s a party, that bad penny shows up uninvited.

english_meaning: Showing courage and confidence without fear. Exceptionally impressive, powerful, or outstanding. Having a rebellious, adventurous, or daring attitude. Extremely attractive, exciting, or remarkable. Informally used to describe someone who is tough and confident.
example_sentence: The firefighter made a badacious rescue during the storm. She gave a badacious presentation that impressed everyone. His badacious attitude helped him overcome every challenge. They built a badacious sports car with incredible performance.

english_meaning: To repeatedly annoy or persuade someone with questions or requests. To pester or bother a person until they agree or respond. A short-legged nocturnal mammal with black and white stripes on its face. To harass someone continuously for something. To press or push someone insistently.
example_sentence: The children badgered their father for a new bicycle. Reporters badgered the minister with tough questions. She kept badgering me until I finally agreed. A badger was seen digging near the forest path.

english_meaning: Striking the ground with a golf club just behind the ball, causing a poor shot. A faulty stroke in golf where the club hits the ground before the ball. A mishit resulting in the club skimming or bouncing off the turf.
example_sentence: The player lost the match due to repeated baffing. Beginners often struggle with baffing on uneven ground. He was embarrassed by his baffing in front of the crowd. Coaches help golfers correct the habit of baffing. Baffing usually happens when the swing is not balanced.

english_meaning: To totally bewilder or perplex someone. It also means to restrain or regulate the flow of a fluid or sound using a specific device. In a general sense, it involves frustrating someone's efforts or making a situation difficult to understand.
example_sentence: The strange noises coming from the attic continued to baffle the homeowners. The complex instructions for the new software managed to baffle even the IT experts. Engineers designed a special plate to baffle the flow of water in the pipe. His sudden decision to quit a high-paying job seemed to baffle his entire family.

english_meaning: A state of being utterly confused or bewildered. It refers to the feeling of being unable to understand or explain something complex or mysterious. This mental state often arises when someone is faced with a puzzling situation or a lack of clear information.
example_sentence: The magician's final trick left the entire audience in a state of utter bafflement. Scientists expressed their bafflement at the sudden change in the planet's atmospheric pressure. Her face was a mask of sheer bafflement when she looked at the complicated math equation. The mystery novel is designed to maintain a sense of bafflement until the very last page.

english_meaning: Impossible to understand, perplexing or confusing. Causing bewilderment by being difficult to explain. Preventing someone from understanding something. Mysterious or puzzling in nature.
example_sentence: The detective faced a baffling case with no clues. His sudden disappearance is truly baffling. The instructions were so baffling that no one could follow them. Scientists are still studying this baffling phenomenon. She gave a baffling answer that left everyone confused.

english_meaning: To proudly mention an achievement. To exaggerate personal success. To show superiority through words. A statement full of pride
example_sentence: He always brags about his expensive car. She bragged that she could finish the work alone. They never brag about their success. Winning the competition gave him something to brag about.

english_meaning: To criticize, mock, or complain about someone or something in a rude/unfair way. To speak badly or make fun of.
example_sentence: Don’t bag out your friends behind their backs. He kept bagging out the new teacher, which was very disrespectful. She bags out every movie she watches, even the good ones. Instead of helping, they just bagged me out for making mistakes.

english_meaning: Put into a bag, packed in a sack. Succeeded in obtaining, catching, or killing something, especially in hunting. Informally, secured or claimed something for oneself. Sagging or hanging loosely like an empty bag.
example_sentence: The shopkeeper bagged the groceries quickly. The hunter bagged two deer in a single day. She bagged the top prize at the competition. He has finally bagged a high-paying job. His trousers bagged at the knees after long use.

english_meaning: To claim the right to have or do something before anyone else. To call dibs on something. An informal British expression used, especially by children, to reserve something for oneself. It is used to quickly stake a claim on an object, seat, or task so that others cannot take it. It is a casual and playful word.
example_sentence: I bagsy the front seat of the car! He bagsied the last slice of pizza before anyone else could reach it. The kids always bagsy the window seats on long trips. She bagsied first turn on the new bicycle. I bagsy not doing the dishes tonight.

english_meaning: Bail on means to leave someone suddenly or fail to do something you promised.
example_sentence: He bailed on his friends. She bailed on the event. They bailed on the agreement. He bailed on me at the last minute.

english_meaning: To help someone or an organization out of a difficult situation, often by giving money, support, or assistance. It can also mean leaving a difficult situation quickly or abandoning a commitment.
example_sentence: They bailed him out of trouble. She bailed out of the project. He bailed out during the crisis. Investors bailed out the company.

english_meaning: To withdraw from something abruptly. To withdraw from a commitment, obligation, or situation.
example_sentence: He bailed out of the plan. They bailed out of the meeting. She bailed out of the deal. The team bailed out of the event.

english_meaning: To block someone or corner them usually to demand something. To stop someone suddenly and hold them in a way that they cannot leave.
example_sentence: The robbers bailed him up. He was bailed up by reporters. They bailed her up with questions. The man was bailed up in a corner.

english_meaning: To trap or corner someone on a point or issue. To confront someone about something they did or were supposed to do. It can also mean putting pressure on someone to explain or take responsibility.
example_sentence: They bailed him up on the mistake. Reporters bailed her up on the claim. He was bailed up on his statement. She was bailed up on the budget issue.

english_meaning: A person's area of skill, knowledge, authority, or work. The district or jurisdiction of a bailiff. A sphere of operations or interest in which one is particularly involved or expert.
example_sentence: Marketing is not really my bailiwick. Tax law is the lawyer's bailiwick. Cooking exotic dishes is her bailiwick. Please ask the engineer, this is his bailiwick. Foreign policy falls within the bailiwick of the prime minister.

english_meaning: Baker's dozen

Thirteen items instead of twelve. Slightly more than expected. An extra item added as a bonus. A group of thirteen items. Historically, bakers added one extra item to avoid punishment for selling underweight goods. Today, it simply refers to thirteen instead of twelve.
example_sentence: The shop gave me a baker’s dozen of cookies for the same price. She bought a baker’s dozen of roses for her mother. We invited a baker’s dozen of guests to the small party. He collected a baker’s dozen of rare coins over the years.

english_meaning: A rich sweet pastry made of thin layers of filo filled with chopped nuts and soaked in honey or syrup. A traditional dessert of Turkish, Greek, and Middle Eastern cuisine. A layered nut pastry served in small diamond-shaped pieces.
example_sentence: She served baklava with strong black coffee after dinner. The bakery is famous for its pistachio baklava. He brought a box of baklava back from Istanbul. Baklava is usually cut into small diamond shapes.

english_meaning: A small sum of money given as a tip, gratuity, or alms, especially in parts of Asia and the Middle East. A bribe or payment given to influence someone. To give such a tip or gratuity.
example_sentence: The porter expected some baksheesh after carrying the luggage. He gave the waiter baksheesh for his good service. Tourists are often asked for baksheesh in crowded markets. The clerk demanded baksheesh to speed up the paperwork. She handed a few coins as baksheesh to the beggar.

english_meaning: An even distribution of weight that keeps something steady and upright. A state in which different parts or forces are equal or in correct proportion. The amount of money remaining in an account after all payments. Mental or emotional steadiness. To keep or put something in a steady position. To compare and make two sides equal, especially in accounts.
example_sentence: She lost her balance and fell off the ladder. A good diet requires a balance of protein and vegetables. He checked the balance in his bank account online. Try to balance the book on your head without dropping it.

english_meaning: Having different parts or elements in the correct proportion. Fair and considering all sides of an issue without bias. Kept in a steady position without falling. Mentally and emotionally stable and sensible.
example_sentence: A balanced diet keeps the body healthy and strong. The newspaper gave a balanced report of the debate. The stone was balanced carefully on the edge of the wall. She is a balanced person who rarely loses her temper.

english_meaning: In a balanced manner, with all parts in correct proportion. In a fair and unbiased way that considers every side. In a steady and stable manner without leaning to one side.
example_sentence: The report presented both viewpoints balancedly. He answered the difficult question balancedly and calmly. The weight was distributed balancedly across the shelf. She manages work and family life balancedly.

english_meaning: Senseless, meaningless talk or writing. Nonsense. Foolish or absurd statements. Empty or worthless words.
example_sentence: His speech was pure balderdash from start to finish. Don't believe that balderdash he told you. The old man dismissed the theory as balderdash. She was tired of listening to his balderdash.

english_meaning: Threatening harm or menacing in appearance or manner. Having a harmful or destructive effect. Expressing anger, hatred, or ill will through a look. Foreshadowing evil or misfortune.
example_sentence: He gave her a baleful stare across the crowded room. The baleful influence of the war was felt for decades. Dark, baleful clouds gathered over the valley. The dog watched the stranger with baleful eyes.

english_meaning: A machine element that constrains relative motion to only the desired motion and reduces friction between moving parts by using small hardened steel balls. One of the individual hardened metal spheres used in such a bearing mechanism to facilitate smooth rotation. A complete mechanical assembly consisting of an inner and outer ring with a set of balls between them used in wheels or engines. A type of anti-friction rolling-element bearing that carries loads by using round balls to maintain the separation between the bearing races. A component used in various mechanical devices ranging from bicycle hubs to industrial turbines to ensure fluid and efficient movement.
synonyms: ["Bearing","Roller Bearing","Anti-friction Bearing","Thrust Bearing","Race","Steel Ball","Rotation Element","Mechanical Support","Pivot","Bushing","Wheel Bearing","Precision Bearing","Glide","Rotator"]
example_sentence: The bicycle wheel spins freely thanks to a newly greased ball bearing. I heard a rattling sound because a single ball bearing had escaped from the assembly. Industrial machines require heavy-duty ball bearings to handle high-speed rotations without overheating. You need to replace the entire ball bearing unit if the outer race becomes pitted or worn.

english_meaning: To confuse or complicate something. To mess up or make a mistake. To crumple something into a ball.
example_sentence: He really balled up the project by not submitting the report on time. Don’t ball up the instructions, just follow them carefully. She balled up the piece of paper and threw it in the trash. The situation got balled up because of poor communication.

english_meaning: A person, typically a woman, who is perceived as intimidating, domineering, or overly aggressive. A task, situation, or physical activity that is extremely difficult, exhausting, or demanding to complete. A supervisor or boss who enforces strict rules and demands an unreasonable amount of work from subordinates. A devastatingly sharp or critical remark intended to deflate someone's ego or confidence. A person or thing that ruins a pleasant situation or breaks the momentum of an activity through harsh behavior.
example_sentence: Working for that ball-breaker of a manager left the entire team burnt out within months. The mountain climb was a real ball-breaker, especially during the final steep ascent. She has a reputation for being a ball-breaker in the boardroom, never backing down from a fight. That exam was a total ball-breaker; even the smartest students struggled to finish in time.

english_meaning: Extremely difficult, arduous, or physically and mentally demanding to the point of exhaustion. Cruelly or excessively demanding and harsh, often used to describe a supervisor or a taskmaster. Crushing or humiliating to someone's pride, confidence, or masculinity. Characterized by intense pressure or stress that feels unbearable. An informal or vulgar way to describe an activity that is tedious and soul-crushing.
example_sentence: Working fourteen hours a day in the sun was absolute ball-breaking labor. She has a reputation for being a ball-breaking boss who never accepts excuses. The training camp was a ball-breaking experience designed to weed out the weak. Filling out all these redundant forms is a ball-breaking waste of my time.

english_meaning: A poem or song that tells a story, often about love, tragedy, adventure, or heroism, and usually written in simple language with regular rhythm and rhyme.
example_sentence: The poet composed a beautiful ballad about a brave soldier. Old English ballads often tell stories of love and loss. She sang a romantic ballad at the concert. The movie ends with a haunting ballad that captures the hero’s sacrifice.

english_meaning: Heavy material such as gravel, sand, or iron placed low in a vessel to improve stability. Coarse stones or gravel laid to form a bed for a railroad track or road. A device used in an electrical circuit to regulate the amount of current, especially for discharge lamps. Something that gives stability or substance to a person's character or a situation. To provide stability to a ship or structure by adding weight. To fill the space between railroad sleepers with gravel or crushed stone.
example_sentence: The ship had to take on extra ballast to survive the heavy storms in the Atlantic. Workers were busy replacing the old gravel ballast along the commuter rail line. If the fluorescent lamp flickers constantly, the magnetic ballast might be failing. Her solid upbringing served as a moral ballast during the most turbulent years of her career.

english_meaning: A young male attendant who retrieves and provides balls for players during a tennis match or other sports game. A person stationed behind the goal or along the sidelines to ensure the game continues quickly by supplying extra balls. A junior assistant or trainee in a sports setting tasked with managing equipment. A metaphorical term for someone performing menial or subordinate tasks for a more prominent figure in a competitive environment. In historical contexts, a young boy employed to keep track of balls during recreational games in private estates.
example_sentence: The ballboy quickly ran across the court to retrieve the stray tennis ball. During the final match, a young ballboy was praised for his speed and focus. He started his career as a humble ballboy before becoming a professional athlete. The coach told the ballboy to keep a fresh set of balls ready for the next serve.

english_meaning: A mechanism used to control the flow of water into a tank or cistern, typically consisting of a float and a valve. A mechanical device that automatically regulates the water level in a flush toilet or storage tank. A valve assembly operated by a hollow ball that rises and falls with the liquid level to open and shut the supply. The internal plumbing component that prevents overflow in water systems by stopping the intake once a set level is reached.
synonyms: ["Float valve","Float-operated valve","Water level controller","Cistern valve","Inlet valve","Tank valve","Control valve","Shut-off valve","Automatic valve","Liquid level valve","Plumbing valve","Flow regulator"]
antonyms: ["Manual tap","Open pipe","Continuous flow","Unregulated drain","Manual valve","Fixed outlet","Constant stream","Hand-operated pump"]
example_sentence: The plumber had to replace the rusted ballcock inside the toilet tank to stop the continuous leak. If the ballcock is misaligned, the water will keep running even when the cistern is full. I adjusted the arm of the ballcock to ensure the water level stayed below the overflow pipe. A faulty ballcock is a common cause of high water bills in residential buildings.

english_meaning: A female dancer who performs ballet professionally, often specifically a principal dancer in a company. A performer who is highly skilled in the classical and technical art of ballet dancing. A specific type of lightweight, flat-soled shoe worn by women that resembles a ballet slipper. Figuratively, a person who moves with the extreme grace, precision, and poise associated with professional dance. In a historical context, the leading female performer in a ballet troupe who holds the highest rank.
example_sentence: The young ballerina practiced her pirouettes for hours in front of the studio mirror. She was promoted to the rank of prima ballerina after her breathtaking performance in Swan Lake. She wore a pair of stylish pink ballerinas with her summer dress for a casual look. Even in her everyday movements, she carried herself with the elegance of a trained ballerina.

english_meaning: A highly formalized and artistic style of theatrical dance characterized by grace and precision of movement. A theatrical performance that consists of this style of dance, often telling a story with music but without words. A company or organized group of professional dancers who perform this style of dance. The music composed specifically for such a theatrical dance performance. A sequence of movements or actions in a creative work that resembles the stylized flow of professional dancing.
synonyms: ["Classical Dance","Artistic Dance","Choreography","Performance Dance","Theatrical Dance","Stage Dance","Interpretive Dance","Formal Dance","Plié","Pas De Deux","Dance Troupe","Rhythmic Movement","Graceful Motion","Artistic Expression"]
example_sentence: She has been practicing ballet since she was five years old to perfect her technique. The local theater is staging a beautiful production of the Nutcracker ballet this winter. The Royal Ballet is world-renowned for its talented performers and rigorous training. Tchaikovsky composed some of the most famous music ever written for the ballet.

english_meaning: Relating to projectiles such as bullets, shells, or missiles and their flight through the air. Moving under the force of gravity alone after an initial thrust. Concerning the science of the motion of thrown or fired objects. Used informally in the phrase 'go ballistic', meaning to become suddenly very angry.
example_sentence: The country tested a long-range ballistic missile. Experts examined the ballistic evidence found at the scene. The rocket followed a simple ballistic path. He went ballistic when he saw the damaged car.

english_meaning: Mild and pleasant, or slightly silly. Pleasantly warm, mild, and comfortable weather. Gentle, soothing, or refreshing atmosphere. Slightly foolish or crazy in an informal sense.
example_sentence: The evening was balmy, perfect for a walk by the sea. A balmy breeze made the garden feel peaceful and relaxing. He gave a balmy excuse that no one believed. The island is known for its balmy climate throughout the year.

english_meaning: Foolish or deceptive talk. Nonsense. Something considered untrue or exaggerated. A type of sausage (also 'bologna').
example_sentence: That story about winning the lottery is a load of baloney. Don't feed me that baloney; tell me the truth. His excuses were pure baloney. She made a sandwich with baloney and cheese.

english_meaning: To cheat, deceive, or trick someone by confusing them. To perplex or mystify a person. To get the better of someone by trickery or deception.
example_sentence: The salesman tried to bamboozle the old lady into buying a faulty product. Don't let him bamboozle you with his sweet talk. The magician bamboozled the entire audience with his tricks. She was bamboozled by the complicated legal language. They bamboozled investors out of their savings.

english_meaning: So ordinary and unoriginal that it is boring. Lacking freshness, originality, or interest. Commonplace and predictable, especially of remarks or ideas.
example_sentence: His speech was full of banal remarks about hard work. The film relies on a banal love story. She grew tired of their banal small talk. Even a banal idea can be saved by good writing.

english_meaning: The quality of being dull, ordinary, and lacking originality. A remark, idea, or thing that is boringly commonplace. The state of being predictable or unoriginal in thought or expression.
example_sentence: The speech was full of banality and offered nothing new. She was tired of the banality of daily office conversation. Critics complained about the banality of the film's dialogue. His writing rises above the banality of ordinary travel books.

english_meaning: A long curved fruit with soft sweet flesh and thick yellow skin. A tropical fruit that grows in hanging clusters on a tall plant. The plant that produces this fruit. Something shaped like a banana, or used informally to describe a curved form.
example_sentence: He eats a banana before every morning workout. The market was full of ripe yellow bananas. Bananas are grown widely along the river belt. She blended a banana with milk to make a smoothie.

english_meaning: A small group of musicians who play popular music together. A flat, thin strip or loop of material used as a fastener or for reinforcement. A group of people who share the same interests or beliefs and act together. A specific range of frequencies or wavelengths in radio transmission. To unite or form a group for a specific purpose.
example_sentence: The local band played a fantastic set at the downtown club. She tied her hair back with a colorful rubber band. A small band of rebels attempted to overthrow the government. They decided to band together to protect their neighborhood from crime.

english_meaning: A person who commits crimes, usually by robbing people or taking property by force. Often associated with organized gangs or outlaws operating in remote areas.
example_sentence: The bandit stole gold from the travelers. A group of bandits ambushed the village at night. He was captured for being a notorious bandit. The police tracked the bandits through the forest.

english_meaning: A sudden loud sharp noise, such as that of an explosion. To strike or hit something hard, producing a loud noise. To shut a door or other object noisily and with force. Suddenly, abruptly, or exactly.
example_sentence: We heard a loud bang from the kitchen. He banged the door shut in anger. The child banged his head against the table. The fireworks went off with a huge bang. She arrived bang on time for the meeting.

english_meaning: To send someone away or remove something. To make something disappear completely. To forbid something from existing in a place or situation. To forcefully separate someone from a group. To force a person to leave a place as a punishment or to drive away thoughts, feelings or things completely.
example_sentence: The king decided to banish the corrupt officials from the kingdom. She tried to banish negative thoughts before the exam. Cold water helped him banish the sleepiness from his eyes. The community banished the habit of littering through awareness campaigns.

english_meaning: Expulsion from a place or society. The act of forcing someone to leave a place, often as a punishment, and prohibiting their return for a period of time or permanently. It can also imply exile from a community or country.
example_sentence: The king ordered the banishment of the traitor from the kingdom. 2. After repeated offenses, she faced banishment from the club. 3. His writings led to his banishment during the regime. 4. Banishment from her hometown left her feeling isolated and alone.

english_meaning: The railing on the side of stairs for support. The handrail and supporting structure along a staircase that people hold while going up or down for balance and safety. It usually includes both the rail and the vertical posts. Sometimes used to refer only to the handrail or sometimes the whole stair railing system.
example_sentence: She held the banister while walking down the stairs. The wooden banister was polished and shiny. The child slid his hand along the banister as he climbed up. The old house had a broken banister that needed repair.

english_meaning: To rely on or depend on someone or something. To trust that someone will do what they say or that something will happen as expected. It implies confidence in the reliability or support of a person, plan, or situation.
example_sentence: I’m banking on you to finish this project. She banked on her experience to get the job. Don’t bank on it happening tomorrow. We can bank on him for advice

english_meaning: To tilt or lean an aircraft or boat to one side, usually during a turn. To leave a place, withdraw from an activity, or back out of an arrangement
example_sentence: The pilot banked out to avoid the mountain. The plane banked out smoothly. The car banked out around the corner. They banked out of the project at the last minute. He decided to bank out of the meeting.

english_meaning: To overflow beyond the edge or limit. To exceed a limit or boundary, not only physically but in behavior, rules, or capacity. To pile up or rise gradually until it spills over. To lose balance or stability due to excess.
example_sentence: After heavy rain, the river began to bank over into nearby fields. The tank will bank over if it is filled too much. His anger seemed to bank over during the argument. Emotions banked over when the results were announced. The meeting banked over its scheduled time. Work pressure banked over after weeks of overtime.

english_meaning: To pile up, heap, or build up something together, often in a protective or supportive way (materials, fuel, snow). To increase the amount of something gradually or to fortify. Commonly used for fires, snow, earth, or resources.
example_sentence: They banked up the sandbags before the storm. She banked up the fire to keep warm. The snow was banked up along the road. Farmers bank up soil around crops

english_meaning: To entertain with a feast. A large formal meal or feast for many people, usually to celebrate an event. A grand and formal meal where many guests are invited. It is usually arranged to celebrate weddings, achievements, ceremonies, or official events. Banquets often include multiple courses of food and organized seating.
example_sentence: The wedding banquet was held at a five-star hotel. They invited all the guests to a grand banquet after the ceremony. The king hosted a banquet for foreign diplomats. After winning the award, she attended a celebratory banquet. The company banqueted its employees after completing the project.

english_meaning: To perform the religious ceremony of baptism on a person, typically involving water as a symbol of purification and admission into the Christian faith. To formally name or admit someone into a particular group or belief system through a ceremonial act. Used figuratively to describe an initial, often challenging, introduction to a new experience. To give someone a name or title through a formal or symbolic act.
example_sentence: The priest baptized the infant in front of the entire congregation.  She was baptized at a small church in her hometown as a child.  The new recruits were jokingly said to have been baptized by their first difficult mission.  His grandparents baptized him according to their family's traditions.  The ship was baptized with a bottle of champagne during its launch ceremony.

english_meaning: A sharp projection near the end of an arrow, fishhook, or similar object, angled to prevent easy removal. A deliberately hurtful remark or pointed criticism. To provide with a barb or sharp point.
example_sentence: The fishhook had a sharp barb to hold the fish. Her speech contained several barbs aimed at the minister. The arrow's barb made it difficult to remove. He responded to the criticism with a clever barb of his own. The wire was barbed to keep intruders away.

english_meaning: A member of a people regarded as primitive, uncivilized, or savage. A cruel and violent person. An uncultured or rude individual. Relating to such a people or behavior.
example_sentence: The city was destroyed by invading barbarians. Only a barbarian would treat animals so cruelly. He behaved like a barbarian at the dinner table. Ancient Rome often fought against barbarian tribes. Such barbarian acts have no place in civilized society.

english_meaning: Cruel and violent behavior. Extreme cruelty, savageness, or inhuman behavior. It refers to actions that show a lack of compassion, mercy, or civilization.
example_sentence: The soldiers were shocked by the barbarity of the attack. History is full of stories about the barbarity of ancient wars. The victims suffered great pain because of such barbarity. Acts of barbarity against innocent people must never be tolerated.

english_meaning: A meal or gathering where food is cooked outdoors on a rack over an open fire or hot coals. A portable or stationary apparatus used for cooking food, typically meat, outdoors. A method of cooking meat slowly over low heat with wood smoke or indirect heat, often involving a flavorful sauce. To cook food over an open fire or on a grill, especially outdoors. A social event or party characterized by the preparation and consumption of grilled food. Meat that has been grilled or smoked in this manner.
example_sentence: We decided to host a backyard barbecue to celebrate the beginning of summer. He cleaned the barbecue thoroughly before putting the steaks on the grill. The restaurant is famous for its slow-cooked Texas-style barbecue brisket. We plan to barbecue some chicken and corn on the cob this weekend.

english_meaning: A series of outdoor social gatherings or parties where food is grilled, typically occurring during the summer season. english_meaning: To be tired, annoyed, or frustrated with something or someone.
example_sentence: I’m fed up with this weather. She’s fed up with her noisy neighbors. He was fed up with waiting. They’re fed up with the system.

english_meaning: To serve or support a worthy purpose, principle, or aim that benefits others. To be engaged in an effort that is morally right or socially beneficial. To justify an action because it supports a noble objective.
synonyms: ["Serve a noble purpose","Support a worthy aim","Advance a good cause","Champion a principle"]
antonyms: ["Serve a bad cause","Pursue an unworthy aim","Harm others"]
example_sentence: Working to educate poor children is to be in a good cause. He gave up his weekends because he knew he was in a good cause. She felt proud to be in a good cause that helped the elderly. Volunteers joined the project, knowing they were in a good cause.

english_meaning: To be in a state of irritable, sulky, or petty bad temper, often over something trivial. To be sulking or annoyed in a way others find childish.
synonyms: ["Be sulky","Be huffy","Be in a mood","Be peeved","Be irritated","Be piqued","Be cross"]
example_sentence: She has been in a snit ever since her sister borrowed her sweater without asking. Do not be in a snit just because you lost the game. He was in a snit all afternoon after the meeting got postponed. My brother is in a snit because no one remembered his birthday.

english_meaning: To like, enjoy, or be very interested in something or someone.
example_sentence: She’s really into music. I’m into learning new languages. He’s into fitness and health. They’re into watching classic movies.

english_meaning: To be very different and unable to mix or get along. To have personalities or ideas that cannot combine. Used to describe two things or people who don't match at all. To be incompatible with each other. Never able to work or exist together peacefully.
example_sentence: The two brothers are like oil and water; they never agree. Their opinions are like oil and water. She and her sister-in-law are like oil and water. Our styles of working are like oil and water.

english_meaning: To be given someone’s name in their honor. To receive the same name as another person, place, or thing in their honor.
example_sentence: He was named after his grandfather. The city was named after a king. My son is named after my father. This award is named after a great scientist.

english_meaning: To depart, leave, or go away. To leave. To start going, running, etc.
example_sentence:
He was anxious to be off. His boss ordered him to be off. I must be off if I want to make the next bus.
And the runners are off.

english_meaning: To be wrong or mistaken about something. To have an incorrect understanding, assumption, or judgment about something. It is commonly used when someone’s opinion, guess, or statement does not match reality.
example_sentence: Your assumption about the project is completely off base. I thought he was angry, but I was off base. Her analysis of the situation turned out to be off base. If you think the exam will be easy, you are off base.

english_meaning: To be much better, higher, stronger, or more impressive than expected or than anything measured before. Used when something or someone performs exceptionally well or is extremely intense (in a positive or negative way).
example_sentence: Her confidence level was off the charts during the presentation. The team’s performance was off the charts, they broke every record!. The movie’s popularity is off the charts this year. His energy and enthusiasm were absolutely off the charts.

english_meaning: To be involved in dishonest or illegal activity, especially to get money. To cheat, especially by handling money dishonestly at work. To be secretly making money in a wrong or unfair way.
antonyms: ["Be honest","Be truthful","Play fair","Act lawfully","Be trustworthy","Be upright"]
example_sentence: The manager suspected that one of the clerks was on the fiddle. He lost his job after it turned out he was on the fiddle. Nobody knew for years that she had been on the fiddle. If staff are on the fiddle, the accounts will show it.

english_meaning: To be the person that an action is directed at, especially an unpleasant one. To be the person who experiences something, often something unpleasant. to be the one who receives the effect of an action, treatment, criticism, blame, violence or punishment rather than causing it. It is often used when the experience is negative or unwanted, but it can also be neutral or positive depending on context.
example_sentence: She found herself on the receiving end of a great deal of criticism. He was on the receiving end of harsh criticism from his manager. Villages near the border are often on the receiving end of violence. As a junior officer, she was frequently on the receiving end of blame. The team was on the receiving end of unexpected praise after the project.

english_meaning: To like or be attracted to someone or something.
example_sentence: She was taken with his charm. I was taken with the city’s beauty. He’s taken with her kindness. They were taken with the new idea.

english_meaning: To be the person or thing responsible for something bad. To be at fault for a problem or failure. To deserve criticism for a wrong that has occurred.
synonyms: ["Be responsible","Be at fault","Be guilty","Be culpable","Be answerable"]
example_sentence: Nobody is to blame for the accident. The heavy rain was to blame for the delay. If the project fails, we are all to blame. He admitted that he alone was to blame.

english_meaning: To be awake, active, or out of bed, sometimes also means that something is happening or has ended (depending on context).
example_sentence: She’s been up since dawn. What’s up with you today? I was up all night studying. The prices are up again.

english_meaning: Located beside or near a beach. Situated close to the sea or shore. Relating to an area along the seashore. Used to describe places, properties, or activities found near a beach.
example_sentence: We stayed at a beautiful beachside resort during our holiday. They enjoyed dinner at a small beachside café. The beachside view from our room was breathtaking. Beachside properties are usually expensive. The festival was held at a beachside venue.

english_meaning: A lipped cylindrical glass container used in a laboratory for mixing, heating, and stirring liquids. A large drinking vessel with a wide mouth, often used in historical contexts or for children. A traditional open cup or goblet that does not have a handle. A container used as a unit of measurement in chemical experiments. A specialized vessel used in biology for culturing or observing small specimens in liquid.
example_sentence: The chemist carefully poured the acidic solution into a glass beaker. The toddler struggled to hold the heavy plastic beaker with both hands. During the excavation, archaeologists discovered a bronze age drinking beaker. Please ensure the beaker is cleaned and dried before the next titration.

english_meaning: A seed or pod produced by certain leguminous plants, often used as food. Any of various other seeds that resemble a bean, such as a coffee bean or cocoa bean. A small amount or a thing of little value, often used in negative constructions. Slang term for the head of a person. A unit of data or an object in certain computer programming contexts.
example_sentence: She decided to plant a row of green beans in her backyard garden. The aroma of freshly roasted coffee beans filled the entire cafe. He doesn't know a bean about how a car engine actually functions. The pitcher accidentally hit the batter right on the bean with a fast pitch.

english_meaning: To continue feeling anger or resentment toward someone because of a past wrong; to refuse to forgive someone and keep negative feelings for a long time. A person who bears a grudge does not forget a bad experience. Even after time passes, they still feel upset and may avoid or dislike the person who caused the hurt. It often prevents forgiveness and peace of mind.
example_sentence: He still bears a grudge against his friend for not helping him. She does not bear a grudge and quickly forgives people. Don’t bear a grudge, try to move on with your life. They bear a grudge because of what happened many years ago.

english_meaning: To apply pressure, force, or effort toward something.
example_sentence: The students bore down on their studies before the final exams. The wind bore down on the small fishing boats in the sea. She bore down and managed to finish the marathon despite the pain. During labor, the doctor told her to bear down and push.

english_meaning: To move toward something or someone with force or determination, or to apply strong pressure or effort.
example_sentence: The army bore down on the enemy’s position. She bore down on her studies before the exam. The storm bore down on the village. He bore down on me with anger.

english_meaning: To produce a successful or desired result. To show positive outcomes after effort or hard work. Literally, it means “to produce fruit,” but figuratively it means “to achieve results.”
example_sentence: After years of hard work, their business finally bore fruit. The government’s education reforms are beginning to bear fruit. His continuous training and patience bore fruit when he won the gold medal. Her kindness and generosity will surely bear fruit someday.

english_meaning: It means to remember a piece of information when making a decision or thinking about a matter. It urges someone to consider or note a specific fact. It means to keep something in one's consciousness or thoughts. It is a polite way to remind someone of an important detail before they act.
synonyms: ["Remember","Keep In Mind","Consider","Note","Take Into Account","Be Mindful Of","Heed","Be Aware Of","Acknowledge","Retain","Take Note Of"]
antonyms: ["Forget","Ignore","Disregard","Overlook","Neglect","Pay No Attention To","Dismiss","Omit","Leave Out","Turn A Blind Eye"]
example_sentence: You must bear in mind that the deadline for the project is approaching rapidly. Bear in mind that the weather can change unexpectedly in the mountains. We need to bear in mind the cost of the materials before we finalize the budget. Bear in mind she has only been working here for a week and is still learning.

english_meaning: To relate to or influence something, often used when something affects or has relevance to a situation, issue, or discussion.
example_sentence: His research bears on climate change. The facts bear on our decision. The question bears on behavior. The law bears on the issue.

english_meaning: To confirm or support, used when evidence or facts prove something to be true.
example_sentence: His story was borne out by witnesses. The data bear out our hypothesis. Experience bears out his claims. The facts bore out the theory.

english_meaning: To suffer the worst part of something unpleasant. To endure the main force or impact of an attack, blow, or difficulty. To carry the heaviest share of a burden.
example_sentence: Coastal villages bore the brunt of the storm. She bore the brunt of the criticism after the failure. Junior staff often bear the brunt of budget cuts. The old wall bore the brunt of the explosion.

english_meaning: To stay strong in difficulty, used when someone remains positive or endures hardship courageously.
example_sentence: She bore up well after her loss. You must bear up under pressure. The team bore up despite defeat. He bore up through pain.

english_meaning: To endure hardship or stress. To remain strong and unbroken while under strain or criticism.
example_sentence: He bore up under criticism. The structure bore up under weight. She bore up under stress. They bore up under pressure.

english_meaning: To be patient or tolerant, used when asking someone to wait or show understanding.
example_sentence: Please bear with me for a moment. He bore with his rude friend. If you bear with us, we’ll finish soon. She can’t bear with his attitude.

english_meaning: The hair that grows on the chin, cheeks, and jaw of a man’s face. A symbol of maturity, manhood, or style in many cultures.
example_sentence: He trimmed his beard to look neat and tidy. A long beard is considered a sign of wisdom in many cultures. He decided to shave off his beard before the interview. The beard made him look older and more mature.

english_meaning: Expecting the price of stocks, currencies, commodities, or other assets to decrease. Having a pessimistic opinion about future business or economic conditions. Showing a lack of confidence in growth or success. Indicating downward market movement or declining value. Describing investors who believe selling is better than buying because prices are likely to fall. Having a negative outlook toward a company, industry, economy, or investment.
example_sentence: Many investors became bearish after the company reported weak earnings. The analyst remains bearish about the stock market this year. Rising inflation has created a bearish outlook for the economy. Traders adopted a bearish strategy because they expected prices to decline.

english_meaning: A wild animal that hunts and kills other animals for food. A predatory creature that survives by preying on weaker animals. Any carnivorous beast known for hunting, such as lions, tigers, or wolves. A fierce animal that lives by capturing and eating other creatures.
example_sentence: The lion is a fearsome beast of prey that dominates the African savanna. Farmers protect their livestock from beasts of prey at night. Wolves are cunning beasts of prey that hunt in packs. The forest is home to many beasts of prey.

english_meaning: Animals, especially large or dangerous four-footed ones. Inhumanly cruel, violent, or unpleasant people.
example_sentence: The forest is full of wild beasts. The story was about mythical beasts and heroes. His captors were cruel beasts. They treated their prisoners like beasts.

english_meaning: To beat a dead horse means to waste time and effort trying to do something that has already been decided, completed, or failed beyond recovery. It describes continuing to debate an issue after a conclusion or agreement has already been reached. It signifies bringing up an old topic repeatedly when no further progress can be made.
synonyms: ["Waste Effort","Labor In Vain","Flog A Dead Horse","Repeat Futilely","Belabor The Point","Waste Time","Overdiscuss","Drag Out An Issue","Pursue Lost Causes"]
antonyms: ["Make Progress","Drop The Subject","Move On","Advance","Let Go","Accept The Outcome","Achieve Results"]
example_sentence: There is no need to beat a dead horse when the decision is already finalized. He kept trying to persuade the committee, but he was just beating a dead horse. Discussing yesterday arguments is simply beating a dead horse at this point. Stop beating a dead horse and let us move on to the next topic.

english_meaning: To avoid talking directly about the main point. To speak indirectly or evasively, usually to delay or avoid giving a clear answer.
synonyms: ["Equivocate","Prevaricate","Dodge the issue","Evade","Hem and haw","Go around in circles"]
antonyms: ["Be direct","Speak frankly","Come to the point","Address directly","Speak plainly"]
example_sentence: Instead of beating about the bush, please tell me exactly what happened. The manager kept beating about the bush when we asked about our bonuses. Yesterday I heard of speech of politician he was only beating about the bush. Please don't beat about the bush, come to the point.

english_meaning: To avoid talking about the main point. To speak indirectly or vaguely instead of being straightforward. To delay coming to the real issue.
example_sentence: Stop beating around the bush and answer directly. The manager kept beating around the bush instead of explaining the real problem. If you keep beating around the bush, we’ll never solve this issue. He was beating around the bush because he didn’t want to hurt her feelings.

english_meaning: To beat someone very badly so that the body is covered with bruises. To physically assault someone with great force, causing severe injuries and dark bruises on the skin.
example_sentence: The thieves beat him black and blue before running away. He was beaten black and blue during the street fight. The report said the prisoner was beaten black and blue. She was afraid he would beat her black and blue if she spoke out.

english_meaning: To strike or fall with force, or to make someone accept a lower price or position. (Weather-related: When rain or sunlight falls very strongly).
example_sentence: The sun beat down on the desert. The rain beat down on the roof. The police beat down the door. The sun was beating down all day. He beat the seller down to a fair price. Heavy rain beat down on the rooftops during the storm.

english_meaning: To defeat or extinguish. To overcome, put out fire, or form metal by hammering
example_sentence: She beat out five applicants. They beat out the flames. The blacksmith beat out iron. He beat out his rival.

english_meaning: To finish a task before a set time limit expires. To succeed in doing something within the available time. To work quickly in order to avoid running out of time. To complete an action just before the deadline is reached.
synonyms: ["Meet the deadline","Finish in time","Race against time","Make it on time","Beat the deadline"]
antonyms: ["Run out of time","Miss the deadline","Be late","Fall behind","Overrun"]
example_sentence: The team worked all night to beat the clock. She managed to beat the clock and submit her application. Builders are trying to beat the clock before the rainy season. He beat the clock by finishing the exam with two minutes to spare.

english_meaning: To succeed despite a very low chance of success or difficult conditions. To overcome extreme challenges. To defy expectations. To win against strong competition. To survive or succeed against probability.
synonyms: ["Overcome difficulties","Defy the odds","Succeed against all odds","Triumph","Prevail"]
example_sentence: She beat the odds and recovered from a serious illness. Despite financial problems, he beat the odds and built a successful business. The team beat the odds and won the championship. He came from a poor background but beat the odds to become a doctor.

english_meaning: To attack violently. To physically assault or severely criticize. To injure someone by hitting.
example_sentence: The gang beat him up. His car looks beat up. The boxer beat up his opponent. She felt beat up after the trip.

english_meaning: An informal way of saying that you do not know the answer to something. Used to express complete puzzlement about a question or situation. A casual admission that something is beyond your understanding. Said when you cannot explain why something has happened.
synonyms: ["I don't know","No idea","Search me","Who knows","I'm clueless","Your guess is as good as mine"]
antonyms: ["I know","I understand","I'm certain","That's clear to me","Obviously"]
example_sentence: How did he pass the test without studying? Beats me. Beats me why she left the job so suddenly. When I asked about the missing keys, he just said, Beats me. Beats me how they finished the work so quickly.

english_meaning: A man who is romantically involved with a woman or who admires her. A man who accompanies a woman to social events or formal occasions. A man known for his elegant appearance and stylish clothing.
example_sentence: Emily's beau planned a romantic dinner for their anniversary. Everyone complimented her beau on his polite manners. The young beau waited patiently outside the theatre. His reputation as a fashionable beau spread throughout the town.

english_meaning: Someone or something that is extremely attractive, pleasing to the eyes, or delightful in appearance, often used in a poetic or literary sense.
example_sentence: The beauteous landscape took everyone’s breath away. She wore a beauteous dress that sparkled in the sunlight. The poet described the moon as beauteous and calm. Visitors admired the beauteous architecture of the old palace.

word: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder
english_meaning: Everyone sees beauty in their own way. Different people see things differently based on personal taste or opinion.
example_sentence: She may not be a model, but to him, she’s the most beautiful woman, beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Some people love modern art, others don’t; beauty is in the eye of the beholder. He admires old buildings, while others call them ugly, beauty is in the eye of the beholder. To a mother, her child is always beautiful, proving that beauty is in the eye of the beholder.

english_meaning: A gesture or signal of command, chiefly used in the phrase at someone's beck and call. A small stream or brook, especially in northern England. Historically, a nod or motion used to summon someone.
example_sentence: He expected his assistants to be at his beck and call. I cannot remain at your beck and call all weekend. A narrow beck flowed behind the cottage. Wildflowers grew along the banks of the beck. At the king's beck, the servant stepped forward.

english_meaning: To make a gesture with the hand or head to signal someone to come or follow. Also used figuratively to mean to attract or invite someone toward something.
example_sentence: She beckoned him to come closer with a wave of her hand. The bright lights of the city beckoned the young man from his village. He beckoned to the waiter for another round of drinks. Adventure beckoned her to leave her comfortable life behind.

english_meaning: An easy, comfortable, and pleasant situation in life. Without problems or difficulties. A smooth and pleasant life or situation.
example_sentence: Life is not a bed of roses; you have to struggle to succeed. He thought marriage would be a bed of roses, but it takes effort and understanding. Being a leader is not a bed of roses; it comes with many responsibilities. Her journey to success was not a bed of roses; she faced many challenges.

english_meaning: A small flat blood-sucking insect that lives in beds, furniture, and cracks. A household pest whose bite causes itching and red marks on the skin.
example_sentence: The hotel room was infested with bedbugs. Bedbug bites left red marks on his arms. They washed all the bedding to kill the bedbugs. A bedbug can hide in the smallest crack.

english_meaning: Coverings for a bed, such as sheets and blankets. A layer of straw or similar material for animals to sleep on. The stratification or layering of rocks.
example_sentence: She changed the bedding on all the beds. We need to buy new bedding for the guest room. The horse had fresh bedding in its stall. The geologist noted the bedding of the sedimentary rock.

english_meaning: A flying insect that collects nectar and pollen and often produces honey. An important pollinating insect that lives in a hive or colony. A social gathering where people work together on a shared task.
example_sentence: A bee buzzed softly among the flowers. Bees play a vital role in pollinating crops. He was stung by a bee in the garden. The villagers held a sewing bee last Sunday.

english_meaning: The flesh of a cow, bull, or ox used as food. Informal term for a complaint, grievance, or disagreement. To strengthen or add substance to something. Muscular strength or bulk.
example_sentence: She served roast beef for dinner. He had a beef with his manager. They plan to beef up security at the airport. The wrestler had plenty of beef on his frame.

english_meaning: To make something stronger, larger, more effective, or better by adding more resources, people, effort, or improvements. o increase the strength, size, quality, security, or effectiveness of something. It can refer to adding staff, improving security, increasing funding, enhancing skills, or making a plan more comprehensive.
example_sentence: The company decided to beef up its cybersecurity after several hacking attempts. The school plans to beef up its science program by hiring more teachers. Police officers were sent to beef up security during the festival. You should beef up your resume by adding your recent achievements.

english_meaning: To improve or increase your knowledge, skills, or understanding of a subject by studying, practicing, or reviewing it. To refresh previously learned knowledge. To prepare more thoroughly for an exam, interview, or presentation. To increase expertise in a professional or academic field. To strengthen understanding through additional reading or practice. To become better informed about a topic.
example_sentence: I need to beef up on my grammar before the English exam. She spent the weekend beefing up on her computer programming skills. The new employee is beefing up on company policies before starting work. They decided to beef up on climate science before attending the conference.

english_meaning: Expression of boredom or familiarity with something experienced before. Already experienced something before.
example_sentence: I don’t want to go skydiving again – been there, done that. She rolled her eyes and said, “Been there, done that.” It means you’re not excited because it’s not new. He spoke about his travels saying, “Been there, done that.”

english_meaning: Easy and enjoyable life. Refers to a life of pleasure and comfort without troubles, often suggesting things are not always easy in reality
example_sentence: Life is not all beer and skittles; you must work hard. He thought moving abroad would be beer and skittles, but it was challenging. Success isn’t beer and skittles; it requires effort. Retirement isn’t always beer and skittles if health issues arise.

english_meaning: An insect with hard wing cases covering its back, belonging to a very large group of insects. A heavy wooden hammer used for driving in stakes or crushing. To move or hurry along quickly, especially in a busy manner.
example_sentence: A shiny black beetle crawled across the path. Beetles can damage stored grain very quickly. He crushed the stones with a heavy beetle. She beetled off to catch the last bus.

english_meaning: A round, dark red root vegetable with an earthy sweet taste. A vegetable rich in iron, vitamins, and natural antioxidants. A root often eaten boiled, roasted, pickled, or juiced. A plant whose leaves and roots are both edible and nutritious. A vegetable commonly used to add color and sweetness to salads and dishes.
example_sentence: Beetroot juice is very good for boosting hemoglobin levels. She added slices of beetroot to her salad. Roasted beetroot has a naturally sweet flavor. The doctor advised him to eat beetroot for his low blood count.

english_meaning: To happen to someone, especially something unpleasant. To take place or occur as an event. To come upon as a fate or destiny. To happen by chance to a person or place. To occur, especially in a fateful or unfortunate way.
example_sentence: May no harm befall you on your journey. A great tragedy befell the family. Whatever befalls, we will stand together. Misfortune befell him after he lost his job.

english_meaning: To be suitable or appropriate for someone or something. To be in keeping with a particular standard or occasion. To match what is expected or proper. To suit a person's status or situation. To be fitting or worthy of.
example_sentence: Such rude behavior does not befit a gentleman. She wore a dress that befitted the occasion. His humble attitude befits a true leader. The grand ceremony befitted the king's coronation.

english_meaning: Suitable, appropriate, or right for a particular person, occasion, or situation. Being in keeping with what is proper or expected. Fitting the circumstances in a graceful or dignified way. Worthy of or matching the character of someone or something.
example_sentence: She wore a dress befitting the grand occasion. He gave a speech befitting a true leader. The hotel offered service befitting royalty. They received a welcome befitting honored guests.

english_meaning: Done, prepared, or known prior to a specific event or time. In advance or ahead of time. Before something else takes place.
example_sentence: You should buy your tickets beforehand to avoid long queues. She prepared her speech beforehand so she would feel confident. Please let us know beforehand if you cannot attend the meeting. He had checked the weather forecast beforehand.

english_meaning: Unable to think clearly; confused. Made muddled or puzzled by something difficult. Mentally dulled, sometimes by tiredness or drink. In a state of bewilderment about what is happening. Confused so that decisions become hard to make.
example_sentence: He looked befuddled by the complicated instructions. She was befuddled after working two night shifts. The old man seemed befuddled by the new machines. Their contradictory answers left me completely befuddled.

english_meaning: To bring into existence (used metaphorically). To sire offspring (archaic or biblical use). To lead to a result or consequence. To create or induce an effect. Originally refers to fathering children but is also used metaphorically to mean producing a result, effect, or consequence. It often conveys a chain reaction, where one thing causes another.
example_sentence: Violence begets more violence. Hard work begets success. Pride can beget arrogance. The king begot many children. Laziness begets failure. The king begot many heirs.

english_meaning: To father or produce offspring, to cause or bring about. An archaic form of “begets,” typically found in older English texts like the King James Bible. It means to generate, create, or produce something, especially offspring, but it can also mean causing a particular effect or result.
example_sentence: Abraham begetteth Isaac, and Isaac begetteth Jacob. Hatred begetteth more hatred among enemies. The king begetteth many heirs to the throne. Laziness begetteth poverty in the long run.

english_meaning: People who are in need must accept whatever is offered to them. Those without options should not be picky. A reminder to be grateful for what one receives. Used to advise someone to accept help even if it is not ideal. Poor circumstances leave little room for choice.
synonyms: ["Accept what you get","Be grateful","No room to choose","Take what's offered","Settle for less"]
example_sentence: The shirt isn't my favorite color, but beggars can't be choosers. He accepted the small job because beggars can't be choosers. She wanted a bigger room, but beggars can't be choosers. When you have no money, beggars can't be choosers.

english_meaning: A feast made from humble, cheap, or donated food. An ironic description of a meal that is plentiful but lacks luxury. A gathering where people with little share whatever is available. Figuratively, a collection of poor choices or meager benefits presented as something generous. Also the title of a 1968 album by the Rolling Stones.
synonyms: ["Humble feast","Poor man’s feast","Shared meal","Meager offering","Makeshift banquet"]
example_sentence: The neighbors turned donated vegetables into a beggars’ banquet. The offer was a beggars’ banquet of small discounts and hidden fees. Everyone brought one simple dish to the beggars’ banquet. He found an old copy of Beggars Banquet in the record shop.

english_meaning: To start something once more after stopping. To restart or resume from the beginning.
example_sentence: After the interruption, the speaker had to begin again. Let's begin again from where we left off. She erased the drawing and began again. The teacher asked us to begin again from the top.

english_meaning: To start in a particular role, form, or capacity. To have a specified beginning or origin.
example_sentence: He began as a clerk and rose to become a manager. She began as a volunteer at the hospital. The company began as a small family business. He began as a poet before writing novels.

english_meaning: To start at a specific place, time, or point. To have a starting location or moment.
example_sentence: The lecture will begin at nine o'clock. Charity begins at home. The race begins at the school gate. Our tour begins at the museum entrance.

english_meaning: To start by doing a particular action. To take a specific action as the first step.
example_sentence: Let us begin by introducing ourselves. He began by thanking the audience. She began by explaining the rules. I will begin by summarizing the main points.

english_meaning: To start from a particular point, place, or time. To have origin in a specified source.
example_sentence: The story begins from his childhood days. Let us begin from page ten. Their friendship began from college. Counting begins from one.

english_meaning: To start work on a particular task or project. To commence something on a specific day or subject.
example_sentence: He began on his new novel last month. The workers began on the new road today. She began on her homework immediately. They begin on the project next week.

english_meaning: To start something completely from the beginning again, especially after a mistake. To redo from scratch.
example_sentence: The mistake was too big; he had to begin over. She decided to begin over with a fresh page. If it fails, we will begin over. He wanted to begin over and correct his errors.

english_meaning: To start something with a particular element or point. To have as the first part or step. To use as an initial item.
example_sentence: Let's begin with a short prayer. The book begins with an interesting quotation. We shall begin with chapter one. Every good speech begins with a strong opening line.

english_meaning: The past participle of “beget,” which means to father or produce a child, or more broadly to cause something to exist. It often appears in religious, literary, or formal contexts. Example: “Only begotten son” refers to a child uniquely born from a parent. Produced or brought into existence; generated.
example_sentence: He is the only begotten son of his parents. From these efforts, new opportunities were begotten. The poem speaks of the begotten love between two souls. In theology, Jesus is referred to as the begotten Son of God.

english_meaning: To charm or enchant someone, often in a deceptive way. To help time pass pleasantly.
example_sentence: He beguiled the audience with his stories. She was beguiled by his charm and good looks. To beguile the time, they played cards. The salesman tried to beguile the customers into buying faulty products.

english_meaning: As a representative of someone or in the interests of a person, group, or principle.
example_sentence: She spoke on behalf of all the employees. I am writing to you on behalf of my client. He accepted the award on behalf of his team. Donations were collected on behalf of the charity.

english_meaning: The way in which a person or animal acts in response to a particular situation. The manner of conducting oneself. The actions or reactions of something under specified conditions. The way in which something functions or operates.
example_sentence: His behavior in class has improved significantly. Animal behavior is studied in zoology. The teacher praised her good behavior. Chemical behavior changes with temperature.

english_meaning: Related to the way someone acts or behaves. Concerning or describing patterns, tendencies, or characteristics of a person's actions, reactions, or conduct. Often used in psychology, education, or organizational studies to describe observable actions.
example_sentence: The teacher focused on the students’ behavioural changes after the new program. Behavioural therapy can help patients manage anxiety. Companies analyze behavioural patterns to improve customer experience. His behavioural issues at work were addressed by the HR department.

english_meaning: To cut off someone's head. To execute a person by removing the head. To kill by decapitation. To remove the head of an animal. Figuratively, to remove the leader or chief of a group or organization. To cut off the head of a person or animal, usually as a form of execution, punishment, murder, or in violent situations.
synonyms: ["Decapitate","Execute","Kill","Slay","Sever the head","Chop off the head","Put to death","Remove the head"]
example_sentence: In ancient times, some rulers ordered criminals to behead prisoners as a form of punishment. The story describes a knight who was ordered to behead a dangerous enemy. The documentary explains how beheading was used as a method of execution in certain historical periods. The company decided to behead the leadership team by removing several top executives. This is a figurative use of the word.

english_meaning: A command, request, or order given by someone who has authority. Something done because a person with influence, power, or respect asked or ordered it. It often shows that the action happened because someone important wanted it.
example_sentence: The committee acted at the chairman's behest. She donated the books at her teacher's behest. The investigation started at the minister's behest. He traveled abroad at his company's behest.

english_meaning: In private, secretly, or away from the public eye. When something happens without others knowing or without public discussion. Often used for private meetings, decisions, or personal matters.
antonyms: ["In public","Openly","Publicly","In the open","Out in the open"]
