example_sentence: The peace talks were held behind closed doors to avoid media pressure. Many important business deals are made behind closed doors. The committee discussed the issue behind closed doors before announcing the decision. What happens behind closed doors should stay private.

english_meaning: Old-fashioned; not modern; not aware of current ideas or developments. A person, idea, system, or practice that is outdated and does not keep up with modern trends, technology, or thinking. It often suggests resistance to change or lack of awareness of current developments.
example_sentence: His teaching methods are behind the times and need improvement. That company is behind the times because it still uses outdated technology. Wearing such clothes makes him look behind the times. Some people think printed newspapers are behind the times in the digital age.

english_meaning: Late. Not on time. Delayed.(Used when a person, event, or activity happens later than the expected or scheduled time. It shows delay or lack of punctuality)
example_sentence: The train arrived behind time because of the heavy rain. He reached the office behind time and missed the meeting. Our project is running behind time due to technical issues. She apologized for being behind time for the class.

english_meaning: To see or observe a thing or person, especially a remarkable or impressive one.
example_sentence: Behold the beauty of the sunset! We were lucky to behold such a rare sight. The crowd gathered to behold the queen. The mountains were a magnificent sight to behold.

english_meaning: Owing thanks or having a duty to someone in return for help or a service.
example_sentence: I am beholden to you for your kindness. She didn't want to be beholden to anyone. We are all beholden to those who fought for our freedom. He felt beholden to his mentor for his success.

english_meaning: To discuss or explain something in too much detail or for too long. To attack or beat someone repeatedly. To work at a task with excessive effort. To labour over a point that is already clear.
example_sentence: There is no need to belabor the point; we already understand. The teacher belabored the simple concept for an entire hour. Critics belabored the author for his minor mistakes. He belabored the issue until everyone lost interest. Don't belabor the obvious in your essay.

english_meaning: To explain or discuss something for too long or with unnecessary detail. To criticize someone or something repeatedly. To hit or beat someone or something heavily and repeatedly.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the student not to belabour the same point during the presentation. The newspaper continued to belabour the government's mistakes for several weeks. The blacksmith belaboured the hot metal until it took the desired shape. There is no need to belabour the issue because everyone already understands it.

english_meaning: Coming or happening later than should have been the case.
example_sentence: He sent a belated birthday card. Please accept my belated apologies. The belated train finally arrived. She made a belated attempt to join the conversation.

english_meaning: To release gas noisily from the stomach through the mouth. To expel air or gas from the stomach with a loud sound. To emit or pour out something forcefully, like smoke, fire, or flames. A sudden, often noisy expulsion of gas from the stomach through the mouth.
example_sentence: After drinking soda, he belched loudly. The volcano belched smoke and ash into the sky. He tried to hold it in but ended up belching in public. The factory chimneys belched thick black smoke.

english_meaning: To cause a lot of problems or difficulties for someone. To surround someone in order to attack them.
example_sentence: They were beleaguered by enemy armies. The lack of funds that beleaguers schools. At the same time, the public believed they were beleaguered by crime.

english_meaning: To give a false impression of something. To fail to fulfil or justify a claim or expectation. To contradict or be in conflict with something. To disguise or misrepresent the true nature of a person or thing.
example_sentence: Her calm face belied the anxiety she felt inside. His youthful appearance belies his actual age. The peaceful village belied its violent history. The report belies the official claim of progress. His smile belied his true feelings of sorrow.

english_meaning: An acceptance that something is true or exists. Trust or confidence in someone or something. A religious conviction or faith. A firmly held opinion. Something accepted as true without proof.
example_sentence: He has a strong belief in honesty. Her belief in God gives her strength. It is a common belief that hard work pays off. Beliefs vary widely across cultures.

english_meaning: To make someone or something seem unimportant or of little value. To speak of in a disparaging manner. To undermine or diminish a person's achievements, abilities or worth. To treat with contempt or look down upon.
example_sentence: Don't belittle her efforts; she worked very hard. He always belittles his younger brother's achievements. A good teacher never belittles a student's questions. She felt belittled by her boss's sarcastic comments. We should not belittle the contributions of unsung heroes.

english_meaning: Relating to Belize, its people, culture, or language. A person who is a citizen or native of Belize.
example_sentence: She is a Belizean writer living abroad. We enjoyed several Belizean dishes during our visit. The Belizean guide explained the history of the ruins. Many Belizeans speak more than one language.

english_meaning: A large, hollow, sweet pepper with thick crisp flesh and no heat. A colourful vegetable eaten raw in salads or cooked in dishes. The plant that produces these peppers. A vegetable available in green, red, yellow, and orange varieties.
example_sentence: She stuffed the bell peppers with rice and meat. Red bell peppers are sweeter than green ones. He sliced bell pepper into the pasta sauce. Bell peppers add colour to any salad.

english_meaning: To take on a dangerous or difficult task for the benefit of others. To do something risky that no one else is willing to do. To face a tough challenge on behalf of a group. To attempt a task despite its high risks. To be brave enough to try what others avoid.
synonyms: ["Take the risk","Face the danger","Take initiative","Step up","Brave the challenge","Volunteer"]
example_sentence: Someone must bell the cat and talk to the boss about the low pay. Everyone complained, but no one was willing to bell the cat. She belled the cat by reporting the issue directly. It takes courage to bell the cat in such situations.

english_meaning: A beautiful and charming woman, especially the most admired at a social event. A pretty and popular young lady. A woman known for her elegance and attractiveness. A term used historically for a well-dressed lady of society. Any female considered outstandingly lovely.
example_sentence: She was the belle of the ball in her beautiful gown. Every belle in the town admired the new dress design. The belle smiled gracefully at her guests. The young belle became famous for her charm.

english_meaning: Demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight. Eager or inclined to start arguments or wars. Hostile and combative in attitude. Used to describe people, nations, speeches, or policies that are openly aggressive and ready for conflict rather than peace or compromise.
example_sentence: The bellicose speech of the leader alarmed neighbouring countries. His bellicose attitude made it difficult to negotiate with him. The two nations exchanged bellicose statements through the media. Bellicose policies often lead to long and damaging wars. The bellicose tone of his email surprised his colleagues.

english_meaning: A hostile or warlike attitude or nature. The act of engaging in war or physical conflict. An aggressive disposition that seeks to provoke a fight. The state of being engaged in open hostilities. A combative readiness to confront others aggressively.
example_sentence: The negotiator tried to calm the belligerence of the rebel leaders. Her constant belligerence made it difficult to maintain a peaceful work environment. The nation's sudden belligerence threatened the stability of the entire region. He spoke with a level of belligerence that shocked everyone in the room.

english_meaning: A person, group, or country engaged in war or conflict. Aggressive and ready to fight. Showing hostility, aggression, or a willingness to fight. It can refer to physical fighting, verbal arguments, or an aggressive attitude in general.
example_sentence: The treaty was signed by both belligerents. Each belligerent blamed the other for starting the war. The organization called for talks between the belligerents. Aid was sent to civilians affected by the belligerents. He gave a belligerent reply during the meeting. The belligerent crowd refused to calm down. Her belligerent attitude caused tension in the office.

english_meaning: In a manner that shows a readiness to fight or argue. With a hostile and aggressive attitude. In a warlike or combat-ready fashion. In a way that aggressively challenges others.
example_sentence: The drunk man yelled belligerently at the bartender. She crossed her arms and stared belligerently at her opponent. The neighboring country belligerently amassed troops along the border. He responded belligerently to the polite request for silence.

english_meaning: To shout or roar in a very loud and deep voice. To make a loud sound like a bull or other large animal. To speak angrily or loudly. A loud, deep roar or shout.
example_sentence: The angry coach bellowed instructions across the field. The bull bellowed loudly from the pasture. The captain bellowed orders during the storm. The wind bellowed through the narrow valley all night.

english_meaning: The soft front part of the human or animal body between the chest and hips where the stomach and other organs are located. It is also used in everyday speech to mean the stomach or the area that holds food after eating. To bulge or swell outward. To become round or swollen outward like a stomach because of air, wind, or pressure.
example_sentence: The child rubbed his belly after eating a big meal. The cat lay on its back and showed its belly. The boat hit the rocks and damaged its belly. The sail began to belly in the strong wind. The baby laughed when his mother tickled his belly.

english_meaning: The small mark or hollow in the center of the abdomen where the umbilical cord was attached before birth. Also called the navel or umbilicus, is the scar left on a person's abdomen after the umbilical cord is cut following birth. It is a natural part of the human body and can be either an "innie" (sunken inward) or an "outie" (protruding outward).
example_sentence: The baby had a small belly button after the umbilical cord healed. She cleaned her belly button carefully during her bath. The doctor examined the area around his belly button. The child laughed when his mother touched his belly button.

english_meaning: A pain in the stomach or abdomen. To complain repeatedly in a whining, irritating manner.
example_sentence: He went home early with a bad bellyache. Too many sweets gave the child a bellyache. Stop bellyaching and start working. They bellyached about the weather all afternoon.

english_meaning: Persistent, irritating complaining or grumbling. The act of complaining about small matters.
example_sentence: I am tired of his constant bellyaching. There was a lot of bellyaching about the new rules. Enough bellyaching; let us solve the problem. Her bellyaching spoiled an otherwise pleasant trip.

english_meaning: To be included as part of a group or collection. To feel or be rightly placed as part of a group of people or things.
example_sentence: She belongs among the best students. These artifacts belong among ancient treasures. He doesn’t belong among dishonest people. Such words don’t belong among polite society.

english_meaning: To be in the proper or suitable place. To show that something or someone fits naturally or appropriately in a particular place, situation, or category.
example_sentence: The cups belong in the cupboard. You belong in this company. That word doesn’t belong in this sentence. Such items belong in a museum. That painting belongs in a museum.

english_meaning: To show possession, relationship, or connection. To be the property of, to be part of or associated with a group, place, or person.
example_sentence: This book belongs to Ali. I feel I belong to this team. Who does this car belong to? The islands belong to the country.

english_meaning: To be classified or placed in a particular category, group, or section.
example_sentence: This law belongs under criminal justice. These files belong under archives. That topic belongs under biology. The data belongs under confidential records.

english_meaning: To be in the right place or to match well with someone or something. To fit emotionally, socially, or logically with another person or thing. To be meant to stay together or exist together. To form a natural pair or set.
example_sentence: This color belongs with that shade perfectly. He really belongs with this team. These books belong with the classics. She feels she belongs with her friends here. These files belong with the documents in the finance folder. This color belongs with the warm tones of the room’s design.

english_meaning: Not up to the usual or expected standard. Of poorer quality than normal. Feeling slightly unwell or lacking energy. Performing worse than average or below the accepted level.
example_sentence: His performance in the final match was well below par. I've been feeling below par since the weather changed. The food at the new restaurant was disappointingly below par. Sales this quarter remained below par despite the advertising campaign.

english_meaning: To cause someone to become confused or uncertain about something. To make someone think deeply but in a way that leads to puzzlement rather than clarity. To distract someone’s attention so they appear lost in thought or confused. To leave someone wondering what is happening or what something means.
example_sentence: The complex instructions bemused the new employees. His strange answer bemused everyone in the meeting. She looked bemused after hearing the unexpected question. The magician’s trick left the audience bemused and curious.

english_meaning: A long seat, typically made of wood or metal, designed for several people to sit on. The position or status of a judge in a court of law, often used to refer to judges collectively. In sports, to remove a player from active participation in a game, often as a penalty or tactical decision. A worktable used by craftsmen, scientists, or technicians for manual tasks.
example_sentence: They sat on a wooden bench overlooking the lake.  The judge has served on the bench for over twenty years.  The coach decided to bench the star player after his poor performance.  The scientist worked at the laboratory bench late into the night.  The park benches were freshly painted for the spring season.

english_meaning: Something that can be measured and used as a standard that other things can be compared with. To judge the quality of something in relation to that of other similar things.
example_sentence: Tests at the age of seven provide a benchmark against which the child's progress at school can be measured. Her outstanding performances set a new benchmark for singers throughout the world. Projects are assessed and benchmarked against the targets. The journal was recently benchmarked against other IT journals.

english_meaning: To lower or move your upper body forward and downward, usually to reach something or show respect.
example_sentence: She bent down to tie her shoes. He bent down to pick up the pen. The old man bent down to greet the child. Please bend down so I can whisper something.

english_meaning: To be determined or resolved to achieve something.
example_sentence: He was bent on success. She’s bent on proving them wrong. They are bent on revenge. He’s bent on completing this task.

english_meaning: To become angry or upset, to get distorted or deformed.
example_sentence: Don’t get bent out of shape over minor issues. The metal rod bent out of shape in the heat. He gets bent out of shape when criticized. The car’s frame bent out of shape after the crash.

english_meaning: To lean forward from the waist, often to pick something up or to show subservience.
example_sentence: He bent over to pick up the fallen coin. She bent over the desk reading the letter. Don’t bend over too much or you’ll hurt your back. The workers bent over their tools.

english_meaning: To make a great effort to help someone, often going beyond what is necessary. To try extremely hard to please or accommodate others.
example_sentence: She bent over backwards to help. The teacher bent over backwards to help the weak students pass the exam. She bent over backwards to make her guests feel comfortable. He always bends over backwards to keep his boss happy. The company bent over backwards to satisfy the customer’s complaint.

english_meaning: To yield or submit to someone’s will or circumstances, to adapt.
example_sentence: He refused to bend to pressure. They bent to the new company rules. She never bends to injustice. The trees bent to the strong wind. The government had to bend to public demand.

english_meaning: In or to a lower position than something Directly under something. At a lower level, rank, or importance. Hidden or covered by something. Not suitable for someone (figurative use).
example_sentence: The keys were beneath the newspaper. The diver explored the world beneath the waves. She felt the ground shake beneath her feet. He wore a shirt beneath his sweater.

english_meaning: Having a good or favorable influence. Producing beneficial effects. (Astrology) Refers to planets believed to bring positive or lucky effects (such as Venus and Jupiter). Kind, helpful, or advantageous in result or nature. Something that brings good results, advantages, or positive influence in a situation, person, or event. In astrology, it is specifically used for planets considered to have positive effects on human life.
example_sentence: The benefic rays of the sun warmed the earth. It was a benefic organization dedicated to helping the poor. His benefic influence was felt by everyone. The new policy had a benefic effect on the economy.

english_meaning: Something that helps, improves, or has a positive effect on a person, situation, or thing. Anything that produces good results, supports growth, improves health, or adds value. It is used when something has a helpful or advantageous impact on someone or something.
example_sentence: Regular exercise is beneficial for heart health. Drinking plenty of water is beneficial in hot weather. Reading books is beneficial for improving vocabulary. The new policy proved beneficial for small businesses.

english_meaning: The quality of being kind, generous, and willing to help others. A genuine desire to do good to others without expecting anything in return. It includes kindness, generosity, compassion, and a helpful attitude toward people in need.
example_sentence: The queen was known for her benevolence. His benevolence was shown through his generous donations. A spirit of benevolence filled the community. She was loved for her benevolence and compassion.

english_meaning: A person who shows kindness, goodwill, and a desire to help others. A benevolent person actively cares about the well being of people and often gives support, money, or time to improve others' lives.
example_sentence: The benevolent teacher stayed after school to help struggling students. A benevolent businessman donated money to build a hospital. She gave a benevolent smile to the orphaned child. The king was remembered as a benevolent ruler who cared for his people.

english_meaning: In a kind and generous way. With goodwill and a desire to help others. In a manner showing warmth and compassion. Charitably and with genuine care for people's welfare.
example_sentence: The old man smiled benevolently at the children. She benevolently offered to pay for his studies. The foundation benevolently supports poor students. He looked benevolently upon their efforts.

english_meaning: Kind and gentle in nature. Not harmful or dangerous. (Medical) Not cancerous. Mild or not severe.
example_sentence: He had a benign smile. The tumor was benign, not cancerous. The climate is benign. Her benign nature made her popular with her students.

english_meaning: Sharply curved or having an angle. Physically not straight or damaged out of shape. Determined or strongly focused on something (informal). Dishonest or corrupt (informal). Natural tendency or inclination.
example_sentence: He had a bent for music from an early age. The tree was bent by the wind. She looked at him with a bent head. He is bent on getting his own way.

english_meaning: To leave property or something valuable to someone through a will after death. To legally pass money, property, or possessions to another person through a will after one's death. It can also mean leaving ideas, traditions, knowledge, or responsibilities for future generations.
example_sentence: The old man decided to bequeath his house to his youngest daughter. She plans to bequeath her valuable books to the university library. The leader hoped to bequeath a legacy of peace to the next generation. In his will, he bequeathed a large sum of money to charity.

english_meaning: Money or property that you ask to be given to a particular person when you die. The money or property belonging to someone that they say that, after their death, they wish to be given to other people. A disposition in a will. The act of giving or leaving something by will. Something that is or may be inherited.
example_sentence: He left a bequest to each of his grandchildren. Her will included small bequests to her family, while most of her fortune went to charity.

english_meaning: To scold, criticize, or speak angrily to someone because of their behavior or mistakes. To strongly and angrily criticize someone. It is used when a person speaks harshly to another person for doing something wrong, careless, or unacceptable. The criticism is usually severe and emotional.
example_sentence: The teacher berated the student for cheating in the exam. She berated her brother for breaking her laptop. The manager berated the workers for arriving late. He was berated by his parents for wasting money.

english_meaning: A soft, round, flat-crowned cap, usually made of woven or felted wool, without a peak or brim. Often worn tilted to one side. Commonly associated with artists, soldiers, and certain national costumes. Used as both fashion wear and as part of military uniforms.
example_sentence: The artist wore a black beret while painting. French soldiers are often seen wearing green berets. She matched her red beret with a white coat. The boy looked smart in his school beret. Berets are part of the official uniform of many army units.

english_meaning: To beg or request earnestly. To ask someone very seriously and emotionally for help, mercy, or something important. It shows deep urgency, humility, or desperation.
example_sentence: She beseeched the doctor to save her child. The villagers beseeched the authorities for clean drinking water. He beseeched his friend to forgive his mistake. The prisoner beseeched the judge for mercy.

english_meaning: A fault or weakness that a person constantly struggles with. A habitual failing that repeatedly troubles someone. A characteristic flaw that keeps recurring in a person or group. The particular temptation to which someone most easily yields.
example_sentence: Procrastination is his besetting sin. Impatience remains her besetting sin as a manager. Waste is the besetting sin of large organisations. He confessed that pride was his besetting sin.

english_meaning: Used for making an extra comment that adds to what you have just said. In addition, also. In addition to somebody, something, apart from somebody, something.
example_sentence: I don't really want to go besides, it's too late now. Discounts on televisions, stereos and much more besides. We have lots of things in common besides music. Besides working as a doctor, he also writes novels in his spare time. I've got no family besides my parents. I’ve got plenty of other things to do besides talking to you. She won't mind if you're late - besides, it's hardly your fault. Do you play any other sports besides basketball?

english_meaning: To surround a place, especially a city or building, with armed forces in order to capture it. It can also mean to crowd around someone with many requests, questions, or problems.
example_sentence: The army besieged the ancient city for several weeks. Reporters besieged the minister with questions after the meeting. The castle was besieged by enemy forces during the war. After the announcement, fans besieged the actor for autographs.

english_meaning: To damage the opinion that people have of somebody, something. To say bad things about someone to influence other people's opinion of them. To make dirty. To damage reputation or honor. To soil or tarnish.
example_sentence: He had deliberately set out to besmirch her reputation. His accusations were false, but they served to besmirch her reputation. His shirt was besmirched with blood. He has accused local people of trying to besmirch his reputation. Inconsiderately besmirched the carpet with their dirty feet.

english_meaning: To deeply absorb or strongly fascinate someone, often so much that they forget other things. To captivate the mind or senses completely. When someone is besotted, they are so interested, pleased, or emotionally involved that they may act without clear judgment. It is often used for love, beauty, or intense interest. Deeply infatuated or completely absorbed.
example_sentence: He was besotted with her smile and forgot everything else. The child was besot by the colorful cartoon on TV. She became besotted with the idea of traveling the world. The audience was besot by the singer’s powerful voice. He looked besot when he talked about her. She had a besot expression on her face.

english_meaning: Made specially to a customer's individual order. Designed or produced for one particular person or purpose. Dealing in specially made goods, such as a bespoke tailor. Past tense of bespeak, meaning to indicate or suggest.
example_sentence: He ordered a bespoke suit for the wedding. The company offers bespoke software for small businesses. She works with a bespoke tailor in the old market. His silence bespoke a deep disappointment.

english_meaning: To enjoy the advantages of two different things at the same time. A situation where you get benefits from two different opportunities without the disadvantages of either. Having two good things together. Enjoying benefits from two sides.
example_sentence: Working part-time gives me the best of both worlds. By working part-time and studying part-time, He lives in the city but has a farmhouse in the countryside, so he enjoys the best of both worlds. This job lets me work from home and travel when I want, truly the best of both worlds. She married a British man and lives in Pakistan; her children enjoy the best of both worlds, Eastern culture and Western lifestyle.

english_meaning: Resembling a beast in nature or behavior. Savage, brutal, or cruel. Lacking human qualities of kindness or compassion. Used to describe acts, behavior, or instincts that are extremely violent, inhumane, or animal-like, especially involving cruelty toward others.
example_sentence: The villagers were shocked by the bestial attack on the travelers. War often brings out the bestial side of human nature. The criminal was punished for his bestial behavior. Such bestial cruelty has no place in a civilized society. The film depicted the bestial conditions of the prisoners.

english_meaning: To grant or confer a title, honor, or privilege. To present a gift or reward. To provide or give something in a respectful or formal way. To endow someone with a quality or ability. To give, present, or confer something as an honor, gift, or right.
example_sentence: The university will bestow an honorary degree on him. The king bestowed a title upon the loyal knight. She bestowed her favor on the young artist. The prize was bestowed upon the winner by the judge.

english_meaning: To risk money on the result of an event or a competition, Risk a sum of money or valued item against someone else’s on the basis of the outcome of an unpredictable event such as a race or game
example_sentence: He bet Rs 50000 on final score of game. She bet me Rs 6000 that I wouldn’t do it. We have got a bet on who’s going to arrive first.

english_meaning: An informal expression meaning to be completely certain about something. Used to emphasise that one is absolutely sure about a fact or outcome. A way of expressing total confidence in a prediction.
synonyms: ["Be certain","Guarantee","Stake my life on","Be absolutely sure"]
example_sentence: You can bet your boots that she will finish the project on time. If it starts raining, you can bet your boots the roads will become crowded. You can bet your boots he knows the answer to that question. They may be late, but you can bet your boots they will eventually arrive.

english_meaning: The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet. A soft, bilabial consonant sound represented by this letter, used in Hebrew, Yiddish, and related Semitic scripts. Sometimes used as a feminine given name in English-speaking countries, typically as a short form of Elizabeth or Bethany.
example_sentence: Beth is the second letter in the Hebrew alphabet and carries a soft b sound.  The scholar explained the pronunciation of beth in ancient Semitic languages.  She introduced herself simply as Beth, short for Elizabeth.  The manuscript used beth as the opening letter of the first verse.  In some transliterations, beth appears as the letter b in English renderings.

english_meaning: To lead astray. To give information about somebody, something to an enemy. To hurt somebody who trusts you, especially by lying to or about them or telling their secrets to other people.
example_sentence: He has been accused of betraying his former socialist ideals. He was accused of betraying his country during the war. Childhood friends of movie stars often betray them by telling their secrets to the supermarket tabloids.

english_meaning: The act of being disloyal or breaking someone’s trust. Revealing secrets to others. Acting against one’s group, country, or friend. Cheating in loyalty or duty. Political or national disloyalty. An action where a person breaks trust, confidence, or loyalty. It often involves deceiving someone who believed in you, such as a friend, partner, or group.
example_sentence: His betrayal of his best friend shocked everyone. She felt deep pain after his betrayal in their relationship. The spy was accused of betrayal of his country. Betrayal of trust can destroy friendships permanently.

english_meaning: It is better to do something late than not do it at all. Late action is preferable to no action. Even delayed effort has value. Encouragement to complete a task despite the delay. A phrase used to accept a late arrival kindly.
example_sentence: You finally started studying, better late than never. She apologized after years, but better late than never. He joined the class late, better late than never. Better late than never, they finally acknowledged the mistake.

english_meaning: The act or process of making something better, especially in terms of improving living conditions, quality of life, or a situation. Improvement in the condition, quality, or status of something or someone. The state of being improved or having moved to a higher or more desirable level. Often used in the context of social, economic, or personal progress.
example_sentence: The charity was founded for the betterment of underprivileged communities across the region.  Education is widely regarded as the key to personal betterment.  The government launched several programs aimed at the betterment of rural infrastructure.  He dedicated his career to the betterment of public health services.  The new policies brought about a clear betterment in working conditions.

english_meaning: Caught between two serious dangers where avoiding one puts you closer to the other. A situation where someone must choose between two difficult or dangerous options. Whichever choice they make, there is a real risk involved. It is similar to being stuck between two threats with no easy escape.
synonyms: ["Dilemma","Predicament","Quandary","Facing a catch-22","On the horns of a dilemma"]
example_sentence: He was between Scylla and Charybdis in that decision. She faced a choice between Scylla and Charybdis. The company is between Scylla and Charybdis financially. Negotiators are often between Scylla and Charybdis, balancing demands from two hostile sides. She was caught between Scylla and Charybdis when deciding whether to accept the risky job offer or stay unemployed.

english_meaning: A drink, especially one other than plain water, that is prepared and consumed for pleasure, nourishment, or social occasions. Any drinkable liquid intended for human consumption, including hot, cold, alcoholic, or non-alcoholic drinks. A term used commercially or formally to refer to any kind of drink product.
example_sentence: The menu offered a wide selection of hot and cold beverages.  She ordered a refreshing beverage to cool down after the long walk.  The café was known for its unusual and exotic beverage combinations.  Alcoholic beverages are not permitted on school premises.  He never drank any beverage with artificial sweeteners.

english_meaning: A large group of people or things. A number of people gathered together, often used for women or girls in traditional usage. A considerable amount or collection of things. A collective noun used for certain birds, especially quail or larks.
example_sentence: A bevy of movie stars arrived at the White House. A bevy of girls waited outside. A bevy of reporters gathered outside the courthouse. She received a bevy of compliments after her speech. A bevy of quail flew across the field. The new policy sparked a bevy of questions from the staff.

english_meaning: To express great sorrow or grief about something, especially through crying, lamenting, or mourning. To complain about or regret something deeply and openly. To mourn or grieve bitterly over a loss, misfortune, or unfortunate situation. To express loud and heartfelt sorrow.
example_sentence: She bewailed the loss of her childhood home after it was demolished.  The poet bewailed the suffering caused by years of conflict in the region.  He bewailed his misfortune loudly, drawing attention from passersby.  The community gathered to bewail the tragic deaths of the young soldiers.  She did not bewail her failure but instead resolved to try again.

english_meaning: To cause to lose one's bearings. To confuse somebody. To throw into a state of mental uncertainty.
example_sentence:
She was totally bewildered by his sudden change of mood.
His complete lack of interest in money bewilders his family.
He was rather bewildered at seeing her there. The change in policy seems to have bewildered many of our customers.

english_meaning: To attract or impress somebody so much that they cannot think in a sensible way. To put a magic spell on somebody. To attract or interest someone a lot so that you have the power to influence them. To put a magic spell on someone or something in order to control him, her, or it.
example_sentence: He was bewitched by her beauty. The painter bewitched the crowd with his latest work. She lost her power to bewitch. She was not moving, as if someone had bewitched her. Mary bewitched him with her smile.

english_meaning: Something too difficult to understand, achieve, or obtain. Out of reach, either physically or mentally.
example_sentence: The concept of quantum physics is beyond my grasp. The advanced scientific theory was beyond his grasp. For many poor families, luxury cars remain beyond their grasp. Peace in the region often seems beyond one’s grasp. Her dream of becoming a world-class singer was not beyond her grasp; she worked hard and achieved it.

english_meaning: To influence someone unfairly. An unfair preference or dislike for someone or something. A tendency to support or oppose a person, group, or idea in an unfair way. It can be conscious or unconscious. Bias can also mean a natural inclination or preference. In technical fields, it may refer to a systematic error in data or judgment.
example_sentence: The judge showed no bias during the trial. Media bias can influence public opinion. Her cultural bias affected her decision. The results were inaccurate due to sampling bias.

english_meaning: Tending to show favor towards or against one group of people or one opinion for personal reasons, making unfair judgements. Inclined to favor one side over another.
example_sentence: He seemed a bit biased against women in my opinion. The newspapers are notably biased. Many parents are biased against popular music. The article was heavily biased against the current regime. Managers are naturally biased towards projects showing a quick return.

english_meaning: Related to the Bible or its teachings. Very great in size or importance. Anything connected with the Bible, its stories, teachings, characters, language, or time period. It can describe religious beliefs, moral principles, historical events mentioned in the Bible, or writing style that resembles the language of the Bible.
example_sentence: The community's links with Syria date back to biblical times. They named their son Isaac after the biblical figure. He quotes Shakespeare as well as Biblical passages. Many of the allusions in the film are biblical. After rain of biblical proportions, the match was cancelled. There were so many insects, it was almost biblical.

english_meaning: A person who compiles bibliographies or studies the history and classification of books. An expert in bibliography. Someone who catalogs and describes books systematically. A scholar who researches book production and publishing history.
example_sentence: The bibliographer compiled a comprehensive list of medieval texts. She works as a bibliographer at the university. Bibliographers help researchers locate sources. The bibliographer's work is invaluable to scholars.

english_meaning: A list of books, articles, or other sources used or referred to in a piece of writing or research. A systematic list of sources such as books, journals, articles, websites, and documents that an author has consulted or cited while preparing a research paper, book, or academic work. It is usually placed at the end of the document and helps readers verify information or explore the topic further.
antonyms: ["Ignorance of sources","Unreferenced work","Plagiarism (in opposite sense of citing sources)","Undocumented writing"]
example_sentence: The research paper included a detailed bibliography at the end. She checked the bibliography to find more books on climate change. A good bibliography helps readers verify the sources used in a study. The professor asked students to prepare a bibliography for their project.

english_meaning: An obsessive-compulsive disorder involving the collecting or hoarding of books. An extreme passion for acquiring and possessing books. A mania or excessive enthusiasm for books. The compulsive desire to own books, often beyond practical need or use.
example_sentence: His bibliomania led him to buy books he never read. Bibliomania can become a serious financial burden. The disease of bibliomania affected his relationships. She struggled with bibliomania and filled every room with books.

english_meaning: A person with an extreme passion for collecting and owning books. Someone obsessed with acquiring books, often beyond practical use. A compulsive book collector. A person suffering from bibliomania, an obsessive-compulsive disorder involving books.
example_sentence: The bibliomaniac owned thousands of rare books. As a bibliomaniac, he couldn't resist buying every book he saw. Her bibliomaniac tendencies filled her house with books. The bibliomaniac's collection was legendary.

english_meaning: Book lover. A person who loves, collects, or has a deep appreciation for books, especially rare or valuable ones.
example_sentence: She is a true bibliophile, spending hours in antique bookstores searching for first editions. The bibliophile proudly displayed his collection of rare manuscripts. As a bibliophile, he always carries a book wherever he goes. Libraries are a paradise for any bibliophile.

english_meaning: A person who has an irrational fear or hatred of books. Someone with an aversion to reading or books. A person who avoids books and reading. Someone suffering from bibliophobia.
example_sentence: As a bibliophobe, he never entered a library. The bibliophobe felt anxious around books. Her bibliophobic tendencies kept her from academia. Being a bibliophobe, he preferred oral traditions.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of books or reading. A person with bibliophobia may avoid books, libraries, or any situation involving reading.
example_sentence: His bibliophobia made school extremely difficult. She had bibliophobia so severe she could not enter a library. Bibliophobia is sometimes linked to bad experiences with education. He overcame his bibliophobia through gradual reading exercises.

english_meaning: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm that bends the elbow. A muscle with two points of origin, most commonly the biceps brachii. The muscle that becomes visible as a bulge when the arm is flexed. A muscle at the back of the thigh also known as the biceps femoris.
example_sentence: He flexed his biceps to show off his training results. The biceps bends the elbow and turns the palm upwards. Lifting weights every week strengthened her biceps. A sudden strain tore the tendon of his biceps.

english_meaning: To argue about petty or trivial matters in an irritable or quarrelsome way. To engage in repeated, minor disputes, often without any serious purpose. Used to describe ongoing, small-scale arguments that occur frequently between people. To exchange irritable or annoyed remarks during a disagreement.
example_sentence: The siblings constantly bickered over whose turn it was to do the dishes.  The couple bickered about minor household chores almost every evening.  Team members often bickered over trivial scheduling issues during meetings.  The children bickered in the back seat for most of the car ride.  Despite their friendship, the two co-workers occasionally bickered about small details.

english_meaning: A situation where people argue repeatedly in a weak, irritating, and pointless way. The arguments are usually over very small issues, not serious problems. Like mice making tiny but constant noises, the people involved create disturbance without achieving anything useful. It often suggests immaturity, lack of cooperation, and wasted time.
example_sentence: The siblings were bickering like mice over who took the last cookie. Instead of solving the issue, the team kept bickering like mice all morning. Neighbors bickering like mice can make apartment living stressful. The meeting failed because managers were bickering like mice about minor details.

english_meaning: To offer a particular amount of money for something, especially at an auction. To make an attempt to obtain, achieve, or do something. To say a greeting or farewell to someone. To command, order, or invite someone to do something. An offer, attempt, or invitation.
example_sentence: He bid two thousand rupees for the antique vase at the auction. The company plans to bid for the new construction contract. She paused at the door to bid her guests goodnight. He made a strong bid for the leadership of his party. Their bid to climb the mountain in winter ended in failure.

english_meaning: To divide or split something into two branches, parts, or directions. To fork into two separate paths or streams. To cause a single thing to separate into two distinct sections. It is commonly used in geography, biology, law, and any context where a single entity divides into two.
example_sentence: The road bifurcates near the old bridge. The committee decided to bifurcate the project into two phases. The river bifurcates into two streams further north. The court ordered to bifurcate the trial. The province was bifurcated for better administration.

english_meaning: An important or powerful person in an organization. An informal expression used for a person who has a lot of power, influence, or authority in a company, group, or organization. It is often used in a slightly humorous or casual way.
example_sentence: He became the big cheese in the company after years of hard work. Everyone listens carefully when the big cheese enters the meeting. She is the big cheese in the marketing department now. The big cheese approved the final project proposal.

english_meaning: An important and influential person in an organization. The boss or a top executive who holds a lot of power. A highly significant individual within a specific group or company. The main leader who makes all the final decisions.
example_sentence: He thinks he is the big cheese now that he got promoted to manager. The big cheese is visiting our branch tomorrow to inspect the operations. You will have to ask the big cheese if you want approval for this budget. She became the big cheese of the company after years of hard work.

english_meaning:
An important or powerful person. A person of great importance, power, or influence in a particular field.
It can also mean a leading figure or important authority.
example_sentence: He is a big gun in politics. He is a big gun in the business world. Many big guns attended the international conference. The company hired a big gun to improve their marketing strategy. When the issue became serious, the big guns were called in to handle it.

english_meaning: A person who talks too much or reveals secrets is often called a big mouth. It refers to someone who lacks discretion and cannot keep confidential information safe. This term describes the habit of speaking boastfully or without thinking. It points to an individual who inappropriately shares others' private matters.
example_sentence: I shouldn't have trusted that big mouth with my surprise party plans. He is such a big mouth that the entire office knows about my promotion before it is official. Tell your brother to keep quiet and stop being a big mouth. Her reputation as a big mouth made people hesitant to share their personal struggles with her.

english_meaning: The largest and thickest toe on the human foot. The first toe counting from the inner side of the foot. The toe that plays the main role in balance and pushing the body forward while walking. The toe also known medically as the hallux.
example_sentence: He broke his big toe while moving the furniture. The big toe carries most of the weight when we walk. Her big toe was swollen after the long hike. The doctor examined the joint of his big toe.

english_meaning: To praise or promote someone or something, to give importance or recognition.
example_sentence: He’s always bigging up his achievements. The manager bigged up the new project in the meeting. She bigged up her team’s hard work. Stop bigging yourself up all the time.

english_meaning: To praise or show pride in yourself, to give yourself credit or respect.
example_sentence: Big up yourself for finishing the task!. He always tells others to big up themselves. Big up yourself, you deserve it!. She bigged herself up after the presentation.

english_meaning: To have more important things to do. To have more important or more pressing matters to deal with than the current one. It shows that a person is not interested in something because there are greater priorities or more valuable tasks to focus on.
example_sentence: I can’t help now, I’ve got bigger fish to fry. I cannot attend the meeting right now, I have bigger fish to fry. She did not argue about the small mistake because she had bigger fish to fry. The manager ignored the minor complaint as there were bigger fish to fry in the project. He refused to join the small debate since he had bigger fish to fry in his business.

english_meaning: It refers to the overall, broad perspective of an issue or situation rather than the minor details. It means looking at the overarching context or long-term consequences. It represents the most important facts about a situation and how they are connected. It urges someone to ignore trivial matters and focus on what truly matters in the end.
synonyms: ["Grand Scheme","Broad View","Wide Perspective","Overall Context","Long Term View","Main Issue","Entire Context","Macro Perspective","Bird's Eye View","General Overview"]
antonyms: ["Minor Details","Nitty Gritty","Minutiae","Small Details","Trivialities","Specifics","Narrow View","Short Term Focus","Microscopic View","Insignificant Details"]
example_sentence: You need to look at the bigger picture instead of getting upset over one small mistake. The manager asked the team to focus on the bigger picture and not get bogged down by minor technicalities. In the bigger picture, this temporary setback will not affect our long-term goals. Understanding the bigger picture helps leaders make better strategic decisions for the company.

english_meaning: A person who strongly and unfairly hates or dislikes people with different beliefs, religion, race, or opinions. A person who is strongly prejudiced and intolerant toward people who are different in religion, race, culture, political views, or way of life. A bigot does not respect others' differences and often judges or mistreats them unfairly.
antonyms: ["Tolerant person","Open-minded person","Fair-minded person","Impartial person","Liberal person","Broad-minded person","Accepting person"]
example_sentence: A bigot refuses to accept people who have different beliefs. The community stood against the bigot's hateful remarks. Nobody respected him because he behaved like a bigot. Education can help people avoid becoming a bigot.

english_meaning: Strongly biased and intolerant toward others who have different beliefs, religion, or background. A person who is firmly attached to their own opinions, often in an unfair way, and shows intolerance or prejudice against people with different views, cultures, religions, or identities
example_sentence: He made a bigoted remark about people from a different religion. Her bigoted attitude made it difficult for her to work in a diverse team. The organization does not tolerate bigoted behavior of any kind. His bigoted views prevented him from understanding other cultures.

english_meaning: In a narrow-minded and prejudiced way. Acting or thinking with strong, unfair opinions against people or ideas, often without reason or openness to other views.
example_sentence: He spoke bigotedly about people from different cultures. She judged others bigotedly without understanding their situation. The decision was made bigotedly, ignoring all opposing views. He reacted bigotedly to ideas that challenged his beliefs.

english_meaning: Intolerance toward people with different beliefs, religion, or opinions. Strong and unfair dislike or hatred toward people who are different in religion, race, culture, or opinions. A person who refuses to accept or respect others' views and often treats them unjustly.
example_sentence: Bigotry can divide communities and create conflict. Education helps reduce bigotry and promotes understanding. His bigotry prevented him from accepting different cultures. Laws are needed to protect people from discrimination and bigotry.

english_meaning: An important or powerful person, especially in business, politics, or an organization. A top executive. A high ranking official. A leading or prominent figure. A person with strong influence in a specific field
example_sentence: Several corporate bigwigs attended the international conference. The party bigwigs gathered to discuss the election strategy. He became a media bigwig after years of hard work. Local bigwigs were invited to the charity event.

english_meaning: A Sanskrit term meaning seed, used widely in Hindu and Buddhist philosophy to refer to the root syllable or seed sound of a mantra. Believed to contain within it the essence or potential of a complete spiritual idea or divine energy. Used in tantric practices to refer to single-syllable sacred sounds that hold concentrated spiritual power. The foundational unit from which all mantra is considered to grow or expand.
example_sentence: The yogi meditated on the bija mantra to connect with divine energy.  Each deity in Hindu tradition is associated with its own unique bija sound.  The teacher taught students to chant the bija at the beginning of each practice.  Om is often considered the universal bija of all mantras.  Understanding the bija requires deep study of Sanskrit and its phonetic system.

english_meaning: Involving two sides, parties, or countries. Refers to anything that has, affects, or is agreed upon by two sides. Often used in politics, law, diplomacy, and biology. For example, agreements, relationships, or symmetry can be bilateral.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a bilateral trade agreement. Bilateral talks are ongoing to resolve the border dispute. The patient had bilateral knee pain. Bilateral symmetry is common in most animals.

english_meaning: Able to speak, read, or write two languages fluently. Written, spoken, or presented in two languages. Relating to or involving the use of two languages. A person who has command of two languages.
example_sentence: She is bilingual and switches easily between English and Sindhi. The school offers a bilingual programme for young children. All road signs in the city are bilingual. Being bilingual helped him find a job abroad.

english_meaning: To cheat someone out of money or property. To defraud or deceive a person, especially for financial gain. To avoid paying a debt owed to someone. To trick someone by dishonest means. To swindle or con.
example_sentence: The con artist tried to bilk elderly people out of their savings. He was accused of bilking the company of thousands of dollars. She managed to bilk her partners with a fake investment scheme. Don't let strangers bilk you with false promises.

english_meaning: A love letter, especially one that is tender, romantic, and written with affection. A short, sweet written message sent to express romantic feelings toward another person. A term borrowed from French, literally meaning sweet letter, used in English to refer to any loving personal correspondence. Often used humorously or playfully to describe a romantic note.
example_sentence: He slipped a billet-doux under her door before she woke up.  The novel's plot revolved around a discovered billet-doux from a secret admirer.  She kept every billet-doux he had ever written to her in a box under the bed.  Writing a billet-doux is an old-fashioned but charming way to express affection.  The billet-doux was written in delicate handwriting and sealed with wax.

english_meaning: The number one thousand million, written as 1,000,000,000. A quantity equal to a thousand millions. An extremely large but unspecified number of things. Used to describe amounts of money or population on a very large scale.
example_sentence: The project will cost nearly two billion dollars. The world's population has crossed eight billion. He earned his first billion before the age of forty. Billions of stars fill the visible universe.

english_meaning: To swell out and rise in large rounded masses, as smoke or fabric does. To move in great waves or surges. A large rolling wave of water, smoke, or cloud. To increase greatly in volume or intensity.
example_sentence: Smoke billowed from the chimney all evening. Her long dress billowed in the sea breeze. A billow of dust followed the truck down the track. Anger billowed through the crowd after the announcement.

english_meaning: To tie or fasten something tightly. To hold things together. To make someone legally or morally obligated. To restrict or limit someone's freedom. A difficult or troublesome situation. The edge or covering that holds pages together.
example_sentence: Please bind the papers with a clip. The agreement will bind both companies for five years. Fear can bind people more strongly than rules. He found himself in a bind when both meetings started at once.

english_meaning: A person who writes an account of another person's life. An author who researches and records the life story of a real individual. Someone who documents the events, achievements and character of a person in book form.
example_sentence: She is the official biographer of the former prime minister. The biographer spent five years researching the artist's early life. His biographer had access to hundreds of private letters. A good biographer must separate fact from legend.

english_meaning: Relating to or describing a person's life. Containing information about the events and details of someone's life. Concerned with the written record of a real person's life.
example_sentence: The museum has a biographical film about the founder. She wrote a short biographical note for the programme. The book gives biographical details of every scientist mentioned. He read a biographical account of the poet's childhood.

english_meaning: A written account of a person's life, usually by someone else, covering their experiences, achievements, and significant events. The literary genre consisting of such accounts of real individuals' lives, often with historical or cultural significance. A detailed narrative of a person's life from birth to death or to the present, written in a factual manner. The story of someone's life, as written or recorded by another person.
example_sentence: She spent three years researching and writing a biography of the famous scientist.  The biography revealed many previously unknown details about the politician's early life.  His biography became a bestseller shortly after publication.  Students were asked to read a biography of a historical figure of their choice.  The authorized biography was written with full cooperation from the subject's family.

english_meaning: A biological substance that poses a threat to the health of living things. A risk to humans or the environment caused by bacteria, viruses or other organisms. Contaminated material that must be handled and disposed of with special care.
example_sentence: All used needles must be placed in the biohazard container. The laboratory was sealed after a suspected biohazard. Workers wore protective suits because of the biohazard risk. A yellow biohazard symbol was fixed to the door.

english_meaning: Relating to living organisms and the science of biology. Connected by blood or genetic relationship rather than by adoption. Involving natural physical processes of the body. Relating to weapons that use living organisms or toxins.
example_sentence: She finally met her biological mother after twenty years. The biological effects of the drug are still being studied. Biological weapons are banned under international law. Sleep is governed by our internal biological clock.

english_meaning: A medical test in which a small piece of tissue is removed from the body to examine it for disease. A diagnostic medical procedure where a doctor removes a small sample of cells or tissue from a part of the body. The sample is then examined under a microscope or tested in a laboratory to detect diseases such as cancer, infections, inflammation, or other abnormal conditions. It helps doctors confirm a diagnosis and decide the proper treatment.
example_sentence: The doctor recommended a biopsy to check if the lump was cancerous. She felt nervous before the biopsy, but the procedure was quick. The biopsy results confirmed that the tumor was benign. A skin biopsy helped identify the cause of the rash.

english_meaning: An animal that walks on two legs. A creature having two feet. Relating to two-footed movement.
example_sentence: Human beings are the best known biped. Birds are bipeds although they can also fly. The robot was designed as a walking biped. Fossils show that this dinosaur was a biped.

english_meaning: A mental health condition characterized by extreme mood swings between mania and depression. Having two opposite poles or extremes. Relating to or occurring in both polar regions. Having two opposite or contradictory ideas or qualities.
example_sentence: She was diagnosed with bipolar disorder. His bipolar moods swing from extreme happiness to deep sadness. The bipolar magnetic field has two opposite poles. Bipolar political views create division.

word: Birds of a feather flock together
english_meaning: People who are similar in character, interests, or behavior tend to spend time with each other. Like-minded or similar people naturally form groups.
synonyms: ["Like attracts like","Kindred spirits stick together","Similar people associate together"]
example_sentence: All the artists in the city hang out together, birds of a feather flock together. You’ll notice that the hardworking students always study in the same group, birds of a feather flock together. Those who love adventure often become friends; birds of a feather flock together. The cricket team is full of enthusiastic players, and they always support each other, birds of a feather flock together.

english_meaning: A person who experiences romantic or sexual attraction toward both men and women. Someone or something relating to sexual or romantic attraction toward both men and women.
example_sentence: Midrash and Zohar present Adam as hermaphroditic or bisexual. A number of insects combine the advantages of parthenogenesis with those of bisexual reproduction using an alternation of generations. he Bionic Woman of the television serial of the seventies  has the bisexual name of Jamie Summers.

english_meaning: Attraction to both males and females. The condition of having both male and female sexual organs. The state of being sexually or romantically attracted to members of either sex. The state of being sexually attracted to people of more than one gender.
example_sentence: She openly spoke about her bisexuality and the importance of acceptance. Bisexuality is recognized as a valid sexual orientation. He learned more about bisexuality through books and community discussions. Many societies are becoming more aware of bisexuality and gender diversity.

english_meaning: A senior Christian religious leader who oversees churches and priests in a specific area. Also a piece in the game of chess that moves diagonally. A person holding a high authority position in certain religious organizations.
example_sentence: The bishop delivered a powerful sermon at the cathedral. The bishop visited several churches in his diocese. In chess, the bishop moved diagonally to capture the knight. The community respected the bishop for his wisdom and leadership.

english_meaning: The smallest unit of information in computing, having a value of either 0 or 1. A single binary digit used to store or transmit data in digital systems. A small piece, amount, or part of something. A short period of time. A metal bar placed in a horse's mouth to control it. A tool part fitted into a drill for making holes. The past tense of the verb bite.
example_sentence: A single bit can store only a zero or a one. The file size is measured in bits and bytes. Please wait a bit before you start the test. He drilled the wall after changing the bit.

english_meaning: To spoil, mess up, or ruin something by doing it badly or carelessly. To make a mistake or do something very poorly. (It is an informal and impolite used mostly in spoken English)
example_sentence: He bitched up the whole plan. They bitched up the presentation. He totally bitched up the report and had to start over. Don’t bitch up the presentation, we’ve worked too hard on it. They bitched up the whole plan by ignoring the main instructions. I tried to fix the computer, but I bitched it up even more.

english_meaning: To cut, grip, or wound with the teeth. To sting or pierce the skin. To have a sharp or painful effect. A small piece of food taken into the mouth. A wound or mark made by teeth or an insect. Sharpness of flavor, cold, or criticism.
example_sentence: The puppy tried to bite my shoelace. A mosquito bit her on the ankle. He took one bite of the sandwich. There was a real bite in the winter air.

english_meaning: To respond to an attack with words or action. To suppress or hold back an emotion, remark, or reaction. To retaliate after being criticized or harmed.
example_sentence: She bit back when the interviewer questioned her honesty. He bit back an angry reply. I had to bite back my laughter during the ceremony. The team bit back with two late goals.

english_meaning: To close the teeth firmly. To apply pressure with the jaws. To control pain, fear, or emotion by clenching the teeth.
example_sentence: Bite down gently on the dental pad. He bit down as the doctor cleaned the wound. The athlete bit down on his mouthguard. She bit down hard to stop herself from crying out.

english_meaning: To grip or press a particular object firmly between the teeth. To clench the teeth around something to endure pain or steady oneself.
example_sentence: The dentist asked me to bite down on the strip. He bit down on a towel while they treated his injury. The baby eagerly bit down on the teething ring. She bit down on her lip to remain silent.

english_meaning: To cut or pierce something with the teeth. To begin eating something with a firm bite. To reduce or use a noticeable part of money, time, or resources. To start affecting something substantially.
example_sentence: She bit into the crisp apple. Be careful when you bite into the hot pastry. Rising fuel costs are biting into our savings. Extra meetings have bitten into my writing time.

english_meaning: To remove a piece by using the teeth. To undertake a task or responsibility, especially one that may be difficult. To speak a word or phrase abruptly or incompletely.
example_sentence: He bit off a piece of bread. She may have bitten off more work than she can handle. The dog bit off the end of the stick. He bit off his sentence when the manager entered.

word: Bite off more than one can chew
english_meaning: To take on more responsibility or work than one can handle. To attempt something that is too difficult or ambitious. To overestimate one's abilities and take on too much. To commit to more than one is capable of completing.
example_sentence: He bit off more than he could chew by accepting three projects at once. Don't bite off more than you can chew with your commitments. She realized she had bitten off more than she could chew. Taking on both jobs proved he had bitten off more than he could chew.

word: Bite off more than you can chew
english_meaning: To take on a task that is too big or difficult to handle. This idiom is used when someone accepts more responsibility, work, or challenges than they can manage successfully. It often leads to stress, failure, or incomplete results.
synonyms: ["Take on too much","Overestimate oneself","Overburden oneself","Take on more than one can handle"]
antonyms: ["Know one's limits","Act within capacity","Take on manageable tasks","Be realistic"]
example_sentence: He started three businesses at once and quickly realized he had bitten off more than he could chew. By taking five courses in one semester, she bit off more than she could chew. I thought I could finish the project in one day, but I bit off more than I could chew. They tried to build a large house without enough resources and ended up biting off more than they could chew.

english_meaning: To stop yourself from saying something you really want to say, usually to avoid hurting someone’s feelings, causing conflict, or making a situation worse. To hold back words of anger, criticism, or truth.
example_sentence: I had to bite my tongue to avoid arguing. He was angry but he bit his tongue instead of saying anything. He wanted to complain, but he bit his tongue to keep the peace.

english_meaning: To remove a section by biting. To form or cut a hollow or shape with the teeth. To say something in a tense, sharp, or forced way.
example_sentence: The child bit out the soft center of the biscuit. The horse bit out a patch of grass. She bit out each word through clenched teeth. The insect had bitten out tiny sections of the leaf.

english_meaning: To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage and without complaining, especially when it cannot be avoided. It means to accept something painful or challenging bravely.
example_sentence: She had to bite the bullet and face the truth. I decided to bite the bullet and go to the dentist. She didn’t want to go to the dentist, but she decided to bite the bullet and make an appointment. He knew quitting smoking would be painful, but he bit the bullet for his health. It was hard to apologize, but I bit the bullet and said I was sorry.

word: Bite the hand that feeds you
english_meaning: To harm or criticize someone who helps or supports you. This idiom means showing ingratitude by acting against a person or organization that provides help, support, money, or opportunities. It highlights disloyalty and thanklessness.
example_sentence: He bit the hand that feeds him by insulting his mentor. Do not bite the hand that feeds you. The company accused critics of biting the hand that fed them. She regretted biting the hand that fed her.

english_meaning: To cut completely through something with the teeth. To penetrate or sever a material by repeated biting. To eat through a barrier or covering.
example_sentence: The puppy bit through the thin cable. She could not bite through the tough meat. Rats had bitten through the grain sacks. The beaver can bite through a small branch quickly.

english_meaning: To stop yourself from saying something you might regret. To keep quiet even when tempted to speak. To hold back words that could cause trouble. To restrain oneself from speaking out. To avoid making a hurtful or inappropriate comment.
example_sentence: I had to bite my tongue during the meeting. She bit her tongue to avoid an argument. Sometimes it is better to bite your tongue than reply. He bit his tongue when his boss criticized him unfairly.

english_meaning: Small enough to be eaten in one bite. Divided into small, manageable portions. Brief and easy to understand or complete.
example_sentence: Serve the fruit in bite-sized pieces. The course presents grammar in bite-sized lessons. She divided the project into bite-sized tasks. These bite-sized videos are easy to watch during a break.

english_meaning: Using the teeth to cut, grip, or wound. Sharply cold or painfully harsh. Cruel, sarcastic, or severely critical in speech. Strong and pungent enough to sting.
example_sentence: The biting dog was kept behind a secure gate. A biting wind swept across the empty field. Her biting reply ended the argument. The sauce had a biting taste of raw mustard.

english_meaning: In a sharply critical, sarcastic, or cruel manner. In an intensely cold or painfully sharp way. With a pungent or stinging quality.
example_sentence: She spoke bitingly about the failed policy. The wind blew bitingly across the platform. His review was bitingly funny but unfair. The vinegar smelled bitingly sharp.

english_meaning: A digital image made from a rectangular grid of individual pixels. A file or representation that stores an image pixel by pixel. A raster graphic whose quality depends on its resolution. A map of binary data corresponding to points on a display.
example_sentence: The designer exported the logo as a bitmap. Enlarging a small bitmap can make the pixels visible. This program converts vector drawings into bitmap images. The printer reads the bitmap one row at a time.

english_meaning: Having a sharp, unpleasant taste. Feeling deep anger or resentment. Painful and difficult to accept. Extremely cold and biting, as of weather.
example_sentence: The medicine had a bitter taste. He is still bitter about losing his job. Defeat in the final was a bitter experience. A bitter wind swept across the valley.

english_meaning: A long green vegetable with a rough surface and a strongly bitter taste. A tropical vine vegetable widely used in Asian cuisines. A vegetable known for its medicinal benefits, especially for diabetes. A gourd cooked with onions, spices, or stuffed with fillings. A plant of the cucurbit family valued for both food and traditional medicine.
example_sentence: Bitter gourd is known to help control blood sugar levels. She stuffed the bitter gourd with spices and onions. Many people dislike bitter gourd because of its strong taste. My grandmother drinks bitter gourd juice every morning.

english_meaning: A temporary camp or resting place without tents or with only very basic shelter, especially one used by soldiers or explorers in the field. To camp in the open air or in improvised shelters, typically for a short period during a journey or military operation. A rough or makeshift encampment set up quickly in emergency or field conditions. To spend the night outdoors in a temporary and minimally equipped camp.
example_sentence: The soldiers were ordered to bivouac in the forest until dawn.  The mountaineers set up a bivouac on a narrow ledge during the unexpected storm.  They bivouacked beside the river after hiking all day through the hills.  A bivouac sack is a lightweight alternative to a full tent.  The general chose a hidden valley for the regiment's overnight bivouac.

english_meaning: Very strange, unusual, or unconventional in a way that seems strikingly odd or out of the ordinary. Markedly unusual in appearance, character, or behavior, often to the point of seeming surreal. Used to describe events, ideas, or experiences that defy normal expectations. Strikingly out of the ordinary, sometimes in an eerie or fantastical way.
example_sentence: They witnessed a bizarre scene unfold right outside their hotel window.  The detective found the bizarre clues at the crime scene difficult to explain.  Her bizarre behavior at the party left everyone confused.  It was a bizarre coincidence that they ended up on the same flight.  The documentary explored some of the most bizarre customs found around the world.

english_meaning: To talk carelessly or reveal secrets unintentionally. To chatter or gossip. A person who talks too much or reveals secrets.
example_sentence:
Someone must have blabbed to the police. 
Try not to blab the whole story. She blabbed all the details to her friends. Stop blabbing or the secret will be out. He is such a blab; never tell him anything private. Don’t be a blab; keep this to yourself. That blab told everyone about the plan.

english_meaning: An odd or disreputable member. Someone who behaves differently (often negatively) from the rest of the group. A person who is considered a disgrace, embarrassment, or outcast within a family, group, or community.
example_sentence: He is the black sheep of the family because he never follows traditions. He became the black sheep of the team after he was caught cheating. The teacher called him the black sheep of the class for disturbing others. His criminal activities made him the black sheep of the village.

english_meaning: A thin, transparent coating of ice on a road or other surface, hard to see. Ice that appears black because it is smooth and reflects the surface beneath. A dangerous form of ice that causes slipping and accidents. A hidden layer of frozen water on pavement. Any nearly invisible sheet of ice.
example_sentence: The driver lost control on the black ice. Black ice is one of the most dangerous winter hazards. Several accidents occurred because of black ice last night. Walk carefully; there may be black ice on the path.

english_meaning: To color or fill an area with black, to obscure text or drawing using black color.
example_sentence: She blacked in the spaces on the drawing. The censor blacked in the sensitive parts. He blacked in the outline to make it bold. The student blacked in the missing sections.

english_meaning: To lose consciousness, faint or temporarily lose memory. To turn off lights or censor information. To suppress or block information from public view. To cause a temporary cessation of electrical power.
example_sentence: He blacked out after the accident. The city blacked out during the storm. The government blacked out parts of the report. I completely blacked out and don’t remember what happened.

english_meaning: To forget or lose control during an event or emotional reaction, often due to stress or alcohol.
example_sentence: He blacked out on stage from fear. She blacked out on her way home. After too much stress, he blacked out on his duties. The soldier blacked out on the battlefield.

english_meaning: To describe the sky when dark clouds appear, showing that rain or a storm is coming.
example_sentence: The sky blacked over before the storm. It suddenly blacked over and started raining. The horizon blacked over quickly. The weather blacked over by evening.

english_meaning: A spice used to season food. The dried fruit of the black pepper plant. A seasoning that gives food a hot or pungent taste. A dark-colored spice usually used in powdered or whole-grain form. A natural flavoring used in cooking, soups, sauces, salads, and many other dishes. The dried peppercorns obtained from the plant Piper nigrum. A spice commonly paired with salt as a table seasoning. A substance used to make food more flavorful and slightly spicy.
example_sentence: I added some black pepper to the soup. Black pepper gives the chicken a spicy flavor. She sprinkled black pepper over the salad. Please pass me the salt and black pepper.

english_meaning: A rare and highly unexpected event with major consequences. An occurrence that seems predictable only after it has happened. A surprising discovery that overturns an accepted belief. Literally, a swan with black plumage, especially the species native to Australia.
example_sentence: The sudden market collapse was described as a black swan. Good risk plans prepare for the impact of a black swan. The discovery acted as a black swan for the scientific community. We saw several black swans while traveling in Western Australia.

english_meaning: A dark-coloured bee, especially the black honey bee kept for honey production. A common name used for the native dark European honey bee. Any bee having a mainly black body.
example_sentence: A blackbee settled quietly on the sunflower. Farmers here keep the blackbee for its rich honey. The blackbee is well suited to cold climates. A blackbee buzzed around the garden all morning.

english_meaning: A small, dark purple-black fruit made up of many tiny juicy segments. An edible berry that grows on a thorny bush or bramble. The prickly shrub that bears this fruit. To gather or pick blackberries from bushes.
