example_sentence: I need to boost up my confidence before the interview. The company plans to boost up sales by offering discounts. Exercise can boost up your energy levels. New policies were introduced to boost up student performance.

english_meaning: A strong covering for the foot and lower leg. The space at the back of a car for luggage. To start a computer so that it becomes ready to use. To kick something hard, or to force someone to leave.
example_sentence: She wore leather boots in the rain. Put the suitcase in the boot of the car. The computer takes a minute to boot up. He booted the ball across the field.

english_meaning: A person who flatters others excessively to gain favor. Someone who behaves in a servile manner to impress superiors. A person who seeks approval through insincere praise. An overly obedient follower who acts to please. Someone who does whatever their boss wants to gain benefit.
example_sentence: Nobody respects a bootlicker in the office. He got the promotion by being a bootlicker, not by hard work. She is known as a bootlicker among her colleagues. Bootlickers rarely earn true respect.

english_meaning: Military forces physically deployed in an area. Field staff working directly in communities. Personnel carrying out operations instead of planning from headquarters. Ground level workers who collect data or implement programs.
synonyms: ["Field personnel","Ground forces","On site staff","Deployed troops","Frontline workers","Field team"]
antonyms: ["Remote staff","Headquarters personnel","Desk workers","Off site management","Back office staff"]
example_sentence: The government decided to send boots on the ground to help control the wildfire. The aid organization deployed boots on the ground after the flood to assist local communities. Good planning is important, but real progress happens when there are boots on the ground. The company sent boots on the ground to understand the market conditions directly.

english_meaning: A small loop at the back of a boot used to pull it on. To start or improve something using only one's own resources, without outside help. A popular free framework used to design responsive websites. The process by which a computer starts itself up.
example_sentence: They bootstrapped the company with their own savings. The site was built quickly using Bootstrap. He pulled the boot on by its bootstrap. The system bootstraps itself when power is restored.

english_meaning: Alcoholic drink. Liquor. To drink large quantities of alcohol. An informal word for any alcoholic beverage such as beer, wine, whisky, or spirits. To consume alcohol heavily, usually at a party or social gathering. The word is casual and often used in everyday conversation rather than in formal writing.
example_sentence: They brought plenty of booze to the party. He spent all his money on booze and cigarettes. The guests boozed until late at night. Try not to booze too much before the meeting tomorrow. There was no booze allowed at the wedding.

english_meaning: The rumbling or gurgling sounds produced by the movement of gas and fluid through the intestines. These sounds are a normal part of digestion.
example_sentence: The silence of the classroom made his borborygmi embarrassingly loud. Borborygmi is perfectly normal and happens to everyone. She could hear her own borborygmi after skipping lunch. The doctor said the borborygmi were a sign of healthy digestion.

english_meaning: The feeling of being tired and impatient because nothing interesting is happening. A state of weariness caused by lack of activity or interest. Dullness or monotony experienced by a person. Emotional flatness due to repetition. Lack of stimulation or excitement.
example_sentence: Long summer afternoons often bring boredom to children. He started painting to escape boredom during the lockdown. The lecture caused terrible boredom among the students. Boredom is a common cause of overeating.

word: Born with a silver spoon in one's mouth
english_meaning: Born into a rich or privileged family. To be born into a wealthy, privileged, or influential family, to have advantages from birth without having to struggle for them.
example_sentence: She never worked; she was born with a silver spoon in her mouth. He never had to work hard because he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth. She travels around the world easily since she was born with a silver spoon in her mouth. People think he achieved success alone, but he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth. Unlike his brother, Ali was not born with a silver spoon in his mouth and had to build his career from scratch.

english_meaning: Carried or transported. Supported or sustained. Endured or tolerated. Produced or given birth to. Carried or spread by a particular agent such as air, water, insects, or blood. Accepted or paid as a cost or responsibility. The past participle of bear and normally used with an auxiliary verb.
example_sentence: The cost will be borne by the company. She had borne the hardship with remarkable courage. The injured climber was borne down the mountain on a stretcher. Mosquito-borne diseases are common in tropical regions. The trees had borne fruit earlier than expected.

english_meaning: To take and use something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it. To receive money from a person, bank, or institution that must be paid back, usually with interest. To take a word, idea, or custom from another language or culture and use it as one's own. The opposite of lend. The act of using something temporarily without claiming permanent ownership.
example_sentence: Can I borrow your pen for a minute? She borrowed a book from the library yesterday. They had to borrow money from the bank to buy a new house. English has borrowed many words from French and Latin. He borrowed his brother's car for the weekend.

english_meaning: Having large or prominent breasts. Full-figured, especially in the chest area. Curvaceous with a well-developed bust.
example_sentence: The painting depicted a bosomy woman in traditional attire. The dress was designed for a bosomy figure. She was tall and bosomy, with an elegant walk. The character in the novel was described as bosomy and charming.

english_meaning: The scientific study of plants. The branch of biology concerned with plant life, structure, growth, classification, reproduction, and uses. The plant life of a region.
example_sentence: She studied botany at college. Botany helps farmers understand plant diseases. The botany of the island includes many rare flowers. A microscope is useful in botany. The teacher asked us to label the parts of a leaf in botany class.

english_meaning: To do something badly or carelessly. To spoil a task or job by doing it in a careless, clumsy, or unskilled way. It can also refer to a job that has been done very badly and needs fixing.
example_sentence: He botched the repair and made the problem worse. The plan was botched due to poor coordination. She apologized for botching the presentation. The company botched the product launch.

english_meaning: To take the trouble to do something; to annoy or cause worry. To give effort or concern for something, often reluctantly. To disturb, worry, or annoy someone. A source of trouble, annoyance, or inconvenience. Something that causes difficulty or annoyance.
example_sentence: Tell the children to stop bothering their father. Don’t bother me with foolish question. The man is always bothering me to lend him money. Don’t put yourself to any bothering. His lazy son is quite a bother to him. This drawer won't shut isn't it a bother.

english_meaning: A long, light green vegetable shaped somewhat like a bottle. A vine plant of the cucurbit family widely grown in warm regions. A vegetable known for being light, watery, and easy to digest. A gourd often used in curries, sweets, and traditional dishes. A plant whose dried shell is used as a container or musical instrument.
example_sentence: Bottle gourd is often recommended for people with high blood pressure. She made a delicious kheer using bottle gourd. Bottle gourd curry is very light and easy to digest. My mother cooks bottle gourd with lentils every week.

english_meaning: A dark green color like that of green glass bottles. A deep, rich shade of green. Having the dark green color of bottle glass.
example_sentence: She wore a bottle green velvet jacket to the dinner. The car was painted a deep bottle green. Bottle green curtains hung in the library. The team's uniform featured bottle green stripes.

english_meaning: To lose courage at the last moment and fail to do something because of fear or nervousness.
example_sentence: He bottled out at the last moment. He was going to ask for a promotion, but he bottled out at the last minute. The player bottled out of taking the final penalty She wanted to speak on stage but bottled out when she saw the crowd. They were supposed to confront the manager, but they bottled out.

english_meaning: To hide or suppress one's emotions instead of expressing them. To keep feelings inside without letting them out. To restrain or hold back strong emotions. To prevent something from moving or escaping. To conceal one's true feelings for a long time.
example_sentence: Do not bottle up your feelings; talk to someone. He bottled up his anger for years. She tends to bottle up her grief instead of sharing it. Bottling up stress can harm your health.

english_meaning: A narrow or busy section of road where the traffic often gets slower and stops. Anything that delays development or progress, particularly in business or industry. A crowded mass (as of cars) that impedes or blocks movement. A narrow route.
example_sentence: He drove around the outside of the town to avoid the bottleneck in the center. Opponents argue that the traffic lights would cause a bottleneck at the junction. Understaffing has caused a real bottleneck. Computer buffs call this a bottleneck.

english_meaning: A main branch of a tree. A large limb growing from the trunk of a tree, often bearing smaller branches. In poetry, a leafy branch used as a symbol of nature or shelter.
example_sentence: A heavy bough broke under the weight of the snow. Birds nested in the highest bough of the old tree. Children sat in the shade of a spreading bough. The gardener sawed off a dead bough.

english_meaning: A large, rounded rock, especially one that has been worn smooth by water or weather. A massive stone, usually too big to be lifted easily, that lies on the surface of the ground or in a river. Boulders are larger than ordinary stones and are often found in mountains, valleys, rivers, and along coastlines. The word is also used figuratively to describe something heavy or burdensome.
example_sentence: A huge boulder blocked the mountain road after the landslide. Children climbed over the smooth boulders by the river. The boulder rolled down the hill and crashed into the trees. Workers used machines to move the giant boulder. The path was covered with rocks and boulders.

english_meaning: A wide street in a city or town, usually lined with trees on both sides. A broad avenue, often considered grand or important, that may feature shops, restaurants, monuments, or fashionable buildings. Boulevards are typically found in major cities and are designed for both traffic and pedestrians. The term originally comes from French and refers to a fortified rampart that was later turned into a public road.
example_sentence: We walked along the famous boulevard in Paris. The hotel is located on a busy boulevard near the city center. Tall palm trees lined the entire boulevard. A parade was held on the main boulevard yesterday. Their new house overlooks a quiet, tree-lined boulevard.

english_meaning: To recover from difficulty or loss in a stronger and improved way.
example_sentence: After failure, he bounced back better. They bounced back better after the loss. She always bounces back better from setbacks. Our team will bounce back better next season.

english_meaning: Certain or very likely to happen. Tied or fastened firmly. Legally or morally obliged to do something. Travelling in a particular direction, or to leap.
example_sentence: He is bound to succeed with such hard work. The parcel was bound with strong rope. We are bound by the terms of the agreement. The train is bound for Karachi.

english_meaning: Existing in large quantity; plentiful and abundant. Generous in giving; willing to share freely with others. Providing more than enough of what is needed.
example_sentence: The farmers enjoyed a bountiful harvest this year. She thanked her bountiful hosts for their kindness. The valley is bountiful in fruit and clean water. A bountiful supply of food was sent to the flood victims.

english_meaning: A generous reward. A payment offered for capturing a person or animal or for completing a task. A plentiful supply or abundance of something. Generosity freely given. Historically, money paid by a government to encourage recruitment or production.
example_sentence: The police offered a bounty for information leading to the fugitive's arrest. The garden provided a rich bounty of fresh vegetables. We shared the autumn bounty with our neighbors. Her family was grateful for nature's bounty. The company paid a bounty to employees who recruited skilled workers.

english_meaning: A bunch of flowers arranged together, usually for decoration or as a gift. A carefully arranged collection of flowers, often tied together and given as a gift, used in ceremonies, celebrations, or decoration. It can also refer to a pleasant smell, especially in wine or perfumes.
example_sentence: She received a beautiful bouquet of roses on her birthday. The bride carried a bouquet of fresh flowers. He gave her a bouquet to express his love. The wine has a rich bouquet of fruity aromas.

english_meaning: A boundary or limit. A small stream or brook, especially one that flows from a spring. A goal or destination, often used in a literary or poetic sense. An archaic or literary word that can mean either a physical boundary, a small watercourse, or the final point of a journey. Famously used by Shakespeare in 'Hamlet' to refer to the undiscovered country from which no traveller returns.
example_sentence: Death is the bourne from which no traveller returns. The little bourne flowed gently through the meadow. They reached the bourne of their long journey at sunset. His ambition knew no bourne. The old map marked the bourne between the two estates.

english_meaning: A short period of activity or a contest. A limited period during which something happens with intensity, such as illness, emotion, or activity. It also means a competitive match, especially in boxing or wrestling.
example_sentence: He had a short bout of fever last night. The boxer won the final bout easily. She went through a bout of sadness after the loss. The two fighters prepared for a tough bout.

english_meaning: Short periods of intense crying. Repeated or sudden episodes of crying that happen for a short time, often caused by strong emotions such as sadness, stress, pain, or emotional shock.
synonyms: ["Episodes of crying","Fits of crying","Spells of weeping","Crying episodes"]
example_sentence: After hearing the bad news, she had several bouts of crying throughout the day. The child experienced bouts of crying due to fear and exhaustion. He tried to stay calm, but bouts of crying interrupted his speech. Post surgery recovery included pain and unexpected bouts of crying.

english_meaning: Relating to or resembling cattle. Connected with cows, bulls, oxen, or buffaloes. Slow-moving, dull, or stolid in manner, like a cow. In biology and zoology it describes animals of the cattle family. Also used figuratively to describe a person who appears sluggish, expressionless, or lacking in intelligence or emotion.
example_sentence: Bovine diseases can spread quickly if cattle are not vaccinated. The farm specializes in bovine health and breeding. He stared at the screen with a bovine expression. Bovine milk is the most common type consumed worldwide. Scientists studied the bovine immune system in detail.

english_meaning: Something that curves or is curved. To incline the head or body in salutation or assent or to acknowledge applause. To incline especially in respect or submission. To move your head or the top half of your body forwards and downwards as a sign of respect or to say hello or goodbye
example_sentence: The people all bowed down before the emperor. She bowed her head in shame. They stood in silence with their heads bowed. We bowed our heads in prayer. They bowed deferentially as she came into the room.

english_meaning: To kneel or bend low in respect, worship, or submission. To accept someone’s authority or power completely.
example_sentence: The visitors bowed down to the sacred statue. She would not bow down to fear. The defeated army bowed down to the emperor’s authority. We should not bow down to injustice.

english_meaning: A short strip of fabric tied in the shape of a bow and worn around the neck. A formal necktie commonly worn with a tuxedo.
example_sentence: He wore a red bow tie with his dinner jacket. The child learned how to tie a bow tie. Her bow tie matched her dress. A bow tie is traditional formal wear for some ceremonies.

english_meaning: To bend the head or upper body as a sign of respect or greeting. To accept or submit to a demand, rule, or influence.
example_sentence: The performers bowed to the audience. He refused to bow to political pressure. She bowed to the king as a sign of respect. The company finally bowed to public demand.

english_meaning: The intestine inside the body that helps digest food and remove waste. It also refers to the act of passing stool. The deepest or inner part of something. Used informally to express deep feelings such as fear or compassion.
example_sentence: The doctor examined his bowel for infection. She has regular bowel movements every morning. The miners were trapped deep in the bowels of the earth. Anxiety can sometimes affect the bowel.

english_meaning: Bending the upper body or head forward as a sign of respect, greeting, agreement, or submission. The act of inclining the body in front of a person, audience, or sacred object. Used in formal greetings, religious ceremonies, theatrical performances, and martial arts. Can also refer to the act of playing a stringed musical instrument with a bow, or bending under pressure or weight.
example_sentence: Bowing is a common form of greeting in Japan. The actor was bowing to the audience after the performance. He kept bowing his head out of respect for the elder. Bowing under the weight of the heavy bag, he walked slowly. She practiced bowing techniques for her violin lesson.

english_meaning: Plural of bow. Curved weapons used for shooting arrows. Decorative knots tied from ribbon or string, often used on gifts or in hair. Acts of bending the body forward as a sign of respect or greeting. The front parts of ships or boats. Long, thin sticks with horsehair stretched along them, used to play stringed instruments such as the violin or cello.
example_sentence: The hunters carried bows and arrows into the forest. She tied colorful bows on all the gift boxes. The performers gave three bows to the cheering audience. Waves crashed against the bows of the fishing boats. The violinists tightened their bows before the concert.

english_meaning: The string stretched between the ends of a bow and used to propel an arrow. A strong, tightly stretched cord used with an archery bow.
example_sentence: The archer replaced the broken bowstring. He pulled the bowstring carefully. A loose bowstring makes accurate shooting difficult. The instructor checked the bowstring before practice.

english_meaning: An imitation of the barking sound made by a dog. A childish or informal word for a dog. Used especially by or with young children to refer to dogs in a friendly way. It can be used as a noun for the dog itself or as an interjection imitating its bark. The word reflects how the sound of a dog's bark is represented in English onomatopoeia.
example_sentence: The little boy laughed and pointed at the bowwow in the garden. We could hear the bowwow of the neighbor's dog all night. She bought a tiny bowwow as a pet for her daughter. The puppy let out a soft bowwow when it saw the stranger. 'Look at the bowwow!' the child shouted happily.

english_meaning: Able to float in water or rise in air; buoyant. Cheerful, confident, and full of positive energy. Describing a market or economy that is doing well and rising in value. Quick to recover after a setback.
example_sentence: The wooden raft was light and buoyant on the river. She was in a buoyant mood after the good news. The housing market remained buoyant throughout the year. His buoyant personality lifted the whole team.

english_meaning: To refuse to buy, use, or take part in something as a form of protest. To avoid dealing with a person, company, or country in order to show disapproval. An organized refusal to support or participate in something.
example_sentence: The students decided to boycott the classes in protest. Several countries agreed to boycott the games. The boycott lasted for nearly three months. Consumers boycotted the brand after the scandal.

english_meaning: A device used to support, strengthen, or hold something firmly in place. A pair of two similar things, especially birds or animals. To prepare oneself mentally or physically for something difficult or unpleasant. To make stronger by adding a support. In dentistry, a wire device worn to straighten the teeth. Also used to describe a pair of suspenders that hold up trousers.
example_sentence: He wore a brace on his knee after the injury. The pilot told the passengers to brace for landing. She got a brace fitted to straighten her teeth. They shot a brace of pheasants during the hunt. Wooden braces were used to support the roof.

english_meaning: Prepare yourself for something difficult, shocking, or exciting that is about to happen. To mentally prepare for impact or shock. To get ready for difficulty or emotional stress. To strengthen yourself before an event. To get mentally or physically ready for something intense, unexpected, or challenging. It is often used as a warning before bad news, strong impact, or exciting events.
example_sentence: Brace yourself, the results of the exam are very low this year. Brace yourself, the storm is getting closer. Brace yourself before you watch this scary movie. Brace yourself, there is some bad news coming.

english_meaning: To talk with excessive pride about oneself or one's achievements. To boast about possessions, abilities, or successes. A statement made in a boastful manner. An act of boasting.
example_sentence: He likes to brag about his new car to everyone. She never brags about her achievements, despite her success. Stop bragging and show us what you can actually do. His constant bragging annoyed his classmates.

english_meaning: A person who boasts a lot. Someone who talks about their achievements, possessions, or abilities in an exaggerated or prideful way to impress others.
example_sentence: He is such a braggart, always talking about his expensive car. Don’t be a braggart; nobody likes constant showing off. She acted like a braggart after winning the prize. Braggarts often exaggerate their skills in interviews.

english_meaning: A person who talks proudly and boastfully about himself or his achievements. Someone who exaggerates his abilities or possessions to impress others.
example_sentence: Nobody likes a bragger who never stops talking about himself. He is a bragger, so ignore half of what he says. The bragger claimed he had met the president. She is confident but never a bragger.

english_meaning: The soft mass of nerve tissue inside the skull that controls thought, memory, movement, and the senses. The central organ of the nervous system that receives signals from the body and sends out instructions. A person's intelligence or ability to think clearly. A highly intelligent person or the leading planner behind a project or scheme. To think about something carefully or use one's mind.
example_sentence: The human brain contains billions of nerve cells. Regular reading keeps the brain active and alert. She was the brain behind the company's new marketing plan. A serious blow to the head can injure the brain.

english_meaning: A state of mental confusion or lack of clarity. Difficulty in concentrating or focusing on tasks. A feeling of mental fatigue or being 'spaced out'. Inability to think clearly or remember things quickly. Reduced cognitive function often caused by stress or illness.
example_sentence: After recovering from the flu, she suffered from lingering brain fog for several weeks. Lack of sleep can often lead to a frustrating sense of brain fog during the workday. I tried to finish the report, but the brain fog made it impossible to organize my thoughts. Changing his diet helped him eliminate the afternoon brain fog he used to experience.

english_meaning: A puzzle, riddle, question, or problem that requires careful thinking, logic, creativity, or intelligence to solve. A challenging puzzle or problem designed to test a person's thinking ability, reasoning skills, and mental agility.
synonyms: ["Puzzle","Riddle","Conundrum","Enigma","Mind bender","Logic puzzle","Mental challenge","Intellectual problem","Head scratcher","Thinking exercise"]
antonyms: ["Simple question","Easy task","Straightforward problem","Obvious answer","Plain exercise","Routine activity"]
example_sentence: This brain teaser took me almost an hour to solve. The teacher gave the students a brain teaser to improve their logical thinking. Solving brain teasers regularly can sharpen the mind. The interview included a difficult brain teaser question.

english_meaning: Electrical impulses produced by activity in the brain. Sudden clever ideas or inspirations. Patterns of brain activity recorded by an EEG. Bright thoughts that solve a problem quickly.
example_sentence: The doctor measured his brain waves during sleep. She suddenly had a brain wave and solved the puzzle. Researchers study brain waves to understand memory. His brain wave saved the company a lot of money.

english_meaning: Mental deterioration or obsession with trivial content. A state where a person’s mind is overwhelmed or “rotting” due to excessive consumption of trivial, absurd, or low-quality content, often online. It can also describe a repetitive obsession with something silly or nonsensical.
example_sentence: Watching too many meme compilations gave him brainrot. That TV show is pure brainrot. Playing that game nonstop will cause brainrot. The internet is full of harmless brainrot.

english_meaning: The stalk-like lower part of the brain that connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord. The structure made up of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. The part of the brain that controls vital automatic functions such as breathing, heartbeat, blood pressure, and swallowing.
example_sentence: The brainstem controls breathing even while we sleep. All signals between the brain and body pass through the brainstem. Damage to the brainstem is usually life-threatening. Doctors tested the brainstem reflexes of the unconscious patient.

english_meaning: To think of many ideas quickly, especially in a group. To generate a large number of ideas, solutions, or suggestions in a short time. It is often done in groups to encourage creativity and free thinking without criticism. A session where people share ideas.
example_sentence: We need to brainstorm some new ideas for the project. The team brainstormed for hours before choosing a solution. Let’s have a brainstorming session tomorrow morning. She brainstormed a creative plan to solve the issue.

english_meaning: A part of a tree which grows out from the trunk. A division or office of a large organization. To divide into two or more subdivisions.
example_sentence: The monkey swung from one branch to another. Our company is opening a new branch in London. Physics is a branch of science. The river has several small branches that flow into the valley.

english_meaning: To wave or swing something, especially a weapon, in a threatening or excited way. To display something boldly or aggressively in order to impress, threaten, or attract attention. Usually used when a person shows a sword, knife, gun, or other object by moving it through the air. Can also be used figuratively for showing off documents, awards, or ideas.
example_sentence: He brandished a sword at the intruder. The protester brandished a banner above the crowd. The robber brandished a knife and demanded money. She brandished her award proudly in front of her friends. The soldier brandished his rifle to scare away the attackers.

english_meaning: A valuable prize, opportunity, or success that people try hard to achieve.
example_sentence: He reached for the brass ring when he applied for the company’s top position. Many young athletes dream of grabbing the brass ring by playing professionally. After years of hard work, she finally caught the brass ring with her promotion. Some people take big risks in life just to grab the brass ring of success.

english_meaning: Bright yellow like brass in color. Resembling brass in appearance or sound. Bold, loud, and shameless in manner. Harsh and metallic in tone, like a brass instrument. Cheap and showy in taste.
example_sentence: Her hair had turned a brassy orange after the dye. The brassy sound of the trumpets filled the hall. She spoke in a loud, brassy voice that annoyed everyone. The cheap jewelry had a brassy shine.

english_meaning: A badly behaved or annoying child. A spoiled, rude, or unruly young person. Often used in a disapproving or affectionate way to describe a child who acts in a selfish or troublesome manner. Can also refer informally to the child of a person in a particular profession, such as an 'army brat'. The word is usually used in casual or humorous speech.
example_sentence: That child is such a spoiled brat. Stop behaving like a brat and listen to your mother. The little brat threw his food on the floor. He grew up as an army brat, moving from city to city. She loves her nephew, even though he is a cheeky brat.

english_meaning: Courageous behavior or character. The quality of being brave. The ability to face danger, difficulty, fear, or pain without showing fear. A noble and admirable quality shown by people who act with strength of mind in challenging situations. Bravery is often praised in soldiers, firefighters, doctors, and ordinary people who perform heroic acts.
example_sentence: The soldier was honored for his bravery in battle. Her bravery in speaking out inspired many others. It takes great bravery to admit one's mistakes. The firefighters showed remarkable bravery during the rescue. Children learn about bravery from stories of real heroes.

english_meaning: To fight or argue noisily and roughly. A loud, disorderly quarrel or fight, often in a public place. It usually involves shouting, pushing, or hitting among a group of people.
example_sentence: A brawl broke out outside the stadium after the match. The police tried to stop the brawl before anyone got hurt. He was arrested for joining a street brawl. Two students started to brawl in the cafeteria.

english_meaning: To face a difficult or embarrassing situation with bold shameless confidence. Acting without shame or respect for social rules. Showing bold confidence even when behavior is wrong or rude. Very obvious or open without trying to hide. Related to brass in old usage.
example_sentence: He tried to brazen it out after being caught cheating. The official brazened out the accusations during the meeting. She decided to brazen it out and continue her speech despite criticism. He made a brazen lie in front of everyone. The thief showed a brazen attitude and refused to admit his crime. It was a brazen attempt to cheat the customers.

english_meaning: A person who behaves in a very shameless, bold, or disrespectful way without feeling guilt or embarrassment, even when their behavior is wrong or offensive. It often describes someone who openly ignores social rules or moral standards.
example_sentence: The brazen-faced thief denied the crime even when the evidence was clear. She gave a brazen-faced reply to the teacher in front of the whole class. The politician made a brazen-faced claim that shocked many people. His brazen-faced behavior angered everyone at the meeting.

english_meaning: Shameless or bold in a rude way. A person who behaves with open shamelessness. Such a person does not feel embarrassment even when doing something wrong or socially unacceptable. It often refers to someone who lies, argues, or acts boldly without any sense of shame.
example_sentence: The student gave a brazenfaced excuse even though everyone knew the truth. He made a brazenfaced claim that he had done nothing wrong. The thief showed a brazenfaced attitude when questioned by the police. Her brazenfaced denial surprised everyone in the meeting.

english_meaning: Doing something openly and boldly without shame, respect, or fear of criticism. It often describes behavior that ignores social rules or moral limits and shows strong confidence even when the action is wrong or improper.
example_sentence: He brazenly lied to the teacher even though everyone knew the truth. The thief brazenly walked into the store during the day. She brazenly ignored the rules and continued her actions. The politician brazenly denied the evidence shown to the public.

english_meaning: To not keep to an agreement or not keep a promise. To make a hole in a wall, fence, etc. so that somebody, something can go through it. A failure to do something that must be done by law. An action that breaks an agreement to behave in a particular way. A break in a relationship between people or countries. An opening that is created during a military attack or by strong winds or seas.
example_sentence: The government is accused of breaching the terms of the treaty. A doctor was sacked for allegedly breaching patient confidentiality. The proposed changes breached trade union rules. The dam had been breached. Demonstrators breached police lines around the embassy. They are in breach of Article 119. Selling goods constituted a breach of regulation 10B. The disagreement caused a serious breach in Franco-German relations. They escaped through a breach in the wire fence. A breach in the mountain wall permits warm sea air to penetrate inland.

english_meaning: A person’s main source of income or livelihood, the work or activity that provides money for living. Something essential or basic for survival or success.
example_sentence: Teaching is his bread and butter. Writing articles provides his bread and butter. Writing articles provides his bread and butter. Don’t take away his job, it’s his bread and butter!.

english_meaning: A small fragment of bread, often used in cooking as a coating or filler. In digital design, a navigational aid that shows the path a user has taken through a website or application, usually displayed as a trail of links. Used figuratively to describe a small clue or piece of information that helps lead someone toward a larger discovery or conclusion.
example_sentence: She coated the chicken in breadcrumbs before frying it.  The website uses breadcrumbs to help users navigate between pages easily.  The detective followed a trail of breadcrumbs that eventually led to the suspect.  A few breadcrumbs were left on the table after breakfast.  The clues in the story acted like breadcrumbs guiding the reader toward the twist.

english_meaning: A person who earns money to support their family. A family member who provides the main financial support for the household. This person earns income to pay for basic needs such as food, housing, education, clothing, healthcare, and other living expenses.
example_sentence: After his father retired, Ali became the breadwinner of the family. She works two jobs because she is the only breadwinner in her household. Losing his job made it difficult for him to continue as the breadwinner. In many modern families, both parents are breadwinners.

english_meaning: To separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain. To interrupt a continuity or cause a gap in something. To fail to observe a law, promise, or regulation. To cause a sudden and significant change in direction or state. A short period of rest or relief from work or an activity. An opportunity or a stroke of luck. To surpass a record or previous achievement. To decipher or solve a code or mystery. To domesticate a wild animal. To lessen the force of an impact. To emerge or become public, as with news. A crack or fracture in a bone or object.
example_sentence: He managed to break the record for the fastest sprint. We should take a short break after this meeting. Be careful not to break that expensive vase. The news will break tomorrow morning on the front page.

english_meaning: To wish someone good luck. It is commonly said before a stage performance, speech, exam, interview, or any important event. The phrase sounds negative, but it actually carries a positive meaning. It comes from theatre tradition where directly saying “good luck” was considered unlucky. Sometimes used casually among friends before any challenge.
synonyms: ["Good luck","Best of luck","Knock ‘em dead","Do well","All the best"]
antonyms: ["Bad luck","I hope you fail","Wish you misfortune"]
example_sentence: Before the actor went on stage, his friend smiled and said, "Break a leg!". You’ve prepared well for the exam, go on and break a leg. You have worked very hard for your play. Break a leg tonight. Break a leg in your final exam tomorrow. She whispered, break a leg, before he went on stage. I know you will do great in the interview. Break a leg.

english_meaning: To escape from control or leave an organization. To separate or escape from something or someone’s control.
example_sentence: The prisoner broke away from the guards. She broke away from the traditional style. Some members broke away to form a new party. The horse broke away from the stable.

english_meaning: To stop working, to collapse emotionally, or to separate something into parts. To divide something into smaller parts to understand it better.
example_sentence: My car broke down on the way. She broke down in tears. The talks broke down after hours. The machine broke down again.

english_meaning: To make neither a profit nor a loss. The total income equals total expenses.
example_sentence: After six months of business, the company finally managed to break even. We sold enough tickets to break even on the event costs. Despite hard work, the farmer could only break even this season. Our goal this year is at least to break even before making profits next year.

english_meaning: To enter a place by force or interrupt someone. To enter a building illegally or by force, especially to commit theft or damage. To interrupt someone while they are speaking. To make something comfortable or usable through use, such as new shoes or a new machine. To train a person or animal, especially a horse or a new employee.
example_sentence: Thieves broke in last night. Please don’t break in while I’m talking. The police broke in to rescue hostages. They broke in during the meeting. The manager will break in the new employees next week.

english_meaning: To enter a place forcefully or suddenly, often without permission.
example_sentence: Someone broke into my house. The burglars broke into the bank. She broke into a smile. The crowd broke into laughter.

english_meaning: To do something innovative or original, to start something that has not been done before. To innovate or pioneer something new. To explore unknown areas or ideas. To achieve something for the first time.
synonyms: ["Pioneer","Innovate","Blaze a trail","Lead the way","Open new horizons"]
example_sentence: The scientist broke new ground with her research in renewable energy. This software breaks new ground in artificial intelligence technology. The company broke new ground by introducing eco-friendly products. His novel broke new ground in modern literature.

english_meaning: To bring something to an abrupt end, such as a conversation, relationship, or agreement.
example_sentence: They broke off their engagement. Talks were broken off due to conflict. She broke off mid-sentence. The branch broke off the tree.

english_meaning: To fail to keep a promise. To not do what one has said they would do. It shows unreliability or dishonesty in fulfilling one’s commitment.
synonyms: ["Break a promise","Go back on one’s word","Be unfaithful","Betray one’s trust","Default on a promise"]
antonyms: ["Keep one’s word","Keep a promise","Honor one’s word","stay true","fulfill a commitment"]
example_sentence: He promised to help me, but he broke his word. A true gentleman never breaks his word. People lose respect for those who break their word. She broke her word by not attending the meeting she had agreed to join.

english_meaning: To suddenly begin or happen, to escape from a place or situation.
example_sentence: Fire broke out last night. War broke out between two nations. She broke out in a rash. Prisoners broke out of jail.

english_meaning: To cost a lot of money. To be too expensive. To use up all of one’s money or resources. To win all the money in a casino/bank.
example_sentence: Buying that luxury watch will break the bank. We want to go on vacation, but nothing that will break the bank. He bought a designer suit without breaking the bank. Paying for her medical treatment nearly broke the bank.

english_meaning: To initiate conversation in a social setting. To overcome initial shyness or tension.
example_sentence: He told a joke to break the ice at the party. He told a funny joke to break the ice at the meeting. She broke the ice with a friendly smile.

english_meaning: To do something different to make a dull or repetitive routine more interesting. To add variety to a boring situation. To interrupt sameness or tedium.
example_sentence: We took a short walk to break the monotony of the long study session. The teacher played a quiz game to break the monotony of the lesson. A weekend trip helped break the monotony of city life. Music can break the monotony of a long drive.

english_meaning: To do something in a completely new way instead of following the usual pattern or tradition. Acting differently from established conventions, traditions, or expectations. It emphasizes innovation, originality, and challenging norms. This phrase often describes creative thinkers, leaders, or actions that stand out because they are unconventional.
example_sentence: The startup broke the mould by offering a subscription model no one had tried before. Her artwork breaks the mould of traditional painting styles. He broke the mould by introducing a gender-neutral dress code at his company. The new smartphone design breaks the mould of standard rectangular devices.

english_meaning: To inform someone about something, usually something important or bad.
example_sentence: He broke the news of her death. I had to break the news to her that her flight was canceled. The doctor broke the news to the family about the patient’s condition. He broke the news of his promotion to his team. It's never easy to break the news of a loved one’s passing.

english_meaning: To end a romantic relationship. To separate into pieces or parts. To stop or disperse a meeting, crowd, or gathering. To interrupt something such as a fight or event. To close a school for holidays. To weaken or destroy unity. To experience poor signal or unclear sound during communication.
example_sentence: They decided to break up after five years together. The glass broke up into small pieces. The police broke up the protest. School will break up next week for summer vacation.

english_meaning: The point at which total cost and total revenue are equal, meaning there is no net loss or gain. To reach a state where expenses and income are balanced. A situation in a competition where one regains a lost position to reach a neutral standing. Relating to a business operation that generates just enough money to cover its costs. The level of sales or production at which a project becomes financially self-sustaining without profit.
example_sentence: The new restaurant expects to reach its break-even point within the first six months of operation. After losing the first set, the tennis player managed to break-even in the second set score. We need to calculate the break-even volume to determine if the project is viable. The company reported a break-even quarter despite the recent economic downturn.

english_meaning: An illegal entry into a building with the intent to steal or commit a crime. The act of entering a property forcibly. A period of initial operation of a new machine or vehicle to ensure long-term functionality.
example_sentence: The police are currently investigating a break-in at the local bank. She decided to upgrade her home security after a scary break-in. The break-in period for a new motorcycle engine is crucial for its longevity. Security cameras captured clear footage of the suspect during the break-in.

english_meaning: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning. The food that is eaten at that meal. To eat the morning meal. A morning meal served in a hotel, home, or restaurant.
example_sentence: I usually have breakfast at seven in the morning. Breakfast is included in the room price. She breakfasted quickly and left for work. A good breakfast helps children concentrate at school.

english_meaning: A sudden important discovery or progress. A major and sudden advance in knowledge, technology, science, or any difficult situation. It refers to overcoming a barrier or solving a problem that previously seemed impossible or very hard to solve. A moment of success after long struggle.
example_sentence: Scientists made a breakthrough in cancer research. The new software represents a breakthrough in technology. His promotion was a major breakthrough in his career. The peace talks led to a breakthrough between the two countries. After months of therapy, she finally had a breakthrough.

english_meaning: The ending of a relationship, division of something into parts, or separation of a group. End of a Romantic Relationship. The collapse or separation of a team, union, or country. Disturbance or interruption in sound, internet, or communication.
example_sentence: After the breakup, she focused on her studies. The breakup of the old building started yesterday. Political breakup caused unrest in the region. Poor weather caused a breakup in the radio transmission.

english_meaning: One of the two soft, rounded parts on the upper front of a woman's body that can produce milk. The front part of the chest in humans and animals. The seat of emotions, used in literary expressions such as 'a feeling in one's breast'. The part of a bird that covers the front of its body. To face or move forward against something with courage.
example_sentence: Mothers are encouraged to breastfeed their babies. He felt a sudden pain in his breast. The chef prepared a delicious chicken breast for dinner. She held the child gently to her breast. The swimmer breasted the waves with great strength.

english_meaning: To take air into the lungs and let it out again through the nose or mouth. To live or be alive. To say something softly or in a whispering manner. To allow fresh air to enter or pass through something. To pause and relax for a short time after stress or effort.
example_sentence: It is hard to breathe at such a high altitude. Open the windows so the room can breathe. She breathed a few soft words into his ear. After the exam, the students could finally breathe again. Plants breathe in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

english_meaning: The back part of a gun barrel where the ammunition is loaded. The lower or rear part of something. Relating to a birth in which the baby's buttocks or feet come out first. The buttocks or lower rear part of the body.
example_sentence: He loaded the cartridge into the breech of the rifle. The breech of the cannon was damaged in the blast. The baby was born in a breech position. A breech delivery often requires close medical supervision.

english_meaning: To produce young animals or plants through reproduction. A particular type or kind of animal or plant. To raise animals or plants for a specific purpose, such as appearance, behavior, or productivity. To cause a feeling, condition, or situation to develop. Often used both literally about animals and figuratively about ideas, emotions, or social problems.
example_sentence: This farm breeds horses for racing. Poverty often breeds crime and frustration. The Labrador is a very friendly breed of dog. Scientists are trying to breed a disease-resistant variety of wheat. Familiarity is said to breed contempt.

english_meaning: To produce offspring very quickly and in large numbers. To increase or multiply rapidly, often said disapprovingly. To grow in number at an unusually fast rate. Used figuratively for things that spread quickly.
example_sentence: Mice breed like rabbits in a warm barn. Cheap coffee shops seem to breed like rabbits in this street. He joked that their pets breed like rabbits. Rumours breed like rabbits on social media.

english_meaning: Pleasantly windy with light, fresh air. Cheerful, relaxed, and casual in manner. Light and informal in style, especially of writing or speech.
example_sentence: It was a bright, breezy morning by the sea. She greeted everyone in her usual breezy manner. The book is written in a breezy, readable style. We sat on the breezy terrace after dinner.

english_meaning: Speaking or writing in a very brief and concise way. The quality of expressing ideas using very few words while still conveying the complete meaning clearly. It is often valued in communication because it saves time and avoids unnecessary detail.
example_sentence: His breviloquence made the presentation easy to understand. The teacher appreciated her breviloquence in answering complex questions. In professional writing, breviloquence is often preferred over lengthy explanations. His breviloquence sometimes made others wish for more detail.

english_meaning: The quality of using few words when speaking or writing. Shortness of time or duration. Concise and exact use of language. The state of being brief or lasting for only a short period. A short and to-the-point manner of expression.
example_sentence: The teacher praised the student for the brevity and clarity of his essay. Brevity is the soul of wit, as Shakespeare wrote. Please answer the questions with the utmost brevity. The brevity of life reminds us to value every moment. He is admired for the brevity and force of his speeches.

english_meaning: To make beer, ale, or other drinks by mixing, boiling, and fermenting ingredients. To prepare tea or coffee by mixing it with hot water. To be in the process of developing, especially something unpleasant such as a storm or trouble. A drink made by brewing, especially beer or tea. To plan or plot something secretly.
example_sentence: She brewed a fresh pot of tea for the guests. This company has been brewing beer for over a hundred years. A storm is brewing on the horizon. Trouble was brewing between the two rival groups. He sat quietly, sipping his morning brew.

english_meaning: A drink produced by brewing, such as beer or ale. The process or product of brewing. A concoction or mixture prepared by boiling or steeping ingredients.
example_sentence: The old inn was famous for its dark brewage. He offered us a bitter herbal brewage. Every village had its own traditional brewage. The brewage was left to ferment for two weeks.

english_meaning: To give money, gifts, or favors to someone to persuade them to act dishonestly. A payment or gift given to influence someone’s actions dishonestly. Money, gifts, or favors offered to someone, especially in a position of power or authority, to persuade them to act in your favor or ignore rules or laws. It implies corruption or unethical behavior.
example_sentence: She was bribed into handling over secret information. They bribed the guard with cigarettes. The official accepted a bribe to approve the construction project. She refused to bribe the inspector, even though it would have been easier. The company offered a bribe to secure the contract. Bribing a judge is illegal in every country.

english_meaning: The illegal and unethical practice of offering, giving, receiving, or asking for something valuable in order to influence the actions or decisions of a person in a position of authority. It often occurs in business, politics, law enforcement, and public services. Bribery damages trust, fairness, and justice in society.
example_sentence: The officer was arrested for accepting bribery from a businessman. Bribery is considered a serious crime in many countries. The company was fined for engaging in bribery practices. She refused to participate in bribery despite pressure from her colleagues.

english_meaning: A harsh or critical remark, especially one made publicly about a person's performance, work, or behavior. A piece of brick or hard rubble used as a missile, especially when thrown at someone. Used figuratively to describe blunt criticism or insults directed at someone, often in contrast to compliments or praise.
example_sentence: The new policy received brickbats from critics across the political spectrum.  He threw a brickbat through the shop window during the riot.  The actor faced both brickbats and bouquets for his controversial performance.  Reviewers hurled brickbats at the poorly written script.  Despite the brickbats, she remained confident in her decision.

english_meaning: Relating to a bride or a wedding. Belonging to or used by a bride. Connected with the ceremony or celebration of marriage. Suitable for a wedding. Associated with the period around a wedding.
example_sentence: She looked stunning in her white bridal gown. The bridal shop has a wide collection of wedding dresses. The bridal suite was beautifully decorated with flowers. The bridal procession moved slowly toward the venue. Her bridal jewellery was passed down from her grandmother.

english_meaning: A woman on her wedding day or just before and after the event. A woman who is about to get married or has just got married. A female partner in a marriage ceremony. The female counterpart of the groom in a wedding.
example_sentence: The bride wore a beautiful red dress on her wedding day. Everyone praised the bride for her grace and elegance. The bride and groom cut the wedding cake together. The bride was escorted to the stage by her father. Photographs of the bride were taken before the ceremony began.

english_meaning: Restrained or controlled as if with a bridle. Showed resentment or anger by pulling the head up and back. Equipped with a harness to direct or govern movement. Curbed or held back from expressing an emotion or action. Controlled or managed strictly to ensure order.
example_sentence: He bridled his anger and remained silent during the confrontation. The horse was bridled and ready for the long journey ahead. She bridled at the suggestion that she was being dishonest. The scientist’s enthusiasm was bridled by the lack of funding for the project.

english_meaning: Of short duration or lasting only a short time. Concise or using few words. A set of instructions or information given in advance. To instruct or inform someone about something. A summary of facts and legal arguments. Short in length or extent.
example_sentence: Please keep your comments brief. The meeting was mercifully brief. The lawyer prepared a brief for the case. She briefed the team on the new project. His visit was brief but productive.

english_meaning: A clever, lively and quick-witted person, especially a young one. Someone who is full of good ideas and enthusiasm. Often used ironically to describe a person who has done something obviously foolish. A promising person expected to do well in a group or organisation.
example_sentence: The new intern is a bright spark who learns very quickly. Some bright spark left the freezer door open all night. We need a few bright sparks in the team to push this project forward. She was the bright spark of her class and won every science prize.

english_meaning: To be full to the point of overflowing or to be abundant with emotion, energy, or liquid. The upper edge of a cup, hat, or any hollow object. The top edge of a container or something filled to the top.
example_sentence: Tears brimmed in her eyes. Her eyes brimmed with tears. The team were brimming with confidence before the game. She watched the crowd from beneath the brim of her hat. He filled his cup to the brim. She poured the cream until it reached the brim.

english_meaning: Completely full of something. Containing or seeming to contain the greatest quantity or number possible. Ready to overflow. Filled to full capacity.
example_sentence: She's certainly brimful of energy. Nobody could call this year's Cannes film festival brimful of wonderful surprises. The United States is brimful with highly paid doctors. Young people are always brimful of new ideas and hope.

english_meaning: Water strongly saturated with salt. A salty solution used for preserving or pickling food. The salt water of the sea. To soak or preserve food in salt water.
example_sentence: The olives are stored in brine. She brined the chicken overnight for extra flavour. Waves of cold brine crashed against the rocks. Brine from the plant must be disposed of safely.

english_meaning: To cause something to happen or make something take place.
example_sentence: The reforms brought about major changes. Hard work brings about success. His speech brought about a revolution. The incident brought about his downfall.

english_meaning: To take someone or something with you when going somewhere.
example_sentence: Please bring your friend along. She brought along her notes. Can I bring my dog along? He brought his cousin along to the party.

english_meaning: To change someone’s opinion or make them accept an idea after discussion or effort. To help a person become conscious again after fainting or illness.
example_sentence: I tried hard to bring him around to our point of view. The doctor finally brought the patient around after the accident. It took several meetings to bring the committee around. She was fainted, but cold water brought her around quickly.

english_meaning: To return something or to make someone remember something from the past.
example_sentence: Please bring back my book. The song brought back memories. They brought back old traditions. He brought back souvenirs from Paris.

english_meaning: To cause something or someone to fall, lose power, or become lower in position or mood.
example_sentence: The scandal brought the leader down. The plane was brought down by a missile. High taxes bring down profits. His speech brought down the house.

english_meaning: To produce, present, or cause something to appear or happen. To cause something to exist, to give birth to something.
example_sentence: The tree brings forth fruit in season. The speech brought forth strong emotions. The project brought forth great results. The mother brought forth a child.

english_meaning: To provide something useful or profitable. To supply material that can be turned to advantage. To bring in work, business, or income. To offer facts or experience that can be used for a purpose.
synonyms: ["Be profitable","Prove useful","Provide material","Bring business","Serve a purpose","Be advantageous"]
example_sentence: Every small order brings grist to the mill for a new shop. His travels bring grist to the mill of his novels. The scandal brought grist to the mill of the opposition. Part-time clients still bring grist to the mill.

english_meaning: To earn money and provide financial support for one’s family. To be the main earner in a household. To achieve success that results in financial gain. To fulfill financial responsibilities.
synonyms: ["Earn a living","Make money","Support the family","Be the breadwinner","Provide income"]
antonyms: ["Be unemployed. Lose income","Depend on others","Be financially dependent","Fail to provide"]
example_sentence: She works hard to bring home the bacon. He works two jobs to bring home the bacon. After getting a promotion, she proudly brings home the bacon for her family. Many people travel abroad just to bring home the bacon. The team’s victory brought home the bacon for their supporters.

english_meaning: To make a law, rule, or agreement officially begin to apply. To put a regulation into effect from a stated date. To give legal power to a decision so that it must be obeyed. To implement an official measure so that it starts working in practice. To activate a rule that has already been approved.
example_sentence: The government plans to bring the new tax law into force next year. Parliament voted to bring the amendment into force immediately. The council will bring the parking rules into force from Monday. They brought the treaty into force after both sides signed it.

english_meaning: To punish, reprimand, or hold someone accountable for their mistakes, crimes, or wrongdoings.
example_sentence: The corrupt officer was finally brought to book for accepting bribes. The company’s accountant was brought to book after the audit revealed fraud. All those responsible for the accident must be brought to book. After months of investigation, the criminal was brought to book by the police.

english_meaning: To care for a child, teaching him or her how to behave, etc. To start to talk about a particular subject. To care for a child, teaching him or her how to behave, etc. To make something appear on a computer screen. To vomit. To bring (a person) to maturity through nurturing care and education.
example_sentence: He was brought up by his aunt. She's always bringing up her health problems. He's forever bringing up the past. The meeting seemed to be going well until Charles brought up the issue of holiday pay. She was crying so much I thought she'd bring up her breakfast. Nobody was willing to bring up the subject of pay at the meeting.

english_meaning: To mention or discuss problems or matters from the past that were previously resolved or forgotten. To raise past disputes again.
synonyms: ["Revive disputes","Rehash","Dig up the past","Reopen old wounds"]
example_sentence: Please don't bring up old issues during the family dinner. Every argument turns bad when he brings up old issues. Bringing up old issues will not help us move forward. She promised not to bring up old issues again.

english_meaning: To succeed in doing something difficult or unexpected. To accomplish or achieve something successfully, especially when it is hard or risky.
example_sentence: He brought off a great performance. They brought off the deal after months. The rescue was brought off successfully. She brought off the challenge bravely.

english_meaning: To reveal or publish. To make something appear, show clearly, or publish.
example_sentence: The company brought out a new model. Her smile brings out her beauty. The teacher brought out the best in students. The writer brought out a new book.

english_meaning: A purple, egg-shaped vegetable widely used in cooking. It is a plant of the nightshade family cultivated for its edible fruit. The dark purple or brownish-purple fruit is cooked and eaten as a vegetable. It is also known as eggplant in some regions.
example_sentence: I made a delicious curry using fresh brinjal from the garden. The recipe calls for roasted brinjal mashed with spices. Brinjal can be grilled, fried, or baked in various cuisines. My mother bought some purple brinjal from the vegetable market.

english_meaning: The edge or margin of a steep place or at a critical point. The extreme edge or verge of something, often a situation, condition, or physical place. It can describe the physical edge of a cliff or a metaphorical critical point, such as a crisis or turning point.
example_sentence: Scientists are on the brink of making a major new discovery. He's pulled the company back from the brink (= he has saved it from disaster). Extreme stress had driven him to the brink of a nervous breakdown. Scientists are on the brink of (= extremely close to) a major new discovery. These countries are on the brink of a disastrous famine. The company was on the brink of collapse.

english_meaning: Enthusiasm and individual style. Quality of being active or spirited or alive and vigorous. Energy and confidence. Liveliness or vigor, spirit.
example_sentence: She told her story with some brio. She stepped into her new role with brio. The rest of her declaration is composed with athletic brio. Most academic writers, however, don't really aim for brio. And they must be conducted with confidence and brio. In case of any disputes, the decision of BRIO is final. Her brio astounds everyone.

english_meaning: A short net curtain that covers only the lower half of a window. A café curtain hung across the bottom part of a window for privacy while still letting in light. Literally a wind break, from the French for breaking the breeze.
example_sentence: She hung a white brisebise across the kitchen window. A lace brisebise kept the room private but bright. The café used simple brisebise curtains on every window. He measured the window before ordering a new brisebise.

english_meaning: Quick, busy, energetic, and active. Practical and confident, showing a desire to get things done quickly. Having much high-spirited energy and movement.
example_sentence: His tone became brisk and businesslike. We went for a brisk walk before lunch. He set a brisk pace and we struggled to keep up. Her tone on the phone was brisk (= she spoke quickly and used few words) and businesslike. I took a brisk walk.

english_meaning: Quickly. In a practical and confident way. in a way that shows a desire to get things done quickly. With great speed.
example_sentence: She walked briskly over to the phone and answered it. The game is selling briskly. She walked briskly in the cold air. He rubbed his face briskly with the towel. Walking briskly can burn off a lot of calories.

english_meaning: Short, stiff hair or fiber; also to become annoyed or defensive. A short, stiff hair, especially on animals or on a brush. To stand up stiffly, often because of anger, fear, or cold.
example_sentence: The cat’s bristles stood up when it saw the dog. The brush has hard bristles for cleaning shoes. His skin began to bristle in the cold wind. She bristled at the criticism during the meeting.

english_meaning: A traditional unit of heat energy. The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one pound of liquid water by one degree Fahrenheit at a constant pressure of one atmosphere. Approximately equal to 1,055 joules. A measure commonly used in the power, steam generation, heating, and air conditioning industries. A unit representing the energy content of fuels. The energy equivalent of 252 international calories.
synonyms: ["BTU","Heat Unit","Thermal Energy Unit","1055 Joules","252 Calories","Energy Measure","Power Metric","Heating Capacity","Fuel Energy Value","Caloric Unit","Thermodynamic Unit","Quantitative Heat Measure"]
antonyms: ["Kilowatt-hour","Joule","Ergs","Absolute Zero","Coldness","Lack Of Heat","Cooling Metric","Non-thermal Unit","SI Unit","Metric Energy Unit"]
example_sentence: The air conditioner is rated at twelve thousand British thermal units per hour. Natural gas prices are often quoted per million British thermal units. The technician calculated the total British thermal unit output of the heating system. We need to measure the British thermal unit content of the coal sample.

english_meaning: Hard but easily broken or snapped due to a lack of flexibility. Liable to crack, shatter, or fracture under pressure or stress. Used figuratively to describe a person's emotional state, mood, or temperament as fragile, tense, or easily upset. Describes relationships, systems, or situations that appear stable but could fail suddenly under strain.
example_sentence: The dry leaves had become brittle and crumbled at the slightest touch.  Old glass can be extremely brittle and should be handled with great care.  Her brittle mood made it difficult to discuss the issue calmly.  The brittle ceasefire could collapse at any moment under renewed tension.  His brittle bones meant that even a minor fall could result in a fracture.

english_meaning: To introduce a topic for discussion or to open something. To bring up a subject for the first time, often one that may be sensitive or difficult. To pierce or cut into something, or to open a sealed container such as a barrel. A pointed tool used for piercing or enlarging holes, especially in metalwork.
example_sentence: She finally broached the issue of salary with her manager. He was nervous to broach the topic of climate change at the meeting. The sailor broached the barrel to check the contents. It is not easy to broach personal matters in public.

english_meaning: Wide from one side to the other, having a large distance across. Covering a wide range of subjects, people, or activities. General rather than detailed or specific. Clear, obvious, and easily noticed, as in broad daylight. Of an accent, strongly marked and typical of a particular region. The wide part of something.
example_sentence: The river is very broad at this point. She has a broad knowledge of world history. We agreed on the broad outline of the plan. The robbery happened in broad daylight.

english_meaning: A large flat green bean with a mild, buttery taste. A legume grown in cooler climates and eaten fresh or dried. A vegetable often used in stews, soups, and traditional dishes. A bean known for its high protein and fiber content. A plant cultivated for centuries in the Middle East, Europe, and Asia.
example_sentence: Broad beans are often served with olive oil and lemon. She added fresh broad beans to the stew. Broad beans are a good source of protein for vegetarians. In spring the farmers harvest fresh broad beans.

english_meaning: To transmit programs or information by radio, television, or the internet to a wide audience. To make something widely known by telling many people. To scatter seeds over a large area rather than in rows. A radio or television program that is transmitted. The act of sending out a signal, message, or program to be received by many people.
example_sentence: The news channel will broadcast the speech live tonight. She quickly broadcast the good news to all her friends. Farmers used to broadcast wheat seeds by hand across the field. The morning broadcast covered the results of the election.

english_meaning: In a general way, without considering small details. To a large extent or in most respects. Widely, over a large area or range. With a wide movement of the face, especially when smiling.
example_sentence: Broadly speaking, the plan has been successful. The two reports are broadly similar. The disease has spread broadly across the region. He smiled broadly when he saw his old friend.

english_meaning: A green vegetable with a thick stalk and dense flowering heads. A nutritious cruciferous vegetable eaten steamed, boiled, or stir-fried. The plant grown for these green heads. A vegetable rich in vitamins and fibre.
example_sentence: Steamed broccoli keeps most of its nutrients. He added broccoli florets to the stir-fry. Broccoli grows best in cool weather. The children slowly learned to enjoy broccoli.

english_meaning: A strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one, when speaking English. A type of strong, sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations along the seams. The word can describe a way of speaking that clearly shows a person's regional origin, or a classic style of formal shoe popular in both men's and women's fashion.
example_sentence: He spoke English with a thick Irish brogue. You can recognize him by his Scottish brogue. She bought a pair of brown leather brogues for the office. His brogue made him sound charming and unique. The shop sells handmade brogues in many colors.

english_meaning: A person who buys and sells goods or assets for others. An agent who negotiates business deals. To arrange or negotiate a settlement, agreement, or deal between two parties.
example_sentence: He works as a stockbroker in a leading financial firm. The property broker helped them find a new house. The two countries asked a neutral state to broker peace talks. She brokered a deal between the workers and the management. A good broker always keeps the interests of his client first.

english_meaning: A ruling class dominated by wealthy, powerful men who share close personal bonds. A satirical term for a small group of tech or business bros wielding enormous influence. A government or society controlled by an elite circle of men. A blend of 'bro' and 'oligarchy' used in political commentary. Rule by a boys' club of the ultra-rich.
example_sentence: Critics warn that the country is sliding into a broligarchy. The article described the tech industry as a broligarchy. In a broligarchy, few women reach top positions. Voters accused the party of building a broligarchy.

english_meaning: A commonplace or unoriginal remark, especially one intended to soothe or please. A trite, dull, or boring statement. In chemistry, a compound of bromine with another element or group, formerly used as a sedative. A person who is conventional, dull, or tiresome in conversation. The word can be used both literally in chemistry and figuratively in language.
example_sentence: His speech was full of bromides and offered no real advice. 'Time heals all wounds' is an old bromide. Doctors once prescribed bromides to calm nervous patients. She found the lecture full of dull bromides. Avoid bromides if you want your writing to sound fresh.

english_meaning: The very small airways that branch off from the bronchi inside the lungs. The narrow tubes that carry air to the alveoli. The smallest air passages of the respiratory tree.
example_sentence: The bronchioles carry air deep into the lungs. Asthma causes the bronchioles to narrow. Inflamed bronchioles make breathing difficult for young children. Air finally reaches the alveoli through the bronchioles.

english_meaning: Either of the two main airways that branch from the trachea into the lungs. A large air passage that carries air into and out of a lung. Any of the larger tubes of the airway tree inside the chest.
example_sentence: The trachea divides into a right and a left bronchus. Each bronchus carries air into one lung. Infection of a bronchus can cause a persistent cough. The doctor found a blockage in the right bronchus.

english_meaning: The fear of thunder or thunderstorms. An anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear, discomfort, or panic when hearing thunder or expecting a thunderstorm. It may cause physical reactions such as trembling, sweating, fast heartbeat, and a strong desire to hide or seek shelter.
example_sentence: The child suffers from brontophobia and hides under the bed during storms. Her brontophobia makes her anxious whenever she hears thunder. People with brontophobia avoid going outside during rainy weather. His brontophobia began after a severe thunderstorm in childhood.

english_meaning: An ornament fastened to clothing with a hinged pin and clasp. A decorative jewelled pin worn on a dress, coat, or shawl. A piece of jewellery used both to decorate and to fasten garments.
example_sentence: She wore a silver brooch on the collar of her coat. The antique brooch had belonged to her grandmother. He pinned a small brooch to her shawl as a gift. A diamond brooch sparkled at the neckline of her dress.

english_meaning: To think deeply and sadly about something. To worry continuously about a problem. Of birds, to sit on eggs to keep them warm until they hatch. A group of young birds or animals born at one time. A family or group of children.
example_sentence: He continued to brood over his past mistakes for many years. She sat quietly by the window, brooding about her future. The hen brooded over her eggs carefully. The farmer watched the brood of chicks running around the yard.

english_meaning: To think persistently and worriedly about something; to be preoccupied with anxious thoughts over a subject.
example_sentence: He spent the evening brooding about the argument. She was brooding about whether she had made the right choice. Stop brooding about the past and focus on today. He was brooding about the unfair treatment he had received.

english_meaning: To think long and unhappily about something; to fix the mind anxiously on a subject. Same as 'brood over'.
example_sentence: He brooded on the injustice done to him. She brooded on her lost opportunities for years. Don't brood on things you cannot control. He brooded on the memory of his late father.

english_meaning: To think deeply and unhappily about something for a long time; to dwell on worries or troubles repeatedly.
example_sentence: He brooded over his failure for months. Don't brood over what you cannot change. She brooded over the argument long after it was resolved. Brooding over the past prevents you from moving forward.

english_meaning: To think anxiously or sadly about something for a prolonged period. Essentially the same as 'brood over' or 'brood on'.
example_sentence: She brooded upon the mystery of his sudden disappearance. He brooded upon his mistakes until they consumed him. Do not brood upon what has already happened. She brooded upon the decision all week.

english_meaning: A thin soup made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in water. The liquid in which meat, fish, or vegetables have been cooked. A nutritious clear liquid often used as a base for soups, stews, and sauces. Considered comforting and healthy, especially for those who are sick or recovering. Sometimes used figuratively to refer to a mixture of different elements.
example_sentence: She made a warm chicken broth for her sick son. Add the noodles to the boiling broth and stir well. A good broth is the foundation of many delicious soups. The cook simmered the bones for hours to prepare the broth. He drank a bowl of vegetable broth before dinner.

english_meaning: A house where people go to pay for sexual services. House of prostitution. Whorehouse. Bordello. Red light house. Pleasure house.
example_sentence: The old building was rumored to have once been a brothel. In some countries, a brothel operates legally under government regulation. The novel described life inside a nineteenth century brothel. Authorities shut down the illegal brothel last week.

english_meaning: Behavior or activities associated with a brothel. Lewd, immoral, or vulgar conduct. An archaic word used to describe shameful or indecent practices and the people involved in them. Rarely used in modern English, the term carries strong moral disapproval and refers broadly to debauchery, prostitution, or scandalous behavior.
example_sentence: The preacher condemned all forms of brothelry in his sermon. Old laws were passed to prevent brothelry in the town. The novel describes the brothelry of the corrupt nobles.
