He was ashamed of the brothelry that had taken over the district. Such brothelry has no place in a respectable society.

english_meaning: A feeling of friendship, unity, and mutual support among people. A strong sense of unity, loyalty, and mutual respect among people who share common interests, beliefs, goals, or human values. It is not limited to family relations and often reflects social, religious, or moral bonds.
example_sentence: Brotherhood among the community helped them overcome difficult times. The organization promotes brotherhood and peace across cultures. Brotherhood is essential for maintaining social harmony. Sports can create a strong sense of brotherhood among players.

english_meaning: To mix up, confuse, blur, or make unclear. To scramble or mix physically (food, liquids, objects). To confuse information or signals. To blur understanding or perception. To disturb relationships or communication. To make something unclear or uncertain.
example_sentence: The chef brouilled the eggs before adding spices. The heavy rain brouilled the radio signals. His explanation only brouilled the situation further. The sudden news brouilled their plans for the trip.

english_meaning: Quarrels, disagreements, or fallings-out between people. A French-origin word used in English to describe states of conflict, estrangement, or misunderstanding, often between friends, lovers, or allies. The term suggests minor disputes that disturb a previously good relationship and may or may not be easily resolved.
example_sentence: Their friendship survived many small brouilles over the years. The diplomat tried to settle the brouilles between the two nations. Old brouilles were forgotten at the family reunion. Such brouilles often arise from simple misunderstandings. The letters reveal the brouilles between the famous writers.

english_meaning: A rough or unfinished version of a piece of writing or plan that is not final. A preliminary version of written work, notes, or ideas that are messy, incomplete, or not yet properly organized. It is usually created before the final draft and may contain corrections, deletions, and informal writing. It is commonly used in French and adopted in academic or editorial contexts to mean a draft or rough copy.
example_sentence: I wrote a brouillon of my essay before submitting the final version. The author shared a brouillon of the novel with his editor. Her notebook was full of brouillons for future articles. This document is just a brouillon, not the final report.

english_meaning: The forehead. The arch of hair above each eye, also called the eyebrow. The upper edge or projecting part of something such as a hill or cliff. Used figuratively to refer to facial expressions that show thought, worry, or anger, as in 'a furrowed brow'. A literary and poetic word often used to describe a person's appearance or mood.
example_sentence: She wiped the sweat from her brow with a cloth. He raised his brow in surprise at the news. A deep frown appeared on his brow. They camped on the brow of the hill overlooking the valley. The old man's brow was wrinkled with worry.

english_meaning: To pressure or intimidate someone through harsh words or a threatening manner so they submit or agree. To dominate, intimidate, or force someone to accept an opinion or decision by using aggressive speech, bullying behavior, or strong pressure. It often happens in arguments, debates, or positions of authority where one person tries to overpower another psychologically.
example_sentence: The manager tried to browbeat the employees into accepting the new rules. The lawyer attempted to browbeat the witness during the cross examination. She refused to let anyone browbeat her into changing her decision. Some leaders use fear to browbeat their opponents into silence.

english_meaning: A color produced by mixing red, yellow, and black, similar to that of wood, soil, or chocolate. Having this color. To cook food until it turns brown on the outside. To become brown, especially due to sunlight or heat. Used to describe skin, hair, eyes, or objects of this color. Also a common family name in English-speaking countries.
example_sentence: She has beautiful brown eyes and dark hair. The leaves turned brown in autumn. Brown the onions in oil before adding the meat. He wore a brown suit to the meeting. The bread should be golden brown when fully baked.

english_meaning: A person who flatters others, especially superiors, to gain advantage. Someone who behaves in an insincerely obedient way to win favour. An offensive informal term for a shameless flatterer.
example_sentence: Everyone in the office knew he was a brown noser. She refused to become a brown noser just to get promoted. The team disliked the brown noser who agreed with every order. Being a brown noser rarely earns real respect.

english_meaning: To try to please someone excessively, often to gain advantage. To act in a very flattering or obsequious way toward someone, especially a superior, in order to gain favor or advantage. It often has a negative connotation, suggesting insincerity or manipulation.
example_sentence: He always brown-noses the manager to get a promotion. She’s accused of brown-nosing her teacher to get better grades. Stop brown-nosing and be honest about your opinions. The new employee tried to brown-nose everyone in the office.

english_meaning: A small, rich, usually square chocolate cake. A small mythical helpful fairy or household spirit in folklore. A junior member of the Girl Guides or Girl Scouts in some countries. It can also refer informally to a brown-colored thing or animal.
example_sentence: She baked a tray of warm brownies for the guests. I had a brownie with coffee after lunch. In old stories, a brownie secretly helped with housework at night. Her little sister joined the Brownies last year. The bakery sells walnut brownies every Friday.

english_meaning: An imaginary mark of approval earned by doing something helpful, pleasing, or responsible. Credit gained for good behavior, kindness, effort, or clever action, often in an informal or humorous sense.
example_sentence: He earned brownie points by staying late to finish the report. Bringing flowers may win you a few brownie points at home. She scored brownie points with the teacher by helping a new student. The team gained brownie points for admitting the mistake honestly. I am not doing this for brownie points; I genuinely want to help.

english_meaning: To look at or glance through books, products, websites, or other items in a leisurely or casual way. In animals, to feed on leaves, grass, or plants by grazing or nibbling. An act of looking through items without intent to buy or study deeply.
example_sentence: She browsed the bookstore for interesting novels. I like to browse online shops without buying anything. The deer browsed on the tender leaves in the forest. He browsed through the magazine while waiting.  I had a quick browse through the store. Just a browse, no purchase today.

english_meaning: A software application used to access and view websites on the internet. A program that allows users to navigate the World Wide Web, open websites, display web pages, run web applications, and manage bookmarks and downloads. Examples include Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. It can also refer to a person or animal that casually looks through items or objects, like in a store or in the wild.
example_sentence: I opened my browser to check the latest news. Safari is my favorite browser on the iPhone. The deer is a browser, feeding on leaves and shrubs. He is just a browser, looking around without buying anything.

english_meaning: To injure or damage by hitting or pressure. To cause injury to skin, fruit, or objects by impact, pressure, or rough handling. A dark mark on the skin caused by a hit. A visible injury where blood vessels under the skin are damaged by impact, causing discoloration and tenderness.
example_sentence: He got a bruise on his arm after falling from the bike. The apple was bruised during transport. She covered the bruise with a bandage. The bruise on his leg was very painful. She noticed a bruise on her arm the next day. Rough handling can bruise soft fruit easily.

english_meaning: A meal eaten in the late morning that combines elements of both breakfast and lunch. A social gathering or event where this late morning meal is served to guests. A specific menu style featuring dishes typically associated with mid-morning dining such as eggs and pancakes alongside savory items. The act of eating a late morning meal instead of individual breakfast and lunch sittings. A transitionary time period between early morning and early afternoon often used for relaxed dining.
synonyms: ["Late Breakfast","Early Lunch","Mid-morning Meal","Buffet","Smorgasbord","Dejeuner","Tiffin","Repast","Feast","Elevated Breakfast","Sunday Social","Morning Spread","Light Meal","Combined Meal"]
example_sentence: We decided to meet for a boozy brunch on Sunday morning. The hotel offers a spectacular buffet brunch every weekend. Instead of waking up early, they preferred to sleep in and brunch at noon. The wedding festivities concluded with a farewell brunch for the out-of-town guests.

english_meaning: The main force, impact, or worst part of something unpleasant. The greatest pressure or burden of an attack, blow, or difficult situation. Often used in the phrase 'bear the brunt of' to describe who or what suffers the most from a problem, criticism, or disaster.
example_sentence: The coastal villages bore the brunt of the storm. She faced the brunt of her boss's anger. Small businesses are bearing the brunt of the economic crisis. The soldiers in the front lines took the brunt of the attack. His criticism fell on those who bore the brunt of the work.

english_meaning: A tool with bristles used for cleaning, painting, or grooming. The bushy tail of a fox. A short, light touch against something. A brief unpleasant encounter. To clean, tidy, or touch lightly with a brush or hand.
example_sentence: She cleaned the paint brush carefully. The fox disappeared, its brush flashing in the light. He had a brush with the law in his youth. Brush your teeth twice a day.

english_meaning: To ignore, reject, or dismiss someone’s opinion, suggestion, or concern as unimportant or not worth considering. To pay no attention to something or someone.
example_sentence: The manager brushed aside all the complaints from the workers. She brushed aside his apology and walked away. The government brushed aside the criticism from the media. He brushed aside my advice and did what he wanted.

english_meaning: To remove something (especially dust, dirt, tears, or worries) by brushing lightly with the hand, or to dismiss an idea or feeling as unimportant.
example_sentence: She brushed away the dust from the old photograph. He brushed away his tears and smiled again. The teacher brushed away the student’s excuses. They brushed away all doubts and started the project.

english_meaning: To clean something or someone using a brush, usually to remove dirt, dust, or loose particles. (It can also mean to tidy up a surface, clothes, or an animal’s coat using a brush.)
example_sentence: He brushed down his jacket before entering the office. The groom brushed down the horse after the ride. She brushed down the furniture to make it look neat. The worker brushed down his clothes after finishing the work.

english_meaning: To reject or ignore someone or something casually. (It means not taking something seriously or not giving attention to a person or issue.)
example_sentence: He tried to talk to her, but she brushed him off. The manager brushed off their complaints about the salary. She brushed off the criticism and continued working confidently. The government brushed off the report as unimportant.

english_meaning: To clean, remove, or smooth something by using a brush. To clean something (such as hair, fabric, carpet, or an object) by brushing it to remove dust, dirt, or tangles.
example_sentence: She brushed out her hair before going to bed. The tailor brushed out the dust from the coat. He brushed out the carpet to make it look new. Please brush out the dog’s fur after washing it.

english_meaning: To hide, ignore, or avoid dealing with a problem, mistake, or unpleasant situation, instead of facing it honestly or solving it. To pretend something did not happen or to cover it up so that others do not notice.
synonyms: ["Hide the truth","Cover up","Ignore the problem","Conceal","Sweep under the carpet"]
antonyms: ["Bring to light","Admit the truth","Face the problem","Expose","Deal with openly"]
example_sentence: The company tried to brush the financial mistake under the rug. Instead of fixing the problem, they just brushed it under the rug. You can’t brush the truth under the rug forever, it will come out one day. She brushed her bad behavior under the rug and acted like nothing happened.

english_meaning: To revise or practice something again to become better at it.
example_sentence: I need to brush up my English before the interview. She brushed up her driving skills after many years. The teacher advised the students to brush up their grammar. He brushed up on computer basics for the new job.

english_meaning: To review, refresh, or improve your existing knowledge or skill in a subject that you have learned before but may have forgotten.
example_sentence: I need to brush up on my English before the interview. She brushed up on her driving skills before taking the test. He is brushing up on history for his upcoming exam. You should brush up on your computer skills to get that job.

english_meaning: Speaking or behaving in a very direct, brief, and unfriendly way. So short and abrupt that it may seem rude, even if not intended.
example_sentence: The manager’s brusque reply made the employee feel uncomfortable. He spoke in such a brusque tone that people thought he was angry. Her brusque manners hide a very kind heart. The doctor was brusque, but he gave clear instructions.

english_meaning: Small green vegetables that look like miniature cabbages. Buds that grow along a thick stalk and are eaten cooked. The plant cultivated for these small buds. A winter vegetable usually roasted, boiled, or steamed.
example_sentence: Roasted Brussels sprouts taste sweet and nutty. She halved the Brussels sprouts before cooking. Brussels sprouts are a traditional winter dish. Many people dislike overcooked Brussels sprouts.

english_meaning: Extremely cruel, violent, or harsh. Without mercy or pity. Direct and unpleasant in a way that may hurt others' feelings. Used to describe people, actions, conditions, or experiences that involve severe physical or emotional harm. Can also describe weather, criticism, or competition that is very difficult to endure.
example_sentence: The dictator was known for his brutal treatment of opponents. They survived a brutal winter in the mountains. He gave her a brutal but honest answer. The match was a brutal contest from start to finish. Brutal attacks on civilians shocked the world.

english_meaning: Cruel, violent, and harsh treatment of others. The quality of being brutal. Acts of physical or emotional cruelty, often performed without mercy. Used to describe the behavior of individuals, groups, regimes, or systems that inflict severe suffering. Often appears in discussions of war, crime, oppression, and human rights abuses.
example_sentence: The world condemned the brutality of the regime. Witnesses described the brutality of the attack in shocking detail. Police brutality became a major issue in the country. The novel exposes the brutality of war on ordinary people. Such brutality has no justification under any circumstances.

english_meaning: A person or animal that behaves in a cruel, violent, or uncontrolled way. It often suggests lack of reason or compassion. Extremely cruel, violent, or savage in behavior or action.
example_sentence: He behaved like a brute during the argument. The brute force of the storm destroyed the village. No one liked him because he treated people like a brute. The guard used brute strength to open the jammed gate.

english_meaning: A male deer, antelope, or rabbit. An informal term for a US dollar or money. To oppose or resist something fiercely. To jerk or leap violently, especially of a horse.
example_sentence: A majestic buck walked gracefully through the forest. Can I borrow a buck to buy a coffee? The young employee decided to buck the company trend. The wild horse started to buck as soon as the rider sat on it.

english_meaning: An open container with a handle, used for carrying liquids. The amount that such a container holds. A large quantity of something, especially rain or tears. A group or category into which items are sorted.
example_sentence: She filled a bucket with clean water. He poured two buckets of sand into the mixer. It rained buckets throughout the night. We placed these expenses in a separate bucket.

english_meaning: A plant with triangular seeds used as a grain-like food. The flour or groats made from these seeds, common in pancakes and noodles. A pseudocereal grown in cool climates. A nutritious gluten-free grain substitute.
example_sentence: She made pancakes from buckwheat flour. Buckwheat noodles are popular in Japanese cuisine. Farmers grow buckwheat in cool mountain regions. Buckwheat is a healthy option for those avoiding wheat.

english_meaning: Related to the pleasant aspects of the countryside or rural life. Things associated with the countryside, rural scenery, or simple country life. It often evokes peaceful, pastoral, and charming rural settings.
example_sentence: The artist painted a bucolic landscape with grazing sheep. They enjoyed a bucolic weekend away from the city noise. The novel depicts a bucolic life in the mountains. Her poems often celebrate bucolic scenes and country simplicity.

english_meaning: A compact growth on a plant that develops into a leaf or flower. To begin to develop or grow.
example_sentence: The rose bushes are full of buds ready to bloom. The tree is just starting to bud in the spring warmth. He is a budding young artist with a lot of potential. We must nip this problem in the bud before it gets worse.

english_meaning: A close friend or companion. A partner assigned to work with or look after someone. An informal way of addressing a man, sometimes friendly and sometimes unfriendly. To become friendly with someone, as in buddy up.
example_sentence: He went fishing with his old army buddy. Each new student is given a buddy for the first week. Hey buddy, you dropped your wallet. The two boys buddied up during the summer camp.

english_meaning: To move slightly or make something move a little. To change one’s opinion or position slightly (usually when someone refuses to change). To give way or yield under pressure.
example_sentence: I pushed the door, but it wouldn’t budge. He refused to budge from his decision. The car was stuck in the mud and didn’t budge an inch. Despite all the arguments, she didn’t budge from her opinion.

english_meaning: To move over to make space for someone else, especially on a seat. To shift one's position slightly. To squeeze together to allow another person to sit. To make room by moving a little. Informal request to move a bit.
example_sentence: Could you budge up a little so I can sit? Please budge up and let the kids join us. Everyone budged up on the bench. Budge up, there's plenty of room for one more.

english_meaning: A pale yellowish-brown color like that of soft leather. A strong, soft leather of a dull yellow color. Having a pale brown-yellow color. To polish or shine something by rubbing. A person who is very interested in and knowledgeable about a subject. Physically fit and muscular.
example_sentence: The soldiers wore uniforms of buff color. He buffed the car until it shone like a mirror. She is a real film buff who watches movies every weekend. The envelope was made of thick buff paper.

english_meaning: To reduce impact or soften effect. To protect something by lessening force. To separate and prevent conflict or damage. To store data temporarily before processing. A person or thing that reduces damage between two forces. An additional amount kept to avoid problems. Memory used to hold data temporarily. A solution that keeps pH level stable.
example_sentence: Trees buffer the town from strong winds. The manager tried to buffer the team from criticism. The app buffers data before playing the video. The bushes acted as a buffer against the strong wind. We added extra time as a buffer for delays. The video paused because the buffer was full. The company kept cash as a buffer during the crisis.

english_meaning: An area or space created to separate two things and reduce conflict, risk, or pressure. A neutral or protective area between two groups, places, or situations. It helps prevent direct contact, reduces tension, or provides safety. It can be physical, social, environmental, or even emotional.
example_sentence: The trees were planted as a buffer zone between the highway and the houses. The countries agreed to create a buffer zone to avoid military conflict. Keeping savings acts as a financial buffer zone during emergencies. The manager created a buffer zone in the schedule to handle delays.

english_meaning: To hit repeatedly or to strike with force, especially by wind or waves. To strike or hit something repeatedly and forcefully. A meal where people serve themselves from a variety of dishes placed on a table. It can also mean a long table or counter where food is placed.
example_sentence: We enjoyed a delicious buffet at the wedding. The hotel offers a breakfast buffet every morning. Strong winds buffeted the small boat all night. The company was buffeted by financial problems last year.

english_meaning: A small insect, especially one considered a nuisance. A germ or minor illness caused by infection. A fault or error in a computer program or machine. A hidden microphone used for secret listening. To annoy or irritate someone repeatedly.
example_sentence: A tiny bug was crawling on the kitchen shelf. He caught a stomach bug during the trip. The developer fixed a serious bug in the app. Stop bugging me while I am working.

english_meaning: To leave someone alone or go away, often used as an informal way to tell someone to stop bothering you.
example_sentence: Bug off! I’m trying to concentrate. He told the reporters to bug off. Just bug off and mind your own business. She got annoyed and told them to bug off. I’m busy right now, so why don’t you just bug off?. She waved him away and said, “Bug off!”.

english_meaning: To suddenly leave, especially in a hurry or panic, also, to open one’s eyes wide in surprise. To leave a place suddenly, often due to fear, danger, or urgent circumstances. It can also be used in a military context, meaning to retreat rapidly.
example_sentence: The soldiers bugged out when the alarm sounded. His eyes bugged out when he saw the price. They bugged out before anyone could stop them. We had to bug out fast due to the storm.

english_meaning: To suddenly leave, abandon, or fail someone, often in an unexpected or irresponsible way. To leave a situation abruptly, usually disappointing others. It can also imply acting erratically or unexpectedly.
example_sentence: He bugged out on his friends when trouble started. Don’t bug out on me now!. She bugged out on the project halfway through. They bugged out on the team at the last minute.

english_meaning: To annoy, irritate, or make someone angry. To mess something up, depending on the context, but most commonly it refers to causing annoyance.
example_sentence: His rude comments really bug me up. Don’t bug me up with your complaints. That constant noise is bugging me up. She got bugged up by his behavior.

english_meaning: A baby carriage or stroller. A small open vehicle, sometimes horse-drawn. Something that has many insects. Containing errors or faults. Acting in a strange or irrational way.
example_sentence: The old house was dark and buggy during the summer. This app is still buggy and needs updates. He gave me a buggy explanation that made no sense. She pushed the baby in a buggy through the park.

english_meaning: To make unrealistic plans or dreams that are impossible or not practical. To imagine success or wealth without any real foundation.
example_sentence: He keeps talking about becoming a billionaire without any plan, he’s just building castles in the air. Without proper education and hard work, dreaming of success is like building castles in the air. Don't build castles in the air; make practical goals and start working on them. She spent her time building castles in the air instead of taking real action.

english_meaning: To include something as part of a structure or system. To design or incorporate a feature, function, or quality within something so it is a permanent or integral part
example_sentence: The new software has built-in security features. They built in a pause for discussion. The architect built in extra storage. This plan builds in flexibility

english_meaning: To create or improve something by taking inspiration or material from an existing source. To take an existing idea, work, or situation and expand, improve, or develop new ideas based on it.
example_sentence: The movie builds off the previous series. Let’s build off her ideas. His speech builds off the earlier discussion. We can build off last year’s achievements

english_meaning: To use something as a foundation or basis to develop further. To take an existing idea, achievement, or situation and develop it further or improve it. It often implies progress based on something already established.
example_sentence: The project builds on previous research. Let’s build on our success. His career builds on his early experiences. We can build on this idea for the next plan

english_meaning: To construct, extend, or develop something to reach a complete form. To develop, expand, or complete a structure, system, or plan by adding the necessary parts or infrastructure
example_sentence: The company plans to build out its network. They built out the new office space. We need to build out our online services. The stadium was built out to accommodate more fans

english_meaning: To increase or develop gradually. To strengthen, develop, or accumulate something over time. Can refer to physical, emotional, or abstract things like confidence, tension, or resources.
example_sentence: She is trying to build up her strength after the illness. The city is building up new infrastructure for better transport. His anger built up during the long meeting. Reading daily can build up your vocabulary.

english_meaning: A person whose job is to construct houses and other buildings. A company or contractor engaged in construction work. Someone who develops or strengthens something over time. A tool or program used to create or assemble something.
example_sentence: The builder finished the roof before the rainy season. They hired a local builder to extend the kitchen. He is regarded as the builder of the nation's railway system. The website builder makes designing pages simple.

english_meaning: To swell, stick out, or expand beyond usual limits. It is often used for objects, body parts, or even numbers and statistics. A rounded swelling or protrusion on a surface, object, or body. It can be physical, like a bulge in a wall or pocket, or figurative, like a bulge in prices or population.
example_sentence: The wallet began to bulge because it was full of coins. There was a noticeable bulge in the tire that made driving unsafe. His pockets bulged with papers and notebooks. The report shows a bulge in population growth this year.

english_meaning: Sticking out or swelling outward. Something that pushes outward from its normal shape due to pressure, fullness, or internal force. It is often used for eyes, muscles, walls, bags, or containers that appear swollen or protruding.
example_sentence: His eyes were bulging with surprise when he heard the news. The bag was bulging because it was overfilled. The wall showed bulging signs after heavy rain. The athlete had bulging muscles from years of training.

english_meaning: The mass, size, or volume of something, especially when large. The greater or main part of something. Large quantity, as in buying or selling in bulk. To make something appear larger or more important than it is. Used in commerce, science, and everyday speech to describe quantity or physical mass, and also figuratively for the major share of a group or thing.
example_sentence: The bulk of the work has already been completed. The company buys rice in bulk to save money. The huge bulk of the ship appeared on the horizon. Most of the bulk of his fortune was donated to charity. Heavy clothes can bulk up your appearance in winter.

english_meaning: A person who is very clumsy or careless in a delicate situation. Someone whose rough behavior causes damage or upset. A person lacking tact and grace when handling sensitive matters. Behavior that is destructive or reckless in refined surroundings. Anyone who moves or acts without care for what might break.
example_sentence: He handled the situation like a bull in a china shop. Do not send him to the meeting, he is a bull in a china shop. She entered the discussion like a bull in a china shop and upset everyone. The child ran through the museum like a bull in a china shop.

english_meaning: To clear, demolish, or move using a bulldozer. To force or push through something with great pressure. To intimidate or coerce someone into doing something. To force a decision or plan against opposition. To flatten or destroy completely.
example_sentence: The old buildings were bulldozed to make way for a park. He tried to bulldoze the committee into accepting his plan. Storms bulldozed through the coastal villages. Do not let anyone bulldoze you into a hasty decision.

english_meaning: A short official statement or broadcast giving the latest news or information. A regular printed report or newsletter issued by an organization, institution, or group. A brief news item announced on radio, television, or other media to inform the public about current events. An official announcement made by an authority concerning an important matter such as health, security, or weather.
example_sentence: The news bulletin announced the prime minister’s visit. The hospital issued a daily bulletin about the patient’s condition. Students receive a weekly bulletin from the university. A special bulletin was broadcast after the earthquake. The company publishes a monthly bulletin for its employees.

english_meaning: Feeling confident and hopeful about something, especially about success or improvement in the future. (In finance) Showing expectations that prices in the stock market will rise. Aggressive, forceful, and confident in attitude or behaviour.
example_sentence: Investors remain bullish about the future of the technology sector. The CEO sounded very bullish during the annual meeting. The market is bullish after the latest economic report. He took a bullish stance in the negotiations. Analysts are bullish on the company's new product line.

english_meaning: A large tropical fruit resembling a heart in shape, related to custard apple. A fruit with reddish-brown skin and creamy sweet flesh. A member of the Annona family grown in warm regions. A fruit rich in nutrients and used in traditional desserts. A sweet edible fruit named for its heart-like appearance.
example_sentence: The bullock's heart fruit is sweet and creamy inside. Bullock's heart is often mistaken for custard apple. Farmers grow bullock's heart trees in tropical climates. She tasted bullock's heart for the first time on her trip.

english_meaning: Nonsense or a lie. A rude informal word used for something untrue, foolish, misleading, or said only to impress. To fool someone or talk confidently without knowing the truth. Used to reject something as false or ridiculous.
example_sentence: He was bullshitting about his job experience. Don’t bullshit me; I know the truth. Everything he said was pure bullshit. Don’t believe that bullshit story. Bullshit! That can’t be true. Bullshit! You never met that actor. Bullshit! That excuse makes no sense. Bullshit! That deal is clearly unfair.

english_meaning: A large hairy bee with a loud buzzing sound and a black and yellow striped body. A social bee that is an important pollinator of flowers and crops.
example_sentence: A bumblebee hovered over the purple flowers. Bumblebees are excellent pollinators of tomatoes. The loud bumblebee frightened the little boy. We saw a bumblebee nesting under the shed.

english_meaning: To hit somebody, something by accident. To hit something, especially a part of your body, against or on something. To move across a rough surface. To move somebody from one group or position to another, to remove somebody from a group. The action or sound of something hitting a hard surface.
example_sentence: The car bumped against the kerb. Be careful not to bump your head on the beam when you stand up. The jeep bumped along the dirt track. She entered the subway, bumping her bags down the steps. The airline apologized and bumped us up to first class. We could hear loud bumps from upstairs where the children were playing. He fell to the ground with a bump.

english_meaning: A person who behaves in an overly confident and arrogant manner. A person who talks in a bossy or superior tone, Interrupts others to show off knowledge, shows exaggerated self importance and lacks humility in social setting.
example_sentence: He gave a bumptious speech as if he knew everything about the subject. The bumptious manager refused to listen to his team. Her bumptious attitude made it hard for others to work with her. The young politician sounded confident but slightly bumptious.

english_meaning: Doing something in a clumsy or careless way. Making mistakes because of lack of skill or attention. Handling a task badly and inefficiently. Awkward and incompetent behavior. The act of spoiling something by clumsy work.
example_sentence: His bungling attempt to fix the car made things worse. The bungling of the project cost the company millions. She apologized for her bungling of the presentation. Their bungling efforts amused everyone in the room.

english_meaning: A narrow bed, especially one built like a shelf into a wall, on a ship, train, or in a dormitory. Foolish, insincere, or nonsensical talk; humbug. To sleep in a bunk or to occupy a sleeping place for the night. (Informal) To run away from school, duty, or an obligation without permission.
example_sentence: The children climbed into their bunks and fell asleep. Don’t talk such bunk; nobody believes you. The sailors bunked together below deck. He decided to bunk school and go to the cinema. We had to bunk down in the office during the storm.

english_meaning: A reinforced underground shelter, typically used in wartime to protect people from bombs, shells, or other attacks. A large container or compartment for storing fuel, coal, or other materials, especially on a ship. A sand-filled hollow or hazard on a golf course. To place fuel or supplies in a bunker, or to find oneself in a difficult and seemingly hopeless situation.
example_sentence: The soldiers took cover in the underground bunker. The ship’s fuel bunker was filled before the long voyage. His golf ball landed in the bunker near the green. During the air raid, families rushed into the nearest bunker. The general directed the operation from his command bunker.

english_meaning: Insincere or foolish talk; nonsense. Empty or pretentious speech, especially that made by politicians to please an audience rather than to convey real meaning. Words that sound impressive but actually contain no truth, sense, or value. A statement intended to deceive or flatter rather than to inform.
example_sentence: The minister’s speech was full of bunkum and empty promises. Don’t believe everything he says — most of it is bunkum. Voters are tired of political bunkum before every election. She dismissed the rumours as utter bunkum. His explanation sounded like complete bunkum to the experts.

english_meaning: A person, usually a woman, who behaves in an obsessive, jealous, or dangerously possessive way in a romantic relationship. Someone who becomes emotionally unstable, obsessive, or even threatening after or during a romantic relationship. The term suggests extreme jealousy, controlling behavior, and sometimes harmful actions toward a partner or others connected to them.
antonyms: ["Calm partner","Trusting person","Emotionally stable individual","Independent partner","Easygoing lover"]
example_sentence: After their breakup, he described his ex as a bunny boiler because she kept calling him nonstop. The movie shows how a normal person can turn into a bunny boiler when jealousy takes over. She warned him not to date someone who behaves like a bunny boiler. His friends joked that his clingy behavior was turning him into a bunny boiler. Shah Rukh Khan played a bunny boiler in the film Darr released in 1993.

english_meaning: The ability or tendency of an object to float in a liquid or gas. The upward force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an immersed object. A cheerful, optimistic, and resilient quality of mind that allows a person to recover quickly from difficulties. The ability of an economy, market, or price to rise or recover quickly after a fall.
example_sentence: The buoyancy of the boat kept it afloat in rough seas. Salt water increases the buoyancy of swimmers. Despite many setbacks, she maintained her natural buoyancy of spirit. The buoyancy of the housing market surprised the analysts. Children show a remarkable buoyancy after disappointment.

english_meaning: Able to float on water or in the air. Cheerful, confident, and full of positive energy. Showing a tendency to rise or recover quickly. Describing a market or economy that is doing well and rising. Light enough to keep something else afloat.
example_sentence: Wood is buoyant, so it floats easily on water. She was in a buoyant mood after receiving the good news. The housing market remained buoyant throughout the year. The life jacket keeps swimmers buoyant in deep water.

english_meaning: Difficult to bear because it involves much effort, worry, or expense. Causing hardship or trouble to the person who must deal with it. Heavy and tiring to carry or manage. Imposing an unwelcome duty or responsibility.
example_sentence: The new taxes proved burdensome for small businesses. Caring for the estate became burdensome over time. She found the paperwork increasingly burdensome. Long working hours were burdensome for the whole family.

english_meaning: To grow or develop quickly and vigorously. To begin to grow or increase rapidly; to flourish. To send forth new buds, leaves, or branches, as a plant in spring. To expand and thrive in numbers, size, or importance.
example_sentence: The city’s population began to burgeon after the new industries opened. Wildflowers burgeon across the meadows in spring. Online businesses have burgeoned during the past decade. Her talent burgeoned under the guidance of a skilled mentor. Demand for electric vehicles is burgeoning worldwide.

english_meaning: A person who illegally enters a place to steal. A person who breaks into a house, shop, or building without permission, usually at night, with the intention of stealing money or valuables.
example_sentence: The burglar broke into the house while the family was asleep. Police caught the burglar near the jewelry shop. The alarm scared the burglar away. He was arrested for being a repeat burglar

english_meaning: The crime of illegally entering a building, usually a house or shop, with the intention of stealing. The act of breaking into premises to commit theft or another serious offence. A criminal offence in which a person enters another's property unlawfully. Housebreaking for the purpose of robbery.
example_sentence: There has been a sharp rise in burglary cases in the city. The police arrested two men for the burglary at the jewellery shop. Their house was the target of a burglary last week. He was sentenced to five years in prison for burglary. The insurance policy covers loss caused by burglary.

english_meaning: A deep red color like that of red wine. A dark purplish-red shade. Red wine from the Burgundy region of France. Having a dark wine-red color.
example_sentence: She chose a burgundy lipstick for the evening. The curtains were a rich burgundy shade. He ordered a bottle of Burgundy with dinner. The autumn leaves turned a deep burgundy.

english_meaning: The act or ceremony of placing a dead body in a grave or tomb. The formal disposal of a corpse in the earth or at sea. A place where a body has been buried. The act of covering or hiding something completely under the ground or under other material.
example_sentence: The burial took place early the next morning. Archaeologists discovered an ancient burial site. His family arranged a quiet burial in the village. The burial of the cables under the road took two weeks.

english_meaning: To be destroyed, consumed, or removed completely by fire, heat, or strong emotion.
example_sentence: The old papers burned away in the fire. His anger slowly burned away after he heard the truth. The candle burned away until only wax remained. All her fears burned away as she gained confidence.

english_meaning: To destroy a relationship, opportunity, or connection permanently so that it cannot be used again in the future. To act in a way that makes it impossible to return to a previous state, job, friendship, or position.
example_sentence: He burned his bridges when he resigned angrily. He left the company angrily and burned his bridges with his manager. If you insult your teammates, you will burn bridges and lose their support. She didn’t want to burn bridges with her old friends, so she left politely. Quitting without notice is like burning bridges with your employer.

english_meaning: To destroy something completely by fire, especially a building or structure. It can also mean that something burns until it is reduced to ashes.
example_sentence: The old factory burned down after a short circuit. The villagers watched helplessly as the barn burned down. Firefighters prevented the school from burning down completely. The wooden house burned down within minutes.

english_meaning: To feel a strong desire, passion, or longing for someone or something. To be filled with intense emotion such as love, ambition, or anger. To have an inner drive or motivation that feels powerful and consuming.
synonyms: ["Long for","Yearn for","Crave","Desire","Thirst for","Ache for","Be eager for"]
example_sentence: She burns for success in her career. He burns for the woman he loves. They burn for justice after years of silence. I burn for a chance to prove my abilities.

english_meaning: To make a deep and lasting mark on something, especially by heat or fire. To leave a strong or permanent effect on someone’s mind, memory, or feelings.
example_sentence: The tragic scene was burned into his memory forever. The logo was burned into the wood with a hot iron. Her words burned into his heart, and he never forgot them. The smell of smoke burned into my clothes after the fire.

english_meaning: To remove, destroy, or get rid of something by burning. To use energy or calories through physical activity. When fog, mist, or clouds disappear due to heat or sunlight. To burn a thin layer or unwanted material from a surface.
example_sentence: The morning sun will burn off the fog soon. He goes jogging every day to burn off extra calories. The fire burned off the dry grass around the field. She tried to burn off her frustration by exercising.

english_meaning: To take an action that makes it impossible to return to an earlier position. To damage relationships or opportunities permanently. To act in a way that removes any backup option. To commit fully to a decision by eliminating alternatives. To create a situation where reversal is not possible
synonyms: ["Cut ties","Sever relations","Break connections","Close the door","Cut off","End relations permanently"]
antonyms: ["Keep options open","Maintain relations","Preserve ties","Stay connected","Leave the door open"]
example_sentence: He burned his bridges with his boss by arguing loudly in public. She burned her bridges when she quit her job without notice. If you insult your partners, you may burn your bridges with them. He burned his bridges and moved abroad without any plan to return.

english_meaning: To do something that cannot be undone, leaving no way to go back; to commit oneself completely to a course of action by eliminating all other options.
synonyms: ["Irreversible decision","Commit completely","Cut off all escape routes","Take a bold step"]
antonyms: ["Reversible decision","Keep options open","Play it safe","Stay undecided"]
example_sentence: He burned his boats by resigning. When he left his secure job to start his own business, he really burned his boats. She burned her boats by telling her boss she would never return to the company. Once the soldiers destroyed the bridge behind them, they had burned their boats. By investing all his savings in that project, he burned his boats completely.

english_meaning: To be exhausted or stop functioning due to too much work or use. To lose interest, motivation, or energy after continuous effort.
example_sentence: She burned out after working 14-hour days. The teacher felt completely burned out by the end of the school year. The motor burned out after running all night. If you never take a break, you will burn out sooner or later.

english_meaning: To destroy any possibility of returning to a previous situation or relationship. To make a decision that prevents going back to an earlier option. To act in a way that permanently damages relationships or opportunities. To commit fully to a new path by removing all alternatives. To cut off connections intentionally, often after conflict or strong disagreement
synonyms: ["Cut ties","Sever relations","Break off connections","Close the door on something","Cut off completely"]
example_sentence: He burned the bridges with his boss when he left the job angrily. By speaking harshly to his friends, he burned the bridges forever. She burned the bridges behind her and started a new career abroad. If you quit without notice, you may burn the bridges with your employer.

word: Burn the candle at both ends
english_meaning: To work or stay active for very long hours without enough rest, often by being busy early in the morning and late at night. It suggests overworking in a way that cannot be sustained for long and may harm health or performance.
synonyms: ["Overwork oneself","Exhaust oneself","Work day and night","Push oneself too hard"]
antonyms: ["Take it easy","Rest properly","Maintain balance","Work at a steady pace"]
example_sentence: She has been burning the candle at both ends to finish the project on time. If you keep burning the candle at both ends, you will fall sick. During exams, many students burn the candle at both ends and ignore their health. He burned the candle at both ends by working all day and studying all night.

english_meaning: To work late into the night.
example_sentence: Ali is burning the midnight oil to prepare for exams. She burned the midnight oil to finish her project.

english_meaning: To destroy something completely by fire. To mean total destruction or ruin of something (such as a plan, idea, or organization).
example_sentence: The old factory was burned to the ground after the fire spread overnight. The villagers watched helplessly as their homes burned to the ground. The scandal burned the company to the ground, leaving its reputation in ashes. The rebels burned the palace to the ground during the war.

english_meaning: To be completely destroyed by fire or heat. To use a lot of energy or fuel. To make someone very angry. To become very hot (especially body temperature).
example_sentence: The old papers burned up quickly in the fire. You will burn up if you stand in the sun too long. He burned up with anger when he heard the bad news. The rocket burns up as it enters the Earth’s atmosphere.

english_meaning: To be filled with a strong feeling such as anger, jealousy, or excitement. To feel intense anger or rage. To be very jealous of someone. To become extremely excited or enthusiastic. To be strongly affected emotionally. To become emotionally intense. To react strongly to something
synonyms: ["Boil with","Filled with","Overcome by","Consumed by","Inflamed with","Tormented by"]
example_sentence: He was burning up with anger after hearing the unfair decision. She was burning up with jealousy when she saw them together. The child is burning up with fever and needs to rest. He was burning up with shame after realizing his mistake.

english_meaning: To feel a very strong emotion such as anger, jealousy, shame, desire, or enthusiasm.
synonyms: ["Be filled with","Be consumed by","Be overwhelmed with","Be inflamed with","Seethe with"]
example_sentence: He burned with anger when he heard the unfair decision. She burned with jealousy after seeing his success. They burned with enthusiasm to start their new project. He burned with shame for his rude behavior.

english_meaning: Having had a bad or painful experience before, making someone cautious, distrustful, or unwilling to take the same risk again. It means that a person has previously suffered disappointment, betrayal, failure, loss, or emotional pain. Because of that experience, they become careful, hesitant, or reluctant to trust people or repeat similar actions. The expression often refers to relationships, business, friendships, investments, or any situation where someone learned a difficult lesson.
synonyms: ["Deceived before","Let down previously","Hurt in the past","Had one's fingers burned"]
example_sentence: She is burned in the past, so she takes time before trusting new people. After losing money in a scam, he was burned in the past and now checks every investment carefully. They were burned in the past, which is why they prefer written agreements. Being burned in the past has made her stronger and wiser when making important decisions.

english_meaning: A dark reddish-brown color made by heating ochre pigment. A deep orange-brown shade used in painting. An earthy color resembling roasted clay.
example_sentence: The artist used burnt ochre for the desert landscape. The walls were painted in a warm burnt ochre tone. Burnt ochre gave the pottery an earthy appearance. She mixed burnt ochre with white to soften the color.

english_meaning: A dark reddish-brown pigment made by roasting raw sienna. A rich brownish-red color used by artists. A warm earthy shade between red and brown.
example_sentence: The painter used burnt sienna for the tree trunks. Her autumn coat was a beautiful burnt sienna color. Burnt sienna is a favorite color in oil painting. The bricks were a deep burnt sienna in the evening light.

english_meaning: A dark brown pigment made by heating raw umber. A deep, rich brown color used in painting. A dark earthy brown shade.
example_sentence: The artist shaded the portrait with burnt umber. The wooden door was stained a deep burnt umber. Burnt umber gives warmth to landscape paintings. She chose burnt umber tones for the living room decor.

english_meaning: To expel gas from the stomach through the mouth, often making a sound. It usually happens after eating or drinking. It can also mean helping a baby release trapped gas by gently patting their back. Informally, it may describe a short interruption in sound or movement.
example_sentence: After drinking soda, he let out a loud burp. The mother gently burped the baby after feeding. Excuse me, that burp was unexpected. The speaker made a strange burp sound during the call.

english_meaning: A small, fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between moving parts of the body. A cushion-like pouch found between bones, tendons, muscles, or skin. A structure that allows tissues to glide smoothly over one another near a joint. A sac that can become painfully inflamed through pressure or overuse.
example_sentence: Kneeling for hours inflamed the bursa in his knee. A bursa reduces friction where a tendon rubs against bone. The doctor drained fluid from the swollen bursa. Each shoulder contains a bursa that helps the joint move freely.

english_meaning: Try to avoid a difficult situation. To deliberately ignore or refuse to acknowledge something unpleasant, difficult, or threatening, hoping it will go away on its own.
synonyms: ["Ignore reality","Avoid the truth","Neglect","Turn a blind eye","Refuse to acknowledge"]
antonyms: ["Face the facts","Confront reality","Deal with the problem","Accept the truth","Acknowledge"]
example_sentence: Instead of facing his debts, he just buried his head in the sand and ignored the bills. Leaders cannot bury their heads in the sand when it comes to climate change.

english_meaning: To put an end to fighting or conflict. To make peace and become friendly again after an argument or disagreement. To stop arguing or fighting and reconcile with someone. To forgive and forget past disagreements and restore friendship.
example_sentence: After years of rivalry, the two friends decided to bury the hatchet. It’s time we bury the hatchet and work together again. The brothers finally buried the hatchet after their long family dispute. The countries buried the hatchet and signed a peace treaty.

english_meaning: In a busy, active, or occupied manner. With energetic and continuous attention to work or a task. In a way that involves many activities or purposeful movement.
example_sentence: The bees buzzed busily among the flowers. She worked busily at her desk all morning. The staff were busily preparing the hall for the ceremony. Children moved busily between the different activity tables.

english_meaning: The activity of producing, buying, or selling goods or services, usually for profit. A commercial organization, company, shop, or enterprise. A person’s regular occupation, profession, trade, or work. A matter, task, situation, or responsibility that concerns someone. The amount of commercial activity or customer demand. Serious work or action rather than amusement. An affair that is private or not another person’s concern. A group of related commercial dealings or a particular industry.
example_sentence: She started a small business selling handmade jewelry. Tourism is an important business in this region. Please finish your business before the office closes. How he spends his savings is none of my business.

english_meaning: A sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. It also refers to a period of economic difficulty, a police raid, or the act of breaking something. As an action, it means to break, smash, or arrest someone.
example_sentence: A beautifully carved marble bust of the famous emperor sits elegantly in the library. The police executed a massive drug bust at the abandoned coastal warehouse. During the painful economic bust, many long-standing businesses were forcibly closed forever. He bravely promised he would bust the heavy lock if nobody could quickly find the key. This grand new festival project turned out to be a complete and utter financial bust.

word: Bust a cap in someone's ass
english_meaning: To shoot or attack someone (usually with a gun). Often used as a threat or expression of anger. It can also be used jokingly among friends to mean “punish” or “teach someone a lesson,” but literally it refers to firing a bullet at a person.
example_sentence: He threatened to bust a cap in his enemy’s ass. The gangster threatened to bust a cap in his rival’s ass. He was so angry he said he’d bust a cap in the thief’s ass. The movie scene showed a man busting a cap in the villain’s ass. They were just joking when they said they’d bust a cap in his ass.

english_meaning: To end a relationship, friendship, or partnership. To break or damage something badly. To interrupt or stop something suddenly. To disperse a group of people. To ruin plans or arrangements.
example_sentence: They decided to bust up after many arguments. The business partners busted up last year. The storm busted up several boats. The kids busted up the old chair while playing.

english_meaning: A serious argument, quarrel, fight, or breakup between people. An informal word used when two or more people have a major disagreement, emotional argument, physical fight, or separation in a relationship, friendship, or partnership.
example_sentence: They had a big bust-up over money issues. The business partners ended their partnership after a bust-up. She stopped talking to her friend after their bust-up. A bust-up broke out during the meeting.

english_meaning: Problem solver. Tough guy. Powerful machine. Crime fighter. Nickname for a young boy. A thing that destroys obstacles. An informal word used for a person or thing that breaks, destroys, defeats, or stops something.
example_sentence: The new medicine is a pain buster. He became a crime buster in the city. Hey, buster, come here for a minute. She is a myth buster on social media. The team was known as a record buster.

english_meaning: To hurry or move energetically. A state of lively movement, noise, or activity, often involving many people doing things at the same time. An atmosphere or scene full of active movement and excitement.
example_sentence: The market was full of bustle early in the morning. She bustled around the kitchen preparing dinner. There was a lot of bustle at the railway station before sunset. Office workers bustled through the streets during lunch hour.

english_meaning: Full of busy activity, movement, noise, and energy. A place or environment that is lively, crowded, active, and full of movement. It is often used for markets, streets, cities, offices, and public places where many people are working, talking, or moving around energetically.
example_sentence: The bustling market was filled with shoppers and street vendors. Karachi is a bustling city with heavy traffic and active business centers. We enjoyed walking through the bustling streets during the festival. The restaurant remained bustling even late at night.

english_meaning: A person who is always working hard and staying active. Someone who is constantly occupied with many tasks. A hardworking and industrious individual. A person who cannot sit still and keeps busy. Someone admired for their productivity and energy.
example_sentence: My mother is a busy bee around the house every morning. She is such a busy bee that she never takes a break. The office is full of busy bees before the deadline. Even on holidays, he is a busy bee in his garden.

english_meaning: A person who interferes in other people's affairs. Someone overly curious about matters that do not concern them. A meddler who gossips or pries into private lives. An officious individual who cannot mind their own business.
example_sentence: The neighborhood busybody knew everyone's secrets. Stop being a busybody and mind your own work. She is such a busybody that no one shares news around her. Every office has at least one busybody.

english_meaning: Used to introduce a contrast with what has already been said. Except; other than. However; on the contrary. Only; no more than, as in 'she is but a child'. An objection or difficulty, used as a noun.
example_sentence: She is young but very capable. Everyone left but him. I would help, but I am busy today. No buts about it, the work must be finished today.

english_meaning: To kill animals for meat. To kill people brutally or carelessly. To ruin something through bad performance (for example to butcher a song). A person whose job is cutting up and selling meat in a shop. A person who kills animals for meat. A cruel or brutal killer.
example_sentence: The butcher cut the meat into small pieces for the customer. A skilled butcher knows how to prepare every part of the animal. The army was accused of butchering innocent people during the war. He completely butchered the speech by forgetting the main points.

english_meaning: To hit or push somebody, something hard with your head. To interrupt convention rudely. The part of a finished cigarette that has not been smoked. The thick end of a rifle. A person who is joked about or laughed at. A large round container for storing or collecting liquids. The part of the body that you sit on. The act of hitting somebody with your head.
example_sentence: How can I explain if you keep butting in. She was the butt of some very unkind jokes. Get off your butt and do some work!. She told him to get off his butt and do something useful. They struck him with their rifle butts. He was fed up with being the butt of their jokes. She often butted heads with school officials in disagreements over her teaching methods.

english_meaning: To interrupt or interfere in others’ talk or actions. (It usually shows rudeness or lack of manners.)
example_sentence: Please don’t butt in while I’m talking. He always butts in when others are having a private conversation. I didn’t mean to butt in, but I thought I could help. She hates when people butt in on her decisions.

english_meaning: To stop interfering in someone else’s business, mind your own business. Informal and sometimes rude way to tell someone not to involve themselves.
example_sentence: This is private, butt out!. He told them to butt out of his business. He told me to butt out of his personal affairs. You should butt out before you make things worse. I wish my neighbor would butt out of my family matters. She told her coworkers to butt out of her project.

english_meaning: An isolated hill with steep sides and a flat top. A small flat-topped landform, usually smaller than a mesa, shaped by erosion.
example_sentence: A red butte rose above the desert floor. We camped near the base of the butte. Wind and rain slowly shaped the butte. The flat top of the butte was visible for miles.

english_meaning: A soft yellow or white food made by churning cream or milk. A butter-like substance made from nuts, seeds, or fruit. To spread butter on food. To flatter someone excessively, especially to gain a favor. In informal use, to defeat or succeed against someone easily.
example_sentence: She spread butter on a warm slice of bread. This recipe uses almond butter instead of dairy butter. Please butter the baking dish before adding the mixture. He tried to butter up his supervisor before asking for leave.

english_meaning: To flatter someone excessively to gain a favor or advantage. To win someone’s favor through insincere praise. To manipulate someone using compliments.
example_sentence: He tried to butter the teacher up before asking for extra marks. She is always buttering up her boss to get promotions. Don’t butter me up, just tell me what you want. They buttered him up so he would agree to their plan.

english_meaning: To praise or flatter someone too much in order to gain favor, advantage, or approval. To gain someone’s support through praise. To speak nicely for selfish benefit. To impress someone with fake admiration. To use flattery as a tool for advantage.
example_sentence: He tried to butter up the manager before asking for a promotion. The student buttered up the teacher to get extra marks. She keeps buttering up her parents whenever she wants money. You do not need to butter up people to make friends.

word: Butter wouldn't melt in someone's mouth
english_meaning: Said of a person who looks completely innocent but may not be. Used to suggest that someone's harmless appearance hides mischief or guilt. Describing a falsely modest or overly sweet manner. Used ironically about a child or adult behaving suspiciously well. Referring to a person who seems too good to be true.
example_sentence: He sat there quietly as if butter wouldn't melt in his mouth. She looks as though butter wouldn't melt in her mouth, but she planned the whole prank. The boy smiled sweetly, butter wouldn't melt in his mouth. Don't be fooled by that innocent face; butter wouldn't melt in her mouth.

english_meaning: A feeling of nervousness or excitement in the stomach before an important or stressful event. Nervous excitement before an event. Anxiety mixed with anticipation. Emotional tension felt physically in the stomach. Light fear or thrill before something important.
example_sentence: I always get butterflies in my stomach before giving a speech. She had butterflies in her stomach before her job interview. He felt butterflies in his stomach when he saw his crush. There were butterflies in my stomach while waiting for the exam results.

english_meaning: A day-flying insect with large, often brightly coloured wings. The adult stage that develops from a caterpillar through a pupa. A person who moves from one interest or person to another without commitment. A swimming stroke in which both arms move forward together.
example_sentence: A colourful butterfly settled on the flower. The caterpillar finally turned into a butterfly. He is a social butterfly who knows everyone. She won the hundred metres butterfly race.

english_meaning: The idea that a very small change can eventually cause large and unpredictable consequences. In chaos theory, the sensitive dependence of a system on its initial conditions. A minor action whose effects grow through a complex chain of events.
example_sentence: The story explores the butterfly effect of one missed train. A tiny coding error produced a butterfly effect across the system. Chaos theory often illustrates the butterfly effect through weather patterns. Her casual introduction had a butterfly effect on their lives.

english_meaning: Either of the two rounded fleshy parts of the body on which a person sits. The muscular area at the lower back of the body below the hips. The rear part of the body forming the seat.
example_sentence: He fell and injured his left buttock. The nurse gave the injection in the buttock. Sitting for long hours can cause pain in the buttocks. The exercise strengthens the muscles of the buttocks.

english_meaning: A small, round, white or pale brown mushroom with a mild taste. The most commonly cultivated edible mushroom. A fungus used in soups, sauces, and stir-fries. A vegetable-like ingredient eaten raw or cooked.
example_sentence: She sliced button mushrooms into the pasta sauce. Button mushrooms are sold in every supermarket. He sauteed the mushrooms with butter and garlic. Fresh button mushrooms should feel firm and dry.

english_meaning: Plump, healthy, and attractive in appearance, especially used to describe a woman with a full and shapely figure. Lively, cheerful, and full of vigour. Having a pleasantly rounded form. (Archaic) Obedient, yielding, or compliant.
example_sentence: The painter often portrayed buxom village women working in the fields. She was a buxom, cheerful woman who laughed easily. The buxom waitress greeted every guest with a smile. He described his grandmother as a buxom lady full of life. The novel’s heroine is a buxom young farmer’s daughter.

english_meaning: A low, continuous humming sound made by insects or machines. A feeling of excitement, energy, or pleasant intoxication. A rumor or piece of news that is spreading quickly. To make a low humming sound. To call someone using a buzzer or intercom.
example_sentence: There was a loud buzz of bees near the flowers. A buzz of excitement filled the stadium. There is a buzz that the company will launch a new product. Please buzz me when the guest arrives.

english_meaning: Making a low, continuous humming or vibrating sound like that of a bee. Filled with lively activity, excitement, or energy. Feeling a sense of thrill, excitement, or pleasant tingling. Spreading quickly through talk, rumor, or gossip. Slightly intoxicated or lightheaded.
example_sentence: The bees were buzzing around the garden all afternoon. The city was buzzing with excitement before the festival. She felt her phone buzzing in her pocket. The office was buzzing with rumors about the new manager.

english_meaning: Before long; after a short time. Gradually, as time passes. At some point in the near future.
synonyms: ["Soon","Shortly","Presently","Before long","In due course","Eventually","Gradually","After a while","In time","Later on"]
example_sentence: By and by, the noise of the crowd faded away. Don't worry; things will improve by and by. By and by, she learned to enjoy her new city. The clouds cleared by and by and the sun appeared.

english_meaning: On the whole. Everything considered. In general terms, without considering specific details.
example_sentence: By and large, the project was a great success. By and large, people are friendly in this town. The weather here is quite pleasant by and large. By and large, students performed very well in the final exam.

english_meaning: Done as a favor, permission, or acknowledgment of someone’s help or permission. Used to indicate that something is provided, done, or allowed out of politeness, permission, or respect. It often implies that the action is not required but offered as a courtesy or favor.
example_sentence: The pictures have been reproduced by courtesy of British museum. The document was provided by courtesy of the library. By courtesy of his manager, he attended the meeting. The photograph is used by courtesy of the artist. She was invited to the event by courtesy of the organizers.

english_meaning: By continuing to do a particular action, usually with great effort. Through the process of repeatedly performing something. As a result of persistent activity or practice. By managing to do something over a period of time.
synonyms: ["By means of","Through","As a result of","Owing to","By virtue of","Thanks to"]
example_sentence: By dint of working late every night, he met the deadline. She learned the language by dint of listening to the radio daily. By dint of saving carefully, they bought their first home. He passed the exam by dint of studying every weekend.

english_meaning: By means of something, especially through great effort or persistence. As a result of a particular quality, action, or force. Because of the power or influence of something. Through the use of a particular method or means.
synonyms: ["By means of","Through","Owing to","Because of","By virtue of","As a result of","Thanks to"]
example_sentence: By dint of hard work, she finished the project on time. He succeeded by dint of sheer determination. The team won by dint of superior fitness. By dint of long practice, he became an excellent speaker.

english_meaning: By a great amount or margin. Used to emphasise that something is much greater or better than the rest. Very much, when comparing two or more things. Beyond any doubt or comparison.
example_sentence: This is by far the best restaurant in the city. She is by far the strongest player on the team. The new model is by far more efficient than the old one. His speech was by far the most memorable of the evening.

english_meaning: Irregularly. Not in a steady or consistent way. Something that happens for a short time, then stops, and then starts again
example_sentence: He studies by fits and starts, sometimes for hours, then not at all for days. The construction work progressed by fits and starts due to funding issues. Her efforts to learn French continued by fits and starts, so she never became fluent. Our internet connection works by fits and starts, making it hard to watch videos.

english_meaning: By any means possible, whether fair or unfair; to achieve something no matter what it takes. To do something by any method, right or wrong, legal or illegal, fair or unfair.
example_sentence: He decided to pass the exam by hook or by crook. They wanted to win the match by hook or by crook. She said she would get the job by hook or by crook. He managed to reach the top by hook or by crook.

english_meaning: Something happening very quickly and in large amounts of progress or improvement. Very fast progress or rapid improvement over a short period of time.
example_sentence: The city has grown by leaps and bounds in the last decade. Her English speaking skills are improving by leaps and bounds. Technology is advancing by leaps and bounds these days. The company’s profits increased by leaps and bounds after the new policy.

english_meaning: To follow rules, laws, or instructions exactly as they are written, without bending them. Doing something strictly according to official rules, procedures, or instructions without making changes, shortcuts, or personal interpretations. It often suggests discipline, fairness, or sometimes a lack of flexibility.
synonyms: ["By the rules","According to procedure","Strictly following rules","Officially","Precisely","Textbook style"]
example_sentence: The police officer handled the investigation by the book. She always works by the book and never takes shortcuts. The company follows safety rules by the book. If you do everything by the book, you will avoid mistakes.

word: By the skin of your teeth
english_meaning: To narrowly succeed or escape from danger. To achieve something with the very smallest margin, almost failing but still managing.
example_sentence: He passed by the skin of his teeth. We caught the train by the skin of our teeth; the doors were just about to close. She escaped the burning building by the skin of her teeth, just seconds before it collapsed. The football team won the match by the skin of their teeth, scoring the winning goal in the last minute.

english_meaning: This phrase is used to introduce a new, less important topic into a conversation. It serves as a casual transition to mention something incidentally without breaking the overall flow. Speakers use it when they suddenly remember something they want to add. It effectively shifts the current flow of discussion to an unrelated but relevant side note.
synonyms: ["Incidentally","Apropos","Speaking of which","In passing","As an aside","While on the subject","Casually","Parenthetically"]
example_sentence: I really enjoyed the movie, and by the way, the soundtrack was absolutely fantastic. By the way, did you happen to see my keys on the kitchen counter? We are going to the mall later; by the way, you are more than welcome to join us. Oh, by the way, your mother called while you were in the meeting.

english_meaning: An informal way of saying goodbye when leaving or ending a conversation. In sports, a situation in which a player or team advances to the next round without playing because there is no opponent. A short form of farewell.
example_sentence: She waved and said bye before getting on the bus. Bye, see you tomorrow at the office. Our team got a bye in the first round of the tournament. He quickly said bye and rushed out of the door.

english_meaning: A road that passes around a town or city rather than through it. A secondary channel or connection that diverts the flow around something. To go around or avoid something. To ignore or circumvent a rule, procedure or person. A surgical operation to redirect blood flow around a blocked artery.
example_sentence: We took the bypass to avoid the city traffic. He tried to bypass the official procedure. The new bypass has reduced congestion in the town centre. The patient underwent a successful heart bypass surgery. You cannot bypass the security check at the airport.

english_meaning: A person who is present at an event or incident but does not take part in it. An onlooker or witness who watches something happen without becoming involved. A spectator who happens to be at the scene of an occurrence by chance.
example_sentence: Several bystanders rushed to help the injured man. The police questioned the bystanders about the accident. An innocent bystander was hit by a stray bullet. The bystanders watched in silence as the fire spread. He was an unfortunate bystander caught in the chaos.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information that usually consists of eight bits. The amount of memory needed to store a single character of text. A basic unit used to measure the size of files and computer storage. A group of binary digits processed as one unit by a computer.
example_sentence: One byte is normally made up of eight bits. Each letter you type takes about one byte of memory. The program reads the file one byte at a time. Storage capacity is usually measured in bytes.

english_meaning: A highly contagious respiratory disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. A global pandemic that emerged in 2019. An infectious illness with symptoms ranging from mild to severe. A disease that led to worldwide health and economic crises.
example_sentence: COVID-19 vaccines have saved millions of lives. Social distancing helped reduce COVID-19 transmission. He tested positive for COVID-19. The COVID-19 pandemic changed the world.

english_meaning: A small group of people who plan secretly to do something, especially in politics. A secret political clique or faction working against established authority. A private intrigue or conspiracy carried out by a small group. To form or take part in such a secret group or plot.
example_sentence: A cabal of senior officers tried to overthrow the government. The decision was taken by a small cabal within the party. Historians describe the ministers as a cabal that ruled behind the king. They were accused of cabaling against their own leader. A secret cabal of investors controlled the entire market.

english_meaning: A cultivated plant with thick green or purple leaves surrounding a spherical heart or head. It is eaten as a vegetable, either raw in salads or cooked in various dishes. The leafy biennial plant is grown as an annual crop for its dense-leaved heads. It is a staple ingredient in dishes like coleslaw and kimchi.
synonyms: ["Head Cabbage","Red Cabbage","Savoy Cabbage","Kale","Collard Greens","Bok Choy","Greens","Cruciferous Vegetable","Cole","Napa Cabbage"]
example_sentence: She shredded a small head of cabbage to make homemade coleslaw. Cabbage is a very nutritious and inexpensive vegetable to include in your diet. The farmer harvested the cabbage just before the first frost arrived. Fermented cabbage is the main ingredient in traditional German sauerkraut.

english_meaning: A piece of furniture with shelves or drawers that is used for storing or displaying objects. A small group of senior government officials who advise the head of state and help make important decisions. A cupboard with a door or doors that is often built into a wall or used in a kitchen or bathroom. A private room or small apartment where meetings were historically held. The case or box that contains a piece of electronic equipment like a radio or television.
example_sentence: He installed a new medicine cabinet in the bathroom to organize his supplies. The Prime Minister called an emergency meeting of the cabinet to discuss the crisis. She keeps her fine china displayed in a glass-fronted wooden cabinet. The computer's internal components are protected by a sturdy metal cabinet.

english_meaning: A hidden or secure store of things, especially weapons, food, money, or valuables, kept for future use. A collection of items of the same type stored in a hidden or inaccessible place. (Computing) A part of a computer’s memory where information is kept so that it can be quickly accessed. To store something in a cache or hide it in a secure place.
