example_sentence: I can't think of a catchy name for my blog.  The new slogan isn't as catchy as the old one. Professor Hartman's exams always include at least one catchy question.

english_meaning: To reach someone who is ahead. To meet someone after a while and talk about what’s new To face consequences of one’s actions
example_sentence: I ran fast to catch up with my friends. You need to catch up with your studies. Let’s catch up with each other soon. The police finally caught up with the suspect. His lies finally caught up with him.

english_meaning: Definite, clear, without any doubt or condition. Firmly stated without hesitation. Describing something that belongs to a specific category or class. In logic, relating to statements that assert something directly.
example_sentence: They gave him a categorical assurance that he would not be hurt. He replied with a categorical assertion that no such offer was made. We want categorical proof. The categorical distinction is fairly clear.

english_meaning: In a very clear and definite way. As in absolutely, downright. In a way that is without any doubt or possibility of being changed.
example_sentence: We categorically reject the use of violence. The company categorically denied any wrongdoing. He categorically rejected our offer. She stated categorically that she had no intention of leaving

english_meaning: To provide food, services, or what is required for a particular event, group, or situation. To satisfy needs or wishes. To make arrangements for a particular group or situation.
example_sentence: The hotel caters to international tourists. This restaurant caters vegetarian dishes. The program caters to children of all ages. The speaker catered his lecture to the audience’s interests.

english_meaning: To provide what is needed or required, especially food, services, or facilities. To arrange or supply what is necessary for someone’s needs, wants, or preferences. It often refers to providing food or service for an event, group, or type of people
example_sentence: The hotel caters for tourists. The school caters for children with special needs. A restaurant caters for vegetarians. A hotel caters for business travelers. A school canteen caters for hundreds of students daily. The app caters for the needs of small businesses.

english_meaning: To provide what is wanted or needed, especially to satisfy desires or demands.
example_sentence: The restaurant caters to vegetarian customers. This app caters to young users. The event was designed to cater to all age groups. Don’t just cater to one side of the audience.

english_meaning: In a diagonal or slanting position. Situated diagonally opposite someone or something.
example_sentence: The post office is catercorner to the bank. She placed the rug catercorner in the room to make it look bigger. They lived catercorner from us for years. The two buildings stood catercorner at the intersection. The mark on the wall ran catercorner from the ceiling.

english_meaning: The worm-like larva of a butterfly or moth. A soft, segmented creeping insect larva that feeds mainly on leaves. A heavy vehicle or machine that moves on continuous tracks instead of wheels.
example_sentence: A green caterpillar was eating the cabbage leaves. The caterpillar will soon turn into a beautiful butterfly. Caterpillars destroyed a large part of the crop. The caterpillar tracks left deep marks in the mud.

english_meaning: A noisy or aggressive fight, usually between women. A physical or verbal fight that is loud, aggressive, and often emotional. The word is commonly used for conflicts between women and can involve insults, shouting, or physical struggle. It is often informal and sometimes considered disrespectful.
example_sentence: The argument between the two actresses turned into a catfight. Social media rumors sparked a public catfight between the rivals. The show was criticized for promoting catfights instead of healthy debate. What started as a disagreement quickly became a catfight.

english_meaning: The process of releasing strong or repressed emotions in order to achieve relief or renewal. A purification or purgation of the emotions through art, especially tragedy. An experience that brings about emotional release and clarity.
example_sentence: After talking to her best friend, she felt a sense of catharsis. Writing in his journal provided catharsis after a stressful week. Watching the emotional film gave many viewers a feeling of catharsis. Crying openly was a catharsis that helped him recover from his grief.

english_meaning: A thin, flexible tube inserted into the body to drain fluid, deliver medicine, or examine an organ. A medical tube passed into a blood vessel or the bladder for treatment or diagnosis.
example_sentence: The nurse inserted a catheter to drain the fluid. A catheter was used to deliver medicine directly to the heart. The patient needed a urinary catheter after the operation. Doctors removed the catheter once he had recovered.

english_meaning: A member of the part of the Christian Church that has the Pope as its leader. Belonging to or connected with the part of the Christian Church that has the Pope as its leader.
example_sentence: As a young person he had more catholic tastes than he does now. She is a novelist who is catholic in her interests.

english_meaning: Catoptrophobia is an irrational and persistent fear of mirrors or seeing one's own reflection. It often involves dread regarding supernatural entities believed to reside within or behind reflective surfaces. The condition may stem from deep-seated anxieties about self-perception or traumatic experiences related to mirrors. Individuals suffering from this phobia frequently avoid reflective surfaces or keep mirrors covered.
synonyms: ["Fear of mirrors","Eisoptrophobia","Spectrophobia","Mirror dread","Fear of reflections","Mirror phobia","Dread of reflections","Fear of looking in mirrors","Reflective surface fear"]
antonyms: ["Catoptrophilia","Love of mirrors","Mirror fascination","Admiration of reflections","Self reflection comfort","Vanity","Narcissism","Reflection fondness"]
example_sentence: She covered all the mirrors in her house because of her severe catoptrophobia. People who suffer from catoptrophobia often experience intense anxiety when passing reflective shop windows. His catoptrophobia was triggered after watching a terrifying film involving haunted mirrors. Cognitive behavioral therapy can help individuals overcome catoptrophobia through gradual exposure.

english_meaning: To hold or participate in a meeting of party members to decide policy or strategy. A private meeting of party members to plan strategy, discuss policy, or select candidates. A group of people within an organization with shared interests or goals. An organized faction or bloc within a larger assembly. A meeting of members of a political party or group to make decisions or select candidates.
example_sentence: The senators held a caucus to decide their stance on the new bill. A caucus of environmental activists met to plan a campaign. During the convention, the youth caucus pushed for more representation. The party’s caucus voted unanimously on the leadership candidate. The senators caucused for two hours before announcing their decision.

word: Caught between a rock and a hard place
english_meaning: To face a difficult situation with no easy options. Being in a very difficult situation where you have to choose between two unpleasant or harmful options. No matter which choice you make, the outcome will not be favorable.
example_sentence: He was caught between a rock and a hard place when he had to choose between losing his job or moving to another city. She felt caught between a rock and a hard place, either betray her friend’s trust or lie to her parents. The government is caught between a rock and a hard place: raising taxes will anger people, but not raising them will increase debt. I was caught between a rock and a hard place when both of my friends asked me to support their opposite sides in the argument.

english_meaning: Unable to choose between two options and failing in both. A situation where a person tries to deal with two different choices, tasks, or loyalties at the same time but cannot successfully manage either. As a result, both efforts fail or are unsatisfactory.
synonyms: ["Between two options and failing both","Torn between two choices","Unable to decide","In a dilemma","Hesitating and losing both sides"]
antonyms: ["Decisive","Clear-minded","Firm decision-maker","Focused on one goal","Committed to one choice"]
example_sentence: He was caught between two stools when choosing between a stable job and a risky business. She tried to support both teams but ended up caught between two stools and lost trust from both sides. The manager was caught between two stools while deciding which project to prioritize. Students who try to prepare for two exams at once often end up caught between two stools.

english_meaning: A vegetable with a firm white head surrounded by green leaves. An edible flower head eaten cooked, roasted, or pickled. The plant grown for this white head. A popular winter vegetable in many cuisines.
example_sentence: Cauliflower and potato curry is a family favourite. She roasted the cauliflower with garlic and spices. Fresh cauliflower is available all winter. The cauliflower heads must be cut before they open.

english_meaning: Relating to or acting as a cause. Describing a relationship in which one event produces another. Expressing the reason why something happens. In grammar, indicating cause, as with words like 'because'.
example_sentence: Researchers found no causal link between the two events. The study explains the causal factors behind the decline. A correlation does not always prove a causal relationship. 'Because' is a causal conjunction in English.

english_meaning: Having the power or function of causing something. Relating to the cause of an event or condition. In grammar, a form that shows one person makes another person do something.
example_sentence: Scientists searched for the causative factor behind the disease. The report identified smoking as a causative agent. “Have” can be used in a causative construction. The doctor explained the causative link between the exposure and the illness.

english_meaning: A person, thing, or event that makes something happen. The reason or motive behind an action or situation. A principle, aim, or movement that people support and work for. A legal case or matter brought before a court. To make something happen or bring about a particular result.
example_sentence: Heavy rain was the main cause of the flooding. She has no cause to complain about the arrangements. He donated generously to a worthy cause. Careless driving can cause serious accidents.

english_meaning: To create a strong public reaction or stir. To produce a noticeable and often controversial effect. To make something that draws widespread attention.
synonyms: ["Create a stir","Cause a sensation","Make waves","Stir up attention","Spark controversy","Make headlines"]
example_sentence: The unexpected announcement caused a splash in the industry. Her bold design caused a splash at the fashion show. The report caused a splash by revealing hidden corruption. The celebrity's visit caused a splash in the small town.

english_meaning: Care taken to avoid danger or mistakes. A warning against possible danger or trouble. Prudence in handling risky matters. To warn someone against something. A formal warning given by authority.
example_sentence: You should exercise caution while driving in the fog. The doctor cautioned him against smoking. A word of caution before you sign the contract. The police officer gave him a caution for speeding.

english_meaning: Careful to avoid danger, risk or mistakes. Acting with thought and attention to possible problems. Showing hesitation and restraint before deciding.
example_sentence: He is a cautious driver, especially at night. The doctors gave a cautious welcome to the new treatment. She took a cautious step onto the frozen lake. Investors remain cautious about the market.

english_meaning: In a careful, watchful, and attentive manner. With care and attention to avoid danger or mistakes. Prudently. In a way that shows caution.
example_sentence: He walked cautiously across the icy road. She cautiously opened the old wooden door. The soldier moved cautiously through the forest. He cautiously answered the tricky question.

english_meaning: Showing a lack of proper concern; offhand. Disdainful or arrogant. A supporter of King Charles I in the English Civil War.
example_sentence: She has a cavalier attitude about her health. His cavalier disregard for the rules got him into trouble. The official's cavalier response to the crisis angered the public. He dismissed my concerns with a cavalier wave of the hand. Such a cavalier attitude towards safety is unacceptable.

english_meaning: A large hole in the side of hill or under the ground. A naturally formed underground chamber with an opening to the surface. To fall in or down especially from being undermined
example_sentence: The area contains vast underground cave systems. They were trapped in the cave for 19 hours.

english_meaning: A warning or caution about a particular condition or limitation. It can indicate a legal or formal warning to prevent misunderstanding or risk.
example_sentence: There is a caveat to this rule. He agreed with one caveat. The report included several caveats. Read the contract caveats carefully.

english_meaning: A large cave or a deep chamber within a cave system. A vast underground hollow formed naturally in rock. Any deep, dark, enclosed space resembling a cave. To hollow something out like a cave.
example_sentence: The explorers discovered a huge underground cavern. Bats hung from the roof of the cavern. His voice echoed through the dark cavern. Water had caverned out the soft limestone over centuries.

english_meaning: To raise trivial objections or find fault over small matters. To argue about something unimportant in an annoying way. A petty or unnecessary objection. Needless criticism about minor details.
example_sentence: He always cavils at the wording instead of the idea. Do not cavil over such a small expense. Her only cavil was the colour of the cover. The committee cavilled about the order of the names.

english_meaning: A hollow space or an empty area within a solid object. A decayed part of a tooth that has formed a hole. A localized area of decay or structural weakness in a material. An anatomical space or chamber within the body of an organism. A small pit or depression on a surface.
example_sentence: The dentist found a small cavity in one of my back molars. The chest cavity protects vital organs like the heart and lungs. Moisture had caused a deep cavity to form in the old wooden beam. The explorers discovered a hidden cavity behind the waterfall.

english_meaning: To jump or dance around in a lively and high-spirited manner. To engage in frisky and playful behavior often without restraint. To physically display great joy or excitement through rhythmic or erratic movement. To behave in a festive or boisterous way, especially when celebrating. To romp or prance about in a manner that expresses lightheartedness.
example_sentence: The children began to cavort through the sprinklers on the hot summer afternoon. Puppies often cavort in the grass when they are first let outside. The winning team started to cavort on the field after the final whistle blew. It was heartwarming to see the elderly couple cavort at their granddaughter's wedding.

english_meaning: To come to an end. To stop doing something. To bring an activity or process to a halt. To discontinue permanently or for a period of time.
example_sentence: The rain finally ceased in the afternoon. The factory ceased production last year. He never ceases to amaze his teachers. Both sides agreed to cease fighting immediately.

english_meaning: A temporary suspension of fighting, especially by mutual agreement between opposing sides. A formal order to stop firing or fighting. A truce that allows time for talks or peace efforts.
example_sentence: Both sides agreed to a ceasefire after weeks of intense fighting. The United Nations called for an immediate ceasefire in the region. The ceasefire allowed aid workers to reach the affected people. Violations of the ceasefire were reported on both sides. A lasting ceasefire is the first step towards peace.

english_meaning: The pouch-like first part of the large intestine, joined to the small intestine. The sac to which the appendix is attached. A blind-ended pouch at the beginning of the colon.
example_sentence: The cecum is the first part of the large intestine. The appendix hangs from the cecum. Food waste enters the cecum from the small intestine. Inflammation of the cecum can cause pain in the lower abdomen.

english_meaning: To give up control or ownership of something. To formally give up power, land, rights, or authority to another person, group, or country, often unwillingly or due to pressure, agreement, or law.
example_sentence: The country agreed to cede the disputed territory after negotiations. He refused to cede control of the company to external investors. The king was forced to cede power to the new government. She would not cede her rights without legal protection.

english_meaning: A person who performs or participates in a religious ceremony or festival. The officiating priest or minister at a Eucharist or other religious rite. A person who celebrates or takes part in a celebration.
example_sentence: The celebrant led the congregation through the traditional rites of the ceremony. She was chosen to be the celebrant at the outdoor wedding ceremony in the garden. The celebrant spoke warmly about the couple before inviting them to exchange their vows. As the principal celebrant, the bishop presided over the Easter Mass at the cathedral. The celebrant welcomed everyone to the graduation ceremony and asked for silence before beginning.

english_meaning: To mark an important event with enjoyment and special activities. To honour a person or achievement publicly. To perform a religious ceremony such as a mass or ritual. To praise something widely and enthusiastically.
example_sentence: We celebrated her birthday with a quiet family dinner. The whole village came together to celebrate the harvest. The article celebrates the work of unsung local heroes. The priest will celebrate the ceremony early in the morning.

english_meaning: A special social event held to mark a happy occasion. The act of showing joy and honour for an achievement, festival, or anniversary. A formal ceremony or ritual performed on an important occasion. The expression of praise and appreciation for someone or something.
example_sentence: The family arranged a small celebration for her graduation. Independence Day celebrations were held across the country. The victory called for a proper celebration. His book is a celebration of rural life and its traditions.

english_meaning: A famous person, State of being of famous
example_sentence: Does he find his new celebrity intruding on his private life. He achieved instant celebrity status.

english_meaning: A vegetable with long, crisp, pale green stalks and feathery leaves. A crunchy stalk eaten raw in salads or cooked in soups. The plant grown for these stalks and seeds. A low-calorie vegetable often used for flavouring stocks.
example_sentence: She dipped celery sticks in peanut butter. Celery adds a fresh crunch to the salad. Chopped celery goes into the soup base. Celery is often eaten as a light snack.

english_meaning: A small keyboard musical instrument that produces soft, bell like sounds. A percussion keyboard instrument that looks similar to a small piano. When a key is pressed, a hammer strikes metal plates instead of strings, producing a clear, sweet, and bell like tone. It is often used in orchestral music to create magical or dreamy sound effects.
example_sentence: The composer added a celesta to give the melody a magical touch. The soft sound of the celesta filled the concert hall. She learned to play the celesta for the school orchestra. The celesta created a dreamy mood in the film soundtrack.

english_meaning: Of the sky or of heaven. Of or from the sky or outside this world. Of, relating to, or suggesting heaven or divinity. Pertaining to the sky or visible heaven, or to the universe beyond the earth’s atmosphere.
example_sentence: The moon is a celestial body. Gravity governs the motions of celestial bodies. Angels are celestial beings. In my case it really was a form of celestial cannon ball.

english_meaning: An irrational fear of the sky, outer space, celestial bodies (such as stars, planets, and the moon), or anything related to the vastness of the universe. A person with this phobia may feel intense anxiety, panic, or discomfort when looking at the sky or thinking about space.
example_sentence: She avoids going outside at night due to celestiphobia. His celestiphobia worsens when he sees stars in the sky. The patient was diagnosed with celestiphobia after panic attacks during astronomy class. Even pictures of space can trigger his celestiphobia.

english_meaning: The state of remaining unmarried, especially for religious reasons. Voluntary abstention from sexual relations. A vow or discipline of sexual purity undertaken as a spiritual practice. The condition of living a single, chaste life.
example_sentence: Catholic priests take a vow of celibacy. He chose celibacy in order to devote himself to study. Celibacy is required in several monastic traditions. Her decision to embrace celibacy surprised her family.

english_meaning: The smallest structural and functional unit of a living organism. A small room in which a prisoner is locked up or a monk lives. A small compartment or enclosed space in a larger structure. A device that produces electricity through chemical reactions. A small group of people forming part of a larger political or terrorist organization.
example_sentence: The human body is made up of trillions of cells. The prisoner was locked in a small cell. He replaced the battery cells in his flashlight. Police uncovered a secret cell operating in the city.

english_meaning: A scale of temperature in which water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred degrees. The standard metric unit used for measuring temperature in most countries. Relating to or measured on this temperature scale. Also known as the centigrade scale.
example_sentence: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius at sea level. Today's temperature reached forty degrees Celsius. Set the oven to one hundred and eighty degrees Celsius. The thermometer showed a Celsius reading of thirty two.

english_meaning: A large area of land, often separate from a church, used for burying the dead. A place containing graves, tombs, and memorials where deceased individuals are laid to rest. A burial ground typically organized with marked plots, headstones, and pathways. A site set aside by a community for the interment of the deceased, often maintained as a place of remembrance.
example_sentence: The old cemetery on the hill has been there for over two hundred years.  Families visited the cemetery to lay flowers on their loved ones' graves.  The cemetery was peaceful, with rows of weathered headstones under tall trees.  Local historians often research old cemeteries to learn about a town's past.  The soldiers were buried with honors in the military cemetery.

english_meaning: To express severe disapproval of someone or something, especially in a formal statement. The expression of formal disapproval.
example_sentence: The senator was censured for his unethical behavior. The report contained a strong censure of the company's practices. He faced public censure for his controversial remarks. The judge censured the lawyer for wasting the court's time. His actions drew a sharp censure from his colleagues.

english_meaning: An official and systematic process of collecting information about the population of a country or region. It usually includes data about the number of people, age, gender, occupation, education, housing, and other social and economic details. Governments conduct a census to plan public services, development projects, and policy decisions.
example_sentence: The government conducts a census every ten years. The latest census showed rapid urban growth. Census data helps in planning schools and hospitals. Many people work temporarily as census workers during the survey period.

english_meaning: A mythical creature that is half human and half horse. A legendary being with the upper body of a human and the lower body of a horse. Centaurs often represent a mix of wisdom and wild behavior and are commonly shown as warriors, teachers, or untamed beings in ancient stories, art, and literature.
example_sentence: The centaur guarded the forest in the ancient legend. In mythology class, we studied stories about centaurs and heroes. The painting showed a centaur teaching a young warrior. Many fantasy novels include centaurs as wise and powerful characters.

english_meaning: A person who is 100 years old or older. The word can also refer to members of a group of people aged 100 years or more in demographic studies. It is often used in discussions about life expectancy, population aging, and public health.
synonyms: ["Hundred year old person","Long lived person","Elderly person of one hundred years","Person aged one hundred"]
example_sentence: The village proudly celebrated its oldest centenarian on her hundredth birthday. Researchers interviewed several centenarians to learn about their lifestyle. The country has an increasing number of centenarians due to better healthcare. His grandmother became a centenarian last year and still enjoys gardening.

english_meaning: A numerical prefix used in the metric system denoting a factor of one one-hundredth. A unit of measurement indicating the hundredth part of a basic unit. An informal shortening often referring to a centimeter in technical contexts. A prefix derived from the Latin 'centum' meaning hundred. A decimal multiplier representing 10 to the power of negative two. A standardized prefix used to signify division by one hundred.
example_sentence: The measurement was recorded in centiliters to ensure precision for the liquid mixture. One centimeter is exactly one hundredth of a meter in length. The engineer added the centi prefix to indicate the scale of the component. She calculated the difference in centigrams to account for the minute weight variance.

english_meaning: Relating to a temperature scale divided into one hundred degrees between the freezing and boiling points of water. Another name for the Celsius scale. Measured in degrees on this scale. Describing a thermometer that uses this system.
example_sentence: Water freezes at zero degrees centigrade. The temperature rose to forty-two degrees centigrade yesterday. The recipe requires an oven set to one hundred and eighty centigrade. Most countries use the centigrade scale rather than Fahrenheit.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to one hundredth of a gram. A tiny unit used for very light substances. A unit equal to 10 milligrams.
example_sentence: One centigram equals ten milligrams. The tablet contains only a few centigrams of the drug. Laboratory scales can measure a single centigram. She noted the weight in centigrams.

english_meaning: A metric unit of volume equal to one hundredth of a liter. A measure of liquid equal to ten milliliters, written as cl. A small metric capacity unit commonly used for drinks and bottled liquids in some countries.
example_sentence: The label says the glass holds twenty centiliters of juice. One centiliter is equal to ten milliliters. European wine bottles are often measured in centiliters. She poured five centiliters of syrup into the cup.

english_meaning: A metric unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre. A small unit used to measure short distances and object sizes. A unit equal to ten millimeters.
example_sentence: The book is twenty centimeters wide. One hundred centimeters make one meter. He grew five centimeters taller this year. Measure the cloth in centimeters before cutting it.

english_meaning: A fast-moving arthropod with a flattened segmented body and one pair of legs on each segment. A predatory crawling creature with venomous front claws used to catch small insects.
example_sentence: A centipede ran quickly across the bathroom floor. The bite of a large centipede can be painful. Centipedes hide under stones and dry leaves. He removed the centipede carefully with a stick.

english_meaning: Situated in or near the middle of an area or object. Most important, main, or essential to something. Controlled from one main place or authority. Easily reached from many other places.
example_sentence: Their office is in a central part of the city. Trust is central to any healthy relationship. The central government announced new reforms. The hotel is very central and close to the station.

english_meaning: To bring activities or control together under one authority. To concentrate power or administration in a single place. To organize a system so that decisions are made centrally. To gather scattered parts into one central point.
example_sentence: The government plans to centralize all health services. They decided to centralize purchasing in the head office. Efforts to centralize power met strong opposition. The company centralized its records in one database.

english_meaning: Bringing control or activities together under one authority. Tending to concentrate power in a single centre. The process of making a system centrally controlled. Present participle of the verb centralize.
example_sentence: The government is centralizing control of the railways. Centralizing decisions can slow down local action. They adopted a centralizing policy after the merger. Centralizing the data saved the company both time and money.

english_meaning: The middle point of a circle, sphere, or other symmetrical object. The point equidistant from all edges or surfaces. The main or most important area for a specific activity. A place where a particular activity is concentrated.
example_sentence: Mark the centre of the circle with a dot. The park is located in the centre of the city. The shopping centre attracts many visitors. All radii extend from the centre to the circumference.

english_meaning: Moving or tending to move away from a centre or axis. Relating to or using the force that pushes objects outward when they rotate around a central point.
example_sentence: The centrifugal force threw the passenger outward on the curve. A centrifugal pump uses rotation to move fluid outward. The centrifugal effect can be felt on a spinning fairground ride. Washing machines use centrifugal force to dry clothes.

english_meaning: An apparent force felt by an object moving in a circular path that seems to push the object outward from the centre of the circle. It is a fictitious force observed in a rotating reference frame.
example_sentence: Centrifugal force keeps water in a bucket when swung overhead. The centrifugal force in a washing machine spins out the water. Astronauts experience the effects of centrifugal force in training. The car's turn made him feel centrifugal force pushing him sideways.

english_meaning: A machine that uses centrifugal force to separate substances of different densities by spinning them rapidly. Widely used in laboratories, medicine, and industry.
example_sentence: The laboratory used a centrifuge to separate blood plasma from cells. A centrifuge is essential for analysing urine samples. The dairy industry uses a centrifuge to separate cream from milk. Scientists used a high-speed centrifuge to isolate the virus.

english_meaning: A tiny cylindrical structure found in animal cells that plays a key role in cell division by organising the spindle fibres that separate chromosomes during mitosis.
example_sentence: Centrioles are absent in the cells of higher plants. The centriole duplicates before cell division begins. Biologists studied the role of the centriole in cancer cell division. Each cell contains two centrioles forming the centrosome.

english_meaning: Moving or tending to move toward a centre or axis. Relating to the force that makes an object follow a curved path by pulling it inward toward the centre of rotation.
example_sentence: Centripetal acceleration keeps the moon orbiting the earth. The string provides centripetal force when swinging a ball in a circle. Gravity acts as a centripetal force for planets orbiting the sun. The centripetal pull of the drain created a small whirlpool.

english_meaning: The real inward force required to keep an object moving in a circular path. It acts toward the centre of the circle and prevents the object from flying outward.
example_sentence: Centripetal force keeps a car on a curved road without skidding. The tension in a string provides centripetal force for circular motion. Earth's gravity acts as centripetal force for the moon's orbit. The centripetal force decreases if the speed of rotation increases.

english_meaning: A person who holds moderate political views, neither strongly left-wing nor strongly right-wing. Someone who supports compromise and balance between opposing political positions.
example_sentence: The centrist candidate won support from both sides of the political spectrum. She described herself as a centrist who believed in practical solutions. The centrist party tried to bridge the gap between left and right. A centrist approach is often necessary to pass legislation in a divided parliament.

english_meaning: An officer in the ancient Roman army who commanded a unit of about one hundred soldiers. A military commander of a century in a Roman legion. A person holding a rank of authority and discipline in Roman military service. Figuratively, a strong, disciplined leader or guardian.
example_sentence: The centurion led his soldiers into battle with great courage. A Roman centurion was responsible for training and discipline. The museum displayed the armour of a centurion. He stood guard like a centurion at the entrance.

english_meaning: A period of one hundred years. Each hundred-year division of a historical era. A score of one hundred runs made by a batsman in cricket. A long stretch of time counted in hundreds of years.
example_sentence: The building was constructed in the nineteenth century. He scored a brilliant century in the second innings. Many customs have survived for more than a century. The twentieth century saw remarkable scientific progress.

english_meaning: A person who is deeply attracted to and finds joy in thunder and lightning. One who loves storms and atmospheric electrical activity. A lover of thunder and lightning. Someone who feels a sense of peace or excitement during thunderstorms. An individual with a strong preference for storm-watching.
example_sentence: As a ceraunophile, she always runs to the window the moment she hears the first rumble of thunder. While others hide during the storm, the ceraunophile feels an incredible sense of exhilaration. He considers himself a ceraunophile because the sight of lightning brings him immense inner peace. The photographer, a dedicated ceraunophile, spent his entire vacation chasing storms across the plains.

english_meaning: The extreme and irrational fear of thunder and lightning. A specific phobia often associated with astraphobia or brontophobia. An intense anxiety triggered by electrical storms. A psychological condition characterized by panic during thunderstorms. An avoidant behavior towards weather patterns involving thunder. A subtype of environmental phobia.
example_sentence: She refuses to leave the house during a storm because of her ceraunophobia. Many animals exhibit signs of ceraunophobia when they hear loud thunder claps. Therapy can help individuals manage the panic attacks associated with ceraunophobia. His ceraunophobia is so severe that he monitors weather reports constantly.

english_meaning: The part of the brain located at the back of the head, below the cerebrum. The region of the brain that coordinates voluntary movements, balance, and posture. The 'little brain' that makes movement smooth, accurate, and well-timed.
example_sentence: The cerebellum helps you walk in a straight line. Injury to the cerebellum often causes unsteady movement. A dancer's grace depends heavily on the cerebellum. The cerebellum sits just below the back of the cerebrum.

english_meaning: Relating to the brain or the intellect. Intellectual rather than emotional or physical. Concerning thought, reasoning and mental activity. Of or relating to the cerebrum of the brain in anatomy and medicine.
example_sentence: Chess is a highly cerebral game that requires deep concentration. He prefers cerebral films over action movies. The doctor diagnosed a cerebral haemorrhage. Her writing has a cerebral quality that appeals to thoughtful readers. Philosophy is a cerebral discipline.

english_meaning: To think deeply. To use the brain actively, especially for serious, careful, or intellectual thinking. It often refers to deep or analytical thought rather than casual thinking.
example_sentence: He sat quietly to cerebrate on the complex problem. Scientists cerebrate for years to develop new theories. She likes to cerebrate before making important decisions. The philosopher spent his life cerebrating about human existence.

english_meaning: The largest part of the brain, divided into left and right hemispheres. The upper part of the brain that controls voluntary movement, speech, learning, reasoning, and emotion. The region of the brain where conscious thought and sensory interpretation take place.
example_sentence: The cerebrum makes up about eighty percent of the brain's weight. Speech and reasoning are controlled by the cerebrum. Damage to the cerebrum may affect memory and behaviour. The two halves of the cerebrum are joined by a thick band of fibres.

english_meaning: A burial cloth used to wrap a dead body. A cloth or shroud in which a dead body is wrapped before burial. It is often used in literary or poetic contexts rather than everyday speech.
example_sentence: The ancient ritual required the body to be wrapped in a fine cerement. The ghost was described as rising in its cerement. In poetry, the hero was laid to rest in a white cerement. The old tomb still held fragments of a decayed cerement.

english_meaning: A formal religious or public occasion celebrating a particular event. The strict adherence to conventional etiquette or formal behavior. A prescribed ritual observance conducted on a solemn state occasion. An act or series of acts performed according to traditional or prescribed form. A mere formal act stripped of its original deep significance.
example_sentence: The wedding ceremony took place in a beautiful old church. They were married without much ceremony or grand celebration. The opening ceremony of the Olympic games was spectacular. He accepted the award during a brief ceremony at the town hall.

english_meaning: A bright, deep pinkish-red color like that of cherries. A vivid cherry-red shade. Having a strong pink-red color.
example_sentence: She wore a cerise gown to the gala. The flowers bloomed in shades of cerise and magenta. He bought a cerise tie to brighten his suit. The logo was printed in a bold cerise color.

english_meaning: Completely sure about something and free from doubt. Known to be true or bound to happen. Particular but not named or described in detail. Some but not a large amount of something. Reliable and not likely to fail.
example_sentence: I am certain that I locked the door. Success is certain if you keep working hard. A certain gentleman was asking about you. There is a certain charm in old houses.

english_meaning: Without any doubt; definitely. Used to give a strong yes in reply to a request. Surely and beyond question. In a way that is clearly true. Used to emphasise agreement or confirmation.
example_sentence: He is certainly the best player in the team. Certainly, I will help you with the forms. The new rules will certainly affect small businesses. She certainly knows how to handle difficult customers.

english_meaning: To formally state, confirm, or verify that something is true, accurate, legal, qualified, or approved. It is often used when an authority, institution, doctor, officer, or official body gives written or formal proof.
example_sentence: The doctor certified that the patient was fit to travel. This document has been certified by the local authority. The course certifies students to work as technicians. She asked the officer to certify a copy of her passport.

english_meaning: A state of complete confidence or certainty about something, often without doubt. Firm conviction that something is true, correct, or will happen as expected. The quality of being free from doubt, especially regarding one's own beliefs or judgments. Absolute assurance in one's knowledge, opinion, or decision.
example_sentence: She spoke with such certitude that no one dared to question her conclusions.  The scientist avoided certitude, acknowledging that further research was needed.  His certitude about the outcome of the election proved to be misplaced.  There is a certain comfort in the certitude of long-held beliefs.  The judge required more than personal certitude before reaching a verdict.

english_meaning: A rich, clear shade of blue that resembles the color of a bright, cloudless sky. It is often used in art, design, fashion, and painting to describe a calm and vivid blue tone.
example_sentence: The cerulean waters of the Caribbean were breathtaking. She wore a dress of a stunning cerulean shade. The painter used cerulean to capture the color of the summer sky. We sailed under a vast cerulean sky. Her eyes were a bright cerulean blue.

english_meaning: Relating to the neck. Relating to the cervix of the uterus. Located in or affecting the neck region of the spine. Used in medical terms for structures in the neck or cervix.
example_sentence: The scan showed a problem in the cervical spine. Cervical pain can spread into the shoulders. The doctor recommended regular cervical screening. A cervical collar helped support his neck after the accident.

english_meaning: The neck area of the body, located between the head and the trunk. The part of the spine made up of the seven cervical vertebrae. An anatomical region that supports the head and allows it to move. In gynaecology, the area relating to the cervix of the uterus.
example_sentence: The cervical region supports the weight of the head. He suffered a serious injury to the cervical region. There are seven vertebrae in the cervical region of the spine. Poor posture often causes pain in the cervical region.

english_meaning: Any one of the seven small bones that form the neck region of the spinal column. A vertebra of the neck that supports the head and allows it to turn, nod, and tilt. The uppermost segment of the backbone, lying between the skull and the chest region. One of the lightest and most mobile bones of the spine.
example_sentence: A sudden jolt in the crash injured his cervical vertebra. The seven cervical vertebrae allow the head to move freely. Poor posture can strain the cervical vertebrae over time. The scan revealed swelling around the third cervical vertebra.

english_meaning: The narrow lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina. The neck of the womb through which a baby passes during birth. A structure that produces mucus which changes during the menstrual cycle. Any narrow neck-like part of a body organ.
example_sentence: The cervix widens during labour to let the baby out. Regular screening can detect early changes in the cervix. Mucus from the cervix changes during the monthly cycle. The doctor examined the cervix during the check-up.

english_meaning: A variant spelling of Caesarean, referring to the surgical delivery of a baby through the abdomen. Relating to such a surgical birth. Relating to Caesar or the Roman emperors.
example_sentence: The hospital records list a cesarian delivery. She had a cesarian with her first child. A cesarian may be planned in advance or performed in an emergency. The nurse explained how to care for the cesarian wound.

english_meaning: A shape like a curved sliver, similar to the moon in its first or last quarter. The curved figure of the moon when it is less than half full. Growing or increasing gradually (archaic usage). Shaped like a crescent moon.
example_sentence: A thin cescent moon hung low in the evening sky. The flag featured a cescent and a star. The cescent shape of the bay was visible from the hill. She wore earrings shaped like silver cescents.

english_meaning: To cause someone to feel embarrassed, disappointed, or annoyed. A strong feeling of being upset, embarrassed, or disappointed, especially when something goes wrong, when someone fails, or when a person feels humiliated. It is often used when a person feels both emotional discomfort and frustration.
example_sentence: He felt great chagrin after forgetting his best friend’s birthday. To her chagrin, she arrived at the meeting on the wrong day. The team lost the final match, much to the coach’s chagrin. His careless remark chagrined her in front of everyone.

english_meaning: Concerned, attentive, or eager about something. A rare back-formation from 'nonchalant', used mainly in humorous or informal writing. Showing enthusiasm rather than indifference. Not a standard dictionary word in formal English.
example_sentence: He was surprisingly chalant about the upcoming exam. She joked that she felt very chalant about the news. For once he looked chalant rather than bored. Writers use chalant only in a playful, informal way.

english_meaning: Used to describe two people or things that are completely different from each other. Having no common characteristics or similarities. Being poles apart in temperament or appearance. Distinctly separate and incompatible in nature. Fundamentally unlike each other in every way.
example_sentence: Although they are twins, their personalities are like chalk and cheese. The two proposals for the new park are as different as chalk and cheese. My brothers are chalk and cheese; one loves sports while the other prefers reading. You cannot compare these two movies because they are really chalk and cheese.

english_meaning: To plan or outline something. To carefully plan or design a course of action often in detail before execution.
example_sentence: They chalked out a new strategy for the project. The teacher chalked out the lesson plan for the week. The government chalked out reforms for education. She chalked out her career goals early in life.

english_meaning: To record an achievement or assign a reason. To officially record something such as a win or success or to attribute something to a particular cause.
example_sentence: The team chalked up another victory this season. She chalked up her success to hard work. The company chalked up high profits last year. He chalked up the mistake to lack of training.

english_meaning: To be impatient or eager to start something. A strong desire to start an activity or take action, often mixed with restlessness or impatience because of waiting. It comes from horse riding, where a horse bites impatiently on the bit while waiting to move.
example_sentence: The players were champing at the bit to start the match. She’s champing at the bit to show her new project. We’re all champing at the bit for the weekend. He was champing at the bit to prove himself.

english_meaning: To decide to do something different from what was planned earlier. To alter one’s opinion, decision, or intention.
example_sentence: She was going to study medicine, but she changed her mind and chose engineering instead. I wanted to go out tonight, but I changed my mind after seeing the bad weather. He changed his mind about selling the house when he realized its value. The manager changed her mind after hearing the team’s suggestions.

english_meaning: To say or sing something repeatedly in a steady rhythm, usually in a group. It is often used in religious gatherings, protests, sports events, or ceremonies. A repeated phrase or sound that people say or sing together, often to show support, faith, or unity.
example_sentence: The crowd began chanting anti Govt slogans. The crowd began to chant the team’s name during the match. The monks chant prayers every morning at sunrise. Protesters chanted slogans outside the building. She softly chanted a mantra to calm her mind.

english_meaning: A state of complete confusion & disorder. Economic, political, domestic chaos
example_sentence: Heavy snow has caused total chaos on the roads. The house was in chaos after the party.

english_meaning: In a state of complete confusion or disorder
example_sentence: The traffic in the city is chaotic in the rush hours. Eyewitness said the situation was chaotic & the area was littered with bodies & burnt vehicles.

english_meaning: An older or responsible person who accompanies young people to ensure proper behaviour. An adult who supervises a group on a trip or at an event. A person who escorts someone for safety or propriety. To accompany and supervise someone, especially a young person.
example_sentence: Two teachers acted as chaperones on the school trip. Her aunt served as a chaperone at the wedding. Parents were asked to chaperone the students at the concert. In earlier times, a young woman rarely travelled without a chaperone.

english_meaning: A small wreath, garland, or a string of prayer beads. A circular band of flowers or leaves worn on the head, often as a symbol of honor or celebration. It also means a string of beads used for prayer, especially in Christian traditions. In a broader sense, it can describe a series or group of related things arranged together.
example_sentence: She wore a chaplet of fresh flowers during the ceremony. The monk counted his prayers using a wooden chaplet. Ancient poets were often shown wearing a chaplet on their heads. The chaplet symbolized peace and devotion.

english_meaning: The combination of mental and moral qualities that make a person who they are. A person in a novel, play, film, or story. Strong moral qualities such as honesty and courage. A distinctive quality or feature that makes a place or thing special. A letter, number, or symbol used in writing or printing. An unusual or amusing person.
example_sentence: He is a man of strong character and honesty. My favorite character in the novel is the old sailor. The narrow streets give the town its special character. Each Chinese character carries its own meaning.

english_meaning: A feature or quality belonging typically to a person, place, or thing and serving to identify it. Typical of a particular person, place, or thing.
example_sentence: Her generosity is one of her most admired characteristics. The pointed ears are a characteristic of that breed of dog. It was characteristic of him to be late. The building has many unique architectural characteristics. With characteristic charm, he greeted every guest personally.

english_meaning: Typical features or qualities that make a person or thing recognizable. Distinguishing traits or attributes of someone or something. The properties that define the nature of a person, animal, or object.
example_sentence: Honesty and kindness are her most admirable characteristics. The desert has unique climatic characteristics. Scientists studied the physical characteristics of the new species. Patience is one of the key characteristics of a good teacher.

english_meaning: To be typical of a person, place or thing. To describe or show the qualities of somebody, something in a particular way.
example_sentence: The city is characterized by tall modern buildings in steel and glass. How would you characterize the mood of the 1990s? Bright colours and bold strokes characterize his early paintings. In her essay, she characterizes the whole era as a period of radical change. This election campaign has been characterized by violence. Both companies have characterized the relationship as friendly. This play is characterized as a comedy.

english_meaning: To demand money. To rush forward aggressively. To energize a battery. The cost or price asked for something. Responsibility or duty. Accusation or allegation
example_sentence: The hotel added a service charge to the bill. She is in charge of the new project. The soldier took charge of the camp. They charged me $50 for the repair. The store charges extra for home delivery. The soldiers charged the enemy lines. I need to charge my phone. He faced a charge of theft.

english_meaning: Having a natural charm that attracts and influences people, A person who has a strong personal appeal. Such a person easily attracts attention, inspires trust, and influences others through confidence, warmth, and presence rather than force or authority.
example_sentence: The charismatic leader motivated the entire community. She is a charismatic speaker who captivates her audience. His charismatic personality helped him succeed in politics. The teacher was charismatic and students loved attending his class.

english_meaning: Generous in giving help or money to those in need. Relating to charity or organisations that help people. Kind and tolerant in judging others. Showing sympathy and a willingness to forgive faults.
example_sentence: She made a charitable donation to the local hospital. The money was given to a charitable organisation. He took a charitable view of his friend's mistake. Their family has always been charitable towards the poor.

english_meaning: In a kind, generous, or benevolent manner. With tolerance and understanding when judging others. Through or by means of charitable giving. In a way that shows compassion and goodwill.
example_sentence: She charitably overlooked his mistakes. The donation was charitably given to help families. He spoke charitably about his opponent's efforts. The community charitably supports local causes.

english_meaning: The voluntary giving of help, typically money, to those in need. An organization set up to provide help and raise money for those in need. Kindness, generosity, and tolerance in judging others. Love and goodwill toward humanity.
example_sentence: She donates regularly to several charities. They organized a charity event to raise funds. The church is known for its charity work in the community. We should judge others with charity and understanding.

english_meaning: A proverb meaning that one should take care of one's own family and close community before helping others. The idea that concern for others should start with those closest to you. The principle that people should prioritize their immediate responsibilities before extending help to strangers.
synonyms: ["Take care of your own first","Family comes first","Look after your own","Priority to family"]
example_sentence: He believes charity begins at home and takes care of his family first. While she volunteers abroad, she remembers that charity begins at home. The organization focuses locally because charity begins at home. They help neighbors first, knowing charity begins at home.

english_meaning: A person who falsely claims to have special knowledge, skill, or ability in order to deceive people. Someone who pretends to be an expert, professional, healer, scholar, or skilled person, but in reality is dishonest or not truly qualified. This word is often used for people who trick others for money, fame, trust, or influence. A charlatan may appear confident and convincing, but their claims are false or exaggerated.
example_sentence: The man who claimed to cure every disease was later exposed as a charlatan. Many people trusted the charlatan because he spoke with great confidence. The fake spiritual leader turned out to be nothing more than a charlatan. She warned her friends not to believe the charlatan selling miracle medicine.

english_meaning: The power or quality of pleasing or attracting people. An attractive feature or trait. A small object worn for its supposed magical power. A magical spell or incantation. To delight or influence someone through personal appeal.
example_sentence: She has a natural charm that draws people to her. The old village has a certain rustic charm. He wore a lucky charm around his neck. The salesman charmed the customers with his friendly manner.

english_meaning: A person who is very pleasant, attractive, and good at making others like them. A person who easily attracts, pleases, or influences others through a friendly manner, sweet speech, confidence, politeness, or appealing personality. The word can be used in a positive sense for someone delightful and likable. Sometimes it can also suggest a person who wins others over very skillfully.
example_sentence: He is such a charmer that everyone enjoys talking to him. The little girl was a charmer and made the whole room smile. She handled the guests like a true charmer. Although he was a charmer, some people thought he was too clever with words. He is a real charmer at social events. She is a charmer who can calm any angry customer.

english_meaning: A written document from an authority granting rights, privileges, or powers. The formal establishment or constitution of an organization or institution. To hire or rent a vehicle, especially an aircraft or ship, for private use. A contract for the hire of transportation. The fundamental principles or constitution guiding an organization.
example_sentence: The company received its charter from the government. The United Nations Charter outlines its principles. They chartered a yacht for their vacation. The school operates under a special charter. The city charter defines municipal powers.

english_meaning: A flight on an aircraft that has been hired for a specific group, purpose, or journey rather than sold seat by seat to the general public. A non-scheduled flight arranged privately, often by a tour operator, sports team, company, or government. A booked aircraft service that does not follow a regular published timetable.
synonyms: ["Chartered plane","Private flight","Hired flight","Non-scheduled flight","Special flight","Booked aircraft"]
example_sentence: The pilgrims travelled to Madinah on a special charter flight. A charter flight was arranged to bring the stranded tourists home. Charter flights are often cheaper than scheduled flights during the holiday season. The football club booked a charter flight for the away match.

english_meaning: Hired or rented for exclusive use, especially a plane, ship, bus, or boat. Officially granted a charter, meaning a formal written document that establishes rights, powers, or professional status. Fully qualified in a profession after being admitted to a professional body that holds a royal charter. Established or founded by an official charter, as in a chartered bank or chartered company.
example_sentence: The team travelled to the tournament on a chartered plane. He is a chartered accountant with fifteen years of experience. The chartered bank opened three new branches this year. They chartered a boat for a week-long trip along the coast.

english_meaning: To pursue in order to catch or catch up with. An act of pursuing someone or something. To try to obtain something that is difficult to get.
example_sentence: The police car chased the stolen vehicle through the city. The dog likes to chase squirrels in the park. After years of chasing his dream, he finally became a successful actor. The movie ended with a dramatic car chase. Children love to chase bubbles in the yard.

english_meaning: To waste time searching for something that is impossible to find or achieve. A situation where someone is pursuing a goal, idea, or task that has little or no chance of success. It often involves being misled or following false information, resulting in wasted effort, time, and energy.
synonyms: ["Wild goose chase","Fool’s errand","Waste of time","Lost cause","Running after illusions"]
example_sentence: He spent the whole day chasing a wild goose, looking for a shop that does not exist. Trying to fix that broken system without tools is like chasing a wild goose. The detective realized he was chasing a wild goose after finding false clues. Do not chase a wild goose by trusting every rumor you hear online.

english_meaning: To pursue someone or something until you catch them. To search hard for something until you find it. To make persistent efforts to obtain information, payment, or an answer from someone.
example_sentence: The officer chased down the thief on foot. It took me hours to chase down the missing file. She is still chasing down the unpaid invoices. Reporters chased down every lead in the story.

english_meaning: To pursue dreams or goals that are unrealistic or impossible to achieve. It refers to chasing something beautiful or attractive but not real or attainable.
example_sentence: He keeps chasing rainbows instead of working on real goals. Stop chasing rainbows and focus on something practical. She is chasing rainbows if she thinks success will come without effort. They warned him not to chase rainbows all his life.

english_meaning: To follow up with someone to get information, action, or a response. To contact someone to get a reply, update, or action.
example_sentence: I need to chase up the supplier about the delayed shipment. She chased up her manager to approve the budget. We must chase up all pending invoices before the month ends. He chased up the client to confirm the meeting time.

english_meaning: Pursuing unrealistic or impossible goals, Trying to achieve something impossible or unrealistic. It describes wasting time on dreams that cannot come true or goals that have no real chance of success.
example_sentence: He spends his life chasing rainbows instead of focusing on real goals. They warned her that starting the project with no money was just chasing rainbows. Stop chasing rainbows and work on something practical. The idea of becoming famous overnight is mostly chasing rainbows.

english_meaning: Trying to achieve something impossible or wasting effort on something that cannot be caught or solved. A situation where a person is putting effort into something that is unrealistic, unreachable, or self-created confusion. It often means wasting time on illusions, unnecessary fears, or goals that cannot be achieved.
synonyms: ["Chasing illusions","Wasting effort","Running after impossibilities","Beating the air","Futile pursuit"]
antonyms: ["Focused effort","Practical approach","Realistic goal setting","Productive work","Purposeful action"]
example_sentence: He keeps doubting everyone, as if he is chasing his own shadow. Trying to prove that rumor true is like chasing your own shadow. She spent years chasing her own shadow instead of focusing on her career. Worrying about things that will never happen is just chasing your own shadow.

english_meaning: A deep crack or opening in the earth's surface. A wide and deep gap between two things. A profound difference of opinion, feeling, or interest between people. An unbridgeable divide. A yawning hollow or void.
example_sentence: The hikers carefully crossed the deep mountain chasm. A cultural chasm separates the two generations. The disagreement created a chasm between the friends. Sunlight barely reached the bottom of the chasm.

english_meaning: The scientific study of yawning and its causes. A field of research examining why humans and animals yawn. The study of yawning behaviour and its contagious nature.
example_sentence: Chasmology tries to explain why yawning is so contagious. A study in chasmology linked yawning to brain temperature. He became interested in chasmology after reading about sleep science. Chasmology shows that even unborn babies yawn.

english_meaning: To strongly criticize or punish someone for doing something wrong. To correct someone through strong criticism, scolding, or punishment because of bad behavior, mistakes, or disobedience. It is often used by parents, teachers, leaders, or authorities when they want someone to improve their behavior.
example_sentence: The teacher chastised the students for making noise in the classroom. His mother chastised him for coming home late at night. The manager chastised the worker for ignoring safety rules. The coach chastised the team after their careless performance.

english_meaning: The state or practice of refraining from extramarital, or especially from all, sexual intercourse. The quality of being morally pure or celibate. Simplicity of style.
example_sentence: Some religious orders require a vow of chastity. He believed in the importance of chastity before marriage. The novel explores themes of love and chastity. Chastity was considered a great virtue in that society. The knight took a vow of chastity and poverty.

english_meaning: To talk to someone in a friendly or flirtatious way in order to attract them. To speak charmingly to a person hoping to start a romantic relationship. To talk to someone pleasantly in order to gain a favour or advantage. To engage a person in casual conversation with a hidden purpose.
example_sentence: He tried to chat up the girl sitting near the window. She was chatting up the manager to get a better table. Do not chat up strangers online without being careful. He spent the whole evening chatting up new clients.

english_meaning: An attempt to start a friendly or flirtatious conversation with someone. Informal talk intended to attract a person romantically. Persuasive or charming talk used to win someone's interest. Used before a noun, as in chat-up line, a remark used to begin flirting.
example_sentence: He used an old chat-up line that made everyone laugh. Her clever chat-up won her a new group of friends. That chat-up did not impress her at all. He practised his chat-up in front of the mirror before the party.

english_meaning: To talk quickly and continuously about small or unimportant things. Also, a series of quick sounds or casual talk. To talk a lot, often quickly and about unimportant things. It can also refer to rapid repeated sounds, such as teeth shaking from cold, birds making short sounds, or machines making repeated clicking noises. Light talk, gossip, or repeated noise.
example_sentence: The children chattered happily on their way to school. Her teeth chattered because of the cold wind. We could hear the birds chattering in the trees. There was a lot of chatter about the new policy in the office.

english_meaning: A person who talks a lot, especially about unimportant things. Someone who cannot stop chatting. A very talkative or gossipy individual. A person known for constant, lively conversation. Informal term for a highly communicative person.
example_sentence: My little sister is a real chatterbox at home. The teacher told the chatterbox to be quiet. He became a chatterbox after making new friends. She is such a chatterbox that no one else gets to speak.

english_meaning: A person employed to drive a private or luxury car for someone else. A professional driver hired to transport a passenger. To drive someone around in a car, especially as a duty or service. To act as a driver for another person.
example_sentence: The chauffeur opened the door and helped her into the car. He worked as a chauffeur for a wealthy family for many years. Her father chauffeured the children to school every morning. A chauffeur was waiting outside the hotel to collect the guests.

english_meaning: An exaggerated and aggressive belief in the superiority of one's own group, country, or cause. Excessive and blind patriotism that shows contempt for other nations. An unreasonable belief that one's own sex is superior to the other, especially male chauvinism. Prejudiced loyalty or devotion to a particular group or idea.
example_sentence: His chauvinism made it difficult for him to respect other cultures. Male chauvinism still limits opportunities for women in some workplaces. The speech was criticized for encouraging national chauvinism. She challenged the chauvinism she faced during her early career.

english_meaning: A person who shows excessive or prejudiced loyalty to a particular group, cause, or gender, often believing it is superior. Showing excessive loyalty or bias toward a particular group, cause, or gender.
example_sentence: He is a male chauvinist who believes women shouldn’t hold managerial positions. Her father’s chauvinist views often lead to arguments at home. The company was criticized for its chauvinist hiring practices. In the debate, his chauvinist attitude offended many participants.

english_meaning: Showing excessive and prejudiced support for one's own group, country, or gender. Aggressively patriotic in a biased way. Believing one's own group is superior to others.
example_sentence: His chauvinistic remarks offended many people. The group held chauvinistic views about other nations. She criticized his chauvinistic attitude toward women. The speech was full of chauvinistic pride.

english_meaning: In a chauvinistic or prejudiced manner. With excessive and biased loyalty to one's own group. In an aggressively patriotic or discriminatory way.
example_sentence: He spoke chauvinistically about his country's superiority. She was treated chauvinistically at the workplace. The leader behaved chauvinistically during the debate. They chauvinistically dismissed all foreign ideas.

english_meaning: Costing little money or less than expected. Of low quality or poorly made. Deserving little respect because of meanness. Easily obtained and therefore of little value.
example_sentence: I bought this shirt at a very cheap price. The furniture looks cheap and will not last. His cheap remarks upset everyone at the table. Cheap labour is common in that industry.

english_meaning: A person who is extremely stingy and reluctant to spend money. Someone who tries to avoid paying their fair share of expenses. An individual who constantly looks for the lowest price, often at the expense of quality. A miserly person who hoards wealth rather than enjoying it or sharing it.
example_sentence: My uncle is such a cheapskate that he never leaves a tip at restaurants. Don't be a cheapskate and at least chip in for the birthday gift. The cheapskate refused to pay for a taxi and made us walk three miles in the rain. She bought the lowest quality paint because she is a notorious cheapskate.

english_meaning: To act dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage. To deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true. To be sexually unfaithful to a spouse or partner. A person who behaves in a dishonest way or a swindler. A strategy or trick used to bypass rules in a game or task.
example_sentence: He tried to cheat on the final exam by hiding notes under his desk. It is heartbreaking when someone decides to cheat on their loyal partner. The salesman was a known cheat who sold broken appliances to unsuspecting customers. You shouldn't cheat at cards even if it is just a friendly game among friends.

english_meaning: To return, revisit, or inquire again after some time to find out new information, updates, or results. It’s often used when something is not ready yet or when information is expected later.
example_sentence: I’ll check back later to see if he’s in. Check back with me tomorrow for an update. You should check back after lunch. The manager said to check back next week.

english_meaning: To stop and examine something or someone while passing. To visit briefly.
example_sentence: I’ll check by your office this afternoon. Could you check by the store on your way home? She checked by to drop off the papers. Please check by later for the results.

english_meaning: To register at a hotel or airport. To officially report your presence at a place. To contact or update someone about your status or location.
example_sentence: We checked in at the hotel at 3 PM. I usually check in online. I’ll check in with you later to see how you’re doing. He forgot to check in at the reception and went straight to his room.

english_meaning: To investigate or look into something. To register at a hotel or facility. To register or book yourself in.
example_sentence: The police are checking into the case. We checked into the hotel at noon. He checked into rehab last week. I’ll check into the reason for the delay.

english_meaning: To mark items on a list after verifying or completing them. To tick (✓) something to show it is done, noted, or confirmed.
example_sentence: She checked off the tasks one by one. I’ll check off the names as they arrive. Please check off each task on the list as you complete it. The teacher asked the students to check off the items they had studied.

english_meaning: To leave a hotel after paying the bill. To inspect or look at something with attention. To try something to see how it works or feels. To make sure something is correct. To take something after recording, like from a library. To notice someone, often with admiration. To leave, examine, try, or confirm something.
example_sentence: They checked out of the hotel at noon. Let’s check out the new restaurant in town tonight. Can you check out if the report has any mistakes? She caught him checking her out at the party.

english_meaning: To examine something carefully to make sure it is correct or in good condition.
example_sentence: Check over your answers before submitting. The mechanic checked over the car. She checked over the report twice. Let’s check over the details once more.

english_meaning: To confirm or consult with someone before taking action. To ask, confirm, or verify something with someone.
example_sentence: You should check with your doctor first. Check with your manager before sending the email. I’ll check with her about the meeting time. Please check with HR for approval.

english_meaning: A number or value calculated from a block of digital data and stored or transmitted with it. A value recalculated and compared with the original to detect accidental errors, corruption, or alteration in data.
example_sentence: The software calculates a checksum to verify the downloaded file. If the checksum matches, the data is considered valid. An incorrect checksum indicates that the file was corrupted during transfer. The network protocol uses a cyclic redundancy checksum for error detection.

english_meaning: Either side of the face below the eye and between the nose and the ear. The soft fleshy part of the side of the face. Rude, bold, or disrespectful behavior or speech. To speak or behave in a rude and disrespectful way toward someone.
example_sentence: The cold wind made her cheeks turn red. He kissed his mother on the cheek before leaving. Tears rolled down the child's cheeks. She had the cheek to ask for another favor after all that.

english_meaning: Very close together, side by side. Crowded closely with little space in between. Living or existing in close association with something else.
example_sentence: Old houses stand cheek by jowl in the narrow lane. The passengers sat cheek by jowl in the crowded bus. Luxury towers rise cheek by jowl with poor settlements. The two shops operate cheek by jowl on the same street.

english_meaning: Rude in a funny or annoying way. A lightly rude or showing no respect, but often in a funny way. Displaying or marked by rude boldness.
example_sentence: You're getting far too cheeky!. She's got such a cheeky grin. Don't be so cheeky!. The response seems to me cheeky. He's just so cheeky, he can get away with anything.

english_meaning: A shout of applause or encouragement. Lightness of mind and feeling. Something that gladdens. To utter a shout of applause or triumph. To be mentally or emotionally disposed. To make glad or happy. To applaud with shouts.
example_sentence: The players were greeted with loud cheers. The audience let out a cheer.  Loud cheers were coming from the bleachers. Everyone cheered as the winners received their medals.

english_meaning: To encourage or support someone. To shout, clap, or speak positively in order to give someone confidence, motivation, or support, especially during a competition, performance, or difficult task
example_sentence: The crowd cheered on the team until the final whistle. Parents stood by the field to cheer on their children. Her friends cheered her on during the race. We cheered on the workers as they completed the project.

english_meaning: Become happier or make someone feel happier after sadness, worry, or disappointment. It is often used as a friendly request or encouragement to improve mood.
example_sentence: Cheer up, things will get better soon. She tried to cheer up her friend after the bad news. Music always cheers me up when I feel low. He bought her flowers to cheer her up.

english_meaning: Noticeably happy and optimistic. Bright and pleasant. Causing happiness by its nature or appearance.
example_sentence: She has a very cheerful personality. The room was decorated in cheerful colors like yellow and orange. He gave a cheerful wave as he drove away. Despite his problems, he remained cheerful. A cheerful fire was burning in the hearth.

english_meaning: A food made from the pressed curds of milk. A dairy product available in many varieties and flavors. Informal word said to make people smile in photos. Slang for something cheesy or overly sentimental.
example_sentence: He loves cheese on his sandwiches. Say cheese and smile for the camera. Italy is famous for its many types of cheese. The film was full of cheese but people enjoyed it.

english_meaning: To annoy or irritate someone intensely. To make someone feel frustrated or fed up. To provoke a sense of resentment or dissatisfaction. To cause someone to lose their patience. To bother or disturb someone's peace of mind.
example_sentence: It really cheeses me off when people talk loudly in the cinema. His arrogant attitude managed to cheese off the entire committee. Don't cheese her off right now because she is already stressed. The constant delays at the airport began to cheese off the passengers.

english_meaning: To love, value, or protect something deeply. To hold someone or something dear in your heart. It also means to care for something with affection, protect it carefully, or keep a memory or hope alive for a long time.
example_sentence: Children need to be cherished. She will always cherish her childhood memories. He cherishes the time he spends with his family. They cherish their cultural traditions. I cherish the hope of a better future.

english_meaning: A small round fruit with shiny red or dark skin and a single stone. The tree that produces cherries, often admired for its blossom. A bright red colour like that of the ripe fruit. Something considered the best or most desirable part of a group.
example_sentence: He placed a cherry on top of the ice cream. The cherry trees turn pink every spring. She wore a cherry red dress to the dinner. That contract was the cherry of the whole deal.

english_meaning: The front part of the upper body between the neck and the abdomen. The part of the body that contains the heart and lungs, protected by the ribs. A large strong box with a lid used for storing things. A supply of money belonging to an organization, as in a war chest.
