example_sentence: He felt a sharp pain in his chest and called the doctor. The old wooden chest was full of family letters. She held the baby close to her chest. Deep breathing exercises help expand the chest.

english_meaning: A glossy brown nut that may be roasted and eaten. The large European tree that produces these nuts. A reddish-brown color. A horse of a reddish-brown color. An old or stale joke or story.
example_sentence: We roasted chestnuts over the open fire. The furniture was made of dark chestnut wood. That old joke is a real chestnut; I've heard it a dozen times. Her hair was a beautiful shade of chestnut. He rode a handsome chestnut mare.

english_meaning: To have a long, relaxed conversation with someone. To chat in a friendly and informal way. To gossip or share stories with friends. To discuss unimportant matters casually. To spend time talking pleasantly.
example_sentence: We sat on the porch and chewed the fat for hours. Grandpa loves to chew the fat with his old friends. Let us chew the fat over a cup of tea. They often chew the fat during lunch breaks.

english_meaning: A rhetorical device in which words or ideas are repeated in reverse order. A crossed arrangement of parallel phrases. A structure that balances two clauses by reversing their order. An inverted pattern used for emphasis or elegance.
example_sentence: Ask not what your country can do for you is often discussed as chiasmus. The poet used chiasmus to give the line a memorable shape. Chiasmus can make an argument sound balanced. Students practiced writing chiasmus with opposite word order.

english_meaning: Very fashionable. Being or in accordance with the current fashion. The quality or state of being stylish, fashionableness.
example_sentence: A chic new restaurant. She is always so chic. The phone was small & chic & fit perfectly into the palm of my hand.

english_meaning: A common domestic fowl raised for its eggs and meat. The flesh of this bird used as a food source. A person who is perceived as cowardly or lacking courage. To act in a cowardly manner or to withdraw from a situation due to fear. A young bird, especially a domestic hen or rooster. A competition or game of nerves where two parties head toward a collision to see who swerves first.
example_sentence: The farmer feeds the chicken every morning at dawn. We decided to roast a whole chicken for Sunday dinner. Don't be such a chicken and jump into the pool. He was going to ask her out but he chickened out at the last minute.

english_meaning: Easily frightened and lacking courage. Timid and unwilling to take risks. Cowardly in the face of danger or difficulty.
example_sentence: He was too chicken hearted to complain about the mistake. Don't be chicken hearted; just tell her the truth. The chicken hearted soldier fled at the first shot. She called him chicken hearted for avoiding the interview.

english_meaning: To decide not to do something because of fear at the last moment. To back out of a plan due to nervousness or cowardice. To lose courage and avoid a challenge. To withdraw from a commitment because of fear. To become too scared to follow through with an action.
example_sentence: He was ready to jump but chickened out at the last second. Don't chicken out now, we have come too far. She chickened out of giving the speech in front of the class. I hope he doesn't chicken out of the fight.

english_meaning: A dilemma in which two things depend on each other, making it difficult or impossible to determine which came first or caused the other. A problem of circular cause and effect.
example_sentence: Whether low confidence causes poor performance or the reverse is a chicken-and-egg situation. Startups and investors often face a chicken-and-egg situation over funding and growth. The need for users and the need for content created a chicken-and-egg situation for the platform. Economists debate whether low wages reduce skills or low skills reduce wages, another chicken-and-egg situation.

english_meaning: Bad actions eventually bring unpleasant consequences to the person responsible. Past mistakes or wrongdoing eventually return to cause trouble. The results of one's choices, especially harmful ones, cannot be avoided forever.
synonyms: ["Face the consequences","Reap what you sow","Pay the price","Get one's comeuppance","Actions have consequences"]
antonyms: ["Escape the consequences","Go unpunished","Get away with it","Avoid accountability"]
example_sentence: After years of dishonest dealing, his chickens finally came home to roost. The company ignored safety rules, and now the chickens have come home to roost. Her careless spending caught up with her when the chickens came home to roost. When the scandal became public, the politician's chickens came home to roost.

english_meaning: A cowardly or petty person, something not worth attention. Cowardly, afraid to take risks or face challenges. Petty, mean, or small-minded in behavior. Something trivial or unimportant.
example_sentence: He was too chickenshit to tell the truth. Don’t be chickenshit, take responsibility for your actions. The argument was just a bunch of chickenshit drama. She called him chickenshit for running away from the fight.

english_meaning: A round, pale brown pulse used widely in cooking. A protein-rich legume eaten boiled, roasted, or ground into flour. The plant grown for these seeds. The main ingredient in dishes such as hummus and chana curry.
example_sentence: Chickpea curry is served with hot bread. She soaked the chickpeas overnight. Roasted chickpeas make a healthy snack. Chickpea flour is used to make fritters.

english_meaning: Small round beige legumes often used in cooking. They are a rich source of protein and fiber. They are commonly used in dishes like hummus, salads, curries and soups. They can be eaten boiled, roasted or ground into flour.
example_sentence: She cooked chickpeas to make a fresh bowl of hummus. Roasted chickpeas are a healthy snack. Chickpeas add a rich texture to vegetable soups. They bought dried chickpeas from the market for the weekend meal.

english_meaning: To scold or rebuke. To voice disapproval to; to reproach in a mild and constructive manner.
example_sentence: She chided him for his bad manners. The mother gently chided her child for not sharing his toys. 'You should have been more careful,' he chided. I chided myself for my carelessness. The teacher chided the student for being disruptive.

english_meaning: A small, hot-tasting pod of a variety of capsicum, used in chopping and spicing food. It refers to the dried pod of this plant, often ground into a powder. The plant bearing these spicy fruits is cultivated worldwide. It provides a sharp and pungent flavor to dishes.
example_sentence: The chef added a pinch of chili powder to make the soup spicy. We grew some green chili plants in our backyard. Be careful not to touch your eyes after chopping a fresh chili. The red chili gives this dish its vibrant color and fiery taste.

english_meaning: An unpleasant feeling of coldness in the atmosphere, one's surroundings, or the body. To make something cold. To relax or calm down. A feeling of fear or dread.
example_sentence: There was a chill in the autumn air. Chill the wine before serving. You need to chill and stop worrying so much. A chill went down my spine when I heard the news. He caught a chill after walking in the rain.

english_meaning: Horrifying or frightening. Frightening, usually because it is connected with something violent or cruel. Causing or likely to cause a chill. Making chilly or cold, depressing, discouraging, cold, distant.
example_sentence: The film evokes chilling reminders of the war. The monument stands as a chilling reminder of man's inhumanity to man. The chilling plot of this suspenseful novel moves with amazing quickness.

english_meaning: A musical sound produced by a set of bells or a clock. To make a clear ringing sound when struck. To be in agreement or harmony with something else. To interrupt or join a conversation, often by adding a comment. A set of tuned bells or metal tubes used in an orchestra.
example_sentence: The grandfather clock began to chime exactly at midnight. His views on the project chime perfectly with the company's long-term goals. I wanted to chime in with a suggestion before the meeting ended. The wind caused the tubular bells to chime softly in the garden.

english_meaning: To interrupt a conversation politely or abruptly to express an opinion. To join in a discussion or contribute a comment. To harmonize or agree with what is being said. To ring out or sound in unison like bells. To enter into a conversation after someone else has spoken.
example_sentence: I waited for a pause in their argument to chime in with my own suggestion. Feel free to chime in if you have any ideas regarding the new project. My brother would always chime in with a joke whenever the mood got too serious. The clocks in the hallway began to chime in together at the stroke of midnight.

english_meaning: To interrupt or join a conversation to add one's opinion. To express agreement with what someone else has said. To harmonize or be consistent with another thing. To break into a discussion suddenly with a comment. To contribute a thought to a group dialogue.
example_sentence: He waited for a pause in the discussion to chime in with his own suggestion. She was quick to chime in with her support for the new policy. It is rude to chime in with a criticism before hearing the full story. His observations chime in with the findings of the recent research study.

english_meaning: To interrupt a conversation by offering one's opinion or adding information. To join a discussion or debate, often suddenly or unexpectedly. To harmonize or agree with what others are saying. To break into a group talk to provide support for a point. To participate in a verbal exchange with a timely comment.
example_sentence: She decided to chime into the debate when she heard the incorrect statistics. Everyone was silent until Mark chose to chime into the discussion with a joke. Feel free to chime into our conversation if you have any suggestions. I didn't mean to chime into your private talk, but I couldn't help overhearing.

english_meaning: Something imaginary or unrealistic. An illusion or fabrication of the mind. A creature with a lion's head, a goat's body and a snake’s tail that can breathe out fire.
example_sentence: His plan to become rich overnight was nothing but a chimera. Perfect equality in society is often seen as a chimera. She finally realized that her dream was a chimera. The project was based on a chimera rather than real facts.

english_meaning: A vertical channel or pipe which conducts smoke and combustion gases up from a fire, furnace, or boiler. A glass tube fitted round the flame of an oil or gas lamp to protect it from drafts and promote combustion.
example_sentence: Smoke billowed from the factory chimney. Santa Claus is said to come down the chimney on Christmas Eve. The old house had a tall brick chimney. We need to get the chimney cleaned before winter. The bird built its nest on top of the chimney.

english_meaning: The front part of the lower jaw below the mouth. The protruding part of the face beneath the lower lip. Courage or the ability to endure difficulty, as in the phrase to keep one's chin up.
example_sentence: He rested his chin on his hand while thinking. The boxer was hit hard on the chin. She lifted her chin proudly and walked away. Keep your chin up; things will get better soon.

english_meaning: A pale or medium blue color like that seen on Chinese porcelain. A soft greyish-blue shade. A blue dye formerly used in laundering to whiten clothes.
example_sentence: The vase was decorated in a delicate china blue pattern. She painted the kitchen walls china blue. The china blue design reminded her of antique porcelain. Old houses often used china blue for door frames.

english_meaning: Of a pale or soft blue color like Chinese porcelain. Having a light greyish-blue shade typical of fine china. A gentle blue tone used in art and decoration.
example_sentence: The china-blue plates were arranged on the shelf. She wore a china-blue scarf with her white dress. The china-blue tiles gave the bathroom a classic look. He admired the china-blue glaze on the old teapot.

english_meaning: A person, animal, or plant that loves or thrives in snowy conditions. Someone or something that prefers snow and cold environments. The word is also used in biology and ecology for organisms that live well in snowy climates such as alpine plants, polar animals, or people who enjoy winter landscapes and snow activities.
example_sentence: The mountaineer was a true chionophile who always looked forward to winter expeditions. Some alpine plants are chionophiles, growing best under snow covered conditions. As a chionophile, she enjoys skiing and walking through snowy forests. Many polar animals can be considered chionophiles because they thrive in snowy habitats.

english_meaning: A person who fears snow. A person who experiences fear, anxiety, or strong dislike toward snow or snowy weather. This fear may come from past experiences, discomfort with cold climates, or worry about accidents and problems caused by snow such as slippery roads or storms.
synonyms: ["Snow phobic person","Cryophobic person","Winter averse person","Person afraid of snow"]
example_sentence: The chionophobe avoided traveling to northern countries during winter. Because she was a chionophobe, the sight of heavy snowfall made her anxious. Many people enjoy skiing, but a chionophobe prefers warm climates. The chionophobe stayed indoors whenever the weather forecast predicted snow.

english_meaning: Reduce gradually. To remove small amounts gradually or diminish slowly over time.
example_sentence: The debt was chipped away over years. He chipped away at the ice. Critics chipped away at the proposal. Time chipped away at their patience.

english_meaning: To contribute or give help, money, or ideas. To voluntarily contribute something often money, time, effort, or advice towards a shared goal, project, or cause. It implies participating alongside others to achieve a collective result.
example_sentence: Everyone chipped in for the gift. She chipped in with advice. They chipped in to help. He chipped in with some money.

english_meaning: Break small piece. To break off a small fragment from a larger object.
example_sentence: A piece chipped off the vase. He chipped off a corner of chocolate. Paint chipped off the wall. The stone chipped off the monument.

english_meaning: Remove part by cutting. To hollow out, carve, or remove a portion of a solid material by repeatedly striking or cutting small pieces from it. Often used for wood, stone, ice, or other hard surfaces.
example_sentence: He chipped out a piece of wood. She chipped out ice from the tray. They chipped out the damaged tile. He chipped out a section of the rock.

english_meaning: Cheerful and lively in manner. Full of energy and happiness. Talking or behaving in a bright and joyful way. Sounding pleasant and enthusiastic. Making short, high sounds like a bird.
example_sentence: She was in a chirpy mood after receiving the good news. His chirpy voice filled the room with happiness. The children were chirpy on their first day of holiday. The birds sounded chirpy in the early morning.

english_meaning: To talk informally about simple and casual topics. To engage in light and friendly conversation without serious purpose. Light and informal conversation about ordinary things. It is casual talk meant to pass time or create a friendly atmosphere.
example_sentence: We chit chat whenever we meet after work. They were chit chatting near the gate. She loves to chit chat while cooking. Their chit chat made the long wait easier. I enjoy morning chit chat with my colleagues. The room was full of light chit chat before the event began.

english_meaning: Courteous, honorable, and noble behavior, especially by men toward women. A set of qualities associated with knighthood, including bravery, honor, and respect for women. It often implies courteous behavior and moral integrity in social interactions.
example_sentence: The knight was praised for his chivalry during the battle. He opened the door for her out of simple chivalry. Chivalry is rare in modern times but still appreciated. She admired his chivalry and kind manners.

english_meaning: An organized group of singers, typically one that performs in a church. The part of a cathedral or large church between the altar and the nave used by the singers. A group of instruments of the same family playing together. A group of people singing in unison. The act or art of singing in a chorus or group setting.
example_sentence: The church choir sang beautifully during the Sunday service. She decided to join the local choir to improve her vocal skills. The orchestra featured a magnificent brass choir. They stood in the choir behind the altar.

english_meaning: To be unable to breathe due to blocked airway. To block or clog a passage or opening. To fail under pressure, especially in sports or performance. To suppress or restrain emotions or speech. A device controlling the air supply to an engine.
example_sentence: He almost choked on a piece of bread. Weeds began to choke the flower beds. The player choked during the final minutes of the game. She tried not to choke on her tears.

english_meaning: To restrain or suppress strong emotion, tears, or laughter. To hold back words that one wants to say. To prevent an emotional reaction from being visible. To stop oneself from crying or shouting. To control a strong feeling with effort.
example_sentence: He choked back tears while telling the story. She choked back a laugh during the serious meeting. I had to choke back my anger and stay polite. He choked back the harsh words he wanted to say.

english_meaning: A chain collar used on dogs that tightens when pulled. A training tool designed to control a dog's behavior through pressure. A metal loop worn around the neck to correct pulling on the leash. A controversial device criticized for causing harm. A restraint used mainly in dog training.
example_sentence: The trainer used a choke chain to control the large dog. Many experts warn against using a choke chain on pets. She replaced the choke chain with a soft harness. A choke chain should never be left on a dog unattended.

english_meaning: A collar designed to tighten around an animal's neck, especially a dog, when it pulls on the leash. A training collar made of metal chain or rope that constricts to correct a dog's behavior. A type of restraining collar used to control strong or disobedient animals by applying pressure. Any tight neckband or restraint that limits movement or breathing.
example_sentence: The trainer used a choke collar to teach the large dog to walk beside him. Many animal welfare groups oppose the use of a choke collar on pets. She replaced the choke collar with a softer harness for her puppy. A choke collar can injure a dog if it is not used correctly.

english_meaning: To swallow something with great difficulty. To force oneself to eat or drink unpleasant food. To suppress a strong emotion or reaction. To accept something reluctantly. To hold back tears, anger, or laughter.
example_sentence: He managed to choke down the bitter medicine. She had to choke down her tears in public. The soldiers choked down cold rations before the march. He choked down his anger and stayed silent.

english_meaning: To stop or restrict the flow or supply of something. To prevent something from developing or continuing. To silence or suppress a person or opinion. To cut off communication or resources. To hinder growth or progress.
example_sentence: High taxes could choke off economic growth. The government moved to choke off illegal funding. Critics say the policy will choke off innovation. Sanctions were used to choke off arms supplies.

english_meaning: To say something with difficulty due to emotion. To render someone unconscious by cutting off airflow. To suppress or eliminate something completely. To overpower and silence someone. To grow so densely that other plants cannot survive.
example_sentence: She managed to choke out a few words of thanks. The wrestler choked out his opponent in the third round. Weeds can choke out young crops. He tried to choke out an apology.

english_meaning: To become too emotional to speak clearly. To be overcome by strong feelings such as sadness or gratitude. To become blocked or clogged. In sports, to grip a bat or racquet closer to the head. To lose composure due to emotion.
example_sentence: She choked up while giving her father's eulogy. He tried to speak but choked up before the audience. Dust made the vents choke up quickly. The batter chose to choke up on the bat for better control.

english_meaning: A small wild cherry tree native to North America that produces bitter dark red or black fruit. The tart astringent fruit of this tree, often used in jams, jellies, syrups, and wines. A shrub or tree of the rose family known for its clusters of white flowers and sour berries. The wood of this tree, sometimes used in small woodworking projects.
example_sentence: The children were warned not to eat the raw chokecherry berries. My grandmother made delicious jelly from chokecherry fruit every summer. A large chokecherry tree grew beside the old farmhouse. Birds love to feed on ripe chokecherry clusters in late summer.

english_meaning: Unable to breathe properly because the throat or airway is blocked. Overcome by strong emotion so that one cannot speak clearly. Filled or blocked completely with something, such as smoke, dust, or weeds. Prevented from growing, developing, or functioning normally. Failed to perform well under pressure, especially in a competition.
example_sentence: He choked on a piece of bread and started coughing. Her voice choked with emotion as she thanked her family. The garden was choked with weeds after the rainy season. The player choked in the final minutes of the match.

english_meaning: A close-fitting necklace worn tightly around the neck. A person who chokes, especially one who fails under pressure. Something that causes choking or restricts breathing. A high collar or narrow band around the neck. In sports, a player known for failing in crucial moments.
example_sentence: She wore a pearl choker to the wedding. Fans called him a choker after the missed penalty. The dog's choker chain must be used carefully. Her diamond choker sparkled under the lights.

english_meaning: A serious infectious disease that causes severe diarrhea and dehydration, usually spread through contaminated water or food. (A bacterial disease caused by Vibrio cholerae. It affects the small intestine, leading to rapid loss of fluids and salts from the body. Without quick treatment, it can be fatal. The disease is often linked to poor sanitation and unsafe drinking water.)
example_sentence: Cholera spread quickly in the village after heavy rains contaminated the water supply. The doctors set up emergency camps to treat cholera patients. Proper sanitation and clean drinking water can prevent cholera outbreaks. In the 19th century, cholera epidemics claimed thousands of lives across Europe and Asia.

english_meaning: To pick one thing or person from a number of possibilities. To decide on a particular course of action. To prefer or want something rather than something else.
example_sentence: You may choose any two subjects from the list. She chose to stay quiet during the meeting. It is hard to choose between the two offers. Voters will choose a new mayor next month.

english_meaning: Relating to or sung by a choir or chorus. Written for or performed by a group of singers. Connected with choral music or singing in a group.
example_sentence: The church is famous for its beautiful choral music. She joined a choral society soon after moving to the city. The choir gave a moving choral performance of the symphony. He composed several choral works for the festival.

english_meaning: A straight line segment connecting two points on a circle. A group of musical notes played simultaneously. An emotional response or feeling evoked by something. A structural member in engineering.
example_sentence: Draw a chord across the circle. The musician played a beautiful chord on the guitar. The story struck a chord with the audience. The bridge uses steel chords for support.

english_meaning: A routine task, especially a small job done regularly at home. A regular or everyday task that needs to be done, often related to household work.
example_sentence: I have to finish my chores before I can watch TV. Cleaning the kitchen is my least favorite chore. Feeding the chickens is part of his daily chores. For him, attending long meetings is a real chore.

english_meaning: The thin, dark-coloured middle layer of the eyeball lying between the retina and the sclera. A layer densely packed with blood vessels that supplies oxygen and nutrients to the retina. The pigmented tissue that absorbs stray light and prevents reflection inside the eye.
example_sentence: The choroid supplies blood to the outer part of the retina. Its dark pigment stops light from scattering inside the eye. The choroid lies between the sclera and the retina. Inflammation of the choroid can affect vision.

english_meaning: A part of a song which is repeated after each verse. A large organized group of singers, especially one that performs in concerts or church services. Something said or sung by many people at the same time.
example_sentence: I'll sing the verses and I'd like you all to join in the chorus. She quickly left the chorus for a starring role. The newcomers added their voices to the chorus expressing delight at the result. ‘Hello, Paul,’ they chorused.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving chromosomes. Concerning the structures in cells that contain genetic information. Associated with chromosomal abnormalities or genetic disorders. Of or pertaining to DNA organization in the nucleus.
example_sentence: Down syndrome is a chromosomal disorder. Chromosomal abnormalities can be detected prenatally. The test revealed a chromosomal mutation. Chromosomal research advances genetic understanding.

english_meaning: A thread-like structure in the cell nucleus carrying genetic information. A DNA molecule containing many genes organized with proteins. The structure that holds hereditary information in living organisms. A carrier of genetic material passed from parents to offspring.
example_sentence: Humans have 46 chromosomes in each cell. The X and Y chromosomes determine biological sex. Chromosomes contain thousands of genes. Chromosomal abnormalities can cause genetic disorders.

english_meaning: Relating to time, according to time. Lasting for a long time, difficult to cure. Having had a disease for a long time. That continues over an extended period of time. Suffering from such affliction.
example_sentence: Chronic patients must learn to live with their condition. He's a chronic smoker. They left him in a chronic condition.

english_meaning: In a manner that persists over a long period of time. Habitually or constantly recurring. In a way characteristic of chronic conditions. Persistently or continually.
example_sentence: He is chronically late to meetings. The patient is chronically ill with diabetes. The region is chronically affected by drought. She suffers chronically from migraines.

english_meaning: To record or describe events in the order they happen. To document or record events carefully and systematically. Factual and detailed record of historical events arranged according to time. It often describes events of a nation, community, or individual life.
example_sentence: The historian wrote a chronicle of the ancient kingdom. The book chronicles the struggles of the freedom movement. The newspaper became a daily chronicle of city life. She carefully chronicled her journey in her diary. She chronicled her daily life in a journal. The museum displayed an ancient chronicle written on parchment. Family albums often become a visual chronicle of generations.

english_meaning: Arranged according to the order of time. Relating to dates, sequence, or the order in which events occur. Presented from earliest to latest or in another clear time order.
example_sentence: The book gives a chronological account of the war. Please make a chronological list of your jobs. The museum display follows a chronological order. Chronological records help researchers track changes. His memory of events was not chronological.

english_meaning: A person's actual age measured from the date of birth. Age expressed in years, months, and days according to calendar time. The amount of time a person has lived, regardless of physical, mental, or emotional development.
synonyms: ["Actual age","Calendar age","Age by birth date","Time age","Legal age"]
example_sentence: Her chronological age is ten years. Chronological age does not always match emotional maturity. Doctors compared the child's bone age with his chronological age. The form asks for chronological age in years and months. Fitness can differ greatly among people of the same chronological age.

english_meaning: In the order in which events happened. According to time sequence from earliest to latest or from latest to earliest. In a way arranged by date or historical order.
example_sentence: Arrange the events chronologically. The story is told chronologically from childhood to old age. Chronologically, the letter came before the meeting. The files were sorted chronologically by date. It is easier to understand history when it is presented chronologically.

english_meaning: The arrangement of events in the order in which they happened. A timeline showing important dates and events. The science of arranging historical records by date. A sequence of developments in a particular field.
example_sentence: The teacher explained the chronology of the independence movement. It is important to understand the chronology of events in a criminal case. The book presents the chronology of human evolution. She arranged her experiences in strict chronology for her autobiography.

english_meaning: A very accurate timekeeping instrument. A precise clock or watch, especially one used in navigation, science, or measuring exact time. A device designed to keep time reliably under changing conditions.
example_sentence: The ship carried a marine chronometer for navigation. A chronometer must keep very accurate time. The scientist used a chronometer during the experiment. Old chronometers are valuable to collectors. The watch was tested and certified as a chronometer.

english_meaning: Fear of time passing or the future. Chronophobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by a persistent fear or extreme discomfort related to the passage of time, aging, deadlines, or the future. It can cause stress, panic, or obsessive behaviors around time management.
example_sentence: He could not relax because his chronophobia made him anxious about growing old. Her chronophobia caused her to avoid looking at clocks or calendars. Students with chronophobia often panic as exams approach. The elderly man’s chronophobia made him obsess over each day passing.

english_meaning: The hard protective case of a moth or butterfly during the pupal stage. The pupa of a butterfly, especially while enclosed in its case. A protected stage of development before a major transformation. A state or place in which something new gradually forms.
example_sentence: The caterpillar formed a chrysalis beneath a leaf. A butterfly eventually emerged from the chrysalis. The quiet studio became a chrysalis for her new ideas. The organization is still in a chrysalis stage of development.

english_meaning: A flowering plant of the daisy family with brightly colored ornamental blooms. The flower of this plant, often called a mum. A plant cultivated for gardens, displays, medicine, tea, or symbolic ceremonies. A symbol of longevity, joy, honor, grief, or remembrance in different cultures.
example_sentence: She planted yellow chrysanthemums along the path. The vase held a single white chrysanthemum. Chrysanthemum tea has a light floral taste. Gardeners protect chrysanthemums from early frost.

english_meaning: Plump and rounded. Having a full, rounded shape.
example_sentence: He was a chubby baby with rosy cheeks. Her fingers were short and chubby. The chubby cat lay sleeping in the sun. I was a bit chubby as a child. He pinched the baby's chubby cheeks.

english_meaning: To throw something carelessly or casually. To touch someone playfully under the chin. To give up or quit. A cut of beef from the neck to the ribs.
example_sentence: Chuck the ball over here. She gave him a playful chuck under the chin. He decided to chuck his job and travel the world. Just chuck your coat on the bed. He chuckled the old newspapers into the bin.

english_meaning: A close friend or companion. Someone with whom one spends a lot of friendly time. Bait consisting of chopped fish thrown into the water to attract fish. To be friendly or intimate with someone.
example_sentence: He has been my chum since childhood. She invited her old chums to the party. The fishermen used chum to attract sharks. They chummed together during their college days.

english_meaning: A thick, compact piece or lump of something. A substantial part of a larger amount. To cut or break something into chunks.
example_sentence: He ate a chunk of bread with the soup. A large chunk of the budget went to repairs. Cut the vegetables into small chunks. The rock broke into a chunk of stone.

english_meaning: Rude, impolite, harsh, or unfriendly in behavior. A person’s behavior when they are bad-tempered, rude, uncivil, ill-mannered, or lacking politeness and kindness. It can also describe someone who behaves in a gruff, insensitive, or ungracious way, especially when they should be more respectful or thankful.
example_sentence: His churlish reply offended everyone in the room. It was churlish of her not to thank them for their help. The shopkeeper gave us a churlish look and refused to listen. Even when he was upset, he tried not to sound churlish.

english_meaning: To stir or shake something strongly, especially liquid like milk or cream, to make butter. To move water, mud, or another substance violently. To feel upset or uneasy in the stomach or mind. To produce something continuously in large amounts, often carelessly. To repeatedly replace customers, employees, or products in business. A container or machine used for making butter. A state of constant movement or change. The rate at which customers or employees leave and are replaced.
example_sentence: The farmer churned the cream to make fresh butter. Strong winds churned the sea into huge waves. My stomach began to churn before the interview. The factory churns out thousands of products every day. The company is worried about customer churn this year. There was a churn of emotions after the surprising announcement.

english_meaning: A sloping channel or slide used for sending things down to a lower level. A steep natural descent in a river or on a mountainside. A short informal word for a parachute. A narrow passage through which animals are moved.
example_sentence: The workers dropped the rubble down the chute into the truck. Children slid down the water chute again and again. The pilot pulled the cord and his chute opened at once. Cattle were driven one by one through the narrow chute.

english_meaning: A large insect known for the loud continuous sound made by the males in hot weather. A tree-dwelling insect whose young live underground for years before emerging.
example_sentence: The cicadas sang loudly all through the afternoon. A cicada clung to the bark of the old tree. The sound of cicadas filled the summer evening. Cicadas emerge from the soil after many years.

english_meaning: A guide who shows and explains places of interest to visitors. A knowledgeable person who leads sightseers around antiquities or monuments. A mentor who introduces someone to a subject or field.
example_sentence: An elderly cicerone led us through the ruined fort. She acted as our cicerone in the old city. The cicerone explained every carving on the temple wall. He was a patient cicerone to young researchers.

english_meaning: The small end part of a cigarette left after smoking. The small piece that remains of a cigarette after it has been smoked, usually the filter with a little tobacco left.
example_sentence: Don’t throw cigarette butts on the ground. He picked up the cigarette butt. He threw the cigarette butt on the street instead of using the ashtray. The park was full of cigarette butts after the concert.

english_meaning: To gird or surround with a band or enclosure. A belt, sash, or cord worn around the waist, especially as part of religious clothing. Something that encircles or surrounds like a ring, band, or boundary.
example_sentence: The priest tied a cincture around his robe before the ceremony. A ring of hills formed a natural cincture around the village. The warrior cinctured his armor tightly before battle. The forest acted as a green cincture surrounding the lake.

english_meaning: A small piece of partly burned coal or wood that has stopped giving off flames but still has combustible matter in it. A piece of burnt material.
example_sentence: The fire had burned down to just cinders. A hot cinder from the fireplace landed on the rug. The path was made of cinders. The volcano spewed ash and cinders into the air. By morning, only cinders remained of the campfire.

english_meaning: A building or hall where films are shown to the public. The art and industry of making films. Films considered as a whole or as a form of art. The experience of watching movies on a large screen.
example_sentence: We went to the cinema on Sunday evening. Pakistani cinema has changed a great deal. The new cinema has six screens. He has written widely about world cinema.

english_meaning: A person who goes to the cinema to watch films, especially regularly. A member of a film audience. Someone who enjoys watching movies at a cinema hall.
example_sentence: The average cinemagoer prefers comedy to drama. Ticket prices have risen for the ordinary cinemagoer. As a regular cinemagoer, she knows every new release. The survey questioned two hundred cinemagoers.

english_meaning: Relating to the cinema or the making of films. Having the visual quality, atmosphere, or scale typical of a good film. Beautifully composed and dramatic in appearance. Suitable for being filmed or shown on the big screen.
example_sentence: The documentary has a strikingly cinematic style. Sunset over the valley created a cinematic view. He praised the film's cinematic camera work. The novel is written in a highly cinematic manner.

english_meaning: The person responsible for filming and lighting a motion picture. A director of photography who shapes the visual look of a film. A professional camera artist in film production.
example_sentence: The cinematographer chose soft light for the final scene. She works as a cinematographer for documentaries. A skilled cinematographer can transform a simple set. The director praised his cinematographer publicly.

english_meaning: Relating to cinematography or the art of motion-picture photography. Concerned with the techniques of filming and camera work. Having qualities typical of film photography and lighting.
example_sentence: The film won an award for its cinematographic quality. Students learn basic cinematographic techniques. The scene shows fine cinematographic skill. He studies the cinematographic history of the region.

english_meaning: The art and technique of photographing scenes for a film. The work of lighting and operating cameras in film production. The visual style created by camera work in a movie.
example_sentence: The cinematography in this film is breathtaking. She studied cinematography in London. Good cinematography can lift an ordinary story. The award for best cinematography went to a young artist.

english_meaning: A genus of evergreen trees and shrubs known for aromatic bark, commonly called cinnamon. A genus of trees and shrubs in the family Lauraceae. These plants are notable for their fragrant bark and leaves, which are used as a spice (cinnamon) and in essential oils. They are native to Asia and are cultivated in tropical regions.
example_sentence: The bark of Cinnamomum trees is harvested to make cinnamon powder. Cinnamomum oil is widely used in aromatherapy. Farmers in Sri Lanka cultivate Cinnamomum for export. The flavor of baked goods is enhanced by dried Cinnamomum bark.

english_meaning: A sweet and aromatic spice from tree bark. A fragrant spice obtained from the inner bark of trees belonging to the genus Cinnamomum. It is widely used in cooking, baking, and traditional medicine for its warm flavor and health benefits.
example_sentence: She added cinnamon to her tea for extra flavor. The cake smelled delicious because of cinnamon. Cinnamon is often used in traditional medicine. The room had a warm cinnamon scent.

english_meaning: To calculate using numbers. To write something in secret code. A secret code. The number zero. A person who has no influence or importance. A system of writing or communication in which letters or messages are changed into coded symbols so that others cannot understand them.
example_sentence: The spy wrote the message in a cipher to keep it secret. His bank balance fell to cipher after heavy losses. In the meeting, he felt like a cipher with no real authority. She learned how to cipher complex equations quickly.

english_meaning: Relating to a cycle of about 24 hours. Recurring naturally on a twenty-four-hour cycle, even in the absence of light fluctuations.
example_sentence: Jet lag can disrupt your circadian rhythm. Our sleep patterns are governed by our circadian clock. Shift work can have a negative impact on circadian rhythms. Many biological processes follow a circadian cycle. Exposure to sunlight helps regulate the body's circadian rhythm.

english_meaning: A round plane figure whose boundary consists of points equidistant from a fixed center. A group of people with shared professions, interests, or acquaintances. A process or chain of events or systems that ends where it began. To move all the way around someone or something. To draw a round line around an item to highlight it.
example_sentence: The children sat in a wide circle to listen to the story. She is very well known within her professional circle. The hawk began to circle above the field looking for prey. Please circle the correct answer on your examination paper.

english_meaning: A complete and closed path through which an electric current can flow. A regular route or journey around a specific area, especially one made for a particular purpose like a judge or a preacher. A series of sporting events or competitions that take place at different locations. A circular journey or a lap around something such as a racing track. A set of exercises performed one after the other with short rest periods in between. The act of moving all the way around something. A group of people or organizations linked by a common interest or professional activity. To move or travel all the way around a place or thing. A specific administrative district or judicial territory over which a court has authority. A communication path between two or more points.
example_sentence: The technician replaced the blown fuse to restore the electrical circuit. The judge traveled the rural circuit twice a year to hear cases. She completed three laps of the racing circuit in record time. Our morning workout consists of a high-intensity circuit at the local gym.

english_meaning: A thin rigid board containing an arrangement of copper tracks and electronic components used to connect and support parts of a device. A specific physical module or card, like a motherboard, that forms the backbone of a computer system. The foundational plate where electrical connections are soldered to facilitate the flow of current between integrated circuits. A platform used in prototyping or manufacturing to organize complex wiring into a compact, standardized layout. The internal hardware component responsible for managing the logic and signals within an electronic appliance.
synonyms: ["PCB","Motherboard","Logic Board","Control Board","Printed Circuit","Breadboard","Electronic Plate","Backplane","Wiring Board","Module","Panel","Card","Hardware Component"]
example_sentence: The technician carefully soldered the new capacitor onto the green circuit board. A crack in the main circuit board caused the entire television to malfunction. Modern smartphones use multi-layered circuit boards to save space within the thin chassis. Before mass production, engineers test the logic on a breadboard before printing the final circuit board.

english_meaning: A safety device that automatically stops the flow of electricity in a circuit when there is a fault or overload. A mechanism in a financial market that halts trading temporarily to prevent a panic sell-off or extreme volatility. A person or event that acts to stop a sequence of events or a deteriorating situation from continuing. A specific type of short-term lockdown or restriction intended to break the chain of infection during a pandemic. A legislative or procedural rule designed to interrupt a process if certain conditions are met.
example_sentence: The circuit breaker tripped when I plugged in the space heater. Stock market trading was suspended after the circuit breaker was triggered by a ten percent drop. The diplomat acted as a circuit breaker in the escalating conflict between the two nations. The government implemented a two-week circuit breaker to reduce the rising number of virus cases.

english_meaning: A specific type of court that holds sessions in various locations within a particular judicial district. A high-level appellate court that hears cases appealed from lower district courts. A court that travels a regular route or path to administer justice in different towns or regions. A judicial body with jurisdiction over a wide geographical area rather than a single fixed city. A historical legal system where judges moved from place to place to ensure the law was applied uniformly across a territory.
synonyms: ["Appellate Court","District Court","Regional Court","Itinerant Court","Superior Court","Judicial Body","Tribunal","High Court","Court Of Appeals","Legal Forum","Judiciary","Traveling Court","Provincial Court","Sessions Court"]
antonyms: ["Lower Court","Local Court","Stationary Court","Fixed Court","Municipal Court","Petty Court","Small Claims Court","Trial Court"]
example_sentence: The case was elevated from the local magistrate to the federal circuit court for a final ruling. The judge traveled for weeks as part of the rural circuit court system in the nineteenth century. Lawyers prepared their briefs for the upcoming session of the appellate circuit court. Residents of the remote province waited for the circuit court to arrive and settle their land disputes.

english_meaning: A form of body conditioning or resistance training using high-intensity aerobics. A workout routine that involves a series of specific exercises performed one after another with minimal rest. A method of physical exercise that targets strength building and muscular endurance through a sequence of stations. A group-based or individual fitness program that cycles through different movements to keep the heart rate elevated. A structured exercise regimen designed to provide a full-body workout in a short period by rotating through various activities.
synonyms: ["Interval training","Cross-training","Round-robin workout","Station training","Body conditioning","Fitness routine","Aerobic circuit","Resistance training","Boot camp","Metabolic conditioning","High-intensity workout","Sequence training"]
example_sentence: The gym offers a high-intensity circuit training class every Tuesday morning. I find circuit training much more engaging than just running on a treadmill for an hour. Our coach designed a circuit training routine that focuses on core strength and agility. Circuit training is an excellent way to improve cardiovascular health while building muscle.

english_meaning: Describing a route or journey that is longer than the most direct way. Indirect and roundabout in language or method. Deviating from a straight course or a direct path. Using more words or time than necessary to express an idea. Characterized by a lack of straightforwardness or honesty in behavior.
example_sentence: The taxi driver took a circuitous route to the hotel to increase the fare. Her circuitous explanation left everyone in the room more confused than before. We spent the afternoon on a circuitous hike through the dense forest. The negotiations followed a circuitous path before finally reaching a compromise.

english_meaning: In a roundabout or indirect manner rather than by a direct route. In a way that uses many words or complicated arguments instead of being clear and concise. By following a path that is longer and less efficient than the most obvious way. In a manner that avoids direct confrontation or straightforward communication. In a way that winds or curves significantly instead of going straight.
example_sentence: He explained the complex physics theory circuitously, leaving the students more confused than before. Instead of addressing the issue head-on, she approached the subject circuitously during the meeting. The taxi driver took us circuitously through the city backstreets to avoid the heavy afternoon traffic. The river flowed circuitously through the valley, creating deep loops in the green landscape.

english_meaning: A system or collection of electrical circuits and their components designed for a specific function. The detailed arrangement and interconnection of electrical elements within a device. The physical wiring and electronic pathways that allow current to flow in a computer or machine. The metaphorical pathways or neural networks in the brain that process information and responses. The complex internal workings or structural design of an electronic system.
example_sentence: The engineer spent hours mapping out the complex circuitry of the new smartphone. Water damage can easily corrode the delicate internal circuitry of a laptop. Scientists are still studying the neural circuitry that governs human emotions and memory. The old radio failed because its circuitry was outdated and many components had burnt out.

english_meaning: Round in shape, like a circle. Moving around in a circle or loop. Distributed to many people, especially an official notice or letter. Returning to the starting point. Related to a circle. Indirect or repetitive, especially when an argument keeps returning to the same point. Involving a cycle, where one stage leads back to the beginning.
example_sentence: The table has a circular top. The bus follows a circular route around the city. The school issued a circular about the new examination schedule. His argument was circular and did not provide any new evidence.

english_meaning: To move continuously through a system or around a place. To pass from person to person or place to place. To spread news, information, or rumors among people. To move around at a social gathering and talk to different people. To distribute copies of a document, book, or magazine.
example_sentence: Blood circulates through the body via the heart. Rumors began to circulate about the manager's resignation. The host circulated among the guests to greet everyone. The library will circulate the new book next week.

english_meaning: The continuous movement of blood through the vessels of the body. The distribution or spreading of something, such as information or a virus, among a group. The movement or passage of something through a system, such as air or water. The number of copies of a newspaper or magazine sold or distributed regularly. The act of moving from one place to another or among people in a social setting.
example_sentence: Regular exercise is essential for maintaining healthy blood circulation. The old coins were eventually withdrawn from public circulation by the central bank. The newspaper has a daily circulation of over one hundred thousand copies. The library allows the circulation of books to students for a period of two weeks.

english_meaning: A person who spreads information, rumors, or items among a group. A device such as a pump or fan designed to move a fluid or gas through a closed system. A specific electronic component used in microwave circuits to direct signals between ports in a particular sequence. A pamphlet or letter intended for wide distribution to multiple recipients. An individual who moves from place to place within a specific community or network.
example_sentence: The air circulator kept the room cool during the sweltering afternoon. As a dedicated circulator of the petition, she gathered over five hundred signatures in one week. The technician replaced the faulty circulator in the heating system to restore hot water. In microwave engineering, a three-port circulator is essential for isolating transmitted and received signals.

english_meaning: Relating to the movement of blood through the body. Concerning the movement of fluid or air in a closed system. Pertaining to the distribution or circulation of items or information. Used to describe the heart, veins, and arteries as a collective system. Characterized by moving in a circle or circuit. Serving to pass something from person to person or place to place.
example_sentence: The circulatory system is responsible for transporting oxygen to all cells. Exercises like running can significantly improve your circulatory health. Doctors monitored the patient for any signs of circulatory failure after the surgery. The old pipes were part of a complex circulatory network for heating the entire building.

english_meaning: To walk all the way around something. To move in a circle around a sacred object or place as part of a ritual. To go round and round rather than moving directly. To approach a topic indirectly instead of speaking plainly.
example_sentence: The pilgrims circumambulate the shrine three times. Visitors slowly circumambulated the ancient monument. He tends to circumambulate the question instead of answering it. We circumambulated the lake before sunset.

english_meaning: Walking around something, especially in a circular path. Performing a ritual circle around a sacred place or object. Moving repeatedly around a central point. Dealing with a subject in an indirect, roundabout manner.
example_sentence: The devotees were circumambulating the shrine in silence. Circumambulating the stupa is an old tradition. She spent the evening circumambulating the garden path. He kept circumambulating the real issue in his speech.

english_meaning: The act of walking around something, especially in a circle. A ritual walk around a sacred object, shrine, or place as an act of devotion. The practice of moving round and round a central point. Figuratively, a roundabout or indirect way of speaking or approaching a subject.
example_sentence: Circumambulation of the shrine is part of the ceremony. The pilgrims began their circumambulation at sunrise. His circumambulation of the main issue annoyed the committee. Seven rounds of circumambulation complete the ritual.

english_meaning: The surgical removal of the foreskin from the penis. A medical or religious procedure in which the foreskin of the penis is removed. It is performed for health, cultural, or religious reasons, commonly in Judaism, Islam, and some other communities.
example_sentence: At about twelve or fourteen circumcision took place daily in this hospital. Many families choose circumcision for religious reasons. The doctor explained the benefits and risks of circumcision. Circumcision is performed shortly after birth in some cultures. There is debate over whether circumcision should be mandatory.

english_meaning: The distance around the edge of a circle or curved object. The outer boundary or perimeter of a circular area. The length of the enclosing boundary of a round shape.
example_sentence: The circumference of the Earth is approximately 40,000 kilometers. Calculate the circumference using the formula 2πr. We measured the circumference of the tree trunk. The circumference of the circle is three times its diameter.

english_meaning: The act of turning, rotating, or whirling around a central point. A circular or spiral motion.
example_sentence: The circumgyration of the planets around the sun is a fundamental astronomical fact. The dancer's rapid circumgyration mesmerized the audience. The machine's fan performed a constant circumgyration to cool the engine. The dervishes are known for their spiritual practice of circumgyration. The spinning top's circumgyration slowly wobbled to a halt.

english_meaning: The use of many words where fewer would do, especially in a deliberate attempt to be vague or evasive. An indirect way of speaking.
example_sentence: The politician was a master of circumlocution, never giving a direct answer. Please avoid circumlocution and get to the point. His letter was full of circumlocutions and vague promises. I grew tired of his constant circumlocution. 'The financial instrument is experiencing a period of negative growth' is a circumlocution for 'the stock is losing money'.

english_meaning: To limit somebody, something’s freedom, rights, power, etc. To draw a circle around another shape.
example_sentence: The power of the monarchy was circumscribed by the new law.

english_meaning: The act of limiting somebody, something's freedom, rights, power, etc. Something that limits or encloses. A surrounding substance. An inscription, as around a coin or medal. Something that limits one's freedom of action or choice.
example_sentence: Such circumscriptions on the freedom of speech are antithetical to a free and open society. Electronic monitoring bracelets are sometimes used to impose a circumscription of movement on people awaiting trial. The transportation circumscription is for induction in early time, but for confining in later time.

english_meaning: Cautious. Wary. Careful. Watchful. Prudent. Discreet. Heedful and unwilling to take risks. Considering all circumstances and possible consequences before acting or speaking. Showing thoughtful awareness and prudence in dealing with situations to avoid mistakes, danger, or unwanted outcomes.
example_sentence: She was circumspect in her dealings with strangers. A circumspect leader weighs every decision before announcing it. He gave a circumspect answer to the journalist's tricky question. Investors should be circumspect when markets are volatile. The diplomat remained circumspect about the ongoing negotiations.

english_meaning: Caution. Prudence. Wariness. Carefulness. Discretion. The quality of being watchful and considering all circumstances before acting. Thoughtful attention to the possible consequences of one's actions or words in order to avoid risk, harm, or mistakes.
example_sentence: He handled the sensitive matter with great circumspection. Her circumspection saved the company from a costly mistake. Acting with circumspection is essential in legal matters. The judge spoke with circumspection about the pending case. Diplomats are trained to behave with circumspection at all times.

english_meaning: A condition, fact, or event connected with or affecting a situation. The surrounding details or facts that influence what happens. A particular situation or state of affairs in which someone finds themselves. The conditions under which something takes place or is considered.
example_sentence: Under no circumstance should you open this door. The accident happened due to unusual circumstances. She adapted quickly to her new circumstances. The circumstances of his death remain a mystery. We must judge his behaviour according to the circumstances.

english_meaning: To cleverly avoid a rule, law, or difficulty, often in a way that is not straightforward or honest. To bypass an obstacle or overcome a challenge by ingenuity rather than confrontation.
example_sentence: The company tried to circumvent the new regulations by creating a subsidiary abroad. She found a way to circumvent the traffic jam by taking a narrow side road. Hackers attempt to circumvent security systems to gain unauthorized access. He circumvented the rules by using a loophole in the contract.

english_meaning: Relating to a person whose personal identity and gender corresponds with the sex assigned to them at birth. Denoting someone who is not transgender. Describing an individual whose gender identity matches the biological sex they were born with.
example_sentence: He identifies as a cisgender man. Many cisgender people are unaware of the challenges transgender individuals face. The survey included both cisgender and transgender participants. She is a cisgender woman who supports gender equality. The professor explained the difference between cisgender and transgender identities.

english_meaning: An insulting term for a boy or man who is seen as weak, timid, or not traditionally masculine.
example_sentence: The other boys called him a cissy because he did not like fighting. He was tired of being treated like a cissy for expressing his feelings. It is unfair to label someone a cissy just because they are gentle. She told them to stop using the word cissy as an insult.

english_meaning: In ancient times, a citadel was the strongest part of a city, often surrounded by walls. It served as the last defense point in case of invasion. Figuratively, it can describe something that protects important values or ideas.
example_sentence: The soldiers took refuge in the citadel when the enemy attacked. The citadel stood proudly on the hill overlooking the city. The university is regarded as a citadel of learning and wisdom. During the war, people sought safety within the walls of the citadel.

english_meaning: A reference to a source of information, or an official notice given for recognition or for a legal matter. Reference to a source used in writing or speech. An official award for bravery or achievement.  A formal notice to appear in court. Formal praise recorded in writing.
example_sentence: The report included a citation for every statistic. She received a citation from the governor for her service. The police issued a citation for parking in a restricted area. Always provide a citation when you use someone else's ideas.

english_meaning: To mention something as evidence or support. To quote, refer to, or mention a source, example, rule, case, or fact in order to explain a point or support an argument. To officially call someone to appear in court or before authorities. To praise someone formally, especially for bravery or good work. To point out or list something as an example. It is often used in academic writing, legal discussions, speeches, and reports.
example_sentence: She cited three research papers to support her argument. The teacher asked the students to cite reliable sources in their essays. Lawyers often cite previous court cases during trials. He cited his busy schedule as the reason for not attending the meeting.

english_meaning: A legally recognized member of a country or state who has certain rights and responsibilities. A person who lives in a particular town or city. An inhabitant of a particular place. A civilian, as opposed to a member of the military or police. A person entitled to the protection and privileges of a nation.
example_sentence: Every citizen has the right to vote in elections. She became a naturalized citizen after living here for five years. Good citizens contribute positively to their communities. The government must protect the rights of all citizens.

english_meaning: The legal status of being a recognised member of a particular country, with its rights and duties. The condition of belonging to a state and owing loyalty to it. The behaviour of a person in relation to their duties as a member of a community. A school subject that teaches young people about rights, responsibilities, and civic life.
example_sentence: He applied for citizenship after living there for six years. Voting is an important duty of citizenship. The school teaches citizenship alongside history. She holds dual citizenship of two countries.

english_meaning: Relating to or derived from citrus fruits such as lemons, limes, and oranges. Containing or having the sharp, sour quality of citrus. Of or relating to citric acid.
example_sentence: The drink has a fresh citric flavour. Citric compounds are common in many household cleaners. He is sensitive to citric fruits like oranges and lemons. The sauce needs a citric note to balance the sweetness.

english_meaning: A weak organic acid found naturally in citrus fruits such as lemons, limes, and oranges. A white crystalline substance widely used as a flavouring, preservative, and cleaning agent. A compound that gives many fruits their sharp, sour taste and plays a role in the body's energy cycle.
example_sentence: Lemons contain a high level of citric acid. Citric acid is added to soft drinks to give a tangy flavour. She used citric acid to remove limescale from the kettle. Too much citric acid can wear away tooth enamel.

english_meaning: A tree of a genus that includes the lemon, lime, orange, and grapefruit. The fruit from these trees, characterized by a sharp, acidic flavor and a high concentration of citric acid.
example_sentence: The scent of citrus filled the air in the orchard. She added a splash of citrus juice to brighten the flavor of the dish. Florida is famous for its vast citrus groves. Many cleaning products use citrus oil for its fresh scent and degreasing properties. A diet rich in citrus fruits can provide a good amount of vitamin C.

english_meaning: Related to a city, town, citizenship, or the duties of citizens. Something connected with a city, town, community life, public affairs, or the responsibilities and rights of citizens. It is often used for public duties, social participation, local government, and community welfare.
example_sentence: Civic responsibility includes obeying laws and helping the community. The mayor spoke about improving civic services in the city. Schools should teach students about civic duties and voting rights. Her civic engagement helped bring positive change to the neighborhood.

english_meaning: The study of the rights and duties of citizens and how government works. A school subject dealing with citizenship, laws, and public affairs. Knowledge of how a community and its institutions are organised and run. The practical understanding of civic responsibility and participation in public life.
synonyms: ["Citizenship studies","Political science","Civic education","Government studies","Public affairs","Social studies"]
example_sentence: Civics is taught in the ninth class in most schools. A good civics course teaches students about voting. She credits her interest in politics to her civics teacher. The curriculum includes civics, history, and geography.

english_meaning: To state or assert that something is the case without providing evidence or proof. To formally request or demand what one is entitled to. A statement asserting that something is true. A demand or request for something considered one's due.
example_sentence: The company makes a false claim about the health benefits of their product. He decided to claim his inheritance after his grandfather passed away. She will claim that she was not present at the time of the incident. You must submit your insurance claim within thirty days of the accident.

english_meaning: To state or argue that your position is morally better than that of others. To present yourself as more ethical or principled in a disagreement. To assert moral superiority in order to strengthen your argument. To publicly insist that your actions are guided by higher principles.
synonyms: ["Assert moral superiority","Take the moral high ground","Profess righteousness","Pose as principled","Moralise"]
example_sentence: The opposition tried to claim the moral high ground on the issue. You cannot claim the moral high ground after breaking your promise. Both leaders claimed the moral high ground in their speeches. The company claimed the moral high ground by publishing its ethics policy.

english_meaning: A person who claims or demands something as a right, especially money, property, or a title. Someone who formally states that something belongs to them or that they deserve something. A person who makes a legal or official claim, for example in court or for insurance or compensation.
example_sentence: The court will hear the claimant's case next week. There are several claimants to the late king's throne. The insurance company asked the claimant to submit all documents. Only one claimant turned up to receive the prize money. Each claimant must prove his right to the property.

english_meaning: A person claimed to have the supernatural ability to perceive events, objects, or information beyond the reach of normal senses. Relating to or possessing the supposed power of seeing into the future or perceiving things that are hidden from ordinary perception. Used to describe someone with an unusually accurate sense of foresight or insight. Often associated with psychic practices, fortune-telling, or paranormal claims.
example_sentence: The clairvoyant claimed to have foreseen the disaster weeks before it happened.  Many people remain skeptical about the abilities of self-proclaimed clairvoyants.  Her clairvoyant insight into the situation surprised everyone at the meeting.  The novel's main character is a clairvoyant who can see glimpses of the future.  He visited a clairvoyant hoping to find answers about his missing relative.

english_meaning: To suddenly stop talking, usually due to fear, shyness, or secrecy.
example_sentence: When asked about his plans, he clammed up. He clammed up in front of the police. She clammed up when the topic came up. They all clammed up after the accident.

english_meaning: To climb or move in an awkward and laborious way, typically using both hands and feet. To scramble up, over, or through something with difficulty. To make one's way clumsily by climbing.
example_sentence: The children clambered up the rocks to see the view. He clambered over the fence to escape the dog. She clambered into the back of the truck. They clambered through the bushes to reach the river. The old man clambered onto the bus with difficulty.

english_meaning: Unpleasantly damp, sticky, or cold to the touch. Something that feels slightly wet, cold, and sticky, often causing discomfort. It can describe skin, hands, weather, or an atmosphere that is damp and chilling.
example_sentence: His clammy hands made me nervous during the handshake. The room felt clammy after the rainstorm. She wiped the clammy sweat off her forehead. The old walls of the basement were cold and clammy.

english_meaning: To make a loud noise or demand loudly. To shout, protest, or insist loudly. To demand something publicly and with force.
example_sentence: Citizens clamored for justice after the incident. The students clamored to meet the speaker. Fans clamored for autographs at the event. The clamor of the crowd could be heard from blocks away. The clamor for change grew louder every day. There was a clamor of voices in the market.

english_meaning: A device used to hold or fasten things tightly together. To fasten, hold, or secure something firmly with such a device. To press or hold something tightly in place. To impose a restriction or control firmly upon something.
example_sentence: He used a clamp to hold the two pieces of wood together. The mechanic clamped the pipe before cutting it. She clamped her hand over her mouth in shock. The government decided to clamp down on illegal trade. Police clamped the car for illegal parking.

english_meaning: To take strict measures to prevent or control something considered undesirable or illegal
example_sentence: The government clamped down on illegal mining. Authorities clamped down on fake products. Schools clamped down on cheating during exams. Police clamped down on street racing

english_meaning: To take strict action. To enforce strict control or restrictions on something, usually to stop unwanted behavior or illegal activities
example_sentence: The government clamped down on tax evasion. Authorities clamped down on illegal street vendors. Schools clamped down on cheating during exams. Police clamped down on public drinking

english_meaning: To stop talking. To suddenly stop speaking or refuse to give information
example_sentence: He clamped up during the interrogation. She clamped up when asked about the incident. Witnesses clamped up out of fear. The child clamped up when strangers approached

english_meaning: Covert, undercover, concealed, confidential. Secret, hidden, done privately. Something kept secret, often to avoid attention, rules, or authority.
example_sentence: They held a clandestine meeting late at night. The journalist uncovered a clandestine operation. He made clandestine plans to start his own company. The group carried out a clandestine mission.

english_meaning: A loud, sharp, metallic sound made when heavy metal objects strike against each other. To make or cause to make such a sound.
example_sentence: The heavy chains clanked as the gate opened. We heard the clank of metal from the workshop. His sword clanked against the stone wall. The old train clanked slowly into the station. The prisoner's chains clanked with every step.

english_meaning: Silly or meaningless talk used to impress people. Exaggerated, false, or nonsensical statements that are often used to attract attention, gain applause, or impress an audience rather than to convey truth or useful information. It is commonly used in speeches, advertisements, or dramatic situations.
example_sentence: His speech was full of claptrap and had no real value. The advertisement used claptrap to attract customers. People quickly realized that his promises were just claptrap. She ignored the claptrap and focused on facts.

english_meaning: A deep purplish-red color like that of claret wine. A dry red wine from the Bordeaux region of France. Having a dark wine-red shade.
example_sentence: She chose a claret carpet for the dining room. He ordered a glass of claret with his meal. The team's jerseys were claret and blue. Her claret evening dress attracted many compliments.

english_meaning: Loud, clear, and powerful in sound, like a trumpet. A high-pitched trumpet used in the Middle Ages. A clear and stirring call to action or attention. Shrill and unmistakable in tone.
example_sentence: The general's clarion voice inspired the soldiers before the battle. Her speech was a clarion call for environmental protection. The clarion rang out across the medieval battlefield. He issued a clarion call to the youth to join the movement.

english_meaning: The quality of being clear and easy to understand. Clearness of thought, expression, or explanation. Transparency or purity, as of water, glass, or sound. Sharpness of an image or picture.
example_sentence: The report was written with admirable clarity. We need clarity about who is responsible. The clarity of the mountain water surprised them. The new lens improves image clarity.

english_meaning: A violent confrontation or fight between people or groups. A serious disagreement or argument. An incompatibility between things, such as colours, opinions, or schedules. A loud, harsh noise made by metal objects striking together. To come into conflict or be incompatible.
example_sentence: There was a violent clash between the protesters and the police. Their opinions clashed on every major issue. The two meetings clash, so I can only attend one. Her red scarf clashes with her pink dress. The swords clashed loudly in the duel.

english_meaning: A device or action used to hold things tightly together. A small object or fastener used to hold two things together, such as parts of a bag, necklace, or clothing. To grip or hold something tightly with hands or fingers. To embrace someone tightly in arms (hold closely).
example_sentence: She fastened the necklace with a golden clasp. The bag has a broken clasp. He clasped her hand before she left. The soldier clasped the weapon tightly in his hands.

english_meaning: The action or process of arranging things into categories or groups. A system of organizing items based on shared characteristics. The category or group to which something belongs. The assignment of organisms or objects to taxonomic groups.
example_sentence: The classification of plants is based on their characteristics. This document has a confidential classification. The library uses the Dewey classification system. Scientists use classification to organize species.

english_meaning: Arranged or organized into categories or groups. Designated as officially secret and restricted. A small advertisement in a newspaper or online. Having been sorted or categorized systematically.
example_sentence: The files contain classified information. She found a job through the classified ads. The documents are classified as top secret. All items have been classified by category.

english_meaning: A person or system that arranges things into categories. A word or morpheme that indicates the class or category of a noun. An algorithm or model used in machine learning to categorize data. A device or tool used for sorting or classification.
example_sentence: The machine learning classifier accurately predicts categories. In Chinese, 'ge' is a common noun classifier. The email classifier sorts messages into folders. The data classifier organizes information efficiently.

english_meaning: To arrange things into categories or groups based on shared characteristics. To designate something as belonging to a particular category. To assign a security level to information. To organize systematically.
example_sentence: Scientists classify animals into different species. Please classify these documents by date. The government classified the information as secret. We need to classify the data before analysis.

english_meaning: Having no social or economic classes or divisions. Not belonging to any particular social class. Without hierarchy or stratification. Lacking elegance or sophistication in behavior or appearance.
example_sentence: They dream of a classless society with equal opportunities. The party aims to create a classless system. His behavior was crude and classless. In a classless society, everyone has equal status.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being without social or economic classes. The absence of hierarchical divisions in society. A social system where all people have equal status. The lack of elegance or sophistication.
example_sentence: The ideology promotes classlessness in society. True classlessness means equal opportunities for all. The movement advocates for social classlessness. Economic classlessness remains an ideal for many.

english_meaning: A clumsy or careless mess. A messy or sticky lump of something. Used informally to describe a disorganized or jumbled collection of things. (Dialectal) A small group or cluster.
