english_meaning: Knowledge or understanding of something. A state of being aware. Awareness, realization, or knowledge, notice, perception.
example_sentence: The guests took cognizance of the snide remark. In the light of the new evidence that the court can now take cognizance of, the case is dropped. The lawyer asked the jury to take cognizance of the defendant's generosity in giving to charity.

english_meaning: Having knowledge or being aware of something. Being fully informed; conscious. Exhibiting knowledge or awareness; mindful. Possessing intelligence or understanding. Characterized by perception and comprehension. Entrusted with knowledge of something at hand.
example_sentence: She was cognizant of the challenges that lay ahead. The committee members were fully cognizant of their responsibilities. He was cognizant of the fact that his actions had consequences. It is essential for all employees to be cognizant of company policies. Being cognizant of global events is crucial in today's interconnected world.

english_meaning: To understand, recognize, perceive, or become aware of something through thinking or mental processes. To know, understand, identify, or mentally process something using the mind, intelligence, or awareness. It refers to the act of thinking carefully and becoming conscious of facts, ideas, situations, or experiences.
example_sentence: She could finally cognize the importance of education after years of struggle. The scientist tried to cognize the hidden pattern in the data. Young children gradually cognize the difference between right and wrong. He failed to cognize the danger until it was too late.

english_meaning: A body of persons who are especially competent in a particular field or art; connoisseurs or experts. These individuals possess a profound understanding and refined taste in a specific subject. They are often sought for their authoritative opinions and deep knowledge. Their expertise is usually gained through extensive study, practice, and experience, allowing them to discern subtle qualities and nuances others might miss. They are the informed elite within a given domain. They often influence trends and standards within their field. They are highly discerning individuals with specialized knowledge.
example_sentence: The cognoscenti of the art world gathered for the exclusive exhibition. Her detailed critique proved she was one of the cognoscenti in culinary arts. Only the true cognoscenti could appreciate the subtle brushstrokes of the master painter. The film festival attracted cognoscenti from across the globe, eager to discuss the latest indie productions. He was considered one of the cognoscenti in classical music, with an encyclopedic knowledge of composers and their works.

english_meaning: Capable of being known or understood. Possessing the quality of being knowable or discernible. Referring to something that can be perceived, comprehended, or ascertained through observation, study, or experience. Open to recognition and interpretation. Accessible to intellectual apprehension.
example_sentence: The scientific principle was entirely cognoscible through experimentation. The subtle nuances of the artwork were cognoscible only to a trained eye. The historical facts were easily cognoscible after reviewing the documents. The complex legal text was cognoscible with careful study. Her intentions became cognoscible as she explained her plan.

english_meaning: To have a clear logical connection so that together they make a whole. To work closely together. To unite or to hold together as a unit. To hold together firmly as parts of the same mass. To become united in principles, relationships, or interests.
example_sentence: This view does not cohere with their other beliefs. The various sections of the report fail to cohere into a satisfactory whole. It can be difficult to get a group of people to cohere. His vision is of a world that coheres through human connection rather than rules.

english_meaning: The situation in which all the parts of something fit together well. A clear relationship between parts, especially in a work of literature or art. Systematic or logical connection or consistency. A sticking or cleaving together, union of parts of the same body.
example_sentence: The points you make are fine, but the whole essay lacks coherence. He managed to impose a new coherence on the machinery of the state. There was no coherence between the first and the second half of the movie. The essay as a whole lacks coherence.

english_meaning: Logical and well organized, easy to understand and clear. Able to talk and express yourself clearly. Working closely and well together. Relating to or composed of waves having a constant difference in phase.
example_sentence: She only became coherent again two hours after the attack. You're not being very coherent. He proposed the most coherent plan to improve the schools. The drunk man was not coherent. They are able to function as a coherent group team.

english_meaning: In a logical and consistent way. In a way that is clear and easy to understand. Speaking or writing in an articulate and comprehensible manner. Expressing thoughts, ideas, or arguments in a well-structured and unified way, making it easy for others to follow and grasp the intended message. When something is presented coherently, its parts fit together harmoniously, forming a single, understandable whole.
example_sentence: She explained her complex theory very coherently, so everyone in the room understood. The witness struggled to speak coherently after the accident, due to the shock. He could not string together a coherent sentence. The lawyer presented his case coherently, leaving no room for doubt. Despite the interruption, she continued her speech coherently.

english_meaning: Forming a united whole. Causing people or things to become united. Having the parts agreeably related. Marked by the ability to withstand stress without structural damage or distortion.
example_sentence: Their tribe is a small but cohesive group.  His argument was both cohesive and persuasive. The album is cohesive from beginning to end. They prefer to sculpt with clay because of its cohesive properties.

english_meaning: A group of people who share a common feature or aspect of behavior. A member of a group of people who support another person. A group of people who share a characteristic, usually age. A company of companions or supporters.
example_sentence: The 1999 birth cohort (= all those born in 1999). Robinson and his cohorts were soon ejected from the hall. The director made his entrance followed by his cohort of technicians and production assistants. This study followed up a cohort of 386 patients aged 65+ for six months after their discharge home. The police arrested the gang's leader and his cohorts.

english_meaning: The way a person's hair is styled or arranged. It often implies a carefully styled or elaborate arrangement of hair. It can also refer to the act of styling or arranging hair. It is typically used for a formal or elegant hairstyle. It's a term that carries a sense of artistry and design in hair treatment.
example_sentence: Her elaborate coiffure for the ball took several hours to complete. The salon specializes in modern coiffures for both men and women. He always maintained a perfect coiffure, even on casual days. The opera singer's coiffure was adorned with dazzling jewels. She changed her coiffure frequently to match her adventurous spirit.

english_meaning: A literary or architectural word meaning a corner or angle of a building or structure. It can especially refer to an external corner or projecting corner of a wall. The word is uncommon in modern everyday English and is more often found in literature, historical writing, or architectural descriptions. It can also be used figuratively in the expression "coign of vantage," meaning a favorable or advantageous position from which to observe something.
example_sentence: From his coign of vantage on the hill, he watched the whole parade. The mason carefully placed each coign of the new wall. She found a quiet coign in the old library where nobody disturbed her. The tower's stone coign had weathered for over two hundred years.

english_meaning: A flat piece of metal used as money. Metal money in general. To make coins by stamping metal. To invent a new word or phrase.
example_sentence: She dropped a coin into the beggar's hand. The museum displays coins from the Mughal era. The government began to coin new one-rupee pieces. Shakespeare coined many words still used today.

english_meaning: The process of making coins. The system of currency in a country. A newly invented word or phrase. The act of inventing a new word or phrase.
example_sentence: The government is responsible for the coinage of money. The country has a new coinage system. The word "byte" is a modern coinage. The coinage of new terms is common in the tech industry.

english_meaning: To occur at the same time. To agree or be in accord with something. To occupy the same position in space. To correspond exactly in some respect. To happen together by chance.
example_sentence: Our holidays coincide with the school break. His arrival coincided with the beginning of the meeting. Their opinions coincide on most issues. The two lines coincide at this point.

english_meaning: A remarkable occurrence of events without an apparent connection. The fact of two or more things happening at the same time by chance. Correspondence in position or nature. An unexpected agreement of circumstances. Simultaneous existence or occurrence.
example_sentence: It was a strange coincidence that we met at the airport. By coincidence, we were both wearing the same shirt. The similarity is only a coincidence, not a copy. What a coincidence to see you here!

english_meaning: Occurring at the same time or place. In agreement or harmony with something. Happening together by chance. Corresponding exactly in position or nature. Concurrent or simultaneous.
example_sentence: The two festivals are coincident this year. His views are coincident with those of his teacher. The meeting was coincident with the arrival of the delegation. Their interests happened to be coincident.

english_meaning: Very little consolation in a difficult situation. Comfort that does not really help or reassure. A poor substitute for real relief. Something meant to console but of little value.
example_sentence: His apology was cold comfort after the damage was done. The small refund was cold comfort to the passengers. Praise is cold comfort when the salary is low. Knowing others failed too was cold comfort to her.

english_meaning: To lose courage or become afraid to do something at the last moment. To feel nervous, scared, or hesitant to go through with something once planned or promised.
example_sentence: He got cold feet before his wedding and decided to delay it. The player had cold feet before the final match. She wanted to start a new business but got cold feet at the last moment. The company backed out of the deal after getting cold feet about the risks.

english_meaning: A person who seems unfriendly, emotionally distant, or does not show feelings. Someone who appears emotionally detached, quiet, and unfriendly. Such a person does not easily show warmth, affection, or social openness. They may seem hard to approach or unresponsive in social situations.
example_sentence: He never smiles or talks much, he is really a cold fish. Everyone tried to be friendly, but she remained a cold fish. The manager seems like a cold fish, but he is very intelligent. Don’t expect warmth from him, he is a cold fish at work.

english_meaning: To deliberately ignore someone or treat them with indifference. To show unfriendliness or a lack of interest as a form of rejection.
example_sentence: After their argument, she gave him the cold shoulder for a week. When I entered the meeting, my boss gave me the cold shoulder and didn’t even say hello. He tried to apologize, but his friends gave him the cold shoulder. Instead of supporting the new idea, the committee gave it the cold shoulder.

english_meaning: Having a body temperature that is the same as the surrounding environment. Lacking in feeling, sympathy, or sensitivity; cruel and ruthless. Done without emotion or pity; deliberately and dispassionately. Used to describe animals whose body temperature is not internally regulated. Characterized by a lack of emotion or a disregard for others' feelings. Performing an action in a stark and unfeeling manner. Describes an action carried out with premeditation and a lack of remorse.
example_sentence: Reptiles are cold-blooded animals. The cold-blooded killer showed no remorse for his actions. He made a cold-blooded decision to fire his entire staff. The cold-blooded murder shocked the entire community. Her cold-blooded efficiency made her a formidable opponent in business.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove all or part of the colon. A procedure used to treat bowel cancer, Crohn's disease, or ulcerative colitis. The removal of a diseased section of the large intestine. An operation that may require a temporary or permanent stoma.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed a colectomy to remove the tumour. After the colectomy, he needed a temporary stoma. A partial colectomy was enough to treat the diseased section. Recovery from a colectomy usually takes several weeks.

english_meaning: To work jointly on an activity or project. To cooperate with an enemy. To produce or create something by working with others. To willingly assist an enemy of one's country, especially an occupying force.
example_sentence: The two scientists collaborated on the research project for over a decade. He was accused of collaborating with the enemy during the war. We collaborated on a new design for the company logo. She refused to collaborate with her colleagues on the task. The artists often collaborate to produce stunning murals.

english_meaning: The action of working with someone to produce something. Joint effort by two or more people or groups. Cooperation between individuals, teams, or organizations. Traitorous cooperation with an enemy. A shared piece of work.
example_sentence: The song is a collaboration between two famous singers. Successful projects require close collaboration between teams. Our company values collaboration more than competition. The report was written in collaboration with local experts.

english_meaning: In a way that involves two or more people or groups working together toward a shared goal. Through joint effort, cooperation, and teamwork. In a manner that emphasizes partnership and mutual contribution. By working in collaboration.
example_sentence: The researchers worked collaboratively to publish the study. Students were encouraged to learn collaboratively through group projects. The companies collaborated collaboratively to develop new technology. Teams across different countries worked collaboratively on the initiative.

english_meaning: A person who works jointly with others on a project or activity. A partner in a shared task or creative work. Someone who cooperates with an enemy occupying their country. A co-worker or helper in academic or artistic work. A joint contributor.
example_sentence: The two scientists have been long-time collaborators. She is a frequent collaborator with the award-winning director. Collaborators were punished after the war ended. The book was written by three collaborators.

english_meaning: A piece of art made by sticking different materials like photos, paper, or fabric together. An artistic composition created by assembling various visual elements such as pictures, newspaper cuttings, colored paper, textures, or digital images to form a new unified design.
example_sentence: She created a collage using old magazines. The wall displayed a collage of family photos. Students made a collage for art class. The designer used a digital collage for the poster.

english_meaning: To fall down, to fail suddenly. To fall suddenly after breaking apart. To decrease in value, amount
example_sentence: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow. Talks between management and union have collapsed. Share prices collapsed after news of poor trading figures.

english_meaning: A band or fold of fabric around the neck of a garment. A band of leather or metal placed around the neck of an animal for identification or control. To seize or detain someone, especially by the neck or clothing. A ring or band used to join two pipes or to hold a machine part in place. To capture or arrest a criminal.
example_sentence: She straightened the collar of her shirt before the interview began. The dog wore a shiny leather collar with its name engraved on a tag. The police managed to collar the suspect just as he was leaving the building. The mechanic tightened the metal collar around the pipe to prevent a leak.

english_meaning: The long slender bone joining the breastbone to the shoulder blade. The bone that lies horizontally at the base of the neck, also called the clavicle. One of the two bones that support the shoulders and keep them in place. A commonly fractured bone located just above the first rib.
example_sentence: He broke his collarbone in a cycling accident. The doctor felt along her collarbone for swelling. A fractured collarbone usually heals within a few weeks. The necklace rested just below her collarbone.

english_meaning: A type of non-heading cabbage with large, thick, dark green leaves that are edible. A variety of the plant species Brassica oleracea known for its loose leaves. The vegetable typically eaten after being boiled or steamed, popular in Southern American cuisine. A member of the Acephala group of cultivars, closely related to kale and spring greens. The leafy foliage of certain cruciferous vegetables used as fodder or human food.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a traditional side dish of slow-cooked collard greens with smoked turkey. Gardeners often plant collard in the late summer for a fall harvest. Nutritiously dense, collard leaves are an excellent source of vitamins A and C. She chopped the tough stems off the collard before sautéing the leaves with garlic.

english_meaning: Large, smooth, dark green leaves eaten as a cooked vegetable. A leafy green traditionally simmered slowly with seasoning. The plant grown for these broad leaves. A nutritious vegetable rich in calcium and vitamins.
example_sentence: Collard greens are slowly cooked with spices. She washed the collard greens leaf by leaf. Collard greens are a traditional southern dish. The greens shrink a lot while cooking.

english_meaning: The act of seizing, catching, or arresting someone, especially by grabbing the neck or collar. Stopping a person forcefully in order to speak with them or detain them. Capturing a criminal or suspect. Informally, taking hold of someone to confront or question them. Putting a collar on an animal.
example_sentence: The police succeeded in collaring the thief near the market. He was busy collaring guests at the door to share his news. The officer was praised for collaring a dangerous criminal. She kept collaring her colleagues to discuss the new project. The trainer was collaring the dog before the walk.

english_meaning: Describing a garment, particularly a shirt or jacket, that is designed without a band or fold of cloth around the neck. Having no distinctive or contrasting markings around the neck area of an animal. Referring to a style of dress that lacks the formal structure provided by a neckline band. Lacking a piece of equipment used to restrain or identify a domestic animal around its neck.
example_sentence: He preferred wearing a collarless linen shirt during the hot summer months. The modern jacket featured a sleek collarless design for a minimalist look. The vet examined the collarless stray dog to check for an identification chip. Many traditional South Asian tunics are intentionally crafted as collarless garments.

english_meaning: To collect and combine different pieces of information into a single whole. To compare pieces of information in order to identify similarities or differences. To arrange sheets of paper or pages in their proper sequence. To provide or assign a benefice to a member of the clergy. To gather and examine data critically to ensure accuracy.
example_sentence: The software will collate all the responses into a single spreadsheet. Please collate the reports before the board meeting begins. The historian spent years trying to collate the scattered manuscripts. It is necessary to collate the two versions of the document to find discrepancies.

english_meaning: Something pledged as security for repayment of a loan. Secondary or subordinate, accompanying but not primary. Additional damage or effect, often unintended (in military or figurative context). Something accompanying a primary obligation or claim. Related by side or parallel, not direct. Indirect consequence or secondary result of an action.
example_sentence: The bank required collateral before approving the loan. The explosion caused collateral damage to nearby houses. His success had collateral benefits for his entire team. The company offered real estate as collateral for the business loan.

english_meaning: A person with whom one works, especially in a profession or business. A fellow worker or associate in a profession, often used in academia or white-collar jobs. One of a group of people having a common purpose or belonging to the same profession. A professional peer with whom tasks, duties, or projects are shared. A person who belongs to the same organization or team. An associate in a shared endeavor. Someone who cooperates with another or others.
example_sentence: I'd like you to meet my colleague, Dr. Alvi. She often consults with her colleagues on complex medical cases. My colleagues and I are presenting our research at the conference next month. He enjoys a good working relationship with all his colleagues. We are fortunate to have such supportive colleagues in our department.

english_meaning: To bring things together from different places or people. To gather objects of a particular kind as a hobby or interest. To go to a place and take someone or something away. To receive or gather payments, donations, or taxes. To regain control of one's thoughts or emotions.
example_sentence: He collects rare coins from different countries. She went to collect her children from school. The charity collects donations for flood victims. Please give me a moment to collect my thoughts.

english_meaning: To gather your thoughts and calm yourself down. To regain composure after being upset or confused. To pull yourself together mentally. To start thinking clearly again. To recover mental steadiness.
synonyms: ["Compose yourself","Pull yourself together","Regain focus","Calm down","Get a grip","Steady yourself"]
example_sentence: Take a moment and collect your marbles before answering. She stepped outside to collect her marbles. He tried to collect his marbles after hearing the shocking news. Collect your marbles and try again.

english_meaning: Done by or belonging to a group of people acting together. Shared by all members of a group rather than by individuals. A business or farm owned and run jointly by its members. In grammar, a noun that refers to a group as a single unit.
example_sentence: The decision was the result of a collective effort. Collective responsibility rests with the whole committee. The farmers formed a collective to sell their produce. Team is a collective noun in English grammar.

english_meaning: As a group rather than individually. Taken all together as a whole. By the joint action or agreement of several people. Considered in total rather than separately.
example_sentence: The staff collectively agreed to change the working hours. These islands are collectively known as the archipelago. Collectively, the donations amounted to a large sum. The villagers collectively rebuilt the damaged bridge.

english_meaning: A person who gathers and keeps items of a particular kind as a hobby. An official who receives payments such as taxes, bills or fares. A device or part that gathers something, such as heat or dust. A senior administrative officer of a district in South Asia.
example_sentence: He is a passionate collector of old coins. The ticket collector checked every passenger on the train. A solar collector heats water on the roof. The collector visited the flood-hit villages.

english_meaning: Characterized by or having a collegium, a body of colleagues. Having authority or responsibility shared among a number of colleagues. Relating to a college or its students. Relating to or denoting the joint responsibility of the Pope and the bishops for the government of the whole Church. United in a common purpose; cooperative. Marked by an agreeable cooperative interplay among colleagues. Denotes the shared power by a group of colleagues.
example_sentence: A collegial atmosphere enhances productivity and job satisfaction. The decision was made after a collegial discussion among all department heads. We strive to create a collegial environment where everyone feels valued. The new principal fostered a more collegial relationship with the teachers. Collegial support is essential for new faculty members.

english_meaning: A violent encounter of a moving body with another, often resulting in damage or destruction. An accidental clash between two or more things or people. A conflict of opposing ideas, interests, or principles. The act of two or more vehicles or objects hitting each other. A sudden, forceful coming together of two entities. An instance of things striking against each other. A severe impact.
example_sentence: The collision of the two cars caused significant damage to both vehicles. The political parties are on a collision course over the proposed legislation. The data suggests a possible collision between the asteroid and our planet. The cyclists narrowly avoided a collision at the intersection. The collision of their ideas sparked a new innovative project.

english_meaning: To place or arrange people or things together in a suitable position. To assign or position something in relation to something else. In linguistics, for one word to naturally occur with another word in normal language use. To group items according to a meaningful relationship. A word that commonly appears together with another word (For example: Strong coffee, Heavy rain, Make a decision, Fast food).
example_sentence: The librarian collocated books by subject to make them easier to find. In English, the adjective strong commonly collocates with coffee. Researchers collocated the equipment in one laboratory for easier testing. Students should learn which words naturally collocate in everyday English.

english_meaning: A natural combination of two or more words that are commonly used together by native speakers. These word combinations sound correct and fluent. A group of words that frequently occur together in a language. Although the words may be understood individually, their natural combination is preferred by native speakers. Learning collocations improves vocabulary, fluency, writing, and speaking skills.
synonyms: ["Word combination","Word partnership","Lexical combination","Lexical pairing","Word association","Fixed expression","Common phrase","Set phrase","Standard combination","Typical expression"]
antonyms: ["There is no exact antonym for collocation"]
example_sentence: Learning collocations helps students speak English more naturally. The teacher explained several common collocations during the lesson. Good writers use the correct collocations to make their writing fluent. Dictionaries often include collocations to help learners choose the right words.

english_meaning: To have a secret conference. To conspire. To have a confidential discussion. To confer secretly on important matters.
example_sentence: The two rivals were seen to collogue in a quiet corner of the room. The managers collogued late into the night, discussing the company's future. They collogued for hours before presenting their proposal. It was clear from their hushed voices that they were colloguing about something sensitive.

english_meaning: A homogeneous, non-crystalline substance consisting of large molecules or ultramicroscopic particles of one substance dispersed through a second substance. Colloids include gels, sols, and emulsions; the particles do not settle and cannot be separated by ordinary filtering or centrifuging. In a colloidal system, the dispersed phase is spread evenly throughout the continuous phase. The particles in a colloid are larger than molecules but small enough that they remain suspended rather than settling out. Colloids are very common in everyday life and include materials like milk, fog, and paint. The stability of colloids is often due to the electrostatic repulsion between the dispersed particles. Many biological fluids, such as blood, are colloidal suspensions.
example_sentence: The paint is a colloid where solid particles are dispersed in a liquid medium. Milk is a classic example of a colloid, an emulsion of fat globules in water. Fog is a natural colloid, consisting of tiny water droplets suspended in the air. Many pharmaceutical products are formulated as colloids for better drug delivery. The blood in our bodies is a complex colloidal suspension.

english_meaning: Informal language used in ordinary conversation. Words, phrases, or expressions that are used in everyday speech rather than in formal writing. It often reflects the regional, cultural, or casual way people speak.
example_sentence: He used colloquial expressions. “Gonna” is a colloquial form of “going to”. He uses colloquial expressions in his stories to sound natural. “Y’all” is a colloquial term commonly used in the southern United States. The teacher asked students to avoid colloquial language in their essays.

english_meaning: A word or phrase used in ordinary or familiar conversation rather than in formal speech or writing. The use of informal, everyday expressions in language. An informal expression typical of a particular region or group.
example_sentence: The essay was rejected for its heavy use of colloquialism. "Gonna" is a common colloquialism for "going to". He explained the meaning of a local colloquialism to the visitors. Avoid colloquialism when writing an academic report.

english_meaning: In an informal, everyday manner of speaking. Using words or expressions typical of ordinary conversation rather than formal language. As commonly or popularly called.
example_sentence: The disease is colloquially known as sleeping sickness. He spoke colloquially, which made everyone comfortable. Colloquially, people call the building "the old post office". Avoid writing colloquially in your final examination.

english_meaning: An academic meeting or seminar in which specialists give talks and discuss a subject. A formal conference or gathering held for discussion. A university course or session based on group discussion rather than lectures.
example_sentence: The department is holding a colloquium on medical ethics. She presented her research at an international colloquium. Students are required to attend the weekly colloquium. The colloquium brought together scholars from five countries.

english_meaning: A formal conversation or discussion between two or more people. A literary work written in the form of a dialogue. A gathering held for discussion, especially on a serious or academic subject.
example_sentence: The judge held a brief colloquy with the two lawyers. Their colloquy on ethics lasted well into the evening. The book is written as a colloquy between teacher and student. A colloquy on climate change was arranged at the university.

english_meaning: To cooperate secretly, often for deceitful or fraudulent purposes. To coordinate with others to gain an unfair advantage. To act in conspiracy, sometimes even without explicit criminal intent, but still unethical. To manipulate situations or people secretly for personal or collective benefit.
example_sentence: The two companies colluded to fix prices. Politicians were accused of colluding with foreign agents. The players colluded to manipulate the outcome of the game. Several banks were found to have colluded in fraudulent practices.

english_meaning: Secret or illegal cooperation, especially in order to cheat or deceive others. A secret understanding between two or more people for a wrongful purpose. Conspiring together to do something dishonest.
example_sentence: The two companies were accused of collusion to fix the prices. There was clear collusion between the officials and the contractors. The judge found evidence of collusion in the case. They acted in collusion to deceive the investors. Collusion among players led to the cancellation of the match.

english_meaning: Involving secret or illegal cooperation to deceive or cheat others. Actions, agreements, or behavior where two or more parties secretly cooperate, often for dishonest or fraudulent purposes, to gain an unfair advantage or mislead others.
example_sentence: The companies were found to have a collusive agreement to fix prices. The investigation revealed collusive behavior between the two officials. Collusive bidding in the auction led to inflated prices. The politicians were accused of collusive tactics to manipulate the vote.

english_meaning: The main part of the large intestine that absorbs water and salts from digested food. The section of bowel between the cecum and the rectum. A punctuation mark (:) used to introduce a list, explanation, or quotation.
example_sentence: The colon absorbs water from the remaining food. Regular screening can detect problems in the colon early. He wrote the list after a colon. A healthy diet supports a healthy colon.

english_meaning: A person who lives in a colony and who comes from the country that controls it. Connected with or belonging to a country that controls another country.
example_sentence: The colonial power of Europe exploited the muslim countries by taking away their raw material at low prices and selling them machinery and furnished goods at high prices. Turkey was once an important colonial power.

english_meaning: To establish a colony in; settle in such a way as to take control of. To appropriate for one's own use or benefit. To settle in large numbers. To inhabit as a colonist.
example_sentence: The European powers began to colonize various parts of the world in the 16th century. The bacteria started to colonize the wound, leading to an infection. We need to colonize Mars for the future of humanity. The local species was outcompeted as the invasive plants began to colonize the area. The artist sought to colonize new aesthetic territory with her experimental work.

english_meaning: A row of regularly spaced columns supporting a roof, or part of a building. A series of columns placed at regular intervals. A structure consisting of a row of columns with a continuous entablature. Any structure composed of a series of columns. An architectural feature where a sequence of columns is closely set, often framing an entrance or courtyard. A long sequence of columns united by an entablature, often freestanding.
example_sentence: The ancient temple was surrounded by a stately colonnade. The museum's entrance is marked by a grand colonnade leading to the main hall. We walked through the colonnade, admiring the intricate carvings on each column. The colonnade provided a shaded walkway around the courtyard. The impressive colonnade added a sense of majesty to the municipal building.

english_meaning: The natural color, coloring, or arrangement of colors in an animal or plant. The act or process of coloring or being colored. The effect or result of coloring. The quality or fact of being colored. A particular combination of colors.
example_sentence: The bright coloration of the male bird attracts mates. The artist used a unique coloration technique in her painting. The coloration of the chameleon helps it blend into its surroundings. The vibrant coloration of the coral reef is breathtaking. Her paintings are known for their bold coloration and expressive brushstrokes.

english_meaning: Extremely large. Of a bulk, extent, power, or effect approaching or suggesting the stupendous or incredible. Of an exceptional or astonishing degree.
example_sentence: The singer earns a colossal amount of money. The variety of wines available is colossal. The variety of wines available is colossal. There has been a colossal waste of public money. A single puppy can make a colossal mess.

english_meaning: A person or thing that is extremely important or large in size. An extremely large statue. A person or thing of great size, influence, or ability. Something that is unusually large and powerful.
example_sentence: She has been described as the creative colossus of the literary world. He talked about the emerging colossus of the Internet.

english_meaning: A medical surgical procedure in which a part of the colon is brought through the abdominal wall to create an artificial opening called a stoma. This opening allows stool to pass into a special bag attached outside the body. It may be temporary or permanent and is usually done due to conditions like cancer, injury, infection, or blockage of the colon.
example_sentence: She became unable to digest food and needed a colostomy. We have been told the colostomy will have to stay in place for another few months, but at least he can now poo happily. A colostomy was performed in an attempt to relieve her large bowel symptoms, and subsequently closed.

english_meaning: The first thick yellow milk produced by mammals just after giving birth, rich in nutrients and antibodies. It is often called "first milk". It acts as a natural vaccine for newborns. It supports early growth and gut health. It is also collected from cows for use in health supplements.
example_sentence: The nurse explained that colostrum is very important for the newborn baby. Mothers are encouraged to feed colostrum to strengthen the baby's immunity. The farmer collected cow colostrum for nutritional supplements. Colostrum helps protect infants from early infections.

english_meaning: A tall upright pillar that supports a building or stands as a monument. A vertical division of a table, page, or spreadsheet. A regular article written by the same person in a newspaper or magazine. A long line of people, vehicles, or figures arranged one behind or below another.
example_sentence: Marble columns support the roof of the old hall. Enter the totals in the last column of the table. She writes a weekly column on health and fitness. A long column of soldiers marched through the town.

english_meaning: To search something very carefully and thoroughly. To examine every part of a place or document in detail. To look through a large amount of information in order to find something. To sift through material in search of a specific item. To investigate closely in order to find or verify something.
example_sentence: The detectives combed through every file for clues. She combed through the report to find the missing figures. Investigators combed through the wreckage after the crash. He combed through his notes before the exam.

english_meaning: Armed fighting between opposing forces. Active fighting in a war or battle. A fight or struggle between people or groups. To take action to reduce or prevent something undesirable. To engage in fighting or battle.
example_sentence: Soldiers engaged in hand-to-hand combat. The government launched a campaign to combat corruption. She has combat experience from two tours overseas. New measures will combat climate change.

english_meaning: A person or group engaged in fighting or combat, especially in war. A member of armed forces actively participating in hostilities. Someone involved in a battle or conflict. Engaged in or ready for fighting.
example_sentence: International law protects non-combatants during war. All combatants must follow the rules of engagement. The injured combatant was evacuated from the battlefield. Both combatants suffered heavy casualties.

english_meaning: To happen. To be mentioned, discussed, To be dealt with by a court of law, To arrive. To occur in the course of time.
example_sentence: The daffodils are just beginning to come up. I am afraid something urgent has come up. The question is bound to come up at meeting.

english_meaning: To meet or find someone or something by chance, also, to appear or seem a certain way.
example_sentence: I came across an old photo album yesterday. She came across as very confident. We came across a rare flower in the forest. He came across the idea while reading.

english_meaning: To follow someone or something in time, order, or sequence. To pursue, chase, or try to catch someone. To succeed or take the place of someone. To attack or criticize someone.
example_sentence: The police came after the thief. The letter B comes after the letter A in the alphabet. Success often comes after years of hard work and patience. He came after his father as the new leader of the community. Darkness usually comes after the sunset

english_meaning: To be completely expected. To cause no surprise because the facts or circumstances already suggested it.
example_sentence: Her promotion came as no surprise because she had worked hard for years. It came as no surprise when the team won the final. The delay came as no surprise after the heavy snowfall. His decision to resign came as no surprise to his closest colleagues.

english_meaning: To obtain, gain, or manage to get something (often something rare or difficult). To visit someone casually or unexpectedly.
example_sentence: Good jobs are hard to come by. He promised to come by my office in the evening to discuss the project. Opportunities like this do not come by very often, so you should take it seriously. I came by an old book in the market that reminded me of my childhood.

english_meaning: To admit the truth after hiding it. To confess honestly, especially about something wrong or secret.
example_sentence: He finally came clean about the mistake he made at work. After months of lying, she finally came clean about where she had been. The politician was forced to come clean about the corruption scandal. If you come clean now, the punishment will be lighter. He didn’t want to disappoint his parents, but he had to come clean about failing the exam. It’s better to come clean than to keep hiding the truth.

english_meaning: To move or fall from a higher position to a lower one. To decrease in price, level, or amount. To reach a decision or state an opinion in favour of one side. To be passed on from earlier generations or times. To become ill with a particular disease.
example_sentence: Please come down from the ladder before you fall. House prices have come down slightly this year. The committee came down in favour of the new proposal. I think I am coming down with a cold.

english_meaning: To engage in a physical fight/ To exchange punches or strikes. To resort to violence after an argument/ To become involved in a brawl or scuffle. To settle a dispute through physical confrontation. To start fighting physically, usually after an argument, disagreement, or heated exchange. It refers to a situation where people stop arguing with words and begin hitting, punching, or attacking each other.
synonyms: ["Fight","Brawl","Scuffle","Clash","Exchange blows","Come to blows","Engage in a fistfight","Wrestle","Attack each other","Get into a fight"]
example_sentence: The two players came into blows after a heated argument on the field. Neighbors came into blows over a property dispute. The protesters and security guards nearly came into blows during the demonstration. The brothers came into blows when they could not resolve their disagreement peacefully.

english_meaning: To start being legally valid and applicable. To become effective from a particular date. To begin operating as an official rule or law. To take effect after being formally approved. To become binding on the people concerned.
example_sentence: The new rules come into force on the first of January. The ban came into force after months of debate. When does the agreement come into force? Higher fines will come into force from next month.

english_meaning: To result from. To happen because of, or to be the outcome of something.
example_sentence: Success comes of hard work. Nothing good can ever come of lying to your friends. Great success often comes of patience and hard work. No harm will come of trying to speak the truth.

english_meaning: To appear, become visible, or be revealed, sometimes to disclose personal truth. To be published or released. To attend a social event or go outside.
example_sentence: The sun came out after the rain. He finally came out with the truth. Her new book will come out next month. He came out to play with his friends.

english_meaning: To reveal a secret, especially to openly disclose one's sexual orientation or gender identity for the first time. To publicly acknowledge a belief, preference, or identity that was previously kept hidden.
example_sentence: It took years of courage for him to come out of the closet to his family. She finally decided to come out of the closet as a supporter of the opposition party. Coming out of the closet can be an emotional experience for many people. Many public figures have come out of the closet in recent years to inspire others.

english_meaning: To do something no matter what happens, in all situations, whether conditions are good or bad. It is used when someone is determined to continue an action regularly or stay committed regardless of difficulties such as weather problems, obstacles, or challenges. It shows strong dedication and consistency.
synonyms: ["No matter what","Whatever happens","In all conditions","Through thick and thin","Without fail"]
antonyms: ["Only in good weather","Under certain conditions only","Sometimes","Occasionally","With conditions"]
example_sentence: He goes for a walk every morning, come rain or shine. The school remains open, come rain or shine. She promised to support her friend, come rain or shine. The workers continue their job, come rain or shine.

english_meaning: To become noticeable, important, or publicly known.
example_sentence: His talent came to fore in the competition. Issues came to fore after the debate. The problem came to fore unexpectedly. Her skills came to fore during the project.

english_meaning: To become known, discovered, revealed, or exposed after being hidden or unknown. Information, facts, secrets, evidence, or truths that were previously hidden, unknown, or unnoticed become known to people. It is often used when something important is discovered after investigation, inquiry, or the passage of time.
antonyms: ["Remain hidden","Be concealed","Be suppressed","Be covered up","Disappear","Be obscured","Stay secret","Be withheld"]
example_sentence: New evidence came to light during the police investigation. Several financial irregularities came to light after the audit. The truth about the incident finally came to light years later. Important facts came to light when the witnesses were questioned.

english_meaning: To come quickly into your thoughts or memory. Suddenly remember or think of it. To be remembered suddenly, or to occur in someone’s thoughts.
example_sentence: When discussing influential modern artists, three names immediately come to mind. When you mentioned travel, Paris immediately came to mind.

english_meaning: To think of or produce an idea, plan, or solution. Provide or produce something needed. Offer or suggest something. Reach or achieve something unexpectedly.
example_sentence: She came up with a clever way to solve the problem. Can you come up with a new slogan for our campaign? He came up with an explanation for the delay. They came up with a plan to improve sales.

english_meaning: Pleasing and attractive to the eye. Having a pleasing appearance, especially referring to a woman. Suitable or appropriate. In accordance with what is proper or fitting.
example_sentence: The comely maiden captivated everyone with her grace. She had a comely face and a gentle smile. It was a comely gesture of kindness. The comely arrangement of flowers brightened the room.

english_meaning: Relating to a comet or comets. Resembling a comet in appearance or motion, often implying a bright, hazy, and fast-moving quality. Pertaining to the celestial bodies characterized by a nebulous head and often a luminous tail when near the sun. Associated with the study, observation, or characteristics of comets. Suggesting a transient, spectacular, or unpredictable nature, much like the infrequent appearance of a comet.
example_sentence: The cometary dust trail stretched across the night sky, a spectacular sight. Scientists are studying the cometary origins of water on Earth. Her cometary rise to fame was both swift and dazzling. The cometary fragment impacted the planet with immense force. The artist depicted a cometary shower in his latest abstract work.

english_meaning: To go somewhere with someone. To appear or arrive. To make progress or develop.
example_sentence: Come along with us to the park. How’s your project coming along? A new idea came along during the meeting. We waited for her to come along.

english_meaning: To return to a place, memory, or situation.
example_sentence: I’ll come back in an hour. Old memories came back to me. He came back from vacation yesterday. Don’t forget to come back after lunch.

english_meaning: To begin to suffer from an illness. To become ill with a particular disease.
example_sentence: She came down with the flu last night. I think I’m coming down with a cold. He came down with a fever after the trip. They all came down with food poisoning.

english_meaning: To regain consciousness, visit someone, or change opinion. To visit someone. To occur again.
example_sentence: She came round after fainting. Come round for tea sometime. He finally came round to our opinion. It took him a while to come round after surgery.

english_meaning: A state of physical ease and freedom from pain or constraint. A feeling of relief or consolation in times of distress. Something that provides ease or contentment. To soothe or console someone in grief or worry.
example_sentence: The soft cushions added comfort to the room. She tried to comfort her friend after the sad news. Modern homes provide every comfort of life. His kind words brought her great comfort.

english_meaning: A periodic publication containing comics, typically in the form of a brightly colored magazine. A comedian. A person who acts in a funny manner. Characterized by or relating to comedy. Humorous or amusing.
example_sentence: I love reading comic books every weekend. The new stand-up act was incredibly comic, everyone was laughing. He always has a comic take on serious situations. She found his sudden seriousness quite comic given his usual demeanor. The play was a comic masterpiece, full of wit and humor.

english_meaning: Comity, as a noun, refers to an atmosphere of social amenity. It implies a courteous and respectful attitude between parties, often nations or political entities, ensuring mutual esteem. It can also describe a spirit of friendly civility between nations. In a legal sense, it denotes the courtesy by which one court enforces the decisions of another of a different jurisdiction. Furthermore, it signifies a reciprocal respect for each other's laws and institutions. It is a harmonious understanding and a friendly agreement. It means a group of people who share the same interests.
example_sentence: The comity between the neighboring countries helped resolve the trade dispute peacefully. There was a notable comity among the scholars attending the conference, despite their differing viewpoints. The judge emphasized the importance of comity among the different legal systems. A spirit of comity prevailed in the community, fostering a sense of belonging. Despite political differences, a sense of comity often guides international relations.

english_meaning: To remind an important person or even from past with a special action or object, celebrate in memory
example_sentence: A series of movies will be shown to commemorate the 30th anniversary of his death. Many of the people & places in the book have been commemorated in the names of start.

english_meaning: An action, or a ceremony, etc. that makes people remember and show respect for an important person or event in the past. A statue in commemoration of a national hero. Something that is done to remember officially and give respect to a great person or event.
example_sentence: Protests and commemorations took place in several cities on the anniversary of the uprising. A set of stamps has been commissioned in commemoration of Independence Day. Thousands of veterans will take part in a commemoration of the battle.

english_meaning: To begin or start. To cause something to begin. To enter the first stage of an activity, process, or event. To formally start a ceremony, meeting, or legal action.
example_sentence: The ceremony will commence at noon. Work on the bridge will commence next week. The judge asked the lawyers to commence their arguments. We cannot commence the project without approval.

english_meaning: To praise formally or officially. To present as suitable for approval or acceptance; to recommend. To entrust someone or something to.
example_sentence: I must commend you on your excellent handling of a difficult situation. The teacher commended the students for their hard work. The judge commended the witness for her courage. I can commend this book to anyone interested in history. In his final moments, he commended his soul to God.

english_meaning: Deserving praise or approval. Worthy of admiration because of good conduct, effort, courage, or quality. Meeting a high moral or practical standard.
example_sentence: Her commitment to helping the poor is commendable. The firefighters showed commendable courage. He made a commendable effort despite limited resources. The students maintained a commendable level of discipline. Your honesty in admitting the mistake was commendable.

english_meaning: In a way that deserves praise or approval. In an admirable and worthy manner. To a notably high moral or practical standard. In a manner showing good effort, courage, restraint, or responsibility.
example_sentence: The volunteers responded commendably during the emergency. She acted commendably by admitting her mistake. The young team performed commendably against experienced opponents. He remained commendably calm under intense pressure.

english_meaning: An award or official statement giving public praise for somebody, something. Praise, or an official statement that praises someone. Praise, Approval
example_sentence: The film deserves the highest commendation. There were 16 prize winners and 18 commendations. Their hard work deserves commendation.  The President issued a commendation praising the volunteers for their exceptional work during the relief effort.

english_meaning: Matching something in size, importance, quality, etc. Suitable in amount or quality compared to something else, matching in degree.
example_sentence: Salary will be commensurate with experience. The agency’s workload has increased without any commensurate increase in staff.

english_meaning: In a way that is equal in size, degree, or importance. In correct proportion to something else. To an extent corresponding to the value, effort, risk, or responsibility involved. Suitably or appropriately in relation to circumstances.
example_sentence: As her responsibilities increased, her salary rose commensurately. The price should fall commensurately when the quality declines. Greater risks must be rewarded commensurately. The budget expanded commensurately with the size of the project.

english_meaning: A spoken or written remark expressing an opinion or reaction. A critical observation or a remark. An annotation or a note added to a text, diagram, or program. A casual or brief statement. A reference or an allusion.
example_sentence: She made a comment about the beautiful scenery. The teacher asked for comments on the student's essay. He added a comment to the design specifications. Please feel free to interject with comments or questions. His comments about the new policy were quite insightful.

english_meaning: A person who explains or discusses events on radio, television, or online. A person who gives opinions or analysis on news, sport, politics, or culture. A writer who comments on a text or subject. An observer who interprets events for an audience.
example_sentence: The football commentator described every move clearly. A political commentator discussed the election results. The commentator noted a change in public opinion. She became a respected commentator on modern literature.

english_meaning: The activity of buying and selling, especially on a large scale. Social dealings between people.
example_sentence: The city has been a major centre of commerce for centuries. International commerce has been affected by the recent trade tariffs. The Chamber of Commerce works to support local small businesses. The internet has completely transformed the way global commerce operates.

english_meaning: Relating to buying, selling, or business activities. Intended to make a profit rather than serve art, research, or public interest. Concerning trade on a large scale or the movement of goods. An advertisement broadcast on television or radio.
example_sentence: The area is being developed for commercial use. The film was a great commercial success. They run a commercial vehicle business in the city. A new commercial for the product will air tonight.

english_meaning: To officially assign or authorize a task. To formally authorize a person or organization to carry out a specific duty or project, or to order something to be produced for a particular purpose. A payment for services or the act of assigning authority. Money paid to someone for completing a task or making a sale. It also means a formal group appointed to perform a specific duty or the act of officially authorizing someone to do a task
example_sentence: The artist was commissioned to paint a mural. The army commissioned him as an officer. The city commissioned a study on flood risks. She earns a commission on every car she sells. The government formed a commission to investigate the issue. He was commissioned to design the new bridge.

english_meaning: To do something, especially something important or wrong. To perform or execute an act. To devote time, effort, or loyalty. To put something into a permanent record. To send to prison or a hospital by authority.
example_sentence: He committed a serious mistake at work. She committed herself to helping the poor. The company committed funds to the new project. The judge committed the criminal to prison.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being dedicated to a cause or activity. An engagement or obligation that restricts freedom of action.
example_sentence: Her commitment to her studies resulted in top grades this year. Marriage is a long-term commitment that requires trust and patience. I have a prior commitment this evening so I cannot attend the meeting. The company's commitment to quality is evident in every product.

english_meaning: A group of people appointed for a specific function by a larger group. A body of persons delegated to consider, investigate, or take action on some matter. A subordinate group acting as an advisory or decision-making body. An individual to whom the care of a mentally incompetent person's estate is entrusted in some jurisdictions. The managing body of a club or society.
example_sentence: The disciplinary committee decided to suspend the student for his severe misconduct. She was appointed as the chairperson of the finance committee. The planning committee meets every Tuesday to discuss upcoming local events. A special committee was formed to investigate the corruption allegations.

english_meaning: Commodate is a gratuitous loan for use, meaning a loan of something that can be used without being consumed, with the understanding that it will be returned. It is a type of bailment where the borrower (commodatary) receives an article or chattel from the lender (commodant) to use for a specific purpose and period without payment. The commodatary is obliged to return the identical item in the same condition as received, barring normal wear and tear. This legal arrangement is distinct from a loan for consumption, where the borrowed items are consumed and replaced with equivalent ones. It is often applied to movable property, such as tools, vehicles, or books, but not to money or goods meant for consumption.
synonyms: ["Loan for use","Gratuitous loan","Bailment for use","Lending","Temporary loan","Free loan","Lending agreement","Use agreement"]
example_sentence: The old farmer offered a commodate of his tractor to his neighbor during harvest season. The library operates on a commodate system, lending books to patrons for a set period. In some legal systems, a commodate agreement does not require a formal contract to be valid. She offered her bicycle as a commodate to her friend for the weekend trip. The museum often engages in commodate agreements with other institutions to display rare artifacts temporarily.

english_meaning: Having a lot of space. Offering ample space and comfortable accommodation. Large and roomy. Convenient and spacious. Providing plenty of room for comfort or storage.
example_sentence: The old house had commodious rooms, perfect for a large family. We found the hotel suite to be quite commodious, with plenty of space to relax. The new office building offers commodious workspaces for all employees. Her studio apartment, while small, felt surprisingly commodious due to clever design. The car interior was surprisingly commodious, making long journeys comfortable.

english_meaning: Raw materials or primary agricultural products that can be bought and sold, such as oil, wheat, cotton, or gold. Useful or valuable things. Articles of trade or commerce, especially products as opposed to services. Goods that have economic value and can be exchanged in markets.
example_sentence: Oil and gas are among the most important commodities in the world market. Prices of basic commodities have risen sharply this year. Farmers sell their commodities directly to wholesalers. The country exports several agricultural commodities to Europe. Honest information has become one of the most valuable commodities of our age.

english_meaning: The process by which goods or services lose their unique qualities and become simple commodities in the eyes of consumers. The act of turning a product or service into a commodity. The stage when differentiation between products disappears and price becomes the primary factor. The transformation of something distinctive into something generic and interchangeable.
example_sentence: The commoditization of smartphones has driven prices down. Commoditization threatens brand loyalty. Many industries face commoditization as technology advances. Companies must innovate to escape commoditization.

english_meaning: To turn a product or service into a commodity by making it widely available and interchangeable. To reduce something to the status of a commodity where price becomes the main distinguishing factor. To make something lose its unique qualities and become generic. To treat something as a mere commodity.
example_sentence: Technology has commoditized many consumer electronics. The market has commoditized generic drugs. Airlines have commoditized travel experiences. Companies try to avoid having their products commoditized.

english_meaning: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold. An article of trade or commerce, especially a product as distinguished from a service. Something useful or valued. Goods that are all the same type and quality, making them interchangeable.
example_sentence: Gold is a valuable commodity traded worldwide. Oil is one of the most important commodities. Fresh water is becoming a scarce commodity. Agricultural commodities include wheat and corn.

english_meaning: A naval rank above captain and below rear admiral. The president of a yacht club or sailing association. A senior captain commanding a group of ships. A title used in some navies and maritime organizations.
example_sentence: The commodore led the naval squadron into battle. He was elected commodore of the yacht club. Commodore Perry opened Japan to Western trade. The commodore inspected all ships under his command.

english_meaning: Occurring or appearing frequently, happening often. Shared by or belonging to two or more people or groups. Ordinary or of no special quality or interest. Of the most familiar type or standard. Showing a lack of refinement or good manners.
example_sentence: Colds are common during winter. They share a common interest in music. It is common knowledge that smoking is harmful. The park is common ground for the community.

english_meaning: An ordinary person who is not royalty or of noble birth. They are a member of the general populace, distinct from the aristocracy or the ruling class. The term can also refer to a person who is not a member of the peerage in the United Kingdom. Historically, commoners held fewer rights and privileges compared to nobles. In a more general sense, a commoner might simply be someone who is not particularly distinguished or prominent in their field or society. The term carries a historical weight, often implying a lack of status or power in a hierarchical society. It can sometimes be used in a slightly dismissive or condescending way, highlighting an individual's perceived ordinariness.
example_sentence: The queen, despite her immense power, often tried to connect with the commoners in her kingdom. As a commoner, he never expected to be invited to such an exclusive event. The revolution was fueled by the grievances of the commoners against the ruling elite. She always preferred the company of commoners, finding them more genuine and down-to-earth than the nobles. In that era, the life of a commoner was often harsh and unforgiving.

english_meaning: In a way that happens or appears frequently or in many places. Usually or ordinarily. In a manner that is typical or widespread. By most people or in most situations.
example_sentence: This word is commonly used in everyday conversation. Dogs are commonly kept as pets. It is commonly believed that exercise improves health. Such problems are commonly encountered in this field.

english_meaning: A state of noisy confusion or disturbance. A situation with loud noise, disorder, or uproar caused by many people or things moving or shouting.
example_sentence: There was a lot of commotion in the street after the accident. The teacher entered the class to find students in complete commotion. A loud noise caused a commotion among the crowd. When the lights went out, there was commotion in the hall.

english_meaning: Relating to a community or a commune. Shared by all members of a community. Concerning the relations between different communities, often with implied conflict. For example, communal violence. For shared use by members of a group or community.
example_sentence: The communal kitchen was always busy with residents preparing meals. The communal harmony in the village was exemplary. The communal tensions escalated after the incident. We all contributed to the communal fund for the new park. The students shared communal bathrooms in the dormitory.

english_meaning: To share or exchange information, news, or ideas with someone. To express thoughts, feelings, or information clearly to others. To pass on a disease from one person or organism to another. To connect or make a connection between two places or things. To successfully convey meaning through words, signs, or behavior.
example_sentence: Parents should communicate openly with their children. She can communicate in three different languages. The two rooms communicate through a small door. He struggled to communicate his feelings to her.

english_meaning: Willing, ready, or able to talk or share information. Relating to communication. Open and expressive in conveying thoughts or feelings.
example_sentence: She is friendly and very communicative with her students. He was not communicative about his personal life. Good teachers need to be communicative. Modern technology has made us more communicative.

english_meaning: A person who is able to share information, ideas, or feelings clearly with others. Someone skilled at expressing thoughts so that people understand them easily. A device or system used to send and receive messages.
example_sentence: She is a gifted communicator who can explain difficult ideas simply. Good teachers are usually excellent communicators. The manager praised him as a clear communicator. The rescue team carried a small radio communicator.

english_meaning: The sharing or exchanging of intimate thoughts and feelings, especially when the exchange is on a mental or spiritual level. The service of Christian worship at which bread and wine are consecrated and shared. An act or instance of sharing.Holy Communion, a Christian rite in which consecrated bread and wine are consumed as symbols of Christ's body and blood.The state of being in close relationship or agreement, often implying spiritual or emotional closeness.A body of Christians having a common faith and discipline.Intimate fellowship or rapport.
example_sentence: They found communion in their shared love of music. The congregation received communion during the Sunday service. The artist sought communion with nature through his paintings. Through sincere prayer, she found a deep communion with God. The various churches enjoy a close communion.

english_meaning: An official announcement or statement, especially one issued to the public or the press. A formal message sent between governments, organisations, or officials. A written report giving news of a meeting, decision, or agreement.
example_sentence: The two governments issued a joint communique after the talks. A short communique confirmed the president's visit. The ministry released a communique explaining the new policy. Reporters waited outside for the official communique.

english_meaning: A political theory derived from Karl Marx, advocating class war and leading to a society in which all property is publicly owned and each person works and is paid according to their abilities and needs. An elaborate and pervasive philosophical system developed in the 19th and 20th centuries. A system of social organization in which all economic and social activity is controlled by a totalitarian state. The final stage of society as conceptualized by Marxist theory, in which the state has withered away and economic goods are distributed equitably. The political and economic doctrines of the Communist Party. Practice based on this ideology.
example_sentence: The collapse of the Berlin Wall symbolized the decline of communism in Eastern Europe. Many debates throughout the 20th century centered on the merits and demerits of communism. He wrote an extensive thesis on the history of communism. Cuba has often been cited as a modern example of a communist state.

english_meaning: A person who believes in or supports communism. Relating to communism, a system in which property and the means of production are owned by the community or the state. A member of a communist party or movement.
example_sentence: He was a lifelong communist who believed in equal ownership. The communist party won many seats in the election. She studied communist theory at university. Their communist ideals shaped the country's early policies.

english_meaning: People living in the same place or sharing interests, identity, or circumstances. A social group with common values or goals. The locality and its inhabitants. A group of interacting plants and animals. A feeling of fellowship and mutual support.
example_sentence: The community raised money for the new library. She found support in the local artistic community. Scientists studied the insect community in the wetland. The festival created a strong sense of community.

english_meaning: The official reduction of a punishment, such as changing a death sentence to life imprisonment or reducing the length of a prison term. Traveling regularly between one’s home and workplace or school. Converting a series of future payments into a single lump sum payment. In mathematics, the property where the order of numbers does not change the result, such as in addition and multiplication.
example_sentence: The governor granted commutation of the prisoner’s death sentence. Daily commutation to Karachi takes him two hours. The insurance company offered commutation of the pension into a lump sum. The commutation of numbers in addition makes calculations easier.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving the exchange or substitution of one thing for another. In mathematics, describing an operation in which changing the order of the operands does not change the result, such as addition and multiplication. Of or relating to commuting or travel between home and work. Pertaining to interchange or replacement.
example_sentence: Addition is a commutative operation because 3 + 5 equals 5 + 3. Multiplication is also commutative in basic arithmetic. Subtraction, however, is not a commutative operation. The teacher explained the commutative property using simple examples. Many algebraic structures rely on the commutative property.

english_meaning: A device in an electric motor or generator that reverses the direction of current.  A rotary switch in electric motors and generators that periodically reverses the current direction between the rotor and the external circuit. It allows the motor to produce a steady rotational motion or the generator to produce direct current.
example_sentence: The commutator in the motor needs regular maintenance. Sparks appeared at the commutator due to worn brushes. Engineers designed a new commutator for higher efficiency.  A faulty commutator can stop the generator from working.

english_meaning: To travel regularly by bus, train, car, etc. between your place of work and your home. To replace one punishment with another that is less severe. To exchange one form of payment, for something else. The journey that a person makes when they commute to work.
example_sentence: She commutes from Oxford to London every day. She commutes from Sunset Park to Manhattan each morning. He spent that year commuting between New York and Chicago. I live within commuting distance of Dublin. People are prepared to commute long distances if they are desperate for work. The death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.

english_meaning: Affixed closely together. Small in size or amount. Fitting in a small space. Having all the necessary elements. A small, flat cosmetic case.
example_sentence: The car is compact and easy to park. She bought a compact camera for her travels. The new apartment is compact but functional. They signed a compact agreement to work together. She powdered her nose using her compact.

english_meaning: A close friend or companion. An associate or comrade. A ceremonial kinsman, especially as a godfather or sponsor. A person with whom one shares a close bond, often implying mutual support or shared experiences. Often used informally to address a friend.
example_sentence: He greeted his compadre with a hearty handshake. My compadre always has my back, no matter what. We've been compadres since our college days. She introduced him as her compadre from the old neighborhood. It's good to see you, compadre!

english_meaning: A person or animal with whom one spends time or travels. A close friend or associate. One of a matching pair or set. A handbook or reference book on a particular subject. A person employed to live with and assist another.
example_sentence: The dog has been his loyal companion for many years. She travelled to Europe with a close companion. This book is a good companion for beginners in music. He hired a companion to care for his elderly mother.

english_meaning: The quality of being able to be compared. A sufficient degree of similarity that allows a fair comparison. The condition in which data, objects, or results are measured on consistent terms. The extent to which financial information can be evaluated alongside other information.
example_sentence: Researchers questioned the comparability of the two surveys. Standard units improve the comparability of international data. Differences in accounting rules reduce comparability between the reports. The teams used identical tests to ensure comparability.

english_meaning: Able to be compared with something else because of shared qualities. Similar in size, quality, or importance. Of an equivalent standard or value. Suitable for being judged alongside another thing.
example_sentence: The two houses are comparable in size and price. Her achievements are comparable with those of far more experienced players. There is no comparable service available in this area. Results were comparable across all three groups.

english_meaning: In a similar or equivalent way. To a degree that can be measured against something else. Equally well when set beside another example. In a manner that allows fair comparison.
example_sentence: Both machines performed comparably during the trial. The two candidates are comparably qualified for the post. Rural schools are not always comparably funded. The new model runs comparably well on older devices.

english_meaning: Involving the comparison of two or more things. Measured or judged in relation to something else rather than absolutely. In grammar, the form of an adjective or adverb expressing a greater degree. A relative rather than complete quality or amount.
example_sentence: She wrote a comparative study of two education systems. The patient is now living in comparative comfort. Bigger is the comparative form of the adjective big. Comparative analysis showed clear differences between the samples.

english_meaning: In relation to something else rather than in absolute terms. Fairly or rather, when judged against a standard. By way of comparison with other cases. To a moderate degree when set beside something different.
example_sentence: This winter has been comparatively mild. The task was comparatively easy for an experienced worker. Comparatively few people attended the second session. Prices here are comparatively lower than in the city centre.

english_meaning: To examine two or more objects or ideas in order to note similarities and differences. To represent as similar or to liken one thing to another. To form the degrees of comparison of an adjective or adverb. To be of an equal or similar nature or quality to something else. To view in relation to others of a similar category.
example_sentence: It is difficult to compare these two smartphones because they serve different markets. Scientists compare the DNA sequences of different species to trace their evolution.
