The monk spent hours in deep contemplation every morning. The painting invites the viewer into a moment of peaceful contemplation. The new policy is still under contemplation by the board.

english_meaning: Involving or given to deep, serious thought. Thoughtful, reflective, or meditative in nature. Showing a calm and quiet attitude of careful consideration. Relating to religious or spiritual meditation. A person who spends much time in thought or prayer.
example_sentence: He gave her a long, contemplative look before answering the question. She is a quiet, contemplative woman who enjoys reading and writing poetry. The old man sat in a contemplative mood beside the river. They lead a contemplative life in the mountain monastery. His contemplative essays explore the meaning of human suffering.

english_meaning: Belonging to or occurring in the present time. Modern. Living or existing at the same time as someone or something else. Up-to-date in style, design, or thinking. Used both for things of the current era and for people or events from the same historical period.
example_sentence: She is one of the most respected contemporary writers in the country. The museum displays both classical and contemporary art. Shakespeare and Marlowe were contemporaries. The house is built in a contemporary style with large glass windows. Many contemporary issues were discussed at the conference.

english_meaning: The feeling that somebody, something is without value and deserves no respect at all. A lack of worry or fear about rules, danger, etc. The crime of refusing to obey an order made by a court, not showing respect for a court or judge.
example_sentence: She looked at him with contempt. I shall treat that suggestion with the contempt it deserves. Politicians seem to be generally held in contempt by ordinary people. They had shown a contempt for the values she thought important. The firefighters showed a contempt for their own safety. He could be jailed for two years for contempt.

english_meaning: Disrespect or disobedience toward a court of law or its officers. An act that shows disrespect, defiance, or disregard for the authority, orders, or dignity of a judicial body. It may include ignoring court orders, disrupting proceedings, insulting judges, or obstructing justice.
synonyms: ["Disrespect toward court","Defiance of court","Judicial disobedience","Insolence to court"]
antonyms: ["Respect for court","Compliance with court","Obedience to court","Deference to judiciary"]
example_sentence: The lawyer was fined for contempt of court after refusing to follow the judge’s instructions. Posting private court documents online can be considered contempt of court. Shouting at the judge during the hearing is an act of contempt of court. Failure to appear in court without valid reason may lead to contempt of court charges.

english_meaning: Something or someone that is considered morally or socially worthless, despicable, or shameful. It evokes strong disapproval or disgust.
example_sentence: Lying to your friends is contemptible behavior. Betraying someone’s trust is a contemptible act. The criminal’s actions were contemptible in every way. Cheating in the exam is contemptible.

english_meaning: Showing contempt or deep disrespect. Expressing the belief that someone or something is worthless, inferior, or undeserving of consideration. Scornful in manner, speech, or appearance.
example_sentence: She gave him a contemptuous glance and walked away. His contemptuous remarks offended the entire team. The critic was contemptuous of the amateur performance. He laughed in a contemptuous manner. Such a contemptuous attitude makes respectful discussion impossible.

english_meaning: An action, expression, or tone that shows scorn, disrespect, or a feeling that someone or something is worthless or beneath consideration.
example_sentence: She looked at the messy room contemptuously. He spoke contemptuously about the idea without considering it. The critic laughed contemptuously at the amateur performance. They treated the new employee contemptuously because of his inexperience.

english_meaning: To say that something is true, especially in an argument. To compete against somebody in order to gain something. To say that something is true or is a fact. To state as the truth, claim. To struggle in opposition. To strive in debate, dispute earnestly. To assert or maintain earnestly. Two traditional rivals contending for the championship.
example_sentence: I would contend that the minister's thinking is flawed on this point. Three armed groups were contending for power. Two traditional rivals contending for the championship. There are three world-class tennis players contending for this title. He's contending against someone with twice his experience. The lawyer contended (that) her client had never been near the scene of the crime. I contend that a novel should tell a story and tell it well.

english_meaning: The things contained in something. The subject matter or ideas of a book, speech, or program. The amount of a substance contained in something. A state of satisfaction or happiness. Willing to accept something as adequate.
example_sentence: The content of the book was very informative. She was content with her simple life. Please check the fat content of the food. The website updates its content daily.

english_meaning: Causing or likely to cause disagreement and argument. Relating to a dispute or controversy. Involving heated debate between opposing sides. Describing a person who tends to argue and quarrel readily.
example_sentence: Land ownership remains a contentious issue in the region. The proposal proved highly contentious among the members. He avoided contentious topics at the family dinner. Her contentious manner made teamwork difficult.

english_meaning: A state of happiness and satisfaction. The peaceful ease of mind. Fulfillment of one's wishes or expectations. The feeling of being comfortable with one's situation. Freedom from worry or restlessness
example_sentence: He found true contentment in his simple rural life. A sigh of contentment escaped her lips after the pleasant meal. Material wealth does not always bring lasting peace and contentment. She smiled with deep contentment as she watched her children play.

english_meaning: A situation where two or more parties argue, challenge, or compete over an idea, claim, right, or position. It often involves disagreement, debate, or rivalry.
example_sentence: The contestation between the two candidates was intense during the debate. There was a contestation over the ownership of the land. Academic theories often face contestation before gaining acceptance. The policy faced contestation from several interest groups.

english_meaning: The situation, background, or circumstances surrounding an event, statement, or idea. The circumstances, background, or conditions in which something exists or occurs. It helps explain the meaning, relevance, or significance of a word, event, or action.
example_sentence: You need to understand the historical context to fully grasp the novel. His comments were misunderstood because they were taken out of context. The decision makes sense in the context of recent events. Teachers should provide context before introducing new topics.

english_meaning: Related to the situation, background, or setting in which something happens. Something that depends on or is influenced by the surrounding circumstances, background, or conditions. It helps in understanding the full meaning of an event, statement, or idea by considering the situation in which it occurs.
example_sentence: The meaning of the word is contextual, so it changes depending on how it is used. Teachers should provide contextual explanations to help students understand better. His decision was contextual, influenced by the situation at that time. Understanding history requires a contextual analysis of events.

english_meaning: Sharing a common border; touching or connected without a gap. Things that are physically next to each other, touching, or connected in an unbroken sequence. It is often used for land, areas, regions, or objects that share a boundary.
example_sentence: The two farms are contiguous, separated only by a small fence. These districts form a contiguous urban area. The forest stretches across several contiguous regions. Their offices are in contiguous buildings, making communication easy.

english_meaning: One of the world's main continuous expanses of land such as Africa or Asia. The exercise of self-restraint or moderation in regard to desires and passions. The ability to control the bladder and bowels. A characterization of remaining continuous or connected in a geographical or physical sense. An archaic term referring to something that contains or holds another thing within it.
example_sentence: Asia is the largest and most populous continent on Earth. He practiced a continent lifestyle, avoiding all forms of excess. The patient struggled to remain continent after the major abdominal surgery. The vast continent masses were once joined together in a single supercontinent called Pangea.

english_meaning: Relating to or forming part of a continent. Belonging to mainland Europe rather than the British Isles. Describing a light breakfast of bread, jam, and coffee. A person who lives on the mainland of Europe.
example_sentence: The hotel serves a continental breakfast every morning. Continental climates have hot summers and cold winters. She prefers continental cheeses to local ones. Many continentals travel to Britain for work.

english_meaning: The state of being dependent on chance or uncertain events. The quality or condition of being contingent, meaning something that may happen but is not certain. It often relates to events, conditions, or situations that are dependent on other factors or chance occurrences.
example_sentence: The success of the project has a high degree of contingence on funding. In philosophy, the concept of contingence explores events that could have been otherwise. Disaster planning accounts for all contingences to reduce risks. The outcome of the match was subject to contingence due to sudden weather changes.

english_meaning: A possible event or situation that might happen in the future, especially one that is unexpected. An event or condition that may occur but is not certain. It often relates to planning for unforeseen circumstances, risks, or emergencies. It implies preparation or provision for something that could happen.
example_sentence: The company set aside funds for any financial contingency. We need a contingency plan in case of bad weather. The contract included clauses for unforeseen contingencies. He prepared for every contingency during the expedition.

english_meaning: A group of people representing a larger organization or attending an event together. Describes something that may happen depending on another event or condition.
example_sentence: The success of the project is contingent on funding from donors. Attendance at the meeting is contingent upon prior approval. A contingent of soldiers was sent to maintain peace in the city. The students formed a contingent to participate in the cultural festival.

english_meaning: In a way that depends on something else happening. Only if certain conditions are met. By chance rather than by necessity. In a manner that is possible but not certain.
example_sentence: The bonus will be paid contingently on meeting the sales target. Funding was approved contingently upon the committee's final review. Events that occur contingently cannot be predicted with certainty. The agreement applies contingently, depending on the outcome of the vote.

english_meaning: Happening repeatedly with short breaks in between. Frequent and recurring over a period of time. Constant enough to be annoying or noticeable.
example_sentence: His continual complaints annoyed the whole office. Continual power cuts have disrupted business in the city. She suffered continual pain in her left knee. The continual noise from the street made sleep impossible.

english_meaning: Repeatedly and frequently, with short breaks in between. Again and again over a long period. In a way that happens very often and seems never to end.
example_sentence: He was continually interrupting the speaker with questions. The machine continually breaks down and needs repair. Prices have risen continually over the past decade. She continually reminded us about the deadline.

english_meaning: The state of continuing to exist or operate. The length of time something lasts. A postponement or adjournment of a court case to a later date. The act of remaining in a particular office or condition.
example_sentence: The continuance of the project depends on further funding. The judge granted a continuance until the following month. They prayed for the continuance of peace in the region. His continuance in office surprised many observers.

english_meaning: A speech sound that can be held for as long as the breath lasts, such as a fricative or nasal. Relating to a sound produced with an incomplete closure of the vocal tract. Something that continues or persists.
example_sentence: The sound of 's' is a continuant in English phonetics. Students learned to distinguish continuants from stops. Nasal consonants are treated as continuants in this analysis. The teacher gave 'f' and 'v' as examples of continuant sounds.

english_meaning: The action of carrying something on without stopping. A part that follows and extends something already begun. The act of resuming after a break. Something added that makes a work or process longer.
example_sentence: The novel is a continuation of the author's earlier work. They voted for the continuation of the aid programme. This meeting is a continuation of yesterday's discussion. The path is a continuation of the old railway line.

english_meaning: To keep doing something without stopping. To begin again after an interruption. To remain in a particular place, state, or condition. To carry on further in a stated direction. To extend or prolong something in time or space.
example_sentence: Please continue with your work while I make a call. The meeting will continue after a short break. She continued as chairperson for another two years. The road continues for another ten kilometres.

english_meaning: Kept going without stopping or being interrupted. Resumed after a pause or break. Ongoing and still in progress. Extended further in time, space, or amount.
example_sentence: We are grateful for your continued support during difficult times. The trial continued for another three weeks. The story is continued on page twelve. Continued rainfall has damaged crops across the province.

english_meaning: The state of continuing without interruption over a period of time. A logical and consistent connection between the parts of something. The maintenance of consistency in details across scenes of a film or story. An unbroken succession or flow of events.
example_sentence: The new manager was appointed to ensure continuity of policy. There is little continuity between the first and second chapters. A continuity error was spotted in the final scene of the film. The family business has maintained continuity for four generations.

english_meaning: A bass part that runs throughout a piece of Baroque music, providing harmonic support. The instruments, usually a keyboard and a bass instrument, that play this part. Short for basso continuo, the continuous accompaniment in early music.
example_sentence: The harpsichord played the continuo throughout the concerto. A cello and organ provided the continuo for the choir. Baroque composers relied heavily on the continuo. She studied continuo playing at the conservatory.

english_meaning: Going on without any interruption or break. Forming an unbroken whole in space or time. Steady and uninterrupted in flow or extent. (Grammar) Describing a verb form that shows an action in progress.
example_sentence: The machine produces a continuous stream of plastic sheets. We heard a continuous humming from the generator. She has been in continuous employment since 2015. The present continuous tense describes actions happening now.

english_meaning: Without interruption or pause. In an unbroken or uninterrupted manner. Steadily and constantly over a period of time. Without stopping or breaking.
example_sentence: It has been raining continuously for three days. The machine works continuously without stopping. He talked continuously for two hours. She has been studying continuously since morning.

english_meaning: To shape or define the edges of something. To trace, shape, or define the outline of something. The general shape, outline, or form of an object or surface. Lines on a map connecting points of equal elevation. Adjusting curves or outlines for better fit or appearance. Shaping by shading or highlighting.
example_sentence: The artist drew the contour of the mountains carefully. The makeup artist highlighted her cheekbones using contour techniques. The map shows contour lines representing different elevations. The designer contoured the furniture to fit the small room. Contour lines represent the elevation and shape of the land. She contoured the edges of the cake with frosting

english_meaning: Shaped to follow a curved outline or surface. Formed or moulded to fit the natural curves of a body or object. Marked with contour lines showing height, depth, or shape.
example_sentence: The contoured seat supports the lower back. The road follows the contoured hillside. She used makeup to create a contoured look. Engineers studied a contoured map of the valley.

english_meaning: Goods that are illegal to import, export, possess, or trade. Items smuggled into or out of a place in violation of law or rules. Prohibited articles secretly brought into a prison, school, military area, or other controlled place. Relating to illegal or prohibited goods. Historically, an enslaved person who escaped to Union lines during the American Civil War and was classified as seized enemy property.
example_sentence: Customs officers discovered contraband hidden inside the truck. Mobile phones are considered contraband in the prison. The ship was suspected of carrying contraband weapons. Guards searched every package for contraband items.

english_meaning: The lowest-pitched instrument or voice in a family of instruments. A double bass, especially in orchestral or jazz contexts. Relating to an instrument pitched below the bass range, often an octave lower. A performer who plays a contrabass instrument, in occasional usage.
example_sentence: The contrabass provides a warm foundation for the string section. He plays contrabass in a local jazz group. The composer added a contrabass clarinet for extra depth. A contrabass line moved slowly beneath the melody.

english_meaning: A very large double-reed woodwind instrument pitched an octave below the bassoon. One of the lowest-pitched instruments in the orchestra. A musician who plays the contrabassoon, by occasional metonymic use.
example_sentence: The contrabassoon added a deep rumble to the final movement. She began studying the contrabassoon after years of playing bassoon. The orchestra placed the contrabassoon near the other woodwinds. A quiet contrabassoon solo introduced the mysterious scene.

english_meaning: The deliberate prevention of pregnancy by using a drug, device, procedure, or method. The practice of controlling conception or fertility.
example_sentence: The couple discussed contraception with their doctor. Modern contraception includes pills, implants, and barrier methods. Reliable contraception can prevent unintended pregnancy. Education about contraception supports informed choices.

english_meaning: A drug, device, or method used to prevent pregnancy. Relating to or intended for contraception.
example_sentence: The clinic offers several contraceptive options. Condoms are a common contraceptive. She discussed contraceptive methods with her doctor. Correct contraceptive use reduces the chance of pregnancy.

english_meaning: To make a legal agreement or to become smaller or shorter. A legal or formal agreement between two or more parties. A legally binding agreement that sets out rights and duties between parties.
example_sentence: She signed a contract with the construction company. The workers demanded a fair contract before starting the job. He contracted a new supplier for raw materials. Metals contract when the temperature drops. Muscles contract when you move your arm. The company contracted a local firm to complete the project.

english_meaning: The process of becoming smaller or shorter. A shortened form of a word or group of words. A tightening of a muscle, especially during childbirth. A decline in economic activity or size.
example_sentence: Metal undergoes contraction when it cools. The word "can't" is a contraction of "cannot". Her contractions started early in the morning. The country faced a sharp economic contraction last year.

english_meaning: A duty, responsibility, or commitment that a person or party is legally bound to perform according to the terms of a contract. It means something you must do because you agreed to it in a written or verbal contract. It’s a promise or requirement in a contract that must be fulfilled.
example_sentence: The company failed to meet its contractual obligations under the supply agreement. Paying the rent on time is a contractual obligation for every tenant. Breaking a contractual obligation can lead to legal action. He completed all his contractual obligations before leaving the project.

english_meaning: To say the opposite of something or disagree with a statement. To deny the truth of something. To be inconsistent with something. To disagree with a person or idea. To show opposition in statements or facts.
example_sentence: He contradicted his own statement during the meeting. The witness contradicted the lawyer’s argument. Her actions contradict her promises. Don’t contradict your teacher in class.

english_meaning: Saying that a statement, person, or claim is wrong or untrue. Asserting the opposite of what someone else has said. Being inconsistent with or in conflict with another fact, statement, or action. Present participle of contradict.
example_sentence: The witness kept contradicting his earlier statement. She apologized for contradicting the teacher so sharply. Two reports are contradicting each other on the key issue. The evidence is contradicting the company’s public claim.

english_meaning: A combination of statements, ideas, or features that are opposed to one another. A denial of the truth of something. A situation in which inconsistent elements are present. Direct opposition between things. The act of saying the opposite.
example_sentence: There is a clear contradiction between his words and actions. The report contains several contradictions that must be explained. Her behavior is a contradiction of what she preaches. I noticed a small contradiction in his statement.

english_meaning: Tending to contradict, deny, or oppose. Expressing or involving contradiction. Inconsistent with another statement, fact, or idea. A rare adjective more commonly expressed as contradictory.
example_sentence: His contradictive reply confused the entire committee. The two clauses have a contradictive effect when read together. She adopted a needlessly contradictive tone during the discussion. Contradictive evidence weakened the original argument.

english_meaning: Expressing the opposite of something else. Inconsistent with or opposed to another statement. Containing elements that disagree with each other. Mutually opposed or inconsistent. Producing conflicting results or ideas.
example_sentence: The two witnesses gave contradictory accounts of the accident. His actions were contradictory to his words. The report contained contradictory information. She received contradictory advice from her friends.

english_meaning: A distinction made by contrasting one thing with another. The state of being clearly different when compared with something else.
example_sentence: In contradistinction to his brother, Ali is quiet and reserved. The essay defines liberty in contradistinction to control. Modern practice was discussed in contradistinction to tradition. The teacher explained prose in contradistinction to poetry.

english_meaning: Contrary to actual fact or to what really happened. Describing a statement, belief, or representation that conflicts with the facts. Counterfactual or factually opposite. A rare adjective used in logic, linguistics, and academic discussion.
example_sentence: The article rejects the contrafactive claim that no warning was given. Her contrafactive account conflicts with the recorded evidence. The scholar examined contrafactive statements in political speeches. A contrafactive assumption can lead the entire argument astray.

english_meaning: A temporary traffic arrangement in which vehicles use lanes normally carrying traffic in the opposite direction. Traffic moving against the usual direction. A system in which public transport or cyclists travel opposite to general traffic.
example_sentence: A contraflow system operated during the roadworks. Signs warned drivers about the contraflow ahead. Buses use a contraflow lane in the city centre. Police guided traffic safely through the temporary contraflow.

english_meaning: The prevention of implantation of a fertilized egg or the interruption of a very early pregnancy. The action or use of a contragestive agent.
example_sentence: The article distinguishes contragestion from contraception. Contragestion occurs after fertilization. Researchers examined the timing of contragestion. The clinic provided neutral information about contragestion.

english_meaning: Relating to or denoting an agent or method intended to prevent implantation of a fertilized egg or interrupt a very early pregnancy. A substance or method with such an effect.
example_sentence: Researchers studied a possible contragestive drug. The doctor explained how a contragestive method differs from contraception. A contragestive agent acts after fertilization. The paper discusses the medical use of contragestives.

english_meaning: A visible line of condensed water vapour or ice crystals formed behind an aircraft or rocket at high altitude. A condensation trail in the sky.
example_sentence: A white contrail stretched across the blue sky. The jet left a long contrail behind it. Scientists study how contrails affect climate. The contrail slowly dispersed in the wind.

english_meaning: To show that a drug, treatment, activity, or procedure should not be used because it may be harmful. To make a course of action medically inadvisable under particular conditions.
example_sentence: Pregnancy may contraindicate the use of this medicine. His heart condition contraindicates strenuous exercise. A severe allergy can contraindicate certain antibiotics. The test results contraindicated immediate surgery.

english_meaning: A condition, symptom, factor, or circumstance that makes a particular drug, treatment, test, or procedure inadvisable or dangerous. A reason not to use or perform something medically.
example_sentence: Pregnancy is a contraindication for this medicine. The doctor checked for contraindications before surgery. A severe allergy may be an absolute contraindication. Age alone is not always a contraindication to treatment.

english_meaning: Opposite in nature, direction, or meaning. Mutually opposed or inconsistent. Perversely inclined to disagree or to do the opposite of what is expected. An exact opposite. Unfavorable or adverse
example_sentence: His actions are entirely contrary to his promises. The politicians hold contrary views on the new tax laws. Don't be so contrary when we are trying to help you. On the contrary, I genuinely enjoyed the long performance. The boat slowly advanced against the contrary winds.

english_meaning: Acting against or reducing the effects of a sedative. An agent used or intended to counter sedation or excessive drowsiness. Opposed to sedation or calming effects. A rare medical or technical term whose meaning depends on context.
example_sentence: The researchers tested the compound for a possible contrasedative effect. A contrasedative agent may reduce excessive drowsiness in carefully controlled conditions. The paper uses contrasedative to describe activity opposing sedation. Doctors did not administer any contrasedative treatment without monitoring the patient.

english_meaning: To act against an established law, rule, or agreement. To violate a regulation or order. To go against or be in conflict with something. To deny the truth of a statement. To oppose or contradict openly.
example_sentence: Smoking in public places contravenes the new health regulations. His actions contravene the terms of the contract. The new policy contravenes basic human rights. Building without permission contravenes municipal laws. Their statement contravenes the official version of events.

english_meaning: An action that goes against a law, rule, or agreement. The act of violating or breaking a law, regulation, rule, or formal instruction.
example_sentence: Parking in a no parking zone is a contravention of traffic rules. The company was fined for contravention of environmental laws. Any contravention of the contract may lead to legal action. He was arrested for contravention of public safety regulations.

english_meaning: To give something, especially money or time, in order to help achieve or provide something. To help to cause an event or situation. To supply an article, piece of writing, or other material for publication. To play a significant part in bringing about an end or result. To share responsibility or play a part in a group effort.
example_sentence: She decided to contribute a large sum of money to the local charity. Several factors contribute to the rapid growth of the company. Everyone is expected to contribute their ideas during the brainstorming session. He regularly contributes articles to the science magazine.

english_meaning: The act of giving money, time, or effort to a common cause. A sum of money or resources provided to a fund or charity. An article, story, or piece of writing submitted for publication in a magazine or book. A significant role played in achieving a particular result or advancing a field. A regular payment made by an employer or employee to a health or pension insurance scheme.
example_sentence: Her contribution to the scientific community is truly remarkable. We are asking for a small contribution to help fund the new community center. All employees must make a mandatory contribution to the pension plan. The magazine welcomes an original contribution from freelance writers.

english_meaning: A rare or archaic term sometimes used to mean to ride against or in opposition; to counter-ride. Not widely used in modern English.
example_sentence: The knight would contride against his enemy in the tournament. He seemed to contride every suggestion made by the team. She had a tendency to contride opinions she disagreed with. The faction would contride the policies of the ruling party.

english_meaning: Feeling deeply sorry for one's mistakes. Experiencing genuine regret for wrongdoing. Showing sincere repentance for bad behaviour. Feeling guilty about hurting or disappointing someone. Being remorseful after committing an offence. Having a humble and apologetic attitude. Recognizing one's faults and wishing to correct them. Feeling sorrow for having acted dishonestly or unfairly. Expressing heartfelt regret for causing harm. Being sincerely ashamed of one's misconduct. Seeking forgiveness because of genuine regret. Being willing to accept responsibility for one's mistakes.
example_sentence: He looked contrite after realizing that his careless words had hurt his friend's feelings. The student gave a contrite apology to his teacher for cheating in the examination. She was genuinely contrite about her dishonest behaviour and promised never to repeat it. The politician appeared contrite and admitted his mistakes during the press conference.

english_meaning: Sincere remorse for wrongdoing. The feeling of deep regret and sorrow for having committed a fault or offense. It implies acknowledgment of guilt and a genuine wish to make amends.
example_sentence: After lying to his parents, he showed true contrition. Her contrition was evident in her apology letter. The criminal expressed contrition for his actions in court. Contrition often leads people to seek forgiveness.

english_meaning: A clever plan, device, or method created to achieve a specific. Something that is deliberately planned or invented, often showing cleverness or ingenuity.
example_sentence: The machine was a clever contrivance that saved hours of manual work. The story relied on an unrealistic contrivance to resolve the conflict. He escaped through a secret contrivance hidden behind the wall. The law was seen as a political contrivance rather than a genuine reform.

english_meaning: To manage or plan something cleverly, often with effort or ingenuity. To deliberately plan, invent, or bring about something, usually by using clever ideas, skill, or careful effort.
example_sentence: She contrived a plan to finish the project before the deadline. He contrived to escape without anyone noticing. They contrived a solution that saved both time and money. The author contrived an unexpected ending to surprise readers.

english_meaning: To be governed, managed, or regulated by someone or something. Being regulated or directed by someone or something. Authority or influence exercised over a person, process, or system. Supervision or management by a governing body. Restriction or limitation imposed by an external factor.
example_sentence: The project is controlled by regulations. Funds are controlled by the committee. Data is controlled by the system. Workflow is controlled by guidelines.

english_meaning: A person who directs or manages an organisation or activity. An officer in charge of financial accounts and spending. A device used to operate a machine, game, or system. Something that regulates or limits the working of a process.
example_sentence: The financial controller reviewed the annual accounts. Air traffic controllers guide planes safely to the runway. He bought a new controller for his game console. The temperature controller keeps the room comfortable.

english_meaning: Provoking or likely to cause public disagreement. Relating to or causing a dispute. Tending to argue or provoke severe debate. Highly debated among different opposing groups or individuals. Creating an atmosphere of ideological conflict or division.
example_sentence: The politician made a highly controversial statement regarding healthcare. Her new book was so controversial that it was banned in several countries. The referee's controversial decision led to an uproar among the fans. They avoided discussing controversial topics during the family dinner. Building the new highway right through the ancient forest is a controversial project.

english_meaning: In a way that causes public disagreement, heated discussion, or intense debate. Done in a manner that provokes opposing views.
example_sentence: The referee controversially awarded a penalty in the final minute of the game. The mayor controversially decided to close the community center. She controversially claimed that the project was a total waste of money. The book was controversially banned in several regions.

english_meaning: A prolonged public disagreement or heated debate about a subject. A state of conflict, dispute, or opposition among different parties.
example_sentence: The new law sparked intense controversy among the public. The politician managed to avoid controversy during his campaign. There was much controversy surrounding the publication of the report. The decision to demolish the historical building caused widespread controversy.

english_meaning: To deny the truth or validity of something. To argue against, dispute, or contradict a statement or belief. To engage in controversy over a matter.
example_sentence: The attorney attempted to controvert the evidence presented by the prosecution. It is difficult to controvert well-documented historical facts. She wrote an article to controvert the popular scientific myth. No one dared to controvert the judge's ruling during the trial.

english_meaning: Stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority. Rebellious and obstinate in resisting control. Showing a willful refusal to comply with court orders or official requests.
example_sentence: The contumacious witness refused to answer any of the prosecutor's questions. He was fined for his contumacious behavior in the courtroom. The teacher struggled to manage the contumacious student in class. A contumacious refusal to obey orders can lead to severe penalties.

english_meaning: Criticisms or insults that show a lack of respect. Insulting display of contempt in words or actions, contemptuous or humiliating treatment. Scornful or insulting language or behavior. Haughty and contemptuous rudeness, insulting and humiliating treatment or language.
example_sentence: She was indifferent to praise and contumely alike. The oppressor's wrong, the proud man's contumely. And as the contumely is greater towards God, so the danger is greater towards men.

english_meaning: To injure something by hitting or pressing it so that it becomes bruised but the skin does not break. To damage the body or an object through a blunt impact or pressure.
example_sentence: He contused his arm while playing football. The fall contused her shoulder badly. The accident contused several muscles in his leg. A heavy object can contuse soft tissue without cutting the skin.

english_meaning: A bruise or injury to tissue without breaking the skin. A type of injury where the skin remains intact, but underlying tissues, blood vessels, and muscles are damaged, causing swelling, pain, and discoloration. It commonly occurs due to a blow or impact.
example_sentence: He suffered a contusion on his leg after falling from the stairs. The athlete had several contusions from the rough game. The doctor examined the contusion and recommended rest. A minor contusion on her arm turned purple within hours.

english_meaning: A confusing or difficult problem or question that is hard to answer or solve. A tricky question that requires clever thinking. A confusing or complex problem. A situation with no clear solution. A logical puzzle or paradox.
example_sentence: The missing keys created a real conundrum for the family. Scientists are still trying to solve the conundrum of dark matter. Choosing between two equally good job offers is a conundrum. The detective faced a conundrum with no clear evidence.

english_meaning: Recover health and strength after illness or weakness. Make progress toward recovery of health. Recupe from a medical treatment or surgery. Regain one's physical well-being. Rest in order to get better.
example_sentence: He was given a few weeks off work to convalesce after his surgery. She went to the seaside to convalesce from her severe illness. The doctor advised him to stay home and convalesce properly. It took him several months to fully convalesce and regain his strength. They set up a quiet room where the patient could comfortably convalesce.

english_meaning: Bring together for a meeting. Come together for a common purpose. Assemble a group of individuals. Hold a formal gathering. Summon people for an official session.
example_sentence: The board of directors will convene at noon to discuss the new policy. The president decided to convene an emergency meeting immediately. Representatives from all nations will convene next month. They plan to convene the assembly to resolve the ongoing crisis. We must convene a panel of experts to analyze the situation.

english_meaning: Someone responsible for bringing people together for a meeting, discussion, or event. They coordinate, plan, and ensure the meeting runs smoothly. Often used in committees, academic, or organizational contexts.
example_sentence: The convener of the committee scheduled the meeting for next Monday. As the convener, she made sure all participants received the agenda in advance. The convener called an emergency session to discuss the new policy. University departments usually appoint a convener for every seminar series.

english_meaning: Someone responsible for bringing people together for a meeting, discussion, or event. They coordinate, plan, and ensure the meeting runs smoothly. Often used in committees, academic, or organizational contexts.
example_sentence: The convenor scheduled the committee meeting. The convenor sent the agenda to everyone. The convenor welcomed the guests. The convenor called an emergency meeting.

english_meaning: A building where nuns live and work. A community or residence for nuns, usually attached to a church or religious institution. It often includes living quarters, a chapel, and spaces for work or study.
example_sentence:
She entered a convent at the age of sixteen.
She spent her whole life in a convent. She spent her childhood studying in a convent school.  The convent had a beautiful garden where the nuns prayed. After joining the convent, she devoted her life to charity. They visited an old convent while traveling through Italy.

english_meaning: The way in which something is done that most people in a society expect and consider to be polite or the right way to do it. A large meeting of the members of a profession, a political party, etc. An official agreement between countries or leaders. A traditional method or style in literature, art or the theatre.
example_sentence: She is a young woman who enjoys flouting conventions. By convention the deputy leader was always a woman. Convention demands that a club member should resign in such a situation. The Democratic Party Convention (= to elect a candidate for president). The Geneva convention. The United Nations convention on the rights of the child.

english_meaning: Tending to follow what is done or considered acceptable by society in general, normal and ordinary, and perhaps not very interesting, Following what is traditional or the way something has been done for a long time. Using the usual scientific methods of Western medicine such as artificial drugs and operations. Not nuclear.
example_sentence: She's very conventional in her views. It's not a hotel, in the conventional sense, but rather a whole village turned into a hotel. You can use a microwave or cook it in a conventional oven.  Conventional treatments for this condition have been only partially successful. A conventional war would still cause unacceptable devastation.

english_meaning: A person who attends a convention or large organised meeting. Someone taking part in a conference, assembly, or professional gathering. A delegate present at a formal meeting of an organisation or party. A visitor who travels to a city specifically to attend a convention. A participant in a trade fair or industry congress.
example_sentence: The hotel was full of conventioneers from around the world. Conventioneers gathered in the main hall for the opening speech. The city earns millions each year from visiting conventioneers. A badge was issued to every conventioneer at the entrance.

english_meaning: To come together and meet at a common point from different directions. To move towards one another and eventually join. When people gather at the same place from various locations. When ideas, opinions, or aims gradually become similar or identical. In mathematics, to approach a particular fixed value or limit.
example_sentence: The two roads converge just outside the city. Thousands of supporters converged on the main square. Their opinions began to converge after a long discussion. Several small streams converge to form the river.

english_meaning: The process of moving toward and meeting at one point. The act of becoming similar or coming together. The merging of different technologies, ideas, or groups. In mathematics, the property of a series approaching a fixed value.
example_sentence: The convergence of the two roads happens near the bridge. We are seeing a convergence of media and technology. There is a growing convergence of opinion on this issue. Scientists studied the convergence of the two ocean currents.

english_meaning: Tending to move toward one point or to approach each other. Coming together from different directions. Merging or intersecting in ideas or characteristics. Approaching a definite limit in mathematics or science
example_sentence: The two countries have convergent interests in stopping global warming. A convergent lens focuses parallel rays of light to a single focal point. Their research paths were highly convergent despite starting from different academic fields. The theory suggests a convergent evolution where unrelated species develop similar traits.

english_meaning: Familiar with something through study or experience. Having a good practical knowledge of a subject or skill. Able to discuss a topic with confidence and understanding. Well informed about a particular matter or field. Able to speak and communicate easily in a language.
example_sentence: She is fully conversant with the new company policies. He is conversant in three languages. Every teacher should be conversant with modern teaching methods. The lawyer is conversant with international trade law.

english_meaning: An informal talk between two or more people in which news, ideas, and feelings are exchanged. The activity of talking with others in a friendly and relaxed way. A discussion about a particular subject, sometimes at a public or official level.
example_sentence: We had a long conversation about our future plans. Their conversation was interrupted by a phone call. She started a conversation with the stranger beside her. The book has opened a national conversation about education.

english_meaning: The act or process of changing something from one form, use, or purpose into another. A change in a person's religious faith or strong beliefs. The adaptation of a building or space for a new use. In finance, the exchange of one currency, security, or unit into another.
example_sentence: The conversion of the old mill into flats took two years. His conversion to Islam surprised many of his old friends. The conversion of miles into kilometres is easy with this app. Solar panels allow the conversion of sunlight into electricity.

english_meaning: To change or transform something into a different form, purpose, or system. To cause someone to change their beliefs, religion, or opinion. A person who has been persuaded to change their religious faith or another belief system.
example_sentence: They plan to convert the old industrial factory into modern apartments. Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electrical energy. He decided to convert to a new religion after years of spiritual searching. As a recent convert to the cause, she speaks with great enthusiasm.

english_meaning: A device, apparatus, or system that changes one form of energy, electrical current, signal, or format into another. A person or thing that converts something.
example_sentence: You will need a electrical power converter when traveling abroad with electronic appliances. The media converter changed the signal from fiber optic to standard Ethernet cable. Steelmakers use a specialized converter to refine molten iron into quality steel. A catalytic converter reduces harmful emissions coming from the automobile exhaust.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being convertible. The capability of a currency, asset, or security to be freely exchanged for another currency, asset, or cash without significant loss or legal restrictions.
example_sentence: The convertibility of the local currency attracted international investors. Gold was once famous for its easy convertibility into cash. The economic reform program aims to maintain the full convertibility of foreign capital. Limited convertibility can hinder the growth of international trade.

english_meaning: Capable of being changed in form, function, or character. A car with a folding or removable roof. A currency or security that can be converted into another form.
example_sentence: They bought a sporty convertible for their summer road trips. The sofa is convertible into a full-sized bed for guests. Convertible bonds allow investors to change debt into equity. The currency is freely convertible into foreign currencies.

english_meaning: Having a surface that curves outward like the exterior of a circle or sphere. Bulging or curving outward rather than inward.
example_sentence: A convex mirror provides a wider field of view for drivers. The outer surface of an eyeball is slightly convex. Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses and cameras. He preferred using a convex mirror to monitor the shop floor.

english_meaning: A polygon where all interior angles are less than 180 degrees. A polygon in which any line segment connecting two points inside stays completely inside. A polygon that curves outward at every vertex.
example_sentence: A regular hexagon is a convex polygon. All triangles are convex polygons. A convex polygon has no indentations. Convex polygons are easier to work with mathematically.

english_meaning: A quadrilateral in which every interior angle is less than 180 degrees. A four-sided figure with no inward-pointing corners. A quadrilateral whose diagonals both lie completely inside the shape. The usual type of quadrilateral, including squares and rectangles.
example_sentence: Every square is a convex quadrilateral. The diagonals of a convex quadrilateral intersect inside it. All interior angles of a convex quadrilateral are less than 180 degrees. He shaded the convex quadrilateral in the figure.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being convex. A convex curve or surface. Bulging or curving outward.
example_sentence: The convexity of the lens helps focus the light rays efficiently. Scientists measured the exact degree of convexity on the mirror. The design utilizes subtle convexity to enhance structural strength. Changes in convexity affect how light passes through the glass.

english_meaning: Make an idea, impression, or feeling known or understandable to someone. Transport or carry to a place. Communicate a message or information. Transfer the title to a property. Transmit a disease or illness
example_sentence: Please convey my apologies to your wife. Colors like red convey a sense of energy and strength. Pipes were laid to convey water to the house. He found it hard to convey his true feelings in words. The donor will convey the property to the trust next week.

english_meaning: The action of transporting or carrying someone or something from one place to another. A vehicle or means of transport. The legal process of transferring property ownership from one person to another.
example_sentence: The conveyance of raw materials across the country takes several days. Horse-drawn carriages were once the primary mode of conveyance. The lawyer prepared the deed of conveyance for the new property owners. They arranged for the conveyance of the patient to a specialized hospital.

english_meaning: A lawyer or specialist who prepares documents for the conveyance of property. A legal professional involved in transferring the ownership of real estate from one person to another.
example_sentence: We hired a licensed conveyancer to handle the legal paperwork for buying our house. The conveyancer checked the property title for any outstanding debts. You should consult a conveyancer before signing the property transfer agreement. The process was delayed because the conveyancer needed additional documents.

english_meaning: The branch of law concerned with the preparation of documents for the transferring of property. The legal process of transferring property ownership from one person to another.
example_sentence: The lawyer specializes in residential conveyancing. The conveyancing process took longer than expected due to legal delays. Make sure to hire a qualified solicitor for conveyancing. Fees for conveyancing usually vary depending on the property value.

english_meaning: A person or thing that conveys, transports, or communicates something. A continuous moving band or mechanism used for transporting objects from one place to another.
example_sentence: The luggage was placed on the airport conveyor belt. He acted as the conveyor of good news to the family. The factory relies on an automated conveyor system to move heavy parts. She was the main conveyor of local traditions to the younger generation.

english_meaning: To declare someone guilty of a crime. To find someone guilty of a crime in a court of law. A person who has been legally found guilty and is serving a sentence.
example_sentence: The jury convicted him of theft. He is a convicted criminal. After years of trial, she was finally convicted. Convicts in the prison follow strict rules.

english_meaning: Found guilty of a crime by a court of law. Officially declared to have committed an offence. Describing a person who has received a legal verdict of guilt. Sentenced after being proved guilty.
example_sentence: He was convicted of fraud last year. The convicted man appealed against the sentence. She was convicted after a long trial. Convicted offenders may lose certain civil rights.

english_meaning: A firmly held belief or opinion that someone is certain about. The legal act of declaring someone guilty of a crime after a trial. A feeling of being sure about the truth of something.
example_sentence: She spoke with conviction about climate change. His conviction in the courtroom led to a five-year sentence. I have a strong conviction that honesty is the best policy. The jury returned a conviction after hours of deliberation. His speech was full of conviction, and the audience agreed.

english_meaning: To persuade someone firmly that something is true through reasoning, evidence, or argument. To cause a person to believe in or agree with a particular idea, plan, or fact. To remove doubt from someone's mind by presenting compelling reasons. To succeed in making someone confident about a decision or course of action.
example_sentence: The evidence convinced the jury of the defendant's innocence.  She tried to convince her parents to let her study abroad.  His confident presentation convinced the investors to fund the project.  It took several attempts to convince him that the plan was safe.  The doctor convinced her patient to follow a healthier diet.

english_meaning: To make someone believe that something is true. Persuade someone to accept an opinion or idea. Assure someone about a fact, often with reasoning or evidence. Induce confidence or trust in someone regarding a decision or action. Influence someone’s judgment or attitude toward something.
example_sentence: The evidence convinced them of the risk. She convinced him of the need. Data convinced officials of the gap. Experts convinced communities of the danger.

english_meaning: Completely certain about something. Fully persuaded or firm in a belief or belief system.
example_sentence: I am fully convinced that this is the right decision. She was convinced of his innocence despite the accusations. The evidence was strong enough to leave everyone convinced. He was so convinced by the presentation that he invested immediately.

english_meaning: Capable of causing someone to believe that something is true or real. Serving to convince or persuade through logic, evidence, or appeal. Powerful, believable, or credible.
example_sentence: She gave a convincing argument in favor of the new policy. The actor provided a very convincing performance as the villain. There was no convincing proof to support the claim. The team scored a convincing victory over their rivals.

english_meaning: In a persuasive or credible manner. In a way that causes someone to believe that something is true or real. Firmly establishing belief or trust through strong evidence or argument.
example_sentence: She argued her case convincingly before the judge. The actor played the role so convincingly that everyone believed he was a real doctor. The team won the championship convincingly with a six-goal lead. He spoke convincingly about the need for immediate environmental action.

english_meaning: Friendly, lively, and enjoyable. Often used to describe an atmosphere, event, or a person who is cheerful, fond of feasting, drinking, and good company. It refers to a pleasant and sociable environment where people enjoy being together happily.
example_sentence: The restaurant has a highly convivial atmosphere that attracts many customers. He was a convivial party host who made everyone feel welcomed. We enjoyed a convivial evening with good food and lots of laughter. Her convivial nature makes her very popular among her colleagues. The festival was a highly convivial event where people celebrated and mingled together.

english_meaning: To feast or dine together. To share food and drink in friendly company. To live or socialize together harmoniously. A rare and literary verb connected with convivial gathering.
example_sentence: The travelers convived at a long table after the journey. Friends gathered to convive and exchange stories. The villagers convived peacefully during the harvest festival. The author describes artists who worked and convived in the same house. We convived late into the evening over a simple meal.

english_meaning: Relating to, occupied with, or fond of feasting, drinking, and good company. It describes an atmosphere or event that is friendly, lively, and enjoyable. When describing a person, it means they are cheerfully sociable, welcoming, and hospitable.
example_sentence: The friends had a convivial evening filled with laughter and good food. She was a convivial host who made everyone feel right at home. The local pub has a very convivial atmosphere on Friday nights. He is widely known for his convivial nature and ability to make friends easily.

english_meaning: To twist or coil. To make something complicated or intricate. Twisted, coiled, or extremely complicated in structure or meaning.
example_sentence: The wire was convoluted into a tight coil. The professor’s explanation was so convoluted that no one understood it. He wrote a convoluted argument full of unnecessary details. The plot of the movie is convoluted but interesting.

english_meaning: Extremely complex, complicated, or difficult to follow. Having many twists and turns (literally or figuratively). Used for: plans, arguments, stories, explanations, sentences, or paths that are hard to understand because of complexity.
example_sentence: The novel’s plot is so convoluted that I had to read it twice to understand it. He gave a convoluted explanation that confused everyone. The city’s streets are so convoluted that tourists often get lost. Her reasoning was too convoluted for the audience to follow.

english_meaning: A shout used to attract attention, especially over a long distance. Originally an Australian Aboriginal call used as a signal in the bush. Also used in the phrase 'within cooee' meaning nearby.
example_sentence: She called out cooee to find her friends in the bush. He let out a loud cooee across the valley. Within cooee of the town, they finally found shelter. They were well within cooee of the finish line. Cooee! I am calling you from the hilltop. She cooeed across the field for her brother. His cooee echoed through the valley.

english_meaning: A small, flat, sweet baked food made from flour, sugar, and butter, often with added chips, nuts, or dried fruit. A small piece of data stored on a user's computer by a web browser to remember information about the user. A person of a specified kind (informal).
example_sentence: She baked a batch of chocolate chip cookies for the children. The website stores a cookie on your browser to remember your login details. He is one tough cookie who never gives up under pressure. Please accept cookies to continue browsing the site.

english_meaning: Very calm and relaxed, especially in a stressful situation. A person who remains very calm, composed, and unbothered even when situations are stressful, difficult, or surprising. It shows strong emotional control.
example_sentence: Even during the emergency, she was cool as a cucumber. The player remained cool as a cucumber before taking the penalty shot. While everyone panicked, he stayed cool as a cucumber. The speaker was cool as a cucumber despite the huge crowd.

english_meaning: Very calm and relaxed, especially in a stressful situation. Completely composed and untroubled under pressure.
example_sentence: Even during the crisis, she remained cool as a cucumber. He walked into the interview cool as a cucumber. The pilot stayed cool as a cucumber during the emergency landing. While everyone panicked, Ali was cool as a cucumber.

english_meaning: To come together and form one whole. To unite or merge into a single group, mass, or idea. To grow together as parts of a body or system. To combine elements so that they cannot be easily separated. To blend or fuse different things into a unified form.
example_sentence: Small groups eventually coalesced into a powerful movement. The tiny droplets coalesced into a large puddle. Different opinions coalesced into a single policy. Various tribes coalesced to form a new nation.

english_meaning: To work together with others to achieve a shared aim. To help someone willingly by doing what they ask. To act together in a useful and helpful way. To be willing to assist rather than to resist.
example_sentence: The two countries agreed to cooperate on trade. Please cooperate with the police during the inquiry. If we all cooperate, the work will finish quickly. He refused to cooperate with the investigation.

english_meaning: The act of working together with others for a common purpose. Willing help and assistance given to someone. Joint effort between people, groups, or countries. A helpful attitude that makes shared work easier.
example_sentence: Thank you for your cooperation during the inspection. The project succeeded through close cooperation between the teams. There is growing cooperation between the two nations. Without your cooperation, we cannot finish on time.

english_meaning: Willing to help and work together with others. Involving joint effort or shared work. A business or farm owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits. Relating to cooperation between people or organizations.
example_sentence: The witness was very cooperative with the police. Farmers formed a cooperative to sell their crops. We need a cooperative effort to solve this problem. She joined the local housing cooperative.

english_meaning: In a manner that involves working together with others toward a common goal. Acting in a helpful, willing, and collaborative way. Through cooperation and mutual assistance. In the spirit of teamwork and joint effort.
example_sentence: Students were asked to work cooperatively on group assignments. The nations acted cooperatively to address the crisis. Employees cooperatively shared their expertise. The community cooperatively raised funds for the project.

english_meaning: To expertly bring the different elements of a complex activity or organization into a harmonious or efficient relationship. To securely negotiate with others in order to happily work together effectively. A distinct set of reliable numbers used to specify the exact geographical location of a specific point.
example_sentence: The complex global relief efforts were extremely difficult to coordinate adequately due to the severe unseasonal weather. We desperately need to coordinate our busy daily schedules so we can swiftly hold an important meeting. She was officially hired early to expertly coordinate the massive logistics of the entire international event. Please carefully enter the incredibly precise flight coordinates directly into the advanced navigation system.

english_meaning: Arranged in proper order. Working together efficiently. Having matching or well-matched parts. Brought into a common action or movement. Planned together effectively
example_sentence: The rescue efforts were highly coordinated to save the victims. She planned a beautifully coordinated outfit for the special event. The team launched a coordinated attack on the enemy base. Management requires coordinated action from all departments to succeed. The dancers moved in a smoothly coordinated routine.

english_meaning: The organizing of different people or activities so that they work well together. The smooth and balanced movement of parts of the body. Cooperation between groups working towards a common goal. The act of bringing things into a proper or harmonious relationship.
example_sentence: Good coordination between departments improved the results. The exercise improves hand-eye coordination. The rescue operation required careful coordination. She is responsible for the coordination of the event.

english_meaning: A person who organises people or activities so that they work well together. Someone responsible for managing the different parts of a project. An official who arranges cooperation between groups or departments. A person who brings order and harmony to a joint effort.
example_sentence: She works as the project coordinator for the whole region. The event coordinator arranged everything within a week. Please contact the course coordinator for further details. A good coordinator keeps every team informed.

english_meaning: A police officer whose job is to enforce the law and prevent crime. To catch or arrest an offender or criminal. To receive or obtain something, often a punishment or an attitude. To plead guilty to a lesser charge in order to receive a lighter sentence.
example_sentence: The cop patrolling the neighborhood stopped to help a lost child. He decided to cop a plea to avoid a lengthy and unpredictable trial. She managed to cop some tickets to the sold-out concert. The traffic cop gave him a ticket for running the red light.

english_meaning: To deal successfully with a difficult situation. To manage, handle, or endure a challenging, stressful, or adverse situation effectively. It involves using skills, strategies, or resilience to maintain stability or continue functioning despite difficulties. A covering or protective layer in specific contexts, such as architecture or geology.
example_sentence: He wasn't able to cope with the stresses & strains of the job. I got to the stage where I wasn't coping with any one. She is learning to cope with stress at work. It was hard to cope with the loss of a loved one. He copes with criticism by focusing on solutions. Students must cope with exam pressure. The roof has a protective cope to prevent water damage.

english_meaning: To deal effectively with a difficult situation or problem. Handle or manage challenges.
example_sentence: He tried to cope up after the loss. Students cope up during exams. Teams cope up in stress. Workers cope up with workload shifts.

english_meaning: To deal successfully with a difficult situation or challenge. To handling, managing, or enduring challenges, stress, or difficult circumstances effectively. It often implies maintaining stability or finding solutions despite obstacles.
example_sentence: She struggled to cope up with the sudden changes at work. It's hard to cope up with the pressure of exams. He learned to cope up with the loss of his pet. They had to cope up with the unexpected storm during the trip.

english_meaning: To deal successfully with a difficult situation or problem. To face problems or challenges without letting them overwhelm you. To adjust or adapt to a new or stressful situation. To survive or endure adversity while maintaining stability.
example_sentence: Nurses often cope with long shifts and emotional stress. He coped with the criticism by focusing on his strengths. Small businesses cope with economic downturns in creative ways. We must cope with climate change through planning and adaptation

english_meaning: Abundant in supply or quantity. Yielding something abundantly. Affording a plentiful supply. Large in quantity or number. Plentiful in words or matter. Having or producing a large amount
example_sentence: She took copious notes during the extremely fast lecture. The storm produced copious amounts of rain over the weekend. He drank copious amounts of coffee to stay awake. The author provided copious details about the historical event. The garden yielded a copious harvest this year.

english_meaning: Having the reddish-brown color of copper. Resembling copper in color or shine. Tasting or smelling like copper or metal. Made of or containing copper.
example_sentence: Her hair shone with a coppery glow in the sunlight. The autumn leaves turned a coppery red. He noticed a coppery taste in his mouth after the fall. The old coins had a dull coppery shine.

english_meaning: A small area covered with trees or bushes, smaller than a forest or woodland. It is often found in the countryside and may provide shelter for wildlife. The word copse is commonly used in literature, nature writing, and geography to describe a small wooded area that is larger than a grove but smaller than a forest.
example_sentence: The deer disappeared into a nearby copse of trees. Birds were singing from the small copse behind the farmhouse. We rested in a shady copse during our hike. A narrow path led through the copse to the river.

english_meaning: To write something again exactly as it is written or printed somewhere else.
example_sentence: Copy out the passage in your notebook. He copied out the poem neatly. Don’t just copy out the answers—understand them. The student copied out every line carefully.

english_meaning: A person who imitates or copies another person's actions, style, or ideas. Someone who mimics others without originality. A child's word for one who copies. Describing behavior that closely follows another's example. An imitator who lacks creativity of their own.
example_sentence: Stop being a copycat and think of your own ideas. His little brother is such a copycat. The company was accused of copycat marketing tactics. She called her friend a copycat for wearing the same dress.

english_meaning: A person (especially a woman) behaves in a playful, teasing, or flirtatious way to attract attention or admiration, often charming but not serious in romantic interest.
example_sentence: She gave him a coquettish smile before turning away. Her coquettish behavior at the party drew everyone’s attention. The actress played a coquettish role in the romantic comedy. With a coquettish glance, she teased him playfully.

english_meaning: A hard, stony substance formed by tiny sea creatures in warm oceans. The colourful marine structure known as a reef built by these creatures. A pinkish-orange colour resembling coral. Made of or having the colour of coral.
example_sentence: Divers explored the colourful coral near the island. Rising sea temperatures are damaging coral reefs. She wore a coral necklace with her white dress. The walls were painted a soft coral shade.

english_meaning: A long thin flexible string or rope made from twists of threads. An insulated electrical cable or wire used to connect appliances to a power source. A specific anatomical structure in the body that resembles a rope. A customary unit of volume used for measuring cut firewood. To secure or bind something firmly with a rope or twine
example_sentence: She tied the package securely with a strong cord. The computer power cord is too short to reach the wall outlet. The doctor examined his vocal cords using a tiny camera. We need to order a cord of wood for the upcoming winter. Please cord these heavy boxes together before the moving truck arrives.

english_meaning: Warm and friendly. Hearty and sincere. Strongly felt or deeply experienced. A sweet, non-alcoholic fruit-flavored drink. An invigorating and stimulating medicine or drink.
example_sentence: The two nations maintain a cordial relationship. She gave us a cordial greeting when we arrived. We shared a glass of cherry cordial after dinner. Despite their differences, they remained cordial to each other.

english_meaning: In a warm and friendly way. With sincere affection. Politely and graciously. With deep and heartfelt feelings. In a deeply welcoming or hospitable manner
example_sentence: You are cordially invited to attend the annual gala. The host cordially greeted every guest at the door. She cordially thanked them for their invaluable support. We cordially welcome you to our new home. He cordially accepted the invitation to speak at the event.

english_meaning: To surround or block off an area for safety or security reasons.  A line of police, soldiers, or guards forming a barrier around a place to restrict access. A rope, ribbon, or tape used to enclose or block off an area. In architecture or decoration, a carved or molded ornamental band.
example_sentence: Protesters tried to break through a police cordon. A cordon of police surrounded the building. Police officers threw a cordon around his car to protect him. There was a police cordon around the building. The police cordon was unable to hold back the crowd.

english_meaning: To block or seal an area so that people cannot enter it. To surround or close off a place using ropes, tape, barriers, police lines, or guards in order to restrict access. It is often used in situations involving accidents, crime scenes, construction areas, protests, or emergencies to keep people safe or protect evidence.
example_sentence: The police cordoned off the street after the accident. Security forces cordoned off the building during the investigation. The damaged bridge was cordoned off to protect the public. The school playground was cordoned off while repairs were being done.

english_meaning: To cut from the central part. The most important or central part of something. The central part of an object. The hard central part of a fruit such as an apple, that contains the seeds. he muscles of the lower back and stomach area which help you to maintain good balance, etc. A small group of people who take part in a particular activity. Most important, main or essential. Used to describe the most important or central beliefs, etc. of a person or group. Used to describe the most important members of a group.
example_sentence: You need four cooking apples, cored and sliced. This report goes to the core of the argument. Dutch paintings form the core of the collection. She claimed the original six countries of the EU constituted an inner core within the larger union. The standards of housing and education are often lower in the older urban cores (= the centers of towns or cities). Your posture will improve as your core becomes stronger. He gathered a small core of advisers around him. We need to concentrate on our core business. The government's proposed solution fails to address the core issue. The use of new technology is core to our strategy. The party is losing touch with its core values. The team is built around a core group of players.

english_meaning: A fragrant herb whose fresh green leaves are used to garnish food. The dried seeds of this plant, used as a spice. The plant grown for both its leaves and seeds. A common flavouring in South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking.
example_sentence: She sprinkled chopped coriander over the curry. Ground coriander is a key spice in the mix. Coriander grows quickly in a small pot. The soup tasted fresher with a little coriander.

english_meaning: A large, dark seabird with a long neck and hooked bill that dives for fish. A waterbird known for its excellent underwater swimming and fishing ability. Figuratively, a greedy person who takes far more than a fair share. Used in literature as a symbol of greed and endless appetite.
example_sentence: A cormorant dived into the lake and caught a fish. We watched a cormorant drying its wings on the rock. Fishermen in some regions train the cormorant to catch fish. He was called a cormorant for his endless greed.

english_meaning: A North American cereal plant that yields large grains set in rows on a cob. It refers to the edible seed of this plant used as food for humans and livestock. The plant produces tall, stout stems and is a staple crop globally. Sweet corn is a popular variety eaten boiled or roasted.
example_sentence: We enjoyed eating roasted corn on the cob during the winter evening. Corn is widely grown as a staple food crop in many countries. She bought a tin of sweet corn to mix into the chicken soup. The farmer harvested a large field of golden corn this season.

english_meaning: The clear, dome-shaped front layer that covers the iris and pupil of the eye. The transparent window of the eyeball through which light first enters. The part of the eye that provides most of its focusing power and protects the inner structures.
example_sentence: The cornea must stay clear for vision to remain sharp. A scratch on the cornea is extremely painful. Laser surgery reshapes the cornea to correct eyesight. The cornea has no blood vessels of its own.

english_meaning: An important quality or feature on which a particular thing is based or depends. A stone that forms the base of an angle of a building, joining two walls. Something that is essential, indispensable, or fundamental.
example_sentence: Trust and mutual respect are the cornerstone of any healthy relationship. The mayor laid the cornerstone for the new municipal library today. Free speech is considered a crucial cornerstone of modern democracy. Hard work has always been the cornerstone of his financial success.

english_meaning: An ornamental molding around the wall of a room just below the ceiling. A horizontal molded projection crowning a building or structure. An overhanging mass of hardened snow at the edge of a mountain ridge. To furnish or top with a cornice. A decorative framework to conceal curtain fixtures.
example_sentence: We admired the elaborate plaster cornice in the historic living room. The climbers carefully avoided the fragile snow cornice on the ridge. The architect designed a beautiful wooden cornice for the roofline. They decided to cornice the new library to give it a classical look. He installed a hidden track behind the window cornice.

english_meaning: A direct or natural consequence or result. A proposition that follows from one already proved. Something that naturally follows or results from another thing. An immediate deduction or inference. A supplementary consequence
example_sentence: Blind jealousy is a frequent corollary of passionate love. The huge increases in taxes were a corollary to the massive government spending. In mathematics, a corollary is a theorem connected by a short proof to an existing theorem. An inevitable corollary of the new law is a rise in unemployment.

english_meaning: Relating to the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle. Concerning the blood vessels surrounding the heart. Associated with heart disease or heart attacks. Of or relating to a crown or crown-like structure.
