example_sentence: He suffered a coronary artery blockage. Coronary heart disease is a leading cause of death. The patient underwent coronary bypass surgery. Regular checkups can detect coronary problems early.

english_meaning: One of the arteries that supply blood to the muscle of the heart itself. A vessel that keeps the heart muscle supplied with oxygen. The artery whose blockage causes a heart attack.
example_sentence: A blocked coronary artery can cause a heart attack. The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle. Doctors placed a stent in the narrowed coronary artery. Exercise helps keep every coronary artery healthy.

english_meaning: An official who investigates violent, sudden, or suspicious deaths. A medical examiner. An inquiring officer for unwitnessed deaths. A public official responsible for determining the cause of death. An official presiding over an inquest.
example_sentence: The coroner confirmed the exact time of death. A local coroner was called to investigate the accident scene. She works as a deputy coroner in the county. The coroner ruled the incident an accidental drowning. The body was taken to the coroner for a post-mortem examination.

english_meaning: Plural of "Corpus", see Corpus,
example_sentence: The linguist analyzed a corpus of Shakespeare’s plays to study language patterns. The museum displayed the corpus of ancient manuscripts. The investor’s corpus was placed in a high-yield account. The surgeon examined the corpus of the deceased carefully.

english_meaning: A military rank in some armies above private and below sergeant. Pertaining to the physical body rather than the mind or spirit.
example_sentence: The corporal led the squad during training. He received corporal punishment for breaking the rules. Soldiers respect the corporal’s orders. The doctor checked the patient’s corporal health.

english_meaning: Physical punishment intended to cause pain as a disciplinary measure, usually applied to children or subordinates. The deliberate infliction of physical pain by an authority figure, such as hitting, spanking, or caning, to discipline someone. It is often used in schools, homes, or military contexts. Modern views increasingly consider it harmful and discourage its use.
example_sentence: The school banned corporal punishment for misbehaving students. Many psychologists argue that corporal punishment can harm a child’s mental health. In the past, corporal punishment was common in military training. Parents were encouraged to use alternative methods instead of corporal punishment.

english_meaning: Relating to a large company or group. Of or shared by all members of a group. Forming a legal corporation. Belonging to a business firm. Combined into a single body or entity. Collective and communal in nature.
example_sentence: The corporate headquarters are located in the heart of the city. We need to maintain a professional corporate image at all times. They reached a corporate decision after several hours of deliberation. Many people are leaving the corporate world to start their own small businesses.

english_meaning: Government financial support, tax advantages, or favorable policies given to businesses. Public assistance that benefits corporations rather than individuals. Subsidies or protections granted to private companies.
example_sentence: Opponents described the tax break as corporate welfare. The report listed billions spent on corporate welfare. Supporters argued that the subsidy would create jobs rather than corporate welfare. Voters demanded greater transparency about corporate welfare.

english_meaning: A large company or group of companies authorized to act as a single entity and recognized as such in law. A legal organization established by a charter for specific purposes. The governing body of a city or town. A business organization formed by a group of people and having a distinct legal existence. A collective body of individuals treated as a single person in the eyes of the law.
example_sentence: The multinational corporation has offices in over fifty different countries. Small businesses often find it difficult to compete with a large corporation. The city corporation is responsible for the maintenance of local parks and roads. Lawyers worked for months to draft the legal documents required to form the new corporation.

english_meaning: A political or economic system in which organized groups such as business, labor, and professions help govern society. The influence or control of large corporations over public policy. A culture that prioritizes corporate interests and structures.
example_sentence: The scholar compared corporatism with pluralist democracy. Critics said the reform encouraged corporate corporatism. Historical corporatism gave trade groups formal political roles. The debate focused on corporatism and state power.

english_meaning: A dead body, especially of a human. The remains of something discarded or defunct. To lose control during a performance and laugh uncontrollably
example_sentence: The corpse was barely recognizable. The actor had to play a corpse lying in a morgue. Most of the corpses were badly burned, making identification almost impossible. The corpse had lain preserved in the soil for almost two millennia. The scene was so ludicrous it was hard to play without corpsing. He had a tendency to corpse in the middle of the sketch.

english_meaning: The state of being fat or overweight. Excessive bodily fatness. Bulkiness of body. Physical stoutness. A heavy or bulky body condition.
example_sentence: His corpulence made climbing stairs difficult. The doctor warned him about his growing corpulence. She lost some weight and reduced her corpulence. Old paintings often showed kings with noticeable corpulence.

english_meaning: Excessively fat or overweight in body size. Having a large, bulky body. Portly or stout in physical build. Fleshy and heavy-set. Characterized by excessive adiposity or obesity. Possessing a substantial amount of body mass.
example_sentence: The corpulent man found it difficult to climb the narrow staircase. Despite his corpulent frame, he moved with surprising agility on the dance floor. The doctor advised the corpulent patient to adopt a healthier diet and exercise routine. His corpulent appearance was a result of many years of sedentary lifestyle and rich food.

english_meaning: Large collection of written or spoken texts. Body or collection of knowledge, documents, or works. main body of a legal text or the substance of a document. Principal amount of money (not including interest).

example_sentence: The hotel staff are friendly and courteous. Although she often disagreed with me, she was always courteous. The ticket clerk was courteous and helpful. He was a kind and courteous man. My friend's reply was courteous but firm. Their customer service department always gives courteous responses, even to rude people.

english_meaning: A woman, especially in historical or royal times, who was well-educated, cultured, and often maintained relationships with wealthy or powerful men in exchange for influence, gifts, or financial support. In some historical contexts, courtesans were respected for their beauty, charm, intelligence, and artistic accomplishments.
example_sentence:
In ancient Europe, a courtesan was admired for her grace and intelligence. The courtesan entertained poets, artists, and noblemen at her palace. 
She lived the life of a courtesan, surrounded by luxury and admiration. Many courtesans of history were known for their influence in royal courts.

english_meaning: Behavior showing respect for others, A polite thing that you say, do while meeting with people. Provided free, at no cost to the person using it (like bus, car etc).
example_sentence: I was treated with the utmost courtesy by the staff. A courtesy bus operates between the hotel & town center.

english_meaning: A person who attends or serves at a royal court. A companion, adviser, official, or flatterer around a king, queen, prince, or ruler.
example_sentence: The courtier carried the king's message to the council. Many courtiers competed for the queen's favor. A wise courtier knew when to speak and when to remain silent. The old painting shows a courtier in embroidered clothes. Some courtiers gained power through flattery.

english_meaning: A formal agreement or contract between two or more parties. A solemn promise or pledge, especially in a religious context. An agreement that creates a legal obligation. In biblical terms, an agreement between God and humanity. A clause in a contract specifying certain conditions.
example_sentence: The two nations signed a peace covenant. The covenant between God and Abraham is central to the faith. Property deeds often contain restrictive covenants. They entered into a covenant to protect the environment.

english_meaning: To conceal/hide something (especially the truth, facts, or a mistake). To dress or cover the body (for protection, modesty, or warmth). To disguise / mask (so that something is not noticed).
example_sentence:
The government tried to cover up the scandal. 
She used makeup to cover up the scar. 
It was cold, so he covered up with a blanket.

english_meaning: An attempt to prevent people from discovering the truth about a serious mistake or crime. An action or strategy intended to conceal a scandal or illegal activity.
example_sentence: The government was accused of a massive cover-up regarding the scandal. They tried to organize a cover-up, but the journalists exposed the truth. A thorough investigation revealed the corporate cover-up. She refused to participate in the cover-up of her colleague's error.

english_meaning: The extent to which something is included, protected, or reported. News or media reporting about an event. Protection provided by an insurance policy. The area reached by a service such as a mobile network or Wi-Fi.
example_sentence: The news channel provided live coverage of the earthquake. Our insurance coverage includes medical emergencies abroad. Mobile coverage is weak in remote mountain areas. The research paper gives comprehensive coverage of climate change.

english_meaning: Hidden, secret, or not openly shown. It refers to actions, plans, or operations that are done in a way that avoids being noticed. Something covered or sheltered, like a protected place for animals.
example_sentence: The agent carried out a covert operation in the city. They had a covert plan to surprise everyone. Covert surveillance was used to monitor the situation. The animals found a covert place in the forest to rest.

english_meaning: To strongly desire something that belongs to someone else. To feel a strong and often inappropriate desire for something that belongs to another person. It usually refers to material things like money, property, status, or possessions.
example_sentence: He began to covet his neighbor’s luxury car. She covets her friend’s success in business. Many people covet fame and wealth. He was warned not to covet what does not belong to him.

english_meaning: Having a strong desire to possess something that belongs to someone else, especially material things. A person who strongly desires wealth, possessions, or success that belongs to others. It often suggests envy and greed, and is usually used in a negative sense.
example_sentence: He gave a covetous look at his neighbor’s luxury car. The covetous businessman always wanted more than his fair share. She became covetous after seeing her friend’s success. His covetous nature made it hard for him to be satisfied with what he had.

english_meaning: A person who lacks courage. Someone who is easily frightened and avoids danger, pain, difficulty, or responsibility, especially when bravery is expected.
example_sentence: Do not call someone a coward just because they are careful. The coward ran away when his friends needed help. He felt like a coward for not speaking up. A true leader is not a coward in difficult moments. The story contrasts a coward with a brave soldier.

english_meaning: Lack of courage. Fearful avoidance of danger, duty, difficulty, or moral responsibility. Behavior that shows weakness when bravery is expected.
example_sentence: His silence was seen as cowardice by many people. Cowardice kept him from defending his friend. The novel shows how cowardice can damage trust. She refused to mistake caution for cowardice. In a crisis, cowardice can cost lives.

english_meaning: Lacking courage. Showing fear in a shameful or weak way. Done without bravery, honor, or willingness to face danger or responsibility.
example_sentence: It was cowardly to blame the mistake on a child. The attack was cruel and cowardly. He gave a cowardly excuse instead of accepting responsibility. A cowardly person may hide behind lies. She refused to take the cowardly path.

english_meaning: A person who herds and takes care of cattle, often on horseback.
example_sentence: The cowboy rode across the open plains at sunrise. Old western movies often show brave cowboys fighting for justice. The cowboy fixed his hat and began his long journey home. He behaves like a cowboy, taking risks without thinking.

english_meaning:
To bend or crouch down in fear, shame, or submission.
It describes someone shrinking away from danger, threat, or authority due to fear or intimidation.
example_sentence: The little boy cowered behind the chair when he heard the thunder. Soldiers do not cower in front of the enemy. She cowered as the angry dog barked at her. He cowered in shame after being caught lying.

english_meaning: To bend or crouch down in fear, shame, or submission. It describes the act of shrinking or lowering oneself due to being afraid or intimidated.
example_sentence: he child cowered down when he heard the loud thunder. The dog cowered down in the corner when its owner shouted. He never cowers down in front of challenges. They cowered down to avoid being seen by the guards.

english_meaning: A person who tends, guards, or drives cows. A cattle keeper, especially one who looks after cows in fields or villages.
example_sentence: The cowherd led the cattle to the river at dawn. A young cowherd watched the cows in the meadow. The village cowherd knew every animal by name. The cowherd repaired the fence before sunset. In the tale, the cowherd becomes a wise leader.

english_meaning: A vain and conceited man who is overly concerned with his appearance. A foolish, showy person. The cap worn by a court jester, resembling a cock's comb. A plant with a crested flower head, also called celosia.
example_sentence: He dismissed the young man as a vain coxcomb. The play features a coxcomb who admires himself constantly. The jester's coxcomb was bright red and yellow. She planted coxcomb along the garden path.

english_meaning: To cheat, deceive, trick, or swindle someone. To persuade by fraud, flattery, or dishonest cleverness.
example_sentence: The fraudster tried to cozen elderly people out of their savings. He was too honest to cozen his customers. Smooth words can cozen careless buyers. The plot shows how a servant was cozened by a false friend. Do not let anyone cozen you into signing blank papers.

english_meaning: Giving a feeling of comfort, warmth, and relaxation. Small, snug, and comfortable in a pleasant way. Friendly and intimate in atmosphere. Convenient but sometimes suggesting favoritism. A warm and comfortable small space or covering.
example_sentence: We sat by the fireplace in the cozy little cabin. Her bedroom felt warm and cozy on winter nights. The café had a cozy atmosphere with soft lighting. They enjoyed a cozy chat over hot chocolate.

english_meaning: To try to become friendly with someone in order to gain favor, advantage, or approval. To behave in a very friendly, attentive, or flattering way toward someone, often because you want something from them. It can sometimes feel insincere or strategic.
example_sentence: He tried to cozy up to the manager to get a promotion. She is always cozying up to the teacher before exams. Some politicians cozy up to rich donors for support. He doesn’t trust people who cozy up to him too quickly.

english_meaning: A narrow break, split, or opening in a surface. A sudden sharp sound. To break, split, solve, decode, open slightly, or lose control under pressure. It can also mean excellent or highly skilled in informal use.
example_sentence: There is a crack in the kitchen wall. We heard the crack of thunder before the rain began. The detective finally cracked the case. Do not crack the door too wide. Even strong people can crack under constant pressure.

english_meaning: To make a popping or cracking sound by bending or pressing one’s knuckles (finger joints), often as a habit or to relieve tension. It refers to the action of intentionally making joints pop.
example_sentence: He likes to crack his knuckles before starting work. Some people find the sound of cracking knuckles annoying. Doctors say cracking your knuckles doesn’t cause arthritis, but it can be a bad habit. She cracked her knuckles nervously before the presentation.

english_meaning: To take strong and severe action to stop or punish illegal or unacceptable behaviour. To enforce rules or laws much more strictly than before. To deal firmly with people who are breaking regulations.
example_sentence: Police are cracking down on drunk driving this month. The school has decided to crack down on latecomers. Authorities cracked down hard on illegal construction. The bank is cracking down on fraudulent transactions.

english_meaning: To enforce rules strictly or take severe action against. To take strong or severe measures to stop or control unwanted behavior, activities, or rule-breaking
example_sentence: The police are cracking down on speeding The government is cracking down on tax evasion Schools are cracking down on bullying Authorities plan to crack down on illegal trade. The government is cracking down on illegal activities.

english_meaning: Continue quickly. To continue with something energetically or without delay
example_sentence: We should crack on with the work. She cracked on despite difficulties. Let’s crack on and finish this. He cracked on with the project.

english_meaning: To continue doing something with determination. To proceed with a task or activity with determination or focus.
example_sentence: We need to crack on with the project Let's crack on with our work They cracked on with the preparations It's time to crack on with the plan

english_meaning: To open or split something with a sharp movement. To break or open something slightly or suddenly, especially to see what’s inside. It can also mean to start something or reveal hidden information.
example_sentence: He used a stone to crack open the coconut. The police finally cracked open the case after months of investigation. She cracked open the window to let in some fresh air. The scientist cracked open the sample to examine its contents. He cracked open a bottle of soda.

english_meaning: To laugh uncontrollably. To laugh so much that you cannot control yourself. To suffer a mental or emotional collapse due to stress or pressure
example_sentence: The joke cracked him up She cracks up every time she sees that movie His story cracked up the whole class The comedian cracked us up

english_meaning: Severe and sudden action taken to stop illegal or unacceptable behaviour. A strict enforcement of rules or laws against a particular group or activity. An official campaign of strong measures against wrongdoing.
example_sentence: The government announced a crackdown on tax evasion. There has been a crackdown on illegal parking in the city centre. The crackdown on smuggling continued for several months. Police launched a crackdown against street crime.

english_meaning: Broken or split but not completely separated. Damaged by cracks. Informally, slightly crazy, foolish, or mentally strained. Also means having been solved, opened, or decoded.
example_sentence: The cracked mirror was still hanging in the hall. His lips were cracked from the cold wind. The police found the cracked password in the file. That cracked idea somehow worked in the end. She spoke in a cracked voice after crying.

english_meaning: To make a series of short sharp popping or snapping sounds. A pattern of fine cracks on a surface. The lively sound made by fire, paper, electricity, or dry leaves.
example_sentence: The fire began to crackle in the stove. Dry leaves crackled under our feet. The old radio crackled during the storm. A fine crackle appeared on the painted vase. You could hear the crackle of electricity in the wires.

english_meaning: To hold in arms. A small baby bed which can be pushed up and down. A bed or cot for a baby usually on rockers or pivots. To support protectively or intimately. To hold somebody, something gently in your arms or hands.
example_sentence: The baby slept peacefully in the cradle. This region is known as the cradle of civilization. She cradled the injured bird in her hands. He cradled the phone between his shoulder and ear.

english_meaning: Clever in a sly, tricky, or deceitful way. Skilled at using plans, tricks, or hidden methods to get what one wants.
example_sentence: The crafty salesman hid the extra charges in small print. She made a crafty move during the debate. A crafty fox often appears in folk tales. The plan was clever but too crafty to trust. He gave a crafty smile before answering.

english_meaning: To force things into a small space. To eat too much food quickly. To study intensively in a short time. To crowd many people or things into a limited area. A short period of intense study. To overload information into memory. To pack a schedule with too many activities. To force ideas or facts into someone’s mind
example_sentence: She had to cram all night for her final exam. They crammed too many clothes into the suitcase. The bus was crammed with passengers. He crammed his mouth with food during lunch.

english_meaning: To study quickly and intensively for an exam in a short time, usually at the last moment. To study hard for a short time before an exam. To memorize information quickly for a test. To prepare urgently at the last moment
example_sentence: I had to cram for the math exam last night. She crammed for hours before the final test. He always crams for exams instead of studying daily. We crammed for the history paper at the last moment.

english_meaning: To force people or things into a limited space. To study or put a lot of information into a short time. To include something in a tight schedule. To fit extra activities into available time.
example_sentence: We had to cram in all our luggage into the small car. She tried to cram in three meetings before lunch. He crammed in a week of study before the exam. They crammed in one more activity during the trip.

english_meaning: To force a lot of things or people into a small space in a hurried or untidy way. Used when something is put into a limited space in a crowded, messy, or forced way. It often shows that there is not enough space, but still things are pushed inside. It can be used for physical objects, people, or even information. To study intensively in a short time before an exam. To force information into memory quickly.
example_sentence: They crammed into the small elevator. We crammed all the books into one bag. The passengers were crammed into the bus during rush hour. She crammed her clothes into the suitcase quickly.

english_meaning: To force someone to accept an idea, belief, opinion, or rule in a way that feels aggressive, repeated, or unwanted. It often implies pressure or lack of choice.
synonyms: ["Force on someone","Impose on someone","Push something on someone","Preach to someone","Brainwash (in extreme cases)"]
antonyms: ["Let someone decide freely","Respect someone’s opinion","Offer rather than force","Suggest gently","Give freedom of choice"]
example_sentence: The teacher tried to cram the rules down the students’ throats instead of explaining them clearly. He felt that the company was cramming new policies down everyone’s throat. Parents should not cram their opinions down their children’s throats. The advertisement was cramming the product down viewers’ throats all day long.

english_meaning: To fill something tightly or to study something quickly in a short time before an exam. To push or fit things into a space in a very crowded way. To study a large amount of information in a short time, especially before exams.
synonyms: ["Stuff","Pack","Jam","Overcrowd","Memorize quickly (for study context)","Mug up (informal British usage)"]
example_sentence: The students had to cram up all the notes before the test. Don’t cram up your suitcase or it will not close. He crammed up for the exam the night before. The small room was crammed up with furniture.

english_meaning: A sudden, painful, and involuntary contraction of one or more muscles. It often occurs after intense exercise, dehydration, or keeping a muscle in the same position for a long time. It restricts movement temporarily until the muscle relaxes.
example_sentence: He suffered a painful cramp in his leg during the marathon. Swimmers are advised not to eat right before swimming to avoid a stomach cramp. The cold water gave her a sudden muscle cramp. Dehydration is known to cause a severe muscle cramp. She massaged her foot to relieve the debilitating cramp.

english_meaning: A small, hard, sour red berry that grows on low evergreen shrubs. A tart fruit commonly used to make juice, sauce, and dried snacks. The shrub that produces this berry, often grown in bogs. A deep red colour like that of the ripe berry.
example_sentence: Cranberry sauce is served with roast dinners in many homes. She drinks a glass of cranberry juice every evening. Dried cranberries taste wonderful in a green salad. The farmers flood the fields to harvest cranberries.

english_meaning: Relating to the skull. Relating to the cranium or head. Located inside or near the skull. Connected with the brain or nerves that arise from the brain.
example_sentence: The child was treated for a cranial injury. Cranial nerves control many functions of the head and face. The museum displayed an ancient cranial bone. Doctors ordered imaging to check for cranial bleeding.

english_meaning: Any of the twelve pairs of nerves that arise directly from the brain rather than the spinal cord. A nerve that passes through openings in the skull to supply the head, neck, and face. A nerve responsible for the special senses such as smell, sight, taste, and hearing, as well as facial movement and swallowing.
example_sentence: There are twelve pairs of cranial nerves in the human body. The facial nerve is the seventh cranial nerve. Doctors test each cranial nerve during a neurological examination. Damage to a cranial nerve can affect vision or speech.

english_meaning: The part of the head that encloses and protects the brain. The upper area of the skull formed by the cranial bones. An anatomical region referring to structures near the top of the head. A directional term meaning towards the head end of the body.
example_sentence: The cranial region protects the brain from injury. Doctors examined the cranial region after the accident. Eight bones form the cranial region of the skull. The scan showed no damage in the cranial region.

english_meaning: The part of the skull that encloses the brain. The domed upper section of the skull excluding the jawbone. The bony case that surrounds and protects the brain tissue. A medical term for the braincase of the head.
example_sentence: The cranium protects the brain from injury. Doctors examined the patient's cranium after the fall. The cranium is formed by several fused bones. Growth of the cranium continues during early childhood.

english_meaning: A small narrow opening, crack, or hidden gap. A tiny corner or space that is hard to see or reach.
example_sentence: Dust had collected in every cranny of the old shelf. A tiny plant grew from a cranny in the wall. The key slipped into a cranny behind the cupboard. They searched every nook and cranny of the house. Light entered through a narrow cranny in the door.

english_meaning: Something of very poor quality, nonsense, excrement, rubbish. Something worthless, low-quality, or inferior. Foolish or nonsense talk or ideas. Feces or excrement (informal).  Used as an interjection to express frustration, disbelief, or annoyance.
example_sentence: The dog crapped right in the middle of the street. Let's cut the crap and get down to business. He's so full of crap. You're talking a load of crap!. What a bunch of crap!. I'm not going to take this crap any more. The concert was crap. The team played crap yesterday. She thinks that most of what’s on television now is crap.

english_meaning: Feeling sick or unwell due to eating or drinking too much. A condition in which a person feels physically uncomfortable, heavy, or ill after excessive eating or drinking. It often relates to overeating rich food or drinking too much alcohol.
example_sentence: After the wedding feast, he felt completely crapulent and could not move. She avoided dessert because she already felt crapulent from dinner. The festival left many guests crapulent after hours of eating. He lay on the couch, crapulent and regretting his overeating.

english_meaning: A loud sudden noise made by collision or breaking. A violent accident or collision. A sudden failure of a computer, system, market, or plan. To collide, fall, fail suddenly, or sleep somewhere informally.
example_sentence: We heard a crash from the kitchen. The car did not crash because the driver braked in time. My computer may crash if too many programs are open. The market began to crash after the bad news. He asked if he could crash on our sofa for one night.

english_meaning: Falling, colliding, or breaking with a loud noise. Sudden, forceful, or overwhelming. In informal British use, very boring or unpleasant when used as crashing bore.
example_sentence: The crashing waves shook the old pier. We heard crashing glass in the next room. A crashing defeat ended their hopes. The storm sent branches crashing onto the road. His crashing entrance startled everyone.

english_meaning: To make an emergency landing of an aircraft or spacecraft, usually due to mechanical failure, that results in significant damage but is not necessarily fatal. To bring a vehicle down forcefully and often dangerously, typically without the usual safety procedures. Used figuratively to describe an abrupt and rough ending or interruption to a plan or process.
example_sentence: The pilot managed to crashland the damaged aircraft safely on the open field.  The spacecraft was forced to crashland after losing contact with mission control.  After the engine failed, the small plane had to crashland in a nearby lake.  Their ambitious plans crashlanded when funding was suddenly withdrawn.  The drone crashlanded in the backyard after its battery died mid-flight.

english_meaning: A large bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, usually made by a volcano, explosion, or meteorite impact. A pit-like depression on a surface.
example_sentence: The meteor left a deep crater in the desert. Smoke rose from the volcanic crater. The road was full of crater-like holes after the rain. Scientists studied the crater on the moon. An explosion created a crater near the old factory.

english_meaning: To strongly desire or want something. To feel an intense longing or desire for something, often something that provides pleasure or relief. It can refer to food, experiences, attention, or other emotional needs.
example_sentence: She craves chocolate every evening. After months of traveling, he craved the comfort of his home. Many people crave attention on social media. The baby craved her mother’s warmth.

english_meaning: Lacking courage; very cowardly. Showing complete fear and avoids facing danger or challenges. It emphasizes moral or physical cowardice.
example_sentence: He was too craven to admit his mistake. The craven soldier ran from the battlefield. She felt craven for not standing up to the bully. Craven behavior is never respected in a leader.

english_meaning: In a cowardly or fearful manner. Describes an action done with extreme fear, lacking courage, or showing cowardice. It emphasizes moral or physical weakness in the face of danger or challenge.
example_sentence: He cravenly avoided speaking out against injustice. The soldier cravenly ran from the battlefield. She cravenly refused to help her friend in trouble. The manager cravenly ignored the complaints of the employees.

english_meaning: A strong desire for something. An intense, often urgent longing for a particular thing, experience, or substance, often difficult to resist
example_sentence: She had a sudden craving for chocolate. After a long day at work, he craved rest. Pregnant women often experience unusual food cravings. He craved recognition for his efforts.

english_meaning: To move slowly on hands and knees or with the body close to the ground. To move very slowly, like a car in heavy traffic. To be full of insects, worms, or unpleasant things. A slow rate of movement or a swimming stroke.
example_sentence: The baby learned to crawl at seven months. Traffic was crawling due to the accident. The old kitchen was crawling with ants. She won the medal in the front crawl race.

english_meaning: To hide away because of shame, embarrassment, fear, or because someone wants to avoid people and the outside world. It is an informal idiom used when a person feels so embarrassed, ashamed, guilty, or upset that they want to disappear and avoid everyone. It can also mean staying completely unaware of what is happening around you, as if someone has been hiding from the world.
antonyms: ["Face the situation","Stand confidently","Confront openly","Show up proudly","Be visible"]
example_sentence: After forgetting her speech on stage, she wanted to crawl under a rock. When he realized he sent the wrong email to his boss, he wished he could crawl under a rock. I missed my best friend’s birthday, and now I feel like crawling under a rock. After everyone laughed at his mistake, he just wanted to crawl under a rock.

english_meaning: To behave in an overly humble or flattering way toward someone powerful in order to gain favor, benefit, or approval. It is used when a person acts submissively, flatters excessively, or behaves in a servile way toward someone important, usually to gain advantage, promotion, protection, or rewards. It often carries a negative meaning because the behavior is seen as insincere or self-serving.
synonyms: ["Flatter","Fawn on","Butter up","Sycophant","Grovel before","Praise excessively","Seek favor from","Toady to"]
example_sentence: He always crawls up to the manager to get special treatment. She refused to crawl up to powerful people for success. Some employees crawl up to their boss for promotion. You do not need to crawl up to anyone to prove your talent.

english_meaning: A short-lived intense fashion, enthusiasm, or popular trend. To make someone wildly excited or mentally disturbed, though this verb use is uncommon. It can also mean to produce fine cracks on a surface.
example_sentence: The new dance craze spread through the school. Fitness crazes often disappear after a few months. The toy became a craze during the holidays. Heat can craze the surface of some glass. She never understood the craze for that game.

english_meaning: A long high or harsh sound made by something old, dry, rusty, or under strain. To make such a sound.
example_sentence: The stairs creak whenever someone walks up them. I heard the creak of the gate at midnight. The old chair began to creak under his weight. A cold wind made the sign creak outside. The floorboards creaked softly in the hallway.

english_meaning: The thick fatty part that rises to the top of milk. A soft, smooth cosmetic or medicinal preparation. The best or finest part of something. To beat or mix ingredients until smooth.
example_sentence: She poured cream over the strawberries. He applied a soothing cream to his skin. Only the cream of the students were selected. Cream the butter and sugar together until fluffy.

english_meaning: A nitrogenous organic acid that occurs naturally in vertebrates and helps to supply energy to all cells in the body, primarily muscle. A popular dietary supplement used by athletes to increase muscle mass, strength, and exercise performance. A substance found in red meat and seafood. A compound formed during protein metabolism and involved in the supply of energy for muscular contraction. A crystalline compound that exists in the blood and muscle tissue.
synonyms: ["Methylguanidinoacetic Acid","Muscle Supplement","Performance Enhancer","Organic Acid","Nitrogenous Compound","Ergogenic Aid","Dietary Supplement","Bodybuilding Supplement","Amino Acid Derivative","Protein Metabolite"]
example_sentence: Many bodybuilders take creatine to improve their strength and power during high-intensity training. Creatine is naturally produced by the human body in the liver, pancreas, and kidneys. Scientific studies suggest that creatine can enhance recovery after strenuous physical activity. You can obtain small amounts of creatine by consuming red meat or fish in your regular diet.

english_meaning: Any living being, especially an animal. A person regarded with a particular feeling such as pity or affection. An imaginary or strange being found in stories and legends. Someone who is completely controlled or influenced by another. A living thing viewed as a product of its environment or habits.
example_sentence: Every creature in the forest depends on the river. The poor creature was shivering in the cold. Children love stories about strange creatures from the sea. Man is largely a creature of habit.

english_meaning: Belief in or acceptance of something as true. The quality of being believable or trustworthy. Trust placed in a report, statement, or theory. Often used in phrases such as give credence to or lend credence to, meaning to make something seem more believable.
example_sentence: The new evidence gave credence to the witness's earlier statement. I find it hard to give credence to such wild rumours. His long experience lends credence to his opinion on the matter. The report has gained wide credence among scientists. We should not give credence to information from unknown sources.

english_meaning: To be provided with credentials. To give official acceptance of as satisfactory. To furnish with credentials.
example_sentence: Faculty members needed to be properly credentialed in their respective disciplines. She was credentialed as a speech pathologist in August.

english_meaning: Holding official qualifications or certificates for a particular role. Formally recognised as qualified by an authority. Provided with documents proving identity, status, or ability.
example_sentence: Only credentialed teachers may apply for this position. The hospital employs fully credentialed nursing staff. She is a credentialed translator with fifteen years of experience. Credentialed journalists were allowed inside the hall.

english_meaning: The qualities, training or experience that make you suitable to do something. Documents such as letters that prove that you are who you claim to be, and can therefore be trusted. Something that gives a title to credit or confidence.
example_sentence: She has impeccable credentials as a researcher. He has all the credentials for the job. She will first have to establish her leadership credentials.

english_meaning: The quality of being believed or trusted by other people. The degree to which something appears convincing or reliable. A reputation for honesty and dependability. The ability to inspire confidence through knowledge or evidence.
example_sentence: The scandal seriously damaged the minister's credibility. Independent research gave the report much-needed credibility. He has built up credibility over twenty years of honest work. Without evidence, the claim lacks credibility.

english_meaning: Believable or trustworthy. Something or someone that can be trusted, accepted as true, or convincing. It implies reliability and plausibility.
example_sentence: She gave a credible explanation for being late. The witness provided a credible account of the incident. His research is credible and well-documented. The news source is considered credible by experts.

english_meaning: In a way that can be believed or trusted. Convincingly and in a manner that seems reasonable and reliable. With enough evidence or authority to be accepted as true. In a way that inspires confidence in one's ability or claims.
example_sentence: The witness spoke credibly about what she had seen. He argued credibly that the plan would save money. The report is credibly sourced and well documented. Only a few teams can credibly challenge for the title.

english_meaning: Praise, recognition, or approval given to someone for something good they have done. An arrangement that allows a customer to buy goods or services and pay for them later. Money available in a bank account or added to an account. Trust or confidence in someone's honesty, ability, or truthfulness. A unit of study completed successfully at a school, college, or university. To add money to an account or to believe that something is true.
example_sentence: She deserves credit for finishing the project on time. We bought the furniture on credit and paid it off monthly. The bank credited five thousand rupees to my account. He needs three more credits to complete his degree.

english_meaning: Having or showing too great a readiness to believe things. Easily convinced that something is true or real. Trusting too readily without sufficient evidence. Gullible and easily deceived by false statements or promises.
example_sentence: The credulous old man was tricked into giving away his savings. Young children are often credulous and believe whatever they are told. He is too credulous to deal with cunning businessmen. Credulous investors lost their money in the fake scheme. She gave a credulous nod to every story he told her.

english_meaning: A set of beliefs, principles, or guiding ideas. A formal statement of religious faith. A philosophy or code by which a person or group lives.
example_sentence: Freedom was the central creed of the movement. The church recited its creed every Sunday. His personal creed was to work hard and treat people fairly. People of every creed were welcome at the event. The party's creed changed over time.

english_meaning: A small stream or narrow watercourse. A narrow inlet of the sea or a tidal channel. A minor branch of a river, especially in American usage. A small harbour or landing place on a coast.
example_sentence: The children spent the afternoon splashing in the creek. A narrow creek runs behind the old fishing village. Their boat was tied up in a sheltered creek. Heavy rain turned the quiet creek into a rushing torrent.

english_meaning: To move slowly and quietly, often in a sneaky or careful way. To move forward slowly, quietly, or carefully, often to avoid being noticed. A person who behaves in an unpleasant, suspicious, or socially uncomfortable way.
example_sentence: The cat crept quietly toward the bird. Fog began to creep over the hills. Fear crept into his mind during the night. She felt uncomfortable because a stranger was creeping behind her.

english_meaning: To approach quietly or slowly. To move toward someone or something without being noticed, or for a situation or feeling to develop gradually so that people do not realize it until it is already happening
example_sentence: The cat crept up on the bird without making a sound. Fear crept up on him as the room grew darker. Old age can creep up on you faster than expected. She did not notice the deadline creeping up on her.

english_meaning: To reduce (a dead body) to mostly tiny bits of bones resembling ash through exposure to flame and intense heat followed by pulverization of bone fragments. To burn a dead body, especially as part of a funeral ceremony.
example_sentence: When she dies she wants to be cremated, not buried.

english_meaning: The process of reducing a dead body to mostly tiny bits of bone resembling ash that involves exposing the body to flame and intense heat followed by pulverization of bone fragments.
example_sentence: More people are choosing cremation rather than burial. The body was sent for cremation.

english_meaning: A crackling or rattling sound. In medicine, the crackling noise heard in the lungs or produced by broken bone ends rubbing together. The act of making a series of short sharp sounds.
example_sentence: The doctor heard crepitation in the patient's chest. Crepitation at the joint suggested a fracture. Fine crepitation was noted at the base of both lungs. The crepitation of dry leaves filled the quiet path.

english_meaning: Very sad disappointed or depressed, With drooping crest or bowed head, Dispirited and depressed, dejected
example_sentence: His crestfallen look should have been a victory, but instead she wished she could eat the words. She was crestfallen when she found out she hadn't got the job.

english_meaning: A group of people who work together to operate a ship, aircraft, vehicle, or to perform a specific task. A team of workers who share responsibilities in a common job. It is commonly used for people working on ships, airplanes, film sets, rescue operations, or sports teams. Each member has a specific role, and together they complete the work efficiently. To work as part of a group.
example_sentence: The ship’s crew worked hard during the storm. The flight crew prepared the passengers for landing. A film crew arrived early to set up the equipment. The rescue crew saved many people during the flood.

english_meaning: To copy or plagiarize. To take someone else’s work or ideas and use them as your own, especially in schoolwork or exams. A small bed, usually with high sides, designed to prevent an infant or young child from falling out while sleeping. It can also mean a place of residence informally or a place for copying work (cheating).
example_sentence: He cribbed the answers from his neighbor. Students are warned not to crib homework. She cribbed lines from the famous poem. The baby slept peacefully in the crib. She decorated the crib with colorful blankets. He stayed at his friend's crib for the weekend.

english_meaning: A small jumping insect that produces a chirping sound by rubbing its wings together. An outdoor game played by two teams of eleven players with a bat and ball. Fair and honourable behaviour, in informal British usage.
example_sentence: A cricket chirped somewhere in the garden. The boys played cricket until sunset. Pakistan won the cricket match by six wickets. Cheating in a friendly game is simply not cricket.

english_meaning: A person who commits a crime. A person convicted of an offense. Relating to crime or the legal punishment of crime. Wicked, disgraceful, or shockingly negligent. Extremely bad or unacceptable in informal usage.
example_sentence: The police arrested the suspected criminal. She specializes in criminal law. The court opened a criminal investigation. It was criminal to leave the children without food.

english_meaning: Behavior that is illegal or connected with crime. The quality or state of being criminal. The amount or pattern of criminal activity in a place or group. Moral wickedness or serious wrongdoing in broader usage.
example_sentence: The study examined the causes of youth criminality. Poverty alone does not explain criminality. Investigators found no evidence of criminality in the transaction. The novel explores guilt, punishment, and criminality.

english_meaning: The act or process of making an activity illegal and punishable as a crime. The legal classification of conduct as criminal. The process of treating people or groups as criminals. The expansion of criminal-law control into a social issue.
example_sentence: The criminalization of peaceful protest drew strong criticism. Researchers studied the criminalization of homelessness. New legislation led to the criminalization of online harassment. The debate concerns criminalization rather than prevention.

english_meaning: To make an action illegal by law. To define or treat particular conduct as a criminal offense. To subject a person or group to criminal penalties for specified behavior. To portray or treat someone as a criminal, sometimes unfairly.
example_sentence: The new law would criminalize the sale of fake medicines. Critics say the policy may criminalize poverty. Many countries have moved to criminalize cyberstalking. We should not criminalize people for seeking help.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to or constitutes a crime. In violation of criminal law. In a manner deserving criminal punishment. Shockingly, disgracefully, or extremely badly in informal usage.
example_sentence: The company was found criminally responsible for the accident. He was criminally charged with fraud. The building had been criminally neglected. It is criminally wasteful to destroy usable food.

english_meaning: Relating to criminology or the scientific study of crime. Concerned with criminal behavior, its causes, patterns, prevention, or social effects. Based on theories or methods used by criminologists.
example_sentence: The report offers a criminological analysis of gang violence. Researchers collected criminological data from several cities. Her argument is supported by criminological evidence. The journal publishes criminological research from around the world.

english_meaning: A specialist who scientifically studies crime and criminal behavior. A researcher who examines why crimes occur and how they may be prevented. An expert who analyzes offenders, victims, punishment, and justice systems.
example_sentence: The criminologist interviewed prisoners for the study. A leading criminologist discussed the rise in cybercrime. The police consulted a criminologist about repeat offending. She works as a criminologist at a research institute.

english_meaning: The scientific study of crime, criminals, and criminal behavior. The study of the causes, patterns, prevention, and social effects of crime. The academic field examining law enforcement, punishment, victims, and justice systems.
example_sentence: She earned a degree in criminology. Modern criminology draws on sociology and psychology. The course examines major theories of criminology. Criminology can help shape effective crime-prevention policies.

english_meaning: To press or pinch something into small folds or ridges. To make hair wavy by pressing or heating it. To join or secure material by squeezing a metal fitting around it. To restrict, weaken, or obstruct something. A small fold, ridge, wave, or compressed fastening. A restriction or obstacle.
example_sentence: Use the tool to crimp the wire connector firmly. She crimped the edges of the pastry with a fork. Higher costs may crimp the company’s growth. The stylist added a soft crimp to her hair.

english_meaning: A trademark for a durable, crease-resistant polyester fabric. A textured synthetic cloth widely used for clothing in the 1960s and 1970s. A garment made from this type of fabric.
example_sentence: Her grandmother still owns a Crimplene dress from the 1970s. Crimplene became popular because it was easy to care for. The vintage shop sold several Crimplene skirts. He remembered his mother sewing dresses from Crimplene fabric.

english_meaning: A deep, rich red color. A dark red shade with a slightly purplish tone. To turn red, as from embarrassment or anger. Having a deep red color.
example_sentence: The sky turned crimson as the sun set. Her face crimsoned with embarrassment. He wore a crimson tie to the formal dinner. Crimson roses bloomed along the garden wall.

english_meaning: To physically move back or shrink due to fear or pain. To feel embarrassed or awkward because of someone’s actions. To react with discomfort to something unpleasant or awkward. A feeling of embarrassment or awkwardness
example_sentence: She cringed when she heard the loud noise. I cringe every time I watch that awkward scene. He cringed at his own mistake during the presentation. That joke gave everyone a cringe feeling.

english_meaning: To severely damage something so that it cannot function normally or becomes very weak. A person who has a serious physical disability that limits movement or ability to walk. It can refer to a person, system, economy, organization, or machine. In modern usage this word can be considered offensive, so people usually say “person with a disability”.
example_sentence: He was crippled by polio as a child. She's eighty and crippled with arthritis. The industry has been financially crippled by these policies. Sugar producers have been crippled by plummeting prices. The pilot tried to land his crippled plane. The accident crippled him.

english_meaning: The plural form of criterion. The standards or principles used together to judge or decide something. A set of requirements that must be satisfied.
example_sentence: Candidates must meet all the criteria listed below. The criteria for the award were changed this year. These criteria are applied to every application equally. Our selection criteria include experience and language skills.

english_meaning: A standard or principle by which something is judged or decided. A rule used to measure quality, suitability or success. A single requirement that must be met.
example_sentence: Price is not the only criterion for choosing a school. The main criterion is relevant work experience. Each application is judged against a single clear criterion. Honesty was the chief criterion for selection.

english_meaning: A type of bicycle race held on a short circuit, usually through city streets. A fast, multi-lap cycling race around a closed course.A criterium is a standard, rule, or principle used to judge or evaluate something. A specific standard or condition that is used to decide whether something meets a particular requirement or is considered acceptable, suitable, successful, or good. It is used when making judgments, comparisons, or evaluations.
example_sentence: He won the criterium after a dramatic final sprint. The city center was closed to traffic for the annual criterium. Dozens of riders competed in the evening criterium. She trained hard all winter to prepare for the criterium season. Cost is an important criterium when choosing a new computer.

english_meaning: A person who judges, evaluates, or gives opinions about something, especially pointing out strengths and weaknesses. A person who expresses opinions about books, movies, art, music, or performances. Someone who finds faults or points out mistakes. An expert who evaluates quality professionally. A person who analyzes and comments on ideas or actions.
example_sentence: The film critic praised the acting. He is a harsh critic of government policies. Every artist needs a thoughtful critic. She worked as a food critic for a magazine.

english_meaning: Expressing careful judgment or disapproval. Extremely important or decisive. At a dangerous or unstable stage. Relating to detailed analysis and evaluation. Inclined to find faults.
example_sentence: The report was critical of the new regulations. Clean water is critical to public health. The injured driver remains in critical condition. Students must develop critical thinking skills.

english_meaning: In a way that expresses analysis or disapproval. To an extremely important degree. In a dangerously serious condition. Using careful and objective judgment.
example_sentence: The editor examined the article critically. Reliable transport is critically important to the village. Two passengers were critically injured. We should think critically about information found online.

english_meaning: The act of judging, analyzing, or pointing out faults. A remark that expresses disapproval. Careful evaluation of art, literature, ideas, or behavior.
example_sentence: The manager accepted the criticism calmly. Constructive criticism can improve your writing. The film received harsh criticism from reviewers. She offered criticism without insulting anyone. Public criticism forced the company to change its policy.

english_meaning: To point out faults or weaknesses. To judge or evaluate something, often negatively. To express disapproval of a person, action, idea, or work.
example_sentence: It is easy to criticize a plan after it fails. Please criticize the essay honestly but kindly. The newspaper criticized the new tax law. He did not criticize her in front of the team. Good teachers criticize work, not the student's worth.

english_meaning: A detailed analysis, assessment, or evaluation of something such as a piece of writing, art, or performance. To examine or judge something carefully and give a detailed opinion about its merits or faults. A careful review that discusses both strengths and weaknesses.
example_sentence: The professor asked the students to critique the research article in class. Her critique of the film focused on its storytelling and acting. The editor carefully critiqued the writer’s draft to improve its clarity. A constructive critique helps people improve their work.

english_meaning: A display of sorrow that is not genuine. It is used when someone pretends to be sad or regretful, but their emotions are not real. The person may cry or act upset to gain sympathy, avoid blame, or manipulate others. Fake or insincere tears that show false sadness.
example_sentence: He shed crocodile tears when he was caught cheating. The politician showed crocodile tears after the scandal was exposed. She cried crocodile tears to avoid punishment. His apology sounded like crocodile tears rather than real regret.

english_meaning: A light crescent-shaped pastry made from layered buttery dough. A flaky French-style breakfast bread or baked item.
example_sentence: She ordered a croissant and black coffee. The bakery makes fresh croissants every morning. He spread jam on a warm croissant. A good croissant should be flaky outside and soft inside. We shared a chocolate croissant at the cafe.

english_meaning: A very close friend, often used for someone who gains unfair advantage through friendship, especially in business or politics. A long time close companion or trusted friend. A person who benefits from favoritism because of personal relationship. Someone in a powerful person's inner circle. A friend involved in improper or unfair support.
example_sentence: The minister appointed his cronies to important positions. He spent the evening laughing with his old crony from school. The company hired the owner's cronies instead of qualified candidates. She avoided business deals that involved political cronies.

english_meaning: The practice of giving jobs, favors, contracts, or advantages to friends and close associates rather than choosing people fairly by merit.
example_sentence: Cronyism weakened public trust in the department. The contract was criticized as an example of cronyism. A fair hiring system reduces cronyism. Voters were angry about cronyism in local government. Cronyism can keep talented people out of important jobs.

english_meaning: To bend something or form a curve. A dishonest person or criminal. A bend or curve. A hooked staff used by shepherds. A sharp turn in a road or river.
example_sentence: That salesman is a real crook. The film portrays a world of small-time crooks, petty crime and drinking clubs. The police finally caught the crook. There is a crook in the river ahead. The shepherd carried a crook. He crooked his finger to call me.

english_meaning: Not straight, bent, or twisted out of shape. Dishonest or unfair in behavior. Irregular or not properly aligned. Suspicious or not trustworthy. Not straight in line. Corrupt in actions. Distorted shape. Suspicious behavior.
example_sentence: The old tree had a crooked trunk. He gave me a crooked smile. The picture is hanging crooked on the wall. They were involved in crooked business deals. The road becomes crooked after the bridge. His crooked handwriting is hard to read. Please stop asking crooked question.

english_meaning: A plant or plant product grown and harvested in large quantities, especially for food. The total yield of such plants in a season. A group of people or things appearing at the same time. A very short haircut. A pouch in a bird's throat where food is stored. To cut something short or trim its edges. To remove unwanted parts of a photograph.
example_sentence: Wheat is the main crop in this region. Heavy rain destroyed most of this year's crop. She cropped the photo to remove the background. This year's crop of graduates is exceptionally talented.

english_meaning: To remove part of an image by cutting away its edges. To leave someone or something out of a picture. To appear or show on the surface, as rock or soil. To come up or arise unexpectedly.
example_sentence: She cropped out her ex-boyfriend from the holiday photos. Please crop out the messy background before posting. Layers of granite crop out along the hillside. New problems kept cropping out during the project.

english_meaning: To appear or happen suddenly or unexpectedly. To emerge suddenly or become noticeable. To occur or present itself as an issue or topic
example_sentence: New problems often crop up during software development Unexpected guests cropped up at the party Questions about the project cropped up during the meeting Errors cropped up when we tested the new system

english_meaning: A small roll made of minced meat, fish, vegetables, or potatoes that is coated in breadcrumbs and fried. A small cylindrical or oval shaped food item prepared from mashed potatoes, minced meat, fish, cheese, or vegetables. The mixture is shaped, coated with breadcrumbs, and then deep fried or baked until crisp on the outside and soft inside.
example_sentence: She served chicken croquettes at the dinner party. The potato croquette was crispy on the outside and soft inside. He ordered fish croquettes as an appetizer. The chef prepared vegetable croquettes for the guests.

english_meaning: To meet someone by chance. To encounter a person unexpectedly. To have one's life intersect briefly with another's. To come across someone during a journey or period. To meet again after some time.
example_sentence: I hope we cross paths with each other again someday. She crossed paths with an old friend at the airport. Our paths crossed at the conference last year. If you ever cross paths with him, say hello from me.

english_meaning: To argue or fight with someone, especially in a formal or verbal way. To engage in a verbal battle. To strongly oppose someone’s opinion. To take part in a heated discussion or debate. To confront someone intellectually or politically.
example_sentence: The two politicians crossed swords during the debate on education policy. She often crosses swords with her manager about work decisions. The lawyers crossed swords in the courtroom over the evidence. We crossed swords over the best way to solve the problem.

word: Cross that bridge when you come to it
english_meaning: To deal with a problem only when it actually arises. To postpone worrying about a possible difficulty until it truly happens. Used to advise someone not to worry about future problems in advance. A phrase encouraging patience and focus on present matters. To handle a situation as it comes, rather than anticipating trouble.
synonyms: ["Deal with it later","Handle it when it happens","Face it in time","Wait and see","Take one step at a time","Postpone worry","Address later"]
example_sentence: Don't worry about the interview now; we'll cross that bridge when we come to it. If the payment gets delayed, we'll cross that bridge when we come to it. She refused to plan for problems that might never happen and said they'd cross that bridge when they came to it. Let's finish today's work first and cross that bridge when we come to it.

english_meaning: To make a final decision that cannot be changed and leads to important consequences. To take a decisive step after which there is no turning back. It describes a moment when someone commits to a risky or significant action knowing the outcome will permanently change the situation. It often involves courage, uncertainty, or accepting consequences. This idiom is commonly used in professional, business, and personal decision contexts where commitment is final and impactful.
synonyms: ["Pass the point of no return","Take the plunge","Make a bold decision","Commit fully","Burn one's boats","Take a decisive step"]
example_sentence: After investing all his savings in the startup, he crossed the Rubicon. When she resigned from her job, she knew she had crossed the Rubicon. The company crossed the Rubicon by entering the international market. Once the agreement was signed, both sides had crossed the Rubicon.

english_meaning: Misunderstand each other or confuse communication. When two or more people misunderstand each other due to unclear communication. When messages, instructions, or ideas get mixed up. When people act based on different assumptions and cause confusion. A polite way to admit confusion without blaming anyone. Used when instructions were unclear or interpreted differently. Indicates crossed communication lines.
example_sentence: We must have crossed wires somewhere because I thought the meeting was tomorrow. They crossed wires during the discussion and ended up arguing about nothing. I think we crossed wires when planning the event; I booked the wrong date. The teacher and students crossed wires about the homework deadline. I think we crossed wires about the meeting location.

english_meaning: Produced by breeding two different breeds, varieties, or species. Of mixed breed or mixed parentage.
example_sentence: The farm raises crossbred cattle for better milk production. A crossbred dog may inherit traits from both parents. Scientists studied the crossbred plants in the greenhouse. The crossbred sheep were strong and healthy. Crossbred varieties can be useful in agriculture.

english_meaning: A pair of fine wires crossing in the focus of an optical instrument, used as a sighting device.
example_sentence: He centered the target in the crosshairs of his scope. The surveyor used the crosshairs to align the instrument. The pilot adjusted the display so the crosshairs were visible. Looking through the lens, the crosshairs appeared sharp against the sky.

english_meaning: The part of the human body where the legs join the torso, often referred to as the groin area. The section of a garment, such as pants or shorts, that covers this specific area. A place where something divides or forks into two parts, especially the angle formed by the parting of two branches of a tree.
example_sentence: The attacker dropped to the ground after receiving a sharp kick to the crotch. A squirrel was seen resting peacefully in the crotch of the large oak tree. My favorite pair of jeans is completely worn out and torn at the crotch. He awkwardly held the heavy package in the crotch of his arm while unlocking the door.

english_meaning: A musical note equal to one beat in common time, also called a quarter note. A strange or unreasonable idea or belief held by a person. A whim, fancy, or odd notion. A small hook or hook-shaped tool or instrument.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the students to clap on every crotchet. A crotchet lasts twice as long as a quaver. He is a good man, despite his odd crotchets. The old craftsman used a fine crotchet to shape the metal.

english_meaning: Easily annoyed and often complaining, especially about small things. Bad-tempered, irritable, or difficult to please. Having odd or stubborn opinions and habits. Often used to describe an older person who becomes grumpy.
example_sentence: The crotchety old man complained about the noise every evening. She becomes crotchety when she does not sleep well. He is a kind person, though a little crotchety at times. Their crotchety neighbour rarely spoke to anyone.

english_meaning: Having no fabric in the crotch area, used to describe certain garments. Designed with an open section between the legs. A term commonly used for particular styles of underwear or clothing. Lacking the piece of material that normally covers the crotch.
example_sentence: The shop sells both regular and crotchless designs. Crotchless garments are made for specific purposes. She found the crotchless style uncomfortable. The catalogue listed the item as crotchless underwear.

english_meaning: To lower the body close to the ground by bending the knees and leaning forward. To stoop or bend down, especially in order to hide or to be ready to move. To adopt a low, defensive, or fearful posture. A position in which the body is bent low with the knees drawn up.
example_sentence: The cat began to crouch before jumping on the bird. He had to crouch to enter the low doorway. The soldiers crouched behind the wall for safety. She waited in a crouch, ready to start the race.

english_meaning: To bend the body low above something, usually while paying close attention to it. To lean forward and downward over an object or person. To hunch over a task, such as a book, a screen, or a fire. To position oneself protectively above someone or something.
example_sentence: He would crouch over his desk for hours while studying. The travellers crouched over the fire to keep warm. She crouched over the injured bird to protect it. Do not crouch over your phone for so long.

english_meaning: Bent low with the knees drawn up and the body close to the ground. Having taken a low position, often to hide or to prepare for action. Past tense and past participle of the verb crouch. Describing a posture that appears tense, ready, or defensive.
example_sentence: He stayed crouched behind the bushes until the danger passed. The crouched figure in the corner turned out to be a child. She crouched down to tie her shoelaces. The tiger remained crouched, watching its prey.

english_meaning: A childhood illness of the throat and windpipe that causes a harsh, barking cough. An infection that makes breathing noisy and difficult, especially in young children. The rump or hindquarters of a horse or similar animal. The rounded part of an animal's back just above the hind legs.
example_sentence: The child was admitted to hospital with severe croup. Croup usually improves within a few days. The rider patted the croup of his horse. A horse's croup lies between its back and its tail.

english_meaning: A person employed at a casino to run a gaming table. An attendant who collects and pays out money during a game of chance. The staff member who deals cards or spins the roulette wheel. A person responsible for managing bets and enforcing the rules of a game.
example_sentence: The croupier dealt the cards to each player. A croupier must be quick with numbers. The croupier announced the winning number. He worked as a croupier for several years.

english_meaning: A small piece of toasted or fried bread served with soup or salad. A crisp bread cube used as a garnish in food. A snack-like topping made by baking or frying seasoned bread. A small crunchy bread piece added for texture and flavour.
example_sentence: She sprinkled croutons over the tomato soup. The salad was topped with garlic croutons. He makes croutons at home from leftover bread. A few croutons add a nice crunch to the dish.

english_meaning: A large number of people gathered together in a disorganized or unruly way. A group of people who are linked by a common interest or activity. The mass or multitude of people in general. To fill a space almost completely leaving little or no room for movement. To move too close to someone so that they feel uncomfortable.
example_sentence: A large crowd gathered outside the stadium to buy tickets. He prefers to stand out rather than blend in with the crowd. The fans started to crowd around the famous actor for autographs. Too many thoughts began to crowd her mind at once.

english_meaning: Forming the most successful, important, or final part of something. Supreme. Highest. Topmost. The act of placing a crown on a new king or queen. Used to describe an achievement, moment, or event that represents the peak or finest example of a series of things.
example_sentence: Winning the gold medal was the crowning achievement of his career. The crowning ceremony of the new king was attended by world leaders. The beautiful garden is the crowning glory of the old palace. Her latest novel is considered the crowning work of her life. The fireworks were the crowning moment of the entire festival.

english_meaning: Extremely important or necessary. Something that is very important because it has a strong effect on the result of a situation. Critical, essential for success. Decisive at an important moment. Of great significance
example_sentence: Education plays a crucial role in personal development. It is crucial to save your work before closing the program. The final match was crucial for the team's success. Good communication is crucial in any relationship.

english_meaning: Shaped like or arranged in the form of a cross. Cross-shaped. In anatomy, especially referring to two important ligaments in the knee that cross each other and provide stability to the joint. A medical and biological term used to describe structures that have a crossing or cross-like arrangement, most commonly the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments of the knee.
example_sentence: The footballer tore his anterior cruciate ligament during yesterday's match and will need surgery. The cruciate ligaments play a key role in keeping the knee joint stable during movement. The leaves of this plant grow in a cruciate pattern around the stem. Cruciate injuries are common among athletes who play sports involving sudden direction changes. The surgeon explained how the cruciate structures inside the knee work together.

english_meaning: A cross with a figure of Jesus on it, used as a symbol of Christianity.  An image or representation of the cross with the body of Jesus Christ affixed, symbolizing his crucifixion. It is often used in Christian worship, prayer, and as a reminder of Christ’s sacrifice.
example_sentence: The priest held the crucifix during the ceremony. She wore a small crucifix around her neck. The old church had a golden crucifix on the altar. He touched the crucifix for comfort during the storm.

english_meaning: Execution by nailing or binding someone to a cross. The act of putting a person to death by nailing or binding them to a cross or similar structure. Historically, it was used as a form of capital punishment, most famously for Jesus Christ. It can also metaphorically describe extreme suffering or severe criticism.
example_sentence: They watched the crucifixion from a distance. He was executed by crucifixion. The crucifixion of Jesus is central to Christian belief. The prisoner faced crucifixion for his rebellion. The novel described the character’s emotional crucifixion after betrayal. Historical accounts show that crucifixion was a common Roman punishment.

english_meaning: Shaped like a cross. Having the form of a cross with arms at right angles. Arranged in the shape of a cross. Relating to a cross-shaped design or structure.
example_sentence: The cathedral was built in a cruciform shape. The ancient church had a cruciform floor plan. The flowers of the mustard plant are cruciform. The medal was designed with a cruciform pattern.

english_meaning: To kill somebody as a punishment by fastening them to a wooden cross. To criticize or punish somebody very severely.
example_sentence: The prime minister was crucified in the press for his handling of the affair. He's going to crucify me when he finds out what I've done!. She'll crucify me if she finds you still here. Crucify my love. If my love is blind.

english_meaning: In a natural, raw, or unrefined state. Rough, simple, or not carefully made. Rude, offensive, or lacking good manners. It can also refer to petroleum before refining.
example_sentence: The factory processes crude oil. His drawing was crude but easy to understand. She disliked his crude jokes. The shelter was built with crude wooden boards. Early estimates are often crude and later become more accurate.

english_meaning: To negatively affect an opportunity or a chance of success. Having a desire to cause physical or mental pain and make somebody suffer. Causing physical or mental pain and making somebody suffer.
example_sentence: He cruelled his interview by arriving late and being completely unprepared. A back injury cruelled her chances in the final. He was known to be a cruel dictator. Her eyes were cruel and hard. It was a cruel irony that he, being gravely ill, would survive his family would be a cruel twist of fate if he escaped only to starve to death once outside. Her father's death was a cruel blow.

english_meaning: Painful behavior. A cruel action. Something that happens that seems unfair. Disposition to willfully inflict pain and suffering on others. Behavior that causes physical or mental pain to others and makes them suffer, especially deliberately.
example_sentence: He has treated her with extreme cruelty. We can’t  stand cruelty to animals. The deliberate cruelty of his words cut her like a knife.

english_meaning: To travel by ship for pleasure. To move smoothly at a steady speed. To drive, sail, or fly around without hurry. Informally, to win or progress easily.
example_sentence: They went on a cruise around the Mediterranean. The car can cruise comfortably at highway speed. We cruised through the old town after dinner. The team cruised to victory in the final match. A cruise ship arrived in the harbor at sunrise.

english_meaning: To break food into crumbs or scatter small bits. A very small piece of bread, cake, or food. A tiny fragment of bread, biscuit, or cake that breaks off easily. Any small piece or particle of something. Informal use: a small amount or bit of something.
example_sentence: There were crumbs all over the table after breakfast. He brushed the crumbs off his shirt. She gave the birds some crumbs of bread. The cookie crumbled into fine crumbs in his hand.

english_meaning: To break into small pieces. To break or fall apart into small fragments, often due to pressure, age, or weakness. It can also describe a gradual failure of something such as a system, relationship, or confidence. A type of dessert made with fruit covered by a mixture of flour, butter, and sugar baked until crisp. It also means small fragments of something that has broken apart.
example_sentence: The dry bread started to crumble in his hands. Her confidence began to crumble after repeated failures. The ancient wall is slowly crumbling due to weather. The plan crumbled when key members left the team. She baked a delicious apple crumble for dessert. The crumble on top was golden and crunchy. He brushed the crumbles off the table.

english_meaning: To crush together or press into wrinkles. To become creased or violently wrinkled. To collapse or fall down from weakness or exhaustion. To suddenly lose energy and give way completely.
