example_sentence: She watched him crumple the letter and throw it into the fire. The front of the car started to crumple upon impact with the wall. He felt like he would crumple to the floor from sheer exhaustion. Be careful not to crumple your fresh new shirt before the interview.

english_meaning: Crushed or pressed out of shape so that it is full of irregular creases and folds. Wrinkled and untidy, especially of clothes or paper. Collapsed suddenly, as a person falling to the ground. Looking tired, worn, or disheveled. Bent or twisted out of shape after an impact.
example_sentence: He pulled a crumpled receipt from his pocket. Her dress looked crumpled after the long journey. The car's bonnet was crumpled in the accident. He lay crumpled on the floor after fainting.

english_meaning: To crush or chew something with a loud, hard sound. To make or hear a sharp crushing sound. A difficult situation caused by a shortage of time, money, or resources. A decisive period when pressure is greatest. To process large amounts of numerical data.
example_sentence: She crunched an apple during the break. Gravel crunched beneath our boots. The company faces a serious cash crunch. The analysts crunched the numbers before presenting their forecast.

english_meaning: To bite hard on something with a loud crushing sound. To chew firmly on something crisp or hard. To press down heavily on something so that it breaks or crackles. To deal strictly or forcefully with a problem or behavior.
example_sentence: He crunched down on a piece of ice and winced. The dog crunched down on the bone with obvious delight. Her boots crunched down on the frozen snow. The new manager promised to crunch down on wasteful spending.

english_meaning: To move or walk over something while making a crushing, crackling sound. To eat through something crisp steadily and noisily. To work through a large amount of data, numbers, or tasks quickly and efficiently. To break a path through a brittle surface such as snow or ice.
example_sentence: We crunched through the fallen leaves on our way home. The hikers crunched through the fresh snow at dawn. He crunched through a whole bag of crisps during the film. The computer can crunch through millions of records in seconds.

english_meaning: To crush, squash, or crumple something into a small, compact shape. To break something into small pieces by pressing or biting it noisily. To bend or curl the body tightly, as during an abdominal exercise. To fold something roughly so it becomes creased and compressed.
example_sentence: She crunched up the letter and threw it in the bin. He crunched up the empty can before recycling it. Lie on your back and crunch up slowly to work your stomach muscles. The children crunched up the dry leaves as they walked through the park.

english_meaning: A determined campaign for a cause, reform, belief, or social change. Historically, a medieval religious military expedition. To campaign strongly for something.
example_sentence: She began a crusade against corruption in the schools. The doctor led a public health crusade. Medieval crusades changed the history of Europe and the Middle East. They crusade for cleaner rivers every summer. His crusade for justice inspired many students.

english_meaning: To press, squeeze something so hard that it is damaged, injured. To push something in a small place. To break into pieces. To upset or shock someone badly. To use violent methods to defeat people who are opposing you.
example_sentence: I have a crush on a fellow teacher when I asked to marry me. The car was completely crushed under the truck. The army was sent in to crush the rebellion.

english_meaning: To press something down with great force until it breaks or flattens. To suppress or put an end to opposition or feelings.
example_sentence: The machine crushes down the cans for recycling. He crushed down the rubbish to make space. The regime crushed down every protest. She crushed down her fear and spoke.

english_meaning: To extinguish something, especially a cigarette, by pressing it firmly. To suppress or stamp out something completely, such as resistance or hope.
example_sentence: He crushed out his cigarette on the pavement. She crushed out the flame with her boot. The new law crushed out all dissent. Years of failure crushed out his last hope.

english_meaning: To break something into very small pieces or powder by pressing or pounding.
example_sentence: Crush up the tablet and mix it with water. He crushed up the biscuits for the cheesecake base. Crush up the ice before adding the juice. The pharmacist warned against crushing up the capsule.

english_meaning: Causing severe damage, defeat or disappointment. Extremely heavy or overwhelming in pressure or effect. The act or process of pressing something with great force.
example_sentence: The team suffered a crushing defeat at home. She felt a crushing sense of disappointment. Crushing debt forced the family to move. The plant handles the crushing of limestone.

english_meaning: In a way that is overwhelming or severely disappointing. To a devastating degree.
example_sentence: The proposal was crushingly rejected by the members. He was crushingly honest about her chances. The exam turned out to be crushingly difficult. She lost crushingly in the final round.

english_meaning: To form a hard layer, to cover something with a hard layer. The outer layer of rock that forms the surface of the earth or another planet. The hard outer surface of bread. A layer of pastry, especially on top of a pie. A hard layer or surface, especially above or around something soft or liquid.
example_sentence: Water was beginning to crust over with ice as temperatures dropped. Once the blisters have crusted over, the disease is not likely to spread. Dirt crusted her cheek. We saved a few crusts of bread for the birds. Bake until the crust is golden.

english_meaning: A support used under the arm to help a person walk. Anything relied on too heavily for support, confidence, or comfort.
example_sentence: He used a crutch after breaking his leg. The injured player walked with two crutches. Some people use humor as an emotional crutch. Do not let the calculator become a crutch for basic math. The old wall needed a wooden crutch to stay upright.

english_meaning: The most important or difficult part of a problem or an issue. The most important or serious part of a matter, problem, or argument. The central part or aspect of something under consideration.
example_sentence: The crux of the country's economic problems is its foreign debt. The issue of an arms embargo will be at the crux of the negotiations in Geneva. The crux of the matter is how do we prevent a flood occurring again? Now we come to the crux of the problem.

english_meaning: To ask for something that is impossible or unattainable.
example_sentence: Wanting perfection is crying for the moon. She wants a luxury car and a mansion on her first salary, she’s crying for the moon. Asking him to finish this project in one day is like crying for the moon. He keeps applying for top positions without experience; it’s like crying for the moon. Expecting perfect weather for the picnic is crying for the moon.

english_meaning: A sarcastic phrase telling someone that you do not feel sorry for their complaints. Used to mock someone who is complaining or self-pitying. Meaning that someone's troubles do not deserve sympathy.
synonyms: ["Boo Hoo","Tough Luck","Get Over It","Poor You","Who Cares"]
example_sentence: You lost a bit of money at the casino? Cry me a river. He complained about his huge bonus being late, and she said, 'Cry me a river'. When the rich kid moaned about his old car, his friends told him to cry me a river. Oh, you have to work one Saturday? Cry me a river.

english_meaning: To be upset about something that cannot be undone. Wasting time in regret instead of moving forward.
example_sentence: Don’t cry over spilt milk; move on. It was a mistake to miss the train, but there’s no use crying over spilt milk. He failed the exam, yet instead of crying over spilt milk, he started preparing harder for the next one. We lost the match yesterday, but crying over spilt milk won’t change the result. She broke her phone last night, but her father told her not to cry over spilt milk and to focus on buying a new one.

english_meaning: To raise a false alarm, to lie about danger, or to ask for help when it is not really needed, so that people stop believing when real danger actually comes.
example_sentence: The boy cried wolf so many times that when he was really in danger, no one came to help. If you keep crying wolf about your health, people won’t take you seriously when you are truly sick. She cried wolf by exaggerating the issue at work, and now no one trusts her reports. Politicians often cry wolf to gain attention, but it weakens public trust over time.

english_meaning: A cold loving microorganism found in ice or frozen water. An organism adapted to life in polar or alpine climates. A bacterium or algae that grows best at very low temperatures.
example_sentence: Scientists discovered a cryophile living inside Antarctic ice. Certain algae act as cryophiles and grow on frozen lakes. The bacterium is a cryophile that survives in extremely cold water. Researchers study cryophiles to understand life in polar ecosystems.

english_meaning: An underground room or vault beneath a church, used as a chapel or burial place. A chamber beneath the floor of a building, especially a church. An underground compartment for burials. A cellar or underground chamber.
example_sentence: The royal family was buried in the cathedral crypt. The ancient crypt contained medieval artifacts. They descended into the cold stone crypt. The crypt served as both chapel and burial chamber.

english_meaning: With a meaning that is hidden or not easily understood. With difficult clues that involve a kind of word puzzle. Having or seeming to have a hidden or ambiguous meaning. Being beyond one's powers to know, understand, or explain.
example_sentence: He has issued a short, cryptic statement denying the spying charges. I received a cryptic message through the post. Meliponine nests are often fairly cryptic and can be difficult to locate. Manville perused the cryptic message with satisfaction.

english_meaning: Something hidden, secret, or obscure. Can describe secretive practices or encrypted technology. Short for cryptocurrency, digital or virtual money secured by cryptography, for example Bitcoin.
example_sentence: Many investors are interested in crypto for potential high returns. She uses a crypto wallet to store her Bitcoin. The company specializes in crypto security technologies. Some messages on the forum were written in crypto language to avoid detection.

english_meaning: A digital or virtual currency that uses cryptography for security and operates independently of a central authority. A type of digital currency designed to work as a medium of exchange through a computer network, using encryption techniques to regulate the generation of units, verify transactions, and secure the system. Unlike traditional currencies, it is decentralized and not controlled by any government or central bank.
example_sentence: Bitcoin is the most well-known cryptocurrency in the world. She invested in several cryptocurrencies hoping for high returns. Governments are exploring regulations for cryptocurrency trading. Cryptocurrency transactions can be faster than traditional banking transfers.

english_meaning: The science and practice of protecting information by converting it into secret codes so that only authorized people can read or understand it. A branch of computer science and mathematics that focuses on securing communication and data. It uses techniques such as encryption and decryption to keep information private, authentic, and safe from hackers or unauthorized access. It is widely used in banking, messaging apps, military systems, websites, and digital security.
example_sentence: Modern banking systems rely heavily on cryptography to protect customer data. The hacker failed to break the cryptography used in the secure messaging app. Cryptography helps keep online transactions private and secure. Students of computer science often study cryptography and cybersecurity together.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid object with six equal square faces. A regular hexahedron with all edges of equal length. The third power of a number in mathematics. To cut something into small cube-shaped pieces.
example_sentence: A dice is a perfect example of a cube. The cube of 3 is 27. Please cube the potatoes for the soup. The building has a distinctive cube shape.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or having the shape of a cube. Having three dimensions: length, breadth, and thickness. Pertaining to the third power of a quantity or number. Representing a volume equal to a cube whose edge is a specified unit. Relating to a crystal system characterized by three equal axes at right angles. Denoting a mathematical equation in which the highest power of the variable is three. Measured in units of volume.
example_sentence: The container has a capacity of one cubic meter. He solved a complex cubic equation during his math exam. Pyrite crystals often form in a perfect cubic structure. The volume of the box is calculated in cubic inches.

english_meaning: A unit of volume equal to the volume of a cube whose sides are one centimeter long. A common metric measurement used for capacity in clinical and scientific contexts. One thousandth of a liter or one milliliter. A standard measure for engine displacement in small motors. A derivative unit of volume in the CGS (centimeter-gram-second) system. The amount of liquid or gas required to fill a cubic space measuring one centimeter on each edge.
synonyms: ["Milliliter","mL","cc","Cubic cm","0.001 Liters","10^-6 Cubic Meters","One Thousandth Litre","Small Volume Unit","Metric Unit of Capacity","Displacement Unit","Cm3","Volumetric Measure"]
example_sentence: The doctor administered ten cubic centimeters of the saline solution to the patient. The small motorcycle engine has a displacement of 125 cubic centimeters. Please calculate the total volume of the container in cubic centimeters. One cubic centimeter of pure water weighs exactly one gram at standard temperature.

english_meaning: A unit of volume in the International System of Units (SI) equal to a cube with sides of one meter in length. The fundamental SI unit used for measuring the volume of three-dimensional spaces or substances. A capacity equivalent to 1,000 liters or approximately 264·17 U·S. liquid gallons. The amount of space occupied by a liquid, solid, or gas that fills a one-meter cube. A derived unit representing length cubed, symbolized as m³. A measurement used in trade and engineering to quantify bulk commodities like concrete, water, or timber.
synonyms: ["Stere","Kiloliter","1000 Liters","M3","Volume Unit","Three-dimensional Unit","Capacity Measure","Bulk Measurement","Spatial Unit","Geometric Cube","Displacement Unit","Quantitative Volume","Metric Volume","Standard Unit"]
antonyms: ["Square Meter","Linear Meter","Milliliter","Point","Zero Volume","Flat Surface","Single Dimension","Two Dimensions","Infinitesimal","Empty Space"]
example_sentence: The construction project required fifty cubic meters of high-quality concrete. You can calculate the pool's volume in cubic meters by multiplying length, width, and depth. Natural gas consumption is often billed based on the number of cubic meters used per month. The shipping container has a total internal capacity of thirty-three cubic meters.

english_meaning: A metric unit of volume equal to a cube whose sides are one millimeter long. One thousandth of a cubic centimeter. A standard unit used in scientific measurements for very small volumes of liquids or solids. Equivalent to 10 to the power of negative nine cubic meters. A measurement frequently used in microscopy and blood cell counts. One microliter in terms of liquid volume capacity. A three-dimensional measure of space occupied by a tiny object.
synonyms: ["Mm³","Cubic Millimetre","Microliter","0.001 Cubic Centimeter","10-9 Cubic Meters","Tiny Volume","Three-dimensional Millimeter","Small Measure","Metric Volume Unit","Volumetric Unit","Capacity Unit","Spatial Unit"]
antonyms: ["Cubic Meter","Cubic Kilometer","Liter","Gallon","Massive Volume","Infinite Space","Cubic Mile","Hectoliter","Megaliter","Large Capacity"]
example_sentence: The scientist calculated the concentration of cells per cubic millimeter. A single cubic millimeter of water is approximately equal to one milligram in mass. The diamond was so small that its volume was less than one cubic millimeter. Modern high-resolution scanners can capture details at the level of a cubic millimeter.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional rectangular solid with six rectangular faces. A box-shaped object with parallel opposite faces. A rectangular prism with all angles being right angles.
example_sentence: A shoebox is a common example of a cuboid. Most rooms are cuboid in shape. The package was a perfect cuboid. Calculate the volume of the cuboid.

english_meaning: A man whose wife is sexually unfaithful to him. To make a husband a cuckold by committing adultery with his wife. The word is old-fashioned and often insulting.
example_sentence: The old play mocks a jealous cuckold. The word cuckold is rarely used in polite modern speech. In the story, rumors made him fear he was a cuckold. Writers once used cuckold as a comic insult. The term carries a harsh and humiliating tone.

english_meaning: A long green vegetable with crisp watery flesh, usually eaten raw. A salad vegetable with thin edible skin and soft seeds. The climbing plant that produces this vegetable. A vegetable often used in salads, raita, and pickles.
example_sentence: He sliced a cucumber for the salad. Cucumber and yogurt make a cooling raita. The cucumber vines need plenty of water. She placed cucumber slices over her eyes to relax.

english_meaning: Food that a cow or similar animal brings back from its stomach to chew again. Partly digested food chewed a second time by ruminant animals. The act or process of such chewing. Figuratively, something reflected on slowly and repeatedly.
example_sentence: The cows lay in the field chewing the cud. Sheep chew the cud for hours after grazing. Farmers know that a healthy animal chews its cud regularly. He sat quietly, chewing the cud over the day's events.

english_meaning: To hold someone close in a loving or comforting way. To hug someone gently and closely to show affection, warmth, care, or comfort. It often involves wrapping arms around a person, child, or animal in a tender and protective manner. The act of holding someone closely with love or warmth.
example_sentence: The mother cuddled her baby to help him sleep. The little girl cuddled her puppy on the sofa. They cuddled together during the cold winter evening. After a long day, the child asked for a cuddle from his father.

english_meaning: A signal, hint, or prompt for action or speech. A stick used in billiards or snooker. A line or action that tells an actor when to speak. To give a signal or prompt.
example_sentence: That was my cue to leave the room. The actor missed his cue on stage. She picked up the cue and took a difficult shot. A nod from the teacher was the cue to begin. The producer cued the music at the right moment.

english_meaning: To strike lightly, usually on the hand or back of neck. To hit someone gently or roughly, often as a warning or playful gesture. Can also mean to handcuff someone. End of a sleeve. The band at the end of a shirt, coat, or sleeve that can be folded back or buttoned.
example_sentence: He rolled up his cuffs before washing his hands. She wore a shirt with embroidered cuffs. The teacher cuffed the student lightly on the shoulder to get his attention. The police cuffed the suspect after the arrest.

english_meaning: A time in colder months when many people look for a romantic partner so they do not feel lonely during winter.
synonyms: ["Winter dating period","Seasonal romance period","Cold weather relationship trend","Winter coupling trend"]
antonyms: ["Single life","Independence in relationships","Avoiding romantic commitment","Staying unattached"]
example_sentence: Many dating apps become more active during cuffing season because people want companionship. She joked that she needed a boyfriend before cuffing season started. Some relationships that begin in cuffing season end when summer arrives. Social media users often talk about cuffing season as a fun cultural trend.

english_meaning: A Latin phrase meaning to whose benefit. Used to ask who gains from a particular action or event. A principle used in law to identify the beneficiary of a crime or act. Questioning who profits from a certain situation. Investigating the motive behind an act by examining who benefits.
synonyms: ["Who benefits","For whose advantage","To whose profit","Beneficiary question"]
example_sentence: In every investigation, we must ask cui bono. Cui bono is a key question in criminal cases. The lawyer applied the principle of cui bono to find the real culprit. Cui bono often reveals hidden motives behind events.

english_meaning: Style or method of cooking, especially from a particular country or region. The distinctive style of cooking and food preparation associated with a particular culture, region, or country. It includes traditional recipes, ingredients, and culinary techniques that characterize that style.
example_sentence: Italian cuisine often uses olive oil and fresh herbs. French cuisine is known for its rich sauces. Street food has become part of modern urban cuisine. She enjoys experimenting with fusion cuisine combining Asian and European flavors.

english_meaning: The scientific study of mosquitoes, including their biology, behavior, and diseases they transmit. A branch of entomology that focuses on the scientific study of mosquitoes, which belong to the family Culicidae. It deals with the identification, classification, structure, development, reproduction, feeding habits, and ecological importance of mosquitoes. It also examines mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and yellow fever, as well as methods of mosquito surveillance, prevention, and control.
example_sentence: Culicdology plays a key role in the fight against malaria. Experts in culicdology tracked the spread of the new mosquito species. The laboratory specializes in culicdology and pest control. Her research in culicdology focused on breeding habits in stagnant water.

english_meaning: Connected with cooking or food. Connected with cooking, especially as a developed skill or art. Of or relating to the kitchen or cookery.
example_sentence: She was keen to acquire more advanced culinary skills. A three course dinner completes the culinary delights. My culinary skills are limited to boiling water (= I am not very good at cooking). Savour the culinary delights of Mexico. She is studying culinary arts. They serve a variety of culinary delights.

english_meaning: To end with a particular result, or at a particular point. To bring to a head or to the highest point. To reach a climax, to come to the decisive point (especially as an end or conclusion).
example_sentence: My arguments with the boss got worse and worse, and finally culminated in my resignation. Their many years of research have finally culminated in a cure for the disease. The meeting culminated in a tearful embrace.

english_meaning: The fact of being responsible and deserving blame for having done something wrong. The fact that someone deserves to be blamed or considered responsible for something bad.
example_sentence: The punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and the degree of culpability of the offender. After the accident, the company refused to accept culpability. The Army denied any culpability, but later compensated owners. Two elements are necessary to prove culpability for a crime. I'm merely suggesting you try to see your own culpability in this. Industrial manufacturers all share culpability for air pollution.

english_meaning: Deserving blame or responsibility for a fault or wrong. Someone or something that is responsible for a mistake, wrongdoing, or offense, implying moral or legal responsibility.
example_sentence: The driver was found culpable for the accident. She was culpable in the company's financial losses. Ignoring safety protocols makes you culpable. The official was held culpable for corruption.

english_meaning: In a way that deserves blame or is blameworthy. When someone acts culpably, they are acting in a manner for which they can be held responsible for a fault or wrongdoing. It implies moral or legal blame.
example_sentence: He acted culpably by ignoring the safety rules. The company was culpably negligent in maintaining equipment. She culpably failed to report the incident on time. The officer was found culpably responsible for the mishandling of the case.

english_meaning: A person who is responsible for a crime or wrongdoing. Someone who has committed a crime, mistake, or harmful act. It can be used for both serious crimes and small everyday faults. Sometimes it also refers to the cause of a problem.
example_sentence: The police finally caught the culprit behind the robbery. He admitted that he was the culprit of the mistake. Smoking is often the main culprit behind lung disease. The real culprit of the problem was poor planning.

english_meaning: To prepare land and grow crops on it. To develop or improve a skill, quality, or relationship through effort. To try to gain someone's friendship or support. To encourage the growth of something such as an idea, habit, or attitude. To refine one's mind, taste, or behavior through learning and practice.
example_sentence: Farmers cultivate wheat and rice in this region. She works hard to cultivate patience in her daily life. He tried to cultivate a friendship with his new neighbor. Teachers cultivate curiosity and creativity in young students.

english_meaning: The act of preparing and using land to grow crops. The process of growing plants. The development, improvement, or refinement of skills, qualities, relationships, or habits.
example_sentence: Rice cultivation requires plenty of water. The cultivation of patience takes time. Farmers improved the cultivation of vegetables with better tools. The garden is under careful cultivation. Good leadership includes the cultivation of trust.

english_meaning: A person who prepares and works on land to grow crops. A farmer who tills and manages agricultural land. A tool or machine used to loosen the soil and remove weeds. A person who develops or improves something over time, such as skills, friendships, or ideas. Someone who encourages growth of qualities, habits, or relationships.
example_sentence: The cultivator ploughed his fields before the monsoon rains. He bought a new cultivator to prepare the land faster. A skilled cultivator can produce healthy crops every season. She is a great cultivator of lasting friendships.

english_meaning: Relating to the ideas, customs, arts, beliefs, and social behavior of a society. Connected with intellectual and artistic activity. Relating to the cultivation of microorganisms, plants, or cells in controlled conditions. Shared by or characteristic of a particular group.
example_sentence: The festival celebrates the region's cultural heritage. Cultural differences can shape how people communicate. The city offers many cultural events throughout the year. Researchers used cultural methods to identify the bacteria.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the customs, beliefs, arts, or social behavior of a society. From the perspective of a particular culture. In terms of intellectual or artistic development. By means of laboratory culture, in scientific contexts.
example_sentence: The gesture is interpreted differently across culturally diverse communities. The program is culturally appropriate for local families. The two regions are culturally connected through music and trade. The sample was culturally identified as a common bacterial strain.

english_meaning: The customs, beliefs, arts, and way of life of a particular people or society. The shared attitudes and behaviour within an organization or group. Achievement in the arts, literature, and intellectual life. The growing of plants or bacteria under controlled conditions. To grow cells or microorganisms in a laboratory.
example_sentence: Sindhi culture is rich in music, poetry, and craft. The company is trying to build a culture of trust. She has a deep interest in art and culture. Scientists cultured the bacteria for further testing.

english_meaning: A person who is excessively or avidly interested in the arts and cultural activities. Someone who aggressively seeks out cultural experiences like art exhibitions, theater plays, and classical concerts. A person who consumes art and literature, sometimes merely to appear sophisticated or elevated in social status.
example_sentence: As a self-proclaimed culture vulture, Sarah spends every weekend visiting art galleries and attending the opera. The city attracts thousands of culture vultures every summer for its world-renowned theater festival. You do not have to be a culture vulture to appreciate the immense historical value of this museum. He became a total culture vulture after moving to London, constantly reading rare books and visiting heritage sites.

english_meaning: With praise, an academic distinction awarded for notably high achievement. A Latin honor generally indicating a strong academic record at graduation.
example_sentence: He graduated cum laude with a degree in history. The university awarded her diploma cum laude. Consistent effort enabled him to finish cum laude. Her résumé notes that she graduated cum laude.

english_meaning: Large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use. Complicated and hard to manage or deal with. Awkward or inefficient to handle. Hard to manage due to size, weight, or complexity.
example_sentence: The organization has promised to eliminate cumbersome and unnecessary bureaucracy. The organization changed its cumbersome title to something easier to remember. He had to carry a cumbersome bag up the stairs. The application process is cumbersome and confusing.

english_meaning: An aromatic seed used as a spice. The plant that produces cumin seeds. A warm earthy spice common in South Asian, Middle Eastern, Mexican, and North African cooking.
example_sentence: Add a teaspoon of cumin to the curry. Cumin gives the soup a warm earthy flavor. She roasted cumin seeds before grinding them. The recipe uses coriander and cumin together. Cumin is common in many traditional dishes.

english_meaning: Something that increases or grows by addition over time or includes everything up to a point. Increasing or becoming greater by gradual addition. It refers to a total that keeps building up over time by adding parts together.
example_sentence: The cumulative effect of lack of sleep can harm your health. The cumulative rainfall this month is higher than average. His cumulative score improved after each test. The company showed cumulative growth over five years.

english_meaning: In a way that increases by successive additions. In a combined or total manner. Gradually building up over time. Considering all previous amounts together.
example_sentence: The projects have cumulatively improved the city's economy. Cumulatively, these small changes make a big difference. His savings grew cumulatively over the years. The team scored cumulatively higher than their rivals.

english_meaning: A type of cloud with a flat base and rounded, fluffy tops, usually seen in fair weather. A heap or accumulation of something. A large white cloud formation seen in the sky during daytime.
example_sentence: Beautiful cumulus clouds filled the summer sky. The pilot flew above the cumulus formations. Children often see shapes in cumulus clouds. A cumulus of documents was piled on the desk.

english_meaning: Tending to delay taking action. Inclined to hesitate before making a decision. Taking longer than necessary to act or proceed. Characterized by postponement or lingering. Slow to make a decision or take action. Prone to using delay as a method or strategy. Describing a person or behavior that unnecessarily puts something off.
example_sentence: His cuncatatious habits annoyed the whole department. A cuncatatious approach may be safe but it wastes time. The manager was too cuncatatious to seize the opportunity. Critics described the response as cuncatatious and weak.

english_meaning: Delay or slowness in acting. The act of putting something off, especially through hesitation. Deliberate postponement used as a tactic or strategy. A tendency to linger or waste time instead of deciding. Procrastination in formal or literary usage.
example_sentence: His cunctation cost the team a valuable opportunity. The general's cunctation was actually a clever military strategy. Endless cunctation in the committee delayed the report for months. She warned that cunctation would only make the problem worse.

english_meaning: A person who delays or puts things off. Someone who uses delay as a deliberate strategy. A title given to the Roman general Fabius Maximus for his delaying tactics. One who hesitates instead of acting quickly. A procrastinator in formal or literary use.
example_sentence: Fabius the Cunctator wore down Hannibal by refusing open battle. His colleagues called him a cunctator because he never met deadlines. A wise cunctator sometimes wins more than a hasty commander. The report was delayed again by our office cunctator.

english_meaning: Causing or involving delay. Tending to postpone action. Of the nature of a delaying tactic. Slow and hesitant in behaviour. Serving to gain time rather than settle a matter.
example_sentence: The lawyer used cunctatory tactics to delay the hearing. A cunctatory reply is often worse than a clear refusal. Their cunctatory strategy exhausted the enemy's supplies. The board's cunctatory attitude frustrated the investors.

english_meaning: The ability to achieve something by tricking or cheating other people in a clever way. Able to get what you want in a clever way, especially by tricking or cheating somebody.
example_sentence: It took energy and cunning just to survive. He was as cunning as a fox. That cunning old rogue is up to something, I'm sure.

english_meaning: In a clever, sly, secretive, or deceitful way. With skillful planning intended to achieve an advantage.
example_sentence: The trap was cunningly hidden under dry leaves. He cunningly avoided a direct answer. The room was cunningly designed to save space. She cunningly turned the argument in her favor. The thief cunningly changed his appearance.

english_meaning: A small open container with a handle, used for drinking tea, coffee, or other liquids. The amount of liquid that such a container holds. A unit of measurement in cooking equal to about two hundred and forty milliliters. A decorated metal vessel given as a prize in a competition. To form the hands into a rounded shape, or to hold something gently in that shape.
example_sentence: She poured me a hot cup of tea. Add one cup of flour to the mixture. The team lifted the cup after winning the final. He cupped his hands to drink water from the stream.

english_meaning: Something that someone likes or prefers. A person’s personal taste, interest, or preference. If something is your "cup of tea," it suits your liking or is enjoyable to you. If it is not your "cup of tea," it means you do not particularly enjoy or like it.
example_sentence: Jazz music is not really my cup of tea, but I can appreciate it. Hiking on mountains is her cup of tea; she does it every weekend. Horror movies are not his cup of tea, so he avoids them. Gardening is my cup of tea; it relaxes me after work.

english_meaning: Extreme greed for wealth, possessions, or gain. Strong selfish desire for money or material advantage.
example_sentence: Cupidity led the official to accept bribes. The novel condemns the cupidity of corrupt merchants. His cupidity destroyed his friendships. A society ruled by cupidity cannot remain fair. She saw through the cupidity behind the generous offer.

english_meaning: Describing a disease or condition that can be remedied or healed by medical treatment. Capable of being corrected or set right. Referring to something that is amenable to a solution or recovery. Possible to overcome or alleviate through specific interventions. Able to be restored to a healthy or sound state.
example_sentence: Modern medicine has ensured that many previously deadly infections are now fully curable. The doctor provided a hopeful prognosis, stating that the tumor was curable through surgery. While the technical glitch was frustrating, the lead engineer assured us it was easily curable. Early detection is vital in ensuring that most skin cancers remain curable.

english_meaning: To carefully selecting, organizing, and presenting content or items, often for public display. A member of the clergy, especially one assisting a parish priest.
example_sentence: She curated a collection of rare photographs for the exhibition. The museum curator carefully curated the historical artifacts. He curated playlists on the music streaming app for different moods. The gallery curator discussed the significance of each painting with visitors.

english_meaning: Having the power or quality of curing or healing a disease or injury. Relating to or used in the treatment of illness. Something that possesses the capability to restore health or sound condition. Providing a remedy or a solution to a problematic situation. Serving to counteract harmful effects or medical symptoms.
example_sentence: The hot springs are believed to have curative properties for skin ailments. Many patients seek curative treatments rather than just palliative care. The new law was intended to be a curative measure for the economic crisis. Doctors hope that the drug will have a curative effect on the aggressive infection.

english_meaning: A person who manages, selects, and organizes items in a museum, art gallery, library, or similar place. Someone responsible for taking care of a collection such as artworks, historical objects, or exhibits. They decide how items are displayed, preserved, and explained to the public.
example_sentence: The museum curator arranged a new exhibition on ancient civilizations. She works as a digital curator for an online art platform. The curator carefully preserved the old manuscripts. A good curator explains the historical value of each object to visitors.

english_meaning:
To control, limit, or restrain something. To keep something under control such as emotions, spending, or behavior. 
To reduce or limit something harmful or excessive. The raised edge along a street that separates it from the pavement. A controlling influence.
example_sentence: The government is trying to curb inflation. She struggled to curb her anger during the meeting. New laws were introduced to curb illegal activities. He parked his car near the curb.

english_meaning: A yellow chemical compound found in turmeric. The main active pigment of turmeric, often discussed for color, flavor, and possible health-related properties.
example_sentence: Curcumin gives turmeric its bright yellow color. Researchers are studying curcumin in nutrition science. The supplement contains curcumin extract. Curcumin stains cloth easily. Many curries get their color from turmeric and curcumin.

english_meaning: To separate or cause to separate into lumps or curds, especially milk. To spoil or turn sour as a result of fermentation. To undergo a change in texture from smooth to lumpy due to heat or acid. To cause a physical or emotional reaction of coldness or fear, often in the phrase 'curdle the blood'. To thicken or congeal into a mass. To fail or go wrong in a metaphorical sense.
example_sentence: If you add lemon juice to the warm milk, it will begin to curdle immediately. The chef warned that the sauce might curdle if the heat was set too high. The high-pitched scream in the dark was enough to curdle her blood. The stagnant economy caused many small business ventures to curdle and fail.

english_meaning: To make a person or an animal healthy again after an illness. To make an illness go away. Something that will solve a problem, improve a bad situation, etc. Something that makes someone who is sick healthy again.
example_sentence: Will you be able to cure him, Doctor?. Prevention is better than cure. There's still no cure for cancer. Researchers are working to find a cure for the disease. There is no known cure but the illness can be treated.

english_meaning: A strong desire to know or learn something. It can also refer to a strange or unusual object or circumstance. It is the fundamental drive behind exploration and investigation.
example_sentence: The child's curiosity about the nature of stars led him to study physics. Her curiosity was piqued by the mysterious letter on the table. The antique shop was filled with rare curiosities from around the globe. Driven by curiosity, the researchers spent years in the jungle.

english_meaning: Eager to know or learn something. It can also describe something strange or unusual. A curious person asks many questions and seeks new information.
example_sentence: The curious kittens explored every corner of the new house. I am curious to know why he decided to leave so suddenly. A curious noise echoed through the empty hallway at midnight. He has a curious habit of reading the last page of a book first.

english_meaning: A curved or spiral shape, especially in hair. To form or make something into a curve, ringlet, or coil. To bend, roll up, twist, or move in a curved path.
example_sentence: Her hair falls in soft curls. The paper began to curl at the edges. Smoke curled above the chimney. He curled his fingers around the cup. The cat curled up beside the heater.

english_meaning: Belonging to the present time or happening now. A steady flow of a fluid or gas in a specific direction. The flow of electrical charge through a conductor. A prevailing trend or general tendency of opinions or events.
example_sentence: The current situation requires immediate attention from the authorities. The boat was swept away by the strong river current. It is important to stay updated with current events in the world. An alternating current is used to power most household appliances.

english_meaning: At the present time. Now, or during the period that is happening at the moment.
example_sentence: The museum is currently closed for repairs. She is currently working from home. Currently, the company has three offices. No vacancies are currently available.

english_meaning: The plural form of curriculum. The complete sets of subjects and courses taught in a school, college, or university. The planned programmes of study that describe what learners are expected to know and be able to do. The organised bodies of content, activities, and assessments used in different educational institutions.
example_sentence: The two universities follow very different curricula. New science curricula were introduced across the province last year. The committee reviewed the curricula of all partner colleges. Modern curricula place greater emphasis on critical thinking.

english_meaning: The subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college. It encompasses the collective set of learning experiences provided by an educational institution. The term often refers to the planned interaction of pupils with instructional content, materials, and processes.
example_sentence: The school is designing a new curriculum to include more technology courses. The national curriculum sets out the standards for all primary schools. Students must complete the core curriculum before they can specialize in a major. Extracurricular activities complement the academic curriculum provided by the university.

english_meaning: A brief account of a person's education, qualifications, and previous experience, typically sent with a job application. It is a detailed document highlighting a person's professional history and clinical or academic achievements. This document is longer and more comprehensive than a standard resume.
example_sentence: Please attach your curriculum vitae to the email before submitting the application. Her curriculum vitae includes several publications in prestigious medical journals. The hiring manager spent several minutes reviewing my curriculum vitae during the interview. A well-organized curriculum vitae can significantly improve your chances of getting the job.

english_meaning: A solemn utterance intended to invoke a supernatural power to inflict harm or punishment on someone or something. It can also refer to an offensive word used to express anger or annoyance. In a general sense, it is something that causes great trouble or misfortune.
example_sentence: The old legend says a curse was placed on the hidden treasure. He let out a loud curse when he accidentally stubbed his toe on the table. Living in a small town can be both a blessing and a curse. People believed the family was under a curse because of their constant bad luck.

english_meaning: Rudely brief in speech or manner. Using few words in a way that seems unfriendly or impatient. Short and abrupt to the point of appearing impolite.
example_sentence: His curt reply made it clear that the meeting was over. She gave a curt nod and walked away. The manager sent a curt email refusing the request. I was surprised by his curt tone on the phone.

english_meaning: To reduce, shorten, limit, decrease, or stop something before it is completed. To cut short or reduce the length, amount, size, time, or extent of something. It is often used when something is limited due to rules, shortage, safety concerns, financial issues, or other reasons.
example_sentence: The company decided to curtail unnecessary expenses during the financial crisis. Heavy rain curtailed the outdoor event before sunset. The government introduced new policies to curtail illegal activities. Due to security concerns, the team curtailed travel to remote areas.

english_meaning: The act of reducing or limiting something. A cutback in the size, amount, or extent of something. A shortening of duration or activity. The imposition of restrictions on something. A decrease or restriction imposed upon rights or freedoms.
example_sentence: The curtailment of expenses helped the company survive. Citizens protested against the curtailment of their rights. There has been a curtailment of public transport services. The curtailment of working hours pleased many employees.

english_meaning: A unit used to measure the flow of water equal to one cubic foot per second. The volume of water passing a point in a river, canal, or pipe in one second. It is commonly used in hydrology, irrigation systems, flood forecasting, and water management to describe discharge rates. A volume of 1 cubic foot of water passing through a point in 1 second.
synonyms: ["Cubic foot per second","Water discharge rate","Flow rate","Streamflow unit"]
example_sentence: 1 cusec is equal to 28.317 liters per second. The river discharge increased to five thousand cusecs after the heavy rain. The canal supplies water at the rate of two hundred cusecs during the irrigation season. Engineers measured the flow at seventy cusecs to assess flood risk. The dam released an extra fifty cusecs to stabilize the water level.

english_meaning: A soft padded object used for sitting, leaning, or support. A protective layer that absorbs shock, pressure, or impact. To soften the effect of a blow, difficulty, or loss. To protect or support someone or something from harm.
example_sentence: She placed a cushion behind her back. Air bags cushion passengers during a crash. Savings helped cushion the family against rising prices. The thick carpet cushioned his fall.

english_meaning: Soft, thick, and comfortable like a cushion. Providing gentle support or protection from pressure or impact. Having a springy or padded feel.
example_sentence: The shoes have a cushiony sole. We sank into the cushiony sofa. A cushiony layer of moss covered the ground. The mattress feels firm but pleasantly cushiony.

english_meaning: A pointed end or projecting tip. A point of transition between two states, periods, signs, or conditions. In mathematics or anatomy, a pointed part or meeting point.
example_sentence: The company is on the cusp of major growth. She stood on the cusp of adulthood. The moon's cusp was bright in the evening sky. A tooth may have more than one cusp. The decision came at the cusp of winter.

english_meaning: A tropical fruit with a soft, creamy sweet flesh and a green scaly skin. A fruit known for its custard-like texture inside. A member of the Annonaceae family widely grown in South Asia. A fruit rich in vitamins, minerals, and natural sugars. A dessert-like fruit often eaten fresh or in shakes.
example_sentence: The custard apple has a sweet and creamy taste. She loves eating custard apple after dinner. Custard apples are available in the market during autumn. My grandmother made a delicious custard apple milkshake.

english_meaning: A person responsible for caring for, guarding, or maintaining something. A keeper, caretaker, guardian, or person in charge of property, records, buildings, or funds.
example_sentence: The school custodian unlocked the doors early. A bank can act as custodian of important documents. The museum custodian protects rare objects. Parents are custodians of their children's welfare. The custodian cleaned the hall after the event.

english_meaning: A traditional practice or usual way of behaving that is common to a group, society, or place. A habitual action regularly followed by a particular person. Made or done to order for a specific customer rather than produced in large numbers. Relating to something specially designed to suit an individual's requirements. The regular support given to a shop or business by its buyers. Duties or taxes charged on goods brought into a country, and the department that collects them.
example_sentence: Removing your shoes before entering a home is an old custom here. It was his custom to walk in the park every evening. They ordered a custom table built from local wood. The shop lost much of its custom after the new mall opened.

english_meaning: British spelling of customize. To modify or build something according to a person's individual needs, taste, or requirements. To change the settings, appearance, or features of a product so that it suits a particular user. To adapt a standard item or service for a specific purpose or customer.
example_sentence: You can customise the layout of your profile page at any time. The tailor will customise the suit to fit him perfectly. Many users customise their browsers with helpful extensions. The agency customises holiday packages for each family.

english_meaning: The process of changing a product, service, software system, or experience to suit particular needs or preferences. The act of making or altering something to order.
example_sentence: The software allows extensive customization. Car customization can include new paint and seats. Customers value the customization of their orders. The dashboard offers simple customization options.

english_meaning: To modify or build something according to a person's individual needs, taste, or requirements. To change the appearance, settings, or features of a product so that it suits a particular user. To adapt a standard item or service for a specific purpose or customer. To personalise software, a device, or a document by adjusting its available options.
example_sentence: You can customize the dashboard to show only the reports you need. The company allows buyers to customize the interior of every car. She customized her phone with a new theme and ringtone. Teachers often customize lessons to match the level of their students.

english_meaning: To be less strict, less critical, or more forgiving toward someone because they are having difficulties, made a mistake, or deserve understanding. To treat a person with patience, understanding, or leniency instead of judging or criticizing them harshly. It is commonly used when someone has made a mistake, is under pressure, is learning something new, or is facing difficult circumstances.
synonyms: ["Be lenient","Give a break","Go easy on","Show some understanding"]
example_sentence: Please cut me some slack. I'm still learning how to use this software. The teacher cut the students some slack because the exam was unusually difficult. After working all night, she hoped her manager would cut her some slack. Everyone makes mistakes, so you should cut him some slack.

english_meaning: To look embarrassed, ashamed, weak, or unsuccessful, especially in a situation where someone expected to do well. It means to make a poor impression or appear in a pitiful state in front of others.
example_sentence: After forgetting his speech, the politician cut a sorry figure on the stage. The team cut a sorry figure after losing all their matches. He cut a sorry figure when he couldn’t answer a single question in the interview. Without proper preparation, the student cut a sorry figure in front of the class.

english_meaning: To go across something instead of following the usual path. To affect or include different groups, categories, or areas. To go beyond boundaries or limitations. To oppose or go against something
example_sentence: We cut across the park to save time. We cut across the field to reach the school faster. The issue of climate change cuts across political and social boundaries. His influence cuts across age and gender. Her views cut across the traditional thinking of the community.

english_meaning: To remove something by cutting. To run away quickly (informal/old-fashioned). To switch to another scene suddenly.
example_sentence: The surgeon cut away the damaged tissue. The thief cut away before the police arrived. The director cut away to a close-up shot.

english_meaning: To reduce in amount or size. To prune or trim plants. To move back to an earlier position (less common, cinematic use).
example_sentence: They cut back on expenses during the crisis. The government announced to cut back expenses. The gardener cut back the plants in the garden.

english_meaning: To do something in the easiest, quickest, or cheapest way, often by ignoring rules, quality, or safety. To save time, money, or effort by using shortcuts
example_sentence: Don’t cut corners on safety. They cut corners to save money. The builders cut corners by using cheap materials, and now the wall is cracking. If you cut corners on safety, you put everyone at risk. The company was fined because it cut corners to finish the project quickly. Students who cut corners while studying often struggle in exams.

english_meaning: To reduce or decrease something, or to make less.
example_sentence: You should cut down on sugar. They cut down the old tree in the garden. We need to cut down our expenses. The doctor told him to cut down on smoking.

english_meaning: To involve oneself suddenly or unexpectedly in someone else’s activity. To allow someone to share in a profit, business, or opportunity. To pull in or move ahead suddenly, often considered rude. To ask someone to dance, especially interrupting another pair. To begin to work automatically or unexpectedly.
example_sentence: She cut in while I was speaking. She was telling a story when he rudely cut in. That car cut in front of us on the highway. May I cut in? (asking to dance with someone’s partner). The generator cuts in when the electricity goes off. The middleman cut in on the profits.

english_meaning: To have no effect or influence, to fail to impress. When something “cuts no ice,” it means that it does not convince, persuade, or make an impact on someone or a situation. It is often used to indicate that an argument, excuse, or attempt has no effect.
synonyms: ["Have no effect","Fail to impress","Make no difference","Fall flat"]
example_sentence: His apology cut no ice with the manager. Excuses like that cut no ice in our company. Her warnings cut no ice with the teenagers. The politician’s promises cut no ice with voters.

english_meaning: To stop the supply, connection, or relationship. To kill / bring to an end. To interrupt. To isolate
example_sentence: The electricity was cut off due to non-payment. She tried to explain, but he cut her off in the middle. After the fight, he cut off all contact with his friends. The village was cut off by heavy floods. His life was tragically cut off at an early age.

english_meaning: To create your own way in life instead of following others. A person who chooses independence and originality. It means making decisions based on personal beliefs, goals, and vision rather than copying traditions, expectations, or the actions of others. It often reflects courage, leadership, and self-confidence.
synonyms: ["Forge your own way","Blaze your own trail","Go your own way","Be independent","Think for yourself"]
antonyms: ["Follow the crowd","Copy others","Conform","Depend on others","Stick to tradition"]
example_sentence: She decided to cut her own path and start her own business instead of joining a corporate job. Rather than following family expectations, he cut his own path and became an artist. Great leaders often cut their own path and inspire others to follow. In a competitive world, you need confidence to cut your own path and succeed.

english_meaning: It means to be naturally suited or equipped for a particular task or role. It indicates having the right qualities or personality for a specific job. It is often used in negative contexts to show someone lacks the necessary traits. It describes a person who has the inherent aptitude to succeed in a chosen field. It implies that a certain path matches one's inherent capabilities.
synonyms: ["Suited for","Fitted for","Appropriate for","Tailored for","Qualified for","Capable of","Apt for","Designed for","Meant for","Equipped for","Right for"]
example_sentence: I quickly realized that I am not cut out for a desk job. She is definitely cut out for a career in medicine because of her empathy. He wondered if he was truly cut out for the challenges of parenthood. You need a lot of patience, and I just don't think I am cut out for it.

word: Cut the ground from under somebody’s feet
english_meaning: To suddenly remove the support, basis, or advantage on which someone depends. To make someone's argument, plan, or position ineffective. To anticipate someone's action and thereby leave them unable to proceed
example_sentence: His resignation cut the ground from under the committee's feet. By announcing the deal early, they cut the ground from under their rival's feet. The new evidence cut the ground from under the defense team's feet. Her boss cut the ground from under her feet by approving a different plan.

english_meaning: To perform well enough to meet expectations or standards. To be successful, skilled, or capable of doing something properly.
example_sentence: He cut the mustard in the final test. She worked hard but could not cut the mustard in the final round of the competition. He really cuts the mustard when it comes to public speaking. The new player did not cut the mustard in his first match. Only those who cut the mustard will be selected for the team.

english_meaning: To end a relationship, connection, or association with someone or something. To completely stop communication or dealings with a person, group, or organization. To break off long-standing bonds, whether emotional, social, or professional. To disconnect oneself from influences, habits, or people considered harmful. To formally sever links or agreements between individuals, families, or nations.
example_sentence: After years of conflict, he decided to cut those ties with his old business partners. She had to cut those ties with friends who kept dragging her down. The two countries chose to cut those ties following the diplomatic dispute. Sometimes you must cut those ties to protect your peace of mind.

english_meaning: To stop unnecessary talk and go straight to the main point. To avoid introductions, explanations, or irrelevant details and focus immediately on what is most important. It is often used when someone wants clarity or efficiency in a conversation.
synonyms: ["Get to the point","Be direct","Come to the point","Speak plainly"]
antonyms: ["Beat around the bush","Ramble on","Go off topic","Drag out the discussion"]
example_sentence: We are short on time so let us cut to the chase and discuss the budget. Instead of long stories he cut to the chase and explained the problem. The manager asked everyone to cut to the chase during the meeting.

english_meaning: An old word for a pickpocket or thief who steals money from a purse or pocket, especially in a crowd.
example_sentence: A cutpurse moved through the market crowd. In old London, a cutpurse could steal a coin pouch in seconds. The guard caught the cutpurse near the gate. The play includes a clever cutpurse as a comic character. Travelers were warned about cutpurses at the fair.

english_meaning: The most advanced or modern stage of development in a field. The forefront of new ideas, technology, or techniques. Extremely innovative and ahead of the current standard. The sharp edge of a blade or tool. Leading a new direction in innovation.
example_sentence: This lab works on cutting edge medical research. Their technology is truly cutting edge. She wears cutting edge fashion designs. The cutting edge of the knife was extremely sharp.

english_meaning: Highly advanced or innovative. At the newest and most developed stage of a field, technology, or activity. The leading position in new ideas or development.
example_sentence: The company invests heavily in cutting-edge research. This hospital uses cutting-edge medical technology. The laboratory is at the cutting edge of cancer research. Their cutting-edge designs have transformed the industry.

english_meaning: A genus of leguminous plants, best known for the species Cyamopsis tetragonoloba, also called cluster bean or 'guar'. Widely grown in South Asia for food and industrial gum.
example_sentence: Cyamopsis tetragonoloba is commonly known as cluster bean. Farmers in Rajasthan grow Cyamopsis for its gum. Cyamopsis seeds are a valuable export commodity. Research on Cyamopsis has increased due to its industrial uses.

english_meaning: A quadrilateral whose four vertices all lie on a single circle. A four-sided figure inscribed in a circle. A quadrilateral in which opposite angles add up to 180 degrees. A key figure in circle geometry and related theorems.
example_sentence: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. He proved the theorem using a cyclic quadrilateral. All four corners of a cyclic quadrilateral touch the circle. The exam question involved a cyclic quadrilateral.

english_meaning: A person who rides a bicycle. Someone who cycles for travel, exercise, or sport. A competitor in bicycle racing.
example_sentence: A cyclist was hurt at the crossing this morning. Cyclists must wear helmets on the main road. She is a keen cyclist who rides every weekend. The leading cyclist finished the race in record time.

english_meaning: A giant creature that has a single eye in the center of its forehead. Cyclopes were known for great strength and lived isolated lives.
example_sentence: The Cyclops guarded the cave with great strength. In Greek myths, Odysseus outsmarted a Cyclops. The story describes a fierce Cyclops living alone on an island. The movie showed the Cyclops as a terrifying giant.

english_meaning: A powerful synthetic explosive compound commonly known as RDX. It is used in controlled industrial and military applications due to its very high explosive energy. A man-made nitramine compound known for its high stability compared to many other explosives and its strong explosive performance. It is widely studied in chemistry and materials science due to its molecular structure and energy release characteristics.
example_sentence: Cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine is studied in chemistry due to its strong energy release properties. RDX is another name for cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine. The molecular structure of cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine makes it highly energetic. Scientists analyze cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine for its stability under different conditions.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with two parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface. A tube-shaped object with uniform circular cross-section. The chamber in an engine where the piston moves.
example_sentence: A can of soda is shaped like a cylinder. The cylinder holds 500 milliliters. The engine has six cylinders. Calculate the surface area of the cylinder.

english_meaning: A person who believes that people are mostly selfish and not sincere, and who tends to doubt good intentions. A person who does not easily trust others’ good intentions. Someone who believes people act mostly out of selfish reasons. A person with a negative or doubtful view of human behavior
example_sentence: He is such a cynic that he never believes anyone is telling the truth. The cynic in him said the charity event was only for publicity. Don’t be a cynic, sometimes people really do good things without selfish reasons. After many betrayals, she became a cynic about relationships.

english_meaning: Believing that people act only for their own benefit and not trusting sincere intentions. A person who doubts honesty, goodness, or sincerity in others and assumes that actions are motivated by selfishness or personal gain rather than genuine concern.
example_sentence: He is cynical about politicians and does not believe their promises. Her cynical attitude made it hard for her to trust anyone. After years of corruption, people became cynical about the system. The movie presents a cynical view of modern society.

english_meaning: In a way that shows distrust of human sincerity or integrity. Acting or speaking with a belief that people are motivated purely by self-interest. Showing contempt for accepted standards of honesty or morality.
example_sentence: She smiled cynically, knowing his promises were empty. He cynically ignored the warnings, hoping nothing bad would happen. The politician cynically used the tragedy to gain votes. He laughed cynically at the idea of honest business in the city.

english_meaning: Distrust of human sincerity. An attitude where a person believes that people act mainly out of self interest and not from honesty or kindness. It often includes doubt, disbelief, and negative judgment about motives.
example_sentence: His cynicism about politics comes from years of broken promises. She listened to the speech with clear cynicism and doubt. Too much cynicism can damage relationships and trust. The journalist wrote the article with sharp cynicism toward authority.

english_meaning: An extreme fear of dogs. A specific phobia in which a person feels intense, irrational fear or anxiety when seeing, hearing, or even thinking about dogs. This fear can cause panic, avoidance behavior, and physical symptoms like sweating or rapid heartbeat.
example_sentence: Due to cynophobia, she avoids parks where dogs are present. His cynophobia developed after a dog bite in childhood. Therapy helped her manage her cynophobia effectively. Cynophobia can interfere with daily social activities.

english_meaning: A person or thing that attracts everyone’s attention. Someone or something that becomes the main focus of attention, admiration, or interest in a place or situation.
example_sentence: The young scientist became the cynosure of the conference after her discovery. The bride was the cynosure of all eyes at the wedding ceremony. His bold speech made him the cynosure of the entire gathering. The new building quickly became the cynosure of the city.

english_meaning: A feminine given name. A poetic name associated with the moon goddess Artemis or Diana. It is used as a personal name and sometimes in literary references to the moon.
example_sentence: Cynthia sent the invitation yesterday. The poem uses Cynthia as a name for the moon. Cynthia speaks three languages fluently. We met Cynthia at the library. The old novel has a heroine named Cynthia.

english_meaning: A secret or disguised way of writing; a code. It can also refer to a person of no importance or influence. In mathematics, it is an archaic term for the figure zero.
example_sentence: The spy used a complex cypher to send messages to his headquarters. He felt like a mere cypher in the large corporation where nobody knew his name. The cryptic note was written in a cypher that took weeks to crack. The old captain used a simple substitution cypher for his personal diary.

english_meaning: A male personal name. A masculine given name of Greek origin. It comes from the Greek word Kyrios meaning lord or master. The name is often associated with Saint Cyril, a Christian scholar and missionary, and it symbolizes authority, wisdom, and leadership.
example_sentence: Cyril is known for his calm leadership style. The book was written by a scholar named Cyril. Cyril spoke confidently during the conference. Saint Cyril played an important role in early Christian history.

english_meaning: A closed sac or pouch in the body containing fluid, air, or other material. An abnormal growth under the skin or inside an organ. A protective capsule formed by some parasites or microorganisms. A medically defined swelling that may be harmless or require treatment.
example_sentence: The doctor said the lump was a harmless cyst. A small cyst developed under her skin. Some cysts disappear without surgery. The scan showed a cyst near the kidney.

english_meaning: Relating to or characterized by cysts. Concerning fluid-filled sacs or cavities in the body. Associated with cystic fibrosis, a genetic disease. Having the nature or form of a cyst.
example_sentence: The ultrasound showed cystic lesions in the liver. Cystic acne requires specialized treatment. He was born with cystic fibrosis. The cystic mass was removed surgically.

english_meaning: To take part in an activity in a casual or superficial way. To splash or play around in water with the hands or feet. To move something in and out of a liquid lightly. To work at something occasionally or without serious intent. To wet or moisten by splashing.
example_sentence: He decided to dabble in painting during his summer vacation. The children love to dabble their feet in the cool stream. She doesn't want a full career in music but likes to dabble in songwriting. Many amateur investors dabble in the stock market without proper research.

english_meaning: To engage in an activity in a casual or superficial manner. To work at something occasionally or without serious intent. To splash or play around in water. To experiment with different ideas or hobbies briefly. To involve oneself in a field without committing deeply.
example_sentence: He likes to dabble around in oil painting during his weekends. She decided to dabble around with coding before choosing a major. The children love to dabble around in the shallow end of the pool. Instead of a full-time career, he prefers to dabble around in various freelance projects.

english_meaning: To take part in an activity casually, occasionally, or without serious commitment. To try a subject or pursuit only superficially.
example_sentence: He likes to dabble in painting during his free weekends. She dabbled in stock trading before deciding it was not for her. Many students dabble in different hobbies before finding their true passion. He has dabbled in politics but never pursued it seriously.

english_meaning: In computing, a background program that runs continuously and handles requests without direct user control. In classical mythology, a supernatural being or spirit standing between gods and humans. An inner guiding spirit, inspiration, or driving force within a person. An older spelling of demon, meaning an evil spirit.
example_sentence: The print daemon runs quietly in the background of the system. A daemon restarts the service automatically if it fails. In the myth, a daemon guided the hero through the forest. He spoke of the creative daemon that drove him to write.

english_meaning: A spring flowering plant with a yellow or white trumpet-shaped bloom growing from a bulb. A member of the narcissus family, widely grown in gardens and parks. A bright yellow colour resembling this flower. A symbol of spring, cheerfulness, and new beginnings.
example_sentence: A single daffodil had opened beside the path. The daffodil is the national flower of Wales. She wore a scarf in a soft daffodil shade. Plant each daffodil bulb about ten centimetres deep.

english_meaning: Plural of daffodil; spring flowers with bright yellow or white trumpet-shaped blooms growing from bulbs. A group of well-known garden and wild flowers that appear in early spring. Flowers often used as a symbol of spring, hope, and renewal.
example_sentence: Daffodils covered the hillside in early March. She picked a bunch of daffodils for the table. The poem describes a field of golden daffodils. Daffodils are among the first flowers of spring.

english_meaning: Silly, foolish, or slightly crazy in an amusing way. Behaving in an eccentric or scatterbrained manner. Informally, extremely fond of or enthusiastic about someone or something.
example_sentence: He told a daffy joke that made everyone laugh. Her daffy sense of humour lifts the whole office. The film features a daffy inventor and his talking dog. She is absolutely daffy about old motorcycles.

english_meaning: Silly, foolish, or lacking good sense. Behaving in a ridiculous or absurd manner. Not sensible or showing poor judgment. Somewhat crazy or eccentric in a harmless way. Lacking intelligence or common sense.
example_sentence: That was a daft thing to do in such cold weather. Don't be daft, of course you can come with us. His daft sense of humor always makes people laugh. She felt daft for forgetting her own birthday.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being silly, foolish, or lacking good sense. Foolish behaviour or a foolish idea. Mild craziness or absurdity, often used humorously or affectionately.
example_sentence: The whole plan was a piece of complete daftness. There is a charming daftness in his early poems. She laughed at the daftness of the situation. His daftness sometimes hides a very sharp mind.

english_meaning: In Australian and New Zealand informal use, a person who is unfashionable or socially awkward, often said in an affectionate way. An amusing or eccentric person who is not concerned with appearances. A lock of matted, dirty wool hanging from the rear of a sheep. Informally, a small piece or hanging clump of something.
example_sentence: Don't worry about your clothes, you look like a happy dag. He is a bit of a dag, but everyone loves him. The shearer trimmed the dags from the sheep. My uncle is such a dag at family parties.

english_meaning: A long white radish with a mild, slightly sweet flavour. An East Asian vegetable eaten raw, pickled, or cooked. The plant grown for this large root. A common ingredient in salads, soups, and pickles.
example_sentence: Grated daikon is served beside grilled fish. Daikon pickles are crunchy and refreshing. She simmered daikon slices in the broth. The daikon grew almost a foot long.

english_meaning: A set of actions performed regularly at the same time each day. A fixed personal habit or routine that gives structure to the day. A customary religious or ceremonial practice carried out every day.
example_sentence: Morning tea on the balcony is her daily ritual. He follows a strict daily ritual of exercise and reading. For many families, the evening meal is a daily ritual. The monks begin each day with a simple daily ritual.

english_meaning: In a delicate, graceful, careful, or refined manner. In a small, neat, or elegant way, especially while eating, moving, or handling something.
example_sentence: She lifted the teacup daintily. The child stepped daintily around the puddle. He ate the pastry daintily with a fork. The dancer moved daintily across the stage. Flowers were arranged daintily in a small vase.

english_meaning: Delicately small, pretty, and attractive. Refined and elegant in manner or appearance. Fastidious or particular, especially about food. Something small and tasty to eat.
example_sentence: She wore a pair of dainty gold earrings. The child ate the biscuit with dainty little bites. He is dainty about what he eats. The table was set with dainty pastries.

english_meaning: A brief and casual romantic or sexual relationship. A short period of involvement with an activity that is not taken seriously. Idle time spent in play or amusement instead of work. Flirtatious behaviour without serious intention.
example_sentence: His brief dalliance with acting ended after one play. The novel describes a summer dalliance by the sea. She admitted to a youthful dalliance with radical politics. There is no time for dalliance when the deadline is near.

english_meaning: To waste time or move slowly. To delay without purpose. To flirt or treat something lightly without serious intention.
example_sentence: Do not dally on the way home. The committee cannot dally over such an urgent matter. He dallied with the idea of moving abroad. They dallied by the river until sunset. She warned him not to dally with her feelings.

english_meaning: To treat something or someone in a casual, unserious way. To flirt with a person without genuine intention. To consider an idea briefly without real commitment. To play or toy with a possibility for amusement.
synonyms: ["Toy with","Trifle with","Flirt with","Play with","Consider casually","Fool around with"]
example_sentence: He dallied with the idea of moving abroad. It is unkind to dally with someone's feelings. She dallied with painting for a while before returning to music. Do not dally with such a serious offer.

english_meaning: A barrier built across a river or stream to hold back water. The body of water held back by such a barrier. To build a dam across something. To block or hold back a flow, feeling, or expression.
example_sentence: The dam supplies electricity to the entire region. Engineers inspected the dam after the earthquake. Villagers dammed the stream to store water. She could no longer dam her tears.

english_meaning: Slightly wet or moist. Moisture in the air, walls, or ground. To make less strong, lively, or intense. To moisten slightly.
example_sentence: The clothes were still damp after the rain. Damp walls can damage a house. The bad news damped our excitement. Wipe the table with a damp cloth. The cave smelled cold and damp.

english_meaning: To make something slightly wet or moist. To reduce the strength, intensity, or enthusiasm of something. To lessen the force or effect of something such as sound, emotion, or enthusiasm. Used both literally to describe adding moisture and figuratively to describe reducing the effect or energy of something.
