example_sentence: She dampened the cloth before using it to clean the surface. The bad news dampened everyone's spirits at the party. The thick curtains help to dampen the noise from the busy street outside. His rude comments dampened her enthusiasm for the project. The unexpected rain dampened the mood of the outdoor festival.

english_meaning: Something that discourages enthusiasm, enjoyment, or success. A device that reduces vibration, noise, or movement. A movable plate that controls the flow of air in a chimney, flue, or duct. A pad in a piano that stops a string from vibrating. To put a damper on something means to spoil its cheerful mood.
example_sentence: The heavy rain put a damper on our picnic plans. Engineers installed a damper to reduce the bridge's vibration. Close the damper to stop heat escaping from the chimney. His bad news cast a damper over the celebration.

english_meaning: A young unmarried woman or girl. A young, unmarried woman, often portrayed as delicate, graceful, or in need of help. It is mostly found in fairy tales or poetic expressions
example_sentence: The knight rescued the damsel from the burning tower. A fair damsel was waiting by the riverside. In many old tales, a brave hero saves a damsel in distress. The painter captured the beauty of the young damsel in his artwork.

english_meaning: A woman in trouble needing help. Traditionally a woman in trouble, danger, or a difficult situation who depends on someone to rescue her.
example_sentence: The hero saved the damsel in distress. She doesn’t want to be a damsel in distress. Old stories often feature a damsel in distress. The movie had a classic damsel in distress scene.

english_meaning: Small flakes of dead skin that fall from the scalp. A common condition causing white flakes and itching on the head. Loose scales that appear in the hair due to dryness or irritation.
example_sentence: He uses a special shampoo to control dandruff. Cold weather often causes dandruff to increase. She was embarrassed by the dandruff on her shoulders. Doctors suggest oiling the scalp to reduce dandruff.

english_meaning: To hang or swing freely. To hang loosely from a point so that the object moves or swings gently, often without support at the bottom. It can also mean to tempt someone by offering something attractive.
example_sentence: The keys dangle from the hook near the door. His legs dangled over the edge of the chair. A broken wire was dangling from the ceiling. The company dangled a promotion to motivate employees.

english_meaning: A person or thing that hangs loosely from something. In grammar, a modifier that is not clearly attached to the word it should modify. Something suspended or trailing without support. A person who lingers or hovers around others.
example_sentence: The keychain had a small dangler shaped like a star. Editors quickly spot a dangler in a sentence. The earrings featured a delicate dangler. He was a dangler at every social event.

english_meaning: Neat, stylish, and well-dressed. Describes someone, usually a man, who is tidy in appearance, wears fashionable clothes, and carries themselves smartly.
example_sentence: He looked very dapper in his new suit. The dapper gentleman greeted everyone at the party. She admired his dapper appearance at the wedding. A dapper young man walked confidently into the room.

english_meaning: A warning sign of coming problems, difficulties, or dangers. An indication that the future may bring trouble. Symbol of uncertainty, threat, or something negative approaching. A sign of coming trouble or future danger.
synonyms: ["A brewing storm","Trouble ahead","Warning signs","Ominous signs","Threat approaching","Foreboding","Impending danger"]
antonyms: ["Bright future","Clear skies ahead","Hopeful signs","Calm before progress","Positive outlook"]
example_sentence: The country’s economy is improving, but rising inflation is dark clouds on the horizon. Although their business is growing, rising debts are dark clouds on the horizon. Peace talks are happening, but political unrest remains a dark cloud on the horizon. The team is strong, yet injuries are dark clouds on the horizon.

english_meaning: A candidate or competitor about whom little is known but who unexpectedly wins or succeeds. A person who keeps their interests and ideas secret, especially someone who has a surprising ability or skill. An unexpected winner in a contest or election. Someone who emerges from obscurity to achieve great prominence.
synonyms: ["Unknown Quantity","Underdog","Surprise Winner","Secret Talent","Hidden Competitor","Unlikely Candidate","Unforeseen Victor","Outsider","Mystery Participant"]
antonyms: ["Favorite","Frontrunner","Expected Winner","Sure Thing","Leading Candidate","Obvious Choice","Champion","Predictable Winner","Top Dog"]
example_sentence: He was considered a dark horse in the election but ended up winning by a landslide. The newly formed team proved to be a dark horse in the tournament. I never knew she could sing so beautifully, she is a real dark horse. As a dark horse, the independent filmmaker took home the best picture award.

english_meaning: A small pointed missile that can be thrown or fired. As an action, it means to move or run somewhere suddenly and rapidly. It illustrates a sudden, quick, and sharp movement across a short distance.
example_sentence: She suddenly watched a small rabbit dart quickly across the narrow road. He threw a pointed dart perfectly into the central bullseye of the heavy board. The suspicious guard saw a dark shadow dart stealthily behind the large building. Whenever the heavy doorbell rings, my anxious cat will dart under the old bed. He cast a sharp, angry dart with his eyes towards his noisy neighbors.

english_meaning: To run or move quickly. To strike or break forcefully. To destroy or ruin something suddenly. A sudden fast run or movement. A small quantity of something. A punctuation mark. Energy or stylish confidence
example_sentence: He made a quick dash to catch the bus. Add a dash of salt to improve the taste. She dashed across the road in a hurry. The news dashed all his hopes for success.

english_meaning: To move quickly from one place to another in a hurried or energetic way. To move quickly and energetically from place to place, to be very active or busy.
example_sentence: The kids dashed about in the playground. He dashed about trying to fix everything. She dashed about the office collecting papers. They dashed about preparing for the party.

english_meaning: To go into a place very quickly or suddenly, often in a hurry or with excitement.
example_sentence: He dashed in as the rain started. She dashed in to grab her umbrella. I dashed in to avoid the storm. The children dashed in after school.

english_meaning: To do something quickly and hurriedly, often without much care. To do or write something in a hurry. To leave somewhere quickly
example_sentence: I must dash off to the meeting. She dashed off a quick note to her friend. He dashed off without saying goodbye. I dashed off a sketch before class started.

english_meaning: To leave somewhere very quickly. To produce or write something in a short time.
example_sentence: He dashed out when he heard the fire alarm. She dashed out to catch the bus. I dashed out to grab some lunch. The kids dashed out to play.

english_meaning: The panel in a vehicle containing instruments and controls for the driver. A digital interface displaying key information, data, or performance metrics. A visual summary of important business or system indicators. A control screen for software applications or online services. A board historically used to block mud splashed by horses.
example_sentence: The car's dashboard lit up when he turned the key. She checked the dashboard to monitor daily sales. The new app has a clean and simple dashboard. Warning lights on the dashboard indicated a problem.

english_meaning: Stylish, attractive, and confident in appearance or manner. Lively, spirited, and full of energy. Moving or acting with great speed. Boldly adventurous or showy.
example_sentence: He looked dashing in his new navy suit. The dashing young officer won everyone's admiration. She made a dashing entrance just before the ceremony began. The film tells the story of a dashing adventurer.

english_meaning: Wicked and cruel in a cowardly way. Showing meanness combined with a lack of courage. Deliberately evil and treacherous.
example_sentence: The attack on unarmed civilians was a dastardly act. He hatched a dastardly plan to ruin his rival. Newspapers condemned the dastardly crime. Such dastardly behaviour deserves severe punishment.

english_meaning: A Zoroastrian high priest, especially among the Parsi community. An established custom, practice, or traditional rule. A customary fee, commission, or allowance.
example_sentence: The dastur led the prayers at the fire temple. According to old dastur, the eldest son inherits the family land. The community still follows the dastur set by their ancestors. A small dastur was paid to the agent for arranging the sale.

english_meaning: Facts and figures collected for reference, analysis, or decision making. Information stored or processed by a computer. The results of observation or measurement in research. The plural form of datum, though often used as a singular mass noun.
example_sentence: The data show a clear rise in average temperatures. All personal data must be stored securely. Researchers spent months collecting data from rural areas. The company analysed sales data before launching the product.

english_meaning: A large organised collection of information stored in a computer so it can be searched easily. A structured set of records that can be updated, sorted, and retrieved quickly. A software system used to store and manage data for an organisation. Any systematic store of related information kept for reference.
example_sentence: All student records are kept in a central database. The company updated its customer database last month. He wrote a query to search the database quickly. A secure database protects personal information from misuse.

english_meaning: A sweet, sticky brown fruit that grows in clusters on the date palm. A dried or fresh fruit eaten as a snack or used in desserts. The palm tree that produces this fruit. A particular day of the month or year, or a social appointment with someone.
example_sentence: He breaks his fast with two dates and a glass of water. Dates are grown widely in the desert regions. Please write the date at the top of the page. They fixed a date for the wedding ceremony.

english_meaning: A single piece of information or fact. One item in a set of data used for analysis. A fixed starting point or reference level used in surveying and measurement. A known value from which other measurements are calculated.
example_sentence: Each datum was recorded carefully in the notebook. A single datum is not enough to prove the theory. Heights are measured from a fixed datum above sea level. The engineer marked the datum before starting the survey.

english_meaning: To smear, spread, or apply something roughly. A patch or smear of paint, mud, color, or other substance. To paint in a careless or unskilled way.
example_sentence: The child daubed paint on the wall. A daub of mud marked his sleeve. Workers daubed clay between the wooden beams. She daubed cream on the burn. The sign looked as if someone had daubed it in a hurry.

english_meaning: To make someone feel afraid, discouraged, or less confident. To intimidate, dishearten, or reduce courage.
example_sentence: The difficult climb did not daunt her. A long list of tasks can daunt a new employee. His calm voice helped daunt nobody in the room. Do not let criticism daunt you. The scale of the project would daunt many teams.

english_meaning: Showing fearlessness and determination. Not discouraged or intimidated by danger, difficulty, or failure. Brave, bold, and resolute in facing challenges.
example_sentence: The dauntless explorer crossed the icy mountains alone. She showed a dauntless spirit during the rescue operation. Our dauntless leader inspired everyone to keep working. The dauntless soldiers defended the post until the end. His dauntless attitude helped him face every challenge in life.

english_meaning: To waste time by moving slowly or delaying unnecessarily. To move slowly, act lazily, or delay doing something without a good reason. It often suggests carelessness or lack of urgency, especially when time matters.
example_sentence: Stop dawdling and get to work. He dawdled over his breakfast. The children dawdled on their way to school. Don’t dawdle; we’re late!. He was dawdling on the way to school and arrived late.

english_meaning: A person who wastes time and moves or works very slowly. Someone who delays work or movement unnecessarily. Such a person takes longer than needed, often because of laziness, lack of focus, or carelessness.
example_sentence: The teacher warned the dawdler to finish his assignment on time. Do not be a dawdler if you want to succeed in your career. The team lost the match because one player acted like a dawdler. He was known as a dawdler who missed deadlines regularly.

english_meaning: The first light of day before sunrise. The beginning or first appearance of something. To begin to become clear or understood.
example_sentence: We left the village at dawn. A new era seemed to dawn after the election. It finally dawned on me that I was lost. Birds began singing before dawn. The dawn light touched the mountains.

english_meaning: The early morning obligatory prayer offered before sunrise, known as Fajr in Islam. The first of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed at dawn. A prayer said at the break of day. The act of worship carried out in the early hours before the sun rises.
example_sentence: He wakes up early every day to offer the dawn prayer. The mosque was full of worshippers for the dawn prayer. Offering the dawn prayer requires waking up before sunrise. She felt peaceful after completing the dawn prayer. The call for the dawn prayer echoed across the quiet town.

english_meaning: A period of twenty four hours, from one midnight to the next. The time between sunrise and sunset when it is light. A particular date set aside for an event or purpose. A period or era in history or in someone's life.
example_sentence: There are seven days in a week. We spent the whole day at the beach. Independence Day is celebrated with great enthusiasm. In his day, he was the finest player in the country.

english_meaning: Repeatedly every day; happening continuously for many days without change. It expresses continuity and sometimes boredom or persistence.
example_sentence: He worked hard day after day. Day after day, he waited for her reply, but she never responded. The workers continued their protest day after day without losing hope. She practiced the piano day after day until she became perfect. The weather remained cloudy day after day, and people began to worry.

english_meaning: Every single day repeatedly and continuously. Something that happens continuously every day for a long time without change. Daily without interruption. Repeated again and again. Constant routine activity. Ongoing continuously.
example_sentence: She worked hard day in and day out to support her family. Day in and day out, the guard stood at the gate in every kind of weather. He practiced English day in and day out until he became fluent. The machine runs day in and day out without stopping.

english_meaning: To impress greatly with brightness, beauty, or skill. To temporarily blind someone with a strong light. To amaze or impress someone deeply with beauty, talent, intelligence, or performance. To shine very brightly. A bright glare or a showy display that attracts attention.
example_sentence: The bright headlights dazzled the driver at night. She dazzled the audience with her powerful speech. The diamond dazzled under the sunlight. His confidence and style dazzled everyone at the event.

english_meaning: Extremely bright, impressive, beautiful, skillful, or exciting. So brilliant that it can amaze or momentarily blind.
example_sentence: She wore a dazzling white dress. The team gave a dazzling display of skill. The sun was dazzling on the snow. His rise to fame was dazzlingly quick. A dazzling smile lit up her face.

english_meaning: Existing in fact, whether legally recognized or not. Actually the case, though not formally established. In reality, as opposed to in law. Describing a practical rather than legal status. Effectively or truly, though unofficially.
example_sentence: He became the de facto leader of the group. English is the de facto language of business worldwide. The general assumed de facto control of the country. She is the de facto head of the household.

english_meaning: A dead duck refers to someone or something that is doomed to fail or has no chance of success. It describes a plan, project, or idea that is no longer viable or effective. It can also denote a person in serious, inescapable trouble.
example_sentence: Without fresh investment, our startup is a dead duck. The proposed policy was a dead duck from the moment it was introduced. If the manager catches him lying again, his career at this company is a dead duck. They tried to revive the old proposal, but everyone knew it was already a dead duck.

english_meaning: Complete opposition or refusal toward an idea, plan, or action. It implies a firm stance where persuasion is unlikely to succeed.
example_sentence: She was dead set against moving to another city. The manager is dead set against changing the project plan. They were dead set against adopting new technology. I am dead set against selling my house at a loss.

english_meaning: Something or someone that is no longer useful. People, objects, or parts of an organization that do not contribute anymore and only take up space, effort, or resources. It is often used in workplaces, teams, or systems that need improvement.
example_sentence: The company removed all the dead wood to cut costs. It’s time to clear out the dead wood from the team. The manager said there’s no room for dead wood here. The club replaced its dead wood with fresh talent.

english_meaning: A person who avoids paying their debts or fulfilling responsibilities. A lazy or useless person who does not contribute. An idle or good-for-nothing individual. Informal term for someone who lives off others.
example_sentence: He turned out to be a deadbeat who never paid his rent. Her ex-husband was a deadbeat father. The company sued several deadbeat clients. Don't lend him money he's a known deadbeat.

english_meaning: To make something less strong, sharp, loud, painful, lively, or sensitive. To reduce feeling, sound, force, or effect.
example_sentence: Thick curtains help deaden outside noise. The medicine deadened the pain for a while. Bad news can deaden enthusiasm. Snow deadened the sound of footsteps. Repetition may deaden a reader's interest.

english_meaning: More likely to cause death. More dangerous, harmful, destructive, or effective than another person or thing.
synonyms: ["More fatal","More lethal","More dangerous","More harmful","More destructive","More poisonous"]
example_sentence: The new virus strain was deadlier than the first. Careless driving can be deadlier at night. The second weapon proved deadlier in close combat. Heat waves are becoming deadlier in many cities. A deadlier mistake would have cost the team the match.

english_meaning: A situation in which no progress or agreement is possible because opposing sides are equally strong or unwilling to compromise. A complete standstill in negotiations or decision-making. In computing, a condition in which processes wait indefinitely for one another's resources. To bring or come to such a standstill.
example_sentence: Negotiations ended in deadlock after both sides rejected the proposal. The committee remained deadlocked over the budget. A compromise finally broke the political deadlock. Poor resource management can cause a deadlock in the program. The tied vote left the council in a deadlock.

english_meaning: Unable to hear or having very little hearing. Unwilling to listen, notice, or respond to advice, requests, or warnings.
example_sentence: She has been deaf since childhood. The school provides support for deaf students. He remained deaf to our warnings. Loud music can make a person temporarily deaf. The committee was deaf to public complaints.

english_meaning: Very loud. A sound that is extremely loud and so intense that it hurts the ears or makes it hard to hear anything else. It is often used for noises like explosions, heavy traffic, loud music, or crowds.
example_sentence: The deafening noise of the explosion shook the entire building. The crowd gave a deafening cheer when the team won. Deafening music was coming from the nearby house. The silence after the deafening blast felt strange.

english_meaning: Somewhat deaf or slightly hard of hearing. Partly unable to hear clearly. The word is informal or old-fashioned.
synonyms: ["Hard of hearing","Partly deaf","Slightly deaf","Hearing-impaired","Dull of hearing"]
example_sentence: Grandfather is a little deafish, so speak clearly. The word deafish sounds old-fashioned today. A deafish patient may miss soft instructions. He became deafish after years of factory work. She leaned closer because she was slightly deafish.

english_meaning: To negotiate, arrange, or complete a deal or agreement. To give, offer, or allocate something to someone. To take action to manage or cope with a situation. To exchange or trade something for another thing. To reach an understanding or terms for a contract or arrangement.
example_sentence: The company plans to deal for the new contract next week. He had to deal for a fair price when buying the car. She knows how to deal for difficult situations calmly. They are trying to deal for better terms in the business agreement.

english_meaning: To trade, sell, or specialize in a particular product or service. To specialize in a certain type of business or activity. To engage in a particular kind of activity, sometimes professionally or habitually.
example_sentence: The company deals in organic teas and coffees. He deals in antiques and rare collectibles. She deals in software solutions for small businesses. Some journalists deal in investigative reporting and breaking

english_meaning: To distribute or give something to people. To hand out, assign, or give portions of something, often in a formal or organized way. It can also imply imposing something, such as punishment or criticism.
example_sentence: The teacher dealt out the worksheets to the students. During the meeting, he dealt out tasks to each team member. The commander dealt out severe punishment to the offenders. She dealt out advice to everyone who asked for it.

english_meaning: To take action to solve a problem, handle a situation, or manage someone or something. To handle or manage. It can also mean to give attention to something or resolve it.
example_sentence: I have to deal with many emails before I leave the office. She knows how to deal with difficult customers. The government is trying to deal with climate change. He couldn’t deal with the stress of his new job. Teams deal with emergencies. Reports deal with policy gaps. Researchers deal with uncertainty. Leaders deal with crises.

english_meaning: Showing strong emotional attachment or love. Very much or intensely, not always emotional. Suffering serious loss, punishment, or expense. Strongly felt sadness, usually after loss. Treated as something important or treasured.
example_sentence: She dearly loves her children. Your advice is dearly appreciated. They paid dearly for ignoring the warning. The community dearly mourned the loss of its leader. Freedom is dearly held by the people.

english_meaning: The quality of being dear, beloved, or precious. The state of being expensive or high in price (commonly used in economics).
example_sentence: All the efforts in procession and strikes went in vain to decrease the dearness. The dearness of his friends made him emotional. Due to the rising dearness, people are struggling to buy daily necessities. She spoke with dearness and affection in her voice. The dearness of goods has become a major economic issue.

english_meaning: A shortage, lack, or insufficient supply of something that is needed or desired. It refers to a situation where there is too little of something (especially food, resources, or skilled people).
example_sentence: There was a dearth of reliable information on the subject. There is a dearth of clean drinking water in many rural areas. The company failed because of a dearth of skilled workers. During the drought, farmers faced a dearth of rainfall. A dearth of good leadership can harm an organization.

english_meaning: The final struggles or agony before dying. The last violent movements or suffering of a dying being. The final stages of decline of something. The last painful phase before collapse or end. Intense final convulsions or difficulties.
example_sentence: The wounded soldier lay in his death throes on the battlefield. The empire was in its death throes before it finally collapsed. The old company is now in its death throes. The animal's death throes were painful to watch.

english_meaning: A complete failure, sudden collapse, or disaster. A situation that ends in a total defeat or embarrassment.
example_sentence: The company’s new product launch was a debacle; nothing worked as planned. The politician’s campaign ended in a debacle after multiple scandals. The match turned into a debacle when the team lost by 10 goals. Poor planning turned the festival into a complete debacle.

english_meaning: Excessive and immoral indulgence in sensual pleasures. Wild behavior involving heavy drinking, sexual excess, or other moral wrongdoing.
example_sentence: The novel describes a life of wealth and debauchery. The ruler’s debauchery angered the poor citizens. They rejected the party culture of drinking and debauchery. Years of debauchery damaged his health and reputation.

english_meaning: To make someone or something weak, feeble, or less effective; to reduce strength or energy. To weaken the physical strength, mental ability, or effectiveness of a person, organization, or system.
example_sentence: The long drought debilitated the entire farming community. A severe fever can debilitate even the strongest person. Corruption and mismanagement have debilitated the organization. Lack of proper nutrition debilitated the soldiers during the war.

english_meaning: Making someone or something weak, exhausted, or less able to function. Seriously reducing strength, energy, health, or effectiveness.
example_sentence: The illness was painful and debilitating. Long heat waves can be debilitating for older people. Stress had a debilitating effect on his work. She recovered slowly from a debilitating injury. Debilitating fatigue made simple tasks difficult.

english_meaning: Physical weakness, especially as a result of illness or old age. A state of being feeble and lacking strength or energy. A weakness or defect that reduces the effectiveness of something. Long-lasting frailty of the body or mind.
example_sentence: Months of illness left him in a state of complete debility. The doctor treated her general debility with proper nutrition. Old age brought increasing debility and fatigue. Financial debility forced the company to close two branches.

english_meaning: An amount of money taken out of a bank account. A record in an account showing money that has been spent or is owed. The left-hand side of an account book where payments and expenses are entered. To remove or deduct money from someone's bank account. A card that allows a customer to pay directly from their bank account.
example_sentence: The bank will debit the monthly fee from your account. There was an unexpected debit of two thousand rupees last week. He paid for the groceries with his debit card. Every debit must be balanced by a matching credit in the ledger.

english_meaning: Scattered pieces of broken material or remains after destruction or damage. Fragments, pieces, or remains of objects that are broken, destroyed, or scattered after events such as storms, earthquakes, explosions, accidents, or construction activities. It can include wood, metal, glass, soil, or other materials left behind after damage or collapse.
example_sentence: Rescue teams searched through the debris after the earthquake. The storm left a lot of debris on the roads and streets. Workers removed the debris from the collapsed building. Scientists track space debris to protect satellites.

english_meaning: Money that is owed by one person to another. Something, such as a favor or service, owed in return. A state of being under obligation to repay. A feeling of gratitude for help received from someone. A financial liability held by an individual, company, or country.
example_sentence: He worked two jobs to pay off his debt. The country is struggling under a huge national debt. I owe you a great debt for your kind help. She finally cleared all her old debts this year.

english_meaning: To show that something is less important, less good, or less true than it has been made to appear. Expose while ridiculing, especially of pretentious or false claims and ideas. To prove to be false.
example_sentence: The writer's aim was to debunk the myth that had grown up around the actress. Some advertising slogans should be debunked The newspaper debunked the youth cult as the tool of a foreign government.

english_meaning: A decimal prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of ten (101). Specifically used to signify ten units of a particular measure. A numerical element used in scientific and mathematical nomenclature to represent tenfold increases. A combining form derived from the Greek word 'deka' meaning ten. A scaling factor applied to base units like meters or liters to create larger denominations.
synonyms: ["Ten","Tenfold","Decimal","Denary","Decuple","Decagonal","Decenary","Decade","X","Tally of ten","Metric prefix","Power of ten","Numerical factor"]
example_sentence: A decagram is a unit of mass equal to ten grams. The decahedron is a solid geometric figure that possesses ten flat faces. Scientists use the prefix deca to denote a tenfold increase in a base metric unit. In ancient measurements, a decameter was often used to describe a length of ten meters.

english_meaning: A period of ten years. A set or group of ten items or units. A ten-year stage used to divide a century or a person's life. A long span of time measured in tens of years.
example_sentence: Technology has changed dramatically over the past decade. She spent a decade working as a teacher. The city grew rapidly during the last decade. It took nearly a decade to complete the project.

english_meaning: Moral or cultural decline, especially after a period of high achievement. Excessive indulgence in luxury and pleasure. A state of low moral standards and self-indulgence. The process of falling into decay or deterioration.
example_sentence: Historians describe the decadence of the late empire. He criticized the decadence of modern consumer culture. The novel portrays wealth, decadence, and decline. Decadence slowly weakened the ruling class.

english_meaning: Showing moral or cultural decline. Characterized by excessive luxury and self-indulgence. Rich and indulgent, especially of food. A person who lives a life of luxury and low moral standards.
example_sentence: They served a decadent chocolate cake after dinner. The film shows the decadent lifestyle of the elite. Critics called the era decadent and wasteful. He was seen as a decadent among serious reformers.

english_meaning: A ten-sided polygon with ten angles. A geometric shape with ten straight sides and ten vertices. Any flat shape with ten corners and ten edges.
example_sentence: A regular decagon has ten equal sides and angles. The fountain base was designed as a decagon. Students learned to construct a decagon using geometric tools. The medal was shaped like a beautiful decagon.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to 10 grams. One hundredth of a kilogram. A small unit used for weighing light items or ingredients.
example_sentence: A decagram is equal to ten grams. The chemist weighed one decagram of the powder. Add two decagrams of butter to the mixture. The label shows the weight in decagrams.

english_meaning: A metric unit of length equal to ten meters. A measure written as dam, used mainly in surveying and land measurement. Ten times the length of one meter.
example_sentence: The field is about twelve decameters long. One decameter equals ten meters. Surveyors sometimes record distances in decameters. He converted the reading from decameters into kilometers.

english_meaning: To cut off the head of a person or animal. To behead. To remove the top or upper part of something. To destroy the leadership of an organization by removing its top people. Used both literally for cutting off heads and figuratively for eliminating leaders or upper sections.
example_sentence: In ancient times, prisoners of war were sometimes decapitated by the king's order. The storm decapitated several tall trees in the area. The military operation aimed to decapitate the terrorist organization. The executioner was ordered to decapitate the condemned man at dawn. A sudden gust of wind decapitated the flowers in the garden.

english_meaning: The gradual deterioration or decline of something. The process by which dead organic matter decomposes. The weakening or reduction of strength, quality, health, or influence. In science, the transformation or breakdown of radioactive substances. The state of being neglected and falling into ruin.
example_sentence: The old wooden fence began to decay after years of exposure to rain. Poor maintenance led to the decay of the historic building. Fallen leaves decay and enrich the soil with nutrients. Scientists study how radioactive materials decay over time.

english_meaning: The death of a person. The permanent stopping of all the vital bodily activities. To stop living.
example_sentence: He died at Munich on the 7th of June 1826, and was buried near Reichenbach, whose decease had taken place eight years previously.

english_meaning: Dead. A person who has died recently. No longer living. A dead person.
example_sentence: Her deceased parents. The recently deceased tenant was found by a concerned neighbor. His mother is now sadly deceased. her recently deceased husband

english_meaning: Dishonest behavior that is intended to make somebody believe something that is not true, an example of this behavior.
example_sentence: He was accused of lies and deceit. Everyone was involved in this web of deceit. Their marriage was an illusion and a deceit. She realized that their whole relationship had been based on lies and deceit.

english_meaning: To cause to accept as true or valid what is false or invalid. To refuse to admit to yourself that something unpleasant is true. To make somebody have a wrong idea about somebody, something.
example_sentence: Her husband had been deceiving her for years. She deceived him into handing over all his savings. The insurance company deceived me when they told me they were covering my house.

english_meaning: A person who deliberately misleads or tricks others. Someone who tells lies to gain an advantage. An individual who creates a false impression to cheat others. A person who is dishonest or fraudulent in dealings. One who betrays trust through falsehood.
example_sentence: The deceiver was finally caught and sent to prison. She realized too late that he was nothing but a deceiver. History has judged him as a clever deceiver. A skilled deceiver can hide his true intentions for years.

english_meaning: To slow down or reduce speed. To make a vehicle, process, rate, or movement slower.
example_sentence: The driver had to decelerate before the sharp turn. Economic growth may decelerate next year. The train began to decelerate near the station. Good brakes help a bicycle decelerate safely. The spacecraft must decelerate before landing.

english_meaning: Honest polite behavior that follows accepted moral standards and shows respect, Standards of behavior in society that people think are acceptable
example_sentence: Her behavior showed a total lack of common decency. Have you no sense of decency? He might have had the decency to apologize.

english_meaning: The act of hiding the truth, especially to get an advantage. Dishonest or illegal methods that are used to get something, or to make people believe that something is true when it is not.
example_sentence: He was found guilty of obtaining money by deception. The couple were accused of obtaining money by deception. The Insolvency Act makes stringent provision for company fraud and deception.

english_meaning: Likely to make you believe something that is not true. Tending or having power to deceive. Given to or marked by cheating and deception.
example_sentence: The firm was found guilty of publishing a misleading and deceptive advertisement.

english_meaning: A decimal prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one-tenth (10⁻¹). One-tenth part of a specific unit of measurement. A prefix used to indicate division by ten. A numerical combining form derived from the Latin 'decimus' meaning tenth. A standard SI prefix utilized to scale units downwards for smaller measurements.
synonyms: ["Tenth","One-Tenth","0.1","10-1","Tithe","Decimal Part","Submultiple","Fraction","Tenth Part","Diminutive Prefix","Metric Step","Small Fraction","Fractional Unit"]
example_sentence: A deciliter is exactly one-tenth of a standard liter. Scientists often use the decibel to measure the intensity of sound relative to a reference level. The decimeter is a common unit of length in some regions for school measurements. Converting a value to its deci-prefix equivalent involves moving the decimal point one place to the left.

english_meaning: A logarithmic unit used to express the ratio of two values of a physical quantity. A measurement of sound intensity or electrical power levels. A degree of loudness that compares a sound to a reference level. A unit representing one-tenth of a bel. A mathematical scale used to measure signal-to-noise ratios in electronics. A way to describe the relative power or voltage of an acoustic signal.
synonyms: ["Sound Level","Acoustic Unit","Loudness Measure","Power Ratio","Bel Fraction","Intensity Unit","Volume Level","Signal Strength","Auditory Degree","Sonic Scale","Audio Metric","dB Unit","Electronic Ratio","Magnitude"]
example_sentence: The loud music reached a dangerous decibel level at the concert. Every ten decibel increase represents a tenfold increase in sound intensity. Engineers use the decibel scale to measure signal loss in cables. Prolonged exposure to high decibel noise can lead to permanent hearing damage.

english_meaning: To make a final choice or judgment after considering options.
example_sentence: They decided upon a new plan. I can’t decide upon which course to take. We finally decided upon the blue design. She decided upon a career in medicine.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to one tenth of a gram. A very small unit used in laboratories and pharmacies. A unit equal to 100 milligrams.
example_sentence: A decigram is one tenth of a gram. The sample weighed only two decigrams. Chemists often record results in decigrams. He measured a decigram of the fine powder.

english_meaning: A metric unit of volume equal to one-tenth of a liter. A capacity measurement equivalent to 100 cubic centimeters. A volume of liquid roughly equal to 3·38 fluid ounces in the US system. A decimal fraction of the base unit liter used in scientific and culinary contexts. A specific measure often used in medical blood tests and chemical analysis. A quantity representing 0·1 liters in the International System of Units.
synonyms: ["Tenth Of A Liter","100 Milliliters","0.1 Liters","10 Centiliters","Metric Volume Unit","Liquid Measure","Capacity Unit","100 Cubic Centimeters","0.211 Pints","3.38 Fluid Ounces","Metric Capacity","Measurement Unit","Scientific Volume","Small Liquid Volume"]
antonyms: ["Dekaliter","Hectoliter","Kiloliter","Ten Liters","Hundred Liters","Thousand Liters","Large Volume","Solid Measure","Mass Unit","Infinite Volume"]
example_sentence: The medical report indicated the glucose levels per deciliter of blood. Please measure exactly one deciliter of water for this chemical reaction. The chef added a deciliter of cream to thicken the gourmet sauce. Converting liters to deciliters requires multiplying the value by ten.

english_meaning: To kill, destroy, or remove a large percentage or part of something. Historically, it referred to the practice of killing one in every ten of a group of soldiers as a punishment. In modern usage, it implies drastic reduction or severe damage to a population or system.
example_sentence: The disease threatened to decimate the entire population of the island. A severe drought could decimate the region's agricultural output this year. The budget cuts will decimate the funding for local community projects. The army was decimated during the long and brutal winter campaign.

english_meaning: The killing or destruction of a large proportion of a group or species. It is the act of drastically reducing the strength or number of something. This term is often used in the context of ecology, warfare, or economics to describe catastrophic loss.
example_sentence: The decimation of the forest led to the extinction of several bird species. Economic policies led to the decimation of the local manufacturing industry. Historians documented the decimation of the tribe during the colonial era. The decimation of the team's starting lineup due to injuries was a major setback.

english_meaning: A metric unit of length equal to one tenth of a meter. A measure equal to ten centimeters, written as dm. A small unit of length used in scientific and technical measurement.
synonyms: ["dm","Tenth of a meter","Metric length unit","Ten centimeters"]
example_sentence: One decimeter is equal to ten centimeters. The box measures four decimeters in width. Students converted decimeters into meters during the lesson. A cubic decimeter of water is exactly one liter.

english_meaning: To succeed in understanding, interpreting, or identifying something that is difficult to read or understand. This often refers to converting a text written in code or cipher into normal language. It also applies to making sense of messy handwriting or a complex situation.
example_sentence: The archaeologist worked for years to decipher the ancient stone inscriptions. It was nearly impossible to decipher his messy handwriting on the prescription. Can you decipher the hidden meaning behind his cryptic remarks? Specialists are trying to decipher the encrypted data found on the computer.

english_meaning: Very important for the final result of a particular situation. Able to make decisions quickly and confidently, or showing this quality. Making choices quickly and surely, without having any doubts.
example_sentence: She is a decisive leader who acts confidently in difficult situations. The decisive vote ended the long debate in the meeting. His decisive action saved the company from serious loss. Weather conditions played a decisive role in the success of the mission.

english_meaning: In a firm and determined manner. In a way that settles a question or result clearly. Quickly and with confidence.
example_sentence: The team won decisively by four goals. She answered the question decisively. The army acted decisively to end the conflict. He spoke decisively in the meeting.

english_meaning: The ability to make decisions quickly and firmly. The quality of settling matters with confidence.
example_sentence: Her decisiveness saved the company from loss. A good leader needs decisiveness in a crisis. His decisiveness impressed the board. Lack of decisiveness delayed the project.

english_meaning: A flat surface or floor of a ship, bus, or building. A pack of playing cards. A platform or outdoor floor. To decorate, furnish, or knock someone down informally.
example_sentence: We stood on the deck and watched the sea. Shuffle the deck before dealing the cards. They built a wooden deck behind the house. The hall was decked with flowers. One punch nearly decked him.

english_meaning: Wooden or composite boards used to build an outdoor platform. The material forming the floor of a deck. The act of decorating or knocking down, informal.
example_sentence: They installed new decking around the pool. The garden decking needs a fresh coat of oil. We sat on the decking enjoying the evening sun. He slipped on the wet decking after the rain.

english_meaning: A formal or explicit statement or announcement. An official or public statement of intentions, terms, or beliefs. The act of declaring or proclaiming something. A written statement submitted to authorities. A formal assertion of facts or claims.
example_sentence: The Declaration of Independence was signed in seventeen seventy-six. He made a declaration of his intentions to run for office. Customs requires a declaration of all goods. Her declaration of love surprised everyone.

english_meaning: Having the form or function of making a statement rather than asking a question or giving a command. Serving to declare, announce, or state something clearly and openly. In grammar, describing a sentence that states a fact or opinion and normally ends with a full stop. In computing, describing a style of programming in which the desired result is described rather than the steps to achieve it. A declarative sentence or statement itself.
example_sentence: A declarative sentence always ends with a full stop. The teacher explained the difference between declarative and interrogative forms. His declarative tone left no room for argument. Modern web developers often prefer a declarative style of coding.

english_meaning: To announce or state something formally or officially. To make something known publicly or openly. To assert or proclaim with confidence. To state goods or income for tax or customs purposes. To reveal or make evident.
example_sentence: The president declared a state of emergency. She declared her candidacy for mayor. You must declare all income on your tax return. He declared his love for her in front of everyone.

english_meaning: To state publicly that one is opposed to something or someone. To announce one's opposition to a plan, policy, decision, or candidate. To take a clear public stand rejecting an idea or course of action. To speak out openly in criticism of something.
example_sentence: Several members declared against the new tax proposal. The union declared against the management's decision. She declared against the war in a powerful speech. Two senior leaders have already declared against the bill.

english_meaning: To state publicly that one supports someone or something. To announce one's backing for a candidate, party, policy, or cause. To formally choose a side or option in a contest or debate. In sport, to announce an intention to take part or to end an innings.
example_sentence: The governor declared for the reform package yesterday. Most of the delegates declared for the younger candidate. He finally declared for his old political party. The court declared for the plaintiff after a long hearing.

english_meaning: Made known formally or officially. Announced or stated openly and publicly. Acknowledged or admitted openly. Having been proclaimed or asserted. Officially recognized or announced.
example_sentence: The government declared a state of emergency. She was declared the winner of the competition. He declared his assets as required by law. War was declared after the attack.

english_meaning: To become smaller, weaker, worse, or less. To politely refuse. A downward slope or gradual deterioration. To change word forms in grammar.
example_sentence: Sales began to decline after winter. She declined the invitation politely. The village is in slow decline. His health declined during the long illness. Students learned how to decline Latin nouns.

english_meaning: To organize a messy place. To remove unwanted belongings. To simplify a space. To tidy up a room or workplace. To clear unnecessary digital files or emails. To create a neat and peaceful environment. To reduce distractions. To simplify one's lifestyle.
example_sentence: I decided to declutter my bedroom before buying new furniture. She spent the weekend decluttering her office to improve productivity. We should declutter our computer by deleting old files and unused programs. Decluttering your home can reduce stress and make daily life more comfortable.

english_meaning: To extract the essence of something by boiling it. To boil a substance, usually herbs or plant material, in water to extract its medicinal or essential properties. It is commonly used in traditional medicine and herbal preparations.
example_sentence: The herbalist decocted the roots to prepare a healing drink. She decocts dried leaves to make traditional tea. The medicine is made by decocting bark in hot water. He decocted the mixture until it became thick and concentrated.

english_meaning: A liquid made by boiling plant materials such as herbs, bark, or roots in water to extract their essence.
example_sentence: The doctor advised her to drink a ginger decoction for her sore throat. The herbalist prepared a decoction of neem leaves to treat skin problems. After boiling the roots for an hour, the decoction was ready to use. The soup tasted like a strange decoction of unfamiliar spices.

english_meaning: To rot or decay naturally (especially organic matter). To separate something into simpler components. To analyze something by breaking it into parts. In science, to break a compound into elements.
example_sentence: Leaves decompose quickly in wet soil. Scientists decompose the compound into simpler elements. The old food started to decompose in the kitchen. We decompose the problem into smaller parts to solve it easily.

english_meaning: To make something look more attractive by adding extra items or images. To confer an award or honor on someone, especially in the military.
example_sentence: We plan to decorate the living room with new curtains and paint. The children helped decorate the Christmas tree with handmade ornaments. The soldier was decorated for his bravery during the difficult rescue mission. She likes to decorate cakes with intricate patterns of icing.

english_meaning: The process or art of decorating something. A thing that serves as an ornament; a medal or award.
example_sentence: The wall decoration consisted of framed photos and vintage maps. She received a high military decoration for her service abroad. We spent the afternoon putting up decorations for the birthday party. The interior decoration of the palace was incredibly opulent and detailed.

english_meaning: Serving to make something look more attractive; ornamental. Providing decoration.
example_sentence: The vase is purely decorative and cannot hold water effectively. They added decorative tiles to the bathroom to enhance its appearance. Decorative lighting was installed throughout the garden for the party. She enjoys creating decorative items using recycled materials.

english_meaning: A person whose job is to decorate the interior of buildings. A person who paints and wallpapers rooms professionally. Someone who adds ornaments, colors, or visual details to objects, spaces, food, or events. In computing, a function or design pattern that adds behavior or features to another function, class, or object without changing its basic structure.
example_sentence: We hired a decorator to redesign the living room. The cake decorator created delicate sugar flowers. A professional decorator painted every room in the hotel. In Python, the decorator adds logging to the function.

english_meaning: Polite, proper, and in good taste. Behaving with dignity and respect for social conventions. Appropriate to a formal situation or occasion. Modest, restrained, and unlikely to cause offense or embarrassment.
example_sentence: Everyone maintained a decorous silence during the memorial. Her decorous manner impressed the interview panel. The restaurant offers a quiet and decorous setting. They reached a decorous compromise without public argument.

english_meaning: In a polite, proper, and socially acceptable manner. With dignity, good taste, and respect for convention. In a way appropriate to a formal occasion or setting. Modestly and without causing offense or embarrassment.
example_sentence: The guests behaved decorously throughout the ceremony. She was decorously dressed for the formal reception. The disagreement was discussed quietly and decorously. He bowed decorously before leaving the room.

english_meaning: Behaviour in keeping with good taste and propriety. Etiquette and dignified conduct. Proper, polite, and respectable behaviour. Adherence to social rules and customs in speech, dress, or manner.
example_sentence: The judge demanded complete decorum in the courtroom. Guests were expected to maintain proper decorum during the ceremony. His behaviour at the meeting showed a lack of decorum. She always speaks with great decorum and respect. The school strictly enforces decorum among its students.

english_meaning: The decorative art of cutting out paper pictures or designs and gluing them onto an object. An object or surface decorated with pasted paper cutouts, often finished with layers of varnish. The technique or finished work produced by this method.
example_sentence: She decorated the wooden box with floral decoupage. The class learned how to make decoupage using old magazines. A layer of varnish protected the decoupage on the table. The museum displayed an eighteenth-century decoupage screen.

english_meaning: To separate two things that are connected, linked, or dependent on each other. To make one process or system operate independently of another. To reduce or remove the connection between economic growth and resource use or environmental harm. In electronics or engineering, to prevent unwanted transfer of energy or signals between circuits or components.
example_sentence: The company plans to decouple salaries from short-term sales figures. Engineers used a capacitor to decouple the two circuits. We must decouple economic growth from rising carbon emissions. The new design decouples the screen from the main control unit.

english_meaning: A person, animal, object, or imitation used to lure someone or something into a trap. Something used to distract attention from the real target, purpose, or activity. A model bird or animal used to attract live game. To lure, mislead, or draw someone away by using a decoy.
example_sentence: The police used an empty van as a decoy. Wooden ducks served as decoys on the lake. The first email was a decoy designed to distract the security team. The thieves decoyed the guard away from the entrance.

english_meaning: To become smaller or fewer in size, amount, number, strength, value, or intensity. To make something smaller or less. A reduction or downward change in quantity, rate, degree, or level. The amount by which something becomes smaller.
example_sentence: Temperatures will decrease after sunset. The new system should decrease waiting times. The report shows a sharp decrease in road accidents. There was a ten percent decrease in monthly expenses.

english_meaning: To officially order, decide, or declare something by authority. A decision believed to be made by divine will. An official order issued by a legal authority, government, or court. A final judgment of a civil court that determines the rights of the parties.
example_sentence: The government decreed a state of emergency. We cannot decree what the committee should do. It was decreed that the following day would be a holiday. He has been governing by emergency decree under the provisions of the constitution. The president issued a decree prohibiting trade unions.

english_meaning: A final legal order that formally ends a marriage under the former divorce terminology of England and Wales. The final stage of a divorce following a decree nisi, after which the parties are legally free to remarry. A conclusive court decree with full legal effect. Now generally called a final order in England and Wales.
example_sentence: The marriage legally ended when the court issued the decree absolute. She applied for the decree absolute several weeks after the earlier order. Neither party could remarry before receiving the decree absolute. Older case files refer to the final divorce order as a decree absolute.

english_meaning: Very old and weak. A person, animal, or building that has become very weak, damaged, or worn out because of age, illness, or long use.
example_sentence: The decrepit old man needed help to walk across the road. They decided to demolish the decrepit building because it was unsafe. The hospital still used decrepit equipment from decades ago. After years of neglect, the house looked dark and decrepit.

english_meaning: The state of being old, weak, worn out, or in serious disrepair. Physical weakness and decline caused by old age. A condition of deterioration in a building, institution, system, or object. Extreme feebleness or dilapidation.
example_sentence: Years of neglect left the mansion in a state of decrepitude. Despite his physical decrepitude, his mind remained sharp. The report exposed the decrepitude of the city’s water system. The old bridge showed clear signs of decrepitude.

english_meaning: The act or process of removing criminal penalties from an action or conduct. A legal change under which an act is no longer treated as a crime, although it may still be regulated or subject to civil penalties. The policy of reducing criminal punishment without necessarily making an activity fully legal.
example_sentence: The council debated the decriminalization of minor offenses. Decriminalization does not always mean that an activity becomes completely legal. Supporters say decriminalization could reduce pressure on the courts. The study examined the effects of drug decriminalization on public health.

english_meaning: To remove criminal penalties from an action, possession, or conduct. To change the law so that something is no longer treated as a criminal offense. To replace criminal punishment with regulation, civil penalties, treatment, or no penalty. Not necessarily to make something fully legal or unrestricted.
example_sentence: Several groups want the government to decriminalize the minor offense. The proposal would decriminalize possession of a very small amount. Lawmakers voted to decriminalize conduct that had rarely been prosecuted. To decriminalize an act is not always to permit it without regulation.

english_meaning: To openly and strongly criticize something because you believe it is wrong, harmful, unfair, or unacceptable. It is often used in formal or public contexts such as politics, social issues, policies, or public behavior.
example_sentence: Many citizens decry corruption in government offices. Environmental groups decry the destruction of forests. Teachers decried the sudden change in the examination policy. The community decried the unfair treatment of workers.

english_meaning: To convert secret or coded information into readable or understandable form. To unlock, decode, or translate encrypted information, messages, files, or data so that it can be understood. It is commonly used in computer security, communication systems, and secret codes.
example_sentence: The engineer decrypted the secured file successfully. Police experts decrypted the secret message quickly. The software can decrypt protected data in seconds. Scientists decrypted the ancient coded manuscript after many years.

english_meaning: Converting coded, encrypted, or hidden information back into its original readable form. The process of unlocking or decoding protected information by using a key, password, software, or method so the original message or data can be understood. It is commonly used in computer security, banking systems, messaging apps, military communication, and digital privacy.
example_sentence: The technician completed the decryption of the secured file successfully. Decryption helps users read encrypted messages safely. The police used advanced software for the decryption of hidden data. Without the correct password, decryption of the document was impossible.

english_meaning: Ten times as many or as much. Consisting of ten parts, members, or elements. A group or amount of ten. To make or become ten times as great or numerous.
example_sentence: The survey used a decuple set of ten indicators. The audience grew to decuple its former size. Automation may decuple the team's processing speed. The researcher arranged the samples in a decuple group.

english_meaning: To commit yourself completely to a task, goal, cause, or responsibility. To spend time, effort, and energy on achieving something. To officially present, honor, or devote a book, building, performance, or work to a person. To reserve something for a particular purpose.
example_sentence: She dedicated her life to helping poor children. The author dedicated his new book to his parents. He dedicates several hours each day to learning English. The hospital was dedicated to serving the local community.

english_meaning: Committed, devoted, loyal, hardworking, and focused on a particular task, purpose, person, or goal. A person who is highly committed and loyal to a duty, goal, profession, cause, or person. It can also refer to something specially designed or intended for a particular purpose.
example_sentence: She is a dedicated teacher who always helps her students. The dedicated team worked day and night to complete the project. He remained dedicated to his goals despite many difficulties. This computer is dedicated to graphic design work.

english_meaning: Strong commitment to a goal or activity. Act of devoting time, effort, or oneself to something. Formal opening statement in a book, speech, or work. Religious or ceremonial act of offering something to a sacred purpose.
example_sentence: Her dedication to her studies helped her achieve top grades. The team showed great dedication during the final match. His dedication to helping poor people is inspiring. The book contains a dedication to his parents.

english_meaning: To reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence, facts, or general principles. To infer or work out logically.
example_sentence: From the footprints, we can deduce that someone entered the room. She deduced the answer from two clues. Scientists deduce causes from careful observation. It is wrong to deduce too much from one example. He deduced that the train had already left.

english_meaning: To take away an amount or part from a total. To subtract a sum, especially from wages, taxes, or a bill.
example_sentence: The employer will deduct tax from your salary. Please deduct the discount from the total bill. Ten marks were deducted for late submission. They deducted the loan installment automatically. Charges will be deducted from your account each month.

english_meaning: Acts or actions, especially important, brave, legal, or moral acts. Written legal documents that prove ownership or transfer of property.
example_sentence: Good deeds are remembered long after words are forgotten. The lawyer checked the deeds of the house. His brave deeds became part of village history. People judged him by his deeds, not his promises. The charity records every donor's deeds of service.

english_meaning: To consider or judge something in a particular way. To form an opinion or judgment about something, especially after thinking carefully or based on authority, belief, or assumption
example_sentence: The court deemed the evidence insufficient. She was deemed responsible for the project’s success. His behavior was deemed unacceptable by the committee. The teacher deemed the answer correct.

english_meaning: The act of damaging the good reputation of someone through false statements. Communication of false information that harms another person's character. Slander or libel that lowers a person's standing in society. A false statement, spoken or written, that injures someone's reputation.
example_sentence: He filed a lawsuit for defamation against the newspaper. Spreading false rumors is a form of defamation. The politician accused his rival of defamation. Defamation cases can lead to heavy fines in court.

english_meaning: To ruin someone’s public image. To damage a person’s reputation. To spread harmful false information. To speak badly about someone unfairly. To disgrace a person publicly.
example_sentence: The politician claimed that the newspaper tried to defame him with false allegations. Spreading fake rumors on social media can defame innocent people. He filed a case against those who attempted to defame his reputation. It is wrong to defame someone without knowing the truth.

english_meaning: Someone or something that can become weary, exhausted, or worn out after prolonged work, exercise, stress, or activity. It is the opposite of indefatigable, which means "never seeming to get tired".
example_sentence: Unlike his partner, he was quite defatigable and needed frequent breaks. Human beings are inherently defatigable and require sufficient sleep. The marathon showed just how defatigable the untrained runners were. As a defatigable worker, she could only focus for two hours at a time.

english_meaning: To pass waste matter from the body through the anus.  To remove solid waste from the digestive system through the anus. To empty or cleanse of impurities in a general sense. In older usage, to purify or clear something unwanted. In biology, to eliminate waste materials from an organism.
example_sentence: The baby began to defecate shortly after feeding. Animals usually defecate in open areas. Doctors asked the patient if he could defecate normally. Some medicines can make it easier to defecate.

english_meaning: The act of passing waste matter from the bowels. Defecation is the natural biological process in which solid waste, called feces or stool, is expelled from the body through the anus. It is an important function of the digestive system and helps remove undigested food and harmful substances from the body.
example_sentence: Proper hydration helps maintain regular defecation. The doctor asked about the patient's defecation habits. Pain during defecation can be a sign of a medical problem. Diet plays an important role in healthy defecation.

english_meaning: To throw someone or something out of a window. It can also be used figuratively to mean to abruptly remove someone from a position of power or authority.
example_sentence: The angry mob threatened to defenestrate the tyrant. He was effectively defenestrated from his position as CEO. The rioters defenestrated furniture during the protest. The politician was defenestrated by his own party.

english_meaning: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window. By extension, the sudden removal of a person from office, power, or position.
example_sentence: The defenestration in the old story shocked the court. Historians discuss the Defenestration of Prague. The joke described his firing as a corporate defenestration. No one expected such a sudden defenestration of the minister. The word sounds dramatic because the act is dramatic.

english_meaning: Without protection or the means of defending oneself. Weak and open to attack or harm. Unable to resist criticism, danger, or force. Helpless and vulnerable.
example_sentence: The village was left defenseless after the troops withdrew. A newborn animal is completely defenseless. He felt defenseless against so many accusations. Defenseless civilians suffered the most in the conflict.

english_meaning: To put off or postpone something to a later time. To delay an action, decision, or event. To yield respectfully to another person’s opinion, wishes, or authority. Commonly used in two senses: postponing tasks or payments, and showing polite respect by submitting to someone else’s judgement.
example_sentence: The meeting was deferred until next Monday due to the storm. Students may defer their admission for one academic year. I will defer to your expertise in this matter. He decided to defer payment of the loan for six months. The court agreed to defer the hearing to a later date.

english_meaning: Respectful submission to the wishes, opinions, authority, or status of another person. Polite regard shown through behavior or speech.
example_sentence: She spoke with deference to the elders. Out of deference to his teacher, he remained silent. The judge was treated with formal deference. Deference should not become blind obedience. He showed deference without losing his own opinion.

english_meaning: Showing polite respect towards someone, especially a senior person. Willing to yield to the opinions or wishes of others out of respect. Marked by courteous submission or humility. Behaving in a way that acknowledges another's higher status.
example_sentence: He was polite and deferential towards his teachers. She spoke in a deferential tone to the elderly guests. The staff were unusually deferential to the visiting director. His deferential manner impressed the committee.

english_meaning: Open resistance or bold disobedience. A refusal to obey, submit, or accept authority, rules, threats, or expectations.
example_sentence: He raised his voice in defiance of the order. The protest was an act of peaceful defiance. Her eyes flashed with defiance. Defiance of safety rules can be dangerous. The city stood in defiance against the invaders.

english_meaning: Openly resisting or refusing to obey authority. Showing bold disobedience or challenge. Displaying a strong and fearless attitude against control. Refusing to accept rules, orders, or opposition.
example_sentence: The defiant child refused to listen to his parents. She gave a defiant look to the officer. The protesters remained defiant despite the warnings. His defiant tone shocked the audience.

english_meaning: Lack or shortage of something. A state in which something is missing, inadequate, or insufficient. It can refer to a shortage in quantity, quality, or a necessary element. Often used in medical, nutritional, or general contexts.
example_sentence: The patient suffers from a vitamin D deficiency. There is a deficiency of skilled workers in the region. Her argument showed a deficiency in logical reasoning. The report highlighted deficiencies in the safety procedures.

english_meaning: Not having enough of something. Lacking quality, quantity, skill, or requirement. A person, thing, system, or condition that lacks something important, necessary, or sufficient. It may refer to shortage, weakness, incompleteness, or poor performance.
example_sentence: The report was deficient in important details. Many children are deficient in vitamins due to poor diet. His knowledge of mathematics is deficient. The school building is deficient in safety measures.

english_meaning: A shortage or lack of something, especially money. Financial loss or shortfall. Lack of resources. Insufficient amount. Gap between demand and supply.
example_sentence: The country is facing a large budget deficit this year. There is a deficit of clean drinking water in rural areas. His sleep deficit affected his performance at work. The company reduced its deficit by cutting unnecessary costs.

english_meaning: To damage the purity or appearance of something, often making it foul or dirty. It can also mean to desecrate something sacred or to spoil the reputation of a person or thing. The term is frequently used in both physical and moral contexts.
example_sentence: The river was defiled by toxic waste from the nearby industrial factories. Protesters were arrested for attempting to defile the national monument with graffiti. He felt that the scandalous rumors would defile his family’s honorable name. No one should be allowed to defile such a sacred place of worship.

english_meaning: Able to be defined, explained, described, or given clear limits. Having a meaning, boundary, or nature that can be stated clearly.
example_sentence: The term is definable only in context. A good goal should be clear and definable. The illness has no easily definable cause. Their duties are definable in the contract. Love is real, though not always neatly definable.

english_meaning: Clearly stated or decided; not vague. Certain and unlikely to change. Having exact and observable limits. Free from doubt or ambiguity.
example_sentence: We need a definite answer by tomorrow. There has been a definite improvement in her health. The teacher gave definite instructions. He has a definite plan for the future.

english_meaning: Without any doubt. In a clear and certain manner. Used to emphasize agreement or certainty. Absolutely and firmly.
example_sentence: I will definitely attend the meeting tomorrow. She is definitely one of the best students in class. The movie was definitely worth watching. He definitely knows what he is doing.

english_meaning: Final, complete, authoritative, and not needing further change. Providing a clear and reliable answer. Best, most complete, or most accepted of its kind.
example_sentence: The report gives a definitive answer to the question. This is the definitive edition of the book. We need definitive proof before acting. Her goal in the final minute was definitive. The doctor could not give a definitive diagnosis yet.

english_meaning: To release air or gas from a tire, balloon, or similar object so it becomes smaller or collapses. To reduce the confidence, pride, or strength of someone or something; to make someone feel less important or less confident. In finance or economics, to reduce the level of prices or money supply.
example_sentence: He deflated the balloon before storing it. The criticism deflated her confidence. The tire slowly deflated after the puncture. The government’s policy deflated the housing market.

english_meaning: A decrease in the general level of prices. A reduction in air, size, confidence, value, or force. The act of letting air out of something inflated.
example_sentence: Deflation can make people delay spending. The tire showed signs of slow deflation. The bad review caused a deflation of his confidence. Economists debated the risk of deflation. Balloon deflation is normal after a party.

english_meaning: To clear an area of its trees and forest cover. To cut down forests, especially on a large scale. To strip land of woodland for farming, mining, or building. To remove natural vegetation from a region.
example_sentence: Companies continue to deforest the hillsides for timber. Farmers deforest land to grow more crops. It is illegal to deforest protected reserves. Once you deforest a slope, erosion soon follows.

english_meaning: The large-scale cutting down or clearing of forests. The permanent removal of tree cover from an area. A major environmental problem contributing to climate change and soil erosion. The loss of woodland caused by human activity.
example_sentence: Deforestation is destroying habitats across the region. Heavy deforestation has increased the risk of floods. The report links deforestation with rising temperatures. Laws were passed to slow deforestation in the north.

english_meaning: To spoil the natural shape or form of something. To become misshapen or distorted. To change the appearance of something for the worse. In physics, to alter the shape of a material under stress.
example_sentence: Heat can deform plastic pipes very quickly. The disease began to deform his fingers. Heavy loads deform the metal beams over time. Rough handling deformed the wheel of the bicycle.

english_meaning: The action of changing or spoiling the shape of something. A change in shape or size caused by applied force. The condition of being distorted or misshapen. A harmful alteration of an original form or structure.
example_sentence: Engineers measured the deformation of the steel beam. Deformation of the tyre showed it was overloaded. The illness caused a slight deformation of the bone. Heat treatment reduces deformation in the mould.

english_meaning: Having an abnormal or distorted shape. Spoiled in form or appearance. Twisted or misshapen as a result of injury, disease, or pressure. Not conforming to the normal or expected structure.
example_sentence: The tree grew deformed because of constant wind. He was born with a deformed left foot. Fire left the metal frame badly deformed. Deformed fruit is often sold at a lower price.

english_meaning: A physical condition in which a part of the body is not the normal shape. The state of being disfigured or misshapen in appearance. A moral or mental blemish or distortion of character. An irregularity in the structural form of an object or landscape. The result of injury, disease, or birth defect that alters physical symmetry.
example_sentence: The surgery was performed to correct a congenital deformity of the foot. The intense heat caused a permanent deformity in the plastic structure. He looked past her physical deformity to see her kind heart. Historical biases often viewed physical deformity as a sign of bad luck.

english_meaning: To illegally take money or property from someone by deception. To cheat a person or organisation out of something that belongs to them. To obtain a benefit dishonestly by using tricks, lies, or false documents. To deprive someone of a right or possession through fraud.
example_sentence: He was jailed for trying to defraud the company of millions. They used fake invoices to defraud the government. She was accused of defrauding elderly customers. The scheme was designed to defraud investors.

english_meaning: Skillful, quick, and clever in movement or action. Demonstrating skill, precision, and agility in performing tasks, especially with hands or mind. Can describe someone who handles situations or objects with ease and competence.
example_sentence: He gave a deft performance on the piano. The pianist’s deft fingers moved across the keys with grace. She gave a deft reply that silenced the critics. The chef prepared the meal with deft hands. He handled the delicate negotiations in a deft manner.

english_meaning: Skillfully and quickly in movement or action. Performed with dexterity, cleverness, and precision. Showing neat skill in handling tasks, tools, or situations.
example_sentence: She deftly avoided the oncoming cyclist. The chef deftly chopped the vegetables without a single mistake. He handled the delicate negotiations deftly, avoiding any conflict. The magician deftly performed the card trick, leaving everyone amazed.

english_meaning: No longer existing, operating, or functioning. Having ceased to work or be used. Describing an organisation or business that has closed down. Dead or extinct.
example_sentence: The company has been defunct for over a decade. He found an old map published by a defunct society. The defunct factory now stands empty. They revived a defunct tradition from the village.
