english_meaning: To stop providing money or financial support to an organisation or programme. To withdraw funding as a political or administrative decision. To reduce the budget of a public body significantly. To cut off the financial resources needed for something to continue.
synonyms: ["Cut funding","Withdraw support","Discontinue","Starve of funds","Slash budget","Withhold money"]
example_sentence: The government threatened to defund the programme. Activists campaigned to defund the project entirely. Schools suffered after the council decided to defund them. Lawmakers voted to defund the agency next year.

english_meaning: To remove the fuse from a bomb so that it cannot explode. To make a dangerous or tense situation calmer and less harmful. To reduce anger, stress, or hostility in a conflict. To make something less likely to cause trouble.
example_sentence: Experts were called to defuse the bomb safely. She managed to defuse the argument with a joke. The talks helped defuse tension between the two countries. A calm response can quickly defuse an angry customer.

english_meaning: To openly resist or refuse to obey someone or something. To boldly oppose, challenge, or refuse to obey rules, authority, or expectations. It also means to show courage by not accepting limits or pressure.
example_sentence: The students defied the school rules and went out early. She defied her parents and chose her own career. The soldier defied the enemy orders and acted bravely. The strong wind seemed to defy all predictions.

english_meaning: To treat someone with contempt or disrespect. To lower the quality, value, or character of something. To reduce someone to a lower rank or status. To break down chemically or physically into simpler parts. To cause a decline in condition or standing.
example_sentence: Such language degrades both the speaker and the listener. Pollution continues to degrade the natural environment. He refused to degrade himself by begging for help. Plastic takes hundreds of years to degrade completely.

english_meaning: To remove grease, oil or fat from something. To clean a surface, machine or dish of oily residue.
example_sentence: Degrease the pan before adding fresh oil. The mechanic degreased the engine parts thoroughly. You must degrease the metal before painting it. Skim the stock to degrease the soup.

english_meaning: A unit for measuring temperature or angles. An academic qualification awarded by a university. The amount, level or extent of something. A stage in a scale or series, as in comparison of adjectives.
example_sentence: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius. She has a degree in civil engineering. There is a high degree of risk in this plan. A triangle's angles add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

english_meaning: To lose or remove water or moisture from something or someone. To cause the body or a substance to lose more water than is taken in. When the human body loses too much fluid, it becomes dehydrated and is unable to function properly. Also used in food science and industry to describe the process of removing water from food to preserve it.
example_sentence: Running in extreme heat without drinking water can dehydrate you quickly. The patient was hospitalised because she had severely dehydrated during the illness. Manufacturers often dehydrate fruits to make dried snacks with a longer shelf life. Working long hours under the sun can dehydrate the body rapidly. Alcohol and caffeine can cause the body to dehydrate if consumed in large amounts.

english_meaning: To do something that one considers beneath their dignity. To reluctantly or condescendingly agree to do something, usually because the speaker feels they are too important or superior to do it.
example_sentence: The manager did not deign to reply to the complaint. She finally deigned to speak to the interns after weeks of silence. He would not deign to explain his decision to anyone. The celebrity deigned to sign only one autograph.

english_meaning: Belief that God created the universe but does not intervene in it through miracles or revealed religion. A religious or philosophical belief based mainly on reason and nature.
example_sentence: Deism influenced some thinkers of the Enlightenment. He studied deism alongside other religious philosophies. Deism differs from atheism because it accepts a creator. Many forms of deism reject revealed scripture. The debate compared deism with traditional theism.

english_meaning: A person who believes in the existence of God or a supreme being, based on reason and observation of the natural world, rather than on religious revelation, scripture, or organized religion. One who accepts that God created the universe but does not intervene in its workings or in human affairs.
example_sentence: Thomas Jefferson is often described as a deist. A deist believes in God through reason rather than scripture. Many philosophers of the Enlightenment era were deists. The author argues that being a deist does not contradict scientific thinking. As a deist, he respects all religions but follows none.

english_meaning: Relating to deism or to a deist. Believing in or based on the idea of a God who created the universe but does not interfere with it. Based on reason and observation of nature rather than on revelation or scripture. Pertaining to the philosophical belief in a non-interventionist creator.
example_sentence: His writings reflect a strongly deistic point of view. The deistic philosophy was popular in the eighteenth century. She holds a deistic belief about the origin of the universe. The book examines deistic ideas in modern thought. His arguments are based on a deistic understanding of nature.

english_meaning: A god or goddess. A divine being who is worshipped. In religion and mythology, a supernatural being with divine status, powers, or control over part of the world or human life. One exalted or revered as supremely good or powerful.
example_sentence: We prayed to the Deity for guidance. In ancient Greece, Zeus was considered the most powerful deity. Hindus worship many deities, each representing different aspects of life. The temple was built in honor of a local deity believed to protect the village. Some cultures believe natural forces like the sun and the river are living deities.

english_meaning: In linguistics, the use of words or expressions whose meaning depends on the context in which they are used, especially the speaker's location, time of speaking, or identity. The function of pointing or specifying through words such as 'this,' 'that,' 'here,' 'there,' 'now,' 'then,' 'I,' and 'you'. The reliance of certain expressions on situational context for their interpretation.
example_sentence: Words like 'here' and 'now' are common examples of deixis. The professor explained deixis with simple everyday sentences. Personal pronouns are a key part of deixis in any language. Understanding deixis helps learners grasp natural conversation. Deixis often causes confusion in written communication where context is missing.

english_meaning: To make someone sad or dispirited. To cast down in spirits. To cause loss of hope or courage. To depress emotionally. To lower someone’s mood or confidence.
example_sentence: The bad news dejected the whole family. His failure in the exam dejected him for days. She was dejected by the harsh criticism. Nothing could deject his positive spirit.

english_meaning: To give part of your work, power or authority to somebody in a lower position than you. To choose somebody to do something. A person who is chosen or elected to represent the views of a group of people and vote and make decisions for them. A person who attends a conference. A person who is chosen to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of other people, specially at a conference or a meeting.
example_sentence: Some managers find it difficult to delegate. The job had to be delegated to an assistant. I've been delegated to organize the Christmas party. Congress delegates rejected the proposals. The conference was attended by delegates from 56 countries. They decided not to send a delegate to the conference. Delegates have voted in favour of the motion. Each union elects several delegates to the annual conference.

english_meaning: The act of giving authority or responsibility to someone, or a group chosen to represent others.  A group of people officially selected to represent an organization, country, or institution in meetings or events. Assigning tasks to team members according to their skills while keeping overall responsibility.
example_sentence: The manager improved efficiency through proper delegation of tasks. The government sent a delegation to attend the international conference. Good delegation helps leaders focus on strategic planning. The school delegation participated in the national debate competition.

english_meaning: A person or program that removes text, data or files. Something used to erase or wipe out recorded information. One who cancels or takes out part of a document. A tool that permanently removes unwanted content.
example_sentence: The file deleter removed all temporary documents. He acted as the deleter of every offensive comment. A duplicate deleter helped clean up the photo library. The deleter cannot recover files once they are gone.

english_meaning: Causing harm or damage. Harmful to health or well-being. Producing negative or destructive effects. Injurious in a subtle or gradual manner. Used especially for influences, substances, or actions that quietly damage a person, system, environment, or relationship over time rather than instantly.
example_sentence: Smoking has deleterious effects on the lungs and heart. The deleterious impact of pollution on marine life is well documented. Constant criticism can have a deleterious influence on a child’s confidence. Excessive screen time may prove deleterious to mental health. The new policy had a deleterious effect on small businesses.

english_meaning: Take counsel (advice) with others. Decided on as a result of careful thought. To give serious and careful thought to.
example_sentence: The speech was a deliberate attempt to embarrass the govt. They deliberated on whether to continue with talks. The jury deliberated for five days before finding him guilty.

english_meaning: On Purpose. Slowly & carefully. Done by planning, not by chance. With careful thought or consideration. In a calm and unhurried way. With full awareness of what one is doing : in a way that is intended or planned.
example_sentence: She has been deliberately ignoring him all day. She was accused of deliberately misleading Parliament. The fire had been started deliberately. Her tone was deliberately insulting. Her tone was deliberately insulting. Calmly and deliberately, she cut up his suits one by one.

english_meaning: Fineness, softness, sensitivity, or refinement. A rare or expensive food. A situation requiring tact and careful handling. Fragility or subtle beauty.
example_sentence: The glass must be handled with delicacy. Truffles are considered a delicacy in many places. She discussed the issue with great delicacy. The painting has a rare delicacy of color. Illness gave his features a strange delicacy.

english_meaning: To take pleasure in someone or something’s company or actions. To find joy in performing an activity, often repeatedly or habitually. To feel satisfaction in noticing or experiencing something.
example_sentence: She delights in helping others every day. He delights in the success of his students. They delight in simple pleasures like tea and conversation. The children delight in hearing bedtime stories.

english_meaning: To determine or fix the limits or boundaries of something. It involves clearly stating where something begins and ends, whether it is a physical area or a conceptual topic. This ensures that the extent of a task or territory is well-defined.
example_sentence: The treaty was signed to delimit the borders between the two warring nations. We must delimit the scope of our research project to remain within the budget. The authorities will delimit the protected zone to save the endangered species. It is difficult to delimit the exact responsibilities of each department.

english_meaning: The action of fixing the boundary or limits of something. It is the process of defining the extent of a specific area, power, or subject. In geography and law, it specifically refers to the mapping and description of boundaries.
example_sentence: The delimitation of the maritime zones took several months of negotiation. Clear delimitation of duties is essential for the efficiency of the team. The committee is responsible for the delimitation of electoral constituencies. He argued that the delimitation of the project was too narrow to be effective.

english_meaning: A character, symbol, word, or sequence used to separate, mark, or indicate the boundaries between different parts of data, text, code, or information. Anything that divides or separates one element from another. It is commonly used in computing, linguistics, databases, spreadsheets, and writing.
example_sentence: The comma serves as a delimiter between values in a CSV file. The programmer used a semicolon as a delimiter to separate statements. Spaces act as delimiters between words in a sentence. The system reads each record by identifying the delimiter in the text file.

english_meaning: To describe or portray something precisely or with great detail. It can also mean to indicate the exact position of a border or outline on a map or diagram. This involves making a clear distinction or representation of an idea or object.
example_sentence: The report clearly delineates the steps needed to achieve our goals. Architects use precise drawings to delineate the structure of the building. The law should clearly delineate the rights and obligations of the citizens. The author tries to delineate the complex emotions of the protagonist.

english_meaning: Minor crime or wrongdoing, especially by young people. Failure to do what is required by law, duty, or payment. Neglect of obligation.
example_sentence: The program aims to reduce juvenile delinquency. Loan delinquency increased during the recession. Parents worried about rising delinquency in the area. His delinquency began with small acts of theft. The report separates crime from school delinquency.

english_meaning: A person, especially a young one, who behaves in an illegal or antisocial way. Failing in one's duty. Guilty of a minor crime or misdeed. Overdue in payment. A young offender. Behaviour, accounts, or duties that are neglected, unpaid, or in violation of the law.
example_sentence: The school has started a special program for juvenile delinquents. He was a delinquent in his teens but later turned his life around. The bank sent a notice about her delinquent account. They were delinquent in paying their taxes for two years. Several delinquents were caught vandalizing the public park.

english_meaning: In a disturbed mental state, often because of fever, illness, shock, or excitement. Wildly excited, confused, or irrational.
example_sentence: The patient became delirious during the night. Fans were delirious with joy after the victory. He was too delirious to answer clearly. High fever can make a child delirious. The news sent the crowd into delirious celebration.

english_meaning: A serious mental disturbance, often caused by high fever or illness, in which a person becomes confused, restless, and may see or hear things that are not there. A state of wild excitement, ecstasy, or uncontrollable emotion. Temporary loss of clear thought.
example_sentence: The patient was in a state of delirium because of his high fever. He spoke of strange visions during his delirium that night. The crowd cheered the team into a delirium of joy after the victory. Doctors warned the family that the delirium would pass with rest. In her delirium, she kept calling out her mother's name.

english_meaning: Deliberately obscure or ambiguous in meaning. Relating to the ancient oracle of Delphi. Mysterious and difficult to interpret. Prophetic in a puzzling or cryptic way. Enigmatic in expression or statement.
example_sentence: The minister gave a Delphic reply that no one could interpret. Her Delphic remarks left the audience puzzled. The old priest was famous for his Delphic pronouncements. He offered a Delphic smile but said nothing.

english_meaning: A tall garden plant bearing spikes of blue, purple, pink, or white flowers. Any plant of the genus Delphinium in the buttercup family, commonly known as larkspur. A cut flower widely used in decorative arrangements.
example_sentence: Tall blue delphiniums lined the garden wall. She planted delphiniums along the sunny border. The florist added delphinium stems to the bouquet. Delphiniums need staking because their stems are so tall.

english_meaning: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as Δ or δ. A triangular area of land formed where a river divides before entering the sea. In mathematics and science, a symbol representing change or difference. Anything shaped like a triangle.
example_sentence: The Nile delta is one of the most fertile regions in Africa. In physics, delta usually denotes a change in a quantity. Rich farmland covers the delta of the Indus River. The Greek letter delta appears throughout the equation.

english_meaning: An elite special operations unit of the United States Army trained for counter-terrorism and hostage rescue. A highly trained military team used for secret and dangerous missions. Informally, any small group chosen for a difficult or urgent task.
synonyms: ["Commando unit","Special forces","Task force","Strike team","Elite unit","SEAL team","Squad","Detachment"]
example_sentence: Delta Force was deployed to rescue the hostages. The film tells the story of a Delta Force operation. Only a few soldiers qualify for Delta Force each year. The mission was handed over to Delta Force because of its complexity.

english_meaning: The thick, triangular muscle that covers the shoulder joint and lifts the arm. The muscle that gives the shoulder its rounded shape. A muscle divided into front, middle, and back parts that move the arm in different directions. Shaped like a triangle.
example_sentence: Shoulder presses are a good way to develop the deltoid. The deltoid lifts the arm away from the body. An injection is often given into the deltoid muscle. The pain spread from his deltoid down to his elbow.

english_meaning: To mislead someone into believing something that is not true. To deceive someone mentally by making them believe something false.
example_sentence: He deluded himself into thinking he would win without preparation. The fraudster tried to delude investors with false promises. She was deluded by fake news on social media. Do not delude yourself with unrealistic expectations.

english_meaning: To send or give somebody/something a large number of things at the same time. To flood a place with water. A severe flood; a sudden very heavy fall of rain. A large number of things that happen or arrive at the same time.
example_sentence: We have been deluged with applications for the job. He was deluged with phone calls from friends and colleagues. Applicants deluged the office with calls. The campsite was deluged by a flash flood. When the snow melts, the mountain stream becomes a deluge. The earlier deluge had given way to more normal rain. An unseasonable deluge had washed away a section of river bank. The firm was at a loss to explain the sudden deluge of publicity.

english_meaning: A false belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by reality or rational argument. A mistaken or misleading idea or belief.
example_sentence: He was under the delusion that everyone admired him. Her delusion that she was being followed led to her hospitalisation. The cult leader used delusion to control his followers. Living in delusion prevents personal growth.

english_meaning: To reduce or remove shine, gloss, or brightness from a surface. To reduce prestige, attractiveness, or reputation. To diminish appeal, charm, or excitement of something. In textiles or metals, to make fibers or surfaces less reflective.
example_sentence: The harsh cleaning chemicals delustered the silverware. Scandals can deluster a politician’s reputation. Overexposure to sunlight can deluster painted walls. His repeated failures delustered his image as a competent manager.

english_meaning: Plural of deluster. Substances, treatments, or processes that reduce shine or gloss, especially in fibers, fabrics, plastics, or surfaces.
example_sentence: Manufacturers add delusters to make fibers less shiny. Different delusters change the appearance of synthetic fabric. The lab compared several delusters for plastic film. Too many delusters can make the surface look dull. Textile engineers choose delusters carefully.

english_meaning: To search deeply and carefully for information. To investigate, examine, or research. To dig or reach into something.
example_sentence: The journalist decided to delve into the records. We need to delve deeper into the cause of the problem. Children love to delve in old boxes. The course delves into modern poetry. She delved through the files for evidence.

english_meaning: A political leader who tries to gain support by stirring emotions, fears or prejudices rather than using honest arguments. Someone who rises to influence by appealing to emotions, biases and frustrations of the public. Instead of presenting rational, fair or fact based arguments, this leader uses manipulation, exaggeration, fear and anger to control or persuade people. The term is usually negative and suggests dishonesty and exploitation of the public.
example_sentence: The crowd cheered, but many knew he was acting like a demagogue to win votes. A true leader guides with wisdom while a demagogue plays with people's fears. History shows how dangerous a demagogue can become when people stop questioning him. She warned that supporting a demagogue could lead the country toward instability. That politician is just a demagogue who preys upon people's fears and prejudices.

english_meaning: To set the boundaries or limits of something. To distinguish between categories or concepts. To set limits in a figurative sense. To clearly define or mark the edges, boundaries, or distinctions of an area, concept, or object. Often used in legal, geographical, or organizational contexts.
example_sentence: The surveyors will demarcate the land before construction begins. The teacher demarcated the responsibilities of each team member. International borders are demarcated with markers and maps. The park area was demarcated with fences for safety.

english_meaning: The action of setting boundaries or limits, marking off an area.  The process of establishing clear boundaries or distinctions between areas, ideas, roles, or objects. It can be physical, like drawing a line on a map, or abstract, like defining limits in responsibilities or concepts.
example_sentence: The demarcation between the two properties was clearly marked with a fence. There is a demarcation of roles between the project manager and the team members. International treaties often involve demarcation of borders between countries. In debates, demarcation of facts from opinions is essential.

english_meaning: A formal diplomatic communication or official step taken by one government or organization to express a position, request action, protest, or negotiate with another. It is usually delivered through diplomatic channels and carries serious political weight.
example_sentence: The ambassador delivered a demarche to express concern over the border violation. The government issued a demarche demanding the release of detained citizens. A strong demarche was sent to protest the new trade restrictions. The foreign ministry prepared a demarche regarding the security situation in the region.

english_meaning: To cause someone to lose dignity or respect. To lower in character, status, or reputation. To behave or conduct oneself in a particular way. To make someone feel that they are unimportant or worthless. To reduce the value or standing of a person or thing.
example_sentence: Do not demean yourself by arguing with rude people. His unkind remarks demeaned everyone in the room. She felt he was trying to demean her in front of others. Such jokes only demean the person who tells them.

english_meaning: A person's outward behavior, manner, bearing, or way of conducting themselves. The visible attitude shown through speech, expression, and actions.
example_sentence: Her calm demeanor reassured the children. The officer's stern demeanor made everyone quiet. He has a friendly demeanor at work. A professional demeanor matters in interviews. His nervous demeanor revealed his anxiety.

english_meaning: A medical condition involving serious decline in memory, thinking, judgment, language, or daily functioning, usually because of brain disease or aging.
example_sentence: Dementia can affect memory and judgment. Her father was diagnosed with dementia. Families need support when caring for someone with dementia. Not every memory problem is dementia. Doctors assessed his speech and behavior for signs of dementia.

english_meaning: A type of raw cane sugar with large golden-brown crystals and a light molasses flavor. Natural brown sugar originally from the Demerara region of Guyana. A minimally processed sugar that retains some natural molasses.
synonyms: ["Raw sugar","Brown sugar","Turbinado sugar","Golden sugar","Natural sugar","Cane sugar"]
example_sentence: She sprinkled demerara sugar on top of the muffins. Demerara sugar adds a rich flavor to coffee. The recipe calls for demerara sugar instead of white sugar. Demerara sugar crystals give a lovely crunch to baked goods.

english_meaning: To separate a previously merged company, organization, or entity back into independent parts. To reverse a merger by splitting a combined business into separate companies. The process of undoing a corporate merger or consolidation.
example_sentence: The board decided to demerge the two divisions into separate companies. After the demerger, shareholders received stock in both new entities. The conglomerate plans to demerge its healthcare unit. Regulatory authorities approved the decision to demerge.

english_meaning: The process or act of separating a previously merged company or organization into independent entities. A corporate restructuring where a business splits into two or more separate companies. The opposite of a merger, involving the division of a combined business.
example_sentence: The demerger created two successful independent companies. Shareholders voted in favor of the demerger. The demerger will allow each division to focus on its core business. The demerger process took over a year to complete.

english_meaning: A fault, disadvantage, or undesirable feature of something. A mark or point given for a fault or failure, especially in a disciplinary system. The opposite of merit, indicating something negative or unworthy. A quality or action that deserves blame or criticism.
example_sentence: The main demerit of this plan is its high cost. Students received demerits for breaking school rules. The proposal has several demerits that need addressing. Each late arrival earned him a demerit point.

english_meaning: Death or end of something. The death of a person. The end or termination of something (such as an era, system, or organization). In legal usage, the transfer of property or estate (archaic or formal).
example_sentence: The sudden demise of the leader shocked the entire nation. After the demise of the company, thousands of employees lost their jobs. The old empire saw its demise after years of internal conflict. The demise of traditional farming methods has changed rural life.

english_meaning: To resign from an office, position, or membership. To formally give up a post or responsibility. In Scottish and legal use, to relinquish a duty or claim. To step down from a role, usually in a formal manner.
example_sentence: He decided to demit office at the end of the year. The chairman demitted his post after the inquiry. She will demit charge next Monday. Several members demitted from the committee in protest.

english_meaning: A demonstration of how something works or what it can do. A sample recording made to showcase a musician's ability. A trial version of software or a product. A short display of a product's features for promotion. To show or explain how something functions.
example_sentence: The salesman gave us a quick demo of the new phone. She recorded a demo to send to record labels. You can try the free demo before buying the software. Let me demo how this machine works.

english_meaning: A system of government in which people choose leaders by voting. Rule by the people. A society based on political equality, rights, and participation.
example_sentence: Democracy depends on free elections. Citizens have responsibilities in a democracy. The movement demanded democracy and basic rights. A healthy democracy protects minority voices.

english_meaning: A person who supports democracy. A person who believes that government should represent the people. A person who supports democratic rights and participation. A supporter of government by elected representatives. A member or supporter of the Democratic Party in the United States
example_sentence: She has always been a committed democrat. The senator is a Democrat from California. A true democrat respects free elections. Democrats debated the new policy.

english_meaning: Relating to or supporting democracy. Based on the principle that everyone has equal rights and a voice. Practicing fairness and equality in decision-making. Open to participation by all members of a group.
example_sentence: They live in a democratic country with free elections. The teacher used a democratic approach in the classroom. A democratic society values every citizen's voice. The decision was made through a democratic vote.

english_meaning: To make something accessible to ordinary people. To make an organization or system more democratic. To spread power, opportunity, or knowledge more widely.
example_sentence: The internet helped democratize information. Reforms aimed to democratize local government. Low-cost tools can democratize education. The movement tried to democratize access to art.

english_meaning: A specific segment or group within a population. A group of people sharing certain characteristics. A statistical category used in surveys or census.  Related to the structure or characteristics of a population. Pertaining to statistical study of populations.
example_sentence: The company studies the demographic trends before launching a new product. Younger demographics are more likely to use social media. The survey collected demographic information such as age and occupation. Marketing strategies should target specific demographics.

english_meaning: The study of human populations, especially their size, structure, distribution, and changes. It examines population size, age structure, gender ratio, birth rates, death rates, migration patterns, and population growth. It helps governments and organizations plan for education, health care, housing, employment, and development.
synonyms: ["Anthropology","Population Analysis","Population Density","Population Growth","Population Size","Population Studies","Population Vital Statistics"]
example_sentence: The increase in the number of young people leaving to work in the cities has had a dramatic impact on the demography of the villages. Demography is the statistical study of human populations. The demography of the area is predicted to change radically over the next 30 years, with large increases in the number of older people. The census can not total up its own demography. The equation needed to adjust for practice demography will be difficult to validate.

english_meaning: To destroy, tear down, or knock down a building or structure. To defeat completely. To disprove an argument or idea forcefully.
example_sentence: The old bridge will be demolished next month. Their team demolished the champions in the final. The lawyer demolished the witness's argument. Workers used machines to demolish the wall. One fact can demolish a weak theory.

english_meaning: The act or process of destroying, tearing down, or knocking down a structure. Complete defeat, destruction, or dismantling.
example_sentence: Demolition of the old factory began at dawn. The city approved the demolition permit. The match ended in the demolition of the visiting team. Safety rules are strict during demolition. The demolition crew cleared the site by evening.

english_meaning: An evil spirit or a supernatural being often associated with the devil. In a metaphorical sense, it refers to an extremely wicked or cruel person. It can also describe a persistent and harmful habit or feeling that plagues someone.
example_sentence: Ancient legends speak of a demon that haunted the old forest. He fought hard to overcome the inner demon of alcohol addiction. The cruel dictator was described as a demon in human form by his victims. She was a demon for work, staying at the office until midnight every day.

english_meaning: The quality of being able to prove or show something clearly. The ability or capacity to present evidence, reasoning or facts in a way that makes something clear, verifiable or understandable. It refers to how easily a claim, idea or fact can be shown to be true.
example_sentence: The demonstrability of the results made the research more convincing. Her argument lacked demonstrability, so the panel did not accept it. Good data improves the demonstrability of scientific findings. The company focused on the demonstrability of its product benefits during the presentation.

english_meaning: Something that can be shown, proven or clearly demonstrated. Used for anything that can be supported with evidence, facts or visible proof. It shows that the truth or existence of something is clear enough to be verified. Clear enough to be proven or shown with evidence. Capable of being illustrated with examples. Easy to explain or show. Supported by measurable data
example_sentence: There is demonstrable evidence that the project improved community resilience. His progress in writing skills is demonstrable after one month of practice. The policy failed because it lacked demonstrable results. Climate risks have a demonstrable impact on vulnerable communities.

english_meaning: The quality of being able to be shown, proven, or clearly explained. The state in which something can be demonstrated, proven with evidence, shown through reasoning, or made clearly understandable. It highlights how clear, verifiable, or explainable something is.
example_sentence: The demonstrableness of his theory made it easy for the judges to accept it. She questioned the demonstrableness of the data presented in the report. Scientific claims must carry a high level of demonstrableness. The lawyer focused on the demonstrableness of the evidence to strengthen the case.

english_meaning: A formal expression, explanation, or showing of something. An act of showing, presenting, or explaining something clearly. It can also mean a formal statement made to prove a point or express a concern. A formal protest or objection presented to authorities. A public or visible act meant to show support or disagreement. An act of proving something through evidence. A clear manifestation of a feeling or idea.
example_sentence: Her demonstrance of the data helped everyone understand the issue. The committee requested a clear demonstrance of the proposed plan. His calm demonstrance of facts changed the direction of the debate. The report served as a demonstrance of the team’s progress.

english_meaning: (plural of demonstrandum). Things that must be proven or demonstrated. The set of statements, claims or points in logic, philosophy or mathematics that someone needs to prove. It is used when listing items that require evidence or logical demonstration. Things that need to be shown or established through proof.
example_sentence: Before the debate started, the moderator outlined the main demonstranda for both teams. The scientist listed the demonstranda that her experiment would try to confirm. In logic, every argument begins with clear demonstranda that guide the proof. The report highlights several demonstranda that require further research.

english_meaning: Something that must be demonstrated or proven. The statement, claim, or proposition that needs to be shown as true within an argument or logical proof. It is the target conclusion that a person sets out to justify using evidence, reasoning, or demonstration.
example_sentence: In this mathematical proof, the main demonstrandum is that both sides of the equation are equal. Every scientific experiment begins with a hypothesis that becomes the demonstrandum of the study. The lawyer identified the demonstrandum that needed to be proven in court. The researcher presented data to support the demonstrandum of his argument.

english_meaning: A person who takes part in a public protest or demonstration. Someone who joins a public gathering to express support or opposition to an issue, policy, decision or event. A demonstrant can be peaceful or active in their protest activity.
antonyms: ["Supporter of the status quo","Bystander","Non participant","Opponent of protests"]
example_sentence: The police guided the demonstrants to a safer area during the rally. Hundreds of demonstrants gathered outside the parliament building. The demonstrants demanded immediate action on climate change. Each demonstrant carried a sign showing their message.

english_meaning: To show something clearly or prove it. To take part in a public protest. To show the existence or truth of something through evidence. To display a skill or quality clearly. To explain, show or prove something by giving evidence, examples, actions or practical display. It can also mean to show a feeling or skill clearly through behavior or performance.
example_sentence: The teacher demonstrated the experiment to the class. Her actions demonstrated real courage. He demonstrated how the new machine works. The data clearly demonstrates a rise in temperature. The graph demonstrates a sharp decline in rainfall. Students demonstrated for better educational facilities. He demonstrated kindness by helping the injured man.

english_meaning: Showing something clearly or proving how something works. Proof or evidence of something. A public protest or march. A practical explanation using actions rather than words. A test showing the effectiveness of a product or method. A presentation, display or practical showing of how something works. It can also mean a public gathering where people show their support or protest about an issue.
example_sentence: The teacher gave a demonstration of the new science experiment. The company arranged a demonstration to show how the machine works. A large demonstration took place in the city to demand better services. He used a simple model for the demonstration of his idea.

english_meaning: Serving to demonstrate or prove something. Tending to show feelings, especially affection, openly.
example_sentence: He grew up in a very demonstrative family where hugs were common. Her demonstrative behavior at the airport showed how much she missed him. The results provided demonstrative proof that the new vaccine was effective. In grammar, words like this and that are known as demonstrative pronouns.

english_meaning: In a way that clearly shows or proves something. In a manner that expresses feelings or affection openly.
example_sentence: She demonstratively hugged her sister after the long period apart. The speaker demonstratively argued against the proposed budget cuts. He showed his disapproval demonstratively by walking out of the room. The new evidence was demonstratively superior to the previous findings.

english_meaning: A person who takes part in a public protest or march. A person who explains or shows how something works, especially a product.
example_sentence: Each demonstrator carried a sign expressing their dissatisfaction with the law. The product demonstrator showed the crowd how to use the new kitchen appliance. A lone demonstrator stood outside the embassy to protest the recent decision. The police monitored the demonstrator to ensure the protest remained peaceful.

english_meaning: A person who loves people and enjoys being among crowds. One who is fond of the common people or the masses. A lover of humanity and social gatherings. Someone drawn to communities and public life.
example_sentence: As a demophile, he loves attending festivals. She is a demophile who thrives in busy markets. True demophiles find energy in the company of others. The politician was known as a genuine demophile.

english_meaning: An intense fear of crowds, mobs, or large gatherings of people. Similar to enochlophobia but specifically focused on the fear of mobs and their potential danger.
example_sentence: Her demophobia flared up at the political rally. He avoided city centres because of his demophobia. Demophobia became common after violent mob incidents. She felt her demophobia worsen at the overcrowded festival.

english_meaning: The process of undermining the morale or confidence of a person or group. A state of being corrupted or deprived of spirit.
example_sentence: The long period of unemployment led to a deep sense of demoralization. Economic instability often results in the demoralization of the working class. The general was worried about the demoralization of his troops after the retreat. Effective leadership is necessary to prevent the demoralization of the workforce.

english_meaning: To cause someone to lose confidence or hope. To corrupt the morals or spirit of a group or individual.
example_sentence: The sudden defeat served to demoralize the entire team before the finals. Repeated criticism can demoralize even the most dedicated employees. The enemy aimed to demoralize the civilian population through constant propaganda. Don't let a small failure demoralize you from pursuing your lifelong dreams.

english_meaning: The common people of an ancient Greek state. The populace or ordinary citizens as a political unit. More than one demonstration or sample. Plural form of demo, referring to trial versions or samples. The people considered as the source of political power in a democracy.
example_sentence: In ancient Athens the demos held real political power. The band released several demos before their first album. The company shared free demos of its new software. True democracy respects the will of the demos.

english_meaning: To lower someone to a lower rank, position, grade, or status. To reduce in importance or responsibility.
example_sentence: The company may demote him for repeated mistakes. She was demoted from manager to assistant. A poor result can demote a team in the rankings. Do not demote an issue simply because it is uncomfortable. The officer was demoted after the inquiry.

english_meaning: The act of moving someone to a lower rank, grade, or position. A reduction in status, importance, or responsibility at work. The lowering of a team or player to a lower division or league. The state of having been reduced to a less important level.
example_sentence: His repeated mistakes led to a sudden demotion. She accepted the demotion rather than lose her job. The club faced demotion to the second division. A demotion can be as damaging to morale as a pay cut.

english_meaning: Quiet, modest, and reserved in behavior or appearance. Showing a reserved, shy, or modest demeanor; often associated with polite or understated behavior, not drawing attention to oneself.
example_sentence: She gave a demure smile when complimented. The actress appeared demure in her elegant dress. He was surprised by her demure behavior at the party. The demure child stayed close to her mother in the crowd.

english_meaning: In a quiet, modest, reserved, or shy manner. With a composed and decorous appearance. In an affectedly modest or coy way.
example_sentence: She smiled demurely at the compliment. He sat demurely beside his grandmother. The actor lowered her eyes demurely. She answered demurely but confidently.

english_meaning: A size of paper, traditionally about 17.5 by 22.5 inches in printing. A scholar receiving a demyship at Magdalen College, Oxford. A half-sized or lesser form in older usage.
example_sentence: The printer asked whether the sheet was demy or crown size. Old books sometimes mention demy paper. He was elected a demy at Magdalen College. The term demy is uncommon in everyday speech. Collectors recognize demy as a traditional paper size.

english_meaning: The act or process of making something difficult, mysterious, or confusing easier to understand. A clear explanation that removes secrecy, misconceptions, or unnecessary complexity. The exposure of the ordinary reality behind an intimidating subject.
example_sentence: The book offers a useful demystification of modern economics. Demystification of the legal process helped the families. Her lecture began the demystification of genetic testing. Good science writing encourages demystification rather than confusion.

english_meaning: To make something easier to understand by explaining it clearly and removing confusion, mystery, or misunderstanding. To simplify or explain a subject, process, idea, or concept so that ordinary people can understand it without feeling confused or intimidated. It involves revealing how something works and making it less mysterious or complicated.
example_sentence: The teacher used simple diagrams to demystify the concept of quantum physics for her students. The workshop helped demystify the process of starting a small business. The documentary was created to demystify artificial intelligence for the general public. The doctor took time to demystify the medical procedure before the surgery.

english_meaning: A person who loves or has a deep affection for trees. This can involve appreciating trees for their beauty, studying them, or actively working to protect and care for them. Someone who finds joy and spiritual connection in trees. A person with a hobby or profession related to trees, like botany or forestry.
example_sentence: The dendrophile spent his weekends planting new trees in the community park. She is a true dendrophile, always photographing old oak trees. As a dendrophile, he opposed cutting down the forest for commercial purposes. The dendrophile joined a local conservation group to protect endangered tree species.

english_meaning: The extreme or irrational fear of trees. An intense anxiety or phobia triggered by being in or near wooded areas. A pathological dread of forest environments. A psychological condition where an individual avoids forests and parks. The persistent fear of trees and their potential to fall or cause harm.
example_sentence: His dendrophobia makes it impossible for him to enjoy a simple walk in the park. She sought therapy to overcome her dendrophobia after moving to a wooded suburb. Even looking at pictures of dense forests can trigger a panic attack in those with dendrophobia. People suffering from dendrophobia often feel trapped when surrounded by tall vegetation.

english_meaning: A mosquito-borne viral disease causing severe flu-like symptoms. A tropical illness transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. An infection characterized by high fever, severe headache, and joint pain. A disease that can progress to dangerous hemorrhagic fever.
example_sentence: Dengue fever is common in tropical regions. She was hospitalized with severe dengue. Dengue prevention focuses on mosquito control. There is no specific treatment for dengue.

english_meaning: The action of declaring something to be untrue. A refusal to satisfy a request or a rejection of a right. In psychology, it is a defense mechanism in which a person refuses to admit the reality of a stressful situation.
example_sentence: The government issued an official denial regarding the rumors of a tax hike. She lived in denial of her health problems for many years. The court's denial of the appeal came as a shock to the legal team. His sudden denial of the previous agreement caused a lot of confusion.

english_meaning: To criticize unfairly, attack someone's reputation, or speak of someone or something as worthless. To belittle, defame, or disparage.
example_sentence: It is wrong to denigrate people because of their background. The article tried to denigrate her achievements. He refused to denigrate his opponent. Gossip can denigrate a person's reputation quickly. Strong debate should not denigrate human dignity.

english_meaning: To give a name to something or to classify it under a specific name. To assign a name, title, or designation to a person, thing, place, or group. It can also mean to classify something under a particular category or to express something in a specific unit, such as currency.
example_sentence: The committee decided to denominate the new building after a national hero. The bonds are denominated in US dollars. The scientist denominated the newly discovered species carefully. The law denominates certain actions as criminal offenses.

english_meaning: The bottom number in a fraction that shows into how many parts the whole is divided. In a fraction, the denominator is the number below the fraction line. It indicates the total number of equal parts that make up a whole. Denominator can also refer to a shared characteristic or common factor among a group of things. A unifying factor that connects different ideas, cultures, or problems. It highlights similarity within diversity.
example_sentence: In 3/4, 4 is the denominator. To add fractions, they must have the same denominator. Patience is a common denominator among successful leaders. The common denominator of all these problems is poor planning. A larger denominator means smaller pieces.

english_meaning: The final part of a story or play where the plot is resolved and everything is explained. The outcome or resolution of a complex sequence of events. The climax and conclusion of a dramatic situation.
example_sentence: The denouement of the mystery novel surprised all the readers. Everyone waited eagerly for the denouement of the political crisis. The film's denouement tied together all the loose threads. In the denouement, the hero finally reveals his true identity.

english_meaning: To strongly criticize or publicly condemn someone or something. To publicly declare that something or someone is wrong or evil. To criticize strongly and officially. To condemn openly.
example_sentence: The leader denounced the violent actions of the protesters. She denounced corruption in the government. The organization denounced the unfair treatment of workers. He was quick to denounce the decision made by the committee.

english_meaning: Closely packed together with very little space in between. Thick and difficult to see through, as with fog or smoke. Difficult to understand because it is complicated or heavy in style. Informally, slow to understand or rather stupid.
example_sentence: The village is surrounded by dense forest. Dense fog delayed all morning flights. The book is dense and requires careful reading. He can be a bit dense when it comes to jokes.

english_meaning: The amount of mass in a given volume. The degree of compactness, thickness, concentration, or crowdedness. The quality of being dense in matter, population, information, or style.
example_sentence: Lead has a high density. Population density is greater in cities. The density of the fog made driving difficult. The professor reduced the density of the lecture notes. Scientists measured the density of the liquid.

english_meaning: The hard, dense tissue that forms the main body of a tooth beneath the enamel. A calcified material surrounding the pulp cavity of a tooth. The layer that gives a tooth its shape and strength. Also spelled dentin, especially in American English.
example_sentence: Dentine lies just below the enamel of every tooth. Exposed dentine often causes sensitivity to cold drinks. The X-ray showed decay reaching the dentine. Dentine is softer than enamel but harder than bone.

english_meaning: A medical professional who specializes in diagnosing and treating diseases and conditions of the teeth and gums. A healthcare practitioner who performs dental procedures like cleanings, fillings, and extractions. A doctor of dental surgery or dental medicine.
example_sentence: I visit my dentist twice a year for checkups. The dentist recommended braces for my crooked teeth. She is a skilled dentist with many years of experience. The dentist performed a root canal procedure.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine dealing with the teeth, gums and mouth. The profession and practice of treating dental problems. The study and treatment of diseases affecting the oral cavity. The work carried out by a dentist, including cleaning, filling and surgery.
example_sentence: She studied dentistry at a well-known university. Modern dentistry is far less painful than before. He runs a small clinic specialising in cosmetic dentistry. Preventive dentistry can save patients a great deal of money.

english_meaning: The arrangement, type and number of teeth in a person or animal. The development and cutting of teeth. The natural set of teeth considered as a whole. A term used in dentistry and zoology to describe tooth structure.
example_sentence: The dentist examined the child's dentition carefully. Human dentition includes incisors, canines, premolars and molars. Poor diet can affect the dentition of young children. Scientists studied the dentition of the fossil skull.

english_meaning: An artificial replacement for one or more missing teeth. A dental plate holding false teeth. A removable device fitted in the mouth to restore chewing. The singular form used for a complete or partial set of false teeth.
example_sentence: A partial denture was fitted on the lower jaw. The denture felt uncomfortable for the first few days. He dropped his denture and it cracked. The clinic makes each denture to measure.

english_meaning: A set of artificial teeth worn to replace natural ones. Removable false teeth fitted for people who have lost their own. Dental plates made to restore chewing and appearance. Plural form of denture, referring to full or partial sets.
example_sentence: He cleans his dentures every night before sleeping. New dentures made it easier for her to eat. The dentist adjusted his dentures for a better fit. Modern dentures look almost like natural teeth.

english_meaning: To strip something of its covering, especially trees, plants or soil. To make a place bare by removing what covers it. To deprive someone or something of an essential quality or resource. In geology, to wear away the surface of land by erosion.
example_sentence: Heavy logging has denuded the hillsides of trees. Floods denuded the fields of fertile topsoil. The company was denuded of its most experienced staff. Strong winds denuded the branches within hours.

english_meaning: The public condemnation of someone or something as being wrong or evil. An act of informing against someone to the authorities. It can also refer to the formal notice of the termination of a treaty.
example_sentence: The politician faced a harsh denunciation from the opposition party. Her denunciation of the corruption within the company was very courageous. The group issued a formal denunciation of the recent violent attacks. The treaty's denunciation led to a period of diplomatic uncertainty.

english_meaning: To say that something is not true. To refuse to admit, accept, allow, or give something. To reject a request, claim, accusation, or fact.
example_sentence: He denied taking the money. The school denied the request for extra leave. No one can deny the importance of clean water. She denied herself sweets during training. The company denied any responsibility for the accident.

english_meaning: Relating to the branch of ethics that focuses on the inherent rightness or wrongness of actions themselves. It suggests that actions are judged based on rules or duties rather than their consequences. It is a normative ethical position.
example_sentence: The philosopher argued from a deontological perspective that lying is always wrong. Deontological ethics prioritize moral rules over the ultimate outcome of an action. Her decision was based on deontological principles rather than practical benefits. Many religious moral codes are essentially deontological in nature.

english_meaning: The study of the nature of duty and obligation. It is an ethical theory that uses rules to distinguish right from wrong. This framework focuses on the morality of actions regardless of their results.
example_sentence: Deontology suggests that we should follow the law even if breaking it might help someone. Students of philosophy often compare deontology with utilitarianism. According to deontology, the ends do not justify the means. Immanuel Kant is a key figure associated with the development of deontology.

english_meaning: The act of leaving a place, especially to start a journey. A deviation from an accepted or usual course. The action of leaving a job or position. The starting point of a train, bus, or flight. A new or different way of doing something.
example_sentence: His sudden departure surprised the whole family. The train departure is scheduled at 6 AM. Her new film is a departure from her usual style. They watched the departure of the ship from the harbor.

english_meaning: To rely on someone or something for support, help, or outcome.
example_sentence: Outcomes depend on data quality. Progress depends on funding. Growth depends on stability. Results depend on accuracy.

english_meaning: To rely on someone or something for support, help, or outcome. To be determined or decided by something else; conditional on. To trust or have confidence in the reliability, ability, or character of someone.
example_sentence: Decisions depend upon evidence. Impacts depend upon exposure. Success depends upon teamwork. Plans depend upon resources.

english_meaning: The act of removing personal or human qualities from something. A feeling of being detached from one's own body, thoughts, or feelings. A mental state in which a person feels unreal or like an outside observer of their own life. Treating people as numbers or cases rather than as individuals. Loss of a sense of personal identity.
example_sentence: Long hours of stress led to a strange feeling of depersonalization. Critics complain about the depersonalization of modern healthcare. Depersonalization can make familiar places feel unreal. The report warns against the depersonalization of students by exam numbers.

english_meaning: To remove personal or individual qualities from something. To treat a person as an object, number, or case rather than a human being. To make something impersonal, standardised, or emotionally neutral. To take the human warmth out of a service or system. To cause someone to feel detached from their own identity.
example_sentence: Automated systems can depersonalize customer service. The hospital was careful not to depersonalize its patients. Large classes tend to depersonalize the learning experience. Do not depersonalize the letter; mention the reader by name.

english_meaning: To show or represent someone or something in a picture, drawing, or photograph. To describe something in words with clear detail. To portray a person, event, or situation in art, film, or writing. To present something in a particular way or from a particular point of view. To give a clear image or impression of something.
example_sentence: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunrise. The novel depicts life in a small fishing town. The film depicts the struggles of ordinary workers. Newspapers often depict the issue as far simpler than it is.

english_meaning: A representation of someone or something in a picture or story. The act of showing or describing something. The way a subject is portrayed in art, film, or writing. A description that creates a clear mental image. A particular version or portrayal of events.
example_sentence: The film's depiction of village life is warm and honest. Her depiction of the accident was vivid and detailed. Some viewers objected to the depiction of violence in the drama. The museum offers a rich depiction of ancient trade routes.

english_meaning: A device or substance used to remove unwanted hair. An electric appliance that pulls out hair from the root. A tool used in salons for hair removal. Any agent that strips hair from the skin. A person or machine that performs depilation.
example_sentence: She bought a small electric depilator for home use. The salon uses a professional depilator for quick treatment. Read the instructions before using any depilator on sensitive skin. A depilator can be painful if the skin is dry.

english_meaning: A cream, lotion, or powder used to remove hair from the skin. Capable of removing hair. Relating to the removal of body hair. A hair-removing product sold for cosmetic use. Describing a treatment that dissolves hair at skin level.
synonyms: ["Hair remover","Epilating cream","Waxing agent","Shaving cream","Hair-removal product","Smoothing agent"]
example_sentence: She applied a depilatory cream before the wedding. Test the depilatory on a small patch of skin first. Some depilatory products can irritate sensitive skin. The chemist stocks several depilatory lotions and waxes.

english_meaning: To get off an aeroplane after landing. To leave an aircraft. To unload passengers or goods from a plane. To disembark from an aircraft in an orderly way. Used in aviation for exiting a plane.
example_sentence: Passengers began to deplane as soon as the doors opened. We were asked to deplane through the rear exit. The crew helped elderly travellers deplane safely. Please remain seated until it is your turn to deplane.

english_meaning: To remove someone from an online platform or social media service. To ban a person or group from a website, app, or public forum. To take away someone's opportunity to speak publicly. To cancel an invitation to speak at an event. To restrict access to the means of reaching an audience.
example_sentence: The network decided to deplatform the account for repeated abuse. Students campaigned to deplatform the controversial speaker. Critics argue that to deplatform someone rarely changes their views. Several apps moved to deplatform accounts spreading false claims.

english_meaning: To use up or reduce the amount of something. To significantly diminish the quantity, supply, or resources of something. It can refer to physical resources like water, money, or energy, or abstract things like strength or confidence.
example_sentence: Overfishing can deplete fish populations quickly. Long hours of work depleted her energy. The war has depleted the country's resources. Frequent withdrawals have depleted his savings.

english_meaning: Reduction or exhaustion of something in quantity or supply. The gradual or significant reduction in the amount, quantity, strength, or availability of something. It is commonly used for natural resources, energy levels, finances, nutrients, and environmental elements.
example_sentence: The depletion of groundwater is becoming a serious problem in many countries. Excessive fishing has caused the depletion of marine life. Continuous stress can lead to the depletion of mental energy. The depletion of forest resources affects climate balance.

english_meaning: Very bad, shameful, or deserving strong disapproval. Something extremely bad in quality or morally wrong, often causing sadness, disappointment, or strong disapproval. It is used for actions, conditions, or behavior that people strongly criticize.
example_sentence:
The living conditions in the camp were deplorable.
His deplorable behavior shocked everyone at the meeting. The road is in a deplorable state after the heavy rains. It is deplorable that such injustice still exists in society.

english_meaning: To strongly disapprove & criticize publicly. To say or think that something is very bad. To criticize something, especially publicly, because you think it is very bad. To feel or express grief for. To regret strongly.
example_sentence: I deplore and condemn this killing. We deeply deplore the loss of life. He said that he deplored all violence.

english_meaning: To move or arrange people or equipment into position for use. To organize, position, or utilize resources, people, or tools effectively for a particular purpose. It often refers to soldiers or military equipment being sent out to specific locations, but it can also describe using plans, strategies, or technology efficiently.
example_sentence: The army was deployed along the border to maintain security. The company plans to deploy new technology next month. Teachers were deployed to different schools after the training. The government deployed additional police during the festival.

english_meaning: The act of distributing or placing troops and weapons in a position for military action. The movement of resources or equipment into an area of operation. The process of bringing a software application into use or making it available for production. The organized distribution of personnel or resources for a specific purpose. The state of being spread out or utilized effectively.
example_sentence: The general ordered the rapid deployment of troops to the border. The software deployment was scheduled for midnight to minimize user disruption. We need to coordinate the deployment of medical supplies to the disaster zone. Efficient deployment of staff is essential for the project's success.

english_meaning: A person who has been officially expelled from a country. Someone forced to leave a country because they have no legal right to stay there. A person sent back to their own country by the authorities. Someone removed from a state as a punishment or under immigration law.
example_sentence: The deportee was put on a flight back to his home country. Several deportees arrived at the airport under police escort. Charities offer support to deportees who have lost everything. The deportee claimed that his life would be in danger back home.

english_meaning: To remove someone from power, or to give formal evidence under oath. To remove a king, president, or leader from position. To give sworn evidence as a witness. To declare or state something formally. To testify officially in legal documents.
example_sentence: The military decided to depose the corrupt ruler. The king was deposed after years of public unrest. She was called to court to depose as a witness. The witness will depose before the judge tomorrow.

english_meaning: The act of removing someone from a position of power or authority. A formal written statement given under oath, especially for use in court. The process by which sediment or material is laid down naturally. The act of depositing something in a particular place. The removal of a monarch or leader by force or authority.
example_sentence: The deposition of the king marked the end of an era. The witness gave her deposition before the trial began. Geologists study the deposition of minerals in the rocks. The deposition of dust on the surface caused problems.

english_meaning: A person who places money or valuables in a bank or safe. Someone who deposits something in a specific location for storage. An individual who entrusts property or money to another for safekeeping. A person or organization that puts materials into a deposit account. Any party making a deposit in an account or facility.
example_sentence: The bank offers special interest rates to long-term depositors. Every depositor received a receipt after the transaction. The number of depositors in the new scheme has increased. Depositors were informed about the changes in policy.

english_meaning: A place where things are stored for safekeeping. A building or institution where money, documents, or valuables are deposited. A repository of information, knowledge, or resources. A person or organization entrusted with keeping something safe. A storage facility for goods or materials.
example_sentence: The bank serves as a depository for valuable documents. The library is a depository of rare books and manuscripts. The company built a new depository for its goods. This archive is a depository of local history.

english_meaning: A place where goods, equipment, fuel, or vehicles are stored. A station or terminal for buses, trains, or other transport. A military storehouse or supply center. A place from which workers, vehicles, or supplies are dispatched.
example_sentence: The bus leaves the depot at six every morning. Food supplies were stored in a central depot. The army established a fuel depot near the base. Damaged trains are repaired at the maintenance depot. Please deliver the equipment to the regional depot.

english_meaning: To make someone morally bad or corrupt. To lead someone into wicked or immoral behavior. To corrupt the character or values of a person or society. To debase or spoil something that was once pure. To cause moral deterioration.
example_sentence: Bad company can deprave even the most innocent minds. Critics argued that such films deprave young viewers. Greed and power depraved the once-honest official. Some believe that violent games can deprave children over time.

english_meaning: Morally corrupt and wicked. Showing complete disregard for accepted standards of decency. Perverted in character or behaviour. Describing an act of extreme cruelty or immorality.
example_sentence: The court described the crime as utterly depraved. He led a depraved and reckless life. Such depraved behaviour shocked the entire town. The novel explores the depraved side of human nature.

english_meaning: The state of being morally corrupt or wicked. Extreme immorality or evil behavior. A depraved act or practice. Moral degradation or decadence in society. The quality of being deeply sinful or corrupt in nature.
example_sentence: The novel portrays the depravity of a corrupt society. He was shocked by the depravity of the criminals' acts. Historians have written about the depravity of ancient tyrants. The report exposed the moral depravity of the officials.

english_meaning: To express strong disapproval of something. To criticize or condemn. To belittle or play down the value of something, often one’s own achievements. To regard as unfavourable or unwise. Also used in technology to mark a feature as outdated and discouraged from use, though still functional.
example_sentence: Critics deprecated the government’s decision to raise taxes again. He tends to deprecate his own efforts even when they are praised. The committee strongly deprecated the use of violence. Many users still rely on the deprecated version of the software. She deprecated his rude behaviour in front of the guests.

english_meaning: Expressing strong disapproval or criticism. Showing modesty by belittling one's own achievements. Discouraging or protesting against something. Speaking or acting in a self-critical or humble way. Expressing polite objection to something.
example_sentence: He gave a deprecating smile when praised. Her deprecating tone made her seem humble. The article was full of deprecating remarks about the plan. He spoke in a deprecating manner about his own success.

english_meaning: In a way that expresses disapproval or criticism. In a self-critical or humble manner. With modesty that downplays one's own achievements. In a way that softly protests or objects to something. With a tone that belittles or minimizes.
example_sentence: He smiled deprecatingly when everyone applauded him. She spoke deprecatingly of her own contribution. The author deprecatingly described his early works. He shrugged deprecatingly at the compliment.

english_meaning: Strong disapproval or criticism of something. The act of expressing regret or dissatisfaction. A humble or self-critical remark or attitude. In computing, the marking of a feature as outdated and no longer recommended. A polite objection or protest against something.
example_sentence: The deprecation of violence must come from every leader. Her deprecation of her own achievements surprised the audience. The developers announced the deprecation of the old software feature. There was general deprecation of the government's new policy.

english_meaning: To decrease in value over time. To lose worth. To reduce the price or value of something. To belittle, undervalue, or speak of with disrespect. Used in finance for assets losing value, and in general speech for making something seem less important or worthy.
example_sentence: New cars depreciate quickly within the first few years. The value of the currency continues to depreciate against the dollar. He should not depreciate the efforts of his hardworking team. Machinery tends to depreciate as it grows older. Critics often depreciate the work of young writers.

english_meaning: A fall in the value of something over time. The reduction in the worth of an asset due to age, wear, or use. A decrease in the value of one currency against another. The act of belittling or speaking of something with little respect.
example_sentence: The car loses value through depreciation every year. Accountants recorded the depreciation of the machinery. The depreciation of the rupee raised import costs. He spoke with clear depreciation of their efforts.

english_meaning: An act of attacking and robbing, causing damage or loss. Plundering or destruction carried out by armed groups. Gradual damage caused by a harmful force, often used in the plural. Serious harm done to property, land, or the environment.
example_sentence: The village suffered years of depredation by raiders. Farmers complained about the depredations of wild boar. The depredation of forests continues at an alarming rate. Historians recorded the depredations of the invading army.

english_meaning: To make someone feel sad and without hope. To reduce the level, value, or activity of something. To press something downwards. To weaken or slow down a process or system.
example_sentence: The bad news depressed the whole family. Poor harvests depressed the price of wheat. Gently depress the button to start the machine. Long working hours can depress the immune system.

english_meaning: Feeling very sad, hopeless, and without energy. Suffering from clinical depression as a medical condition. Suffering from poor economic conditions, as of an area or industry. Pushed down or lower than the surrounding surface.
example_sentence: He felt depressed after losing his job. She is being treated for depressed mood and anxiety. The factory closed in an economically depressed area. The depressed centre of the lid holds the seal.

english_meaning: In a way that makes someone feel sad or without hope. To a degree that causes low spirits. In a discouraging or disheartening manner. Used to stress how disappointing something is.
example_sentence: The results were depressingly poor this term. Prices remain depressingly high for ordinary families. The room was depressingly dark and cold. It is depressingly common to see such waste.

english_meaning: A mental health disorder characterized by persistent sadness and loss of interest. A mood disorder causing feelings of hopelessness, worthlessness, and lack of energy. A period of economic decline with reduced trade and investment. A sunken or hollow area in a surface.
example_sentence: She sought treatment for her depression. Depression is a common mental health condition. The Great Depression lasted from 1929 to 1939. There is a depression in the ground where the meteor struck.

english_meaning: The condition of being without something essential, such as food, shelter, education, or basic comforts. It often refers to social, economic, or personal deficiency.
example_sentence: Children in the remote village suffer from severe deprivation. Sleep deprivation can affect your mood and concentration. Economic deprivation is a major cause of social unrest. The prisoners faced deprivation of basic human rights.

english_meaning: To take something necessary, valuable, or desired away from someone. To prevent a person from having or enjoying a right, benefit, need, or opportunity.
example_sentence: Lack of sleep can deprive the body of energy. The law should not deprive citizens of basic rights. Poverty may deprive children of education. Do not deprive yourself of rest. The injury deprived the team of its best player.

english_meaning: A person appointed to act on behalf of a superior. The second-in-command in an organization or office. An elected representative in some legislatures. A law-enforcement officer who works under a sheriff. Acting as a substitute or assistant to a senior official.
example_sentence: The deputy director chaired the meeting in her absence. A sheriff's deputy arrived at the scene. Each region elected a deputy to the national assembly. He serves as deputy head of the department. The manager appointed a deputy to handle daily operations.

english_meaning: To uproot a plant completely from the ground. To remove people from their native land or culture by force. To destroy or wipe out something entirely, including its roots. To separate someone from their familiar traditions and surroundings.
example_sentence: The storm deracinated several old trees in the park. War can deracinate entire communities within days. The regime tried to deracinate the local language and customs. Migration had deracinated him from his village life.

english_meaning: Pulled up completely by the roots. Removed from one's native land, culture, or community. Feeling cut off from familiar traditions and a sense of belonging. Destroyed or eliminated from the very root.
example_sentence: The deracinated trees lay across the flooded road. He felt deracinated after twenty years abroad. Deracinated families struggled to rebuild their lives. Their deracinated culture survived only in old songs.

english_meaning: To obstruct, interrupt, or cause failure in a process, plan, or situation. To cause a train to go off the tracks.
example_sentence: The accident derailed the train near the station. His careless remarks derailed the meeting. The scandal derailed his political career. Heavy rains derailed our travel plans.

english_meaning: To mock, ridicule, laugh at, or speak about someone or something with contempt. To treat as foolish or worthless.
example_sentence: The critics derided the plan at first. It is cruel to deride someone for a mistake. His classmates derided his old shoes. She did not deride their fears; she listened carefully. Ideas once derided can later become accepted.

english_meaning: Contemptuous ridicule or mockery intended to show that something is considered stupid or worthless. The use of ridicule or scorn to show contempt. It is a harsh form of laughter or verbal attack.
example_sentence: His proposal was met with derision by the rest of the board members. The critics treated the new play with great derision. She could not hide the derision in her voice when she spoke to him. The crowd's derision grew louder as the performer stumbled on stage.
