english_meaning: To criticize or insult indirectly, to make a sarcastic remark.
example_sentence: He made a dig at her weight. Stop digging at your coworkers. That comment was a clear dig at me. She couldn’t resist digging at his mistakes.

english_meaning: To search deeply, either physically or emotionally, to use stored effort or resources.
example_sentence: You’ll have to dig down to find the cause. He dug down into his pockets for coins. She dug down to overcome her fears. The workers dug down to the foundation.

english_meaning: To begin eating eagerly, to start doing something with determination.
example_sentence: Let’s dig in before the food gets cold. Everyone dug in as soon as dinner was served. We need to dig in and finish this project. The soldiers dug in before the storm.

english_meaning: To investigate deeply, to begin eating eagerly, to use effort to uncover or understand something.
example_sentence: He dug into the old files for evidence. She dug into the topic for her research paper. The journalist dug into the story. Let’s dig into our savings to buy a car.

english_meaning: To remove something buried or hidden, to search and find something with difficulty.
example_sentence: He dug out his old coat from the closet. Rescue teams dug out the trapped miners. I dug out my notes for the meeting. They dug out the truth from lies.

english_meaning: To go through something thoroughly to find what is needed. To search carefully by removing or going through things.
example_sentence: I dug through the files for your letter. She dug through her bag to find the keys. The archaeologists dug through the ruins. He dug through memories of the past.

english_meaning: To remove something from the ground or to discover hidden or forgotten information. To find or reveal facts, secrets, or old information that was not known or had been forgotten.
example_sentence: They dug up old records from the archive. The gardener dug up the weeds. Reporters dug up new evidence. He dug up his childhood memories.

english_meaning: To search for and reveal secret or damaging information about someone. To investigate someone’s private or hidden matters to find information that can harm their reputation or expose their mistakes.
example_sentence: The journalist dug up dirt on the politician. They tried to dig up dirt on their rivals. Stop digging up dirt about people. He loves to dig up dirt for gossip.

english_meaning: To bring up old memories, events, or issues that were forgotten or buried. To revisit painful or unpleasant past matters.
synonyms: ["Revive memories","Reopen old wounds","Bring up old issues","Rehash"]
example_sentence: Why do you always dig up the past during arguments? Let bygones be bygones and stop digging up the past. Reporters love to dig up the past of celebrities. Digging up the past won't solve our current problems.

english_meaning: To do something that will cause serious trouble or ruin for yourself. To bring about your own downfall through your own actions. To behave in a way that guarantees future failure or punishment. To create the conditions of your own destruction.
synonyms: ["Bring about one's downfall","Self-destruct","Ruin oneself","Shoot oneself in the foot","Court disaster"]
example_sentence: By lying to the committee, he dug his own grave. If you keep missing deadlines, you are digging your own grave. The company dug its own grave by ignoring customer complaints. She warned him that arguing with the boss was digging his own grave.

english_meaning: To break down food in the stomach and intestines. To process and absorb nutrients from food. To think about and understand information thoroughly. A summary or condensed version of written material.
example_sentence: It takes hours to digest a heavy meal. The body digests proteins into amino acids. I need time to digest this information. He read the monthly news digest.

english_meaning: The process of breaking down food into nutrients the body can absorb. The chemical and mechanical breakdown of food in the digestive system. The conversion of food into substances that can be used for energy and growth. The body's system for processing food from mouth to intestines.
example_sentence: Good digestion is essential for health. Fiber aids in digestion. The digestion process begins in the mouth. Poor digestion can cause discomfort.

english_meaning: Relating to or aiding the process of digestion. Concerning the breakdown of food in the body. Associated with the digestive system and its organs. Having the function of processing food.
example_sentence: Digestive enzymes help break down food molecules. She has a digestive disorder that causes discomfort. The digestive process begins in the mouth. Fiber promotes healthy digestive function.

english_meaning: The group of organs that work together to break down food and absorb nutrients. The biological system consisting of the mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestines, and related organs. The body's mechanism for converting food into energy and waste. The pathway from mouth to anus involved in processing food.
example_sentence: The digestive system processes all the food we eat. Enzymes in the digestive system help break down proteins. A healthy digestive system is crucial for overall wellness. Diseases of the digestive system can affect nutrition absorption.

english_meaning: A person who works remotely using technology while travelling from place to place. Someone with no fixed office who earns a living online. A worker who combines a mobile lifestyle with internet-based employment. A modern professional who chooses location independence.
example_sentence: As a digital nomad, she writes code from a different city each month. Many digital nomads gather in cheap coastal towns. He became a digital nomad after his company allowed remote work. Reliable internet is essential for any digital nomad.

english_meaning: Showing calm seriousness and self-respect. Noble, honorable, and worthy of respect. Formal or stately in manner or appearance. Made to seem important, respectable, or honorable.
example_sentence: She gave a dignified response to the criticism. The old building has a dignified simplicity. He remained dignified even after the defeat. The ceremony dignified the achievements of the volunteers.

english_meaning: To give honour, respect or importance to someone or something. To make a thing appear more impressive than it really is. To treat a simple matter as worthy of serious notice. The word is used positively when something is genuinely honoured and ironically when an unimportant thing is given too much weight.
example_sentence: Her hard work has dignified the entire family. He refused to dignify the silly question with an answer. The award was given to dignify his lifetime services. Such cruel acts should not be dignified by silence. Simple clothes can dignify a person more than expensive ones.

english_meaning: To leave the main subject temporarily in speech or writing. To turn aside from the main topic of an argument or discussion. To wander from a direct course or path. To stray from a planned subject and discuss something else briefly. To deviate from the central theme before returning to it.
example_sentence: I do not want to digress, but this point is also important. The speaker began to digress from the main topic and lost the audience's attention. She often digresses into childhood memories while telling a simple story. Please do not digress; let us focus on the main issue. The writer digresses for a few pages to describe the history of the city.

english_meaning: To cause or allow a building or other structure to fall into a state of decay, neglect, or partial ruin. It refers to the process of deterioration over time due to lack of maintenance. The term is also used in a legal sense regarding the failure to keep a property in good repair.
example_sentence: Without regular maintenance, the salt air will quickly dilapidate the coastal villa. If you neglect the roof, the rain will eventually dilapidate the entire interior. The landlord was sued for choosing to dilapidate the historic building rather than fixing it. Time and weather continue to dilapidate the ancient stone walls.

english_meaning: In a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect. It typically describes buildings, furniture, or vehicles that are falling apart. A structure in this condition often looks shabby and neglected.
example_sentence: The old, dilapidated house on the corner is finally being demolished. They bought a dilapidated barn and converted it into a beautiful modern home. The explorers found a dilapidated ship abandoned on the remote beach. Walking through the dilapidated neighborhood felt like stepping back in time.

english_meaning: Situation with problems. To make difficult choice between things of equal importance
example_sentence: To face dilemma. To be in dilemma

english_meaning: A person who cultivates an area of interest, such as the arts, without real commitment or knowledge. It often describes someone who dabbles superficially in a subject rather than studying it deeply. The term can sometimes imply a lack of serious intent or professional skill.
example_sentence: He is a bit of a dilettante who spends a few weeks on a hobby before moving to the next. The art critic dismissed the young painter as a mere dilettante with no formal training. She enjoys playing the piano as a dilettante rather than pursuing it as a career. Despite his vast collection of books, he was often regarded as a scientific dilettante.

english_meaning: Hard work with care and attention. Careful and continuous effort in doing work or duties with attention, responsibility, and dedication. It refers to working hard with focus and sincerity to achieve good results.
example_sentence: Her diligence helped her achieve excellent grades in school. The manager appreciated the employee’s diligence and honesty. With diligence and patience, he completed the difficult project successfully. Diligence is one of the most important qualities for professional success.

english_meaning: Careful and persistent effort in work or duty. The quality of being hardworking and attentive. Constant and earnest application of one's energy to a task. The word emphasises consistent care, seriousness and steady effort in the performance of any work or responsibility.
example_sentence: The teacher praised the boy for his diligency in studies. Diligency is the key to success in any field. She completed the project with great diligency. His diligency at work earned him a promotion. Without diligency, no real progress is possible.

english_meaning: Hard-working, careful, and showing consistent effort in completing tasks. A person works carefully, consistently, and with great attention to detail. Such a person puts sincere effort into their duties and does not give up easily.
example_sentence: She is a diligent student who always completes her assignments on time. The diligent worker earned the respect of his manager. Through diligent practice, he improved his English speaking skills. The researcher was diligent in collecting accurate data for the project.

english_meaning: To waste time by being slow, indecisive, or delaying unnecessarily.
example_sentence: Stop dilly dallying and get to work. The teacher told the students not to dilly dally and start their work immediately. We lost our chance to buy the tickets since we dilly dallied too long. Stop dilly dallying in the market and choose what you want quickly.

english_meaning: To waste time by being slow or unable to make up one's mind. To move or act far more slowly than necessary. To hesitate and delay instead of getting on with something. Informally, to dawdle when there is work to be done.
antonyms: ["Hurry","Hasten","Rush","Speed up","Act promptly","Decide quickly","Get on with it"]
example_sentence: Stop dilly-dallying and finish your homework. We dilly-dallied so long that we missed the bus. He tends to dilly-dally whenever a decision is required. Do not dilly-dally on the way home from school.

english_meaning: To make a liquid weaker by adding water or another liquid. Also used for making something less strong, less effective, or less concentrated. To reduce the strength, concentration, purity, or effectiveness of something by mixing it with another substance or by weakening its impact. It is commonly used for liquids such as chemicals or drinks, and also used figuratively for ideas, laws, or power that become weaker.
example_sentence: The nurse diluted the medicine with water before giving it to the patient. Adding too much water will dilute the juice. Critics say the new policy may dilute the effectiveness of the law. He tried to dilute his responsibility by blaming others. The drink tasted very dilute because too much water was added. The solution became dilute after mixing it with more liquid.

english_meaning: The act of making a liquid weaker or thinner by adding water or another substance. The state of being diluted. A reduction in strength, value or effect, as of shares or authority.
example_sentence: Add water for a one-in-ten dilution of the syrup. The dilution of the acid must be done carefully. Shareholders objected to the dilution of their holdings. Critics warned of a dilution of academic standards.

english_meaning: A measurable extent such as length, width, height, or depth. An aspect or feature of a situation or problem. The size or scope of something. In physics, one of the fundamental coordinates needed to describe a point in space or time. A particular way of looking at or considering something.
example_sentence: The room's dimensions are perfect for a small office. This discovery adds a new dimension to the research. We must consider every dimension of the problem before deciding. Time is often called the fourth dimension.

english_meaning: Relating to measurements such as length, width, or height. Having a specified number of dimensions, as in three-dimensional. Concerning the size, shape, or extent of something. Adding depth or complexity to something. Used to describe objects that appear to have volume rather than being flat.
example_sentence: The engineer studied the dimensional properties of the new material. Modern films often use three-dimensional imaging. The dimensional analysis helped solve the physics problem. Her artwork has a strong dimensional quality.

english_meaning: To make or become smaller, fewer, or less in size, amount, importance, or intensity. To reduce gradually. To lessen the reputation or value of someone or something. Used both for physical reduction and for decline in significance, power, or quality.
example_sentence: The supply of clean water is rapidly diminishing in many regions. Her enthusiasm did not diminish despite many setbacks. Loud arguments only diminish the respect between family members. The pain began to diminish after taking the medicine. Modern technology has diminished the need for manual labor.

english_meaning: The act of becoming or making something smaller, fewer or less. A reduction in size, importance, power or quantity. A noticeable decrease over time. The word is used in formal contexts to describe a clear lessening of any measurable quality or condition.
example_sentence: There has been a sharp diminution in the number of visitors. The diminution of his powers worried his supporters. The medicine causes a slow diminution of pain. Pollution has led to a diminution of fish in the river. Old age brought a diminution in his physical strength.

english_meaning: To eat dinner. To have one's evening meal, often formally. To entertain someone with a meal. The word usually suggests a slightly formal or social occasion of eating, especially in the evening, either at home, in a restaurant or as a guest.
example_sentence: We usually dine at eight in the evening. They dined together at a small Italian restaurant. The president dined with foreign guests last night. We dined on fresh fish by the seaside. She invited her friends to dine at her house.

english_meaning: A small open boat used for short trips, fishing or as a tender to a larger ship. A small rowing or sailing boat. An inflatable rubber boat used in emergencies. The word refers to various kinds of small boats used for both pleasure and practical purposes on water.
example_sentence: They rowed to the shore in a small dinghy. The sailors used a dinghy to reach the harbour. After the accident, the passengers escaped in an inflatable dinghy. He keeps a dinghy tied to the back of his yacht. The children learned to sail on a wooden dinghy.

english_meaning: The main meal of the day, eaten either in the middle of the day or in the evening. A formal evening meal held for guests or to mark a special occasion. The food that is served at such a meal. An organised social event centred on an evening meal.
example_sentence: We usually have dinner at eight o'clock. She invited us to dinner on Friday. The company held a formal dinner for its staff. Dinner is almost ready, so please wash your hands.

english_meaning: The plates, dishes, bowls, and other items used for serving and eating a meal. A matching set of crockery used at the dining table. Tableware intended especially for dinner. Household items used for presenting food at meals.
example_sentence: They received a set of dinnerware as a wedding gift. The shop sells handmade dinnerware. Please put the dinnerware back in the cupboard. She chose simple white dinnerware for the restaurant.

english_meaning: A large extinct reptile that lived on the earth millions of years ago. Any member of the extinct group of reptiles that dominated the Mesozoic era. A person, idea, or thing that is very old-fashioned and no longer useful. Someone who refuses to accept modern methods or change.
example_sentence: Dinosaurs disappeared from the earth millions of years ago. My son is fascinated by dinosaur bones. Some critics called the old machine an industrial dinosaur. He is a dinosaur who still refuses to use email.

english_meaning: A small hollow mark or dent made in a surface by a blow or pressure. Force, effort, or means by which something is achieved, chiefly used in the phrase by dint of. To make a dent or hollow mark in something. A slight depression left after something has been pressed.
example_sentence: There was a small dint in the side of the car. The hammer left a dint in the soft metal. Only by dint of patience did he finish the task. Heavy boxes had dinted the wooden floor.

english_meaning: Relating to a diocese, the district under the care of a bishop. Belonging to or controlled by a diocese. A bishop who has charge of a diocese. Concerning the administration or affairs of a diocese.
example_sentence: The diocesan office issued a statement this morning. She teaches at a diocesan school. The diocesan met the parish priests last week. Diocesan funds are used to repair old churches.

english_meaning: A district or group of churches under the care and authority of a bishop. The area of responsibility of a bishop in the Christian church. The community of believers living within such a district. An administrative division of certain Christian churches.
example_sentence: The diocese includes more than fifty parishes. He was appointed bishop of the diocese last year. The diocese runs several schools and hospitals. News of the appointment spread quickly through the diocese.

english_meaning: An electronic component that allows current to flow in one direction only. A two-terminal device used to convert alternating current into direct current. A semiconductor device used in rectifiers, radios, and light-emitting circuits.
example_sentence: The diode prevents current from flowing backwards. A faulty diode caused the circuit to fail. Each light-emitting diode glows when current passes through it. He replaced the burnt diode on the circuit board.

english_meaning: Relating to Dionysus, the ancient Greek god of wine, fertility, and drama. Wild, joyful, and lacking restraint. Marked by unrestrained celebration, music, and dancing. Sensual and emotional rather than calm and rational.
example_sentence: The festival had a wild, Dionysiac atmosphere. Critics described the dance as Dionysiac in its energy. Ancient Dionysiac rites involved music and wine. The painting captures a Dionysiac scene of celebration.

english_meaning: A unit of measurement of the refractive power of a lens. A measure equal to the reciprocal of the focal length of a lens in metres. The unit used by opticians to describe the strength of spectacles or contact lenses.
synonyms: ["Lens power unit","Refractive unit","Optical unit","Measure of refraction"]
example_sentence: Her new lenses are rated at two dioptres. The optician measured the correction in dioptres. A dioptre is the standard unit for lens power. He needs a stronger prescription of about three dioptres.

english_meaning: Relating to the refraction of light through a lens. Concerning the measurement of the refractive power of lenses. Assisting vision by means of refraction rather than reflection.
example_sentence: The instrument relies on a dioptric lens system. Dioptric correction improved his distance vision. The telescope uses a dioptric rather than a reflecting design. She studied the dioptric properties of the new glass.

english_meaning: The branch of optics that deals with the refraction of light, especially through lenses. The study and science of refracting optical systems.
example_sentence: He wrote a short treatise on dioptrics. Dioptrics explains how lenses bend light. Students of physics study dioptrics in their optics course. Advances in dioptrics improved early telescope design.

english_meaning: To put something quickly into a liquid and take it out again. To go downward or become lower for a short time. A thick sauce into which food is dipped. A brief swim.
example_sentence: Dip the bread in the olive oil. Sales dipped slightly in the winter months. She served a garlic dip with the bread. We went for a quick dip in the lake.

english_meaning: A sound formed by the combination of two vowels in a single syllable, in which the sound begins as one vowel and moves towards another. A gliding vowel sound. The word is used in linguistics to describe such combined vowel sounds in English and other languages.
example_sentence: The word 'boy' contains the diphthong 'oi'. English has several common diphthongs such as the one in 'house'. The teacher explained diphthongs with clear examples. Learners often find diphthongs difficult to pronounce. A diphthong is different from a pure vowel sound.

english_meaning: A very large plant-eating dinosaur with a long neck, a long whip-like tail, and four thick legs. A genus of huge sauropod dinosaurs that lived in the late Jurassic period. A fossil skeleton or model of such a dinosaur displayed in a museum.
example_sentence: The museum displays a huge Diplodocus skeleton in its main hall. A Diplodocus could grow more than twenty-five metres long. Children gathered around the model of the Diplodocus. The Diplodocus used its long neck to reach low plants.

english_meaning: Having two complete sets of chromosomes, one from each parent. Describing a cell or organism with paired chromosomes. A cell that contains the full number of chromosomes typical of a species. Relating to the normal chromosome condition of most body cells.
example_sentence: Human body cells are diploid. A diploid cell contains forty-six chromosomes in humans. The zygote is diploid because it receives chromosomes from both parents. Most animals are diploid organisms.

english_meaning: An official document or certificate showing that a person has completed a course of study. A qualification awarded by a college, school, or training institution. A certificate given as evidence of success in an examination or programme. A course of study leading to such a certificate.
example_sentence: She received a diploma in graphic design last year. He hung his diploma on the office wall. The college offers a two-year diploma in nursing. A diploma is not the same as a full degree.

english_meaning: The practice of managing relationships, negotiations, and communication between countries, organizations, or people in a peaceful and skillful way. The art and practice of conducting negotiations and maintaining good relations between nations, governments, organizations, or individuals. It involves tact, respect, communication, compromise, and peaceful conflict resolution rather than force or confrontation.
example_sentence: Good diplomacy helped the two countries avoid a conflict. The ambassador used diplomacy to settle the disagreement peacefully. She handled the difficult meeting with remarkable diplomacy. Effective diplomacy strengthens international cooperation and trust.

english_meaning: A person who has been awarded a diploma, especially in a medical or professional field. A holder of a diploma indicating specialist competence in a particular field. Used specifically in medicine to describe a doctor who has passed a specialty board examination.
example_sentence: She became a diplomate of the American Board of Internal Medicine after years of rigorous training. The hospital required all consultants to be board-certified diplomates in their respective specialities. He was proud to become a diplomate and display his credentials in his consultation room. The diplomate in cardiology was considered one of the foremost specialists in the region. Becoming a diplomate requires passing a comprehensive examination set by a recognised professional board.

english_meaning: Relating to diplomacy or international relations between countries. Skillful and tactful in dealing with people, especially in sensitive situations. Able to handle delicate matters without causing offense. Showing the ability to negotiate, mediate, and maintain good relationships through careful and polite communication. Someone or something connected with the management of relations between nations or characterized by tact, sensitivity, and skill in handling people and situations.
example_sentence: The diplomatic talks between the two nations ended successfully. She gave a diplomatic answer that did not offend anyone. He is known for his diplomatic skills in handling difficult clients. The ambassador attended a diplomatic meeting at the embassy. A diplomatic approach is needed to resolve this dispute peacefully.

english_meaning: An uncontrollable craving for alcoholic drinks. A condition in which a person has periodic, intense urges to drink alcohol excessively. Chronic and compulsive alcoholism. A psychological dependence on alcohol that leads to repeated heavy drinking. An abnormal and irresistible desire for intoxicating liquor.
example_sentence: His dipsomania slowly destroyed his career and his family life. She joined a support group to overcome her dipsomania. The novel describes a poet who struggled with dipsomania for years. Doctors treated his dipsomania with therapy and medication.

english_meaning: Extremely serious, urgent, or terrible. Causing great fear, anxiety, or distress. Describing a situation that is very bad and likely to get worse if not addressed. Used for warnings, consequences, needs, or conditions that are critical and demand immediate attention.
example_sentence: The country is facing dire economic conditions. He gave a dire warning about climate change. The flood victims are in dire need of food and shelter. Failure to act now could have dire consequences. The patient is in a dire state and needs immediate surgery.

english_meaning: Going straight from one point to another without stopping or changing direction. Honest and clear in speech or behavior; saying exactly what you mean. To control, manage, or guide an activity, organization, or group of people. To aim or point something in a particular direction.
example_sentence: We took a direct flight from Karachi to Dubai. She gave a direct answer to the journalist's question. He was chosen to direct the new film. Please direct your complaints to the manager.

english_meaning: The way or path along which someone or something moves, faces, or points. Guidance or instructions about how to do something or where to go. Control, management, or leadership of an activity or organization. A general aim, purpose, or course of development.
example_sentence: The wind suddenly changed direction during the storm. Can you give me directions to the nearest hospital? The company is moving in a new direction under its young CEO. The project was completed under the direction of an experienced engineer.

english_meaning: Relating to direction or the way something moves or points. Designed to send or receive signals in a particular direction. Giving guidance about which way to go.
example_sentence: The hikers followed the directional signs through the forest. The antenna is highly directional and must face the transmitter. Directional microphones pick up sound from only one direction. The airport installed new directional lighting on the runway.

english_meaning: Having no clear direction, purpose, or goal. Lacking guidance or leadership. Moving or drifting without a definite aim.
example_sentence: After losing his job, he felt directionless for months. The company seemed directionless under weak leadership. The boat drifted directionless in the open sea. Without a plan, the project quickly became directionless.

english_meaning: An official instruction or order issued by an authority. A formal guideline that tells people what to do or how to act. Giving clear direction or guidance.
example_sentence: The government issued a new directive on workplace safety. All departments must follow the directive from head office. The European Union passed a directive on data protection. The manager's directive was clear: finish the project by Monday.

english_meaning: In a direct way; without anything or anyone in between. Immediately; without delay. In a clear and honest manner; exactly.
example_sentence: The new road connects the village directly to the highway. Please report any problems directly to the supervisor. He looked directly into her eyes and told the truth. The manager will contact you directly after the meeting.

english_meaning: A person who manages or controls an organization, company, or department. A member of the board that governs a company. The person responsible for the artistic and creative aspects of a film, play, or television program.
example_sentence: The director of the museum welcomed the visitors personally. She was appointed as the new director of the hospital. The film director explained his vision to the actors. The board of directors approved the annual budget.

english_meaning: A department or section of a large organization responsible for a particular area of work. The group of directors who manage a company or organization. The office or position of a director.
example_sentence: She works for the directorate of education in the regional government. The new policy was approved by the directorate last week. He was appointed head of the finance directorate. The directorate announced changes to the examination system.

english_meaning: Relating to a director or to the work of directing. Connected with the management or leadership of an organization. Relating to the duties, style, or position of a director, especially in film or theater.
example_sentence: The film marks her directorial debut after years as an actress. His directorial style is known for long, quiet scenes. The board praised his directorial skills during the crisis. She received an award for her directorial achievements in theater.

english_meaning: A sad song or poem for a dead person. A slow and mournful song, poem, or piece of music performed at funerals or during times of grief. It expresses sorrow, loss, and mourning for someone who has died.
example_sentence: The choir sang a dirge during the funeral ceremony. The poem sounded like a dirge filled with sorrow and loss. Slow drums played a dirge as the procession moved forward. His speech turned into a dirge about the decline of old traditions.

english_meaning: A type of sugar molecule formed when two simple sugars (monosaccharides) join together by a chemical bond. A carbohydrate consisting of two monosaccharide units linked together. Common examples include sucrose, lactose, and maltose. It is broken down in the body into two simple sugars during digestion to provide energy.
example_sentence: Sucrose is a common disaccharide found in table sugar. Lactose is the disaccharide present in milk. Maltose is a disaccharide produced during the digestion of starch. The body breaks down each disaccharide into simpler sugars for energy. Students studied the structure of a disaccharide in their chemistry class.

english_meaning: To have a different opinion from someone else. To fail to correspond or match with other facts or figures. To argue or quarrel about something. To have a bad effect on someone, especially food on the stomach.
example_sentence: I completely disagree with your conclusion. The two reports disagree on the number of victims. They disagreed about the best route to take. Spicy food seems to disagree with him.

english_meaning: A feeling of sadness because something did not happen as hoped. The state of having one's expectations unfulfilled. A person or thing that fails to meet expectations. An unhappy result or outcome.
example_sentence: He could not hide his disappointment at the result. The film was a great disappointment to its fans. To her disappointment, the shop was already closed. Life is full of small disappointments and small joys.

english_meaning: Strong moral disapproval. Formal or serious condemnation of someone's behaviour. A feeling that something is morally wrong. Public expression of censure or blame.
example_sentence: His actions were met with public disapprobation. She expressed her disapprobation of the committee's decision. The scandal drew widespread disapprobation from the community. Their silence spoke of quiet disapprobation.

english_meaning: The feeling of not liking or agreeing with something. An expression of criticism or objection. A negative judgement about someone's behaviour or ideas. Refusal to give consent or support.
example_sentence: He shook his head in clear disapproval. Her disapproval of the plan was obvious to everyone. The proposal met with strong disapproval from the committee. They expressed their disapproval by walking out of the meeting.

english_meaning: To have or express a negative opinion about something. To think that something is wrong or unacceptable. To refuse to approve, accept, or officially permit something. To show dislike or objection towards someone's behaviour.
example_sentence: Her father strongly disapproved of the marriage. The board disapproved the request for extra funding. Many citizens disapprove of the new tax policy. I disapprove of the way he spoke to his colleagues.

english_meaning: Showing that you do not like or agree with something. Expressing criticism or a negative opinion. Indicating displeasure through words, looks, or behaviour. Judgemental in attitude towards someone's actions.
example_sentence: She gave him a disapproving look across the table. His parents were disapproving of his choice of career. A disapproving murmur ran through the audience. The teacher's disapproving tone made the students uneasy.

english_meaning: In a way that shows criticism or dislike. With an attitude of objection or displeasure. In a manner expressing negative judgement. Showing that one does not agree.
example_sentence: She looked at him disapprovingly and said nothing. The old man shook his head disapprovingly. He frowned disapprovingly at the noisy children. They spoke disapprovingly about the new rules.

english_meaning: To take weapons away from a person, group, or country. To give up or reduce one's own weapons and armed forces. To make a bomb or explosive device safe. To remove someone's anger or suspicion by being charming or friendly.
example_sentence: The police managed to disarm the attacker without injury. Both nations agreed to disarm after the treaty. Experts worked for hours to disarm the bomb. Her warm smile completely disarmed the angry customer.

english_meaning: To separate or disconnect oneself or something from another person, group, or idea. To break the connection or association between things. To distance oneself from someone or something.
example_sentence: He tried to disassociate himself from the corrupt group. The company disassociated itself from the controversial advertisement. She wants to disassociate her name from the scandal. It is hard to disassociate the singer from her famous song. The party disassociated itself from the extremist views.

english_meaning: Unexpected event, Very bad accident, Flood or fire that kills a lot of people, Unwanted mishap, Sudden misfortune
example_sentence: Thousand of people died in disaster. The party's first night was a total disaster. As a teacher he's a disaster.

english_meaning: To deny any responsibility for or connection with something. To refuse to acknowledge, accept, or support. To deny any involvement or association with something, often publicly or formally.
example_sentence: The politician disavowed the controversial statement made by his aide. She disavowed any knowledge of the incident. The company disavowed the use of unsafe practices in its factories. He disavowed his previous beliefs after learning new evidence.

english_meaning: Refusal to acknowledge, support, or accept something. A formal or strong denial of responsibility, support, or connection to something. It often implies publicly stating that one does not agree with or endorse a statement, action, or belief.
example_sentence: His disavowal of the controversial statement surprised everyone. The politician issued a disavowal of the actions taken by his party. She made a public disavowal of her former beliefs. The company’s disavowal of the faulty product angered customers.

english_meaning: Someone who openly rejects or denies involvement in something. This can include denying responsibility for actions, refusing to support a belief, or distancing themselves from a group, statement, or decision. It is commonly used in legal, political, or formal contexts.
example_sentence: The politician acted as a disavower of the controversial statement. He became a disavower of his earlier beliefs after the debate. The company played the role of a disavower to avoid legal responsibility. A disavower often tries to separate themselves from public criticism.

english_meaning: To break up or dissolve an organization, group, team, or society. To officially stop existing as a group. To cause members of a group to separate and go their own ways. To formally end the activities of a group, especially a military unit, band, or organization, so that it no longer functions as a single body.
example_sentence: The committee decided to disband after completing its task. The army unit was disbanded after the war ended. The famous music band disbanded last year due to internal conflicts. The government ordered the militant group to disband immediately. The club had to disband because of a lack of funding.

english_meaning: The refusal or inability to accept that something is true. A feeling of shock or surprise that something has happened. Lack of faith or religious belief. The state of doubting a statement or claim. An expression of amazement at something hard to believe.
example_sentence: She stared at the letter in complete disbelief. His story was met with disbelief by the whole class. There was disbelief among fans after the sudden defeat. He shook his head in disbelief when he heard the price.

english_meaning: To distribute or pay out money, funds, or resources to different people, organizations, or purposes. It is often used in official, financial, or administrative contexts such as banks, governments, or companies.
example_sentence: The bank will disburse the loan within three working days. The government disbursed relief funds to flood victims. The company disburses salaries at the end of each month. The NGO disbursed financial assistance to needy families.

english_meaning: To remove something that is no longer useful, needed, or wanted. It can also mean rejecting or abandoning an idea, plan, or item. In card games, it refers to putting a card out of play. Something that has been thrown away or rejected.
example_sentence: Discarded food containers and bottles littered the streets. Cut the melon in half and discard the seeds. He makes toys from things people discard. The company discarded outdated equipment. He discarded the idea after realizing it was impractical. In the card game, she discarded her lowest card.

english_meaning: To recognize, notice, understand, or identify something clearly, especially something not obvious. To perceive or detect something with careful observation, intelligence, or insight. It is often used when someone understands subtle differences, hidden meanings, truth, quality, or details that are difficult for others to notice.
example_sentence: She could discern a smile on his face even in the dark. It is difficult to discern the difference between the two paintings. A wise leader can discern truth from lies. The teacher quickly discerned the student's hidden talent.

english_meaning: The ability to judge well. Good judgment and understanding. Keen insight or perception. The quality of being able to grasp and comprehend what is obscure. The power to see and understand things clearly, especially to distinguish between what is true and false, or right and wrong. A sharp sense of judgment that allows a person to make wise decisions and recognize subtle differences in situations or people.
example_sentence: She showed great discernment in choosing the right candidate for the job. His discernment of character helped him avoid dishonest business partners. The judge is respected for his discernment and fairness. It takes discernment to understand the deeper meaning of poetry. Parents need discernment when guiding their children's decisions.

english_meaning: A follower or learner. A person who follows a teacher, leader, or philosophy and learns from them with commitment and loyalty. Often used in religious, academic, or ideological contexts.
example_sentence: She became a disciple of the famous philosopher. The prophet taught his disciples important moral lessons. As a disciple, he followed his mentor with great dedication. Every disciple is expected to respect the teachings they receive.

english_meaning: Relating to or used for discipline. It refers to the enforcement of rules and the maintenance of order within an organization or system. It often involves corrective measures or training to ensure behavioral compliance.
example_sentence: The company initiated a disciplinary hearing against the employee. He was sent to a disciplinary committee to address his misconduct. Educational institutions often have clear disciplinary guidelines for students. The manager took a disciplinary approach to solve the recurring issues.

english_meaning: An official action taken against an individual for breaking rules or performance failure. It typically involves a series of steps ranging from warnings to termination. It serves as a formal response to misconduct in professional or institutional settings.
example_sentence: The supervisor warned that further lateness would result in disciplinary action. After the investigation, the board decided to take disciplinary action. Failure to follow safety protocols will lead to immediate disciplinary action. Disciplinary action was taken to maintain workplace integrity.

english_meaning: Training that produces obedience, self-control, or a particular skill. A branch of knowledge or field of study. The practice of making people obey rules and standards of behavior, with punishments when rules are broken. Controlled behavior resulting from such training. The ability to control one's feelings and overcome weaknesses to follow a course of action. To punish or correct someone for misbehavior. To train someone to follow rules.
example_sentence: Discipline is essential for success in any field of life. The teacher maintained strict discipline in the classroom. Mathematics is a difficult academic discipline. The soldier was disciplined for violating the rules. Self-discipline helps a person achieve long-term goals. Sports require both physical training and mental discipline.

english_meaning: To deny or refuse to acknowledge any connection with, responsibility for, or knowledge of something. To renounce a claim or right to something. To state that one is not responsible for or associated with something. To reject or repudiate formally.
example_sentence: The company disclaimed any responsibility for the accident. He quickly disclaimed knowledge of the illegal activities. The website contains a disclaimer of liability. She disclaimed all interest in the inheritance.

english_meaning: A statement that denies responsibility for something. An official statement intended to limit legal liability, clarify that the writer or speaker does not take responsibility for certain information, actions, or outcomes, or to caution the reader/listener about something.
example_sentence: The website includes a disclaimer stating that it is not responsible for third-party content. He signed the contract after reading the disclaimer carefully. The email contained a disclaimer warning about confidential information. The product packaging had a disclaimer about potential side effects.

english_meaning: To make secret or new information known or public. To reveal or uncover something previously hidden or unknown. To allow something to be seen or known. To provide information that was previously kept confidential.
example_sentence: The company refused to disclose its financial records. He disclosed the truth about what happened that night. The document discloses important information about the project. She was reluctant to disclose personal details.

english_meaning: The action of making new or secret information known or public. The revelation of previously hidden facts or details. Information that is disclosed or revealed. A legal obligation to reveal certain information, especially in business or financial contexts.
example_sentence: Full disclosure of financial information is required by law. The disclosure of confidential documents caused controversy. Companies must make proper disclosure to shareholders. The witness made important disclosures during the trial.

english_meaning: The act of making secret or new information known. Information that has been revealed to the public. The legal duty to reveal relevant facts or documents. The uncovering of something that was previously hidden.
example_sentence: The disclosure of the report shocked the public. Companies must make full disclosure of their earnings. He signed an agreement preventing disclosure of the details. Her disclosure about the accident helped the investigation.

english_meaning: A complete list of the recordings made by a musician or band. The study and cataloguing of sound recordings. A published catalogue of records on a particular subject.
example_sentence: The band's discography spans over thirty years. You can find her full discography on the website. His discography includes rare live recordings. The book contains a detailed discography of folk music.

english_meaning: Having the shape of a disc. Flat, thin, and circular in form. Resembling a disc in appearance. Used in biology and medicine to describe structures, cells, or rashes that have a round, flat shape. Often applied to certain skin conditions, flowers, or anatomical parts that are disc-shaped.
example_sentence: The patient was diagnosed with a discoid skin rash on his arm. The flower has a discoid shape with petals around the center. Red blood cells are typically discoid in form. The artist painted a discoid sun above the horizon. Scientists examined the discoid structure under the microscope.

english_meaning: To make someone feel uneasy, embarrassed, or confused. To defeat or thwart someone's plans. To upset or disturb someone's composure. To cause a person to lose confidence by surprising or confronting them unexpectedly. To frustrate the plans or expectations of another person, often resulting in awkwardness or embarrassment.
example_sentence: The unexpected question seemed to discomfit the speaker on stage. His sharp criticism discomfited the entire panel. The team's surprise attack discomfited their opponents. She tried not to let his rude remarks discomfit her. The lawyer's clever argument discomfited the witness completely.

english_meaning: A botanical term used to describe plants or flowers whose disc florets and ray florets are clearly distinct from each other. Relating to a flower head in which the central disc flowers are separate and different from the outer ray flowers. Used in the classification of composite flowers in plant taxonomy.
example_sentence: The botanist identified the plant as a disconanthous species. Many sunflower family members display a disconanthous flower head. The textbook explained the structure of disconanthous flowers in detail. Researchers studied the disconanthous arrangement of petals under the lens. A disconanthous bloom is easy to distinguish from a uniform flower head.

english_meaning: To make someone unhappy or dissatisfied. To cause a feeling of dissatisfaction, unrest, or discontent in a person. It refers to disturbing someone’s peace of mind or making them unhappy with a situation.
example_sentence: The unfair decision discontended the workers. His harsh words discontended his friends. Continuous failure can discontend even a strong person. The sudden change in plans discontended the entire team.

english_meaning: To make someone dissatisfied or unhappy. A feeling of dissatisfaction or unhappiness with a situation, condition, or authority.
example_sentence: The students were discontent with the new grading system. A discontent workforce can lower productivity. The manager’s unfair decision discontented the employees. Rising prices discontented many citizens. Public discontent grew after the government increased taxes. Workers showed their discontent by organizing a peaceful protest. Her constant complaints revealed her deep discontent with the job.

english_meaning: To disagree or clash. To be in conflict or disagreement with someone or something; to be out of harmony. Disagreement or conflict. A state of conflict, tension, or lack of harmony among people, ideas, or sounds.
example_sentence: His views discord with the company’s policy. The facts presented discord with her statement. Their actions discord with their promises. There was discord in the boardroom over the decision. Family discord can harm relationships. Political discord delayed the legislation.

english_meaning: To cause someone to lose confidence, enthusiasm, or hope. To try to prevent something by expressing disapproval or raising objections. To make someone less willing to do something. To deter a person from a course of action through doubt, warning, or difficulty. To dishearten or dampen the spirit and motivation of another person.
example_sentence: Failure should not discourage you from trying again. The teacher tried to discourage cheating during the exam. Heavy rain discouraged people from going outside. His parents discouraged him from quitting his studies. The harsh criticism discouraged the young writer.

english_meaning: Written or spoken communication or debate. A formal discussion of a topic in speech or writing. A long and serious treatment of a subject. Conversation or dialogue between people. To speak or write authoritatively about a topic. Discourse refers both to the exchange of ideas through conversation and to formal, extended treatments of specific subjects in lectures, essays, or scholarly works.
example_sentence: The professor delivered a fascinating discourse on modern philosophy. Public discourse on climate change has grown more urgent in recent years. The book is essentially a discourse on the nature of human freedom. He loves to discourse at length about ancient civilizations. Healthy political discourse is essential for any democracy.

english_meaning: Showing bad manners and a lack of respect. Rude or impolite in speech or behaviour. Failing to show the ordinary courtesy expected of people. Inconsiderate towards the feelings of others. Behaving in an unfriendly and disrespectful way.
example_sentence: It was discourteous of him to leave without saying goodbye. The staff apologised for the discourteous reply. She found his interruption quite discourteous. Ignoring a guest's question is discourteous.

english_meaning: To make a discovery that turns out to be worthless or false. To find something that seems important but proves imaginary. To uncover a confusing and useless muddle.
example_sentence: The inspector thought he had a clue but discovered a mare's nest. Their long research only discovered a mare's nest. He boasted of a great find and discovered a mare's nest. The rumour led the police to discover a mare's nest.

english_meaning: Careful in speech and behavior so that secrets or private matters are not revealed. Showing good judgment and self control in speech or actions, especially when dealing with private or sensitive information. A discreet person knows what should remain confidential and behaves in a careful and respectful way.
example_sentence: He was very discreet, only saying what was necessary. With a discreet gesture, she signalled to her husband that she was ready to leave the party. The family made discreet enquiries about his background. You ought to make a few discreet enquiries before you sign anything.

english_meaning: A lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts. It represents an illogical or unexplained difference between things that should be the same. Often used in accounting or data analysis to describe errors.
example_sentence: There was a slight discrepancy between the two financial reports. The police found a major discrepancy in the witness's statement. We need to resolve the discrepancy in our inventory counts. The discrepancy between his words and actions was obvious.

english_meaning: Not being in agreement or harmony. Showing a difference between two things that should be the same.
example_sentence: Discrepant results have been described by one group of scientists. These findings are discrepant with data from several other studies. In case discrepant documents are presented, we shall deduct USD 55.00 for each discrepant.

english_meaning: Separate, distinct, or individually different. Something that is clearly separate or distinct from other things. It refers to items, units, or elements that are individually separate and not continuous or connected. In mathematics and science, it also describes values or data that exist as individual units rather than a continuous range.
example_sentence: The data was divided into discrete categories for analysis. Each discrete unit in the system performs a different function. The island ecosystem consists of several discrete habitats. In mathematics, integers are discrete numbers.

english_meaning: The freedom or power to decide what should be done in a particular situation. Individual choice or judgment. The ability to make intelligent decisions especially in everyday matters. The trait of judging wisely and objectively.
example_sentence: This is confidential, but I know that I can rely on your discretion. Jane is the soul of discretion (= you can trust her). You must show discretion in choosing your friend. Discretion is the better part of valor.

word: Discretion is the better part of valour
english_meaning: It is wiser to be cautious than to take unnecessary risks. Caution and good judgment are more valuable than reckless bravery. Avoiding danger sensibly is a form of true courage. Knowing when not to fight shows real wisdom.
example_sentence: He walked away from the argument, believing discretion is the better part of valour. Rather than climb in the storm, they decided discretion is the better part of valour. The captain retreated, knowing discretion is the better part of valour. She kept quiet in the meeting because discretion is the better part of valour.

english_meaning: A function, formula, or factor that allows for the distinguishing or grouping of different elements. In mathematics, it specifically refers to the part of a quadratic formula that determines the nature of roots. In statistics, it is a variable that helps distinguish between different groups.
example_sentence: The discriminant of a quadratic equation is given by b squared minus four ac. Researchers used literacy as a discriminant for their social study. This diagnostic tool acts as a discriminant between different types of infections. The discriminant analysis proved that the groups were statistically distinct.

english_meaning: To recognize a distinction or differentiate between people or things. It can also mean to treat a person or group unfairly based on characteristics like race or gender. It involves the ability to perceive subtle differences accurately.
example_sentence: It is difficult to discriminate between the two shades of blue. The law prohibits employers to discriminate against workers based on age. A connoisseur can easily discriminate between cheap and expensive wine. Babies can discriminate their mother's voice from other people.

english_meaning: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people. It is also the ability to perceive fine differences between things. In social contexts, it often refers to bias and systemic inequality.
example_sentence: The organization is committed to fighting racial discrimination. The restaurant was sued for discrimination against disabled patrons. His keen discrimination allowed him to choose only the finest fabrics. Employment discrimination based on religion is illegal in many countries.

english_meaning: Talking about a subject in detail with one or more people in order to share ideas, exchange opinions, or reach a decision. The act of considering, debating, or examining a topic through conversation. Engaging in an exchange of views about something, often to analyze it or find a solution.
example_sentence: They are discussing the new project in the meeting room. We were discussing politics when you called. The committee is discussing the budget for next year. The friends spent hours discussing their travel plans. The teacher is discussing the lesson with her students.

english_meaning: The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration or respect. It involves a feeling of contempt or looking down upon something as inferior. To be unworthy of dignity.
example_sentence: She looked at his messy room with an expression of pure disdain. He treated the suggestions of his subordinates with open disdain. The aristocrat walked past the beggars with a look of cold disdain. Many critics disdain popular culture as being shallow and unrefined.

english_meaning: A disorder of structure or function in a living organism that produces specific symptoms. An illness or sickness affecting the body or mind. A harmful condition that affects normal functioning. A particular quality or disposition regarded as adversely affecting a person or group.
example_sentence: Heart disease is preventable through lifestyle changes. The disease spread rapidly through the community. Doctors are searching for a cure for this disease. Early detection of disease improves treatment outcomes.

english_meaning: The state of being separated from the physical body. The idea of existing without a physical form, often spiritual or abstract. In literature/philosophy it may refer to detachment of mind, soul, or identity from the body.
example_sentence: Some religions describe death as the disembodiment of the soul from the body. Virtual reality creates a strange feeling of disembodiment, as if the body is left behind. The novel explores the disembodiment of consciousness in a digital world. Meditation can sometimes bring a sense of disembodiment from physical reality.

english_meaning: Disappointed by someone or something previously respected or admired. No longer believing that someone or something is good or worthwhile. Freed from illusion or false belief. Feeling dissatisfied or disillusioned after discovering the truth about a person, situation, or ideal that once seemed attractive.
example_sentence: Many voters became disenchanted with the political leadership. She felt disenchanted with her job after years of hard work. He grew disenchanted with city life and moved to a village. The fans were disenchanted by the team's poor performance. After the scandal, people became disenchanted with the organization.

english_meaning: To separate or release something from a connection or attachment. To withdraw from involvement in an activity or situation. To detach oneself emotionally or physically from another person. To free something that is caught or held. To stop being involved or participating in something, especially conflict or combat.
example_sentence: He tried to disengage his hand from her tight grip. The army was ordered to disengage from the conflict zone. She decided to disengage from the toxic relationship. Please disengage the clutch before changing the gear. It is sometimes wise to disengage from heated political arguments.

english_meaning: To bring shame or dishonor upon someone or something. Loss of honor, respect, or reputation due to shameful action.
example_sentence: The officer was disgraced for his corrupt actions. Cheating in exams disgraces the reputation of the school. He disgraced his family by lying in court. He was dismissed from the army in disgrace after being caught cheating. The scandal brought great disgrace to the politician’s family. Cheating in an exam is a disgrace to the student’s character.

english_meaning: Shockingly unacceptable. Bringing shame or dishonor. Deserving strong disapproval because of being morally wrong or extremely bad. Causing loss of respect or reputation. Used to describe behavior, actions, or conditions that are scandalous, shameful, or socially unacceptable.
example_sentence: His disgraceful behavior shocked everyone at the party. It is disgraceful that such corruption exists in the system. The condition of the public hospital is absolutely disgraceful. The team's disgraceful performance disappointed the fans. Lying to your parents is a disgraceful act.

english_meaning: In a manner that brings shame, dishonor, or strong disapproval. Behaving in a shameful or scandalous way. In a way that deserves to be condemned because of being morally wrong or socially unacceptable. Acting in a manner that damages one's own reputation or the honor of others.
example_sentence: He behaved disgracefully at the official dinner. The players acted disgracefully after losing the match. She was disgracefully dismissed from her job for theft. The minister disgracefully misused his authority. They treated the elderly man disgracefully.

english_meaning: Change appearance. To prevent giving away or revealing (something secret). To furnish with a false appearance.
example_sentence: The hijackers were heavily disguised. She disguised herself as a boy. He disguised his true intentions.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of dislike or disapproval caused by something unpleasant. A sense of revulsion or nausea aroused by something offensive. Deep displeasure at moral wrongdoing or bad behaviour. To cause someone to feel strong distaste or revulsion. A reaction of horror or aversion to something repulsive.
example_sentence: She turned away in disgust at the sight of the rotting food. The audience watched the violent scene with growing disgust. Many citizens expressed disgust at the politician's corrupt behaviour. The dirty kitchen disgusted her so much that she refused to eat. He shook his head in disgust and walked out of the room.

english_meaning: Causing a strong feeling of dislike, revulsion, or nausea. Extremely unpleasant or offensive. Morally or socially unacceptable in a way that produces anger or disapproval. Used to describe things that are repulsive in smell, taste, sight, or behavior.
example_sentence: The smell coming from the kitchen was absolutely disgusting. It is disgusting how some people litter in public parks. The food at the restaurant tasted disgusting. His disgusting behavior offended everyone present. The condition of the washroom was simply disgusting.

english_meaning: To serve food onto plates for people to eat. To give out or distribute something, often freely or in large amounts. To give criticism, punishment, or advice to others. To hand out money or resources generously or carelessly.
example_sentence: She began to dish out the rice as soon as the guests arrived. The coach is quick to dish out advice to young players. He can dish out criticism but cannot take it himself. The charity dishes out free meals to the homeless every evening.

english_meaning: Untidy in appearance, especially the hair, clothes, or general look. Looking messy, ruffled, or in disorder. Not neatly arranged or groomed. Used to describe a person whose appearance is disordered, often due to haste, sleep, stress, or carelessness.
example_sentence: He arrived at the office looking tired and disheveled. Her disheveled hair showed that she had just woken up. The disheveled appearance of the room suggested a burglary. After the long journey, the children looked disheveled. He gave a presentation despite his disheveled clothes.

english_meaning: The act of not being truthful or fair. Behavior involving lies, cheating, or deceit. A lack of integrity in a person's character. The tendency to hide the truth for personal benefit. Fraudulent or misleading conduct.
example_sentence: His dishonesty cost him his job and reputation. Dishonesty in business destroys long-term trust. She was disappointed by her friend's dishonesty. No relationship can survive constant dishonesty.

english_meaning: To free someone from a false belief or mistaken idea. The state of being disappointed after learning the truth. To cause someone to lose faith or admiration for something.
example_sentence: I hate to disillusion you, but the offer is not real. His experience abroad only served to disillusion him. There was a growing disillusion among the supporters. She spoke with a deep sense of disillusion.

english_meaning: Disappointed after discovering that something is not as good as one believed. Having lost faith or trust in something previously admired. Freed from a false belief or idealistic notion.
example_sentence: She became disillusioned with politics after years of broken promises. Many young workers are disillusioned with the company. He grew disillusioned with the fame he had once craved. The fans were disillusioned by their idol's behaviour.

english_meaning: A feeling of disappointment resulting from the discovery that something is not as good, true, or ideal as one believed. The loss of a previously held belief or ideal.
example_sentence: His disillusionment with politics grew after years of broken promises. She felt deep disillusionment after the relationship ended badly. The disillusionment of the voters was visible at the polls. His disillusionment with religion began in his early twenties.

english_meaning: Not having a physical body. Existing without a material form. Used to describe spirits, souls, or beings that have no bodily form. Freed or separated from the body. Often used in religious, spiritual, or philosophical contexts to refer to immaterial existence.
example_sentence: Some philosophers believe in disincarnate souls after death. The novel describes a disincarnate spirit roaming the old castle. Religious texts often mention disincarnate beings. He claimed to have sensed a disincarnate presence in the room. The lecture explored the concept of a disincarnate existence.

english_meaning: To clean something with a substance that kills germs and bacteria. To make an object or place free from infection. To remove harmful microorganisms from a surface, wound, or instrument.
example_sentence: Please disinfect the wound before applying the bandage. The staff disinfect the floors twice a day. Boiling water can help disinfect the instruments. They disinfected the entire building after the outbreak.

english_meaning: A chemical substance used to destroy germs and harmful bacteria. A cleaning liquid that kills microorganisms on surfaces or objects. Having the power to kill germs and prevent infection.
example_sentence: Wipe the table with a strong disinfectant before cooking. The hospital uses medical-grade disinfectant in every ward. She sprayed disinfectant on the door handles. This liquid has a powerful disinfectant effect.

english_meaning: The process of killing germs and harmful bacteria on surfaces or objects. The act of making something clean and free from infection. A method used to prevent the spread of disease.
example_sentence: Regular disinfection of the wards is strictly required. Disinfection of drinking water prevents many diseases. The lab follows a strict disinfection procedure. Proper disinfection reduced infections in the clinic.

english_meaning: False information spread deliberately to deceive people. Misleading facts or news created to influence opinion. Propaganda intended to confuse or mislead the public. The deliberate act of spreading lies as if they were true.
example_sentence: Social media has made disinformation spread faster than ever. The agency was accused of a deliberate disinformation campaign. Voters were misled by disinformation about the new law. Journalists must check facts to avoid publishing disinformation.

english_meaning: Not candid or sincere, especially in pretending that one knows less about something than one really does. Slightly dishonest or insincere in intention. Giving a false impression of frankness.
example_sentence: It was disingenuous of him to claim he had no involvement. Her apology sounded disingenuous to everyone. The politician gave a disingenuous reply to the question. It would be disingenuous to pretend we did not know.

english_meaning: To break into small pieces or fragments. To crumble or decay gradually. To lose structure, organization, or unity. To collapse physically or emotionally. To dissolve into separate parts. To weaken until something no longer functions properly. To decompose or rot over time. To destroy the cohesion of a group, system, or relationship.
example_sentence: The old wall began to disintegrate after years of exposure to rain and wind. Without proper leadership, the organization started to disintegrate. The ancient manuscript disintegrated when it was handled carelessly. His confidence seemed to disintegrate after repeated failures.

english_meaning: A lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern about something. Impartiality; freedom from bias or personal advantage in a matter. The state of being unaffected by the possible gain or loss involved. To cause someone to lose interest in something.
example_sentence: His disinterest in the project was obvious from the very first meeting. A judge must decide every case with complete disinterest. She spoke about the offer with polite disinterest. Public disinterest caused the campaign to fail quietly.

english_meaning: To forcefully remove something that is fixed, stuck, or firmly positioned from its place, position, or situation. Can also refer to causing someone to leave a position or office.
example_sentence: The storm dislodged several roof tiles. Protesters tried to dislodge the barricade. The dentist dislodged a piece of food stuck between my teeth. The new manager was able to dislodge the old leadership.

english_meaning: To take apart a machine, structure, or system into pieces. To remove the equipment or fittings from something. To gradually break down or do away with an organization, system, or arrangement. To deconstruct something piece by piece for repair, transport, or destruction.
example_sentence: The workers had to dismantle the old machine before moving it. The government plans to dismantle the corrupt system. They dismantled the stage after the concert ended. Engineers dismantled the bridge for repair work. The committee decided to dismantle the outdated rules.

english_meaning: To make somebody feel shocked and disappointed. A worried, sad feeling after you have received an unpleasant surprise.
example_sentence: They were dismayed to find that ferry has already left. The suggestion was greeted by a dismay silence.

english_meaning: Feeling shocked, worried, or discouraged by something unexpected. Filled with distress or apprehension. Deeply disappointed or disheartened by a situation. Feeling a loss of confidence due to trouble or danger. Struck with sudden fear or concern.
example_sentence: She was dismayed to hear the news of the accident. He looked dismayed at the poor results of the exam. The residents were dismayed by the increase in crime. I was dismayed to find my luggage missing at the airport.

english_meaning: To cut, tear, or separate the limbs or parts of a body. To divide something, such as a country or organization, into pieces. To break up or destroy something that was once united. To take apart forcefully. To split into fragments or sections.
example_sentence: The empire was dismembered after the war. The wolves dismembered their prey quickly. Critics feared the reforms would dismember the national health system. The old machine was dismembered for spare parts.

english_meaning: The act of cutting off or tearing apart the limbs of a body. The division of a country, organization, or system into separate parts. The breaking up of something that was once whole or united. The state of being torn into pieces. A violent or forceful separation into fragments.
example_sentence: The dismemberment of the empire led to years of conflict. The report described the brutal dismemberment of the victim. The dismemberment of the party weakened its influence. Historians study the dismemberment of ancient kingdoms.

english_meaning: To send someone away or allow them to leave. To remove someone from a job or position of employment. To decide that something or someone is not important and stop considering it. To reject a legal case without further consideration. To put thoughts or feelings out of one's mind.
example_sentence: The teacher dismissed the class early today. The company decided to dismiss him for repeated absences. The judge dismissed the case due to lack of evidence. He tried to dismiss his worries and focus on the task.

english_meaning: The act of ordering or allowing someone to leave; the termination of someone's employment. Also means the act of treating something as unworthy of serious consideration.
example_sentence: His dismissal came as a shock to the entire team. The teacher's dismissal of the student's idea was discouraging. She received a dismissal letter on Monday morning. The court ordered the dismissal of all charges.

english_meaning: Showing that something or someone is not considered worthy of attention or consideration. Feeling or expressing rejection or disregard for something. Having an attitude that treats another person's ideas or feelings as unimportant. Rejecting something with contempt or lack of interest. Behaving in a way that ignores or belittles others.
example_sentence: He gave a dismissive wave of his hand when I raised the issue. Her dismissive attitude toward new ideas frustrated the team. The manager was dismissive of the employee's suggestions. His dismissive tone hurt her feelings deeply.

english_meaning: In a way that shows something or someone is not considered important. With an attitude of rejection or disregard. In a manner that belittles or brushes off another's ideas or feelings. Scornfully and without interest. In a disdainful or contemptuous way.
example_sentence: He waved dismissively when I tried to explain. She smiled dismissively and turned away. The critic dismissively rejected the young writer's book. He shrugged dismissively at his colleague's suggestion.

english_meaning: To get down from a horse, bicycle, or other vehicle. To remove something from its mounting or support. To descend from an elevated position, especially in gymnastics. To take apart or disassemble a machine or equipment. To get off something one has been riding.
example_sentence: The rider dismounted from his horse gracefully. Please dismount from your bicycle before entering the park. The gymnast performed a perfect dismount from the beam. Workers dismounted the old machine for repairs.

english_meaning: To refuse or fail to help someone. To act against the wishes of another person. To cause inconvenience to others by not cooperating. To be unhelpful or uncooperative in a way that disappoints or annoys others. To deliberately ignore someone's request or need.
example_sentence: I do not wish to disoblige you, but I cannot lend you the money. He never disobliges his friends in times of need. She felt hurt when her colleague disobliged her on the project. Please do not disoblige us by refusing the invitation. The manager rarely disobliges his hardworking staff.

english_meaning: A state of confusion and lack of order. A disruption of normal physical or mental functions. An irregularity or abnormal condition in health or behaviour.
example_sentence: The classroom was in complete disorder when the substitute teacher arrived. She was diagnosed with a chronic sleep disorder that had affected her for years. The disorder in the aftermath of the announcement led to serious public safety concerns. He experienced episodes of mood disorder that were eventually managed through medication and therapy. The filing system had fallen into such disorder that it took days to find what was needed.

english_meaning: To cause someone to lose their sense of direction. To confuse someone about time, place, identity, or circumstances. To unsettle or disturb a person mentally.
example_sentence: The identical corridors can disorient new visitors. A loud explosion may temporarily disorient people nearby. The misleading signs disoriented the tourists. Waking suddenly in darkness can disorient anyone.

english_meaning: To make someone lose their sense of direction. To make someone confused about where they are, what is happening, or what time it is. To disturb a person’s normal understanding or mental balance.
example_sentence: The maze was designed to disorientate visitors. Bright lights can disorientate a tired driver. The sudden change in routine may disorientate some patients. The spinning ride began to disorientate me.

english_meaning: Unable to recognize one’s location or direction. Confused about time, place, circumstances, or identity. Mentally unsettled and unsure how to respond.
example_sentence: I felt disorientated when I woke in the unfamiliar room. The injured hiker was cold and disorientated. She became disorientated after walking through the crowded station. Jet lag left him tired and disorientated.

english_meaning: A loss of the sense of direction. Confusion about time, place, identity, or circumstances. A temporary state of mental uncertainty or bewilderment. A disturbance of normal spatial awareness.
