example_sentence: The patient experienced brief disorientation after surgery. Thick fog caused disorientation among the hikers. He felt a sense of disorientation in the unfamiliar city. Memory loss and disorientation can require medical attention.

english_meaning: To refuse to acknowledge or accept any connection with someone or something. To formally reject a family member, especially a child. To deny ownership or responsibility for something. To declare that one no longer has any association with a person, action, statement, or belief.
example_sentence: The father threatened to disown his son for his disobedience. The politician was quick to disown the controversial statement. She disowned all responsibility for the mistake. The family disowned him after he committed the crime. He disowned the property left to him in the will.

english_meaning: To regard or represent as being of little worth. It is the act of belittling someone or something to make it seem unimportant or inferior. This often involves making negative or derogatory comments to lower someone's reputation.
example_sentence: It is never a good idea to disparage your previous employer during a job interview. He tends to disparage his own achievements out of a sense of false modesty. You should not disparage the efforts of those who are trying to help. The rivals continue to disparage each other's political platforms.

english_meaning: The act of speaking about someone or something in a disrespectful or belittling way. A remark that lowers someone’s reputation or value. Unfair criticism that presents something as inferior or unimportant.
example_sentence: Her disparagement of her colleagues damaged team morale. The article contained an unfair disparagement of local artists. He objected to the constant disparagement of his work. Constructive criticism should not become personal disparagement.

english_meaning: Expressing the opinion that something is of little worth; derogatory. Speaking of someone or something in a critical or belittling way. Showing a lack of respect or approval.
example_sentence: He made several disparaging remarks about his colleagues. She was hurt by his disparaging tone. The article was full of disparaging comments about the film. Avoid using disparaging language in the workplace.

english_meaning: In a way that shows little respect for someone or something. In a manner intended to belittle, criticize, or make something seem unimportant. Scornfully or contemptuously.
example_sentence: She spoke disparagingly about her former employer. He referred disparagingly to the opposing team. The critic wrote disparagingly of the new exhibition. They should not speak disparagingly about people’s accents.

english_meaning: Essentially different in kind or not allowing comparison. It refers to things that are distinct and diverse, often having no common ground. These items are so unlike that they cannot be grouped together realistically.
example_sentence: The two cultures have disparate origins and very different traditions. Scientists are trying to link disparate pieces of evidence to solve the mystery. The debate brought together people from disparate backgrounds and ideologies. It is difficult to manage such a disparate group of volunteers with different goals.

english_meaning: A great difference or inequality between things. It is often used to describe unfair gaps in status, wealth, or treatment. This term highlights the lack of proportion or balance between two or more entities.
example_sentence: There is a growing economic disparity between the rich and the poor. The disparity in their ages did not seem to affect their friendship at all. Investigators noticed a significant disparity between the two witness accounts. We must work to close the health disparity found in rural communities.

english_meaning: Not influenced by strong emotion; calm and impartial. Able to judge or act objectively without bias. Free from personal feelings or prejudice. Cool-headed and rational.
example_sentence: The judge gave a dispassionate ruling on the sensitive case. Scientists must remain dispassionate when analyzing data. He offered a dispassionate view of the political situation. Her dispassionate tone calmed everyone in the room.

english_meaning: To drive away, remove, or make something disappear (often doubt, fear, or a false idea). To get rid of something that is negative, unclear, or unwanted such as fear, doubt, myths, or darkness. It is often used for abstract things rather than physical objects.
example_sentence: The teacher tried to dispel the students’ doubts before the exam. His explanation helped dispel the confusion in the meeting. Sunlight began to dispel the morning fog. She spoke kindly to dispel his fears.

english_meaning: Something that can be done without. A person, object, or thing that is not essential and can be removed, replaced, or ignored without causing serious problems or harm.
example_sentence: Extra staff were considered dispensable during the budget cuts. In an emergency, luxury items become dispensable. The manager felt that the outdated system was dispensable. Some rules are useful, but others are dispensable in practice.

english_meaning: Official permission to do something that is normally not allowed. The act of distributing or providing something, especially in portions. A particular religious or political system prevailing at a certain time. Exemption from a rule, obligation, or punishment granted by an authority.
example_sentence: The student received a special dispensation to take the exam later. The dispensation of food and water continued throughout the flood. The Pope granted a dispensation for the royal marriage. The new dispensation brought many social reforms. Under the current political dispensation, freedom of speech is respected.

english_meaning: To distribute or give out a portion of something to others. It can also mean to provide or manage a service or medication. In a formal sense, it can mean to waive or get rid of a requirement or rule.
example_sentence: The machine is designed to dispense coffee and snacks automatically. The pharmacist will dispense the medication once the prescription is verified. The judge decided to dispense with the formalities and get straight to the facts. The charity began to dispense food and blankets to the refugees.

english_meaning: To do without. To stop using somebody/something because you no longer need them. To get rid of or do without something. To give up what is not strictly needed. Manage without, forgo, as in We can dispense with the extra help. To set aside.
example_sentence: Debit cards dispense with the need for cash altogether. I think we can dispense with the formalities (= speak openly and naturally to each other). They've had to dispense with a lot of luxuries since Mike lost his job. Let’s dispense with the formalities and get right down to business. Electronic records can dispense with 80% of paper files and reduce the need for office space. The new chairman has said he will dispense with any directors who can't accept radical change.

english_meaning: Something that can be done without. A person, object, or thing that is not essential and can be removed, replaced, or ignored without causing serious problems or harm.
example_sentence: Extra staff were considered dispensible during the budget cuts. In an emergency, luxury items become dispensible. The manager felt that the outdated system was dispensible. Some rules are useful, but others are dispensible in practice.

english_meaning: To spread out or scatter in different directions. To cause something to break up and go in different ways. To distribute over a wide area. To break up a group or crowd. To dissolve or scatter particles (like light, fog, smoke). To distribute things such as resources, people, or information. To vanish gradually by spreading out.
example_sentence: The crowd began to disperse after the event ended. The teacher asked the students to disperse quietly. The sunlight dispersed through the clouds. Police used barriers to disperse the protesters.

english_meaning: A person or device that spreads something over a wide area. Something that causes a crowd or group to break up and move away. A substance or agent that keeps particles separated in a mixture. One who distributes items widely rather than keeping them together.
example_sentence: The machine works as an efficient disperser of fertiliser. Rain proved to be the best disperser of the crowd. A chemical disperser was used to break up the oil spill. Birds are natural dispersers of many forest seeds.

english_meaning: To cause someone to lose enthusiasm or hope. To make someone feel discouraged. To lower the morale or spirit of a person. To depress or sadden. To weaken someone’s confidence or motivation.
example_sentence: The repeated failures began to dispirit the team. Bad weather dispirited the players during the match. His harsh words dispirited her deeply. Nothing could dispirit him from pursuing his dream.

english_meaning: Designed to be used once or for a short time and then thrown away. Available for use or spending after necessary commitments, especially income. Considered easily replaceable or unimportant. A product intended to be discarded after use.
example_sentence: The nurse put on disposable gloves. Disposable cameras remain useful at some events. Her disposable income increased this year. Workers should never be treated as disposable.

english_meaning: To get rid of something, especially waste (usually with 'of'). To arrange or place things in a particular order or position. To make someone willing or inclined to do something. To deal with a matter finally or settle it.
example_sentence: Please dispose of the waste in the proper bin. The gardener disposed the pots along the wall. His kindness disposed us to trust him. The court disposed of the case within a month.

english_meaning:
To get rid of something that is no longer wanted or needed. To throw away or discard waste or unwanted items. To deal with or finish something. 
To kill or defeat someone or something (formal or figurative use).
example_sentence: We should dispose of waste properly to protect the environment. She disposed of the old documents after scanning them. The committee disposed of all pending matters in the meeting. The army quickly disposed of the enemy forces.

english_meaning: To make someone likely or willing to behave in a particular way, or to have a certain attitude, feeling, or tendency toward something. It shows a natural inclination or readiness for a specific action or behavior.
example_sentence: His kind nature disposes him to help others. The cool weather disposed us to go for a walk. Her upbringing disposed her to be respectful toward elders. The calm environment disposed him to study with focus. She is disposed to forgive him.

english_meaning: To make someone likely or willing to think or feel in a particular way about someone or something, to influence a person’s attitude or tendency.
example_sentence: I am not disposed toward taking unnecessary risks. His kindness disposed me toward trusting him. Her honesty disposed others toward respecting her opinion. The teacher’s patience disposed students toward liking the subject. Their generosity disposed the community toward supporting their cause.

english_meaning: A person's inherent qualities of mind and character. A tendency or inclination to behave in a particular way. The way in which something is arranged or ordered.
example_sentence: She has a naturally cheerful disposition that makes her pleasant to be around. His disposition toward kindness and generosity was evident from a very early age. The soldier was praised for his courageous disposition under extreme pressure. The disposition of the furniture in the room was altered to allow for better natural light. A calm disposition is a great asset when dealing with difficult or stressful situations.

english_meaning: The action of depriving someone of land, property, or other possessions. The state of being deprived of possessions, especially by force or law. The loss of ownership or control over one's assets. A historical process of removing people from their ancestral lands.
example_sentence: The indigenous tribes suffered from widespread dispossession during the colonial era. Legal battles over the dispossession of the family estate lasted for years. The war resulted in the mass dispossession of thousands of refugees. Many families faced total dispossession after the sudden economic collapse.

english_meaning: A lack of proper proportion, balance, or symmetry. A difference in size, amount, degree, or importance that is too great or unsuitable. An instance or condition in which related parts do not correspond fairly or harmoniously.
example_sentence: There is a noticeable disproportion between the two sides of the building. The disproportion of power in the relationship led to frequent arguments. Economists are concerned about the growing disproportion between rich and poor. The disproportion of the evidence suggested the theory was flawed.

english_meaning: Too large or too small in comparison with something else. Lacking proper proportion or balance. Unfairly excessive or insufficient. Out of scale.
example_sentence: The death penalty is viewed by many as a disproportionate punishment. He spent a disproportionate amount of time on the easiest tasks. The small town receives a disproportionate share of the state's funding. The giant's head seemed disproportionate to the rest of his body.

english_meaning: To an extent that is too large or too small in comparison with something else. In a way that lacks balance or fairness. Excessively or inordinately.
example_sentence: The poorest families spend a disproportionately large part of their income on food. Women are still disproportionately affected by poverty in many regions. The new law will disproportionately benefit wealthy investors. His reaction to the minor criticism was disproportionately angry.

english_meaning: To prove that a statement, theory, belief, or accusation is false. To show through evidence or reasoning that something is incorrect. To refute a claim conclusively rather than merely question it.
example_sentence: The DNA evidence disproved the suspect's alibi. One unusual result does not disprove the entire theory. Researchers designed the experiment to test and possibly disprove the claim. The records disproved the rumor that the building had been sold.

english_meaning: To make someone feel uneasy, troubled, or anxious. Worry, uneasiness, mental disturbance. A feeling of worry, restlessness, or lack of peace in the mind.
example_sentence: News of war spread disquiet in the city. The news of the storm caused great disquiet among the villagers. She felt a sense of disquiet before the interview began. His rude tone seemed to disquiet everyone in the room. There was growing disquiet about the future of the company.

english_meaning: A state of anxiety, uneasiness, restlessness, or mental worry. A feeling of inner disturbance caused by fear, doubt, or uncertainty. It describes a lingering sense of discomfort that prevents someone from feeling calm or settled.
example_sentence: She felt a growing disquietude as the meeting approached. His unexplained silence filled the room with disquietude. The news created a sense of disquietude among the residents. The delay in results caused widespread disquietude at the office.

english_meaning: A long, formal, detailed discussion or essay on a subject. A long, careful, and formal examination or discussion of a topic. It is often written or spoken in an academic, scholarly, or serious style.
example_sentence: The professor delivered a long disquisition on ancient philosophy. Her disquisition on climate change impressed the entire audience. The book contains a disquisition about the history of language. He wrote a thoughtful disquisition on moral responsibility.

english_meaning: To pay no attention to something. To ignore or treat as unimportant. To refuse to consider or take notice of. The act of ignoring or showing lack of respect for someone or something. To deliberately overlook rules, advice, warnings, or feelings.
example_sentence: He chose to disregard the doctor's advice about smoking. Please do not disregard the safety warnings at the construction site. Her disregard for the rules caused a lot of trouble. The driver was fined for his disregard of traffic signals. We cannot disregard the feelings of others.

english_meaning: To interrupt or stop something from continuing normally. To cause disorder, disturbance, or interruption in a process, system, activity, or situation so that it cannot continue as planned or smoothly.
example_sentence: The heavy rain disrupted traffic across the city. Loud noise can disrupt students during exams. The strike disrupted public transportation services. Technical issues disrupted the online meeting.

english_meaning: A disturbance or problem that interrupts an event, activity, or process. The act of preventing something from continuing in its normal way. A radical change in an industry, system, or way of doing things, especially one caused by innovation. Sudden interference that throws something into disorder.
example_sentence: Heavy snowfall caused major disruption to the train service. The protest led to a serious disruption of traffic in the city. Technological disruption has changed the entire industry. The power cut caused a great disruption in our work. Students complained about the disruption of online classes.

english_meaning: An informal word meaning to speak disrespectfully about someone. To insult or criticise a person openly and rudely. To show a lack of respect through words or attitude. An insulting remark or act of disrespect.
example_sentence: He felt hurt when his friend dissed him in public. Please don't diss her work without reading it. That comment was a clear diss aimed at the manager. Rappers often diss each other in their songs.

english_meaning: To cut apart a body, plant, or object for study. To examine something closely and in detail. To separate an idea, argument, or text into parts. To analyze carefully and critically.
example_sentence: The class will dissect a flower to study its parts. Analysts dissected the budget line by line. She likes to dissect every sentence in a poem. The surgeon dissected the tissue with great care.

english_meaning: The careful cutting apart of a body, plant, or object for study. A detailed analysis of something complex. The act of separating parts to understand structure. A critical examination of an idea, text, or event.
example_sentence: The students watched a frog dissection in biology class. Her dissection of the speech revealed hidden assumptions. The report offers a careful dissection of the problem. Dissection helped the doctors understand the damaged tissue.

english_meaning: To spread information, ideas, knowledge, or news widely so many people can know about it. It is often used for sharing knowledge, research, or messages with a large audience.
example_sentence: The organization works to disseminate health information in rural areas. Scientists disseminate their research findings through journals and conferences. The government used social media to disseminate safety guidelines during the flood. Teachers help disseminate knowledge to students every day.

english_meaning: Disagreement that causes conflict among people. Conflict, division, or tension among members. The word is usually used when people who are expected to work together begin to oppose each other.
example_sentence: Dissension within the committee delayed the final decision. The new policy created dissension among the employees. Political dissension weakened the unity of the party. Religious dissension led to conflict in the region.

english_meaning: To hold or express opinions that differ from those commonly or officially held. Disagreement with a prevailing view, decision, or policy. The expression of objection or protest. A formal disagreement, especially within a court, political party, or religious group.
example_sentence: Two judges dissented from the majority decision. Public dissent grew against the new taxation policy. He dared to dissent in the meeting despite the pressure. Their dissent was peaceful but firm. Freedom to dissent is essential in a true democracy.

english_meaning: The expression or holding of opinions at variance with those commonly or officially held. Active opposition to official policy. The state of disagreeing strongly and publicly with an established authority.
example_sentence: Political dissidence was ruthlessly suppressed by the authoritarian regime for decades. She was exiled from her homeland because of her public dissidence against the ruling party. The history of the country is filled with examples of brave dissidence in the face of oppression. His dissidence was expressed through art and poetry rather than through political activism. The government made it clear that any form of open dissidence would be dealt with severely.

english_meaning: The act of hiding one's true feelings, thoughts, or intentions. Deliberate concealment carried out by pretence. Deceit practised by pretending that something is not the case.
example_sentence: His calm face was pure dissimulation; inside he was furious. Politics often rewards dissimulation more than honesty. She saw through his dissimulation at once. Years of dissimulation had left him unable to speak plainly.

english_meaning: To divide and spread into small pieces or particles. To reduce strong emotions such as tension, excitement, or anxiety. To consume resources, strength, or effort little by little. To scatter over a large area. To spread widely in different directions.
example_sentence: The crowd began to dissipate after the event ended. His nervousness dissipated once the interview started. Their energy dissipated after hours of hard work. Smoke from the fire slowly dissipated into the sky. The explanation helped dissipate their doubts. Friction causes mechanical energy to dissipate as heat.

english_meaning: A way of living focused too much on entertainment, drinking, or luxury, often leading to moral or physical weakness. A state in which attention is scattered and not focused on serious matters. The process of spreading something over a wide area until it loses strength or concentration. Gradual weakening of emotions, anger, fear, or excitement over time.
example_sentence: His dissipation of family wealth left him bankrupt. The dissipation of heat from the engine prevents overheating. Years of dissipation affected his health badly. The dissipation of fog made the road visible again. Too much dissipation distracted him from his studies.

english_meaning: To disconnect or separate oneself from a person, group, idea, or activity. To regard as separate or unconnected. To detach mentally or emotionally from a thought, feeling, or experience. To formally end one's connection with an organization or belief.
example_sentence: He tried to dissociate himself from the controversial group. The company quickly dissociated itself from the false advertisement. It is hard to dissociate the writer from his characters. She wished to dissociate from her painful memories. The party dissociated itself from the violent protesters.

english_meaning: Living an immoral life devoted to pleasure and self-indulgence. Lacking moral restraint or discipline in behaviour. Given to drinking, gambling, or other excesses.
example_sentence: He wasted his fortune on a dissolute lifestyle. The novel describes the dissolute habits of the young lord. Years of dissolute living ruined his health. She left the city to escape its dissolute society.

english_meaning: The act or process of breaking up, ending, or dissolving something such as a marriage, partnership, organization, or agreement. The formal closing down of an assembly, parliament, or institution. The process by which a solid is dissolved in a liquid. The act of breaking down or disintegrating into smaller parts. Moral decline or a state of indulgence in immoral pleasures.
example_sentence: The dissolution of their marriage was finalized last month. The president announced the dissolution of the national assembly. The dissolution of sugar in water happens quickly when stirred. The dissolution of the company left many employees jobless. Years of dissolution had ruined his health and reputation.

english_meaning: To mix into a liquid and become part of it. To end or break apart. To become incorporated into a liquid so that it forms a solution. To officially end or disband something like a group or partnership. To lose strength or intensity. A smooth transition where one image fades out while another fades in. A gradual blending or merging of one thing into another
example_sentence: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot tea. The fog began to dissolve as the sun rose. The company decided to dissolve the partnership. His anger slowly dissolved into sadness. The director used a dissolve to move between scenes. The film opens with a slow dissolve from black.

english_meaning: A lack of agreement or harmony between people or ideas. In music, it refers to a tension or clash resulting from the combination of disharmonious sounds. It often implies a harsh or disagreeable connection of elements.
example_sentence: The cognitive dissonance she felt led her to change her long-held beliefs. There is a noticeable dissonance between his words and his actual actions. The modern musical composition was filled with unsettling dissonance. The unexpected political dissonance caused a rift within the party leadership.

english_meaning: Lacking harmony or agreement between elements. Characterized by a harsh or unpleasant sound produced by a lack of musical concord. In a broader sense, it refers to ideas or beliefs that are inconsistent or in conflict with one another.
example_sentence: The orchestra produced a dissonant sound as the musicians tuned their instruments. His actions were dissonant with his stated beliefs about environmental protection. The modern building felt dissonant against the backdrop of the historic village. The composer used dissonant chords to create a sense of tension in the film score.

english_meaning: To persuade someone not to do something. To convince or advise someone against doing something, usually by giving reasons or warnings so that the person changes their mind. Dissuade is commonly used in formal or advisory situations where someone tries to stop another person from making a risky or unwise decision.
example_sentence: I tried to dissuade him from quitting his job. The teacher dissuaded the students from cheating in the exam. Her friends dissuaded her from traveling alone at night. The doctor dissuaded him from smoking.

english_meaning: Situated away from the centre of the body or from the point of attachment. Farther from the origin or main part of a structure. Used in anatomy to describe the outer end of a limb or bone. Located at the far end of something.
example_sentence: The distal end of the bone was fractured in the accident. Doctors examined the distal joints of her fingers. Blood flow to the distal tissues was carefully monitored. The distal part of the tube must be kept sterile.

english_meaning: The amount of space between two points, places, or objects. A long space between things. The state of being far apart in time, space, or relationship. To keep oneself apart or uninvolved.
example_sentence: The distance between the two cities is about fifty kilometres. She kept her distance from the arguing group. He tried to distance himself from the controversy. From this distance, the writing is hard to read.

english_meaning: Far away in space or time. Not closely related in family or connection. Cold and unfriendly in manner. Faint or vague, as in a sound or memory.
example_sentence: They live in a distant village near the mountains. He is a distant cousin whom I rarely meet. Her manner was polite but distant throughout the meeting. A distant sound of music came from the garden.

english_meaning: In a way that is far away in space or time. In a manner that shows little warmth or friendliness. Vaguely or faintly, as in a memory or sound. In a way that indicates a remote family connection.
example_sentence: He smiled distantly and walked away without speaking. Thunder rumbled distantly across the valley. She is distantly related to the royal family. He distantly remembered visiting the town as a child.

english_meaning: A feeling of mild dislike or aversion toward something. A lack of enjoyment or appreciation of something. A sense of disapproval or discomfort.
example_sentence: She expressed her distaste for the rudeness of the comment with a firm but measured response. He looked at the unfamiliar dish with distaste but agreed to try a small portion. Her distaste for gossip was well known among the people who worked with her. The audience showed its distaste for the performance by leaving early in large numbers. He could not hide his distaste for the way the situation had been handled.

english_meaning: To swell or cause to swell by pressure from inside. To stretch or expand outward. To become enlarged or bulging due to internal pressure of gas, liquid, or contents. Used often in medical and physical contexts to describe the expansion of organs, vessels, or containers.
example_sentence: The patient's stomach began to distend due to excess gas. Balloons distend when filled with air. The veins on his forehead distended with anger. Heavy meals can distend the abdomen and cause discomfort. The pipe will distend if the pressure becomes too high.

english_meaning: Swollen, enlarged, or stretched because of pressure, gas, fluid, or internal expansion. Extended beyond the normal size or shape.
example_sentence: His distended stomach hurt after the meal. The balloon was distended with air. The patient had a distended abdomen. The distended river threatened to overflow its banks.

english_meaning: The action of swelling or the state of being swollen or enlarged. Expansion or stretching of an organ or part of the body by internal pressure. An abnormal enlargement caused by fluid, gas, or pressure.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the patient for abdominal distension. Gas can cause painful distension of the stomach. The distension of the balloon indicated increasing pressure. Distension of the veins was clearly visible.

english_meaning: To purify or separate a liquid by heating it and then cooling the vapor. To extract the essential meaning or qualities of something. British spelling of distill.
example_sentence: The plant distils fresh water from seawater. The report distils years of research into a clear summary. Lavender oil is distilled from the flowers. Good teaching distils complex ideas into simple examples.

english_meaning: To purify or separate a liquid by heating it and cooling the vapor. To obtain the essential part or meaning of something. The standard American spelling of distil.
example_sentence: The laboratory distills alcohol for the experiment. She distilled the main argument into one sentence. The machine distills polluted water. The teacher distilled the lesson into three key points.

english_meaning: A liquid obtained by distillation. A purified or concentrated product produced from a mixture.
example_sentence: The distillate was collected in a clean glass flask. The chemist tested the distillate for impurities. The plant produces a fragrant distillate from rose petals. This distillate is more concentrated than the original mixture.

english_meaning: The process of purifying or separating liquids by heating, vaporizing, and condensing them. The extraction of an essential or concentrated part of something.
example_sentence: Distillation is used to separate alcohol from water. The laboratory demonstrated the process of fractional distillation. Oil distillation produces several useful fuels. The article is a careful distillation of the author’s ideas.

english_meaning: Clearly different or separate from something else of a similar type. Easily heard, seen, or recognized. Well-defined and unmistakable. Used to describe things that are noticeable, unique, or sharply different from others in nature, appearance, or sound.
example_sentence: There is a distinct difference between the two paintings. We heard a distinct sound coming from the basement. Her voice has a distinct accent. The two species belong to distinct categories. He has a distinct way of solving problems.

english_meaning: A clear difference or contrast between two or more things. The act of recognizing or making a difference between things. Excellence or superiority that sets someone apart from others. A special honour, award, or mark of recognition given for outstanding achievement. A grade or result awarded for work of a very high standard.
example_sentence: There is a clear distinction between knowing a rule and understanding it. She graduated with distinction from a well-known university. The judge drew a careful distinction between the two cases. He is a writer of great distinction in his field.

english_meaning: Clearly different from others in a way that is easy to notice. Having a special quality or character that makes something recognizable. Typical of one particular person, group, or thing. Serving to mark something as separate or unique.
example_sentence: The bird has a distinctive red mark on its wings. Her distinctive voice is easy to recognize on the radio. The building has a distinctive style that attracts visitors. Each region has its own distinctive food and culture.

english_meaning: In a way that is clearly different from others. In a manner that makes something easy to recognize. In a way that is typical of a particular person, place, or group. Notably or characteristically.
example_sentence: The dish is distinctively spicy and full of flavour. He speaks distinctively, so you always know it is him. The house is distinctively designed in an old local style. Her paintings are distinctively bold and colourful.

english_meaning: In a way that is clear and easy to see, hear, or understand. Without any doubt; definitely or noticeably. In a separate and clearly different way. To a degree that cannot be mistaken.
example_sentence: I distinctly remember locking the door before leaving. The mountains were distinctly visible in the morning light. His tone was distinctly unfriendly during the meeting. She spoke slowly and distinctly so everyone could follow.

english_meaning: The quality of being clear and easy to see, hear, or understand. The state of being clearly different or separate from something else. Clarity of appearance, sound, or expression. The condition of having a special character that sets something apart.
example_sentence: The distinctness of the photograph surprised everyone. He spoke with such distinctness that no word was lost. The two cultures keep their distinctness despite living side by side. Fog reduced the distinctness of the road signs.

english_meaning: To recognize or point out the difference between two or more things. To be a feature that makes someone or something different from others. To see, hear, or understand something clearly despite difficulty. To perform so well that one earns respect or honour.
example_sentence: Children learn to distinguish colours at an early age. It is hard to distinguish the twins from a distance. His honesty distinguishes him from the rest of the team. She distinguished herself as an excellent researcher.

english_meaning: Able to be recognized as different from something else. Able to be clearly seen, heard, or understood. Having features that make separate identification possible.
example_sentence: The two brands are barely distinguishable in taste. Her handwriting is easily distinguishable from mine. The shape was hardly distinguishable in the dark. Real pearls are distinguishable from fake ones by weight.

english_meaning: Highly respected and admired for great achievement or service. Having a dignified and impressive appearance. Marked by excellence or superior quality. Well known and honoured in a particular field.
example_sentence: A distinguished professor delivered the opening lecture. He had a distinguished career in public service. The award honours distinguished work in medicine. She looked distinguished in her simple grey suit.

english_meaning: Serving to identify or set apart from others. A feature, quality, or characteristic that makes one person or thing different from another. The act of recognizing or pointing out differences. Used to describe traits that mark something as unique or special.
example_sentence: His beard is his most distinguishing feature. The distinguishing mark on the bag helped him identify it. She has a distinguishing style of writing. Tigers have distinguishing stripes on their bodies. The teacher pointed out the distinguishing qualities of each poem.

english_meaning: In a manner that is easily perceivable or noticeable. In a way that stands out with dignity or excellence. By means of showing a clear difference or distinction.
example_sentence: She spoke distinguishly among the crowd of ordinary presenters. The two species can be distinguishly identified by their leaf patterns. He carried himself distinguishly throughout the formal ceremony. The colors were distinguishly separated by a dark boundary.

english_meaning: To pull or twist out of shape; to give a misleading or false account of something. To change the original form, meaning, or nature of something in an inaccurate or deceptive way.
example_sentence: The mirror distorted their reflections in a funny way. The media often distorts facts to attract more viewers. Stress can distort your perception of reality. He distorted the truth to avoid taking blame.

english_meaning: To draw someone's attention away from what they are focusing on. To prevent someone from concentrating. To divert the mind, thoughts, or attention to something else. To provide a pleasant or amusing diversion from worries or problems.
example_sentence: Loud music can distract students during their studies. He tried to distract the child by giving him a toy. Mobile phones often distract drivers on the road. She watched a movie to distract herself from her worries. Please do not distract me while I am working.

english_meaning: Something that prevents someone from giving full attention to something else. The state of being unable to concentrate. An activity that provides entertainment or amusement, especially as a way of forgetting worries. Mental agitation or extreme emotional disturbance.
example_sentence: Mobile notifications are a major distraction during work. Reading is a pleasant distraction from daily stress. The noise outside was a constant distraction. Children need to study in a place free from distractions. Music is sometimes used as a distraction from boring tasks.

english_meaning: An incorrect answer choice offered in a multiple-choice question. Something designed to draw attention away from the correct option. A person or thing that causes distraction.
example_sentence: Each question had three distractors and one correct answer. A good distractor looks plausible to the test taker. The teacher explained how to eliminate distractors. Poorly written distractors make a test too easy.

english_meaning: To seize someone's goods or property legally in order to force payment of a debt. To take possession of a tenant's belongings to recover unpaid rent. To impose a legal seizure on property as security for an obligation. To confiscate assets under legal authority until a debt is settled. To enforce a claim by holding a person's property.
example_sentence: The landlord threatened to distrain on the tenant's furniture for unpaid rent. The court allowed the bank to distrain on his goods. Tax officials may distrain on property if taxes remain unpaid. The creditor distrained on the machinery until the debt was cleared.

english_meaning: A person who seizes another person's goods legally to recover a debt. A landlord or creditor who takes property to obtain unpaid rent or money. An official who carries out a legal seizure of property. A party who holds goods as security until a debt is paid. One who exercises the legal right of distress.
example_sentence: The distrainer took the tenant's furniture to cover three months' rent. A distrainer must follow strict legal procedures. The court ruled that the distrainer had acted unlawfully. The distrainer agreed to return the goods once the debt was paid.

english_meaning: The legal seizure of someone's property in order to obtain payment of money owed, especially rent. The act of distraining or taking goods to enforce payment of a debt. A legal remedy by which a landlord recovers unpaid rent by seizing the tenant's belongings. The process of holding property as security until a debt is paid.
example_sentence: The landlord threatened distraint when the rent remained unpaid. The court ordered the distraint of the debtor's property. Distraint is allowed by law only under specific conditions. Officials carried out distraint to recover unpaid taxes. The shopkeeper feared distraint of his goods by the authorities.

english_meaning: Extremely worried, upset, or emotionally troubled. So anxious or grief-stricken that one cannot think or behave normally. Deeply distressed because of fear, loss, or shock. Showing great agitation and confusion of mind.
example_sentence: The distraught mother searched the streets for her missing son. He looked distraught when he heard about the accident. She was too distraught to answer any of the questions. Distraught passengers waited for news of the delayed flight.

english_meaning: To put someone in a state of anxiety, sorrow, or difficulty. A state of extreme worry, sorrow, or physical discomfort caused by a difficult situation.
example_sentence: She was in deep distress after hearing the bad news. The ship sent a distress signal during the storm. Financial problems distressed him greatly. The abandoned animals were in distress.

english_meaning: A branch of a river that flows away from the main channel and does not rejoin it. A smaller waterway that carries water from a large river towards the sea, a lake, or irrigated land. In a delta, one of the many channels through which a river splits before reaching the sea. A canal offtake that distributes water from a larger canal to smaller watercourses.
example_sentence: The Indus splits into several distributaries before reaching the sea. Farmers depend on a small distributary for irrigation water. Silt has blocked the mouth of the main distributary. Each distributary of the delta supports its own wetland.

english_meaning: To give things out to several people or share them among a group. To spread something over an area or throughout an object. To supply goods to shops, stores, or customers. To divide something into parts and assign each part somewhere. To arrange or place things at different points within a space.
example_sentence: The volunteers distributed food to the flood victims. The company distributes its products across many countries. Please distribute these handouts to the students. Weight should be distributed evenly on both feet.

english_meaning: The action of sharing something out among a number of recipients. The way something is spread over an area or among groups. The delivery of goods to shops and customers. The pattern in which something occurs. The mathematical arrangement of values.
example_sentence: The distribution of food began after the flood. The company handles distribution across the region. The distribution of wealth is very unequal. This chart shows the distribution of ages in the class.

english_meaning: Concerned with the distribution or sharing of something. Relating to a mathematical property of operations. Serving to distribute or spread out. In grammar, referring to members of a group individually. Concerning fair allocation among people.
example_sentence: The court emphasized distributive justice in its ruling. Multiplication has a distributive property over addition. Each and every are distributive words in English grammar. The policy is designed on distributive principles.

english_meaning: A public official who prosecutes criminal cases for a local government district. The chief prosecutor representing the state or government in a particular area.
example_sentence: The district attorney decided to bring charges. Police sent the evidence to the district attorney. The district attorney questioned the witness in court. She was elected district attorney last year.

english_meaning: Lack of trust or confidence in someone or something. To regard with doubt or suspicion. The feeling that you cannot rely on a person, statement, or system. To question the honesty, motives, or reliability of others.
example_sentence: He has a deep distrust of strangers. Repeated lies created distrust between the partners. People often distrust politicians who break promises. She distrusted the offer because it sounded too good. There is growing distrust between the two communities.

english_meaning: Having no confidence or faith in someone or something. Feeling doubt or suspicion about a person's honesty or motives. Unwilling to believe or rely on others. Showing wariness and lack of trust.
example_sentence: She remained distrustful of strangers after the incident. Years of broken promises made the villagers distrustful of officials. He gave the salesman a distrustful look. Voters are increasingly distrustful of political advertising.

english_meaning: To cause a group, organization, or system to become divided or separated. To destroy the unity or harmony of something. To break apart something that was previously united. To create division or disagreement among people or things.
example_sentence: Personal interests can disunify even the closest teams. The new policy threatened to disunify the workers. Rumors often disunify families and communities. Bad leadership can disunify a strong nation. Do not let small disputes disunify the organization.

english_meaning: A long narrow channel dug in the ground, typically used for drainage or irrigation along the side of a road or field. To get rid of something or someone that is no longer wanted. To make a forced landing of an aircraft on water. In informal use, to leave a class, meeting, or person abruptly.
example_sentence: The car skidded off the road and landed in a deep ditch. Farmers dig ditches to bring water to their fields. He decided to ditch his old phone and buy a new one. The pilot had to ditch the plane in the sea after engine failure. She ditched her friends and went home early.

english_meaning: The same as what has just been said or written. A mark or word used to repeat an item above. Used to show agreement or that the same thing applies. A duplicate or copy.
example_sentence: I ordered the soup, and she said ditto. The clerk wrote ditto marks under the repeated names. His answer was short: ditto. The second report was almost a ditto of the first.

english_meaning: Active during the day or happening every day. Relating to the daytime. Occurring every day. Animals or plants active during daylight hours. Daily recurring cycle
example_sentence: Humans are mostly diurnal and sleep at night. The diurnal temperature changes were significant in the desert. Many birds have diurnal feeding habits. The scientist studied the diurnal cycle of plant growth.

english_meaning: To plunge headfirst into water or to descend rapidly. It can also refer to an act of sudden and deep involvement in an activity or situation. Figuratively, it implies intense focus or a quick, often downwards, movement in price or value.
example_sentence: She decided to dive into the ocean despite the cold water. The stock market took a dive after the unexpected news. He watched the pelican dive for fish. We need to dive deeper into the data to find the root cause. The swimmer prepared to dive off the high board.

english_meaning: To re-engage with something after a period of absence or a break. It implies a renewed and often enthusiastic return to an activity, task, or situation. This phrase suggests picking up where one left off, often with a sense of excitement or dedication.
synonyms: ["Re-engage","Resume","Rejoin","Recommence","Return to","Get back into","Pick up again","Plunge back into","Immerse oneself again in"]
example_sentence: After a long vacation, I'm ready to dive back into my work. She took a break from painting, but now she's eager to dive back into her art. Even after a minor setback, he was determined to dive back into his studies. Let's dive back into the discussion where we left off. The team is excited to dive back into training after their win.

english_meaning: To descend quickly or plunge headfirst into water or another medium. It can also metaphorically mean to delve deeply into a topic or investigate something thoroughly. This phrasal verb often implies a rapid and focused movement either physically or intellectually.
example_sentence: The submarine prepared to dive down to the ocean floor. The reporter decided to dive down into the archives to find more information. We watched the pelican dive down to catch a fish. Let's dive down into the details of this proposal. The engineers will dive down into the system's code to find the bug.

english_meaning: To 'dive in' means to enthusiastically and fully immerse oneself in an activity or task, often without hesitation. It implies a readiness to start something with vigor and commitment. It can also literally refer to jumping into water, but its more common idiomatic use is about beginning a new project or challenge with great enthusiasm and energy.
example_sentence: When the project was announced, she was eager to dive in and take on the most challenging tasks. The children couldn't wait to dive in to the swimming pool on such a hot day. Don't be afraid to dive in; the water's fine once you get used to it. After a long discussion, everyone was ready to dive in and implement the new strategy. Let's not overthink it, just dive in and see what happens.

english_meaning: To fully immerse oneself into an activity or subject with great enthusiasm and focus. This idiom suggests a profound engagement, often implying a quick and deep involvement rather than a gradual approach. It can also mean to begin a task or exploration with intensity and commitment.
synonyms: ["Plunge Into","Immerse Oneself","Delve Into","Engage In","Get Stuck Into","Become Absorbed","Undertake Enthusiastically","Embark On","Tackle Vigorously","Commit Fully"]
example_sentence: She decided to dive into learning a new language during her sabbatical. He dove into the project with such enthusiasm that he forgot about the time. Let's dive into the details of the financial report. The students were encouraged to dive into the research topic. He will dive into the role with his characteristic passion.

english_meaning: To plunge suddenly from a height into water, usually headfirst. This action implies a deliberate and often vigorous descent, distinguishing it from merely falling into water. It can also metaphorically refer to a sudden and rapid decrease or fall in some quantity or value.
example_sentence: She decided to dive off the high cliff into the clear blue ocean. The children loved to dive off the side of the swimming pool. He watched the stock prices dive off after the announcement. The birds would dive off the branches to catch fish. Be careful when you dive off that unstable platform.

english_meaning: To dive through something means to quickly move or pass through an opening, a body of water, or an obstacle. It often implies a swift, immersive, or even challenging passage. This phrase can be used literally, referring to plunging into water, or metaphorically, indicating a rapid progression through information or a difficult situation.
synonyms: ["Plunge Through","Submerge Through","Immense Through","Penetrate Through","Pass Through","Go Through","Navigate Through","Traverse Through","Burrow Through","Pierce Through"]
example_sentence: The submarine was able to dive through the narrow underwater passage. We had to dive through a pile of old documents to find the key report. The swimmer will dive through the ring of fire as part of the stunt. Scientists often dive through vast amounts of data to uncover new patterns in research. The small boat managed to dive through the crashing waves during the storm.

english_meaning: To go beneath the surface of water or another medium. It implies a deliberate and often quick movement to submerge oneself or something. The phrase can be used literally for swimming or figuratively for escaping a situation or hiding from view.
example_sentence: The children loved to dive under the waves at the beach. He had to dive under the table to escape the falling debris. The submarine can dive under the polar ice cap. She would often dive under her blanket when she heard strange noises. The swimmer quickly dove under the surface to retrieve the lost item.

english_meaning: To separate and go in different directions from a common point. To differ or become different from something else. To depart from an expected course, standard, or plan. In mathematics, to fail to approach a finite limit.
example_sentence: The two roads diverge just beyond the bridge. Their opinions began to diverge after the first meeting. The film diverges from the original novel in several ways. The series diverges and has no finite sum.

english_meaning: The act of moving or developing in different directions. A difference between two things that were expected to be similar. A departure from a common path, opinion, or standard. In mathematics or science, a measure or pattern of spreading apart.
example_sentence: There was a clear divergence between the two reports. The divergence of opinions made agreement difficult. Scientists measured the divergence of the two species over time. A sudden divergence in the data caught the analyst's attention.

english_meaning: Moving or extending in different directions from a common point. Differing from each other or from a standard. Tending to be different or develop in different ways. Used to describe opinions, paths, ideas, or views that move away from each other.
example_sentence: The two friends had very divergent views on politics. The road becomes divergent after the bridge. Their interests are divergent but they remain close. Scientists studied the divergent paths of evolution. The discussion produced many divergent opinions.

english_meaning: Showing a great deal of variety and difference. Made up of people or things of many different kinds. Differing from one another in nature, form, or quality. Including many different cultures, backgrounds, or opinions.
example_sentence: The city has a diverse and welcoming population. She has diverse interests, from music to astronomy. The company hires people from diverse backgrounds. Pakistan is home to diverse languages and cultures.

english_meaning: In a varied manner, showing many differences. In several different ways or forms. With variety in kind, quality, or character. From many different points of view or backgrounds.
example_sentence: The poem has been diversely interpreted by critics. The species is diversely distributed across the continent. Their opinions were diversely expressed during the debate. Resources are diversely allocated among the departments.

english_meaning: The ability of an investment, asset, or risk to be diversified to reduce exposure. The characteristic of an investment, project, or financial portfolio that allows it to be spread across different assets, sectors, or regions to lower overall risk. It measures how effectively risks can be mitigated through diversification.
example_sentence: The diversifiability of her investments allowed her to reduce potential losses. Diversifiability is key when constructing a balanced financial portfolio. Not all risks have high diversifiability; some are systemic. The company focused on diversifiability to enter multiple markets safely.

english_meaning: Capable of being spread or varied to reduce risk or dependence. Something, especially investments, risks, or activities, that can be distributed among different options or categories to minimize potential loss or to create variety.
example_sentence: The risk in this portfolio is largely diversifiable. Diversifiable investments help protect against market fluctuations. By choosing diversifiable strategies, companies reduce financial exposure. Not all risks are diversifiable; some are inherent to the industry.

english_meaning: The process of varying products, investments, or activities to reduce risk or expand opportunities. The act of introducing variety in business, finance, agriculture, or other areas to minimize risks, increase stability, and explore multiple growth opportunities. It can involve investing in different industries, creating new product lines, or spreading resources across sectors.
example_sentence: The company pursued diversification by entering the renewable energy market. Farmers practiced diversification by growing multiple crops instead of relying on a single one. Diversification of investments can protect your savings from market fluctuations. The restaurant’s diversification into catering helped increase its revenue.

english_meaning: Varied or including many different types. Having a wide range of different elements, activities, or forms. It often implies variety in investments, skills, products, or experiences to reduce risk or broaden scope.
example_sentence: The company has a diversified portfolio of products to serve different markets. She has a diversified skill set, including writing, coding, and graphic design. Farmers are encouraged to grow a diversified range of crops to reduce risk. The investment fund is diversified, with stocks from multiple industries.

english_meaning: Something or someone that makes things more varied or introduces variety. A person, company, or tool that adds variety, reduces risk, or broadens scope in a system, business, investment, or activity. It is often used in finance, business, agriculture, or strategy.
example_sentence: The company acted as a diversifier by investing in multiple industries. Introducing new crops can be a diversifier for farmers facing climate risks. Mutual funds serve as diversifiers for investors. Technology has become a diversifier in traditional business models.

english_meaning: Having flowers of many kinds or of different forms. Used for plants or vegetation that produce a variety of flowers differing in size, shape, color or type. It describes botanical diversity within one plant or within a group of plants. A description for ecosystems or habitats that show floral variation, often used in ecology and botany. It can also be applied metaphorically for anything showing wide floral variety.
example_sentence: The garden looked diversiflorous with dozens of species blooming together. A diversiflorous meadow attracts more insects and birds. The scientist studied a rare diversiflorous shrub found in the valley. Their field became diversiflorous after years of careful restoration.

english_meaning: Having leaves of different shapes or types. A plant or tree that bears more than one type of leaf, showing diversity in leaf forms or shapes. Often used in botany or horticulture.
example_sentence: The garden featured a diversifoliate tree that attracted botanists. Diversifoliate plants can adapt better to different climates. She studied the diversifoliate patterns of the tropical forest. The new park included diversifoliate shrubs for ornamental purposes.

english_meaning: Having leaves of different shapes. A plant with leaves that are not uniform in shape but show noticeable variety. Used in botany to describe a plant that bears leaves of varied forms on the same stem or plant. It highlights natural variation in leaf shape due to growth stage, environment, or genetic traits. Used to emphasize natural diversity in leaf morphology within a single plant. Sometimes applied metaphorically in literature to describe anything showing mixed forms or patterns.
example_sentence: The diversifolious shrub caught the botanist’s attention during the field survey. Many aquatic plants become diversifolious as they adapt to changing water levels. The tree looked unusual because its diversifolious leaves changed shape from branch to branch. Diversifolious species often thrive in regions with varied temperatures.

english_meaning: Shaped in various forms. Having mixed or different shapes. Something that appears in a variety of shapes, patterns or structures. It is used for objects, natural forms, designs or anything that does not follow a single uniform shape.
example_sentence: The artist used diversiform patterns to make the painting more vibrant. Coral reefs have a diversiform structure that supports many species. The museum displayed diversiform pottery from ancient cultures. The landscape was diversiform with hills, plains and rocky cliffs.

english_meaning: To make something more varied or add different types. To change or expand something so it includes a wider range of types, activities, products, skills or investments. It often refers to spreading risk, improving variety or broadening options.
example_sentence: The company decided to diversify its products to attract more customers. Farmers diversify their crops to reduce the risk of loss. She wants to diversify her skills to improve her career opportunities. Investors diversify their portfolios to manage financial risk.

english_meaning: The act of changing the direction or course of something. An alternative route used when the usual road is closed. Something that takes a person's attention away from the main matter. An activity done for enjoyment or amusement.
example_sentence: There is a diversion in place because of roadworks. The magician used a clever diversion to fool the audience. Reading is his favourite evening diversion. The army created a diversion to hide its main advance.

english_meaning: Intended to draw attention away from something more important. Designed to mislead or distract an opponent. Relating to a change of route or direction. Serving as a distraction or false target in a plan or attack.
example_sentence: The troops launched a diversionary attack on the eastern front. Critics called the announcement a diversionary tactic. A diversionary route was arranged for heavy vehicles. His angry outburst was merely a diversionary move.

english_meaning: Variety or a wide range of different things or people. The presence of many different types of people, ideas, cultures or elements within a group, environment or situation.
example_sentence: The school celebrates cultural diversity by organizing international festivals. A healthy ecosystem depends on biological diversity. Workplace diversity can lead to more creative solutions. The city is known for its diversity of languages and traditions.

english_meaning: To change the direction or route of something. To turn a person's attention away from something else. To use money or resources for a different purpose than intended. To entertain or amuse someone and give them pleasure.
example_sentence: Police diverted traffic away from the damaged bridge. He told a joke to divert her attention from the bad news. Funds were diverted from education to defence. The pilot had to divert the flight to another airport.

english_meaning: To move something away from a place, path, or purpose. To draw attention away from an unwanted issue. To steer people or traffic away from danger or congestion. To shift resources away from one area to another. To keep someone away from harmful influences or activities.
example_sentence: Police diverted traffic away from the flooded road. The minister tried to divert blame away from himself. The program diverts young people away from crime. Resources were diverted away from research to marketing.

english_meaning: To turn something away from its usual course or direction. To draw attention away from a subject or problem. To take money or resources away from their intended purpose. To distract someone from what they are doing. To prevent someone from following a planned path or goal.
example_sentence: The scandal was created to divert attention from the real issue. Water was diverted from the river to irrigate the fields. Nothing could divert her from her goal of becoming a doctor. Funds were illegally diverted from the school budget.

english_meaning: To redirect something so that it flows or moves into a new place or channel. To put money, energy, or effort into a different use. To change the course of a river or traffic into another route. To turn one's attention or talent into a new activity. To transfer resources into a particular project.
example_sentence: Rainwater is diverted into large storage tanks. He diverted his anger into hard work at the gym. The government diverted extra funds into education. Engineers diverted the stream into a new canal.

english_meaning: To change the direction or route of something so that it goes to another place. To redirect money, resources, or attention to a different purpose. To send traffic, flights, or water along a different path. To shift someone's focus to another subject. To transfer something from its original use to a new one.
example_sentence: The flight was diverted to Lahore because of bad weather. The council diverted funds to the new hospital. Police diverted traffic to a side road after the accident. She quickly diverted the conversation to a safer topic.

english_meaning: Inflammation or infection of small pouches (diverticula) that develop in the walls of the intestines.
example_sentence: She was hospitalized due to severe diverticulitis. Diverticulitis can be managed with antibiotics and dietary changes. Chronic diverticulitis may require surgery. A high-fiber diet can help prevent diverticulitis.

english_meaning: To deprive someone of power, property, rights, or possessions. To sell off business interests, investments, or assets. To take off clothing or remove something from oneself. To rid oneself of a quality, feeling, or characteristic.
example_sentence: The company decided to divest its loss-making units. The king was divested of all his powers. He divested himself of his coat before sitting down. Investors often divest from risky markets. She divested herself of all bitterness and forgave them.

english_meaning: To deprive someone of power, rights, rank, or possessions. To strip or remove something from a person or thing. To sell off or get rid of a business, investment, or asset. To free oneself of a feeling, idea, or responsibility. To take off clothing or covering.
example_sentence: The officer was divested of his rank after the inquiry. The company divested itself of its loss-making units. He tried to divest himself of old prejudices. She divested herself of her heavy coat at the door.

english_meaning: A share of profit given to shareholders by a company, or in mathematics, a number that is divided by another number. The portion of a company’s profit distributed to its shareholders, usually on a quarterly or yearly basis, as a reward for holding shares. A dividend is the number that is being divided in a division operation.
example_sentence: The company announced a dividend for all its shareholders. She receives a yearly dividend from her investments. The dividend increased after the company made higher profits. In 12 ÷ 3, the number 12 is the dividend.

english_meaning: A thing that separates one part or area from another. A screen, wall or partition used to divide a room. A person who causes disagreement and splits people into groups. In mathematics, the number by which another number is divided.
example_sentence: A wooden divider separates the office from the waiting area. The road divider was damaged in the accident. Such speeches make him a divider rather than a leader. Write the divider below the number you are dividing.

english_meaning: The practice of seeking knowledge of the future or hidden things by supernatural means. Fortune-telling through signs, omens, cards, or stars. A clever or insightful guess about something unknown. The act of foreseeing or predicting events.
example_sentence: Ancient cultures practiced divination using animal bones. She turned to divination through tarot cards to understand her future. The priest's divination was believed to guide the king's decisions. His accurate guess seemed almost like divination.

english_meaning: Of, from, or like God or a god. Excellent, delightful, or remarkably good in a way that seems superhuman. It can also refer to the act of discovering something by intuition or supernatural means.
example_sentence: The sunrise over the mountains was a truly divine sight to behold. In many ancient cultures, kings were believed to possess divine authority. This homemade chocolate cake tastes absolutely divine. People once looked to the stars to divine the will of the heavens.

english_meaning: An order or decision made by God, fate decided by divine will. A command, judgment, or determination believed to come directly from God. It suggests that events in the world happen according to a higher will or sacred plan. In religious belief systems, it often relates to destiny, fate, or predestination, where outcomes are understood as part of God's ultimate wisdom and authority.
example_sentence: The king accepted his loss as a divine decree. Many believers trust that success and failure are part of a divine decree. She faced her illness with patience, believing it was a divine decree. In some traditions, natural disasters are seen as a divine decree.

english_meaning: In a way that comes from or relates to God or a god. Extremely well, delightfully, or wonderfully. In a heavenly or supremely beautiful manner. By divine will or authority.
example_sentence: Many believed the ancient king was divinely chosen to rule. She sang divinely at the concert last night. The cake tasted divinely rich and creamy. The prophets were said to be divinely inspired.

english_meaning: Causing disagreement or separation among people. A person, idea, issue, or action that creates strong disagreement, conflict, or division within a group, community, or society. It often leads people to take opposing sides and weakens unity.
example_sentence: The new law proved to be highly divisive among the public. His divisive remarks created tension within the team. Religion can become a divisive issue in politics. The leader tried to avoid divisive language during the speech.

english_meaning: The quality of causing disagreement or separation among people. Divisiveness refers to attitudes, actions, language, or situations that create conflict, disagreement, or separation within a group, community, or society, often weakening unity and cooperation.
example_sentence: The divisiveness of the political debate damaged trust among citizens. Social media can increase divisiveness when false information spreads. Leaders should avoid language that promotes divisiveness in society. The policy was criticized for increasing divisiveness within the community. Divisiveness weakens teamwork and damages trust. Social media often adds to political divisiveness.

english_meaning: To make known or reveal private, secret, or confidential information. To disclose something that was previously hidden or unknown. To tell people about something which should have been kept secret. Often used in the context of names, sources, plans, or sensitive details.
example_sentence: The journalist refused to divulge the name of his source. She would not divulge the details of the secret meeting to anyone. Company employees are not allowed to divulge confidential client information. He finally divulged the truth after years of silence. The witness was forced to divulge what he had seen that night.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or derived from two separate fertilized eggs or ova. Used to describe twins who are not identical and share approximately fifty percent of their genetic material. Relating to twins that develop in the uterus simultaneously but originate from distinct zygotes. Characteristic of siblings born at the same birth but possessing different genetic compositions. Not monozygotic. Non-identical in biological origin.
example_sentence: Dizygotic twins are often called fraternal twins because they are no more alike than regular siblings. Doctors confirmed that the pregnancy involved dizygotic embryos after performing an ultrasound. Unlike identical twins, dizygotic pairs can be of different genders. The study focused on the genetic differences between monozygotic and dizygotic twins.

english_meaning: Two offspring born at the same time who developed from two separate fertilized eggs. Non-identical twins who share approximately 50 percent of their genes like ordinary siblings. Fraternal twins who may or may not be of the same sex. A pair of siblings resulting from a multiple pregnancy where two ova are fertilized by two different sperm cells. Twins that are no more alike than any other pair of brothers or sisters.
synonyms: ["Fraternal Twins","Non-identical Twins","Binovular Twins","Biovular Twins","Dissimilar Twins","Siblings","Multiple Births","Twofold","Dual","Pair","Two-egg Twins","Multiples"]
example_sentence: Dizygotic twins are commonly referred to as fraternal twins in casual conversation. Unlike identical twins, dizygotic twins can be a boy and a girl. Research shows that the tendency to conceive dizygotic twins can sometimes run in families. The genetic similarity between dizygotic twins is the same as that between any two siblings born at different times.

english_meaning: To make someone feel as if they are spinning or losing balance. Feeling that everything is spinning or moving around you. Having a sensation of spinning or losing balance. Feeling confused or mentally unclear. Feeling very excited or overwhelmed. Causing someone to lose physical balance.
example_sentence: The strong smell dizzied her. The sudden movement dizzied him. Too much spinning can dizzy a child. I felt dizzy after riding the roller coaster. She looked dizzy and had to sit down. The heat made him dizzy.

english_meaning: In a way that makes someone feel as if they are spinning or unable to balance. In a spinning manner. In a confused or disoriented way. In an overwhelmed emotional state. At a very fast or overwhelming rate
example_sentence: She stood up dizzily after spinning around too many times. He walked dizzily after getting off the fast ride. The room seemed to move dizzily before her eyes. The prices rose dizzily within a few weeks.

english_meaning: A sensation of spinning around and losing one's balance. A feeling of lightheadedness or instability often caused by physical ailment or looking down from a great height. It can also metaphorically describe a state of confusion or rapid change.
example_sentence: The medication caused a slight feeling of dizziness and nausea. Looking down from the skyscraper's edge gave her a sudden bout of dizziness. He struggled with dizziness after getting off the spinning carnival ride. The sheer speed of the technological advancements caused a sense of social dizziness.

english_meaning: Feeling as if everything is spinning and you may fall. A condition in which a person feels unsteady, lightheaded, or as if the surroundings are moving or spinning. It may happen due to illness, fear, height, hunger, or sudden movement.
example_sentence: I felt dizzy after standing in the sun for too long. She became dizzy when she looked down from the tall building. The news left him dizzy with confusion. He made a dizzy decision without thinking carefully.

english_meaning: To kill or exhaust someone, to ruin or destroy.
example_sentence: The long hike really did me in. The criminals did him in. That exam nearly did me in. He was done in by exhaustion.

english_meaning: Ready to accept control or instruction; submissive. Easily managed or handled, often used to describe animals or people who are quiet and easy to influence. It implies a temperament that is peaceful and non-resistant.
example_sentence: The once wild horse became quite docile after months of careful training. She was a docile child who always followed her parents' instructions without question. The lab's golden retriever was known for its incredibly docile and friendly nature. Despite the chaotic situation, the crowd remained surprisingly docile and calm.

english_meaning: A platform or area in a harbor where ships are loaded, unloaded, or repaired. The enclosed space in a court where the accused stands during a trial. To bring a ship into a dock. To deduct a part from someone's wages or score. To cut short an animal's tail. To join two spacecraft together in space.
example_sentence: The ship arrived at the dock early in the morning. The accused stood silently in the dock during the trial. The captain skillfully docked the boat at the harbor. They will dock his pay for being late. The two spacecraft successfully docked in orbit.

english_meaning: The highest academic degree awarded by a university. A qualification obtained after advanced research and a written thesis. Often abbreviated as PhD or similar titles. Earned after years of in-depth study in a specific subject and recognized as the top level of academic achievement.
example_sentence: She earned her doctorate in physics from a top university. He is working on his doctorate in literature. A doctorate requires years of dedicated research. The professor holds a doctorate in economics. After completing his doctorate, he started teaching at the college.

english_meaning: A set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted as true.  A system of ideas, principles, or teachings that form the foundation of a religion, political ideology, philosophy, or organization. It guides how people think, behave, or make decisions. Doctrines are often officially stated and widely followed by a group.
example_sentence: The church strictly follows its traditional doctrine. The government introduced a new economic doctrine. Freedom of speech is an important doctrine in many democracies. The court applied the legal doctrine to resolve the case.

english_meaning: A twelve-sided polygon with twelve angles. A geometric shape with twelve straight sides and twelve vertices. Any flat shape with twelve corners and twelve edges.
example_sentence: A regular dodecagon has twelve equal sides and angles. The clock face was designed as a dodecagon. Some architectural domes feature dodecagonal patterns. The decorative window had a dodecagon shape.

english_meaning: To avoid something quickly or cleverly. To move quickly to escape being hit. To avoid answering or dealing with something. A clever way to avoid something. To move suddenly in another direction.
example_sentence: He dodged the ball and ran away. She dodged my question. The driver dodged a sudden obstacle. He tried to dodge responsibility.

word: Does exactly what it says on the tin
english_meaning: An idiom meaning that something performs precisely as its name, description, or advertising promises. Straightforward, reliable, and free from hidden surprises. Suitable for a product, service, title, or person whose function is accurately described.
