example_sentence: The lecture was so boring that I began to drowse in the back row. He watched the fire burn down and started to drowse. Cats often drowse in the warm afternoon sun. I usually drowse for a few minutes after lunch before returning to work.

english_meaning: To do something in a sleepy or sluggish manner. It describes an action performed while one is half-asleep or lacking alertness. It is often used to describe someone moving or speaking as if they just woke up.
example_sentence: She rubbed her eyes and spoke drowsily to her mother. The cat stretched drowsily before curling back up into a ball. He walked drowsily toward the kitchen to make some coffee. The students stared drowsily at the chalkboard during the early morning class.

english_meaning: The state of feeling sleepy or tired. It is a condition of being nearly asleep or having a strong desire to sleep. It often results from a lack of sleep, medication, or a monotonous environment.
example_sentence: The medicine causes extreme drowsiness, so do not drive after taking it. He struggled to overcome the drowsiness that hit him after the heavy meal. Dark rooms and soft music often induce a sense of drowsiness. Constant drowsiness can be a symptom of various underlying health issues.

english_meaning: A personal preference or choice. It is commonly used in the phrase "if I had my druthers", meaning if I could choose freely or if it were up to me. An informal word that means preference, personal choice, or desire. It comes from the spoken phrase "I'd rather", which gradually became "druther" in informal English.
example_sentence: If I had my druthers, I would spend my vacation on a secluded beach. She always gets her druthers when it comes to planning family events. He made it clear that, given his druthers, he would prefer to work from home. They decided to let him have his druthers on the project's direction. When it comes to dessert, I always give my druthers to chocolate cake.

english_meaning: A tree spirit from Greek mythology. A female nature spirit or nymph that lives in and protects trees, especially oak trees. Dryads are closely connected to forests and are believed to share the life of the tree they inhabit.
example_sentence: The poet wrote about a dryad guarding the ancient oak tree. In Greek legends, a dryad would perish if her tree was cut down. The painting showed a dryad emerging from the forest at dawn. The novel describes a dryad as a symbol of nature and life.

english_meaning: To give someone or something a name, title, or nickname. To confer knighthood by touching a person on the shoulder with a sword. To replace the original speech in a film or program with recorded speech in another language. To copy, transfer, mix, or add sound to a recording. To dress leather with grease. A new soundtrack or dubbed version of a recording. A style of reggae music built around remixed instrumental tracks and strong bass.
example_sentence: The newspapers dubbed her the queen of comedy. The studio dubbed the Spanish film into English. The monarch dubbed the soldier a knight for his bravery. The producer created a spacious dub from the original reggae track.

english_meaning: A greasy preparation used to soften, condition, and waterproof leather. Wax or fat applied especially to boots, shoes, saddles, and other leather goods.
example_sentence: Apply some dubbin to your boots to keep the leather supple. The old saddle needed a fresh coat of dubbin. He bought a tin of dubbin to protect his hiking gear from the rain. Regular use of dubbin prevents leather from cracking over time.

english_meaning: A state of feeling unsettled or doubtful about something. The quality of being doubtful or uncertain. A matter that is uncertain or questionable.
example_sentence: There was a note of dubiety in her voice when she agreed. The historical accuracy of the document is a matter of great dubiety. He looked at the strange contraption with obvious dubiety. Despite his dubiety, he decided to follow the leader's plan.

english_meaning: Not certain or doubtful. Something that is uncertain, questionable, or not to be trusted. It can refer to doubt about truth, honesty, or reliability.
example_sentence: I was rather dubious about the whole idea. They consider the plan to be dubious benefit to most families. She had dubious honour of being the last woman to be hanged in England.

english_meaning: In a manner that expresses doubt or hesitation. With a feeling of skepticism or uncertainty. In a way that is questionable or suspect.
example_sentence: She looked dubiously at the leftovers in the fridge. The witness answered the prosecutor's questions dubiously. The project's success was dubiously claimed by the manager. He shook his head dubiously when he heard the wild excuse.

english_meaning: The wife or widow of a duke. A woman holding the rank of duke in her own right. A high-ranking noblewoman. A term of respect for an elegant or dignified lady. A female ruler of a duchy.
example_sentence: The duchess wore a beautiful gown to the royal event. She was granted the title of duchess by the king. The duchess visited the hospital to meet the patients. Every duchess in the kingdom attended the grand ball.

english_meaning: A common waterbird with a broad blunt bill, short legs, and webbed feet. To quickly lower the head or body in order to avoid being hit or seen. To plunge or submerge someone or something briefly under water. A person who is considered dear or charming, often used as a term of endearment. The female of such a bird, as opposed to the drake.
example_sentence: The white duck glided peacefully across the surface of the pond. You should duck your head when walking through that low doorway. He tried to duck his opponent's punch during the boxing match. The children began to duck each other in the swimming pool for fun.

english_meaning: To quickly crouch down and seek shelter beneath a sturdy object to protect oneself from sudden danger or explosion. To evade, dodge, or avoid taking responsibility or dealing with unpleasant criticism. A defensive emergency procedure designed to shield individuals from harm during attacks or natural disasters.
example_sentence: Students were trained to duck and cover under their heavy wooden desks during earthquake drills. The soldiers had to duck and cover as soon as they heard the incoming artillery fire. Instead of addressing the scandal directly, the executive chose to duck and cover. When the sudden hail storm started, pedestrians tried to duck and cover beneath store awnings.

english_meaning: To leave a place quietly, quickly, or unobtrusively. To evade or avoid a responsibility, duty, or commitment. To slip away or escape from a situation without being noticed.
example_sentence: He managed to duck out of the party before anyone noticed he was gone. You should not duck out on your promises to your family. She tried to duck out of the assignment by pretending to be sick. The thief managed to duck out through the narrow alleyway.

english_meaning: A formal fight between two people, often with weapons, Any struggle or contest between two opponents.
example_sentence: The knights prepared for a duel at sunrise. The tennis match turned into a thrilling duel between the two champions. In history, many politicians fought duels to defend their honor. The debate was less a discussion and more a verbal duel.

english_meaning: A male noble ranking just below a prince. The male ruler of a small independent state called a duchy. A title of high rank in European nobility. A powerful or important man. In informal English, a fist, as in 'put up your dukes'.
example_sentence: The duke owned vast lands across the country. She married a duke and became a duchess. The duke welcomed the king to his castle. Put up your dukes and fight fair.

english_meaning: Something that is sweet and soothing to the ear, often used to describe sounds or voices. It implies a pleasing and melodious quality, capable of calm or delight. It can also describe something agreeable or pleasant in a general sense, extending beyond just auditory experiences to things that are figuratively sweet or charming. The word evokes a sense of gentle harmony and often carries a slightly formal or poetic connotation, suggesting a refined pleasantness. It's frequently used to characterize music, tones, or speeches that possess an inherently soft and agreeable sound.
example_sentence: Her dulcet tones filled the entire concert hall with a sense of peace. The dulcet melody of the flute drifted through the open window on the gentle breeze. He delivered his speech with such dulcet words that everyone in the audience felt at ease. The dulcet aroma of freshly baked bread wafted from the kitchen, tempting everyone. The stream babbled with a dulcet murmur as it flowed over smooth stones.

english_meaning: The inability to speak, often due to a congenital condition or injury. This can also extend to a temporary loss of speech. Additionally, "dumb" is frequently used informally to describe someone as unintelligent or foolish, suggesting a lack of common sense or mental acuity. In some contexts, it can also describe something as silent or lacking sound, like a "dumb" piano. Lastly, "dumb" can refer to something that is not activated or is without power, such as a "dumb" terminal.
example_sentence: The accident left him temporarily dumb, unable to utter a single word for days. It was a really dumb move to forget my umbrella on such a rainy day. The old silent film featured a dumb show, relying solely on visual storytelling. He felt dumb for not understanding the simple instructions. The machine remained dumb, its power source disconnected.

english_meaning: A site or place where garbage and waste materials are deposited. To get rid of something that is no longer wanted or needed. A large quantity of materials stored or thrown away. To end a romantic relationship suddenly and without much consideration. To empty out a container or a pile of materials by tilting it.
example_sentence: They decided to dump the old furniture in the yard. The truck arrived at the municipal dump early in the morning. She was devastated when her boyfriend decided to dump her. We should not dump our toxic waste into the local rivers.

english_meaning: To criticise, blame, or treat someone unfairly and harshly. To tell someone all your problems and worries so that they feel burdened. To leave an unwanted task or responsibility with somebody else. To defeat someone easily or humiliate them in an informal sense.
example_sentence: Please do not dump on him just because the project failed. She dumps on her friends whenever she feels stressed. The manager always dumps the boring work on the new staff. Their team dumped on us in the final match.

english_meaning: A small ball of dough that is boiled, steamed, or fried, often served with soup or stew. A piece of dough wrapped around a filling of meat, vegetables, or fruit. A baked pudding made of fruit covered in pastry. An affectionate or humorous name for a short, plump person.
example_sentence: She served chicken soup with soft homemade dumplings. The restaurant is famous for its steamed pork dumplings. My grandmother baked an apple dumpling for dessert. He called his little son a chubby dumpling and laughed.

english_meaning: A state of low spirits, sadness, or depression, usually used in the phrase 'in the dumps'. Places where rubbish or waste is officially left. Stores of military supplies kept at a particular place. Present tense form of the verb 'dump', meaning to drop, unload, or get rid of something carelessly.
example_sentence: She has been down in the dumps since she lost her job. The city council closed two rubbish dumps last year. The army guarded its ammunition dumps day and night. He dumps his bag on the floor as soon as he gets home.

english_meaning: A very large metal container used for collecting and carrying away rubbish. A skip placed outside buildings for waste from homes, shops, or construction sites. A place where unwanted things are thrown away. Used figuratively for something regarded as worthless or a complete mess.
synonyms: ["Skip","Bin","Rubbish container","Waste bin","Trash container","Refuse bin","Garbage bin","Receptacle","Wheelie bin"]
example_sentence: The workers threw the broken furniture into the dumpster. A large dumpster stood behind the restaurant kitchen. Please do not leave old paint beside the dumpster. Critics called the whole plan a complete dumpster fire.

english_meaning: Short and rather fat in appearance. Having a squat, heavy, and unattractive shape. Untidy, shabby, or in poor condition, especially of a place. Feeling low, dull, or slightly depressed in an informal sense.
example_sentence: He was a dumpy little man with a friendly smile. She disliked the dumpy shape of the old teapot. They rented a dumpy flat near the railway station. I felt dumpy and tired after the long journey.

english_meaning: A dull greyish-brown color. Having a muddy brown or grey-brown color. A horse of a dull greyish-brown color. To demand payment of a debt persistently. A debt collector or a demand for payment.
example_sentence: The hills looked dun and bare in the winter. He rode a dun horse across the plain. The landlord dun him for the overdue rent. The walls were painted a dull dun color.

english_meaning: Animal feces, especially from large animals like cows or horses. The solid waste excreted by animals. It is often used as fertilizer in agriculture. Historically, it has also been used as fuel when dried. It can refer to manure from domestic or wild animals.
example_sentence: The farmer spread cow dung on the fields as fertilizer. The smell of horse dung filled the stable. Ancient people used dried dung as fuel for fires. Dung beetles play an important role in recycling dung in nature. He dismissed the rumor as pure dung.

english_meaning: A dark underground room used as a prison, especially in a castle. An underground prison. A dark cell (usually underground) where prisoners can be confined.
example_sentence: Throw him into the dungeons!. The king threw them in the dungeon

english_meaning: A pile of animal dung collected for use as manure. A heap of farm waste or rotting refuse. A filthy or disgusting place. Something considered worthless or degraded.
example_sentence: The farmer spread manure from the dungheap onto his fields. A rooster stood proudly on top of the dungheap. The old yard had turned into a stinking dungheap. He described the corrupt system as a political dungheap.

english_meaning: A heap of animal dung or farmyard manure. A pile of waste or refuse, especially near a farm. A dirty, squalid place or condition. Figuratively, a situation or position regarded as low and worthless.
example_sentence: The chickens scratched around the dunghill behind the barn. He rose from a dunghill to become a wealthy merchant. Flies swarmed over the steaming dunghill. The alley smelled worse than a dunghill.

english_meaning: To dip food briefly into a liquid such as tea or soup. To push someone or something under water. In basketball, to thrust the ball down through the hoop.
example_sentence: He likes to dunk his biscuit in hot tea. The boys dunked each other in the pool. She rose high to dunk the ball. Dunk the brush in water before painting.

english_meaning: Relating to the duodenum, which is the first part of the small intestine immediately beyond the stomach. Pertaining to the proximal portion of the small bowel where most chemical digestion occurs. Describing medical conditions, structures, or functions located in the section of the gut between the pylorus and the jejunum. Used to characterize ulcers, secretions, or surgical procedures specifically involving this anatomical region.
example_sentence: The patient was diagnosed with a chronic duodenal ulcer after experiencing abdominal pain. Surgeons performed a duodenal bypass to address the intestinal blockage. Bile and pancreatic juices enter the digestive tract through the duodenal wall. Careful monitoring is required for any duodenal inflammation detected during the endoscopy.

english_meaning: The first part of the small intestine immediately beyond the stomach. A short, C-shaped section of the digestive tract that receives partially digested food (chyme). The site where pancreatic enzymes and bile are introduced to neutralize stomach acid. A vital organ for the chemical digestion and absorption of minerals. The segment of the bowel connecting the pylorus to the jejunum.
synonyms: ["Small Intestine Segment","Proximal Intestine","Foregut","Digestive Tube","C-loop","Intestinal Tract","Bowel Segment","Alimentary Canal","First Part Of Small Bowel","Gut Section"]
example_sentence: The doctor explained that the ulcer was located in the first section of the duodenum. Bile from the gallbladder enters the duodenum to help break down fats. Digestion of carbohydrates and proteins continues rapidly within the duodenum. An endoscopic procedure was performed to examine the lining of the patient's duodenum.

english_meaning: A situation in which two suppliers dominate the entire market for a commodity or service. A market form in which two companies own all or nearly all of the market share for a given product. A specific type of oligopoly where only two sellers exist. A competitive state where two major players influence the pricing and supply of a specific industry.
synonyms: ["Oligopoly","Market Dominance","Exclusive Possession","Two-party Control","Limited Competition","Bipolarity","Market Control","Joint Monopoly","Paired Dominance","Commercial Rivalry","Twin Supremacy","Binary Competition"]
example_sentence: The smartphone operating system market is effectively a duopoly between Android and iOS. Economists often study how prices are set within a duopoly compared to a monopoly. The two major beverage companies maintained a duopoly over the soft drink industry for decades. Anti-trust regulators monitored the merger to ensure it would not create a duopoly that harms consumers.

english_meaning: A person who is easily deceived or tricked. To deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true. A person who serves as the unwitting tool of another person or power. An exact copy or duplicate, often used as shorthand in photography or data. To delude or mislead by using false pretenses.
example_sentence: The swindler managed to dupe the elderly couple out of their life savings. He felt like a complete dupe for falling for such an obvious internet scam. The spy was used as a dupe to deliver the false documents to the enemy. She bought a high-quality dupe of the designer handbag for a fraction of the price.

english_meaning: A building that is divided into two separate residential apartments or houses. A system of communication that allows two people to communicate in both directions simultaneously. Something consisting of two parts, especially a twofold or double structure. A two-story apartment where rooms are connected by an internal staircase. Double or twofold in nature or character.
example_sentence: They decided to buy a duplex so they could rent out the other half for extra income. The new telephone system supports full duplex communication for clearer calls. The printing press was equipped with a duplex unit for double-sided printing. The luxury hotel offered a stunning duplex suite with a view of the city.

english_meaning: The tough, thick outermost membrane of the three meninges covering the brain and spinal cord. A strong fibrous layer that lies just beneath the skull and gives the brain firm protection. The membrane that contains large venous channels draining blood from the brain.
example_sentence: The dura mater is the toughest of the three meninges. Bleeding above the dura mater is called an extradural haemorrhage. The surgeon carefully opened the dura mater during the operation. The dura mater lines the inner surface of the skull.

english_meaning: Something that is able to withstand wear, pressure, or damage, and lasting for a long time. It refers to items designed to be strong, sturdy, and resistant to breaking or deteriorating, even with frequent use or exposure to harsh conditions. A durable product maintains its quality and functionality over an extended period. This characteristic is highly valued in manufacturing and consumer goods for reliability and longevity. Durable goods are expected to have a long lifespan, reducing the need for frequent replacement.
example_sentence: The old leather briefcase proved to be incredibly durable, lasting through decades of daily use. We need to invest in more durable materials for the construction of roads to prevent frequent repairs. This brand of outdoor furniture is known for its durable design, perfect for all weather conditions. Her durable spirit helped her overcome countless challenges throughout her life.

english_meaning: A large tropical fruit with a thorny husk, strong smell, and rich creamy flesh. A Southeast Asian fruit known as the king of fruits. The tall tree that bears this fruit. The pungent-smelling edible pulp of this fruit.
example_sentence: Many hotels do not allow durian inside the rooms. He loves durian despite its powerful smell. The durian season draws crowds to the markets. She tried durian ice cream in Malaysia.

english_meaning: The time of twilight in the evening when the sky is dark, but some light is still visible. It is when the sun has dipped below the horizon, but its rays still illuminate the upper atmosphere, creating a soft, diminishing glow. This period marks the transition from day to night, characterized by fading light and the emergence of stars. It is often associated with a sense of calm, mystery, or melancholy. Many nocturnal animals begin their activity during dusk. The exact duration of dusk varies depending on geographical location and time of year.
example_sentence: As dusk settled, the streetlights flickered on. We enjoyed a quiet walk along the beach at dusk. The city slowly came alive with lights after dusk. The painting beautifully captured the subdued colors of dusk. She preferred to start her work at dusk, finding inspiration in the fading light.

english_meaning: The prayer offered just after sunset, known as Maghrib in Islam. One of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed at dusk when the sun has set. A prayer said at twilight. An act of worship carried out immediately after the sun disappears below the horizon.
example_sentence: They broke their fast and then offered the dusk prayer. The dusk prayer is performed soon after sunset. He hurried to the mosque for the dusk prayer. The family gathered together for the dusk prayer. The call for the dusk prayer was heard as the sky turned orange.

english_meaning: Dim or shadowy, as in the half-light of evening. Having a darkish color or shade. Somewhat dark in complexion or hue. Gloomy, misty, or poorly lit.
example_sentence: The dusky evening settled over the valley. She had dusky skin and bright eyes. Bats flew out in the dusky twilight. The dusky pink roses smelled sweet.

english_meaning: To remove dust or dirt from something by brushing or wiping it. To bring something out and use it again after a long time. To prepare or refresh something that has not been used for a while. To get ready to use an old skill or plan again.
example_sentence: He dusted off his old guitar and started playing again. She dusted off her resume before applying for a new job. The team decided to dust off their old strategies for the upcoming match. I need to dust off my shoes before going to the party.

english_meaning: A dazed, confused, dreamy, or absent-minded state, especially in South African English. A trance-like condition in which someone is not fully aware of the surroundings. A temporary lapse of attention or mental clarity.
example_sentence: He walked around in a dwaal after the long flight. She seemed to be in a dwaal throughout the meeting. The afternoon heat put everyone into a dwaal. He could not concentrate because he was in a dwaal all morning.

english_meaning: A person, animal, or plant that is much smaller than the ordinary size of its species. To cause something to seem small by comparison. It can also refer to a legendary creature in folklore known for being short but skilled.
example_sentence: The skyscraper was so tall it seemed to dwarf the surrounding buildings. In many fairy tales, the dwarf is a skilled blacksmith living in the mountains. The new cargo ship is so huge that it will dwarf all previous models. Scientists have discovered a new species of dwarf lemur in the jungle.

english_meaning: To live or exist in the company of certain people or within a particular place or environment.
example_sentence: He dwelled among the villagers peacefully. Angels dwell among us in disguise. The tribe dwelled among the hills. The artist dwelled among nature for inspiration. Many legends say that fairies dwell among the trees and flowers.

english_meaning: To live or reside in a place or state (often used poetically or spiritually).
example_sentence: They dwell in the countryside. Peace dwells in the hearts of kind people. He dwelled in a small village for years. Wisdom dwells in those who listen. The poet often dwelt in memories of his childhood.

english_meaning: To spend a lot of time thinking, talking, or writing about something, especially something unpleasant or negative.
example_sentence: Don’t dwell on your past mistakes. She tends to dwell on negative thoughts. Let’s not dwell upon the problem, let’s find a solution. He dwelled on his failures instead of his achievements. He couldn’t stop dwelling on what went wrong during the interview. There’s no use dwelling on things you can’t change.

english_meaning: To spend a lot of time thinking, talking, or writing about something, especially something unpleasant or negative.
example_sentence: Don’t dwell upon your past mistakes; learn and move forward. He tends to dwell upon negative thoughts. The teacher dwelt upon the importance of honesty in her lecture. There’s no need to dwell upon what went wrong.

english_meaning: To exist or remain inside something, often referring to emotions, thoughts, or spiritual states.
example_sentence: Kindness dwells within every human heart. Hope dwells within every heart. A sense of calm dwelled within the temple. Evil dwells within those who envy. A deep fear dwells within him even today.

english_meaning: An inhabitant of a particular place or type of dwelling. It refers to someone who lives in a specific location, whether it be a house, city, or even a different planet. The term emphasizes the act of residing and making a home in an area, often implying a sense of permanence or long-term occupancy. It can also suggest a connection or familiarity with the environment they inhabit.
example_sentence: The cave dwellers adapted to their harsh environment. Urban dwellers often face higher living costs. The mountain dweller built a sturdy home. She is a lifelong dweller of this quiet village. As a city dweller, he appreciates green spaces.

english_meaning: To diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength. It describes the process of something becoming steadily less or smaller until it disappears or becomes insignificant. It is frequently used regarding resources, populations, or abstract concepts like hope.
example_sentence: Our water supplies began to dwindle during the long summer drought. As the years passed, his savings started to dwindle away. Their hopes of finding the lost hikers began to dwindle as night fell. The number of students in the evening class has started to dwindle recently.

english_meaning: To change the color of something. To apply color to something by using a dye, such as coloring cloth, hair, or other materials. A substance used to give color. A natural or chemical substance used to change the color of fabric, hair, leather, paper, or other materials.
example_sentence: She dyed her hair brown. They dye cotton using modern machines. He dyed the cloth at home. Artisans dye fabric by hand. The red dye faded after washing. She bought hair dye from the market. Natural dyes are eco friendly.

english_meaning: Strongly fixed in beliefs. A person whose beliefs, habits, or loyalties are very strong and unlikely to change because they have been held for a very long time. (Often used for political, religious, or personal beliefs)
example_sentence: He is a dyed in the wool supporter of the old political party. She remains a dyed in the wool traditionalist despite modern trends. My grandfather was a dyed in the wool believer in hard work and discipline. They are dyed in the wool fans who never miss a match.

english_meaning: Active, energetic, and always changing. A person, situation, system, or process that is full of energy, movement, and change. It often refers to something that does not stay still or fixed and keeps developing or improving over time.
example_sentence: She is a dynamic leader who inspires her team. The city has a dynamic culture that keeps evolving. Climate risks require dynamic planning approaches. He gave a dynamic presentation that held everyone’s attention.

english_meaning: Characterized by constant change, activity, or progress. It implies a process that is energetic, forceful, and interactive. To do something dynamically is to do it in a way that is not static or fixed but evolves and adapts. It often suggests a powerful and effective mode of operation. For example, a company might dynamically adjust its strategies to market shifts.
example_sentence: The software dynamically adjusts its display based on the screen size. The economy grew dynamically in the last quarter. She dynamically led the team through the challenging project. The dynamically changing weather made hiking difficult. The company dynamically responded to customer feedback.

english_meaning: The forces or properties that stimulate growth, development, or change within a system or process. It also describes the branch of mechanics concerned with the forces that cause motions of bodies. Furthermore, in music, dynamics indicate the variations in loudness between notes or phrases. In a broader sense, dynamics can encapsulate the interactive forces within a group or situation, influencing their behavior and evolution. The study of dynamics is crucial across various scientific and artistic disciplines for understanding change and movement. It helps in analyzing how different elements interact and bring about observable outcomes.
example_sentence: The dynamics of the team changed significantly after the new leader took over. She adjusted the dynamics of her piano playing to convey more emotion. Understanding the dynamics of the market is crucial for successful investment. The scientist studied the population dynamics of the endangered species. The internal dynamics of the organization led to its eventual restructuring.

english_meaning: The quality of being full of energy, action, and new ideas. Great force or drive that produces change and progress. A theory that explains phenomena in terms of forces and energy. Constant activity and forward movement in a person, group, or system.
example_sentence: The dynamism of the young team impressed the investors. Her dynamism turned a small shop into a national brand. The city is known for its cultural dynamism. Economic dynamism has created thousands of new jobs.

english_meaning: A line of rulers from the same family who reign over a country for a long period. A powerful family that maintains control or influence for many generations. A succession of leaders belonging to a single family. A period during which a particular family holds power. A group or family that dominates in a field for a long time.
example_sentence: The Mughal dynasty ruled India for several centuries. The Tang dynasty was known for its cultural achievements. His family has built a business dynasty over three generations. The dynasty came to an end after the king’s death.

english_meaning: A specific learning difficulty that primarily affects reading, spelling, and writing skills. It is a neurological difference that causes difficulty in processing language and recognizing word patterns. It does not affect a person's general intelligence.
synonyms: ["Learning Disorder","Word Blindness","Reading Difficulty","Learning Disability","Cognitive Condition","Processing Problem"]
example_sentence: Dyslexia makes it incredibly challenging for him to spell words correctly. The teacher used special learning methods to assist students with dyslexia. Despite her dyslexia, she became a highly successful and prolific writer. Early intervention can greatly improve reading skills in children with dyslexia. Dyslexia has absolutely nothing to do with a person's level of intelligence.

english_meaning: A mental condition where a person sees their body in a distorted or unrealistic way. It refers to a psychological condition in which a person has a distorted or inaccurate perception of their own body or appearance. They may believe that some part of their body is flawed, ugly, or abnormal even when it appears normal to others. It is commonly associated with Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), a mental health condition where this distorted self-image causes anxiety, stress, and repetitive behaviors such as mirror checking or excessive grooming.
synonyms: ["Body image distortion","Body dysmorphic disorder","Distorted self perception","Appearance preoccupation","Negative body image"]
antonyms: ["Body acceptance","Self acceptance","Positive body image","Realistic self perception","Body satisfaction"]
example_sentence: She avoided mirrors because her dysmorphia made her believe her face was deformed. His dysmorphia caused him to spend hours worrying about his nose. The therapist helped her understand that her dysmorphia was affecting her confidence. Even though others saw no problem, his dysmorphia made him feel unattractive.

english_meaning: A developmental neurological condition affecting the planning and coordination of movement. Difficulty performing skilled or purposeful movements despite having the physical ability to do them.
example_sentence: Dyspraxia can make handwriting difficult for some children. An occupational therapist helped him manage his dyspraxia. Dyspraxia may affect balance and fine motor skills. Early support can help people with dyspraxia build confidence.

english_meaning: A silvery rare-earth chemical element with the symbol Dy and atomic number 66. A highly magnetic metal used in powerful magnets, lasers, nuclear reactors, and other technologies.
example_sentence: Dysprosium is used in some high-performance magnets. The alloy contains a small amount of dysprosium. Scientists value dysprosium for its magnetic properties. Demand for dysprosium has grown with clean-energy technology.

english_meaning: An imagined society or state in which people suffer greatly because of oppression, injustice, disaster, or deprivation. A frightening and undesirable future world. A work of fiction portraying such a society.
example_sentence: The novel depicts a dystopia ruled by an oppressive government. In this dystopia, citizens have no privacy. The film’s dystopia warns about unchecked technology. Her story turns a perfect city into a dystopia.

english_meaning: Relating to an imagined society marked by suffering, injustice, oppression, or environmental ruin. Describing a frightening and undesirable future. Belonging to the literary or cinematic genre that portrays such societies.
example_sentence: The novel presents a dystopian society under constant surveillance. The film imagines a dystopian future without clean water. She enjoys reading dystopian fiction. The abandoned city gave the landscape a dystopian appearance.

english_meaning: A disorder involving defective nourishment, development, or degeneration of an organ or tissue. Progressive wasting or weakening, especially of muscles, often caused by an inherited condition.
example_sentence: Muscular dystrophy gradually weakens the muscles. Researchers are testing treatments for inherited dystrophy. Physical therapy helps some patients manage dystrophy. The diagnosis of retinal dystrophy explained her loss of vision.

english_meaning: Commercial transactions conducted electronically on the internet. Buying and selling goods and services online.
example_sentence: E-commerce has made it easier for people to shop from home. Many traditional retailers are moving toward a heavy e-commerce focus. Secure payment systems are essential for the growth of e-commerce. The rise of e-commerce has led to a decline in physical store visits.

english_meaning: A strong and impatient desire or interest in something. It implies enthusiasm and anticipation. An eager person is often keen to start an activity or to achieve a goal. It suggests a positive and proactive attitude. This word is typically used to convey a sense of genuine excitement and readiness.
example_sentence: She was eager to start her new job. The children were eager for the summer holidays to begin. He showed an eager interest in learning about ancient history. We are all eager to see the results of the competition. The crowd was eager to hear the band play their new song.

english_meaning: A person who is very enthusiastic and hardworking. Someone who is always ready to do more than what is required. An overly keen and diligent worker or student. A person full of energy and willingness to please. Someone excessively eager to start or complete tasks.
example_sentence: The new intern is a real eager beaver at the office. Our teacher praised the eager beaver students in class. He is such an eager beaver that he arrives an hour early. The team needs an eager beaver like her to succeed.

english_meaning: Strong desire or interest to do something. Enthusiastic willingness. A feeling of impatience to begin or achieve. Keen anticipation. Excitement about an upcoming event.
example_sentence: The children waited with eagerness for the show to begin. She showed great eagerness to learn new skills. His eagerness to help impressed everyone. There was eagerness in his voice as he shared the news.

english_meaning: The organ of hearing on either side of the head in humans and animals. The visible outer part of the hearing organ. The ability to recognize and appreciate sounds, especially music. Willingness to listen to someone with attention and sympathy. The seed-bearing head of a cereal plant such as maize or wheat.
example_sentence: He whispered something into her ear. The child covered his ears because of the loud noise. She has a good ear for classical music. The farmer picked a ripe ear of corn from the field.

english_meaning: The narrow tube that runs from the outer ear inwards to the eardrum. The passage that carries sound waves towards the middle ear. The channel lined with fine hairs and glands that produce protective earwax.
example_sentence: Sound travels down the ear canal to reach the eardrum. Never push cotton buds deep into the ear canal. Wax slowly moves out of the ear canal on its own. An infection of the ear canal can be very painful.

english_meaning: The act of whispering something secretly into someone's ear. A gesture of showing affection or intimacy by kissing the ear. A close, private conversation held in a low voice. Speaking to someone in a very confidential manner. A romantic or affectionate touch of the lips to the ear.
example_sentence: Their ear-kissing during the meeting made everyone suspicious. The couple exchanged an ear-kissing moment at the party. She was annoyed by their constant ear-kissing behind her back. The politicians were seen ear-kissing before the vote.

english_meaning: The thin, cone-shaped membrane that separates the ear canal from the middle ear. The tightly stretched sheet of tissue that vibrates when sound waves strike it. The structure that passes sound vibrations on to the tiny bones of the middle ear.
example_sentence: The eardrum vibrates whenever sound reaches it. A very loud noise can rupture the eardrum. The doctor used a torch to look at the eardrum. A perforated eardrum usually heals within a few weeks.

english_meaning: One who wakes early. A person who wakes up early or arrives early for something. It also refers to someone who takes advantage of an opportunity before others. Someone who takes initiative, wakes up early, or arrives before others.
example_sentence: The early bird catches the worm (= The person who arrives early or acts quickly has an advantage). She is an early bird, always reaching the office before everyone else.

english_meaning: A person who earns money, income, or a living through work, business, or other activities. A person who earns money, wages, a salary, or other income through employment, business, professional services, or any other income-generating activity. It is often used to describe someone who contributes financially to their own living expenses or to the needs of their family.
example_sentence: She is the main earner in her family. High earners pay more tax in this system. Rental properties can be a steady earner. He became a high earner after starting his own business.

english_meaning: Serious, sincere, and showing genuine intention or strong determination. It means being serious, sincere, and deeply committed to something. It describes a person who genuinely means what they say, acts with honesty and sincerity, or makes a serious and determined effort to achieve a goal. It can also describe a conversation, request, promise, or effort that is made with genuine feelings, strong intention, and a sincere desire for a particular result.
example_sentence: He made an earnest attempt to solve the problem. In earnest, she promised to change her ways. The two sides began negotiations in earnest. Her earnest expression convinced us of her honesty.

english_meaning: In a serious, sincere, and determined manner. With genuine effort and deep conviction. In a way that shows strong feeling or commitment.
example_sentence: She earnestly believes that education can change lives. He spoke earnestly about the need for reform. The volunteers worked earnestly to finish the project on time. I earnestly hope that peace will return to the region.

english_meaning: The quality of being serious, sincere, and deeply committed. An attitude of genuine dedication and honest effort. Intense conviction and wholehearted devotion to a purpose.
example_sentence: Her earnestness impressed everyone at the interview. He spoke with such earnestness that no one doubted his words. The earnestness of the students showed in their work. I admired the earnestness with which he pursued his goals.

english_meaning: The money a person receives through employment, business, investment, or other activities. It can also refer to the process of obtaining money, rewards, recognition, or other benefits through work, effort, skill, or achievement. The ongoing process of gaining money, respect, trust, or a reward through effort.
example_sentence: His monthly earnings are enough to support the family. She invested her earnings in a small business. The company's earnings rose sharply this quarter. Online platforms offer new ways of earning from home.

english_meaning: A long, soft, segmented worm that lives in soil. A burrowing creature that improves soil fertility by breaking down organic matter.
example_sentence: An earthworm wriggled out of the wet soil. Earthworms improve the quality of garden soil. He found several earthworms while digging. Farmers value earthworms for natural composting.

english_meaning: A small brown insect with a pair of pincers at the end of its body. A night-active insect often found in damp places and among plants.
example_sentence: An earwig crawled out from under the flower pot. Earwigs are usually harmless to humans. She found an earwig hiding in the damp corner. Earwigs sometimes nibble the petals of flowers.

english_meaning: Used to say that something sounds like a good idea but is difficult to actually do.
example_sentence: Finding a new job is easier said than done in this economy. We need to stay calm, but that's easier said than done. Quitting smoking is definitely easier said than done. Saving money every month is often easier said than done.

english_meaning: Gained without effort and lost without pain. A casual acceptance that loss is not a big deal if it came easily. Used to comfort someone who loses something gained without effort. Shows a carefree attitude toward temporary gains. Expresses emotional detachment from quick wins. Used when losses are expected because gains were unstable
synonyms: ["Casual loss","Lighthearted acceptance","No big deal","Here today gone tomorrow"]
antonyms: ["Hard earned","Well deserved","Painful loss","Difficult to give up"]
example_sentence: He won some cash in a game but spent it the same day. Easy come easy go. She got a quick promotion and lost it soon after. Easy come easy go. I found a little money on the street and donated it because easy come easy go. The company made fast profits but lost them in a week. Easy come easy go.

english_meaning: Move slowly and carefully. Take things gently, do not rush. Often used as advice to proceed cautiously to avoid mistakes or accidents.
example_sentence: Easy does it! Don’t spill the paint while moving the ladder. When lifting the heavy box, easy does it so you don’t hurt your back. Easy does it, we don’t want to break anything valuable. He told the children, “Easy does it,” as they carried the fragile vase. When introducing the puppy to other dogs, easy does it to avoid scaring it.

english_meaning: Pleasant or attractive to look at. Physically good-looking or handsome. Visually soothing and comfortable to view. Not harsh or straining to the sight. Aesthetically pleasing in appearance.
example_sentence: The new actor is really easy on the eyes. The soft lighting in the room is easy on the eyes. Her paintings are colorful and easy on the eyes. The website design is clean and easy on the eyes.

english_meaning: Relaxed and not easily worried or upset. Calm and tolerant in dealing with people and problems. Not strict about rules or details. Comfortable and unhurried in manner or lifestyle.
example_sentence: My uncle is an easy-going man who rarely complains. The office has a friendly, easy-going atmosphere. She has an easy-going attitude towards deadlines. Their easy-going manager never shouts at the staff.

english_meaning: To admit your mistake and accept humiliation or embarrassment. To acknowledge that you were wrong, often after acting proudly or arrogantly, and to accept the consequences in a humble way. It usually involves apologizing or accepting criticism.
antonyms: ["Stand firm","Deny responsibility","Remain proud","Justify oneself","Refuse to apologize"]
example_sentence: After arguing all day, he had to eat humble pie when he realized he was wrong. She laughed at his idea at first but later had to eat humble pie when it succeeded. The manager ate humble pie after blaming the team for a mistake he made. He refused to eat humble pie even after clear evidence proved him wrong.

english_meaning: To eat very little food at a time. To have a noticeably small appetite. To consume portions that are unusually small for an average person. To peck at one's meals without taking substantial bites.
synonyms: ["Eat Very Little","Pick At Food","Nibble","Have A Small Appetite","Starve Oneself","Consume Barely Anything","Diet Strictly","Fast","Eat Lightly","Peck At"]
example_sentence: She is very thin because she tends to eat like a bird. You cannot survive on that salad alone, you eat like a bird. Whenever we go to a buffet, my grandmother will only eat like a bird. I used to eat like a bird, but my appetite has grown recently.

english_meaning: To suffer from envy, jealousy, or deep longing. To feel intense jealousy, envy, or longing.
example_sentence: He’s eating his heart out over her success. She saw him with another woman and ate her heart out. Let them eat their hearts out with envy. He ate his heart out for years after losing her.

english_meaning: To admit that something one said earlier was wrong. To retract a statement in an embarrassed or humbled way. To be forced by events to take back a confident claim.
example_sentence: He had to eat his words when the team finally won. If she succeeds, the critics will eat their words. I was made to eat my words after the results came out. Be careful with such predictions, or you may eat your words.

english_meaning: To consume someone emotionally by causing intense guilt, anxiety, or internal distress over a prolonged period. It describes a situation where a secret or regret constantly torments a person's conscience. It refers to a deep emotional pain or worry that slowly destroys an individual's peace of mind. It illustrates the feeling of being overwhelmed by negative emotions that one cannot easily express or release. It denotes an agonizing mental state where suppressed feelings cause severe psychological discomfort.
example_sentence: Keeping the truth about the accident from his family began to eat him up inside. The guilt of lying to her best friend will eventually eat her up inside. He tried to hide his jealousy, but watching them together was eating him up inside. If you do not confess your mistakes, the regret will eat you up inside for years.

english_meaning: A restaurant or other place where people can buy and eat food. A small or informal dining establishment.
example_sentence: We found a quaint little eatery near the beach. The new downtown eatery serves the best burgers in the city. After the movie, they went to a local eatery for some late-night snacks. Every weekend, she visits a different eatery to review its menu.

english_meaning: To have a meal at a restaurant instead of at home. Used when people go out for food or social dining.
example_sentence: We usually eat out on weekends. Let’s eat out tonight. They ate out to celebrate their anniversary. He doesn’t like eating out often.

english_meaning: The lower edges of a roof which usually project beyond the side of a building. The overhanging edge of a structure. A place where water drips from a roof. The underside of the edge of a roof. Architectural projections used to shed water away from walls.
example_sentence: The sparrows built their small nests under the eaves of the old farmhouse. Heavy icicles hung from the eaves during the peak of the winter storm. He stood under the eaves to shelter himself from the sudden downpour of rain. The wooden eaves were carved with intricate patterns reflecting the local architecture.

english_meaning: To secretly listen to a private conversation without the permission of the speakers. This often involves lurking near a conversation or using electronic devices to intercept communication. Eavesdropping is generally considered a breach of privacy and can be illegal depending on the context and jurisdiction. It can be done out of curiosity, suspicion, or with malicious intent to gather information for personal gain or to cause harm. The act often implies surreptitious behavior. It can also refer to the accidental overhearing of a conversation.
example_sentence: She was accused of eavesdropping on her neighbors' conversation. He suspected his phone calls were being monitored through eavesdropping. The security agency was caught eavesdropping on foreign diplomats. Accidental eavesdropping can sometimes lead to misunderstandings. Modern technology has made electronic eavesdropping more sophisticated.

english_meaning: A multinational e-commerce corporation that facilitates consumer-to-consumer and business-to-consumer sales through its website. It is one of the world's largest online marketplaces, offering a wide array of products from electronics and fashion to collectibles and vehicles. The platform allows users to buy and sell new or used items, often through auction-style listings or "Buy It Now" fixed-price options. Ebay also owns other businesses like StubHub and operates in numerous countries, providing a global reach for its users. It has been a significant force in shaping the landscape of online retail and remains a popular destination for both casual shoppers and serious collectors.
synonyms: ["Online marketplace","E-commerce platform","Auction site","Retail website","Internet store","Pee-to-peer sales","Digital retailer","Web retailer","Bidding site","Exchange platform"]
antonyms: ["Brick-and-mortar store","Physical shop","Local retailer","Offline market","Traditional store","Walk-in shop"]
example_sentence: I found a rare vintage watch on Ebay last night. She sells her handmade jewelry exclusively on Ebay. He regularly scours Ebay for unique comic book finds. My old smartphone was sold on Ebay within hours. Many small businesses use Ebay to reach a global customer base.

english_meaning: The reflux of the tide toward the sea. A point or condition of decline. To recede from the flood. To fall from a higher to a lower level or from a better to a worse state. A change to a lower state or level. To become worse or of less value. To grow less in scope or intensity especially gradually.
example_sentence: It was difficult sailing upstream against a strong ebb. They left port on the ebb tide. They went out to sea with the ebb. The pain was ebbing. As night fell, our enthusiasm began to ebb away. Her strength began to ebb. We'll sail on the ebb.

english_meaning: A hard, heavy, black wood from tropical trees. A very deep black color like ebony wood. Made of ebony wood. Having an intense black color.
example_sentence: The piano keys were made of ebony and ivory. Her ebony hair fell to her waist. The craftsman carved a statue from solid ebony. The night sky was a deep ebony black.

english_meaning: Someone full of cheer, enthusiasm, and energy. It suggests a bubbling over of high spirits and excitement, often displayed through lively and expressive behavior. An ebullient person is typically optimistic, joyful, and radiates positivity. They often exude a contagious enthusiasm that can uplift those around them. This term is frequently used to characterize individuals who are vibrant and effervescent in their demeanor.
example_sentence: The ebullient crowd cheered wildly as their team scored the winning goal. Her ebullient personality makes her a joy to be around. He was in an ebullient mood after receiving the good news. The speaker delivered an ebullient address that captivated the audience. Despite the challenges, she maintained an ebullient spirit.

english_meaning: Unconventional or strange. It describes a person whose behavior or thinking deviates markedly from the norm. An eccentric individual might have unusual habits, dress in peculiar ways, or hold very peculiar beliefs that are not widely shared. Despite their oddities, eccentrics are often harmless and sometimes even charming or brilliant. Their unique perspectives can lead to innovative ideas or artistic expressions, making them stand out in a crowd. However, extreme eccentricity might sometimes border on the pathological if it significantly impairs their daily functioning or social interactions.
example_sentence: Dr. Smith is known for his eccentric habit of wearing a different colored sock on each foot. Her grandfather was a brilliant but eccentric inventor who lived in a house filled with his peculiar contraptions. The artist's eccentric lifestyle often fueled rumors and fascination in the community. He had an eccentric way of speaking, often pausing for long periods before delivering a punchline. The old mansion, with its uneven floors and secret passages, had an undeniably eccentric charm.

english_meaning: A level or rank in an organization, a profession, or society. It can also refer to a formation of troops, ships, or aircraft in parallel rows. It essentially represents a tier within a hierarchical structure.
example_sentence: The upper echelon of the government made the final decision on the policy. She quickly rose to the highest echelon of the corporate world. Airplanes often fly in a V-shaped echelon formation for better visibility. Decisions are typically passed down from the top echelon to the subordinates.

english_meaning: A sound that is heard again because it is reflected from a surface such as a wall, mountain, or cave. The repetition of a sound caused by reflection of sound waves. (Figuratively) A repetition or imitation of someone else's opinions, words, ideas, or style. A trace or sign that something still exists or has an influence. To repeat a sound or to express the same opinion as someone else.
example_sentence: We could hear the echo of our voices in the empty hall. The mountains sent back a clear echo of his shout. His latest speech was just an echo of his earlier ideas. The new policy is an echo of the old one. Her words echoed in my mind for days.

english_meaning: A member of the generation born after Generation X. Refers to someone born roughly between 1981 and 1996, also called a Millennial. The term comes from the “echo” of the Baby Boomer generation, as this generation is the children of Baby Boomers.
example_sentence: Many Echo Boomers are tech-savvy and value work-life balance. The company targets Echo Boomers in its marketing campaigns. Echo Boomers grew up with the internet and social media. Housing preferences of Echo Boomers differ from previous generations.

english_meaning: Deriving ideas, style, or taste from a wide range of sources. Selecting what seems best from various styles or systems. Combining diverse elements in a harmonious way. A person who chooses from different sources. Showing broad and varied interests.
example_sentence: Her taste in music is eclectic, ranging from jazz to rock. The restaurant serves an eclectic mix of dishes. He has an eclectic collection of books. The gallery displays eclectic works from many artists.

english_meaning: Something related to the environment, ecology, or environmentalism. It often functions as a prefix, indicating a connection to ecological principles or sustainability. The term is widely used in contemporary discussions about conservation, green technology, and sustainable living. It can also denote a system or an approach that aims to minimize negative impacts on the natural world. This concept emphasizes the interconnectedness of living organisms and their physical surroundings.
example_sentence: The company is committed to eco-friendly practices. She

english_meaning: Anxiety or worry caused by environmental problems and climate change. A persistent feeling of stress, fear, or concern about environmental destruction, climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss, and the future of the planet. It often appears when someone feels overwhelmed or powerless about environmental issues.
antonyms: ["Environmental calm","Eco confidence","Peace about environment","Climate optimism","Environmental reassurance"]
example_sentence: Many young people experience eco anxiety after reading about climate change. Her eco anxiety increased when she saw reports of rising sea levels. Talking about solutions helped reduce his eco anxiety. Social media discussions sometimes worsen eco anxiety among students.

english_meaning: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings. Characterized by the interdependence of living organisms.
example_sentence: The oil spill caused an ecological disaster in the Gulf region. Scientists are studying the ecological impact of the new dam construction. We must maintain the ecological balance to protect endangered species. The park serves as an important ecological sanctuary for migratory birds.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings. With regard to ecology.
example_sentence: The new housing project was designed to be ecologically friendly. Ecologically, the destruction of the forest will have severe impacts. They are working to restore the ecologically damaged coral reefs. The farm is managed ecologically without the use of toxic pesticides.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies ecology, which is the relationship between living organisms and their environment. A person who examines how plants, animals, and other living things interact with each other and with their physical surroundings. Someone who advocates for the protection and preservation of natural ecosystems. A specialist in the branch of biology concerned with how species relate to one another and to their habitat.
example_sentence: The ecologist spent months studying the impact of deforestation on local wildlife.  She trained as an ecologist after witnessing widespread pollution in her hometown.  The government consulted an ecologist before approving the construction of the new dam.  As an ecologist, his research focused on the interaction between soil organisms and plant life.  The ecologist's findings revealed alarming changes in the region's biodiversity.

english_meaning: The branch of biology that studies the relationships between living organisms and their environment, including both living and non-living components. The scientific study of the distribution and abundance of organisms and how they interact with their surroundings. The system of relationships that exists among living things and the world they inhabit. The study of how ecosystems function and how environmental factors affect the survival and behavior of species.
example_sentence: Ecology teaches us how every organism plays a role in maintaining the balance of nature.  Her PhD thesis explored the ecology of freshwater rivers in tropical regions.  Urban ecology examines how cities affect local plant and animal populations.  Climate change has become one of the most pressing concerns in modern ecology.  Understanding ecology is essential for designing effective conservation programmes.

english_meaning: Relating to the economy, trade, industry, or the management of money. Concerning the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. Justified in terms of profit and financial return. Related to the material needs and financial condition of people or countries. Involving practical financial considerations.
example_sentence: The country is facing a serious economic crisis. Economic growth has slowed down this year. The government announced new economic reforms. Many families are struggling due to economic pressure.

english_meaning: Careful in using money, resources, or time to avoid waste. Giving good value or return in relation to the money or effort spent. Using no more of something than is necessary. Sparing in speech, writing, or action. Efficient and thrifty in habits or design.
example_sentence: This small car is very economical to run. She is economical with both her time and money. The new design is more economical than the previous one. He was economical in his choice of words during the speech.

english_meaning: The branch of knowledge concerned with the production, consumption, and transfer of wealth. The condition of a region or group as regards material prosperity.
example_sentence: She decided to major in economics to understand global markets better. The basic principles of economics involve supply and demand forces. The economics of the project simply do not make sense right now. He works as a consultant specialising in health care economics.

english_meaning: An expert who studies the relationship between a society's resources and its production or output. A person who practices economics.
example_sentence: The lead economist predicted a slow recovery for the national market. As an economist, he tracks inflation and employment rates closely. The government hired a famous economist to advise on new tax laws. She is a respected economist who publishes regularly in major journals.

english_meaning: The wealth and resources of a country, region, or community, especially in terms of production and consumption. The careful management of money, materials, or resources to avoid waste. A system of trade and industry by which the wealth of a country is created. Thrifty use of something in order to save cost or effort. A cheaper class of travel or product.
example_sentence: The country's economy has grown rapidly in recent years. We must practice economy in our daily expenses. The government is trying to strengthen the local economy. He always travels in economy class to save money.

english_meaning: A biological community of interacting organisms together with their physical environment, functioning as a system. The complex network of relationships between all living organisms in a particular area and the non-living physical environment they share. A self-sustaining unit consisting of producers, consumers, decomposers, and the abiotic factors that support them. Used figuratively to describe any complex, interconnected system of businesses, technologies, or communities.
example_sentence: The coral reef ecosystem supports thousands of species of fish and marine life.  Human activity has severely disrupted the ecosystem of the Amazon rainforest.  A healthy ecosystem depends on the balanced interaction of all its components.  The tech company described its network of partners and suppliers as a thriving digital ecosystem.  Scientists warned that the destruction of wetlands would destabilize the entire local ecosystem.

english_meaning: A light beige or greyish-brown color like unbleached linen. Having the pale brownish color of raw silk or unbleached fabric. A soft, natural off-white shade.
example_sentence: The wedding invitations were printed on ecru paper. She chose ecru curtains for the sunny room. The tablecloth was a soft ecru shade. He wore an ecru linen suit to the beach wedding.

english_meaning: An overwhelming feeling of great happiness or joyful excitement. Intense pleasure or delight. A state of being beyond reason or self-control, often due to emotion or spiritual experience. A trance-like state of rapture
example_sentence: She was in ecstasy after hearing the good news. Winning the championship filled him with ecstasy. The music took him to a state of ecstasy. The painter felt ecstasy while finishing his masterpiece. The artist painted with ecstasy in every stroke. Winning the award filled her with ecstasy. Listening to the symphony sent him into ecstasy.

english_meaning: Extremely happy or overjoyed. Feeling or expressing overwhelming happiness, joy, or delight. A state of intense pleasure or excitement.
example_sentence: She was ecstatic when she received the acceptance letter from her dream university. The fans were ecstatic after their team won the championship. He felt ecstatic upon hearing the news of his promotion. The children were ecstatic to see the fireworks display.

english_meaning: Relating to animals that depend on external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature. Cold-blooded, having a body temperature that varies with the environment. Describing organisms unable to produce sufficient internal heat. Used for reptiles, amphibians, fish, and most invertebrates.
example_sentence: Snakes are ectothermic animals that bask in the sun to warm up. Most reptiles are ectothermic and depend on the environment for heat. Ectothermic species become less active in cold weather. Fish are typically ectothermic creatures. Ectothermic animals require less food than warm-blooded animals.

english_meaning: Fit or safe to eat. Suitable for eating. Safe for human consumption. Non poisonous food item. Food grade. Something that can be eaten safely and is suitable for food. It may be raw or cooked but should not be harmful.
example_sentence: These berries are edible but not very tasty. The leaves of this plant are edible after cooking. Make sure the mushrooms are edible before eating them. The oil is edible and safe for cooking.

english_meaning: To teach or improve someone morally or intellectually. To instruct someone in a way that improves their knowledge, character, or moral values. It is often used for learning that uplifts a person’s thinking or behavior.
example_sentence: Good books can edify readers and broaden their minds. The teacher tries to edify students through real life examples. His speech was meant to edify the audience, not just entertain them. Religious teachings often aim to edify people morally.

english_meaning: A person who prepares written material for publication by correcting and improving it. The person in charge of a newspaper, magazine or broadcast programme. Someone who selects and arranges film, video or audio content. A computer program used for writing and modifying text or code.
example_sentence: The editor asked for a shorter version of the article. She was promoted to editor of the science magazine. A skilled editor turned hours of footage into a short film. He opened the text editor to fix the code.

english_meaning: An article in a newspaper or magazine expressing the opinion of its editors. A broadcast commentary presenting the views of a network or station. Relating to the editing or content of a publication. Connected with the work and judgement of an editor.
example_sentence: The newspaper published a strong editorial on climate policy. She writes a weekly editorial about education reform. The magazine maintains full editorial independence. Editorial standards must be applied to every article.

english_meaning: Relating to education, teaching, or learning. Providing knowledge, information, or useful experience. Intended to teach something. Connected with schools, colleges, or the system of study.
example_sentence: The museum visit was highly educational for the children. Educational standards have improved in recent years. She works for an educational charity in rural areas. The programme is both entertaining and educational.

english_meaning: A long, slender fish with a snakelike body. Any of various freshwater or marine fishes of the order Anguilliformes. A slippery or evasive person, used figuratively. Something long and flexible that resembles an eel. To catch or fish for eels. To move or wriggle in a smooth, twisting way.
example_sentence: An eel slipped between the rocks and vanished. Some eels travel thousands of kilometers to breed. The child eeled through the narrow gap in the fence. They went eeling in the river after sunset.

english_meaning: Strange and frightening. Mysterious in a way that makes a person feel nervous or afraid. Unnaturally quiet, unfamiliar, or disturbing.
example_sentence: An eerie silence filled the old building. We heard an eerie sound from the forest. The fog gave the village an eerie appearance. There was something eerie about his smile.

english_meaning: In a strange and frightening way. In a manner that creates an uneasy feeling of mystery or fear. In an unexpectedly unusual or uncanny way.
example_sentence: The abandoned house was eerily quiet at night. Her voice sounded eerily familiar. The empty streets glowed eerily under the moonlight. The prediction was eerily accurate.

english_meaning: The quality of being strange, mysterious, and frightening. An unsettling feeling caused by something unnatural or unfamiliar. A haunting or uncanny atmosphere.
example_sentence: The empty station had an unmistakable eeriness. Fog added to the eeriness of the forest. The film creates eeriness without showing any monsters. We felt the eeriness of the silent house as soon as we entered.

english_meaning: A mild written or spoken substitute for a strong swear word. To use that substitute as an exclamation or insult. To spoil, damage, or interfere with something, in informal usage.
example_sentence: What the eff is happening here? He was careful not to eff up the presentation. She told him to eff off after the insult. They effed the schedule by changing it at the last minute.

english_meaning: To waste time by behaving aimlessly or foolishly. To avoid doing a task seriously. To handle or experiment with something casually. A chiefly British softened informal expression.
example_sentence: We cannot eff about when the deadline is tomorrow. He effed about all morning instead of cleaning. Stop effing about with the controls. They were effing about at the back of the class.

english_meaning: To use many swear words, especially repeatedly or angrily. To curse and complain loudly.
example_sentence: He effed and blinded when he saw the repair bill. There is no need to eff and blind over a small mistake. She could hear the driver effing and blinding outside. They effed and blinded throughout the heated argument.

english_meaning: To waste time instead of doing something useful. To behave foolishly or without seriousness. To experiment casually without a clear purpose. A mildly softened form of a vulgar informal expression.
example_sentence: Stop effing around and finish your homework. We spent the afternoon effing around with the new camera. He was fired for effing around at work. They effed around until they missed the last bus.

english_meaning: A rude and offensive command telling someone to go away. To leave, especially when told to do so. To dismiss or reject someone angrily.
example_sentence: He rudely told the reporters to eff off. She wished the noisy stranger would eff off. Do not tell people to eff off during an argument. The character effed off before anyone could question him.

english_meaning: To make a serious mistake. To spoil, damage, or ruin something. To cause someone emotional or physical harm. A softened informal substitute for a vulgar phrasal verb.
example_sentence: I really effed up the presentation by using the wrong figures. Do not eff up this opportunity. The accident effed up his shoulder. That experience effed her up for years.

english_meaning: To annoy, provoke, or treat someone badly. To interfere with, alter, or tamper with something. To challenge or deceive someone. A softened informal version of a vulgar expression.
example_sentence: Do not eff with the settings unless you know what they do. Nobody wanted to eff with the experienced boxer. She warned them not to eff with her team. Someone had effed with the lock.

english_meaning: To erase or remove something from a surface. To make something less visible, prominent, or memorable. To cause oneself to appear modest or inconspicuous. To wipe out a mark, memory, or distinction.
example_sentence: Time had effaced the writing on the stone. The renovation effaced much of the building’s original character. She tried to efface herself in the crowded room. No apology could efface the painful memory.

english_meaning: A change, result, or consequence caused by an action or event. The power to influence or produce a result. A particular impression or appearance. Personal belongings, especially when used in the plural. To cause something to happen or bring it about.
example_sentence: The medicine had an immediate effect on her pain. The lighting created a dramatic effect. The new manager effected several important changes. The traveler collected his personal effects before leaving.

english_meaning: Successful in producing the intended or desired result. Having a noticeable or powerful effect. In operation or legally valid from a stated time. Actually available for use after deductions. Impressive or striking in appearance.
example_sentence: This is an effective treatment for mild pain. The new policy becomes effective on Monday. Clear communication is the most effective solution. Her simple design was highly effective.

english_meaning: In a way that achieves the intended result. In a manner that produces a strong effect. In practical terms or in reality, even if not officially. From the time when a rule or agreement begins to operate.
example_sentence: She communicated her concerns effectively. The road closure effectively isolated the village. He is effectively the leader of the group. The changes will apply effectively from next month.

english_meaning: Having traits, habits, or characteristics traditionally associated with women rather than men. Exhibiting qualities such as delicacy, softness, or weakness traditionally considered uncharacteristic of a male. Characterized by excessive refinement or a lack of physical vigor.
example_sentence: He was often teased at school for his effeminate mannerisms. Critics described the artist's early works as delicate and somewhat effeminate. The actor adopted an effeminate tone of voice to play the eccentric character. In ancient times, some rulers were accused of living an effeminate lifestyle of luxury.

english_meaning: Full of bubbles or lively energy. Describes a liquid that gives off bubbles or a person who is cheerful, enthusiastic, and full of positive energy.
example_sentence: The effervescent drink fizzed as soon as it was opened. Her effervescent personality made everyone feel welcome. The tablet became effervescent when dropped into water. He remained effervescent even during stressful situations.

english_meaning: Effective; producing the intended result. Something that works well or achieves the desired effect. It refers to a method, action, or remedy that is successful in producing a result.
example_sentence: Meditation proved efficacious in reducing stress. The new policy was efficacious in improving productivity. Vaccines are efficacious in preventing diseases. Her persuasive speech was highly efficacious in winning support.

english_meaning: Achieving a result with minimal waste of time, effort, energy, or money. Working in a well-organized and competent way. Producing a high useful output relative to input.
example_sentence: The new heating system is highly efficient. She is an efficient and dependable manager. We need a more efficient way to deliver supplies. Efficient appliances can reduce electricity costs.

english_meaning: In a way that achieves results with little waste of time, effort, energy, or money. In an organized and competent manner. With maximum useful output from available resources.
example_sentence: The staff handled every request efficiently. This engine uses fuel more efficiently than the old one. She organized the files quickly and efficiently. The new system allows orders to be processed efficiently.

english_meaning: A model, statue, or image representing a person, often made to be burned or destroyed in protest or anger. It can also refer to a likeness or figure made to honor or criticize someone.
example_sentence: Protesters burned an effigy of the corrupt leader in the city square. The museum displayed an effigy of the ancient king made of stone. During the festival, villagers carried an effigy of the demon before setting it on fire. The artist sculpted an effigy of the national hero to honor his bravery.

english_meaning: The process or period of flowering. A flourishing or full development of art, culture, or ideas. A powdery crystalline deposit appearing on masonry or other surfaces. Redness or a skin eruption.
example_sentence: Spring brought an efflorescence of wildflowers. The period saw an efflorescence of music and poetry. White efflorescence appeared on the damp brick wall. The doctor examined the sudden efflorescence on her skin.

english_meaning: Liquid waste or sewage discharged into water or the environment. A stream flowing out of a body of water or treatment facility. Flowing outward from a source.
