Photographic emulsions must be stored in cool, dark conditions to remain effective.

english_meaning: Forming a single unit, especially a bedroom with a bathroom directly attached to it. A bathroom that is connected to and accessible only from a bedroom. Describing rooms that are joined together as one set. Arranged as part of a continuous set or series.
example_sentence: The hotel room has an en suite bathroom with a shower. All bedrooms in the house are en suite. We booked a double room en suite for the weekend. Guests prefer an en suite to sharing a bathroom.

english_meaning: A hyphenated form of 'en suite', describing a bathroom joined directly to a bedroom. Belonging to or forming part of the same set of rooms. A private bathroom accessible from within a bedroom. Arranged as a connected unit rather than separately.
example_sentence: Each apartment comes with an en-suite bathroom. The en-suite shower room was clean and modern. They converted the storeroom into an en-suite. We requested an en-suite room for our elderly parents.

english_meaning: To put a plan, law, or policy into action or effect, especially through official or legislative procedure. To pass a law or official resolution and bring it into force. To act out or perform a story, scene, or role, especially in a theatrical or ceremonial context. To officially make something legally valid or operative.
example_sentence: The parliament voted to enact new legislation on data privacy.  The children were asked to enact the scene from the story in front of the class.  The government plans to enact a series of economic reforms in the coming months.  The new safety regulations were enacted following a series of workplace accidents.  The play enacted events from the country's turbulent history.

english_meaning: The process of passing a law and making it officially valid. A law or rule that has been formally passed by a legislative body. The act of performing or acting out something, such as a scene or event. A formal performance or representation of something. The carrying out of a plan, policy, or decision.
example_sentence: The enactment of the new law took several months of debate in parliament. Citizens welcomed the enactment of stronger laws against corruption. The play included a moving enactment of historical events. The enactment of the government's reform plan has been delayed again. The court will examine the enactment of the recent ordinance.

english_meaning: To inspire with love. To fill someone with admiration or affection. To be filled with a feeling of love or strong liking for someone or something. Usually used in the form 'enamoured of' or 'enamoured with'.
example_sentence: He was enamoured of the beautiful actress from the first sight. She is completely enamoured with the new city. The audience was enamoured by his soulful singing. He became enamoured of poetry during his college years. Tourists are often enamoured with the charm of the old town.

english_meaning: A territory, district, or group of people that is completely surrounded by another territory or a different culture. It may refer to a piece of land that lies within the borders of another country or to a social or cultural group living inside a larger community while keeping its own traditions, language, or lifestyle.
example_sentence: The city has a small Italian enclave where many Italian families live. The embassy area functions like an international enclave within the capital. The mountain village remained an isolated enclave for many centuries. Many immigrants settled in a cultural enclave where they could speak their own language.

english_meaning: To surround or close something off on all sides, typically with a fence, wall, or other barrier. To include something within a letter, package, or container along with other items. To contain or shut something in so that it cannot freely move or escape. To place something within enclosing boundaries for protection, privacy, or security.
example_sentence: Please enclose a copy of your passport with the completed application form.  The garden was enclosed by a tall stone wall that provided complete privacy.  The farmer used wooden fencing to enclose the pasture for the sheep.  She enclosed a cheque for the full amount with her letter of acceptance.  The courtyard was enclosed on three sides by the old university buildings.

english_meaning: An area of land that is surrounded by a fence or wall and separated from the surrounding area. A document, photograph, or other item included with a letter or package. The historical process in Britain of fencing off common land for private use. A structure used to contain or confine animals at a zoo, farm, or similar setting.
example_sentence: The children watched the elephants from a safe distance outside the enclosure.  Please find the enclosure with this letter, which includes the signed contract.  The enclosure movement of the eighteenth century displaced thousands of rural farming families.  The zoo built a larger enclosure to give the lions more space to roam.  A secure enclosure around the building was installed after the security breach.

english_meaning: A formal expression of high praise, especially in speech or writing. A speech or piece of writing that warmly praises a person, thing, or achievement. A tribute paid publicly to honour someone's qualities or work. Enthusiastic admiration expressed openly. A eulogy delivered in honour of someone.
example_sentence: The principal delivered a warm encomium at the retiring teacher's farewell. Critics wrote a glowing encomium for her debut novel. His encomium moved many people in the audience to tears. The article was less a review than an encomium to the young scientist.

english_meaning: To surround or include something completely within its scope or extent. To include a wide range of things within a single category, subject, or area. To encircle or form a boundary around something. To contain, cover, or deal with a broad variety of subjects, factors, or elements at once.
example_sentence: The curriculum was redesigned to encompass a broader range of cultural perspectives.  The national park encompasses over one million acres of protected wilderness.  Her research interests encompass history, politics, and international relations.  The wall was built to encompass the entire ancient city within its boundaries.  A good manager must encompass both technical knowledge and strong interpersonal skills.

english_meaning: A repeated or extra performance given after the main show. A demand by an audience for more, usually by shouting. To call for or perform an additional piece. Used as an exclamation meaning perform it again.
example_sentence: The band played two songs as an encore. The audience shouted encore at the end of the concert. She was encored three times that evening. His piano encore delighted the whole hall.

english_meaning: To meet someone or something unexpectedly. To experience or face something, especially something difficult or unpleasant. A meeting, especially one that is unexpected or brief. An instance of facing or dealing with something.
example_sentence: I encountered an old friend at the supermarket yesterday. The explorers encountered many difficulties during their journey. It was a brief encounter that changed my life. Scientists often encounter unexpected results in their experiments.

english_meaning: To give someone support, courage, or hope. To urge a person to do something by showing confidence in them. To help an activity or process to develop and grow. To make something more likely to happen. To offer praise that increases confidence and effort.
example_sentence: Her parents always encouraged her to read widely. Good teachers encourage students to ask questions. The new policy is designed to encourage small businesses. Warm weather encourages the growth of these plants.

english_meaning: The action of giving someone support, confidence, or hope. Words or actions intended to motivate someone to continue. The act of stimulating and supporting a person's development or efforts.
example_sentence: A few words of encouragement from her mentor were enough to turn her self-doubt into determination. He needed constant encouragement from his family to keep going through the most difficult period. The team responded brilliantly to the encouragement of the crowd behind them. Without encouragement from her teachers, she would never have believed she was capable of so much. The charity's work focuses on providing encouragement and practical support to vulnerable young people.

english_meaning: To convert information, data, or a message into a secret code so unauthorized people cannot read or understand it. To protect information by changing it into coded text using a special method or key. Only authorized people or systems with the correct key can decode and read the original information. Encryption is widely used in computers, mobile phones, banking, messaging apps, and cybersecurity to keep data safe and private.
example_sentence: The company encrypts customer data to protect privacy. Please encrypt the file before sending it by email. Modern messaging apps encrypt conversations for security. The hacker could not read the encrypted information.

english_meaning: The process of converting readable information into a secret coded form to protect it from unauthorized access. A cybersecurity and data protection method in which data, messages, files, or information are transformed into coded text using mathematical algorithms and keys. Only authorized persons or systems with the correct key can read or decrypt the information. Encryption is widely used in mobile phones, banking systems, messaging apps, emails, websites, and computer networks to maintain privacy, confidentiality, and security.
example_sentence: The bank uses encryption to protect customer data. End to end encryption keeps messages private. Strong encryption prevents hackers from reading files. The company added encryption to secure online transactions.

english_meaning: To restrict or burden someone or something in a way that makes movement or progress difficult. To weigh down, hamper, or impede someone with excessive loads, duties, or obligations. To saddle something with debts, claims, or legal obligations that limit its use or transfer. To place obstacles or burdens on something that slow it down or make it less effective.
example_sentence: Heavy equipment encumbered the soldiers during their march through the dense jungle.  The estate was encumbered with significant debts that had to be settled before it could be sold.  Too many regulations can encumber businesses and prevent them from growing.  She felt encumbered by the weight of other people's expectations.  The hikers chose lightweight gear specifically to avoid encumbering themselves on the long trail.

english_meaning: A burden or impediment that restricts movement or freedom. A legal claim, mortgage, or charge on a property. Anything that limits action, progress, or liberty. A person or thing that becomes a hindrance. A liability attached to ownership. An encumbrance is something that weighs down, restricts, or holds back a person, organization, or property, whether in a physical, legal, or financial sense.
example_sentence: The old house was sold with a legal encumbrance attached to it. He considered the heavy luggage an unnecessary encumbrance during the trip. Debt can become a serious encumbrance on a young family. She wished to live a simple life free from any encumbrance. The lawyer ensured the property was free of any encumbrance before purchase.

english_meaning: Things that weigh someone down or restrict movement. Burdens or obstacles that limit freedom or progress. Legal claims, mortgages, or liabilities attached to a property. Items that are inconvenient to carry. Difficulties that hinder action. Encumbrances refer to anything that hampers, burdens, or restricts a person, organization, or property, whether physically, legally, or financially.
example_sentence: He set out on the journey free from all encumbrances. The lawyer checked the property for any legal encumbrances before the sale. Heavy debts proved to be serious encumbrances on the family. She traveled light, avoiding unnecessary encumbrances. The new policy aims to remove bureaucratic encumbrances on small businesses.

english_meaning: A formal letter or document issued by the Pope to all the bishops of the Roman Catholic Church. It is an official statement or communication intended for wide circulation among a specific community. The term describes something that is intended for general or universal distribution. It relates to a circular letter concerning matters of faith, morals, or discipline. A proclamation or address sent to a group of people to provide guidance or clarification on important issues.
example_sentence: The Pope issued a new encyclical addressing the global climate crisis and environmental stewardship. The local bishop read the latest encyclical to the congregation during the Sunday service. Historically, an encyclical serves as a vital tool for teaching Catholic social doctrine to the faithful. The document was distributed as an encyclical to ensure every member of the clergy received the instruction.

english_meaning: A comprehensive reference work containing articles on a wide range of subjects or on numerous aspects of a particular field. A book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically. A work that contains exhaustive knowledge of a single branch of study. A database or digital resource providing deep insight and facts across diverse human knowledge. A vast repository of information designed for research and educational verification.
example_sentence: She consulted the encyclopedia to find information about ancient civilizations. The library houses a twenty-volume encyclopedia of world history. Modern researchers often use digital encyclopedias for quick fact-checking. Writing a comprehensive encyclopedia requires the collaboration of hundreds of experts.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or resembling an encyclopedia in scope. Covering a wide range of subjects or fields of knowledge. Extremely comprehensive or exhaustive in information. Relating to the entirety of human learning. Marked by detailed and vast knowledge across many disciplines.
example_sentence: His encyclopedic knowledge of history amazed everyone at the conference. The professor published an encyclopedic survey of marine life in the Pacific. She has an encyclopedic memory for vintage movie trivia. The library is famous for its encyclopedic collection of ancient manuscripts.

english_meaning: The final part of something. The point at which something stops or ceases to exist. The conclusion or termination of an event, activity, period of time, or object. The furthest or last part of a place or thing. A purpose, goal, or intended result. To bring or come to a finish. The death of a person. End refers to the place, time, or situation in which something stops, finishes, or reaches its limit, and can also mean an aim someone is trying to achieve.
example_sentence: We waited patiently until the end of the film before leaving the cinema. The end of the war brought great relief to the people of the country. He tied a knot at the end of the rope to stop it from fraying. She has worked hard for years to achieve this very end. All good things must come to an end sooner or later.

english_meaning: To finish an activity by doing something specific at the end. To conclude by performing a particular action. To close a discussion or event with a certain step. To finalize something by taking a specific final measure. To reach the end of an action through a particular means.
example_sentence: He ended by thanking everyone in the audience. She ended by reminding us of the deadline. The teacher ended by giving us a short assignment. They ended by singing the national anthem.

english_meaning: To finish in a particular way or with a specific result. To conclude with a certain outcome. To have a specified letter, sound, or word at the end. To reach a certain condition or state at the finish. To close with a specific event or emotion.
example_sentence: Their long argument ended in silence. Most fairy tales end in happiness. Words that end in 'ly' are often adverbs. Their marriage sadly ended in divorce.

english_meaning: To fail completely or come to nothing after effort or planning. When a plan, hope, or effort produces no result or is destroyed.
example_sentence: All his plans to start a business ended in smoke after the market crashed. Their hopes of winning the championship ended in smoke when their best player got injured. The project ended in smoke because of poor management and lack of funding. His efforts to impress the boss ended in smoke when he missed the deadline.

english_meaning: To bring something to a complete finish. To conclude an activity or event fully. To close off something with a final action. To finish neatly by tying up loose ends. To complete a process or performance in the last stage.
example_sentence: They ended off the show with a lively dance. Let us end off this discussion with a summary. She ended off her letter with warm regards. The children ended off the day with a bedtime story.

english_meaning: To finish with a particular note, feeling, or moment. To conclude on a specific tone or point. To close an event or performance with a certain emotion. To reach the final moment with a specific mood. To finalize something in a memorable or particular way.
example_sentence: The film ended on a happy note. Let us end on a positive thought. Her speech ended on a very emotional moment. The meeting ended on a hopeful tone.

english_meaning: In a line, with the ends touching. Describes something that is continuous or arranged so that the end of one part connects directly to the beginning of another, covering the entire length or process without breaks.
synonyms: ["From start to finish","Completely","All the way through","Fully connected"]
example_sentence: They arranged the tables end to end. The road was blocked end to end by traffic. We reviewed the project end to end before submitting it. The cable runs end to end across the bridge. She managed the process end to end without help.

english_meaning: To reach a particular place, situation, or condition, usually unexpectedly. To finally be in a certain state after a series of events. To arrive somewhere or become something without planning. To result in a specific outcome. To finish in a way one did not originally intend.
synonyms: ["Wind up","Finish","Conclude","Result in","Turn out","Land","Come to be","Arrive at"]
example_sentence: We got lost and ended up in a small village. If you keep spending like this, you will end up broke. He ended up as the manager of the company. She ended up living in Canada after her studies.

english_meaning: To finally become something, especially after many changes or events. To reach a certain role, position, or identity in the end. To turn into something as the result of a process or choice. To take on a particular status after a long journey or effort. To finish one's path with a specific title or role.
example_sentence: He ended up as a famous writer after years of struggle. She ended up as the leader of the group. Many students end up as engineers in this city. He ended up as the owner of the very shop where he once worked.

english_meaning: To finally do something that one did not originally plan to do. To be led into an action after a series of events. To do something unexpectedly at the end of a situation. To perform a task or activity as an unintended outcome. To find oneself doing something without planning it.
synonyms: ["Wind up doing","Find oneself doing","Get to doing","Turn to doing"]
example_sentence: I ended up doing all the work myself. We went for a walk and ended up doing some shopping. He ended up doing his homework late at night. She ended up doing a job she never expected to enjoy.

english_meaning: To finally arrive at a certain place or situation, often unintentionally. To reach a location after a series of events or decisions. To land in a specific condition, often unexpected. To be placed somewhere as a final outcome. To come to be in a particular place after wandering, traveling, or choosing.
synonyms: ["Land in","Arrive in","Wind up in","Find oneself in","Get stuck in"]
example_sentence: He ended up in the hospital after the accident. If you break the law, you may end up in jail. We took a wrong turn and ended up in a small town. She ended up in a difficult situation because of her choices.

english_meaning: To finally have or receive something, often unexpectedly. To be left with a particular result, item, or situation. To possess something as the final outcome of an event or process. To gain something at the end of a series of choices or events. To finish holding or owning something, whether desired or not.
synonyms: ["Wind up with","Be left with","Finish with","Result in","Come away with"]
example_sentence: If you keep arguing, you will end up with no friends. She ended up with a huge phone bill last month. He ended up with the best score in the class. They ended up with more money than they expected.

english_meaning: To finish with a particular thing, person, or event. To have something specific as the last part. To close a talk, letter, or performance with a certain item. To conclude by including or featuring something at the end. To finalize with a specific action or word.
example_sentence: The ceremony ended with a beautiful song. She ended her speech with a strong message. The movie ends with an unexpected twist. Let us end with a prayer for peace.

english_meaning: To make someone feel love, affection, or fondness toward a person or thing. To cause someone to feel closer, warmer, or more affectionate toward someone or something. It is often used when a quality, action, or behavior makes a person more likable or lovable.
example_sentence: His kindness will endear him to everyone in the community. Her cheerful nature endears her to her colleagues. The child’s innocent smile endears him to all who meet him. Simple gestures of respect can endear you to others.

english_meaning: To try hard to achieve something; a serious effort. To make a strong and sincere attempt to achieve a goal. A determined and continuous effort toward something important.
example_sentence: She made every endeavor to complete her project on time. They endeavor to improve the quality of education in rural areas. His scientific endeavor led to an important discovery. We should always endeavor to help others in need.

english_meaning: To try hard to achieve something; a serious effort. To make a strong and sincere attempt to achieve a goal. A determined and continuous effort toward something important.
example_sentence: She will endeavour to complete her project on time. They endeavoured to improve the quality of education in rural areas. His endeavour to start a small business was successful. We should always endeavour for excellence in our work.

english_meaning: Native or restricted to a certain place or group. Something that is regularly found or naturally occurring in a particular region, environment, or population. Often used for diseases, species, or social issues that are specific to a location.
example_sentence: Malaria is endemic in some tropical regions. The kangaroo is endemic to Australia. Corruption has become endemic in local politics. Certain plants are endemic to the Himalayan mountains.

english_meaning: A leafy vegetable with crisp, pale leaves and a mildly bitter taste. A salad green eaten raw or braised as a side dish. The plant grown for these tightly packed leaves. A vegetable often used in winter salads.
example_sentence: Endive leaves make excellent salad cups. She braised the endive in butter and stock. Endive tastes slightly bitter but very fresh. The chef served endive with walnuts and cheese.

english_meaning: Having or seeming to have no end or limit. Continuing for a long time without stopping.
example_sentence: The desert stretched out in an endless expanse of golden sand. They had endless discussions about where to go for the summer. The project seemed to involve an endless series of complicated tasks. Her patience with the naughty children was truly endless.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specializes in treating disorders of the endocrine system and hormones. A physician who treats conditions like diabetes, thyroid disorders, and metabolic problems. A specialist in hormone-related diseases and glandular functions.
example_sentence: The endocrinologist manages my diabetes treatment. She consulted an endocrinologist for her thyroid problem. Endocrinologists treat hormonal imbalances. The endocrinologist prescribed insulin for the patient.

english_meaning: To declare one's public approval or support of something or someone. To sign the back of a cheque or bill in order to make it payable to another person or to cash it. To recommend a product, service, or candidate, especially in advertising or politics. To add a note to an official document, such as a driving licence, recording a penalty.
example_sentence: Several famous athletes endorse this brand of sports shoes. The committee unanimously endorsed the new education policy. Please endorse the cheque before depositing it in the bank. The party leader refused to endorse the controversial candidate. His licence was endorsed after the traffic offence.

english_meaning: A medical procedure in which a long, thin, flexible tube with a camera attached is used to examine the interior of a body cavity or organ. The use of an endoscope to visually inspect the gastrointestinal tract, airways, joints, or other internal areas without open surgery. A minimally invasive diagnostic technique used to detect abnormalities, take tissue samples, or carry out minor treatments inside the body.
example_sentence: The doctor ordered an endoscopy to investigate the patient's persistent stomach pain.  During the endoscopy, a small polyp was discovered and immediately removed.  Endoscopy is generally performed under mild sedation and is over within twenty minutes.  Upper endoscopy allows doctors to examine the oesophagus, stomach, and duodenum.  She was relieved to hear that the endoscopy showed no signs of any serious condition.

english_meaning: A process, reaction, or change that absorbs heat energy from its surroundings. Any physical or chemical change that requires energy, usually in the form of heat, to occur. During an endothermic reaction, the surroundings become cooler because heat is taken in by the reacting substance.
example_sentence: The melting of ice is an endothermic process because it absorbs heat from the surroundings. Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction that uses energy from sunlight. The scientist observed an endothermic reaction when the temperature of the mixture decreased. Water evaporation is endothermic since it requires heat energy to change into vapor.

english_meaning: To provide or give someone or something a quality, ability, or gift. To furnish with a talent or resource. To naturally provide someone with a particular quality or feature, or to give a large gift, often of money or property, for a specific purpose. It often implies generosity or natural ability.
example_sentence: She is naturally endowed with a beautiful singing voice. The university was endowed with a large donation for research. He endowed the charity with a generous sum of money. Nature has endowed him with remarkable intelligence.

english_meaning: A gift, donation, or natural ability given to a person or organization. Money, property, or other assets donated to an institution such as a university, mosque, or charity for long term use. It also refers to natural talents or qualities that a person is born with, such as intelligence or artistic ability.
example_sentence: Few people are blessed with her mental endowments. The school has received an endowment of $50,000 to buy new books for the library. There are tests that can establish a baby's genetic endowment. We are trying to set up an endowment to support the library.

english_meaning: To provide someone with a quality or ability. To endow with a gift or trait. To clothe or invest with something. To furnish with a power or attribute. To bestow naturally upon someone.
example_sentence: Nature has endued him with great strength. She was endued with wisdom beyond her years. The leader was endued with courage and vision. He is endued with a remarkable memory.

english_meaning: The ability to withstand hardship, pain, stress, or prolonged effort without giving up. Lasting strength and patience. The power of bearing difficulty over time. Used both for physical stamina in sports or work and for mental and emotional capacity to face challenges.
example_sentence: Marathon running requires great physical endurance. Her endurance during the long illness inspired everyone. Soldiers are trained to build mental and physical endurance. The endurance of the workers in harsh weather was admirable. Success often depends on hard work and endurance.

english_meaning: To experience and deal with something that is painful or unpleasant without giving up. To put up with (something painful or difficult).
example_sentence: They had to endure a long wait before the case came to trial. The pain was almost too great to endure. He cant endure being defeated. I felt that life was no longer endurable.

english_meaning: Having or showing great energy, enthusiasm, and vitality. Full of physical or mental power and the capacity to sustain activity or effort over time. Characterized by vigorous, lively, and forceful activity or expression. Done or carried out with great force, liveliness, and determination.
example_sentence: She was an energetic and enthusiastic teacher who kept her students completely engaged.  The energetic child ran about the playground from morning until evening.  He took an energetic approach to solving the company's long-standing problems.  Regular exercise helps maintain an energetic lifestyle well into old age.  The energetic performance of the dancers brought the entire audience to their feet.

english_meaning: The strength and vitality needed for sustained physical or mental activity. Power obtained from physical or chemical resources to run machines. The ability of a system to do work, as studied in physics. Liveliness and enthusiasm shown in a person's manner.
example_sentence: After a good sleep I felt full of energy. The country is investing in renewable energy. Children seem to have endless energy. She brought great energy to the whole team.

english_meaning: To make someone feel weak, tired, or without energy. To drain strength or vitality.
example_sentence: The long illness enervated him completely. Extreme heat can enervate even the strongest person. A lack of motivation can enervate a whole team. Constant failure had enervated his spirit and confidence.

english_meaning: Lacking energy, strength, or vitality. Weakened physically, mentally, or emotionally. To cause someone to feel drained of power or vigor.
example_sentence: After the long journey in the heat, he felt completely enervated. The team was enervated by the constant defeats. She looked pale and enervated after working all night. The humid weather enervated everyone, making it hard to stay active.

english_meaning: Able to be imposed or carried out by authority or law. Capable of being legally upheld in a court. Describing a rule that can actually be applied in practice. Possible to compel obedience to.
example_sentence: The contract is legally enforceable in both countries. Without witnesses the agreement is not enforceable. They wrote clear and enforceable safety rules. The court found the clause enforceable.

english_meaning: The act of making sure that a law, rule, or obligation is obeyed. The process of compelling observance of something by authority. The officials or agencies responsible for applying the law. The act of imposing something forcefully upon others.
example_sentence: Strict enforcement of traffic rules has reduced accidents. Law enforcement agencies are investigating the case. The new regulations will require careful enforcement. Weak enforcement of the ban made it almost meaningless.

english_meaning: To cut, carve, or mark a design, letters, or pattern on a hard surface. It can also mean to fix something deeply in memory. To carve or cut words, images, or designs into materials like metal, wood, or stone. To impress something deeply into the mind so it is not easily forgotten. To prepare a design on a surface for printing or decoration.
example_sentence: The jeweler engraved her name on the ring. The artist engraved a beautiful pattern on the wooden box. His teacher’s advice was engraved in his mind forever. The monument was engraved with the names of the heroes.

english_meaning: To occupy the mind or attention completely. To absorb or consume someone's interest or time. In legal terms, it can mean to formalize a document in large, clear writing.
example_sentence: The captivating novel seemed to engross her for the entire afternoon. The complex puzzle will engross the children for hours. He was so engrossed in his work that he didn't hear the bell. The lawyer had to engross the final deed before the signing ceremony.

english_meaning: To sweep over something so as to surround or cover it completely. To swallow up or submerge. It can also refer to being overwhelmed by a feeling or situation.
example_sentence: The massive waves threatened to engulf the tiny fishing boat. Dark clouds began to engulf the mountain peak as the storm approached. A feeling of profound sadness began to engulf him after the loss. The fire quickly spread to engulf the entire warehouse within minutes.

english_meaning: To improve something by making it better, stronger, more attractive, or more valuable. To increase the quality, value, beauty, effectiveness, or strength of something. It is used when something is made better than its original state. To make something look better or more attractive. To make an activity more enjoyable or valuable.
example_sentence: The new lighting will enhance the beauty of the room. Regular practice can enhance your communication skills. This software update enhances the overall performance of the system. Adding spices can enhance the flavor of the dish.

english_meaning: Improved, increased, or made better in quality or value. Made more attractive, powerful, or effective. Strengthened or upgraded in some way. Having added features or improvements.
example_sentence: The phone comes with enhanced security features. Her enhanced skills helped her get promoted. The photo looks amazing after enhanced editing. The team delivered enhanced performance this season.

english_meaning: An improvement or addition that increases quality, value, or effectiveness. The process of making something better or more attractive. An increase in strength, level, or amount. A feature added to improve performance or appearance.
example_sentence: The new software includes several performance enhancements. This training will lead to significant skill enhancement. The enhancement of security measures has reassured residents. Photo enhancement tools have become very advanced.

english_meaning: A person or thing that improves the quality, value, or attractiveness of something. A substance or feature that increases the effect or performance of another. A tool or product that adds strength or appeal.
example_sentence: This spice acts as a natural flavor enhancer. The new update includes a performance enhancer. She uses a color enhancer to brighten her photos. Music can be an enhancer of mood and creativity.

english_meaning: Something mysterious or difficult to understand. A person, thing, or situation that is puzzling, confusing, or hard to explain. It can refer to something that hides its true nature or meaning.
example_sentence: Her behavior remains an enigma to everyone around her. The ancient structure is an enigma that historians still study. He is an enigma, never revealing his true thoughts. The disappearance of the plane is still an enigma.

english_meaning: Mysterious and difficult to understand. Cryptic in nature, hard to interpret, ambiguous or unclear, full of hidden meaning. Something or someone that is puzzling, mysterious, or not easy to explain. It is often used for people, expressions, statements, or situations that hide their true meaning.
example_sentence: Her smile was enigmatic, making everyone curious about her thoughts. The artist is known for his enigmatic paintings that invite many interpretations. He gave an enigmatic reply instead of a clear answer. The old letter contained an enigmatic message that no one could decode.

english_meaning: In a mysterious or puzzling manner. In a way that is difficult to understand or interpret. In a manner that seems hidden or secretive. With an air of mystery.
example_sentence: She smiled enigmatically when asked about her plans. The old man spoke enigmatically about his past. He answered the question enigmatically, leaving everyone confused. The message ended enigmatically without any explanation.

english_meaning: To continue a sentence without pause beyond the end of a line in poetry. The fact of a sentence continuing beyond the end of a line of poetry without a break
example_sentence: The poet chose to enjamb the verse to create suspense. In her sonnet, every line is carefully enjambed to maintain flow. The imagery in the poem is strengthened by enjambment between lines. Without enjamb, the poem might feel choppy and disconnected.

english_meaning: A poetic technique where a sentence or clause continues from one line to the next without a pause or punctuation. A literary device used mainly in poetry. It happens when a line breaks before the sentence or phrase is finished, and the thought continues onto the next line. This creates a smooth flow, builds suspense, and keeps the reader moving forward.
example_sentence: Enjambment allows the idea to continue without a pause at the end of the line. The use of enjambment makes the poem feel more natural and less rigid. Many modern poets prefer enjambment over strict line endings. By using enjambment, the poet connects thoughts across multiple lines.

english_meaning: To order or instruct someone to do something with authority. To urge or strongly advise a particular action. To prohibit someone from doing something by a legal order or injunction. To impose a duty or rule of behavior. To command formally and seriously.
example_sentence: The doctor enjoined him to rest for at least a week. The court enjoined the company from selling the product. Religious teachings enjoin kindness to parents. She was enjoined to keep the matter strictly confidential.

english_meaning: To impose a duty, rule, or course of action on someone. To press something firmly upon a person as an obligation. To make something binding on someone by command. To emphasize a principle strongly to someone. To charge someone with a responsibility.
example_sentence: The coach enjoined discipline on every player. Our parents enjoined honesty on us from childhood. The rules enjoin silence on all visitors to the library. The manager enjoined strict punctuality on the new staff.

english_meaning: To take pleasure in looking at something. To find visual delight in a scene or view. To appreciate something visually. To feel happy while observing something beautiful. To relish watching a particular thing.
example_sentence: We enjoyed the sight of the birds flying over the lake. He enjoys the sight of children playing in the park. Tourists enjoy the sight of the sunset from the hilltop. She enjoyed the sight of her garden in full bloom.

english_meaning: To make or become bigger in size or amount. To expand the scope of something. To describe something in greater detail. To increase the capacity or importance of something. To reproduce a photograph on a larger scale.
example_sentence: They plan to enlarge the school building next year. He asked her to enlarge on her previous statement. We can enlarge the picture for better viewing. Reading widely helps enlarge one's understanding of the world.

english_meaning: The act of making something bigger in size or amount. A photographic print that is larger than the negative. An extension or expansion of something. An increase in scope, importance, or range. Growth in physical size of a body part or organ.
example_sentence: The enlargement of the photograph shows great detail. The company announced the enlargement of its office. Doctors noticed the enlargement of his liver. The enlargement of the park pleased local residents.

english_meaning: To give someone greater knowledge or understanding about a subject or situation. To inform. To explain. To free someone from ignorance, prejudice, or false belief. To give spiritual insight. Used both for sharing information that clarifies something and for the deeper sense of gaining wisdom or spiritual awareness.
example_sentence: Can you enlighten me about the new company policy? The teacher tried to enlighten the students on the importance of honesty. His lecture enlightened the audience on environmental issues. She wrote the book to enlighten people about mental health. Travel can enlighten one's view of the world.

english_meaning: To make something more interesting, lively, or exciting. To add energy, vitality, or animation to a situation, conversation, or environment. To bring new life or spirit to something that has become dull, flat, or monotonous. To stimulate or inspire someone or something to become more active or cheerful.
example_sentence: A few fresh flowers can enliven even the dullest office environment.  The arrival of the comedian's act helped to enliven what had been a rather flat event.  Music has an extraordinary power to enliven the spirit and lift the mood.  She tried to enliven the conversation by introducing a topic everyone had an opinion on.  The sudden burst of sunshine seemed to enliven everyone on the morning walk.

english_meaning: To give someone a noble title or rank, raising them to the peerage. To make something more dignified, honorable, or morally elevated. To enhance the quality or character of something so that it becomes more worthy of respect. To uplift or elevate someone's moral standing or improve the dignity of a situation or object.
example_sentence: The king chose to ennoble the general in recognition of his courage during the war.  Great art has the power to ennoble the human spirit.  Her act of selfless sacrifice did more to ennoble her in the eyes of the public than any award could.  Literature can ennoble the mind by exposing it to the full complexity of human experience.  The architect sought to ennoble the space by filling it with light and natural materials.

english_meaning: A feeling of boredom, weariness, dissatisfaction, or lack of interest caused by having nothing exciting, meaningful, or stimulating to do. A deep feeling of boredom and dissatisfaction. It is more than ordinary boredom. It often describes a state in which a person feels mentally tired, uninterested, unfulfilled, or emotionally drained because life seems repetitive, meaningless, or lacking excitement.
example_sentence: After months of doing the same job, he was overcome with ennui. The quiet town filled her with a sense of ennui. Reading new books helped him escape his ennui. Despite his success, he often felt ennui and dissatisfaction.

english_meaning: An intense fear of crowds or densely populated places. A person with enochlophobia feels extreme anxiety, panic, or discomfort when surrounded by large groups of people.
example_sentence: Her enochlophobia made it impossible to attend concerts. He experienced panic attacks due to enochlophobia at the market. Enochlophobia became worse for many people after the pandemic. She avoided shopping malls because of her enochlophobia.

english_meaning: Extremely large in size, amount, or degree. Something that is much bigger, greater, or more powerful than usual.
example_sentence: The elephant is an enormous animal. She made an enormous effort to finish her project on time. The company has made enormous progress this year. The flood caused enormous damage to the village.

english_meaning: To make someone extremely angry or furious. To cause great anger or irritation. To make feel very angry, often because of unfairness, insult, or provocation.
example_sentence: The unfair decision enraged the players. His rude behavior enraged everyone at the meeting. The delay in justice enraged the citizens. She was enraged when she found out the truth.

english_meaning: To improve the quality, value, or character of something by adding to it. To make someone wealthy or wealthier, especially through profit or the acquisition of resources. To add nutrients, minerals, or vitamins to food to make it more nourishing. To enhance the depth and meaning of an experience, relationship, or piece of work.
example_sentence: Travelling widely has greatly enriched her understanding of different cultures.  The new teaching methods were designed to enrich the learning experience for all students.  The company was accused of enriching its shareholders at the expense of its workers.  Flour is often enriched with vitamins and iron during the milling process.  Reading literature can deeply enrich a person's emotional intelligence and vocabulary.

english_meaning: To cover something or someone completely, usually with a layer of material. To dress, wrap, or coat something so it is fully covered. Often used for food items coated in chocolate or icing, or for someone being dressed in a robe or garment.
example_sentence: I dreamed that one day she would be enrobed in satins and silks. The chef enrobed the strawberries in melted chocolate. The statue was enrobed in a protective layer before transport. She was enrobed in a soft white robe after the ceremony. The dessert was enrobed with a glossy sugar glaze.

english_meaning: To settle oneself firmly and comfortably in a place. To establish someone securely in a position or role. To place or hide something safely, often in a concealed location.
example_sentence: He ensconced himself in his favourite armchair with a book. The cat ensconced itself comfortably on the warm windowsill. The treasure was ensconced deep within the castle walls. She was soon ensconced as the head of the department.

english_meaning: A group of items viewed as a whole, especially a set of clothes worn together as a coordinated outfit. A group of musicians, actors, or dancers who perform together. A piece of music or a scene performed by a group rather than a soloist. In physics and statistics, a collection of possible states of a system.
example_sentence: She wore a stylish ensemble of a matching skirt and jacket. The theatre group performed as a tight ensemble cast. The orchestra's ensemble playing impressed the audience. Physicists use the term ensemble to describe a set of possible system states.

english_meaning: To preserve something as sacred, honored, or permanent. To place an important principle, right, or person in a position of lasting respect or protection.
example_sentence: The constitution enshrines freedom of speech. The memorial enshrines the memory of the victims. The museum enshrines the nation’s artistic heritage. These principles are enshrined in international law.

english_meaning: To cover, envelop, or conceal something completely, as if with a shroud. To obscure something from view or from understanding. To surround with mystery or secrecy.
example_sentence: Thick fog enshrouded the entire valley by morning. Mystery enshrouded the ancient ruins for centuries. Smoke from the fire enshrouded the city skyline. Grief enshrouded the family after the sudden loss.

english_meaning: A flag, especially a national flag flown by ships to show their nationality. A badge, symbol, or sign of rank, authority, or office. The lowest commissioned rank of officer in the United States Navy or Coast Guard. A symbol or emblem representing a person's position, allegiance, or identity.
example_sentence: The ship sailed proudly under its national ensign as it entered the harbor.  The ensign was raised at dawn and lowered at dusk according to naval tradition.  He was commissioned as an ensign shortly after graduating from the naval academy.  The ensign of the ancient house was displayed above the main gate of the castle.  Each regiment carried its own ensign as a symbol of its identity and honor.

english_meaning: To make someone a slave. To take away a person's freedom and force them to work or obey. To control someone completely. To make someone dependent on a habit, desire, system, or power.
example_sentence: The invaders tried to enslave the defeated population. Debt can enslave families for generations. No society has the right to enslave another people. Addiction may enslave a person slowly and silently.

english_meaning: The act of making a person a slave. The condition of being held in slavery, bondage, or forced servitude. Complete domination or loss of freedom under a person, system, habit, or powerful influence.
example_sentence: The historical legacy of enslavement continues to affect social structures today. Many people suffer from enslavement to their own destructive habits. The abolitionist movement fought tirelessly against the systemic enslavement of people. Economic debt can often lead to a form of modern-day enslavement.

english_meaning: To catch in or as if in a trap. To involve someone in a difficult situation. To entangle or entice into wrongdoing. To capture through cunning. To draw into a snare or trick.
example_sentence: The hunter used a net to ensnare the birds. She was ensnared by his false promises. The gang tried to ensnare young people in crime. Debt can easily ensnare unsuspecting borrowers.

english_meaning: To happen or occur afterwards as a result of something. To follow as a consequence of an earlier action or event. To take place in an orderly sequence after something else. To come next in time or order.
example_sentence: A heated argument ensued after the announcement. If the rules are ignored, chaos will ensue. Silence ensued when the teacher entered the room. A long legal battle ensued between the two companies.

english_meaning: Happening or coming afterwards as a result of something. Following immediately in time or order. Occurring as a consequence of an earlier event. The present participle of the verb 'ensue', meaning to follow or result.
example_sentence: In the ensuing weeks, the city slowly returned to normal. The argument and the ensuing silence made everyone uncomfortable. Many people were injured in the ensuing panic. The ensuing debate lasted for several hours.

english_meaning: To make certain that something happens or is done. To take necessary steps or actions to guarantee a specific outcome or result. It implies responsibility for confirming that something occurs as intended.
example_sentence: Please ensure that the door is locked before leaving. The manager ensured all staff received proper training. To ensure success, we must plan carefully. They ensured the safety of all passengers during the journey.

english_meaning: In classical architecture, the horizontal band resting on top of columns and consisting of three main parts: the architrave, the frieze, and the cornice. The upper section of a classical building above the columns, typically decorated with carvings, inscriptions, or ornamental details. A structural and decorative element in ancient Greek and Roman architecture that defined the style and proportion of a building. A term referring specifically to the complete horizontal superstructure supported by columns in classical architectural design.
example_sentence: The temple's entablature was decorated with intricate carvings depicting scenes from mythology.  Students of classical architecture study the proportions of the entablature in detail.  The museum's facade featured a beautifully restored entablature above its six Doric columns.  Each order of Greek architecture, whether Doric, Ionic, or Corinthian, has its own distinctive entablature.  The entablature of the ancient building had survived remarkably intact despite centuries of exposure.

english_meaning: To involve something as a necessary or inevitable part or consequence. To impose, involve, or imply as a necessary accompaniment or result.
example_sentence: The project will entail considerable expense and effort. A leadership position entails a great deal of responsibility. His decision to move abroad would entail leaving his friends and family behind. What does the new job actually entail? The journey entailed a long and tiring bus ride through the mountains.

english_meaning: To twist together, trap, or involve someone or something in a complicated or difficult situation. To twist or catch in something such as a net, rope, or hair so that it cannot move freely. To involve someone in a complicated or troublesome situation. To mix things together in a confusing or complex way. To trap emotionally or socially in a difficult relationship or issue.
example_sentence: The fishing net entangled the turtle in the water. He did not want to entangle himself in their family dispute. The long wires became entangled behind the computer desk. She was entangled in a complicated legal case.

english_meaning: The action of being twisted or caught in something. A complicated or compromised relationship or situation. In physics, it refers to the quantum state of particles being linked together regardless of distance.
example_sentence: The bird struggled to escape its entanglement in the discarded fishing net. He found himself in a messy romantic entanglement that he couldn't resolve. The diplomat worked hard to avoid any political entanglement with the warring nations. Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon that challenges our understanding of space.

english_meaning: The complete realization of something potential. The state in which something fully achieves its purpose, nature, or potential. It is the condition of being complete or fully developed, not just having the ability but actually realizing it.
example_sentence: The mature oak tree is the entelechy of the acorn. Education helps a person reach the entelechy of their abilities. The artist believed his final painting represented his creative entelechy. In philosophy, entelechy explains how potential becomes actual reality.

english_meaning: An informal alliance or understanding between states or factions. A friendly understanding or agreement between parties. Often used in historical contexts regarding European diplomacy.
example_sentence: The two neighboring countries signed an entente to ensure regional peace. The diplomatic entente helped prevent the outbreak of a major conflict. There was a growing entente between the two rival political parties. Historians often discuss the 1904 Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.

english_meaning: To come or go into a place. To gain admission to or become a member of an organization, profession, competition, or activity. To put names, details, or data into a record, list, computer, or form. To begin or move into a particular state, period, agreement, or situation. To submit something for consideration in a competition. To appear formally in a legal record, as a plea or judgment.
example_sentence: Please enter the room quietly. She entered the competition with a short story. Enter your name and email address on the form. The country entered a period of rapid economic growth.

english_meaning: To officially become valid and legally binding. To begin to apply, especially in the case of a treaty or international agreement. To take effect from an agreed date after ratification. To start operating as a legal instrument. To become enforceable on all parties involved.
synonyms: ["Take effect","Become binding","Become operative","Be ratified","Come into effect","Commence"]
example_sentence: The treaty will enter into force once ten countries ratify it. The agreement entered into force last summer. New safety standards enter into force in March. The protocol entered into force without further delay.

english_meaning: To begin an activity, course, stage, or period. To start carrying out duties or occupying an office. To take possession of property or formally assume a right. To record information in a book, form, or system, in less common usage.
example_sentence: She is ready to enter on a new phase of her career. The minister will enter on his duties next Monday. After the legal transfer, the buyer may enter on the property. The clerk entered the payment on the official record.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove a part of the intestine. A procedure performed for blockage, injury, tumour, or dead bowel tissue. The excision of a damaged segment of the small intestine. An operation usually followed by joining the healthy ends of the bowel.
example_sentence: An emergency enterectomy saved the patient's life. The damaged bowel was removed during the enterectomy. After the enterectomy, the healthy ends were joined together. Nutrition must be monitored carefully following an enterectomy.

english_meaning: A business or company, especially one involving initiative or risk. A planned project or undertaking, often difficult or important. The ability and willingness to begin new ventures with energy and resourcefulness. Purposeful activity or industrious effort.
example_sentence: She built a successful farming enterprise from a small plot. The research project was a difficult but rewarding enterprise. His energy and enterprise impressed the investors. The family enterprise now employs more than fifty people.

english_meaning: Businesses or companies, especially those involving initiative and risk. Planned projects or undertakings that require effort. Activities showing energy, resourcefulness, and a willingness to take action. The plural form of enterprise.
example_sentence: Small enterprises provide many jobs in the region. The charity supports local social enterprises. Both scientific enterprises required years of careful research. Her family owns several agricultural enterprises.

english_meaning: A measure of the total heat content of a thermodynamic system. The sum of the internal energy and the product of pressure and volume of a system. A quantity used in thermodynamics to describe heat changes during a process. The energy released or absorbed during a chemical reaction at constant pressure.
example_sentence: The change in enthalpy is an important factor in chemical reactions. Scientists measured the enthalpy of the system at constant pressure. Negative enthalpy indicates an exothermic reaction. The enthalpy of vaporization of water is relatively high. Students learned how to calculate enthalpy changes in the lab.

english_meaning: To capture the fascinated attention of someone. To hold someone spellbound or enchanted. It implies a sense of being enslaved by beauty or charm.
example_sentence: The magician's performance was enough to enthral the entire audience. She was enthralled by the breathtaking beauty of the Himalayan landscape. The ancient myths continue to enthral readers of all ages. His storytelling abilities could enthral anyone who sat by the campfire.

english_meaning: To capture the fascinated attention or interest of someone. To hold someone spellbound or to enslave mentally. It implies a state of being completely charmed or captivated by something beautiful or intense.
example_sentence: The circus performer's daring acts never fail to enthrall the young audience. She was completely enthralled by the vivid colors and intricate details of the painting. The speaker's eloquent words managed to enthrall every person in the crowded hall. The magical atmosphere of the ancient forest can enthrall any traveler.

english_meaning: The state of being completely captivated or fascinated by someone or something. The condition of being held spellbound or deeply absorbed, typically by something of great beauty, interest, or power. Historical reference to the condition of being enslaved or held in bondage. The act of capturing and holding someone's complete attention and admiration.
example_sentence: The audience sat in a state of complete enthrallment throughout the extraordinary performance.  Her enthrallment with ancient history began when she first visited Rome as a teenager.  The novel held its readers in enthrallment from the very first page to the last.  His enthrallment with the mysteries of the deep sea drove his entire career as a marine biologist.  The exhibit on ancient Egypt produced a sense of enthrallment in visitors of all ages.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of active interest, excitement, or eagerness about something that you like or enjoy. Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval. The energy and willingness with which a person approaches a task, idea, or activity. A subject or activity that arouses such interest.
example_sentence: The students greeted the new teacher with great enthusiasm. He talked about his project with so much enthusiasm that everyone wanted to join. Her enthusiasm for music began when she was only six years old. The audience cheered the players with unmatched enthusiasm. Despite many failures, he never lost his enthusiasm for learning.

english_meaning: A person who is highly interested in a particular activity or subject. Someone who pursues an interest with strong excitement and enjoyment. An eager admirer or supporter of something.
example_sentence: He is a photography enthusiast who travels widely. Car enthusiasts gathered for the annual show. As a history enthusiast, she visits many museums. The club welcomes beginners as well as experienced enthusiasts.

english_meaning: Very excited and interested. Feeling or showing strong excitement, interest, or eagerness about something.
example_sentence: She is enthusiastic about learning new languages. The students were enthusiastic during the science fair. He gave an enthusiastic response to the new project. They felt enthusiastic before starting the match.

english_meaning: With great excitement, energy, and eagerness. Marked by or showing great enthusiasm. This describes performing an action with a lively and cheerful spirit, often involving vigorous and passionate expression. It implies a wholehearted and unreserved engagement in an activity, stemming from a strong feeling of interest and enjoyment.
example_sentence: She enthusiastically accepted the job offer. The crowd cheered enthusiastically for the home team. He talked enthusiastically about his new project. They participated enthusiastically in the discussion. The children enthusiastically opened their presents.

english_meaning: To attract or tempt by offering pleasure or advantage. To lure someone into a specific action or place by making it seem appealing. This involves persuading someone to do something, often by offering a reward or creating a sense of desire. The act of enticing can sometimes have a negative connotation, suggesting deception or leading someone into a trap, but it can also be neutral.
example_sentence: The smell of freshly baked cookies will entice anyone. They tried to entice the kitten down from the tree with a piece of fish. The advertisement was designed to entice customers to buy the new phone. He was enticed by the promise of a large salary. She could not be enticed to join the risky venture.

english_meaning: To give someone the right to have or do something. To qualify a person officially for a benefit, service, or claim. To give a title or name to a book, film, or piece of work. To give a person a rank or honourable title.
example_sentence: This ticket entitles you to free entry for one day. Full-time employees are entitled to paid annual leave. He entitled his first novel The Long Road Home. The king entitled him a lord for his loyal service.

english_meaning: To give someone the right to have or do something. To qualify a person for a benefit, reward, or privilege. To make someone legally or morally deserving of something. To authorize someone to claim or receive something. To allow someone a particular opportunity or treatment.
example_sentence: This ticket entitles you to free entry to the museum. Every citizen is entitled to a fair trial. Full-time staff are entitled to thirty days of annual leave. Membership entitles you to a ten percent discount.

english_meaning: Having the official right to receive or do something. Believing that one deserves special privileges or better treatment than others. Given a particular title or name, as of a book or film. Formally granted a rank, honour, or claim.
example_sentence: You are entitled to a full refund within thirty days. Only registered voters are entitled to take part. He behaves like a spoilt and entitled child. She read a poem entitled Hope in the Morning.

english_meaning: The legal or moral right to receive or do something. An amount or benefit that a person is officially allowed to have. The belief that one deserves special treatment or privileges. A government payment or service that citizens have a right to claim.
example_sentence: Every worker has a holiday entitlement of twenty days. She checked her pension entitlement before retiring. His sense of entitlement annoyed his colleagues. The government reduced spending on welfare entitlements.

english_meaning: A thing with distinct and independent existence. Something that exists as a particular and discrete unit. This term can refer to a living being, an inanimate object, a concept, a business, or a legal organization. It emphasizes the separateness and self-contained nature of the thing in question, whether it is physical or abstract.
example_sentence: The company is a separate legal entity from its owners. A ghost is considered a supernatural entity. Each person is a unique entity. The university is a large and complex entity. A new political entity was formed after the revolution.

english_meaning: To place a dead body in a tomb or grave. To bury someone or something completely under earth, snow, or rubble. To trap or enclose something so that it cannot escape or be seen. To preserve or hide something as if buried away.
example_sentence: The pharaoh was entombed with gold and precious jewels. Two climbers were entombed by the sudden avalanche. The old village lies entombed beneath the reservoir. His memories remained entombed in silence for years.

english_meaning: Relating to the scientific study of insects. Concerning insects, their classification, and their behaviour. Connected with research, collections, or societies devoted to insects. Used to describe methods or evidence based on the study of insects.
example_sentence: The museum has a large entomological collection. She published an entomological study of desert beetles. Entomological evidence helped the police fix the time of death. He attended an entomological conference in Germany.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the study of insects. From the point of view of insect science. Using methods or knowledge drawn from entomology. In terms of insects and their classification or behaviour.
example_sentence: Entomologically speaking, this specimen is extremely rare. The site was examined entomologically by two experts. The samples were entomologically identified as house flies. Entomologically, the region is still poorly explored.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies insects. An expert in the classification, biology, and behaviour of insects. A specialist who identifies insects for research, agriculture, or criminal investigations. A person who collects and examines insect specimens.
example_sentence: The entomologist spent years studying honeybee colonies. A forensic entomologist helped solve the murder case. She became an entomologist after visiting a butterfly farm. Entomologists warn that insect numbers are falling fast.

english_meaning: The branch of zoology that deals with the scientific study of insects. The study of insect life, structure, classification, and behaviour. A field of science applied in agriculture, medicine, and forensic investigation. Knowledge concerning insects as a group of animals.
example_sentence: He studied entomology at an agricultural university. Forensic entomology can help estimate the time of death. Her interest in entomology began with a book about ants. Modern entomology relies heavily on genetic analysis.

english_meaning: Attraction or love for insects. The interest, fondness, or attraction that a person or organism shows toward insects. In biology, it can also describe pollination that occurs through insects.
example_sentence: His entomophilia led him to collect rare butterflies. Entomophilia plays a crucial role in the pollination of many flowers. The museum had a section dedicated to people with entomophilia. She showed entomophilia by studying ants in her backyard.

english_meaning: Fear of insects. An intense, irrational, and persistent fear of insects. It can cause anxiety, avoidance behavior, and distress when a person encounters or even thinks about insects.
example_sentence: Her entomophobia made it impossible for her to visit the garden. He screamed when a butterfly landed near him, showing his entomophobia. Entomophobia can affect daily life if it prevents someone from going outside. Therapy helped him reduce his entomophobia over time.

english_meaning: A group of people who travel with and attend to an important person. The assistants, advisers, and followers who surround a famous figure. A circle of companions who accompany someone in public. The people or surroundings closely associated with a person.
example_sentence: The singer arrived with a large entourage of assistants. His entourage waited outside the conference hall. The president travelled with an entourage of security officers. She dislikes moving anywhere with a noisy entourage.

english_meaning: An opening, such as a door, passage, or gate, that allows access to a place. The action of entering somewhere. It can refer to the physical point of entry or the right to enter. In a broader sense, it can also mean the act of becoming a member of or being admitted into a group, society, or profession.
example_sentence: He stood at the entrance of the cave. She was denied entrance to the club. The grand entrance to the palace was guarded by soldiers. His entrance into the room was barely noticed. The application for entrance to the university must be submitted by Friday.

english_meaning: To catch someone or something in a trap. To trick someone into a difficult or illegal situation, often by deception. To lure into a position from which escape is difficult.
example_sentence: The hunters used nets to entrap the birds. The undercover agent tried to entrap him into selling stolen goods. She felt entrapped in a loveless marriage. The scheme was designed to entrap innocent investors.

english_meaning: The act of entrapping or the state of being entrapped. In law, the action of tricking someone into committing a crime so that they can be prosecuted. A situation in which someone is caught or confined against their will.
example_sentence: The court dismissed the case, ruling it was entrapment. He claimed police entrapment and refused to accept guilt. The narrow cave became a deadly entrapment for the climbers. Entrapment by false promises ruined many families.

english_meaning: To ask someone earnestly and anxiously to do something. To make an urgent, heartfelt request or plea. To beg with politeness and deep feeling.
example_sentence: She entreated her brother to stay a little longer. The villagers entreated the soldiers to spare their homes. He entreated them to believe his story. "Help us," the refugees entreated the border guards.

english_meaning: An earnest or humble request; a plea. A serious appeal made with deep feeling. An act of begging or pleading for help or favor.
example_sentence: She ignored his tearful entreaties to stay. The prisoner's entreaty for mercy moved the court. At his mother's entreaty, he agreed to visit home. The letter was a desperate entreaty for help.

english_meaning: To firmly establish something so it is difficult to change. To set ideas, habits, power, or positions deeply so they become fixed and resistant to change. It is also used for digging or protecting a position, especially in military contexts.
example_sentence: Corruption became deeply entrenched in the political system. These traditions are entrenched in local culture. The army entrenched its forces along the border. Old habits can become entrenched over time.

english_meaning: The act of digging trenches for defense. The process by which an attitude, habit, or system becomes firmly established and difficult to change. Something that protects or strengthens a position.
example_sentence: The entrenchment of old habits makes reform difficult. Winter brought the entrenchment of troops along the border. The entrenchment of corruption weakened the institutions. Continuous conflict led to the entrenchment of both sides.

english_meaning: A person who sets up and runs a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of making a profit. Someone who identifies opportunities and organises resources to exploit them.
example_sentence: The young entrepreneur launched a successful tech startup at age twenty. She became an entrepreneur after years of working for others. The entrepreneur raised capital from investors to expand her business. Many successful entrepreneurs failed multiple times before succeeding.

english_meaning: Having the qualities or mindset of an entrepreneur; relating to the activity of setting up businesses and taking financial risks to achieve success.
example_sentence: She had an entrepreneurial spirit from a very young age. His entrepreneurial approach transformed the failing company. The entrepreneurial culture of the city attracted many investors. An entrepreneurial mindset is valuable even in traditional jobs.

english_meaning: The activity of setting up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit. The capacity and willingness to develop, organise and manage a business venture.
example_sentence: Entrepreneurship requires courage, creativity, and hard work. The university introduced a course on entrepreneurship for students. Entrepreneurship drives economic growth and job creation. She chose entrepreneurship over a stable government job.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving entropy; tending toward disorder, randomness, and the degradation of energy in a system.
example_sentence: The universe follows an entropic path toward greater disorder. Entropic decay is visible in aging buildings and infrastructure. The entropic nature of the process made it impossible to reverse. Scientists study entropic behaviour in thermodynamic systems.

english_meaning: In a manner relating to entropy. In a way that tends toward disorder, randomness, or degradation of energy.
example_sentence: The system behaved entropically, gradually losing its structure. Energy in the universe flows entropically towards disorder. The organisation declined entropically over decades of neglect. Without maintenance, machines deteriorate entropically.

english_meaning: A thermodynamic quantity representing the degree of disorder or randomness in a system. In general use, it refers to the gradual decline into disorder or chaos.
example_sentence: Entropy always increases in an isolated system according to the second law of thermodynamics. The entropy of the universe is constantly growing. Social entropy increased as the government lost control. The entropy of the old machine made it unreliable.

english_meaning: To give someone the responsibility of doing something or taking care of something. To place trust in a person by handing over an important task or item. To assign a duty to someone with confidence. To commit something to another's care.
example_sentence: They entrusted the project to the most experienced engineer. She entrusted her savings to her elder brother. The family entrusted the child to a kind nanny. He was entrusted with the safety of the entire team.

english_meaning: To give someone the responsibility for a task, duty, or thing. To place something valuable in someone's care because you trust them. To assign an important job to a reliable person. To hand over authority or control to someone. To confide a secret or private matter to someone.
example_sentence: She was entrusted with the keys to the office. The board entrusted him with managing the new branch. I entrusted my neighbor with the care of my plants. He entrusted his closest friend with the family secret.

english_meaning: To mention a number of things one by one. To establish the number of something or to list items individually. It is often used in formal contexts to provide a detailed account or count of objects or reasons.
example_sentence: The document serves to enumerate all the rights guaranteed to the citizens. She began to enumerate the many reasons why the project had failed. The census taker must enumerate every person living in the household. He paused to enumerate the various species of birds he had observed.

english_meaning: The action of mentioning a number of things one by one. A complete, ordered listing of all the items in a collection. This term refers to the process of counting or listing items systematically. It is often used in formal, mathematical, or computational contexts to ensure that all elements of a set are accounted for without omission or repetition.
example_sentence: The book begins with an enumeration of the author's many accomplishments. The census is a systematic enumeration of the country's population. His long enumeration of grievances bored everyone. The enumeration of their duties took over an hour. An enumeration of the system's features was provided in the manual.

english_meaning: A person who counts or lists things systematically. Someone responsible for collecting information by counting, listing, or recording items, people, or data, often used in surveys, censuses, or data collection processes.
example_sentence: The enumerator visited every house in the village to collect population data. During the census, enumerators recorded information about each household. She worked as an enumerator for the national survey last year. The enumerator carefully listed all the books in the library.

english_meaning: To pronounce words clearly and distinctly. To state something formally, clearly, or precisely. To express a theory or idea in a definite way. To announce or proclaim publicly. To articulate thoughts with clarity.
example_sentence: Teachers should enunciate every word clearly. He enunciated his views on the reforms. The leader enunciated a new policy of tolerance. Please enunciate so the audience can understand.

english_meaning: The clear pronunciation of words when speaking. The way in which sounds and syllables are articulated. A clear and formal statement of an idea, theory, or principle. The act of expressing something in precise words. Public declaration or announcement of something.
