example_sentence: Her enunciation was so clear that everyone understood her easily. Actors practise enunciation before going on stage. The document offers a careful enunciation of the party's principles. Poor enunciation made his speech difficult to follow.

english_meaning: To wrap up, cover, or surround something completely. To hide or obscure something by surrounding it. To surround an enemy force on all sides in military tactics.
example_sentence: Thick fog began to envelop the valley. She let the warm blanket envelop her completely. Flames quickly enveloped the entire building. A sense of calm enveloped the room after the music stopped.

english_meaning: A flat paper container used for sending a letter or document. Any covering or outer layer that encloses something. The outer structure of an aircraft, balloon, or spacecraft. The limits of what is possible, as in 'pushing the envelope'.
example_sentence: Please seal the envelope before posting it. He found an old envelope full of family photographs. The balloon's envelope was made of strong nylon. Their new design really pushes the envelope.

english_meaning: Feeling or showing jealousy of someone's advantages or possessions. Wanting what another person has. Resentful of another's success or good fortune.
example_sentence: She was envious of her sister's success. He gave an envious look at his neighbor's new car. They were envious of his luxurious lifestyle. The envious colleagues tried to undermine her work.

english_meaning: In a way that shows envy or jealousy. With a feeling of wanting what others have. In a resentful manner toward another's success.
example_sentence: She looked enviously at her friend's new dress. He spoke enviously about his brother's wealth. They watched enviously as the winners received their prizes. The child stared enviously at the other boy's toys.

english_meaning: The natural world around us, including air, water, and land. The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives. The conditions that influence growth and development. The setting or context of an activity.
example_sentence: We must protect the environment for future generations. Pollution is damaging the environment badly. Children need a safe learning environment. The company created a friendly work environment.

english_meaning: Relating to the natural world and the impact of human activity on it. Connected with the protection of nature. Concerned with the surroundings or conditions of life.
example_sentence: Environmental pollution is a global problem. The government introduced new environmental laws. She studies environmental science at university. The project raised environmental concerns among the locals.

english_meaning: The movement or philosophy concerned with protecting the natural environment. Advocacy for the preservation of nature. A political and social movement focused on ecological issues.
example_sentence: Environmentalism has grown rapidly in recent decades. He became interested in environmentalism after college. The movement of environmentalism fights against pollution. Many young people support environmentalism today.

english_meaning: A person who works to protect the natural environment. An activist concerned with ecological issues. Someone who campaigns against pollution and destruction of nature.
example_sentence: The environmentalist gave a speech about climate change. Environmentalists protested against the new factory. She is a well-known environmentalist in her country. The environmentalist planted a hundred trees this year.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the environment. With regard to the natural world and its protection. In an ecological manner.
example_sentence: The product is environmentally friendly. The company acts environmentally responsibly. The factory was shut down for being environmentally unsafe. They disposed of the waste in an environmentally safe way.

english_meaning: To imagine or picture something in the future. To form a clear mental picture of something that has not yet happened. It is used when someone thinks seriously about a possible plan, outcome, or situation in the future. It can also mean to consider something as likely or possible.
example_sentence: She envisages a future where renewable energy powers every home. The company envisaged expanding into international markets. I did not envisage so many challenges at the beginning of the project. They envisage building a school in the rural area next year.

english_meaning: To imagine or picture something in your mind as a future possibility. To foresee or visualize a future event or condition. It involves forming a mental image of something that does not yet exist but could exist in the future, often with a sense of hope or planning.
example_sentence: She would often envision herself as a successful novelist. The company envisions a future where its products are used in every home. It's hard to envision a world without the internet. He envisioned a day when he would be free from all his troubles. Can you envision the final design of the building?

english_meaning: A person sent as a representative to another country or organization, especially for diplomatic purposes.  A diplomatic agent of lower rank than an ambassador. A messenger sent for a special mission. A representative in peace talks or conflict resolution. A delegate assigned to handle specific international issues.
example_sentence: The envoy was therefore dismissed. In 1864 he went as Hessian envoy to Vienna, retiring in 1872 when the post was abolished.

english_meaning: A feeling of jealousy or desire for something that someone else has. To feel jealous of someone or to strongly desire what they have. Desire for another’s advantages. Jealous admiration mixed with resentment. Feeling unhappy because others are better off.
example_sentence: He could not conceal his envy of me. They looked with envy at her latest purchase. She has always envied my success. I envy you having such a close family.

english_meaning: The quality of being fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing. It refers to the art of using language with skill, grace, and effectiveness to please or persuade. This involves not just clarity and fluency, but also the ability to stir emotions, be convincing, and articulate thoughts in a clear and powerful manner.
example_sentence: The lawyer's eloquence won over the jury. Her eloquence was matched only by her beauty. He was a preacher of great eloquence. Martin Luther King Jr. is remembered for his powerful eloquence. Lack of eloquence can be a major hurdle in a public-facing career.

english_meaning: Lasting for a very short time. Short-lived or transitory in nature. It often describes things in nature like flowers or fleeting emotions that do not endure.
example_sentence: The beauty of the sunset is ephemeral, lasting only a few precious minutes. Many internet trends are ephemeral and are forgotten within a few weeks. The ephemeral nature of fashion means that styles change every season. We must cherish these ephemeral moments of joy before they pass away.

english_meaning: A long poem that tells the story of a hero's adventures. A long book, movie, etc that usually tells a story about exciting events or adventures. Large and impressive in size, grandeur, extent, or conception
example_sentence: It's one of those old Hollywood epics with a cast of thousands. The problem of inflation has reached epic proportions. The football game was an epic battle between two great teams.

english_meaning: Having characteristics of both sexes or neither sex. Often used to describe something that is effeminate or lacks a distinct gender identity. In linguistics, it refers to nouns that have one form for both masculine and feminine.
example_sentence: The fashion designer focused on creating an epicene collection suitable for everyone. His epicene features made it difficult to determine his gender at a glance. The novel features an epicene protagonist who defies traditional gender roles. Some artists prefer an epicene aesthetic to challenge societal norms.

english_meaning: The part of the earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake. The point on the earth’s surface where the effects of an earthquake are felt most strongly. A thing or place that is of greatest importance to an activity or interest.
example_sentence: The Great Nicobar islands lie at the closest point to the epicenter of the earthquake. The U.S. cannot simply assume that it will remain the epicenter of scientific research and technological innovation.

english_meaning: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the true center (the focus or hypocenter) of an earthquake. By extension, it also refers to the central point of a difficult, unpleasant, or momentous situation. It is the place where an activity or event is most intense or has its origin.
example_sentence: The epicentre of the earthquake was 50 miles from the city. The town became the epicentre of the political crisis. New York City is an epicentre of global finance. The investigation focused on the epicentre of the outbreak. The family was at the epicentre of the scandal.

english_meaning: A person who enjoys fine food and drink. A person devoted to pleasure, especially in eating and drinking. Someone with refined and discriminating taste. A lover of luxury and comfort. A person who appreciates luxury and sensory pleasures in life. A person seeks high quality meals, unique flavors, and carefully prepared dishes. A person who appreciates luxury and sensory pleasures in life.
example_sentence: He is an epicure who travels the world to taste different cuisines. As an epicure, she only dines at the finest restaurants. The dinner party was designed to impress every epicure present. Being an epicure, he values quality over quantity in food.

english_meaning: A sudden increase in the number of cases of a disease in a particular area or among a specific group of people. A situation in which a disease spreads quickly and affects many individuals within a community, region, or population at the same time. The term can also be used for rapid spread of non medical problems such as misinformation, crime, or social issues.
example_sentence: Car theft is now reaching epidemic proportions. An epidemic of measles broke out, and over 200 children died. Effectively, tobacco companies will be exporting an epidemic of smoking-related diseases, the campaign suggests. The city faced an epidemic of dengue during the rainy season. Social media misinformation became an epidemic among teenagers.

english_meaning: Relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of the skin. Concerning the surface layer of skin or plant tissue. Belonging to the outermost protective covering of an organism.
example_sentence: The cream treats epidermal problems effectively. Epidermal cells regenerate very quickly. The doctor examined the epidermal layer for damage. Sunlight can cause epidermal burns.

english_meaning: The outer layer of the skin covering the body. The protective outermost tissue of plants and animals. A thin surface layer that shields underlying cells. The visible layer of skin exposed to the environment.
example_sentence: The epidermis protects the body from harmful bacteria. Sunburn damages the epidermis of the skin. The epidermis of the leaf prevents water loss. Doctors examined the epidermis for signs of infection.

english_meaning: A long coiled tube lying at the back of each testis. The structure in which sperm mature and are stored. A duct that connects the testis to the vas deferens. A tightly folded tube several metres long when stretched out.
example_sentence: Sperm mature as they pass through the epididymis. The epididymis lies along the back of the testis. Infection of the epididymis causes pain and swelling. Sperm may be stored in the epididymis for several weeks.

english_meaning: The flap of cartilage at the base of the tongue that covers the windpipe during swallowing. A small lid-like structure that stops food and drink from entering the airway. The cartilage that directs swallowed material into the esophagus.
example_sentence: The epiglottis closes automatically when we swallow. Food enters the windpipe when the epiglottis fails to close. Inflammation of the epiglottis can make breathing difficult. The epiglottis protects the lungs from food particles.

english_meaning: A neurological disorder marked by sudden, recurrent episodes of sensory disturbance, loss of consciousness, or convulsions. It is associated with abnormal electrical activity in the brain. The seizures vary in intensity and frequency among affected individuals.
example_sentence: She takes medication to successfully control the seizures caused by her epilepsy. The flashing strobe lights at the concert triggered his epilepsy. Epilepsy is a complex neurological disorder that requires careful medical management. Children diagnosed with epilepsy can still lead perfectly normal and active lives. He wears a medical alert bracelet in case an attack of epilepsy occurs.

english_meaning: A sudden clear understanding or realization. A moment when a person suddenly understands something important or sees a situation in a new and meaningful way.  An intuitive grasp of reality through something as simple as a common occurrence. In a religious sense, it refers to the manifestation of a divine being.
example_sentence: She had an epiphany while reading the report and finally understood the problem. His travel experience led to an epiphany about what truly matters in life. During the meeting, the solution came to her as an epiphany. The teacher’s explanation gave the students an epiphany about the concept.

english_meaning: Excessive watering of the eyes. A medical and rhetorical term. In medicine, it refers to excessive tearing caused by irritation, infection, or blockage of tear ducts. In rhetoric, it means repetition of a word or phrase at the end of successive sentences for emphasis.
example_sentence: The patient complained of epiphora due to blocked tear ducts. Cold wind often causes temporary epiphora in winter. The poet used epiphora to give rhythm to his speech. Repeating the phrase at the end of each line is a form of epiphora.

english_meaning: An individual installment of a serialized television program, radio show, or podcast. A specific event or period of time that is part of a longer sequence of events. An incident or occurrence that is distinct and often noteworthy. A sudden brief period of an illness or a specific symptom manifesting. A section between two choric songs in a Greek tragedy.
example_sentence: I missed the latest episode of my favorite drama series last night. The financial crisis was a dark episode in the country's history. He experienced a brief episode of dizziness during the workout. The final episode of the season left viewers with a massive cliffhanger.

english_meaning: Happening in separate or disconnected parts or episodes. Something occurring occasionally or in irregular intervals rather than continuously. Often used for events, memories, or storytelling that happens in distinct segments.
example_sentence: His memory of childhood was episodic and incomplete. The TV series is episodic, with each episode telling a separate story. Rainfall in this region is episodic and unpredictable. The patient experienced episodic headaches over several months.

english_meaning: The branch of philosophy that studies knowledge, its nature, sources, and limits. The theory of how we know what we know and how beliefs are justified. A particular way of understanding what counts as valid knowledge. The study of the difference between genuine knowledge and mere opinion.
example_sentence: He wrote his thesis on the epistemology of modern science. Epistemology asks how we can be certain of anything. Their debate turned into a question of epistemology. Western and Eastern epistemology often differ in method.

english_meaning: Relating to the branch of philosophy that studies knowledge, belief, and justification. Concerning how we know what we know and the limits of human understanding. Belonging to theories about the nature and sources of knowledge.
example_sentence: The debate raised difficult epistemological questions. Her thesis takes an epistemological approach to memory. Scientists rarely discuss the epistemological basis of their methods. The book examines the epistemological limits of observation.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the theory of knowledge. From the point of view of how knowledge is acquired and justified. In terms of epistemology or philosophical enquiry into knowing.
example_sentence: Epistemologically, the claim rests on very weak evidence. The two theories differ epistemologically as well as practically. He argued that the method is epistemologically unsound. Epistemologically speaking, certainty is rarely possible.

english_meaning: The branch of philosophy that studies the nature, origin, and limits of knowledge. The theory of how we come to know things and how beliefs can be justified. A particular set of ideas about what counts as valid knowledge.
example_sentence: Epistemology asks how we can be sure of what we believe. He teaches epistemology at the university. Modern epistemology draws heavily on cognitive science. The two thinkers differ sharply in their epistemology.

english_meaning: A person who loves knowledge and learning. Someone strongly motivated to seek information, understanding, and intellectual discovery.
example_sentence: As an epistemophile, she reads books on many different subjects. The young epistemophile asked questions throughout the lecture. Epistemophiles often enjoy exploring unfamiliar fields. His friends knew him as an epistemophile who never stopped learning.

english_meaning: A strong love of knowledge and learning. An intense or excessive desire to know, investigate, and understand. In psychoanalytic usage, a powerful drive to acquire knowledge, sometimes concerning hidden or forbidden matters.
example_sentence: His epistemophilia drove him to read widely across many subjects. Her epistemophilia was evident in the thoughtful questions she asked. The course encouraged healthy epistemophilia rather than passive memorization. Psychoanalytic writers have examined epistemophilia as a powerful human drive.

english_meaning: A person with an intense love of knowledge and learning. Someone strongly driven to discover, understand, and acquire information. A person characterized by intellectual curiosity, especially to an unusually high degree.
example_sentence: As an epistemophiliac, she is always enrolled in a new course. The library is a natural refuge for an epistemophiliac. His friends call him an epistemophiliac because he asks questions about everything. An epistemophiliac often enjoys exploring subjects far beyond a formal curriculum.

english_meaning: A formal or literary letter, especially a long one. Any of the letters written by the apostles and included in the New Testament. A written communication in an elegant or old-fashioned style.
example_sentence: He wrote a long epistle to his old teacher. The epistles of Paul are studied in theology classes. Her weekly epistle from abroad delighted the whole family. The novel is written as a series of epistles.

english_meaning: Relating to or written in the form of letters. Describing a novel or work of literature told through the exchange of letters. Concerning correspondence between people.
example_sentence: Dracula is a famous epistolary novel. Their epistolary friendship lasted for thirty years. The author chose an epistolary style for the memoir. Scholars study the epistolary habits of eighteenth-century writers.

english_meaning: A rhetorical device in which the same word or phrase is repeated at the end of successive sentences or clauses.
example_sentence: We demand justice for the poor, justice for the weak, justice for all. She believed in love, lived for love, and died for love. The people wanted change in the streets, change in the homes, change in the nation. He worked with passion, spoke with passion, and led with passion.

english_meaning: An inscription written on a tombstone in memory of the person buried there. A short text or verse composed to honour someone who has died. Any brief statement that sums up a person, era, or event that has ended. A final commemorative remark.
example_sentence: His epitaph reads simply, “A kind and honest man.” The poet wrote his own epitaph before he died. The closing of the mill served as an epitaph for the town's industry. Visitors stopped to read the weathered epitaph.

english_meaning: A tissue that covers the outer surfaces of the body and lines internal cavities and organs. A sheet of closely packed cells that forms a protective barrier. Tissue involved in protection, absorption, secretion, and sensation. One of the four basic tissue types found in the human body.
example_sentence: Epithelial tissue covers the entire surface of the skin. The lining of the stomach is made of epithelial tissue. Epithelial tissue helps absorb nutrients in the intestine. Damage to epithelial tissue can allow germs to enter the body.

english_meaning: A word or short phrase used to describe a person's most noticeable quality. A descriptive title added to or used instead of a name. An offensive or insulting word aimed at someone.
example_sentence: Alexander earned the epithet the Great. The crowd shouted racial epithets at the players. Poets often use fixed epithets for their heroes. His courage won him the epithet of lionheart.

english_meaning: A perfect example of a quality, type, or characteristic. A person or thing that represents the highest standard or embodiment of something.
example_sentence: She is the epitome of kindness, always helping those in need. His dedication to work is the epitome of professionalism. The Taj Mahal is considered the epitome of Mughal architecture. He is the epitome of courage in the face of danger.

english_meaning: A particular period of time in history marked by notable events. A long span of time associated with distinctive characteristics. The beginning of a distinctive period in history. A division of geological time smaller than a period.
example_sentence: The invention of the printing press marked a new epoch in human history. We are living in an epoch of rapid technological change. Geologists study each epoch through layers of rock. That victory opened a fresh epoch for the nation.

english_meaning: A lyric poem in which a short line follows a long one, a metrical form favored by ancient Greek and Latin poets. It is also the third and final part of a triadic Greek choral ode, which follows the strophe and the antistrophe, completing the stanzaic structure. It serves as a concluding section in certain odes.
example_sentence: The poet Archilochus was a master of the epode. The structure of the poem is a classic epode. In an epode, the second line of the couplet is shorter than the first. The chorus sang the strophe, antistrophe, and then the final epode. Pindar's odes often conclude with an epode.

english_meaning: A person after whom a discovery, invention, place, etc., is named or thought to be named. A name or noun formed after a person. An eponym is a person, whether real or fictitious, from whom a particular place, tribe, discovery, or other thing is said to have taken its name. For example, the Achilles tendon is named after the Greek hero Achilles. The word can also refer to the name itself, such as 'sandwich,' which is an eponym derived from John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich.
example_sentence: The word 'sandwich' is an eponym derived from the Earl of Sandwich. Parkinson's disease is named after James Parkinson, making him the eponym for the condition. Many medical terms are eponyms, honoring the physicians who first described them. The fictional character 'Don Quixote' became the eponym for the term 'quixotic'.

english_meaning: Of, relating to, or being the person or thing for whom or which something is named. Giving one's name to something. This describes something that is named after a particular person or thing. For instance, in the novel 'Jane Eyre,' Jane Eyre is the eponymous heroine. It signifies that the title of the work, the name of a band, or a place is derived from the name of the main character, the band itself, or a significant individual associated with it.
example_sentence: The band's eponymous album was their most successful. 'Forrest Gump' features the eponymous character in a journey through American history. She is the eponymous founder of the charitable organization. The eponymous hero of the film is a struggling musician. The play's eponymous role is famously difficult to cast.

english_meaning: An adhesive, plastic, or paint made from a class of synthetic thermosetting polymers containing epoxide groups. A strong glue. Any of the basic components or the cured end products of epoxy resins, as well as a common name for the epoxide functional group. To glue or coat something with epoxy resin. This material is known for its strong adhesive properties, chemical resistance, and durability, making it widely used in construction, electronics, and art.
example_sentence: He used epoxy to repair the broken ceramic vase. You can find epoxy resin at any hardware store. The garage floor was coated with a layer of grey epoxy. Make sure to mix the two parts of the epoxy thoroughly before applying. We need to epoxy these two pieces of wood together.

english_meaning: To have been glued, filled, or coated with epoxy resin. The past tense and past participle of the verb 'epoxy'. It describes something that has undergone the application of epoxy. For example, an 'epoxyed floor' is a floor that has been coated with epoxy for protection and a glossy finish. This treatment makes surfaces more durable and resistant to wear and tear.
example_sentence: The cracked countertop was skillfully epoxyed and looked as good as new. He epoxyed the legs back onto the broken chair. We admired the beautifully epoxyed river table. The two metal plates were epoxyed together for a permanent bond. All the joints were epoxyed to prevent any leaks.

english_meaning: Calm and even-tempered, not easily upset or annoyed. Free from sudden or extreme changes. Describing a climate that stays moderate and steady. Uniform and consistent in nature or quality.
example_sentence: He has an equable temperament that keeps the team calm. The island enjoys an equable climate throughout the year. She responded to the criticism in an equable tone. Their equable relationship has lasted for decades.

english_meaning: Being the same in quantity, size, value, or degree. Having the same rights, status, or opportunities. To be the same as something in amount or quality. A person or thing of the same rank or ability as another.
example_sentence: All citizens are equal before the law. Two plus three equals five. She had an equal share in the business. He has no equal in the field of mathematics.

english_meaning: The state of being equal in rights, status, or opportunities. Fair treatment of all people without discrimination. The condition of being the same in quantity or value. In mathematics, the relation of two expressions having the same value.
example_sentence: The movement fought for equality between men and women. Equality of opportunity is essential in education. The law guarantees equality for every citizen. They demanded equality in pay for the same work.

english_meaning: To make things equal in size, amount, or status. To remove differences between people or groups. In sport, to score a goal or point that makes the score level. To balance pressure, sound, or force evenly.
example_sentence: The new policy aims to equalize educational opportunities. He scored late to equalize the match. Divers must equalize the pressure in their ears. Taxes were adjusted to equalize incomes.

english_meaning: A device that adjusts the balance of sound frequencies. A goal or point that makes the scores level in a game. Something that makes conditions equal for everyone. A person or thing that removes advantage or difference.
example_sentence: He adjusted the equalizer to improve the bass. Their striker scored the equalizer in the last minute. Education is often called the great equalizer. The engineer installed a digital equalizer in the studio.

english_meaning: To the same extent or degree. In equal parts or amounts. In a fair and even manner. Used to introduce a point of similar importance.
example_sentence: The cake was divided equally among the children. Both options are equally attractive. She treats all her students equally. Equally, we must consider the long-term costs.

english_meaning: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations. The ability to remain emotionally stable and composed under pressure, stress, or adversity.
example_sentence: She faced the tragedy with remarkable equanimity. His equanimity during the crisis inspired everyone around him. It takes great equanimity to remain calm during a storm. She accepted the criticism with equanimity and grace.

english_meaning: An officer in a royal household who attends a monarch or another royal family member. Historically, an officer responsible for the horses and stables of a royal or noble household.
example_sentence: The equerry accompanied the king at the ceremony. Her equerry arranged the princess’s daily engagements. In earlier times, an equerry supervised the royal stables. The queen thanked her equerry for his assistance.

english_meaning: Relating to horses or horse riding. A person who rides horses, especially a skilled rider or participant in riding sports. Mounted on horseback, especially in a statue.
example_sentence: She competed in an international equestrian event. The park has a long equestrian trail. He is an experienced equestrian. An equestrian statue stands in the square.

english_meaning: The art, sport, or practice of horse riding. The skill of riding, driving, or handling horses. A competitive sport that includes dressage, show jumping, and eventing. Activities and disciplines connected with horses and horsemanship.
example_sentence: Equestrianism has been part of the Olympic Games for over a century. She developed a lifelong passion for equestrianism as a child. The club promotes equestrianism among young riders. Modern equestrianism demands both skill and patience.

english_meaning: Being at an equal distance from two or more points. Placed at the same distance apart from each other. Located centrally between two places. Evenly spaced in position or arrangement.
example_sentence: The town is equidistant from both cities. Plant the trees equidistant from one another. Every point on a circle is equidistant from the centre. The offices are equidistant from the main station.

english_meaning: A triangle in which all three sides are of equal length. A triangle whose three angles each measure sixty degrees. A perfectly symmetrical three-sided figure. A regular polygon with three equal sides.
example_sentence: Each angle of an equilateral triangle measures sixty degrees. He drew an equilateral triangle using a compass. The logo is based on an equilateral triangle. An equilateral triangle is also equiangular.

english_meaning: A state of balance between opposing forces or influences. A condition of physical stability where forces cancel out. Calmness and balance of mind or emotions. In chemistry or economics, a state where opposing rates or forces are equal.
example_sentence: The scales settled into perfect equilibrium. She regained her emotional equilibrium after the news. Supply and demand reached equilibrium in the market. The chemical reaction finally reached equilibrium.

english_meaning: Relating to or resembling horses. Belonging to the horse family. A horse or a member of the horse family. Typical of the features or behaviour of a horse.
example_sentence: The vet specialises in equine medicine. She has a slightly equine profile. Equine influenza spread quickly through the stables. The farm cares for more than fifty equines.

english_meaning: Relating to the equinox, when day and night are of equal length. Occurring at or near the time of an equinox. Relating to the celestial equator. Happening at regular equinox periods, such as equinoctial gales.
example_sentence: Equinoctial storms often batter the coast in late September. The equinoctial line divides the celestial sphere into two halves. Farmers plan sowing around the equinoctial period. He recorded the equinoctial sunrise from the hilltop.

english_meaning: The time or date (twice each year) at which the sun crosses the celestial equator, when day and night are of approximately equal length. Vernal and autumnal points. An equinox is an astronomical event in which the plane of Earth's equator passes through the center of the Sun's disk. This occurs twice each year, around March 20th (the vernal or spring equinox) and September 22nd or 23rd (the autumnal equinox). On these days, the Sun appears to be directly above the equator, resulting in the length of day and night being nearly equal across the entire planet.
synonyms: ["Equal day and night","Vernal point","Autumnal point","Solstice counterpart","Celestial crossing","Equilibrium","Balance point"]
example_sentence: The spring equinox signals the beginning of warmer weather. In the Southern Hemisphere, the March equinox is the start of autumn. Many ancient cultures celebrated the vernal and autumnal equinoxes. The balance of light and dark during the equinox holds symbolic meaning for many traditions. The farmer always planted his crops after the spring equinox.

english_meaning: To provide with the necessary items for a particular purpose. To supply with the appropriate tools, gear, or clothing for a specific activity or task. This involves furnishing or outfitting someone or something with what is needed to be effective or prepared.
example_sentence: The soldiers were equipped with the latest technology. We need to equip the new office with computers and furniture. She equipped herself with a map and compass before the hike. Make sure you equip your children with the skills they need to succeed.

english_meaning: The tools, machines, clothing, or other items needed for a particular activity or purpose. The process of supplying someone or something with necessary items. Mental or practical preparation for a task.
example_sentence: The laboratory purchased new equipment. Climbers must carry proper safety equipment. All camping equipment was packed in the van. Her training gave her the equipment needed for leadership.

english_meaning: A state of balance between opposing forces or interests. Equal distribution of weight or influence. A counterbalance that keeps something steady. To balance or hold something in equilibrium.
example_sentence: The two arguments were held in perfect equipoise. She maintained an emotional equipoise during the crisis. Political power rested in a delicate equipoise. The weights equipoise each other on the scale.

english_meaning: Fair and impartial to everyone concerned. Treating all people in a just and reasonable way. Dealing with people according to their needs so that outcomes are fair. In law, relating to the principles of equity rather than strict legal rules. Free from favouritism, bias, or prejudice.
example_sentence: The committee promised an equitable distribution of resources. Everyone deserves equitable access to quality education. The court reached an equitable settlement between the two parties. They are working towards a more equitable society.

english_meaning: In a fair and impartial manner. In a way that treats everyone justly and reasonably. Without favouritism or bias in distribution. According to the principles of fairness.
example_sentence: The profits were divided equitably among the partners. Resources must be shared equitably between the provinces. The teacher treated all students equitably. Work was distributed equitably across the team.

english_meaning: The art and practice of horse riding. Skill in handling and controlling a horse. Formal training in riding technique and posture. A competitive discipline judging a rider's form.
example_sentence: She has studied equitation since childhood. The academy offers lessons in classical equitation. Good equitation requires balance and patience. He won first place in the equitation class.

english_meaning: The quality of being fair and impartial. Fairness and justice in the way people are treated. In finance, it represents the value of an ownership interest in property, such as a business or a home, after subtracting any debts or liabilities associated with it.
example_sentence: The company is committed to promoting equity and diversity in the workplace. He has a lot of equity in his home. The new law aims to ensure equity in the distribution of resources. Achieving equity in education is a long-term goal.

english_meaning: The condition of being equal in value, amount, meaning, importance, or function. A close correspondence between two things that makes them interchangeable. In mathematics and logic, a relationship in which two statements or expressions always have the same value. In language, the state of two words or phrases carrying the same meaning. The quality of matching another thing exactly in worth or effect.
example_sentence: There is no exact equivalence between the two currencies. The translator searched for the closest equivalence in meaning. The teacher explained the equivalence of the two fractions. The university accepted the diploma on the basis of academic equivalence.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being equal in value, meaning, or effect. Official recognition that a qualification, degree, or certificate is equal to another. A measure showing that one thing corresponds exactly to another. The condition in which two amounts, units, or standards match. A document or certificate confirming that two qualifications are of equal standing.
example_sentence: She obtained an equivalency certificate for her foreign degree. The board grants equivalency to diplomas earned abroad. He passed a high school equivalency examination last year. The two courses were approved on the basis of equivalency.

english_meaning: Equal in value, amount, meaning, or importance. Having the same effect or function as something else. A thing or amount that corresponds to another. Similar enough to be considered the same.
example_sentence: One mile is roughly equivalent to 1.6 kilometres. Her role is equivalent to that of a manager. There is no exact equivalent for this word in English. He earns the equivalent of a full year's salary in six months.

english_meaning: Unclear or having more than one possible meaning. Something that is ambiguous, uncertain, or open to more than one interpretation. It is often used for statements, answers, or behavior that avoid a clear commitment or definite meaning.
example_sentence: His answer was equivocal, so no one understood his real opinion. The politician gave an equivocal response to avoid controversy. Her feelings about the decision were equivocal and confused. The evidence was equivocal and did not clearly prove anything.

english_meaning: A long and distinct period of history. A period marked by particular events, characteristics, or developments. A memorable or important stage in the history of a person, group, or civilization. A system of chronology reckoned from a notable event. A significant point in geological time.
example_sentence: The invention of the internet marked the beginning of a new era. We are living in an era of rapid technological change. The Victorian era produced many great writers. His presidency was seen as the end of an era.

english_meaning: To emit or radiate light, heat, or other energy. To shine brightly or to send out rays. Although it sounds similar to "eradicate", its meaning is related to radiation and emission.
example_sentence: The sun eradiated light and warmth across the valley. The glowing coals eradiated a gentle heat. A feeling of joy seemed to eradiate from her. The lantern eradiated a dim light in the darkness.

english_meaning: Rigidly upright or straight. To construct or build a building, wall, or other upright structure. To create or establish something, such as a system or an institution.
example_sentence: He stood erect with his shoulders back. The monument was erected in memory of the war heroes. They plan to erect a new office building downtown. The company was erected on a foundation of trust. She has an erect posture.

english_meaning: The act of building, constructing, raising, or setting something upright. It can also refer to the state of being upright. In medical and biological contexts, it refers to the enlargement and stiffening of an organ, especially the penis, due to increased blood flow.
example_sentence: The erection of the new bridge will take several months. The erection of the tent was a complicated process. The medieval erection stood on the hill for centuries. The book provides a guide to the erection and maintenance of fences.

english_meaning: A hermit or recluse, especially one who has retired to a solitary place for religious reasons. A person who lives in seclusion from society. An eremite chooses to withdraw from the world to pursue a life of solitude, contemplation, and spiritual devotion, often in a remote or desolate location.
example_sentence: The eremite lived in a small cave on the mountainside. Many early Christian saints were eremites who sought spiritual purity in the desert. He abandoned his city life to become an eremite in the wilderness. The life of an eremite is one of extreme solitude and self-discipline.

english_meaning: An irrational fear of blushing in front of others. Extreme anxiety about turning red in the face in social situations. A phobia in which a person dreads visible embarrassment. Also spelled erythrophobia.
example_sentence: His ereuthophobia made public speaking almost impossible. People with ereuthophobia often avoid group meetings. She sought therapy for her ereuthophobia last year. Ereuthophobia can begin during the teenage years.

english_meaning: The day before yesterday. An archaic English term referring to two days prior to the present day. Rarely used in modern English, having been replaced by the phrase the day before yesterday. Sometimes used in literary, historical, or whimsical writing.
example_sentence: He told me he had visited the city ereyesterday, though I find that hard to believe.  Ereyesterday's storm caused significant damage to the coastal villages.  In her diary, she often used old-fashioned words like ereyesterday instead of modern phrases.  The package was supposed to arrive ereyesterday but is still missing.  Ereyesterday seems like such a distant memory already.

english_meaning: An excessive and obsessive desire to work. A compulsive need to keep working without rest. Workaholism carried to an unhealthy extreme. A mental state in which work dominates a person's entire life. An abnormal devotion to work that harms health and relationships.
example_sentence: His ergomania kept him in the office until midnight every day. Her ergomania left no time for family or friends. The doctor warned that his ergomania was damaging his health. Many start-up founders suffer from ergomania in their early years.

english_meaning: Work-lover, someone passionate about working. A person who loves work, is highly enthusiastic about working, and finds satisfaction in productivity.
example_sentence: John is an ergophile who often spends extra hours at the office. The company appreciates ergophiles because they boost overall productivity. Unlike his peers, Tom is an ergophile and finds joy in challenging projects. Being an ergophile, she volunteers for tasks that others avoid.

english_meaning: A person who argues merely for the sake of conflict or victory, not for truth. Relating to arguments that are intended to win rather than to reach the truth. Characterized by disputing, controversy, or argument for argument’s sake.
example_sentence: His eristic debating style won him many arguments but few friends. The discussion turned eristic when both sides stopped listening and just tried to outsmart each other. She avoided eristic conversations because they led nowhere productive. An eristic thinker enjoys challenging others, even without a clear purpose.

english_meaning: To slowly wear away, destroy, or reduce something by natural forces like water, wind, or by gradual influence. It can refer to physical wearing of land or the slow weakening of power, trust, values, or systems.
example_sentence: Heavy rain can erode the soil on hillsides. Years of corruption began to erode public trust in the government. Strong ocean waves slowly erode the coastline. Constant criticism can erode a person's confidence.

english_meaning: A short journey or trip that you make because you need to do a particular task. It is commonly used for everyday activities such as going to a shop to buy something, going to the post office to send a letter, picking up medicine, or delivering a message or package. It can also refer to the task itself, especially when someone asks you to go somewhere and do something for them.
example_sentence: I need to run an errand before dinner. She went on an errand to buy some medicine. My father asked me to run an errand for him. I have several errands to do this afternoon.

english_meaning: Short trips taken to perform necessary tasks or chores, such as buying something, delivering a message, or paying bills. It refers to the routine daily tasks or small jobs that need to be done usually outside the house. It can also refer to specific missions or commissions assigned to someone to complete on behalf of another person.
example_sentence: I have a few errands to run this afternoon before I can meet you. She spent the entire weekend running errands around town. Can you help me with some household errands today? He left the office early to do some personal errands.

english_meaning: Moving or behaving in a way that is not regular, certain, or expected. Lacking consistency or regularity in conduct or movement. Deviating from the usual or proper course in opinion or conduct. Having no fixed or regular course. Characterized by lack of predictability.
example_sentence: His behavior has become increasingly erratic since he lost his job. The weather in this region is quite erratic during the spring season. Investors are worried about the erratic movements of the stock market. She gave an erratic performance that confused the judges.

english_meaning: Making a mistake or failing to adhere to correct standards. Behaving wrongly or straying from the path of virtue. Deviating from the truth or a prescribed course of action. Committing a sin or moral transgression. Falling into error or inaccuracy. Being in a state of oversight or blundering.
example_sentence: The erring employee was given a formal warning regarding his conduct. She felt a deep sense of guilt for her erring ways during her youth. The umpire admitted to erring in his judgment during the final play. Even the most erring individual deserves a chance at redemption.

english_meaning: Wrong or based on incorrect information. Containing or characterized by error. Mistaken in judgement or opinion. Not accurate or correct. Resulting from a mistake or a faulty assumption.
example_sentence: The report was based on erroneous data and had to be revised. He held an erroneous belief about the company's financial position. Her erroneous assumptions led to a wrong conclusion. The newspaper apologized for publishing erroneous information. Erroneous calculations caused a major loss to the firm.

english_meaning: A person who has deep knowledge gained through extensive study and reading. Someone scholarly, well educated, and intellectually refined.
example_sentence: The professor is an erudite scholar known for his vast knowledge of history. She gave an erudite explanation of climate change during the seminar. His erudite writing style impressed readers around the world. The panel included several erudite thinkers from different fields.

english_meaning: To burst out suddenly, especially with force, emotion, or activity. To explode or burst out suddenly, like a volcano or liquid. To suddenly show strong emotions like anger, laughter, or excitement. To begin suddenly, especially conflicts, protests, or noise. To break out on the skin, like rashes or pimples. To come out forcefully (lava, smoke, sound)
example_sentence: The volcano erupted after years of silence. The crowd erupted in cheers when the team won. Violence erupted in the city after the protest. She erupted in anger when she heard the news.

english_meaning: To increase in intensity, seriousness, or size. To become more intense, serious, or severe. It is often used for conflicts, problems, costs, or situations that grow quickly.
example_sentence: The argument began to escalate after the meeting. Prices may escalate during the holiday season. The manager stepped in before the issue could escalate. Tensions escalated between the two teams.

english_meaning: A rise or increase in intensity, seriousness, or scale. A situation where something becomes more intense, serious, or larger in scale over time. It is often used for conflicts, prices, problems, or tensions that keep increasing.
example_sentence: The escalation of prices has made life difficult for many families. There was an escalation in the conflict between the two countries. The manager tried to stop the escalation of the issue in the office. Emotional escalation during arguments can lead to misunderstandings

english_meaning: A moving staircase that carries people between floors. A motor driven moving staircase found in malls, airports, stations and large buildings. It helps people travel between floors without climbing regular stairs. A system or process that increases or rises step by step, often used metaphorically. A mechanical device designed to move people efficiently in busy places.
example_sentence: The mall installed a new escalator near the main entrance. The escalator stopped working, so everyone had to use the stairs. She stood on the escalator while it carried her to the second floor. The airport has several escalators to manage the heavy crowd.

english_meaning: A thin slice of boneless meat, usually veal, chicken, or pork, often flattened and cooked quickly by frying or grilling. A boneless piece of meat that is sliced very thin and usually tenderized. It is commonly coated with flour, breadcrumbs, or seasoning and then fried or grilled quickly. It is popular in European cuisine, especially French and Italian dishes.
antonyms: ["Thick steak","Whole cut of meat","Bone-in meat piece"]
example_sentence: I ordered a chicken escalope with fries for dinner. The chef prepared a veal escalope with lemon sauce. She prefers a lightly fried escalope over grilled meat. The restaurant is famous for its crispy pork escalope.

english_meaning: A fun, daring, or adventurous act, often slightly risky or mischievous. An adventure that is exciting, bold, or slightly irresponsible. It often involves playful or mischievous behavior, something done for thrill rather than seriousness.
example_sentence: They went on a late-night escapade to explore the old castle. The children’s escapade caused laughter rather than trouble. His mountain-climbing escapade became the highlight of the trip. She always remembers their summer escapade with a smile.

english_meaning: To get free from danger or confinement. To break free from a place, person, or situation, especially from danger, control, or confinement. It can also mean avoiding something unpleasant or forgetting worries for a short time. The act of getting away or a way to get free. Running away from danger or prison. Avoiding stress, worries, or reality. Something getting out accidentally.
example_sentence: The prisoner managed to escape from the jail at night. She reads books to escape from daily stress. The gas began to escape from the pipe. They found a secret escape through the tunnel.

english_meaning: Relating to death, judgment, and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind. Concerned with the end of the world or the ultimate climax of history. It is a term primarily used in theology and philosophy.
example_sentence: The preacher delivered an eschatological sermon about the end of days. Many ancient cultures had complex eschatological myths regarding the afterlife. The movie explores eschatological themes through a post-apocalyptic setting. His research focuses on the eschatological beliefs of medieval scholars.

english_meaning: In a manner relating to the final events in the history of the world or of humankind. It refers to the theological study of the end times, death, and judgment. This adverb describes actions or perspectives focused on the ultimate destiny of humanity.
example_sentence: The author framed his narrative eschatologically to emphasize the final judgment. The prophet spoke eschatologically about the coming of a new era. Many ancient texts are interpreted eschatologically by modern scholars. He viewed the global crisis eschatologically rather than politically.

english_meaning: The part of theology concerned with death, judgment, and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind. It is the study of 'last things' or the ultimate end of the world. Different religions have distinct eschatologies involving concepts like resurrection or nirvana.
example_sentence: The professor specialized in Christian eschatology and the Book of Revelation. Different cultures have unique myths regarding their eschatology. Islamic eschatology involves a detailed description of the Day of Judgment. The student wrote a thesis on the eschatology of ancient Norse mythology.

english_meaning: To deliberately avoid or stay away from something. To consciously choose not to do something or to avoid something, usually because it is considered wrong, harmful, unnecessary, or undesirable. It often reflects a thoughtful or moral decision.
example_sentence: He decided to eschew junk food to improve his health. The writer eschewed complicated language to make the book easy to understand. She eschews gossip and prefers meaningful conversations. Many people eschew violence and choose peaceful solutions.

english_meaning: The act of deliberately avoiding or abstaining from something. To shun or keep away from something seen as wrong, undesirable, or distasteful. This involves a conscious and often moral decision to reject or forgo a particular action, habit, or way of life.
example_sentence: She is eschewing processed foods in favor of a healthier diet. By eschewing violence, the protesters made their message more powerful. The minimalist philosophy involves eschewing unnecessary possessions. He made a point of eschewing political arguments at family gatherings.

english_meaning: To accompany or guide someone for protection, courtesy, or direction. To go with someone to provide protection or show respect. To guide or lead a person to a place. A person, group, or vehicle that accompanies another for safety. In social situations, a person who accompanies someone to an event.
example_sentence: The guard escorted the visitors to the main hall. She was escorted home after the event. Police escorted the convoy through the city. He came as her escort to the wedding.

english_meaning: "Escribe" is a Spanish word. It comes from the verb "escribir" which means "to write" in English. It is used when someone tells another person to write something. It is commonly used as a command in Spanish. It can refer to writing a letter, message, note, book, article, or any form of text.
example_sentence: Please escribe your full name on the form. She escribe letters to her friend every week. The teacher asked the students to escribe a short story. He likes to escribe notes during meetings.

english_meaning: To place money, property, or documents with a third party until certain conditions are met. A legal arrangement in which money, property, or important documents are held by a neutral third party on behalf of two other parties involved in a transaction. The third party releases the asset only after all agreed conditions are satisfied. Commonly used in real estate transactions, online purchases, business agreements, and financial dealings to protect both buyer and seller.
example_sentence: The buyer placed the deposit in escrow until the house inspection was complete. The lawyer held the documents in escrow for both parties. The payment will remain in escrow until the service is delivered. The funds were released from escrow after all conditions were met. The company escrowed the funds until the contract was finalized. We will escrow the payment until the service is delivered.

english_meaning: The muscular tube that carries food and liquid from the throat to the stomach. The passage commonly known as the food pipe. The part of the digestive tract that moves food downward by wave-like contractions.
example_sentence: Food travels down the esophagus to the stomach. Acid from the stomach can irritate the esophagus. The esophagus is about twenty-five centimetres long. He felt a burning pain in his esophagus after eating.

english_meaning: Hard to understand, secretive, or for a limited audience. Likely to be understood by a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest. Intended to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge or interest. Something obscure, abstract, or hard to understand.
example_sentence: The professor’s lecture on quantum mechanics was so esoteric that only a few students could follow it. Specialist dictionaries may be required to understand some of the more esoteric texts. His esoteric interests set him apart from his contemporaries. She has a somewhat esoteric taste in clothes.

english_meaning: To a greater degree than is usual or than for others. Used to single out one person, thing, or situation above the rest. For one particular purpose or reason. Very much or particularly so.
example_sentence: The garden is beautiful, especially in spring. He especially enjoys reading historical novels. This book was written especially for young learners. Traffic is heavy, especially during the morning hours.

english_meaning: The practice of spying or of using spies, typically by governments to obtain political and military information. It involves gathering secret or confidential information without the permission of the holder. Modern espionage often includes cyber-attacks and digital surveillance.
example_sentence: The government official was arrested under charges of international espionage. Industrial espionage allows companies to steal trade secrets from competitors. Cold War history is filled with fascinating stories of espionage. He was trained in the art of espionage and covert operations.

english_meaning: To adopt or support a cause, belief, or way of life. It can also mean to marry or become betrothed to someone. The term is often used in a formal or literary context to signify a strong commitment to an idea, principle, or person.
example_sentence: He espoused the principles of non-violent resistance. The political party espoused a platform of economic reform. She has espoused the cause of animal rights for many years. The theory he espoused has now been widely discredited. In his youth, he espoused radical ideas.

english_meaning: A short piece of writing on a particular subject, usually presenting the writer's own argument. A formal composition written as academic work or for publication. An attempt or effort to do something. To attempt or try to do something, especially something difficult. To test, try out, or examine the qualities of something.
example_sentence: She wrote a thoughtful essay on climate change for the school magazine. The professor asked us to submit a two-thousand-word essay. He essayed a difficult climb despite the bad weather. Her first essay at public speaking went surprisingly well.

english_meaning: The intrinsic nature or indispensable quality of something, especially something abstract, that determines its character. A concentrated substance, such as an extract or concentrate obtained from a plant or other matter, used for flavoring or scent. It is the fundamental, unchangeable core of a thing, its very soul or spirit.
example_sentence: The essence of his argument was that the new law is unfair. Vanilla essence is used to flavor cakes and cookies. They have managed to capture the essence of the book in the film adaptation. In essence, both sides agree on the final goal. The very essence of democracy is individual freedom.

english_meaning: Absolutely necessary; extremely important. Fundamental or central to the nature of something. A basic and indispensable element or thing. Belonging to the very essence of a person or thing. Required or unavoidable.
example_sentence: Water is essential for all forms of life. Honesty is an essential quality of a good leader. Please carry only the essential items for the trip. Regular exercise is essential to good health.

english_meaning: To set up or found something such as an organisation or system on a permanent basis. To prove or demonstrate something definitively. To achieve recognition or acceptance for something or someone.
example_sentence: The charity was established in 1987 to support children living in poverty. She worked hard to establish herself as a leading authority in her field. The investigation aimed to establish the precise cause of the accident. The company established a new office in three additional cities last year. It took years to establish trust between the two communities after the long conflict.

english_meaning: Set up firmly and successfully. Recognized and accepted over time. Proven to be true or reliable. Officially appointed or introduced. Long settled in a place or profession.
example_sentence: She is an established author with a loyal audience. The clinic follows established safety procedures. The inquiry established that no money was missing. They established a small business near the station.

english_meaning: The act of creating or founding something. An organization, institution, or business. A place of business or residence. The dominant social, political, or economic group. The process of proving a fact or relationship.
example_sentence: The establishment of the school took three years. This family-run establishment serves excellent food. The political establishment opposed the proposal. The evidence led to the establishment of his innocence.

english_meaning: Great respect and approval, a good opinion of somebody. The regard in which one is held. To respect and admire somebody, something very much.
example_sentence: She is held in high esteem by her colleagues.  Over the years, he has earned our affection and esteem. Many of these qualities are esteemed by managers. He was esteemed as a dedicated and imaginative scholar. We esteem it a privilege to have you with us.

english_meaning: Worthy of great respect or admiration; deserving of esteem. Capable of being estimated or calculated. This term is used to describe someone or something whose qualities, such as character, achievements, or abilities, are highly regarded and respected by others. It implies a significant level of worthiness and honor.
example_sentence: She has an estimable record of public service. The company has an estimable reputation for quality. He is an estimable opponent. Her contributions to science are estimable. The professor is an estimable figure in her field.

english_meaning: Of or relating to the summer season. It describes things that occur in or are characteristic of summer. The word is often used in biological or poetic contexts to describe seasonal changes.
example_sentence: The forest was filled with estival blooms during the month of July. They enjoyed the estival warmth of the Mediterranean sun. The birds began their estival migration toward the northern lakes. She preferred the estival glow of the long evening hours.

english_meaning: To spend the summer in a state of torpor or dormancy, similar to hibernation. This behavior is common in some animals to survive periods of extreme heat or drought. It can also more generally mean to spend the summer at a specific place.
example_sentence: Certain desert snails estivate deep underground during the hottest months. Many wealthy families used to estivate in the cooler mountain retreats. Some amphibians estivate in the mud until the autumn rains return. We plan to estivate by the coast this year to escape the city heat.

english_meaning: To cause someone to be no longer close or affectionate to someone; to alienate. It involves turning a person's affections away from another, often resulting in a loss of contact. It can also mean to move away from a traditional environment or habit.
example_sentence: Years of arguments began to estrange the two brothers from each other. His radical political views served to estrange him from his family. Misunderstandings can easily estrange friends who were once inseparable. The long absence did not estrange her from her native culture.

english_meaning: The fact of no longer being on friendly terms or part of a social group. It refers to a state of emotional distance or alienation between people who were once close. It often involves a formal or informal separation due to a loss of affection.
example_sentence: The long-standing estrangement between the two brothers finally ended at the wedding. Emotional estrangement can be more painful than physical distance. The strategy led to the estrangement of the company from its core customers. Years of silence resulted in a permanent estrangement from his family.

english_meaning: Extremely hungry; greedy or eager for food, wealth, or gain.
example_sentence: After a long day without food, the travelers were esurient and ready to eat anything. The esurient businessman wanted more profits, even at the cost of ethics. Children came esurient to the dinner table after playing outside all day. His esurient eyes looked at the dessert table with uncontrollable desire.

english_meaning: To cut or engrave a design on a hard surface using acid or tools. To fix something deeply in one's memory. To outline something clearly and sharply. To create a picture or pattern by scratching a surface. To mark or leave a lasting impression on something.
example_sentence: The artist etched a beautiful design on the glass. That moment is etched forever in my memory. Workers etched the company logo onto the metal plates. Years of hardship were etched on his face.

english_meaning: Cut or carved into a hard surface using acid or a sharp tool. Marked with a clear and lasting design. Fixed permanently in the memory or mind. Showing something clearly and sharply, as if drawn in fine lines.
example_sentence: Her name was etched on the silver trophy. The design was etched into the glass by hand. That day is etched in my memory forever. Deep lines of worry were etched on his face.

english_meaning: Without an end, Existing or continue for ever, Happening often & seeming never to stop
example_sentence: She's an eternal optimist (=She always expects that the best will happen). I am tired of your eternal arguments. Women try to look eternally young.

english_meaning: Infinite or unending time. A seemingly endless or immeasurably long period of time. In many religious and philosophical traditions, eternity is a state that exists outside of time, often referring to the timeless nature of God or the afterlife. It represents a duration without a beginning or an end.
example_sentence: They felt like they waited for an eternity. The lovers promised to be together for all eternity. It took an eternity for the bus to arrive. Some believe our souls will live on for eternity. The vastness of space gives a sense of eternity.

english_meaning: Something very delicate, refined, or light that seems too perfect for this world. It can refer to physical appearance, music, beauty, atmosphere, or even a person’s manner that feels heavenly or spiritual rather than earthly.
example_sentence: The bride looked ethereal in her white dress. The singer’s voice had an ethereal quality that touched everyone’s heart. A soft mist gave the mountains an ethereal appearance. The painting captured an ethereal light that made the scene magical.

english_meaning: Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge concerned with them. Morally correct or honest in conduct and decisions. Conforming to accepted standards of professional behaviour.
example_sentence: She raised several ethical concerns about the way the research was being conducted. The company committed to ethical sourcing of all its raw materials. It is not always easy to make the ethical choice when business pressures are high. The committee was established to ensure that all clinical trials were conducted in an ethical manner. He was praised for his ethical leadership during a period of significant corporate pressure.

english_meaning: In a way that follows moral principles. In a manner that is morally right and fair. With regard to accepted standards of conduct. In accordance with the rules of a profession. Honestly and responsibly.
example_sentence: The company must operate ethically to gain public trust. Doctors are expected to behave ethically at all times. He always tries to act ethically, even under pressure. Journalists should report ethically and accurately.

english_meaning: The moral principles that guide a person's behavior. The branch of knowledge that studies right and wrong conduct. Rules and standards followed by a profession or group. A system of moral values shared by a society. The study of what is good, just, and fair in human actions.
example_sentence: Medical ethics guide doctors in treating patients fairly. He is known for his strong professional ethics. The company was fined for violating business ethics. Ethics teaches us the difference between right and wrong.

english_meaning: The small spongy bone between the eye sockets at the roof of the nasal cavity. The light bone that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. A delicate skull bone through which the nerves of smell pass. The bone that forms part of the inner wall of the eye socket.
example_sentence: The ethmoid bone is one of the lightest bones in the skull. Nerves of smell pass through the ethmoid bone. A blow to the nose can damage the ethmoid bone. The ethmoid bone helps form the wall of the eye socket.

english_meaning: The fact or state of belonging to a social group that has a common national or cultural tradition. A particular ethnic group. Ethnicity is a complex concept that includes shared ancestry, language, culture, history, and often religion. It is distinct from race, which is primarily based on physical characteristics.
example_sentence: The city is home to people of many different ethnicities. Her ethnicity is a mix of Irish and Italian. The census form asked for my ethnicity. We celebrate the diversity of ethnicity in our community. Ethnicity is an important part of a person's identity.

english_meaning: The scientific description of the customs of individual peoples and cultures. A detailed, qualitative, and interpretive study of a culture or social group, in which the researcher is typically immersed in the life of the people they are studying for an extended period. It involves documenting the behaviors, beliefs, social structures, and language of a particular group from the members' own perspective. This method aims to provide a holistic and in-depth understanding of the social world of the subjects.
synonyms: ["Cultural anthropology","Descriptive anthropology","Folklore","Field research","Cultural study","Social anthropology","Participant observation","Cultural description","Societal study"]
antonyms: ["Armchair anthropology","Statistical analysis","Quantitative research","Survey research","Laboratory experiment","Theoretical analysis","Macro-sociology"]
example_sentence: Her ethnography of a remote Amazonian tribe won several awards. The book is a classic ethnography of urban poverty. He is conducting an ethnography on the workplace culture of tech startups. The study uses ethnography to explore the lives of migrant workers. Ethnography requires careful observation and detailed note-taking.

english_meaning: A type of chemical compound that is a cyclic ester. Specifically, it is a lactone (a cyclic ester) of a hydroxy fatty acid. Etholides are naturally occurring lipids found in some plants and microorganisms, characterized by the ester linkage of a hydroxyl group of one fatty acid to the carboxyl group of another, forming a chain that may then cyclize.
example_sentence: Scientists have isolated a novel etholide from the plant extract. The biosynthesis of etholides is a complex enzymatic process. This particular etholide has shown promising antimicrobial properties. The chemical structure of the etholide was determined using spectroscopy. Research is ongoing to synthesize new etholides with therapeutic potential.

english_meaning: Pertaining to ethology, the science of animal behavior. Relating to the study of the behavior of animals in their natural habitats. It focuses on the evolutionary, ecological, and physiological basis of behavior, including concepts like instinct, imprinting, and fixed action patterns.
example_sentence: The scientist made ethological observations of chimpanzee tool use. Ethological research has revealed the complexity of animal communication. The documentary provided an ethological perspective on bird migration. His theories were grounded in an ethological understanding of instinct. An ethological approach considers the adaptive value of behaviors.

english_meaning: The scientific and objective study of animal behavior, especially under natural conditions. A branch of zoology concerned with the study of animal behavior in its natural environment, viewing behavior as an evolutionarily adaptive trait. It seeks to understand the causes, functions, development, and evolution of behavior.
example_sentence: Konrad Lorenz is considered one of the founders of modern ethology. Ethology has provided key insights into the instinctual behaviors of animals. She is a leading expert in the field of primate ethology. The study of birdsong is an important area of ethology. Ethology emphasizes the importance of observing animals in their natural habitats.

english_meaning: Polite and proper behavior in social or professional situations. A set of rules or accepted behavior in society, organizations, or specific situations that show respect, good manners, and proper conduct.
example_sentence: You should learn table etiquette before attending a formal dinner. Good telephone etiquette creates a positive impression. He showed excellent etiquette during the meeting.

english_meaning: Relating to the origin and historical development of words. Concerned with changes in a word’s form, meaning, or pronunciation over time. Based on etymology or the study of word histories.
example_sentence: The dictionary includes an etymological note for each entry. Scholars disagree about the word’s etymological origin. Her article presents an etymological study of place names. The two terms have no etymological connection.

english_meaning: With reference to the origin or history of a word. From the standpoint of etymology. In a way that traces changes in form and meaning across time. By historical derivation.
example_sentence: Etymologically, the two words come from different roots. The name is etymologically related to an ancient verb. This modern usage is etymologically surprising. Etymologically speaking, the prefix means “before.”

english_meaning: The study of the origin and history of words and how their meanings have changed over time. The branch of linguistics that explores where words come from, how they were formed, and how their spelling, pronunciation, and meaning have evolved over time. It often traces words back to older languages such as Latin, Greek, Arabic, Sanskrit, or other root languages.
synonyms: ["Word origin study","Linguistic history","Word history","Origin of words"]
antonyms: ["Modern usage only","Current meaning study","Contemporary language use"]
example_sentence: The etymology of the word “school” comes from the Greek word scholē, meaning leisure or learning. Studying etymology helps students understand the deeper meaning of words. The teacher explained the etymology of “alphabet” during the lesson. Many English words have interesting etymology from Latin and French origins.

english_meaning: The Christian religious ceremony in which bread and wine are blessed, shared, and consumed as symbols, or in some traditions the actual body and blood, of Jesus Christ. The sacrament of Holy Communion. The consecrated bread and wine used in this ceremony. A central Christian rite, also known as the Lord's Supper or Holy Communion, commemorating the Last Supper of Jesus Christ with his disciples and considered one of the most important sacraments of the Church.
example_sentence: The faithful gathered in the cathedral to celebrate the Eucharist on Sunday morning. Receiving the Eucharist is considered one of the holiest moments in a Catholic's life. The priest carefully prepared the altar before the Eucharist began. Children usually receive their First Communion, or first Eucharist, at around the age of seven. The meaning of the Eucharist is explained to new believers during catechism classes.

english_meaning: The study of geometry based on the axioms and theorems of the ancient Greek mathematician Euclid. Classical geometry dealing with flat surfaces and spaces. The geometric system using postulates about points, lines, and planes. Traditional plane and solid geometry.
example_sentence: Euclidean geometry is taught in high school. The Pythagorean theorem is part of Euclidean geometry. Euclidean geometry assumes parallel lines never meet. We studied Euclidean geometry before learning non-Euclidean concepts.

english_meaning: The discredited belief and practice of trying to improve the human race by controlling who may have children. The study of methods to increase desirable inherited traits in a population. A set of ideas historically used to justify discrimination and forced sterilisation.
example_sentence: Eugenics was widely promoted in the early twentieth century. Many countries passed cruel laws inspired by eugenics. Modern scientists reject eugenics as unethical and unscientific. The documentary explored the dark history of eugenics.

english_meaning: An organism whose cells have a nucleus enclosed within a membrane. Any plant, animal, fungus, or protist made of such cells.
example_sentence: Yeast is a simple single-celled eukaryote. Every animal on Earth is a eukaryote. Scientists study how the first eukaryote evolved. A eukaryote has a more complex cell structure than a bacterium.

english_meaning: Relating to organisms whose cells contain a clear nucleus enclosed in a membrane. Describing cells that have organelles such as mitochondria. Belonging to plants, animals, fungi, or protists.
