example_sentence: Human cells are eukaryotic, while bacterial cells are not. The lecture compared prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Eukaryotic organisms include plants, animals, and fungi. Mitochondria are found only in eukaryotic cells.

english_meaning: Full of high praise. Relating to or having the nature of a eulogy. Expressing admiration, especially for someone who has died.
example_sentence: The newspaper published a eulogistic article about the late poet. His speech was warm and eulogistic. Critics gave the new novel eulogistic reviews. She wrote a eulogistic tribute to her grandfather.

english_meaning: To praise someone or something highly, typically in a speech or piece of writing. To deliver a eulogy for a person, especially at a funeral. It involves speaking or writing in formal and elaborate praise, extolling the virtues and accomplishments of the subject.
example_sentence: The late professor was eulogized for his groundbreaking research and dedication to students. At the funeral, his son stood up to eulogize his father. The article eulogized the retired CEO for his vision and leadership. He was a humble man who would have been embarrassed to be eulogized so lavishly. It is traditional to eulogize a fallen soldier.

english_meaning: A speech or piece of writing praising someone who has recently died, often given at a funeral. High praise or a tribute for a person or thing. A formal expression of admiration.
example_sentence: His son delivered a moving eulogy at the funeral. The article was a eulogy to the town's forgotten heroes. She wrote a heartfelt eulogy for her teacher. The critic's review read almost like a eulogy for the film.

english_meaning: Used as a personal female name. Symbol of victory, happiness, and success. Common in Christian and Western naming traditions. Represents kindness and strength in cultural contexts
example_sentence: Eunice was a popular name in the early 20th century. My grandmother's name is Eunice. The main character in the novel is named Eunice. We are expecting a baby and considering the name Eunice.

english_meaning: A state of beautiful thinking, a pure and balanced mind, or goodwill toward others. A well-balanced, healthy, and positive state of mind characterized by wisdom, kindness, and clarity. A sincere feeling of kindness, favor, or goodwill toward another person.
example_sentence: Her kindness reflected a rare sense of eunoia that inspired everyone around her. Meditation helped him achieve eunoia, allowing him to face challenges with calmness and wisdom. The leader governed with eunoia, always placing the well-being of the people first. The novel celebrates eunoia by showing how beautiful thoughts can transform lives.

english_meaning: A man who has been castrated, especially in the past, often employed in royal courts to guard women or serve in special roles. A male whose reproductive organs have been removed or rendered inactive. Historically, eunuchs were often trusted servants in royal households, particularly assigned to guard harems or serve queens because they were considered safe and loyal. In a broader or figurative sense, the term can also refer to a man who lacks power, vitality, or masculinity.
example_sentence: In ancient kingdoms, a eunuch was often appointed to guard the royal harem. The king trusted the eunuch with important responsibilities in the palace. Some historical records describe eunuchs as powerful advisors. He was mocked as a eunuch because he failed to show courage in difficult situations.

english_meaning: A mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh or blunt when referring to something unpleasant or embarrassing. The use of an agreeable or inoffensive expression for one that may offend or suggest something unpleasant. For instance, using 'passed away' instead of 'died'.
example_sentence: He used a euphemism to disguise his real feelings. 'Creative accounting' is a euphemism for 'falsifying financial records'. The article was full of euphemisms for the violent acts. She spoke in euphemisms to avoid upsetting the children.

english_meaning: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness. It is an affective state of exaggerated well-being or elation. This intense feeling is often disproportionate to its cause.
example_sentence: A feeling of euphoria swept over the crowd as the home team won. The drug can induce a transient state of euphoria. After the successful surgery, she was in a state of pure euphoria. The stock market boom created a sense of false euphoria among investors.

english_meaning: A drug or substance that tends to induce feelings of euphoria or extreme well-being. It is a chemical agent that stimulates the nervous system to produce happiness. These substances are often used medically or recreationally to alter mood.
example_sentence: The patient was prescribed a mild euphoriant to combat severe lethargy. Certain herbal teas are believed to act as a natural euphoriant. The scientists studied the chemical structure of the new euphoriant. Abuse of any euphoriant can lead to long-term psychological dependence.

english_meaning: Feeling or expressing intense happiness, excitement, or well-being. Extremely elated or cheerful. Filled with a sense of joy that is sometimes exaggerated or unrealistic. Describes a state of overwhelming delight, often following a great success, achievement, or pleasant experience.
example_sentence: She felt euphoric after receiving the scholarship. The team was euphoric after winning the championship. He was in a euphoric mood on his wedding day. The fans were euphoric when their favourite singer came on stage. The euphoric crowd cheered for hours.

english_meaning: To put an animal or person to death painlessly, especially to relieve suffering from an incurable or painful disease. It is often called “mercy killing.”
synonyms: ["Mercy kill","Put to sleep","Put down","End suffering humanely","Assist in dying"]
example_sentence: The veterinarian decided to euthanize the dog to end its suffering. The hospital obtained consent to euthanize the terminally ill patient. It was a difficult choice for the family to euthanize their old cat. Some countries have strict laws about when a doctor can euthanize a patient.

english_meaning: To avoid something intentionally, especially by using cleverness or trickery. To escape or avoid something (law, responsibility, danger) by cleverness or trick. To avoid answering a question directly. To stay away from something unpleasant or difficult. To avoid capture or punishment.
example_sentence: The thief tried to evade the police. She evaded my question about her salary. The company evaded paying taxes for years. He evaded responsibility for the mistake.

english_meaning: To form an idea of the amount, number, or value of; assess. To judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something. This process involves a systematic determination of a subject's merit, worth and significance, using criteria governed by a set of standards.
example_sentence: The committee will evaluate the applications. It is important to evaluate the results of the experiment. She had to evaluate her own performance. The teacher will evaluate your progress at the end of the term.

english_meaning: The process of assessing or judging the value, quality, condition, effectiveness, or significance of something. A considered judgment or appraisal. The calculation or determination of the value of an expression or quantity
example_sentence: The annual performance evaluation determines employee bonuses. Teachers conduct evaluations to measure student progress. The evaluation of the new drug's safety took several years. An honest self-evaluation can reveal areas for personal growth.

english_meaning: Relating to the assessment or judgment of value, quality, effectiveness, or performance. Expressing an opinion or judgment after careful examination. Designed to measure or appraise something
example_sentence: The teacher used an evaluative rubric to grade the essays. This report takes an evaluative approach to the company's performance. Evaluative feedback helps employees understand their strengths and weaknesses. The study employed evaluative criteria to compare the two programs.

english_meaning: The quality or process of quickly fading, vanishing, or passing away. The condition of lasting for only a very short time. A brief and fleeting existence
example_sentence: The evanescence of youth reminds us to cherish every moment. Poets often write about the evanescence of beauty and time. The evanescence of the morning mist added a mystical charm to the valley. She was fascinated by the evanescence of soap bubbles in sunlight.

english_meaning: Quickly fading, vanishing, or disappearing. Lasting for only a very short time. Fleeting or difficult to hold onto
example_sentence: The evanescent glow of the fireflies disappeared within seconds. Fame can be evanescent, vanishing as quickly as it arrives. She admired the evanescent colors of the sunset before they faded. His evanescent smile revealed a moment of hidden joy.

english_meaning: Relating to a Protestant Christian tradition that emphasizes personal conversion, the authority of the Bible, and spreading the gospel. Relating to the Christian gospel or its teaching. Fervently enthusiastic in advocating a cause or belief. A member of an evangelical Christian church or movement
example_sentence: He belongs to an evangelical church known for its passionate preaching. The reformer spoke with evangelical zeal about environmental protection. Evangelical Christians place strong emphasis on personal faith and scripture. She became an evangelical after joining the local congregation.

english_meaning: A movement within Protestant Christianity emphasizing personal conversion, biblical authority, the saving work of Jesus Christ, and active evangelism. The beliefs and practices associated with evangelical Christians. Fervent advocacy of a cause, by extension
example_sentence: Evangelicalism has played a major role in shaping American religious politics. The rise of evangelicalism led to a renewed focus on personal faith. Evangelicalism emphasizes the importance of spreading the gospel worldwide. Scholars study evangelicalism as a significant force in modern Christianity.

english_meaning: To turn from liquid into vapor. To disappear or cease to exist, especially suddenly. This can refer to a physical process, like water turning into steam, or a more figurative disappearance, such as when a feeling or a problem vanishes.
example_sentence: The water in the puddle evaporated in the sun. Her hopes of winning the lottery evaporated. The morning mist will soon evaporate. His courage seemed to evaporate.

english_meaning: The process by which a liquid changes into a gas or vapour. The gradual disappearance of moisture from a surface into the air. A natural stage of the water cycle in which water rises as vapour. The slow loss or fading away of something such as hope, money, or support. A technique used to remove liquid from a substance in order to concentrate it.
example_sentence: Evaporation from the lake increases sharply during the summer months. The experiment measured the rate of evaporation of salt water. Farmers cover the soil to reduce evaporation of moisture. The evaporation of public support forced the leader to resign.

english_meaning: Avoiding something such as a question, duty, or responsibility. The act of escaping or avoiding a duty, question, rule, or problem, often in a clever or indirect way. It may also refer to avoiding taxes, laws, or responsibilities.
example_sentence: The politician’s answer sounded like evasion rather than a clear response. His constant evasion of responsibility annoyed the whole team. The thief managed evasion by hiding in the crowded market. The government is taking strict action against tax evasion.

english_meaning: Avoiding giving a direct answer or response. A person, reply, or behavior that tries to avoid giving clear or honest information. It often involves indirect answers, changing the topic, or hiding the truth.
example_sentence: He gave an evasive answer when asked about the missing money. The politician remained evasive during the interview. She was evasive about her plans for the future. His evasive behavior made everyone suspicious.

english_meaning: In a way that avoids giving a direct or honest answer. In a manner intended to escape a question, duty, or difficulty. Vaguely and unclearly, so as to hide the truth. In a way that avoids being caught, seen, or confronted. Indirectly and cautiously, without committing to anything.
example_sentence: He answered the reporter's question evasively and quickly changed the subject. She smiled evasively when asked about her future plans. The witness spoke evasively throughout the hearing. The suspect moved evasively through the crowded street.

english_meaning: The day or evening before an important event or festival. Evening before a festival or holiday. A poetic or literary word for evening or the time before night. The beginning of something or the moment before an important change. Also the first woman in the Bible.
example_sentence: The family gathered together on the eve of the festival. The country was on the eve of an important election. Many people attend church services on Christmas Eve. The scientist made a discovery on the eve of his retirement.

english_meaning: Flat, smooth, and level, without bumps or holes. Equal in number, amount, or level. A number that can be divided exactly by two. Used to emphasize something surprising or extreme. To make something level, equal, or smooth.
example_sentence: The floor is smooth and even. The scores were even at the end of the match. Four and six are even numbers. He did not even say goodbye before leaving.

english_meaning: A whole number that can be divided exactly by two with no remainder. Any integer ending in zero, two, four, six, or eight. A number that forms equal pairs when divided into two groups.
synonyms: ["Divisible number","Paired number","Multiple of two","Balanced number","Equal number"]
example_sentence: Eight is an even number because it divides exactly by two. Write down all the even numbers between one and twenty. The houses on this side of the street have even numbers. An even number added to an even number always gives an even number.

english_meaning: Two people or sides are equal, fair, or balanced, especially after an exchange or competition. (When things are Even Steven, there is no advantage or loss for either side. It shows that both are equal in score, situation, or settlement)
example_sentence: After paying him back, we are even steven now. The game ended even steven; both teams scored the same points. She helped me last time, and I helped her today, so we’re even steven. He returned my book, and I gave back his pen, now it’s even steven.

english_meaning: Fair and impartial. Treating all people or sides equally. Not favouring one side over another. Just. Balanced. Used to describe a person, judgment, treatment, or decision that is fair and shows no bias or favouritism toward any individual, group, or point of view, especially in matters of dispute, judgement, or competition.
example_sentence: The judge is known for his evenhanded approach to every case. The newspaper provided an evenhanded report on the political dispute. As a teacher, she is firm but always evenhanded with her students. We need an evenhanded mediator to resolve this conflict. The committee gave an evenhanded review of all the proposals.

english_meaning: The prayer offered in the late afternoon before sunset, known as Asr in Islam. One of the five daily Muslim prayers, performed in the latter part of the day. A prayer said in the evening hours. An act of worship carried out before the sun sets.
example_sentence: He reached home in time for the evening prayer. The evening prayer is offered before the sun goes down. They gathered in the mosque for the evening prayer. She finished her tasks and went for the evening prayer. The evening prayer brought a sense of calm after a busy day.

english_meaning: In a way that is equal in amount, size, or share. Smoothly and regularly, without sudden changes. In a calm and steady manner. Spread out in a uniform way over a surface or area.
example_sentence: Spread the butter evenly over the bread. The work was divided evenly among the team members. She breathed evenly while she slept. The heat is distributed evenly inside the oven.

english_meaning: Occurring or existing at the end of a process or period of time. Taking place or happening at an unspecified later time; ultimate. This is used to describe something that will happen in the end, after a long period, or after a series of events.
example_sentence: The eventual outcome of the negotiations was a success. His hard work led to his eventual promotion. The eventual cost was much higher than expected. It is impossible to predict the eventual winner.

english_meaning: A possible event or situation that may happen in the future. A possible outcome or circumstance that might occur, especially one that people prepare for or consider in planning. It often refers to uncertain situations that could arise later.
example_sentence: The emergency team prepared for every eventuality during the disaster drill. We saved extra funds to deal with any eventuality that might occur. Good planning considers every possible eventuality. The company created backup systems for any technical eventuality.

english_meaning: In the end or after some time. Something that happens after a long delay, effort, or series of events. It shows that the result comes later rather than immediately.
example_sentence: She hopes to get a job on the local newspaper & eventually work for it. After many attempts, she eventually solved the difficult puzzle. The rain continued for hours but it eventually stopped. He worked hard and eventually became a successful doctor. The lost dog eventually found its way back home.

english_meaning: Lasting forever or a very long time. Never coming to an end. It refers to something that is eternal, enduring, and continues indefinitely without fading or stopping.
example_sentence: The lovers promised each other everlasting devotion. We are grateful for his everlasting contribution to our community. Many religions believe in everlasting life after death. She gave him a bouquet of everlasting flowers.

word: Every cloud has a silver lining
english_meaning: Even in difficult or bad situations, there is always something positive or hopeful.
example_sentence: Although she lost her job, she soon realized that every cloud has a silver lining when she found a better opportunity. The accident was terrible, but every cloud has a silver lining, it brought the whole family closer together. He failed his first business, but every cloud has a silver lining, and the experience taught him valuable lessons. The long power outage was frustrating, but every cloud has a silver lining; the neighbors spent time together and built stronger friendships.

english_meaning: Every situation has both good and bad aspects. Nothing in life is completely good or completely bad. Every situation, decision, or person has advantages and disadvantages. We should understand both sides before judging.
synonyms: ["Look at both sides of the picture","Every situation has pros and cons","There are two sides to every story","Nothing is one-sided"]
example_sentence: Losing a job feels bad, but it can also open doors to better opportunities, Every coin has two sides. Social media connects people, but it can also waste time, Every coin has two sides. Moving to a new city is difficult, but it brings new experiences, Every coin has two sides. Exams are stressful, but they help students improve knowledge, Every coin has two sides.

word: Every morsel counts when hunger is real
english_meaning: When someone is genuinely starving or in deep need, even the smallest amount of food or assistance is highly valuable and deeply appreciated. It emphasizes that in times of severe scarcity, extreme poverty, or true necessity, nothing should be wasted and every little bit is profoundly significant.
synonyms: ["Beggars Can't Be Choosers","Every Little Helps","Half A Loaf Is Better Than None","Every Drop Counts","Small Things Matter In Times Of Need"]
example_sentence: During the devastating famine, the relief workers realized that every morsel counts when hunger is real. Please do not waste any food on your plate because every morsel counts when hunger is real. The refugees deeply appreciated the scarce rations distributed to them, proving that every morsel counts when hunger is real. Surviving in the harsh wilderness taught him not to leave behind even crumbs, for every morsel counts when hunger is real. Generations who have survived extreme poverty always teach their children that every morsel counts when hunger is real.

english_meaning: Every small piece, bit, or fragment of something, especially food. The completely consumed or utilized entirety of a given thing, leaving absolutely nothing behind. It is used to emphasize that the whole amount, extent, or portion of something is taken, eaten, or experienced without any waste.
synonyms: ["Every Bit","Every Piece","Every Scrap","Every Crumb","The Entirety","Every Last Drop","Every Fragment","Every Particle","The Whole"]
example_sentence: The hungry child ate every morsel of the food on his plate. She savored every morsel of the delicious chocolate cake. He was determined to finish every morsel of the feast prepared in his honor. The birds picked up every morsel of bread scattered in the garden. They enjoyed every morsel of the meal and left absolutely nothing behind.

english_meaning: To force someone to leave a place, especially property or land. To legally remove a person from property, land, or a building where they are living or staying, usually by order of a landlord or court. It is often used when a tenant fails to pay rent or violates an agreement.
example_sentence: The landlord decided to evict the tenant for not paying rent. The court ordered the authorities to evict the illegal occupants. The company tried to evict the shopkeeper after the contract expired. Heavy floods forced many families to evict their homes temporarily.

english_meaning: The available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true or valid. Information, documents, or objects presented in a court to prove a claim. It is anything that helps to establish or demonstrate the truth of an assertion.
example_sentence: The police found crucial evidence at the crime scene. There is not enough evidence to convict him of the crime. Scientific evidence supports the theory of climate change. She presented her emails as evidence in court.

english_meaning: Something that is clearly seen or easily understood without needing explanation. Clearly visible or noticeable from facts. Leaving no doubt about something. Easily recognized from evidence or situation.
example_sentence: It was evident that he was not ready for the exam. The joy on her face was evident after the result. It became evident that the plan would not work. His experience was evident in the way he handled the situation.

english_meaning: A look believed to cause harm due to jealousy or envy. A belief that a person can cause harm, bad luck, illness, or misfortune to another person simply by looking at them with jealousy, envy, or ill intention. This belief exists in many cultures and is often associated with superstition and folk traditions.
example_sentence: She believes the child fell sick because of the evil eye. Many people wear charms to protect themselves from the evil eye. He avoided talking about his success out of fear of the evil eye. In some cultures, the evil eye is taken very seriously.

english_meaning: The act of removing the internal organs or essential parts of something. The removal of vital or essential parts, either literally, such as organs from a body, or metaphorically, such as weakening or stripping something of its core functions or elements.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed a careful evisceration of the damaged tissue. The book faced evisceration by critics who removed its central arguments. The hurricane caused evisceration of the coastal town’s infrastructure. His speech led to the evisceration of the opponent’s position.

english_meaning: To call forth or summon a spirit, memory, or feeling. To bring back to mind by association. To arouse or evoke a particular emotion or reaction. To recall something from the past.
example_sentence: The old song evocated memories of her childhood. His words evocated deep emotions in the audience. The photograph evocated a sense of nostalgia. The perfume evocated her mother's presence.

english_meaning: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind. Tending to arouse thoughts or emotions vividly. Powerful in producing a mental picture or recollection. Suggestive or reminiscent of something.
example_sentence: The novel contains many evocative descriptions of village life. Her painting is deeply evocative and moving. The music was evocative of a peaceful summer evening. His speech was evocative and inspired the audience.

english_meaning: To bring a feeling, memory, or image into the mind. To cause a memory, feeling, image, or response to come into a person's mind. It is often used when something reminds people of the past or creates a strong emotional reaction.
example_sentence: The music evoked memories of her youth. The story evoked sympathy for the poor family. That song always evokes memories of my school days. The painting evokes the beauty of nature. His words evoked anger among the listeners.

english_meaning: A large, decorative jug or pitcher, usually with a wide spout and handle, used for holding water or other liquids. A vessel, often made of metal, ceramic, or glass, designed for holding and pouring liquids. Traditionally, it has a handle and a spout, and is sometimes used as a decorative item in homes or for ceremonial purposes. Historically, ewers were often paired with basins for washing hands.
example_sentence: The antique ewer on the shelf caught everyone's attention. She poured water from the silver ewer into the basin. The museum displayed a collection of 18th-century ewers. He polished the brass ewer until it gleamed. The daily wash usually involved collecting water in a ewer, heating it, then pouring it into a large basin to be used for scrubbing.

english_meaning: Out of nothing. Created without pre-existing material, especially in philosophical or theological discussion.
example_sentence: Many religious traditions teach that the universe was created ex nihilo. Philosophers have long debated whether anything can truly arise ex nihilo. The theologian explained the doctrine of creation ex nihilo to his students. The artist seemed to create an entire imaginary world ex nihilo.

english_meaning: A metric prefix meaning one quintillion (1018) times the base unit. Used for measuring enormous quantities of data, such as the total digital information in the world. Represented by the symbol E in the International System of Units.
example_sentence: The world's total data is expected to reach hundreds of exabytes soon. An exabyte is one billion gigabytes. Researchers estimate global data creation in exabytes per year. Cloud providers now design systems that scale to exabytes.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,024 petabytes, or about one quintillion bytes. An extremely large measure of data storage. A unit used to describe global internet traffic and very large data centres.
example_sentence: Global internet traffic is now measured in exabytes. One exabyte equals 1,024 petabytes. The company plans to build an exabyte data centre. Scientists collect exabytes of data from space telescopes.

english_meaning: To make something worse or more severe. To aggravate pain or illness. To worsen a conflict or disagreement. To intensify negative emotions such as anger or stress. To increase the intensity, seriousness, or severity of a problem, situation, feeling, or condition. It is often used for negative situations like pain, conflict, or difficulties.
example_sentence: His rude comments exacerbated the situation. Pollution can exacerbate respiratory problems. Stress may exacerbate her illness. The delay only exacerbated their frustration.

english_meaning: The process of making a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse. It refers to an increase in the severity of a disease or its signs and symptoms. It is often used in medical or social contexts to describe a worsening state.
example_sentence: The cold weather led to a sudden exacerbation of his asthma symptoms. Poor communication resulted in an exacerbation of the existing conflict. Doctors are concerned about the frequent exacerbation of the patient's condition. The new policy caused an exacerbation of the social unrest in the city.

english_meaning: Completely accurate and correct in every detail. Precise and not approximate. Strictly careful about details and correctness. To demand and obtain something by force or authority. To inflict something unpleasant such as revenge or punishment. To require effort, time, or skill from someone.
example_sentence: Please tell me the exact time of your arrival. The two copies are exact in every detail. The invaders exacted a terrible price from the city. Surgery exacts great concentration from doctors.

english_meaning: To demand and obtain something from someone, often forcefully. To collect money, taxes, or payment from a person by authority. To force someone to give something such as a promise or confession. To inflict revenge or punishment on someone. To require effort, sacrifice, or obedience from someone.
example_sentence: The king exacted heavy taxes from the poor farmers. She exacted a promise from him that he would return. The gang exacted revenge from their rivals. The training exacts great discipline from every soldier.

english_meaning: In a precise, accurate, or exact manner. In every detail and without any difference. At precisely the stated time, place, amount, or point. Used to confirm complete agreement or that a statement is correct. Used in questions to request precise information.
example_sentence: The train arrived exactly on time. She measured exactly two cups of flour. That is exactly what I meant to say. He copied the design exactly as instructed.

english_meaning: To make something seem larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is. To overemphasize facts. To amplify feelings or reactions. To distort reality for effect. To overstate or stretch the truth. It is often used to emphasize a point, express emotions, or make a story more interesting, but it can also mislead if used improperly.
example_sentence: He tends to exaggerate his achievements in interviews. The fisherman exaggerated the size of the fish he caught. She is not lying, but she often exaggerates small problems. The media sometimes exaggerates news to attract attention.

english_meaning: Represented as larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is. Overstated or magnified beyond the truth. Made to seem greater or more dramatic than the actual reality. Showing or describing something in a way that goes beyond what is reasonable, true, or believable. Excessive or extreme in expression, gesture, or description.
example_sentence: His account of the accident was clearly exaggerated. She gave an exaggerated smile to hide her nervousness. The media often presents exaggerated versions of small incidents. His exaggerated gestures made the audience laugh. The dangers of the journey have been exaggerated in the news.

english_meaning: In a way that represents something as greater, more extreme, or more important than it really is. With overstatement or excessive emphasis. In a manner that goes beyond the truth or normal limits. In an exaggerated, dramatic, or overdone way.
example_sentence: He spoke exaggeratedly about his role in the project. She smiled exaggeratedly to please the photographer. The actor moved exaggeratedly across the stage. He bowed exaggeratedly in front of the audience. The story was told exaggeratedly to entertain the children.

english_meaning: A statement or description that makes something seem larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is. The act of representing something as more extreme than it actually is. An overstatement that goes beyond the truth. A form of expression in which facts are stretched or magnified, often for emphasis or dramatic effect.
example_sentence: His story of the fight was full of exaggeration. To say he is the best player in the world is a slight exaggeration. Without exaggeration, this is the most beautiful place I have ever seen. The advertisement was criticized for its obvious exaggeration. Poets often use exaggeration to create powerful imagery.

english_meaning: To hold someone or something in very high regard or to think or speak very highly of them. It also means to raise someone to a higher rank or a position of greater power. To praise or glorify someone excessively.
example_sentence: The citizens wanted to exalt their leader after the great victory. High-tech firms often exalt innovation above all other corporate values. The poem was written to exalt the beauty of the natural world. He was exalted to the position of chief of staff last year.

english_meaning: A feeling or state of extreme happiness, joy, or elation. The act of raising someone or something to a higher rank, position, power, or dignity. High praise or glorification, especially of God or a noble idea. A state of being elevated in mood or spirit, often spiritual in nature. A group or flock of larks (a poetic collective noun).
example_sentence: The team experienced a sense of exaltation after winning the championship. The hymns are sung in exaltation of the Lord. His exaltation to the position of chief minister surprised many. The pilgrims felt a deep exaltation upon reaching the holy site. The poet described the exaltation of larks rising into the morning sky.

english_meaning: Placed at a high or powerful level or held in high regard. It describes a state of being noble, lofty, or extremely grand. It can also refer to a person's high social or professional rank.
example_sentence: The guest of honor held an exalted rank within the international community. She felt an exalted sense of joy when she finally finished her novel. He spoke in an exalted tone about the future of mankind. Only a few people ever reach such an exalted position in the government.

english_meaning: To inspect something carefully in order to learn about it. To study or consider a subject in detail. To check a person's health as a doctor. To test a student's knowledge formally. To question a witness in a court of law.
example_sentence: The mechanic examined the engine carefully. Researchers examined the effects of the new drug. The doctor examined her and prescribed rest. Students will be examined in three subjects this term.

english_meaning: To irritate or annoy someone intensely. To make a person extremely frustrated or angry. To provoke impatience or exasperation in someone through repeated or persistent behaviour. To cause feelings of deep annoyance, displeasure or vexation, often when patience has already worn thin.
example_sentence: His constant complaints began to exasperate his colleagues. It exasperates me when people arrive late without any apology. The teacher was exasperated by the students' refusal to listen. Slow internet speed exasperates me beyond words. She sighed in an exasperated tone when the meeting was postponed again.

english_meaning: Intensely irritated and frustrated. Feeling immense annoyance, especially when someone is unable to solve a problem or change a situation. It describes a state of having lost one's patience.
example_sentence: The exasperated teacher finally shouted at the noisy class. He let out an exasperated sigh when the computer crashed again. She was totally exasperated by his constant interruptions. The delayed passengers grew increasingly exasperated.

english_meaning: To dig out earth, soil, or rock to uncover something buried. To remove soil, sand, or other material from the ground in order to create a hole or uncover objects such as buildings, fossils, or artifacts. It is often used in construction, mining, and archaeology when digging carefully to reveal hidden things.
example_sentence: In tin mining today, workers excavate tunnels horizontally from a vertical shaft. They excavated an ancient city. Workers excavate the ground to build the foundation of the new school. Archaeologists excavated an ancient temple buried under the sand. The construction company will excavate the area before laying pipes. Scientists carefully excavated the site to find dinosaur bones.

english_meaning: To go beyond a set limit, number, or amount. To be greater or better than something expected. To surpass a standard, rule, or expectation. To perform better than someone or something else. To go past what is allowed, required, or reasonable.
example_sentence: The cost of the project may exceed our initial budget. Her performance exceeded everyone's expectations. Drivers who exceed the speed limit will be fined. The demand for tickets has exceeded the supply.

english_meaning: The quality of being extremely good or outstanding. A very high standard of skill, performance, or achievement. Something in which a person or thing is especially good. A title of honour used to address certain high officials. The state of surpassing ordinary standards in quality.
example_sentence: The school is known for its excellence in science teaching. She received an award for excellence in nursing. They aim for excellence in every product they make. His excellence as a leader was recognized by all.

english_meaning: Extremely good and of the highest quality. Much better than the usual standard. Outstanding in skill, value, or performance. Used to express strong approval of something. Very satisfactory and free from faults.
example_sentence: She did an excellent job on the presentation. The hotel offers excellent service at a fair price. His English is excellent for someone who started last year. Excellent! We can begin the work tomorrow.

english_meaning: Higher, always upward. Fine wood shavings used for packing fragile goods. It is often used as a motto meaning to strive for higher goals or superiority.
example_sentence: The state motto of New York is Excelsior, meaning ever upward. The fragile glass vases were packed safely in excelsior. He shouted excelsior as he reached the mountain peak. The company adopted excelsior as its guiding principle.

english_meaning: Not including; other than. Used to introduce the only thing that does not fit a statement. To exclude someone or something from a group or rule. But; used before stating an exception.
example_sentence: Everyone attended the meeting except Ali. The shop opens daily except on Sundays. I would help you, except that I am busy tonight. Children under five are excepted from the fee.

english_meaning: A person, thing, or case that does not follow the general rule. Something that is different from the usual or expected. An objection or criticism, especially in the phrase 'take exception to'. In law, a formal objection raised against a ruling or statement.
example_sentence: Every rule has an exception. He took exception to my remark about his work. With the exception of John, everyone attended the meeting. This case is an exception to the general policy. The lawyer raised an exception during the trial.

english_meaning: Unusually good or impressive. Not typical or ordinary. Rare or uncommon. Forming an exception to a rule or general pattern. Needing special treatment because of unusual qualities or circumstances.
example_sentence: She has exceptional talent for languages. The school gives extra support to children with exceptional needs. This was an exceptional case and required special approval. His performance in the final match was exceptional.

english_meaning: To an unusually great degree; extremely. In a way that is much better than the normal standard. Only in rare or special cases, as an exception to the usual rule. Remarkably or outstandingly, in a manner that stands out from others.
example_sentence: She is an exceptionally talented young violinist. The summer was exceptionally hot this year. Exceptionally, the office will remain open on Sunday. He performed exceptionally well in the final examination.

english_meaning: An amount of something that is more than necessary, permitted, or desirable. Lack of moderation in eating or drinking.
example_sentence: An excess of sugar in your diet can lead to health problems. The airline charged her for the excess weight of her luggage. He lived a life of excess and eventually ran out of money. The company had to trim the excess staff to remain profitable.

english_meaning: Much more than is necessary, normal, or reasonable. Going beyond acceptable or proper limits. Too great in amount, degree, or intensity. Immoderate in behaviour, spending, or demand.
example_sentence: The company was criticised for its excessive charges. Excessive rainfall damaged crops across the region. He suffers from headaches caused by excessive screen time. The court found the punishment excessive for such a minor offence.

english_meaning: To a degree that is far greater than necessary or reasonable. In an immoderate or extreme manner. More than is proper, healthy, or acceptable. Beyond the usual or permitted limit.
example_sentence: He worries excessively about small mistakes. The room was excessively hot during the afternoon. She was criticised for spending excessively on decorations. The instructions were excessively long and difficult to follow.

english_meaning: An act of giving one thing and receiving another in return. A short conversation or an argument between two or more people. The process of changing one currency for another. A place where stocks and shares are traded. To part with for some equivalent value.
example_sentence: They had a friendly exchange of ideas during the meeting. I would like to exchange this shirt for a larger size. The stock exchange saw a significant drop in prices today. We had a brief exchange regarding the new project details.

english_meaning: Able to be exchanged for something else. Capable of being traded, swapped, or returned. Suitable for conversion into another form or currency. Replaceable by an equivalent item.
example_sentence: This voucher is exchangeable at any branch. Sale items are not exchangeable after seven days. The tokens are exchangeable for cash prizes. These notes are freely exchangeable for foreign currency.

english_meaning: The act of cutting something out, especially by surgery. The removal of a part of a text, film, or record. In biology, the cutting out of a section of DNA or tissue.
example_sentence: The surgeon recommended excision of the small tumour. The excision of that scene shortened the film. Excision of the damaged tissue was successful. Editors defended the excision of several paragraphs.

english_meaning: The quality of becoming excited or emotionally stirred very easily. A tendency to react quickly and strongly to stimulation. In biology, the ability of a cell or tissue to respond to a stimulus.
example_sentence: His excitability makes him a lively companion. The doctor noted the excitability of the patient's nerves. Excitability increases when people are short of sleep. She controlled her excitability during the interview.

english_meaning: Easily made enthusiastic, nervous, or emotionally stirred. Tending to react strongly to small events. Responsive to stimulation, as in nerves or cells.
example_sentence: He is an excitable child who talks very fast. The excitable crowd cheered every shot. She becomes excitable when she drinks too much tea. Nerve cells are highly excitable tissues.

english_meaning: To make someone feel very enthusiastic, eager, or emotionally stirred. To cause a particular feeling or reaction to arise. To stimulate a physical or chemical activity. To arouse interest or curiosity in something.
example_sentence: The idea of studying abroad excites her. His speech excited the crowd. The discovery excited great interest among scientists. Loud noises can excite young children before bedtime.

english_meaning: In a very enthusiastic and eager manner. With a high level of energy, joy, or anticipation. It describes actions done while feeling thrilled about something that is happening or will happen.
example_sentence: The children excitedly opened their birthday presents. She excitedly told her friends about her new job. The fans cheered excitedly as the band took the stage. He excitedly pointed out the rare bird to his son.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of enthusiasm and eagerness. A state of being emotionally stirred or lively. An event or situation that causes such feelings. Increased activity or agitation in a person or place.
example_sentence: There was great excitement before the final match. She could hardly hide her excitement about the trip. The news created excitement across the whole village. In his excitement, he forgot to lock the door.

english_meaning: Causing strong feelings of interest, enthusiasm, or pleasure. Full of activity, energy, or thrilling events. Likely to make someone eager and emotionally stirred.
example_sentence: It was the most exciting game of the season. She has an exciting new job in Karachi. The film has an exciting opening scene. Travelling alone can be both exciting and difficult.

english_meaning: In a way that causes excitement, interest, or enthusiasm. So as to make something thrilling or full of energy. In a manner that stirs strong positive feelings.
example_sentence: The match ended excitingly in the final minute. The project developed excitingly fast. She spoke excitingly about her new business. The story begins slowly but ends excitingly.

english_meaning: To cry out suddenly and loudly because of strong emotion. To say something quickly and with feeling, especially surprise or anger. To declare something forcefully in speech.
example_sentence: "What a beautiful garden!" she exclaimed. He exclaimed in pain when the door hit his hand. The children exclaimed with delight at the snow. She exclaimed that the news could not be true.

english_meaning: A sudden cry or remark expressing surprise, anger, joy, or pain. A word or phrase spoken loudly and with strong feeling. In grammar, a sentence that expresses emotion and often ends with an exclamation mark.
example_sentence: He gave an exclamation of surprise when he saw the bill. Her exclamation startled everyone in the room. The teacher explained the use of the exclamation mark. A loud exclamation came from the back of the hall.

english_meaning: A part of a country that is separated from the main territory and surrounded by foreign land. A portion of a state that is geographically separated from the main part of that state and is surrounded by the territory of one or more other states. It remains politically connected to the parent country but is physically cut off.
example_sentence: Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave pinched between Poland and Lithuania. Yes, the exclave is a Russian base inside NATO’s borders. Alaska is an exclave of the United States because it is separated from the main country by Canada. Kaliningrad Oblast is an exclave of Russia located between Poland and Lithuania. The village functioned as an exclave after the border agreement divided the region. Traveling to the exclave required passing through another country.

english_meaning: The act of leaving someone or something out. The action of keeping someone or something out of a group, place, activity, or opportunity. It may happen intentionally through rules or decisions, or unintentionally through social, economic, or cultural barriers.
example_sentence: The exclusion of poor communities from education creates social inequality. His name appeared on the guest list, so his exclusion from the event surprised everyone. The policy caused the exclusion of many small farmers from financial support. Social exclusion can lead to poverty and lack of opportunities.

english_meaning: A person or policy that favors excluding certain people or groups from a place, society, or privilege. Someone who supports keeping others out based on race, class, or other criteria. It refers to discriminatory practices or mindsets.
example_sentence: The politician was criticized for his exclusionist immigration policies. Exclusionist attitudes can deeply divide a community. The club had an exclusionist entry policy that angered many. He argued against the exclusionist laws of the era.

english_meaning: Restricted to a particular person, group, or thing, not shared. Something available only to a specific group or individual, not open to everyone. It can also mean high-quality, luxurious, or special. In media, it can refer to a news story or report obtained or published by only one source.
example_sentence: The hotel has exclusive access to the beach. This room is for the exclusive use of guests. We feature an exclusive on the mothers whose babies were swapped at birth. The paper printed a world exclusive on the presidential scandal.

english_meaning: Only. Limited to a particular person, group, or purpose. Used to indicate that something is restricted to a single person, group, or thing and not shared with others. It emphasizes uniqueness or sole rights.
example_sentence: This room is reserved exclusively for VIP guests. The offer is available exclusively online. She writes exclusively about environmental issues. The club admits men exclusively.

english_meaning: To criticise someone or something very severely and harshly. To damage or remove part of the skin by abrasion or chemical action. To strip or remove the skin or surface layer from something.
example_sentence: The reviewer excoriated the film for its poor writing and lack of originality. The report excoriated the management for its handling of the crisis. She excoriated the policy in a strongly worded article published the following morning. The skin had been excoriated by the rough fabric worn for hours without protection.

english_meaning: To cause great physical or mental pain. To torture. To torment. To inflict severe suffering. Used for situations, illnesses, or experiences that cause extreme agony, anguish, or distress, whether of the body or of the mind. It emphasizes pain that is intense, prolonged, and very hard to bear.
example_sentence: The injury continued to excruciate him for many weeks. The thought of failure excruciated her every night. The dentist's treatment excruciated the poor patient. Long hours of waiting excruciated the parents of the missing child. The harsh memories excruciated him in his old age.

english_meaning: To clear someone from blame or guilt. To declare a person free from accusation. To prove someone innocent of wrongdoing. To absolve from a charge or fault. Often used in legal and formal contexts when evidence, testimony, or investigation shows that a person was not responsible for an offence.
example_sentence: New evidence exculpated the accused after years in prison. The witness’s statement helped exculpate him from the charges. The report exculpates the company of any wrongdoing. She tried to exculpate her brother by taking the blame herself. The court refused to exculpate the officer involved in the incident.

english_meaning: Tending to clear someone from fault or guilt. Describing evidence or statements that prove a defendant's innocence. It is often used in a legal sense regarding facts that justify or excuse an accused person's actions.
example_sentence: The defense attorney requested all exculpatory evidence from the prosecution. Exculpatory clauses in the contract shielded the company from lawsuits. The witness provided a crucial exculpatory statement. Withholding exculpatory evidence is a serious violation of legal ethics.

english_meaning: A short journey taken away from one's usual place, usually for enjoyment, education, exploration, or a particular activity. It can also mean a sudden movement into a different area, subject, or activity.
example_sentence: Our school arranged an excursion to the museum. They went on a weekend excursion to the hills. The teacher allowed a short excursion into a related topic during the lecture. The boat made a brief excursion across the river.

english_meaning: Extremely bad or unpleasant. Deserving of hate or being detested due to its inferior quality or moral corruption. It is used to describe something of the poorest quality imaginable.
example_sentence: The food at the roadside diner was absolutely execrable and nearly inedible. He was criticized for his execrable behavior toward his younger colleagues. The film received poor reviews due to its execrable script and wooden acting. Living conditions in the overcrowded camp were described as execrable.

english_meaning: To carry out or put a plan, order, or course of action into effect. To perform a task or skill with competence. To put someone to death as a legal punishment. To complete and make a legal document valid by signing it. To run a computer program or command. To produce a work of art or design.
example_sentence: The team executed the plan perfectly. The gymnast executed a flawless routine. The prisoner was executed at dawn. The will was executed in the presence of two witnesses.

english_meaning: To enforce a court judgment by seizing someone's property or assets. To carry out a legal claim against a debtor. To complete a trade or order against another party's offer. To run a program or test against a particular set of data or system. To carry out a plan in opposition to a rival or target.
example_sentence: The creditor obtained permission to execute against the debtor's house. The judgment was executed against the company's bank accounts. The broker executed the order against the best available price. We executed the tests against the live database.

english_meaning: To carry out or deliver on a plan, strategy, or promise. To put ideas into practical action successfully. To act effectively on an opportunity or goal. To enforce a legal judgment on property or assets. To run a command or process on a particular system or device.
example_sentence: The new manager quickly executed on her growth strategy. Having a great idea is useless if you cannot execute on it. The company failed to execute on its promises to customers. The script executes on the main server every night.

english_meaning: To carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or decision. To enforce a legal judgment upon a person's property. To carry out a death sentence on someone. To act on an instruction or command. To perform a task upon a particular object or system.
example_sentence: The officers executed upon the warrant without delay. The court's order was executed upon his land and property. The sentence was executed upon the traitor. The software executes upon receiving a user command.

english_meaning: A senior person responsible for managing an organisation or part of it. The branch of government that puts laws into effect. Relating to the management or administration of an organisation. Having the power to make decisions and put plans into action. Designed for or suited to senior managers, often meaning high quality or expensive.
example_sentence: She was promoted to a senior executive at the age of thirty. The executive must implement the laws passed by parliament. He booked an executive suite for the two-day conference. The board gave the manager full executive authority over the project.

english_meaning: Critical explanations or interpretations of a text, especially a religious one. It refers to the plural form of analysis intended to uncover the deeper meaning of a scripture or literature. It involves a systematic examination to clarify the author's original intent. (plural of exegesis).
example_sentence: The professor provided several exegeses of the ancient manuscript. Her exegeses focused on the historical context of the parables. Students were required to write two exegeses on different biblical passages. These diverse exegeses offer unique perspectives on the poem.

english_meaning: A detailed explanation or critical interpretation of a text, typically a legal or religious document. It is the process of drawing out the meaning from a text rather than reading one's own ideas into it. This singular term denotes a formal analysis to clarify complex passages.
example_sentence: He published a brilliant exegesis of the new constitutional amendment. The scholar spent years on the exegesis of the sacred scrolls. A clear exegesis helps the audience understand the subtle nuances of the text. The minister provided an exegesis of the Sunday gospel.

english_meaning: Serving as a desirable model. Representing the best of its kind. It describes behavior or quality that is so good that it deserves to be imitated or praised. Sometimes it means a warning example.
example_sentence: His exemplary behavior in class earned him the student of the month award. The company received an award for its exemplary customer service. The general was honored for his exemplary leadership during the crisis. The judge imposed exemplary damages to deter future offenses.

english_meaning: Free from an obligation, duty, or liability imposed on others. Not subject to a particular rule, tax, or requirement. To officially release someone from a duty or payment. To excuse someone from a rule that applies to others. A person who is freed from a duty, especially from paying tax.
example_sentence: Medicines are exempt from this new tax. The government exempted farmers from paying the fee this year. Her disability exempts her from certain duties. He is an exempt employee and does not receive overtime pay.

english_meaning: Free from a duty, rule, or payment that applies to others. Not required to do or pay something. Officially excused from a requirement or law. To release someone from an obligation or liability. To free someone from being affected by a rule or penalty.
synonyms: ["Free from","Excused from","Immune to","Spared from","Released from","Absolved from","Excluded from","Relieved of","Excuse","Release"]
antonyms: ["Liable to","Subject to","Responsible for","Bound by","Obliged to","Answerable to","Exposed to","Accountable for"]
example_sentence: Basic food items are exempt from sales tax. Senior citizens are exempt from the entry fee. The new rule exempts small farms from inspection. Nobody is exempt from the law.

english_meaning: Freedom from an obligation, duty, or liability that others must meet. Official permission not to follow a rule or pay a charge. An amount of income that is not subject to tax. The state of being excused from a requirement. Special privilege granted to a person or group.
example_sentence: Charities often receive a tax exemption. She applied for an exemption from the final exam due to illness. The law grants an exemption to small businesses. No exemption will be made for latecomers.

english_meaning: Freedom from a particular duty, rule, tax, or requirement. Official release from having to do or pay something. The right not to be subject to a specific law or obligation. Permission to be excused from a task or test. Protection from a penalty or responsibility.
example_sentence: He was granted exemption from military service. Students with medical reasons may seek exemption from sports. The factory received an exemption from import duties. Diplomats enjoy exemption from local taxes.

english_meaning: To apply or bring into use a force, influence, pressure, or quality. To make a strong physical or mental effort in order to achieve something. To use one's power, authority, or skill in an active and deliberate way. To put pressure on someone or something in order to produce a particular result. To tire or strain oneself through hard and continuous effort.
example_sentence: He had to exert considerable pressure on the lever to open the door. The senator continues to exert great influence over the committee. She exerted herself to finish the project before the deadline. Try not to exert yourself too much while recovering from the illness.

english_meaning: The process of removing dead cells from the surface of the skin. The natural shedding of the outer layer of skin. A cosmetic treatment that cleanses and renews the skin. The peeling off of rock, bark, or skin in layers.
example_sentence: Regular exfoliation makes the skin smoother and brighter. The spa offers a full-body exfoliation treatment. Exfoliation helps remove dry and dead skin cells. Geologists study the exfoliation of large rocks.

english_meaning: The process or action of exhaling or breathing out. That which is breathed out or emitted, such as air, vapor, or scent. It refers to the expulsion of air from the lungs.
example_sentence: With a long exhalation, she finally relaxed her tense shoulders. During yoga, focus on making your exhalation longer than your inhalation. The cold air turned his exhalation into a visible cloud of vapor. The exhalation of toxic gases from the factory is strictly monitored.

english_meaning: To breathe out air from the lungs. To emit or give off vapor, smoke, or a smell. It is the necessary respiratory counterpart to inhaling.
example_sentence: He took a deep puff of his cigarette and exhaled slowly. Try to inhale through your nose and exhale through your mouth. The machine exhaled a continuous plume of black smoke. She exhaled a sigh of relief when she heard the good news.

english_meaning: To make somebody feel very tired. To use all of something so that there is none left. To talk about or study a subject until there is nothing else to say about it. Waste gases that come out of a vehicle, an engine or a machine.
example_sentence: Even a short walk exhausted her. There's no need to exhaust yourself clearing up, we'll do it. Within three days they had exhausted their supply of food. I think we've exhausted that particular topic. My car needs a new exhaust.

english_meaning: Capable of being used up or depleted; not infinite in supply. Describing a resource or thing that can eventually run out.
example_sentence: Oil is an exhaustible resource that will eventually run out. The company's exhaustible supply of materials caused production delays. Unlike solar energy, coal is exhaustible. Human patience, while great, is not inexhaustible.

english_meaning: Examining, including, or considering all elements or aspects. Fully comprehensive and thorough. It implies leaving nothing out and researching a topic to the absolute limits.
example_sentence: The police conducted an exhaustive search of the surrounding woods. She read an exhaustive study on the impacts of global warming. The manual provides an exhaustive list of all product features. After an exhaustive investigation, the cause of the fire was discovered.

english_meaning: To publicly display a work of art, item of interest, or particular behavior. An object or collection of objects shown in a public space. A document or object presented as evidence in a court.
example_sentence: The museum will exhibit the new dinosaur fossils next month. The lawyer presented the bloody shirt as Exhibit A. Despite his fear, he managed to exhibit great courage. Over fifty artists will exhibit their paintings at the fair.

english_meaning: To make someone feel very happy, animated, or elated. To thrill or invigorate someone immensely. It implies a strong rush of joy, energy, and excitement.
example_sentence: The fast rollercoaster ride exhilarates the young children. The crisp mountain air never fails to exhilarate me. She was exhilarated by her sudden and unexpected success. Winning the championship game exhilarated the entire town.

english_meaning: Feeling very happy, lively, and full of energy. Filled with excitement and joy after an experience. Refreshed and uplifted in spirit. Thrilled by something enjoyable or successful. Emotionally raised to a state of delight.
example_sentence: She felt exhilarated after her morning run. The climbers were exhilarated when they reached the top. He was exhilarated by the roar of the crowd. We came home tired but exhilarated.

english_meaning: To strongly urge or encourage someone to do something. To advise earnestly and persistently. To address with stirring words in order to motivate or inspire action. To appeal urgently for a particular course of behaviour.
example_sentence: The leader exhorted his followers to remain united. The coach exhorted his players to give their best in the final match. She exhorted the students to study with full dedication. The speaker exhorted the audience to vote in large numbers. He exhorted them never to lose hope.

english_meaning: An address or speech that strongly encourages or urges someone to take a particular course of action. A statement intended to inspire, motivate, or persuade someone toward improvement or effort. An earnest appeal or warning, often delivered with passion or moral urgency. The act of urging or advising someone strongly to do something.
example_sentence: The coach's exhortation before the final match inspired the entire team to give their best effort.  Her exhortation to study harder fell on deaf ears.  The preacher's exhortation moved many members of the congregation to tears.  Despite repeated exhortations from his parents, he refused to change his habits.  The general's exhortation rallied the troops before the battle.

english_meaning: To remove a dead body from a grave, usually for legal or scientific reasons. To revive or bring to public attention something that was forgotten, hidden, or suppressed.
example_sentence: The police decided to exhume the body to investigate the cause of death. Historians exhumed old letters to learn about the era. Archaeologists exhumed artifacts from the ancient tomb. He tried to exhume memories he had long forgotten.

english_meaning: An urgent need or demand. A situation that requires immediate action or attention. It refers to a sudden unforeseen crisis or an pressing requirement of a particular circumstance.
example_sentence: The government declared a state of emergency due to the exigency of the flood. Economic exigencies forced the company to lay off workers. He acted swiftly, completely understanding the exigency of the matter. The general modified his plans to meet the exigencies of warfare.

english_meaning: Very small in amount or size; insufficient. Something extremely limited, scanty, or meager. Often used to describe resources, quantities, or space that are barely adequate or almost negligible.
example_sentence: The evidence against him was exiguous, making the case weak. She lived on an exiguous income, barely covering her expenses. The exiguous rainfall this year has affected crops severely. His knowledge of the subject was exiguous, but he tried to answer confidently.

english_meaning: To send someone away from their native land. Forced removal from one's country or home. A situation where a person is sent away from their homeland by authority or chooses to live away from it for political or personal reasons. It can also refer to the person who is forced to live outside their country.
example_sentence: The king ordered the exile of the rebel leader from the kingdom. After the political conflict, the writer lived in exile for many years. The government decided to exile the traitor to a distant island. Many artists created powerful works while living in exile. Musharaf wants exiled leader to stay away.

english_meaning: To be real or present in the world. To live, especially under difficult conditions. To continue to be or remain in a particular state. To occur or be found.
example_sentence: Do you believe ghosts exist? Many families exist on very little income. Such customs still exist in remote villages. The problem existed long before he arrived.

english_meaning: The state or fact of being real or alive. The continued state of living or being present. A particular way of living. The occurrence or presence of something.
example_sentence: Scientists debated the existence of water on the planet. They led a quiet existence in the mountains. The company came into existence in 1985. He questioned the existence of such a rule.

english_meaning: Having reality or being. Existing now or at a stated time. Present, actual, or currently in force. A thing or being that exists, in philosophical usage.
example_sentence: No existent record supports that claim. The species is still existent in a few remote valleys. Philosophers ask whether every existent thing has a cause. The policy remains existent but is rarely enforced.

english_meaning: Relating to existence or the fact of being alive. Concerning the nature, meaning, or purpose of human existence. Associated with existentialism, which emphasizes freedom, choice, responsibility, and individual experience. So serious or fundamental that it threatens survival, identity, or continued existence. Arising from deep anxiety about death, freedom, isolation, or meaninglessness.
example_sentence: She began asking existential questions about the purpose of her life. Climate change presents an existential threat to many island nations. The novel explores existential anxiety and personal freedom. Losing the family business created an existential crisis for him.

english_meaning: A philosophy emphasizing individual freedom, choice, and personal responsibility in a seemingly meaningless world. The theory that humans are free and responsible for their own actions in a world without meaning.
example_sentence: Jean-Paul Sartre is one of the most famous writers on existentialism. Existentialism teaches that we must create our own meaning in life. The novel explores existentialism through a character facing moral dilemmas. Existentialism often deals with themes of death, freedom, and isolation.

english_meaning: A person who studies or believes in existentialism, emphasizing individual choice, responsibility, and creating one’s own purpose in life. Thoughts, actions, or works that reflect existentialist philosophy, focusing on freedom, choice, and the search for meaning.
example_sentence: Jean-Paul Sartre was a famous existentialist. She identifies as an existentialist in her philosophy. Many existentialists question traditional moral values. His existentialist writings explore human freedom. The novel has existentialist themes about choice and responsibility. She gave an existentialist perspective on life’s uncertainties.

english_meaning: In a way that concerns existence, especially human existence and its meaning. From the perspective of existentialism. At the deepest level of identity, purpose, or survival. With anxiety arising from freedom, mortality, isolation, or meaninglessness.
example_sentence: Existentially, the character feels trapped by the choices before her. The long period of isolation affected him existentially. The company was existentially threatened by the sudden loss of funding. She felt existentially unsettled after questioning her long-held beliefs.

english_meaning: A mass departure of people, especially emigrants. A large-scale movement of individuals leaving a particular place. Commonly refers to the biblical departure of the Israelites from Egypt.
example_sentence: The war caused a massive exodus of refugees across the border. There is a continuous exodus of young people from rural villages to cities. After the concert, an exodus of fans flooded the streets. The economic crisis triggered a brain drain and exodus of professionals.

english_meaning: To clear from a charge of wrongdoing or to release someone from a duty or obligation. To state officially that someone is not to blame. It completely removes the burden of guilt.
example_sentence: The DNA results will exonerate him completely. The official inquiry was able to exonerate the officers involved. She felt a huge relief when the court exonerated her. They were exonerated from entirely paying the heavy fine due to their age.

english_meaning: The official clearing of someone from blame or criminal charges. The act of declaring or proving that a person is not guilty.
example_sentence: His exoneration came after twenty years in prison for a crime he didn't commit. The DNA evidence led to his exoneration. She celebrated her exoneration with tears of relief. The court ordered his exoneration after new evidence emerged.

english_meaning: Too high, unreasonable, or excessive in amount or price. Something that goes far beyond what is fair, reasonable, or expected, usually referring to prices, demands, or fees. It often carries a negative sense, implying unfairness or greed.
example_sentence: The hotel charged an exorbitant amount for a single night. Many people complained about the exorbitant price of fuel. He demanded an exorbitant fee for his simple advice. The cost of education has become exorbitant for most families.

english_meaning: In a way that is unreasonably or excessively high, especially in price or amount. To a degree that goes far beyond what is fair, normal, or acceptable. In an extravagant or immoderate manner. Excessively, beyond proper limits.
example_sentence: The hotel charged us exorbitantly for a small room. Medicines are being sold exorbitantly in that pharmacy. The lawyer was paid exorbitantly for the case. Some shops price their goods exorbitantly during festivals.

english_meaning: The act of adorning or decorating. An embellishment or decoration, specifically relating to elevated or highly decorated speech and writing. It represents an intricate aesthetic addition.
example_sentence: The poet's liberal use of exornation made his work difficult to understand for laymen. The grand ballroom was filled with beautiful exornations for the royal gala. His speech lacked exornation but delivered a powerful, blunt message. Classical rhetoric highly valued the exornation of persuasive arguments.

english_meaning: Clear, public, easily understandable. Information or ideas that are not hidden or secret. Knowledge that is applied or understandable without specialized training. Intended for or likely to be understood by the general public.
example_sentence: The professor gave an exoteric lecture so that all students could follow the main ideas. The book contains both esoteric theories and exoteric explanations for beginners. Her writing style is highly exoteric, making complex concepts simple for everyone. Many religions have both exoteric teachings for followers and esoteric teachings for initiates.

english_meaning: A process, reaction, or change that releases heat energy to its surroundings. Any physical or chemical change that gives off heat, light, or energy to the surrounding environment. During an exothermic reaction, the products have less energy than the reactants because some energy is released. Common examples include combustion, respiration, and many oxidation reactions.
example_sentence: The burning of wood is an exothermic reaction because it releases heat and light. Human respiration is an exothermic process that produces energy for the body. The reaction between fuel and oxygen in an engine is highly exothermic. Hand warmers work through an exothermic chemical reaction that generates heat.

english_meaning: Originating from or characteristic of a distant foreign country. Strikingly unusual or strange in appearance or effect. Attractive or exciting because of being unfamiliar. Not native to the place where found. Colorfully unusual and intriguing.
example_sentence: The market was full of exotic fruits from Asia. She wore an exotic dress at the party. They traveled to many exotic destinations. He keeps exotic birds as pets.

english_meaning: The quality of being strikingly unusual, foreign, or colourful. The charm or appeal of things that come from distant places. A style in art, music, or literature that draws on foreign cultures. Fascination with what seems strange and far away.
example_sentence: The exoticism of the market attracted many tourists. Her paintings are admired for their exoticism and bright colours. Critics noted the exoticism in the composer's later works. There is a certain exoticism about the island's cuisine.

english_meaning: To become or make something larger in size, number, or importance. To spread out or increase in volume. To develop a business or activity into new areas. To give a fuller account of something.
example_sentence: Metals expand when they are heated. The firm plans to expand into overseas markets. He expanded his notes into a full research paper. The city has expanded rapidly over the last decade.

english_meaning: To give more details about something already mentioned. To explain an idea more fully. To develop a point further in speech or writing. To add extra information to a brief statement.
example_sentence: Could you expand on your last point for the class? The author expands on this theme in the second chapter. She refused to expand on her earlier comments. I would like you to expand on the reasons behind this decision.

english_meaning: To provide a fuller explanation of something already stated. To discuss a topic in greater depth. To add further detail or reasoning to an argument. A slightly more formal form of the phrase expand on.
example_sentence: The minister was asked to expand upon his proposal. He expanded upon the theory in his final lecture. The report expands upon findings published last year. She declined to expand upon the details of the agreement.

english_meaning: Capable of being made larger in size, amount, or capacity. Able to increase or be increased when needed. Describing equipment or software that can accept additional parts or features. Able to spread out or grow in volume.
example_sentence: The laptop comes with expandable memory. We chose an expandable travel bag for the long trip. The seating area is expandable for larger events. Their business model is easily expandable to new cities.

english_meaning: The act or process of becoming larger in size, number, or extent. Growth of a business, city, or economy into new areas. An increase in volume caused by heat or pressure. A part added to something to make it bigger or more complete.
example_sentence: The company announced a major expansion into Asia. Thermal expansion can cause cracks in concrete. Rapid urban expansion has increased traffic problems. The library's expansion added two new reading halls.

english_meaning: A person living outside their native country. A foreign resident (short form of expatriate). A person temporarily or permanently living abroad. Someone settled outside their homeland.  A person who lives or works in a country other than the one where they were born or hold citizenship. It is often used for people who move abroad for jobs, business, or lifestyle reasons.
example_sentence: Many expats move to Dubai for better job opportunities. He works as an expat engineer in Germany. The city has a large expat community from different countries. She enjoys the expat lifestyle in Spain.

english_meaning: A person living outside their native country. A citizen working abroad. A person who has chosen to live outside their homeland.
