example_sentence: This case falls under the category of fraud. This topic falls under the subject of psychology. His actions fall under criminal behavior. The city falls under federal jurisdiction. Many young people fall under the influence of social media.

english_meaning: To attack suddenly or violently. To turn one’s attention to something suddenly. To come upon or happen to someone unexpectedly (for example a burden or duty). To start eating something eagerly.
example_sentence: The soldiers fell upon the enemy camp at night. The responsibility of caring for the family fell upon his shoulders. The hungry travelers fell upon the food as soon as it arrived. His eyes fell upon an old photograph on the table.

english_meaning: A mistaken belief, especially one based on wrong reasoning. A false or misleading argument that seems logical but is not. A common wrong idea widely accepted by people. An error in thinking that leads to an incorrect conclusion. A deceptive or unsound argument used in debate or discussion.
example_sentence: It is a common fallacy that money brings happiness. His argument was based on a logical fallacy. The idea that only rich people are successful is a fallacy. Many people believe this fallacy without questioning it.

english_meaning: Capable of making mistakes. Describes a person, system, or belief that is not perfect and can be wrong or make errors
example_sentence: Even experienced doctors are fallible and can make mistakes. Humans are fallible, which is why learning never stops. The plan failed because it was designed by fallible judgment. He admitted that his memory is fallible under pressure.

english_meaning: One of the two tubes that carry eggs from the ovaries to the uterus. The passage in which fertilisation of the egg usually takes place. A tube lined with tiny hairs that move the egg along. A structure that may become blocked and cause infertility.
example_sentence: The egg travels to the uterus through the fallopian tube. Fertilisation usually happens inside the fallopian tube. A blocked fallopian tube can make pregnancy difficult. An ectopic pregnancy may develop in the fallopian tube.

english_meaning: The negative results or consequences of an event or action. The side effects, aftereffects, or repercussions following an event, especially one that is harmful or controversial. It can also literally mean radioactive particles that settle after a nuclear explosion.
example_sentence: The political scandal caused widespread fallout within the party. Many people were affected by the economic fallout of the pandemic. Scientists measured the radioactive fallout after the test. The decision had serious fallout for the local community.

english_meaning: To fail to keep up with others in progress, work, or performance. To move slower than others, fail to make progress at the same rate, or not complete something on time.
example_sentence: He fell behind in rent. The runner fell behind the group. She fell behind in her studies after being sick for a month. If you don’t practice regularly, you’ll fall behind the others. The company fell behind on its payments. He fell behind because he didn’t understand the new topic.

english_meaning: An act that is done to mislead people by making it appear that someone else did it. A deceptive action in which a person, group, or country carries out an act but makes it look as if another person, group, or country is responsible. This term is often used in politics, war, intelligence, media discussion, and security matters. Its purpose is usually to confuse people, create blame, justify retaliation, or gain support for a certain action.
example_sentence: The analyst warned that the attack might be a false flag intended to blame a rival group. Some historians study whether certain incidents were planned as false flag operations. The report found no evidence that the event was a false flag. Spreading unverified claims about a false flag can create confusion and fear.

english_meaning: The act of wrongly attributing a fault, crime, or bad quality to someone without justification. A baseless accusation or charge made against a person. Falsely blaming someone for something they did not do. An untrue statement that damages someone's reputation by charging them with wrongdoing.
example_sentence: He was deeply hurt by the false imputation against his honesty. The false imputation ruined her reputation in the community. The court dismissed the case as a false imputation. Making a false imputation about someone can lead to legal action. He filed a complaint over the false imputation of theft.

english_meaning: A statement that is not true; a lie. The state of being untrue or dishonest. The practice of telling lies. Untruthfulness in general. A misleading impression.
example_sentence: He was punished for spreading a dangerous falsehood. Do not build your success on falsehood. There is not a shred of truth in this falsehood. Children should be taught to avoid falsehood.

english_meaning: To make false or incorrect. To lie about or alter information. To deliberately alter information, documents, or facts to make them untrue or misleading. It can also mean misrepresenting the truth in statements, records, or evidence.
example_sentence: He tried to falsify his academic records to get the job. The company was accused of falsifying financial statements. She falsified her signature on the contract. Politicians sometimes falsify data to support their claims.

english_meaning: The state of being known or talked about by many people, especially on account of notable achievements. The condition of having a widespread reputation. Public eminence or celebrity. Distinguishing glory or renown that follows a person or action. A state of being widely honored and acclaimed.
example_sentence: The young actor achieved international fame almost overnight. She went to Hollywood in search of fame and fortune. His fame as a great surgeon spread throughout the country. Fame can be a double-edged sword for those who are not prepared for the lack of privacy. The writer's fame rests primarily on her final novel published posthumously.

english_meaning: Well known from long or close association. Easily recognized because it has been seen or heard before. Having a good knowledge of something. Friendly and informal in manner, sometimes too much so. A spirit or animal believed to serve a witch.
example_sentence: His face looked familiar but I could not recall his name. She is familiar with the rules of the game. The old song brought back familiar memories. He became too familiar with his seniors at work.

english_meaning: A writing style, alphabet, or set of characters that someone already knows or recognizes. Something written in a way that feels ordinary, known, or understandable. Can also be used figuratively for a “pattern” or “narrative” someone has seen before.
example_sentence: The old manuscript was written in a familiar script, so the historian could easily read it. Children learn faster when they read in a familiar script before moving to new styles. The letter was in a familiar script, reminding me of my grandmother’s handwriting. For Urdu speakers, Nastaliq is the most familiar script compared to Roman Urdu.

english_meaning: Close knowledge or understanding of something gained through experience. The state of being well known or easily recognized. A relaxed and friendly relationship between people. Behaviour that is too informal or over-friendly for the occasion.
example_sentence: Her familiarity with the software impressed the interviewers. There was an easy familiarity between the old friends. He spoke to his manager with surprising familiarity. Familiarity with local customs makes travel much easier.

english_meaning: The process of making oneself or someone else familiar with something. Training or instruction given so that a person becomes comfortable with a task or place. The act of getting to know something thoroughly.
example_sentence: New staff attend a two-day familiarization course. Pilots complete familiarization flights before carrying passengers. The tour offered a quick familiarization with the campus. Familiarization with the equipment reduces accidents.

english_meaning: To make someone well acquainted with something. To learn about or make oneself aware of the details of something. To give knowledge or understanding of a subject. To accustom someone to a new place, task, or situation. To bring into common use.
example_sentence: The teacher familiarized the students with the new syllabus. You should familiarize yourself with the safety rules first. New employees are familiarized with the office system. She quickly familiarized herself with the software.

english_meaning: A severe shortage of food that causes widespread hunger and suffering among people, often due to drought, war, crop failure, or economic crisis.
example_sentence: The country faced a terrible famine after years of drought. Thousands of people migrated to the city to escape the famine. Relief organizations provided food aid to famine-affected areas. Famine not only destroys lives but also weakens the economy.

english_meaning: To suffer from extreme hunger or to make someone very hungry. To experience severe hunger due to lack of food or to cause someone to suffer from extreme hunger. It emphasizes an intense state of starvation rather than just ordinary hunger.
example_sentence: The prisoners were famished after days without food. The famine caused many villages to famish. He felt famished after the long hike. The neglected pets were famished and weak.

english_meaning: Known about by very many people. Widely recognized for a particular quality or achievement. Celebrated, renowned, or highly regarded in public life. Well known in an admirable or notable way.
example_sentence: She became famous after her first novel was published. The city is famous for its ancient monuments. He is a famous surgeon respected across the country. Their restaurant is famous for its seafood.

english_meaning: To move or spread inward toward a central point. In computer science or electronics: the number of input signals or connections going into a single component (like a logic gate). To gather people, things, or energy toward one point or area.
example_sentence: After the performance ended, the audience began to fan in toward the exit. The soldiers fanned in to secure the central area. In this circuit, the logic gate has a high fan-in capacity. As the rain started, the tourists fanned in under the shelter.

english_meaning: To spread out or move in different directions from a single point, similar to how the ribs of a fan open outward.
example_sentence: The police officers fanned out across the field to search for clues. The crowd fanned out as the concert ended. He fanned out the cards on the table for everyone to see. The rescue teams fanned out in different directions after the earthquake.

english_meaning: To make a difficult situation, argument, or emotion worse. To intensify anger, conflict, or excitement.
example_sentence: His speech only fanned the flames of protest. Don't fan the flames by taking sides in their quarrel. The media fanned the flames of controversy. Her sarcastic remarks fanned the flames of his anger.

english_meaning: An unusually high or excessive price. A price much higher than normal. A cost that reflects luxury or exclusivity. An inflated or exaggerated price. A price paid for something rare or fashionable.
example_sentence: He paid a fancy price for the antique clock. The painting was sold at a fancy price at the auction. Tourists often pay fancy prices for souvenirs. She refused to pay such a fancy price for a bag.

english_meaning: Everywhere. From long distances and close by. Refers to places both far away and nearby. Often used to express wide coverage or people from many places. In all directions, including distant and close places.
example_sentence: People came from far and near to see the festival. His fame spread far and near because of his honesty. The news was heard far and near. They searched far and near for the lost child.

english_meaning: Over a large area or distance, everywhere. in many different places.
example_sentence: His fame spread far and wide. The news of his success spread far and wide. People came from far and wide to see the festival. Her fame reached far and wide across the country. They searched far and wide for the missing child.

english_meaning: A type of comedy that uses exaggeration, ridiculous situations, and absurd characters to make people laugh. It can also mean something that is so badly organized, false, or ridiculous that it seems like a joke.
example_sentence: The play was a farce filled with silly misunderstandings and exaggerated acting. The trial was a complete farce; justice was never served.

english_meaning: Silly or unreasonable, often in a way that is humorous. Something ridiculous, absurd, or laughably foolish, often like a farce (a type of comedy where events are exaggerated and nonsensical).
example_sentence: The meeting turned into a farcical display of shouting and confusion. Such a farcical situation could never happen in Germany. It was a farcical trial. It is preposterous, ridiculous, almost farcical. The whole situation has become farcical. There were farcical scenes at the meeting.

english_meaning: Relating to food produced locally and served fresh in restaurants. A movement promoting direct sourcing from farms to consumers. Describing meals made with ingredients from nearby farms. Emphasizing freshness, sustainability, and local support. A dining concept focused on seasonal, local produce.
example_sentence: The new restaurant follows a strict farm-to-table philosophy. They enjoyed a delicious farm-to-table dinner. Farm-to-table dining supports local farmers. The menu changes weekly based on farm-to-table produce.

english_meaning: A specialist in equine hoof care, including the trimming and balancing of horses' hooves. A person who manufactures and fits shoes for horses. Traditionally, this role combines blacksmithing skills with detailed knowledge of horse anatomy to ensure the animal's mobility and health. One who treats diseases of horses' legs and feet.
example_sentence: The farrier arrived early to replace the stallion's worn-out iron shoes. A skilled farrier must understand the complex biomechanics of a horse's gait. We scheduled a visit from the farrier to trim the hooves of the new ponies. Throughout history, the local farrier was often the most essential craftsman in a rural village. The farmer called the farrier when he noticed the mare was limping during the harvest.

english_meaning: A release of gas from the bowels through the anus, often making a sound or smell. (informal, humorous). To release gas from the bowels through the anus.
example_sentence: He accidentally farted in the classroom and everyone laughed. A loud fart broke the silence during the meeting. Children often find fart jokes funny. He tried to hold in a fart during the lecture.

english_meaning: A thin sheet of connective tissue that surrounds and separates muscles and organs. A continuous layer of tissue that holds the structures of the body in place. A tough covering that allows muscles to slide against one another during movement. A flat board or band on the front of a building, or the panel of a shop sign.
example_sentence: The surgeon carefully cut through the fascia covering the muscle. Tight fascia in the sole can cause heel pain. Fascia holds the muscles and organs neatly in place. The shop's new fascia was painted a bright green.

english_meaning: Inflammation of fascia, the connective tissue surrounding muscles, blood vessels, nerves, and other structures. A painful inflammatory condition that may result from strain, injury, infection, or disease. A general medical term used in specific conditions such as plantar fasciitis.
example_sentence: The runner developed fasciitis after months of overtraining. Rest and stretching may help some forms of fasciitis. The doctor examined her foot for signs of fasciitis. Severe fasciitis requires prompt medical assessment.

english_meaning: To attract and hold someone’s attention strongly. To charm or enchant someone.  To make someone very curious. To strongly attract interest or admiration. To capture someone’s interest or attention so deeply that they feel attracted, curious, or amazed. It often involves a sense of charm, beauty, or mystery.
example_sentence: The magician fascinated the audience with his amazing tricks. She is fascinated by ancient history and cultures. The child was fascinated by the colorful butterflies. His story fascinated everyone in the room.

english_meaning: Strongly interested, attracted, or captivated by someone or something. Having one's attention completely held by curiosity, admiration, beauty, or mystery. Historically, enchanted or held as if by a spell.
example_sentence: The children were fascinated by the magician. I am fascinated with how languages change. She watched, fascinated, as the sculpture took shape. He became fascinated by local history.

english_meaning: Extremely interesting, attractive, or captivating. Holding attention through unusual beauty, complexity, novelty, or mystery. Exercising a powerful charm or irresistible influence.
example_sentence: The museum contains a fascinating collection of maps. We had a fascinating conversation about memory. It is fascinating to watch bees communicate. Her research offers a fascinating view of ancient life.

english_meaning: In an extremely interesting, attractive, or captivating way. In a manner that strongly holds attention or arouses curiosity. Remarkably or intriguingly.
example_sentence: The documentary fascinatingly connects art with science. She spoke fascinatingly about desert wildlife. The two languages are fascinatingly similar. The author fascinatingly reconstructs the lost city.

english_meaning: A powerful attraction or intense interest. The state of being deeply absorbed or charmed. Something that irresistibly attracts attention. The act or power of captivating someone.
example_sentence: Her fascination with astronomy began in childhood. The old castle held a strange fascination for visitors. He watched the glassblower at work with complete fascination. The documentary renewed my fascination with ocean life.

english_meaning: A political philosophy or regime that exalts nation and often race above the individual. A system of government characterized by dictatorial power, forcible suppression of opposition, and strong regimentation of society and of the economy. A far-right, authoritarian ultranationalism that rose to prominence in early 20th-century Europe. Any movement or attitude that is perceived as being excessively authoritarian or intolerant of dissent.
example_sentence: European history between the world wars was dominated by the rise of fascism. The regime was accused of practicing a modern form of corporate fascism. Many scholars study the psychological roots of fascism in stagnant societies. The dictator’s ideology was a dangerous blend of populism and fascism. Opposition leaders warned that the new laws were a step toward fascism and the erosion of civil liberties.

english_meaning: A lifestyle that is full of excitement, luxury, and pleasure but often careless or risky.
example_sentence: He spent his youth in fast living and never saved any money. Fast living can lead to health problems and regret later in life. Many celebrities are known for their fast-living lifestyle. She gave up fast living and chose a peaceful, simple life.

english_meaning: To attach or fix something securely so that it cannot easily be moved or opened. To close or secure something such as a garment or container. To direct one's attention or gaze firmly on something.
example_sentence: Please fasten your seatbelt before the vehicle begins to move. She fastened the buttons on her coat quickly before stepping out into the cold. He fastened the rope securely to the post so that the boat would not drift away. The carpenter fastened the planks together with long nails and a strong adhesive. Her eyes fastened on the stranger the moment he entered the room.

english_meaning: Hard to satisfy. Showing refinement or delicacy in taste. Sensitive to imperfections. Very attentive to detail, meticulous, or hard to please. Showing excessive care about cleanliness or correctness. Demanding, particular, or critical.
example_sentence: She is fastidious about her appearance and always dresses perfectly. The chef was fastidious when it came to plating the dishes. He is fastidious in checking every detail of the report before submission. Fastidious readers often notice even minor mistakes in a book.

english_meaning: A wealthy and powerful person, especially one who earns huge profits in business or politics. A rich corporate executive who is perceived as greedy or excessively overpaid. A wealthy individual who makes large political donations to secure influence. A person living in extreme financial luxury without proportional effort.
example_sentence: The government faced severe backlash for giving tax breaks to fat cats in the financial sector. Many voters feel that politics is dominated by fat cats who buy political influence. The corporate fat cat received a massive bonus despite the company performing poorly. Activists protested outside the luxury hotel where the industry fat cats were meeting.

english_meaning: Almost no possibility. it’s an ironic way to express hopelessness or disbelief about something happening. (Used to show strong doubt or disbelief that something will happen),
example_sentence: You think he’ll lend you money? Fat chance!. Fat chance of getting tickets for that concert, it’s been sold out for weeks!. They said they would apologize, fat chance of that happening!. Fat chance he’ll finish the work on time; he hasn’t even started yet!.

english_meaning: The best and most luxurious things that life can offer. Abundance of food, comfort, and wealth. Living in luxury without effort. Rich resources of a place. The finest produce or benefits available.
example_sentence: After winning the lottery, they lived off the fat of the land. The wealthy family enjoyed the fat of the land for generations. Farmers who own fertile fields live off the fat of the land. He dreams of retiring and enjoying the fat of the land.

english_meaning: Causing death or leading to serious failure or disaster. Something that results in death or causes very serious and irreversible damage. It can also mean something that leads to a complete failure or major negative outcome, especially in decisions or mistakes.
example_sentence: The accident was fatal for the driver. A fatal mistake in the experiment ruined the results. Lack of safety measures can lead to fatal injuries. The doctor confirmed the disease could be fatal if untreated.

english_meaning: A  person who believes that everything is decided by fate and cannot be changed. Someone who thinks that events in life are already decided by fate, destiny, or a higher power. Such a person may believe that human effort cannot change what is meant to happen. Sometimes, a fatalist accepts problems passively because he or she thinks, “Whatever has to happen will happen”.
synonyms: ["Determinist","Predestinarian","Believer in destiny","Believer in fate","Necessitarian","Defeatist","In some contexts","Resigned person","In some contexts"]
antonyms: ["Believer in free will","Non fatalist","Optimist","In some contexts","Activist","In some contexts","Self determined person","Free thinker","In some contexts","Person who believes in personal choice"]
example_sentence: He is a fatalist who believes that no one can escape destiny. As a fatalist, she accepted the loss without trying to change the situation. The old man was not a planner, but a fatalist who trusted fate completely. A fatalist may think that success and failure are already written in life.

english_meaning: Believing that all events are fixed by fate and cannot be changed by human actions. A fatalistic person thinks that whatever happens in life is already decided by destiny, luck, or fate, and people cannot avoid or change it. This attitude may cause a person to accept situations without trying to improve them.
example_sentence: He became fatalistic after losing his job several times. Her fatalistic attitude stopped her from trying again. Many people felt fatalistic during the difficult economic crisis. The old man was fatalistic and believed that everything happens for a reason.

english_meaning: The development of events beyond a person's control, regarded as determined by a supernatural power. The predetermined course of events in the universe. The final outcome or destiny of a person or thing. A power or agency that is often personified as determining the future. Death, destruction, or a disastrous end.
example_sentence: Many people believe that their lives are governed by fate. It was fate that we met at the airport after so many years. The tragic hero met his fate at the end of the play. No one knows what fate awaits the missing ship and its crew. She decided to temp fate by driving through the storm.

english_meaning: A unit of length equal to six feet (1.83 meters) used especially for measuring the depth of water. To understand a difficult problem or an enigmatic person after much thought. To measure the depth of water by means of a sounding line. To penetrate and come to understand the nature or meaning of something deep or mysterious.
example_sentence: The sailors used a weighted rope to fathom the depth of the harbor. He could not fathom why she decided to quit her job so suddenly. The mysteries of the universe are difficult for the human mind to fathom. The water was recorded at a depth of ten fathoms. It took me a long time to fathom the true meaning of his cryptic message.

english_meaning: Capable of being understood, comprehended, or grasped fully. Able to be measured in depth. Something whose meaning, nature, or extent can be figured out through thought or analysis. Used for ideas, feelings, or situations that are not too difficult to understand.
example_sentence: His reasons for leaving the job are fathomable once you know the full story. The problem is complex but still fathomable with careful thought. Her sadness was fathomable to anyone who had lost a loved one. The depth of the lake is easily fathomable using modern instruments. The instructions were clear and fathomable for every student.

english_meaning: Extreme tiredness resulting from mental or physical exertion or illness. It also refers to the weakening of a material caused by repeated stress. It describes a state where one's capacity for work is significantly reduced.
example_sentence: She was suffering from severe fatigue after the long journey. Metal fatigue was identified as the primary cause of the bridge's failure. The soldiers were overcome by heat and fatigue during the drill. Chronic fatigue can be a symptom of various underlying health issues.

english_meaning: Silly and pointless. Lacking intelligence or seriousness despite being complacent. It describes a remark or action that is foolish in a self-satisfied way.
example_sentence: The politician's fatuous remarks during the debate alienated many serious voters. It was a fatuous suggestion to think that we could finish the project in one hour. She ignored the fatuous questions asked by the intrusive reporters. His fatuous grin indicated that he didn't understand the gravity of the situation.

english_meaning: Something that is not genuine but is made to imitate or resemble the real thing. It is commonly used for materials, fashion, design, or behavior that copies something authentic.
example_sentence: She wore a jacket made of faux leather. The room had a faux marble finish on the walls. His faux confidence was easy to detect. They decorated the house with faux flowers.

english_meaning: An action, remark, or behavior that is socially awkward, improper, or tactless, often causing embarrassment.
example_sentence: Forgetting her guest’s name was a real faux pas. Wearing sneakers to the wedding was a fashion faux pas. He committed a faux pas by interrupting the speaker. Making jokes at the funeral would be a serious faux pas.

english_meaning: The practice of giving unfair preference to one person or group over others. Treating someone better than others without a valid reason. Showing partiality, often based on personal liking, relationship, or bias. It is generally viewed negatively, especially in workplaces, families, and institutions where fairness is expected.
example_sentence: The teacher was accused of favoritism by the students. Favoritism in promotions has damaged the company's morale. Parents should avoid favoritism among their children. The manager's favoritism caused resentment in the team. Many believe favoritism is widespread in government appointments.

english_meaning: To try to please somebody by praising them or paying them too much attention. To seek attention and admiration (from) by cringing and flattering. To show affection in a solicitous or exaggerated way usually with over. A deer less than one year old. A light yellow-brown color.
example_sentence: He seemed unaware of the girl’s fawning admiration. Why is everybody fawning over him as if he were a national hero? People fawn over you when you're famous. The fawn ran to the top of the ridge.

english_meaning: To give someone excessive praise or attention, often to gain favor.
example_sentence: She fawns over her boss all the time. Don’t fawn over celebrities. The students fawned over their teacher. He dislikes people who fawn over others.

english_meaning: Showing excessive flattery or praise to gain favor. Acting overly submissive or obedient. Trying to please someone in an insincere way. Behaving like a servant to impress someone.
example_sentence: The assistant gave a fawning smile to impress the boss. His fawning behavior made everyone uncomfortable. She spoke in a fawning tone to gain special treatment. The employee was criticized for his fawning attitude.

english_meaning: To disturb the composure of someone. To disconcert or cause to feel confused or worried. To make someone feel nervous or uneasy, typically by something unexpected. To affect the confidence or self-possession of a person. It is often used in negative sentences (e.g., 'not fazed').
example_sentence: She was so confident that the difficult questions did not faze her at all. Even though the dog barked loudly, the little boy wasn't fazed. The sudden change in the schedule did not faze the experienced manager. High pressure situations rarely faze professional athletes. He seemed completely unperturbed, as if nothing could faze him.

english_meaning: The state of being bothered, worried, or disturbed by something unexpected. It describes a person who has lost their calm or focus due to an external pressure. It is the past participle form acting as an adjective.
example_sentence: She looked slightly fazed by the criticism she received. He remained unphased even though everyone else felt fazed by the news. The new intern felt fazed by the complexity of the software. I was a bit fazed when the audience started shouting.

english_meaning: The front or face of a building, especially an imposing or decorative one. An outward appearance that is maintained to conceal a less pleasant or creditable reality. A deceptive outer show. A false front put on by a person to hide true feelings or intentions.
example_sentence: The façade of the old palace was decorated with intricate carvings. Behind his cheerful façade, he was deeply worried about his future. The company's friendly façade hid its ruthless business practices. Workers spent months restoring the façade of the historic building. She kept up a façade of confidence during the difficult interview.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being possible, practical, or able to be done successfully. The likelihood that a plan, idea, or project can be carried out effectively. An assessment of whether something can be achieved given available resources, time, and conditions. Often used in business and engineering studies to evaluate proposed projects before implementation.
example_sentence: The engineers studied the feasibility of building a bridge over the river. A feasibility report must be submitted before the project starts. The committee doubted the feasibility of the new education plan. We are conducting a feasibility study for the proposed solar power plant. The feasibility of the idea depends on the available budget.

english_meaning: Capable of being done, accomplished, or carried out successfully. Possible to do easily or conveniently under the given circumstances. Likely to work or to be effective in practice. Reasonable and likely to succeed. Used for plans, ideas, solutions, or projects that can realistically be put into practice.
example_sentence: Is it feasible to complete this project within a month? The plan seems feasible if we get enough funding. Solar power is now a feasible alternative to conventional energy. We must find a feasible solution to the traffic problem. The proposal is feasible but requires careful planning.

english_meaning: In a way that is possible or practical. Refers to doing something in a manner that can realistically be achieved or carried out given the circumstances, resources, or conditions.
example_sentence: We could feasibly finish the project by Friday if everyone works extra hours. The plan seems risky but feasibly achievable. It is not feasibly possible to travel across the desert without proper supplies. She argued that the budget could feasibly cover all necessary expenses.

english_meaning: A large or special meal, especially for a lot of people and to celebrate something. To eat a large amount of food with great pleasure. To enjoy some unusual pleasure or delight.
example_sentence: The evening was a real feast for music lovers. The women were busy preparing the wedding feast.

english_meaning: To look at something with great pleasure and admiration. To enjoy the sight of something beautiful, impressive, or extraordinary. To gaze at something with delight and satisfaction. To take visual delight in a scene, object, or view. To behold something remarkable with joy.
example_sentence: Feast your eyes on this breathtaking sunset over the ocean. Come and feast your eyes on the beautiful paintings in the gallery. The tourists feasted their eyes on the snow-capped mountains. Feast your eyes on the delicious dishes prepared for the wedding.

english_meaning: An act or deed that shows great courage, strength, or skill. A remarkable or noteworthy achievement. A performance or operation of great difficulty that requires courage and stamina. In a technical or computational context, it may refer to a specific milestone achieved through design or programming.
example_sentence: Climbing Mount Everest is a remarkable feat of human endurance. The new skyscraper is a magnificent feat of engineering. The magician performed several incredible feats of illusion before the stunned audience. Completing the marathon was no small feat for someone of his age. The pilot's successful emergency landing was an extraordinary feat of skill.

english_meaning: An achievement to be proud of. A special honor or accomplishment. A notable success that brings recognition. A personal victory added to one's record. A distinction earned through effort.
example_sentence: Winning the award was a feather in her cap. This promotion is a real feather in his cap. Publishing a book is a feather in any writer's cap. The championship was another feather in the team's cap.

english_meaning: Relating to or characterized by a fever. Having or showing the symptoms of a fever. A state of nervous excitement or high energy. Pertaining to a high body temperature resulting from illness. Indicating an intense or frantic emotional state or activity.
example_sentence: The doctor monitored the patient's febrile condition throughout the night. A febrile illness can often cause intense shivering and dehydration. The stock market reached a febrile state as investors panicked over the news. She felt febrile and weak after the long journey in the sun. The atmosphere in the stadium was febrile as the final whistle approached.

english_meaning: Waste matter discharged from the bowels. Solid or semisolid excretory matter eliminated from the digestive tract through the anus. It consists of undigested food, bacteria, cells, and waste products. It is a key indicator in medical diagnostics and environmental studies.
example_sentence: The doctor tested the patient’s feces. The doctor collected a feces sample for testing. Farmers often use animal feces as natural fertilizer. Proper disposal of human feces is crucial for sanitation. Scientists studied the feces of wild animals to understand their diet.

english_meaning: Lacking in efficiency or vitality. Having no sense of responsibility. Lazy, weak, or ineffective in character. Describing a person who is unable or unwilling to take useful actions or make meaningful progress. Often used to describe someone who lacks strength of character or is habitually irresponsible.
example_sentence: The feckless administrator failed to solve even the simplest problems within the department. She grew tired of her feckless brother, who refused to find a job or help around the house. The government was criticized for its feckless response to the escalating economic crisis. It is frustrating to work with such feckless individuals who have no motivation to succeed. He was a feckless youth who spent his days wandering aimlessly without any goals.

english_meaning: Producing or capable of producing a lot of offspring or new growth. Highly fertile. Intellectually productive or creative. Rich in invention or imagination. Used both literally for soil, plants, and animals that produce abundantly, and figuratively for minds, periods, or environments full of ideas.
example_sentence: The fecund soil of the valley produces excellent crops. She has a fecund imagination that fuels her writing. The Renaissance was a fecund period for art and science. Rabbits are remarkably fecund animals. His fecund mind generated dozens of business ideas every week.

english_meaning: A system of government in which power is divided between a central national authority and smaller regional governments. The principle or advocacy of federal political organization. A governmental structure where both national and state levels have defined powers and authority.
example_sentence: The United States operates under a system of federalism. Federalism allows states to have their own laws within certain limits. The debate centered on the balance of power in federalism. Many countries have adopted federalism to manage diverse regions.

english_meaning: A person who supports or advocates for federalism. Someone who believes in a strong central government alongside regional authorities. A member or supporter of a federalist political party or movement. Relating to or supporting federal government structure.
example_sentence: The Federalists believed in a strong national government. She identifies as a federalist in political debates. The Federalist Papers explained the benefits of the proposed Constitution. Federalist principles shaped the nation's founding.

english_meaning: A group of states or organizations united under a central authority. A political system in which power is shared between a central government and regional units. An association of clubs, unions, or societies working together. The act of forming such a union. A large organization that represents smaller groups.
example_sentence: The Russian Federation includes many regions. He is the president of the football federation. A federation of trade unions organized the protest. The federation was formed to protect workers' rights.

english_meaning: Weak, lacking strength (physical or mental). Without force, effectiveness, or convincing power. Frail or faint in intensity (sound, effort, light, etc).
example_sentence: He gave a feeble attempt to lift the box. He was too feeble to lift the box. The argument was feeble and unconvincing. A feeble light shone through the window.

english_meaning: To gain strength, energy, advantage or benefit from something, especially negative emotions or situations.
example_sentence: Some people feed off drama. The media feeds off scandals. They feed off each other’s energy. Parasites feed off their hosts. Some rumors feed off fear and uncertainty. The company feeds off the demand for quick online shopping.

english_meaning: To eat or live on a particular type of food. To use something as a source. To eat or get nourishment from something. It can also mean to gain strength, energy, or motivation from a particular thing or situation.
example_sentence: Lions feed on other animals. The project feeds on innovation. The fire feeds on oxygen. They feed on hope.

english_meaning: To make someone eat more to become healthier or stronger. To become tired, annoyed, or bored with something unpleasant or repetitive.
example_sentence: She’s trying to feed up her son. They feed up the animals before winter. He was fed up before training. The doctor said to feed him up. I’m fed up with this terrible weather. She’s fed up with doing all the work alone.

english_meaning: Information or comments about how well someone is doing something, used as a basis for improvement. A reaction or response to a product, service, or performance. The return of part of a system's output to its input, affecting the process. The unpleasant noise produced when sound from a loudspeaker returns to a microphone.
example_sentence: The teacher gave detailed feedback on my essay. We collect customer feedback to improve our service. Positive feedback from the team encouraged him to continue. The microphone produced loud feedback during the speech.

english_meaning: To feel sad or unhappy. To experience sadness, low mood, or emotional heaviness, often without a clear reason or because of disappointment, loneliness, or stress
synonyms: ["Feel sad","Feel down","Feel low","Be unhappy","Be depressed lightly"]
antonyms: ["Feel happy","Feel cheerful","Feel joyful","Be in high spirits","Feel upbeat"]
example_sentence: She felt blue after missing her family for so long. I always feel blue when it rains all day. He was feeling blue because his plans did not work out. Music helps me when I start to feel blue.

english_meaning: To have a strong intuitive feeling that something is true. To sense something instinctively without proof. To know something deeply through intuition. To have an inner conviction about something. To strongly believe in something without logical reasoning.
example_sentence: I feel it in my bones that we'll win this match. She felt it in her bones that something was wrong. He felt it in his bones that the plan would succeed. My grandmother feels it in her bones when rain is coming.

english_meaning: To feel unimportant or embarrassed. Describes emotional discomfort when someone feels inferior or ashamed.
example_sentence: His words made me feel small. She felt small after the criticism. I felt small in front of the experts. He tried not to make others feel small.

english_meaning: To understand the current mood, trends, or situation of a group, place, or activity. Being aware of what is really happening in a particular situation. It involves sensing opinions, emotions, or changes in a group, society, market, or environment. It is often used in leadership, business, media, and social contexts.
synonyms: ["Understand the mood","Gauge the situation","Read the room","Stay in touch","Be aware"]
antonyms: ["Be unaware","Misjudge the situation","Ignore reality","Be out of touch"]
example_sentence: A good leader must feel the pulse of the people before making decisions. Journalists try to feel the pulse of society through interviews and reports. The company regularly surveys customers to feel the pulse of the market. Teachers should feel the pulse of their students to improve learning.

english_meaning: To touch someone in a sexual or inappropriate way (informal, often negative).
example_sentence: He was accused of feeling up a colleague. She complained that someone felt her up. Don’t feel up others. The man was arrested for feeling up a passenger.

english_meaning: To have the energy, strength, or confidence to do something.
example_sentence: I don’t feel up to going out tonight. Do you feel up to hiking? She didn’t feel up to talking. He feels up to working again.

english_meaning: To feel sad, unhappy, or depressed.
example_sentence: After hearing the sad news, she was feeling blue all day. He often feels blue when he is away from his family. Rainy days sometimes make people feel blue without any reason. She tried to cheer up her friend who was feeling blue after the exam results.

english_meaning: To pretend that you have a particular feeling or that you are ill, tired, etc. To give a false appearance of. Make believe with the intent to deceive.
example_sentence: He survived the massacre by feigning death. She feigned sleep to avoid having to answer. He feigned sickness so he wouldn’t have to go to school. He feigned that he was not feeling well so that he could leave the party early.

english_meaning: A deceptive movement made to distract an opponent. A pretended attack or blow intended to mislead. To make such a misleading movement in sport or combat. Any action meant to conceal one's real intention.
example_sentence: The boxer made a feint with his left hand and struck with his right. Their advance on the bridge was only a feint. He feinted to the right and then slipped past the defender. The whole offer turned out to be a clever feint.

english_meaning: To congratulate someone warmly on an achievement or good fortune. To express good wishes or compliments to another person. To formally praise or honor an individual on a special occasion or for a specific success. It often implies a formal or ceremonial gesture of appreciation toward someone's luck or hard work.
example_sentence: The President will felicitate the award-winning scientists at a grand ceremony tomorrow. Friends and family gathered to felicitate the couple on their fiftieth wedding anniversary. The school principal decided to felicitate the students who secured top ranks in the board exams. He sent a bouquet of flowers to felicitate his colleague on her recent promotion. Members of the club met to felicitate the retiring coach for his years of dedicated service.

english_meaning: A man or boy. A person in the same position, involved in the same activity, or having the same interests.
example_sentence: He is a very friendly fellow who always helps his neighbours. My fellow students and I are studying for the final exams. He was elected as a fellow of the Royal Society last year. The young fellow looked lost as he stood at the train station.

english_meaning: A friendly association, especially with people who share one's interests. A group of people meeting to pursue a shared interest or activity. A guild or corporation. An award or grant made to a scholar. Companionship, community, or mutual support among people. The position or status of a fellow at a college or university.
example_sentence: The students enjoyed the warm fellowship of their study group. She received a research fellowship at the university. The church holds a fellowship dinner every Sunday. He values the fellowship of his old friends more than anything. The scholar was awarded a prestigious fellowship abroad.

english_meaning: The intentional killing of women or girls because they are female. A gender-based hate crime involving the murder of a female specifically because of her gender. The systematic killing of women by men, often driven by misogyny, domestic violence, or harmful cultural practices. It represents the extreme end of a continuum of violence against women.
example_sentence: The government is introducing new laws to combat the rising rates of femicide in the country. example_sentence: He likes to fiddle around with old computers at weekends. Stop fiddling around with the volume and listen. She fiddled around with the recipe until it tasted right. I fiddled around with the settings and fixed the problem.

english_meaning: To touch or play with something repeatedly, often nervously. To make small changes to something to adjust or repair it. To interfere with something in a way that may cause damage. To alter figures or records dishonestly.
example_sentence: She kept fiddling with her ring during the interview. He fiddled with the radio until he found the station. Please don't fiddle with the camera settings. The clerk was accused of fiddling with the accounts.

english_meaning: Playing a violin, especially informally or in a folk style. Making small, restless, or aimless movements with something. Altering, adjusting, or tampering with something, often dishonestly. Trivial, petty, or annoyingly small. The act of wasting time on unimportant details.
example_sentence: We heard cheerful fiddling from the room next door. Stop fiddling with your phone and listen carefully. The accountant was accused of fiddling the company records. They charged a fiddling amount for the repair.

english_meaning: Difficult to do because it involves small parts, fine detail, or careful movements. Complicated and awkward to use or manage. Requiring excessive attention to minor details.
example_sentence: Replacing the tiny battery is a fiddly job. The clasp is too fiddly for me to fasten quickly. This recipe is delicious but rather fiddly to prepare. He lost patience with the fiddly controls on the camera.

english_meaning: Faithfulness, loyalty, and devotion to a person, duty, promise, or belief. Being loyal, faithful, trustworthy, and committed to someone or something. It can describe loyalty in relationships, dedication to duties, adherence to commitments, or accuracy in reproducing information, sound, or images.
example_sentence: Her fidelity to her family earned everyone's respect. The company values employee fidelity and dedication. He showed great fidelity to his promises even during difficult times. This audio system is known for its high fidelity sound quality.

english_meaning: To make small, quick movements with your hands, feet, or body, especially because you are nervous, bored, or restless. To move restlessly or uneasily. To play or fiddle with something absentmindedly. A person who fidgets. A small movement caused by restlessness or nervousness.
example_sentence: The child began to fidget during the long lecture. She fidgeted nervously with her pen while waiting for the results. Please stop fidgeting and sit still. He is such a fidget that he can never stay in one place.

english_meaning: Involving trust, especially with regard to the relationship between a trustee and a beneficiary. Refers to a person or institution that has the legal or ethical duty to act in the best interest of another party. Relating to or of the nature of a legal or ethical relationship of confidence and trust. Financial or legal responsibility where one manages money or property for someone else and is required to put that person's interests above their own. Often used in legal contexts to describe the duty of care and loyalty.
example_sentence: The company directors have a fiduciary duty to act in the best interests of the shareholders. A bank has a fiduciary responsibility to manage its clients' investment portfolios wisely. He was sued for breach of fiduciary duty after he used client funds for personal gain. As a fiduciary, Mike must prioritize his client's financial stability over his own commission bonuses. Most legal systems recognize the relationship between an attorney and a client as fiduciary in nature.

english_meaning: Very strong, violent, intense, or aggressive. Someone or something that shows strong intensity, power, or aggression. It can refer to violent weather, strong emotions, dangerous animals, strict competition, or a brave and determined personality.
example_sentence: The fierce storm damaged many houses in the village. The tiger gave a fierce roar that frightened everyone. She faced fierce competition in the final exam. He showed fierce determination to achieve his goals.

english_meaning: A short period during which an ordinary person receives public attention. Brief and temporary celebrity that quickly fades away. The idea that everyone will be famous for a very short time. A fleeting moment of media exposure.
synonyms: ["Brief celebrity","Passing fame","Momentary glory","Short-lived renown","Flash in the pan","Media moment","Transient limelight"]
example_sentence: The viral video gave him his fifteen minutes of fame. She enjoyed her fifteen minutes of fame after the interview. Reality shows offer contestants fifteen minutes of fame. His fifteen minutes of fame ended as quickly as they began.

english_meaning: A sweet soft fruit with tiny seeds inside. A fig is a soft pear shaped fruit that has sweet flesh and many tiny seeds.
example_sentence: I bought fresh figs from the market this morning. She added dried figs to the dessert to make it sweeter. The tree in our garden gives plenty of figs every season. He does not care a fig about what others think.

english_meaning: To resist strongly or attack somebody who has attacked you. To defend yourself when someone attacks you physically. To defend yourself against attack or criticism.
example_sentence: I was fighting back the tears, Don't let them bully you. Fight back!. It is time to fight back against street crime. Collins fought back to level the match at two sets all. You’ve seen him fight back every time he’s been unfairly attacked. Jones has denied the charge and has fought back publicly.

english_meaning: To try hard not to do or show something, especially not to show your feelings. To control or suppress a feeling or urge.
example_sentence: He fought down his disgust. He fought down his anger. She fought down the urge to cry.

english_meaning: To successfully defend yourself against an attacker or enemy. To resist and overcome a disease or infection. To prevent something unpleasant from affecting you. To drive away or repel someone or something unwanted. To struggle against negative feelings, fears, or temptations.
antonyms: ["Surrender to","Yield to","Accept","Welcome","Submit to","Give in to","Succumb to","Allow"]
example_sentence: The soldiers managed to fight off the enemy attack. Her strong immune system helped her fight off the infection. He drank coffee to fight off sleep during the long drive. The company worked hard to fight off competition from larger rivals.

english_meaning: To fight, argue or compete until an argument or competition has been settled. To argue until a decision is reached between two people or groups.
example_sentence:
The conflict is still being fought out.
They hadn't reached any agreement so we left them to fight it out.
Four teams will fight it out in the play-offs. Let them fight it out. There's only one ticket so you'll have to fight it out between you. They fought out their differences. The rivals fought it out in court.

english_meaning: Expressing ideas in a symbolic or non-literal way. Used to describe language, expressions, or speech that represents something in a symbolic, metaphorical, or imaginative way rather than literally. Often used in poetry, literature, or creative writing to convey ideas more vividly.
example_sentence: Her speech was full of figurative expressions. The poet used figurative language to describe love. “Time is a thief” is a figurative statement. He spoke figuratively about the hardships of life.

english_meaning: To include or consider something or someone as part of a plan or calculation.
example_sentence: Did you figure in the cost of food? His opinion doesn’t figure in my decision. We have to figure in travel expenses. She figured herself in the project’s success.

english_meaning: To plan or expect something to happen, to count on or anticipate.
example_sentence: We didn’t figure on so many guests. I figured on leaving early. You can’t figure on getting help from him. They didn’t figure on the rain ruining their trip.

english_meaning: To understand or find the answer to something after thinking carefully, to solve or comprehend a problem or situation.
example_sentence: I can’t figure out what she means. He finally figured out the solution. Can you figure out how this machine works? It took me hours to figure out the problem.

english_meaning: To calculate the total amount of something, to add up numbers or figures.
example_sentence: Let’s figure up the total cost. He figured up the expenses quickly. The accountant figured up last month’s profits. I need to figure up how much I owe.

english_meaning: To steal something small or of little value, especially secretly or casually. To take something dishonestly or without permission. To appropriate an idea, phrase, or other intangible thing in a sneaky way.
example_sentence: Someone filched my pen from the reception desk. The child tried to filch a biscuit before dinner. A thief filched several wallets from the crowded bus. The writer was accused of filching a memorable phrase from an older novel.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or befitting a son or daughter. Denoting the generation or generations after the parental generation. Relating to the relationship between an offspring and their parents. It describes the sense of duty, respect, or affection that a child owes to their mother or father. In genetics, it refers to the sequence of generations following a controlled cross.
example_sentence: He felt a strong sense of filial duty to care for his aging parents in their home. The photograph reflected a beautiful moment of filial affection between the daughter and her father. In Chinese culture, filial piety is a fundamental virtue involving respect for ancestors. The scientist observed the traits appearing in the first filial generation of the pea plants. She struggled to balance her own career goals with her deep filial obligations.

english_meaning: To copy or repeat data into multiple cells (in spreadsheets) or to continue filling downward.
example_sentence: Fill down the data in the Excel sheet. You can fill down the formula. Fill down all the rows. The teacher said to fill down answers.

english_meaning: To complete something by adding missing information or to temporarily take someone’s place.
example_sentence: Fill in the blanks. Can you fill in for me tomorrow? She filled in the missing details. The assistant filled in the report.

english_meaning: To complete a form or document by providing required information. To become larger or rounder in shape.
example_sentence: Please fill out this form. He filled out the survey. The child has filled out since last year. Fill out the application carefully.

english_meaning: To cover something completely by filling it, usually with liquid or material. To become completely full and start to overflow.
example_sentence: The jar was filled over with honey. The cracks were filled over with cement. She filled over the container. The lake filled over after rain.

english_meaning: To make something completely full or occupy all available space, often used for containers or vehicles.
example_sentence: Please fill up the tank. The room filled up quickly. She filled up her bottle. The form filled up with names.

english_meaning: Very dirty or disgusting condition, something unclean or morally offensive. Physical dirt or waste (garbage, mud, sewage). Moral impurity (obscene talk, indecent behavior). Very dirty condition or place. Something offensive or disgusting in speech or content. Dirt, waste, or anything that is extremely unclean and unpleasant. It can describe physical dirt like garbage and mud, or moral impurity such as obscene language or behavior.
example_sentence: The streets were covered in filth after the storm. He refused to live in such filth. The room was full of filth and trash. She was shocked by the filth in his language.

english_meaning: Very dirty, unclean, or morally offensive. Something extremely dirty, covered with dirt, grease, or unpleasant substances. It can also describe language, behavior, or thoughts that are morally offensive or disgusting.
example_sentence: The kitchen was filthy after the party. His clothes were filthy after working in the field. The water in the drain is filthy and smells bad. He used filthy language during the argument.

english_meaning: Having hands that are physically dirty or soiled. Characterized by involvement in dishonest, corrupt, or unethical actions, particularly involving money. Being guilty of bribery, embezzlement, or illegal dealings. Describing a person who has gained wealth or success through immoral or fraudulent means.
example_sentence: The corrupt official was known for being filthy-handed and accepting bribes from local contractors. After working in the coal mines all day, the laborers returned home exhausted and filthy-handed. No one wanted to go into business with him because he had a reputation for being filthy-handed in his previous ventures. The investigation revealed a network of filthy-handed politicians who had siphoned off public funds. Justice cannot be served when the judges themselves are filthy-handed and biased.

english_meaning: A flattened appendage or organ used by fish and other aquatic animals for swimming, steering, and balance. A wing-like projection on an aircraft or missile designed to provide stability or control in flight. A vertical stabilizer on a vehicle or device used to manage airflow or dissipate heat. A small, thin, or sharp-edged component often found on machinery like a radiator to increase surface area. An underwater paddle attached to a swimmer's foot to aid propulsion.
example_sentence: The shark's dorsal fin sliced through the water with terrifying speed. The engineer added cooling fins to the motor to prevent overheating. Most airplanes have a vertical fin on the tail to maintain stability during flight. Divers use rubber fins to swim more efficiently and cover more distance underwater. You could see the golden fins of the goldfish shimmering in the sunlight.

english_meaning: A person or team that reaches the final stage of a competition. A competitor selected for the last round. A candidate still eligible for the final decision.
example_sentence: She was a finalist in the spelling contest. Three finalists will interview tomorrow. The team became a finalist after a close match. Every finalist received a certificate.

english_meaning: To become comfortable, confident, or familiar with a new situation. To adjust to a new environment, role, or situation after an initial period of uncertainty. It often refers to gaining confidence, understanding how things work, and performing effectively after starting something new.
example_sentence: It took her a few weeks to find her feet in the new job. After moving to a new city, he quickly found his feet and made new friends. The new teacher is still finding her feet in the classroom. Once you find your feet, everything will become easier.

english_meaning: Completely fine, satisfactory, and going well. Used to say that everything is in good order. Often used ironically to suggest that a situation is not really acceptable.
example_sentence: Everything is fine and dandy at the new office. That's all fine and dandy, but who will pay for it? He said business was fine and dandy this quarter. The plan sounds fine and dandy on paper.

english_meaning: Great subtlety and skill in handling a situation. Delicate skill or artfulness in performance or execution. The ability to handle difficult or sensitive situations with diplomacy and tact. In card games, it refers to a technique to win a trick with a lower card while a higher card remains unplayed. To do something with great skill and elegance. To manage or deal with a situation by using clever strategy or social skill.
example_sentence: She handled the difficult interview with great finesse and avoided the trap questions. The architect showed incredible finesse in merging the old building with the modern expansion. The diplomat used his political finesse to prevent the conflict from escalating. He managed to finesse his way through the complex bureaucracy to get the permit. The pianist played the delicate passage with impressive artistic finesse.

english_meaning: One of the five slender jointed parts attached to the palm of the hand. Any of the four digits of the hand excluding the thumb. A part of the hand used for touching, holding, and pointing. Something shaped like a finger, such as a narrow piece of land or food. To touch, feel, or handle something with the fingers.
example_sentence: She wore a silver ring on her middle finger. He pointed a finger at the map to show the route. The child burned his finger on the hot pan. She fingered the soft fabric before buying it.

english_meaning: The hard protective covering at the tip of a finger. A thin layer of keratin that grows over the upper surface of the fingertip. The nail on a finger, used for scratching, picking, and protecting the fingertip. A small hard plate on the finger that people often trim or decorate.
example_sentence: She trimmed her fingernails before the interview. A broken fingernail can be quite painful. He scratched the sticker off with his fingernail. The doctor examined the pale colour of her fingernails.

english_meaning: Hard to please. Excessively particular about small details. Requiring careful handling or precise conditions to work properly. Fussy about food, appearance, quality, or procedure.
example_sentence: The child is finicky about vegetables. This old printer is finicky and jams unless the paper is perfectly aligned. She is finicky about the quality of her coffee. The recipe is finicky, so measure every ingredient carefully. Our cat can be extremely finicky at mealtimes.

english_meaning: Having definite or definable limits or boundaries. Not infinite or everlasting in nature. Subject to limitations or conditions, especially in time or space. Existing in a limited and measurable quantity.
example_sentence: We must remember that the earth's natural resources are finite. A human life is a finite journey that must eventually end. The mathematical problem has a finite number of solutions. Our patience is finite and we cannot wait forever.

english_meaning: A person who stirs up trouble or passionately supports a cause. An energetic and often rebellious agitator. A piece of burning wood. Someone whose fiery speech inspires or provokes others.
example_sentence: The young firebrand challenged the party leadership. He was known as a political firebrand in his youth. She pulled a firebrand from the campfire. The firebrand preacher drew huge crowds.

english_meaning: A strip of land that has been cleared of all vegetation and combustible material to prevent the spread of a wildfire. A metaphorical barrier or mechanism designed to stop a process or trend from worsening or spreading into other areas. A wall built between or through buildings designed to prevent the spread of fire from one structure to another. A safety measure or circuit breaker in technical systems intended to isolate a failure. Any intentional gap or obstacle created to halt the progression of an undesirable force.
example_sentence: The forest rangers worked quickly to bulldoze a firebreak before the wind shifted. The central bank introduced a new firebreak to prevent the local financial crisis from affecting the global market. Residents were thankful that the wide highway acted as a natural firebreak during the brush fire. Architects included a reinforced firebreak between the two wings of the warehouse to ensure safety compliance.

english_meaning: A small flying insect that produces light from its body at night. A nocturnal beetle belonging to the Lampyridae family. It produces light through a natural chemical reaction in its lower abdomen. This light is mainly used to attract mates and communicate. Fireflies are commonly seen in warm, humid regions during summer evenings.
example_sentence: The children watched the fireflies glowing in the garden at night. A single firefly lit up the dark forest path. The scientist studied how a firefly produces light. Her smile shone like a firefly in the darkness.

english_meaning: Taking control or replacing your superior. Informally, it means turning the tables at work, either by gaining power over your boss, resigning in a way that impacts them, or forcing change in leadership. Leaving your job to regain freedom or influence, standing up to authority, or restructuring management.
example_sentence: She felt empowered after firing her boss through smart negotiation. He joked about firing his boss when he proposed new ideas. The startup allowed employees to have a say in firing their boss. Firing your boss can mean leaving your job in a way that shows independence.

english_meaning: Solid, hard, or not easily moved. Strong and definite in decision or opinion. A business organization or company. Showing determination and steadiness. Not likely to change or weaken.
example_sentence: The chair has a firm and comfortable seat. She is firm in her decision to study abroad. He works in a large law firm. The teacher was firm but kind with the children.

english_meaning: In a strong, steady, or secure manner. With determination and confidence. Without hesitation or doubt. In a way that shows unwavering belief or commitment. Solidly and unmovably.
example_sentence: He held her hand firmly during the ceremony. She firmly believes in equal rights for all. Tie the rope firmly to the post. The manager firmly rejected the unfair proposal.

english_meaning: The quality of being strong, solid, and not easily moved or changed. Determination and steadiness in decisions, opinions, or actions. The physical hardness or solidity of an object. Strength and stability of character or will. The state of being resolute and not yielding to pressure.
example_sentence: She handled the difficult situation with great firmness. The firmness of his decision impressed everyone. He spoke with calm firmness and did not change his stance. The firmness of the mattress provided good support for the back. The teacher maintained firmness while remaining kind to the students.

english_meaning: A humorous version of the saying first catch your hare. It means secure the essential thing before making further plans. A warning not to count on something you do not yet have. Advice to complete the first necessary step before proceeding.
synonyms: ["Put first things first","Secure the essentials","Do not count your chickens","Begin at the beginning"]
antonyms: ["Put the cart before the horse","Count your chickens early","Jump ahead","Presume"]
example_sentence: Before planning the menu, first catch your bare. They were choosing colours for a house they had not bought, so I said first catch your bare. First catch your bare, then talk about profits. The old cook's rule was simple: first catch your bare.

english_meaning: Relating to government revenue, especially taxes and public spending. Concerning financial matters in general, particularly those of a state or business. Pertaining to the financial year used for accounting and taxation purposes.
example_sentence: The government announced its new fiscal policy yesterday. The company's fiscal year ends in June. Strong fiscal discipline helped reduce the deficit. The minister presented the fiscal report in parliament. Fiscal reforms are needed to strengthen the economy.

english_meaning: A person who feels uncomfortable, uneasy, or out of place in a particular situation or environment.
example_sentence: When I attended the fancy party, I felt like a fish out of water because I did not know anyone there. He looked like a fish out of water during his first day at the new job. Without her friends, she felt like a fish out of water in the new school. John is a fish out of water when he talks about fashion; he prefers sports.

english_meaning: A person who sells fish and seafood, usually in a market or shop. Someone whose business is catching, preparing, or selling fresh fish and other seafood for food.
example_sentence: The fishmonger displayed fresh fish on ice early in the morning. My mother bought salmon from the local fishmonger. The fishmonger cleaned and cut the fish before selling it. Many restaurants buy seafood directly from a trusted fishmonger.

english_meaning: To form a crack or cause something to split into narrow openings. A narrow crack or split in something, especially in rock or ground. A small opening or separation in tissue or an object. A long, narrow opening or crack that forms naturally in hard surfaces such as rocks, earth, or even in parts of the body. It can occur due to pressure, movement, drying, or damage.
example_sentence: A deep fissure appeared in the ground after the earthquake. Water flowed through the fissure in the rock. The scientist studied a fissure in the skull. A small fissure formed in the wall due to heat. The earthquake fissured the ground in several places. Heat can fissure rocks over time.

english_meaning: A person's hand when the fingers are bent in toward the palm and held there tightly. It is often used for striking something or someone in a fight. A closed hand intended for punching or holding something securely. A symbolic representation of power, defiance, or solidarity. To clench one's hand into such a shape.
example_sentence: He clenched his fist in anger when he heard the news. She knocked on the heavy wooden door with her fist. The boxer threw a powerful right fist at his opponent. He held the gold coin tightly inside his closed fist. The protesters raised their fists in the air as a sign of defiance.

english_meaning: An abnormal or surgically made passage between a hollow or tubular organ and the body surface, or between two hollow organs. A pipe-like inflammatory track that connects an abscess or internal organ to the surface of the body. A long-term medical condition characterized by a permanent connection that is not usually present. An opening that may result from injury, infection, or inflammation. A specialized connection created between an artery and a vein to facilitate medical treatments like dialysis.
example_sentence: The patient underwent surgery to repair a complex anal fistula. Doctors often create an arteriovenous fistula in the arm for patients requiring long-term hemodialysis. A dental fistula can develop if a tooth infection is left untreated for a long period. Prolonged obstructed labor is one of the leading causes of obstetric fistula in developing nations.

english_meaning: Very healthy and full of energy. Someone who is in excellent physical condition, active, and free from illness. It can also imply mental alertness and overall well-being.
example_sentence: After a few weeks of rest, he felt as fit as a fiddle again. Even at seventy, she is as fit as a fiddle and walks every day. He recovered quickly from the illness and is now fit as a fiddle. With regular exercise and a healthy diet, you can stay fit as a fiddle.

english_meaning: To focus one's attention or thoughts obsessively on something. To fasten or make stable. To become emotionally attached to a person or idea in an unhealthy way. To stare fixedly at something.
example_sentence: She tends to fixate on small mistakes. Please don't fixate on the past. The child fixated on the shiny toy in the window. Investigators fixated on one suspect from the start.

english_meaning: An item that is fixed to a building or property and is considered a permanent part of it. A planned game or competition between two teams or players. A person, object, or activity that is always present or regularly seen in a particular place. A device or fitting installed to perform a particular function.
example_sentence: The bathroom fixtures were replaced last week. Saturday's fixture between the two teams was thrilling. He has become a fixture at the local café. All fixtures are included in the sale of the house.

english_meaning: To gradually fail, weaken, or come to an end after starting with excitement or energy. To end weakly or without result.
example_sentence: The party started lively but fizzled out before midnight. His business plan fizzled out due to poor management. Their enthusiasm for the project fizzled out after a few weeks. The peace talks fizzled out without any agreement.

english_meaning: To surprise someone greatly. To astonish or amaze a person so much that they are speechless. To shock or overwhelm with something unexpected. To leave someone stunned and unable to react.
example_sentence: The news of his sudden promotion will flabbergast everyone. Her sharp reply flabbergasted the entire audience. The magician's trick flabbergasted the children. The final result flabbergasted the whole team.

english_meaning: Extremely surprised or shocked. Stunned into silence by something unexpected. Amazed and unable to think clearly. Overwhelmed with astonishment.
example_sentence: I was flabbergasted when I saw my old friend after twenty years. She looked flabbergasted at the surprise party. He was flabbergasted by the amount of the electricity bill. The teacher was flabbergasted by the student's rude reply.

english_meaning: A piece of cloth with a design used as a symbol of a country, group, or signal. The bushy tail of a dog such as a setter. To mark something for attention. To become tired, weak, or less enthusiastic. To signal someone to stop.
example_sentence: The national flag flew above the building. Please flag any errors in the report. His energy began to flag after midnight. She flagged a taxi outside the station.

english_meaning: Extremely wicked or criminal. Marked by scandalous or shameful conduct. Guilty of grave offences. Outrageously evil in nature or action. A strong and formal word used to describe deeply immoral acts, crimes, or persons whose behaviour is considered shocking and unforgivable.
example_sentence: The flagitious crimes of the gang shocked the entire city. He led a flagitious life that ruined his family’s reputation. The book exposes the flagitious behaviour of corrupt officials. Such flagitious acts deserve the strictest punishment. Historians describe the king’s reign as flagitious and cruel.

english_meaning: A tall pole on which a flag is raised and displayed. A vertical post used for flying a national or ceremonial flag.
example_sentence: The national flag flew proudly from the flagpole. Workers installed a new flagpole outside the school. The flag was lowered to half-mast on the flagpole. Wind rattled the rope against the metal flagpole.

english_meaning: Clearly and openly bad, shocking, or wrong. Done in a very obvious way without any attempt to hide it. Outrageously noticeable, especially when referring to wrongdoing or violation of rules. Boldly offensive or scandalous. Used for behaviour, actions, or violations that are impossible to ignore.
example_sentence: The referee punished the player for a flagrant foul. This is a flagrant violation of human rights. His flagrant disregard for the rules shocked everyone. The company was fined for flagrant misuse of public funds. She told a flagrant lie in front of the whole class.
