english_meaning: Criticism or opposition. Strong criticism, disapproval, or verbal attack, often publicly or from multiple sources. It can also refer to anti-aircraft fire in a military context.
example_sentence: The politician faced flak for his controversial remarks. The movie received flak from critics for weak storytelling. The company took flak after the product failure. Pilots had to fly through heavy flak during the mission.

english_meaning: A small, flat, thin piece of something, typically one that has broken away or been peeled off from a larger object. A snowflake. A person who is considered unreliable, eccentric, or likely to cancel plans at the last minute. To come off in small, thin layers or scales. To break or divide into such pieces. To behave in an unpredictable or unreliable manner.
example_sentence: The old paint began to flake off the wooden door. Huge white flakes of snow fell silently from the gray sky and covered the garden. You can't rely on him to finish the project because he is such a flake. Gently flake the cooked fish with a fork before serving. The dry skin on her elbows began to flake during the cold winter months.

english_meaning: Tending to break into small, thin pieces. Behaving in a strange or unusual way. Tending to forget things
example_sentence: The croissant was light and flaky. His flaky skin needs proper moisturizing. She is talented but flaky when it comes to deadlines. Do not rely on him, he can be very flaky.

english_meaning: Tending to attract attention because of their exuberance, confidence, and stylishness. Noticeable or attracted due to bright colors or unusual style. Excessively showy or ornate in appearance or manner. Characterized by colorful or flashy behavior or design. Elaborate and decorative, often in a way that suggests a bold personality.
example_sentence: The flamboyant singer wore a suit made entirely of gold sequins. Her flamboyant personality made her the center of attention at every party. The architect is known for his flamboyant and unconventional building designs. He made a flamboyant gesture with his hands to emphasize his point. The garden was filled with flamboyant tropical flowers in shades of red and orange.

english_meaning: Burning with flames or on fire. Bright red or orange like fire. Very hot or glowing like flames. Passionate, intense, or violent in emotion. Used informally to express annoyance or emphasis.
example_sentence: Firefighters rushed to the flaming building. She wore a flaming red scarf. His flaming temper got him into trouble. The flaming sunset lit up the whole sky.

english_meaning: Easily set on fire. Capable of burning quickly and easily. Combustible in nature. Referring to any material that can catch fire readily under normal conditions. A property indicating high fire risk.
example_sentence: Petrol is a highly flammable liquid and must be stored carefully. Keep flammable materials away from open flames. The warehouse contained several flammable chemicals. Cotton clothing is more flammable than wool. Workers wore protective suits while handling flammable substances.

english_meaning: Easily upset or confused by pressure. Tending to become nervous or excited in difficult situations. Lacking the composure to deal with unexpected problems. Characterized by a tendency to panic or lose one's calm. Prone to agitation or being rattled by external stress.
example_sentence: The new intern proved to be quite flappable when the office phones started ringing incessantly. Even the most flappable pilot must learn to maintain focus during turbulence. He has a flappable personality that makes him unsuitable for high-stakes emergency work. Being flappable in a crisis can lead to poor decision-making and further chaos.

english_meaning:
To spread outward or widen, especially suddenly. 
To blaze or burst out in flame or anger. To expand in shape like a cone or skirt. To suddenly become more intense or noticeable
example_sentence: The skirt flared out beautifully as she twirled. The fire flared out when the wind blew. Tensions flared out during the heated meeting. The road flares out into a wide intersection near the city gate.

english_meaning: To suddenly become more intense or violent. To suddenly show anger or emotion. To start burning or shining brightly for a short time. To reappear after being quiet or calm for a while (especially an illness or conflict).
example_sentence: The old dispute flared up again between the two neighbors. His temper flared up when he heard the unfair decision. The fire flared up when the wind blew strongly. Her skin allergy flared up after eating spicy food.

english_meaning: To suddenly become angry, lose one’s temper, or react sharply toward someone or something.
antonyms: ["Stay calm","Keep one’s cool","Control oneself","Be patient","Remain composed"]
example_sentence: He flared up at his friend for arriving late to the meeting. She flared up at the students who were making noise in class. The manager flared up at the staff for not completing the report on time. Don’t flare up at small mistakes; learn to stay calm.

english_meaning: A sudden, strong flood caused by heavy rainfall or the rapid melting of water, usually within a short time. It develops quickly and often causes damage because people have little time to prepare.
example_sentence: The heavy rain caused a flash flood that destroyed several houses. Villagers had to evacuate quickly due to the flash flood. The government issued a warning for possible flash floods in the valley. A flash flood swept away cars and blocked the main road.

english_meaning: A place, event, or time at which trouble or violence suddenly breaks out. The lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off vapour that can ignite. A situation that is likely to become dangerous very quickly. A critical moment when tension turns into open conflict.
synonyms: ["Trigger","Tinderbox","Crisis point","Hotspot","Breaking point","Turning point","Catalyst","Ignition point","Conflict zone","Tipping point"]
example_sentence: The border region has long been a flashpoint between the two states. Rising prices became the flashpoint for nationwide protests. Diesel has a higher flashpoint than petrol. The meeting reached a flashpoint when old disputes resurfaced.

english_meaning: Having no money at all. Completely without funds and unable to pay for ordinary needs.
example_sentence: I was flat broke by the end of the month. He returned from the trip flat broke. They could not buy dinner because they were flat broke. She started the business when she was almost flat broke.

english_meaning: At the greatest possible speed or with maximum effort. Completely or absolutely. Openly and directly without hesitation. Lying fully extended. Extremely busy or exhausted.
example_sentence: We worked flat out to finish the report. She flat out refused to change her mind. The horse ran flat out toward the finish line. He lay flat out on the grass after the race.

english_meaning: A truck, trailer, or railway vehicle with a flat open platform and no fixed sides or roof. A scanner whose document surface is a flat glass plate. A flat supporting base or surface on a machine.
example_sentence: The steel beams arrived on a flatbed truck. Place the photograph face down on the flatbed scanner. Workers secured the machinery to the flatbed. A flatbed trailer is useful for carrying oversized loads.

english_meaning: Bread made in a thin, flat shape, usually with little or no yeast. Any of various breads baked as a flat disc or sheet, often on a hot surface.
example_sentence: We served the curry with warm flatbread. She baked the flatbread on a hot stone. This flatbread is made with whole-wheat flour. They topped the flatbread with herbs and cheese.

english_meaning: To make something flat or flatter in shape. To press or beat something down so that it loses height or roundness. To knock someone or something to the ground, often with great force. To completely defeat or overwhelm someone. To remove the differences in level, tone, or detail from something.
example_sentence: Use the rolling pin to flatten the dough evenly. The strong storm flattened several houses in the coastal village. One powerful punch was enough to flatten his opponent. The new policy aims to flatten the differences between the rich and the poor regions. She tried to flatten the curve on the chart by adjusting the data.

english_meaning: To lavish praise and compliments on someone, often insincerely and with a view to furthering one's own interests. To make someone or something appear more attractive or better than they a To praise and compliment someone in a way that makes them feel honored and pleased.
example_sentence: He tried to flatter the manager by complementing his new suit. I feel flattered by your kind words. That color doesn't flatter you at all. She was flattered that he had remembered her birthday. Don't believe him; he's just trying to flatter you into lending him money.

english_meaning: Excessive and insincere praise, given especially to further one's own interests. The act of giving compliments that are not genuine in order to please someone or gain an advantage. Adulation or blandishment used to influence someone's opinion or feelings. A type of false appreciation or honeyed words often used to manipulate a person of higher status.
example_sentence: She used flattery to get her boss to agree to the promotion. Most politicians are accustomed to hearing constant flattery from their supporters. Don't fall for his flattery; he just wants to borrow your car. Imitation is said to be the highest form of flattery. The salesman's flattery was so obvious that it made the customers uncomfortable.

english_meaning: To show something you are proud of to other people, in order to impress them. To display or obtrude oneself to public notice. To present so as to invite notice or attention.
example_sentence: He did not believe in flaunting his wealth. She open flaunted her affair with the senator.

english_meaning: The particular taste of food or drink. A distinctive quality or atmosphere. To give something a particular taste or character.
example_sentence: The soup has a rich flavour. I prefer the lemon flavour of this drink. The experience added a new flavour to the story. Herbs flavour the rice beautifully.

english_meaning: Having a rich, pleasant, or distinctive taste. Full of flavor and satisfying to eat or drink.
example_sentence: The flavourful sauce transformed the simple pasta. These tomatoes are ripe and flavourful. She cooked a flavourful stew with herbs and vegetables. The tea is strong, fragrant, and flavourful.

english_meaning: A substance added to food or drink to give it a particular taste or smell. The act of adding flavor.
example_sentence: Vanilla is a common flavouring in cakes. The manufacturer uses natural fruit flavouring. Add a little flavouring to the milk. The soup needs no extra flavouring.

english_meaning: Having little or no taste or distinctive quality. Bland and lacking flavor.
example_sentence: The soup was watery and flavourless. The doctor recommended a flavourless diet for a few days. Without spices, the beans tasted flavourless. The critic called the speech dull and flavourless.

english_meaning: Having a pleasant and strong taste. Full of flavor and enjoyable to eat or drink.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a flavoursome vegetable curry. This soup is light but very flavoursome. Fresh herbs make the dish more flavoursome. We enjoyed a flavoursome meal at the village restaurant.

english_meaning: A defect in physical structure or form. An imperfection or weakness and especially one that detracts from the whole or hinders effectiveness. To become defective. A mistake in something that means that it is not correct or does not work correctly.
example_sentence: My parents have not been able to find any flaw in my cousin.

english_meaning: Having a fault, defect, weakness, or mistake. Not perfect, reliable, or completely correct.
example_sentence: The report was based on flawed data. Their flawed plan failed under pressure. The argument is logical but flawed. The bridge design was flawed from the beginning.

english_meaning: Without any faults, defects, mistakes, or imperfections. Perfectly executed or exceptionally smooth.
example_sentence: She gave a flawless performance. The jeweler displayed a flawless diamond. His explanation was clear and flawless. The team completed a flawless operation.

english_meaning: In a perfect way, without mistakes or defects. With exceptional smoothness, accuracy, or skill.
example_sentence: The choir performed flawlessly. She executed the plan flawlessly. The machine worked flawlessly throughout the test. He explained the process flawlessly to the new staff.

english_meaning: Having a pale yellow color like flax fibers. Having light yellow or blonde hair. Made of flax. Of a soft, pale golden-yellow shade.
example_sentence: The little girl had long flaxen hair. She braided her flaxen locks into two plaits. The field of ripe wheat looked flaxen in the sun. His flaxen beard was tied with a ribbon.

english_meaning: To strip off the skin of a person or animal. To criticize or scold severely. To whip or beat harshly. To remove an outer layer or covering. To attack verbally with harsh words.
example_sentence: The hunters flayed the animal before preparing the meat. Critics flayed the author for his careless remarks. The minister was flayed in the press for his statement. Cold winds seemed to flay their faces during the trek.

english_meaning: A small wingless jumping insect that lives on the skin of animals (like dogs and cats) and feeds on their blood. Fleas can cause itching and can carry diseases.
example_sentence: The dog was scratching because it had fleas. A flea can jump many times its own height. Flea bites can cause itching and irritation on the skin. They used a special shampoo to kill the fleas on their cat.

english_meaning: A market where second-hand goods are sold. An open-air market or a large indoor venue where people sell used, old, or second-hand items such as clothes, furniture, books, antiques, and collectibles. It is often informal and may operate on weekends or special occasions.
example_sentence: I bought an antique clock from the flea market. Every Sunday, the flea market is full of people looking for bargains. She sells handmade crafts at the local flea market. You can find unique vintage clothes in the flea market.

english_meaning: To develop feathers or to grow enough feathers to fly; also to leave the nest after becoming able to fly. To “fledge” means when a young bird grows feathers that are large and strong enough for flight. It also means the stage when the bird leaves its nest for the first time. In broader use, it can also mean becoming fully developed or ready for independence.
example_sentence: The baby sparrow finally fledged and left the nest. These chicks will fledge in about three weeks. The bird was too weak to fledge properly after the storm. Once they fledge, they start learning to fly on their own.

english_meaning: A young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. A person or organisation that is new and inexperienced. Just beginning to develop or establish itself; immature but showing promise.
example_sentence: The fledgling struggled at the edge of the nest, spreading its wings for the very first time. The company was still a fledgling when it secured its first major contract with a national retailer. She was a fledgling journalist who showed enormous talent and a sharp instinct for a good story. The fledgling democracy faced enormous challenges in its first years of independence. He supported the fledgling organisation with both funding and valuable professional advice.

english_meaning: To leave a person or place very quickly, especially because you are afraid of possible danger. To escape by running away, especially because of danger or fear. To escape by running away, especially because of danger or fear.
example_sentence: She burst into tears and fled. He was caught trying to flee the country. The driver had already fled the scene of the accident. Thousands of refugees fled across the border. The family fled from the war-torn zone.

english_meaning: The woolly coat of a sheep or similar animal. Wool removed from a sheep in one piece. A soft warm fabric resembling sheep’s wool. A jacket made from this fabric. To cheat someone by taking too much money from them.
example_sentence: The farmer collected the sheep’s fleece after shearing. She wore a warm fleece on the hike. This blanket is made from soft synthetic fleece. Dishonest traders tried to fleece the tourists.

english_meaning: Perfectly done or looking great. Used to describe something that is perfectly done, flawless, stylish, or looking extremely good.
example_sentence: Her hair is on fleek today. The makeup artist made her eyebrows look so fleek. His outfit was totally on fleek at the party. The design of this room is on fleek.

english_meaning: A group of ships sailing together or under one command. A number of vehicles or aircraft operated by one organization. Fast and quick in movement. To pass quickly or fade away. The word fleet refers both to a collection of ships, vehicles, or aircraft acting together under unified management and to the quality of being swift or moving rapidly.
example_sentence: The naval fleet sailed across the ocean to participate in the joint exercise. The company has a fleet of more than two hundred delivery trucks. The deer was so fleet that the hunters could not catch it. Years of happiness seem to fleet by all too quickly. The airline expanded its fleet by purchasing several new aircraft.

english_meaning: Lasting for a very short time. Passing quickly. Temporary and brief.
example_sentence: She caught a fleeting glimpse of the bird. Happiness can feel fleeting. A fleeting smile crossed his face. The chance was fleeting, so we acted quickly.

english_meaning: For a very short time. Briefly or momentarily. In a way that passes quickly.
example_sentence: She looked at him fleetingly. The idea crossed my mind fleetingly. Sunlight appeared fleetingly between the clouds. He smiled fleetingly and walked away.

english_meaning: A behavior in which an animal curls back its upper lip, exposing its front teeth, inhales with the nostrils usually closed, and holds this posture. Commonly seen in cats, horses, and other mammals to detect scents. A response that helps transfer pheromones to the vomeronasal organ.
synonyms: ["Lip curl response","Scent analysis","Grimace response","Sniffing gesture","Pheromone detection"]
example_sentence: The stallion showed a flehmen response after smelling the mare. Cats often display flehmen when they detect an unfamiliar odor. Zookeepers noted the tiger performing a flehmen reaction. Flehmen helps animals analyze chemical signals in their environment. The horse curled its lip in a classic flehmen pose.

english_meaning: Soft tissue of the body, especially muscles and fat. The soft part of the human or animal body that covers the bones. Meat of animals used as food. Human nature related to physical desires and weaknesses. Skin or body in a general sense. To add more detail or substance. To develop or expand something by adding more details. To make an idea, plan, or story clearer and more complete. To train or encourage someone or an animal to enjoy something.
example_sentence: The writer needs to flesh out the main character. Let us flesh out the plan before the meeting. She fleshed out her argument with strong evidence. The team is working to flesh out the project proposal.

english_meaning: To bend or stretch a part of the body, especially a muscle or joint. To show off one's strength, wealth, skills, or achievements. To tighten a muscle to display its size or power. To demonstrate ability or influence in a proud manner. A flexible cable or wire used for carrying electric current.
example_sentence: He flexed his arm to show his strong muscles. She loves to flex her new car on social media. Athletes flex their muscles before a big competition. The electrician replaced the old flex behind the television.

english_meaning: The ability to bend or be bent easily without breaking. The quality of being able to change or adapt to new conditions. Willingness to accept different ideas, plans, or ways of working. The ease with which arrangements can be adjusted to suit needs. The physical ability of the body to move its joints and muscles freely.
example_sentence: The flexibility of the material makes it useful for packaging. Working from home gives employees greater flexibility. Daily stretching improves the flexibility of your muscles. The manager showed flexibility by changing the deadline.

english_meaning: Able to bend easily without breaking. Willing or able to change to suit new conditions or situations. Adaptable in nature or approach. Capable of being modified or adjusted. Open to different possibilities.
example_sentence: The gym mat is soft and highly flexible. Good managers must be flexible in their approach. Our working hours are flexible for parents. She has a flexible mind and learns new things quickly.

english_meaning: Having many turns, bends, or windings. Characterized by a series of curves rather than a straight line. Flexible or supple in a way that allows for easy bending or curving. In botany, it refers to stems or structures that zigzag or bend alternately in opposite directions. Not straight or rigid.
example_sentence: The flexuous river wound its way through the lush green valley. The serpent moved in a flexuous motion across the sandy desert. We followed a flexuous path that twisted around the ancient oak trees. The designer drew a flexuous line to represent the flow of the silk fabric. The plant has a flexuous stem that enables it to climb up the trellis easily.

english_meaning: A sudden light blow or movement, especially with the fingers or a whip. A quick, light brush or stroke. To move or hit something with a short, sudden jerk. To turn something on or off with a quick movement of a switch. A slang term for a cinema movie or film. The sound produced by a sudden light snap or movement.
example_sentence: He gave the horse a light flick with the whip to make it move. She flicked the dust off her shoulder with her hand. With a flick of the switch, the room was filled with light. We decided to go see a romantic flick at the theater. He spent the afternoon flicking through the pages of a magazine.

english_meaning: To shine or burn with an unsteady, wavering light. To move quickly with short, irregular movements. A brief, faint appearance of an emotion or feeling. An unsteady light or a small quick movement.
example_sentence: The candle flickered in the cold night breeze. A flicker of hope appeared on her tired face. The old bulb flickered before going out completely. Shadows flickered across the wall as the fire burned.

english_meaning: To deceive or swindle someone. Dishonest or deceptive behavior intended to cheat or trick people. It can also describe meaningless or silly talk that is used to confuse others or avoid giving a clear answer.
example_sentence: The salesman’s promises turned out to be nothing but flimflam. She saw through his flimflam and refused to invest money. Stop all this flimflam and tell me the truth. He tried to flimflam the customers with fake offers.

english_meaning: Thin, weak, and easily broken or torn. Lacking strength, durability, or solidity. Not strong enough to be reliable. Used both for physical objects of poor quality and for arguments, excuses, or evidence that are weak, unconvincing, or unlikely to be believed.
example_sentence: The house was made of flimsy wooden planks. She gave a flimsy excuse for being late again. The evidence presented in court was too flimsy to convict him. He wore a flimsy shirt on the cold winter day. The roof was so flimsy that it leaked during the rain.

english_meaning: To make a sudden small movement because of pain, fear, or surprise. To shrink or pull back from something unpleasant or frightening. To show reluctance to face difficulty or duty. It can describe both a physical reaction and an emotional unwillingness.
example_sentence: He did not flinch when the doctor gave him the injection. She flinched at the loud sound of the explosion. The boxer never flinched, no matter how hard the punch. He didn't flinch from telling the truth, even when it hurt. She flinched at the sight of blood.

english_meaning: To turn or move something so it faces the opposite direction, can also mean to change one’s attitude or opinion.
example_sentence: Flip the chair around to face the window. He flipped around his attitude after talking to her. The picture was flipped around by mistake. The situation flipped around overnight.

english_meaning: To turn or move something back to its previous position, often quickly or with a small motion.
example_sentence: Flip back to page ten for the answer. He flipped back to check his earlier notes. The reader flipped back to the introduction. She flipped back the calendar to see the date.

english_meaning: To turn something off quickly, also a rude gesture meaning to show the middle finger at someone.
example_sentence: Please flip off the lights when you leave. He flipped off the machine after work. The driver flipped off another car in anger. She quickly flipped off her laptop.

english_meaning: To quickly switch something on, usually an electrical device or a feature. To respond suddenly, often with anger or intensity. To direct attention quickly to something.
example_sentence: Flip on the lights, it’s too dark here. He flipped on the radio to hear the news. She flipped on the TV as soon as she got home. The guard flipped on the alarm system. Don’t flip on him just because he disagreed with you. The coach flipped on the players when they weren’t listening.

english_meaning: To suddenly lose control of one’s emotions, to become very angry, excited, or upset. Often used informally to describe an emotional overreaction.
example_sentence: She flipped out when she saw the mess. Don’t flip out, it’s just a small mistake. He flips out every time someone criticizes him. The kids flipped out with excitement at the surprise.

english_meaning: To turn something onto its other side or upside down, can also mean to become very enthusiastic about something.
example_sentence: Flip the pancake over before it burns. She flipped over the magazine to see the back cover. He flipped over the news of his promotion. The car flipped over after hitting the curb.

english_meaning: To look quickly through the pages of a book, magazine, or documents without reading in detail. Browse quickly through pages
example_sentence: She flipped through the catalog for ideas. I flipped through the book but didn’t find the answer. He flipped through his notes before the exam. The reporter flipped through her files during the interview.

english_meaning: To quickly turn, lift, or open something, often by a light or sudden motion. It can also mean to appear unexpectedly.
example_sentence: Flip up the lid to open it. He flipped up his collar in the cold. She flipped up the seat cover. The mechanic flipped up the car hood. She flipped up the lid of the box to see what was inside. He flipped up the page in his book to check the answer.

english_meaning: To change suddenly or repeatedly between two choices or opinions. A light sandal held on the foot by a strap between the toes. A sudden or complete change in opinion, position, or decision.
example_sentence: The politician was criticized for his flip-flop on the tax issue. He tends to flip-flop between different career choices. I bought a new pair of flip-flops for the beach. Her sudden flip-flop surprised everyone in the meeting.

english_meaning: Showing a lack of proper respect or seriousness. Characterized by levity and a dismissive attitude toward something that deserves more gravity. Treating serious matters with inappropriate humor or lack of concern. Not showing a serious or respectful attitude when dealing with someone or something important.
example_sentence: His flippant remark about the tragedy upset everyone in the room. You shouldn't be so flippant when discussing financial security with your family. The student's flippant response to the teacher's question resulted in a detention. Despite the severity of the situation, she maintained a flippant tone during the interview. No one appreciated his flippant attitude toward the sacred traditions of the community.

english_meaning: To rest or remain on the surface of a liquid without sinking. To move or drift slowly through the air or a liquid. To offer a security or company for sale on the stock market for the first time. To suggest an idea or plan to see if it is accepted. An object or device designed to stay on the surface of water to support or mark something.
example_sentence: Empty plastic bottles will easily float on the surface of the lake. The colorful balloons began to float away into the clear blue sky. The company decided to float its shares on the stock exchange next month. She decided to float the idea of a four-day work week during the meeting.

english_meaning: A number of birds of one kind feeding, resting, or traveling together. A large group of people. To gather or go in a flock or crowd. It refers to congregating in large numbers, often moving with a shared purpose or forming a unified herd.
example_sentence: A flock of birds flew over the lake. Sheep graze in a flock. People flocked to the cinema to watch the new movie. Tourists flock to the beach during summer.

english_meaning: To beat someone with a whip or stick as a punishment. To promote or sell something aggressively. It refers to a severe physical punishment inflicted on a person or occasionally vigorous promotion of goods in modern British slang.
example_sentence: He was flogged for his crimes. The merchant tried to flog his cheap goods to the tourists. In ancient times, criminals were frequently flogged. The teacher threatened to flog the disobedient student.

english_meaning: An overflow of a large amount of water beyond its normal limits, especially over land. To cover or become covered with water. To arrive or come in overwhelming numbers or quantities. An outpouring of something such as tears, light, or emails.
example_sentence: The flood destroyed hundreds of homes along the river. Heavy rain flooded the basement overnight. The office was flooded with job applications. Morning light flooded the little room.

english_meaning: An extreme passion or craze for flowers. An obsessive enthusiasm for growing, collecting, or displaying flowers.
example_sentence: Her florimania turned the small balcony into a garden. Seventeenth-century Holland was swept by a famous florimania. His florimania cost him a fortune in rare bulbs. The festival celebrates the town's cheerful florimania.

english_meaning: A soft thread of silk or cotton. To clean between one's teeth with dental floss. It describes fine filaments, or the action of maintaining personal dental hygiene using a specialized thread to remove trapped food.
example_sentence: My dentist told me to floss every day. She bought a new pack of dental floss. It is important to brush and floss regularly. He used a piece of floss to remove the food stuck in his teeth.

english_meaning: A small group of ships or boats. A fleet of small ships or boats, usually organized for a particular purpose such as naval operations, transportation, or fishing. It is smaller than a full navy fleet but still coordinated.
example_sentence: he navy sent a flotilla to patrol the coast. A flotilla of fishing boats left the harbor early in the morning. During the parade, a flotilla of yachts sailed along the river. The explorers traveled in a flotilla across the calm waters.

english_meaning: To grow, develop, or succeed strongly. To thrive in growth, success, or well-being; can also mean to wave something dramatically or showily. A bold or showy gesture; a period of success or growth. Can refer to an impressive or extravagant movement or action, or to a time of prosperity, growth, or achievement
example_sentence: The business flourished after the new management took over. Children flourish in a supportive environment. The artist flourished his brush across the canvas. The musician ended the performance with a flourish. She signed the document with a stylish flourish. The festival was celebrated with great flourish.

english_meaning: To openly disobey, ignore, or show disrespect for a rule, law, custom, or authority. To mock or show contempt for something. To openly reject accepted social norms. To deliberately disregard authority or expectations.
example_sentence: Many drivers flout traffic laws by speeding through red lights. The company was fined because it continued to flout environmental regulations. Some students flout the school dress code despite repeated warnings. He chose to flout tradition and start the ceremony in a completely different way.

english_meaning: To change or vary irregularly and continuously. To rise and fall in number, amount, or intensity. To shift back and forth in a way that is unpredictable or uncertain. To experience frequent and often sudden changes between different levels or states. To waver or vacillate between different opinions or courses of action.
example_sentence: The stock market prices continue to fluctuate based on global economic news. During the storm, the temperature began to fluctuate wildly between warm and cold. Public opinion on the new policy tends to fluctuate depending on the latest media reports. Her moods fluctuate so much that it is difficult to know how she will react today.

english_meaning: Able to speak or write a particular foreign language easily and accurately. Articulate and natural in expression. It describes a smooth, effortless, and continuous flow of speech or writing mastered through practice.
example_sentence: She is fluent in three languages. He gave a fluent presentation without any notes. Practice will help you become highly fluent. The author has a very fluent writing style.

english_meaning: In a flowing or smooth manner. Speaking or writing easily, smoothly, and expressively. It refers to executing language skills effortlessly without taking frequent pauses or making structural errors.
example_sentence: He speaks French fluently. She read the difficult poem fluently. To communicate fluently requires years of practice. You must be able to write fluently to pass the exam.

english_meaning: To spoil by a mistake. To shake or brush something so that it looks larger and, or softer. To make something fluffy. Any light downy material. A soft airy substance or covering. An unintentional departure from truth or accuracy.
example_sentence: Most actors fluff their lines occasionally. The female sat on the eggs, fluffing out her feathers. Let me fluff up your pillows for you. That article was basically a bunch of fluff. It didn't say anything substantive. Her sweater was covered with fluff.

english_meaning: Covered in very soft fur or feathers. Soft, light and containing air. Light and not serious, having no substance, depth or power. Pleasant but not serious or important.
example_sentence: Beat the eggs and sugar together until they are fluffy. It's a fluffy romantic comedy. They thought she was too fluffy to be a serious politician. The fluffy fur of a kitten.

english_meaning: A narrow, artificial channel built to carry water, often used for transporting logs. A deep, steep-sided ravine through which a stream flows. A water slide or ride in which people travel along a channel of flowing water. To transport something by means of such a channel.
example_sentence: Loggers used a wooden flume to move timber down the mountain. The stream rushed through a narrow flume between the rocks. The children queued for the water flume at the park. Water was flumed from the reservoir to the mill.

english_meaning: To confuse somebody so that they do not know what to say or do. To throw into a state of mental uncertainty. (not used in the progressive tenses)
example_sentence: I was flummoxed by her question. He was flummoxed by the legal jargon. The puzzle flummoxed the students. The complicated instructions flummoxed the students. The teacher’s difficult question flummoxed the students.

english_meaning: A small swirling mass of something, especially snow or leaves, moved by sudden gusts of wind. A sudden short period of activity, excitement, or commotion. A brief and light snowfall. A sudden burst of emotion or activity. To move or cause to move in a nervous, hurried way.
example_sentence: A sudden flurry of snow covered the windshield. There was a flurry of activity before the guests arrived. The announcement caused a flurry of excitement in the office. Autumn leaves flew up in a small flurry.

english_meaning: To fly away suddenly. A sudden flow (as of water). A red color that appears on your face or body because you are embarrassed, excited or hot.  A hand of playing cards all of the same suit. To flow and spread suddenly and freely. Having a healthy reddish skin tone.
example_sentence: A pink flush spread over his cheeks. A pink flush spread over his cheeks. The birds were flushed out of the trees.

english_meaning: Having a red or pink colour in the face because of heat, exercise, emotion, embarrassment, illness, or alcohol. Filled with strong emotion such as pride, excitement, or success. Cleaned out with a sudden flow of water, as in a toilet or pipe. Even or level with another surface.
example_sentence: Her cheeks were flushed after the long walk in the sun. He came home flushed with excitement after winning the match. The patient looked flushed and feverish to the doctor. The pipes were flushed thoroughly before the new water was supplied. The cabinet doors are flushed with the wall for a neat look.

english_meaning: To make someone nervous, confused, or agitated. A state of agitated confusion. To upset someone's composure. To become flustered or unsettled. A sudden feeling of nervous excitement.
example_sentence: The sudden question flustered the young student. Try not to fluster the speaker during his presentation. She was in a fluster before the job interview. His calm attitude did not fluster easily under pressure.

english_meaning: To fly unsteadily or hover by flapping the wings quickly and lightly. A state of nervous excitement or confusion. It describes a rapid, trembling physical motion or a psychological feeling of anxious anticipation.
example_sentence: The butterfly fluttered its wings gracefully. He felt a flutter of excitement before his performance. Flags fluttered in the strong breeze. Her heart fluttered when she saw him.

english_meaning: A person or thing that flutters. A bird or insect that moves its wings quickly and lightly. Someone who moves about restlessly or in an unsettled manner. A person who bets small amounts casually, in informal British use.
example_sentence: The butterfly was a delicate flutterer among the roses. He is a restless flutterer who never settles in one job. Every flutterer in the aviary rose at once. She is an occasional flutterer on the horse races.

english_meaning: To flow or move continuously. To keep changing. Continuous movement or change. Flowing of liquid, energy, or particles. A state of uncertainty or instability. In science, the rate of flow through a surface. A substance used to help metals melt or join together.
example_sentence: The weather is in constant flux during the spring season. The company remained in flux after the manager resigned. Scientists measured the magnetic flux in the experiment. Ideas and emotions often flux with time.

english_meaning: A small two-winged insect that often spreads germs and dirt. To move through the air using wings or in an aircraft. To travel or pass very quickly. To operate an aircraft or make something move in the air.
example_sentence: A fly kept landing on the plate of food. Birds fly south before the winter. Time flies when you are busy. He learned to fly a small plane last year.

english_meaning: A bridge that carries one road or railway over another system of traffic. A low-altitude flight by a group of aircraft, often for ceremonial purposes. An elevated road structure designed to bypass busy intersections.
example_sentence: The city council constructed a new flyover to ease the daily traffic jams. A spectacular military flyover marked the beginning of the national day parade. My exit is just after the large concrete flyover on the main highway. The fighter jets performed a synchronized flyover above the stadium.

english_meaning: Extremely angry. To be furious or enraged, often uncontrollably. To be so enraged or furious that it seems uncontrollable, often used metaphorically to describe someone who is visibly seething with anger or reacting violently to a situation
example_sentence: He was foaming at the mouth with anger. They foamed at the mouth over the decision. She foamed at the mouth when insulted. He foamed at the mouth after the argument.

english_meaning: Relating to the center or main point of interest. Having or situated at a focus. It points to the most important or central part of something that overwhelmingly draws attention.
example_sentence: The fireplace is the focal point of the living room. Identifying the focal issues is important for a solution. The museum is a focal point for tourism in the city. Her painting became the focal element of the exhibition.

english_meaning: The center of interest, attention, or activity. The point at which rays of light or sound meet. To concentrate on a particular subject or task. To adjust a lens to produce a clear image.
example_sentence: She lost her focus during the meeting. The camera lens was not in focus. He needs to focus on his studies. The focus of the report is climate change.

english_meaning: To give close attention to something specific, usually by narrowing your view or concentrating on one part of a larger subject. Often used in academic English when discussing research focus or analysis.
synonyms: ["Concentrate on","Zero in on","Pay attention to","Home in on","Highlight"]
example_sentence: The study focuses in on water scarcity in rural areas. The report focuses in on two key economic indicators. The discussion focused in on the main causes of the problem. Researchers focus in on high risk districts to design better plans.

english_meaning: Pay close attention to something. To direct your thoughts, effort, or attention toward a particular subject, task, person, or goal instead of being distracted by other things.
example_sentence: She needs to focus on her studies before the exams. The meeting will focus on climate change adaptation strategies. He tried to focus on his work despite the noise. The report focuses on disaster risk reduction in coastal areas.

english_meaning: To direct attention away from something; to stop concentrating on something.
antonyms: ["Focus on","Concentrate on","Pay attention to","Zero in on"]
example_sentence: During the meeting, he tried to focus out on the minor errors and concentrate on the bigger picture. It’s hard not to focus out on distractions when working from home. She decided to focus out on the negative comments and appreciate the constructive feedback. Instead of worrying about the past, we should focus out on the opportunities ahead.

english_meaning: Food for animals, especially cattle. Dried or fresh food given to animals such as cows, buffaloes, and horses. It also has a figurative meaning, where it refers to material or ideas used for a specific purpose, often in media, discussion, or criticism.
example_sentence: Farmers stored fodder for the winter season. The cows were fed fresh green fodder. His careless comment became fodder for the media. The soldiers were treated as mere fodder in the battle.

english_meaning: An enemy or opponent. Someone who has hostility toward another person or is fighting against them. It refers to an adversary in war, a contest, or strict ideological opposition.
example_sentence: He fought bravely against his deadly foe. They were political foes for many years. A true friend defends you against a foe. The superhero finally defeated his arch foe.

english_meaning: A thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the atmosphere at or near the earth's surface. State of confusion. To become covered with condensation or cause to be obscured.
example_sentence: The morning fog made driving very dangerous. My glasses fogged up when I entered the warm room. Thick fog enveloped the entire city. His brain was in a fog after taking the medication.

english_meaning: The lack of reliable information during military operations, making it difficult for commanders and soldiers to understand the true situation. This uncertainty can result from poor communication, misinformation, hidden enemy movements, changing conditions, or limited visibility. The phrase is also widely used outside the military to describe business, politics, emergency response, sports, cybersecurity, and everyday situations where people must make important decisions despite incomplete or confusing information.
synonyms: ["Uncertainty","Confusion","Ambiguity","Chaos","Lack of clarity","Information gap","Situational uncertainty","Unclear circumstances","Disorder","Battlefield confusion","Information uncertainty","Decision uncertainty"]
example_sentence: The commander had to make a difficult decision in the fog of war. Investors often face a fog of war when markets change unexpectedly. During the cyberattack, the security team worked through the fog of war to identify the source. In the early hours of the disaster, rescue workers operated in the fog of war with very little reliable information.

english_meaning: (superlative of foggy) Describes a place or time with the thickest or heaviest fog. Describes ideas, memories, explanations, or situations that are extremely unclear. The phrase "not the foggiest" means having absolutely no knowledge or understanding.
example_sentence: I haven’t the foggiest idea where she has gone. He hadn’t the foggiest clue about the answer. Don’t ask me, I haven’t the foggiest. She had not the foggiest notion of what was happening in the office. They hadn’t the foggiest about the new rules.

english_meaning: Full of or characterized by fog. Unable to think clearly or confused. It represents extreme weather conditions with poor visibility or a state of mental unclarity and sluggishness.
example_sentence: It was a cold and foggy morning. I only have a foggy memory of my early childhood. The driver slowed down due to the foggy weather. His explanation was rather foggy and hard to understand.

english_meaning: A small weakness, minor fault, or harmless personal habit that makes someone imperfect but often endearing. A slight weakness, imperfection, or peculiar habit in a person's character or behavior. It is usually not serious and may even make the person more relatable or charming. The word can also refer to a minor flaw in a system or plan.
example_sentence: His greatest foible is that he can never arrive on time. She laughs at her father's foible of collecting old newspapers. Every leader has a foible, but honesty can outweigh small flaws. The manager's foible for telling long stories often delayed meetings.

english_meaning: To stop something from happening, especially something illegal, to prevent somebody from doing something. To prevent (someone) from accomplishing something. A particular algorithm for multiplying two binomials. To prevent from attaining an end. To bring to naught. Very thin sheet metal.
example_sentence: They were foiled in their attempt to smuggle priceless paintings.

english_meaning: To impose an unwelcome or unnecessary person or thing on. To secretly introduce something false or inferior. It implies forcing a burden, fake object, or unwanted responsibility onto someone unwilling.
example_sentence: He tried to foist his extra work onto his colleagues. The shopkeeper foisted inferior goods on the unsuspecting tourists. She refused to let them foist their beliefs on her. The bad policy was foisted upon the public.

english_meaning: People of a particular community, nation, or group. Traditional or rural people, often associated with customs, stories, or music. Relating to folklore, folk music, folk art, or common traditions. Informally, family or relatives (“my folks”).
example_sentence: Folk music is popular in many countries. The local folk are very friendly. My folks are coming to visit this weekend. Folk tales often teach moral lessons.

english_meaning: The traditional beliefs, customs, and stories of a community, passed through the generations by word of mouth. It represents a body of popular myth, traditional wisdom, and cultural legends defining a society.
example_sentence: Sindhi folklore is rich with tales of love and bravery. He studies the cultural folklore of ancient tribes. The story of Robin Hood is a classic piece of English folklore. Dragons are a significant part of Chinese folklore.

english_meaning: Refers to people in general, often in a friendly or informal way. Refers to one’s family, especially parents. Can indicate a community or group of people with shared characteristics.
example_sentence: I invited my folks to the party. Folks around here are very friendly. My folks always support my decisions. There are a lot of interesting folks at the festival.

english_meaning: To go or come after someone or something. To act according to instructions, rules, or advice. To understand the meaning of something. To take an interest in and keep up with events or a person. To happen as a result of something else.
example_sentence: Please follow me to the meeting room. You must follow the safety instructions carefully. I could not follow his explanation at all. A long silence followed her announcement.

english_meaning: To remain devoted to someone or something until death. To follow a path or cause right up to the end of one's life. To accompany a dead person's coffin to the burial place. To continue on a course that inevitably leads to one's death.
synonyms: ["Stay loyal until death","Accompany to the end","Remain devoted","Attend a burial"]
example_sentence: He vowed to follow the grave rather than betray his friend. The whole village came to follow the grave of the old teacher. She was loyal enough to follow the grave with him. Some soldiers follow the grave for a cause they truly believe in.

english_meaning: To pursue a curious clue that leads into an unknown world. To let curiosity guide you towards a surprising truth. To begin an adventure by following a strange signal. A popular phrase for chasing hidden knowledge.
synonyms: ["Chase a clue","Explore the unknown","Go down the rabbit hole","Pursue curiosity"]
example_sentence: The message told him to follow the white rabbit. She decided to follow the white rabbit and read the whole archive. Sometimes you must follow the white rabbit to find the truth. The documentary invites viewers to follow the white rabbit.

english_meaning: A person who supports and admires a particular person, belief, or idea. Someone who accepts the leadership of another. A person who subscribes to another's updates on social media. One who comes or travels behind another.
example_sentence: He is a loyal follower of the movement. The singer has millions of followers online. Every great leader needs committed followers. The old teacher had many devoted followers.

english_meaning: Lack of good sense or judgment. A foolish act, idea, or practice. It often describes actions taken without forethought, resulting in a disastrous, costly, or highly absurd outcome.
example_sentence: It would be folly to travel in such bad weather. He realized the folly of his actions too late. Building a house on a swamp was an act of folly. The king's folly led to the downfall of the empire.

english_meaning: To instigate or stir up an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action. It means to deliberately promote trouble, widespread rebellion, or fierce discord among groups of people.
example_sentence: The rebels tried to foment a revolution among the working class. He was arrested for fomenting violence during the protest. Rumors were spread to foment discord within the community. Her provocative speech fomented anger among the listeners.

english_meaning: An object that can carry infectious agents and transmit disease. Any inanimate object or surface that can become contaminated with pathogens like bacteria, viruses, or fungi, and act as a vehicle for infection. Common examples include doorknobs, towels, utensils, or medical instruments. The term is mainly used in medical, epidemiological, and public health contexts.
example_sentence: The doorknob was identified as a fomite in the outbreak. Shared towels in gyms can act as fomites. Hospital instruments are carefully sterilized to prevent fomites. Toys in daycare centers may serve as fomites if not cleaned regularly.

english_meaning: Having an affection or liking for. Having a gentle, loving, and tender feeling towards something or someone. It signifies an enduring warmth and attachment toward a memory, hobby, or individual.
example_sentence: She is very fond of chocolate. He gave her a fond embrace before leaving. I have fond memories of our time at the university. He grew quite fond of the stray dog.

english_meaning: A person who has a strong interest in food, especially in trying and learning about new dishes. A gourmet or lover of fine cuisine. Someone who follows food trends closely. A person who enjoys cooking or eating as a hobby. An enthusiast of culinary culture.
example_sentence: As a true foodie, she travels only to try new cuisines. The blog is followed by foodies from around the world. My cousin is a foodie who reviews every restaurant he visits. Foodies filled the streets during the food festival.

english_meaning: To behave in a silly or playful way, waste time or engage in casual or improper activity. To joke, play, or behave without seriousness. To spend time doing useless or unproductive things. To flirt or have a casual relationship without commitment. To not take something seriously or treat it irresponsibly.
example_sentence: Stop fooling around and finish your homework. The kids were fooling around in the park all afternoon. He got into trouble for fooling around during office hours. She accused him of fooling around with someone else.

english_meaning: Lacking good sense or judgement; unwise. Silly and likely to cause embarrassment. Resulting from a lack of careful thought.
example_sentence: It was foolish to travel without a map. He felt foolish after his mistake was noticed. Do not make foolish promises. That was a foolish way to spend your savings.

english_meaning: Lack of good sense or judgement. Silly behaviour or ideas. An action or remark that shows poor thinking.
example_sentence: His foolishness cost the team the match. I regret the foolishness of my youth. She laughed at the foolishness of the argument. Such foolishness cannot be excused.

english_meaning: False happiness based on illusion. A happy feeling based on something that is not true. A state in which a person feels satisfied or hopeful because they believe something that is unrealistic or false. The comfort is temporary because it is built on an illusion.
example_sentence: He’s living in a fool’s paradise thinking he’ll win. She lived in a fool’s paradise about her marriage. Don’t live in a fool’s paradise. It’s all a fool’s paradise—nothing is real.

english_meaning: The lower part of the leg below the ankle on which a person stands and walks. The part of the body that supports the weight of the whole body. The bottom or lowest part of something, such as a hill, page, or bed. A unit of length equal to twelve inches or about thirty centimetres.
example_sentence: He hurt his right foot while playing cricket. The village lies at the foot of the mountain. A note was printed at the foot of the page. The table is about three feet long.

english_meaning: A small opportunity that could lead to bigger chances. Getting an initial opportunity or first chance.
example_sentence: Her internship gave her a foot in the door at the company. Getting that internship was his foot in the door to the film industry. She volunteered at the hospital just to get her foot in the door for a nursing job. His uncle’s company gave him a small role, which became his foot in the door to a big career. Selling a few products online gave her a foot in the door for starting her own business.

english_meaning: To pay the bill or bear the cost of something, especially when it is large or unexpected. It often suggests paying for others or taking financial responsibility.
synonyms: ["Bear the cost","Settle the bill","Cover the expenses"]
example_sentence: Don't worry, I'll foot the bill for dinner. He invited everyone to dinner and decided to foot the bill himself. The company will foot the bill for the new training program. When the party ended, I had to foot the bill for all the food and drinks. The government will foot the bill for flood relief efforts.

english_meaning: To say something foolish, embarrassing, or inappropriate without thinking, especially in a social situation It describes the act of speaking carelessly and then regretting it because it offends or embarrasses someone.
synonyms: ["Blunder","Slip of the tongue","Verbal mistake","Gaffe","Faux pas","Tactless remark"]
example_sentence: He has a foot-in-mouth disease at parties. He really put his foot in his mouth when he commented on her age. I put my foot in my mouth by mentioning his ex-wife during the party. She often suffers from foot-in-mouth disease because she speaks before she thinks. The manager put his foot in his mouth when he criticized the idea that the director had suggested.

english_meaning: A note, line, or section at the bottom of a page, document, table, or webpage. The bottom area that may contain page numbers, dates, or contact details. A block of information placed after main content in computing. A person or thing positioned at the foot in rare use.
synonyms: ["Bottom note","Page foot","Closing section","End section","Bottom line","Foot","Contact section","Closing information"]
example_sentence: The page number appears in the footer. Add the company address to the footer of every page. The website footer includes privacy links. The report footer shows the file name and date.

english_meaning: A small or firm position that helps someone stand, progress, or gain control. A place where you can put your foot safely while climbing or standing. It also means an initial but stable position that allows growth, influence, or success in a difficult situation
example_sentence: The climber searched carefully for a foothold on the steep rock. The company gained a foothold in the local market after years of effort. She finally found a foothold in her new career. Education gave him a foothold to improve his life.

english_meaning: A note printed at the bottom of a page. Extra information or a reference linked to a word or passage in a text. A minor or supplementary detail. To add a note or reference at the bottom of a page.
example_sentence: The source is listed in a footnote. Please add a footnote explaining the quotation. His role became only a footnote in the larger story. The editor footnoted every historical reference.

english_meaning: Being overly concerned about one's clothes and appearance in a vain way. Dressing in an excessively fashionable and showy manner. Behaving in a manner that seems too refined or artificial. Displaying vanity through dress or manners. Excessively dandyish or affected in style.
example_sentence: He had a foppish manner and always wore fancy clothes. His foppish appearance drew attention at every party. The character in the play was portrayed as a foppish gentleman. She disliked his foppish behavior and boastful talk.

english_meaning: In support of a purpose that is helpful, charitable, or morally right. Done to raise money or awareness for people in need or for society's benefit. Justified by the worthy objective it serves.
synonyms: ["For charity","For a noble purpose","For a worthy cause","In the public interest","For humanitarian ends"]
antonyms: ["For selfish ends","For a bad cause","For personal gain","For a corrupt purpose"]
example_sentence: They organized a charity run for a good cause. Donating to the flood relief fund is money spent for a good cause. The concert was held for a good cause, raising funds for the hospital. She volunteers every weekend for a good cause.

english_meaning: Done for fun, amusement, or as a joke without any serious purpose. Doing something just for enjoyment, curiosity, excitement, or entertainment rather than for profit, necessity, or any serious reason. It often suggests acting on a whim or trying something simply because it seems fun.
synonyms: ["Just for fun","For amusement","As a joke","On a whim","For kicks","For laughs. Recreationally","Casually","Playfully","Out of curiosity"]
example_sentence: We entered the singing competition for a lark, never expecting to win. He dyed his hair green for a lark, just to surprise his friends. They visited the abandoned house for a lark, hoping for an adventure. She applied for the television show for a lark, thinking nothing would come of it.

english_meaning: For a very low price; extremely cheap. Something that is bought or sold at a price much lower than its real value. It often suggests a great bargain or a missed opportunity by the seller.
synonyms: ["Dirt cheap","For next to nothing","At a giveaway price","Cheap as chips"]
example_sentence: He bought that old car for a song at an auction. The house was sold for a song because the owner needed quick cash. She picked up those books for a song at the market. They got the furniture for a song during the clearance sale.

english_meaning: Permanently or forever. Not temporarily
example_sentence: She has moved to Karachi for good. He decided to quit smoking for good. The old bridge was closed for good after the storm. I think they have finished their argument for good.

english_meaning: British informal expression meaning at all, or to any degree — used in negative statements. Used to express that someone cannot do something even to the smallest extent. A colloquial phrase emphasising complete inability. For nothing or for free. Very cheaply. Without any reward or benefit. Sometimes used humorously to mean "without any good reason".
example_sentence: He cannot sing for nuts — it is quite painful to listen to. She admitted she could not cook for nuts and relied entirely on ready meals. I cannot draw for nuts but I enjoy trying anyway. He cannot keep a secret for nuts, which makes him a terrible confidant.

english_meaning: An expression used to show strong emotion such as frustration, anger, or pleading.
example_sentence: For the love of God, please stop shouting. For the love of God, drive carefully!. For the love of God, can you listen for once?. For the love of God, help me finish this work on time.

english_meaning: To search widely for food or provisions, especially in the wild. To hunt or look around for something needed. Food, especially for horses and cattle, obtained by grazing or searching. To make a search or hunt through something. To rummage for what one needs.
example_sentence: Wild animals forage for food throughout the forest. The children love to forage for berries in the summer. Farmers store forage to feed cattle during winter. He had to forage in the drawer to find his keys.

english_meaning: A person or animal that searches widely for food or provisions. Someone who gathers wild food from natural surroundings. A worker or soldier historically sent out to collect food and supplies. An individual who scavenges or hunts around for useful items. A creature dependent on searching rather than farming for sustenance.
example_sentence: The forager returned with a basket full of wild mushrooms. Ants are natural foragers that collect food for the colony. He works as a forager for a well-known restaurant. Early humans were skilled foragers before farming began.

english_meaning: A sudden short attack or raid, especially into enemy territory. A brief attempt or venture into a new activity, field, or area. A short trip made for a specific purpose, such as obtaining something. It can describe both a military incursion and a person's first attempt at something unfamiliar.
example_sentence: The soldiers made a quick foray into enemy territory. Her first foray into politics was surprisingly successful. He made a brief foray into the world of acting. The company's foray into the smartphone market failed. They made a foray into the forest to collect firewood.

english_meaning: To refrain from doing something, especially out of patience or self-control. To hold back from acting on an impulse or provocation. To be patient and tolerant in a difficult situation. An ancestor or forefather from an earlier generation.
example_sentence: She could not forbear from laughing at his remark. He forbore to mention the mistake in front of the guests. Please forbear with me while I explain the situation. Our forbears settled in this valley over two centuries ago.

english_meaning: To order someone not to do something. To officially refuse to allow. To make a rule against something. To prevent or hinder an action.
example_sentence: The teacher forbade the students from using mobile phones in class. Smoking is strictly forbidden in this area. My parents forbid me to stay out late. God forbid such a tragedy should happen again.

english_meaning: Physical strength, power, or energy used on a person or object. Violence or pressure used to make someone do something. A group of people organised for a particular purpose, such as the police or army. In physics, an influence that changes the motion or shape of a body. To make someone do something against their will. To push, break, or open something using physical effort. The legal power or effect of a rule or agreement.
example_sentence: The door was opened by force during the rescue. A large police force was deployed at the stadium. Gravity is the force that keeps us on the ground. Nobody can force you to sign this document.

english_meaning: To push an enemy, crowd, or object backwards by using strength. To restrain or suppress an emotion such as tears or anger. To compel someone to return to a previous place or position. To hold something in check so that it does not appear.
example_sentence: The troops forced the attackers back across the river. She forced back her tears as she said goodbye. Police forced the crowd back from the gate. He forced back a smile during the serious discussion.

english_meaning: To compel an aircraft to land, usually against the pilot's wishes. To make oneself swallow food or drink with difficulty. To push or press something downwards using strength. To reduce prices, levels, or rates through pressure.
example_sentence: Fighter jets forced down the unidentified plane near the border. She forced down a piece of dry bread before leaving. He forced the lid down until it clicked shut. Increased supply has forced down the price of wheat.

english_meaning: The tendency to do something simply because you have always done it. Behaviour repeated automatically without conscious decision. The strong influence that routine has on a person's actions. An action performed out of long practice rather than need. The power of habit to control everyday behaviour.
example_sentence: I still wake up at five out of force of habit. He reached for his keys by force of habit. Force of habit made her take the old route home. Out of force of habit, he checked the door twice.

english_meaning: To make someone accept, take, or endure something against their will. To impose an idea, decision, or duty on a person who does not want it. To press something upon another person insistently. To compel acceptance of a situation through pressure or authority.
example_sentence: She tried to force her opinions on everyone at the meeting. The new rules were forced on the staff without any discussion. Don't force the extra food on him if he is not hungry. A settlement was forced on the villagers by the authorities.

english_meaning: To compel someone to leave a particular place, position, or situation. To extract information, money, or a response from someone unwillingly. To push or press something out of a container or opening. To drive a person or thing away from where it belongs.
example_sentence: The family was forced out of their home by the floods. Detectives finally forced a confession out of the suspect. He was forced out of the race by a knee injury. Rising rents are forcing small shops out of the city centre.

english_meaning: To make a person or animal eat or drink, usually through a tube and against their will. To force information, beliefs, or ideas on someone repeatedly. To supply something in excessive quantity whether it is wanted or not.
example_sentence: The hunger strikers were force-fed by prison doctors. The sick calf had to be force-fed for several days. Students are force-fed facts instead of being taught to think. Viewers are force-fed advertisements every few minutes.

english_meaning: To compel a person to leave a position, job, place, or organization. To drive something out of a space or container by pressure. In baseball, a play in which a runner is put out because he is compelled to advance. The act of pushing or squeezing something out with effort.
example_sentence: The board decided to force out the chief executive after the scandal. He was forced out of the company within a year. She managed to force out a few words between sobs. The runner was retired on a force-out at second base.

english_meaning: A pair of pincers or tweezers used in surgery or in a laboratory. It is a precise medical tool explicitly designed for safely grasping, securely holding, or pulling delicate objects or bodily tissues.
example_sentence: The surgeon asked the nurse for a forcep. The dentist used a forcep to extract the broken tooth. These delicate pieces must be handled with a forcep. The laboratory technician picked up the sample using a sterile forcep.

english_meaning: Using physical force or violence. In a way that is robust, compelling, or completely against someone's will. It describes brutalizing or powerfully executing actions without earning consent from the other party.
example_sentence: The protesters were forcibly removed from the square. He was forcibly confined to his room. The door had been forcibly opened. They forcibly entered the locked building during the raid.

english_meaning: The part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist. The lower section of the arm containing the radius and ulna bones. To prepare or arm oneself in advance against possible danger.
example_sentence: He has a tattoo on his left forearm. The player strengthened his forearms with daily training. She blocked the ball with her forearm. Wise leaders forearm themselves against likely criticism.

english_meaning: An ancestor. A person from whom one is descended. It refers to family members from deeply preceding generations who profoundly figure in a person's genealogical heritage.
example_sentence: His forebears lived in a small farming village. We must honor the traditions of our forebears. She traced her forebears back to the 18th century. Our forebears fought hard for the freedom we enjoy today.

english_meaning: To predict, warn, or have a strong feeling that something (usually bad or unpleasant) is going to happen. To sense or show a warning of coming trouble or misfortune.
example_sentence: Dark clouds forebode a coming storm. Her sudden silence foreboded trouble. The strange behavior of the animals forebodes an earthquake. He had a feeling that the meeting would forebode bad news.

english_meaning: To predict what is likely to happen in the future based on available information. A statement about expected future weather, prices, or events. To estimate future results using data and experience. A calculation of what is expected in business, sales, or economics. To give advance warning of a likely development.
example_sentence: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow. Experts forecast a slow rise in fuel prices. The company's sales forecast for next year looks promising. Nobody could forecast how quickly the situation would change.

english_meaning: To legally take possession of a property because the owner failed to pay a loan. To prevent or rule out a possibility. Mainly used in financial and legal contexts. It refers to a situation where a lender takes control of a borrower’s property when the borrower fails to repay a loan, especially a mortgage. It can also be used in a general sense to describe stopping or preventing something from happening.
example_sentence: The bank decided to foreclose on the house after months of missed payments. His decision to resign foreclosed any chance of promotion. The new law may foreclose future opportunities for small businesses. They tried to negotiate before the lender could foreclose the property.

english_meaning: The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline. The flat front area of the head where a person's expression lines often appear. The front upper surface of the skull.
example_sentence: She wiped the sweat from her forehead with a tissue. The nurse placed her hand on the child's forehead to check for fever. A deep line appeared on his forehead as he concentrated. He kissed his daughter gently on the forehead.

english_meaning: Belonging or connected to a country that is not your own. Coming or introduced from outside a particular place or system. Dealing with or relating to other nations and their governments. Being strange or unfamiliar in nature or character.
example_sentence: He enjoys studying foreign languages and learning about different cultures. The government relies heavily on foreign aid to support its economy. A foreign object was found in the engine block during the inspection. This concept is completely foreign to someone who grew up in a rural area.

english_meaning: Related to courts of law, legal matters, or scientific methods used in crime investigation. Anything connected with the law, especially the use of scientific techniques to investigate crimes. It includes fields like forensic science, forensic medicine, and forensic analysis, where evidence is examined for legal purposes.
example_sentence: The police used forensic evidence to solve the case. She is studying forensic science at university. Forensic experts analyzed the fingerprints carefully. The lawyer presented forensic data in court.

english_meaning: To expect or predict something before it happens. To become aware of a future event in advance, using knowledge, reasoning or intuition. It refers to the ability to anticipate what is likely to happen and prepare for it mentally or practically.
example_sentence: Experts can foresee the effects of climate change on coastal areas. She could not foresee how quickly the project would grow. Good planners try to foresee possible risks before making a decision. No one could foresee that the weather would change so suddenly.

english_meaning: Able to be anticipated or predicted. It describes something that can be reasonably expected to happen based on current knowledge or trends.
example_sentence: The company has no plans to change its policy for the foreseeable future. We need to prepare for any foreseeable complications during the surgery. It was a foreseeable accident that could have been prevented with safety goggles. There are no foreseeable changes to the weather pattern this week.

english_meaning: [past participle of foresee]. To have knowledge or awareness of something before it actually happens. To predict based on evidence or intuition. To expect an outcome ahead of time. Something that was known, expected or predicted before it happened. An event, result or situation that someone already anticipated or expected ahead of time. It shows awareness or prediction before the actual occurrence.
example_sentence: The risks were already foreseen by the experts. She handled the problem calmly because she had foreseen it. The company’s losses could have been foreseen with proper planning. The storm’s impact was not fully foreseen. Dangers foreseen are the sooner prevented. A danger foreseen is half avoided. That is something no one could have foreseen.

english_meaning: Having the ability to predict what is likely to happen in the future. Wise in planning ahead and preparing for future events. Showing careful thought about consequences before acting. Having good judgment about future needs and outcomes. Prudent and far-sighted in decisions.
example_sentence: A foresighted leader prepares the nation for future challenges. He is foresighted enough to invest in education. Her foresighted planning saved the company from major losses. Foresighted farmers store grain for difficult times.

english_meaning: To prevent or obstruct something by taking action in advance. To act ahead of time in order to stop something from happening. To anticipate and act before another person can. To delay or stop an event by precautionary measures. To buy up goods in advance to control the market.
example_sentence: The government took strict measures to forestall a possible riot. She spoke quickly to forestall any objections from the audience. The company lowered its prices to forestall competitors. Early diagnosis can forestall many serious diseases. He resigned to forestall being dismissed by the board.

english_meaning: The forward or leading part of a tail-like structure. In older usage, a portion set aside or reserved in advance. A rarely used term referring to something that trails at the front rather than behind.
synonyms: ["Front part","Fore section","Leading end","Prow","Forepart","Reserved portion","Advance share","Head","Front end","Foresection"]
example_sentence: The carving showed a strange creature with a long foretail. He explained that the foretail of the estate had been reserved by an earlier deed. Sailors used the word foretail for the trailing rope at the bow. The term foretail appears only in a few old manuscripts.

english_meaning: To lose or lose the right to especially by some error, offense, or crime. Something deposited (as for making a mistake in a game) and then redeemed on payment of a fine. To lose something or have something taken away from you because you have done something wrong.
example_sentence: If you cancel your flight, you will forfeit your deposits. He has forfeited his right to be taken seriously.

english_meaning: To avert, keep away, or prevent something evil. Often deeply used in old exclamations wishing heavenly powers to fervently protect someone from a terrible or agonizing fate.
example_sentence: Heaven forfend that such a disaster should ever happen here. He prayed that the gods would forfend the coming storm. They took every precaution to forfend tragedy. May the saints forfend us from evil times.

english_meaning: To create something strong, enduring, or successful. To produce a fraudulent copy or imitation. It means forging alliances, shaping metals in a fire, or deceitfully creating documents.
