example_sentence: He was convicted of an attempt to forge a passport. The two countries forged a strong alliance. The blacksmith shaped the glowing iron in his forge. She forged her mother's signature on the permission slip.

english_meaning: To create your own direction in life instead of following others. It means making independent choices, building your own career or identity, and taking responsibility for your journey.
synonyms: ["Create your own way","Go your own way","Carve your own path","Be independent","Follow your own direction","Blaze your own trail"]
antonyms: ["Follow the crowd","Conform to others","Imitate others","Depend on others","Walk a beaten path"]
example_sentence: She decided to forge her own path and start a business instead of joining a corporate job. Rather than following family traditions, he forged his own path in the arts. Young entrepreneurs are encouraged to forge their own path and think creatively. He left his hometown to forge his own path and explore new opportunities.

english_meaning: The action of producing a copy of a document, signature, banknote, or work of art for the purpose of deception. A fake or exact duplicate item knowingly presented as an authentic piece.
example_sentence: The painting was proven to be a clever forgery. She is currently serving a prison sentence for forgery. The bank detected a forgery on the submitted cheque. The expert could easily spot the differences in the forgery.

english_meaning: Ready and willing to excuse or pardon someone's mistakes or offenses. Showing mercy or leniency instead of seeking punishment or revenge. Having a character or disposition that does not harbor resentment or grudges. Designed to be easy to use or to accommodate errors without negative consequences. Characterized by a generous spirit that overlooks faults in others.
example_sentence: She has a very forgiving nature and never holds a grudge against her friends. The new software is very forgiving of user errors and allows for easy corrections. He was in a forgiving mood and decided not to press charges. A forgiving landscape or climate makes survival much easier for early settlers.

english_meaning: To willingly decide not to take, use, or enjoy something that is available or desirable. To abstain from something voluntarily. To give up a benefit or opportunity. To go without something. To refrain from taking or doing something. To sacrifice for a greater goal. To deliberately avoid something. To decline politely.
example_sentence: She decided to forgo dessert to maintain her diet. He chose to forgo the promotion to spend more time with family. They had to forgo their vacation due to financial issues. Students sometimes forgo sleep before exams.

english_meaning: To give up or skip a fast, choosing not to observe it. To break or not keep a religious fast, sometimes due to a valid reason such as illness or travel. To deliberately abstain from fasting. To leave out the act of fasting that one would normally perform.
synonyms: ["Skip a fast","Break a fast","Omit fasting","Abstain from fasting","Give up fasting"]
antonyms: ["Keep a fast","Observe a fast","Maintain fasting","Complete a fast"]
example_sentence: She had to forgo the fast because she was unwell. Travelers are allowed to forgo the fast and make it up later. He decided not to forgo the fast despite the long journey. Patients may forgo the fast on a doctor's advice. They were warned not to forgo the fast without a valid reason.

english_meaning: An implement with two or more prongs used for lifting food to the mouth or digging. The point where a road or river divides into two distinct parts. To naturally divide into branches.
example_sentence: Please place a knife and fork next to the plate. Turn left when you reach the fork in the road. The river forks about two miles from here. He used a pitchfork to move the hay in the barn.

english_meaning: Sad, lonely, and unhappy, especially because of being left alone or abandoned. Looking pitiful and miserable. (Of a place) Empty, deserted, and giving a feeling of sadness. (Of hope or attempt) Unlikely to succeed; almost hopeless.
example_sentence: The little boy looked forlorn at the railway station. She gave him a forlorn smile as he walked away. The old house stood forlorn at the end of the street. They made one last forlorn attempt to save the project. He felt forlorn after his best friend moved to another city.

english_meaning: Done in accordance with established rules, customs, or official procedures. Suitable for serious or official occasions rather than everyday use. Relating to the outward form or structure rather than the content. Polite and reserved in manner rather than friendly and relaxed.
example_sentence: Please submit a formal application before the deadline. Guests were asked to wear formal dress for the dinner. He made a formal apology on behalf of the company. Their conversation remained polite and rather formal.

english_meaning: The way in which something is arranged or set out. To arrange or put into a particular form, especially preparing a computer drive or text document for official usage.
example_sentence: The meeting will follow a standard format. I need to format my hard drive before selling the computer. They changed the formatting of the magazine this month. Please submit your essay in the correct format.

english_meaning: A colourless, sharp-smelling acid found naturally in ant venom and nettles. A simple carboxylic acid with the chemical formula HCOOH. A chemical used in leather processing, textiles, and preservatives. A corrosive liquid used in industry and laboratories.
example_sentence: Ant stings burn because of formic acid. Formic acid is widely used in the leather industry. The students prepared formic acid in the laboratory. Formic acid can irritate the skin and eyes.

english_meaning: A hard, durable plastic laminate used for covering surfaces such as tables and counters. A trade name for a heat-resistant laminated sheet material. A genus of ants in scientific classification. A smooth, easy-to-clean surfacing material used in kitchens.
example_sentence: The kitchen counter was covered with white Formica. Formica surfaces are easy to clean and maintain. They replaced the old Formica table with a wooden one. Ants of the genus Formica are common in forests.

english_meaning: Inspiring fear, respect, or awe because of size, strength, or ability. Difficult to deal with, defeat, or overcome. Impressively powerful or capable. Causing worry because of seriousness or difficulty.
example_sentence: They faced a formidable opponent in the final match. She has a formidable reputation as a lawyer. The mountain presented a formidable challenge to the climbers. He built a formidable collection of rare books.

english_meaning: In a way that inspires fear, respect, or awe. To an impressive or intimidating degree. In a manner that is difficult to overcome. Powerfully and strikingly.
example_sentence: The team was formidably prepared for the tournament. She is formidably intelligent and hardworking. The fortress was formidably built on high rocks. He argued formidably against the proposal.

english_meaning: A person who strongly supports or follows a particular form, rule, or system.
example_sentence: He is such a formite that he refuses to change the traditional format of the meeting. The manager acted like a formite, insisting on strict adherence to company rules. As a formite, she prefers classical designs over modern trends. The teacher was known as a formite because she followed the curriculum without deviation.

english_meaning: Having no clear shape, structure, or outline. Lacking definite form or organization. Vague and difficult to describe or define. Without a fixed physical or artistic form.
example_sentence: A formless mist covered the valley at dawn. His fears were vague and formless. The clay was still a formless lump. The essay felt formless and hard to follow.

english_meaning: To have sexual intercourse between people who are not married to each other. To engage in voluntary sexual intercourse between two people who are not legally married to each other.
synonyms: ["Commit adultery","Engage in premarital sex","Have illicit relations","Copulate"]
example_sentence: The preacher warned the congregation not to fornicate before marriage. In some ancient societies, people were punished if they fornicated. Certain religious teachings strongly discourage individuals from fornicating. The law in that era treated those who fornicated very strictly.

english_meaning: Sexual intercourse between people who are not married to each other. Voluntary unlawful sexual relations outside marriage. In religious usage, sexual immorality in general.
example_sentence: The law of that country still treats fornication as a punishable offence. He preached against fornication and dishonesty. The novel deals openly with fornication and its consequences. Charges of fornication were brought against both parties.

english_meaning: To abandon someone or something. To leave a person, place, duty, or belief entirely. To give up or renounce a habit, practice, or way of life. To desert someone in a time of need.
example_sentence: He promised never to forsake his family. She chose to forsake luxury and live simply. Many villagers had to forsake their homes during the flood. A true friend will not forsake you in trouble.

english_meaning: A thing at which someone powerfully excels. A person's strongest suit or deeply special ability. In instrumental music, it commands sections to be forcefully and loudly played.
example_sentence: Cooking is definitely not my forte. Mathematics has always been her forte. He played the musical piece forte, as instructed by the conductor. Though she sings well, dancing is her true forte.

english_meaning: It describes something that is planned to happen or appear in the near future. It refers to a person who is candid, open, and willing to divulge information. It denotes help or resources that are ready and available when needed.
example_sentence: Details of the event will be announced in the forthcoming week. The witness was not very forthcoming with information during the interrogation. Financial aid was quickly forthcoming after the natural disaster struck. Her forthcoming book is expected to top the bestseller list.

english_meaning: Immediately, without delay. Straight away. It strictly dictates that an action must be executed instantly, with zero hesitation or further prolonged waiting times.
example_sentence: The contract is to be signed forthwith. He ordered the guards to release the prisoner forthwith. If you break the rules, you will be dismissed forthwith. We requested that the errors be corrected forthwith.

english_meaning: Courage and strength to face difficulty or pain. The mental and emotional strength that enables a person to endure adversity, pain, or challenges with patience and resilience. It reflects inner courage and steadfastness in difficult situations.
example_sentence: She showed remarkable fortitude during her long illness. The soldiers faced the storm with fortitude. He endured the criticism with fortitude and dignity. Fortitude helped her overcome the challenges of life.

english_meaning: A period of two weeks. Fourteen consecutive days.
example_sentence: The course lasts a fortnight. We will return in a fortnight. She spent a fortnight visiting relatives in the countryside. The notice must be submitted within a fortnight.

english_meaning: Happening by chance rather than by plan. Lucky or fortunate in an unexpected way. Accidental but producing a good result. Occurring without deliberate intention or clear cause.
example_sentence: Their fortuitous meeting led to a successful partnership. A fortuitous delay saved us from the storm. The discovery was fortuitous but extremely valuable. It was fortuitous that a doctor happened to be nearby.

english_meaning: Having good luck or receiving favorable outcomes. Lucky in a particular situation or in life generally. Blessed with success, wealth, or advantages that others may not have. Occurring by a happy chance rather than by design. Being in a position of advantage or privilege.
example_sentence: She feels fortunate to have such a supportive family. He was fortunate enough to survive the accident without injury. We are fortunate to live in a peaceful neighborhood. It was fortunate that the rain stopped before the ceremony began.

english_meaning: Chance or luck as an external, arbitrary force affecting human affairs. A large amount of money or assets. It profoundly represents massive wealth or the unexpected events structurally shaping one's destiny.
example_sentence: He made a massive fortune in the stock market. Fortune favors the brave. She had the good fortune to meet the president. Buying that luxury car must have cost a fortune.

english_meaning: The remains or impression of a prehistoric plant or animal embedded in rock and preserved in petrified form. Slang for someone who is completely outdated or stubbornly opposed to societal change.
example_sentence: The archaeologists discovered a rare dinosaur fossil. Fossil fuels are non-renewable energy sources. He is considered a bit of an old fossil by the younger generation. The museum has a vast collection of plant fossils.

english_meaning: To encourage the development of something. To lovingly bring up a child that is not one's own by birth. Raising, nursing, or richly nurturing ideas, familial relations, or living beings over time.
example_sentence: She fostered several children over the years. The school aims to foster a love of reading. Good communication fosters strong relationships. They became a foster family for the abandoned puppy.

english_meaning: A boy who is raised by the same foster parents as another child, but is not related by blood. A male child in a family that takes care of children not born to them. A boy brought up in the same household as another under foster care. A non-biological brother sharing the same guardians. A brother by upbringing, not by birth.
example_sentence: He grew up with his foster brother in a small village. My foster brother and I are very close, though not related by blood. They treat each other as real siblings even though he is her foster brother. His foster brother helped him through difficult times.

english_meaning: A girl raised by the same foster parents as another child, without a blood relation. A female child brought up in a foster family alongside another child. A sister by upbringing rather than by birth. A non-biological sister sharing the same guardians. A girl treated as a sister through foster care.
example_sentence: Her foster sister was like a real sister to her. He often visits his foster sister on holidays. The two foster sisters share a strong emotional bond. My foster sister taught me how to cook.

english_meaning:
Offensive to the senses. Constituting an infringement.
Full of dirt or mud. To tangle or come into collision with. Placed in a situation that impedes physical movement. Being vulgar or insulting.
example_sentence: The medicine left a foul taste in my mouth. The foul smelling grease turned her stomach

english_meaning: The lowest load-bearing part of a building, typically below ground level. An underlying basis or principle on which something is built or established. An institution or organization that is established with an endowment for a specific purpose, such as charity or research. A tinted cream or powder used as a base for makeup to create an even skin tone. The action of establishing an institution, organization, or theory. The quality of being grounded in fact or truth.
example_sentence: The workers poured concrete to create a solid foundation for the new skyscraper. Trust is the foundation of any healthy and long-lasting relationship. The charitable foundation provides scholarships to underprivileged students every year. She applied a light layer of foundation to even out her complexion before the photo shoot.

english_meaning: A person who starts an organization, company, institution, or movement. Someone who establishes something and shapes its original purpose. A person who provides the initial idea, resources, or leadership for a new venture. In metalworking, a worker who casts metal objects. A hoof disorder in horses caused by inflammation, also called laminitis.
example_sentence: The founder explained why she started the company. He was a founder of the local arts society. Every founder must learn when to delegate responsibility. The veterinarian treated the horse for founder.

english_meaning: A management style in which a company founder remains deeply involved in important details and decisions. Direct leadership that cuts through layers of management and communicates across levels. An intense, hands-on approach intended to preserve the founder’s vision, speed, and standards. Informally, a period of highly focused and personally driven work by a founder.
example_sentence: The chief executive returned to founder mode during the crisis. Founder mode helped the small company make decisions quickly. Critics warned that founder mode could weaken experienced managers. She entered founder mode and reviewed the product with every team.

english_meaning: A workshop or factory where metal is melted and cast into shapes. A place where metal casting is carried out. A works producing type for printing.
example_sentence: His grandfather worked in an iron foundry. The foundry produces engine parts for tractors. Sparks flew across the floor of the busy foundry. The old foundry has been turned into an art gallery.

english_meaning: An ornamental structure in a pool or lake from which one or more jets of water are pumped into the air. A natural flowing spring of water, or a continuous source of a highly desirable quality.
example_sentence: The city park features a magnificent water fountain. He is a fountain of knowledge on history. The children played joyfully around the fountain. Water flowed continuously from the stone fountain.

english_meaning: The original source or spring of a stream or river. The primary origin of something, such as an idea or movement. A chief source of inspiration or authority. The starting point from which something develops. A person or place seen as the ultimate origin.
example_sentence: The Himalayas are the fountainhead of many great rivers. Greek philosophy was the fountainhead of Western thought. She is considered the fountainhead of the reform movement. His writings became the fountainhead of modern poetry.

english_meaning: A mathematical operation that converts a signal from the time domain into the frequency domain. A method of expressing a function as a sum of sine and cosine waves of different frequencies. A tool used in signal processing, physics, and engineering to analyse the frequency content of data. The resulting frequency representation of a signal.
example_sentence: The Fourier transform shows which frequencies dominate the signal. Engineers use the fast Fourier transform for real-time analysis. He applied a Fourier transform to filter out background noise. The Fourier transform of a pure tone is a single sharp peak.

english_meaning: A bird of any kind, especially one kept for eggs or meat. Domestic birds such as chickens, ducks, turkeys, or geese. The flesh of such birds used as food. To hunt or catch wild birds. A general term for poultry.
example_sentence: The farmer keeps many kinds of fowl. Roast fowl is served at the feast. Wild fowl fly overhead during winter. He went out early to fowl in the marshes.

english_meaning: A person who hunts or traps wild birds. Someone whose occupation is catching fowl. A bird-catcher, often for sport or food. One who deals in poultry or wild birds. A hunter specializing in birds.
example_sentence: The fowler set traps in the marsh before dawn. In old times, a fowler earned his living from selling birds. The village fowler was known for his skill with nets. The fowler returned home with a bag full of ducks.

english_meaning: Cunning, sly, or clever like a fox. Physically very attractive (slang). Having reddish-brown coloring inherently akin to a native fox. The primary meaning points deeply to being a crafty and cunning individual.
example_sentence: He had a foxy smile that made me suspicious. It was a foxy plan to trick his enemies. She looked very foxy in her new red dress. The foxy salesman convinced them to buy a faulty car.

english_meaning: A clever, cunning, and shrewd way of thinking. A mind that is quick, sly, and capable of outsmarting others. A person with a foxy mind is intelligent and tricky, often using craftiness to achieve goals. The expression highlights cleverness mixed with a touch of slyness.
synonyms: ["Cunning mind","Shrewd mind","Sly mind","Crafty mind","Clever mind","Astute mind","Wily mind"]
example_sentence: He has a foxy mind and always finds a way out of trouble. With his foxy mind, he easily outsmarted his opponents in the deal. A politician with a foxy mind is hard to defeat. Her foxy mind helped her solve the puzzle in minutes. Only someone with a foxy mind could plan such a clever strategy.

english_meaning: Wonderful, delightful, or splendid. Remarkably joyful or excellent. Used playfully to describe something highly pleasing. Fabulous in an imaginative or whimsical way.
example_sentence: We had a frabjous afternoon at the festival. The children declared the enormous cake absolutely frabjous. Her frabjous costume delighted everyone at the party. What a frabjous piece of news this is!

english_meaning: A small part or amount of something. A numerical quantity that is not a whole number, such as one half. A tiny proportion of a larger whole. A separated portion of a mixture in chemistry.
example_sentence: He bought the car for a fraction of its value. Students learned to add fractions today. Only a fraction of the audience stayed till the end. She paused for a fraction of a second.

english_meaning: A break or crack in a bone or other hard material. To break or crack something. A break or disruption in a relationship, system, or agreement.
example_sentence: He sustained a fracture to his wrist during the fall from the bicycle. The earthquake caused fractures to appear in the walls of dozens of buildings. The scandal caused a serious fracture in the previously unified party. She returned to training six weeks after the hairline fracture was diagnosed.

english_meaning: A small fold or delicate ridge of tissue that supports or physically checks the free movement of the body part to which it is attached, such as the small layer beneath the tongue.
example_sentence: The doctor noted that a tight fraenulum was causing the baby's feeding issues. Snapping the fraenulum can cause a bit of bleeding. A surgery was performed to release his lingual fraenulum. The upper lip fraenulum keeps the lip anchored to the gums.

english_meaning: To deliberately kill an unpopular senior officer with a fragmentation grenade (military slang). Also widely used in modern gaming communities to mean eliminating an opponent. A small shattered fragment.
example_sentence: He managed to frag three opponents in the multiplayer match. The term originated in the Vietnam War when soldiers would frag their officers. I scored the final frag to win the game. She fragged the enemy sniper just in time.

english_meaning: Easily broken, damaged, or weakened. Something that lacks strength or durability. It can refer to physical objects like glass or emotional states such as confidence or health. It is also used for delicate situations or systems that can be disturbed easily.
example_sentence: This package contains fragile items so keep it upright. Be careful not to drop it; it’s very fragile. The economy remains extremely fragile. In her job she was used to dealing with actors’ fragile egos. The woman's fragile face broke into a smile. Her father is now 86 and in fragile health.

english_meaning: A small piece broken off or separated from something larger. An incomplete or isolated portion of something. As a verb, to break or cause something to break into small pieces or parts. Often used to describe the remains of something that has been broken, damaged, or left incomplete.
example_sentence: Fragments of broken glass were scattered across the floor. The archaeologist found a fragment of an ancient pottery bowl. The explosion fragmented the rock into dozens of pieces. Only a fragment of the original manuscript has survived. The mirror fragmented into hundreds of tiny pieces when it hit the ground.

english_meaning: A pleasant, sweet smell. A natural or artificial scent. The aroma given off by flowers, perfumes, or spices. A quality that makes something smell attractive.
example_sentence: The fragrance of roses filled the garden. She wore a light fragrance to the party. Fresh coffee has a wonderful fragrance. The room was full of the fragrance of jasmine.

english_meaning: Weak and highly delicate. Easily damaged or immediately broken. Often refers to an older person who is physically weak due to old age or a structure that completely lacks heavy sturdiness.
example_sentence: The old woman's health is very frail. He spoke in a frail, trembling voice. The delicate flowers looked frail in the strong winter wind. Our local economy remains frail despite the recent reforms.

english_meaning: A basic structure underlying a system, concept, or text. The supporting structure around which something is built. A set of rules, ideas, or beliefs that you use in order to deal with problems or to decide what to do. The structural skeleton of a physical object.
example_sentence: The new law provides a legal framework for settling disputes. We need to establish a theoretical framework before starting the research. The building has a steel framework to support its weight. The negotiations were conducted within the framework of the United Nations.

english_meaning: An authorization granted by a company or government to an individual or group to operate a business or service under the company's name and system. A right or privilege officially given to a person or organization. A professional sports team that is a member of a league. The right to vote in public elections.
example_sentence: She bought a franchise from a well-known fast-food chain and opened her first restaurant. The football franchise has won three championships in the past decade. The government granted a franchise to the telecommunications company to operate in the region. Owning a franchise gives entrepreneurs the advantage of an established brand. The new franchise agreement included strict guidelines on product quality and customer service.

english_meaning: A person or company that has been granted a franchise to sell a company's goods or services in a specific area. An individual or business that operates under a franchisor's brand and system by paying a fee or royalty. The party that receives the rights in a franchise agreement.
example_sentence: The franchisee was responsible for maintaining the brand standards set by the parent company. As a new franchisee, she attended a two-week training programme before opening her store. The franchisee paid a monthly royalty fee to the franchisor based on total sales. He became a successful franchisee after years of working in the retail industry. The franchisee agreement clearly outlined the rights and responsibilities of both parties.

english_meaning: Open, honest, and direct in speech. Saying what one really thinks without hiding anything. Free from disguise or pretence. To mark a letter so it can be posted free of charge.
example_sentence: To be frank, I did not enjoy the film. She gave a frank account of the accident. He was frank about his own mistakes. The office franked the envelopes before posting them.

english_meaning: Honestly, directly, without hiding feelings. Used to express that one is speaking in an open, honest, and straightforward way, often about something that might be uncomfortable or blunt. It emphasizes sincerity or frankness.
example_sentence: Frankly, I don’t think this plan will work. She spoke frankly about the challenges she faced. I’ll tell you frankly, I was disappointed with the outcome. Frankly, he should have apologized earlier.

english_meaning: Extremely worried, anxious, or hurried. Feeling or showing intense fear, anxiety, or excitement; acting in a hurried or uncontrolled way due to stress or urgency
example_sentence: She made a frantic search for her lost keys. The parents were frantic when their child did not return home. He gave a frantic effort to finish the project on time. The crowd was in a frantic rush to escape the storm.

english_meaning: Of or befitting a brother or brothers. Characterized by a sense of brotherly fellowship and camaraderie. Relating to a social organization or society of people sharing common interests. Derived from two separate fertilized eggs, as in twins. Involving members of the same profession or group working together in unity. Expressing goodwill and mutual support among individuals.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a treaty to promote fraternal relations and cooperation. They shared a fraternal bond that lasted throughout their military service. The university's fraternal organizations host several charity events each year. Fraternal twins do not always look identical because they develop from different eggs.

english_meaning: Two children born at the same birth who developed from two separate fertilized eggs. Non-identical twins who share about fifty percent of their genetic material like ordinary siblings. Twins who can be of the same or different sex and may not look alike. Siblings born together but from different ova. Dyzogotic twins.
synonyms: ["Dizygotic Twins","Non-identical Twins","Biovular Twins","Binovular Twins","Dissimilar Twins","Sibling Twins","Multizygotic Twins","Heterologous Twins","Two-egg Twins","Non-monozygotic Twins","Pair Of Siblings","Doublets"]
example_sentence: Fraternal twins are no more genetically similar than regular siblings born at different times. The doctor explained that since they were different genders, they must be fraternal twins. Unlike identical twins, fraternal twins do not share the exact same DNA profile. My cousins are fraternal twins; one has curly black hair while the other has straight blonde hair.

english_meaning: A group of people sharing same profession, interests, belief, Feeling of friendship, support that exists between member of group
example_sentence: The ideals of liberty, equality & fraternity.

english_meaning: The killing of one's own brother or sister. The crime of murdering a sibling. The accidental killing of soldiers by their own side in war. A person who kills a brother.
example_sentence: The ancient legend ends in fratricide. He was imprisoned for fratricide after the quarrel. Modern armies use technology to prevent fratricide on the battlefield. The civil war was described as national fratricide.

english_meaning: The crime of cheating someone to gain money or advantage. A person who deceives others by pretending to be someone else. A deceitful act or trick. Dishonest business or financial practices. False representation intended to mislead.
example_sentence: He was arrested for committing bank fraud. That online seller turned out to be a fraud. Insurance fraud costs companies billions each year. The scheme was exposed as a complete fraud.

english_meaning: Done in an intentionally dishonest or deceptive way, especially to gain an unfair or illegal advantage. Based on fraud or involving deliberate deception for personal or financial gain. Not genuine or authentic; false and misleading.
example_sentence: The company was shut down after investigators discovered fraudulent accounting practices. He was arrested for making fraudulent claims on his insurance policy. The fraudulent documents were identified by an expert within minutes. Several employees were fired for their involvement in a fraudulent scheme. The court declared the contract void because it was signed under fraudulent circumstances.

english_meaning: Full of or accompanied by something undesirable, especially anxiety, tension, or difficulty. Causing or feeling great worry or stress. Loaded with or characterized by a particular quality, especially a negative one.
example_sentence: The negotiations were fraught with tension and neither side was willing to compromise. Her journey to the border was fraught with danger and uncertainty. The project launch was fraught with technical difficulties from the very beginning. Managing a large team can be fraught with challenges if communication is not clear. The relationship between the two leaders has always been fraught with mistrust.

english_meaning: To cause fabric, rope, or material to become worn or unravel at the edges through rubbing or use. A situation involving conflict, argument, or competitive struggle, especially one that is intense or chaotic. To become weakened, strained, or damaged, especially in relation to nerves, emotions, or relationships. To enter into or join a fight, conflict, or competitive struggle.
example_sentence: The edges of the carpet began to fray after years of foot traffic.  Tempers began to fray as the negotiations dragged on for hours.  Several new candidates have entered the political fray ahead of the election.  Her patience started to fray after the third delay.  The two companies were drawn into a bitter legal fray over the contract.

english_meaning: Having threads or fibers worn away or loosened at the edge of fabric, rope, or material due to wear or rubbing. Showing signs of strain, exhaustion, or breakdown, especially in relationships, emotions, or nerves. Worn down through repeated use or stress, often to the point of damage. Used to describe something that is becoming weak, unraveled, or close to breaking.
example_sentence: The old rope was frayed and looked dangerous to use for climbing.  Months of stress had left his nerves completely frayed.  She noticed the frayed edges of the antique tablecloth.  Their friendship became frayed after the heated argument.  The frayed cable needed to be replaced before it caused an accident.

english_meaning: To wear out, to exhaust. To make someone or something extremely tired or stressed physically or mentally. A state of extreme tiredness, nervous strain, or being worn out. It can describe both mental and physical exhaustion, often from continuous work or stress.
example_sentence: After the long hike, I was completely frazzled. The kids left me feeling frazzled after a full day at the park. She looked frazzled after finishing the report under tight deadlines. He’s frazzled from managing both work and home responsibilities.

english_meaning: Something that is provided free of charge, often as a promotional gift. This is a common variant spelling of 'freebie'.
example_sentence: The magazine comes with a freebee lipstick attached to the cover. I managed to score a freebee ticket to the concert from my cousin. The tech conference was full of freebee pens and notebooks. Everyone loves a good freebee when shopping online.

english_meaning: A thing given free of charge. It is typically used to refer to promotional items or complimentary services provided by businesses.
example_sentence: The hotel provides small bottles of shampoo as a freebie. I got this t-shirt as a freebie at the marathon. Many apps offer a freebie version to entice users to buy the full software. Reporters often get a freebie meal at grand press events.

english_meaning: Past tense and past participle of 'free'. It means to have been released from confinement, slavery, or physical restraint.
example_sentence: The prisoners were finally freed after years of negotiation. She freed the bird from the tangled net and watched it fly away. He felt freed from a heavy burden once he told the truth. The soldiers freed the town from the occupying forces.

english_meaning: The power or right to act, speak, think, or choose without undue restraint. The state of not being imprisoned, enslaved, or controlled. Political independence or self-government. Release from an unwanted condition, burden, or obligation. Ease and openness in movement or expression.
example_sentence: Freedom of speech is a basic right. The prisoner finally regained his freedom. The nation fought for freedom from foreign rule. Financial freedom allowed her to choose meaningful work.

english_meaning: To turn into ice or become solid because of extreme cold. To make something very cold or to preserve food by keeping it below zero. To stop moving suddenly and stay completely still, usually out of fear or surprise. To hold prices, wages, or funds at a fixed level so that they cannot change. A period of very cold weather, or an official stop on spending, hiring, or prices.
example_sentence: The pond will freeze if the temperature drops any further. You can freeze the leftover soup and use it next week. She froze the moment she heard footsteps behind her. The government announced a freeze on public sector hiring.

english_meaning: To become completely still because of fear, shock, or surprise. To stop moving instantly and be unable to continue. To be so startled that you cannot take another step. To make someone stand motionless with fright. To halt suddenly as if unable to move at all.
example_sentence: I froze in my tracks when I saw the snake on the path. The sudden shout froze him in his tracks. She froze in her tracks at the sound of breaking glass. The headlights froze the deer in its tracks.

english_meaning: To deliberately exclude someone from a group, activity, or conversation. To force a person or company out of a business or market by unfair competition. To make someone feel unwelcome by treating them coldly. To drive someone away by creating difficult or hostile conditions. To keep someone from taking part in a decision or benefit.
example_sentence: His colleagues tried to freeze him out after the argument. Large firms often freeze out smaller competitors with low prices. She felt frozen out of every important meeting. They froze out anyone who disagreed with the new policy.

english_meaning: To become completely covered with a layer of ice. To turn to ice across the whole surface of water. To be made icy by very low temperatures. Used figuratively to describe something extremely unlikely ever happening. To become cold and unwelcoming in atmosphere or attitude.
example_sentence: The lake freezes over every year in late December. The windscreen had frozen over during the night. Children waited for the canal to freeze over so they could skate. He said he would apologise when hell freezes over.

english_meaning: To become blocked or stop working because of ice. To stop functioning suddenly, especially a machine or computer. To become unable to speak or act because of fear or nervousness. To become emotionally cold or unresponsive. To bring an activity to a complete standstill.
example_sentence: The pipes froze up during the coldest night of the year. My laptop froze up in the middle of the presentation. She froze up as soon as she stepped onto the stage. He tends to freeze up whenever someone asks him a personal question.

english_meaning: To fill someone with sudden and intense fear. To terrify a person so much that they cannot move. To cause a chilling feeling of horror. To shock someone deeply with something frightening. Used of sounds, sights, or news that are extremely alarming.
example_sentence: The scream from the empty house was enough to freeze your blood. His description of the accident would freeze your blood. A shadow moved behind the curtain and froze my blood. The story he told that night froze the blood of everyone present.

english_meaning: Extremely cold, often below the temperature at which water turns to ice. Feeling very cold and uncomfortable. The process of turning into ice or being preserved by very low temperature. Relating to the temperature of zero degrees Celsius. Present participle of freeze, meaning becoming solid or motionless.
example_sentence: It was freezing outside, so we stayed indoors all evening. I am freezing without my coat. The freezing of fresh vegetables keeps them usable for months. Temperatures are expected to fall below freezing tonight.

english_meaning: The temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid. The point at which water turns into ice, normally zero degrees Celsius. A fixed value used in science to identify or compare substances. The lowest limit of temperature before something becomes frozen. Figuratively, the point at which a relationship or situation becomes completely cold.
synonyms: ["Solidification point","Ice point","Congealing point","Zero point","Critical temperature","Threshold","Lower limit","Cold point","Set point","Crystallization point"]
antonyms: ["Boiling point","Melting point","Evaporation point","Heat point","Upper limit","Warmth","High temperature","Flash point","Thawing point","Vaporization point"]
example_sentence: The freezing point of pure water is zero degrees Celsius. Adding salt lowers the freezing point of water. Students recorded the freezing point of each liquid in the lab. Their friendship had reached freezing point after the argument.

english_meaning: Goods transported in bulk by truck, train, ship, or aircraft. It can also refer to the charge or cost for such transportation.
example_sentence: The truck was carrying heavy freight across the country. They decided to send the equipment by sea freight to save money. The train station handles a large volume of freight every day. Freight costs have risen significantly due to the increase in fuel prices.

english_meaning: Someone who pretends to be a friend but is actually an enemy. A person with whom one has a friendly relationship on the surface, but underneath, there is rivalry, jealousy, or hidden hostility. They can be supportive sometimes, but their actions or intentions may not always be sincere.
example_sentence: She laughed and joked with her frenemy, though she knew not to trust her completely. Office politics made him treat many colleagues as frenemies. They act like best friends, but they are actually frenemies competing for the same promotion. Social media has turned some acquaintances into frenemies.

english_meaning: Very fast and energetic in a wild or uncontrolled way. Showing extreme excitement, activity, or agitation that is often chaotic and uncontrolled.
example_sentence: The crowd made a frenetic rush toward the stage. She worked at a frenetic pace to finish the project. The stock market saw frenetic trading today. His frenetic gestures showed his nervousness.

english_meaning: In a very fast, energetic, and often uncontrolled way. Describes actions done with extreme intensity, excitement, or nervous energy, often appearing chaotic or uncontrolled.
example_sentence: She searched frenetically for her lost keys before leaving for work. The crowd waved their hands frenetically when the band appeared on stage. He typed frenetically to meet the deadline. Children ran frenetically around the playground after the bell rang.

english_meaning: A small fold of tissue that secures or restricts the motion of a mobile organ in the body. A narrow band of tissue that connects two parts of the body, commonly found in the mouth (under the tongue or upper lip) or other areas. It limits movement and helps in proper function. Examples include the lingual frenulum (under the tongue) and labial frenulum (inside the upper or lower lip).
example_sentence: The dentist checked the baby’s lingual frenulum to ensure it wasn’t too tight. A torn frenulum can cause bleeding after an accident. Some people need minor surgery to release a tight frenulum under the tongue. The upper lip frenulum can affect how the teeth align.

english_meaning: Wild or uncontrolled. Showing extreme, uncontrolled excitement, activity, or emotion; behaving in a chaotic or frantic way
example_sentence: The crowd became frenzied when the singer appeared. She made a frenzied attempt to finish the work on time. The stock market saw frenzied trading today. Children ran in frenzied joy during the festival.

english_meaning: In a very excited or uncontrolled way. Performing an action with intense, wild, or uncontrolled energy or emotion; acting in a state of frenzy.
example_sentence: She typed frenziedly to finish the report on time. Fans waved flags frenziedly at the concert. He searched frenziedly for his lost passport. The children played frenziedly in the garden.

english_meaning: A state of extreme excitement, anger, or wild behavior. A temporary state of uncontrolled emotion or activity, often characterized by intense excitement, agitation, or violent behavior. It can describe both positive excitement and negative emotional outbursts.
example_sentence: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared on stage. She worked in a frenzy to finish the project on time. News of the victory sent the city into a frenzy of celebration. The dog chased the cat in a frenzy.

english_meaning: The rate at which something happens or is repeated over time. The number of times an event occurs in a given period. In physics, the number of waves or vibrations per second. The commonness or regularity of something happening. A specific band on which radio or sound signals are transmitted.
example_sentence: The frequency of earthquakes in this area has increased. Radio stations broadcast on different frequencies. Please note the frequency of these headaches. High-frequency sounds are hard for humans to hear.

english_meaning: Happening or occurring often. Regular or common in a certain place or time. To visit a place regularly or habitually. Occurring at short intervals repeatedly. Done or seen many times.
example_sentence: He is a frequent visitor to our house. Storms are frequent in this region during summer. She used to frequent the old library as a student. Frequent breaks help improve concentration.

english_meaning: In a way that happens often. On many occasions or at short intervals. Regularly or repeatedly. In a manner that is common or usual. Very often, without long gaps.
example_sentence: He frequently visits his grandparents on weekends. She frequently forgets her keys at home. Traffic jams occur frequently on this road. I frequently read books before going to bed.

english_meaning: To be constantly worried or anxious about something. To feel irritated or troubled. To wear away or erode something by rubbing. One of the metal ridges on the fingerboard of a stringed instrument such as a guitar.
example_sentence: She tends to fret over small problems that are often beyond her control. Don't fret about the exam — you have studied hard and done your best. The constant rubbing caused the rope to fret and eventually snap. He learned to play the guitar by first understanding the position of each fret. His mother would always fret whenever he came home late from school.

english_meaning: Relating to Sigmund Freud and his theories of psychoanalysis. Describing an interpretation based on unconscious desires and repressed feelings. A person who follows or supports Freud's psychological theories.
example_sentence: He made a Freudian slip during the interview. The novel offers a Freudian reading of childhood memories. Many Freudian ideas remain controversial among psychologists. She is a committed Freudian in her clinical practice.

english_meaning: Members of certain religious orders in the Christian church, especially mendicant orders such as the Franciscans or Dominicans. Men who have taken religious vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience and live in a community or travel to preach. The plural form of friar.
example_sentence: The friars walked through the village every morning, offering prayers and assistance to those in need. Two friars from the monastery visited the school to speak about the history of their order. The friars devoted their lives to serving the poor and spreading the teachings of the church. Medieval friars were known for their brown robes and their commitment to simplicity. The friars established a small library in the town to educate the local community.

english_meaning: A building or community where friars live and carry out their religious duties. A monastery or convent that belongs to one of the mendicant orders. The place where a community of friars resides.
example_sentence: The old friary was converted into a museum and opened to the public last year. The friars returned to the friary every evening after their work in the community. The friary was built in the thirteenth century and is considered a historical monument. Visitors can tour the grounds of the friary and learn about its rich religious history. The local friary provided shelter and food for homeless people throughout the winter.

english_meaning: A speech sound made by forcing air through a narrow passage in the mouth, creating audible friction. A consonant such as f, s, v, or z produced with continuous airflow. Relating to this type of speech sound.
example_sentence: The sound /f/ is a voiceless fricative. Students practiced producing English fricatives. The word begins with a fricative consonant. Fricative sounds are formed by narrowing the vocal tract.

english_meaning: The resistance that occurs when one surface moves against another. Conflict, tension, or disagreement between people or groups. Difficulty that slows a process or makes an interaction less smooth. The rubbing of one object against another.
example_sentence: Friction between the tires and the road helps the car stop. Constant friction damaged the moving parts. Political differences created friction within the coalition. The new checkout system reduces friction for customers.

english_meaning: Having little or no friction between moving surfaces. Smooth and easy, without obstacles, delays, or conflict. In physics, idealized as operating without resistance caused by contact.
example_sentence: Air bearings allow nearly frictionless movement. The app aims to provide a frictionless payment experience. Their cooperation made the transition almost frictionless. In the model, the block slides on a frictionless surface.

english_meaning: A sudden intense feeling of fear or terror. An experience that causes someone to feel sudden fear. A person or thing that looks strange, ugly, or ridiculous.
example_sentence: The sudden noise gave her a terrible fright. He was shaking with fright after the accident. She looked a fright in that old oversized dress. The children experienced a severe fright during the thunderstorm.

english_meaning: To cause someone to feel afraid or scared. To alarm, terrify, or startle. To drive or force someone by causing fear. To make a person or animal suddenly afraid.
example_sentence: The loud thunder frightened the little child. Do not frighten the birds away from the garden. The horror movie frightened everyone in the theater. She was frightened by the sudden noise outside. Try not to frighten your younger brother with scary stories.

english_meaning: Extremely cold in temperature. Unfriendly, cold, or distant in manner or emotion. Lacking warmth, passion, or enthusiasm. Stiffly formal and unresponsive.
example_sentence: The explorers survived the frigid temperatures of the Arctic. She gave him a frigid stare when he arrived late. The frigid waters of the lake discouraged swimmers. His frigid manner made it hard to talk to him.

english_meaning: A person who loves cold weather and cold environments. Someone who feels comfortable and happy in low temperatures. An organism that thrives in cold conditions.
example_sentence: As a true frigophile, she keeps the air conditioner on all night. Frigophiles look forward to the first snowfall of the year. He is such a frigophile that he never wears a coat. Some frigophile bacteria survive in polar ice.

english_meaning: An ornamental border of threads or tassels. The outer edge or margin of an area, group, or activity. Something that is considered peripheral or extreme relative to the mainstream.
example_sentence: The curtains were decorated with a golden fringe at the bottom. We lived on the fringe of the forest where it was quiet. His ideas were once considered part of the lunatic fringe. The festival celebrates fringe theater and experimental performances.

english_meaning: A plastic disc, usually round and slightly curved, that people throw and catch as a game. A brand name that has become a common word for a flying disc used in recreation or sport. Used in outdoor games including ultimate frisbee and disc golf.
example_sentence: The children played with a frisbee in the park. He can throw a frisbee across the entire field. The dog loves to catch the frisbee in mid air. They organized a frisbee tournament on the beach. A red frisbee got stuck in the tree.

english_meaning: To carefully examine a person's clothing and body by feeling with the hands, especially to check for weapons, illegal items, or hidden objects. To skip, jump, or run around happily with energy and excitement. A rapid physical search of a person, commonly performed by police or security officers. To search a person's body or clothing by touch, usually for weapons or illegal items.
example_sentence: The security officer frisked every passenger before they entered the stadium. The police decided to frisk the suspect after receiving a safety warning. The young lambs frisked across the green field on a sunny morning. Children frisked around the playground with laughter and excitement. A routine frisk revealed nothing suspicious on the suspect. The security guard performed a frisk before allowing visitors into the building.

english_meaning: To waste or squander. To break or tear into small pieces, shred. To waste (money, time, etc) bit by bit on petty things usually with away. To separate or break into fragments. Round pieces of fruit, vegetables, or meat that are dipped in batter and fried. A small cake of fried batter, usually containing corn, fruit, or other filling. A small piece, fragment, or shred.
example_sentence: I fritter my time away at coffee mornings. The fritters should be golden brown and sizzling. When both sides are golden brown, transfer the fritters to a serving platter. She served apple fritters with tea. He frittered away his savings on expensive gadgets. Do not fritter your time on meaningless arguments.

english_meaning: Not serious or important, silly or trivial. Describes something that lacks seriousness, value, or sense. Often refers to actions, behavior, or things that are unworthy of attention or overly playful when seriousness is expected.
example_sentence: He spent money on frivolous things. She spent her money on frivolous things instead of saving it. His frivolous remarks annoyed the teacher. The court dismissed the case as frivolous. He has a frivolous attitude towards his responsibilities.

english_meaning: In a light, careless, or unserious way. Doing or treating something in a way that shows a lack of seriousness, responsibility, or careful thought. It is often used to criticize behavior, speech, or decisions that should have been taken more seriously.
example_sentence: He laughed frivolously during the serious meeting. The issue of climate change should not be discussed frivolously. She spent money frivolously without thinking about the future. The lawyer argued that the case was not filed frivolously.

english_meaning: Lack of seriousness or importance. Light and careless behavior. An attitude or behavior that treats serious matters as unimportant. It shows a lack of responsibility, depth, or thoughtful concern, especially in situations that require seriousness or careful judgment.
example_sentence: His frivolousness during the meeting annoyed the senior staff. The judge criticized the lawyer for the frivolousness of his arguments. Frivolousness has no place in matters of public safety. Her tone showed a level of frivolousness that weakened her message.

english_meaning: To form or cause hair to form into tight, unruly, or wiry curls, especially due to humidity or heat. The condition of hair that is rough, dry, or unmanageable with small tight curls. To become or make frizzy.
example_sentence: The humid weather tends to cause her hair to frizz uncontrollably. She used a special serum to tame the frizz in her curly hair. His hair started to frizz as soon as he stepped out in the rain. Too much heat from the dryer can cause serious frizz and damage to the hair. She prefers to embrace her natural frizz rather than spending hours straightening it.

english_meaning: Something messy, confused, silly, or lacking clear order. A situation, idea, or thing that feels mixed up, awkward, or hard to understand. People use it when they do not want to be precise and prefer a light or joking tone. It often suggests disorganization without serious consequences.
example_sentence: His explanation was all frobly mobly and no one understood the main point. The notes from the meeting were frobly mobly and needed rewriting. She laughed and said her plan was still frobly mobly but exciting. The room looked frobly mobly after the kids finished playing.

word: From a single morsel, gratitude begins
english_meaning: Gratitude can stem from the smallest of gifts or acts of kindness. Even a single bite of food or a minimal gesture of help is enough to inspire profound thankfulness. True appreciation does not require grand gestures but starts with recognizing small favors and blessings.
synonyms: ["Gratitude For Small Mercies","Appreciate The Little Things","Every Little Bit Helps","Small Things Matter","Count Your Blessings"]
antonyms: ["Ingratitude","Unthankfulness","Taking Things For Granted","Greed","Biting The Hand That Feeds You","Entitlement"]
example_sentence: When the starving man thanked the baker for a crust of bread, we realized that from a single morsel, gratitude begins. Do not brush off a small favor, for from a single morsel, gratitude begins. The charity organization believes that from a single morsel, gratitude begins, and every tiny donation matters. She always says that from a single morsel, gratitude begins when teaching her children to appreciate whatever little they have. Even though it was just a small cup of tea, he was deeply thankful, proving that from a single morsel, gratitude begins.

english_meaning: Throughout the whole day, from early morning (when the sun rises) until evening (when the sun sets). It refers to doing something continuously during the daytime without rest.
example_sentence: The farmers worked from dawn to dusk in the fields. She studied from dawn to dusk to prepare for her exams. The children played outside from dawn to dusk during the summer holidays. The shop remains open from dawn to dusk to serve travelers.

english_meaning: From one place or person to another without any clear result. Being sent repeatedly from one authority to another while seeking help. Moving about in a hurried, confused, and often fruitless manner.
synonyms: ["To and fro","Here and there","Back and forth","Hither and thither","Around in circles","From place to place","Aimlessly about","Up and down"]
example_sentence: He was sent from pillar to post while trying to get his documents approved. The poor family was driven from pillar to post in search of shelter. I ran from pillar to post all morning but achieved nothing. Patients are often pushed from pillar to post in overcrowded hospitals.

english_meaning: Starting something from the very beginning without using preexisting materials. Creating something entirely on one's own without help or shortcuts. Building or preparing something completely from basic elements. Beginning again with nothing already prepared.
synonyms: ["From the beginning","From zero","From nothing","From square one","From the ground up"]
example_sentence: She baked the cake from scratch. He built his business from scratch. After the fire, they had to start their lives from scratch. Learning a new language from scratch takes patience.

word: From the cradle to the grave
english_meaning: For the whole of a person's life, from birth until death. Covering every stage of life without interruption. Describing care, support, or service provided throughout a lifetime.
example_sentence: The state promised welfare from the cradle to the grave. He lived in the same village from the cradle to the grave. The scheme offers health cover from the cradle to the grave. Their friendship lasted from the cradle to the grave.

english_meaning: From the very beginning or most basic level. Completely and thoroughly. By building or learning every stage in a logical order. As something entirely new rather than by modifying what already exists
example_sentence: They rebuilt the company from the ground up after the bankruptcy. The software was designed from the ground up to be secure. He learned the business from the ground up, starting as a delivery assistant. The city plans to redevelop the old district from the ground up.

english_meaning: Directly from the person who is the original or most reliable source. Information received first hand rather than through rumour. Used to stress that news is authentic and trustworthy.
example_sentence: I heard it straight from the horse's mouth, so there is no doubt. Don't trust the gossip; get the facts from the horse's mouth. The manager confirmed the news himself, right from the horse's mouth. She wanted the story from the horse's mouth before printing it.

english_meaning: The large bone that forms the forehead and the upper part of the eye sockets. The bone at the front of the skull above the eyes. The flat bone that shapes the front of the cranium. The bone protecting the front lobes of the brain.
example_sentence: The frontal bone forms the shape of the forehead. He suffered a hairline fracture of the frontal bone. The frontal bone joins the parietal bones at the top of the skull. Doctors examined the frontal bone after the head injury.

english_meaning: A thin layer of ice formed on cold surfaces when water vapor freezes. A period of cold weather when temperatures fall below freezing. To cover with frost or a sugary icing. Coldness in manner or attitude. To damage plants by freezing.
example_sentence: The garden was covered with frost this morning. A sudden frost destroyed most of the crops. She frosted the cake with white icing. There was a clear frost in her voice.

english_meaning: To bring your eyebrows together and wrinkle your forehead, usually when you are angry, worried, or thinking hard. The expression on your face that shows disapproval or worry.
example_sentence: She frowned when she heard the bad news. The teacher frowned at the noisy students. He looked at me with a deep frown on his face. People usually frown when they are confused or upset.

english_meaning: Careful with money or resources; not wasteful. Someone who spends money and resources wisely, avoids unnecessary expenses, and prefers simplicity. It reflects prudence and careful management rather than stinginess.
example_sentence: She lives a frugal life and saves most of her income. He made frugal choices when furnishing his new apartment. The company adopted frugal measures to cut costs. Even though he was wealthy, he remained frugal in his daily habits.

english_meaning: A person who eats modestly or economically. Someone who is careful about the quantity and cost of food they consume, preferring simple meals and avoiding waste or extravagance.
example_sentence: John is a frugal eater and prefers simple home-cooked meals. Despite his wealth, he remains a frugal eater. She became a frugal eater after moving to a small apartment. Being a frugal eater helped him save money for his travels.

english_meaning: Careful use of money or resources, avoiding waste. The quality of being economical with resources, especially money. It involves avoiding unnecessary expenses, using what you have wisely, and prioritizing needs over wants.
example_sentence: Her frugality allowed her to save enough money for a house. He is known for his frugality and rarely spends on luxuries. Frugality in cooking can help reduce household expenses. Practicing frugality does not mean living poorly but managing resources wisely.

english_meaning: In a careful way to avoid waste or spending too much. Acting with economy, prudence, or simplicity in the use of resources, money, or materials; avoiding extravagance while still meeting needs
example_sentence: She lived frugally to save enough money for her children’s education. They furnished their home frugally, using mostly second-hand items. He ate frugally during his travels to avoid spending too much. The company managed its resources frugally to survive the recession.

english_meaning: To make someone feel annoyed, disappointed, or discouraged. To prevent a plan, effort, or desire from succeeding. To block or defeat someone's purpose. To cause a feeling of helplessness by repeated obstacles.
example_sentence: Constant delays frustrated the passengers waiting at the airport. Bad weather frustrated our plans for the weekend. It frustrates me when people arrive late without warning. The defenders frustrated every attack in the second half.

english_meaning: The feeling of being annoyed, upset, or discouraged when something is difficult or impossible. A situation or event that causes such a feeling. The act of preventing something from succeeding. A sense of helplessness caused by unmet needs or repeated failure.
example_sentence: He slammed the door in frustration after the meeting. Long queues are a daily frustration for commuters. She could hear the frustration in his voice. The frustration of their plans forced the team to start again.

english_meaning: To cook food (usually quickly) by frying, often used for breakfast or leftovers.
example_sentence: She fried up some eggs for breakfast. Let’s fry up the leftovers. He fried up the fish for dinner. They fried up some vegetables.

english_meaning: A vulgar slang word for sexual intercourse. To have sex with someone (vulgar). A rude exclamation used to express anger, frustration, surprise, or emphasis. To ruin, damage, or treat someone unfairly (vulgar slang). Used as an intensifier in informal, offensive speech.
example_sentence: The word fuck is considered highly offensive in polite conversation. He shouted a loud fuck when he hit his thumb with the hammer. The editor removed every fuck from the interview transcript. Teachers warned the students not to use words like fuck at school.

english_meaning: To waste time doing unimportant or silly things (vulgar slang). To behave in a careless or irresponsible way. To interfere with someone or something in a harmful way. To be sexually unfaithful or promiscuous (vulgar).
example_sentence: Stop fucking around and finish your work. They fucked around all afternoon instead of studying. Don't fuck around with the wiring unless you know what you're doing. He warned them not to fuck around with the deadline.

english_meaning: A vulgar phrase used to show that one no longer cares about something. An expression of giving up, frustration, or reckless decision. Used to dismiss worry and act anyway.
synonyms: ["Forget it","Never mind","Who cares","To hell with it","Whatever","Let it go"]
example_sentence: He finally said fuck it and quit the job. Fuck it, let's go to the beach instead. She thought about the risk, then muttered fuck it and signed. After hours of arguing, he threw up his hands and said fuck it.

english_meaning: A very rude way of telling someone to go away. To leave a place, often abruptly (vulgar slang). To avoid work or waste time (British vulgar slang). Used as an expression of angry refusal or disbelief.
synonyms: ["Go away","Clear off","Get lost","Push off","Leave","Beat it","Buzz off","Scram"]
example_sentence: He told the intruder to fuck off and shut the door. She was so angry that she just said fuck off and walked away. They fucked off home before the meeting ended. When he asked for another loan, his brother told him to fuck off.

english_meaning: To make a serious mistake or handle something very badly (vulgar slang). To ruin, spoil, or damage something. To disturb someone emotionally or mentally. A serious blunder or a person who repeatedly fails.
example_sentence: He fucked up the presentation by forgetting the main figures. Don't fuck up this chance; it may not come again. The whole schedule was a complete fuck-up. Losing the files was a serious fuck-up on their part.

english_meaning: Badly damaged, ruined, or in a very bad condition (vulgar slang). Emotionally or mentally disturbed. Morally wrong, unfair, or shocking. Very drunk or under the influence of drugs.
example_sentence: The engine is completely fucked up after the accident. He felt fucked up for weeks after the news. What they did to her was really fucked up. He came home fucked up after the party.

english_meaning: A person who is old-fashioned and resists change. Someone who strongly prefers traditional ways of thinking or behaving and often dislikes new ideas, modern styles, or changes in society. Such a person may criticize trends simply because they are new.
example_sentence: He refuses to use a smartphone and prefers handwritten letters like a true fuddy-duddy. The young staff think their manager is a fuddy-duddy because he dislikes flexible work hours. She called him a fuddy-duddy for opposing modern teaching methods. Not everyone who likes tradition is a fuddy-duddy, but he clearly resists all change.

english_meaning:
Language, behavior, or ideas that are absurd and contrary to good sense. 
To avoid giving a definite answer or position. To use dishonest methods to achieve a goal. A soft sweet made from sugar, butter, and milk. To change so much as to create a wrong impression or alter the meaning of.
example_sentence: I was starting to realize that Grandpa's tales about when he was a boy were a lot of fudge.

english_meaning: The act of pretending to work or appearing busy while actually doing nothing productive. An old, humorous English word describing the practice of making a show of effort without accomplishing anything useful. Used informally and somewhat archaically to describe idleness disguised as activity. Often used in modern vocabulary lists as an obscure or whimsical word for procrastination.
example_sentence: He spent the entire afternoon fudgeling at his desk instead of finishing the report.  Despite all the fudgeling, nothing had actually been accomplished by the end of the day.  She was an expert at fudgeling, always looking busy without doing real work.  The office was full of fudgeling employees waiting for the clock to strike five.  After hours of fudgeling, he finally got down to the actual task.

english_meaning: Lasting only a short time. Fleeting and quickly passing away. Tending to disappear or fade rapidly. Transitory in nature. Often used in poetic, literary, or scientific contexts to describe moments, emotions, beauty, or even botanical features like petals that fall soon after blooming.
example_sentence: The beauty of cherry blossoms is wonderfully fugacious. Fame in show business can be sadly fugacious. He experienced a fugacious moment of joy after the news. The flower’s petals are fugacious and fall within a day. Childhood happiness is often fugacious yet unforgettable.

english_meaning: A person who is running away, especially from the law. A person who escapes or is in hiding, often to avoid arrest or danger. Something that is fleeting, temporary, or hard to capture.
example_sentence: The fugitive was finally caught after hiding for months. Police are searching for a fugitive who escaped last night. His fame was fugitive and disappeared quickly. She had only a fugitive glimpse of the rare bird.

english_meaning: A musical composition in which one or more themes are introduced by one part and then repeated and developed by others in complex patterns. A state of mind in which a person temporarily loses their sense of identity and memory, often wandering away from home. A period of confused or dreamlike behavior. Any complicated interweaving of different elements.
example_sentence: Bach is famous for his beautiful fugues. The patient suffered a fugue and could not remember his own name. She composed a fugue for the piano and violin. He wandered for two days in a state of fugue before he was found.

english_meaning: Fully developed, trained, or established. Having all the necessary qualifications, rights, or characteristics. Complete and mature in every respect. Describing something or someone that has reached a complete or official status.
example_sentence: After years of training, she finally became a full-fledged doctor and opened her own clinic. The country has grown into a full-fledged democracy since gaining independence. What started as a small argument soon turned into a full-fledged conflict between the two groups. He completed his apprenticeship and is now a full-fledged electrician. The small startup has grown into a full-fledged technology company with offices in three countries.

english_meaning: Very lively, energetic, active, and enthusiastic. Full of life, excitement, and high spirits. Sometimes (informally) also means talking nonsense in British English.
example_sentence: The kids are full of beans today. The children were full of beans after the party. He came to the meeting full of beans and new ideas.

word: Full of the joys of spring
english_meaning: Very cheerful. Feeling very happy, lively, and full of energy, just like the freshness and beauty of springtime.
example_sentence: After hearing the good news, she was full of the joys of spring. He came into the office full of the joys of spring, greeting everyone happily.

english_meaning: Completely developed, trained, or established. Having all the qualities, rights, or status of a particular kind. Fully equipped and able to function independently.
example_sentence: The small workshop grew into a full-fledged factory. She is now a full-fledged member of the team. The prototype became a full-fledged product. They built a full-fledged studio in the basement.

english_meaning: In a completely developed, established, or fully qualified manner. With all the features, rights, or status expected of something complete. The word is rare and fully is usually more natural.
example_sentence: The organization now operates full-fledgedly across the region. After certification, the clinic functioned full-fledgedly. The service was launched full-fledgedly after months of testing. Although rare, the term describes something working full-fledgedly.

english_meaning: Completely developed, trained, or established. Possessing all the necessary features, rights, or qualifications. Fully capable of operating independently.
example_sentence: He became a fully-fledged pilot after completing his training. The project has developed into a fully-fledged business. She joined the committee as a fully-fledged member. The website is now a fully-fledged learning platform.

english_meaning: To express vehement protest or criticism. To rail loudly and angrily against something or someone. To explode or cause to explode. To issue a formal denunciation or severe criticism.
example_sentence: The opposition leader began to fulminate against the government's new economic policy. He continued to fulminate about the injustice he had experienced for years. The chemical compound will fulminate under certain conditions of heat and pressure. The journalist fulminated against the corruption that had spread through the institution. Critics fulminated over the court's controversial decision for weeks after it was announced.

english_meaning: Of a dull yellowish-brown or tawny colour, resembling the colour of a lion's coat. Tawny in appearance. Often used in biological or scientific descriptions to describe the colouring of animals, birds, or plants.
example_sentence: The fulvous markings on the bird's wings made it easy to identify in the field. The naturalist described the animal's fulvous coat in detail in his research notes. The fulvous colour of the grass in late summer gives the plains a warm golden tone. She painted the landscape using fulvous and amber tones to capture the savannah scenery. The fulvous duck is a species known for its distinctive tawny plumage.

english_meaning: To handle something clumsily or fail due to lack of control. To use the hands awkwardly, often dropping something, or to make a mistake because of nervousness, confusion, or poor coordination. It can also mean failing to say or do something smoothly. A clumsy action or mistake, especially in sports or physical handling.
example_sentence: He fumbled with the keys and could not open the door. She fumbled the ball during the final moments of the match. The speaker fumbled his words because he was nervous. I fumbled in my bag to find my phone. The fumble cost the team the match. After a Pittsburgh fumble, Miami scored a touchdown.

english_meaning: A material made from synthetic fibers designed to resemble real animal fur. It is commonly used in the fashion industry to create ethical and animal-friendly clothing and accessories. A decorative or functional textile that mimics the texture and appearance of natural pelts. A type of pile fabric often used for crafts, costumes, and soft toys. A synthetic alternative to genuine fur, typically made from acrylic or polyester.
synonyms: ["Faux Fur","Artificial Fur","Synthetic Fur","Imitation Fur","Fake Fur","Man-made Fur","Mock Fur","Pile Fabric","Plush","Acrylic Fur","Eco-fur","Non-animal Fur"]
antonyms: ["Real Fur","Genuine Leather","Natural Pelt","Animal Skin","Authentic Hide","Raw Wool"]
example_sentence: She bought a stylish fun fur coat that looked exactly like real mink. The interior of the winter boots was lined with soft fun fur for extra warmth. Designers are increasingly using fun fur to promote ethical fashion choices on the runway. The craft project required a small piece of brightly colored fun fur to make the monster's mane.

english_meaning: The art or practice of walking, balancing, or performing on a tightrope or high wire. Tightrope walking as a performance or skill. The ability to walk or balance on a rope or wire suspended at a great height.
example_sentence: Funambulism has been performed as a circus act for centuries around the world. The performer's skill in funambulism left the entire audience holding their breath. Funambulism requires years of dedicated training and an exceptional sense of balance. He studied funambulism under a renowned circus master during his time in France. The ancient practice of funambulism was celebrated in many cultures as a display of courage and skill.

english_meaning: The special purpose or activity for which a person or thing exists or is used. The way in which something works or operates. A large formal social event such as a wedding, dinner, or ceremony. In mathematics, a relation in which each input has exactly one output. To work or operate in a proper or particular way.
example_sentence: The main function of the heart is to pump blood. The machine does not function properly in cold weather. We attended a family function last weekend. Draw the graph of the given function on the board.
