english_meaning: To serve or be used in the role of something else. To operate or work in a particular capacity or manner. To take the place of something and perform its duties. To have the practical effect of being something, even if not formally so.
synonyms: ["Serve as","Act as","Work as","Operate as","Double as","Perform as","Stand in as","Be used as"]
example_sentence: The sofa can also function as a bed for guests. She functions as the head of the department in his absence. This hall functions as an examination centre during finals. The app functions as both a diary and a planner.

english_meaning: Designed to be practical and useful rather than attractive. Working properly and able to perform its intended task. Relating to the way in which something works or the purpose it serves. In medicine, affecting the working of an organ rather than its structure.
example_sentence: The kitchen is small but highly functional. The old lift is still functional after thirty years. The building's design is functional rather than decorative. The doctor described it as a functional disorder, not a structural one.

english_meaning: An approach to grammar that studies language in terms of the functions it performs in communication. A theory that explains grammatical structures by the meanings and purposes they express. A model of language analysis focused on how speakers use grammar in real social contexts. A framework contrasted with formal grammar, which studies rules and structures in isolation.
example_sentence: The course introduces students to functional grammar. Functional grammar looks at how language works in real conversation. Halliday's functional grammar is widely used in discourse analysis. She compared functional grammar with traditional grammar in her thesis.

english_meaning: The theory that the design of a building or object should be based mainly on its purpose and use. In sociology, the view that society is a system of parts that work together to keep it stable. In psychology, the study of mental processes in terms of the purposes they serve. In linguistics, an approach that explains language structures by the functions they perform.
example_sentence: Functionalism shaped much of twentieth-century architecture. The lecture compared functionalism with conflict theory. Functionalism explains language in terms of communication needs. Critics argue that functionalism ignores social inequality.

english_meaning: A person who believes that the design of something should be based on its purpose and use. A supporter of functionalism in sociology, psychology, architecture, or linguistics. Relating to the theory that parts of a system exist because of the roles they perform. Describing an approach that explains things by the functions they serve.
example_sentence: The architect was a strict functionalist in his early years. Functionalist thinkers see society as a working system. She offered a functionalist explanation of family roles. Critics challenged the functionalist view of education.

english_meaning: In terms of the way something works or the purpose it serves. In a practical or useful manner rather than a decorative one. For all practical purposes, even if not officially or technically so. In a way that relates to the function of an organ, system, or structure.
example_sentence: The two machines are functionally identical. The room is functionally arranged for group study. He is functionally in charge, though not officially appointed. Many patients remain functionally independent after therapy.

english_meaning: A person who holds an official position, especially a minor one in a government or organisation. An official who performs routine administrative duties. Often used with a slightly negative sense for someone who follows rules without judgement. Relating to a function or an official duty.
example_sentence: A junior functionary stamped our documents at the counter. The party functionary refused to comment on the matter. Several government functionaries attended the ceremony. He behaved like a mere functionary rather than a leader.

english_meaning: Forming a necessary base or core. Of central importance. Serving as an original or primary source. A basic principle, rule, or essential constituent.
example_sentence: Freedom of speech is a fundamental human right. Respect is a fundamental part of any healthy relationship. They need to make fundamental changes to their business model. We learned the fundamental principles of physics in high school.

english_meaning: A person who adheres strictly and literally to the fundamental principles of any religion, ideology, or belief system. Someone who insists on a strict and literal interpretation of religious texts. A person who is unwilling to compromise on core beliefs or principles.
example_sentence: The fundamentalist group refused to accept any changes to the traditional religious practices. He was known as a political fundamentalist who never compromised on his core ideology. The debate between moderates and fundamentalists has shaped much of the country's religious history. The fundamentalist faction rejected the reforms proposed by the liberal wing of the party. Growing up in a fundamentalist household made it difficult for her to question the beliefs she was raised with.

english_meaning: A ceremony, often a religious one, for burying or cremating (= burning) a dead person. A ceremony honoring someone who has recently died, which happens before burying or burning the body.
example_sentence: Hundreds of people attended the funeral. Only family attended the funeral. I had to trade our fifth anniversary for her funeral.

english_meaning: Suitable for or suggesting a funeral. Very sad, solemn, and gloomy in mood or appearance. Extremely slow and mournful in pace or tone.
example_sentence: The room fell into a funereal silence after the announcement. He spoke in a slow, funereal tone. The procession moved at a funereal pace. Her funereal expression told us the news was bad.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or characteristic of a fungus or fungi. Caused by or relating to an infection involving fungi. Resembling a fungus in terms of its growth pattern or physical appearance. Associated with the biological kingdom that includes yeasts, molds, and mushrooms. Used to describe diseases that result from the presence of pathogenic spores.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed a special ointment to treat the fungal infection on his skin. Fungal spores can spread rapidly in warm and humid environments. Scientists are studying the unique fungal growth patterns found in deep forest soil. Many forest trees rely on a complex fungal network for nutrient exchange.

english_meaning: A diverse group of eukaryotic organisms that include microorganisms such as yeasts and molds, as well as multicellular mushrooms. They are classified as a separate kingdom from plants and animals because they lack chlorophyll and obtain nutrients through absorption. These organisms play a crucial role as decomposers in various ecosystems by breaking down organic matter. They can exist as single cells or as long filamentous structures called hyphae. Some members of this group are edible or used in fermentation, while others can cause diseases or decay.
example_sentence: The fallen logs were covered in a variety of colorful fungi that helped decompose the wood. Fungi play an essential role in the production of bread and cheese through fermentation. Scientists are studying how certain fungi can be used to clean up environmental pollutants. Not all fungi are safe to eat, as some species contain deadly toxins.

english_meaning: Able to be replaced by another identical item of the same kind and value. Mutually interchangeable, especially in trade or finance. Treated as equivalent units rather than unique items.
example_sentence: Money is a fungible asset because one note is as good as another. Crude oil is largely fungible on the world market. The contract treats the shares as fungible units. Skilled labour is not always fungible between industries.

english_meaning: A chemical substance or biological organism used to kill or inhibit the growth of fungi or their spores. A specialized pesticide formulation designed specifically for agricultural crop protection against blights and mildews. A medicinal treatment applied topically or systemically to eliminate fungal infections in humans or animals. Any agent that exerts a lethal effect on the fungal kingdom through the disruption of cellular processes. An industrial preservative used to prevent mold and rot in building materials or textiles.
example_sentence: The farmer applied a potent fungicide to protect the wheat crop from rust disease. You should wear protective gloves when handling this industrial-grade fungicide. The doctor prescribed a topical fungicide to treat the persistent skin infection. Copper sulfate has been used as a traditional fungicide in vineyards for centuries.

english_meaning: Resembling or characteristic of a fungus or mushroom. Relating to a group of spore-producing organisms that feed on organic matter. Growing or spreading rapidly and uncontrollably like a fungal infection. Having the spongy or porous consistency of a fungal growth. Appearing suddenly or unexpectedly in a manner suggestive of mold.
example_sentence: The scientist observed a fungoid growth on the damp walls of the cellar. Her skin developed a strange fungoid texture after exposure to the spores. The tumor exhibited a fungoid appearance under the microscope. The rapid development of the city's slums was described as a fungoid expansion.

english_meaning: A group of spore-producing organisms feeding on organic matter, including molds, yeast, mushrooms, and toadstools. It refers to any member of the kingdom Fungi which lacks chlorophyll and leaves. A spongy, abnormal growth or diseased condition in plants or animals caused by fungal infection. Something that grows or spreads rapidly and often destructively like a mold. A botanical classification for organisms that absorb nutrients from their surroundings rather than photosynthesizing.
example_sentence: The damp basement walls were covered in a thick green fungus. Scientists are studying the unique properties of this rare forest fungus. A common foot fungus can often be treated with over-the-counter creams. The fallen tree trunk was slowly being decomposed by various types of fungus.

english_meaning: A building or structure in an amusement park that contains various devices designed to surprise, trick, or amuse people. A place filled with optical illusions such as distorted mirrors or tilting floors. A situation or environment that is confusing, surreal, or unpredictable in a way that resembles a carnival attraction. An establishment providing lighthearted entertainment and laughter through gimmicks.
example_sentence: The children laughed uncontrollably as they tried to navigate the tilting floors of the funhouse. We walked through the funhouse and saw our reflections stretched out in the distorted mirrors. The political landscape has become a surreal funhouse where nothing is as it seems. They spent the entire afternoon exploring every hidden passage and trapdoor in the old funhouse.

english_meaning: A cable railway, especially one on a steep incline, in which ascending and descending cars are counterbalanced. Relating to or operated by a rope, cable, or cord. Pertaining to the umbilical cord or its structure. In anatomy, referring to a small bundle of nerve or muscle fibers. A system of transportation where traction is provided by a cable and gravity.
example_sentence: The tourists took the funicular to reach the monastery at the top of the cliff. Engineers designed a new funicular system to transport residents up the steep mountainside. Doctors monitored the funicular pulse to ensure the health of the fetus during the procedure. The old funicular railway has been operational since the late nineteenth century.

english_meaning: A state of deep depression or low spirits. A strong, musty, or unpleasant smell, often associated with sweat or lack of hygiene. A style of popular dance music evolved from soul music, characterized by a heavy rhythmic beat and syncopated basslines. A state of great fear or panic. To avoid or shirk something due to fear or lack of courage.
example_sentence: He has been in a deep funk ever since he lost his job. The gym locker room was filled with a thick, sweaty funk. The band played a groovy style of funk that kept everyone dancing all night. He tried to funk out of the competition because he was afraid of losing.

english_meaning: A crisp, sweet fried pastry made by pouring batter through a funnel into hot oil in overlapping strands. A popular fairground or carnival food, usually dusted with powdered sugar and sometimes served with fruit, syrup, or other toppings.
example_sentence: We shared a warm funnel cake at the county fair. The vendor dusted the funnel cake with powdered sugar. She topped her funnel cake with strawberries and cream. The smell of freshly fried funnel cakes drifted across the carnival.

english_meaning: To restore the appearance of something by cleaning, polishing, or repairing it. It can also mean to improve or refresh an idea, image, or reputation.
example_sentence: She furbished her old jewelry to make it sparkle again. The carpenter furbished the wooden table before selling it. They furbished up the town hall for the festival. The author furbished the manuscript before submitting it to the publisher.

english_meaning: Feeling extremely angry. A very strong and intense feeling of anger. It is used when someone is much angrier than usual, often because of injustice, insult, or serious disappointment. It can also describe actions, reactions, or situations that show extreme anger.
example_sentence: She was furious when she found out the truth. The manager became furious after repeated delays. His furious reaction surprised everyone in the room. The public was furious about the unfair decision.

english_meaning: A traditional unit of distance equal to one eighth of a mile, or about 201 meters. A measure of two hundred and twenty yards, still used in horse racing. An old English unit originally based on the length of a ploughed field.
synonyms: ["Eighth of a mile","220 yards","Imperial distance unit","Racing distance"]
example_sentence: The horse led the race by two furlongs. Eight furlongs make one mile. The old map shows distances in furlongs. Spectators cheered as the runners passed the final furlong.

english_meaning: A long narrow trench made in the ground by a plough. A deep wrinkle or line on a person's face, especially on the forehead. Any long narrow groove or channel in a surface. To make grooves in soil, or to wrinkle the brow in thought or worry.
example_sentence: The farmer walked slowly along the freshly cut furrow. Deep furrows lined his forehead after years of worry. Rainwater collected in the furrows between the rows. She furrowed her brow as she read the letter again.

english_meaning: In addition to what has already been said. Used to introduce a new point that adds to or supports the previous one. Moreover; besides; also.
example_sentence: The house is too small, and furthermore, it is too far from the city. He is a talented writer; furthermore, he is an excellent speaker. The report is incomplete, and furthermore, it contains several errors. Furthermore, the committee decided to extend the deadline by one week.

english_meaning: Done in a secretive or sneaky way, as if trying to avoid being seen or noticed. Suggesting that someone has something to hide. Behaving in a cautious or secretive manner. Stealthy and sly in movement or action.
example_sentence: She gave a furtive glance toward the door before slipping the document into her bag. His furtive behaviour during the meeting made everyone suspicious. The thief cast a furtive look around before reaching for the wallet on the counter. He made a furtive phone call from the corridor during the conference. The child gave a furtive smile before hiding the sweets behind her back.

english_meaning: Extreme anger including violent behavior. Intense, disordered, and often destructive rage.
example_sentence: Her eyes were blazing with furry. He flew into a furry when I refused.

english_meaning: A safety device in an electrical circuit that melts and breaks the connection when the current is too strong. A length of material that is burned to set off an explosive. To join or blend two or more things into a single whole. To melt together under heat. To stop working because a fuse has melted.
example_sentence: The fuse blew when we switched on the heater. Engineers fuse copper wires with great care. The film fuses comedy and social criticism. He lit the fuse and stepped back quickly.

english_meaning: The act or process of joining or blending two or more things into one single form. It is used in science for combining atoms or materials and in general language for mixing ideas, cultures, foods, or styles to create something new.
example_sentence: The movie displayed a perfect fusion of image and sound. Scientists study nuclear fusion to produce clean energy. The restaurant is famous for its fusion of Asian and European cuisine. The artist created a fusion of traditional and modern music styles. The doctor recommended spinal fusion surgery to reduce the patient's pain.

english_meaning: To show worry or concern over something small. To repeatedly complaining, worrying, or paying excessive attention to minor details or problems. Making a big deal out of a minor issue, showing unnecessary concern, or creating noise and commotion.
example_sentence: He fussed over the table setting before the guests arrived. 4 Stop fussing about your homework; it’s fine. She made a fuss over the broken vase. 2 There was a fuss about who would speak first.

english_meaning: To pay excessive attention to someone or something. To show unnecessary concern about minor details. To treat someone with too much care or affection. To worry excessively about the comfort of a guest.
example_sentence: Grandmothers always tend to fuss over their grandchildren during family visits. He dislikes it when people fuss over him while he is feeling sick. There is no need to fuss over the arrangement of the pillows. She started to fuss over the minor details of the wedding decorations.

english_meaning: Pompous, inflated, or pretentious language that sounds impressive but lacks real meaning or depth. A type of thick cotton fabric, usually dyed in a dark colour. Bombastic or high-sounding speech that is empty of substance.
example_sentence: The politician's speech was full of fustian that impressed few in the audience. Critics dismissed his writing as nothing more than fustian and hollow rhetoric. The tailor used fustian to make the heavy working trousers worn by the labourers. He was known for his fustian manner of speaking, full of big words but little meaning. The professor warned his students against the use of fustian in academic writing.

english_meaning: Useless or pointless; having no useful result. Something that is futile has no chance of success or achieves nothing despite effort. It implies that actions, attempts, or efforts are ineffective or unproductive.
example_sentence: Trying to convince him was futile because he had already made up his mind. All efforts to save the old building proved futile. It is futile to argue with someone who refuses to listen. The doctor admitted that further treatment would be futile.

english_meaning: An early twentieth-century artistic movement that celebrated speed, machinery, and modern life. A style in art, music, or literature that rejects tradition and praises technology. The belief that society should be shaped by future possibilities rather than the past.
example_sentence: Futurism began in Italy in the early 1900s. The exhibition explains the influence of futurism on design. Futurism admired machines, speed, and city life. Critics argue that futurism ignored the value of tradition.

english_meaning: A person who studies or predicts what will happen in the future. Someone whose ideas, work, or designs are focused on the future. Relating to art or design movements concerned with modern speed and technology. A follower of futurism in art or literature.
example_sentence: The futurist believes robots will assist in most homes. Her futurist ideas influenced modern architecture. He is a futurist who advises large companies. The gallery displays futurist paintings from the last century.

english_meaning: Having a modern design or quality that seems to belong to the future. Relating to ideas, technology, or styles that are far ahead of the present time. Imagining or describing what life may be like in years to come. Unusually advanced or innovative in appearance or function.
example_sentence: The museum has a futuristic glass dome. He wrote a futuristic novel about life on Mars. Their new office looks bright and futuristic. The concept car has a futuristic shape and silent engine.

english_meaning: The future considered as a whole or as a period yet to come. The quality or state of being in the future. Events, conditions, or possibilities that lie ahead. A literary or formal word for time still to come.
example_sentence: The poem reflects on love and futurity. No one can be certain about futurity. He spoke of futurity with quiet hope. Their plans were built on an uncertain futurity.

english_meaning: A person who studies and predicts future developments in society, science, and technology. An expert who analyses present trends in order to forecast what may happen later. A specialist in the field of futurology.
example_sentence: The futurologist predicted that most cars would be electric within a decade. A well-known futurologist addressed the technology conference. Futurologists study data to understand coming social changes. She works as a futurologist for a research institute.

english_meaning: The systematic study of possible future events and conditions. The practice of forecasting social, economic, and technological developments. A field of research that uses current data and trends to describe likely futures.
example_sentence: He teaches futurology at a European university. Futurology helps governments plan for long-term challenges. Her interest in futurology began with science fiction. The report applies futurology to the energy sector.

english_meaning: A device that triggers the explosion of a bomb, shell, or missile. A mechanism designed to detonate an explosive at a chosen moment. An alternative spelling of fuse used mainly in military contexts. To fit an explosive device with such a mechanism.
example_sentence: The shell was fitted with a delayed-action fuze. Engineers inspected the fuze before the test. A faulty fuze can make a weapon extremely dangerous. Technicians carefully fuze each device in the workshop.

english_meaning: A mass of short, soft, light fibres or hairs. A blurred or unclear appearance in an image or sound. A distorted electric guitar effect. To become blurred or indistinct. An informal and slang term for the police.
example_sentence: There was a soft fuzz on the surface of the peach. The old photograph has lost detail and shows only fuzz. He added fuzz to the guitar for a rougher sound. The picture began to fuzz as the signal weakened.

english_meaning: An electronic device that distorts the sound of an electric guitar. A guitar effects pedal used to create a rough, buzzing tone. A common name for a fuzz effect unit in music.
example_sentence: He switched on the fuzzbox for the guitar solo. The band's sound depends heavily on an old fuzzbox. She bought a vintage fuzzbox from a music shop. A fuzzbox can turn a clean tone into a growling one.

english_meaning: In a blurred or unclear manner. Without sharp definition or precise detail. In a soft, fluffy way. In a confused or vague manner of thinking or speaking.
example_sentence: The distant hills appeared fuzzily through the mist. He remembered the evening only fuzzily. The text was printed fuzzily on cheap paper. She spoke fuzzily after waking from a deep sleep.

english_meaning: The state of being blurred, unclear, or lacking sharp detail. The quality of being covered with soft short hairs. Vagueness or lack of precision in thought, language, or definition.
example_sentence: The fuzziness of the image made the text unreadable. There is some fuzziness in the definition of the term. He complained about the fuzziness of the old television screen. The fuzziness of the fabric made it pleasant to touch.

english_meaning: Not clear, unclear, or having a soft texture. Something that is difficult to see, understand, or describe clearly; can also refer to a texture that is soft, fluffy, or covered with fine hairs or fibers. It is used for both physical objects and abstract ideas.
example_sentence: The picture is fuzzy because the camera was shaking. I have a fuzzy memory of my childhood house. The kitten’s fur is soft and fuzzy. The edges of the drawing were fuzzy and unclear.

english_meaning: Talkative in a chatty way, especially about unimportant matters. Fond of talking a lot. Excessively communicative.
example_sentence: My gabby neighbor kept me on the phone for an hour. He becomes gabby after a cup of tea. She is friendly but a bit gabby at parties. The gabby tour guide entertained everyone with stories.

english_meaning: A fly that bites livestock, especially a horsefly. A person who persistently criticises or provokes others into action. Someone who annoys authorities by asking uncomfortable questions. An irritating but useful critic who stirs up complacent people.
example_sentence: A gadfly settled on the horse's back in the summer heat. The journalist was a gadfly who exposed official corruption. Every council needs a gadfly to question lazy decisions. He enjoyed his role as the gadfly of the university board.

english_meaning: A small mechanical or electronic device or tool, especially an ingenious or novel one. A handy appliance designed to perform a particular task. A useful little tool or contrivance. Any small manufactured item that helps with a specific job.
example_sentence: This kitchen gadget makes peeling fruit much easier. He loves buying the latest tech gadgets. Every year new gadgets are launched at the electronics fair. The mechanic used a small gadget to fix the engine. Children are fascinated by clever little gadgets.

english_meaning: To stop someone from speaking or to choke/nauseate. To prevent someone from speaking by force or constraint, or to cause someone to feel nausea or choke. A device to prevent speech or silence someone. A gag is an object or action used to stop someone from speaking, often by covering the mouth. It can also mean a joke, trick, or comic stunt
example_sentence: The kidnappers gagged the hostages before moving them. He tried to gag his laughter during the serious meeting. The smell of the chemicals made her gag. The robber put a gag on the victim to keep him silent. The comedian’s gag made everyone laugh. She tried to gag her anger but failed.

english_meaning: To obtain or secure something desired or valuable. To increase in amount, weight, or value. To reach a place with effort. Something acquired or won, especially a profit. To make progress or improvement.
example_sentence: She hopes to gain new skills from the training. The company reported huge financial gains this year. He gained ten pounds during the winter. It took hours to gain the top of the mountain.

english_meaning: To make progress, become stronger, or increase in influence, success, or popularity.
example_sentence: The new political party is gaining ground among young voters. Solar energy is gaining ground as an alternative to fossil fuels. Our team gained ground in the second half of the match. Education for girls is gaining ground in rural areas.

english_meaning: A nonstandard and uncommon form of gain ground. To make progress or become more successful. To advance or improve one's position relative to others. To win increasing support, acceptance, territory, or advantage
example_sentence: The party is beginning to gain ground in the latest polls. The brand gained ground against its main rival last year. He felt he was gaining ground after months of hard practice. The reform movement continues to gain ground among younger voters.

english_meaning: To deny or contradict a fact, statement, or opinion. To dispute. To speak against. To refuse to accept the truth of something. Used mostly in formal or literary contexts and often in negative sentences such as 'no one can gainsay' to mean that something is undeniable.
example_sentence: No one can gainsay his contribution to the success of the company. It is impossible to gainsay the importance of education in modern life. The minister tried to gainsay the reports published by the media. Few would gainsay that he is the finest writer of his generation. She did not gainsay a single word of the witness's statement.

english_meaning: A day of celebration or festivities. It is typically a day marked by special events, public holidays, or joyful gatherings. It refers to an occasion when people come together to celebrate a victory or tradition.
example_sentence: The town celebrated the harvest with a grand gala day. The king's coronation was declared a gala day for the entire nation. Children look forward to the annual school gala day every summer. The city was decorated with flags and lights for the independence gala day.

english_meaning: To travel or roam around in search of pleasure and excitement, often in a carefree or irresponsible manner. To go from place to place for amusement without a serious purpose. To wander about in a playful or leisure-seeking way.
example_sentence: Instead of studying, he spent the weekend galivanting around the city with his friends. She loves to galivant through the old bazaars whenever she visits a new country. Stop galivanting and come home — there is work to be done. They galivanted from one coffee shop to another all afternoon without any plan. Her parents were tired of her galivanting abroad every summer instead of saving money.

english_meaning: Third-person singular present tense of galivant. Refers to the action of travelling or wandering around in search of pleasure and amusement, especially in a carefree way.
example_sentence: He galivants around town every evening instead of focusing on his responsibilities. She galivants from one party to another without a care in the world. Everyone knows he galivants more than he works. She galivants through the countryside on her days off. He galivants to a new city every month just for the thrill of it.

english_meaning: Brave, heroic, and chivalrous, especially in the face of danger. Politely attentive and respectful, especially toward women. Strikingly fine or splendid in appearance. A man who is attentive, courteous, and charming.
example_sentence: The gallant soldier rescued three civilians from the burning building. He made a gallant effort to save the drowning child despite the strong current. She admired his gallant manners and the way he treated everyone with respect. The gallant knight pledged his loyalty to the king and the people of the land. His gallant behaviour at the event made a lasting impression on all who were present.

english_meaning: A small pear-shaped organ located beneath the liver. A hollow sac that stores and concentrates bile produced by the liver. An organ that releases bile into the small intestine to help digest fatty foods. A part of the biliary system that can develop stones and become inflamed.
example_sentence: The gallbladder stores bile until the body needs it. She had her gallbladder removed after months of pain. Fatty meals often trigger gallbladder attacks. An ultrasound revealed several stones in his gallbladder.

english_meaning: A building or room for the exhibition of art or photographs. A balcony or upper level in a theater or church providing seating. A long narrow passage or hallway often used for a specific purpose. A group of spectators at a sporting event or public performance. A collection of images or items displayed for viewing on a digital platform.
example_sentence: The modern art gallery is hosting a new exhibition of local landscape paintings. We managed to secure cheap tickets in the gallery of the old opera house. The photographer uploaded her latest travel portfolio to an online gallery. He walked down the long gallery connecting the two wings of the mansion.

english_meaning: A long, narrow ship propelled chiefly by oars, often also fitted with sails. A long rowing boat formerly carried by a warship. The kitchen on a ship, aircraft, or train. A metal or wooden tray formerly used to hold composed type. A preliminary printed proof used for correction before publication.
example_sentence: The ancient Greeks used galleys for naval warfare. The flight attendant was busy preparing meals in the galley. I need to review the galley proofs before the book goes to print. The narrow galley was filled with the smell of cooking.

english_meaning: A unit of liquid volume equal to about 3·785 liters in the United States and about 4·546 liters in Britain. A measure equal to four quarts or eight pints. A container holding this amount of liquid. A large quantity of liquid, used informally in the plural.
example_sentence: The truck uses about ten gallons of fuel each day. She bought a gallon of drinking water for the trip. One gallon equals eight pints. Gallons of rainwater collected in the yard overnight.

english_meaning: To shock, excite, inspire, or motivate someone into taking action. To encourage or stimulate people to act with energy and determination. To strongly influence or awaken someone emotionally or mentally. To coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc to prevent rusting. To energize or unite people for a common purpose.
example_sentence: The leader’s speech galvanised the community to help flood victims. The shocking news galvanised the workers into protesting for their rights. The coach galvanised the team before the final match. The factory galvanised the steel pipes to prevent rust.

english_meaning: To shock, excite, inspire, or motivate someone into taking action. To encourage or stimulate people to act with energy and determination. To strongly influence or awaken someone emotionally or mentally. To coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc to prevent rusting. To energize or unite people for a common purpose.
example_sentence: The leader's speech galvanized the team to work harder. The tragic event galvanized the community into helping the victims. Good teachers galvanize students to achieve success. The factory galvanizes steel pipes to protect them from rust.

english_meaning:
To jump, skip or move lightly.
Also used for playful leaping or springing. To move with light jumping steps often in a playful or energetic way. In older or dialectal English it can refer to a skipping movement similar to frolicking.
example_sentence: The children began to gambel across the field after school. A young goat might gambel around the yard on a sunny morning. She felt so happy that she started to gambel down the path. The puppy would gambel whenever it saw its owner.

english_meaning: To risk money or something valuable on an uncertain outcome. To take a risky chance in hopes of gaining something. To play games of chance for money. A risky decision or move that may bring either success or failure. To act without certainty hoping for a positive outcome. A risky action or decision. A situation, choice or move that involves uncertainty where the outcome can be success or failure. It can also refer to an act of betting money in games of chance.
example_sentence: He likes to gamble on horse races. Starting a new business is always a gamble. They gambled all their savings and lost. She decided to gamble on a new career path. Choosing that route was a gamble but it saved us time. His decision to quit his job was a personal gamble.

english_meaning: A person who bets money on games, chances or risky decisions. Someone who regularly takes risks for possible gain, especially by betting on cards, sports, lotteries or other uncertain outcomes. It can also describe a person who takes big chances in life or business.
example_sentence: He became a gambler after he started visiting casinos every weekend. A smart gambler knows when to stop. She is not a gambler in life and prefers safe choices. The company took a gambler’s approach by investing in an unpredictable market.

english_meaning: Risking money or something valuable on a game, event, or decision where the result is uncertain. The act of placing money or something valuable on an uncertain outcome, usually in games, sports, betting, lotteries, casinos, or risky decisions. It involves the hope of gaining something but also the chance of losing what is staked. It can be casual, recreational, online, or professional.
example_sentence: Many people lose their savings because of gambling. Online gambling has become more popular in recent years. He quit gambling after realizing its negative effects on his life. Gambling can be addictive if someone is not careful.

english_meaning: To jump or skip about playfully; to frolic. To move about in a lively, playful, or carefree manner, often with jumps and skips. Commonly used to describe the energetic, joyful movements of children or animals. A playful skip or jump; frolic. An instance of lively, joyful movement, often jumping or skipping about.
example_sentence: The lambs gambolled in the sunny meadow. Children were gamboling on the playground after school. Puppies love to gambol around in the garden. The deer gambolled across the field without a care.

english_meaning: An abnormal obsession with marriage. An excessive and uncontrollable desire to get married. A compulsion to make repeated or unusual marriage proposals. An unhealthy preoccupation with weddings and married life. A mania in which marriage becomes the centre of a person's thoughts.
example_sentence: His gamomania led him to propose to almost every woman he met. The counsellor described her behaviour as a case of gamomania. Gamomania is rarely discussed outside psychology books. The character in the play suffers from clear gamomania.

english_meaning: Fear of marriage or commitment. An intense and persistent fear of marriage or long term romantic commitment. A person with gamophobia may feel anxiety, panic, or emotional distress when thinking about getting married or entering a serious relationship.
example_sentence: He avoided long term relationships due to his gamophobia. Gamophobia can sometimes be linked to past emotional trauma. Her gamophobia made wedding discussions very stressful. Therapy helped him understand and manage his gamophobia.

english_meaning: An organized group of criminals or hoodlums. A group of friends or associates who frequently meet or socialize. A group of workers or laborers organized together for a specific task. A set of similar or related objects that work together. To form a group against someone or something in a hostile manner.
example_sentence: The notorious street gang was finally arrested by the local police. I am planning to hang out with the old gang this weekend. A gang of laborers was hired to repair the damaged railway tracks. The neighborhood kids decided to gang up on the school bully.

english_meaning: Material that is no longer useful, such as household waste, old or spoiled items, or anything considered worthless. Waste material; trash; things that are discarded.
example_sentence: He threw the old papers into the garbage. Don’t leave garbage on the street. The kitchen smelled of garbage. Sorting garbage helps the environment. Delete all garbage emails from your inbox.

english_meaning: To reproduce or transmit a message, sound, or signal in a confused, distorted, or unclear way. To mix up or distort information so that it is difficult to understand. To scramble or alter the meaning of something, often unintentionally.
example_sentence: The poor phone signal caused his voice to garble and we could barely understand him. She tended to garble instructions when she was nervous or under pressure. The radio operator's message was garbled by interference and could not be decoded. Please repeat clearly — your message was garbled by the background noise. He was known to garble facts when he tried to speak too quickly.

english_meaning: A wreath or rope of flowers, leaves, or other material used as decoration. An honour or prize given as a sign of distinction. To decorate something with a garland. A chain of decorative material hung in a curve or loop.
example_sentence: The guests placed a garland of fresh flowers around the statue during the ceremony. She was presented with a colourful garland of marigolds as a traditional welcome. The children made paper garlands to decorate the classroom for the festival. A beautiful garland of roses and jasmine hung above the entrance of the wedding hall. Garlands of lights were strung between the trees to illuminate the garden for the party.

english_meaning: A strong-smelling pungent-tasting bulb used as a flavoring in cooking and in herbal medicine. It is a plant of the onion genus, widely cultivated for its culinary uses. The bulb is composed of several individual cloves enclosed in a papery skin. It is known for its distinctive aroma and numerous health benefits.
synonyms: ["Allium Sativum","Clove","Ail","Rustic Treacle","Camphor Of The Poor","Stinking Rose","Garlic Bulb","Flavoring","Seasoning","Herb"]
example_sentence: He crushed three cloves of garlic to add to the pasta sauce. The strong smell of garlic filled the entire kitchen. Roasted garlic has a much milder and sweeter flavor than raw garlic. Many people believe that eating raw garlic boosts the immune system.

english_meaning: A deep red semi-precious stone used in jewellery. Any of a group of silicate minerals occurring in several colours. A dark red colour resembling that of the stone. The birthstone traditionally associated with the month of January.
example_sentence: She wore a brooch set with a dark garnet. Garnet is the traditional birthstone for January. The stone was polished until the garnet shone. He chose a garnet pendant for his sister.

english_meaning: To decorate or add a finishing touch to a dish of food with a small amount of another food or herb. Something used as a decoration on a plate or dish. To seize a portion of a debtor's wages or assets by legal authority. An embellishment added to food for visual appeal.
example_sentence: She added a sprig of parsley as a garnish to the soup before serving it. The chef used a slice of lemon as a garnish on the grilled fish. The colourful garnish of fresh herbs made the dish look professional and appetising. His salary was garnished by the court to repay the debts he owed. A simple garnish can make even the most basic dish look elegant and well-presented.

english_meaning: A body of troops stationed in a town or fort to defend it. The building or fortification where troops are stationed. To station troops in a place for defensive purposes. A military post or installation.
example_sentence: The garrison was reinforced with additional troops as the threat of attack increased. The medieval castle served as the main garrison for the king's army. The soldiers returned to the garrison after completing their patrol of the border. A small garrison of fifty soldiers was left behind to guard the abandoned fort. The garrison commander ordered all troops to be on high alert throughout the night.

english_meaning: Excessive talking, especially about trivial matters. The habit of talking too much, often in a way that is unimportant, repetitive, or lacks serious purpose. It usually describes someone who cannot stay silent and tends to speak more than necessary.
example_sentence: His garrulity during meetings often wastes valuable time. The teacher warned the student about his garrulity in class. Her garrulity made it difficult for others to share their opinions. Despite his intelligence, his garrulity reduces his impact in discussions.

english_meaning: A substance that has no fixed shape or volume and expands to fill its container. One of the three common states of matter, lighter and less dense than liquid or solid. A fuel such as natural gas used for cooking, heating, or power. In American usage, petrol used in vehicles. To attack or poison with gas.
example_sentence: Oxygen is a colourless gas. The cooker runs on natural gas. He stopped to fill the car with gas before the trip. Heating the liquid turns it into a gas.

english_meaning: Extravagant boasting or bragging. Vain and empty talk intended to impress others. To boast or brag in an extravagant manner. Pompous and self-aggrandizing speech.
example_sentence: His constant gasconade about his wealth eventually annoyed everyone around him. She dismissed his speech as nothing more than gasconade and empty promises. He was quick to gasconade about his achievements, whether anyone was listening or not. The politician's gasconade impressed no one who knew the true state of the economy. After his gasconade about his abilities, he was given a test and failed immediately.

english_meaning: To psychologically manipulate a person into questioning their own sanity or perception of reality. To deceive someone by persistently denying facts or events that occurred. To undermine a person's confidence in their own memory or judgment. To present false information with the intent of making a victim doubt their own senses. To engage in subtle emotional abuse by invalidating someone's experiences.
example_sentence: He tried to gaslight her into believing that the argument never happened. Victims often feel confused when someone attempts to gaslight them over a long period. The manipulative boss would gaslight his employees to avoid taking responsibility for his mistakes. It is a form of emotional abuse to gaslight a partner by denying their valid feelings.

english_meaning: The large, powerful muscle at the back of the lower leg that forms most of the visible bulge of the calf. A two-headed superficial calf muscle that arises from the lower end of the thigh bone and joins the Achilles tendon. The muscle mainly responsible for pointing the foot downward and for pushing the body forward while walking, running, or jumping.
synonyms: ["Calf muscle","Gastroc","Triceps surae (part)","Lower leg muscle","Superficial calf muscle"]
example_sentence: The gastrocnemius is the muscle that gives the calf its rounded shape. Runners often stretch the gastrocnemius before a long race. He tore his gastrocnemius while playing football last season. The doctor examined the swelling in her gastrocnemius muscle.

english_meaning: A medical practitioner who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the digestive system. A doctor who focuses on the health of the gastrointestinal tract and liver. A specialist who performs endoscopic procedures to examine the internal organs. A clinical expert in managing conditions like acid reflux, ulcers, and inflammatory bowel disease.
example_sentence: The gastroenterologist recommended a colonoscopy to investigate the patient's recurring abdominal pain. After years of struggling with digestion issues, she finally made an appointment with a leading gastroenterologist. A gastroenterologist may treat conditions ranging from minor heartburn to complex liver diseases. He spent four additional years in specialized training to become a board-certified gastroenterologist.

english_meaning: Related to the stomach and intestines. Anything connected with the digestive system, especially the stomach and intestines. It is commonly used in medical and health contexts to describe organs, diseases, symptoms, or treatments involving digestion.
example_sentence: He visited the doctor due to a gastrointestinal problem. Spicy food can cause gastrointestinal discomfort. The patient was treated for a gastrointestinal infection. Stress sometimes affects gastrointestinal health.

english_meaning: A person who attends a party, event, or gathering without being invited or without permission.
example_sentence: The wedding was going smoothly until a few gatecrashers created chaos. Security guards stopped the gatecrasher from entering the concert without a ticket. He is such a gatecrasher, always showing up uninvited at private parties. The host politely asked the gatecrashers to leave the birthday celebration.

english_meaning: To bring things or people together in one place. To collect information, items, or resources gradually. To come together as a group. To increase in force, speed, or amount over time. To understand or conclude something from information available.
example_sentence: The family gathered around the table for dinner. She gathered flowers from the garden for the vase. The storm gathered strength as it moved inland. I gather from your message that you cannot attend.

english_meaning: A meeting or assembly of people. The act of coming together in one place. The collection or bringing together of things. A group of people assembled for a common purpose or social occasion.
example_sentence: A large gathering of community members attended the town hall meeting last night. The family gathering during the holidays brought everyone together after years apart. She found the annual gathering of writers both inspiring and deeply motivating. The gathering of evidence took several months before the case could be taken to court. Authorities restricted public gatherings during the period of the health emergency.

english_meaning: Someone or something that is socially awkward, tactless, or crude in manner. It often describes behavior that is inelegant or unpolished, especially in social settings.
example_sentence: His gauche remarks at the dinner offended many guests. She felt gauche wearing the old-fashioned dress among the stylish crowd. The new employee’s gauche handling of the client meeting embarrassed the team. He gave a gauche attempt at dancing, knocking over a chair in the process.

english_meaning: Extremely thin and bony, usually because of illness, hunger, or worry. Looking pale, hollow-cheeked, and worn out. Describing a place that appears bleak, bare, and grim. Having a harsh and desolate appearance.
example_sentence: He looked gaunt after months of illness. Her gaunt face showed the strain of the long journey. The gaunt ruins stood alone on the hillside. Refugees arrived tired, gaunt and hungry.

english_meaning: A strong protective glove, especially one worn as part of armour. A challenge or confrontation, as in the phrase 'throw down the gauntlet'. A difficult ordeal in which a person faces criticism or danger from several sides. Historically, a military punishment in which a person ran between two rows of men who struck him.
example_sentence: The knight removed his gauntlet before shaking hands. The new policy had to run the gauntlet of public criticism. She picked up the gauntlet and accepted the challenge. He wore heavy gauntlets while welding the metal frame.

english_meaning: The state of being extremely thin and bony. A pale, worn, and hollow appearance caused by illness or hardship. Bleakness or bareness in the look of a place. A grim and desolate quality.
example_sentence: The gauntness of his face shocked his old friends. Years of famine had left a gauntness in every village. There was a striking gauntness about the abandoned factory. Doctors noted the gauntness typical of long malnutrition.

english_meaning: A thin, transparent fabric with a loose open weave, often used in surgical dressings. A very fine mesh of wire or similar material. A light, airy material used in clothing or medical bandages. Any thin, delicate, and transparent fabric or material.
example_sentence: The nurse wrapped the wound carefully with several layers of sterile gauze. The costume designer used layers of white gauze to create a flowing, ethereal dress. Gauze curtains allowed the soft morning light to filter gently into the room. The doctor placed a square of gauze over the cut before applying the bandage. Surgical gauze is kept sterile to prevent infection when applied to open wounds.

english_meaning: To stare openly and stupidly at something or someone. To look at something in a rude or unintelligent manner. To gaze awkwardly or with open curiosity. To stare in an obvious, clumsy way.
example_sentence: People began to gawk at the unusual street performer who had gathered a large crowd. Don't gawk at people — it is impolite and makes them uncomfortable. The tourists gawked at the enormous skyscraper as they passed it on the tour bus. Passersby stopped to gawk at the accident scene on the side of the motorway. She felt uncomfortable when she noticed people gawking at her through the café window.

english_meaning: Awkward, clumsy, and ungraceful in movement or appearance. Tall and thin in an awkward way, especially of a young person. Lacking grace or social ease. Ungainly and stiff in the way one moves.
example_sentence: The gawky teenager tripped over his own feet during the dance. He was a gawky boy who grew into a confident young man. Her gawky movements made her feel embarrassed at the party. The gawky calf struggled to stand on its long legs.

english_meaning: To stare openly in a stupid or rude manner. To look at something with open-mouthed curiosity or amazement. British informal term similar in meaning to gawk. To look in a dumb, fascinated way.
example_sentence: The crowd began to gawp at the performer who was breathing fire in the town square. Stop gawping and help me move this heavy box, please. She couldn't help but gawp at the enormous diamond ring in the jewellery shop window. The children gawped at the magician as he pulled item after item from an empty hat. He was so astonished that he simply stood there and gawped for several seconds.

english_meaning: Homosexual; sexually or romantically attracted to people of the same sex, especially used of men. (Old use) Happy, cheerful, lively, and full of fun. Bright and attractive in appearance, especially of colours or decorations.
example_sentence: He has been openly gay since his college days. The couple recently got married in a small gay wedding ceremony. The children were in a gay mood at the picnic. The streets were decorated with gay lights for the festival. She wore a gay floral dress to the party.

english_meaning: To look steadily and intently at something or someone. A long, fixed look, often showing deep thought, curiosity, admiration, or surprise. As a verb, it means to look at something with steady attention. As a noun, it describes the act or state of looking intently.
example_sentence: She gazed at him in an amazement. He sat for hours just gazing into space. She dropped her gaze(-stopped looking). He met her gaze(=looked at her while she looked at him)

english_meaning: An official journal or newspaper, especially one published by a government or official body. To publish or announce something officially in a gazette. A newspaper or periodical that reports news, announcements, or official matters.
example_sentence: The appointment was officially announced in the government gazette last Tuesday. She searched through old copies of the gazette to find records of her great-grandfather's land. The soldiers' names were published in the gazette after the official award ceremony. The government uses the gazette to inform the public of new laws and regulations. He submitted an article about the town's history to the local gazette for publication.

english_meaning: A small lizard often found on walls in warm regions. A small to medium sized reptile belonging to the lizard family. It is known for its ability to climb walls and ceilings using special toe pads. Geckos are mostly active at night and are common in tropical and subtropical areas.
example_sentence: A gecko was sitting quietly on the wall near the light. Geckos help control insects in homes. The gecko disappeared quickly across the ceiling. Many people see geckos in warm climates at night.

english_meaning: A person who is extremely enthusiastic and knowledgeable about a specific subject, especially technology or computers. An obsessive fan or enthusiast. Informally, someone who is considered socially awkward but intellectually focused. A person deeply absorbed in a niche interest.
example_sentence: He is a total tech geek who spends his evenings building and testing new computer hardware. She is a cinema geek and has watched every film that won the Academy Award. The conference attracted thousands of science geeks eager to hear the latest research. Being a geek about your hobby can actually lead to a successful career. He embraced his reputation as a geek after his blog about programming earned him global recognition.

english_meaning: Fond of technology, computers, or niche interests
example_sentence: He is geeky about computers. That movie is for geeky fans. Geeky people love coding. She has a geeky obsession with gadgets.

english_meaning: Extremely cold, icy, or frigid. Chilly to a very high degree. Having or producing a very cold temperature, especially in a way that is unpleasant or severe.
example_sentence: The gelid wind swept across the mountain pass and made it impossible to continue. She stepped out into the gelid morning air and immediately wished she had worn a heavier coat. The gelid water of the mountain stream took his breath away when he stepped in. A gelid silence fell over the room when the announcement was made. The explorers struggled to survive in the gelid conditions of the polar region.

english_meaning: The scientific study of laughter and its effects on the human body and mind. A branch of research examining the physiological and psychological benefits of laughter. The study of humour and laughter in medicine and therapy.
example_sentence: Gelotology explains why laughter can reduce stress and pain. Researchers in gelotology study how humour affects the immune system. She wrote her thesis on gelotology and its use in therapy. Gelotology suggests that shared laughter strengthens social bonds.

english_meaning: A precious or semi-precious stone, especially when cut and polished. Something that is highly prized or considered to be of exceptional value. A person or thing that is considered remarkable, wonderful, or outstanding. A jewel or treasure.
example_sentence: The museum displayed a stunning gem that had once belonged to a royal dynasty. This old novel is a real gem that deserves to be read by far more people. The antique shop had several hidden gems tucked among the ordinary items. She is a gem of a person — always kind, generous, and willing to help others. The designer used a rare gem at the centre of the ring to make it truly unique.

english_meaning: The generation born after Gen Z. People born roughly from 2010 to the mid 2020s. They are the first generation fully born in a world of smartphones, artificial intelligence, social media, and constant internet access. Their upbringing is strongly shaped by digital technology, online learning, and rapid social change.
synonyms: ["Generation Alpha","Digital native generation","Post Gen Z generation","Tech native children"]
example_sentence: Gen Alpha children learn to use tablets before they learn to write. Schools are adapting their teaching methods for Gen Alpha students. Gen Alpha is expected to be more tech savvy than any previous generation. Parents are concerned about screen time for Gen Alpha kids.

english_meaning: The generation expected to be born roughly from 2025 to 2039. This generation is predicted to grow up in a highly digital, AI driven, and climate conscious world, with technology deeply integrated into daily life.
example_sentence: Gen Beta children are expected to interact with AI from a very young age. Education systems will likely change significantly for Gen Beta. Climate awareness may shape the values of Gen Beta more strongly than earlier generations. Gen Beta is predicted to live in a world where digital and physical life are closely connected.

english_meaning: People born roughly between 1965 and 1980. The generation following the Baby Boomers and preceding Millennials. They grew up during political changes, the rise of technology, and shifting social norms. Often seen as independent, resourceful, and skeptical of authority.
example_sentence: Many Gen X employees are comfortable balancing work and life. Gen X witnessed the transition from analog to digital technology. Some of the most influential entrepreneurs today are from Gen X. Gen X values stability but also seeks personal fulfillment.

english_meaning: Generation Y refers to people born roughly between 1981 and 1996. Gen Y, also called Millennials, is the generation that grew up during the rise of the internet, mobile phones, and globalization. They are often described as tech aware, adaptable, socially conscious, and focused on work life balance
example_sentence: Gen Y values flexibility and purpose in the workplace Many Gen Y professionals adapted quickly to remote work Gen Y witnessed the transition from analog to digital life Companies often design products keeping Gen Y in mind

english_meaning: The generation born roughly between 1997 and 2012. The cohort following Millennials, characterized by being tech-savvy, socially aware, and influenced by digital media from a young age. They value diversity, climate action, and digital connectivity.
example_sentence: Gen Z prefers online learning platforms over traditional classrooms. Many Gen Z members use social media for activism. Fashion trends among Gen Z change rapidly. Gen Z is more conscious of mental health issues than previous generations.

english_meaning: To obtain or provide detailed information about something. To study or prepare quickly so as to become well informed. To brief someone thoroughly before an event or task.
example_sentence: I need to gen up before tomorrow's interview. She spent the evening genning up for the test. Can you gen me up on the new procedures? He genned up quickly and answered every question.

english_meaning: To learn detailed information about a particular subject. To research or read thoroughly about something before dealing with it. To make oneself well informed on a specific topic.
synonyms: ["Read up on","Study","Research","Brush up on","Learn about","Investigate","Swot up on"]
example_sentence: You should gen up on the company before applying. He genned up on local history before the tour. I must gen up on the new tax rules. She genned up on first aid over the weekend.

english_meaning: The plural form of genus. Groups of related living organisms ranking above species and below family in biological classification. Broad classes or categories of things sharing common features.
example_sentence: Several genera of orchids grow in this forest. Botanists have described thousands of plant genera. The two species belong to different genera. New genera are added as research continues.

english_meaning: Affecting or concerning all or most people, places, or things. Not specialised or limited to one particular area. Normal, usual, or widespread. A senior officer in the army, air force, or marines. Considering only the main features without details.
example_sentence: There is general agreement that the plan should go ahead. She gave us a general idea of the costs. The general retired after forty years of service. In general terms, the results were encouraging.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who treats a wide range of health conditions and provides primary care. A physician who offers comprehensive healthcare for patients of all ages. A family doctor who handles routine medical issues and refers to specialists when needed.
example_sentence: I visit my general practitioner for annual checkups. The general practitioner treated my cold. General practitioners provide comprehensive family care. She referred me to a specialist after consulting with my general practitioner.

english_meaning: The generation born after Gen Z. People born roughly from 2010 to the mid 2020s. They are the first generation fully born in a world of smartphones, artificial intelligence, social media, and constant internet access. Their upbringing is strongly shaped by digital technology, online learning, and rapid social change.
synonyms: ["Generation Alpha","Digital native generation","Post Gen Z generation","Tech native children"]
example_sentence: Generation Alpha is expected to be the most educated generation in history. Many children in Generation Alpha are learning to use tablets before they can read. Parents of Generation Alpha often worry about the effects of screen time. Marketing strategies now target Generation Alpha with interactive digital content.

english_meaning: The generation expected to be born roughly from 2025 to 2039. This generation is predicted to grow up in a highly digital, AI driven, and climate conscious world, with technology deeply integrated into daily life.
example_sentence: Generation Beta children often learn coding before they start school. Marketing strategies now target Generation Beta using interactive apps. Teachers need new methods to engage Generation Beta students. Social media platforms are evolving to suit Generation Beta’s preferences.

english_meaning: People born roughly between 1965 and 1980. The generation following the Baby Boomers and preceding Millennials. They grew up during political changes, the rise of technology, and shifting social norms. Often seen as independent, resourceful, and skeptical of authority.
example_sentence: Generation X grew up during the rise of personal computers. Many Generation X workers value work-life balance. Generation X experienced the transition from analog to digital media. The book discusses Generation X’s cultural impact.

english_meaning: Generation Y refers to people born roughly between 1981 and 1996. Gen Y, also called Millennials, is the generation that grew up during the rise of the internet, mobile phones, and globalization. They are often described as tech aware, adaptable, socially conscious, and focused on work life balance
example_sentence: Generation Y often prefers flexible working hours over a traditional 9-to-5 job. Social media plays a major role in the lives of Generation Y. Many members of Generation Y are highly conscious of environmental issues. Generation Y values experiences like travel and learning new skills over material possessions.

english_meaning: The generation born roughly between 1997 and 2012. The cohort following Millennials, characterized by being tech-savvy, socially aware, and influenced by digital media from a young age. They value diversity, climate action, and digital connectivity.
example_sentence: Many Generation Z students prefer online learning over traditional classrooms. Generation Z often leads trends on social media platforms. Companies are designing products specifically for Generation Z consumers. Environmental activism is common among Generation Z.

english_meaning: Willing to give, share, or help others kindly and freely. A generous person gladly gives money, time, help, love, or support to others without expecting anything in return. It can also describe something large or plentiful, such as a generous amount of food or money.
example_sentence: The generous man donated books to poor students. She is always generous with her time and support. They offered us a generous amount of food. His generous nature made him popular among friends.

english_meaning: Relating to genes or heredity. Involving or determined by the genetic material inherited from one's parents or ancestors. Pertaining to the study or science of genetics. Connected to characteristics passed down through biological inheritance.
example_sentence: The researchers identified a genetic mutation that increases the risk of the disease. Eye colour is largely determined by genetic factors inherited from one's parents. Genetic testing is now widely used to screen for hereditary conditions before birth. The genetic similarities between the two species suggest they share a common ancestor. Scientists have made remarkable progress in understanding the genetic basis of many disorders.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to genes or heredity. By inheritance from biological parents or ancestors. Through alteration or analysis of genetic material.
example_sentence: The twins are genetically identical. Some diseases are genetically inherited. The crops were genetically modified to resist pests. The two populations are genetically distinct.

english_meaning: Someone who is warm, cheerful, and easy to get along with. Can also describe a pleasant atmosphere.
example_sentence: The teacher had a genial smile that made the students comfortable. He is known for his genial personality and easygoing nature. The evening was genial, with soft music and warm lighting. Her genial manner helped resolve the conflict quickly.

english_meaning: The quality of being friendly, cheerful, and pleasant. Warmth and kindness in one's manner or attitude. A pleasant and good-natured disposition. Cordiality and warmth in social behavior. A friendly and welcoming nature.
example_sentence: His natural geniality made everyone feel welcome at the party. The teacher's geniality helped students feel comfortable in class. She greeted her guests with warmth and geniality. The manager was known for his geniality and kindness.

english_meaning: The deliberate and systematic destruction of a racial, political, or cultural group. It is a crime against humanity involving the mass killing of people based on their identity. It aims to wipe out an entire population or community.
example_sentence: The international court aims to prevent and punish the crime of genocide. History books record the horrific details of the genocide committed during the war. Many refugees fled their homes to escape the threat of systematic genocide. The world must stand together to ensure that genocide never happens again.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of sexual intimacy. A phobia in which a person feels panic at the thought of sexual contact. Extreme anxiety related to physical closeness with a partner. Also known as coitophobia.
example_sentence: Genophobia can seriously affect a person's relationships. Therapy helped her overcome her genophobia. The counsellor explained that genophobia is more common than people think. He avoided dating because of his genophobia.

english_meaning: The genetic makeup of an organism, as distinguished from its physical appearance or phenotype. The complete set of genes present in an individual. The specific combination of alleles that an organism carries for a particular trait.
example_sentence: The researchers analysed the genotype of each patient to determine their response to treatment. A plant's genotype determines many of its physical characteristics, including leaf shape and colour. The genotype of an individual remains constant throughout their life, unlike the phenotype. Scientists use genotype analysis to trace hereditary diseases through generations. Comparing the genotype of wild and cultivated varieties helps breeders develop improved crop strains.

english_meaning: A style or category of art, music, film, or literature. A type or class of creative work defined by form, style, or subject matter. A classification of creative works based on their shared characteristics or conventions.
example_sentence: She prefers reading in the mystery genre but occasionally enjoys literary fiction. The film is hard to classify because it blends the thriller and comedy genres so effectively. Hip-hop has grown from a local music genre into a global cultural phenomenon. He experimented with several genres before finding his voice as a romantic novelist. The publisher asked her to choose a specific genre so that the book could be marketed correctly.

english_meaning: Kind, calm, and careful in behaviour or manner. Not harsh, severe, or forceful in effect. Moderate in degree, strength, or slope. To make something softer or less severe.
example_sentence: She has a gentle voice that calms the children. A gentle breeze moved the curtains. The doctor advised gentle exercise after the surgery. The path rises with a gentle slope towards the temple.

english_meaning: A polite, honorable, and well-mannered man. A courteous form of address for a man. Historically, a man of high social rank or independent means. A man who behaves with dignity and consideration.
example_sentence: He behaved like a gentleman throughout the dispute. A gentleman offered his seat to the elderly passenger. Ladies and gentlemen, the show will begin shortly. The old portrait depicts a country gentleman.

english_meaning: The quality of being kind, mild, and considerate. Softness or tenderness in touch, movement, or manner. Freedom from harshness, violence, or severity. A calm and moderate nature.
example_sentence: Her gentleness put the frightened child at ease. Handle the injured bird with gentleness. He answered the criticism with patience and gentleness. The gentleness of the rain refreshed the garden.

english_meaning: A courteous, refined, and well-mannered woman. Historically, a woman of high social rank or good family. A woman considered honorable and dignified.
example_sentence: Everyone regarded her as a true gentlewoman. The novel follows a young gentlewoman in Victorian society. She spoke with the courtesy of a gentlewoman. A gentlewoman treated every guest with dignity.

english_meaning: In a mild, kind, or tender manner. With little force or pressure. Slowly and carefully to avoid damage or distress. In a gradual, slight, or moderate way. With a soft sound, movement, or slope.
example_sentence: She gently placed the sleeping baby in the crib. The nurse spoke gently to the frightened patient. Rain fell gently throughout the afternoon. The road slopes gently toward the river.

english_meaning: The process by which a poorer urban area changes as wealthier people and businesses move in. The renovation and rising value of property in such an area. Social change that may improve services but displace existing lower-income residents.
example_sentence: Gentrification brought new cafés to the neighborhood. Rising rents are a common effect of gentrification. Residents organized to prevent displacement caused by gentrification. The study examines both the benefits and costs of gentrification.

english_meaning: To renovate and improve a poorer urban area so that wealthier people and businesses move in. To make a place more fashionable or expensive. To cause social and economic change that may displace existing residents.
example_sentence: Developers plan to gentrify the old warehouse district. New luxury apartments may gentrify the neighborhood. Some residents welcome investment but fear efforts to gentrify the area. The once modest street has begun to gentrify rapidly.

english_meaning: People of high social position, especially those owning land but below the nobility. The upper or respectable class of a particular place or profession. People regarded as influential or socially prominent.
example_sentence: The local gentry attended the ceremony. Many country estates once belonged to the landed gentry. The town gentry supported the new library. He was born into a family of minor gentry.

english_meaning: To lower one's body briefly by bending one knee to the ground, typically in worship or as a sign of respect. It is a gesture of reverence often seen in religious ceremonies. Historically, it was also used to show subservience to royalty.
example_sentence: The followers were taught to genuflect before the altar. He chose to genuflect as a sign of deep respect for the ancient tradition. The knight would genuflect whenever the queen entered the throne room. It is customary in some cultures to genuflect before elderly spiritual leaders.

english_meaning: The act of bending the knee or touching it to the ground. This physical gesture is used to express reverence, worship, or extreme respect. It is a common practice in liturgical worship and traditional ceremonies.
example_sentence: The priest performed a solemn genuflection before the high altar. Her quick genuflection showed her deep devotion to the religious rite. The protocol required a formal genuflection when meeting the monarch. He made a genuflection and then took his seat in the quiet chapel.

english_meaning: The act of bending the knee as a sign of respect, reverence, or worship. It is a gesture often performed in religious contexts or when approaching a high-ranking official or monarch. The term can also refer to a servile or sycophantic display of obedience.
example_sentence: The devotee performed a deep genuflexion before the altar in the cathedral. In ancient times, a genuflexion was required when the king entered the hall. Her sudden genuflexion seemed more like a performance than a genuine act of faith. He showed his loyalty through a humble genuflexion during the ceremony.

english_meaning: Truly what something is said to be and completely authentic. Sincere and honest in character or intentions. Produced by or originating from the stated source. Not fake or counterfeit in any way.
example_sentence: The art expert confirmed that the painting was a genuine Picasso. She showed genuine concern for the welfare of the rescued animals. Only genuine leather was used to craft this luxury handbag. His apology felt genuine and helped to mend their broken relationship.

english_meaning: In a sincere and honest way, without pretence. Truly and really, as opposed to apparently. In a manner that is authentic and not imitated.
example_sentence: He was genuinely sorry for what he had said. She seemed genuinely surprised by the news. The painting is genuinely from the sixteenth century. I genuinely believe this is the right decision.

english_meaning: The quality of being real, authentic, and not false or copied. Sincerity and honesty of feeling or behaviour. The state of truly being what something is claimed to be.
example_sentence: Experts confirmed the genuineness of the manuscript. Her genuineness made everyone feel at ease. There is no doubt about the genuineness of his concern. The court examined the genuineness of the signature.

english_meaning: A group of closely related species in biological classification, ranking above species and below family. A class or kind of things sharing common characteristics. A category used in logic to include several subordinate kinds.
example_sentence: The domestic cat belongs to the genus Felis. Each genus contains one or more species. Scientists placed the fossil in a new genus. He explained the difference between a genus and a family.

english_meaning: Relating to geography; describing the physical features, boundaries, or location of an area. Based on position on the earth's surface.
example_sentence: The company divides its sales into geographic regions. Geographic data is stored in a digital map. The island's geographic isolation protected its wildlife. Prices differ by geographic area.

english_meaning: Relating to geography or to the physical features of an area. Concerned with the location, land, climate, or population of a place.
