example_sentence: The region has great geographical importance. Geographical barriers made travel difficult. The survey covers a wide geographical area. Rainfall varies according to geographical conditions.

english_meaning: In terms of geography or physical location. According to the arrangement of places on the earth's surface.
example_sentence: The two towns are geographically close but culturally different. Geographically, the province is mostly desert. The team is geographically spread across four countries. Rainfall is geographically uneven in the region.

english_meaning: The study of the earth's surface, its physical features, climate, resources, and populations. The physical layout and characteristics of a particular place. The general arrangement or structure of something.
example_sentence: She teaches geography at a secondary school. The geography of the valley makes farming difficult. We studied the geography of South Asia this term. He explained the geography of the political parties.

english_meaning: The identification of the real-world geographic position of a person, device, or object. The data that describes such a position, usually as latitude and longitude.
example_sentence: The app uses geolocation to find nearby restaurants. Please allow geolocation access in your browser. Geolocation data helped the rescue team reach the hikers. Some websites restrict content by geolocation.

english_meaning: Relating to geology; concerning the structure of the earth, its rocks, and their history. Occurring over very long periods of time, as in the formation of rocks and landforms.
example_sentence: A geological survey was carried out before drilling. These cliffs are of great geological interest. Mountains form over geological time. Geological faults run beneath the city.

english_meaning: From the point of view of geology. In terms of the earth's structure, rocks, or long-term physical processes.
example_sentence: Geologically, the region is still very young. The area is geologically unstable. The two ranges are geologically related. Geologically speaking, the change happened quickly.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies the structure, composition, and history of the Earth. An expert in rocks, minerals, and the processes that shape the land. A person who examines the Earth to locate resources such as oil or metals.
example_sentence: The geologist collected rock samples from the valley. Geologists warned that the slope was unstable. She works as a geologist for an oil company. A team of geologists studied the earthquake zone.

english_meaning: The scientific study of the Earth, including rocks, minerals, fossils, landforms, and the processes that shape the planet. The physical structure and history of a region's rocks.
example_sentence: Geology explains how mountains and valleys form. She collected rocks for her geology class. The geology of the area suggests an ancient riverbed. Mining companies study geology before digging. Fossils are an important part of geology.

english_meaning: Relating to the magnetic field of the Earth. Concerning the study of the Earth's magnetism and its effects. Describing disturbances caused by solar activity on the Earth's magnetic field.
example_sentence: A strong geomagnetic storm disrupted satellite signals. Scientists monitor geomagnetic activity from several stations. The compass needle responds to the geomagnetic field. Geomagnetic changes can affect migrating birds.

english_meaning: The magnetism of the Earth. The study of Earth's magnetic field, its causes, changes, and effects. Magnetic forces and patterns produced by the Earth and its interior. The branch of geophysics concerned with terrestrial magnetism.
example_sentence: Geomagnetism helps scientists understand the Earth's magnetic field. Compass needles work because of geomagnetism. Changes in geomagnetism can affect satellites and navigation systems. The students studied geomagnetism in their geophysics course. Solar storms can disturb geomagnetism for a short time.

english_meaning: Divination by means of figures, lines, or marks made on the ground. The practice of foretelling the future by interpreting patterns of earth or sand. A traditional method of arranging buildings in harmony with the land.
example_sentence: Geomancy was widely practised in medieval times. He wrote a book on the history of geomancy. Some builders still follow rules derived from geomancy. The old manuscript explains the symbols used in geomancy.

english_meaning: Relating to geometry or its rules and methods. Made up of regular shapes and lines such as squares, circles, and triangles. Increasing in a fixed ratio, as in a geometric progression.
example_sentence: The carpet has a bold geometric pattern. Geometric shapes dominate the building's design. The population grew at a geometric rate. She painted a mural of interlocking geometric forms.

english_meaning: The central value of a set of numbers calculated by multiplying them and taking the nth root. A type of average calculated by the product method rather than sum. A measure of central tendency for data sets involving rates or ratios. The nth root of the product of n numbers.
example_sentence: The geometric mean of 2 and 8 is 4. Use geometric mean for growth rates. The geometric mean is useful for averaging ratios. Investment returns are often calculated using geometric mean.

english_meaning: The plural of geometric mean. Values found by multiplying numbers together and taking the appropriate root. Average measures useful for ratios, rates, percentages, and proportional growth. Terms inserted between two numbers so that all terms form a geometric progression.
example_sentence: The geometric means are useful when comparing growth rates. We calculated the geometric means of the investment returns. The numbers 3 and 12 are geometric means between 1 and 36. Geometric means reduce the effect of extreme values in ratio data. The textbook explains how to find geometric means with roots.

english_meaning: A sequence of numbers in which each term is found by multiplying the previous term by the same fixed number. A mathematical progression with a constant ratio between consecutive terms. A pattern of growth or decrease by repeated multiplication.
example_sentence: The numbers 2, 6, 18, and 54 form a geometric progression. In a geometric progression, the common ratio stays the same. Population growth is sometimes modeled as a geometric progression. The teacher asked us to find the fifth term of the geometric progression. A savings plan can grow like a geometric progression when interest is compounded.

english_meaning: A sum of terms from a geometric progression. A mathematical series in which each term after the first is multiplied by a fixed common ratio. A finite or infinite sum with proportional terms.
example_sentence: The class learned how to find the sum of a geometric series. A geometric series may have a finite number of terms. Some infinite geometric series have a fixed sum. The formula depends on the first term and common ratio. The bouncing ball problem can be described by a geometric series.

english_meaning: Relating to geometry and its principles. Consisting of or resembling regular shapes and precise lines. Following exact mathematical proportions in design or arrangement.
example_sentence: The mosque is famous for its geometrical designs. He solved the problem using a geometrical method. Geometrical figures were drawn on the blackboard. The garden was laid out in a strict geometrical plan.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to geometry or uses geometric methods. In a pattern made of regular shapes and straight lines. At a rate that increases by a constant ratio, very rapidly.
example_sentence: The tiles are arranged geometrically across the floor. He proved the theorem geometrically rather than algebraically. The number of users increased geometrically after the launch. The hedges were trimmed geometrically into neat cubes.

english_meaning: The branch of mathematics dealing with points, lines, shapes, and space. The study of properties and relationships of figures in space. The mathematical science of size, shape, and position. The arrangement or configuration of objects.
example_sentence: We study triangles and circles in geometry class. Geometry is essential for architecture. Euclidean geometry studies flat surfaces. The geometry of the building is impressive.

english_meaning: Relating to the physics of the Earth. Concerning the study of Earth's physical properties and processes. Associated with geological and atmospheric phenomena. Involving the application of physics to Earth sciences.
example_sentence: Geophysical surveys help locate oil deposits. The geophysical characteristics of the region are unique. Earthquakes are studied using geophysical methods. Geophysical data reveals Earth's internal structure.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies the physical properties and processes of the Earth. A professional who applies physics principles to understand Earth's structure. A specialist in geophysics studying earthquakes, magnetic fields, and gravity. Someone who researches Earth's interior, atmosphere, and oceans.
example_sentence: The geophysicist studied seismic waves from the earthquake. She works as a geophysicist for an oil company. Geophysicists use sophisticated instruments for their research. The geophysicist explained plate tectonics.

english_meaning: Related to old age or elderly people. It refers to anything connected with old age, especially the health care, treatment, and medical needs of elderly people. It is commonly used in medicine, hospitals, and social care to describe services, patients, or conditions associated with aging.
example_sentence: The hospital has a special geriatric ward for elderly patients. She is studying geriatric medicine at the university. Geriatric care focuses on improving the quality of life for seniors. The doctor specializes in treating geriatric conditions.

english_meaning: Related to old age or elderly people, especially concerning their medical care. Refers to anything connected with the health, care, or treatment of older adults. It is often used in medical contexts to describe practices, studies, or services designed for elderly people.
example_sentence: The hospital has a geriatrical ward for elderly patients. She chose a geriatrical course to specialize in elderly care. The clinic focuses on geriatrical assessments for aging individuals. Geriatrical medicine requires understanding both physical and mental health of seniors.

english_meaning: A doctor who specializes in the health care of elderly people. A medical professional who diagnoses, treats, and manages diseases and conditions commonly affecting older adults, focusing on improving their quality of life and addressing age-related health issues.
example_sentence: The geriatrician recommended a new exercise plan for her elderly patient. He consulted a geriatrician to manage his father’s arthritis. Geriatricians often work in nursing homes and hospitals. The hospital hired a geriatrician to help with elderly patient care.

english_meaning: Relevant and appropriate to a subject being discussed. Closely connected with a matter or issue. Suitable and to the point. Fitting for the situation. Bearing directly on the topic.
example_sentence: Your comment is not germane to the discussion. She raised a point germane to the case. Please stick to issues germane to the agenda. The evidence was highly germane to the trial.

english_meaning: The scientific and social study of old age, ageing processes, and the particular problems of elderly people. A branch of knowledge that deals with the physical, mental, and social aspects of ageing. The study of the ageing process and its effects on human beings.
example_sentence: She pursued a career in gerontology after noticing the lack of care for elderly people in her community. The university introduced a new degree in gerontology to prepare students for working with ageing populations. Gerontology covers physical, psychological, and social aspects of growing older. Research in gerontology has led to significant improvements in the quality of life for elderly individuals. Gerontology is becoming increasingly important as the global population continues to age.

english_meaning: A form that is derived from a verb but that functions as a noun. It is typically formed by adding "-ing" to a verb root in English. It acts as a subject, object, or complement in a sentence. It represents an action or a state of being in a substantive way.
synonyms: ["Verbal Noun","Noun Equivalent","-ing Form","Substantive","Verbal","Activity Noun","Process Noun","Action Noun"]
antonyms: ["Finite Verb","Active Verb","Main Verb","Auxiliary Verb","Infinitive Verb","Stative Verb","Base Form","Conjugated Verb"]
example_sentence: Swimming is his favorite hobby on weekends. She enjoys reading more than watching television. The teacher focused on explaining the gerund to the students. Walking every day improves your overall cardiovascular health.

english_meaning: An adventure, exploit, or notable deed, especially one that is heroic or romantic. A tale of adventure, especially a verse romance from medieval literature. An archaic or literary term for a journey or adventure.
example_sentence: The bard recited the ancient gest of a hero who crossed seven mountains to save his people. Medieval gest literature was often performed aloud at royal courts and public gatherings. The gest of the wandering knight was recorded in one of the oldest manuscripts in the library. The poem narrated the gest of a soldier who returned home after a long and dangerous war. Scholars of medieval literature study the gest as an important form of early narrative poetry.

english_meaning: A movement that you make with your hands, your head or your face to show a particular meaning. Something that you do or say to show a particular feeling or intention. To move your hands, head, face, etc as a way of expressing what you mean or want.
example_sentence: They sent some flowers as a gesture of sympathy to the parents of the child. We do not accept responsibility but we will refund the money as a gesture of goodwill. He made a rude gesture at the driver of the other car. He gestured around the room, lost for words. He gestured abruptly for Virginia to get in the car. He gestured his desire to leave.

english_meaning: An action that shows kindness, friendly intention, or desire to improve relations. Something done voluntarily to show friendliness, peace, or cooperation, often to build trust or reduce tension between people, groups, or countries.
synonyms: ["Peace offering","Friendly gesture","Act of kindness","Token of goodwill","Olive branch"]
example_sentence: The company donated books as a gesture of goodwill to the local school. He apologized as a gesture of goodwill after the argument. The two countries released prisoners as a gesture of goodwill. She sent flowers as a gesture of goodwill to her colleague.

english_meaning: To enjoy something or find it exciting or amusing. To derive pleasure, excitement, or amusement from an activity, situation, or experience. It often implies a sense of fun, thrill, or delight in doing something or observing it.
example_sentence: I really get a kick out of watching old comedy movies. She gets a kick out of teasing her little brother. They get a kick out of traveling to new countries. He gets a kick out of trying extreme sports.

english_meaning: To regain energy or strength after being tired. A situation where someone feels very tired or exhausted, but after a short rest or change in activity, they suddenly regain energy and feel able to continue.
example_sentence: After walking for hours, I got a second wind and finished the hike easily. She felt exhausted during the meeting, but a cup of coffee gave her a second wind. The team got a second wind in the last quarter and scored two quick goals. He was struggling with the project, but seeing his progress gave him a second wind.

english_meaning: To succeed, progress, or advance, especially in one’s career or life.
example_sentence: Hard work helps you get ahead. She’s getting ahead in her studies. He works extra hours to get ahead. They plan to get ahead financially.

english_meaning: To surpass or move in front of someone in progress or rank.
example_sentence: She got ahead of her competitors. He’s trying to get ahead of the others. They got ahead of schedule. We must get ahead of our rivals.

english_meaning: To have a friendly or harmonious relationship with someone, or to manage or cope with a situation.
example_sentence: They get along very well. How are you getting along at work? The kids don’t get along. We got along despite differences.

english_meaning: To be on friendly terms or have harmony with someone.
example_sentence: I get along with my neighbors. She can’t get along with him. Do you get along with your boss? They get along despite disagreements.

english_meaning: To move from place to place or to overcome a problem.
example_sentence: He gets around by bus. News gets around quickly. We found a way to get around the rules. She gets around town easily.

english_meaning: To escape, leave, or go somewhere (especially for rest or freedom). To leave a situation.
example_sentence: The thief got away. Let’s get away this weekend. He barely got away alive. She needs to get away for a while.

english_meaning: To succeed in doing something wrong without being punished. To perform an action that is wrong, dishonest, or against rules and avoid punishment or consequences. It often implies skill, luck, or loopholes allow someone to escape accountability.
example_sentence: He got away with cheating. The thief got away with the robbery. Kids sometimes get away with mischief. She got away with lying. He got away with not paying his taxes for years. She got away with missing work because her boss liked her. The students got away with copying homework. He got away with using company resources for personal gain.

english_meaning: To recover after a difficult time. To recover or regain strength or success.
example_sentence: After losing his job, he worked hard to get back on his feet. It took her months to get back on her feet after the accident. The company is finally getting back on its feet after the financial crisis. With family support, he managed to get back on his feet quickly.

english_meaning: To become upset or angry, often over something small, to take offense unnecessarily.
synonyms: ["Lose temper","Get upset","Get angry","Take offense","Fly off the handle"]
example_sentence: Don’t get bent out of shape over a joke. He got bent out of shape when his friend canceled. She gets bent out of shape too easily. There’s no need to get bent out of shape—it’s not serious.

english_meaning: To suddenly become nervous or afraid to do something. To lose courage or confidence at the last moment, especially before an important or risky action like marriage, travel, business, or a decision
example_sentence: He got cold feet before his wedding. She got cold feet and canceled the trip. Don’t get cold feet now; you can do it. Investors got cold feet after the market crash.

english_meaning: To begin doing something seriously. To start focusing seriously on a particular task or activity, especially after some delay or distraction.
example_sentence: Let’s get down to business and start the meeting. After a short break, the students got down to studying. It’s time to get down to work if we want to finish on time. She finally got down to writing her report last night.

english_meaning: To get married. Informal expression used to describe two people entering into marriage, often in a casual or humorous context.
example_sentence: They finally decided to get hitched next summer. After dating for five years, John and Maria got hitched last weekend. He told all his friends he’s getting hitched. The couple got hitched in a small ceremony by the beach.

english_meaning: To move close to somebody so that you can talk about something without other people hearing. To gather closely together in a small group (often to talk privately, plan, or discuss something). In sports (especially football), when players form a circle to quickly plan strategy.
example_sentence: Students got into a huddle after the exam to talk. The teachers got into a huddle to decide how to handle the situation. The players got into a huddle before the final play of the match.

english_meaning: To become familiar with a task or situation after starting it. To find one’s natural rhythm or pace after some adjustment.
synonyms: ["Settle down","Find one’s rhythm","Adapt","Adjust","Get used to","Gain momentum"]
example_sentence: It took her a week to get into stride at her new job, but now she’s very confident. The team struggled in the beginning, but after half-time they really got into their stride.

english_meaning: To begin to do something with confidence and at a good speed after a slow uncertain start. To start doing something confidently and efficiently after a slow or uncertain beginning. To reach your natural pace, rhythm, or performance level.
synonyms: ["Find one’s rhythm","Gain confidence","Get the hang of it","Settle in","Hit one’s pace","Perform smoothly"]
example_sentence: After a nervous start, he finally got into his stride in the second set. She was nervous at the start of the presentation, but once she got into her stride, she spoke with confidence.

english_meaning: To make no progress at all. To achieve nothing despite effort. To fail to reach a goal or agreement. To end up in the same situation as before. To have no success in an attempt.
example_sentence: We argued for hours but got nowhere. Without proper planning, you will get nowhere in life. The negotiations got nowhere after two days. She tried her best but got nowhere with the project.

english_meaning: To leave or step down from something (like a vehicle or surface). To start a journey or leave a place. To avoid punishment. To stop touching or disturbing something or someone.
example_sentence: He got on the train at Karachi and got off in Lahore. She got off work early today. He got off without any punishment. Get off the table! It’s not safe.

english_meaning: To demand freedom from someone’s interference. To express irritation toward constant supervision. or criticism. To ask someone to stop controlling or monitoring your actions. To reject unwanted advice or pressure, Stop bothering me. Leave me alone. Stop interfering in what I am doing.
synonyms: ["Leave me alone","Back off","Stop bothering me","Give me a break","Mind your own business"]
example_sentence: Get off my back! I know what I am doing. My boss keeps checking everything, I wish he would get off my back. She told her brother to get off her back about studies. Please get off my back, I need some space to think.

english_meaning: To enter or climb onto a vehicle. To like someone and live or work well together. To move forward in work or life. To become old. To continue or carry on. To board, to have a good relationship, to make progress.
example_sentence: He got on the train at Karachi and got off in Lahore. I think they get on the wrong train. She got on the bus quickly before it left. I get on well with my colleagues at work. He is getting on in his career very fast. My grandfather is getting on in age but still active.

word: Get on like a house on fire
english_meaning: To get along extremely well with someone very quickly. It means two people feel an instant connection, enjoy each other’s company, and develop a strong bond right away, like a friendship that grows fast.
example_sentence: They met and got on like a house on fire. We got on like a house on fire at the party. The kids get on like a house on fire. They instantly got on like a house on fire.

word: Get one's ducks in a row
english_meaning: To organize things properly before starting something. To arrange all necessary details and preparations in order. To become well prepared and efficient.
synonyms: ["Organize","Prepare","Sort out","Arrange","Line up","Plan ahead","Tidy up","Set in order"]
example_sentence: Get your ducks in a row before you meet the investors. She got her ducks in a row and submitted the application early. We need to get our ducks in a row before the audit begins. He finally got his ducks in a row and launched the business.

english_meaning: To recover from something difficult or to overcome a problem, illness, or emotional pain.
example_sentence: She got over the flu. It took him years to get over his loss. He can’t get over his mistake. You’ll get over it soon.

english_meaning: To remove, discard, or eliminate something unwanted. To free oneself from something that is unnecessary, unwanted, or harmful. It can refer to objects, habits, situations, or even people in some contexts.
example_sentence: I need to get rid of old clothes in my wardrobe. She got rid of all the unnecessary papers on her desk. The company wants to get rid of outdated technology. He finally got rid of his bad habit of smoking.

english_meaning: To start a project, plan, organization, or venture successfully. To move an idea beyond planning and make it operational. To secure the effort, support, or resources needed for something to begin
example_sentence: It took years to get the new business off the ground. The charity finally got its literacy program off the ground last month. They struggled to get the film project off the ground because funding was limited. Once we get the app off the ground, we can look for investors.

word: Get taste of your own medicine
english_meaning: To receive the same unpleasant treatment that one has given to others. To experience the same bad behavior one has shown to someone else. A situation in which a person is treated unkindly in the way they treated others. Used when someone finally faces the consequences of their own actions. To be repaid in kind for one's unfair conduct.
example_sentence: He always mocked others, and today he got a taste of his own medicine. When she was ignored by her friends, she finally got a taste of her own medicine. The bully got a taste of his own medicine when a bigger boy pushed him. It felt satisfying to see him get a taste of his own medicine.

english_meaning: To start something, especially a process, activity, or discussion. It means to initiate an action so that progress begins. Often used when someone takes the first step to begin work, a project, conversation, or event.
example_sentence: Let’s get the ball rolling on the new project today She made a phone call to get the ball rolling on the event planning The manager held a meeting to get the ball rolling If we want success, we must get the ball rolling early

english_meaning: To find or discover true and often secret information or evidence about someone, especially that shows their faults, mistakes, or wrongdoing. It means to collect facts that can be used against a person.
example_sentence: The lawyer got the goods on the suspect. The journalist tried to get the goods on the corrupt politician. The detective finally got the goods on the thief and arrested him. She threatened to get the goods on her boss if he treated her unfairly. The lawyer got the goods on the company and proved the case in court.

word: Get the wrong end of stick
english_meaning: To misunderstand something or interpret a situation incorrectly. This idiom is used when someone completely misunderstands what is being said or done. The person may take a comment, action, or situation in the wrong way and form an incorrect conclusion. It often leads to confusion or unnecessary arguments because the real meaning was not understood properly.
synonyms: ["Misunderstand","Misinterpret","Get it wrong","Take something the wrong way","Be mistaken"]
antonyms: ["Understand correctly","Comprehend properly","Get the right meaning","Interpret accurately"]
example_sentence: I think you got the wrong end of the stick, I was talking about the meeting, not your work. She got the wrong end of the stick and thought I was angry with her. Don’t get the wrong end of the stick, I only asked a question to help you. He completely got the wrong end of the stick and left the room thinking he was fired.

word: Get the wrong end of the stick
english_meaning: To misunderstand something completely or interpret it in the wrong way. Jump to the wrong conclusion. Read something incorrectly. Miss the point. It is used when someone misunderstands a situation, message, or explanation, often leading to confusion or an incorrect reaction. It usually implies that the person has taken the meaning in a completely different or opposite way than intended.
synonyms: ["Misunderstand","Misinterpret","Get it wrong","Take it the wrong way","Misconceive"]
antonyms: ["Understand correctly","Interpret properly","Comprehend","Grasp the meaning","Get the point"]
example_sentence: I think you got the wrong end of the stick. I was only joking. She got the wrong end of the stick and thought I was angry with her. He completely got the wrong end of the stick about the meeting schedule. Don’t get the wrong end of the stick. I support your idea.

english_meaning: To finish, complete, or successfully deal with something. It can also mean to make contact (especially by phone) or to survive a difficult situation.
example_sentence: We got through the hard times. She got through the exam. I couldn’t get through to him by phone. They got through safely.

english_meaning: To rise from bed or stand up, to organize or prepare something.
example_sentence: I get up at 7 every morning. Get up and help me. They got up a meeting. He got up early for work.

english_meaning: To become aware of something secret or private. To hear a rumor or gain indirect information about a situation. To discover a hidden plot or clandestine activity. To detect the beginning of a development before it is public.
example_sentence: The authorities managed to get wind of the protest before it even started. She didn't want the media to get wind of her secret wedding plans. We need to be careful so that the competitors don't get wind of our new product. Once the neighbors got wind of the scandal, the rumors spread quickly.

word: Get your mind out of the gutter
english_meaning: Stop thinking about something inappropriate or sexual. To tell someone to stop interpreting something in a crude, sexual, or inappropriate way. It suggests that the person’s thoughts are “low” or morally impure, and encourages a shift to more appropriate thinking.
synonyms: ["Stop overthinking sexually","Think properly","Keep it clean","Stop being perverse"]
example_sentence: "You think every joke is about sex? Get your mind out of the gutter!".  Stop imagining things that aren’t there, Get your mind out of the gutter.  He laughed at the comment, but I told him to get his mind out of the gutter. Just because she mentioned a beach scene, don’t get your mind out of the gutter.

english_meaning: Causing great horror or shock; terrible. Extremely unpleasant or of very poor quality. Very pale and ill in appearance. Frightful and deeply disturbing.
example_sentence: The accident was a ghastly sight that no one could forget. He looked ghastly after the long illness. The food at the hotel was absolutely ghastly. She described the ghastly details of the incident.

english_meaning: To suddenly stop all communication with someone especially in a relationship or friendship without any explanation. You ignore their calls, messages, or attempts to contact you.
example_sentence: He ghosted me after our second date, no calls, no messages. If you don’t want to continue, just say it, don’t ghost people. She felt hurt when her best friend ghosted her without any reason. Nowadays, many people ghost others instead of ending relationships properly.

english_meaning: A town that has been completely abandoned by its inhabitants. A once populated place now empty and silent. A location that feels deserted or lifeless. A place that used to be busy but is now nearly empty. Figuratively, any area that seems unusually quiet.
example_sentence: After the mines closed, the settlement became a ghost town. The streets were empty and the market looked like a ghost town. Once a busy port, the area is now a ghost town. During the lockdown, the entire city felt like a ghost town.

english_meaning: Resembling or characteristic of a ghost. Faint, shadowy, or eerie in appearance. Relating to spirits or the supernatural. Causing a feeling of fear because of its strange, unearthly quality.
example_sentence: A ghostly figure appeared at the end of the corridor. The fog gave the old house a ghostly appearance. We heard a ghostly sound coming from the attic. Moonlight cast a ghostly glow over the ruins.

english_meaning: An imaginary or mythical being of human form but superhuman size and strength. A very large person, animal, or thing. A person of extraordinary ability or importance. Something of great size or power.
example_sentence: The old fairy tale told the story of a young boy who outwitted the fierce giant. He was a giant in the world of literature, having written more than thirty celebrated novels. The tech giant released its most powerful smartphone model at a global event last week. The crane towered over the construction site like a giant made of steel. She felt like a giant among her classmates because she was almost two metres tall.

english_meaning: Speech or writing that has no meaning or is difficult to understand. Words that sound like nonsense. Unclear or foolish talk. Language that is confusing or unintelligible. Meaningless chatter without any logical sense.
example_sentence: The baby was speaking gibberish, but everyone enjoyed listening. His explanation sounded like complete gibberish to me. Stop talking gibberish and speak clearly. The old document was full of gibberish no one could read.

english_meaning: A sensation of spinning and losing one's balance or feeling light-headed. It often refers to physical dizziness or a state of flightiness and lack of seriousness. It can also describe a feeling of intense excitement or whirling confusion.
example_sentence: The height of the cliff caused a sudden wave of giddiness to wash over him. She felt a certain giddiness after hearing the wonderful news of her promotion. The spinning ride at the fair left the children in a state of laughter and giddiness. His chronic giddiness made it difficult for him to walk in a straight line.

english_meaning: Having a sensation of whirling and a tendency to fall. It also describes a person who is impulsive, light-hearted, or frivolous in behavior. Often used to describe feelings of extreme happiness that cause one to feel unsteady.
example_sentence: I felt giddy after spinning around in circles for several minutes. The young lovers were giddy with excitement on their wedding day. She is a giddy girl who rarely takes her academic responsibilities seriously. The fast-paced movie left him feeling slightly giddy and confused.

english_meaning: A unit prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one billion (109). Used to represent a quantity equivalent to one thousand million. Often applied in computing to signify 1,073,741,824 (230) bytes in binary contexts. Denotes a massive or immense scale in informal colloquial language. Used as a multiplier for scientific units such as watts, hertz, or meters. Represents a high level of magnitude or intensity in technological measurement.
example_sentence: The new hard drive has two terabytes of storage, which is two thousand gigabytes. The processor speed is measured in gigahertz to indicate how many billion cycles per second it performs. In scientific terms, a gigawatt represents one billion watts of electrical power. She downloaded a giga amount of data over the weekend using the high-speed connection.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,024 megabytes, or about one billion bytes. A common measure for the capacity of memory cards, phones, and hard drives. A large unit used to describe file sizes such as videos and software.
example_sentence: My phone has sixty-four gigabytes of storage. One gigabyte equals 1,024 megabytes. The movie file is nearly two gigabytes. I bought a data package of ten gigabytes.

english_meaning: A unit of frequency equal to one billion hertz. A measure commonly used for processor clock speed, radio waves, and wireless frequency bands. One billion cycles per second.
example_sentence: The new processor runs at 3.5 gigahertz. Many wireless routers use the 2.4-gigahertz and 5-gigahertz bands. Engineers measured the signal frequency in gigahertz. The specification lists a clock speed of four gigahertz.

english_meaning: Of very great size or huge proportions. It characterizes something that is massive, colossal, or far exceeding the average size or power. Often used to describe physical objects, projects, or even abstract efforts.
example_sentence: The construction of the dam was a gigantic undertaking for the small engineering firm. A gigantic statue of the founder stood at the center of the city square. The dinosaur skeleton displayed at the museum was truly gigantic. They were faced with a gigantic challenge that required international cooperation.

english_meaning: A medical condition causing abnormally excessive growth, usually because too much growth hormone is produced before the growth plates close. Abnormal enlargement of the whole body or one of its parts. The state or quality of being gigantic.
example_sentence: The doctor diagnosed the boy with gigantism after noticing his rapid growth. Gigantism is often caused by a tumor on the pituitary gland. The specialist explained how gigantism differs from acromegaly. Untreated gigantism can cause serious health complications.

english_meaning: To laugh in a silly way because you are embarrassed or nervous or you think that something is funny. A slight, silly, repeated laugh.
example_sentence: The girls giggled at the joke. They giggled nervously as they waited for their turn. She gave a nervous giggle. Matt collapsed into giggles and hung up the phone.

english_meaning: Inclined to giggle frequently. Laughing in a light, nervous, playful, or silly way. Easily amused or unable to suppress small laughs.
example_sentence: The giggly schoolchildren could not stop laughing during the lesson. She became giggly after hearing the private joke. His giggly mood made the meeting less formal. The children were giggly with excitement before the party.

english_meaning: A man paid to accompany or entertain a woman socially. A male escort or lover supported financially by a woman. A man who forms relationships primarily for money, gifts, or material support.
example_sentence: The wealthy widow hired a gigolo to accompany her to social events. The film portrayed the glamorous but lonely life of a gigolo. He was rumored to have worked as a gigolo in his youth. The word gigolo often carries a negative social judgment.

english_meaning: A leg of lamb or mutton prepared as food. A cut of meat from the hind leg of a sheep. A sleeve that is very full at the shoulder and narrow at the wrist, also called a leg-of-mutton sleeve.
example_sentence: The chef roasted a gigot of lamb for Sunday dinner. She ordered gigot at the French restaurant. The dress featured fashionable gigot sleeves. Traditional recipes pair slow-cooked gigot with garlic and rosemary.

english_meaning: A lively dance of the Baroque period derived from the jig. Music written for that dance, usually in a rapid compound meter. A movement commonly placed at the end of a Baroque suite.
example_sentence: Bach composed a lively gigue to close the suite. The orchestra performed a spirited gigue at the concert. The dancers moved quickly to the rhythm of the gigue. A gigue often forms the final movement of a Baroque suite.

english_meaning: The respiratory organs of fish and other aquatic animals, used to extract oxygen from water. The thin, blade-like structures on the underside of a mushroom cap. An informal unit of measurement equal to a quarter of a pint. The flesh below the jaws and ears of a person, especially when considered in the context of looking pale or unwell.
example_sentence: Fish breathe by drawing water over their gills to extract dissolved oxygen. The fresh fish at the market had bright red gills, a sign that it had been caught that morning. The gills of the mushroom can help identify the species when foraging in the wild. The seasoned cook checked the gills of the fish to confirm how fresh it was. He looked pale about the gills after hearing the unexpected and shocking news.

english_meaning: A trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or business. Something designed to impress or lure customers that lacks real value. A deceptive or publicity-seeking feature.
example_sentence: The free toy in the cereal box was just a marketing gimmick. He relies on cheap publicity gimmicks to stay in the news. The new smartphone feature turned out to be a useless gimmick. The restaurant used live music as a gimmick to attract more customers.

english_meaning: A hot, fragrant spice made from the rhizome of a plant, which may be chopped or powdered for cooking. A light reddish-yellow or orange-brown colour. A highly aromatic tropical plant with thick fleshy roots.
example_sentence: She added some freshly grated ginger to the stir-fry. His sister has bright ginger hair and freckles. We drank hot ginger tea to soothe our sore throats. The recipe calls for a pinch of ground ginger.

english_meaning: Having a reddish-orange or sandy color like ginger. Having hair of a ginger or orange-red color. Tasting or smelling of ginger. Somewhat spicy or pungent in flavor.
example_sentence: The cat had soft gingery fur. Her gingery hair glowed in the afternoon sun. The tea had a warm gingery flavor. He stroked his gingery beard thoughtfully.

english_meaning: A belt or cord worn around the waist. A corset or elastic undergarment worn to shape the waist and hips. Something that encircles or surrounds something else. To encircle or surround something completely.
example_sentence: She wore a wide leather girdle over her dress to complete the medieval costume. The mountains form a natural girdle around the valley and protect it from strong winds. The ancient warriors fastened a metal girdle around their waists before going into battle. Trees were used to girdle the settlement and provide a natural boundary. The explorer described how the river seemed to girdle the entire island.

english_meaning: The substance or general meaning of a speech or text. It refers to the core essence or the main point of a matter without including the specific details. It is the central part or the heart of an argument.
example_sentence: I didn't hear every word, but I got the gist of his long explanation. The lawyer summarized the gist of the witness's testimony for the jury. Could you just give me the gist of the story instead of telling the whole thing? The gist of her argument was that we need more funding for schools.

english_meaning: To care about something or someone. To feel concern or interest in a matter. To consider something important enough to worry about. Used mostly in the negative to show complete indifference.
example_sentence: He doesn't give a damn about what people say. Nobody seemed to give a damn about the broken street lights. If you gave a damn, you would have called earlier. She stopped giving a damn about their opinions long ago.

word: Give him an inch and he will take a mile
english_meaning: Misusing kindness. Taking unfair advantage. Becoming greedy after receiving help. Asking for more than offered. Crossing limits after getting permission
synonyms: ["Give someone a finger and they will take the whole hand","Abuse someone’s kindness","Take advantage of generosity","Push the limits","Demand too much"]
antonyms: ["Respect boundaries","Be satisfied with little","Appreciate kindness","Know one’s limits","Show gratitude"]
example_sentence: I allowed Ahmed to borrow my bike for one day, but he kept it for a whole week, Give him an inch and he will take a mile. The manager permitted the workers to leave early once, and now they expect it every Friday, Give him an inch and he will take a mile. Sara asked to use my laptop for homework, then she started using it for games all night, Give him an inch and he will take a mile. If you let the children stay awake a little longer, they will demand extra screen time too, Give him an inch and he will take a mile.

english_meaning: To behave in a boastful, arrogant, or aggressive manner. To talk confidently or loudly in order to impress or intimidate others.
example_sentence: He started to give it large after winning the local match. Don't give it large just because you bought a new car. He was giving it large at the pub last night. She was giving it large about her recent promotion.

english_meaning: To put 100% effort, energy, and dedication into doing something without holding back. Try with full strength and dedication. Work as hard as you can without stopping. Fully commit your effort to something.
synonyms: ["Give your best","Do your best","Put in full effort","Go all out","Put your heart into it","Leave no stone unturned"]
example_sentence: You have trained hard for this match, now give it your all. She told her team to give it their all during the final presentation. Even if the task is difficult, you should give it your all and not quit. He gave it his all in the exam and felt satisfied with his effort.

english_meaning: An informal invitation to slap palms together as a greeting or in celebration. A friendly gesture of agreement, congratulation, or shared success. A casual way of saying well done.
example_sentence: Give me five! That was a brilliant shot. The coach smiled and said, 'Give me five, champion'. After finishing the project, they gave each other five. Give me five, buddy, we did it together.

english_meaning: To offer time, energy, or care selflessly to help others.
example_sentence: Teachers give of themselves to students. She always gives of herself to support her friends in difficult times. Teachers give of themselves every day to help their students succeed. Volunteers who give of themselves make the world a better place. He gave of himself completely to the service of humanity.

english_meaning: To allow space, ventilation, or a short break. To let fresh air into a room or space. To allow someone or something to have freedom or relief from pressure. To give a chance to relax or breathe. Can be used figuratively for letting feelings, ideas, or opinions be expressed.
example_sentence: Open the window to give some air to the room. After hours of work, I decided to step outside and give some air to my mind. The coach gave some air to the players by letting them rest for ten minutes. She needed to give some air to her thoughts before replying.

english_meaning: To help or assist someone with a task. To offer physical or practical help. To applaud or clap for someone as a sign of appreciation. To provide support in an activity or job.
example_sentence: Could you give me a hand with these bags? Let's give the performers a big hand for their wonderful show. He kindly gave her a hand moving the furniture. Please give me a hand setting up the chairs.

english_meaning: To give someone a lot of freedom or trust to act independently, even if they may make mistakes. To trust someone with responsibility. To allow freedom of action. To avoid strict control. To let someone prove themselves. To give enough space for decision-making. To permit someone to continue until consequences appear.
synonyms: ["Give freedom","Trust someone","Allow independence","Give free rein","Let someone act freely","Give autonomy"]
example_sentence: The manager gave Ali a long rope to handle the project on his own. Parents should not always give children a long rope without guidance. The teacher gave the students a long rope during the research activity. The company gave its employees a long rope to develop creative ideas.

word: Give someone a run for their money
english_meaning: To compete strongly with someone, making it difficult for them to win or succeed. It implies giving tough competition even if you do not win. This idiom is used when a person or thing performs so well in a competition or comparison that the other side has to work hard to win. It suggests a close contest where the outcome is not easy or guaranteed.
synonyms: ["Compete closely","Challenge strongly","Give tough competition","Rival seriously","Push someone hard"]
antonyms: ["Lose easily","Offer no competition","Be outclassed","Be inferior","Surrender without effort"]
example_sentence: The new team gave the champions a run for their money in the final match. Her presentation gave the senior manager a run for their money. This budget phone gives expensive models a run for their money. The young player is giving experienced athletes a run for their money this season.

english_meaning: To scold someone angrily and at length. To tell someone strongly how annoyed or displeased you are. To complain loudly to someone about something.
example_sentence: My mother gave me an earful for coming home so late. The customer gave the manager an earful about the poor service. If he misses another meeting, the boss will give him an earful. She gave her brother an earful for borrowing her car without asking.

english_meaning: To allow someone complete freedom to act as they wish. To let a person make their own decisions without restriction. To give full authority or control to someone. To permit someone unrestricted action. To trust someone with independent decisions.
example_sentence: The director gave the artist free rein over the design. Parents should not give children free rein all the time. She was given free rein to manage the project. The coach gave free rein to the players during practice.

english_meaning: To force someone to leave a place quickly and roughly. To dismiss or get rid of a person abruptly. To hurry someone through something without proper attention. To eject a person unceremoniously.
example_sentence: The guards gave the troublemaker the bum's rush. He was given the bum's rush after the argument. Don't give the customers the bum's rush; listen to them. She felt she had been given the bum's rush by the committee.

english_meaning: To successfully escape from someone who is following or chasing you. It means to evade capture or detection by sneaking away. This phrase describes the act of losing a pursuer through cleverness or speed. It signifies avoiding an unwanted encounter by slipping away unnoticed.
example_sentence: The suspect managed to give the police the slip by ducking into a crowded subway station. I saw my annoying neighbor at the store, but I was able to give him the slip. They tried to follow our car, but we took a sharp turn to give them the slip. He gave the reporters the slip by leaving through the hotel's back entrance.

english_meaning: To deliberately ignore someone or treat them in an unfriendly way. To show a lack of interest or affection. To reject socially.
example_sentence: After he was promoted, some of his colleagues gave him the cold shoulder. She gave me the cold shoulder when I tried to talk to her about the mistake. Instead of helping, they gave him the cold shoulder during his tough time.

english_meaning: A rare or nonstandard form usually intended to mean give ground. To retreat or yield a position, territory, advantage, or point in an argument. To concede under pressure. Literally, to provide land or a surface for a purpose
example_sentence: The troops refused to give ground despite the heavy attack. In the debate, she would not give ground on her main argument. The company gave ground to its competitor after months of pressure. The council agreed to give the ground for a new community garden.

english_meaning: To stop trying or quit doing something. To surrender or stop a habit.
example_sentence: Don’t give up so easily. She gave up smoking. They gave up hope. He gave up his job.

english_meaning: To die. To stop functioning or working, especially of a machine. To give up trying and abandon an effort or hope.
example_sentence: The old man finally gave up the ghost after a long illness. My laptop gave up the ghost in the middle of the presentation. After three failed attempts, the team gave up the ghost. Their ancient car gave up the ghost on the motorway.

english_meaning: To donate or hand something for free, to reveal a secret unintentionally.
example_sentence: She gave away her old clothes. He gave away the ending of the movie. The company gave away free samples. His face gave away his emotions.

english_meaning: To return something to its owner or restore a previous state.
example_sentence: Please give back my book. He gave back the borrowed money. The government gave back the land. She gave back the pen.

english_meaning: To produce, emit, or issue something like sound, light, or information.
example_sentence: The flowers gave forth a sweet scent. The machine gave forth a loud noise. The book gives forth wisdom. The factory gave forth smoke.

english_meaning: To surrender or yield to pressure or temptation. To stop resisting, to yield or agree after initial refusal. To submit.
example_sentence: He finally gave in to her request. Don’t give in to fear. The rebels gave in after negotiation. She gave in after arguing for hours.

english_meaning: To produce, release or emit something such as a smell, light, heat, or gas.
example_sentence: The flowers give off a pleasant aroma. The engine gave off smoke. The fire gave off warmth. The candle gave off light.

english_meaning: To distribute or hand out. To stop working or functioning.
example_sentence: The teacher gave out the papers. The engine gave out after 10 years. They gave out free tickets. My energy gave out.

english_meaning: To stop doing something annoying or unpleasant. To hand something to someone or devote something to a purpose.
example_sentence: Give over complaining!. He gave over the keys to the new owner. The land was given over to farming. She gave over the management to her assistant.

english_meaning: The smooth area of the forehead located between the eyebrows and above the nose. The flat surface of bone between the brow ridges. An anatomical landmark used in medical and biological studies.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the patient's glabella carefully. The glabella is often used as a reference point in facial measurements. Wrinkles between the eyebrows appear on the glabella. Anthropologists study the shape of the glabella to identify skulls.

english_meaning: Extremely cold, like ice. Relating to ice, glaciers, or the ice age. Very slow, like the movement of a glacier. Cold and unfriendly in manner or attitude.
example_sentence: A glacial wind blew across the open fields. Progress on the reforms has been glacial. She gave him a glacial stare and walked away. The valley was carved by glacial activity.

english_meaning: A large, slow-moving mass of ice formed from compacted snow over many years, found in mountainous regions or polar areas. A persistent body of dense ice that constantly moves under its own weight. A large body of ice that has formed over long periods and advances or retreats with climatic conditions.
example_sentence: The glacier has retreated significantly over the past century due to rising global temperatures. Scientists drilled deep into the glacier to extract ice cores for climate research. The hike to the base of the glacier took nearly five hours through rough mountain terrain. Meltwater from the glacier feeds the rivers that supply drinking water to millions of people below.

english_meaning: An attractive or exciting quality that makes someone or something seem special or desirable. Charm created by beauty, luxury, fame, fashion, or mystery. A deceptively appealing appearance that can hide ordinary or unpleasant reality. To make something appear more attractive or romantic than it really is. An archaic enchantment or magic spell.
example_sentence: The glamor of the film industry attracts many young performers. Travel magazines often add glamor to ordinary destinations. The old theater retains the glamor of a bygone age. Advertisers glamor the product with elegant photography.

english_meaning: To make a person, activity, or situation seem more attractive, exciting, or desirable than it truly is. To present something in an idealized, romantic, or luxurious way. To conceal risks, hardships, or unpleasant facts by emphasizing appealing features.
example_sentence: Films should not glamorize violence. The campaign glamorized life in the armed forces. Social media can glamorize unrealistic lifestyles. The novel does not glamorize poverty or hardship.

english_meaning: Possessing exciting beauty, charm, elegance, or attractiveness. Associated with luxury, fame, fashion, or a desirable lifestyle. Appearing more appealing or romantic than everyday reality. Full of sophistication, spectacle, or prestige.
example_sentence: She wore a glamorous silver dress to the ceremony. The job sounds glamorous, but it involves long hours. They spent a glamorous weekend at a seaside resort. Old photographs show the glamorous side of city life.

english_meaning: In an attractive, elegant, exciting, or sophisticated manner. In a way associated with luxury, fame, fashion, or prestige. In a manner that makes something seem more appealing or romantic than it really is.
example_sentence: She dressed glamorously for the evening reception. The hotel was glamorously decorated for the awards night. The magazine portrayed city life glamorously. He arrived glamorously in a classic car.

english_meaning: An attractive quality associated with beauty, excitement, wealth, or success. A charming and often idealized appeal that makes a person, place, or activity seem special. Stylish beauty and sophistication. Historically, a magical enchantment or spell.
example_sentence: The old cinema still retains a sense of glamour. Travel magazines often emphasize the glamour of distant cities. She brought elegance and glamour to the event. The job involves hard work despite its public glamour.

english_meaning: To take a quick or brief look at something or someone. A rapid, short look. To read or examine something hurriedly. To strike something lightly and bounce off at an angle. A brief direct look that lasts only a moment.
example_sentence: She glanced at her watch and realised she was late. He glanced over the newspaper headlines during breakfast. The two friends exchanged a quick glance and smiled. The ball glanced off the bat and went past the wicketkeeper. A single glance at the painting was enough to impress the visitors.

english_meaning: The rounded head at the tip of the penis. The sensitive end of the penis covered by the foreskin in uncircumcised males. The part of the penis containing the opening of the urethra. A highly sensitive structure rich in nerve endings.
example_sentence: The glans penis is the most sensitive part of the organ. The foreskin normally covers the glans penis. Inflammation of the glans penis is called balanitis. The urethral opening lies at the tip of the glans penis.

english_meaning: A pair of lenses set in a frame that rests on the nose and ears, worn to correct or improve eyesight or to protect the eyes from sunlight, dust, or glare. Also refers to multiple drinking vessels made of glass used for holding liquids. Spectacles worn for vision correction, reading, or as a fashion accessory. Eyewear designed for various purposes such as sun protection, safety, or style.
example_sentence: She wore glasses to read the small print on the bottle. He cleaned his glasses with a soft cloth before the meeting. The waiter brought two glasses of cold water to the table. My grandfather has been wearing glasses since he was forty. She bought a new pair of glasses with a stylish frame.

english_meaning: To extract information from various sources or to collect bit by bit. It originally referred to gathering leftover grain after a harvest. It implies a slow and painstaking process of assembly or learning.
example_sentence: We managed to glean several useful facts from the old historical documents. The researchers had to glean data from dozens of different scientific journals. After the party, the poor were allowed to glean the leftovers from the field. She tried to glean some clues about the surprise from her brother's conversation.

english_meaning: A feeling of great delight, joy, happiness, or triumphant satisfaction, especially because of one's own success or another's misfortune. An intense emotion of pleasure and excitement that is often expressed openly. A lively, jubilant mood that overflows into laughter, smiles, or cheerful behavior. A sense of merriment and high spirits.
example_sentence: The children jumped with glee when they saw the new toys. She laughed with glee as she opened her birthday presents. His eyes sparkled with glee at the surprise announcement. The crowd cheered with glee when their team scored the winning goal. He could not hide his glee at being promoted.

english_meaning: It refers to speaking or being spoken in a fluent and confident way, but often without careful thought or genuine honesty. It also describes a response or attitude that shows little preparation or thought, resulting in a superficial or insincere impression.
example_sentence: The politician gave a glib answer that completely ignored the complexity of the issue. He was a glib salesman who could talk anyone into buying his products. She was careful not to make glib remarks during such a serious discussion. His glib apologies were no longer enough to repair the damaged relationship.

english_meaning: A person who speaks fluently and smoothly but often lacks sincerity or depth. Someone who uses persuasive and plausible words to deceive or manipulate others easily. An individual skilled in superficial conversation who can talk their way out of difficult situations effortlessly.
antonyms: ["Blunt speaker","Straight shooter","Plain-spoken person","Hesitant speaker","Inarticulate speaker","Honest person","Sincere talker"]
example_sentence: The salesman was a glib talker who managed to sell useless products to unsuspecting customers. Do not be fooled by that glib talker because his promises rarely have any substance behind them. As a glib talker, he effortlessly charmed his way through the job interview without answering the tough questions directly. Her reputation as a glib talker made people hesitant to trust her business proposals completely.

english_meaning: A brief or quick look, sight, or view of someone or something. A momentary or partial impression that does not provide complete understanding. A short experience or insight into something. To see or perceive something only for a very short time and not completely.
example_sentence: I caught a glimpse of the actor as he walked into the hotel. She got only a brief glimpse of the mountains through the clouds. The documentary offers a glimpse into the lives of refugees. He glimpsed his old friend in the crowded market. We had a glimpse of the sunrise before the fog returned.

english_meaning: A small, brief flash of light, especially one reflected from a shiny surface. A faint or fleeting expression in someone's eyes that suggests a particular emotion. To give out or reflect small flashes of light. A quick gleam or sparkle that catches the eye.
example_sentence: The glint of the sun on the water made it hard to see. There was a mischievous glint in her eyes when she smiled. He saw the glint of a knife in the dark alley. The diamonds glinted under the bright stage lights. A glint of hope appeared on his tired face.

english_meaning: To shine with a sparkling, soft, or wet light, especially because of being covered with a liquid or smooth surface. To reflect light in a wet or oily way. To appear shiny and bright due to moisture. To gleam softly and attractively.
example_sentence: The dew glistened on the grass in the early morning. Tears glistened in her eyes as she said goodbye. His forehead glistened with sweat after the long run. The wet streets glistened under the streetlights. The fish glistened in the sunlight as the fisherman pulled it from the water.

english_meaning: A sudden, usually temporary malfunction or fault in equipment, a system, or a plan. A minor problem that interrupts the normal working of something. An unexpected technical defect, especially in software or electronic devices. A brief irregularity that causes something to stop functioning correctly.
example_sentence: A small software glitch delayed the launch of the website. There was a glitch in the system that caused all the data to disappear. The concert started late due to a technical glitch in the sound system. We faced a minor glitch during the live broadcast. The game has several glitches that need to be fixed.

english_meaning: The time of day just after the sun has set and before it becomes fully dark. Twilight or dusk, especially when it has a soft, dim, and romantic quality. The dim light of evening before nightfall. A poetic word for the period of fading light at the end of the day.
example_sentence: They walked along the river in the gloaming. The village looked peaceful in the gloaming. Birds returned to their nests in the gloaming. We sat on the porch and watched the gloaming settle over the fields. In the gloaming, the mountains turned a deep shade of purple.

english_meaning: To express or feel great pleasure or self-satisfaction over one's own success or another person's failure or misfortune, often in an annoying or unkind way. To take pleasure in something selfishly or maliciously. To dwell on one's own achievement in a smug manner.
example_sentence: He gloated over his rival's defeat in the elections. She could not help gloating when she got the promotion instead of her colleague. Do not gloat about your success in front of those who failed. The winning team gloated over their easy victory. It is unkind to gloat over someone's misfortune.

english_meaning: Relating to the whole world rather than to one country or region. Worldwide in scope, effect, or importance. Covering or considering all parts of a group, system, or situation as a whole. In computing, applying to an entire program, file, or system rather than a limited part.
example_sentence: Climate change is a global problem that needs urgent action. The company has a global network of offices in forty countries. Their music has earned them a global audience. The manager took a global view of the department's performance.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to or covers the whole world. Throughout the world; on a worldwide scale. Considering something as a complete whole rather than in separate parts.
example_sentence: The film was released globally on the same day. Prices for wheat have risen globally this year. The brand is globally recognised for its quality. We need to think globally but act locally.

english_meaning: A spherical or rounded object such as a ball. A three-dimensional scale model of the Earth or another celestial body. The planet Earth itself when considered as a whole. A glass covering for a lamp or light bulb. Any object having the shape of a sphere.
example_sentence: The teacher used a globe to show the students the location of the equator. Many explorers dreamed of traveling around the entire globe. She carefully cleaned the glass globe of the antique lamp. New satellite images offer a stunning view of our blue globe from space.

english_meaning: A state of partial or total darkness, especially when it creates a sad or depressing atmosphere. A feeling of deep sadness, hopelessness, or despondency. A dull and dim light that suggests sorrow. An atmosphere of melancholy and depression.
example_sentence: The news of the accident spread gloom across the whole town. He sat alone in the gloom of the empty room. A deep gloom settled over the family after the loss. The cloudy weather added to the gloom of the day. She tried to cheer him up and lift his gloom.

english_meaning: Dark, dim, or poorly lit in a way that creates a sad atmosphere. Causing or expressing feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or depression. Feeling sad, low-spirited, or without hope. Pessimistic about future events or outcomes.
example_sentence: It was a cold and gloomy winter morning. He looked gloomy after hearing the bad news. The room was gloomy because the curtains were closed. The economic forecast for next year is rather gloomy. She has been feeling gloomy since her best friend moved away.

english_meaning: Having or deserving great fame, honor, or admiration. Marked by great beauty, splendor, or magnificence. Extremely pleasant or enjoyable in a wonderful way. Bringing pride, distinction, or great achievement.
example_sentence: The army won a glorious victory in the battle. We had a glorious time on our holiday by the sea. The sunset over the mountains was absolutely glorious. She has had a glorious career in the field of medicine. It was a glorious day with clear blue skies.

english_meaning: Great honour, fame, or praise won by notable achievement. Magnificence and great beauty. Worship, adoration, and praise offered to God. A source of pride or distinction. To take great pride or delight in something.
example_sentence: The team returned home covered in glory. We watched the sunset in all its glory. The hymn gives glory to God. He gloried in his son's success.

english_meaning: A smooth and shiny appearance on a surface. A brief explanation of a difficult word or passage. An attractive appearance that hides the truth. To give a surface a smooth and shiny finish.
example_sentence: The new paint gave the furniture a high gloss finish. She tried to gloss over her mistake in the report. The glossy magazine covered glamour but glossed over real issues. The politician glossed over the corruption scandal in his speech.

english_meaning: To mention something briefly while avoiding important or unpleasant details. To conceal, minimize, or make a problem seem less serious. To pass over a fault or difficulty without proper discussion. To give a smooth but incomplete account of something.
example_sentence: The report glossed over the causes of the accident. Do not gloss over the risks when speaking to investors. He apologized but glossed over his own responsibility. The textbook glosses over several important historical disputes.

english_meaning: A list of specialized, technical, or uncommon words with their meanings. An alphabetical collection of terms used in a particular subject, book, or field. A short dictionary placed at the end of a book or document. An explanatory vocabulary that helps readers understand difficult expressions. A reference section that may include definitions, translations, pronunciations, or usage notes.
example_sentence: The biology textbook includes a useful glossary of scientific terms. I checked the glossary to understand the unfamiliar legal phrase. Please add the new technical terms to the project glossary. A clear glossary makes this manual easier for beginners to read.

english_meaning: Fear of speaking in public. Intense fear or anxiety that a person feels when they have to speak in front of an audience, ranging from mild nervousness to severe panic. It can affect confidence, voice, and body language during presentations.
antonyms: ["Eloquence","Confidence in public speaking","Comfort with speaking","Oratory skill"]
example_sentence: She suffers from glossophobia, so she avoids giving presentations. Glossophobia can make even a short speech feel overwhelming. He took a public speaking course to overcome his glossophobia. Despite his knowledge, glossophobia stopped him from addressing the crowd.

english_meaning: Having a smooth, shiny, and lustrous surface that reflects light. Characterized by a polished or sleek appearance often associated with luxury. Relating to a type of paper or photograph finished with a high-sheen coating. Appearing superficially attractive or stylish but perhaps lacking depth or substance. Printed on expensive, high-quality paper, typically referring to a magazine.
example_sentence: The high-end car featured a glossy black finish that shimmered in the sun. She preferred to have her wedding photos printed on glossy paper rather than matte. The fashion industry is often criticized for its glossy and unrealistic portrayal of life. He handed me a glossy brochure detailing the amenities of the new luxury resort.

english_meaning: A covering for the hand with separate parts for each finger and the thumb. A protective hand covering used in work, sport, or medical care. A padded leather covering used in boxing or baseball. To provide or cover the hands with gloves.
example_sentence: The surgeon put on a pair of sterile gloves. She wore woollen gloves to protect her hands from the cold. The boxer tightened his gloves before the match. Always wear gloves when handling chemicals.

english_meaning: To have an angry, gloomy, or sullen look on one's face. To look or stare at someone with sudden annoyance, anger, or hostility. It refers to an intense and threatening stare directed at someone or something. It can also be used as a noun to describe the angry look itself.
example_sentence: The angry teacher glowered at the disruptive students. He just glowered at me without saying a single word. She stood there, glowering at him with intense frustration. The old man sat on his porch, glowering at the passing cars.

english_meaning: Sad and silent. Looking unhappy or gloomy. In a low mood. Disappointed and quiet. Feeling and showing a moody dejection. Used to describe a person who looks dejected, sullen, or downcast, often without speaking much, usually because of disappointment or worry. It can also describe an atmosphere or expression that feels heavy and joyless.
example_sentence: She looked glum after hearing the bad news. He sat in the corner with a glum expression on his face. The team was glum after losing the final match. There was a glum silence in the room. Don't look so glum; everything will be fine.

english_meaning: Either of two empty bracts at the base of the spikelet in grasses. Small dry membranous bract found in inflorescences of Gramineae and Cyperaceae.
example_sentence: The scientist examined the glume under a microscope. Each grain of wheat is surrounded by two glumes. The glumes protect the delicate parts of the flower from damage. The outer glume was slightly longer than the inner one.

english_meaning: The largest and most superficial muscle of the buttock. The powerful muscle that straightens the hip and pushes the body forward. A muscle used strongly in climbing stairs, running, and rising from a seated position. The muscle that gives the buttock its rounded shape.
example_sentence: Squats are one of the best exercises for the gluteus maximus. The gluteus maximus straightens the hip when you stand up. Sitting all day can weaken the gluteus maximus. Sprinters rely heavily on a strong gluteus maximus.

english_meaning: A person who eats or consumes too much. Someone who has an excessive desire for food or drink, often without regard to moderation. It can also be used figuratively for someone with an excessive desire for something, such as work or wealth.
example_sentence: He is a glutton for chocolate and can eat an entire box in one sitting. She became a glutton for work, staying late at the office every night. The young boy was a glutton and never left food on his plate. Some people are gluttons for punishment, always seeking difficult challenges.

english_meaning: Having an excessively greedy approach to eating or consuming. Eating far more than necessary; marked by greed or excess in consumption.
example_sentence: He was so gluttonous he ordered three full meals for himself. The gluttonous king held banquets every night. Her gluttonous habits led to serious health problems. The gluttonous child ate all the candy meant for the whole class.

english_meaning: To bite or chew on something persistently, usually with small, sharp movements. It can also describe a feeling, worry, or pain that continues to trouble someone over time.
example_sentence: The mouse began to gnaw on the wooden box. Hunger gnawed at him all night. The dog gnawed the bone happily. Guilt continued to gnaw at her conscience.

english_meaning: Related to special spiritual knowledge or insight. Relating to mystical or spiritual knowledge. Possessing deep inner understanding. Connected with ancient religious philosophy. Having or relating to deep, often secret spiritual knowledge, especially knowledge about divine matters. It is commonly linked with early religious ideas that emphasized personal insight over formal teachings.
example_sentence: He had a gnostic understanding of life that went beyond ordinary beliefs. The ancient gnostic texts reveal hidden spiritual teachings. She followed a gnostic path to seek truth within herself. His ideas were influenced by gnostic philosophy.

english_meaning: Try your best / give everything / use full effort. To put in maximum effort, energy, or resources to do something. It means to do something with full strength, enthusiasm, or commitment without holding back.
synonyms: ["Give it your all","Put in maximum effort","Go full force","Try your hardest","Spare no effort","Give 100 percent"]
example_sentence: She went all out to win the competition and practiced every day. The team went all out in the final match and scored three goals. They went all out to make the wedding event perfect. He went all out on his presentation to impress the clients.

english_meaning: To accompany someone or to agree or cooperate with an idea or plan.
example_sentence: I’ll go along with your plan. Things are going along smoothly. She decided to go along despite her doubts. Just go along and see what happens.

english_meaning: To break a promise, not keep one’s word, or take back what one has said earlier; to change one’s decision or statement.
antonyms: ["Keep promise","Stand by one’s word","Fulfill one’s commitment"]
example_sentence: He promised to support me, but later went back upon his words. A gentleman never goes back upon his words. The company went back upon its words and canceled the agreement. She lost trust because he went back upon his words too many times.

english_meaning: To suddenly become extremely angry or lose control of emotions. An informal idiom used when someone reacts with intense anger, outrage, or emotional explosion. It often describes overreaction to a situation.
synonyms: ["Lose temper","Freak out","Blow up","Fly into a rage","Go crazy"]
example_sentence: He went ballistic when he saw the broken phone. My boss will go ballistic if the report is late again. She went ballistic over a small misunderstanding. The coach went ballistic after the team lost the match.

english_meaning: To become very excited, enthusiastic, or overjoyed. To act in a crazy, silly, or irrational way.
example_sentence: The children went bananas when they saw the magician at the party. He’ll go bananas if he finds out that you broke his phone. The fans went bananas when their team scored the winning goal. She went bananas after hearing the surprising news.
