english_meaning: To be ignored, discarded, or fail to be considered. Abandoned, forgotten, or allowed to fail. It often refers to plans, rules, or ideas that are no longer followed or respected.
example_sentence: All her efforts to be polite went by the board and she started to shout. Does this mean our holiday plans will have to go by the board? It seems that loyalty has gone by the board. Their principles have gone by the board. All his promises went by the board once he got the power. Due to lack of funds, the project went by the board.

english_meaning: To strictly follow established rules and official procedures without deviation. To behave in exactly the way that is expected and required by authority. To execute a task rigidly adhering to the standard guidelines. To refuse to take shortcuts or make exceptions in a structured environment.
synonyms: ["Follow The Rules","Play By The Rules","Toe The Line","Stick To The Rules","Act According To Regulations","Follow Protocol","Adhere To Procedures","Observe The Law","Keep To The Guidelines","Abide By The Book"]
antonyms: ["Break The Rules","Bend The Rules","Cut Corners","Go Rogue","Improvise","Take Shortcuts","Think Outside The Box","Disobey Orders","Flout The Law","Rebel Against The System","Deviate From The Norm"]
example_sentence: The manager expects everyone to go by the book when dealing with customer complaints. The police officer decided to go by the book and issue a fine instead of a warning. You cannot expect to innovate if you always go by the book in every project. During the safety inspection, they had to go by the book to avoid any legal liabilities.

english_meaning: To fail suddenly and dramatically. To end in a spectacular disaster. To be defeated completely and publicly. To collapse in a very visible way. To ruin one's plans or reputation in a dramatic manner.
example_sentence: His political career went down in flames after the scandal. The startup went down in flames within a year. Their plans went down in flames due to poor planning. He fought bravely but went down in flames.

english_meaning: To share the cost of a meal or activity equally among all participants. Each person paying for their own expenses.
synonyms: ["Share The Bill","Split The Check","Pay Your Own Way","Halve The Cost","Divide The Expenses","Chip In Equally","Pool Resources","Share Expenses","Share And Share Alike"]
antonyms: ["Pay For Everyone","Foot The Bill","Treat Someone","Sponsor","Pick Up The Check","Subsidize","Cover The Cost","Bear The Expense","Invite And Pay"]
example_sentence: When we go out for dinner, we usually prefer to go dutch. I don't want you to pay for my ticket, so let's go dutch. Going dutch is a common practice among college students to save money. They decided to go dutch on the road trip expenses so no one felt burdened.

english_meaning: To move close to somebody so that you can talk about something without other people hearing. To gather closely together in a small group (often to talk privately, plan, or discuss something). In sports (especially football), when players form a circle to quickly plan strategy.
example_sentence: The managers went into a huddle before making the final decision. The players went into a huddle to plan their next move.

english_meaning: To become very angry. To become crazy or lose self control. To become extremely excited or enthusiastic. To react wildly or emotionally.
example_sentence: The crowd went nuts when the band played their most famous song. She went nuts when she found out she had won the competition. He went nuts trying to fix the computer before the deadline. The children went nuts over the surprise announcement of a school trip.

english_meaning: To examine, review, or discuss something carefully.
example_sentence: Let’s go over the report before submitting it. The teacher went over the answers with the class. He went over his notes before the exam. I need to go over these figures again.

english_meaning: To do something excessively, too much, or in an extreme way. To become too excited, emotional, involved, or excessive in actions, spending, reactions, celebrations, punishment, or behavior. It is used when someone crosses normal limits.
example_sentence: He went overboard with the wedding decorations and spent too much money. Don’t go overboard while criticizing others. She went overboard preparing for the exam and barely slept for a week. The fans went overboard after their team won the match.

english_meaning: To decline or deteriorate rapidly in quality or value. To fail or stop working correctly. To decrease in quantity or performance level. To experience a turn for the worse in a situation.
example_sentence: The business deal started to go south after the main investor backed out. Our vacation plans began to go south when it started raining heavily. The stock market price will go south if the inflation rises. The software update made the whole computer system go south.

english_meaning: To make a special effort to achieve something or help someone. To do more than what is expected or required.
synonyms: ["Do more than required","Make an extra effort","Go above and beyond"]
example_sentence: She always goes the extra mile to make her students feel comfortable in class. The company went the extra mile to ensure customer satisfaction. If you want to succeed in life, you must go the extra mile. He went the extra mile to help his friend in need.

english_meaning: To move into a leading or prominent position. It means stepping ahead of others in importance, attention, or influence, especially in discussions, decisions or situations.
example_sentence: She went to fore in the campaign. Ideas went to fore during the meeting. The topic went to fore in discussion. His achievements went to fore in the report.

english_meaning: To hide or become inaccessible in order to avoid capture, attention, or trouble. To go into hiding or lie low. Of a hunted animal, especially a fox, to enter its burrow. To withdraw temporarily from public view or communication
example_sentence: After the scandal broke, the politician went to ground for several weeks. The fugitive went to ground in the mountains to avoid the police. The fox went to ground in its den when the hounds approached. Facing intense media scrutiny, the celebrity decided to go to ground.

english_meaning: To decline or deteriorate in condition or quality. To become ruined or destroyed over time. To lose all former excellence or value. To fail completely due to neglect.
example_sentence: Since the new management took over, the company has completely gone to pot. If we don't maintain the garden, it will go to pot by the end of the summer. His health began to go to pot after he stopped exercising. The entire project went to pot when funding was abruptly cut.

english_meaning: To hide or keep out of sight, especially to avoid being found, caught, or noticed. (This idiom is used when a person or group disappears from public view, often to avoid attention, danger, arrest, or unwanted publicity. It can also mean operating secretly or privately rather than openly.)
example_sentence: The gang went underground after the police raid. During the war, many freedom fighters went underground to escape arrest. The activist went underground to continue her work secretly. The company went underground for a few months before relaunching its brand.

english_meaning: It means to be completely obvious or self-evident. It describes a fact or situation that is so clear it does not need to be mentioned. It implies that everyone already understands and agrees upon the point being made. It signifies an unquestionable or inherently understood truth.
synonyms: ["Be Obvious","Be Self-evident","Be Clear","Be Understood","Be Unquestionable","Be Unmistakable","Need No Explanation","Be Undeniable","Be Manifest","Be Apparent"]
antonyms: ["Be Unclear","Be Ambiguous","Need Explanation","Be Doubtful","Be Questionable","Require Clarification","Be Obscure","Be Hidden","Be Disputed"]
example_sentence: It should go without saying that you will be paid for the extra hours. It goes without saying that health is more important than wealth. Although it goes without saying, I want to thank you for all your hard work. It goes without saying that the company will cover your travel expenses.

english_meaning: An energetic, ambitious, and highly motivated person who is very determined to achieve success. Someone who takes initiative and pursues goals with enthusiasm and drive. A self-starter who does not wait to be asked before taking action.
example_sentence: From the first day on the job, it was clear she was a go-getter who would not wait for opportunities to come to her. The company was looking to hire a go-getter who could open up new markets quickly. He was a natural go-getter who had started his first business at the age of seventeen. His go-getter attitude made him one of the most productive members of the entire sales team. The go-getter in the group always had proposals ready before anyone else had finished thinking.

english_meaning: To provoke, urge, or stimulate someone to take action, often by causing annoyance, anger, or irritation. To drive or push someone toward doing something. A pointed stick used to make animals such as cattle move. Something that motivates or pressures a person into action.
example_sentence: His friends goaded him into accepting the dangerous challenge. She tried to goad her brother into an argument. The crowd goaded the boxer to keep fighting. Poverty was the goad that pushed him to work harder. Do not let his insults goad you into a fight.

english_meaning: To eat something very quickly and often in a careless or greedy way. It suggests haste, eagerness, or lack of attention while eating.
example_sentence: She gobbled down her breakfast. He gobbled down the sandwich. They gobbled down the meal before the meeting. I gobbled down a snack.

english_meaning: To eat something very quickly and often greedily. To consume or use something rapidly, often resources, money, or time.
example_sentence: The kids gobbled up the cookies. The project gobbled up all the funds. The machine gobbles up power. He gobbled up the news.

english_meaning: Language that is meaningless or is made unintelligible by excessive use of abstruse technical terms. Nonsense, gibberish, or wordy and confusing language. Official or professional jargon that is difficult for the public to understand. A sequence of words or symbols that do not make any sense. Pretentious or long-winded talk that obscures the actual meaning.
example_sentence: The legal document was written in such dense gobbledygook that I couldn't understand a single clause. Don't give me all that technical gobbledygook; just tell me why the computer isn't working. The politician's speech was full of empty gobbledygook intended to avoid answering the direct question. To a layperson, the complex mathematical formulas might look like total gobbledygook.

english_meaning: A small, mischievous, and often grotesque creature from folklore, typically depicted as malevolent or troublesome. A mythical being commonly portrayed in fairy tales and fantasy fiction as living underground or in hidden places. Used to describe a person, especially in a playful or insulting way, who behaves in a sly or troublesome manner. A creature often associated with trickery, greed, or minor mischief in stories and games.
example_sentence: In the story, a mischievous goblin guarded the entrance to the cave.  The video game featured armies of goblins attacking the player's castle.  Children love stories about goblins hiding treasure in dark forests.  The illustration depicted the goblin as small, green, and sharp-toothed.  Local folklore warned travelers about goblins lurking near the old bridge.

english_meaning: A foolish or annoying person who talks a lot of nonsense. A slang insult used for a person who speaks foolishly, makes silly comments, or talks without sense. It often refers to someone who is loud, annoying, or overconfident while saying things that are untrue or stupid.
example_sentence: Stop talking like a gobshite and think before you speak. He sounded like a complete gobshite during the meeting. She ignored him because he was acting like a gobshite online. Only a gobshite would believe such a silly rumor.

english_meaning: To shock or greatly surprise someone. To surprise someone so much that they are left speechless or stunned. It is often used in informal British English when something is extremely unexpected or shocking.
example_sentence: I was gobsmacked when I saw my exam result. She was gobsmacked by the sudden promotion. The price of the car completely gobsmacked him. We were gobsmacked by the magician’s final trick.

english_meaning: Extremely surprising or shocking in a way that leaves someone speechless. Something so astonishing, impressive, or unbelievable that a person is left unable to speak for a moment. It is often used for events, news, achievements, or visuals that create strong surprise or shock.
example_sentence: The view from the mountain was absolutely gobsmacking. Her performance in the final was gobsmacking. The price of the painting was gobsmacking for everyone. He gave a gobsmacking answer that no one expected.

word: God helps those who help themselves
english_meaning: People who work hard, take initiative, and try to solve their own problems are more likely to receive success, support, and opportunities. Hard work brings success. Self effort leads to achievement. Initiative attracts support. One must act before expecting help. Determination opens doors.
synonyms: ["Fortune favors the brave","Hard work pays off","Where there is a will","There is a way","Heaven helps the diligent","Self help is the best help"]
antonyms: ["Laziness leads to failure","Waiting for others solves nothing","Idleness brings poverty","Dependence weakens success","Sitting idle achieves nothing"]
example_sentence: Ali studied day and night for the exam because he believed that God helps those who help themselves. Instead of waiting for financial support, she started her own small business because God helps those who help themselves. The team practiced regularly and finally won the match, proving that God helps those who help themselves. He searched for a job actively rather than sitting idle because he knew that God helps those who help themselves.

english_meaning: A female deity worshipped in many religions and mythologies. A woman who is greatly loved or admired for her beauty, grace, or talent. A female figure considered to have divine or supernatural powers. A woman regarded as exceptionally charming, beautiful, or powerful.
example_sentence: The ancient Greeks worshipped many gods and goddesses. Athena was the goddess of wisdom in Greek mythology. The actress looked like a goddess in her elegant gown. To him, his mother was nothing less than a goddess. The temple was built in honor of a local goddess.

english_meaning: Figures representing chaos or enemies. In religious and historical texts, Gog and Magog are symbolic names for nations or tribes associated with evil, chaos, or apocalyptic destruction. Mentioned in the Bible, Quran, and other traditions, they often represent forces opposing divine order or humanity in the end times.
example_sentence: The ancient map showed the lands of Gog and Magog beyond the mountains. Many legends speak of the destruction caused by Gog and Magog. The story of Gog and Magog warns of unchecked violence. Scholars debated whether Gog and Magog were literal tribes or symbolic forces. The legend says Gog and Magog will rise during the apocalypse. In literature, Gog and Magog often represent humanity's darkest fears. Some historians think Gog and Magog were based on real nomadic tribes.

english_meaning: To look at someone or something with wide open eyes, often in surprise, amazement, or shock. To stare with bulging or rolling eyes. To gaze fixedly with eyes wide open in wonder or astonishment.
example_sentence: The children goggled at the magician as he performed his tricks. He goggled at the enormous size of the cake. She goggled in disbelief when she heard the news. Tourists goggled at the tall skyscrapers in the city. The boy goggled at the fireworks lighting up the sky.

english_meaning: Close-fitting protective glasses worn over the eyes to shield them from water, wind, dust, chemicals, or harmful light. Special eyewear used in activities such as swimming, skiing, welding, or laboratory work. Protective eye equipment that creates a tight seal around the eyes.
example_sentence: He wore goggles before diving into the swimming pool. The welder put on his goggles to protect his eyes. Skiers use special goggles to avoid snow blindness. Lab workers must wear goggles when handling chemicals. She forgot her goggles and could not open her eyes underwater.

english_meaning: An abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck. A swelling in the neck caused by thyroid dysfunction or iodine deficiency. A visible lump in the throat area due to thyroid problems. A condition that can affect hormone production and metabolism.
example_sentence: Iodine deficiency can cause goiter. The patient has a visible goiter on the neck. Goiter may require medication or surgery. Using iodized salt helps prevent goiter.

english_meaning: A person who forms a relationship mainly to obtain money or gifts. Someone who pursues wealthy partners for financial gain. A person who searches for gold in the earth. Someone motivated by material benefit rather than genuine affection.
example_sentence: People unfairly called her a gold digger after the marriage. He warned his friend that she might be a gold digger. The old town was founded by gold diggers in the last century. She proved she was no gold digger by refusing the money.

english_meaning: To avoid working while pretending to work. To waste time instead of doing one's duties or responsibilities. To shirk work or responsibilities, especially by pretending to be busy. To be lazy or deliberately unproductive while on the job. A person who avoids work or responsibility. A lazy or unproductive person who pretends to be working. Fake or deceptive, especially something that appears valuable but is not.
antonyms: ["Work","Labor","Strive","Toil","Perform","Diligently work","Be productive","Be industrious","Fulfill one's duties","Take responsibility"]
example_sentence: He was fired because he spent most of his working hours goldbricking. Stop goldbricking and finish the report before the deadline. The manager noticed that several employees were goldbricking instead of helping customers.

english_meaning: A person who deliberately avoids doing their work, wastes working time, or pretends to be busy without actually accomplishing anything. The word is usually used negatively for someone who is lazy, unproductive, or intentionally shirks their responsibilities. It can describe someone who appears to be working but secretly spends their time doing nothing useful.
example_sentence: The manager warned the goldbricker that his poor performance could cost him his job. Everyone was working hard, but the goldbricker was pretending to be busy. The company introduced new rules to prevent employees from goldbricking during working hours. Nobody wanted to work with him because he was known as a goldbricker.

english_meaning: Financial rewards that encourage an employee to remain with an organization. High pay, bonuses, shares, or benefits that are lost if a person leaves early. An attractive arrangement that limits freedom by making departure costly. Figuratively, any valuable advantage that traps someone in an unwanted situation.
example_sentence: The share options became golden handcuffs after five years. She disliked the job but stayed because of the golden handcuffs. Golden handcuffs can help a company retain senior employees. He finally gave up his golden handcuffs to pursue teaching.

english_meaning: A person who makes objects and jewelry from gold and other precious metals. A skilled craftsman who designs, shapes, and repairs gold ornaments. An artisan who works with fine metals to create decorative or valuable items. A jeweler specializing in gold work.
example_sentence: The goldsmith crafted a beautiful necklace for the bride. She took her old bangles to the goldsmith to be redesigned. The goldsmith weighed the gold carefully before starting the work. His family has been working as goldsmiths for generations.

english_meaning: Ruined or in very poor condition. Fallen into disrepair or decline. No longer working well or looking good. Deteriorated because of neglect. Something that has become worse over time.
example_sentence: The old house has completely gone to pot. His health has gone to pot since the accident. The business went to pot after the manager left. The garden has gone to pot due to neglect.

english_meaning: To be on good terms with someone, to have their approval, or to be liked or trusted by them. To be liked, approved of, or favored by.
example_sentence: After helping his teacher, Ali is now in her good books. You’ll stay in your boss’s good books if you meet your deadlines. She tried hard to get back in her parents’ good books after the mistake. Honesty and kindness always keep a person in everyone’s good books.

english_meaning: A basically good, kind, and reliable person. Someone who possesses a dependable and trustworthy character. An individual who is fundamentally decent and helpful. A person of genuinely good nature who does the right thing.
synonyms: ["Good Person","Decent Fellow","Reliable Individual","Trustworthy Person","Stand-up Guy","Solid Citizen","Angel","Gem","Mensch","Honest Soul"]
example_sentence: He always volunteers to help his neighbors because he is a good egg. You can trust her with your secrets as she has always been a good egg. Even though he complains sometimes, deep down he is a really good egg. My grandfather was a good egg who would give you the shirt off his back.

english_meaning: A person who is lazy, useless, or incapable of doing anything productive or valuable. Someone who does not contribute or is of no help.
example_sentence: He is a good-for-nothing fellow who never helps anyone. Stop being a good for nothing—do something useful with your time. People called him good for nothing, but he proved them wrong later. She doesn’t want to marry a good for nothing man.

english_meaning: Used to say you are glad that an unpleasant person, thing, or situation has gone away. To show relief or satisfaction when someone or something annoying, harmful, or unwanted leaves or ends. It often carries a strong emotional tone and can sound rude if said directly to a person. It is usually said after the departure, not during it.
synonyms: ["Glad it is over","Good to be free of it","Finally gone","What a relief"]
antonyms: ["Sorry to see it go","Miss someone or something","Regret the loss","Sad farewell"]
example_sentence: He finally quit his job and everyone said good riddance. That broken phone is gone for good. Good riddance. She was always causing trouble, so good riddance to her. The noisy construction is over. Good riddance.

english_meaning: Items that are produced to be sold. Merchandise or products carried by traders or transported by rail or road. Possessions or personal property. Something of high quality or the proof someone needs, used informally.
example_sentence: The shop sells household goods at low prices. Goods are transported by train to the port. All his goods were destroyed in the fire. The new manager really delivered the goods.

english_meaning: Friendly, helpful, or cooperative feelings towards others. A kindly attitude and desire for the welfare of people. The established reputation of a business regarded as a valuable asset. Willingness to be generous or forgiving.
example_sentence: The visit was made as a gesture of goodwill between the two nations. She has earned the goodwill of everyone in the neighbourhood. The company's goodwill was valued at several million rupees. He released the prisoners as a sign of goodwill.

english_meaning: To make a stupid mistake. To make a silly mistake. To make a foolish or embarrassing mistake. A silly or stupid person.
example_sentence: f Tom hadn't goofed and missed that shot, we'd have won the game. I made a real goof by forgetting his name. We were just goofing by painting the neighbors cat green.

english_meaning: To behave in a silly or playful way instead of being serious. To waste time doing unimportant or foolish things. To joke, fool, or mess about without purpose. To avoid work or responsibility by acting unserious.
synonyms: ["Fool around","Mess around","Joke around","Waste time","Play around","Clown around"]
example_sentence: The students were goofing around instead of finishing their homework. Stop goofing around and focus on your work. They spent the afternoon goofing around at the park. He got into trouble for goofing around during the meeting.

english_meaning: To waste time, avoid work, or act in a silly way instead of doing something serious. To idle away time. To avoid responsibility. To fool around playfully. To slack off from duties.
example_sentence: He always goofs off instead of finishing his homework. The workers were caught goofing off during office hours. Stop goofing off and focus on your studies. They spent the whole afternoon goofing off at the park.

english_meaning: To do something wrongly because of carelessness or lack of attention. To spoil or mess up a task or situation. To make an error that causes problems or embarrassment. To fail in doing something properly.
example_sentence: I really goofed up the presentation by forgetting important points. He goofed up his chances of promotion by arriving late repeatedly. Don’t goof up this opportunity, it is very important for your career. The team goofed up the project due to poor planning.

english_meaning: A careless or silly mistake caused by lack of attention. An error that leads to confusion or problems. A failure to do something correctly. A situation where something goes wrong due to poor judgment or planning.
example_sentence: I made a goof-up while entering the data in the system. His goof-up caused the whole project to be delayed. She realized her goof-up and corrected it immediately. They goofed up the presentation by missing important points.

english_meaning: Silly, foolish, or slightly ridiculous in a harmless way. Behaving in a funny or awkward manner. Having a strange or amusing appearance. Not serious; playful and lighthearted.
example_sentence: He made a goofy face to make the baby laugh. She wore a goofy hat to the party. My little brother has a goofy sense of humor. Stop being so goofy and finish your homework.

english_meaning: A criminal who is paid to frighten or injure people. A violent criminal who is paid to hurt or threaten people. A silly or stupid person.
example_sentence: Just call off your goons and no one will get hurt. The goons at the next table were just itching to finish him off.

english_meaning: A small edible fruit that grows on a gooseberry bush. A fruit that is usually round or oval and has thin, slightly translucent skin. A fruit that can taste very sour, especially when unripe. A fruit that may become sweeter as it ripens. A fruit commonly used for making jams, jellies, pies, desserts, sauces, and preserves. The plant or bush that produces this fruit. In British English, gooseberry can also refer to a person who is unintentionally present with two people who are spending time together romantically. Gooseberry can refer to different plants and fruits in different parts of the world, so the exact fruit can depend on regional usage.
example_sentence: The gooseberries in our garden are still green and very sour. She made delicious gooseberry jam from the fresh fruit. Gooseberries can be used in pies, desserts, and sauces. He felt like a gooseberry when his two friends started talking about their relationship.

english_meaning: Small raised bumps that appear on the skin due to cold, fear, excitement, or strong emotion. The tiny rough spots that form on the skin when the small muscles at the base of body hairs contract. A physical reaction of the skin to thrilling music, scary stories, or emotional moments.
example_sentence: The cold breeze gave me goosebumps. Her beautiful singing voice gives me goosebumps every time. He got goosebumps while watching the horror movie. The national anthem still gives him goosebumps. I had goosebumps all over my arms after the scary story.

english_meaning: An extremely complicated problem that seems impossible to solve. A difficulty that can only be resolved by bold or unconventional action. A tangled situation requiring a decisive solution.
example_sentence: The dispute over water rights became a Gordian knot. He cut the Gordian knot by resigning from both posts. Reforming the system is a Gordian knot for any government. Their finances had turned into a real Gordian knot.

english_meaning: Blood that has been shed, especially as a result of violence or injury. Graphic violence and bloodshed. To pierce, stab, or wound with a horn, tusk, or similar pointed object. A triangular piece of material used to widen a garment, sail, or other item.
example_sentence: The horror movie contained scenes of blood and gore. The bull gored the matador in the leg. The tailor added a gore to give the skirt more width. Critics felt that the film relied too heavily on gore for shock value.

english_meaning: A narrow valley with steep rocky sides, usually with a stream or river running through it. A deep ravine cut into the earth by flowing water. To eat greedily and in very large quantities until completely full. To fill oneself with something to excess. The throat or gullet, especially in older or literary usage.
example_sentence: The river carved a deep gorge through the mountains. We hiked along the edge of the gorge at sunrise. The children began to gorge themselves on sweets at the party. He gorged on pizza after the long day of training.

english_meaning: Extremely beautiful, attractive, or pleasing to look at. Stunningly impressive, magnificent, or splendid in appearance. Very enjoyable or delightful. Used to describe people, places, weather, or things that are exceptionally lovely.
example_sentence: She looked absolutely gorgeous in her wedding dress. We had a gorgeous view of the lake from our hotel room. The weather today is just gorgeous. They live in a gorgeous old house in the countryside. He gave her a gorgeous bouquet of red roses.

english_meaning: Lacking sense or intelligence; foolish. Looking or behaving in a stupid, vacant way. Slow to understand things. Clumsy and unaware of what is going on around one.
example_sentence: He stood there with a gormless expression on his face. Don't be so gormless; read the instructions first. The film's hero is a gormless but likeable young man. She gave a gormless answer to a simple question.

english_meaning: The teachings of Jesus Christ as recorded in the first four books of the New Testament. Any of the four books of the Bible — Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John — that describe the life and teachings of Jesus. Something that is accepted as completely true and reliable. A set of principles or beliefs that someone strongly upholds.
example_sentence: He reads the gospel every morning before breakfast. The priest delivered a sermon based on the Gospel of John. She takes her doctor's advice as gospel. Do not accept everything you read on the internet as gospel truth. The teacher's words were considered gospel by the students.

english_meaning: A very fine, light, delicate, and thin material, especially silk or fabric. Light, flimsy threads of cobweb spun by small spiders, often seen floating in the air or covering grass. Something extremely delicate, soft, or fragile in nature. Anything light, airy, and almost transparent.
example_sentence: The bride wore a gown made of gossamer silk. Tiny drops of dew clung to the gossamer threads on the grass. Her dreams were as fragile as gossamer. The dancer wore gossamer wings for her fairy costume. The morning sun shone through the gossamer curtains.

english_meaning: Casual or unconstrained conversation or reports about other people, typically involving details that are not confirmed as being true. Idle talk or rumor, especially about the personal or private affairs of others. A person who habitually talks about other people's private lives. To engage in such talk.
example_sentence: Office gossip can damage relationships between colleagues. She loves to gossip about her neighbors. Do not believe every gossip you hear about celebrities. They were gossiping in the corner during the meeting. He is known as the biggest gossip in the village.

english_meaning: A person who spreads rumors or talks about other people's private matters. A rumor spreader. A tale bearer. A person who talks excessively about others' private lives. One who enjoys spreading scandal.
example_sentence: Nobody trusted him because he was known as a gossipmonger in the office. The small village quickly learned about the incident through a local gossipmonger. A gossipmonger can damage friendships by spreading private stories. She avoided the neighbor who acted like a gossipmonger and always talked about others.

english_meaning: Relating to a style of architecture common in Western Europe between the 12th and 16th centuries, characterized by pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses. Belonging to a style of literature or film that uses dark, mysterious, gloomy, and often supernatural elements. A bold and ornate style of printing or typeface. Relating to the ancient Goths, a Germanic tribe.
example_sentence: The cathedral is a fine example of Gothic architecture. She loves reading Gothic novels full of mystery and suspense. The movie has a dark Gothic atmosphere. The university building has tall Gothic windows. Many Gothic churches in Europe attract thousands of tourists every year.

english_meaning: A large fleshy fruit with a hard outer skin, grown on trailing or climbing plants of the cucumber family. The hollowed and dried shell of such a fruit, used as a bottle, bowl, ladle, or musical instrument. The plant that produces this fruit. Informally, a person's head.
example_sentence: The farmer grew bottle gourds along the fence of his vegetable garden. The villagers carried water in dried gourds during the long journey. She cooked a light curry with fresh gourd and lentils for dinner. The musician played a traditional instrument made from a hollow gourd.

english_meaning: A person who enjoys eating and often eats too much. A glutton. A person who loves good food and drink; a gourmet. Describing someone fond of eating.
example_sentence: The gourmand ordered three desserts after an enormous dinner. He was a cheerful gourmand who never refused a second helping. The city's food festival attracts gourmands from all over the country. Unlike her gourmand brother, she ate small and simple meals.

english_meaning: A connoisseur of good food and drink. Involving or featuring high-quality or exotic ingredients and skilled preparation. A person who knows a lot about fine dining and culinary arts.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a gourmet meal for the special guests. She enjoys shopping at gourmet food stores for rare ingredients. He considers himself a gourmet and loves trying new restaurants. The hotel offers gourmet dining options for its affluent visitors.

english_meaning: To officially rule or control a country, state, organization, or group of people. To conduct the policy, actions, and affairs of a state or community. To control, influence, or regulate a person's actions, behavior, or course of events. To determine or guide an action or decision.
example_sentence: The prime minister governs the country with the help of his cabinet. Strict rules govern the use of mobile phones in the examination hall. He could not govern his temper during the heated argument. The committee governs all financial matters of the school. Many laws govern the import and export of goods.

english_meaning: The action, manner, or system of governing a country, organisation, or people. The process of decision-making and the process by which decisions are implemented. The exercise of authority and control in managing public affairs. The framework of rules, practices, and processes by which an institution is directed.
example_sentence: Good governance is essential for economic development. The report highlighted weaknesses in corporate governance. Citizens demanded transparency in the governance of public funds. The new leadership promised better governance and accountability.

english_meaning: To start or continue doing something, especially in a usual or planned way.
example_sentence: She went about her chores quietly. How should I go about applying for the job? He went about fixing the car. The doctor went about his rounds.

english_meaning: To chase, follow, or try to get something or someone.
example_sentence: He went after the thief. She’s going after a promotion. They went after their dreams. The police went after the suspect.

english_meaning: To oppose, resist, or not follow something or someone.
example_sentence: I can’t go against my principles. The ruling goes against the law. He went against his family’s wishes. It goes against my conscience to lie.

english_meaning: To proceed or continue with something, to start doing something.
example_sentence: Go ahead, you can start now. They went ahead with the project despite risks. Please go ahead and eat. The meeting will go ahead as planned.

english_meaning: To move or travel in a circular direction, to spread, or to be enough for everyone. To visit people or places.
example_sentence: A flu bug is going around. There’s enough food to go around. She went around visiting friends. Rumors are going around about him.

english_meaning: To leave a place or move away from someone.
example_sentence: Please go away and leave me alone. The pain won’t go away. They went away for the weekend. Old habits die hard—they never go away.

english_meaning: To move or return to a previous position, situation, or state. It can refer to going back physically to a location, recalling something from the past, or returning to an earlier topic, stage, or condition.
example_sentence: I have to go back to work. They went back to their hometown. Let’s go back to the main topic. This tradition goes back centuries.

english_meaning: To take hold of something or someone suddenly, quickly, and roughly. To seize or snatch something with the hands. To take an opportunity or chance eagerly. To attract someone's attention or interest in a strong way. A sudden attempt to seize or take something.
example_sentence: He grabbed the book and ran out of the room. She grabbed her child's hand before crossing the road. Let us grab a cup of coffee before the meeting. The headline grabbed my attention immediately. The thief grabbed her bag and disappeared into the crowd.

english_meaning: Moving in a smooth, elegant, and attractive way. Having or showing beauty of form, movement, or expression. Polite and pleasant in behavior, especially in difficult situations. Characterized by charm, ease, and refinement.
example_sentence: The dancer moved across the stage with graceful steps. She accepted her defeat in a graceful manner. The swan glided gracefully across the calm lake. His graceful handwriting impressed the teacher.

english_meaning: Displaying kindness, courtesy, and a pleasant demeanor. Characterized by elegance, refinement, and good taste. Showing divine grace, mercy, or compassion. Acting in a polite and accommodating manner, especially towards those of lower status.
example_sentence: The host was incredibly gracious and made everyone feel welcome at the party. She accepted the defeat with a gracious smile and congratulated the winner. We were treated to a gracious lifestyle during our stay at the historic estate. He offered a gracious apology for the misunderstanding that occurred yesterday.

english_meaning: The degree of slope or steepness of a road, hill, or surface. A gradual change in colour, tone, or intensity from one point to another. The rate at which a physical quantity such as temperature or pressure changes over distance. In mathematics, a measure of the steepness of a line or curve.
example_sentence: The road has a steep gradient near the top of the hill. The designer used a soft gradient from blue to green. Scientists measured the temperature gradient in the lake. Cyclists struggled with the sharp gradient of the mountain pass.

english_meaning: Happening, changing, or developing slowly over a long period of time rather than suddenly. Taking place in small stages or steps. Proceeding by degrees rather than abruptly. Used to describe slopes or inclines that rise slowly and steadily.
example_sentence: There has been a gradual improvement in his health. The road has a gradual slope toward the river. We are seeing a gradual rise in temperatures every year. Learning a new language is a gradual process. The change in her attitude was slow and gradual.

english_meaning: To successfully complete a course of study or training and receive an academic degree or diploma. A person who has successfully completed a course of study or training. To change something by degrees or to arrange in a series of grades or steps. To mark a scale or a set of measurements on a container or instrument. To move up to a more advanced level or a higher stage of development.
example_sentence: She is a graduate of one of the most prestigious law schools in the country. The laboratory uses a graduate cylinder to measure liquids with high precision. After years of hard work, he will finally graduate from university this spring. The company decided to graduate its pricing structure to accommodate different customer budgets.

english_meaning: The successful completion of a course of study at a university, college, or school, for which a degree or diploma is awarded. A formal ceremony where degrees or diplomas are conferred upon students who have finished their studies. The arrangement or classification of something in a series of gradual steps or stages. The act of dividing something into units or marking a scale for measurement. A gradual change or transition from one level, state, or color to another.
example_sentence: She felt a sense of immense pride during her college graduation ceremony. The thermometer shows precise graduation marks for accurate temperature reading. There is a subtle graduation of color in the sunset from orange to deep purple. After graduation, he plans to travel across Europe before starting his career.

english_meaning: A prefix relating to ancient or modern Greece or its people. Pertaining to the Greek language, culture, or history. Used in combination to describe things influenced by Greek traditions alongside another culture. A formal descriptor for Hellenic origins in academic or historical contexts.
example_sentence: The Graeco-Roman wrestling style is a staple of the Olympic Games. Scholars often study Graeco-Buddhist art to understand early cultural exchange. The architectural ruins displayed classic Graeco-Persian influences. Many modern scientific terms have Graeco-Latin roots.

english_meaning: Writing or drawings on walls. Refers to words, drawings, symbols, or paintings written or sprayed on public surfaces such as walls, bridges, trains, or buildings. It can be illegal vandalism or a form of street art used to express ideas, protest, identity, or creativity.
example_sentence: The city cleaned graffiti from the walls of the old building. Some graffiti carries powerful social and political messages. The artist is famous for turning graffiti into modern art. Graffiti on public property is considered illegal in many countries.

english_meaning: A piece of living tissue that is surgically moved from one part of the body to another or from one person to another. A shoot or twig inserted into a slit on the trunk or stem of a living plant, from which it receives sap. The practice of using one's position or influence for dishonest or illegal gain, especially in politics. To join or insert a part of one plant into another to allow them to grow together. To transplant living tissue to a new site on the body. Hard work or strenuous labor, often in a physical or manual sense.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed a skin graft to treat the severe burn. The gardener decided to graft a branch from the apple tree onto the pear tree. The politician was accused of using his office for personal graft and corruption. After years of hard graft in the mines, he finally decided to retire.

english_meaning: The horticultural technique of joining a shoot or bud of one plant onto the stem or root of another so that they grow together. The surgical procedure of transplanting living tissue from one part of the body to another or from one person to another. The act of inserting or integrating something into an existing structure to become a permanent part of it. A process of incorporating foreign material into a substance to alter its properties. Hard work or labor, often in a physical or strenuous context. The acquisition of money or advantage through dishonest or illegal means in politics or business.
example_sentence: The gardener spent the afternoon grafting apple branches onto the pear tree. The patient required extensive skin grafting after suffering severe burns in the fire. Political analysts reported widespread grafting and corruption within the local administration. Success in this industry requires years of hard grafting and dedication.

english_meaning: The small hard seeds of food plants such as wheat, rice, corn, or oats. A single small piece or particle of a substance such as sand, salt, or sugar. The smallest possible amount of something. The natural arrangement of fibers or particles in wood, stone, or fabric. A unit of weight used for measuring small quantities.
example_sentence: Farmers store grain in large silos after the harvest. There is not a grain of truth in his story. A few grains of salt can make a big difference in cooking. The carpenter polished the table along the grain of the wood. Rice is the main grain eaten in many Asian countries.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a kilogram. A small unit used to weigh light objects, food, and medicine. The basic unit of mass in the older centimetre-gram-second system.
example_sentence: Please add fifty grams of sugar to the batter. One thousand grams make one kilogram. The gold ring weighs only eight grams. The doctor prescribed five grams of the medicine daily.

english_meaning: Relating to grammar or the rules of a language. Concerning the structure and formation of sentences. Connected with the correct arrangement of words in a sentence. Related to grammatical rules, forms, or structures. Concerning the way words function and relate to one another in a language. Related to the study or analysis of grammar. Describing something that follows the rules of grammar.
example_sentence: The teacher explained the grammatic structure of the sentence. The book provides a detailed analysis of grammatic patterns in the language. Students should understand the grammatic rules before writing complex sentences. The researcher examined the grammatic features of the two languages.

english_meaning: Relating to grammar. Following the rules of grammar correctly. Concerning the structure and form of sentences.
example_sentence: The essay contains a few grammatical errors. He explained the grammatical rules with examples. That form is not grammatical in standard English. Grammatical accuracy improves with regular reading.

english_meaning: In a way that follows the rules of grammar. With regard to grammar. Correctly in terms of sentence structure and word form.
example_sentence: The sentence is grammatically correct but sounds odd. Grammatically, the phrase needs a comma here. She writes grammatically even in informal messages. The translation is grammatically sound and clear.

english_meaning: Magnificent and impressive in appearance or size. Very large or ambitious in scope or intention. Highest in rank or importance. Wonderful or very pleasant. Used in titles to show senior family relationship.
example_sentence: The wedding was a grand and colorful ceremony. She has grand plans for her new business. My grand uncle lives in a nearby city. They stayed in a grand hotel overlooking the sea.

english_meaning: Pompous, exaggerated, or overly fancy speech or writing. A style of speaking or writing that sounds important, dramatic, or impressive but often uses more words than necessary. It can seem artificial or showy rather than simple and clear.
example_sentence: His grandiloquence made a simple apology sound like a royal speech. The politician’s grandiloquence impressed some listeners but confused others. She avoided grandiloquence and spoke in clear, simple words. The writer’s grandiloquence made the essay hard to understand.

english_meaning: Using language that is pompous and overly elaborate. Speaking or writing in a lofty, inflated, or showy style intended to impress. Marked by extravagant expression with little real substance. Often used disapprovingly for orators, writers, or politicians who use big words instead of plain meaning.
example_sentence: The politician’s grandiloquent speech impressed no one. He has a grandiloquent style of writing that few readers enjoy. Her grandiloquent promises were never fulfilled. The lecture was full of grandiloquent phrases but lacked substance. Critics mocked the author’s grandiloquent prose.

english_meaning: Impressive or imposing in appearance, size, or style, often more than is necessary or reasonable. Excessively grand or ambitious in a way that may seem unrealistic or pretentious. Marked by an attempt to seem more important, magnificent, or impressive than one really is. Showing greatness combined with pomposity.
example_sentence: He has grandiose plans to build the tallest tower in the city. The palace was decorated in a grandiose style. Her grandiose ideas were never put into practice. The politician made grandiose promises before the elections. His speech was full of grandiose claims about the future.

english_meaning: To agree to give or allow something requested. To admit or accept that something is true. A sum of money given by an organization or government for a specific purpose. To transfer legally.
example_sentence: The government granted him a scholarship for higher studies. She was granted permission to leave early. I grant that you have a valid point. The university offers research grants to students.

english_meaning: A small round juicy fruit that grows in bunches on a vine. A green, red, or purple berry eaten fresh or used to make wine and raisins. The climbing vine that produces this fruit. The source of juice, wine, and dried fruit in many cultures.
example_sentence: He bought a kilo of seedless green grapes. The grapes hung in heavy bunches from the vine. Raisins are simply dried grapes. She washed the grapes before serving them.

english_meaning: A large round citrus fruit with thick yellow or pink skin and slightly bitter juicy flesh. A tart citrus fruit often eaten at breakfast or juiced. The tree that produces this citrus fruit. A pale pink colour similar to the flesh of the fruit.
example_sentence: He eats half a grapefruit with his morning tea. Grapefruit juice can interact with certain medicines. The grapefruit tasted sharper than she expected. Pink grapefruit is sweeter than the yellow variety.

english_meaning: Fear of writing or handwriting. An anxiety disorder where a person experiences fear, avoidance, or extreme discomfort when required to write or engage in handwriting tasks. It can affect personal, academic, or professional life.
example_sentence: Her graphophobia made it difficult for her to complete school assignments on time. He avoided filling out forms due to his graphophobia. Therapy helped him gradually overcome his graphophobia. Teachers noticed his reluctance to write essays and suspected graphophobia.

english_meaning: To hold someone tightly and struggle physically with them, or to try hard to deal with a difficult problem or situation that is not easy to solve.
example_sentence: The police officer had to grapple with the suspect to stop him. She is grappling with a tough decision about her career. The country continues to grapple with economic challenges. He grappled with his fear before speaking in public.

english_meaning: To seize and hold firmly. To understand something clearly. An act of holding.
example_sentence: She tried to grasp his hand tightly. He quickly grasped the main idea of the lecture. I quickly grasped the main idea of the lecture. The child slipped from his mother’s grasp. The child slipped from his mother’s grasp.

english_meaning: To try anything, no matter how hopeless, in order to improve a desperate situation. Acting without logic, relying on very weak or unlikely chances of success.
example_sentence: After losing his job, he was grasping at straws to find income. After losing his job, he was grasping at straws by applying for positions he was not qualified for She tried herbal remedies for her illness, but it was just grasping at straws. The company is grasping at straws to avoid bankruptcy. Believing that a miracle will solve all your problems is like grasping at straws.

english_meaning: To deal with a difficult or unpleasant situation boldly. To tackle a difficult, unpleasant, or risky problem with courage and determination, instead of avoiding it.
example_sentence: She decided to grasp the nettle and tell her boss the truth. The manager decided to grasp the nettle and fire the dishonest employee. It’s time to grasp the nettle and admit that the project has failed. The government finally grasped the nettle and introduced tough economic reforms. If you want to solve this conflict, you’ll have to grasp the nettle and talk to them honestly.

english_meaning: A plant-eating insect with long back legs that allow it to jump long distances. An insect that makes a chirping sound and can damage crops in large numbers.
example_sentence: A grasshopper jumped out of the tall grass. Grasshoppers destroyed a large part of the maize. The children chased a green grasshopper. You can hear grasshoppers in the field at noon.

english_meaning: To shred food such as cheese, vegetables, or chocolate into small pieces by rubbing it against a rough surface. To make an unpleasant scraping or harsh sound by rubbing against something. To irritate, annoy, or be unpleasant to someone over time. A metal frame of bars used to hold burning fuel in a fireplace or to cover a drain.
example_sentence: She grated some cheese over the pasta. Please grate a carrot for the salad. The sound of the chalk on the board grated on my nerves. His constant complaining really grates on me. Burning logs crackled in the iron grate of the fireplace.

english_meaning: In a way that shows thanks or appreciation. With a feeling of gratitude for kindness or help received. Thankfully and with relief.
example_sentence: She gratefully accepted the offer of help. He gratefully sank into the chair after the long walk. We gratefully acknowledge the support of our donors. The travellers gratefully drank the cold water.

english_meaning: The state of being gratified or satisfied. A feeling of pleasure when you get something you wanted or did something you wanted to do. It also refers to the source of such pleasure.
example_sentence: The children's smiles were all the gratification she needed. Some people seek immediate gratification instead of long-term goals. Reading a good book provides immense intellectual gratification. He joined the club for the simple gratification of meeting new people.

english_meaning: To give pleasure or satisfaction to someone. To indulge or satisfy a desire, need, or appetite. It means to make someone feel pleased by doing what they want.
example_sentence: It gratified him to see his students succeed in their careers. She was gratified by the positive response to her artwork. He decided to gratify his curiosity by opening the mysterious box. The chef was gratified to see the guests enjoying the meal.

english_meaning: Giving pleasure or satisfaction. Making someone feel pleased because something has turned out well. Rewarding and emotionally fulfilling.
example_sentence: It is gratifying to see your children do well. The response from readers was most gratifying. Teaching is hard work but deeply gratifying. She found the praise very gratifying.

english_meaning: A framework of parallel or crossed metal bars used to cover an opening such as a window, drain, or vent. Unpleasant and irritating in sound or manner. Making a harsh scraping noise. Causing annoyance through being repetitive or unpleasant.
example_sentence: A heavy iron grating covered the basement window. The grating sound of the gate woke me up. He has a grating voice that is hard to listen to for long. The constant grating of the wheels was unbearable. Workers replaced the broken grating on the street drain.

english_meaning: Given or done for nothing in return. Something provided without charge or payment being required. Costing nothing to the recipient or user. Offered as a favor or gift rather than a commercial transaction. A state of being complimentary or free of expense.
example_sentence: The hotel provides a gratis breakfast for all of its guests. He offered his legal services gratis to the local charity. Additional software was included gratis with the computer purchase. You can obtain a copy of the pamphlet gratis at the information desk.

english_meaning: The feeling of being grateful and wanting to express your thanks. A strong feeling of appreciation to someone or something for what the person has done to help you.
example_sentence: He smiled at them with gratitude. I would like to express my gratitude to everyone for their hard work. She was presented with the gift in gratitude for her long service.

english_meaning: Done without good reason or necessity, especially something unpleasant or harmful. Given or done free of charge, without payment or obligation. Unwarranted, uncalled for, and excessive in nature. Often used to criticize violence, insults, or details that serve no real purpose in a film, book, or conversation.
example_sentence: The film was criticized for its gratuitous violence that added nothing to the story.  His gratuitous remarks about her appearance were completely uncalled for.  The lawyer objected to the gratuitous details included in the witness statement.  She offered her help free of charge, with no gratuitous strings attached.  The article included a gratuitous insult that had nothing to do with the topic.

english_meaning: Without any good reason or justification. In a way that is unnecessary and often offensive. Free of charge, without payment being required. In an uncalled-for or excessive manner.
example_sentence: The film was gratuitously violent from beginning to end. He gratuitously insulted a guest who had done nothing wrong. The lawyer offered her advice gratuitously to the poor family. Critics said the scene was gratuitously shocking.

english_meaning: A sum of money given to someone for a service, in addition to the standard charge. A tip given to a waiter, driver, or other service worker. A payment made to an employee at the end of service or on retirement. A voluntary gift of money as a token of appreciation.
example_sentence: A ten percent gratuity is included in the final bill. He received a generous gratuity after thirty years of service. Passengers often leave a small gratuity for the driver. The hotel staff are not permitted to ask for a gratuity.

english_meaning: A hole dug in the ground to receive a corpse. Serious or solemn in manner or appearance. Giving cause for alarm or serious concern. To carve or engrave a design or words into a hard surface.
example_sentence: They visited the family grave to lay fresh flowers on the headstone. The doctor had a grave expression as he delivered the biopsy results. The country is facing a grave economic crisis that requires urgent action. The craftsman began to grave the intricate pattern onto the silver plate.

english_meaning: An extremely serious or severe violation of rights or fairness. A situation where an innocent person suffers significantly due to systemic failure. A deep-seated wrong that demands immediate rectification. A profound lack of justice that affects moral sensibilities.
example_sentence: Sending an innocent man to prison for twenty years is a grave injustice. The community protested against the grave injustice committed by the corrupt officials. It would be a grave injustice to ignore the contributions of the minor staff. History reflects many cases of grave injustice against marginalized populations.

english_meaning: Containing or covered with gravel. Rough, deep and harsh in sound, as of a voice. Having a coarse, grainy texture. Resembling small stones in feel or appearance.
example_sentence: We walked slowly along the gravelly path. He spoke in a deep, gravelly voice. The soil here is dry and gravelly. Her gravelly laughter filled the room.

english_meaning: In a very serious and solemn manner. To a dangerous or severe degree. In a way that shows deep concern or worry. Seriously enough to cause alarm about health, safety, or outcome.
example_sentence: He was gravely injured in the road accident. The doctor spoke gravely about her condition. She nodded gravely as the news was announced. The country is gravely affected by the ongoing drought.

english_meaning: A place where dead bodies are buried, especially near a church. A cemetery or burial ground. Figuratively, a place where things are discarded, forgotten, or no longer used. A location associated with death, decay, or endings. An area filled with abandoned or unused objects.
example_sentence: The old graveyard behind the church is very quiet at night. Many soldiers are buried in this graveyard. His garage has become a graveyard for broken machines. That website turned into a graveyard of forgotten posts.

english_meaning: A work shift that runs through the late night into the early morning hours. The overnight period of work, usually from midnight to dawn. A shift considered tiring due to its unusual hours. Employment during the quietest and darkest part of the night. Any job scheduled during nighttime hours.
synonyms: ["Night shift","Overnight shift","Late shift","Nocturnal shift","Third shift","Midnight duty"]
example_sentence: He works the graveyard shift at the hospital. Doing the graveyard shift can affect your sleep. Nurses on the graveyard shift often feel very tired. She earns extra money by taking the graveyard shift.

english_meaning: A serious, dignified, and solemn manner or attitude that commands respect from others. A quality of substance, weight, or seriousness in speech, behavior, or character. The dignity and importance that a person carries in their personality, often associated with leadership or wisdom.
example_sentence: The judge spoke with great gravitas during the trial. He brings a sense of gravitas to every important meeting. Her speech had the gravitas required for such a serious occasion. The new leader lacks the gravitas needed for the position. His gravitas earned him the respect of all his colleagues.

english_meaning: To eat grass or other plants growing in a field, especially in the case of cattle, sheep, or other animals. To touch or scrape something lightly while passing. To injure the surface of the skin by rubbing against a rough surface. To eat small amounts of food frequently rather than full meals.
example_sentence: Cows were grazing peacefully in the green field. The bullet only grazed his shoulder. She fell and grazed her knee on the pavement. Sheep graze on the hills throughout the summer. He prefers to graze on snacks rather than eat a full meal.

english_meaning: Much noise, little result. Used when people make a lot of fuss, complaints, or promises but produce very little useful outcome or benefit.
synonyms: ["Much ado about nothing","All talk and no action","Big talk","Small results","Empty promises"]
antonyms: ["Actions speak louder than words","Great effort","Great reward","Real results","Effective action"]
example_sentence: The meeting was a great cry little wool because no real decisions were made. His long speech about reform turned out to be great cry little wool. The protest caused noise everywhere but achieved nothing, truly great cry little wool. Their marketing campaign promised a lot but delivered very little, a case of great cry little wool.

english_meaning: A humorous saying used when two people have the same idea at the same time. An expression suggesting that intelligent people often reach similar conclusions. A light-hearted remark acknowledging a shared thought.
example_sentence: I was just about to call you — great minds think alike! We both ordered the same dish; great minds think alike. She laughed and said, great minds think alike, when they submitted identical plans. Great minds think alike, though fools seldom differ.

english_meaning: Having or showing an excessive desire for food, wealth, or power. Excessively eager or keen to obtain something in large quantities. Wanting to possess more than what one actually needs or deserves. Marked by an insatiable appetite or longing for personal gain.
example_sentence: The greedy ruler imposed high taxes on the poor peasants to fund his lavish lifestyle. He was so greedy that he refused to share a single piece of cake with his friends. The investors lost money due to their greedy financial decisions during the market bubble. She gave a greedy look at the buffet table filled with sweet desserts.

english_meaning: A natural talent for growing plants. An exceptional ability to garden and cultivate flowers or vegetables successfully. A special skill that makes plants thrive under one's care.
synonyms: ["Good With Plants","Gardening Skill","Horticultural Talent","Expert Gardener","Plant Lover","Cultivator","Agricultural Expert","Magic Touch With Plants"]
antonyms: ["Bad With Plants","Plant Killer","Incompetent Gardener","Clumsy Grower","Brown Thumb","Unskilled Cultivator","Poor Farmer","Unsuccessful Gardener"]
example_sentence: My grandmother has a green thumb and her garden is always blooming. You need a green thumb to keep these exotic orchids alive. I definitely do not have a green thumb because every houseplant I buy ends up dying. He developed a green thumb after spending a summer working at the local nursery.

english_meaning: A long, slender green pod eaten whole as a vegetable. An immature bean pod cooked by boiling, steaming, or frying. The plant that produces these pods. A common side vegetable in many cuisines.
example_sentence: She trimmed the ends of the green beans. Green beans stay crisp if lightly steamed. The garden produced a heavy crop of green beans. He fried green beans with garlic and pepper.

english_meaning: A small green pepper with a hot, pungent taste. A vegetable used fresh or cooked to add heat to food. The plant that produces these peppers. A common ingredient in curries, salads, and pickles.
example_sentence: He added two green chilies to the curry. Green chili makes the salad sharper and tastier. She grows green chilies on the balcony. Remove the seeds if you want less heat.

english_meaning: Extremely jealous or envious of someone. Feeling intense jealousy or resentment towards someone because of their possessions, achievements, or qualities.
example_sentence: She was green with envy when she saw her friend’s new car. He turned green with envy at his brother’s promotion. I was green with envy watching their amazing vacation photos. She was green with envy over her colleague’s recognition at work.

english_meaning: A small green sap-sucking insect, also known as an aphid, that feeds on plants. A tiny soft-bodied garden pest that damages leaves, stems, and buds by drawing out sap. An insect commonly found in large colonies on roses, vegetables, and young shoots. A common agricultural and garden pest that can spread plant viruses.
example_sentence: The rose bushes were covered with greenfly by early summer. Gardeners often use soapy water to control greenfly. A single greenfly can multiply into a large colony within days. Ladybirds feed on greenfly and help protect the crop.

english_meaning: A person who is new, inexperienced, or naive in a particular activity or field. Someone who lacks experience or knowledge in a specific area, often eager but untrained. Typically beginners who may make mistakes due to their inexperience.
example_sentence: The greenhorn struggled to complete the task without help. She was a greenhorn in the company but learned quickly. The greenhorn made several mistakes during the first practice session. Even a greenhorn can succeed with proper guidance.

english_meaning: To welcome or address someone in a polite or friendly way when meeting them. To receive someone with a particular reaction or response. To be the first thing that someone sees, hears, or notices upon arrival. To acknowledge someone's presence with words, gestures, or expressions.
example_sentence: She greeted her guests at the door with a warm smile. The teacher greeted the students cheerfully every morning. The news was greeted with great excitement by the public. A beautiful view of the mountains greeted us when we opened the window. He greeted his old friend with a tight hug.

english_meaning: Enjoys being with people; sociable. Someone who is friendly, outgoing, and enjoys spending time in social groups rather than being alone. Often refers to people who are cheerful and like interacting with others.
example_sentence: She is very gregarious and makes friends wherever she goes. Gregarious animals often live in herds or flocks. His gregarious nature made him popular in the office. The gregarious host entertained all guests warmly.

english_meaning: Relating to Pope Gregory I or Pope Gregory XIII. Describing the calendar introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 and now used worldwide. Relating to the plain, unaccompanied chant used in the early Roman Catholic Church.
example_sentence: Most countries follow the Gregorian calendar today. The monks are famous for their Gregorian chant. The Gregorian reform corrected errors in the Julian calendar. She studied Gregorian music at the conservatory.

english_meaning: To search for specific text or pattern, especially in files. To search through text, files, or data to find lines that match a given word or pattern. Often used in computing or programming. A command or tool used for searching text patterns.
example_sentence: I used grep to find the error in the log file. She grepped the folder for all occurrences of the word. You can grep this document to locate the keyword. The developer grepped through the code for bugs.

english_meaning: A heavy, flat metal pan or surface used for cooking food by dry heat, often used to make pancakes, eggs, or flatbreads. A circular iron plate placed on a stove or fire for baking or frying. A piece of cookware with a smooth flat top suitable for grilling on a stove.
example_sentence: She poured the pancake batter onto the hot griddle. The chef cooked the eggs on a large griddle. Place the bread on the griddle for a few minutes on each side. We bought a new electric griddle for the kitchen. The griddle should be greased lightly before cooking.

english_meaning: Deep sorrow or sadness, especially after a loss. An intense emotional pain people feel when they lose someone or something very important, such as a loved one, relationship, or valued possession. It can also refer to trouble, suffering, or a cause of distress.
example_sentence: She was overcome with grief after hearing about her friend's death. His family shared their grief with the community during the difficult time. The loss of the old house brought unexpected grief to the family. He tried to hide his grief, but his silence revealed his pain.

english_meaning: Overwhelmed by deep sorrow, especially after a death or severe loss. Suffering intense emotional pain. Showing the visible effects of bereavement. Unable to function normally because of sadness. Heartbroken by tragic news or personal loss.
example_sentence: The grief-stricken family gathered quietly after the funeral. She was grief-stricken when she heard about the accident. Friends stayed close to support the grief-stricken father. His grief-stricken expression revealed how deeply he felt the loss.

english_meaning: A real or imagined cause for complaint or protest. A feeling of resentment caused by unfair treatment. A formal complaint submitted to an employer, organization, or authority. A wrong or hardship believed to deserve correction. A long-held dissatisfaction that may damage a relationship. An issue raised through an official dispute procedure.
example_sentence: The workers filed a grievance about unsafe conditions. She still carries a grievance against her former manager. The committee listened carefully to every student grievance. Open discussion helped the neighbors resolve their grievances peacefully.

english_meaning: To feel deep sorrow or sadness, usually because of loss, death, or disappointment. It also means to cause someone emotional pain.
example_sentence: They are still grieving for their dead child. She grieved the death of her husband. It grieved him that he could do nothing to help her. Their lack of interest grieved her. It grieved her to leave.

english_meaning: Causing great pain, suffering, or sorrow. Very serious, severe, or harmful in nature. Characterized by severe physical or emotional distress. Flagrant or atrocious in a moral sense. Resulting in tragic or disastrous consequences.
example_sentence: The family suffered a grievous loss following the accident. He was found guilty of causing grievous bodily harm. The kingdom faced a grievous famine that lasted for three years. It was a grievous error that cost the company millions of dollars.

english_meaning: In a very severe or serious manner. To a degree that causes great physical or mental pain. In a way that is very harmful or damaging. Mournfully or with great sorrow. In an extremely offensive or flagrant manner. To a high and intense degree of distress.
example_sentence: The soldiers were grievously wounded during the intense skirmish. The community was grievously affected by the sudden economic collapse. She felt she had been grievously wronged by her closest friend. He sighed grievously as he looked over the ruins of his former home.

english_meaning: To cheat or swindle. To cheat someone, usually by tricking them out of money or advantage in a dishonest way. Police officer or detective. A police officer, especially a detective involved in investigations or undercover work.
example_sentence: He tried to griff customers with false promises. The company was fined for Griffing people online. She felt angry after being Griffing by a fake agent. Everyone knew he was a griff working undercover. The story follows a retired griff solving old cases. The suspect tried to avoid the griff.

english_meaning: To obtain money or property dishonestly by deceiving people, especially through small swindles or confidence tricks. A petty or minor swindle, fraud, or dishonest scheme. Money made by dishonest means. The practice of cheating people through clever tricks or schemes.
example_sentence: He spent years grifting tourists in the busy market. The two men were arrested for running a long grift on elderly people. She made her living through grifts and small frauds. The movie tells the story of a clever grift on a wealthy banker. They tried to grift money from innocent investors.

english_meaning: To cook food on a metal frame over an open fire or under direct heat. A metal framework or device used for cooking food over heat. To question someone closely, intensely, and persistently. A restaurant or section of a restaurant that specializes in grilled food.

english_meaning: Very serious, harsh, or unpleasant. Something that looks severe, frightening, depressing, or showing no humor. It can refer to a person's facial expression, a difficult situation, or something that seems dark and hopeless.
