english_meaning: To make a twisted facial expression, especially one showing disgust or pain. A facial expression showing dislike, pain, or disapproval.
example_sentence: He made a grimace when he tasted the sour lemon. She couldn’t hide her grimace when she saw the messy room. The child grimaced in pain after falling off the swing. He tried to smile, but it turned into a grimace of embarrassment. He grimaced in pain when the doctor cleaned his wound.

english_meaning: An ugly, twisted facial expression that shows pain, disgust, displeasure, or strong emotion. A look on the face caused by suffering or dislike. To make such a facial expression in response to something unpleasant. A distorted facial gesture used to express a feeling. Note: commonly spelled grimace.
example_sentence: He made a grimace of pain when the doctor touched his wound. She grimaced after tasting the bitter medicine. A grimace of disgust appeared on his face. The child grimaced when asked to eat the vegetables. He grimaced as he lifted the heavy box.

english_meaning: Dirt, soot, or other unwanted material ingrained on the surface of something, often difficult to remove. Thick, sticky, or oily dirt that has built up over time. A layer of filth that covers skin, clothes, or surfaces. Stains caused by dust, smoke, or pollution.
example_sentence: His hands were covered in grime after working in the garage. Years of grime had built up on the kitchen walls. She scrubbed the floor to remove the grime. The windows were thick with grime from the busy road outside. He came home from the mine covered in grime.

english_meaning: Smiling very widely because of happiness or excitement. Someone who is extremely happy, pleased, or delighted, showing it clearly by a very wide smile that stretches from one ear to the other. It conveys strong joy, satisfaction, or pride.
example_sentence: She was grinning from ear to ear when she heard she got the job. The children were grinning from ear to ear after opening their gifts. He couldn’t help grinning from ear to ear when his team won the championship. I was grinning from ear to ear when I saw my old friend after ten years.

english_meaning: To hold something tightly and firmly. A firm hold or tight grasp. The ability to understand or master something. Strong control or influence over a person or situation. To attract and hold someone's complete attention. The part of an object that is designed to be held. A travelling bag or holdall.
example_sentence: She gripped the railing tightly as the boat rocked. He has a good grip on the subject after months of study. The film gripped the audience from the opening scene. Fear kept the whole town in its grip.

english_meaning: Held tightly or firmly with the hands. Strongly affected or held by an emotion, feeling, or situation. Having attention or interest completely captured by something. Past tense and past participle of grip, meaning to seize and hold fast.
example_sentence: He gripped the steering wheel tightly during the storm. The audience was gripped by the suspenseful movie. Fear gripped her heart as she heard the strange noise. The country was gripped by an economic crisis. She gripped my arm and would not let go.

english_meaning: A device or tool designed for holding, grasping, or seizing objects firmly. A mechanical part of a machine, robot, or vehicle used to grip materials. A person or thing that grips. A surface or attachment that increases friction to prevent slipping.
example_sentence: The robot has a special gripper for picking up small parts. He used a gripper to open the tight jar. The new tires have excellent grippers for wet roads. Factory workers wear gloves with rubber grippers. The mechanical gripper can hold objects of various shapes.

english_meaning: Inspiring horror or intense fear. Extremely unpleasant and frightening and usually connected with death and violence.
example_sentence: The 55-year-old Canadian had suffered a grisly death. The jurors saw grisly photos of the crime scene. Jostein is unfaithful and sleeps with a woman before being called to the site of a grisly murder.

english_meaning: To prepare yourself to face something difficult or unpleasant with determination. To consciously press your teeth together and hold them firmly as a way to cope with stress, frustration, or discomfort.
example_sentence: He gritted his teeth and faced the pain. You’ll have to grit your teeth and finish the job. She gritted her teeth and smiled despite her anger. I gritted my teeth through the tough exam.

english_meaning: To make a deep, long sound to express pain, sadness, disappointment, or annoyance. To utter a low, mournful sound, often involuntarily. To complain or protest in a low voice. A deep sound made by a person or thing under strain or pressure.
example_sentence: He groaned in pain as the doctor examined his leg. She groaned when she heard about the extra homework. The old wooden floor groaned under the weight of the heavy furniture. The patient gave a low groan and turned over. Everyone groaned at his terrible joke.

english_meaning: A person who sells food and household goods in a shop. The owner or keeper of a grocery store. A shop that sells food and other everyday supplies.
example_sentence: The local grocer knows all his customers by name. She bought fresh vegetables from the grocer on the corner. My grandfather worked as a grocer for forty years. The grocer's shop was busy before the holiday.

english_meaning: A shop that sells food and household supplies. Food and other goods bought from such a shop, usually in the plural. The business or trade of a grocer. Items needed for daily household use.
example_sentence: I need to stop at the grocery on my way home. She carried the groceries up three flights of stairs. The price of groceries has risen sharply this year. He opened a small grocery in the village.

english_meaning: A self-service grocery store. An early type of supermarket in which customers select goods from shelves themselves.
example_sentence: The new groceteria let shoppers select their own canned goods. In the 1920s, a groceteria was a novel idea in retail. She found lower prices at the local groceteria. The groceteria eventually developed into the modern supermarket.

english_meaning: Dazed, weak, or unsteady, especially after sleep, illness, alcohol, medication, or a blow. Mentally slow and unable to think clearly. Faint or exhausted.
example_sentence: He woke up feeling groggy after only three hours of sleep. The boxer was groggy after taking a heavy punch. She felt groggy from the cold medicine. Jet lag left the travelers groggy for two days.

english_meaning: The area of the body where the lower abdomen meets the inner part of the thigh. The fold or hollow on either side of the body where the legs join the trunk. A part of the human body often referred to in sports and medical contexts. In architecture, the curved edge formed by the intersection of two vaults.
example_sentence: The footballer suffered a painful groin injury during the match. He felt a sharp pain in his groin while lifting the heavy box. The doctor examined the groin area for any swelling. Groin injuries are common in sports like football and tennis. The architect admired the groin vaults of the old cathedral.

english_meaning: To understand something deeply, completely, and intuitively. To comprehend through empathy or direct experience. To absorb an idea so fully that it becomes part of one's thinking.

english_meaning: To stare at someone while they are eating, hoping they will share food. To watch someone eat in a fixed and often uncomfortable way with the silent expectation that they might give you some of their food. It is usually used humorously and suggests mild social awkwardness rather than rudeness.
example_sentence: The dog sat near the table and began to groke while everyone was eating. He felt awkward when his friend groked him during lunch. Stop groking me and just ask if you want some food. She smiled because her little brother was groking her sandwich.

english_meaning: A reinforced eyelet in cloth or leather. A ring of rubber or plastic used to protect a wire or pipe passing through a hole. A surgical tube inserted into the eardrum to allow air to enter the middle ear. A sleeve or gasket used for sealing or insulation. A young surfer or extreme sports enthusiast, often used informally. A rope ring used on ships to secure sails or tackle.
example_sentence: The sailmaker reinforced the edges with a brass grommet to prevent tearing. The technician inserted a rubber grommet into the chassis to protect the electrical cables. After repeated infections, the specialist recommended placing a grommet in the child's ear. The young grommet spent all morning at the beach practicing his surfing technique.

english_meaning: A man on his wedding day or just before and after the event. A person who looks after horses, especially in a stable. To brush and clean an animal, especially a horse. To prepare or train someone for a particular role, position, or job. To make oneself neat and tidy in appearance. To carefully prepare someone over time for a future responsibility.
example_sentence: The groom looked very handsome in his traditional wedding outfit. She spends an hour every morning to groom her long hair carefully. The manager is grooming his assistant to take over the department. The trainer groomed the horse before the race. Parents groom their children to face the challenges of life.

english_meaning: A long narrow cut or channel in a surface. An established routine or habit. A rhythmic feel in music.
example_sentence: The wheels left deep grooves in the mud. He got into a comfortable groove at his new job. The needle fits into the groove of the record. The band found its groove after the first song.

english_meaning: Total amount before any deductions. Extremely unpleasant or repulsive. Very obvious and unacceptable, as of an error. A quantity equal to twelve dozen.
example_sentence: His gross income last year exceeded all expectations. The kitchen was in a gross condition. It was a gross violation of the rules. They ordered a gross of pencils for the school.

english_meaning: A person who is extremely ugly in a strange way, especially in a book or painting. Strange in a way that is unpleasant or offensive. Extremely ugly in a strange way that is often frightening or funny.
example_sentence: The mask had a grotesque expression that frightened the children. His sense of humor was so dark it bordered on grotesque. The building's architecture was a grotesque mix of styles. The movie featured grotesque creatures from another world.

english_meaning: A small picturesque cave, especially one that is artificial. A cave-like recess or shelter, often decorated with shells or stones. A natural hollow in rock used as a shrine or retreat. An ornamental structure imitating a cave in a garden.
example_sentence: The garden contains a small grotto with a fountain. Pilgrims gather to pray at the grotto every evening. We sheltered from the rain inside a sea grotto. The grotto was lit with hundreds of tiny candles.

english_meaning: A person who complains a lot and is often in a bad mood. A grumpy or bad-tempered individual. To complain in an irritable way. A cause of complaint or annoyance. Someone who is habitually sulky or discontent.
example_sentence: My uncle is a real grouch every morning before coffee. Stop being such a grouch and enjoy the party. He tends to grouch about the weather all day. Nobody wanted to sit next to the old grouch on the bus.

english_meaning: A fast-running beetle that lives on or near the soil surface and hunts other insects. A dark, hard-shelled beetle belonging to the family Carabidae. A largely nocturnal predatory insect regarded as beneficial because it eats crop pests. A beetle usually found under stones, logs, or leaf litter.
example_sentence: A ground beetle scurried across the path when I lifted the stone. Farmers value the ground beetle because it eats slugs and caterpillars. The ground beetle hides during the day and hunts at night. We found a shiny black ground beetle under the fallen log.

english_meaning: Introducing new ideas or methods; highly innovative. Marking an important first step or discovery in a field. Relating to the ceremony of beginning construction on a new building.
example_sentence: Her ground-breaking research changed how doctors treat the disease. The film was ground-breaking for its time. Scientists published a ground-breaking study on climate change. The mayor attended the ground-breaking ceremony for the new hospital.

english_meaning: Another name for the peanut, a legume whose pods ripen underground. An oil-rich seed used for food, cooking oil, and animal feed. A common crop grown in sandy soils in warm regions. The edible tuber of certain other plants, in some regional uses.
example_sentence: Groundnut is one of the main crops of the region. She roasted groundnuts for the children. Groundnut oil is widely used in cooking. The price of groundnut has risen this season.

english_meaning: To complain or grumble about something, To express dissatisfaction, annoyance, or complaint about something, often in a repeated or petty way. A complaint or grumble.
example_sentence: He always grouses about work. She groused over the delay. Employees grouse about low pay. Don’t grouse, take action instead.

english_meaning: To complain or grumble about something repeatedly or persistently, expressing dissatisfaction or annoyance over an issue. It often implies minor or petty complaints rather than serious grievances.
example_sentence: He always grouses about his workload. They groused about the long meeting. She kept grousing about the slow service. People often grouse about the weather.

english_meaning: To complain repeatedly about something specific. To keep bringing up a problem or disappointment and expressing irritation about it
example_sentence: She groused over the delayed payment. He kept grousing over the broken equipment. They groused over the unfair rules. The team groused over the poor management.

english_meaning: A small group of trees growing together. A small cluster of trees standing together in an open area. A grove is a natural or planted area where trees grow closely together, usually without dense undergrowth. It is smaller than a forest and often has a peaceful or cultivated appearance. Groves are commonly found in parks, gardens, orchards, or rural areas.
example_sentence: We walked through a peaceful grove of olive trees. The children played in a small grove near the river. A grove of coconut trees shaded the beach. Birds were singing in the mango grove early in the morning.

english_meaning: To behave in an overly submissive or respectful way toward someone in authority, often in an unpleasant or humiliating manner, usually to gain favor or avoid punishment. To act in a very humble, weak, or self-degrading way in front of someone powerful or important. It often includes excessive flattery, apology, or submission, sometimes like begging for approval or mercy. It can also imply lowering one’s dignity to please someone.
example_sentence: He had to grovel to his boss after missing the deadline. The servant grovelled to the king for mercy. She refused to grovel to anyone for approval. Many people grovel to authority figures just to keep their jobs.

english_meaning: A person or farm that grows a particular type of crop or plant. Something that grows or increases in size or number. In a business context, it can refer to a company or industry experiencing rapid development.
example_sentence: The local apple grower won an award for the best organic fruit. He is a prominent grower of roses in the valley. The region is a major grower of high-quality cotton. Small-scale growers often struggle with market fluctuations.

english_meaning: To make a low, deep, threatening sound, especially in the throat, as a dog or other animal does. To speak in a low, angry, and aggressive voice. To express dissatisfaction or anger in a rough way. A deep guttural sound made by an animal or person.
example_sentence: The dog growled at the stranger near the gate. He growled angrily when his work was interrupted. The lion let out a loud growl that scared the visitors. My stomach growled because I had not eaten all day. She growled a sharp warning at her brother.

english_meaning: The process of increasing in physical size or amount. A stage of development or gradual increase in maturity. The act of growing or expanding in scope or influence. A tumor or abnormal mass of tissue appearing in the body. The cultivation or production of something such as a crop or business. An increase in value or wealth over time.
example_sentence: The company has seen significant growth in its international sales this year. Regular watering is essential for the healthy growth of young plants. Doctors are monitoring the small growth found on his left arm. Personal growth often comes from overcoming difficult challenges.

english_meaning: To become an adult, to mature or develop over time. To pass from childhood to adulthood or to start behaving in a more mature, responsible way. It can describe both physical development (becoming older) and emotional growth (acting sensibly or responsibly).
example_sentence: I grew up in Karachi. She’s grown up into a responsible person. It’s time you grew up!. They grew up together as neighbors.

english_meaning: The thick, soft, worm-like larva of an insect, especially a beetle. Food, in informal everyday speech. To dig or search in the ground for something. To search about untidily for something.
example_sentence: White grubs were eating the roots of the plants. The workers sat down for some hot grub. He grubbed in the soil looking for old coins. She grubbed around in her bag for the keys.

english_meaning: Dirty, grimy, or covered in dust and stains. Shabby and unwashed in appearance. Morally unpleasant, sordid or contemptible.
example_sentence: The child came home with grubby hands and a torn shirt. He wiped the table with a grubby cloth. They uncovered a grubby deal between the two officials. Her grubby little office had not been cleaned in weeks.

english_meaning: A feeling of anger or dislike towards somebody because of something bad they have done to you in the past. To do or give something unwillingly. To be unwilling to give or admit. A feeling of deep-seated resentment or ill will.
example_sentence: He has a grudge against the world. I had a strange feeling in my gut before the exam. Trust your gut when making difficult decisions. The fish was cleaned and gutted before cooking. The fire gutted the entire building.

english_meaning: Very shocking, horrifying, or causing disgust. Something that is extremely unpleasant, frightening, or repulsive, often related to injury, violence, or horror. It evokes fear, disgust, or horror in people.
example_sentence: The crime scene was so gruesome that the police officers looked away. The movie contained gruesome scenes of war. The gruesome details of the accident shocked everyone. He described the gruesome injuries with horror.

english_meaning: Rough and low in sound, especially of a voice. Abrupt or unfriendly in speech or manner. Outwardly stern but often kind underneath.
example_sentence: He answered in a gruff voice from behind the door. Despite his gruff manner, the old man was very kind. The coach gave a gruff nod of approval. She was startled by his gruff reply.

english_meaning: To complain quietly To express dissatisfaction, annoyance, or unhappiness in a low voice or in a way that is not direct or open. It often refers to repeated or habitual complaining. A complaint or expression of dissatisfaction, often quiet or low-key. It can refer to a single instance or habitual complaining.
example_sentence: He always grumbles about the weather. She grumbled quietly when the meeting was delayed. The workers began to grumble about low wages. There is no point in grumbling instead of solving the problem. His main grumble is that the food is never hot enough. There was a loud grumble from the crowd when the concert was canceled.

english_meaning: A person who complains often or expresses dissatisfaction. Someone who frequently complains, murmurs, or expresses unhappiness about situations, often in a low voice or in a persistent manner.
example_sentence: He is a constant grumbler about the office rules. Stop being a grumbler and try to find a solution. The old man is a grumbler who complains about the weather every day. Even a small delay makes her a grumbler.

english_meaning: Bad-tempered, irritable, easily annoyed, and unwilling to be pleasant or sociable. In a mood of sullen displeasure or mild anger. Complaining frequently and showing dissatisfaction. Acting in an unfriendly way because of being tired, hungry, or upset.
example_sentence: He becomes grumpy when he does not get enough sleep. The grumpy old man shouted at the children. Why are you so grumpy today? She felt grumpy because she had skipped breakfast. The teacher was in a grumpy mood after the long meeting.

english_meaning: Making a short, deep sound from the throat, especially because of physical effort, pain, or to express disapproval. The act of producing low, rough sounds, often used by people or animals. Communicating in monosyllabic, rough sounds rather than clear words. A repeated low noise made under stress or exertion.
example_sentence: He was grunting as he lifted the heavy weights at the gym. The pigs were grunting loudly in the barn. She heard him grunting in pain after the fall. The workers were grunting under the load of the wooden beams. He just kept grunting instead of answering my questions.

english_meaning: To promise that something will happen, be true, or meet a stated standard. To accept responsibility for repairing, replacing, or refunding a product if it fails. To provide security for a debt or obligation. To make an outcome certain. A formal promise or assurance. A written warranty protecting a buyer. A person or thing that provides certainty or security.
example_sentence: The manufacturer guarantees the washing machine for five years. A balanced diet cannot guarantee perfect health. She offered her watch as a guarantee for the loan. Clear communication helps guarantee that everyone understands the plan.

english_meaning: A person who protects or defends something. A legal representative appointed to care for a minor or someone unable to manage their own affairs. A defender, keeper, or protector of a particular set of values or institutions. Someone who has the legal right and responsibility to care for another's property. A celestial being or spirit believed to protect a person or place.
example_sentence: The court appointed his aunt as his legal guardian after his parents passed away. The ancient library was watched over by a silent guardian of the scrolls. She has always been a fierce guardian of her family's privacy and reputation. Many people believe in a guardian angel who protects them from unseen dangers.

english_meaning: A round or oval tropical fruit with green skin and sweet pink or white flesh full of small seeds. A fragrant fruit eaten fresh or made into juice and jelly. The small tree that produces this fruit. A common winter fruit in South Asia.
example_sentence: Guavas are cheap and plentiful in the winter market. She sprinkled salt on the sliced guava. The guava tree behind the house is loaded with fruit. Guava juice is a popular drink in the region.

english_meaning: A person who is invited to visit someone's home or attend an event. A person staying at a hotel, restaurant, or similar place. A well-known person invited to take part in a programme or show.
example_sentence: We invited twenty guests to the wedding. The hotel guests were served breakfast at eight. She was the special guest on last night's show. Please make our guests feel comfortable.

english_meaning: A person who shows others the way or leads them on a journey. To direct or lead someone towards a place, decision, or goal. A book or document that gives information and advice about a subject. Something that influences or shapes behaviour and choices. To control the movement or direction of something carefully.
example_sentence: Our guide explained the history of the old fort. Let your teacher guide you through the difficult chapters. I bought a travel guide before visiting the city. He guided the boat safely into the harbour.

english_meaning: Full of cunning and deceit. Skilled in using tricks to mislead others. Sly and crafty in behaviour or intention. Marked by deliberate dishonesty.
example_sentence: His guileful promises tricked several investors. She saw through his guileful smile at once. The story features a guileful fox and a trusting crow. Their guileful tactics eventually came to light.

english_meaning: The fact of having committed a wrong, a crime, or an offense. A feeling of having done something wrong or having failed in an obligation. A painful emotion caused by believing one has caused harm. Legal responsibility for a wrongful act.
example_sentence: He could not hide the guilt on his face after the lie. The court finally proved his guilt beyond any doubt. She felt deep guilt for not visiting her parents often. A sense of guilt kept him awake all night. He confessed his guilt before the judge.

english_meaning: A large area of sea that is partly surrounded by land. A deep hollow or wide separation in the ground. A wide difference or division between people, groups, or ideas. A large distance or gap that is hard to cross. Something that swallows or engulfs.
example_sentence: The ship sailed slowly through the Persian Gulf. There is a huge gulf between the rich and the poor. A wide gulf of misunderstanding grew between the two friends. The soldiers were stationed near the coast of the gulf.

english_meaning: Easily persuaded to believe something. Trusting people too readily and therefore easily deceived. Naive and likely to be fooled or cheated by others.
example_sentence: Gullible customers often fall for fake advertisements. He is so gullible that he believes every story he hears. Online scammers usually target gullible users. She was gullible enough to lend money to a stranger. Teachers warned the students not to be gullible on social media.

english_meaning: Excessive greed or appetite, especially for food. The quality of being extremely gluttonous or greedy in eating and drinking. A formal or literary word for greediness, voracity, or excessive desire for food.
example_sentence: His gulosity at the dinner table embarrassed everyone. The book criticized the gulosity of the rich rulers. She is famous for her gulosity for sweets. Doctors warn that gulosity can lead to serious health problems. The character in the novel was a man of great gulosity.

english_meaning: To swallow drink or food quickly or in large amounts. To breathe in air quickly. A large mouthful of liquid or food swallowed at once. To try to hold back tears or emotion. A sudden nervous swallow.
example_sentence: He gulped down the water in seconds. She took a deep gulp of fresh mountain air. The boy gulped nervously before answering the teacher. He drank his tea in a single gulp.

english_meaning: The firm pink flesh in the mouth that surrounds and supports the base of the teeth. A sticky substance produced by certain trees and plants. A soft sweet substance that is chewed but not swallowed. An adhesive used for sticking things together. To stick or fasten something with a sticky substance.
example_sentence: Brushing gently protects your gums from bleeding. His gums were sore after the dental treatment. She offered me a piece of chewing gum. He gummed the torn pages back together.

english_meaning: To flow or pour out suddenly in large quantities. To express enthusiasm, admiration, or pleasure in an exaggerated and emotional way. A sudden and rapid flow of liquid. An outpouring of strong feeling or emotion.
example_sentence: Blood gushed from the deep wound on his arm. Water gushed out of the broken pipe. She gushed about her new car for hours. Tears gushed down her cheeks when she heard the sad news. A gush of cold air rushed in when he opened the window.

english_meaning: A sudden, strong rush of wind. A brief, powerful blast of air, smoke, rain, or similar element. A sudden outburst of emotion such as anger, laughter, or passion. A short, intense burst of something.
example_sentence: A sudden gust of wind blew his hat off. Gusts of rain hit the windows during the storm. She felt a gust of cold air when the door opened. He let out a gust of laughter at the joke. Strong gusts of wind made it difficult to walk on the bridge.

english_meaning: The tube in the body through which food passes when it leaves the stomach. To damage the inside through fire. A person’s stomach, especially when it is large. To destroy the inside or contents of a building or room. Empty completely, destroy the inside of. Something connected to the digestive system.
example_sentence: I was gutted (= I am disappointed). A factory gutted by fire. It can take up to 72 hours for food to pass through the gut. The hotel was completely gutted by fire last year. The fish was already cleaned and gutted. Good nutrition supports gut health.

english_meaning: The internal organs of a person or animal, especially the intestines and stomach. Personal courage, determination, or strength of character to do something difficult or unpleasant. The essential or most important part of something. Informal word for the inner workings of an object or system.
example_sentence: It takes a lot of guts to speak in front of a large audience. He did not have the guts to tell her the truth. The mechanic took out the guts of the engine to repair it. The film shows the guts of how the political system really works. She showed great guts during the difficult interview.

english_meaning: To remove the inside parts of something, or to completely destroy the inside of a building. A person who feels deep disappointment, sadness, or emotional pain. Extremely disappointed or very upset. Something that has been emptied inside.
example_sentence: She was gutted when she did not get the job. He felt gutted after his team lost the final match. The old house was gutted by fire. They gutted the building before starting renovation.

english_meaning: Literacy, of a flam or candle, to burn in unsteady way, long curved channel of metal, plastic under edge of roof carrying away water
example_sentence: The line of intersection forming a descending gutter which runs to the outlet.

english_meaning: A man or boy, used in an informal way. (In plural 'guys') People of any gender, used to address a group informally. A rope, chain, or wire used to hold something firmly in place, such as a tent or pole. (Old use) A strange-looking person.
example_sentence: He is a really nice guy and everyone likes him. Hey guys, are you ready to leave? That guy at the door is asking for you. The campers tied the tent with strong guys. Some guy called for you while you were out.

english_meaning: To drink something quickly and greedily in large amounts. To eat food fast and noisily without proper manners. To consume fuel, energy, or resources at a wasteful rate. To use up something rapidly and in excessive quantity.
example_sentence: He guzzled a whole bottle of water after the run. The children guzzled their juice within seconds. This old truck guzzles fuel on long journeys. They guzzled the snacks before the guests arrived.

english_meaning: A medical professional specializing in the health of the female reproductive system. A physician who treats diseases and conditions unique to women. A surgeon expert in female pelvic medicine and reproductive surgery. A doctor who focuses on preventative care and wellness for the female anatomy. A specialist providing clinical care throughout various stages of a woman's life cycle.
example_sentence: The gynaecologist recommended a routine screening to ensure reproductive health. After experiencing pain, she scheduled an appointment with a leading gynaecologist in the city. A gynaecologist may also be trained as an obstetrician to manage pregnancy and childbirth. The clinic employs a gynaecologist who specializes in hormonal disorders.

english_meaning: The branch of physiology and medicine which deals with the functions and diseases specific to women and girls. The medical practice focusing on the female reproductive system and breasts. The study of health and disease relating to the female reproductive organs. A specialized field of medical science focused on clinical care for women outside of pregnancy.
synonyms: ["OB-GYN","Female Medicine","Women's Health","Reproductive Medicine","Midwifery","Pelvic Medicine","Feminine Pathology","Clinical Gynaecology","Urogynaecology","Women's Care"]
example_sentence: She decided to specialize in gynaecology after completing her general medical degree. Advances in gynaecology have significantly improved the early detection of reproductive cancers. The hospital opened a new department dedicated solely to gynaecology and obstetrics. Regular consultations in gynaecology are essential for maintaining female reproductive health.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specializes in the health of the female reproductive system, including diseases and conditions of the uterus, ovaries, and breasts. A specialist who provides care related to women's reproductive health, pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical issues.
example_sentence: She made an appointment with her gynecologist for a checkup. Every woman should visit a gynecologist regularly. The gynecologist explained the test results to the patient. He is a well-known gynecologist in the city. The hospital is hiring a new gynecologist for the women's ward.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine that deals with the functions, diseases, and health care of the female reproductive system. The medical study and treatment of conditions affecting women, especially those related to the reproductive organs. A specialized field of medical science focused on women's health issues.
example_sentence: She is studying gynecology at the medical university. Gynecology is an important branch of medical science. The hospital has a separate department for gynecology. Modern gynecology has made childbirth much safer. He has written several research papers on gynecology.

english_meaning: An intense fear of women. A psychological condition in which a person has an irrational, persistent, and overwhelming fear of women. This fear may cause anxiety, panic, avoidance behavior, and difficulty in social or professional interactions.
synonyms: ["Fear of women","Female related phobia","Specific social phobia involving women"]
antonyms: ["Confidence with women","Comfort around women","Social ease with women"]
example_sentence: His gynophobia made it difficult for him to speak to female colleagues. Therapy helped her brother manage his gynophobia over time. Gynophobia can affect personal relationships if left untreated. The psychologist explained that gynophobia is different from simple shyness.

english_meaning: A person who wanders or roams from place to place. To travel or roam from place to place.
example_sentence: The old stories described a gypsy family traveling across many countries. She had a gypsy spirit and loved exploring new places every year. The festival included music inspired by traditional gypsy culture. He lived like a gypsy, moving from town to town for work.

english_meaning: To move or cause to move in a circle or spiral pattern. To rotate or revolve rapidly. To dance with circular movements of the body. To whirl or spin around a central point.
example_sentence: The dancers gyrated to the rhythm of the music. The leaves gyrated in the strong wind. Planets gyrate around the sun in fixed orbits. The top gyrated rapidly before falling down. Smoke gyrated upward from the chimney.

english_meaning: Something a person does regularly, often without thinking about it. A settled tendency or usual way of behaving. A practice that is hard to give up once established. An addiction or dependence on something such as smoking. A long piece of clothing worn by monks and nuns.
example_sentence: Reading before bed is a good habit. He is trying to break the habit of smoking. Old habits are difficult to change. The nun wore a simple black habit.

english_meaning: Suitable or good enough to live in. Providing the basic conditions needed for people to live safely. Describing a place, house, or planet that can support life. Fit for human occupation after repair or preparation. Capable of being inhabited.
example_sentence: The old house is barely habitable in winter. Scientists are searching for habitable planets. After repairs, the flat became habitable again. Only a small part of the region is truly habitable.

english_meaning: The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism. A place where a species normally lives and grows. The surroundings in which something exists or lives. A particular setting suited for certain living beings.
example_sentence: The forest is the natural habitat of many wild animals. Pollution is destroying the habitat of marine creatures. The zoo recreated the natural habitat of the lions. Climate change is threatening the habitats of polar bears. Scientists studied the habitat of rare birds in the mountains.

english_meaning: Done regularly and repeatedly until it becomes a habit. Describing a person who does something so often that it is part of their nature. Usual, customary, or typical of a particular person or place. Occurring as a fixed pattern of behaviour. Established by long practice and hard to change.
example_sentence: He is a habitual early riser. The court dealt firmly with the habitual offender. Tea after dinner is his habitual practice. Habitual lateness can damage your reputation at work.

english_meaning: In a way that is done regularly and as a matter of habit. Again and again over a long period of time. As one's normal or usual practice. In a manner that has become fixed through repetition. Customarily and without needing conscious thought.
example_sentence: He habitually arrives ten minutes early. She habitually checks her phone before sleeping. The manager habitually ignores small complaints. They habitually walk together after dinner.

english_meaning: To train or condition a person or animal to become familiar and comfortable with a situation, environment, or activity through repeated exposure. It can also mean to adapt mentally or physically to something over time.
example_sentence: Parents should habituate children to healthy eating habits early in life. The trainer habituated the dog to loud noises. It takes time to habituate yourself to a new work environment. Soldiers are habituated to strict discipline during training.

english_meaning: Lacking originality or freshness due to overuse. Overly familiar through repetition. Stale, clichéd, or commonplace. Used to describe phrases, ideas, expressions, plots, or themes that have been used so often that they no longer feel interesting, creative, or effective.
example_sentence: The speech was full of hackneyed phrases and lacked originality. Many writers avoid such hackneyed expressions in their novels. The film’s plot felt hackneyed and predictable. He used the same hackneyed argument again. Hackneyed slogans no longer impress modern voters.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of blood. A phobia that may cause fainting at the sight of blood. Severe anxiety triggered by injuries, wounds, or medical procedures. Also spelled hemophobia or hematophobia.
example_sentence: His haematophobia made blood tests very difficult. Children with haematophobia may faint during vaccinations. She could not watch the surgery because of haematophobia. Gradual exposure therapy is used to treat haematophobia.

english_meaning: An inherited disorder in which the blood’s ability to form clots is impaired. This happens because of the absence or low levels of clotting factors, leading to prolonged bleeding even from minor injuries.
example_sentence: The boy was diagnosed with haemophilia at an early age. People with haemophilia must avoid activities that could cause injury. Treatment for haemophilia often includes injections of clotting factor. Haemophilia can be life-threatening if not managed carefully.

english_meaning: A medical condition where the blood does not clot properly. Someone with deficiency in clotting factors, which makes even minor injuries lead to excessive bleeding. The term can also describe traits or things related to this condition.
example_sentence: The haemophiliac required careful medical supervision after a small cut. He learned how to manage life as a haemophiliac. Being a haemophiliac made him cautious about contact sports. Advances in medicine have improved treatment options for haemophiliacs.

english_meaning: To greet or acclaim someone enthusiastically. To call out to attract attention, like stopping a vehicle. To come from a particular place. Small balls or pellets of ice that fall from the sky during a storm. A greeting or salute. To greet, salute, or praise someone with respect or excitement.
example_sentence: Large hail damaged many cars during the storm. People hailed the scientist as a national hero. She hailed a taxi outside the airport. He hails from a small village in Sindh. Hail, Caesar! The crowd shouted loudly. Hail, brave warriors!. The king welcomed them. Hail! The champion of the tournament arrives.

english_meaning: A fine thread-like strand that grows from the skin of humans and animals. The mass of such strands covering the human head. A slender filament made of the protein keratin that grows out of a follicle in the skin. The coat of fur or filaments covering the body of a mammal. A very small distance or narrow margin, used figuratively.
example_sentence: She brushed her long black hair before going to school. Human hair is mainly made of a protein called keratin. The dog left hair all over the sofa. The car missed the wall by a hair.

english_meaning: A small tube-like structure in the skin from which a hair grows. The tiny pocket of cells in the dermis that produces and anchors a hair. A skin organ that surrounds the root of the hair and supplies it with nourishment. The site where hair growth begins and where oil glands often open.
example_sentence: Each hair on the body grows from its own hair follicle. Damaged hair follicles can lead to permanent hair loss. The doctor explained how a hair follicle receives blood and nutrients. Oil produced near the hair follicle keeps the skin soft.

english_meaning: The larva of certain moths whose body is covered with dense hairs or bristles. A furry caterpillar whose hairs may cause skin irritation or itching. A common garden pest that feeds on leaves before turning into a moth.
example_sentence: A hairy caterpillar crawled slowly across the leaf. Do not touch that hairy caterpillar, it can irritate your skin. The children watched a hairy caterpillar climbing the wall. Hairy caterpillars damaged most of the young plants.

english_meaning: Calm, peaceful, and happy, often referring to a time in the past. A period or situation that is calm, stable, and free from trouble. It is often used nostalgically to talk about earlier times that are remembered as happier or more peaceful than the present. A mythical bird linked with calm seas.
example_sentence: She often talks about the halcyon days of her childhood. The town enjoyed a halcyon period before rapid development began. They longed for a return to the halcyon calm of earlier years. The lake looked halcyon in the early morning light.

english_meaning: To haul, drag, or pull someone or something with effort or force, often against resistance. This can be used literally (physical pulling) or figuratively (forcing someone to do something). Someone who is in good health, robust, and free from illness or weakness, often used especially for older adults.
example_sentence: The police haled the suspect into the station. Workers haled the heavy logs up the hill. She was haled before the committee for questioning. They haled the boat ashore during the storm. The doctor declared her hale after the checkup. They were a hale couple, full of energy. He remained hale despite years of hard work.

english_meaning: To make holy or sacred. To honour as holy. To respect and venerate someone or something greatly. To consecrate by religious rites. To regard with deep reverence.
example_sentence: The temple is a place hallowed by centuries of worship. They hallowed the memory of the martyrs. The ground was hallowed by the blood of brave soldiers. People hallow this saint as a symbol of peace. The chapel was hallowed in a special ceremony.

english_meaning: Regarded as holy, sacred, or greatly respected. Honoured and revered because of long history, religious importance, or deep tradition. Consecrated or made holy through religious ceremony. Used to describe places, names, traditions, or memories that are treated with great respect.
example_sentence: The mosque is a hallowed place for the people of this town. He spoke of his teacher with hallowed respect. Cricket has a hallowed tradition at this historic ground. Their names are written in the hallowed pages of history. The hallowed silence of the library should never be broken.

english_meaning: To see, hear, feel, or experience something that is not actually present. It often happens due to illness, mental stress, drugs, extreme fear, or lack of sleep. The mind creates false sensory experiences that feel real to the person.
example_sentence: He began to hallucinate after staying awake for three days. The patient hallucinated voices that were not real. High fever can cause a person to hallucinate. She hallucinated shadows moving in the room.

english_meaning: A false experience where a person sees, hears, or feels something that is not real. A mental condition in which a person perceives sights, sounds, smells, or sensations that do not exist in reality. It often happens due to illness, mental stress, drugs, lack of sleep, or extreme fear. The experience feels real to the person even though it is not actually happening.
example_sentence: The patient reported visual hallucinations during the illness. Lack of sleep can cause hallucinations. He heard voices, but they were only hallucinations. The drug induced hallucination faded after treatment.

english_meaning: To bring or come to a complete stop. To stop the progress or continuation of an activity. A temporary or permanent stopping of movement or action. A small stopping place on a railway line.
example_sentence: The soldiers were ordered to halt at the checkpoint. Heavy snow brought the traffic to a halt. The government decided to halt all construction work. The train stopped briefly at a small country halt.

english_meaning: To stop moving suddenly and completely where you are. To come to an immediate standstill because of surprise or fear. To be stopped abruptly by something unexpected. To cause someone or something to stop instantly. To bring progress or an activity to a sudden end.
example_sentence: He halted in his tracks when he heard his name called. The strange noise made her halt in her tracks. The soldiers halted in their tracks at the officer's command. News of the accident halted the celebrations in their tracks.

english_meaning: A small village or a group of houses in the countryside, smaller than a town and usually without its own church or local government. A very small settlement, often rural, consisting of only a few houses or families. It is smaller than a village and typically lacks major facilities like a school or marketplace.
example_sentence: The old hamlet lies hidden among the hills. He grew up in a quiet hamlet far from the city. The earthquake destroyed several houses in the mountain hamlet. Tourists visited the charming hamlet for its traditional culture.

english_meaning: A tool with a heavy metal head and a handle, used for driving nails or breaking things. To hit something repeatedly with a hammer or with force. To defeat someone decisively. To work at something persistently until it is finished. A heavy ball on a wire thrown in an athletic event.
example_sentence: He used a hammer to drive the nails into the wood. The rain hammered against the windows all night. Our team hammered their opponents in the final. She hammered away at the problem until she solved it.

english_meaning: To strike something repeatedly and forcefully. To attack a problem, argument, or opponent persistently. To criticize someone or something again and again. To emphasize a point through forceful repetition.
example_sentence: Rain hammered at the windows throughout the night. The opposition hammered at the weakness in the policy. She hammered at the keyboard to finish on time. His lawyer hammered at the witness’s changing story.

english_meaning: To hit something repeatedly with a hammer or similar object. To work persistently and energetically on a difficult task. To criticize, question, or attack a point repeatedly. To repeat an idea until it is understood or accepted.
example_sentence: He hammered away at the old lock for several minutes. The researchers hammered away at the problem all winter. Reporters hammered away at the minister’s inconsistent answer. The coach hammered away at the importance of discipline.

english_meaning: To fasten or flatten something by striking it with a hammer. To force a price, rate, or amount lower through pressure or negotiation. To suppress resistance or impose control forcefully. To press a vehicle’s accelerator hard and move faster, informally.
example_sentence: He hammered down the loose edge of the metal sheet. We managed to hammer down the supplier’s price. The regime tried to hammer down every form of protest. She hammered down and passed the slow truck safely.

english_meaning: To drive something into a surface by striking it. To teach or impress an idea through forceful repetition. To make someone understand or remember something by repeating it often. To shape material by repeated hammering into a particular form.
example_sentence: He hammered the nail into the wooden frame. The instructor hammered safety rules into the trainees. Years of practice hammered the routine into her memory. The smith hammered the hot metal into a curved blade.

english_meaning: To strike something repeatedly. To continue emphasizing or talking about one point, often annoyingly. To criticize or pressure someone persistently. To keep working forcefully at a task or problem.
example_sentence: Someone hammered on the door before sunrise. The speaker kept hammering on the need for reform. Critics hammered on the company’s poor safety record. We hammered on until the software finally worked.

english_meaning: To produce or shape something by striking it with a hammer. To reach an agreement or solution through long and difficult discussion. To work out the details of a plan carefully. To play a tune loudly or forcefully on a piano or similar instrument.
example_sentence: The two sides hammered out a compromise before midnight. We need another meeting to hammer out the details. The artisan hammered out a thin sheet of copper. She hammered out the melody on the old piano.

english_meaning: To force a tool or object through a surface by repeated blows. To push a proposal or decision through despite opposition. To complete difficult work through sustained force or effort. To make a path by striking through an obstruction.
example_sentence: The worker hammered through the damaged wall. The majority hammered the bill through parliament. She hammered through the final chapter before dawn. Rescuers hammered through the debris to reach the room.

english_meaning: To join objects quickly or roughly using a hammer and nails. To assemble something with limited time or materials. To create a plan, group, or solution rapidly from available parts. To put something together in a forceful, makeshift way.
example_sentence: They hammered together a simple shelter before the storm. He hammered the broken crate together with spare nails. The committee hammered together a temporary agreement. We hammered together a presentation in one afternoon.

english_meaning: To hinder, obstruct. To prevent something from happening easily. To hold back progress or movement. A large basket, usually with a lid, used for carrying food, clothes, or laundry. A gift basket containing food and drinks.
example_sentence: Heavy rain hampered their progress. Heavy traffic hampered our journey. Lack of funds hampered the project. She brought a picnic hamper full of fruit and snacks. The hotel sent us a complimentary gift hamper.

english_meaning: Any of the group of muscles at the back of the thigh. The muscles that bend the knee and help extend the hip. A tendon at the back of the knee that can be felt as a tight cord. To severely limit, weaken, or prevent someone from acting effectively.
example_sentence: The sprinter pulled a hamstring during the race. Stretching before exercise helps prevent hamstring injuries. You can feel the hamstring tendons behind your knee. Budget cuts have hamstrung the entire research programme.

english_meaning: The part of the body at the end of the arm, including the palm, fingers, and thumb. Help or assistance given to someone. A pointer on a clock or measuring device. A worker, especially on a farm or ship. The set of cards held by a player in a card game. To give or pass something to someone.
example_sentence: He washed his hands before dinner. Could you give me a hand with these boxes? The minute hand of the clock had stopped. She handed the letter to her teacher.

english_meaning: To distribute items among a group of people so that everyone receives one.
example_sentence: She handed around the chocolates during the party. Please hand around these leaflets to the audience. They handed around the forms for everyone to fill out. The teacher handed around the answer sheets.

english_meaning: To return something to its rightful owner after borrowing or using it.
example_sentence: She handed back the book after reading it. Please hand back the documents once checked. The students handed back the borrowed materials. He handed back the pen he had borrowed.

english_meaning: To pass something, such as knowledge, tradition, or property, from one generation to another.
example_sentence: These customs were handed down from our ancestors. The old watch was handed down to him by his grandfather. Stories are handed down through oral tradition. Values are often handed down in families.

english_meaning: To formally submit something, such as an assignment, document, or resignation, for official consideration or record.
example_sentence: She handed in her homework before the deadline. Please hand in your resignation letter by Friday. Students must hand in the forms at the office. He handed in his ID card before leaving the company.

english_meaning: To be very close or work together in complete agreement, often for a shared goal or purpose. This idiom is used when two or more people, organizations, or groups are very closely connected or cooperate so smoothly that their actions seem almost unified.
example_sentence: The two companies worked hand in glove on the project. The manager and his assistant worked hand in glove to complete the project on time. The two companies are hand in glove in developing the new technology. The politician was hand in glove with the businessmen involved in the scandal. Teachers and parents should work hand in glove for children’s better education.

english_meaning: To give credit or praise to someone for their effort or achievement.
example_sentence: You have to hand it to her, she did a great job. I’ll hand it to John; he always works hard. You must hand it to the team for their dedication. We should hand it to them, they never gave up.

english_meaning: To pass or transfer responsibility or control of something to another person.
example_sentence: The manager handed off the project to his assistant. You can hand off the task when you’re finished. The quarterback handed off the ball to the running back. I’ll hand off this report once I review it.

english_meaning: To pass or give something to someone, especially knowledge or information.
example_sentence: The teacher handed on her experience to the new staff. He handed on the family traditions to his children. Please hand on this document to the manager. Wisdom is often handed on from generation to generation.

english_meaning: To transfer the possession or control of something to another person, often formally or under obligation.
example_sentence: The manager handed over the documents to the director. He was forced to hand over the keys to the police. The power was handed over peacefully after the elections. Please hand over the package at the reception.

english_meaning: To give control or leadership to someone else. To transfer authority or responsibility. To pass management to another person. To relinquish one’s position of power. To let another person take charge.
example_sentence: The CEO handed over the reins to his successor. She handed over the reins of the project to her deputy. After many years, the coach handed over the reins to a younger man. He is preparing to hand over the reins of the family business.

english_meaning: Used when a person wants to emphasize that they are telling the absolute truth. It is a strong expression of honesty, sincerity, or promise. (It’s similar to saying “I swear to God.”)
example_sentence: Hand to God, I didn’t take your book Hand to God, I have never met that person before. Hand to God, everything I said is true. Hand to God, I was at home the whole time.

english_meaning: Living without savings, Whatever one earns (by the hand) is immediately spent on necessities (for the mouth). There’s nothing left for future savings. Having no savings and struggling to meet daily needs. It describes a person or family who earns just enough to get by, often in poverty or financial hardship.
example_sentence: Many poor families in the village live a hand-to-mouth life. After losing his job, he was forced to live hand to mouth for several months. Despite working hard, some people remain hand to mouth because of rising prices. Farmers often live a hand-to-mouth existence during dry seasons.

english_meaning: To surrender yourself to the authorities, especially the police.
example_sentence: The criminal decided to hand himself in to the police. You should hand yourself in before they find you. After days on the run, he finally handed himself in. She handed herself in out of guilt.

english_meaning: A pair of lockable linked metal rings used by the police to fasten a prisoner's wrists together. To put handcuffs on someone. To restrain or limit the freedom or ability of a person to act. Figuratively, anything that prevents someone from doing what they want or need to do.
example_sentence: The officer placed handcuffs on the suspect and led him to the car. The thief was led away in handcuffs. New regulations have handcuffed small businesses. The judge ordered that the prisoner be handcuffed during the trial. He felt handcuffed by the strict rules of his job.

english_meaning: A condition that makes progress or success difficult. A physical or mental disability. A disadvantage imposed on a superior competitor to make a contest fairer. To place someone at a disadvantage. To hinder or impede.
example_sentence: Lack of education proved to be a major handicap in his career. The golfer played with a handicap of ten. Poor eyesight is a handicap for many students. Heavy traffic handicapped the rescue operation. Financial problems handicap small businesses.

english_meaning: Having a physical or mental disability. Affected by a condition that limits normal functioning. Placed at a disadvantage. Hindered or restricted in some way.
example_sentence: The government provides special facilities for handicapped persons. He was handicapped by a lack of resources. Handicapped children study in this special school. The accident left him handicapped for life. Many handicapped athletes compete in international games.

english_meaning: To select something or someone with great care and deliberation. To choose personally and manually rather than by an automated process. To pick out specific items based on their individual quality or suitability. To harvest fruits or vegetables by hand to ensure they are not damaged. To nominate a particular person for a role or task based on specific preferences.
example_sentence: The chef decided to handpick the freshest herbs from his private garden. It is common for the CEO to handpick his own successor after years of service. Each grape is handpicked at the peak of ripeness to ensure the best wine quality. She will handpick the members of the special committee to guarantee expertise.

english_meaning: True goodness or beauty is shown by actions, not appearance. It means a person is judged by behavior, kindness and character rather than looks.
example_sentence: Handsome is as handsome does—he helps everyone. She’s kind and generous; handsome is as handsome does. The proverb means good deeds define beauty. Handsome is as handsome does, not how one looks.

english_meaning: To give something to a group of people, especially as a share, gift, or information. It can also mean to distribute items such as papers, food, or aid. To distribute or give something.
example_sentence: The teacher handed out the worksheets. They handed out food to the poor. The teacher handed out the exam papers to the students. Volunteers handed out food and water to the flood victims. The manager handed out the new company policies to the staff. They were handing out flyers about the health awareness campaign.

english_meaning: To stay or move around a place without a clear purpose or just passing time. To wait or linger near someone or somewhere. Informally, it can also mean “wait a moment” (used in speech).
example_sentence: Boys were hanging about the street. Some boys were hanging about outside the shop after school. I don’t like to hang about doing nothing. We hung about the park waiting for the rain to stop. Hang about! Did you just say you’re moving abroad?

english_meaning: To stay in a place without a particular purpose, to linger or loiter. It can also mean spending time with someone casually or aimlessly. Often used to describe people waiting, idling, or socializing without urgency.
example_sentence: They hung around the park all evening. Stop hanging around the shop door. We hung around until the show started. He likes to hang around with his friends.

english_meaning: To delay taking action or making a decision. To remain unresolved or held up for a time. To wait before proceeding with a plan. Originally, of a gun, to be slow in firing after the trigger is pulled.
example_sentence: Let's hang fire until we hear from the lawyers. The project has hung fire for several months. She decided to hang fire before replying to the offer. The old musket would sometimes hang fire in damp weather.

english_meaning: To wait or hold tightly. It means asking someone to wait a moment or hold something firmly for safety or support.
example_sentence: Hang on, I am coming. Hang on to the rail. Can you hang on for a minute. She told him to hang on while she checked the report.

english_meaning: To listen very carefully, with great interest and attention to everything someone says. It describes being deeply focused or captivated by a speaker’s words.
synonyms: ["Listen attentively","Be captivated","Be engrossed","Pay close attention","Be absorbed"]
example_sentence: Students hung on every word of the professor. The students hung on every word their teacher said during the lecture. The audience hung on every word of the famous poet’s speech. She hung on every word he spoke, as if his voice gave her hope. The children hung on every word of the storyteller’s tale.

english_meaning: To spend time casually with friends or in a particular place, often for leisure or social purposes. To stay somewhere for a while without a specific purpose.
example_sentence: They hang out at the café daily. We used to hang out after school. He hangs out with his cousins. Let’s hang out this weekend.

english_meaning: A lingering effect, usually after drinking alcohol or an event. To remain as a worry or threat. It means something unpleasant continuing to affect someone’s mind or a situation.
example_sentence: The hang over of the financial crisis affected small businesses for years. Old disputes left a hang over of tension in the office. He woke up with a hang over after the wedding party. Too much beer left her with a terrible hang over. A dark cloud hung over the city before the storm.

english_meaning: To end a call or hang something. It means disconnecting a phone call or placing clothes or objects on a hook or hanger.
example_sentence: She hung up the phone quickly. Hang up your coat. He hung up without saying goodbye. Please hang up your jacket neatly.

english_meaning: A robe designed to be hung on a hook or hanger, often used after bathing or in a bedroom. A garment kept on a wall hook for easy access and quick wear. A loose gown that hangs from a rack or door when not in use. A robe stored by hanging rather than folding to preserve its shape. An informal term for a bathrobe or dressing gown kept on a peg.
example_sentence: She wrapped herself in a soft hang up robe after her shower. He kept his hang up robe on the bathroom door. A cozy hang up robe was waiting for guests in the hotel room. Please put the hang up robe back on its hook.

english_meaning: Secret, dishonest, or improper behavior, especially in romantic or financial matters.
example_sentence: The manager was fired because of some financial hanky panky in the accounts. The tabloid suggested there was hanky panky between the actor and his co star. The teacher warned the students not to try any hanky panky during the exam. The police found evidence of hanky panky in the business deal.

english_meaning: Lacking any obvious principle of organisation. Done without proper planning or order. Random and not carefully thought out. Marked by carelessness or lack of method.
example_sentence: His work was done in a haphazard manner. The files were arranged in a haphazard way on the table. They made haphazard attempts to solve the problem. The construction looked haphazard and unsafe. Her haphazard approach to study led to poor results.

english_meaning: In a way that lacks order or planning. Without method or organization. In a random or careless manner. By chance rather than design.
example_sentence: Books were stacked haphazardly on the floor. He answered the questions haphazardly without thinking. The boxes were placed haphazardly in the storeroom. She wrote her notes haphazardly during the lecture. Decisions taken haphazardly often lead to failure.

english_meaning: The fear of being touched. It is a specific phobia where a person feels extreme discomfort, anxiety, or panic when someone touches them, even in harmless or casual situations.
example_sentence: She avoided handshakes because of her haphephobia. His haphephobia made it difficult for him to sit in crowded buses. Even a pat on the back could trigger panic for someone with haphephobia. Therapy helped him manage his haphephobia over time.

english_meaning: Unlucky and deserving of pity. Suffering repeated misfortune through no fault of one's own. Unfortunate in a way that often seems helpless or pitiful. Having bad luck in a situation one cannot control.
example_sentence: The hapless traveller lost his passport on the first day. A hapless goalkeeper watched the ball slip through his hands. She felt sorry for the hapless victims of the flood. The hapless team lost every match of the season.

english_meaning: Having a single set of unpaired chromosomes in a cell. Describing a cell or organism with half the usual number of chromosomes. A cell, such as a sperm or egg cell, that contains one set of chromosomes. Relating to the single chromosome condition found in gametes.
example_sentence: Sperm and egg cells are haploid. The haploid number in humans is twenty-three. Fertilisation joins two haploid cells to form a diploid one. Many fungi spend most of their life cycle in a haploid state.

english_meaning: A person who is completely satisfied with their situation or circumstances. Someone who is content and has no complaints about their current state. An individual who feels joyful and comfortable in a particular environment. A thoroughly pleased and agreeable person, especially in a group setting.
synonyms: ["Contented Person","Satisfied Individual","Cheerful Soul","Joyful Person","Pleased Individual","Glad Camper","Merrymaker","Optimist"]
example_sentence: After getting the promotion, he was one happy camper. Give her a good book and a cup of tea, and she is a happy camper. Since we fixed the air conditioning, everyone in the office is a happy camper. As long as he has his guitar, he remains a happy camper anywhere.

english_meaning: Relating to the sense of touch. Involving or based on the perception of objects by touch. Concerned with tactile sensations, especially in technology and design. Used in devices that simulate the sense of touch.
example_sentence: The phone gives haptic feedback when you type. Haptic technology is widely used in modern gaming. The doctor used a haptic device for remote surgery. Haptic sensors improve the user experience in virtual reality. Engineers are developing advanced haptic gloves.

english_meaning: To give a long, angry, or passionate speech. A long, aggressive speech. An angry or passionate speech meant to convince or scold others.
example_sentence: The manager harangued the team for missing deadlines. The politician delivered a long harangue against corruption. The teacher’s harangue about discipline made the students silent. She harangued her team for being late to the meeting. He gave a harangue on the importance of honesty. The coach harangued the players after their poor performance.

english_meaning: To persistently annoy, trouble, or torment someone. To pressure or intimidate a person repeatedly. To subject someone to aggressive behaviour or unwanted attention. To make repeated small-scale attacks on an enemy.
example_sentence: She complained that her colleague was harassing her at work. Bullies often harass weaker students at school. The army harassed enemy supply lines. Reporters harassed the actor outside his home. He was punished for harassing customers on the phone.

english_meaning: To give shelter or refuge to someone or something. To keep (a thought or feeling) in one’s mind secretly especially a negative one like anger or suspicion. A place on the coast where ships and boats can safely dock or stay protected from rough water. A place of shelter or safety.
example_sentence: The ship entered the harbour after a long voyage. Fishermen keep their boats in the harbour during storms. He still harbours anger towards his old friend. The island once harboured many pirates.

english_meaning: Fixed or strict rule that cannot be changed. Sometimes used to mean something definite or firmly established without flexibility.
example_sentence: There are no hard and fast rules about how to raise children. The company has a hard and fast policy on attendance. You cannot make hard and fast judgments about people you just met. Laws should guide us, but they should not always be hard and fast.

english_meaning: Used to express mock sympathy or to say 'too bad' about someone's misfortune. A situation where things have not gone as planned or luck is poor. A stiff or firm variety of cheese such as cheddar or parmesan. A phrase indicating that one must simply accept an unpleasant outcome. An old-fashioned British slang expression for bad luck.
synonyms: ["Tough luck","Bad luck","Misfortune","Pity","Shame","Calamity","Adversity","Hard lines","Rotten luck","Ill luck","Firm cheese","Aged cheese"]
example_sentence: If you didn't get a ticket in time, well, hard cheese. It is hard cheese that he lost his job just before the holidays. You missed the bus? Hard cheese, you'll have to walk now. This recipe specifically calls for a grated hard cheese like Pecorino.

english_meaning: A condition of severe suffering, difficulty, or deprivation. A state of great struggle, especially due to lack of resources. Pain, trouble, or misfortune experienced over a period of time. Tough conditions that test endurance.
example_sentence: The family faced great hardship after losing their home. He overcame many hardships to achieve success. Hardship taught him the value of patience. Many people endure financial hardship during inflation. Soldiers endure hardships during long missions.

english_meaning: The physical parts and machinery of a computer, such as the keyboard, screen, and processor. Tools, equipment, and metal goods such as nails, locks, and hinges sold in a shop. Heavy military equipment, including weapons and vehicles. Any solid, physical equipment used to carry out a task, as opposed to programs or ideas.
example_sentence: The office is upgrading its computer hardware this year. You can buy nails and screws at the hardware store. The army displayed its latest military hardware at the parade. A good program is useless without reliable hardware.

english_meaning: A fast-running mammal similar to a rabbit but larger, with longer ears and legs. An animal often associated with speed in folk tales. To run or move very quickly. To hurry along at high speed.
example_sentence: A hare ran across the field at incredible speed. The boys saw a hare hiding in the bushes. He hared down the street to catch the bus. The story of the tortoise and the hare teaches us patience. Hares are usually shy and avoid humans.

english_meaning: Foolish and unlikely to succeed. Showing poor judgement and little thought. Rash, silly or impractical in nature. Describing a person who is scatterbrained.
example_sentence: He came up with another hare-brained scheme to get rich. The plan was hare-brained from the start. Her hare-brained idea nearly cost them everything. Do not waste money on such hare-brained ventures.

english_meaning: Physical or mental damage or injury. To hurt, damage, or cause injury to someone or something. A bad effect on health or well-being. Damage caused to a person or thing.
example_sentence: The storm caused great harm to the crops. He did not mean any harm by his words. Too much sugar can harm your teeth. She was lucky to escape without harm.

english_meaning: Causing damage, injury, or bad effects. Likely to hurt or damage someone or something. Dangerous to health or well-being. Having a negative effect.
example_sentence: Smoking is harmful to your health. The chemicals in the river are harmful to fish. Excessive sun exposure can be harmful to the skin. The report warned about harmful effects of pollution.

english_meaning: The quality of being harmful. The state or fact of causing damage. The degree to which something can cause injury or bad effects.
example_sentence: Scientists studied the harmfulness of the new chemical. The harmfulness of smoking is well known. They tested the harmfulness of the pesticide. Public awareness about the harmfulness of junk food is growing.

english_meaning: In a way that causes harm or damage. In a manner that is dangerous or damaging. So as to produce a bad effect.
example_sentence: The factory harmfully polluted the river. He behaved harmfully toward his colleagues. The chemical spread harmfully through the soil. She spoke harmfully about her friends.

english_meaning: Not able or likely to cause harm. Safe and not dangerous. Innocent and unlikely to offend or hurt anyone.
example_sentence: The spider in the garden is completely harmless. It was just a harmless joke. The snake in the picture is harmless to humans. She kept a harmless little dog as a pet.

english_meaning: Agreement or peaceful arrangement. A state where different elements exist together without conflict, creating balance and a pleasing result. It can refer to relationships, sounds, colors, or ideas that complement each other.
example_sentence: They lived together in perfect harmony. He imagined a society in which all races lived together in harmony. The choir sang in perfect harmony. Living in harmony with nature is important for sustainability. Their opinions are in harmony with each other. The colors in the painting are in harmony.

english_meaning: A set of straps used to control or hold an animal, especially a horse. Equipment used to attach a person safely to something. To control and use the natural force or power of something. To put a harness on an animal. To exploit a resource productively.
example_sentence: The horse was fitted with a new leather harness. Workers must wear a safety harness at construction sites. Scientists are trying to harness solar energy more efficiently. We must harness modern technology for development. The farmer harnessed the bull to the cart.

english_meaning: A large musical instrument with strings stretched across a triangular frame, played by plucking. To talk or write persistently and tediously about a particular subject. To dwell on something repeatedly.
example_sentence: She learned to play the harp at a young age. The angel was shown playing a golden harp. He keeps harping on the same old issue. Please stop harping about my mistakes. The harp produced soft and soothing music.

english_meaning: To keep talking about something again and again, usually in an annoying way. To complain continuously about something. To emphasize one point repeatedly. To dwell on past mistakes or problems. To lecture someone again and again about the same issue.
synonyms: ["Go on about","Dwell on","Keep repeating","Nag about","Rant about","Keep emphasizing"]
example_sentence: He keeps harping on about my mistakes in front of everyone. Stop harping on the past and focus on the present. She harped on the importance of punctuality during the meeting. My father always harps on about saving money.

english_meaning: A heavy farming implement with spikes or discs used to break up and level ploughed soil. To draw a harrow over land in order to prepare it for sowing. To cause someone acute distress, pain, or torment. To wound the feelings deeply and repeatedly.
example_sentence: The farmer used a harrow to level the field before sowing. They harrowed the land after the first rains. The harrowing details of the accident shocked everyone. Memories of the war continued to harrow him.

english_meaning: Cruel, severe, or cruel in a way that is hard to endure. It describes something that is unpleasant to the senses, like a loud noise or bright light. It can also refer to conditions that are difficult and uncomfortable.
example_sentence: The desert has a very harsh climate during the summer months. She spoke in a harsh tone that surprised everyone in the room. The prisoner received a harsh punishment for his crimes. The bright fluorescent lights felt harsh on my tired eyes.

english_meaning: A troublesome, inconvenient, or annoying situation. An argument or disagreement. To annoy, harass, or pressure someone repeatedly.
