example_sentence: Renewing my passport turned out to be a real hassle. She did not want the hassle of moving to a new city. Stop hassling me about the deadline. The two drivers hassled over the parking space.

english_meaning: A thick cushion used as a footstool or low seat. A cushion used for kneeling during worship, especially in a church. A firm clump or tuft of grass found in marshy or boggy ground.
example_sentence: She knelt on the hassock during the church service. He rested his feet on the hassock beside the sofa. The old chapel's hassock was embroidered by hand. We stepped carefully between the grassy hassocks in the marsh.

english_meaning: An archaic second-person singular form of have, used with thou. An old literary form meaning you have.
example_sentence: Thou hast spoken wisely, said the old sage. What hast thou done with the treasure? Thou hast been a loyal friend to me. Where hast thou traveled these many years?

english_meaning: Excessive speed or urgency of movement or action. Swiftness of motion or activity without due care. To hurry or move with speed.
example_sentence: In his haste to leave, he forgot his keys on the table. Haste makes waste, so take your time to do it properly. She wrote the letter in great haste before the post office closed. The doctor acted with haste to save the injured patient.

english_meaning: Acting quickly leads to mistakes. Doing things in a hurry causes waste of time, effort, or resources. If you do something too quickly or carelessly, you are likely to make mistakes, and in the end, it will take more time or cause loss.
example_sentence: He failed because haste makes waste. He finished the project in a hurry, but made many mistakes, truly, haste makes waste. Don’t rush your homework; remember, haste makes waste. She cooked the meal too quickly and burned it, haste makes waste. They built the house in a hurry, and now it needs repairs, haste makes waste.

english_meaning: To move, act, or travel quickly. To cause something to happen sooner or proceed more rapidly. To hurry toward a place, action, or result.
example_sentence: She hastened to finish her work before dinner. He hastened his pace when the storm approached. Warm weather may hasten the ripening of the fruit. They hastened to apologize after the misunderstanding.

english_meaning: With excessive speed or urgency. In a hurried manner, often without enough thought, care, or preparation. Quickly because time is limited.
example_sentence: He hastily packed his bags and left for the airport. The report was written hastily and contained several errors. She hastily agreed without reading the contract. They hastily changed their plans when the weather worsened.

english_meaning: Said made or done very quickly. Acting or deciding too quickly without enough thought.
example_sentence: The army beat a hasty retreat. Let's not make any hasty decision. Perhaps I was too hasty in rejecting his offer.

english_meaning: A series of three successes or wins, especially in a row. The feat of scoring three goals in a single game of football or hockey. Taking three wickets with three consecutive deliveries in cricket. Any three consecutive achievements within a short period. A triple accomplishment in professional sports.
example_sentence: The striker celebrated his hat-trick after scoring the final goal. Our team achieved a hat-trick of championship titles this year. The bowler took a stunning hat-trick in the final over. She completed a hat-trick of wins in the annual tennis tournament.

english_meaning: To emerge from an egg or to cause young birds or fish to emerge. It also means to conspire or create a secret plan.It refers to an opening or door in a deck, floor, or ceiling.
example_sentence: The baby turtles will hatch and head toward the ocean tonight. They began to hatch a plan to surprise their friend on his birthday. The submarine captain ordered the hatch to be closed immediately. We watched the chicks hatch from their shells in the incubator.

english_meaning: A small axe with a short handle, mainly used for cutting wood, branches, or small logs. In a figurative sense, it refers to hidden hostility or conflict, especially in the phrase bury the hatchet which means to end a disagreement.
example_sentence: He used a hatchet to cut firewood for the camp. The gardener carried a hatchet while trimming trees. After years of conflict, they decided to bury the hatchet. The story revealed the political hatchet buried behind polite words.

english_meaning: Strong feeling of intense dislike or deep hostility. A very strong and often lasting feeling of dislike, anger, or hostility toward someone or something. It may come from personal experiences, beliefs, jealousy, or conflict.
example_sentence: His hatred for injustice made him stand up for the poor. Hatred can destroy relationships and create distance between people. She tried to overcome her hatred and forgive others. Years of conflict increased hatred between the two communities.

english_meaning: An expression used to praise or show admiration for someone's achievement. A way of giving respect or acknowledgement. Used to congratulate or honour someone. A salute to someone's hard work or talent.
example_sentence: Hats off to the doctors who served during the pandemic. Hats off to her for completing the project on time. Hats off to the teachers for their dedication. Hats off to the team for winning the championship. Hats off to the volunteers who helped the flood victims.

english_meaning: In a manner that shows excessive pride or arrogance. With a tone or expression that suggests one is superior to others. Acting in a way that is disdainful or scornful of others. Behaving with an air of self-importance that disregards the feelings of those around. Displaying a sense of condescension in one's actions or speech.
example_sentence: She looked at the waiter haughtily when he brought the wrong order. The king spoke haughtily to the messengers from the rival kingdom. He walked haughtily past his former colleagues after his promotion. The actress answered the reporter's personal questions very haughtily.

english_meaning: The quality of being arrogantly superior and disdainful. A state of excessive pride that results in looking down on others. The display of an overbearing or conceited attitude. The characteristic of having a high opinion of oneself while devaluing others. A mannerism that reflects a sense of elite status and aloofness.
example_sentence: Her haughtiness made it difficult for her to make new friends. The nobleman's haughtiness offended everyone present at the banquet. Behind his mask of haughtiness lay a deep sense of insecurity. The teacher corrected the student's haughtiness with a gentle reminder about humility.

english_meaning: Arrogantly superior and disdainful. Showing a feeling of being better than others. Proud and looking down on others. Behaving in a way that shows excessive pride.
example_sentence: She gave him a haughty look and walked away. His haughty attitude annoyed everyone in the office. The queen had a haughty manner of speaking. He is too haughty to admit his mistakes. Her haughty smile showed that she felt superior.

english_meaning: To pull or drag something heavy with great effort. To transport goods, usually by road or rail, over a distance. A quantity of something obtained, especially illegally or with difficulty. The distance covered on a journey, often described as long or short.
example_sentence: They hauled the boat onto the sandy beach. Trucks haul coal from the mine to the port. Police recovered a large haul of stolen jewellery. It is a long haul from Karachi to Islamabad by road.

english_meaning: The fleshy part of the body about the hip and buttock of an animal or a human. A leg and loin of an animal, especially a deer, supplied as meat. Either side of an arch between the springing and the crown. The hindquarters of a quadruped.
example_sentence: The dog sat on its haunches waiting for a treat. He bought a large haunch of venison for the feast. The horse was branded on its right haunch. The arch was supported firmly at each haunch.

english_meaning: If a ghost or spirit visits a place regularly. To trouble or disturb someone constantly, especially with memories. To stay in a place often. A place that someone visits frequently. To linger persistently in the mind.
example_sentence: People say that an old ghost haunts this castle. The memories of the accident still haunt him. The café was his favourite haunt during college days. Fear of failure haunted her for years. This forest is believed to be haunted by spirits.

english_meaning: Of high social standing or quality, especially in fashion. Elegant and stylish, often in a sophisticated way. Used to describe high-class or refined things, often in French-influenced English. High, lofty, or elevated.
example_sentence: She loves wearing haut couture dresses. The boutique sells haut fashion items. He moves in haut society circles. The hotel is famous for its haut cuisine. The film captured the haut lifestyle of Paris.

word: Have a bone to pick with someone
english_meaning: To have a complaint or disagreement with someone that needs to be discussed or settled. To “have a bone to pick with someone” means you are annoyed or dissatisfied with a person because of something they did, and you want to talk about it or confront them to resolve the issue. It usually suggests a personal complaint or unresolved argument.
synonyms: ["Have an issue with someone","Have a complaint","Be unhappy with someone","Want to confront someone","Hold a grudge (slightly stronger meaning)"]
antonyms: ["Be satisfied with someone","Agree with someone","Be at peace with someone","Have no issues","Be on good terms"]
example_sentence: I have a bone to pick with you about yesterday’s meeting. She has a bone to pick with her manager over the salary issue. He came to my office because he had a bone to pick with me. Do you have a bone to pick with me, or are we okay now?

english_meaning: To suddenly have a very good idea. A moment when someone suddenly thinks of an excellent or clever solution to a problem or an innovative idea.
example_sentence: I suddenly had a brainwave and knew how to fix the broken engine. She had a brainwave about how to improve the marketing strategy. During the meeting, he had a brainwave that impressed everyone. I had a brainwave and decided to ask for help from an expert.

english_meaning: To stop being friendly with someone because of a disagreement. To experience a serious disagreement with someone, especially a friend or family member, which leads to a break in the relationship or loss of friendship.
example_sentence: They had a falling out over money issues and stopped talking to each other. She had a falling out with her best friend after a misunderstanding. The brothers had a falling out about their business partnership. We had a falling out last year, but now we are friends again.

word: Have a frog in your throat
english_meaning: To have difficulty speaking because your throat feels dry or blocked. To experience temporary hoarseness or a loss of voice.
synonyms: ["Lose One's Voice","Be Hoarse","Have A Husky Voice","Speak Croakily","Have A Tickle In The Throat","Have A Dry Throat","Be Rasping","Suffer From Hoarseness"]
antonyms: ["Speak Clearly","Have A Clear Voice","Be Articulate","Speak Smoothly","Have Perfect Diction","Communicate Clearly","Vocalize Perfectly","Speak Fluently"]
example_sentence: I had a frog in my throat and had to cough before answering. She couldn't finish her speech because she had a frog in her throat. Excuse me, I seem to have a frog in my throat today. Drink some water if you have a frog in your throat.

english_meaning: To suddenly understand something that was confusing before. To get a bright new idea all at once. To experience a flash of insight or realization. To find the answer to a problem in a sudden moment of clarity.
synonyms: ["Have an epiphany","See the light","Realize suddenly","Have a brainwave","Have an aha moment","Get an insight","Dawn on someone"]
antonyms: ["Be confused","Remain puzzled","Draw a blank","Be in the dark","Miss the point","Fail to understand"]
example_sentence: I had a light bulb moment while walking home from work. She had a light bulb moment and finally solved the puzzle. During the meeting he had a light bulb moment about cutting costs. Reading that book made me have a light bulb moment about my career.

word: Have a lot on your plate
english_meaning: To be very busy with many tasks or responsibilities at the same time. To be mentally overloaded with responsibilities. To manage multiple urgent tasks simultaneously. To feel pressure due to workload or commitments.
example_sentence: She cannot join the meeting today because she has a lot on her plate. The manager has a lot on his plate during the project deadline. I can’t take new work right now because I already have a lot on my plate. He looks stressed because he has a lot on his plate at home and office.

english_meaning: To have a strong liking or fondness for sweet foods such as cakes and chocolate. To particularly enjoy sugary or dessert items. To crave sweets or sugary treats regularly. To be inclined toward eating sweets.
example_sentence: I have a sweet tooth, so I can't resist chocolate cake. My grandmother has a sweet tooth and always keeps candy at home. He admits he has a sweet tooth and eats dessert every night. Children usually have a sweet tooth from a very young age.

english_meaning: To be narrow-minded or unwilling to consider other perspectives. The phrase comes from horse racing, where blinkers are placed on a horse’s eyes to prevent it from seeing sideways and getting distracted. Figuratively, it means a person is focused only on one viewpoint or course of action, ignoring other possibilities or information.
example_sentence: People who have blinkers on can’t see reality. He always has blinkers on when judging others. Politicians often have blinkers on during debates. Don’t have blinkers on while making decisions.

english_meaning: To benefit from two conflicting choices, arguments, or situations at the same time. To avoid the disadvantages of a decision while keeping its advantages. To hold two inconsistent positions for personal gain.
synonyms: ["Want it both ways","Play both sides","Straddle the fence","Equivocate","Hedge one's bets"]
example_sentence: You can't have it both ways; either you join us or you stay home. He wants low prices and high wages, but nobody can have it both ways. The company tried to have it both ways with its environmental promises. Critics said the minister was attempting to have it both ways.

english_meaning: To enjoy oneself wildly or extravagantly, especially by partying, drinking, or going out. To live life intensely and indulge in celebrations.
example_sentence: They went to Ibiza to have it large for a week. It was Friday night, so everyone was ready to have it large. He loves to have it large on the weekends with his friends. We decided to hit the town and have it large.

english_meaning: To have no dealings or relationship with a person. To refuse to accept, tolerate, or engage with someone or something. To keep completely apart from an idea or practice one disapproves of.
synonyms: ["Want no truck with","Shun","Avoid","Reject","Disown","Boycott","Have nothing to do with"]
example_sentence: He has no truck with gossip of any kind. The committee has no truck with members who break the rules. My grandmother had no truck with modern gadgets. They have no truck with anyone who cheats customers.

english_meaning: To refuse to accept, allow, or tolerate something. To reject a suggestion, excuse, or behaviour firmly. To receive no share of something.
example_sentence: I offered to pay, but he would have none of it. The committee will have none of this delay. She had none of the profits from the sale. Their father would have none of such rudeness at the table.

word: Have one foot in the grave
english_meaning: To be very old or so ill that death seems near. To be close to dying. To be in a very weak or failing condition. Used humorously to say that someone is getting old.
synonyms: ["At death's door","Dying","Failing","On one's last legs","Near the end","Ailing"]
antonyms: ["In the prime of life","Healthy","Thriving","Robust","Full of life","Youthful"]
example_sentence: He is ninety and has one foot in the grave, yet he still gardens daily. The old man looked as if he had one foot in the grave. Stop teasing me about my age; I do not have one foot in the grave yet. After the illness, she seemed to have one foot in the grave.

word: Have someone by the short and curlies
english_meaning: To have complete power or control over someone so they cannot resist or escape.
example_sentence: The manager has the employees by the short and curlies because he knows about their secret mistake. Once the company took his passport, they had him by the short and curlies. The politician has the media by the short and curlies through his financial influence. She has her business partner by the short and curlies because she controls all the legal documents.

word: Have the courage of your convictions
english_meaning: To act according to one's beliefs or values, especially despite criticism, danger, or opposition. It means standing up for what you believe is right regardless of social pressure.
synonyms: ["Stand by one's guns","Stick to one's principles","Be true to oneself","Hold firm","Stand strong"]
example_sentence: She had the courage of her convictions and resigned from the unethical company. It takes time to develop the courage of your convictions in the face of widespread dissent. He always had the courage of his convictions, speaking out against injustice. You must have the courage of your convictions if you want to lead real change.

word: Have your feet on the ground
english_meaning: To be sensible, practical, and realistic. To understand ordinary life and real conditions. To remain emotionally balanced and not be carried away by hopes, pride, or success
antonyms: ["Be Unrealistic","Have One's Head in the Clouds","Be Impractical","Be Deluded"]
example_sentence: Despite her sudden fame, she still has her feet on the ground. A good leader has his feet on the ground and listens to ordinary people. He has his feet on the ground when making financial decisions. Even after winning the lottery, they had their feet on the ground.

word: Have your nose in a book
english_meaning: To be deeply absorbed in reading. To spend most of one's time reading books. To be so busy reading that one ignores the surroundings. Describing a person who constantly reads.
synonyms: ["Be engrossed","Read avidly","Be absorbed","Study","Pore over","Be buried in reading","Devour books","Be immersed","Concentrate","Peruse"]
example_sentence: She always has her nose in a book during the holidays. He had his nose in a book and did not hear the bell. Even at parties, my brother has his nose in a book. The child sat quietly with her nose in a book all afternoon.

english_meaning: To undergo a surgical procedure in which the fallopian tubes are blocked or cut for permanent contraception. To be sterilised through tubal ligation. To have an operation that prevents future pregnancy. A medical expression for female sterilisation.
synonyms: ["Be sterilised","Undergo tubal ligation","Have surgery","Be operated on","Undergo sterilisation","Be made infertile","Have contraception surgery","Be rendered sterile","Undergo ligation","Have a permanent procedure"]
antonyms: ["Conceive","Remain fertile","Reverse sterilisation","Be reversible","Bear children","Stay fertile","Undergo reversal","Become pregnant","Retain fertility","Avoid surgery"]
example_sentence: After her fourth child, she decided to have her tubes tied. The doctor explained the risks of having your tubes tied. Many women have their tubes tied only after careful counselling. She had her tubes tied last year and has no regrets.

english_meaning: To face a difficult or demanding task ahead. To have a hard job that will require great effort. To be confronted with a challenge that is barely manageable. To have plenty to do in a limited time.
synonyms: ["Face a challenge","Have a tough job","Be hard pressed","Struggle","Have a tall order","Be up against it","Have a big task","Toil","Be stretched","Grapple"]
antonyms: ["Have it easy","Breeze through","Coast","Relax","Idle","Find simple","Sail through","Rest","Be free","Have little to do"]
example_sentence: The new manager has her work cut out turning the company around. With only three days left, we have our work cut out. He will have his work cut out convincing the committee. The team has its work cut out against the league champions.

english_meaning: The people who are wealthy and those who are poor. A phrase contrasting privileged groups with deprived groups in society. The division between those who own resources and those who lack them. A general expression for economic inequality.
synonyms: ["Rich and poor","Wealthy and needy","Privileged and deprived","Upper and lower classes"]
example_sentence: The gap between the haves and the have-nots keeps widening. Education can reduce the distance between the haves and the have-nots. The city clearly divides the haves and the have-nots. Politicians often promise to help the have-nots.

english_meaning: To cause chaos or destruction. Widespread destruction or chaos. Severe damage, disorder, or confusion, often causing disruption in a situation or environment. It can describe physical destruction or metaphorical turmoil.
example_sentence: The disease can play havoc with the body's immune system. These insects can wreak havoc on crops. This new virus has created havoc for computer users. The sudden strike caused havoc in the stock market. The children created havoc in the classroom. The new policy led to havoc in the local transport system.

english_meaning: To try to sell things by going from place to place asking people to buy them. A strong fast bird of prey. One who urges or attempts to cause a war. A type of large bird that catches small birds and animals for food.
example_sentence: He made a living hawking cleaning products from door to door. He waited, watching her like a hawk (= watching her very closely). He waited, watching her like a hawk (= watching her very closely).

english_meaning: A person who makes money by selling goods, going from place to place and asking people to buy them. A person who offers goods for sale by shouting his or her wares in the street or going from door to door. A person who hunts with hawks or other birds of prey.
example_sentence: He worked as a street hawker, selling cheap lighters at two for a pound. The hawker cried his wares throughout the town. Newspaper Hawker

english_meaning: A thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship. A heavy line used in nautical operations. A strong cord typically made of fibre or steel used at sea.
example_sentence: The sailors tied the ship to the dock with a heavy hawser. A thick hawser snapped during the storm. The tugboat pulled the ship using a strong hawser. Hawsers are made of strong synthetic fibres these days. The hawser was wrapped around the metal post.

english_meaning: Out of control; not working properly; in a state of disorder or confusion. When something stops functioning normally or goes wrong unexpectedly.
example_sentence: The computer went haywire and deleted all my files. When the teacher left the class, the students went haywire. The weather has gone haywire due to climate change. My plans went haywire because of the sudden rain.

english_meaning: A potential source of danger or harm. Something that can cause adverse effects to health, property, or the environment. It can also refer to a chance or risk taken in a game or venture.
example_sentence: The bridge was closed because it was deemed a structural hazard. Careless disposal of chemicals is a major environmental hazard. I would hazard a guess that the train will be late today. Tall trees near power lines can become a serious hazard during a storm.

english_meaning: Involving danger or risk. Likely to cause harm or injury. Unsafe or risky in nature. Posing a threat to health, safety, or property.
example_sentence: Working with chemicals can be hazardous to health. Driving in heavy fog is hazardous. The factory produces hazardous waste. Hazardous materials must be stored carefully. Mountaineering is a hazardous sport.

english_meaning: Slightly unclear, foggy, or not sharp. Something that is not clear or sharp. It can refer to physical visibility, like weather, or to thoughts, memories, or ideas that are not well defined.
example_sentence: The mountains looked hazy in the early morning. I have only a hazy memory of that event. The sky became hazy due to pollution. His explanation was hazy and difficult to understand.

word: He who can’t be advised can also not be helped
english_meaning: A person who refuses to listen to good advice cannot be guided or supported. If someone ignores warnings and guidance, others cannot fix the consequences for them.
example_sentence: You can’t save him—he who can’t be advised can’t be helped. The saying means stubborn people ruin themselves. He lost everything because he wouldn’t listen. The wise listen, the foolish don’t.

english_meaning: The upper part of the human body, or the front part of an animal's body, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth. The mind, intelligence, or ability to think clearly. A person who leads or is in charge of a group, organization, or institution. The top or front part of something. To lead or be in charge of something. To move in a particular direction. To hit a ball with the head in football.
example_sentence: She turned her head to see who was calling her. He is the head of the marketing department. Use your head before making such an important decision. We decided to head home before the storm arrived.

english_meaning: Using both logic (head) and emotion (heart) together in thinking or making decisions.
example_sentence: A good leader makes decisions with both head and heart. She followed her head and heart before choosing her career. To live a happy life, you must keep your head and heart in harmony. His head told him to walk away, but his heart wanted to stay.

english_meaning: To return to the place you came from. To start going back toward an earlier location, situation, or direction, usually after finishing something or deciding not to continue forward.
example_sentence: We headed back home after the trip. After the party, we decided to head back home. It’s getting late, we should head back now. They had to head back because they forgot their tickets.

english_meaning: To go toward a place or move in a particular direction. To start moving toward a destination or goal, either physically or figuratively. It can describe traveling to a place or moving toward a situation, result, or future outcome.
synonyms: ["Go towards","Move to","Make for","Be bound for","Approach","Go to","Travel toward","Proceed"]
example_sentence: We decided to head for the airport early in the morning. After work, she headed for home to rest. The hikers are heading for the mountain trail. Without planning, the project may head for failure.

english_meaning: Not paying attention to reality. A person who is dreamy, unrealistic, distracted, or lost in thoughts and imagination instead of focusing on what is happening around them.
example_sentence: He walked into the meeting with his head in the clouds and missed the main point. She often has her head in the clouds, dreaming about travel and adventure. If you keep your head in the clouds, you will miss important details. The teacher warned him to stop having his head in the clouds and focus on his studies.

english_meaning: To prevent something from happening or to leave for a place before others. It is often used for stopping trouble early or starting a journey.
example_sentence: The manager acted quickly to head off the crisis. She headed off early to avoid traffic. Police were able to head off the protest. We should head off before it gets dark.

english_meaning: To deal with a problem directly and bravely without avoiding it. To face a situation, problem, or opponent directly with courage and honesty, without delay or evasion.
example_sentence: She decided to head on the challenge. He faced the issue head on. The team tackled the problem head on. You must meet your fears head on.

english_meaning: To leave a place or to start a journey. To depart from a location, often with a specific purpose, destination, or plan in mind.
example_sentence: We are heading out for dinner. He headed out early in the morning. She headed out of the office quietly. They headed out toward the mountains

english_meaning: Completely, deeply, or totally, especially in love. To be completely in love with someone. To be fully involved or absorbed in something. Sometimes used to describe a chaotic or disordered situation.
example_sentence: She fell head over heels in love with her classmate. He is head over heels involved in his new business project. They turned the house head over heels while searching for the keys. After hearing the news, his life went head over heels.

english_meaning: A title or line of information at the top of a page, document, table, or email. The top section of a document or webpage. A block of data placed before the main content in computing. A person or thing that heads something in older or specialized use.
example_sentence: Put the date in the header of the document. The table header should describe each column. The website header contains the logo and menu. The email header showed the sender's address.

english_meaning: To recruit a professional directly from another company. To search for top talent for a specific position. To attract highly qualified employees through targeted recruitment. To seek out experts or specialists rather than waiting for job applications. Historically, the word had a different meaning in some tribal cultures, referring to taking an enemy's head after battle, but in modern business English it usually refers to recruiting talented people.
example_sentence: The tech giant tried to headhunt the software engineer from a rival firm. They plan to headhunt a new CEO with international experience. Many companies use agencies to headhunt top talent for leadership roles. She was headhunted for the position while she was still leading another project.

english_meaning: A person or agency that identifies and approaches suitable candidates for high-level jobs. Historically, it also referred to a member of a society who collects the heads of dead enemies as trophies. In business, they serve as intermediaries between employers and potential employees.
example_sentence: The headhunter contacted him regarding a prestigious role in London. A specialized headhunter can help find the perfect niche expert for your team. After years in management, she decided to work as an independent headhunter. The company hired a headhunter to find a replacement for the departing director.

english_meaning: With the head foremost. In a rushed or reckless manner. Without thinking carefully. With great speed and force. Eagerly and quickly into a situation.
example_sentence: He fell headlong into the swimming pool. She rushed headlong into a hasty decision. The driver drove headlong into the wall. They plunged headlong into the new business. He jumped headlong into the river to save the boy.

english_meaning: The channel or pipe that carries water to a water wheel, mill, or turbine. The upstream part of a watercourse leading to the point where the water is used.
example_sentence: Water flows down the headrace to the turbine. The old mill's headrace has been restored. Silt had blocked the headrace after the flood. Engineers widened the headrace to increase power output.

english_meaning: A person who is energetic and highly determined to do what they want. Someone who is stubbornly willful and resistant to advice or direction.
example_sentence: She was too headstrong to listen to her parents' advice. The headstrong young horse refused to be ridden. He is a headstrong manager who insists on doing things his own way. Despite warnings, the headstrong explorer ventured into the dangerous cave.

english_meaning: Progress or movement forward in work, plans or travel. Gradual improvement in a long and difficult process. Any positive change after effort. The progress you make when moving forward in a task, project, goal or journey. It shows improvement or advancement after effort.
example_sentence: We are finally making some headway on the report. The team made little headway because of the bad weather. She worked all night but could not make much headway. The project is slow but we are starting to see headway.

english_meaning: A wind that blows directly against the direction in which someone or something is moving. A wind blowing from the front, opposite to the direction of travel. Any condition that makes success, growth, or progress more difficult. It can also be used figuratively to mean a difficulty, obstacle, challenge, or unfavorable condition that slows progress.
example_sentence: The pilot reported a strong headwind that delayed our arrival by an hour. Cyclists often find it exhausting to pedal against a stiff headwind. High interest rates acted as a major headwind for the housing market last year. The ship struggled to maintain its speed due to the persistent headwind.

english_meaning: Mental effort; work done with the mind rather than the hands. In engineering, the main structure built at the head of a canal or river to control and divert water. Decorative or structural work at the top or head of something.
example_sentence: The job requires more headwork than physical labour. Engineers repaired the canal headwork before the flood season. Careful headwork saved the team a great deal of time. The headwork regulates the flow of water into the fields.

english_meaning: To cure a disease, wound, or injury. To become healthy again after sickness or injury. To reduce emotional pain, sadness, or trauma. To repair or restore something damaged, broken, or divided. To bring peace, reconciliation, or harmony between people or groups.
example_sentence: The medicine helped heal the patient's infection. It took several weeks for the broken bone to heal completely. Time can heal emotional wounds after a difficult experience. Community dialogue helped heal the conflict between the two groups.

english_meaning: Good health is the greatest blessing and more valuable than money or material things. Good health is better than riches. A healthy life brings happiness and success. Physical and mental fitness are priceless. Taking care of health is the key to a better life.
synonyms: ["Good health is priceless","Health comes first","A sound mind in a sound body","Well-being is true wealth"]
antonyms: ["Wealth without health","Sickness is misery","Poor health ruins happiness"]
example_sentence: My grandfather always says, “Health is wealth,” so he walks every morning. After falling sick, Ali realized that health is wealth. Eating healthy food proves that health is wealth. People who exercise regularly understand that health is wealth.

english_meaning: A large untidy collection of things piled together. A large quantity or number of something. To pile things up in a disordered way. To give something in large amounts. An accumulation of items.
example_sentence: There was a heap of clothes on the bed. He has heaps of work to finish today. They heaped praise on the new teacher. The leaves formed a huge heap in the garden. She heaped food on his plate.

english_meaning: The muscular organ that pumps blood through the body. The center of a person's feelings, love, and emotions. The central or most important part of something. Courage, determination, or enthusiasm.
example_sentence: The heart pumps blood to every part of the body. She has a kind and generous heart. The old market lies in the heart of the city. He put his whole heart into the project.

english_meaning: With complete enthusiasm, energy, and devotion. To do something with full passion, sincerity, and involvement. Refers to the deepest emotions, dedication, or true essence of a person or thing.
example_sentence: She worked heart and soul to make the project a success. The teacher puts her heart and soul into helping he students. He is heart and soul devoted to his family. The musicians played with heart and soul, moving everyone to tear

english_meaning: As much as one wants. Until one is fully satisfied or pleased. To the full extent of one's desires. Without any limitation or restraint. In a way that brings complete gratification. To the maximum degree possible.
example_sentence: After months of dieting, he finally ate his favorite cake to his heart's content. The children played in the park to their heart's content until the sun went down. Since the library was empty, she stayed and read to her heart's content. We spent the entire weekend shopping to our heart's content in the city.

english_meaning: A hard and unkind person with no sympathy. Someone who appears emotionally hard and uncaring. Such a person may ignore the suffering, feelings, or needs of others. The phrase compares the human heart with stone to show absence of warmth, love, mercy, or emotional softness.
synonyms: ["Cruel person","Cold hearted person","Merciless person","Unfeeling person","Hard hearted person","Ruthless person"]
antonyms: ["Kind hearted person","Compassionate person","Merciful person","Sympathetic person","Caring person","Soft hearted person"]
example_sentence: The landlord had a heart of stone and refused to help the poor family. Anyone with a heart of stone could ignore the cries of hungry children. She thinks her boss has a heart of stone because he never listens to employees’ problems. Despite the tragedy, the criminal showed a heart of stone and felt no regret.

english_meaning: One of the four flap-like structures that keep blood flowing in one direction through the heart. A valve that opens and closes with each heartbeat. A structure that prevents the backward flow of blood inside the heart.
example_sentence: A heart valve keeps blood moving in one direction. A leaking heart valve can cause tiredness. Surgeons replaced the damaged heart valve. Each heart valve opens with every heartbeat.

english_meaning: Showing warm and friendly feelings. Strong, enthusiastic, and sincere. Large and satisfying, especially of meals. Healthy and full of energy. Wholehearted and genuine.
example_sentence: He gave me a hearty welcome at the airport. They enjoyed a hearty meal after the long journey. She has a hearty laugh that fills the room. The soldiers received a hearty welcome from the public. He gave a hearty handshake to the new employee.

english_meaning: To lift or pull something heavy with great effort. To rise and fall with strong, regular movements. To throw something heavy with force. To utter a deep sound, especially a sigh. To vomit or feel as if one is about to vomit.
example_sentence: They heaved the heavy box onto the truck with great effort. His chest heaved as he tried to catch his breath. She heaved a deep sigh of relief. He heaved the sack of grain over his shoulder. The patient began to heave after taking the medicine.

english_meaning: Strong, repeated efforts to lift or pull something. Acts of vomiting or trying to vomit. Deep breaths or sighs. A common respiratory disease in horses similar to asthma. Up-and-down movements like waves.
example_sentence: After several heaves, they managed to move the rock. The horse suffered from heaves and could not run. His chest heaves after the long run. The patient had violent heaves during the night. The boat heaves with the strong waves.

english_meaning: To interrupt a speaker or performer with shouted comments, questions, or abuse. To harass with persistent rude remarks. To disturb a public speech or event noisily.
example_sentence: Some protesters tried to heckle the minister during his speech. The comedian handled the hecklers very well. They heckled the politician at every public meeting. He was angry when audience members started to heckle him. Hecklers were removed from the auditorium by security.

english_meaning: A metric unit of square measure, equal to 10,000 square meters. The standard unit for measuring large areas of land like farms or parks. An area equivalent to 2·471 acres of land. A derivative unit of the are, equal to 100 ares. A tool for expressing geographical and agricultural surface area. A common measurement used in international real estate and land surveys. A unit symbolized by the abbreviation ha.
synonyms: ["Metric Unit","Land Measure","Surface Area","100 Ares","10000 Square Meters","2.471 Acres","Area Unit","Measurement","Plot Size","Estate Measure","Agricultural Unit","Land Area","Spatial Measure","Metric Acre"]
antonyms: ["Millimeter","Centimeter","Square Inch","Tiny Fragment","Point","Linear Meter","Microscopic Area","Cubic Meter","Non-spatial","Single Dimension"]
example_sentence: The farmer decided to plant wheat on one hectare of his fertile land. The new national park covers over a thousand hectares of dense forest. We need to calculate how many hectares of space the solar farm requires. The land was divided into several small plots of half a hectare each.

english_meaning: Full of incessant or frantic activity. Characterized by intense excitement, confusion, or haste. It can also relate to a fever that causes a flush on the cheeks.
example_sentence: Life in the city is often too hectic for those used to the countryside. The holiday season is always a hectic time for retail workers. I’ve had a really hectic schedule this week with back-to-back meetings. Despite the hectic environment of the stock exchange, he remained focused.

english_meaning: A numerical prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one hundred. Used primarily in scientific and mathematical contexts to multiply a base unit by 102. It represents the quantity of one hundred units of measure. A prefix derived from the Greek word 'hekaton' meaning hundred. It is a standard unit multiplier used within the International System of Units (SI). A term signifying a scale larger than 'deca' but smaller than 'kilo'. A prefix commonly paired with liters, grams, or pascals in specific industries.
example_sentence: The farm produced one hectoliter of olive oil this season. The atmospheric pressure was recorded as one hectopascal. A hectometer is equal to exactly one hundred meters in distance. We use the prefix hecto to denote a hundredfold increase in the base unit.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to 100 grams. One tenth of a kilogram. A unit sometimes used for weighing small quantities of food in Europe.
example_sentence: One hectogram is equal to a hundred grams. The recipe requires three hectograms of flour. Shopkeepers in Italy often sell cheese by the hectogram. He measured out a hectogram of sugar.

english_meaning: A metric unit of length equal to one hundred meters. A measure written as hm, used in land surveying and mapping. One tenth of a kilometer.
synonyms: ["hm","Hundred meters","Metric length unit","Tenth of a kilometer"]
example_sentence: The running track is one hectometer long. Ten hectometers make one kilometer. The map marks each hectometer along the road. Farmers measured the boundary in hectometers.

english_meaning: To talk to someone in a bullying, threatening, or aggressive way. To intimidate by loud and persistent harassment. To bully. To pressurize someone through harsh words. Used to describe a person who tries to control or frighten others by speaking in a domineering, boastful, or scolding manner.
example_sentence: The senior employee used to hector the new staff members constantly. He hectored his younger brother into doing all the housework. The coach hectored the players for their poor performance. She refused to be hectored by anyone, no matter how powerful. The boss tried to hector everyone in the meeting, but no one listened.

english_meaning: To reduce the risk of loss or uncertainty. To speak cautiously or indirectly to avoid commitment. A line of closely planted shrubs or small trees used as a boundary or fence. An investment made to reduce financial risk.
example_sentence: The farmer planted a hedge around his field. Investors often hedge against market uncertainty. She hedged when asked about her future plans. The tall hedge provided privacy for the house.

english_meaning: A person who seeks pleasure as the main goal of life. Someone who believes that pleasure, enjoyment, and comfort are the most important things in life. Such a person focuses on experiences that bring happiness, whether physical, emotional, or sensory.
example_sentence: He lived like a true hedonist, always chasing pleasure and luxury. Some people think a hedonist cannot live a disciplined life. She is not a hedonist, she values hard work more than comfort. The character in the novel is a hedonist who avoids responsibility.

english_meaning: To pay attention to something or take notice. To listen carefully, consider advice, warnings, or instructions, and act accordingly. Careful attention or notice given to something.
example_sentence: You should heed your teacher’s advice. He did not heed the warning and got into trouble. Please heed the instructions before using the machine. She heeded her doctor and took rest.

english_meaning: The rounded back part of the human foot below the ankle. The part of a shoe or sock that covers the back of the foot. The raised part under the back of a shoe. To follow closely behind someone, especially used as a command to a dog.
example_sentence: A blister formed on his heel after the long walk. She wore shoes with a very high heel. The dog walked obediently at his heel. Cracked heels are common during the winter months.

english_meaning: Large, heavy, and powerful. Of considerable size or weight. Large in amount or number, especially of money. Strong and impressive in size or force.
example_sentence: He paid a hefty price for his new car. The boxer is a hefty man with a strong build. They received a hefty fine for breaking the rules. She carried a hefty bag full of books. The company made a hefty profit this year.

english_meaning: Control, dominance or strong influence of one group, country or leader over others. Dominant leadership or influence by one group over others, especially in politics or international relations. A situation where one state, group, institution or ideology holds leading power or influence over others, often shaping their decisions, culture or direction.
example_sentence: The country's economic hegemony shaped trade policies across the region. Cultural hegemony can influence how people think, behave and consume media. The alliance was formed to resist the military hegemony of a powerful neighbor. Some scholars argue that global hegemony shifts from one superpower to another over time.

english_meaning: A young female cow that has not yet had a calf. A young cow being raised for milk production or breeding. In farming, a female bovine animal older than a calf but younger than a mature cow that has produced offspring.
example_sentence: The farmer bought a healthy heifer at the cattle market. Each heifer in the herd is carefully fed and looked after. The young heifer will give milk after she has her first calf. Heifers are usually separated from the older cows on the farm. He proudly showed the visitors his prize-winning heifer.

english_meaning: The measurement of how tall a person or thing is from bottom to top. The distance of something above the ground or sea level. The highest or most intense point of something. A high place or position.
example_sentence: The doctor measured his height and weight. The plane flew at a height of ten thousand metres. The festival was at the height of its popularity. She is afraid of heights.

english_meaning: To make something more intense or greater. To raise the height of something. To increase in degree or amount. To strengthen a feeling, effect, or condition. To make someone more aware of something.
example_sentence: The music heightened the drama of the scene. The news heightened public awareness about the issue. Fear only heightened during the long dark night. They plan to heighten the wall for extra security.

english_meaning: Extremely wicked, evil, or shocking. Deeply criminal, hateful, or morally outrageous. Used to describe acts or crimes that are utterly disgraceful and abominable. Such acts usually arouse strong feelings of horror and condemnation.
example_sentence: Murder is one of the most heinous crimes against humanity. The terrorists were punished for their heinous acts. Such heinous behaviour cannot be tolerated in a civilised society. The court described it as a heinous offence deserving the strictest punishment. People were shocked by the heinous nature of the attack.

english_meaning: Love or preference for sunlight, tendency to seek or thrive in sunlight. The condition or inclination of organisms, especially plants and animals, to seek out sunlight for growth, energy, or comfort. It can also refer to humans who enjoy spending time in sunlight for health or pleasure.
example_sentence: Sunflowers exhibit heliophilia by turning their heads toward the sun. The cat showed heliophilia, lounging in the warm sunlight all afternoon. People with heliophilia often go outside to enjoy sunny days. Certain plants display heliophilia to maximize photosynthesis.

english_meaning: A person, animal, or organism that avoids sunlight, either due to fear, sensitivity, or discomfort. It is often used in psychology for humans or in biology for plants and animals sensitive to bright light.
example_sentence: The heliophobic cat stayed indoors all day to avoid the sun. Some plants are heliophobic and grow better in shaded areas. His heliophobic tendencies made him prefer evening walks over daytime outings. The researcher studied heliophobic behaviors in certain desert animals.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional spiral shape like a corkscrew or spring. A curve that winds around a cylinder or cone at a constant angle. The spiral structure of the DNA molecule. The curved outer rim of the ear. A thing having a spiral form.
example_sentence: The staircase wound upward in a graceful helix. DNA has the shape of a double helix. The metal spring was formed into a tight helix. The snail's shell grows in a spiral helix.

english_meaning: Extremely determined to do something, often without caring about risks or consequences. When a person is hell-bent on something, they are strongly fixed on achieving it. They may act stubbornly or aggressively in pursuit of their goal, even if others advise against it or if it may cause problems.
example_sentence: He is hell-bent on starting his own business this year. She is hell-bent on winning the competition no matter what it takes. They were hell-bent on finishing the project before the deadline. My brother is hell-bent on buying that expensive car.

english_meaning: In an extremely unpleasant or difficult way. To an extreme degree, often negatively. Very intensely or severely. In a way that resembles hell.
example_sentence: The weather was hellishly hot during the summer afternoon. The exam was hellishly difficult. He worked hellishly hard to meet the deadline. Traffic was hellishly bad on the highway. The journey was hellishly long and tiring.

english_meaning: To assist someone, especially in a difficult situation or with extra work.
example_sentence: Can you help out with the dishes? He helped out his friend during exams. She often helps out at the shelter. Thanks for helping me out today. He often helps out his neighbors with gardening.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine concerned with the study, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases related to blood. The scientific study of the blood and blood-forming organs. The medical field dealing with disorders such as anaemia, leukaemia, and clotting problems.
example_sentence: She is doing her specialisation in hematology. The hospital has a well-equipped hematology department. Hematology helps in diagnosing diseases like leukaemia. He published a research paper in a hematology journal. Modern hematology has improved cancer treatment.

english_meaning: A swelling or collection of blood outside blood vessels, usually caused by an injury. A localized collection of blood in tissues, organs, or under the skin due to the rupture of blood vessels. It often results from trauma, surgery, or medical conditions affecting blood clotting. The swelling may be painful, discolored, and can vary in size.
example_sentence: The patient developed a large hematoma on his thigh after the fall. The doctor drained the hematoma to relieve the pressure. She noticed a small hematoma forming on her arm after the injection. Hematomas can sometimes resolve on their own without treatment.

english_meaning: One half of a sphere or globe divided by a plane passing through its centre. Either half of the Earth as divided by the equator into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, or by a meridian into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres. Either of the two halves of the brain, known as the cerebral hemispheres. A dome-shaped object or structure having the form of half a ball.
example_sentence: Australia lies in the Southern Hemisphere. Winter in the Northern Hemisphere begins in December. The right hemisphere of the brain controls the left side of the body. The roof was built as a perfect hemisphere of glass and steel.

english_meaning: A genetic disorder in which a person’s blood lacks sufficient clotting factors. This results in prolonged bleeding after injuries, cuts, or surgery. Internal bleeding in joints and muscles is common in severe cases.
example_sentence: He was diagnosed with hemophilia as a child and must avoid injuries. People with hemophilia need careful medical attention during surgeries. Severe hemophilia can cause spontaneous bleeding in joints. Advances in treatment have improved the life expectancy of those with hemophilia.

english_meaning: An extreme and irrational fear of blood. People with hemophobia may faint, feel nauseous, or experience intense anxiety at the sight of blood.
example_sentence: His hemophobia made it impossible to become a doctor. She fainted in biology class due to her hemophobia. Hemophobia often causes people to avoid medical checkups. His hemophobia was triggered even by seeing blood in a movie.

english_meaning: An escape of blood from a ruptured blood vessel, especially when it is severe. A heavy loss of something valuable, such as money or people. To bleed heavily, especially internally. To lose something rapidly and in large quantities.
example_sentence: The patient died due to severe internal hemorrhage. The company is hemorrhaging money every month. Doctors immediately stopped the hemorrhage after surgery. The country is hemorrhaging talented professionals to foreign lands. A brain hemorrhage can be life-threatening.

english_meaning: The process that stops bleeding by clotting blood. Physiological process through which the body stops bleeding at the site of an injury. It involves blood vessel constriction, platelet aggregation, and the formation of a blood clot to prevent excessive blood loss.
example_sentence: The doctor applied pressure to achieve hemostasis after the surgery. Platelets play a crucial role in hemostasis. Hemostasis is vital to prevent excessive blood loss after an injury. The nurse monitored the patient to ensure proper hemostasis.

english_meaning: A tall plant grown for its strong fibre and seeds. A type of cannabis plant cultivated for industrial use. The coarse fibre obtained from the stem of this plant, used to make ropes, sacks, cloth, paper, and other coarse fabrics. The seeds of this plant are also used to make oil and as food. It is a fast-growing plant that has been cultivated for thousands of years for many practical purposes.
example_sentence: Hemp ropes are stronger and more durable than ordinary cotton ropes. Farmers in some regions grow hemp as a cash crop for its fibre. The bag was woven from rough hemp fibre. Hemp oil is widely used in cosmetics and skin care products. Workers were busy twisting hemp into thick ropes for the ship.

english_meaning: A loyal and trusted follower who obeys orders without question. A faithful supporter, especially one who carries out unpleasant, dishonest, or violent tasks for a powerful person. A close associate of a criminal, gangster, or corrupt leader. A devoted aide or attendant who serves a master or chief. The word usually carries a negative meaning, suggesting a person who blindly serves a wrongdoer.
example_sentence: The gangster always travelled with two armed henchmen by his side. The corrupt minister ordered his henchman to threaten the journalist. Police arrested the drug lord along with several of his henchmen. He was nothing more than a henchman, carrying out his boss's dirty work.

english_meaning: A plane geometric figure with eleven straight sides and eleven angles. An eleven-sided polygon, also called an undecagon. Any shape or design based on an eleven-sided figure.
example_sentence: The teacher drew a hendecagon on the whiteboard. A hendecagon has eleven equal sides when it is regular. Students measured each angle of the hendecagon carefully. The coin was minted in the shape of a hendecagon.

english_meaning: To harass or control a person, typically a husband, by persistent nagging or criticism. It describes a situation where one partner is intimidated into submission by the other. It usually implies a domestic setting.
example_sentence: He felt henpecked because he wasn't allowed to go out with his friends. The comedy show featured a henpecked husband trying to hide his new hobby. Some people mistakenly believe that being helpful means being henpecked. He didn't want his colleagues to think his wife was henpecking him.

english_meaning: Describing a man who is continually criticized and controlled by his wife. It refers to someone who is intimidated by their spouse and lacks the courage to stand up for themselves. This term is often used in a pejorative or mocking manner.
example_sentence: He was so henpecked that he had to ask his wife's permission to go for a walk. The comedian made several jokes about being a henpecked husband. Neighbors often whispered about the henpecked man who did all the housework while his wife relaxed. He never went out with his friends anymore because of his henpecked nature.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove all or part of the liver. A procedure used to remove liver tumours or damaged liver tissue. The removal of a liver segment from a donor for transplantation. A major operation made possible by the liver's ability to regenerate.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed a hepatectomy to remove the tumour. A partial hepatectomy is often enough to treat early liver cancer. The liver regrows steadily after a hepatectomy. He remained under observation for a week following the hepatectomy.

english_meaning: A seventeen-sided polygon with seventeen angles. A geometric shape with seventeen straight sides and seventeen vertices. Any flat shape with seventeen corners and seventeen edges.
example_sentence: A regular heptadecagon has seventeen equal sides and angles. The rare geometric construction showed a perfect heptadecagon. Mathematicians proved that a heptadecagon can be constructed with compass and straightedge. The decorative ceiling had a heptadecagonal pattern.

english_meaning: A seven-sided polygon with seven angles. A geometric shape with seven straight sides and seven vertices. Any flat shape with seven corners and seven edges.
example_sentence: A regular heptagon has seven equal sides and angles. The ancient coin was shaped like a heptagon. Drawing a perfect heptagon requires careful measurement. Some British coins feature heptagonal shapes.

english_meaning: An official messenger bringing news. A person or thing viewed as a sign that something is about to happen. To be a sign that something is about to happen; to announce or acclaim.
example_sentence: The blooming of crocuses is a herald of spring. The article heralded a new era in cancer research. The king's herald announced the royal decree to the townspeople. Dark clouds on the horizon often herald an approaching storm. He was heralded as the greatest writer of his generation.

english_meaning: A collection of dried and preserved plant specimens used for scientific study. A systematically arranged collection of plant specimens that have been dried, pressed, and mounted on sheets. These specimens are labeled with scientific information such as name, location, and date of collection. Herbariums are used by botanists and researchers to study plant classification, identification, and biodiversity.
synonyms: ["Plant collection","Botanical collection","Dried plant archive","Plant specimen archive"]
example_sentence: The university has a large herbarium for botanical research. Scientists added a rare flower to the herbarium collection. Students visited the herbarium to study plant classification. The herbarium contains specimens collected over a hundred years.

english_meaning: An organism that primarily consumes plant material such as leaves, grass, fruits, and seeds.
example_sentence: Cows are herbivores and eat grass daily. Elephants are large herbivores that feed on leaves and bark. Rabbits are herbivores that prefer carrots and lettuce. Giraffes are herbivores that eat tall tree leaves.

english_meaning: Requiring very great strength, effort, or determination. Extremely difficult and demanding. Unusually large or powerful in size or force. Relating to Hercules, the hero of Greek mythology famous for his enormous strength.
example_sentence: Rebuilding the bridge in one month was a Herculean task. She made a Herculean effort to finish her thesis on time. The rescue workers showed Herculean strength during the flood. Cleaning the entire warehouse alone proved Herculean.

english_meaning: A hero of ancient Greek and Roman mythology famous for his extraordinary physical strength and courage. The son of the god Jupiter (Zeus) and a mortal woman, known for performing twelve nearly impossible tasks called the Labours of Hercules. Figuratively, a person of unusual strength, power, or great achievement. The name is often used to describe anyone who is exceptionally strong or who completes very difficult work.
example_sentence: According to legend, Hercules completed twelve impossible labours to prove his strength. The wrestler was so muscular that everyone called him a modern-day Hercules. It will take a Hercules to lift that huge stone alone. Building the bridge in just six months was a task fit for Hercules. Children love to read stories about the adventures of Hercules.

english_meaning: A group of animals of the same type that live and feed together. A large group of people of the same type. To make animals move together as a group. A crowd especially of ordinary or undistinguished persons or things. To urge, push, or force onward.
example_sentence: The great herds of cattle that cowboys once drove across the plains. An old woman was herding the goats. The guards briskly herded us through the museum in order to prevent overcrowding.

english_meaning: A negative phrase that is used to describe that the team members are disagreeable or difficult to deal with. To control or organize a group of people or things that are very difficult to manage, like cats that refuse to be herded. Dealing with something extremely hard to organize or control.
synonyms: ["Managing chaos","Organizing the unmanageable","Controlling the uncontrollable","Coordinating the impossible"]
example_sentence: Trying to get all of the different department heads to agree on a single budget proposal felt like herding cats. Managing that team is like herding cats. He says managing lawyers is like herding cats. Managing a political party is a lot like herding cats. "It's like herding cats sometimes", she said of the logistical challenges.

english_meaning: Used to express good wishes for someone. Used to honor an achievement or milestone. Used to introduce a toast during celebrations. Used to show appreciation for a person or group. A phrase used when raising a glass to honor someone or something. It is an expression used during a toast to show good wishes, appreciation, celebration, respect or hope for someone or something. It often comes before the name of the person, event or idea being honored.
synonyms: ["Cheers to","Salute to","A toast to","In honor of","In celebration of"]
example_sentence: Here’s to your success and happiness in the future. Here’s to the newly married couple, may their life be full of joy. Here’s to our friendship that has stood the test of time. Here’s to new beginnings and better days ahead.

english_meaning: In this general area or vicinity. Near this place or location. Around here or in the surrounding region. In or near the place being discussed or referred to.
synonyms: ["Around here","In this area","Nearby","In this vicinity","Locally","In these parts"]
example_sentence: There are several good restaurants hereabouts. The people hereabouts are very friendly. You won't find many stores hereabouts. Weather hereabouts can be unpredictable.

english_meaning: From this time forward or in the future. After this point in time or text. Life after death or the future world. In what follows in a document or text. Subsequently or later on.
example_sentence: Hereafter, all meetings will be held online. The company shall hereafter be known as Tech Solutions. He believed in the hereafter and an afterlife. This document shall hereafter be referred to as the Agreement.

english_meaning: By means of this document, statement, or action. As a result of this. Through this act or declaration. Used in formal or legal contexts to indicate that something is being done or declared.
synonyms: ["By this means","Through this","By this","Herewith","By means of this","By this declaration"]
example_sentence: I hereby declare this meeting officially open. The contract is hereby terminated. You are hereby notified of the changes. We hereby confirm receipt of your application.

english_meaning: Passed down from parents to children through the genes. Relating to qualities, diseases, or features that are inherited biologically from one's ancestors. Also used for titles, positions, or property that are passed from one generation to the next by right of birth rather than by choice or election. Anything that is transmitted by inheritance, whether physical, social, or legal.
example_sentence: Diabetes can sometimes be a hereditary disease that runs in families. The king's throne was hereditary and passed to his eldest son. Eye colour and height are largely hereditary traits. He inherited the hereditary title of lord from his late father. Doctors believe that certain types of cancer have a hereditary link.

english_meaning: The biological process by which physical and mental characteristics are passed from parents to their children through genes. The sum of qualities and traits that a person inherits from their ancestors. The transmission of features such as appearance, intelligence, temperament, and certain diseases from one generation to the next. In a broader sense, the natural inheritance of qualities that shapes an individual's identity.
example_sentence: Scientists study heredity to understand how traits pass from parents to children. Both heredity and environment shape a child's personality. Heredity plays an important role in determining a person's height. Some diseases are caused by heredity rather than by lifestyle. The professor gave an interesting lecture on the laws of heredity.

english_meaning: In this document, statement, or matter. Within this place, text, or context. In this particular aspect or respect. Contained or included in this.
synonyms: ["In this","Within this","In this document","Here","In this matter","In this respect"]
example_sentence: The terms herein are binding for all parties. All information herein is confidential. The problem herein lies in the implementation. The facts herein stated are accurate.

english_meaning: In the following part of this document, statement, or text. Later in this same document or text. From this point forward in the writing. Subsequently mentioned or referred to in what follows.
synonyms: ["Hereafter","Later in this document","Below","In what follows","Subsequently herein"]
example_sentence: The company hereinafter referred to as the Supplier. This agreement shall hereinafter be called the Contract. The parties hereinafter mentioned agreed to the terms. All conditions hereinafter specified must be met.

english_meaning: Of this document, matter, or thing. Concerning or relating to this. From or out of this. About or regarding what has been mentioned.
example_sentence: In witness hereof, we sign our names. The date hereof is clearly stated. The purpose hereof is to establish guidelines. The provisions hereof shall remain in effect.

english_meaning: It indicates that something is enclosed or attached with a document or letter. It serves as a formal legal term meaning by means of this document. It denotes an action taking place simultaneously with the presentation of a statement.
synonyms: ["Enclosed","Attached","Hereby","With This","Along With This","In This Package","In This Letter","By Means Of This","Hereunto","Accompanying"]
example_sentence: Please find enclosed herewith a copy of the signed contract. I herewith resign from my position as director of the company. The required payment is submitted herewith for your review. We send herewith the documents requested in your previous letter.

english_meaning: The traditions, culture, history, values, property, or achievements that are passed down from previous generations. Traditions, customs, language, arts, and values inherited from ancestors. Historical monuments, buildings, and sites that represent the past. Family traditions, beliefs, ancestry, and inherited property. Natural resources, landscapes, forests, wildlife, and ecosystems preserved for future generations.
example_sentence: The ancient fort is an important part of our national heritage. She is proud of her cultural heritage and traditional customs. The museum helps preserve the heritage of the region. Children should learn about their heritage to understand their roots.

english_meaning: An organism or person having both male and female reproductive organs. A hermaphrodite is an individual, either in humans or animals, who possesses both male and female sexual characteristics or reproductive organs. In biology, some plants and animals naturally develop both types of reproductive organs, allowing them to produce both eggs and sperm. In humans, the term historically referred to intersex conditions.
example_sentence: Some snails are naturally hermaphrodites and can self-fertilize. The biologist studied a hermaphrodite fish that had both testes and ovaries. In literature, the character was described as a hermaphrodite symbolizing duality. Certain plants are hermaphrodites, producing both male and female flowers on the same plant.

english_meaning: Having both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual. Relating to an organism, plant, or animal that possesses characteristics of both sexes. In biology, used to describe species in which a single individual can produce both eggs and sperm. Figuratively, it may describe something that combines two opposing qualities or natures.
example_sentence: Earthworms are hermaphroditic creatures that have both male and female organs. Many flowering plants are hermaphroditic in nature. The biologist explained how hermaphroditic species reproduce. Some species of fish are hermaphroditic and can change their sex when needed. The painting showed a strange hermaphroditic figure standing in the moonlight.

english_meaning: A person who, usually for religious reasons, lives a very simple life alone and does not meet or talk to other people. A person who lives alone and apart from society.
example_sentence: He's like a hermit. If a hermit lives in a state of ecstasy, his lack of comfort becomes the height of comfort. He must relinquish it.

english_meaning: A medical condition in which an organ or tissue protrudes through an abnormal opening in the wall of the cavity that contains it. The protrusion of a loop of an organ or tissue through an abnormal opening. A rupture or swelling caused by the displacement of a body part. A physical injury often caused by heavy lifting or strain. The state of having a portion of the intestine or other internal organ displaced from its normal position.
example_sentence: He had to undergo surgery to repair a painful inguinal hernia. Lifting that heavy refrigerator without help might give you a hernia. The athlete spent months recovering from a severe sports hernia. Doctors monitored the small hiatal hernia to ensure it did not cause further digestive complications.

english_meaning: A scientist who studies reptiles and amphibians. A biologist who specializes in studying reptiles such as snakes, lizards, turtles, and amphibians like frogs and salamanders. They often study behavior, habitats, physiology, and conservation of these animals.
example_sentence: The herpetologist discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest. She consulted a herpetologist to identify the snake in her backyard. Universities often invite herpetologists to give lectures on reptile conservation. His dream is to become a herpetologist and travel the world studying lizards and snakes.

english_meaning: A branch of zoology that studies reptiles and amphibians such as snakes, lizards, turtles, frogs, and salamanders. It focuses on their behavior, biology, evolution, and habitats.
synonyms: ["Study of reptiles and amphibians","Branch of zoology"]
example_sentence: She chose herpetology because she loves studying snakes and frogs. Herpetology helps scientists understand reptile conservation. The university offers a specialized course in herpetology. His research in herpetology focuses on desert lizards.

english_meaning: Someone who loves reptiles and amphibians. A person who is interested in, collects, studies, or has a strong liking for reptiles (like snakes, lizards) and amphibians (like frogs, salamanders).
example_sentence: She is a herpetophile and keeps several snakes at home. The herpetophile joined a local reptile conservation group. He bought a rare frog as a gift for the herpetophile in his family. Her herpetophile friend spends hours observing lizards in the garden.

english_meaning: Fear of reptiles such as snakes, lizards, or similar creatures. An intense or irrational fear of reptiles. People with this phobia may experience anxiety, panic, or avoidance behaviors when they see or think about reptiles. It is a type of specific phobia.
example_sentence: Jane could not enter the zoo because her herpetophobia made her panic at the sight of snakes. His herpetophobia was so severe that even pictures of lizards caused anxiety. During the camping trip, her herpetophobia prevented her from walking near the riverbank. Therapists often help patients overcome herpetophobia through gradual exposure.

english_meaning: A unit of frequency defined as one cycle per second. The derived unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI). A term used to describe the speed of a microprocessor or clock rate. A measurement typically applied to periodic phenomena such as sound waves or electromagnetic waves. A unit named after the German physicist Heinrich Hertz. A quantification of how often a repetitive event occurs over a specific duration.
synonyms: ["Cycles Per Second","Frequency Unit","SI Unit","Rate Of Recurrence","Periodic Rate","Oscillation Count","Vibrational Rate","Wave Frequency","CPS","Clock Rate","Rhythm","Pulse","Cadence","Tempo"]
example_sentence: The standard household electricity in many countries operates at fifty Hertz. Modern computer processors are often measured in Giga Hertz to indicate their processing speed. Human hearing typically ranges from twenty Hertz to twenty thousand Hertz. The radio station broadcasts its signal at a specific frequency of one hundred Mega Hertz.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being unwilling or slow to act because of doubt. A tendency to pause or delay before making a decision. Lack of confidence that leads to indecision.
example_sentence: There was noticeable hesitancy in his reply. Vaccine hesitancy slowed the health campaign. Her hesitancy cost the team valuable time. He spoke with hesitancy about the sensitive topic.

english_meaning: Slow to act or speak because of uncertainty or lack of confidence. Unwilling to do something immediately because of doubt. Showing signs of doubt in speech or movement.
example_sentence: He was hesitant to share his opinion in the meeting. She gave a hesitant smile to the new guests. The company is hesitant about expanding this year. His hesitant voice revealed his nervousness.

english_meaning: In a slow and uncertain way that shows doubt or nervousness. Without confidence, with pauses or reluctance. In a manner that shows unwillingness to act immediately.
example_sentence: She hesitantly raised her hand to answer. He hesitantly agreed to join the trip. The child hesitantly stepped into the cold water. They hesitantly accepted the stranger's offer.

english_meaning: To pause before saying or doing something because of uncertainty or nervousness. To be slow to act or speak because of doubt. To be unwilling to do something because you are not sure it is right.
example_sentence: Do not hesitate to call me if you need help. He hesitated before opening the letter. She hesitated at the door for a few seconds. They hesitated to invest in such a risky project.

english_meaning: A pause or delay before doing or saying something because of uncertainty. The state of being unwilling or unsure about acting. A moment of doubt that slows down speech or action.
example_sentence: After a brief hesitation, she answered the question. He agreed without hesitation to help his friend. Her hesitation showed that she was unsure. There was a moment of hesitation before the crowd clapped.

english_meaning: The quality of being diverse or different in kind. he presence of variation, diversity, or differences within a group, system, or substance. It describes a condition where elements are not uniform and show distinct characteristics. It can be used in social, scientific, economic, or cultural contexts.
example_sentence: The cultural heterogeneity of the city makes it vibrant and dynamic. Researchers studied the genetic heterogeneity of the population. Economic heterogeneity within the region affects development planning. The classroom showed heterogeneity in students’ learning styles.

english_meaning: To be sexually or romantically attracted to the opposite sex. Attraction to the opposite sex
example_sentence: He heterexes women exclusively. Some people heterosex naturally, others do not. They heterex in line with their personal preferences. Heterosex is the most common orientation worldwide. The survey focused on heterosex adults.

english_meaning: A person who is sexually attracted to people of the opposite sex.
