example_sentence: He identifies as heterosexual and has dated women. The film explores heterosexual relationships in modern society. Heterosexual couples often face societal expectations regarding marriage. She prefers heterosexual dating apps to meet men.

english_meaning: A method or technique that helps someone discover or learn something for themselves, often through exploration or experimentation. Enabling a person to learn, discover, or solve problems by trial and error, experience, or self-learning rather than by following fixed rules.
example_sentence: A heuristic approach encourages students to find answers through discovery rather than memorization. Scientists often use heuristic methods to explore new theories. The software uses a heuristic algorithm to detect suspicious behavior. Heuristic learning makes students more independent and creative.

english_meaning: To cut or chop something, especially wood or stone, with heavy blows using an axe, sword, or other sharp tool. To shape, form, or carve something by cutting. To strike repeatedly to break or fell something. Figuratively, to stick to, conform to, or follow a particular rule, principle, or course strictly.
example_sentence: The lumberjacks began to hew the huge oak tree with their sharp axes. He had to hew a path through the thick jungle. The sculptor carefully hewed the statue out of a single block of marble. The new government promised to hew closely to the will of the people. Workers were hired to hew stones from the quarry for the temple.

english_meaning: A magic spell or curse believed to cause harm or bad luck. A person believed to bring misfortune; a jinx. To put a curse or harmful spell on someone or something. In computing, an informal abbreviation for hexadecimal. A six-sided figure or object in informal usage.
example_sentence: According to the legend, a witch placed a hex on the castle. Fans joked that the unlucky mascot was a hex on the team. The character tried to hex his rival in the fantasy novel. Programmers often use hex to represent colors and memory addresses.

english_meaning: A sixteen-sided polygon with sixteen angles. A geometric shape with sixteen straight sides and sixteen vertices. Any flat shape with sixteen corners and sixteen edges.
example_sentence: A regular hexadecagon has sixteen equal sides and angles. The ornamental design featured a hexadecagonal frame. Students explored the geometric properties of hexadecagons. The fountain was constructed with a hexadecagonal outline.

english_meaning: A six-sided polygon with six angles. A geometric shape with six straight sides and six vertices. Any flat shape with six corners and six edges.
example_sentence: Honeycomb cells are shaped like regular hexagons. A hexagon has six equal sides when it is regular. The bolt head was designed as a hexagon for better grip. Students measured the angles inside a hexagon.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with two parallel hexagonal bases connected by six rectangular faces. A prism with a six-sided cross-section throughout its length. A polyhedron with eight faces, two hexagonal and six rectangular.
example_sentence: Many pencils are hexagonal prisms. A hexagonal prism has eight faces. The honeycomb structure resembles hexagonal prisms. Calculate the volume of the hexagonal prism.

english_meaning: A six-pointed star formed by two overlapping equilateral triangles. A geometric figure or symbol shaped like a six-pointed star, often used in religion, art, and heraldry. In the Chinese I Ching, any of the sixty-four figures made up of six broken or unbroken lines.
example_sentence: The tile floor was decorated with a golden hexagram. A hexagram is formed by two interlocking triangles. The ancient manuscript showed a hexagram at the top of each page. He drew a hexagram to explain the geometry lesson.

english_meaning: A solid geometric figure having six plane faces. A three-dimensional shape with six flat surfaces, the most common example being the cube. Any polyhedron whose faces number exactly six.
example_sentence: A cube is the most familiar type of hexahedron. The model of the hexahedron was made from cardboard. Each face of a regular hexahedron is a square. The students calculated the volume of the hexahedron.

english_meaning: A pause, break, or interruption in an activity. A gap in a sequence, record, or series. A temporary absence from work, study, or performance. In anatomy, an opening or passage in an organ or body structure.
example_sentence: The band returned after a two-year hiatus. There is a long hiatus in the historical record. She took a short hiatus from social media. The doctor explained the meaning of a hiatus in the diaphragm.

english_meaning: To spend the winter in a dormant or inactive state, as some animals do. It involves a significant drop in body temperature and metabolic rate to conserve energy. Figuratively, it can mean to remain inactive or in seclusion for an extended period.
example_sentence: Bears typically hibernate in caves during the coldest months of the year. Some species of bats hibernate in clusters to maintain warmth. The software project had to hibernate for a few months due to a lack of funding. During the blizzard, many villagers chose to hibernate in their homes with plenty of food.

english_meaning: A state of deep sleep or inactivity in which certain animals spend the winter months in order to survive cold weather and lack of food. During hibernation, the animal's body temperature, heart rate, and breathing slow down to save energy. Figuratively, a period during which a person, activity, or organisation becomes inactive or dormant for a long time.
example_sentence: Bears go into hibernation during the long cold winter months. Frogs and snakes also undergo hibernation to survive freezing temperatures. The company was in hibernation for several years before its sudden revival. After months of hibernation, the political party became active again before the elections. Scientists study how animals slow their heartbeat during hibernation.

english_meaning: A tropical or subtropical plant with large, brightly coloured trumpet-shaped flowers, usually red, pink, yellow, or white. The hibiscus belongs to the mallow family and is grown both for its ornamental beauty and for its uses in herbal teas, medicines, and dyes. The flower is a national symbol in several countries and is often used in religious and decorative purposes.
example_sentence: She planted red hibiscus along the garden wall. The hibiscus is the national flower of Malaysia. Dried hibiscus petals are used to make a refreshing herbal tea. The bright hibiscus flowers attracted many butterflies and bees. In some cultures, the hibiscus is offered during religious ceremonies.

english_meaning: A sudden, involuntary contraction of the diaphragm muscle followed by the closing of the vocal cords. It can also refer to a minor setback or a temporary interruption in a process. Typically, it occurs as a series of short, sharp sounds.
example_sentence: He tried to hold his breath to stop a persistent hiccup. A small technical hiccup delayed the launch of the new website by an hour. She drank a glass of water quickly to get rid of her hiccups. The project proceeded smoothly despite a brief hiccup in the initial planning stage.

english_meaning: To put or keep something in a place where it cannot be seen or found. To go somewhere secretly so that others cannot see you. To keep information, feelings, or emotions secret. To cover something so it is not visible. The skin of a large animal, especially when used for leather.
example_sentence: The children love to hide behind the curtains. She tried to hide her tears from her family. He hid the gift in the closet before her birthday. The company sells shoes made from cow hide.

english_meaning: To avoid people or difficult situations by keeping to oneself. To retreat into a private, protected world instead of facing others. To behave in a shy, withdrawn way out of fear or insecurity.
example_sentence: After the failure he chose to hide in his shell. Shy children often hide in their shell at new schools. You cannot hide in your shell forever. She hid in her shell until she felt safe again.

english_meaning: A person who holds a high or chief position in a hierarchy, especially in a religious order such as a high priest, bishop, archbishop, or patriarch. A leader who occupies a position of authority over others in any ranked organisation. By extension, any influential or ruling figure in a structured group or institution.
example_sentence: The hierarch led the prayers at the grand cathedral. Each hierarch of the church was invited to the special meeting. Only a senior hierarch had the authority to make such an important decision. The young priest hoped to one day become a hierarch of his order. The hierarchs gathered to elect a new spiritual leader.

english_meaning: A system in which people or things are arranged according to rank or importance. A chain of command in an organization. A ranking system based on power or authority. Classification of things according to levels. Social order based on status. Arrangement of biological categories such as kingdom, phylum, class.
example_sentence: The company has a clear hierarchy of management. In many societies, wealth determines social hierarchy. The military follows a strict hierarchy. Animals are classified in a biological hierarchy.

english_meaning: Left alone without help or support, often in a difficult situation. It is used when someone is abandoned or left helpless, especially when they expected support. The phrase originally comes from sailing, where a boat is left stranded on land after the tide goes out. In modern use, it describes emotional, financial, or practical abandonment.
example_sentence: When the company shut down suddenly, the workers were left high and dry. He promised to help but disappeared, leaving us high and dry. The guide left the tourists high and dry in the middle of the journey. After the funding was canceled, the project team was left high and dry.

english_meaning: Arrogant. Behaving as if one is more important or superior to others. Acting proudly or with a sense of self-importance. Looking down on others. Showing pride or haughtiness.
example_sentence: He behaves high and mighty. Ever since he got promoted, he’s been acting all high and mighty. She became high and mighty after winning the award. Don’t get high and mighty just because you have a new car. He talks to people in such a high and mighty way, as if they don’t matter.

english_meaning: A condition where the force of blood against artery walls is consistently too high. Hypertension that can lead to heart disease, stroke, and other health problems. Elevated blood pressure readings above normal range. A chronic medical condition requiring monitoring and often treatment.
example_sentence: High blood pressure often has no symptoms. Reducing salt intake can help lower high blood pressure. His high blood pressure requires daily medication. Regular exercise helps control high blood pressure.

english_meaning: Highly accurate reproduction of sound or images with very little distortion. Equipment or technology designed to reproduce sound with great accuracy. A high degree of faithfulness to an original signal, recording, model, or source.
example_sentence: These headphones provide high fidelity sound at a reasonable price. The studio invested in high fidelity recording equipment. The digital copy preserved the painting in high fidelity. Engineers tested whether the model represented the system with high fidelity.

english_meaning: A state of enthusiasm, energy, confidence, or cheerfulness; showing positive attitude and strong motivation, especially in difficult times.
example_sentence: Even after losing the match, the team remained in high spirits. She started her new job in high spirits, eager to learn and contribute. The soldiers marched in high spirits, proud of their mission. Despite the heavy rain, the students continued the trip in high spirits.

english_meaning: Very nervous, tense, or easily upset. Emotionally sensitive, excitable, or quick to react. Sometimes describes someone with a “sensitive temperament” who worries or stresses easily.
example_sentence: She is too high strung to handle stress. I was so high strung, worried and nervous. Sh's so high-strung that even a small delay makes her panic. She gets high-strung whenever exams are near. She is talented but very high-strung and gets upset easily.

english_meaning: A gesture of celebration or greeting in which two people raise a hand and slap their palms together. To give someone this gesture as congratulations, encouragement, or greeting.
example_sentence: The players exchanged a high-five after scoring the goal. Give me a high-five for finishing the project on time. She high-fived her teammate at the finish line. The children ran over to high-five their favorite player.

english_meaning: Very nervous, tense, or easily upset. Extremely sensitive and quick to react emotionally. Having a temperament that is restless and highly excitable. Constantly on edge and unable to relax.
example_sentence: She is rather high-strung before every examination. High-strung horses need calm and patient handling. His high-strung nature made teamwork difficult. Long working hours left him tired and high-strung.

english_meaning: Using language or ideas that sound overly grand, important, or sophisticated. Pompous, pretentious, or affected in style or manner. Intended to impress others but lacking sincerity or practical value.

english_meaning: To draw special attention to something important. To mark part of a text with a bright colour so that it stands out. The best, most interesting, or most memorable part of something. A bright area in a picture or a lighter streak of colour in the hair. In computing, to select text or an item so that it appears marked on screen.
example_sentence: The report highlights the need for better public transport. Please highlight the key points in yellow. Meeting the players was the highlight of the trip. She had blonde highlights put in her hair.

english_meaning: To go for a long walk in the country, To increase prices. To increase the amount or cost of something, especially suddenly or by a large amount. A long walk in the country. A large or sudden increase in prices, costs, etc. An increase in the cost of something, especially a large or unwanted increase.
example_sentence: The Govt. hiked up the prices of milk by 40%. We could go into town but it’s a real hike from here. They went on a ten-mile hike through the forest. We could go into town but it's a real hike (= a long way) from here. Retailers have hiked (up) prices again. We plan to hike from lake to lake. I’ve got to hike back to my car to get my jacket. Dairies have hiked milk prices again. The recent hike in train fares came as a shock to commuters.

english_meaning: Extremely funny or amusing. Something that causes loud laughter or great amusement. It is used to describe situations, events, or people that make others laugh a lot.

english_meaning: To create difficulty or to delay the progress of someone or something. To prevent or obstruct an action, movement, or development. To stand in the way of something happening as quickly or as smoothly as it should. To slow down or interfere with a process, plan, or person. The word is used both physically (blocking the way) and figuratively (obstructing progress or success).

Do not let fear hinder you from following your dreams. The fallen tree on the road hindered the traffic for hours. Constant interruptions hindered her from completing the report on time.

english_meaning: Something that makes it difficult for someone or something to make progress or to act freely. An obstacle, barrier, or difficulty that delays, prevents, or interferes with an action, plan, or movement. The act of hindering or the state of being hindered. Anything that comes in the way of success, work, or development.

The bad weather proved to be a serious hindrance to the climbers. Old laws are sometimes a hindrance to economic growth. She refused to be a hindrance to her friend's career.

english_meaning: To depend on something or be determined by something. A situation or decision that everything depends on. A movable joint or mechanism that connects two objects and allows them to swing open or closed. A metal or plastic joint fixed to a door, lid, or gate that allows it to swing.
example_sentence: The door hinge is rusty and needs oil. His decision hinges on the final results. The success of the project hinges on teamwork. She carefully fixed the broken hinge of the box.

english_meaning: To depend on, be determined by, or be influenced by a particular thing or condition. It is used when the success, result, decision, or outcome of something depends largely on one important factor. If that factor changes, the outcome may also change.
synonyms: ["Depend on","Rely on","Be based on","Rest on","Be contingent on","Be determined by","Be tied to","Turn on"]
antonyms: ["Be independent of","Be unrelated to","Ignore","Disregard","Disconnect from","Detach from"]

english_meaning: To depend on, be determined by, or be based on something. The outcome of one thing is controlled or influenced by another thing. When something hinges upon a particular factor, condition, decision, or event, its success, failure, result, or future depends entirely or largely on that factor.
synonyms: ["Depend on","Rely on","Be based on","Rest on","Turn on","Be determined by","Be contingent on","Be subject to","Lean on","Count on"]
antonyms: ["Be independent of","Disregard","Ignore","Disconnect from","Be unrelated to","Detach from","Separate from","Stand alone"]
example_sentence: The success of the project hinges upon proper planning. Our decision will hinge upon the results of the survey. The team's future hinges upon winning the final match. Whether the event takes place may hinge upon the weather conditions.

english_meaning: The remote or less developed areas of a country, located away from the coast, major cities, or main rivers. The inland regions lying behind a coastal area or a port and supplying it with goods. By extension, an area that is far from the centres of culture, politics, or trade. Figuratively, an unknown, unexplored, or undeveloped area of knowledge, experience, or thought.

He spent his childhood in a quiet village in the hinterland. The company is opening new branches in the hinterland of the country. The novel explores the cultural hinterland of rural life.

A genre of popular music featuring rhythmic vocal delivery known as rapping set to a beat. A modern style of street dance that developed alongside hip-hop music. Relating to or characteristic of the music, fashion, and subculture of hip-hop.

english_meaning: The study of horses. A field covering the anatomy, behaviour, breeding, and care of horses. Knowledge and science relating to horsemanship.

english_meaning: A protective enzyme that prevents histamine overload. A regulator of allergic and inflammatory responses. A digestive enzyme involved in metabolizing biogenic amines. A biological catalyst found mainly in the intestines, kidneys, and placenta`
example_sentence: The action of histaminase on the gastric secretory response to histamine and to a meal. Low histaminase levels can lead to histamine intolerance symptoms. The doctor recommended testing her histaminase activity. Histaminase helps prevent allergic reactions by breaking down excess histamine. Some foods may affect the production of histaminase in the body.

english_meaning: A chemical substance in the body that is released during allergic reactions and causes itching, swelling, redness, and other symptoms. A mediator of inflammation and allergic reactions. A neurotransmitter involved in wakefulness and alertness. Stimulates the secretion of gastric acid in the stomach.
example_sentence: Histamine release causes itching during an allergic reaction. Antihistamine medicines block the effects of histamine. High levels of histamine can lead to swelling and redness. Certain foods may trigger histamine production in sensitive individuals

english_meaning: A person who studies or writes about history. An expert in or student of historical events and periods. Someone who researches and interprets the past. A scholar specializing in historical analysis and documentation.
example_sentence: The historian wrote a detailed account of the war. Historians debate the causes of the revolution. She is a respected historian of ancient Rome. The historian's research uncovered new evidence.

english_meaning: Decorated with figures of people, animals, or scenes that tell a story. Describing an ornamental initial letter in a manuscript containing pictures. Adorned with narrative or pictorial designs, especially in medieval art.

english_meaning: Famous or important in history, or likely to be remembered. Having great and lasting significance. Marking an important moment or turning point. Relating to places or objects preserved because of their importance in the past.
example_sentence: The signing of the treaty was a historic moment for the nation. They stayed in a historic building near the old city walls. The team achieved a historic victory in the final. It was a historic day for women's rights.

english_meaning: Connected with the study of history or with past events. Belonging to the past rather than the present. Based on or dealing with real people and events of the past. Concerning the development of something over time.
example_sentence: She is writing a historical novel set in the sixteenth century. The museum keeps important historical documents. There is little historical evidence for this story. Historical records show the city was founded in 1750.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to history or past events. According to the record of what happened in the past. Traditionally or over a long period of time. From a historical point of view.

english_meaning: To act unfairly or do something morally wrong, especially in a way that is intended to hurt someone emotionally or unfairly in an argument or competition.

It’s hitting below the belt to bring up his financial problems in the meeting. She felt that mocking his accent was hitting below the belt.

english_meaning: To quickly become good friends or get along very well with someone, especially when you meet for the first time. It shows natural friendship, connection, or chemistry between two people.
example_sentence: John and Ali hit it off the moment they met at the conference. The teacher and her new students hit it off right away. I didn’t expect to hit it off with her, but we became close friends instantly. They hit it off so well that they decided to start a business together.

english_meaning: To show romantic or sexual interest in someone. To find, discover, or come up with a solution or idea. To arrive at a place or point, often unexpectedly.
example_sentence: He hit on a great solution. She hit on a plan to save money. He tried to hit on her at the party. The scientist hit on a new theory. He was hitting on his classmate at lunch. She hit on a brilliant plan to solve the problem. During our walk, we hit on a small hidden garden.

english_meaning: Something that is unpredictable or done without planning or accuracy, it may succeed or fail by chance.
example_sentence: His cooking is hit or miss, sometimes the food tastes great, sometimes it’s terrible. The internet connection in this area is hit or miss; it works well one day and not at all the next. Their customer service can be hit or miss depending on who answers the phone. Learning online without guidance can be hit or miss; some lessons help, others just confuse you.

english_meaning:
To find success or something valuable. To suddenly become successful, discover something valuable, or achieve great profit or good results after effort.
Originally, the phrase came from gold mining, where “pay dirt” means the layer of earth that contains gold or valuable minerals.
synonyms: ["Succeed","Strike gold","Achieve success","Find something valuable","Make a breakthrough"]
example_sentence: After months of searching for investors, the company finally hit pay dirt. The researchers struck pay dirt when they discovered a new species of butterfly. His latest novel hit pay dirt and became a bestseller. She dug into her family history and hit pay dirt with an old photograph collection. After digging for weeks, the miners finally struck pay dirt when they found a vein of gold. The scientist hit pay dirt with a discovery that could change modern medicine.

english_meaning: To study very hard, especially before an exam or test. To start focusing on academic work seriously.
example_sentence: I can’t go to the party tonight; I need to hit the books for my math exam. She usually watches TV in the evening, but today she decided to hit the books instead. If you want to pass the entrance test, you’d better start hitting the books now. After wasting a whole week, he finally realized it was time to hit the books.

english_meaning: To start something quickly with energy and immediate action, without delay or preparation. It means beginning a task, job, or project at full speed and effectiveness from the very first moment. The person is already prepared, confident, and productive, rather than needing time to adjust or learn.
synonyms: ["Start quickly","Begin energetically","Get off to a fast start","Jump right in","Start immediately"]
example_sentence: She joined the company and hit the ground running on her first day. The new manager hit the ground running and improved team performance quickly. After months of planning, they hit the ground running when the project launched. He studied the system in advance so he could hit the ground running at his new job.

english_meaning: To go to bed or go to sleep.
example_sentence: I’m tired, time to hit the hay. He hit the hay early last night. We should hit the hay before the long trip. After studying all night, she finally hit the hay.

english_meaning: To win a large amount of money, especially suddenly. To have great and unexpected success or good luck. To find exactly what one needs or wants. To gain a very large reward from a small effort or chance.
antonyms: ["Lose out","Fail","Miss out","Come up empty","Suffer loss","Flop","Bomb","Fall short"]
example_sentence: He hit the jackpot when his small business went international. She hit the jackpot with her very first novel. They hit the jackpot by buying that land before the prices rose. We hit the jackpot when we found this flat at such a low rent.

english_meaning: To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem. Describe exactly what is causing a situation.
example_sentence: You really hit the nail on the head with your analysis. You hit the nail on the head when you said she was unhappy at work. His analysis hit the nail on the head.

english_meaning: To say or do something exactly appropriate for the situation. To express something in a way that pleases or suits people. To produce the correct or desired effect through speech, action, or performance. To match the mood, tone, or expectation of an audience. To succeed in appealing to the feelings or opinions of others.
example_sentence: The president’s speech hit the right note with the grieving nation. Her apology hit the right note and calmed everyone down. The advertisement hit the right note with young viewers. His opening remarks hit the right note at the ceremony.

english_meaning: To start a journey, leave a place, or begin traveling.
example_sentence: It’s time to hit the road for our trip. It’s getting late; we should hit the road before sunset. After spending a week at the hotel, they finally hit the road for home. We need to hit the road early if we want to reach Karachi by noon. The police told the campers to hit the road because the park was closing.

english_meaning: To become extremely angry suddenly. To rise to a very high level, said of prices or figures.
example_sentence: My father hit the roof when he saw the broken window. Prices hit the roof during the shortage. She hit the roof when she heard the news. Rents in the city have hit the roof this year.

english_meaning: To go to bed or go to sleep. To stop activities for the day and go to bed in order to sleep. It is commonly used after a long or tiring day.
synonyms: ["Go to bed","Turn in","Go to sleep","Call it a night"]
antonyms: ["Stay awake","Pull an all nighter","Wake up","Get up"]
example_sentence: I am exhausted, so I am going to hit the sack early tonight. After studying all night, he finally hit the sack at dawn. Let us finish this work and hit the sack. She hit the sack as soon as she got home from the trip.

english_meaning: To set off on a journey or begin travelling. To leave a place and start moving on. To depart, especially after a period of rest or a visit. To begin a hike, ride, or long walk along a path.
example_sentence: It is getting late, so we should hit the trail. The hikers hit the trail just after sunrise. We packed our bags and hit the trail before the storm arrived. After a short break, the group hit the trail again.

english_meaning: To fasten or tie something. To pull or lift suddenly, or to get a free ride by stopping vehicles. A minor problem, difficulty, or delay that interrupts smooth progress. It can also mean a knot or a device used to fasten something.
example_sentence: The event went smoothly without any hitch. There was a small hitch in the plan due to bad weather. He hitched the rope to the pole firmly. She hitched her bag onto her shoulder and left.

english_meaning: Moving in different directions or here and there without any fixed order. Moving from one place to another in a scattered or aimless way.
example_sentence:
The children ran hither and thither in the park, chasing butterflies. Papers were scattered hither and thither across the floor after the wind blew in. 
People rushed hither and thither when the fire alarm rang. She looked hither and thither for her lost keys but couldn’t find them.

english_meaning: Until now or until the point in time under discussion. Up to this time or up to the present moment. Previously or before a specific point in time.
synonyms: ["Until Now","Up To Now","Previously","Heretofore","So Far","Up To This Point","Formerly","Ere Now","Until This Time","Till Now","Beforehand","In The Past"]
example_sentence: The scientist discovered a hitherto unknown species of frog in the rainforest. Hitherto, the team had suffered no defeats in the entire season. The quiet village was hitherto undisturbed by heavy industrial traffic. She revealed details about her life that were hitherto kept secret.

english_meaning: To place bees in a hive or to gather together. A home for bees or a busy place full of activity. A structure where bees live and produce honey. A place full of people working actively. A storage or shelter for bees, natural or man-made. A place full of energy and work. Refers to structured living systems of social insects like bees. To collect or store in one place.
example_sentence: The beekeeper checked the hive for honey. The office was a hive of activity before the deadline. Bees returned to the hive at sunset. They decided to hive the bees in a new box.

english_meaning: To collect and store away large amounts of money, food, valuable items, or supplies, often secretly and for future use. To accumulate and hide something out of fear, greed, or insecurity. A hidden store or stock of valuable things, especially money, treasure, or food that someone keeps for themselves rather than sharing or using.
example_sentence: During the crisis, many people began to hoard food and water at home. The miser used to hoard every coin he earned. Archaeologists discovered a huge hoard of ancient gold coins. It is unethical for traders to hoard essential goods during shortages. She kept a small hoard of chocolates hidden in her drawer.

english_meaning: Having a rough, weak, or harsh voice, usually because of illness, shouting, or overuse. A voice that sounds rough, raspy, or strained. This often happens due to throat infection, cold, excessive speaking, shouting, smoking, or dryness of the throat. A hoarse voice lacks clarity and smoothness.
example_sentence: After shouting all night, his voice became hoarse. She sounded hoarse because she had a bad cold. The singer rested because his throat felt hoarse. Speaking for hours made her voice hoarse and weak.

english_meaning: Grey or white with age, especially used to describe hair or beard. Very old, ancient, or belonging to a distant past. Covered with short, soft white or grey hairs, especially in plants. Figuratively, used to describe jokes, stories, or ideas that are so old they have become stale, worn out, or overused.
example_sentence: The hoary old man sat quietly in the corner of the mosque. He told the same hoary joke at every family gathering. The hoary peaks of the mountains were covered with snow. The professor began his lecture by quoting a hoary proverb. The leaves of the plant had a hoary appearance in the morning frost.

english_meaning: A trick or act of deception in which someone makes others believe that something false is true. A humorous or malicious plan intended to deceive people, usually with a false claim, story, or report. A fraud, prank, or made-up incident designed to mislead the public. As a verb, to deceive someone by means of such a trick.
example_sentence: The news about the alien landing turned out to be a complete hoax. He played a cruel hoax on his younger brother. The bomb threat was a hoax made by a college student. People were angry when they discovered that the email was a hoax. Some websites spread hoaxes to gain attention on social media.

english_meaning: A vulgar slang term used in informal American English, generally considered offensive and disrespectful, used to refer to women in a derogatory way, suggesting promiscuity or low character. The word is a combination of slang elements and is mostly used in rude or insulting speech. It is not used in polite, formal, or standard English.
example_sentence: The word hobags is considered highly offensive and should be avoided in polite conversation. Many people complained when the rapper used the word hobags in his song. Teachers warned the students never to use words like hobags in class. The film was criticised for using insulting terms such as hobags. Using words like hobags shows disrespect towards women.

english_meaning: An imaginary creature created by the British writer J. R. R. Tolkien in his famous novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. Hobbits are small, peaceful, human-like beings who live in cosy underground homes, love good food, comfort, and quiet country life, and have hairy feet. Figuratively, the word is sometimes used to describe a short, gentle, home-loving person.
example_sentence: Frodo is the most famous hobbit in Tolkien's novels. Children love reading stories about the adventures of a brave little hobbit. The film The Hobbit was based on Tolkien's classic book. He is so short and shy that his friends jokingly call him a hobbit. A hobbit's home is usually a cosy hole in the ground full of comfort.

english_meaning: To walk with difficulty because of pain or injury. To move awkwardly with a limp. To tie the legs of an animal to restrict movement. To hinder someone’s progress or ability. An awkward or unsteady walk.
example_sentence: He hobbled to the doctor after twisting his ankle. The old lady hobbled across the room with her cane. Farmers hobble their horses at night. Financial problems hobbled the company’s growth.

english_meaning: An activity done regularly for pleasure during one’s free time. A subject or pursuit followed for interest rather than as paid work. An enjoyable pastime used for relaxation or personal development.
example_sentence: Gardening is her favorite hobby. He turned his photography hobby into a career. A relaxing hobby can reduce stress. My hobbies include reading, cycling, and cooking.

english_meaning: A person who regularly does an activity for pleasure rather than as a profession. An amateur with a strong interest in a particular craft, subject, or pastime. Someone who practices a skill in their free time.
example_sentence: The camera is affordable enough for a hobbyist. A local gardening hobbyist won the flower competition. The workshop attracts both professionals and hobbyists. He began as a hobbyist before becoming a full-time carpenter.

english_meaning: To spend time with someone in a friendly or informal way, especially with people of higher social rank, wealth, or status. To mix or associate socially with important or influential people. To chat, drink, or socialise on familiar terms with others. Sometimes used with a slight hint of disapproval when someone tries to gain favour by mixing with the elite.
example_sentence: He loves to hobnob with film stars at every party he attends. She often hobnobs with politicians and businessmen at charity events. As a journalist, he had the chance to hobnob with world leaders. The young actor was seen hobnobbing with famous directors at the festival. People criticised the minister for hobnobbing with wealthy industrialists.

english_meaning: No real choice; take it or leave it. A situation in which there appears to be a choice, but in reality, there is only one option available. Named after Thomas Hobson, who offered customers only the horse nearest the door or none at all.
synonyms: ["Take it or leave it","Forced choice","No alternative"]
example_sentence: When offered the standard model, it was a Hobson’s choice for the buyers. He had a Hobson’s choice: accept the terms or lose the job. The committee gave us a Hobson’s choice between attending the meeting online or not at all. Faced with no other option, it was a Hobson’s choice to move abroad.

english_meaning: The joint in the back leg of a four-legged animal such as a horse, cow, or dog, equivalent to the human ankle. A cut of meat taken from the leg of a pig (ham hock) or other animal. As a verb (informal), to pawn something, that is, to leave a valuable item with a pawnbroker in exchange for money. Also used in the phrase 'in hock' meaning in debt.
example_sentence: The horse injured its hock while jumping over the fence. She slowly cooked the ham hock with vegetables and herbs. He had to hock his watch to pay the rent. The family was deep in hock after the long illness of their father. The vet examined the hock of the lame cow carefully.

english_meaning: Meaningless words spoken by a magician while performing a trick. Language or activity that is meant to deceive, obscure, or confuse people. A trick or deceptive action used to mislead others. To deceive or cheat someone using trickery.
example_sentence: The magician shouted hocus pocus and made the coin disappear. Do not fall for the financial advisor's economic hocus pocus. The agreement contained legal hocus pocus intended to hide the extra fees. He managed to hocus pocus the customers into buying outdated products.

english_meaning: A confused mixture or jumbled collection of different things. To form a disorganized or messy collection of various elements. A heterogeneous mass or medley of diverse ingredients. An untidy assortment or a mishmash of unrelated items. Something that is compiled without a coherent order or plan.
example_sentence: The artist's studio was a hodgepodge of half-finished canvases and old brushes. She decided to hodgepodge the leftover vegetables into a quick stew for dinner. His speech was a hodgepodge of disconnected ideas that failed to inspire the crowd. The antique shop displayed a hodgepodge of Victorian furniture and modern gadgets.

english_meaning: A person who loves travel, roads, and journeys. Someone who experiences a strong passion for exploring new destinations and cultures. An individual who feels happiest while on the move or planning upcoming trips.
example_sentence: Being a true hodophile, he spends all his savings on international backpacking trips. Her social media profile clearly showed that she was a hodophile who lived for adventure. A hodophile enjoys the journey just as much as reaching the final destination. Every weekend, the hodophile sets out to explore a new city or scenic road.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of travel or of being in transit. A person with hodophobia may avoid any form of travel including road trips, flights, or even short journeys.
example_sentence: Her hodophobia meant she had never left her hometown. His hodophobia was triggered by a bad car accident. Hodophobia can severely limit a person's career opportunities. She turned down the job offer abroad due to her hodophobia.

english_meaning: A man who keeps, rears, looks after, or deals in pigs (hogs); a swineherd or pig farmer. The word is now rare and is mostly found in older English texts. In some old dialects, it also refers to a person who drives pigs to market. (Not to be confused with 'Hogmanay', which is the Scottish word for New Year's Eve.)
example_sentence: The old hogman lived in a small hut near the pig farm. As a hogman, his job was to feed and look after the pigs every day. The hogman drove his herd of pigs to the village market. In the old days, every village had its own hogman. The novel described the simple life of a poor hogman in the countryside.

english_meaning: New Year’s Eve (31 December) and the celebrations that happen on that day. The last day of the year and the parties to celebrate it that start in the evening and continue until the next day.
synonyms: ["New Year’s Eve celebration","Year-end festival","Scottish New Year"]
example_sentence: We always attend the Hogmanay festival in Edinburgh. Their Hogmanay celebration included fireworks and music. First-footing is a key part of Hogmanay traditions. I sent my New Year greetings during Hogmanay.

english_meaning: Nonsense or foolish talk. Something that is untrue or ridiculous. Worthless or absurd statements. Ideas that have no truth or value. A term used to dismiss meaningless or dishonest remarks.
example_sentence: His claim of being a millionaire is complete hogwash. Don't believe such hogwash without checking the facts. The whole story turned out to be hogwash. She dismissed the rumors as pure hogwash.

english_meaning: To raise or lift something, especially by using ropes or machinery. It involves pulling or hauling an object upward to a higher position. It is commonly used in nautical, construction, or mechanical contexts.
example_sentence: The sailors worked together to hoist the heavy sails before the storm. Construction workers used a crane to hoist the steel beams to the top floor. They decided to hoist the national flag at the break of dawn. He managed to hoist the heavy suitcase onto the overhead rack.

english_meaning: Behaving in a way that suggests that you think you are more important than other people. Informal having or showing the insulting attitude of people who think that they are better, smarter, or more important than other people.
example_sentence: It is not a matter, therefore, of being hoity-toity about it on our part.

english_meaning: To control, restrain or stop something or someone. To keep emotions, information or actions from being expressed or released.
example_sentence: Don’t hold back your feelings. She held back her tears. The dam held back the water. Fear held him back from success.

english_meaning: To delay doing something or prevent it from happening. To postpone an action or decision, or to keep something away temporarily.
example_sentence: Let’s hold off on making the decision. The rain held off all day. They held off the attack. Hold off until we get more data.

english_meaning: Wait for a moment or stop what you’re doing. To pause, wait or not proceed yet. It can also mean to stay strong during a difficult situation or to physically keep a firm grip on something.
example_sentence: Hold on, I’ll be right there. Hold on to the railing. We have to hold on during tough times. Hold on while I get the key.

english_meaning: Be patient or wait before acting. To wait, be patient, or slow down, especially when someone is too eager or in a hurry to do something.
example_sentence: Hold your horses, we’ll leave soon. Hold your horses, we will leave after everyone arrives. You need to hold your horses before buying that car; check the price first. Hold your horses, I am not finished explaining the plan yet. Hold your horses, let’s think carefully before we decide.

english_meaning: To resist pressure or difficulty for some time. To survive or continue until help or change arrives. To offer something, usually a hand or an item. To expect or hope for something, often with patience.
example_sentence: They held out for better pay. The soldiers held out for three days. He held out his hand to greet her. We can’t hold out much longer.

english_meaning: To keep something under control or within limits. To restrain an emotion or a physical force. To prevent something from growing or spreading uncontrollably. To maintain order or balance by limiting an action.
example_sentence: The new regulations are designed to hold inflation in check. You must learn to hold your temper in check during arguments. The dam was built to hold the floodwaters in check. Security guards were stationed to hold the crowd in check.

english_meaning: It means to reflect or reveal the true nature of a person, society, or situation. The phrase describes exposing reality in a way that forces people to confront uncomfortable truths. It involves portraying things exactly as they are without any flattering alterations. The expression is used when art or literature accurately represents the characteristics of its time. It signifies an objective examination that shows the raw and unvarnished facts of an issue.
example_sentence: The controversial documentary aims to hold up a mirror to modern society. Her latest novel manages to hold up a mirror to the complexities of human relationships. Good satire should hold up a mirror to the flaws of political leadership. The investigation will hold up a mirror to the corruption within the department.

english_meaning: To refuse to retreat, yield, or change one's position under pressure. To defend a physical position against attack. To maintain an opinion, demand, or principle during disagreement. To remain steady and confident in a difficult situation
example_sentence: Despite the criticism, she held her ground and refused to change her opinion. The soldiers held their ground against the enemy attack. He held his ground during the negotiation and got a better deal. Even when everyone disagreed, the scientist held her ground on the evidence.

english_meaning: Wait, slow down, or be patient before acting. Used to tell someone to stop rushing, think carefully, or wait for more information before making a decision or taking action. It often carries a slightly informal or friendly tone.
synonyms: ["Wait a moment","Slow down","Be patient","Not so fast","Take it easy"]
example_sentence: Hold your horses, we have not finished the plan yet. He was about to invest all his money, but his friend said, hold your horses. Hold your horses before reacting to the news, it might not be true. She wanted to quit immediately, but her manager advised her to hold her horses.

english_meaning: To deliberately prevent, restrain, or delay someone or something from progressing or being expressed. An obstacle, limitation, or amount withheld. It can refer to emotional restraint, financial retention, or anything that stops movement or progress.
example_sentence: He tried not to holdback his opinions during the meeting. Financial issues held back the project for months. The company applied a holdback of 10% until the work was done. His lack of confidence is a holdback in his career. Legal issues caused a holdback in the property transfer. There was a holdback on the bonus payments this year.

english_meaning: To refuse to surrender, submit or give up while facing pressure or opposition. To resist someone or something.
example_sentence: They held out against the enemy. She held out against temptation. The workers held out against the unfair policy. We must hold out against fear.

english_meaning: To postpone something or continue it to a later time. To continue in a position or role for a short period.
example_sentence: The meeting was held over until Monday. The law was held over from last year. Let’s hold this issue over for now. The play was held over for another week.

english_meaning: To delay or stop progress. To support or keep something raised. To rob or stop someone using force. To remain strong or not break under pressure
example_sentence: Sorry I’m late, traffic held me up. The robbers held up the bank. The bridge is holding up well. He’s holding up under stress.

english_meaning: To agree with something or approve of it. To accept, support or approve an idea or behavior.
example_sentence: I don’t hold with lying. She doesn’t hold with violence. Do you hold with this idea? He doesn’t hold with wasting time.

english_meaning: The idea that something should be understood as a whole rather than only by looking at its separate parts. A theory, philosophy, or approach that emphasizes the importance of the complete system. It suggests that the characteristics and behavior of a whole cannot always be fully explained by studying its individual components separately. In medicine, education, psychology, ecology, and management, a holistic approach considers all related factors together.
example_sentence: The doctor’s approach was based on holism, considering the patient’s lifestyle and emotions. Holism suggests that analyzing individual cells cannot fully explain the behavior of a human body. In social sciences, holism looks at the entire community rather than just individuals. Environmental holism emphasizes the interconnectedness of all living organisms within an ecosystem.

english_meaning: Considering the entire system rather than isolated parts. Relating to the idea that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. Looking at physical, mental, emotional, social, and environmental factors together. Comprehensive and integrated in nature. Taking all aspects of a situation into account before making decisions.
example_sentence: The school adopted a holistic approach to education by focusing on character and skills. Holistic medicine focuses on the health of the entire body and mind rather than a single organ. We need a holistic strategy to solve the housing crisis in the city. Her holistic view of life includes regular meditation and a balanced diet.

english_meaning: To make empty or form a cavity. To remove the inside of something or create a space inside. A small valley or depression. A sunken or low area in the ground; a cavity or empty space. Empty inside. Having a space or cavity inside; lacking real value, substance, or sincerity.
example_sentence: They hollowed out the pumpkin for Halloween. He hollowed a hole in the log to store food. The children played in the forest hollow. The valley was a deep hollow between the mountains. The tree trunk was hollow and could shelter small animals. The hollow sound of the drum echoed in the hall.

english_meaning: To remove the inside of something so it becomes empty. To scoop out or carve out the inner part of an object. It can also mean to weaken something by taking away its core strength.
example_sentence: They hollowed out the pumpkin to make a lantern. The workers hollowed out a tunnel through the mountain. Constant budget cuts hollowed out the department over the years. She hollowed out the bread to make space for the filling.

english_meaning: To remove the core or essential part from something. To take away the central or most important part of an object, idea, or system, leaving it empty or weakened.
example_sentence: The corruption hollowed out of the institution’s credibility. Over time, greed hollowed out of the organization’s values. Mining hollowed out of the mountain’s core. The scandal hollowed out of the community’s trust.

english_meaning: To fill or support something weak. To reinforce, fill in, or support a hollow or weak spot in a structure or object.
example_sentence: They hollowed up the weak wall with bricks. The engineer hollowed up the trench to prevent collapse. He hollowed up the holes in the old fence. The cracks were hollowed up with cement.

english_meaning: A success that brings little joy, value, or lasting benefit. A victory achieved at such a high cost that it feels like a loss. An apparent triumph that fails to solve the underlying problem. A win that is morally unsatisfying or emotionally empty.
example_sentence: Winning the case felt like a hollow victory after years of conflict. The team earned a hollow victory because its best players were injured. His promotion was a hollow victory without the respect of his colleagues. Forcing an apology would only produce a hollow victory.

english_meaning: A large scale destruction or massacre, especially by fire. A catastrophic destruction or slaughter of people. A mass killing, especially by fire or nuclear disaster. Historically, it refers to the systematic genocide of about six million Jews and millions of others by Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler between 1941 and 1945.
example_sentence: The atomic explosion caused a terrible holocaust in the city. The museum displays photographs from the Holocaust to educate future generations. Survivors of the Holocaust shared their painful memories. Many historians study the Holocaust to understand the dangers of hatred and extremism.

english_meaning: Special respect, honour, or admiration shown publicly for a person, achievement, work of art, or memory. A formal act, ceremony, speech, or tribute paid in recognition of someone's greatness, service, or sacrifice. In old feudal times, a public ceremony in which a vassal swore loyalty to his lord. A sincere expression of devotion, reverence, or tribute.
example_sentence: The whole nation paid homage to the brave martyrs of the war. The poet wrote a beautiful poem in homage to his mother. Thousands of people gathered to pay homage to the late leader. The film is a homage to the golden age of cinema. Soldiers stood silently in homage at the war memorial.

english_meaning: A person who prefers staying at home rather than going out. Someone who enjoys quiet domestic life and avoids socialising. A friend or companion with whom one shares a home or stays in.
example_sentence: She is a home buddy who spends weekends reading. My brother is a home buddy and rarely goes to parties. As a home buddy, he turned his living room into a studio. They became home buddies during the long rainy season.

english_meaning: A person who prefers to stay at home rather than go out. Someone who enjoys domestic life. A person who feels most comfortable in their home. An individual who avoids social gatherings. A stay-at-home type.
example_sentence: She is a homebody who loves reading in her room. He became a homebody after retirement. Homebodies enjoy cooking and watching movies at home. Being a homebody, she rarely attends parties.

english_meaning: An organism that maintains a relatively constant internal body temperature regardless of changes in the surrounding environment. A homeothermic animal can regulate its body temperature through physiological processes such as sweating, shivering, panting, or adjusting blood flow. Most mammals and birds are homeothermic. This ability helps them remain active in a wide range of environmental conditions.
example_sentence: Humans are homeothermic and can maintain a stable body temperature in different climates. Most birds are homeothermic, allowing them to remain active during cold weather. A homeothermic animal uses various biological mechanisms to regulate its body heat. The homeothermic nature of mammals helps them survive in diverse environments.

english_meaning: Experiencing a longing for one's home during a period of absence from it. Feeling sad or depressed because one is away from family and familiar surroundings. Missing one's native land or hometown intensely.
example_sentence: She felt extremely homesick during her first week at the boarding school. The soldiers often grew homesick after months of deployment overseas. Listening to traditional music made him feel deeply homesick. I bought a plane ticket back because I was too homesick to continue the trip.

english_meaning: Cloth that is woven or spun at home, usually plain, simple, and coarse in texture. Made of such cloth. By extension, anything that is simple, plain, unsophisticated, and lacking in fancy style; especially used for ideas, advice, philosophy, or wisdom that is straightforward and based on common sense rather than on formal learning.
example_sentence: She wore a long homespun dress made by her grandmother. His grandfather often shared bits of homespun wisdom at the dinner table. The villagers wore simple homespun clothes throughout the winter. The speech was full of homespun humour that made everyone laugh. The cottage had a warm, homespun atmosphere that made guests feel at home.

english_meaning: Comfortable and pleasant in a way that reminds one of home. Simple, warm, and unpretentious in style or atmosphere. Informally, a close friend from one's neighbourhood.
example_sentence: The little cafe has a homey atmosphere. She decorated the room to make it feel homey. Guests praised the homey comfort of the guest house. He greeted his old homey with a warm hug.

english_meaning: Likely or intending to kill another person. Relating to the crime of killing a human being. Showing violent rage that could lead to murder.
example_sentence: The patient was described as homicidal and dangerous. Police investigated a homicidal attack in the city centre. He flew into a homicidal rage during the argument. The court ordered treatment for his homicidal tendencies.

english_meaning: The killing of one person by another. The legal term for causing the death of a human being, whether lawful or unlawful. A person who kills another. A police department division dealing with murder cases.
example_sentence: The police are treating the death as a homicide. He was charged with homicide after the investigation. Homicide rates have fallen in the past decade. Two detectives from homicide arrived at the scene.

english_meaning: An informal word for a close friend from one's own neighbourhood. A trusted companion or member of one's group. A friendly term of address used among peers in casual speech.
example_sentence: He went to the match with his homies. Thanks for the help, homie. She has been my homie since primary school. The song is a tribute to his homies back home.

english_meaning: A religious talk or sermon given during a church service. A lecture that offers moral advice or guidance. A tedious speech about how someone should behave.
example_sentence: The priest delivered a short homily on forgiveness. We had to listen to another homily about punctuality. Her homily moved many people in the congregation. He ended the lesson with a gentle homily.

english_meaning: Relating to the ability of an animal to find its way back home. Describing a device that guides itself towards a target or signal. Moving steadily towards a particular place or objective.
example_sentence: Homing pigeons can travel hundreds of miles. The missile uses a homing device to track its target. Scientists study the homing instinct of sea turtles. The signal helped the homing system locate the ship.

english_meaning: An extinct species of early human that lived in Africa and Asia roughly two million to one hundred thousand years ago. An ancestor of modern humans known for walking fully upright, using stone tools, and possibly controlling fire. A key stage in human evolution between Homo habilis and Homo sapiens.
example_sentence: Fossils of Homo erectus have been found across Africa and Asia. Homo erectus was among the first humans to walk fully upright. The museum displays a reconstructed skull of Homo erectus. Scientists believe Homo erectus learned to control fire.

english_meaning: An extinct early species of the genus Homo, living about two million years ago in Africa. An early human ancestor known for making simple stone tools. The species whose name means 'handy man'.
example_sentence: Homo habilis is regarded as one of the earliest members of our genus. Fossils of Homo habilis were found in East Africa. Homo habilis made simple stone tools. The brain of Homo habilis was larger than that of earlier hominins.

english_meaning: The scientific name for the species to which all modern human beings belong. The only living species of the genus Homo, characterized by upright walking, a large brain, and the ability to use language and tools. A term used to refer to human beings as a biological species.
example_sentence: Homo sapiens first appeared in Africa hundreds of thousands of years ago. Scientists study fossils to understand how Homo sapiens evolved. Homo sapiens are the only species known to create complex languages. Climate change forced early Homo sapiens to migrate to new regions.

english_meaning: A person who practises homoeopathy as a system of alternative medicine. A practitioner who treats patients with highly diluted natural substances based on the principle that like cures like. A medical practitioner trained in homoeopathic treatment rather than conventional medicine.
example_sentence: She visited a homoeopath for her long-standing allergy. The homoeopath prescribed a course of diluted remedies. Many families in the town still consult a local homoeopath. He trained as a homoeopath before opening his own clinic.

english_meaning: A system of alternative medicine based on treating illness with very small, highly diluted doses of natural substances. A therapeutic method founded on the principle that a substance causing symptoms in a healthy person can cure similar symptoms in a sick person. The practice and theory of homoeopathic treatment.
example_sentence: She turned to homoeopathy after conventional treatment failed. Homoeopathy remains popular in several parts of the world. Doctors continue to debate the effectiveness of homoeopathy. He studied homoeopathy for four years before practising.

english_meaning: The tendency of a living organism to maintain a stable and balanced internal environment. The biological process by which body temperature, blood sugar, and fluid levels are kept within a narrow healthy range. Any system's ability to regulate itself and remain steady despite external changes.
example_sentence: Homoeostasis keeps our body temperature close to thirty-seven degrees. The kidneys play a vital role in maintaining homoeostasis. Illness often disturbs the body's normal homoeostasis. The teacher explained homoeostasis with a simple thermostat example.

english_meaning: Relating to or arousing sexual desire between people of the same sex. Describing art, literature, or imagery that expresses same-sex attraction. Concerning feelings, themes, or undertones of same-sex romantic or physical attraction.
example_sentence: Critics noted the homoerotic imagery in the poet's later work. The film was praised for its subtle homoerotic themes. Scholars debated the homoerotic undertones of the ancient text. The exhibition explored homoerotic art from the last century.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being similar or uniform in structure, type, or character. The condition in which all parts or members of something are alike in nature, composition, or characteristics.
example_sentence: The cultural homogeneity of the village made communication easier among residents. Scientists tested the chemical mixture to ensure its homogeneity. The committee lacked homogeneity because members had very different viewpoints. Social homogeneity can sometimes limit exposure to new ideas.

english_meaning: Of the same kind, type, or nature throughout. Consisting of parts or elements that are all alike or similar in character, quality, or composition. Uniform in structure, appearance, or thought. Used in science to describe a substance or mixture that has the same composition throughout, and in society to describe a group whose members share similar features such as race, religion, or culture.
example_sentence: The class was made up of a homogeneous group of engineering students. Milk and water do not form a truly homogeneous mixture without mixing. The society in that small town is very homogeneous in its traditions. The company prefers a homogeneous team to ensure smooth coordination. The surface of the metal sheet was perfectly smooth and homogeneous.

english_meaning: Made uniform in composition throughout. Of milk, treated so that the cream does not separate from it. Made all the same, often losing individual character.
example_sentence: We only buy homogenized milk. The mixture is homogenized before bottling. Critics say the town has become homogenized by chain stores. Modern media has homogenized popular taste.

english_meaning: A word that is spelled the same as another but has a different meaning and sometimes a different pronunciation. One of two or more words with identical spelling but distinct senses.
example_sentence: 'Lead' the metal and 'lead' the verb are homographs. Homographs can confuse young readers. The dictionary lists homographs as separate entries. 'Bow' is a homograph with two pronunciations.

english_meaning: Having the same relation, relative position, value, or structure. In biology, used for body parts of different species that have a common evolutionary origin, even though they may now perform different functions, such as the human arm and a whale's flipper. In chemistry, used for compounds belonging to the same series with similar properties. In general, corresponding or matching in nature.
example_sentence: The wings of a bird and the arms of a human are homologous structures. Scientists study homologous organs to understand evolution. Methane and ethane are part of a homologous series of compounds. The two languages share many homologous words from a common root. The two committees have homologous functions in their respective organisations.

english_meaning: A word that has the same spelling or pronunciation as another word but a different meaning. Two or more words that sound alike or look alike yet differ in sense and often in origin. A term used in grammar for words identical in form but distinct in meaning.
example_sentence: The words bat and bat are classic homonyms in English. Learners often confuse homonyms while writing. The teacher gave a list of homonyms for practice. Bank and bank form a well-known pair of homonyms.

english_meaning: A person who feels or shows hatred, fear, or strong prejudice towards homosexual people. Someone who discriminates against others because of their sexual orientation. An individual with hostile attitudes towards gay, lesbian, or bisexual people.
example_sentence: The club expelled the member for behaving like a homophobe. He was widely criticised online as a homophobe. Schools run programmes to teach students not to become homophobes. The comment revealed him to be an unapologetic homophobe.

english_meaning: Fear or dislike of gay people. Fear, hatred, prejudice, or negative attitudes toward homosexual people or same sex relationships. It can appear in beliefs, language, behavior, laws, or social practices that discriminate against LGBTQ+ individuals.
example_sentence: Homophobia can prevent people from living openly and honestly. Schools should work actively to reduce homophobia among students. Laws against discrimination help combat homophobia in society. Education plays a key role in challenging homophobia and stereotypes.

english_meaning: Having or showing a strong dislike, fear, or prejudice against homosexual people. Relating to attitudes or behavior that discriminate against gay people. Characterized by an irrational fear or hatred of homosexuality.
example_sentence: The organization campaigns against homophobic bullying in schools. His homophobic remarks were widely criticized by the public. The law was introduced to protect people from homophobic discrimination. She challenged her colleague's homophobic attitude during the meeting.

english_meaning: A word that sounds the same as another but differs in meaning, and often in spelling. One of two or more words pronounced alike but written differently. A same-sounding word such as 'see' and 'sea'.
example_sentence: 'Flour' and 'flower' are homophones. Homophones often cause spelling mistakes. The teacher gave a list of common homophones. 'Right' and 'write' are a well-known pair of homophones.

english_meaning: Having the same pronunciation as another word but a different meaning, origin, or spelling. Relating to words that sound alike but differ in meaning. In music, relating to a texture in which all the parts move together in the same rhythm.
example_sentence: The words "bare" and "bear" are homophonous in English. Students often confuse homophonous words in their writing. "Flour" and "flower" are homophonous but have very different meanings. The hymn was sung in a homophonous style, with all voices moving together.

english_meaning: To engage in sexual activity with someone of the same sex. A person who is sexually attracted to the same sex.
example_sentence: The law criminalized people who homosex in public. The documentary explores how teens homosex despite social pressures. He refuses to homosex openly due to fear of discrimination. The conference discussed the challenges faced by homosex individuals. Homosex rights are gaining more recognition globally.

english_meaning: A person who is attracted to people of the same sex.
example_sentence: He came out as homosexual to his friends. The novel explores the life of a homosexual man in a conservative town. Many countries now protect homosexual rights legally. She supports homosexual couples in adopting children.

english_meaning: To sharpen, improve, refine, or develop a skill, ability, tool, or quality through practice and effort. To make something better, sharper, more effective, or more skillful over time. It can refer to physically sharpening a blade or improving talents, knowledge, techniques, and abilities through continuous practice and experience.
example_sentence: She spent years honing her writing skills. The chef honed his cooking techniques through daily practice. Athletes train regularly to hone their performance. He honed his communication skills to become a better manager.

english_meaning: A sweet sticky substance made by bees from flower nectar. A yellowish-brown color resembling honey. An affectionate form of address for someone loved. Something especially pleasant, excellent, or attractive. To sweeten, flatter, or make pleasant with honey or charm.
example_sentence: She stirred a spoonful of honey into her tea. Honey bees stored fresh honey in the comb. Are you ready to leave, honey? The roasted carrots were honeyed with a light glaze.

english_meaning: Speaking in a very sweet, charming, or persuasive way. Skilled at using flattering language. Pleasant in speech but sometimes insincere or deceptive. Smooth-spoken and able to influence others easily.
example_sentence: The honey-tongued salesman persuaded them to buy the expensive package. She distrusted the honey-tongued adviser and checked every claim. A honey-tongued speaker welcomed the guests to the ceremony. His honey-tongued apology softened their anger.

english_meaning: Sweetened with honey or tasting of honey. Having a warm golden-yellow colour like honey. Of a voice or words, soft, smooth, and pleasing to listen to. Flattering or persuasive in a way that may not be sincere.
example_sentence: She served honeyed cakes with green tea. The evening light gave the walls a honeyed glow. He spoke in honeyed tones to calm the angry crowd. Do not be fooled by his honeyed words.

english_meaning: A holiday taken by a couple soon after their marriage. An early period of happiness and harmony in a relationship or situation. A temporary period in which a new leader, employee, or policy receives goodwill and little criticism. To spend a honeymoon. To begin with an unusually pleasant period.
example_sentence: They spent their honeymoon near a quiet lake. The new manager enjoyed a brief honeymoon with the staff. The couple plans to honeymoon in Turkey. Once the honeymoon ended, the coalition faced serious disagreements.

english_meaning: A person spending a holiday immediately after getting married. One member of a newly married couple on a honeymoon. A newlywed traveler celebrating marriage. Figuratively, someone enjoying an early period of enthusiasm or harmony.
example_sentence: The hotel prepared a special suite for each honeymooner. Honeymooners often visit the island in spring. The young honeymooner photographed every sunset. As political honeymooners, the partners initially agreed on every issue.

english_meaning: A container used for storing honey. Something attractive that draws people toward it. A person, place, or opportunity used as a lure or trap. A computer system or resource deliberately set up to attract and detect cyberattackers. A desirable area that attracts investment, visitors, or activity.
example_sentence: The old ceramic honeypot sat beside the breakfast tray. The police used the abandoned warehouse as a honeypot for thieves. The security team deployed a honeypot to study suspicious network activity. Low taxes turned the region into a honeypot for new businesses.

english_meaning: A climbing or shrubby plant with fragrant tubular flowers. Any plant of the genus Lonicera. The sweet-smelling flowers of this plant. A flowering vine often grown over walls, fences, and arches.
example_sentence: Honeysuckle climbed over the wooden garden fence. The evening air carried the scent of honeysuckle. Bees gathered around the pale honeysuckle flowers. She planted honeysuckle beside the front gate.

english_meaning: High respect, esteem, or recognition given to someone. A source of credit or distinction. Adherence to what is right or to a conventional standard of conduct. To regard with great respect. To fulfill an obligation or keep an agreement.
example_sentence: It is a great honor to receive this award. We must honor our parents and teachers. The soldier fought bravely to defend his country's honor. The company always honors its commitments to customers.

english_meaning: Given as an honour or mark of respect rather than for actual work, qualifications, or payment. Used for titles, degrees, memberships, or positions awarded to a person in recognition of their achievements, services, or status. Such positions usually carry no salary, formal duties, or active responsibilities and are mainly symbolic in nature.
example_sentence: The university awarded him an honorary doctorate for his services to literature. She was appointed as the honorary president of the women's welfare society. He works as the honorary secretary of the local sports club. The retired general was given an honorary rank in the new force. Several writers received honorary memberships of the literary academy.

english_meaning: Deserving respect, praise, and admiration because of good character or behaviour. Acting in a way that is honest, fair, and morally right. Used as a title of respect for certain high officials, judges, and members of parliament. Bringing credit, dignity, or a good reputation to someone. Showing a strong sense of duty and moral principles.
example_sentence: He is an honourable man who always keeps his word. She made an honourable decision to resign from the post. The Honourable Justice will hear the case tomorrow. Serving one's country is considered an honourable duty.

english_meaning: A violent criminal. A gangster. A tough and aggressive young man involved in crime or violence. A member of a gang of street thugs. A person who behaves in a rough, lawless, and threatening way, often as part of a group, and is associated with petty crime, vandalism, or organized criminal activity.
example_sentence: A gang of hoodlums attacked the shopkeeper at night. The police arrested several hoodlums during the raid. He grew up in a neighborhood plagued by hoodlums. The film portrays the life of a young hoodlum in the city. The hoodlums smashed the windows of the parked cars.

english_meaning: To deceive, trick, or mislead someone.
example_sentence: He hoodwinked the old lady into giving him money. The company hoodwinked customers with false promises. Don’t let them hoodwink you into signing the contract. They tried to hoodwink the public with fake news.

english_meaning: The hard, horny covering at the end of the foot of certain mammals such as horses, cows, goats, sheep, deer, and camels, on which the animal stands and walks. As a verb (informal), to walk, kick, or travel on foot. The word is also used in expressions like 'on the hoof', meaning while moving, or 'hoof it', meaning to walk briskly.
example_sentence: The blacksmith carefully cleaned the horse's hoof before fitting a new shoe. The cattle's hooves left deep marks in the muddy field. The deer's hoof was injured by a sharp stone. We had to hoof it all the way to the next village. The farmer noticed an infection in one of the cow's hooves.

english_meaning: To connect or link devices, people, or systems, can also mean to meet socially or romantically.
example_sentence: Can you hook up the printer? They hooked up last summer. We got hooked up with a new supplier. He hooked up his phone to Wi-Fi.

english_meaning: A person (especially woman) who offers sexual services in exchange for money. A player in rugby who throws the ball into a scrum or lineout. Someone who catches or pulls something using a hook. A type of small sailing vessel.
synonyms: ["Prostitute","Sex worker","Call girl","Front row player","Catcher","Puller","Fishing boat","Small vessel"]
example_sentence: The police arrested a hooker during the late night patrol. The hooker threw the ball perfectly into the lineout. The fisherman acted as a hooker, pulling the nets with a metal hook. The old records mention a hooker that traded along the coast.

english_meaning: A person who behaves violently or disruptively in public. Someone who engages in rowdy, violent, or antisocial behavior, often in a public place, and ignores social rules or laws. Commonly used for troublemakers at sports events or riots.
example_sentence: The football match was delayed because a group of hooligans started fighting in the stands. Hooligans vandalized the park after the concert. The police arrested several hooligans causing chaos in the city center. Parents warned their children to stay away from hooligans in the neighborhood.

english_meaning: Disruptive, aggressive, or unlawful behavior, often associated with groups of people in public places, sports events, or protests. It usually involves vandalism, fighting, or creating chaos.
example_sentence: The police arrested several youths for hooliganism after the football match. Hooliganism in the city center caused damage to shops and vehicles. The government promised strict action against hooliganism at public events. His arrest was linked to an act of hooliganism at a concert.
