english_meaning: To bind or surround with a ring. To fasten, bind, or strengthen something by fitting a circular band around it, such as placing hoops around a barrel. A round ring or circular frame. A circular ring made of metal, wood, or plastic. It is used in games, sports like basketball, performances, or to hold objects together such as barrels.
example_sentence: The workers hooped the barrel tightly. The wooden tub was hooped with iron bands. Farmers hoop large containers for storage. The craftsman hooped the frame to give it strength.

english_meaning: Hope never dies. Aways keep hoping, even in difficult situations. (saying) people never stop hoping. It reflects the idea that human beings naturally remain optimistic, no matter how bad things get.
synonyms: ["Optimism never dies","There is always hope","Faith endures","Keep believing","Positive outlook"]
antonyms: ["Hope fades away","Despair takes over","Losing faith","Giving up","Pessimism"]
example_sentence: Even after many failures, she hasn’t given up, hope springs eternal. Though the crops failed this year, the farmers are planting again because hope springs eternal. He has been looking for a job for months, but he hasn’t given up, hope springs eternal.

english_meaning: A large group or crowd of people. A large number of people moving in a disorderly way. A nomadic tribe or wandering group. A swarm of insects or animals.
example_sentence: A horde of shoppers rushed into the store at opening time. Hordes of tourists visit the valley every summer. The ancient hordes swept across the plains. A horde of mosquitoes ruined our evening.

english_meaning: The line where the earth or sea seems to meet the sky. The apparent line that separates the earth from the sky. The limit of a person’s knowledge, experience, or interest. The range or scope of something such as ideas or opportunities. A boundary or limit that can be physical or imaginary.
example_sentence: The sun slowly disappeared below the horizon. New experiences can broaden your horizon. The ship sailed toward the distant horizon. Education helps expand our horizons in life.

english_meaning: Lying flat and parallel to the ground. Going from side to side rather than up and down. Level with the horizon. Relating to people or units of the same rank or level.
example_sentence: Draw a horizontal line across the chart. The patient must remain in a horizontal position. The shelf is not perfectly horizontal. The two firms agreed on a horizontal merger.

english_meaning: Relating to hormones or the glands that produce them. Caused or influenced by hormones in the body. Concerning changes in the body due to hormone activity. Relating to emotional or physical changes driven by hormone levels.
example_sentence: Teenagers often experience hormonal changes during puberty. Her mood swings were caused by hormonal imbalance. The doctor recommended a hormonal test to check her thyroid. Hormonal treatments can help patients with certain conditions.

english_meaning: A chemical substance produced in the body that regulates the activity of cells or organs. A natural compound made by glands and carried by the blood to control body functions. Any of the chemical messengers that influence growth, mood, or metabolism. A synthetic version of such a substance used in medicine.
example_sentence: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar levels. The body releases stress hormones during difficult situations. Growth hormone plays an important role in children's development. Doctors sometimes prescribe hormone therapy for certain patients.

english_meaning: Extremely angry or furious, like a bull ready to attack. In a state of raging madness or uncontrolled fury. So angry that one loses all reason or self-control. Wildly enraged, especially over jealousy or betrayal. Driven to fury, often in an old-fashioned literary sense.
example_sentence: He was horn-mad when he heard about the betrayal. She became horn-mad after losing all her savings. The manager was horn-mad at the team's careless mistake. Do not go near him now, he is completely horn-mad.

english_meaning: A large, powerful kind of social wasp with a painful sting, usually brown, yellow, or red in colour, that lives in big paper nests and is known for its aggressive behaviour when disturbed. Figuratively, used to describe an angry, irritable, or dangerous person. The phrase 'stir up a hornets' nest' means to cause a sudden and dangerous reaction.
example_sentence: A hornet flew into the room and frightened the children. He was stung by a hornet while working in the garden. Their constant complaints stirred up a hornet's nest in the office. The angry old man was as fierce as a hornet. Hornets build their large grey nests under the roof of old buildings.

english_meaning: The study or measurement of time and the art of making clocks and watches.
example_sentence: He studied horology to become a master watchmaker. The museum has an exhibition on the history of horology. Modern horology involves highly precise mechanical and electronic devices. Horology enthusiasts often collect antique clocks and watches.

english_meaning: Something that is extremely unpleasant, horrifying, or dreadful. Often used to describe situations, events, or actions that provoke fear, shock, or disgust.
example_sentence: The accident left a horrendous mess on the highway. She endured a horrendous experience during the storm. The film depicted the horrendous effects of war. His horrendous behavior shocked everyone at the meeting.

english_meaning: Extremely or shockingly bad. In a way that causes horror, shock, or is extremely unpleasant, severe, or terrible.
example_sentence: The movie was horrendously scary for the children. He was paid horrendously low for his hard work. The roads were horrendously congested during the festival. She handled the situation horrendously, making it worse.

english_meaning: Causing horror; very unpleasant. Extremely disagreeable or nasty in behaviour. Unkind and cruel towards others.
example_sentence: What a horrid smell is coming from the kitchen. Do not be horrid to your little sister. The weather has been horrid all week. He had a horrid dream and woke up frightened.

english_meaning: Filled with horror, fear, shock, or disgust. Deeply disturbed by something frightening or offensive. Terrified or appalled. Made to feel extreme alarm or moral revulsion.
example_sentence: She was horrified by the cruelty in the report. The audience looked horrified when the accident happened. I was horrified to find the door wide open. His parents were horrified by the dangerous stunt.

english_meaning: To fill someone with deep fear, terror, shock, disgust, or great horror. To cause a strong feeling of dread, alarm, or moral outrage. To shock someone so much that they are unable to react normally. Often used when a sight, news, act, or behaviour is so terrible that it disturbs people emotionally or morally.
example_sentence: The terrible news of the accident horrified the entire family. The cruel treatment of the prisoners horrified the world. Scenes of the war continue to horrify viewers even today. His rude behaviour horrified all the guests at the dinner. The teacher was horrified by the children's poor exam results.

english_meaning: The condition of having one's hair stand on end, especially due to cold, fear, or strong emotion. The medical term for goose bumps. A reaction of the skin in which tiny bumps appear and hair rises. It can occur from chills, excitement, or intense emotional experiences.
example_sentence: The horror movie caused horripilation throughout my body. The sudden cold breeze led to horripilation on her arms. He felt horripilation while listening to the national anthem. Fear gripped him and horripilation spread over his skin. The story of the haunted house gave the children horripilation.

english_meaning: To behave in a silly, noisy, or playful way, often when you should be serious. Acting in a playful, careless, or foolish manner. It often involves joking, teasing, or rough play, especially in situations where such behavior is inappropriate, like in school, workplace, or during serious tasks.
example_sentence: The teacher told the students to stop horsing around and focus on their work. They were horsing around in the playground and accidentally broke a window. Stop horsing around and listen carefully to the instructions. The kids love to horse around when no one is watching.

english_meaning: A unit for measuring the power of engines, equal to about 746 watts or 550 foot-pounds of work per second. The rate at which work is done or energy is transferred, originally defined by comparing engines to the work of horses.
example_sentence: The sports car has an engine with over four hundred horsepower. One horsepower equals approximately 746 watts. Farmers once measured tractors in horsepower to compare them with horses. The motor delivers enough horsepower to pull the heavy trailer.

english_meaning: Giving strong encouragement or advice. Used for speech or writing that urges, advises, or encourages people to act in a particular moral or practical way. It often sounds persuasive and motivational rather than neutral.
example_sentence: The teacher gave a hortatory speech encouraging students to work honestly. His writing has a hortatory tone that urges social reform. The leader’s hortatory message inspired people to help the poor. The article was hortatory rather than informative.

english_meaning: The friendly, generous, and warm reception, welcome, and treatment of guests, visitors, or strangers. The quality or practice of being hospitable, kind, and welcoming. The business or industry concerned with providing food, drink, accommodation, and entertainment to guests, including hotels, restaurants, and resorts. A polite way of showing care, respect, and good manners towards others.
example_sentence: Sindhi people are famous all over the world for their warm hospitality. The hotel is known for its excellent hospitality and friendly service. Many young people now study hospitality management as a career. We will always remember the hospitality of our hosts in the village. Her hospitality made every guest feel like a member of the family.

english_meaning: To send or admit a person to a hospital for medical care, observation, or treatment. To place under hospital care because of illness, injury, or surgery. The word is mainly used in formal, medical, or news contexts when a patient needs continuous treatment that cannot be given at home.
example_sentence: Doctors decided to hospitalize the patient after his condition got worse. The injured workers were immediately hospitalized after the accident. Her father had to be hospitalized for surgery last week. During the epidemic, hundreds of people were hospitalized in a single day. He was hospitalized for high fever and weakness for three days.

english_meaning: A person who receives or entertains guests. A large number of people or things. In computing, a computer that provides data or services to others. To organize and hold an event or gathering. In biology, an organism on or in which a parasite lives.
example_sentence: She was the perfect host at last night's dinner party. A whole host of problems came up during the project. The website is hosted on a fast server. They will host the international conference next year.

english_meaning: A person who is captured and held prisoner by a person or group, and who may be injured or killed if people do not do what the person or group is asking.
example_sentence: Three children were taken hostage during bank robbery. He was held hostage for almost a year. The rebels took several villagers as hostages. Negotiators worked to secure the hostage’s release. He was held hostage until the ransom was paid. The children were used as hostages during the conflict.

english_meaning: A woman who receives or entertains guests. A female employed to welcome customers in a restaurant or club. A woman who introduces a television or radio show. The feminine form of host. A woman who organizes a social event.
example_sentence: The hostess greeted every guest with a warm smile. She works as a hostess at a five-star restaurant. The talk show hostess interviewed a famous author. Their hostess had arranged a lovely dinner for them.

english_meaning: Unfriendly, aggressive, opposed, or showing dislike and anger toward someone or something. A person, attitude, action, environment, or situation that is unfriendly, antagonistic, aggressive, or opposed. It can refer to people showing anger or hatred, groups in conflict, or conditions that are unfavorable to growth, success, or survival.
example_sentence: The manager became hostile when employees questioned his decision. The two neighboring countries have maintained hostile relations for many years. She received a hostile response after expressing her opinion online. Some plants cannot survive in a hostile environment with extreme temperatures.

english_meaning: A witness who gives evidence against the party that called them. A person in court who becomes uncooperative or changes their statement. A witness treated as adverse and allowed to be cross-examined by their own side.
example_sentence: The prosecution declared him a hostile witness. She turned hostile witness during the trial. A hostile witness can weaken the entire case. The judge allowed cross-examination of the hostile witness.

english_meaning: Unfriendly or aggressive behavior toward someone. Strong opposition or resistance to a person, idea, or thing. A feeling of intense dislike or enmity. The state of being hostile. Acts of warfare or armed conflict between groups or nations. Hostility describes both emotional antagonism shown through words and actions and the open conflict that arises between individuals, groups, or nations when relations break down.
example_sentence: There was open hostility between the two neighboring tribes. She faced hostility from her colleagues when she suggested major changes. The peace talks aim to end years of hostility between the two nations. His comments were met with surprising hostility from the audience. Hostilities resumed after the brief ceasefire collapsed.

english_meaning: To make someone or something hostile. To cause antagonism or enmity between people. To turn a person or group against another. To create feelings of opposition or aggression. To provoke hostility. Refers to the act of making relations unfriendly or causing one party to develop hostile feelings or behavior toward another.
example_sentence: His harsh remarks only served to hostilize the local community further. Unfair policies can hostilize even the most loyal employees. The leader's actions hostilized neighboring countries against his nation. Repeated insults will hostilize anyone over time. Such propaganda is designed to hostilize one group against another.

english_meaning: An old or rare English word meaning an inn, lodging, or place where travellers could find food and shelter for the night, including a stable for their horses. A hostelry; a guest house. The word is now archaic and is rarely used in modern English except in literature, history, or old poetry.
example_sentence: The weary travellers reached the old hostry just before sunset. Long ago, every main road had a hostry for caravans and traders. The poet described a quiet hostry standing beside the river. They spent the cold night at a small hostry near the mountain pass. Few hostries from that era still survive today.

english_meaning: Following someone or something very closely and about to catch them. Close behind a person, animal, or thing being pursued. Very near to discovering or finding what is being searched for.
example_sentence: The police were hot on the tracks of the escaped prisoner. Reporters were hot on the tracks of the missing documents. The dogs stayed hot on the tracks of the wounded deer. Our team is hot on the tracks of a major discovery.

english_meaning: Very close to catching or finding someone or something. Actively pursuing a person, animal, or clue with little distance remaining. Near to solving a mystery or uncovering the truth.
example_sentence: Detectives are hot on the trail of the missing painting. The hunter was hot on the trail of the wounded animal. Journalists were hot on the trail of a political scandal. She felt she was hot on the trail of the answer.

english_meaning: A very bright, vivid shade of pink with a strong purple-red tone. A colour of intense pink used in fashion, design, and printing. Describing something coloured in such a bright pink shade.
example_sentence: She wore a hot pink dress to the party. The poster was printed in hot pink and black. Hot pink was the dominant colour of the summer collection. He painted the bicycle hot pink.

english_meaning: Feeling very angry, annoyed, or embarrassed, especially because of something unfair, insulting, or frustrating.
example_sentence: He got hot under the collar when his friend made fun of him. She was hot under the collar after being blamed for something she didn’t do. The manager became hot under the collar during the heated meeting. Don’t get hot under the collar; it was just a joke.

english_meaning: A long, soft bread roll filled with a hot cooked sausage, usually served with mustard, ketchup, onions, or other toppings; a very popular fast food, especially in the United States. As a verb (informal), to show off or perform daring tricks, especially in skiing, surfing, or other sports. As an exclamation, used to express excitement or delight.
example_sentence: He ordered a hotdog with extra mustard and onions. Hotdogs are a popular snack at American baseball games. The skier began to hotdog down the slope to impress the crowd. They sold hundreds of hotdogs at the football stadium. Hotdog! We finally won the match.

english_meaning: A type of dog used in hunting, known for its strong sense of smell and ability to track or chase animals such as foxes, hares, or deer. As a verb, to chase, pursue, or follow someone persistently, often in a troubling or annoying way. To harass someone constantly with questions, demands, or threats. Also used to describe a despicable or contemptible person.
example_sentence: The hunter trained his hounds to track foxes in the forest. Reporters continued to hound the actress wherever she went. Creditors began to hound him for the unpaid loans. The old hound followed its master loyally everywhere. He was hounded out of office by constant criticism.

english_meaning: A unit of time equal to sixty minutes, or one twenty fourth of a day. A particular point of time in the day. A period set aside for a specific activity, such as working or visiting. An important or difficult time in someone's life.
example_sentence: The journey takes about three hours by train. Our office hours are from nine to five. She studied for an hour before dinner. He stood by his friend in his darkest hour.

english_meaning: A structure, plan, or organization that is very weak and likely to collapse. A situation that is extremely unstable and precarious. A metaphor for a fragile arrangement based on unstable foundations. Something that is easily destroyed because it lacks a solid basis.
example_sentence: Their financial empire turned out to be nothing more than a house of cards. The new government’s coalition proved to be a fragile house of cards. Without proper funding, the entire project is just a house of cards waiting to fall. The legal defense was a house of cards that collapsed under cross-examination.

english_meaning: Extremely attentive to the cleanliness and decoration of one's home. Taking great pride in the appearance of one's house. Being fastidious or obsessive about domestic order and maintenance. Having a home that is kept in an exceptionally neat and stylish condition. Characterized by a strong desire to impress guests with one's living space.
example_sentence: She is so house-proud that she insists everyone take their shoes off at the front door. After the renovation, the couple became very house-proud and hosted parties every weekend. My grandmother was incredibly house-proud and spent hours polishing the antique furniture. You don't need to be house-proud to appreciate a tidy living room.

english_meaning: Past tense and past participle of heave, meaning to lift, raise, or throw with effort. To rise or appear, especially of a ship coming into view. Also a place name in England, but as a verb it indicates a past act of heaving or coming into sight.
example_sentence: A ship hove into view on the horizon. He hove the heavy sack onto his shoulder. The sailors hove the anchor up. Suddenly a stranger hove into sight around the corner. The workers hove the crates onto the truck.

english_meaning: To stay in one place in the air or move around slowly nearby. To remain floating in the air without moving forward. To stay close to a place or person, often waiting. To be uncertain or undecided. To remain at a particular level or position. The act of staying in one place in the air.
example_sentence: A hawk hovered over the hill. He hovered nervously in the doorway. Temperature hovered around freezing. A smile hovered on her lips. He hovered on the edge of consciousness. The bird remained in a hover above the lake. The drone held a steady hover for several minutes. His career is in a hover due to uncertainty.

english_meaning: To remain suspended in the air near a particular location. To linger close to a person or place in an expectant or overly attentive manner. To stay near a specific figure, level, or condition without changing much.
synonyms: ["Linger near","Loiter around","Hang around","Flutter near","Remain close","Wait nearby","Float around","Stay near","Skirt around","Circle"]
example_sentence: The drone continued to hover around the rooftop before landing smoothly. Anxious parents often hover around their young children during play dates. Temperatures are expected to hover around the freezing point all weekend. He decided to hover around the kitchen area while dinner was being prepared.

english_meaning: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something said before; nevertheless. In whatever way or manner. To whatever extent or degree.
example_sentence: The plan is expensive; however, it may be worth the cost. However hard he tried, he could not finish on time. You may arrange the chairs however you like. She was tired; however, she continued working.

english_meaning: To make a long, loud, mournful cry, as that of a wolf, dog, or wind. To cry out loudly in pain, anger, sorrow, or laughter. A long, loud cry or wail. Used both literally for animals and the wind, and figuratively for human cries or strong expressions of feeling such as a howl of protest or a howl of laughter.
example_sentence: The wolves began to howl as the full moon rose over the mountains. The strong wind howled through the empty streets all night. The child started to howl when his toy broke. There was a howl of laughter from the back of the classroom. The crowd let out a loud howl of protest against the new law.

english_meaning: A very silly or stupid mistake, especially in speech or writing. A monkey that produces very loud howling sounds. A person or thing that howls. Informally, something very funny or a glaring error.
example_sentence: The student's answer contained a real howler. Howler monkeys can be heard from miles away in the jungle. The newspaper report had a hilarious howler on the front page. That was a howler of a mistake in the exam. The comedian's speech was full of amusing howlers.

english_meaning: A loud, confused noise; a commotion or uproar. A situation where many people are talking, shouting, or making noise at the same time, creating confusion or excitement. It can describe the noise in a busy place, a public event, or general clamor.
example_sentence: The marketplace was full of hubbub as vendors shouted to attract customers. She could hardly hear him over the hubbub of the party. The sudden hubbub in the street made everyone look outside. There was a hubbub of voices in the courtroom as the verdict was announced.

english_meaning: Excessive pride or self-confidence. Arrogance that leads to one’s downfall. Overbearing presumption against gods, rules, or other people. A dangerous overestimation of one’s own abilities or status. Often used in literature, history, and politics to describe the fatal flaw that brings about ruin.
example_sentence: His hubris led him to ignore every warning from his advisors. The hubris of the empire eventually caused its collapse. She paid a heavy price for her hubris in the courtroom. Many tragic heroes are destroyed by their own hubris. The CEO’s hubris alienated the entire board of directors.

english_meaning: Characterized by excessive pride or dangerous self-confidence. It describes an attitude that leads to arrogance and often results in retribution or failure. It reflects an inflated sense of one's own ability or importance.
example_sentence: His hubristic behavior alienated his friends and colleagues over time. The CEO made a hubristic decision that ultimately bankrupt the firm. Pride comes before a fall, as proven by the general's hubristic strategy. Her hubristic attitude prevented her from accepting constructive criticism.

english_meaning: A person who sells small goods or articles in the street or from door to door, especially in a noisy or pushy way. A pedlar or hawker. A person who uses aggressive, dishonest, or showy methods to sell, advertise, or promote something. As a verb, to sell goods or advertise products in a pushy, noisy, or sometimes dishonest way.
example_sentence: The huckster shouted loudly to attract customers in the busy market. He worked for years as a huckster selling fruits from a cart. People are tired of TV hucksters making false promises. The huckster tried to sell us a fake watch at a high price. Politicians sometimes act like hucksters during election campaigns.

english_meaning: To crowd together in a group, often for warmth or to discuss something privately. It can also refer to a close gathering of people or animals. In sports, it describes players gathering to plan their next move.
example_sentence: The shivering travelers decided to huddle around the small campfire. The team called a quick huddle to discuss their strategy for the final minute. Small birds huddle together on the branches during cold winter nights. They sat in a tight huddle, whispering about the secret project.

english_meaning: A particular shade, tint, or variety of a colour. The attribute of colour by which one may distinguish red from blue, yellow from green, etc. In a wider sense, any aspect, character, or quality of something, as in the phrase 'political hue'. Also occurs in the old phrase 'hue and cry', meaning a loud public protest or noisy outcry.
example_sentence: The sky turned a beautiful golden hue at sunset. Her dress was of a soft pinkish hue. Leaders of every political hue attended the meeting. The painting was full of warm hues of red and orange. There was a great hue and cry over the new tax policy.

english_meaning: Loud protest. A loud public outcry. A strong protest or noisy reaction by many people often against something wrong, unfair, or alarming. It also refers to a public alarm or commotion raised to catch attention or draw action.
example_sentence: There was a hue and cry when the government increased the taxes. The villagers raised a hue and cry after the robbery. A hue and cry was raised against the unfair treatment of workers. The media created a hue and cry over the environmental issues.

english_meaning: To express annoyance, irritation, or anger, sometimes by sighing, grumbling, or leaving in anger. A state of annoyance or a fit of irritation.
example_sentence: She huffed when she heard the news. He left in a huff after the argument. Don’t huff at me for asking a simple question. I could see the huff on his face.

english_meaning: To breathe heavily or express anger, frustration, or effort. A person showing strong effort, often physically (like running or lifting something heavy), or expressing annoyance or impatience vocally. It often conveys exaggerated or noisy action.
example_sentence: After running up the stairs, he was huffing and puffing. She huffed and puffed at the meeting, complaining about the new rules. The old man huffed and puffed as he carried the heavy bag. Don’t just huff and puff; explain what the problem is.

english_meaning: To put your arms around somebody and hold them tightly, especially to show that you like or love them.
example_sentence: They hugged each other. At the end she smiled & hugged me tight.

english_meaning: An informal blend of hug and snuggle, meaning to hug someone in a warm, affectionate, cuddly way. To embrace closely and lovingly. A tender embrace combined with cuddling.
example_sentence: She loves to huggle her puppy every morning. The children huggled their mother tightly. He gave his little sister a warm huggle. On cold nights they huggle under the blanket. The friends shared a long huggle after meeting.

english_meaning: To make a low, continuous sound similar to that of a bee. To sing a tune with closed lips, without using words. To be full of activity, energy, or busy movement. To produce a steady murmuring noise, especially from machines or crowds. To emit a soft and even sound.
example_sentence: She likes to hum her favourite songs while cooking. The bees were humming softly in the garden. The whole market was humming with activity in the morning. You can hear the fridge humming in the quiet room. He hummed a tune as he walked down the street.

english_meaning: To hesitate, be indecisive, speak unclearly, or take too long to decide because of confusion or uncertainty.
example_sentence: When asked about his future plans, he began to hum and haw without giving a clear answer. Instead of making a quick decision, the committee hummed and hawed for hours. She hummed and hawed before finally accepting the job offer. Stop humming and hawing, just tell me what you really think!.

english_meaning: A person belonging to the species Homo sapiens. An individual man, woman, or child. A conscious social being capable of thought, language, emotion, and moral choice. A person viewed with ordinary strengths, needs, and weaknesses.
example_sentence: Every human being deserves dignity and respect. A human being needs food, water, and companionship. The remains were identified as those of a human being. Even a skilled leader is still a human being who can make mistakes.

english_meaning: Showing kindness, mercy, sympathy, and compassion towards people and animals. Treating others with care, gentleness, and respect, especially those who are weak, suffering, or in need. Marked by understanding and consideration of others' pain and feelings. Also used for actions, laws, or methods that avoid causing unnecessary pain or cruelty.
example_sentence: She is known for her humane treatment of stray animals. The new law promotes more humane conditions in prisons. Doctors should always behave in a humane manner with their patients. He is a kind and humane person who helps the poor every day. The organisation works for the humane treatment of all living beings.

english_meaning: Connected with helping people who are suffering and improving the conditions. A person who tries to help people who are suffering and improve the conditions that they are living in. Having or showing a concern for the welfare of others.
example_sentence: We will also do everything in our power to improve delivery of food, medicine, water, incredibly essential humanitarian needs. The actor and humanitarian took to the platform Friday to share a picture of a handwritten letter from a teenage girl in Afghanistan, according to the post's caption.

english_meaning: A reason or justification based on human welfare, compassion, or the need to help people. Refers to actions, decisions, or considerations made to protect, aid, or improve the wellbeing of humans, often in emergencies, conflicts, or situations of suffering. It emphasizes moral responsibility and human rights.
example_sentence: They are calling for release of hostages on Humanitarian Grounds. The refugees were allowed to enter the country on humanitarian ground. She appealed to the court on humanitarian ground for the prisoner’s early release. Aid workers provide food and medical help on humanitarian ground during disasters. The government granted special permits on humanitarian ground to the injured victims.

english_meaning: Belief in promoting human welfare and reducing suffering. The principle that every person deserves dignity, compassion, and assistance. Organized action to protect lives and meet basic needs during crises. A social or ethical movement devoted to helping people without discrimination.
example_sentence: Her humanitarianism inspired decades of relief work. Modern humanitarianism emphasizes neutrality and human dignity. The organization was founded on the principles of humanitarianism. Critics debated how humanitarianism should respond to political conflict.

english_meaning: All human beings considered collectively. The human race or humankind. The quality of being compassionate, kind, and considerate. The condition or nature of being human. Human culture, experience, and civilization. The humanities as fields of study in older usage.
example_sentence: Climate change presents a serious challenge to humanity. The nurse treated every patient with humanity. The story explores both the beauty and weakness of humanity. Advances in medicine have benefited all of humanity.

english_meaning: To make someone or something seem more human, relatable, or sympathetic. To make a system, place, or process kinder and more considerate of human needs. To give human qualities to a nonhuman thing. To improve behavior by encouraging compassion or culture.
example_sentence: The interview helped humanize the public figure. Art can humanize difficult historical events. The hospital redesigned its rooms to humanize patient care. The author humanizes the robot by giving it doubts and hopes.

english_meaning: All human beings collectively. The human species. People throughout the world and across history. Humanity considered as a single community.
example_sentence: The invention changed the course of humankind. Clean water is essential to the future of humankind. The museum tells the story of humankind through ancient objects. Humankind has always looked at the stars with curiosity.

english_meaning: Having a modest opinion of one's own importance. Not proud or arrogant in behaviour or attitude. Of low social rank or simple in nature. To lower someone's pride or make them feel less important.
example_sentence: Despite his success, he remained a humble man. She came from a humble background in a small village. The team was humbled by an unexpected defeat. He offered a humble apology for his mistake.

english_meaning: A statement that appears modest but is really intended to draw attention to an achievement. To boast about something while pretending to complain or be humble. An indirect form of showing off disguised as self criticism. The act of making such a remark.
example_sentence: Complaining about too many job offers is a classic humblebrag. She posted a humblebrag about how tiring her holiday abroad had been. He tends to humblebrag whenever his results are announced. Social media is full of humblebrags disguised as ordinary updates.

english_meaning: Deceptive or false talk or behavior; nonsense. It can refer to a person who is an impostor or a deceptive trick. Sometimes used to describe something boring or hypocritical.
example_sentence: He dismissed the entire story as nothing but pure humbug. The old merchant was known to be a humbug who cheated his customers. 'Bah! Humbug!' shouted the character when asked about the holiday spirit. Don't listen to his excuses, it is all a load of humbug.

english_meaning: Boring, dull, routine, Lacking excitement, variety, or interest. Repetitive and boring due to routine. Dull and ordinary with nothing special. Monotonous in nature, especially daily life or work.
example_sentence: His job became humdrum after doing the same tasks every day. She wanted to escape her humdrum routine and travel the world. The movie started well but turned humdrum in the middle. Life in the small town felt humdrum to him.

english_meaning: The long bone of the upper arm that extends from the shoulder to the elbow. The bone that forms the ball of the shoulder joint and the upper half of the elbow joint. A strong limb bone that gives attachment to the muscles that move the arm. The largest bone of the upper limb.
example_sentence: He broke his humerus in a cycling accident. The humerus fits neatly into the socket of the shoulder. Nerves running close to the humerus can be injured in a fracture. The elbow is formed where the humerus meets the forearm bones.

english_meaning: Containing a high level of moisture, water vapour, or dampness in the air. Used to describe weather, climate, or atmosphere that feels wet, sticky, and uncomfortable, especially when combined with heat. Marked by a damp and sultry feeling caused by too much moisture in the surrounding air.
example_sentence: The weather in Karachi is usually hot and humid during the summer. It was a humid evening, and everyone was sweating in the room. Plants like ferns grow well in humid conditions. The humid air made it difficult to breathe inside the closed hall. Coastal areas tend to be more humid than inland regions.

english_meaning: To make someone feel ashamed or foolish by injuring their dignity and self-respect, especially publicly. To cause a painful loss of pride. To embarrass someone intensely.
example_sentence: The teacher did not mean to humiliate the student in front of the class. Losing the game by such a large margin served to humiliate the defending champions. He felt that the supervisor was trying to humiliate him during the meeting. It is cruel to humiliate others just to make yourself feel superior.

english_meaning: The state of feeling ashamed or foolish due to the loss of dignity or self-respect. An instance or event that causes a painful loss of pride. Public embarrassment or disgrace.
example_sentence: He couldn't face the humiliation of losing his job in such a public manner. She felt a deep sense of humiliation when her secret was revealed. The team suffered a crushing humiliation in the final match. He endured the humiliation silently to protect his family's reputation.

english_meaning: Wise people stay humble. Real education teaches respect. Knowledgeable people avoid arrogance. Learning develops modest behavior. Intelligence with humility earns respect.
synonyms: ["Modesty shows wisdom","Wisdom brings humility","Knowledge creates modesty","True learning removes arrogance","Humble wisdom"]
example_sentence: The professor spoke kindly to every student because humility reflects knowledge. Despite his success, he remained polite and calm, proving that humility reflects knowledge. Great scientists often listen carefully to others because humility reflects knowledge. A wise leader understands mistakes and learns from them because humility reflects knowledge.

english_meaning: A smooth, creamy food made mainly from mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic. It is commonly eaten as a dip or spread.
synonyms: ["Chickpea dip","Chickpea spread","Garbanzo bean paste","Middle Eastern dip"]
example_sentence: I ate hummus with warm pita bread for lunch. She spreads hummus on her sandwich instead of butter. Hummus is a healthy snack rich in protein and fiber. They served hummus with fresh vegetables at the party.

english_meaning: Funny or amusing; causing laughter. Having or showing a sense of humor, able to make others laugh, playful in nature, amusing in a lighthearted way.
example_sentence: She has a humorous way of telling stories that always makes us laugh. His humorous comments lightened the tense meeting. The movie was full of humorous scenes that kept everyone entertained. A humorous personality often helps in making friends easily.

english_meaning: To agree with somebody’s wishes, even if they seem unreasonable, in order to keep the person happy. The quality in something that makes it funny, The ability to laugh at things that are funny.
example_sentence: She thought it best to humour them rather than get into an argument. She ignored his feeble attempt at humour. I can't stand people with no sense of humour. She has her very own brand of humour. The remarks were made in good humour.

english_meaning: The rich, dark organic matter in soil that forms when plants, leaves, and animals decompose. It improves soil fertility, increases moisture retention, supports beneficial microorganisms, and helps plants grow stronger. Humus plays a key role in agriculture, forestry, and environmental sustainability.
example_sentence: Farmers add compost to increase the humus content of the soil. Humus helps the soil retain water during dry seasons. Forest floors are rich in humus due to fallen leaves. The presence of humus improves soil structure and fertility.

english_meaning: To bend your body forward, especially your back or shoulders. To make a decision based on instinct rather than facts. An intuitive feeling, guess, or suspicion without concrete evidence. The act of bending forward, often with shoulders or back rounded. Someone who looks worried or tense because of posture.
example_sentence: It seemed that the doctor's hunch had been right. I have a hunch that Jane likes me. My hunch is that the burglars are still in the area. Her hunches were confirmed the next day. I had a hunch that you might be here. We hunched round the fire to keep warm. She leaned forward, hunching over the desk. He hunched his shoulders and thrust his hands deep into his pockets.

english_meaning: Everything is fine, satisfactory, or going well. A situation, condition, or state of affairs that is completely satisfactory, without problems, or proceeding smoothly. Often informal and conversational.
example_sentence: After fixing the car, everything was hunky dory. He thought the meeting went well and that everything was hunky dory. After a short argument, things were hunky dory between them. The project started with a few delays, but now it’s hunky dory.

english_meaning: To chase and try to kill or catch wild animals or birds for food, sport, or profit. To search carefully and thoroughly for someone or something that is hidden, lost, or hard to find. The act of hunting, a search, or an organised chase. Used both literally for animals and figuratively for looking for jobs, criminals, information, or objects.
example_sentence: Ancient people used to hunt wild animals for food and clothing. The police are still hunting for the missing child. She spent the whole morning hunting for her lost ring. The hunt for the dangerous criminal lasted several weeks. He went on a hunt for a good job after finishing his studies.

english_meaning: To search carefully and persistently to find something hidden or not immediately obvious.
example_sentence: I hunted out my old notes. They hunted out the lost files. She hunted out the best restaurant. Let’s hunt out a solution.

english_meaning: A shout of joy, triumph, or approval. An exclamation used to celebrate success. A cheer given by a crowd. To cheer or shout in celebration.
example_sentence: Hurrah! Our team has won the championship. The crowd gave three hurrahs for the returning soldiers. Hurrah, the examinations are finally over. They hurrahed loudly as the flag was raised.

english_meaning: A violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean. A tropical cyclone with winds of 74 miles (119 kilometers) per hour or greater that is usually accompanied by rain, thunder, and lightning, and that sometimes moves into temperate latitudes. A state of noisy, confused activity.
example_sentence: A powerful hurricane hit the Florida coast. Hurricane Sandy devastated the area. After a hurricane comes a rainbow. The hurricane left a trail of destruction behind it.

english_meaning: Done in haste or very quickly. Doing something quickly, rapidly, or in a rush because of limited time, pressure, excitement, fear, or urgency.
example_sentence: She hurriedly packed her bag before leaving for school. The driver hurriedly moved the car after hearing the warning. He hurriedly finished his homework before dinner. The staff hurriedly evacuated the building during the emergency.

english_meaning: The care, cultivation, and breeding of crops and animals. The careful management and conservation of resources. Skill in managing or using something efficiently
example_sentence: Modern husbandry focuses on sustainable farming methods. He studied animal husbandry to improve dairy production. Good husbandry ensures that the land remains fertile for generations. The family practiced careful husbandry of their savings.

english_meaning: A sudden silence or quietness that falls over a place. To make someone or something become quiet or silent. To suppress information or keep something secret. An exclamation used to command silence. To calm or soothe a person, especially a crying baby.
example_sentence: A sudden hush fell over the room when the principal walked in. She tried to hush the crying child by rocking him gently. The government tried to hush up the scandal before the elections. Hush, you are going to wake the neighbors if you keep talking.

english_meaning: Quiet and still without noise. Spoken in a low or soft voice to ensure secrecy. Suppressed or kept from public knowledge or discussion. Characterized by a lack of activity or excitement. Made silent or peaceful by calming influence. Toned down or muted in color or intensity.
example_sentence: The audience sat in a hushed silence as the pianist began to play. They spoke in hushed tones so the children wouldn't wake up. The hushed atmosphere of the library was perfect for concentrated study. A hushed agreement was made behind closed doors to avoid a public scandal.

english_meaning: To move or work rapidly and energetically. To urge someone to act quickly. To obtain something by energetic effort or sometimes by trickery. Busy, energetic activity. A state of commotion. Aggressive effort to achieve something.
example_sentence: She had to hustle to finish the project on time. Street vendors hustle tourists for tips. The team’s hustle on the field won them the match. He hustled his way through the crowded station to catch the train.

english_meaning: Busy, noisy activity and fast movement, usually in a crowded place. An environment full of energy, movement, and noise where many people are active at the same time. It is often used for markets, cities, offices, or events where there is constant motion and lively interaction.
example_sentence: The hustle and bustle of the city never stops, even at night. She moved to the countryside to escape the hustle and bustle of urban life. The market was full of hustle and bustle during the festival. He enjoys the hustle and bustle of working in a busy office.

english_meaning: A small wooden cage or box-like enclosure, usually with wire mesh on one side, used for keeping pet animals such as rabbits, guinea pigs, or chickens. A piece of furniture similar to a cupboard or sideboard, often with open shelves on top and closed cabinets below, used for storing and displaying dishes. Informally, a small, simple, or untidy room or house.
example_sentence: He built a small wooden hutch for his pet rabbits in the garden. The chickens were kept safe inside a large hutch at night. She placed her best plates on the top shelf of the hutch. They lived in a tiny hutch on the outskirts of the city. The carpenter is making a new hutch for the kitchen.

english_meaning: Something made by combining two different things. Biology: offspring of two different species or varieties. Technology: a system combining two different technologies. Vehicle: a car using both fuel and electricity. General: a mixture of different ideas or styles.
example_sentence: This plant is a hybrid of two rare species. He drives a hybrid car to save fuel. The course uses a hybrid learning model with online and classroom sessions. Her music is a hybrid of classical and modern styles.

english_meaning: To cause a person, animal, or substance to absorb or be supplied with water or moisture. To restore or maintain the water balance in the body or a substance. As a noun in chemistry, a compound containing water molecules chemically combined in a definite ratio. To keep the body adequately supplied with fluids to maintain health and proper function.
example_sentence: Doctors advised the athlete to hydrate well before and after the race. You should hydrate your skin daily using a good moisturiser. It is important to hydrate yourself by drinking plenty of water in hot weather. The plant needs to be hydrated regularly during the dry season. She drank several glasses of water to hydrate herself after the long walk.

english_meaning: The lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, with the symbol H and atomic number one. A colourless, odourless, highly flammable gas that combines with oxygen to form water. An element widely used in industry and increasingly as a clean fuel source.
example_sentence: Water is formed when hydrogen combines with oxygen. Hydrogen is being tested as a clean fuel for buses and trains. The sun produces energy by fusing hydrogen atoms. Hydrogen is the lightest element on the periodic table.

english_meaning: An extremely powerful nuclear weapon whose energy comes from the fusion of hydrogen isotopes. A thermonuclear bomb that is many times more destructive than an atomic bomb. A weapon in which a fission explosion triggers a much larger fusion reaction.
example_sentence: The hydrogen bomb is far more destructive than the first atomic bombs. Testing of the hydrogen bomb caused worldwide alarm. A hydrogen bomb releases energy through nuclear fusion. World leaders called for a ban on hydrogen bomb tests.

english_meaning: Treated or combined with hydrogen, especially in a chemical process. Describing a liquid oil that has been made solid or semi-solid by adding hydrogen. Processed in a way that increases shelf life but often produces unhealthy trans fats.
example_sentence: Many processed snacks contain hydrogenated vegetable oil. Doctors advise avoiding hydrogenated fats in the daily diet. The margarine is made from hydrogenated oils. Hydrogenated products usually have a longer shelf life.

english_meaning: The scientific study of water on and beneath the earth's surface, including its movement, distribution, and quality. The branch of science dealing with rivers, lakes, groundwater, rainfall, and the water cycle. The study of how water interacts with the environment and human activity.
example_sentence: She studied hydrology to help manage the region's water supply. Hydrology plays a key role in planning flood defences. The report is based on years of hydrology research. Experts in hydrology warned about falling groundwater levels.

english_meaning: A chemical reaction in which a compound is broken down by reacting with water. The process by which water splits a molecule into two or more simpler substances. A reaction widely used in digestion, industry, and biology to break large molecules into smaller ones.
example_sentence: Starch is broken down into sugars by hydrolysis. Hydrolysis of the salt produced a mildly acidic solution. Enzymes speed up hydrolysis inside the human body. The factory uses hydrolysis to recycle plastic waste.

english_meaning: Fear of water. An extreme or irrational fear of water. Medically, it also refers to a symptom of rabies in humans, causing difficulty in swallowing water or fear of drinking.
example_sentence: His hydrophobia made swimming impossible. The doctor explained that hydrophobia is a symptom of rabies. She developed hydrophobia after nearly drowning as a child. Awareness campaigns help prevent rabies, which can cause hydrophobia.

english_meaning: A light, fast motorboat designed to skim across the surface of the water. A seaplane that can take off from and land on water. A horizontal fin on a submarine used to control its depth. To slide uncontrollably on a wet road because a layer of water separates the tyres from the surface.
example_sentence: The hydroplane raced across the lake at astonishing speed. A hydroplane landed smoothly on the calm water. Drive slowly in heavy rain or your car may hydroplane. The submarine adjusted its hydroplanes to dive deeper.

english_meaning: The practice of keeping oneself, one's surroundings, and one's food clean in order to stay healthy and prevent the spread of disease. The set of conditions or activities, such as washing hands, bathing, brushing teeth, cleaning the house, and safe food handling, that help maintain good health. The branch of science concerned with the protection of health through cleanliness.
example_sentence: Good personal hygiene helps in preventing many diseases. Children should be taught the importance of hygiene from an early age. The hospital follows strict hygiene rules in every ward. Poor hygiene in restaurants can cause food poisoning. Regular hand washing is the simplest rule of hygiene.

english_meaning: A religious song or poem of praise, usually addressed to God or a deity, sung in a place of worship by a congregation. A song expressing strong feelings of devotion, gratitude, or admiration. By extension, any song or expression that strongly praises a person, an idea, or a thing. As a verb, to praise or celebrate someone or something in song.
example_sentence: The congregation sang a beautiful hymn at the end of the service. She loves to listen to old hymns on Sunday mornings. The poet wrote a hymn in praise of nature and its beauty. The national anthem is a hymn of love for the country. The children's choir hymned the glory of their teacher.

english_meaning: The small U shaped bone in the front of the neck below the jaw. The only bone in the human body that is not joined to any other bone. The bone that supports the tongue and helps in swallowing and speech. A horseshoe shaped bone held in place by muscles and ligaments.
example_sentence: The hyoid bone supports the muscles of the tongue. It is the only bone that does not touch another bone. A fractured hyoid bone is often linked to strangulation. The hyoid bone plays an important role in speech.

english_meaning: To promote, praise, or advertise something in an exaggerated and exciting way to attract attention or increase interest. To make something seem more exciting, important, successful, or impressive than it may actually be. It is often used in advertising, social media, movies, products, events, games, or public discussions.
example_sentence: The company hyped up its new smartphone before the launch. Social media influencers hyped the movie up for weeks. He keeps hyping up the event as if it will change everyone’s life. The game was heavily hyped up, but many players were disappointed later.

english_meaning: A person obsessed with buying trendy or hyped fashion items. Someone who follows streetwear trends mainly for status. A collector of limited-edition sneakers and branded clothing. Informally, a person who values brand hype over personal style.
example_sentence: He spends his entire salary like a true hypebeast. The store was crowded with hypebeasts waiting for the new release. She calls her brother a hypebeast because of his sneaker collection. Being a hypebeast can be an expensive habit.

english_meaning: Extreme exaggeration used for emphasis or effect. A way of speaking or writing that makes something sound better, more exciting, more dangerous, etc than it really is.
example_sentence: The film is being promoted with all the usual hyperbole. He’s not usually given to hyperbole. I have told you a million times to be careful. This bag weighs a ton. She cried a river after watching the movie. He was so hungry that he could eat a horse.

english_meaning: Extremely rapid and uncontrolled rise in prices. A severe economic condition in which money loses value very quickly. Inflation running at very high monthly rates.
example_sentence: Hyperinflation destroyed the value of household savings. The country suffered hyperinflation after the war. Prices doubled weekly during the hyperinflation. Economists warned of possible hyperinflation.

english_meaning: A clickable link that takes the user to another document or web page. An electronic connection between two pieces of digital content. To connect text or images to another location using a link.
example_sentence: Click the hyperlink to read the full report. The article contains several useful hyperlinks. He hyperlinked the references to their sources. A broken hyperlink can frustrate readers.

english_meaning: Focused on a very small geographical area, such as a neighbourhood. Relating to news or services aimed at a specific local community. Extremely local in scope or coverage.
example_sentence: The website provides hyperlocal news for our district. Hyperlocal advertising works well for small shops. She started a hyperlocal delivery service. Hyperlocal reporting keeps residents well informed.

english_meaning: A condition in which distant objects are seen clearly but nearby objects appear blurred. Long-sightedness caused by the eye focusing images behind the retina. A common refractive error of vision.
example_sentence: The optician diagnosed hypermetropia in both eyes. Hypermetropia is corrected with convex lenses. Children with hypermetropia may struggle while reading. His hypermetropia worsened with age.

english_meaning: A word with a broad meaning that includes more specific words. A general term that covers a class of items. The opposite of a hyponym in the study of word relations.
example_sentence: The word flower is a hypernym of rose and tulip. Teachers explain hypernyms to build vocabulary. Every hyponym has a corresponding hypernym. Animal serves as a hypernym for dog and cat.

english_meaning: A person who is able to speak, read, or write in an exceptionally large number of languages, typically six or more at a high level of proficiency. Someone with an extraordinary ability to learn and use many languages. A term used to describe individuals with exceptional multilingual capabilities beyond the ordinary polyglot.
example_sentence: The hyperpolyglot could hold fluent conversations in more than twenty languages across four different continents. She was recognised as a hyperpolyglot after demonstrating mastery of eleven languages to an independent panel. The documentary explored the lives of several hyperpolyglots and the methods they used to learn so many languages. Scientists are studying whether hyperpolyglots have any structural differences in the language centres of the brain. He was a self-taught hyperpolyglot who had never formally studied any of the twelve languages he spoke.

english_meaning: Very easily upset or offended by criticism. Reacting strongly to a substance, light, sound, or touch. Excessively sensitive in body or feeling. Overly responsive to small changes.
example_sentence: He is hypersensitive to any kind of criticism. Her skin is hypersensitive to strong sunlight. Some children are hypersensitive to loud noises. The patient proved hypersensitive to the medicine.

english_meaning: An excessive physical reaction to a substance such as a drug or food. Extreme emotional sensitivity to criticism or comments. The condition of reacting far more strongly than normal.
example_sentence: The test confirmed hypersensitivity to certain antibiotics. His hypersensitivity makes teamwork difficult. Hypersensitivity to dust can trigger asthma. She was treated for food hypersensitivity.

english_meaning: Exhibiting unusual or excessive concern with or indulgence in sexual activity. Extremely or excessively sexual or given to sexual activities. Having an abnormally high or excessive interest in sexual activity, fantasies, or behavior. It often describes a condition where sexual thoughts or actions become overwhelming, frequent, or difficult to control.
example_sentence: The movie unfairly portrayed the character as being hypersexual, which was not true to her personality. Some people wrongly label teenagers as hypersexual when they are simply curious about relationships. The doctor explained that hypersexual behavior could be a symptom of certain mental health conditions. The article criticized the fashion industry for creating hypersexual images of women.

english_meaning: A theoretical space with more than three dimensions. In science fiction, a region that allows travel faster than light. A mathematical space of many dimensions.
example_sentence: The spaceship jumped into hyperspace to escape. Mathematicians study hyperspace in advanced geometry. Hyperspace travel remains a work of fiction. The novel describes a journey through hyperspace.

english_meaning: To put someone into a state of focused attention where they are more open to suggestion. To induce a trance-like mental state in a person, usually through relaxation and concentration techniques. In this state, the person becomes highly focused and may respond more easily to suggestions. It can also be used figuratively to describe something that strongly captures attention or fascinates someone.
example_sentence: The therapist tried to hypnotize the patient to reduce anxiety. The magician hypnotized a volunteer during the stage show. Her voice seemed to hypnotize everyone in the room. The beautiful scenery hypnotized the travelers as they watched silently.

english_meaning: A person who is excessively worried about having serious illnesses without medical proof. Someone who has an ongoing and unreasonable fear about their health. They often misinterpret normal body sensations as signs of serious illness and frequently seek medical reassurance.
example_sentence: He visits the doctor every week because he is a hypochondriac. As a hypochondriac, she often believes minor headaches are serious problems. His friends joke that he is a hypochondriac due to his constant health worries. The hypochondriac spent hours searching symptoms online.

english_meaning: Behavior that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that somebody claims to have. A feigning to be what one is not or to believe what one does not. Behavior that contradicts what one claims to believe or feel
example_sentence: When his private letters were made public, they revealed his hypocrisy. He condemned the hypocrisy of those politicians who do one thing and say another. It’s hypocrisy for them to pretend that they were shocked at the news.

english_meaning: Pretending to be virtuous, moral, or sincere while acting against those principles, when someone claims high moral standards but behaves inconsistently or deceptively. It points out the presence of insincerity or double standards in actions compared to words.
example_sentence: Hypocrisy is real in politics. Many people admit hypocrisy is real. Hypocrisy is real in social media. Teachers preach honesty but hypocrisy is real sometimes.

english_meaning: A person whose behavior does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that they claim to have. A person who puts on a false appearance of virtue or religion. A person who acts in contradiction to his or her stated beliefs or feelings.
example_sentence: Charles was a liar and a hypocrite who married her for money. Your coach is such a hypocrite. He demands that we maintain a healthy diet but seems to be always eating fast-food after practice.

english_meaning: Pretending to have good morals or beliefs while behaving in the opposite way. A person is hypocritical when they claim to follow certain values, rules, or principles but their actions show the opposite. They criticize others for something they themselves do.
example_sentence: It is hypocritical to tell others not to lie while you lie frequently. Many people thought his speech about honesty was hypocritical because he had cheated in business before. She criticized corruption in public but accepted bribes privately, which seemed hypocritical. His hypocritical behavior made people lose trust in him.

english_meaning: A proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation. A tentative assumption or proposition. A theory that requires testing to be proven true.
example_sentence: The researchers formulated a hypothesis to explain the unusual weather patterns. Our initial hypothesis was proven wrong after the first round of experiments. You must provide evidence to support your hypothesis during the science fair. A scientific hypothesis must be testable and falsifiable.

english_meaning: To suggest a possible explanation or theory for a phenomenon based on limited evidence. It serves as a starting point for further investigation or experimentation. To form a tentative assumption in order to test its consequences.
example_sentence: Scientists hypothesize that the new drug will significantly reduce symptoms. Researchers often hypothesize about the long-term effects of climate change. It is difficult to hypothesize without having access to the primary data. She began to hypothesize why the ancient civilization suddenly disappeared.

english_meaning: Based on or serving as a hypothesis. Something that is assumed or presumed rather than researched or proven as a fact. Related to the nature of a supposition.
example_sentence: The professor presented a hypothetic scenario to the class. We discussed a hypothetic model of the economic recovery. The results were based on a purely hypothetic set of circumstances. He offered a hypothetic explanation for the sudden drop in pressure.

english_meaning: Involving or based on a suggested idea or theory rather than facts or reality. It describes a situation that could possibly happen but has not happened yet. Pertaining to a hypothesis.
example_sentence: Let us look at a hypothetical situation where gravity is doubled. The argument is based on a hypothetical case that may never occur. She asked a hypothetical question to test his reaction. Scientists often use hypothetical models to predict future weather patterns.

english_meaning: By way of hypothesis or as a matter of theory. It is used to describe something that is imagined or supposed for the sake of argument. In a manner that is not necessarily based on fact.
example_sentence: Hypothetically speaking, what would you do if you won the lottery? We are considering the project hypothetically until the funding is secured. The engine could, hypothetically, last for twenty years. If we move hypothetically through time, the changes become apparent.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove a woman’s uterus. A medical surgical procedure in which a woman’s uterus is removed. After this operation, a woman can no longer become pregnant, and menstrual periods permanently stop. It may be performed due to medical conditions such as fibroids, cancer, heavy bleeding, chronic pain, or infections.
synonyms: ["Uterus removal surgery","Uterine surgery","Surgical removal of the uterus"]
example_sentence: The doctor recommended a hysterectomy due to severe uterine fibroids. After her hysterectomy, she needed time to recover fully. A hysterectomy can be partial or complete depending on the condition. The patient discussed the risks and benefits of hysterectomy with her surgeon.

english_meaning: A state of extreme emotional excitement, fear, or panic that makes people lose control of their behavior or emotions. Uncontrolled laughter, crying, or fear, often shared by a group of people.
example_sentence:
When the actor appeared on stage, the crowd erupted in hysteria. The news of the disaster caused widespread hysteria among the villagers. 
The teacher tried to calm the hysteria in the classroom after the loud explosion. The rumor about ghosts created a wave of hysteria in the small town.

english_meaning: Extremely emotional, uncontrollable. Experiencing or showing overwhelming fear, panic, or laughter that is difficult to control. Can refer to both negative emotions (panic, fear) or extreme laughter.
example_sentence: She became hysterical when she heard the news. The crowd was hysterical with excitement. He laughed hysterically at the joke. The mother was hysterical after losing her child.

english_meaning: In an extremely emotional or uncontrolled way. Acting or reacting in a way that shows overwhelming emotion, often fear, excitement, or laughter, beyond what is normal or rational. It can describe behavior that is frenzied, uncontrollable, or emotionally intense.
example_sentence: She laughed hysterically at the comedian’s joke. The children were running around the playground hysterically after the announcement of a holiday. He called his friend hysterically when he lost his passport. The crowd reacted hysterically when the celebrity appeared on stage.

english_meaning: A state of extreme emotional excitement, often uncontrollable laughter, crying, or panic. A sudden, intense, and often uncontrollable emotional reaction. It can involve laughter, crying, panic, or anger, usually appearing exaggerated or disproportionate to the situation. Historically, it was sometimes used to describe emotional instability, often linked to psychological stress.
example_sentence: She went into hysterics when she saw the spider in her room. The comedian’s joke sent the audience into hysterics. He broke down in hysterics after hearing the shocking news. The children were in hysterics after the clown’s funny act.

word: I am rubber you are glue
english_meaning: This is a playful or childish phrase used to deflect insults or negative comments. The idea is that any insult directed at the speaker bounces off like rubber, while it “sticks” to the person who made it, like glue. It implies resilience and deflection. An insult or criticism you give will come back to you. Whatever bad thing you say about me bounces off me and sticks to you.
synonyms: ["Sticks back like a boomerang","Tit for tat","What goes around comes around","Bounce back"]
antonyms: ["Take insult seriously","Absorb criticism","Be sensitive to insults","Self-blame"]
example_sentence: Child 1: You can’t run fast!, Child 2: I am rubber, you are glue. Your words stick to you, not me. Friend 1: Your memes are lame, Friend 2: I am rubber, you are glue, Whatever you say boomerangs back. Mom: You left your toys everywhere again!, Child: I am rubber, you are glue, Your scolding sticks to you.

english_meaning: I am in charge, I control everything, or I am the one who manages or makes all the important decisions.
example_sentence: In our family business, I run the show, everyone reports to me. She likes to run the show and make all the important decisions herself. Don’t worry about the event, John is running the show this time. When the boss is away, Sarah runs the show in the office.

english_meaning: Became very angry suddenly. This expression is used when someone experiences a sudden burst of intense anger, often losing control for a moment. The "red" symbolizes rage or fury.
synonyms: ["Flew into a rage","Lost one’s temper","Got furious","Became enraged"]
example_sentence: When he found out someone had scratched his car, he saw red. She saw red when she heard the unfair decision. I saw red after being insulted in front of everyone. The teacher saw red when students ignored the safety rules.

english_meaning: I am very angry. A situation when someone feels extreme anger or rage. It refers to the physical reaction of anger, such as flushed face or intense emotion.
example_sentence: When he insulted me, I saw red. She saw red after hearing the unfair decision. I saw red when I found out someone had lied to me. He saw red at the reckless driving.

english_meaning: A quality of extreme calmness or fearlessness, especially in a dangerous or high-pressure situation. The ability to act without emotion under extreme pressure. Describing someone who remains completely composed when others would panic.
example_sentence: To make that penalty kick with the match on the line, you need ice in your veins. She walked into the boardroom with ice in her veins and delivered the presentation flawlessly. He has ice in his veins — nothing ever seems to rattle him. The surgeon must have ice in her veins to operate so calmly in such difficult conditions.

english_meaning: A very pale, cool shade of blue resembling the colour of ice. Describing something of such a pale bluish colour. Of eyes or a look, pale blue and appearing cold or distant.
example_sentence: The bedroom walls were painted ice-blue. She chose an ice-blue scarf to match her coat. His ice-blue eyes stared at us without emotion. The lake shone ice-blue in the winter light.

english_meaning: A very large mass of floating ice that has broken away from a glacier or an ice sheet and drifts in cold ocean waters; only about one-tenth of an iceberg is visible above the surface while the rest lies hidden underwater. Figuratively, the phrase 'tip of the iceberg' is used to describe a small visible part of a much bigger hidden problem or situation. Also used for an emotionally cold or unfeeling person.
example_sentence: The Titanic sank after striking a huge iceberg in the North Atlantic. Climate change is causing more icebergs to break away from the polar ice. What we see is only the tip of the iceberg of the country's economic problems. From the air, the iceberg looked like a floating white mountain. He was so cold and silent that his colleagues called him an iceberg.

english_meaning: A biologist specializing in the study of fish, including their behavior, anatomy, classification, and ecology.
example_sentence: The ichthyologist discovered a new species of freshwater fish in the river. Ichthyologists often work in marine laboratories to study fish habitats. She consulted an ichthyologist to understand why the local fish population was declining. The ichthyologist published a paper on the migratory patterns of salmon.

english_meaning: A hanging piece of ice formed by the freezing of dripping water. A tapering spike of ice hanging from a surface. A pointed rod of ice suspended from a roof or ledge. A frozen drop that hangs downward. A slender formation of ice.
example_sentence: A long icicle hung from the edge of the roof. Children broke icicles from the fence and laughed. The cave was full of shining icicles. Icicles glittered in the morning sunlight.

english_meaning: Widely recognised and admired as a symbol of something. Very famous and representing an era, place, or idea. Relating to or resembling an icon or image. Having a lasting cultural significance.
example_sentence: The building is an iconic landmark of the city. She wore an iconic red dress to the premiere. That song became iconic for an entire generation. The photograph is one of the most iconic images of the war.

english_meaning: A person who challenges or opposes traditional beliefs or customs. Someone who questions or criticizes widely accepted ideas, traditions, or institutions, often seeking change or reform. Historically, the term referred to people who destroyed religious images or icons, but today it is used more broadly for anyone challenging established norms.
example_sentence: She was considered an iconoclast for challenging the old educational system. The artist became an iconoclast, rejecting conventional painting techniques. Many innovators in technology are iconoclasts who disrupt industries. His iconoclastic ideas often caused debates in the conservative community.

english_meaning: The study, description, interpretation, or collection of images, symbols, and visual representations, especially in art, religion, culture, or design. Visual symbolism, Symbolic imagery, Artistic symbols, Religious imagery, Collection of icons. Graphic icon system, Visual communication through symbols, Study of symbolic art. Interface icon design, Pictorial language.
antonyms: ["Text","Plain writing","Literal description","Verbal explanation","Nonvisual communication","Aniconism (avoidance of religious images)","Image prohibition"]
example_sentence: The professor explained the iconography of ancient Egyptian temples during the lecture. The museum guide described the religious iconography found in medieval paintings. The designer updated the application's iconography to make it more modern and user friendly. Understanding the iconography of a culture helps people interpret its artwork correctly.

english_meaning: A twenty-sided polygon with twenty angles. A geometric shape with twenty straight sides and twenty vertices. Any flat shape with twenty corners and twenty edges.
example_sentence: A regular icosagon has twenty equal sides and angles. The decorative medallion was shaped like an icosagon. Geometry students learned to calculate the area of an icosagon. The building's floor plan resembled an icosagon.

english_meaning: Having high moral, social, or political ideals. Guided by hopes and principles more than practical limits. Noble but sometimes unrealistic.
example_sentence: The idealistic student wanted to change the world. Her plan was generous but idealistic. Idealistic leaders can inspire people. He remained idealistic despite many failures.

english_meaning: Exactly the same in every relevant detail. So alike that no difference can be seen or measured. Referring to twins developed from the same fertilized egg. The very same person or thing, not merely a similar one.
example_sentence: The two documents are identical. They bought identical chairs for the dining room. The brothers are identical twins. Her account was almost identical to mine.

english_meaning: In exactly the same way. With no difference in form, appearance, arrangement, or value. So similarly that two or more things match completely.
example_sentence: The twins were dressed identically. Both machines are identically designed. The two samples reacted identically under heat. These forms must be completed identically.

english_meaning: Able to be recognized, named, or established as a particular person or thing. Having features that make recognition possible. Capable of being traced to a known source or cause.
example_sentence: The bird is identifiable by its red wings. No identifiable fingerprints were found. Each payment must come from an identifiable source. The suspect was clearly identifiable in the video.

english_meaning: The act of recognising or establishing who or what someone or something is. An official document that proves a person's identity. The process of discovering or pointing out something such as a problem. A strong feeling of sympathy or association with another person or group.
example_sentence: Please bring some form of identification with you. Early identification of the disease improves the chance of recovery. The identification of the body took several days. His identification with the workers made him very popular.

english_meaning: A name, label, number, sign, or any piece of information that is used to identify, recognise, or distinguish one person, object, or thing from another. In computing and databases, a unique string or code used to refer to a specific record, file, variable, or user, such as a username, ID number, or product code.
