Anything that serves as a mark of identity.
example_sentence: Each student is given a unique identifier at the time of admission. In the database, the employee ID acts as the main identifier for every worker. Your email address is often used as an identifier on online platforms. Fingerprints are a reliable identifier of a person. The product is marked with a special barcode identifier on its box.

english_meaning: To recognise someone or something and be able to say who or what they are. To establish the identity of a person or object. To discover or point out a problem, need, or cause. To treat one thing as being the same as another.
example_sentence: Witnesses were able to identify the man from a photograph. Doctors identified the cause of the infection within hours. The report identifies three main areas for improvement. Please identify yourself before entering the building.

english_meaning: To regard oneself as belonging to a particular group, gender, or category. To publicly describe oneself in terms of a certain identity. To be officially recognised or classified as something. To state which group one considers oneself part of.
synonyms: ["Regard oneself as","Consider oneself","Class oneself as","Describe oneself as","Label as","Categorise as"]
example_sentence: Many respondents identify as members of a minority community. He does not identify as a religious person. The species was later identified as a new variety of orchid. She identifies as an artist rather than a designer.

english_meaning: To feel that one is similar to someone and can understand them. To share the feelings, ideas, or experiences of another person. To associate a person or thing closely with a particular quality or group. To support a cause as though it were one's own.
example_sentence: Readers easily identify with the main character of the novel. He strongly identifies with the struggles of working families. The brand is identified with quality and reliability. Young viewers identify with the show's honest portrayal of school life.

english_meaning: A written symbol that represents an idea or thing rather than a particular word or sound. A character used in writing systems such as Chinese to convey meaning directly. A graphic sign like an arrow or a warning symbol understood without words.
example_sentence: The arrow on the sign is a simple ideogram. Chinese writing makes extensive use of ideograms. Ancient scripts often began with pictures and ideograms. An ideogram can be understood across many languages.

english_meaning: Relating to a system of ideas, beliefs, or political theory. Based on or concerned with ideology rather than practical matters. Reflecting strong adherence to particular principles.
example_sentence: The debate was purely ideological rather than practical. Ideological differences split the movement in two. She wrote a book on the ideological roots of the reform. Their ideological stance has never softened.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to a particular system of ideas or beliefs. According to the principles of an ideology. From the point of view of political or philosophical doctrine.
example_sentence: The two parties are ideologically opposed on this issue. He is ideologically committed to free trade. The group remains ideologically divided. Ideologically, the reform makes perfect sense.

english_meaning: A person who strongly and often rigidly supports a particular ideology. A theorist who is uncompromising about political or social beliefs. Someone who advocates a doctrine without allowing for practical exceptions.
example_sentence: He is an ideologue who never accepts compromise. The committee needs practical thinkers, not ideologues. Critics called the minister a stubborn ideologue. As an ideologue, she judges every policy by theory alone.

english_meaning: A system of ideas and beliefs that forms the basis of a political or economic theory. The set of principles held by a person, group, or movement. A way of looking at the world that shapes goals and actions.
example_sentence: The party's ideology has changed over the past decade. He rejected any ideology that limited personal freedom. Education should not be shaped by a single ideology. Their ideology values equality above all else.

english_meaning: In the ancient Roman calendar, the fifteenth day of March, May, July, and October, and the thirteenth of other months. A specific date used in Roman dating, best known from the Ides of March. A historical term for a mid-month division of time.
example_sentence: Beware the Ides of March, the soothsayer warned. Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March. Roman writers often dated letters by the Ides. The students learned about the Ides in a history lesson.

english_meaning: Extremely stupid behaviour or a very foolish act. A complete lack of good sense or judgement. Something said or done that is absurdly senseless.
example_sentence: It would be sheer idiocy to drive in this weather. His idiocy nearly cost the team the match. She stared at him, amazed by such idiocy. The plan was dismissed as complete idiocy.

english_meaning: The unique speech habits and language use of an individual person. The personal variety of a language, including vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. A linguistic term for one speaker's distinctive way of talking.
example_sentence: Every speaker has an idiolect shaped by upbringing and education. The novelist captured her narrator's idiolect perfectly. Linguists study idiolect to understand language variation. His idiolect includes many words from his village.

english_meaning: A form of expression or a group of words whose meaning cannot be understood by interpreting the words literally. A common phrase or expression that has a figurative meaning, different from the literal meaning of the words.
example_sentence: She used an idiom I didn’t understand. Break the ice’ is a common English idiom. Idioms often cannot be translated word for word. Learning idioms is important for fluency in any language. Every culture has its own unique idioms. He explained the idiom using a simple example. Some idioms are hard even for native speakers

english_meaning: Using expressions that are natural to a native speaker of a language. Relating to idioms or fixed phrases whose meaning is not literal. Characteristic of a particular language, style, or dialect. Sounding correct and natural rather than word-for-word.
example_sentence: His English is fluent and thoroughly idiomatic. The translation is accurate but not very idiomatic. Learners struggle with idiomatic expressions like 'kick the bucket'. She writes in a warm, idiomatic style.

english_meaning: Relating to a disease or condition that arises spontaneously or from an unknown cause. Not caused by any identifiable or previously existing disease. Used in medicine to describe conditions with no known origin.
example_sentence: The patient was diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis after all known causes were ruled out. Idiopathic epilepsy accounts for a large proportion of seizure disorders in children. Doctors classified her condition as idiopathic because no underlying cause could be identified. He was told his hearing loss was idiopathic and could not be traced to any specific event. The research team is studying idiopathic cases to better understand the mechanisms of the disease.

english_meaning: To spend time doing nothing. To run a machine without doing useful work. Not active or not working. Avoiding work, lazy. Not in use or unemployed. Without purpose or effect.
example_sentence: He spent the whole day idle at home. The workers remained idle due to the strike. Do not let your mind stay idle for too long. The engine was idling in the parking area.

english_meaning: A soft, steamed savory rice cake popular in South India. A traditional South Indian breakfast dish made from fermented rice and lentil batter. A light and healthy steamed food often served with sambar and chutney. A fluffy round cake, white in color, made without frying. A staple food of South Indian cuisine.
example_sentence: We had idli and sambar for breakfast this morning. Idli is considered one of the healthiest Indian breakfasts. She learned how to make soft idli from her grandmother. The restaurant is famous for its fluffy idli.

english_meaning: An image or statue worshipped as a god. A person who is greatly admired, loved, or revered by many. Something to which excessive devotion is given. A false god or object of misplaced worship.
example_sentence: The ancient temple was filled with stone idols. That singer has been her idol since childhood. Money became the idol of his entire life. Young players often try to imitate their sporting idols.

english_meaning: If it becomes necessary. If circumstances require it. Used to express willingness to act when required. Only if the situation demands. In case there is a real need.
synonyms: ["If necessary","If required","When needed","Should it be necessary","In case of need"]
example_sentence: I will stay late if need be. We can call the doctor if need be. She will travel abroad if need be. If need be, I will help you with the payment.

word: If you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen
english_meaning: A saying meaning that if you cannot cope with the pressure of a job, you should leave it. Advice that difficult work is not for those who cannot handle stress. A warning that responsibility always comes with strain.
synonyms: ["Face the music","Sink or swim","Toughen up","Stand your ground","Endure","Persevere","Handle pressure","Step aside","Quit","Withdraw"]
example_sentence: If you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen, he told the new manager. Politics is demanding; if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen. She reminded her staff that if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen. The coach's motto is simple: if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen.

english_meaning: Not honourable in character or purpose. Morally low, mean, or shameful. Of humble or low birth and social standing. Deserving contempt because of a lack of dignity.
example_sentence: He was ashamed of his ignoble behaviour towards his friend. Greed drove him to an ignoble act of betrayal. She rose from ignoble beginnings to national fame. It would be ignoble to abandon them now.

english_meaning: Deserving or causing public shame, disgrace, or humiliation. Bringing dishonour or great embarrassment. Extremely shameful or degrading in nature.
example_sentence: The general suffered an ignominious defeat and was forced to surrender in front of his own troops. His ignominious behaviour at the ceremony shocked everyone who was present. The politician resigned after a series of ignominious scandals tarnished his reputation beyond repair. She refused to accept such an ignominious outcome after years of hard work and dedication. The team's ignominious performance in the final match was widely criticised in the press.

english_meaning: In a shameful, disgraceful, or humiliating manner. In a way that brings dishonour or public embarrassment. Done in a degrading or undignified way.
example_sentence: He was ignominiously removed from his position following the investigation. The army retreated ignominiously after suffering heavy losses in the first engagement. She was ignominiously dismissed from the competition for breaking the rules. The team was ignominiously knocked out of the tournament in the very first round. He had to walk away ignominiously after the crowd booed him off the stage.

english_meaning: Public shame, disgrace, or dishonour, especially as a result of bad behaviour or a serious failure. A state of severe humiliation in front of others. A deeply embarrassing situation that damages one's reputation. The word is formal and usually used for serious, lasting disgrace rather than minor embarrassment.
example_sentence: He suffered the ignominy of being dismissed from his post. The team faced the ignominy of defeat by a much weaker side. She could not bear the ignominy of public failure. The scandal brought ignominy upon the whole family. He resigned to avoid further ignominy.

english_meaning: A person who lacks knowledge or is unaware. Someone who is uneducated, uninformed, or shows a lack of awareness about important facts or knowledge. A person who ignores learning. Someone who speaks or acts without proper knowledge. A person unaware of basic facts.
example_sentence: He acted like an ignoramus during the discussion on climate change. Do not be an ignoramus, try to learn the facts before speaking. She felt embarrassed when others thought she was an ignoramus. Only an ignoramus would ignore such clear evidence.

english_meaning: The lack of knowledge, education, or awareness about something specific or in general. It refers to a state of being uninformed or uneducated. A condition of not knowing.
example_sentence: His ignorance of the local customs led to several misunderstandings. They acted out of pure ignorance regarding the safety regulations. Overcoming ignorance is the first step toward social progress. Constant study is the only true remedy for ignorance.

english_meaning: A proverb meaning that not knowing about a problem can keep a person happy. The idea that knowledge of unpleasant facts brings worry, so it is sometimes better not to know. A remark used when someone is untroubled only because they are unaware of the truth.
synonyms: ["Blissful ignorance","What you don't know can't hurt you","Blind contentment","Willful blindness","Innocence","Unawareness","Naivety","Oblivion","Carefree ignorance","Untroubled unawareness"]
example_sentence: He never reads the news because for him ignorance is bliss. She smiled and said ignorance is bliss when asked about the results. Sometimes ignorance is bliss, but not when your health is at stake. They kept the bad news from him, believing ignorance is bliss.

english_meaning: Not having or showing much knowledge or information about things, not educated. Not having any knowledge or information about a particular thing. With very bad manners.
example_sentence: Never make your students feel ignorant. At that time I was ignorant of events going on elsewhere. He's ignorant about modern technology. You're behaving like a stupid ignorant child!. Many teenagers are surprisingly ignorant about current politics. We remained blissfully ignorant of the troubles that lay ahead.

english_meaning: To deliberately pay no attention to something or someone. To disregard or refuse to take notice of a person, fact, or situation. To treat something as if it does not exist or does not matter.
synonyms: ["Disregard","Overlook","Neglect","Dismiss","Snub","Pay no attention to","Turn a blind eye to"]
example_sentence: She chose to ignore his rude comment and continued with her presentation calmly. The government cannot afford to ignore the warnings issued by the environmental scientists. He tried to ignore the pain in his shoulder and carry on with the match. Please do not ignore the safety guidelines posted on the walls of the laboratory. The teacher asked the students not to ignore any question in the examination paper.

english_meaning: The final and longest segment of the small intestine, situated between the jejunum and the cecum. A anatomical region responsible for the absorption of vitamin B12 and bile salts. The part of the digestive tract that concludes at the ileocecal valve where it joins the large intestine. A thin-walled tubular structure characterized by the presence of Peyer's patches which are important for immune function. The third portion of the small bowel following the duodenum and jejunum.
synonyms: ["Small Intestine Segment","Lower Bowel","Digestive Tube","Terminal Small Bowel","Third Part Of Small Intestine","Intestinal Section","Gut Segment","Alimentary Canal Part","Distal Small Intestine","Viscera","Enteric Canal"]
example_sentence: The ileum is primarily responsible for absorbing nutrients that were not absorbed by the jejunum. Crohn's disease often affects the terminal ileum more severely than other parts of the gut. Surgeons identified a blockage within the ileum during the emergency procedure. Bile salts are recycled through the walls of the ileum back into the bloodstream.

english_meaning: The largest and uppermost of the three bones that form each half of the pelvis. The broad, fan-shaped bone that can be felt as the hip at the side of the waist. A bone that provides attachment for the abdominal and gluteal muscles. The part of the hip bone that forms the wide flaring rim of the pelvis.
example_sentence: You can feel the top of the ilium just below your waist. Bone marrow samples are often taken from the ilium. The gluteal muscles are attached to the outer surface of the ilium. A fall from the ladder fractured the wing of his ilium.

english_meaning: To raise or bring up someone with poor manners or bad behavior. To fail to teach proper etiquette or values. Rude, impolite, or lacking good upbringing. Behavior showing a lack of refinement or good manners. A person who has not been taught proper conduct.
example_sentence: It is a shame to ill-breed a child in such a rough environment. His ill-breed manners embarrassed his parents. Do not ill-breed your children by ignoring their behavior. She was clearly an ill-breed guest at the formal dinner.

english_meaning: Destined to end in failure or misfortune. Unlucky and marked by a sad or tragic outcome. Suffering bad luck from the very beginning. Associated with disaster or an unhappy ending. Doomed to have a bad result despite good intentions.
example_sentence: The ill-fated ship sank on its first voyage. Their ill-fated business closed within a year. He joined the ill-fated expedition to the mountains. It was an ill-fated decision that cost them everything.

english_meaning: Not clear enough to be read. Impossible or very difficult to decipher due to poor handwriting or damage. Unreadable because of faded, smudged, or unclear text. Writing that cannot be understood or made out.
example_sentence: The doctor's handwriting on the prescription was completely illegible. His signature was so illegible that the clerk asked him to sign again. The old manuscript had become illegible over the centuries. Please rewrite this note, as your writing is illegible.

english_meaning: The state of being born to parents who are not legally married or something not accepted as lawful or proper. Lack of authenticity or correctness. Failure to meet legal or moral standards. A condition that society views as improper. A condition where a child is born outside a legally recognized marriage or when something lacks legal, moral or formal validity. It can be used for people, actions or claims considered improper or unlawful.
example_sentence: The law no longer treats children differently because of illegitimacy. Many people questioned the illegitimacy of his claim to the property. The court dismissed the evidence due to its illegitimacy. In the past, illegitimacy carried a heavy social stigma. The journalist exposed the illegitimacy of the organization’s funding sources. The illegitimacy of the data raised doubts about the entire study. The committee reviewed the contract and found several points of illegitimacy.

english_meaning: Forbidden by law, rules, or custom. Not permitted or sanctioned by accepted standards or norms. Illegal or unlawful in nature. Something done in secret because it is socially or legally unacceptable.
example_sentence: The authorities seized a large quantity of illicit drugs at the border checkpoint. He was arrested for his involvement in an illicit trading network. The investigation revealed illicit financial transactions worth millions of dollars. She knew that accepting the offer would be illicit and could cost her the job. Illicit activities such as smuggling continue to pose a serious challenge to law enforcement agencies.

english_meaning: In a manner that is forbidden by law, rules, or social norms. Done unlawfully, secretly, or without permission. In an illegal or improper way, often involving wrongdoing or moral violation. Carried out against accepted standards or regulations.
example_sentence: Drugs were being sold illicitly in the neighbourhood. He had illicitly transferred company funds to his account. The goods were illicitly imported across the border. They were caught for illicitly using government property. Many people illicitly download films from the internet.

english_meaning: Unable to read or write. Lacking education or knowledge in a particular subject. Ignorant or uneducated in general matters. A person who cannot read or write.
example_sentence: Many adults in rural areas remain illiterate due to lack of schools. He was computer illiterate and needed help sending emails. The government launched a campaign to help illiterate citizens learn to read. She felt illiterate in matters of finance and sought advice.

english_meaning: To light up or make bright with light. To make something clearer or easier to understand. To enlighten or inform someone. To decorate a manuscript or text with coloured illustrations. To shed light on a topic, idea, or problem.
example_sentence: The street lamps were switched on to illuminate the road during the heavy fog. Her detailed explanation helped to illuminate the complexities of the new tax policy. The documentary was designed to illuminate the struggles faced by refugees around the world. Candles were placed along the path to illuminate the garden during the evening celebration.

english_meaning: The action of lighting up or brightening a place or object. The light provided by a source. Spiritual or intellectual enlightenment. The decoration of manuscripts or texts with illustrations and coloured designs. The process of making something clearer or better understood.
example_sentence: The illumination of the cathedral on Christmas Eve was a truly breathtaking sight. She experienced a sudden illumination after reading the philosopher's work for the first time. The illumination of medieval manuscripts was a painstaking art that took years to perfect. Adequate illumination in the workplace is essential for the health and productivity of all employees.

english_meaning: A false idea or belief, especially about somebody or about a situation. An unreal image presented to the bodily or mental vision, a deceptive appearance, a false show, mockery, hallucination.
example_sentence: He could no longer distinguish between illusion and reality. I don’t want to have my illusions shattered!. He had no illusions about his talents as a singer.

english_meaning: Not real although seeming to be. Deceiving by false show, deceitful, deceptive, false, illusory, unreal. Based on or producing illusion.
example_sentence: There is an illusive sense of depth. The illusive security of yesteryear

english_meaning: Use of descriptive language to create mental pictures. Words and expressions that appeal to the senses such as sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch. It helps readers imagine scenes, emotions, or experiences clearly, especially in poetry and literature.
example_sentence: The golden sunlight flooded the quiet room. The smell of rain filled the dry air. Her voice was as soft as falling snow. The dark clouds painted the sky with fear.

english_meaning: Capable of being imagined, conceived, or believed possible. Used for emphasis to mean every possible kind or the greatest possible degree.
example_sentence: She tried every imaginable solution. It was the best imaginable outcome. The journey presented every imaginable difficulty. The shop sells furniture in every imaginable style.

english_meaning: Existing only in the imagination and not in reality. Invented, fanciful, or fictitious. In mathematics, involving the square root of a negative number.
example_sentence: The child has an imaginary friend. The story takes place in an imaginary kingdom. We considered an imaginary situation to test the idea. Imaginary numbers are essential in complex mathematics.

english_meaning: The ability to form mental images, ideas, or concepts not present to the senses. Creative ability and inventiveness. The part of the mind that imagines. An unfounded belief or fanciful idea.
example_sentence: Children use their imagination during play. Her imagination helped her write a vivid novel. Solving the problem required skill and imagination. The strange sound was only his imagination.

english_meaning: Having or showing creativity and a high degree of originality. Existing only in the imagination rather than in reality. Relating to the ability of the mind to invent new ideas or concepts. Displaying resourcefulness and cleverness in problem solving.
example_sentence: The author wrote an imaginative novel filled with incredible mystical creatures. Her imaginative design transformed the small cramped room into a spacious artistic studio. Young children are naturally imaginative and can turn simple cardboard boxes into spaceships. The team came up with an imaginative solution to solve the complex technical problem.

english_meaning: To form a mental image or concept of something that is not present to the senses. To believe, suppose, or think that something is true or likely. To create or invent something new using one's mind and creativity. To assume or picture a hypothetical scenario for the sake of argument.
example_sentence: She tried to imagine what her future life in the big city would look like. I cannot imagine living in such extreme cold weather conditions without heating. Children often imagine elaborate fantasy worlds when playing outdoors together. Do you imagine that he will agree to our new proposal without any objections?

english_meaning: A stupid or foolish person. Someone who acts without sense or good judgment. A person of very low intelligence, in older medical usage. Silly or idiotic in nature. Marked by great foolishness.
example_sentence: Only an imbecile would leave the door open at night. He called himself an imbecile for missing the deadline. The imbecile plan wasted everyone's time. Do not make such imbecile remarks in public.

english_meaning: Extremely foolish or stupid. Showing a complete lack of good sense or judgement. Describing behaviour or ideas that are silly and unreasonable. An offensive older term relating to severe intellectual disability.
example_sentence: That was an imbecilic decision made without any thought. He apologised for his imbecilic remarks at the meeting. Their imbecilic plan was rejected immediately. She refused to answer such an imbecilic question.

english_meaning: To drink something, especially alcohol. To absorb or soak up liquid. Figuratively, it means to absorb or take in ideas, knowledge, or information.
example_sentence: Plants imbibe water through their roots to survive. The scholars gathered to imbibe the wisdom of the ancient texts. He likes to imbibe a glass of wine with his dinner. The sponge will imbibe the spilled ink quickly.

english_meaning: To arrange or overlap in a regular pattern like roof tiles or fish scales. To lay one edge over another in a series. Having overlapping edges. To cover with overlapping layers. Arranged in a tiled, layered fashion.
example_sentence: The scales of the fish imbricate along its body. Roof tiles are imbricated to keep out rain. The petals imbricate to form a tight bud. Artists imbricated colored papers to create the design.

english_meaning: A complicated, confusing, or embarrassing situation, especially one involving disagreement, misunderstanding, or scandal. A messy or entangled state of affairs that is difficult to resolve. The word is often used in political, diplomatic, or personal contexts where many parties and issues are tangled together.
example_sentence: The government found itself in a diplomatic imbroglio with its neighbour. The political imbroglio lasted for several months. He got entangled in a legal imbroglio over his property. The company's financial imbroglio damaged its reputation. Reporters covered every detail of the celebrity imbroglio.

english_meaning: To stain or drench something, especially with blood. To saturate or soak deeply with a liquid. To contaminate or taint morally.
example_sentence: The battlefield was imbrued with the blood of those who had fallen in the conflict. His conscience was imbrued with guilt after he failed to speak the truth when it mattered most. The cloth was imbrued with deep red dye and left to dry in the afternoon sun. The tyrant's hands were said to be imbrued with the suffering of countless innocent people. The poet wrote of a land imbrued with the sorrow of centuries of oppression.

english_meaning: To inspire or permeate with a feeling, quality, or idea. It refers to deeply saturating something with a particular characteristic or emotion so that it becomes completely influenced. The term is often used when a teacher or parent instills values into a person.
example_sentence: The coach tried to imbue his team with a sense of confidence before the big game. Her poetry is often imbued with a deep sense of melancholy and loss. The sunset seemed to imbue the entire valley with a golden, ethereal glow. Teachers aim to imbue their students with a lifelong love for learning and curiosity.

english_meaning: To copy or reproduce the actions, speech, appearance, or behavior of someone or something. It can be done for learning, admiration, practice, or sometimes for humor or mockery.
example_sentence: Teacher provide a model for children to imitate. She knew that girls used to imitate her & laugh at her behind her back. Children often imitate their parents' behavior. The actor can imitate famous leaders very well. She tried to imitate her teacher’s pronunciation. Some artists imitate nature in their paintings.

english_meaning: Copying or reproducing someone or something. The act of copying the actions, appearance, speech, style, or behavior of another person, object, or thing. It can be done for learning, entertainment, practice, or sometimes deception.
example_sentence: The child learned language through imitation of his parents. Her imitation of the teacher made the whole class laugh. The bag was an imitation of a famous brand. Good habits can develop through imitation of positive role models.

english_meaning: A person or thing that copies another person’s appearance, voice, behavior, methods, or style. A performer who mimics famous people or recognizable sounds. A person whose work closely follows another’s and lacks originality. An animal or object that resembles another for protection or effect.
example_sentence: The comedian is a gifted imitator of famous politicians. Critics called the painter an imitator of earlier masters. The young singer began as an imitator before finding her own voice. This harmless insect is an imitator of a dangerous wasp.

english_meaning: Perfectly clean, spotless, pure, flawless, or free from any mistakes, faults, or impurities. Something that is exceptionally clean, neat, pure, or perfect. It can refer to physical cleanliness, moral purity, or a condition that is free from defects and errors.
example_sentence: The hotel room was immaculate and beautifully organized. She always keeps her office immaculate. The mechanic returned the car in immaculate condition. His immaculate reputation earned him the trust of everyone.

english_meaning: In a perfectly clean, neat, or tidy manner. Without any stain, mark, error, or fault. With exceptionally careful, precise, elegant, or flawless execution.
example_sentence: He was immaculately dressed for the formal dinner. The kitchen was kept immaculately clean. She performed the difficult routine immaculately. Every document had been immaculately prepared and organized.

english_meaning: Not fully developed or grown. Behaving in a childish way that is not suitable for one's age. Lacking experience or emotional maturity. Not yet ripe or ready.
example_sentence: His immature reaction disappointed his teachers. The fruit is still immature and should not be picked. Some adults behave in an immature manner when angry. Immature plants need special care to grow properly.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being not fully developed, grown, or mature. Behaviour or thinking that is childish or not suited to one's age. Lack of emotional or intellectual development.
example_sentence: His immaturity was evident in the way he reacted to every small problem with frustration. The manager attributed the team's failures to the immaturity of its youngest members. Her emotional immaturity made it difficult for her to maintain any long-term relationship. Immaturity is normal in young children but becomes a concern if it continues into adulthood. The therapist noted signs of emotional immaturity that needed to be addressed in the sessions.

english_meaning: Too great, vast, or intense to be measured. Impossible to calculate precisely. Extremely large in amount, degree, or importance. Beyond any practical standard of measurement. Limitless or seemingly without bounds.
example_sentence: Her support was of immeasurable value to the project. The disaster caused immeasurable suffering across the region. He felt immeasurable relief when the child was found safe. The library has made an immeasurable contribution to education.

english_meaning: To an extent too great to measure. By an extremely large amount or degree. In a way that cannot be calculated precisely. Beyond ordinary limits or comparison.
example_sentence: The new treatment improved her quality of life immeasurably. We are immeasurably grateful for your kindness. His confidence grew immeasurably after the successful presentation. The quiet garden made the house immeasurably more appealing.

english_meaning: Extremely large in size, amount, degree, or intensity. It can refer to physical size, emotional strength, importance, or quantity.
example_sentence: The desert stretched across an immense area of land. She felt immense joy after hearing the good news. The project required an immense amount of effort. The mountain looked immense from a distance.

english_meaning: To a very great degree or extent. Extremely or enormously. Used to emphasise the large scale or intensity of something.
example_sentence: She was immensely grateful for all the support she received during the difficult period. The new policy has proved immensely popular among the younger generation of voters. He found the experience immensely rewarding despite the many challenges he faced. The documentary was immensely informative and changed the way she thought about the issue. The team worked immensely hard to complete the project before the deadline.

english_meaning: To dip or submerge completely in a liquid or activity. To involve oneself deeply in a particular activity, subject, or environment, or to put something completely into a liquid so that it is fully covered.
example_sentence: She immersed the vegetables in boiling water. He immersed himself in his studies to prepare for the exam. The artist immersed the brush in paint before starting. They were immersed in the festival, enjoying every moment.

english_meaning: A person who moves from their native country to another country with the intention of settling there, usually for work, education, safety, or family reasons. The focus is on entering and living in the new country, often on a long term or permanent basis.
example_sentence: The immigrant worked hard to build a new life in a foreign country. Many immigrants contribute positively to the economy. She is an immigrant who moved for better educational opportunities. The city is home to immigrants from many cultures.

english_meaning: To come to live permanently in a foreign country. To move from one country to another with the intention of settling there permanently. It focuses on entering and living in a new country, usually for work, safety, family, or better opportunities. The word is used from the point of view of the country being entered.
example_sentence: Many people immigrate to Canada for better job opportunities. Her parents immigrated from Pakistan in the 1990s. He plans to immigrate after completing his studies. Families often immigrate to escape conflict or poverty.

english_meaning: The act of coming to live permanently in another country. The process in which people enter a foreign country to live there permanently or for a long period.
example_sentence: Immigration has increased due to better job opportunities abroad. The government introduced new immigration policies last year. Many families rely on immigration to reunite with relatives. Immigration can contribute positively to a country’s economy.

english_meaning: The state or fact of being about to happen, especially something threatening or unavoidable. It refers to the quality of being immediate or physically close in time. It creates a sense of urgent pressure or expectation.
example_sentence: The imminence of the storm forced the sailors to seek shelter in the harbor immediately. Everyone in the city felt the imminence of the impending economic crisis. The imminence of the deadline caused a great deal of stress among the staff members. Despite the imminence of danger, the soldiers remained remarkably calm and focused.

english_meaning: About to happen or take place very soon. Often used to describe a danger or an event that is hanging over one's head and cannot be avoided. It denotes something that is likely to occur at any moment.
example_sentence: The dark clouds suggested that a heavy downpour was imminent and unavoidable. We were told that a change in leadership was imminent due to the recent scandal. The scientists warned that a volcanic eruption was imminent following the seismic activity. After weeks of negotiation, a final agreement between the two nations seemed imminent.

english_meaning: Very soon. At any moment. In the immediate future. About to happen. On the verge of occurring. Impendingly. Right away. Shortly. Within a very short period of time. With urgency and proximity. In a way that is about to occur without delay.
example_sentence: The storm is expected to arrive imminently, so please seek shelter. Authorities believe that an agreement will be reached imminently. The species is imminently threatened with extinction if we do not act. She was told that her flight would be boarding imminently.

english_meaning: Describing two or more liquids that cannot be mixed together to form a uniform solution. Unable to mix or blend, especially of liquids. Incapable of combining smoothly.
example_sentence: Oil and water are immiscible liquids that separate into distinct layers when left to settle. The chemist noted that the two solutions were immiscible and would not form a homogeneous mixture. Understanding which substances are immiscible is important in industrial and pharmaceutical processes. The experiment demonstrated how immiscible fluids behave differently from miscible ones. He added the immiscible solvent carefully to avoid disturbing the layers.

english_meaning: Not able to move or not moving at all. It can describe a person, object, or situation that stays completely still, either physically or mentally. It is often used for injury, shock, fear, or fixed positions.
example_sentence: After the accident, his leg was immobile for weeks. The statue remained immobile despite the strong wind. She stood immobile with fear when she heard the noise. The broken machine lay immobile on the factory floor.

english_meaning: The state of not being able to move or be moved. The quality of being fixed in one place. A lack of social or economic movement or change. The condition of being stationary or paralyzed.
example_sentence: The patient suffered from total immobility after the severe spinal injury. The heavy snowfall caused the complete immobility of traffic throughout the city. Economic immobility remains a significant challenge for the lower class in this region. The sheer weight of the ancient stone statue ensured its permanent immobility.

english_meaning: The act of preventing something or someone from moving. The state of being unable to move or be moved. The medical procedure of fixing a joint or limb in one position to allow for healing. The process of making capital or assets unavailable for use. The reduction of bioavailability of a substance in the soil or environment.
example_sentence: The doctor ordered the immobilization of his fractured leg using a plaster cast. Proper immobilization of the spine is crucial after a severe car accident. The police used a specialized device for the immobilization of the suspect's vehicle. The immobilization of assets during the legal dispute caused significant financial strain.

english_meaning: To prevent something or someone from moving or operating as normal. To fix in place or make incapable of movement, especially a limb or joint for medical reasons. To restrict the movement of assets or capital. To render something ineffective or useless by stopping its motion.
example_sentence: The doctor had to immobilize her leg with a plaster cast to allow the bone to heal. The security system is designed to immobilize the vehicle if an unauthorized key is used. Heavy snowfall managed to immobilize the entire city's public transport system for two days. The sudden strike by the labor union threatened to immobilize the factory's production line.

english_meaning: An electronic security device fitted to a motor vehicle that prevents the engine from running unless the correct key or token is present. A medical device or bandage designed to keep a limb or joint from moving during the healing process. Any person or thing that renders someone or something motionless or unable to act.
example_sentence: The insurance company offers a discount if your car is fitted with a factory-installed immobilizer. After the surgery, the patient had to wear a knee immobilizer for six weeks to ensure proper recovery. The anti-theft system includes an engine immobilizer that cuts off the fuel supply. The doctor checked the fit of the shoulder immobilizer to prevent further injury to the rotator cuff.

english_meaning: Excessive or beyond reasonable limits. Too large or too intense to be acceptable. Lacking self control or restraint. Going far beyond what is considered normal. Showing extreme behavior or habits. Used for behavior, actions, feelings, or quantities that exceed normal, acceptable or sensible limits.
example_sentence: His immoderate spending caused serious financial problems. She received criticism for her immoderate reaction to a small mistake. An immoderate amount of sugar can harm your health. The leader warned against immoderate demands during negotiations.

english_meaning: Too much or beyond a reasonable limit. Excessively or overly. In a way that lacks restraint. Beyond acceptable or normal limits. Without proper control or balance. An action done in an excessive, uncontrolled or overly intense way. It suggests going beyond what is normal, sensible or balanced.
example_sentence: He ate immoderately and felt sick afterward. She spent money immoderately during the holiday season. The crowd cheered immoderately when the team scored. He reacted immoderately to a small mistake.

english_meaning: Lacking humility or decency; boastful or conceited. It can also refer to something that is indecent or shamelessly bold in behavior or appearance. It describes a person who overestimates their own importance or behaves inappropriately.
example_sentence: His immodest behavior at the formal dinner party embarrassed all of his close friends. She made an immodest claim about being the most talented musician in the entire country. The performer wore an immodest costume that many spectators found quite shocking. It was immodest of him to brag about his wealth in front of people who were struggling.

english_meaning: In a way that lacks modesty, restraint, or propriety. In an indecent, excessive, or boastful manner. Without regard for acceptable social standards of behaviour or dress.
example_sentence: She was criticised for speaking immodestly about her own achievements in front of colleagues. He dressed immodestly for the formal occasion and attracted many disapproving looks. The actor spoke immodestly in the interview, claiming to be the best in the industry. She immodestly compared herself to the greatest writers who had ever lived. He boasted immodestly about his wealth at every opportunity he got.

english_meaning: Lack of modesty or decency in behaviour, dress, or speech. Excessive pride, boastfulness, or indecency. The quality of behaving or dressing in a way that is considered improper or shameless.
example_sentence: Her immodesty in taking all the credit for a team effort embarrassed her colleagues. The audience was shocked by the immodesty displayed in the performer's act. His immodesty in constantly praising himself made it difficult for others to work alongside him. Teachers often address immodesty in dress codes to maintain a respectful school environment. The public figure was widely criticised for the immodesty of his remarks.

english_meaning: To kill or offer as a sacrifice, especially by burning. To sacrifice a person or animal in a ritual, historically by burning. To kill as an offering to a deity or cause. To destroy something completely, often for a symbolic purpose. To burn oneself intentionally, usually as protest or devotion.
example_sentence: The ancient tribe used to immolate animals during religious ceremonies. He threatened to immolate himself to protest against injustice. The ritual required them to immolate offerings at dawn. She would never immolate her values for personal gain.

english_meaning: The act of killing or destroying something by fire or offering it as a sacrifice. Ritual killing by fire. The act of destroying something in flames. Giving up something valuable for a moral or emotional reason. Martyr like sacrifice. The act of burning something completely, often as a ritual sacrifice. It can also describe giving up or sacrificing something valuable for a cause.
example_sentence: The ancient tribe practiced immolation during their religious ceremonies. The novel describes the hero’s immolation for the freedom of his people. They were shocked by the immolation of rare artifacts in the fire. Her immolation of personal comfort for her children earned everyone's respect.

english_meaning: Not conforming to accepted moral standards or principles. Wicked, wrong, or unethical. Going against the generally accepted rules of right and wrong behaviour.
example_sentence: The committee declared the experiment immoral because it violated the rights of the participants. Stealing from the poor to enrich the already wealthy is considered deeply immoral. He knew that lying to the court would be immoral and could have serious consequences. The novel explored how ordinary people can be drawn into immoral acts under pressure. She refused to participate in what she considered an immoral business practice.

english_meaning: Behavior that is wrong, unethical, or against accepted moral standards. Lack of moral principles. Behavior that harms others. Actions showing disrespect for ethical values. A general decline in moral behavior.
example_sentence: The judge condemned the politician's immorality during the corruption case. Many stories warn children about the dangers of immorality. Immorality in society often increases when rules are ignored. She refused to take part in any act of immorality.

english_meaning: In a way that is wrong according to accepted standards of behaviour. Without regard for honesty, decency, or moral principles. In a manner considered sinful or ethically unacceptable. Wickedly and against the rules of right conduct.
example_sentence: He acted immorally by cheating his own partners. The company behaved immorally towards its workers. She was accused of immorally profiting from the crisis. Many felt the officials had acted immorally, if not illegally.

english_meaning: Living forever, never dying. A being that never dies, Remembered forever because of great work. Something lasting forever. Gods or characters that cannot die. Existing without end. Continuing forever. Not subject to death.
example_sentence: The hero became immortal in history. Many cultures believe gods are immortal. Her immortal poetry is still read today. The story made him immortal among his people.

english_meaning: A person who believes that human beings can or should live forever. Someone who supports research aimed at ending ageing and death. A believer in the immortality of the soul or of the body. Relating to the belief that death can be overcome.
example_sentence: The conference was attended by scientists and immortalists. As an immortalist, he funds research into ageing. Immortalist thinkers argue that death is a solvable problem. Her immortalist views were widely debated in the press.

english_meaning: The state of living forever and never dying. Endless life or existence beyond physical death. Lasting fame that keeps a person's name alive long after they have died. In religion, the eternal life of the soul.
example_sentence: Many ancient stories describe a search for immortality. His poetry earned him immortality among readers. Believers hold that the soul has immortality. Scientists do not claim to have discovered immortality.

english_meaning: To make someone or something remembered forever. To give lasting fame through art, writing, music, or achievement. To preserve the memory of a person or event permanently. To grant endless life, especially in myth or belief.
example_sentence: The painter immortalized the village in his landscapes. Her courage was immortalized in a famous poem. The monument immortalizes those who died in the flood. Old photographs immortalize moments that would otherwise be forgotten.

english_meaning: Not able to be moved from one place to another. Firmly fixed in position and impossible to shift. Refusing to change one's opinion, decision, or attitude. In law, describing property such as land and buildings.
example_sentence: The statue is immovable without heavy machinery. He remained immovable in his decision to resign. Immovable property is taxed under a separate law. She stood immovable at the door, refusing to let anyone pass.

english_meaning: Protected against a particular disease because of the body's defences or vaccination. Not affected or influenced by something unpleasant. Officially free from an obligation, tax, or punishment. Relating to the body's system that fights infection.
example_sentence: Most children are now immune to measles. She seems immune to criticism from her rivals. Diplomats are immune from prosecution in the host country. A healthy diet strengthens the immune system.

english_meaning: The ability of the body to resist a particular infection or toxin through the action of specific antibodies or white blood cells. Protection or exemption from something, especially an obligation, penalty, or duty. In law, freedom from prosecution or legal action granted to a person. Resistance to something unpleasant.
example_sentence: Vaccines help the body build immunity against dangerous diseases. The witness was given immunity from prosecution in exchange for his testimony. Diplomats often enjoy immunity from local laws while serving abroad. Regular exercise and good food strengthen the body's immunity. No one has complete immunity from criticism in public life.

english_meaning: A medical specialist who studies and treats disorders of the immune system. A doctor who specializes in immunology, including allergies and autoimmune diseases. A scientist who researches how the body defends against infections and diseases.
synonyms: ["Immune system specialist","Allergy specialist","Immunology expert","Immune disorder doctor"]
example_sentence: The immunologist is treating her autoimmune condition. He consulted an immunologist for his severe allergies. Immunologists play a crucial role in vaccine development. The immunologist explained how the immune system works.

english_meaning: Not changing; unchangeable. Something that cannot be changed, altered, or modified; fixed and permanent in nature.
example_sentence: The laws of physics are immutable. Her commitment to honesty was immutable. Time is immutable and moves forward without pause. The king’s decree was considered immutable by the people.

english_meaning: A strong effect or influence; also the force of one object hitting another. To strike or come into contact forcefully. The powerful effect or result of something on a person, situation, or thing. It can also mean a physical collision between objects.
example_sentence: The new law had a major impact on students. The impact of the earthquake was felt across the city. Her speech made a strong impact on the audience. The car stopped just before impact with the wall.

english_meaning: Strongly affected or influenced by something. Having been hit or struck with force. Firmly wedged, packed, or pressed tightly into a space. (Of a tooth) unable to grow out properly because it is wedged against another tooth or bone. Affected negatively by a situation, event, or decision.
example_sentence: Thousands of families were impacted by the sudden floods. The new policy has impacted small businesses across the country. The dentist removed an impacted tooth from the back of his jaw. Soil that is heavily impacted makes it difficult for roots to grow.

english_meaning: Having a strong effect on someone or something. Producing a powerful and lasting impression. Capable of creating meaningful or noticeable change. Effective and memorable in the way it influences people.
example_sentence: Her speech was short but incredibly impactful. The charity ran an impactful campaign that changed public opinion. We need a more impactful way to present these findings. His impactful leadership transformed the entire organisation.

english_meaning: To damage or weaken something, especially a faculty or function. To make something less effective, strong, or valuable. To diminish the quality, ability, or strength of something.
example_sentence: Excessive noise can permanently impair hearing if workers are not provided with proper protection. Drinking alcohol before driving is dangerous because it impairs judgement and reaction time. The injury to her knee did not impair her ability to return to competitive sport within months. Poor nutrition during childhood can impair cognitive development and academic performance. The medication was known to impair concentration, so patients were warned not to drive.

english_meaning: Weakened or damaged so that it no longer works properly. Having a reduced ability such as poor sight, hearing, or movement. Affected by alcohol or drugs so that judgement is not reliable. Reduced in quality, strength, or value.
example_sentence: The new law protects visually impaired passengers. His memory was impaired after the long illness. Driving while impaired is a serious criminal offence. Heavy rain impaired visibility on the motorway.

english_meaning: A condition in which a part of the body or mind does not work fully. Damage or weakening that reduces the strength, value, or quality of something. A loss of ability such as hearing, sight, or movement. In accounting, a permanent reduction in the recorded value of an asset.
example_sentence: The accident left him with a serious hearing impairment. Schools must support children with learning impairments. Long working hours caused a clear impairment of his judgement. The company reported an impairment of its overseas assets.

english_meaning: To pierce or transfix with a sharp pointed object such as a spike or spear. To thrust a pointed object through something or someone. To fix in a helpless or vulnerable position.
example_sentence: The fence was designed with pointed tops to prevent anyone from climbing over and getting impaled. The knight was nearly impaled on the opponent's lance during the tournament. The insect was impaled on a pin and mounted in the display case for the natural history collection. He accidentally impaled his hand on a rusted nail while working in the old barn. The author described how the warrior impaled his enemy's shield with a single powerful thrust.

english_meaning: To give, share, or pass on information, knowledge, or a quality to someone. To cause something such as knowledge, information, advice, or a feeling to be known or received by someone. It usually refers to sharing something that the other person did not previously have.
example_sentence: The teacher imparts knowledge to her students every day. He tried to impart his experience to the younger employees. Good leaders impart confidence in their team. The workshop aims to impart practical skills to participants.

english_meaning: Treating all rivals or disputants equally; fair and just. It describes a person or a decision that is not influenced by personal feelings, interests, or prejudice. It is a vital quality for judges, referees, and leaders.
example_sentence: A judge must remain completely impartial when listening to the arguments of both sides. We need an impartial observer to help resolve this dispute between the departments. The committee promised to conduct an impartial investigation into the allegations. It is difficult to remain impartial when the outcome affects your own family members.

english_meaning: Equal treatment of all rivals or disputants; fairness. The quality of being objective and not favoring one side over another. It is the concept of justice that relies on lack of bias.
example_sentence: The integrity of our legal system relies heavily on the absolute impartiality of the jury. Reporters are expected to maintain strict impartiality when covering political elections. The referee's impartiality was questioned after he made several controversial calls. We chose an outside firm to ensure the impartiality of the auditing process.

english_meaning: To act in a way that does not favor one person or side over another. It involves treating all rivals or disputants equally and maintaining a neutral stance. It is the quality of making decisions based on objective criteria rather than personal bias.
example_sentence: The judge listened to both sides of the argument impartially. Information should be presented impartially so that the public can make their own minds up. The committee promised to review every application impartially. It is difficult to judge your own children impartially.

english_meaning: Impossible to travel along or through. Describing a road, path, or route that cannot be crossed or passed. Blocked or obstructed to the point where movement is not possible.
example_sentence: Heavy snowfall had made the mountain roads impassable for several days. The flood left the main highway impassable and cut off several villages from the rest of the country. The jungle trail was impassable due to the dense undergrowth and fallen trees. Rescue teams were unable to reach the affected area because the bridge had become impassable. The river crossing became impassable during the monsoon season when water levels rose sharply.

english_meaning: A deadlock or situation where no progress is possible. A stalemate in negotiations. A blocked road or dead end. A point in a process where further action is impossible. Emotional or mental standstill. A situation in which two sides cannot reach an agreement or make progress. It often happens in negotiations, discussions, conflicts, or decision making when neither side is willing to change position. It can also describe any condition where forward movement becomes impossible.
example_sentence: Negotiations have reached an impasse. An arbitrator was called in to break the impasse. She had reached an impasse in her career. The committee faced an impasse over budget allocation. We are at an impasse and need a new strategy to solve the problem. The peace talks ended in an impasse after both sides refused to compromise. The project reached an impasse due to lack of funding. After hours of debate, the committee found itself at an impasse.

english_meaning: The feeling of annoyance caused by having to wait. A lack of willingness to tolerate delay, difficulty, or the faults of others. Eager restlessness to do something or for something to happen. Irritability shown when things do not move as quickly as desired.
example_sentence: He tapped his fingers on the desk with growing impatience. Her impatience with slow service was obvious to everyone. The children waited for the parade with cheerful impatience. Try to control your impatience while the team learns the new system.

english_meaning: To formally accuse a public official of wrongdoing. To officially charge a public official with misconduct or illegal actions while in office. It can also mean to question the truth or validity of something such as a statement or evidence.
example_sentence: The parliament decided to impeach the president for corruption. The lawyer tried to impeach the witness's credibility. Lawmakers voted to impeach the governor after the scandal. The defense attempted to impeach the evidence presented in court.

english_meaning: Capable of being questioned, accused, or charged with wrongdoing. Something or someone described as impeachable can be legally or morally challenged. It may refer to a person whose actions can lead to formal charges, or to evidence or statements that can be doubted or discredited.
example_sentence: The official’s actions were clearly impeachable under the law. His testimony was found to be impeachable due to contradictions. Any misuse of public funds is considered impeachable conduct. The lawyer argued that the witness’s statement was impeachable.

english_meaning: A formal process to accuse a public official of wrongdoing. A formal legal process by which a legislative body brings charges against a high-ranking public official, such as a president or judge, for misconduct or violation of law. It may lead to removal from office after trial.
example_sentence: The parliament started impeachment proceedings against the president. The judge faced impeachment due to corruption charges. The lawyer attempted the impeachment of the witness's credibility. The constitution explains how impeachment works in detail.

english_meaning: Perfect, without any faults or errors. Flawless in behavior, appearance, or quality. Free from mistakes or wrongdoing.
example_sentence: Her performance in the play was impeccable and earned a standing ovation. The chef’s presentation of the dish was impeccable, impressing all the guests. He has impeccable manners and always treats everyone with respect. The report was impeccable, leaving no room for criticism.

english_meaning: In a way that is perfect, flawless, without any fault, mistake, or flaw.  With the highest standards of correctness, neatness, or behavior.
example_sentence: The airport was new, impressive, and impeccably clean. Her work is well written and impeccably researched. Medical practitioners tend to be impeccably honest, devoted to their patients, and incredibly hardworking. His logic is impeccably straightforward. He was impeccably polite. His mother was always impeccably groomed. He had behaved impeccably both times.

english_meaning: Having little or no money. It is a more formal way of describing someone who is poor or penniless. The term often suggests a habitual state of lacking financial resources rather than a temporary setback.
example_sentence: The impecunious artist lived in a tiny attic and struggled to afford basic art supplies. Despite his impecunious upbringing, he eventually became a successful businessman. She offered a small loan to her impecunious cousin to help him pay the rent. The charity provides assistance to impecunious students who cannot afford tuition fees.

english_meaning: To delay or prevent something from happening; to obstruct. To make it difficult or slow for someone or something to progress, move, or succeed. It involves causing an obstacle or hindrance that restricts smooth action.
example_sentence: Heavy traffic can impede emergency vehicles from reaching the hospital on time. His lack of experience may impede his chances of promotion. Snowstorms often impede travel during winter. Political disagreements can impede the progress of important legislation.

english_meaning: Something that hinders or obstructs progress. An obstacle that makes movement or success difficult. A defect, especially in speech, that prevents normal functioning. A legal obstacle to marriage. A barrier to achieving a goal. An impediment is anything that gets in the way of progress, communication, or action, whether it is a physical obstacle, a personal disability, or a legal restriction.
example_sentence: His speech impediment did not stop him from becoming a great leader. Lack of education is a major impediment to economic progress. The fallen tree was a serious impediment on the highway. Financial problems became an impediment to his higher studies. The court found no legal impediment to their marriage.

english_meaning: Equipment, baggage, or other things that make movement difficult. Burdens or obstacles that hinder progress.
example_sentence: The hikers left unnecessary impedimenta behind. Heavy luggage became impedimenta during the climb. Bureaucracy can become impedimenta to innovation. She removed every piece of impedimenta from the narrow path.

english_meaning: To drive or strongly encourage someone to take action. To force or motivate something to move forward.
example_sentence: A desire to help others impelled her to volunteer. The evidence impelled the police to investigate. His conscience impelled him to tell the truth. Rising costs impelled the company to change its strategy.

english_meaning: To be about to happen, especially in a threatening or imminent way. To hang over someone or something as a threat or danger. To be imminent or close at hand.
example_sentence: Dark clouds gathered on the horizon, signalling the storm that impended. A sense of doom impended over the community as the news of the disaster spread. The threat of war impended over the region for several months before diplomacy prevailed. He could feel that change impended as the political situation grew more unstable by the day. A severe economic crisis impended, and the government was under pressure to act quickly.

english_meaning: About to happen, especially something unpleasant or important. Near in time and likely to occur soon.
example_sentence: Dark clouds warned of an impending storm. The workers prepared for the impending deadline. She felt nervous about the impending examination. The town was evacuated because of the impending flood.

english_meaning: The quality of being impossible to enter, pass through, see through, or understand. Resistance to penetration or explanation.
example_sentence: The impenetrability of the armor protected the vehicle. Readers complained about the impenetrability of the technical article. The forest’s impenetrability slowed the search. Researchers tested the material’s impenetrability to water.

english_meaning: Impossible to pass through, enter, or see through. Impossible to understand or solve because it is extremely difficult or obscure.
example_sentence: The fortress was protected by an impenetrable wall. Thick fog made the forest impenetrable to sight. His explanation was impenetrable to beginners. The security system is designed to be impenetrable.

english_meaning: In a way that cannot be entered, passed through, seen through, or understood. So obscurely or densely that understanding is difficult.
example_sentence: The author writes impenetrably about the theory. The cave was impenetrably dark. The hedge grew impenetrably thick. The legal document was written impenetrably for ordinary readers.

english_meaning: Not feeling regret or remorse for wrongdoing. Unrepentant and unwilling to change one’s behavior.
example_sentence: The impenitent criminal showed no regret. He remained impenitent after hurting his colleague. Her impenitent attitude angered the victims. The judge noted that the offender was still impenitent.

english_meaning: Very important and needing immediate attention or action. A thing that is very important and needs immediate attention or action, a factor that makes something necessary. Ahe form of a verb that expresses an order.
example_sentence: It is imperative to continue the treatment for at least two months. In ‘Go away!’ the verb is in the imperative.

english_meaning: Too small, slight, or subtle to be noticed or detected. So slight, gradual, or tiny that it cannot be seen, heard, or felt easily. It is below the level of human perception.
example_sentence: The change in his behavior was almost imperceptible. There was an imperceptible movement in the curtain. The temperature dropped in an imperceptible way during the night. Her smile had an imperceptible sadness behind it.

english_meaning: In a way that is too slight, gradual, or subtle to be noticed. Without being detected by the senses or attention.
example_sentence: The temperature rose imperceptibly during the afternoon. The colors changed imperceptibly from blue to green. His accent improved imperceptibly over the year. The boat moved imperceptibly away from the shore.

english_meaning: Not complete, flawless, or entirely correct. Having faults, weaknesses, or defects. Not yet perfected.
example_sentence: The plan is imperfect but workable. We live in an imperfect world. The vase has an imperfect shape. Her English is imperfect, but her meaning is clear.

english_meaning: A fault, defect, or weakness. The state of being incomplete or not perfect.
example_sentence: The small imperfection made the handmade bowl unique. Everyone has some imperfection. The inspector found an imperfection in the surface. The artist embraced the imperfection of natural materials.

english_meaning: Relating to an empire, emperor, or empress. Grand, majestic, or impressive in quality or character. Pertaining to a system of non-metric weights and measures.
example_sentence: The imperial palace was decorated with gold and silk. The army marched under the imperial flag. They still use imperial units like miles and gallons in some places. Her imperial posture commanded respect from everyone present.

english_meaning: A British unit of weight equal to two thousand two hundred and forty pounds, or about 1016 kilograms. Also known as the long ton or gross ton. A traditional measure used for shipping, mining, and heavy cargo.
example_sentence: The ship carried eight hundred imperial tons of coal. An imperial ton is heavier than a US ton. Mining output was once recorded in imperial tons. The cargo weighed just over one imperial ton.

english_meaning: A policy or ideology of extending a nation's rule over foreign countries, often through military force or political dominance. The state or advocacy of extending power and dominion.
example_sentence: The country fought hard to liberate itself from Western imperialism. Economic imperialism can sometimes be as damaging as military conquest. Students of history study the rise and fall of European imperialism. The speech condemned all forms of foreign imperialism.

english_meaning: A person who supports, advocates, or practices imperialism. Relating to or characteristic of imperialism or an empire.
example_sentence: The imperialist powers divided the continent into colonies. He was criticized for holding imperialist views on foreign policy. The historical museum displays artifacts taken during the imperialist era. Resistance grew against the imperialist government.

english_meaning: To put something or someone into a situation where they are exposed to danger or risk. To endanger or jeopardize safety or existence.
example_sentence: Toxic waste spills imperil the surrounding wildlife and water supply. Driving at such high speeds will imperil the safety of everyone in the vehicle. Delaying the medical treatment could seriously imperil her health. High inflation rates imperil the financial stability of many families.

english_meaning: Commanding, arrogant, domineering, expecting complete obedience. A person who behaves as if they have absolute authority over others. Such a person gives orders confidently, expects immediate obedience, and often appears proud, arrogant, or domineering. It can also describe a forceful or urgent manner.
example_sentence: The manager's imperious tone made the employees uncomfortable. She gave an imperious command that everyone obeyed immediately. His imperious attitude made it difficult for others to work with him. The queen spoke in an imperious voice that demanded respect.

english_meaning: In an arrogant, domineering, or dictatorial manner. Acting with an assumption of superior authority without justification.
example_sentence: She imperiously demanded to speak with the manager immediately. The boss gestured imperiously for his assistant to bring the file. He spoke imperiously, expecting no one to challenge his orders. The king clapped his hands imperiously to dismiss the council.

english_meaning: To remain undamaged or never decay. To stay everlasting. To resist destruction. To avoid decline. To stay unharmed, unchanged, or undestroyed over time. It refers to anything that does not fade, rot, weaken, or disappear. It can be used for memories, values, objects, or anything that endures without losing its quality.
example_sentence: Great ideas often imperish even after centuries. His love for knowledge will imperish in every stage of life. Ancient traditions can imperish despite social changes. True friendships sometimes imperish through the hardest times.

english_meaning: Not subject to decay, death, or destruction. Lasting forever or for a very long time. Enduring beyond normal limits; undying or immortal.
example_sentence: The poet's words became imperishable, surviving long after his death and continuing to inspire generations. Her contribution to science is imperishable and will be remembered for centuries to come. The ancient monument stands as an imperishable testament to the skill of those who built it. He believed that the human spirit was imperishable and could not be defeated by suffering. The work of truly great artists is imperishable and transcends the boundaries of time.

english_meaning: Not allowing fluid, gas, or other substances to pass through. Impossible to penetrate or permeate. Resistant to the passage of liquids or gases.
example_sentence: The waterproof jacket is made from an impermeable material that keeps the wearer completely dry. The underground storage facility is lined with impermeable concrete to prevent any leakage. Impermeable rock layers beneath the soil can prevent water from draining properly. The laboratory suit was designed to be impermeable to dangerous chemicals and airborne particles. The dam was constructed with impermeable materials to ensure it would not allow any seepage.

english_meaning: Rude or disrespectful behaviour or speech that is not appropriate to the situation. The quality of being insolent or showing a lack of respect. Irrelevance or inappropriateness in speech or action.
example_sentence: She was shocked by the impertinence of his response to the senior manager's question. The teacher warned the student that such impertinence would not be tolerated in the classroom. His impertinence in interrupting the speaker several times annoyed the entire audience. The young employee's impertinence cost him any chance of promotion within the company. She chose to ignore his impertinence rather than cause a scene in front of the guests.

english_meaning: Acting or done quickly and without thought or care. Marked by sudden energy or emotion. Impulsive and rash in behaviour. Moving with great force and speed. Used for people who act on impulse and for natural forces or actions that are sudden, powerful, and uncontrolled.
example_sentence: His impetuous decision to quit the job surprised everyone. She made an impetuous remark that she later regretted. The impetuous young man rushed into the burning house. An impetuous current swept the boat downstream. Impetuous actions often lead to long-term problems.

english_meaning: To pledge, pawn, or mortgage something as security for a debt. To place property in the hands of a creditor until a loan is repaid.
example_sentence: He had to impignorate the family jewels to pay the debt. The merchant impignorated his land during the famine. They chose to impignorate the shop rather than sell it. Old records show that the estate was impignorated in 1782.

english_meaning: Lacking reverence or respect for God or religion. Not devout or religiously observant. Disrespectful toward sacred things or beliefs. Showing a lack of piety or religious devotion.
example_sentence: The priest condemned the impious behaviour of those who desecrated the holy site. His impious remarks about religious ceremonies offended many people in the community. The novel featured an impious character who challenged every established religious tradition. She was raised in a devout family and was deeply troubled by the impious attitudes she encountered. The judge described the desecration of the monument as an impious and unacceptable act.

english_meaning: To insert or fix something firmly into a person's body, often through surgery. To instill or fix an idea, attitude, or belief firmly in someone's mind. To plant something securely in the ground or a specific location. A small medical device or tissue placed inside the body for a specific function. To embed or graft an object into a surrounding mass.
example_sentence: The doctor decided to implant a pacemaker to help regulate the patient's heartbeat. It is difficult to implant new habits in adults who are set in their ways. Researchers managed to implant a tracking chip into the migratory bird. The dental implant felt just like a natural tooth after the healing process was complete.

english_meaning: The process of placing or embedding something in a fixed position. In medical and biological contexts, it often describes the stage in early pregnancy when the fertilized egg attaches to the lining of the uterus. It can also refer to inserting devices or objects into a body or system.
example_sentence: The doctor explained the implantation of the pacemaker. Implantation of the embryo occurs a few days after fertilization. The company focused on the implantation of new safety protocols. Dental implantation can restore missing teeth effectively.

english_meaning: To put a plan, decision, agreement, or policy into action. To carry out, execute, or fulfil something formally. A tool, instrument, or piece of equipment used for a particular purpose. It is widely used in administrative, technical, and everyday contexts.
example_sentence: The government will implement the new tax policy next year. The school implemented several safety measures after the incident. Farmers use modern implements for cultivation. It is easier to plan than to implement. The company implemented the software across all branches.

english_meaning: Something that indicates or suggests a meaning, conclusion, or relation without stating it directly. In logic and mathematics it can also mean a condition or expression that guarantees another statement is true.
