english_meaning: Not in harmony or keeping with the surrounding context or environment. Out of place or unsuitable. Strange or odd because of not fitting in with its surroundings.
example_sentence: The bright red sofa looked incongruous in the otherwise minimalist grey living room. His laughter seemed incongruous given the solemnity of the occasion. The modern office tower appeared incongruous beside the ancient stone cathedral. She wore a formal dress to the casual beach party, looking rather incongruous among the relaxed guests. The cheerful poster seemed incongruous in the sombre waiting room of the hospital.

english_meaning: Too small or unimportant to be worth consideration. Of little significance or value. Trivial or negligible in amount, degree, or importance.
example_sentence: The donation was by no means inconsiderable and helped fund the project for six months. The risk involved was not inconsiderable and required careful management throughout. The sum may seem inconsiderable to a large corporation but it was significant for the small charity. The additional cost was an inconsiderable fraction of the overall project budget. She dismissed his concerns as inconsiderable, which upset him greatly.

english_meaning: Showing a lack of manners or consideration for others. Not giving enough thought to other people’s feelings or needs. Not thinking or worrying about other people or their feelings.
example_sentence: He was rude and inconsiderate to the waiter. There is no excuse for such inconsiderate behavior. she was inconsiderate by nature, never bothering to hold the door for the next person.  It was inconsiderate of you not to call.

english_meaning: A state where something does not follow a regular pattern, is unreliable, or contradicts itself. It can describe actions, behavior, statements, or results that are not steady or uniform. Lack of consistency, not staying the same.
example_sentence: The inconsistence in his reports made it difficult to trust the data. Her performance showed inconsistence; sometimes excellent, sometimes poor. The inconsistence of the weather ruined our plans. There is inconsistence between what he says and what he does.

english_meaning: The state of being inconsistent, unreliable, or irregular. It can describe behavior, statements, patterns, or results that are contradictory or not uniform.
example_sentence: His inconsistency in submitting reports makes it hard to trust his work. The inconsistency between her words and actions confused everyone. Weather patterns show inconsistency in this region year after year. There is an inconsistency in the data provided by the two departments.

english_meaning: Something or someone that does not follow a regular pattern, standard, or set of rules. It can refer to behavior, quality, performance, or statements that are unreliable, contradictory, or irregular.
example_sentence: Her work is inconsistent; sometimes excellent, sometimes sloppy. The weather here is inconsistent, sunny one moment and rainy the next. His statements were inconsistent, making it hard to trust him. The team’s performance is inconsistent this season.

english_meaning: Not easily noticed or seen. Attracting little or no attention. Modest and unobtrusive in appearance or behaviour.
example_sentence: He sat in an inconspicuous corner of the café. The door was small and quite inconspicuous. She wore plain clothes to remain inconspicuous in the crowd. The camera was hidden in an inconspicuous position.

english_meaning: To crown or officially make someone king, queen, or ruler. To formally place a crown on a monarch's head as a sign of investiture, or to appoint someone to a high position of authority.
example_sentence: The ceremony was held to incoronate the new king. The council decided to incoronate her as the chief of the tribe. They planned a grand event to incoronate the elected leader. The queen was incoronated in the historic cathedral.

english_meaning: To include or combine something as part of a whole. To unite or blend parts into a single entity, to make something part of a larger system or structure, or to form a legally recognized company.
example_sentence: The new design incorporates feedback from users. The company was incorporated last year. The teacher incorporated games into the lesson. The plan incorporates several innovative ideas.

english_meaning: Impossible to correct, reform, or improve. Firmly rooted in bad habits or behavior that cannot be changed. Beyond correction or discipline. A person whose faults cannot be reformed.
example_sentence: He is an incorrigible liar who never tells the truth. Their son proved to be an incorrigible troublemaker. She is an incorrigible optimist despite all her hardships. The teacher finally gave up on the incorrigible student.

english_meaning: The quality of being impossible or extremely difficult to bribe or morally corrupt. Complete honesty, integrity, and resistance to improper influence. The condition of being unable to decay or perish. In religious contexts, preservation of a body from normal decomposition.
example_sentence: Her incorruptibility made her a trusted leader. The commission praised the investigator’s proven incorruptibility. Voters valued his incorruptibility more than his popularity. The tradition treats the body’s incorruptibility as a sacred sign.

english_meaning: Not capable of being bribed, morally corrupted, or persuaded to act dishonestly. Completely honest and guided by strong principles. Unable to decay, perish, or be physically corrupted. In religious usage, miraculously preserved from bodily decay.
example_sentence: The judge was respected as an incorruptible public servant. They needed an incorruptible officer to lead the investigation. The legend describes the saint’s body as incorruptible. Her incorruptible commitment to justice inspired the entire team.

english_meaning: To become greater in size, amount, number, strength, value, or intensity. To make something greater or more numerous. A rise or upward change in quantity, rate, degree, or level. The amount by which something becomes greater.
example_sentence: Food prices may increase during the winter. Regular exercise can increase your energy levels. The school reported an increase in enrollment. We received a five percent increase in salary.

english_meaning: Made or having become greater in size, amount, number, degree, strength, value, or intensity. More frequent, extensive, or severe than before. Raised above a previous level. Past tense and past participle of increase.
example_sentence: Increased demand has pushed prices higher. The clinic reported an increased number of patients this week. We increased the budget after reviewing the costs. Increased security helped visitors feel safer.

english_meaning: Extremely good, surprising, or hard to believe. Something that is so unusual, impressive, or surprising that it seems difficult to believe. It can refer to positive things like achievements or negative things like unbelievable excuses. Extremely impressive.
example_sentence: She did an incredible job on the project. The athlete showed incredible strength. It is incredible how fast technology is changing. His story sounded incredible but it was true. The hotel was incredible. The trip to Costa Rica was an incredible experience. The view from the mountain was incredible.

english_meaning: Extremely; to a very high degree. Used to emphasize that something is surprising, extraordinary, or to an extreme degree. It can describe how remarkable, difficult, impressive, or unusual something is.
example_sentence: The view from the mountain was incredibly beautiful. She worked incredibly hard to finish the project on time. It’s incredibly difficult to learn a new language in a short time. He was incredibly kind to everyone he met.

english_meaning: The state of being unable or unwilling to believe something. A feeling of disbelief, doubt or scepticism when faced with surprising or unlikely information. An expression of astonishment combined with refusal to accept what one hears or sees. Lack of belief or confidence in the truth of a statement.
example_sentence: She stared at him in complete incredulity when he confessed. His eyes widened with incredulity at the unexpected news. The audience listened to the claim with growing incredulity. There was a tone of incredulity in her voice as she repeated the question. He laughed in incredulity at the absurd suggestion.

english_meaning: An increase or addition, especially one of a series on a fixed scale. A small regular increase in salary or value. A tiny amount by which something changes. A step-by-step growth in a quantity. An added portion that raises a total.
example_sentence: He received a small increment in his monthly salary. The temperature rises in tiny increments each hour. Every yearly increment brought him closer to his goal. The software updates come in regular increments.

english_meaning: To make someone appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing. To provide evidence that implicates a person in illegal or unethical activity. To cause someone to seem responsible for something criminal.
example_sentence: The email records were used to incriminate the executive in the fraud investigation. She refused to answer the questions because she feared the answers might incriminate her. The witness was reluctant to give a statement that might incriminate his close friend. The fingerprints found at the scene were enough to incriminate the suspect beyond reasonable doubt. He was warned by his lawyer not to say anything that could be used to incriminate him in court.

english_meaning: To instill or teach an attitude, idea, or habit by persistent instruction. It involves impressing something upon the mind of another through frequent repetition. The goal is to ensure the message is deeply rooted in the person's character or lifestyle.
example_sentence: Parents try to inculcate good manners in their children from an early age. The coach worked hard to inculcate a sense of discipline in the players. Teachers aim to inculcate a love of reading in their students. It is important to inculcate the value of hard work in young minds.

english_meaning: Teaching an idea, habit, or value to someone by repeating it many times. Firmly fixing a belief or principle in a person's mind through steady instruction. Instilling good qualities such as honesty and discipline in children or students. Impressing something on the mind by persistent urging or example.
example_sentence: The school focuses on inculcating discipline in young students. Parents play a key role in inculcating good manners. He spent years inculcating a love of reading in his children. The training aims at inculcating a sense of responsibility.

english_meaning: The person currently holding an office or position. Necessary as a duty or responsibility
example_sentence: The president incumbent of White house. The incumbent president will run for re-election. It is incumbent on students to complete their assignments on time. The incumbent CEO has introduced major reforms. The incumbent must defend their seat in the upcoming election.

english_meaning: To become subject to something unpleasant as a result of one's own actions. To bring upon oneself a cost, loss, debt, or penalty. To experience or suffer a consequence, especially an unwanted one. To become liable for an expense or obligation.
example_sentence: The company incurred heavy losses last year. You will incur a penalty if the payment is late. He incurred his father's anger by lying. They incurred large debts while building the house.

english_meaning: Lack of curiosity or interest. The state of not wanting to learn about or investigate something. Indifference to new ideas, information, or experiences.
example_sentence: His incuriosity about the world around him meant he rarely learned anything new. The children's incuriosity about science worried their teacher, who tried to make lessons more engaging. Incuriosity in a researcher is a serious flaw that can limit the scope of any investigation. Her incuriosity about other cultures made it difficult for her to connect with colleagues from different backgrounds. The author argued that incuriosity is a form of intellectual laziness that must be actively overcome.

english_meaning: Lacking a normal or usual curiosity. Having no interest in knowing or discovering things.
example_sentence: She is remarkably incurious about the natural world.

english_meaning: In a way that shows no interest in knowing or discovering things. Lacking a normal or usual curiosity
example_sentence: He listened incuriously, as if it did not concern him. The students looked incuriously at the experiment, waiting for the teacher to finish. They nodded incuriously at the proposal, without asking any questions.

english_meaning: A sudden invasion or attack into another's territory. An act of entering a place, especially in a way that is unwanted or harmful. An unwelcome intrusion into a domain, situation, or area. It is often used for military advances, but also for any forceful entry where someone is not welcome.
example_sentence: The army repelled the enemy's incursion across the border. There were repeated incursions into the protected wildlife area. The incursion of foreign goods threatened the local industry. The general warned of further military incursions. The journalist criticized the incursion into people's private lives.

english_meaning: The middle bone of the three ossicles in the middle ear, shaped like an anvil. The bone that connects the malleus to the stapes. An anvil-shaped ossicle that transmits sound vibrations across the middle ear.
example_sentence: The incus lies between the malleus and the stapes. Its shape gives the incus the common name anvil. The incus passes vibrations deeper into the ear. Doctors examined the incus during the ear surgery.

english_meaning: In a way that is offensive to accepted standards of morality. In a manner that is improper, shameful, or obscene. Without regard for modesty or decency. In an unseemly or shockingly inappropriate way. Used to stress unseemly haste, as in 'indecently quick'.
example_sentence: He was fined for behaving indecently in a public place. The magazine was banned for indecently portraying young people. They moved into the house indecently soon after the funeral. She felt he had spoken indecently about a private matter.

english_meaning: Impossible to read or understand. So unclear that the meaning cannot be worked out. Describing handwriting or a code that cannot be made out. Not able to be translated or interpreted. Hopelessly confusing or unintelligible.
example_sentence: The doctor's handwriting was completely indecipherable. Rain had made the old inscription indecipherable. His indecipherable notes were of no use to anyone. The message was written in an indecipherable code.

english_meaning: The inability to make a choice or decision. A state of doubt in which a person keeps hesitating. Difficulty in choosing between two or more options. Delay caused by uncertainty of mind. Lack of firmness or resolve in deciding.
example_sentence: His indecision cost the company an important contract. After hours of indecision, she finally chose the blue dress. Indecision at the top created confusion among the staff. Fear of failure is often the real cause of indecision.

english_meaning: Not able to make decisions quickly and effectively. Not providing a clear and definite answer or result.
example_sentence: He is too indecisive to choose a career path. Her indecisive nature caused delays in the project. The indecisive voter waited until the last moment. Being indecisive can sometimes lead to missed opportunities.

english_meaning: In a hesitant way that shows no clear decision. Without firmness or confidence in choosing. In a manner that leaves a matter unsettled. So as to produce no definite result. With visible doubt and wavering.
example_sentence: He answered indecisively when asked about his plans. The committee voted indecisively and the matter was postponed. She stood indecisively at the door for several minutes. The battle ended indecisively with heavy losses on both sides.

english_meaning: Used to emphasise a statement or response. In truth or in fact. Used to introduce a point that strengthens what has already been said. Expressing agreement, emphasis, or an element of surprise.
example_sentence: The results of the experiment were indeed surprising and challenged existing theories. She is indeed one of the most talented musicians of her generation. He said he would come, and indeed he arrived even earlier than expected. The task was indeed difficult, but the team managed to complete it on time. Indeed, there is no easy solution to such a complex and long-standing problem.

english_meaning: Possessing or showing a tireless capacity for work or effort. Persisting tirelessly in an endeavor without yielding to fatigue.
example_sentence: She was an indefatigable defender of human rights. The rescue workers were indefatigable in their search for survivors. His indefatigable spirit inspired everyone around him. Annie's indefatigable efforts led to the project's success.

english_meaning: In a manner that shows a tireless capacity for work or effort. Acting persistently and without yielding to fatigue in an endeavor.
example_sentence: She worked indefatigably to ensure the event was a complete success. The lawyer argued indefatigably on behalf of his client. He campaigned indefatigably throughout the entire election season. They fought indefatigably against the unfair regulations.

english_meaning: It refers to something that is not able to be protected against a physical attack. It also describes a behavior, action, or argument that cannot be justified, excused, or supported.
example_sentence: The fort was left completely indefensible after the wall collapsed. His actions during the meeting were entirely indefensible. The lawyer struggled to argue such an indefensible position. They abandoned the town because its location was strategically indefensible.

english_meaning: Not polite or showing poor sensitivity. Behavior, words, or actions that lack politeness, tact, or respect for other people’s feelings, especially in sensitive situations.
example_sentence: It was indelicate to joke about his failure in front of others. She asked an indelicate question that made everyone uncomfortable. Discussing money at the dinner table can be considered indelicate. His indelicate remarks damaged his professional reputation.

english_meaning: Compensation for damage, loss, or injury suffered. Protection against financial loss by legal agreement. The act of making someone secure against responsibility or loss. Security or exemption from penalties or liabilities.
example_sentence: The contract included an indemnification clause to protect the supplier. The insurance company promised full indemnification for the damages. Indemnification agreements are common in construction projects. The victim received indemnification for his losses.

english_meaning: Compensated for loss, damage, or injury. Protected or secured against legal responsibility or financial loss. Made safe from penalties or liabilities by agreement.
example_sentence: The farmer was indemnified for the crops destroyed by the flood. The company indemnified its employees against legal claims. The insured party was indemnified within thirty days. He felt indemnified knowing the policy covered all losses.

english_meaning: To compensate someone for harm, loss, or damage. To provide financial protection against loss or liability. To secure someone against future legal or financial responsibility.
example_sentence: The insurance policy was designed to indemnify the business against any losses caused by fire or theft. The government agreed to indemnify victims of the industrial accident with a compensation fund. The contract included a clause to indemnify the contractor against any claims arising from the project. She was indemnified by the company after suffering an injury on the premises during working hours. Lawyers often advise businesses to include provisions to indemnify themselves against unexpected legal claims.

english_meaning: A person or party who receives compensation or protection against loss or damage. The one who is indemnified under a contract or agreement. A party legally entitled to be compensated for losses.
example_sentence: The indemnitee submitted a claim for the property damage. Under the agreement, the tenant was the indemnitee. The indemnitee was fully compensated for the fire losses. Both parties reviewed the rights of the indemnitee.

english_meaning: A person or party who agrees to compensate another for loss or damage. The one who provides indemnity or guarantees protection against loss. A party legally bound to make good any loss suffered by another.
example_sentence: The indemnitor agreed to cover all legal costs arising from the dispute. As the indemnitor, the company paid for the damages. The contract clearly defined the duties of the indemnitor. The insurance firm acted as the indemnitor in the agreement.

english_meaning: To start a line of print or block of text further away from the edge of the page than the other lines. To make a space at the edge or on the surface of something. To make an official request for goods. An official order for goods or equipment. A space at the edge or on the surface of something,
example_sentence: Please indent the first line of each paragraph. We indented for the engine spares last month. The teacher asked students to indent their essays properly. The company decided to indent new equipment from abroad. There is a small indent on the edge of the metal sheet.

english_meaning: A space left at the beginning of a line or paragraph. The act or result of setting text inward from the left margin. It is commonly used in writing, printing, coding, and official documents to show the start of a new paragraph, structure information, or improve readability.
example_sentence: The teacher asked students to use proper indentation in their essays. Indentation helps readers understand where a new paragraph begins. In computer programming, indentation shows the structure of the code. The document looked messy because indentation was missing.

english_meaning: To bind someone by a formal legal contract, usually for a fixed period. A formal legal agreement, especially one that binds a person to work for a fixed period or records property or financial obligations. A written legal contract that sets out duties, rights, or obligations between parties.
example_sentence: The company agreed to indenture the apprentice for three years. Young workers were indentured under strict conditions. He signed an indenture that required him to work for five years. The indenture clearly stated the terms of employment and payment. Many laborers arrived under indenture during the colonial period. The bond indenture protected the rights of investors.

english_meaning: Free from outside control or influence. Not depending on another for livelihood or opinions. Self-governing or self-sufficient. Not connected with others of the same kind. A person who acts or thinks freely.
example_sentence: She is a strong and independent woman. Pakistan became independent in 1947. He runs an independent business. Independent thinkers challenge old ideas.

english_meaning: An alphabetical list of names or topics at the end of a book with page numbers. A number or figure showing the level or change of something such as prices. A sign or indicator of a particular condition or trend. To arrange information in a systematic list. To link a value such as wages to a measure such as inflation.
example_sentence: Look up the topic in the index at the back of the book. The share index fell sharply after the announcement. Rising crime is often taken as an index of social decay. The library has indexed all its new manuscripts.

english_meaning: The finger next to the thumb, used for pointing. The first finger of the hand. The forefinger, commonly used to indicate direction or press buttons. In anatomy, the second digit of the human hand.
synonyms: ["Forefinger","First finger","Pointer","Digit","Pointing finger","Second digit","Trigger finger","Finger","Forefinger digit","Hand digit"]
example_sentence: She pointed at the map with her index finger. He tapped the screen gently with his index finger. The doctor asked him to touch his nose with his index finger. A cut on his index finger made typing painful.

english_meaning: The practice of linking wages, pensions, or prices to a price index such as inflation. Automatic adjustment of payments in line with the cost of living. The process of compiling or arranging an index. In economics, a mechanism that protects the real value of money over time.
example_sentence: The union demanded full indexation of salaries to inflation. Indexation of pensions protects retired people from rising prices. The government suspended indexation during the financial crisis. Indexation of the documents took the archivists several months.

english_meaning: To show, point out, or make something clear. To be a sign that something exists or is likely to be true. To state or express something briefly or indirectly. To signal the direction in which a vehicle is about to turn. To show a reading or value on a measuring device.
example_sentence: Please indicate your choice on the form. The results indicate a steady improvement in performance. He indicated the door and asked us to leave. Always indicate before changing lanes.

english_meaning: A sign, remark, or piece of evidence that shows what is happening or likely to happen. Something that points to a particular fact or conclusion. A reading given by a measuring instrument. In medicine, a symptom or condition that suggests a particular treatment is needed.
example_sentence: There is every indication that the weather will improve. He gave no indication of his real intentions. The gauge gave a clear indication of rising pressure. Fever may be an indication of infection.

english_meaning: Showing or suggesting that something is true or likely. Serving as a sign or evidence of a particular situation. In grammar, the mood of a verb used to state facts or ask questions. A verb form belonging to that grammatical mood.
example_sentence: These symptoms are indicative of a serious illness. His silence was indicative of deep disappointment. The prices quoted are indicative and may change. In this sentence the verb is in the indicative mood.

english_meaning: A sign or piece of information that shows what a situation is like. A measurement used to judge the condition or progress of something. A device such as a dial, light, or pointer that gives information. The flashing light on a vehicle used to show which way it will turn. In chemistry, a substance that changes colour to show acidity or alkalinity.
example_sentence: Literacy is an important indicator of social progress. The fuel indicator showed that the tank was almost empty. He forgot to use his indicator before turning left. The chemist added an indicator to test the solution.

english_meaning: The plural form of index, meaning lists of names or topics with page numbers. In mathematics, the small numbers written above and to the right showing powers. Figures used to show changes in prices, values, or performance over time. Signs or measures that point to a particular condition or trend.
example_sentence: The teacher explained the laws of indices in algebra. Both volumes contain detailed indices at the end. Stock market indices fell sharply last week. Economic indices suggest a slow recovery this year.

english_meaning: To formally accuse someone of a serious crime. To officially charge a person with a crime through a legal process, usually by a grand jury or court. It can also mean to show that someone or something is responsible for a fault or wrongdoing.
example_sentence: The court decided to indict the businessman for fraud. The report seemed to indict the entire system for corruption. A grand jury may indict a suspect after reviewing evidence. The evidence could indict him in the robbery case. His own words may indict him during the trial. The documentary indicts the healthcare system for inequality.

english_meaning: Capable of being charged with a serious crime in a court of law. An offense or behavior that is serious enough to warrant a formal legal charge or trial. It is used in legal contexts to indicate crimes that require an indictment by a grand jury or formal legal proceeding.
example_sentence: Theft over a certain amount is an indictable offense. The suspect was involved in an indictable crime and faced trial. Murder is always considered an indictable act. Fraud involving large sums of money is indictable.

english_meaning: Historically, a cycle of 15 years used in the Roman and Byzantine empires to calculate taxes or dates. An official proclamation or formal announcement, often by a government or authority. A declaration or act of indicating something, such as warning or signaling.
example_sentence: The indiction of the new tax laws was announced yesterday. Ancient manuscripts often include the indiction year to indicate when they were written. His speech served as an indiction of upcoming changes in policy. The emperor’s indiction was recorded in the official chronicle.

english_meaning: A formal charge or accusation of a serious crime. An official statement by a legal authority, usually a grand jury, that a person has committed a crime. It is used in serious criminal cases and starts the formal trial process. It can also mean strong criticism of something, especially a system or situation.
example_sentence: The court issued an indictment against the businessman for fraud. Her speech was a powerful indictment of corruption in the system. The indictment included several serious charges. He denied all claims mentioned in the indictment.

english_meaning: A lack of interest, concern, or sympathy. An attitude of not caring about someone or something. Emotional coldness towards a situation or person. The state of being neither for nor against something. Neglect or inattention shown to important matters.
example_sentence: His indifference to her feelings hurt her deeply. Public indifference allowed the problem to grow worse. She responded with cold indifference to the news. The government showed indifference toward the flood victims.

english_meaning: Showing no interest, concern, or sympathy. Not caring one way or the other. Of average or mediocre quality. Emotionally detached or cold in attitude. Neither good nor bad, ordinary in nature.
example_sentence: He was indifferent to the criticism of others. The audience remained indifferent throughout the show. The food at the restaurant was rather indifferent. She seemed indifferent to her final results.

english_meaning: A native or indigenous person of a particular place. An original inhabitant of a region. One who is born of or belongs to a specific land.
example_sentence: The rights of the indigen to their ancestral lands were recognised in the new legislation. Many activists work to protect the culture and traditions of the indigen communities. Organisations working with the indigen have called for greater representation in government. The indigen of the region have maintained their language and customs for thousands of years.

english_meaning: A person who is indigenous to or native to a particular place. An original inhabitant of a region before the arrival of settlers or colonisers. A member of a group that has lived in a place since before recorded history.
example_sentence: The rights of the indigene to their ancestral land were finally recognised in the new legislation. Every indigene of the island had a deep connection to its landscape and history. The anthropologist spent years studying the culture and language of the local indigene. The indigene community gathered to protest the construction of the dam on their sacred river. The documentary gave the indigene a platform to tell their own story in their own words.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being indigenous to a particular place or culture. The status of belonging to a native people of a land, particularly in relation to colonial history. The set of rights, characteristics, and identities associated with being an original inhabitant.
example_sentence: The concept of indigeneity is central to the legal framework of many international human rights documents. Scholars continue to debate how indigeneity should be defined in the context of global migration. The campaign focused on celebrating indigeneity and preserving the traditional knowledge of the community. Questions of indigeneity often arise in discussions of land rights and cultural preservation. Her research explored how indigeneity shapes identity in post-colonial societies.

english_meaning: Native to a particular place; originating naturally in a specific region. People, plants, animals, languages, or cultures that originated naturally in a particular region and have existed there for a long time before outside influences or settlers arrived. It can also describe something that is naturally found in a place rather than introduced from elsewhere.
example_sentence: Many indigenous communities have preserved their traditions for centuries. The park is home to several indigenous plants and animals. Scientists are studying indigenous crops that grow well in dry climates. The museum highlights the art and history of indigenous people.

english_meaning: In a manner that is native or originating naturally in a particular region. By people or practices that are original to a specific place or culture. In a way that reflects indigenous origins.
example_sentence: The crop was grown indigenously before commercial farming methods were introduced to the region. The craft is produced indigenously by artisans using traditional tools and methods. The community governed itself indigenously long before the arrival of colonial authorities. The language developed indigenously and has no known connection to any neighbouring tongue. The medicinal plant is prepared indigenously using recipes passed down through generations.

english_meaning: Poor and needy; lacking sufficient means of support. Extremely poor to the point of requiring assistance. Destitute of the necessities of life.
example_sentence: The charity was set up specifically to provide legal assistance to indigent people who could not afford a lawyer. The indigent families in the area relied on the food bank for their daily meals. She worked for a non-profit organisation that provided healthcare to the indigent. The government established a fund to support indigent students who could not pay their tuition fees. The shelter offered temporary housing to the most indigent members of the community.

english_meaning: Anger or annoyance provoked by what is perceived as unfair treatment. It is a feeling of righteous frustration when one encounters injustice, disrespect, or wrongful accusation. It represents an offended sense of dignity or justice.
example_sentence: Her sheer indignance at being rudely ignored was entirely visible on her flushed face. The massive crowd expressed growing indignance over the new, incredibly unfair tax laws. He wrote intensely about his fierce indignance regarding global human rights violations. The customer stormed out of the bright store in a huff of pure indignance. An undeniable feeling of deep indignance fueled their passionate and vocal protests.

english_meaning: Feeling angry or upset because something is unfair or wrong. Feeling strong displeasure or resentment at something perceived as unjust, insulting, or offensive. It is an emotional response to perceived unfair treatment or wrongdoing.
example_sentence: She was indignant when accused of lying. He gave an indignant reply to the unfair criticism. The citizens were indignant at the government's negligence. I felt indignant when someone took credit for my work.

english_meaning: In a way that shows anger or annoyance at something unfair or insulting. With a feeling of offended pride or righteous anger. Reacting as if one has been treated unjustly.
example_sentence: "I would never lie!" she replied indignantly. He indignantly denied the accusation of cheating. The workers protested indignantly against the unfair decision. She indignantly refused to apologize for something she had not done.

english_meaning: Strong anger or annoyance caused by something considered unjust, unfair, or unworthy. A feeling of righteous anger provoked by perceived injustice. An emotional response to something that is felt to be wrong or insulting.
example_sentence: She expressed her indignation at the unfair treatment she had received from the company. The public's indignation over the decision led to large protests in several cities. He struggled to control his indignation when he read the false accusations made against him. Her indignation was justified given the way the situation had been handled by those in authority.

english_meaning: A situation or treatment that makes a person feel ashamed, embarrassed, or without respect. An insulting or humiliating act that damages someone's dignity. The state of being treated without the respect one deserves.
example_sentence: He suffered the indignity of being searched in front of everyone. The prisoners were subjected to many indignities. She felt the indignity of having to beg for help. Losing his job was an indignity he never forgot.

english_meaning: A deep purplish-blue color. A natural dye obtained from certain plants, historically used to color cloth. The plant from which this blue dye is produced.
example_sentence: She dyed the fabric a rich shade of indigo. Indigo was once a valuable export from South Asia. The artist mixed indigo with violet to create the evening sky. Farmers in the region used to grow indigo as a cash crop.

english_meaning: Not going in a straight line or by the shortest route. Not caused directly by something; happening as a secondary result. Not saying something clearly or openly; roundabout in speech.
example_sentence: We took an indirect route through the countryside to avoid the traffic. The new policy had an indirect effect on food prices. She gave an indirect answer that left everyone guessing. Indirect lighting creates a softer atmosphere in the room.

english_meaning: In a way that is not direct or straightforward. Through an intermediate person, action, or cause. In a roundabout or implied manner rather than openly.
synonyms: ["Secondhand","By implication","Obliquely","In a roundabout way","Circuitously","Through an intermediary"]
example_sentence: The new tax will indirectly affect small businesses. He indirectly suggested that I should resign. The news reached her indirectly through a mutual friend. Smoking indirectly harms the health of the people around you.

english_meaning: Done without careful judgment, selection, or distinction. Affecting or including everyone or everything without considering differences. Actions, behavior, or decisions made without careful choice, judgment, or discrimination. It refers to treating all people or things the same regardless of differences, quality, suitability, or consequences. The word is often used negatively to describe careless, random, excessive, or uncontrolled actions.
example_sentence: The police warned against the indiscriminate use of fireworks in crowded areas. Indiscriminate cutting of trees can seriously damage the environment. She avoids the indiscriminate sharing of personal information on social media. The disease spread because of the indiscriminate movement of infected animals.

english_meaning: Without making careful choices or distinctions. In a random, uncontrolled, or impartial manner. Doing something without selecting carefully, without considering differences, or without proper judgment. It often describes actions that affect everyone or everything equally, whether appropriate or not. Depending on the context, it may carry a negative meaning (carelessly or recklessly) or a neutral meaning (equally without favoritism).
example_sentence: The storm damaged houses indiscriminately across the entire village. He spent money indiscriminately without thinking about the future. The disease spread indiscriminately among people of all ages. Do not use pesticides indiscriminately because they can harm helpful insects.

english_meaning: Something that is absolutely necessary and cannot be done without. A person, thing, or quality that is so important that it is essential for success, functioning, or survival. If something is indispensable, it cannot be replaced or ignored because without it, the task or situation would fail.
example_sentence: Clean water is indispensable for human survival. The internet has become indispensable for modern education. Her experience made her indispensable to the team. Discipline is indispensable for long term success.

english_meaning: Something that is absolutely necessary and cannot be done without. A person, thing, or quality that is so important that it is essential for success, functioning, or survival. If something is indispensable, it cannot be replaced or ignored because without it, the task or situation would fail.
example_sentence: Clean water is Indispensible for human survival. The internet has become Indispensible for modern education. Her experience made her Indispensible to the team. Discipline is Indispensible for long term success.

english_meaning: Slightly ill or temporarily unable to do something, to make someone unwell or unavailable. It can refer to a minor sickness or a temporary incapacity.
example_sentence: He was indisposed yesterday. She was indisposed due to flu. I am indisposed and cannot attend. He was indisposed and stayed home.

english_meaning: Cannot be denied or questioned. Something that is clearly true, certain, or beyond doubt, leaving no room for argument or disagreement.
example_sentence: he evidence against the suspect was indisputable. Her talent for music is indisputable. It is indisputable that the Earth revolves around the Sun. His honesty is indisputable in all matters.

english_meaning: Not clear or easy to see, hear, or understand. Unclear or blurred in outline, sound, or meaning. Vague and difficult to distinguish from surrounding things.
example_sentence: The photograph was too indistinct to use as evidence in the court case. Her voice on the recording was indistinct and could not be clearly made out by the investigators. The outlines of the mountains were indistinct in the early morning mist. His instructions were so indistinct that no one was sure what he actually wanted them to do. The indistinct shape in the corner of the room turned out to be a pile of old luggage.

english_meaning: A single human being as distinct from a group or society. A person considered separately rather than as part of a collective. Relating to or meant for one person. Characteristic of a particular person; distinctive.
example_sentence: Every individual has the right to express their opinion freely and without fear. The programme was designed to meet the individual needs of each student in the class. She is a remarkable individual who has overcome many obstacles to reach where she is today. The rights of the individual must be balanced against the needs of the wider community. Each individual in the team was given a specific role to ensure the project ran smoothly.

english_meaning: The habit of being lazy or avoiding activity or work. A state of comfortable inactivity. Unwillingness to make an effort or exert oneself.
example_sentence: His indolence was evident in the way he spent most of the day lounging about without purpose. Indolence is one of the greatest barriers to achieving personal and professional goals. The teacher was frustrated by the indolence of students who refused to complete their assignments. She overcame her natural indolence and forced herself to exercise every morning. Years of indolence had left him unprepared for the demands of a full-time job.

english_meaning: Wanting to avoid activity or exertion; habitually lazy. It describes a person who lacks the motivation to work or make an effort. In medical terms, it can also refer to a condition that causes little or no pain and is slow to develop.
example_sentence: The indolent student failed to complete his homework assignments. On a hot summer afternoon, many people feel relaxed and indolent. His indolent nature prevented him from achieving his true potential. The doctor monitored the indolent tumor to ensure it didn't change.

english_meaning: Impossible to subdue or defeat. Showing great determination and strength of spirit. Unconquerable in nature, will, or courage. Used for people who never give up even in the face of difficulty.
example_sentence: She showed indomitable courage while fighting her illness. The soldiers had an indomitable spirit on the battlefield. His indomitable will helped him achieve his dreams. The team's indomitable performance won them the championship. Despite many failures, her indomitable determination never faded.

english_meaning: To persuade or influence somebody to do something To use a drug to make a pregnant woman start giving birth. To cause something to happen.
example_sentence: Nothing would induce me to take the job. To cause something, Pills for seasickness often induce drowsiness. The advertisement is meant to induce people to eat more fruit.

english_meaning: To allow yourself or someone to enjoy something, often more than is good or necessary. To give in to desires, especially in a way that may be excessive. To allow someone to have or do what they want. To take part in something enjoyable or satisfying. To satisfy a wish, feeling, or interest.
example_sentence: She decided to indulge in some chocolate after dinner. Parents should not always indulge their children’s demands. He likes to indulge in long conversations about history. On weekends, they indulge themselves by watching movies all day.

english_meaning: The state or act of having or doing whatever you want, the state of allowing somebody to have or do whatever they want.
example_sentence: There is no limit to the indulgence he shows to his grandchildren.

english_meaning: Willing to allow someone to have or do what they want, often too much. Very kind and lenient, especially towards children. Showing tolerance and generosity in judgment. Fond of pleasure and comfort for oneself.
example_sentence: His indulgent grandparents buy him whatever he wants. She gave her son an indulgent smile. The teacher was too indulgent with late homework. They spent an indulgent weekend at a luxury hotel.

english_meaning: To intoxicate someone with alcohol or another substance, causing drunkenness. A  person who regularly consumes alcohol to the point of being drunk.
example_sentence: The bartender refused to inebriate the underage customers. Excessive wine can inebriate even a seasoned drinker. He became an inebriate after years of heavy drinking. Society often stigmatizes inebriates instead of helping them.

english_meaning: Drunk or intoxicated; affected by alcohol or other substances. Experiencing the effects of alcohol or drugs to the point of impaired judgment, coordination, or consciousness. Often used formally or humorously to describe someone as tipsy or drunk.
example_sentence: After the party, he was so inebriated that he could barely walk. The captain refused to let an inebriated sailor operate the machinery. She laughed loudly, clearly inebriated from the celebration. I felt inebriated after just one glass of the strong wine.

english_meaning: The state of being drunk or intoxicated. To the condition of being affected by alcohol or other intoxicating substances, resulting in impaired physical and mental control, altered judgment, and sometimes euphoria.
example_sentence: His inebriation was obvious after the party. She was arrested for public inebriation. The smell of alcohol signaled his inebriation. Inebriation can impair decision-making and coordination.

english_meaning: The state of being drunk or intoxicated, usually because of alcohol. Habitual or excessive intoxication, especially due to alcohol consumption. It can describe a temporary condition of drunkenness or a more persistent pattern of alcohol abuse. The word is often used in formal, legal, or medical contexts rather than everyday conversation.
example_sentence: His repeated arrests were linked to public inebriety. The report discussed alcohol abuse and chronic inebriety among adults. Inebriety affected his judgment and decision making. The law penalizes disorderly behavior caused by inebriety.

english_meaning: Too great, beautiful, or extreme to be expressed in words. Indescribable in nature or feeling. Beyond ordinary description or explanation. Not to be spoken because of its sacred nature.
example_sentence: She felt an ineffable joy at the birth of her child. The beauty of the sunset was simply ineffable. He stood in ineffable awe before the mountain. There was an ineffable sadness in his eyes.

english_meaning: Impossible to erase, remove or rub out. Leaving a permanent mark or impression. Unable to be forgotten or wiped from memory. Lasting and indelible in effect.
example_sentence: The war left an ineffaceable mark on the city. Her kindness made an ineffaceable impression on me. Those memories are ineffaceable after so many years. The ink left an ineffaceable stain on the cloth.

english_meaning: Not producing the desired result; not successful or not working well. A person, action, method, plan, medicine, rule, or system that fails to achieve its intended purpose or desired outcome. It refers to something that does not work efficiently or successfully.
example_sentence: The medicine proved ineffective against the infection. Their efforts to reduce pollution were largely ineffective. The old security system was ineffective in preventing theft. Repeating the same strategy was ineffective because the market had changed.

english_meaning: Not producing the desired result or effect. Lacking the ability or power to achieve something. Weak and unable to bring about change or success.
example_sentence: The manager's ineffectual leadership led to a sharp drop in the team's performance. All their efforts to contain the fire proved ineffectual against such strong winds. He was an ineffectual speaker who struggled to hold the attention of his audience. The policy was widely regarded as ineffectual because it failed to address the root causes of the problem. Despite trying several times, her attempts to resolve the conflict were completely ineffectual.

english_meaning: Not able to be stretched or changed in shape easily. Describing a material or substance that does not return to its original shape after being deformed. In economics, describing demand or supply that does not change significantly when price changes.
example_sentence: The old elastic band had become inelastic and snapped as soon as it was stretched. Demand for essential medicines is typically inelastic because people need them regardless of the price. Inelastic materials are often preferred in construction where rigidity is important. The economist noted that the demand for fuel remained inelastic even when prices rose sharply. Unlike rubber, this synthetic material is inelastic and will not recover its original form once stretched.

english_meaning: Unable to be resisted, avoided or struggled against. Certain to occur no matter what efforts are made. Inevitable in a solemn or literary sense. Following necessarily as a consequence.
example_sentence: Ageing is an ineluctable fact of nature. He accepted the ineluctable outcome of the trial. The story moves towards its ineluctable ending. Poverty made his departure ineluctable.

english_meaning: Lacking skill, ability, or competence. Someone or something that is not capable, unskilled, clumsy, or inappropriate in action or behavior. It refers to incompetence or inability to do a task properly.
example_sentence: He was completely inept at handling customer complaints. Her attempts at cooking were inept and often ruined the meal. The politician’s speech revealed his inept understanding of economic issues. Despite his enthusiasm, he was inept at fixing the car.

english_meaning: Lack of skill, ability, or competence. The state of being clumsy, awkward, or unsuitable for a task. Inefficiency or incapability in performing duties properly. A foolish or inappropriate quality in actions, behaviour, or remarks. Often used to criticise poor performance or bad judgement.
example_sentence: The manager was dismissed because of his ineptitude in handling the project. His ineptitude as a driver caused several accidents. The team lost the match due to the ineptitude of its captain. Her ineptitude in dealing with customers cost the company dearly. The report exposed the ineptitude of the administration.

english_meaning: Lacking the ability or strength to move. Chemically inactive and not readily reacting with other substances. Deficient in active properties or completely unreactive. Having no inherent power of action, motion, or resistance.
example_sentence: Neon is an inert gas that does not easily react with other elements. The injured animal lay completely inert on the side of the road. The medicine contained inert ingredients used only as fillers. The inert leadership of the committee led to zero progress on the project.

english_meaning: The tendency of a physical object to remain still or continue moving unless acted upon by a force. A feeling of laziness or a lack of energy and desire to move. The resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity. A state of stagnation or inability to change a current situation.
example_sentence: The spacecraft continued to drift through the void due to inertia. Bureaucratic inertia prevented the new policy from being implemented quickly. It was hard to overcome my morning inertia and get out of bed. The physics teacher demonstrated inertia by pulling a tablecloth out from under the dishes.

english_meaning: Relating to or arising from the physical property of inertia. Characterized by a lack of movement or a resistance to change. Pertaining to a frame of reference in which a body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity. Exhibiting a tendency to maintain the current state of motion.
example_sentence: The satellite relies on an inertial guidance system to navigate through space. We need an inertial frame of reference to apply Newton's first law correctly. The company's inertial response to the market changes caused it to lose customers. The engineer measured the inertial mass of the new vehicle component.

english_meaning: Impossible to avoid or escape from. Certain to happen whatever one does. Logically unavoidable as a conclusion. Binding and impossible to get away from.
example_sentence: The conclusion is inescapable: we must cut costs. Death is an inescapable part of life. He felt trapped by inescapable family duties. The evidence led to one inescapable answer.

english_meaning: That you cannot avoid or prevent. Certain to happen and unable to be avoided or prevented
example_sentence: A rise in interest seems inevitable. It is inevitable consequence of the decision. It was inevitable that there would be job losses. There was an inevitability about their defeat.

english_meaning: Existing in such large quantity that it can never be used up. Never becoming tired or weakened. Seemingly endless in energy or supply.
example_sentence: Sunlight is an almost inexhaustible source of energy. She has an inexhaustible patience with children. The library holds an inexhaustible supply of stories. His inexhaustible enthusiasm kept the team going.

english_meaning: The quality of being impossible to stop, prevent or alter. Relentlessness of a process or force.
example_sentence: The inexorability of ageing is a common theme in poetry. Economists wrote about the inexorability of the decline. He accepted the inexorability of the court's decision. There is a quiet inexorability to the changing seasons.

english_meaning: Impossible to stop, prevent or change. Continuing relentlessly towards an outcome. Unyielding to persuasion, pleas or requests.
example_sentence: The inexorable rise of costs forced the shop to close. Time's inexorable passage spares no one. He faced the inexorable logic of the evidence. Their advance was slow but inexorable.

english_meaning: In a way that cannot be stopped or changed. Relentlessly and inevitably. Without yielding to persuasion.
example_sentence: The river moved inexorably towards the sea. Costs rose inexorably through the year. He was drawn inexorably into the dispute. The talks led inexorably to a split.

english_meaning: Not advisable or suitable in the circumstances. Likely to cause difficulty or disadvantage if done. Unwise from a practical point of view.
example_sentence: It would be inexpedient to raise the issue before the election. The board found the merger inexpedient at that stage. He considered silence inexpedient but safe. Delaying payment proved inexpedient for the company.

english_meaning: Something that cannot be explained or understood. A situation, action, or feeling that is mysterious, puzzling, or impossible to give a clear reason for. It often conveys surprise or confusion about the lack of explanation.
example_sentence: Her sudden disappearance was completely inexplicable. He felt an inexplicable sense of sadness that he couldn’t describe. The machine stopped working for an inexplicable reason. There was an inexplicable tension in the room despite everyone being friendly.

english_meaning: Not clearly stated or explained; vague or not explicit. Something that is not clearly expressed, not fully explained, or left unclear. It can refer to speech, writing, instructions, or ideas that are confusing or indirect.
example_sentence: His instructions were inexplicit, so we could not complete the task correctly. The contract was inexplicit about the payment terms. She gave an inexplicit answer that confused everyone. The teacher’s explanation was inexplicit and needed further clarification.

english_meaning: Something that never makes mistakes and is always correct. Describes a person, method, belief, or system that is completely reliable and incapable of being wrong. It suggests absolute accuracy and certainty, often used in serious, religious, scientific, or formal contexts.
example_sentence: No human being is infallible, even the most experienced leader. The test is not infallible and may give incorrect results. He speaks with confidence but that does not make him infallible. Many people once believed the system was infallible.

english_meaning: A very young child or baby. A child who is in the earliest stage of life, usually from birth up to around one year old. It refers to a baby who is still completely dependent on others for care, feeding, and protection.
example_sentence: The infant was sleeping peacefully in the cradle. Hospitals provide special care for sick infants. The mother held her infant close during the flight. Infant nutrition is very important for healthy growth.

english_meaning: The crime or practice of killing an infant or very young child. The killing of a newborn baby, especially soon after birth. A person who kills an infant. The custom, found in some societies, of killing unwanted newborn children. In zoology, the killing of young offspring by an adult animal of the same species.
example_sentence: The tribe was accused of practising infanticide during times of famine. Infanticide is treated as a serious criminal offence in most countries. Historians have studied infanticide in ancient societies. Researchers observed infanticide among lions in the reserve.

english_meaning: Relating to infants or early childhood. Behaving in a childish or immature way. Silly and lacking maturity, especially in an adult. Characteristic of a very young child.
example_sentence: His infantile behavior at the meeting annoyed everyone. The doctor specializes in infantile diseases. Stop making infantile excuses and act your age. Infantile care requires great patience and attention.

english_meaning: To enter a body or organism and cause disease. To contaminate something with harmful microorganisms or computer code. To spread a feeling, attitude, or influence to others. To corrupt or adversely affect.
example_sentence: The virus can infect people of any age. Dirty water may infect an open wound. Malware infected several office computers. Her enthusiasm began to infect the whole team.

english_meaning: The invasion and multiplication of harmful microorganisms in the body. A disease or illness caused by such organisms. The process or state of being infected. The harmful spread of corrupting ideas, feelings, or computer code.
example_sentence: The doctor treated the ear infection. Clean the cut to prevent infection. The virus caused a serious chest infection. Updated software reduced the risk of computer infection.

english_meaning: Capable of being transmitted from one person to another through infection. Relating to diseases caused by microorganisms like bacteria or viruses. Likely to spread quickly to others. Spreading enthusiasm or emotion easily to others.
example_sentence: COVID-19 is a highly infectious disease. The infectious laughter spread through the room. Wash your hands to prevent infectious illnesses. Her enthusiasm is infectious and motivates everyone.

english_meaning: Capable of causing or transmitting infection. Relating to infection or an infectious agent. An infective organism, stage, or agent.
example_sentence: The infective agent was identified as a bacterium. Patients remain infective for several days. Scientists measured the virus’s infective dose. The parasite enters its infective stage inside the host.

english_meaning: To reach a conclusion or understand something based on evidence, facts, reasoning, or clues rather than direct statements. To form an opinion, conclusion, or understanding from available evidence instead of being told directly. It involves logical thinking and reasoning. People infer information from facts, behavior, expressions, tone of voice, written text, or circumstances.
example_sentence: From her smile, I inferred that she was happy with the results. The detective inferred that the thief had entered through the back door. We can infer from the report that sales have increased this year. Although he said very little, I inferred that he disagreed with the decision.

english_meaning: A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning. A logical deduction drawn from facts or premises. The act or process of deriving logical conclusions from known or assumed facts. Something that is inferred rather than directly stated. An opinion or judgment formed by considering available information.
example_sentence: The detective drew an inference from the fingerprints found at the scene. Her silence led me to the inference that she was upset. Scientists make inferences based on experimental data. The inference from the report is that sales are declining. His inference proved to be correct.

english_meaning: Lower in rank, quality, or status than another. Of lesser value or importance. Below average in quality or performance. A person who is lower in rank or status than another.
example_sentence: The cheaper product was clearly inferior in quality to the more expensive version. He refused to accept a position that he felt was inferior to his qualifications and experience. The general regarded the new recruits as inferior to the veterans of the previous campaign. Inferior workmanship was the main reason why the building required such extensive repairs. She never allowed anyone to make her feel inferior because of her background.

english_meaning: The large vein that carries oxygen-poor blood from the lower body into the right atrium. The biggest vein in the human body. The main vein draining the abdomen, pelvis, and legs.
example_sentence: The inferior vena cava returns blood from the legs. It is the largest vein in the human body. Blood from the inferior vena cava enters the right atrium. The surgeon carefully avoided the inferior vena cava.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being lower in rank, status, or importance than someone or something else. The condition of being of poorer quality or value. A feeling that one is less capable or less worthy than others.
example_sentence: He could not hide his sense of inferiority in the meeting. The inferiority of the material was obvious to everyone. She struggled with feelings of inferiority at her new school. The report highlighted the inferiority of the older equipment.

english_meaning: A persistent feeling of being less important, capable, or worthy than other people. A psychological condition in which a person constantly doubts their own abilities and value. A deep sense of inadequacy that often causes shyness or, sometimes, aggressive behaviour.
example_sentence: His inferiority complex stopped him from speaking in public. Constant criticism can give a child an inferiority complex. She overcame her inferiority complex through counselling. People with an inferiority complex often avoid social gatherings.

english_meaning: Relating to hell or the underworld. Extremely unpleasant, annoying, or irritating. Devilish, wicked, or hellish in nature or appearance.
example_sentence: The old machine made an infernal noise all night. Ancient poets described the infernal regions in detail. He complained about the infernal heat of the afternoon. There was an infernal glow above the burning building.

english_meaning: In a hellish or devilish manner. Extremely or annoyingly, used to emphasise something unpleasant. In a way that suggests hell or torment.
example_sentence: The room was infernally hot during the summer. He was infernally slow in answering the letters. The traffic noise is infernally loud at this hour. She found the whole process infernally complicated.

english_meaning: A large and dangerous fire that is out of control. Hell, or a place resembling hell in its heat and suffering. Any situation of extreme heat, chaos, or torment.
example_sentence: Firefighters battled the inferno for several hours. The building was turned into a blazing inferno within minutes. The kitchen felt like an inferno in mid-July. Dante described the inferno in vivid detail.

english_meaning: Not able to produce offspring or young. Of land or soil, unable to support the growth of healthy crops or plants. Lacking in productivity, ideas, or creativity.
example_sentence: The couple discovered that they were infertile. Much of the land in that region is dry and infertile. Infertile soil cannot support a healthy crop. Years of overuse left the fields infertile.

english_meaning: The condition of being unable to have children or produce young. The state of soil or land being unable to produce good crops. A lack of productiveness or creative output.
example_sentence: The clinic offers modern treatment for infertility. Infertility can affect both men and women. Soil infertility is a serious problem for these farmers. They sought medical advice after years of infertility.

english_meaning: To spread in large numbers and cause damage or problems, usually referring to pests, insects, or unwanted things. To occupy or overrun an area in large numbers, especially harmful insects, parasites, or unwanted organisms. It can also be used metaphorically for problems or negative influences spreading widely.
example_sentence: The kitchen was infested with ants & cockroges. Rats infested the old warehouse and damaged the goods. Mosquitoes infest stagnant water during the rainy season. The ship was infested with cockroaches after weeks at sea. Fear and rumors can infest a community during a crisis.

english_meaning: The presence of large numbers of insects, animals, parasites, or other harmful organisms in a place or host. The state of being invaded or overrun by pests. A widespread and troublesome presence of something undesirable.
example_sentence: The restaurant closed after inspectors discovered a rat infestation. Regular cleaning can prevent an infestation of insects. The farmer treated the trees at the first sign of infestation. A severe weed infestation reduced the crop yield.

english_meaning: A person who does not believe in a particular religion, especially Islam or Christianity. A traditional term used to describe someone who does not believe in a particular religion or is seen as outside the faith. It is often used in historical, religious, or literary contexts. In modern usage, it can sound outdated or offensive depending on context.
example_sentence: In ancient texts, the term infidel was often used for people outside the religion. He was wrongly labeled an infidel by those who misunderstood his beliefs. The word infidel is considered offensive in many modern discussions. Historical writers frequently used infidel to describe foreign communities.

english_meaning: The act of being unfaithful to a spouse or romantic partner. A sexual or emotional relationship outside a committed partnership. Lack of loyalty, faithfulness, or adherence to a duty, belief, or promise. Disbelief in a religion, especially in older usage.
example_sentence: Their marriage ended after repeated infidelity. The counselor helped the couple discuss the pain caused by infidelity. The novel examines loyalty, temptation, and infidelity. In older texts, infidelity can mean a lack of religious belief.

english_meaning: The inner part of a sports field. In baseball, the area enclosed by the bases. The players who defend that area. Land situated away from a coast, boundary, or outer edge. In farming, a field near a farmhouse or settlement.
example_sentence: The ground crew covered the infield before the rain began. A hard ground ball rolled across the infield. The manager called the infield together for a brief talk. Cattle grazed in the sheltered infield near the farm.

english_meaning: To enter a place or group quietly and secretly. To move into an area, organization, or system gradually and often secretly, usually to gain information, influence, or control without being noticed.
example_sentence: The spy managed to infiltrate the enemy camp at night. Hackers tried to infiltrate the company network. The journalist infiltrated the group to expose the truth. Water began to infiltrate the walls after heavy rain.

english_meaning: A person who secretly enters a place or group to gather information or cause harm. Someone who deliberately and quietly gains access to an organization, area, or system without permission, often pretending to belong there, usually for spying, sabotage, or criminal purposes.
example_sentence: The army captured an infiltrator near the border late at night. The infiltrator pretended to be an employee to access confidential files. Security cameras revealed the movements of an infiltrator inside the building. The novel revolves around an infiltrator working within the enemy camp.

english_meaning: Lacking limits or bounds in time or space. Extending indefinitely without any end. Immeasurably great in extent, size, or degree. Being impossible to measure or calculate due to endlessness.
example_sentence: The universe is so vast that it appears to be completely infinite. She has infinite patience when it comes to teaching young children. There is an infinite variety of insect species in the rainforest. The possibilities for innovation in technology seem practically infinite.

english_meaning: Extremely small, to the point of being almost immeasurably tiny. Very minute in degree or amount. In mathematics, relating to a quantity approaching zero as a limit.
example_sentence: The infinitesimal differences between the two samples were only visible under a powerful microscope. Even an infinitesimal error in the calculations could have serious consequences for the mission. The scientist measured an infinitesimal trace of the compound in the water supply. The chances of finding the exact match were infinitesimal given the vast number of possibilities. Calculus deals with infinitesimal quantities to calculate rates of change and areas under curves.

english_meaning: The basic form of a verb, usually preceded by the word 'to'. A verb form that does not show tense, person, or number. The dictionary form of a verb used after certain other verbs or adjectives. Relating to or being this basic verb form.
example_sentence: In the sentence 'She wants to sing', the words 'to sing' form an infinitive. Some verbs are always followed by an infinitive. The teacher explained how to use the infinitive correctly. English learners often confuse the infinitive with the gerund.

english_meaning: To fix or fasten something firmly. To implant or instil something deeply in the mind. In linguistics, a word element inserted within the body of a word to alter its meaning or form.
example_sentence: The teacher tried to infix the value of honesty in her students from an early age. In some languages, infixes are added within a root word to change its grammatical function. The coach sought to infix a winning mentality into every member of the squad. He managed to infix the bolt deep into the wall so that it could not be pulled out easily. The linguist explained how the infix alters the meaning of the base word in Tagalog.

english_meaning: To provoke strong feelings of anger, excitement, or passion. To make a situation worse or more intense. To cause bodily inflammation or make an existing inflammation worse. To set on fire.
example_sentence: His comments served only to inflame the already tense situation between the two groups. The injury inflamed the tendon and caused her considerable pain for several weeks. The speaker's words inflamed the passions of the crowd and led to an outburst of protest. Spicy food can inflame the lining of the stomach in people who have acid reflux. She worried that publishing the article at that moment would inflame public anger even further.

english_meaning: A localised physical condition in which part of the body becomes reddened, swollen, hot, and often painful, especially as a reaction to injury or infection. The process by which the body's immune system responds to harmful stimuli. A state of intense public feeling or controversy.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed anti-inflammatory medication to reduce the swelling and inflammation in her knee. Chronic inflammation has been linked to a wide range of serious health conditions. Applying ice to the affected area can help reduce inflammation after a sports injury. The inflammation in his throat made it extremely difficult for him to swallow any food. Scientists are investigating the role of gut health in controlling inflammation throughout the body.

english_meaning: A humorous or informal expression meaning to do something pointless, absurd, or unnecessarily complicated. It can also mean to exaggerate or blow something out of proportion.
synonyms: ["Exaggerate","Blow out of proportion","Make a mountain of a molehill"]
example_sentence: Trying to fix that old machine is like inflating a cow. He inflated the cow by turning a minor issue into a major scandal. Stop inflating the cow and focus on real problems. She had a habit of inflating the cow in every team meeting.

english_meaning: A general rise in the prices of services and goods in a particular country, resulting in a fall in the value of money, the rate at which this happens
example_sentence: Wage increases must be in line with inflation.

english_meaning: To change the form of a word to express tense, number, gender, case, mood, or voice. It can also mean to change tone or pitch of the voice. In grammar, to modify a word so it shows different grammatical functions such as past tense, plural form, or comparison. To vary the pitch, tone, or modulation of the voice while speaking. To slightly change or influence something in direction or form.
example_sentence: In English, we inflect verbs to show past and present tense. She inflected her voice to express surprise. Latin verbs are heavily inflected for tense and person. `The teacher asked students to inflect the noun correctly in plural form.

english_meaning: Not able to bend or be bent easily; stiff. Unwilling to change opinions, decisions, or plans; stubborn. Not able to be changed or adapted to new circumstances. Strict and firm in rules or demands.
example_sentence: The inflexible metal rod would not bend under pressure. The manager was inflexible about the deadline. His inflexible attitude made negotiations difficult. The school's inflexible rules frustrated many parents.

english_meaning: To cause something unpleasant or painful to be suffered by someone. To impose something difficult or unwelcome on another person. To deal a blow, wound, or punishment.
example_sentence: The earthquake inflicted enormous suffering on the people of the affected region. He had no right to inflict his personal problems on everyone around him. The judge inflicted the maximum penalty allowed under the law for such a serious offence. War always inflicts terrible damage on civilian infrastructure and communities. The disease inflicted lasting damage on his hearing and required long-term treatment.

english_meaning: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behaviour of someone or something. A person or thing that has the power to affect others. To have an effect on or change the way someone thinks, behaves, or decides.
example_sentence: Her early teachers had a profound influence on the direction she chose for her career. The media has enormous influence over the opinions and attitudes of the general public. Growing up in a musical family influenced her decision to become a professional pianist. His influence in the organisation allowed him to push through important reforms. She refused to let peer pressure influence her choices and always stayed true to her values.

english_meaning: A contagious viral infection affecting the respiratory system. A flu illness characterized by fever, cough, body aches, and fatigue. An infectious disease that spreads easily from person to person. A seasonal illness that can be prevented by annual vaccination.
example_sentence: Influenza spreads rapidly during winter months. The influenza vaccine is recommended annually. She was sick with influenza for a week. Influenza can be serious for elderly people.

english_meaning: A visual representation of information or data designed to make complex information easy to understand. A collection of imagery, charts, and minimal text that provides an easy-to-understand overview of a topic. A graphic tool used by communicators to illustrate data patterns and trends visually. A medium for storytelling that combines design elements with factual data to engage an audience quickly. A digital or printed diagram that simplifies large amounts of data for educational or marketing purposes.
example_sentence: The marketing team created an infographic to summarize the annual sales report. This infographic simplifies the complex scientific process into five easy steps. Many news organizations use infographics to explain election results to the public. You can convey a lot of data quickly if you design a clear and engaging infographic.
