english_meaning: Able to learn, understand, and think about things quickly and well. Showing good judgement, sense, and clear reasoning. Describing a machine or device able to adjust its behaviour according to conditions. Well thought out and based on careful understanding of a subject.
example_sentence: He is an intelligent boy who reads a great deal. That was a very intelligent question to ask. Modern cars have intelligent braking systems. She gave an intelligent answer to a difficult problem.

english_meaning: Educated people in a society who are involved in intellectual, cultural, political, or artistic life. The class of writers, scholars, thinkers, critics, and professionals who shape public ideas.
example_sentence: The city's intelligentsia debated the new policy. Writers and professors formed part of the local intelligentsia. The novel criticizes the silence of the intelligentsia. Political movements often seek support from the intelligentsia. Members of the intelligentsia helped shape public opinion.

english_meaning: The quality of being understandable or clear. The degree to which speech, writing, sound, or meaning can be understood. Clarity of expression or communication.
example_sentence: The teacher improved the intelligibility of the lesson with examples. Background noise reduced the intelligibility of the recording. Clear pronunciation increases speech intelligibility. The report needs better structure for intelligibility. Font size affects the intelligibility of text on a screen.

english_meaning: Able to be understood. Clear in meaning, speech, writing, sound, or explanation. Comprehensible to the mind or senses.
example_sentence: His explanation was simple and intelligible. The recording was barely intelligible because of the noise. Scientific ideas should be made intelligible to ordinary readers. Her pronunciation is clear and intelligible. The map became intelligible after he explained the symbols.

english_meaning: In a clear and understandable way. So that words, ideas, speech, or writing can be understood easily.
example_sentence: Please speak slowly and intelligibly. She explained the rule intelligibly to the class. The witness answered clearly and intelligibly. Technical information should be presented intelligibly. He writes intelligibly even about difficult subjects.

english_meaning: A proper name associated with international satellite telecommunications. The name of a satellite communications organization and company. A term used for satellites, services, or systems connected with global communication by satellite.
example_sentence: Intelsat provides satellite communication services. The broadcaster used an Intelsat link for the live event. Engineers monitored the Intelsat satellite during the operation. Intelsat is often mentioned in discussions of global telecommunications. The remote station received data through an Intelsat system.

english_meaning: Lacking self-control, especially in eating, drinking or behaviour. Excessive, unrestrained or immoderate in action or speech. Showing a lack of moderation or balance. Characterised by harsh or extreme words and conduct.
example_sentence: His intemperate remarks during the debate offended many people. She regretted her intemperate behaviour at the party. An intemperate lifestyle damaged his health. The leader was criticised for his intemperate language. He gave an intemperate response to a polite question.

english_meaning: To have a plan, purpose, or aim. To mean or want to do something. To have a clear purpose or decision in your mind to do it, even if you haven’t done it yet.
example_sentence: I intend to finish my homework tonight. She intends to become a doctor. They didn’t intend to hurt your feelings. We intend to travel next summer.

english_meaning: Planned, meant, or designed for a particular purpose or person. Expected or meant to happen. A person whom one plans to marry, chiefly in informal usage. Deliberately signified or implied.
example_sentence: The medicine had the intended effect. This entrance is intended for staff only. Her intended arrived early for the ceremony. The remark carried an intended warning.

english_meaning: Existing in an extreme degree. Having or showing a characteristic in extreme degree. Exhibiting strong feeling or earnestness of purpose.
example_sentence: The president is under intense pressure to resign. He is very intense about every thing. She dislikes him intensely. She is prepared to carry out her threat to resign. She had an intent look on her face.

english_meaning: To make or become stronger, greater, or more extreme. To increase in degree, force, or effect. To make more concentrated or severe. To heighten emotions, efforts, or actions.
example_sentence: The storm continued to intensify throughout the night. The company decided to intensify its marketing efforts. His anger began to intensify as he listened. Doctors intensify treatment when symptoms worsen.

english_meaning: The quality of being very strong, extreme, or concentrated. The degree of strength or force of something. A feeling of extreme strength or concentration of effort, emotion, or activity.
example_sentence: The intensity of the storm caught many residents completely off guard and unprepared. She trained with great intensity to prepare for the marathon that was now just three weeks away. The intensity of his gaze made her feel both flattered and slightly uncomfortable. The film's emotional intensity left many members of the audience in tears by the end. The intensity of the competition increased significantly as the final rounds approached.

english_meaning: The thing that you plan to do or achieve. An aim or purpose. Showing strong interest & attention. Determined to do she, The state of mind with which an act is done.
example_sentence: His eyes were sudden intent. They were intent on murder. Are you intent upon destroying my reputation.

english_meaning: A plan, aim, or purpose that shows what someone wants to do or achieve. It refers to the state of mind directing one’s actions.
example_sentence: Her intention was to help the poor, not to gain fame. He went there with the intention of meeting his old friend. I had no intention of hurting your feelings. Good intentions are not enough without actions.

english_meaning: Done deliberately and with a clear purpose. Planned or meant rather than accidental. Relating to a conscious aim, decision, or design. In philosophy, directed toward or representing an object.
example_sentence: The change was intentional, not a mistake. She made an intentional effort to listen carefully. Intentional practice helped him improve quickly. The novel's repetition is an intentional stylistic choice.

english_meaning: Deliberately and with a particular aim or purpose. By conscious choice rather than by accident. In a planned, knowing, or willful manner.
example_sentence: She intentionally left the final page blank. He did not intentionally hurt anyone. The designer intentionally used simple colors. They intentionally delayed the announcement until Friday.

english_meaning: With close, fixed, and concentrated attention. In an earnest, determined, or purposeful manner. With one's eyes or mind focused strongly on something.
example_sentence: The child listened intently to the story. She stared intently at the map. The scientists worked intently throughout the night. He watched intently as the bird built its nest.

english_meaning: To communicate or work with someone or something. To act together, communicate, influence each other, or respond mutually in a situation
example_sentence: Students interact with teachers during class. Social media helps people interact easily. Children interact while playing games. The two chemicals interact with each other. Teachers encourage students to interact more. Apps allow users to interact in real time.

english_meaning: Communication or action between two or more people or things. The process where people, groups, or objects communicate, influence, or work with each other. It can be social, physical, verbal, or digital.
example_sentence: Interaction between students improves learning. There was little interaction during the online class. Social media increases human interaction. The interaction between teacher and students was friendly.

english_meaning: Involving active participation or communication between people, systems, or devices. Something that allows two way communication. The user does not just watch or read but also responds, clicks, types, or controls what happens. It is commonly used for software, apps, websites, learning tools, and presentations.
example_sentence: The app has an interactive learning module for students. The website is interactive and allows users to customize themes. The teacher used an interactive presentation in class. This game is highly interactive and keeps players engaged.

english_meaning: To take control of or prevent something (like a message, object, or person) from reaching its intended target. The event, instance, or object that is caught, blocked, or stopped. Often used in communication, sports, and military contexts.
example_sentence: The defender intercepted the pass and ran towards the goal. Police intercepted the smuggled goods at the border. She intercepted the letter before it reached him. The missile was intercepted mid-air by the defense system. His intercept of the football changed the game. The spy's intercept of the secret letter prevented a disaster. The missile intercept saved the city.

english_meaning: A person or thing that stops or catches something before it reaches its destination. A fast military aircraft designed to attack enemy planes or missiles in flight. A defensive player who catches a pass intended for the opposing side. A device used to trap or divert a flow of liquid, gas, or signals.
example_sentence: An interceptor was scrambled to meet the unidentified aircraft. The missile interceptor destroyed the incoming rocket. He acted as an interceptor of enemy radio messages. A grease interceptor is fitted below the kitchen sink.

english_meaning: To exchange one thing for another between two parties. A place where two or more roads or motorways connect. The act of exchanging ideas, words or goods. To put each of two things in the place of the other.
example_sentence: They interchange letters every month. Take the next interchange to join the motorway. The conference allowed a free interchange of ideas. You can interchange these two components safely.

english_meaning: Able to be exchanged or used in place of each other. Identical in function so that either one may be used. Describing words with the same meaning that can replace one another. Easily substituted without any loss of effect.
example_sentence: The two machine parts are completely interchangeable. These words are interchangeable in everyday speech. The tyres are interchangeable between both models. Players in this system have interchangeable roles.

english_meaning: Communication or dealings between people or groups. Sexual relations between individuals. The exchange of ideas, goods, or services between parties. Social interaction and communication.
example_sentence: The merchant's diary recorded his regular commercial intercourse with traders from distant lands. The philosopher argued that intellectual intercourse between cultures is essential for human progress. Social intercourse between the two communities had been severely limited by years of conflict. The course of normal social intercourse was disrupted by the outbreak of the epidemic. The ambassador sought to restore friendly intercourse between the two nations after years of diplomatic tension.

english_meaning: A non standard comparative form sometimes used in place of more interesting. An informal or humorous way of saying that something is more engaging than another thing. Considered incorrect in formal English, where more interesting is the accepted form. Occasionally used in playful speech or writing for effect.
example_sentence: Children sometimes say interestinger instead of more interesting. The teacher explained why interestinger is not correct English. He used interestinger in a joke and everyone laughed. In writing, always prefer more interesting to interestinger.

english_meaning: In a way that attracts attention or curiosity. Used to introduce a fact that the speaker finds notable or surprising. Engagingly, so as to hold the listener's or reader's attention. Remarkably, in a manner worth mentioning.
example_sentence: Interestingly, the oldest building in town is also the smallest. She writes interestingly about ordinary daily life. Interestingly enough, both experiments produced the same result. The guide spoke interestingly about the region's history.

english_meaning: A point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc., meet and interact. The means by which a user interacts with a computer or software. A device or program that enables a user to communicate with a computer. The shared boundary across which two separate components of a computer system exchange information. To connect with or interact with another person or entity.
example_sentence: The graphical user interface makes the software very easy to navigate. Scientists are exploring the interface between psychology and biology. We need to interface the new printer with the existing server. The project requires a seamless interface between different government departments.

english_meaning: Involving or relating to people of different religions or faiths. Activities, relationships, or dialogue between people or groups belonging to different religions. It emphasizes mutual respect, understanding, and cooperation among followers of various faiths. Interfaith efforts aim to promote peace, tolerance, and harmony in diverse societies.
example_sentence: The city organized an interfaith conference to promote peace. Interfaith dialogue encourages respect among communities. Many schools hold interfaith prayers to foster unity. She joined an interfaith group supporting social justice. The school’s interfaith program teaches students about respect for all religions.

english_meaning: To take part in or meddle in the affairs of others without being invited or welcome. To prevent something from working correctly. To obstruct or hinder a process or activity. To intervene in a situation without permission.
example_sentence: She asked him not to interfere with the decisions she had made about her own career. The electrical signal began to interfere with the navigation system, causing serious concern. He had a habit of interfering in arguments that had nothing to do with him. The new regulations were designed to prevent large corporations from interfering in local affairs. Foreign powers should not interfere in the internal political processes of sovereign nations.

english_meaning: To become involved in a situation or another person’s affairs without being asked. To intervene in a matter where one has no proper role or authority. To influence a process improperly.
example_sentence: I do not want to interfere in their family dispute. Foreign powers should not interfere in the election. She was accused of interfering in police work. His parents rarely interfere in his career choices.

english_meaning: To prevent, delay, or make an activity more difficult. To disturb the operation or progress of something. To touch, alter, or tamper with something without permission. To sexually molest someone, especially in legal or formal usage.
example_sentence: Loud music interfered with my concentration. This medicine may interfere with your sleep. Do not interfere with the evidence. The law protects children from anyone who tries to interfere with them.

english_meaning: The act of intervening in or meddling with something. Something that prevents a system or signal from functioning clearly. An obstruction or impediment to a process. Unwanted involvement in someone else's affairs.
example_sentence: The satellite signal was disrupted by interference from a nearby power station. She resented any interference in the way she chose to manage her own household. The radio broadcast was almost impossible to hear due to the interference from other stations. The referee penalised the player for interference with an opponent who was about to score. There were accusations of foreign interference in the election that were taken very seriously.

english_meaning: Getting involved in other people’s affairs without invitation or need. Tending to obstruct, disturb, or prevent a process. Producing unwanted interaction between signals, waves, or systems.
example_sentence: His interfering relatives kept offering unwanted advice. An interfering signal disrupted the broadcast. She disliked people interfering in her decisions. The judge stopped the lawyer from interfering with the witness.

english_meaning: A protein produced by body cells in response to viruses and other threats. Any of a group of signaling proteins that help regulate the immune system. A manufactured form of such a protein used to treat certain diseases.
example_sentence: Interferon helps the body respond to viral infections. The doctor discussed interferon therapy with the patient. Researchers measured interferon levels in the blood. Some medicines contain laboratory-produced interferon.

english_meaning: Existing, happening, or traveling between galaxies. Relating to more than one galaxy. Extremely vast or far-reaching in an imaginative or humorous sense.
example_sentence: The novel follows an intergalactic trading ship. Scientists study the possibility of intergalactic travel. An intergalactic war drives the film’s plot. The children imagined an intergalactic football tournament.

english_meaning: Existing or occurring between different generations. Involving interaction, cooperation, conflict, or exchange between age groups. Passed from one generation to another.
example_sentence: The project encourages intergenerational learning. They discussed intergenerational differences in the workplace. Poverty can become an intergenerational problem. The center hosts intergenerational activities for children and older adults.

english_meaning: Existing, conducted, or agreed between two or more governments. Relating to cooperation among national, regional, or local government bodies. Involving an organization whose members are governments.
example_sentence: The countries signed an intergovernmental agreement. An intergovernmental committee will monitor the project. Climate change requires strong intergovernmental cooperation. She works for an intergovernmental organization.

english_meaning: The intervening time or an internal arrangement made for a temporary period. It describes something intended to last for only a short time until a permanent replacement is found or a final decision is made. This can apply to government leaders, financial reports, or legal orders.
example_sentence: An interim government was established to oversee the transition to democracy. He was appointed as the interim CEO while the board searched for a permanent successor. The company released its interim financial results for the first six months of the year. They reached an interim agreement to stop the fighting until a treaty could be signed.

english_meaning: The inner part or inside of something. The inside of a building, vehicle, or container. The inland part of a country, away from the coast. Relating to the inside or central part. Concerned with internal affairs.
example_sentence: The interior of the car is very spacious and comfortable. They hired a designer to decorate the interior of their home. The team explored the interior regions of the country. The Ministry of Interior handles internal security. The interior walls were painted a soft cream colour.

english_meaning: To weave, cross, or entwine things together. To mix or blend closely and intricately. To layer or alternate elements in a complex pattern.
example_sentence: The craftsman interlaced strips of leather to create the strong and flexible belt. The branches of the two old trees had grown to interlace overhead, forming a natural arch. She interlaced her fingers nervously as she waited to hear the result of the examination. The documentary interlaced personal testimonies with archival footage to create a powerful narrative. Traditional basket weavers interlace natural fibres with great skill and precision.

english_meaning: To place something between layers. To put one material, object, or layer between other layers. It is often used in construction, textile work, printing, design, or technical processes where different materials are combined in layers.
example_sentence: The process involves interlaying very thin layers of silicon. Three slices of toasted bread were interlaid with pieces of chicken. The workers interlay insulation between the wooden panels. She interlaid soft cotton between the fabric layers. The artist interlays colored sheets to create texture. Engineers interlay protective material to strengthen the structure.

english_meaning: People who take part in a dialogue or conversation. Those who speak or engage in discussions during formal or informal exchanges. Participants in an interview, negotiation, or formal discussion.
example_sentence: The interlocutors in the peace talks agreed to suspend hostilities for a period of thirty days. She found it difficult to concentrate when her interlocutors kept interrupting each other. The two interlocutors in the documentary offered sharply contrasting views on the same event. Skilled diplomats know how to listen carefully to their interlocutors before formulating a response. The interlocutors in the focus group were from a wide range of professional and cultural backgrounds.

english_meaning: A person who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or do not belong. Someone who intrudes in the affairs of others. An unwanted presence who meddles in matters that do not concern them.
example_sentence: She felt like an interloper at the family gathering she had not been formally invited to attend. The interloper had managed to gain access to the restricted area without any authorisation. He was viewed as an interloper by the established members of the exclusive club. The new employee was treated as an interloper until she proved her worth to the team. The spy entered the organisation as an interloper, hiding his true identity for months.

english_meaning: To mix together or become mixed up with other people or things. To blend different elements together. To mingle freely and without distinction.
example_sentence: Guests from all over the world were invited to intermingle at the international reception. The two rivers intermingle before flowing together into the sea. Traditional and modern designs were allowed to intermingle throughout the new exhibition space. She was encouraged to intermingle with colleagues from other departments to broaden her network. The flavours of the spices begin to intermingle after the dish is left to rest for an hour.

english_meaning: A temporary pause or gap in an activity or process. The short interval between parts of a play, movie, or concert. An interruption or recess that allows for a break. A period of time during which something is stopped or put on hold. The act of suspending an event temporarily to provide rest or transition.
example_sentence: The audience rushed to the lobby for snacks during the fifteen-minute intermission. There was a brief intermission in the heavy rain before the storm resumed. The playwright decided to add an intermission after the second act to build suspense. The workers took a short intermission to rest before finishing the final phase of the project.

english_meaning: Occurring at irregular intervals or not continuous or steady. It describes something that starts and stops repeatedly over a period of time. This word is frequently used to describe weather patterns, mechanical faults, or communication signals.
example_sentence: The region experienced intermittent rain showers throughout the afternoon. We had to deal with an intermittent internet connection during the storm. Her sleep was intermittent due to the loud noise coming from the street. The car engine made an intermittent clicking sound that was hard to diagnose.

english_meaning: In a manner that occurs at irregular intervals rather than continuously. It refers to actions or events that happen from time to time with breaks in between. This focuses on the frequency and lack of continuity of an action.
example_sentence: The siren wailed intermittently throughout the night, waking the residents. He worked intermittently on his novel over a period of many years. The sun shone intermittently through the heavy clouds during the hike. Light flashed intermittently from the lighthouse across the dark sea.

english_meaning: To work as a trainee in an organization for practical training. A trainee working in a professional setting to gain experience. A person, usually a student or recent graduate, who temporarily works in an organization such as a company, hospital, or office to gain practical knowledge and job experience. Internships are often part-time or short-term and may be paid or unpaid.
example_sentence: She joined the hospital as a medical intern after graduation. The company hired five interns for the summer program. He worked as an intern at a software house to gain experience. Interns are often supervised by senior professionals.

english_meaning: Existing or occurring inside a person, place, or thing. Relating to the inner nature or workings of something. Within an organization, country, or system. Concerned with domestic rather than foreign matters. Not visible from the outside.
example_sentence: He suffered from internal injuries after the accident. The company conducted an internal investigation. Internal affairs are handled by another department. The clock has a complex internal mechanism.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the inside of something. Within an organization, country, or system. Concerning inner thoughts or feelings. Not visibly or outwardly. Handled inside a group rather than externally.
example_sentence: The medicine should not be taken internally. The matter will be handled internally. She was bleeding internally. Internally, he was furious but stayed calm.

english_meaning: Describes conflict within the same group. Internecine refers to violence, struggle, or conflict between members of the same group, family, organization, or nation, often causing serious damage to all sides involved.
example_sentence: The party collapsed due to internecine fighting among its leaders. Years of internecine conflict weakened the country’s economy. Internecine disputes within the family destroyed their unity. The company suffered because of internecine rivalry between departments.

english_meaning: A doctor who specializes in internal medicine. A physician trained to diagnose and treat adult diseases. A medical specialist for complex conditions of internal organs.
example_sentence: The internist ordered several blood tests. She visited an internist for ongoing stomach problems. An internist often treats diabetes and high blood pressure. The hospital hired a senior internist.

english_meaning: The confinement of people during war, political emergency, or security concern. Detention without ordinary trial. The act of placing people in camps or restricted areas.
example_sentence: The museum documented wartime internment. Many families suffered during the internment period. The court reviewed the legality of internment. Survivors described life in the internment camp.

english_meaning: A temporary position for practical training in a profession. A period of supervised work experience. A student or trainee placement. An opportunity to learn job skills while working.
example_sentence: She completed an internship at a hospital. The internship gave him useful office experience. Students must apply early for a summer internship. Her internship turned into a full-time job.

english_meaning: Existing or sent between offices of the same organization. Relating to communication, mail, or work among different offices. Used within a company or institution.
example_sentence: She sent an interoffice memo about the meeting. Interoffice mail arrives every afternoon. The company improved interoffice communication. An interoffice transfer moved him to another branch.

english_meaning: The ability of systems, devices, or organizations to work together. Compatibility that allows data or services to be exchanged. Functional cooperation between different platforms.
example_sentence: Interoperability is essential for electronic health records. The team tested interoperability between the apps. Lack of interoperability made the system expensive. Better interoperability helps customers move data easily.

english_meaning: Able to work or operate with another system, device, or organization. Designed to exchange information and function together. Compatible across different platforms or networks.
example_sentence: The new software is interoperable with older databases. Hospitals need interoperable health records. Interoperable devices save time for users. The two payment systems are not fully interoperable yet.

english_meaning: To penetrate or pass into one another mutually. To mix deeply with something else. To overlap or permeate each other. To blend so that boundaries become less clear.
example_sentence: The roots of the two trees interpenetrate underground. In the novel, dreams and reality interpenetrate. Their cultures began to interpenetrate over centuries. Light and color interpenetrate in the painting.

english_meaning: Mutual penetration or passing into one another. The blending or overlapping of two things so each affects the other. A deep mixing of ideas, cultures, forces, or substances.
example_sentence: Cultural interpenetration shaped the city's language. The painting suggests an interpenetration of light and shadow. The theory describes the interpenetration of mind and body. Global trade caused interpenetration among distant societies.

english_meaning: Relating to relationships or communication between people. Involving personal interaction. Existing between two or more persons. Connected with social behavior and emotional exchange.
example_sentence: Good interpersonal skills help in every job. The conflict was caused by interpersonal tension. Therapy improved her interpersonal relationships. Managers need strong interpersonal communication.

english_meaning: Existing, traveling, or occurring between planets. Relating to space between planets. Involving more than one planet. Suitable for travel from one planet to another.
example_sentence: The probe entered interplanetary space. Scientists planned an interplanetary mission to Mars. Interplanetary dust can affect spacecraft. The novel imagines interplanetary trade.

english_meaning: A reciprocal effect or interaction between people, forces, ideas, or things. The way different elements influence each other. A dynamic relationship of action and response.
example_sentence: The film shows the interplay between memory and identity. Economic policy depends on the interplay of supply and demand. Their music relies on the interplay of two guitars. The study examines the interplay between diet and health.

english_meaning: INTERPOL, officially called the International Criminal Police Organization, is an international organization that facilitates cooperation and information sharing among police authorities in different countries. It helps countries work together against crimes that cross international borders, such as terrorism, human trafficking, drug trafficking, cybercrime, financial crime, and organized crime.
example_sentence: Interpol issued a notice for the suspect. The police contacted Interpol during the investigation. Interpol helps track fugitives across borders. The agency shared the fingerprints through Interpol channels.

english_meaning: To insert words, figures, or material into a text or sequence. To estimate a missing value between known values. To add something between existing parts. To introduce material that was not originally present.
example_sentence: The software can interpolate missing data. The translator did not interpolate personal comments into the text. Scientists interpolate values between two measurements. A later scribe may have interpolated the sentence.

english_meaning: The insertion of extra words, numbers, or material into a text, data set, or sequence. An added passage not originally present. Estimation of a value between known values. A mathematical or textual insertion.
example_sentence: The editor marked a doubtful interpolation in the manuscript. Interpolation helped estimate the missing temperature value. The poem contains a later interpolation by another writer. The chart uses interpolation between measured points.

english_meaning: To place something between two things. To interrupt or insert a comment, objection, or action. To intervene between people or events. To come between for protection or delay.
example_sentence: She tried to interpose herself between the fighters. The lawyer interposed an objection. A screen was interposed between the beds. He interposed a brief question during the lecture.

english_meaning: To explain or clarify the meaning of words, actions, signs, symbols, laws, dreams, or events. To understand something in a particular way, based on your own opinion or judgment. To translate spoken or signed language from one language into another. To perform or express the meaning of a piece of music, drama, or art in your own style.
example_sentence: The teacher helped the students interpret the poem correctly. Different people may interpret the same event in different ways. A professional interpreter can interpret the speech from English into Urdu. Scientists continue to interpret the data before reaching a conclusion.

english_meaning: Able to be understood, explained, or translated. Capable of being given a meaning. Clear enough to analyze or make sense of.
example_sentence: The data is interpretable only with context. Her handwriting was barely interpretable. The model should produce interpretable results. The symbol is interpretable in several ways.

english_meaning: The act of explaining the meaning of something. A particular way of understanding or explaining an event, text, or idea. The performance of a piece of music, drama, or dance in a personal style. The process of translating spoken language from one tongue to another.
example_sentence: His interpretation of the poem was quite unusual. The law is open to different interpretations. Her interpretation of the role won wide praise. Simultaneous interpretation was provided at the conference.

english_meaning: Relating to explanation or interpretation. Designed to explain meaning, especially in art, law, text, or performance. Expressing a particular understanding of something.
example_sentence: The museum offers interpretative signs for visitors. Her dance was an interpretative response to the poem. The judge used an interpretative approach to the law. Students wrote interpretative essays on the novel.

english_meaning: A person who translates spoken or signed language. A program that executes code line by line. Someone who explains meaning, symbols, or events.
example_sentence: The interpreter translated the speech into Urdu. A sign-language interpreter stood beside the speaker. Python uses an interpreter to run code. The guide served as an interpreter of local history.

english_meaning: Involving people of different races. Existing between racial groups. Relating to relationships, marriage, families, or cooperation across racial lines.
example_sentence: They celebrated an interracial marriage. The study examined interracial friendships at school. Interracial cooperation improved the neighborhood. The film tells the story of an interracial family.

english_meaning: A period between two reigns, governments, or leaders. A gap in authority or regular rule. A temporary interval between two phases.
example_sentence: The country faced unrest during the interregnum. An interregnum followed the king's death. The university had an interregnum before the new president arrived. Artists used the political interregnum creatively.

english_meaning: To connect or show a relationship between things. To be mutually related. To affect one another through a network of connections.
example_sentence: The lessons interrelate history and literature. Climate, food, and health interrelate closely. The report shows how the factors interrelate. Teachers help students interrelate different ideas.

english_meaning: Connected with each other. Mutually related or dependent. Linked by cause, meaning, function, or influence.
example_sentence: The two problems are interrelated. Health and education are deeply interrelated. The book explains several interrelated themes. Interrelated systems can fail together.

english_meaning: A mutual relationship between two or more things. The way different factors are connected and affect each other. A network of related connections.
example_sentence: The interrelationship between poverty and health is complex. The chart shows the interrelationship of all departments. Scientists studied the interrelationship among species. Her essay explores the interrelationship between memory and language.

english_meaning: To question someone closely and formally. To examine information, data, or ideas by asking detailed questions. To question a suspect or witness.
example_sentence: The detective began to interrogate the suspect. Researchers interrogate the data before drawing conclusions. The lawyer will interrogate the witness tomorrow. Good readers interrogate the assumptions in a text.

english_meaning: The act of questioning someone closely. Formal questioning by police, officials, or investigators. A detailed examination through questions.
example_sentence: The interrogation lasted for two hours. She remained calm during the police interrogation. The report is based on interrogation of several witnesses. Interrogation of the evidence revealed new facts.

english_meaning: Asking a question. Having the form or force of a question. A word, phrase, or sentence used to ask something.
example_sentence: What is an interrogative pronoun. The sentence has an interrogative form. Her tone became interrogative at the end. Students practiced interrogative sentences in class.

english_meaning: To cross or meet at a point or along a line. To divide something by passing through or across it. To share a common area or element. The point or line where two things cross.
example_sentence: The two roads intersect at the town center. These lines intersect at a right angle. The Venn diagrams show where the sets intersect. Their interests intersect in several areas.

english_meaning: Two or more circles that cross each other at one or more points. Circles that share common points where their circumferences meet. Circles that overlap and create intersection points.
synonyms: ["Overlapping circles","Crossing circles","Circles with common points","Cutting circles"]
example_sentence: The Venn diagram shows two intersecting circles. Intersecting circles share common points. The Olympic logo consists of five intersecting circles. Calculate the area where the circles intersect.

english_meaning: Describing a person born with reproductive or sexual anatomy, chromosomes, or hormones that do not fit typical definitions of male or female. Relating to a natural biological variation in sex characteristics. A term used to describe people whose bodies do not fit neatly into the binary male or female categories.
example_sentence: Many intersex people report that they were not adequately informed about their condition during childhood. The organisation works to protect the rights of intersex individuals in healthcare settings. Intersex variations occur naturally and are more common than most people realise. She identified as intersex and spoke openly about her experiences to raise awareness. Medical professionals are increasingly moving away from unnecessary surgeries on intersex infants.

english_meaning: To scatter or place things at irregular intervals among other things. To distribute throughout something at random or varying points. To introduce variety into something by adding different elements throughout.
example_sentence: The teacher interspersed the lecture with short video clips to keep students engaged throughout. She interspersed the formal report with colourful charts and personal anecdotes. Wildflowers had been interspersed among the formal rose beds to create a more natural effect. The author chose to intersperse poems throughout the novel to give it a lyrical quality. The garden designer interspersed tall plants among shorter ones to create a layered visual effect.

english_meaning: Relating to or connecting different states. Existing or carried on between states, especially of the US. A highway serving two or more states. Involving the mutual relations of states or provinces. One of a system of expressways extending between the major cities.
example_sentence: They drove along the interstate to reach the next city. Interstate commerce is regulated by the federal government. She moved to another state and had to pay interstate shipping fees. The fugitive crossed interstate lines to avoid capture.

english_meaning: Occurring or situated between the stars. Relating to the space, matter, or travel between stars in a galaxy. Concerning the vast regions of empty space outside of our solar system. Used to describe phenomena, dust, gas, or missions that exist or operate between star systems. In popular usage, anything connected with deep space exploration.
example_sentence: Scientists are studying clouds of interstellar dust and gas. The novel describes an interstellar journey to a distant planet. Voyager 1 has now entered interstellar space. Interstellar travel remains a great challenge for modern science. Many films explore the dream of interstellar exploration by humans.

english_meaning: Something that exists in the small spaces between things. Anything located in or relating to the spaces between structures, objects, or parts. It is commonly used in medicine, biology, construction, and digital media. For example, in healthcare it describes spaces between tissues, and in advertising it refers to ads that appear between content.
example_sentence: The doctor diagnosed an interstitial lung disease. Interstitial fluid surrounds the cells in the body. The app shows interstitial ads between levels. The interstitial spaces in the wall help with insulation.

english_meaning: To come between people or events in order to change or prevent something. To take action in a situation to alter or stop what is happening. To interrupt a process or conflict in order to improve the outcome.
example_sentence: The teacher had to intervene when the disagreement between the two students began to escalate. The government decided to intervene in the market to stabilise prices for essential goods. She chose not to intervene in the dispute and let the parties resolve it themselves. International observers were called to intervene when the ceasefire appeared to be breaking down. A passing officer intervened just in time to prevent the argument from turning violent.

english_meaning: The action or process of intervening or becoming involved in a situation to change its outcome. It can refer to a state's interference in the affairs of another, a medical procedure, or a psychological aid. The goal is usually to improve a situation or prevent harm.
example_sentence: The central bank's intervention helped to stabilize the falling currency. Military intervention was considered a last resort by the international community. Early medical intervention is crucial for a full recovery from this disease. The teacher’s intervention stopped the argument before it turned into a fight.

english_meaning: A formal meeting in which a person is asked questions to judge their suitability for a job or course. A conversation in which a journalist questions someone for a report. A meeting arranged to obtain information or opinions. To question someone formally in such a meeting.
example_sentence: She has an interview for the teaching post tomorrow. The minister gave a long interview to the newspaper. The researchers interviewed fifty families for the study. He prepared carefully before the job interview.

english_meaning: To twist or twine together. To connect or link closely. To become mutually involved or interconnected. To weave one thing with another so that they cannot be easily separated. When two or more things are joined, mixed, or related so closely that they form a single whole or cannot be considered separately. It is often used for physical things like threads, branches, or hands, and also for abstract things like lives, stories, or destinies.
example_sentence: The branches of the two old trees intertwine above the garden path. Their fingers intertwined as they walked along the beach. The lives of the two families have been intertwined for generations. History and politics are deeply intertwined in this region. The vines intertwined around the wooden fence.

english_meaning: The long, tube-like organ in the abdomen that completes the process of digestion. The segment of the alimentary canal extending from the stomach to the anus. A vital organ responsible for water absorption and waste excretion. Divided into two main sections known as the small and large intestines. A major component of the gastrointestinal tract in vertebrates.
synonyms: ["Gut","Bowel","Viscera","Entrails","Alimentary Canal","Gastrointestinal Tract","Digestive Tract","Innards","Small Bowel","Large Bowel","Colon","Internal Organs"]
example_sentence: Nutrients are absorbed through the walls of the small intestine. The doctor examined her lower intestine for signs of inflammation. Drinking plenty of water is essential for a healthy intestine. The surgeon performed a procedure to remove a blockage in the large intestine.

english_meaning: A state of having a very close personal relationship or detailed knowledge of something. It often refers to a close familiar and usually affectionate or loving personal relationship. It can also imply a private, cozy atmosphere or a deep understanding of a subject.
example_sentence: The long-married couple shared a deep sense of intimacy. Little by little, they developed an intimacy that transcended friendship. The small room provided an atmosphere of quiet intimacy for the meeting. Her intimacy with the local history made her an excellent guide.

english_meaning: Marked by very close association, contact, or familiarity. It describes a person with whom one has a very close relationship or a place that is private and cozy. It can also mean relating to the fundamental nature of something or being very personal.
example_sentence: They have been intimate friends since their early childhood. The restaurant offered an intimate setting for their wedding anniversary. He has an intimate knowledge of how the modern engine works. She shared the intimate details of her life with her sister.

english_meaning: An indirect suggestion or a slight sign of something. It refers to the action of making something known in an indirect or subtle way. Often, it is a hint or inkling about a future event or a hidden truth.
example_sentence: The first intimation of the coming storm was a sudden drop in temperature. She gave no intimation that she was planning to resign from her post. I had not the slightest intimation of his intentions until he spoke. He received an intimation that his presence was requested at the palace.

english_meaning: To frighten or threaten someone so they do what you want or stop them from doing something. To make a person feel scared, nervous, or less confident, often by using threats, strong behavior, or pressure. It can be physical, verbal, or psychological. When someone is intimidated, they feel weak, unsafe, or unable to respond freely.
example_sentence: The manager tried to intimidate the workers into accepting lower wages. Big dogs sometimes intimidate small children. He was intimidated by the strict teacher and stayed quiet. She refused to be intimidated by their threats.

english_meaning: The act of frightening or threatening someone to make them do something or stop them from doing something. The use of fear, threats, pressure, or aggressive behavior to influence, control, or discourage another person. It may involve verbal threats, physical gestures, emotional pressure, or abuse of authority. Intimidation can occur in workplaces, schools, politics, sports, families, or legal situations.
example_sentence: The witness refused to stay silent despite the intimidation from the criminals. Workplace intimidation can lower employee confidence and productivity. The coach warned the players that bullying and intimidation would not be tolerated. She reported the intimidation to the authorities before the situation became worse.

english_meaning: Unwillingness to accept views, beliefs, or behavior that differ from one's own. It can also refer to the incapacity of the body to endure a particular substance, such as a food or drug. This state often leads to prejudice or physical discomfort.
example_sentence: Religious intolerance has been the cause of many wars throughout history. His intolerance for any kind of delay made him a difficult boss. The child suffers from a severe lactose intolerance. We must fight against social intolerance and promote equality for all.

english_meaning: The rise and fall of the voice in speaking. The pattern or variation of pitch used while speaking a sentence. The musical quality or melody of speech that conveys meaning, emotion or attitude. The accurate production of pitch in singing or playing a musical instrument.
example_sentence: Her rising intonation made the statement sound like a question. The actor's intonation perfectly conveyed the character's sadness. English learners often struggle with correct intonation. The violinist was praised for her flawless intonation. He read the poem with beautiful intonation and rhythm.

english_meaning: A substance that affects the mind or body and causes drunkenness, loss of control, or altered mental state. Any chemical substance, especially alcohol or drugs, that temporarily changes how the brain works. It can reduce awareness, slow reactions, and affect judgment. It may cause a feeling of pleasure at first, but it can also lead to confusion, addiction, or harmful behavior.
example_sentence: Alcohol is a common intoxicant used in many countries. The doctor warned him about the harmful effects of intoxicants. Some plants contain natural intoxicants that affect the nervous system. Driving under the influence of any intoxicant is illegal.

english_meaning: To affect someone strongly, usually by alcohol or drugs, so that they lose control or clear judgment. To make someone drunk or mentally affected by alcohol, drugs, or any strong influence that reduces normal thinking or behavior. It can also mean to strongly excite or overwhelm someone emotionally, like joy, power, or love.
example_sentence: The strong wine began to intoxicate him quickly. He was intoxicated by the smell of expensive perfume. Fame can intoxicate people and change their behavior. The celebration atmosphere intoxicated the crowd with joy.

english_meaning: Under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or strongly excited by emotion or joy. A person is affected by alcohol or drugs so that normal thinking, movement, and behavior are disturbed. It can also be used figuratively for strong emotional states like love, joy, or excitement.
example_sentence: He was intoxicated after drinking too much wine at the party. The driver was arrested because he was intoxicated while driving. She felt intoxicated with happiness after hearing the good news. They were intoxicated by the beauty of the mountain view.

english_meaning: State of being affected by alcohol, drugs, or strong emotion. A condition in which a person loses normal control because of alcohol, drugs, or overwhelming emotions such as happiness, love, or anger.
example_sentence: His intoxication made him unable to walk properly. She felt an intoxication of success after winning the competition. Driving under intoxication is dangerous and illegal. The crowd was in intoxication of excitement during the concert.

english_meaning: Refusing to agree or compromise. Unwilling to change one's views or position despite pressure or argument. Holding firmly and stubbornly to one's own position.
example_sentence: The two sides remained intransigent throughout the negotiations and no agreement was reached. His intransigent attitude made it impossible to find a mutually acceptable solution. The intransigent faction within the party refused to back the compromise put forward by the leadership. She was known as an intransigent opponent of any changes to the original design. The union leaders were accused of being intransigent in their refusal to consider any wage reduction.

english_meaning: In grammar, describing a verb that does not take a direct object. Referring to an action that is complete in itself without acting on something else. Used of verbs such as sleep, arrive, and laugh. An intransitive verb itself.
example_sentence: The verb sleep is intransitive and takes no object. Students must learn to distinguish transitive from intransitive verbs. In this sentence the verb is used intransitively as an intransitive. Many verbs can be both transitive and intransitive.

english_meaning: In a way that does not take a direct object. Used to describe how a verb functions grammatically without an object. In grammar, in the manner of an intransitive verb. Without transferring the action to another person or thing.
example_sentence: The verb run can also be used intransitively. Here the word grows is used intransitively. Explain how this verb behaves intransitively in the sentence. Some verbs change meaning when used intransitively.

english_meaning: Very complicated, detailed, or difficult to understand. Containing many small parts or details arranged in a complex way. Hard to follow, analyse, or solve due to complexity. Often used to describe designs, patterns, machines, problems, or relationships that involve many interrelated elements.
example_sentence: The watchmaker repaired the intricate mechanism of the old clock. She wore a sari with intricate embroidery on the borders. The novel has an intricate plot with many characters. Solving this intricate puzzle took him several hours. The court is examining the intricate details of the case.

english_meaning: The activity of making secret plans. The practice of engaging in secret schemes. To secretly plan with other people to harm somebody. To make somebody very interested and want to know more about something.
example_sentence: Throughout history, people have been intrigued by the question of whether there is intelligent life elsewhere in the universe. It intrigues me that no one appears to have thought of this before. The young heroine steps into a web of intrigue in the academic world.

english_meaning: Aroused curiosity or interest in someone. Fascinated or deeply interested by something mysterious, unusual or attractive. Made to wonder or want to know more about a particular matter. Captivated mentally by something puzzling or appealing.
example_sentence: I was intrigued by the strange noise coming from the attic. The professor seemed intrigued by the student's unusual question. She was intrigued enough to read the entire book in one night. He looked intrigued when she mentioned the secret meeting. The detective was intrigued by the missing clue.

english_meaning: Belonging naturally; essential. Existing as a basic and inseparable part of something. Inherent, inborn, or built-in by its very nature. Relating to the true or fundamental qualities of a thing rather than external factors. Often contrasted with 'extrinsic'.
example_sentence: Honesty has intrinsic value in every culture. Gold has an intrinsic worth that does not depend on fashion. Curiosity is an intrinsic part of a child's nature. The intrinsic beauty of the landscape attracts thousands of tourists. Kindness is an intrinsic quality of a good leader.

english_meaning: To make a person known to another by name for the first time. To bring something into use, practice, or existence for the first time. To present a topic, speaker, or programme to an audience. To insert or put something into a place or substance. To formally propose a new law or bill for consideration.
example_sentence: Allow me to introduce you to my colleague. The school introduced a new reading programme this year. She was invited to introduce the keynote speaker. The government plans to introduce stricter safety rules.

english_meaning: The act of examining one's own thoughts and feelings. Careful self-examination of one's motives and behaviour. Quiet reflection about one's inner life and experiences. A method of studying the mind by observing one's own mental states.
example_sentence: A long walk gave him time for quiet introspection. Her diary is full of honest introspection. Failure often leads to painful introspection. The retreat encouraged meditation and introspection.

english_meaning: A person who practises or advocates introspection as a method of psychological investigation. A psychologist or thinker who relies on self-examination of one's own mental and emotional states. One who believes in the study of the mind through personal inner observation.
example_sentence: As an introspectionist, she believed that understanding oneself was the first step toward understanding others. The early introspectionists sought to map the structure of the human mind through careful self-analysis. He was a committed introspectionist who kept detailed journals of his daily thoughts and feelings. The introspectionist school of psychology fell out of favour with the rise of behaviourism in the twentieth century. She read the work of the great introspectionists before beginning her own research into consciousness.

english_meaning: Examining or contemplating one's own thoughts, feelings, and mental processes. Tending to look inward rather than at external events. Reflective and self-examining in nature.
example_sentence: She became increasingly introspective after the loss of her father and spent long hours in quiet reflection. His poetry has always had a deeply introspective quality that resonates with many readers. The retreat was designed to give participants the time and space to be fully introspective. After the failure of the project, the entire team entered an introspective period to assess what had gone wrong. She was an introspective child who preferred reading and drawing to playing with others.

english_meaning: To concentrate or direct upon oneself. A quiet person who is more interested in their own thoughts and feelings than in spending time with other people. Someone who is shy, quiet, and prefers to spend time alone rather than often being with other people.
example_sentence: He was described as an introvert, a reserved man who spoke little. His teachers perceived him as shy and introverted. His research further shows that about 70% of top executives are introverts. Bill Gates is quiet and bookish, but apparently unfazed by others' opinions of him: he's an introvert, but not shy.

english_meaning: To go or be somewhere where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be. To enter into something in a way that is not wanted or to have an unpleasant effect on it.
example_sentence: Personal, subjective elements should not be allowed to intrude.We should not intrude upon their private grief. I'm sorry to intrude, but I need to talk to someone.

english_meaning: A person who enters a place, property, group, or system without invitation, permission, or legal right. A trespasser who enters private property. A person who interferes in others’ affairs or privacy. Someone who enters a computer system without authorization. A person who joins a group or activity where they are not welcome.
example_sentence: The security guard caught an intruder inside the office building at night. The alarm system warned the family about an intruder in the house. The hacker acted like an intruder in the company’s computer network. She felt like an intruder when she accidentally joined their private meeting.

english_meaning: Unwanted and entering someone’s space, thoughts, or life without permission. Describes something or someone that interferes in a way that feels unwelcome, invades privacy, or interrupts normal flow.
example_sentence: His intrusive questions made everyone uncomfortable. She found the pop up ads intrusive while reading. The reporter’s intrusive behavior annoyed the actor. He tried to stop intrusive thoughts before sleeping.

english_meaning: To know that something is true based on your feelings rather than on facts, what somebody tells you, etc. To perceive or comprehend something immediately through instinctive feeling rather than through rational thought or explicit evidence. It involves sensing the truth or outcome without needing step-by-step reasoning.
example_sentence: She intuited that he was lying even though he seemed confident. Scientists often intuit patterns before they can prove them. He intuited the solution to the problem without needing a formula. Children can intuit emotions more easily than adults sometimes.

english_meaning: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning. It is often described as a 'gut feeling' or a sense of knowing something based on experience rather than facts. It represents a quick and ready insight.
example_sentence: She had an intuition that something was wrong even before she entered the house. Following his intuition, the detective decided to search the basement again. Intuition told me that I should not trust the salesman's promises. Artists often rely on their intuition rather than formal rules.

english_meaning: Relating to or derived from intuition rather than through reasoning or experience. It describes a process or thought that occurs through immediate apprehension. It is the quality of knowing or perceiving by an instinctive sense.
example_sentence: Her approach to solving the puzzle was more intuitional than logical. He had an intuitional grasp of the complex mathematical theories. The decision was based on an intuitional sense of timing. Intuitional knowledge is often difficult to explain to others in words.

english_meaning: The philosophical belief that moral truths or fundamental principles are known through intuition rather than reason or experience. It suggests that human beings possess an innate faculty to perceive right and wrong directly. This perspective emphasizes the immediacy of knowledge over discursive thought.
example_sentence: The philosopher argued that intuitionalism provides the foundation for our moral convictions. Many critics of intuitionalism suggest that it lacks a systematic way to resolve conflicting beliefs. Her approach to ethics was rooted in intuitionalism, relying on internal feelings rather than external rules. The study of intuitionalism often involves exploring the origins of human conscience.

english_meaning: A doctrine in ethics holding that moral values are known by intuition. In mathematics, it refers to the theory that mathematics is a product of the human mind and that mathematical objects do not exist independently of our mental constructions. It emphasizes the direct apprehension of truth.
example_sentence: Mathematical intuitionism rejects the idea of the law of the excluded middle. He applied intuitionism to his ethical framework to explain how people perceive beauty. Critics of intuitionism argue that it is too subjective for scientific application. The school of intuitionism gained popularity in the early twentieth century.

english_meaning: Having the ability to understand or know something immediately, without conscious reasoning. Something that feels natural or easy to grasp because it aligns with instinct or perception.
example_sentence: She had an intuitive sense that something was wrong. The app has an intuitive interface that is easy to navigate. His intuitive decision-making often leads to success. Artists often rely on their intuitive feelings to create.

english_meaning: In a way that is based on instinct or immediate understanding rather than conscious reasoning. By using your feelings rather than by considering the facts.
example_sentence: She intuitively knew something was wrong. He solved the problem intuitively without checking the manual. The design feels intuitively easy to use. Children often learn language intuitively.

english_meaning: To give or send somebody so many things that they cannot deal with them all. To cover an area of land with a large amount of water. To bring to a place or person too much of something, so that it cannot be dealt with.
example_sentence: We have been inundated with offers of help. She's inundated with work at the moment. Flood waters inundate the river plain each spring. Many sheep were lost in the floods and the city was inundated. The agency was inundated with phone calls.

english_meaning: A flood or the covering of land with a large amount of water. The act of overwhelming a place or person with too much of something. A very large quantity arriving all at once. In agriculture, the deliberate flooding of fields with water.
example_sentence: The inundation destroyed crops across the whole district. Villagers fled before the inundation reached their homes. The office faced an inundation of complaints after the notice. Annual inundation makes the soil unusually fertile.

english_meaning: To make someone accustomed to something unpleasant through long experience. To harden a person so that difficulties no longer trouble them. In law, to come into effect or operate for the benefit of someone. To toughen by repeated exposure.
example_sentence: Years of hard work had inured him to long hours. Soldiers are inured to discomfort during training. Nurses become inured to the sight of blood. The benefit shall inure to the heirs of the deceased.

english_meaning: To become or make someone used to something difficult or unpleasant. To grow hardened to hardship, pain, or criticism through repeated exposure. To accept an unwelcome condition without being disturbed by it. To train a person to endure something over time.
synonyms: ["Get used to","Become hardened to","Grow accustomed to","Adapt to","Adjust to","Toughen against"]
antonyms: ["Be shocked by","Remain sensitive to","Recoil from","Be unsettled by","Reject"]
example_sentence: The villagers are inured to long power cuts. He soon became inured to the harsh winter climate. Public figures grow inured to criticism over time. Training inured the recruits to extreme physical strain.

english_meaning: To enter a place by force or without permission. To enter a country or area using military force. To spread into something harmful or unwanted. To interrupt or disturb someone’s privacy or space. To overrun or overwhelm. To intrude physically or emotionally. To spread like disease, insects, or unwanted thoughts.
example_sentence: The army planned to invade the neighboring country. It is wrong to invade someone’s privacy without permission. Ants invaded the kitchen after the rain. Negative thoughts can invade your mind if you are not careful.

english_meaning: To make something officially void, not valid, or without legal force. To demonstrate that something is not true or correct. To render an argument, claim, or document ineffective.
example_sentence: The missing signature was enough to invalidate the entire document. His argument was invalidated by several pieces of contradictory evidence. The research findings were used to invalidate the previously accepted theory. The election result could be invalidated if widespread fraud is proven. Failure to comply with the conditions will automatically invalidate the warranty.

english_meaning: Never changing; always the same. Constant and unvarying in nature or amount. Something that remains fixed and does not alter. Always occurring in the same way.
example_sentence: His invariable morning routine included a walk and coffee. The invariable laws of physics apply everywhere. She greeted everyone with her invariable smile. Rain is the invariable result of those dark clouds.

english_meaning: Entering a place by force, especially by an army. The act of entering a place, territory, or country using force, often in a hostile or aggressive way. It is commonly used in military contexts, but it can also describe unwanted interference, spread of harmful things, or violation of privacy.
example_sentence: The army launched an invasion of the neighboring country. The invasion of privacy made her feel uncomfortable. Farmers are worried about the invasion of locusts this season. The country prepared its defenses against a possible invasion.

english_meaning: Something that enters, spreads, or intrudes where it is not welcome. Entering or spreading into an area where it is not wanted. Involving medical procedures that enter the body. Intruding into someone's privacy or personal space. Spreading rapidly and harming the environment, especially plants or species.
example_sentence: The doctor recommended a less invasive treatment. This invasive plant is damaging local crops. His questions felt invasive and uncomfortable. The species became invasive in the new environment.

english_meaning: To speak or write about something with great hostility or strong criticism. To protest or complain bitterly and at length about something. To rail against something with force and passion.
example_sentence: He would regularly inveigh against the corruption and inefficiency that he saw in the political system. The editorial inveighed against the government's failure to address the housing crisis. She inveighed passionately against the policy in her speech before the full assembly. The philosopher was known to inveigh against any form of intellectual dishonesty or hypocrisy. The columnist inveighed against the treatment of prisoners in the article published last week.

english_meaning: To create or design something that has not existed before. To produce something original through imagination and skill. To fabricate or make up something that is not true. To devise a new method, process, or product.
example_sentence: Thomas Edison is credited with helping to invent the practical electric light bulb. She had a gift for finding gaps in the market and inventing products to fill them. Children often invent imaginative stories to explain things they do not yet understand. He had to admit that he had invented part of the story to make it more interesting. The challenge was to invent a material that was both lightweight and extremely strong.

english_meaning: Having the ability to create or design new ideas or things. Showing creativity, originality, and skill in coming up with new ideas, solutions, or methods. It refers to the talent for thinking in innovative and imaginative ways.
example_sentence: She is very inventive and always finds unique ways to solve problems. The engineer came up with an inventive solution to reduce energy consumption. His inventive mind led to several successful patents. Children are often more inventive than adults in their play.

english_meaning: A person who creates or designs something that did not exist before. Someone who originates or develops a new device, method, or process through study and experimentation. A creative individual who conceives and brings into existence new machines, tools, or techniques. One who pioneers or introduces innovations in science, technology, or industry. A person who imagines and produces novel solutions to practical problems.
example_sentence: The inventor spent ten years developing a new type of solar panel. Alexander Graham Bell was the inventor of the telephone. Many inventors work tirelessly in their garages to create revolutionary products. The young inventor received a patent for her innovative water purifier. Great inventors throughout history have changed the way we live and communicate.

english_meaning: A complete list of items such as property, goods in stock, or the contents of a building. It can also refer to the act of making such a list or the quantity of goods currently on hand. In a broader sense, it can mean a summary of one's personal traits or resources.
example_sentence: The store manager stayed late to complete the annual inventory. They kept a careful inventory of all the historical artifacts in the museum. Our inventory of office supplies is running low and needs restocking. The company uses specialized software to track its inventory in real-time.

english_meaning: Turned upside down or inside out. Reversed in position, order, or direction. Changed to the opposite of what was expected. Having an inverted relationship or correlation. Made to go backward or in the opposite way.
example_sentence: The inversed image on the screen confused the viewers. In inversed order, the last item became the first. The inversed relationship between the two variables surprised the researchers. He described the inversed logic of the argument. The inversed sequence of events was difficult to follow.

english_meaning: An animal that lacks a backbone or spinal column. A creature without an internal skeleton made of bone or cartilage. Organisms such as insects, worms, mollusks, and arachnids that rely on external structures or fluid pressure for support. Any animal belonging to the large group of species without vertebrae. A soft-bodied creature that often has an exoskeleton or hydrostatic skeleton.
example_sentence: Jellyfish and octopuses are well-known invertebrates found in the ocean. The biologist studied various invertebrates in the tidal pools. Invertebrates make up the vast majority of animal species on Earth. Spiders are invertebrates that have an exoskeleton instead of a backbone. The museum displayed colorful shells and preserved invertebrates from around the world.

english_meaning: Having a habit or interest so firmly established that it is unlikely to change; long-established and deep-rooted.
example_sentence: He was an inveterate gambler who could not stop despite his losses. She was an inveterate reader, finishing a book every week. The inveterate liar was trusted by no one. His inveterate optimism kept him going through hard times.

english_meaning: To give strength, energy, or fresh life to someone or something. To make a person feel healthier, livelier, and more active. To stimulate or revive an activity, business, or economy. To refresh the mind and restore enthusiasm.
example_sentence: A brisk morning walk always invigorates me. The new manager was hired to invigorate the struggling company. Cold mountain air invigorated the tired hikers. Fresh investment helped invigorate the local economy.

english_meaning: Impossible to defeat, overcome, or destroy. A person, group, spirit, or thing that cannot be defeated, conquered, or broken. It may refer to real strength, great power, or strong confidence. Sometimes it is also used figuratively for someone who feels unbeatable.
example_sentence: The champion looked invincible throughout the tournament. Her courage made her seem invincible in difficult times. The army believed its strong walls were invincible. After several victories, the team felt invincible.

english_meaning: Something that must not be broken, harmed, or violated. A rule, right, place, or principle that is protected by law, morals, or strong belief and should never be broken, attacked, or ignored.
example_sentence: Freedom of religion is considered inviolable in many constitutions. The sanctity of human life should remain inviolable at all times. The agreement stated that national borders are inviolable. Medical confidentiality is an inviolable ethical principle.

english_meaning: Unable to be seen, either because it is hidden or because it does not physically exist. Not perceptible by the eye. Concealed from view or hidden from sight. Not noticeable or recognized by others. Impossible to detect visually.
example_sentence: The wind is invisible but powerful. She felt invisible in a room full of strangers. Germs are invisible to the naked eye. He wished he could become invisible for a day.

english_meaning: To call upon or appeal to a higher power or deity. To invoke or summon through prayer or ritual. To request earnestly or beg for divine aid. To utter or recite a prayer or incantation. To conjure or appeal to spiritual forces for help or protection.
example_sentence: The priest began to invocate the blessings of the gods upon the harvest. Ancient shamans would invocate spirits during sacred ceremonies. She learned to invocate peace and harmony in her daily meditation. The villagers gathered to invocate rain for their dying crops. He tried to invocate the wisdom of his ancestors before making the decision.

english_meaning: To call upon something, especially a higher power, authority, or law, for help, support, or inspiration. To cite or appeal to something as a justification. To cause something to happen or bring something into effect. To call on a higher power or deity for assistance. To call a function, method, or procedure in programming. To cite or refer to as evidence or justification. To summon someone or something formally.
example_sentence: The priest invoked blessings upon the congregation. She invoked her right to remain silent during the trial. The programmer invoked the function to run the application. The manager invoked company policy to resolve the dispute. The villagers invoked the rain god during the drought. The app invoked the login API to authenticate the user. The teacher invoked previous research to support her argument.

english_meaning: To include someone or something as a necessary part. To cause a person to take part in an activity. To require or imply a particular action, risk, or result. To affect or concern someone directly.
example_sentence: The project will involve several local schools. Do not involve children in adult arguments. The job involves travel and long meetings. The decision may involve serious financial risk.

english_meaning: To make someone take part in an activity or situation. To include a person in a process, problem, or event. To connect someone with a matter. To draw someone into something, especially responsibility or difficulty.
synonyms: ["Include in","Engage in","Draw into","Bring into","Connect with","Implicate in","Enlist in","Associate with"]
antonyms: ["Exclude from","Keep out of","Remove from","Detach from","Free from","Separate from","Omit from"]
example_sentence: The teacher tried to involve every student in the discussion. Do not involve me in your private dispute. The charity involves volunteers in community projects. The scandal involved several officials in serious accusations.

english_meaning: Actively participating in an activity, event, or organization. Closely related to or connected with something.
