Having many details or parts that make something difficult to understand. Having strong emotional feelings for someone or something. Connected with an illegal act, problem, or difficult situation. (past tense and past participle of involve)
example_sentence: She is involved in many charity projects. Several companies were involved in the project. The instructions are quite involved. She became emotionally involved with the family. He was involved in the robbery.

english_meaning: The act or state of taking part in something. Participation or engagement in an activity. A connection with a person, event, or situation. Emotional or practical commitment.
example_sentence: Her involvement improved the whole campaign. Police questioned him about his involvement in the case. Parents are encouraged to increase their involvement in school life. His emotional involvement made the decision harder.

english_meaning: Someone or something that cannot be harmed, damaged, or defeated. It refers to being completely safe from attack, injury, criticism, or danger. Also used in emotional or abstract sense, meaning someone who is not affected by criticism, fear, or emotional harm.
example_sentence: The fortress was considered invulnerable to enemy attacks. He felt invulnerable after wearing the protective armor. No one is truly invulnerable to criticism. The superhero seemed invulnerable to all weapons.

english_meaning: Directed toward the inside or center. Existing within the mind or spirit. Relating to one's inner thoughts and feelings. Moving toward the interior. In a private or personal sense.
example_sentence: He gave an inward sigh of relief. The door opens with an inward push. She has a strong inward sense of peace. His inward struggles were hidden from everyone.

english_meaning: In a way that is felt or experienced in the mind but not shown outwardly. Privately or secretly within oneself, without expressing it openly. Toward the inside or interior of something. In one's thoughts, feelings, or spirit rather than in visible behavior. In a manner that is directed within oneself.
example_sentence: He inwardly cursed himself for the mistake. She smiled politely but was inwardly furious. Inwardly, he knew the plan would fail. The petals of the flower curl inwardly at night.

english_meaning: A chemical element essential for thyroid hormone production. A trace mineral needed for proper metabolism and growth. A dark purple-black solid used as a disinfectant. A nutrient found in seafood, dairy, and iodized salt.
example_sentence: Iodine is essential for thyroid function. The wound was cleaned with iodine solution. Seafood is a good source of dietary iodine. Iodine deficiency causes goiter.

english_meaning: Relating to one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, marked by scroll-shaped capitals on columns. In chemistry, relating to or containing ions. Belonging to Ionia or its ancient Greek people and dialect.
example_sentence: The temple is supported by tall Ionic columns. Students learned to tell Ionic capitals from Doric ones. Salt is held together by an ionic bond. The museum displays pottery from Ionic settlements.

english_meaning: By that very fact or act itself. As an inevitable result of something that has happened. Automatically, because of the nature of the fact itself.
example_sentence: A member who fails to pay the fee is ipso facto disqualified. Breaking the agreement ipso facto ends the partnership. Being wealthy does not ipso facto make a person generous. The contract becomes void ipso facto on the date of default.

english_meaning: Easily angered or irritated. A person who becomes angry very quickly, often over small or unimportant matters.
example_sentence: The irascible teacher shouted when the class became noisy. His irascible nature made it hard for others to work with him. She avoided arguments because her boss was irascible. Age and stress had made him more irascible than before. He has an irascible temperament.

english_meaning: Intense anger or rage. A feeling of great wrath or fury. Strong displeasure or hostility aroused by wrongdoing. The state of being furious or enraged. A poetic or literary term for anger.
example_sentence: The boss's ire was evident when he discovered the mistake in the report. She tried to calm her friend's ire after the unfair accusation. The public's ire grew as the scandal unfolded in the media. His careless words provoked the ire of the entire community. The king's ire could be terrifying for those who displeased him.

english_meaning: Not showing a proper sense of duty or care about the consequences of one's actions. Behaving in a careless way that may cause harm or loss to others. Not able or willing to be trusted with duties or obligations. Done without thinking about the possible results.
example_sentence: It was irresponsible of him to leave the children alone at home. The company was criticised for its irresponsible handling of waste. Driving at that speed on a wet road is highly irresponsible. She apologised for her irresponsible remarks on social media.

english_meaning: The coloured, ring-shaped part of the eye surrounding the pupil. The muscular curtain that widens or narrows the pupil to control how much light enters the eye. The structure that gives a person's eyes their brown, blue, green, or grey colour. A tall garden plant with sword-shaped leaves and large, showy flowers.
synonyms: ["Coloured part of the eye","Eye diaphragm","Flag flower","Fleur-de-lis plant"]
example_sentence: The iris controls how much light reaches the retina. Her iris is a striking shade of green. In bright sunlight the iris makes the pupil smaller. A row of purple iris bloomed along the garden path.

english_meaning: To annoy, irritate, or bother someone; to make someone feel slightly angry or uncomfortable. To make feel uneasy or frustrated, not extremely angry, but irritated enough to disturb peace of mind
example_sentence: His constant complaining began to irk everyone in the office. It irks me when people don’t say thank you. The noise from the construction site really irks me in the morning. She tried to stay calm, but his rude tone irked her deeply.

english_meaning: A dark, dull shade of grey resembling the colour of iron. Describing hair that has turned dark grey with age. Suggesting hardness, sternness, or lack of warmth in appearance.
example_sentence: He had thick iron-grey hair and a neat beard. The sky turned iron-grey before the storm. She wore an iron-grey suit to the meeting. The old ship was painted iron-grey.

english_meaning: Something that happens in an opposite or unexpected way. A situation where the outcome is opposite to what is expected, or when something happens in a surprising and often funny or sad way. It can also mean using words to express something different from their literal meaning, usually for humor or criticism.
example_sentence: It was ironic that the fire station burned down. She found it ironic that the health coach was always unhealthy. It is ironic that he failed the safety test. The weather was ironic because it rained on the day they planned a beach picnic.

english_meaning: In a way that is opposite to what is expected or intended, often in a surprising or funny way. Used when something happens in a way that is unexpected, opposite, or contradictory to what was intended or believed. It often highlights a situation where reality is very different from expectation, sometimes in a humorous or sad way.
example_sentence: Ironically, the fire station burned down during a fire. He studied hard for the exam but, ironically, he failed it. Ironically, the doctor who advised healthy eating died of a heart attack. She was afraid of water, but ironically became a swimming coach.

english_meaning: The expression of meaning by using language that normally signifies the opposite, typically for humorous or emphatic effect. A situation, event, or outcome that is strange or amusing because it is the opposite of what was expected. A literary technique in which the intended meaning is different from, or opposite to, the literal meaning. A state of affairs that seems deliberately contrary to what one expects.
example_sentence: The irony of the situation was that the fire station itself caught fire. She used heavy irony when she called the rainy, cold day 'perfect weather'. There is a bitter irony in losing your job at a company you helped to build. The novel is filled with irony and dark humour. It is an irony of history that the peace treaty led to another war.

english_meaning: Not based on reason or clear thinking. A person, action, belief, or feeling that is not guided by logic, reason, or sound judgment. It may involve emotions that overpower sensible thinking or ideas that do not make practical sense. number that cannot be written as a simple fraction and has a non repeating, non ending decimal form.
example_sentence: His fear of harmless insects is completely irrational. She made an irrational decision when she refused medical help. The market sometimes reacts in irrational ways during a crisis. He became irrational with anger and shouted at everyone. It is irrational to expect success without hard work.  Pi is an irrational number.

english_meaning: A number that cannot be written as a simple fraction of two integers. A number whose decimal expansion never ends and never repeats. A real number that is not rational, such as pi or the square root of two.
example_sentence: Pi is the best known irrational number. The square root of two is an irrational number. Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as exact fractions. Students often find irrational numbers difficult to understand.

english_meaning: Impossible to deny or disprove. So clear and certain that it cannot be argued against. Beyond question or doubt. Supported by evidence that cannot be challenged. Absolutely undeniable and conclusive.
example_sentence: The prosecution presented irrefutable evidence of the defendant's guilt. Her irrefutable logic convinced everyone in the debate. The fingerprints provided irrefutable proof of his presence at the scene. There is irrefutable scientific data supporting climate change. His honesty was an irrefutable fact known to all his colleagues.

english_meaning: Not even or balanced in shape or arrangement. Occurring at uneven or varying intervals. Not conforming to a standard or a set of rules. Not belonging to a permanent or organized military force. Departing from the usual or expected pattern of behavior.
example_sentence: The gardener used irregular stones to create a natural looking path. He has an irregular heartbeat that requires medical monitoring. The troops launched an attack against the irregular forces in the mountains. She was disciplined for her irregular attendance at the weekly meetings.

english_meaning: A polygon with sides of different lengths or angles of different measures. A geometric shape that does not have all sides or angles equal. A polygon that lacks uniformity in its dimensions.
example_sentence: Most real-world shapes are irregular polygons. An irregular polygon has no specific pattern of symmetry. The plot of land formed an irregular polygon. The artist created designs using various irregular polygons.

english_meaning: A four-sided polygon where all sides have different lengths and all angles have different measures. A quadrilateral that does not have equal sides or equal angles. A four-sided shape that is not regular in its dimensions.
example_sentence: The kite is an example of an irregular quadrilateral. Most real-world quadrilaterals are irregular in nature. An irregular quadrilateral has no specific symmetry pattern. The plot of land formed an irregular quadrilateral shape.

english_meaning: The state of not being regular, even, or smooth. Something that does not follow the usual rules or pattern. An action that is improper or against accepted procedure. A rough or uneven part of a surface. An unusual or unhealthy variation in bodily rhythm.
example_sentence: The auditors found several irregularities in the accounts. There is a slight irregularity in the surface of the wall. Any irregularity in the election must be reported. The doctor examined an irregularity in his heartbeat.

english_meaning: In a way that does not follow a regular pattern or time. At uneven intervals rather than steadily. In a manner that breaks the usual rules or standards. With an uneven shape, surface, or arrangement.
example_sentence: The buses run irregularly on public holidays. His heart was beating irregularly, so the doctor was called. The committee meets irregularly throughout the year. The stones were placed irregularly along the path.

english_meaning: The state of having no connection with or importance to a matter. Lack of usefulness or significance in a situation. Something that is not related to the subject under discussion. The condition of no longer mattering to people.
example_sentence: The irrelevance of his argument was obvious to everyone. She dismissed the question because of its irrelevance. The party has slipped into political irrelevance. Do not waste time on such irrelevances.

english_meaning: Not connected with or important to the matter being discussed. Having no bearing on the subject or situation. Not useful or significant in a particular context. Unimportant in relation to what is being considered.
example_sentence: His comments were completely irrelevant to the discussion. Please leave out any irrelevant details. Age is irrelevant when judging this competition. The lawyer objected that the question was irrelevant.

english_meaning: In a way that has no connection with the subject. Without any bearing on the matter being discussed. In an unimportant or unrelated manner. Off the point, especially when speaking or writing.
example_sentence: He spoke irrelevantly about matters no one had asked about. She irrelevantly mentioned her holiday during the report. The witness answered irrelevantly several times. Do not comment irrelevantly during the meeting.

english_meaning: Impossible to repair, restore, or put right. Beyond recovery or fixing. Permanent and lasting in nature. Causing damage that cannot be undone. Used for harm, loss, or injury that is so severe that no remedy, compensation, or correction can fully restore the original state.
example_sentence: The earthquake caused irreparable damage to the ancient buildings. His careless words did irreparable harm to their friendship. The factory suffered an irreparable loss in the fire. Pollution is causing irreparable damage to the environment. The accident left him with an irreparable injury.

english_meaning: Too valuable or unique to be replaced by something else. Impossible to substitute with an equivalent. One of a kind and indispensable. Having such special value that nothing else can fill its place. Not able to be duplicated or replicated.
example_sentence: The irreplaceable antique vase was kept in a secure glass case. She was an irreplaceable member of the research team. The photographs were irreplaceable memories of his childhood. Some ecosystems are irreplaceable and must be preserved at all costs. His mentor's guidance was irreplaceable in shaping his career.

english_meaning: Beyond criticism or blame. So good that no fault can be found. Completely honest and morally faultless. Perfect in behaviour, manners, or quality. Free from any wrongdoing or error.
example_sentence: His conduct throughout the inquiry was irreproachable. She has an irreproachable record of public service. The hotel offered irreproachable service to its guests. He was chosen because of his irreproachable honesty.

english_meaning: Showing or feeling hesitancy. Uncertain about how to act or proceed. Lacking firmness of decision or purpose. Wavering and indecisive. Used to describe a person who finds it difficult to make up their mind or to stick to a chosen plan of action.
example_sentence: His irresolute attitude cost the team a clear victory. She felt irresolute about leaving her hometown. An irresolute leader cannot inspire confidence in others. He stood irresolute at the doorway, unsure whether to enter. The committee remained irresolute on the matter for months.

english_meaning: Without taking something into account or being influenced by it. Regardless of a particular fact, condition, or circumstance. Not affected by or dependent on the thing mentioned. Used to show that something applies equally in all cases.
synonyms: ["Regardless of","Without regard to","No matter","Notwithstanding","Despite","In spite of","Whatever","Disregarding","Apart from","Aside from"]
antonyms: ["Depending on","Subject to","Conditional on","Because of","According to","Influenced by","Contingent on","Determined by","Based on","In view of"]
example_sentence: The scholarship is open to all students irrespective of their background. Everyone must follow the rules irrespective of rank. Irrespective of the weather, the match will begin on time. The policy applies to all employees irrespective of their years of service.

english_meaning: Impossible to get back, recover, or put right again. Permanently lost or damaged beyond repair. Describing a situation or relationship that cannot be restored to its former state. Not able to be recovered even with great effort.
example_sentence: The court ruled that the marriage had suffered an irretrievable breakdown. Deleting the file caused an irretrievable loss of data. The damage to the old manuscript is irretrievable. Their friendship reached an irretrievable point after the quarrel.

english_meaning: Lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously. Disrespectful behavior or attitude. Failure to show due honor, especially towards religion or authority.
example_sentence: His irreverence toward tradition upset the elders. The comedian is known for his irreverence. She spoke with a certain irreverence about politics. Irreverence in a place of worship is unacceptable. His irreverence made the meeting uncomfortable.

english_meaning: A substance or thing that causes irritation or annoyance. Something that provokes anger or discomfort. A physical agent that inflames the skin or eyes. A minor but persistent source of trouble.
example_sentence: Smoke can be a serious irritant to the eyes. Loud music was an irritant to the neighbors. Certain chemicals act as skin irritants. Constant interruptions were an irritant during the meeting.

english_meaning: To make someone annoyed or impatient. To cause slight anger or frustration. To provoke an unpleasant reaction in a person. To disturb or bother someone persistently. To create a feeling of discomfort or impatience in another.
example_sentence: Loud music from the neighbor's house began to irritate everyone on the street. His constant questions started to irritate the teacher. The scratchy fabric of the sweater irritated her sensitive skin. Waiting in long queues always seems to irritate him. It irritates me when people are consistently late for appointments.

english_meaning: Causing annoyance or impatience. Making someone feel slightly angry or frustrated. Bothering or disturbing in a persistent way. Tending to provoke an unpleasant reaction. Creating a sense of discomfort or impatience.
example_sentence: The irritating sound of the dripping faucet kept me awake all night. He has an irritating habit of interrupting conversations. The mosquito's irritating buzz made it impossible to concentrate. Her irritating remarks pushed everyone away from the discussion. The irritating delay at the airport caused passengers to complain.

english_meaning: The lower and rear part of the hip bone, on which the body rests when sitting. One of the three bones that fuse together to form the pelvis. The curved bone that forms the back and lower portion of the pelvic ring. A bone that gives attachment to several muscles of the thigh and buttock.
example_sentence: The weight of the body rests on the ischium when sitting. Hamstring muscles arise from a bony bump on the ischium. Prolonged sitting on hard surfaces can bruise the ischium. The ischium fuses with the ilium and pubis during adolescence.

english_meaning: A line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure. In physics, one of two or more atoms of different elements having the same mass number. A term used in meteorology to show pressure patterns.
example_sentence: Closely spaced isobars indicate strong winds. The forecaster explained the isobars on the chart. Argon and calcium can form an isobar pair. Students learned to read isobars in geography class.

english_meaning: One of two nuclides having the same difference between their number of neutrons and protons. A nuclear physics term describing atoms related by an equal neutron excess. A classification used when comparing nuclides after alpha decay.
example_sentence: Uranium-238 and thorium-234 form an isodiapher pair. The lecturer defined isodiapher with a clear example. Isodiapher relationships appear during alpha decay. Students often confuse isodiapher with isotope.

english_meaning: Having the same number of electrons or the same electronic structure. Describing atoms, ions, or molecules whose electron arrangements are identical. Used in chemistry to compare species with matching electron counts.
example_sentence: Sodium ions and neon atoms are isoelectronic. The teacher asked us to list isoelectronic species. Isoelectronic molecules often have similar shapes. Carbon monoxide and nitrogen gas are isoelectronic.

english_meaning: A line drawn on a map separating areas where different linguistic features are used. It marks the boundary between two regions that differ in pronunciation, vocabulary, or grammar. Used in dialectology and sociolinguistics to study geographical distribution of language variation.
antonyms: ["Unified speech area","homogeneous dialect zone","standard language region"]
example_sentence: The isogloss between these two villages separates speakers who say house and hoose. Linguists plotted an isogloss showing where rhotic pronunciation ends. An isogloss map reveals how dialect boundaries follow rivers and mountains. The boundary line called an isogloss helps trace historical language change.

english_meaning: To set someone or something apart from others; to separate. To keep a person alone or away from social contact. To identify and separate something, such as a virus or substance, for study. To cause someone to feel alone or cut off.
example_sentence: The doctor isolated the patient to prevent the infection from spreading. Scientists isolated the virus in the laboratory. He felt isolated in the new city without friends. The police isolated the area after the explosion.

english_meaning: The state of being separated from others or being alone. The condition of being kept apart, especially to prevent disease. A feeling of loneliness or being cut off from society. The process of separating something for examination.
example_sentence: The patient was kept in isolation for two weeks. Living in isolation can harm mental health. The isolation of the compound took several months. The mountain village exists in almost complete isolation.

english_meaning: Tending to isolate or separate from others. Characterized by a desire to be alone or apart. Relating to keeping things or people separated from external influences. Having the quality of insulation or detachment. Causing or promoting isolation.
example_sentence: His isolative behavior worried his family and friends. The isolative properties of the material make it ideal for soundproofing. She had an isolative personality that made teamwork difficult. The isolative environment of the laboratory protected the experiments from contamination. The isolative nature of the job led to feelings of loneliness.

english_meaning: A molecule that has the same chemical formula as another molecule but a different structural arrangement. A compound with identical atoms but different spatial organization. One of two or more substances with the same molecular formula but different properties. A chemical species that shares the same number and type of atoms as another but differs in configuration. A structural or stereochemical variant of a compound.
antonyms: ["Different compound","Distinct molecule","Non-isomer","Unrelated chemical","Different formula","Heterologue","Contrast species","Foreign compound","Alien molecule","Unrelated substance"]
example_sentence: The chemist studied the isomer to understand its unique properties. Glucose and fructose are isomers with the same formula but different structures. The two isomers react differently despite having identical compositions. Identifying the correct isomer is crucial for drug development. Each isomer of the compound exhibited distinct physical characteristics.

english_meaning: The existence of two or more compounds with the same formula but different structures. A chemical property in which molecules share a formula yet differ in arrangement of atoms. The relationship between isomers of a substance. In nuclear physics, the existence of atomic nuclei in different energy states. The general phenomenon of same composition but different properties.
example_sentence: Isomerism explains why two sugars can taste completely different. The teacher used models to demonstrate isomerism in organic compounds. Optical isomerism is important in the design of new medicines. Butane and isobutane are a classic example of isomerism.

english_meaning: Having the same or similar form, shape, or structure. Corresponding in form and structural relations. Related in appearance or organization despite different origins. In biology, having similar structures in different species due to common ancestry. In mathematics, related by an isomorphism preserving structure.
example_sentence: The two species are isomorphic in their skeletal structures. The isomorphic relationship between the groups was proven mathematically. Isomorphic crystals can form under similar pressure conditions. The biologist compared isomorphic organs in different vertebrates. The isomorphic mapping preserved all the algebraic properties.

english_meaning: A triangle that has two sides of equal length. A triangle with two equal angles opposite the equal sides. A symmetrical three-sided figure in geometry. A shape often used in design because of its balance.
example_sentence: An isosceles triangle has two sides of equal length. The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. She folded the paper into an isosceles triangle. The roof was designed as an isosceles triangle.

english_meaning: A term for molecules or ions that have the same number of atoms and the same number of valence electrons, also written as isostere. A compound showing similar physical properties because of a similar electronic arrangement. A concept used in chemistry and drug design to compare similar structures.
example_sentence: Carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide are classic isoster examples. Chemists use isoster relationships to predict properties. The drug designer replaced a group with a suitable isoster. An isoster often shows similar boiling behaviour.

english_meaning: A line on a map connecting points that have the same temperature. A curve on a graph showing changes at constant temperature. A term used in geography, physics, and chemistry for equal-temperature conditions.
example_sentence: The map shows isotherms across the northern region. An isotherm marks places with identical temperatures. The experiment produced a smooth isotherm. Geographers use isotherms to compare climates.

english_meaning: Having the same osmotic pressure as another solution, especially a body fluid. Referring to a solution in which the concentration of dissolved particles equals that inside a cell, so there is no net movement of water across the cell membrane. Also used to describe muscle contraction in which tension remains constant while the muscle changes length.
example_sentence: The doctor administered an isotonic saline solution to rehydrate the patient. Isotonic sports drinks help replace lost fluids and electrolytes during exercise. In an isotonic contraction, the muscle shortens while maintaining steady tension. Red blood cells remain normal in shape when placed in an isotonic medium.

english_meaning: One of two or more forms of an element having the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. A variant of a chemical element with a different atomic mass. A form of an atom used in medicine, dating, and research.
example_sentence: Carbon has several isotopes, including carbon-14. Doctors use a radioactive isotope to trace blood flow. Scientists dated the fossil using a stable isotope. Each isotope of hydrogen behaves slightly differently.

english_meaning: The act of supplying or distributing something for official use. The formal act of making something available to the public or a specific group. A process of publishing or releasing a document or currency. The official delivery of documents like passports or licenses.
example_sentence: The issuance of new passports has been delayed due to technical issues. The company announced the issuance of new shares to the public. Strict guidelines govern the issuance of driving licenses in the state. The timely issuance of the final report helped in resolving the dispute.

english_meaning: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas, usually with water on either side. A thin land bridge that connects two larger landmasses while separating two bodies of water. It is important in geography and often serves as a route for transportation, trade, or strategic purposes.
example_sentence: The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America. Ancient civilizations often built cities along an isthmus for trade advantages. The soldiers defended the narrow isthmus against enemy forces. Ships pass through the canal that cuts across the isthmus.

word: It takes one to know one
english_meaning: A person who recognizes a particular bad quality in someone else often has that quality themselves. The expression is usually used as a humorous or defensive reply to an insult.
synonyms: ["Pot calling the kettle black","Hypocrite","Self-accusation","Tit for tat"]
example_sentence: “You are being selfish.” “It takes one to know one,” she replied with a smile. He called me a gossip, but it takes one to know one. The phrase “it takes one to know one” turned the insult into a joke. When the critic accused others of laziness, someone whispered, “It takes one to know one.”

word: It takes two to make a quarrel
english_meaning: A quarrel or fight usually happens because both sides contribute to the disagreement. One person alone cannot continue an argument if the other refuses to participate. Arguments grow when both people react emotionally. Disagreements need participation from both sides. Peace can be maintained if one person stays calm. Shared anger often creates conflict.
synonyms: ["Both sides are responsible","It takes two to tango","Conflict needs participation from both sides","Mutual disagreement","Shared responsibility in conflict"]
example_sentence: Ahmed and Ali kept insulting each other in class because it takes two to make a quarrel. My teacher advised us to stay calm during arguments because it takes two to make a quarrel. The neighbors finally realized that it takes two to make a quarrel and decided to solve the issue peacefully. Sara ignored the rude comments, proving that it takes two to make a quarrel.

english_meaning: A situation or conflict usually involves two people, and both are responsible for it. Many actions, arguments, relationships, or problems cannot happen because of just one person. Both sides contribute, so both share responsibility. It is often used when blaming or explaining a disagreement or situation involving two people.
synonyms: ["Both sides are responsible","It needs cooperation from both sides","Shared responsibility","Two-way involvement"]
antonyms: ["One-sided responsibility","Only one person is guilty","Single-handed effort","One-way action"]
example_sentence: The couple keeps blaming each other, but it takes two to tango. If the project failed, remember it takes two to tango between manager and worker. Don’t blame only him for the fight; it takes two to tango. In every argument, it takes two to tango, so both should reflect on their actions.

english_meaning: I do not understand it at all. Used when something is confusing, unclear or impossible to understand because it feels like a foreign language. Used to express total lack of understanding. Sometimes said jokingly when someone uses big or complicated words. Can refer to any unfamiliar subject or skill.
synonyms: ["I cannot make sense of it","I do not get it","It makes no sense to me","It is confusing"]
antonyms: ["I understand it clearly","It makes perfect sense","I get it","I follow it"]
example_sentence: I tried reading the report but the technical terms made it all Greek to me. When he explained the math formula, it was all Greek to me. The computer code looks Greek to me because I have never learned programming. She talked about astronomy and to me it was all Greek.

english_meaning: An uncomfortable sensation on the skin that causes a desire to scratch. It can also refer to a restless desire or strong urge to do something or go somewhere. To feel or cause this sensation.
example_sentence: The mosquito bite caused a persistent itch on my arm. I have been feeling an itch to travel across Europe this summer. Wearing that wool sweater always makes her skin itch. He had an itch to tell the secret but managed to keep quiet.

english_meaning: To repeat. To say or do something repeatedly. To repeat a process or action, often to improve or refine it.
example_sentence: The designer iterated the app interface until it looked perfect. Software developers iterate their code to fix bugs and improve performance. The teacher iterated the instructions to ensure every student understood. During the meeting, she iterated her key points several times.

english_meaning: The process of repeating something, usually to improve it or reach a desired outcome. A single repetition or version in a sequence of attempts. In computing, a step in a loop or repeated process. An instance of doing something again in a systematic way.
example_sentence: The software went through several iterations before the final version was released. Each iteration of the design improved user experience. The teacher asked the student to review his essay after the first iteration. In programming, an iteration refers to one complete cycle of a loop.

english_meaning: Traveling from place to place, especially for work. Traveling worker. Wandering person. Nomadic professional. Moving preacher or teacher. Someone who moves regularly from one location to another, often without staying long, usually for employment, trade, or duty
example_sentence: The itinerant doctor visited remote villages every week. He worked as an itinerant photographer across the country. The itinerant vendor sold snacks in different towns. An itinerant teacher taught students in rural areas.

english_meaning: A planned route or schedule of a journey. A document or plan that outlines the sequence of places to visit, activities to do, and the timing of each step during a trip. It helps travelers organize their journey efficiently.
example_sentence: I shared my travel itinerary with my colleagues before the business trip. The tour company provided a detailed itinerary of all the attractions in Paris. We followed the itinerary carefully to ensure we didn’t miss any sights. She keeps a digital itinerary to track her flights and hotel bookings.

english_meaning: A small green vegetable that grows on a climbing vine. A tropical plant whose fruit is used both raw and cooked. A vegetable known for its crisp texture and mild flavor. A gourd often stir-fried with spices, potatoes, or coconut. A plant valued in traditional medicine, especially for diabetes.
example_sentence: Ivy gourd is often cooked with potatoes and mild spices. She sliced the ivy gourds and fried them with onions. Ivy gourd is known to help control blood sugar. Many South Indian dishes are made using ivy gourd.

english_meaning: To poke, hit, or prod quickly, often repeatedly, usually with a finger, stick, or object. To criticize, tease, mock, or make sharp comments about someone or something repeatedly.
example_sentence: He jabbed at the rope. She jabbed at the paper. He jabbed at the target. I jabbed at the button.

english_meaning: To push or poke something quickly and forcefully into something else. To thrust or poke an object, often a tool or needle, quickly and sharply into a surface, body, or material. It can be used literally (physically jabbing) or figuratively (inserting words or comments abruptly).
example_sentence: He jabbed in the key. She jabbed in the needle. I jabbed in the card. He jabbed in the pin.

english_meaning: To push, poke, or hit suddenly into something or someone. To a quick or sudden thrust, poke, or collision, either physically or metaphorically,
example_sentence: He jabbed into the box. She jabbed into the pile. He jabbed into the soil. I jabbed into the wall.

english_meaning: To punch, strike, or thrust suddenly; often in boxing or a quick action. To make a quick, sharp punch or thrust, usually with the hand in sports like boxing, or metaphorically, to express something suddenly or forcefully.
example_sentence: The boxer jabbed out with his left hand. She jabbed out at the target during practice. He jabbed out a comment during the meeting. The child jabbed out at the balloon playfully.

english_meaning: To inject someone with a vaccine or medicine. To give a quick shot of a drug for treatment or prevention. In informal use, it refers to getting vaccinated. To push, poke or hit upward with a quick motion, usually with a hand, stick or object.
example_sentence: He jabbed up the lever. She jabbed up the button. I jabbed up the stick. The nurse jabbed up the syringe.

english_meaning: A person who can do many different kinds of work reasonably well. Someone who has skills in a wide variety of tasks but is not an expert in any single one. A versatile worker who can turn a hand to almost any job. Often used in the fuller saying 'a jack of all trades, master of none' to suggest broad but shallow ability.
example_sentence: My uncle is a jack of all trades and can fix almost anything in the house. She is a jack of all trades, handling design, writing and accounts on her own. Small startups often need a jack of all trades rather than a specialist. He is a jack of all trades, master of none, but that suits this job perfectly.

english_meaning: To raise something using a jack, to increase suddenly (price or rate).
example_sentence: The mechanic jacked up the car. They jacked up the prices overnight. You can jack up the table to adjust height. The rent was jacked up last month.

english_meaning: A very large tropical fruit with a spiky green rind and sweet yellow bulbs inside. The largest tree-borne fruit, often used ripe as a dessert or unripe as a vegetable. The tall tree that produces this fruit. A fibrous meat substitute made from the unripe fruit.
example_sentence: A single jackfruit can weigh more than ten kilograms. Unripe jackfruit is cooked as a curry in many homes. The ripe jackfruit filled the room with its sweet smell. Jackfruit is often used as a meat substitute.

english_meaning: A large prize or unexpected success. The most valuable prize in a game or lottery, especially when the game involves increasing the value of the prize until someone wins it.
example_sentence: She hit the jackpot and won a million dollars in the lottery. Landing that contract was a real jackpot for the company. He felt like he hit the jackpot when he found a rare book in the market. Their new app became a jackpot, attracting millions of users in a month.

english_meaning: To make someone tired or annoyed. To wear someone out through repeated effort, pressure, or annoyance. Person or animal that is worn out or exhausted due to hard use.
example_sentence: The long hours of work jad him completely. Constant complaints can jad even the most patient person. The old horse was a jad after years of hard labor. Repeating the same argument began to jad the team.

english_meaning: Feeling tired, bored, or no longer interested due to too much experience. A person who has lost enthusiasm, excitement, or freshness because of overuse, repeated experiences, or emotional exhaustion.
example_sentence: After years of the same job, he felt jaded and unmotivated. She looked jaded after attending too many social events. The traveler was jaded by constant delays and long journeys. He sounded jaded when talking about politics.

english_meaning: Unrefined natural sugar made from sugarcane juice or palm sap, usually brown in color, used widely in Asia and Africa for cooking and sweetening. It is less processed than white sugar and retains more minerals.
example_sentence: Jaggery is often used to make traditional sweets in South Asia. Many people prefer jaggery over refined sugar because it is more natural. Adding a small piece of jaggery to tea gives it a rich, earthy flavor. Farmers produce jaggery by boiling sugarcane juice in large pans.

english_meaning: To press or apply something suddenly and forcefully (for example brakes). To push or press forcefully or to continue an activity with full effort.
example_sentence: The driver jammed on the brakes to avoid hitting the dog. She jammed on the accelerator and the car moved forward quickly. The mechanic jammed the cover on the machine to protect it. When the fire alarm rang, he jammed on the emergency switch.

english_meaning: A person employed to clean and maintain a building. A caretaker responsible for minor repairs, security, heating, supplies, and general upkeep. In some varieties of English, a doorkeeper or building custodian.
example_sentence: The janitor cleaned the classrooms after the students left. We asked the janitor to repair the broken door handle. The building's janitor keeps the hallways spotless. A janitor unlocked the gym early in the morning. She worked as a school janitor for twenty years.

english_meaning: Special words or expressions used by a particular group or profession. These words are often difficult for others to understand. It is language that feels technical or specialized.
example_sentence: The doctor used medical jargon that the patient could not follow. Legal jargon often confuses people who are not trained in law. Tech experts sometimes forget how strange their jargon sounds to beginners. The report was full of business jargon that made it hard to read.

english_meaning: Inharmonious or harsh to the senses. Producing a sudden, unpleasant effect. Causing a shock or disturbance because of incongruity. Making a rough, discordant sound. Strikingly unpleasant or conflicting in appearance or tone.
example_sentence: The jarring noise from the construction site made it hard to concentrate. There was a jarring contrast between her cheerful words and sad expression. The jarring colors of the painting disturbed many viewers. His sudden jarring laugh surprised everyone in the quiet room. The jarring transition between scenes confused the audience.

english_meaning: A dark purple fruit native to South Asia, also known as jamun. A tropical fruit with sweet-sour flesh and medicinal value. A fruit that stains the tongue purple when eaten. A summer fruit used in juices and desserts. A traditional remedy for diabetes and digestive issues.
example_sentence: Java plums are widely eaten during the summer season. My mother makes delicious juice from Java plums. Java plum seeds are used in herbal medicines. He enjoyed a bowl of fresh Java plums after lunch.

english_meaning: Either of the two bony structures of the face that hold the teeth and form the framework of the mouth. The lower part of the face that moves when a person chews or speaks. A pair of gripping parts in a tool or machine, such as a vice or wrench. To talk at length in an informal way.
example_sentence: He broke his jaw in a cycling accident. The dog held the stick firmly in its jaws. Her jaw dropped when she saw the surprise party. They sat jawing about old times for hours.

english_meaning: To talk continuously or idly about something.
example_sentence: They sat jawing away for hours. Stop jawing away and listen. The men were jawing away about politics. She kept jawing away during class.

english_meaning: Move energetically. To move, behave, or perform in a lively or playful manner. To move around energetically, casually, or aimlessly, often having fun.
example_sentence: The kids were jazzing around in the garden. He jazzed around the stage before the show. Musicians jazzed around the studio while recording. They jazzed around the park playing games.

english_meaning: Leave quickly. To leave or go away quickly, often abruptly. To leave quickly or tell someone to go away. Often informal and casual.
example_sentence: He jazzed off after the meeting ended. She jazzed off to catch her train. They jazzed off when it started raining. I need to jazz off before traffic gets worse.

english_meaning: To make something more lively, attractive, or exciting.
example_sentence: Let’s jazz up this room with colors. He jazzed up his outfit with a hat. The band jazzed up the old tune. She jazzed up the speech with humor.

english_meaning: Feeling resentment because someone else has something you want. Suspicious or protective of a loved one's affection. Envious of another person's success or possessions. Fiercely protective of one's rights or possessions. Feeling insecure about a relationship.
example_sentence: He felt jealous of his brother's new car. She became jealous when her friend received a promotion. The child was jealous of the attention given to the new baby. He is jealous of his reputation and works hard to maintain it.

english_meaning: A feeling of resentment towards someone because of their advantages or success. Fear or anger caused by the belief that a loved one may prefer someone else. Envy of another person's possessions, qualities, or achievements. A protective and possessive attitude towards what one has.
example_sentence: Her success stirred jealousy among some colleagues. Jealousy slowly destroyed their friendship. He could not hide his jealousy when she won the prize. Constant jealousy makes any relationship difficult.

english_meaning: To laugh at someone or shout rude remarks to insult, mock, or show disrespect. A rude remark or insulting shout. Expressing contempt or ridicule toward someone, often in a loud or public way. It is commonly used in situations like crowds reacting negatively to a performer, speaker, or player. It shows disrespect and lack of approval.
example_sentence: The crowd began to jeer when the actor forgot his lines. Students should not jeer at their classmates during presentations. The fans jeered at the referee after the bad decision. It is rude to jeer at someone who is trying their best.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or located in the jejunum, which is the middle section of the small intestine. Relating to the anatomical part of the digestive tract situated between the duodenum and the ileum. Specifically identifying biological processes, tissues, or fluids originating from the central small bowel. Describing surgical procedures or medical instruments applied to the second portion of the small intestine.
example_sentence: The patient required a jejunal feeding tube due to severe gastric issues. The surgeon noted a small lesion on the jejunal wall during the laparoscopy. Nutritional absorption primarily occurs across the jejunal mucosa. The biopsy results confirmed a jejunal inflammatory response.

english_meaning: Naive, simplistic, or lacking maturity and experience. Dull, boring, or lacking interest and substance. Intellectually unsatisfying or superficial. Immature and childish in nature or expression.
example_sentence: His arguments were jejune and unconvincing. The film was criticized for its jejune dialogue. She dismissed the essay as jejune and shallow. The lecture felt jejune to the experienced audience.

english_meaning: The middle segment of the small intestine situated between the duodenum and the ileum. A long, coiled section of the digestive tract where the majority of nutrient absorption takes place. The part of the small bowel characterized by a larger diameter and thicker walls compared to the ileum. The anatomical region of the intestine that utilizes villi and microvilli to transport nutrients into the bloodstream. The portion of the alimentary canal extending from the duodenojejunal flexure to the beginning of the ileum.
synonyms: ["Middle Small Intestine","Mid-gut","Digestive Tube Section","Alimentary Segment","Intestinal Tract","Bowel Segment","Nutrient Absorber","Small Bowel","Mid-intestine","Enteron Part","Visceral Tube","Gut Portion"]
example_sentence: The surgeon examined the jejunum for any signs of obstruction during the procedure. Most of the nutrients from the food we eat are absorbed in the jejunum. The jejunum has a rich blood supply which gives it a deep red color in living subjects. Unlike the ileum, the jejunum typically contains fewer Peyer's patches.

english_meaning: A person with a dual personality that alternates between good and evil behavior. A literary allusion to someone who appears kind but hides a dark or destructive side. A character or situation marked by unpredictable and extreme contradictions in temperament. Someone who experiences a split personality or a profound psychological struggle between moral opposites.
example_sentence: His coworkers were terrified of his Jekyll and Hyde personality when he was under pressure. The politician was a true Jekyll and Hyde, charming in public but cruel behind closed doors. She found it difficult to maintain a relationship with someone who had such a Jekyll and Hyde temperament. The city itself has a Jekyll and Hyde quality, with beautiful parks right next to decaying slums.

english_meaning: To put something or someone in danger, risk, or the possibility of loss or harm. It means to endanger, to expose to danger or harm, or to risk something valuable.
example_sentence: It can even jeopardise the whole operation. However, if you stop payments you may jeopardise future benefits. Why would he jeopardise his future by taking unauthorized drugs? You will not jeopardise that job I perjured myself to get for you by a vagrancy charge tonight of all nights.

english_meaning: To put something or someone in danger, risk, or the possibility of loss or harm. It means to endanger, to expose to danger or harm, or to risk something valuable.
example_sentence: He would never do anything to jeopardize his career. This scandal could seriously jeopardize his chances of being re-elected. She knew that by failing her finals she could jeopardize her whole future. The rate increase may jeopardize economic recovery. He jeopardized his life every time he dived from the tower.

english_meaning: A state of danger, risk, or exposure to harm or loss. The possibility of being injured, damaged, or destroyed. Often used to describe situations where safety, success, or life is at risk.
example_sentence: For a moment his life was in jeopardy. The spy was in constant jeopardy of being discovered. Thousands of jobs are in jeopardy. The deal could be in jeopardy if it emerges the company is engaged in activities prohibited by the US government. The 1.2 billion euro investment programme was being put in jeopardy by the strikes. Bad investments have put the company’s future in jeopardy. The lives of thousands of birds are in jeopardy as a result of the oil spill. The city's firefighters routinely put their lives in jeopardy by executing daring rescue.

english_meaning: A lengthy, mournful complaint or lamentation. A prolonged expression of grief or sorrow. A complaint or criticism presented as a sorrowful prophecy. A doleful tirade about society's problems. A lament or grievance delivered in a tone of deep sadness.
example_sentence: The politician's speech turned into a jeremiad about the decline of moral values. His jeremiad about modern technology lasted for nearly an hour. The book is a jeremiad against the corruption in the government. She delivered a jeremiad about the loss of community spirit. The editorial was a jeremiad lamenting the state of public education.

english_meaning: To pull, push, or move something suddenly or abruptly. A sudden, sharp movement. A rude or unpleasant person.
example_sentence: He jerked the door open. She jerked the rope to free it. The car jerked forward unexpectedly. I felt a jerk when the train started. The sudden jerk of the cable broke it. Don’t be a jerk and help out.

english_meaning: Sudden, uneven, or irregular movements. Dried meat. Characterized by quick, abrupt, and uneven motions. Meat that has been cut into strips and dried.
example_sentence: The car came to a jerky stop at the traffic light. His speech was jerky, making it hard to follow. I like to snack on beef jerky during hiking. The video froze, and the movement became jerky.

english_meaning: A thing said or done for amusement or to cause laughter. A joke or witty remark. A playful or humorous action. Something not intended to be taken seriously. A humorous anecdote or quip intended to entertain.
example_sentence: His witty jest made everyone at the dinner table laugh. She said it in jest, but her friend took it seriously. The court jester's jest entertained the king and his guests. He could not resist a jest even during serious meetings. The conversation was filled with light jest and friendly banter.

english_meaning: A movement or gesture of the body or limbs to express an idea or emotion. A physical action used to communicate nonverbally. A pose or motion intended to convey meaning. An expressive movement made with the hands, arms, or face. A bodily action accompanying or replacing speech.
example_sentence: His jesture of raising his hand indicated he wanted to speak. She made a welcoming jesture by opening her arms wide. The actor used a dramatic jesture to emphasize his lines. A simple jesture can sometimes communicate more than words. The teacher's jesture pointed toward the correct answer on the board.

english_meaning: A rapid stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening. A type of aircraft powered by jet engines. A dense black mineral used for jewelry. To travel by jet aircraft. To spurt or shoot out in a stream.
example_sentence: The jet of water from the fountain reached ten feet high. She flew across the Atlantic in a private jet. The jet black stone was polished and set into a ring. The volcano sent a jet of molten rock into the air. He plans to jet off to Paris for the weekend.

english_meaning: A very deep, glossy black colour, like that of the mineral jet. Describing hair, fur, or objects that are intensely black and shining. Completely dark, with no light at all.
example_sentence: She has long jet black hair. The cat's jet black coat shone in the sunlight. He drove a jet black car. The room was jet black once the lamp went out.

english_meaning: To travel quickly by airplane, usually to another city or country. It can also carry a sense of leaving suddenly or in a hurry.
example_sentence:
She’s jetting off to Dubai for a business trip. 
He suddenly jetted off without saying goodbye. They jetted off to Paris right after the wedding. I wish I could jet off to some peaceful island right now.

english_meaning: Extremely black in color. Something that is very dark black with no visible lighter shade, often used to emphasize depth and intensity of black color.
example_sentence: She has jet-black hair that shines in the sunlight. The night sky looked jet-black without the moon. He wore a jet-black suit to the formal event. Smoke rose in a jet-black cloud after the fire.

english_meaning: To throw away or get rid of something that is no longer needed, especially to reduce weight or avoid trouble. To deliberately discard something, often suddenly and for a practical reason. It is commonly used for throwing cargo from a ship or aircraft to make it lighter or safer. In modern usage, it also refers to abandoning plans, ideas, policies, or responsibilities that are causing problems or are no longer useful. The act of throwing away goods or cargo, especially from a ship or aircraft.
example_sentence: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to make a safe landing. The company decided to jettison its outdated policies. During the storm, the crew jettisoned heavy cargo from the ship. She chose to jettison negative habits to improve her life. The jettison of cargo saved the aircraft from crashing. Emergency jettison is practiced during pilot training. The captain ordered the jettison of heavy containers.

english_meaning: A landing stage or small pier at which boats can dock. A structure that projects from the land into the water to protect a harbour or influence a current.
example_sentence: The boat was tied to the wooden jetty. We walked along the jetty to see the sunset. A new jetty has been built for the ferry service. Children were fishing from the jetty. The storm damaged the jetty badly.

english_meaning: To be in accord or to agree with something. It also means to make mocking or insulting remarks. In a nautical context, it refers to shifting a sail from one side of a vessel to the other while sailing before the wind.
example_sentence: The witnesses' stories did not jibe with the evidence found at the crime scene. He couldn't help but jibe at his rival's failure during the public debate. Her sunny disposition doesn't quite jibe with the somber mood of the meeting. The sailors had to jibe the mainsail quickly as the wind direction suddenly shifted.

english_meaning: A very short period of time. An instant or moment. A brief span of time. A colloquial term for a short while. An informal word for a split second.
example_sentence: Wait here, I will be back in a jiff. The message was sent in a jiff using the new app. I will finish this task in a jiff. She promised to return in a jiff but took an hour. The computer restarted in a jiff after the update.

english_meaning: A very short space of time. An extremely brief moment. Informal term for an instant. A quick or rapid interval. A split second or a flash of time.
example_sentence: I will be ready in a jiffy. The soup will heat up in a jiffy. She solved the puzzle in a jiffy. The package arrived in a jiffy thanks to express delivery. He fixed the error in a jiffy and continued working.

english_meaning: To perform a trick or cunning maneuver. To dance, move, or shift quickly with a jerky motion. To move or shake slightly, often repeatedly. A lively musical composition used for dancing. A device to guide or hold workpieces for precise cutting, drilling, or shaping. A type of lure or weighted hook that moves up and down to attract fish.
example_sentence: She learned a traditional Irish jig at the festival. The children jiggled with excitement when they saw the gifts. He set up a jig to hold the metal in place while welding. The puppy jiggled its tail happily.

english_meaning: Deceitful or dishonest behavior aimed at tricking someone. Underhanded or suspicious manipulation used to gain an unfair advantage. Sly or secretive maneuvering designed to conceal the truth. Fraudulent or tricky conduct in business, legal, or political affairs.
example_sentence: There was a lot of jiggery-pokery involved in hiding the company's financial losses. The voters suspected some jiggery-pokery behind the sudden change in election rules. He claimed the contract was signed fairly without any jiggery-pokery. She refused to tolerate any jiggery-pokery in her business transactions.

english_meaning: To move or shake lightly up and down or from side to side. To cause a small, quick, and repeated movement, usually shaking slightly in a playful or careless way. Can also refer to causing something to move by shaking it.
example_sentence: She jiggled the key to unlock the door. The children jiggled with excitement. He jiggled the handle but the drawer wouldn’t open. The jelly jiggled on the plate.

english_meaning: To suddenly reject or abandon a lover. To end a romantic relationship callously. A person who rejects a lover.
example_sentence: She jilted her fiancé a week before the wedding. He was jilted by his longtime girlfriend. The jilted lover wrote sad poems. No one expected her to jilt him so suddenly.

english_meaning: Feelings of extreme nervousness or anxiety. A state of nervous unease. Slight, rapid, involuntary movements caused by nervousness. To feel anxious or act nervously. A technical term for small fluctuations in signal or image.
example_sentence: The jitter before the exam made it hard for her to sleep. He felt a jitter of excitement mixed with fear. The jitter in the video feed was caused by a poor internet connection. She tried to hide the jitter in her hands during the presentation. The caffeine gave him a slight jitter that lasted all morning.

english_meaning: Nervous and unable to relax. Feeling anxious so that the body shakes slightly. Easily frightened or made uneasy. Unsteady and restless because of worry. Describing markets or situations that are unstable and tense.
example_sentence: She felt jittery before her first interview. Too much coffee makes him jittery. The markets were jittery ahead of the announcement. He gave a jittery laugh and looked away.

english_meaning: A blockhead or a naturally dull person. A stupid or foolish individual lacking intelligence. A clumsy or slow-witted fellow. A thick-headed person who is often the butt of a joke. A heavy, dull head or someone who possesses one. An archaic term for a simpleton or dolt.
example_sentence: The old farmer called the clumsy apprentice a jobbernowl for spilling the grain. He acted like a complete jobbernowl when he forgot his own house keys for the third time. The comedy featured a lovable jobbernowl who constantly misunderstood simple instructions. Don't be such a jobbernowl and pay attention to what you are doing.

english_meaning: Given to joking. Playful, humorous, or characterized by good-natured joking.
example_sentence: His jocose comments kept the office atmosphere light. The old professor was known for his jocose lectures. She gave a jocose wink before revealing the surprise. Even in difficult times, he remained jocose and cheerful.

english_meaning: Fond of joking and making people laugh. Humorous, playful, or lighthearted in manner or character.
example_sentence: He gave a jocular reply to lighten the tense mood. Her jocular tone made everyone smile. Despite the serious topic, his jocular manner put the audience at ease. The teacher's jocular remarks made the lesson enjoyable.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being humorous, playful, and fond of joking. A joking remark, manner, or instance of good-humored merriment.
example_sentence: The dinner was full of jocularity and laughter. His jocularity helped ease the tension in the room. Beneath her jocularity, she was actually quite anxious. The new employees were surprised by the meeting's jocularity.

english_meaning: In a joking, humorous, cheerful, or playful manner. In a way intended to amuse rather than be taken seriously.
example_sentence: He jocularly remarked that he would never cook again. She jocularly teased her brother about his new haircut. The coach jocularly warned the team not to celebrate too early. He spoke jocularly, although his advice was serious.

english_meaning: The place in the body where two or more bones meet and are held together. A structure that allows movement between bones, such as the knee, elbow, or hip. A point of connection between two parts of a structure or machine. Shared, held, or done by two or more people together. To join or connect parts together.
example_sentence: Cold weather makes the pain in her knee joint worse. The elbow is a hinge joint that bends in one direction. The carpenter sealed every joint in the wooden frame. They opened a joint account after getting married.

english_meaning: A legal provision made for a wife, usually giving her income or property after marriage or after her husband’s death. An estate, property, or fixed income settled on a wife by her husband, either before or during marriage, to support her during marriage or after his death instead of traditional dower rights.
example_sentence: The jointure ensured that she would not face financial hardship after her husband’s death. Under the marriage contract, a jointure was settled in her name. The court reviewed the jointure to confirm it complied with inheritance laws. In historical England, jointure often replaced traditional dower rights.

english_meaning: Happy and cheerful. Full of good humor and lively enjoyment. Pleasant and entertaining. To encourage or cheer someone along. A British informal term for a pleasant outing or event.
example_sentence: The jolly old man greeted everyone with a warm smile. We had a jolly time at the holiday party. Her jolly laughter filled the room with joy. The children were jolly after eating their ice cream. He tried to jolly his friend out of a bad mood with jokes.

english_meaning: Used to strongly emphasize that something will or did happen. Used to stress certainty, insistence, or sometimes irritation. It strengthens a statement, often making it more forceful or definite.
example_sentence: I’m going to finish this work, jolly well. She jolly well knew the answer but stayed quiet. He jolly well refused to sign the agreement. You can jolly well wait your turn.

english_meaning: To push roughly against somebody in a crowd. To come in contact or into collision. To make one's way by pushing and shoving. To force by pushing. The state of being crowded or pushed together.
example_sentence: The visiting president was jostled by angry demonstrators. People were jostling, arguing and complaining. The class giggled and jostled each other.

english_meaning: To write something quickly or in brief, usually notes, ideas, or information, to remember it or use later
example_sentence: I will jot down the address before I forget it. She jotted down the key points during the meeting. He jotted down his thoughts in a small notebook. Please jot down any questions you have for the lecturer.

english_meaning: A unit of energy or work in the International System of Units (SI). The amount of energy exerted when a force of one newton is applied over a displacement of one meter. One watt of power dissipated for one second. The work required to move an electric charge of one coulomb through an electrical potential difference of one volt. A measure of heat energy equivalent to approximately 0·239 calories. The energy stored in an electric field of a capacitor at specific parameters. A derived unit representing the capacity to do work.
synonyms: ["Energy Unit","Watt-second","Newton-meter","Work Unit","Calorific Measure","SI Unit","Metric Energy","Kinetic Unit","Potential Measure","Heat Quantity","Thermal Unit","Power Increment"]
example_sentence: The scientist calculated the energy output in joules to maintain accuracy in the experiment. One joule is a relatively small amount of energy in everyday domestic contexts. If you apply a force of one newton for one meter, you have performed one joule of work. The label on the battery indicates its total energy capacity measured in kilojoules.

english_meaning: An act of traveling from one place to another. A long and often difficult process of personal change and development. The distance covered or time taken in traveling. A trip made for a particular purpose. The passage or progress from one stage to another.
example_sentence: They set out on a long journey across the country. Life is a journey full of ups and downs. Her journey to success was inspiring. The journey by train takes about six hours.

english_meaning: Cheerful and friendly. A person who is full of happiness, good humor, and a friendly, sociable nature. It often implies a lively and positive spirit that makes others feel comfortable.
example_sentence: He was in a jovial mood. He seemed a very jovial guy. He addressed Molly in his usual jovial manner. It is a relationship that we have, he's very jovial, open and a lot of fun, but he's also very serious.

english_meaning: A feeling of supreme triumph and excessive happiness. It is typically a reaction to a great success, victory, or milestone achievement. It involves openly expressing great joy and celebration with others.
example_sentence: The entire crowded stadium erupted in deafening jubilance as the final whistle blew. Her bright face completely radiated undeniable jubilance when she saw the fantastic test results. The grand streets were totally filled with the loud jubilance of the celebrating citizens. Such immense jubilance naturally follows a incredibly long, difficult, and fought-for victory. No one could ignore the wild jubilance of the happy athletes embracing each other.

english_meaning: Feeling or expressing great happiness and joy, especially because of success or a happy event. Extremely joyful.
example_sentence: The team was jubilant after winning the championship. She felt jubilant when she received the award. The jubilant crowd cheered loudly during the celebration. He was jubilant at the news of his promotion.

english_meaning: To rejoice, celebrate, or show great happiness. To express joy loudly or publicly.
example_sentence: After winning the championship, the players jubilated in the stadium, waving to their fans. People jubilated when peace was finally restored in the country. The students jubilated after hearing that their school trip had been approved. Families jubilated together during the festival with music, dance, and laughter.

english_meaning: A feeling of great happiness, joy, and triumph. Public expression of celebration and delight. Exultation over success or victory. A state of rejoicing. The strong emotion of happiness shown openly when something very pleasing, successful, or long-awaited happens.
example_sentence: There was great jubilation in the city after the team won the championship. The announcement of independence was met with national jubilation. His face showed jubilation when he received the award. The crowd erupted in jubilation as the results were declared. Jubilation filled the hall when the project was finally approved.

word: Judge a book by its cover
english_meaning: Don’t judge by appearance. Don’t form an opinion about someone or something based only on appearance. The outer look doesn’t always reflect the true value or nature. Appearances can be misleading, true worth lies inside.
example_sentence: She looks shy, but don’t judge a book by its cover. She looks quiet, but she’s very talented, never judge a book by its cover. That small restaurant doesn’t look fancy, but the food is amazing, don’t judge a book by its cover. He seems rude at first, but once you know him, he’s very kind. Never judge a book by its cover. The old building looks broken, but inside it’s well-decorated, Don’t judge a book by its cover.

english_meaning: Relating to courts of law, judges, or the administration of justice. Ordered or decided by a court. Characteristic of a judge; showing fair and careful judgement. Connected with the legal process of hearing and deciding cases.
example_sentence: The judicial system must remain independent of political pressure. A judicial inquiry was ordered into the accident. She weighed the evidence with judicial calmness. Judicial reforms were introduced to speed up trials.

english_meaning: The system of courts that interprets and applies the law in a country. The branch of government responsible for administering justice. Judges collectively as a body. Matters relating to the judgment of legal cases. The judicial authority of a nation or state.
example_sentence: An independent judiciary is essential for democracy. The judiciary plays a key role in protecting citizens' rights. Reforms are needed to strengthen the country's judiciary. The judiciary ruled against the government's decision.

english_meaning: Showing good judgment and careful thinking. A person, action, or decision that is wise, balanced, and made after thoughtful consideration of facts and consequences. A judicious person avoids rash choices and acts with fairness and prudence.
example_sentence: He is judicious in his investments. She made a judicious investment in her business. She made a judicious decision to save money for the future. The teacher’s judicious advice helped the students choose their careers. A judicious use of resources can prevent waste. The manager was praised for his judicious handling of the conflict.

english_meaning: A huge, powerful, and overwhelming force or institution. Something that cannot be stopped or resisted. A massive object or movement that crushes everything in its path. An unstoppable destructive force. A person, group, or thing that is dominant and unstoppable.
example_sentence: The tech company became a juggernaut in the industry within a decade. The economic juggernaut of the region attracted global investors. Once started, the political campaign was a juggernaut. The sports team was a juggernaut, winning every game of the season. The floodwaters became a juggernaut that destroyed everything in their path.

english_meaning: To keep several objects such as balls in the air at the same time by throwing and catching them in a continuous pattern. To manage or handle several activities, tasks, or responsibilities at the same time. To try to balance different demands, especially with difficulty. To manipulate figures or facts in order to deceive.
example_sentence: The circus artist can juggle five balls at once. She has to juggle her job, studies, and family life every day. Working mothers often juggle multiple responsibilities. He was accused of juggling the company accounts to hide the losses. It is difficult to juggle so many appointments in a single day.

english_meaning: The liquid naturally contained in fruit, vegetables, or meat. A drink made from fruit or vegetable liquid. The flavorful liquid released from food during cooking. Informally, electricity, energy, power, influence, or vitality. Informally, alcohol, fuel, or performance-enhancing steroids. To extract juice from something. To add juice, energy, power, or excitement to something.
example_sentence: She squeezed fresh orange juice for breakfast. The battery ran out of juice halfway through the trip. His connections gave him enough juice to secure a meeting. Juice the lemons before adding the liquid to the sauce.

english_meaning: To make something more lively, exciting, attractive, powerful, or effective. To increase power, energy, speed, or performance. To stimulate or enliven a person or group.
example_sentence: The designers juiced up the old website with clearer images and livelier language. The mechanic juiced up the engine to improve its performance. A short pep talk juiced up the team before the final. The chef juiced up the bland sauce with fresh herbs and spices.

english_meaning: An interesting, exciting, or scandalous piece of information, often about someone's private life. A rich or entertaining bit of gossip. A colorful and vivid part of a story. An eagerly awaited piece of news.
example_sentence: She loves to share the juicy details of every wedding she attends. The reporter uncovered some juicy details about the scandal. Don't leave out the juicy details of your trip. Everyone was waiting to hear the juicy details of the meeting.

english_meaning: To push oneself off the ground into the air using the legs. To move suddenly and quickly from one place to another. To increase suddenly and by a large amount. To react with a sudden movement because of surprise or fear. To pass over something by leaping. An act of leaping. A sudden rise in amount or level.
example_sentence: The cat jumped over the wall easily. Prices have jumped sharply this month. She jumped when she heard the loud noise. The children love to jump on the trampoline. He took a huge jump forward in his career.

english_meaning: To move quickly forward, often skipping over intermediate steps or time. It can imply an advance in time or sequence, or a physical movement. This phrase suggests an abrupt or notable progression, potentially missing details in between.
example_sentence: Let's jump ahead to the conclusion of the report. The movie jumps ahead five years in the next scene. If we jump ahead, we might miss crucial details. She found it easier to jump ahead to the more challenging problems. I had to jump ahead in the book to find the answer.

english_meaning: To move or bounce around with energetic, usually uncontrolled, movements. This can refer to literal physical movement, often in a lively or excited manner. It can also metaphorically describe shifting between topics or ideas erratically, without a clear focus or direction.
example_sentence: The children love to jump around in the bouncy castle. He tends to jump around from topic to topic during his presentations. When the music started, everyone began to jump around energetically. The puppy was so excited that it couldn't stop jumping around everywhere. Let's just jump around and have some fun!

english_meaning: To accept an opportunity, offer, or chance eagerly and without hesitation. To take advantage of something immediately when it is offered.
example_sentence: She jumped at the chance to study abroad. He jumped at the offer of a promotion. Any student would jump at such a scholarship. I would jump at the opportunity to work with him. They jumped at the suggestion of a weekend trip.

english_meaning: To quickly move or spring backward from a position, often due to surprise, fear, or a sudden realization. It implies a swift, involuntary, or deliberate recoil.
example_sentence: She saw the snake and immediately jumped back. The sudden noise made him jump back in his seat. I had to jump back to avoid being hit by the swinging door. The boxer showed agility, jumping back to evade his opponent's punch. He jumped back from the edge of the cliff when he saw how far down it was.

english_meaning: To enter a place or vehicle quickly. To join a conversation or activity suddenly. To become involved in a situation without hesitation, often to help.
example_sentence: Jump in, I will give you a lift home. He jumped in whenever there was a chance to speak. Feel free to jump in if you have any questions. She jumped in to defend her brother. The teacher jumped in to explain the point.

english_meaning: To begin doing something with great energy and enthusiasm. To become involved in an activity or situation very quickly. To enter something such as water by leaping in.
synonyms: ["Plunge into","Dive into","Embark on","Throw oneself into","Start eagerly"]
example_sentence: She jumped into her new job with great enthusiasm. The children jumped into the swimming pool. Do not jump into a business without proper research. He jumped into the debate confidently. They jumped into action as soon as the alarm rang.

english_meaning: To jump off typically means to propel oneself into the air from a surface. It can refer to a literal physical act, like a person jumping off a diving board, or it can be used figuritively to mean to start a journey, an activity, or a discussion from a particular point or advantage.
