The authentic recipe requires alternating layers of lasagne sheets and rich meat sauce. He ordered a generous portion of classic meat lasagne at the newly opened Italian restaurant.

english_meaning: Feeling or revealing an overt and often offensive sexual desire. It describes behavior that is lewd, lustful, or driven by carnal passion. The term is often used to characterize literature, gestures, or looks that are suggestive or indecent.
example_sentence: The king was known for his lascivious lifestyle and many scandals. He gave her a lascivious wink that made her feel very uncomfortable. The book was banned for its lascivious descriptions of the protagonist's affairs. Their lascivious behavior at the party shocked the more conservative guests.

english_meaning: In a lewd, lustful, or sexually suggestive manner. It describes actions or behaviors performed with a strong, offensive, or uncontrolled sexual desire. It implies acting in a way that is driven by inappropriate or unchaste carnal thoughts.
example_sentence: He stared at her lasciviously from across the crowded room. The magazine was severely criticized for depicting the models lasciviously. The manager was accused of making inappropriate comments and behaving lasciviously towards his subordinates. The creepy stranger smiled lasciviously, making everyone around him feel extremely uncomfortable.

english_meaning: The quality or state of feeling or revealing an overt and often offensive sexual desire. It refers to behavior that is driven by strong, uncontrollable, and often inappropriate sexual urges. Showing a lack of restraint in sexual matters, characterized by lustfulness, lewdness, and a tendency to engage in indecent behavior.
example_sentence: The politician's career ended abruptly when allegations of lasciviousness were proven true. His absolute lasciviousness made everyone in the office incredibly uncomfortable. The classic novel was initially banned for its perceived lasciviousness and explicit content. She reported the manager to the human resources department for his inappropriate remarks and undeniable lasciviousness. The historical figure was infamous for his drunkenness and lasciviousness at royal banquets.

english_meaning: A device that produces a narrow, intense beam of light of a single wavelength. The beam of light produced by such a device. Relating to equipment or treatment that uses such a beam. To cut, mark, or treat something using a laser beam.
example_sentence: The surgeon used a laser to remove the tissue. A red laser pointer helped him highlight the chart. Laser technology is widely used in manufacturing. The factory lasers each component with a serial number.

english_meaning: A handheld device that emits a concentrated beam of laser light. A speed-detection instrument used by police to measure the speed of vehicles. A weapon, real or fictional, that fires an intense beam of light. A toy or game device that projects a harmless laser beam.
synonyms: ["Laser weapon","Ray gun","Beam weapon","Speed gun","Radar gun","Blaster","Laser device"]
example_sentence: The officer used a laser gun to check the car's speed. Children played happily with their toy laser guns. The film features soldiers armed with laser guns. Engineers tested the laser gun in a controlled laboratory.

english_meaning: A printer that uses a laser beam and toner to produce sharp text and images on paper. An office machine that prints quickly and at high resolution using electrostatic technology.
example_sentence: The office bought a new laser printer last month. A laser printer is faster than most inkjet models. Please load fresh paper into the laser printer. The laser printer produced a crisp, clean copy.

english_meaning: An early optical disc format used for storing films and video. A large silver disc read by a laser beam, popular before DVDs. A home video system based on such discs and their players.
example_sentence: His father still keeps a collection of old laserdiscs. The laserdisc offered better picture quality than videotape. Collectors pay high prices for rare laserdisc releases. The museum displayed a working laserdisc player.

english_meaning: A blow with a whip or a stick. A stroke of a whip. To strike with a whip. To tie or fasten something tightly with a rope or cord. An eyelash. A sharp criticism or verbal attack. To beat forcefully as of rain or waves.
example_sentence: The horse was driven with a sharp lash. Rain lashed against the windows all night. She has long, beautiful lashes. They lashed the boxes securely to the truck. The critic lashed the movie in his review.

english_meaning: To tie, fasten, or secure an object firmly, usually with rope, cord, or straps, so it does not move. To strike repeatedly with force, often used for rain or wind (“the storm lashed down”). To criticize harshly in some contexts.
example_sentence: Lash down the boxes before driving. The rain lashed down all night. Sailors lashed down the sails. Lash down the tent before the storm. It started to lash down just as we left the office. The wind grew stronger and the rain lashed down all night.

english_meaning: To attack verbally or physically. To criticize someone severely, scold angrily, or strike someone or something with sudden force.
example_sentence: The coach lashed into the team after their poor performance. The politician lashed into the media for spreading false news. He lashed into the wall with a stick out of frustration. Critics lashed into the film for its weak storyline.

english_meaning: To criticize someone strongly. To spend money freely and suddenly. To strike out with a part of the body such as a hand or foot.
example_sentence: He lashed out at his friend during the argument. The child lashed out when he was scolded. She lashed out at the media for spreading rumors. The horse lashed out with its back legs.

english_meaning: A final event or action that causes the complete failure or end of something already weakening or in trouble. The final blow that destroys something completely.
example_sentence: His repeated mistakes were bad, but the final fraud was the last nail in the coffin of his career. The loss of their biggest client was the last nail in the coffin for the struggling business. The team’s defeat in the final match became the last nail in the coffin of their championship hopes. Ignoring customer feedback proved to be the last nail in the coffin for the company’s reputation.

english_meaning: A final option chosen only when all other choices have failed. A course of action taken when nothing else is left. The ultimate solution when every alternative has been exhausted. Something used only in the most desperate circumstances.
example_sentence: Surgery should be the last resort after all treatments fail. Borrowing money from him was my last resort. The government used force only as a last resort. Calling the police felt like a last resort.

english_meaning: The final small problem that makes a person unable to bear the situation any longer, like the drop that overflows the cup. The final problem or annoyance in a series that causes a person to lose patience or take action. The breaking point.
example_sentence: He had been late to work many times, but missing the meeting was the last straw for his boss. Her rude comment was the last straw; I decided to end the friendship. The last straw came when the landlord raised the rent again. After all the stress, losing his phone was the last straw that made him cry.

english_meaning: Made as a final desperate effort. Done at the last possible moment. Relating to a last attempt to avoid failure. Used to describe a final resort. Employed when no other option remains.
example_sentence: They made a last-ditch attempt to reach an agreement. The soldiers put up a last-ditch defense. The doctor tried a last-ditch treatment. It was a last-ditch move to save the sinking business.

english_meaning: A final attempt made after all others have failed. A desperate try to achieve something at the last moment. An ultimate effort in a hopeless situation. A final push to succeed. A last try before giving up.
example_sentence: They made a last-ditch effort to save the company. In a last-ditch effort, doctors performed an emergency surgery. The team’s last-ditch effort helped them win the match. He made a last-ditch effort to convince her to stay.

english_meaning: Continuing for a long time. Enduring in effect or influence. Not easily forgotten or removed. Permanent in nature.
example_sentence: The visit left a lasting impression on the children. They hope for a lasting peace in the region. Good habits bring lasting benefits. The paint gives the wood a lasting finish.

english_meaning: A small metal or wooden bar used to fasten a door, gate, or window. A type of lock that is opened from the outside with a key and from the inside with a handle. To fasten something with a latch. To attach oneself to a person or idea and not let go.
example_sentence: Please make sure the latch on the gate is properly closed at night. The old wooden door had a heavy iron latch. The wind blew the door open because the latch was broken. The baby latched onto his mother's finger and would not let go. He latched onto the new idea and refused to consider any other plan.

english_meaning: To fasten or become firmly attached. To understand something, often suddenly. To become interested in and adopt an idea or trend. To attach oneself to a person or group, sometimes for support or advantage. To continue holding firmly.
example_sentence: The gate will latch on when you push it shut. It took him a while to latch on to the joke. Young customers quickly latched on to the trend. The frightened child latched on and would not let go.

english_meaning: To take hold of something firmly. To become strongly interested in an idea, person, or opportunity. To understand and adopt an idea quickly. To attach oneself to someone for support, advantage, or companionship. To focus persistently on a detail or remark.
example_sentence: The child latched onto his mother’s arm. Investors quickly latched onto the new opportunity. She latched onto one careless remark and ignored the explanation. The students latched onto the main idea immediately.

english_meaning: The state of existing but being not yet developed or manifest. In computing, it refers to the delay before a transfer of data begins following an instruction. It is a period of dormancy or inactivity during which something is hidden or inactive.
example_sentence: The virus has a long period of latency before symptoms appear. Decreasing network latency is crucial for high-speed online gaming. The artistic talent of the child remained in latency until she started school. Psychologists study the latency period in child development.

english_meaning: The time that passes between being exposed to something and having a reaction to it. It often refers to the interval between exposure to a pathogen or carcinogen and the first clinical signs of disease. In psychology, it describes a stage where certain impulses are hidden.
example_sentence: The latency period for this specific virus can be up to two weeks. Researchers are studying the long latency period of asbestos-related lung diseases. During the latency period, the patient may feel entirely healthy despite the underlying infection. Identifying the latency period helps in tracking the source of an outbreak.

english_meaning: Something that exists but is not yet developed or manifest. It refers to a state of being hidden, concealed, or dormant. In a clinical sense, it describes an infection or disease that is present without symptoms.
example_sentence: The artist had a latent talent for sculpture that she only discovered in her fifties. Latent heat is released when water vapor condenses into liquid. The virus can remain latent in the body for many years without causing harm. He had a latent desire to travel the world but never acted upon it.

english_meaning: The interval between the occurrence of a stimulus and the beginning of the response. In medicine, it is the lag time between exposure to a harmful agent and the onset of symptoms. It is frequently used interchangeably with 'incubation period' in infectious diseases.
example_sentence: The latent period of the drug's effect was shorter than the doctors anticipated. We must account for the latent period when measuring the speed of nerve impulses. Environmental toxins often have a long latent period before health issues arise. The experiment measured the latent period between the light flash and the muscle twitch.

english_meaning: Relating to the side or sides of something. Situated on, directed toward, or coming from the side. A part or extension on the side. In sports, a sideways pass. Involving sideways movement or thinking that departs from usual patterns.
example_sentence: The player made a lateral pass to his teammate. The building has lateral supports on both sides. Lateral thinking often leads to creative solutions. Fish use their lateral line to sense water movement. The doctor examined the lateral muscles of the leg.

english_meaning: Something very difficult to understand. To describe something confusing, obscure, or unintelligible, implying that the subject is as hard to understand as a foreign or ancient language.
example_sentence: The legal document was Latin and Greek to most people. Quantum physics can feel like Latin and Greek if you don’t study it. The instructions for the software were Latin and Greek to the beginners. Ancient manuscripts can seem like Latin and Greek at first glance.

english_meaning: The distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees. An imaginary line running around the earth parallel to the equator. Freedom to act, choose, or think as one wishes. Scope or room for variation within limits.
example_sentence: The island lies at a latitude of ten degrees north. Lines of latitude never meet. The manager gave her staff considerable latitude in planning the project. Students are allowed some latitude in choosing their topics.

english_meaning: Fear of doctors. An intense and irrational fear of doctors or medical professionals. A person with this fear may avoid medical checkups, hospitals, or even talking to doctors, which can harm their health.
example_sentence: Due to latrophobia, he avoided visiting a doctor even when he was seriously ill. Her latrophobia developed after a painful medical experience in childhood. People with latrophobia often delay treatment and risk worsening their condition. Counseling helped him overcome latrophobia and attend regular health checkups.

english_meaning: A structure or pattern made of crossed strips of wood, metal, or other material, forming a diamond or square shape. A framework used as a screen, support, or decoration. A regular repeating arrangement of points, as in a crystal.
example_sentence: The garden gate had a beautiful lattice design. She baked a pie with a lattice crust on top. The lattice fence let sunlight through. Scientists studied the lattice structure of the crystal. Climbing roses covered the wooden lattice.

english_meaning: To praise or honor someone or something highly. To express approval or admiration for. To glorify or celebrate. To commend or extol publicly. To speak or write in appreciation of.
example_sentence: The critics laud the young director for her bold vision. The community gathered to laud the firefighters for their bravery. The poem was written to laud the beauty of the countryside. His colleagues laud him for his dedication to the project. The award ceremony was an opportunity to laud outstanding achievements.

english_meaning: Deserving praise and commendation. Worthy of admiration and approval. Meritorious and honorable. Deserving of being lauded. Reflecting high moral standards or excellence.
example_sentence: Her laudable efforts to help the homeless were recognized by the city. The charity's laudable mission is to provide education for all. It is a laudable goal to reduce pollution in our rivers. His laudable honesty made him a trusted figure in the community. The teacher's laudable patience with struggling students was admirable.

english_meaning: A person or thing that everyone laughs at or ridicules. Someone who has become an object of public mockery. A target of jokes because of a foolish mistake. Something regarded as ridiculous and not to be taken seriously.
synonyms: ["Butt of jokes","Object of ridicule","Figure of fun","Joke","Mockery","Fool"]
example_sentence: His careless remarks made him the laughing stock of the office. The team became a laughing stock after that defeat. She feared becoming a laughing stock in front of her classmates. The badly built bridge is now the laughing stock of the city.

english_meaning: To send a rocket, missile, or spacecraft into the air or space. To start or introduce something new such as a plan, product, or campaign. To set a boat or ship into the water for the first time. To begin an activity with energy and enthusiasm. The act of launching something.
example_sentence: NASA will launch a new satellite next month. The company plans to launch its new smartphone this year. They launched the ship with a grand ceremony. She launched into a long speech about her achievements. The launch of the new product was a huge success.

english_meaning: To initiate an attack or a strong protest against someone or something. It implies a forceful and often public beginning of an action intended to oppose, criticize, or harm the target. This phrase suggests a deliberate and sometimes aggressive commencement of hostility or opposition.
example_sentence: The opposition party decided to launch against the government's new policies. They plan to launch a full-scale legal challenge against the company. Scientists launched a strong protest against the cutting of research funds. The activists organized a campaign to launch against the proposed construction project. The army was ordered to launch against the rebel forces.

english_meaning: To begin to do or say something with great energy or enthusiasm. It often implies a sudden or vigorous start to an activity, a speech, or a topic of discussion. This phrasal verb suggests an immediate and often unreserved engagement in the action or discourse.
example_sentence: She decided to launch into her presentation without any further delay. He launched into a passionate speech about social justice. After a small technical glitch, the rocket launched into the sky. Don't launch into conclusions before hearing all the facts. They launched into a fierce debate about the new policy.

english_meaning: To launch off from means to start a journey, project, or action from a particular point or place. It implies a sense of initiating or beginning something, often with momentum or a clear starting location. This phrasal verb suggests the act of propelling oneself or something else away from a base or origin.
example_sentence: The rocket will launch off from the Cape Canaveral complex at dawn. We decided to launch off from our existing business model to explore new markets. The team will launch off from the base camp tomorrow morning for the final ascent. She plans to launch off from her current project to pursue a more ambitious goal. The birds decided to launch off from the branch simultaneously.

english_meaning: To launch on means to embark upon or initiate a significant undertaking, project, or journey. It implies a formal or decisive start to something that often requires considerable effort or planning. This phrase can also refer to the act of starting discussions, arguments, or an attack with vigor.
example_sentence: The company decided to launch on a new marketing campaign to reach a wider audience. After years of research, they were finally ready to launch on their ambitious space mission. The politician used his speech to launch on a scathing critique of his opponent's policies. We are excited to launch on this journey of discovery together. The board will launch on a full investigation into the matter next week.

english_meaning: To venture into something new or unknown, especially with determination and enthusiasm. It suggests taking a bold step or embarking on a significant endeavor that requires courage and initiative. It often implies leaving a familiar or safe situation to explore new possibilities or take on a challenging task.
synonyms: ["Venture Forth","Embark On","Set Out","Dive In","Blaze A Trail","Initiate","Undertake","Plunge Into","Start Up","Kick Off"]
example_sentence: After years of working for others, she decided to launch out into her own business. The explorer was determined to launch out into the uncharted wilderness. It's time for us to launch out into more innovative marketing strategies. He encouraged his team to launch out into new areas of research. They needed to launch out into the deep end of the pool to truly learn how to swim.

english_meaning: To embark on or begin a new venture or activity with enthusiasm and determination. It implies initiating something significant, often with a sense of excitement or urgency, and can refer to starting a project, a journey, or an attack. The phrase suggests a decisive and vigorous beginning.
example_sentence: The company decided to launch upon a new marketing campaign to boost sales. They were keen to launch upon the archaeological excavation as soon as the funding was secured. We must launch upon serious discussions with the stakeholders if we want to resolve this issue. After months of preparation, the team is ready to launch upon their ambitious space mission. The politician announced his intention to launch upon a nationwide tour to gather support.

english_meaning: A poetic or literary term for a laurel tree or wreath. In historical context, a name associated with honor and victory. A feminine given name of Latin origin meaning laurel. Symbolic of poetic achievement or distinction. A classical symbol of triumph and recognition.
antonyms: ["A proper name does not have antonyms."]
example_sentence: Laura received an award for her outstanding performance. I met Laura at the conference last week. Laura always helps her friends whenever they need support. Everyone admired Laura for her kindness and honesty.

english_meaning: A person honored with an award. A person who receives official recognition or a prestigious award for outstanding achievement in a field such as literature, science, peace, or the arts. The term is commonly used with major honors like Nobel Prize winner or Poet Laureate.
example_sentence: She became the youngest Nobel laureate in her country. The poet laureate wrote a poem for the national ceremony. As a laureate, he inspired many young scientists. The award turned her into an internationally respected laureate.

english_meaning: A type of evergreen tree with aromatic leaves, especially bay laurel. A wreath made from laurel leaves used in ancient times to honor winners. Symbol of honor, victory, or achievement. Praise or fame given for success.
example_sentence: The athlete was crowned with laurel after winning the championship. She refused to rest on her laurel after receiving the award. Ancient poets were often honored with a laurel wreath. His scientific success brought him many laurel and respect.

english_meaning: A room or compartment with a toilet and washbasin. A plumbing fixture used for urination and defecation.
example_sentence: The airplane lavatory is located at the back of the cabin. Please ensure the lavatory is kept clean. He went to the lavatory to wash his hands. The public lavatories were closed for maintenance.

english_meaning: A small aromatic plant with narrow leaves and pale purple flowers, commonly used in perfumes, oils, soaps, and medicines. Something that is light purple in color. Associated with calmness, relaxation, purity, and elegance.
example_sentence: She planted lavender in her garden for its pleasant fragrance. The walls were painted a soft lavender shade. Lavender oil helps many people sleep better at night. She wore a beautiful lavender dress to the party. Lavender oil is used to reduce stress, improve sleep, and relieve anxiety.

english_meaning: A marriage between a man and a woman arranged to hide one or both partners’ true sexual orientation, usually for social, cultural, or professional reasons. A formal marriage between a heterosexual appearing couple in which at least one partner is gay, lesbian, or bisexual and wishes to conceal their sexual orientation. Such marriages were more common in the past when social stigma, legal restrictions, or career risks made it difficult for LGBTQ individuals to live openly. The term is often associated with early Hollywood, politics, or conservative societies where public image was very important.
synonyms: ["Marriage of convenience","Sham marriage","Cover marriage","Strategic marriage","Protective marriage"]
antonyms: ["Love marriage","Genuine marriage","Romantic marriage","Open same sex marriage"]
example_sentence: The actor entered into a lavender marriage to protect his career in a conservative era. Historians believe several celebrities in the early film industry had lavender marriages. Their lavender marriage allowed both partners to maintain their public image. In some societies, a lavender marriage was seen as a safer option than coming out openly.

english_meaning: very rich, luxurious, or given in large amounts. Something that is expensive, rich, and impressive in appearance. Given or spent in a generous or excessive way. To give something in large quantities.
example_sentence: They hosted a lavish wedding at a five star hotel. The room was decorated with lavish furniture. She received lavish praise for her work. He spent lavishly on his new house.

english_meaning: In a way that shows great abundance or generosity. Doing something in a very generous, extravagant, or elaborate manner, often spending a lot of resources, money, or effort freely.
example_sentence: She decorated her house lavishly for the party. The king was lavished with gifts by his subjects. He spends his money lavishly on vacations. The chef presented the meal lavishly on a golden platter.

english_meaning: The quality of being extravagant or excessively generous. The act or quality of giving or spending much more than necessary, often in a luxurious, abundant, or over-the-top way. It can relate to money, gifts, attention, or resources.
example_sentence: The lavishness of the wedding impressed all the guests. His lavishness with gifts made everyone feel special. The palace was famous for its architectural lavishness. Lavishness in spending without planning can lead to financial problems.

english_meaning: The quality of being in accordance with the law. The state of being legal, permitted, or justified by rules. Respect for and obedience to the laws of a society.
example_sentence: The judge questioned the lawfulness of the arrest. Citizens must respect the lawfulness of the government. The lawfulness of his actions was widely praised. The report examined the lawfulness of the new policy.

english_meaning: Legal cases brought before a court to enforce a right or seek a remedy. Actions taken by one party against another in a court of law. Legal proceedings involving disputes between individuals or organizations. Claims or complaints filed in a judicial system. The process of litigating a dispute.
example_sentence: The company faced several lawsuits from former employees. He filed one of the largest lawsuits in the history of the state. The lawsuits claimed damages for environmental pollution. Settling lawsuits out of court can save both time and money. The attorney specializes in handling complex commercial lawsuits.

english_meaning: Not sufficiently strict, severe, or careful. Lacking in rigor or discipline. Careless or negligent in duties or responsibilities. Loose or relaxed in texture or structure. Slack or not taut.
example_sentence: The school was criticized for its lax security policies. His lax attitude toward deadlines frustrated his coworkers. Lax regulations allowed pollution to increase in the area. The rope became lax and the tent started to collapse. The lax enforcement of rules led to widespread cheating.

english_meaning: A medicine, food, or substance that loosens the bowels and relieves constipation. Something that has the effect of stimulating bowel movements. A substance used medicinally to ease or promote defecation.
example_sentence: The doctor recommended a mild laxative to relieve the patient's severe constipation. Prunes and other dried fruits are well known for their natural laxative effect. He was advised to use the laxative only for a short period and not as a long-term solution. The pharmacist suggested a gentle laxative that would be safe for elderly patients. Some herbal teas contain laxative compounds that can help regulate digestion.

english_meaning: The quality of being lax, loose, or not strict enough. A lack of firmness, discipline, or proper control. Looseness or slackness in attitude, standards, or physical structure.
example_sentence: The report blamed laxity in safety procedures for the accident that occurred at the factory. Critics accused the management of laxity in enforcing the company's code of conduct. The team's laxity in the second half of the match allowed the opponents to score three quick goals. Laxity in border controls had allowed a significant number of illegal goods to enter the country. She was determined to address the laxity that had crept into the daily routines of her department.

english_meaning: To set aside something, especially money or goods, for future use. To reserve an item at a store by making a deposit until fully paid. To save or store safely for later. To put away for safekeeping.
example_sentence: She laid away some money for her children's education. He laid away a new coat for the winter season. They lay away a portion of every paycheck. The store allowed customers to lay away gifts before the holidays.

english_meaning: To reveal something completely, especially facts, feelings, secrets, or the true nature of a situation that was hidden before.
example_sentence: The investigation laid bare the corruption in the system. His speech laid bare his true intentions. The report laid bare the failures of the project. Years of hardship laid bare her emotional strength.

english_meaning: To save something, especially money, for future use. To stop or rest temporarily. To keep something aside or store it safely. To park a vehicle at the side of a road.
example_sentence: He laid by some money every month for his children's education. The workers laid by their tools and took a short break. She laid by some food for the coming winter. The driver laid by the car to check the engine.

english_meaning: To exaggerate praise, emotion, or behavior in an obvious or excessive way, often to flatter someone or make something seem bigger or more important than it really is. Used when someone is being too expressive, too complimentary, or too dramatic. It usually suggests that the behavior feels insincere, artificial, or overdone. It can be used in both positive and negative situations, but most often it implies exaggeration for effect or flattery.
example_sentence: He was laying it on thick when he said I was the best employee in the entire company. Don’t lay it on thick, just tell me honestly how I performed. She started laying it on thick about how amazing the food was, even though she didn’t like it much. The salesman was laying it on thick to convince us to buy the product.

english_meaning: To terminate or suspend employment, often due to business reasons. To refrain from doing something, especially something annoying or harmful. To reduce or stop production or activity. Informally, to leave someone alone or stop criticizing
example_sentence: The company had to lay off 50 workers due to budget cuts. The teacher told the students to lay off joking during class. Factory management decided to lay off production for a week. He told his brother to lay off criticizing his choices.

english_meaning: To organize or supply something for people. To put or spread something on a surface. To arrange meals, drinks, or events for guests. To overstate or make something seem stronger than it is. To place responsibility, blame, or duty on someone.
example_sentence: The company laid on free lunch for the staff. She laid on sunscreen before going outside. The host laid on live music at the party. He laid on the compliments to impress her.

word: Lay one's cards on the table
english_meaning: To speak honestly and openly about one's intentions, plans, feelings, or facts without hiding anything. To reveal all relevant information, intentions, or feelings honestly and directly. The idiom comes from card games where players show their cards openly. It is often used when someone decides to stop hiding facts and be completely transparent.
synonyms: ["Be honest","Be open","Come clean","Tell the truth","Be straightforward","Be transparent","Speak frankly","Reveal one's intentions"]
antonyms: ["Hide the truth","Conceal information","Be secretive","Mislead","Deceive","Withhold facts","Keep something hidden","Cover up"]
example_sentence: Before signing the agreement, both companies laid their cards on the table and discussed all concerns openly. If we want to solve this problem, everyone must lay their cards on the table. During the meeting, she laid her cards on the table and explained her true intentions. He decided to lay his cards on the table and tell his family about his future plans.

english_meaning: To arrange things neatly or clearly. To explain a plan or idea in detail. To spend money for a purpose. To expose or present for view. To knock someone unconscious. To stretch out fully. To plan financially or strategically.
example_sentence: She laid out all the documents on the table. The architect laid out the plans for the new building. He laid out a lot of money for his new car. The instructions were laid out clearly in the manual.

english_meaning: To stop or stay somewhere for a short time during a journey. To make a temporary halt between two parts of a trip. To postpone or delay something to a later time. A short break in a journey, especially between flights. To spread something flat over a surface.
example_sentence: We had to lay over in Dubai for six hours. The pilot decided to lay over the flight due to bad weather. Let us lay over this discussion until tomorrow. Passengers can rest in the lounge during a long lay over.

english_meaning: Temporary or permanent termination of employment by an employer. The dismissal of employees, usually for economic reasons, reduction of workforce, or company restructuring. It can be temporary (employees may be recalled) or permanent. It can also refer to a pause or suspension in production or activity.
example_sentence: The company announced a lay-off of 200 employees due to declining sales. During the pandemic, many workers faced temporary lay-offs. The lay-off period gave her time to pursue further studies.

english_meaning: A person without specialized knowledge of a subject. Someone who is not trained, experienced, or professionally qualified in a specific field, especially in law, medicine, religion, or technical subjects. It can also refer to a non-clerical member of a church.
example_sentence: The professor explained the theory so even a layman could understand it. He approached the problem like a layman, without technical tools. Laymen should not attempt complicated legal procedures without guidance. The lecture was designed for laymen, not experts.

english_meaning: A one-handed shot made from near the basket in basketball. An easy task or a guaranteed success. A period of being laid up or inactive due to illness or repairs.
example_sentence: The player easily scored a layup during the fast break. Winning this negotiation should be a layup for our experienced team. The ship is currently in a layup for scheduled maintenance. After his injury, he had a long layup before returning to work.

english_meaning: Be idle, To spend time being lazy, doing nothing useful or productive, and relaxing instead of working or being active
example_sentence: He spent Sunday lazing about. On Sundays, I like to laze about and watch movies all day. The students were lazing about instead of studying for their exams. After finishing the project, he lazed about at home for a week. It’s too hot today; everyone is just lazing about.

english_meaning: The quality of being unwilling to work or use energy. The state of avoiding effort and preferring inactivity. A habitual disinclination to exertion.
example_sentence: His laziness in completing assignments was the main reason he fell behind in his studies. She overcame her natural laziness by setting herself small daily targets. Laziness is often misunderstood — what looks like laziness may sometimes be exhaustion or anxiety. The supervisor had no patience for laziness and expected full effort from every team member. He admitted that laziness had cost him opportunities he would never be able to recover.

english_meaning: Unwilling to work or use energy to complete tasks. Moving or reacting slowly and without enthusiasm or effort. Characterized by lack of activity or exertion, often encouraging relaxation. Inducing or suited to a relaxed and restful state.

The dog was too lazy to bark when the mail carrier walked up the driveway. Her teacher warned her that lazy study habits would lead to poor exam results.

english_meaning: An open area of grassy or arable land. A meadow used for grazing animals. A poetic word for a field or pasture. A stretch of grassland in the countryside.

english_meaning: To guide or direct someone by going in front. To be in charge of. A position of advantage or the front position in a race. A heavy soft grey metal used in many industries. A wire conveying electric current. The main role in a film or play. A leash for a dog.

english_meaning: To guide or take someone or something from one place to another, often implying a movement from a group or situation. It can also suggest distraction from a task or purpose.

english_meaning: To begin an event, discussion, performance, or action.  To initiate an action that prompts a reaction. To begin a series of moves or steps in a process.

english_meaning: To cause something to happen or result in a particular situation.

A slow-moving plant-eating insect of the family Phylliidae. An example of natural mimicry in which an animal imitates part of a plant.

english_meaning: To bend or move from an upright position towards one side. To rest against something for support. Containing little or no fat; thin and fit. Providing little; not productive or abundant.

english_meaning: To form an opinion or judgment quickly without enough information. To make hasty decisions based on limited facts. To assume something is true without proper evidence. To jump to a conclusion prematurely. To decide too quickly without careful thought.

english_meaning: A year containing 366 days instead of the usual 365, with an extra day added to February (February 29). english_meaning: To control, restrain, or guide an animal (or figuratively, a person or thing) by using a leash. A strap, cord, or chain used to control, guide, or restrain an animal, usually a dog.

word: Leave a lot to be desired
english_meaning: To be far from satisfactory and clearly in need of improvement. To fall well below the expected standard. To be disappointing in quality or performance.

english_meaning: To abandon someone in a difficult or dangerous situation, especially when they need help or support the most.

english_meaning: To make something longer in size, distance, or extent. To become longer over time. To increase the duration of an activity, period, or event. To extend a piece of clothing or material by adding to it.
example_sentence: The tailor agreed to lengthen the sleeves of my coat. Shadows lengthen as the sun sinks lower in the sky. They decided to lengthen the meeting by another hour. Regular stretching can lengthen the muscles safely.

english_meaning: Continuing for a long time; unusually long. Long in duration or extent, often tediously so. Using too many words; long-winded.
example_sentence: The meeting turned into a lengthy debate. After a lengthy delay, the train finally arrived. He wrote a lengthy reply to the complaint. The lengthy process tested everyone's patience.

english_meaning: More merciful or tolerant than expected. Not strict or harsh in discipline or punishment. Permissive and gentle in the treatment of others. Showing willingness to be understanding rather than severe.
example_sentence: The judge was criticised for being too lenient with repeat offenders who came before the court. She was a lenient parent who rarely raised her voice and always tried to reason with her children. The school adopted a more lenient approach to homework during the exam preparation period. He was grateful for the lenient treatment he received after admitting his mistake openly. A lenient policy on late submissions was introduced to reduce student stress during the semester.

english_meaning: The clear, flexible structure inside the eye that focuses light onto the retina. The part of the eye that changes shape to allow clear vision of both near and distant objects. A curved piece of glass or plastic used in spectacles, cameras, microscopes, and telescopes. A particular way of looking at or interpreting a situation.
example_sentence: The lens of the eye becomes less flexible with age. A cloudy lens is known as a cataract. He cleaned the camera lens before taking the photograph. She viewed the whole issue through the lens of experience.

english_meaning: A small pigmented spot on the skin that resembles a freckle but is not affected by sunlight. A flat brown or dark spot found on the skin, especially in older people. A benign skin lesion caused by a localised increase in the number of melanocytes.
example_sentence: The dermatologist examined the lentigo on her forearm and confirmed it was completely benign. A lentigo differs from a freckle in that it does not fade during the winter months. Elderly patients often develop a form of lentigo on areas of skin that have been exposed to the sun. The cosmetic treatment was designed to lighten the lentigo without damaging the surrounding skin. She asked the specialist whether the lentigo on her cheek could be safely removed.

english_meaning: A small flat edible seed used as food. A small round or flat seed from a legume plant. It is commonly used in cooking, especially in soups, stews, and curries. Lentils are rich in protein, fiber, and nutrients.
example_sentence: She cooked lentils for dinner. Lentils are healthy and full of protein. I added lentils to the soup. Many people eat lentils every day

english_meaning: A woman who is emotionally, romantically, or sexually attracted to other women. The word can also describe anything related to such attraction or identity.
synonyms: ["Gay woman","Homosexual woman","Sapphic woman","Woman attracted to women"]
example_sentence: She openly identifies as a lesbian and supports equal rights for all people. The novel tells the story of a lesbian couple living in a small town. Many communities organize events to celebrate lesbian culture and identity. She joined a support group for lesbian women in her city.

english_meaning: A Greek island in the Aegean Sea, known historically as a centre of poetry and culture. The birthplace of the ancient Greek poet Sappho, whose work was associated with female love. A place of significant historical, literary, and cultural importance in ancient Greece.
example_sentence: Lesbos has been inhabited since prehistoric times and holds great archaeological significance. The ancient poet Sappho was born on Lesbos and wrote some of the most celebrated lyric poetry of her era. Lesbos is now a popular tourist destination known for its natural beauty and historical heritage. The island of Lesbos has played a significant role in modern history as a point of arrival for refugees. Scholars of classical literature often visit Lesbos to study the legacy of its ancient literary tradition.

english_meaning: A region in an organ or tissue which has suffered damage through injury or disease. This can include wounds, ulcers, abscesses, or tumors. In pathology, it signifies any localized abnormal structural change in the body.
example_sentence: The MRI scan revealed a small lesion on the patient's brain. Skin lesions can be caused by excessive exposure to the sun. The surgeon removed the cancerous lesion during a four-hour operation. Scientists are studying how the lesion affects the nervous system's function.

english_meaning: A person or organization who takes land, property, or an asset on lease from the owner and pays rent for its use. A lessee is the party in a lease agreement who obtains the right to use and occupy a property, equipment, or asset for a specific period of time in exchange for regular payments called rent or lease payments. The ownership remains with the lessor (owner), while the lessee only has usage rights under the contract terms.
example_sentence: The lessee must pay rent on the first day of every month. The company became the lessee of the building for ten years. If the lessee damages the property, they may lose their security deposit. The lessee signed a contract agreeing to all lease conditions.

english_meaning: A person or organisation that leases or rents out property, land, or equipment to another party (the lessee) in exchange for payment. Owner who rents out property or goods. Person who gives something on lease. Landlord or leasing party in a contract.
example_sentence: The lessor agreed to reduce the monthly rent after negotiations. As the lessor, she was responsible for maintaining the property. The lessor signed the lease agreement for five years. The lessor had the right to inspect the property every six months.

english_meaning: Used to say that something is even less likely or possible. Not to mention something more important or difficult. Used to compare two things where the second is more extreme. To emphasize that something is beyond consideration. Used to strengthen a previous negative statement.
example_sentence: He cannot walk, let alone run. She has no time for lunch, let alone dinner. The child cannot read, let alone write. We do not own a car, let alone a house.

english_meaning: Forget past mistakes, arguments, or unpleasant events and move forward peacefully. It is an idiom used when people decide not to discuss or remain angry about past problems. It encourages forgiveness, peace, and a fresh start in relationships, friendships, family matters, or work situations.
synonyms: ["Forgive and forget","Move on","Make peace","Bury the hatchet","Start afresh","Reconcile"]
antonyms: ["Hold a grudge","Remember past wrongs","Seek revenge","Continue the conflict","Refuse to forgive"]
example_sentence: After years of disagreement, the two brothers decided to let bygones be bygones. We argued last week, but I think we should let bygones be bygones and work together again. The manager encouraged the employees to let bygones be bygones after the conflict. She apologized sincerely, so I chose to let bygones be bygones.

english_meaning: To disappoint someone by not meeting their expectations. To fail to support, help, or fulfill someone’s expectations or trust. It can also mean to lower or release something physically.
example_sentence: He promised to help, but he let me down. The team was let down by their captain’s absence. I felt let down when the package arrived late. Don’t let me down on this project.

english_meaning: To allow someone or something to enter. To allow feelings, emotions, or thoughts to affect oneself. To share secret or private information; to include someone in knowledge. To allow opportunities, influences, or changes to enter one’s life.
example_sentence: I let him in through the back door. She let in the cat after it meowed. Don’t let negative thoughts in. He finally let her in on the secret.

english_meaning: To excuse someone from punishment or responsibility. To allow something to explode or release (like fireworks). To release someone from a duty or obligation. To let something happen without interference.
example_sentence: The teacher let him off for being late this time. The police let off the driver with a warning. They let off fireworks on New Year’s Eve. She was let off from her duty because of illness.

english_meaning: To reveal or disclose something, especially a secret or information you were keeping hidden.
example_sentence: She didn’t let on that she had already solved the problem. He let on about the surprise party by accident. Don’t let on that you know about the deal. They let on the secret only to their closest friends.

english_meaning: To allow a person, animal, or object to exit or leave a place. To release something contained, such as air, sound, or emotion. To enlarge a piece of clothing or extend space. To reveal or disclose information.
example_sentence: She let out the cat before leaving the house. He let out a sigh of relief when the exam was over. I need to let out this dress; it’s too tight now. He accidentally let out the secret about the surprise party.

english_meaning: To avoid bringing up an old issue that could cause trouble. To leave a situation alone in order to prevent conflict. To not disturb something that is currently peaceful. To refrain from discussing sensitive matters from the past. To let a matter stay as it is because raising it may create problems.
synonyms: ["Leave well alone","Don't stir things up","Let it be","Drop the matter","Move on","Avoid trouble"]
example_sentence: It is better to let sleeping dogs lie and forget the argument. She wanted to raise the old issue but decided to let sleeping dogs lie. Sometimes it is wiser to let sleeping dogs lie than to seek revenge. I did not remind him of the mistake and chose to let sleeping dogs lie.

word: Let the cat out of the bag
english_meaning: To reveal a secret or tell something that was supposed to be kept hidden, often by mistake. When someone “lets the cat out of the bag,” they tell others a secret that was not meant to be shared.
example_sentence: He let the cat out of the bag about the surprise. John let the cat out of the bag about Mary’s surprise birthday party. Don’t let the cat out of the bag; it’s supposed to be a secret!. She let the cat out of the bag and everyone knew about the new project. When he mentioned the promotion, he realized he had let the cat out of the bag.

english_meaning: To avoid raising an old problem or quarrel that could cause trouble. To leave a sensitive matter alone rather than reopening it. To refrain from interfering in a situation that is currently peaceful. To keep silent about something that might create fresh conflict.
synonyms: ["Leave well alone","Don't stir up trouble","Avoid conflict","Let bygones be bygones","Keep the peace"]
antonyms: ["Stir up trouble","Open old wounds","Provoke","Rake up the past","Interfere"]
example_sentence: I did not mention the old dispute; it is better to let the sleeping dogs lie. My father advised me to let the sleeping dogs lie and move on. Rather than reopen the case, the family chose to let the sleeping dogs lie. She wanted to argue again, but I told her to let the sleeping dogs lie.

english_meaning: To become less intense or severe. To stop or cease an activity.
example_sentence: The rain didn't let up all day long. We hope the pressure at work will let up soon. He never lets up on his training, even on weekends. If the wind lets up, we can go sailing.

english_meaning: To talk seriously and directly about a practical matter, especially about business, money, or final decisions, without wasting time on small talk. To get straight to the point or start a serious discussion about an important issue.
synonyms: ["Get to the point","Be direct","Cut to the chase","Discuss seriously"]
antonyms: ["Beat around the bush","Talk nonsense","Avoid the main issue","Make small talk"]
example_sentence: We’ve discussed enough background, now let’s talk turkey and finalize the deal. They sat down after dinner and talked turkey about the project budget. Enough small talk, let’s talk turkey about your salary expectations. Before signing the contract, the partners talked turkey about the risks involved.

english_meaning: A pause or reduction in intensity of something undesirable.
example_sentence: There has been no let-up in the cold weather recently. The team worked for twelve hours without a let-up. We are looking for a let-up in the high inflation rates. The loud music continued without any let-up until dawn.

english_meaning: A powerful feeling of wanting something very much, such as food, success, attention, or another object of desire. In informal or dialectal English, "letch" may describe strong sexual desire or lust. More commonly, the related word letch is used to refer to a person with excessive sexual interest.
example_sentence: He had a strong letch for adventure and travel. Her letch for success motivated her to work every day. The old story described a man driven by letch rather than wisdom.  His letch for fame eventually led him into trouble.

english_meaning: Something that is capable of causing death or is deadly. Anything that can cause death, either instantly or over time. It is often used for poisons, weapons, diseases, or dangerous conditions.
example_sentence: The snake has a lethal bite that can kill within minutes. The chemical gas was lethal when inhaled in large amounts. A lethal disease spread quickly in the remote village. The soldier was trained to handle lethal weapons safely.

english_meaning: Affected by lethargy; sluggish, drowsy, and lacking energy. Feeling a lack of enthusiasm or motivation to act. Moving or reacting with unusual slowness and heaviness.
example_sentence: She felt lethargic after the long journey and went straight to bed upon arriving home. The hot and humid weather made everyone in the office feel lethargic and unproductive. He had been lethargic for several days and decided to see a doctor about his low energy levels. The medication made him lethargic in the mornings and he found it difficult to concentrate. The team appeared lethargic in the second half and failed to create any clear chances.

english_meaning: A state of mental and physical sluggishness and inactivity. Lack of energy, enthusiasm, or willingness to do anything. A condition of abnormal drowsiness or torpor.
example_sentence: A deep lethargy had settled over the village after years of economic decline and unemployment. The patient's lethargy was one of the key symptoms that led the doctor to order further tests. She struggled to shake off a persistent lethargy that had stayed with her since the illness. The policy failed partly because of the lethargy of those responsible for implementing it. He drank several cups of coffee in an attempt to fight off the lethargy that followed the heavy lunch.

english_meaning: The temporary inability to remember a word or name that you know but cannot recall at that moment. A psychological condition in which a person struggles to retrieve a specific word from memory, even though they are sure they know it. A linguistic state in which a person feels certain they know a word but cannot access it immediately.
synonyms: ["Tip of the tongue state","Word finding difficulty","Retrieval failure","Verbal recall problem"]
example_sentence: I experienced lethologica when I tried to remember my teacher's name. During the speech, she paused because of lethologica. Lethologica can make conversations slightly awkward. Almost everyone faces lethologica at some point in life.

english_meaning: Correct in every detail, without a single mistake. Knowing or reciting something exactly as written. Flawless in performance or execution. Precisely accurate word for word.
example_sentence: Her recitation of the poem was letter perfect. The actors were letter perfect on opening night. He handed in a letter perfect final draft. After weeks of practice, the routine was letter perfect.

english_meaning: A leafy green vegetable eaten raw in salads and sandwiches. A plant grown for its crisp edible leaves. The leaves of this plant used as food. A common salad crop found in many varieties.
example_sentence: Add some lettuce to the sandwich. She washed the lettuce before making the salad. This farm grows lettuce all year round. The burger came with tomato, onion and fresh lettuce.

english_meaning: A mild and gentle form of melancholy or sadness. A quiet, pensive kind of sorrow tinged with pleasure. A soft, thoughtful state of low spirits. A rare literary term for a soothing melancholy. A pleasant sadness often associated with reflection.
example_sentence: A soft leucocholy filled her heart on the rainy evening. The poet wrote about a strange leucocholy in his letters. He felt a gentle leucocholy while looking at old photographs. Autumn always brought a mild leucocholy to his mood.

english_meaning: The act of rising or getting up. The condition of cattle or livestock rising from rest, traditionally paired with couchancy in legal contexts of trespass. The state of being raised or lifted up. An obsolete or rare term referring to the act of rising.
example_sentence: The old legal term levance referred to the rising of cattle. Levance and couchancy described livestock that lay down and rose on the land. The word levance is rarely used in modern English. Scholars studied the meaning of levance in ancient property law. The concept of levance appeared in old grazing rights.

english_meaning: A horizontal position or line. A particular height or amount. A specific stage or degree in a scale or process. To make flat or even. Honest or straightforward in dealings.
example_sentence: The water reached the level of the window. She has reached a high level of expertise. Please level the ground before laying tiles. He was completely level with me about his mistakes. The next level of the game is very challenging.

english_meaning: A situation where everyone has equal opportunities, rights, and conditions. A level playing field refers to fairness in a system where no individual or group has an unfair advantage. It is often used in business, education, sports, and policy discussions to highlight equal competition and justice.
example_sentence: The government aims to create a level playing field for all businesses. Scholarships help provide a level playing field for students from poor backgrounds. Fair rules ensure a level playing field in sports competitions. Technology can create a level playing field by giving equal access to information.

english_meaning: To use something (resources, skills, influence, or connections) to gain a strategic advantage or achieve a desired result. The power or ability to influence people, situations, or outcomes effectively. To gain an upper hand in a situation using resources, skills, or relationships. Using personal qualities or reputation to influence outcomes.
example_sentence: She leveraged her experience to get the promotion. The company leveraged social media to increase sales. Investors use leverage to amplify returns. He leveraged his connections to secure the contract. He leveraged his reputation as a trusted expert to win the contract. She leveraged her network to find new clients.

english_meaning: A Hebrew personal name meaning joined or attached. One of the twelve sons of Jacob in the Bible and the ancestor of the Levite tribe. A surname associated with the Levitical priestly class in ancient Hebrew tradition. Also a widely used brand name for denim jeans.
example_sentence: Levi was the third son of Jacob and Leah according to the Book of Genesis in the Bible. The tribe descended from Levi was appointed to serve as priests and keepers of the tabernacle. Levi Strauss founded the company that became one of the world's most recognised denim brands. The name Levi has remained popular across many cultures and continues to be widely used today. He named his son Levi in honour of his grandfather who had emigrated from Eastern Europe.

english_meaning: To rise or float in the air without any physical support, seemingly in defiance of gravity. To cause something to rise and float in the air. To achieve a state of floating through claimed supernatural or physical means.
example_sentence: The magician appeared to levitate his assistant several metres above the stage. Scientists have developed magnetic technology that can levitate small objects without physical contact. Yogis in certain traditions claim to be able to levitate through intense meditation and breathing techniques. The illusion was so convincing that the audience truly believed the performer could levitate. Children were fascinated by the demonstration showing how superconductors can levitate magnets.

english_meaning: An extra amount of money that has to be paid, especially as a tax to the government. To use official authority to demand and collect a payment, tax, etc. A charge imposed and collected. The act of drafting into military service.
example_sentence: The government imposed a levy on gasoline. A new tax was levied on consumers of luxury goods. The City Council can levy a fine of $250 for a first offence.

english_meaning: Treating sexual matters in an open, offensive, or crude manner. Lascivious, indecent, or obscene in behaviour or expression. Showing or characterised by sexual desire in a way that is considered vulgar or inappropriate.
example_sentence: He was dismissed from his position after making lewd remarks to a junior colleague. The comedian was criticised for including lewd jokes that were considered inappropriate for a family audience. She reported the lewd messages she had received to the human resources department. The film was given an adult rating because of its lewd content and explicit language. His lewd behaviour at the office party was the subject of a formal complaint.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being lewd, obscene, or indecent. Behaviour or expression that is sexually vulgar, offensive, or inappropriate. The characteristic of showing sexual desire in a crude or inappropriate manner.
example_sentence: The lewdness of his remarks made several colleagues feel deeply uncomfortable and disrespected. She reported the lewdness she had witnessed at the event to the organising committee. The play was banned in several cities because of the perceived lewdness of certain scenes. Laws against public lewdness are designed to protect people from unwanted exposure to indecent behaviour. He was charged with lewdness after his behaviour in the shopping centre was reported by witnesses.

english_meaning: Related to vocabulary of a language. Connected with dictionary words and their meanings. Refers to word choice and word structure. Used in linguistics to describe word-level elements.
example_sentence: The lexical meaning of the word changed over time. Students studied the lexical features of the text. The dictionary provides lexical information for each entry. Lexical analysis helps in understanding word usage in sentences.

english_meaning: In terms of words, vocabulary, or the meaning and use of words in a language. Something related to the vocabulary of a language, the meanings of words, or the way words are used and organized in a language. It focuses on words themselves rather than grammar or sentence structure.
example_sentence: The two words are lexically similar but have different meanings. The dictionary explains the term lexically and grammatically. English and German are lexically related in many ways. The sentence is lexically simple and easy to understand.

english_meaning: The vocabulary of a language, a person, a group, or a subject. It can also mean a dictionary that contains words and their meanings. The complete set of words in a language. The vocabulary used by a particular person, profession, or field. A dictionary or reference book containing words and their meanings. The collection of terms associated with a specific subject or discipline.
example_sentence: The scientist used a specialized lexicon of technical terms in her research paper. Children gradually expand their lexicon as they learn new words. The professor recommended a historical lexicon for studying ancient languages. Medical students must become familiar with the lexicon of anatomy and physiology.

english_meaning: Someone who loves words. A person who loves words, enjoys wordplay, puns, or the study of words.
example_sentence: The lexophile collected dictionaries from around the world. As a lexophile, she enjoyed creating puns at every opportunity. Crossword puzzles are a favorite pastime for many lexophiles. The lexophile explained the origins of unusual words to his friends.

english_meaning: The state of being legally responsible for something. A debt or financial obligation. A person or thing whose presence is likely to cause embarrassment or disadvantage. The amount of money that a person or company owes. Legal responsibility for one's acts or omissions.
example_sentence: The company has huge liabilities on its balance sheet. Drivers must accept liability for any accident they cause. His drinking habit has become a serious liability to the team. The insurance covers the liability of the employer towards workers. Total assets minus total liabilities equal the owner's equity.

english_meaning: Legally responsible or obligated for something. Likely to do or be subject to something. Exposed to a particular risk, penalty, or consequence.
example_sentence: The company was held liable for the injuries sustained by workers on the construction site. Anyone found in possession of the substance will be liable to a heavy fine. She was warned that ignoring the contract terms would make her personally liable for any losses. He felt liable for the misunderstanding and immediately offered to correct the mistake. If the product is faulty, the manufacturer is liable to replace it or provide a full refund.

english_meaning: To establish a working relationship or communication link between groups or individuals. It involves acting as a bridge to ensure coordination and information exchange. It is frequently used in business and military contexts to describe cooperation.
example_sentence: She was hired to liaise between the marketing department and the production team. It is essential to liaise regularly with local authorities during the construction project. The officer will liaise with the embassy to coordinate the dignitary's visit. Our school needs to liaise more closely with parents regarding student progress.

english_meaning: A relationship between two organizations or different departments in an organization, involving the exchange of information or ideas. A person whose job is to make sure there is a good relationship between two groups or organizations. A secret sexual relationship, especially if one or both partners are already in a relationship with somebody else. Communication between people or groups who work with each other.
example_sentence: She works as a liaison between the school and parents. The manager acted as a liaison to resolve the conflict. There is a strong liaison between the two companies. He was accused of having a secret liaison.

english_meaning: Someone is lying, mockingly accusing. To accuse someone of lying, often in a humorous way, suggesting that their dishonesty is obvious and exaggerated.
example_sentence: Liar liar pants on fire, admit the truth. He shouted liar liar pants on fire at the kid for sneaking cookies. Friends teased him saying liar liar pants on fire. The chant “liar liar pants on fire” is often used in playful arguments.

english_meaning: A published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation. The act of publishing a false and injurious statement about someone. To write and publish defamatory statements about a person. A written defamation, as opposed to spoken defamation which is slander.
example_sentence: The newspaper was sued for libel after publishing a false story about the businessman's finances. She threatened to take legal action for libel if the magazine did not retract the article immediately. The court ruled that the statements made in the report amounted to libel and awarded damages. He had to prove that the claim was false and damaging in order to succeed in his libel case. Publishing a libel can result in serious legal and financial consequences for both the writer and the editor.

english_meaning: Open minded or generous. A person or idea that supports freedom, tolerance, and progress. It may also describe someone who gives freely or does not follow strict traditional limits. In politics it refers to supporting individual rights, equality, and social reform.
example_sentence: She has a liberal attitude toward different cultures and beliefs. The charity received a liberal donation from a local businessman. The professor encourages liberal thinking and open discussion in class. Many young voters support liberal social policies. Her parents are very liberal & allow her a lot of freedom.

english_meaning: To free a country or a person from the control of somebody else. To free somebody from something that limits their control over and pleasure in their own life. To release someone from control, duties, limits, or prison.
example_sentence: The soldiers worked hard to liberate the captured city. Education can liberate people from ignorance. She felt liberated after speaking the truth. The organization aims to liberate victims from exploitation.

english_meaning: Freedom from slavery or oppression. Release from captivity or prison. Independence from foreign control. Emotional or mental freedom. Relief from difficulties or suffering. The act of freeing someone or something. Deliverance from fear or limitations. Social or political emancipation.
example_sentence: The nation celebrated its liberation from colonial rule. Education gave her liberation from ignorance and fear. The prisoners finally gained liberation after many years. Meditation brought him a sense of mental liberation.

english_meaning: A person who freely indulges in sensual pleasures without regard for moral principles. Someone who acts without moral or sexual restraint. A person who rejects accepted morality and pursues a life of indulgence.
example_sentence: The novel's protagonist was a libertine who lived entirely for pleasure and refused to be bound by social conventions. He was known as a libertine whose extravagant lifestyle scandalised polite society. Her memoir described how she had once been a libertine before a personal crisis changed her outlook on life. The libertine made no apology for his way of life and claimed that it harmed no one. Historical accounts describe the court as a gathering of libertines who spent vast fortunes on entertainment.

english_meaning: Freedom to act, speak, or think without unfair restriction. The state of being free. A person has liberty when they can make choices, express opinions, and live without unnecessary control or oppression.
example_sentence: Everyone deserves liberty and justice. The country fought for its liberty. She values her personal liberty. Freedom of speech is an important liberty.

english_meaning: Plural of louse. Small parasitic insects that live on the skin or in the hair of mammals and birds. External parasites that feed on blood or skin debris and are commonly associated with poor hygiene or close contact.
example_sentence: The school sent a letter home informing parents that several children had been found to have head lice. Lice can spread quickly among children who share hats, combs, or other personal items. The pharmacist recommended a medicated shampoo to treat the head lice effectively. Lice infestations can cause intense itching and irritation of the scalp. It is important to treat all members of the household if one person is found to have lice.

english_meaning: An official permit allowing a person to do or own something. Formal permission granted by an authority. Excessive freedom in behaviour or expression. Freedom taken by a writer or artist from strict rules.
example_sentence: He renewed his driving licence last month. The restaurant lost its licence to sell food. Such licence in speech cannot be tolerated. The poet used poetic licence to change the facts.

english_meaning: Official permission to do, own, sell, or use something. A document or certificate proving that legal permission has been granted. Permission given by an owner to use intellectual property, technology, or a product. Freedom to behave or create with fewer usual restrictions. To officially permit a person, business, product, or activity. To authorize another party to use or sell something under stated conditions.
example_sentence: She renewed her driving license before it expired. The restaurant has a license to serve food late at night. The company licensed its software to several schools. The novel gives the writer license to imagine events beyond the historical record.

english_meaning: An opportunity, right, or business arrangement that makes it unusually easy to earn very large profits. A situation in which income is almost guaranteed with little risk or competition. A figurative expression for a highly lucrative advantage, not a literal authority to create currency.
example_sentence: The exclusive contract became a license to print money. During the boom, owning that patent was like having a license to print money. Critics called the new monopoly a license to print money. The popular franchise gave the studio a license to print money.

english_meaning: Having official or legal permission to perform an activity, operate a business, or possess something. Formally qualified, approved, or certified by an authorized body. Produced, sold, or used with the permission of the legal owner. Granted under a license.
example_sentence: She is a licensed pharmacist at the local hospital. Only licensed drivers may operate these vehicles. The shop sells officially licensed sports merchandise. The software is licensed for use on three computers.

english_meaning: An old or literary word meaning a dead body or corpse. In fantasy stories, games, and novels, a lich is an undead wizard or magician who gains immortality through dark magic. The word is rarely used in modern everyday English except in fantasy contexts.
synonyms: ["Corpse","Cadaver","Dead body","Remains","Undead sorcerer","Undead wizard","Necromancer (related","but not identical)","Dark mage"]
example_sentence: The ancient legend spoke of a powerful lich guarding the hidden treasure. The villagers discovered a lich buried beneath the old church. In the fantasy game, the hero fought a terrifying lich. The wizard feared becoming a lich after practising forbidden magic.

english_meaning: Permitted by law or accepted rules. Lawful, legal, and sanctioned by authority. Not forbidden or prohibited by any relevant rules or regulations.
example_sentence: The transaction was confirmed to be entirely licit and had been approved by the relevant authorities. She made sure all her business activities were licit before signing any contracts. The use of certain substances is licit in some jurisdictions but strictly prohibited in others. He was careful to ensure that every aspect of the arrangement was licit and properly documented. The legal team verified that the practice was licit under both national and international law.

english_meaning: To move your tongue over the surface of something in order to eat it, make it wet or clean it. To easily defeat somebody or deal with something. To pass the tongue over. A quick stroke of the tongue or a light blow. In music, it can mean a short, catchy phrase.
example_sentence: He licked his fingers. I am tired of licking envelopes. Can I have a lick of your ice cream? The child tried to lick the ice cream before it melted. The dog licked his owner's hand happily. Our team managed to lick the opponents in the final match.

english_meaning: A severe defeat in a battle game. The act of inflicting corporal punishment with repeated blows. An unsuccessful ending to a struggle or contest. The act of passing the tongue over something.
example_sentence: The flames were now licking at their feet. His father threatened to give him a licking if he didn't stop misbehaving. The dog was licking its paws after playing outside. She kept licking the ice cream before it melted. The child got a licking for breaking the window. Our team took a licking in the final match.

english_meaning: A person who flatters someone in power to gain favor. A person who behaves in an overly submissive and flattering way toward someone powerful, usually for personal benefit. The word carries a strong negative tone and suggests lack of self respect and sincerity.
example_sentence: He was known as a lickspittle who praised the boss at every opportunity. The politician surrounded himself with lickspittles instead of honest advisors. She refused to act like a lickspittle just to secure a promotion. No one respected him because he behaved like a lickspittle around authority.

english_meaning: To rest with the body or an object stretched horizontally against a surface. To remain level, smooth, or pressed down without rising or curling.
example_sentence: Lie flat on your back and relax your shoulders. The map will lie flat after you press the folds. He had to lie flat to avoid being seen. Let the wet pages dry while they lie flat.

english_meaning: A feudal lord entitled to allegiance and service. A loyal subject or vassal bound to serve their lord. Describing the relationship of loyalty between a lord and their subjects. Used historically to address or refer to a sovereign or feudal superior.
example_sentence: The knight swore an oath of loyalty to his liege and vowed to defend the kingdom. Every vassal owed their liege a period of military service each year. The villagers pledged their allegiance to their liege at the ceremony held in the great hall. In medieval society the relationship between a liege and his subjects was one of mutual obligation. The term liege is still used in some ceremonial contexts to describe the bond between a monarch and their subjects.

english_meaning: Something given instead of another thing. A substitute or replacement, often used in formal or legal language to mean one thing is provided in place of another, such as time off instead of payment or an alternative option instead of the original one.
example_sentence: He received extra leave in lieu of overtime pay. The company offered compensation in lieu of a bonus. She accepted an apology in lieu of legal action. Tea was served in lieu of coffee at the meeting.

english_meaning: An officer in the armed forces ranking below a captain. A deputy who acts on behalf of a superior. A trusted assistant carrying out a leader's orders.
example_sentence: He was promoted to lieutenant last year. The lieutenant led the patrol through the valley. She is the mayor's most trusted lieutenant. Two lieutenants were assigned to the investigation.

english_meaning: To place oneself in a flat or horizontal position, usually for rest, sleep, or relaxation. It can also mean yielding or surrendering in some contexts.
