example_sentence: After a long day at work, I just want to lie down. The doctor advised him to lie down for a few minutes. She lay down on the grass and watched the clouds. The tired child lay down immediately after reaching home.

english_meaning: A person who brings energy, enthusiasm, joy, and liveliness to a group, event, or situation. A person makes others happy, keeps conversations alive, and spreads positive energy wherever they go.
example_sentence: He is the life and soul of the party. Ali is the life and soul of every party, everyone feels happy when he’s around. Without her, the meeting felt dull; she’s truly the life and soul of our team. His jokes and laughter make him the life and soul of any gathering. Even in difficult times, she remains the life and soul of her family.

english_meaning: The way in which a person lives, including habits, attitudes, and daily activities. The typical manner of living that reflects values and interests. A style of life associated with a particular group or culture. The choices one makes about diet, exercise, work, and leisure.
synonyms: ["Way of life","Living habits","Routine","Life pattern","Behavior pattern","Daily life"]
example_sentence: A healthy lifestyle includes regular exercise and balanced diet. His busy lifestyle leaves little time for relaxation. They adopted a more sustainable lifestyle. Lifestyle choices can affect long-term health.

english_meaning: A strong band of fibrous tissue that connects bones to other bones, stabilizing and supporting joints. It helps limit movement to prevent injury. Ligaments are flexible but not elastic; they maintain joint stability. Injuries to ligaments include sprains and tears.
example_sentence: The anterior cruciate ligament in the knee is commonly injured in athletes. She tore a ligament in her ankle while playing football. Proper warm-up exercises help protect ligaments from damage. Ligaments are less elastic than tendons but equally important for joint stability.

english_meaning: To tie or bind something tightly with a thread or cord. To tie off a blood vessel, duct, or tube during a surgical procedure. In biochemistry, to join two molecules or strands of DNA together.
example_sentence: The surgeon had to ligate the artery to stop the bleeding. Doctors ligate the tube during this type of operation. The technician learned how to ligate DNA fragments in the lab. They ligate the vessel carefully to avoid further damage.

english_meaning: The act of tying or binding something tightly, especially a blood vessel or duct during surgery. A surgical procedure in which a tube or vessel is tied off, as in tubal ligation. In biochemistry, the joining together of two strands of DNA or other molecules.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed ligation of the damaged artery. She chose tubal ligation as a permanent method of contraception. Ligation of the vessel stopped the bleeding immediately. The experiment required the ligation of two DNA fragments.

english_meaning: A thread, cord, or band used to tie something tightly, especially a blood vessel during surgery. Something that binds or unites two things. In printing, two or more letters joined together as a single character. In music, a curved line joining notes to be played smoothly.
example_sentence: The doctor applied a ligature to stop the bleeding. A tight ligature was found around the parcel. Old manuscripts often use a ligature for certain letter pairs. The nurse handed the surgeon a fresh ligature.

english_meaning: A person who attends events, parties, or functions in order to enjoy free food, drink, or entertainment. In angling, a floating line or baited tackle left in the water to catch fish, especially pike. A plank or beam laid horizontally, used in scaffolding or building work.
example_sentence: The party was full of liggers looking for free drinks. He was dismissed as a ligger by the other guests. The angler left a ligger in the lake overnight. Workers fixed another ligger across the scaffolding.

word: Light at the end of the tunnel
english_meaning: A sign of hope after a long period of difficulty or struggle. The feeling that hardships are coming to an end and better times are ahead.
example_sentence: After months of struggle, he saw the light at the end of the tunnel. After months of hard work, he finally saw the light at the end of the tunnel when he got a job offer.

english_meaning: A sudden moment of understanding or realization. A moment when a bright new idea comes to mind. A flash of insight that makes something clear. The instant when a solution to a problem becomes obvious.
example_sentence: That conversation was a real light bulb moment for me. Her light bulb moment led to a successful new business. The experiment gave the students a light bulb moment. After hours of study, he finally had a light bulb moment.

english_meaning: The distance that light travels in one year, about 9·46 trillion kilometers. A unit used in astronomy to measure vast distances between stars and galaxies. An extremely great distance or difference, used informally for emphasis.
example_sentence: The nearest star is more than four light-years away. Astronomers measure galactic distances in light-years. A light-year is a measure of distance, not of time. Their views on the subject are light-years apart.

english_meaning: A feeling of dizziness, faintness, or a sensation that one might lose consciousness. A sense of unsteadiness or confusion in the head. The condition of feeling woozy or about to faint, often caused by a drop in blood pressure or lack of oxygen.
example_sentence: She experienced lightheadedness when she stood up too quickly from the chair. The patient reported lightheadedness and shortness of breath after climbing the stairs. Dehydration is one of the most common causes of sudden lightheadedness in otherwise healthy people. He sat down immediately when he felt a wave of lightheadedness come over him during the presentation. The doctor warned that the medication could cause lightheadedness, particularly during the first week of use.

english_meaning: A rare or unusual event is unlikely to happen again in the same way. Rare events do not usually repeat. Bad luck is unlikely to happen again. Extraordinary success is hard to repeat. Situations rarely occur exactly the same way twice.
synonyms: ["Once in a blue moon","A rare occurrence","History does not repeat itself exactly","Unlikely to happen again"]
antonyms: ["History repeats itself","It can happen again","Recurring event","Patterns repeat"]
example_sentence: After failing the exam once, she stayed calm because lightning never strikes twice. He lost his wallet last week, but he believes lightning never strikes twice. The team lost badly in the first match, but they are confident lightning never strikes twice. She got a rare opportunity and doubts she will get the same chance again, since lightning never strikes twice.

part_of_speech: Verb, Noun, Adjective, Adverb, Preposition, Conjunction
english_meaning: To enjoy, approve of, or feel attracted to someone or something. To want or prefer something. Similar to or resembling someone or something. In the same way as. Used to introduce an example. A preference or thing one enjoys. A social-media indication of approval. Typical of or characteristic of.
example_sentence: I like the way you explained the problem. This fabric feels like silk. Outdoor activities like hiking can reduce stress. Her post received more than a thousand likes.

english_meaning: With great ease and little resistance. Smoothly and quickly through something that would normally be difficult. Used to emphasize effortless cutting, movement, or progress.
example_sentence: The sharp blade went through the rope like a knife through butter. Their striker cut through the defense like a knife through butter. The new drill passed through the wood like a knife through butter. She moved through the simple questions like a knife through butter.

english_meaning: To enjoy an activity in general. To take pleasure in repeatedly performing an action. To have a positive preference for an experience or habit. To find a particular activity pleasant or satisfying.
synonyms: ["Enjoy doing","Take pleasure in","Be fond of","Delight in","Prefer doing"]
example_sentence: I like walking along the beach at dawn. He likes cooking for his friends on weekends. They like learning new languages together. She does not like waiting in long queues.

english_meaning: A son often behaves, thinks, or has qualities similar to his father. Used when a boy or man shows behavior, talents, habits, personality, or character similar to his father. It may be used positively for good qualities or negatively for bad habits.
synonyms: ["A chip off the old block","The apple does not fall far from the tree","Following in his father’s footsteps","Two peas in a pod"]
antonyms: ["Different as night and day","Nothing like his father","Opposites in nature"]
example_sentence: Ahmed is a brilliant carpenter just like his father, Like father, like son. His father was very generous, and he helps everyone too, Like father, like son. Both the father and son love cricket and play professionally, Like father, like son. The boy became a successful teacher, following his father’s path, Like father, like son.

english_meaning: Used to ask what someone wants for a particular purpose, meal, occasion, or result. To desire something in exchange for or in relation to something else. To prefer a person or thing for a particular role or use. To wish a particular outcome for someone or something.
synonyms: ["Want for","Prefer for","Choose for","Desire for","Wish for","Select for"]
example_sentence: What would you like for breakfast? I would like for everyone to remain calm. Which candidate would you like for the leading role? She asked what he would like for his birthday.

english_meaning: Two people or things that do not mix or get along well together. Completely different in nature.
example_sentence: My brother and I are like oil and water; we never agree on anything. Politics and honesty often seem like oil and water. She and her coworker are like oil and water; they can’t work together peacefully. Their ideas are like oil and water, so cooperation is difficult.

english_meaning: To enjoy or prefer doing something, especially as a choice or habit. To want to do something. To consider an action pleasant or desirable. Used politely to express a wish, intention, or offer.
example_sentence: I like to read before going to sleep. She would like to speak with the manager. We like to arrive early for important meetings. Would you like to join us for dinner?

word: Like two peas in a pod
english_meaning: So similar as to be indistinguishable or very closely alike. Having a very close relationship or sharing exactly the same interests.
synonyms: ["Identical","Indistinguishable","Exactly Alike","Very Similar","Inseparable","Carbon Copies","Dead Ringers","Spitting Images","Closely Knit"]
example_sentence: The twins are like two peas in a pod, always dressing exactly the same. My best friend and I are like two peas in a pod. Those two brothers are like two peas in a pod when it comes to their sense of humor. Growing up, they were like two peas in a pod and went everywhere together.

english_meaning: Plural of likeness. The state of being similar or alike in appearance. A representation or portrait of a person or thing. Similarities shared between two or more people or objects.
example_sentence: The artist was renowned for the likenesses she captured in her portrait paintings. The twins bore remarkable likenesses to each other that often confused their teachers at school. The gallery displayed likenesses of important figures from the town's history. She noted the striking likenesses between the two ancient artefacts found at different archaeological sites. The sculptor was commissioned to produce likenesses of all twelve founding members of the institution.

english_meaning: In the same way or manner. Also or in addition. Used to return a greeting or good wish. Similarly in a comparable situation. Equally or correspondingly.
example_sentence: She completed the assignment carefully, and her partner did likewise. The first proposal was rejected; likewise, the second failed to gain support. It was lovely meeting you, and likewise to you. Parents should listen to children, and children should likewise respect their parents.

english_meaning: A shrub or small tree bearing fragrant clusters of purple, pink, or white flowers. The pale purple colour of these flowers. Describing something of a light purple shade.
example_sentence: The garden was filled with the scent of lilac. She painted her room a soft lilac. A lilac bush grew beside the gate. He gave her a bunch of lilac flowers.

english_meaning: Pure white in colour, like the petals of a lily. Completely clean, innocent, or free from guilt. Describing a reputation or record that is entirely without fault.
example_sentence: She wore a lily-white gown at the ceremony. The mountain peaks were lily-white after the snowfall. His record is not as lily-white as he claims. The child raised her lily-white hands.

english_meaning: A flat, pale green or white bean with a soft, buttery texture. A legume eaten fresh or dried in soups and stews. The plant that produces these beans. A protein-rich food also known as the butter bean.
example_sentence: Lima beans give the stew a creamy texture. She simmered lima beans with herbs. Dried lima beans need soaking before cooking. Lima beans are also called butter beans.

english_meaning: An arm or leg of a person or four-legged animal. A large branch of a tree. The edge of the disk of a celestial body.
example_sentence: He lost the use of one limb after the accident. The heavy snow caused a large limb of the oak tree to break. Birds were perched on every limb of the tree. The lunar limb was clearly visible through the telescope.

english_meaning: A small green citrus fruit with sharp, acidic juice. A fruit used for flavouring food and drinks. A white substance made from limestone, used in building and farming. A bright yellowish-green colour.
example_sentence: He added a squeeze of lime to the salad. Lime juice makes the drink wonderfully refreshing. The farmer spread lime to improve the soil. She chose lime green tiles for the bathroom.

english_meaning: A bright yellowish-green colour resembling the skin of a lime. Describing something of this vivid green shade. Used in design and fashion to suggest freshness or energy.
example_sentence: He bought a lime-green shirt for the trip. The kitchen walls were painted lime-green. Her lime-green bag stood out in the crowd. The team's new kit is lime-green and black.

english_meaning: An intense, involuntary state of romantic attraction toward another person. An overwhelming infatuation with strong emotional dependence. Passionate longing for reciprocation of feelings. A psychological state of deep romantic obsession. Intense emotional attachment marked by intrusive thoughts.
example_sentence: He was experiencing limerence for his new colleague. Limerence often fades as a relationship matures. Psychologists distinguish limerence from true love. Her limerence made her think about him constantly.

english_meaning: A humorous or comic poem of five lines with a specific rhythm and rhyme scheme. A form of verse in which the first, second, and fifth lines rhyme with each other, while the shorter third and fourth lines rhyme with each other. A city in the southwest of Ireland.
example_sentence: He entertained the children by reciting a silly limerick about a cat who refused to wear a hat. Writing a good limerick requires a sharp sense of humour and a feel for rhythm and rhyme. The class competition challenged every student to compose an original limerick on the theme of school life. She burst out laughing when she read the limerick her friend had scribbled on a birthday card. Limerick is the third largest city in Ireland and has a rich history dating back to Viking times.

english_meaning: Relating to a transitional or intermediate state, stage, or position. Occupying the threshold between two phases or conditions. Of or relating to a sensory threshold or the point of crossing a boundary.
example_sentence: Adolescence is widely described as a liminal stage between childhood and full adulthood. The abandoned train station had a haunting, liminal quality that made it feel suspended in time. She found herself in a liminal space between the job she had left and the one she was about to start. The liminal period between one government and the next can be a time of uncertainty and transition. Artists are often drawn to liminal spaces because they carry an atmosphere of ambiguity and possibility.

english_meaning: To restrict something according to a particular factor, rule, amount, or condition. To cause a person or thing to have less freedom, scope, or capacity because of something. To determine a boundary through a specified constraint.
example_sentence: Production is limited by the available supply of water. The project was limited by a small budget. Our choices are limited by time and distance. Growth may be limited by poor soil conditions.

english_meaning: To restrict someone or something to a particular amount, number, place, group, or activity. To allow only a specified range or choice. To confine the effect, discussion, or use of something to a stated boundary.
example_sentence: Please limit your answer to two paragraphs. The offer is limited to new customers. We should limit the discussion to relevant facts. Doctors advised him to limit himself to light exercise.

english_meaning: A person or organism that loves or prefers lakes and calm freshwater environments
synonyms: ["Lake lover","Freshwater organism","Still water species","Lake dwelling organism"]
example_sentence: The scientist studied several limnophile species living in the lake. As a limnophile, she enjoys spending weekends near quiet lakes. Many aquatic plants in the region are limnophile and grow well in still water. The park attracts limnophile visitors who appreciate lake ecosystems.

english_meaning: A large luxurious car, often driven by a chauffeur. A long formal vehicle used for special events or important passengers. Historically, a closed passenger compartment separated from the driver.
example_sentence: A limousine waited outside the hotel. They hired a limousine for the wedding. The actor arrived at the theater in a black limousine. A chauffeur opened the limousine door for the guests.

english_meaning: To walk with difficulty, especially due to an injured leg or foot. Lacking firmness, stiffness, or energy. A walking gait characterised by uneven steps due to injury or pain. Weak or floppy in consistency or character.
example_sentence: He limped off the field after sustaining a painful injury to his ankle during the match. The dog returned home with a limp and was taken to the vet for examination. She held out a limp handshake that conveyed a lack of confidence and enthusiasm. The flowers had gone limp in the heat and needed to be placed in water immediately. Despite his limp, he insisted on completing the last stretch of the charity walk.

english_meaning: Having a wrist that is bent, loose, or lacking firmness. Weak, indecisive, or lacking force. Sometimes used as an offensive stereotype about an effeminate man and therefore best avoided when referring to people.
example_sentence: The dancer avoided a limp-wristed pose by holding her hands firmly. Critics described the response as limp-wristed and ineffective. His limp-wristed handshake suggested nervousness. The term can be offensive when used to describe a person’s manner.

english_meaning: A small marine mollusk with a low cone-shaped shell that clings tightly to rocks. A person who stays very close to someone and is difficult to detach. Something that attaches itself firmly to a surface.
example_sentence: A limpet clung to the rock below the waterline. The child held on to her mother like a limpet. We found several limpets in the tidal pool. He became a limpet at social events and never left his friend’s side.

english_meaning: An explosive device designed to attach magnetically or otherwise to the hull of a ship. A naval mine placed directly on a target by a diver or operative. A concealed charge that adheres firmly to a metal surface.
example_sentence: The divers searched the hull for a suspected limpet mine. A limpet mine can be attached below a ship’s waterline. The navy trained crews to detect and remove limpet mines. Investigators found evidence of a limpet mine on the damaged vessel.

english_meaning: Clear and transparent, especially of water or other liquids. Easy to understand; clear and lucid in style or expression. Having a quality of serene clarity.
example_sentence: The limpid waters of the mountain lake reflected the surrounding peaks perfectly on a still morning. Her limpid prose style made even the most complex ideas accessible to a general readership. The limpid blue of the sky above the desert was unlike anything he had ever seen before. The limpid stream ran over smooth white pebbles, making a gentle musical sound. She admired the limpid clarity of the crystal glass as she held it up to the light.

english_meaning: In a weak, loose, or lifeless way. Without firmness, energy, or resistance. In a manner that hangs or moves without strength.
example_sentence: His injured arm hung limply at his side. The wet flag drooped limply from the pole. She sank limply into the chair after the race. He shook my hand limply and looked away.

english_meaning: To place people or objects in a row or order. To schedule or organize activities or events. To be ready or prepared for something. To match or correspond with something.
example_sentence: Students lined up outside the classroom before the assembly. We need to line up the chairs for the meeting. He lined up several interviews for next week. The planets line up perfectly during the eclipse.

english_meaning: Direct descent from an ancestor. A family line or ancestry. A sequence of people, animals, ideas, or things connected by origin. A historical chain of development or inheritance.
example_sentence: The family traced its lineage back several centuries. The horse came from a famous racing lineage. Scholars studied the lineage of that philosophical idea. Her music has a clear lineage in folk tradition.

english_meaning: In a direct line of descent from an ancestor. Relating to or consisting of lines. Inherited or transmitted in a direct family line from parent to child.
example_sentence: He was the lineal descendant of one of the country's founding leaders. The estate was passed to the lineal heir according to the terms of the original grant. She traced her lineal ancestry back seven generations to a small village in the highlands. The law required lineal proof of descent before any claim to the title could be considered. His lineal connection to the royal family was documented in the official records held by the court.

english_meaning: A strong cloth made from the fibres of the flax plant. Fabric woven from flax, valued for its coolness and durability. Household articles such as sheets, tablecloths, and towels. Clothing or bedding made from such cloth. Made of or resembling flax fabric.
example_sentence: He wore a white linen shirt in the summer heat. The hotel changes its bed linen every day. Linen wrinkles easily but feels wonderfully cool. She stored the table linen in a wooden chest.

english_meaning: To continue to exist for longer than expected. To be slow in parting or in quitting something. To stay somewhere for longer because you do not want to leave, to spend a long time doing something.
example_sentence: His eyes lingered on the diamond ring on her finger. He lingered on for several month after the heart attack.

english_meaning: Women’s underwear and nightwear, usually designed to be attractive, delicate, or fashionable. It includes items like bras, panties, camisoles, and nightgowns.
example_sentence: She bought new lingerie for her honeymoon. The shop specializes in luxury lingerie made of silk and lace. Her wardrobe includes both comfortable and stylish lingerie. The fashion show featured elegant lingerie designs.

english_meaning: A person who is skilled in foreign languages. A person who studies linguistics, the science of language. An expert in or student of the structure and development of language and languages.
example_sentence: As a trained linguist, she could identify the origin of a dialect from just a few sentences. The linguist spent her career studying the grammar of endangered languages in the Pacific. He was a gifted linguist who had mastered seven languages by the age of thirty. The university's linguistics department attracted some of the most respected linguists in the world. The linguist argued that every language, however small, encodes unique ways of understanding the world.

english_meaning: Relating to language or the study of language and linguistics. Of or pertaining to the structure, history, or use of language. Concerned with the formal and analytical study of language as a system.
example_sentence: The study identified several interesting linguistic patterns shared across three unrelated languages. She had a remarkable linguistic ability and could switch between five languages with ease. The university offered a course in linguistic analysis that covered everything from phonetics to syntax. Linguistic diversity is one of humanity's greatest cultural assets and must be preserved. The researcher compared the linguistic features of the two dialects spoken in neighbouring valleys.

english_meaning: To connect one thing with another so that they work together or become part of a larger system. It can be used for physical connections like machines and cables, or for abstract ideas such as linking a plan with a strategy or linking people with an organization.
example_sentence: The new software will link in with the existing database. The community project is designed to link in with local schools. Please link in the new device before starting the system. His research links in closely with climate policy discussions.

english_meaning: To connect, relate, or associate one thing with another. It can be used in physical, digital, or abstract contexts. For example, connecting two ideas, attaching a webpage to another webpage, or relating a problem to a specific cause.
example_sentence: Researchers link air pollution to respiratory diseases. This button links to the company’s official website. The report links poor planning to project failure. He linked his success to hard work and discipline.

english_meaning: To connect people, systems, or things so they work together. To join with someone for a shared purpose such as work, travel, or partnership. To meet someone at a planned place. To establish communication between groups, devices, or individuals.
example_sentence: The two companies decided to link up for a new project. We will link up with the research team tomorrow morning. The railway lines link up several major cities. She linked up with her old friends after many years.

english_meaning: To connect, join, or cooperate with a person, group, or organization. It can refer to meeting someone, forming a partnership, or establishing communication for work, travel, or shared goals.
antonyms: ["Separate from","Disconnect from","Break away from","Split from","Part from"]
example_sentence: We will link up with our partners to complete the project. She linked up with her old classmates during the reunion. The two companies linked up with each other for a new business venture. The hikers planned to link up with the rest of the group at the campsite.

english_meaning: Extremely brave, courageous, and fearless. Having great strength of character and determination. Displaying bravery in the face of danger. Bold and heroic in nature. Showing the courage of a lion.
example_sentence: The lion-hearted soldier saved many lives that day. She is a lion-hearted leader admired by everyone. Only a lion-hearted person can face such trials. The captain gave a lion-hearted speech before the match.

english_meaning: To treat someone as very important or famous. To give someone a lot of public attention, admiration, or praise, often like they are a celebrity or a hero
example_sentence: The media lionized the young scientist for her groundbreaking research. After the championship, the team was lionized by their fans. Critics often lionize actors for their latest performances. The author was lionized at the book festival for her new novel.

english_meaning: Refers to the biblical idea of peace and harmony between natural enemies, inspired by Isaiah's prophecy. Also used in the saying 'March comes in like a lion and goes out like a lamb' meaning a rough start and peaceful end.
example_sentence: The peace agreement was celebrated as a lions and lambs moment. March came in like a lion and went out like a lamb this year. The coalition government was a rare lions and lambs arrangement. She described their unlikely friendship as a lions and lambs situation.

english_meaning: The largest portion or most important share of something. To get or take most of something, often leaving little for others.
example_sentence: He took the lion’s share of the profit. The manager took the lion’s share of the credit for the project. When profits were divided, the owner received the lion’s share. In most families, the mother does the lion’s share of the household work. The city spends the lion’s share of its budget on education.

english_meaning: Either of the two soft fleshy edges that form the opening of the mouth. The outer edge or rim of a container, cup, or wound. Rude or impertinent talk. To touch something with the lips or to speak words quietly.
example_sentence: Her lips were dry because of the cold weather. He put a finger to his lips to ask for silence. The child chipped the lip of the glass. Do not give me any lip about the rules.

english_meaning: A substance that flows freely and takes the shape of its container while keeping a fixed volume. One of the three common states of matter, between solid and gas. Having the smooth, flowing quality of a liquid. In finance, describing assets that can quickly be converted into cash. Clear, bright, and pure in sound or appearance.
example_sentence: Water is the most common liquid on earth. Pour the liquid slowly into the measuring cup. The company keeps part of its wealth in liquid assets. She admired the liquid movement of the dancer.

english_meaning: To sell property or business assets in order to obtain cash, usually to pay debts. It can also mean to close or dissolve a business, organization, or financial position. In some contexts it means to eliminate or completely remove something.
example_sentence: The company decided to liquidate its assets to pay off outstanding debts. After years of losses, the owners chose to liquidate the business. He had to liquidate some investments to cover his medical expenses. The court ordered the firm to liquidate its properties and distribute the money to creditors. The Govt tried to liquidate the rebel movement and failed.

english_meaning: The process of closing a business by selling its assets to pay debts. It can also mean converting assets into cash or eliminating something.
example_sentence: The company went into liquidation after suffering heavy financial losses. During liquidation, the firm's assets were sold to repay creditors. The court ordered the liquidation of the bankrupt corporation. Investors agreed to the liquidation of the failing project.

english_meaning: To change a solid or gas into a liquid. To become liquid. To melt or dissolve something into liquid form. To convert assets into cash.
example_sentence: Heat is used to liquify the frozen butter. The gas liquifies under high pressure. You can liquify the honey by warming it slightly. The company decided to liquify some of its assets to pay debts.

english_meaning: Alcoholic drink, especially spirits. Any liquid substance used in industry or cooking. A concentrated solution produced by boiling or dissolving a substance. Strong alcoholic beverages collectively.
example_sentence: The liquor store closed early on Sunday evenings in accordance with local regulations. He had never touched liquor in his life and politely declined the offer of a drink. The recipe called for a small amount of cooking liquor left over from the boiling of the vegetables. Bootleggers smuggled liquor across state borders during the era of prohibition in America. The island was known for producing a distinctive local liquor that tourists often brought home as a gift.

english_meaning: A speech defect in which the sound s is pronounced like th. To speak with such a defect. To say something in a soft or childish way. A slight speech impediment. The act of pronouncing sibilant sounds imperfectly.
example_sentence: The little boy speaks with a slight lisp. She had a lisp that made her sound charming. He lisped his words shyly. The child began to lisp her first sentences.

english_meaning: To pay attention to sound. To make an effort to hear someone or something. To give thoughtful attention to advice, a request, or an explanation. To obey or accept what someone says. Used to draw attention before speaking.
example_sentence: Please listen carefully to the instructions. She listens to her grandmother when she needs advice. Listen, we need to discuss this calmly. He stopped walking and listened for footsteps.

english_meaning: To try to hear a particular sound. To pay attention for an expected word, signal, or announcement. To use hearing to detect something specific. To wait attentively for an audible sign.
synonyms: ["Attend for","Wait to hear","Keep an ear out for","Detect","Monitor","Hear out for"]
example_sentence: Listen for the click before opening the lid. The doctor listened for changes in the patient’s breathing. We stood quietly and listened for the owl. Students listened for their numbers to be called.

english_meaning: To listen to a conversation, broadcast, or event. To secretly hear a conversation not intended for you. To join a call or meeting mainly as a listener. To tune in to a radio or online program.
example_sentence: Millions listened in to the live radio interview. I listened in while the engineers discussed the repair. She was accused of listening in on a private conversation. You may listen in without speaking during the meeting.

english_meaning: To secretly or quietly hear a conversation involving other people. To monitor a call, meeting, or discussion. To join an exchange as an observer rather than a participant. To overhear something deliberately.
example_sentence: The supervisor listened in on the customer-service call. I was invited to listen in on the planning meeting. They discovered someone listening in on their private discussion. Trainees listened in on experienced negotiators at work.

english_meaning: To pay special attention in order to hear a particular sound or message. To remain alert for an expected announcement. To try to notice someone approaching or calling. To monitor sounds for a specific signal.
synonyms: ["Listen for","Be alert for","Watch for","Await","Monitor","Keep an ear out for"]
example_sentence: Listen out for your name at the reception desk. We listened out for the sound of the rescue helicopter. Please listen out for the doorbell while I am outside. The mechanic listened out for any unusual engine noise.

english_meaning: To hear an entire recording, speech, or piece of music from beginning to end. To continue listening despite difficulty or interruption. To review audio carefully and completely. To hear all parts before forming an opinion.
example_sentence: I listened through the entire album on my journey home. Please listen through the recording before editing it. She listened through his long explanation without interrupting. The producer listened through every track twice.

english_meaning: To direct attention toward a sound or speaker. To hear and consider what someone says. To follow advice, instructions, or a warning. To play and pay attention to music, speech, or other recorded sound.
example_sentence: We listened to the rain falling on the roof. You should listen to your doctor’s advice. She listens to classical music while studying. The committee listened to both sides before deciding.

english_meaning: Used to tell people to pay close attention. To become attentive to what is about to be said. To hear and understand an important instruction. To focus carefully, especially in a group.
example_sentence: Listen up, everyone; the schedule has changed. The coach told the players to listen up. You need to listen up because this rule is important. The guide waited for the group to listen up before continuing.

english_meaning: An article written in the form of a list. A type of article that presents information as a numbered or bullet list. Each point usually explains one idea. Listicles are common in blogs, news websites, and social media because they are easy to read and quick to understand.
example_sentence: She shared a listicle about healthy eating habits. The website published a listicle on top travel destinations. Readers like listicles because they save time. He wrote a listicle explaining climate change facts.

english_meaning: The basic metric unit of volume, equal to one thousand milliliters. The amount of space taken up by one cubic decimeter of liquid. A common measure used for fuel, water, milk, and other liquids. A container or quantity holding this amount.
example_sentence: Please buy two liters of milk on your way home. The car's fuel tank holds forty liters of petrol. Doctors advise drinking at least two liters of water daily. She filled a one liter bottle before the hike.

english_meaning: Being the most basic meaning of a word or phrase, rather than an extended or poetic meaning. According with the letter of the scriptures. Not having or showing any imagination. That follows the original words exactly.
example_sentence: I am not referring to ‘small’ people in the literal sense of the word. The literal meaning of ‘petrify’ is ‘turn to stone’. The literal meaning of "television" is "seeing from a distance".

english_meaning: Using the real or original meaning of a word or phrase. In a literal, true, or accurate way. Used to emphasize the truth and accuracy of a statement or description.
example_sentence: They were responsible for literally millions of deaths. The word ‘planet’ literally means ‘wandering body’. She refused food and literally starved herself to death. The event literally stopped the traffic.

english_meaning: Relating to or concerned with literature or the writing of books. Of, relating to, or characteristic of literature as an art form. Knowledgeable about or interested in literature. Written in a style associated with high-quality literary works.
example_sentence: She published her first literary essay in a respected journal when she was only nineteen years old. The literary festival attracted writers, poets, and readers from across the world. His literary achievements were recognised with a lifetime award at the annual ceremony. The novel was praised for its rich literary style and deeply nuanced characters. She joined a literary society where members discussed and analysed works of fiction each month.

english_meaning: Written works, especially those considered to have artistic or intellectual value. The body of written works produced in a particular language, country, or period. Written material on a particular subject. The art of writing or producing written works of lasting value.
example_sentence: She devoted her life to the study of classical literature from ancient Greece and Rome. The library holds an extensive collection of literature from every continent and period. He had a deep passion for literature and could quote passages from memory at any time. The course introduced students to a wide range of literature spanning five centuries. Scientific literature on the subject suggests that the effects are far more complex than first thought.

english_meaning: Characterized by being thin, supple, and graceful. It often describes a person's body or movements that are flexible and elegant. It implies a natural ease of motion.
example_sentence: The lithe gymnast performed a series of flawless flips on the balance beam. She moved with the lithe grace of a cat through the crowded room. His lithe frame allowed him to squeeze through the narrow opening easily. Yoga helps practitioners maintain a lithe and flexible physique.

english_meaning: To take a dispute or claim to a court of law; to engage in legal proceedings.
example_sentence: He decided to litigate the case rather than accept the settlement. The company had to litigate to protect its patent rights. She was prepared to litigate if the insurer refused to pay. Some landlords choose to litigate rather than negotiate.

english_meaning: The process of taking legal action; engaging in or being subject to a lawsuit in a court of law.
example_sentence: The company faced costly litigation over its faulty products. He avoided litigation by settling the dispute out of court. Litigation can take years and cost millions of dollars. The two neighbours entered litigation over the boundary wall.

english_meaning: A lawyer who specialises in taking cases to court and arguing them. A legal professional who conducts lawsuits on behalf of clients. A person actively involved in legal proceedings as an advocate.
example_sentence: She is one of the finest litigators in the country. The firm hired an experienced litigator for the case. A good litigator prepares every detail before trial. He built his reputation as a fearless litigator.

english_meaning: Tending to go to law to settle disputes; overly eager or quick to take legal action. Concerned with lawsuits and legal proceedings. Showing a strong inclination to argue or quarrel. A litigious person or society frequently resorts to courts even over minor disagreements.
example_sentence: He has a litigious nature and sues anyone who annoys him. The company was caught in a long and litigious battle with its rivals. America is often described as a litigious society. Their litigious neighbour took them to court over the boundary wall. Doctors today work in an increasingly litigious environment.

english_meaning: The tendency to go to court or bring lawsuits too readily. Excessive eagerness to engage in legal disputes. A quarrelsome nature that leads to frequent legal action.
example_sentence: The company's litigiousness has cost it millions in legal fees. Critics complain about the growing litigiousness of modern society. His litigiousness made neighbours avoid him. Litigiousness often delays simple settlements.

english_meaning: A natural dye obtained from lichens that turns red in acid and blue in alkali. A substance used on paper strips to test acidity or alkalinity. Something used figuratively as a clear indicator of true nature.
example_sentence: The teacher dipped litmus paper into the solution. Litmus turns red when it touches an acid. We keep blue litmus strips in the laboratory cupboard. Litmus is one of the oldest chemical indicators.

english_meaning: A single decisive factor used to judge or evaluate something. A test that clearly shows the true nature, quality, or opinion of a person or thing. In chemistry, a test using litmus paper to show whether a substance is acidic or alkaline.
example_sentence: This vote will be a litmus test of public trust in the government. Honesty in small matters is a litmus test of character. The students performed a litmus test in the school laboratory. Support for the reform became a litmus test for the party.

english_meaning: A figure of speech in which an idea is expressed by denying its opposite. Understatement used deliberately for emphasis or politeness. A rhetorical device such as saying 'not bad' to mean 'very good'.
example_sentence: Saying she is not unkind is a classic example of litotes. The poet uses litotes to soften his criticism. Litotes can make praise sound modest and sincere. English speakers often use litotes without noticing it.

english_meaning: A metric unit of volume equal to one thousand cubic centimetres. The standard measure used for liquids such as water, milk, and fuel. A quantity of liquid equal to this unit.
example_sentence: Please buy two litres of milk from the shop. The car uses about seven litres of fuel per hundred kilometres. She drinks at least two litres of water every day. The bottle holds exactly one litre.

english_meaning: Trash or rubbish left lying around. Waste scattered in public places. Babies born to an animal in one birth. Objects lying in a messy way. A seat or bed carried by people. To drop trash carelessly. To spread around. To give birth to young animals.
example_sentence: Please do not throw litter in the park. The beach was covered with litter after the picnic. The cat had a litter of five kittens. Clothes littered the floor. The injured man was carried on a litter. The king traveled in a litter. People should not litter the streets. Books littered the table. The rabbit littered last night.

english_meaning: The smallest and thinnest finger of the hand, located at the outer edge. The fifth digit of the hand counting from the thumb. The finger often called the pinky in everyday speech. The smallest digit, used to add grip and balance when holding objects.
example_sentence: He broke his little finger during the football match. The little finger is the smallest digit on the hand. She hooked her little finger around his as a promise. A ring slipped easily off her little finger.

english_meaning: The smallest toe on the outer edge of the human foot. The fifth toe counting from the big toe. The tiny outer digit of the foot, often bumped against furniture. The smallest digit of the foot that helps with balance and stability.
example_sentence: He hit his little toe on the leg of the bed. The little toe is the smallest digit of the foot. Tight shoes often hurt the little toe. She broke her little toe last winter.

english_meaning: Relating to or situated on the shore of a sea, lake, or large body of water. The region lying along a shore. Belonging to the coastal area. A zone between high and low water marks.
example_sentence: The littoral zone is rich in marine life. Many countries depend on their littoral states for trade. The navy strengthened its littoral defence system. Littoral plants grow well near the water's edge. Researchers studied the littoral ecology of the region.

english_meaning: Used when you learn something new through experience, often after making a mistake or being surprised.
example_sentence: I thought the shop was open on Sundays, but it was closed, Well, live and learn. He trusted the wrong person and lost money, but he said, “You live and learn”. I never knew mango skin is edible; live and learn!. We made a few mistakes in the project, but that’s how we live and learn.

english_meaning: To follow or be guided by certain principles, rules, or values. To act according to certain beliefs, morals, or rules in daily life. It can also mean to survive or earn a living through a particular method or activity.
example_sentence: He lives by honesty. We live by our traditions. She lives by her faith. They live by hard work.

english_meaning: To overcome shame, embarrassment, or a bad reputation caused by a past mistake.
example_sentence: He’ll never live down that embarrassing moment. She lived down her past mistakes. It took years to live down the scandal. He couldn’t live down the failure.

english_meaning: Living longer than expected or continuing in a situation that should have ended already; surviving, functioning or lasting even though the end could come at any moment
example_sentence: After the crash, he’s living on borrowed time. The patient is living on borrowed time. Some say the company is living on borrowed time. We are all living on borrowed time.

english_meaning: To experience a difficult event and survive it. To endure or come through a hardship or dangerous period. To remain alive despite serious trouble. To pass through a memorable or historic time. To witness and get past a significant experience.
example_sentence: My grandfather lived through two world wars. She lived through a very painful divorce. Few people lived through the great famine. He lived through years of hardship before finding success.

english_meaning: To retreat or avoid loss today in order to try again later. To survive or withdraw from a difficult situation so that you can try again later. (It is wise to accept temporary defeat or step back instead of risking everything, so that you can make another attempt in the future.)
synonyms: ["Withdraw wisely","Accept defeat temporarily","Retreat for now","Wait for another chance","Survive for future success"]
antonyms: ["Right recklessly","Refuse to give up","Face defeat blindly","Continue despite danger"]
example_sentence: He decided to quit the argument and live to fight another day. Sometimes it is better to walk away and live to fight another day. After losing the match, the team promised to live to fight another day. She accepted her failure calmly, hoping to live to fight another day.

english_meaning: To accept or tolerate a difficult situation. Also means to share a home with someone.
example_sentence: You have to live with the consequences. I can’t live with this noise. She lives with her parents. They learned to live with their loss.

english_meaning: A large reddish-brown organ in the upper right part of the abdomen. The body's largest internal organ, which produces bile and helps digest fats. An organ that filters the blood and removes toxins, drugs, and waste products. An organ that stores glycogen, vitamins, and minerals and regulates blood sugar. The liver of an animal used as food.
example_sentence: The liver filters harmful substances out of the blood. Drinking too much alcohol can seriously damage the liver. The doctor ordered a scan to check the size of his liver. She cooked chicken liver with onions for dinner.

english_meaning: Very angry or extremely furious. Also used for a bluish or pale color caused by bruising or lack of oxygen.
example_sentence: She was livid when she found out that her project was deleted. He became livid after hearing the false accusation. The coach was livid at the team’s careless mistakes. His arm turned livid after he bumped into the door.

english_meaning: A heavy object or quantity that is being carried. The amount of work or responsibility placed on someone. To put things into a vehicle, container, or machine. To insert bullets into a gun or film into a camera. A burden either physical or mental.
example_sentence: The truck carried a heavy load of bricks. The workers loaded the boxes into the van. He carries a huge workload every day. Please load the washing machine before leaving.

english_meaning: In baseball, to put a runner on first, second, and third base at the same time. To create a situation in which all three bases are occupied. Informally, to arrange several favorable conditions or resources before taking action.
synonyms: ["Fill the bases","Put runners on every base","Set the stage","Prepare the ground"]
antonyms: ["Clear the bases","Empty the bases","Leave the bases unoccupied"]
example_sentence: A walk in the eighth inning loaded the bases. The team managed to load the bases with only one out. The pitcher remained calm after the opponents loaded the bases. The campaign loaded the bases by securing money, volunteers, and endorsements.

english_meaning: A person who is habitually lazy and avoids work. A comfortable shoe that is slip-on and has no laces. A person who idles away their time without purpose or productivity.
example_sentence: He was considered a loafer by his family, who could not understand his reluctance to find steady work. She kicked off her loafers and settled comfortably into the armchair with a book. The loafer spent his afternoons sitting in the park doing absolutely nothing. A good pair of leather loafers is a versatile addition to any wardrobe. He was no loafer at heart — he had simply not yet found the work that truly motivated him.

english_meaning: A sum of money lent to someone that must be repaid, usually with interest. Something given for temporary use. The act of lending. Formal permission to use another’s property. To give something to another person for a period of time.
example_sentence: He took a loan from the bank to buy a car. She kindly gave me a loan of her laptop. The government offers loans to small farmers. I need a short-term loan to pay for tuition.

english_meaning: Unwilling or reluctant; strongly opposed to doing something. Feeling disgust or aversion toward something. Feeling strong hesitation or resistance. Slow or cautious in agreeing or doing.
example_sentence: She was loath to admit her mistake. She was loath to leave her hometown after graduation. He seemed loath to admit his mistake. They were loath to cancel the event despite the rain. I am loath to spend money on things I do not need.

english_meaning: To hate something very much. To feel intense dislike or disgust for someone or something. It is stronger than simply disliking.
example_sentence: I loathe waking up early on weekends. She loathes dishonesty in any form. They loathe crowded places. He loathes doing unnecessary paperwork.

english_meaning: Extremely unpleasant or disgusting. Causing intense dislike or disgust; something morally or physically repulsive; arousing strong feelings of aversion
example_sentence: The loathsome smell from the garbage made everyone leave the room. He was punished for his loathsome behavior towards the children. The villain in the movie had a loathsome personality. Corruption in the system is a loathsome issue that must be addressed.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove a lobe of an organ such as the lung, liver, thyroid, or brain. A procedure commonly performed to treat lung cancer by removing one lobe. The excision of a defined lobe while preserving the rest of the organ. A brain operation carried out in some cases of severe epilepsy or tumour.
example_sentence: The surgeon removed the affected lobe in a lobectomy. A lobectomy is often preferred over removing the whole lung. She returned to work six weeks after her lobectomy. A temporal lobectomy helped control his severe seizures.

english_meaning: To argue or fight; to strongly disagree and enter into conflict. Used when two people or groups confront each other head-on over an issue.
example_sentence: The two politicians locked horns during the debate. They often lock horns over financial decisions. The managers locked horns about the new policy. The teams locked horns in a heated match.

english_meaning: An emergency protocol that prevents people from leaving or entering a building or area due to a threat. A state of isolation or restricted access instituted as a security measure. A situation where people are required to stay in their homes to prevent the spread of a contagious disease. The confining of prisoners to their cells, typically after a riot or for security reasons. A complete halt or freezing of a process, system, or activity.
example_sentence: The government announced a nationwide lockdown to curb the rising cases of the virus. The school went into an immediate lockdown after a suspicious person was spotted on the playground. Following the prison riot, the facility remained in a total lockdown for forty-eight hours. During the final stage of the project, the software undergoes a feature lockdown to ensure stability.

english_meaning: A classical or authoritative passage often quoted as the best example on a subject. A standard reference or original text on a particular topic. A well-known passage considered the finest illustration of an idea. A definitive source used to explain or support a concept. The most cited or respected example in literature or study.
example_sentence: This paragraph is the locus classicus for the theory of justice. The book is considered a locus classicus in modern philosophy. Scholars often refer to this line as the locus classicus of the debate. The Quranic verse serves as a locus classicus in Islamic teachings.

english_meaning: A large grasshopper that migrates in huge swarms and destroys crops. An insect known for causing severe agricultural damage during outbreaks. A member of the grasshopper family that changes behaviour and forms dense swarms. Figuratively, a person or group that consumes or ruins things greedily. Also the name of certain trees, such as the black locust.
example_sentence: A swarm of locusts destroyed the wheat crop within hours. Farmers spent the night trying to drive the locusts away. The government sprayed the fields to stop the locust attack. Locusts can travel hundreds of kilometres in a single day.

english_meaning: A star that leads or guides, especially the Pole Star used by navigators. A person or thing that serves as an inspiration or guide. Something that acts as a directing principle or guiding light.
example_sentence: The Pole Star has served as a lodestar for sailors navigating the open seas for centuries. Her mentor became the lodestar of her career, guiding every major decision she made. Justice remained the lodestar of his long and distinguished legal career. The ancient text served as a lodestar for the community's spiritual and ethical values. In the absence of a clear lodestar, the organisation struggled to maintain a consistent direction.

english_meaning: A piece of magnetite or other naturally magnetised mineral that can attract iron. Something that strongly attracts attention or interest. A magnet or object with powerful magnetic properties.
example_sentence: The ancient sailors used a lodestone to create a primitive compass for navigation at sea. The city became a lodestone for artists and intellectuals from across the world. His charisma made him a lodestone that drew people naturally toward him in every situation. The magnetite lodestone was one of the first materials discovered to have magnetic properties. The historic market became a lodestone for tourists seeking authentic local crafts and produce.

english_meaning: To provide someone with a place to stay temporarily, especially in rented accommodation. To become firmly fixed or stuck in a particular position. To formally submit a complaint, appeal, or official document to an authority. A small house or cabin, especially one used by hunters, travelers, or as a temporary residence.
example_sentence: They decided to lodge at a small inn near the mountains.  A piece of food had lodged in his throat, causing him to cough violently.  She lodged a formal complaint with the human resources department.  The hunting lodge was surrounded by dense forest.  The bullet lodged in the wooden frame of the door.

english_meaning: Of imposing height; very tall or elevated. Grand or noble in character, spirit, or ambition. Arrogant or haughtily superior in manner. Morally elevated or inspiring.
example_sentence: The lofty towers of the ancient cathedral dominated the skyline of the medieval city. She set herself lofty goals and worked tirelessly to achieve every one of them. His lofty manner of speaking made him seem dismissive of those who disagreed with him. The speech was full of lofty ideals but offered little in the way of practical solutions. The eagle soared above the lofty mountain peaks without any apparent effort.

english_meaning: To enter a computer system, website, or application by providing a username and password. To access a digital system by entering identification details. To record the time of arrival or work hours in an official system.
example_sentence: Please log in to your account before making any changes. Employees must log in by 9 AM every day. I forgot my password and could not log in. Make sure you log in using the official website.

english_meaning: To enter a computer system, website, or account by providing a username and password.
example_sentence: Log into your Gmail account. He logged into the portal. She couldn’t log into the app. I just logged into the website.

english_meaning: To sign out or disconnect from a computer system, website, or online account. To officially end your session on a computer, website, application, or network.
example_sentence: Don’t forget to log off when done. He logged off after work. Please log off the shared computer. I’ll log off now.

english_meaning: To access a computer system, website, application, or network by entering required credentials such as a username and password. It can also mean to start using a digital device or online service.
example_sentence: She logged on to check her mail. You must log on before accessing files. He logged on to the system. I log on every morning.

english_meaning: To exit or sign off from a computer system, website, or application.
example_sentence: Always log out before leaving. He logged out and shut down the computer. I forgot to log out of my account. Please log out when finished.

english_meaning: A mathematical quantity that shows the power to which a fixed number, called the base, must be raised to produce a given number. The exponent indicating how many times a base must be multiplied by itself to reach a certain value. A function used in mathematics and science to simplify calculations involving very large or very small numbers. The inverse operation of exponentiation.
example_sentence: The logarithm of one hundred to base ten is exactly two. Students learn how to use a logarithm to simplify long multiplication. Engineers often apply a logarithm when working with sound intensity. The calculator can compute the logarithm of any positive number instantly.

english_meaning: Relating to or expressed in terms of logarithms. Describing a scale in which each unit represents a fixed multiple rather than a fixed amount. Growing or decreasing at a rate that slows down or speeds up according to a logarithm. Involving the mathematical use of logarithms in calculation or measurement.
example_sentence: The data was plotted on a logarithmic scale for better clarity. Sound levels are measured using a logarithmic unit called the decibel. The population showed logarithmic growth in the early years. A logarithmic curve flattens out as the values increase.

english_meaning: A book in which regular records of events, journeys, or performance are kept. An official record of a ship's or aircraft's voyage. A document recording the details and history of a vehicle. A notebook used to log activities, hours, or observations systematically.
example_sentence: The captain recorded the storm in the ship's logbook. Drivers must update the logbook after every long journey. She keeps a logbook of all her laboratory experiments. The vehicle was sold along with its original logbook.

english_meaning: A very stubborn or foolish person who refuses to change their opinion. A large sea turtle known as the loggerhead turtle. Often used in daily English to describe arguments or conflicts between people who refuse to agree. In nature, it refers to a specific large turtle species found in oceans worldwide.
example_sentence: He is such a loggerhead that he never listens to anyone’s advice. The two politicians acted like loggerheads during the debate. A loggerhead turtle was found near the shore yesterday. Don’t be a loggerhead, try to understand other people’s opinions.

english_meaning: A covered corridor or gallery with one or more open sides, supported by columns. An open-sided extension of a building, often found in Italian architecture. A roofed arcade or porch attached to a house.
example_sentence: They had breakfast on the shaded loggia overlooking the garden. The palace featured a beautiful marble loggia. Guests gathered in the loggia to escape the afternoon sun. The artist painted the arches of the old loggia.

english_meaning: The study of correct reasoning. A system of principles used to judge whether arguments are valid. Sound reasoning or good sense. The reason or pattern behind an action, idea, or system. A particular method of thinking.
example_sentence: The professor taught a course in logic. I do not understand the logic behind that decision. Good logic helps students write stronger arguments. The software follows a simple logic when sorting names.

english_meaning: A fundamental building block of digital systems that performs a specific logical operation based on one or more binary inputs. An electronic pathway composed of interconnected components that processes signals according to Boolean algebra. A configuration of gates such as AND, OR, and NOT designed to control the flow of data in a computer processor. The physical implementation of a mathematical logic function within an integrated circuit or hardware device. A conceptual diagram representing how discrete signals are manipulated to produce a determined output within a larger machine.
synonyms: ["Digital Circuit","Gate Array","Logical Gate","Boolean Circuit","Integrated Circuit","Switching Circuit","Processor Component","Binary Network","Control Circuit","Computing Element","Hardware Logic","Electronic Module"]
antonyms: ["Analog Circuit","Linear Circuit","Random Noise","Chaos","Physical Matter","Manual Control","Continuous Signal","Unstructured Data"]
example_sentence: Engineers are designing a new logic circuit to speed up data processing. Each logic circuit in the CPU responds to binary instructions. The simplest logic circuit is a single inverter gate. Troubleshooting a faulty logic circuit requires a detailed schematic and an oscilloscope.

english_meaning: Based on clear reasoning. Sensible and reasonable. Following the rules of logic. Expected or natural as a result of the facts. Arranged in a coherent order.
example_sentence: Her explanation was simple and logical. It is logical to save money before making a large purchase. The chapters follow a logical order. His conclusion was logical, even if people disliked it.

english_meaning: In a way that follows reason or logic. Sensibly and coherently. As a natural result of facts or evidence. In an ordered and consistent manner.
example_sentence: If we think logically, the answer becomes clear. The report is logically organized into three sections. Logically, the team with more evidence should win the argument. She explained each step logically and calmly.

english_meaning: The detailed organisation and coordination of a complex operation or activity. The commercial activity of transporting goods to customers. The planning and management of the flow of resources, information, and services. The practical arrangements that make a process work smoothly.
example_sentence: The logistics of organising an event for ten thousand people required months of careful planning. The company specialises in the logistics of moving large quantities of goods across international borders. She was responsible for managing the logistics of the entire relief operation after the earthquake. Getting all the equipment to the remote location was a major logistics challenge for the team. Advances in technology have transformed the logistics industry over the past two decades.

english_meaning: An abnormal and excessive talkativeness. An obsessive fascination with words and their use. A condition in which a person talks endlessly and cannot stop. Extreme enthusiasm for collecting or studying words. Uncontrollable and rapid flow of speech.
example_sentence: His logomania kept the whole room from speaking. The old scholar's logomania filled his notebooks with rare words. Logomania can be a symptom of certain mental disorders. She admits to a mild logomania whenever she finds a new dictionary.

english_meaning: A person who loves words, enjoys learning new words, and is passionate about language. Someone fascinated by the structure, meanings, and use of words.
example_sentence: The logophile spent hours reading dictionaries just for fun. As a true logophile, she enjoyed collecting rare words from old books. The teacher encouraged her logophile students to write creative stories. He was a logophile who could recall the meaning of almost every word he encountered.

english_meaning: A strong love or fascination with words and language. An intense attraction toward words, vocabulary, and language in general. A person with logophilia enjoys learning new words, exploring their meanings, origins, and usage, and often finds pleasure in reading, writing, or studying languages.
synonyms: ["Word love","Lexical passion","Love of language","Verbal appreciation","Linguistic interest"]
antonyms: ["Logophobia","Fear or dislike of words","Indifference to language","Language apathy","Disinterest in vocabulary"]
example_sentence: Her logophilia made her spend hours reading dictionaries for fun. His logophilia is clear from the way he collects rare words. Logophilia often drives writers to explore language deeply. A teacher with logophilia can inspire students to love words.

english_meaning: Fear or dislike of words. A person who has a strong dislike or fear of words, speaking, or verbal communication. Often avoids reading or writing due to discomfort with language. Reluctance to engage with literature or written materials. Social anxiety related to verbal communication. Extreme discomfort with new or complex words.
example_sentence: The logophobe avoided writing emails and preferred communicating through gestures. Despite being intelligent, he was a logophobe and rarely spoke in meetings. Schools often encourage children to overcome being logophobes for better learning. Her logophobia made reading novels a stressful experience.

english_meaning: An intense fear of words, particularly certain words, or a fear of speaking or expressing oneself verbally. It can also refer to a fear of the power or consequences of words.
example_sentence: His logophobia made public speaking nearly impossible. She developed logophobia after being mocked for her vocabulary. Logophobia can interfere with daily communication significantly. The therapist worked with him to overcome his logophobia.

english_meaning: To stand or wait around without purpose. To linger in a place without any clear reason, often wasting time or moving slowly. It can also mean hanging around somewhere in a way that looks suspicious or unnecessary. To move slowly without direction. To stay somewhere longer than needed. To delay in finishing something. To hover or wait without a clear purpose.
example_sentence: Teenagers were loitering near the store. Don’t loiter in front of the building. The guard told them not to loiter here. He loitered in the park all afternoon. She loitered in the hallway waiting for her friend. A few people were loitering near the bus stop late at night. He spent the afternoon loitering around the market with nothing to do.

english_meaning: To sit, lie, or stand in a lazy or relaxed manner. To hang loosely or droop. To rest or recline in a comfortable or idle way. To let the tongue hang out loosely.
example_sentence: He spent most of the afternoon lolling on the sofa watching films without any sense of purpose. The dog sat by the gate with its tongue lolling in the afternoon heat. She lolled back in the garden chair and enjoyed the last warmth of the summer sun. The children were lolling about on the grass after finishing their picnic. His head lolled to one side as he drifted off to sleep during the long meeting.

english_meaning: An outstanding or remarkable person, thing, or event. Something extraordinary that impresses people greatly. An unusually large, exciting, or excellent example of its kind.
example_sentence: The final match was a real lollapalooza. She wore a lollapalooza of a dress to the party. That storm was a lollapalooza by any standard. His speech turned out to be a lollapalooza.

english_meaning: To spend time aimlessly or to dawdle. To move slowly or waste time doing nothing in particular. To engage in idle or frivolous activity when one should be doing something productive.
example_sentence: Stop lollygagging and get your work done before the deadline tomorrow morning. He had been lollygagging all day and had not made any progress on the assignment. She tends to lollygag on Saturday mornings rather than getting up and doing anything useful. The supervisor warned the workers to stop lollygagging and get back to their stations. They lollygagged through the market without buying anything or even knowing what they wanted.

english_meaning: Being by oneself with no one else present. Single or solitary in number. Standing apart from others in an isolated position. Feeling or appearing alone and without company.
example_sentence: A lone traveller walked along the empty road. Only a lone tree stood in the middle of the field. She was the lone survivor of the accident. A lone light burned in the upstairs window.

english_meaning: A person who prefers to act, live, or work alone rather than with others. Someone who avoids group membership and keeps to themselves. An individual who carries out an action independently, without support from any organisation.
example_sentence: He has always been a lone wolf who avoids office gatherings. As a lone wolf, she prefers projects she can finish by herself. The investigators believe the attacker was a lone wolf. Being a lone wolf made him effective but hard to manage.

english_meaning: A sad feeling caused by having no friends or company. The unhappy state of being isolated from other people. The quality of a place that is deserted and far from others.
example_sentence: Loneliness is a growing problem among the elderly. She felt a deep loneliness after moving to the new city. The loneliness of the long winter nights was hard to bear. He filled his loneliness with books and music.

english_meaning: Feeling sad because one has no friends or company. Without companions and therefore unhappy. Describing a place that is remote, empty, and rarely visited. Spent or passed alone.
example_sentence: He felt lonely during his first week at the new school. They live in a lonely cottage on the moor. She spent a lonely evening waiting for the phone to ring. Many lonely people find comfort in community groups.

english_meaning: A long, narrow piece of leather, cloth, plastic, or other flexible material used for fastening, carrying, hanging, or holding something. Often attached to bags, watches, cameras, or belts to allow them to be worn on the shoulder, around the body, or hung from an object.
example_sentence: The bag had a long strap that could be worn across the shoulder. She adjusted the long strap of her camera before the trip. The traveler tightened the long strap of his backpack. A long strap is more comfortable for carrying heavy items. The watch came with a long strap suitable for larger wrists.

english_meaning: The quality of bearing suffering or hardship with patience and calmness. Patience in the face of provocation or misfortune. A disposition to endure difficulties without complaint.
example_sentence: She endured the long illness with remarkable longanimity and never lost her spirit or sense of humour. His longanimity in the face of persistent criticism earned him the deep respect of his colleagues. The peace negotiator was praised for his longanimity during months of difficult and frustrating talks. Longanimity is considered a virtue in many religious and philosophical traditions around the world. The community displayed extraordinary longanimity as they rebuilt their lives after the devastating flood.

english_meaning: Long life or the great duration of a life. The long duration of existence of an organism, institution, or thing. A tendency to live longer than average.
example_sentence: Regular exercise and a balanced diet are widely associated with greater longevity. The longevity of the company can be attributed to its ability to adapt to changing market conditions. Scientists are studying the genetics of populations known for their exceptional longevity. Her grandmother's longevity was the subject of great admiration within the family. The longevity of the ancient bridge is a testament to the quality of the craftsmanship that went into its construction.

english_meaning: In a way that expresses a strong desire or yearning for something or someone. With a feeling of wistful longing or deep wish. Looking or thinking about something with an aching sense of desire.
example_sentence: She looked longingly at the photographs from her childhood summer holidays by the sea. He gazed longingly at the shop window display, knowing he could not afford what was inside. The dog sat longingly by the door, waiting for its owner to return from work. She spoke longingly of the years she had spent living in that small quiet village. He stared longingly at the open fields, wishing he could leave the city behind and start again.

english_meaning: The distance of a place east or west of the Greenwich meridian, measured in degrees. An imaginary line running from the North Pole to the South Pole on a map or globe. One of the two main coordinates used to locate a point on the earth. A measure used in navigation and mapping.
example_sentence: The city lies at a longitude of seventy degrees east. Sailors used the stars to calculate longitude. Lines of longitude meet at the poles. Give me the latitude and longitude of the location.

english_meaning: British informal term for a toilet or bathroom. A lavatory or place for urination and defecation. A room or facility equipped with a toilet.
example_sentence: She excused herself from the dinner table to nip to the loo before the main course arrived. He asked the waiter where the loo was as soon as they were seated in the restaurant. The old country house had only one loo for all the guests staying on the upper floor. Could you show me where the loo is, please, before we start the meeting? The loo at the service station was out of order and they had to wait until the next stop.

english_meaning: To look around. To turn your eyes around, to observe the surroundings, or to search around in different directions.
example_sentence:
She paused in the garden to look about, enjoying the beauty of the flowers. When he entered the old house, he looked about to see if anyone was inside.
The child looked about in the park, trying to find his lost ball. At the station, travelers looked about in confusion, searching for the right platform.

english_meaning: To think about and plan for the future. Refers to anticipating future events, opportunities, or challenges, and preparing for them mentally, emotionally, or practically. It implies foresight, planning, and proactive thinking rather than reacting only when events occur.
example_sentence: We must look ahead to future challenges. She’s always looking ahead in her career. It’s time to look ahead rather than dwell on the past. Investors look ahead before making decisions.

english_meaning: To explore a new place. To search casually. To observe surroundings. To turn your head or eyes in different directions to see what is nearby.
example_sentence: We looked around the old city during our trip. I looked around the room but couldn’t find my phone. It’s good to look around before making a big decision. We looked around the city before deciding where to eat.
