english_meaning: To direct your eyes towards someone or something. To consider, think about, or examine carefully. To regard someone/something in a particular way. To read, check, or review something.
example_sentence: Look at that beautiful painting. The doctor will look at your injury. We need to look at the problem from another angle. Please look at my essay and give feedback.

english_meaning: To turn your eyes aside or ignore. To turn your eyes in another direction or to avoid seeing or noticing something. It can also mean to ignore something unpleasant or embarrassing.
example_sentence: She looked away when the injured animal appeared on the screen. He looked away to hide his tears. You cannot look away from the truth forever. The child looked away shyly when the teacher smiled at him.

english_meaning: Think carefully about the possible results before taking any action. A person should think carefully, examine the situation, and understand the risks before making a decision or taking action. It advises people not to act in haste or excitement because careless decisions may lead to trouble, loss, or regret.
synonyms: ["Think before acting","Be cautious","Act wisely","Use caution","Consider carefully","Be careful","Use good judgment"]
antonyms: ["Act rashly","Jump to conclusions","Be reckless","Act without thinking","Rush blindly"]
example_sentence: Before investing all his savings in a new business, Ali remembered to look before he leaped. She accepted the job offer without checking the company properly, and later realized she should have looked before she leaped. Buying a house is a major decision, so it is wise to look before you leap. Students should look before they leap when choosing a career path.

english_meaning: To try to find someone or something. To search, seek, or expect.
example_sentence: I am looking for my keys; I think I lost them in the car. She is looking for a new job in Karachi. They are looking for a solution to the problem. We are looking for someone who can speak English, Sindhi, and Urdu.

english_meaning: To feel excited or pleased about something that is going to happen in the future. Anticipate with pleasure.
example_sentence: I look forward to meeting you. She looks forward to her holidays. We’re looking forward to your visit. They look forward to good news.

english_meaning: To make a short visit to someone, usually informally. To inspect or check on a person, place, or situation. To appear in a place, often unexpectedly.
example_sentence: I’ll look in on my parents this evening. Can you look in on the baby while I cook? She looked in at the shop while passing by. The manager looked in to see if everything was okay

english_meaning: To search for something where it is not actually present or cannot be found. To waste time or effort searching for something in an unsuitable or incorrect location or situation. It is often used when someone is not able to find a solution or answer because they are focusing on the wrong source or direction.
synonyms: ["Misguided search","Wrong approach","Searching in vain","Misplaced effort","Off track"]
antonyms: ["Looking in the right place","Correct approach","Accurate search","Proper direction","Right focus"]
example_sentence: He has been looking for his keys in the kitchen, but he is looking in the wrong place. If you are blaming your teammates, you are looking in the wrong place. She was looking for happiness in money, but she was looking in the wrong place. You are looking in the wrong place if you think success comes without effort.

english_meaning: To examine, investigate, or study something carefully in order to understand it or find out the truth.
example_sentence: The police will look into the matter. The committee will look into the causes of the recent flood to prevent it in the future. She promised to look into the matter and get back with a solution. The teacher decided to look into why so many students failed the test.

english_meaning: To appear suitable for a role or situation. To have the right appearance, clothing, behavior, or style that matches a particular job, role, or expectation, even if the actual ability is not yet proven
example_sentence: He really looks the part of a CEO. You need to look the part for the audition. She looked the part of a princess at the ball. He doesn’t look the part of a teacher.

english_meaning: To search for information in a reference source such as a dictionary, database, or online. To improve in condition or become more positive. To raise your eyes and look towards someone or something.
example_sentence: Look up the word in the dictionary. Things are looking up now. She looked up his address. Business is looking up this year.

word: Look what the cat dragged in
english_meaning: A playful or sarcastic way of saying that someone has arrived, especially when they are unexpected, late, or not welcome. An informal and humorous expression used when someone shows up in a place after being absent or late. It often carries a teasing tone, sometimes friendly, sometimes slightly rude depending on context. It suggests surprise at the person’s arrival, as if they were “brought in” unexpectedly.
synonyms: ["Long time no see","Well","Look who’s here","Who do we have here","Guess who showed up"]
antonyms: ["Glad to see you","Welcome","Nice to meet you","Happy you arrived"]
example_sentence: Look what the cat dragged in! We thought you forgot about us. Well, look what the cat dragged in, the late guest has finally arrived. Look what the cat dragged in, haven’t seen you in months!. Oh, look what the cat dragged in, Mr always-late is here again.

english_meaning: The action of searching for information in a book or database. A feature in a program that retrieves data from a table.
example_sentence: I performed a quick lookup in the dictionary for the word. The software includes a lookup function to find customer names. A simple table lookup can provide you with the correct tax rate. The database lookup was slow because of the high server traffic.

english_meaning: To take care of someone or something.
example_sentence: She looks after her younger brother. Please look after the house. He looked after the old man. Nurses look after patients.

english_meaning: To think about or remember the past, To turn one’s eyes backward.
example_sentence: Don’t look back, move on. She looked back fondly on her childhood. He never looked back after success. Looking back, I realize my mistakes.

english_meaning: To respect or admire someone.
example_sentence: I look up to my parents. She’s someone we all look up to. Children look up to their teachers. He looks up to his older brother.

english_meaning: To appear as a shadowy form, especially one that is large or threatening. To come into view indistinctly and often in enlarged form. It also refers to an event regarded as ominous or extremely likely to happen in the near future.
example_sentence: A dark shape began to loom through the heavy morning fog. The deadline for the project started to loom over the exhausted team. Storm clouds loom on the horizon, threatening to ruin our outdoor plans. The specter of a global recession continues to loom in the minds of economists.

english_meaning: To appear important, threatening, or hard to ignore. To seem very significant in someone's thoughts or plans. To be close at hand in a worrying way. To dominate a situation or discussion.
example_sentence: The final exams loom large in every student's mind. Economic uncertainty looms large over the industry. The deadline loomed large as the week ended. His reputation loomed large in the negotiations.

english_meaning: To form a circle or repeat. To bend or twist something into a circular shape, or to cause an action, sound, or process to repeat continuously. A circular or curved shape. Something shaped like a circle, ring, or bend. It also means a route, system, or process that returns to its starting point or repeats continuously.
example_sentence: She looped the ribbon around the box. The path loops through the forest. The video was looped for display. Make a loop with the string. The road forms a loop near the park. He put the key on a metal loop.

english_meaning: To return to an earlier point or topic. To go back physically to a previous place, or to return in conversation, thinking, planning, or communication to something discussed or done before.
example_sentence: We need to loop back to the main issue before making a decision. The road loops back to the village after the bridge. Let me loop back to you once I confirm the details. The discussion looped back to budget concerns again.

english_meaning: To include someone in information or a process. To intentionally involve someone by sharing information, keeping them informed, or making them part of a discussion, decision, or activity, especially in work or planning contexts
example_sentence: Please loop me in on any updates about the project. She looped the finance team in before finalizing the budget. Make sure to loop the manager in if the plan changes. He was looped in late, so he missed the earlier discussion.

english_meaning: To come out of a loop, cycle, or repeated pattern. To exit or break free from a repeated cycle, process, or circular movement. It can be used literally, such as pulling something out of a loop, or figuratively, such as stopping a repetitive action or ending a cycle in thinking, programming, or routine.
example_sentence: The program will loop out once the condition is met. She felt relieved when she finally looped out of the same daily routine. Pull the wire gently so it can loop out without breaking. The system failed to loop out and kept repeating the same command.

english_meaning: To repeat a process or go through a sequence of items one by one. To perform an action repeatedly for each element in a set or sequence, usually in programming or systematic tasks. It implies iterating through items, often until a condition is met.
example_sentence: We need to loop over all the files to check for errors. The program will loop over each item in the list until it finds a match. She likes to loop over her notes before exams. The robot will loop over its instructions until the task is complete.

english_meaning: Slightly crazy, silly, or eccentric in a harmless way. Feeling dizzy, confused, or lightheaded. Behaving in a strange or foolish manner. Full of loops or curves in shape. Informally used to describe odd or amusing behavior.
example_sentence: The medicine made her feel a bit loopy. He tells such loopy stories that everyone laughs. She gave me a loopy smile after waking up. Don't listen to him; he's being loopy today.

english_meaning: An unpredictable person who can cause damage if not controlled. Someone whose reckless behavior endangers their own team or group. A person who lacks self-restraint and acts impulsively. An uncontrollable individual likely to create a public relations disaster.
antonyms: ["Reliable Person","Steady Hand","Predictable Individual","Safe Bet","Team Player","Dependable Worker","Cautious Person","Stable Character","Controlled Individual","Rock"]
example_sentence: The company fired the executive because he had become a loose cannon during press conferences. You never know what that loose cannon will say next to ruin the event. He is a brilliant strategist but a bit of a loose cannon when he is angry. The coach decided to bench the player who acted like a loose cannon on the field.

english_meaning: To make something less tight, firm, or compact. To relax or release something that was previously tightly held or secured. To become less strict, tense, or controlled.
example_sentence: He had to loosen the bolt with a wrench before he could remove it completely. She loosened her grip on the rope as the tension in the situation began to ease. The coach encouraged the players to loosen up before the match began. The government decided to loosen the restrictions on public gatherings. He loosened his tie and took a long breath after the stressful meeting ended.

english_meaning: To give someone more freedom or flexibility. To relax control over a person or situation. To reduce strict supervision. To allow more independence. To ease restrictions previously imposed.
example_sentence: Parents should loosen the reins as their children grow up. The manager loosened the reins to boost creativity. The government loosened the reins on trade regulations. She decided to loosen the reins on her team’s work hours.

english_meaning: Goods that have been stolen or taken by force, especially during a war or disaster. To steal goods from a place, especially during a war, riot, or natural disaster. Informal term for money or valuable items. To plunder or pillage.
example_sentence: Soldiers were accused of taking loot from homes as they advanced through the captured town. Rioters began to loot shops in the city centre after the protest turned violent. The museum held artefacts that critics argued were loot taken during the colonial era. Police were deployed to prevent people from attempting to loot the abandoned properties. The pirates divided their loot equally among the crew after a successful raid on the merchant ship.

english_meaning: Uneven or not balanced on one side. Tilted, heavier, or larger on one side than the other. It can refer to physical objects, situations, or comparisons that are unfair or unequal.
example_sentence: The painting looked lopsided because it was hung too high on one side. The election results were lopsided, favoring one party heavily. His smile was slightly lopsided, giving him a quirky look. The table is lopsided because one leg is shorter than the others.

english_meaning: In a manner that is uneven or leaning to one side. Not balanced or symmetrical. Tilted or crooked in appearance. In an unequal or unfair way. Done or arranged with one side heavier or lower than the other.
example_sentence: The picture was hanging lopsidedly on the wall. He smiled lopsidedly at her joke. The cake had risen lopsidedly in the oven. The building leaned lopsidedly after the earthquake.

english_meaning: Very talkative or fond of speaking. Tending to talk a great deal, especially about unimportant matters. Given to constant conversation. Chatty or extremely communicative. Expressive and eager to share thoughts through speech.
example_sentence: She is a loquacious speaker who never runs out of words. The loquacious host kept the guests entertained. His loquacious nature made him popular in the group. The teacher's loquacious style made lessons interesting.

english_meaning: Talkativeness, the habit of speaking a lot. A tendency to talk continuously or excessively. It often describes someone who enjoys speaking at length, sometimes more than necessary or expected.
example_sentence: His loquacity made the meeting much longer than expected. She was known for her loquacity and could talk for hours. The teacher gently controlled his loquacity in class. Due to his loquacity, he often shared more information than needed.

english_meaning: A small yellow-orange fruit similar to a plum, native to China. The evergreen tree that bears this fruit. A fruit with sweet, tangy flesh and large seeds. A tropical fruit used in jams and desserts. A member of the rose family known for its fragrant flowers and edible fruit.
example_sentence: The loquat tree in the garden bears fruit every spring. She made delicious jam from fresh loquats. Loquats are known for their sweet and tangy flavor. My grandfather planted a loquat tree many years ago.

english_meaning: To feel embarrassed or humiliated, especially in front of others. To suffer a loss of respect, honor, or reputation due to a mistake, failure, or public embarrassment. It is commonly used in social, professional, or cultural situations where dignity and image matter.
example_sentence: He refused to apologize because he did not want to lose face in front of his team. The manager lost face after making a wrong decision publicly. She tried to hide her mistake to avoid losing face. If the plan fails, the company may lose face in the market.

english_meaning: To fall behind or become less successful. To lose a previous advantage, position, influence, support, or territory. To retreat physically. To decline in value or strength
example_sentence: The local currency lost ground against the dollar this week. Their party has lost ground in recent opinion polls. He lost ground to his rival after a poor performance. The company is losing ground to newer competitors.

english_meaning: To suddenly become angry or upset. To fail to control one’s anger.
example_sentence: He lost his temper during the debate. He lost his temper when the children broke the vase.

english_meaning: To lose control or ability to manage something. To fail to understand or hold on to an idea, situation, or opportunity. To no longer be in control of power, position, or reality.
example_sentence: The teacher felt he was losing his grasp of the noisy class. After the sudden crisis, the manager lost his grasp on the team’s direction. She studied hard, but she began to lose her grasp of advanced mathematics. The old king was slowly losing his grasp on power. He tried to remember the details, but he lost his grasp of the conversation.

english_meaning: To become mentally confused or behave strangely. To lose one's ability to think clearly. To act in a foolish or irrational way. To seem to be going crazy. To lose control of one's mind or senses.
synonyms: ["Go crazy","Lose sanity","Go mad","Lose it","Flip out","Become confused","Go nuts"]
antonyms: ["Stay calm","Be rational","Keep sane","Think clearly","Stay composed","Remain sensible"]
example_sentence: Have you lost your marbles? That plan will never work. Sometimes I feel like I'm losing my marbles from stress. He acts like he has lost his marbles today. She hasn't lost her marbles; she just needs rest.

english_meaning: A man who seduces women frequently. A man known for being a seducer or womanizer, often charming but unfaithful.
example_sentence: He behaved like a true Lothario at the party. The novel portrayed him as a charming Lothario. Women warned each other about the local Lothario. He gained a reputation as a Lothario in the city.

english_meaning: A large aquatic flower that grows in ponds and shallow waters. A symbol of purity, beauty, and spiritual awakening in many cultures. A plant whose flowers, seeds, and roots are widely used in cooking and medicine. A sacred flower in Hindu, Buddhist, and other Asian traditions. A plant known for rising clean and beautiful from muddy water.
example_sentence: The lotus is considered a sacred flower in many Eastern religions. A beautiful pink lotus was blooming in the middle of the pond. She got a lotus tattooed on her shoulder as a symbol of peace. Lotus flowers rise clean above the muddy water beneath them.

english_meaning: The long, tube-like root of the lotus plant that grows under water. A crunchy vegetable widely used in Asian cooking. A nutritious food that is often stir-fried, boiled, or added to soups. A root known for its unique pattern of holes when sliced. A traditional ingredient valued for both taste and health benefits.
example_sentence: Lotus root is often served in Chinese and Japanese dishes. She sliced the lotus root and fried it with soy sauce. Lotus root is rich in fiber and considered good for digestion. My grandmother makes a delicious curry with lotus root.

english_meaning: Producing a great deal of noise; strong in sound. Easily heard from a distance. Of colours or clothing, unpleasantly bright or showy. Of a person or behaviour, noisy and lacking restraint.
example_sentence: The music was too loud for the small room. She called his name in a loud voice. He was wearing a loud checked jacket. The children became loud as soon as the teacher left.

english_meaning: A small parasitic insect that lives on the hair or skin of humans or animals. A tiny wingless insect that lives on mammals or birds. It feeds on blood or skin and commonly infests hair, clothing, or feathers. It is often associated with poor hygiene but can spread through close contact. A contemptible or unpleasant person. Informal term for someone considered dirty. Used figuratively for annoyance or irritation
example_sentence: The child scratched his head because he had a louse. Farmers checked the animals for lice. He called the dishonest man a louse. The school nurse found a louse during inspection.

english_meaning: To spoil something by making mistakes or handling it badly. It is often used informally when someone messes up a task, plan, or situation due to carelessness, confusion, or poor judgment.
example_sentence: He loused up the presentation by forgetting the key points. Try not to louse up this opportunity, it may not come again. The technician loused up the repair and the machine stopped working. She was nervous and loused up her lines during the speech.

english_meaning: A rude and ill mannered person. A person who behaves in a rough, disrespectful, and uncivilized way. Such a person lacks social manners, shows little respect for others, and often acts offensively in public or private settings.
example_sentence: He behaved like a lout at the formal dinner. Only a lout would speak so rudely to elders. His loutish behavior embarrassed everyone in the room. The crowd was disturbed by a loud lout shouting insults.

english_meaning: Rude and badly behaved, especially in a loud or uncultured way. A person whose behavior is rough, disrespectful, and socially unacceptable. Such a person ignores manners, behaves loudly in public, and shows little respect for others.
example_sentence: His loutish behavior embarrassed everyone at the dinner table. The teacher warned him to stop his loutish jokes in class. Loutish conduct in public places is not tolerated. Despite his intelligence, his loutish manners hurt his reputation.

english_meaning: In a rude, rough, or ill mannered way. Behavior that is socially crude, disrespectful, or lacking manners. It refers to actions done in a careless, offensive, or uncivil way, often showing no concern for others.
example_sentence: He spoke loutishly to the waiter and embarrassed everyone at the table. The guest behaved loutishly at the formal dinner. Laughing loutishly in a serious meeting can damage your reputation. The crowd reacted loutishly instead of listening calmly.

english_meaning: A condition where blood pressure is lower than normal range. Hypotension that can cause dizziness, fainting, and fatigue. Blood pressure readings below the healthy threshold. A state where blood flow to organs may be insufficient.
example_sentence: Low blood pressure can cause fainting spells. She experiences dizziness due to low blood pressure. Dehydration can lead to low blood pressure. Some medications cause low blood pressure as a side effect.

english_meaning: The part of the body that includes the hip, thigh, leg, ankle, and foot. The area extending from the hip joint to the tips of the toes. An anatomical region that supports the body's weight and enables walking. The division of the body containing the bones of the leg and foot.
example_sentence: The lower limb region carries the entire weight of the body. She fractured a bone in her lower limb region. Strong muscles in the lower limb region improve balance. The doctor examined the swelling in his lower limb region.

english_meaning: Low in rank, status or importance. Humble and modest in nature or behaviour. Simple and unpretentious in position. Of humble origin or condition.
example_sentence: He began his career in a lowly position at the mill. The lowly clerk rose to become a manager. She spoke with a lowly and gentle manner. Even the lowliest worker deserves respect.

english_meaning: Faithful and devoted to a person, cause, or duty. Showing firm and constant support or allegiance. True and reliable in friendship or commitment. Remaining steadfast even in difficult times.
example_sentence: The dog remained loyal to its owner until the end. She is a loyal friend who never shares secrets. Loyal employees are the strength of any company. He stayed loyal to his principles throughout his career.

english_meaning: A strong feeling of support or allegiance to a person, group, or cause. Faithfulness and devotion over time. Consistent and reliable commitment despite difficulties.
example_sentence: She demonstrated unwavering loyalty to her employer even during the most difficult period. His loyalty to his friends was one of his most admired and respected qualities. The soldier's loyalty to his country was tested by years of gruelling service. Brand loyalty among customers is one of the most valuable assets any company can develop. The team's loyalty to their coach never wavered, even during the losing streak.

english_meaning: A small medicated tablet that is dissolved slowly in the mouth to soothe the throat. A rhombus or diamond-shaped figure in geometry. A diamond-shaped design used in heraldry, decoration, or window panes.
example_sentence: He sucked a throat lozenge during the meeting. The chemist sold me a box of honey lozenges. The window was made of small glass lozenges. Draw a lozenge and measure its diagonals.

english_meaning: An awkward stupid person. A large person who often breaks things or has accidents. An inexperienced sailor, a sailor on the first voyage.
example_sentence: The two lubbers who came to deliver my furniture. Although he's something of a lubber, everyone agrees that he has a kind heart.

english_meaning: A small unofficial payment made to quicken an official or routine service.
example_sentence: He made a lubrication payment to speed the process. The company refused to make a lubrication payment to get customs clearance faster. Lubrication payments are sometimes used in countries where bureaucracy causes delays. Paying lubrication money to speed up approval is against the organization’s policy. The official hinted that a small lubrication payment could help move the file quickly.

english_meaning: Expressed clearly and easy to understand. Showing the ability to think clearly, especially in the middle of confusion or illness. Bright, shining, or transparent. A lucid explanation, writing, or person is clear and free from confusion.
example_sentence: The professor gave a lucid explanation of the difficult theory. Despite his high fever, he had a few lucid moments in the afternoon. Her writing is lucid and a pleasure to read. The water in the lake was so lucid that we could see the bottom. He presented a lucid argument that convinced the entire committee.

english_meaning: Producing wealth. Producing a sizeable profit. Producing much money or making a large profit. Producing a lot of money(especially of a business, job, or activity).
example_sentence: Had the plan worked it would have proved highly lucrative. The merger proved to be very lucrative for both companies. The new manager's mission was to turn the failing store into a lucrative operation.

english_meaning: Money, especially when regarded as sordid or distasteful or gained in a dishonorable way. It is often used in the phrase 'filthy lucre' to describe ill-gotten wealth. The term implies a focus on profit at the expense of ethics or morality.
example_sentence: The corrupt official was driven only by the desire for filthy lucre. He cared more about personal lucre than the welfare of his community. Many high-stakes crimes are motivated purely by the pursuit of lucre. She refused to compromise her principles for the sake of mere lucre.

english_meaning: A person who dislikes or avoids modern technology. Someone who resists or opposes new technology, especially because they believe it may harm jobs, traditions, or society. The term comes from a group of 19th century English workers who destroyed machinery to protest industrial changes.
example_sentence: My grandfather is a Luddite and refuses to use a smartphone. Some people label him a Luddite because he avoids social media. She is not a Luddite, but she prefers writing letters instead of emails. The company was criticized for having a Luddite attitude toward innovation.

english_meaning: Something that is so foolish, unreasonable, or out of place as to be amusing or completely ridiculous. It describes actions, ideas, or situations that defy logic and provoke mocking laughter. It represents ultimate absurdity.
example_sentence: It was completely ludicrous to suggest that we could finish the project in one day. He looked absolutely ludicrous wearing that gigantic, brightly colored hat. The new company policy imposing a dress code for remote workers is ludicrous. They charged a ludicrous amount of money for a small cup of coffee. The explanation she provided for being late was frankly ludicrous.

english_meaning: A person who loves games, especially board games, card games, or video games. Someone who has a deep enthusiasm for playing games of all kinds.
example_sentence: As a ludophile, he owned over two hundred board games. The ludophile organised weekly game nights for friends. She was a true ludophile who never missed a gaming convention. His ludophile nature made him an expert at chess.

english_meaning: Suitcases, bags, and other containers used to carry personal belongings during travel. All the items and containers that a traveller takes with them on a journey. The bags and cases in which clothes and other possessions are packed for transport.
example_sentence: We checked our luggage at the airport before boarding the flight. She packed her luggage carefully for the week-long trip. The hotel porter helped carry the heavy luggage to the room. Please make sure your luggage is properly tagged with your name.

english_meaning: Very sad or mournful. A person, voice, expression, or situation that shows deep sadness, grief, or gloom, often in an exaggerated or noticeable way
example_sentence: He spoke in a lugubrious tone after hearing the bad news. The movie had a dark and lugubrious atmosphere. Her lugubrious expression showed how deeply she was hurt. The rainy weather added to his lugubrious mood.

english_meaning: A first name for boys. Luke is a male given name. One of the four Gospels in the New Testament, contains details of Jesus's birth and early life. Luke is the name of one of the twelve disciples of Jesus Christ. He is traditionally believed to be the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles in the Bible.
example_sentence: Luke is my best friend from college. Luke wrote a detailed research paper on climate change. Many parents choose the name Luke for its biblical connection. Luke showed great courage during the competition.

english_meaning: To soothe or cause someone to fall asleep or relax. To make someone feel safe or confident, often in a deceptive way. A temporary interval of quiet or lack of activity. To quiet down or subside in intensity, like a storm or noise. To cause a person's suspicions to diminish through calm behavior.
example_sentence: The gentle rocking of the boat began to lull the baby to sleep. The unexpected lull in the conversation made everyone feel slightly awkward. The general tried to lull the enemy into a false sense of security before the attack. After the heavy rain, there was a brief lull before the wind picked up again.

english_meaning: To calm or make someone sleepy by singing softly. A gentle song sung to help a child sleep. A soft, calm song usually sung by a parent or caregiver to soothe a baby or young child and help them fall asleep.
example_sentence: The mother sang a lullaby to help her baby fall asleep. The gentle lullaby calmed the crying child. Soft music played like a lullaby in the quiet room. She tried to lullaby the baby with a sweet song.

english_meaning: The lower part of the back between the ribs and the pelvis. The section of the spine formed by the five lumbar vertebrae. The area of the body that bears much of the upper body's weight. An anatomical region often associated with back pain and stiffness.
example_sentence: He suffered a muscle strain in the lumbar region. The lumbar region carries most of the body's weight. There are five vertebrae in the lumbar region of the spine. The doctor advised exercises to strengthen the lumbar region.

english_meaning: Any one of the five large bones of the spine located in the lower back. A vertebra that carries most of the body's weight and allows bending and twisting of the trunk. The strongest and largest of the movable vertebrae. A spinal bone lying between the chest region and the sacrum.
example_sentence: Lifting heavy boxes injured his lumbar vertebra. The lumbar vertebrae bear most of the upper body's weight. An MRI revealed a slipped disc between two lumbar vertebrae. Core exercises help protect the lumbar vertebrae from strain.

english_meaning: Timber that has been processed into beams and planks for construction and woodworking. Wood that has been sawn and prepared for use in building. Rough or finished wood used for structural or decorative purposes. To move clumsily or heavily with difficulty.
example_sentence: The carpenter ordered a large supply of lumber for the new house. They used high-quality lumber to build the sturdy wooden deck. The old warehouse was stacked with unused lumber. He had to lumber up the steep stairs with his heavy bags.

english_meaning: A person who inspires or influences others, especially in a particular field. A person of eminence or brilliant achievement. A natural light-giving body, especially the sun or moon. A famous or influential person in a particular area of knowledge or activity.
example_sentence: The conference was attended by luminaries from the world of science. She is regarded as a luminary in the field of modern architecture. Many young writers look up to him as a literary luminary. The luminary of the evening was the award-winning novelist.

english_meaning: Giving off light; bright or shining. Glowing in the dark, especially after absorbing light. Full of brightness or radiance in appearance. Clear, easily understood, and intellectually brilliant.
example_sentence: The dial of his watch is luminous at night. A luminous moon lit up the whole valley. Her face was luminous with joy. The professor gave a luminous explanation of the theory.

english_meaning: A compact mass of a substance, especially one without a definite or regular shape. A swelling or protuberance under the skin. An awkward or clumsy person. To tolerate or accept a disagreeable situation. A heavy or dull person. To put together in a single group without distinction.
example_sentence: There was a lump of coal in the fireplace. She found a strange lump on her arm and visited the doctor. He lumped all the expenses together into one bill. I will lump it rather than complain about the poor service. The old coat was filled with lumps from the stuffing.

english_meaning: A person or thing that appears heavy, awkward, slow, or lacking energy. It can refer to physical heaviness or clumsiness, as well as mental dullness or laziness. Something that looks shapeless or bulky.
example_sentence: The lumpish dog refused to get up from the sofa. He felt lumpish after eating too much food. The actor gave a lumpish performance with no energy. The sculpture looked lumpish and unfinished.

english_meaning: Extreme foolishness or madness. A state of severe mental instability or behaving in a way that is extremely foolish or irrational. Historically, it also referred to periodic insanity thought to be influenced by the moon.
example_sentence: It was sheer lunacy to drive in such a storm. The plan to climb the mountain without equipment showed his lunacy. Many considered the decision a form of political lunacy. She laughed at the lunacy of the situation.

english_meaning: Relating to, determined by, or resembling the moon. Measured by the moon's revolution around Earth. Shaped like a crescent moon. Connected with space travel or exploration to the moon.
example_sentence: The lunar calendar is based on moon phases. They celebrated the lunar new year with festivities. The lunar surface is covered with craters. Scientists study lunar rocks brought back from Apollo missions.

english_meaning: An astronomical event that occurs when the Earth passes between the sun and the moon, causing Earth's shadow to fall on the moon. A phenomenon where the moon appears darkened as it passes through Earth's shadow. The blocking of moonlight by Earth's position between the sun and moon.
synonyms: ["Moon eclipse","Eclipse of the moon","Lunar darkening","Blood moon (for total eclipse)"]
example_sentence: The lunar eclipse was visible from most parts of the continent. Astronomers predicted a total lunar eclipse for next month. During the lunar eclipse, the moon turned a reddish color. Many cultures have myths about lunar eclipses.

english_meaning: A person who is mentally ill, especially one who suffers from a disorder that affects behaviour. An extremely foolish or reckless person. A person whose actions are wildly unpredictable or irrational. Relating to or affected by the moon. Originally used to describe someone affected by periodic insanity believed to be caused by phases of the moon.
example_sentence: The old asylum was built to house lunatics in the nineteenth century. Only a lunatic would drive at such high speeds in the rain. He was behaving like a complete lunatic during the argument. Some ancient physicians believed that a lunatic was influenced by the moon.

english_meaning: A meal eaten in the middle of the day. The food prepared or served for the midday meal. The period of time set aside during the working day for this meal. To eat the midday meal.
example_sentence: We had lunch in a small café near the office. She packed a sandwich for lunch. The meeting will continue after lunch. They lunched together before the flight.

english_meaning: Either of the two spongy organs in the chest used for breathing. The organ that takes oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide. A respiratory organ that expands and contracts as a person breathes.
example_sentence: Each lung fills with air when we breathe in. Smoking damages the delicate tissue of the lung. The doctor listened carefully to his left lung. Regular exercise improves lung capacity.

english_meaning: A person or animal that lunges or makes a sudden forward movement. In historical contexts, a person suffering from tuberculosis or a lung disease. One who thrusts or moves forward suddenly with force. In slang, a person who attacks or moves aggressively toward someone.
example_sentence: The lungers in the crowd pressed forward to see the celebrity. The boxer was known as one of the best lungers in the ring. Historical records show that many lungers were sent to sanatoriums. He was a lunger who always attacked first in the fencing match.

english_meaning: The white crescent shaped area at the base of a fingernail or toenail. Any crescent shaped structure. A small moon shaped mark or ornament.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the lunula of his patient. A healthy lunula appears clear and white. The lunula is visible on most fingernails. Some ancient jewelry featured a lunula shape. Changes in the lunula can indicate health issues.

english_meaning: A chronic autoimmune disease that can affect various parts of the body. A condition where the immune system attacks healthy tissues and organs. A disease causing inflammation in skin, joints, and internal organs. A systemic disorder with symptoms including fatigue, joint pain, and skin rashes.
example_sentence: She was diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus. Lupus can cause a butterfly-shaped rash on the face. Treatment for lupus includes immunosuppressive medications. Lupus symptoms often flare up and then subside.

english_meaning: To make an abrupt, unsteady, or staggering movement. To move suddenly and unsteadily to one side. To sway or roll suddenly, as a ship or vehicle. A sudden roll or pitch to one side. To leave someone in a difficult or helpless position, especially without warning. An act of lurching.
example_sentence: The boat lurched violently in the stormy sea. He lurched forward as the bus suddenly stopped. The drunk man lurched from side to side along the pavement. She felt sick when the elevator lurched unexpectedly. Do not leave me in the lurch when I need your help most.

english_meaning: To persuade or trick somebody to go somewhere or to do something by promising them a reward. The quality or power that something or someone has that makes it, him, or her attractive.
example_sentence: The child was lured into a car but managed to escape. Young people are lured to the city by the prospect of a job and money. Few can resist the lure of adventure. She can’t resist the lure of the bright lights.

english_meaning: Shocking, very bright, or sensational in a disturbing way. Something that is extremely vivid, exaggerated, or sensational, often in a shocking or disturbing way. It is commonly used for graphic stories, bright unnatural colors, or exaggerated descriptions meant to attract attention.
example_sentence: The newspaper published a lurid story about the crime. He described the accident in lurid detail. The sky turned a lurid red before the storm. The movie was criticized for its lurid scenes.

english_meaning: To be present in a hidden or concealed manner, often with a sinister or threatening intent. To wait in secret or move furtively so as to remain unseen. To read or observe an online discussion without participating. To exist in a hidden or undeveloped state. To prowl or skulk around a place.
example_sentence: A stranger seemed to lurk in the shadows near the entrance. Predators often lurk near watering holes waiting for prey. I noticed someone lurking outside my window last night. He tends to lurk in chat rooms without ever posting a message. Danger can lurk in the most innocent-looking places.

english_meaning: Growing thickly and vigorously, especially with rich vegetation. Luxuriant and abundant in growth. Very attractive or appealing, often with a sensuous quality. A person who drinks alcohol to excess habitually. Rich and elaborate. Opulent and sumptuous in appearance or sensation. An area of dense vegetation, especially tropical rainforest.
example_sentence: The lush green meadows stretched as far as the eye could see. Tropical islands are known for their lush vegetation. She has a lush voice that captivates the audience. The garden was lush with roses and lilies in full bloom. He was known as the town lush who spent his evenings at the pub.

english_meaning: A stringed musical instrument with a long neck and a rounded body, played by plucking. A substance used to make joints airtight or watertight. To seal with lute.
example_sentence: He played a soft melody on the lute. Ancient poets often accompanied their songs with a lute. The workers used lute to seal the pipe joints. She learned to play the lute from her grandfather. The museum displayed a wooden lute from the sixteenth century.

english_meaning: A person who plays the lute. A musician skilled in performing music on the lute instrument. In historical contexts, a professional performer or composer for the lute. A lutist or lutanist, alternate terms for the same role. An expert in the techniques of lute playing and tuning.
example_sentence: The lutenist performed a delicate piece from the Renaissance era. She trained for years to become a professional lutenist. The concert featured a lutenist accompanying the vocalist. Famous lutenists were highly respected in the courts of Europe. He is one of the finest lutenists of his generation.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being thick, fertile, and growing in great abundance. A quality characterized by richness, elegance, and extreme comfort. The condition of being profuse or lush in growth or detail. An overflow or excess of ornamentation or artistic flourish. The state of being productive or fertile in a way that suggests prosperity.
example_sentence: The rainforest was a breathtaking display of green luxuriance. The author was known for the stylistic luxuriance of his descriptive prose. She marveled at the luxuriance of the velvet curtains in the palace. The soil's luxuriance allowed for three harvests in a single season.

english_meaning: Growing thickly, strongly, and in great abundance. Characterized by richness and extravagance in ornament or detail. Producing a great quantity of something, such as hair or vegetation. Having an appealingly rich or lush quality that suggests luxury and comfort.
example_sentence: The tropical island was covered in luxuriant green foliage. She spent hours brushing her luxuriant dark hair before the event. The ballroom was decorated in a luxuriant Baroque style. The writer is known for his luxuriant and descriptive prose.

english_meaning: In a way that is rich, abundant, or profuse in growth. With a high degree of luxury, elegance, or comfort. In a manner that is very elaborate or ornate. Characterized by lushness and fertility. In a way that provides great sensual pleasure.
example_sentence: The tropical vines grew luxuriantly over the old stone walls of the estate. Her long dark hair fell luxuriantly over her shoulders in thick waves. The hotel suite was luxuriantly decorated with velvet curtains and gold leaf. The valley was watered by several streams and bloomed luxuriantly throughout the spring.

english_meaning: To enjoy oneself in a luxurious way. To take great self-indulgent pleasure in something. To thrive or grow profusely and vigorously. To indulge in a state of comfort or sensory delight. To experience something with extreme gratification or relish.
example_sentence: She decided to luxuriate in a long, hot bubble bath after the long day. The cats love to luxuriate in the warm patches of sunlight on the floor. He wanted to luxuriate in the success of his latest novel for a few weeks. The tropical plants began to luxuriate in the humid greenhouse environment.

english_meaning: To take great pleasure in something and provide oneself with a lot of physical comfort. To enjoy something to the fullest extent, especially in a slow and relaxed way. To thrive or grow profusely in a particular environment. To indulge oneself in a specific luxury or sensory experience without restraint. To bask in a feeling, situation, or physical sensation for an extended period.
synonyms: ["Revel In","Bask In","Indulge In","Relish","Enjoy","Delight In","Wallow In","Feast On","Savor","Thrive","Flourish","Bloom","Abound","Take Pleasure In"]
example_sentence: After a long week of work, she decided to luxuriate in a hot bubble bath for hours. The travelers spent their afternoon luxuriating in the warm Mediterranean sun. The cat seemed to luxuriate in the soft velvet of the new sofa cushions. He had finally earned enough money to luxuriate in the finest hotels across Europe.

english_meaning: Very comfortable, elegant, and expensive. Providing great comfort and pleasure to the senses. Showing or involving costly and high-quality materials. Rich, generous, and indulgent in style or quality.
example_sentence: They spent the weekend in a luxurious hotel by the sea. The car has a luxurious leather interior. She wrapped herself in a luxurious woollen shawl. The resort offers luxurious rooms at surprisingly fair prices.

english_meaning: In a way that provides great comfort, especially by being very expensive. In a manner characterized by opulence and sumptuousness. In a richly, lavishly, or elegantly appointed fashion. With a focus on high quality, pleasure, and excessive convenience. In a way that suggests a state of great abundance or ease.
example_sentence: The hotel suite was luxuriously furnished with velvet curtains and gold accents. They spent the afternoon lounging luxuriously by the heated infinity pool. The car was luxuriously appointed with hand-stitched leather seats and a premium sound system. She stretched out luxuriously on the soft silk sheets after a long day of travel.

english_meaning: Great comfort and pleasure obtained from expensive and beautiful things. Something expensive and pleasant that is not necessary for ordinary life. A state of living surrounded by rich and costly surroundings. Relating to goods or services of the highest quality and price.
example_sentence: They lived in luxury after the business succeeded. A quiet morning with a good book is my favourite luxury. The hotel is known for its luxury and excellent service. He bought a luxury watch to celebrate his promotion.

english_meaning: A small round tropical fruit with rough red skin, translucent white flesh, and a single seed. A sweet, fragrant fruit eaten fresh or canned. The tree that bears this fruit. A summer fruit popular in Asian desserts and drinks.
example_sentence: Fresh lychees are available only for a few weeks. She peeled a lychee and popped it into her mouth. Lychee juice is served chilled at the restaurant. The lychee orchard is in full fruit this year.

english_meaning: A clear, pale fluid that circulates through the lymphatic system. The fluid that drains from body tissues into the lymph vessels. A liquid containing white blood cells that helps fight infection. A fluid that carries fats and waste products away from tissues.
example_sentence: Lymph flows slowly through the lymphatic vessels. White blood cells travel in the lymph to fight infection. Excess fluid from the tissues becomes lymph. The lymph is finally returned to the bloodstream near the neck.

english_meaning: A small bean-shaped structure that forms part of the lymphatic system. A gland-like organ that filters lymph and traps bacteria and harmful cells. A structure containing white blood cells that fight infection. A node that swells when the body is fighting illness.
example_sentence: The doctor felt a swollen lymph node in his neck. Lymph nodes filter harmful bacteria out of the lymph. Cancer cells can spread through the lymph nodes. A biopsy was taken from the affected lymph node.

english_meaning: A thin tube that carries lymph through the body. A channel of the lymphatic system that drains fluid from tissues. A vessel that transports lymph towards the lymph nodes and back to the blood. A tube containing valves that keep lymph flowing in one direction.
example_sentence: Lymph vessels carry fluid away from the tissues. Damage to a lymph vessel can cause swelling in the limb. Lymph vessels run alongside veins in most parts of the body. The surgeon avoided cutting the main lymph vessel.

english_meaning: Relating to or containing lymph, the clear fluid that circulates through the lymphatic system. Pertaining to the vessels, nodes, and organs that transport lymph. A person having a sluggish or relaxed temperament, formerly believed to be due to excess lymph. Characterized by a lack of energy or vigour. Relating to the immune system and fluid balance in the body.
example_sentence: The lymphatic system plays a vital role in immune defence. Lymphatic vessels carry fluid away from tissues. The surgeon carefully examined the lymphatic nodes for signs of cancer. Her lymphatic temperament made her appear calm and slow to react. Exercise helps stimulate lymphatic circulation throughout the body.

english_meaning: A surgical incision made into a lymphatic vessel or lymph node. A procedure used to drain, examine, or relieve pressure in lymphatic tissue. The cutting open of a lymph gland for diagnosis or treatment. A rare operation performed in cases of lymphatic swelling or infection.
example_sentence: The surgeon carried out a lymphotomy to drain the swollen gland. A lymphotomy was needed to identify the cause of the infection. Lymphotomy is performed far less often than lymph node biopsy. The patient recovered well after the lymphotomy.

english_meaning: To put a person to death by mob action without legal sanction or a proper trial. This act of violence is typically carried out by a self-constituted group. It is often associated with racial or political prejudice and historical injustice.
example_sentence: A frantic mob attempted to lynch the prisoner before the police arrived. History books record the tragic era when groups would lynch people without trial. The governor took measures to prevent the angry crowd from trying to lynch the suspect. Local laws were strictly enforced to ensure no one would ever lynch another citizen.

english_meaning: A vague feeling of sadness. It refers to a deep but unclear sense of sadness or melancholy where a person feels low or uneasy without knowing the exact reason. It is not linked to a specific event and often feels emotional rather than logical.
example_sentence: He woke up with a strange sense of lypophrenia even though everything in his life seemed fine. The quiet evening triggered a wave of lypophrenia that she could not explain. Artists often describe lypophrenia as a source of creative reflection. His smile hid a lingering lypophrenia that words could not express.

english_meaning: A stringed musical instrument of the harp class used in ancient Greece and later periods. It typically consists of a U-shaped frame with a crossbar from which strings are stretched to a soundboard. A symbol of lyric poetry and artistic inspiration often associated with Apollo. A small handheld instrument played by plucking the strings with the fingers or a plectrum. Any instrument resembling this form used in historical or heraldic contexts.
example_sentence: The ancient poet strummed his lyre while reciting epic verses to the king. A golden lyre is often depicted in art as a symbol of the god Apollo. The museum displayed a well-preserved lyre dating back to the classical period. Musicians in ancient times used the lyre to accompany songs and theatrical performances.

english_meaning: A large ground-dwelling Australian bird of the genus Menura. It is famous for its extraordinary ability to mimic natural and artificial sounds from its environment. The male possesses an elaborate and beautiful tail that, when displayed, resembles a Greek lyre. These birds are known for their intricate courtship rituals and powerful vocalizations.
example_sentence: The lyrebird is capable of perfectly imitating the sound of a chainsaw. During the mating season, the male lyrebird displays its stunning tail feathers to attract a mate. Hikers in the Australian bush are often startled by the loud and complex calls of the lyrebird. The lyrebird belongs to a family of birds that are among the oldest surviving songbirds.

english_meaning: A category of poetry that expresses the writer's emotions, usually briefly and in stanzas. The words of a popular song. Relating to a category of poetry that expresses subjective thoughts and feelings in a songlike style. Characterized by or expressing spontaneous and direct feeling. Having a sweet, flowing, and melodious quality of sound. A short poem of songlike character.
example_sentence: She wrote a beautiful lyric for the new pop single. The poet is famous for his mastery of the lyric form. The soprano's lyric voice enchanted the entire audience. The song's lyric explores themes of loss and redemption.

english_meaning: Expressing the writer's emotions in an imaginative and beautiful way. Relating to the category of poetry that expresses personal emotions or feelings, typically spoken in the first person. Having an artistically beautiful or expressive quality. Characterized by or showing a spontaneous and enthusiastic expression of emotion. Having a musical sound or rhythmic quality reminiscent of a song.
example_sentence: The author's lyrical prose turned a simple story into a masterpiece. She was in a lyrical mood after receiving the wonderful news. The violinist delivered a lyrical performance that moved the entire audience to tears. His description of the countryside was deeply lyrical and evocative.

english_meaning: Disturbing and horrifying because of involvement with or depiction of death and injury. Gruesome and grim, associated with the grisly aspects of mortality. Having a quality that causes unease or fascination with death. Ghastly and shocking in its focus on the morbid. Eerie and dark, often in an artistic or literary context.
example_sentence: The horror film had a macabre atmosphere that unsettled the audience. He had a macabre fascination with old graveyards. The artist's macabre paintings depicted skeletal figures. The macabre details of the crime were too disturbing for some readers. Halloween celebrations often include macabre decorations and costumes.

english_meaning: To soften food by soaking it in a liquid. To break something down into pieces by soaking it. To make someone thin or weak, especially through fasting.
example_sentence: Macerate the strawberries in sugar for an hour before serving. The herbs were macerated in oil to make a fragrant extract. The chef macerated the dried fruit in orange juice. Long fasting had macerated his body.

english_meaning: A broad, heavy knife with a long blade, used for cutting through thick plants or as a weapon. A large chopping blade used in farming.
example_sentence: The guide used a machete to clear a path through the jungle. Farmers cut the sugarcane with sharp machetes. He kept a machete in the truck for clearing branches. The police recovered a machete from the scene.

english_meaning: Cunning and deceitful, especially in politics or in seeking power. Using clever but dishonest methods. Sly. Manipulative. Unscrupulous. Used to describe a person or behaviour that is willing to use any means, including lies, tricks, or unethical actions, in order to achieve personal goals, especially political or professional success. It comes from the Italian writer Niccolò Machiavelli.
example_sentence: He used Machiavellian tactics to remove his rivals from the company. The novel describes the Machiavellian schemes of a corrupt minister. Her Machiavellian behavior shocked even her closest friends. Some leaders are admired for their Machiavellian skill in politics. He saw a Machiavellian plot behind every appointment.

english_meaning: A secret and clever plan to achieve something, usually harmful or dishonest. A scheme or plot. The act of plotting or scheming.
example_sentence: The king's advisers were involved in political machinations. She uncovered the machinations behind the takeover. The film shows the machinations of a corrupt businessman. Despite all their machinations, the rivals failed to win the election.

english_meaning: A device with moving parts that uses power to perform a particular task. A computer or similar electronic device. An organised group or system that controls something, such as a political machine. A person who works tirelessly or mechanically. To make or shape something using a machine.
example_sentence: The washing machine stopped working last night. The factory uses a machine to cut the metal sheets. The party's political machine helped him win the election. He is a machine on the football pitch and never seems tired.

english_meaning: The state of being very thin or lean. Extreme leanness of the body. A wasted or emaciated condition.
example_sentence: The macilency of the patient worried the doctors. Years of hunger explained his macilency. Her macilency was visible even from a distance. The report described the macilency of the stray animals.

english_meaning: Large in scale or scope; concerned with the whole rather than the details. In computing, a single instruction that automatically carries out a set of commands. A close-up photograph or lens used for photographing very small objects. A large-scale view or approach to a subject, such as macro economics.
example_sentence: He wrote a macro to speed up the monthly report. The article takes a macro view of the economy. She bought a macro lens for photographing insects. At the macro level, the policy appears successful.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or relating to a diet based on whole grains and vegetables believed to promote longevity. Promoting or tending to result in long life through dietary and lifestyle choices. A system of holistic living involving meditative eating and balance. Characterized by the consumption of natural, minimally processed foods.
example_sentence: She followed a macrobiotic diet consisting primarily of brown rice and steamed greens. Many proponents of macrobiotic living emphasize the importance of local and seasonal ingredients. He credited his macrobiotic lifestyle for his remarkable health in his eighties. The restaurant specializes in macrobiotic meals that avoid refined sugars and dairy.

english_meaning: The small yellowish area near the centre of the retina responsible for sharp central vision. The part of the eye that allows us to read, recognise faces, and see fine detail and colour. Any small spot or discoloured patch on the skin or another surface.
example_sentence: The macula gives us clear, detailed central vision. Age-related damage to the macula can make reading difficult. The eye specialist photographed the macula of both eyes. Sharp colour vision depends on the health of the macula.

english_meaning: A bright purplish-red colour. One of the three primary colours used in colour printing, along with cyan and yellow. Describing something of this vivid pinkish-purple shade.
example_sentence: The printer has run out of magenta ink. She chose magenta curtains for the living room. The sunset turned the clouds a deep magenta. Magenta and cyan are used in colour printing.

english_meaning: The soft bodied legless larva of a fly. A whim or odd fancy. Slang for a contemptible person. Used as bait in fishing.
example_sentence: Maggots infested the rotting meat. Fishermen use maggots as bait. The bin was full of maggots by summer. Doctors sometimes use maggots to clean wounds. He looked at the maggot with disgust.

english_meaning: A state of chaos, confusion, or disorder. Situations or conditions where there is extreme disorder, turmoil, or uproar. It can describe social unrest, personal confusion, or chaotic environments.
example_sentence: The sudden announcement of the closure caused maghem in the office. Political protests turned the city into a scene of maghem. There was maghem at the airport after the flight cancellations. The classroom descended into maghem when the students started arguing loudly.

english_meaning: To make something disappear suddenly or seem to vanish as if by magic.
example_sentence: The magician magicked the rabbit away. You can’t magic away your problems. The stain was magically magicked away. He wished he could magic away his pain.

english_meaning: Hot molten or partly molten rock beneath the earth’s surface. A thick or pasty mass formed from a liquid suspension. A foundational mixture or source from which something develops, in rare figurative use.
synonyms: ["Molten rock","Lava beneath the surface","Melt","Igneous melt","Pasty mass"]
example_sentence: Magma rose through cracks beneath the volcano. As magma cools, it can form solid igneous rock. Scientists measured the movement of magma below the island. The eruption forced glowing magma toward the surface.

english_meaning: With great praise, an academic distinction awarded for very high achievement. A Latin graduation honor usually ranked below summa cum laude and above cum laude.
synonyms: ["With great honors","With high distinction","With great praise"]
example_sentence: She graduated magna cum laude in economics. His transcript records the honor magna cum laude. Years of careful work helped him finish magna cum laude. The faculty selected twelve students to graduate magna cum laude.

english_meaning: The quality of being generous, noble, and forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person. Greatness of spirit shown by rising above resentment or pettiness. Generous conduct or an act of kindness toward an opponent.
example_sentence: She showed magnanimity by congratulating the winner warmly. His magnanimity toward his former rival surprised everyone. The leader accepted the apology with remarkable magnanimity. True magnanimity is most visible after a hard-fought victory.

english_meaning: Very generous, kind, and forgiving, especially towards an enemy, rival, or weaker person. Having a noble and large-hearted nature. Showing greatness of mind by overlooking insults, injuries, or petty matters. Willing to give more than is necessary or expected. Showing a high-minded and noble character.
example_sentence: The king was magnanimous in his treatment of the defeated enemy. It was magnanimous of her to forgive him after such a betrayal. He made a magnanimous donation to the orphanage. The winner was magnanimous in his victory speech. Only a truly magnanimous person can rise above petty disputes.

english_meaning: In a generous and forgiving manner, especially toward a rival. With nobility of spirit and without petty resentment. In a way that shows graciousness after victory or advantage.
example_sentence: She magnanimously credited the entire team for the success. He magnanimously forgave the colleague who had insulted him. The winner magnanimously praised her closest competitor. They magnanimously withdrew the complaint after receiving an apology.

english_meaning: A wealthy, powerful, and influential person in business or industry. A person of high rank, importance, or influence in a particular field. Historically, a powerful noble or landowner.
example_sentence: The media magnate purchased another television network. A shipping magnate funded the new harbor. The young entrepreneur hoped to become a technology magnate. Several industrial magnates attended the economic summit.

english_meaning: A light, silvery-white metallic chemical element with the symbol Mg and atomic number 12. An essential mineral needed by the body for muscles, nerves, bones, and many chemical processes. A metal that burns with an intense white light and is used in alloys, medicine, and industry.
example_sentence: Magnesium is commonly added to lightweight metal alloys. Leafy green vegetables are a useful source of magnesium. The laboratory demonstration showed magnesium burning with a bright white flame. A doctor may test magnesium levels when muscle cramps persist.

english_meaning: A piece of iron or other material that attracts metal objects. An object that produces a magnetic field. A device used to hold, lift, or guide metal items. A person, place, or thing that strongly attracts people. Something that draws interest or attention powerfully.
example_sentence: He stuck the note on the fridge with a small magnet. A magnet will not attract copper or aluminium. The old city has become a magnet for tourists. Free lessons made the centre a magnet for young learners.

english_meaning: Having the power to attract iron and other metals. Relating to a magnet or a magnetic field. Able to be attracted by a magnet. Extremely attractive or charming in personality. Capable of drawing strong interest or attention.
example_sentence: The compass needle points north because of the magnetic field. Steel is magnetic, but plastic is not. She has a magnetic personality that wins people over. His magnetic voice held the audience for an hour.

english_meaning: The physical force by which magnets attract or repel objects. The branch of science that studies magnetic fields and their effects. The property of attracting iron and certain other metals. A strong personal charm that attracts other people. Powerful influence or appeal that draws attention.
example_sentence: The students studied magnetism in their physics class. Earth's magnetism guides the needle of a compass. His personal magnetism filled the entire hall. The singer's magnetism kept the audience spellbound.

english_meaning: Great beauty, grandeur, splendor, or impressive richness in appearance or style. It refers to something very grand, noble, or visually striking such as architecture, nature, ceremonies, or achievements.
example_sentence: The magnificence of the palace amazed every visitor. We admired the magnificence of the mountains at sunrise. The ceremony was organized with great magnificence and dignity. The artist captured the magnificence of nature in his painting.

english_meaning: Extremely beautiful, impressive, or striking in appearance. Very grand, splendid, or imposing in size, quality, or style. Deserving great praise because of excellence or outstanding performance. Noble and generous in spirit or behaviour. Luxurious and richly decorated in a way that inspires admiration.
example_sentence: The palace looked magnificent in the golden evening light. She gave a magnificent performance at the concert last night. From the hilltop we enjoyed a magnificent view of the valley. He showed magnificent courage during the rescue operation.

english_meaning: In an extremely beautiful, grand, or impressive manner. In a way that deserves great praise or admiration. Splendidly and on a large or luxurious scale. Excellently and with outstanding skill or success. In a noble and generous way.
example_sentence: The hall was magnificently decorated for the wedding. She sang magnificently in front of a large audience. The team played magnificently and won the final match. The old mosque is magnificently preserved.

english_meaning: To make something appear larger, especially using a lens or microscope. To increase the size, importance, or effect of something. To exaggerate or overstate a problem or feeling. To praise or glorify.
example_sentence: The microscope magnifies tiny cells for study. He tends to magnify his problems unnecessarily. The mirror magnified her reflection. The hymn magnifies the greatness of God.

english_meaning: Using high-flown or bombastic language; speaking or writing in an impressive and elevated manner that may be overly grand or pompous.
example_sentence: The magniloquent speaker impressed the crowd but said very little. His magniloquent writing style hid a lack of real substance. She delivered a magniloquent speech at the award ceremony. The magniloquent professor made simple topics sound complex.

english_meaning: The great size or extent of something. The importance or quality of something. A number that represents the brightness of a star or other celestial object. In physics, the absolute or relative size of a quantity or vector. The degree of brightness or intensity. The level of significance or impact of an event or phenomenon.
example_sentence: The magnitude of the earthquake was measured at 7.5 on the Richter scale. We did not realize the magnitude of the problem until it was too late. The star had a magnitude visible to the naked eye. The magnitude of her achievement astonished everyone. Understanding the magnitude of the task helped them plan better.

english_meaning: A young, unmarried woman, first or initial in occurrence. A young woman who is unmarried, often implying purity or innocence. Something occurring for the first time. Something not previously used or operated. Innocence, purity, or idealized youth. Often used for ships, planes, or rockets on their first journey. A “maiden over” means an over in which no runs are scored. Representing purity, honor, or the start of something important. Sometimes used for the first win, goal, or achievement in a season or tournament.
example_sentence: The maiden won the singing competition with ease. The ship completed its maiden voyage yesterday. She gave her maiden speech at the conference. The team celebrated their maiden victory in the tournament.

english_meaning: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional. Belonging to or characteristic of a prevailing current. To bring into the mainstream.
example_sentence: Rock music once considered rebellious is now mainstream. The channel focuses on mainstream news. Special education students were mainstreamed into regular classes. Her ideas were outside the mainstream of politics. Streaming has become the mainstream way of watching movies.

english_meaning: To keep something in good condition by looking after it regularly. To continue something without change or interruption. To provide financial or material support for someone. To state firmly that something is true, especially when others disagree. To keep records or accounts up to date.
example_sentence: The government must maintain the roads and bridges. He struggled to maintain his composure during the interview. She works two jobs to maintain her family. The accused continues to maintain his innocence.

english_meaning: The process of keeping something in good condition through regular care and repair. The act of continuing or preserving a state or situation. Money paid regularly for the support of a spouse or children after separation. Financial support given for living expenses.
example_sentence: The building requires regular maintenance to stay safe. Road maintenance work will continue for two weeks. He pays monthly maintenance for his two children. Poor maintenance of the machines caused the breakdown.

english_meaning: A small flat set on two floors with its own separate entrance. A part of a larger building that works like a small house. A two-storey apartment within a block of flats. A compact dwelling for one family inside a shared building. A small house in older or French-influenced usage.
example_sentence: They rented a small maisonette near the city centre. The maisonette has its own front door and a tiny garden. A maisonette often feels more like a house than a flat. She sold her maisonette and moved to the countryside.

english_meaning: A Central American cereal plant that yields large grains set in rows on a cob. The grain of this plant, also known as corn, which is used for human food or animal feed. A pale yellow colour resembling the grain.
example_sentence: The farmers planted acres of maize to harvest in the autumn. She boiled the maize and served it with butter and salt. The cattle were fed a diet consisting mostly of crushed maize. The artist painted the kitchen walls in a warm maize colour.

english_meaning: Impressive beauty, scale, or dignity. The quality of being majestic or grand. A title used to address or refer to a reigning king or queen. Royal power and authority. The stateliness and splendour associated with sovereignty. An awe-inspiring quality that commands respect and admiration. Sovereign dignity and exalted rank.
example_sentence: The majesty of the mountains took my breath away. Your Majesty is a formal address to the monarch. The palace was decorated with all the majesty fitting a royal wedding. We watched in awe at the majesty of the eagle in flight. The ceremony was conducted with great majesty and solemnity.

english_meaning: Very large, important, or serious in size, extent, or effect. Greater in number, size, or rank than others of the same kind. A military officer ranking above a captain and below a lieutenant colonel. The main subject that a student studies at a college or university. To study a particular subject as one's main course of study.
example_sentence: The city faces a major water shortage this summer. He was promoted to the rank of major last year. Her major is economics with a minor in statistics. Poor planning was a major cause of the delay.

english_meaning: To study a particular subject as the main part of a university degree. To specialise in a chosen field of study at college. To choose a principal subject for one's academic programme. Informally, to be very good at or devote most attention to something.
example_sentence: She decided to major in computer science. Many students major in business studies these days. He plans to major in history and then study law. If you major in physics, you must take extra mathematics.

english_meaning: To give most of one's attention or effort to a particular subject or activity. To treat something as the main focus of a discussion, plan, or business. In British usage, to concentrate mainly on one area or topic. To emphasise one aspect above all others.
example_sentence: The report majors on the need for better schools. Their business majors on imported electronics. His speech majored on economic reform. The training course majors on practical skills.

english_meaning: The greater number or larger part of a group of people or things. The number of votes by which one side wins an election. The state of having reached the legal age of adulthood. The political party or group having the most seats or members.
example_sentence: The majority of students passed the examination. The party won the election with a comfortable majority. He inherited the property after reaching his majority. In a democracy, the majority forms the government.

english_meaning: To twist or change your facial expression to show dislike, disgust, surprise, pain, or funny emotion.
example_sentence: She made a face when she tasted the sour lemon. The child made a face at the bitter medicine. He made a face when he saw the messy room. Don’t make a face at your teacher; it’s rude.

english_meaning: To behave in a silly, careless, or embarrassing way that makes others laugh or lose respect for you. To damage your own reputation through silly behavior. To appear ridiculous in public. To lose respect due to poor judgment.
synonyms: ["Embarrass yourself","Make a spectacle of yourself","Act foolishly","Humiliate yourself","Look ridiculous"]
antonyms: ["Behave wisely","Act sensibly","Maintain dignity","Show maturity","Present yourself well"]
example_sentence: He made a fool of himself by shouting during the meeting. Don’t make a fool of yourself by arguing over something trivial. She made a fool of herself trying to impress everyone. If you lie and get caught, you will make a fool of yourself.

english_meaning: To complain about something usually unimportant. To show unnecessary excitement or worry about something. To create a scene or disturbance over a trivial matter. To shower excessive attention on someone or something.
synonyms: ["Complain","Grumble","Whine","Create A Scene","Raise A Ruckus","Kick Up A Dust","Throw A Fit","Make Much Ado","Overreact","Kick Up A Row"]
antonyms: ["Keep Calm","Be Quiet","Remain Silent","Ignore","Brush Off","Let Go","Accept Peacefully","Downplay","Stay Serene"]
example_sentence: Please do not make a fuss about such a minor mistake. She tends to make a fuss whenever her order is slightly delayed. The grandmother always makes a fuss over her grandchildren when they visit. He made a huge fuss about the seating arrangements at the wedding.

word: Make a mountain out of a molehill
english_meaning: To make a small issue seem very big. To exaggerate a small problem or situation and treat it as something much bigger or more serious than it really is. It means overreacting or blowing things out of proportion.
example_sentence: She made a mountain out of a molehill when her tea spilled on the table. It’s better to stay calm instead of making a mountain out of a molehill. He always makes a mountain out of a molehill whenever something goes wrong. They made a mountain out of a molehill about a simple misunderstanding. The manager made a mountain out of a molehill about a tiny typing mistake.

english_meaning: To become famous, respected, or well known because of one's achievements. This phrase is used when a person gains recognition through hard work, talent, or success. It suggests building a reputation so that others know and respect the person.
synonyms: ["Become famous","Gain recognition","Build a reputation","Establish oneself","Rise to prominence"]
