english_meaning: To measure or regulate. A device to measure. In literature, the structured rhythm of syllables or beats in a line of poetry.
example_sentence: The electricity meter shows our monthly usage. He checked the water meter before paying the bill. The parking meter expired after two hours. A speedometer is a type of meter in vehicles.

english_meaning: Informal short form of methamphetamine, a powerful and highly addictive stimulant drug. An illegal synthetic drug that affects the central nervous system. A shortened colloquial term used in everyday speech for methamphetamine.
example_sentence: The documentary explored the devastating impact of meth addiction on small rural communities. Police seized a large quantity of meth during the raid on the abandoned warehouse. He sought treatment at a rehabilitation centre after struggling with meth addiction for several years. The rise in meth-related crime has placed enormous pressure on local law enforcement. Public health campaigns continue to warn young people about the serious dangers of meth use.

english_meaning: A particular procedure for accomplishing something. An orderly or systematic way of doing something. A regular manner or established process. The means used to achieve a result. A defined technique used in study or work.
example_sentence: He developed a new method for teaching math. This is the best method to solve the problem. The scientist used a reliable method. There are many methods of learning a language.

english_meaning: Done in a systematic, orderly, and careful manner. Characterised by a clear method or organised approach. Showing discipline and precision in carrying out tasks. Thorough and well-planned in execution.
example_sentence: She approached every task in a methodical way, never skipping a single step in the process. The detective conducted a methodical search of the crime scene, leaving nothing unexamined. His methodical preparation for the exam ensured that he covered every topic thoroughly. The engineers followed a methodical procedure to test the safety of the new bridge design. A methodical approach to budgeting helped the family save a significant amount of money each month.

english_meaning: Relating to methods, systems, procedures, or research design. Concerned with the way a study, investigation, or task is planned and carried out. Based on orderly and disciplined techniques.
example_sentence: The reviewer found a methodological weakness in the study. Methodological clarity makes research easier to repeat. The team discussed methodological changes before collecting data. His methodological approach was careful and transparent. A methodological error can affect the final result.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to method, procedure, or research design. According to a planned, systematic, or disciplined method. With attention to the principles and techniques used in a study or task.
example_sentence: The study is methodologically strong. Methodologically, the survey needs a larger sample. She approached the problem methodologically rather than emotionally. The two reports differ methodologically. A methodologically careful experiment is easier to trust.

english_meaning: A system of methods used in a particular area of study, research, or activity. The theoretical analysis of the methods applied to a field of study. A structured approach or set of principles guiding research or practice.
example_sentence: The research paper provided a detailed explanation of the methodology used to collect and analyse the data. The company adopted a new methodology to improve efficiency across all departments. Her thesis included a chapter dedicated entirely to outlining her research methodology. The teaching methodology focused heavily on practical, hands-on learning rather than rote memorisation. Different scientific disciplines often require entirely different methodologies to test their hypotheses.

english_meaning: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. Taking extreme care to get every small detail right, often to the point of being thorough beyond what is expected.
example_sentence: She was meticulous in her research and never missed a detail. The meticulous surgeon prepared every instrument before the operation. His meticulous notes helped him pass every exam with top marks. A meticulous approach is essential in forensic investigations.

english_meaning: In a very careful, precise, and detailed manner. Done with great attention to small details and accuracy. With thoroughness and exactness, leaving nothing unchecked. In a way that shows perfection, neatness, and concern for quality. Often used to describe work, planning, or organisation that is performed with extreme care.
example_sentence: She meticulously planned every detail of the wedding ceremony. The scientist meticulously recorded every observation in his notebook. He meticulously cleaned every corner of the house before the guests arrived. The artist meticulously painted the small details on the canvas. The accountant meticulously checked each entry in the register.

english_meaning: The quality of being extremely careful, precise, and attentive to detail. The trait of doing things with great accuracy and thoroughness. The habit of focusing on every small detail to ensure perfection. A noun describing the careful and exact manner in which something is performed or maintained.
example_sentence: His meticulousness in handling documents earned him a promotion. The meticulousness of the surgeon impressed everyone in the operation theatre. She is known for her meticulousness in financial matters. The meticulousness of the craftsman was visible in every piece of furniture. Meticulousness is an essential quality for a good editor.

english_meaning: A standard for measuring something. A numerical measure used to assess performance, quality, or progress. Relating to the metric system of measurement.
example_sentence: Customer satisfaction is an important metric. The dashboard shows several financial metrics. The ruler uses metric units. The team chose response time as its main performance metric.

english_meaning: A unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms. The same as a tonne. A large unit used in trade and industry for heavy goods. A unit sometimes called a megagram.
example_sentence: The country exported fifty thousand metric tons of rice. One metric ton equals 1,000 kilograms. Coal is usually sold by the metric ton. The ship carried thirty metric tons of cargo.

english_meaning: Relating to metrology, the science of measurement. Concerned with standards, accuracy, calibration, and units of measurement. Connected with precise measuring instruments and measurement systems.
example_sentence: The laboratory follows strict metrological standards. Metrological accuracy is important in engineering. The device requires metrological calibration every year. A metrological error can change the result of an experiment. The institute provides metrological services to manufacturers.

english_meaning: A large, busy, and important city, especially the capital or principal city of a country or region. A central or chief city of a particular activity or sector. An urban area of major significance, population, and influence.
example_sentence: Tokyo is one of the largest and most densely populated metropolises in the world. The novel is set in a sprawling metropolis where millions of people live side by side. Moving from a small town to a bustling metropolis was a significant adjustment for the entire family. The metropolis offers countless cultural attractions, from museums and theatres to world-class restaurants. The skyline of the metropolis was illuminated by thousands of lights as night fell.

english_meaning: Relating to a large city or an important urban area. Characteristic of people, culture, or lifestyle found in a big city. Connected with the capital city of a country. A person living in a large city. In some Christian churches, a bishop with authority over several dioceses.
example_sentence: She enjoys the fast paced metropolitan lifestyle. The metropolitan area has an excellent public transportation system. Many international companies have offices in metropolitan cities. Metropolitan museums attract millions of visitors every year.

english_meaning: A man who is attracted to women sexually but who is also interested in fashion and his appearance. A heterosexual man who lives in a city and is interested in things like fashion, shopping and his appearance.
example_sentence: My metrosexual husband has so many shirts that he needs more wardrobe space. Herbivore man is a dandy metrosexual with an abhorrence of martial arts.

english_meaning: Courage, strength of character, and determination, especially when facing difficulties. A person's ability to remain brave, determined, resilient, and confident when facing challenges, pressure, danger, or hardship. It describes inner strength and character rather than physical power.
example_sentence: The young officer showed his mettle during the emergency. Difficult situations often reveal a person's true mettle. She proved her mettle by completing the project despite many obstacles. The team displayed great mettle in the final match and secured victory.

english_meaning: Full of spirit, courage, and determination. Showing eagerness and resilience, especially when facing challenges. Spirited and energetic in temperament, often used to describe horses or people of strong character.
example_sentence: The mettlesome young rider managed to stay calm and in control of the spirited horse. Her mettlesome attitude helped her push through the most difficult stages of the marathon. The team showed a mettlesome spirit, refusing to give up even when the situation looked hopeless. He was known throughout the regiment as a mettlesome soldier who never backed down from a challenge. The mettlesome pony pranced excitedly around the paddock, eager to begin its training.

english_meaning: A large amount or great quantity of something. Great or much in size or degree. A significant portion or majority. An archaic or dialectal term for 'much'. Often used in the proverb 'many a little makes a mickle'.
example_sentence: They say that many a little makes a mickle, so keep saving your coins. There was a mickle of gold discovered in the ancient cavern. Even a mickle of effort can lead to a great result over time. The old man possessed a mickle of wisdom from his years of travel.

english_meaning: Extremely small in size, scale, or scope. Relating to something very small or examined in fine detail. A prefix meaning one millionth of a unit. An informal short form of microcomputer or microphone.
example_sentence: The company focuses on micro loans for small farmers. Designers added micro animations to the buttons. A micro crack in the glass slowly grew larger. He studies changes at the micro level of the economy.

english_meaning: A tiny wafer of semiconductor material on which an integrated circuit is etched, used to power computers, phones, cars, and countless electronic devices.
example_sentence: Every smartphone contains at least one microchip. The veterinarian implanted a microchip to identify the lost dog. A single microchip can store enormous amounts of data. Manufacturing a microchip requires extremely clean facilities.

english_meaning: The climate of a very small or restricted area, such as a garden, valley, or the space under a tree, which may differ from the climate of the surrounding region.
example_sentence: The south-facing wall creates a warm microclimate for tender plants. Vineyard managers study microclimate to improve grape quality. The city centre has a hotter microclimate than the suburbs. A greenhouse provides a controlled microclimate for exotic flowers.

english_meaning: Very small, round bacteria that usually appear in clusters (plural of Micrococcus). Spherical bacteria belonging to the genus Micrococcus. They are commonly found in soil, water, dust, and on human skin. Most micrococci are harmless, but some may cause infections in people with weak immune systems. They reproduce by cell division and often form clusters.
example_sentence: Micrococci are commonly found on human skin. The laboratory identified micrococci under the microscope. Some micrococci can survive in extreme environmental conditions. The doctor tested the wound for the presence of micrococci.

english_meaning: A very small round bacterium that usually grows in clusters and is commonly found in soil, water, dust, and on human skin.
example_sentence: Scientists observed Micrococcus under the microscope during the lab experiment. Micrococcus species are commonly found on human skin. The soil sample contained colonies of Micrococcus. Certain Micrococcus strains can survive in harsh environmental conditions.

english_meaning: A low-level set of instructions built into a microprocessor that define how higher-level machine-language instructions are executed. It controls the internal operation of the processor.
example_sentence: The processor update included revised microcode to fix security flaws. Engineers patched the microcode without changing the hardware. Microcode translates complex instructions into simpler control signals. Understanding microcode is essential for processor design.

english_meaning: A small computer containing a microprocessor as its central processing unit, designed for individual use. Examples include personal computers, laptops, and early home computers.
example_sentence: The first popular microcomputer arrived in the late 1970s. He learned programming on a simple microcomputer at school. A microcomputer can fit on a desk yet perform complex calculations. Modern smartphones are far more powerful than early microcomputers.

english_meaning: A small community, place, or group that has the same characteristics as a much larger one, and is therefore seen as a miniature representation of it.
example_sentence: The classroom was a microcosm of the wider society. The festival served as a microcosm of national cultures. A coral reef is a microcosm of marine biodiversity. His garden was a microcosm of the entire botanical world.

english_meaning: A very small photographic image, usually of a document, reduced to the size of a dot. Also refers to a tiny spot or point, sometimes used in printing and security features.
example_sentence: Spies used a microdot to hide secret messages during the war. The microdot contained an entire page of text visible only under magnification. Modern identity cards use microdots as anti-counterfeiting measures. He photographed the map and reduced it to a microdot.

english_meaning: Relating to or concerned with very small electronic circuits and devices, typically those built on semiconductor chips. Used in computing, telecommunications, and consumer electronics.
example_sentence: Microelectronic components have revolutionized mobile phone design. The lab specializes in microelectronic engineering for spacecraft instruments. Advances in microelectronic fabrication allow billions of transistors on a single chip. A microelectronic sensor can detect minute chemical changes.

english_meaning: The branch of electronics that deals with the design and manufacture of extremely small electronic circuits and components, especially integrated circuits and semiconductor devices.
example_sentence: She pursued a career in microelectronics after graduating in electrical engineering. Microelectronics has enabled the development of powerful yet compact computers. Clean rooms are essential in microelectronics manufacturing. The company invests heavily in research in microelectronics.

english_meaning: A very fine synthetic fiber, typically thinner than a denier, made from polyester or polyamide. It is used in cleaning cloths, sportswear, and textiles because it is soft, absorbent, and effective at trapping dust.
example_sentence: I prefer microfibre cloths for cleaning glass because they leave no streaks. The jacket is lined with microfibre for extra comfort. Microfibre towels dry much faster than cotton ones. Dust particles cling easily to microfibre surfaces.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to one millionth of a gram. An extremely small unit used for measuring vitamins, hormones, and traces of chemicals. A unit equal to one thousandth of a milligram.
example_sentence: The vitamin dose is measured in micrograms. One milligram contains a thousand micrograms. Even a few micrograms of the substance can be harmful. The report listed the pollution level in micrograms per cubic metre.

english_meaning: An extremely small or miniature version of something that is itself already a small representation of a larger whole. A diminutive microcosm.
example_sentence: The tiny model village was a micromicrocosm of the bustling city. Inside the classroom, the group project became a micromicrocosm of society. The pond ecosystem served as a micromicrocosm of the regional biosphere. Each cell can be seen as a micromicrocosm of the entire organism.

english_meaning: Tiny living organisms invisible to the naked eye. Microscopic life forms including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa. Single-celled or simple multicellular organisms requiring magnification to see. Organisms that can be beneficial, harmful, or neutral to humans.
example_sentence: Microorganisms are found everywhere in nature. Some microorganisms cause diseases. Beneficial microorganisms help in digestion. Scientists study microorganisms under microscopes.

english_meaning: A very small payment made electronically, often for digital content, online services, or small transactions that are too minor for traditional payment systems.
example_sentence: The article costs only a few cents via the micropayment system. Micropayments allow readers to support journalists per article. Blockchain technology can make micropayments more practical. Many apps rely on micropayments for in-game purchases.

english_meaning: Love or strong attraction to small things. A condition or tendency where someone has an unusual fondness, fascination, or admiration for very small objects, creatures, or details. It can also refer to an interest in miniature forms or tiny structures.
synonyms: ["Miniature obsession","Smallness fascination","Little things affection","Tiny objects attraction"]
example_sentence: Her microphilia made her collection of tiny antique buttons extraordinary. The artist’s microphilia is evident in his attention to miniature details in paintings. He developed a microphilia for insects after studying entomology. Microphilia can sometimes influence hobbies like collecting miniature models or tiny figurines.

english_meaning: Fear or strong dislike of small things or microorganisms. An intense fear, aversion, or anxiety about small objects, tiny creatures, or microorganisms, often leading to avoidance or distress when encountering them.
antonyms: ["Comfort with small things","Fascination with microorganisms","Curiosity about tiny objects"]
example_sentence: His microphobia made him avoid using microscopes. She has a microphobia of tiny insects crawling on her skin. Microphobia can make people excessively cautious about germs. His microphobia prevented him from handling soil or sand.

english_meaning: A device that converts sound waves into electrical signals, allowing voices or music to be amplified, recorded, or transmitted.
example_sentence: The speaker held the microphone closer so everyone could hear. Please test the microphone before the podcast begins. The microphone picked up every whisper in the silent room. Wireless microphones give performers freedom to move on stage.

english_meaning: Extremely small pieces of plastic debris, usually less than five millimetres in length, resulting from the breakdown of larger plastic items or manufactured as tiny particles.
example_sentence: Scientists found microplastic in samples taken from deep ocean trenches. Washing synthetic clothes releases microplastic into waterways. Microplastic pollution threatens marine life around the globe. Filters can help reduce microplastic in drinking water.

english_meaning: An integrated circuit that contains all the functions of a central processing unit of a computer. It performs arithmetic, logic, and control operations, serving as the brain of digital devices.
example_sentence: The microprocessor inside this laptop handles billions of instructions per second. Newer microprocessors consume less power while delivering higher speed. The inventor of the first commercial microprocessor changed computing history. A faster microprocessor improves gaming and video editing performance.

english_meaning: An optical instrument used to view objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye. It uses lenses to magnify tiny structures such as cells, bacteria, and crystals.
example_sentence: The biologist examined the tissue sample under a microscope. A microscope revealed bacteria swimming in the drop of water. Students learned to focus the microscope before drawing their observations. Electron microscopes can image structures at the atomic scale.

english_meaning: Too small to be seen without a microscope. Relating to or involving the use of a microscope. Extremely small or detailed.
example_sentence: Microscopic organisms live in every drop of pond water. The forensic team found microscopic traces of paint at the scene. A microscopic examination confirmed the presence of cancer cells. The differences between the two samples were microscopic.

english_meaning: In a manner that requires or involves a microscope. To an extremely small degree; so as to be visible only under magnification.
example_sentence: The samples were examined microscopically for signs of contamination. The two alloys differed microscopically but looked identical to the eye. Microscopically, the crystal structure appeared perfectly ordered. The wound was inspected microscopically after staining.

english_meaning: The scientific field or practice of using microscopes to observe objects and areas that cannot be seen with the unaided eye.
example_sentence: Fluorescence microscopy helps scientists track proteins inside living cells. He specializes in microscopy techniques for materials science. Advances in microscopy have transformed medicine and biology. The course covers both light microscopy and electron microscopy.

english_meaning: A unit of time equal to one millionth of a second. Used in science, computing, and telecommunications to measure extremely fast events.
synonyms: ["Millionth of a second","tiny fraction of time","instant","nanosecond-scale"]
example_sentence: The sensor responds in less than a microsecond. High-speed cameras capture images at intervals of a few microseconds. A microsecond delay can be critical in financial trading networks. Light travels about 300 metres in a microsecond.

english_meaning: A small, specialized website or a single web page that functions as a separate entity from a larger website. Often created for a specific campaign, product, or event.
example_sentence: The company launched a microsite to promote its new smartphone. Visitors to the microsite could register for the webinar instantly. The microsite focused entirely on customer testimonials. Each seasonal sale had its own colourful microsite.

english_meaning: A surgical technique that uses a microscope and specialized instruments to perform operations on very small or delicate structures, such as nerves and blood vessels.
example_sentence: Microsurgery restored feeling to her injured hand. The surgeon trained for years in microsurgery techniques. Microsurgery allows reattachment of tiny blood vessels during transplantation. Precision instruments are essential for successful microsurgery.

english_meaning: The middle point or part of something. Occurring at or near the middle of a period or process. Being the middle one of three or more. A prefix meaning middle or intermediate.
example_sentence: We met in mid-afternoon. The ship sank in mid-ocean. He stopped mid-sentence to think. The project is in mid-stage of completion.

english_meaning: The ability to make everything one does turn into a success or profit. Referring to the Greek myth of King Midas, who could turn everything he touched into gold.
example_sentence: She has the Midas touch, every business she starts becomes profitable. His Midas touch turned the failing company into a market leader. Investors love working with him because of his Midas touch. The Midas touch of this director makes every film a blockbuster.

english_meaning: The uppermost part of the brainstem, situated between the pons and the cerebrum. The small region of the brain that controls eye movement and the size of the pupil. A centre that relays visual and hearing signals and helps regulate body movement, alertness, and temperature.
example_sentence: The midbrain controls reflex movements of the eyes. Dopamine-producing cells are found in the midbrain. The midbrain lies just above the pons. Damage to the midbrain can affect alertness and vision.

english_meaning: The small air-filled chamber lying between the eardrum and the inner ear. The part of the ear containing the three tiny bones known as the hammer, anvil, and stirrup. The section that amplifies sound vibrations and passes them to the inner ear, and which is connected to the throat by the Eustachian tube.
example_sentence: The middle ear contains the three smallest bones in the body. Fluid in the middle ear can cause temporary deafness. The middle ear is connected to the throat by the Eustachian tube. Children often suffer from infections of the middle ear.

english_meaning: The longest finger of the hand, located between the index finger and the ring finger. The third digit of the hand counting from the thumb. A gesture made by raising this finger, considered rude or offensive in many cultures. The central finger used for measuring or comparing hand length.
example_sentence: The middle finger is usually the longest finger on the hand. He cut his middle finger while slicing vegetables. She wore a plain silver band on her middle finger. Raising the middle finger is considered offensive in many countries.

english_meaning: A very dark shade of blue, close to the colour of the night sky. Describing something of this deep, dark bluish colour. A colour often used for formal clothing as an alternative to black.
example_sentence: He wore a midnight blue suit to the dinner. The sea looked midnight blue under the stars. She chose midnight blue paint for the study. Their new car is midnight blue with silver trim.

english_meaning: The middle part of the human torso, between the chest and the waist. The area of the body around the stomach and lower ribs. A part of a garment that covers or exposes this region.
example_sentence: She wore a crop top that left her midriff exposed during the summer festival. The boxer took a strong punch directly to the midriff during the third round. The doctor examined his midriff carefully to check for any signs of internal injury. The dress was designed with a fitted midriff to accentuate her waist. He felt a sharp pain in his midriff after the long and exhausting run.

english_meaning: The middle point or part of something; the central part of a group, place, or period of time. Often used in the phrase 'in the midst of' meaning surrounded by or in the middle of.
example_sentence: She found herself in the midst of a heated argument. He stood in the midst of the crowd, searching for his friend. In the midst of the crisis, they remained calm. The bird nest was hidden in the midst of the dense forest.

english_meaning: The part of a city that is between the central business area and the outer parts. The middle part of a city or town between uptown and downtown. The part of a city near the centre.
synonyms: ["Central district","City center area","Urban center","Downtown area (in some contexts)","Central zone"]
example_sentence: We rented an apartment in midtown because it is close to our office. Many tourists visit midtown to enjoy shopping and dining. The conference will be held at a hotel in midtown. Traffic in midtown is usually heavy during business hours.

english_meaning: A person's appearance, manner, or bearing, especially as an indication of character or mood. The look or expression of someone's face. A dignified or characteristic way of carrying oneself.
example_sentence: He entered the hall with the mien of a confident leader. Her sad mien told us the news was not good. The old professor had a scholarly mien that impressed everyone. Despite the tension, he maintained a calm mien.

english_meaning: Great strength or power, especially physical, military, or political. Used to express possibility, permission, or a suggestion. Past tense form of may, used to indicate a hypothetical or less certain possibility.
example_sentence: The army demonstrated its full military might during the annual parade through the capital. She might join us for dinner later if she finishes work on time. With all his might, he pushed against the heavy door until it finally gave way. The company's economic might allowed it to dominate the market for several decades. He might have forgotten about the meeting entirely, given how busy his schedule has been.

english_meaning: Possessing great power, strength, or force. Impressively large or great in degree. Used informally as an intensifier meaning very or extremely.
example_sentence: The mighty river carved its path through the canyon over millions of years. She felt mighty proud when her daughter graduated at the top of her class. The mighty oak tree had stood in the centre of the village for over three hundred years. The mighty army marched confidently toward the capital, certain of an easy victory. It was a mighty fine meal, and everyone at the table praised the chef's effort.

english_meaning: Severe headache. A recurring, intense headache often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light or sound.
example_sentence: She stayed home because of a migraine. Migraines can be triggered by stress or certain foods. He suffers from chronic migraines. Taking rest in a dark room helps during a migraine.

english_meaning: A person who moves from one place to another, often for work or better living conditions. Relating to people or animals that move from one place to another.
example_sentence: The migrant moved to the city to find better job opportunities. Many migrants send money back to support their families. The government introduced new policies to protect migrant workers. Migrant workers often face difficult living conditions. The region depends heavily on migrant labor.

english_meaning: To move from one place to another, often temporarily or seasonally. To leave one country, region, or place and settle in another, sometimes for work, climate, food, or breeding. Can also refer to animals moving seasonally.
example_sentence: Many birds migrate south during winter. Farmers migrate to cities for better job opportunities. The company decided to migrate its data to a new server. Millions of people migrate every year due to climate changes.

english_meaning: The movement of people, animals, or things from one place to another, often for living, work, safety, or seasonal reasons.
example_sentence: Rural to urban migration has increased due to job opportunities. Seasonal migration of birds happens every winter. Climate change is forcing migration in coastal communities. Many families experienced migration after the flood.

english_meaning: Moving from one place to another, often seasonally. Describes people, animals, or groups that regularly move from one place to another, usually because of seasons, climate, food, or living conditions.
example_sentence: Many birds are migratory and travel thousands of miles every year. The region provides shelter for migratory animals during winter. Migratory workers move to cities in search of seasonal jobs. Climate change is affecting migratory patterns of wildlife.

english_meaning: A title given in the past to the emperor of Japan.
example_sentence: The power of Mikado in Japan is symbolic. The government spokesman confirmed that the Mikado would visit China next fall.

english_meaning: Gentle, not strong, moderate in effect or intensity Describes something that is not extreme, harsh, or severe. It can refer to weather, personality, flavor, illness, or behavior. A mild person is gentle and calm. A mild climate is moderate without extreme temperatures.
example_sentence: The soup is mild and easy to digest. He has a mild temperament and rarely loses his patience. The winter here is mild compared to the north. The medicine caused only mild side effects.

english_meaning: The quality of being gentle in nature or behavior. A state of being not harsh or severe in weather or climate. The characteristic of being moderate in flavor or intensity, especially in food or substances. The lack of intensity in a feeling or emotion. A merciful or lenient disposition towards others.
example_sentence: The mildness of the autumn air made the walk very pleasant. His mildness in the face of provocation surprised his coworkers. The doctor noted the mildness of the symptoms, suggesting a quick recovery. We preferred this brand of salsa because of its mildness and lack of spice.

english_meaning: An imperial unit of distance equal to 1,760 yards or about 1·609 kilometres. A unit used to measure long distances, especially on roads. Informally, a very great distance or amount.
example_sentence: The nearest town is five miles away. One mile is about 1.609 kilometers. She walks two miles every evening. His answer was miles away from the truth.

english_meaning: Plural of mile, a unit of distance equal to 1,760 yards or approximately 1.609 kilometres. A great distance or extent, used figuratively to emphasise a significant gap or difference. A Roman or English personal name.
example_sentence: They walked nearly ten miles before finally reaching the small mountain village. Her opinion on the matter was miles apart from her colleague's perspective. The new smartphone is miles better than the previous model in terms of camera quality. The runners covered over twenty miles during the gruelling endurance race. The two cities are separated by several hundred miles of open desert.

english_meaning: A stone set up beside a road to mark the distance in miles to a particular place. An important event or stage in the development of something. A significant achievement or turning point in a person's life or career. A major point of progress used to measure success. A notable moment marking the change from one phase to another.
example_sentence: Winning the national championship was a major milestone in her career. The launch of the first satellite was a milestone in space exploration. Their fiftieth wedding anniversary is a wonderful milestone to celebrate. The signing of the peace treaty marked an important milestone in the region's history. Every birthday after eighty feels like a special milestone.

english_meaning: A person's social environment or surroundings, especially those that shape character or behaviour. The physical or social setting in which something occurs or develops. The cultural or intellectual context of a particular group or era.
example_sentence: He grew up in a working-class milieu that shaped his strong views on social justice. The artist drew heavily on the bohemian milieu of early twentieth-century Paris for inspiration. Within the academic milieu, her research was widely respected and frequently cited. The novel vividly captures the social milieu of a small fishing village in the 1950s. She struggled to adjust to the corporate milieu after years of working in a more relaxed environment.

english_meaning: Relating to a thousand-year period or millennium. Relating to the belief, especially in some religious traditions, that a future thousand-year age of peace, justice, or divine rule will begin. Expecting a sudden, complete transformation of society and the arrival of an ideal age. A person who holds such beliefs.
example_sentence: Millenarian movements often arise during periods of social crisis. He joined a millenarian sect that expected a coming golden age. The group’s millenarian beliefs shaped its view of history. Historians studied the millenarian who founded the community.

english_meaning: The belief by a religious, social, or political group or movement in a coming major transformation of society, after which all things will be changed. It specifically refers to the Christian doctrine of a future thousand-year age of peace and blessedness, associated with the Second Coming of Christ. A broader expectation of a sudden, utopian era or global spiritual renewal.
example_sentence: The cult's millenarianism led them to prepare for an imminent apocalyptic transformation of the world. Many indigenous movements embraced millenarianism as a hope for a better future free from colonial rule. Historical studies demonstrate that times of great social stress often give rise to millenarianism. Traditional Christian millenarianism anticipates a thousand-year period of peace before the final judgment.

english_meaning: A person born roughly between 1981 and 1996. The generation that reached adulthood around the start of the 21st century. This group grew up with rapid technological change, the internet, and social media, and is often associated with new work styles, digital communication, and social awareness.
synonyms: ["Generation Y","Digital generation","Young adults of the 21st century"]
example_sentence: She is a millennial who prefers online learning over traditional classrooms. Millennials often value work life balance. The company redesigned its products to appeal to millennial consumers. As a millennial, he grew up using smartphones and social media.

english_meaning: A period of one thousand years. A span of one thousand years often used for historical timelines. It can also refer to a future age of peace, prosperity, or an ideal era. A symbolic thousand year reign of peace mentioned in religious texts. A long period marked by major cultural or social shifts. An imagined future era of perfect happiness.
example_sentence: Humanity has entered a new millennium with rapid technological changes. The ruins date back almost a millennium. Many cultures believe a golden millennium of peace will come in the future. The year 2000 marked the start of a new millennium for many people.

english_meaning: A person who owns, manages, or works in a mill. A person who grinds grain into flour. A milling machine or tool in some technical contexts. A common occupational surname originally given to someone who worked at a mill.
example_sentence: The miller ground the farmers’ wheat into flour. A skilled miller checked the stones before starting the mill. The village miller sold fresh flour every morning. Miller is a common surname in many English-speaking countries.

english_meaning: A group of small-seeded grasses cultivated as cereal crops, especially in Africa and Asia. A staple food grain used for human consumption and animal feed. A drought-resistant crop valued for its nutritional content.
example_sentence: Millet has been cultivated for thousands of years and remains a staple food in many parts of Africa and Asia. Farmers in the region prefer to grow millet because it requires far less water than rice or wheat. The porridge was made from finely ground millet flour and served with warm milk. Millet is increasingly being recognised in Western countries for its nutritional benefits and gluten-free properties. Birds in the garden were attracted to the feeder filled with millet seeds.

english_meaning: A unit prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one-thousandth. Used to signify division by one thousand (10-3) in measurements. Represents the smallest common decimal subdivision for units like meters or grams. Functions as a quantitative descriptor in scientific and technical contexts. Indicates a scale that is one-tenth of a centi- and ten times a micro-. Serves as a standard prefix in the International System of Units (SI).
example_sentence: One millimetre is exactly one-thousandth of a standard meter. The doctor prescribed a five milliliter dose of the liquid medicine. A milligram is a very small unit of mass often used for chemical measurements. The precision instrument could detect changes at the milli scale.

english_meaning: One thousand million (1,000,000,000), equal to 1 billion in modern British and American English. A milliard is the number 1,000,000,000 (10⁹). It was traditionally used in many European countries and in older British English to avoid confusion between the short scale and long scale numbering systems. Today, billion is much more commonly used in English.
example_sentence: The company earned one milliard dollars in revenue last year. The city's population is expected to reach one milliard within a few decades. Scientists estimate that the galaxy contains over a milliard stars. The government invested a milliard pounds in infrastructure projects.

english_meaning: A metric unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a gram. A very small unit commonly used for measuring medicine and chemicals. A unit written in short as mg.
example_sentence: Each tablet contains five hundred milligrams of paracetamol. One gram equals one thousand milligrams. The doctor reduced the dose by fifty milligrams. Vitamins are usually measured in milligrams.

english_meaning: A metric unit of volume equal to one thousandth of a liter. A very small measure of liquid capacity, written as ml or mL. The volume occupied by one cubic centimeter of a substance. A standard unit used in medicine, cooking, and laboratories to measure small amounts of liquid.
example_sentence: The nurse injected two milliliters of the vaccine into his arm. Add fifty milliliters of milk to the batter and stir well. This small bottle holds only thirty milliliters of perfume. The recipe calls for five milliliters of vanilla essence.

english_meaning: A metric unit of length equal to one thousandth of a metre. A very small unit used for precise measurements. A unit equal to one tenth of a centimetre. A unit written in short as mm.
example_sentence: The screw is only three millimeters long. Ten millimeters make one centimeter. Rainfall was recorded at twelve millimeters last night. Please cut the paper two millimeters shorter.

english_meaning: The number equivalent to one thousand thousand. A very large but unspecified number. A unit used in currency and measurement. Representing something extremely numerous. A general expression for a huge quantity.
example_sentence: The city has a population of over two million. He earned a million dollars last year. There are a million reasons to be grateful. Millions of people watched the match.

english_meaning: A small crawling arthropod with a long segmented body and two pairs of legs on most segments. A slow-moving soil creature that feeds on decaying plant material and curls up when disturbed.
example_sentence: A millipede curled up when I touched it gently. Millipedes are often found under damp stones. The millipede moved slowly across the wet soil. Unlike a centipede, a millipede does not bite.

english_meaning: A unit of time equal to one thousandth of a second. A very short moment of time. A measure used for timing fast events in computing, sports, and science. An extremely brief instant, used to suggest great speed.
example_sentence: The server responded in just two hundred milliseconds. A camera flash lasts only a few milliseconds. He won the race by fifteen milliseconds. The system records every click to the nearest millisecond.

english_meaning: A shy, nervous person with a weak character, usually a man. Shy, nervous and with a weak character. A timid, meek, or unassertive person.
example_sentence: He changes from a dorky milquetoast to a sexy macho hero. During boxing's bare-knuckle era, gloves were for milquetoasts. Those who thought otherwise were derided as milquetoasts. I wasn't going to be a milquetoast and let him steamroller me. She was no milquetoast girl. She loved a good confrontation.

english_meaning: The imitation or representation of reality, particularly in art, literature, or drama. A concept in philosophy and literary theory referring to the depiction of real life through artistic means. The act of mimicking or replicating behaviour, sound, or appearance.
example_sentence: Aristotle's theory of mimesis explored how drama imitates and reflects human action and emotion. The novel employs mimesis to recreate the social conditions of a war-torn city with striking realism. Critics have debated the role of mimesis in shaping the audience's emotional response to tragedy. The painter's use of mimesis allowed viewers to feel as though they were standing in the actual landscape. Mimesis remains a central concept in literary criticism and the philosophy of art.

english_meaning: To copy someone’s actions, voice, or behavior. To resemble closely. A person who imitates others. Parody, simulate, echo, mirror, impersonate. Someone who copies without originality.
example_sentence: The bird can mimic human speech. He can mimic his teacher perfectly. She tried to mimic her friend's handwriting. The comedian can mimic many famous actors. He is a good mimic of famous leaders. The mimic entertained the audience. The parrot is a clever mimic.

english_meaning: The act of copying or imitating someone or something. Imitation of sounds, behavior, appearance, or characteristics of another person, animal, or thing. It can be used for humor, learning, protection in nature, or acting.
example_sentence: The comedian performed mimicry of famous actors. Children often learn language through mimicry. The parrot is known for its mimicry of human speech. In nature, mimicry helps insects avoid predators.

english_meaning: Expressing or conveying a threat. Menacing or threatening in tone, appearance, or manner. Intended to intimidate or warn of danger.
example_sentence: The general delivered a minatory speech, warning the enemy of severe consequences if they advanced further. A minatory letter was sent to the company demanding immediate compliance with the new regulations. His minatory glance was enough to silence the entire room. The dark clouds gathering on the horizon had a minatory quality that suggested a storm was approaching. The minatory tone of the email left no doubt about the seriousness of the situation.

english_meaning: To cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces. It can also mean to speak or act in an affected, overly careful, or delicate way. To chop food into very small pieces. To speak carefully or indirectly. Meat that has been cut or ground into very small pieces.
example_sentence: She minced the garlic and onions finely for the sauce. He minced across the room in his new shoes. The politician did not mince his words in the press conference. The chef minced the lamb to prepare the keema.

english_meaning: Past tense of mince. Cut or chopped into very small pieces, especially meat. Spoke or moved in an affectedly delicate or polite manner. Softened or modified speech to avoid offence.
example_sentence: The chef minced the garlic finely before adding it to the simmering sauce. She minced no words when expressing her disappointment with the team's performance. He minced across the room in tiny, careful steps, trying not to make a sound. The recipe called for minced beef, finely chopped onions, and a blend of fresh herbs. He minced his criticism slightly so as not to upset the young performer.

english_meaning: The established set of attitudes held by someone. A fixed mental disposition or frame of mind that determines how one responds to and interprets situations. A habitual or characteristic mental attitude that determines how one will interpret and respond to events.
example_sentence: She entered the new job with a positive mindset and a determination to learn quickly. Changing your mindset about failure can be the key to long-term success. The coach worked to develop a winning mindset in each player before the tournament began. His entrepreneurial mindset allowed him to spot opportunities where others saw only obstacles. A growth mindset encourages people to see challenges as chances to improve and develop.

english_meaning: To mix or come together with other things or people. To socialise or move around among a group of people at an event. To blend or combine, especially different elements or qualities.
example_sentence: Guests were encouraged to mingle freely during the cocktail hour before dinner was served. The scent of fresh flowers mingled pleasantly with the aroma of freshly baked bread. She found it difficult to mingle with strangers at large social gatherings. The two cultures began to mingle over centuries of trade and migration along the route. Laughter and conversation mingled together to create a warm and lively atmosphere at the reunion.

english_meaning: A very small version or model of something. Extremely small in size compared to the usual or original. A small-scale painting, especially a portrait. Relating to or denoting something on a reduced scale.
example_sentence: She collected miniature porcelain figurines from countries she had visited around the world. The museum displayed an exquisite miniature painting from the Mughal era. He built a miniature replica of his childhood home using cardboard and paint. The toy company released a miniature version of its bestselling model car for collectors. Despite its miniature size, the device was capable of processing an enormous amount of data.

english_meaning: Something extremely small or insignificant. An old unit used to measure very small quantities of liquid, especially in medicine. In the British system, a minim is approximately 0.059 millilitres. In British musical terminology, a minim is a note equal to two beats in common time. In American English, it is called a half note.
example_sentence: Only a minim of doubt remained. The music lesson introduced the minim. Older prescriptions sometimes used the minim as a measure. Add just a minim of oil to the mixture.

english_meaning: Very small in amount, degree, or importance. The least possible or necessary. Simple and stripped down. Barely adequate.
example_sentence: The plan requires minimal effort. The room had a minimal design. Damage from the storm was minimal. He gave only minimal details.

english_meaning: A style or approach that uses very few elements. Simplicity in art, design, music, or lifestyle. The practice of reducing things to essentials.
example_sentence: Minimalism made the apartment feel calm. The artist is known for minimalism. She adopted minimalism to reduce clutter. Minimalism in music can create powerful repetition.

english_meaning: Someone or something that emphasizes simplicity, clarity, and restraint. In lifestyle, it means living with only what is essential. Preferring simplicity and avoiding anything unnecessary. In art, music, and literature, it refers to a movement that uses very limited elements, repetition, and simple forms to create impact.
example_sentence: She lives a minimalist lifestyle, owning only the essentials. The office design is minimalist with white walls and simple furniture. His approach to writing is minimalist, using short and clear sentences. The artist is known for minimalist paintings with few colors and simple shapes.

english_meaning: To a very small degree. Only slightly. With the least possible amount or effect. In a minimal way.
example_sentence: The patient was minimally injured. The design was minimally decorated. The rule affects us only minimally. She answered minimally and avoided details.

english_meaning: A small convenience store. A little shop selling basic food, drinks, and household items. A neighborhood store for quick purchases.
example_sentence: We bought milk from the minimart. A new minimart opened near the bus stop. The minimart stays open late. She stopped at the minimart for snacks.

english_meaning: The process of reducing something to the smallest possible amount, degree, or size. The act of representing something as less important than it actually is. The reduction of waste or unwanted elements in a system or process. In computing and mathematics, finding the smallest value of a function within a given range. The strategic effort to limit risk or exposure to negative outcomes.
example_sentence: The project focused on the minimization of production costs. Her minimization of the problem made everyone think it wasn't serious. Data minimization is a key principle in modern privacy laws. Mathematical models are used for the minimization of errors in the calculations.

english_meaning: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or degree. To represent something as less important than it really is. To make an on-screen window as small as possible. To lessen the impact, risk, or seriousness of something. To play down or underestimate.
example_sentence: The company introduced new rules to minimize workplace accidents. He tried to minimize his mistake in front of the manager. Please minimize the browser window while presenting. Wearing a helmet minimizes the risk of head injury.

english_meaning: The smallest amount, number, or degree possible or allowed. The lowest limit. The least requirement.
example_sentence: The minimum age is eighteen. We need a minimum of three volunteers. Keep noise to a minimum. The temperature fell to its minimum at dawn.

english_meaning: A small freshwater fish often used as bait or kept in aquariums. A person, team, or organisation considered small, weak, or insignificant compared to others, especially in sport or business. A tiny or unimportant entity in comparison to larger competitors.
example_sentence: The children spent the afternoon trying to catch minnows in the shallow stream behind their house. The small national team was considered a minnow compared to the powerful nations they faced in the tournament. Despite being a minnow in the industry, the start-up managed to outperform several established competitors. Anglers often use live minnows as bait to attract larger predatory fish. The local club was seen as a minnow in the competition but surprised everyone by reaching the final.

english_meaning: Small, less important, or not very serious in comparison with others. Lesser in size, rank, degree, or significance. A person who is under the legal age of adulthood. A secondary subject studied by a student alongside the main one. In music, a scale or key with a sad or softer sound.
example_sentence: He suffered only minor injuries in the accident. These are minor details that we can settle later. The law does not allow a minor to sign such a contract. She played the piece in a minor key.

english_meaning: To study a subject as a secondary part of a university degree. To take a smaller course of study alongside one's main subject. To specialise to a limited extent in an additional field. To choose an extra academic subject that supports the main one.
synonyms: ["Take as a secondary subject","Study additionally","Supplement with","Study on the side"]
example_sentence: She majored in English and minored in psychology. He plans to minor in mathematics next year. Students may minor in a language of their choice. Minoring in statistics helped her research a great deal.

english_meaning: The smaller number or part of a group of people or things. A group of people who differ from the larger population in race, religion, language, or culture. The state of being under the legal age of adulthood. Having fewer votes, seats, or supporters than the opposing side.
example_sentence: Only a small minority opposed the new rule. The government promised to protect the rights of minorities. The party was left in a minority after the election. A minority of readers preferred the older edition.

english_meaning: An aromatic herb with heavily veined leaves, commonly used as a flavouring in cooking and beverages. A place where money is coined, especially under state authority. A vast sum of money. To produce or coin money. In perfect or pristine condition.
example_sentence: We garnished the dessert with a fresh sprig of mint. The government built a new mint to produce the country's currency. She makes a mint from her successful online business. The vintage comic book was still in mint condition.

english_meaning: Very small. Something that is extremely small in size amount or importance. It can also refer to lowercase letters in writing.
example_sentence: There was only a minuscule chance of success. The insect was so minuscule that I could barely see it. He noticed a minuscule crack in the glass. The difference in price was minuscule.

english_meaning: A unit of time equal to sixty seconds. Extremely small in size, amount, or degree. Marked by close attention to small details. A short period of time, often used informally.
example_sentence: Please wait just a minute while I finish writing this important email. The scientist examined the sample under the microscope, noting even the most minute details. A minute crack in the foundation eventually caused significant structural damage to the building. He arrived just one minute before the meeting was due to start. The committee conducted a minute review of every clause in the proposed contract.

english_meaning: An extraordinary event that cannot be explained by natural laws and is often seen as the act of God or a divine power. An amazing and unexpected event that appears impossible according to normal scientific understanding. People often believe it happens through divine intervention or special blessing. It can also refer to something extremely surprising, wonderful, or fortunate.
example_sentence: The child’s recovery from the illness was considered a miracle by the doctors. Many people believe the event was a miracle sent by God. Surviving the accident without injuries felt like a miracle. Finishing the project in one day was nothing short of a miracle.

english_meaning: Of the nature of a miracle; remarkable or extraordinary beyond normal explanation. Astonishingly beneficial or fortunate. Caused by or attributed to a supernatural power.
example_sentence: The doctors described her recovery from the accident as nothing short of miraculous. It seemed almost miraculous that the small business had survived such a difficult economic period. The rescue team achieved a miraculous outcome by finding the missing climbers alive after five days. Many pilgrims travel to the shrine in the hope of witnessing a miraculous healing. Their last-minute victory in the final was viewed by fans as truly miraculous.

english_meaning: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of water in a desert. Something that appears real or possible but is actually illusory or unattainable. A deceptive impression created by certain visual conditions.
example_sentence: Exhausted travellers in the desert sometimes mistake a mirage for a distant oasis. The promise of quick wealth turned out to be nothing more than a mirage. Hot air rising from the asphalt created a shimmering mirage on the long stretch of highway. Her dream of a perfect career soon revealed itself to be little more than a mirage. The mirage disappeared the moment they got closer, leaving only sand and empty sky.

english_meaning: To place or arrange something incorrectly so that it is not in a straight line or proper position. To set parts so they do not fit or work together correctly. To position things out of their intended relationship or agreement. To be out of line with goals or expectations.
example_sentence: If you misalign the wheels, the car will pull to one side. Be careful not to misalign the text boxes on the page. A small error can misalign the entire machine. Poor planning can misalign a company's goals with its budget.

english_meaning: Not placed in a correct straight line or proper position. Positioned so that parts do not fit together correctly. Not in agreement or harmony with goals, values, or expectations. Crooked or out of position, as teeth or joints.
example_sentence: The picture frame on the wall looked slightly misaligned. Misaligned teeth can be corrected with braces. The printer produced misaligned pages. Their personal interests were misaligned with the company's mission.

english_meaning: The condition of being incorrectly positioned or not in a straight line. A lack of proper fit or arrangement between parts. A difference or lack of agreement between goals, interests, or expectations. A mechanical or medical fault where parts are out of place.
example_sentence: Wheel misalignment can cause uneven tyre wear. The doctor found a slight misalignment in her spine. A misalignment between management and staff led to confusion. The engineers corrected the misalignment of the beams.

english_meaning: An unsuitable or unhappy union, especially a marriage between people of very different backgrounds. A relationship or partnership between parties who are poorly matched. An unwise alliance between organizations, groups, or states. Any association that proves inappropriate or damaging to those involved.
example_sentence: Her family considered the marriage a misalliance from the very beginning. The merger turned out to be a costly misalliance between two rival firms. Historians describe the treaty as a misalliance that satisfied neither side. Their partnership was a misalliance of clashing values and goals.

english_meaning: A person who dislikes or is prejudiced against men. Someone who holds a strong bias against men or male behavior, often expressing distrust, dislike, or hostility toward men as a group.
example_sentence: She admitted she was a misandrist after her bad experiences with men. His misandrist views made it hard for him to form friendships with men. The film portrayed a misandrist character who avoided all male contact. Her misandrist remarks sparked a heated debate online.

english_meaning: A person who dislikes or distrusts other people. Someone who has a general dislike, suspicion, or contempt for humankind. They may avoid social interaction or show pessimism about human behavior.
example_sentence: The old man was a misanthrope who rarely spoke to his neighbors. Despite being a talented writer, he lived as a misanthrope, avoiding public events. Her experiences with betrayal made her a misanthrope. The character in the novel is a misanthrope who distrusts everyone he meets.

english_meaning: Disliking or distrusting people in general. Unfriendly and avoiding the company of others. Showing contempt for humankind.
example_sentence: The misanthropic old man rarely left his house. Years of betrayal had made him bitter and misanthropic. The novel's hero has a darkly misanthropic view of society. Despite her misanthropic jokes, she was kind to her friends.

english_meaning: A person who dislikes, distrusts, or hates humankind and prefers to avoid people. A person who avoids social interaction due to dislike of people. Someone who believes human beings are fundamentally flawed or corrupt. A person who prefers isolation over company because of negative views about society. A person who shows cynicism toward human behavior and social systems.
example_sentence: After years of betrayal, he became a misanthropist who avoided all social gatherings. The writer lived alone and was often called a misanthropist by his neighbors. Her misanthropist views made it difficult for her to work in large teams. The character in the novel is a misanthropist who believes society is beyond repair.

english_meaning: The dishonest use of money or property belonging to someone else. The act of taking funds entrusted to one's care for personal use. Wrongful application of resources to an unintended purpose. Embezzlement of public or private assets.
example_sentence: He was charged with the misappropriation of public funds. The audit revealed a clear misappropriation of donations. Misappropriation of company property led to his dismissal. The report documents years of misappropriation.

english_meaning: Poorly conceived, planned, or carried out. Illegitimate or born out of wedlock, in an old-fashioned or literary sense. Resulting from a mistaken or flawed idea. Disreputable or ill-conceived in origin.
example_sentence: The misbegotten plan to cut costs ended up causing far more damage than it ever saved. Critics described the film as a misbegotten attempt to modernise a beloved classic story. The misbegotten merger ultimately led to the collapse of both companies within two years. In the old novel, the misbegotten heir struggled for recognition throughout his entire life. The misbegotten policy was scrapped within months after widespread public backlash.

english_meaning: To experience the spontaneous loss of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive independently. To fail to achieve the intended result, especially of a plan or scheme. To go wrong or come to nothing.
example_sentence: Doctors reassured her that many women go on to have healthy pregnancies even after they miscarry once. The carefully laid plan to surprise her ultimately miscarried when the truth was accidentally revealed early. She was devastated to learn that she had miscarried during the early stages of her pregnancy. The negotiation miscarried after both sides refused to make any further concessions. The scheme miscarried badly, leaving the organisation in a far worse position than before.

english_meaning: Consisting of various kinds or qualities. Having many different aspects or characteristics. Dealing with diverse subjects or topics that are not easily categorized together. Characterized by a mixture of elements. Mixed and varied in composition.
example_sentence: The garage was filled with miscellaneous items like old tools, broken toys, and dusty books. We set aside a small fund for miscellaneous expenses during our vacation. The library contains a section for miscellaneous documents that do not fit into specific categories. Her research involves a miscellaneous collection of data from various unrelated fields.

english_meaning: A collection or group of various items or parts. A mixture of diverse things. A book containing a collection of literary pieces or compositions by different authors. A state of being varied or miscellaneous.
example_sentence: The drawer was filled with a miscellany of old keys, stamps, and loose coins. Her latest book is a delightful miscellany of poems, short stories, and personal essays. The museum curator organized a miscellany of artifacts from the Victorian era. We spent the afternoon browsing through a miscellany of antique furniture and vintage clothing.

english_meaning: An instance of bad luck. An unlucky accident or unfortunate occurrence. The quality of being unlucky or having poor fortune. An unexpected event that results in failure or harm.
example_sentence: By some unhappy mischance, the important documents were lost in the mail. It was a mere mischance that the two cars collided at the intersection. Despite his careful planning, a sudden mischance ruined the entire operation. She viewed her losing the race as a temporary mischance rather than a lack of skill.

english_meaning: Playful behaviour that causes small trouble or annoyance but no serious harm. Harm or damage caused by someone's actions. A tendency to tease or play tricks on others. A person, especially a child, who behaves in a naughty way. Deliberate trouble-making that damages relations between people.
example_sentence: The children were up to some mischief in the garden. There was a hint of mischief in her smile. Careless rumours can do real mischief to a friendship. Keep the puppy busy so it stays out of mischief.

english_meaning: The action or habit of causing trouble, especially by spreading rumors or creating discord between people. The act of provoking unnecessary strife or petty annoyance. Behaviour that causes problems for others through playful or malicious interference.
example_sentence: His constant mischief-making finally led to a serious rift between the two brothers. The office environment was poisoned by her persistent mischief-making and gossip. She was accused of mischief-making after telling lies about her neighbors' financial situation. The children’s mischief-making kept the babysitter busy all evening long.

english_meaning: A person who deliberately creates trouble or spreads rumours to cause conflict. Someone who stirs up quarrels between other people. A troublemaker who enjoys causing disorder or ill feeling.
example_sentence: A few mischief-mongers spread false stories about the new manager. The village elders warned the mischief-mongers to stay quiet. He was known as a mischief-monger who enjoyed other people's quarrels. Social media gives mischief-mongers an easy audience.

english_meaning: Playfully naughty or causing minor trouble. Showing playful misbehavior, often in a way that is slightly annoying but not harmful.
example_sentence: The mischievous child hid her brother’s shoes. He gave a mischievous smile. Dogs can be mischievous at times. She told a mischievous joke.

english_meaning: In a way that shows a playful desire to cause trouble or have fun at someone else's expense. In a manner that is slightly harmful or intended to annoy but is not meant to cause serious damage. Done with a sly or naughty expression or intent. In a teasing or joking way.
example_sentence: He winked mischievously at her before hiding the car keys. The puppy looked at the rug mischievously before starting to chew on it. She smiled mischievously as she prepared the surprise party prank. The children were whispering mischievously in the corner of the room.

english_meaning: Capable of being mixed together to form a uniform or homogeneous solution, especially of liquids. Able to combine or blend smoothly without separating. Compatible substances that dissolve into one another.
example_sentence: Water and ethanol are miscible liquids that combine completely to form a single, uniform solution. The chemist confirmed that the two solvents were miscible before proceeding with the experiment. Unlike oil, which separates from water, this compound is miscible in nearly all aqueous solutions. Understanding which substances are miscible helps pharmacists formulate effective and stable medications. The two paints were tested to ensure they were miscible before being combined for the project.

english_meaning: To fail to understand something correctly. To form a wrong or mistaken idea about a concept or situation. To misinterpret the meaning or intention of another. To have a false or inaccurate perception of something.
example_sentence: It is easy to misconceive the motives of someone you already dislike. Many students misconceive the complex laws of thermodynamics during their first year. Do not misconceive my silence for a lack of interest in your project. The public often tends to misconceive the role of the judiciary in a democracy.

english_meaning: Poorly planned or based on a misunderstanding. Wrongly thought out or poorly devised from the start. Formed incorrectly in the mind. Unwisely planned or executed due to a lack of understanding. Faulty in concept or design.
example_sentence: The project failed because the initial strategy was entirely misconceived. Critics argued that the new tax law was a misconceived attempt to fix the economy. Her plan to renovate the house without a budget was totally misconceived. The movie was a misconceived remake of a classic film that nobody wanted.

english_meaning: A view or opinion that is incorrect because it is based on faulty thinking or understanding. A mistaken belief or idea about something. An inaccurate interpretation of facts or information.
example_sentence: It is a common misconception that learning a second language as an adult is impossible. The article aimed to correct several widespread misconceptions about the causes of climate change. Her teacher addressed the misconception that all spiders are dangerous to humans. The misconception about the company's pricing led to a noticeable drop in customer trust. Public health campaigns are essential for clearing up dangerous misconceptions about vaccines.

english_meaning: Improper, unacceptable, or unprofessional behavior by a person in a position of authority or a professional person. The intentional violation of a rule, law, or standard of behavior. Management or administration that is dishonest or incompetent. Bad or unethical conduct in one's life or work.
example_sentence: The police officer was dismissed from the force for gross misconduct. Several board members were accused of financial misconduct during the audit. The student faced suspension following his repeated misconduct in the classroom. The lawyer was disbarred after evidence of professional misconduct came to light.

english_meaning: The act of misinterpreting or misunderstanding something. A false or mistaken interpretation of words, actions, or intentions. A construction or explanation that is incorrect or distorted. The state of being wrongly understood.
example_sentence: Her silence was a complete misconstruction of her true feelings of anger. The lawyer argued that the jury's verdict was based on a gross misconstruction of the evidence. To avoid any misconstruction of his motives, he explained his reasons clearly to the board. The diplomatic incident was fueled by a simple misconstruction of a local idiom.

english_meaning: To understand somebody’s words or actions wrongly. To form a false understanding of the meaning or intention of something that someone does or says.
example_sentence: He deliberately misconstrued everything I said. She said Harris had misconstrued her comments. Their caution was misconstrued as cowardice. You all will misconstrue things the way you see fit. His behaviour could easily be misconstrued.

english_meaning: A person who behaves badly or criminally. Someone who acts in a way that is morally wrong, villainous, or engages in criminal behavior. Can also describe actions that are wicked or unlawful.
example_sentence: The cable has been cut and stolen by some unknown miscreants. Local people demanded that the District Magistrate apprehend the miscreants. The police arrested the miscreant who vandalized the park. Only a miscreant would spread such false rumors. The king punished the miscreant for his betrayal. She had no tolerance for miscreant behavior at the school.

english_meaning: A person who is extremely unwilling to spend money and prefers to save or hoard it. A person who loves money so much that they avoid spending it, even when spending is necessary or reasonable. A miser may live very cheaply despite having enough wealth.
example_sentence: The miser refused to buy a new coat even though his old one was torn. Everyone knew he was a miser because he never spent money on himself. The old miser kept all his savings hidden in a box. Although she was wealthy, she lived like a miser and avoided unnecessary expenses.

english_meaning: Very unhappy or depressed. Causing discomfort, suffering, or unhappiness. Very poor in quality or condition. Extremely small, inadequate, or mean. Wretched or pitiable.
example_sentence: He felt miserable after hearing the bad news. The refugees lived in miserable conditions. We had a miserable journey through the storm. She offered him a miserable amount for the hard work.

english_meaning: In a very unhappy or uncomfortable way. In a manner that causes suffering or sadness. Very poorly or unsuccessfully. To a pitiful or disappointing degree. In a way that shows great distress.
example_sentence: He failed miserably in the final examination. She sat miserably in the corner after the argument. The plan ended miserably despite everyone's efforts. The children looked miserably at the broken toy.

english_meaning: Great suffering, extreme unhappiness, pain, hardship, or distress. A state of intense suffering, unhappiness, pain, hardship, or distress. It can be physical, emotional, financial, or social suffering that makes a person feel extremely unhappy.
example_sentence: After losing his job, he lived in misery for several months. The flood brought misery to thousands of families. She tried to hide her misery behind a smile. Poverty and disease caused great misery in the village.

english_meaning: Bad luck or an unfortunate event. A difficult or unhappy situation. An accident or disaster that causes suffering. A stroke of bad fate affecting someone's life. Any hardship, loss, or trouble faced by a person.
example_sentence: He faced one misfortune after another this year. Losing his job was a great misfortune for the family. She bore her misfortune with courage and patience. It was his misfortune to arrive late that day.

english_meaning: To cause doubt, fear, or apprehension in someone's mind. To feel uneasy or have reservations about something. To create a troubled or uncertain feeling, especially before an event or decision.
example_sentence: His heart misgave him as he approached the door, sensing that something was terribly wrong. She felt her conscience misgive her the moment she agreed to the dishonest proposal. As the deadline approached, his confidence began to misgive him about whether the plan would succeed. Her instincts misgave her about the unfamiliar route, so she decided to turn back. He could feel his resolve begin to misgive him as the difficulty of the task became clear.

english_meaning: A feeling of doubt, worry, or uncertainty about something that is going to happen. A slight fear that a decision or action may be wrong. An uneasy suspicion or lack of confidence in a plan or person.
example_sentence: She had serious misgivings about signing the contract. Despite his misgivings, he agreed to travel alone. Parents expressed misgivings over the new school policy. I accepted the offer with some misgiving.

english_meaning: A small accident or unfortunate event. An unexpected and unpleasant event, usually minor, that causes inconvenience, damage, or trouble. It is not always serious but is unwanted and accidental.
example_sentence: He had a minor mishap while driving to work. The event was successful despite a few mishaps. She laughed off the small mishap during her speech. A kitchen mishap caused a slight fire.

english_meaning: A confused mix of different things. A mixture made up of many different elements that are poorly organized or do not fit well together, often creating confusion or lack of clarity.
example_sentence: The report was a mishmash of ideas with no clear conclusion. His speech sounded like a mishmash of facts and opinions. The room decor was a mishmash of old and modern furniture. The plan turned into a mishmash after too many changes.

english_meaning: To type or enter something incorrectly on a keyboard or keypad. To press the wrong key while entering data. To make an error while keying in numbers, letters, or codes. An instance of typing something wrongly.
example_sentence: It is easy to miskey a long password in a hurry. The clerk miskeyed the amount and the total came out wrong. If you miskey the code, the system will ask you to try again. A single miskey can change the entire result of the calculation.
