She felt that the constant moralization of her lifestyle was intrusive. The book's moralization of poverty was criticized for being overly simplistic.

english_meaning: To comment on issues of right and wrong, typically with an unfounded air of superiority. To interpret or explain something in a moral sense.
example_sentence: The preacher began to moralize about the youth's behavior in the city. She tends to moralize every situation instead of just listening to the problem. It is annoying when people moralize without understanding the context of the struggle. The fable was written specifically to moralize the value of hard work.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to principles of right and wrong. According to standards of good behaviour and honesty. From an ethical point of view rather than a legal one. In a virtuous and upright manner.
example_sentence: Morally, he had no choice but to tell the truth. The decision was legally correct but morally questionable. She always tried to behave morally in business dealings. We are morally bound to help those in need.

english_meaning: An area of soft, wet, muddy ground. A swamp, marsh, or bog that is difficult to cross. A complicated and confusing situation from which escape is difficult. A mass of problems, rules, facts, or emotions that causes entanglement. A state of moral, political, or financial disorder.
example_sentence: The hikers became trapped in a muddy morass. The case sank into a morass of conflicting regulations. Years of debt left the company in a financial morass. She struggled through a morass of fear and uncertainty.

english_meaning: A temporary official suspension of an activity. A legally authorized delay in performing an obligation or paying a debt. An agreed pause intended to allow review or negotiation. A fixed period during which a particular action is prohibited. A temporary halt in development, testing, punishment, or enforcement.
example_sentence: The city imposed a moratorium on new construction near the coast. Campaigners demanded a moratorium on the use of the chemical. The bank granted borrowers a six-month payment moratorium. Both sides agreed to a temporary moratorium on testing.

english_meaning: A long, snakelike marine eel of warm coastal waters. A predatory fish that often hides in rocks or coral reefs. Any eel belonging to the family Muraenidae. A fish with strong jaws and sharp teeth that opens its mouth to breathe. A reef-dwelling eel that usually hunts fish, crabs, and octopuses.
example_sentence: A moray watched us from a crack in the reef. The diver kept a safe distance from the large moray. Morays use their powerful jaws to seize prey. A spotted moray emerged from beneath the rocks.

english_meaning: Characterized by an unhealthy interest in death, disease, or disturbing subjects. Relating to disease or an abnormal medical condition. Gloomy, gruesome, or unpleasant. Suggesting an unhealthy mental state. Excessively preoccupied with frightening possibilities. Causing horror or disgust because of a connection with death or decay.
example_sentence: He has a morbid fascination with unsolved crimes. The doctor checked the tissue for morbid changes. Her thoughts became increasingly morbid during the long winter. The museum avoided displaying the most morbid photographs.

english_meaning: The state of having a disease or medical condition. The rate or frequency of illness in a population. The number of people affected by a particular disease. The harmful effects or complications caused by an illness or treatment. An unhealthy interest in unpleasant subjects. The quality of being gloomy, gruesome, or concerned with death.
example_sentence: The program reduced childhood morbidity in the region. Researchers measured morbidity among patients after surgery. Early treatment can prevent serious morbidity. Critics disliked the novel’s constant morbidity and gloom.

english_meaning: In an unhealthy manner connected with disease or abnormality. With an excessive interest in death or disturbing subjects. In a gloomy, gruesome, or macabre way. To an extreme degree that harms health or well-being. In a manner suggesting unhealthy anxiety or fascination.
example_sentence: He spoke morbidly about every possible disaster. She became morbidly curious about the abandoned hospital. The patient was classified as morbidly obese. The story dwells morbidly on death and decay.

english_meaning: Approximately or about a certain amount. Almost completely or nearly so. To a moderate or reasonable extent. Roughly, without being exact. Practically the same as.
example_sentence: The work is more or less finished. They arrived more or less at the same time. His answer was more or less correct. The two products are more or less the same.

english_meaning: More skills, qualifications, or options that make you more capable and adaptable. Several additional ways to succeed or earn a living.
example_sentence: The training will give you more strings to your bow. The manager encouraged staff to develop more strings to their bow. Languages and computer skills provide more strings to your bow. Freelancing gave her more strings to her bow.

english_meaning: It is used to introduce a piece of information that adds to or supports the previous statement. It serves as a formal way of saying 'besides' or 'in addition' to strengthen an argument. The word indicates that further, more important evidence is about to be presented. It transitions the discourse to an additional point that reinforces the main idea.
antonyms: ["However","Nevertheless","Conversely","On the contrary","Despite this","Yet","Alternatively","On the other hand"]
example_sentence: The rent for the apartment is reasonable; moreover, the location is perfect. She is an excellent student; moreover, she excels in various sports. The plan is highly innovative; moreover, it is completely feasible within our budget. He didn't have the required experience; moreover, his attitude during the interview was extremely arrogant.

english_meaning: A place where dead bodies are kept, especially for identification or before burial. A room or building, usually in a hospital or forensic department, where dead bodies are stored for examination, identification, or postmortem analysis before burial or cremation.
example_sentence: The police took the unidentified body to the morgue for examination. She works night shifts at the city morgue. After the accident, the victims were transferred to the hospital morgue. The journalist searched the newspaper morgue for old photographs.

english_meaning: A foolish or stupid person. A person of subnormal intelligence. A rude way to refer to somebody that you think is very stupid.
example_sentence: Don't leave it there, you moron!. Some moron smashed into the back of my car yesterday. They're a bunch of morons. The people responsible for this are mindless morons.

english_meaning: Sullen and ill-tempered. Gloomy, sad, and silent. Bad-tempered and unwilling to talk to other people. In a depressed and unhappy mood for a long time. Showing a persistent sense of gloominess or bitterness in behaviour.
example_sentence: He became morose after losing his job and rarely spoke to anyone. She sat in a morose silence throughout the entire dinner. The rainy weather made him feel morose and lonely. His morose expression worried his friends and family. After the argument, he remained morose for several days.

english_meaning: To change gradually from one form into another. To transform in appearance, shape, or character. A changed form or variant in biology or linguistics.
example_sentence: The cartoon face began to morph into an animal. The project morphed into a larger plan. Some insects morph during development. The software can morph one image into another.

english_meaning: The smallest meaningful unit in a language. A word part such as a root, prefix, or suffix that carries meaning.
example_sentence: The word unhappy has two morphemes. A morpheme may be a whole word or a word part. Students identified each morpheme in the sentence. The suffix ed is a past-tense morpheme.

english_meaning: A powerful pain-relieving drug made from opium or produced synthetically. A narcotic medicine used for severe pain. An opioid analgesic that can be addictive.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed morphine after surgery. Morphine must be used carefully. The patient received morphine for severe pain. Misuse of morphine can be dangerous.

english_meaning: A structure-preserving map between mathematical objects. A transformation or form in technical usage. A relation that connects objects while preserving operations or patterns.
example_sentence: The professor explained a morphism between two groups. A morphism preserves important structure. Category theory studies objects and morphisms. The diagram shows how each morphism connects the spaces.

english_meaning: Related to the structure and formation of words, including prefixes, suffixes, roots, and other word parts. Related to the physical form, shape, and structure of an organism or its parts. Related to the form or structural appearance of cells, tissues, or organs. Related to the shape, form, or structure of something.
example_sentence: The study found morphological differences between the plants. Children learn morphological patterns in words. The fossils show clear morphological features. Morphological analysis explains how the word is formed.

english_meaning: The branch of biology concerned with the form and structure of organisms. The study of the forms and structural features of words in linguistics. The systematic study of the structure, shape, and arrangement of parts in any subject.
example_sentence: The morphology of the butterfly's wing was studied in great detail by the research team. Students of linguistics are required to understand basic morphology before moving on to syntax. The morphology of the ancient fish skull revealed important clues about its evolutionary history. Plant morphology helps botanists classify and distinguish between thousands of different species. Advances in digital imaging have transformed the way scientists approach morphology in their research.

english_meaning: Related to word structure and sentence structure. Combining morphology and syntax. Concerning grammatical word forms and their sentence functions. Related to how word forms interact with grammar. Involving both morphology and syntax. Concerned with grammatical relationships expressed through word forms.
example_sentence: The language has complex morphosyntactic rules. Children acquire morphosyntactic patterns gradually. The researcher studied morphosyntactic agreement. This error is morphosyntactic, not purely semantic.

english_meaning: A Latin word meaning death, used in literary, philosophical, and historical contexts. A personification of death in Roman mythology. Used in academic or poetic writing to refer to death or the concept of mortality.
example_sentence: The inscription on the ancient tombstone bore only the word mors, carved deep into the stone. Medieval scholars often used the word mors alongside vita to represent the eternal struggle of life and death. The poet personified mors as a silent figure standing at the edge of every battlefield. The painting depicted mors as a cloaked figure waiting patiently at the end of a long road. In Roman mythology, mors was the counterpart of the Greek god Thanatos.

english_meaning: A small piece or bite of food. It can also mean a small amount of something, especially something pleasant or desirable. A very small portion of food that can be eaten in one bite. It is often used in a gentle or descriptive way, especially when talking about tasty food. In a broader sense, it can also mean a small piece of anything, such as information, pleasure, or experience.
example_sentence: She ate every last morsel on her plate. The dog waited patiently for a morsel of food. He enjoyed every morsel of the delicious cake. Not a single morsel was left after the feast.

english_meaning: Something that will die or cannot live forever. Anything living that is subject to death. Causing death or capable of causing death. A human, especially in contrast to a divine being. Very strong or extreme (mortal fear, mortal hatred). It can also describe something severe, extreme, or related to human weakness and limitations.
example_sentence: All humans are mortal, so life should be valued. The hero received a mortal wound during the battle. She felt a mortal fear when the earthquake started. The story reminds us that even kings are mortal.

english_meaning: The state of being mortal or subject to death. The number of deaths in a given population. Human weakness or vulnerability. A reminder that life is temporary. The fact that all living beings must eventually die. It can also mean the rate at which deaths occur in a particular population or period. The word is used in general life, philosophy, medicine, and population studies.
example_sentence: Doctors are studying the rise in mortality among young adults. The story reminds us of human mortality. Better healthcare has reduced child mortality in many countries. The flood caused a high mortality rate in the affected villages.

english_meaning: A bowl-shaped tool used for crushing or grinding substances. A type of explosive weapon that fires shells at a high angle. A mixture used in building to bind bricks or stones. To apply mortar in order to join, fix or secure bricks, stones or tiles. It refers to spreading or using the masonry mixture to bind construction materials. A square academic cap worn at graduation ceremonies.
example_sentence: She crushed the spices in a stone mortar. The soldiers fired a mortar during the night attack. The mason mixed sand and cement to make fresh mortar. They mortared the bricks to build a strong wall.

english_meaning: To use property as security for a loan. A loan taken to buy property, where the property itself is used as security until the loan is fully paid. A legal agreement in which a bank or financial institution lends money to a person to buy a house or land. The borrower agrees to repay the loan in installments. If they fail to repay, the lender has the right to take the property.
example_sentence: He took a mortgage to buy his first house. The bank approved her mortgage application last week. They are still paying off their mortgage after ten years. She mortgaged her property to start a business.

english_meaning: To cut a hole or cavity into a material so another piece can fit tightly into it.  A rectangular hole or slot cut into a piece of wood, metal, or other material. It is made to receive a projecting part called a tenon so that two pieces can be firmly joined together. This type of joint is common in carpentry, furniture making, and door frames.
example_sentence: He morticed the wood before assembling the frame. The craftsman morticed the beam to hold the support. She morticed each piece carefully to avoid cracks. The worker shaped the mortice with great care. The strength of the table comes from each mortice. A tight mortice ensures a firm connection.

english_meaning: To make someone feel extremely embarrassed, ashamed, or humiliated. To check or curb one’s natural inclinations. To cause someone to feel self-conscious or humbled. To suppress or put an end to something unpleasant.
example_sentence: She was mortified to discover her phone was on speaker during the meeting. The king mortified his soldiers with strict discipline. He mortified himself by admitting his failure publicly. The frost mortified the crops before the harvest.

english_meaning: To cut a hole or cavity into a material so another piece can fit tightly into it.  A rectangular hole or slot cut into a piece of wood, metal, or other material. It is made to receive a projecting part called a tenon so that two pieces can be firmly joined together. This type of joint is common in carpentry, furniture making, and door frames.
example_sentence: The carpenter carefully cut a mortise into the wooden beam. The table legs were secured using a mortise and tenon joint. He installed a mortise lock on the front door. The craftsman mortised the frame to fit the panel perfectly.

english_meaning: A room or building in which dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation. Relating to or connected with death and burial. A place where post-mortem examinations are carried out.
example_sentence: The body was transferred to the mortuary immediately after the accident for formal identification. A post-mortem examination was carried out at the hospital mortuary to determine the cause of death. The mortuary staff worked quietly and professionally to prepare the deceased for burial. Families were asked to attend the mortuary at a specific time to make formal identification. The cold temperature inside the mortuary helps preserve the bodies until burial arrangements are finalised.

english_meaning: A building used by Muslims for prayer and worship. A place of Islamic congregational worship, especially for the Friday prayer. A religious centre that often also serves as a place of learning, community gathering, and charity. A structure typically featuring a prayer hall, a mihrab, and often a minaret and dome.
example_sentence: The call to prayer echoed from the mosque at dawn. They built a small mosque at the edge of the village. Thousands of worshippers gathered at the grand mosque for Friday prayers. The mosque also runs a free school for local children.

english_meaning: A small flying insect whose female bites and sucks blood from humans and animals. A biting insect that transmits diseases such as malaria and dengue. A slender two-winged insect that breeds in still or stagnant water. A common household nuisance known for its irritating buzzing sound.
example_sentence: A mosquito bit me on the ankle while I was reading. Mosquitoes breed quickly in standing water after the rain. We use a net at night to keep mosquitoes away. The health department sprayed the area to reduce the mosquito population.

english_meaning: A night-flying insect related to the butterfly, usually dull in colour with feathery antennae. An insect whose larvae feed on cloth, wool, or stored grain and cause damage.
example_sentence: A moth kept circling around the lamp all night. Moths have damaged my woollen sweater. She saw a large grey moth on the window. Store the clothes properly to keep moths away.

english_meaning: To provide someone with a reason or incentive to act or behave in a certain way. To stimulate enthusiasm, drive, or interest in a person.
example_sentence: A good teacher knows how to motivate students to learn. She was motivated to succeed by her difficult childhood. His speech motivated thousands to take action. Nothing could motivate him to leave his comfortable routine.

english_meaning: Having a strong reason or desire to act or achieve something. Enthusiastic, determined, and willing to work toward a goal. Caused or influenced by a particular motive. Provided with encouragement or an incentive to act.
example_sentence: She is highly motivated to improve her English. The team remained motivated despite losing the first game. His decision was motivated by concern for his family. Clear goals kept the students motivated throughout the course.

english_meaning: The reason or reasons for acting in a particular way. The desire or willingness to do something. A driving force behind actions. Enthusiasm to achieve a goal. The process of inspiring people.
example_sentence: His motivation to succeed was inspiring. She lacks the motivation to study. Money is not his main motivation. The coach provides strong motivation.

english_meaning: Providing encouragement or a reason to act. Designed to increase enthusiasm, confidence, determination, or effort. Relating to the motives or forces that influence behavior. Inspiring a person to pursue goals or overcome difficulties.
example_sentence: The coach gave a motivational speech before the final match. She listens to motivational podcasts on her way to work. The workshop offered practical and motivational advice to young entrepreneurs. A motivational reward can encourage children to complete difficult tasks.

english_meaning: A person who encourages others to act, improve, or succeed. A factor, reason, reward, or need that stimulates action. A person skilled at creating enthusiasm and determination in a group.
example_sentence: Her teacher was the main motivator behind her academic success. Money is not the only motivator for good employees. A skilled motivator understands what inspires each member of the team. Fear can be a powerful but unhealthy motivator.

english_meaning: A reason for doing something, especially one that is hidden or not immediately obvious. A need, desire, or emotion that causes a person to act. In art and music, a recurring theme, figure, or design. Producing or causing physical motion or action.
example_sentence: The police are still trying to establish a motive for the crime. Kindness rather than profit was her main motive. A repeated musical motive links the different sections of the symphony. Engineers studied the motive force generated by the engine.

english_meaning: Having no clear motive, reason, or purpose. Apparently done without a rational cause or understandable intention. Lacking an incentive or desire to act.
example_sentence: The police struggled to explain the apparently motiveless attack. His sudden resignation seemed motiveless to his colleagues. The novel explores the fear created by motiveless violence. Truly motiveless behavior is difficult for psychologists to identify.

english_meaning: A short sentence or phrase chosen as encapsulating the beliefs or ideals of an individual, family, institution, or organisation. A guiding principle or rule of conduct expressed in a brief saying. An inscription or phrase appearing on a coat of arms, flag, or official seal.
example_sentence: The school's motto, carved above the entrance, read simply: knowledge, courage, and integrity. She had adopted a personal motto of never giving up, no matter how great the obstacle. The national motto of the country appeared on every coin and official government document. He lived by a simple motto that guided every decision he made throughout his long career. The military regiment's motto had been chosen centuries ago and remained unchanged to this day.

english_meaning: To shape or influence something’s form, character, or development. To serve as a model or standard for shaping behavior or ideas. A container or form used to give shape to objects such as clay, metal, or plastic. Can also refer to a growth of fungus, often fuzzy, on food or damp surfaces.
example_sentence: The baker poured the dough into a mould. She used a mould to create a clay statue. The walls were covered with mould after the rain. Early experiences mould a person’s character. He is not cut out for this mould of work.

english_meaning: A rounded mass of earth, stones, or other material, either natural or man-made. A raised area of ground or a heap of material. In baseball, the slightly elevated area from which the pitcher throws. To heap or pile something up into a mound.
example_sentence: The archaeologists began carefully excavating the ancient burial mound on the edge of the forest. A mound of fresh earth was visible near the entrance to the rabbit's burrow. He stood on the pitcher's mound and prepared to deliver the opening throw of the game. The children built a mound of sand at the edge of the beach and decorated it with shells. The mound of paperwork on her desk had grown alarmingly over the course of the week.

english_meaning: To climb up onto something, especially an animal or vehicle. To increase in level, number, or intensity. A mountain or large hill, used before a proper name. To fix something on a support or backing for display or use.
example_sentence: She learned to mount and ride the horse with confidence after just a few lessons. Concern was beginning to mount as the rescue team had still not returned by nightfall. The photograph was beautifully mounted on a cream card and placed in a simple silver frame. Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world and has been climbed by thousands of people. Evidence against the suspect continued to mount as the investigation progressed.

english_meaning: A person who deceives others in order to trick them out of money. A charlatan who makes false claims about skills or remedies. A showy speaker who attracts crowds with boastful and dishonest talk. Historically, a seller of fake medicines at fairs and markets.
example_sentence: The so-called healer turned out to be a mountebank. Do not trust that mountebank with your savings. In old markets, a mountebank would sell useless potions. Critics dismissed the speaker as a political mountebank.

english_meaning: To feel and show that you are sad because somebody has died, to feel sad because something no longer exists or is no longer the same.
example_sentence: She is mourning her dead child. He was still mourning his brother's death.

english_meaning: A person who feels deep sorrow after the death of someone. It also refers to a person who attends a funeral, burial, memorial service, or condolence gathering to honor the deceased and offer sympathy to the bereaved family. A mourner may be a family member, friend, relative, colleague, or anyone paying their respects.
synonyms: ["Griever","Bereaved person","Funeral attendee","Funeral-goer","Condolent","Sorrower","Survivor (in the context of bereavement)","Sympathizer","Memorial attendee"]
example_sentence: Every mourner stood silently as the funeral procession passed. The mourners placed flowers beside the grave in memory of their loved one. A kind volunteer offered water and comfort to the mourners after the ceremony. Hundreds of mourners gathered to pay their final respects to the respected leader.

english_meaning: Hair grown on the upper lip of a man.  Facial hair on the upper lip.
example_sentence: His thick moustache made him look older. He trimmed his moustache before the wedding. The police officer had a long, curved moustache. My grandfather’s moustache was his pride.

english_meaning: The opening in the face through which a person or animal takes in food and produces sound. The cavity containing the teeth and tongue used for eating and speaking. The entrance or opening of something such as a cave, bottle, or river. To form words silently with the lips without making a sound. To speak in an insincere or exaggerated manner.
example_sentence: Please do not talk with your mouth full. The river flows into the sea at its mouth. She mouthed the words so no one else could hear. He burned his mouth on the hot soup.

english_meaning: Say (something dull or unoriginal) especially in a pompous or affected way, Move the lips as if saying (something)
example_sentence: This clergyman mouths platitudes in breathy, soothing tones. She mouthed a silent farewell.

english_meaning: So delicious in appearance, smell, or taste that it makes the mouth water. Extremely appetizing or tempting. Highly attractive or desirable. Producing eager anticipation. Wonderfully appealing to the senses.
example_sentence: The bakery had a mouthwatering display of pastries. She served a mouthwatering roast for dinner. The aroma of the curry was absolutely mouthwatering. He described the meal in mouthwatering detail.

english_meaning: A revenue or land record unit with defined boundaries, used for administrative and taxation purposes, typically containing agricultural land and one or more villages.
example_sentence: The land is located in Mouza Qasimabad, as recorded in the revenue documents. Each Mouza has its own map and boundary description maintained by the revenue department. The property dispute arose due to unclear boundaries between two Mouzas. Census data is often collected based on Mouza-level administrative divisions.

english_meaning: Able to be moved from one place or position to another. Not fixed or permanently attached. Capable of changing in date, time, position, or arrangement. In law, relating to personal property that can be moved rather than land or buildings. Able to be emotionally influenced or persuaded.
example_sentence: The room is divided by a movable partition. All the shelves are movable, so you can adjust their height. The meeting date is movable if the director agrees. The museum displayed the movable objects in secure glass cases.

english_meaning: To keep walking or driving and not stop or block the way. To make progress or continue at a steady pace. To order people to leave an area and not gather there. To advance a discussion or process to the next stage.
example_sentence: The officer asked the crowd to move along. The queue moved along faster than expected. Let us move along to the next item on the agenda. Work on the new road is moving along nicely.

english_meaning: To try very hard to do something. To make every possible effort to achieve something, help someone, or make something happen, no matter how difficult it is. It shows strong determination, commitment, and hard work.
synonyms: ["Try one’s best","Go to any length","Make every effort","Do everything possible","Work tirelessly"]
antonyms: ["Do nothing","Give up easily","Make no effort","Stay idle"]
example_sentence: She moved heaven and earth to get her son into that school. I will move heaven and earth to make your dream come true. They moved heaven and earth to rescue the trapped miners. The team moved heaven and earth to finish the project on time.

english_meaning: To begin living in a new house, flat, or room. To start occupying a place, office, or space. To approach someone or something closely, often in order to take control. To become involved in a situation, usually to take advantage of it.
synonyms: ["Take up residence","Occupy","Settle in","Relocate to","Advance on","Close in","Take over"]
example_sentence: We are going to move in next month. The new tenants moved in last Friday. Police moved in to disperse the crowd. Larger companies quickly moved in when prices fell.

english_meaning: To go into a new house, apartment, or building to live or work. To begin to take on a new position, responsibility, or role. To start to involve oneself in a new activity, topic, or field. To gradually become absorbed in a situation or state of mind.
example_sentence: They moved into a new apartment. The company moved into the tech industry. She moved into her office last week. We’re moving into a bigger house soon.

english_meaning: To depart. To start moving / to begin a journey. To leave a place / go away. To change topic / to stop discussing something.
example_sentence: The bus moved off slowly. The bus moved off after picking up passengers. The crowd slowly moved off after the speech. Let’s move off this subject and talk about something else.

english_meaning: To progress. To leave a place and continue forward. To stop focusing on something (often the past) and direct attention to the future. To continue with the next topic or activity.
example_sentence: It’s time to move on from the past. The police told the crowd to move on. After the breakup, she decided to move on with her life. Let’s move on to the next chapter.

english_meaning: To unfairly change the rules or expectations of a task. To make it harder for someone to succeed by shifting the criteria. To alter targets after progress has been made. To keep changing what is required. To act unfairly by adjusting standards.
example_sentence: Every time we finish a task, he moves the goalposts. Do not move the goalposts once the project starts. The company keeps moving the goalposts on employee bonuses. It is unfair to move the goalposts after the agreement.

english_meaning: To make a noticeable change or difference in something. To produce a measurable effect on a situation. To have a significant impact on results or outcomes. To cause visible progress or improvement. To shift the current state of affairs in a meaningful way.
example_sentence: The new marketing campaign really moved the needle on sales. Small donations alone will not move the needle on poverty. His speech moved the needle in the political debate. We need bold reforms that actually move the needle.

english_meaning: To advance, rise in position, or change to a higher level or rank.
example_sentence: He moved up to manager. Students move up a grade each year. She quickly moved up in the company. Prices have moved up again.

english_meaning: Able to be moved or carried from one place to another. Not fixed permanently in one position. Describing property such as furniture and goods rather than land or buildings. Of a date or festival, changing from year to year.
example_sentence: The classroom has light, moveable chairs. Moveable property must be listed separately in the will. Eid is a moveable feast in the solar calendar. The screen is moveable so everyone can see it.

english_meaning: A person who regularly goes to see films at the cinema. A member of the cinema audience. Someone who enjoys watching movies in a theatre.
example_sentence: The film attracted young moviegoers in large numbers. Moviegoers waited patiently outside the hall. Ticket offers are popular with regular moviegoers. As a moviegoer, he prefers thrillers.

english_meaning: Courage, determination, and the ability to face difficulty with energy and spirit. Force of character; the ability to face challenges boldly. Informal term for skill, confidence, and know-how.
example_sentence: It takes real moxie to stand up in front of a crowd and speak your mind without hesitation. She showed extraordinary moxie by launching her own business at the age of twenty-two. The young lawyer had the moxie to challenge even the most experienced opponents in court. Despite all the setbacks, his moxie never faltered, and he kept pushing forward. The team was short on experience but made up for it with sheer moxie and determination.

english_meaning: To bring into a disordered or confusing state. To confuse a person or mix up their thoughts. It can also refer to a state of disorder, confusion, or a disorganized mess. To mix things together in an untidy or chaotic way.
example_sentence: The files got completely muddled up during the office move. Try not to muddle the different concepts together when you write the essay. I was in such a muddle that I couldn't remember where I put my keys. The government handled the economic crisis in a complete muddle. He somehow managed to muddle through the complicated project.

english_meaning: Covered with or full of mud. Cloudy, not clear or transparent, like muddy water. Confused, vague, or unclear in thought or expression. To make something dirty, unclear, or confused.
example_sentence: The children came home with muddy shoes after playing outside. The river water was muddy after the heavy rain. His explanation only muddied the issue further. She has a muddy understanding of the new rules.

english_meaning: To study something quickly and try to memorize it, usually just before an exam or test, without deep understanding. It often implies short-term memorization rather than real learning.
example_sentence: I had to mug up all the formulas before the math exam. She mugged up the history dates just one night before the test. Don’t just mug up the answers, try to understand the concepts. He always mugs up notes at the last moment.

english_meaning: To study something quickly and carefully, especially to memorize facts for an exam, test, interview, or discussion. To learn or revise something in a short time by memorizing important facts, details, or information. It is often used when someone prepares at the last moment before an exam or important event.
example_sentence: I need to mug up on history before tomorrow’s exam. She mugged up on English grammar before the interview. He spent the whole night mugging up on science formulas. We should mug up on current affairs for the quiz competition.

english_meaning: A non-magical person. Someone who does not have magical powers and is unaware of the magical world. More generally, it can refer to someone who is inexperienced in a particular field.
example_sentence: Harry explained to the Muggle world that magic exists. He felt like a Muggle among all the scientists. The Muggle parents were confused by their child’s strange stories. Don’t be a Muggle in the tech world; learn coding.

english_meaning: A photograph of a person's face taken by the police after that person has been arrested. A police photograph showing the front and side view of a suspect or criminal. An official photograph kept in police records for identification purposes. Informally, it can also refer to any close-up photograph of a person's face.
example_sentence: His mugshot appeared on the front page of every newspaper. The police released the mugshots of all five suspects. She was embarrassed when her mugshot was shared online. The detective compared the witness's description with several mugshots. After the arrest, the officer took his fingerprints and mugshot.

english_meaning: A small, sweet berry that grows on the mulberry tree. The deciduous tree that produces this fruit and whose leaves feed silkworms. A dark red or purple color similar to the ripe fruit. A fruit used in jams, juices, and desserts. A tree of great importance in silk production.
example_sentence: The children picked fresh mulberries from the tree. My grandmother makes delicious mulberry jam every year. Silkworms are fed on mulberry leaves. The mulberry tree provides both fruit and shade.

english_meaning: A mule is an animal born from a male donkey and a female horse. It can also mean a stubborn person or someone who illegally carries goods.
example_sentence: The mule carried heavy loads across the mountains. Farmers prefer mules because they are strong and patient. He is as stubborn as a mule when making decisions. The police arrested a mule at the airport for smuggling drugs.

english_meaning: To think about something carefully and at length; to ponder or consider deeply. Also means to heat and spice wine or cider.
example_sentence: She mulled over the job offer for several days. He sat quietly, mulling the decision in his mind. They enjoyed a cup of mulled wine by the fireplace. She needs time to mull before making a final choice.

english_meaning: To think carefully and at length about something before making a decision. To consider all aspects of a situation or problem slowly and thoroughly.
example_sentence: I need a few days to mull over your proposal. She mulled over the decision before accepting the new job. He mulled over every possible outcome before acting. Take your time and mull over all the options.

english_meaning: Having many varied parts, elements, or aspects. Existing in great variety or diversity. Numerous and of many different kinds.
example_sentence: She has multifarious duties as head of the department. The city offers multifarious opportunities to young people. His multifarious interests include music, sport, and painting. The report deals with the multifarious problems of the region.

english_meaning: Involving more than two countries, parties, or groups. Agreements, discussions, or actions that include multiple sides, nations, or organizations, rather than just two. Often used in diplomacy, trade, or international relations.
example_sentence: The UN promotes multilateral cooperation among nations. A multilateral trade agreement benefits all participating countries. Climate change requires a multilateral approach to find effective solutions. Multilateral negotiations were held to resolve the border dispute.

english_meaning: The practice of several countries working together on a shared issue. A system of international cooperation involving three or more nations. A foreign policy approach that prefers joint action and agreements over acting alone. Support for global institutions such as the United Nations in solving problems. The principle that international matters should be settled collectively.
example_sentence: The treaty was hailed as a victory for multilateralism. Climate change can only be solved through genuine multilateralism. Many diplomats warn that multilateralism is under pressure today. The country returned to multilateralism after years of isolation.

english_meaning: Able to speak or understand several languages. Written or expressed in more than one language. Involving or relating to the use of many languages.
example_sentence: She is multilingual and works as a conference interpreter. The museum offers multilingual audio guides. Switzerland is a famously multilingual country. The company published a multilingual safety leaflet.

english_meaning: Having or involving many parts, people, or elements. More than one in number. In mathematics, a number that contains another number an exact number of times. A quantity obtained by multiplying a given number.
example_sentence: He suffered multiple injuries in the accident. The report has multiple authors. Twelve is a multiple of three. There are multiple reasons for the delay.

english_meaning: A large cinema complex containing several separate screens. A building with many parts or units under one roof. In telecommunications, a system that sends several signals over one channel. To combine multiple signals for transmission along a single line.
example_sentence: A new multiplex opened near the shopping mall. The multiplex shows five films at the same time. Engineers multiplex the data before transmission. Families prefer the comfort of a modern multiplex.

english_meaning: To speak quietly and in a way that is difficult to understand, often with the mouth barely open. To utter words indistinctly or unclearly. To mutter or murmur in a low and unclear tone.
example_sentence: She could hear him mumble something under his breath but could not make out the words. Please do not mumble during the presentation — speak clearly so everyone can hear you. The child would often mumble his answers when he was nervous about being wrong. He started to mumble an excuse but was cut off before he could finish his sentence. She sat in the corner and continued to mumble to herself long after the argument had ended.

english_meaning: A person who speaks quietly and unclearly. Someone whose words are hard to understand because they are not spoken distinctly. A person who mutters under their breath.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the mumbler to speak up. He is a natural mumbler, especially on the phone. As a mumbler, he often had to repeat himself. Listeners complained that the presenter was a hopeless mumbler.

english_meaning: To preserve a dead body by embalming, drying, or other methods to prevent decomposition. To make something dry, shriveled, or preserved for a very long time. Figuratively, to make a person, object, or idea inactive, rigid, or lifeless.
example_sentence: The ancient Egyptians learned how to mummify their dead rulers. Archaeologists discovered a chamber where priests used special oils to mummify bodies. The dry desert climate helped mummify the remains naturally. Years of isolation seemed to mummify the old traditions, leaving them unchanged.

english_meaning: Lacking interest or excitement; dull and ordinary. Relating to the everyday world rather than the spiritual. Common, routine, and without special quality. Concerned with practical matters of daily life.
example_sentence: She was tired of her mundane office routine. Even mundane tasks can teach us patience. He escaped his mundane life through books and travel. The film focused on the mundane details of family life.

english_meaning: The quality of being extremely generous with money or gifts. Great liberality in giving to others. A generous act or an unusually large gift. Openhandedness shown especially towards those in need.
example_sentence: The hospital was built through the munificence of one family. Her munificence towards the poor was widely admired. Guests were amazed by the munificence of the host. The scholarship stands as a lasting proof of his munificence.

english_meaning: Extremely generous in giving money or gifts. Showing great liberality and openhandedness towards others. Larger or more valuable than is usual or expected, as of a donation. Characterised by lavish and unselfish giving.
example_sentence: A munificent donor paid for the entire new library. She received a munificent gift on her wedding day. The trust was founded by a munificent businessman. His munificent support kept the orphanage running for years.

english_meaning: Military weapons, ammunition, and equipment used in war. Supplies of bombs, shells, and other explosive materials. To supply a place or force with weapons and military stores. Anything provided as material for defence or attack.
example_sentence: The convoy was carrying munitions to the front line. A munition factory was built outside the city. Soldiers guarded the munition depot day and night. The treaty limits the production of certain munitions.

english_meaning: Dark, gloomy, or unclear. Something that is difficult to see through, understand, or interpret. It can describe physical darkness like water or metaphorical obscurity like a situation or story that is confusing or suspicious.
example_sentence: The river water was murky after the heavy rain. His explanation of the incident was murky and confusing. The alley was murky and filled with shadows. The political situation became murky after the announcement.

english_meaning: A soft, low, unclear sound or speaking quietly. A quiet, gentle, and continuous sound that is not clear. It can also mean speaking in a very soft voice so that words are not fully clear. It is often used for natural sounds like wind, water, or crowd noise, and also for people speaking secretly or softly.
example_sentence: The children began to murmur in the classroom during the lesson. I could hear the murmur of the river at night. The crowd started to murmur when the decision was announced. She murmured a soft apology and walked away.

english_meaning: A body tissue made of fibres that contract to produce movement. Any of the organs made of such tissue that move parts of the skeleton. Physical strength or power produced by well-developed muscles. Influence, force, or authority used to get something done. To force one's way into a situation or place.
example_sentence: Regular training helped him build muscle in his arms. Every muscle in her body ached after the long hike. The company used its financial muscle to win the contract. He tried to muscle his way to the front of the queue.

english_meaning: To force oneself into a situation or group, often without being welcome. To intrude by using strength, power, or influence.
example_sentence: He tried to muscle in on our conversation. A large company muscled in on the local market. Please do not muscle in while others are negotiating. The newcomer muscled in and took control of the meeting.

english_meaning: The body tissue that contracts and relaxes to produce movement. Tissue made of long fibre-like cells capable of shortening. The three types found in the body, namely skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle tissue. Tissue that also generates heat and helps maintain posture.
example_sentence: Muscle tissue allows the body to move and lift objects. The heart is made of a special kind of muscle tissue. Regular exercise increases muscle tissue and strength. Smooth muscle tissue lines the walls of the intestines.

english_meaning: To think about something deeply and at length, often in a quiet or thoughtful way. To ponder, reflect, or meditate. To say something in a thoughtful manner. A source of inspiration, especially for an artist, writer, or musician. In Greek mythology, one of the nine goddesses who inspired learning and the arts.
example_sentence: She sat by the window and began to muse about her childhood. The poet found his muse in the quiet mountains of the north. He mused that life was full of unexpected turns. The artist often mused over his unfinished paintings for hours. Many writers consider nature their greatest muse.

english_meaning: A building in which objects of historical, scientific, artistic, or cultural interest are stored and exhibited. A place where a collection of objects is preserved and shown to the public. An institution dedicated to the preservation and study of artifacts. A metaphorical term for a place that feels outdated or stuck in the past. An organized display of natural history specimens for research purposes. A private repository where an individual keeps personal collections. A repository for digital archives or virtual historical exhibits. An extensive collection of items arranged for aesthetic appreciation. A site where historical structures are preserved in their original context. An institution that serves as a center for cultural heritage and education. A location or entity that preserves a specific tradition or industry. A facility used for the conservation and restoration of historical materials.
example_sentence: We spent the entire afternoon exploring the natural history museum downtown. The old mansion was converted into a local history museum last year. His grandmother’s attic was like a small museum of twentieth-century toys. The university maintains a vast museum of geological specimens for its students.

english_meaning: A fleshy, spore-bearing fruiting body of a fungus, typically produced above ground. To grow, develop, or spread rapidly and often unpredictably. Something that appears or grows with sudden speed and abundance.
example_sentence: She sautéed the mushrooms with garlic and herbs to make a simple but flavourful side dish. The small town began to mushroom into a bustling city after the discovery of oil nearby. Not all wild mushrooms are safe to eat, so identification by an expert is essential. The number of online food delivery services continued to mushroom throughout the pandemic. He found a cluster of wild mushrooms growing at the base of the old oak tree.

english_meaning: Something very pleasant or delightful to hear. Words or news that bring great joy. A statement that satisfies or pleases the listener. Any sound that gives happiness to the hearer. Information that is welcomed warmly.
example_sentence: Her promotion news was music to her ears. His apology was music to my ears. The sound of rain is music to a farmer's ears. Their laughter was music to their mother's ears.

english_meaning: An intense and irrational fear of mice or rats. A person with musophobia may feel extreme panic, disgust, or terror at the sight or thought of rodents.
example_sentence: Her musophobia made her scream at the sight of a mouse. He refused to enter the old warehouse because of his musophobia. Musophobia is one of the most common animal phobias. She avoided the basement due to her musophobia.

english_meaning: Hair grown on the upper lip of a man.  Facial hair on the upper lip.
example_sentence: He grew a thick mustache over the winter. The actor’s mustache made him look older. He twirled his mustache thoughtfully. Mustache styles vary across cultures.

english_meaning: A plant of the cabbage family with yellow flowers, whose seeds are used to make a condiment. A paste or sauce made from the ground seeds of the mustard plant, used as a condiment. A brownish-yellow colour similar to that of mustard paste.
example_sentence: She spread a generous layer of mustard on the sandwich before adding the cold meat. The fields were alive with the bright yellow flowers of the mustard plant in early spring. He wore a mustard-coloured jacket that stood out warmly against the grey autumn day. Mustard has been used as a flavouring and preservative for thousands of years across many cultures. The recipe called for a teaspoon of wholegrain mustard to be stirred into the sauce.

english_meaning: The peppery green leaves of the mustard plant, eaten as a vegetable. A leafy green cooked in curries, soups, and traditional dishes. The plant grown for these leaves and seeds. A winter vegetable popular in South Asian cooking.
example_sentence: Mustard greens are cooked with corn bread in winter. She chopped the mustard greens finely. The fields turn yellow when mustard flowers bloom. Mustard greens have a strong, peppery taste.

english_meaning: To gather or assemble troops or people, especially for inspection or action. To summon up a feeling, attitude, or response. To collect or bring together strength, courage, or resources. A formal gathering or assembly of troops.
example_sentence: The captain ordered the crew to muster on the main deck immediately. She could barely muster the energy to get out of bed after such a long and exhausting week. The troops were told to muster at dawn before the march began. He managed to muster a smile despite feeling overwhelmingly disappointed by the news. The army passed muster after a thorough inspection by the senior commanding officer.

english_meaning: An organism that has undergone a mutation, resulting in a change to its genetic material. Something that has changed significantly from its original form or nature. In popular culture, a creature with unusual or extraordinary characteristics resulting from genetic change.
example_sentence: The scientists discovered a mutant strain of the bacteria that was resistant to all known antibiotics. The science fiction novel featured mutant humans with extraordinary abilities living secretly among ordinary people. The mutant plant produced unusually large fruit that drew significant interest from agricultural researchers. Exposure to high levels of radiation can cause an organism to become a mutant over several generations. The superhero in the comic series was a mutant whose powers had developed after a laboratory accident.

english_meaning: To undergo or cause to undergo a mutation or significant change in genetic material. To change or transform in form, nature, or character, often significantly. To alter or evolve in an unexpected or dramatic way.
example_sentence: Viruses can mutate rapidly, making it challenging to develop vaccines that remain effective over time. The character in the story began to mutate after exposure to a mysterious chemical compound. Scientists observed how the cells began to mutate under the influence of the experimental drug. Over millions of years, the species continued to mutate and adapt to its changing environment. The original design was forced to mutate significantly in response to changing consumer preferences.

english_meaning: A process in which the genetic material of a person, a plant or an animal changes in structure when it is passed on to children, etc, causing different physical characteristics to develop, a change of this kind. (Biology) an organism that has characteristics resulting from chromosomal alteration. A change or alteration in form or qualities. A change in the form or structure of something.
example_sentence: These cells have been affected by mutation. The genetic material has suffered a mutation. It is well known that radiation can cause mutation. This essay examines the mutation of ethnic politics into nationalist politics. The sculpture series underwent several mutations as the artist experimented with different materials and techniques.

english_meaning: Without a point, spine, or sharp projection. In botany and zoology, used to describe a plant, leaf, seed, or animal part that is blunt and lacks an awn, bristle, or sharp tip. Smooth-ended and not pointed. Mainly used in scientific descriptions of plants and insects.
example_sentence: The botanist described the leaf as muticous and smooth-edged. Many grass species have muticous seeds that lack awns. The insect's wings appeared muticous under the microscope. This variety of wheat is preferred for being muticous and easy to handle. The specimen was identified by its muticous tip.

english_meaning: To damage something severely, especially by cutting or tearing off parts of it. To injure a person or animal badly by removing or destroying body parts. To disfigure. To spoil or ruin something by removing essential parts. Often used in serious contexts of violence, accidents, or deliberate destruction.
example_sentence: The accident mutilated his right arm beyond recognition. Vandals mutilated the ancient statue in the museum. Wild animals had mutilated the body of the deer. Censors mutilated the film by cutting out important scenes. It is a crime to mutilate currency notes in any country.

english_meaning: Refusing to obey the orders of a person in authority, especially in the military. Showing rebellious feelings or behavior. Involved in or inclined toward mutiny. Openly disloyal or resistant.
example_sentence: The mutinous sailors took control of the ship. His mutinous behavior led to his dismissal. The soldiers grew mutinous after months without pay. She gave her boss a mutinous look.

english_meaning: Forcible or passive resistance to lawful authority. To rise against or refuse to obey or observe authority. Open fighting against authority (as one's own government). To rise up against established authority.
example_sentence:
There were rumours of mutiny among the troops. The crew mutinied and murdered the ship's captain.
The troops mutinied against their officers.

english_meaning: The flesh of a fully grown or mature sheep used as food. A specific type of red meat distinguished from lamb by the age of the animal. Historically used to refer to the animal itself in certain culinary contexts. Occasionally used in slang to refer to a person's physical appearance or age in derogatory phrases.
example_sentence: The chef recommended slow-cooking the mutton to ensure it became tender. We ordered a spicy mutton curry for dinner at the traditional restaurant. Unlike lamb, mutton has a much stronger and more gamey flavor profile. The butcher displayed various cuts of fresh mutton in the glass case.

english_meaning: A strong sensation of fatigue, extreme strain, or emotional reaction like uncontrollable laughter. It can also convey the idea of aging or facial sagging. Context matters to understand whether it’s physical, emotional, or humorous.
example_sentence: After hiking for 10 hours, I felt like my cheeks were falling off. I laughed so hard at the joke that my cheeks were falling off. Sitting in the freezing wind made me feel like my cheeks were falling off. After working all night, my cheeks were falling off from sheer exhaustion.

english_meaning: Do as I say, or leave. A strict expression used when someone insists that things must be done their way, or others are free to leave. This idiom shows a rigid attitude where a person refuses to compromise. It means only one option is acceptable: follow their decision, rules, or instructions. If someone disagrees, they can step aside or leave. It often describes controlling or authoritarian behavior in personal, work, or social situations.
example_sentence: The manager’s attitude was my way or the highway, which made his employees frustrated. You can’t run a successful team with a my way or the highway attitude. His father was very strict; it was always my way or the highway at home. If she keeps saying my way or the highway, no one will want to work with her. Leaders who listen are respected more than those who believe in my way or the highway. During the project meeting, Tom’s my way or the highway stance created conflict among team members.

english_meaning: A person who loves mushrooms and enjoys studying or hunting them. An enthusiast of fungi and their many varieties. Someone who forages, cooks, or researches mushrooms with passion. A devoted fan of the fungal world.
example_sentence: As a mycophile, he goes foraging every autumn. Mycophiles must learn which mushrooms are safe. The chef is a mycophile who uses rare fungi. She joined a mycophile society last year.

english_meaning: A condition of the eye in which distant objects appear blurry because light is focused in front of the retina rather than on it. Shortsightedness. A lack of foresight or the inability to consider long-term consequences. Narrow-mindedness or a limited perspective.
example_sentence: She was diagnosed with myopia as a child and has worn glasses or contact lenses ever since. The politician was criticised for the myopia of his economic policies, which ignored long-term impacts. Myopia is one of the most common vision problems in the world and is easily corrected with lenses. His myopia in business matters caused him to overlook trends that his competitors had already identified. The increasing prevalence of myopia among children has been linked to reduced time spent outdoors.

english_meaning: Relating to or suffering from myopia; unable to see distant objects clearly. Lacking imagination or foresight. Concerned only with the present or immediate situation without considering the future.
example_sentence: Without his glasses, he was too myopic to read the signs on the other side of the street. The board's myopic focus on short-term profits ignored the serious risks it was creating. She offered a myopic view of the situation that failed to account for the wider social context. A myopic approach to education often results in students who are unprepared for the real world. Scientists warned that a myopic response to climate change would prove disastrous in the long term.

english_meaning: A non-standard or informal term sometimes used to describe a misreading or an incorrect interpretation of a text or message. To misread or incorrectly interpret written or visual information. An error or mistake made in reading something.
example_sentence: He admitted that his interpretation was a myread of the original document's intention. The confusion arose from a simple myread of the email, which caused an unnecessary disagreement. She apologised for the myread and immediately sent a corrected version of her response. The dispute could have been avoided if the message had not been subject to such a serious myread. A careful review of the text confirmed that the earlier myread had led to an incorrect conclusion.

english_meaning: A countless or extremely great number of people or things. A very large and indefinite quantity. Used to describe something existing in great variety or number. It means innumerable or extremely numerous.
example_sentence: The night sky was filled with a myriad of stars. She faced a myriad of challenges while starting her business. The festival offered a myriad of cultural performances and food stalls. Modern technology has created myriad new opportunities for young people. There are myriad reasons why people choose to live in the city.

english_meaning: A hired ruffian or unscrupulous person who carries out orders without question. Originally the name of a legendary warrior race who followed Achilles in Greek mythology.
example_sentence: The dictator's myrmidons carried out every cruel order without hesitation. He was merely a myrmidon doing his master's dirty work. The police chief's myrmidons intimidated witnesses. History remembers those myrmidons as accessories to great crimes.

english_meaning: A bush with shiny leaves, pink or white flowers and blue-black berries. A small tree with shiny green leaves, pleasant-smelling white flowers and blue-black fruit.
example_sentence: The most common plants are olives, maritime pines, oaks, myrtles, junipers. The garden was full of blooming myrtle bushes. Myrtle leaves are used to make fragrant oils. She wore a wreath of myrtle on her wedding day. The ancient symbol of peace often included myrtle branches.

english_meaning: An irrational fear of dirt, germs, and contamination. Excessive anxiety about becoming infected by touching things. A phobia often linked with compulsive washing or cleaning. Also called germophobia.
example_sentence: Her mysophobia made her wash her hands dozens of times a day. Mysophobia grew more common during the pandemic. He avoids public transport because of mysophobia. Treatment for mysophobia often includes cognitive therapy.

english_meaning: Difficult to understand or explain. Full of secrets or unknown facts. Causing curiosity because of being unclear. Strange or unexplained in nature.
example_sentence: The old house has a mysterious atmosphere at night. He received a mysterious phone call without any number. There is a mysterious light in the sky every evening. The disappearance of the document is still mysterious.

english_meaning: In a strange or unexplained manner. In a way that causes curiosity or wonder. Without any obvious reason or explanation. In a secretive or puzzling way. In a manner connected with mystery, secrecy, or the unknown.
example_sentence: The documents mysteriously disappeared from the office overnight. She smiled mysteriously but did not reveal her secret. The lights mysteriously turned on even though nobody was home. The ancient treasure mysteriously vanished centuries ago.

english_meaning: The quality of being enigmatic or puzzling. A sense of secrecy or concealment. An unexplained or strange nature. A condition that arouses curiosity and wonder. The characteristic of being difficult to interpret or understand. Hidden meaning or unknown purpose. An aura of intrigue surrounding someone or something.
example_sentence: The mysteriousness of the old abandoned house attracted many visitors. Her mysteriousness made everyone curious about her life. The mysteriousness surrounding the incident remains unsolved. The novel gains excitement from the mysteriousness of its main character.

english_meaning: Something that is difficult to understand or to explain. A religious truth that one can know only by revelation and cannot fully understand.
example_sentence: It is one of the great unsolved mysteries of this country. It is a complete mystery to me why they chose him

english_meaning: It refers to a situation or person that is profoundly confusing and impossible to understand. The phrase describes an enigma that contains multiple layers of secrecy and complexity. It represents a puzzle that lacks any clear or logical explanation. The expression is used for something highly secretive whose motives or inner workings are completely concealed. It signifies an extremely baffling phenomenon that defies all attempts at rational analysis.
example_sentence: The reclusive author remains a mystery wrapped in a riddle to his fans. Her sudden disappearance was truly a mystery wrapped in a riddle. Trying to figure out the old machine's mechanism is like solving a mystery wrapped in a riddle. The foreign policy of that nation is a mystery wrapped in a riddle.

english_meaning: A person who seeks to gain spiritual knowledge or unity with the divine through meditation, prayer, or contemplation. Relating to mysteries or spiritual matters beyond ordinary understanding. Having a magical or mysterious quality. Connected with secret religious rites or supernatural powers.
example_sentence: The mystic spent years meditating in the mountains. Rumi was a famous mystic and poet of the Sufi tradition. There was a mystic atmosphere inside the ancient temple. She had a mystic belief in the power of dreams. He wrote a book about the mystic experiences of saints.

english_meaning: Relating to mysteries of a spiritual or supernatural nature. Having a magical or spiritual meaning beyond ordinary understanding. Inspiring a sense of wonder and awe. Connected with religious or spiritual experiences.
example_sentence: The old temple had a mystical atmosphere. She had a mystical experience during her meditation. Poets often describe love as a mystical feeling. The forest seemed almost mystical in the moonlight.

english_meaning: The belief that direct knowledge of God, spiritual truth, or ultimate reality can be attained through personal experience, intuition, or meditation rather than through reasoning. A spiritual practice focused on union with the divine. Vague or obscure thinking that is hard to understand. The doctrines and practices of mystics.
example_sentence: He wrote a book on the mysticism of the great Sufi poets. Mysticism plays an important role in many world religions. She turned to mysticism after years of restless searching. The painting reflects the deep mysticism of the East. Many philosophers have explored the connection between mysticism and reality.

english_meaning: A special quality of mystery, charm, or fascination around a person, thing, or place. An attractive sense of mystery or magic that makes someone or something seem special, interesting, or difficult to fully understand. It often gives a feeling of admiration, wonder, or curiosity.
example_sentence: The old castle had a mystique that attracted tourists from around the world. The actor's quiet personality added to his mystique. There is a certain mystique surrounding ancient traditions. The brand built its mystique through elegance and secrecy.

english_meaning: A story from ancient times, especially one that was told to explain natural events or to describe the early history of a people, this type of story
example_sentence: Its time to dispel the myth of a classless society(=to show it doesn't exist).

english_meaning: An abnormal tendency to lie or exaggerate. A compulsive habit of telling untrue stories about oneself. A mental condition marked by constant fabrication of fantastic tales. The uncontrollable urge to invent and believe one's own falsehoods. Pathological lying practised without any clear benefit.
example_sentence: His mythomania made it impossible to trust anything he said. The therapist recognised clear signs of mythomania. Mythomania often begins as a harmless habit of exaggeration. She wrote a novel about a man suffering from mythomania.

english_meaning: To catch or arrest someone, especially a criminal. To take or seize something suddenly. To grab or catch something before it is missed or lost.
example_sentence: Police managed to nab the suspected thief as he was attempting to flee across the rooftop. She was able to nab the last available seat on the morning train to the city. The detective spent months working to nab the fraudster before finally making the arrest. He managed to nab a great deal on the new laptop just before the sale ended. Officers were determined to nab the gang leader before he could escape across the border.

english_meaning: A hard protective plate made of keratin that covers the tip of a finger or toe. The horny covering at the end of the human digits. A small thin metal spike used to join or fasten pieces of wood together. To fasten, fix, or attach something with nails. To achieve or do something perfectly, used informally.
example_sentence: She keeps her nails short and clean. The doctor examined the colour of his nails for signs of illness. He hammered a nail into the wooden board. She really nailed her presentation this morning.

english_meaning: The layer of skin and tissue lying directly beneath the nail plate. The soft vascular tissue that supports the nail and supplies it with blood. The pink area visible under a fingernail or toenail. A part of the nail unit whose colour and condition can indicate a person's health.
example_sentence: A healthy nail bed usually looks pink. The injury damaged the nail bed of his thumb. Doctors check the nail bed to see how well blood is circulating. A pale nail bed may be a sign of anaemia.

english_meaning: To confirm or secure something, such as an agreement, plan, or detail, so that it cannot be changed. It can also mean to clearly understand or identify something.
example_sentence: We need to nail down the date for the meeting. The detective tried to nail down the suspect’s location. They finally nailed down the terms of the contract. I can’t seem to nail down the exact cause of the problem.

english_meaning: To fasten or attach something onto a surface using nails. To fix something firmly on another object.
example_sentence: He nailed the sign on the front door. The workers nailed the boards on the wall. She nailed the poster on the notice board. Please nail this hook on the wall.

english_meaning: To fasten something in a higher position using nails. To close or block an opening by nailing planks over it.
example_sentence: They nailed up the sign above the shop entrance. He nailed up the windows before the storm. The abandoned house had its doors nailed up. She nailed up the picture on the top of the wall.

english_meaning: A person who is innocent, simple, or lacks experience and worldly understanding. A naive person often trusts others easily because they do not expect dishonesty or deceit.
example_sentence: She is too naive to realize that people can take advantage of her kindness. He gave a naive answer to a very complex question. The child’s naive smile showed complete trust and purity. It was naive of me to believe everything I read on the internet.

english_meaning: The quality of being simple, innocent, or lacking experience or wisdom. Lack of sophistication or worldliness in judgement. A show of unaffected simplicity.
example_sentence: There was a charming naivete in her questions. His naivete about politics surprised his friends. She spoke with a childlike naivete about the world. Investors paid a heavy price for their naivete.

english_meaning: Without any clothes or covering. Exposed and unprotected. Visible to the naked eye, without the use of any instrument or aid. Without any disguise or concealment; plain and obvious.
example_sentence: The ancient statue depicted a naked figure carved from white marble with extraordinary skill. Some bacteria are so small they cannot be seen by the naked eye without a microscope. The truth lay naked before them, impossible to deny or avoid any longer. Naked ambition drove him to pursue power at the expense of his personal relationships. The documentary revealed the naked reality of life for those living in extreme poverty.

english_meaning: Lacking energy, strength, courage, or firmness of character. Displaying excessive sentimentality or insipid style. Being overly delicate, childish, or indecisive in taking action. Referring to a person who is foolishly weak or lacking in conviction.
example_sentence: The manager refused to take a namby pamby approach to dealing with company losses. He was tired of reading namby pamby poetry that lacked any real emotional depth. Stop being so namby pamby and make up your mind about the offer. Nobody respects a namby pamby leader who changes his decision every hour.

english_meaning: To give someone or something the same name as another person or thing, usually to honor them.
synonyms: ["Honor with the name","Dedicate","Christen in honor","Call after"]
example_sentence: They named their son after his grandfather. The park was named after the famous poet. She named her dog after her favorite character in a book. The company named the new product after its founder.

english_meaning: A person who seeks to impress others by frequently mentioning famous or important people they supposedly know. Someone who tries to elevate their own social status by casually dropping the names of well-known individuals into conversation. An individual who uses their casual acquaintance with notable figures to gain an advantage. A boaster who constantly alludes to high-profile contacts to appear more important.
example_sentence: He is a shameless name-dropper who cannot tell a story without mentioning a celebrity. It becomes annoying when a name-dropper constantly interrupts to boast about their influential friends. She quickly gained a reputation as a name-dropper at networking events. The politician was accused of being a name-dropper rather than focusing on actual policies.

english_meaning: A person or thing that has the same name as another. Someone or something that is named after another person or thing. Often used to show a connection through naming, like a child named after a parent or a city named after a famous person.
example_sentence: John is my namesake; we share the same name. The city is a namesake of its founder. She was proud to be the namesake of her grandmother. The ship was named as a namesake of the famous explorer.

english_meaning: A person, usually a woman, employed to take care of children in a household. Also used informally to describe a government or authority that is overly protective or controlling.
example_sentence: The nanny took the children to the park every morning. They hired a live-in nanny after the twins were born. Critics accused the new regulations of creating a nanny state. A good nanny becomes like a member of the family.

english_meaning: The activity or behaviour of caring for children as a nanny. Also used critically to describe excessive interference, supervision, or protective control by an authority.
example_sentence: She left her job in banking for full-time nannying. The media criticised the government for nannying its citizens. Nannying regulations can discourage personal responsibility. His friends teased him about nannying his younger sister.

english_meaning: A prefix used in the metric system to denote a factor of one billionth (10 to the power of negative 9). Extremely small or minute in scale or scope. Pertaining to nanotechnology or science at the atomic level. A unit of measurement for sub-microscopic dimensions. Often used metaphorically to describe something very short in duration. Relating to technology that manipulates individual atoms and molecules.
example_sentence: The new processor is built using advanced nano-scale transistors to increase efficiency. Scientists are exploring nano-bots that can deliver medicine directly to specific cells in the body. A nanosecond is a common unit of time used in high-frequency computer calculations. The environmental impact of nano-plastics in the ocean is a growing concern for biologists.

english_meaning: A hypothetical or emerging microscopic robot, measured on the nanometre scale, designed to perform tasks at the molecular or cellular level, such as medical treatment or manufacturing.
example_sentence: Scientists are researching nanobots that could target cancer cells. A nanobot might one day repair damaged tissue from within. The concept of self-replicating nanobots remains largely theoretical. Nanobots could revolutionize drug delivery in medicine.

english_meaning: A unit of length equal to one billionth of a metre, used to measure very small distances such as wavelengths of light and molecular dimensions.
example_sentence: The transistor gates measure only a few nanometres across. Visible light has wavelengths between 400 and 700 nanometres. A DNA molecule is about two nanometres wide. Advances at the nanometre scale drive modern electronics.

english_meaning: A microscopic particle between one and one hundred nanometres in size, often with unique physical or chemical properties due to its small scale, used in medicine, cosmetics, and materials science.
example_sentence: Silver nanoparticles are used in antibacterial coatings. The researchers synthesized gold nanoparticles for drug delivery tests. Nanoparticle size affects colour, reactivity, and strength. Sunscreen often contains titanium dioxide nanoparticles.

english_meaning: Fear of small things or objects. A psychological condition or irrational fear where an individual experiences anxiety or extreme discomfort when encountering very small objects, particles, or details.
synonyms: ["Microphobia","Fear of small things","Fear of tiny objects"]
