english_meaning: Noticeable in an unpleasant or unwelcome way. Standing out too much and attracting unwanted attention. Tending to push oneself or one's opinions forward without invitation. Undesirably prominent or intrusive.
example_sentence: The new sign is far too obtrusive for such a quiet street. He tried to help without being obtrusive. The camera was hidden so it would not be obtrusive. Obtrusive advertising can annoy customers.

english_meaning: In a way that is unpleasantly noticeable. So as to attract unwanted attention. In an intrusive or interfering manner. In a manner that stands out too prominently.
example_sentence: The guard stood obtrusively near the entrance. She spoke obtrusively during the quiet ceremony. The new building rises obtrusively above the old town. He obtrusively checked his watch throughout the meeting.

english_meaning: Not quick to understand or insensitive. Slow to understand, not sharp or intelligent, lacking awareness. Insensitive or not aware of others' feelings. An angle that is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.
example_sentence: He gave an obtuse answer that confused everyone. She is too obtuse to understand the simple instructions. The manager seemed obtuse to the workers' problems. This triangle has one obtuse angle.

english_meaning: An angle that measures more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. A wide, blunt angle larger than a right angle. Any angle between a right angle and a straight angle. A geometric classification of angles by size.
example_sentence: The triangle contains one obtuse angle. An obtuse angle looks wider than a right angle. He measured an obtuse angle of one hundred and twenty degrees. The two walls meet at an obtuse angle.

english_meaning: A triangle in which one interior angle is greater than 90 degrees. A triangle containing exactly one obtuse angle. A wide, flattened triangle with two acute angles and one obtuse angle. One of the three main types of triangle classified by angle.
example_sentence: An obtuse-angled triangle can have only one obtuse angle. The diagram shows an obtuse-angled triangle with a wide top. She measured the largest angle of the obtuse-angled triangle. An obtuse-angled triangle never contains a right angle.

english_meaning: Slowness of understanding; lack of quickness in perception. The quality of being blunt rather than sharp. Insensitivity to the feelings or hints of others. In geometry, the state of being greater than a right angle.
example_sentence: His obtuseness in the meeting frustrated everyone. She was surprised by the obtuseness of his reply. The obtuseness of the blade made cutting difficult. The obtuseness of the angle was clear from the diagram.

english_meaning: The front or main side of something, especially a coin or medal. The opposite or counterpart of a fact or truth. The side of a coin bearing the head or principal design. A counterpart to something. It refers either to the front face of a coin, medal, or document that carries the most important design, or figuratively to the opposite aspect of an idea or situation.
example_sentence: The obverse of the coin shows the portrait of the queen. Poverty is often the obverse of wealth in unequal societies. He examined the obverse of the medal carefully under the light. The obverse side of the document contained the official seal. Joy and sorrow are the obverse of each other in human life.

english_meaning: To remove or prevent a difficulty or need. To make something unnecessary. To avoid an anticipated problem. To eliminate or get rid of something in advance.
example_sentence: New technology will obviate the need for paper files. Careful planning can obviate many problems. The agreement will obviate any future disputes. Proper training helps obviate accidents in the workplace.

english_meaning: Easily seen or understood. Clear. Plain. Evident. Apparent. Self-evident. Not difficult to perceive or recognize. Something that is so clear that it can be easily noticed or understood without explanation. It is used for facts, reasons, signs, or feelings that do not need any proof because they are visible or known to everyone.
example_sentence: It was obvious that he was lying about the incident. The answer to the question is quite obvious. There are obvious reasons for the company's decision to expand. She had an obvious talent for music from a young age. The mistake in the report was so obvious that everyone noticed it.

english_meaning: In a way that is easily seen or understood. Clearly and plainly. Used to introduce something that is not surprising. Without doubt.
example_sentence: She was obviously tired after the long trip. Obviously, we need more time to finish the project. He obviously enjoyed the performance. The plan will obviously require some changes.

english_meaning: The quality of being clear or easy to understand. The state of being plainly visible or evident. Lack of subtlety or hidden meaning. The condition of being self-evident.
example_sentence: The obviousness of his lie shocked everyone. She was surprised by the obviousness of the answer. There was an uncomfortable obviousness in his behavior. The obviousness of the mistake made it easy to correct.

english_meaning: A particular time when an event happens. A special or important event or ceremony. A suitable opportunity or chance to do something. A reason or cause for something. To cause something to happen.
example_sentence: I met him on only one occasion last year. The wedding was a joyful family occasion. She had no occasion to complain about the service. His careless remark occasioned a long argument.

english_meaning: Happening or done sometimes but not regularly. Occurring at irregular or infrequent intervals. Intended for use only on special occasions.
example_sentence: He makes an occasional visit to his old school. There were occasional showers throughout the day. She enjoys an occasional cup of strong coffee. The room is used for occasional meetings only.

english_meaning: Sometimes but not often or regularly. From time to time, at irregular intervals. Now and then, on a few separate occasions.
example_sentence: We occasionally meet for coffee after work. He occasionally writes articles for the local newspaper. It occasionally rains here even in summer. She occasionally visits her grandparents in the village.

english_meaning: Relating to the countries of the West, especially Europe and America. Characteristic of Western culture, customs, or people. A native or inhabitant of the Western world.
example_sentence: The museum compares occidental and oriental art. He adopted an occidental style of dress. Occidental philosophy influenced their political thought. Many occidentals visit the region every winter.

english_meaning: The bone forming the back and lower part of the skull. The skull bone containing the large opening through which the spinal cord passes. The bone at the rear of the head that protects the back of the brain. The bone that joins the skull to the first bone of the neck.
example_sentence: The occipital bone forms the back of the skull. He struck the occipital bone when he fell backwards. The spinal cord passes through an opening in the occipital bone. Anatomy students located the occipital bone on the diagram.

english_meaning: To block, close, or stop up an opening or passage. To obstruct the flow of something such as blood, air, or light. To hide or cover something from view. To cause the upper and lower teeth to meet properly. To shut in or absorb, as gases within a solid.
example_sentence: A blood clot can occlude an artery and cause serious damage. Thick curtains occlude the sunlight from entering the room. The moon can occlude the sun during a solar eclipse. Debris began to occlude the drainage pipe.

english_meaning: The blockage or closing of a passage, opening, or vessel. The act of obstructing or blocking something, especially in the body. In medicine, the closure of a blood vessel or duct. The way the upper and lower teeth come together when the jaws are closed. The state of being hidden or covered from view.
example_sentence: The doctor discovered an occlusion in the patient's artery. Dental occlusion affects the way we chew our food. The occlusion of the pipe caused water to overflow. Cloud occlusion made the solar panels less effective.

english_meaning: A person who lives in or uses a particular property, building, seat, or position at a given time.
example_sentence: The occupant of the flat had not paid rent for three months. Emergency services helped the occupants escape the fire. The new occupant painted the house a bright white. The seat's occupant had left before the show ended.

english_meaning: To reside or have one's place of business in a building or property. To fill or take up a space or time. Also means to take control of a place, especially by military force.
example_sentence: The rebels occupied the town for several days. Reading and writing occupy most of her day. The family occupied the house for twenty years. Protesters occupied the city square for a week.

english_meaning: To happen or take place, especially as an event. To come into existence or appear. To come to mind or be thought of (used with “to”).To exist or be found in a particular place or situation.
example_sentence: The accident occurred at midnight. Changes occur slowly over time. A strange idea occurred to me during the meeting. Earthquakes can occur without warning.

english_meaning: Something that happens or takes place. An event or incident, whether ordinary or unusual. The existence or appearance of something in a particular place or situation. In science and statistics, the frequency or instance of an event happening.
example_sentence: The occurrence of earthquakes in this region is well documented. Lightning strikes are a common occurrence during monsoon season. The sudden occurrence of the disease surprised medical experts. Such an occurrence had never been recorded in the city before.

english_meaning: A very large expanse of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface. Any of the main divisions of this water, such as the Pacific or the Atlantic. Figuratively, a very large quantity or extent of something.
example_sentence: The ship sailed across the ocean for three weeks. Plastic waste is polluting the ocean. She has an ocean of patience with young children. Ocean currents strongly influence the climate.

english_meaning: The scientific study of the sea and its physical, chemical, and biological features. The branch of science dealing with oceans, currents, and marine life. Research into the structure and behaviour of the world's oceans.
example_sentence: She is studying oceanography at a coastal university. Oceanography helps us understand climate change. Modern oceanography relies heavily on satellite data. His research in oceanography won an international award.

english_meaning: A person who enjoys being in crowds or feels comfortable and happy among many people. Someone who loves crowded places, social gatherings, festivals, busy markets, concerts, or public events. Such a person gains energy, excitement, or comfort from being surrounded by many people instead of avoiding crowds.
example_sentence: Ahmed is an ochlophile who enjoys visiting crowded festivals and markets. Being an ochlophile, Sana feels more energetic in large social gatherings. The concert was perfect for an ochlophile because thousands of people attended it. Unlike his quiet brother, Ali is an ochlophile who loves busy public places.

english_meaning: A strong liking for crowds, busy places, or being surrounded by many people. The love, attraction, or comfort a person feels in crowds or highly populated environments. A person with ochlophilia enjoys social energy, public gatherings, festivals, markets, concerts, and lively places filled with people.
example_sentence: Her ochlophilia made her enjoy crowded festivals and public events. Because of his ochlophilia, he preferred busy markets over quiet places. The politician’s ochlophilia helped him feel comfortable among large audiences. People with ochlophilia often enjoy concerts, fairs, and social gatherings.

english_meaning: A person who has an extreme fear or dislike of crowds or large gatherings of people. Someone who experiences anxiety, fear, discomfort, or panic when surrounded by crowds, busy public places, or large groups of people. This fear may cause the person to avoid markets, concerts, festivals, public transport, or crowded streets.
example_sentence: The ochlophobe avoided the shopping mall during the holiday season because of the huge crowds. Being an ochlophobe, Sara felt nervous at the packed concert. The ochlophobe preferred quiet parks instead of busy public events. After experiencing panic in a crowded train station, he realized he had become an ochlophobe.

english_meaning: Fear of crowds or large groups of people. An intense fear or anxiety caused by being in crowded places or among large groups of people. A person with ochlophobia may feel nervous, unsafe, trapped, or panicked in busy markets, public gatherings, festivals, stadiums, or crowded streets.
example_sentence: She avoided concerts because of her ochlophobia. His ochlophobia made shopping malls stressful for him. During the festival, her ochlophobia caused severe anxiety. Therapy helped him control his ochlophobia over time.

english_meaning: A natural earth pigment containing clay and iron oxide, used as a paint colour. A yellowish-orange or brownish-yellow colour. Describing something of this earthy yellow-brown shade.
example_sentence: The cave paintings were made with red ochre. The desert hills glowed a warm ochre at sunset. She painted the wall in soft ochre. Ochre has been used by artists for thousands of years.

english_meaning: An eighteen-sided polygon with eighteen angles. A geometric shape with eighteen straight sides and eighteen vertices. Any flat shape with eighteen corners and eighteen edges.
example_sentence: A regular octadecagon has eighteen equal sides and angles. The architectural dome featured an octadecagonal design. Geometry enthusiasts studied the symmetry of octadecagons. The decorative tile pattern included octadecagonal shapes.

english_meaning: An eight-sided polygon with eight angles. A geometric shape with eight straight sides and eight vertices. Any flat shape with eight corners and eight edges.
example_sentence: The stop sign is a familiar example of an octagon. A regular octagon has all eight sides equal. The gazebo in the park has an octagonal roof. The table was designed with an elegant octagonal shape.

english_meaning: A liquid hydrocarbon found in petroleum, used as a measure of fuel quality. A rating that shows how well a fuel resists knocking in an engine. Figuratively, energy, power, or intensity.
example_sentence: This engine requires high octane fuel. The station sells petrol of several octane ratings. Low octane fuel can damage a modern engine. The debate was a high-octane exchange of views.

english_meaning: The interval between one musical note and another with double or half its frequency. A series of eight notes occupying that interval. The first eight lines of a sonnet. A group or stanza of eight lines. In the church calendar, the eighth day after a festival or the whole period of eight days.
example_sentence: She can sing comfortably over two octaves. The melody rises by an octave in the chorus. The octave of the sonnet sets out the theme. Church bells rang throughout the octave of Easter.

english_meaning: A book size resulting from folding a sheet of paper into eight leaves. A book or page of this size, usually about nine inches tall. Relating to books printed in this format.
example_sentence: The library holds a rare octavo edition of the poems. The volume was printed in octavo. Octavo books are easy to hold and carry. He collected octavos from the eighteenth century.

english_meaning: A group of eight people or things. A musical composition written for eight performers. An ensemble of eight singers or musicians. In poetry, the first eight lines of a sonnet. In computing, a group of eight bits.
example_sentence: A vocal octet opened the evening concert. He arranged the piece for a wind octet. Each address is stored as four octets. The octet of the sonnet introduces the problem.

english_meaning: The symbol (#). The hash sign. The pound sign on a telephone keypad. A typographical symbol consisting of two horizontal and two vertical lines crossing each other. It is the formal name for the '#' character commonly used in telephones, computers, and social media to mark numbers, tags, or commands.
example_sentence: Please press the octothorpe key after entering your account number. The octothorpe is widely known today as the hashtag symbol on social media. He explained that the # symbol is officially called an octothorpe. The octothorpe is used in programming to mark comments in some languages. Few people know that the hash sign has the formal name octothorpe.

english_meaning: Eight times as many or as much. Consisting of eight parts, members, or elements. A group or amount of eight. To make or become eight times as great or numerous.
example_sentence: The telescope contains an octuple mirror arrangement. Online orders climbed to octuple their former level. The upgrade may octuple the system's storage capacity. The dancers formed an octuple group at center stage.

english_meaning: Strange, unusual, or different from what is expected. A number that cannot be divided exactly by two. Not matching or forming a pair. Occasional or happening from time to time.
example_sentence: There was something odd about his behaviour. Three, five and seven are odd numbers. He was wearing two odd socks. She does odd jobs to earn extra money.

english_meaning: A whole number that cannot be divided exactly by two. Any integer ending in one, three, five, seven, or nine. A number that always leaves a remainder of one when divided by two.
antonyms: ["Even number","Divisible number","Paired number","Multiple of two","Balanced number"]
example_sentence: Nine is an odd number. Odd numbers cannot be split into two equal groups. Our house has an odd number on the front door. The sum of two odd numbers is always an even number.

english_meaning: A person who behaves in a strange, unusual, or eccentric manner. An individual who does not fit in with societal norms or standard expectations. Something that is peculiar, bizarre, or atypical compared to its peers. A quirky character who possesses unconventional habits or interests.
example_sentence: He was always considered an oddball because of his unusual fashion sense. The new guy in the office is a bit of an oddball, but he is very friendly. The movie features an oddball detective who solves crimes in unconventional ways. She collects vintage toasters, which makes her somewhat of an oddball in her family.

english_meaning: Extremely unpleasant. Repulsive. Hateful. Disgusting. Detestable. Deserving of hatred. Causing strong dislike or disgust. It is used to describe people, actions, behaviour, or things that are so offensive or evil that they provoke strong feelings of hatred and revulsion.
example_sentence: Slavery is one of the most odious practices in human history. He was charged with the odious crime of betraying his own country. The dictator's odious policies caused suffering to millions of people. I find his arrogant behaviour absolutely odious. Comparing the two friends in public was an odious act.

english_meaning: Widespread hatred or strong dislike directed at a person or action regarded as wrong or evil. General disgust or contempt felt towards someone. The disgrace or unpopularity resulting from a hated act. Used especially in formal contexts to describe intense public condemnation.
example_sentence: The dictator earned the odium of the entire nation. The cruel act brought lasting odium upon the perpetrators. He has suffered great odium for his unjust decisions. The traitor lived the rest of his life in odium. Their corrupt practices invited the odium of the public.

english_meaning: An instrument for measuring the distance traveled by a vehicle. A device that records the total mileage of a car. A mechanical or digital tool showing distance covered. A gauge fitted in vehicles to track journey length. Any instrument for measuring distance in motion.
example_sentence: The odometer showed that the car had done 80,000 miles. He checked the odometer before selling the car. A faulty odometer can hide a vehicle's true mileage. The mechanic reset the odometer during repairs.

english_meaning: A smell, especially one that is unpleasant. The characteristic smell that comes from a substance, place, or person. It can be neutral, pleasant, or unpleasant, though it often implies a noticeable or distinctive smell.
example_sentence: The kitchen was filled with the odor of freshly baked bread. He noticed a strange odor coming from the basement. Perfume can mask the odor of sweat. The garbage emitted a foul odor that made everyone cover their noses.

english_meaning: A smell, especially one that is unpleasant. The characteristic smell that comes from a substance, place, or person. It can be neutral, pleasant, or unpleasant, though it often implies a noticeable or distinctive smell.
example_sentence: The odour of fresh coffee filled the room. He noticed a strange odour coming from the kitchen. The garden had a sweet odour of blooming flowers. Factories can emit an unpleasant odour.

english_meaning: A long and eventful journey or experience. A series of wanderings or adventures. A lengthy adventurous voyage. A long spiritual or intellectual quest. A great Greek epic poem by Homer describing such a journey.
example_sentence: His life has been an odyssey of struggles and triumphs. The book describes an odyssey across seven countries. Their space mission was a real odyssey. Writing this novel was an emotional odyssey for her.

english_meaning: A medical condition in which excess watery fluid collects in the tissues of the body, causing swelling. Swelling of a part of the body, such as the legs or ankles, due to fluid retention. In plants, an abnormal swelling caused by excess water in the cells.
example_sentence: The doctor treated the swelling caused by oedema. Oedema in the legs can be a sign of heart trouble. She was advised to reduce salt to control her oedema. Long flights sometimes cause mild oedema in the ankles.

english_meaning: Relating to the Oedipus complex in psychoanalytic theory. Describing a child's unconscious attachment to the parent of the opposite sex. Relating to the mythological figure Oedipus or his tragic story.
example_sentence: The critic described the film's Oedipal themes. He showed strong Oedipal feelings towards his mother. The play explores an Oedipal conflict between father and son. Psychologists discussed the Oedipal stage of development.

english_meaning: A figure in Greek mythology who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother. The tragic hero of Sophocles' famous play, often used as a symbol of fate and self-discovery. A name used in psychology as the basis of the term 'Oedipus complex'.
example_sentence: The story of Oedipus is one of the greatest Greek tragedies. Oedipus discovered the terrible truth about his birth. Students read Oedipus as part of their literature course. The fate of Oedipus still fascinates modern readers.

english_meaning: In psychoanalysis, a child's unconscious feelings of desire for the parent of the opposite sex and rivalry with the parent of the same sex. A theory introduced by Sigmund Freud to explain a stage of childhood emotional development. An excessive emotional attachment of a son to his mother.
example_sentence: Freud used the Oedipus complex to explain childhood development. The novel explores the hero's Oedipus complex in detail. Some psychologists question the idea of the Oedipus complex. The therapist mentioned an unresolved Oedipus complex.

english_meaning: The scientific study of wines and winemaking. Knowledge and expertise concerning the production, ageing, and tasting of wine.
example_sentence: He studied oenology at a university in France. Oenology combines chemistry with practical craft. The course covers oenology and vineyard management. Her interest in oenology began during a trip to Italy.

english_meaning: A person who enjoys and has a deep knowledge of wines. A wine lover or connoisseur who appreciates the qualities of different wines.
example_sentence: As an oenophile, he keeps a well-stocked cellar. The oenophile described the flavour in careful detail. Only a true oenophile would notice the difference. The magazine is written mainly for the serious oenophile.

english_meaning: The muscular tube that carries food and liquid from the throat to the stomach. The part of the digestive system connecting the pharynx with the stomach, also called the gullet.
example_sentence: Food passes down the oesophagus into the stomach. The doctor examined his oesophagus with a small camera. Acid reflux can damage the lining of the oesophagus. The oesophagus is about twenty-five centimetres long in adults.

english_meaning: A group of female sex hormones that control the development and functioning of the female reproductive system. A hormone responsible for female physical characteristics and the regulation of the menstrual cycle. A substance sometimes given as medicine in hormone therapy.
example_sentence: Oestrogen levels change during different stages of life. The doctor prescribed oestrogen to relieve her symptoms. Low oestrogen can affect bone strength. Oestrogen plays a key role in the menstrual cycle.

english_meaning: The French word for egg. Egg. An egg, especially as used in cooking or on a menu. It is borrowed from French and is occasionally used in English in culinary contexts, particularly on restaurant menus that feature French dishes.
example_sentence: The menu listed oeuf en cocotte as the chef's special. She ordered an oeuf mayonnaise as a starter at the French café. In French cuisine, oeuf is used in many classic recipes. The word oeuf simply means egg in English. He learned that 'oeuf' is pronounced almost like 'uhf' in French.

english_meaning: A child or children of a person, animal, or plant. The young born to humans, animals, or plants. It can be used for a single child or multiple children. It also extends to mean descendants or the result of something, such as ideas or actions.
example_sentence: The lion protects its offspring from danger. They are proud of their offspring and their achievements. This new idea is the offspring of years of research. Many plants produce offspring through seeds.

english_meaning: Happening occasionally rather than continuously. Starting and stopping at irregular intervals. From time to time or now and then. Used to describe an action, event, or condition that occurs intermittently over a period of time.
example_sentence: It rained off and on throughout the day. They have been dating off and on for two years. I worked on the project off and on for several months. He visits his hometown off and on. The machine has been giving trouble off and on this week.

english_meaning: Slightly unwell or not feeling one's usual self. Rather rude, indecent, or in poor taste. Having lost the normal or expected colour.
example_sentence: She stayed home because she was feeling a bit off colour. He looked off colour after the long journey. The comedian told a few off colour jokes. The old curtains have gone off colour in the sunlight.

english_meaning: A day when someone performs worse than usual. A day of rest when a person does not work. A day when things generally go badly.
antonyms: ["Good day","Great day","Peak day","Working day","Productive day","Best form"]
example_sentence: Even the best players have an off day sometimes. The cook must have had an off day; the food was poor. I take Friday as my off day every week. She apologized and said it was just an off day.

english_meaning: To leave or depart very quickly and suddenly. To move away with great speed the moment something happens. To rush off immediately without delay.
example_sentence: As soon as the bell rang, the kids were off like a shot. When he saw the police, he was off like a shot. She was off like a shot to catch the last bus. The dog was off like a shot after the cat.

english_meaning: Something that is not allowed to enter, use, discuss, or touch. A place, topic, or activity that is restricted or forbidden to certain people.
example_sentence: The military base is off limits to civilians. His personal life is off limits during interviews. The construction site is off limits for safety reasons. That cupboard is off limits to children.

english_meaning: British informal expression meaning mentally unstable, crazy, or behaving very strangely. Used to describe someone whose actions or words seem completely irrational. An emphatic informal way of saying someone has lost their mind.
example_sentence: You must be off your nut to think that plan could ever work. He went completely off his nut when he heard the price of the repairs. She thought he was off his nut when he suggested quitting his job without another one lined up. The neighbours thought she was off her nut for staying in the house alone during the flood.

english_meaning: Exceptionally good, wild, exciting, or beyond expectations. Informal slang used to describe something that is extraordinary or outstanding.
example_sentence: The concert last night was totally off the chain. Her performance in the final match was off the chain. The food at that new restaurant is off the chain. The party was off the chain, everyone had an amazing time.

english_meaning: Something that is extremely high, excellent, or beyond normal limits. Much better (or sometimes worse) than expected. To describe performance, success, emotion, or quantity that exceeds usual standards.
example_sentence: Her energy level was off the charts during the event. The new movie’s popularity is off the charts, everyone’s talking about it. The temperature this summer has been off the charts. His kindness and generosity are off the charts.

english_meaning: Done or said without preparation. Something said or done spontaneously, without planning or rehearsal. It is often used for speeches, comments, or remarks that come naturally at the moment. Such actions may sound natural, honest, or sometimes unpolished.
example_sentence: He gave an off-the-cuff speech at the meeting. Don’t make off-the-cuff remarks in an interview. Her off-the-cuff comments surprised everyone. The teacher answered the question off the cuff.

english_meaning: Freed from difficulty, blame, or obligation. No longer in trouble or responsible for something.
example_sentence: The police found the real thief, so John was finally off the hook. I thought I would have to work on Sunday, but my boss said I was off the hook. She blamed herself for the mistake, but her manager told her she was off the hook. Once the project was canceled, the team was off the hook for the deadline.

english_meaning: Unusual, strange, or eccentric. Something surprising or unexpected. Very creative or unconventional. Not what people would normally think or do. Wild and imaginative in a quirky way.
example_sentence: His ideas are always a bit off the wall. She wore an off the wall outfit to the party. The movie has an off the wall sense of humor. He gave an off the wall answer to the simple question.

english_meaning: To move away from the main topic, goal, or correct direction. It is used when someone or something is no longer focused on the main subject, plan, or goal. It can describe losing direction in conversation, work, studies, or life plans.
example_sentence: We went off track during the meeting and started discussing unrelated issues. The project is off track because of poor planning. Don’t go off track while studying for your exams. His thoughts went off track during the speech.

english_meaning: Not exactly in the middle; slightly to one side. Placed or positioned away from the centre. Slightly unusual, strange, or unconventional in style or behaviour.
example_sentence: The picture is hanging slightly off-centre on the wall. The hole was drilled a little off-centre. His humour is off-centre but very clever. The table looks off-centre in this small room.

english_meaning: Not working at the present time; free from official duties. Describing a period when a worker is not required to perform their job. Relating to the behaviour or clothing of someone who is not on duty.
synonyms: ["Free","Not working","Off work","Off the clock","Resting","On leave","Away from work"]
example_sentence: The off-duty officer helped the injured driver. Nurses often meet for tea when they are off-duty. He was off-duty but came to the hospital anyway. Staff must not wear uniforms while off-duty.

english_meaning: Done or said without previous thought or preparation. In a casual or careless manner. Without warmth, politeness, or interest. Immediately, without checking or consulting anything.
example_sentence: I can't tell you the exact figure off-hand. His off-hand reply upset the customer. She spoke in an off-hand manner about the accident. He gave an off-hand answer without thinking.

english_meaning: Not allowed to enter, use, or discuss, forbidden or restricted area or topic. It describes something that people are not permitted to access or talk about.
example_sentence: The military base is off-limits to civilians. Personal questions are off-limits during the interview. This area is off-limits for safety reasons. The teacher made it clear that cheating is completely off-limits.

english_meaning: To remove a load or burden from something or someone. To take goods, weight, responsibility, or pressure away from a vehicle, place, system, or person. It can be used in physical contexts, like unloading cargo, and in abstract contexts, like transferring duties, stress, or work to others.
example_sentence: The workers off-loaded the supplies at the warehouse. The truck must off-load its cargo before entering the city. She off-loaded some of her tasks to her assistant. The company decided to off-load excess stock at a discount.

english_meaning: A road that allows vehicles to leave a highway, motorway, or expressway. A way to leave a difficult situation. A safe exit from a plan, conflict, or process. A practical option to step away from something. A short connecting road used to exit from a main high speed road such as a highway or freeway. It leads drivers away from the main road toward another road, street, city area, or destination.
synonyms: ["Exit ramp","Exit road","Slip road","Turnoff","Highway exit","Escape route","Way out","Exit strategy","Alternative path"]
antonyms: ["On-ramp","Entrance ramp","Entry road","Dead end","Trap","Point of no return"]
example_sentence: Take the off-ramp to reach the city center. We missed the off-ramp and had to drive several more miles. The new off-ramp has reduced traffic near the highway exit. The agreement provided a political off-ramp for both sides.

english_meaning: A period of the year when a particular activity, especially sport or tourism, is not taking place or is at a reduced level. It refers to the time when business or recreational activity is at a low ebb.
example_sentence: Hotels offer significant discounts during the off-season. Athletes usually focus on recovery during the off-season. Visiting popular tourist spots in the off-season allows you to avoid crowds. The local economy slows down considerably during the off-season.

english_meaning: Describing a running play in American football that goes just outside the offensive tackle. Relating to the area of the line next to the tackle position through which the ball carrier runs. Used of a rushing attack aimed at the gap between the tackle and the end. A play designed to gain yards by attacking that particular part of the line.
synonyms: ["Inside run","Rushing play","Ground play","Line play","Power run","Dive play","Attacking run","Offensive play"]
example_sentence: The coach called an off-tackle run on third down. He gained twelve yards on a simple off-tackle play. Their off-tackle attack wore down the tired defence. The team practised off-tackle runs all week before the game.

english_meaning: A white colour with a slight tinge of grey, cream, or yellow. Describing paint, fabric, or paper that is not pure white. A soft neutral shade often used in interior decoration.
example_sentence: The walls were painted a warm off-white. She wore an off-white blouse with grey trousers. Off-white curtains soften the light in the room. The invitation was printed on off-white card.

english_meaning: Unconventional or unusual in style, character, or appearance. Not following traditional or popular norms. Relating to an unaccented beat in music. Eccentric and strangely appealing. Out of the ordinary or quirky. Differing from the standard expectation.
example_sentence: The director is known for his offbeat sense of humor that appeals to a niche audience. She chose an offbeat wedding dress that featured bright colors instead of traditional white. The band experiment with offbeat rhythms that create a unique and complex sound. He has an offbeat way of looking at the world that always sparks interesting conversations.

english_meaning: A piece of material left over after the main part has been cut. A remaining scrap of wood, cloth, paper, or metal. A small leftover piece that is often sold cheaply or thrown away.
example_sentence: The carpenter used an offcut to repair the small shelf. You can buy cheap offcuts of carpet at the shop. She made a photo frame from a wooden offcut. Offcuts of fabric were collected for a quilt.

english_meaning: A breach of a law or rule; an illegal act. A crime or violation of legal or moral standards. Something that causes hurt feelings, anger, displeasure, or resentment in another person. The act of attacking or being on the attacking side in a conflict, game, or sport. Any action that offends someone or breaks accepted norms of behaviour, conduct, or law.
example_sentence: Driving without a licence is a serious offence in this country. He apologised at once so as not to cause any offence. The minister resigned after being charged with a criminal offence. She took offence at his careless remark about her work. Our team has a strong offence but a weak defence.

english_meaning: To make feel upset, To seem unpleasant, To commit crime, To be against what people believe is morally right
example_sentence: They will be offended if you don't go to their wedding. Neil did not mean to offend anybody with his joke. Please do not be offended for this message that comes from me.

english_meaning: Causing someone to feel hurt, angry, or upset. Extremely unpleasant to the senses. Relating to or used for attack rather than defence. An attacking military campaign or a strong organised effort.
example_sentence: His offensive remarks upset the whole gathering. An offensive smell came from the drain. The army launched an offensive at dawn. The company began a major offensive against counterfeit products.

english_meaning: Something presented as a gift, especially to a god or in a religious ceremony. A product or service made available to the public. Money contributed during a religious service. The act of presenting something for acceptance or use.
example_sentence: Villagers placed flowers and fruit as an offering at the shrine. The bakery's latest offering is a honey walnut loaf. The congregation made a generous offering for the flood victims. Their new offering includes both software and support.

english_meaning: Assertive of authority in an annoyingly domineering way. Overly eager to offer unwanted help, advice, or services. Interfering in matters that do not concern one. Meddlesome and intrusive in behavior. Excessively forward in offering unrequested assistance.
example_sentence: The officious clerk kept correcting everyone's paperwork. She grew tired of her officious neighbor's constant advice. An officious guard stopped us at every checkpoint. His officious manner annoyed the whole team.

english_meaning: Something that is likely to happen soon or a distant sea view. Offing refers to something that is approaching or expected in the near future. It is also used in maritime language to mean the open sea visible from the shore but still at a distance
example_sentence: A major policy change is in the offing. Dark clouds in the offing warned of a storm. The ship waited in the offing before entering the harbor. With exams in the offing, students started preparing seriously.

english_meaning: To balance or counter the effect of something. To reduce or neutralize the effect of a cost, loss, or negative impact by an equal or opposite action. To make something stand out by contrasting it with another element. To move or position something slightly away from a main line or center Something that compensates for a loss, disadvantage, or negative effect (A balancing factor). A small distance or shift from a main position. A credit used to reduce a debt or cost. A printing method where ink is transferred from a plate to a surface.
example_sentence: Higher profits offset the increase in production costs. Overtime pay helped offset monthly expenses. Salary benefits are an offset to long working hours. The discount served as an offset to the delay. There is a slight offset between the two lines. Tax offsets reduced the payable amount. The book was produced using offset printing. Job security is an offset to lower pay. Higher income can offset rising living costs. The designer offset the image to the left. Dark walls offset the bright furniture.

english_meaning: A branch that grows from the main stem of a plant. Something that develops from something larger or earlier. A subsidiary or derivative of something. A side branch. A descendant or member of a family branch. It is used both literally for a side branch of a plant and figuratively for a group, organization, or idea that has developed from a larger original one.
example_sentence: The new company is an offshoot of a much larger international corporation. Jazz is considered an offshoot of African American musical traditions. The gardener cut away the small offshoots from the main branch. This research project is an offshoot of our earlier study on climate change. The political party began as an offshoot of a larger reform movement.

english_meaning: Located at sea or outside the main land area, often used for activities done abroad. Something situated away from the coast or outside a country, especially across the sea. It is commonly used for oil drilling, wind farms, banking, companies, or jobs that are based in another country to reduce costs or manage operations internationally.
example_sentence: The company moved its customer service to an offshore location. Offshore drilling plays a major role in energy production. Many firms use offshore banking for financial management. The government approved a new offshore wind project.

english_meaning: Frequently or many times. Happening on numerous occasions. In many instances or cases. Regularly and repeatedly. On a recurring basis.
example_sentence: He often visits his grandparents. It often rains in July. She often forgets her keys. We often go to the beach on weekends.

english_meaning: A green finger-shaped vegetable with ridged skin and small seeds inside. A vegetable that becomes slightly sticky when cooked. The plant that produces these pods. A common ingredient in curries, stews, and stir-fries.
example_sentence: Fried okra is a favourite dish in our home. Okra grows well in hot, dry weather. She washed and dried the okra before cutting it. The curry thickened because of the okra.

english_meaning: A naturally occurring mixture of oil and resin obtained from various plants, used in food flavouring, medicine, and industrial applications. A solution of resin in an essential oil found naturally in plants such as pine, turpentine, and certain spices. A semi-solid substance extracted from plants that contains both volatile and fixed components.
example_sentence: Oleoresin extracted from capsicum peppers is used to produce pepper spray. Pine oleoresin is collected by tapping the bark of certain pine trees. The oleoresin of black pepper provides its distinctive sharp and pungent flavour. Industrial oleoresin is used in the manufacture of adhesives and coatings. The food scientist used oleoresin of turmeric as a natural colouring agent.

english_meaning: A very rich and powerful person who is part of a small group controlling a country or organization.
example_sentence: After the fall of the Soviet Union, several oligarchs gained control over major industries. The country's policies often favor a small group of oligarchs rather than ordinary citizens. Many believe that the media is controlled by a few wealthy oligarchs. The government tried to limit the influence of business oligarchs in politics.

english_meaning: A system of government in which power is held by a small group of people.
example_sentence: The country was ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen. Critics accused the government of turning into an oligarchy controlled by a few elites. Ancient Sparta is often cited as an example of an oligarchy. In an oligarchy, common citizens rarely influence major political decisions.

english_meaning: A symbol or action showing a desire for peace or reconciliation. A peaceful gesture made to end conflict, repair relationships, or reduce hostility between individuals, groups, or nations. It comes from ancient traditions where the olive tree symbolized peace and goodwill. When someone offers an olive branch, they are trying to settle differences and move forward calmly.
example_sentence: After years of dispute, the manager extended an olive branch to the workers. The country sent an olive branch to its neighbor to ease tensions. She offered an olive branch by apologizing for her harsh words. Dialogue was used as an olive branch to rebuild trust between the groups.

english_meaning: An event or phenomenon regarded as a portent of good or evil. A sign or warning indicating a future event or outcome. A prophetic significance attached to a particular occurrence.
example_sentence: The sudden storm was interpreted by the villagers as an ill omen. Many cultures view the appearance of a raven as a dark omen. Finding a four-leaf clover is widely regarded as a lucky omen. Her warm smile seemed like a good omen for the upcoming negotiations.

english_meaning: A fold of peritoneum connecting the stomach with other abdominal organs. It acts as an insulating layer of fat and plays a vital role in immune defense within the abdomen. It helps isolate and wrap around localized infections inside the peritoneal cavity. It consists primarily of two distinct structures known as the greater omentum and the lesser omentum.
synonyms: ["Epiploon","Peritoneal fold","Abdominal membrane","Fatty apron","Visceral membrane","Peritoneal tissue","Abdominal fold","Mesenteric fold","Intestinal apron","Internal peritoneal membrane"]
example_sentence: The surgeon carefully lifted the greater omentum to expose the stomach. The omentum plays a crucial role in limiting the spread of intra-abdominal infections. Fat accumulation in the omentum contributes significantly to central obesity. A biopsy of the omentum revealed localized tissue inflammation.

english_meaning: Giving a feeling that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen. Suggesting or foreshadowing danger, trouble, or disaster; indicating that something threatening or unfavorable is likely in the future
example_sentence: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm. His silence was ominous, hinting at bad news. The eerie music created an ominous atmosphere in the old house. The sudden drop in sales is an ominous sign for the company.

english_meaning: The act of leaving someone or something out. Something that has been left out or excluded. A failure to do something that should have been done. Neglect of duty. In law, a failure to act that results in harm.
example_sentence: The omission of her name from the list upset her. There were several omissions in the final report. His failure to warn us was a serious omission. Sins of omission can be as harmful as sins of commission.

english_meaning: To leave out or exclude something, either accidentally or deliberately. To fail to include or mention something that should be present.
example_sentence: She accidentally omitted her phone number on the form. He deliberately omitted the most important detail from his report. Don't omit the safety steps when assembling the equipment. The editor omitted three paragraphs from the final article.

english_meaning: Having unlimited power and authority, able to do anything. Often used for God,  Allah in religious contexts. Having total power, able to do anything.
example_sentence: God is omnipotent and controls the entire universe. How can a loving, omnipotent God permit disease, war and suffering?

english_meaning: Present everywhere at the same time. Being present everywhere at once. It is often used for God, power, influence, nature, technology, fear, media, or something that seems to exist in all places.
example_sentence: The influence of the internet is omnipresent in modern life. In many religions, God is believed to be omnipresent. During the election season, political posters became omnipresent across the city. A feeling of fear was omnipresent after the shocking news.

english_meaning: Having complete or unlimited knowledge, awareness, or understanding. Knowing everything, past, present, and future. All-knowing, especially used as an attribute of God. A narrator in literature who knows all characters' thoughts and actions.
example_sentence: God is often described as omniscient and all-powerful. The novel is written from an omniscient point of view. No human being can be truly omniscient. The omniscient narrator revealed the thoughts of every character.

english_meaning: Something that is not restricted to a particular gender. It can refer to clothing, roles, or activities that are meant for people of any sex. It emphasizes inclusivity and neutrality regarding gender.
example_sentence: This jacket is omnisex and can be worn by anyone. The event is omnisex, welcoming all genders. She prefers omnisex clothing for comfort. Omnisex toys are designed for everyone.

english_meaning: A person who experiences sexual attraction to individuals of all gender identities, but the attraction may be influenced by gender rather than being completely indifferent to it
example_sentence: Alex identifies as omnisexual and enjoys dating people of all genders. She came out as omnisexual in college and felt more authentic. Being omnisexual means acknowledging attraction without strict gender limits. Omnisexual people may experience different levels of attraction to different genders.

english_meaning: An animal or person that eats both plants and meat. A living being that consumes and can digest both plant based food and animal based food.
example_sentence: Humans are natural omnivores because they eat both vegetables and meat. A bear is an omnivore that feeds on fish, berries, and insects. As an omnivore, she enjoys trying all kinds of dishes.

english_meaning: The study of the navel, or belly button. A branch of anatomy dealing with the umbilicus and its structure. The scientific examination of the navel and its medical significance.
example_sentence: Omphalology sounds unusual, but it has real medical uses. A specialist in omphalology explained the causes of navel infections. The museum exhibit included a light-hearted section on omphalology. Omphalology examines how the navel forms after birth.

english_meaning: Doing something with very little money or resources. Managing or accomplishing a task, project, or lifestyle while having a very limited budget. It emphasizes frugality, careful spending, or minimal financial resources.
example_sentence: She traveled across Europe on a shoestring, staying in hostels. The startup grew on a shoestring budget but still made an impact. He managed to throw a wedding on a shoestring and still made it beautiful. They ran the charity project on a shoestring, relying mostly on volunteers.

english_meaning: Doing something suddenly without planning or serious thought. Acting on a sudden desire or impulse. Following a spontaneous idea without any specific reason. Making a decision based on a passing thought. Doing something purely for fun or a momentary wish.
example_sentence: She bought the dress on a whim without checking the price. On a whim, they decided to travel to the mountains. He quit his job on a whim and regretted it later. I made the cake on a whim just to try the recipe.

english_meaning: From every side or direction. By everyone or from all people. Universally acknowledged or agreed upon. From all quarters or sources. Used to indicate that something is admitted, accepted, or experienced by all parties involved.
example_sentence: It is admitted on all hands that he is the best player in the team. On all hands, people praised her courage and honesty. The proposal was welcomed on all hands by the members. On all hands, the city was surrounded by mountains. His leadership is appreciated on all hands.

english_meaning: Occurring at irregular intervals rather than continuously. Starting, stopping, and starting again over a period of time. Intermittently or from time to time. Used to describe relationships, weather, conditions, or activities that happen with breaks in between.
example_sentence: It snowed on and off all night. They have been friends on and off for many years. He has been studying medicine on and off due to financial issues. The fan keeps working on and off. I have known him on and off since college.

english_meaning: After considering all the facts and arguments; overall. Taking everything into account; all things considered. When the advantages and disadvantages are weighed together.
synonyms: ["Overall","All things considered","On the whole","By and large","Taking everything into account"]
example_sentence: On balance, the new policy has been a success. The trip was tiring, but on balance, it was worth it. On balance, I think we should accept their offer. The report concluded that, on balance, the benefits outweigh the risks.

english_meaning: On or in a ship, an aircraft or a train. In support of a particular objective. To accept and understand an idea or a suggestion. Giving your support to an idea or a project. Present and functioning as a member of a team or organization. As part of a group or team, especially for a special purpose. Being in agreement, supportive, or part of a team, plan.
example_sentence: Have the passengers gone on board yet? Needed to get more senators on board for the bill to pass. I told her what I thought, but she didn't take my advice on board. We must get more sponsors on board. You need to bring the whole staff on board. It’s good to have you on board (= working with us) for this project. Let's bring Rob on board for the Saudi deal - he's the expert. Is that new teammate properly on board yet?

english_meaning: Extremely happy. To feel very happy, as if floating in the clouds with joy.
example_sentence: She’s on cloud nine after the promotion. She’s on cloud nine after success. She was on cloud nine after getting the job she always wanted. When their team won the championship, the fans were on cloud nine. He felt on cloud nine when he became a father for the first time. After receiving her award, she was on cloud nine for days.

english_meaning: Feeling extremely happy, joyful, or delighted. It describes a person who is so pleased or excited that they feel as if they are floating in the clouds.
example_sentence: She was on cloud seven after hearing about her promotion. He felt on cloud seven when he passed his final exams. They were on cloud seven after their wedding ceremony. I was on cloud seven when I received my first salary.

english_meaning: Not understanding each other. two or more people are not thinking the same way, not understanding each other, or having different ideas, opinions, or communication styles.
example_sentence: The two colleagues are on different wavelengths. They are on different wavelengths, so they argue often. I tried to explain, but we were just on different wavelengths.

english_meaning: Perfect, stylish, or flawless. Something that is perfectly done, extremely attractive, stylish, or flawless in appearance or performance.
example_sentence: Her makeup is on fleek today. His speech was on fleek; everyone loved it. The decorations are on fleek for the party. Your handwriting is totally on fleek.

english_meaning: Available or ready for use. Present and available when needed. Close by or ready for use. Nearby or within reach. In someone’s possession at the moment.
example_sentence: I always keep some cash on hand for emergencies. The doctor is on hand if anyone needs help. We have enough food on hand for the whole week. The manager was on hand to welcome the new staff.

english_meaning: Operating under direct human control rather than automatically. In a mode where a person must adjust or operate the system.
example_sentence: The camera is on manual, so I must set the focus. Put the machine on manual before making adjustments. The pilot switched the controls on manual. The heater is on manual until the sensor is repaired.

english_meaning: Extremely tired, weak, or close to failing. About to break down or stop working. In a state of near collapse. Nearly at the end of usefulness or life. Barely able to continue.
example_sentence: After the long trip, he was on his last legs. This old car is on its last legs. The company appears to be on its last legs. She looked on her last legs after the double shift.

english_meaning: In a state of anxious anticipation. Feeling extremely nervous or worried. Waiting eagerly and restlessly for something. In suspense about an outcome. Unable to relax due to worry.
example_sentence: She was on pins and needles waiting for the results. He sat on pins and needles during the interview. The parents were on pins and needles until their son called. I was on pins and needles before the announcement.

english_meaning: To be alert, aware, and quick to respond, to be efficient and focused.
example_sentence: She’s really on the ball with her work. You need to stay on the ball to meet the deadline. He’s always on the ball during meetings. Our teacher is very much on the ball.

english_meaning: Free of charge, provided or given without payment by the owner of a business.
example_sentence: Drinks are on the house tonight. The waiter told us that the dessert was on the house. Drinks were on the house to celebrate the restaurant’s anniversary. The hotel offered breakfast on the house to all guests. After the complaint, the manager made our meal on the house.

english_meaning: Aware of the latest developments or trends. When someone is on the pulse, they stay closely informed about current events, changes, or trends in a particular field, society, or situation. It suggests alertness, awareness, and the ability to respond quickly to new information.
example_sentence: A good journalist is always on the pulse of current events. She stays on the pulse of fashion trends through social media. The manager is on the pulse of the market and reacts quickly. Teachers should remain on the pulse of new teaching methods.

english_meaning: Facing difficulty, likely to fail or break down. A beverage served over ice cubes. Used when something important like a relationship, plan, or business is not going well and may collapse soon. Common in restaurants or bars, especially for juices or soft drinks and other beverages, meaning poured over ice.
example_sentence: Their marriage is on the rocks after constant arguments. The company is on the rocks due to financial losses. He ordered lemon soda on the rocks to cool down. Their friendship went on the rocks after a misunderstanding.

english_meaning: To have the same understanding, agreement, or point of view about something. To share the same knowledge, plan, or expectations in a discussion or project.
example_sentence: The team is finally on the same page. Before we start the project, let’s make sure we are on the same page. The manager and the team are on the same page about the deadlines.

english_meaning: To understand and agree with someone easily because you share similar thoughts, ideas, or feelings. When two or more people think alike or communicate effortlessly.
synonyms: ["In tune","Like-minded","In harmony","In sync","Thinking alike","On the same page"]
antonyms: ["Out of sync","At odds","In disagreement","On different pages","Conflicted"]
example_sentence: My best friend and I are always on the same wavelength; we rarely disagree. The manager and his team were on the same wavelength during the project. It’s easy to work with her because we’re on the same wavelength. They understood each other perfectly, as if they were on the same wavelength.

english_meaning: In a risky or delicate situation. Doing something that could easily cause trouble. Close to failure or disapproval. In a position where one mistake may be costly.
example_sentence: After arriving late again, he is on the thin ice with his boss. You are on the thin ice if you ignore the rules. The company is on the thin ice financially this year. She knew she was on the thin ice during the interview.

english_meaning: Very close to doing or experiencing something. About to happen at any moment. At the point where something is about to begin. In a state near an event, action, or emotion. Just about to reach a particular condition.
synonyms: ["About to","Close to","Near","On the brink of","On the edge of","On the point of","Nearing"]
example_sentence: She was on the verge of tears when she heard the news. The company is on the verge of bankruptcy. He was on the verge of quitting his job. They are on the verge of a major discovery.

english_meaning: Gradually decreasing in strength, size, importance, or popularity. Becoming smaller, weaker, or less noticeable. Used to describe something that is slowly fading away. Declining after having been strong or popular. In a state of decline or reduction.
example_sentence: His popularity is on the wane after the recent scandal. The influence of the old empire was on the wane. Interest in the show is clearly on the wane. Her health has been on the wane for months.

english_meaning: To be in a risky, dangerous, or uncertain situation, especially one where a single mistake could lead to trouble or failure. It often refers to being in a sensitive position, where one must be very careful with actions or words.
synonyms: ["Walking a tightrope","In hot water","In jeopardy","On the edge"]
antonyms: ["Safe and sound","Secure","Out of danger","In a stable position","Comfortable"]
example_sentence: You’re on thin ice with your boss. He’s on thin ice with his boss after missing two deadlines. You’re already on thin ice, don’t argue with her again!. The company is on thin ice financially after several bad investments. She knew she was on thin ice when she arrived late to the meeting again.

english_meaning: Standing or walking on the front part of your feet (toes), often to move quietly or to reach higher. Figuratively, it can mean being in a state of eager or nervous expectation.
example_sentence:
She had to stand on tiptoe to reach the top shelf.
We crept around on tiptoes so as not to disturb him. She stood on tiptoe to reach the top shelf. The children were on tiptoe with excitement before the show began.

english_meaning: Be cautious after bad experience. If something hurt you once, you’ll be cautious the next time. (When someone has had a bad or unpleasant experience once, they become more careful or afraid to do the same thing again.)
example_sentence: After his business failed once, he never tried to start another, once bitten, twice shy. She doesn’t trust easily anymore; once bitten, twice shy. He lent money to a friend who never paid him back, so now he refuses to lend again, once bitten, twice shy. After being cheated in love, she avoids relationships, once bitten, twice shy.

english_meaning: Something that happens very rarely or almost never. It refers to an event that is unusual or uncommon. An event or action that occurs after a long time or only on rare occasions.
example_sentence: We meet once in a blue moon. He visits his hometown once in a blue moon. I eat fast food only once in a blue moon. We go on vacation together once in a blue moon. She calls me once in a blue moon, only when she needs help.

english_meaning: A phrase used to introduce a story or a fable. Occurring at an unspecified time in the past. Used to indicate that a situation existed long ago but no longer does. A conventional opening for a fairy tale or narrative.
synonyms: ["Long ago","Formerly","In days of yore","In the past","Once","Anciently","Time was","Back then","Historically","Aforetime","Erstwhile","Of old"]
example_sentence: Once upon a time, there lived a brave knight in a distant kingdom. Once upon a time, this busy street was just a quiet dirt road. Every child loves a story that begins with once upon a time. Once upon a time, we were the best of friends.

english_meaning: A doctor who treats cancer. A medical specialist trained in diagnosing, treating, and managing cancer. This includes planning therapies, monitoring patients, and providing guidance during cancer care.
antonyms: ["General physician","Non specialist doctor","Surgeon without cancer specialty","Physician with no oncology training"]
example_sentence: The oncologist recommended starting chemotherapy immediately. She visited an oncologist after her test results showed abnormal growth. The hospital hired a new pediatric oncologist to treat children with cancer. His oncologist explained all possible treatment options with patience.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine that deals with the study, diagnosis and treatment of cancer. A medical field focused on understanding how cancer develops, how it can be detected, how it progresses in the body and how it can be treated through methods like chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and surgery. It includes prevention, early detection, patient care and long term follow up.
synonyms: ["Cancer medicine","Cancer treatment field","Tumor science","Medical specialty for cancer"]
example_sentence: She decided to specialize in oncology after completing medical school. Advances in oncology have improved survival rates for many cancer patients. The hospital opened a new oncology ward for specialized treatment. Oncology research focuses on finding safer and more effective therapies.

word: One bad apple spoils the whole barrel
english_meaning: One bad person or thing can negatively affect the whole group. The harmful behavior or influence of a single individual can ruin a larger group, project, or situation. It is often used in social, organizational, or moral contexts.
example_sentence: The manager warned that one bad apple in the team could lower morale. They removed the dishonest employee because one bad apple spoils the whole barrel. In schools, bullying by one student can affect the whole class environment. A single corrupt official can disrupt the integrity of an entire department.

english_meaning: A very short time feels extremely long because of deep longing or emotional distance. This classical Chinese idiom expresses intense emotional waiting. It suggests that separation, love, or anxiety can make a single day feel as long as three years.
synonyms: ["A watched pot never boils","Time drags on","Endless waiting","Painful longing"]
antonyms: ["Time flies","In the blink of an eye","Fleeting moment","Swift passage of time"]
example_sentence: While waiting for news from his family abroad, one day felt like three autumns to him. During their long separation, every silent evening became one day, three autumns. The prisoner said that life in the cell was one day, three autumns without hope. For her, waiting for his return was truly one day, three autumns.

word: One who can't be advised can also not be helped
english_meaning: A person who refuses to listen to advice cannot be helped or saved from problems. (This saying teaches that guidance and help are connected. If someone ignores good advice, even the best efforts to help them will fail. Wisdom and success depend on being open to suggestions and learning from others.)
example_sentence: I warned him not to trust that man, but he ignored me. One who can’t be advised can also not be helped. She keeps making the same mistake even after everyone tells her. Truly, one who can’t be advised can also not be helped. If you refuse to take advice, you’ll face the results alone. One who can’t be advised can also not be helped. He lost his job because he didn’t listen to anyone. One who can’t be advised can also not be helped.

word: One who can’t be advised cannot be helped
english_meaning: A person who refuses guidance cannot be supported or rescued from their problems.
synonyms: ["A stubborn person cannot be guided","Refusing advice blocks solutions"]
antonyms: ["A teachable person can be guided","Willing learners improve easily"]
example_sentence: You warned him many times but he ignored everything. One who can’t be advised cannot be helped. She keeps repeating the same mistakes because she refuses guidance. One who can’t be advised cannot be helped. The coach tried to correct his attitude but he would not listen. One who can’t be advised cannot be helped. They could have avoided trouble if they had accepted advice. One who can’t be advised cannot be helped.

english_meaning: A situation where someone's chances of success are completely ruined. The moment when someone is caught doing something wrong and faces inevitable punishment.
synonyms: ["Finished","Done For","In Deep Trouble","Ruined","Caught Red-Handed","Doomed","In Hot Water","Up The Creek","Out Of Luck","Screwed"]
antonyms: ["In The Clear","Out Of The Woods","Safe And Sound","Off The Hook","Vindicated","Successful","Triumphant","Rescued","Saved","Secure"]
example_sentence: When the boss found out about the embezzled funds, he knew his goose was cooked. If we don't finish this project by tomorrow morning, our goose is cooked. The criminal realized his goose was cooked when the police surrounded the building. She lied about her qualifications, and when they checked her references, her goose was cooked.

english_meaning: Always thinking about the same thing. A person who is so focused on one idea, interest, or goal that they think or talk about almost nothing else. Such a person finds it hard to switch topics or consider other viewpoints.
example_sentence: He's got a one-track mind, everything comes back to football. He’s got a one-track mind; all he ever talks about is cricket. Don’t bother discussing travel with her, she’s got a one-track mind for her career. With his one-track mind, he ignored everything except his business. She has a one-track mind when it comes to fashion.

english_meaning: The scientific study of dreams. Research into the nature, causes, and meaning of dreaming. A branch of psychology and sleep science concerned with dream activity.
example_sentence: Oneirology studies what happens in the brain during dreams. Modern oneirology relies on sleep laboratories and brain scans. She turned to oneirology to understand her recurring nightmares. Oneirology is often confused with dream interpretation.

english_meaning: Involving a great amount of effort, difficulty, or responsibility. Burdensome, troublesome, or oppressive. Describing a task, duty, or condition that is heavy and hard to bear. The word is formal and often used in legal, professional, or moral contexts.
example_sentence: The new manager found his duties extremely onerous. The contract included several onerous conditions. Looking after a large family is an onerous responsibility. He was relieved of his onerous tasks after the reform. Paying back the loan became an onerous burden.

english_meaning: An uncontrollable urge to buy things. A compulsive shopping disorder in which a person cannot stop spending. An excessive obsession with purchasing goods, often unnecessary ones. A mental condition where buying provides temporary relief from stress. Addiction to shopping that leads to financial trouble.
example_sentence: Her oniomania left her deep in credit card debt. Online sales can make oniomania much worse. He sought therapy for oniomania after losing his savings. Oniomania is often linked with anxiety and depression.

english_meaning: A swollen edible bulb used as a vegetable, having a pungent taste and smell. It consists of several fleshy layers covered by a papery skin. The plant is widely cultivated worldwide for its culinary versatility. It is known to cause watering of the eyes when chopped.
example_sentence: She chopped a large onion for the curry. The smell of frying onion and garlic filled the kitchen. He likes a slice of raw onion on his burger. The recipe calls for one finely diced red onion.

english_meaning: A word that imitates a sound. The fact of words containing sounds similar to the noises they describe, for example hiss; the use of words like this in a piece of writing. The use of words whose sound suggests the sense.
example_sentence: The percentages of each lexical class (including exclamations and onomatopoeia) across the three age groups were calculated. In the rest of the chapter, he discusses the processes of reduplication and onomatopoeia. The male singer has a delivery which makes use of words and onomatopoeia with mischievouness and joviality.

english_meaning: The beginning or start of something, especially something unpleasant. A powerful attack or assault. The early stage of an illness or condition. The initial appearance of a situation or event.
example_sentence: The onset of winter brought heavy snowfall to the region. Doctors were able to detect the onset of the disease early. The onset of the storm forced people to stay indoors. The onset of the battle was sudden and unexpected.

english_meaning: Located on or moving toward the land from the sea. Something that is situated on land rather than at sea, or something that moves from the sea toward the land. It is commonly used in geography, wind patterns, marine activities, oil and gas exploration, and business contexts such as onshore services.
example_sentence: The fishermen returned to the onshore village before sunset. Onshore winds brought cooler air to the coastal town. The company decided to keep its customer support onshore. Onshore oil drilling is often cheaper than offshore drilling.

english_meaning: A violent attack, strong criticism, or sudden forceful action. A fierce attack, an aggressive action, or a powerful wave of something harmful or forceful. It can be used for physical attacks, verbal criticism, emotional pressure, or even natural disasters.
example_sentence: The army launched a massive onslaught against the enemy camp. The company faced an onslaught of criticism after the product failed. Villages suffered an onslaught of heavy rain during the storm. She could not handle the emotional onslaught caused by constant pressure.

english_meaning: Relating to the philosophical study of the nature of being, existence, or reality. Concerned with what exists and the categories of being. Pertaining to ontology as a branch of metaphysics. Used in philosophical, theological, and scientific discussions about the fundamental nature of things.
example_sentence: The book deals with ontological questions about human existence. Philosophers have long debated the ontological status of numbers. His argument is based on an ontological assumption about reality. The ontological proof of God's existence is a famous philosophical concept. The thesis examines the ontological nature of consciousness.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to being, existence, or the nature of reality. From the perspective of ontology. With regard to the categories and relationships of things that exist. In computing, according to a formal representation of concepts and their relations.
example_sentence: The theory treats mind and body as ontologically distinct. These objects are ontologically dependent on social agreement. The categories are ontologically related within the model. Ontologically, the argument assumes that numbers exist independently.

english_meaning: The branch of philosophy that studies the nature of being, existence, and reality. The systematic study of what exists and how things can be categorized. In computer science, a formal representation of knowledge through a set of concepts and the relationships between them. A theory concerning the fundamental categories of reality.
example_sentence: Aristotle's writings laid the foundation for modern ontology. Ontology asks what it means for something to exist. The course covers both metaphysics and ontology in detail. In artificial intelligence, ontology helps machines understand information. His research focuses on the ontology of social institutions.

english_meaning: A duty or responsibility. The burden of proving, explaining, or accomplishing something. An obligation placed on a particular person or group.
example_sentence: The onus is on the applicant to provide accurate documents. In court, the onus of proof lies with the prosecution. Parents should not place the entire onus on teachers. The new policy puts the onus on companies to protect customer data. He accepted the onus of resolving the dispute.

english_meaning: Moving forward and making progress toward success or improvement.
example_sentence: Despite challenges, it’s onward and upwards for us. She left the job, but it’s onward and upwards now. The company is moving onward and upwards. Onward and upwards—never look back.

english_meaning: The habit of biting one's nails. A nervous or compulsive behaviour involving nail-biting. A recognised condition often linked with anxiety or stress.
example_sentence: The child was treated for onychophagia by a psychologist. Onychophagia often begins in early childhood. Stress at work worsened his onychophagia. Doctors link onychophagia with anxiety disorders.

english_meaning: The study of birds' eggs. A branch of ornithology dealing with the size, shape, colour, and structure of eggs. The practice of collecting and describing birds' eggs for scientific purposes.
example_sentence: Oology helps scientists identify birds by their eggs. Victorian collectors made oology a popular hobby. The museum holds an important oology collection. Modern oology relies on photographs rather than collecting eggs.

english_meaning: To flow forth slowly through small openings. To move slowly. Soft wet earth. very soft mud, especially at the bottom of a lake or river.
example_sentence: Blood oozed out of wound. His voice oozed with sex appeal. She walked into the party oozing confidence. Thick mud began to ooze from the riverbank after the rain. Blood was oozing from the small cut on his hand. Oil continued to ooze out of the damaged pipe. She oozes confidence during public speaking.
