english_meaning: In an exceptionally good manner. To a degree that clearly surpasses others. Remarkably or strikingly well. Used to emphasise an unusually high standard.
example_sentence: The students performed outstandingly in the national examination. She is outstandingly talented at mathematics. The hotel was outstandingly clean and well managed. He handled the crisis outstandingly well.

english_meaning: A branch or post located far from the main headquarters. A remote place where an official or worker is posted. In Australia, a small settlement away from a main community. Relating to duty or travel outside one's usual station.
example_sentence: He was posted to a remote outstation for two years. Supplies reach the outstation only once a month. The company runs three outstations along the coast. She is on outstation duty until the end of the month.

english_meaning: To stay longer than expected, required, or welcome. To remain beyond a specific duration or time limit.
example_sentence: They did not want to outstay their welcome at the host's house. It is unwise to outstay your visa in a foreign country. The guest decided to leave early so as not to outstay his invitation. She realized she had outstayed her time and quickly apologized.

english_meaning: To go faster than or beyond someone or something. To exceed or surpass in performance, quantity, or degree. To leave behind in a race or competition.
example_sentence: Demand has outstripped supply in the housing market. She outstripped her rivals in the final lap. His achievements outstripped everyone's expectations. Modern technology has outstripped old methods.

english_meaning: To be greater in weight, value, importance, or influence than something else. To exceed in significance or effect.
example_sentence: The benefits of this plan outweigh the risks. Her achievements far outweigh her mistakes. Practical experience often outweighs theoretical knowledge. The advantages outweigh the disadvantages in this case. Duty outweighed his personal wishes.

english_meaning: To defeat or get the better of someone by using cleverness or intelligence. To gain an advantage over someone by being more clever, cunning, or strategic.
example_sentence: She managed to outwit her opponents in the debate. The fox outwitted the hunters and escaped. He tried to cheat, but she outwitted him. In the game of chess, he always finds a way to outwit his rivals.

english_meaning: A rounded elongated shape like an egg. An ellipse-like figure that is not perfectly circular. A shape that is longer in one direction than the other. An egg-shaped or elliptical form.
example_sentence: The mirror is oval in shape. She has an oval face. The Oval Office is the president's workspace. The track has an oval layout.

english_meaning: One of the two female reproductive organs located in the pelvis. The female gonad that produces eggs, or ova. An organ that secretes the hormones oestrogen and progesterone. In plants, the part of the flower that contains the ovules and develops into fruit.
example_sentence: Each ovary releases one egg roughly every month. The ovary produces hormones that control the menstrual cycle. A cyst was found on her left ovary. In flowering plants the ovary ripens into a fruit.

english_meaning: In addition to. More than what is expected or required. Beyond a particular amount or level. Used to show something extra or additional.
example_sentence: He gave help over and above his duty. He was given a car over and above his salary. She received a gold medal over and above her certificate. The company provides free meals over and above the monthly wages. His honesty is over and above his intelligence.

english_meaning: Completely or deeply involved in something, especially in love, work, or debt. To be fully absorbed or engaged in a situation, often beyond one’s control.
example_sentence: He is over head and ears in debt. He is over head and ears in love with her. She was over head and ears in debt after starting her new business. I’m over head and ears in work this week, I can’t even rest!. They got over head and ears in trouble because of their wrong decisions.

english_meaning: Extremely happy and delighted. Feeling great joy or excitement about something.
example_sentence: She was over the moon when she got her first job. He felt over the moon after hearing that he had passed the exam. They were over the moon about their new baby. I’m over the moon with my team’s performance today.

english_meaning: To impress someone so much that they feel silent or nervous due to respect, fear, or wonder. It involves overwhelming someone's mind or will by showing great authority or power. This state often prevents a person from acting or speaking freely.
example_sentence: The majestic beauty of the mountains tended to overawe the hikers. The young soldier was completely overawed by the presence of the general. She was not the type of person to let a prestigious title overawe her. The sheer scale of the historical monument overawed every visitor.

english_meaning: A bridge crossing over a road, railway, or canal. A structure providing safe passage for pedestrians or vehicles above a thoroughfare. An elevated pathway designed to avoid intersecting traffic.
example_sentence: Pedestrians are advised to use the overbridge to cross the busy railway tracks safely. The new overbridge has significantly reduced traffic congestion at the intersection. Funding was approved to construct a pedestrian overbridge near the local school. They stood on the overbridge watching the trains pass underneath.

english_meaning: Excessive confidence in oneself or one's abilities beyond what is justified. An unwarranted sense of certainty about success. The state of trusting oneself too much.
example_sentence: Overconfidence often leads to failure. His overconfidence cost the team the match. She was warned against overconfidence before the interview. Overconfidence can blind us to real dangers.

english_meaning: Excessively confident in one's own abilities or judgment. Having more self-assurance than is warranted. Feeling too sure of success, often leading to mistakes.
example_sentence: He was overconfident and failed the exam. The team became overconfident after their easy wins. Do not be overconfident about your abilities. Her overconfident attitude annoyed her colleagues.

english_meaning: To examine something thoroughly and make any necessary changes or repairs. To reform or improve a system completely. A thorough examination and repair. To overtake.
example_sentence: The engine needs a complete overhaul. The government plans to overhaul the tax system. After a full overhaul, the car ran smoothly. Their strategy requires a serious overhaul. The leader promised to overhaul the education sector.

english_meaning: To make someone extremely happy, delighted, or filled with joy. To fill a person with intense pleasure or great happiness. To cause feelings of overwhelming gladness, delight, or satisfaction. It is usually used when a piece of good news, an event, or a gesture brings extraordinary happiness that goes beyond ordinary pleasure.
example_sentence: The news of her promotion overjoyed the entire family. His safe return from the war overjoyed his parents. The surprise gift overjoyed the little child. Winning the championship overjoyed the whole team. The reunion with her old friend overjoyed her completely.

english_meaning: To fail to notice something or someone, or to forgive/ignore something. Fail to notice or ignore. Forgive or excuse. Have a view from above
example_sentence: I accidentally overlooked an important detail in the report. The teacher overlooked his mistake because he tried hard. The hotel room overlooks the ocean. She tends to overlook minor faults in people.

english_meaning: The day after tomorrow. An archaic or rarely used English word referring to the second day from today. Used historically in English before being largely replaced by the modern phrase the day after tomorrow. Occasionally revived in literary or poetic writing for stylistic effect.
synonyms: ["Day after tomorrow","Two days hence","Second day from now"]
example_sentence: The meeting has been postponed until overmorrow due to scheduling conflicts.  In old English texts, overmorrow was commonly used instead of the day after tomorrow.  We plan to depart for our trip overmorrow, weather permitting.  The festival will begin overmorrow and continue for three days.  She promised to send the documents overmorrow at the latest.

english_meaning: Happening or taking place during the night. Done or occurring very quickly or suddenly. To stay for the duration of a night. A stay or period of travel lasting one night.
example_sentence: The song became an overnight success and topped the charts globally. We packed a small bag for our overnight stay at the mountain cabin. The temperature dropped significantly overnight and froze the lake. You can overnight the package to ensure it arrives by tomorrow morning.

english_meaning: To try to do more than is reasonable, possible, or allowed. To extend authority or influence beyond proper limits. To reach too far and lose balance.
example_sentence: The government overreached by restricting peaceful speech. His ambition led him to overreach. The athlete overreached and lost his balance. The proposal overreaches what the budget can support.

english_meaning: To go beyond control, limit, or capacity. Excess beyond limit or budget. An amount or situation in which something exceeds its expected limit, time, or cost.
example_sentence:
The city was overrun by tourists during the festival. 
Weeds have overrun the garden after the rains. The enemy army overran the border within hours. Costs have overrun the company’s annual budget. The project faced a major cost overrun. There was a time overrun due to bad weather.

english_meaning: To supervise or watch work or activities to make sure they are done correctly. To observe, manage, or direct a task, project, or group of people carefully in order to ensure that everything is carried out properly, efficiently, and according to rules or plans.
example_sentence: The manager oversees the daily operations of the office. A senior engineer was hired to oversee the construction project. She was asked to oversee the training of new employees. The teacher oversees the exam to ensure fairness.

english_meaning: To stay somewhere longer than is expected, wanted, or allowed. To remain past the permitted time, especially regarding a visa or a visit.
example_sentence: Do not overstay your welcome at anyone’s house. He was fined for overstaying his visa. Guests should not overstay after dinner. She overstayed her leave and got a warning. Tourists who overstay may face legal action.

english_meaning: To go beyond an accepted limit or boundary. To exceed proper behavior, authority, or rules. To transgress.
example_sentence: He overstepped his authority by firing the employee. Don't overstep the boundaries of politeness. The officer was punished for overstepping the rules. She felt he had overstepped by asking personal questions.

english_meaning: To place too much emphasis on something. To subject someone or something to excessive stress or strain.
example_sentence: Do not overstress the importance of grades over learning. It is easy to overstress workers with tight deadlines. Teachers should not overstress a single topic. Overstressed machinery breaks down more often. He tends to overstress minor mistakes.

english_meaning: Done or shown openly, without any attempt to hide it. Clearly visible, not secret or hidden. Public and undisguised.
example_sentence: There was overt hostility between the two leaders. The company faced overt criticism from customers. She showed overt support for the movement. Overt discrimination is against the law. His overt behaviour left no room for doubt.

english_meaning: To catch up with and pass someone or something moving in the same direction. To become greater in number or importance than something else. To come upon suddenly, as an event or emotion. To surpass or exceed.
example_sentence: The red car overtook us on the highway. India has overtaken many countries in software exports. He was overtaken by grief after the news. Online sales have overtaken traditional retail.

english_meaning: To remove someone from power or authority, especially by force. It can also mean to defeat or destroy a system, government, or rule. The act of removing or defeating a ruler, government, or system, usually by force.
example_sentence: The army tried to overthrow the government. The rebels succeeded in overthrowing the dictator. The new policy aims to overthrow old traditions. The revolution overthrew the corrupt regime. The overthrow of the king marked the beginning of a new era. People celebrated the overthrow of the corrupt government.

english_meaning: A formal proposal, suggestion, or initiative to start discussions or establish relations. An offer intended to show goodwill, friendship, or cooperation. Any first step or opening move in a process or plan. An attempt to gain attention or interest in a proposal. An instrumental introduction to an opera, ballet, or play.
example_sentence: The company sent an overture to potential investors. She made an overture of friendship after the disagreement. The orchestra played a lively overture before the opera began. His diplomatic overture was warmly received.

english_meaning: To flip something over so that the bottom comes up. To cancel or reverse a decision made by a court or authority. In politics it can mean removing a government or system from power. The act of turning something upside down or cancelling a decision.
example_sentence: The strong wind overturned several boats near the shore. The higher court overturned the previous decision. Protesters tried to overturn the government. The truck overturned on the highway after the driver lost control. The overturn of the truck caused a traffic jam on the road. The court's overturn of the law surprised many people. The sudden overturn of the boat frightened the passengers.

english_meaning: A general summary or outline of a subject. A brief survey or summary of a matter. A comprehensive look at something from a high level. An introductory description of a situation or plan. A bird's-eye view or broad perspective of a topic.
example_sentence: The manager provided a brief overview of the new project during the meeting. Please read this document for an overview of the company's financial status. The first chapter gives a general overview of the historical period. This website offers a quick overview of the city's top tourist attractions.

english_meaning: To affect someone very strongly, making them unable to cope. To overpower someone emotionally, mentally, or physically. It can also mean to defeat completely or to cover something entirely. A strong feeling that is too much to handle.
example_sentence: She was overwhelmed with joy after hearing the good news. The team was overwhelmed by the strength of their opponents. He felt overwhelmed by the amount of work he had to complete. The village was overwhelmed by floodwater during the storm.

english_meaning: To write over existing text or data, replacing it. To record new information in place of old information. To write in an excessively elaborate style.
example_sentence: Be careful not to overwrite the original file. The program will overwrite older backups automatically. He accidentally overwrote an hour of work. Some critics say the author tends to overwrite.

english_meaning: Extremely nervous, anxious, or upset. In a state of emotional exhaustion. Too elaborate or complicated in style. Worked up beyond normal control.
example_sentence: She was overwrought after hours of waiting at the hospital. His overwrought nerves finally gave way. The critic found the prose overwrought and heavy. Parents often become overwrought during exam season.

english_meaning: Showing too much enthusiasm or eagerness. Excessively keen in supporting a cause or duty. Going beyond what is reasonable in effort or strictness.
example_sentence: An overzealous guard stopped every visitor twice. His overzealous cleaning damaged the old painting. Overzealous supporters caused trouble after the match. She was criticised for being overzealous in enforcing the rules.

english_meaning: The tube through which an egg passes from the ovary. A duct that carries eggs in the female reproductive system. The passage connecting the ovary to the uterus in mammals.
example_sentence: The egg travels down the oviduct after ovulation. Infection in the oviduct can cause infertility. In birds the oviduct forms the shell of the egg. The diagram clearly labelled the oviduct.

english_meaning: Relating to sheep. Resembling a sheep in appearance or behaviour. Belonging to the sheep family.
example_sentence: The vet specialises in ovine diseases. Ovine wool is a major export of the region. He wore a patient, almost ovine expression. Ovine farming supports many rural families.

english_meaning: Producing young by laying eggs. Describing animals whose eggs hatch outside the mother's body. Egg-laying in method of reproduction.
example_sentence: Birds and most reptiles are oviparous. The teacher explained the difference between oviparous and viviparous animals. Fish are usually oviparous creatures. Oviparous species lay eggs in safe places.

english_meaning: To be under obligation to pay or repay money to someone. To have a duty to give something to someone, especially gratitude or respect. To have something because of a particular reason or cause. To be indebted to someone for help, kindness, or favors received.
synonyms: ["Be indebted","Be obligated","Have a debt","Be beholden","Need to pay","Must pay"]
antonyms: ["Possess","Own","Be owed","Have no debt","Be free of obligation"]
example_sentence: I owe you twenty dollars from last week. She owes her success to hard work and determination. We owe our parents gratitude for their sacrifices. He owes an apology for his rude behavior.

english_meaning: Required to pay something, especially money, to someone. Under obligation to give or repay something. Indebted to another person for money, gratitude, or favor. Past tense and past participle of "owe". Being due to be paid or given in return.
example_sentence: He owed a large amount of money to the bank. She thanked everyone she owed her success to. The company paid all the salaries owed to its employees. I felt I owed him an apology for my behavior. The respect owed to elders should never be ignored.

english_meaning: Still to be paid; owed as a debt. Resulting from or caused by a particular factor. Used in the phrase owing to, meaning because of or as a result of.
example_sentence: There was still a large sum of money owing on the account at the end of the month. Owing to the heavy rain, the outdoor event was moved inside at the last minute. The delay was owing to an unexpected technical fault in the main system. She had several outstanding bills owing before she could close the account.

english_meaning: In a manner resembling an owl, especially looking solemn, wise, or observant. With a serious or studious appearance. In a way that suggests wisdom or thoughtfulness. Looking at something with wide, unblinking eyes like an owl.
example_sentence: The professor peered owlishly through his thick glasses. She blinked owlishly at the bright light. He stared owlishly at the complex equation. The child looked owlishly serious while listening to the story.

english_meaning: To legally possess or have ownership of something. To acknowledge, admit, or confess something. To take responsibility for an action, decision, or mistake. To recognize something as belonging to oneself. Belonging to oneself and not to another person. Personal or individual.
example_sentence: She owns a beautiful house near the lake. He owned his mistake and apologized to everyone. They own several small businesses in the city. I prefer to make my own decisions.

english_meaning: o honestly admit that you made a mistake. To accept responsibility for something you did. To admit doing something wrong or unlawful. To finally reveal the truth after trying to keep it secret. To admit that you deserve the blame for something.
synonyms: ["Admit","Confess","Acknowledge","Come clean","Accept responsibility","Accept blame","Fess up","Tell the truth","Reveal","Own responsibility"]
antonyms: ["Deny","Hide","Conceal","Cover up","Lie","Reject responsibility","Withhold the truth","Disown","Refuse to admit","Keep secret"]
example_sentence: He finally owned up to breaking the window. You should own up if you make a mistake. She owned up to copying the homework. The employee owned up after the missing money was discovered.

english_meaning: Admit responsibility. Confess to a mistake. Accept blame. Acknowledge the truth. Come clean about something. Admit guilt. Accept accountability. Tell the truth about one's actions.
synonyms: ["Acknowledge","Accept responsibility","Accept blame","Come clean","Fess up","Own it","Tell the truth","Admit guilt","Take responsibility","Admit one's mistake"]
antonyms: ["Deny","Conceal","Hide","Cover up","Lie","Disown","Reject responsibility","Blame others","Withhold the truth","Refuse to admit"]
example_sentence: He finally owned up to breaking the office printer. The student owned up to cheating during the examination. She owned up to forgetting her friend's birthday and apologized sincerely. If you own up to your mistake, people are more likely to forgive you.

english_meaning: A person who owns something, having legal possession and rights. Someone who has purchased or acquired property, goods, or assets. A person with legal title to something. The proprietor of a business or establishment.
example_sentence: The owner of the restaurant greeted us warmly. She is the proud owner of a new car. The property owner refused to sell the land. Business owners must pay annual taxes.

english_meaning: Having legal possession of something. The act of possessing or having something as property. Acknowledging or admitting something, especially a mistake or fault. Taking responsibility for one's actions or words.
example_sentence: Owning a home is a major financial commitment. He is finally owning up to his mistakes. Owning your decisions builds character and integrity. She takes pride in owning her own business.

english_meaning: A phrase combining two opposite or contradictory words. A figure of speech in which two opposite or contradictory words are used together. A literary device where conflicting terms appear side by side to create a new meaning, add emphasis, or express a complex idea, such as combining opposite qualities in one phrase. (Examples: Deafening silence, Bitter sweet, Clearly confused, Living dead)
example_sentence: “Bittersweet” is an example of an oxymoron. The phrase “deafening silence” is an oxymoron. He used an oxymoron for dramatic effect. Oxymorons are common in poetry. The whole concept of the music industry is an oxymoron. That monster is reality television, which hardly any. It may sound like an oxymoron: " A phone booth for the mobile world. "

english_meaning: It refers to a marine bivalve mollusc with a rough irregular shell, often eaten raw. It can denote a shade of greyish-white colour. It represents a source of pearls and valuable materials. It is sometimes used figuratively to describe a silent or uncommunicative person. It is a delicacy enjoyed by seafood lovers around the globe.
example_sentence: We ordered a dozen raw oysters as an appetizer. The living room was painted in a soft oyster colour to reflect the light. He remained an oyster throughout the interrogation and refused to speak. She found a beautiful pearl inside the large oyster.

english_meaning: A soft, fan-shaped mushroom that grows in overlapping clusters. An edible fungus with a delicate, slightly sweet flavour. A mushroom often grown on straw or wood. A meaty ingredient used in stir-fries, soups, and curries.
example_sentence: Oyster mushrooms cook very quickly in a hot pan. He grows oyster mushrooms on straw bales. The soup was rich with oyster mushrooms. Oyster mushrooms have a soft, velvety texture.

english_meaning: To walk back and forth, usually because of nervousness or thinking. To control the speed of an activity. Speed or rate at which someone or something moves or happens. It can describe how fast someone walks, runs, works, or how quickly something develops.
example_sentence: To keep pace with you I have to go fast. It is difficult to keep up with the rapid pace of change. She walks at a fast pace every morning. The project is moving at a steady pace. He began to pace the room while waiting for the call. You should pace yourself during the race.

english_meaning: A person or animal that sets the pace in a race. A horse trained to move both legs on one side together. A person who walks back and forth, especially when anxious. A device that regulates rhythm, such as a heart pacemaker.
example_sentence: The pacer helped the runner maintain a steady speed. The pacer horse won several races last year. He became a nervous pacer while waiting for the results. Her heart pacer keeps her rhythm normal.

english_meaning: A rubber or plastic teat given to a baby to suck on for comfort. A small device used to calm or quieten a crying infant. Something or someone that calms anger or restlessness. A person who restores peace between quarrelling parties.
example_sentence: The baby fell asleep as soon as she was given her pacifier. He kept a spare soother in the nappy bag. Some parents avoid using a pacifier after the first year. The soft music acted as a soother for the restless child.

english_meaning: To calm a person or group that is angry, upset, or violent. To bring peace to a country or area where there is fighting. To soothe or appease.
example_sentence: The mother tried to pacify the crying child. The government sent troops to pacify the region. He raised his hand to pacify the crowd. She could not pacify her angry friend. Sweet words often pacify difficult customers.

english_meaning: To fit many activities, events, or people into a limited period or space. To stop doing something or give up.
synonyms: ["Squeeze in","Include","Fit in","Quit (in sense of stopping)","Give up"]
example_sentence: She tried to pack in as many tourist spots as possible during her weekend trip. The theater can pack in up to 500 people. After years of teaching, he decided to pack in his job and travel the world. They packed in all the training sessions into one intensive week.

english_meaning: To send someone away, often with some urgency or force, usually to a distant place or to remove them from a situation.
example_sentence: They packed the kids off to school. He was packed off to London for training. The manager packed off the interns early. She packed him off with a lunchbox.

english_meaning: To arrange or fill a space (such as a stadium, theatre, or store) with people until it is full. To remove goods, equipment, or belongings from a place by packing them into containers or bags for transport or storage.
example_sentence: The theater was packed out last night. Fans packed out the stadium. The hall was packed out for the concert. The church was packed out for the wedding.

english_meaning: To put things into a bag, box, or container. To stop working, especially because something is broken. To end an activity or close a business. Informal use for telling someone to leave.
example_sentence: We need to pack up our books before leaving the classroom. The workers packed up their tools after finishing the job. My old computer suddenly packed up yesterday. Due to heavy rain, they decided to pack up the event early.

english_meaning: A formal agreement between individuals, groups, or nations. A treaty or contract with binding terms. A promise or arrangement between parties. A solemn commitment made mutually. An understanding reached after negotiation.
example_sentence: The two countries signed a peace pact. They made a pact never to reveal the secret. A trade pact was announced last week. The friends made a pact to meet every year.

english_meaning: To sleep somewhere temporarily, often on a floor or couch. To spend the night or sleep somewhere. To search someone by lightly touching their clothes with the hands to check for hidden objects. To gently press or smooth something down with the hands. To gently press or stroke an animal’s body to calm it. To settle or calm a situation by gentle action. To apply a cosmetic product gently by tapping with fingers or a soft pad. To gently flatten or arrange hair or cloth by pressing lightly. To move downward softly with small pressing movements.
example_sentence: I’ll pad down at your place tonight. They padded down in the living room. The officer padded down the suspect before putting him in the car. Security staff padded down visitors at the entrance. She padded down the soil around the plant. He padded down his hair with a towel after washing it. He padded down the horse before riding it. She padded down her pockets to check for her keys. The teacher padded down the argument between the students. She padded down the foundation evenly across her face. The cat padded down the stairs quietly.

english_meaning: To make something longer, fuller, or thicker by adding extra material, words, or padding. To add extra details or words, often unnecessary, to increase the length of a piece of writing or speech. To add extra tasks or activities to make something last longer.
example_sentence: He padded out his essay with unnecessary quotations. The jacket was padded out with extra cotton for warmth. The speaker padded out the presentation with repeated points. They padded out the schedule with small activities to fill the day.

english_meaning: A quick search of a person’s body by touching over clothes to check for weapons or hidden items. A physical security search in which a police officer or security official runs their hands over a person’s outer clothing to detect concealed weapons, contraband, or suspicious objects.
example_sentence: The police officer performed a pad-down after the traffic stop. Security staff carried out a pad-down at the entrance of the stadium. The suspect was nervous during the pad-down search. Before boarding the plane, passengers may undergo a pad-down.

english_meaning: Soft material used to fill, protect, or make something more comfortable. Extra material added to a garment or object to give it shape. Unnecessary words added to make a piece of writing or speech longer. In design, the space between the content and the border of an element.
example_sentence: The box was filled with padding to protect the glass. His jacket has padding in the shoulders. The essay was full of padding and lacked real content. Increase the padding so the text does not touch the border.

english_meaning: A small enclosed field or area where horses or other animals are kept, trained, or allowed to graze. In horse racing, a paddock is the area where horses are prepared before a race.
example_sentence: The horses were grazing peacefully in the paddock. After the race, the winning horse was led back to the paddock. They built a wooden fence around the paddock to keep the animals safe. Each morning, he checks the paddock to ensure the gates are secure.

english_meaning: Relating to sexual attraction of an adult toward a boy.
example_sentence: The novel explored controversial themes, including paederastic relationships in ancient Greece. Historical texts sometimes describe paederastic mentorships, though modern interpretations criticize them. The court condemned paederastic behavior as a serious criminal offense. He wrote a research paper on paederastic practices in classical societies.

english_meaning: Related to the medical care of children. The branch of medicine that deals with the health, growth, diseases, and medical treatment of infants, children, and adolescents.
example_sentence: The hospital has a well equipped paediatric ward for children. She wants to become a paediatric doctor to help sick children. Paediatric care is important for healthy child development. The clinic offers specialized paediatric services for newborns.

english_meaning: A doctor who treats children. A medical doctor who specializes in the health, growth, and diseases of infants, children, and adolescents. They diagnose illnesses, provide treatment, give vaccinations, and guide parents about child development and nutrition.
example_sentence: The paediatrician examined the baby carefully. She wants to become a paediatrician after medical school. The paediatrician advised regular vaccinations for the child. Parents consulted a paediatrician for their child's fever.

english_meaning: A psychiatric disorder characterized by an adult or older adolescent having a primary or exclusive sexual attraction to prepubescent children. It is considered illegal and morally wrong in almost all societies.
example_sentence: The authorities arrested a man suspected of paedophilia. Awareness campaigns are crucial to prevent paedophilia. Paedophilia is treated as a serious crime in most countries. The psychologist explained the warning signs of paedophilia.

english_meaning: A book that is so exciting that you want to read it very quickly. A literary work that captures the reader's attention completely. A compelling piece of writing that is difficult to put down. An engrossing story that moves at a rapid pace. A high-stakes narrative that maintains intense interest throughout.
example_sentence: Her latest mystery novel is a real page-turner from start to finish. I stayed up all night reading that thriller because it was such a page-turner. Critics have described the biography as a gripping page-turner for history buffs. If you are looking for a page-turner, I highly recommend this spy fiction.

english_meaning: A public entertainment consisting of a procession of people in elaborate, colourful costumes, often depicting scenes from history. A show, especially a beauty competition.
example_sentence: The children performed a Christmas pageant at school. She won the beauty pageant last year. The town holds a historical pageant every summer. The wedding was a grand pageant of colour and music. A pageant was arranged for Independence Day.

english_meaning: To arrange pages of a document, book, report, or digital file in correct order and place numbers on each page so readers can easily follow the sequence. It is commonly used in publishing, printing, editing, and word processing.
example_sentence: The editor will paginate the manuscript before sending it to print. Please paginate the report so readers can find sections easily. The software automatically paginates long documents. She forgot to paginate the thesis, so the pages looked disorganized.

english_meaning: A person who loves beards or is attracted to people with beards. Someone who has a fondness for facial hair, particularly beards.
example_sentence: As a pagonophile, she always admired men with full beards. The pagonophile community celebrates the art of beard grooming. He was a proud pagonophile who grew his own beard for years. The beard festival was a gathering of pagonophiles.

english_meaning: Someone or something that is very annoying or bothersome. A constant source of irritation or inconvenience. An individual who is difficult to deal with and causes intense frustration. A task that is excessively tedious or troublesome to complete.
example_sentence: Filing these long tax forms every year is a real pain in the neck. My little brother can be a pain in the neck when I am trying to study. Taking the bus with all this heavy luggage is a pain in the neck. Dealing with customer service for refunds is always a pain in the neck.

english_meaning: Done with or employing great care and thoroughness. Characterized by careful and diligent effort. Taking great pains or showing careful attention to detail. Requiring or showing meticulous effort.
example_sentence: The restoration required painstaking work. She conducted painstaking research for the project. His painstaking attention to detail impressed everyone. The investigation was thorough and painstaking.

english_meaning: To go out and enjoy oneself in an excited, joyful, and often noisy way, usually by visiting restaurants, clubs, parties, or social gatherings. It suggests celebrating with great enthusiasm, often after a success, special occasion, or reunion.
synonyms: ["Celebrate wildly","Party hard","Go on a spree","Have a big night out","Live it up"]
antonyms: ["Stay home quietly","Mourn","Keep a low profile","Avoid celebration","Remain calm and reserved"]
example_sentence: After winning the championship, the team went out to paint the town red. It is my birthday tonight, so we are going to paint the town red. They painted the town red after their final exams were over. When he got his promotion, he invited his friends to paint the town red.

english_meaning: A false or superficial display of grandeur. Outward show without real substance. Artificial magnificence or pride. Empty grandeur made only for appearance. A hollow display of splendor.
example_sentence: The king’s ceremony was full of painted pomp. Beneath the painted pomp lay a poor and unhappy court. Their wedding was nothing but painted pomp. History is full of rulers who loved painted pomp.

english_meaning: To spend time socially with someone in a friendly way. To hang out or associate closely with someone in a relaxed and friendly manner.
example_sentence: He likes to pal around with his cousins during the holidays. She used to pal around with artists and writers in college. The children pal around together after school. He was often seen pal around with his old teammates.

english_meaning: To become friendly with someone, especially in a casual or informal way. It is often used when two people start spending time together and develop a friendly relationship.
example_sentence: He palled up with the new guy at work. They palled up quickly during the trip. She palled up with her neighbor. We palled up in school and stayed friends.

english_meaning: A covered seat or couch carried by people. A traditional enclosed vehicle made of wood or bamboo, often decorated with cloth or carvings, carried on poles by servants. In South Asia it was used to carry royalty, brides, or wealthy people before modern transport.
example_sentence: The bride was carried to the wedding hall in a beautifully decorated palankeen. The queen traveled through the city in a decorated palankeen. In ancient times, wealthy merchants preferred palankeens for comfort. The museum displayed an old palankeen from the Mughal era. The bride was carried to the ceremony in a traditional palankeen.

english_meaning: A covered seat or bed carried on poles by people. A traditional vehicle used in South and East Asia. It is a covered wooden or cloth structure designed to carry a person, usually royalty or nobles. It is lifted and carried by servants using long poles on the sides.
example_sentence: The queen was carried to the palace in a beautifully decorated palanquin. In ancient times, wealthy families traveled in palanquins. The bride arrived at the wedding venue in a traditional palanquin. The museum displayed an old palanquin used by royal families.

english_meaning: The top part of the inside of your mouth. The roof of the mouth separating the mouth from the nasal cavity.
example_sentence: A person’s palate is also the ability to taste and judge good food and drink. I let my palate dictate what I eat.

english_meaning: Prolonged and idle discussion. Unnecessary fuss or bother about something. To talk unproductively and at length.
example_sentence: There was a lot of palaver about the small change in rules. I do not have time for all this palaver. After much palaver, they finally agreed. The palaver in the meeting achieved nothing. Do not create palaver over such a trivial issue.

english_meaning: In a pale manner; with little colour or brightness. Faintly or weakly, especially of light. In a way that lacks strength, intensity, or conviction.
example_sentence: The moon shone palely through the clouds. She smiled palely and looked away. The lamp glowed palely in the corner. His face gleamed palely in the candlelight.

english_meaning: Relating to or denoting the early phase of the Stone Age, lasting roughly 2.5 million years, when primitive chipped stone tools were used. The Paleolithic era itself. Figuratively, extremely old-fashioned or outdated.
example_sentence: Paleolithic humans relied on stone tools for hunting and gathering. Archaeologists discovered Paleolithic cave paintings in southern France. The Paleolithic era ended with the advent of agriculture. His views on technology are practically Paleolithic.

english_meaning: The scientific study of fossils and ancient forms of life. The branch of science dealing with prehistoric plants and animals. The study of life in past geological periods through fossil remains.
synonyms: ["Fossil science","Study of fossils","Prehistoric biology","Palaeobiology","Earth history studies"]
example_sentence: Paleontology tells us how dinosaurs lived and died. She specialises in the paleontology of marine reptiles. The museum has a fine paleontology collection. Advances in paleontology have reshaped our view of evolution.

english_meaning: Financial support paid by one partner to another after an unmarried couple separates. A maintenance allowance granted to a live-in partner rather than a spouse. Compensation awarded on the breakdown of a long-term unmarried relationship.
example_sentence: She sued her former partner for palimony. The palimony case attracted a great deal of press attention. Courts in some states may award palimony after a long relationship. He agreed to pay monthly palimony out of court.

english_meaning: A word, phrase, number, or sequence that reads the same forward and backward. If you reverse the letters or numbers, they remain exactly the same.
example_sentence: Level, Madam, Racecar and 121 are examples of palindrome. Civic, Rotor, Refer, Noon, Wow and 12321 are palindromes. She enjoys solving puzzles that involve palindromes and symmetrical patterns. Palindromes are not limited to words; they can be numbers (12321), dates (02/02/2020), or even phrases (A man a plan a canal Panama). Palindromes are often used in puzzles, games, and cryptography.

english_meaning: A fence made of strong wooden or metal posts that are pointed at the top, especially used to protect a building in the past. A fence of pales or stakes set firmly in the ground, as for enclosure or defense.
example_sentence: There is a palisade between the two yards. They surrounded the yard with a palisade.

english_meaning: A flat wooden or plastic frame used for stacking and moving goods. A simple, hard, or makeshift bed, often just a mattress on the floor. A flat blade used by potters and craftsmen to shape material. In art, sometimes used for a board on which colours are mixed.
example_sentence: The goods were stacked on wooden pallets in the warehouse. He slept on a straw pallet near the fire. A forklift lifted three pallets at a time. The potter smoothed the clay with a wooden pallet.

english_meaning: A thin mattress filled with straw, chaff, or similar material. A simple, hard bed used in barracks, prisons, or camps. Any rough mattress laid directly on the floor or a bed frame. An old-fashioned bedding item used by soldiers and travellers.
example_sentence: Each soldier was given a blanket and a palliasse. She slept on a thin palliasse in the corner of the room. The prisoners' palliasses were replaced once a year. Travellers carried a rolled palliasse for the journey.

english_meaning: To make pain, illness, or a problem less severe without removing its cause. To ease suffering by giving temporary relief. To make an offence or fault appear less serious than it is. To reduce the harmful effects of something.
example_sentence: The drug palliates the symptoms but does not cure the disease. Nothing could palliate the grief of the family. He tried to palliate his mistake by blaming the weather. Aid can palliate hunger but not end poverty.

english_meaning: A treatment that relieves pain or symptoms without curing the disease. Something that makes a problem seem less serious without solving it. Describing care given to make a seriously ill patient comfortable. Serving to lessen suffering or soften the effect of something.
example_sentence: The medicine is only palliative and will not cure the illness. She was moved to a palliative care unit last week. The tax relief was a palliative rather than a real solution. Doctors offered palliative treatment to ease his pain.

english_meaning: The inner surface of the hand between the wrist and the fingers. The flat part of the hand used for holding and touching. A tall tropical tree with large leaves and no branches, such as a date or coconut palm. A symbol of victory or honour associated with palm leaves. To hide something in the hand, especially while performing a trick.
example_sentence: She held the coin tightly in her palm. The fortune teller read the lines on his palm. Tall palms lined the beach road. The magician palmed the card without anyone noticing.

english_meaning: Very small or insignificant. Refers to something that is trivial, meager, or of little value. It emphasizes worthlessness or inadequacy in quantity, quality, or importance.
example_sentence: He was paid a paltry sum for all his hard work. The company offered a paltry bonus despite the profits. She felt a paltry sense of satisfaction after the minor achievement. His paltry efforts could not change the outcome.

english_meaning: To indulge with every attention, comfort, and kindness. It means to treat with excessive indulgence or to spoil someone by doing too much for them. This action is often done out of great affection or a desire to provide luxury.
example_sentence: The grandparents love to pamper their grandchildren with gifts and sweets. You should take a day off to pamper yourself at the luxury spa. Luxury hotels are designed to pamper their guests with various amenities. She likes to pamper her pet cat with gourmet food and soft pillows.

english_meaning: Characterized by receiving excessive care, attention, or luxury. It describes an individual who has been treated with great indulgence and is used to having their every wish fulfilled. This state often implies being spoiled or over-protected.
example_sentence: The pampered prince had never done a day of hard work in his life. These pampered pets live in environments of absolute luxury and comfort. She felt like a pampered celebrity during her stay at the five-star resort. A pampered childhood can sometimes make adulthood seem very difficult.

english_meaning: To turn or move a camera across a scene, or to examine a wide area systematically. A flat or slightly curved container, usually made of metal, used for frying, cooking, or baking food.
example_sentence: The director panned the camera across the valley. He panned slowly to capture the entire audience. I heated oil in a pan for frying eggs. The chef used a non-stick pan for pancakes.

english_meaning: A remedy believed to cure all diseases or solve all problems. A single solution imagined to fix every difficulty. Something offered as a complete answer to complicated issues. In mythology, a legendary all-healing medicine.
example_sentence: Technology is not a panacea for every social problem. There is no panacea for the country's economic troubles. He wrongly treated exercise as a panacea for all illness. Voters were promised a panacea that never arrived.

english_meaning: A confident and stylish manner of doing things. Flamboyant energy and self-assurance that impresses others. Elegance and flair in dress, speech, or performance. Historically, a plume of feathers worn on a helmet or hat.
example_sentence: She delivered the speech with great panache. The team played with skill and panache throughout the match. He dresses with a panache that few can match. The chef prepares even simple dishes with panache.

english_meaning: A long flat gland lying behind the stomach. An organ that produces digestive enzymes released into the small intestine. An endocrine gland that produces insulin and glucagon to control blood sugar. A gland that has both exocrine and endocrine functions in the body.
example_sentence: The pancreas produces insulin to regulate blood sugar. Inflammation of the pancreas can cause severe abdominal pain. Digestive enzymes from the pancreas break down fats and proteins. Diabetes develops when the pancreas cannot make enough insulin.

english_meaning: A disease that spreads across many countries or continents and affects a large number of people.
example_sentence: The world faced a serious pandemic that changed daily life. Scientists worked together to control the pandemic. The pandemic affected global trade and travel. Vaccination helped reduce the impact of the pandemic.

english_meaning: A situation filled with wild noise, confusion, and disorder. Complete chaos or uproar where people are shouting or behaving in an uncontrolled way.
example_sentence: As soon as the fire alarm rang, pandemonium broke out in the building. The news of the team’s victory caused pandemonium in the streets. When the lights went out during the concert, there was total pandemonium. The sudden announcement created pandemonium in the classroom.

english_meaning: The act of stretching the body and yawning at the same time, usually on waking. The involuntary stretching of muscles accompanied by a yawn. A natural reflex that prepares the body for movement after rest.
example_sentence: Pandiculation is a common reflex after a long sleep. The doctor explained that pandiculation improves blood flow. Animals show pandiculation just as humans do. She began the morning with a slow pandiculation.

english_meaning: In Greek mythology, the first woman on Earth, whose curiosity released evils into the world. A female name of Greek origin meaning 'all-gifted'. A symbol of a source of unexpected or unavoidable troubles, as in 'Pandora's box'. Any situation that unleashes many problems once started. A cultural reference for something dangerous when opened or explored.
example_sentence: The story of Pandora is a famous Greek myth. Opening that investigation turned out to be a real Pandora's box. Pandora could not resist looking inside the forbidden jar. They named their daughter Pandora after the ancient legend.

english_meaning: A source of many unexpected troubles or difficulties. Something that seems harmless at first but releases countless problems once it is opened or started. An action or decision that creates complications which cannot be undone. In Greek mythology, the container that Pandora opened, releasing all the evils into the world.
example_sentence: Investigating the old accounts opened a Pandora's box of financial problems. He warned that changing the law could open a Pandora's box. Her simple question turned out to be a Pandora's box for the whole family. The report opened a Pandora's box of complaints against the department.

english_meaning: A small group of people chosen to give advice, make a decision, or publicly discuss an issue. A flat or curved component forming part of a surface. A distinct section of a door, wall, or vehicle body. A list of available jurors or a specialized committee. An array of instruments or controls on a dashboard.
example_sentence: The interview panel asked the candidate several challenging questions. A solar panel was installed on the roof to generate electricity. The wooden panel on the door was intricately carved. A panel of experts discussed the impact of climate change on television.

english_meaning: A sudden sharp pain or painful emotion. A brief but strong feeling of an unpleasant or distressing emotion such as guilt, regret, or hunger.
example_sentence: She felt a sudden pang of hunger. He experienced a pang of guilt after lying. A pang of jealousy crossed her face. The old memory brought a pang of sadness. He felt a sharp pang in his chest.

english_meaning: Excessively optimistic; believing that everything in the world is as good as it possibly can be, often ignoring real problems. Derived from Dr Pangloss in Voltaire's Candide.
example_sentence: His Panglossian view of the economy ignored the poverty around him. She criticised the government's Panglossian attitude to climate change. A Panglossian outlook can prevent necessary action. His Panglossian speeches were comforting but ultimately misleading.

english_meaning: A sentence that contains every letter of the alphabet at least once. A phrase used to display fonts or test typewriters because it uses all letters. A complete-alphabet sentence created as a linguistic exercise.
example_sentence: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is a famous pangram. Designers use a pangram to show how a typeface looks. The students were asked to write their own pangram. A perfect pangram uses each letter only once.

english_meaning: A sudden strong feeling of fear that prevents clear thinking. Uncontrolled anxiety spreading quickly through a group of people. A rapid loss of confidence causing hurried action, especially in financial markets. To feel or cause sudden overwhelming fear.
example_sentence: There was panic in the hall when the lights went out. Do not panic if the machine stops suddenly. Rumours of a shortage caused panic buying across the city. A wave of panic swept through the stock market.

english_meaning: Feeling sudden fear or anxiety that makes it hard to think calmly. Panicky describes a state where a person feels intense and sudden fear, worry, or nervousness. In this condition, emotions take control and rational thinking becomes difficult.
example_sentence: She became panicky when she realized she had lost her passport. His panicky reaction made the situation worse. The child looked panicky after hearing the loud noise. Try not to sound panicky during an emergency call.

english_meaning: A person who has or claims to have great influence or authority. A self-important or pompous official. A powerful pretentious person, often used humorously or mockingly. Someone who acts as though they are more important than they really are.
example_sentence: The local panjandrum insisted on being greeted before anyone else. He acted like a panjandrum at the small community meeting. Every office seems to have its own little panjandrum. The village panjandrum arrived with great ceremony.

english_meaning: An irrational or excessive fear of everything, often leading to general anxiety, unease, or apprehension in daily life. It is a psychological condition where the person feels threatened by almost all situations or objects, even without a clear cause.
example_sentence: His panphobia made it difficult for him to leave the house. She avoided social gatherings due to her panphobia. Panphobia caused him to constantly worry about minor risks. The therapist helped him understand and manage his panphobia.

english_meaning: A sexual orientation where a person experiences romantic or sexual attraction to others without considering gender or biological sex. Pansexual people may be attracted to men, women, transgender, non-binary, or gender-diverse individuals.
example_sentence: Alex identifies as pansexual and is open to dating anyone. She realized she was pansexual after reflecting on her attractions. Pansexuality challenges traditional ideas of gender-based attraction. Many pansexual individuals advocate for inclusivity in relationships.

english_meaning: A sexual orientation where a person feels attracted to others based on personality, emotional connection, or other qualities rather than gender. Pansexual individuals may be attracted to men, women, transgender people, non-binary people, or people of any gender identity.
example_sentence: Alex identifies as pansexual and is open to relationships with any gender. Pansexuality emphasizes attraction to the person, not their gender. Being pansexual means Riley does not limit themselves to dating men or women only. Some pansexual people feel society misunderstands their orientation.

english_meaning: A person who believes that God and the universe are the same. Someone who holds that divinity exists in all things in nature. Relating to the belief that everything in nature is part of God.
example_sentence: The poet was a pantheist who worshipped nature. A pantheist sees the divine in rivers and mountains. His pantheist beliefs shaped all of his writing. She described herself as a pantheist rather than a theist.

english_meaning: A small room, cupboard, or storage area where food, drinks, cooking ingredients, and kitchen supplies are kept. A dedicated place in a home, restaurant, office, or other building used for storing food items, spices, canned goods, beverages, utensils, and other kitchen necessities. Traditionally, a pantry was a separate room near the kitchen, but today it can also be a cabinet or closet designed for food storage.
synonyms: ["Larder","Store room","Food closet","Storage room","Store cupboard","Kitchen cabinet","Food storage area","Provision room"]
antonyms: ["Kitchen (place for cooking rather than storing)","Dining room","Empty space","Open area","Living room"]
example_sentence: The pantry is full of rice, flour, and cooking oil. She organized all the canned food in the pantry. We need to buy groceries because the pantry is almost empty. The office pantry provides tea, coffee, and snacks for employees.

english_meaning: A large tropical fruit with green or yellow skin and soft orange flesh containing black seeds. A sweet fruit eaten fresh or used in salads and juices. The fast-growing tree that produces this fruit. Unripe papaya used as a vegetable in some cuisines.
example_sentence: Ripe papaya is good for digestion. She cut the papaya into neat orange cubes. The papaya tree grew tall within a single year. Green papaya salad is a popular Thai dish.

english_meaning: To hide real problems instead of fixing them. It describes temporary or superficial solutions that do not fix the real issue.
antonyms: ["Expose the problem","Address the issue","Fix properly","Confront directly","Resolve fully"]
example_sentence: The manager tried to paper over the cracks in the team instead of addressing the real issues. Their marriage looked fine, but they were only papering over the cracks. You can’t paper over the cracks forever; one day the truth will come out. The government’s new policy papers over the cracks rather than fixing the economy.

english_meaning: A person or thing that appears threatening but is actually weak or ineffective. Something that looks powerful but poses no real danger. A false show of strength. An organization or nation that seems strong but lacks true power. An empty threat or hollow authority.
example_sentence: The dictator turned out to be nothing more than a paper tiger. Their threats are just those of a paper tiger. Critics called the new law a paper tiger. Without funding, the agency is a paper tiger.

english_meaning: Standard, equal level, average. A standard or typical level of quality, quantity, or achievement. It can also mean equality with a standard or expectation. Commonly used in golf to indicate the expected number of strokes.
example_sentence: Her performance is on par with the best in the team. The restaurant’s service was not up to par. In golf, he finished the hole in par. Salaries here are on par with industry standards.

english_meaning: A short simple story that teaches a moral or spiritual lesson. A brief tale used to illustrate a religious truth or principle. A short fictional narrative with a deeper meaning. A story told to convey wisdom or guidance. Parables are often used in religious teachings, especially in the Bible, to explain ideas through familiar examples from everyday life.
example_sentence: Jesus often taught his followers through parables. The teacher told a parable about kindness to explain the lesson. This ancient parable carries a powerful message about honesty. The book is a collection of parables from different cultures. He shared a parable to help the children understand the value of patience.

english_meaning: A symmetrical curve formed by the intersection of a cone with a plane parallel to its side. The U-shaped curve produced by a quadratic equation in mathematics. The curved path followed by an object thrown into the air.
example_sentence: The graph of the equation is a parabola. A thrown ball travels in a parabola. The engineer designed the arch as a perfect parabola. Draw a parabola with its vertex at the origin.

english_meaning: A typical example or pattern of something; a model or world view. In science and philosophy, it refers to a distinct set of concepts or thought patterns, including theories and standards for what constitutes legitimate contributions to a field. A shift in this indicates a fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions.
example_sentence: The discovery of DNA created a new paradigm in the field of biology. Her successful business model became a paradigm for young entrepreneurs. The country needs a new economic paradigm to deal with modern challenges. We are currently witnessing a major paradigm shift in how people consume media.

english_meaning: A fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions. A great and important change in the way something is done or thought about. A fundamental change in approach, assumptions, or way of thinking about something. A radical change in underlying beliefs or theory.
example_sentence:
The widespread use of social media represents a paradigm shift in the company's marketing strategy. The invention of the internet caused a paradigm shift in communication. Wegener's theory led to a paradigm shift in the earth sciences.
I could convince only a few of my colleagues of the need for a revolution, a paradigm shift.

english_meaning: A statement, situation, or idea that seems impossible, opposite, or contradictory, but may actually contain a hidden truth. Something that appears confusing because it combines opposite ideas. At first, it may sound wrong or illogical, but after deeper thinking, it can reveal an important truth or reality. Paradoxes are commonly used in literature, philosophy, science, and daily life to express complex ideas.
example_sentence: Less is more is a famous paradox. The more we learn, the more we realize how little we know. He was alone in the crowd, which is a paradoxical feeling. Saving time by rushing often causes more delays, which is a paradox.

english_meaning: Seemingly contradictory, Seemingly absurd, self-contradictory, or against common sense, but may contain a hidden truth. Something that has two opposite features that exist together.
example_sentence: It is paradoxical but true. It is paradoxical that the poorest people often give the most in charity. His paradoxical statement confused everyone in the meeting. The paradoxical nature of technology is that it connects us but also isolates us. The silence of the leader at a time of crisis was paradoxical.

english_meaning: Paradoxically means in a way that seems strange, opposite, or contradictory, but may still be true or logical. It describes a situation where two opposite ideas exist together.
example_sentence: Paradoxically, the more he earned, the less satisfied he became. Paradoxically, staying calm helped her finish the work faster. The medicine paradoxically caused the same symptoms it was meant to cure. Paradoxically, people in large cities sometimes feel more lonely than villagers.

english_meaning: The sport of gliding through the air using a light parachute-like wing after launching from a height. Recreational flying with a fabric wing controlled by lines. The activity of soaring on air currents with a paraglider.
example_sentence: They went paragliding in the mountains last summer. Paragliding requires proper training and good weather. He took up paragliding after watching a documentary. The paragliding festival attracts visitors every year.

english_meaning: A person or thing regarded as a perfect example of a particular quality. A model of excellence to be imitated. A flawless example of its kind.
example_sentence: She is a paragon of patience and kindness. The building is a paragon of modern design. He is no paragon, but he works honestly. Teachers held her up as a paragon of good behaviour.

english_meaning: A distinct section of a piece of writing that deals with one main idea and begins on a new line. A short passage or item in a newspaper. To divide a text into paragraphs.
example_sentence: Each paragraph should contain one main idea. Read the second paragraph on page ten. She wrote a short paragraph about her holiday. The editor asked him to paragraph the text more clearly.

english_meaning: The act of dividing a piece of writing into paragraphs. The arrangement or organization of text into separate paragraphs. The skill of structuring written work into clear and logical sections.
example_sentence: Good paragraphing makes an essay easier to read and understand. The teacher praised the student for her clear paragraphing. Careful paragraphing helps the reader follow the writer's argument. He is still learning the basics of paragraphing in English composition.

english_meaning: Relating to Paraguay, its people, culture, or language. A person who comes from or lives in Paraguay. A native or citizen of Paraguay.
synonyms: ["Paraguay national","Native of Paraguay","Citizen of Paraguay","Paraguayan person"]
example_sentence: The Paraguayan team played brilliantly in the football match. She married a Paraguayan businessman she met in Asunción. Paraguayan culture blends Spanish and Guaraní traditions. He bought a beautiful piece of Paraguayan lace at the market.

english_meaning: Relating to the parts of communication that go beyond actual words. Concerning tone, pitch, volume, pauses, and speed of speech. Involving non-verbal features that add meaning to spoken language. Used in linguistics to describe vocal cues such as sighs or laughter.
example_sentence: Tone of voice is an important paralinguistic feature. The study focused on paralinguistic cues in conversation. Laughter and sighs carry paralinguistic meaning. Teachers should be aware of paralinguistic signals in class.

english_meaning: The apparent change in the position of an object when it is viewed from two different points. An effect in which nearer objects seem to move faster than distant ones as the viewer moves. In astronomy, a method of measuring the distance of stars using this shift. In web and game design, a scrolling effect that creates a sense of depth.
example_sentence: Astronomers use parallax to calculate the distance of nearby stars. The parallax effect makes the background move slowly. Always read the scale straight on to avoid parallax error. The website uses parallax scrolling for a modern look.

english_meaning: Being side by side and always the same distance apart, never meeting. Happening at the same time or in a similar way. A person or thing that is similar or comparable to another. To be similar to something else or to happen in a corresponding way. A line of latitude on a map or globe.
example_sentence: The two roads run parallel to each other for several miles. Her career followed a path parallel to her sister's. There is no parallel for such an event in our history. The new policy parallels the one introduced last year.

english_meaning: The use of similar grammatical structures in related words, phrases, or clauses. A state of being parallel or side by side. Similarity or correspondence between ideas, events, or forms. A rhetorical device that creates balance and rhythm.
example_sentence: The speech uses parallelism to sound powerful. There is a clear parallelism between the two stories. Good parallelism makes a list easier to read. The road and railway run in parallelism for several miles.

english_meaning: A four-sided figure whose opposite sides are parallel and equal in length. A quadrilateral in which opposite angles are also equal. A shape whose area equals base multiplied by perpendicular height. A general class that includes rectangles, squares, and rhombuses.
example_sentence: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are always parallel. He calculated the area of the parallelogram using its height. A rectangle is a parallelogram with right angles. The students constructed a parallelogram with a ruler and compass.

english_meaning: The loss of the ability to move part or all of the body. Loss of muscle function, often with loss of feeling. A complete inability to act, function, or make progress. A state in which activity or a system comes to a total standstill.
example_sentence: The stroke caused paralysis in his right arm. Snake venom can lead to paralysis within minutes. The strike brought about a paralysis of public transport. Fear of failure produced a kind of mental paralysis.

english_meaning: An illicit lover, especially of a married person. It refers to a person with whom someone is having a secret or unauthorized romantic relationship.
example_sentence: The king kept his paramour in a secluded villa away from the court. Their secret letters revealed the intensity of their bond with his paramour. The scandal broke when the politician was seen dining with his paramour. Historians often write about the influence of the queen's secret paramour.

english_meaning: Paranoia is an intense and unreasonable feeling that other people are trying to harm, deceive, watch, judge, or persecute you, even when there is little or no evidence. xcessive suspicion, distrust, or fear of others. A person experiencing paranoia may believe that people are plotting against them, talking about them, spying on them, or intending to cause harm, despite a lack of proof. In everyday language, it can also describe strong feelings of mistrust that are not necessarily part of a medical condition.
example_sentence: His paranoia made him believe that his coworkers were secretly discussing him. After reading too many conspiracy theories, she developed paranoia about being watched online. The constant paranoia prevented him from trusting even his closest friends. Living in a dangerous environment can sometimes increase feelings of paranoia.

english_meaning: Being excessively suspicious, distrustful, or fearful that other people are trying to harm, deceive, watch, or oppose you, often without sufficient evidence. A paranoid person frequently believes that others have bad intentions toward them. They may think people are talking about them, spying on them, plotting against them, or trying to cause harm, even when there is little or no proof. In everyday language, "paranoid" can describe unnecessary suspicion or worry. In psychology, it can refer to more serious patterns of irrational distrust.
example_sentence: He became paranoid and thought his coworkers were secretly discussing him. She was paranoid about someone reading her private messages. After hearing strange noises, he grew paranoid and checked every room in the house. Being paranoid about minor mistakes prevented him from enjoying his work.

english_meaning: Extreme and unreasonable suspicion of others. A tendency to believe that people have hidden harmful motives. A mindset characterized by distrust and fear of persecution. A condition involving paranoid thoughts or beliefs. Excessive concern that one is being watched, judged, or targeted.
example_sentence: His paranoidism made him believe that his coworkers were secretly discussing him all the time. Because of her paranoidism, she often suspected hidden motives behind simple acts of kindness. The character's paranoidism increased after receiving several anonymous messages. Excessive paranoidism can damage relationships by creating unnecessary distrust between people.

english_meaning: In an overly suspicious way. In a distrustful manner. With unreasonable fear of danger or betrayal. In a way that assumes hidden threats or bad intentions. With excessive concern that others are against you.
example_sentence: He checked his phone paranoidly, fearing that someone had accessed his messages. She looked around paranoidly whenever she heard people laughing nearby. The employee paranoidly assumed that every meeting was about his mistakes. After reading false rumors online, he began acting paranoidly toward his friends.

english_meaning: A low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge, or balcony. A defensive earthwork or wall built to shield soldiers. A raised barrier that prevents people from falling. The upper part of a rampart in a fortification.
example_sentence: He leaned over the parapet to look at the river below. Soldiers fired from behind the parapet of the old fort. A child's ball rolled off the parapet of the roof. The bridge's parapet was rebuilt after the flood.

english_meaning: The various items or equipment needed for a particular activity. Miscellaneous belongings or personal possessions. Trappings or accessories associated with a role or occasion. A collection of odds and ends that clutter a place.
example_sentence: He arrived with all the paraphernalia of a professional photographer. The kitchen was full of baking paraphernalia. Wedding paraphernalia filled every corner of the house. She packed her painting paraphernalia into one large bag.

english_meaning: To express the meaning of something using different words. A restatement of a text in clearer or simpler language. To reword a passage while keeping its original sense. A shortened, reworded version of a longer statement.
example_sentence: Can you paraphrase this paragraph in simple English? Her paraphrase of the speech captured its spirit. The teacher asked us to paraphrase the article. He paraphrased the judgment for the newspaper readers.

english_meaning: The act of expressing the meaning of a passage in different words. Restating something in a clearer or simpler form. Rewording text while keeping the original meaning intact. A study technique used to show understanding without copying.
example_sentence: Paraphrasing helps students avoid plagiarism. She is paraphrasing the poem for younger readers. Good paraphrasing shows real understanding of the text. He kept paraphrasing the report until it sounded natural.

english_meaning: Paralysis of the lower half of the body, including both legs. Loss of movement and sensation below the level of a spinal injury. A medical condition usually caused by damage to the spinal cord. Impairment affecting the legs and often the lower trunk.
example_sentence: The accident left him with permanent paraplegia. Physiotherapy can improve daily life for people with paraplegia. Paraplegia usually results from spinal cord injury. She wrote a book about living independently with paraplegia.

english_meaning: A person who is paralysed in the lower half of the body. Relating to or affected by paraplegia. Describing paralysis that involves both legs. Suffering from loss of movement below the waist.
example_sentence: He became paraplegic after falling from the scaffolding. The centre trains paraplegic athletes for the Paralympics. A paraplegic patient may need a specially adapted vehicle. She learned to drive despite being paraplegic.

english_meaning: A slip of the tongue, pen, or memory believed to reveal an unconscious thought. A minor error in speech or action interpreted in psychoanalysis as meaningful. A Freudian slip that exposes hidden feelings or wishes.
synonyms: ["Freudian slip","Slip of the tongue","Verbal slip","Lapse","Blunder","Faux pas","Misstatement"]
example_sentence: Calling his wife by his ex-partner's name was a classic parapraxis. Freud believed every parapraxis has a hidden cause. The lecture explained parapraxis with several amusing examples. Her parapraxis revealed more than she intended to say.

english_meaning: An organism that lives on or in a host organism and benefits at the host's expense. A creature that depends on another for survival without giving benefit. An organism causing disease or harm to its host. A person who habitually relies on others without reciprocating.
example_sentence: Malaria is caused by a parasite. Intestinal parasites can cause digestive problems. Fleas and ticks are external parasites. Some people act like parasites, taking without giving.

english_meaning: Relating to or characteristic of a parasite. Living on or benefiting at the expense of another organism or person without giving anything in return. Taking from others without contributing anything in exchange.
example_sentence: Some fungi have a parasitic relationship with trees, drawing nutrients without providing any benefit. He was described by his former colleagues as a parasitic individual who lived off the efforts of others. The parasite enters the host body and begins a parasitic relationship that can last for years. The relationship had become entirely parasitic — she gave everything while he contributed nothing. Parasitic vines can eventually kill the trees they rely on for support.

english_meaning: A one sided relationship where one person feels emotionally connected to a public figure who does not know them. Often used for fans and celebrities.
example_sentence: Many fans develop parasocial bonds with influencers. The show created parasocial closeness with its host. Parasocial connections can feel real. Social media increases parasocial behavior.

english_meaning: Any of the four tiny glands located behind the thyroid gland. A small endocrine gland that produces parathyroid hormone. A gland that controls the level of calcium and phosphorus in the blood. A structure essential for healthy bones, nerves, and muscles.
example_sentence: The parathyroid gland keeps calcium levels balanced. Removal of a parathyroid gland can affect bone health. Each parathyroid gland is about the size of a grain of rice. Blood tests showed that one parathyroid gland was overactive.

english_meaning: To dry out completely or cause to become very thirsty or dry. Often used for crops, soil, or figuratively for thirst or desire.
example_sentence: The summer sun parched the fields, leaving them cracked. After hours of walking in the desert, he felt parched and needed water. The heat parched the fruit, making it shriveled and tough. His curiosity parched for knowledge could not be satisfied by books alone.

english_meaning: Extremely dry because of hot weather or lack of water. Dried out and cracked, as of land or lips. Feeling very thirsty. Roasted or dried by exposure to heat.
example_sentence: The parched fields cracked under the summer sun. After the long walk we were parched and exhausted. His lips were parched from the desert heat. They chewed parched grain during the journey.

english_meaning: A durable material prepared from the skin of animals such as sheep or goats, used in ancient and medieval times for writing important documents, manuscripts, and religious texts. It can also refer to a formal certificate or document written on such material. In modern usage, it may describe paper that resembles this material in texture or color. Something dry, pale, or shriveled in appearance. An official document such as a diploma or legal certificate.
