example_sentence: She fractured her pelvis in the accident. The pelvis supports the weight of the upper body. A woman's pelvis is generally wider than a man's. The scan showed no damage to the pelvis.

english_meaning: A person with whom you regularly exchange letters, emails, or messages, usually to build friendship, learn about another culture, or practice a language. Someone you communicate with regularly through letters, emails, or online messages without necessarily meeting in person. Penfriends often share their lives, interests, culture, language, hobbies, and experiences. The relationship is usually based on friendship, cultural exchange, language learning, or mutual interests.
synonyms: ["Correspondence friend","Letter friend","Mail friend","Email friend","Writing friend","Correspondent","Long distance friend","Overseas friend"]
example_sentence: I have had a pen friend from Japan for five years. My pen friend teaches me new words in Spanish. We became close friends even though we first met as pen friends. She enjoys writing letters to her pen friend every month.

english_meaning: A person with whom someone regularly exchanges letters, emails, or messages, usually to make friends, learn about another culture, or practice a language. A friend who lives in another city or country and communicates mainly by writing letters, emails, or online messages rather than meeting in person. People often have pen pals to learn about different cultures, improve language skills, exchange ideas, or build lasting friendships.
synonyms: ["Correspondence friend","Letter friend","Writing friend","Mail friend","Epistolary friend","Email friend","Long distance friend","Overseas friend","Correspondent","Writing companion"]
antonyms: ["Close friend","Neighbor","Classmate","Roommate","Face to face friend","Local friend","In person friend"]
example_sentence: I have had a pen pal in Japan for more than five years. My pen pal taught me many interesting facts about his country. She writes to her pen pal every month to practice English. Having a pen pal helped me understand different cultures and traditions.

english_meaning: Voluntary self-punishment inflicted as an outward expression of repentance for having done something wrong. It is often a religious act required to receive absolution. It can also refer to any hardship endured to make up for a mistake.
example_sentence: He performed a long penance to seek forgiveness for his sins. Walking barefoot for miles was a form of religious penance. The priest assigned a simple penance of daily prayers. She took on extra chores as a penance for her earlier rudeness.

english_meaning: A strong liking or tendency to do something. A natural fondness or taste for something. A habitual inclination toward a particular activity or thing.
example_sentence: She has a penchant for collecting rare books. His penchant for adventure took him to remote mountains. The chef's penchant for spicy food is well known. He showed an early penchant for mathematics.

english_meaning: A piece of jewellery that hangs from a chain worn around the neck. A hanging ornament or light fixture.
example_sentence: She wore a beautiful diamond pendant. He gave her a heart-shaped pendant on her birthday. The pendant light hangs above the dining table. The gold pendant matched her earrings. She lost her pendant during the trip.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove part or all of the penis. A procedure usually performed to treat penile cancer. The partial or total removal of the penis for medical reasons. A rare surgery that may be followed by reconstructive treatment.
example_sentence: A penectomy was necessary because the cancer had spread. The surgeon performed a partial penectomy to preserve function. Patients receive counselling before undergoing a penectomy. Reconstructive surgery is sometimes possible after a penectomy.

english_meaning: To force a way into or through something. It describes the act of piercing or entering into the interior of an object or group. It can also mean to understand or solve something complex or mysterious.
example_sentence: The rain began to penetrate the old roof of the house. The army was unable to penetrate the enemy's thick defenses. Scientists are trying to penetrate the mysteries of deep space. Her eyes seemed to penetrate his very soul.

english_meaning: A person with whom you regularly exchange letters, emails, or messages, usually to build friendship, learn about another culture, or practice a language. Someone you communicate with regularly through letters, emails, or online messages without necessarily meeting in person. Penfriends often share their lives, interests, culture, language, hobbies, and experiences. The relationship is usually based on friendship, cultural exchange, language learning, or mutual interests.
synonyms: ["Correspondence friend","Letter friend","Mail friend","Email friend","Writing friend","Correspondent","Long distance friend","Overseas friend"]
example_sentence: I have had a penfriend in Japan for more than five years. My penfriend teaches me new words in Spanish every week. She enjoys writing long letters to her penfriend during the holidays. Having a penfriend helped him understand another country's culture.

english_meaning: A piece of land mostly surrounded by water but connected to the mainland on one side. A landform that extends into a body of water, such as a sea or lake, with water on three sides and a land connection on the fourth side. It is larger than an island but not fully separated from the mainland.
example_sentence: The Iberian Peninsula includes Spain and Portugal. Florida is a peninsula in the southeastern United States. The Korean Peninsula is divided into North and South Korea. The Malay Peninsula connects Thailand and Malaysia.

english_meaning: The external male reproductive and urinary organ. The organ through which urine and semen leave the male body. A structure made of spongy erectile tissue that fills with blood. The male organ of sexual intercourse in humans and many animals.
example_sentence: The penis carries both urine and semen out of the body. Blood flow causes the penis to become erect. The doctor explained the anatomy of the penis to the students. Good hygiene of the penis helps prevent infection.

english_meaning: The feeling of being sorry for having done something wrong. Deep regret for past actions and a desire to make amends.
example_sentence: He felt deep penitence for his mistakes. Her tears showed genuine penitence. The prisoner expressed penitence before the judge. True penitence leads to positive change. Penitence must be followed by good actions.

english_meaning: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong. A person who repents of a sin.
example_sentence: The penitent boy apologized to his teacher. Her penitent look moved everyone. A penitent must be given a chance to reform. He came before the priest as a penitent. His penitent tone changed the mood of the meeting.

english_meaning: A person who is very unwilling to spend money. Someone extremely careful and mean with small amounts of cash. A stingy person who saves at every opportunity.
example_sentence: He is such a penny pincher that he reuses tea bags. Her father was a penny pincher all his life. Penny pinchers rarely enjoy holidays abroad. The office joked that their boss was a penny pincher.

english_meaning: Careful about spending small amounts of money but wasteful with large amounts. Economical in trivial matters while being careless in important ones. Saving little while losing much through poor judgement.
example_sentence: Buying cheap tyres to save money was penny wise and pound foolish. He is penny wise and pound foolish, saving on repairs but replacing the whole machine later. Skipping insurance to cut costs is penny wise and pound foolish. Their budget cuts proved penny wise and pound foolish in the long run.

english_meaning: Deeply thoughtful, often quiet and serious, usually because someone is thinking carefully about something important, emotional, or worrying. It suggests reflection rather than sadness, though it may include concern or introspection.
example_sentence: He sat by the window with a pensive look, thinking about his future. Her pensive silence showed that the decision was not easy. The teacher appeared pensive after reading the report. A pensive mood settled over him as he remembered his childhood.

english_meaning: Adeep, quiet, and serious state of thinking. It often involves thoughtful reflection, mild sadness, or concern about past events or future possibilities. A pensive person appears calm but mentally absorbed in their thoughts.
example_sentence: His pensiveness suggested that something important was troubling him. She sat by the window in quiet pensiveness, thinking about her future. The photograph captured a moment of deep pensiveness on his face. There was a tone of pensiveness in her voice during the conversation.

english_meaning: A fifteen-sided polygon with fifteen angles. A geometric shape with fifteen straight sides and fifteen vertices. Any flat shape with fifteen corners and fifteen edges.
example_sentence: A regular pentadecagon has fifteen equal sides and angles. The mosaic design included a pentadecagonal pattern. Geometry students calculated the area of a pentadecagon. The architectural element was shaped like a pentadecagon.

english_meaning: A five-sided polygon with five angles. A geometric shape with five straight sides and five vertices. Any flat shape with five corners and five edges.
example_sentence: The Pentagon building in Washington has a distinctive five-sided shape. A regular pentagon has all sides and angles equal. Students learned to draw a pentagon in geometry class. The traffic sign was shaped like a pentagon.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with two parallel pentagonal bases connected by five rectangular faces. A prism with a five-sided cross-section throughout its length. A polyhedron with seven faces, two pentagonal and five rectangular.
example_sentence: The pencil has a pentagonal prism shape. A pentagonal prism has seven faces. Calculate the surface area of the pentagonal prism. The building's column is a pentagonal prism.

english_meaning: A five-pointed star drawn with five straight strokes. A geometric figure or symbol in the shape of a five-pointed star, often used in mysticism and heraldry. A decorative motif based on such a star.
example_sentence: The children learned to draw a pentagram in one stroke. A pentagram was carved above the old doorway. The flag features a single white pentagram. He explained the geometry of the pentagram.

english_meaning: A solid geometric figure having five plane faces. A three-dimensional shape such as a square pyramid or triangular prism, made up of five flat surfaces. Any polyhedron with exactly five faces.
example_sentence: A square pyramid is a common pentahedron. The students built a pentahedron out of paper. Each pentahedron in the model had five faces. He calculated the surface area of the pentahedron.

english_meaning: The partially shaded outer region of a shadow cast by an opaque object, especially during an eclipse. A surrounding area of uncertainty or a marginal region.
example_sentence: The penumbra was clearly visible during the solar eclipse. Legal rights often lie in a penumbra of uncertainty. The photograph captured the penumbra of the moon’s shadow. There is a penumbra of doubt around the decision. The penumbra fades gradually into full shadow.

english_meaning: Extremely poor and living in want. Unwilling to spend money, miserly. Marked by extreme poverty or scarcity. Reluctant to share resources with others. Showing a stingy or miserly nature.
example_sentence: The penurious old man refused to buy new clothes. Their penurious lifestyle surprised their wealthy neighbors. He was too penurious to help even his own family. Years of unemployment left them in a penurious state.

english_meaning: A state of severe financial hardship where one cannot afford the basic essentials of life such as food, clothing, and shelter. It often implies destitution and extreme scarcity.
example_sentence: After losing his job, he lived in penury for several years. The charity aims to alleviate penury in rural communities. Despite his wealth, he feared a life of penury in his old age. Many families in the flood-hit region are facing penury.

english_meaning: A pungent spice derived from the dried berries of the Piper nigrum plant. A vegetable that comes in various colors and flavors, ranging from sweet to very hot. To sprinkle or season food with small particles for added flavor. To shower or pelt someone or something with numerous small objects or questions. To season something thoroughly, both literally and figuratively, to make it more interesting.
example_sentence: She added a pinch of black pepper to the soup to enhance its savory flavor. The garden was full of vibrant red and green bell peppers ready for harvest. The reporters began to pepper the politician with difficult questions during the press conference. Hailstones started to pepper the windshield as the storm intensified.

english_meaning: To shoot repeatedly with many bullets. To hit a target with numerous bullets from one or more firearms. To subject a person, vehicle, or structure to heavy gunfire. Figuratively, it can mean to overwhelm something with a large number of similar actions, although this usage is less common.
synonyms: ["Riddle with bullets","Spray with bullets","Blast with gunfire","Shoot repeatedly","Fire upon","Strafe","Attack with gunfire","Saturate with gunfire"]
example_sentence: The attackers peppered the vehicle with bullets during the ambush. The wall was peppered with bullets after the exchange of gunfire. Witnesses said the building was peppered with bullets throughout the night. The armed group peppered the checkpoint with bullets before fleeing.

english_meaning: A small, dried berry of the black pepper plant used as a pungent spice. A tiny, insignificant, or nominal amount of something, especially in legal contexts. A physical object representing a token payment or consideration in a contract. The fruit of the Piper nigrum plant harvested before full maturity. Something that is very small or of very little value.
example_sentence: She ground a single peppercorn over the soup for a hint of heat. The lease was granted for a peppercorn rent to satisfy legal requirements. He sorted through the spice jar to find every dried peppercorn. A peppercorn payment is often used to make a contract legally binding.

english_meaning: A species of mint plant that produces a pungent oil used for flavoring. A hard or soft candy flavored with the aromatic oil of this plant. A cooling sensation or flavor derived from menthol found in the plant. Something that is colored or striped like traditional peppermint candy, typically red and white. A medicinal herb used to aid digestion and soothe headaches.
example_sentence: She sipped a warm cup of peppermint tea to soothe her upset stomach. The candy cane had a strong peppermint flavor that reminded him of Christmas. Peppermint oil is often used in aromatherapy to help clear the sinuses. The gardener planted peppermint in a pot to prevent it from spreading all over the yard.

english_meaning: Out of every hundred, used to express a proportion or rate. A fraction or ratio with one hundred as the denominator. The symbol or term representing parts per hundred. Another spelling of percent.
example_sentence: The interest rate is five per cent per annum. Ninety per cent of students passed the test. The discount is twenty per cent off the original price. Inflation increased by three per cent last year.

english_meaning: A daily allowance provided for expenses, particularly for those traveling for work. It is a Latin phrase meaning 'by the day'. It usually covers meals, lodging, and incidental costs.
example_sentence: The company provides a generous per diem for out-of-town business trips. He submitted his receipts to claim his per diem allowance. Many consultants prefer a per diem rate over a flat salary. The per diem for this city is higher due to the cost of living.

english_meaning: To become aware or conscious of something through the senses. To understand or think of someone or something in a particular way. To notice.
example_sentence: I could perceive a change in his tone. Children perceive the world differently from adults. She perceived him as trustworthy. He perceived a slight movement in the bushes. How you perceive a problem affects how you solve it.

english_meaning: Out of every hundred, used to express a proportion or rate. A fraction or ratio with one hundred as the denominator. For or in every hundred. The symbol % representing parts per hundred.
example_sentence: Fifty percent of the budget went to education. The battery is charged to one hundred percent. There is a ten percent chance of rain today. Housing costs increased by seven percent.

english_meaning: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. A proportion or share in relation to a whole. The result obtained by multiplying a quantity by a percent. A part of a whole expressed as a fraction of one hundred.
example_sentence: A large percentage of the population lives in cities. What percentage of students passed the exam? The percentage increase was significant. Sales increased by fifteen percentage points.

english_meaning: A value on a scale of one hundred that indicates the percentage of a distribution that is equal to or below it. A statistical measure showing the relative standing of a value in a dataset. One of the ninety-nine values that divide a set of data into one hundred equal parts.
example_sentence: She scored in the ninetieth percentile on the exam. The child's height is in the seventy-fifth percentile for his age. Percentiles help compare individual performance to a larger group. Income percentiles show wealth distribution.

english_meaning: Able to be seen, heard, or noticed. Recognizable, especially with the senses or the mind.
example_sentence: There was a perceptible change in her attitude. The improvement in his health is clearly perceptible. A perceptible smell of smoke filled the room. There is a perceptible difference between the two designs. His nervousness was perceptible to everyone.

english_meaning: In a way that is noticeable or able to be perceived. To a degree that can be detected by the senses. In a manner that is recognizable or observable. Noticeably or discernibly.
example_sentence: The temperature dropped perceptibly after sunset. She was perceptibly nervous during the interview. The quality of his work improved perceptibly. The room grew perceptibly darker as clouds covered the sun.

english_meaning: An idea, a belief or an image you have as a result of how you see or understand something. Thinking with care
example_sentence: When you listen, perception in involved while perception is not involved in hearing.

english_meaning: Having or showing sensitive insight and understanding. Able to notice and understand things quickly and accurately. Showing keen awareness and good judgment. Having the ability to perceive or recognize things clearly.
example_sentence: She made several perceptive comments about the issue. He is a perceptive observer of human nature. The critic wrote a perceptive review of the film. Teachers need to be perceptive to students' needs.

english_meaning: In a manner showing sensitive insight and understanding. With keen awareness and good judgment. In a way that demonstrates the ability to notice and understand things quickly. With perceptiveness or discernment.
example_sentence: She spoke perceptively about the challenges ahead. He analyzed the situation perceptively. The author writes perceptively about human relationships. They commented perceptively on the social issues.

english_meaning: The quality of having or showing sensitive insight and understanding. The ability to notice and understand things quickly and accurately. Keen awareness and good judgment. The capacity to perceive or recognize things clearly.
example_sentence: Her perceptiveness helped her understand complex situations. The therapist's perceptiveness made patients feel understood. His perceptiveness as a manager improved team morale. Perceptiveness is a valuable trait in leadership.

english_meaning: A place where a bird rests, especially a branch or bar. A high or narrow place where someone sits. To sit or rest on something, especially something high or narrow. A type of freshwater fish.
example_sentence: The parrot sat on its perch. She perched on the edge of the chair. The child perched on his father’s shoulders. Fishermen caught several perch in the lake. From his high perch he could see the whole valley.

english_meaning: To filter gradually through a porous surface or substance. To spread slowly through an area, group, or system. To prepare coffee by passing hot water through ground coffee.
example_sentence: Rainwater percolates through the soil. New ideas began to percolate through the team. The coffee is percolating in the kitchen. News of the change percolated slowly to the staff. Water percolates down to underground reserves.

english_meaning: Striking, hitting, or tapping, especially to produce sound or in medical examination. The act of striking one object against another to produce sound, especially in music. A group of musical instruments that are played by being struck, shaken, or scraped, such as drums. A medical technique in which a doctor taps parts of the body to check internal conditions.
example_sentence: The drummer used percussion to create a powerful rhythm. The doctor performed percussion on the patient's chest. African music often relies heavily on percussion instruments. The sound of percussion filled the concert hall.

english_meaning: A variant spelling of 'per diem', referring to a daily allowance for expenses or a daily rate of pay. It is used to cover costs incurred while on duty away from one's home base. It ensures that employees do not spend their own money on work-related travel.
example_sentence: The perdiem rate for the international conference was set at fifty dollars. She managed to save some of her perdiem by eating at inexpensive diners. The contract specifies a set perdiem for all field researchers. Does the government provide a perdiem for domestic travel?

english_meaning: The state of eternal punishment and suffering after death. Complete spiritual ruin or destruction. A condition of irreversible loss or moral downfall.
example_sentence: The preacher warned sinners about the path that leads to perdition. His greed and arrogance finally led him to perdition. She prayed that her soul would be saved from eternal perdition. War brings nations to the edge of perdition.

english_meaning: To travel or wander from place to place, especially on foot. To journey through various regions or countries. To roam widely, often for pleasure or exploration. To make a long, meandering trip.
example_sentence: He spent his youth peregrinating across Europe. They peregrinated through the countryside for weeks. Poets often peregrinate in search of inspiration. She loves to peregrinate whenever she gets a chance.

english_meaning: In a commanding or decisive way that does not allow refusal or contradiction. Acting in a manner that is authoritative, final, or insistent, often leaving no room for debate, objection, or delay. It conveys firmness and urgency.
example_sentence: She peremptorily told him to leave the room. The manager peremptorily rejected the proposal without discussion. He peremptorily demanded an explanation from the staff. The teacher peremptorily ended the meeting when the students argued.

english_meaning: Insisting on immediate attention or obedience; not allowing refusal or delay. Showing a commanding, authoritative, or arrogant manner that expects compliance without question. Often used to describe a tone, order, or manner that leaves no room for discussion.
example_sentence: The teacher gave a peremptory order to start the exam immediately. She spoke in a peremptory tone that allowed no argument. His peremptory dismissal of the proposal shocked everyone. The manager’s peremptory instructions left no room for discussion.

english_meaning: Something that lasts for a long time or keeps returning every year. Something that continues for a very long time or happens repeatedly over many years. It is often used for plants that live more than two years and regrow every season, or for issues and ideas that keep coming back again and again.
example_sentence: Water shortage is a perennial problem in many cities. Roses are perennial plants in suitable climates. She has a perennial interest in history. Traffic congestion is a perennial issue in big cities.

english_meaning: Treacherous, deceitful, not loyal. Betraying confidence. False or untrustworthy. Disloyal in relationships or duties. Intentionally deceptive. A person who betrays trust or acts dishonestly. It is used for someone who is deliberately unfaithful or breaks promises in a harmful way.
example_sentence: He made a perfidious deal behind his friend’s back. The perfidious spy leaked secrets to the enemy. She felt hurt by his perfidious behavior. History remembers him as a perfidious leader who betrayed his people.

english_meaning: The state of being deceitful and untrustworthy. It refers to a specific act of betrayal or a general quality of treachery. It characterizes the deliberate violation of a promise, vow, or allegiance.
example_sentence: The general was shocked by the perfidy of his most trusted lieutenant. He could not believe the absolute perfidy of his business partner. The document exposed the perfidy that led to the collapse of the treaty. She was devastated by the hidden perfidy within her own family.

english_meaning: To make a hole or holes in something. To pierce, puncture, or create openings in a surface or object, often for a functional purpose such as ventilation, passage, or separation.
example_sentence: She used a pin to perforate the envelope. The ticket is perforated so it can be easily torn. The metal sheet was perforated with small holes for drainage. The doctor needed to perforate the skin to draw blood.

english_meaning: A hole or series of small holes made through something. The act or result of making a hole or multiple small holes in a material. It can occur naturally, accidentally, or deliberately. The word is commonly used in medicine for holes in body organs, in engineering for punctured materials, and in printing for lines of tiny holes that make paper easy to tear.
example_sentence: The doctor treated the stomach perforation immediately. The paper has a perforation along the edge for easy tearing. Rust caused perforation in the metal pipe. The injury resulted in a perforation of the eardrum.

english_meaning: By necessity or force of circumstances. Unavoidably or inevitably. Because circumstances make it so. As a matter of compulsion rather than choice.
example_sentence: The road was blocked, so he perforce had to take another route. She perforce accepted the decision of the committee. Being the only doctor available, he perforce attended to every patient. The heavy rain perforce delayed our journey.

english_meaning: To carry out an action, task, or duty. To present a play, piece of music, or other entertainment to an audience. To function or work in a particular way, especially well or badly. To fulfil a promise, contract, or obligation.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed the operation successfully. The band will perform live on Saturday night. The engine performs well even in cold weather. Each employee must perform the duties listed in the contract.

english_meaning: The act of presenting a play, concert, or other form of entertainment before an audience. The way in which a person, machine, or organisation carries out a task or function. The level of success achieved in a particular activity. The action or process of carrying out a duty, task, or promise.
example_sentence: The evening performance was completely sold out. Her performance in the exam was outstanding. The car's performance improves after servicing. The company reviewed the performance of every department.

english_meaning: A sweet or pleasant-smelling liquid that people put on their skin or clothes. A fragrant substance made from oils and alcohol used to give a pleasant scent. A pleasant or sweet smell, especially of flowers. To give something a pleasant smell. To fill the air or a place with a sweet scent.
example_sentence: She wore a delicate perfume that reminded him of roses. The flowers perfumed the entire garden with their sweet scent. He bought an expensive French perfume for his mother's birthday. The evening air was perfumed with the fragrance of jasmine.

english_meaning: Carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection. Done as a routine duty without real interest or care. Hasty and superficial. Performed merely as a formality, lacking enthusiasm or thoroughness.
example_sentence: He gave a perfunctory greeting and walked away. The manager made a perfunctory inspection of the factory. Her apology sounded perfunctory and insincere. The guard cast a perfunctory glance at our identity cards. The committee gave only a perfunctory review to the long report.

english_meaning: A trained medical specialist who operates the heart-lung machine during cardiac surgery. A healthcare professional responsible for maintaining a patient's blood circulation and oxygen supply while the heart is stopped.
example_sentence: The perfusionist prepared the heart-lung machine before the operation. A skilled perfusionist is essential in every cardiac surgery team. The perfusionist monitored the blood flow throughout the procedure. He studied for years to qualify as a perfusionist.

english_meaning: Maybe, possibly. Used when something is not certain and there is a chance that it may happen or may be true.
example_sentence: Perhaps he will come tomorrow. She is perhaps the best student in the class. We could perhaps try a different method. Perhaps it will rain later today.

english_meaning: Full of danger or risk. Hazardous. Highly dangerous. Involving serious threat to life, safety, or well-being. Risky and uncertain in outcome. Used to describe situations, journeys, conditions, or actions that carry a high likelihood of harm, injury, loss, or failure.
example_sentence: The climbers began a perilous ascent of the icy mountain. Driving on these narrow roads at night is perilous. The country is going through a perilous economic situation. Sailors faced a perilous journey across the stormy sea. Ignoring safety warnings can be perilous for workers.

english_meaning: The continuous line forming the outer boundary of a closed figure or area. The total length of the boundary of a shape, measured in units. The outer edge or limit of a place, such as a camp or airfield. A defensive boundary around a military position.
example_sentence: Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle. Guards patrolled the perimeter of the camp all night. A high fence runs around the perimeter of the airport. The perimeter of the field is nearly two kilometres.

english_meaning: Traveling from place to place, especially for work. Someone who moves frequently or travels around rather than staying in one location. It can describe a lifestyle, occupation, or a scholar who moves while teaching. Originally linked to Aristotle, who taught while walking.
example_sentence: The peripatetic teacher moved between schools in the region every week. As a peripatetic musician, she performed in towns across the country. His peripatetic lifestyle made it hard to maintain long-term friendships. The peripatetic philosopher preferred discussing ideas while walking through the garden.

english_meaning: Relating to or situated on the edge or periphery of something. Of secondary or minor importance in relation to the main object. It describes things that are on the outside or not part of the main focus.
example_sentence: The system uses several peripheral devices like printers and scanners. They were living in a peripheral settlement far from the city center. Financial issues are often peripheral to the main cause of the argument. The expansion of peripheral vision is essential for athletes during a game.

english_meaning: The outer limits or edge of an area or object. The less important part of a group, subject, or activity. It represents the boundary or the surface of a specific region.
example_sentence: The industrial estate is located on the periphery of the town. These issues are on the periphery of the current political debate. New housing developments are springing up on the city's periphery. Scientists are exploring the periphery of the solar system.

english_meaning: To die, especially in a sudden violent way. To be lost or destroyed. To lose life, to come to an end, to be ruined, or to stop existing. To fail completely. To decay or rot. To be destroyed slowly. To pass away spiritually or emotionally. To disappear beyond recovery.
example_sentence: A family of four perished in the fire. Thousands perished at the hands of the invading forces. Early buildings were made of wood and have perished. Three hundred people perished in the earthquake. One people perished in the plane crash.

english_meaning: Likely to decay or go bad quickly, especially food. Not lasting or enduring. A food item that spoils easily.
example_sentence: Milk and fish are perishable items. Perishable goods must be kept refrigerated. The truck carried a load of perishable food. Fresh vegetables are highly perishable. Store perishables in a cool place.

english_meaning: The crime of lying while under oath in court. A serious legal offense in which a person knowingly gives false statements after swearing to tell the truth in a court of law or in an official legal setting.
example_sentence: He was charged with perjury for lying during the trial. Perjury can lead to heavy fines or imprisonment. The witness denied committing perjury in court. Giving false testimony under oath is considered perjury.

english_meaning: An additional benefit given to employees besides their salary. To become more cheerful, lively, or interesting. To lift up something quickly.
example_sentence: The company offers many perks to its employees. A cup of coffee will perk you up. She perked up when she heard the good news. Free health insurance is a great perk. The dog perked its ears at the sound.

english_meaning: A system of agricultural and social design based on patterns found in natural ecosystems. A holistic approach to land use that seeks sustainable, self-sufficient, and ecologically balanced habitats. The practice of integrating plants, animals, people, water, and structures while minimizing waste.
example_sentence: The farmer redesigned his land using the principles of permaculture. Permaculture encourages diverse crops that support one another naturally. She studied permaculture to create a self-sustaining garden. The community began a permaculture project to reduce waste and improve soil health.

english_meaning: Ground consisting of soil, sediment, or rock that remains at or below freezing for at least two consecutive years. A permanently frozen layer found mainly in polar and high-altitude regions. Terrain underlain by such frozen ground.
example_sentence: Melting permafrost is releasing trapped methane into the atmosphere. Scientists are monitoring permafrost thaw in the Arctic tundra. Buildings on permafrost require special foundations to prevent sinking. The permafrost beneath the soil has remained frozen for thousands of years.

english_meaning: A permanent and stable URL that points directly to a specific web page, post, or item of online content. A hyperlink intended to remain valid even when other parts of a website change. To create or provide such a permanent link.
example_sentence: She copied the permalink to share the blog post with her friends. Every article on the site has a unique permalink. The permalink remained active after the website was redesigned. He saved the permalink so he could return to the article later.

english_meaning: The state or quality of lasting forever or for an indefinitely long time. The condition of remaining fixed, stable, or unchanged. The ability of a material, record, or effect to endure without fading or deterioration.
example_sentence: The permanence of the tattoo made her think carefully before getting it. Scientists study the permanence of climate changes in ecosystems. The artist valued the permanence of oil paint over watercolor. Few things in life have true permanence.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being permanent, lasting, or enduring without interruption. A condition of long-term stability or fixed legal or employment status. The prospect of remaining in a place or position indefinitely.
example_sentence: The employee sought permanency after years of temporary contracts. The agreement was intended to give the arrangement greater permanency. He wanted the permanency of a stable home for his children. The committee debated the permanency of the new policy.

english_meaning: Lasting or intended to last for a very long time. Not temporary or changing. Continuing without interruption or end. A long-lasting hair treatment that creates curls, used as a noun.
example_sentence: She was offered a permanent position at the company. The accident left him with permanent hearing loss. They built a permanent shelter for the flood victims. She had a permanent done at the salon last week.

english_meaning: The state or quality of a material or membrane that causes it to allow liquids or gases to pass through it. In electromagnetism, it is the measure of the ability of a material to support the formation of a magnetic field within itself. It defines how easily a substance can be penetrated.
example_sentence: The permeability of the soil affects how quickly water drains away. High permeability is essential for efficient magnetic cores in transformers. Doctors check the permeability of cell membranes during the study. The heavy clay has very low permeability compared to sandy soil.

english_meaning: Allowing liquids or gases to pass through it. Capable of being permeated or penetrated, especially by fluids. It describes a surface or substance that has pores or openings.
example_sentence: Sandstone is a permeable rock that can hold significant amounts of water. The scientist used a permeable membrane for the filtration experiment. You should wear permeable clothing that allows sweat to evaporate. Certain types of soil are highly permeable to chemical pollutants.

english_meaning: To spread throughout something. To pervade or saturate every part of an object or space. It often refers to a smell, a feeling, or a liquid spreading through a medium.
example_sentence: The smell of fresh coffee began to permeate the entire house. A feeling of deep sadness seemed to permeate the atmosphere. Water will permeate through the cracks in the old concrete floor. New ideas began to permeate the traditional society slowly.

english_meaning: Allowed by rules, law, or custom. Acceptable within certain limits.
example_sentence: Smoking is not permissible in this area. The permissible limit of noise has been fixed by law. Photography is permissible only with a special pass. It is permissible to ask questions during the lecture. Only permissible items may be brought inside.

english_meaning: Allowing or tolerating a great deal of freedom, especially in behavior. Not strict in enforcing rules. Granting permission or consent easily. Liberal or lenient in attitude, especially toward moral matters.
example_sentence: His parents were very permissive and let him do as he pleased. Some schools have a permissive attitude toward mobile phones. The society has become more permissive over the years. A permissive teacher may lose control of the class.

english_meaning: The quality or condition of being permissive; excessive tolerance of behavior. A liberal attitude that allows a wide range of freedom. Leniency, especially in moral or social matters.
example_sentence: Critics blame the rising crime rate on social permissiveness. The permissiveness of modern parents worries the elders. Too much permissiveness can spoil children. The book explores the permissiveness of the sixties.

english_meaning: To officially allow someone to do something. To make something possible. An official document that gives someone permission to do or have something.
example_sentence: The rules do not permit smoking in this building. If time permits, we will visit the museum. You need a permit to fish in this lake. He was granted a work permit. Please show your parking permit at the gate.

english_meaning: The ability of a substance to store electrical energy in an electric field. It is a measure of how an electric field affects, and is affected by, a dielectric medium. This property is crucial in the design of capacitors and electronic components.
example_sentence: The permittivity of a material determines its response to an electric field. High permittivity materials are used to increase the capacitance of electronic devices. Vacuum has a constant permittivity known as the vacuum permittivity. Engineers must calculate the permittivity of the insulation for safety.

english_meaning: Very harmful or destructive, often in a way that is not obvious at first. Something that causes serious harm or has a damaging effect, often gradually or subtly. It can refer to physical, moral, social, or psychological harm.
example_sentence: Pernicious lies spread quickly. Smoking has a pernicious effect on health. The pernicious rumors damaged her reputation. A pernicious weed invaded the farmland. Pernicious habits can slowly ruin one’s life.

english_meaning: Relating to or situated near the ear, especially the bones surrounding the inner ear. Pertaining to the periotic region of the skull. Used in anatomical and zoological contexts to describe the bone structure around the ear.
example_sentence: The perotic bone plays an important role in protecting the delicate structures of the inner ear. Researchers studying whale evolution have focused particularly on the perotic structure of fossil specimens. The perotic region of the skull was carefully examined during the post-mortem examination. In dolphins, the perotic bone is unusually dense and is thought to be connected to their sound reception.

english_meaning: To commit or carry out, usually something harmful or illegal. To perform, execute, or be responsible for an action, often a crime, wrongdoing, or immoral act. It often implies intentionality and culpability.
example_sentence: The thieves perpetrated a series of burglaries in the neighborhood. He perpetrated a fraud that cost the company millions. The government condemned those who perpetrated violence during the protests. She tried to cover up the mistake instead of admitting she had perpetrated it.

english_meaning: The act of committing a harmful, illegal, or immoral action. The process or act of carrying out an action, usually one that is wrongful, criminal, or unethical. It often implies responsibility for causing harm or committing a crime.
example_sentence: The perpetration of the fraud was discovered by the auditors. Authorities are investigating the perpetration of cybercrimes. The law punishes the perpetration of violent acts. Witnesses testified about the perpetration of the robbery.

english_meaning: A person who commits a harmful, illegal, or immoral act. Someone who carries out a crime, wrongdoing, or any act that causes harm to others. This can include crimes like theft, assault, fraud, or violence. The term emphasizes the responsibility for committing the act.
example_sentence: The police arrested the perpetrator of the robbery. Witnesses identified the perpetrator of the cyber attack. Society must hold perpetrators of violence accountable. The perpetrator of the fraud was sentenced to five years in prison.

english_meaning: Never ending or changing. Occurring repeatedly so frequently that it seems endless and uninterrupted. Continuing forever or for an indefinitely long period of time.
example_sentence: The mountain peaks are covered in perpetual snow throughout the year. He lived in a state of perpetual fear during the war. The contract includes a perpetual right to use the brand name. She was tired of his perpetual complaints about the weather.

english_meaning: In a way that never ends or changes. Continuously. Constantly. Endlessly. Forever. All the time. Without interruption or pause. Used to describe an action, state, or condition that continues without stopping or that seems to happen again and again over a long period of time.
example_sentence: She is perpetually late for important meetings. The factory operates perpetually, day and night. He seems perpetually worried about his children's future. The mountain peaks are perpetually covered with snow. My little brother is perpetually asking questions about everything.

english_meaning: The state or quality of lasting forever. In perpetuity means for all time. A payment or annuity that continues indefinitely.
example_sentence: The land was granted to the family in perpetuity. He wants his legacy to live in perpetuity. The trust pays a small sum in perpetuity. This right is guaranteed in perpetuity by the contract. Fame in perpetuity is difficult to achieve.

english_meaning: To confuse and worry someone slightly by being difficult to understand or solve. To cause someone to be confused or uncertain over something that is not understood. To make more complicated. To make intricate or involved. To throw into a state of mental uncertainty.
example_sentence: They were perplexed by her response. The disease has continued to perplex doctors. The symptoms of the disease have continued to perplex her doctors. Let's not perplex the issue further with irrelevant concerns.

english_meaning: A state of confusion or uncertainty when something is difficult to understand. A mental condition in which a person feels confused because something is complex, unclear, or difficult to explain or solve. It often happens when a situation has many possibilities and no clear answer.
example_sentence: The difficult question caused great perplexity among students. She looked at the map in complete perplexity. His sudden silence created perplexity in the meeting. There was a sense of perplexity when the results were announced.

english_meaning: To treat someone cruelly or unfairly over a long period. To oppress people because of their beliefs, race, or identity. To harass or annoy someone persistently. To subject a person or group to hostility and ill-treatment. To make someone suffer because of who they are. To persecute means to repeatedly inflict suffering, punishment, or unjust treatment on individuals or groups, often due to differences in religion, politics, or ethnicity.
example_sentence: The regime continued to persecute anyone who opposed its policies. Throughout history, rulers have persecuted people for their religious beliefs. She felt the management was trying to persecute her for raising concerns. Innocent civilians should never be persecuted for the actions of others. Journalists are often persecuted in countries that suppress free speech.

english_meaning: The act of treating someone cruelly or unfairly, especially because of their race, religion, or political beliefs. Continuous mistreatment or oppression of a person or group. Harassment and ill-treatment based on identity or beliefs. Systematic cruelty inflicted on individuals or communities. The suffering caused by such ill-treatment. Persecution involves repeated, organized hostility against people because of who they are or what they believe, often resulting in serious harm, discrimination, or even death.
example_sentence: Many families fled the country to escape religious persecution. The persecution of minorities has been condemned by human rights organizations. He wrote a powerful memoir about the persecution he endured during the war. Throughout history, several communities have suffered persecution for their beliefs. The new law aims to protect citizens from persecution.

english_meaning: An irrational and persistent belief that other people are trying to harm, cheat, or mistreat one. A psychological condition marked by constant feelings of being targeted or plotted against. Extreme suspicion of others without real evidence.
example_sentence: His persecution complex made him distrust his closest friends. She developed a persecution complex after years of bullying. A persecution complex can seriously damage relationships. He blamed everyone, showing a clear persecution complex.

english_meaning: A person who treats others cruelly or unfairly, especially because of their race, religion, or beliefs. Someone who continuously harasses, oppresses, or torments another person. An oppressor who causes suffering to a particular group.
example_sentence: The persecutor was finally brought before the court. Many families fled from their persecutors. He turned from a victim into a persecutor. History remembers the names of both martyrs and persecutors.

english_meaning: Continued effort to do or achieve something despite difficulties, failure, or opposition. Steady persistence in a course of action or purpose. The quality of not giving up easily.
example_sentence: Her perseverance finally brought her success. Perseverance is more important than natural talent. With perseverance, he completed the difficult project. The teacher praised the students for their perseverance.

english_meaning: Continuing to try despite difficulties. Someone who continues striving toward a goal regardless of hardship, delay, criticism, or repeated failure.
example_sentence: She remained perseverant even after failing the exam twice. A perseverant student practices every day to improve his skills. His perseverant attitude helped him build a successful business. The scientist was perseverant in her research despite many setbacks.

english_meaning: To repeat or continue an action, thought, or utterance insistently or redundantly. In psychology, to continue doing something even when it is no longer useful or appropriate.
example_sentence: The patient tended to perseverate on the same question. Children may perseverate on a favourite topic. He continued to perseverate about the accident for weeks. Do not perseverate on minor mistakes. Some anxiety disorders make people perseverate on worries.

english_meaning: To continue in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition. To persist in doing something despite obstacles or discouragement. To keep going steadily despite problems.
example_sentence: She chose to persevere with the project even after several major setbacks threatened to derail it entirely. He was told to persevere with the medication despite the unpleasant early side effects. If you persevere long enough, most skills that seem impossible at first will become natural. The young athlete continued to persevere through injury and disappointment to reach the highest level. Only those who persevere when others give up will ultimately achieve lasting success.

english_meaning: A round orange fruit with smooth skin and sweet, soft flesh when fully ripe. An autumn fruit that can taste astringent before ripening. The tree that produces this fruit. A deep orange colour like that of the ripe fruit.
example_sentence: Persimmons ripen on the tree late in autumn. An unripe persimmon leaves a dry feeling in the mouth. She arranged the persimmons in a wooden bowl. Dried persimmon is a traditional winter treat.

english_meaning: Keep doing something or continuing to exist despite difficulty or opposition. To continue firmly in an action, belief, or situation even when facing challenges, resistance, or repeated failures. It also refers to something that continues for a long time without stopping.
example_sentence: The belief that the earth was flat persisted for many centuries. If the symptoms persist, consult your doctor. If you persist in upsetting her, I will have to punish you. The detective stubbornly persisted with his questions.

english_meaning: The quality that allows someone to continue doing something or trying to do something even though it is difficult or opposed by other people. The state of continuing to exist for a long period of time
example_sentence:
He admired her dogged persistence in pursuing the job.
His persistence in asking for a raise was finally rewarded.
She has shown a lot of persistence. His persistence was finally rewarded when the insurance company agreed to pay for the damage.

english_meaning: Continuing firmly despite difficulties, obstacles, or opposition; not giving up easily. A person, effort, behavior, problem, or condition that continues for a long time or keeps trying until success is achieved. It often refers to determination, perseverance, and consistency in pursuing a goal despite challenges.
example_sentence: She was persistent in her studies and eventually topped the class. Despite several rejections, he remained persistent and achieved his goal. The persistent rain continued throughout the night. A persistent employee often succeeds where others give up.

english_meaning: Having a pleasant and attractive appearance and manner. Friendly and easy to get along with. Charming in a way that makes a good impression on others.
example_sentence: The new receptionist is bright and personable. Clients like him because he is so personable. A personable manner helps a great deal in sales. She was personable and confident during the interview.

english_meaning: The process of adapting a product, service, message, or experience to an individual’s needs, preferences, or behaviour. The act of adding a name or unique detail to make something personal. The attribution of human or personal qualities to something.
example_sentence: The website offers personalisation based on reading habits. Gift personalisation includes engraving a name. Personalisation can make lessons more relevant to students. The campaign used email personalisation to improve responses.

english_meaning: To adapt or design something for a particular individual’s needs, preferences, or identity. To add a name, message, or unique detail to something. To treat or present something in personal rather than general terms.
example_sentence: You can personalise the bag with your name. Teachers personalise lessons for different learners. She personalised her desk with family photographs. Try not to personalise a general criticism.

english_meaning: Made or designed to meet the specific needs, tastes, or identity of a particular person. Adapted or customized for an individual rather than kept generic. Bearing a person's name or other unique details.
example_sentence: She received a personalised gift with her name engraved on it. The company sent personalised recommendations based on his browsing history. He ordered a personalised number plate for his new car. The teacher created a personalised learning plan for each student.

english_meaning: The process of designing or adapting something to fit an individual's needs or preferences. The act of making a product, service, message, or experience unique to a particular person. The use of personal details to make communication more relevant.
example_sentence: Personalization of marketing emails has increased customer engagement. The app's personalization features let users customize their dashboards. Retailers are investing heavily in personalization technology. Personalization can make a standard product feel unique.

english_meaning: To design or alter something to suit an individual's particular needs, tastes, or identity. To make something personal by adding a name, initials, message, or distinctive details. To present or interpret an issue in terms of a particular person.
example_sentence: You can personalize your phone case with a favorite photograph. The store can personalize each invitation with the guest's name. She personalizes her emails instead of sending generic replies. Many apps let users personalize their home screens.

english_meaning: Adapted specifically for a particular person, often including that person's name or preferences. Made unique to reflect individual identity, interests, or requirements. Addressed to or directed at a named individual.
example_sentence: He gave her a personalized necklace with her initials on it. The website provides personalized content based on user preferences. They designed a personalized fitness plan for the athlete. The card came with a personalized message from the sender.

english_meaning: A person who has a lot of a particular quality or characteristic. The practice of representing objects, qualities, etc as humans, in art and literature; an object, quality, etc that is represented in this way.
example_sentence: She was the personification of elegance. The personification of autumn in Keats’s poem. Janis Joplin was the personification of the '60s female rock singer. He was usually the personification of kindness. He is the personification of optimism.

english_meaning: To give human qualities to something non human. To describe an object, idea, or natural force as if it were a human, or to represent an idea clearly through a person or character
example_sentence: The writer personified death as a silent visitor. In the poem, the wind is personified as a restless child. The teacher said the statue personifies freedom. Her calm attitude personified patience and strength.

english_meaning: The people who work for an organisation, business, or armed force. The staff considered as a group rather than as individuals. The department of a company that deals with hiring, training, and welfare of employees. Human resources available for a particular task or service.
example_sentence: All personnel must wear identity badges inside the plant. Military personnel were deployed to help the flood victims. The personnel department handles all recruitment. Trained medical personnel arrived within an hour.

english_meaning: A particular way of thinking about something. The art of drawing so as to give the effect of solidity and depth. The ability to view things in their true relations or relative importance.
example_sentence: Try to see the issue from a different perspective. The painting shows an excellent use of perspective. Travel gives you a broader perspective on life. In perspective, the problem is not so serious. Every person has their own perspective on happiness.

english_meaning: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things. It describes someone possessing acute mental vision or discernment. It implies the ability to notice, comprehend, and judge things quickly and accurately.
example_sentence: The perspicacious detective noticed the subtle clue that everyone else had overlooked. Her perspicacious analysis of the financial market helped the company avoid ruin. A perspicacious teacher quickly identifies the strengths and weaknesses of her students. His perspicacious observations during the meeting impressed the entire board.

english_meaning: The process of sweating. The moisture or salty liquid exuded through the pores of the skin. It is the body's natural way of cooling down during physical exertion or heat.
example_sentence: The athlete was soaked in perspiration after the long race. Perspiration beaded on his forehead as he waited for the results. Deodorant helps to control the odor associated with perspiration. The humidity made the perspiration cling to her skin uncomfortably.

english_meaning: To give out sweat through the pores of the skin as a result of heat, physical exertion, or stress. To exude a salty liquid from the body to regulate temperature. This is a vital biological function for thermoregulation.
example_sentence: The runners began to perspire heavily as the temperature rose. He started to perspire under the bright lights of the television studio. It is natural to perspire when you exercise intensely. The spicy food made him perspire almost immediately.

english_meaning: To convince someone to do or believe something. To cause someone to do something or accept a belief or opinion through reasoning, argument, or appeal
example_sentence: She persuaded him to join the team. I tried to persuade my parents to let me travel. The advertisement persuaded many people to buy the product. He was persuaded by his friends to attend the party.

english_meaning: Able to convince someone or make them agree with your idea. Able to shape opinions through strong reasoning. Describing communication that leads someone toward agreement. Showing skill in arguing or presenting ideas. Having qualities that encourage acceptance or belief. A person, speech or writing that has the power to influence others through logic, emotion or strong reasoning. A persuasive statement makes people believe or accept something.
example_sentence: Her persuasive speech changed the committee’s decision. He wrote a persuasive email to convince the manager. The lawyer presented a persuasive argument in court. Good teachers use persuasive methods to motivate students.

english_meaning: To be relevant or applicable to something. To relate to a particular subject. To belong to as a part or attribute.
example_sentence: The rules pertain to all employees of the company. This chapter pertains to modern history. His questions pertain to the safety of the workers. The evidence pertains directly to the case. All rights pertaining to the property belong to the owner.

english_meaning: Being related to or connected with something. Concerning a particular matter or subject.
example_sentence: Please submit all documents pertaining to the case. Laws pertaining to child safety are very strict. Books pertaining to history line the top shelf. All matters pertaining to salary must be discussed with HR. She read every article pertaining to the topic.

english_meaning: The quality of being directly related, relevant, or appropriate to a particular matter. Connection or applicability to the subject under discussion. The state of being to the point. Used to describe how meaningful, useful, or fitting a comment, fact, evidence, or question is in a given context.
example_sentence: The pertinence of his question impressed the entire panel. Please limit your remarks to matters of pertinence. The lawyer challenged the pertinence of the new evidence. Her research has clear pertinence to current social issues. The teacher praised the pertinence of the student’s example.

english_meaning: The quality of being relevant, appropriate, or directly related to the matter under consideration. Relevance to a particular subject or situation. The state of being connected with or applicable to a topic being discussed. Suitability to the context. The condition of having a clear and meaningful relation to the issue at hand.
example_sentence: The pertinency of his remarks impressed the entire committee. The lawyer questioned the pertinency of the evidence to the case. We must consider the pertinency of these statistics before drawing any conclusion. The teacher praised the pertinency of the student's answer. Her comments lacked pertinency to the issue under discussion.

english_meaning: Relevant or applicable to a particular matter. Apposite and relating directly to the subject being considered. Having a clear and decisive relevance to the task at hand.
example_sentence: She asked several pertinent questions during the business meeting. The lawyer presented pertinent evidence that changed the course of the trial. Please include all pertinent details in your formal report. His comments were not pertinent to the current discussion.

english_meaning: To read something carefully and thoroughly. To examine or study a document in detail. To look through something, sometimes casually. To review written material with attention.
example_sentence: Please peruse the contract before signing it. She perused the old letters in the archive. He perused the menu while waiting for his friend. The lawyer perused every page of the file.

english_meaning: Spread widely throughout something. Existing in every part of a place, system, or experience, often in a way that is noticeable or hard to avoid.
example_sentence: The smell of smoke was pervasive throughout the building. Social media has a pervasive influence on modern culture. There is a pervasive sense of fear in the community after the incident. Technology has become so pervasive that it affects almost every part of daily life.

english_meaning: Showing a deliberate and obstinate desire to behave in a way that is unreasonable or unacceptable. Contrary to what is expected or reasonable. Sexually deviant.
example_sentence: He takes a perverse pleasure in making others uncomfortable. The court found the ruling to be perverse. Her perverse behaviour surprised everyone. It is perverse to reject such a fair offer. His perverse arguments confused the audience.

english_meaning: To distort, misuse, or corrupt something from its original purpose. A person whose behavior is considered abnormal or morally wrong, especially in a sexual context.
example_sentence: Some scientific discoveries have been perverted to create weapons of destruction. Some people believe that television can pervert the minds of children. Any reform will destroy and pervert our constitution. Her ideas have been shamelessly perverted to serve the president's propaganda campaign. The two police officers were charged with perverting the course of justice by fabricating evidence in the trial. These journalists are perverting the news. The will of the people is being perverted by their elected representatives.

english_meaning: To act illegally to prevent justice being done. To tell a lie or to do something in order to prevent the police, etc from finding out the truth about a crime. To act illegally to avoid punishment or to get the wrong person punished.
example_sentence: The official was charged with perverting the course of justice. He was charged with conspiring to pervert the course of justice. The two police officers were charged with perverting the course of justice by fabricating evidence in the trial.

english_meaning: Causing trouble, annoying. Troublesome, Vexatious. Causing a great deal of trouble, worrying, upsetting, or annoying. Characterized by violence, turbulent.
example_sentence: A pesky younger brother. Those pesky kids from next door have let the air out of my car tyres again!. No matter how often I weed the garden, those pesky weeds keep coming back. This was due to some pesky chickens that lived nearby who kept making noises and waking him up in the night. Summertime brings pesky mosquitos and thunderstorms which often produce more lightning than rain.

english_meaning: The tendency to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen. An attitude or outlook where a person expects negative outcomes, doubts positive results, and often focuses on problems or difficulties rather than solutions. It can affect decision-making, mood, and behavior.
example_sentence: His pessimism made him doubt the success of the project. Despite the evidence, her pessimism prevented her from trying new things. The book explores the consequences of extreme pessimism in society. Even in difficult times, he tried to overcome his pessimism with positive thinking.

english_meaning: A person who tends to see a worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen. Someone who habitually lacks hope or confidence in the future. A person who focuses on the negative side of any situation.
example_sentence: The pessimist predicted that the new business venture would fail within a month. Don't be such a pessimist; things might actually work out fine. As a pessimist, he always carries an umbrella even when the sun is shining. The pessimist's view of the economy discouraged many potential investors.

english_meaning: Expecting bad things to happen or something not to be successful, showing this. Thinking that bad things are more likely to happen or emphasizing the bad part of a situation. Expecting the worst possible outcome.
example_sentence: They appeared surprisingly pessimistic about their chances of winning. I think you're being far too pessimistic. The tone of the meeting was very pessimistic. The doctors are pessimistic (= not hopeful) about his chances of recovery. The film gives a very pessimistic view of human nature.

english_meaning: Causing or able to cause deadly disease. Highly destructive or harmful. Annoying, troublesome, or causing great irritation. Contagious or infectious in a figurative sense.
example_sentence: The pestilent plague wiped out half the city. Pestilent weeds overtook the garden. His pestilent remarks offended everyone in the room. The pestilent ideas spread like wildfire through the population.

english_meaning: A small habit or action that annoys someone again and again. Something minor but irritating that causes repeated annoyance to a person, even if others do not find it bothersome.
example_sentence: One of my biggest pet peeves is people being late. Loud chewing is a common pet peeve for many people. She said poor customer service is her pet peeve. Everyone has at least one pet peeve at work.

english_meaning: A metric prefix denoting a factor of one quadrillion (1015) of the base unit. Placed before units such as byte or watt to express very large amounts of data or energy. Represented by the symbol P in the International System of Units.
example_sentence: The telescope collects several petabytes of data each year. Global internet traffic is now measured in petabytes per month. A petabyte equals one thousand terabytes. The project archives more than two petabytes of satellite images.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,024 terabytes, or about one quadrillion bytes. A very large measure of data storage used by big organisations. A unit used to describe huge collections of digital information such as scientific or internet data.
example_sentence: The research centre stores several petabytes of data. One petabyte equals 1,024 terabytes. Social media platforms generate petabytes of information every day. The archive was moved to a petabyte-scale storage system.

english_meaning: Each of the segments of the corolla of a flower, which are modified leaves and are typically colored.
example_sentence: The rose petals were scattered all over the floor. Each petal of the flower was a vibrant shade of pink. She carefully pressed a flower petal inside her book. The wind blew the delicate petals off the cherry trees.

english_meaning: An equal-area world-map projection associated with Arno Peters. A rectangular map that preserves the relative sizes of land areas while distorting their shapes. A projection promoted as an alternative to maps that exaggerate high-latitude countries.
example_sentence: The class compared the Peters projection with the Mercator map. Africa occupies a more proportionate area on the Peters projection. The Peters projection preserves relative area rather than local shape. Some educators use the Peters projection to discuss map bias.

english_meaning: A synthetic opioid medicine used to relieve moderate to severe pain. A strong prescription painkiller also known as meperidine. A controlled drug that can cause dependence and serious side effects and is used under medical supervision.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed pethidine for severe postoperative pain. Pethidine must be administered under medical supervision. The nurse checked the dosage before giving the patient pethidine. Some hospitals now use alternatives to pethidine for pain relief.

english_meaning: The slender stalk that attaches a leaf blade to a plant stem. A stalk supporting certain plant structures or, in zoology, a narrow connecting part between body sections. The narrow waist between the thorax and abdomen in some insects.
example_sentence: The long petiole allows the leaf to reach toward the light. A tiny insect rested on the leaf’s petiole. The botanist measured each petiole before examining the blade. Damage to the petiole caused the leaf to droop.

english_meaning: A member of the lower middle class, especially a small business owner or self-employed person. A person regarded as having conventional, materialistic, or narrowly middle-class values. Relating to the social group between the working class and the wealthy bourgeoisie.
example_sentence: The novel portrays a petit bourgeois shopkeeper struggling to protect his status. Critics described the character’s ambitions as petit bourgeois. The movement drew support from workers and the petit bourgeois. His concern with appearances reflected a petit bourgeois outlook.

english_meaning: A small, decorated cake or sweet pastry served as a dessert or with coffee. A bite-sized confection, often iced or glazed. A small savory pastry sometimes served as an appetizer.
example_sentence: Each guest received a chocolate petit four with coffee. The bakery arranged colorful petits fours on a silver tray. She decorated the petit four with a tiny sugar flower. Savory petits fours were served before the main course.

english_meaning: Attractively small, delicate, or dainty. Describing a woman who is short and has a small, slender build. A clothing size or range designed for shorter women. A woman or girl with a small and slender figure.
example_sentence: She chose a jacket from the store’s petite section. The petite dancer moved gracefully across the stage. This brand offers trousers in regular and petite sizes. Although petite, she carried the heavy backpack with ease.

english_meaning: A formal written request signed by many people appealing to an authority. A formal application made to a court in writing. To make a formal request to an authority. To earnestly request or plead for something. A solemn or humble request, especially in prayer.
example_sentence: Thousands of citizens signed a petition against the new law. The lawyer filed a petition in the high court. The residents petitioned the government to build a new hospital. They petitioned the king for mercy.

english_meaning: A person who presents a formal written request to a court or authority. Someone who signs or submits a petition asking for action. In legal terms, the party who begins certain proceedings such as divorce. A person who appeals to a higher body for relief or reconsideration.
example_sentence: The petitioner requested an urgent hearing in the high court. The court accepted the petitioner's written arguments. The petitioner sought relief from the eviction order. Thousands supported the petitioner's demand for reform.

english_meaning: A pleasant, distinctive smell frequently accompanying the first rain after a long period of warm, dry weather.
example_sentence: The petrichor after the summer rain was refreshing. Many people love the smell of petrichor. Petrichor filled the air as the first drops fell. Poets often mention petrichor in their verses. She stood on the balcony to enjoy the petrichor.

english_meaning: To change organic matter into a stony substance over a long time. To make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.
example_sentence: Wood can petrify over millions of years. The horror film petrified the children. She was petrified when she saw the snake. Fossils are formed when remains petrify. His angry look petrified the whole class.

english_meaning: A deep blue colour with a greenish tinge, resembling the sheen of petrol on water. Describing fabric, paint, or objects of this dark blue-green shade. A rich colour often used in fashion and interiors.
example_sentence: She wore a petrol blue velvet jacket. The living room walls are painted petrol blue. Petrol blue looks striking against pale wood. He chose a petrol blue tie for the interview.

english_meaning: Small & unimportant. Having secondary rank or importance. Not very important or serious.
example_sentence: How could you be so petty. He lost his job because of a petty mistake. She is too petty to forgive such a small issue. They argued over petty details that didn’t matter. It was petty of him to criticize her handwriting.

english_meaning: The small bones that form the toes. The fourteen bones of the foot arranged in three rows in each toe and two in the big toe. Bones that help the foot grip the ground and maintain balance. The bony segments lying beyond the ball of the foot.
example_sentence: He stubbed his foot and fractured one of the phalanges of the foot. The phalanges of the foot help the body keep its balance. Each toe except the big one contains three phalanges of the foot. Tight footwear can slowly deform the phalanges of the foot.

english_meaning: The small bones that form the fingers and thumb. The fourteen bones of the hand arranged in three rows in each finger and two in the thumb. Bones that allow the fingers to bend, grip, and perform delicate movements. The bony segments lying beyond the knuckles of the hand.
example_sentence: The X-ray showed a crack in one of the phalanges of the hand. Each finger contains three phalanges, while the thumb has two. Injury to the phalanges of the hand can weaken a person's grip. Tiny muscles and tendons move the phalanges of the hand.

english_meaning: A thing that exists only in your imagination. The soul of a dead person thought of as living in an unseen world or as appearing to living people. Like a ghost. Existing only in your imagination. Something that appears or seems to exist but is not real or is imagined.
example_sentence: A phantom coach is said to pass through the grounds of this house when there's a full moon. The company claimed that the only hazards involving its product were the phantom dangers created by consumer groups. Halloween is supposed to be a time when phantoms return to walk among us

english_meaning: The branch of medicine and science concerned with the study of drugs, their properties, effects, and uses in the treatment of disease.
example_sentence: She is doing her PhD in pharmacology. Pharmacology plays a key role in developing new medicines. The lecture covered the basics of clinical pharmacology. He works as a researcher in a pharmacology department. Pharmacology helps doctors prescribe the right drugs.

english_meaning: The muscular tube behind the nose and mouth that connects them to the esophagus and larynx. The part of the throat that carries both air and food. A passage shared by the respiratory and digestive systems.
example_sentence: Food passes through the pharynx on its way to the stomach. A sore pharynx can make swallowing painful. The pharynx connects the nose to the larynx. Infections of the pharynx are very common in winter.

english_meaning: A distinct stage in a process of development. A period of time. A particular appearance or state in a regularly recurring cycle of changes.
example_sentence: The project is in its initial phase. She is going through a difficult phase. The moon has different phases. We will phase in the new system gradually. The next phase of construction begins tomorrow.

english_meaning: To introduce something gradually. To bring a system, rule, product, or change into use step by step rather than all at once.
