example_sentence: She decided to play along with their joke. He played along with the plan even though he had doubts. The teacher asked the students to play along during the role-play activity. To avoid arguments, I just played along with her suggestions.

english_meaning: To engage in casual or unserious behavior, often for fun. To experiment with something in a non-committed way. To waste time without serious purpose. To flirt or behave romantically in a playful way.
example_sentence: Don’t play around with fire; it’s dangerous. She likes to play around with different painting styles. Stop playing around and finish your homework. They were just playing around at the party.

english_meaning: To replay a recorded sound, video, or message. To reproduce or listen to a recording again. It can refer to audio, video, or any electronic recording. It is commonly used in technology contexts, like music players, video recorders, or phone messages.
example_sentence: They played back the interview. Researchers played back the recording. She played back the lecture. He played back the data file.

english_meaning: To take part in a dangerous contest or confrontation in which each side waits for the other to lose courage and withdraw first. To engage in brinkmanship by risking serious harm rather than backing down.
example_sentence: The two nations seemed to be playing chicken over the disputed border. Both companies played chicken in the negotiations and refused to compromise first. Teenagers who play chicken with oncoming traffic risk their lives. The rival firms played chicken in the price war, each waiting for the other to retreat.

english_meaning: To make something seem less important or serious than it really is. To intentionally reduce the perceived significance, severity, or impact of something, often to avoid attention, criticism, or concern.
example_sentence: The report plays down the risks. He played down the error. They played down the cost. Analysts played down the impact.

english_meaning: To behave recklessly with money or resources by squandering them thoughtlessly. To skip flat stones across the surface of a body of water as a leisure activity. To treat a serious matter, situation, or person with careless disregard and frivolity. To risk or gamble away valuable assets through foolish and irresponsible behavior.
example_sentence: He managed to play duck and drake with his inheritance in less than two years. The children went down to the riverbank to play duck and drake with flat pebbles. You cannot play duck and drake with company funds and expect to keep your job. It is dangerous to play duck and drake with international security treaties.

english_meaning: To take part in a sports game or musical performance on behalf of a team, club, or group. To act with a particular purpose, often seeking a specific outcome or favor. To gamble or risk something with the aim of gain.
example_sentence: She plays for the national football team. He played for the audience’s enjoyment at the concert. They are playing for a chance to win the championship. I wouldn’t play for such high stakes in gambling.

english_meaning:
To act in a very tough, firm, and uncompromising way in order to achieve what you want, especially in business, politics, or negotiations.
It means not being soft, and using strict or forceful tactics to win.
example_sentence: he company decided to play hardball in the salary negotiations. If they don’t accept our offer, we’ll play hardball and withdraw completely. He’s known to play hardball when it comes to business deals. The manager started playing hardball after the team’s poor performance.

english_meaning: To decide how to deal with a situation as it happens, instead of making a fixed plan in advance. To act according to the situation at the moment rather than planning everything before. It is used when someone wants to stay flexible and make decisions depending on how things develop.
synonyms: ["Improvise","Go with the flow","Take it as it comes","Be flexible","Adapt"]
antonyms: ["Plan ahead","Organize strictly","Schedule everything","Prepare in advance","Follow a fixed plan"]
example_sentence: We are not sure about the trip yet, so we will play it by ear. I do not know if I can attend the party, I will play it by ear. Instead of making a strict schedule, let us play it by ear this weekend. The weather may change, so we should play it by ear for the picnic.

english_meaning: To compete in a decisive match or series to determine a champion or ranking. To settle a debt, balance, or financial obligation by using another asset or resource. To manipulate situations, people, or factors against each other for personal or organizational gain.
example_sentence: The proposal plays off two approaches. She played off the strengths of both models. They played off the arguments. The writer plays off contrasting ideas.

english_meaning: To use or exploit something for effect, advantage, or continuation. To continue playing a musical instrument, to manipulate or exploit feelings, or to emphasize or take advantage of a situation.
example_sentence: The speaker tried to play on the audience’s fears. The band will play on until midnight. Advertisements often play on people’s insecurities. He played on his reputation to get the job.

english_meaning: To behave badly, exaggerate, or cause problems. To make something seem more important or dramatic than it really is. To malfunction or act unpredictably. To show a strength or feature prominently. To present a situation as more serious or intense than it is.
example_sentence: The children played up during the lesson and annoyed the teacher. The press played up the scandal to sell more newspapers. My knee is playing up after the long hike. He always plays up his achievements to impress others.

english_meaning: To behave in a way that tries to gain approval, please someone, or take advantage of a situation, often by flattering or acting differently for benefit. To act in a way that is intended to impress, please, or gain favor from someone, often someone in authority or someone you want to benefit from. It can also mean behaving in a slightly exaggerated or insincere way to win approval.
example_sentence: He always plays up to the manager to get better assignments. She played up to her teacher before exams. Don’t play up to people just for favors. Some employees play up to the boss to get promotions.

english_meaning: To take dangerous or foolish risks, especially by doing something that could lead to serious trouble or harm.
synonyms: ["Flirt with danger","Push your luck","Take a risk"]
antonyms: ["Be cautious","Stay safe","Act wisely","Avoid risk","Play it safe"]
example_sentence: He is playing with fire by cheating. If you lie to your boss, you’re playing with fire, you could lose your job. He’s playing with fire by driving so fast on this narrow road. She’s playing with fire by sharing secret information online. Investing all your savings in one risky business is like playing with fire.

english_meaning: Acting in a very tough, firm, aggressive and uncompromising way to achieve your goals. Using strict, aggressive, or no-nonsense tactics in business, politics, or negotiations. Using strict, sometimes harsh tactics in competition, negotiation, or conflict.
example_sentence: The company is playing hardball in salary negotiations. If you want them to agree, you’ll have to play hardball. The politician played hardball to get the new law passed. He used to be friendly, but now he’s playing hardball to get what he wants. The lawyer is known for playing hardball in court to win cases. If you want the contract, you’ll have to play hardball with the competitors.

english_meaning: A serious emotional request, especially for something needing action now. A statement made by somebody or for somebody who is accused of a crime. A reason given to a court for doing or not doing something.
example_sentence: He refused to listen to her tearful plea.

english_meaning: An arrangement in court by which a person admits to being guilty of a smaller crime in the hope of receiving less severe punishment for a more serious crime. A negotiated agreement between the prosecutor and the defendant, where the defendant agrees to plead guilty to a lesser offense or to only some of the charges in exchange for a reduced sentence, lighter punishment, or other concessions. It helps avoid a full trial.
example_sentence: He reached a plea bargain with the authorities. A plea bargain was offered by the state assuring her that she would not go to prison. She accepted a plea bargain and received a general discharge under honorable conditions. The defendant accepted a plea bargain to avoid a lengthy trial. The lawyer advised his client to consider a plea bargain.

english_meaning: To appeal earnestly to a person or authority for a cause or request. To present and argue a case in a court of law. To offer an excuse or defense. To make an emotional appeal.
example_sentence: She began to plead with him to stay. The defendant will plead not guilty in court. I plead with you to reconsider your decision. He pleaded for mercy from the judge. The lawyer will plead the case tomorrow morning.

english_meaning: A source of pleasure or delight. A pleasant feeling or enjoyment. A garden or pleasure ground attached to a mansion. Something that gives satisfaction or gratification.
example_sentence: The pleasance of the garden brought her much joy. He found great pleasance in reading classical literature. The estate included a beautiful pleasance with flowering trees. Walking through the pleasance lifted her spirits. The children played happily in the pleasance behind the manor.

english_meaning: Giving a sense of happy satisfaction or enjoyment. Friendly and considerate in manner. Having qualities that delight the senses or please the mind. Agreeable and charming in character or appearance.
example_sentence: She had a pleasant smile that welcomed everyone. The weather was pleasant for our picnic. It was a pleasant surprise to see him after so many years. They had a pleasant conversation over dinner. The garden has a very pleasant fragrance in the spring.

english_meaning: A feeling of happy satisfaction and enjoyment. It is the state of being pleased or the source of such a feeling. It often refers to sensory or emotional gratification.
example_sentence: The children found great pleasure in playing at the beach. Reading a good book is one of life's simplest pleasures. He takes great pleasure in helping others achieve their goals. It was a pleasure to meet such a distinguished guest today.

english_meaning: An ordinary person, especially someone who is not wealthy, influential, or from the upper class. A commoner. Informal and often insulting, a person considered unsophisticated, uncultured, or lacking good taste.
synonyms: ["Commoner","Plebeian","Ordinary person","Citizen","Everyman","Working class person","Average person","Non aristocrat","Common citizen","Regular person"]
antonyms: ["Aristocrat","Noble","Elite","Upper class person","Patrician","Blue blood","Nobleman","Noblewoman","High society member","Gentleman or Lady"]
example_sentence: He called everyone at the party a pleb, which offended many people. She dislikes people who treat ordinary citizens like plebs. The comedian jokingly referred to himself as a pleb despite his success. Using the word pleb to insult someone is generally considered rude.

english_meaning: A member of the common people, especially in ancient Rome. An ordinary person of low social rank. Belonging to or characteristic of the common people. Lacking refinement, taste, or sophistication. Simple, coarse, or unrefined in style or manner.
example_sentence: The plebeians demanded equal rights from the senate. He dismissed the film as plebeian entertainment. Her plebeian background never held her back. Such plebeian tastes were mocked by the elite.

english_meaning: A direct vote by the people on an important public issue. An official vote in which the citizens of a country or region are asked to decide a major political or constitutional matter. It is often used to determine sovereignty, independence, or approval of major national decisions
example_sentence: The government announced a plebiscite to decide the future of the disputed region. Citizens participated actively in the plebiscite on constitutional reforms. The plebiscite resulted in overwhelming support for independence. International observers monitored the plebiscite to ensure fairness.

english_meaning: A serious promise or commitment to do something or give something. A formal or serious promise to do something or to give money, property, or support for a purpose. To promise seriously or to commit something as security. A thing given as security for a loan. A formal declaration of intent or loyalty
example_sentence: She made a pledge to study harder this year. The company pledged support for environmental protection. He pledged his house as security for the loan. They pledged to help the flood victims.

english_meaning: Full, complete, and absolute in every respect. Attended by all members or participants without restriction. Having unlimited power or authority. Unqualified and entire in scope or application.
example_sentence: The plenary session of the conference was attended by all delegates. The committee was granted plenary powers to investigate the matter. A plenary meeting will be held tomorrow morning. The ambassador has plenary authority to negotiate the treaty. Every member received plenary access to the research materials.

english_meaning: Existing in or yielding great quantities. More than enough in amount or supply. Abundant and copious in availability. Existing in profusion or large numbers.
example_sentence: The harvest was plentiful this year. There is a plentiful supply of clean water in the region. The garden produced plentiful tomatoes throughout the summer. Evidence against the suspect was plentiful and convincing. The rainforest is home to plentiful wildlife species.

english_meaning: A large amount or more than enough. A large quantity of something, enough or more than enough for a need or purpose. It is used to show abundance, richness, or sufficiency.
example_sentence: We have plenty of food for the guests. There is plenty of time to finish the work. The garden has plenty of beautiful flowers. She earned plenty of money from her business.

english_meaning: A space completely filled with matter, as opposed to a vacuum. A meeting attended by all members of a body. An enclosed chamber holding air at higher pressure in a ventilation system. A full assembly or gathering.
example_sentence: The party held a plenum to approve the new policy. Physicists once argued that space was a plenum. Cool air is pushed through the ceiling plenum. All delegates attended the annual plenum.

english_meaning: The use of more words than needed to convey a meaning. A redundant phrase such as burning fire. A figure of speech involving deliberate repetition for emphasis. Unnecessary wordiness in expression.
example_sentence: The expression I saw it with my own eyes is a pleonasm. Teachers warn students against pleonasm in essays. Poets sometimes use pleonasm for emphasis. His report was spoiled by constant pleonasm.

english_meaning: Using more words than are necessary to express a meaning. Containing redundant repetition of an idea. Relating to unnecessary wordiness in speech or writing. Marked by superfluous expressions.
example_sentence: The phrase free gift is pleonastic. Editors removed the pleonastic phrases from the draft. His pleonastic style tires the reader. Avoid pleonastic expressions in formal reports.

english_meaning: A very large or excessive amount of something. An oversupply that is more than needed. An abundance that becomes overwhelming. In old medicine, an excess of blood or bodily fluid.
example_sentence: There is a plethora of choices on the menu. The report contains a plethora of useful data. A plethora of complaints reached the office. She faced a plethora of problems in her first week.

english_meaning: The thin double membrane that surrounds each lung and lines the chest cavity. A protective covering that allows the lungs to move smoothly while breathing. The membrane whose two layers are separated by a thin film of fluid.
example_sentence: The pleura protects the lungs from friction. Fluid may collect between the layers of the pleura. Inflammation of the pleura causes sharp chest pain. The pleura lines the inside of the chest wall.

english_meaning: Inflammation of the membrane surrounding the lungs. A medical condition causing sharp chest pain when breathing. A lung-related illness often following infection. A painful disorder of the pleura.

example_sentence: They stayed at a posh hotel in the city center. She wore a posh dress to the party. The restaurant was very posh and expensive. He speaks with a posh accent. The neighborhood is known for its posh houses.

english_meaning: A number that is greater than zero. Any value shown to the right of zero on the number line. A quantity that represents an increase, gain, or amount above nothing.
example_sentence: Five is a positive number, while minus five is not. The account balance must remain a positive number. Positive numbers are written without a minus sign. Add the two positive numbers and record the total.

english_meaning: A subatomic particle that has a mass equal to an electron and a positive electric charge. It acts as the antiparticle of the electron.
example_sentence: A positron collides with an electron to emit high-energy photons. Scientists detected positrons in the cosmic radiation sample. Medical scanners use positron emission tomography to create detailed body images. The discovery of the positron confirmed key theories in quantum physics.

english_meaning: A group of people gathered to assist a law enforcement officer. A close group of friends or associates who spend time together.
example_sentence: The sheriff organized a posse to search for the escaped prisoner. She arrived at the party surrounded by her usual posse. The posse rode through the valley tracking the trail of cattle thieves. A posse of young fans waited outside the concert venue.

english_meaning: Owned, held, or controlled by someone. Controlled or strongly influenced by a spirit, emotion, desire, or idea. Having a specified quality, ability, or resource, especially in the phrase possessed of. The past tense and past participle of possess.
example_sentence: The family possessed several farms in the valley. He seemed possessed by an urge to prove everyone wrong. She remained calm although the crowd behaved as if possessed. The applicant is possessed of excellent judgment and patience.

english_meaning: To have or own something. To have as a quality or attribute. To control or dominate the mind of someone. To hold or occupy.
example_sentence: She possesses a rare talent for music. The demon possesses the body of the victim. He possesses great wisdom and patience. The country possesses vast natural resources. What qualities do you possess that make you suitable for this job?

english_meaning: The state of owning, having, or controlling something. Something that a person owns, especially a movable personal belonging. Physical custody or control of property, whether or not the holder is its legal owner. A territory controlled by another country. The supposed control of a person by a spirit, demon, powerful emotion, or idea. Control of the ball or puck during a game.
example_sentence: The passport is my most valuable possession. Police charged him with unlawful possession of a weapon. The former colony was once an overseas possession of the empire. Our team kept possession of the ball for most of the match.

word: Possession is nine tenths of the law
english_meaning: A proverb meaning that the person who physically holds or controls something has a strong practical advantage in a dispute over ownership. It suggests that recovering property from its current possessor can be difficult even when another person has a legal claim. It is a popular saying, not a literal rule that possession creates legal ownership.
synonyms: ["Physical Control Gives An Advantage","Possession Strengthens A Claim","Actual Control"]
antonyms: ["Legal Title Prevails","Rightful Ownership Prevails","Possession Does Not Prove Ownership"]
example_sentence: The tenant refused to move, knowing that possession is nine-tenths of the law. He kept the found watch, arguing that possession is nine-tenths of the law. You may have the deed, but he has the keys, and possession is nine-tenths of the law. In property disputes, lawyers often remind clients that possession is nine-tenths of the law.

english_meaning: Wanting to own or control someone or something too much. A person who strongly wants to keep something or someone as their own. It can also describe grammar forms that show ownership, such as “my,” “your,” or “Ali’s book”.
example_sentence: She became possessive about her new phone. His possessive behavior annoyed his friends. The dog was possessive of its food. In grammar, “their” is a possessive adjective.

english_meaning: The fact or state of something being able to happen. A thing that may happen or be true. An option or choice that is available. Potential or promise that can be developed.
example_sentence: There is a strong possibility of rain tomorrow. We must consider every possibility before deciding. The old building has great possibilities. She refused to rule out the possibility of returning.

english_meaning: Able to happen, be done or exist. Likely to be true or to occur, though not certain. Something that may be chosen or achieved. A person or thing that might be suitable.
example_sentence: It is possible to finish the work today. Please reply as soon as possible. There are three possible explanations for the noise. She is a possible candidate for the post.

english_meaning: Perhaps; it may be the case. Used to say that something might be true or might happen. Used with can or could to emphasise what is or is not achievable. Used politely in requests.
example_sentence: He is possibly the best player in the team. Possibly she has already left the city. I cannot possibly finish this by tonight. Could you possibly lend me your notes?

english_meaning: The time after 12 o’clock noon until midnight. The period of time that starts immediately after noon at 12:00 and continues until midnight at 11:59. It is used in the 12 hour clock system to show that the time is in the afternoon or evening. The term comes from Latin and literally means after midday.
example_sentence: The meeting will start at 2 PM. Her flight arrives at 7:30 PM. We usually take a walk in the post meridiem hours. The office remains open until 5 PM.

english_meaning: Future generations of people. All descendants who come after the present time. The people who will remember or judge present actions in the future. A person's offspring collectively.
example_sentence: These records were preserved for posterity. The leader hoped posterity would judge him kindly. We must protect the environment for posterity. Her letters give posterity a glimpse of daily life in that era.

english_meaning: With the greatest possible speed. As quickly as possible. Without any delay. In a very hurried manner. Immediately and swiftly.
example_sentence: He rushed posthaste to deliver the urgent message. The doctor was called posthaste to the accident site. She left posthaste after hearing the news. The soldiers marched posthaste toward the border.

english_meaning: After death. Occurring or published after the death of the originator. Refers to something that happens, is awarded, or is published after the person’s death. For example, awards, books, or recognition received posthumously.
example_sentence: He received a posthumous award. The author’s posthumous book became a bestseller. She was honored posthumously. The artist gained posthumous fame.

english_meaning: Occurring, awarded, or published after the death of the originator or person concerned. Happening following a person's demise. Done in a manner that honors or recognizes someone after they have died.
example_sentence: The soldier was posthumously awarded the highest medal for his bravery. Her final novel was published posthumously by her loving family. He achieved legendary status posthumously after his artwork gained global recognition. The city named a public park posthumously in honour of the founder.

english_meaning: Born after the normal period of pregnancy. Occurring or delivered later than the expected time. Referring to a baby born after 42 weeks of gestation. Later than the usual or expected developmental stage.
example_sentence: The postmature baby required special medical attention. Doctors monitor postmature pregnancies very carefully. A postmature infant may face certain health risks. The hospital has advanced care for postmature deliveries.

english_meaning: The period or effects after taking medication. The state, effects, or conditions experienced by a person after consuming a prescribed drug or treatment. It can relate to side effects, recovery, or any response following medication.
example_sentence: The patient reported dizziness during the postmedication period. Doctors monitor postmedication effects to ensure safety. Postmedication symptoms can vary depending on the type of drug. She kept a diary to track her postmedication recovery.

english_meaning: Happening or done after a surgical operation. Relating to the period of recovery following surgery. Describing the care, treatment, or condition of a patient after an operation.
example_sentence: The patient developed a mild postoperative infection. Postoperative care is essential for a quick recovery. She was kept in hospital for postoperative observation. The doctor explained the postoperative instructions clearly.

english_meaning: To cause or arrange for something to take place at a later time than originally scheduled. To defer or delay. To put off to a future time.
example_sentence: We had to postpone the meeting until next week. The game was postponed due to heavy rain. Please don't postpone your dental appointment. They decided to postpone their vacation. The trial was postponed by the judge.

english_meaning: The action of postponing or deferring something. The state of being delayed to a later time. An act of putting off to a future date.
example_sentence: The postponement of the conference disappointed many attendees. We received notice of the postponement by email. The postponement was unavoidable due to circumstances. Fans were frustrated by the postponement of the concert. The judge announced the postponement of the trial.

english_meaning: A grammatical term for a word or particle placed after the noun or pronoun it governs, as opposed to a preposition which is placed before. A type of adposition found in many languages, particularly those with SOV word order. In certain languages, postpositions serve the same function that prepositions serve in English.
example_sentence: In Japanese, postpositions such as ni and de are placed after the noun to indicate grammatical relationships. Urdu and Sindhi make extensive use of postpositions rather than prepositions. The linguist explained how postpositions function differently in different language families. Unlike English prepositions, postpositions follow the noun they modify.

english_meaning: To suggest or assume something as true for the purpose of argument or explanation. To claim or demand. A thing suggested or assumed as true. A fundamental principle or prerequisite.
example_sentence: Scientists postulate that the universe is expanding. The theory postulates the existence of dark matter. He postulated a new approach to solving the problem. One cannot postulate without evidence. The postulate was accepted by all mathematicians.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting body posture or position. Concerning the way the body is held or positioned. Associated with the alignment of body parts. Of or pertaining to stance and body positioning.
example_sentence: Poor postural habits can cause back pain. Postural exercises improve alignment. The therapist assessed his postural issues. Postural instability is common in elderly patients.

english_meaning: To adopt a particular attitude. To behave in a particular way to create an impression, often deliberately. Position of the body. The way someone holds their body while standing, sitting, or moving; can also refer to a mental or social attitude.
example_sentence: Her posture while speaking showed confidence. The teacher corrected the students’ posture in class. He postured as an expert, but he was new to the field. Soldiers are trained to maintain a straight posture.

english_meaning: A starchy plant tuber which is one of the most important food crops globally. It is cooked and eaten as a vegetable in various forms like boiled, baked, or fried. The plant belongs to the nightshade family and grows underground. It serves as a major source of carbohydrates in many diets.
example_sentence: He ordered a side of mashed potato with his steak. The farmer harvested a large batch of sweet potatoes. She baked a potato and topped it with sour cream. Potato chips are a very popular snack around the world.

english_meaning: To thrust or poke at something. To stir or mix clumsily. A clumsy or awkward push or poke. In Australian slang, a game of pool or billiards played informally.
example_sentence: He gave the ball a potch with his foot. Stop potching around in the kitchen. She made a potch at the ball during the game. The children were potching in the mud. Let's have a quick potch at the pool table.

english_meaning: Power or authority. The quality of being potent or powerful. A state of having great influence or strength. An obsolete term for potency.
example_sentence: The king's potence was felt throughout the land. The potence of the medicine was remarkable. She demonstrated great potence in leadership. The potence of his argument convinced everyone. The ancient text spoke of divine potence.

english_meaning: Having great power or influence. Having a strong effect on the body or mind. Capable of performing sexually. Effective and powerful in action.
example_sentence: The medicine is a potent cure for headaches. He is a potent leader in the community. The drug has potent side effects. The potent spell controlled the kingdom. She is a potent force in the business world.

english_meaning: Ability or capacity to develop, succeed, or become something in the future. The inherent ability, talent, or qualities in a person, object, or situation that may be developed or realized in the future. It indicates what is possible, rather than what currently exists.
example_sentence: She has the potential to become a great scientist. This project has potential for growth in the next year. His potential was not fully recognized at the company. The new technology has the potential to change the industry.

english_meaning: Possibly or capable of happening in the future. Used to describe something that could happen, develop, or become true depending on conditions or circumstances. Used to say that something may develop into something.
example_sentence: This project is potentially beneficial for the community. He is potentially the best candidate for the job. The area is potentially at risk during heavy rains. Small changes can potentially lead to big results.

english_meaning: A state of fuss, confusion, or unnecessary worry. A situation where people make a lot of unnecessary noise, excitement, or worry about something unimportant. To make a fuss, to worry or complain too much about something trivial.
example_sentence: There was a lot of pother about the small mistake in the report. Stop making a pother and focus on solving the problem. The children created a pother while playing in the yard. She pothered over what to wear for the meeting.

english_meaning: Objects made of clay and hardened by heat. The craft or activity of making such objects. A place where pottery is made. Ceramic ware in general.
example_sentence: The museum has a beautiful collection of ancient pottery. She studied pottery at art school. The pottery kiln was heated to a high temperature. I bought some handmade pottery from the local market. Pottery making requires patience and skill.

english_meaning: To move suddenly and swiftly towards a target, usually to catch, attack, or take advantage of an opportunity. It can also mean acting quickly when an opportunity arises. To strongly criticize someone immediately after a mistake. A quick sudden leap or attack made to catch prey, grab something, or take advantage of a situation
example_sentence: The cat pounced on the mouse as soon as it saw it. The reporter pounced on the politician after the controversial statement. Investors pounced on the chance to buy the shares at a low price. The teacher pounced on the mistake in the student's essay. The cat made a sudden pounce on the mouse. With one quick pounce, the tiger caught its prey.

english_meaning: To suddenly jump on or attack something or someone, often quickly or eagerly. To take immediate advantage of a situation or criticize someone suddenly.
example_sentence: The cat pounced on the mouse as soon as it came out of the hole. Reporters pounced on the minister’s mistake during the press conference. He pounced on the opportunity to work abroad. Critics quickly pounced on the new movie’s weak storyline.

english_meaning: An imperial unit of mass equal to about 0·4536 kilograms or sixteen ounces. The basic unit of money in the United Kingdom. To hit something heavily and repeatedly. To beat strongly, as the heart does.
example_sentence: The baby weighed seven pounds at birth. The book costs fifteen pounds in London. He began to pound the door with his fists. Her heart was pounding with excitement.

english_meaning: To flow rapidly in a steady stream. To cause a liquid to flow from a container. To rain heavily and continuously. To express one's feelings or thoughts abundantly.
example_sentence: Could you please pour me a glass of cold water? The rain began to pour just as we started our hike. Fans continued to pour into the stadium before the big match. She decided to pour her heart out in a long letter to her best friend.

english_meaning: To push one’s lips forward to show annoyance, displeasure, or to look attractive. The act of pushing the lips forward in that way.
example_sentence: She pouted when her brother got a bigger gift than hers. He pouted his lips to show he was upset. The little girl sat in the corner, pouting silently. Models often pout during photo shoots to look fashionable.

english_meaning: The state of being very poor and lacking money or basic needs. A condition in which a person or community does not have enough financial resources to meet basic living needs such as food, clothing, shelter, education, and healthcare. It can be absolute (extreme lack of necessities) or relative (compared to others in society).
example_sentence: Poverty forces many children to leave school early. The government is working to reduce poverty in rural areas. He grew up in extreme poverty but became successful later. Poverty affects health, education, and quality of life.

english_meaning: A North American Indian ceremony or social gathering featuring traditional dancing and singing. An informal meeting or discussion among colleagues, advisers, or friends to make a decision. To hold a meeting or confer together for discussion or planning.
example_sentence: The tribe gathered for their annual pow wow to celebrate their cultural heritage. The managers called a quick pow wow in the conference room to discuss the strategy. Before making a final decision, the team decided to pow wow with their legal advisors. People from various communities attended the colorful pow wow held over the weekend.

english_meaning: A soft, pale, greyish shade of blue. A light blue colour resembling powdered smalt used in laundry. A gentle blue tone often used in clothing and interior decoration.
synonyms: ["Pale blue","Light blue","Sky blue","Baby blue","Pastel blue","Cornflower blue"]
example_sentence: He wore a powder blue shirt to the summer wedding. The nursery walls were painted powder blue. She chose powder blue curtains for the living room. The sky faded to a gentle powder blue at dawn.

english_meaning: The ability to do something or act in a particular way. Control or authority over other people or events. Physical strength or force. Energy that is produced by mechanical, electrical, or other means and used to operate a device. A country regarded as having international influence. To supply a machine or device with energy.
example_sentence: The new government came to power after a peaceful election. She has the power to change the outcome of this case. The storm cut off power to thousands of homes. This engine is powered by solar energy.

english_meaning: A short sleep taken during the day to restore energy and alertness. To take a brief daytime sleep for quick refreshment.
example_sentence: I took a twenty-minute power nap after lunch. A short power nap helped her focus on the meeting. He likes to power nap before an evening shift. Even a brief power nap can improve alertness.

english_meaning: Legal authority given to a person to act for someone else. A legal document granting another person the right to make financial, medical, or other decisions on one’s behalf.
example_sentence: She gave her brother power of attorney while she was abroad. The bank requested a certified power of attorney. His power of attorney allows him to manage his mother’s finances. A lawyer prepared the power of attorney for the family.

english_meaning: To switch off a device or system completely. To stop electrical power from reaching equipment. The state or action of shutting down electronic equipment.
example_sentence: Please power off the computer before cleaning it. The technician powered off the server safely. Power off is required before replacing the battery. The screen went dark after the device powered off.

english_meaning: To switch on a device or system so that it begins operating. To supply electrical power to equipment. The state or action of starting electronic equipment.
example_sentence: Press this button to power on the monitor. The system takes a minute to power on. A green light appears during power on. She powered on her phone to check the message.

english_meaning: To switch on a device or system so that it begins working. To energize oneself or prepare mentally and physically for a task. To increase capacity, performance, or readiness in a situation. To gain extra strength, energy, or abilities.
example_sentence: I need to power up my laptop before the meeting. The engineers powered up the new server this morning. Athletes often power up with a healthy breakfast. He powered up his motivation before the presentation. The team powered up their efforts to finish the project on time.

english_meaning: Having great strength or force. Having great control, authority, or influence over people and events. Having a strong effect on someone's feelings or opinions. Very effective or intense in action. Producing a lot of energy or physical force.
example_sentence: He delivered a powerful speech that moved the entire audience. The company has become a powerful force in the industry. This is a powerful medicine, so follow the dosage carefully. The truck has a powerful engine built for steep roads.

english_meaning: Of or concerned with the actual doing or use of something rather than theory. Suitable for a particular purpose or situation. Likely to succeed or be effective in real life. Mindful of sensible and realistic considerations.
example_sentence: She offered practical advice on how to save money each month. The training course provides practical experience in computer repairs. Having a fuel-efficient car is practical when living far from work. He is a practical person who focuses on solving real problems efficiently.

english_meaning: A person who actively practices a profession, especially medicine or law. Someone who regularly performs a particular activity or skill. A professional who applies knowledge in a practical way. A healthcare provider who treats patients.
example_sentence: She is a skilled medical practitioner. The legal practitioner handled the case professionally. He is a practitioner of traditional Chinese medicine. Nurse practitioners provide primary healthcare services.

english_meaning: Dealing with things in a practical and realistic way rather than theoretical ideas. Practical and sensible in attitude. Focused on real outcomes rather than abstract principles. Based on experience and usefulness. Concerned with what is achievable.
example_sentence: She took a pragmatic approach to solve the financial crisis. His decisions are always pragmatic rather than emotional. We need a pragmatic solution that works in real life. The manager made a pragmatic choice to reduce company costs.

english_meaning: A large, open area of flat or rolling grassland, especially in North America, with few trees. Known for its vast, treeless plains and rich biodiversity of grasses and wildlife.
example_sentence: The bison once roamed freely across the American prairie. The vast prairie stretched to the horizon without a single tree. She grew up on a prairie farm in the Midwest of America. Prairie dogs build complex underground tunnel systems.

english_meaning: To express warm approval or admiration for someone or something. To express thanks or respect to a deity. Words that show approval or respect. The expression of gratitude and worship toward God.
example_sentence: The teacher praised her for her hard work. We sang songs of praise in church. He received praise from his boss. The book won praise from literary critics. Praise be to God for all our blessings.

english_meaning: To step or move with high lively steps that show excitement, pride, or playful energy. It is often used for horses lifting their legs high while moving, but it can also describe a person who walks in a proud, showy, or playful way. Sometimes it also means moving around happily or showing off.
example_sentence: The horse began to prance proudly in the parade. The little girl pranced around the room in her new dress. He pranced onto the stage as if everyone was watching him. The pony pranced happily across the field.

english_meaning: To play a trick or joke on someone. To perform an action intended to surprise, amuse, or mildly annoy someone, usually in a playful or humorous way. A playful or mischievous act meant to amuse or trick someone. An action intended to cause surprise, amusement, or mild annoyance.
example_sentence: The incident was a prank that went wrong. I felt really stupid when I realized I’d been pranked. He enjoys playing pranks on his friends. The kids played a prank on their teacher by hiding her chalk. He loves to prank his friends with fake spiders. April Fool’s Day is perfect for harmless pranks. She pranked her brother by putting salt in his sugar jar.

english_meaning: The actual application or execution of an idea, belief, or method. Repeated exercise in an activity to acquire or maintain proficiency. The custom, habit, or usual way of doing something. The professional work or business of a doctor, lawyer, or consultant.
example_sentence: Regular practice is essential to master playing the piano well. The firm has been in legal practice for over twenty years now. It is common practice to greet guests with a warm smile. She puts her theories into daily practice at her art workshop.

english_meaning: A person who talks a lot in a foolish or childish way. Someone who chatters about unimportant things. A talkative child.
example_sentence: The prattler kept everyone amused at the dinner table. Don't be such a prattler; listen for a change. The little prattler asked a hundred questions. He is a harmless prattler who means no offense.

english_meaning: To communicate with a deity in words or thoughts. To make a solemn request or expression of thanks to God. To hope very much for something. To ask earnestly or beg.
example_sentence: I pray every morning before starting my day. They pray to God for good health. We pray for peace in the world. She prayed that her son would return safely. The beggar prayed for some money.

english_meaning: The public call that announces the time for Muslim prayer. The formal announcement inviting Muslims to perform their daily prayers at specific times. In Islam, this call is known as the Adhan and is traditionally delivered from a mosque, often through a loudspeaker or by a person called a muezzin.
example_sentence: The prayer call echoed through the quiet streets before dawn. We stopped our work when we heard the prayer call from the mosque. The prayer call reminds the community of their spiritual duties. Tourists were fascinated by the beautiful sound of the prayer call at sunset.

english_meaning: A small rug or mat used by Muslims to pray on, keeping the place of worship clean. A piece of fabric, often decorated, on which a person kneels and prostrates during prayer. A portable mat reserved for offering prayers. A clean sheet or carpet used specifically for worship.
example_sentence: She laid out her prayer mat facing the direction of the Kaaba. He always carries a prayer mat when he travels. The prayer mat had a beautiful floral design. They rolled up their prayer mats after the prayer. A clean prayer mat is kept ready in the corner of the room.

english_meaning: To act first so that another action cannot happen, or to stop something before it develops. It can also mean to replace or interrupt something by taking priority. In law and politics, it refers to overriding another authority by acting earlier. In broadcasting, it means to interrupt a scheduled program for a special one
example_sentence: The government acted quickly to pre-empt further violence. He tried to pre-empt criticism by apologizing early. The television network pre-empted the show for breaking news. She pre-empted her rivals by launching the product first.

english_meaning: Introduction or opening statement. A preliminary statement or introduction to a document, speech, or text, explaining its purpose or underlying principles. It often sets the stage for what follows, giving context or reasoning.
example_sentence: The preamble of the constitution outlines the fundamental rights of citizens. She read the preamble before starting her speech to explain the purpose. Every book usually has a preamble that introduces the main themes. The committee added a preamble to clarify the objectives of the new policy.

english_meaning: Not securely held or in position. Likely to fall or collapse. Dependent on chance or uncertain circumstances. Dangerous because of instability or insecurity. Used for physical situations, jobs, finances, health, or relationships that could easily change for the worse at any moment.
example_sentence: The climber was in a precarious position on the cliff edge. Many families live in precarious financial conditions. His health remains precarious after the surgery. The vase stood in a precarious spot on the shelf. Peace in the region is currently very precarious.

english_meaning: An earlier event or decision used as an example or guide in a similar situation. A previous legal judgment that influences later cases. An established practice or pattern that may justify similar action in the future. Something that comes before another thing in time, order, or importance.
example_sentence: The court's ruling set an important legal precedent. There is no precedent for canceling the election in these circumstances. We should not create a dangerous precedent by ignoring the rules. Earlier cases provided a useful precedent for the judge. Her appointment established a precedent for greater inclusion.

english_meaning: A teacher or instructor who gives practical guidance, often in morals, religion, or a profession.
example_sentence: The young doctor learned clinical skills under the supervision of an experienced preceptor. In ancient schools, the preceptor shaped students through discipline and moral teaching. She regarded her philosophy preceptor as a lifelong mentor. The monastery assigned a senior monk as a preceptor for new members.

english_meaning: A defined area or district within a city or town, often for administrative, police, or voting purposes. Area controlled by a specific police station. Area assigned for voting in elections. The enclosed area around a church, temple, court, or campus.  A section or quarter of a city.
example_sentence: The police responded quickly to the incident within their precinct. Voters lined up early at the precinct to cast their ballots. The temple precinct was peaceful and beautifully maintained. No vehicles are allowed inside the court precinct without permission.

english_meaning: The area within the walls or boundaries of a place. A district of a city or town for police or administrative purposes. The area immediately surrounding a place. Boundaries or limits of a place.
example_sentence: The police patrol the precincts regularly. The university precincts are beautiful. The crime rate in these precincts is high. The church precincts are open to the public. The precincts of the castle were well defended.

english_meaning: Of great value and not to be wasted. Highly beloved or cherished. Valuable because of rarity or quality. Used as an expression of contempt or irony for someone affectedly nice.
example_sentence: Time is precious so don't waste it. My grandmother's ring is very precious. She gave me a precious gift on my birthday. The precious jewels were kept in a safe. Oh, you're precious with your complaints.

english_meaning: A very steep cliff or mass of rock, the top of which overhangs the edge. A dangerous or precarious situation that could lead to catastrophe.
example_sentence: They stood near the edge of the steep precipice looking down at the ocean. The economy was hanging on the edge of a financial precipice. A misstep near the precipice could lead to a fatal fall. The nation was brought to the precipice of war.

english_meaning: Marked by exactness and accuracy. Clearly expressed or defined. Strictly adhering to a particular standard or rule. Being exactly correct and accurate in all details.
example_sentence: Please give me the precise time of arrival. The scientist made precise measurements. Her instructions were very precise. He is precise in his choice of words. The precise location of the treasure was unknown.

english_meaning: The quality of being exact and accurate. Carefulness and correctness in action or thought. The degree of refinement in measurement or calculation. Sharpness or clarity of definition. Marked by exactness.
example_sentence: The surgeon worked with amazing precision. Watches are made with great precision. He answered every question with precision and confidence. Modern machines cut the metal with precision.

english_meaning: To prevent something from happening. To make an action or event impossible by taking steps beforehand or because of existing conditions.
example_sentence: Heavy rain may preclude the possibility of travel today. His lack of experience precluded him from getting the job. Proper planning can preclude many future problems. The injury precluded her participation in the tournament.

english_meaning: The ability to know or sense something before it happens. Knowledge of a future event obtained through extrasensory means. Foreknowledge of events especially through psychic abilities. A Scots law term for preliminary examination of witnesses.
example_sentence: Some people claim to have precognition of future events. Precognition is a common theme in science fiction. The dream felt like a case of precognition. Studies have tested claims of precognition. In Scots law, precognition is a preliminary examination.

english_meaning: An animal or person that hunts others for food or advantage. A living being that kills and eats other animals. It can also describe a person or group that exploits others for personal gain.
example_sentence: The lion is a powerful predator in the jungle. Sharks are predators that live in the ocean. The fox is a clever predator that hunts at night. Online predators can harm young users, so be careful.

english_meaning: Describes an animal that hunts, kills, and feeds on other animals. Taking unfair advantage of someone who is weak, inexperienced, or vulnerable for money, power, or personal benefit. Showing an attitude of greed, aggression, or a willingness to exploit others. Describes a person who targets others for sexual exploitation or abuse, especially vulnerable individuals.
example_sentence: Predatory animals rely on hunting to survive. The government introduced laws to stop predatory lending practices. Consumers should be careful of predatory companies that hide extra charges. Police work to protect children from predatory criminals.

english_meaning: A food eaten very early in the morning before the sun rises. It is commonly associated with religious practices such as fasting, especially during Ramadan, where Muslims eat a meal called Suhoor before beginning the daily fast. It may also refer to any meal taken before sunrise for work, travel, or special routines.
example_sentence: They woke up at 4 am. to prepare their predawn meal before fasting. The family gathered quietly for the predawn meal during Ramadan. He prefers a light predawn meal so he does not feel sleepy later. Farmers often eat a simple predawn meal before heading to the fields.

english_meaning: A difficult, unpleasant, or confusing situation. A situation in which someone finds themselves facing trouble, uncertainty, or difficulty. It often involves being stuck or unsure of how to act.
example_sentence: She found herself in a financial predicament after losing her job. The hikers were in a dangerous predicament when the storm hit. Choosing between two equally appealing job offers was a real predicament. He was in a legal predicament due to the contract dispute.

english_meaning: To base or found something on a particular idea, fact, or condition. To declare or assert something. In grammar, the part of a sentence that says something about the subject and usually contains a verb. In logic, a statement made about a subject.
example_sentence: Their entire theory is predicated on outdated assumptions. Success is predicated upon hard work and dedication. In the sentence 'She sings beautifully', the predicate is 'sings beautifully'. The judge predicated his ruling on strong evidence. The peace plan is predicated on mutual trust.

english_meaning: To say what will happen in the future based on evidence or knowledge. To estimate or say in advance what will happen in the future using information, data, experience, or signs.
example_sentence: Scientists can predict earthquakes using seismic data. The weather report predicts rain tomorrow. It is hard to predict the outcome of the match. Economists predict growth in the coming year.

english_meaning: The quality of being consistent and able to be foreseen. The degree to which a correct forecast can be made. A state where actions or events follow a regular pattern. The lack of surprises or spontaneity in a system. The ability to be anticipated with confidence.
example_sentence: The predictability of the tides is essential for maritime navigation. Investors value the predictability of a stable government. The main criticism of the book was its extreme predictability. Mathematical models are used to increase the predictability of weather patterns.

english_meaning: Able to be foreseen or anticipated with accuracy. Behaving in a way that is expected and not surprising. Occurring at a regular interval or following a known pattern. Lacking in originality or innovation. Capable of being told in advance.
example_sentence: The ending of the movie was far too predictable for my taste. He has a very predictable routine every Monday morning. High tides are predictable events governed by the moon. Her reaction to the news was entirely predictable based on her character.

english_meaning: A statement about what will happen or might happen in the future. The action of foretelling a specific event or outcome. A prophecy or forecast based on observation or data. The act of declaring something in advance. A logical inference regarding future conditions.
example_sentence: The scientist made a prediction about the comet's return. Market predictions suggest a rise in technology stocks next year. Weather predictions are not always accurate despite modern technology. His prediction that the team would win proved to be correct.

english_meaning: Relating to or capable of predicting something before it happens. Something that is used to forecast, anticipate, or suggest future outcomes based on current information or data. It often refers to tools, models, or behaviors that can indicate what might happen in the future.
example_sentence: The scientist used predictive models to estimate climate changes. His predictive skills helped the team avoid major losses. Predictive analytics is increasingly used in business to understand customer behavior. The teacher’s predictive comments about students’ performance were surprisingly accurate.

english_meaning: A particular liking, preference, or inclination toward something, often formed through habit or natural tendency. A strong personal preference for one thing over another, especially in matters of taste. An established preference for a particular type of food, activity, or style. A tendency to choose or favor something repeatedly over alternatives.
example_sentence: He has a predilection for spicy food that few of his friends can match.  Her predilection for classical music was evident from a very young age.  The chef's predilection for fresh, local ingredients shaped the entire menu.  Critics noted the director's predilection for slow, contemplative storytelling.  His predilection for solitude made him an unlikely choice for the team leadership role.

english_meaning: Superior to or notable above all others. Outstanding in a particular quality or field. The most distinguished, respected, or important. Standing out clearly as the best. Widely recognized as being of the highest excellence.
example_sentence: She is the preeminent scholar in her field. He was the preeminent leader of the movement. The company holds a preeminent position in the market. Einstein was the preeminent physicist of his time. This university is preeminent in medical research.

english_meaning: To take action before someone else does in order to prevent something or gain advantage. To act first so that another action cannot happen, or to stop something before it develops. To strike first in order to prevent an enemy attack. To have a superior legal claim that overrides another claim. To interrupt or replace a scheduled program. To prevent something by acting in advance.
example_sentence: The government decided to preempt the protest by opening dialogue with the leaders. The army launched a strike to preempt a possible attack. The news bulletin preempted the regular television show. She preempted criticism by explaining her decision in advance. The teacher clarified the rules to preempt misunderstandings. Police increased security to preempt any violent incidents. The company lowered its prices to preempt competition from new brands.

english_meaning: Done before someone else to prevent something from happening. An action taken in advance to stop a possible problem, threat, or unwanted situation before it happens. It often refers to measures taken to gain advantage or avoid harm.
example_sentence: The government launched a preemptive strike to prevent further attacks. She made a preemptive apology before anyone could complain. The company took preemptive measures to avoid financial loss. Doctors suggested preemptive treatment to stop the disease from spreading. A preemptive air strike on an enemy base. A preemptive tactic against a ruthless business rival. The prime minister authorized a pre-emptive air strike against the rebels.

english_meaning: To groom oneself carefully or show pride in appearance or achievement. To clean, arrange, or smooth feathers (for birds) or hair/clothes (for humans). To pride oneself or display self-satisfaction in one’s appearance, achievements, or abilities.
example_sentence: The peacock preened its feathers in the morning sun. She preened before the mirror before going to the party. He preened himself after receiving praise from the boss. The actor preened on the red carpet, enjoying the attention.

english_meaning: A district under the government of a prefect. The office, jurisdiction, or residence of a prefect.
example_sentence: The Osaka Prefecture is one of the most populated areas in Japan. He was appointed to lead the local prefecture. The administrative center is located in the heart of the prefecture. Records are kept at the prefecture's main office.

english_meaning: To like one thing or person better than another. To choose one option rather than another when given a choice. To recommend or wish for something as more suitable. In law, to bring a charge or accusation before a court.
example_sentence: I prefer walking to driving in the city. She prefers to work early in the morning. Most customers prefer the smaller size. The police preferred charges against the driver.

english_meaning: More desirable or suitable than another thing. Better to choose because it brings more advantage or less trouble. Worthy of being preferred over the available alternatives.
example_sentence: A short delay is preferable to a serious mistake. Walking is preferable to driving for such a short distance. It would be preferable to finish the work today. Fresh vegetables are preferable to frozen ones.

english_meaning: Ideally or by preference; if possible. In a way that is more desirable than the alternatives. Used to indicate the choice one would rather have.
example_sentence: Please call in the morning, preferably before nine. Bring a jacket, preferably a waterproof one. Applicants should have experience, preferably in teaching. We need a quiet room, preferably away from the road.

english_meaning: A greater liking for one thing or person over another. The fact of being liked or chosen more than others. A thing that is liked or wanted more. Special favour or advantage given to one person or group. In computing, a setting that lets a user choose how a program behaves.
example_sentence: I have a strong preference for tea over coffee. Please state your seating preference when booking. Local residents are given preference in the housing scheme. You can change the language in the preferences menu.

english_meaning: Giving or showing special advantage or favour to one person or group. Relating to treatment that is better than that given to others. Of trade or tariffs, offering reduced rates to particular countries or partners. Having priority in payment or claim, as with certain shares or creditors.
example_sentence: Staff members receive preferential rates at the hotel. The policy gives preferential treatment to local firms. The two countries signed a preferential trade agreement. Preferential creditors are paid before the others.

english_meaning: In a manner that shows favor or preference. By way of priority or special treatment.
example_sentence: The available funds were distributed preferentially to the poorest districts. Some groups are treated preferentially by the current tax laws. The job offers were given preferentially to internal candidates. We must decide whether to treat these applications preferentially or equally.

english_meaning: Promotion to a higher rank or position. A position of profit or honor in the church or government.
example_sentence: He sought preferment within the ecclesiastical hierarchy. Hard work is usually the surest path to preferment. The king granted him a high preferment in the royal court. Many sought political preferment through social connections.

english_meaning: Having a child or young developing in the uterus. Full of meaning or significance that is not stated directly. Rich in significance or implication. Productive or fertile in terms of ideas or outcomes.
example_sentence: She is six months pregnant with her first child. There was a pregnant silence before he finally answered the question. The research was pregnant with possibilities for future medical breakthroughs. The air was pregnant with anticipation as the crowd waited.

english_meaning: Capable of grasping, seizing, or holding on to something, especially by wrapping around it. Adapted for grasping, particularly used of an animal's tail or limb. Able to grip objects firmly. Figuratively, greedy or grasping in nature.
example_sentence: Monkeys use their prehensile tails to swing from branch to branch. The chameleon has a prehensile tongue for catching insects. An elephant's trunk is a highly prehensile organ. Opossums are known for their prehensile tails. The octopus has prehensile tentacles.

english_meaning: Relating to or denoting the period before written records existed. Very old-fashioned or primitive in nature. Belonging to a time in the past that was not documented by history. Extremely ancient and outdated.
example_sentence: Archaeologists found prehistoric tools in the cave. The museum has a vast collection of prehistoric animal skeletons. Some people still hold prehistoric views on social roles. The site dates back to prehistoric times when humans first learned to use fire.

english_meaning: The period of time before written records were kept. The events or conditions leading up to a particular situation or state. The study of the past before the invention of writing systems. The early stages of development of a specific subject or field.
example_sentence: The discovery of cave paintings changed our understanding of human prehistory. We must look at the prehistory of the conflict to understand its current state. Scientists use fossils to reconstruct the prehistory of the planet. The prehistory of computing dates back to simple mechanical calculators.

english_meaning: To form a judgment on an issue or person before having adequate information. To decide the outcome of something beforehand. To make up one's mind about a situation prematurely. To evaluate something without considering all the evidence.
example_sentence: It is unfair to prejudge his performance before he even starts the job. We should not prejudge the outcome of the trial until all evidence is presented. Try not to prejudge people based on their appearance. The committee was accused of trying to prejudge the entire investigation.

english_meaning: To influence someone unfairly before knowing the facts. To cause someone to form an unfair opinion or bias before they have full knowledge. To harm or damage someone’s rights or chances. A fixed opinion formed without proper knowledge. A preconceived opinion or attitude about a person, group, or idea that is not based on reason or actual experience. It often leads to unfair treatment or discrimination.
example_sentence: Do not let rumors prejudice you against her. The negative report may prejudice the committee’s decision. His past mistakes prejudiced the employer against him. His decision was influenced by prejudice rather than facts. Many people suffer because of racial prejudice. The judge asked the jury to avoid prejudice.

english_meaning: Having an unfair opinion about someone or something without proper knowledge. A person who forms opinions or judgments about others in advance, often unfairly, without knowing all the facts. It usually involves bias based on race, religion, gender, or social background.
example_sentence: He was prejudiced against people from different cultures. Her decision seemed prejudiced and not based on facts. The manager was accused of being prejudiced in hiring staff. We should avoid being prejudiced and try to understand others.

english_meaning: In a way that causes harm or unfair bias. Acting or speaking in a manner that harms someone’s rights, reputation, or fair treatment. It often refers to bias, unfair judgment, or negative influence, especially in legal or social contexts.
example_sentence: The judge warned the media not to report the case prejudicially. His remarks were made prejudicially against minority groups. The decision was taken prejudicially, ignoring key evidence. Publishing such details could affect the trial prejudicially.

english_meaning: A high-ranking member of the Christian clergy. A bishop, archbishop, or other senior church official. A religious leader with authority over a diocese or church community. A dignitary in an ecclesiastical hierarchy.
example_sentence: The prelate addressed the congregation after the ceremony. Several prelates attended the council meeting. The old cathedral was restored under the guidance of a respected prelate. The prelate spoke carefully about peace and charity.

english_meaning: Short for 'preliminary'. A preliminary examination, contest, round, or event that comes before the main one. An introductory or preparatory stage. In publishing, the front pages of a book before the main text.
example_sentence: She passed her prelims with excellent marks. The prelim rounds of the tournament start tomorrow. He is preparing hard for the medical prelim. Only twenty candidates cleared the prelim exam. The publisher requested changes to the prelims of the book.

english_meaning: Coming before the main part, introductory, preparatory. Something done to prepare for a main event, action, or process. Often used to describe actions, studies, rounds, or steps that are initial and not final.
example_sentence: The team held a preliminary meeting before the official conference. Scientists conducted preliminary tests to assess the new drug’s safety. She submitted a preliminary draft of her report for review. The preliminary round of the competition will be held next week.

english_meaning: An action or event serving as an introduction to something more important. It can also refer to an introductory piece of music, most commonly an orchestral opening to an act of an opera. It sets the stage or provides a baseline for what follows next.
example_sentence: The ceasefire was a hopeful prelude to the peace negotiations. The pianist played a soft prelude before the main concert began. Rain showers usually serve as a prelude to a heavy thunderstorm in this region. The small skirmishes were unfortunately a prelude to a full-scale war.

english_meaning: Medicine given before a main treatment or procedure to prevent discomfort or complications. The administration of drugs to a patient before a medical procedure or surgery to reduce anxiety, prevent pain, or minimize side effects. I
example_sentence: The patient received premedication to calm her nerves before surgery. Premedication with sedatives helped the child stay relaxed during the procedure. Doctors often prescribe premedication to reduce nausea after anesthesia. He forgot to take his premedication and felt anxious before the operation.

english_meaning: Planned or thought out beforehand. Something done intentionally after careful thought or planning, rather than by accident or spontaneously. Often used in legal contexts for crimes committed deliberately.
example_sentence: The detective concluded it was a premeditated crime. She gave a premeditated speech that impressed everyone. His actions were premeditated, leaving no room for doubt. The company faced backlash for its premeditated strategy against competitors.

english_meaning: Planning or thinking about something, especially a crime, before doing it. The act of considering, planning, or thinking through an action beforehand. It often implies careful thought before committing an act, particularly a deliberate or intentional act like a crime.
example_sentence: The detective proved the crime was done with premeditation. He acted without premeditation, so it was considered an accident. Premeditation is a key factor in first-degree murder charges. She confessed that the argument had been carried out with premeditation.

english_meaning: First in importance, highest in rank, or the head of a government. The head of a government, especially a prime minister or chief minister. The best, leading, or most important of its kind.
example_sentence: She works for the premier medical institution in the country. The premier addressed the nation on economic reforms. This hotel is a premier destination for tourists. He plays in the premier football league.

english_meaning: Extra amount paid for quality or value. An additional charge for something that is considered superior in quality, value, or importance. It can also refer to an amount paid regularly for insurance coverage or special services.
example_sentence: She paid a premium for organic fruits. The car comes with a premium warranty. He has a premium subscription to the music app. Insurance premiums must be paid monthly.

english_meaning: A tooth situated between the canine and the molar teeth. Any of the transitional teeth used for both tearing and grinding food. Relating to the teeth positioned in front of the molars. Also called a bicuspid in dental terminology.
example_sentence: Adults usually have eight premolars in total. The dentist removed a damaged premolar before fitting the brace. Premolars are smaller than molars but larger than canines. He complained of sensitivity in his left premolar.

english_meaning: A strong feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant. A warning or forewarning of a future event. An intuitive sense or foreboding of what will occur. An advance sign or hint of something to come.
example_sentence: She had a premonition that something bad would happen that night. He ignored his premonition and went on the trip anyway. Her premonition about the accident proved correct. I had a strange premonition just before the phone rang. The old man's premonition of danger saved the village.

english_meaning: Serving to prepare someone or something for a later activity or event. Done as a preliminary or introductory step. Relating to education that prepares students for further study or an examination
example_sentence: The students attended a preparatory course before the entrance exam. Preparatory work must be completed before construction begins. She enrolled in a preparatory school to strengthen her academic foundation. The coach conducted preparatory drills before the championship match.

english_meaning: To make something or someone ready for use, action, or an event. To make or arrange something in advance. To produce food by combining or cooking ingredients. To become mentally or physically ready. To create a document, plan, or material for a particular purpose
example_sentence: She began to prepare dinner as soon as she got home. Students must prepare thoroughly for their final exams. The team prepared a detailed plan before launching the product. He took time to prepare himself emotionally for the interview.

english_meaning: To create favorable conditions for something to happen. To make people ready to accept an idea, change, or proposal. To do the preliminary work needed for a later action. Literally, to make soil or a site ready for planting or construction
synonyms: ["Lay the Groundwork","Pave the Way","Set the Stage","Make Ready","Facilitate"]
example_sentence: The minister's speech prepared the ground for major economic reforms. Teachers prepared the ground for the new curriculum with staff training. The negotiators prepared the ground for a peace agreement months in advance. Farmers prepared the ground before sowing the winter crop.

english_meaning: Made ready beforehand for a task, use, situation, or event. Willing and able to deal with something. Planned, produced, or arranged in advance. Made ready by cooking, combining, or processing
example_sentence: She was well prepared for the exam and answered every question confidently. The soldiers were prepared for battle at dawn. He delivered a carefully prepared speech at the ceremony. The chef had all the ingredients prepared before the guests arrived.

english_meaning: The state of being ready for a situation, task, or event. Advance planning and readiness to respond effectively, especially to danger or an emergency. The quality of being mentally, physically, or materially equipped
example_sentence: Disaster preparedness training can save many lives during emergencies. The company's financial preparedness helped it survive the economic downturn. Military preparedness is essential for national security. Schools conduct drills to improve students' preparedness for emergencies.

english_meaning: The quality or fact of being greater in number, quantity, weight, importance, or influence. Superiority in power, force, or amount. The majority or larger part of something. A clear advantage or dominance over others.
example_sentence: The preponderance of evidence supports the prosecution's case. There is a preponderance of women in the teaching profession. The preponderance of opinion favored the new policy. A preponderance of experts agree with the findings. The team won by a clear preponderance of votes.

english_meaning: Greater in number, importance, influence, or strength than others. Dominant or prevailing in a particular situation. Forming the largest or most significant part of something.
example_sentence: The preponderant view in the committee was against the plan. Agriculture remains the preponderant sector of the local economy. His preponderant influence shaped the final decision. Women formed the preponderant group among the applicants.

english_meaning: Mainly or for the most part. To a degree that is greater in number, weight, or influence than anything else. Predominantly, in a way that clearly outweighs other elements. Chiefly, so as to form the largest share of something.
example_sentence: The audience was preponderantly made up of young students. The region is preponderantly agricultural in character. Her work deals preponderantly with rural themes. The committee was preponderantly in favour of the proposal.

english_meaning: To move an event or appointment to an earlier time or date. To bring something forward in the schedule. The opposite of postpone, used mainly in Indian and Pakistani English. To arrange for something to happen sooner than originally planned.
example_sentence: The management decided to prepone the meeting to Monday. Can we prepone the exam by one week? The flight was preponed because of the approaching storm. They preponed the wedding to suit the family's travel plans.

english_meaning: A word placed before a noun or pronoun to show its relation to another word in the sentence. A grammatical term for words such as in, on, at, by, and for. Any word that indicates place, time, direction, or manner in relation to something else.
example_sentence: The word under is a common preposition. Choosing the right preposition can be difficult for learners. He circled every preposition in the paragraph. A preposition usually comes before a noun phrase.
