english_meaning: Relating to a preposition or containing one. Describing a phrase that begins with a preposition and functions as a unit in a sentence. Belonging to the grammatical category of prepositions.
example_sentence: In the garden is a prepositional phrase. The teacher explained prepositional usage with clear examples. Many verbs take a prepositional object in English. Students often misuse prepositional phrases in formal writing.

english_meaning: Attractive or appealing in appearance or manner. Creating a favourable impression on others. Pleasing enough to win the goodwill of people at first sight.
example_sentence: He was not a prepossessing man, but he spoke beautifully. Her prepossessing smile put everyone at ease. The building had a plain and hardly prepossessing exterior. A prepossessing manner helps greatly in interviews.

english_meaning: A preconceived opinion or feeling formed before full knowledge of something. A prejudice or bias, especially a favorable one. A strong idea or impression that occupies the mind. An attractive quality that creates a favorable impression on others. The act of taking possession of something beforehand.
example_sentence: His prepossession in her favor influenced the interview. She approached the topic without any prepossession. Their prepossessions made a fair discussion difficult. He had a natural prepossession that charmed everyone he met.

english_meaning: So unreasonable, absurd, or exaggerated as to be ridiculous or not worth taking seriously. Utterly contrary to common sense or reason. Used to describe a claim, idea, demand, or situation that seems shockingly unbelievable or laughable. Highly unlikely or implausible to the point of being foolish.
example_sentence: It was preposterous to expect the entire project to be finished in just one day.  The lawyer dismissed the claim as preposterous and lacking any evidence.  His excuse for being late was so preposterous that no one believed him.  The idea that the earth was flat now seems preposterous to most people.  She found the price of the item utterly preposterous.

english_meaning: Relating to the period before a child reaches puberty. Children who have not yet begun to develop the physical or hormonal characteristics of adolescence. It is used to indicate the stage before puberty, typically before the onset of secondary sexual characteristics.
example_sentence: The prepubescent boy was excited to join the youth football team. Prepubescent children often show rapid growth in height. The study focused on prepubescent behavior in classroom settings. She specializes in prepubescent dermatology for children

english_meaning: The technical anatomical term for the fold of skin surrounding the end of the penis. The retractable covering of the clitoris in female anatomy. A protective sheath or covering found in certain biological structures. The foreskin that is typically removed during the process of circumcision.
example_sentence: The physician examined the prepuce for signs of inflammation or infection. During the surgical procedure, the prepuce was carefully retracted. Proper hygiene of the prepuce is essential for preventing common dermatological issues. Anatomical studies describe the prepuce as a highly vascularized and sensitive tissue.

english_meaning: A right or advantage belonging to a particular person or group because of their importance or social position.
example_sentence: Alex makes all the big decisions - that's his prerogative as company director. In many countries education is still the prerogative of the rich. The president exercised his prerogative to veto the bill.

english_meaning: To be a sign or warning that something, typically something bad, will happen. To predict or foretell a future event. An omen or sign of what is to come. A feeling of foreboding about the future.
example_sentence: The dark clouds presaged a violent storm. His nervous behavior presaged the bad news that followed. The economic figures presage a difficult year ahead. Such tensions often presage political unrest. The strange silence presaged trouble.

english_meaning: Having knowledge or awareness of events before they take place. Able to foresee or predict the future accurately. Showing foresight and wise anticipation. Insightful about what is likely to happen.
example_sentence: His prescient warnings about the market crash proved correct. She was prescient in choosing that career path. The novel offers a prescient view of modern technology. His prescient advice saved the company.

english_meaning: To advise and authorise the use of a medicine or treatment. To state officially what should be done as a rule or law. To lay down a course of action with authority. To recommend something as beneficial.
example_sentence: The doctor decided to prescribe a milder antibiotic. The rules prescribe a penalty for late submission. The law prescribes how public funds must be spent. Her physician prescribed rest and a change of diet.

english_meaning: An official instruction written by a doctor for medicine or treatment. A formal written order, usually given by a qualified medical professional, that tells a pharmacist which medicine a patient should receive, in what dose, and how often it should be taken. The word can also mean an established rule or recommended way of doing something.
example_sentence: The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics. You cannot buy this medicine without a prescription. She followed the doctor’s prescription carefully. Exercise is often prescribed as part of a healthy lifestyle prescription.

english_meaning: Clean, tidy, and suitable to be seen by others. Good enough in appearance or quality to be shown publicly. Fit to be introduced into company without embarrassment. Reasonably acceptable in standard.
example_sentence: Give me ten minutes to make myself presentable. The old house looks presentable after the repairs. He wore a presentable suit to the interview. The report is now presentable to the committee.

english_meaning: The act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition. The act of maintaining or protecting something from harm or loss. The process of treating food to prevent spoilage.
example_sentence: The preservation of ancient monuments is vital for history. Cold storage is essential for the preservation of meat. We must work toward the preservation of our natural resources. The library is dedicated to the preservation of rare manuscripts.

english_meaning: A person who advocates or works for the preservation of historic buildings, natural environments, or cultural heritage. Someone committed to protecting valued things from destruction or harmful change. Relating to the principles or activities of preservation.
example_sentence: The local preservationist campaigned to save the old theater. Preservationists argued that the historic district should remain intact. As a preservationist, she spent years cataloging endangered species. The preservationist society raised funds to restore the mansion.

english_meaning: To maintain something in its original or existing state. To keep something safe from harm, decay, or destruction. A food preparation method involving the storage of food in sugar, salt, vinegar, or similar. An area managed for the protection of wildlife or a particular activity.
example_sentence: The charity works to preserve ancient woodland habitats across the country. She made jars of strawberry preserve every summer from the fruit grown in her garden. The museum's mission is to preserve artefacts and make them accessible to future generations. He was determined to preserve the family home as it had always been in his grandfather's time. The game preserve was established to protect several endangered species in the region.

english_meaning: To be in charge of a meeting, ceremony, or organization and guide its proceedings. To act as the official head of a meeting. To exercise authority or influence. To officiate at a ceremony. To hold a high or directing role.
example_sentence: The principal will preside over the annual prize distribution ceremony. She was chosen to preside at the board meeting. A senior judge will preside over the case. He presided over the organization for more than ten years.

english_meaning: A gift, usually informal or casual. A present or gift given to someone on a special occasion or just as a friendly gesture.
example_sentence: I bought a small pressie for her birthday. Don’t forget to wrap the pressie nicely. He received a pressie from his secret admirer. The kids were excited to open their pressies on Christmas morning.

english_meaning: The continuous physical force exerted on or against an object. The force per unit area applied in a perpendicular direction to a surface. Mental or emotional stress or urgency. The influence or persuasion applied to someone to do something.
example_sentence: The pressure inside the tire was too low. She felt pressure to succeed in her career. Apply gentle pressure to stop the bleeding. Peer pressure can influence teenage behavior.

english_meaning: To force or strongly persuade someone to do something by applying emotional, social, or practical pressure.
example_sentence: They pressured her into accepting the offer. Do not pressure me into making a decision today. He was pressured into lending money to a friend. The committee pressured the company into improving safety.

english_meaning: The respect and value that somebody, something has because of their social position, or what they have done.
example_sentence: The company has gained international prestige. Many people are attracted by the prestige of working for a top company.

english_meaning: Respected and admired as very important or of very high quality. Causing admiration because of being connected with being rich or powerful.
example_sentence: My parents wanted me to go to a more prestigious university. The Gold Cup is one of the most prestigious events in the racing calendar.

english_meaning: The act of studying or examining something in advance before formal study or research begins. A preliminary study or preparation done before the main work. Advance preparation or reading before a lesson, meeting, or project.
example_sentence: The teacher assigned a prestudy of the chapter before the class discussion. A thorough prestudy helped him grasp the topic quickly. Doctors recommended a prestudy before starting the clinical trial. She always does a prestudy of her lessons at home. The engineers conducted a prestudy of the site.

english_meaning: Used to express that something is likely or reasonable to assume, though not certain. Probably, most likely, or as one would suppose.
example_sentence: He is presumably at work by now. The meeting has presumably been postponed. She presumably knows about the change of plan. They will presumably arrive before dinner.

english_meaning: To suppose that something is true, although you do not have actual proof. To form an opinion from little or no evidence. To take as true or as a fact without actual proof.
example_sentence: A person is presumed innocent until proved guilty.

english_meaning: To take unfair advantage of something, especially someone's kindness or good nature. To rely too much on another's tolerance or generosity.
example_sentence: You should not presume on his generosity for too long. She presumed on their friendship to ask for a big favor. He presumed on my patience once too often. Do not presume on people's kindness.

english_meaning: To take undue advantage of someone's generosity, friendship, or good nature. To rely excessively on another's tolerance without proper regard.
example_sentence: He often presumes upon his uncle's wealth. She presumed upon their long friendship to borrow money. Do not presume upon my good nature. Some employees presume upon the manager's leniency.

english_meaning: An idea or belief taken to be true without proof. Bold or arrogant behavior that goes beyond what is appropriate. An assumption based on probability. The act of taking something for granted.
example_sentence: There is a presumption of innocence until proven guilty. His presumption in speaking to the boss surprised us. The report is based on the presumption that prices will rise. Do not act on mere presumption.

english_meaning: Based on likelihood or reasonable assumption rather than proof. Providing reasonable grounds to believe something to be true. Expected to be, or accepted as, until proven otherwise.
example_sentence: He is the presumptive winner of the election. The prince is the presumptive heir to the throne. Presumptive evidence supports the theory. She is the presumptive nominee of the party.

english_meaning: Failing to observe the limits of what is polite or appropriate; overly bold. Taking liberties or assuming more than one should. Excessively confident or forward in behavior. Acting without proper right or authority.
example_sentence: It would be presumptuous of me to advise the manager. He was presumptuous enough to enter without knocking. She thought it presumptuous to ask personal questions. Do not be presumptuous about other people's affairs.

english_meaning: An attempt to make something that is not true appear true. A false show of feelings, intentions, or abilities. A claim to have a quality or achievement that one does not really possess. The act of pretending, especially in play or imagination.
example_sentence: He made no pretence of being interested in the subject. Their friendship was nothing more than a pretence. She entered the building under the pretence of delivering a parcel. The children kept up the pretence that the box was a spaceship.

english_meaning: To behave in a particular way in order to make others believe that is not true. To give a false appearance of being, possessing, or performing. To make believe.
example_sentence: Packed with numerous conflicting feelings I entered a shop for the very first time & pretended to be confident & aloof.

english_meaning: A person who claims something falsely, especially a title or position. Someone who behaves in a way that is not sincere or true. A person who acts as if something is the case when it is not. A claimant to a throne or high office without a rightful claim. One who pretends to have qualities they do not possess.
example_sentence: He was exposed as a mere pretender to the throne. Do not trust him as he is a pretender at heart. She proved to be a pretender who never really loved him. The pretender was defeated by the true king.

english_meaning: A false appearance or action intended to deceive. The act of pretending or making believe. A claim or profession, especially a false or unsupported one. An outward show meant to conceal one's true feelings or intentions. A pretext or excuse used to justify something. A make-believe game or imaginative play, especially by children.
example_sentence: She made no pretense of being interested in the lecture. Under the pretense of helping, he was actually gathering information. His friendliness was nothing but pretense. The children enjoyed a game of pretense in the garden. He dropped all pretense and admitted the truth.

english_meaning: Attempting to impress by affecting greater importance, talent, or culture than is actually possessed. Showy in a way that is intended to impress others. Making claims to importance or worth that are not justified. Artificial and overly self-important.
example_sentence: The film was criticized as pretentious and boring. He uses pretentious words to sound intelligent. I found the restaurant's decor rather pretentious. Her pretentious manner annoyed everyone. Avoid pretentious language when writing simple reports.

english_meaning: Trying to appear more important, intelligent, or cultured than one really is. Behavior, speech, or appearance that is intended to impress others by showing exaggerated importance, knowledge, or sophistication. It often feels artificial or insincere.
example_sentence: His pretentiousness made it hard for others to relate to him. The movie tried to appear deep, but its pretentiousness was obvious. She disliked the pretentiousness of people who constantly showed off. The restaurant’s pretentiousness made the atmosphere uncomfortable.

english_meaning: A false reason given to hide the real reason. An excuse or reason that is not the true one. It is used to cover up the real motive behind an action. A misleading justification. A cover story. A fabricated explanation. A pretended motive.
example_sentence: He left the meeting on the pretext of feeling sick. She used homework as a pretext to avoid the party. The manager called him into the office under the pretext of discussing work. They entered the building on the pretext of making repairs.

english_meaning: Attractive without being beautiful. To some extent, fairly. Attractive to look at usually in a simple or delicate way.
example_sentence: You look so pretty in this dress. She's very attractive, though not conventionally pretty. The smiles of a pretty woman are the tears of the purse. I found his argument pretty convincing.

english_meaning: A crisp biscuit, typically in the form of a knot or stick and flavored with salt. It is a type of baked bread product that is commonly shaped into a twisted knot. Some varieties are soft and chewy while others are hard and crunchy.
example_sentence: I bought a large, salty pretzel from the street vendor. The child enjoyed the crunchy texture of the miniature pretzels. She dipped her soft pretzel into a bowl of spicy mustard. Pretzels are a popular snack during football games in America.

english_meaning: To exist or be very common at particular time or place, To be accepted to defeat an opponent, Predominant
example_sentence: We were horrible at the condition prevailing in local prisons. Those beliefs still prevail among certain social groups.

english_meaning: Widespread in a particular area or at a particular time. Commonly occurring or existing. Generally accepted or practiced. Dominant or most frequent in a given place or period.
example_sentence: Malaria is prevalent in many tropical regions. Corruption is prevalent in some government departments. Smartphones have become prevalent among young people. The disease was prevalent throughout the country. Such customs are still prevalent in rural areas.

english_meaning: To speak or act in an evasive way to avoid telling the truth. To lie, mislead, or deceive by twisting words. To beat around the bush. To create a false impression by shifting one's position or avoiding a direct answer.
example_sentence: The witness prevaricated when asked about the incident. Politicians often prevaricate to avoid difficult questions. Stop prevaricating and tell me what really happened. He prevaricated for hours before admitting the truth. She tends to prevaricate whenever money is discussed.

english_meaning: The act of avoiding the truth or speaking in a misleading way. Deliberately evasive or vague speech. A statement that is not completely true. Delay or hesitation caused by avoiding a direct answer.
example_sentence: The minister's prevarication only made the journalists more suspicious. After weeks of prevarication, the company finally admitted the fault. The judge warned the witness that prevarication would not be tolerated. Her honest reply was refreshing after so much prevarication.

english_meaning: To keep something from happening or arising. To stop someone from doing something. To hinder, obstruct, or make impossible. To take action in advance so that an event does not occur.
example_sentence: Regular exercise can prevent many diseases. The heavy rain prevented us from going out. Nothing can prevent me from achieving my goal. Vaccination helps prevent serious illness. Safety measures prevent accidents in the workplace.

english_meaning: Capable of being stopped before it happens. Able to be avoided through timely action, care, or precaution. Not inevitable.
example_sentence: Many road accidents are preventable through careful driving. Doctors say that some diseases are preventable through vaccination. The fire was preventable because the faulty wire had been reported. Regular maintenance reduces preventable equipment failures.

english_meaning:
An animal hunted and eaten by another animal. A person or thing that is harmed or tricked by someone stronger. Something that troubles the mind. To hunt for food. To exploit someone.
To bother or trouble continuously.
example_sentence: The lion chased its prey across the grassland. Scammers often target elderly people as prey. Fear became his prey during the dark night. Bigger fish prey on smaller fish.

english_meaning: A casual word for a present or gift. An informal and friendly word used to refer to a present or gift that someone gives to another person on a special occasion such as a birthday, holiday, celebration, or as a gesture of kindness. It usually appears in relaxed conversation rather than formal writing.
synonyms: ["Will validation","Estate administration","Testament certification","Inheritance approval","Authenticate a will"]
example_sentence: She bought a small prezzie for her sister's birthday. The children were excited to open their Christmas prezzies. I brought you a little prezzie from my trip to Lahore. He wrapped the prezzie carefully before giving it to his friend.

english_meaning: To increase the price of something deliberately. To calculate or estimate the cost of something. To work out how much something will cost. It is often used when planning a purchase, preparing a budget, or comparing options before making a decision.
example_sentence: We need to price up the new products. He priced up the items before the auction. The contractor priced up the renovation project. They priced up the jewelry collection.

english_meaning: To pierce or make a small hole in something with a sharp, pointed object. To cause a slight, sharp, stinging pain. To feel a sudden sharp sensation. A small sharp pain or sting caused by a pointed object. A tiny puncture or mark made by something pointed. To prick something means to make a very small hole in it by pushing a sharp object like a needle, pin, or thorn into its surface; it can also refer to the sharp, momentary pain that results from such an action.
example_sentence: She pricked her finger with a needle while sewing the cloth. Be careful not to prick yourself on the thorns of the rose bush. The nurse will gently prick your skin to take a blood sample. Tears pricked her eyes as she listened to the sad news. He pricked a few holes in the lid of the jar so the insect could breathe.

english_meaning: A person who is qualified to perform religious duties and ceremonies in the Roman Catholic. Anglican and Orthodox Churches.
example_sentence: The little boy made his confession to the priest, who told him he was forgiven.

english_meaning: At first sight, based on the first impression or initial evidence before a detailed investigation. A Latin expression meaning "at first sight" or "on the face of it". It is commonly used in law, business, and formal writing to indicate that the available evidence appears sufficient to support a conclusion unless it is disproved by further investigation.
example_sentence: Prima facie, the employee appears responsible for the missing documents. The court found prima facie evidence of fraud and ordered an investigation. Prima facie, the proposal seems beneficial for the organization. There is a prima facie case against the suspect based on the available evidence.

english_meaning: For the most part, mainly, or chiefly. In the first place or before anything else. Used to show the main reason, purpose, or cause of something. Essentially or fundamentally, more than in any other way.
example_sentence: The delay was primarily caused by heavy rain. This course is primarily intended for beginners. She is primarily known for her research on climate change. The company deals primarily in agricultural machinery.

english_meaning: Of chief importance; main or principal. First in order of time, development, or importance. Relating to the early stages of education or development. Original, not derived from something else. A preliminary election.
example_sentence: Education is the primary responsibility of every parent. My primary concern is your safety. She teaches at a primary school in the village. The primary source of energy in our home is solar power.

english_meaning: Of first importance; main or fundamental. Of the best possible quality; excellent. The state or time of greatest strength, vigor, or success. To prepare something for use or action. (Math) A number divisible only by itself and one.
example_sentence: Safety is our prime concern. He is a prime example of hard work. She is in the prime of her life. The wall must be primed before painting. Seven is a prime number.

english_meaning: A whole number greater than one that can only be divided by one and itself. A number that has exactly two distinct factors. A natural number with no divisors other than one and the number itself.
example_sentence: Seven is a prime number because only one and seven divide it. The first four prime numbers are two, three, five, and seven. Prime numbers are widely used in computer encryption. She asked the class to identify the prime numbers below fifty.

english_meaning: To stimulate the growth of something, especially an economy, by investing money in it. To take action that encourages something to start working or developing. To give initial help or support so that a process can continue by itself. To encourage people to talk or give by starting first. Originally, to pour water into a pump so that it can begin drawing water.
example_sentence: The government cut taxes to prime the pump of the slow economy. The teacher primed the pump by sharing her own story first. A small grant helped prime the pump for the community project. Free samples were given out to prime the pump for sales.

english_meaning: The peak broadcasting hours on television or radio when audience viewership or listenership is at its highest level. A period of maximum effectiveness, peak activity, or major prominence in a person's life or career. Being at or suitable for the most important, prestigious, or widely viewed stage or platform.
synonyms: ["Peak hours","Peak time","Rush hour","Highlight","Zenith","Golden age","Heyday","Climax","Top tier","Major league","Choice time","Optimum period"]
example_sentence: The news channel reserves its most famous anchors for the prime time slots. Her new show became an instant hit during Sunday prime time television. He realized that his athletic career had passed its prime time after several injuries. The team proved they were ready for prime time by winning the national championship.

english_meaning: A Portuguese word meaning 'first' (feminine form), commonly encountered in English contexts through names like 'Primeira Liga' (Portugal's top football league). Used to denote the first, foremost, or highest tier of something.
example_sentence: Porto plays in the Primeira Liga of Portugal. Benfica won the Primeira title last season. The Primeira Divisao is the top football league. She holds the primeira position in her class. Their team was promoted to the Primeira.

english_meaning: Belonging to the earliest ages of the world or of history; ancient and primitive. Untouched, wild, and original in character. Relating to instincts or feelings that seem to come from the earliest human times.
example_sentence: The explorers ventured into a primeval forest untouched by humans. Primeval instincts often surface in moments of fear. Scientists study primeval oceans to learn how life began. The documentary depicted the primeval landscape of early Earth.

english_meaning: In a primeval manner. In a way that relates to or resembles the earliest ages of the world. From the very earliest times.
example_sentence: The landscape looked primevally untouched, as if no human had ever set foot there. She described the forest primevally, full of ancient trees and silence. The ritual felt primevally connected to humanity's earliest fears. The cave paintings evoked something primevally familiar in visitors.

english_meaning: Relating to, denoting, or preserving the character of an early stage in the evolutionary or historical development of something. It often refers to something very simple or unsophisticated in nature. In a technical sense, it can describe a cell or organism that is not highly specialized.
example_sentence: The archeologists found primitive stone tools in the dark cave. They had to survive in the wilderness with only primitive equipment. Some tribes still live in primitive conditions far from modern civilization. The first computers were quite primitive compared to today's laptops.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being primitive or simple. It refers to the lack of sophistication or the condition of belonging to an early stage of development. This term can be used to describe artistic styles or social structures that remain basic.
example_sentence: The primitivity of the construction methods surprised the modern engineers. Historians often study the primitivity of early human social structures. There is a certain beauty in the primitivity of these ancient paintings. The explorer was fascinated by the primitivity of the remote village.

english_meaning: The state or fact of being the firstborn child among siblings. The legal or customary right of the eldest child, especially the eldest son, to inherit the whole family estate or title, to the exclusion of other siblings.
example_sentence: Under primogeniture, the eldest son inherited the entire family estate. Many European monarchies historically followed the rule of primogeniture. Primogeniture often left younger siblings without any inheritance. The law of primogeniture has been abolished in most modern legal systems.

english_meaning: Existing from the very beginning of time; belonging to the earliest stage of the world. Original and fundamental, forming the basis of something. Of a feeling or instinct, deep, basic, and seemingly ancient.
example_sentence: Scientists study the primordial gases of the early earth. The forest has a primordial silence about it. Fear of the dark is a primordial instinct. These rocks date back to a primordial era.

english_meaning: To make oneself look neat and attractive by carefully adjusting hair, clothing, or makeup. To groom or dress in a fussy, self-admiring way. To tidy up the appearance of something with excessive care.
example_sentence: She spent an hour primping in front of the mirror before the party. He primped his hair one last time before stepping on stage. The bride was primping nervously while waiting for the ceremony. Teenagers often primp for hours to look perfect for the prom.

english_meaning: A small wild plant with pale yellow flowers that bloom in spring. The pale yellow color of the primrose flower. A plant commonly grown in gardens for its early bright blossoms. Pale yellow in color.
example_sentence: Primroses covered the meadow in early spring. She planted primroses along the garden path. The walls were painted a soft primrose color. A bunch of wild primroses brightened the windowsill.

english_meaning: A soft pale yellow color like that of the primrose flower. A light, delicate shade of yellow. A gentle yellow often used in fashion and decoration.
example_sentence: She wore a primrose yellow dress to the garden party. The curtains were made of primrose yellow silk. Primrose yellow walls made the room feel sunny and warm. He chose primrose yellow paint for the nursery.

english_meaning: A genus of flowering plants that includes primroses, cowslips, and oxlips, known for bright, early-blooming flowers. Any plant of this genus, commonly grown in gardens and woodland borders.
example_sentence: The garden was full of colourful primulas in early spring. She planted primulas along the border of the flower bed. Primulas are among the first flowers to bloom after winter. The nursery sold several varieties of primula in vibrant colours.

english_meaning: A trademark name for a portable pressurised camping stove. In the Scottish Episcopal Church, the title of the presiding bishop. From Latin, meaning 'first', used to indicate seniority or precedence, as in the phrase 'primus inter pares', first among equals.
example_sentence: We cooked our dinner on a Primus stove during the camping trip. The Primus of the Scottish Episcopal Church presided over the meeting. He was regarded as primus inter pares among his colleagues. The old Primus stove was a reliable companion on many expeditions.

english_meaning: First in order of importance; main. The head of a school or organization. A sum of money lent or invested, on which interest is paid. A person with a leading role or highest authority.
example_sentence: The principal cause of the accident was negligence. Our school principal is very kind and strict. He deposited his principal in a fixed account. She was the principal speaker at the seminar. The principal actor received an award.

english_meaning: A fundamental truth, rule, or law that serves as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior. A basic idea or theory that explains how something works. A personal standard of right conduct. A general scientific law.
example_sentence: Honesty is one of his guiding principles. The principle of gravity was discovered by Newton. She refused to compromise her principles. This machine works on a simple scientific principle. Equal opportunity is a basic democratic principle.

english_meaning: A thin board made of insulating material with conductive pathways etched onto its surface for connecting electronic components. An assembly of electronic elements interconnected by tracks on a rigid or flexible substrate. The physical hardware substrate that facilitates electricity flow between microchips and transistors in modern technology. A pre-fabricated electrical network used to minimize wiring and space in devices like smartphones and computers. A manufactured component that integrates active and passive electronic devices into a single functional unit.
synonyms: ["PCB","Circuit Board","Logic Board","Motherboard","Mainboard","Wiring Board","Microcircuit","Electronic Plate","Etched Board","Integrated Circuitry","Substrate","Hardware Interface","Breadboard","System Board"]
antonyms: ["Point-to-point Wiring","Hand-wired Circuit","Loose Wires","Breadboard Prototype","Insulation","Vacuum Tube","Analog Component","Bare Wire","Disconnected Circuit","Manual Connection"]
example_sentence: The technician replaced the damaged printed circuit to fix the laptop's motherboard. Modern electronics rely on a multi-layered printed circuit to achieve high processing speeds. Before mass production, engineers must rigorously test the prototype's printed circuit for any shorts. The miniaturization of the printed circuit allowed for the creation of wearable smart devices.

english_meaning: Existing or happening before something else in time, order, or importance. Earlier or previous. More important or having precedence in a particular situation. A senior monk who ranks below an abbot. The head of a priory.
example_sentence: Please tell us about any prior experience you have. The meeting was canceled because of a prior commitment. The report refers to events from the prior year. The prior welcomed the visitors to the monastery.

english_meaning: The process of arranging tasks, duties, or problems based on their importance and urgency so that the most important work is done first. It is commonly used in time management, business planning, and decision-making.
example_sentence: The manager focused on the prioritization of urgent tasks. Effective prioritization helps students manage exam preparation. In healthcare, prioritization of patients can save lives. Good prioritization improves productivity at work.

english_meaning: To decide what is most important and do it first. To rank tasks, duties, or goals based on importance. To give more attention or resources to something. To treat something as more urgent than other things
example_sentence: I always prioritize my health over work. She prioritizes studying before watching TV. The company prioritizes customer satisfaction. We must prioritize urgent tasks first.

english_meaning: The state of being more important than something else. Something that must be dealt with before other things. A ranking order of importance. A task or goal that is given special attention. The right to be considered or handled first
example_sentence: Health should be your top priority in life. The manager gave priority to urgent tasks. Education is a priority for every country. We must decide which project has higher priority.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with two parallel identical bases and rectangular lateral faces. A transparent object that separates white light into colors. A polyhedron with uniform cross-section along its length.
example_sentence: Light passes through the prism and creates a rainbow. A triangular prism has five faces. The crystal prism separates white light into spectrum. Calculate the surface area of the prism.

english_meaning: Relating to or resembling a prism. Showing bright, varied colours like those formed when light passes through a prism. Brilliantly coloured and rainbow-like. Having the shape or form of a prism.
example_sentence: The crystal scattered prismatic colours across the wall. Her dress shimmered with prismatic light as she moved. The soap bubble displayed a prismatic sheen. Geologists studied the prismatic structure of the mineral.

english_meaning: A person kept in prison as a punishment for a crime. Someone captured and held by an enemy during war. A person who is confined against their will. Anyone trapped by a situation, habit, or feeling. A captive who has lost personal freedom.
example_sentence: The prisoner was released after serving five years. Thousands of prisoners of war were exchanged after the treaty. She felt like a prisoner in her own home. He remained a prisoner of his own fears for many years.

english_meaning: Completely clean and fresh. In its original and unspoiled condition. Pure, untouched, or unaffected by damage, pollution, or change. Perfectly preserved and looking new. Spotless and immaculate. Existing in a natural state without human interference.
example_sentence: The hikers were amazed by the pristine beauty of the mountain lake. The museum preserved the ancient manuscript in pristine condition. After years of careful maintenance, the car still looked pristine. The island is famous for its pristine beaches and clear water.

english_meaning: An old-fashioned or archaic expression meaning please or I ask you. A polite or sometimes urgent word used before a request, question, or command, originally shortened from “I pray thee.”
example_sentence: Prithee, tell me what happened at the castle. Prithee, good sir, listen to my request. “Prithee, do not leave yet,” she pleaded. Prithee, where did you find this curious book?

english_meaning: The state of being alone, undisturbed, or free from public attention. The right or ability to control access to one’s body, personal life, communications, information, or activities. Secrecy or confidentiality concerning personal matters. A secluded place or condition in which one is not observed.
example_sentence: She values her privacy and rarely shares personal details online. The new law protects the privacy of internet users. He closed the door so that the patient could have some privacy. Employees expect privacy for their confidential medical records.

english_meaning: Belonging to or intended for one particular person or group rather than the public. Not open, accessible, or known to everyone. Personal, confidential, or secret. Owned or controlled by individuals or companies rather than the government. Preferring not to reveal personal thoughts or feelings. A soldier of the lowest rank in the army. A person without public office or official status, in formal usage.
example_sentence: They discussed the matter in a private room. Her medical records are strictly private. The project was funded by a private company. He joined the army as a private and later became a sergeant.

english_meaning: A special right, advantage, or immunity granted or available only to a particular person or group. It can also refer to the thing that is a great honor or a source of pleasure to do. In law, it refers to a legally protected right to keep communications confidential.
example_sentence: Education should be a universal right, not a privilege for the wealthy. It was a great privilege to meet the president in person. The diplomat enjoyed the privilege of immunity while traveling abroad. Members of the club have the privilege of using the private gym.

english_meaning: Having special rights, advantages, or immunities that others do not possess. It often refers to a person belonging to a class that enjoys social or financial superiority. It can also describe information that is confidential or legally protected.
example_sentence: The wealthy students come from a very privileged background. He felt privileged to be invited to the royal gala. The conversation between the lawyer and his client is considered privileged information. Only a privileged few have access to the inner sanctum of the temple.

english_meaning: In a private, secret, or confidential manner. Secretly or covertly, without others knowing. In a hidden or stealthy way. Quietly and without public notice. (An older or literary word.)
example_sentence: He privily informed the king of the plot. They met privily to discuss the matter. She privily agreed to help him. The messenger privily delivered the letter. The two leaders privily signed the treaty.

english_meaning: Sharing in the knowledge of something secret or private. It describes someone who is allowed to know about a confidential matter. Historically, it also refers to a toilet, especially an outdoor one.
example_sentence: I was not privy to the details of their private agreement. Only the top executives were privy to the merger plans. She was privy to the secrets of the royal family for many years. The old cottage still had an outdoor privy in the backyard.

english_meaning: Done as a formality or as a matter of routine. Based on estimates or assumed figures rather than actual results. A pro forma invoice; a document sent in advance of goods. A standard form or document.
example_sentence: The meeting was purely pro forma, since the decision had already been made. The company released pro forma figures for next year. Please send us a pro forma invoice before shipping the order. He signed the pro forma agreement without reading it.

english_meaning: Supporting the legal right of a pregnant person to choose whether to continue or end a pregnancy. Favoring personal autonomy and access to abortion in reproductive-health decisions. A person or position that supports abortion rights.
example_sentence: She describes herself as pro-choice. The organization campaigns for pro-choice laws and reproductive healthcare. Several pro-choice voters attended the public meeting. The debate included both pro-choice and pro-life speakers.

english_meaning: In grammar, a word or phrase that stands in place of another word, phrase, or clause. A word such as a pronoun, 'so', 'do', or 'there' that replaces other words to avoid repetition.
example_sentence: In the sentence 'I think so', the word 'so' is a pro-form. Pronouns are the most common type of pro-form. The teacher explained how pro-forms help avoid repetition. 'There' can act as a pro-form for a place already mentioned.

english_meaning: The chance or likelihood that something will happen. The measure of how likely an event is to occur. It is often expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and (certain) or as a percentage. It is commonly used in statistics, mathematics, and everyday life to assess risks and outcomes.
example_sentence: There is a high probability of rain tomorrow. The probability of winning the lottery is very low. Scientists calculate the probability of an earthquake in this area. The probability of passing the exam increases with more study.

english_meaning: Likely to happen or be true. Likely based on facts or signs. Reasonably expected outcome. Seeming true or correct in absence of proof. Something that is expected to happen or is very likely based on evidence or reasoning, but not completely certain.
example_sentence: It is probable that it will rain tomorrow. A rise in prices is probable this year. It is probable he has already left the office. Success is probable if you work hard and stay focused.

english_meaning: Used to show that something is likely to happen or be true. Used when you think something is likely but not certain. Expresses a strong possibility based on opinion or evidence. Used to make polite or uncertain predictions. Shows expectation without full confirmation.
example_sentence: She will probably come to the meeting tomorrow. It will probably rain in the evening. He is probably the best player on the team. They will probably finish the work today.

english_meaning: To prove a will legally in court. The act of submitting a will to a court for validation, confirming the executor, and starting the legal process of estate administration. The legal process of proving a will and managing a deceased person’s estate.
example_sentence: They probated the will in the city court. The lawyer helped her probate the estate efficiently. The probate of his grandfather’s will took six months. She inherited the property after probate.

english_meaning: A trial period to test behavior, performance, or suitability. A fixed period during which a person is tested to decide if they are suitable for a job, school, or position. A legal period when an offender is allowed to stay in the community under supervision instead of going to prison. A time of observation to evaluate conduct, improvement, or reliability.
example_sentence: She is on probation for three months at her new job. The student remained on probation due to low grades. The judge released him on probation instead of sending him to jail. Employees must complete probation before receiving benefits.

english_meaning: On a trial period before permanent approval or confirmation. A period in which a person’s performance, behavior, or suitability is tested before they are given a permanent position, status, or approval. It is commonly used in jobs, training, and legal or institutional settings.
example_sentence: He is working on a probationary period at the company. The teacher gave him a probationary admission for three months. Her probationary job will become permanent after six months. The officer was placed under probationary supervision.

english_meaning: A person who is on trial or training period before becoming a permanent employee or member. Someone who has been newly appointed or admitted to a job, institution, or service but is required to complete a trial period before confirmation. During this time, their performance and behavior are evaluated.
example_sentence: The probationer will be evaluated after six months of training. Every probationer must follow strict rules during the trial period. The company decided to confirm the probationer after good performance. As a probationer, she was not yet eligible for full benefits.

english_meaning: To investigate, examine, or explore deeply. A tool used for examining. To search into or investigate something thoroughly to discover facts. An act of investigation or a device used to explore or examine.
example_sentence: The journalist tried to probe the reasons behind the incident. Doctors used a small probe to examine the wound. The committee will probe the financial records. She asked questions to probe his intentions.

english_meaning: An established way of doing something. A series of actions conducted in a certain order. An official method or process. A medical operation or treatment. A formal sequence followed to complete a task.
example_sentence: Please follow the correct procedure when applying. The surgical procedure lasted two hours. There is a strict procedure for handling complaints. The company introduced a new safety procedure.

english_meaning: To continue doing something that has already been started. To move forward in a particular direction. To begin a course of action after a pause or preparation. To take legal action against someone.
example_sentence: Please proceed with your presentation. The passengers were asked to proceed to gate five. After the break, the meeting proceeded as planned. The company may proceed against him in court.

english_meaning: An action or series of actions carried out in a formal way. A legal action taken in a court of law, usually used in the plural. An event or activity that is taking place. A published record of the papers presented at a conference.
example_sentence: The court proceedings lasted for three days. He watched the proceedings from the back of the hall. Legal proceedings were started against the company. The conference proceedings will be published next month.

english_meaning: A series of actions or stages used to achieve a result. A natural, biological, chemical, or industrial sequence of changes. An established procedure for handling a matter. A legal summons or other formal court document. To treat, prepare, or transform material through a series of operations. To handle information, data, documents, or applications systematically. To understand and mentally absorb information or an experience. To begin legal proceedings against someone or serve them with legal documents.
example_sentence: Learning a language is a gradual process. The factory processes milk before it reaches the shops. Please allow two weeks for us to process your application. She needed time to process what she had heard.

english_meaning: Treated, prepared, altered, or preserved by a series of operations. Made from raw material by industrial or chemical methods. Handled, examined, or completed according to an established procedure. Converted, analyzed, or organized by a computer or system. Mentally understood or absorbed. Having undergone legal processing or formal administrative action.
example_sentence: Processed foods often contain added salt or sugar. The clerk processed our passports before noon. The computer processed the images in a few seconds. After a quiet walk, she had finally processed the difficult news.

english_meaning: A number of people or vehicles moving forward in an orderly or ceremonial manner. It is often associated with religious, festive, or funeral events. It can also refer to the act of moving along in a formal way.
example_sentence: The funeral procession moved slowly through the city streets. A colorful procession of dancers marked the beginning of the festival. We watched the wedding procession pass by the town square. The royal procession was led by a troop of cavalry.

english_meaning: A machine or system that treats or prepares material in a series of steps. The part of a computer that carries out instructions, also called the CPU. A person or company that handles and prepares food or raw materials. Software that performs a specific task, such as a word processor.
example_sentence: The new laptop has a much faster processor. A food processor makes chopping vegetables very easy. The company is a major processor of raw cotton. He typed the report using a simple word processor.

english_meaning: To announce something officially or publicly. To declare something clearly, confidently, or emphatically. To praise or identify someone or something openly as possessing a particular quality. To make a fact or message widely known.
example_sentence: The mayor proclaimed Monday a public holiday. She stood before the court and proclaimed her innocence. The newspapers proclaimed the discovery a major scientific breakthrough. Church bells proclaimed the arrival of the new year.

english_meaning: Announced officially or publicly. Made known clearly or defiantly. Declared openly.
example_sentence: The winner of the election was proclaimed at midnight. He proclaimed his innocence to the entire crowd. The king proclaimed a day of national celebration. The beauty of the landscape was proclaimed by all the travelers.

english_meaning: An official public announcement or declaration made by a person in authority. A formal statement issued to inform the public about something important. A decree or order announced openly. A declaration of a fact, intention, or law.
example_sentence: The king issued a proclamation of peace. The president made a proclamation declaring a national holiday. Their marriage was announced by public proclamation. The Emancipation Proclamation freed the slaves. A proclamation of independence was read aloud.

english_meaning: An unstressed word or grammatical element that is pronounced as part of the word following it. A clitic that phonologically attaches to a following host. Relating to or functioning as such an element.
example_sentence: In rapid speech, the article may behave as a proclitic. The linguist marked each proclitic and the word that hosted it. A proclitic attaches phonologically to the following word rather than the preceding one. Students compared proclitic forms with enclitic forms in the passage.

english_meaning: A natural tendency or strong inclination to behave in a particular way, especially something undesirable. A habitual liking or preference for a certain type of activity or behavior. An innate disposition toward a specific pattern of conduct, often used in formal or psychological contexts. The term often carries a slightly negative connotation when used to describe questionable habits or tendencies.
example_sentence: He had a proclivity for taking unnecessary risks during business negotiations.  Her proclivity for honesty sometimes made her blunt with friends.  The study examined the proclivity of teenagers toward impulsive decision-making.  His proclivity for procrastination often delayed important projects.  The report highlighted a worrying proclivity for violence among certain individuals.

english_meaning: To delay or postpone doing something. To intentionally put off or defer a task or responsibility to a later time, often resulting in unnecessary stress or missed opportunities
example_sentence: She tends to procrastinate whenever she has a difficult assignment. Don’t procrastinate on paying your bills or you might incur penalties. He procrastinated so long that he missed the application deadline. Students often procrastinate when preparing for exams.

english_meaning: The habit of delaying or postponing tasks that should be done now. Delaying work unnecessarily. Putting off tasks or duties instead of completing them on time.
example_sentence: Procrastination can lead to missed deadlines and stress. His procrastination prevented him from finishing the project on time. She is trying to overcome procrastination by making a daily schedule. Procrastination often increases anxiety instead of reducing it.

english_meaning: A person who habitually delays or postpones tasks or decisions. Someone who puts off doing things until a later time, often unnecessarily. A chronic delayer who avoids starting or completing tasks.
example_sentence: As a procrastinator, she often found herself rushing to complete tasks at the last possible minute. He was a classic procrastinator who always meant to do things tomorrow rather than today. The procrastinator in the team caused constant delays and frustrated everyone else. She finally accepted that she was a natural procrastinator and started using time management tools. The procrastinator always had excellent reasons why the work could not begin just yet.

english_meaning: To produce offspring or young. To bring children into existence through natural reproduction. To reproduce as a species. Figuratively, to bring something new into being.
example_sentence: Most species migrate to warmer waters to procreate. They chose not to procreate for personal reasons. Animals in the reserve procreate freely. The urge to procreate is a basic biological instinct.

english_meaning: The act or process of producing offspring. Natural reproduction and the continuation of a species. The bringing of new life into existence.
example_sentence: Procreation ensures the survival of the species. The lecture dealt with human procreation and health. Many religions regard procreation as a sacred duty. Environmental stress can affect procreation in birds.

english_meaning: Enforcing conformity by violent or arbitrary means. Tending to force people or things into a rigid, unsuitable pattern without regard for individual differences. Marked by ruthless and inflexible standardisation.
example_sentence: The school follows a procrustean approach to discipline. Such procrustean rules ignore the needs of individual students. Critics called the policy rigid and procrustean. He rejected the procrustean demands of the committee.

english_meaning: A person who supervises candidates during an examination. An official responsible for discipline or administrative duties at certain universities. A legal representative or agent, especially in ecclesiastical or admiralty courts. To supervise an examination or the people taking it.
example_sentence: The proctor checked each student's identification before the exam. She agreed to proctor the mathematics test on Friday. The university proctor investigated the breach of discipline. No candidate may leave without the proctor's permission.

english_meaning: A public prosecutor in Scotland who investigates suspected crimes and decides whether to bring criminal proceedings. An official who investigates sudden, suspicious, or unexplained deaths in Scotland. The local representative of the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service.
example_sentence: The police submitted their report to the procurator fiscal. The procurator fiscal ordered an inquiry into the unexplained death. Witnesses were contacted by the procurator fiscal's office. The final decision on prosecution rests with the procurator fiscal.

english_meaning: To obtain or acquire something, especially through care, effort, or special means. To arrange for or provide goods or services. To obtain supplies through an official purchasing process. To bring about or cause a particular result. To persuade or induce someone to do something, especially in formal or legal usage.
example_sentence: The museum managed to procure a rare manuscript. We need to procure enough food for the entire team. The agency procures medical equipment through competitive tenders. His timely intervention procured their release.

english_meaning: The act or process of obtaining or acquiring something. The organizational function of sourcing and purchasing goods, works, or services. The goods or supplies obtained. The formal acquisition of military equipment or government resources.
example_sentence: The procurement team invited bids from qualified suppliers. Transparent procurement helps prevent corruption. Rising prices increased the cost of equipment procurement. The hospital reviewed its procurement of medicines and protective gear.

english_meaning: Spending money or resources freely and recklessly. Recklessly wasteful with one's resources or talents. A person who spends resources extravagantly and returns after a period of absence.
example_sentence: The prodigal son returned home after years of wasting his inheritance. Her prodigal spending left her in serious debt before she was thirty. He was known as the prodigal talent of his generation who never fully lived up to his early promise. The company was forced to cut costs after years of prodigal management.

english_meaning: Remarkably or impressively great in size, amount, or degree. Enormous. Huge. Extraordinary. Astonishing. Exceptionally talented or impressive. Used to describe something so large, powerful, or impressive that it causes wonder or amazement in those who see or experience it.
example_sentence: The young pianist showed a prodigious talent at the age of six. The company made a prodigious profit in the last financial year. He has a prodigious memory and can recall thousands of names. The dam holds a prodigious amount of water for the entire region. The author has produced a prodigious number of books in his lifetime.

english_meaning: A young person with exceptional abilities or talents. A person who is very unusually skilled or intelligent. A remarkable or amazing thing. An extraordinary example of a quality.
example_sentence: Mozart was a musical prodigy who composed his first piece at the age of five. The young chess prodigy defeated several grandmasters. She is considered a prodigy in mathematics. The invention was regarded as a prodigy of modern science.

english_meaning: Producing a large amount of work, goods, results, or benefits; efficient and fruitful. A person, activity, system, period, or process that produces useful results, achieves goals efficiently, or generates a large amount of output. It can refer to work, agriculture, business, creativity, learning, and many other fields.
example_sentence: She had a highly productive day and completed all her assignments. Regular planning helps employees become more productive at work. The fertile valley is one of the most productive farming regions in the country. Their discussion was productive and led to several practical solutions.

english_meaning: Work done mainly to create the appearance of being busy rather than to produce useful results. Visible activity performed to impress managers or colleagues. Meetings, messages, reports, or long hours that signal effort but add little real value. A workplace culture that rewards displays of busyness over meaningful outcomes.
example_sentence: Constant status updates can become productivity theatre. She avoided productivity theatre and focused on finishing the report. Staying online late every night was merely productivity theatre. The new manager judged results rather than rewarding productivity theatre.

english_meaning: To treat something holy with a lack of respect. To treat (something sacred) with abuse, irreverence, or contempt. Having or showing a lack of respect for God or religion.
example_sentence: The once-lovely landscape had been profaned by ugly factories. Funny, profane, and fearless, she has become one of America's biggest television celebrities.

english_meaning: Rude, offensive, or vulgar language, especially swear words. The use of words that show disrespect for God or sacred things. Behavior or speech that treats holy matters without reverence. An individual swear word or blasphemous expression.
example_sentence: The film was criticized for its constant profanity. He shouted a profanity when he hit his thumb. Profanity is not tolerated in this classroom. The speaker apologized for using profanity on live television.

english_meaning: To claim that one has a quality or feeling, especially when this is not the case. It also means to affirm one's faith in or allegiance to a religion or set of beliefs. To declare something openly or freely.
example_sentence: He continued to profess his innocence despite the evidence. She professed a great interest in classical music to impress her teacher. Most people in the village profess to be devout Christians. He did not profess to be an expert on the subject.

english_meaning: Claimed or stated openly, often without being sincere. Declared publicly, as a belief, faith, or opinion. Openly admitted or acknowledged by oneself. Having taken the formal vows of a religious order.
example_sentence: His professed love for the country was doubted by many. She is a professed admirer of classical music. Despite his professed honesty, the accounts told another story. The professed nun devoted her life to serving the poor.

english_meaning: A paid job that requires advanced education, training, and special skills. The people working in a particular field taken as a group. An open declaration or statement of belief, feeling, or opinion. A claim made openly, sometimes falsely.
example_sentence: Teaching is a noble and demanding profession. She entered the legal profession after years of study. The medical profession welcomed the new guidelines. His profession of loyalty convinced nobody.

english_meaning: Relating to a job that requires special education, training, or skill. Doing something as a paid occupation rather than as a hobby. Showing the high standards of skill, behavior, and responsibility expected in a job. A person who works in a profession or earns money from an activity. An expert who performs a task with great competence.
example_sentence: She received professional advice before starting her business. He became a professional footballer at the age of nineteen. His professional attitude impressed the whole team. The report was prepared by a team of experienced professionals.

english_meaning: Highly skilled or competent in something. Well-advanced or expert in a particular subject or activity. Capable of performing a task with ease and accuracy. Having thorough knowledge and ability. A skilled person.
example_sentence: She is proficient in three foreign languages. He became proficient at coding within a year. Only proficient drivers should attempt this route. A proficient chef can prepare complex dishes with ease.

english_meaning: A side view of someone's face or head. A short description giving the most important facts or characteristics of someone or something. The extent to which someone attracts public notice. To describe or analyze in a summary form.
example_sentence: The artist drew her profile beautifully. The magazine published a profile of the young scientist. He keeps a low profile in public. The company profiled its top employees. Please update your profile on the website.

english_meaning: Reckless and wasteful spending of money or resources. Extravagance. Shameless immoral behaviour or indulgence in pleasure. Great abundance or excessive use of something.
example_sentence: The government was criticised for its financial profligacy. His profligacy left the family business deeply in debt. The novel describes the profligacy of the royal court. Environmentalists warn against the profligacy of wasting water.

english_meaning: Recklessly wasteful with money or resources. Shamelessly immoral in behaviour, especially in matters of pleasure. A person who spends money extravagantly and carelessly. Someone who lives a dissipated and immoral life.
example_sentence: The government was criticized for its profligate spending. He led a profligate life and lost his entire inheritance. Such profligate use of water cannot continue during a drought. Once a profligate, he later became known for his charity.

english_meaning: Very great or intense, especially regarding an emotion or quality. It describes knowledge or insight that shows great thought or wisdom. It can also refer to something located at or extending to a great depth.
example_sentence: The death of his father had a profound effect on his life. The philosopher offered a profound analysis of the human condition. They shared a moment of profound silence after the announcement. He underwent a profound transformation during his travels abroad.

english_meaning: Great depth of thought, feeling, or meaning. A deep or serious idea. Intellectual depth or insight. The quality of being profound. Great depth in a physical or figurative sense.
example_sentence: The profundity of her words moved the audience. He did not understand the profundity of the problem at first. The poem has beauty as well as profundity. Scientists were struck by the profundity of the discovery.

english_meaning: Very plentiful, abundant, or in large quantity. Given, produced, or existing in great amounts. Excessive or extravagant in expression, such as praise, thanks, or apology. Flowing freely or generously without restraint.
example_sentence: He offered profuse apologies for arriving late. The garden was filled with profuse blossoms in spring. She received profuse praise for her speech. The patient was bleeding profusely from the wound. The host gave us profuse thanks for our gift.

english_meaning: In large quantities; abundantly and generously. Done or produced to an excessive or very great degree.
example_sentence: He apologised profusely for his rude behaviour. She was sweating profusely after the long run. The garden bloomed profusely after the heavy rains. He thanked her profusely for saving his life.

english_meaning: A very large amount of something, an abundance or plentiful supply. A great quantity, richness, or abundance of something. It is used when there is more than enough of something, often in a noticeable or impressive way. It can describe objects, colors, flowers, words, emotions, or anything appearing in large numbers.
example_sentence: The garden was filled with a profusion of colorful flowers. She apologized with a profusion of kind words. A profusion of stars brightened the night sky. The market displayed a profusion of fresh fruits and vegetables.

english_meaning: A person or thing from which others are derived; an ancestor or originator. The first or earliest member of a lineage, movement, or type.
example_sentence: He is considered the progenitor of the modern detective novel. The wolf is the progenitor of the domestic dog. She was the progenitor of a proud family of musicians. Darwin's work is the progenitor of modern evolutionary theory.

english_meaning: A person's children or descendants; the offspring of an animal or plant. Also used figuratively to mean the result or product of something.
example_sentence: The king's progeny ruled the empire for generations. The scientist studied the progeny of the crossbred plants. Her novels are the progeny of years of research and experience. The progeny of the original settlers still live in that village.

english_meaning: A steroid hormone produced mainly in the ovaries and placenta that plays a key role in the menstrual cycle and maintaining pregnancy. Also used in hormone replacement therapy.
example_sentence: Progesterone levels rise significantly during pregnancy. The doctor prescribed progesterone supplements after the miscarriage. Low progesterone can cause irregular menstrual cycles. Progesterone is used in some forms of contraception.

english_meaning: A prediction about what is likely to happen, especially regarding the future course of a disease, situation, or condition. An expert prediction or forecast about the future outcome of something. It is most commonly used in medicine to describe a doctor’s opinion about a patient’s chances of recovery or the expected progress of an illness. It can also be used in business, economics, weather, education, and general situations to indicate a forecast or expectation.
example_sentence: The doctor gave a positive prognosis after reviewing the test results. Economic experts presented a gloomy prognosis for the coming year. Early treatment improved the patient’s prognosis significantly. The weather prognosis suggested heavy rain during the weekend.

english_meaning: Something that predicts or indicates a future event, condition, or result. A sign, indication, prediction, or forecast about what is likely to happen in the future, especially in medicine, weather, business, or general situations. It can describe something that helps predict an outcome or a person or thing that gives a forecast.
example_sentence: The doctor gave a prognostic report about the patient’s recovery. Dark clouds were prognostic of heavy rain. Experts studied the prognostic signs of economic decline. His calm behavior was prognostic of success in the interview.

english_meaning: Forward or onward movement toward a destination or goal. Development toward an improved or more complete condition. To move forward or advance toward a goal or completion.
example_sentence: The project is making steady progress and is expected to be completed on schedule. She was pleased with the progress her students had made during the academic year. The patient's progress after the surgery was encouraging for the entire medical team. He reported that the negotiations were progressing slowly but in the right direction. Medical science continues to progress at a remarkable and accelerating pace.

english_meaning: A sequence of numbers with a specific pattern or rule. The process of developing or moving forward gradually. A series advancing in a regular way. Movement toward a goal or more advanced state.
example_sentence: The arithmetic progression increases by 2 each time. Disease progression was monitored closely. The chord progression sounds harmonious. His career showed steady progression.

english_meaning: Favouring social reform, new ideas, and gradual improvement. Happening or developing steadily over a period of time. Relating to a tax system in which the rate rises as income rises. In grammar, a verb form that shows a continuing action, such as 'is running'.
example_sentence: The party promised a progressive policy on education. Doctors described her illness as a progressive condition. Most countries use a progressive system of income tax. The progressive tense is formed with the verb to be.

english_meaning: In a way that develops or increases gradually over time. Step by step, in a continuing sequence. In a manner that favours reform, modern ideas, or social progress. Increasingly, with each stage becoming greater than the last.
example_sentence: His health improved progressively after the operation. The road becomes progressively narrower near the village. Taxes are charged progressively according to income. The company progressively adopted greener technologies.

english_meaning: A political and social philosophy that supports reform and gradual improvement of society. Belief in advancing social justice, equality, and modern reform through government action. An educational movement that stresses learning by experience and the needs of the child. Support for change and progress rather than tradition.
example_sentence: Progressivism shaped many reforms of the early twentieth century. She defended progressivism in her weekly newspaper column. Critics argue that progressivism ignores traditional values. Progressivism in education encourages learning through activity.

english_meaning: To officially forbid something by law, rule, or authority. To prevent a person from doing a particular thing. To make an action impossible because of circumstances or conditions. To ban an activity within a specified place or time.
example_sentence: The law prohibits the sale of tobacco to children. School rules prohibit the use of mobile phones in class. Heavy snow prohibited any travel through the mountain pass. The court prohibited him from contacting the witness.

english_meaning: Officially forbidden by law, rule, or authority. Not allowed to be used, sold, or carried out. Describing an action that carries a penalty if performed. Prevented or blocked from happening.
example_sentence: Parking is strictly prohibited in front of the gate. The airline listed all prohibited items on its website. Smoking is prohibited in every public building. He was prohibited from entering the stadium for two years.

english_meaning: The act of officially forbidding something by law or rule. A law, order, or rule that bans a particular activity. The period in the United States when making and selling alcohol was banned. The state of being formally not allowed.
example_sentence: There is a strict prohibition on smoking inside the hospital. The new law placed a prohibition on plastic bags. Prohibition in America led to widespread illegal trade. Their religion imposes a prohibition against gambling.

english_meaning: So high in cost that something becomes impossible or unaffordable. Serving to forbid or prevent an action by rule or law. Discouraging people from doing something because of severe difficulty or expense. Very unlikely to be beaten or achieved, as of odds in a contest.
example_sentence: The cost of private treatment is simply prohibitive. Prohibitive taxes discouraged people from importing cars. There are prohibitive rules against parking on this street. The champion started the match as a prohibitive favourite.

english_meaning: To an extent that prevents something from being done or afforded. In a way that forbids or restricts an action. So expensively that buying or doing something becomes impossible. In a manner that strongly discourages people.
example_sentence: Housing in the city centre is prohibitively expensive. The equipment proved prohibitively costly for small farms. Insurance premiums rose prohibitively after the accident. Travelling by air was prohibitively priced last summer.

english_meaning: An estimate or forecast of a future amount, trend, or situation. The act of displaying an image on a surface. A part that sticks out beyond a surface. The representation of the curved earth on a flat map. The unconscious attribution of one’s own feelings to another person. The act of throwing or extending something outward.
example_sentence: The sales projection suggests steady growth next year. The projection of the film began at eight o’clock. A stone projection provided a narrow ledge above the path. This map projection distorts distances near the poles.

english_meaning: The class of industrial wage earners who own little property and live by selling their labour. The working class of a society, especially in Marxist theory. Ordinary labourers regarded as a social and economic group. The lowest social or economic class of a community.
example_sentence: Marx believed the proletariat would eventually rise against the ruling class. Factory conditions in the city were shaped by the demands of the proletariat. The party claimed to speak for the proletariat. Rapid industrialisation created a large urban proletariat.

english_meaning: To increase rapidly in number or amount. To multiply or grow quickly. To reproduce or spread widely. To become more numerous over a short period of time.
example_sentence: Fake news stories proliferate on social media. Cancer cells proliferate rapidly in the body. Coffee shops have proliferated in the city. Rumors began to proliferate after the announcement. Small businesses proliferated during the boom.

english_meaning: A rapid increase in the number or amount of something. Widespread growth or multiplication. The spread of something, especially weapons or technology, to many places or people. Sudden expansion.
example_sentence: The proliferation of nuclear weapons is a global concern. There has been a rapid proliferation of mobile phones. The proliferation of fake news threatens democracy. Governments are worried about the proliferation of drugs. The proliferation of new species amazed scientists.

english_meaning: The state of using too many words; unnecessary long speech or writing. Speech or writing that is excessively long and often boring because it includes too many unnecessary details. It is when someone explains something in a long-winded way instead of being clear and brief.
example_sentence: The professor’s prolixity made the lecture difficult to follow. His prolixity in emails annoys his colleagues. The report suffered from prolixity and needed editing. Good writing avoids prolixity and stays concise.
