english_meaning: To extend the duration of something. To make something continue for a longer time than usual or expected. To lengthen the time, period, or duration of an action, event, situation, or process. It is often used when something continues beyond its normal limit.
example_sentence: Heavy rain may prolong the match. The doctor advised him not to prolong the treatment unnecessarily. Lack of sleep can prolong recovery from illness. They decided to prolong their stay in Karachi for two more days.

english_meaning: The act of making something continue for a longer time. The state of being extended in duration. An extension or lengthening of a period, process, life, sound, or structure. An unnecessary or deliberate delay in ending something.
example_sentence: The prolongation of the conflict caused further suffering. The new medicine may allow the prolongation of healthy life. A prolongation of the deadline was granted after the storm. The singer used the prolongation of the final note for dramatic effect.

english_meaning: Making something last longer than usual or longer than necessary. Extending the duration of an event, condition, process, or period. Delaying the end or completion of something. Continuing pain, difficulty, life, or activity for additional time.
example_sentence: They are prolonging the meeting with unnecessary questions. The treatment may help in prolonging the patient’s life. Avoid prolonging the argument when both sides are tired. Heavy rain is prolonging the construction work.

english_meaning: The act or process of making something last longer. An extension of time, duration, life, or activity. A delay in the ending or completion of something. A prolonged or extended condition. A rare noun commonly replaced by prolongation.
example_sentence: The prolongment of the negotiations frustrated both parties. Doctors discussed the possible prolongment of his life. Further prolongment of the deadline would affect the schedule. The legal dispute resulted in the prolongment of uncertainty.

english_meaning: Well known, important, or easily noticed. Someone or something that stands out clearly, is easily seen, widely known, or holds an important position in society, a group, or a field.
example_sentence: She is a prominent leader in the community. The building has a prominent position in the city center. His prominent role in the project was widely appreciated. There is a prominent mark on the wall.

english_meaning: In a way that is easily seen or noticed. In a position of importance or fame. So as to stand out clearly from the surroundings. In a manner that plays a major or leading part in something.
example_sentence: Her name was printed prominently on the cover. The notice was displayed prominently near the entrance. He featured prominently in the discussion. The issue figured prominently during the election campaign.

english_meaning: A statement telling someone that you will certainly do something. To assure someone that something will happen. An indication of future success or good quality. A reason to expect something good.
example_sentence: He kept his promise and returned the money. She promised to help me with the report. The young player shows great promise. I promise I will never lie to you again.

english_meaning: In a way that shows signs of future success. Encouragingly and hopefully. So as to suggest good results are likely.
example_sentence: The talks began promisingly on the first day. Her career started promisingly after graduation. The experiment progressed promisingly in the early stages. The team played promisingly in the opening match.

english_meaning: A high point of land or rock projecting into a body of water. A headland or cliff extending out into the sea. A prominent mass of land jutting forward. A raised area of land, often used as a lookout.
example_sentence: The lighthouse stood on a rocky promontory. Ships were warned to avoid the dangerous promontory. The village was built on a high promontory overlooking the sea. From the promontory, they watched the sunset. The fort was built on a strategic promontory.

english_meaning: To move someone to a higher rank or position. To support or encourage the development of something. To advertise and publicize a product, idea, or activity to increase its popularity or success.
example_sentence: The company decided to promote her to manager after five years of hard work. The government launched a campaign to promote education in rural areas. Doctors promote healthy eating habits among their patients. The brand uses social media to promote its new products.

english_meaning: Done, performed, or delivered without delay. Quick to act, respond, or perform a task. To cause or bring about an action. Words spoken to help an actor remember lines. In computing, a symbol or message asking for input.
example_sentence: Thank you for your prompt reply. He gave a prompt response to my question. Her fear prompted her to run away. The teacher had to prompt the student during the speech. Type your name at the prompt.

english_meaning: Likely to suffer from or experience something. Having a tendency or habit of doing something. Lying flat, especially facing downward. The word prone is used to describe a person, thing, or situation that is likely to be affected by something or naturally inclined toward a particular behavior. It can also describe a physical position in which someone is lying flat facing downward.
example_sentence: Children are often prone to catching colds during winter. He is prone to making careless mistakes when tired. The area is prone to flooding after heavy rain. The soldier lay prone on the ground during the training exercise.

english_meaning: One of two or more long, pointed parts of a fork or other object. A pointed projecting part. A separate part or aspect of an argument, plan, or attack. A branch of something.
example_sentence: One prong of the fork was bent. The plug has three metal prongs. Their strategy has a two-prong approach. The army launched a three-prong attack. He held the branch by its sharp prong.

english_meaning: The plural of 'prong'. The pointed projecting parts of a fork, tool, plug, or similar object. Separate branches or aspects of a plan, strategy, or attack considered together.
example_sentence: The fork has four sharp prongs. Do not touch the metal prongs of the plug. The deer has magnificent prongs on its antlers. The plan has three main prongs. The army attacked from multiple prongs.

english_meaning: To make the sound of a word or letter in a particular way. To declare or announce something officially or formally. To pass judgment or express an opinion. To utter clearly.
example_sentence: How do you pronounce your name? The judge pronounced the sentence yesterday. The doctor pronounced him fit to travel. She pronounces English words very clearly. The priest pronounced them husband and wife.

english_meaning: To give an official or formal opinion or judgement about something. To make a public statement declaring one's view on a matter. To pass judgement authoritatively, as a judge or expert does. To comment decisively on a question after consideration.
example_sentence: The court will pronounce on the matter next week. He refused to pronounce on issues outside his field. Experts were invited to pronounce on the safety of the bridge. The committee has yet to pronounce on the new proposal.

english_meaning: The way in which a word or language is spoken. The manner in which a person produces the sounds of speech. A particular accepted or standard way of saying a word. The act or skill of uttering sounds correctly and clearly.
example_sentence: Her English pronunciation improved after months of practice. The dictionary shows the correct pronunciation of each word. There are two accepted pronunciations of this name. Poor pronunciation can make even simple sentences hard to follow.

english_meaning: A pole or beam used for support. An object used on stage or screen by actors during a performance. A person or thing providing support or assistance. To support something physically; to position something so it is leaning against something else.
example_sentence: He used a wooden prop to keep the window open. The actor forgot his prop knife in the dressing room. She was more than just a friend; she was my emotional prop during a difficult time. Can you prop the door open while I carry these boxes in? The stage crew was busy arranging the props before the play began.

english_meaning: Information spread to influence opinions, often biased or misleading. Biased or misleading information used to influence people. Organized effort to promote a specific idea or agenda. Communication designed to shape attitudes of a group. Information spread for political or ideological purposes. Information, ideas, or messages deliberately distributed to shape public opinion, promote a political cause, support an ideology, or influence behavior. It may use selective facts, emotional appeal, or repetition to persuade people.
example_sentence: The poster was created as propaganda to support the campaign. Some news on social media is actually propaganda. The government denied spreading propaganda. The film was criticized for political propaganda.

english_meaning: To spread, reproduce, increase, or promote something such as ideas, plants, information, or beliefs. To cause something to spread widely from one place to another. It can be used for plants when growing new plants from seeds or cuttings, for ideas when sharing beliefs or opinions, and for information when making it known to many people.
example_sentence: Farmers propagate plants by using healthy seeds. The internet helps people propagate useful information quickly. Some groups try to propagate their beliefs through social media. Scientists propagate rare plants in special laboratories.

english_meaning: To push, drive, move, or force something forward. To cause someone or something to move forward or ahead. It can refer to physical movement, such as pushing a boat through water, or figurative movement, such as motivating someone toward success or progress.
example_sentence: Strong winds helped propel the boat across the lake. Hard work and determination propelled her toward success. The engine propels the machine at high speed. New technology can propel a business to greater growth.

english_meaning: A natural tendency or strong liking to behave in a particular way. A natural inclination, tendency, or habit to think, act, or behave in a certain way. It is often used for repeated behavior, qualities, or preferences that a person naturally shows.
example_sentence: She has a propensity for helping people in need. His propensity to interrupt others made meetings difficult. Children often show a propensity for curiosity and exploration. The manager noticed his propensity for careful planning and attention to detail.

english_meaning: Suitable, correct, or appropriate for a particular purpose. Following accepted rules, customs, or standards of behaviour. Genuine, real, or of the expected kind. Belonging strictly to a particular thing or place; used after a noun to mean the main part.
example_sentence: Please fill the form in the proper manner. He never had a proper meal all day. That is not the proper way to speak to elders. The suburbs are busy, but the city proper is quiet.

english_meaning: A prediction of what will happen in the future. A divinely inspired revelation or message. The action or practice of prophesying. A declaration of something to come. An inspired utterance from a prophet.
example_sentence: The ancient prophecy foretold of a great hero. Her prophecy about the election proved accurate. Biblical prophecies are studied by scholars. The prophecy warned of dark times ahead.

english_meaning: To predict or foretell future events. To speak as a prophet or by divine inspiration. To declare or indicate in advance. To make a prediction about what will happen.
example_sentence: The oracle prophesied victory in battle. She prophesied that technology would change everything. Prophets prophesy according to divine revelation. He prophesied doom if they ignored the warnings.

english_meaning: A person chosen by God to convey His message to humanity. A person who receives divine revelation and communicates it to others. A religious messenger who teaches people about God, faith, worship, morality, and righteous conduct. A person who calls people toward obedience to God and away from wrongdoing. A divinely appointed teacher who guides people according to religious revelation. A person regarded as an intermediary through whom a divine message is communicated to a community.
synonyms: ["Messenger","Divine messenger","Prophetic messenger","Seer","Spokesperson of God","Religious teacher","Spiritual guide","Revelator","Visionary","Oracle"]
example_sentence: Muslims believe that Prophet Muhammad was the final prophet sent by Allah. The prophet taught his people to worship God and live righteous lives. The people listened carefully to the prophet's message. The prophet warned his people against injustice and wrongdoing.

english_meaning: A person who predicts disaster, failure, or misfortune. Someone who constantly forecasts negative outcomes. A pessimist who warns of impending catastrophe. A person who spreads fear or despair about the future.
example_sentence: He's such a prophet of doom, always predicting the worst. The prophet of doom warned that the economy would collapse. Don't be a prophet of doom; stay positive. Every crisis brings out prophets of doom.

english_meaning: A female prophet. A woman who speaks by divine inspiration or foretells future events. A female spokesperson for a doctrine or cause. A woman regarded as an inspired teacher or messenger of God.
example_sentence: Deborah was a prophetess in the Old Testament. The prophetess warned of coming dangers. Ancient societies revered prophetesses for their wisdom. She was known as a prophetess of social justice.

english_meaning: Accurately predicting or describing what will happen in the future. Having the nature or characteristics of a prophet. Containing or constituting a prophecy. Foreseeing or foretelling future events.
example_sentence: Her warnings proved prophetic when the crisis occurred. The novel's prophetic vision anticipated modern technology. His prophetic words came true years later. The artist's work was prophetic of future trends.

english_meaning: The state of being close to someone or something in space or time. Nearness or proximity. A close kinship or relationship. Similarity or affinity between things. Physical or emotional closeness.
example_sentence: The propinquity of their houses made them close friends. Propinquity often leads to strong relationships. There is a propinquity between the two theories. The propinquity of the deadline made everyone nervous.

english_meaning: To win or regain the favor of someone by doing something that pleases them. To appease, conciliate, or calm someone who is angry or offended, often by offering a gift, apology, or favorable action.
example_sentence: He tried to propitiate his angry friend by apologizing sincerely. The villagers offered prayers to propitiate the gods before the harvest season. She sent flowers to propitiate her offended colleague. The company issued a public apology to propitiate its disappointed customers.

english_meaning: The act of pleasing or calming someone who is angry or offended. The process of gaining someone's favour by doing something acceptable to them. An offering or gift made to appease a god, spirit, or powerful person. In religion, the means by which anger is turned away and peace is restored. Something given or done to make amends and win forgiveness.
example_sentence: The gift was offered as a propitiation of the angry king. Ancient peoples practised sacrifice as a propitiation of their gods. His apology was a simple act of propitiation. The ceremony was held for the propitiation of the spirits.

english_meaning: Intended to please or calm someone who is angry or displeased. Serving to win favour or restore goodwill. Relating to an offering made to appease a god or higher power. Done with the purpose of making amends for a wrong. Conciliatory in tone, manner, or intention.
example_sentence: He offered a propitiatory smile to his angry neighbour. The tribe performed a propitiatory ritual before the harvest. She sent flowers as a propitiatory gesture. His propitiatory tone helped calm the meeting.

english_meaning: Indicating a good or favorable chance of success, especially regarding circumstances or timing. Favorable or auspicious, suggesting that conditions are right for something to happen successfully. Showing or suggesting that future events will turn out well. Suitable, timely, or advantageous for a particular purpose or action.
example_sentence: The investors felt the timing was propitious for launching the new product.  A propitious start to the season gave the team confidence for the months ahead.  The weather conditions were propitious for the outdoor wedding ceremony.  Analysts described the economic climate as propitious for new businesses.  They waited for a more propitious moment to announce the merger.

english_meaning: A person who publicly supports and argues in favour of an idea, cause, or plan. Someone who puts forward a proposal or theory for consideration. An active supporter or defender of a policy or belief. A person who promotes a particular course of action. An advocate who speaks in support of something.
example_sentence: She is a leading proponent of renewable energy. The proponents of the plan presented their arguments clearly. He became a strong proponent of educational reform. Proponents argue that the new law will help small businesses.

english_meaning: A part or share of a whole. The relationship in size, amount, or degree between two or more things. Correct or pleasing balance between the parts of something. The size or importance of something, often used in the plural. To adjust something so that it is in correct relation to something else.
example_sentence: A large proportion of the students passed the examination. The proportion of salt to water must be exact. The artist has a fine sense of proportion. The problem has now grown to alarming proportions.

english_meaning: Corresponding in size, amount, or degree to something else. Increasing or decreasing at the same rate as another quantity. Fair and balanced in relation to what something deserves. In mathematics, having a constant ratio to another quantity. Relating to a system where results are shared according to share or number.
example_sentence: Your salary will be proportional to the hours you work. The punishment should be proportional to the offence. Several countries use a proportional voting system. The cost is directly proportional to the quantity ordered.

english_meaning: The quality of being in correct proportion or balance with something else. The relationship between two amounts that change together at the same rate. Fairness achieved when a response matches the seriousness of a situation. A legal and moral principle requiring that action taken should not exceed what is necessary. Suitable balance between the parts of a whole.
example_sentence: The court examined the proportionality of the punishment. There must be proportionality between risk and reward. Critics questioned the proportionality of the military response. The design is admired for its perfect proportionality.

english_meaning: In a way that corresponds in size, degree, or amount to something else. In a manner that maintains a constant ratio or relationship. According to a particular scale or proportion.
example_sentence: As the company grows, the overhead costs increase proportionally. Both groups were represented proportionally in the final decision-making body. The tax rate increases proportionally with the individual's income level. The size of the text was adjusted proportionally to fit the screen.

english_meaning: Corresponding in size, amount, degree, or intensity to something else. Existing in a constant or suitable ratio. Fair, appropriate, or reasonable in relation to the circumstances or importance involved.
example_sentence: The punishment should be proportionate to the severity of the crime. His salary was not proportionate to the long hours he worked. The company promised a proportionate increase in benefits for senior staff. Resources were allocated in a proportionate manner based on regional needs.

english_meaning: In a way that corresponds in size, amount, degree, or importance to something else. In correct or suitable proportion. Relatively, when compared with another quantity or condition.
example_sentence: Employees contribute proportionately to their income. The smaller room is proportionately easier to heat. Funds were divided proportionately among the participating schools. As demand rose, production costs increased proportionately.

english_meaning: Having dimensions or parts that have a particular relationship to each other in terms of size or shape. Often used with an adverb like 'well' or 'perfectly' to describe physical form. Created or adjusted to fit a specific ratio.
example_sentence: He was a well-proportioned athlete with a powerful build. The architect designed a perfectly proportioned room that felt spacious yet cozy. Her features were finely proportioned and elegant. The rooms were proportioned to allow for maximum natural light.

english_meaning: A plan or suggestion put forward formally for others to consider. A written document setting out a plan of work or research. An offer of marriage. The act of proposing something.
example_sentence: The board approved the proposal without changes. She submitted a research proposal to the university. He accepted her proposal of marriage with joy. Their proposal was rejected by the council.

english_meaning: To put forward an idea or plan for others to consider. To suggest a course of action. To ask someone to marry you. To nominate a person for a position or honour. To intend or plan to do something.
example_sentence: The committee proposed a new plan for the park. He proposed to her on her birthday. I propose that we meet again next week. She was proposed as the next chairperson.

english_meaning: An idea, plan, statement, or suggestion for consideration, acceptance, or rejection. A business deal, a theory, or even a proposal in logic or mathematics.
example_sentence: The manager presented a new business proposition. The manager put forward a business proposition that promised high profits for the company. She rejected his proposition of working late hours because it affected her personal life. The scientist presented a new proposition about climate change which gained global attention.

english_meaning: A person who owns, manages, or has legal rights over a business, property, shop, company, or establishment. An individual who possesses ownership of a business, store, land, building, or other property and has the authority to control, manage, and benefit from it. In a sole proprietorship business, the proprietor is the single owner who is responsible for profits, losses, and decision-making.
example_sentence: The proprietor of the bookstore greeted every customer personally. The proprietor invested money to expand his business. As the sole proprietor, she makes all important decisions herself. The proprietor is responsible for the success and failure of the company.

english_meaning: Correct, proper, and socially acceptable behavior. It also refers to appropriateness, decency, and conformity to moral or social rules. Behaving in a proper, respectful, and socially acceptable way.
example_sentence: The manager conducted the meeting with complete propriety and professionalism. She questioned the propriety of discussing private matters in public. Teachers are expected to maintain propriety in their dealings with students. His behavior lacked the propriety expected at a formal ceremony.

english_meaning: To divide, distribute, or calculate something proportionally according to a share, time, or rate. To allocate an amount in proportion to the relevant period or usage. To adjust a charge or payment so it reflects only the part that applies. To split costs or benefits fairly based on proportion.
example_sentence: The company will prorate the rent for the half month. Your salary will be prorated based on the days you worked. The refund was prorated according to the unused period. They decided to prorate the charges among all the users. The bill was prorated to reflect the actual usage.

english_meaning: To officially stop or suspend a session, especially of a parliament, without dissolving it. The formal act of discontinuing a session of a legislative body such as parliament for a period of time. The body is not dissolved, meaning it can resume later. It is usually done by a head of state or authority.
example_sentence: The president decided to prorogate the parliament until next month. The session was prorogated due to political disagreements. The governor has the authority to prorogate the assembly. Parliament was prorogated before any decision could be finalized.

english_meaning: To discontinue a meeting of parliament or an assembly without dissolving it. To suspend or end a session of a legislative body for a period of time, after which it may resume later. It is usually done officially by a ruler, president, or authority.
example_sentence: The prime minister decided to prorogue parliament rather than face certain defeat from a united opposition. The President decided to prorogue the parliament until next month due to political unrest. The assembly was prorogued after the budget session was completed. The Governor has the constitutional power to prorogue the provincial legislature.

english_meaning: The plural of 'pro'. Arguments, reasons, or considerations in favor of something. The positive or advantageous aspects of an idea, action, or situation. Also used informally for professionals or experts in a field.
example_sentence: Let us weigh the pros and cons before deciding. The pros of the new plan outweigh the cons. She listed all the pros of the job offer. Only true pros can handle such pressure. The team hired several pros for the project.

english_meaning: Advantages & disadvantages. The advantages (pros) and disadvantages (cons) of something. The positive and negative sides of an idea, action, or decision.
synonyms: ["Benefits and drawbacks","Strengths and weaknesses","Gains and losses"]
example_sentence: Consider the pros and cons before deciding. Before buying a new car, you should consider the pros and cons of different models. There are many pros and cons to working from home. He listed the pros and cons before accepting the job offer. Let’s discuss the pros and cons of using social media for education.

english_meaning: Lacking imagination, excitement, or originality; dull and ordinary. Commonplace or unromantic in nature. Having the style or character of prose rather than poetry. Straightforward and matter-of-fact.
example_sentence: His prosaic style of writing bored the readers. She gave a prosaic description of the beautiful landscape. Life in the small town was rather prosaic. The report was factual but prosaic. His speech was prosaic and lacked emotion.

english_meaning: To forbid by law. To officially prohibit something. To ban. To denounce or condemn. To outlaw a person, group, or activity. When an authority such as a government, court, or organization formally forbids an activity, group, book, or substance, often with legal punishment for those who break the ban.
example_sentence: The government has proscribed several extremist organizations. Smoking is proscribed in all public buildings. The book was proscribed by the regime for political reasons. Many religious texts proscribe the consumption of alcohol. The new law proscribes the import of these chemicals.

english_meaning: Written or spoken language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure. Ordinary writing as distinguished from poetry. Plain, straightforward speech or writing. A dull or ordinary manner of expression.
example_sentence: The novel is written in beautiful prose. He prefers poetry over prose. Her prose flows smoothly and clearly. Students learn both prose and poetry in class. The book is a collection of essays and prose.

english_meaning: To take legal action against someone in a court of law for a crime. To officially charge and try someone for breaking the law. To continue or carry out an activity, plan, or task with effort and determination.
example_sentence: The government decided to prosecute the corrupt officials. The lawyer worked hard to prosecute the criminal case successfully. They continued to prosecute their research despite many difficulties. The company may prosecute anyone who copies its software illegally.

english_meaning:
Legal action against an offender, Criminal proceedings in a court, The work of government lawyers in a criminal case.
Persistent pursuit of a task, objective, or investigation. Formal accusation and trial of an alleged criminal. The institution and conduct of legal proceedings against a person accused of a criminal offense. The side in a criminal case that presents evidence to prove that the accused person committed the crime. The act of pursuing or carrying out something persistently until completion.
example_sentence: The prosecution presented strong evidence against the suspect. The prosecution argued that the accused had planned the crime. The judge dismissed the case because the prosecution lacked sufficient evidence. The prosecution of corruption cases is essential for justice.

english_meaning: A person, usually a lawyer or government legal officer, who brings a criminal case against someone accused of a crime and presents evidence in court to prove the charges. A legal officer who conducts criminal proceedings. A person who institutes and carries on a legal action. A government attorney responsible for criminal cases. An advocate who presents evidence against an accused person. A person who formally accuses another in a court of law.
synonyms: ["Attorney","District Attorney","Public Prosecutor","State Attorney","Crown Prosecutor","Legal Representative","Government Lawyer","Advocate"]
example_sentence: The prosecutor presented strong evidence against the accused. The prosecutor questioned several witnesses during the trial. The prosecutor requested a stricter punishment from the court. The prosecutor reviewed all the documents before filing charges.

english_meaning: Relating to or characteristic of a prosecutor or the act of prosecution. Describing the manner, approach, or work of a legal prosecutor.
example_sentence: The prosecutorial strategy focused on eyewitness testimony. She had a sharp prosecutorial mind that left no stone unturned. The judge criticised the prosecutorial misconduct in the case. His prosecutorial experience made him a respected attorney general.

english_meaning: A neurological condition in which a person cannot recognize faces. Face blindness, facial recognition disorder. Face blindness, is a brain-related condition where a person has difficulty recognizing familiar faces, including friends, family, or even their own face in some cases. It is not related to memory loss or poor eyesight, but to how the brain processes facial features.
example_sentence: She has prosopagnosia and often fails to recognize her colleagues. People with prosopagnosia may rely on voice or clothing to identify others. Despite having prosopagnosia, he manages daily life quite well. Prosopagnosia can be present from birth or develop after brain injury.

english_meaning: A person who cannot recognize faces due to a neurological condition. A person affected by face blindness. Someone who struggles to identify people by facial features. Can describe behavior linked to difficulty in facial recognition. A brain disorder in which a person loses the ability to recognize familiar faces, sometimes even their own. It is not related to memory loss or poor eyesight, but to how the brain processes facial features.
example_sentence: The prosopagnosic patient could not recognize his own brother. She felt embarrassed because being prosopagnosic made social situations difficult. A prosopagnosic individual often relies on voice or clothing to identify people. Scientists study prosopagnosic cases to understand how the brain processes faces.

english_meaning: The possibility or likelihood of some future event occurring. An expected or potential outcome. A wide view of an area of land or sea. A potential customer, candidate, or opportunity. To search or explore for something valuable.
example_sentence: There is little prospect of rain today. She has bright prospects in her career. The prospect from the hilltop was breathtaking. Many prospects visited our exhibition. Miners prospected for gold in the mountains.

english_meaning: A printed document that gives information about a school, business, or investment opportunity in order to attract or inform. A formal statement outlining the main features of a new venture. A brochure describing what is offered.
example_sentence: The university sent me its latest prospectus. He read the company's prospectus before investing. The school prospectus lists all the available courses. Please download the admission prospectus online. The prospectus explains the fee structure clearly.

english_meaning: To grow successfully, especially in wealth, health, or overall condition. To achieve progress, stability, or success over time through favorable conditions or effort.
example_sentence: The business began to prosper after expanding into new markets. Farmers prosper when rainfall is timely and sufficient. Education helps societies prosper in the long run. She worked hard and prospered in her career.

english_meaning: A state of being successful, wealthy, or thriving. A condition in which an individual, group, or nation enjoys economic success, good fortune, well-being, or thriving circumstances in life. It often implies financial stability, growth, and overall flourishing.
example_sentence: The country experienced a period of great prosperity after the new trade policies were implemented. Hard work and education can lead to prosperity in life. His business ventures brought him prosperity beyond his expectations. Community programs are essential to ensure shared prosperity among all citizens.

english_meaning: Successful, especially in making money. Enjoying wealth, good fortune, or thriving conditions. Marked by financial success and well-being. Flourishing, thriving, or advancing.
example_sentence: The prosperous merchant owned three shops. She comes from a prosperous family. Their business is very prosperous these days. He wished them a prosperous new year. Small farmers can also become prosperous with hard work.

english_meaning: A German or Austrian toast said before drinking, equivalent to 'cheers' in English. An expression used to wish good health when raising glasses. Sometimes spelled 'Prosit'.
example_sentence: They raised their glasses and said, 'Prost!'. Prost, my friend, to your good health! At Oktoberfest, everyone shouts 'Prost' together. He smiled and replied, 'Prost!' to the toast. The Germans say 'Prost' before drinking beer.

english_meaning: A gland in the male reproductive system located below the bladder that produces a fluid forming part of semen. Relating to this gland. Enlargement or disease of this gland is common in older men.
example_sentence: The doctor examined his prostate gland. Prostate cancer is common in older men. He is undergoing treatment for a prostate problem. Regular checkups can detect prostate issues early. The surgeon performed a prostate operation successfully.

english_meaning: A walnut-sized gland found just below the male bladder. A gland that produces fluid forming part of semen. An organ that surrounds the upper part of the male urethra. A gland that often enlarges in older men and may cause urinary problems.
example_sentence: The prostate gland produces fluid that nourishes sperm. An enlarged prostate gland can make urination difficult. Men over fifty should have their prostate gland checked. The surgeon removed part of the prostate gland.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting the prostate gland. Concerning conditions, diseases, or treatments of the prostate. Used to describe medical procedures, examinations, or medications related to the prostate.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed prostatic medication. He suffers from a prostatic disorder. A prostatic examination is recommended annually after fifty. She specializes in prostatic surgery. The report showed no prostatic abnormalities.

english_meaning: To lay oneself flat on the ground, especially in worship or submission. It can also mean to weaken someone greatly. A person lying flat with the face downward, often as a sign of respect, worship, surrender, or extreme exhaustion. Someone who is physically or emotionally exhausted.
example_sentence: The pilgrims lay prostrate on the ground during prayer. He was prostrate with grief after hearing the sad news. The illness left her prostrate for several weeks. The defeated army lay prostrate before the enemy forces.

english_meaning: The action of lying stretched out on the ground, especially in submission or worship. Extreme physical weakness or exhaustion. A state of complete mental or emotional collapse. Deep respect shown by bowing down.
example_sentence: The devotees offered prostration before the shrine. Heat prostration is common in summer. He suffered nervous prostration after the accident. The old man performed prostration during prayer. Extreme grief led to her total prostration.

english_meaning: The main character in a story, play, novel, or film. This character drives the story forward and usually faces the main challenges or conflicts. The protagonist is often seen as the hero, but can also be morally complex or flawed.
example_sentence: The protagonist struggles to protect his family during the war. In the novel, the protagonist changes greatly by the end of the story. She is the protagonist who challenges unfair traditions in her village. The film presents a flawed protagonist rather than a perfect hero.

english_meaning: To keep someone or something safe from harm, injury, or damage. To defend against attack or danger. To shield from unwanted influence or exposure. To guard the rights, interests, or well-being of others. To preserve from loss or destruction.
example_sentence: Parents always try to protect their children. A helmet protects the head during a fall. The law protects the rights of workers. Sunscreen protects the skin from harmful rays.

english_meaning: A stable subatomic particle with a positive electric charge, found in the nucleus of every atom. The particle whose number in the nucleus determines which chemical element an atom is. A nucleon with a mass about 1,836 times that of an electron.
example_sentence: A proton has a positive charge equal in size to that of an electron. The number of protons defines the atomic number of an element. Hydrogen has a single proton in its nucleus. Protons and neutrons are held together by a powerful force.

english_meaning: A first model or early version of something made to test or improve it before final production. An original or early sample of a product, system, or idea built to test how it works, identify problems, and improve design before it is produced on a large scale or finalized. It is commonly used in engineering, technology, product design, and software development.
example_sentence: The company built a prototype of the new smartphone before mass production. Engineers tested the prototype to find design flaws. The prototype car had advanced features that were not in the final model. She created a prototype of her app to show investors.

english_meaning: To extend beyond a surface or limit. To be noticeable because of sticking out. To thrust forward in a bold or prominent way. To appear or project, sometimes awkwardly or unexpectedly.
example_sentence: Her elbow protruded from the coat sleeve. The window frame protrudes slightly from the wall. A branch protruded into the pathway, making walking difficult. His confidence protruded in every decision he made.

english_meaning: Something that sticks out from a surface. A part of an object, surface, or body that extends outward beyond the surrounding area. It can refer to natural formations, body parts, or any object that juts forward.
example_sentence: The tree had a large protrusion where the branch had broken. A small protrusion of rock made the path difficult to walk on. The doctor noticed a protrusion on the patient’s back. The metal plate had a protrusion that could catch on clothing.

english_meaning: Something that protrudes or sticks out from a surface. A rounded bulge, swelling, or projection. A part that extends outward beyond the surrounding area. A knob-like growth on a surface.
example_sentence: There was a small protuberance on his forehead. The tree trunk had several protuberances. Doctors examined the strange protuberance on his neck. The rocky protuberance made climbing difficult. She noticed a protuberance on the wall.

english_meaning: Sticking out from a surface; bulging outward. Prominently projecting or swelling. Noticeably raised or bulbous in appearance. Having a swollen or protruding quality.
example_sentence: He has a protuberant belly. The frog has protuberant eyes. She noticed protuberant veins on his hands. The child had a protuberant forehead. Protuberant rocks lined the shore.

english_meaning: A short, commonly known saying that expresses a general truth or piece of advice, often metaphorical or based on experience. A wise saying that people use to give advice or explain something based on common sense or traditional knowledge.
example_sentence: The proverb ‘Slow and steady wins the race’ teaches patience. My grandmother always quotes proverbs in her advice. Many proverbs come from ancient cultures. The meaning of a proverb can be different in various regions. Proverbs often use simple language to teach important lessons. People use proverbs to explain difficult situations easily. She learned many English proverbs while studying abroad. Using a proverb in a conversation can make your point stronger. Proverbs have been passed down from generation to generation.

english_meaning: The protective care of God or nature as a spiritual power. Timely preparation for the future; foresight. A fortunate happening seen as divine intervention. The city that is the capital of Rhode Island, USA.
example_sentence: By divine providence, he survived the accident. She trusted in providence during hard times. His providence saved the family from financial ruin. They believe providence guided their meeting. He moved to Providence for a new job.

english_meaning: Wise in planning for the future, especially by saving money and preparing for future needs. A person who carefully plans for the future. A provident person saves money, avoids waste, prepares for unexpected situations, and manages resources wisely.
example_sentence: She is provident and saves part of her salary every month. A provident family always keeps an emergency fund. His provident habits helped him retire comfortably. Being provident today can prevent financial problems in the future.

english_meaning: Happening at a lucky or very suitable time, as if arranged by God or fate. Fortunate and timely in a way that seems more than mere chance. Relating to divine care, guidance, or protection. Bringing unexpected help exactly when it is needed.
example_sentence: Their arrival was providential, as we had run out of water. A providential change in the weather saved the harvest. It was providential that a doctor was on the train. He called his escape providential rather than lucky.

english_meaning: In a manner showing careful planning for the future. With wise foresight and prudent preparation. In a thrifty and economical way to avoid future difficulty. With prudent care and cautious management of resources. In a way that anticipates future needs and prepares for them.
example_sentence: She providently saved a portion of her salary every month. The farmer providently stored grain for the dry season. He providently invested in insurance for his family's security. The company acted providently by expanding its emergency reserves.

english_meaning: To supply or equip with necessary items, especially food or essentials. The act of supplying or providing something. Supplies of food or necessary items. A condition or clause in a legal document or agreement. Preparation made in advance for future needs.
example_sentence: The government made provision for emergency relief. We bought enough provisions for the trip. The contract includes a provision for late payment penalties. The team was provisioned with all necessary equipment.

english_meaning: The action of provoking or stimulating someone into doing something, especially something negative. An action or statement that causes anger or resentment. Something that incites or triggers a response.
example_sentence: She responded with remarkable calm despite the extreme provocation she had faced. The lawyer argued that his client had acted under serious provocation. The referee punished the player for deliberate provocation of the opposing team. There was no provocation for such a violent and disproportionate response. Any provocation from either side could be enough to reignite the dormant conflict.

english_meaning: Causing anger, excitement, or strong reaction. Intended to stimulate discussion or thought. Deliberately arousing sexual interest or attention. Challenging accepted norms in a bold way.
example_sentence: His provocative remarks upset many people. The film raised provocative questions about society. She wore a provocative dress to the party. The article had a provocative title to attract readers.

english_meaning: To cause a reaction, especially anger, annoyance, or response. To irritate someone and make them angry. To trigger a reaction or response. To stimulate feelings, thoughts, or action. To incite or encourage something to happen. To intentionally or unintentionally trigger a strong reaction, such as anger, irritation, or action. It can also mean to stimulate thoughts, emotions, or events.
example_sentence: His rude comments provoked a strong reaction from the audience. Don’t provoke the dog, it may bite you. The speech provoked anger among the students. The article was written to provoke discussion about climate change.

english_meaning: To move about quietly and secretly, especially while hunting or searching for something. To roam stealthily, often with harmful or suspicious intent. To wander like a predator looking for prey or opportunity. The word is used for both animals and people who move silently in search of something.
example_sentence: The lion was prowling through the tall grass. Thieves prowl the streets at night. A strange man was seen prowling around the house. The cat prowled silently behind the mouse. Reporters prowled the corridors waiting for the politician.

english_meaning: Nearest or next in time, order, space, or relationship. Closest in a chain of causation. Immediate rather than remote. Directly related or connected as the closest cause or factor.
example_sentence: The proximate cause of the fire was faulty wiring. Their houses are in proximate locations. We should focus on the proximate goal first. Doctors identified the proximate reason for the illness. The proximate effects were more damaging than expected.

english_meaning: Closeness in distance, time, or relationship. The state of being near or close to something or someone. It can describe physical distance, such as places being close together, or non physical closeness, such as emotional connection, social relations, or events happening close in time.
example_sentence: The school was built in close proximity to the hospital. Living in proximity to the sea affects the local climate. Emotional proximity helps strengthen relationships. The shop benefits from its proximity to the main road.

english_meaning: The tendency to favor people who are physically nearby or seen more often. An unfair preference for office-based employees over remote workers. A judgment distorted by familiarity, visibility, or frequent personal contact. The assumption that visible workers are more committed or productive.
example_sentence: Remote employees worried that proximity bias would affect promotions. Managers can reduce proximity bias by measuring clear results. Proximity bias led him to overlook a talented colleague abroad. The company trained supervisors to recognize proximity bias.

english_meaning: A person authorized to act on behalf of another. The authority given to someone to act for another, especially in voting. A substitute or representative. Something that serves as a replacement or stand-in for another thing. A figure or value used to represent something else in calculations or analysis.
example_sentence: She attended the meeting as a proxy for her father. Shareholders may vote by proxy if they cannot attend in person. The minister sent his secretary as a proxy to the conference. GDP is often used as a proxy for a country's standard of living. He signed the document by proxy due to his illness.

english_meaning: A computer system or intermediary server that receives requests from a user and forwards them to another server on the internet. It acts as a middle layer between a user and the websites or online services they access. It works as a gateway between a user and the internet. When a user sends a request to visit a website, the request first goes to the proxy server. The proxy server then forwards the request to the target website and returns the response to the user.
synonyms: ["Intermediary Server","Gateway Server","Relay Server","Forwarding Server","Mediator Server","Access Proxy","Network Proxy"]
antonyms: ["Direct Connection","End Server","Origin Server","Peer to Peer Connection","Non Proxy Connection"]
example_sentence: The company uses a proxy server to monitor employees' internet usage. A proxy server can hide your real IP address from websites. Many schools use a proxy server to block inappropriate content. The organization installed a proxy server to improve network security.

english_meaning: A war started by a major power that does not itself become involved. A war in which a state attempts to increase its power or influence without taking part in the action, as by providing arms or finance to one of the participants. A war fought between groups or smaller countries that each represent the interests of other larger powers, and may have help and support from these. A war instigated by a major power that does not itself participate.
synonyms: ["Indirect war","Surrogate war","Delegated conflict","Sponsored conflict","Client war","Third party conflict","Representative war"]
antonyms: ["Direct war","Conventional war","Open warfare","Face to face conflict","Direct military confrontation"]
example_sentence: The conflict became a proxy war as foreign powers supported rival groups. Many historians describe the Cold War as a period that included several proxy wars. The neighboring countries accused each other of fighting a proxy war in the region. A proxy war often prolongs violence because external supporters continue providing resources.

english_meaning: A sensible and careful attitude when you make judgements and decisions, behavior that avoids unnecessary risks. Careful good judgment that allows someone to avoid danger or risks.
example_sentence: It might be more prudent to get a second opinion before going ahead.

english_meaning: Having or showing careful good judgment. Sensible and careful when you make judgements and decisions, avoiding unnecessary risks.
example_sentence: It’s prudent to save money for emergencies. She made a prudent decision. He is prudent in his investments. Only prudent expenditure may provide quality within a restrictive budget. He had borrowed a little more than was prudent.

english_meaning: In a sensible and careful way, in a way that avoids unnecessary risks.
example_sentence: They very prudently decided not to take the case to court.

english_meaning: To try to find out something secret, or to force something open using a tool. To look into someone’s personal or secret affairs without permission. To open or separate something using force, often with a tool. To examine something carefully, often out of curiosity. An act of prying or interfering in others' matters.
example_sentence: She tried to pry into my personal life, which made me uncomfortable. He used a screwdriver to pry open the locked box. The reporter was prying for more details about the incident. Keep your diary safe from prying eyes.

english_meaning: A sacred hymn sung in religious worship. A poem expressing praise to God. A devotional song used in prayer. A spiritual composition celebrating faith and gratitude. Any song or poem of praise and thanksgiving.
example_sentence: He recited a verse of the twenty-third psalm. This is a psalm while packing books. Edward read the two Psalms, and then closed the book. The clergyman began droning the psalm. This psalm talks about how God should be praised. The parson droned out the psalm.

english_meaning: False or fake, Not genuine or not real, Pretending to be something it is not. Having the appearance of something without actually being it. Artificial or imitation, Deceptively similar to the real thing, Spurious, Sham or counterfeit. A person who pretends to be something they are not. An impostor, A fake expert or fake intellectual.
example_sentence: The company exposed a pseudo doctor who had fake qualifications. Many pseudo products look similar to famous brands. He presented a pseudo scientific theory without evidence. The website used a pseudo identity to deceive users.

english_meaning: Related to a neurological condition that affects emotional control, especially sudden laughing or crying that is not appropriate to the situation. Conditions caused by damage to brain pathways that control facial muscles and emotions. It is most commonly used in the term pseudobulbar affect, where a person experiences sudden, involuntary, and exaggerated emotional expressions such as laughing or crying that do not match their actual feelings. This condition is often seen in people with stroke, multiple sclerosis, brain injury, or neurodegenerative diseases.
synonyms: ["Neurological emotional disorder","Involuntary emotional expression","Pseudobulbar affect related"]
example_sentence: The patient showed pseudobulbar symptoms after the stroke. Pseudobulbar affect can cause sudden crying without sadness. Doctors diagnosed her emotional outbursts as pseudobulbar in origin. Medication helped reduce his pseudobulbar emotional episodes.

english_meaning: A fictitious name used by an author, artist, or other person instead of their real name. A pen name. An assumed name used to hide the real identity of a writer, performer, or public figure. Often chosen for privacy, marketing reasons, protection, or because the real name is considered unsuitable for professional use.
synonyms: ["Pen name","Alias","Nom de plume","Assumed name","False name","Stage name","Nickname","Sobriquet"]
example_sentence: The author wrote all her novels under a pseudonym. George Eliot was the pseudonym of Mary Ann Evans. He published his political articles under a pseudonym to avoid trouble. Many musicians perform under a pseudonym. Her real name was kept secret because she used a pseudonym.

english_meaning: Relating to psychiatry, mental illness, or the treatment of mental disorders. Anything connected with psychiatry, which is the branch of medicine focused on diagnosing, treating, and preventing mental, emotional, and behavioral disorders. It includes mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, and other psychological illnesses, as well as their medical and therapeutic treatment.
example_sentence: She was admitted to a psychiatric hospital for treatment of severe depression. The doctor specializes in psychiatric disorders such as anxiety and bipolar disorder. He received psychiatric counseling after the traumatic incident. The patient needs psychiatric evaluation before starting medication.

english_meaning: A doctor who specialises in mental, emotional, and behavioural disorders. A medical expert who diagnoses and treats depression, anxiety, and psychosis. A specialist who can prescribe medicines as well as recommend therapy. A physician trained in the branch of medicine called psychiatry.
example_sentence: The psychiatrist helped him manage his severe depression. She was advised to consult a psychiatrist for anxiety. A psychiatrist reviewed the patient's medication weekly. The psychiatrist listened patiently to his concerns.

english_meaning: A medical field focused on mental health. Psychiatrists are doctors who study how the brain and mind affect behavior, emotions, and thinking. They treat conditions such as depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and other psychological illnesses using therapy, counseling, and medication.
synonyms: ["Mental health medicine","Psychological medicine","Behavioral medicine","Psychiatric science","Mind medicine"]
antonyms: ["Physical medicine only","Somatic medicine (non-mental focus)","Neurology (in contrast focus","Not exact opposite but different field)","General surgery (different medical branch)"]
example_sentence: Psychiatry helps doctors understand and treat depression and anxiety disorders. He decided to specialize in psychiatry after medical school. Modern psychiatry uses both therapy and medication for treatment. Psychiatry plays an important role in improving mental health awareness.

english_meaning: Connected with the human mind or soul. Relating to thoughts, emotions, and mental processes. Having abilities such as telepathy, clairvoyance, or predicting future events. Sensitive to spiritual or supernatural influences. Existing beyond ordinary scientific explanation.
example_sentence: She claims to have psychic abilities that help her understand people's emotions. Many people are interested in psychic readings about their future. The novel tells the story of a psychic who can see hidden events. Some believe psychic experiences come from a deeper level of consciousness.

english_meaning: A mentally disturbed or unstable person. A person who behaves in a crazy, violent, or dangerous manner. Someone who is excessively obsessive or irrational. Informal term for a psychopath.
antonyms: ["Sane person","Rational person","Balanced person","Stable person","Sensible person","Calm person","Normal person","Level headed person"]
example_sentence: The movie villain was a complete psycho who frightened everyone. People thought he was a psycho because of his violent behavior. She became psycho about keeping everything perfectly clean. Do not call someone a psycho without understanding their situation.

english_meaning: A psychological theory and method developed by Sigmund Freud that explores how unconscious thoughts, feelings, memories, and desires influence a person's behavior and emotions. A system of psychology and a therapeutic method that aims to understand the hidden mental processes of the mind. It focuses on unconscious conflicts, childhood experiences, dreams, fears, and desires that may affect a person's actions, emotions, and relationships. In therapy, patients discuss their thoughts and feelings freely so underlying psychological issues can be identified and understood.
synonyms: ["Depth psychology","Psychological analysis","Analytic therapy","Psychodynamic therapy","Mental analysis","Freudian analysis"]
antonyms: ["Behaviorism","Surface observation","Ignorance of motives","Nonanalytic approach","Objective behavior study"]
example_sentence: The therapist used psychoanalysis to help the patient understand hidden emotional conflicts. Psychoanalysis examines how childhood experiences affect adult behavior. Many psychologists study dreams through psychoanalysis. The book discusses psychoanalysis and human personality in detail.

english_meaning: A therapist who uses psychoanalysis to treat patients. Someone trained in the theory and practice of psychoanalysis, often tracing mental issues to unconscious conflicts.
example_sentence: She visited a psychoanalyst to understand her recurring nightmares. The psychoanalyst traced his anxiety to childhood trauma. A psychoanalyst typically works with patients over many years. The psychoanalyst helped her uncover deeply buried emotions.

english_meaning: Relating to psychoanalysis; based on or using the theory and methods developed by Sigmund Freud to explore the unconscious mind.
example_sentence: The therapist used a psychoanalytic approach to treat the patient. Psychoanalytic theory emphasises the role of the unconscious mind. Her psychoanalytic training took over seven years to complete. The researcher published a psychoanalytic study on childhood trauma.

english_meaning: To treat or examine someone using the methods of psychoanalysis; to analyse someone's mental and emotional processes through psychoanalytic techniques.
example_sentence: The therapist spent months psychoanalyzing the patient. She tried to psychoanalyze her friend's strange behaviour. It is not helpful to psychoanalyze people without their consent. He was psychoanalyzed to determine the root of his phobia.

english_meaning: The branch of study that deals with the psychological and neurological factors that enable humans to acquire, use, comprehend, and produce language. It explores how language is processed in the mind and brain.
example_sentence: She teaches psycholinguistics at the university. Psycholinguistics helps explain how children learn language. His research in psycholinguistics won an award. Psycholinguistics is a fascinating branch of applied linguistics. Modern psycholinguistics uses brain imaging techniques.

english_meaning: Related to the mind or mental processes. Connected with how the human mind works, including thoughts, emotions, behavior, and mental health
example_sentence: Stress can have serious psychological effects on students. She received psychological support after the accident. Fear is often more psychological than real. The doctor studied the psychological causes of anxiety.

english_meaning: In a way that is connected with a person's mind and the way in which it works. In a way that is connected with the study of psychology.
example_sentence: The disaster affected the community psychologically as well as economically. She is psychologically strong and handles stress calmly. Children can be psychologically harmed by constant criticism. He prepared himself psychologically before the difficult interview.

english_meaning: A person who studies the mind, emotions, and behavior of humans. A qualified expert who diagnoses and treats mental and emotional disorders. A specialist in the science of psychology.
example_sentence: She consulted a psychologist for her anxiety. The psychologist studied children's learning patterns. He is a well-known clinical psychologist. Every school should have a trained psychologist. The psychologist advised her to relax more.

english_meaning: The scientific study of the mind, emotions, and behavior. The mental characteristics or attitude of a person or group. The study of how people think, feel, and act individually and in groups.
example_sentence: She is studying psychology at university. Child psychology is a very interesting subject. Understanding customer psychology helps in marketing. He wrote a book on the psychology of leadership. The psychology of fear is complex.

english_meaning: An organism that grows and lives in very cold environments. A psychrophile is a microorganism, such as certain bacteria, algae, or fungi, that survives, grows, and reproduces in extremely cold temperatures, often near freezing or below.
example_sentence: Scientists discovered a psychrophile living in Antarctic ice. Some psychrophiles grow best at temperatures close to freezing. Researchers study psychrophiles to understand life in extreme environments. The deep ocean contains many microorganisms that behave like psychrophiles.

english_meaning: Related to puberty or the stage of physical and sexual development during adolescence. The period when a child's body develops into an adult body capable of reproduction. It refers to the physical, hormonal, emotional, and developmental changes that occur during adolescence.
example_sentence: Pubertal changes usually begin between the ages of ten and fourteen. Doctors explained that the emotional changes were a normal part of pubertal development. Good nutrition supports healthy pubertal growth and development. Researchers studied the effects of exercise during the pubertal years.

english_meaning: Relating to puberty or the stage of reaching sexual maturity. Concerning the physical and emotional changes during puberty. Characteristic of the period of adolescence when the body matures.
example_sentence: Pubertic changes usually begin between the ages of ten and fourteen. Doctors often study pubertic development in adolescents. The pubertic stage brings both physical and emotional growth. Parents should support their children through the pubertic years.

english_meaning: The period of a person’s life during which their sexual organs develop and they become capable of having children. The stage in people's lives when they develop from a child into an adult. The time of life when sex glands become functional.
example_sentence: At puberty, pubic hair develops and girls begin to menstruate. He reached puberty later than most of his classmates.

english_meaning: The period during which a person reaches sexual maturity. The state of being at the age of puberty. A soft covering of fine hairs on plants or animals. The onset of adolescence marked by physical changes.
example_sentence: Pubescence brings many changes in a young person's body. Doctors study pubescence to understand growth patterns. The leaves have a soft pubescence on their surface. Emotional support is important during pubescence.

english_meaning: In the stage of development where a child becomes capable of sexual reproduction; beginning to show physical signs of puberty.
example_sentence: The pubescent boy was starting to notice changes in his voice and height. Teachers should be sensitive to the needs of pubescent students. The novel describes the pubescent experiences of a young girl navigating adolescence. Pubescent plants begin producing flowers and seeds.

english_meaning: The front, lower part of the hip bone, situated at the base of the abdomen. One of the three bones that unite to form each side of the pelvis. The bone that meets its partner in the middle to form the pubic joint. A bone that supports the lower abdominal wall and gives attachment to several muscles.
example_sentence: The two halves of the pubis meet at the front of the pelvis. During childbirth the joint between the pubis softens slightly. He suffered a stress fracture of the pubis while running. The pubis lies at the very front of the pelvic ring.

english_meaning: Funds, money, or financial resources that belong to the government or the people of a state, used for public purposes such as development, welfare, and administration.
example_sentence: The government allocated new funds from the public treasury for education reforms. Misuse of the public treasury leads to corruption and loss of public trust. Taxes collected from citizens go directly into the public treasury. The finance minister presented the annual report on the condition of the public treasury.

english_meaning: The state of belonging or being available to the public rather than privately owned. Creative work no longer protected by copyright. Information generally known and openly accessible. Publicly owned land or property.
example_sentence: The novel entered the public domain this year. These photographs are freely available in the public domain. The investigation placed new facts in the public domain. The riverbank remains part of the public domain.

english_meaning: A lawyer who represents the government in criminal cases and brings charges against people accused of crimes. The prosecutor presents evidence in court and tries to prove the accused person's guilt according to the law.
synonyms: ["Prosecutor","State Prosecutor","Government Attorney","Prosecuting Attorney","Crown Prosecutor","State Attorney","District Attorney","Legal Prosecutor"]
antonyms: ["Defense Lawyer","Defense Attorney","Defense Counsel","Advocate for the Accused","Criminal Defense Lawyer"]
example_sentence: The public prosecutor presented strong evidence against the accused. The public prosecutor questioned several witnesses during the trial. The judge listened carefully to the arguments of the public prosecutor. The public prosecutor filed charges after reviewing the evidence.

english_meaning: The preparation and issuing of a book, journal, or piece of music for public sale. The action of making something generally known.
example_sentence: The publication of his first novel was a huge success. The research paper is currently awaiting publication in a journal. The company announced the publication of its annual financial report. Internet publication has made information sharing much faster today.

english_meaning: To make information about something widely known to the public. To advertise or promote a product, event, or idea. To draw public attention to something through media coverage. To spread news or reports about an event or activity. To announce something openly so that many people become aware of it.
example_sentence: The company hired an agency to publicize its new product. They used social media to publicize the charity event. The scandal was publicized by every major newspaper. She worked hard to publicize the plight of the refugees.

english_meaning: To prepare and produce a book, newspaper, magazine, or piece of writing for public sale or distribution. To make information available to people through printed or electronic media. To officially announce something to the public. To have one's work printed and released to readers. To formally issue a statement, notice, or law.
example_sentence: The author plans to publish her new novel next spring. The newspaper will publish the interview tomorrow morning. The government decided to publish the report on climate change. He hopes to publish his research in a well-known journal.

english_meaning: A dark reddish or purplish brown colour. A brownish purple shade, traditionally said to resemble the colour of a flea. Of or having this dark purple-brown colour.
example_sentence: She turned puce with embarrassment when her name was called. The old armchair was covered in faded puce velvet. He chose a puce tie to match his jacket. The walls were an unfortunate shade of puce.

english_meaning: A small pool of liquid, especially rainwater, gathered on a surface. A small, shallow amount of water on the ground. To splash or wade through such small pools. To mix clay and water to make it waterproof.
example_sentence: Children love jumping in puddles after the rain. A muddy puddle formed near the gate. The dog drank from a puddle on the road. She stepped over the puddle carefully. The car splashed water from the puddle.

english_meaning: Modesty, decency, or a sense of shame that prevents a person from behaving, speaking, or dressing in an improper or indecent way. A person's sense of modesty, propriety, and moral decency. It is the quality of being reserved and respectful regarding behavior, appearance, or speech, especially in matters related to personal dignity and morality.
example_sentence: Her pudency and respectful behavior earned her admiration from everyone. The culture places great value on pudency and moral conduct. His speech reflected dignity and pudency rather than arrogance. Pudency is often regarded as an important virtue in traditional societies.

english_meaning: Childishly silly and immature in behaviour or speech. Foolish in a way that is expected of a young child rather than an adult. Trivial and lacking seriousness or good sense. Relating to a boy or to childhood in a formal or medical sense.
example_sentence: His puerile jokes annoyed everyone at the meeting. Such puerile behaviour is unacceptable in a professional office. The argument soon turned into a puerile shouting match. She dismissed the letter as puerile nonsense.

english_meaning: To be smoking a cigarette, pipe, etc To make smoke or steam blow out in clouds, to blow out in clouds. An act of breathing in something such as smoke from a cigarette, or drugs. A small amount of air, smoke, etc that is blown from somewhere.
example_sentence: He puffed on the cigar slowly. The chimney puffed smoke into the sky. She puffed her cheeks and blew out the candle. She blew a puff of smoke into the air. The cream came in a small puff. A puff of wind shook the trees.

english_meaning: Swollen or enlarged with air or gas; inflated. Breathing hard and fast, out of breath. Filled with pride or excitement. (Of food) light and airy in texture from cooking or processing.
example_sentence: His eyes were puffed up from crying. She arrived puffed and out of breath. The kids ate puffed rice for breakfast. He was puffed with pride at the news. The bread came out perfectly puffed.

english_meaning: Breathing in short, quick bursts, often due to exertion. Blowing out air or smoke in small bursts. Praising something excessively, often in advertising. Swelling or expanding with air.
example_sentence: He was puffing after climbing the stairs. The old man sat puffing on his pipe. The train came puffing into the station. She was puffing hard during the race. The chef enjoys puffing pastries in the oven.

english_meaning: The art, practice, or profession of fighting with the fists; boxing. The sport where two participants fight with padded gloves. A formal, sometimes literary term for boxing.
example_sentence: He devoted his life to the art of pugilism. Pugilism was very popular in the nineteenth century. She wrote a history book on pugilism. Modern pugilism requires strict training and discipline. Pugilism champions earn great fame and money.

english_meaning: A person who fights with their fists, especially a professional boxer. A boxer or fighter skilled in the sport of boxing. Someone who takes part in boxing matches for sport or competition.
example_sentence: The famous pugilist trained for hours every day. He became a respected pugilist in his hometown. A skilled pugilist knows how to defend as well as attack. The pugilist raised his gloves after winning the match.

english_meaning: Relating to boxing or fighting with the fists. Showing a readiness or eagerness to fight. Having the qualities or manner of a boxer. Aggressive or combative in behavior.
example_sentence: He had a pugilistic stance whenever he felt challenged. The debate turned into a pugilistic exchange of words. His pugilistic attitude made others uncomfortable. She admired the pugilistic skills of the young athlete.

english_meaning: Eager to argue, fight, quarrel, or show aggressive behavior. It describes a person who likes conflicts or is ready to fight verbally or physically. A person who is aggressive, quarrelsome, or always ready to fight.
example_sentence: The pugnacious boy started arguing with everyone in the class. The manager became pugnacious during the heated meeting. His pugnacious attitude created problems among the team members. Although small in size, the dog was highly pugnacious and barked at strangers constantly.

english_meaning: Physical beauty; loveliness, especially of a woman. Great attractiveness in appearance. A formal or literary term for beauty. Comeliness and grace.
example_sentence: Her pulchritude captivated everyone at the party. Poets have long praised the pulchritude of nature. The actress was famous for her pulchritude. Ancient sculptures often celebrated human pulchritude. The painting captured her pulchritude perfectly.

word: Pull a rabbit out of a hat
english_meaning: To produce a surprising solution when it seems impossible. To achieve something unexpected at the last moment. To perform an apparent miracle in a difficult situation. To rescue a situation by a sudden clever act.
synonyms: ["Work a miracle","Save the day","Improvise brilliantly","Come up with a surprise"]
example_sentence: The coach pulled a rabbit out of a hat with that substitution. We need to pull a rabbit out of a hat before the deadline. She pulled a rabbit out of a hat and found the missing file. Investors hoped the CEO would pull a rabbit out of a hat.

english_meaning: To handle roughly or drag around.
example_sentence: The child was pulled about by the crowd. The luggage was pulled about.

english_meaning: To move faster than others and take the lead in a race, competition, or journey. To become more successful, advanced, or stronger than others in business, studies, or performance. To increase a lead after already being slightly ahead.
example_sentence: The red car pulled ahead in the final lap. Our team pulled ahead in the second half. She pulled ahead of her competitors. The company pulled ahead in sales this year.

english_meaning: To separate people or animals that are fighting. To separate something into pieces by pulling different parts of it in different directions. To say that something, usually a piece of work, is very bad.
example_sentence: Customers stepped in and pulled the two men apart. The rolls pull apart easily. She pulled the rolls apart with her hands. His gambling problem is pulling the family apart. The last essay I gave him he completely pulled apart. They pulled apart the old machine. The crowd was pulled apart by police.

english_meaning: To take long deep breaths from a cigarette, etc. To pull something quickly and usually repeatedly. To tug or pull something repeatedly.
example_sentence:
The child pulled at his sleeve to get his attention.
He pulled at his ear as he spoke. The child pulled at his mother’s sleeve. She pulled at the rope.

english_meaning: To start moving, especially a vehicle. To increase a score or improve a rank. To draw oneself back or away.
example_sentence: They waved as the bus pulled away. There was a roar and a cloud of smoke as the car pulled away from the traffic lights. She pulled away just as he was about to kiss her. The Cowboys hit five shots in a row to pull away from Marquette.

english_meaning: To move backwards or away from someone. To decide not to do something that you were intending to do, because of possible problems. To make an army move back from a place. To improve a team’s position in a game. To retreat or withdraw.
example_sentence:
Their sponsors pulled back at the last minute. They pulled back a goal just before half-time. He leaned forward to kiss her but she pulled back.
Michelle pulled back from her mother and wiped the tears from her eyes. Businesses have already pulled back on corporate travel.

english_meaning: To make somebody less happy, healthy or successful. To destroy a building completely. To earn the large amount of money mentioned.
