example_sentence: I reckon she's pulling down over £200 000. A powerful storm pulled down the old fishing shack, which had been immortalized in countless paintings. An ugly billboard that was eventually pulled down. He's pulling down six figures at that job.

english_meaning: To enter a station and stop. To move to the side of the road or to the place mentioned and stop. To arrive at a destination or come to a stop. To earn money.
example_sentence: A company that cannot manage to pull in costs will not be in business for very long. The police car signalled to us to pull in. He was pulled in after a random traffic stop turned up drugs in his car.

english_meaning: To carry through (as a process) to completion. To leave the road in order to stop for a short time. To succeed in doing something difficult. To carry out despite difficulties. To accomplish successfully against odds.
example_sentence: The team pulled off an upset. The rebel forces pulled off a surprisingly successful offensive against the better equipped government troops. We pulled off the deal. I never thought you'd pull it off. The car pulled off and sped up the road. He pulled off a surprise victory. She pulled off the deal successfully.

english_meaning: To put on clothing quickly. To draw or tug something toward yourself. To encourage or motivate someone. To move a vehicle to the side and stop. To start moving with effort.
example_sentence: She pulled on her jacket before going outside. He pulled on the rope to lift the bucket. The coach pulled on the team to win the match. The driver pulled on to the side of the road.

english_meaning: To calm down and regain control of one’s emotions, to get composed after being upset.
example_sentence: She took a deep breath to pull herself together. After the accident, he pulled himself together and helped others. Pull yourself together before the interview. He needed a moment to pull himself together after the bad news.

english_meaning: To move away from the side of the road, etc. To leave a station. Something move away from something or stop being involved in it. To withdraw or remove from an activity or place.
example_sentence: A car suddenly pulled out in front of me. The project became so expensive that we had to pull out. They are pulling their troops out of the war zone. The troops pulled out of the city. He pulled out of the deal.

english_meaning: To use every possible effort, skill, or resource to achieve something. To do everything possible in order to succeed, impress someone, solve a problem, or achieve a goal. It refers to giving maximum effort without holding anything back.
synonyms: ["Do one's best","Go all out","Spare no effort","Give it everything","Leave no stone unturned","Try every possible way","Put in maximum effort"]
antonyms: ["Give up","Hold back","Do little","Neglect effort","Take it easy"]
example_sentence: The company pulled out all the stops to launch the new product successfully. She pulled out all the stops to prepare for her final exams. The wedding planners pulled out all the stops to make the event unforgettable. Our team pulled out all the stops and won the championship.

english_meaning: To move to the side of the road in order to stop or let something pass. To make a driver or vehicle move to the side of the road. To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop.
example_sentence: She saw the ambulance coming up behind her and pulled over. Just pull over here, and I'll get out and walk the rest of the way. The police asked him to pull over. She pulled over to answer the call.

english_meaning: To tease, joke, or make fun of someone in a friendly way, not to insult, but to playfully mislead them for amusement.
example_sentence: Don’t take it seriously, I was just pulling your leg. She said she met a movie star, but she was pulling our legs. I thought he really bought a new car, but he was pulling my leg. Whenever he says something unbelievable, I know he’s pulling my leg again.

english_meaning: To use personal influence or important connections to obtain an advantage. To arrange something through unofficial influence.
example_sentence: She pulled strings to get her brother an interview. The project was approved after someone pulled strings. He refused to pull strings and wanted a fair process. Knowing the director helped them pull strings.

english_meaning: To intentionally stop an activity, project, or operation, often because it is no longer useful, successful, or desired. The phrase comes from the literal act of unplugging an electrical device, causing it to stop working.
example_sentence: The company decided to pull the plug on the failing project. They pulled the plug on the TV series after two seasons. Investors pulled the plug when the startup showed losses. He pulled the plug on his plans to move abroad.

english_meaning: To recover from a difficult situation or illness. To get better after a serious illness, operation, etc. To succeed in doing something very difficult. To help somebody get better after a serious illness, operation, etc. To help somebody succeed in doing something very difficult.
example_sentence: The doctors think she will pull through. It's going to be tough but we'll pull through it together. I relied on my instincts to pull me through. We pulled through most of the victims of the bomb attack. She pulled through the surgery. They pulled through the crisis.

english_meaning: To improve your effort, performance, or behavior. To start doing something in a better, more serious, and more focused way. It is often used when someone is not performing well and needs to improve quickly in studies, work, sports, or life.
synonyms: ["Improve yourself","Shape up","Work harder","Buckle down","Step up your game"]
example_sentence: You are failing in math; you need to pull up your socks. If you want promotion, you must pull up your socks at work. The coach told the team to pull up their socks before the final match. She needs to pull up her socks if she wants better grades.

english_meaning: To calm down and regain control of one’s emotions, to get composed after being upset.
example_sentence: Stop crying and pull yourself together. After the argument, he needed time to pull himself together. She pulled herself together and faced the audience. You can do it—just pull yourself together.

english_meaning: A pulmologist is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases of the lungs and the respiratory system. This specialist is also commonly called a pulmonologist. "Pulmologist" is a less common variant, while pulmonologist is the standard and more widely used term.
synonyms: ["Pulmonologist","Chest physician","Respiratory physician","Lung specialist","Respiratory specialist","Pulmonary specialist","Chest specialist","Respiratory medicine doctor"]
example_sentence: The pulmologist diagnosed the patient with severe asthma after several tests. My family doctor referred me to a pulmologist because I had difficulty breathing. The pulmologist recommended pulmonary rehabilitation to improve lung function. After reviewing the chest scan, the pulmologist explained the treatment plan clearly.

english_meaning: The artery that carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. The only artery in the body that carries deoxygenated blood. The vessel that divides into branches for the right and left lung.
example_sentence: The pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs. It leaves the heart from the right ventricle. High pressure in the pulmonary artery strains the heart. The pulmonary artery splits into two main branches.

english_meaning: One of the veins that carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The only veins in the body that carry oxygenated blood. A vessel that completes the circulation between the lungs and the heart.
example_sentence: The pulmonary vein brings fresh blood back to the heart. Four pulmonary veins open into the left atrium. Unlike other veins, the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood. The scan showed a narrowing of one pulmonary vein.

english_meaning: A physician who specializes in diseases and disorders of the lungs, airways, and respiratory system, such as asthma, pneumonia, tuberculosis, COPD, lung cancer, sleep apnea, and other breathing problems.
synonyms: ["Chest physician","Lung specialist","Respiratory physician","Respiratory specialist","Pulmonary specialist","Pulmonary physician"]
example_sentence: The pulmonologist diagnosed the patient with severe asthma. My family doctor referred me to a pulmonologist because of my persistent cough. The pulmonologist reviewed my lung function test before starting treatment. People with chronic breathing problems often need regular visits to a pulmonologist.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine that deals with the lungs and respiratory system. Pulmonology is the medical specialty focused on diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases and disorders of the respiratory system, including the lungs, bronchi, trachea, and associated structures. Pulmonologists handle conditions such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pneumonia, tuberculosis, and lung cancer.
example_sentence: She consulted a pulmonologist for her persistent cough. Pulmonology focuses on conditions like asthma and bronchitis. Advances in pulmonology have improved treatment for lung cancer. He specialized in pulmonology to help patients with chronic respiratory diseases.

english_meaning: A soft, wet, shapeless mass of material. The soft fleshy part of a fruit or vegetable. Material from wood or rags used to make paper. To crush or beat something into a soft mass. Cheap or sensational writing.
example_sentence: The children love the pulp of the mango. Paper is made from wood pulp. She squeezed the fruit until it became pulp. The magazine publishes pulp fiction. The mixer reduced the vegetables to pulp.

english_meaning: The regular beating of the heart felt in arteries. A regular vibration or signal, like electrical pulses. Edible seeds of leguminous plants such as lentils, beans, and peas. A brief burst of energy or activity. To beat, throb, or move in a regular rhythmic way. To send out waves, signals, or energy in bursts.
example_sentence: The doctor checked my pulse to measure my heartbeat. The machine sends electrical pulses to the device. Lentils are a rich source of protein and belong to pulses. The city had a sudden pulse of activity during the festival. Her heart pulsed faster during the exam. Light pulsed through the dark tunnel.

english_meaning: The main energy, activity, or living force that keeps a person, place, or thing alive and active. It can also mean the rhythm, excitement, and movement of life.
example_sentence: Music is the pulse of life for many people around the world. The busy market showed the true pulse of life in the city. Nature gives us the pulse of life through fresh air and green trees. Hope and love are often called the pulse of life during difficult times.

english_meaning: Edible seeds of plants such as lentils, beans and peas. Regular beating of the heart. Short burst or wave of energy, light, or sound. To beat or throb rhythmically. Electrical signal burst. Vibration or rhythmic movement. Sudden increase of activity.
example_sentence: Pulses are an important source of protein. The doctor checked his pulses carefully. Bright pulses of light came from the machine. Music pulses through the crowded hall.

english_meaning: To hit someone or something repeatedly with force. To strike again and again, usually with fists or heavy blows. It can describe physical attacks, harsh weather effects, or strong criticism that overwhelms someone.
example_sentence: The boxer pummeled his opponent until the referee stopped the match. Heavy rain pummeled the coastal villages for hours. The politician was pummeled by criticism from the media. Waves pummeled the boat during the storm.

english_meaning: To continue pumping or working hard, especially with energy or persistence.
example_sentence: The firefighters pumped away to clear the water. He kept pumping away at the handle. The team pumped away until the job was done. The old machine was still pumping away after hours.

english_meaning: To send or push a liquid or substance back to its original source.
example_sentence: The system pumps back the excess water. The oil was pumped back to the refinery. They had to pump back the coolant. The machine pumps back unused fuel into the tank.

english_meaning: To put a large amount of energy, effort, or money into something, also to physically inject liquid or gas into something.
example_sentence: The company pumped millions into new research. He pumped all his savings into the project. They pumped fuel into the generator. She pumped energy into the campaign.

english_meaning: To produce, release, or expel something in large amounts, often continuously or forcefully. It can refer to liquid, air, energy, information, or work.
example_sentence: The workers pumped out the flooded basement. The factory pumps out hundreds of units daily. They had to pump out the oil from the tank. The radio station pumped out nonstop hits.

english_meaning: To transfer or move liquid, gas, or other substances from one place to another using a pump
example_sentence: The fuel was pumped over to the storage tank. They pumped over the water to another section. The system automatically pumps oil over when full. The engineer pumped over the solution for testing.

english_meaning: To force liquid, gas, or another substance to move through a pipe, system, or network using a pump or mechanical pressure. It can also be used metaphorically to describe sending something through a system quickly.
example_sentence: The heart pumps blood through the body. The new law was pumped through Parliament. Water is pumped through the irrigation system. The air conditioner pumps cool air through the vents.

english_meaning: To fill something (like a tire or ball) with air or gas. To increase something, make it stronger, more intense, or more exciting. It can also mean to make someone feel more enthusiastic or energetic.
example_sentence: He pumped up the football before the game. The coach pumped up the team before the final. Pump up the tires or we can’t drive. The music really pumped up the crowd.

english_meaning: To raise or increase something (like pressure, volume, or enthusiasm) to a higher level.
example_sentence: Pump up the pressure to 100 PSI. The speaker pumped up to full volume. She pumped up to maximum effort before the race. They pumped up to get the crowd’s energy high.

english_meaning: A large round orange vegetable with thick skin and firm sweet flesh. A gourd used in soups, curries, and pies. The trailing plant that produces this vegetable. A hollowed pumpkin used as a lantern during festivals.
example_sentence: She cooked a warm bowl of pumpkin soup. The pumpkin grew larger than expected. Pumpkin seeds are roasted and eaten as a snack. Children carved a face into the pumpkin.

english_meaning: Showing great attention to detail and correct behaviour. Very careful about rules, formalities, and small points of conduct. Extremely precise and conscientious in carrying out duties. Strict in observing etiquette and proper procedure.
example_sentence: He is punctilious about answering every email on the same day. The clerk was punctilious in checking each document. She kept punctilious records of every payment. Their host was punctilious about seating arrangements at dinner.

english_meaning: In a way that shows great attention to small details. Very carefully and correctly, especially about rules or manners. With strict regard for formality and accuracy. In a scrupulously precise manner.
example_sentence: He punctiliously followed every step of the procedure. The documents were punctiliously checked before signing. She punctiliously observed the customs of her hosts. The accounts were punctiliously maintained for years.

english_meaning: Great attention to small details and correct behaviour. The quality of being extremely careful about rules and formalities. Strictness in observing accuracy and etiquette. Scrupulous exactness.
example_sentence: His punctiliousness made him an excellent auditor. The punctiliousness of the host impressed every guest. She is known for her punctiliousness in official matters. Such punctiliousness slows the work but ensures accuracy.

english_meaning: Arriving or happening at the exact time arranged. Doing things at the correct or agreed time. Not late, and respectful of time. Reliable regarding timing.
example_sentence: She is always punctual for her morning classes. A punctual employee earns the trust of the management. The train was punctual despite the heavy rain. Please be punctual, as the meeting starts at nine sharp.

english_meaning: The habit of doing things at the exact arranged time. The quality of being on time. Strict observance of appointed hours. Reliability in keeping to a schedule.
example_sentence: Punctuality is one of the marks of a professional. The school stresses punctuality and discipline. His punctuality impressed the interview panel. Poor punctuality can damage a company's reputation.

english_meaning: At the exact time arranged, without delay. Promptly and on schedule. In a manner that respects agreed timing. Neither early nor late.
example_sentence: The ceremony began punctually at six in the evening. He arrives punctually every morning without fail. The flight departed punctually despite the crowd. She punctually submitted all her assignments.

english_meaning: To insert punctuation marks into a piece of writing. To interrupt something at intervals with a repeated action or sound. To emphasise or give rhythm to something by adding occasional elements. To break up a period of time with separate events.
example_sentence: Remember to punctuate your sentences correctly. Loud cheers punctuated the entire speech. She punctuated her lecture with useful examples. Short breaks punctuate the long working day.

english_meaning: Marked with punctuation such as commas and full stops. Interrupted at intervals by something, especially a repeated event or sound. Emphasised or given rhythm by occasional occurrences. Broken up by pauses or breaks at regular points.
example_sentence: The essay was carefully punctuated and easy to read. The silence was punctuated by distant thunder. His speech was punctuated with long pauses. The journey was punctuated by frequent stops for tea.

english_meaning: The marks used in writing to separate sentences and clarify meaning. The practice or system of using such marks. Something that interrupts or breaks up a continuous activity at intervals. The act of adding these marks to written text.
example_sentence: Correct punctuation makes writing much clearer. The teacher explained the rules of punctuation in simple terms. Poor punctuation can completely change the meaning of a sentence. His frequent jokes served as punctuation to a serious talk.

english_meaning: A small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To pierce or make such a hole. To cause something to lose force, effect, or confidence suddenly. A sudden deflation.
example_sentence: The car has a puncture in the rear tire. A nail punctured my bicycle tube. His remarks punctured her confidence. Doctors punctured the swelling to drain it. We had to stop the journey because of a puncture.

english_meaning: Having a sharply strong taste or smell that is often acidic or spicy. Describing a remark or piece of writing that is sharp, biting, or caustic in its criticism. Being physically stinging or irritating to the senses of touch or sight. Characterized by a power to evoke strong mental or emotional sensations through sharpness. Being intellectually stimulating because of its incisiveness or wit.
example_sentence: The pungent aroma of fried garlic filled the entire kitchen. His pungent criticism of the government's policy sparked a heated debate. The chemical leaked into the air, creating a pungent and irritating haze. She was known for her pungent wit and ability to silence opponents with a single sentence.

english_meaning: Small-time troublemaker; worthless person; rebellious youth. A young person who behaves in a rebellious or defiant way, often associated with a particular subculture of music, fashion, and attitude. A person considered worthless or insignificant. Slang for a young criminal or troublemaker.
example_sentence: The punk spray-painted the walls of the building. He acted like a punk when confronted. Punk rock music became popular in the 1970s. Don’t be fooled by that punk; he can be dangerous.

english_meaning: A small light basket or container for fruit or vegetables. A small box typically used for berries or cherry tomatoes.
example_sentence: She bought a punnet of strawberries at the market. The cherries were packed in small punnets. He emptied the punnet of raspberries into a bowl. A punnet of cherry tomatoes costs two pounds.

english_meaning: A person who makes puns frequently. Someone fond of wordplay and witty jokes based on double meanings.
example_sentence: My uncle is a terrible punster at family dinners. The punster made everyone groan with his jokes. As a punster, she loves playing with words. The comedian is famous as a clever punster.

english_meaning: A long flat-bottomed boat moved by pushing a pole. To travel in or propel such a boat. In football, to kick the ball after dropping it from the hands. To give up or avoid deciding, informally. A small bet, informal British.
example_sentence: We hired a punt for a trip along the river. He punted the ball far down the field. The committee punted the decision to next month. She had a small punt on the horse race.

english_meaning: A person who gambles or places bets, British informal. A customer or client, informal. A football player who punts the ball. Someone who travels by punt.
example_sentence: Punters flocked to bet on the final race. The new design should attract more punters. The punter kicked the ball sixty yards. Punters enjoyed a sunny afternoon on the river.

english_meaning: The round black opening in the centre of the iris that lets light enter the eye. The adjustable hole that becomes smaller in bright light and larger in dim light. A student or child who is being taught, especially at school. A person receiving instruction from a particular teacher or master.
example_sentence: The pupil widens automatically in a dark room. The doctor shone a light to check the patient's pupil. Every pupil in the class passed the examination. He was a pupil of a famous violin teacher.

english_meaning: An animal, especially a dog or horse, bred from parents of the same breed or variety; not mixed. Of unmixed ancestry. Descended from a long line of the same breed.
example_sentence: He owns a purebred Arabian horse. Purebred dogs often cost a lot of money. The farm specializes in purebred cattle. Judges examined the purebred puppies carefully. Their purebred stallion won several races.

english_meaning: A substance, medicine that causes your bowels to empty, Cathartic
example_sentence: I took some purgative medicine. In some febrile and plethoric cases it is difficult to obtain the full action of a purgative.

english_meaning: To remove something unwanted, harmful, or impure. To cleanse or purify. To remove political opponents or undesirable members. To expel bodily substances. To release emotions or stress. To cleanse or rid someone or something of unwanted elements. An act of removal or cleansing.
example_sentence: The company decided to purge outdated records from its database. She felt relieved after purging her anger on paper. The dictator purged the government of opposition members. Drinking plenty of water helps the body purge toxins naturally. The country went through a political purge. He underwent a detox purge to cleanse his system.

english_meaning: The space between the extended thumb and forefinger. A flourish at the end of a piece of writing. A summary or conclusion of a speech or discussion. A curl or twist made with a pen. An ornamental final stroke.
example_sentence: He held the small coin in the purlicue of his hand. The calligrapher ended each page with a delicate purlicue. She gave a brief purlicue of the long discussion. A neat purlicue decorated the bottom of the letter.

english_meaning: To steal something, especially in a sneaky or dishonest way. To take dishonestly without permission. A formal or literary word meaning to filch or pilfer.
example_sentence: He was accused of purloining company funds. The thief purloined jewels from the museum. She purloined a candy bar from the shop. Someone had purloined the secret documents. Employees who purloin will be fired immediately.

english_meaning: A person who steals something, typically in a sneaky or dishonest way. A thief or embezzler who takes someone else's property for their own use.
example_sentence: The police captured the notorious purloiner of rare antiques. The company discovered that an insider was the purloiner of sensitive documents. A sneaky purloiner took my wallet from my backpack while I was not looking. He was known as a master purloiner who left no trace behind.

english_meaning: Stealing something, often in a sly or secretive way. Taking something that belongs to someone else without permission. Committing theft, especially of small items.
example_sentence: The servant was caught purloining silver spoons from the kitchen. He was dismissed for purloining office supplies. The mischievous boy delighted in purloining apples from the orchard. Someone had been purloining documents from the archive.

english_meaning: To appear or claim to be something, often falsely. To profess or intend to convey a particular meaning. The main meaning or substance of something. The apparent or stated purpose of something.
example_sentence: The letter purports to be from the president. What is the purport of your visit? The book purports to reveal government secrets. I did not understand the purport of his speech. This document purports to prove his innocence.

english_meaning: The apparent or intended meaning, significance, or purpose of something like a document or speech. To appear or claim to be or do something, especially falsely or without absolute proof. The general sense or substance of an utterance or text.
example_sentence: The document purports to be a factual account of the events. We should examine the true purport of the senator's speech. This letter purports to come from the prime minister himself. The document purports that the company has made huge profits this year. He ignored the message, missing its dark and hidden purport.

english_meaning: The reason for which something exists or is done. A desired result or aim. A person’s sense of determination or resolve. To intend or design something for a particular use.
example_sentence: The purpose of this meeting is to solve the problem. She found a clear purpose in helping children. The tool was designed for a specific purpose. He purposefully set aside money for his education.

english_meaning: In a deliberate and intentional manner. In a way that shows clear purpose, determination, or meaning.
example_sentence: She walked purposefully toward the stage. The designer purposefully left space around the image. He spoke purposefully so that everyone understood the message. The team purposefully focused on the most urgent task.

english_meaning: Intentionally. Deliberately. With a specific aim or plan rather than by accident.
example_sentence: She purposely arrived early to get a good seat. He purposely left the door open for the dog. The editor purposely used simple language. I did not break the vase purposely.

english_meaning: The act of pursuing something. Effort to achieve or obtain something. The process of following a goal, person, or activity. Attempt to accomplish a purpose.
example_sentence: His pursual of knowledge made him successful. She continued her pursual of a better job. The pursual of happiness is important in life. Their pursual of excellence inspired others.

english_meaning: The act of following or carrying out something. Continuation of an action. In accordance with something. Following a rule or instruction. Doing something in accordance with a plan, rule, order, or intention. It means continuing or carrying out an action to achieve a goal.
example_sentence: The committee acted in pursuance of the new policy. He worked in pursuance of his dream to become a doctor. The police took action in pursuance of the court order. She continued her studies in pursuance of higher education.

english_meaning: To follow, try to achieve, continue doing something. To chase or go after. To work toward something desired. To carry on an activity. To explore or examine further.
example_sentence: She decided to pursue a career in medicine. The police pursued the thief through the streets. He wants to pursue higher education abroad. They continue to pursue their dreams despite difficulties.

english_meaning:
The act of chasing or following something/someone. 
An effort to achieve or attain something (goal, ambition). An activity or interest that one spends time doing.
example_sentence:
The police were in hot pursuit of the thief. 
She dedicated her life to the pursuit of knowledge. Happiness is not a destination, but a pursuit. In his free time, painting became his favorite pursuit.

english_meaning: The range of authority, responsibility, knowledge, or activity covered by a person or organization. The scope within which something operates or is considered. The matters that a law, document, or official position applies to.
example_sentence: Budget approval falls within the committee's purview. Medical advice is outside my professional purview. The new regulations broaden the agency's purview. Hiring decisions are under the purview of the human resources director. The court examined whether the dispute came within its purview.

english_meaning: To treat someone roughly or without respect. To bully or harass. To move things around roughly or without care.
example_sentence: He was pushed about by the bullies at school. The older boys used to push the younger ones about in the playground. Example:

english_meaning: To continue with determination despite difficulties. To make progress with an activity, plan, or work. To move forward with effort and persistence.
example_sentence: They pushed ahead with the project despite obstacles. The government decided to push ahead with the project. Despite challenges, she kept pushing ahead to fulfill her dream.

english_meaning: To treat someone badly by dominating, bossing, or bullying them. To order someone about in a rough or unfair way.
example_sentence: He was tired of being pushed around by his boss. The manager always pushes his junior staff around. She was tired of being pushed around by her elder brother.

english_meaning: To move something or someone to the side by pushing. To ignore, reject, or dismiss something/someone as unimportant.
example_sentence: She pushed aside her doubts and went ahead. He pushed aside the chair to make space. She pushed aside her fears and spoke confidently.

english_meaning: To resist or oppose something. To move something backward / delay something.
example_sentence: The meeting was pushed back to next week. The workers pushed back against unfair policies. He pushed back when they tried to blame him unfairly. Communities are pushing back against environmental destruction.

english_meaning: To press or force something downward. To reduce prices, levels or numbers. To suppress a feeling or thought.
example_sentence: Push down the lever to start the machine. A good harvest pushed down vegetable prices. He pushed down his anger and kept quiet. Competition has pushed down the cost of data.

english_meaning: To strongly try to achieve something. To demand, request, or insist on something with determination.
example_sentence: They are pushing for better wages. The students are pushing for better facilities in their college. She is pushing for a promotion at work. The organization is pushing for stronger climate change policies.

english_meaning: To continue moving ahead despite difficulties. To advance or make progress with determination. To promote or support an idea, plan, or project. To encourage or urge someone to continue.
example_sentence: She pushed forward with her career goals. Despite many obstacles, the team decided to push forward with the project. She was tired but continued to push forward towards her goals. The government is trying to push forward new reforms. The government is trying to push forward new reforms.

english_meaning:
To enter rudely or without waiting. To move something inside by applying force. 
To enter suddenly or without invitation. To occupy space by moving into a place already filled.
example_sentence: He pushed in front of everyone at the store. He pushed in the chair under the table. She pushed in the drawer after taking out the files. They pushed in through the crowd to see the match. A man suddenly pushed in without knocking on the door.

english_meaning: To continue moving forward or traveling, especially despite difficulties. To continue doing a task or activity with determination. To encourage someone to continue.
example_sentence: Despite the heavy rain, the hikers decided to push on to the summit. We must push on with the project if we want to meet the deadline. The commanding officer told his troops to push on. Seeing the finish line ahead helped her to push on through the pain.

english_meaning: To deliberately make someone angry or emotional. Saying or doing something that intentionally triggers an emotional response, such as anger, frustration, or annoyance, in someone. It is often used in informal contexts to describe teasing or provoking behavior.
example_sentence: He really knows how to push my buttons. Don’t push her buttons today. His sarcasm always pushes my buttons. She pushed his buttons until he lost his temper.

english_meaning: To force someone or something to leave a place or position. To produce or manufacture something in large quantities. To extend something outward from a main body or center. To cause someone to lose their job or position by exerting pressure.
example_sentence: The older employees felt they were being pushed out by the new management. The factory can push out thousands of units every single day. The bird pushed out its chest in a display of dominance. As the city expanded, local farmers were gradually pushed out of the area.

english_meaning: To apply force to someone or something so that they fall to the ground. To knock down a physical object or person by pushing. To overcome or easily defeat an opponent in a physical or metaphorical sense. To cause a structure or item to collapse by shoving it.
example_sentence: The strong wind managed to push over the old fence in our backyard. The bully tried to push the smaller kid over in the playground. Be careful not to push over that stack of books on the edge of the desk. The team was determined not to let their opponents push them over in the final game.

english_meaning: A political campaign technique in which an organization attempts to influence voters under the guise of conducting a legitimate opinion poll. A survey designed to manipulate the opinions of the people being interviewed rather than to measure them. A telemarketing tactic used to spread negative information about a political opponent.
synonyms: ["Smear campaign","Negative campaigning","Manipulative survey","Propaganda","Disinformation","Biased poll","Whispering campaign","Deceptive surveying","Phony poll"]
antonyms: ["Objective poll","Legitimate survey","Unbiased research","Scientific poll","Impartial study","Neutral questioning","True opinion poll"]
example_sentence: The candidate was accused of using a push poll to spread rumors about his rival. I received a phone call that sounded like a survey but was clearly a push poll designed to change my vote. Ethics committees often condemn the use of a push poll during tight elections. They disguised their smear campaign as a legitimate questionnaire, effectively creating a push poll.

english_meaning: The practice of using interactive marketing or polling techniques to manipulate voters' opinions under the disguise of a genuine survey. The act of conducting biased phone calls to spread damaging information about a rival candidate. The systematic dissemination of propaganda framed as public opinion research.
synonyms: ["Smear campaigning","Propaganda spreading","Disinformation campaign","Manipulative surveying","Deceptive polling","Biased questioning","Mudslinging","Negative campaigning"]
antonyms: ["Objective research","Fair polling","Unbiased surveying","Scientific sampling","Neutral investigation","Legitimate polling","Impartial surveying"]
example_sentence: Push polling has become a controversial tactic in modern political campaigns. The committee investigated the organization for engaging in aggressive push polling just days before the election. Many voters complained about push polling after receiving highly biased questions over the phone. Legislation has been proposed in several states to ban or restrict push polling.

english_meaning: To drive someone to a state of mental or emotional breakdown. To cause someone to finally lose control, go mad, or take extreme action. To force someone into an irrecoverable or disastrous situation.
example_sentence: The sudden loss of his job was enough to push him over the edge. Constant stress and lack of sleep can push anyone over the edge. She was already struggling, and the bad news finally pushed her over the edge. The detective realized that the suspect's financial ruin had pushed him over the edge into criminality.

english_meaning: To bring someone very close to a breaking point or state of extreme distress. To put intense pressure on someone until they are almost unable to cope. To drive someone to the absolute limit of their patience or endurance.
example_sentence: The intense training program pushed the recruits to the edge of their physical capabilities. His constant complaining is pushing me to the edge of my patience. The financial crisis pushed the small business to the edge of bankruptcy. Being isolated for months pushed her to the edge of despair.

english_meaning: A style of Internet communication where the request for a transaction is initiated by the central server. Systems that send information to a user without the user having to request it each time. A method of data delivery where information is broadcast to a client automatically. An automated delivery mechanism for updates and notifications.
example_sentence: Smartphones rely heavily on push technology to deliver instant email notifications. Most news apps use push technology to keep users updated on breaking events. The transition from pull to push technology changed how we consume digital media. Web developers implement push technology to synchronize data across multiple devices.

english_meaning: To go beyond accepted limits. To test or extend the boundaries of what is considered normal, safe, or acceptable, often to achieve innovation, improvement, or progress.
synonyms: ["Go beyond limits","Break new ground","Innovate boldly","Take risks"]
antonyms: ["Play it safe","Stay within limits","Follow tradition","Avoid risk"]
example_sentence: The scientist pushed the envelope by testing a completely new theory. This company always pushes the envelope in product design. Artists often push the envelope to challenge public taste. He pushed the envelope to improve his performance at work.

english_meaning: To force a plan, law or decision to be accepted despite opposition. To make one's way forcefully through a crowd or obstacle. To continue with difficulty until something is completed.
example_sentence: The government pushed the bill through parliament in a single day. He pushed through the crowd to reach the exit. She was exhausted but pushed through to finish the report. They pushed the reform through despite fierce criticism.

english_meaning: To force someone into a helpless or desperate position. To defeat or overpower a person completely. To leave someone with no room to escape or choose. To press a rival hard until he must give way.
example_sentence: Heavy debts pushed the small traders to the walls. The champion pushed his opponent to the walls in the last round. Rising prices have pushed poor families to the walls. Do not push an honest worker to the walls.

english_meaning: To move or force something upward. To cause prices, numbers or levels to increase. To exert upward pressure from below.
example_sentence: Please push up the window to let some air in. Fuel shortages pushed up transport costs. The plant pushed up through the cracked pavement. New demand pushed up prices across the market.

english_meaning: To start a vehicle by pushing it while the engine is in gear and the clutch is released. The act of starting a motor vehicle by utilizing its motion while being pushed manually. A method used when the electric starter motor or battery is failing. To give an initial impetus or assistance to a project or process to get it moving.
example_sentence: We had to push-start the car because the battery was completely dead. A quick push-start from the neighbors got us on our way to the mechanic. The government hopes the new subsidies will push-start the lagging economy. Can you help me push-start this old motorcycle in the driveway?

english_meaning: An exercise in which the body is raised and lowered with the arms while lying face down. Designed to give lift or support, as with certain garments.
example_sentence: He does fifty push-ups every morning before breakfast. The coach added push-ups to the warm-up routine. She could barely manage a single push-up at first. The store advertised a new push-up design in its swimwear range.

english_meaning: A person who is easily influenced, defeated, or persuaded to do what others want. Someone who cannot stand up for themselves or set boundaries. An opponent or sports team that is very easy to defeat. A task or challenge that requires very little effort to complete or win.
example_sentence: The new manager is no pushover and demands strict discipline from everyone. I thought the negotiation would be tough, but he turned out to be a complete pushover. The opposing team was a pushover, and we won the match effortlessly. Don't think of her as a pushover just because she is polite and kind.

english_meaning: A short pin with a large, thick head used to fasten papers to a noticeboard or wall. A small tack designed to be pressed into a surface with the thumb. A digital map marker shaped like a physical pin used to indicate a specific location.
example_sentence: She used a pushpin to attach the flyer to the bulletin board. He color-coded the map by placing a red pushpin on every city he had visited. The teacher handed out pushpins so the students could display their artwork. Click the pushpin icon on the screen to save your current location.

english_meaning: Excessively forceful or assertive in seeking what one wants. Insistent in an annoying or aggressive way. Overly ambitious and demanding of others.
example_sentence: The salesman was so pushy that we left the shop. I do not want to sound pushy, but the deadline is today. Her pushy parents enrolled her in five classes at once. Being pushy rarely wins people's trust.

english_meaning: Lacking courage or determination. Showing a weak and timid character. Easily frightened and unwilling to take risks. Cowardly in the face of difficulty or danger.
example_sentence: His pusillanimous response disappointed his supporters. It was a pusillanimous decision to avoid the debate. She refused to be pusillanimous in the face of threats. The committee was criticised for its pusillanimous attitude.

english_meaning: An informal or affectionate name for a cat. A playful term for a girl or young woman. In informal use, the face or mouth.
example_sentence: She called the cat with a soft "here, puss!". The old puss slept all afternoon on the windowsill. He told the sly puss to stop teasing her brother. Wipe that grin off your puss and get to work.

english_meaning: A clever cat in a classic European fairy tale who wins fortune and status for his poor master through trickery. Used figuratively for a cunning helper who advances someone's cause by wit.
example_sentence: The children acted out Puss in Boots for the school play. Puss in Boots outwits an ogre to help his master. She has read Puss in Boots to her son a dozen times. Their lawyer was a real Puss in Boots, clever and quick.

english_meaning: A small raised spot on the skin filled with pus. A pimple-like inflamed swelling. A skin lesion caused by infection, irritation, or inflammation. A small blister containing thick yellowish fluid.
example_sentence: A pustule appeared on his chin overnight. The nurse cleaned the pustule carefully. Some skin infections cause clusters of pustules. Do not squeeze a pustule without medical advice.

english_meaning: To interfere with, hinder, or disrupt a plan, activity, or process. To cause a setback that limits progress or success. To reduce the enjoyment, effectiveness, or smooth operation of something.
example_sentence: The sudden rainstorm put a crimp in our picnic plans. Rising costs put a crimp in the company's expansion strategy. His injury put a crimp in the team's championship hopes. The power outage put a crimp in the event schedule.

english_meaning: To restrict, limit, or hinder the extent or effectiveness of something. To impose a constraint on an activity, process, or plan. To slow or reduce the momentum, growth, or enjoyment of something.
example_sentence: The new regulations put a crimp on small-business growth. Budget cuts put a crimp on the department's research efforts. The strike put a crimp on the factory's production. Bad weather put a crimp on tourism this season.

english_meaning: To pause a discussion, idea, or task temporarily and return to it later. It means to set something aside for the moment without forgetting it.
example_sentence: Let’s put a pin in this topic until the manager joins the meeting. We’ll put a pin in the budget discussion and focus on the urgent issue first. They decided to put a pin in their travel plans until the weather improves. You made a good point; let’s put a pin in it and revisit it tomorrow.

word: Put all eggs in one basket
english_meaning: To risk everything on a single plan, resource, or opportunity. To depend completely on one thing, which is risky if it fails.
example_sentence: Investors never put all eggs in one basket. Don’t put all your eggs in one basket by investing only in one company. She put all her eggs in one basket when she chose to rely only on one friend. It’s safer to diversify your income instead of putting all eggs in one basket. By depending on one skill, he is putting all his eggs in one basket.

english_meaning: To be completely honest and open about one's intentions or feelings. It refers to revealing hidden plans to others without any deceit. This phrase implies making your true position known in a negotiation. It means to share all relevant information transparently.
example_sentence: I decided it was time to put my cards on the table and tell her how I really felt. If we want this partnership to work, both sides need to put cards on the table. He refused to put his cards on the table during the early stages of the negotiation. It is always better to put your cards on the table rather than keeping secrets from your team.

english_meaning: To place something inside or into something. To contribute effort, time, or work toward something. To officially submit or request something (for example. application, complaint).
example_sentence: She put in a lot of effort to complete the project on time. They decided to put in a new application for the job opening. The company will put in new machines to increase production. During the meeting, he put in a few useful suggestions.

word: Put money where one's mouth is
english_meaning: To back up words with action. To take action to support what one claims, promises, or believes in. To back up words with deeds, especially by spending time, effort, or money.
example_sentence: She put her money where her mouth is by donating. He always talks about helping the poor, but now it’s time to put his money where his mouth is and actually donate. The company claimed to support the environment, so they put their money where their mouth is by investing in green energy. If you believe this project can succeed, then put your money where your mouth is and fund it.

english_meaning: To postpone or delay something to a later time. To cause someone to lose interest or feel discouraged. To distract or disturb someone while doing something. To remove (clothes, expression, or habit).
example_sentence: The meeting was put off until Friday. We had to put off the meeting because of the rain. His rude behavior really put me off. Don’t put off your homework until the last minute. He put off his coat when he entered the house.

english_meaning: To admire someone so much that one believes they are perfect and cannot make mistakes. To elevate someone to a position of unrealistic superiority.
example_sentence: It is dangerous to put on a pedestal any leader because they are only human. He tends to put on a pedestal the celebrities he follows on social media. She realized her mistake when she put on a pedestal a mentor who eventually let her down. Society often tries to put on a pedestal athletes who achieve international fame.

english_meaning: To postpone, delay, or temporarily stop an action, plan, or project.
example_sentence: The company put the project on ice until they secure more funding. I decided to put our vacation plans on ice because of work commitments. He literally put the drinks on ice to keep them cold for the party. Due to bad weather, they put the construction on ice for a few weeks.

english_meaning: To ignore everything except what you want to see; to focus only on one thing while ignoring other information.
example_sentence: He put his blinkers on and ignored the company’s problems. Don’t put your blinkers on when facing the truth. The government seems to have put its blinkers on. She put her blinkers on and refused to listen.

english_meaning: To extinguish (a fire, light, or flame). To inconvenience or trouble someone. To publish or release (information, news, a product, etc). To produce or display something
example_sentence: She quickly put out the fire before it spread to the other rooms. He was put out by the rude comment made during the meeting. The sailors put out to sea early in the morning to catch the wind. The company will put out a new advertisement for their latest product.

english_meaning: To make somebody take their attention off what they are doing and stop doing it so well. To disturb, distract, or interrupt someone’s concentration or rhythm, especially when they are speaking, working, or performing. It can apply to both physical actions (walking, running) and mental focus (thinking, speaking).
example_sentence: The shouting from the back of the hall completely put me off my stride. The sudden noise put the speaker off his stride, and he forgot his next point. Her constant interruptions put me off my stride while I was presenting.

english_meaning: To force someone to answer a difficult question or make a quick decision immediately, often causing embarrassment or pressure. To place a person in a situation where they must respond, decide, or explain something right away, usually without preparation. It often makes the person feel uncomfortable, embarrassed, or under pressure.
synonyms: ["Pressure someone","Corner someone","Force an answer","Challenge suddenly","Make uncomfortable"]
example_sentence: The teacher put Ali on the spot by asking him to explain the answer in front of the class. My manager put me on the spot when she asked for the report during the meeting. Please do not put me on the spot by asking personal questions at dinner. His friends put him on the spot by asking when he was getting married.

word: Put the cat among the pigeons
english_meaning: To say or do something that causes trouble, shock, or disagreement among people. This idiom is used when someone introduces a statement, idea, or action that disturbs a calm situation and causes arguments, confusion, or strong reactions among a group of people.
synonyms: ["Stir up trouble","Cause controversy","Rock the boat","Create a commotion","Shake things up"]
antonyms: ["Calm things down","Keep the peace","Maintain harmony","Avoid conflict","Settle matters"]
example_sentence: His comment about changing the rules really put the cat among the pigeons at the meeting. The new policy announcement put the cat among the pigeons in the office. She put the cat among the pigeons by revealing the secret. The politician’s statement put the cat among the pigeons across the country.

english_meaning: To build or erect something. To display or attach something. To provide accommodation or stay temporarily. To tolerate or endure something
example_sentence: They put up a tent near the river. We put up new curtains in the room. My friend put me up when I visited Karachi. She won’t put up with lies anymore. She put up a notice on the wall. They put up a new school in the village. They put me up for the night. I can’t put up with his rude behavior.

english_meaning: Act or stop talking. To tell someone to either take action or stop making claims or complaints if they are not willing to follow through
example_sentence: You keep saying you can beat me in chess, now put up or shut up. If you think you can handle this project, put up or shut up. Stop complaining about the rules and put up or shut up. He always brags about his skills, it’s time to put up or shut up

english_meaning: To act firmly and refuse to allow something. To show strong authority or determination by clearly saying no, setting limits, or enforcing rules, especially when others resist or behave wrongly.
synonyms: ["Be firm","Take a stand","Put a stop to","Enforce"]
example_sentence: The manager put his foot down and stopped all late submissions. Parents must put their foot down when children break rules. She finally put her foot down and refused to work overtime. The government put its foot down against illegal construction.

word: Put your head in the lion's mouth
english_meaning: To place oneself in a very dangerous or risky situation intentionally. To face great peril knowingly. To trust someone or something unreliable. To take a bold and reckless action. To expose oneself to certain trouble.
synonyms: ["Risk everything","Court danger","Play with fire","Walk into trouble"]
example_sentence: By trusting that man, you are putting your head in the lion's mouth. Investing without research is like putting your head in the lion's mouth. Speaking against the mob was putting his head in the lion's mouth. Do not put your head in the lion's mouth for such a small gain.

english_meaning: Generally considered or believed to be something, though not proven. Supposed or assumed to exist or be true. Commonly accepted or reputed, sometimes wrongly.
example_sentence: The putative author of the manuscript was never confirmed. The police questioned the putative leader of the gang. The putative benefits of the new drug are still under study. He is the putative heir to the family fortune.

english_meaning: To place something in its proper place after use. To save or store something for future use. To eat or drink a large amount. To send someone to prison or a mental institution.
example_sentence: Put away the dishes after dinner. Please put away your toys after playing. He put away some money for his daughter’s wedding. The little boy put away three burgers in one sitting!. The police finally put away the criminal for ten years.

english_meaning: To save something (especially money or time) for future use. To set aside temporarily or keep something for later. To avoid using something now.
example_sentence: She puts by a little money every month for emergencies. We should put by some food in case of bad weather He put by his studies for a while to help his family business. Try to put by some time this weekend for relaxation.

english_meaning: To place something on a surface gently. To criticize or humiliate someone, especially in front of others. To suppress or stop something (like a rebellion or protest). To kill an animal that is old or suffering (euthanize).
example_sentence: He was put down by his classmates. He put down the book on the table. She always puts me down when we’re in meetings. The army quickly put down the rebellion. They had to put down their sick dog.

english_meaning: To wear or dress in something. To switch on or start something. To gain weight. To organize or perform a show, event, or act. To pretend or show fake behavior or emotion.
example_sentence: She put on her coat before going outside. He put on the fan because it was too hot. He has put on a lot of weight since last year. The students put on a play for the school function. Don’t put on that sad face I know you’re joking.

english_meaning: To connect someone by telephone. To cause someone to experience something difficult. To make something happen or complete a process. To help someone complete a course or training.
example_sentence: Can you put me through to the manager? Please hold the line, I’ll put you through to the manager. She was put through a lot of pain after the accident. The company put the plan through after careful review. His parents put him through college with great effort.

english_meaning: To tolerate, accept, or endure someone or something unpleasant or annoying without complaining. To accept a difficult situation or someone’s behavior even though you don’t like it.
example_sentence: I can’t put up with the noise. I can’t put up with his rude behavior anymore. She has to put up with a lot of noise in her neighborhood. We put up with many challenges during the project. He puts up with his boss’s criticism patiently.

english_meaning: A problem, question, or game that is difficult to understand or solve and requires thinking, logic, or skill. To confuse someone or to make someone think hard in order to understand something. It can also mean something confusing that is hard to explain or understand.
example_sentence: This crossword puzzle is very difficult to solve. The missing keys were a complete puzzle to everyone. She tried to puzzle out the meaning of the message. The detective was puzzled by the strange clue.

english_meaning: Confusing or difficult to understand or explain. Causing confusion or bewilderment. Perplexing or mysterious. Creating doubt or uncertainty about something.
example_sentence: His sudden departure was puzzling to everyone. The test results were puzzling to the doctors. It's puzzling why she refused the offer. The ancient symbols remain puzzling to researchers.

english_meaning: A tall tower-like structure used for carrying overhead power cables. A large vertical structure or post used as a boundary marker or for guiding aviators. A monumental gateway to an ancient Egyptian temple, consisting of a pair of truncated pyramids. A plastic cone used to mark out areas or direct traffic on roads.
example_sentence: The high-voltage power lines were suspended from a massive steel pylon. Pilots used the illuminated pylon as a navigational waypoint during the night flight. Road crews placed orange pylons along the highway to mark the construction zone. The entrance to the temple was flanked by two majestic stone pylons carved with hieroglyphics.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with a polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at a point. An ancient Egyptian stone structure with a square base. A hierarchical structure or system. To increase or build up gradually.
example_sentence: The pyramids of Egypt are ancient wonders. A pyramid has triangular faces. The company has a pyramid organizational structure. He pyramided his investments over time.

english_meaning: A heap of combustible material, especially wood, for burning a corpse as part of a funeral ceremony. A large pile of wood on which a body is placed to be cremated outdoors. Any large heap of flammable materials used for burning something ceremoniously.
example_sentence: The family gathered around the funeral pyre to pay their final respects. The ancient king was honored with a massive pyre adorned with gold. Smoke rose slowly from the pyre into the evening sky. They spent hours collecting dry wood to build the ceremonial pyre. The tradition of the funeral pyre has been practiced for thousands of years in various cultures.

english_meaning: A win that costs so much that it feels like a loss. situation where someone technically wins but pays such a heavy price that the victory loses its value. The effort, damage or sacrifices outweigh the benefit of winning.
example_sentence: The battle was a Pyrrhic victory. They won, but it was a Pyrrhic victory. The lawsuit was a Pyrrhic victory for him. It felt like a Pyrrhic victory after so much loss. The term Pyrrhic victory comes from King Pyrrhus of Epirus, who defeated the Romans but with devastating losses to his own army.

english_meaning: A very large non-venomous snake that kills its prey by coiling around it and squeezing. A widely used high-level computer programming language known for its simple, readable syntax. In Greek mythology, a huge serpent killed by the god Apollo at Delphi.
example_sentence: A python can swallow prey much larger than its own head. She wrote the data analysis script in Python. Pythons are commonly found in tropical forests. Many beginners learn Python as their first programming language.

english_meaning: In the capacity or character of. Considered as or in the role of. Used to show the particular aspect in which something is being discussed. As being, when regarded purely as something.
synonyms: ["As","In the role of","In the capacity of","By way of","Considered as","In the character of"]
antonyms: ["Unlike","Apart from","Regardless of","Other than","Independently of","In no capacity"]
example_sentence: The judge spoke qua citizen, not qua official. Money qua money has no value until it is used. We must study the text qua literature, not qua history. A teacher qua teacher must remain impartial in class.

english_meaning: A person who dishonestly claims to have medical or other skills they do not possess. A fake doctor or fraudulent practitioner. The characteristic harsh sound made by a duck. To make such a sound.
example_sentence: Beware of quacks who promise miracle cures. The patient died after being treated by a quack. The ducks quacked loudly near the pond. He turned out to be a quack with no real qualifications. Newspapers warned the public against quack remedies.

english_meaning: The large group of four muscles at the front of the thigh. The muscles that straighten the knee and help in walking, running, and jumping. The muscle group that stabilises the knee joint and supports the kneecap. The strongest and one of the bulkiest muscle groups in the human body.
example_sentence: Cycling is an excellent workout for the quadriceps. The quadriceps straighten the knee when you kick a ball. He tore his quadriceps during the final sprint. Strong quadriceps help protect the knee from injury.

english_meaning: A flat shape with four straight sides and four angles. A polygon having exactly four edges and four vertices. Involving or formed by four parties or sides. A general category that includes squares, rectangles, rhombuses, and trapeziums.
example_sentence: The sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is 360 degrees. A square is a special type of quadrilateral. They signed a quadrilateral security agreement. Identify each quadrilateral in the diagram.

english_meaning: An animal that walks on four legs. A four-footed creature such as a horse or dog. Relating to movement on four limbs.
example_sentence: The horse is a strong and graceful quadruped. Most farm animals are quadrupeds. Scientists studied how the quadruped balances while running. A cat is a quadruped with excellent agility.

english_meaning: Four times as many or as much. Consisting of four parts, members, or elements. A group or amount of four. To make or become four times as great or numerous.
example_sentence: The laboratory repeated the test in quadruple to improve reliability. Demand for the service quadrupled within two years. They ordered a quadruple portion for the large group. The machine can quadruple its output during peak season.

english_meaning: One of four children or young born at the same birth. Any set or group of four corresponding people or things. A sequence of four notes or beats played in the time normally given to a different number in music.
synonyms: ["One of Four","Set of Four","Foursome","Quartet","Group of Four"]
example_sentence: Each quadruplet wore a different colored cap. The hospital announced the safe birth of four healthy quadruplets. The composer placed a rapid quadruplet at the end of the phrase. The four sculptures form a striking quadruplet in the central gallery.

english_meaning: To drink a beverage, especially an alcoholic one, heartily, eagerly, or in large quantities. To swallow a drink with great enjoyment or in long, deep gulps. A drink, especially one taken in large amounts or with relish.
example_sentence: After the long hike, he quaffed a glass of cold water in one go. The guests quaffed wine throughout the evening celebration. The thirsty traveler quaffed the fresh juice gratefully. They sat by the fire and quaffed their ale. He took a long, satisfying quaff from the cup.

english_meaning: A difficult, confusing, or dangerous situation. Also a soft muddy area that is hard to move through. A soft, wet, muddy piece of land where a person, animal, or vehicle can sink or get stuck. it is used figuratively for a complicated, troublesome, and hard to escape situation, such as a political, financial, legal, or personal
example_sentence: At the end of the game, the pitch was a real quagmire. Since the coup, the country has sunk deeper into a quagmire of violence and lawlessness. When I tried to get my tax situation straightened out with the government, I ran into a bureaucratic quagmire. The heavy rain soon turned the field into a quagmire.

english_meaning: Attractively unusual or old-fashioned. Pleasingly strange or curious in appearance or character. Having an old-world charm. Unfamiliar or different in a way that is interesting or appealing. Odd or peculiar in a pleasant manner.
example_sentence: They lived in a quaint little cottage by the river. The town has many quaint old shops and narrow streets. She wore a quaint hat that everyone admired. The village has retained its quaint charm despite modernization. He has some quaint ideas about marriage and family.

english_meaning: Describing something that is shaking, trembling, or vibrating rhythmically. It refers to a person or thing that is unsteady or prone to tremors, often due to fear, nervousness, or structural instability. It can also describe a sound or voice that is wavering and uncertain.
example_sentence: His quaky voice betrayed how nervous he felt during the public speech. The old wooden bridge felt quaky under the weight of the heavy truck. She took a deep breath to steady her quaky hands before the surgery. The ground felt quaky for a few seconds following the initial earthquake tremor.

english_meaning: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quality of something rather than its quantity. Descriptive of the essential nature or characteristics of a person, thing, or process. Concerned with distinctions based on properties or attributes rather than numeric data. Used in research to describe non-numerical observations such as interview transcripts or observations. Pertaining to the distinctive features that define excellence or character.
example_sentence: The researchers conducted qualitative interviews to understand the patients' experiences. There is a qualitative difference between knowing a language and being able to teach it. Her study focused on qualitative data like personal journals and video recordings. The company is seeking a qualitative improvement in its customer service department.

english_meaning: In a manner relating to the quality or standard of something rather than its quantity. With regard to characteristics, properties, or features. Distinguishable by kind or essence rather than by amount or numerical value. In a way that assesses the nature or excellence of an object. Pertaining to the subjective experience or descriptive attributes of a subject.
example_sentence: The two products differ qualitatively even if they look similar. The research team analyzed the feedback qualitatively to identify recurring themes. Life in the city has changed qualitatively over the last decade. We need to assess the student's performance qualitatively rather than just looking at grades.

english_meaning: A distinctive attribute or characteristic possessed by someone or something. The degree of excellence of something when compared to other things. High social standing or excellence of character. A general or specific property or trait. The standard of something as measured against other things of a similar kind.
example_sentence: The high quality of the fabric makes the dress very expensive. Kindness is a quality that everyone should strive to possess. They focused on improving the quality of life for the elderly. We must maintain a strict standard of quality control in the factory.

english_meaning: A feeling of uneasiness about a point especially of conscience or propriety. A sudden feeling of usually disturbing emotion (such as doubt or fear). A feeling of doubt or worry about whether what you are doing is right.
example_sentence: He had been working very hard so he had no qualms about taking a few days off. They broke the law without a qualm. She had no qualms about lying to the police.

english_meaning: Feelings of doubt, hesitation, or uneasiness about whether something is right or proper. A sense of guilt, worry, or moral objection. A sudden feeling of nausea or sickness. Slight pangs of conscience or apprehension before doing something.
example_sentence: He had no qualms about telling a lie to save himself. She felt some qualms before signing the contract. The soldier had qualms of conscience after the incident. He accepted the money without any qualms. I have qualms about leaving the children alone at home.

english_meaning: The state of not being able to decide what to do in a difficult situation. A situation in which one has to choose between two or more equally unsatisfactory choices.
example_sentence: This placed the government in something of a quandary. I'm in a quandary about whether I should try to repair my stereo or buy a new one, even though I don't have the money to do either.

english_meaning: To measure or express the amount of something. To determine, measure, or express the quantity or extent of something, often in numerical terms. It involves giving a concrete measure to something abstract or general.
example_sentence: It is difficult to quantify the benefits of meditation. The report tries to quantify the economic impact of climate change. Scientists are attempting to quantify the amount of carbon absorbed by forests. He could not quantify the exact number of people who attended the seminar.

english_meaning: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality. Expressible as a number or amount. Based on the amount or number of something. Denoting or relating to the length of a vowel or syllable. Capable of being measured or estimated by quantity.
example_sentence: The researchers collected quantitative data to determine the exact population growth. A quantitative analysis of the chemical compound revealed high levels of nitrogen. She preferred quantitative research methods because they provide objective statistical results. The difference between the two products is purely quantitative rather than qualitative.

english_meaning: In a manner relating to the measurement of quantity. Through the use of numbers or statistical data. Regarding the amount or size of something rather than its quality. By means of mathematical or scientific calculation. In terms of numerical value or magnitude.
example_sentence: The results were analyzed quantitatively to ensure accuracy. We need to measure the chemical changes quantitatively in the lab. The report assesses the impact of the policy quantitatively and qualitatively. Statistics allow us to look at social trends quantitatively over time.

english_meaning: A certain amount or number of something that can be measured or counted. A large or considerable amount of something. The property of things that can be measured in terms of bulk, size, weight, or number. A character or nature of an object which is measurable. In mathematics, a value, variable, or expression that can be evaluated.
example_sentence: The factory produces a large quantity of steel every day. It is often better to focus on quality rather than quantity. They ordered a small quantity of office supplies to test the quality. The police seized a vast quantity of illegal drugs during the raid.

english_meaning: A discrete quantity of energy proportional in magnitude to the frequency of the radiation it represents. The smallest amount of many forms of energy, such as light. A required or allowed amount, especially an amount of money or work. Relating to or based on the principles of quantum mechanics.
example_sentence: The theory explains how a quantum of energy is released when an electron moves to a lower orbit. Scientists are studying the behavior of light at the quantum level. Each member was assigned a specific quantum of the total workload. The discovery represented a quantum leap in the field of modern physics.

english_meaning: A fundamental theory in physics that provides a description of the physical properties of nature at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles. It explains the behavior of matter and its interactions with energy on the scale of atomic and subatomic particles, essentially stating that energy is not continuous but comes in discrete units or packets.
synonyms: ["Quantum mechanics","Wave mechanics","Atomic physics","Particle physics","Subatomic theory","Theoretical physics","Mathematical physics","Modern physics"]
example_sentence: Scientists use quantum theory to understand how electrons move within an atom. The development of the transistor was heavily dependent on the principles of quantum theory. In quantum theory, light can be described as both a particle and a wave. The uncertainty principle is one of the most famous aspects of modern quantum theory.

english_meaning: To keep (a person or animal) away from others to prevent a disease from spreading. Enforced isolation of patients suffering from a contagious disease in order to prevent the spread of disease.
example_sentence: The doctor said I could go home as long as I agreed to stay in quarantine for at least seven days. The government announced mandatory quarantines for high-risk travellers returning from countries with Ebola outbreaks. The hospital quarantined the infected patients.

english_meaning: A fundamental constituent of matter and is an elementary particle. It is a subatomic particle that carries a fractional electric charge and is postulated as a building block of hadrons such as protons and neutrons. In a different context, it refers to a type of low-fat soft cheese made from skimmed milk, popular in Central European cuisine.
example_sentence: Physicists study the properties of a quark to understand the fundamental forces of nature. Protons are composed of three quarks held together by gluons. The recipe for this German cheesecake calls for a specific amount of quark. Scientists have identified six different flavors of a quark including up, down, charm, strange, top, and bottom.

english_meaning: A heated argument or disagreement, typically between people who are usually on good terms. To engage in a verbal conflict or a minor fight over a difference of opinion. A state of formal complaint or an objection against someone or something.
example_sentence: The two neighbors had a long-standing quarrel over the property boundary. It is a pity to see siblings quarrel over such trivial matters. They managed to settle their quarrel without involving the police. She felt no desire to quarrel with his assessment of the situation. After a brief quarrel, they both apologized and shook hands.

english_meaning: To extract stone or minerals from the earth, usually for building or industrial use. A place where stone or minerals are dug out. Also the person or animal being hunted.
example_sentence: The workers extract marble from the quarry every day. The abandoned quarry filled with rainwater over time. The detective followed his quarry through the crowded streets. The company plans to quarry limestone for the new project.

english_meaning: A unit of liquid measurement equal to a quarter of a gallon or two pints. A container that holds this amount of liquid. A quantity of liquid equal to about 1.14 litres in the UK or 0.95 litres in the US.
example_sentence: Please buy a quart of milk on your way home. The jug holds exactly one quart. A quart is smaller than a gallon but larger than a pint. He drank almost a quart of juice after the match.

english_meaning: One of four equal parts into which something can be divided. A period of three months, especially as a division of a financial year. A coin worth 25 cents in US currency. A district or section of a town or city.
example_sentence: She cut the apple into quarters. The company's profits increased in the last quarter. I need a quarter to use the parking meter. They live in the historic quarter of the city.

english_meaning: One-fourth of a circle, formed by two perpendicular radii and the arc between them. A 90-degree sector of a circle. A curved shape that represents 25% of a complete circle.
example_sentence: The corner design featured a quarter circle. A quarter circle has a 90-degree arc. The table's edge was rounded into a quarter circle. Pizza slices often approximate a quarter circle shape.

english_meaning: Plural of quart; units of liquid measurement equal to two pints. Containers holding one quart of liquid each. Several measured quantities of a liquid such as milk or oil.
example_sentence: She bought two quarts of milk from the corner shop. The recipe requires three quarts of water. He poured several quarts of oil into the tank. Two quarts are roughly equal to two litres.

english_meaning: A hard, crystalline mineral made of silicon dioxide, found in many rocks. A mineral widely used in watches, clocks, and electronic devices. A transparent or coloured crystal used in jewellery and industry.
example_sentence: The hillside is rich in quartz and other minerals. He wears a quartz watch that keeps perfect time. A large piece of pink quartz sat on her desk. Quartz crystals are widely used in electronic devices.
