english_meaning: To officially reject, cancel, or annul a decision, verdict, or law by legal authority. To put an end to something forcefully, especially a rebellion, rumour, or protest. To suppress or crush completely. To reject a proposal or suggestion firmly. To stop something from spreading or continuing.
example_sentence: The high court decided to quash the lower court's verdict. The government used the army to quash the rebellion. He issued a statement to quash the rumours about his resignation. The committee voted to quash the new proposal. Police acted quickly to quash the violent protest.

english_meaning: Seemingly; apparently but not really. Resembling something but not truly being it. Used to show a partial or almost complete likeness. Having some, but not all, features of the thing named.
example_sentence: It is a quasi-official body with limited powers. The film has a quasi-documentary style. He offered a quasi-apology that satisfied nobody. The group enjoys quasi-legal status in the region.

english_meaning: The four-hundredth anniversary of an event. A celebration held to mark four hundred years since something happened. Relating to a period or anniversary of four hundred years.
example_sentence: The town marked the quatercentenary of its charter. A festival was held for Shakespeare's quatercentenary. They published a quatercentenary edition of the play. Quatercentenary events continued all year.

english_meaning: A stanza of four lines in a poem. A four-line verse, usually with a fixed rhyme scheme. A poem consisting of four lines.
example_sentence: The poem is made up of five quatrains. Each quatrain rhymes in an alternating pattern. He wrote a short quatrain in her notebook. The final quatrain sums up the poet's argument.

english_meaning: To shake or tremble, especially when speaking or singing. To speak in a trembling, unsteady voice because of fear or emotion. A shaking or trembling sound in the voice. In British music notation, an eighth note.
example_sentence: Her voice quavered as she read the letter. He answered with a quaver in his voice. The old man's hands quavered as he lifted the cup. The tune ends on a long quaver.

english_meaning: Shaking or trembling, especially of the voice. Sounding unsteady and weak because of age, fear, or emotion. Not firm or steady in movement or tone.
example_sentence: She answered in a quavery voice. His quavery singing moved the whole audience. The old letter was written in a quavery hand. A quavery note of fear crept into her reply.

english_meaning: A stone or metal platform beside water where boats and ships are loaded and unloaded. A landing place built parallel to the waterway for handling passengers and cargo.
example_sentence: The ship was tied up at the quay. Fishermen were unloading their catch on the quay. Tourists strolled along the busy quay. Cargo was stacked neatly on the quay. The old quay has been renovated for public use.

english_meaning: The area of land beside a quay where ships are loaded and unloaded. The edge of a harbour wall next to the water. Relating to or situated on this part of a port.
example_sentence: Crowds gathered on the quayside to greet the sailors. Fresh fish is sold every morning at the quayside. The quayside cafe offers a fine view of the harbour. Cranes lined the busy quayside.

english_meaning: In a way that shows or causes a feeling of sickness in the stomach. In a manner marked by nausea or the urge to vomit. In an uneasy, uncomfortable, or slightly nervous way.
example_sentence: He looked queasily at the rocking boat. She smiled queasily and refused the food. The passengers sat queasily through the bumpy flight. He glanced queasily at the blood on the floor.

english_meaning: A feeling of sickness in the stomach with an urge to vomit. Mild nausea caused by illness, travel, or anxiety. A sense of unease, discomfort, or doubt about something.
example_sentence: The medicine helped relieve her queasiness. He felt a sudden queasiness as the ship rolled. There is growing queasiness about the new policy. A wave of queasiness passed over him.

english_meaning: Feeling slightly sick in the stomach or uneasy. Feeling nausea or discomfort in the stomach, as if you might vomit. Emotionally uneasy or uncomfortable about something. Slightly worried, anxious, or disturbed by a situation.
example_sentence: I felt queasy after eating too much street food. The smell of the medicine made her queasy. He felt queasy before going on stage. Watching that scene made me feel queasy.

english_meaning: Strange, odd, or unusual in nature, appearance, or behaviour. Different from what is normal or expected. Slightly unwell or uncomfortable. In modern usage, also used as a term related to sexual orientation or gender identity. To spoil or interfere with something.
example_sentence: There was something queer about his behaviour that evening. She felt a little queer after the long journey. He gave me a queer look when I mentioned the name. His careless remark queered the whole deal. The old house had a queer smell about it.

english_meaning: To put an end to something, typically by the use of force. To suppress or crush a rebellion or disorder. To subdue or silence someone or something. To suppress a feeling, such as fear or anger, or to calm someone down.
example_sentence: The government sent in troops to quell the violent uprising. Extra police were called to quell the disturbance outside the stadium. She took a deep breath to quell her rising nerves before the speech. The company issued a statement to quell the rumors about its bankruptcy. His firm tone was enough to quell their complaints.

english_meaning: To satisfy thirst by drinking. To put out or extinguish a fire or flame. To suppress, stop, or cool down a strong feeling, desire, or activity. To cool hot metal suddenly by plunging it into water or oil.
example_sentence: A glass of cold water quenched his thirst quickly. The firefighters managed to quench the flames before they spread. Nothing could quench her desire for knowledge. The blacksmith quenched the red-hot iron in water. He drank tea to quench his thirst after the long walk.

english_meaning: To search for something seriously or eagerly. A long and difficult search for something important, valuable, or meaningful. A serious journey, mission, or effort to achieve a goal, discover something, gain knowledge, or find truth. It can be a physical journey or a personal struggle for success, happiness, wisdom, or improvement.
example_sentence: The scientist began a quest for a cure to the disease. His quest for knowledge made him read many books. The team went on a quest to find clean water in the village. She spent years in a quest for success and happiness.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,000 ronnabytes. The largest officially recognised unit of digital storage. A metric unit created in 2022 for measuring immense quantities of data.
example_sentence: The quettabyte is the biggest data unit in official use. One quettabyte equals 1,000 ronnabytes. No system today can store a quettabyte of data. The prefix quetta was approved in 2022.

english_meaning: To form a line or wait in order for something. To stand in line. To arrange tasks or events. To get ready for sequence. To line up things.
example_sentence: People queued up for tickets. Students queued up for lunch. They queued up outside the store before opening. Fans queued up to see the celebrity.

english_meaning: A slight objection or criticism about a trivial matter. To argue or raise objections about an irrelevant or minor point. To evade the truth of an issue by raising petty objections. A play on words or a pun.
example_sentence: Lawyers are known to quibble over the specific wording of a contract to find loopholes. Let's not quibble about the cost since the overall project is already a success. Her only quibble with the food was that it was served slightly cold. They spent the entire meeting quibbling over minor details instead of focusing on the main goal. It is frustrating when politicians quibble over semantics rather than addressing the actual crisis.

english_meaning: Able to think and respond rapidly and cleverly. Showing a sharp and intelligent mind that reacts quickly to situations. Mentally alert and clever in speech or action. Having the ability to understand and answer promptly with wit. Sharp, smart, and fast in comprehension or reply.
example_sentence: The quick-witted student answered every question with confidence. His quick-witted reply made everyone laugh. A quick-witted lawyer easily handles tricky questions in court. She is famous for being quick-witted and humorous.

english_meaning: Something done or made quickly. A short, hurried activity. A quick drink, meeting, question, or task that takes very little time. Informally, a brief act of sexual intercourse. Used in casual speech to describe anything that is brief, fast, and informal in nature.
example_sentence: Let's have a quickie coffee before the meeting starts. Can I ask you a quickie before you go? They got married in a quickie ceremony at the courthouse. I just need a quickie answer; it's not a long discussion. The journalist wrote a quickie article to meet the deadline.

english_meaning: A small lump of tobacco kept in the mouth for chewing. Used in phrases like quid pro quo meaning something exchanged for something else. Informal term used for one pound in the United Kingdom. A fixed amount of money. Compensation or payment. Informal slang for cash
example_sentence: He lent me ten quid for lunch. That book costs twenty quid. I found a quid on the floor. Can you spare a quid? She bought a sandwich for two quid. He offered me a quid of tobacco. Can I give you a quid for your help?

english_meaning: Something given in exchange for something else; a mutual exchange. A Latin phrase meaning “this for that,” used to describe a situation where one thing is given or done in return for something of equal value. Often used in legal, business, and political contexts to describe a fair trade or reciprocal arrangement.
example_sentence: The manager offered a promotion as a quid pro quo for extra work. They agreed to share resources as a quid pro quo arrangement. In politics, quid pro quo deals often spark controversy. He gave his advice as a quid pro quo for her support.

english_meaning: The inherent nature or essence of someone or something. That which makes a thing what it is. A small or trivial distinction. A minute point in an argument or a trifling nicety.
example_sentence: The artist spent years trying to capture the quiddity of the desert landscape. He was less interested in the quiddity of the legal argument than in its practical consequences. Philosophical inquiry often begins with a search for the quiddity of human existence. The professor was known for focusing on the quiddity of ancient texts rather than their broader themes.

english_meaning: Quiet, inactive, still, or at rest. A person, thing, condition, or activity that is temporarily inactive, calm, silent, or not developing. It is often used for something that has stopped moving, growing, reacting, or operating for a period of time. It can describe volcanoes, diseases, emotions, social movements, animals, or situations that are presently inactive but may become active again.
example_sentence: The volcano has remained quiescent for over a century. After treatment, the disease became quiescent for several months. The town looked quiescent in the early morning hours. His anger was quiescent, but everyone knew it could return.

english_meaning: Making little or no noise. Free from disturbance or activity. Peaceful or calm. Not speaking or making much sound. A state of calm or tranquility. To make or become silent or calm.
example_sentence: The library was quiet and peaceful. Please keep quiet during the exam. The town is quiet at night. She spoke in a quiet voice. The medicine quieted his cough.

english_meaning: A gradual decline in an employee’s well-being, confidence, or performance while the person continues working. Hidden emotional strain caused by prolonged pressure, uncertainty, or lack of support at work. A state in which someone appears functional but is privately becoming exhausted or disengaged. Subtle workplace burnout that has not yet led to resignation.
example_sentence: Quiet cracking can begin when employees feel ignored for months. Her manager noticed the signs of quiet cracking and offered support. Regular conversations may prevent quiet cracking from becoming burnout. Although he met every deadline, he was experiencing quiet cracking.

english_meaning: A large, stiff feather from a bird's wing or tail, traditionally used as a writing instrument. One of the sharp, stiff, hollow protective spines on the body of a porcupine or hedgehog. A hollow, tube-like structure such as the barrel of a feather. To weave or form into small cylindrical folds.
example_sentence: The medieval monk spent his days transcribing manuscripts with a sharpened goose quill. The porcupine raised its quills as a warning to the approaching predator. She dipped the quill into the inkwell before carefully signing the parchment. Each quill on the bird's wing is designed for both strength and flight. The dress was decorated with intricate quill work and delicate ruffles.

english_meaning: A warm bed covering made of two layers of fabric with padding between them. A stitched blanket often decorated with patterns. To stitch layers of cloth and filling together. A patchwork covering used for warmth or decoration.
example_sentence: Grandmother made a beautiful patchwork quilt. She pulled the quilt up to her chin. He learned to quilt from his aunt. The children snuggled under a warm quilt.

english_meaning: A hard, yellow, pear-shaped fruit that is usually cooked before eating. A fragrant fruit used mainly for jams, jellies, and preserves. The small tree that produces this fruit. A tart fruit that becomes sweet and pink when cooked.
example_sentence: Quince is too hard to eat raw. She simmered the quince until it turned deep pink. Quince jelly is a traditional winter preserve. The old quince tree stands near the wall.

english_meaning: A stanza or poem of five lines. A post or target used in medieval jousting practice. The exercise of tilting at such a target with a lance.
example_sentence: The poet arranged the lines into a neat quintain. A quintain often ends with a striking final line. Knights practised daily at the quintain. The wooden quintain still stands in the castle yard.

english_meaning: The most perfect or typical example of a quality or class. The pure essence of a substance. In medieval philosophy, the fifth and highest essence after the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water. A refined essence or extracted part of a substance that contains its most essential qualities.
example_sentence: She was the quintessence of poise and elegance during the royal gala. The old village is often described as the quintessence of rural British life. Scientists spent years trying to isolate the quintessence of the rare herbal extract. The peaceful garden was the quintessence of tranquility. His performance was the quintessence of dramatic art in the twentieth century.

english_meaning: Representing the most perfect or typical example of a quality or class. Serving as the pure and essential essence of something. Being the most concentrated and purest form. Characterized by being the ultimate embodiment of a particular style or character.
example_sentence: He was the quintessential tough guy with a heart of gold. The valley is the quintessential English countryside scene. Roasting a turkey is the quintessential Thanksgiving tradition. Her style is the quintessential example of modern elegance. The small town festival provided a quintessential glimpse into local culture.

english_meaning: Five times as many or as much. Consisting of five parts, members, or elements. A group or amount of five. To make or become five times as great or numerous.
example_sentence: The camera uses a quintuple-lens system. Membership grew to quintuple its original size. The company plans to quintuple its production capacity. The five musicians performed as a quintuple ensemble.

english_meaning: A clever or witty remark or comment often made on the spur of the moment. A sharp or sarcastic observation intended to be humorous. To make a witty or biting remark.
example_sentence: He ended his speech with a humorous quip about the local weather. When asked about his mistakes, he offered a defiant quip that silenced the room. I was too stunned by her sharp quip to think of a clever comeback. The comedian is well-known for his ability to quip about current events without preparation. She managed to discharge the tension in the elevator with a timely quip.

english_meaning: A peculiar or unusual habit, behavior, or feature of a person. A strange or unexpected twist or turn of events. A small distinctive trait that makes someone or something unique. A sudden curve, flourish, or change. A clever or odd peculiarity in nature or design.
example_sentence: Talking to himself was one of his strange quirks. By a quirk of fate, they met again after many years. Every person has their own little quirks. The old house had many charming quirks. A quirk in the system caused the unexpected error.

english_meaning: Unusual in an interesting, odd, or charming way. A person, thing, style, habit, or idea that is different from the usual in a special, odd, or attractive way. It often suggests originality, playfulness, or unexpected charm rather than something negative.
example_sentence: She has a quirky sense of fashion that makes her stand out in a crowd. The café became popular because of its quirky interior design and unusual menu. His quirky habits made his friends laugh, but they also found him very charming. The movie was quirky, creative, and full of unexpected moments.

english_meaning: A person who collaborates with an enemy force occupying their country. A traitor who accepts an office under the occupying government or helps the enemy for personal gain. One who betrays their country or allies by helping an invader.
example_sentence: He was branded a quisling for his role in the puppet government. The history books remember him as a disgraceful quisling who sold out his people. During the occupation, many secret quislings were exposed and punished. He refused to be a quisling and chose to join the underground resistance. The regime relied on a network of quislings to maintain control over the local population.

english_meaning: A rare Scottish term describing something puzzling, doubtful or hard to settle. Of a person, dubious in character or hard to trust.
example_sentence: The lawyer called it a quisquous matter best left alone. It is a quisquous question with no clear answer. They dealt with a quisquous fellow from the market. The old text uses the quisquous word twice.

english_meaning: To leave a job, place, or activity permanently. To stop doing something, especially a habit. To resign from a position or role. To give up on a task, effort, or challenge. To depart from a location or company.
example_sentence: He decided to quit his job and start his own business. She finally quit smoking after many years. Never quit before you give your best effort. They quit the meeting halfway through.

english_meaning: To shake slightly, often because of strong emotion. To shake because of fear, cold, nervousness, etc. The act or instance of trembling. A slight trembling movement or sound. A container for holding arrows.
example_sentence: Her hands quivered with excitement. The leaves quivered in the wind. He felt a quiver of fear run through him. The archer reached for an arrow from his quiver. Her voice quivered with anger.

english_meaning: Extremely idealistic; unrealistic and impractical in pursuit of ideals. Guided by lofty romantic notions that are not achievable in reality. Acting with noble but impractical goals.
example_sentence: His quixotic plan to end world poverty in one year was inspiring but impossible. She has a quixotic belief that honesty alone can solve all political problems. It was a quixotic adventure, brave but doomed from the start. He made a quixotic decision to quit his job and travel the world with no money.

english_meaning: A test of knowledge, especially as a competition or a brief informal test. To examine someone by asking many questions.
example_sentence: The teacher gave us a surprise quiz on the history chapter. I enjoy participating in the weekly pub quiz. The police began to quiz the witness about the incident. She spent the evening studying for her biology quiz.

english_meaning: The minimum number of members needed to make a meeting or decision official. The smallest number of people who must be present at a meeting, assembly, committee, or organization so that official business can be conducted and valid decisions can be made. Without a quorum, the group usually cannot vote or take formal action.
example_sentence: The meeting was postponed because there was no quorum. At least ten members are needed to form a quorum. The committee could not vote until a quorum was present. Once the quorum was reached, the chairperson began the session.

english_meaning: A fixed share or limited amount that is officially allowed or required. A maximum number of goods or people permitted in a given period. A target that a person or group is expected to achieve. A share allotted to a particular group as part of a larger total.
example_sentence: The country has a strict import quota on sugar. Each salesperson must meet a monthly quota. A quota of seats is reserved for rural students. The factory has already filled its production quota.

english_meaning: Suitable or interesting enough to be repeated as a quotation. Worth quoting because it is witty, memorable, or well expressed. Able to be officially quoted or cited. Describing a person known for making memorable remarks.
example_sentence: The speech was full of quotable lines. He is a highly quotable politician. She said something quotable about hard work and luck. The report contains few quotable figures.

english_meaning: A group of words taken from a text or speech and repeated by someone else. The act of quoting someone's words. A formal statement of the price at which work will be done or goods supplied. The current price of a share or commodity on a market.
example_sentence: He began his speech with a quotation from Shah Latif. Please put the quotation inside inverted commas. We received a quotation for repairing the roof. The latest quotation for gold rose sharply today.

english_meaning: To repeat words that someone else has written or said. To mention something as an example or as proof. To state a price for goods or work. A phrase taken from a text or speech. A stated price or estimate.
example_sentence: She quoted a famous line from the poem. He quoted several studies to support his argument. The mechanic quoted twelve thousand rupees for the repair. My favourite quote is about patience and time.

english_meaning: Occurring or recurring every day. Belonging to each day as something mundane or ordinary. Commonplace and lacking in excitement or novelty. Characterized by the routine experiences of daily life.
example_sentence: The artist found beauty in the most quotidian objects like a chipped coffee mug. His journal was filled with the quotidian details of house chores and grocery lists. Television has become a quotidian escape for millions after work. She missed the quotidian rhythms of her small town after moving to the bustling city. The movie depicts the quotidian struggles of a working-class family.

english_meaning: The state of being extremely fanatical or uncontrolled in behavior. Excessive zeal or fury in support of a cause. The condition of suffering from rabies. Violent or unreasoning intensity. Wild and irrational enthusiasm.
example_sentence: The rabidity of the mob shocked the whole nation. His rabidity in supporting the team amused everyone. The rabidity of the dog was confirmed by tests. Political rabidity often destroys reasoned debate.

english_meaning: A contagious and fatal viral disease of dogs and other mammals that causes madness and convulsions and is transmissible through the saliva to humans. An acute viral infection of the central nervous system that is most commonly transmitted through the bite of an infected animal. Hydrophobia, characterized by a fear of water as a symptom of the disease.
example_sentence: The stray dog was suspected of having rabies after it attacked several people. Public health officials recommend vaccinating all household pets against rabies. If you are bitten by a wild animal, you must seek medical attention immediately to prevent rabies from developing. Rabies is almost always fatal once clinical symptoms appear in the patient. The local clinic provided post-exposure prophylaxis for the rabies virus.

english_meaning: A medium-sized nocturnal mammal native to North America, with grayish fur, a black facial mask, and a ringed tail. An adaptable animal known for dexterous front paws and scavenging near human settlements. The fur or pelt of this animal.
example_sentence: A raccoon searched the trash bins at midnight. We saw a raccoon beside the forest trail. The raccoon washed its food in the stream. Secure the lid so a raccoon cannot open the container.

english_meaning: Relating to the categorization of humans based on physical characteristics or ancestry. Pertaining to the divisions of humankind into distinct groups. Having to do with a particular race of people or the relationship between different races. Often used to describe issues involving prejudice, discrimination, or social dynamics between different ethnic backgrounds.
example_sentence: The country has been working hard to improve racial equality in the workplace. They faced many racial barriers when trying to move into the new neighborhood. The study examined the racial composition of different urban areas. It is important to have an open discussion about racial injustice in our society. The census included a question about each person's racial background.

english_meaning: The belief that different human races possess distinct characteristics, abilities, or qualities, especially so as to distinguish them as inferior or superior to one another. Prejudice, discrimination, or antagonism directed against someone of a different race. A doctrine or system based on racial distinction and favoritism.
example_sentence: The country has a long history of struggling against systemic racialism in its institutions. He spoke out against the inherent racialism present in the old colonial laws. Scientific racialism was used in the past to justify unequal treatment of different ethnic groups. The movement aimed to eradicate racialism and promote social equality for all citizens.

english_meaning: The unfair treatment of people who belong to a different race, violent behavior towards them. The belief that some races of people are better than others, or a general belief about a whole group of people based only on their race.
example_sentence: It is time, once again, to contend with racism. Racism exists at all levels of society. I abhor all forms of racism. Racism continues to be a challenge in many parts of the world. Racism prevents people from living together in peace and harmony.

english_meaning: A person who believes that one race is superior to others. Coming from or having the belief that people who belong to other races are not as good, intelligent, moral, etc as people who belong to your own race.
example_sentence: He's a racist. The family was being harassed by racists. Two of the killers are known to be racists. She cannot understand how her husband could be branded a racist. He was criticized for making racist comments during the meeting. A racist attitude can destroy harmony in a diverse society. She refused to work with a racist who discriminated against others.

english_meaning: A framework with bars, shelves, or pegs used for holding or storing things. To cause great physical or mental pain. To strain or stretch something with force. A historical instrument of torture used to stretch a victim's body. To search or think very hard, as in racking one's brains.
example_sentence: She hung her coat on the rack by the door. He racked his brains but could not remember the name. The patient was racked with pain all night. Spices were neatly arranged on a wooden rack.

english_meaning: A person who engages in dishonest and fraudulent business dealings. Someone who makes money through illegal activities, typically involving intimidation, bribery, or extortion. A criminal who operates an organized illegal scheme or racket.
example_sentence: The police eventually arrested the notorious racketeer for his involvement in the protection racket. He was known as a ruthless racketeer who controlled the city's construction industry. Several racketeers were indicted for money laundering and fraud. The investigation aimed to dismantle the network of racketeers operating in the harbor.

english_meaning: The act of running a dishonest or illegal business scheme for profit. Obtaining money through fraud, extortion, bribery, or organised crime. A pattern of criminal activity carried out repeatedly by an organised group. Illegal dealings that are disguised as a legitimate business.
example_sentence: He was arrested on charges of racketeering and money laundering. The gang was accused of racketeering in the construction industry. Federal agents spent two years investigating the racketeering network. Racketeering damages honest businesses and public trust.

english_meaning: A person who tells stories or anecdotes in a skillful and entertaining way. Someone who is good at narrating events with humour and vivid detail. A gifted and amusing storyteller who holds the attention of listeners. A person known socially for recounting interesting personal experiences.
example_sentence: Her grandfather was a wonderful raconteur who kept everyone spellbound. The dinner guests laughed for hours at the raconteur's tales. As a raconteur, he could turn an ordinary journey into an adventure. The old sailor was a famous raconteur in the coastal town.

english_meaning: A quality of brightness and light that shines forth from something or someone. The glowing heat or light emitted by an object. A state or quality of great happiness, health, or beauty that is clearly visible in someone's face or expression. The physical emission of energy in the form of electromagnetic waves.
example_sentence: The morning sun's radiance filled the entire valley with a golden hue. Everyone remarked on the bride's natural radiance as she walked down the aisle. The scientist measured the thermal radiance coming from the cooling metal. Her face regained its healthy radiance after she returned from the long vacation. The fireplace provided a comforting radiance during the cold winter evening.

english_meaning: Sending out light or shining brightly. Showing great happiness, joy, or health. Emitting warmth, energy, or a strong feeling. Full of hope or love.
example_sentence: The bride looked radiant on her wedding day. The sun was radiant in the clear blue sky. She gave him a radiant smile. His face was radiant with pride when his son graduated.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting the fundamental nature of something, often involving far-reaching change. Advocating thorough or complete political or social reform, sometimes through extreme measures. A person who holds extreme views, especially regarding political or social change. Departing significantly from what is traditional, moderate, or usual.
example_sentence: The new policy represents a radical departure from previous government strategies.  He was known as a radical thinker who challenged conventional academic views.  The party called for radical reforms to the education system.  Her radical approach to design completely transformed the company's brand identity.  The protest was organized by a small group of political radicals.

english_meaning: To cause someone to adopt extreme political, social or religious views. It means pushing a person or group away from moderate thinking toward more intense or extreme positions.
example_sentence: The group tried to radicalise young members through online messages. Some prisoners become radicalised during their time in jail. Extreme speeches can radicalise people who are already frustrated. The organization works to stop youth from being radicalised.

english_meaning: To cause someone to adopt extreme political, social or religious views. It means pushing a person or group away from moderate thinking toward more intense or extreme positions.
example_sentence: The group tried to radicalize youth. Online content can radicalize people. He became radicalized in prison. Some movements radicalize members slowly.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting the root of a nerve, especially one of the spinal nerve roots. It describes something that pertains to the base or root of a structure. In botanical terms, it can refer to the root of a plant. In medicine, it is often associated with symptoms like pain or numbness that radiate along a nerve path.
example_sentence: The patient complained of radicular pain that shot down his left leg. A radicular cyst was discovered during the dental examination of the root canal. Diagnostic imaging was used to confirm the radicular nature of the nerve compression. The doctor explained that the tingling sensation was a result of radicular irritation in the lumbar spine.

english_meaning: Emitting harmful radiation because of the decay of unstable atomic nuclei. Relating to or caused by radioactivity. Describing a substance that gives off alpha, beta, or gamma rays. Contaminated by radiation and therefore dangerous.
example_sentence: The site was closed because of radioactive contamination. Uranium is a naturally radioactive element. Radioactive waste must be stored with extreme care. Doctors use small amounts of radioactive material in some scans.

english_meaning: The property of giving off radiation as unstable atomic nuclei break down. The radiation emitted by such a process. The scientific study or measurement of this phenomenon. The presence of radioactive material in an environment.
example_sentence: Marie Curie carried out pioneering research on radioactivity. Levels of radioactivity near the plant are checked daily. Radioactivity can damage living cells if exposure is high. The instrument measures radioactivity in soil samples.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating diseases using medical imaging. A physician who interprets X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, and other imaging studies. A specialist in radiology who uses radiation and imaging technology.
example_sentence: The radiologist reviewed my chest X-ray. She is a radiologist specializing in breast imaging. The radiologist detected a fracture in the scan. Radiologists use advanced imaging technology.

english_meaning: A swollen pungent-tasting edible root, especially a variety which is small, spherical, and red. It is eaten raw as a salad vegetable and has a crisp texture. The plant belongs to the mustard family and grows very quickly. The leaves of the radish are sometimes used in cooking as well.
example_sentence: He sliced a crisp red radish to add to the green salad. The white radish is often used in making traditional flatbreads. We harvested a bunch of fresh radish from the organic farm. Radish has a sharp flavor that enhances the taste of cold dishes.

english_meaning: One of the two long bones of the forearm, lying on the thumb side. The forearm bone that rotates around the ulna to turn the palm up or down. A bone that forms the main part of the wrist joint. A straight line from the centre of a circle to its edge, or the length of such a line.
example_sentence: She fractured her radius when she landed on her outstretched hand. The radius turns around the ulna when you rotate your palm. The wrist joint is formed mainly by the lower end of the radius. The teacher asked the class to measure the radius of the circle.

english_meaning: Disreputable or worthless people, often seen in the phrase riff-raff. A confused heap, jumble, or rubbish. Low-class or vulgar individuals considered as a collective group.
example_sentence: The guard was hired to keep the raff out of the exclusive event. Old papers and raff were scattered across the floor of the abandoned house. They considered the new crowd in town to be nothing but raff. He brushed away the raff that had collected on his desk.

english_meaning: A flat buoyant structure, usually made of planks or logs fastened together, used as a boat or floating platform. A small inflatable rubber boat used for recreation or emergency survival at sea. A large number or a vast amount of something. To travel or transport something using a flat floating structure.
example_sentence: The survivors escaped the sinking ship by clinging to a makeshift wooden raft. We spent the afternoon using an inflatable raft to float down the calm river. The company has introduced a whole raft of new measures to improve safety. They decided to raft their supplies across the lake instead of carrying them by land. The logs were tied together to form a sturdy raft for the long journey.

english_meaning: A small piece of old or torn cloth often used for cleaning or wiping things. A person who is wearing old or tattered clothing. A piece of music in a specific style, particularly related to ragtime. A newspaper or magazine that is considered to be of poor quality or low status. To tease or make fun of someone in a playful or annoying way.
example_sentence: He used an old rag to wipe the grease off his hands. The team decided to rag their new member as part of the initiation. She dressed her children in rags because they were very poor. I wouldn't believe anything written in that local rag. The pianist played a lively rag that had everyone dancing.

english_meaning: A person who collects rags, waste materials, or discarded items from streets or dumps for a living. Someone who searches through garbage to find items that can be sold or reused. A poor worker involved in informal recycling. A traditional occupation in many countries where people earn by gathering scraps. A person symbolizing extreme poverty and hardship.
example_sentence: A young rag picker was seen sorting waste near the market. Rag pickers play an important role in informal recycling. Many rag pickers live in extreme poverty. The NGO started a school for rag picker children.

english_meaning: Violent and uncontrollable anger or intense fury. A sudden period of extreme violence or aggression. A period of extreme intensity or passion regarding an activity or feeling. To express or manifest intense anger in a loud or uncontrolled manner. To spread or prevail with great force or intensity, such as a storm, fire, or disease.
example_sentence: He flew into a rage when he saw the damage to his car. The storm continued to rage throughout the entire night. Despite her calm exterior, a secret fury began to rage within her. Road rage has become a serious problem in modern urban traffic. The forest fire raged across the hills for several days.

english_meaning: Pieces of old, torn, or worn-out cloth often discarded or used for cleaning purposes. A state of extreme poverty or being dressed in shabby, tattered clothing. Small remnants of fabric left over after a larger piece has been cut.
example_sentence: The mechanic used several dirty rags to wipe the grease off his hands. After years of hard work, he rose from rags to riches through a stroke of luck. She tore the old bedsheet into small rags for dusting the furniture. The beggar was dressed in filthy rags that barely protected him from the cold. Please don't throw away that old shirt as it can be used as a cleaning rag.

english_meaning: Untidy, disorganized, or made of mixed poor quality items. A group made up of very different and often low quality people or things. Disorganized or poorly arranged in appearance. Made from assorted leftover or unmatched items. A collection lacking uniformity or structure.
example_sentence: The ragtag team still managed to win the match. He wore a ragtag collection of old clothes. The volunteers formed a ragtag group but worked efficiently. A ragtag crowd gathered outside the building.

english_meaning: A sudden and unexpected attack on a place by a small group of people or soldiers. A surprise visit by the police to search a building or arrest people. A quick action to take or steal something from a container or room. An investigation or search conducted by authorities to find evidence or illegal goods.
example_sentence: The elite squad carried out a midnight raid on the enemy compound. Police officers conducted a raid on the warehouse looking for stolen property. I catch the children making a late-night raid on the refrigerator for snacks. The sudden bank raid was over in less than three minutes before the alarm sounded. Anti-corruption officials launched a raid on the office to seize financial documents.

english_meaning: A person or group who attacks, steals, or makes a sudden assault. Someone who carries out a surprise attack, often to take goods, resources, or territory. It can refer to military attacks, pirate actions, or aggressive business takeovers.
example_sentence: The Vikings were notorious raiders in medieval Europe. The company acted like a raider, buying out smaller competitors aggressively. The police caught a raider trying to break into the warehouse. During the night, the desert raiders stole livestock from the village.

english_meaning: Water falling in drops from clouds to the ground. A fall of such water, or a period of rainy weather. To fall as rain from the sky. To fall or send down in large quantities, like rain. A large or rapid fall of something such as blows, questions, or gifts.
example_sentence: Heavy rain delayed the start of the match. It began to rain soon after we left home. Reporters rained questions on the minister. The fields turned green after the first rain of the season.

english_meaning: To politely postpone. To delay accepting an invitation or offer while clearly showing interest in doing it later. It is often used in informal conversation. A promise to do something later. An agreement or understanding that an invitation, plan, or offer declined now will be accepted at a later time. It shows intention without fixing a time.
example_sentence: I cannot join you for dinner tonight but can I take a rain check She took a rain check on the meeting due to urgent work Let us take a rain check and plan this trip next week He offered help but asked for a rain check until the weekend

english_meaning: Fall heavily. To fall in large amounts from the sky, often suddenly or intensely.
example_sentence: Bombs rained down on the city. Compliments rained down on her performance. Papers rained down from the shelf. Snow rained down all night.

english_meaning: Accumulate rapidly. To arrive in large amounts or in a sudden rush.
example_sentence: Donations rained in after the appeal. Emails rained in all morning. Orders rained in after the promotion. Complaints rained in about the delay.

english_meaning: Cancel due to rain. To stop or cancel an event because of rain. To stop, postpone, or cancel an event or activity because of rain, making it impossible or unsafe to continue as planned
example_sentence: The match was rained off. The picnic got rained off. Our plans were rained off. The outdoor concert was rained off.

english_meaning: Spoil or dampen. To ruin or interfere with someone’s plans or enjoyment.
example_sentence: Don’t rain on my parade. His comments rained on her excitement. The rain rained on our picnic. Critics rained on the movie’s premiere.

english_meaning: To spoil someone’s happiness or plans, to ruin a joyful moment. The act of doing something that ruins another person’s positive experience or excitement. It often implies discouragement or disappointment caused intentionally or unintentionally.
example_sentence: I didn’t want to rain on her parade, but she should know the truth. The sudden storm rained on our parade during the picnic. Don’t rain on his parade, he just got promoted. Critics rained on the author’s parade with harsh reviews.

english_meaning: Bestow heavily. To cause something, such as praise, gifts, or attention, to fall upon someone heavily or generously, often used figuratively to indicate abundance or overwhelming effect.
example_sentence: Praise rained upon the artist. Luck rained upon the winners. Gifts rained upon the children. Opportunities rained upon the graduates. Blessings rained upon the village after the harvest. Criticism rained upon the politician after the scandal.

english_meaning: Used to describe very heavy rain, when it rains a lot, suddenly and strongly. It doesn’t mean actual cats and dogs are falling; it’s just an expression for torrential rain.
example_sentence: It was raining cats and dogs, so we decided to stay indoors. Don’t forget your umbrella, it might rain cats and dogs tonight!. Yesterday it rained cats and dogs, and the streets were flooded. We couldn’t play football because it was raining cats and dogs all afternoon.

english_meaning: To move something to a higher position or level. To increase the amount, level, or strength of something. To bring up a child or care for them until they are an adult. To cause something to exist or happen. To collect money for a specific purpose.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the students to raise their hands if they knew the answer. The company decided to raise the prices of its products due to inflation. It takes a lot of patience and dedication to raise a child properly. We are organizing a charity event to raise funds for the local hospital. The new evidence was enough to raise serious doubts about the suspect's alibi.

english_meaning: To increase standards or expectations. It means improving the quality, performance, or achievement level so that others must work harder to reach it. To make a standard higher than before
example_sentence: The company raised the bar by launching an innovative product this year. His excellent performance has raised the bar for future employees. The new school principal has raised the bar for academic excellence. Their latest film has raised the bar in the movie industry. Every year, the university raises the bar for academic excellence. The new smartphone design raised the bar for the entire industry.

english_meaning: A dried grape, typically small, dark, and sweet, used in cooking and snacking. It can also refer to a deep purplish-red color similar to that of a dried grape. A variety of vitis vinifera that has been dehydrated naturally or through a process.
example_sentence: She added a handful of raisins to the oatmeal cookies for extra sweetness. The sun-dried raisins were much plumper than the store-bought ones. A traditional Christmas pudding is usually packed with raisins and spices. He prefers golden raisins over the dark ones in his pilaf. The walls were painted in a rich raisin hue to match the velvet curtains.

english_meaning: To gather, scrape, or pull something together using a tool or motion. A garden tool with a long handle and teeth used for collecting leaves, grass, or debris.
example_sentence: She rakes the soil every morning. They raked the sand smooth. The worker raked the debris aside. The rake is kept in the garden shed. He bought a new rake for the yard. The metal rake is strong and durable.

english_meaning: To earn or collect a lot of money. To gain something in large amounts especially money profit or rewards
example_sentence: The company raked in huge profits this year. He rakes in money from online work. The movie raked in millions. She raked in rewards for her performance.

english_meaning: To examine something again. To talk about or examine past events especially unpleasant ones in detail
example_sentence: There is no need to rake over past mistakes. The issue was raked over in court. She hates raking over old wounds. Let us not rake over what is finished.

english_meaning: To search thoroughly. To search a place or things carefully often in a hurried or forceful way.
example_sentence: He raked through the drawers for the file. The police raked through the house. She raked through her bag anxiously. They raked through records for evidence.

english_meaning: To collect with difficulty. To gather money or resources from different places with effort.
example_sentence: He raked together enough money for fees. She raked together old notes for study. They raked together funds for charity. I raked together documents for the case.

english_meaning: To bring up something from the past. To remind people of unpleasant past events or to collect something by searching or gathering.
example_sentence: He tried to rake up old arguments during the meeting. The journalist raked up past scandals. She raked up memories she wanted to forget. Do not rake up painful history again.

english_meaning: The action or process of coming together to support a person, cause, or organization. Gathering, mobilizing, or organizing a group to act together in unison. Recovering, improving, or bouncing back after a period of decline, weakness, loss, or illness. Acting as an inspiration or call to action for a group of people.
example_sentence: The community is rallying behind the victim's family during this difficult time. Her rallying speech gave the struggling team the motivation they desperately needed. Prices are rallying in the stock market after a week of heavy losses. He is slowly rallying after a long and severe battle with pneumonia. Politicians spent the weekend rallying their supporters before the upcoming elections.

english_meaning: A male sheep, specifically one that has not been castrated and is kept for breeding. A powerful device or heavy object used to strike or smash against something with great force. To hit or crash into someone or something with heavy force, often repeatedly. To force or push something into a specific position using pressure.
example_sentence: The ram led the flock across the rocky hillside. The police used a heavy steel ram to break down the reinforced door. A heavy truck managed to ram into the back of the stationary bus. He tried to ram the clothes into the suitcase despite it being full. The ancient warships were equipped with a metal beak to ram enemy vessels.

english_meaning: To walk for pleasure, typically without a definite route. To talk or write at length in a confused or inconsequential way. To follow a winding or irregular course. To grow in an uncontrolled or sprawling manner as a plant.
example_sentence: We decided to ramble through the countryside for the entire afternoon. The elderly professor began to ramble about his childhood during the lecture. The old stone walls were covered in roses that ramble in every direction. Her letter was long and tended to ramble on about minor household problems. It is pleasant to ramble along the riverbank when the weather is clear.

english_meaning: Refers to a person or behavior that is uncontrollably exuberant, boisterous, or difficult to manage. Characterized by being noisy, energetic, and lacking restraint in a playful or unruly manner. Often used to describe children or animals that are full of high spirits and physical energy.
example_sentence: The rambunctious puppies kept knocking over the water bowl in their excitement. The classroom became quite rambunctious once the teacher left the room for a moment. It is difficult to keep a group of rambunctious toddlers sitting still for a long story. The crowd at the concert grew increasingly rambunctious as the band played their greatest hits.

english_meaning: A complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or event. The result of a complicated situation which was not initially expected. A structural branching or offshoot, such as the spreading out of a tree's limbs or a network of nerves.
example_sentence: The political ramifications of the new law were felt throughout the entire country. We must consider every possible ramification before making such a major decision. The discovery of the new virus had global ramifications for public health policy. Scientists are still studying the ramifications of the nerve endings in the spinal cord. I don't think you fully understand the ramifications of your actions.

english_meaning: A sloping surface joining two different levels, especially for disabled access or vehicle movement. To increase something rapidly. An inclined plane used to load vehicles or goods. A fraudulent scheme to inflate the value of shares.
example_sentence: A wheelchair ramp was installed at the main entrance of the building to improve accessibility. The government plans to ramp up production of the vaccine in the coming months. The car was driven slowly up the ramp and into the parking deck. The company was accused of ramping its share price before selling off its own holdings. The loading ramp at the back of the warehouse was wide enough for two lorries to use simultaneously.

english_meaning: To reduce gradually. To lower the level, intensity, or activity of something in a controlled or gradual manner.
example_sentence: The factory will ramp down operations during the off season. Officials decided to ramp down emergency measures after the situation improved. The project budget was ramped down due to funding limits.

english_meaning: To increase something quickly or strongly. To raise the level, speed, amount, or intensity of an activity, effort, production, or process, often in response to demand, pressure, or a planned goal. To accelerate or boost activity, output, or effort.
example_sentence: The company ramped up production before the holiday season. The government is ramping up efforts to control flooding. Schools ramped up online classes during the emergency. The team ramped up training ahead of the tournament.

english_meaning: Spreading or growing in an uncontrolled and widespread way, especially something undesirable. Existing or happening on a large scale without restraint. Used for diseases, crime, corruption, weeds, and similar negative things that flourish without being checked.
example_sentence: Corruption is rampant in the department. Crime was rampant in the city before the new police chief took charge. Weeds were rampant in the neglected garden. Rumours about the merger were rampant in the office. Inflation has been rampant for the past two years.

english_meaning: To raise livestock. A large farm used for raising animals like cattle, sheep, or horses.
example_sentence: They bought a ranch in Texas to raise cattle. The ranch covers over 500 acres of land. He decided to ranch in Montana after college. She spent her summers ranching with her family.

english_meaning: (Of food, especially fats or oils) Smelling or tasting unpleasant because it is no longer fresh. Spoiled, stale, or gone bad with a strong, sour, or disgusting smell. (Figuratively) Unpleasant, offensive, or morally bad.
example_sentence: The butter had turned rancid after being left out in the heat. There was a rancid smell coming from the kitchen. Do not use this oil; it has gone rancid. He gave a rancid laugh that made everyone uncomfortable. The room was filled with the rancid odour of old grease.

english_meaning: A bitter, deep-seated feeling of resentment or ill will. Long-lasting hatred caused by a past injury or insult. Angry bitterness that continues long after a quarrel. A spirit of hostility that prevents forgiveness.
example_sentence: He spoke about his old rival without any rancor. Years of rancor divided the two families. She accepted the decision with surprising lack of rancor. The meeting ended in rancor and mutual blame.

english_meaning: Full of bitter, long-lasting resentment or hatred. Showing deep ill will towards someone because of a past wrong. Marked by angry and spiteful feelings, especially in a dispute. Expressing hostility in a harsh and unforgiving way.
example_sentence: The two brothers had a long and rancorous dispute over land. Their divorce was bitter and rancorous from the start. He made several rancorous remarks about his former partner. The debate turned rancorous within a few minutes.

english_meaning: Lacking a definite plan, purpose, or pattern. Made, done, or happening without method or conscious decision. Relating to an event in which all outcomes are equally likely. Chosen without a specific reason or criteria from a larger group. Characterized by a lack of predictability or systematic arrangement.
example_sentence: The computer generates a random sequence of numbers for security. We conducted a random survey of people walking in the park. The books were arranged in a random order on the shelf. A random stranger offered to help her carry the heavy groceries.

english_meaning: The ordinary members of an organization, group, or society, especially not the leaders or officers. It refers to the common people or regular workers in contrast to the top management or leadership.
example_sentence: The rank and file supported the decision. The leaders decided to meet with the rank and file to discuss their concerns. There was growing dissatisfaction among the rank and file workers. While the executives enjoyed privileges, the rank and file struggled with low wages. The party’s success depends on the support of its rank and file members.

english_meaning: An absolute temperature scale with its zero point at absolute zero. A scale that uses Fahrenheit increments rather than Celsius. A measurement system primarily used in engineering systems in the United States. A thermodynamic scale named after the physicist William John Macquorn Rankine. A unit of temperature where the freezing point of water is 491·67 degrees. A conversion factor where Rankine equals Fahrenheit plus 459·67.
synonyms: ["Absolute Scale","Thermodynamic Scale","Fahrenheit-Based Absolute","Temperature Unit","R Scale","Absolute Fahrenheit","Thermal Measurement","Degree Rankine","Physical Constant","Engineering Unit","Scientific Scale","Measurement Standard"]
example_sentence: The Rankine scale is often used in thermodynamic calculations in the United States. Absolute zero is defined as zero degrees on the Rankine scale. To convert Fahrenheit to Rankine, you must add 459.67 to the temperature. Engineers prefer the Rankine scale when working with power cycles and combustion.

english_meaning: To cause persistent annoyance or resentment over a long period. To cause a feeling of irritation or bitterness that continues to be painful. The act of something, such as an insult or a comment, festering in the mind even after time has passed.
example_sentence: The memory of his unfair criticism continued to rankle for years. His rude comment still rankles even though he apologized later. The sense of injustice really rankles with the local community. It rankles me that she got the credit for my hard work. The defeat still rankles in the minds of the team members.

english_meaning: To release a person or object by giving the required payment. To redeem something by paying a price. To deliver someone from danger through a payment. A payment used to settle unlawful detention. A symbolic price paid to free someone from obligation. Money or payment demanded to release someone held captive. To free someone by paying that amount. Money or payment demanded for the release of a captive. A sum of money required to free someone who is being held against their will. It is often demanded by kidnappers, criminals or hostile groups. It refers to the act of buying back freedom or recovering something taken away.
antonyms: ["Release","Liberation","Freedom","Saving without payment","Liberation","Release without payment","Rescue without paying"]
example_sentence: The kidnappers demanded a large ransom for the businessman's release. The family struggled to collect enough money to pay the ransom. The government refused to ransom the hostages. The painting was held for ransom after being stolen from the museum. The king tried to ransom his captured soldiers.

english_meaning: To speak angrily and loudly. To express anger frustration or strong opinions in a loud emotional and often uncontrolled way. An angry speech or complaint. A long loud emotional speech or written complaint showing anger or strong feelings
synonyms: ["Complain shout Rave fume","Tirade outburst Complaint protest"]
example_sentence: He began to rant about corruption. She ranted at the officials. Don’t rant without facts. His rant annoyed everyone. She posted a rant on social media. The speech turned into a rant.

english_meaning: Aggressively greedy or grasping. Someone or something that takes things by force or greedily, often in a selfish or violent way. It can refer to humans, animals, or organizations.
example_sentence: The rapacious landlord raised the rent without warning. Rapacious predators hunt relentlessly to survive. The company's rapacious practices harmed small local businesses. He had a rapacious appetite for power and control.

english_meaning: In an extremely greedy manner. In a way that shows an aggressive desire to take or gain more. In a grasping, exploitative or ruthless manner. In the manner of a predator seizing its prey.
example_sentence: The company rapaciously bought up every small business in the town. He rapaciously collected wealth without caring for anyone. The traders rapaciously raised prices during the shortage. The eagle rapaciously tore into its prey.

english_meaning: Extreme greed for money, possessions, or power. An aggressive and unrestrained desire to take more than one needs. The quality of being grasping, exploitative, or ruthlessly acquisitive. The behaviour of a predatory animal that hunts and devours other creatures.
example_sentence: The rapacity of the money lenders ruined many small farmers. Critics condemned the rapacity of the mining companies. His rapacity for power destroyed old friendships. The rapacity of the wolves left nothing behind.

english_meaning: The crime of forcing another person into sexual intercourse without consent. A serious sexual assault committed against a person's will. The violent destruction or plundering of a place. An oil-producing plant of the cabbage family grown for its seeds.
example_sentence: The court sentenced him to life imprisonment for rape. New laws aim to protect survivors of rape during trial. Historians describe the rape of the ancient city by invading armies. Farmers in the region grow rape for its valuable oil.

english_meaning: A legal expression describing the reduction or reclassification of a charge of rape to the lesser offence of fornication. A term used in court reporting when a coerced sexual offence is treated as consensual unlawful intercourse. A controversial change of charge that lowers the seriousness of a sexual offence.
example_sentence: Activists criticised the rape-to-fornication conversion of the charges. The report documented several rape-to-fornication cases in the lower courts. Lawyers argued that the rape-to-fornication shift denied the victim justice. Legal reforms aim to prevent rape-to-fornication reclassification.

english_meaning: Past tense of 'rap'. Struck something sharply with a quick, light blow. Knocked sharply on a door or surface to attract attention. Spoke sharply, suddenly, or in a critical manner. Performed rap music by speaking rhythmically over a beat. Informally, criticised or rebuked someone.
example_sentence: She rapped on the door three times before entering. The teacher rapped the desk with his ruler to get attention. The minister was rapped by the press for his careless remarks. The young artist rapped on stage in front of a huge crowd. He rapped out his orders in a sharp voice.

english_meaning: A close and harmonious relationship in which the people or groups concerned understand each other's feelings or ideas and communicate well. It often involves mutual trust and emotional connection. Establishng such a bond is essential for effective teamwork and counseling.
example_sentence: The teacher established a great rapport with her students early in the semester. Building a strong rapport with clients is essential for successful sales. They developed a natural rapport during their first meeting. The peace talks failed because there was no rapport between the two leaders.

english_meaning: Complete or intense focus on something. A state of being fully absorbed or engrossed in what is happening, showing deep interest or fascination
example_sentence: The children listened with rapt attention to the storyteller. She watched the performance with rapt attention. The audience sat in rapt attention throughout the lecture. He studied the painting with rapt attention, noticing every detail.

english_meaning: A state or feeling of intense pleasure, joy, or enthusiasm. The expression of great delight. In some Christian theologies, the event where believers are caught up to meet the Lord in the air. A condition of being carried away by overwhelming emotion.
example_sentence: The pianist played with such skill that the audience listened in silent rapture. She gazed at her newborn baby with a look of pure rapture. The explorers described the rapture they felt upon seeing the hidden valley for the first time. He entered a state of religious rapture while meditating in the temple. The crowd greeted the hero with rapture and thunderous applause.

english_meaning: Existing in very small numbers and therefore difficult to find. Something that is uncommon or unusual and not occurring or found very often. An event or situation that is not frequent. In cooking, it refers to meat that is cooked for a very short time and remains red inside.
example_sentence: It is very rare to find a wild panda in this region now. Collectors are always on the hunt for rare stamps that are no longer in circulation. Since we live in different cities, our family gatherings have become quite rare. I would like my steak rare, please, with just a little searing on the outside. A solar eclipse is a rare celestial event that attracts thousands of observers.

english_meaning: Standing as the superlative form of rare, referring to something occurring with the least frequency or seen most seldom. Denoting an item or event that is exceptionally uncommon, unique, or found in very small numbers. It can also describe food that is cooked for the shortest possible time, remaining extremely red in the center.
example_sentence: This is the rarest diamond ever discovered in this mountain range. It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to witness the rarest celestial alignment. The collector spent decades searching for the rarest edition of the manuscript. Specialists consider this the rarest blood type known to medicine. He ordered the steak in its rarest form, barely seared on the outside.

english_meaning: A person, especially a child or man, who shows a lack of principles or behaves in a dishonest way. A mischievous or cheeky person who causes minor trouble or playfulness. A dishonest or unscrupulous fellow who is regarded with a mixture of amusement and disapproval.
example_sentence: That little rascal hid my car keys again just for fun. The old man was known as a lovable rascal despite his frequent gambling. Don't be such a rascal and return the stolen pencil to your sister. The villain in the play was a charming rascal who stole the hearts of the audience. He called his dog a rascal when it ran away with his slipper.

english_meaning:
A large number of instances in a short period
Acting or done without careful consideration of the possible consequences, impetuous
example_sentence:
The baby has a skin rash.
 The doctor said she developed the rash because of the medicine.

english_meaning: A sudden series of many strikes (workers stopping work in protest) happening in a short period of time. A large number of unpleasant events occurring suddenly.
synonyms: ["Wave of strikes","Spate of strikes","Outbreak of strikes"]
antonyms: ["Settlement of disputes","Period of calm","Harmony at work"]
example_sentence: After the government announced new tax reforms, a rash of strikes broke out across the country. The transport sector faced a rash of strikes, leaving commuters stranded for days. Teachers launched a rash of strikes demanding better salaries and working conditions. A rash of strikes in the factories slowed down production and hurt the economy.

english_meaning:
The quality of state of being rash, inconsiderate or presumptuous haste, headstrong precipitation in decision or action, temerity, unwarranted boldness.
An eruption on the body
example_sentence: In later years he attributed his want of success to the immature style of his early exposition, to the rashness of a young innovator in an old and well-established province of literature.

english_meaning: A situation where different people give different and sometimes contradictory accounts of the same event because each person sees and remembers it differently. The Rashomon effect describes how individuals can experience the same incident in different ways and later explain it according to their own perspective, emotions, memories, interests, or biases. It is often discussed in psychology, journalism, law, history, literature, and social sciences.
synonyms: ["Subjective interpretation","Conflicting perspectives","Multiple viewpoints","Differing testimony","Perceptual bias","Contradictory accounts"]
example_sentence: During the court case, every witness described the accident differently, showing the Rashomon effect. The siblings remembered their childhood argument in completely opposite ways because of the Rashomon effect. Journalists often encounter the Rashomon effect when interviewing several people about the same political event. In team meetings, the Rashomon effect can appear when employees recall the same discussion differently.

english_meaning: A small soft red or black berry made up of many tiny juicy segments. An edible fruit that grows on thorny canes. The plant that produces this fruit. A rude sound made with the tongue and lips to show disapproval.
example_sentence: Fresh raspberries taste wonderful with cream. She grows raspberries along the garden fence. The cake was topped with raspberry sauce. The crowd blew a raspberry at the decision.

english_meaning: Rough and harsh in sound or texture. Used to describe a voice, sound, or surface that feels or sounds rough, scratchy, or unpleasant, often due to dryness, illness, or friction.
example_sentence: He spoke in a raspy voice after shouting all night. The singer’s raspy tone made the song more emotional. She cleared her throat, which sounded raspy and dry. Years of smoking gave him a deep, raspy voice.

english_meaning: A situation where something increases or moves forward step by step and does not easily go back to its previous lower level. A ratchet effect happens when progress, prices, habits, or systems move in one direction, usually upward, and it becomes difficult to reverse that change. It is often used in economics, business, psychology, and social behavior.
synonyms: ["Irreversible increase","One way growth","Upward lock","Progressive rise","Permanent escalation","Sticky increase"]
example_sentence: Due to the ratchet effect, employees found it difficult to accept lower salaries after a pay increase. Inflation often creates a ratchet effect where prices rise quickly but fall very slowly. Government spending sometimes shows a ratchet effect because budgets rarely return to earlier levels. Consumer lifestyles can reflect the ratchet effect when people keep spending at a higher level even after income drops.

english_meaning: The official way to confirm or give formal sanction to something. A formal validation of a treaty, contract, or agreement. The act of signing or giving formal consent to a document, making it officially valid. Legal confirmation or approval of an action performed by an agent. Verification or substantiation of a prior act.
example_sentence: The treaty is subject to ratification by the senate before it becomes law. The group called for the immediate ratification of the new human rights charter. Both countries are waiting for the final ratification of the trade deal. Without official ratification, the agreement remains legally non-binding.

english_meaning: Formally approved or sanctioned by an official body. Made valid by signing or giving formal consent to a treaty or contract. Confirmed and settled as an agreement. Legally binding after a process of validation. Authenticated by authoritative action.
example_sentence: The newly signed peace treaty was ratified by all participating nations. The board of directors ratified the decision during their annual meeting. Each member state must have the agreement ratified by their national parliament. The amendment was eventually ratified after months of intense public debate.

english_meaning: To sign or give formal consent to a treaty, contract, or agreement. To make a document or action officially valid. To confirm something by expressing approval or sanction. To formally validate a previous act done by an agent. To establish as a law or binding regulation through an official vote.
example_sentence: The government is expected to ratify the new trade agreement by the end of the month. All member states must ratify the treaty before it can come into full effect. The board of directors met today to ratify the decisions made during the previous emergency session. It took several years for the parliament to finally ratify the constitutional amendment.

english_meaning: The quantitative relationship between two amounts, showing how many times one value contains the other. A proportion or comparison expressed in numbers. The relative size of two or more values compared with each other. A balance or relationship between different parts of a whole.
example_sentence: The ratio of students to teachers in this school is twenty to one. Mix the cement and sand in a ratio of one to three. The company improved its debt-to-equity ratio last year. In this class the ratio of boys to girls is almost equal.

english_meaning: Based on facts or reason and not on emotions or feelings. Having the ability to reason or think about things clearly. Involving only multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction and only a finite number of times.
example_sentence:
There must be some rational explanation for what happened. There must be some rational explanation for what happened. In that state of mind you can't make a rational decision.
I'm sure there's a perfectly rational explanation for it.

english_meaning: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, where the denominator is not zero. Any number expressible as a ratio of one whole number to another. A number whose decimal form either ends or repeats.
example_sentence: The number three quarters is a rational number. Every integer is also a rational number. Rational numbers can be plotted on a number line. The teacher explained how to add two rational numbers.

english_meaning: The reason or explanation for something. The underlying logic, reasoning, or justification behind a decision, belief, action, or idea. It explains why something is done or why a particular choice is made.
example_sentence: The rationale for the new policy was to improve workplace safety. She explained the rationale behind her decision to switch careers. Understanding the rationale of the experiment helps in interpreting its results. The teacher asked the students to provide a rationale for their answers.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being based on or in accordance with reason or logic. The capacity for logical thought and the ability to exercise reason to form conclusions. A belief or behavior that is characterized by consistency and sound judgment. The exercise of reason to explain or justify a particular action or opinion.
example_sentence: The scientist approached the problem with absolute rationality instead of emotion. Economists often assume that human beings act with perfect rationality in a marketplace. She questioned the rationality of his decision to quit his job without another offer. In a moment of crisis, it is difficult to maintain quiet rationality. The philosopher spent his life exploring the limits of human rationality.

english_meaning: To make a rapid succession of short, sharp, clattering sounds. To cause something to make a series of short, loud noises by shaking it. To move with a rattling sound. To make someone feel nervous, worried, or irritated. To speak or recite something rapidly and easily.
example_sentence: The old windows began to rattle whenever a large truck drove past the house. The baby amused himself by shaking his colorful plastic rattle. The unexpected questions from the reporter seemed to rattle the politician during the interview. She can rattle off the names of all the presidents in less than a minute. The loose coins in the metal box rattle every time the car turns a corner.

english_meaning: To threaten or show readiness for war or conflict, especially to intimidate or warn another person or country. It often refers to a show of force rather than actual fighting. To make aggressive threats or warn of possible action, usually to scare or pressure others.
example_sentence: The government began rattling its sabres after the border dispute escalated. He likes to rattle his sabre whenever negotiations don’t go his way. The country’s leaders are sabre-rattling to gain political advantage. Instead of peaceful dialogue, both sides started rattling their sabres on social media.

english_meaning: Very loud, noisy, and harsh. Sounds or behavior that are unpleasantly loud, rough, and often chaotic. It is commonly used for crowds, laughter, voices, or music that feel uncontrolled or aggressive.
example_sentence: The crowd became raucous after the winning goal. Raucous laughter filled the hall during the comedy show. The bar was raucous late at night with shouting and music. Protesters raised raucous chants outside the building.

english_meaning: To cause severe and widespread damage or destruction to a place, thing, or system. To devastate, ruin, or lay waste. To plunder violently. The destructive effects of something such as war, disease, or time. It is often used for both natural disasters and human actions.
example_sentence: The earthquake ravaged the entire town. War has ravaged the country for years. The disease has ravaged the population. Time has ravaged the once beautiful palace. The forest fire ravaged thousands of acres.

english_meaning: To make a situation or problem more complicated. To fall into perplexity and confusion. To become untwisted or unwoven, to be disentangled, to be relieved of intricacy.
example_sentence: This kind of carpet will never ravel. We have to ravel the matter out. Can you unravel the mystery?

english_meaning: To untangle or undo something that is woven, knitted, or tangled. To solve a complex problem or mystery by examining its individual parts. To become frayed or separated into individual threads at the edges. To clear up a complicated situation or confusion.
