example_sentence: She spent hours trying to ravel out the knotted fishing line. The detective managed to ravel out the mystery by following the smallest clues. If you pull that loose thread, the whole sleeve will start to ravel out. It took a long time to ravel out the truth from the lies he told. The old carpet began to ravel out at the corners after years of use.

english_meaning: Extremely hungry; having a strong desire for food or something else (like power, knowledge, etc)
example_sentence: After the long hike, we were absolutely ravenous and ate everything on the table. He gave the dog a bone because it looked ravenous. She has a ravenous appetite for knowledge. The ravenous wolves attacked the deer in the forest.

english_meaning: To delight greatly or to overpower with strong feeling. To fill someone with intense pleasure, admiration, or joy. To force someone sexually. Modern usage avoids the second sense except in legal or historical contexts.
example_sentence: The beauty of the mountains ravished the tourists. Her performance ravished the audience and earned a standing ovation. He was ravished by the peaceful silence of the desert. In classic literature, the word ravish is often used to describe emotional intensity.

english_meaning: Extremely beautiful, attractive, or delightful. Causing great admiration or wonder due to charm or elegance. Stunningly lovely to look at. Enchanting in a way that captivates the senses.
example_sentence: She looked ravishing in her wedding dress. The garden was a ravishing sight in spring. He gave her a ravishing smile from across the room. The actress made a ravishing appearance on the red carpet.

english_meaning: The unripe green fruit of the jackfruit tree, used as a vegetable. A large tropical fruit cooked before ripening for savory dishes. A meat-like vegetable often used as a plant-based substitute for chicken or mutton. A vegetable commonly cooked with spices, onions, and gravy. A traditional food widely used in South Asian and Southeast Asian cuisines.
example_sentence: Raw jackfruit curry is a popular dish in South India. She cooked raw jackfruit with onions and spices. Many vegetarians use raw jackfruit as a meat substitute. Raw jackfruit is rich in fiber and low in calories.

english_meaning: To completely destroy a building, town, or other structure down to the ground. To level something or demolish it until nothing remains. To erase or scrape off something entirely.
example_sentence: The old factory was razed to the ground to make room for a new shopping mall. Local authorities decided to raze the dilapidated building because it was a safety hazard. Invading forces razed the entire village during the conflict. The developer plans to raze these shacks and build luxury apartments. It took only a few hours for the heavy machinery to raze the historic site.

english_meaning: It refers to noisy, showy, and confusing activity or display intended to impress or distract people. It denotes a brilliant, flashy, or deceptive technique used in sports or entertainment to bewilder spectators. It means to bedazzle, bewilder, or impress someone through elaborate glamour or dramatic showmanship.
example_sentence: The circus performer dazzled the audience with a burst of razzle dazzle. Politicians often use razzle dazzle to distract voters from the real issues. The team used a bit of razzle dazzle on the field to score the winning goal. Despite all the razzle dazzle of the marketing campaign, the product failed to sell.

english_meaning: To start performing at one’s best or most confident level. The point when someone becomes fully comfortable and effective in what they are doing, achieving their optimal pace or skill. Often used in work, sports, or learning contexts.
synonyms: ["Hit one’s stride","Find one’s rhythm","Get into the groove","Come into one’s own"]
example_sentence: After a few months at the new job, she finally reached her stride and started producing excellent reports. The team struggled at first but reached their stride after the third game. Once he reached his stride in the marathon, he maintained a steady pace until the finish. The writer reached her stride with the second novel, gaining critical acclaim.

english_meaning: Something done or felt in response to an event or situation. A chemical process in which substances change into others. A physical response of the body to a substance or stimulus. Opposition to social or political change.
example_sentence: The public reaction to the new law was mostly positive. A chemical reaction takes place when the two liquids are mixed. She had a severe allergic reaction to the medicine. Forces of reaction resisted every attempt at reform.

english_meaning: To understand the hidden or implied meaning of something that is not stated directly in words. It means to notice the deeper message or true feelings behind what is being said or written.
example_sentence: If you read between the lines, you’ll see that she’s not happy with the decision. The letter doesn’t say it directly, but if you read between the lines, you can tell he’s in trouble. When my boss praised my work, I could read between the lines that he wanted me to take more responsibility. You have to read between the lines to understand the true message of this poem.

english_meaning: To understand someone's hidden thoughts or motives very easily. To be able to predict a person's reactions or feelings without them speaking. To have a deep insight into a person's character or intentions. To perceive exactly what another person is thinking through their behavior.
example_sentence: You can't hide your disappointment because I can read you like a book. My mother could always read me like a book whenever I tried to lie. After years of marriage, he could read his wife like a book. The experienced negotiator could read his opponent like a book during the meeting.

english_meaning: To misunderstand or misinterpret written or spoken information. Misread text. Misinterpret instructions. Misjudge a situation. Read incorrectly. Take meaning the wrong way.
example_sentence: I read the address wrong and went to the wrong house. She read the question wrong, so her answer was incorrect. He read my message wrong and thought I was angry. They read the map wrong and got lost in the city.

english_meaning: To severely reprimand someone for their unacceptable behavior. To issue a stern and final warning to stop a particular course of action. To scold someone angrily and lay down strict rules for future conduct. To strongly express disapproval and threaten consequences if behavior does not improve.
synonyms: ["Give A Severe Reprimand","Scold Bitterly","Tell Off","Haul Over The Coals","Give A Piece Of One's Mind","Reprove Harshly","Take To Task","Dress Down","Give A Scolding","Chastise Severely","Rebuke Sharply"]
antonyms: ["Praise Highly","Commend","Applaud","Compliment","Extol","Flatter","Let Off The Hook","Turn A Blind Eye","Approve Of","Encourage Warmly","Reward"]
example_sentence: The teacher had to read the riot act to the students after they continuously disrupted the class. When he came home hours past his curfew, his parents read the riot act to him. The coach read the riot act to the team following their dismal performance in the first half. If they fail to meet the deadline again, the boss will definitely read the riot act to the whole department.

english_meaning: To sense the mood of people around you. To understand the feelings, mood, or atmosphere of a group of people and behave or speak appropriately. (Being aware of what others are thinking or feeling in a social situation before acting or talking)
synonyms: ["Understand the situation","Sense the mood","Gauge the atmosphere","Perceive feelings","Be observant"]
antonyms: ["Misjudge the mood","Ignore feelings","Be insensitive","Be unaware","Misunderstand the situation"]
example_sentence: He made a joke during the meeting, but it was not the right time; he failed to read the room. Before starting your presentation, try to read the room and see if the audience looks interested. She quickly read the room and changed the topic to avoid making anyone uncomfortable. A good leader can always read the room and respond to the team’s emotions.

english_meaning: To read something that has been written or recorded earlier, often to check for accuracy or to review.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the student to read back the paragraph. Before submitting the report, she read back her notes to ensure nothing was missed. The secretary read back the minutes of the meeting for confirmation. The radio host read back listeners’ messages on air

english_meaning: To study or prepare in order to take an exam, perform a task, or gain knowledge in a specific subject.
example_sentence: He’s reading for his final exams. She’s reading for a degree in medicine. I’m reading for my law test next week. They’re reading for their professional certification.

english_meaning: To verbally convey information by referring to a text, screen, or a written list. Often used when announcing results, reading numbers, or giving instructions directly from a source.
example_sentence: The teacher read off the names of the winners. He read off the numbers from the screen. She read off the temperature readings. The clerk read off the order details.

english_meaning: To examine or check written material carefully by reading it completely. To check for errors, understand content, or review information. It emphasizes the act of reviewing or going through the material rather than just reading casually.
example_sentence: Read over your essay before submitting it. She read over the contract twice. The editor read over the article for errors. He read over the report to ensure accuracy.

english_meaning: To gather information by studying or reading about a topic. To spend time reading or researching about a specific subject, often to prepare for something like an exam, meeting, or discussion. It implies focused study rather than casual reading.
example_sentence: I need to read up on climate change before the workshop. She read up about the company before her interview. We should read up on the latest regulations. He read up on ancient history for his research paper.

english_meaning: To study or research a specific subject thoroughly. To spend time reading or researching in order to learn more about a specific topic. It often implies preparation or self-education.
example_sentence: I need to read up on climate change before the workshop. She read up on ancient Egyptian history for her research project. Before interviewing the candidate, he read up on her previous work. The students were asked to read up on renewable energy sources for

english_meaning: To state something again in a firm and clear way. To confirm one's support, belief, or commitment once more. To strengthen a previous decision or promise by repeating it. To assert again the truth or validity of something.
example_sentence: The president reaffirmed his commitment to peace. Both countries reaffirmed their trade agreement. She reaffirmed her faith after the difficult year. The court reaffirmed the earlier judgment.

english_meaning: Any number that can be found on the number line, including rational and irrational numbers. A number that represents a quantity along a continuous line. Any positive number, negative number, or zero that is not imaginary.
example_sentence: Every rational number is also a real number. Real numbers include both fractions and whole numbers. The equation has no real number solution. Temperature values are usually recorded as real numbers.

english_meaning: The attitude or practice of accepting situations as they are and dealing with them pragmatically. An artistic or literary movement emphasizing accurate depiction of reality. The quality of representing things as they actually are. The philosophical view that physical objects exist independently of perception.
example_sentence: Political realism guides her decisions. The novel is known for its stark realism. His artwork embraces realism over idealism. Realism in literature depicts everyday life accurately.

english_meaning: Representing things in a way that is accurate and true to life. Having a practical and sensible view of situations. Not idealistic or overly optimistic. Achievable and reasonable. Based on facts rather than imagination.
example_sentence: You need to set realistic goals for yourself. The painting is very realistic and detailed. He gave a realistic assessment of the situation. Let's be realistic about what we can achieve this year.

english_meaning: A kingdom or a field or domain of activity or interest. It can refer to a physical territory ruled by a monarch or a metaphorical sphere of influence. Often used to describe a specific area of knowledge or thought.
example_sentence: The king ruled over a vast and prosperous realm. Her research is primarily in the realm of theoretical physics. The story takes place in a mythical realm filled with dragons. Such high-level decisions are beyond the realm of my responsibility.

english_meaning: To take care of (a young person or animal), To raise upright. At the back of something, Back part of something, The space or position at the back
example_sentence: He ​describes how these ​birds rear ​their ​young. It took all the men in the village to rear the frame for the barn, pulling hard at the ropes until all the sides were standing. The kitchen door at the rear of the house. Two policemen at the rear fell out of the formation. The field at the rear of the church.

english_meaning: To appear or become noticeable again, especially when referring to something unpleasant, problematic, or unwanted.
example_sentence: After months of peace, political tension reared its ugly head again. Corruption has reared its ugly head in the department once more. The old conflict reared its ugly head despite several peace talks. His jealousy reared its ugly head when he saw her talking to someone else.

english_meaning: Fair and sensible in judgement. Based on good sense and logic rather than emotion. Not excessive or extreme in amount or price. Average or acceptable in quality or degree. Moderate and logical in nature.
example_sentence: His request for more time to finish the project seemed perfectly reasonable. The hotel offers high quality service at a very reasonable price. It is not reasonable to expect a child to sit still for three hours. The doctor said there is a reasonable chance of a full recovery. We need to reach a reasonable compromise that satisfies both parties.

english_meaning: In a fair, sensible, or moderate way. To an acceptable or fairly likely degree. With good judgment and without excess.
example_sentence: The work can reasonably be completed by Friday. She spoke reasonably during the disagreement. The price is reasonably low for this quality. We can reasonably expect better results next month.

english_meaning: To remove someone's doubts or fears. To restore confidence or belief in something. To say or do something that makes another feel calm and safe. To confirm to someone that everything is all right. To provide comfort through words or actions.
example_sentence: The doctor reassured the patient about his condition. She smiled to reassure her worried child. The manager tried to reassure the staff about their jobs. His calm voice reassured everyone in the room.

english_meaning: A partial refund to someone who has paid too much money for tax, rent, or a utility. A deduction from the amount of money to be paid, often as a discount for prompt payment or bulk buying. To give a discount or reduce the price of something.
example_sentence: The government offered a tax rebate to encourage small business owners. I am still waiting for the mail-in rebate check for my new laptop. The store manager offered a ten percent rebate if we paid the full amount in cash. You may be eligible for a significant rebate on your annual heating bill. The company decided to rebate a portion of the subscription fee due to service outages.

english_meaning: To fight or refuse to obey an authority for example: a Govt, a system, parents etc
example_sentence: I have always been the rebel of the family. He later rebelled against his strict religious upbringing. Mist techniques find something to rebel against.

english_meaning: An act of open or violent resistance against an established government or ruler. A refusal of obedience or order. The action of defying convention, authority, or control in favor of an alternative. A state of insurrection or an organized attempt to overthrow the status quo.
example_sentence: The government suppressed the rebellion with military force. Students staged a rebellion against the new school dress code. History books often depict the peasant rebellion as a turning point for the nation. Her dyed hair was a small act of rebellion against her conservative parents. The soldiers were executed for their part in the failed rebellion.

english_meaning: To spring back after hitting a surface. To recover from illness, shock, loss, or failure. To improve after a difficult period. To respond or react strongly after an action. A bounce back or recovery.
example_sentence: The ball hit the wall and rebounded quickly. After the illness, she rebounded faster than expected. The company rebounded from financial losses within a year. He started a rebound relationship soon after his breakup. The rebound of the ball surprised the player. There was a strong rebound in sales this year.

english_meaning: An act of unkindly refusing a friendly offer, request or suggestion. Treatment that is deliberately unfriendly. To refuse a friendly offer, request or suggestion in an unkind way. To reject or criticize sharply.
example_sentence: Her offer of help was met with a sharp rebuff. They rebuffed her request for help. The company rebuffed the bid. She rebuffed him when he asked her for a date. In a rebuff to the president, Congress voted against the bill. The party suffered a humiliating electoral rebuff in 1945.

english_meaning: To ​speak ​angrily to someone because you ​disapprove of what they have said or done. An expression of sharp disapproval or criticism.
example_sentence: She had rebuked him for drinking too much. The judge publicly rebuked the jury. He hadn’t meant it as a rebuke, but Neil flinched. He was ​publicly rebuked for his ​involvement in the ​scandal

english_meaning: To prove that a statement or accusation is false. To argue against a claim by offering evidence or reasoning. To reply to criticism in order to disprove it. To formally contradict an argument in a debate or court case.
example_sentence: The lawyer rebutted the charges with solid evidence. He wrote an article to rebut the false claims. She rebutted every point her opponent raised. The scientist rebutted the theory using new data.

english_meaning: Stubborn refusal to obey rules or authority. It refers to persistent resistance to control, commands, laws, or accepted norms, especially when cooperation is expected. It often implies deliberate defiance rather than simple disagreement.
example_sentence: The manager struggled to deal with the recalcitrance of the employees who refused to follow safety rules. Government reforms failed due to the recalcitrance of powerful interest groups. His recalcitrance during negotiations delayed the agreement. The court warned the company against continued recalcitrance toward environmental laws.

english_meaning: Stubbornly refusing to obey rules or authority. Difficult to manage or control; resistant to guidance or discipline.
example_sentence: The recalcitrant student refused to do his homework despite repeated warnings. The recalcitrant worker challenged every instruction from his supervisor. The government faced recalcitrant citizens who refused to pay taxes. Her recalcitrant attitude made teamwork very difficult.

english_meaning: To summarize or repeat the main points. To go over something again, especially by giving a short summary of the important ideas.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the student to recapitulate the lesson. Before ending the meeting, she recapitulated the key decisions. He recapitulated the story in just a few sentences. The article recapitulates the main arguments of the research.

english_meaning: To move back or away from a previous position. To gradually become less strong, less visible, or less intense.
example_sentence: The floodwaters slowly receded after the heavy rain stopped. His hairline is beginning to recede as he grows older. The pain in her leg receded after she took some medicine. As the applause receded, the speaker began his lecture.

english_meaning: Willing to listen to or accept new ideas, suggestions, or feelings. Able to receive and respond to signals, impressions, or treatment. Showing interest and openness towards what others say or offer. Relating to the understanding of language rather than its production.
example_sentence: The audience was receptive to her bold new proposal. Young minds are highly receptive to fresh ideas. He is always receptive when colleagues offer advice. Patients who stay receptive to therapy usually recover faster.

english_meaning: The quality of being willing to listen to or accept new ideas and suggestions. Openness to receiving impressions, influences, or information. A readiness to respond favourably to something offered. The state of being able to take in and absorb something.
example_sentence: His receptiveness to criticism helped him improve quickly. The teacher praised the class for its receptiveness to new methods. There was little receptiveness among voters to the proposal. Her receptiveness made the discussion easy and productive.

english_meaning: The willingness or readiness to receive something new, such as information, ideas, or suggestions. The state of being open and responsive to new experiences or influences. The ability or capacity of something to accept or take in external stimuli.
example_sentence: The success of the new project depends largely on the receptivity of the local community. The audience showed a great deal of receptivity to the speaker's innovative concepts. Scientists are testing the receptivity of cells to the new medication. A creative mind requires a high degree of receptivity to sudden inspiration. The government was criticized for its lack of receptivity to public complaints.

english_meaning: A cell or group of cells in the body that receives stimuli and sends signals to the nervous system. A molecule on a cell surface to which a substance such as a hormone or drug can bind. A device or organ that receives signals or impressions from outside. Anything that takes in and responds to a particular stimulus.
example_sentence: Pain receptors in the skin send signals to the brain. The drug blocks a specific receptor in the nervous system. Light receptors in the eye respond to changes in brightness. Researchers identified a new receptor linked to appetite.

english_meaning: The tendency of a convicted criminal to reoffend or return to a habit of criminal behavior after being punished. It refers to the likelihood or rate at which former prisoners commit more crimes and return to prison. The chronic relapse into bad habits or anti-social patterns of conduct.
example_sentence: The high rate of recidivism indicates that the current prison system is not effectively rehabilitating inmates. Programs that provide job training often help reduce recidivism among formerly incarcerated individuals. Legislators are looking for new ways to lower the national recidivism statistics. The study tracked recidivism over a five-year period to see how many released convicts were rearrested.

english_meaning: To respond to someone’s action, feeling, or kindness by giving the same kind of response in return. It is often used for emotions such as love, respect, friendship, help, or cooperation. It can also refer to mutual exchange between two sides.
example_sentence: She smiled at him, but he did not reciprocate the gesture. I helped him many times and he always reciprocated my kindness. True friendship grows when both people reciprocate trust and respect. The two countries agreed to reciprocate trade benefits.

english_meaning: Acting or doing something without thinking or caring about the potential consequences of the action. It describes behavior that is rash, careless, and dangerous to oneself or others. It shows a complete disregard for safety precautions.
example_sentence: His reckless driving eventually resulted in a terrible and costly accident. It is reckless to make large financial investments without doing proper research. The company showed a reckless disregard for the safety of its employees. She deeply regretted her reckless decision to quit her job without a backup plan. Reckless behavior on the mountain can easily endanger the lives of other climbers.

english_meaning: In a way that is careless of the consequences of one's actions. Acting without caution or regard for danger or risk. In a headlong or rash manner that ignores potential harm. Performing an action with total indifference to safety or logic. Behavior that displays a lack of forethought or prudence.
example_sentence: He drove recklessly through the narrow streets of the city. The company spent its budget recklessly on unnecessary luxuries. She recklessly jumped into the water without checking the depth. Investing all your savings in one stock is acting recklessly.

english_meaning: The quality of acting without thinking of the consequences. Careless or dangerous behavior. Lack of caution in actions or decisions. A tendency to take unnecessary risks. Foolish boldness that may cause harm.
example_sentence: His recklessness on the road caused a serious accident. The recklessness of youth often leads to regret. She was punished for her recklessness at work. The company suffered because of the manager's recklessness.

english_meaning: To think, believe, or consider something to be true. To calculate or count. To form an opinion or judgement about something, or to estimate/guess a value. To mean “I think” or “I suppose”. In another sense, it can mean to calculate numbers or totals.
example_sentence: I reckon we should leave early. They reckon the total cost carefully. She reckons he will come tomorrow. They reckon the journey will take two hours. I reckon this plan will work well. She is reckoned as a great teacher.

english_meaning: To plan for a particular situation based on the assumption that it will occur. To count or rely upon something as a certainty. To take something into account when making arrangements for the future. To anticipate an event and prepare for its consequences. To place confidence in a specific outcome happening.
example_sentence: We did not reckon on the weather turning so cold so suddenly. You can reckon on his support during the upcoming board meeting. I had reckoned on finishing the project by Friday but ran into issues. They had to reckon on a large crowd attending the annual festival.

english_meaning: To calculate the total amount or sum of something. To add together various figures to reach a final result. To count the number of items in a group systematically. To evaluate or summarize the total value or cost. To perform a mathematical summation of parts.
example_sentence: The accountant began to reckon up the daily expenses of the office. It took her several minutes to reckon up the final score of the game. He sat down to reckon up how much money he had spent on the trip. Please reckon up the items in the inventory before the store closes.

english_meaning: To deal with a difficult person or a challenging situation. To take someone or something into consideration as a powerful force. To settle accounts or face the consequences of one's actions. To acknowledge the influence or power of an opponent. To confront a reality that cannot be ignored.
example_sentence: He is a formidable opponent that you will have to reckon with. We must reckon with the possibility of a total economic downturn. She had to reckon with her past mistakes before moving forward. The company failed because it did not reckon with its competitors.

english_meaning: The process of calculating or estimating something. A time when past mistakes or misdeeds must be punished or paid for. The settlement of an account or a bill. A person's view or judgment regarding a specific matter. The act of determining a ship's position by calculation.
example_sentence: By my reckoning, we should arrive at the destination in an hour. The day of reckoning for his corrupt activities has finally arrived. The final reckoning of the damages caused by the storm was enormous. According to his reckoning, the company is worth millions of dollars.

english_meaning: A person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people. Someone who stays away from society and prefers to live in isolation or seclusion. A person who withdraws from the world for religious, philosophical, or personal reasons. It can also describe a person who lives in voluntary seclusion from the rest of the world.
example_sentence: He became a recluse after the death of his wife, rarely leaving his small cottage. The billionaire lived as a recluse in his mountain mansion, shielded from the public eye. Many medieval monks chose to live as recluses to focus entirely on their prayers. My neighbor is a total recluse and hardly ever answers the door when visitors come. Despite her fame, she lived a life of a recluse for the last twenty years of her life.

english_meaning: Living apart from society, avoiding the company of other people, and preferring solitude. A person who prefers to stay away from social activities and large groups of people. Such a person usually enjoys privacy, solitude, and a quiet lifestyle. Being reclusive does not necessarily mean being unfriendly; it simply means preferring limited social interaction.
example_sentence: The reclusive writer rarely appeared in public after publishing his famous novel. She lived a reclusive life in a small cottage near the mountains. Although reclusive, he was respected for his wisdom and knowledge. The billionaire became increasingly reclusive as he grew older.

english_meaning: Able to be identified from previous knowledge or experience. Familiar enough to be known. Clearly possessing the typical features of a person, thing, style, or condition. Noticeable as a distinct form or pattern.
example_sentence: Her voice was instantly recognizable. The town is barely recognizable after the rebuilding. The artist developed a recognizable style. The symptoms form a recognizable pattern.

english_meaning: In a way that can be identified or recognized. In a manner that clearly shows familiar or characteristic features. To a noticeable and distinguishable degree.
example_sentence: The building remains recognizably Victorian. Her writing is recognizably her own. The melody is recognizably based on a folk song. The city is modern yet recognizably rooted in its past.

english_meaning: To identify someone or something from having seen or heard them before. To acknowledge the existence, validity, or importance of something. To formally accept or approve. To show official appreciation for someone's work or achievement. To perceive clearly.
example_sentence: I did not recognize him with his new beard. The country was quick to recognize the new government. Teachers must recognize the effort of their students. She recognized the tune as soon as it began.

english_meaning: To move or spring back suddenly, often in horror, fear, or disgust. The backward movement or kick of a gun when it is fired. To shrink away from an idea or situation because it is unpleasant or alarming. The physical reaction of an object recoiling after an impact or pressure.
example_sentence: She felt herself recoil in horror at the sight of the spider. The rifle had a powerful recoil that bruised his shoulder. Even the most hardened soldiers would recoil from such a violent scene. He seemed to recoil at the very suggestion of working for his rival. The spring will recoil once the pressure is released.

english_meaning: To begin again after stopping. To restart or resume an activity. To start once more.
example_sentence: Classes will recommence on Monday. Work recommenced after the storm. The meeting recommenced after lunch. They waited for the music to recommence.

english_meaning: To suggest that someone should choose, use, or do something. To speak favorably about a person or thing. To advise as suitable or beneficial.
example_sentence: I recommend this book to beginners. The doctor recommended more rest. She recommended him for the job. Experts recommend saving a little money every month.

english_meaning: A suggestion or piece of advice. A formal statement supporting someone or something. The act of recommending.
example_sentence: The committee made a recommendation. She wrote a recommendation for her student. I followed the doctor's recommendation. The report includes several recommendations.

english_meaning: Payment or reward for effort, loss, or injury. Compensation for damage or service. To repay or make amends.
example_sentence: The workers received recompense for overtime. No money could recompense her for the loss. The court ordered recompense for damages. He hoped kindness would be recompensed.

english_meaning: To restore friendly relations between people after a disagreement. To make two opposing ideas, beliefs, or facts agree or be compatible. To accept something unpleasant that cannot be changed. To settle a quarrel or dispute. To make financial accounts or records consistent.
example_sentence: The couple managed to reconcile after months of separation. It is difficult to reconcile his words with his actions. She had to reconcile herself to the loss of her job. The accountant reconciled the bank statement with the company records. Religion and science can sometimes be hard to reconcile.

english_meaning: The act of restoring friendly relations after a disagreement. The process of bringing people, groups, or ideas back into agreement after conflict, misunderstanding, or hostility
example_sentence: The reconciliation between the two countries took several years of dialogue. Family reconciliation helped heal old emotional wounds. Truth and reconciliation are essential after a long period of conflict. The manager encouraged reconciliation between the coworkers to improve teamwork.

english_meaning: To form something again or anew. To reconstruct the structure or composite parts of an organization or group. To restore a dried or condensed substance to its original liquid state by adding water or another liquid.
example_sentence: The committee was dissolved last year but has now been reconstituted with new members. You can reconstitute the dried soup by adding two cups of boiling water. Scientists are trying to reconstitute the original chemical structure of the ancient artifact. After the merger, the company had to reconstitute its entire board of directors. The chef used a small amount of wine to reconstitute the reduction sauce.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or involving the process of rebuilding or restoration. Specifically relating to surgery intended to restore the function or appearance of body parts. Serving to rebuild something after it has been damaged or destroyed. Involving the mental process of organizing and interpreting past memories rather than just recalling them. Characterized by an effort to reform or re-establish a previous system or structure.
example_sentence: The patient underwent reconstructive surgery to repair the damage from the accident. Historians use various documents for the reconstructive analysis of ancient civilizations. Memory is often a reconstructive process rather than a literal recording of events. The government announced a reconstructive plan to stabilize the war-torn region's infrastructure.

english_meaning: To tell somebody about something, especially something that you have experienced.
example_sentence: She was asked to recount the details of the conversation to the court. They recounted what had happened during those years.

english_meaning: To enlist someone in the armed forces or to enroll someone as a member or worker in an organization. It also refers to a person who has newly joined a group or company. The process involves finding, screening, and hiring potential candidates.
example_sentence: The army is looking to recruit more soldiers this year. The company plans to recruit several new software engineers. He was a promising young recruit in the police force. They are trying to recruit volunteers for the local charity event.

english_meaning: The process of finding and hiring new people for a job or organisation. The act of enlisting new members into a group, army or cause. In biology, the addition of new individuals to a population. The activity or industry concerned with employing staff.
example_sentence: The company has started the recruitment of new engineers. Recruitment into the police force has increased this year. She works in recruitment for a large bank. Poor recruitment can weaken any organisation.

english_meaning: A four-sided flat shape with four right angles and opposite sides equal. A quadrilateral whose angles are all 90 degrees. A common geometric figure whose area equals length multiplied by width. Any object or region shaped like an oblong.
example_sentence: The garden is laid out in a perfect rectangle. Calculate the area of the rectangle in square metres. He drew a rectangle around the important text. A rectangle has two pairs of equal sides.

english_meaning: Having the shape of a rectangle. Having four straight sides with four right angles. Shaped like a box or oblong.
example_sentence: The rectangular table fit perfectly in the dining room. She drew a rectangular box on the paper. The football field is rectangular in shape. He kept his books in a rectangular shelf.

english_meaning: Able to be corrected or put right. Capable of being fixed, repaired, or improved. Possible to remedy or set right.
example_sentence: The mistake was easily rectifiable with a simple correction. The engineer assured us that the fault was rectifiable. The financial errors were rectifiable before the deadline. The damage to the car was rectifiable at a small cost.

english_meaning: The act of correcting something that is wrong. The process of making right. Adjustment or improvement of a fault. Amendment of an error or mistake. Correction of an inaccuracy or defect.
example_sentence: The rectification of the error took several days. He demanded the rectification of the injustice. Rectification of the accounts is necessary before the audit. The company promised the quick rectification of faults.

english_meaning: To put something right that is wrong. To correct an error or a faulty situation. To adjust or make an amendment to a process or document. In electronics, to convert alternating current into direct current.
example_sentence: The company promised to rectify the error in my billing statement immediately. We must take steps to rectify the situation before it gets out of hand. The technician was called in to rectify the fault in the electrical wiring. It is important to rectify any mistakes in the legal document before signing it. A diode is used to rectify the alternating current to direct current.

english_meaning: Straight, direct, or moving in a straight line. Formed by straight lines. Relating to straight lines or right angles. Having a very direct or rigid way of thinking.
example_sentence: The rectilinear design of the building gave it a modern look. The ants moved in a rectilinear path across the floor. The artist used rectilinear shapes in his painting. The garden had rectilinear flower beds.

english_meaning: Moral correctness and honesty in behavior or thinking. The quality of being upright, virtuous, and guided by strong moral principles. Straightness or correctness of judgment and conduct.
example_sentence: He was admired for his moral rectitude throughout his career. The judge handled the case with complete rectitude and fairness. Her rectitude earned her the trust of the entire community. We need leaders who act with rectitude in difficult times.

english_meaning: An official who leads or manages an institution, typically a university, college, or parish. In universities, the rector often serves as the head or chief administrator. In religious contexts, a rector is the priest in charge of a parish.
example_sentence: The rector of the university gave a speech at the convocation. Our parish rector organized a charity event. As rector, she oversees all academic programs. The rector welcomed the new students personally.

english_meaning: The final straight section of the large intestine ending at the anus. The part of the bowel where stool is stored before it is passed. The chamber that signals the need for a bowel movement when it fills.
example_sentence: The rectum stores waste before it leaves the body. The rectum is the last part of the large intestine. The doctor performed a simple examination of the rectum. Bleeding from the rectum should never be ignored.

english_meaning: The long, flat muscle that runs vertically down the front of the abdomen. The muscle that bends the trunk forward and supports the abdominal wall. The muscle divided by tendinous bands, giving the appearance often called a six-pack. A core muscle that helps stabilise the spine and pelvis.
example_sentence: Sit-ups mainly work the rectus abdominis. The rectus abdominis runs from the ribs down to the pelvis. A strong rectus abdominis helps protect the lower back. The visible six-pack is simply a well-defined rectus abdominis.

english_meaning: Lying down or reclining. Leaning backward in a position of rest. Describing a bicycle ridden from a laid-back seated position. A recumbent bicycle or tricycle.
example_sentence: He spent the afternoon in a recumbent position on the sofa. The statue depicts a recumbent figure draped in traditional robes. She prefers riding a recumbent bicycle for better back support. The patient remained recumbent while the doctors performed the examination.

english_meaning: To recover from illness or exertion. To regain something lost, such as health, strength, or money. To get back a sum of money spent or lost.
example_sentence: It took him several weeks to recuperate after the major surgery. The athlete went to the spa to recuperate from the grueling marathon. The company is trying to recuperate its losses through new investments. You need to rest properly to recuperate your energy for the next task.

english_meaning: The process of recovering from an illness or injury. The recovery of health or strength after exertion. The act of regaining something lost, like financial assets.
example_sentence: Her recuperation was slow but steady after the accident. The mountain air is said to be excellent for recuperation. The bank focused on the recuperation of the defaulted loans. A period of recuperation is essential after such a stressful ordeal.

english_meaning: Helping a person recover health, strength, or energy. Relating to the process of recovery after illness, injury, exhaustion, or loss. Restorative or healing in effect.
example_sentence: The patient was prescribed a recuperative diet of soups and juices. She took a recuperative holiday in the countryside to clear her mind. The spa offers various recuperative treatments for tired muscles. The quiet environment had a recuperative effect on his mental state.

english_meaning: To happen again, especially repeatedly or after an interval. To come back into one's mind or thoughts. Of a symptom or illness, to return after seeming to improve. In mathematics, of digits, to repeat endlessly in a decimal.
example_sentence: The same problem recurs every winter. That thought recurred to him during the night. The fever recurred after two weeks. In this fraction the digit three recurs endlessly.

english_meaning: The fact of happening again, especially of something unwanted. A repeated occurrence of an event, illness or problem. The return of a disease after a period of improvement.
example_sentence: Doctors are trying to prevent a recurrence of the infection. There has been a recurrence of violence in the area. Regular checkups reduce the risk of recurrence. The recurrence of these errors is worrying.

english_meaning: Occurring often or repeatedly. It describes something that happens again and again at intervals. Often used in medical or financial contexts to describe patterns that persist over time.
example_sentence: She suffers from recurrent headaches that last for days. The company faced recurrent financial problems throughout the year. The film explores the recurrent theme of lost love. He had a recurrent dream about flying over the ocean.

english_meaning: The repeated application of a recursive procedure or definition. In mathematics and computer science, it is a method where the solution to a problem depends on solutions to smaller instances of the same problem. It involves a function calling itself within its own definition.
example_sentence: The programmer used recursion to solve the complex sorting algorithm. The fractal pattern is a perfect visual representation of recursion. Understanding recursion is fundamental to mastering computer science. The dictionary definition was a joke about recursion, sending the reader back to the same word.

english_meaning: It refers to excessive bureaucracy or adherence to rules and formalities, especially in public business. It describes the rigid application of regulations that prevents decision-making or action. It symbolizes the tedious and time-consuming official procedures required to get something done. It implies unnecessary paperwork and administrative delays.
example_sentence: We had to deal with a lot of red tape to get our business license approved. The new government promised to cut through the red tape hindering local entrepreneurs. Sometimes the hospital's red tape prevents patients from getting immediate care. He frustratedly complained about the endless red tape involved in applying for a visa.

english_meaning: To become very red due to embarrassment. A physical reaction when someone feels shy or embarrassed.
example_sentence: She turned as red as a beetroot after the compliment. He was red as a beetroot when everyone noticed him. I went red as a beetroot after my mistake. The child turned red as a beetroot when praised.

english_meaning: A cell in the blood that carries oxygen from the lungs to body tissues. A disc-shaped blood cell containing the pigment haemoglobin. The most numerous type of blood cell, responsible for the red colour of blood. A cell that also helps carry carbon dioxide back to the lungs for removal.
example_sentence: Red blood cells carry oxygen to every tissue in the body. A low count of red blood cells can cause tiredness and weakness. Red blood cells are produced in the bone marrow. Haemoglobin gives red blood cells their colour.

english_meaning: To catch someone in the act of doing something wrong, especially a crime or misdeed. Catching someone while committing the offense, not after it.
synonyms: ["Caught in act","Caught on the spot","Caught during the crime"]
example_sentence: The police caught the thief red-handed while he was stealing a car. She was caught red-handed cheating during the exam. The manager caught the employee red-handed taking money from the cash drawer. He was caught red-handed lying to his parents about his marks.

english_meaning: Something that misleads or distracts from the main issue. To divert attention away from the real issue or problem. It is often used in arguments, mysteries, or debates to confuse or mislead people.
example_sentence: The argument about cost was a red herring. That clue was just a red herring. Politicians often use red herrings to confuse people. Don’t be misled by red herrings in the discussion.

english_meaning: A very special, joyful, or memorable day, one that stands out from ordinary days because something important, happy, or historic happened. important or festive day.
example_sentence: Graduation day was a red-letter day in my life. The launch of our new project will be a red-letter day for the whole team. Winning the championship was truly a red-letter day for the school. Their wedding anniversary is always a red-letter day for the family.

english_meaning: To edit or revise text for clarity or publication. To black out classified sections of a document. To bring together or compile written material into final form.
example_sentence: The lawyer redacted the client’s personal details before submitting the report. Several names were redacted from the government file. The journalist had to redact sensitive information before publishing the article. The company redacted financial data to protect trade secrets.

english_meaning: The act of editing or censoring text by removing or obscuring sensitive or confidential information. The process of preparing a document for publication by revising its content. A version of a text produced through editing or compilation.
example_sentence: The redaction of the classified document hid the informants' names. Journalists criticized the heavy redaction in the government report. The lawyer requested redaction of sensitive financial details. Redaction software automatically conceals personal information in scanned files.

english_meaning: Specifically referring to something that has more of the color red than something else. Appearing more crimson, scarlet, or flushed in hue compared to a previous state or another object. Often describes a more intense or deeper shade of red. It can also describe a person's complexion becoming more intensely pink or ruby due to embarrassment, anger, or physical exertion.
example_sentence: The sunset tonight is even redder than the one we saw yesterday. Her face grew redder as she realized everyone was staring at her. This variety of apple is much redder than the sour green ones. After the long hike in the sun, his neck became redder by the minute. He chose the redder of the two fabrics to match the curtains.

english_meaning: To decorate a room, building, or space again, usually with new paint, furnishings, or design. To refresh or update the appearance of an interior. To change decorative features without necessarily altering the structure.
example_sentence: They decided to redecorate the living room before the holidays. She redecorated her office with fresh paint and new furniture. We plan to redecorate the house before selling it. He redecorated his bedroom to reflect his new style.

english_meaning: The act or process of decorating a room, building, or space again. The result of updating or refreshing an interior design. A renewal of appearance through new colors, furnishings, materials, or arrangement.
example_sentence: The redecoration of the hotel lobby took several weeks. Her plans for redecoration included new curtains and wallpaper. The redecoration transformed the old office into a modern workspace. They funded the redecoration of the community hall.

english_meaning: To do what is required by the terms of. To free from captivity or punishment by paying a price. To get something back. To carry out a promise or pay back a debt. To pay back a loan. To make better in behavior or character.
example_sentence:
The excellent acting wasn't enough to redeem a weak plot. In an attempt to redeem the situation, Jed offered to help sell tickets.
He was a sinner, redeemed by the grace of God. He was an hour late, but he redeemed himself in her eyes by giving her a huge bunch of flowers.

english_meaning: Able to be exchanged for goods, services, money, or something else of value. Capable of being saved, reformed, or restored to a better state. Able to be repaid, bought back, or discharged at a stated time. Capable of being compensated for by a positive quality or action.
example_sentence: These coupons are redeemable at any branch. He believed that even serious offenders could be redeemable. The bond is redeemable after five years. The flaws are redeemable because the story remains compelling.

english_meaning: Regained possession of something in exchange for payment. Fulfilled a pledge, promise, or obligation. Saved from a state of sin, error, or evil. Compensated for the faults or bad aspects of something. Exchanged a voucher or coupon for goods or currency.
example_sentence: He felt entirely redeemed after finishing the community service he was assigned. The voucher can be redeemed at any participating retail outlet. She redeemed her reputation by working hard to correct her previous mistakes. The hero redeemed himself in the final act by saving the village. He finally redeemed the watch he had pawned months ago.

english_meaning: A person who saves someone or something from harm, failure, sin, or evil. A savior or liberator, especially a divine figure in religious belief. A person who buys back, reclaims, or discharges something pledged or owed.
example_sentence: Christians refer to Jesus Christ as the Redeemer. The hero was seen as the redeemer of the oppressed village. He hoped to become the redeemer of his family's lost honor. The novel's protagonist acts as a redeemer for his troubled community.

english_meaning: The act of being saved, corrected, or brought back to a good state. The act of saving or being saved from sin, error, or evil. It also means making up for a mistake, regaining respect, or fulfilling a promise or obligation. In finance, it means reclaiming or paying off something such as a loan or bond.
example_sentence: He worked hard to earn redemption after his mistakes. The charity program gave him a chance for redemption. Redemption of the loan took several years. Her apology was a step toward redemption.

english_meaning: Bringing improvement, recovery, or saving from fault or suffering. Something that helps to correct a mistake, improve a bad situation, or save someone from guilt, harm, or failure. It often relates to moral, emotional, or spiritual recovery.
example_sentence: His apology had a redemptive effect on their friendship. The charity work gave her life a redemptive purpose. The film tells a redemptive story of forgiveness and change. Helping others can be a redemptive experience after failure.

english_meaning: Extremely silly, stupid, or unreasonable and deserving to be laughed at. Something that is far-fetched or beyond the limits of common sense. Describing a situation that is nonsensical or preposterous.
example_sentence: It is absolutely ridiculous to suggest that she would steal the money. He looked ridiculous in that oversized clown costume. The price they are asking for this old car is ridiculous. I found the entire situation quite ridiculous and started laughing. It is ridiculous that we have to wait three hours for a bus.

english_meaning: To make fun of someone or something in a cruel or harsh way. To represent as being ridiculous or deserving of contemptuous laughter. To mock or deride an idea, person, or situation to make them seem foolish. To subject someone to ridicule or irony.
example_sentence: It is unkind to ridicule someone just because they have different beliefs. The director's new film was ridiculed by critics for its poor dialogue. She was afraid that her colleagues would ridicule her suggestion during the meeting. He ridiculed the idea that the earth might be flat. They continued to ridicule his efforts despite his obvious hard work.

english_meaning: Deserving or inviting derision or mockery. Something that is absurd, preposterous, or completely unreasonable. Often used to describe situations that are so silly or foolish that they are hard to believe.
example_sentence: It is absolutely ridiculous to wait in line for six hours for a cup of coffee. She looked ridiculous in that oversized clown costume. The price they are asking for this old car is ridiculous. He made a ridiculous suggestion that we should walk home in the pouring rain.

english_meaning: To distribute something again or in a different way. To change the allocation of resources or wealth.
example_sentence: The government plans to redistribute the land to the peasants. We need to redistribute the workload among the staff. The tax system aims to redistribute wealth from the rich to the poor. The cards were shuffled and redistributed to the players.

english_meaning: To do something again, usually to correct, improve, or replace the previous result. To perform a task, activity, or piece of work again because the first attempt was incorrect, incomplete, unsatisfactory, outdated, or needs improvement. It can also mean to renovate, redesign, or recreate something.
example_sentence: I had to redo my homework because I made several mistakes. The designer decided to redo the company logo with a modern look. Please redo this report before submitting it to the manager. They plan to redo the kitchen during the summer vacation.

english_meaning: To set right, remedy, or rectify a wrong, injustice, or grievance. To make amends or provide compensation for harm, loss, or damage caused to someone. As a noun, it means the act of correcting a wrong or the compensation or remedy itself given for an injury or injustice. It is often used in legal, moral, or social contexts where fairness needs to be restored.
example_sentence: The victims demanded redress for the losses they had suffered. The court ordered the company to redress the damage caused to the environment. Citizens have the right to seek redress against unlawful actions of officials. The new law was passed to redress historical injustices. She wrote to the manager hoping to redress her complaint.

english_meaning: To make a situation fair or equal again after it has been unfair. To correct an imbalance or injustice between people or groups. To restore equality where one side has had an unfair advantage or disadvantage.
example_sentence: The new law aims to redress the balance between employers and workers. Scholarships were introduced to redress the balance for poorer students. The committee took steps to redress the balance of power in the organization. More funding is needed to redress the balance between rich and poor regions.

english_meaning: To make something smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance. To bring someone or something to a lower or weaker state or condition. To change something into a simpler or different form. To lessen the price of something. To lose weight by dieting. In chemistry, to remove oxygen from or add electrons to a substance. To boil a liquid so that it becomes thicker and more concentrated.
example_sentence: The new measures aim to reduce traffic in the city center. Regular exercise can reduce the risk of heart disease. The shop decided to reduce prices before the holidays. She is trying to reduce her sugar intake. Heat the sauce gently to reduce it until thick.

english_meaning: To bring someone or something to a particular state or condition, often a worse one. To change something into a simpler, smaller, or different form. To force into a lower rank, level, or status.
synonyms: ["Bring to","Change into","Turn into","Degrade to","Lower to","Transform into","Convert to"]
example_sentence: The fire reduced the house to ashes. Poverty reduced him to begging on the streets. The problem can be reduced to a simple equation. The defeat reduced the team to tears.

english_meaning: Capable of being reduced, made smaller, or simplified. Able to be brought to a lower or simpler state. In mathematics, capable of being expressed in a simpler form or divided by a common factor.
example_sentence: The costs are easily reducible with better planning. The fraction is reducible to its simplest form. Many diseases are reducible through vaccination. The complex system is reducible to a few key principles.

english_meaning: A Latin phrase meaning "reduction to the absurd". A method of disproving a statement or argument by showing that it logically leads to a ridiculous or impossible conclusion. An argument form that demonstrates a proposition is false because its consequences are absurd.
synonyms: ["Reduction to the absurd","Proof by contradiction","Argumentum ad absurdum","Disproof by absurdity"]
example_sentence: The lawyer used reductio ad absurdum to dismantle the witness's claim. By reductio ad absurdum, if everyone lied, no statement could ever be believed. The professor demonstrated the fallacy through reductio ad absurdum. Reductio ad absurdum is a powerful tool in mathematical proof.

english_meaning: The action of making something smaller or less in amount, degree, or size. A decrease in price. The process of concentrating a liquid by boiling. A smaller copy of a picture or map. An act of reducing or being reduced.
example_sentence: The shop announced a big reduction on winter clothes. There has been a sharp reduction in air pollution. The chef prepared a rich reduction of tomato and wine. A reduction of the original map was printed on the pamphlet.

english_meaning: The practice of explaining complex things by reducing them to simpler or more basic parts. An approach that analyzes systems by breaking them down into their components. The tendency to oversimplify complicated issues or ideas.
example_sentence: Critics accused the theory of crude reductionism. Reductionism helps scientists understand the building blocks of matter. The article warns against reductionism in studying human behavior. Some philosophers reject reductionism as an incomplete worldview.

english_meaning: The state of being excessive, unnecessary, or more than what is needed. The condition where something is repeated or present in greater quantity than required. It often describes unnecessary repetition in language, writing, ideas, or objects. It can also refer to surplus or overflow of something.
example_sentence: The report contains some redundance that makes it longer than necessary. Good writing avoids redundance and keeps ideas clear and direct. The teacher asked the student to remove redundance from the essay. The speech lost its impact because of redundance in the arguments.

english_meaning: A situation where something is repeated, excessive, or not required. A worker losing a job because the position is no longer needed. In technology or systems, it may also mean extra components added to increase reliability.
example_sentence: The editor removed several sentences because they created redundancy in the paragraph. Many workers faced redundancy when the company automated its production line. The aircraft system includes redundancy to ensure safety if one component fails. Good writing avoids redundancy and keeps ideas clear and concise.

english_meaning: Something that is unnecessary, extra, or not needed. Describes a word, idea, worker, or thing that is no longer useful, needed, or required because there is too much of it or it repeats what is already present.
example_sentence: The report contained several redundant sentences that repeated the same idea. Many workers became redundant after the company installed automated machines. Adding more details here would be redundant because the point is already clear. The editor removed redundant words to make the paragraph concise.

english_meaning: In a repetitive or unnecessary way. It describes something said or written again even though the information is already clear. It can also refer to something done with extra duplication or excess beyond what is needed.
example_sentence: Data are redundantly stored in multiple different locations. The report was written redundantly, repeating the same facts in several paragraphs. He explained the rule redundantly, even though everyone already understood it. Some speakers talk redundantly when they are nervous. The instructions were redundantly detailed and made the process harder to follow.

english_meaning: A tall, hollow-stemmed plant of the grass family that grows in water or on marshy ground. A piece of thin cane or metal, which is vibrated by a current of air to produce the sound of certain musical instruments such as the clarinet or saxophone. A person who is weak or easily influenced by others. A small piece of cane or metal in a loom used to separate the threads of a warp.
example_sentence: The marshes were thick with tall reeds that swayed in the wind. The saxophonist needed to replace the worn reed before the concert. He was considered a broken reed when his support was most needed during the crisis. Many traditional baskets are woven from dried reeds found along the riverbanks.

english_meaning: A ridge of rock, coral, or sand lying near the surface of the sea. A coral formation that provides habitat for marine life. A vein or seam of ore in mining, especially gold-bearing rock. A part of a sail that can be rolled or folded to reduce its area. To reduce the area of a sail by rolling or folding part of it.
example_sentence: The ship struck a hidden reef near the shore. Divers explored the colourful coral reef at dawn. Miners followed the gold reef deep underground. The crew had to reef the sails as the storm approached.

english_meaning: To give off a strong and unpleasant smell. A strong offensive smell or stench. To suggest something unpleasant or suspicious very strongly. Smoke or vapour, especially in older usage.
example_sentence: The whole kitchen reeked of burnt oil. A terrible reek rose from the neglected drain. The entire arrangement reeks of favouritism. The reek of woodsmoke hung over the village at dusk.

english_meaning: To lose balance or feel dizzy. To stagger, sway, or spin, often due to shock, surprise, injury, or intoxication. A round object used to wind rope, film, thread, or fishing line. Can also refer to a lively dance or sequence of events.
example_sentence: He reeled after hearing the shocking news. She reeled from the punch. He bought a new fishing reel. The movie reel was damaged.

english_meaning: To mention or speak about someone or something. To direct someone or something to another person, place, or authority for help, information, or a decision. To look at a book, note, or source in order to get information. To describe or relate to something in particular. To hand over a matter to an official body for consideration.
example_sentence: Please refer to page ten for the full details. The doctor decided to refer him to a specialist. She did not refer to the argument again. The committee will refer the matter to the board.

english_meaning: To mention or look again at something that was said, written, or decided earlier. To send a matter back to a person or group for further discussion or a fresh decision. To relate to something that happened in the past. To check an earlier source again in order to confirm information.
example_sentence: Let me refer back to the point I made earlier. The chairman referred the proposal back to the committee. She kept referring back to her childhood in the interview. Please refer back to chapter two for the definitions.

english_meaning: To send a person to another individual or place for expert help, treatment, or advice. To direct someone to a source of information. To pass a person's case on to a specialist or higher authority. To recommend someone to another person or organisation.
example_sentence: My doctor referred me to a heart specialist. The teacher referred the student to the school counsellor. He referred us to the manual for further instructions. The agency referred her to a local employer.

english_meaning: To send a matter, case, or question to a person or body that has the authority to deal with it. To pass a decision on to a higher level for consideration. To submit an issue formally for judgement or discussion. To hand a problem over to an expert or official group.
example_sentence: The council referred the dispute to an independent panel. She referred the complaint to her supervisor. The case was referred to the high court. They referred the design question to the engineers.

english_meaning: To mention or speak about someone or something. To look at something such as a book, note, or website in order to get information. To describe or apply to a particular person or thing. To use a name or word for someone or something. To turn to a source or authority for guidance.
example_sentence: He referred to his notes during the presentation. The report refers to several recent studies. Who exactly are you referring to? This rule refers only to full-time employees.

english_meaning: To call someone or something by a particular name, title, or description. To use a specific word or phrase when speaking about a person or thing. To describe someone or something in a certain way. To be commonly known by a certain name.
example_sentence: The students always referred to him as Sir. This period is often referred to as the golden age. She prefers to be referred to as a writer, not a poet. Locals refer to the building as the old mill.

english_meaning: A direct vote in which all the eligible people of a country or region are asked to decide on a single political question. A general vote by the electorate on an important issue of public policy, such as a constitutional change. The process of putting a proposed law or decision to the public for approval or rejection. Any occasion on which people are given the chance to express their opinion on a particular matter. An informal test of public opinion about a person, policy, or government.
example_sentence: The government held a referendum on the new constitution. Voters rejected the proposal in a national referendum. A referendum will decide whether the region becomes independent. Many people treated the local election as a referendum on the mayor's performance.

english_meaning: The act of sending someone to another person or place for treatment, information, or help. A recommendation or introductory message that connects one person to another. A person who has been sent to a professional or service for specialized care. The process of directing a patient to a specialist or a consultant by a general practitioner.
example_sentence: The doctor gave me a referral to see a cardiologist for further heart tests. Many companies offer a bonus to employees for a successful job referral. You cannot get an appointment with this specialist without a formal referral letter. The social worker made a referral to the local housing agency to help the family. Our business has grown significantly through word-of-mouth referrals from satisfied clients.

english_meaning: Describing a substance that has been purified or processed to remove impurities. Characterizing a person who has elegant manners, sophisticated taste, and high social standards. Referring to something that has been improved or made more precise through small changes over time. Exhibiting a polished or cultured appearance or behavior.
example_sentence: The sugar is refined in a large factory before being packaged for sale. She has very refined taste in classical music and fine art. The engineers used a refined technique to measure the structural integrity of the bridge. His refined manners made him stand out at the formal gala. After years of practice, his playing style became much more refined.

english_meaning: To throw back heat, light, or sound without absorbing it. To show an image of something in a mirror or shiny surface. To embody or represent something accurately in a particular way. To think deeply or carefully about a subject or past event. To bring about a good or bad impression of someone or something.
example_sentence: The shiny surface will reflect the sunlight perfectly. Her artwork reflects her deep love for nature. He needed time to reflect on his past mistakes. The drop in sales reflects a lack of consumer confidence.

english_meaning: The throwing back of light, heat, or sound by a surface. Careful or serious thought or consideration. An image seen in a mirror or other reflective surface. Something that is a consequence or sign of something else.
example_sentence: The reflection of the mountains in the still lake was breathtaking in the early morning light. She spent a great deal of time in quiet reflection before making her final decision. The teacher encouraged the students to write a reflection on what they had learned. The poor results were a reflection of the lack of preparation by the entire team. He could see his own reflection clearly in the polished surface of the trophy.

english_meaning: An automatic and involuntary response to a stimulus. A quick reaction that happens without conscious thought. Done without thinking; automatic. Light, heat, or sound thrown back from a surface.
example_sentence: The doctor tested his knee reflex with a small hammer. Goalkeepers need lightning-fast reflexes. Blinking is a natural reflex. Her reflex action saved the child from falling.

english_meaning: An angle that measures more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees. The larger angle formed on the outer side of two rays. An angle greater than a straight angle. A geometric term used when measuring the outer turn between two lines.
example_sentence: A reflex angle is always greater than a straight angle. The students calculated the reflex angle as 280 degrees. Subtract the given angle from 360 to find the reflex angle. The diagram highlights the reflex angle in red.

english_meaning: Thought or careful consideration: Deep or serious thinking about something. Contemplation: The process of considering an idea, experience, or situation carefully. Careful thinking about your own actions, feelings, or experiences. An image produced when light from an object is reflected by a mirror or another surface. The appearance of something in water, glass, metal, or another reflective surface. The process by which light, sound, heat, or another wave is sent back after striking a surface. Something that shows or represents the nature or qualities of something else. Something that reveals the state, character, or influence of a person, group, or society. A serious thought or observation about an experience or subject. Thinking carefully about something that has already happened in order to understand or learn from it. The transformation of a figure into its mirror image across a line or plane. The change in direction of a wave when it encounters a surface and returns into the original medium.
example_sentence: After some reflexion, she realized that she had made the wrong decision. He saw his reflexion in the calm water of the lake. The reflexion of sunlight from the glass was very bright. The teacher encouraged students to spend time in reflexion after the activity.

english_meaning: Relating to or produced as an automatic reaction. In grammar, referring back to the subject of the sentence. A pronoun or verb form that reflects the action back on the doer. In mathematics, describing a relation in which every element relates to itself.
example_sentence: The word 'himself' is a reflexive pronoun. Her reflexive response was to step back. Reflexive verbs are common in French. Equality is a reflexive relation in mathematics.

english_meaning: A trained therapist who practises reflexology. A person who applies pressure to points on the feet, hands, or ears to promote relaxation. A complementary-therapy practitioner who believes body areas map to reflex points. A specialist offering reflexology treatments to clients.
example_sentence: The reflexologist worked gently on the soles of her feet. He booked an appointment with a qualified reflexologist. A good reflexologist explains the treatment beforehand. She trained as a reflexologist after leaving nursing.

english_meaning: A complementary therapy in which pressure is applied to specific points on the feet, hands, or ears. A treatment based on the belief that these points correspond to organs and systems of the body. A form of massage used to relieve tension and encourage relaxation. The study and practice of reflex points and their supposed effects on health.
example_sentence: She tried reflexology to relieve her chronic back pain. Reflexology is often used alongside conventional treatment. The clinic offers reflexology every Thursday. Many patients find reflexology deeply relaxing.

english_meaning: To make a stranded or sunken vessel float again. To lift a grounded ship off the seabed or sandbank. To restore something to a floating position. Figuratively, to revive a failing project or business.
example_sentence: Tugs worked all night to refloat the cargo ship. The crew managed to refloat the boat at high tide. Engineers used airbags to refloat the vessel. The government tried to refloat the struggling airline.

english_meaning: A flowing back or return flow of a liquid. The backward flow of body fluids, such as the movement of stomach acid back into the esophagus. A process in chemistry where a liquid is boiled and the vapors are condensed to liquid and returned to the system.
example_sentence: He suffered from acid reflux after eating the spicy meal. The chemist set up a reflux condenser for the long experiment. The ocean tide has a natural flow and reflux. Chronic reflux can cause damage to the lining of the throat.

english_meaning: To improve something by removing faults or correcting mistakes. Making changes to improve a system, law, organization, or behavior by correcting what is wrong or unfair. It can refer to social, political, educational, or personal improvement.
example_sentence: The government plans to reform the education system. He worked hard to reform his bad habits. Social reform is necessary for a better society. The new law aims to reform the justice system.

english_meaning: The process by which a wave of light or sound is deflected when it passes obliquely from one medium to another of different density. The bending of light as it passes through water, glass, or another transparent medium. A fundamental phenomenon studied in optics and physics.
example_sentence: Refraction causes a straw placed in a glass of water to appear bent at the surface. The phenomenon of refraction is responsible for the formation of rainbows in the sky. Lenses in glasses and cameras work by carefully controlling the refraction of light. The physicist explained the principles of refraction to her first-year students. Refraction of sound waves explains why sounds seem to travel differently in hot and cold air.

english_meaning: To stop yourself from doing something. To consciously avoid or hold oneself back from doing something, especially something tempting or habitual. To pause deliberately. A line or group of lines that is repeated regularly in a poem or song.
example_sentence: She tried to refrain from laughing during the serious meeting. Please refrain from using your phone in the classroom. He could not refrain from expressing his opinion. The song’s refrain was catchy and easy to remember.

english_meaning: To give new strength or energy to someone or something. To update or reload something, especially a webpage or display. To remind someone of something or bring it back to their memory. To replenish or restore something to its original condition.
example_sentence: She stepped outside for a few minutes to refresh herself before continuing the long meeting. He pressed the button to refresh the page and the latest results appeared immediately.
