english_meaning: A non-specific medical term used to describe any disease or painful condition of the joints, muscles, or fibrous tissue. It is characterized by inflammation, stiffness, and pain in the affected areas. It commonly refers to forms of arthritis and autoimmune conditions.
example_sentence: The cold, damp weather always causes a sharp flare-up of his rheumatism. My grandmother takes special medication daily to cope with her rheumatism. Rheumatism makes his joints overly stiff and remarkably painful in the mornings. Exercise and physical therapy greatly help manage the symptoms of rheumatism. He wore thick woolen clothing to stop the cold from aggravating his rheumatism.

english_meaning: Relating to or affected by rheumatoid arthritis. Concerning a chronic autoimmune disorder causing joint inflammation. Associated with progressive damage to joints and surrounding tissues. Characterized by painful swelling and stiffness in joints.
example_sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease. She suffers from rheumatoid joint pain. Rheumatoid factor is tested in blood work. Early treatment can slow rheumatoid disease progression.

english_meaning: A medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating rheumatic diseases. A physician who treats arthritis, autoimmune diseases, and musculoskeletal conditions. A specialist in disorders affecting joints, muscles, and connective tissues.
example_sentence: The rheumatologist diagnosed her with lupus. He sees a rheumatologist for his arthritis. Rheumatologists treat many autoimmune disorders. The rheumatologist prescribed medication for joint pain.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of rheumatic diseases, particularly those affecting the joints, muscles, and connective tissues. A medical speciality dealing with conditions such as arthritis, lupus, and gout.
example_sentence: She was referred to a specialist in rheumatology after her GP suspected she had rheumatoid arthritis. Rheumatology is one of the fastest growing medical specialities due to the increasing incidence of autoimmune diseases. The department of rheumatology at the hospital sees over five hundred new patients every month. He studied rheumatology because he wanted to help patients suffering from long-term inflammatory conditions.

english_meaning: A continuously growing horizontal underground stem that puts out lateral shoots and roots at intervals. A root-like stem found in many plants that allows vegetative reproduction. A modified stem that serves as the primary storage organ in many plant species.
example_sentence: Ginger is a rhizome that is used as a spice and as a natural remedy for digestive complaints. The gardener was careful to remove the entire rhizome of the invasive plant to prevent regrowth. Iris plants spread through the garden via underground rhizomes that extend in all directions. The rhizome of the bamboo plant can travel several metres underground in a single growing season.

english_meaning: A parallelogram in which the adjacent sides are of unequal length and the angles are not right angles. Shaped like or resembling a rhombus. A flat, slanted four-sided figure. A muscle of the upper back that connects the shoulder blade to the spine.
example_sentence: The tile was cut into a neat rhomboid. He drew a rhomboid on the whiteboard to explain the formula. The window had an unusual rhomboid shape. She strained a rhomboid muscle while lifting weights.

english_meaning: A quadrilateral with four sides of equal length. A parallelogram whose sides are all equal but whose angles are not right angles. A diamond-shaped figure with opposite angles equal. A geometric shape in which the diagonals bisect each other at right angles.
example_sentence: A square is a special kind of rhombus. The diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles. She cut the cloth into a rhombus. The tiles were arranged in a rhombus pattern.

english_meaning: To match ending sounds. To use words that have the same or similar ending sounds, especially while writing poetry or lyrics. Similar ending sound. The repetition of similar sounds at the end of words, especially in poetry, songs, and nursery verses.
example_sentence: Try to rhyme each line carefully. These two words rhyme perfectly. The poet managed to rhyme difficult words. The rhyme in the last line is very catchy. This poem has a simple rhyme. Children learn faster through rhyme.

english_meaning: A regular pattern of sounds or movements. A repeated and organized pattern of beats, sounds, or actions. It is commonly used in music, poetry, speech, dance, and even daily activities to describe a sense of timing and flow that feels natural or balanced.
example_sentence: The rhythm of the music made everyone want to dance. She spoke with a calm rhythm that was easy to follow. The poem has a strong rhythm that makes it memorable. Daily exercise helped him find a healthy rhythm in life.

english_meaning: Any of the curved bones that extend from the spine and form the protective cage of the chest. One of the twelve pairs of bones that enclose and shield the heart and lungs. A cut of meat containing one or more of these bones. A curved supporting part of a structure, such as in a ship, umbrella, or leaf. To tease someone in a light-hearted, friendly way.
example_sentence: He cracked a rib while playing football last weekend. The ribs protect the heart and lungs from injury. She ordered a plate of grilled ribs for dinner. His friends love to rib him about his terrible singing.

english_meaning: The bony structure formed by the ribs, breastbone, and spine that encloses the chest. The protective framework of bones surrounding the heart and lungs. The curved bones of the chest that expand and contract during breathing.
example_sentence: The X-ray showed a small crack in his rib cage. The rib cage protects the heart and lungs from injury. Her rib cage expanded as she took a deep breath. The doctor pressed gently on the lower rib cage.

english_meaning: A long, narrow strip of fabric used for tying things, decorating, or as an award. A long, narrow strip of anything resembling fabric. A strip of inked material used in a typewriter or printer.
example_sentence: She tied a bright yellow ribbon around the gift box before presenting it to her friend. The winning horse wore a blue ribbon indicating its first-place finish. The old typewriter needed a new inked ribbon before it could be used again. A ribbon of road wound through the green hills and down to the small village. The charity awareness campaign involved distributing small coloured ribbons to supporters.

english_meaning: A disease in children caused by vitamin D deficiency. A condition characterized by soft and weak bones due to inadequate calcium. A skeletal disorder resulting in bone deformities like bowed legs. A preventable childhood disease affecting bone development.
synonyms: ["Vitamin D deficiency disease","Bone softening disease","Osteomalacia (in adults)"]
example_sentence: Rickets causes bone deformities in growing children. Adequate vitamin D prevents rickets. Rickets was common before vitamin D supplementation. Sunlight exposure helps prevent rickets.

english_meaning: The rebound or bounce of an object, especially a bullet, stone, or ball, after it strikes a surface. To rebound or bounce off a surface and move in another direction. To bounce off a surface and travel in a different direction. To move rapidly from one place or person to another after an initial impact. The act of rebounding after hitting a hard surface. A bullet, stone, or other object that bounces off a surface. An indirect effect that spreads from one person, place, or situation to another.
example_sentence: The bullet ricocheted off the wall and struck the ground. The stone ricocheted across the surface of the lake. News of the decision ricocheted around the office. His harsh comments ricocheted through the team and affected morale. The ricochet of the bullet surprised everyone in the shooting range. The stone made a sharp ricochet off the water and landed on the shore.

english_meaning: A fixed, unnatural, or distorted expression on a person's face, often showing pain, fear, disgust, tension, or forced laughter. It refers to a stiff, grim, twisted, or unnatural facial expression. It is commonly used to describe: (1) A grimace caused by pain, fear, shock, or suffering, (2) A forced smile that does not reflect genuine happiness (3) A distorted facial expression resulting from illness, injury, or strong emotions, (4) An expression of horror, disgust, or extreme tension.
example_sentence: A rictus of pain crossed his face after the accident. She tried to smile, but it looked more like a rictus than genuine happiness. The patient lay motionless with a strange rictus on his face. A rictus of fear appeared when he heard the terrifying news.

english_meaning: To remove something unwanted or free from something unpleasant. To make someone or something free from something undesirable, harmful, or unnecessary. It is often used with the preposition "of".
example_sentence: She tried to rid her house of insects. The government aims to rid the city of pollution. He wants to rid himself of bad habits. They worked hard to rid the area of crime.

english_meaning: The act of getting rid of something unwanted, harmful, annoying, or unpleasant. Removal of something unwanted. Freedom from trouble or burden. Deliverance from danger or difficulty. Getting rid of an unpleasant thing. Release from annoyance or harm.
example_sentence: The villagers felt great riddance after the dangerous animal was caught. She sighed with relief after getting riddance from her old debts. Proper cleaning helps in the riddance of harmful germs. The company celebrated the riddance of outdated rules and systems.

english_meaning: Ridden is the past participle of ride. It means to have traveled on, sat on, controlled, or been carried by something such as a horse, bicycle, motorcycle, vehicle, or wave. Having traveled using a horse, bicycle, motorcycle, camel, or other means of transport. Sat on and directed an animal such as a horse. Transported or carried by waves, winds, or another force. Dominated, troubled, or influenced by a feeling, problem, or condition.
example_sentence: I have ridden a bicycle since childhood. She had ridden the horse before the race started. They have ridden through the desert on camels. The village was ridden with poverty for many years.

english_meaning: A puzzling question, statement, or problem that requires thought and cleverness to solve. o fill something with holes, or to affect something throughout. A question or puzzle designed to test a person's ingenuity. A mysterious or confusing thing that is difficult to understand.
example_sentence: The teacher gave the students a riddle to solve during class. The disappearance of the treasure remains a riddle. Can you solve this riddle before the time runs out?. Her sudden decision was a riddle to everyone.

english_meaning: Filled with bullets. Full of bullet holes. Shot repeatedly with bullets. Severely damaged by gunfire. Having many bullet holes because of being shot repeatedly.
synonyms: ["Heavily shot","Scarred by bullets","Pocked with bullet holes","Torn by gunfire","Sprayed with bullets"]
example_sentence: The vehicle was riddled with bullets after the attack. The wall was riddled with bullets. The building was riddled with bullets during the clash. Investigators found a car riddled with bullets.

english_meaning: To travel by train, especially without paying a fare (as hobos did in the past). To move or wander from place to place, often living a hard or unsettled life. Figuratively, to live freely, away from restrictions or stability.
example_sentence: He used to ride the rails in his youth. During the Great Depression, many jobless men rode the rails across the country. He decided to ride the rails for a year, exploring new towns and meeting new people. After quitting his job, he spent months riding the rails and living freely. Writers often romanticize those who ride the rails as seekers of freedom and adventure.

english_meaning: To attempt to control something extremely dangerous or unpredictable. To become involved in a risky situation that is difficult to escape. To live with constant danger or challenge. To manage a powerful force that could turn against you. To take a bold and risky course of action.
synonyms: ["Take a risk","Court danger","Play with fire","Walk a tightrope","Gamble"]
example_sentence: By taking that loan, he was essentially riding the tiger. Politicians who ignore inflation are riding the tiger. The startup rode the tiger of rapid growth for years. Once you ride the tiger, it is hard to get off.

english_meaning: A long green vegetable with ridges along its skin. A vine vegetable widely grown in tropical and subtropical regions. A gourd known for its light, mild, and slightly sweet taste. A vegetable commonly cooked with lentils, spices, or coconut. A plant whose mature fruit is used as a natural loofah for bathing.
example_sentence: Ridge gourd curry is a common dish in Indian households. She peeled the ridge gourd before cooking. Ridge gourd is considered very healthy and easy to digest. My mother makes ridge gourd chutney with roasted peanuts.

english_meaning: The subjection of someone or something to contemptuous mockery or derision. Language or behaviour intended to make a person or thing look absurd or foolish. To make fun of in an unkind way.
example_sentence: She was subjected to ridicule by her classmates for the unusual way she chose to dress. He turned the proposal to ridicule with a series of dismissive and mocking comments. She refused to allow anyone to ridicule her for her ambitions, however unconventional they seemed. He faced public ridicule after the embarrassing clip went viral on social media.

english_meaning: Very silly or unreasonable. Deserving laughter or mockery because it is absurd. Completely unsuitable, excessive, or illogical. Hard to take seriously.
example_sentence: The excuse sounded ridiculous to everyone in the room. It is ridiculous to spend so much money on a broken machine. She wore a ridiculous hat to make the children laugh. The rules became ridiculous when nobody could follow them.

english_meaning: Something very common, widespread, or happening in large amounts. Something unpleasant that exists or spreads widely, often in an uncontrolled way. It is usually used for negative things like rumors, corruption, disease, or problems that are everywhere.
example_sentence: It is a country where corruption is rife. Rumours are rife that he is going to resign. Los Angeles is rife with gossip about the stars' private lives. Dysentery and malaria are rife in the refugee camps. The office was rife with rumours.

english_meaning: A short repeated phrase in popular music and jazz, typically used as an introduction or refrain in a song. A quick or clever remark, spoken piece, or variation on a particular theme. To play a short repeated phrase in music. To perform, speak, or improvise freely on a topic.
example_sentence: The guitarist played a famous rock riff that captivated the audience. She began to riff on the idea of modern technology during her speech. Every musician in the band added their own riff to the song. The comedian delivered a hilarious riff on daily commuting habits.

english_meaning: A serious break, split, or separation in a relationship, friendship, or agreement. A crack, opening, or gap in something (like rock or ground). Something that divides or creates distance between people or things that were once connected.
example_sentence: A rift developed between the two friends after the argument. The earthquake caused a large rift in the ground. Political differences created a rift within the party. The company is trying to repair the rift between management and workers.

english_meaning: To set up or prepare equipment. To arrange something in a specific way. To manipulate or fix dishonestly. A large structure used for drilling oil or gas. Equipment or a set of tools arranged for a task. The way something is arranged or set up. To equip a ship with sails or machinery. A costume or outfit, especially informal usage. A truck or heavy vehicle setup. To fix a game or election unfairly.
example_sentence: The workers assembled the oil rig in the desert. He rigged the lights for the stage performance. They accused him of trying to rig the election. She set up a camera rig for filming videos.

english_meaning: A person who sets up, operates, or maintains rigging, ropes, pulleys, cranes, or other lifting/hoisting equipment in ships, construction, or theaters. A specialist who installs, maintains, or repairs mechanical or industrial equipment, often for lifting or hoisting heavy materials. Someone who manipulates systems, outcomes, or events (an election rigger). A sailor skilled in handling a ship’s sails, ropes, and rigging. A person who installs and operates rigging for theater lights, curtains, or stage equipment.
example_sentence: He had a licence to act as a rigger on a sailing ship around 1880. A whole army of shipwrights, boiler-makers, painters, and riggers slowly rebuilt the ship. The rigger carefully secured the sail before the ship left the harbor. A theater rigger adjusted the lights and stage equipment for the performance. The construction rigger operated the crane to lift heavy steel beams. Experienced riggers are essential on offshore oil platforms for safety. Authorities investigated the election rigger for fraud.

english_meaning: The system of ropes, chains, and other gear used to support a ship's masts and sails. Dishonest manipulation of a market, election, or other process. The equipment used to support or manage a structure.
example_sentence: The rigging on the old sailing vessel had been repaired several times but was still in reasonable condition. The election was marred by widespread allegations of rigging and ballot fraud. She learned to climb the rigging during her first voyage on the tall ship. He was charged with rigging the procurement process to benefit his own company.

english_meaning: An angle of exactly 90 degrees. The angle formed when two lines or surfaces meet perpendicularly. A quarter of a full turn, marked by a small square in diagrams. The standard angle used in building, carpentry, and geometry.
example_sentence: The walls meet at a right angle. Use a set square to draw a right angle. A rectangle has four right angles. The pipe was bent at a right angle.

english_meaning: The upper right chamber of the heart that receives oxygen-poor blood from the body. The chamber that collects blood from the venae cavae. The heart chamber that pushes blood into the right ventricle.
example_sentence: The right atrium receives blood returning from the body. Blood flows from the right atrium into the right ventricle. The doctor studied the right atrium on the scan. A weak right atrium can affect blood circulation.

english_meaning: The kidney situated on the right side of the abdomen. The right one of the pair of kidneys, usually positioned slightly lower than the left. A bean-shaped organ lying just below the liver on the right side of the body. The organ that filters blood on the right side and drains into the right ureter.
example_sentence: The right kidney sits a little lower than the left one. Doctors found an infection in his right kidney. The right kidney was removed during the operation. Pain in the right kidney can be felt in the lower back.

english_meaning: The lung on the right side of the chest, which is divided into three lobes. The larger of the two lungs, lying beside the liver. The right respiratory organ that receives air from the right bronchus.
example_sentence: The right lung has three lobes. The right lung is slightly larger than the left. An infection was found in his right lung. The x-ray showed fluid around the right lung.

english_meaning: A triangle in which one of the interior angles measures exactly 90 degrees. A three-sided figure containing one right angle. A triangle whose longest side, the hypotenuse, lies opposite the right angle. The basic figure used in the Pythagorean theorem and in trigonometry.
example_sentence: The students measured the sides of a right triangle. A right triangle always has one angle of ninety degrees. He used a right triangle to explain the sine ratio. The ladder and the wall formed a right triangle with the ground.

english_meaning: The lower right chamber of the heart that pumps blood to the lungs. The chamber that sends oxygen-poor blood into the pulmonary artery. A thick-walled heart chamber that receives blood from the right atrium.
example_sentence: The right ventricle pumps blood towards the lungs. Blood enters the right ventricle from the right atrium. The right ventricle has thinner walls than the left. Doctors measured the pressure inside the right ventricle.

english_meaning: A triangle that contains one angle of exactly 90 degrees. The British term for a right triangle. A triangle in which the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. A basic geometric figure used in measurement and construction.
example_sentence: Draw a right-angled triangle with sides of three and four centimetres. The theorem applies only to a right-angled triangle. She proved the result using a right-angled triangle. The roof beams form a right-angled triangle.

english_meaning: Moral goodness and acting according to what is right and just. A quality of being morally right, ethical, and virtuous. It involves honesty, fairness, justice, and living according to moral principles. A righteous person chooses good over wrong even when it is difficult.
example_sentence: He was respected for his righteousness and honesty. Righteousness guides people to make fair decisions. She showed great righteousness by helping the poor. True righteousness comes from within a person's character.

english_meaning: Moving or directed towards the right side. Positioned or facing to the right. Tending towards conservative or right-wing political views. Towards the right in direction or movement.
example_sentence: The graph shows a rightward shift in demand. He glanced in a rightward direction before crossing. The party has taken a rightward turn in recent years. The arrow points rightward towards the exit.

english_meaning: Unable to bend or be forced out of shape. Not flexible in opinion, behaviour, or method. Strictly maintained and enforced without any possibility of variation.
example_sentence: The rigid structure of the metal frame made it resistant to bending under heavy loads. She maintained a rigid daily schedule that never varied regardless of the circumstances. The school operated under a rigid code of conduct that left little room for individual expression. The rigid enforcement of the rules caused unnecessary frustration among the staff.

english_meaning: Unnecessarily long, complicated, or confusing procedure or speech. A lengthy and complicated process, set of rules, or explanation that seems unnecessary, confusing, or frustrating. It often suggests wasted time due to too many formalities or steps.
example_sentence: I had to go through a lot of rigmarole just to get my documents approved. The application process is full of unnecessary rigmarole. He explained the simple idea with so much rigmarole that no one understood. Let us skip the rigmarole and get straight to the point.

english_meaning: Very strict, careful, or thorough. Something that is very strict, exact, and done with great care and attention to detail. It can refer to rules, methods, or conditions that are tough and demanding.
example_sentence: The scientist conducted a rigorous experiment to ensure accurate results. The school follows a rigorous academic program. He went through rigorous training to become a pilot. The company has rigorous quality control standards.

english_meaning: To make someone annoyed or irritated. To provoke, irritate, or anger someone, often by persistent teasing, criticism, or provocation. Can also mean to stir up agitation, especially in water (less common).
example_sentence: His constant complaining really riles me up. She knew how to rile her brother with just a few words. The politician’s remarks riled the crowd. Small waves riled the calm lake.

english_meaning: To make someone angry or irritated. To provoke, annoy, or irritate someone, often deliberately, causing them to become upset or agitated. To stir emotions or excitement in a group. To describe causing disturbance in situations, not just people.
example_sentence: His constant teasing really riled me up. The referee’s decision riled up the crowd. Don’t rile him up about the mistake he made. She knew how to rile up her little brother for fun.

english_meaning: To sound familiar or remind someone of something they have heard or seen before, even if they cannot remember it clearly.
example_sentence: Your name rings a bell, but I can’t remember where we met. That song rings a bell, I think I’ve heard it before. His face rings a bell, maybe he studied in my school. Does the name “Sarah Khan” ring a bell to you?

english_meaning: A specific type of electrical wiring installation where the power cable forms a continuous loop from the consumer unit to each socket and back again. A circuit design commonly used in the United Kingdom for household power supply to ensure reliability and load sharing. A closed-loop system of power distribution that allows current to flow in two directions toward an outlet. An arrangement of electrical sockets connected in parallel to a ring-shaped conductor protected by a single fuse or circuit breaker. A technical configuration where the final circuit starts and ends at the same point in a distribution board.
synonyms: ["Ring Main","Electrical Loop","Closed Circuit","Power Loop","Parallel Circuit","Wiring Loop","Circular Circuit","Mains Ring","Distribution Loop","Final Circuit","Radial Alternative","Wiring Configuration"]
antonyms: ["Radial Circuit","Open Circuit","Broken Loop","Single Path","Series Circuit","Disconnected Line","Linear Wiring","Incomplete Circuit"]
example_sentence: The electrician explained that a ring circuit is standard for most British living rooms. If there is a break in the ring circuit, the sockets may still function but could become overloaded. We need to calculate the maximum load for this new ring circuit before installing the kitchen appliances. Unlike a radial circuit, a ring circuit provides two paths for the electrical current to reach each outlet.

english_meaning: The fourth finger of the hand, located between the middle finger and the little finger. The finger on which a wedding or engagement ring is traditionally worn. The digit commonly linked with marriage and commitment in many cultures. The fourth digit counting from the thumb.
example_sentence: She wore her wedding ring on her left ring finger. His ring finger was swollen after the injury. In many cultures the ring finger symbolises marriage. The jeweller measured her ring finger before making the ring.

english_meaning: To wash quickly with clean water. To clean something by pouring or running water over it, usually without using soap or with only light washing. A quick wash with water. Liquid used for washing. It can also mean to remove soap, dirt, or impurities using water.
example_sentence: Please rinse the vegetables before cooking them. She rinsed her hair after applying shampoo. Rinse your mouth with warm water after brushing. He rinsed the cup quickly and put it away.

english_meaning: To make something clean, especially a container, by washing it with water.
example_sentence: Rinse the cup out before use. She rinsed out her coffee cup. I'll just rinse these glasses out and leave them to dry. She rinses out her mouth every morning to prevent bad breath. Don't forget to rinse out your swimsuit. Rinse out the soap from the washing.

english_meaning: A violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd. An occasion when people behave in a wild and uncontrolled way. Something or someone that is extremely amusing or entertaining. To take part in a violent public disturbance.
example_sentence: The riot broke out on the streets following the controversial court verdict. Police were called in to control the riot and restore order in the affected district. The party was an absolute riot — everyone danced and laughed all evening. Groups of angry protesters began to riot when the march was blocked by police.

english_meaning: To tear something quickly or violently. To cut, tear, or pull something apart suddenly, often causing damage or separation. An opening, cut, or break in a material, fabric, or surface caused by tearing, often accidentally.
example_sentence: He ripped the paper into pieces. The storm ripped the roof off the house. She accidentally ripped her dress on the nail. The child ripped the wrapping paper from the gift. There was a rip in my jeans (. tear or hole).

english_meaning: To attack, criticize, or start something with great force or energy. To suddenly and strongly attack another person verbally, criticizes harshly, or to begin an action with intense energy. It can describe angry words, physical force, or enthusiastic action depending on context. The tone is usually strong and aggressive.
example_sentence: The manager ripped into the staff for missing the deadline. She ripped into the report and pointed out every mistake. The dog ripped into the food as if it had not eaten all day. After a short break, he ripped into his studies with full focus.

english_meaning: To cheat someone by charging too much money or to steal something. To cheat or overcharge someone unfairly. To steal something quickly. Copying someone’s idea without permission.
example_sentence: Tourists complain of being ripped off by local cab drivers. Thieves broke in and ripped off five computers. All the ideas in the film are ripped off from other movies. $70 for a T-shirt! What a rip-off!. The single is a rip-off of a 70s hit. They ripped off their clothes and ran into the sea. He rips stuff off from supermarkets to pay for his heroin. We got ripped off buying our new car. Some accuse the company of ripping off the programming language from its competitor. This is going to be a Band-Aid that I’m going to rip off. They went so far as to rip off banks in broad daylight.

english_meaning: To remove something quickly or forcefully. To pull something out suddenly, violently, or completely from its place. It can be used for physical removal like tearing out wires or pages, and also figuratively for removing systems, rules, or emotions
example_sentence: The workers ripped out the old electrical wiring. She ripped out the damaged page from the book. The company decided to rip out the outdated system. He felt like the memory had been ripped out of his heart.

english_meaning: To move through something very quickly and forcefully. To cause serious damage while moving forcefully. To move quickly from person to person, especially emotions or news. To complete or consume something at high speed. To tear something open with force.
example_sentence: The fire ripped through the village within minutes. The earthquake ripped through old buildings. A wave of panic ripped through the crowd. Fear ripped through the community after the warning. The storm ripped through the coastal areas last night. She ripped through her reading list in a week. He ripped through the exam paper because he was well prepared. The blade ripped through the fabric.

english_meaning: A strong current flowing away from the shore that can carry swimmers seaward. A powerful narrow flow of water commonly called a rip current. Strictly, a tidal current flowing through an inlet or channel.
example_sentence: The lifeguard warned swimmers about a dangerous rip tide. She stayed calm when the rip tide pulled her offshore. Rip tides can form near breaks in sandbars. Never try to swim directly against a strong rip tide.

english_meaning: To tear something into pieces, usually paper or a document. To tear something forcefully into many pieces. It is commonly used for papers, letters, contracts, or documents to show anger, rejection, or cancellation. In informal speech, it can also mean to criticize something very harshly, such as an idea, plan, or performance.
example_sentence: She ripped up the old contract and walked away. He ripped up the letter after reading it. The manager ripped up the proposal during the meeting. She was so angry that she ripped up all the papers.

english_meaning: Extremely lively, exciting, or entertaining. Very successful, impressive, or vigorous. Loud, energetic, and full of action.
example_sentence: The band gave a rip-roaring performance. We had a rip-roaring time at the festival. The team enjoyed a rip-roaring victory. It is a rip-roaring adventure from beginning to end.

english_meaning: A small wave or a series of small waves on the surface of water. A gentle wave-like movement or appearance. A sound, feeling, or effect that spreads gradually through a group or place. To form small waves. To spread or pass gently through something.
example_sentence: A breeze made the water ripple. A ripple of laughter moved through the audience. The stone created ripples across the pond. Concern rippled through the office after the announcement.

english_meaning: A spreading series of consequences caused by a single event or action. An indirect influence that moves outward and affects other people, places, or systems. A chain reaction resembling ripples spreading across water.
example_sentence: The factory closure had a ripple effect on local businesses. One kind act can create a positive ripple effect. Rising fuel prices caused a ripple effect throughout the economy. Her resignation produced a ripple effect across the department.

english_meaning: To become widely known, important, or successful. To move from being unknown or less important to becoming well known, respected, or influential in a field, society, or situation. It is often used for people, companies, ideas, or places that gain attention or success over time.
synonyms: ["Become famous","Gain recognition","Come into spotlight","Gain prominence","Rise to fame","Achieve popularity"]
antonyms: ["Fall into obscurity","Lose importance","Become unknown","Decline in fame","Fade away"]
example_sentence: The young scientist rose to prominence after discovering a new medicine. The company rose to prominence in the global market within five years. She rose to prominence as a talented singer on social media. The city rose to prominence because of its growing technology industry.

english_meaning: Causing laughter or amusement; amusing. Relating to or capable of laughter. So absurd as to be laughable.
example_sentence: The defence lawyer described the charge as entirely risible and demanded an immediate dismissal. His attempt to explain the mistake was so risible that even the judge struggled not to smile. The proposal was so impractical that it was greeted with risible disbelief by the committee. The risible logic of the argument made it impossible for anyone to take it seriously.

english_meaning: To recover, rebuild, or succeed again after complete destruction, loss, or failure. It refers to a new beginning or revival after hardship
example_sentence: After the earthquake, the city is rising from the ashes with new schools and hospitals. She lost her business during the pandemic but is now rising from the ashes with a new company. The football team rose from the ashes to win the championship after years of failure. His confidence is slowly rising from the ashes after the disappointment he faced.

english_meaning: Meat that has been cut up into very small pieces, made into a small flat mass or ball and fried. It is sometimes covered with breadcrumbs or, in the US, with pastry before it is cooked. Fried in deep fat until brown.
example_sentence: This is clearly because we are not making enough rissoles. Rissoles were very nice, but now it is hamburgers. Remove to hot-platter, garnish with rissole potatoes, and pass mint jelly with them. A well-cooked rissole, brought pleasantly to you, is good eating.

english_meaning: A ceremony performed by a particular group of people, often for religious purposes. A prescribed form or manner governing the words or actions for a ceremony. An oft-repeated action or series of actions performed in accordance with tradition or a set of rules.
example_sentence: The annual summer rite of loading up the car for the big family vacation. You have to go through an initiation rite before you become a full member. A cleansing rite was performed before building started.

english_meaning: To bring a legal case to court again. To take a matter that has already been decided by a court and try it again in a new legal action, often because one party is dissatisfied with the earlier judgment or wants a different outcome.
example_sentence: The company tried to ritigate the dispute after losing the initial case. Courts usually discourage parties from attempting to ritigate settled matters. He cannot ritigate the same issue without new evidence. Ritigating old cases wastes both time and judicial resources.

english_meaning: A series of actions that are always performed in the same way, especially as part of a religious ceremony. Something that is done regularly and always in the same way. Done in accordance with social custom or normal protocol. The established form for a ceremony.
example_sentence: Sunday lunch with the in-laws has become something of a ritual. She objects to the ritual of organized religion. Some religions employ ritual more than others. The centuries-old ritual seems headed for extinction. A strange ritual was enacted before our eyes.

english_meaning: Excessive adherence to rituals or formalities, often without understanding their purpose. Ritualism can imply a focus on rules or customs to the point where the original meaning or spirit is lost. It can also describe any behavior characterized by rigid, repetitive, or ceremonial actions.
example_sentence: He criticizes the bishops for acting against ritualism. The rise of Ritualism in the second half of the nineteenth century prompted the first split in the Protestant Episcopal Church. He is very aware of the danger of bureaucratic ritualism.

english_meaning: In accordance with or as part of a ritual or ceremony. As part of a fixed and repeated pattern or set of actions. In a formal and ceremonially prescribed manner.
example_sentence: The villagers ritually gather at the old well each spring to mark the beginning of the planting season. She ritually lit a candle each morning as part of her daily meditation practice. The document was ritually signed by all parties in the presence of official witnesses. They ritually washed their hands before entering the sacred space of the temple.

english_meaning: A person, company or thing that competes with another in sport, business, etc. To be as good, impressive, etc as somebody, something else. Competing with another person, company, thing, etc.
example_sentence: It was a personal triumph over her old rival. I could not help but smile with triumph as I went home.

english_meaning: A large natural stream of fresh water flowing towards an ocean, lake, or another river. The valley or course through which such water flows. A large flowing quantity of any liquid or of moving people.
example_sentence: The river floods its banks almost every summer. They crossed the river by a narrow wooden bridge. A river of molten lava flowed down the hillside. The city grew along the eastern bank of the river.

english_meaning: A short metal pin or bolt used to fasten two pieces of metal together. To fasten or join something with rivets. To hold someone's attention completely. To fix one's eyes or thoughts firmly on something.
example_sentence: The metal plates are held together with steel rivets. Workers riveted the beams before the roof was installed. The story riveted the attention of every listener. His eyes were riveted on the screen throughout the match.

english_meaning: Extremely interesting and holding one's complete attention. So fascinating that it is impossible to look away. Compelling and absorbing to watch, read, or listen to. Relating to the process of fastening with rivets.
example_sentence: The documentary was absolutely riveting from start to finish. She told a riveting story about her travels. It was a riveting performance by the young actress. The riveting work on the bridge took several weeks.

english_meaning: A very small stream of water; a tiny brook. A narrow flow of liquid, especially water, blood, or tears, that moves in a thin line. A small natural watercourse, smaller than a river or stream. Often used in literary descriptions of landscapes.
example_sentence: A clear rivulet ran through the green meadow behind our house. Children love to play in the shallow rivulet during the summer. After the rain, tiny rivulets formed along the dusty road. A rivulet of sweat trickled down his forehead as he worked. The rivulet eventually joined a larger river in the valley.

english_meaning: A freshwater fish found widely in European rivers and lakes. Informal term for a cockroach. The butt end of a smoked cigarette or cannabis joint. A curved or straight edge on the foot of a sail.
example_sentence: The angler pulled a large roach from the river as the afternoon light began to fade. She screamed when she spotted a roach scuttling across the kitchen floor in the middle of the night. He flicked the roach of his cigarette into the gutter and walked on without looking back. The exterminator was called in after a roach infestation was discovered behind the kitchen units.

english_meaning: A person who drives in a selfish or inconsiderate manner, taking up more than their share of the road. An inconsiderate driver who makes it difficult for other road users. Someone who monopolises road space and fails to respect other drivers.
example_sentence: The road hog in the left lane refused to move over despite a long queue of cars behind him. She had to brake sharply when the road hog cut across her lane without any warning. Driving like a road hog is not only inconsiderate but also genuinely dangerous to other users. He was reported to the police for behaving like a road hog on the motorway. There is nothing more frustrating than being stuck behind a road hog who drives at half the speed limit.

english_meaning: A document or plan that outlines the steps, goals, and timeline needed to achieve a particular objective. A strategic plan showing the planned stages of development for a project, product, or organization. A printed or digital map showing roads and routes for travelers. Used metaphorically to describe a clear path or guide toward a future outcome.
example_sentence: The company presented a detailed roadmap for the next five years of growth.  The peace agreement included a roadmap for political reform.  We used a printed roadmap to navigate the unfamiliar countryside.  The development team created a clear roadmap for the new software release.  Government officials unveiled a roadmap aimed at reducing carbon emissions.

english_meaning: A full, deep, prolonged cry of a lion or other large animal. A loud, deep sound made by a person, crowd, engine, or other source. To make such a deep, loud sound.
example_sentence: The lion let out a powerful roar that echoed across the entire savannah. The crowd gave a roar of delight when the home team scored in the final minute. The engine roared to life as the driver turned the key and pulled out of the garage. The waves roared against the cliff face during the height of the storm.

english_meaning: To cook food, especially meat, with dry heat in an oven or over a fire. A piece of meat that has been roasted. To criticise or mock someone harshly, often humorously. Very hot, as of weather.
example_sentence: She will roast the chicken with herbs and lemon. We had a Sunday roast with the whole family. His friends roasted him about his singing. It was a roasting afternoon in June.

english_meaning: A person or appliance that roasts food. A pan or container used for roasting food in an oven. An animal or food item suitable for roasting. A person who humorously criticizes or mocks someone at a roast.
example_sentence: She placed the chicken in a large roaster. This electric roaster can cook a whole turkey. The chef is an expert coffee roaster. The comedian was the sharpest roaster on the panel.

english_meaning: To date, marry, or become romantically involved with someone who is much younger than oneself. To choose a romantic partner from a far younger age group. To recruit or select someone considered too young for a role or position.
synonyms: ["Cradle-snatch","Date down","Marry young","Court a minor-aged partner","Pair with a youngster"]
antonyms: ["Marry an older partner","Date up","Pair with a contemporary","Match in age"]
example_sentence: Everyone teased him for robbing the cradle when he married a woman twenty years younger. She joked that dating a college student would be robbing the cradle. His friends said he was robbing the cradle again. The coach was accused of robbing the cradle by signing a fifteen-year-old player.

english_meaning: Strong and healthy. Strong, able to survive being used a lot and not likely to break. Strong and determined, showing that you are sure about what you are doing or saying. (Of a system or an organization) strong and not likely to fail or become weak.
example_sentence: She was almost 90, but still very robust. He seems to be in robust (good) health. The company is taking a more robust approach to management. Exports will continue to be bolstered by the robust economy. We should be able to generate stronger sales with robust profit margins.

english_meaning: The hard solid mineral material forming part of the surface of the earth. To move gently back and forth or from side to side. A style of popular music that originated in the 1950s. Something that provides a stable and dependable source of support.
example_sentence: The hikers scrambled over the loose rock to reach the summit of the ridge. She rocked the baby gently in her arms until it finally fell asleep. He has been a rock throughout this entire difficult period and never once let us down. Rock music has undergone many transformations since it first emerged in the mid-twentieth century.

english_meaning: The act of moving back and forth or from side to side in a gentle and rhythmic manner. Present participle of rock. Characterised by or relating to rock music.
example_sentence: The sound of the rocking chair creaking gently was the only noise in the quiet house. She sat by the window rocking the sleeping infant with slow, careful movements. The rocking of the ship on the rough sea made several passengers feel unwell. The rocking motion of the train eventually sent him to sleep before the journey was half over.

english_meaning: A small animal that gnaws with sharp front teeth. A mammal such as a rat, mouse, squirrel, or beaver that has strong front teeth which keep growing and are used for cutting and chewing food.
example_sentence: The mouse is a common rodent found in houses. Rodents can damage crops if they are not controlled. A squirrel is a rodent that lives in trees. Scientists study rodents to understand diseases.

english_meaning: A public event where cowboys show their skills in riding horses and bulls, and in roping cattle.
example_sentence: The cowboy won first prize in the rodeo competition. We went to the rodeo to watch bull riding and barrel racing. His horse threw him off during the rodeo, but he still smiled. The annual rodeo attracts thousands of tourists every summer.

english_meaning: A person who behaves in a dishonest, tricky, or mischievous way. Something that behaves abnormally, unpredictably, or dangerously, such as a rogue wave or rogue state. It can also describe someone who acts independently and does not follow rules or norms.  A playful but slightly dishonest person. An animal living separately from the group.
example_sentence: The rogue tricked everyone with his clever lies. A rogue elephant attacked the village after leaving its herd. The company removed the rogue employee who broke the rules. A rogue wave suddenly hit the ship during the storm. A rogue gene police officer. He's a bit of rogue but very charming. A rogue's gallery(=collection of pictures of criminals)

english_meaning: To behave in a loud, noisy, or boisterous manner, often during celebrations or partying. It may involve revelry, loud laughter, or raucous enjoyment.
example_sentence: The earl's wastrel son had spent the best part of his youth roistering and gambling. The students roistered in the streets after the exam results were announced. The villagers roistered around the bonfire all night. He roistered with his friends after winning the match. They roistered through the town, laughing and shouting.

english_meaning: To laugh a lot; to laugh uncontrollably, often so much that one moves around physically. Can also mean to move or turn around on the ground.
example_sentence: The audience rolled about at the comedian’s jokes. The children were rolling about on the grass after hearing the silly story. He told such a hilarious tale that we were rolling about for minutes. They were rolling about after watching the comedy movie.

english_meaning: To move or turn repeatedly in a circular motion. To arrive or happen again in a regular cycle. To spread or come gradually. To laugh or enjoy greatly.
example_sentence: The ball rolled around the yard until it stopped near the tree. When summer rolls around, we usually go to the beach. News of the decision quickly rolled around the office. The kids rolled around with laughter after hearing the funny story.

english_meaning: To move something back to its previous position or state. To reverse or reduce the effect of something (policy, price, decision). To undo recent changes. In computing, to return a system or database to a previous state.
example_sentence: The government rolled back the new taxes. The government decided to roll back the new tax policy after public protests. After criticism, the manager had to roll back his earlier decision.

english_meaning: To move down by turning over and over (like a ball, tear, or stone). To cause something (like a window, curtain, or sleeve) to move downward. To flow or slide downward. To unfold or extend downward.
example_sentence: The ball rolled down the hill. Tears rolled down her cheeks. He rolled down the car window. She rolled down her sleeves before starting the work.

english_meaning: To arrive in large numbers or amounts. To arrive casually, often later than expected. To appear or come gradually (like clouds, fog, or waves).
example_sentence: Donations began to roll in after the disaster. Guests rolled in late to the wedding ceremony. Dark clouds rolled in before the storm began. Money rolled in quickly after he launched his new business.

english_meaning: Very rich, having a lot of money, wealthy. A person has a great amount of money and lives in financial comfort. It is used for someone who is very wealthy or financially strong.
example_sentence: After his business became successful, he was rolling in money. People think movie stars are always rolling in money. She is not rolling in money, but she lives comfortably. His family has been rolling in money for generations.

english_meaning: To officially introduce or launch something new. To spread or unfold something. To move out slowly or smoothly. To begin using a plan, policy, service, or product gradually. Bring into operation, put into action, make available to people. Open for public use, expand gradually, present officially.
example_sentence: The school rolled out a new learning system for students. The company rolled out free internet services in rural areas. They rolled out the red carpet for the chief guest. The software update was rolled out worldwide.

english_meaning: The American form of 'turn in one's grave'. Said of a dead person who would be shocked, upset, or angry at something happening now. Used to show that an action strongly violates the values of someone who has died.
synonyms: ["Turn in one's grave","Be appalled","Be horrified","Be scandalised","Strongly disapprove"]
example_sentence: My grandmother would roll over in her grave if she heard that language. The old coach would roll over in his grave watching this performance. He is probably rolling over in his grave right now. Selling the family land would make our father roll over in his grave.

english_meaning: To adapt to adverse circumstances and continue functioning despite setbacks. To handle difficult situations with flexibility and resilience. To take things as they come and not be easily discouraged by problems. To maintain composure during stressful or changing events. To go with the flow when facing obstacles rather than resisting them directly.
example_sentence: When the project budget was cut unexpectedly, the manager had to roll with the punches. Life is full of surprises, so it is best to learn how to roll with the punches. Even though she lost her job, she rolled with the punches and started her own business. In competitive sports, athletes must learn to roll with the punches to stay focused on the game.

english_meaning: A person who moves from place to place and never settles down. Someone who changes jobs, homes or relationships frequently. A restless wanderer who avoids permanent commitments. Taken from the proverb 'a rolling stone gathers no moss', suggesting such a person gains little stability or wealth.
example_sentence: He has been a rolling stone all his life, never staying in one city for long. A rolling stone gathers no moss, as my grandmother often reminded us. She was a rolling stone in her twenties, working in a different country every year. Being a rolling stone made it hard for him to keep close friendships.

english_meaning: The introduction, launch, or implementation of something new such as a product, plan, policy, software, or program. The process of officially starting or introducing a new system, service, product, strategy, or project to people. It may happen gradually in stages or all at once. The word is commonly used in business, technology, government, security planning, marketing, and project management.
example_sentence: The company announced the rollout of its new mobile application next month. The government started the rollout of the new security policy across all districts. The software rollout was delayed because of technical issues. Our organization completed the nationwide rollout of the training program successfully.

word: Rome wasn't built in a day
english_meaning: Great achievements take time and cannot be rushed. Big projects require patience and effort. A reminder that success does not come instantly. Encouragement to be patient with progress. Important things need time to develop.
example_sentence: Do not worry about slow progress, Rome wasn't built in a day. She reminded him that Rome wasn't built in a day. Learning a language takes time, Rome wasn't built in a day. Building a business is hard, Rome wasn't built in a day.

english_meaning: To play, run, or move about in a lively, energetic, and carefree way, especially among children or animals. To achieve an easy and decisive victory in a competition or contest. A boisterous and playful activity or session of fun. Used informally to describe a movie, story, or performance that is light, entertaining, and full of action.
example_sentence: The puppies romped happily across the garden in the morning sunshine.  The team romped to an easy victory in the final match.  The children spent the afternoon romping through the fields near their house.  The film is an entertaining romp full of action and humor.  The dog romped around the park, chasing every ball thrown at it.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,000 yottabytes, introduced in 2022. An extremely large data measurement using the metric prefix ronna. A unit created to describe future amounts of digital storage.
example_sentence: The ronnabyte was officially adopted in 2022. One ronnabyte equals 1,000 yottabytes. Scientists expect data to reach ronnabyte levels one day. The term ronnabyte is still rarely used.

english_meaning: A person new to a job, sport, or activity. A beginner without much experience. A first-year professional player. Someone still learning the basics of a field.
example_sentence: The rookie scored a goal in his very first match. As a rookie, she made a few small mistakes. The coach praised the rookie for his effort. Every expert was once a rookie.

english_meaning: A place or perch where birds or bats rest or sleep. A group of birds occupying such a place. Informally, a temporary place to sleep or stay. To settle or gather for rest or sleep, especially on a perch.
example_sentence: The hens returned to their roost as the sun began to set. Hundreds of bats roost in the cave during the day. The old barn served as a roost for dozens of pigeons. After the long journey, the travelers found a roost for the night.

english_meaning: An adult male chicken. A male domestic fowl known for crowing, especially at dawn. A proud, confident, or showy man, used informally.
example_sentence: The rooster crowed just before sunrise. A bright red comb stood on the rooster's head. The farmer keeps one rooster with the hens. He strutted into the room like a proud rooster.

english_meaning: The underground part of a plant that absorbs water and holds it in place. The basic cause, origin, or source of something. A family, cultural, or historical connection to a place or group. The essential or embedded part of a word from which other forms develop. In mathematics, a value that satisfies an equation or a number produced by a radical operation. To establish roots or cause a plant to do so. To search by pushing or digging around. To cheer for or support someone, especially in North American English. To remove completely from the ground.
example_sentence: The tree’s roots damaged the old pavement. Poor communication was the root of the conflict. The cuttings should root within a few weeks. We always root for the local team.

english_meaning: To search among things by moving them about, often untidily. To look for something in a drawer, bag, room, or similar place. To investigate informally or curiously. To dig or push around with the nose or snout, as an animal does.
example_sentence: She rooted around in her bag for the keys. I rooted around the attic and found an old photograph. The journalist began rooting around in the company’s history. Wild pigs rooted around beneath the trees.

english_meaning: To support, encourage, or cheer for a person, team, or cause. To hope strongly that someone succeeds. To express loyalty during a competition or difficult situation. To give emotional encouragement to someone.
example_sentence: We will be rooting for you during the final interview. Most of the crowd rooted for the home team. I always root for the underdog in a close contest. Her whole family rooted for her recovery.

english_meaning: To find and remove something harmful, hidden, or unwanted completely. To discover someone or something after a thorough search. To eliminate corruption, disease, bad habits, or other deeply established problems. To pull a plant out by its roots.
example_sentence: The inquiry aims to root out corruption in the department. Detectives rooted out the source of the false documents. Farmers must root out the infected plants. She worked hard to root out her habit of delaying tasks.

english_meaning: To search carefully through a collection of things, often by moving them aside. To rummage in a container or place for a particular item. To examine records or information in detail to find something. To disturb an ordered group of objects while searching.
example_sentence: He rooted through the drawer for a spare battery. She rooted through old records to verify the date. The children rooted through the costume box excitedly. I had to root through dozens of emails to find the address.

english_meaning: To pull a plant or tree completely out of the ground with its roots. To dig up soil or plants, often roughly. To discover hidden facts or objects through determined searching. To remove or destroy something that is firmly established.
example_sentence: The storm rooted up several young trees. The pigs rooted up the grass near the fence. Reporters rooted up new evidence about the scandal. The reform was designed to root up long-standing discrimination.

english_meaning: A strong, thick cord made by twisting together strands of hemp, flax, or wire. To fasten, bind, or secure something using a cord. A lasso or a noose used for catching animals or for hanging. A number of things twisted or strung together, like a rope of pearls. To limit or enclose an area with a cord to prevent access.
example_sentence: The sailors used a thick rope to secure the ship to the dock. He learned how to rope cattle on his grandfather's ranch. The police decided to rope off the crime scene to keep bystanders away. She wore a long rope of pearls that hung down to her waist.

english_meaning: To persuade or convince someone to participate in a task or activity. To trick or deceive someone into getting involved in something they might avoid otherwise. To enlist someone's help or cooperation, often through social pressure or charm. To draw someone into a specific group, scheme, or situation. To successfully involve someone in a project by emphasizing the benefits or using influence.
example_sentence: I didn't want to attend the meeting, but my boss managed to rope me in at the last minute. The scammers tried to rope in unsuspecting tourists with a fake investment scheme. We need to rope in a few more volunteers for the charity auction this weekend. She is so charming that she can rope in almost anyone to support her cause.

english_meaning: To persuade someone to get involved in a task or activity that they may not want to do. To trick or entice someone into participating. To enlist someone for a project against their initial inclination. To maneuver a person into a commitment. To talk someone into doing a favor or joining a group.
example_sentence: I didn't want to go to the meeting, but my boss managed to rope into me helping with the presentation. They are trying to rope into several volunteers for the charity car wash this weekend. Somehow, my brother always manages to rope into me cleaning his room for him. She was roped into joining the committee even though she was already very busy.

english_meaning: To enclose or isolate an area by means of ropes. To prevent people from entering a specific location using a barrier of cord. To cordon off a space for safety or privacy. To mark the boundaries of a designated zone. To restrict access to a crime scene or event space.
example_sentence: The police had to rope off the entire street while they investigated the accident. They will rope off a section of the park for the private wedding ceremony. Please rope off the wet floor to prevent anyone from slipping. The security guards started to rope off the red carpet area before the celebrities arrived.

english_meaning: To tie or fasten two or more people or things together using a cord. To connect individuals for safety during climbing or exploration. To unite different elements or groups into a single cohesive unit. To bind objects securely so they do not separate. To link together physically or metaphorically for a common purpose.
example_sentence: The climbers decided to rope together before ascending the dangerous glacier. We need to rope together these logs so they can float down the river as a raft. The community leaders worked to rope together various local organizations for the festival. Make sure you rope together the suitcases on top of the car roof tightly.

english_meaning: To bind, fasten, or secure something or someone using a rope. To connect a group of climbers together with a rope for safety. To organize or cordone off an area by stringing ropes across it. To lasso or catch an animal by throwing a rope. To bring people together for a joint task or purpose.
example_sentence: The climbers decided to rope up before starting the steep ascent on the glacier. He began to rope up the heavy luggage to ensure it stayed on the roof of the car. The police had to rope up the crime scene to keep bystanders away. The rancher will rope up the stray calf before it wanders too far from the herd.

english_meaning: A string of prayer beads used especially by Christians for counting prayers. A chain or string of beads used mainly in Christianity, especially in the Catholic Church, to count prayers such as the Hail Mary and the Lord’s Prayer. The word can also refer to the set of prayers recited using these beads.
example_sentence: She held her rosary quietly while praying in the church. The rosary was passed down through generations in the family. Many Catholics pray the rosary every day. He kept a rosary in his pocket for comfort and faith.

english_meaning: Rose-coloured; deep pink. Tinged with pink, especially of the sky or light. Excessively optimistic or idealistic in outlook.
example_sentence: The dawn sky took on a soft roseate glow. A flock of roseate spoonbills waded through the shallow water. He held a roseate view of the project's chances. The marble had a faint roseate tint.

english_meaning: The bud of a rose, before it has fully opened. Something young, tender, or about to blossom. Often used as a term of affection or in poetic language to describe delicate beauty.
example_sentence: She wore a small rosebud in her hair on the morning of the wedding. The garden was dotted with rosebuds that would be in full bloom within a few days. He presented her with a single rosebud and a handwritten note expressing his feelings. The young dancer was described by the critic as a rosebud talent on the verge of full blossoming.

english_meaning: To include someone in an official list, often for work shifts, duties, sports teams, or other organized activities. A list of people or things, often showing duty, schedule, or membership. An organized list, often used in workplaces, schools, sports teams, or organizations, indicating who is assigned to which task, shift, or role. It can also refer to a record of members of a group or team.
example_sentence: The manager rostered all staff for the holiday shifts. The coach rostered three new players for the next match  The manager posted the weekly roster for all staff members. The football team’s roster includes ten new players this season. Check the roster to see who is on duty today. The conference roster lists all the speakers and their topics.

english_meaning: Pink or light red in colour, like a rose. Having a healthy pink glow, especially of cheeks or skin. Hopeful, promising, or full of optimism. Presenting things in an overly favourable light.
example_sentence: The children came inside with rosy cheeks after playing in the snow. A rosy light spread across the sky at sunset. The company's future looks rosy after this year's profits. He painted a rosy picture of life in the countryside.

english_meaning: To decay, decompose, or become spoiled because of age, moisture, bacteria, or fungi. To weaken or deteriorate gradually. The process or state of decay or decomposition. A condition of corruption, decline, or moral decay.
example_sentence: The apples began to rot after being left outside for a week. Constant moisture can cause wooden beams to rot. If food starts to rot, it should be thrown away immediately. Years of neglect allowed the old house to rot beyond repair.

english_meaning: Learning something by repeating it many times without understanding it deeply. Memorizing or learning something through repetition rather than understanding the meaning. It is often used in education when students repeat information again and again until they remember it.
example_sentence: The student learned the poem by rote. He memorized the multiplication table by rote. Rote learning does not always help in real understanding. She repeated the answers by rote during the test.

english_meaning: A person who leads a debauched or morally unrestrained lifestyle. A man who pursues pleasure, especially involving many sexual relationships. An older man of disreputable character who pursues pleasure without regard for morality.
example_sentence: The novel's villain is a classic roue who charms and then ruins every woman he encounters. He had lived the life of a roue in his youth but claimed to have reformed entirely in later years. She was warned about the roue who was known to prey on the wealthy and the naive. The roue made no apologies for the way he lived and seemed to revel in his own notoriety.

english_meaning: A day filled with difficulties or stress. A period of time characterized by challenges and hardships. A demanding day that causes exhaustion or frustration. An unpleasant day where things do not go as planned.
synonyms: ["Bad day","Hard day","Difficult day","Tough day","Tiring day","Exhausting day","Stressful day","Challenging day","Unpleasant day"]
antonyms: ["Good day","Great day","Easy day","Relaxing day","Pleasant day","Smooth day","Fantastic day","Wonderful day","Joyful day"]
example_sentence: He poured himself a glass of water after having a rough day at work. I can see you had a rough day, so just relax for the evening. She complained about her rough day to her sympathetic best friend. Everyone has a rough day occasionally when nothing seems to work out.

english_meaning: To plan, install, or sketch something in a basic and unfinished form. It is often used in construction, design, writing, or planning when only the main structure is prepared and details will be added later.
example_sentence: The electrician roughed in the wiring before the walls were closed. She roughed in the outline of the report and planned to revise it later. The plumber roughed in the pipes during the early stage of construction. We roughed in a schedule but changed it after the meeting.

english_meaning: To live without comfort. To live or stay in difficult conditions without modern comforts, often by choice or necessity, such as sleeping outdoors or managing with very limited resources
example_sentence: During the field trip, we had to rough it without electricity or running water. The hikers decided to rough it and camp in the forest for a week. After the flood, many families were forced to rough it until help arrived. He enjoys roughing it when he goes on adventure tours.

english_meaning: To prepare something quickly in basic form. To make an initial plan, sketch, or draft without fine details. It focuses on the main structure, not perfection.
example_sentence: The team roughed out the project plan in one meeting. She roughed out her speech before adding details. The architect roughed out the building design on paper. We need to rough out the budget before final approval.

english_meaning: To physically attack or treat someone violently. To hit, beat, or handle someone roughly, often to intimidate or punish them. It can also mean treating something roughly or carelessly.
example_sentence: The gang tried to rough him up after the argument. He was roughed up by the police during the protest. Don’t rough up the equipment; it’s fragile. She got roughed up in the schoolyard fight.

english_meaning: To attack or treat someone roughly. To use physical force against someone or to handle a person or thing in a violent, aggressive, or careless way. It often implies intimidation, beating, or causing harm rather than a serious fight. In daily English, speakers usually say rough up without on.
example_sentence: The gang threatened to rough up on anyone who entered their area. He was roughed up on his way home by unknown attackers. The guards roughed up on the prisoner during the arrest. The coach warned the players not to rough up on the weaker team.

english_meaning: To gather people, animals, or things together in one place. To bring to a conclusion or complete an activity. To increase a number to the nearest whole or higher figure (in mathematics or estimation). To arrest or capture a group of people.
example_sentence: The teacher rounded up all the students after the trip. The police rounded up the thieves last night. Let’s round up the meeting with some final thoughts. Please round up the bill to the nearest dollar.

english_meaning: A circular intersection where drivers must travel in one direction around a central island. A large revolving platform in a playground for children to ride on. A communicative style that is indirect, circuitous, or not straightforward. A short close-fitting jacket often worn by men or boys in the 19th century. A route or journey that is longer than the direct way.
example_sentence: The driver took the second exit at the busy roundabout. The children were laughing as they spun around on the roundabout. He gave a very roundabout explanation instead of answering the question directly. We took a roundabout route to the village to enjoy the scenic views of the countryside.

english_meaning: To cause someone to wake from sleep. To stir or excite someone into activity. To evoke a strong emotion or response in someone.
example_sentence: She was unable to rouse him in the morning and called for medical assistance. The general's speech was designed to rouse the troops before the decisive battle. The news was enough to rouse the entire community to demand answers from the authorities. The passionate performance of the choir was enough to rouse the whole audience to their feet.

english_meaning: To defeat someone completely and force them to flee or withdraw. A complete and overwhelming defeat in a battle, game, election, or competition. It can also mean a chaotic retreat or disorderly escape.
example_sentence: The army suffered a terrible rout in the battle. Our team routed the opponents by ten goals. The frightened crowd fled in rout after the explosion. The king’s soldiers routed the enemy forces quickly.

english_meaning: A way or course taken to get from one place to another. A regular line of travel or delivery. A method or means of achieving something. The path chosen for a journey. To send or direct along a particular course.
example_sentence: We took the shortest route to the airport. The bus follows the same route every day. Hard work is the surest route to success. Please route the package through Karachi.

english_meaning: A regular, fixed way of doing things in the same order. A sequence of actions repeated regularly as part of daily life or work. Performed as part of normal practice rather than for a special reason. Ordinary, dull, and lacking variety or excitement. A set piece of dance, music, or comedy performed by an entertainer. In computing, a set of instructions that performs a particular task.
example_sentence: Morning exercise is part of my daily routine. The doctor ordered a routine blood test. He found office work dull and routine. The dancers performed a beautifully rehearsed routine.

english_meaning: A horizontal line of people or things arranged side by side. A horizontal series of cells in a table or spreadsheet. A noisy quarrel or serious argument. To move a boat through water using oars.
example_sentence: We sat in the front row of the hall. Add the new entry in the third row of the table. They had a serious row over money. He likes to row across the lake every morning.

english_meaning: Someone or something that is loud, disruptive, and difficult to control, often causing trouble in a group or gathering. Noisy and disorderly
example_sentence: The rowdy crowd cheered loudly at the match. Some rowdy students were sent out of the classroom. He is known for his rowdy behavior at parties. The rowdy dogs chased each other around the yard.

english_meaning: Noisy, rough, and disorderly behaviour, especially in a public place. Conduct that disturbs peace through shouting, fighting, or wild activity. The habit of behaving in an unruly and uncontrolled manner in groups. Public disorder created by excited or aggressive crowds.
example_sentence: Rowdyism at the stadium forced the referee to stop the match. The teacher warned the students against rowdyism during the trip. Police were called to control rowdyism outside the hall. Their rowdyism spoiled an otherwise pleasant evening.

english_meaning: Belonging to or connected with a king, queen, or member of a ruling family. Suitable for or worthy of a monarch; splendid and impressive. Used in the names of organisations under the patronage of a monarch. A member of a royal family. Informally, complete or utter, as in a royal mess.
example_sentence: The royal family attended the opening ceremony. They were given a royal welcome at the airport. The Royal Society funds scientific research. Several royals were present at the wedding.

english_meaning: To apply pressure with hands or a cloth to massage, soothe, or relax muscles. To clean or polish a surface by rubbing. To apply something over a surface by rubbing (like oil or lotion). Sometimes, to reduce tension or calm a situation through a figurative "rubbing down".
example_sentence: After the long run, he asked someone to rub down his legs. She rubbed down the wooden table until it shined. The mechanic rubbed down the car with oil to prevent rust. He tried to rub down the tension in the room with a joke.

english_meaning: To annoy or irritate someone, often without intending to. To irritate or annoy a person through behavior, tone, or actions, even if no harm was intended. It often happens due to personality clashes or communication style differences.
synonyms: ["Irritate someone","Annoy someone","Rub up the wrong way","Get on someone’s nerves","Bother someone"]
example_sentence: His sarcastic jokes always rub me the wrong way. She didn’t mean to be rude, but her tone rubbed him the wrong way. The new manager rubs many employees the wrong way with strict rules. I think I rubbed her the wrong way when I interrupted her speech.

english_meaning: The act of massaging or rubbing someone’s body, often after exercise to relax muscles. It can also mean wiping or cleaning a surface thoroughly. In sports, it’s a post-workout massage. In mechanical or cleaning contexts, it means rubbing a surface to remove dirt, grease, or polish.
example_sentence: After the match, the players received a quick rub-down. She gave the table a good rub-down with a cloth. The massage therapist performed a thorough rub-down of his back. Mechanics gave the engine a rub-down before assembling it.

english_meaning: A driver who slows down to stare at a traffic accident or roadside event. A overly curious person who gapes or stares inquisitively at something unusual or shocking. A tourist or sightseer who turns their head around constantly to view surrounding attractions.
example_sentence: Traffic slowed down because every rubbernecker wanted to see the minor car crash. A crowd of rubberneckers quickly gathered around the street performer. Emergency services asked rubberneckers to keep moving and clear the area. The open-top bus was filled with rubberneckers admiring the city skyscrapers.
