english_meaning: Waste material or garbage. Worthless or foolish talk, ideas, or writing. Something of very poor quality. To criticize severely or dismiss as worthless.
example_sentence: Please throw the rubbish in the bin. Don't talk such rubbish in front of the guests. The film was absolute rubbish. Critics rubbished the government's new plan.

english_meaning: Broken pieces of stone, brick, or concrete from a destroyed building or structure. Fragments of rock, stone, bricks, or concrete that remain after the destruction of a building, wall, or other structure. It can also describe loose debris from a demolished area or natural disaster.
example_sentence: The bomb reduced the houses to rubble. After the earthquake, the streets were filled with rubble. The demolition left a heap of rubble behind. Workers cleared the rubble from the collapsed bridge. Rubble from the old castle was used in building the new road.

english_meaning: A precious stone of a deep red colour, valued as a gem. A red variety of the mineral corundum used in jewellery. A rich, deep red colour resembling that of the stone. Made of or set with rubies, used as an adjective.
example_sentence: She wore a necklace studded with rubies. A fine ruby can be more valuable than a diamond. The evening sky turned a deep ruby colour. He inherited a ruby ring from his grandmother.

english_meaning: A loud noise, disturbance, or chaotic commotion. A situation where there is a lot of noise, confusion, or disorder, often caused by people arguing, shouting, or reacting strongly. It is commonly used when something attracts sudden attention due to chaos or protest.
example_sentence: The children created a ruckus in the classroom when the teacher left. A ruckus broke out in the market after the accident. Don’t make a ruckus over small issues. The loud music caused a ruckus in the neighborhood. His sudden complaint created a ruckus in the meeting. The neighbors made a ruckus late at night, disturbing everyone.

english_meaning: A noisy quarrel, disturbance, or fight. An angry protest or uproar about something. A commotion caused by strong disagreement. (Often plural) Trouble or objections raised by people.
example_sentence: There was a terrible ruction in the street last night. The decision caused a ruction among the club members. If we cancel the trip, there will be ructions at home. A ruction broke out between the two neighbours over the boundary wall.

english_meaning: Having a healthy red or rosy colour, especially of the complexion. Used as a mild expletive in British English to express irritation or emphasis. Reddish in colour.
example_sentence: His ruddy cheeks and bright eyes suggested he spent a great deal of time working outdoors. She had a ruddy complexion that deepened whenever she was embarrassed or overheated. He was absolutely ruddy furious when he discovered what had happened to his car. The ruddy hue of the desert rocks in the evening light was breathtaking.

english_meaning: Offensively impolite or ill-mannered. Roughly made or executed in a basic way. Used to describe something surprising or unwelcome. Vigorous or robust in a healthy way.
example_sentence: It was extremely rude of him to answer his phone during the middle of the dinner. She gave a rude awakening to anyone who thought the problem had already been solved. The rude shelter was constructed hastily from branches and leaves to provide temporary protection. He had a rude shock when he realised how much his careless mistake was going to cost.

english_meaning: To bitterly regret something one has done or allowed to happen. It involves a feeling of deep sorrow, repentance, and wishing that a past situation had been different. It denotes carrying a burden of remorse for a past mistake.
example_sentence: He will certainly rue the day he arrogantly insulted his best friend. I deeply rue my hasty decision to quit that excellent job without a plan. You will live to rue this deeply tragic and foolish mistake. She came to bitterly rue the missed opportunity to travel the entire world. They secretly rue the harsh, unforgiving words spoken in the extreme heat of anger.

english_meaning: To deeply regret the time when something happened. To feel bitter sorrow about a past decision or action. To suffer the unpleasant consequences of a choice and wish it had never been made. Used as a warning that someone will be sorry for what they are doing.
example_sentence: You will rue the day you trusted that man with your savings. He came to rue the day he left his steady job. She warned that they would rue the day they ignored her advice. Many investors now rue the day they entered the market so hastily.

english_meaning: Causing sorrow, regret, or deep sadness. Something that makes a person feel remorse or emotional pain. An event, situation, or memory that causes emotional pain, sorrow, or a feeling of regret. It is often used for actions or outcomes that are deeply unfortunate and leave a lasting sense of remorse.
example_sentence: The accident was a ruesome reminder of careless driving. He spoke about his past mistakes in a ruesome tone. Losing the village to floods was a ruesome experience for the community. The story ends on a ruesome note of regret and loss.

english_meaning: A violent or cruel person, A person who behaves in a rough, aggressive, and lawless way. Such a person often uses force, threats, or intimidation and shows no respect for others or social rules.
example_sentence: The ruffian attacked the shopkeeper without any reason. The police arrested the ruffian who was terrorizing the neighborhood. He was once a street ruffian but later changed his life. The movie portrayed the villain as a ruthless ruffian.

english_meaning: Having a rough and uneven surface or edge. Strong and able to withstand harsh conditions or rough treatment. Having or requiring great physical endurance and strength. Having strong and attractive features that are not smooth or delicate. Durable and sturdy in construction or design.
example_sentence: The hikers struggled to navigate the rugged terrain of the mountain range. He was known for his rugged good looks and weathered skin. This smartphone is designed with a rugged exterior to survive accidental drops. The pioneers lived a rugged life in the wilderness during the early years.

english_meaning: To damage something so badly that it loses all its value, pleasure, etc. To spoil or destroy something completely. To cause a person or company to lose all their money or their good reputation. The state or process of being destroyed or severely damaged.
example_sentence: That one mistake ruined his chances of getting the job. The crops were ruined by the late frost. e ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them. The house went to rack and ruin. Drinking was his ruin.

english_meaning: Causing or likely to cause great damage, destruction, or loss. Extremely harmful to success, wealth, or health. Something that brings ruin (complete destruction or downfall)
example_sentence: The flood had a ruinous effect on the village. He suffered ruinous losses in the stock market. Their constant arguments had a ruinous impact on their marriage. The company went bankrupt after a ruinous decision by its management.

english_meaning: To include something or someone as a possibility or consideration. To decide that something should be considered as part of the explanation or decision.
example_sentence: The police ruled in theft as a motive. Doctors have ruled in infection as the cause of his illness. We cannot rule in John’s involvement until we have more evidence. The company has ruled in remote work for certain employees.

english_meaning: To end or conclude something. To draw a line to separate or end something. To mark off or close a section of writing, accounts, or a page.
example_sentence: The teacher ruled off the section for notes. Please rule off the page before starting the next question. The accountant ruled off the account book at the end of the month. Let’s rule off this discussion and move to the next topic.

english_meaning: To eliminate or exclude something as a possibility. To decide that something cannot happen, or is not suitable. To dismiss or reject an option, explanation, or person.
example_sentence: Police have not rule out the possibility that man was murdered. The proposed solution was ruled out as too expensive. A shoulder injury ruled him out for most of the season. We cannot rule out the chance of rain tomorrow. His lack of experience rules him out as a candidate for this job.

english_meaning: To eliminate, exclude, or consider something as impossible. To decide that something cannot happen or someone cannot be chosen.
example_sentence: His injury ruled him out of the game. The doctor ruled out cancer after seeing the test reports. His injury ruled him out of the final match.

english_meaning: To be the person who has the greatest authority, influence, or control in a household, group, workplace, or situation. To dominate or be in charge.
example_sentence: In their household, Grandmother clearly rules the roost. Although she is a junior employee, she seems to rule the roost in every meeting. The oldest child ruled the roost while the parents were away. Since the manager left, no one has really ruled the roost in the office.

english_meaning: To make a deep, low, continuous sound. To move while making such a sound. To discover or expose a secret plan. To fight or argue loudly. A deep rolling sound. A noisy fight or quarrel.
example_sentence: Thunder began to rumble in the distance. The trucks rumbled along the rough road. The police finally rumbled the criminal gang. A rumble broke out between the two groups.

english_meaning: To move forward slowly while making a low, heavy, continuous sound. To continue steadily without much progress, change, or excitement. To keep going in an unremarkable but persistent way.
example_sentence: The old bus rumbled along the dusty country road. The investigation rumbled along for another two years. Their conversation rumbled along without reaching any conclusion. A heavy cart rumbled along beneath our window at dawn.

english_meaning: To continue for a long time without being resolved. To keep going noisily or persistently in the background. To carry on rolling forward with a deep, continuous sound.
example_sentence: The dispute over land ownership rumbled on for a decade. Thunder rumbled on long after the rain had stopped. Debate about the new tax rumbled on in parliament. Their old rivalry rumbled on beneath the polite conversation.

english_meaning: To gather, collect, or bring something together, often quickly or informally. To stir up, rouse, or set something in motion. To approach or arrive while making a low, heavy, continuous sound. To manage to produce or arrange something with the resources at hand.
example_sentence: The old truck rumbled up the hill and stopped outside the gate. She managed to rumble up a meal from whatever was left in the kitchen. He rumbled up enough volunteers to finish the work before dark. A storm rumbled up from the south late in the afternoon.

english_meaning: A low, deep, continuous sound like distant thunder. Making such a heavy rolling noise. The first signs of discontent, complaint, or trouble among people. A growling noise made by an empty stomach.
example_sentence: We heard the rumbling of thunder in the distance. There are rumblings of discontent among the workers. His stomach was rumbling loudly during the lecture. The rumbling of heavy trucks kept us awake all night.

english_meaning: Noisy, energetic, and difficult to control. Boisterous and full of high spirits in a cheerful but disorderly way. Rough and lively in behaviour, especially in a way that disturbs others.
example_sentence: The rumbustious children ran through the house all morning. It was a rumbustious party that lasted well past midnight. He has a rumbustious sense of humour that fills the room. The team celebrated in their usual rumbustious fashion.

english_meaning: An animal that chews cud, such as cows and goats. A herbivorous animal that digests plant food in two steps. It first swallows the food, then brings it back to the mouth (cud) to chew it again for better digestion. Common examples include cows, buffaloes, sheep, and goats.
example_sentence: A cow is a ruminant animal that chews cud. Sheep and goats are common ruminants found on farms. The farmer raised several ruminant animals for milk production. Ruminant digestion helps animals extract more nutrients from grass.

english_meaning: To think deeply about something for a long time. To think carefully and slowly about something, often for a long time. It can also mean for animals like cows to chew food again after swallowing.

example_sentence: The old sage shared his wisdom with the villagers. Her sage advice helped me make the right choice. He is considered a sage in the field of philosophy. Following a sage approach, they solved the conflict peacefully. Sage leaves add a unique flavor to roasted meats. The tea was made from dried sage to soothe a sore throat.

english_meaning: To manage your own affairs or move forward in life in your own way. An informal expression meaning to do what suits you or to follow your own path. To make progress steadily by using your own effort and judgement. Used to encourage someone to continue with their chosen course of action.
synonyms: ["Go your own way","Chart your course","Steer your ship","Manage your affairs","Carry on","Proceed","Move forward","Take charge"]
antonyms: ["Follow blindly","Depend on others","Give up","Stay stuck","Hesitate","Surrender","Drift aimlessly"]
example_sentence: You know your goals best, so sail your boat the way you want. He decided to leave the family business and sail his boat alone. Stop worrying about their opinions and simply sail your boat. She sailed her boat quietly and built a successful career.

english_meaning: A piece of material extended on a mast to catch the wind and propel a boat or ship. To travel in a boat with sails. To move smoothly and rapidly.
example_sentence: The ship's sails billowed in the wind. The yacht sails around the bay every weekend. She sails through her exams with ease. The boat sails at dawn.

english_meaning: A person acknowledged as holy or virtuous and typically regarded as being in heaven after death. A very virtuous, patient, or long-suffering person.
example_sentence: He was canonized as a saint. My grandmother is a saint for putting up with all of us. She has the patience of a saint. The city is named after a famous saint.

english_meaning: A small amphibian that looks like a lizard and lives both on land and in water. A mythical creature believed to live in fire. A symbol of endurance or resistance to heat in literature. A metal heating tool used to heat food or surfaces.
example_sentence: The salamander hid under the wet leaves near the stream. Scientists study salamanders because they can regenerate lost limbs. After the rain, several salamanders appeared on the forest floor. In ancient legends, the salamander was believed to survive inside fire.

english_meaning: A person who loves the moon and finds it pleasing to the eye. One who is attracted to and captivated by the moon's beauty. A lunar enthusiast or observer of the night sky. Someone who feels a deep spiritual or emotional connection to the moon. An individual who finds solace and comfort in moonlight. A person who is fascinated by the various phases and cycles of the moon.
example_sentence: As a true selenophile, she spent every full moon night sitting on her balcony. The artist described himself as a selenophile whose paintings were inspired by the lunar glow. Being a selenophile, he invested in a high-quality telescope to observe the craters of the moon. Her social media bio simply read 'selenophile' to reflect her lifelong obsession with the night sky.

english_meaning: An abnormal and persistent fear of the moon. A specific phobia where an individual experiences anxiety regarding the moon's light or appearance. Irrational dread of the lunar cycle or lunar effects. Intense psychological discomfort when viewing the moon or thinking about it. A type of clinical phobia classified under anxiety disorders.
synonyms: ["Fear Of The Moon","Lunar Phobia","Moon Dread","Anxiety","Phobia","Panic","Apprehension","Terror","Fright","Neurosis","Irrational Fear","Specific Phobia"]
example_sentence: Individuals suffering from selenophobia may experience panic attacks during a full moon. She avoided walking outside at night because of her intense selenophobia. Therapists often use exposure therapy to treat cases of selenophobia. The sight of the crescent moon through the window triggered his selenophobia.

english_meaning: Most noticeable or important. Prominent; conspicuous. The salient parts of something are the most important things about it. It describes something that stands out or is easily seen.
example_sentence: She began to summarize the salient points of the proposal. The salient feature of the house was its large, open-plan kitchen. He presented the salient facts of the case. In the military, a salient is a battlefield feature that projects into enemy territory.

english_meaning: The process of making something salty, especially soil or water. The accumulation or increase of salts in soil or water, often making the environment less suitable for agriculture or drinking. It can happen naturally or due to human activities like irrigation with saline water.
example_sentence: Excessive irrigation led to the salination of farmland. Coastal regions often face salination due to seawater intrusion. Salination of groundwater can harm local agriculture. Proper drainage systems can prevent salination in irrigated areas.

english_meaning: Containing or impregnated with salt. Salty. It is often used to describe water that has a high concentration of salt. A saline solution is a mixture of salt and water, frequently used in medical contexts.
example_sentence: The patient was given a saline solution intravenously. The Great Salt Lake is a large saline lake. Many organisms cannot survive in such a saline environment. The coastal soil was too saline for most crops to grow.

english_meaning: Any of the glands in the mouth that produce saliva. A gland that secretes fluid to keep the mouth moist. A gland whose secretion begins the digestion of starch in food. One of the three main paired glands: parotid, submandibular, and sublingual.
example_sentence: The salivary glands produce about a litre of saliva each day. A blocked salivary gland can cause painful swelling. Saliva from these glands helps us chew and swallow food. The infection had spread to his left salivary gland.

english_meaning: Of a person's face or complexion, having an unhealthy yellow or pale brown color. Having a yellowish, sickly color. It suggests a lack of health or vitality.
example_sentence: His face was sallow after weeks of illness. The long winter had left her skin looking sallow. She had a sallow complexion and dark circles under her eyes. The doctor noted his sallow appearance and ordered some tests. The flickering candlelight cast a sallow glow on the room.

english_meaning: A pale pinkish orange colour resembling the flesh of a salmon. A soft warm pink with an orange undertone. Of or having this delicate pink-orange shade.
example_sentence: The bedroom walls were painted a warm salmon pink. She carried a bouquet of salmon pink roses. His shirt was a faded salmon pink. The clouds turned salmon pink as the sun went down.

english_meaning: A surgical operation to remove one or both fallopian tubes. A procedure performed for ectopic pregnancy, infection, or cancer risk. The removal of a fallopian tube as a permanent method of contraception. A gynaecological surgery that may be partial or complete.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed a salpingectomy after diagnosing an ectopic pregnancy. A salpingectomy may be chosen as a permanent form of birth control. She was discharged two days after the salpingectomy. Recent studies link salpingectomy with a lower risk of ovarian cancer.

english_meaning: A person of great kindness and honesty. Someone with strong moral values. A humble and reliable individual. A person who is trustworthy and sincere. One who represents the best qualities of humanity.
synonyms: ["Good person","Honest person","Noble person","Kind-hearted person","Genuine person","Upright person"]
example_sentence: My grandfather was the salt of the earth and always helped everyone in the village. The teacher is the salt of the earth, caring deeply about her students. Farmers are often considered the salt of the earth because of their hard work and honesty. He may not be rich, but he is the salt of the earth and respected by all.

english_meaning: To save money or goods carefully for future use. To store something in a safe place over a long period. To put aside savings quietly, often in secret. To keep resources in reserve for a time of need.
example_sentence: He salted away a small fortune over thirty years. She salts away a little money from every paycheque. They had salted away enough grain to survive the winter. The company salted away profits for future expansion.

english_meaning: Health-giving, healthy, and pleasant, especially in reference to climate or surroundings. Promoting good health or well-being. Favorable to physical or moral well-being. Clean, refreshing, and beneficial.
example_sentence: They moved to a more salubrious part of the country. The mountain air is very salubrious. He recommended a salubrious diet for quick recovery. The resort is known for its salubrious climate.

english_meaning: Producing a good effect, especially through a warning or unpleasant experience. Beneficial or helpful in improving a situation. Promoting good health or well-being. Serving as a useful lesson.
example_sentence: The accident was a salutary reminder to drive carefully. Losing the match had a salutary effect on the team's attitude. A short walk each morning is salutary for both body and mind. The report offers a salutary lesson for other companies.

english_meaning: The act of rescuing a wrecked or disabled ship or its cargo from loss at sea. The rescue of property from damage or destruction. To save or retrieve something from potential loss or failure.
example_sentence: An attempt was made to salvage the ship's cargo. They were able to salvage some of their belongings from the fire. He is trying to salvage his reputation. The team managed to salvage a draw from the match. The salvage operation took several weeks.

english_meaning: The act of being saved or protected from harm, danger, loss, or destruction. Deliverance from sin and its consequences in religious belief, especially the saving of the soul. A source or means of being rescued from a difficult or undesirable situation. Preservation from ruin or failure.
example_sentence: Christians believe in salvation through faith. Education proved to be his only salvation from poverty. The timely loan was the salvation of the struggling business. Many people seek spiritual salvation through prayer and meditation. The lifeboat was the salvation of the stranded sailors.

english_meaning: A soothing medicinal ointment applied to the skin to heal wounds, burns, or irritation. Something that comforts or relieves emotional pain. To apply a healing ointment to a wound. To soothe, comfort, or ease physical or emotional pain.
example_sentence: She applied a soothing salve to her sunburn. His apology was a salve for her hurt feelings. The beautiful music was a salve to his troubled soul. The government offered financial aid as a salve to the impoverished region. This herbal salve is good for cuts and scrapes.

english_meaning: Used to say that nothing has changed, things are just as usual, often in a dull or routine way. This idiom used to express that the situation, routine, or events are the same as before, often implying boredom or lack of change.
antonyms: ["A big change","Something new","A fresh start","A different experience"]
example_sentence: Every weekend it’s the same old, same old, eat, sleep, and watch TV. I asked her how life was, and she said, “Same old, same old”. Nothing exciting is happening these days, just the same old, same old routine. How’s work going same old, same old, just busy with reports.

english_meaning: The secret copying and distribution of banned literature, especially in the former Soviet Union. Literature that is privately printed and circulated to avoid government censorship. Clandestine publications produced by dissidents.
example_sentence: The banned novel circulated widely through samizdat networks. Poets risked imprisonment to produce samizdat journals. The samizdat press kept free thought alive under the regime. He received a worn samizdat copy of the forbidden book.

english_meaning: A small part or quantity that represents or demonstrates the whole. A specimen taken for testing or analysis. A short extract of recorded sound reused in music. To take, examine, or try a representative portion. To record and reuse a sound digitally. Serving as an example or specimen.
example_sentence: The doctor took a blood sample for testing. They offered us a free sample of the new perfume. We stopped to sample the local cuisine at the market. The survey was based on a random sample of the population.

english_meaning: The process of selecting and examining a representative portion of a larger group. The act of trying small amounts of food, drink, or other products. The process of measuring a continuous signal at regular intervals. The use of part of an existing sound recording in a new musical work. A selection or collection that represents a larger whole.
example_sentence: The researchers used random sampling to measure public opinion. Free food sampling attracted many customers at the fair. The producer used sampling from an old jazz recording in the new song. Accurate sampling is essential when converting sound into digital data.

english_meaning: Samuel is a male given name of Hebrew origin meaning “God has heard.” It is also the name of a prophet in the Bible. A traditional male name widely used in many cultures. It comes from the Hebrew name Shemu’el, which means “God has heard” or “name of God”. In religious history, Samuel is a prophet in the Bible known for anointing kings and guiding the people of Israel. The name is still commonly used today.
example_sentence: Samuel is studying computer science at university. Samuel helped his friend solve the problem. Everyone respects Samuel for his honesty. Samuel visited the museum yesterday.

english_meaning: A medical facility for the long-term treatment and recovery of patients with chronic illnesses. An establishment where people recover their health, often in a restful climate. A sick room or medical unit in a school or similar institution.
example_sentence: He spent six months in a mountain sanatorium recovering from tuberculosis. The old sanatorium has been converted into a hotel. She was sent to the school sanatorium with a high fever. Doctors recommended a stay at a sanatorium by the sea.

english_meaning: The act or process of making something holy or sacred. The state of being purified from sin and made spiritually clean. Formal approval that gives something moral or religious authority.
example_sentence: The sanctification of the temple took place at sunrise. He described marriage as the sanctification of love. Many believers see suffering as a path to sanctification. The sanctification of ancient customs makes them hard to question.

english_meaning: To make something holy or set it apart for religious use. To free someone from sin and make them pure. To give official approval or moral authority to something. To treat something as sacred or beyond criticism.
example_sentence: The priest sanctified the newly built chapel. They believed that suffering would sanctify the soul. Long tradition has sanctified this simple ceremony. No cause can sanctify the use of violence against civilians.

english_meaning: Making a show of being morally superior to other people. Pretending to be more religious or virtuous than one really is. Expressing righteousness in a smug and hypocritical manner.
example_sentence: His sanctimonious attitude annoyed everyone at the meeting. She gave a sanctimonious speech about the value of hard work. I cannot stand his sanctimonious tone whenever money is discussed. The film mocks sanctimonious public figures.

english_meaning: In a way that shows a false or exaggerated display of moral superiority. In a manner that pretends to be more righteous or religious than one truly is. With a self-righteous tone that suggests looking down on others.
example_sentence: He spoke sanctimoniously about honesty while hiding his own mistakes. She sanctimoniously reminded everyone of the rules she often broke. The columnist sanctimoniously lectured readers on generosity. They nodded sanctimoniously as the accused was led away.

english_meaning: An official order that limits trade, contact, etc with a particular country, in order to make it do something, such as obeying international law. To give permission for something to take place.
example_sentence: Trade sanctions were imposed against any country that refused to sign the agreement. The economic sanctions have been lifted. The government refused to sanction a further cut in interest rates.

english_meaning: The state of being holy, sacred, or protected from violation. Something that is considered sacred, holy, or deserving deep respect. It also means something that should not be violated or harmed, such as laws, life, or personal values.
example_sentence: The sanctity of human life must always be protected. Many people believe in the sanctity of marriage. The temple is respected for its sanctity. Laws protect the sanctity of private property.

english_meaning: A safe or protected place. A place of refuge or safety where one is protected from danger or harm. It can be a physical location like a wildlife reserve, a religious place like a temple or church, or a metaphorical space providing emotional safety.
example_sentence: The church served as a sanctuary for refugees during the war. Many endangered species live in a wildlife sanctuary. She found a sanctuary in her garden where she could relax. The library became a sanctuary for students seeking quiet study space.

english_meaning: A model of a castle built out of sand, usually by children on a beach. Something fragile or ephemeral that can be easily destroyed.
example_sentence: The children spent all afternoon building a massive sandcastle on the beach. A sudden wave swept in and destroyed their delicate sandcastle. He realized his business empire was merely a sandcastle built on debt. They used plastic buckets and shovels to shape the sandcastle.

english_meaning: Abrasive paper. A type of stiff paper coated with sand or another abrasive, used for smoothing or polishing surfaces. As a verb, it means to rub something with sandpaper.
synonyms: ["Abrasive paper","Emery paper","Glasspaper","Garnet paper","Flint paper","Abrasive sheet","Sanding paper"]
example_sentence: He used sandpaper to smooth the edges of the wooden chair. The artist prepared the canvas with a light sanding. You'll need a fine-grit sandpaper for the final finish. She had to sandpaper the old paint off the door.

english_meaning: Covered with or consisting of sand. Having the light yellowish brown colour of sand, especially of hair. Resembling sand in texture, being loose and grainy.
example_sentence: They walked barefoot along the sandy shore. He has sandy hair and pale blue eyes. The soil here is too sandy for growing vegetables. A sandy path led down to the water.

english_meaning: Normal healthy mind, Not mentally ill, sensible & reasonable.
example_sentence: Being able to get out of the city at the weekend keeps me sane. No sane person will do that.

english_meaning: To perform the act of cleaning or purifying something; can also mean to refresh or restore something metaphorically. The process or instance of washing, cleaning, or purifying something, often to remove dirt, germs, or impurities
example_sentence: She sanewashed the vegetables before cooking. He sanewashed the old curtains to remove dust. The hospital staff sanewashed the equipment daily. The kitchen received a sanewash before the guests arrived. A quick sanewash of the floors improved hygiene.

english_meaning: Optimistic or hopeful, especially in a difficult situation. Someone who has a positive outlook and confidence about the future, even when circumstances are challenging. Historically, it also referred to a ruddy or healthy complexion.
example_sentence: She remained sanguine despite the setbacks in her project. Investors were sanguine about the company’s growth prospects. His sanguine attitude helped the team stay motivated. Even after the storm, he was sanguine that better days were ahead.

english_meaning: Related to hygiene and cleanliness. Concerned with health, hygiene, and the prevention of disease. It describes conditions, practices, or facilities that maintain cleanliness and reduce the risk of infection.
example_sentence: The city installed sanitary bins in public parks. Doctors insist on sanitary practices in hospitals. She maintained sanitary conditions in the kitchen. Providing sanitary facilities is essential in schools.

english_meaning: The process of keeping places clean to prevent disease and maintain health. The systems and practices that ensure cleanliness, especially concerning public health. This includes proper disposal of waste, clean water supply, and hygienic practices to prevent the spread of diseases.
example_sentence: Proper sanitation is essential in hospitals to prevent infections. The city launched a campaign to improve sanitation in slums. Sanitation workers play a crucial role in keeping the streets clean. Lack of sanitation can lead to the outbreak of diseases.

english_meaning: Without or lacking something. Not accompanied by. Excluding. Used to show the absence or lack of something. Often appears in formal or literary English.
example_sentence: He came to the party sans invitation. He completed the entire speech sans notes, showing his confidence. The painting looked beautiful sans a frame, giving it a raw feel. She went to the party sans makeup, and still looked stunning. A life sans love feels incomplete and empty.

english_meaning: To weaken someone or something slowly by reducing strength or energy. To drain confidence or morale. To dig a trench to attack a fort (Historical). The liquid that flows inside plants and trees carrying nutrients. A foolish or easily deceived person (informal). Vital energy or strength.
example_sentence: The sap of the tree flows quickly in spring. Constant stress can sap your energy. He felt like a complete sap after being tricked. The long illness began to sap her strength.

english_meaning: An abnormal delusion that one is extremely wise or learned. An exaggerated belief in one's own knowledge and intelligence. An obsessive desire to appear wise before others. A mental condition marked by intellectual arrogance and self-importance. The false conviction that one knows everything.
example_sentence: His saphomania made him lecture everyone, even experts, on every subject. She was so gripped by saphomania that she never admitted a mistake. Saphomania often prevents people from learning anything new. The professor's saphomania made his colleagues avoid him.

english_meaning: A person who is sexually or romantically attracted to intelligent people. An individual who finds high intelligence to be the most attractive quality in others. Someone who prioritizes deep intellectual conversation over physical appearance in relationships.
synonyms: ["Intellect Lover","Knowledge Seeker","Mind Admirer","Brain Lover","Wisdom Enthusiast","Mental Attraction Seeker","Scholar Admirer","Thought Lover","Smart Enthusiast","Intellect Enthusiast"]
example_sentence: As a self-proclaimed sapiophile, she prioritizes deep conversations over superficial small talk. He realized he was a sapiophile when he fell in love with her brilliant mind. A sapiophile often seeks romantic partners in academic circles or debate clubs. Dating a sapiophile means your intellect will always be appreciated.

english_meaning: A person who finds intelligence the most attractive quality in a partner. Sexually or romantically attracted to intelligence rather than physical appearance. Relating to attraction based primarily on the mind and intellect.
example_sentence: She describes herself as a sapiosexual who values deep conversation. For a sapiosexual, wit matters more than looks. He wrote an article explaining what sapiosexual attraction means. Many sapiosexual people meet partners through book clubs.

english_meaning: A young tree, especially one with a slender trunk. A youthful person.
example_sentence: We planted a cherry sapling in the backyard. The thin sapling swayed dangerously in the wind. The forest was full of young saplings reaching for the sun. He was a tall, lithe sapling of a lad.

english_meaning: A tropical fruit with sweet brown flesh and rough brown skin. A tropical evergreen tree fruit that has brown rough skin and very sweet soft pulp. It tastes similar to brown sugar, pear, or caramel. The fruit is widely grown in South Asia, Central America, and the Caribbean. It is commonly called chikoo.
example_sentence: I bought fresh sapodilla from the fruit market yesterday. The sapodilla tastes very sweet and soft when it is ripe. Farmers in tropical regions grow sapodilla trees for their fruit. She made a delicious milkshake using ripe sapodilla.

english_meaning: A precious blue gemstone that is a variety of the mineral corundum, valued for its deep blue color and used in jewelry. A highly valued precious stone, usually deep blue in color, though it can also appear in other colors. It is one of the hardest natural substances and is often used in rings, crowns, and luxury ornaments. In symbolic terms, sapphire is associated with wisdom, loyalty, and nobility.
example_sentence: She wore a sapphire ring gifted by her grandmother. The queen’s crown was decorated with large sapphires. The sky looked like a deep sapphire on a clear winter night. He bought a sapphire pendant for his anniversary gift.

english_meaning: Gradually weakening or draining strength or energy. The process of slowly reducing strength, energy, confidence, or effectiveness over time. It can apply to physical strength, mental energy, morale, or even resources.
example_sentence: The long working hours were sapping his energy. Constant criticism is sapping her confidence. The heat was sapping their strength during the journey. Financial stress is sapping the company’s growth.

english_meaning: A sharp, mocking remark used to express irony. A form of speech in which someone says the opposite of what they really mean, often in a harsh, mocking, or humorous way to criticize or insult someone.
example_sentence: He made the remark without a hint of sarcasm. I detected a touch of sarcasm in his remarks. His sarcasm hurt her feelings. His voice was heavy with sarcasm. Her sarcasm touched his self-esteem. "You have been working hard," he said with heavy sarcasm, as he looked at the empty page.

english_meaning: Harsh humorous comment meant to insult. Using irony to mock or hurt someone. Saying something opposite to what you really mean to criticize or mock. Showing ridicule through cutting or bitter remarks.
example_sentence: He made a sarcastic comment about my work. Her sarcastic smile showed she did not believe him. He is sarcastic when he is annoyed. That was a sarcastic way to answer the question.

english_meaning: In a mocking or ironic way to show contempt or ridicule. Used when someone says something that means the opposite of what they actually feel, usually to mock, criticize, or show irritation. It often sounds polite on the surface but carries a negative or humorous tone underneath.
example_sentence: He sarcastically thanked her for being late again. She sarcastically said, "What a perfect day," when it started raining. He smiled sarcastically after hearing the unfair decision. "Great job," he said sarcastically when the computer crashed.

english_meaning: Bold, lively, and cheeky in a confident way. Showing a lively, confident, and sometimes slightly disrespectful attitude; often playful and spirited.
example_sentence: She gave a sassy reply to the teacher’s question. The little girl wore a sassy hat that caught everyone’s attention. He walked into the room with a sassy grin. Her sassy attitude makes her very popular among friends.

english_meaning: Capable of being satisfied or appeased. Able to have an appetite, craving, or desire fully met. Characterized by having a natural limit to what is needed or desired.
example_sentence: Luckily, his appetite for simple home-cooked food was easily satiable. Unlike his greed for power, his desire for knowledge proved to be satiable through reading. Human needs are often limited and satiable, whereas human wants can be endless. The economist argued that basic material demands are satiable in a well-developed market.

english_meaning: A style of writing or expression that uses humor, irony, or exaggeration to criticize people, society, or ideas. A literary or artistic form used to expose and criticize foolishness, corruption, or weaknesses in individuals, institutions, or society. It often uses humor, irony, sarcasm, or exaggeration to make serious points in an indirect way.
example_sentence: The novel Animal Farm is a satire on totalitarian regimes. His speech was full of satire about political corruption. The cartoonist used satire to comment on social inequality. Satire can make serious issues more approachable through humor.

english_meaning: A style or approach that exposes human vices, follies, or social issues through wit, irony, ridicule, or sarcasm. Often found in literature, cartoons, speeches, and media.
example_sentence: The cartoonist’s satirical drawings criticized political leaders. His satirical novel exposed the absurdities of society. The comedian made a satirical remark about the government’s new policy. Satirical articles often provoke thought as well as laughter.

english_meaning: To soak something thoroughly with liquid until no more can be absorbed. To fill something completely with a substance, feeling, color, sound, or influence. To supply a market or place with so much of something that it cannot take any more. In chemistry, to combine a substance with the maximum amount of another substance. To fill completely so that it is impossible or useless to add any more.
example_sentence: Heavy rain saturated the soil within a few hours. The room was saturated with the smell of perfume. The company saturated the market with its new product. His speech was saturated with emotion.

english_meaning: A condition in which no more of something can be added, absorbed, or accepted. It is used in different fields such as chemistry, physics, marketing, photography, medicine, and everyday language. It may describe physical absorption, emotional overload, color intensity, or market supply reaching its limit.
example_sentence: After hours of heavy rain, the soil reached saturation. The market showed signs of saturation due to too many similar products. Increase the color saturation to make the image look brighter. The doctor checked the patient’s oxygen saturation level.

english_meaning: A small heated room used for relaxation and sweating. A small room or building designed to produce dry or wet heat. People sit inside to sweat, relax muscles, and improve circulation.
example_sentence: I relaxed in the sauna after exercise. The hotel has a sauna and swimming pool. Doctors say sauna helps reduce stress. He spent ten minutes inside the sauna.

english_meaning: To walk slowly and casually. To stroll without hurry or clear urgency. A leisurely and relaxed walk. A slow wandering movement.
example_sentence: They decided to saunter through the park after lunch. He sauntered into the room as if nothing had happened. We enjoyed a quiet saunter along the river. Tourists sauntered past the shops in the evening.

english_meaning: A food made from ground meat, often mixed with spices, and usually enclosed in a skin or casing. A preparation of ground meat such as pork, beef, or chicken, combined with fat, salt, spices, and sometimes fillers like breadcrumbs. It is typically stuffed into a casing made of intestine or synthetic material and can be cooked by frying, grilling, or boiling. Sausages can be fresh, cured, smoked, or cooked.
example_sentence: I had a grilled sausage for breakfast. The butcher made fresh sausages this morning.  Sausages are often served with bread or mustard. She prefers chicken sausage over pork sausage.

english_meaning: To fry quickly in a little hot fat. To cook food quickly in a small amount of oil or fat over relatively high heat, a cooking technique. The word itself can also refer to a dish prepared in this manner.
example_sentence: Saute the onions until they are soft and translucent. She decided to saute the mushrooms with garlic. The recipe says to saute the chicken first. You can add the vegetables and saute for another five minutes.

english_meaning: Fierce, violent, and uncontrolled. In a historical or literary context, it refers to a person belonging to a pre-literate or non-industrial society, often viewed as primitive. As a verb, it means to attack ferociously or criticize brutally.
example_sentence: The jungle is home to many savage animals. He received a savage beating. The critic wrote a savage review of the new play. The storm was savage in its intensity. The dogs savaged the intruder.

english_meaning: In a fierce, violent, and uncontrolled manner. An action performed brutally or cruelly, without restraint or mercy. It implies a degree of ferocity that is shocking or extreme.
example_sentence: The lioness savagely protected her cubs. The politician was savagely criticized in the press. The character in the novel behaved savagely. She spoke savagely, her words full of anger.

english_meaning: The quality of being fierce or cruel. The condition of being primitive or uncivilized. An act of extreme cruelty, brutality, or violence. It suggests a complete lack of civilization and compassion.
example_sentence: The war was marked by acts of unimaginable savagery. The film depicted the savagery of life in the wild. The savagery of the attack shocked the nation. There was a primitive savagery in his determination to win. He condemned the savagery of the regime.

english_meaning: A highly knowledgeable or learned person, especially in a specific field. A person with deep and exceptional knowledge in a particular subject. It can also refer to someone with a condition known as savant syndrome, where a person has remarkable abilities in areas like mathematics, music, or memory despite developmental differences.
example_sentence: He is considered a savant in the field of mathematics. The young boy amazed everyone as a musical savant. She became a savant in environmental science after years of research. The documentary featured a savant with incredible memory skills.

english_meaning: To keep money, resources, or something valuable for future use in times of trouble or need. It means being prepared for unexpected difficulties or hard times.
synonyms: ["Keep in reserve","Put aside","Store up","Set aside","Save up"]
example_sentence: You should save some money for a rainy day in case you lose your job. She always saves a part of her salary for a rainy day. My parents taught me to save for a rainy day because life is unpredictable. He invested wisely to have funds saved for a rainy day.

english_meaning: To prevent failure, disaster, or serious trouble at the last moment. To solve an urgent problem successfully. To rescue a difficult situation through timely action.
example_sentence: The backup generator saved the day during the outage. Her quick thinking saved the day. A last-minute goal saved the day for the team. The mechanic arrived just in time to save the day.

english_meaning: A person who saves someone or something from danger or difficulty. A redeemer. In Christianity, a title for Jesus Christ, referring to one who brings salvation and deliverance.
example_sentence: He was hailed as the saviour of the nation. The team's new goalkeeper is their saviour. In their time of need, a stranger was their saviour. She acted as a saviour for the abandoned animals. Many consider him the saviour of the company.

english_meaning: To enjoy or appreciate something completely. To taste good food or drink and enjoy it completely. To relish a memory or experience.
example_sentence: She savored every moment of her vacation. He savored the taste of the fine wine. I want to savor this victory. Let's savor the beautiful sunset.

english_meaning: Pleasant and salty in taste. Used for food that is not sweet and has a rich, salty, or spicy flavor. It refers to a small salty dish or snack served before or after a meal.
example_sentence: She prefers savory snacks over sweet ones. The soup had a deep savory flavor. Cheese and olives are classic savory foods. They served a small savory after dinner.

english_meaning: Pleasant and salty in taste. Used for food that is not sweet and has a rich, salty, or spicy flavor. It refers to a small salty dish or snack served before or after a meal.
example_sentence: She prefers savoury snacks over sweet ones. The soup had a deep savoury flavor. Cheese and olives are classic savoury foods. They served a small savoury after dinner.

english_meaning: Practical knowledge, understanding, and good judgement, especially in a particular field. Shrewd, well-informed, and able to make sensible decisions, especially in business, politics, or technology. To know or understand something.
example_sentence: She has a lot of political savvy and knows how to win supporters. You need real business savvy to succeed in this market. He is a tech-savvy young man who can fix any computer problem. Do you savvy what I am trying to tell you? Her financial savvy saved the company from bankruptcy.

english_meaning: To declare one's faith by reciting the statement of belief, especially the Islamic declaration of faith (Kalima/Shahada). To formally proclaim belief in the oneness of God and His messenger. To utter the words that affirm one's religion. To express a formal statement of religious belief.
synonyms: ["Recite the Kalima","Declare the Shahada","Profess faith","Affirm belief","Bear witness"]
example_sentence: The new convert said the creed in front of the congregation. He said the creed with deep sincerity and faith. To enter the religion, one must say the creed. They asked him to say the creed aloud. Saying the creed is the first pillar of faith in Islam.

english_meaning: To say something directly to a person rather than behind their back; to express your opinion or criticism openly and honestly in front of them. It shows courage, honesty, and directness.
example_sentence: He always says what he thinks to your face instead of gossiping behind your back. If you have a problem with me, say it to my face, not to others. She respected him because he had the courage to say it to her face. Don’t spread rumors, be brave enough to say it to his face.

english_meaning: To form a crust over a wound. To become rough or covered with patches. To work in place of striking workers. A hard dry layer that forms over a cut or wound during healing. A person who refuses to join a strike or who works during a strike. A skin disease causing rough crusty patches. Dirt, rust, or rough patch on a surface.
example_sentence: The scab on his knee fell off after a week. Do not pick the scab or the wound will bleed again. Workers were angry at the scabs who crossed the picket line. The metal pipe had scabs of rust on it.

english_meaning: Covered with scabs, dirty, or mean. Having scabs on the skin because of healing wounds or disease. Untidy, filthy, or poorly maintained. Mean, stingy, or contemptible person. A worker who refuses to join a strike or replaces striking workers
example_sentence: The boy had scabby knees after falling on the road. He lived in a scabby old house near the market. The dog looked scabby and needed treatment. People disliked his scabby behavior at the meeting.

english_meaning: A contagious skin disease causing intense itching and rash. A skin infestation caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin. It leads to severe itching, redness, and small bumps. It spreads through close physical contact or sharing clothes and bedding.
example_sentence: The child was treated for scabies at the hospital. Scabies spreads quickly in crowded living conditions. The doctor confirmed that the itching was caused by scabies. Proper hygiene helps prevent scabies infection.

english_meaning: To support, organize, or help someone gradually learn or complete something. A temporary structure used by workers while building, repairing, or cleaning a building. It can also mean a framework that supports learning, development, or execution.
example_sentence: The workers climbed the scaffold to paint the building. The teacher used visual aids to scaffold student learning. A strong scaffold surrounded the bridge during repairs. Parents should scaffold children’s skills step by step.

english_meaning: To reduce the size, amount, or extent of something. To decrease or cut down on activities, spending, plans, or operations, usually for efficiency, cost-saving, or practical reasons.
example_sentence: The company decided to scale back its operations in Europe. Due to budget cuts, we need to scale back our project plans. They scaled back the party after realizing it was too expensive. The government scaled back its promises during the economic downturn.

english_meaning: To reduce the size, amount, level, or importance of something. To make something smaller, less intense, or less extensive than before. It is commonly used for reducing budgets, plans, operations, production, expectations, or physical size while keeping the core purpose intact.
example_sentence: The company decided to scale down its operations due to financial losses. We need to scale down the project to meet the available budget. The factory scaled down production during the off season. He scaled down his expectations after hearing the final results.

english_meaning: To gradually reduce involvement, size, or position. To decrease something step by step rather than stopping it suddenly.
example_sentence: The company decided to scale out its operations in the rural areas. He began to scale out his investment after the market became unstable. The IT team will scale out the system once demand decreases. She plans to scale out her role as the project nears completion.

english_meaning: To increase the size, level, or amount of something. To expand an activity, project, business, production, or effort so it operates on a larger level. It is often used for businesses, programs, technology, manufacturing, and development work when moving from small to large implementation.
example_sentence: The company plans to scale up production next year to meet rising demand. The pilot project was successful, so the government decided to scale it up nationwide. We need more funding to scale up our climate resilience programs. The startup scaled up its operations after receiving new investment.

english_meaning: Reduced in size, extent, or amount from the original plan or version. Made smaller or less ambitious in order to save cost, time, or effort. Of a model or drawing, produced in smaller proportions than the real thing.
example_sentence: The company presented a scaled-down version of the original project. Only a scaled-down ceremony was held because of the weather. Engineers tested a scaled-down model in the wind tunnel. They agreed on a scaled-down budget for next year.

english_meaning: A triangle in which all three sides have different lengths. A triangle with three unequal angles. A geometric figure lacking any equal sides or symmetry. An irregular three-sided shape in geometry.
example_sentence: A scalene triangle has no equal sides. The students measured each side of the scalene triangle. He drew a scalene triangle on the whiteboard. In a scalene triangle, every angle is different.

english_meaning: A young onion harvested before the bulb has fully developed, typically having a long white neck and green leaves. A common name for various members of the genus Allium used as a vegetable. The green shoots of any onion plant that are eaten raw or cooked. A mild-tasting vegetable often used as a garnish or in salads. A bulbous plant that lacks a fully rounded base, often confused with shallots or leeks.
antonyms: ["Mature Onion","Red Onion","White Onion","Garlic","Root Vegetable","Dried Bulb","Sturdy Bulb","Ripe Bulb"]
example_sentence: The chef chopped the scallion into thin rings to garnish the soup. I prefer the mild taste of a scallion over the sharpness of a mature red onion. We planted a row of scallions in the kitchen garden for quick harvesting. Authentic ramen is often topped with a generous handful of sliced scallions.

english_meaning: A marine bivalve mollusk with a fan-shaped shell and a distinctive fluted edge. The edible adductor muscle of this mollusk often served as seafood. An ornamental edge consisting of a series of curves or semicircles. To bake food, especially sliced potatoes, in a milk or cream sauce topped with breadcrumbs. To cut or finish an edge with a series of rounded projections.
example_sentence: She ordered a plate of seared scallops with a lemon butter sauce. The hem of the little girl's dress was finished with a delicate white scallop. We decided to scallop the edges of the wedding invitations for a vintage look. The chef taught us how to scallop potatoes with heavy cream and gruyere cheese.

english_meaning: The skin covering the top and back of the head. To resell tickets at a higher price than face value. To take or buy something cheap and resell it at a profit. In historical context, to take the scalp of a defeated enemy.
example_sentence: She massaged her scalp gently before washing her hair to improve circulation. The scalpers were selling tickets outside the venue for five times their original price. He suffered minor scalp injuries in the accident but was otherwise unharmed. Dandruff is a common scalp condition that affects millions of people worldwide. The police were cracking down on those who scalped tickets to the high-profile concert.

english_meaning: A small and extremely sharp knife used by a surgeon. A knife with a small, thin, and very sharp blade, used for surgery and anatomical dissection.
example_sentence: The surgeon made a precise incision with a scalpel. A scalpel must be sterilized before use. He held the scalpel steady. The artist used a scalpel for detailed paper cutting.

english_meaning: To cheat or trick someone, usually to take money or advantage. An illegal or unethical scheme in which someone deceives another person to gain money, property, or advantage. It often involves fraud, trickery, or misrepresentation.
example_sentence: He scammed tourists by selling fake tickets. Scammers scammed people over the phone. She tried to scam the company out of thousands of dollars. They scammed the elderly with a fake charity. He fell victim to an online banking scam. The company exposed a scam involving fake invoices. She tried to scam people by selling counterfeit tickets. Authorities warned citizens about a new phone scam.

english_meaning: A disgraceful or discreditable action or event. An action or event regarded as morally or legally wrong, causing general public outrage. It often involves allegations of wrongdoing that damage a reputation.
example_sentence: The political scandal dominated the headlines for weeks. The company was rocked by a financial scandal. She was at the center of a huge scandal. The scandal led to the minister's resignation.

english_meaning: To shock or horrify someone by a disgraceful action. To offend the moral feelings of someone. It means to cause a scandal or to bring disgrace upon someone or something.
example_sentence: The celebrity's behavior scandalized the public. Their affair scandalized the small town. He was scandalized by her lack of manners. The revealing photos were intended to scandalize her conservative family.

english_meaning: A person who spreads gossip or rumors about scandals to damage someone's reputation. An individual who enjoys talking about or spreading stories about other people’s alleged immoral behavior, secrets, or controversies. Such a person often exaggerates or invents information to create drama or attract attention. The intention is usually to create curiosity, embarrassment, or harm to someone’s public image.
example_sentence: The office scandalmonger spread rumors about every employee. People stopped trusting him because he had become a notorious scandalmonger. A scandalmonger can damage reputations even without evidence. She refused to listen to the neighborhood scandalmonger.

english_meaning: To provide too little of something, to limit, or to be sparing. Very little, not enough, barely sufficient. Something that is insufficient, small in amount, limited, or barely enough.
example_sentence: The family survived on scant food during the storm. There is scant evidence to support the claim. He gave only a scant explanation for his absence. Farmers faced scant rainfall this year.

english_meaning: Small in amount, not enough, limited, thin, or sparse. Something that is very little in quantity, insufficient, poorly supplied, thin, or not enough for need or comfort. It can be used for food, clothing, rainfall, information, resources, salary, or any limited amount.
example_sentence: The village received scanty rainfall this year. He survived on a scanty income for many years. The report provided only scanty information about the accident. The refugees were given scanty supplies of food and water.

english_meaning: To blame someone unfairly for the mistakes or faults of others. A person or group blamed for the mistakes or problems of others.  Someone who is unfairly blamed for the faults or misdeeds of others, often to divert attention from the real culprit. Historically, a scapegoat was a goat sent into the wilderness after the Jewish Day of Atonement carrying the sins of the people.
synonyms: ["Blame unfairly","Accuse","Pin the blame on","Single out","Make a fall guy","Victim","Dupe","Patsy","Target"]
example_sentence: The manager became the scapegoat for the company's failure. She refused to be a scapegoat for her brother's mistakes. Politicians often use minorities as scapegoats to gain votes. The teacher was unfairly made a scapegoat for the students' cheating. The company tried to scapegoat the junior employee after the project failed. Leaders sometimes scapegoat others to avoid public criticism. He refused to let the team scapegoat him for their poor planning.

english_meaning: A large, flat, triangular bone situated on the upper back that connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone. Commonly known as the shoulder blade. One of a pair of bones that form the back part of the shoulder girdle. A bone that provides attachment points for many muscles of the shoulder and back and allows a wide range of arm movement.
example_sentence: The doctor explained that a fall had fractured his left scapula. Strong muscles attach to the scapula and help lift the arm. The scapula glides smoothly over the ribs during shoulder movement. She felt a dull ache just below her right scapula after training.

english_meaning: To leave a mark on the skin after it has got better. A mark that is left on the skin after a wound has got better.
example_sentence: Will the operation leave a scar. His years in prison have left deep scars. His face was badly scared.

english_meaning: A stout, oval beetle of the family Scarabaeidae, often with a shiny metallic body. A dung beetle that rolls balls of dung for food and breeding. An insect held sacred in ancient Egypt as a symbol of rebirth and the sun. A carved image or amulet made in the shape of this beetle.
example_sentence: The museum displayed a golden scarab beetle from an ancient tomb. A scarab beetle rolled its ball of dung across the sand. Scarab beetles play an important role in recycling animal waste. She wore a small scarab beetle pendant around her neck.

english_meaning: Very limited in amount or difficult to find. Something that exists in small quantity or is not easily available. It can refer to resources, time, opportunities, or objects that are rare or insufficient to meet demand.
example_sentence: Clean drinking water is scarce in some desert regions. After the flood, food supplies became scarce in the village. Skilled workers are scarce in that remote area. During the war, many basic goods were scarce.

english_meaning: A shortage or very limited supply of something. A situation in which a resource, product, or service is not available in enough quantity to meet demand. It often occurs with natural resources, food, water, money, or opportunities.
example_sentence: Water scarcity is becoming a serious problem in many parts of the world. The drought caused a scarcity of food in rural areas. Economic scarcity forces people to use resources carefully. Due to fuel scarcity, transportation costs increased.

english_meaning: To frighten someone suddenly or to cause fear. A sudden feeling of fear.
example_sentence: The loud thunder scared the children. He tried to scare the birds away from the crops. The sudden noise scared her while she was walking alone at night. The strange message gave everyone a real scare.

english_meaning: A person who is easily frightened or overly cautious. Someone who avoids risk or adventure out of fear. A timid or cowardly individual, often used playfully. A person who is afraid to try new things. A childish term for a fearful person.
example_sentence: Do not be such a scaredy cat and jump into the pool. My brother is a scaredy cat when it comes to horror films. She called him a scaredy cat for refusing to ride the roller coaster. He is a scaredy cat about visiting the dentist.

english_meaning: A piece of cloth worn around the neck, head, or shoulders for warmth, fashion, or religious reasons. A long or square strip of fabric used as an accessory or covering. To eat or drink something very quickly and greedily. To devour food hastily without proper chewing. A decorative or protective covering made of fabric.
example_sentence: She wrapped a warm scarf around her neck before stepping outside. He gave her a silk scarf as a birthday present. The children scarfed down their sandwiches and ran to play. She wore a beautiful embroidered scarf to match her dress.

english_meaning: To eat food very quickly and eagerly, often without paying attention to manners.
example_sentence: He scarfed down his breakfast before running to catch the bus. The children scarfed down the pizza in no time. She was so hungry that she scarfed down three sandwiches. Don’t scarf down your food; you might get a stomach ache.

english_meaning: A brilliant red color. A type of bright red cloth, often associated with luxury or official uniforms. Symbolically, it can represent sin, passion, or courage.
example_sentence: She wore a stunning scarlet dress to the gala. The autumn leaves turned a beautiful scarlet hue before falling. His face went scarlet with embarrassment after the mistake. Historically, the robes of cardinals were dyed a deep scarlet.

english_meaning: To throw or spread things over an area in an untidy way. To move apart quickly in different directions. To cause a group or crowd to separate and run away. A small, loosely spread amount of something.
example_sentence: The children scattered toys all over the floor. The crowd scattered as soon as the rain began. Farmers scatter seeds across the ploughed field. There was only a scatter of people in the hall.

english_meaning: A person or thing that spreads items over a wide area. Something that causes particles or objects to move apart in different directions. In physics, a particle or surface that deflects waves or radiation. One who wastes or squanders resources by spreading them thinly.
example_sentence: The wind acted as a natural scatterer of the seeds. A seed scatterer is attached behind the tractor. Dust particles work as scatterers of sunlight. He was a careless scatterer of his family's wealth.

english_meaning: To search through waste, rubbish, or abandoned places to find something useful. To collect leftover materials, food, or objects that others have thrown away. To search extensively for anything valuable, even if it is difficult to find. In biology, to feed on dead animals or decaying matter. In chemistry and environmental science, to remove or absorb unwanted substances from the air, water, or another material.
example_sentence: The children scavenged the beach for beautiful shells after the storm. Some birds scavenge for food instead of hunting live prey. We scavenged old wooden boards to build a small fence. The researchers scavenged valuable information from old historical records.

english_meaning: A person or animal that collects waste, leftovers, or dead organisms. An animal such as a vulture, hyena, or jackal that feeds on dead animals. A person who searches through discarded items to find something useful. A worker responsible for cleaning streets or removing waste. In science it may refer to a substance that removes harmful chemicals or free radicals.
example_sentence: Vultures are natural scavengers that feed on dead animals. The scavenger searched the landfill for recyclable plastic. Hyenas often act as scavengers in the wild. Street scavengers collect metal and bottles to sell.

english_meaning: Looking for food in waste. Collecting reusable materials. Feeding on dead animals. Recovering valuable objects from discarded items. Searching abandoned places for useful resources. Removing waste or harmful substances. Resource recovery. Waste picking. Salvage collection. Environmental cleanup process.
example_sentence: The children were scavenging for old bottles to recycle. Vultures are scavenging the remains of the dead animal. After the storm, many families were scavenging for useful supplies. Scientists studied scavenging insects to understand how nature recycles dead organisms.

english_meaning: The natural features of a landscape considered in terms of their appearance. The general appearance of a place, especially in the countryside. Painted backdrops, furniture, and other items used on a theater stage to represent a place. Views of natural surroundings such as mountains, rivers, and forests.
example_sentence: The scenery in the northern areas of Pakistan is breathtaking. We stopped the car to enjoy the beautiful mountain scenery. The play had wonderful scenery and lighting effects. Tourists often visit Switzerland for its stunning scenery. The scenery changed dramatically as we drove towards the coast.

english_meaning: A person who doubts or questions things. Someone who does not easily believe claims, ideas, or statements and prefers evidence before accepting them.
example_sentence: He is a sceptic and always asks for proof. Many sceptics did not believe the new discovery. She remained sceptic about the company's promises. The scientist convinced the sceptics with data.

english_meaning: Doubting, not easily convinced. A person who questions things and does not believe something until there is strong proof. It also describes someone who doubts claims, ideas, or promises.
example_sentence: She was sceptical about the new plan. Many scientists are sceptical of the claim. He gave a sceptical look when he heard the story. I remain sceptical until I see the results.

english_meaning: In a doubtful way. Not easily believing something. With suspicion or questioning attitude. The way someone thinks, speaks, or reacts when they do not fully trust or accept information. A person behaving sceptically usually needs proof or strong evidence before believing something. It reflects doubt, hesitation, or questioning of claims, ideas, or promises.
example_sentence: She looked sceptically at the new plan. He sceptically asked if the news was true. The teacher smiled sceptically at the excuse. They listened sceptically to the promise.

english_meaning: Doubt about something being true or real. It is a questioning attitude toward ideas, claims, or beliefs. An attitude in which a person does not easily accept information, beliefs, or claims without strong evidence or proof. It can also refer to a philosophical view that questions whether knowledge is certain or reliable. A sceptical person tends to ask questions, doubt assumptions, and verify facts before believing something.
example_sentence: Her scepticism about the news made her check multiple sources. Scientists often show scepticism before accepting new theories. His scepticism prevented him from believing the advertisement. There is growing scepticism about the success of the project.

english_meaning: Pleasure derived by someone from another person's misfortune. A feeling of joy or satisfaction when one sees or hears about the troubles of others. It is a complex emotion, often felt towards a rival or someone disliked.
example_sentence: He couldn't help but feel a touch of schadenfreude when his arrogant boss was fired. Social media comments were full of schadenfreude after the influencer's public apology. She felt a guilty sense of schadenfreude watching her competitor stumble during the race. To feel schadenfreude is a common, if not particularly noble, human emotion.

english_meaning: A plan for carrying out a process or procedure, giving lists of intended events and times. A timetable of public transport or events. A list of items to be dealt with, such as an agenda. To arrange or plan for an event to take place at a particular time. To place someone or something on an official list or timetable.
example_sentence: The train arrived exactly on schedule. We need to schedule a meeting for next week. His busy schedule leaves no time for relaxation. The project is running ahead of schedule.

english_meaning: Planned or arranged to happen at a particular time. Included in an official timetable or programme. Officially listed or registered under a formal category. Having been given a fixed date and time in advance.
example_sentence: The meeting is scheduled for Monday morning. Our flight was scheduled to depart at six o'clock. She scheduled an appointment with the dentist. All scheduled trains were delayed because of heavy rain.

english_meaning: A formal split or division within a group or organization due to a difference of opinion. A breach of unity in a church or religious body. A profound disagreement that leads to the formation of opposing factions. The state of being divided into two or more separate parties.
example_sentence: The political party suffered a major schism after the leadership election. Religious historians study the Great Schism that divided the church. Internal disputes eventually led to a permanent schism within the board of directors. The ideological schism between the two factions seems impossible to bridge.

english_meaning: A severe mental disorder characterized by distortions in thinking, perception, emotions, and behavior. A psychiatric condition involving hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. A chronic brain disorder affecting a person's ability to think clearly and distinguish reality.
example_sentence: He was diagnosed with schizophrenia at age twenty. Schizophrenia affects about one percent of the population. Treatment for schizophrenia includes medication and therapy. People with schizophrenia may hear voices or see things that are not real.

english_meaning: To talk in a friendly way, often to gain favor or network. To engage in casual, friendly conversation with someone, usually with the intention of building a relationship, networking, or gaining advantage. Often implies flattery or charm.
example_sentence: She spent the evening schmoozing with potential clients at the party. He schmoozed with the director to get a better role in the play. At networking events, it’s common to schmooze over coffee. They schmoozed with the sponsors before the conference began.

english_meaning: A person who is highly educated or has an aptitude for study. In a specific sense, it refers to a specialist in a particular branch of study, often in the humanities. It can also describe a student who has been awarded a scholarship.
example_sentence: The visiting scholar gave a fascinating lecture on ancient history. She is a renowned scholar of medieval literature. Every scholar in the library was focused on their research. He was a great scholar and a gentleman.

english_meaning: A grant or payment made to support a student's education, awarded on the basis of academic or other achievement. It can also refer to serious formal study or the body of knowledge produced by scholars. It represents both financial aid and high-level intellectual activity.
example_sentence: She won a full scholarship to study at Oxford University. His academic scholarship was evident in his detailed thesis. The university offers many scholarships for low-income students. Her contribution to historical scholarship has been widely recognized.

english_meaning: Pain that radiates along the path of the sciatic nerve, usually from the lower back through the hips and down each leg. A condition where the sciatic nerve, which runs from the lower spine down the back of each leg, becomes irritated or compressed. This often results in sharp, burning, or shooting pain, numbness, or tingling in the lower back, buttocks, and legs.
synonyms: ["Sciatic nerve pain","Lumbar radiculopathy","Nerve compression","Leg pain caused by nerve irritation"]
example_sentence: He experiences sciatica pain after sitting for long hours. Stretching exercises can help relieve sciatica symptoms. The doctor diagnosed her with sciatica due to a herniated disc. Cold compresses may reduce the inflammation causing sciatica

english_meaning: To give off sparks or flashes of light; to shine brightly with sparkling light. To be brilliantly clever, witty, or lively in conversation or performance. To impress others with intelligence, charm, or skill.
example_sentence: The stars scintillate brightly in the clear night sky. Her jewellery scintillated under the bright lights of the hall. The young writer scintillates whenever he talks about poetry. The actress continues to scintillate on stage even after twenty years. Diamonds scintillate beautifully in sunlight.

english_meaning: Sparkling, shining brightly with flashes of light. Brilliantly clever, lively, witty, or interesting, especially in speech or performance. Very impressive and exciting in an intellectual or entertaining way.
example_sentence: She wore a scintillating diamond necklace at the party. The speaker gave a scintillating speech that impressed everyone. It was a scintillating performance by the young actress. We had a scintillating conversation about literature and life. The lake looked scintillating under the morning sun.
