english_meaning: A descendant of a notable family; the youngest member of a dynasty. Also refers to a shoot or twig cut from a plant and used in grafting.
example_sentence: He was the scion of a wealthy banking family. As the scion of a political dynasty, she entered parliament early. The gardener attached the scion to the rootstock carefully. She was the last scion of the royal bloodline.

english_meaning: The tough, white outer coat of the eyeball. The fibrous layer that gives the eye its shape and protects the delicate inner parts. The visible white area surrounding the coloured iris of the eye.
synonyms: ["White of the eye","Sclerotic coat","Outer eye coat","Fibrous tunic"]
example_sentence: The sclera is the white part of the eye. Yellowing of the sclera may be a sign of jaundice. The sclera keeps the eyeball firm and round. Six small muscles are attached to the sclera.

english_meaning: The abnormal hardening of body tissue. A disease characterized by the hardening and thickening of tissue. A condition involving the formation of scar tissue that replaces normal tissue. The loss of elasticity in body structures due to fibrous tissue buildup.
example_sentence: Multiple sclerosis affects the nervous system. Arteriosclerosis is the hardening of arteries. The patient was diagnosed with liver sclerosis. Sclerosis can lead to organ dysfunction.

english_meaning: To speak angrily to someone for a mistake. To express anger or disapproval toward someone, usually because they have done something wrong. It often involves speaking in a sharp or harsh tone to correct behavior.
example_sentence: The teacher scolded the student for being late. She scolded her brother for breaking the window. He got scolded by his boss for missing the deadline. Parents often scold their children to teach discipline. She is known as a scold in her family. Nobody likes a constant scold. The old man had a reputation as a village scold.

english_meaning: A utensil resembling a spoon, with a short handle and a deep bowl. A piece of exclusive news published or broadcast before one's rivals. The quantity of material taken up by a scoop. The act of picking something up in a swift, continuous movement.
example_sentence: Use the metal scoop to measure the coffee beans. The journalist received an anonymous tip and got the biggest scoop of her career. Can I have one scoop of vanilla and one of chocolate? The crane will scoop up the debris from the construction site.

english_meaning: To move quickly or suddenly. To go or leave in a hurry. To slide or move a short distance while seated.
example_sentence: The kids scooted down the hill on their scooters. He scooted over to make space for her on the bench. It’s getting late, I’d better scoot home before dark. The cat scooted under the table when it heard the noise.

english_meaning: To move slightly to make space for someone else to sit or fit. To shift or slide a short distance, usually sideways.
example_sentence: Could you please scoot over a bit so I can sit down? He scooted over to make room for his friend on the bench. When the cat jumped on the bed, she scooted over to give it space. The kids had to scoot over to fit everyone in the picture.

english_meaning: To burn the surface of something slightly. To become discolored or damaged by heat.
example_sentence: The fire scorched the walls. His shirt was scorched by the iron. The sun scorched the fields. Hot water scorched her hand.

english_meaning: Pass rapidly and intensely. To move through or across something quickly while producing heat, energy, or impact, often used figuratively.
example_sentence: The athlete scorched through the finish line. Flames scorched through the forest. His anger scorched through the room. The car scorched through the tunnel.

english_meaning: Heat intensely. To cause something to burn, dry, or blacken, usually by direct heat.
example_sentence: The stove scorched up the pan. The sunlight scorched up the soil. He scorched up the toast. Fire scorched up the wooden beams.

english_meaning: Burnt or damaged. Having been burned, charred, or damaged by heat, often used as an adjective describing objects or surfaces.
example_sentence: The scorched bread smelled terrible. His scorched hair needed treatment. The scorched earth glowed under the sun. Scorched marks were visible on the carpet.

english_meaning: Total destruction strategy. A military or figurative tactic of destroying everything that might be useful to an enemy or rival.
example_sentence: The army left a scorched earth behind. They practiced a scorched earth policy in business. The retreating troops used scorched earth tactics. The forest fire left a scorched earth.

english_meaning: Extremely hot, often uncomfortably so. Burning the surface of something with intense heat. Severely critical or harsh in tone. Very fast or intense in speed or performance.
example_sentence: We walked through the market in the scorching afternoon heat. The scorching sun made the metal too hot to touch. The critic wrote a scorching review of the film. He set a scorching pace in the final lap.

english_meaning: The feeling or expression of contempt or derision. Open disrespect for someone or something. To reject, refuse, or dismiss something with contempt. It implies a strong sense of superiority over the object of contempt.
example_sentence: She looked at him with utter scorn when he lied. The determined artist scorned the critics' negative reviews and continued her work. His offer of a bribe was met with scorn. They poured scorn on his revolutionary ideas, only to adopt them years later.

english_meaning: Showing open contempt or strong disrespect. Mocking or rejecting someone or something as worthless or inferior. Characterized by derision, disdain, or a proud lack of respect.
example_sentence: He was scornful of their attempts to solve the problem. She responded with a scornful smile. The audience gave the dishonest speaker a scornful reception. His scornful tone made the young employee feel small. They rejected the proposal with scornful laughter.

english_meaning: A venomous arachnid with pincers and a curved tail ending in a stinger. A nocturnal desert creature that paralyses its prey with venom. A sign of the zodiac represented by this creature, also called Scorpio. Figuratively, a person who is bitter, spiteful, or quick to harm others.
example_sentence: A scorpion was hiding beneath the old wooden crate. He was stung by a scorpion while camping in the desert. Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light. Always shake out your shoes to check for a scorpion.

english_meaning: To escape without punishment or harm. Escaping a difficult situation, crime, mistake, or responsibility without receiving any punishment, damage, or negative consequence, even when punishment was expected.
example_sentence: The thief got off scot-free. He made a mistake but escaped scot-free. No one should go scot-free after breaking the law. The politician walked scot-free despite corruption.

english_meaning: Fear of darkness. An intense, irrational, and persistent fear of darkness or being in the dark. It may cause anxiety, panic attacks, or avoidance behaviors.
example_sentence: She avoids walking home at night because of her scotophobia. Scotophobia can make sleeping alone very difficult. Children with scotophobia often need a night light. His scotophobia worsened after the power outage.

english_meaning: A dishonest or wicked person. Someone who behaves in a morally wrong, deceitful, or dishonorable way. Often used to describe a person who cheats, betrays, or harms others for personal gain.
example_sentence: He turned out to be a scoundrel who lied about his past. Only a scoundrel would steal from an old friend. The villain in the story was a cunning scoundrel. Don’t trust him; he is a known scoundrel in town.

english_meaning: To explore or examine an area. To search for information or opportunities. To look for talent or resources. A person who collects information, especially about an unknown place or enemy. A member of an organization like Boy Scouts. Someone who searches for talent, locations, or opportunities.
example_sentence: The scout went ahead of the team to check the route. She works as a talent scout for a sports company. The soldiers were sent to scout the area before the mission. He scouted several locations before choosing the perfect one.

english_meaning: Frown. A facial expression of displeasure. To frown in an angry or bad-tempered way. It involves furrowing one's brows and turning down the corners of the mouth.
example_sentence: He scowled at me from across the room. The teacher gave a scowl to the noisy students. She had a permanent scowl on her face. Don't scowl, it will give you wrinkles.

english_meaning: To scratch or grope around with one's fingers to find or hold onto something. A popular board game where players form words.
example_sentence: She had to scrabble around in her bag to find her keys. The climber had to scrabble for a grip on the loose rocks. We spent the rainy Sunday afternoon playing a game of Scrabble. The hungry puppy began to scrabble at the door for food.

english_meaning: Growing in an untidy, irregular, and uneven way. Ragged and poorly kept in appearance. Thin and straggling, as of hair, plants, or a beard.
example_sentence: He had a scraggly beard that needed trimming. A few scraggly bushes grew beside the wall. Her scraggly hair fell over her tired face. The garden was full of scraggly, neglected plants.

english_meaning: Unpleasantly thin and bony. Lean with visible bones and little flesh. Rough and jagged in outline, as of rocks or land.
example_sentence: A scraggy cat wandered around the empty yard. He looked pale and scraggy after his long illness. The scraggy cliffs rose sharply above the sea. She fed the scraggy stray dog every morning.

english_meaning: To leave a place quickly, especially when told to go away. To depart in a hurry. An emergency shutdown of a nuclear reactor. To shut down a reactor rapidly in an emergency.
example_sentence: The shopkeeper shouted at the boys to scram. You had better scram before the manager returns. Engineers ordered a scram when the temperature rose. The reactor was scrammed within seconds of the alert.

english_meaning: To move or climb quickly using hands and feet, especially in a hurried or awkward way. To struggle or compete eagerly with others to get or do something. To mix things together in a disordered manner. To cook eggs by beating and stirring them in a pan. To make a radio or telephone signal unintelligible.
example_sentence: The children scrambled up the rocks to reach the top. Reporters scrambled to get the first interview. She scrambled the eggs for breakfast. Soldiers scrambled to their positions when the alarm sounded. The transmission was scrambled to keep it secret.

english_meaning: A small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over. Discarded material, especially metal, that can be reused or recycled. To decide not to continue with something such as a plan or project. A short fight or quarrel, usually not serious. A small item cut out from a newspaper or magazine and kept.
example_sentence: The dog ate every scrap of food from the plate. They sold the old car for scrap metal. The government decided to scrap the outdated policy. The two boys had a small scrap in the playground.

english_meaning: An album for keepsakes. A book with blank pages for sticking cuttings, drawings, or pictures in. People use scrapbooks to preserve memories.
example_sentence: My mother keeps a scrapbook of all my childhood photos. We made a scrapbook to remember our trip to Europe. He showed me his scrapbook filled with newspaper clippings. She pasted the ticket stub into her scrapbook.

english_meaning: A person or business that buys and sells scrap metal, old materials, or discarded items. A trader who collects, sorts, and resells waste metal, paper, or plastic. A middleman in the recycling and salvage trade. A merchant dealing in used or broken goods.
example_sentence: The scrap dealer bought all the old iron from our workshop. He earns his living as a scrap dealer in the city. A scrap dealer came to the neighborhood collecting newspapers. The scrap dealer weighed the metal before paying us.

english_meaning: To scratch. A mark or sound of scraping. To drag or pull a hard or sharp implement across a surface. An difficult situation, especially one that one has brought on oneself.
example_sentence: I scraped my knee when I fell off my bike. He scraped the paint off the wall. The sound of her chair scraping on the floor was annoying. He's always getting into scrapes with the law.

english_meaning: To manage to live or survive with very little money or resources. To barely succeed at a task.
example_sentence: They had to scrape by on a very small pension every month. During the war, many families had to scrape by with no food. He managed to scrape by in the exam with the minimum mark. Even though he lost his job, he found ways to scrape by.

english_meaning: To narrowly succeed in entering a place or being accepted into a group. To barely win or pass.
example_sentence: He managed to scrape in through the door just before it closed. With a lot of luck, she might scrape in the top ten lists. The team managed to scrape in the playoffs by winning the last game. I barely managed to scrape in for the interview after the train delay.

english_meaning: To barely gain admission to a university, school, or qualification. To succeed in reaching a position with great difficulty.
example_sentence: He was lucky to scrape into the law school with his grades. The athlete hoped to scrape into the final round of the race. She managed to scrape into the orchestra as a substitute player. It took years of work to scrape into the elite circle of artists.

english_meaning: To remove a substance from a surface by rubbing or pushing it with a sharp or hard edge. To clean something by scratching away dirt, paint, or an unwanted layer. To take off a thin covering with effort.
example_sentence: Scrape off the mud before you enter the house. He scraped off the old wallpaper with a blunt knife. She scraped the burnt bits off the toast. Workers scraped off the rust before repainting the gate.

english_meaning: To remove something from a container by scraping. To narrowly obtain a victory or result.
example_sentence: Use a spatula to scrape out the remaining batter from the bowl. They managed to scrape out a narrow victory in the last minute. The miners had to scrape out the last bits of gold from the vein. She tried to scrape out the burnt bits from the bottom of the pan.

english_meaning: To succeed in passing an examination or test, but only by a very small margin. To manage to get through a difficult situation with great effort and little to spare. To survive or continue financially with barely enough resources.
synonyms: ["Barely pass","Squeak through","Survive","Manage","Get by","Scrape by","Pull through","Muddle through"]
example_sentence: He scraped through the final exam with the lowest passing grade. The team scraped through to the next round after a late goal. She scraped through her first year at university. Somehow we scraped through the winter on very little income.

english_meaning: To manage to collect or gather a small amount of something, especially money, with difficulty. To bring together the last remaining bits of a resource from different sources. To assemble a group, team, or amount barely sufficient for a purpose. To succeed in producing something with the limited means available.
example_sentence: They scraped together enough money to pay the rent. We scraped together a team of five players for the match. She scraped together the last of the flour to bake bread. The family scraped together their savings to send him abroad.

english_meaning: To gather or collect something together with difficulty, especially money. To find something by looking in many places.
example_sentence: I need to scrape up enough money to pay the rent this month. He managed to scrape up a few volunteers to help with the move. The chef had to scrape up some ingredients for a last-minute meal. She tried to scrape up the courage to speak in front of the crowd.

english_meaning: A tool or device with a blade or edge used for removing material from a surface. A person who scrapes something, such as dirt, paint, or ice. In computing, a program that automatically extracts data from websites or documents. A machine used in construction for levelling or removing layers of earth.
example_sentence: He used a metal scraper to remove the old paint. Keep an ice scraper in the car during winter. The developer wrote a scraper to collect product prices. A large scraper levelled the ground before construction began.

english_meaning: To damage or mark a surface by dragging a sharp object across it. To rub the skin with fingers or nails to relieve itching. To remove dirt, paint, or another material from a surface. To make rough writing or drawings. To remove someone or something from a list, plan, or competition. To manage to get something with great effort. A small mark or cut on a surface or skin. The action of rubbing an itchy place.
example_sentence: The cat scratched the furniture. I have a scratch on my arm from a rose bush. He scratched his head in confusion. She scratched the winning numbers on her lottery ticket.

english_meaning: Very thin in an unhealthy or unattractive way. A person or animal that is extremely thin, often lacking muscle or strength. It usually carries a negative sense, suggesting weakness, poor health, or an unattractive appearance due to being underweight.
example_sentence: The scrawny cat wandered through the streets looking for food. He was a scrawny child but very intelligent. The dog looked scrawny after being lost for weeks. She adopted a scrawny kitten and cared for it until it became healthy.

english_meaning: To shout very loudly. To express strong emotion vocally. To make a loud, piercing sound. A sharp, loud cry produced suddenly, often due to strong emotions such as fear, surprise, pain, anger, or even excitement. It can also mean shouting loudly in general speech or expressing something in a very intense way.
example_sentence: She let out a loud scream when she saw the snake. The baby screamed all night due to discomfort. He screamed for help when he got lost in the forest. The audience screamed with excitement at the concert.

english_meaning: The process of sending the current contents of a computer screen to a printer or file. A raw copy of the data displayed on a monitor at a specific moment. A captured image of the entire user interface. An output of visual data for documentation or troubleshooting.
synonyms: ["Screenshot","Screen capture","Print screen","Snapshot","Hard copy","Image grab","Display output","Data dump","Capture","Recording","Digital image","Frame grab"]
example_sentence: Please provide a screen dump of the error message for the IT department. I performed a screen dump to save the results of the simulation. A screen dump is often the fastest way to record complex visual information. The manual includes a screen dump to show users what the interface looks like.

english_meaning: To fasten or fix something firmly in place using screws. To tighten something by turning it, such as a lid or valve. To force someone to reduce a price or accept harder terms through pressure. To restrict or limit something severely.
example_sentence: Screw down the lid tightly before shaking the bottle. The carpenter screwed down the loose floorboards. They screwed the supplier down to a much lower price. Management screwed down spending across every department.

english_meaning: To make a serious mistake and spoil something. To handle a task so badly that it fails. To twist or crumple something tightly, such as paper. To tighten the eyes or face into a wrinkled expression.
example_sentence: I hope I don't screw up the presentation tomorrow. He screwed up the order and sent the wrong parcel. She screwed up the letter and threw it in the bin. He screwed up his eyes against the bright sunlight.

english_meaning: A serious mistake or badly handled situation. A failure caused by carelessness or poor judgement. An informal word for a person who often makes mistakes. A muddle or mess created by someone's error.
example_sentence: The delay was caused by an administrative screw-up. It was a small screw-up, but the client noticed it. He apologised for the screw-up in the accounts. Losing the file was a major screw-up on my part.

english_meaning: A tool with a shaped tip used for turning screws. A hand tool designed to fit into the head of a screw to tighten or loosen it. An alcoholic drink made from vodka and orange juice.
example_sentence: He tightened the hinge with a small screwdriver. Do you have a flat-head screwdriver in your toolbox? The screwdriver slipped and scratched the wooden panel. A magnetic screwdriver makes the job much easier.

english_meaning: To write, record, or copy something. A person who writes or copies documents, especially in earlier times. A professional writer who copied manuscripts before printing was common. A person who writes down what someone else says, such as in a meeting or examination. In ancient contexts, an educated person skilled in reading and writing, often keeping records.
example_sentence: The scribe carefully copied the ancient manuscript. During the meeting, she acted as a scribe and noted every detail. In ancient Egypt, a scribe held an important position in society. He was asked to scribe the professor’s lecture for the absent students.

english_meaning: A written text of a play, film, speech, or broadcast. The words that actors or speakers are expected to say. A system or style of writing letters or characters. A set of instructions used by a computer program. To write the text for a performance or program.
example_sentence: The actor read the script before rehearsal. She wrote a script for a short documentary. Arabic is written in a flowing script. The developer used a simple script to rename the files.

english_meaning: Fear of writing. An extreme or irrational fear of writing, including fear of putting thoughts on paper or creating written documents. This can affect personal, academic, or professional tasks that involve writing.
example_sentence: Her scriptophobia made it difficult for her to complete the report on time. Despite being talented, he struggled with scriptophobia and avoided journals. Therapy helped him overcome his scriptophobia and start writing letters again. Scriptophobia can hinder academic performance if students are afraid to take notes.

english_meaning: The sacred writings of a religion, especially the Bible in Christianity. Any writing or book regarded as authoritative or sacred. A passage from a sacred text. The collective body of religious texts considered holy.
example_sentence: The pastor read from scripture during the service. Holy scripture guides the faithful in their beliefs. She studies scripture every morning. Many religions have their own sacred scriptures.

english_meaning: The pouch of skin that hangs behind the penis and contains the testes. A sac of skin and muscle that protects the male reproductive glands. A structure that keeps the testes slightly cooler than body temperature. An external pouch divided into two compartments by a septum.
example_sentence: The scrotum protects the testes from injury. Cool temperatures inside the scrotum are necessary for sperm production. Swelling of the scrotum should be checked by a doctor. The muscles of the scrotum tighten in cold weather.

english_meaning: To rub something hard with a brush or cloth to clean it. To cancel or abandon a plan or event. To remove dirt, stains, or marks by rubbing. Low, rough bushes or vegetation. A cleansing product used to exfoliate the skin.
example_sentence: She had to scrub the floor to remove the stains. They decided to scrub the mission due to bad weather. He used a brush to scrub the rusted pan clean. A gentle face scrub can keep the skin fresh.

english_meaning: Shabby and untidy in appearance. Dirty or worn out and poorly maintained. Careless about neatness in dress or grooming.
example_sentence: He turned up for the interview in scruffy clothes. The scruffy old building needs urgent repair. Their scruffy dog followed them everywhere. She apologised for her scruffy appearance after the journey.

english_meaning: In rugby, to form a scrum with the opposing forwards in order to restart play. To crouch and bind together as a pack of players around the ball. Informally, to gather closely together in a tight group to discuss or deal with something.
example_sentence: The two packs scrummed down near the halfway line. The referee ordered the teams to scrum down again. Both sides scrummed down for the final play of the match. The staff scrummed down in the corner to finalise the plan.

english_meaning: A feeling of doubt, guilt, or moral concern that prevents someone from doing something they think is dishonest, unfair, or wrong. It also refers to a person's strong moral standards or conscience. To hesitate or refuse to do something because of moral or ethical concerns.
example_sentence: She refused to cheat because she had strong scruples. He had no scruples about telling the truth, even when it was difficult. My scruples prevented me from accepting the dishonest offer. The lawyer scrupled to reveal confidential information without permission.

english_meaning: Diligent, thorough, and extremely attentive to details. Very careful and precise. Having or showing a strict regard for what one considers right; principled. Very concerned to avoid doing wrong.
example_sentence: He had a scrupulous regard for the truth. The research was carried out with scrupulous attention to detail. She is scrupulous in her work. He is too scrupulous to take advantage of the situation. The scrupulous accountant would not let even a penny go unaccounted for.

english_meaning: To examine something very carefully. To look at or inspect something closely and thoroughly in order to understand it or find any problems.
example_sentence: The lawyer scrutinized every clause in the agreement before advising his client. The teacher scrutinized the students’ essays for plagiarism. Investigators scrutinized the security footage to find clues. She scrutinized the painting, noting every brushstroke and color choice.

english_meaning: Careful and complete examination. A close look at or over someone or something in order to judge condition.
example_sentence: The documents should be available for public scrutiny. Her arguments doesn’t really stand up to scrutiny. Foreign policy has come under close scrutiny recently.

english_meaning: To swim underwater using special breathing equipment called scuba gear. To explore underwater areas such as oceans, seas, lakes, or rivers while carrying a self contained breathing apparatus. A person who scuba dives can stay underwater for a long time and observe marine life, coral reefs, shipwrecks, and underwater environments. The word SCUBA stands for: Self Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus.
synonyms: ["Deep sea diving","Underwater diving","Skin diving","Aqua diving","Underwater exploration"]
example_sentence: My brother learned to scuba dive during his vacation in Thailand. The tourists scuba dived near the coral reef to watch colorful fish. She wants to scuba dive in the Arabian Sea next summer. Professional divers scuba dive to explore underwater caves. Our scuba dive lasted for almost one hour. The scuba dive revealed beautiful coral reefs and sea animals.

english_meaning: To fight or struggle briefly in a rough way. To engage in a short and usually sudden physical struggle. It often involves pushing, grabbing, or hitting and is not a long or planned fight. A short and sudden physical fight or struggle. A brief and unplanned physical fight involving pushing, hitting, or struggling. It usually happens suddenly and does not last long. As a verb, it means to fight or struggle in such a way.
example_sentence: A scuffle broke out between two students after the match. Police quickly stopped the scuffle before it became serious. He got injured during a scuffle at the market. The players scuffled over the ball for a few seconds.

english_meaning: To create a work of art by carving, molding, or shaping materials like stone, wood, clay, or metal. It can also mean shaping something carefully, such as the body, a hairstyle, landscape, or even ideas and skills.
example_sentence: The artist will sculpt a statue from marble. She sculpted the clay into a beautiful bowl. Regular exercise helps sculpt the body. The designer sculpted the garden into a peaceful space.

english_meaning: A person who makes statues or artistic forms by carving, shaping, or modeling materials like stone, wood, clay, or metal. A person who shapes or builds something carefully, such as ideas, careers, or policies. A digital artist who designs 3D models using software.
example_sentence: The sculptor spent months carving the marble statue. She is a talented sculptor known for her abstract art. The sculptor displayed his work in the city gallery. A skilled sculptor can turn a simple block of stone into a masterpiece.

english_meaning: A three dimensional artwork made by shaping materials like stone, clay, or metal. The practice or skill of making three dimensional art. A carved or modeled artistic figure or form. Any object shaped artistically in solid form. A decorative or symbolic three dimensional structure. To create or shape something as a sculpture by carving or modeling material.
example_sentence: The artist created a beautiful sculpture from marble. The park is famous for its modern metal sculptures. She studied sculpture at art school for five years. The ancient sculpture shows the culture of that civilization.  The artist sculptured a statue from marble. He sculptured the clay into a human figure.

english_meaning: A layer of impure matter on the surface of a liquid. A worthless or contemptible person or group of people. This informal term expresses strong disdain.
example_sentence: He skimmed the scum off the jam as it cooled. The pond was covered with a thick layer of green scum. They considered him the scum of the earth. The politician referred to the protestors as scum. She felt like scum after her mistake.

english_meaning: A highly despicable, contemptible, or objectionable person. It refers to someone who is considered mean, dishonest, or completely worthless in character. The term is widely used as a strong informal insult to describe an individual who behaves in a morally reprehensible, deceitful, or sleazy manner.
example_sentence: He turned out to be a real scumbag who stole money from his own family. The scumbag who vandalized the newly built school has finally been caught. You should stop hanging out with that lying scumbag. She broke up with him immediately after realizing he was a total scumbag.

english_meaning: Informal, chiefly Australian and New Zealand: dirt, grime, slime, or an unpleasant residue. A dirty, shabby, mean, or disreputable person. To obtain something by begging, borrowing, or scrounging. To clean grime from a surface.
example_sentence: There was a layer of scunge on the old cooker. He is a scunge who is always borrowing money and never repaying it. She scrubbed the scunge off the bathroom tiles. The children tried to scunge free tickets from the box office.

english_meaning: Informal, chiefly Australian and New Zealand: dirty, grimy, unpleasant, shabby, or in poor condition. Mean, stingy, or miserly.
example_sentence: The motel room was scungy and smelled of mildew. He wore a scungy old jacket to the interview. Nobody wanted to rent the scungy flat above the shop. His scungy attitude toward tipping annoyed the waiter.

english_meaning: To prevent something from happening or succeeding. To ruin, spoil, or destroy plans, hopes, or efforts. In naval usage, to deliberately sink one's own ship. The word is mostly British and informal, used when something causes a plan or chance to fail completely.
example_sentence: The sudden rain scuppered our picnic plans. His careless remark scuppered the business deal. Lack of funding scuppered the project. The captain ordered the crew to scupper the ship before surrender. The scandal scuppered his chances of becoming president.

english_meaning: Small dry flakes of dead skin, especially on the scalp or skin of humans or animals. Tiny dry flakes of dead skin that naturally come off the surface of the skin or scalp. It is commonly associated with dandruff in humans, but the word can also describe flaky skin or scales on animals, especially dogs, cats, horses, and birds. Scurf may result from dry skin, poor grooming, skin disorders, allergies, or infections.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the scurf on the patient's scalp before recommending a treatment. Regular brushing helps remove scurf from a horse's coat. Dry weather can increase the amount of scurf on your skin. The veterinarian advised a special shampoo to reduce the dog's scurf.

english_meaning: Covered in or resembling scurf; flaky or scaly. Having a rough, peeling, or crusty surface.
example_sentence: The plant's leaves looked unhealthy and scurfy. His skin became dry and scurfy in the winter. The old book had a scurfy, disintegrating leather cover. A scurfy scalp needs immediate and special treatment. The unpolished wood had a scurfy texture.

english_meaning: Making false and insulting claims intended to damage someone's reputation. Rude, abusive, or coarsely offensive in language. Grossly vulgar or obscene in humour.
example_sentence: The magazine published scurrilous rumours about the actor. He sued the writer over a scurrilous article. The candidate refused to respond to scurrilous attacks. The comedian's scurrilous jokes offended many people.

english_meaning: In a grossly insulting, abusive, or indecent manner. In a scandalous or defamatory way intended to damage someone's reputation.
example_sentence: The tabloid wrote scurrilously about the actor's private life. He spoke scurrilously about his former business partner. The blog scurrilously accused the mayor of taking bribes without evidence. Critics said the pamphlet attacked the senator scurrilously and unfairly.

english_meaning: A hasty tidying of the house between the time you see a visitor and the time they knock on the door. To quickly clean or straighten up a place in a rush. A rushed and last-minute cleaning effort before guests arrive.
example_sentence: She did a quick scurryfunge before her mother-in-law arrived. We had to scurryfunge the living room when guests came unexpectedly. A good scurryfunge can hide a lot of mess in minutes. He is an expert at the last-minute scurryfunge.

english_meaning: A disease caused by severe vitamin C deficiency. A condition characterized by weakness, anemia, and bleeding gums. A nutritional disorder resulting from lack of fresh fruits and vegetables. A preventable disease that was common among sailors on long voyages.
example_sentence: Scurvy can be prevented by eating foods rich in vitamin C. Sailors in the 18th century often suffered from scurvy. Symptoms of scurvy include fatigue and bleeding gums. Citrus fruits help prevent scurvy.

english_meaning: The short, erect tail of a rabbit, hare, or deer. A dull, unpleasant, or menial piece of work. A contemptible person, used informally.
example_sentence: The rabbit's white scut vanished into the bushes. Junior doctors often complain about endless scut. He was left with all the scut work. The old farmer called him a lazy scut.

english_meaning: Rumor or gossip. An informal term often used in nautical or military contexts. A drinking fountain on a ship, which traditionally served as a place for sailors to gather and chat.
example_sentence: The scuttlebutt around the office is that the CEO is resigning. I don't pay much attention to scuttlebutt; I prefer facts. What's the latest scuttlebutt from the naval base?. The crew exchanged scuttlebutt while on their break. She heard the scuttlebutt about the surprise party.

english_meaning: A large body of salt water that is smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land. The salt water that covers most of the earth, considered as a whole. The state or movement of the waves on such water. A vast amount or expanse of something.
example_sentence: They built a small house by the sea. The sea was rough during the storm. Fishermen go out to sea before dawn. A sea of people filled the stadium.

english_meaning: Relating to travel by sea. The practice of traveling by sea. This term can describe people who work on ships or the act of journeying across the ocean for trade, exploration, or transport.
example_sentence: The Vikings were a famous seafaring people. His seafaring adventures took him to many distant lands. The port was bustling with seafaring activity. She wrote a book about her family's seafaring history.

english_meaning: A line where two pieces of fabric or material are joined. To join pieces together with or as if with a seam.
example_sentence: The seam on his shirt came undone during the meeting. The miners discovered a rich seam of coal underground. She checked every seam of the dress before wearing it. They will seam the two fabric pieces before stitching the final design. Years of sunlight had seamed the leather with tiny cracks.

english_meaning: Something smooth, continuous and without any gaps or interruptions. It can also describe work, transitions or processes that feel natural and well connected.
example_sentence: The team delivered a seamless presentation that impressed everyone. The transition from one scene to the next was seamless. We want the customer experience to feel seamless from start to finish. The software update made the system run in a seamless way.

english_meaning: A woman who sews clothes professionally. A skilled woman who makes, stitches, alters, or repairs garments using a needle, thread, or sewing machine. She may work independently, in tailoring shops, fashion houses, or garment factories.
example_sentence: The seamstress stitched the wedding dress with great care. She works as a seamstress in a local tailoring shop. The seamstress repaired my torn jacket quickly. A skilled seamstress can turn simple fabric into elegant clothing.

english_meaning: To burn or scorch the surface of something with a sudden, intense heat. To brown food quickly at a high temperature to lock in moisture. To cause to wither or dry up as if by heat. To make someone feel a sudden and intense pain or emotion. To brand or mark the surface of something with a hot iron. To become dry, withered, or parched due to exposure.
example_sentence: The chef told the apprentice to sear the steak on both sides to trap the juices inside. The hot desert sun will sear the leaves of any plant left without water. A searing pain shot through his leg when he tried to stand up after the fall. The haunting memory of that night continued to sear his soul for many years.

english_meaning: To look carefully for someone or something. To examine a place or person thoroughly to find something hidden. To try to find information, usually using a computer or the internet. To explore in order to discover something. An act of looking for or trying to find something or someone.
example_sentence: The police searched the house for stolen goods. She searched the internet for a suitable recipe. Rescue teams continued to search for the missing hikers. His search for the truth took many years.

english_meaning: A small gland in the skin that produces an oily substance called sebum. A skin gland that opens into a hair follicle and keeps the hair and skin soft. A gland that protects the skin from drying out and from harmful bacteria. One of the oil-producing glands found almost everywhere on the body except the palms and soles.
example_sentence: The sebaceous glands produce oil that keeps the skin moist. Blocked sebaceous glands often cause pimples. These glands are found next to almost every hair follicle. Hormonal changes can make the sebaceous glands more active.

english_meaning: A skin condition marked by excessive oil production from the sebaceous glands. A disorder that causes greasy, scaly patches on the scalp or face. Overactivity of oil glands leading to dandruff, redness, and irritation.
example_sentence: Seborrhea is common in both infants and adults. The doctor prescribed a medicated shampoo for seborrhea. Seborrhea often affects the scalp and face. Stress can worsen the symptoms of seborrhea.

english_meaning: To formally withdraw from a federation or body. To break away from a larger group or political entity. This verb is often used in the context of political states or regions seeking independence from a country.
example_sentence: The southern states attempted to secede from the Union. The region threatened to secede and form its own country. After much debate, the small province decided not to secede. The group voted to secede from the national organization.

english_meaning: To keep yourself, somebody away from contact with other people. To set or keep apart from others.
example_sentence: The monks secluded themselves from the rest of society. She secludes herself in her study to work. You can't seclude yourself from the world.

english_meaning: The state of being private and away from other people. A condition in which a person lives or stays away from others, often in a quiet, private, or isolated place. It may be chosen for peace, safety, religious practice, reflection, or rest. It can also sometimes mean being kept apart for protection or medical reasons.
example_sentence: The writer lived in seclusion in a small mountain village. After the incident, he chose seclusion to recover peacefully. The monk spent years in seclusion for spiritual growth. The celebrity escaped to an island for seclusion and privacy.

english_meaning: A person who prefers to be alone or secluded. A person who prefers to live in isolation, away from society, or avoids social contact.
example_sentence: The writer was known as a seclusionist, preferring to live far from society in his mountain cabin. As a seclusionist, she avoided social gatherings and valued her privacy above all else. The village considered him a seclusionist because he rarely interacted with others.

english_meaning: The toe next to the big toe on the human foot. The second digit of the foot counting from the inner side. The toe that is often longer than the big toe in some people. One of the smaller toes that helps maintain balance while walking.
example_sentence: Her second toe is slightly longer than her big toe. He injured his second toe while playing barefoot. The shoe pressed painfully against his second toe. A blister formed under her second toe after the walk.

english_meaning: Coming after, less important than, or resulting from something else. Relating to education for children between primary school and higher education. Of second rank or importance. Derived from something original or primary. Not the main or first.
example_sentence: He completed his secondary education at a local school. The cost was only a secondary consideration. Secondary infections often follow the flu. The car has a secondary fuel tank for long trips.

english_meaning: The temporary transfer of an employee to another position or organization. A period of time when an employee is sent to work elsewhere to gain new skills or experience. This is a common practice in large corporations and government bodies for professional development.
example_sentence: She is on a six-month secondment to our marketing department. The secondment gave him valuable experience in a different field. He applied for a secondment to the company's international branch. The agreement outlines the terms of his secondment.

english_meaning: Something kept hidden from others. Information known only to a limited group. Not meant to be revealed or shared. A method or reason not commonly known. Something private or confidential.
example_sentence: She kept the surprise party a secret. The recipe is a family secret passed down for generations. He shared a secret with his best friend. The document contained several government secrets.

english_meaning: A hidden enemy, betrayer, or person with concealed hatred. A person who is an enemy in disguise. Someone who pretends to be friendly but secretly works against you.
example_sentence: He acted like my friend, but deep inside, he was a secret foe. Beware of secret foes who smile to your face but hurt you behind your back. A secret foe is more dangerous than an open enemy. She realized too late that her closest colleague was actually a secret foe.

english_meaning: The process by which substances are produced and discharged from a cell, gland, or organ. A substance that is secreted. In biology, it refers to the movement of material from one point to another, such as a hormone into the blood. It can also refer to the act of concealing something.
example_sentence: The secretion of hormones is essential for bodily functions. The plant has a sticky secretion that traps insects. This gland is responsible for the secretion of saliva. The police were investigating the secretion of illegal funds.

english_meaning: A subgroup that separates from a larger religious, philosophical, or ideological tradition. It usually develops distinct beliefs, interpretations, or practices that differ from the main body. Sects may arise because of disagreements about doctrine, leadership, rituals, or interpretation of sacred texts.
example_sentence: The country has many religious sects with different traditions. A small sect separated from the main church centuries ago. Some sect members follow very strict rules in their daily life. The historian studied how the sect developed its unique beliefs.

english_meaning: Relating to or supporting a particular religious, political, or social sect. Narrow-minded loyalty to one group over others. Often involving prejudice, hatred, or violence between different sects. Used to describe conflicts, attitudes, or actions based on rigid group identity.
example_sentence: The country has suffered from years of sectarian violence. Sectarian politics has weakened national unity. The government banned sectarian hate speech in the media. Leaders should rise above sectarian interests. Sectarian conflicts often have deep historical roots.

english_meaning: Capable of being cut smoothly with a knife. Relating to a mineral that can be cut into thin shavings. This property is characteristic of certain soft minerals like gypsum or talc.
example_sentence: Gold is a sectile metal that can be easily shaped. The geologist identified the mineral as sectile. Unlike brittle minerals, sectile ones do not crumble when cut. Talc is known for being very soft and sectile.

english_meaning: A distinct part or branch of a society, economy, or area of activity. A subdivision of an area, such as a military zone or a district of a city. In geometry, the area enclosed by two radii of a circle and their intercepted arc.
example_sentence: The financial sector is a critical component of the economy. A new military sector was established along the border. The city was divided into several administrative sectors. She works in the public sector.

english_meaning: Related to non religious life or worldly affairs. Government or state that does not support any specific religion. Education or institutions not controlled by religious groups. In historical usage, something lasting for a very long time or many centuries.
example_sentence: The country follows a secular constitution that treats all religions equally. Many public schools provide secular education rather than religious instruction. The organization focuses on secular social services such as health and education. Some historians study secular trends in society instead of religious movements.

english_meaning: Calm, dignified, and unhurried in manner or speed. It can also refer to a person who is quiet and rather dull. In a medical context, it refers to a person being under the influence of a calming drug.
example_sentence: The wedding was a sedate affair with very little music and dancing. They took a sedate stroll through the botanical gardens. The doctor decided to sedate the patient before the MRI scan. She maintained a sedate pace throughout the long marathon.

english_meaning: In a quiet, relaxed, or slow manner without any excitement or hurry. It describes an action performed with composure and steady dignity. It can also imply a lack of emotional agitation or speed.
example_sentence: The elderly couple walked sedately across the park. He spoke sedately, choosing his words with great care. The horse trotted sedately down the country lane. The procession moved sedately toward the temple entrance.

english_meaning: The administration of a sedative drug to produce a state of calm or sleep. It is the state of being calmed or made drowsy, often for medical procedures. It helps reduce anxiety and physical movement in patients.
example_sentence: The patient was under heavy sedation during the complex surgery. The dentist recommended light sedation for the nervous child. Sedation is often necessary to perform a clear CT scan on pets. She slowly woke up from the effects of the sedation.

english_meaning: A drug taken for its calming or sleep-inducing effect. Anything that has a soothing or calming influence on a person. It reduces irritability or excitement by depressing the central nervous system.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed a mild sedative to help him sleep. Music can sometimes act as a natural sedative after a stressful day. He was given a sedative to calm his nerves before the flight. The herbal tea had a surprisingly sedative effect on her.

english_meaning: Spending much time sitting; not physically active. Characterized by a lifestyle involving a lot of sitting or minimal physical activity; often used to describe jobs, habits, or lifestyles that require little movement.
example_sentence: A sedentary lifestyle can lead to health problems. Office jobs often require long hours of sedentary work. He became overweight due to his sedentary habits. Yoga helps counteract the effects of a sedentary life.

english_meaning: Material such as sand, mud, minerals, or organic particles that sink and collect at the bottom of water, rivers, lakes, or any liquid after being carried or suspended in it. It may also refer to matter that settles gradually over time in a place or container.
example_sentence: The river carried sediment that slowly settled at the bottom of the lake. Scientists studied the ocean sediment to learn about ancient climate conditions. After boiling the herbal mixture, a thick sediment remained in the pot. Over centuries, layers of sediment formed the rocks seen in the canyon.

english_meaning: Relating to or denoting rocks formed from sediment deposited by water, wind, or ice. Consisting of layers of material that have settled over time.
example_sentence: Sedimentary rocks like sandstone are formed over millions of years. The geologist was an expert in sedimentary basins. Fossils are most commonly found in sedimentary layers. Sedimentary processes are crucial for soil formation.

english_meaning: Incitement to rebellion. Encouragement of revolt. Promotion of insurrection. Instigation against lawful authority. Agitation against the government. Subversive activity. Provocation to public disorder. Treasonous agitation (not always the same as treason)
example_sentence: The speaker was accused of sedition after urging people to overthrow the government by force. The court examined whether the publication contained evidence of sedition. Historians continue to debate whether the protest leaders were guilty of sedition or were exercising free speech. Laws relating to sedition differ significantly from one country to another.

english_meaning: Encouraging people to oppose, rebel against, or overthrow a government or lawful authority. It escribes speech, writing, actions, or ideas that encourage people to rebel against a government or lawful authority. It often refers to attempts to create public disorder, resistance, or disobedience against the state. The word is commonly used in legal, political, and historical contexts.
example_sentence: The court examined whether the speech contained seditious statements against the government. The newspaper was accused of publishing seditious articles during the political crisis. The teacher explained the historical difference between peaceful protest and seditious activities. Authorities investigated several individuals for allegedly distributing seditious pamphlets.

english_meaning: To persuade someone to do something wrong or immoral, often by using charm or attraction. To lead someone into a harmful or unwise action by appealing to their desires or emotions, often with charm or sexual attraction. It can refer to influencing someone to act against their better judgment.
example_sentence: He tried to seduce her into lying for him. The advertisement seemed designed to seduce young customers. She was careful not to be seduced by the promises of quick wealth. He used flattery to seduce his colleagues into supporting the plan.

english_meaning: A person who tempts or attracts someone, often romantically. Someone who entices or charms another person, usually in a sexual or romantic way, often leading them to do something they might not otherwise do.
example_sentence: He was known as a seducer who won hearts easily. The story describes a seducer who tricks women for his gain. She realized he was a seducer after he manipulated her feelings. Famous actors are sometimes unfairly labeled as seducers.

english_meaning: The process of enticing someone to do something, often by appealing to desire or attraction. It can involve persuasion, charm, or allure. It is sometimes used in a romantic or sexual context but can also apply to convincing someone to act against their better judgment.
example_sentence: The movie explored the theme of seduction and desire. He fell victim to her seduction and made a risky decision. The advertisement used seduction to attract customers. Ancient stories often warn of the dangers of seduction.

english_meaning: Attractive in a way that tempts or entices. Having the quality of tempting or attracting someone often in a way that is hard to resist. Can refer to charm, appearance, or behavior that draws interest or desire.
example_sentence: Her smile was extremely seductive. The advertisement used seductive colors to attract customers. He found her voice seductive. The movie had a seductive plot that kept everyone engaged.

english_meaning: Acting in a manner intended to entice, charm, or attract someone, often with allure or appeal.
example_sentence: She smiled seductively at him across the room. The model posed seductively for the camera. He spoke seductively, making everyone listen to his story. The perfume smelled seductively sweet.

english_meaning: The quality of being attractive or charming in a way that tempts or entices someone.
example_sentence: Her seductiveness made everyone at the party notice her. The seductiveness of the city drew tourists from all over the world. He admired the seductiveness of her writing style. Seductiveness in marketing can influence people’s choices.

english_meaning: A woman who deliberately attracts someone, often using charm, beauty, or allure to influence or manipulate them emotionally or romantically. A woman who entices or tempts someone, especially in a sexual way
example_sentence: The novel portrayed her as a cunning seductress. He fell for the charms of a seductress at the party. The movie featured a seductress who led men into trouble. Legends often speak of a seductress whose beauty was irresistible.

english_meaning: Showing dedication and careful attention to work or duty. Someone who is persistent, diligent, and meticulous in completing tasks. It conveys consistent effort and attention to detail over time.
example_sentence: She was sedulous in her studies, reviewing notes every evening. The researcher conducted sedulous experiments to ensure accuracy. His sedulous efforts at work earned him a promotion. Sedulous planning made the event run smoothly.

english_meaning: Diligently, with careful and persistent effort. Performing a task with constant, careful, and attentive effort, showing dedication and persistence in completing work.
example_sentence: She sedulously prepared for the final exams to ensure top marks. The researcher sedulously gathered data for the study. He sedulously maintained his garden every morning. They sedulously followed the instructions to complete the project perfectly.

english_meaning: It means to become extremely angry or furious suddenly. It describes a state of losing control over one's temper due to intense rage. It signifies an overwhelming feeling of hostility or wrath. It represents a psychological reaction where anger blinds a person to reason.
synonyms: ["Become Furious","Lose One's Temper","Go Mad","Blow One's Top","Fly Into A Rage","Hit The Roof","Go Ape","Boil Over","Lose Control","Fly Off The Handle"]
antonyms: ["Keep Calm","Stay Cool","Be Peaceful","Remain Composed","Keep One's Temper","Be Serene","Hold One's Peace","Stay Placid","Be Unfazed"]
example_sentence: Whenever anyone mocks his family, he tends to see red immediately. I saw red when I found out someone had stolen my bicycle. The unfairness of the committee's decision made her see red. He is usually calm, but blatant disrespect makes him see red.

english_meaning: To arrange, deal with, or take responsibility for something. To look into a matter, make arrangements, or take steps to solve a problem or fulfill a request. It often implies future action rather than immediate completion.
example_sentence: I will see about booking the meeting room tomorrow. The manager said she would see about the complaint. Can you see about repairing the broken chair? He promised to see about the travel arrangements.

english_meaning: To agree fully or have the same opinion with someone; to think in the same way about something. It is often used when two people share the same views, ideas, or understanding.
synonyms: ["Agree","Have the same opinion","Be in harmony","Be of one mind","Concur"]
example_sentence: We see eye to eye on this issue. My brother and I don’t always see eye to eye on politics. The manager and the staff finally saw eye to eye about the new plan. They rarely see eye to eye, but they respect each other’s opinions. After a long discussion, we began to see eye to eye on the solution.

english_meaning: To decide or consider it appropriate to do something. To choose to do something because one believes it is right or suitable. To think it proper or acceptable to take a particular action. To judge that a certain course of action is reasonable.
example_sentence: The manager did not see fit to reply to my email. She saw fit to inform the police about the incident. If you see fit to join us, we would be delighted. The court saw fit to reduce his sentence.

english_meaning: To investigate or understand something carefully. To examine a matter closely in order to discover facts, causes, problems, or hidden intentions. It can also mean to perceive beyond what is obvious.
example_sentence: The committee promised to see into the complaints made by the workers. I will see into the reason for the delay tomorrow. The manager saw into the issue and found the real cause. Police are seeing into the matter seriously.

english_meaning: To accompany someone leaving to say goodbye. To go with someone to a place, usually a station, airport, or exit, to say goodbye and wish them well on their journey.
example_sentence: We went to the airport to see off our friends. She saw off her brother at the train station. They saw off the guests after the party. I always feel sad when I see off my cousins.

english_meaning: To remain until the end of a period, event, or situation. To continue with someone or something until it finishes. It can be used for a time period, a task, or a person until the end of a particular event or situation. It sometimes also means to escort someone to the door at the end of a visit.
example_sentence: She decided to see out the meeting even though she was tired. The old manager promised to see out the project before retiring. We stayed to see out the concert until the final song. He saw me out to the car after the party.

word: See something with your own eyes
english_meaning: To witness something personally rather than hearing about it from others. To observe an event or fact directly. To confirm the truth of something by direct observation. To be an eyewitness. To personally verify what actually happened.
example_sentence: I saw the accident with my own eyes. She wouldn't have believed it unless she saw it with her own eyes. The reporter saw the destruction with her own eyes. He wanted to see the miracle with his own eyes.

english_meaning: To be completed, discovered, published, revealed, or become available to the public.  When something becomes visible, known, available, completed, published, or comes into existence after being hidden, delayed, or kept secret. It can refer to books, plans, projects, ideas, documents, inventions, or any work that finally becomes public.
synonyms: ["Become public","Appear","Emerge","Surface","Be revealed","Be published","Come out","Materialize","Be disclosed","Come into existence"]
antonyms: ["Remain hidden","Be concealed","Stay secret","Be suppressed","Be buried","Be withheld","Disappear","Be obscured"]
example_sentence: After years of research, the scientist's invention finally saw the light of day. The manuscript remained hidden for decades before it saw the light of day. Many good ideas never see the light of day because of a lack of funding. The company's new product saw the light of day after several delays.

english_meaning: Understand the truth. To recognize the true nature of someone or something, especially when they are trying to hide it or deceive you.
example_sentence: I could see through his excuses. She saw through their plan immediately. Don’t try to lie to me; I can see through you. He saw through the tricky situation and acted wisely.

english_meaning: To take care of something or make sure it is done. To give attention to a task, responsibility, or person, to manage it properly, or to ensure that something happens as required.
example_sentence: Please see to the arrangements before the guests arrive. The manager will see to the customer complaints. She asked him to see to the documents immediately. I will see to it that the report is submitted on time.

english_meaning: A long plank balanced in the middle on which two people sit at opposite ends and move up and down. A repeated up-and-down or back-and-forth movement or change. To move or change repeatedly between two states or positions.
example_sentence: The children took turns on the see-saw in the park. Prices have been on a see-saw for the past month. His mood see-sawed between hope and despair. A broken see-saw was removed from the playground.

english_meaning: The small hard part of a plant from which a new plant can grow. A grain or unit used for sowing crops. The beginning or source of something, used figuratively. To sow land with seeds, or to place a player in a ranked position in a tournament.
example_sentence: She planted a few sunflower seeds in the garden. The farmer bought good quality wheat seed. His speech sowed the seeds of change. The champion was seeded first in the tournament.

english_meaning: Appearing to be true or real but perhaps not so. Apparent rather than actual. An outward appearance that may be misleading. Giving a certain impression on the surface.
example_sentence: His seeming calm hid a great deal of worry. Despite her seeming confidence, she was nervous. The seeming simplicity of the plan was deceptive. There is a seeming contradiction in his two statements.

english_meaning: Appearing to be true or real but possibly not actually so. Something that looks true or appears a certain way based on available information, but there is doubt about its reality. It suggests an outward impression that may change when more facts are known.
example_sentence: He was seemingly calm during the meeting. The task was seemingly easy but proved difficult later. She made a seemingly harmless comment. The town was seemingly deserted at night.

english_meaning: To leak slowly. To pass, flow, or ooze gradually through a porous substance. A place where water or other liquid oozes out.
example_sentence: Water began to seep through the cracks in the basement wall. The secret of the plan started to seep out to the public. He felt a sense of dread seep into his mind. The rain started to seep through the roof.

english_meaning: The slow escape of a liquid or gas through small holes or porous material. The gradual leaking of water into or out of a surface such as soil, a wall, or a container. The quantity of liquid that has leaked out in this way.
example_sentence: Seepage from the old pipe damaged the kitchen wall. Engineers measured the seepage through the dam foundation. Constant seepage had weakened the building's plaster. Farmers lose water through seepage in unlined channels.

english_meaning: A person believed to be able to see the future through supernatural insight. A prophet or visionary who predicts what will happen. A wise person whose judgement about coming events is trusted.
example_sentence: The ancient seer warned the king of a coming famine. Villagers travelled far to consult the old seer. He was regarded as a seer for predicting the market collapse. Legends describe the seer as a woman of great wisdom.

english_meaning: A playground plank balanced at its centre on which two people ride up and down. A situation that keeps changing from one state to another. To rise and fall or change repeatedly between two positions.
example_sentence: The park has a new seesaw for younger children. The match was a seesaw of missed chances and quick goals. Oil prices seesawed throughout the week. Their fortunes seesawed for several years.

english_meaning: A part or section of something. One of the parts into which something is or may be divided. To divide into segments or sections.
example_sentence: She divided the orange into segments for the children. The company is targeting a specific segment of the market. The last segment of the race was the most difficult. They decided to segment the project into manageable tasks.

english_meaning: To separate or set apart from others. To keep people, things, or groups apart from each other, often based on differences such as race, religion, gender, or type. It can refer to both physical separation and social exclusion.
example_sentence: The school decided to segregate students by age for the science classes. Factories segregate waste materials for recycling. During the event, volunteers segregated the donations into clothes, food, and books. Some societies historically segregated communities based on social status.

english_meaning: The state of being alone or kept apart from others. The act or policy of separating people from different groups, for example people of different races, religions or sexes, and treating them in a different way.
example_sentence: The report recommends segregation of cyclists from both cars and pedestrians. They objected to the college's strict segregation of men and women.

english_meaning: Relating to earthquakes or vibrations of the earth's crust. Caused by or measuring such vibrations. Very great in size or effect; causing sudden and dramatic change.
example_sentence: The building was designed to resist seismic activity. Seismic waves were recorded far from the epicentre. The election brought a seismic shift in policy. Engineers studied the seismic risk of the valley.

english_meaning: To take hold of something suddenly and firmly. To capture or take control by force or legal authority. To take an opportunity quickly. To affect someone suddenly and strongly. To confiscate property or goods.
example_sentence: The officer tried to seize the stolen goods. She seized the chance to study abroad. Panic seemed to seize the crowd after the alarm. He seized my arm before I could fall.

english_meaning: Act now and do not miss the opportunity. To take immediate advantage of an opportunity without delay. It suggests acting quickly before the chance disappears and making the most of the present time.
synonyms: ["Take advantage of the opportunity","Act now","Make the most of it","Grab the chance","Carpe diem"]
example_sentence: You should seize the moment and apply for the scholarship today. He seized the moment and started his own business when the opportunity came. She decided to seize the moment and express her true feelings. They seized the moment to invest in the market at the right time.

english_meaning: To quickly take a position that appears morally superior, especially before an opponent can. To gain an advantage in a dispute by acting on strong moral principles. To take firm control of the ethical argument in a debate or conflict. To act decisively in a way that makes your side look more just.
synonyms: ["Take the moral high ground","Claim moral superiority","Gain ethical advantage","Assert principle","Outflank morally"]
antonyms: ["Lose credibility","Act dishonourably","Yield the argument","Compromise principles","Concede fault"]
example_sentence: The government seized the moral high ground by announcing free treatment. She seized the moral high ground by apologising first. The campaign seized the moral high ground with its honest message. He seized the moral high ground before his rivals could respond.

english_meaning: Act quickly to take advantage of a chance. To recognize a favorable situation and act on it without delay. It implies courage, readiness, and smart decision-making to benefit from a moment that may not come again.
synonyms: ["Take advantage","Grab the chance","Make use of the opportunity","Capitalize on","Act on"]
antonyms: ["Miss the opportunity","Ignore the chance","Waste the chance","Let it pass","Hesitate"]
example_sentence: She seized the opportunity to study abroad and changed her life. He seized the opportunity to start his own business during the crisis. If you seize the opportunity now, you can achieve great success. They seized the opportunity to learn new skills during their free time.

english_meaning: A sudden attack of illness, like an epileptic fit. The action of capturing someone or something using force. The act of taking something by force or by legal authority.
example_sentence: The child had a febrile seizure due to the high fever. The government's seizure of the illegal shipment was a major victory. He suffered a massive seizure and was rushed to the hospital. The bank's seizure of their property was a devastating blow.

english_meaning: Strange and uncommon in a way that is marvelous or wonderful. Unfamiliar, rare, and yet beautiful or fascinating. Something that appears unusual but leaves a pleasant sense of wonder. A rare experience or sight that feels new and enchanting.
example_sentence: The old village had a selcouth charm that captivated every visitor. She wandered through the selcouth streets of the ancient town. The forest at dawn felt selcouth and full of quiet magic. His paintings capture a selcouth beauty rarely seen in modern art.

english_meaning: Not often. Almost never. Sometimes. As few times. In few instances.
example_sentence: We seldom go to the theater downtown because its prices are so high. Two dogs over one bone seldom agree. I seldom drive my car into the city. He had seldom seen a child with so much talent. They seldom watch television these days.

english_meaning: To carefully choose something from a group as being the best or most suitable. To pick out or designate a specific item for a particular purpose or task. To indicate a choice or preference between different options or alternatives. To highlight or mark a piece of data or text for an operation on a computer. A collection of items that have been chosen for their high quality or special characteristics.
example_sentence: Please select the best candidate for the vacant position. You can use the mouse to select the text you want to copy. The shop offers a select range of imported gourmet chocolates. Users must select their preferred language from the dropdown menu.

english_meaning: Relating to selection or the process of choosing. In linguistics, concerned with the restrictions that determine which words can combine with others. Involving criteria used to select particular items or people.
example_sentence: The committee explained its selectional criteria to the applicants. Selectional restrictions prevent that verb from taking such an object. The study examines selectional patterns in early language learning. Their selectional process was praised for being transparent.

english_meaning: Careful in choosing only the best or most suitable. Affecting or applying to only some things or people rather than all. Able to choose or separate particular items from a larger group.
example_sentence: She is very selective about the friends she keeps. The college has a highly selective admission policy. The report gives only a selective account of events. This spray is selective and harms only weeds.

english_meaning: Applying moral principles only when convenient.
example_sentence: Selective morality causes double standards. He shows selective morality at work. Laws should avoid selective morality. Selective morality creates social injustice.

english_meaning: In a careful way, choosing only certain things or people. Not generally but only in particular cases. With the ability to affect or respond to some items and not others.
example_sentence: The gardener selectively removed the weaker plants. Information was selectively shared with the press. The drug acts selectively on damaged cells. He listens selectively and ignores the rest.

english_meaning: Someone who thinks mainly about himself. A person who focuses on his own needs, feelings, and interests while giving little or no attention to others.
example_sentence: He became self centered after gaining success. A self centered attitude can damage relationships. She was so self centered that she ignored her team’s efforts. Self centered people often struggle to maintain friendships.

english_meaning: Achieving success through one’s own effort. Describes a person who becomes successful through personal hard work, determination, and skill, without significant help, wealth, or status inherited from family or others.
example_sentence: He is a self made businessman who started with nothing. She is proud to be self made and independent. The company was built by a self made entrepreneur. Many self made leaders inspire young people.

english_meaning: The act of promoting one's own importance, power, or reputation, often in an excessive way. Behaviour aimed at making oneself look greater or more successful than one really is.
example_sentence: His speech was pure self-aggrandizement. She helps others without any hint of self-aggrandizement. Critics saw the ceremony as an act of self-aggrandizement. Leadership should mean service, not self-aggrandizement.

english_meaning: Confidence in one’s own abilities, judgment, or character. A calm certainty when speaking or acting. Freedom from nervousness or self-doubt.
example_sentence: She answered the difficult questions with self-assurance. His quiet self-assurance impressed the interview panel. Experience gave her greater self-assurance on stage. The child approached the new class with surprising self-assurance.

english_meaning: Concerned mainly with one’s own needs, wishes, or interests. Giving little thought to other people’s feelings or needs. Viewing situations chiefly in relation to oneself.
example_sentence: His self-centred behavior upset the rest of the team. She seemed self-centred because she never asked about anyone else. A self-centred manager may ignore employees’ concerns. He is becoming less self-centred as he grows older.

english_meaning: Able to remove dirt or unwanted material automatically. Designed so that it requires little or no manual cleaning. Capable of cleaning itself through a special surface, mechanism, or cycle.
example_sentence: The oven has a self-cleaning cycle. We installed self-cleaning glass in the roof. This fabric has a self-cleaning coating. Self-cleaning filters reduce routine maintenance.

english_meaning: Belief in your own abilities and worth. The feeling of trust in yourself. It means believing that you can handle tasks, make decisions, and face challenges without constant doubt or fear.
example_sentence: Her self-confidence helped her speak clearly in front of a large audience. Success in small tasks can build self-confidence over time. Lack of self-confidence often stops people from trying new things. Teachers should encourage self-confidence in their students.

english_meaning: Feeling sure about your own abilities, qualities, or judgment. Certain that you can manage any situation by yourself. Such a person is comfortable making decisions, expressing opinions, and taking responsibility without excessive fear or doubt.
example_sentence: She is self-confident enough to speak in front of a large audience. A self-confident leader inspires trust in the team. He became more self-confident after gaining work experience. Self-confident students participate actively in class discussions.

english_meaning: Able or inclined to examine and criticize one’s own actions or qualities. Excessively conscious of personal faults. Honestly reflective about one’s weaknesses and mistakes.
example_sentence: A good leader can be self-critical without losing confidence. She became overly self-critical after the performance. His self-critical essay acknowledged several mistakes. Being self-critical helped the team improve its methods.

english_meaning: The act of protecting oneself from harm or attack. The use of reasonable force to defend one's body, property, or rights. Skills or techniques used to protect oneself, such as martial arts. A legal justification for using force to prevent harm. The natural instinct to guard oneself.
example_sentence: She joined a class to learn self-defence. He acted in self-defence when the attacker approached. Every citizen has the right to self-defence. Martial arts teach children discipline and self-defence.

english_meaning: The act of deceiving oneself about the truth of a situation. A false belief that a person holds about themselves. The tendency to see things as one wishes rather than as they are. Mistaken confidence in one's own abilities or importance. A form of denial or unrealistic thinking.
example_sentence: His belief in easy success was pure self-delusion. Self-delusion can prevent people from seeing their real problems. She lived in self-delusion about her role in the failure. Overcoming self-delusion requires honest reflection.

english_meaning: The act of refusing oneself something, especially for moral, religious, or personal reasons. The practice of intentionally giving up personal desires, pleasures, or comforts, often to achieve higher goals, moral discipline, or spiritual growth.
