A utensil with a mesh or perforated bottom used for separating coarse particles from fine ones. A tool for straining liquids to remove solids. A device used in cooking, construction, or laboratory work to separate materials by size.
example_sentence: She sieved the flour before baking the cake. He sieved the water to remove impurities. The editor sieved through hundreds of submissions. The baker poured the flour through a fine sieve. The sand was run through a sieve to remove pebbles. His mind is like a sieve; he forgets everything.

english_meaning: To put a substance (like flour or sand) through a sieve to remove lumps or larger pieces. To examine information, evidence, or ideas thoroughly to find what is important or useful.
example_sentence: She sifted the flour before baking the cake. The detective sifted through the files for clues. We need to sift the facts from the rumors. The teacher sifted through the essays to find the best ones.

english_meaning: To let out a deep, often audible breath that expresses emotions such as disappointment, fatigue, sadness, relief, or longing. The act of sighing or the sound produced when sighing.
example_sentence: She sighed deeply after finishing her work. He let out a sigh of relief when the exam was over. I could hear her sigh from across the room. He sighed, realizing he had forgotten his keys.

english_meaning: A welcome or pleasant sight. Something or someone that you are very pleased or happy to see, especially after a long time or in an unpleasant situation.
example_sentence: After walking all day in the desert, the river was a sight for sore eyes. When I saw my family waiting for me at the airport, it was a sight for sore eyes. The green valley after miles of barren land was truly a sight for sore eyes. Her smiling face early in the morning is always a sight for sore eyes.

english_meaning: To officially receive something by writing your signature. Also to agree formally to take responsibility for something.
example_sentence: I had to sign for the courier package this morning. She signed for the registered letter at the post office. The company signed for new office equipment last week. The football club signed for a young striker before the season started.

english_meaning: To log into a system, website, or account by providing credentials. To officially record your attendance or presence at an event or place.
example_sentence: I need to sign in to my email before checking messages. Please sign in at the reception desk when you arrive. You can sign in using your Google account. He forgot to sign in, so his visit was not recorded.

english_meaning: To formally approve or authorize something, such as a document, plan, or message. To conclude a broadcast, message, or correspondence, indicating completion. To leave work or log out from a system. To end participation or withdraw from an activity.
example_sentence: The manager will sign off on the budget tomorrow. Please sign off your emails before sending them. The news anchor signed off with a thank-you to viewers. Don’t forget to sign off the system when you leave.

english_meaning: To agree to join or participate in something, often a job or contract. To officially register for unemployment benefits. To start working on a new project or team. To log into a digital system or platform.
example_sentence: She decided to sign on with the new marketing agency next week. The company asked him to sign on for a two-year contract. I need to sign on to the website to access my account. Many volunteers signed on to help with the relief program

english_meaning: To log out from a system, account, or device. To withdraw from participation in an activity. To mark the end of attendance or leave a place officially.
example_sentence: Please sign out of your account before leaving the computer. She forgot to sign out from the online banking site. The app automatically signs out users after 15 minutes of inactivity. He reminded everyone to sign out of the shared tablet.

english_meaning: To register or enroll for something, such as a service, event, or program. To commit to a responsibility or role. To agree to participate in a challenge or program. In online context, to create an account. To indicate interest.
example_sentence: I decided to sign up for the yoga class. She signed up for the newsletter to get updates. Many students sign up for online courses during summer. He signed up as a volunteer for the community project.

english_meaning: Importance or the quality of being meaningful or valuable. The importance, value, or meaning of something. It shows why something matters or why it has an effect on people, ideas, events, or results. It can also describe the meaning behind an action, symbol, or event.
example_sentence: The discovery has great significance for medical science. Teachers explained the significance of education in shaping the future. The color white has cultural significance in many traditions. Scientists studied the significance of climate changes in coastal regions.

english_meaning: Important or meaningful. Something that has importance, influence, or clear meaning. It may show a noticeable effect, value, or message. In research or statistics it can describe a result that is meaningful or not due to chance.
example_sentence: The study revealed significant changes in climate patterns. Education plays a significant role in social development. There was a significant increase in rainfall this year. Her contribution to the project was significant and widely appreciated.

english_meaning: In an important or noticeable way, to a large or meaningful extent. Something that has a considerable, important, or meaningful effect or influence on a situation or outcome. It emphasizes the degree or importance of change, difference, or impact.
example_sentence: The new policy significantly improved employee satisfaction. Temperatures have dropped significantly this week. The treatment significantly reduced the risk of infection. Customer complaints have decreased significantly since last year.

english_meaning: The meaning, sense, or importance of something. The expression of meaning or the act of indicating what something represents. It can apply to words, symbols, gestures, or actions that convey a particular sense or concept.
example_sentence: The signification of this symbol is peace. The poet explained the signification of his verses. Different colors have different significations in culture. The gesture’s signification was understood by everyone present.

english_meaning: Something that indicates, represents, or symbolizes something else. An element, such as a word, symbol, or gesture, that conveys meaning and points to an underlying concept or idea (the “signified”). It is used in linguistics and semiotics to describe how meaning is communicated.
example_sentence: The color red can be a signifier of danger. In semiotics, a flag is a signifier of a nation. Smiling often acts as a signifier of happiness. Certain logos serve as signifiers for brand identity.

english_meaning: To indicate, show, or represent something. To be a sign or symbol of something. To make something known, to express or convey meaning. To have importance or relevance.
example_sentence: The red traffic light signifies that you must stop. His frown signified his disapproval. A wedding ring signifies commitment. The results signify a major breakthrough in research.

english_meaning: Complete absence of sound or noise. The state of not speaking. A situation in which people refuse or fail to speak about something. To cause someone or something to stop making noise. A peaceful quietness.
example_sentence: A deep silence filled the empty church. She kept silence during the whole meeting. The teacher silenced the noisy classroom quickly. The soldiers observed a moment of silence for the fallen.

english_meaning: Sometimes staying quiet and speaking less shows intelligence, maturity, and good judgment. A wise person does not speak unnecessarily. Silence can prevent arguments, mistakes, and misunderstandings. Listening carefully and speaking at the right time often reflects intelligence and self control. The proverb also teaches patience, calmness, and thoughtful behavior.
synonyms: ["Silence is golden","Wise silence","Thoughtful quietness","Tacit wisdom","Calm restraint","Speaking less wisely"]
example_sentence: During the heated argument, Ali stayed calm because he believed that silence is wisdom. The teacher remained quiet and listened carefully, showing that silence is wisdom. Instead of reacting angrily to criticism, she chose silence because silence is wisdom. Wise leaders know that silence is wisdom when emotions are high.

english_meaning: A device fitted to a gun to reduce the noise of firing. A device on an engine or exhaust system that reduces noise. Anything or anyone that stops others from speaking out.
example_sentence: The pistol was fitted with a silencer. A broken silencer makes the car extremely loud. Police found a silencer hidden in the bag. Fear can act as a powerful silencer of dissent.

english_meaning: Making no sound at all. Not speaking or refusing to speak. Not expressed in words but understood. Of a letter, written but not pronounced.
example_sentence: The whole class fell silent when he entered. She remained silent about the accident. The letter k in knife is silent. We walked home through the silent streets.

english_meaning: People born roughly between 1928 and 1945, known for being disciplined, cautious, and conformist. Those born during the Great Depression and World War II, often characterized by a strong sense of responsibility, loyalty, and traditional values. They tended to avoid political activism and outspoken behavior, focusing on careers and family stability.
example_sentence: My grandfather belongs to the Silent Generation and values hard work above all. Members of the Silent Generation witnessed major historical events like WWII and the Korean War. The Silent Generation preferred steady jobs and long-term commitments. Many Silent Generation individuals are now retirees sharing wisdom with younger generations

english_meaning: Without making any sound. Without speaking or expressing anything aloud. In a quiet, unnoticed manner.
example_sentence: He slipped silently out of the room. She silently prayed for their safety. The cat moved silently across the floor. They sat silently, waiting for the news.

english_meaning: The dark shape and outline of someone or something visible against a lighter background. It is a representation of someone showing only the outline, usually in black on white. It can also refer to a profile or a shadow cast by an object.
example_sentence: The mountain peaks were visible as silhouettes against the sunset. I could see the silhouette of a man standing by the window. She cut a beautiful silhouette of her daughter out of black paper. The trees stood like dark silhouettes in the bright moonlight.

english_meaning: A fine, soft fiber produced by silkworms and used to make fabric. A smooth, luxurious cloth known for its shine. Anything soft, glossy, and smooth in texture. Threads or yarn made from silkworm cocoons.
example_sentence: She wore a beautiful silk saree. Silk is one of the most valued natural fibers. His hair felt smooth like silk. The scarf was woven from pure silk.

english_meaning: Lacking good sense or judgment. Foolish or not showing intelligence. Ridiculous or absurd. Playful or not serious.
example_sentence: He made a silly mistake on the test. Stop being silly and listen carefully. She wore a silly hat to the party. It was silly of him to forget his keys.

english_meaning: A foolish or silly person, usually said in a gentle and affectionate way. A playful name for someone who has done something a little stupid or careless. A mild, humorous scolding used especially with children or close friends. Someone who behaves in a childish or clownish manner.
example_sentence: You put the milk in the cupboard again, you silly billy. Don't be such a silly billy and hold the ladder properly. He called himself a silly billy for forgetting his own birthday. The children laughed and called their uncle a silly billy.

english_meaning: A precious greyish-white metal used for coins, jewellery, and cutlery. The shiny pale grey colour of this metal. Coins, cutlery, or ornaments made of this metal. A medal awarded for second place in a competition. To coat or cover something with silver.
example_sentence: The ring was made of pure silver. She polished the family silver before the dinner party. He won a silver at the national championships. The lake shone like silver in the moonlight.

english_meaning: A positive or hopeful aspect of an otherwise negative or difficult situation. The good or beneficial part hidden within misfortune or trouble.
example_sentence: Although he lost his job, the silver lining was that he finally started his own business. The silver lining of the heavy rain was that it filled the reservoirs. She was sick for weeks, but the silver lining was that she learned to take better care of her health. Even in failures, there is always a silver lining, lessons for the future.

english_meaning: A person who speaks in a very smooth, persuasive, and attractive way. A person with excellent speaking ability. Someone who can easily persuade others through speech. A smooth and charming speaker. A person gifted in public speaking or conversation. Someone whose words impress or influence people strongly.
example_sentence: The lawyer used his silver tongue to convince the jury. Her silver tongue helped her win the debate competition. The salesman had a silver tongue and sold all the products quickly. With his silver tongue, he easily made new friends everywhere.

english_meaning: Having the shine or pale grey-white colour of silver. Resembling silver in appearance or lustre. Clear, soft, and pleasantly ringing, as of a sound or voice.
example_sentence: The moon cast a silvery light over the lake. His hair had turned silvery with age. She laughed with a silvery, musical sound. Silvery fish darted beneath the surface of the stream.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being similar to someone or something. A feature or way in which two or more things are alike. Resemblance between people, things, or ideas.
example_sentence: There is a striking similarity between the two paintings. The similarity in their accents suggests they come from the same region. Despite their differences, the sisters share many similarities. The teacher pointed out the similarity between the two historical events.

english_meaning: In a similar way; in almost the same manner. Used to show that two things, ideas, or situations are alike. Likewise; by the same token.
synonyms: ["Likewise","In the same way","Correspondingly","Equally","By the same token","Analogously"]
example_sentence: The two brothers dress similarly and share the same hobbies. The first experiment failed; similarly, the second one produced no results. She loves classical music, and similarly, her husband enjoys opera. The north of the country is mountainous; similarly, the south has many hills.

english_meaning: A figure of speech that compares two different things using like or as. A literary device used to make descriptions more vivid by directly comparing one thing with another different thing, usually by using the words like or as
example_sentence: Simile is used to emphasize or exaggerate a specific quality of one thing by comparing it to something else. Her smile was like sunshine on a rainy day. He fought as brave as a lion. Life is like a rollercoaster, full of ups and downs. The clouds were like cotton floating in the sky. "My love is like a red rose" is a well-known simile from literature. He often employs a simile to paint a picture with words.

english_meaning: To cook something by keeping it almost at boiling point. To be filled with a strong feeling, especially anger, which you have difficulty controlling. (Of an argument, a disagreement, etc) to develop for a period of time without any real anger or violence being shown. To stew gently below or just at the boiling point.
example_sentence: Simmer the sauce gently for 10 minutes. Leave the soup to simmer. She was still simmering with resentment. Anger simmered inside him. She was still quietly simmering from her argument with Natha. This argument has been simmering for months. The simmering dispute finally erupted. Ensure timely resolution of salary and benefits issues to prevent simmering resentment.

english_meaning: To become calm after being angry or excited. It is often used as an instruction for someone to control their temper. It can also mean to reach a state of quiet after a period of intense activity.
example_sentence: I think you need a few minutes to simmer down before we talk. The argument finally began to simmer down after they reached an agreement. Please simmer down and listen to what I have to say. The crowd began to simmer down once the police arrived.

english_meaning: A person who is not very intelligent or is easily fooled. A foolish or gullible person who does not think things through. Someone who lacks good judgment, acts in a naïve way, or understands things slowly. The word often suggests innocence rather than malice.
example_sentence: Everyone knew he was a simpleton but also a kind soul. She treated me like a simpleton even though I understood everything. Only a simpleton would fall for such an obvious trick. They considered him a simpleton because he trusted people too easily. The instructions were so complicated I felt like a complete simpleton.

english_meaning: Too simple and ignoring important details. Overly basic or superficial. Treating a complex matter as if it were easy.
example_sentence: The article gives a simplistic explanation of poverty. His solution was neat but simplistic. We should avoid simplistic answers to complex problems. The diagram is useful but somewhat simplistic.

english_meaning: To imitate or reproduce the behavior, appearance, or conditions of something. It can also mean to pretend to have a feeling or condition that is not real. In science and technology it refers to creating a model of a real situation to study how it works.
example_sentence: Scientists simulate climate conditions to study future environmental changes. The flight training program simulates real flying situations for pilots. The child tried to simulate the voice of his teacher during the play. The patient was accused of trying to simulate illness to avoid work.

english_meaning: An imitation or representation of a real-world process, system, or situation. The act of creating a model or scenario that imitates real events or conditions, often used for training, analysis, or testing without engaging in the actual situation. It can apply to physical systems, computer models, or role-playing exercises.
example_sentence: The manager prepared a computer simulation of likely sales performance for the rest of the year. Young should have been booked for simulation, not awarded a penalty. Training includes realistic simulation of casualty procedures. He began to develop a flight simulation program when he found pilots were taking longer than anticipated to train.

english_meaning: A device or program that imitates real-world conditions for training, testing, or experimentation. A machine, software, or setup designed to replicate the conditions, experiences, or operations of something real. It allows people to practice or experiment in a safe, controlled environment without the risks of the actual scenario.
example_sentence: The flight school uses a simulator to train pilots. Racing drivers practice on a simulator before real competitions. The weather simulator predicts storm patterns. Engineers tested the new machinery in a simulator before full production.

english_meaning: To broadcast the same program on multiple channels or platforms at the same time. The act of transmitting a television or radio program simultaneously over multiple channels or platforms so that different audiences can watch or listen at the same time. Often used in TV, radio, or online streaming contexts.
example_sentence: The football match was simulcast on TV and radio. They decided to simulcast the concert across multiple platforms. News channels often simulcast breaking news to reach a wider audience. The awards ceremony was simulcast online and on local TV stations.

english_meaning: The state of occurring at the same time. Events, actions, or processes happening exactly at the same moment, often emphasizing coordination or concurrency in time. It can apply in daily life, physics, communications, and other contexts.
example_sentence: The simultaneity of the fireworks made the show spectacular. In physics, simultaneity can appear differently depending on the observer’s motion. The simultaneity of their announcements caused confusion in the office. The project requires the simultaneity of multiple teams working together.

english_meaning: Happening at the same time. Two or more events, actions, or processes that occur at exactly the same moment or during the same time period without delay between them. Occurring together, concurrent, coinciding in time, happening collectively at the same moment.
example_sentence: The two explosions were simultaneous and shocked everyone in the area. The translator provided simultaneous interpretation during the conference. Several students pressed the buzzer simultaneously to answer the question. The festival featured simultaneous performances on different stages.

english_meaning: At the same time. When two or more actions, events, or processes happen at exactly the same moment or during the same time period. At the same moment, concurrently, at once, at one time, together in time.
example_sentence: The two singers started the song simultaneously. The lights in the stadium turned on simultaneously. Several alarms rang simultaneously during the emergency drill. The teacher answered two students' questions simultaneously.

english_meaning: Offence against God or against a religious or normal law. A breaking of a moral or legal code.
example_sentence: To commit a sin. Confess your sins to God & He will forgive you. He was more sinned against than sinning=although he is wrong other people treated him even worse.

english_meaning: A special tax imposed by the government on goods and services that are considered harmful to health, society, or morality, such as tobacco, alcohol, gambling, and sugary drinks. It aims both to discourage people from using such products and to raise government revenue for public welfare programs.
example_sentence: The government imposed a sin tax on cigarettes to discourage smoking. Many people believe a sin tax on alcohol helps promote public health. Some economists argue that sin taxes unfairly target the poor. The revenue from the sin tax is used to fund healthcare programs.

english_meaning: From a particular time in the past until now. During the period after a stated event. For the reason that, or because. Used to introduce a cause or explanation of something.
example_sentence: She has lived in Karachi since two thousand and ten. We have not met since the last conference. Since you are already here, you may as well help us. The city has changed a great deal since then.

english_meaning: Honest and truthful in what one says or feels. Free from pretence, deceit, or hypocrisy. Genuine in emotion, intention, or belief. Expressing real feelings rather than an act.
example_sentence: Please accept my sincere thanks for all your help. He is a sincere friend who never hides the truth. Her sincere concern for the patients was evident. They made a sincere effort to resolve the dispute.

english_meaning: In a genuine and honest way, without pretence. With true and heartfelt feeling. Used at the end of a formal letter before the writer's signature. In a manner that reflects real belief or emotion.
example_sentence: I sincerely hope that you recover soon. He sincerely apologised for the misunderstanding. She thanked the teachers sincerely for their support. The letter ended with the words Yours sincerely.

english_meaning: The quality of being honest and free from pretence. Genuineness of feeling, belief, or intention. Truthfulness in what one says or does. The absence of deceit or hypocrisy in a person's character.
example_sentence: No one doubted the sincerity of her apology. He spoke with such sincerity that the audience was moved. The sincerity of his efforts earned him great respect. She questioned the sincerity behind their sudden generosity.

english_meaning: In mathematics, a trigonometric function of an angle, equal to the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle. The curve or wave produced by this function. In anatomy and older usage, a curve, fold or hollow. Used in Latin phrases to mean 'without'.
example_sentence: The sine of a thirty degree angle is exactly one half. Students learned to plot a sine curve on graph paper. The signal was displayed on the screen as a smooth sine wave. In Latin phrases, sine simply means without.

english_meaning: Without a fixed date being set for a future meeting or resumption. Adjourned indefinitely. A Latin legal phrase meaning literally without a day.
example_sentence: The assembly was adjourned sine die after the vote. The hearing stands adjourned sine die pending further inquiry. Talks between the two sides were postponed sine die. The committee rose sine die that evening.

english_meaning: An essential condition or element without which something cannot exist or succeed. An absolutely necessary requirement. A thing that is indispensable to a plan, quality or achievement.
example_sentence: Hard work is the sine qua non of lasting success. Trust is the sine qua non of any healthy relationship. A valid passport is a sine qua non for international travel. Clean water is the sine qua non of public health.

english_meaning: A position or job that requires little or no work but usually provides a salary or benefits. An office or role that offers pay without responsibility. A comfortable and undemanding post held mainly for its rewards. A church benefice without pastoral duties.
example_sentence: The advisory role turned out to be a sinecure with almost no actual duties. Critics claimed the appointment was a political sinecure. He was rewarded for his loyalty with a comfortable sinecure. Many considered the honorary chairmanship a mere sinecure.

english_meaning: A tough fibrous tissue that joins muscle to bone; a tendon. Physical strength, power or muscular energy. The essential source of strength or support of something, such as an institution or an economy.
example_sentence: The cook trimmed the sinew from the meat before cooking. Years of farming had built sinew in his arms. Small businesses are the sinew of the local economy. You could see the sinews standing out on the runner's legs.

english_meaning: Having strong, visible muscles; lean and muscular. Consisting of or resembling sinews; tough and fibrous. Difficult to chew because it is full of tough tissue. Forceful and vigorous in style or expression.
example_sentence: The blacksmith had sinewy arms from years of work. The meat was dry and sinewy and hard to chew. She admired his lean, sinewy build. The poet is known for his sinewy prose.

english_meaning: A short or light symphony, usually simpler in structure than a full symphony. A small symphony orchestra, often with fewer players than a standard orchestra.
example_sentence: The composer wrote a charming sinfonietta for strings. The city sinfonietta performed at the town hall. Her sinfonietta lasts only fifteen minutes. He joined the sinfonietta as a violinist.

english_meaning: Grave as a sin; wicked or immoral. To be characterized by or involving sin. To be offensive or highly objectionable to a religious or moral standard. Very bad or excessive in a way that suggests a lack of restraint.
example_sentence: He realized that his greedy actions were deeply sinful. The dessert was so delicious it felt almost sinful to eat the whole thing. They led a sinful life according to the strict teachings of their church. It is a sinful waste of money to buy things you never intend to use. The dictator’s sinful treatment of his people led to an uprising.

english_meaning: In a way that breaks religious or moral law; wickedly. In a manner considered morally wrong or immoral. Informally, to an enjoyable degree that feels almost wrong; extremely or indulgently.
example_sentence: He admitted that he had lived sinfully in his youth. The chocolate cake was sinfully rich. She spoke of those who behave sinfully and feel no shame. The hotel was sinfully luxurious.

english_meaning: To speak very highly of someone and openly praise their qualities, skills, or achievements. To praise a person in a very strong and enthusiastic way, often by telling others about their good qualities or achievements. It is usually used when someone is impressed and wants to highlight how good another person is.
example_sentence: The teacher sang her student’s praises after he won the science competition. Everyone is singing the manager’s praises for improving the company. My friend keeps singing his brother’s praises because he is very talented. After the performance, the audience sang the actor’s praises.

english_meaning: Only one in number; not one of several. Separate, individual, or considered alone. Unmarried or not currently in a romantic relationship. Intended or suitable for one person. A one-way ticket rather than a return ticket. A recording released separately, usually featuring one main song. One run scored in cricket or a hit that reaches first base in baseball. A banknote worth one unit, especially one dollar. To select or distinguish one person or thing from a group. To hit a single in baseball.
example_sentence: Not a single light was on in the building. She booked a single room for one night. The singer released a new single in June. The batter singled to left field and drove in a run.

english_meaning: Suggesting or giving the impression that something harmful or evil is happening or will happen. Something that seems threatening, evil, or likely to cause trouble. Often describes a feeling, appearance, or action that is ominous or harmful.
example_sentence: The old abandoned house had a sinister look at night. There was a sinister smile on the villain’s face. The storm clouds gave a sinister feeling to the evening. He had a sinister plan that nobody suspected.

english_meaning: To go down below the surface of something, especially a liquid; to become submerged. A fixed basin with a water supply and a drain. To drop or descend to a lower level or state. To gradually decrease in amount, value, or intensity. To pass into a specified condition, usually a negative one. To penetrate or go deep into something.
example_sentence: The heavy stones will sink to the bottom of the lake. She filled the kitchen sink with soapy water to wash the dishes. His heart began to sink when he saw the test results. The sun began to sink below the horizon, painting the sky orange. Investors worried as they watched the stock prices continue to sink.

english_meaning: To attack something with energy or enthusiasm. To engage in something with great determination, intensity, or focus; can be literal (biting) or figurative (tackling a task or problem aggressively)
example_sentence: She really sank her teeth into the project and finished it ahead of schedule. The dog sank its teeth into the bone. He sank his teeth into the issue of corruption during the debate. Once he started reading the book, he sank his teeth into it and couldn’t stop.

english_meaning: Having many curves and turns. Moving in a winding or wavy manner like a snake. Characterized by a supple and lithe quality in movement or form.
example_sentence: The river followed a sinuous path through the deep valley. The dancers moved with sinuous grace across the stage. A sinuous vine climbed slowly up the brick wall. We drove along the sinuous mountain road with extreme caution.

english_meaning: A mathematical curve that describes a smooth periodic oscillation. It is named after the function sine, of which it is the graph. A waveform that oscillates above and below a central value in a regular pattern.
example_sentence: The oscilloscope displayed a perfect sinusoid on the screen. Engineers use the sinusoid to model alternating current in electricity. The vibrations of the tuning fork produced a pure sinusoid. The movement of the pendulum can be mapped as a sinusoid over time.

english_meaning: Relating to, shaped like, or varying according to a sine curve. Used to describe waves or motions that follow a regular, repetitive, and smooth undulating pattern. Frequently used in physics and engineering to describe electrical currents or sound waves.
example_sentence: The alternating current follows a sinusoidal pattern. Sinusoidal waves are fundamental to the study of trigonometry. Sound travels through the air as sinusoidal pressure variations. The heart rate monitor showed a steady sinusoidal rhythm.

english_meaning: A device that makes a loud warning sound, used on emergency vehicles and alarms. In Greek mythology, a creature that was part woman and part bird who lured sailors to their death with beautiful singing. A woman who is dangerously attractive and seductive. A warning or signal.
example_sentence: The siren of the ambulance could be heard long before the vehicle came into view. In the Odyssey, Odysseus had himself tied to the mast so he could hear the sirens without being lured. She was described in the press as a siren whose charm had undone many powerful men. The factory siren signalled the end of the working day. The wailing siren of the fire engine cut through the noise of the traffic.

english_meaning: A person, usually a boy or man, who is considered weak, overly sensitive, or lacking courage. It is often used as an insult. A cowardly person. Someone easily frightened. A person who avoids tough or risky situations. A term used teasingly among friends in a lighthearted way
example_sentence: He called his brother a sissy for being afraid of the dark. Do not be a sissy, try the roller coaster at least once. Some boys are unfairly labeled as sissies just because they are gentle. It is wrong to tease someone by calling them a sissy.

english_meaning: Relating to a task that can never be completed. Something that is pointless, fruitless, and exhausting despite constant effort. Named after the mythical King Sisyphus who was condemned to roll a boulder up a hill for eternity. An endless and ineffective struggle.
example_sentence: Cleaning a house with three toddlers often feels like a Sisyphean struggle. The diplomat faced the Sisyphean task of trying to bring peace to a region plagued by centuries of conflict. Bureaucracy can turn a simple application into a Sisyphean ordeal. He felt his life was a Sisyphean cycle of debt and repayment. Writing a dictionary alone is a Sisyphean undertaking.

english_meaning: To remain inactive while something happens. To watch a harmful, unfair, or important situation without intervening. To fail to act despite having the opportunity or responsibility to do so.
synonyms: ["Stand by","Look on","Remain Passive","Do Nothing","Stay Inactive","Be a Bystander"]
example_sentence: We cannot sit idly by while families go hungry. She refused to sit idly by when her colleague was treated unfairly. The authorities sat idly by as the problem grew worse. Good neighbors do not sit idly by during an emergency.

english_meaning: To stay in one place and wait patiently without taking action until the right moment or until further instructions are given. It often means to remain calm and not to panic or interfere when something is happening or being decided.
synonyms: ["Wait patiently","Say put","Remain still","Hold on","Be patient","Stand by"]
example_sentence: Sit tight and wait for news. The teacher told the students to sit tight until the principal arrived. We just have to sit tight and wait for the results. During the storm, the villagers sat tight in their houses. Don’t worry, sit tight and everything will be fine.

english_meaning: To participate in a peaceful protest by sitting in a place to demand change or express disagreement. A peaceful form of protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave until their demands are met. Protest by staying seated
example_sentence: Students sat in to demand better facilities. Activists sat in at city hall for several hours. The students staged a sit-in in the library. The workers held a sit-in at the factory. Activists held a sit-in to support environmental reforms.

english_meaning: An easy target or vulnerable person that is open to attack, harm, or criticism. Someone or something that is unaware of impending danger and completely undefended. A situation or object dangerously exposed to harm without any shelter or protection.
synonyms: ["Easy target","Vulnerable target","Soft target","Open target","Defenseless person","Unprotected target","Easy prey","Helpless victim","Sitting target","Exposed target"]
antonyms: ["Protected target","Well-defended person","Fortified position","Secure individual","Hard target","Invulnerable object","Guarded target","Safe person"]
example_sentence: Without air defense, the military base was a sitting duck for enemy air strikes. Walking alone through the dark alley at night made him feel like a sitting duck. The unsophisticated computer network was a sitting duck for cyber attackers. Tourists who leave their belongings unattended on the beach are sitting ducks for thieves.

english_meaning: To place or position something in a particular location. To build or establish something at a chosen site. To understand or describe something in relation to its wider context.
example_sentence: They decided to situate the school near the park. The architect situated the windows to capture morning light. We must situate the poem in its historical context. The factory is situated away from residential streets.

english_meaning: Located or positioned in a particular place. Placed in particular circumstances or surroundings. Having a stated financial, social, or practical position.
example_sentence: The hotel is situated beside the river. Our office is conveniently situated near the station. The village is situated in a fertile valley. She is well situated to lead the new project.

english_meaning: The set of circumstances at a particular time. A condition or state of affairs. The position or location of something. A job or employment. A problem or challenge to deal with.
example_sentence: The situation in the country is improving. We must handle this situation carefully. The house is in a beautiful situation near the lake. He found himself in a difficult situation.

english_meaning: Relating to a particular situation or set of circumstances. Caused or shaped by the immediate environment rather than permanent traits. Designed to fit or respond to a specific context.
example_sentence: Good leaders develop strong situational awareness. His anxiety was situational rather than chronic. The training uses situational examples from real workplaces. Humor is often situational and difficult to translate.

english_meaning: An intuitive ability to perceive things beyond the normal five senses. A strong feeling that something is true without logical proof. Instinctive knowledge or awareness. A natural gift for sensing hidden truths. Perception based on intuition rather than reasoning.
example_sentence: Her sixth sense told her something was wrong. He has a sixth sense for detecting lies. A mother often has a sixth sense about her children. My sixth sense warned me not to trust him.

english_meaning: To move or glide over a surface using shoes with wheels or blades. A tool or shoe equipped with a metal runner for ice or small wheels for pavement. To glide through a situation easily or without much effort. Any of various flat-bodied marine fish related to rays. To perform a maneuver on a skateboard. To avoid dealing with a difficult task or consequence.
example_sentence: She learned how to skate on the frozen pond during the winter. The professional athlete replaced the worn-out wheels on his inline skate. The student tried to skate through the semester without doing any homework. We watched a large skate swimming gracefully near the ocean floor.

english_meaning: The framework of bones in a body. The hard internal structure made of bones that supports the body of a human or animal and protects important organs
example_sentence: The human skeleton consists of 206 bones. The disease has reduced him to skeleton. Scientists studied the skeleton of the dinosaur in the museum. The doctor explained how the human skeleton supports the body. After months of illness he looked like a skeleton. The writer first prepared a skeleton plan of the story.

english_meaning: A shameful secret from the past that is kept hidden. A private fact that would cause embarrassment if it became known. A hidden scandal within a family or organisation.
example_sentence: Every old family has a skeleton in the cupboard. The journalist found a skeleton in the cupboard of the firm. He resigned before the skeleton in the cupboard came out. She feared her past was a skeleton in the cupboard.

english_meaning: A person who doubts the truth of claims without evidence. Someone who questions accepted ideas or beliefs. A person who refuses to accept something until it is proven. A critical thinker who demands facts before belief.
example_sentence: The skeptic refused to believe the story without evidence. She is a skeptic when it comes to advertisements and marketing claims. Even after the explanation, the skeptic asked for more proof. Scientists are often skeptics who test ideas before accepting them.

english_meaning: Having doubt about something and not easily convinced. Questioning the truth, validity, or reliability of something. Showing a cautious attitude before accepting claims or information. Not believing something until strong evidence is given
example_sentence: I am skeptical about his explanation because it sounds incomplete. She was skeptical of the new marketing strategy at first. Many scientists remain skeptical until they see strong evidence. He looked skeptical when he heard the unbelievable story.

english_meaning: In a doubtful or questioning way, not easily believing something. With suspicion about truth or honesty. In a critical thinking manner. With doubt about success or reality. With cautious disbelief.
example_sentence: She looked at the news skeptically because it sounded unrealistic. He smiled skeptically when they promised instant success. The scientist listened skeptically to the unusual claim. They reacted skeptically to the sudden price drop.

english_meaning: Doubting or questioning the truth of something until there is enough proof. An attitude of doubt or disbelief toward claims, ideas, or information until they are supported by strong evidence or logical reasoning. A person with skepticism does not easily accept things as true without verification.
example_sentence: She showed skepticism about the new medical treatment. His skepticism made him ask for strong evidence before believing the news. There is widespread skepticism about the government's promise. Scientists use skepticism to test theories carefully.

english_meaning: Not thorough or detailed. Dishonest or disreputable. Not complete or detailed and therefore not very useful. That people consider to be dishonest or bad. Containing few details. Not completely safe or not completely honest.
example_sentence: The information they had was sketchy. He gave us a very sketchy account of his visit. He was a man with a sketchy past and even sketchier morals. So far we only have sketchy information about what caused the explosion. They lived in a sketchy neighborhood. That street looks pretty sketchy.

english_meaning: To suddenly change direction or position. To make something biased or distorted in a way that is not accurate. To cause a set of data or results to be asymmetrical or misleading. To look obliquely or squint at something.
example_sentence: The presence of the supervisor might skew the results of the employee survey. He tried not to skew the picture frame when hanging it on the wall. The media's coverage tends to skew public opinion toward one political party. The statistician noticed a significant skew in the distribution curve.

english_meaning: To slide suddenly and uncontrollably, especially of a vehicle on a wet or slippery surface. A sudden slide or slip, often resulting in loss of control. A wooden or metal plank used to support or move heavy objects. To experience a sudden decline, especially in value, performance, or quality.
example_sentence: The car skidded on the icy road and nearly hit the barrier.  He lost control of his bike when it skidded on the wet pavement.  The company's profits began to skid after the new policy was introduced.  The truck skidded to a halt just inches from the pedestrian.  Heavy crates were moved across the warehouse on wooden skids.

english_meaning: To read, look at, or examine something quickly. To remove a substance floating on the surface of a liquid. To move lightly and rapidly over or near a surface. To steal small amounts of money, especially before it is officially recorded. A thin layer or film on a liquid. A rapid, superficial reading or examination. Made with most or all cream removed from milk.
example_sentence: Skim the article before deciding whether to read it fully. She skimmed the foam from the soup. Swallows skimmed the surface of the pond. The accountant was caught skimming cash from daily sales.

english_meaning: To remove a floating layer from the top of a liquid. To take the best, most useful, or most profitable part of something. To divert or steal a small portion of money. To separate selected people or resources from a larger group.
example_sentence: Skim off the fat after the soup has cooled. Large firms sometimes skim off the most profitable clients. The cashier was accused of skimming off a portion of the receipts. The program skimmed off the strongest candidates for advanced training.

english_meaning: To read or examine something quickly and without close attention. To move lightly across the surface of something. To treat a subject briefly without discussing its details. To overlook information during a rapid review.
example_sentence: I skimmed over the email before the meeting. The stone skimmed over the calm surface of the lake. The speaker skimmed over the most controversial issue. She skimmed over the contract and missed an important clause.

english_meaning: To move quickly past or just above something. To read beyond a part without giving it attention. To pass a subject briefly in conversation or writing. To overlook a detail while reviewing material rapidly.
example_sentence: The boat skimmed past the rocks without touching them. I skimmed past the introduction and went to the results. She skimmed past the awkward subject in her speech. Do not skim past the safety instructions.

english_meaning: To read or look through material quickly to get its main ideas. To search a collection rapidly without examining every item. To review a document superficially. To pass quickly through a large amount of information.
example_sentence: She skimmed through the report during lunch. I skimmed through the files until I found the receipt. Please skim through these notes before class. He skimmed through the morning news on his phone.

english_meaning: To expend or use less time, money, or material on something than is necessary in an attempt to save. To provide a person or thing with inadequate quantity or quality. To be stingy or frugal. To manage with difficulty by being very economical.
example_sentence: Don't skimp on the butter if you want the cake to taste delicious. They had to skimp and save for years to afford their own home. It is never a good idea to skimp on safety equipment. The company was accused of skimping on employee benefits to increase profits. Even though they were poor, they never skimped on their children's education.

english_meaning: Small, insufficient, very short, or revealing in amount, size, or clothing. Too small in amount or quantity. Not enough for comfort or need. Very short or revealing clothes. Lacking fullness or completeness.
example_sentence: The workers received a skimpy salary for their hard work. She wore a skimpy dress at the beach party. The report gave only skimpy details about the incident. We had a skimpy meal because food was limited.

english_meaning: The thin layer of tissue that covers the outside of the body. The body's largest organ, which protects it from injury, germs, and water loss. The outer covering that helps control body temperature and allows us to feel touch. The hide or outer covering of an animal, or the natural covering of a fruit or vegetable. To remove the outer covering from something, such as a fruit or an animal.
example_sentence: The skin protects the body from harmful bacteria. Sunlight can damage the skin if you stay outside too long. She has very sensitive skin and uses gentle soap. He skinned the potatoes before boiling them.

english_meaning: Very thin or lean, often unusually so. Having little flesh or fat on the body. Fitting very closely to the body, as in tight clothing. Made with reduced fat, as in certain drinks or foods. Informal term for confidential or inside information.
example_sentence: He was a tall, skinny boy with long legs. She wore a pair of skinny jeans to the party. The skinny cat looked like it needed a good meal. He ordered a skinny latte with no sugar. Tell me the skinny on what happened at the meeting.

english_meaning: A garment hanging from the waist worn by women and girls. An outer edge or border of an area or group. To pass along or around the edge of something. To attempt to avoid dealing with a difficult issue or topic.
example_sentence: She bought a colorful summer skirt at the local market. The road skirts the edge of the dense forest. The speaker tried to skirt around the sensitive political subject. They live on the skirts of the growing metropolis.

english_meaning: To avoid work or duty, especially by leaving or staying away without a valid excuse. A British informal term meaning to dodge one's responsibilities. To slice or shave leather or rubber thinly.
example_sentence: He would regularly skive on Wednesday afternoons when the workload was lightest. She knew she could not afford to skive with such an important deadline approaching. The apprentice was taught how to skive the leather carefully before stitching. They decided to skive and spent the afternoon in the park instead of the office. The bookbinder used a skiving tool to thin the edges of the leather cover.

english_meaning: To leave work or school early without permission or a valid excuse. To avoid duties or responsibilities by sneaking away. A British informal expression for dodging work.
example_sentence: He managed to skive off the last two lessons of the afternoon without the teacher noticing. She was caught trying to skive off work early on a Friday afternoon by her supervisor. He had a reputation for skiving off whenever things got difficult or boring. They decided to skive off the training session and go to a café instead. She could not afford to skive off any more shifts if she wanted to keep her job.

english_meaning: To move stealthily or hide, especially with bad intentions. To lurk in a secretive way. To avoid work or duty by hiding. To sneak around in a suspicious manner. To conceal oneself while waiting or watching.
example_sentence: The thief was skulking in the alley behind the house. He skulked around the office instead of doing his work. A fox was seen skulking near the henhouse. She skulked in the shadows to avoid being noticed.

english_meaning: The bony framework of the head that encloses and protects the brain. The complete set of bones forming the head and face. The hard structure that gives shape to the head. The bone case of the head, often used as a symbol of death.
example_sentence: The helmet protects the skull during an accident. Archaeologists found an ancient human skull at the site. A fractured skull requires immediate medical attention. The flag carried a skull and crossbones symbol.

english_meaning: There is no restriction on success, growth, or achievement. It is used to encourage someone by saying that their potential is unlimited. It often refers to ambitions, dreams, business success, education, or personal goals.
example_sentence: With her talent and hard work, the sky's the limit. If you invest wisely, the sky's the limit for your business growth. He believes that with education, the sky's the limit. Once you gain confidence, the sky's the limit for what you can achieve.

english_meaning: Extremely tall, multi-story building designed for office, residential, or commercial use. Typically, it is a symbol of modern architecture and urban development.
example_sentence: New York City has many famous skyscrapers. The company moved its headquarters into a new skyscraper downtown. Tourists admired the skyscraper for its glass facade. Living in a skyscraper gives a great view of the city.

english_meaning: To become less active, to reduce effort, to loosen. Lack of activity, laziness, loose part of rope or system. Not tight, lacking energy, inactive.
example_sentence: The rope became slack after some time. Business is usually slack during the winter season. Do not slack in your studies if you want success. His efforts began to slack after the initial excitement.

english_meaning: To work less hard than usual. To become lazy or careless in duties. To reduce effort or stop putting in full energy. To slow down in performance or activity. To avoid responsibilities or delay work.
example_sentence: He started to slack off after getting the promotion. Students should not slack off before exams. She never slacks off even under pressure. The team began to slack off in the final minutes of the game.

english_meaning: A person who avoids work, avoids effort, or does things slowly and carelessly. Someone who does not put in proper effort, avoids responsibilities, or performs tasks with very little interest. The word is often used for people who intentionally delay work or waste time instead of being productive.
example_sentence: He was called a slacker because he never finished his assignments on time. The manager warned the slackers in the team to improve their performance. She used to be a slacker, but now she works very hard. No one wants to work with a slacker who avoids every task.

english_meaning: Stony waste matter separated from metals during the smelting or refining of ore. In a colloquial sense, it is used to describe harsh criticism or verbal abuse. It also broadly denotes worthless matter left over from a process.
example_sentence: The factory produced mountains of black slag during the intensive smelting process. In the interview, she refused to publicly slag off her former employers. The heavy slag is carefully separated from the pure molten metal. It is not professional to constantly slag your coworkers behind their backs. The road was reinforced using layers of cooling industrial slag.

english_meaning: The process of producing stony waste from metals, or the accumulation of slag. In informal use, it means severely criticizing, mocking, or verbally attacking someone. It conveys continuous disparagement or ridicule.
example_sentence: The furnace required constant monitoring to prevent improper slagging of the metal. She was severely reprimanded for openly slagging off the company's new policies. The continuous slagging severely affected the morale of the entire office team. Slagging off the competition might make you look extremely desperate. Proper slagging ensures that the extracted iron is incredibly pure.

english_meaning: Put to death intentionally or with great force. Killed violently. Killed in a harsh or forceful manner. Destroyed or ruined completely. Used in storytelling or poetry to describe tragic death. Past participle (V3/Third form) of slay.
example_sentence: Many innocent people were slain in the conflict. The monster was finally slain after a long struggle. He felt emotionally slain by the betrayal. The police found the slain victim near the abandoned building. Many soldiers were slain in the fierce battle. The family mourned their slain relative for months. The report described the slain leader as a man of courage.

english_meaning: To satisfy thirst or desire. To reduce intensity of something such as thirst, curiosity, or anger. To relieve or satisfy a strong need such as thirst, hunger, curiosity, or desire. It can also mean to cool, moisten, or chemically react with water such as slaking lime.
example_sentence: A glass of cold water helped slake his thirst after the long walk. She read many books to slake her curiosity about history. The rain began to slake the dry soil of the field. Workers used water to slake the lime during construction.

english_meaning: To shut something with force, hit hard, or criticize strongly. To hit something with great force. To express strong disapproval. Close something loudly and with force. Put someone in jail. System crash or overload.
example_sentence: I heard the door slam behind him. The window slammed shut in the wind. He stormed out of the house slamming the door as he left. He slammed on the car brakes.

english_meaning: To make false and damaging statements about someone. To defame a person's character through spoken false statements. To harm someone's reputation by lying about them. The act of speaking untrue and harmful things about another person. A false spoken statement that damages a person's reputation. Slander refers to the spoken form of defamation, in which a person deliberately tells lies about another to injure their reputation, honor, or standing in society.
example_sentence: He was sued for slander after making false accusations against his colleague. Spreading slander about innocent people is both unethical and illegal. The politician accused his rival of slander during the campaign. She refused to slander her former employer despite being mistreated. The court fined him heavily for the slander he had spread.

english_meaning: False and malicious, especially when referring to spoken statements. Characterized by or uttering character-damaging falsehoods. Intended to harm someone's reputation through lies.
example_sentence: The journalist was fired for making slanderous remarks about the CEO. She filed a lawsuit to stop the distribution of slanderous pamphlets. He regretted his slanderous comments the moment they left his mouth. The article was filled with slanderous lies and baseless rumors.

english_meaning: Informal words or expressions used in casual speech, not considered standard language. Informal language that is usually used by specific groups of people. It is not part of formal writing or standard grammar. Slang changes quickly over time and often reflects culture, trends, or social groups.
example_sentence: “That movie was awesome, totally cool slang among teens”. “He is my buddy, a common slang word for friend”. “She said the food was lit, which is modern slang for excellent”. “Don’t be a noob, a slang term for a beginner”.

english_meaning: Done too quickly and without enough care or thought. Characterized by a lack of order or planning. Haphazard and slipshod in manner. Performing work in a careless or hurried fashion.
example_sentence: The builders did such a slapdash job that the roof began to leak within a week. She made a slapdash attempt to tidy the room before the guests arrived. I could tell by the slapdash way the report was written that it was finished at the last minute. The government's slapdash response to the crisis was widely criticized. Don't be so slapdash with your homework if you want a good grade.

english_meaning: Something impressive, exciting, or enjoyable. To criticize or scold sharply. To have a sudden, strong effect. To hit someone with an open hand.
example_sentence: That new track really slaps!. The manager slaps the team for missing the deadline. The news slaps you in the face with reality. He slaps his friend on the back in greeting. He slaps the mosquito off his arm.

english_meaning: To cut something with a long quick stroke. To reduce something sharply such as prices, budgets, or staff. To attack strongly with words or criticism. A long deep cut made by a sharp object. A strong reduction in amount or a punctuation mark used between words or numbers like /.
example_sentence: She tried to kill herself by slashing her wrists. The work force has been slashed by half. The government plan to slash down the petrol price by half. The thief tried to slash the bag with a knife. The government decided to slash fuel prices this month. The editor slashed the article because it contained many errors. A deep slash was visible on the wooden door.

english_meaning: A dark bluish grey colour resembling the stone slate. Of a dull, heavy grey shade, often used of the sky or the sea. Having a cold, sombre grey appearance.
example_sentence: The sky was slate-grey before the storm broke. He wore a slate-grey suit to the meeting. Slate-grey waves crashed against the harbour wall. The house had a slate-grey roof and white walls.

english_meaning: To kill animals for meat or to kill brutally. To defeat someone completely in a competition or argument. Killing animals for food or killing many people or animals in a very cruel or violent manner. It may also refer to a situation where many people are killed in war, attack, or conflict.
example_sentence: Farmers slaughter animals to produce meat for food. The battle resulted in the slaughter of many soldiers. The team slaughtered their opponents with a huge score. The movie shows the tragic slaughter of innocent villagers.

english_meaning: A person who is legal property of another and is forced to obey them. A person who is strongly influenced and controlled by something. To work excessively hard. To labor in a state of servitude.
example_sentence: In ancient times, many people lived their entire lives as slaves. He is a slave to his work and rarely sees his family. She slaved away in the kitchen all day preparing the feast. History books document the struggles of those who were kept as slaves. Don't let yourself become a slave to fashion trends.

english_meaning: The state of being a slave and being owned by another person. The practice or system of owning slaves. A condition of having no freedom or being under the intense control of something. The state of being subject to a specific influence or habit.
example_sentence: The abolition of slavery was a major turning point in human history. They were sold into slavery and taken far from their homes. Poverty can often feel like a form of economic slavery. The long hours of the job felt like a modern kind of slavery. Many activists fight to end modern-day human trafficking and slavery.

english_meaning: Behaving like a slave by being overly submissive or showing no originality. Copying something exactly without independent thought. Characteristic of a slave or the status of a slave. Showing a lack of spirit or autonomy.
example_sentence: He gave a slavish adherence to the rules without considering the context. The movie was a slavish imitation of the original book. No one respected his slavish devotion to the corrupt leader. She followed the fashion trends with a slavish enthusiasm. A slavish translation often fails to capture the soul of the poetry.

english_meaning: To kill someone or something in a violent way. To defeat someone decisively. To impress people strongly, especially with performance, style, or skill. To affect someone deeply with laughter, shock, or admiration.
example_sentence: Recognize the vampires in your life and slay them. The knight slayed the dragon bravely. She slayed the audience with her singing. His joke completely slayed everyone in the room. Our team slayed the competition in the final match.

english_meaning: Having a smooth, shining, and healthy surface or appearance. Well-groomed and sophisticated. Moving with ease and grace. Streamlined and elegant in design.
example_sentence: The cat's fur was black and sleek. The new sports car has a sleek and modern design. He looked very sleek in his tailored Italian suit. The seal’s sleek body helped it glide through the water. She smoothed back her sleek hair before the interview.

english_meaning: To stay asleep longer than usual in the morning. To sleep later than usual in the morning. To stay in bed intentionally for extra rest.
example_sentence: I like to sleep in on weekends. We slept in after the long flight. He missed the meeting because he slept in. She enjoys sleeping in during holidays.

english_meaning: To delay a decision until the next day so you can think more clearly. To take extra time before giving an answer to something important. To postpone judgement in order to reflect calmly and avoid mistakes. To let time pass so that your feelings settle before you choose.
synonyms: ["Think it over","Mull over","Consider","Reflect on","Take time","Deliberate","Weigh up"]
example_sentence: Don't answer now; sleep on it and tell me tomorrow. I decided to sleep on it before signing the contract. She slept on it and changed her mind by morning. It is always wise to sleep on it before making a big purchase.

english_meaning: Needing or ready for sleep; feeling tired and drowsy. Lacking activity, movement, or excitement; quiet and peaceful. Inducing or tending to cause sleep. Moving or acting slowly or lethargically.
example_sentence: The warm afternoon sun made everyone feel very sleepy after lunch. They live in a sleepy little village tucked away in the hills. The baby rubbed her sleepy eyes and began to fall asleep. Soft music played in the background created a sleepy atmosphere in the room.

english_meaning: To stay overnight at someone else’s house. To think carefully about something before making a decision.
example_sentence: The kids slept over at their grandparents’ house. Can I sleep over at your place tonight? My cousin used to sleep over when we were young. I need to sleep over your proposal before replying

english_meaning: To remain asleep during something that normally might wake you, such as an alarm, noise, or an important event. It implies missing out on something because of uninterrupted sleep.
example_sentence: I slept through the entire storm. She slept through her alarm again. The baby slept through the night. He slept through the movie.

english_meaning: To fall from the sky as small ice pellets or as a mixture of rain and snow. A form of precipitation that occurs when rain drops freeze before reaching the ground, forming small ice pellets. It may also refer to a mixture of rain and partially melted snow that falls during cold weather.
example_sentence: The rain turned into sleet during the cold evening. Drivers slowed down because sleet made the road slippery. It began to sleet heavily in the afternoon. The hikers continued walking despite the sleet.

english_meaning: The part of a garment that covers an arm. A protective cover or casing for an object. To provide an object with a sleeve. A paper or plastic cover for a record or document.
example_sentence: I rolled up my sleeves and started cleaning the garage. He wore a shirt with long sleeves even in the summer. The mechanic put a metal sleeve over the pipe to stop the leak. She slid the vinyl record back into its protective sleeve. You should wear a long-sleeved shirt to protect yourself from mosquito bites.

english_meaning: A vehicle on runners used for travelling over snow or ice. A light sledge drawn by horses or reindeer. To travel or ride in such a vehicle.
example_sentence: The children rode a sleigh down the snowy slope. A horse-drawn sleigh carried them to the village. Bells jingled on the sleigh as it passed. They sleighed across the frozen valley at dusk.

english_meaning: Skill or cleverness, especially in a quick, deceptive, or tricky way. Often used in the phrase “sleight of hand”, meaning skill in performing tricks, especially to deceive or entertain.
example_sentence: So my secret can be hidden behind the sleight of a venial fib after all. Sleight was a genuine friend of deaf and dumb people. Must have employed some sophisticated sleight to con that wary couple out of their money. A brilliant new theory that pays tribute to his remarkable sleight of mind.

english_meaning: Movements of your hand that are done with skill so that other people cannot see them. The fact of tricking people in a clever way. Skillful hiding of the truth in order to win an advantage. Speed and skill with the hands when performing tricks that seem to be magic.
example_sentence: The trick is done simply by sleight of hand. Last year's profits were more the result of financial sleight of hand than genuine growth. Most of these conjuring tricks depend on sleight of hand. By some statistical sleight of hand the government has produced figures showing that unemployment has recently fallen. He's used sleight of hand on the accounts.

english_meaning: Thin and gracefully built; slim and attractive in shape. Small in width or thickness compared with the length. Small in amount, size, or extent. Barely sufficient or only just enough. Weak or insufficient, as in evidence, hope, or chances.
example_sentence: She has a tall, slender figure and long dark hair. The slender vase looked beautiful on the wooden table. He won the election by a slender margin of just fifty votes. The family was living on a very slender income. There is only a slender chance that the missing climbers will be found alive.

english_meaning: A person who carefully investigates crimes, mysteries, or hidden facts by searching for clues and evidence. The word is often used for detectives, investigators, or anyone who skillfully discovers information.
example_sentence: The sleuth examined the footprints near the window. She became a skilled sleuth while solving local mysteries. The journalist acted like a sleuth to uncover the truth. The young boy played the role of a sleuth in the school drama.

english_meaning: A large number or amount of something. A considerable amount. To turn or slide suddenly in another direction. To turn, slide, or rotate violently or uncontrollably. To kill or slay. A swamp or muddy area.
example_sentence: The car skidded and slewed sideways. This year has seen a whole slew of novels set in Hong Kong. The truck slewed on the icy road, narrowly missing a tree. He slew the opponents in the debate with strong arguments. The project produced a slew of unexpected problems. The knight slew the dragon. The hunter slew the wild boar. The car got stuck in the slews near the river.

english_meaning: A person who investigates crimes or solves mysteries. A detective or private investigator who tracks clues and follows trails to uncover the truth. The act of tracking or following someone secretly. To investigate or trail someone closely.
example_sentence: The famous sleuth was able to solve the cold case in just two days. She decided to play amateur sleuth to find out who was stealing her mail. The private sleuth followed the suspect through the crowded city streets. He spent his weekends acting as a sleuth for historical mysteries. Many classic novels feature a brilliant sleuth at the center of the plot.

english_meaning: To cut something from a larger piece with a sharp tool. To remove a portion by cutting smoothly, usually with a knife or sharp tool, often creating a clean and even piece.
example_sentence: She sliced off a piece of bread. He sliced off the excess fabric. The chef sliced off the fat from the meat. Be careful not to slice off your finger!.

english_meaning: Small in degree, amount, or intensity. Not sturdy or strongly built; thin or slender. An insult or act of being treated with a lack of respect. To insult someone by treating them as unimportant. To neglect or ignore someone or something intentionally.
example_sentence: I felt a slight chill in the air as the sun went down. The two machines have a slight difference in their design. He took it as a personal slight when he wasn't invited to the wedding. She is quite slight in build but very strong. Even a slight mistake in the calculations could lead to failure.

english_meaning: To a small degree or extent. In a manner that is not large or significant. Somewhat or a little bit. By a slim margin. In a slender or thin manner when describing physique. To a limited or negligible amount.
example_sentence: The new model is slightly more expensive than the previous one. I felt slightly offended by his casual remark. She leaned slightly forward to hear the whisper. The results of the experiment differed slightly from our expectations.

english_meaning: A thick, slippery, and typically unpleasant liquid substance. A moist, soft, or slippery mud or clay. A repulsive person who is considered dishonest or untrustworthy. To cover or smear something with a slippery substance.
example_sentence: The stones near the river were covered in green slime. The snail left a silvery trail of slime behind it as it moved. He felt like a total slime after lying to his best friend. The stagnant pond had a layer of thick slime on the surface. Be careful not to slip on the slime in the cave.

english_meaning: Covered with or resembling slime, which is a moist, soft, and slippery substance. Often used figuratively to describe a person who is dishonest, sycophantic, or repulsive. Slippery and unpleasant to the touch.
example_sentence: The rocks at the bottom of the pond were green and slimy. I don't trust that slimy salesman at the used car lot. The trail left by the snail was thin and slimy. He gave me a slimy grin that made me feel very uncomfortable.

english_meaning: Used for a person, movement, or clothing that appears soft, flowing, and slightly seductive. It often suggests elegance and a smooth, curving style of motion. A well known toy made from a flexible metal or plastic coil that can stretch and move down steps while keeping its spring shape.
example_sentence: The model walked with a slinky elegance on the stage. She wore a slinky silver gown at the party. The cat made a slinky movement across the floor. The children played with a slinky on the stairs.

english_meaning: A long, narrow cut or opening. To make a long, narrow cut in something. To cut into or through something with a sharp instrument. A thin opening for receiving something, like a coin in a machine.
