example_sentence: A snake slithered across the dusty path. The children slithered down the muddy slope. He slithered out of the room without being noticed. With a quick slither, the lizard disappeared under the rock.

english_meaning: A catchy phrase used to promote a product or brand. A phrase used to express a political message or campaign idea. A chant or phrase used to unite people for a cause. Any short phrase that represents an idea or principle
example_sentence: The crowd began chanting anti govt slogans. The company created a powerful slogan to attract customers. The protesters shouted their slogan loudly in the streets. A good slogan helps people remember a brand easily. The campaign slogan inspired many young voters.

english_meaning: A surface of which one end or side is at a higher level than another; a rising or falling ground. To be inclined from a horizontal or vertical line.
example_sentence: The skiers raced down the steep mountain slope at high speeds. The garden has a gentle slope leading down to the river bank. The roof began to slope downwards to allow rain to run off. Be careful when walking on the icy slope behind the house.

english_meaning: Reluctance to work or make an effort; laziness. One of the seven deadly sins in Christian tradition. A slow-moving mammal of South and Central America that hangs upside down from tree branches.
example_sentence: His sloth was legendary in the office, where he was known for never completing a task without being chased repeatedly. The three-toed sloth spends most of its life hanging motionless from the branches of rainforest trees. Sloth is listed as one of the seven deadly sins in medieval Christian theology. Her sloth in responding to emails caused significant delays in the project. The sloth moved at such a slow pace that algae had begun to grow on its fur.

english_meaning: Lazy, inactive, unwilling to work or make effort. A person who avoids work, effort, or activity. It refers to laziness, idleness, or lack of motivation. A slothful person usually delays tasks and prefers rest over responsibility.
example_sentence: The slothful student failed to complete his homework on time. A slothful worker cannot achieve success easily. He became slothful during the long vacation and avoided all exercise. The manager warned the slothful employees to improve their performance.

english_meaning: To stand, move, or sit in a lazy and drooping way. A lazy, incompetent, or clumsy person. The action or posture of slumping over carelessly. To bend one's head or shoulders forward ungracefully.
example_sentence: He tends to slouch in his chair when he is tired. My mother always told me not to slouch while eating at the dining table. He is no slouch when it comes to playing the guitar. The teenager walked into the room with a lazy slouch.

english_meaning: To shed or cast off dead skin, old leaves, or unwanted material. A layer of dead skin or tissue that has been shed. A swamp, marsh, or muddy backwater (mainly North American).
example_sentence: The snake sloughed its old skin after several weeks. She decided to slough old habits and start a healthier lifestyle. The nurse cleaned the slough from the patient's wound. Ducks gathered around the quiet slough at sunset.

english_meaning: Loose snow, rock, or earth that slides down a slope. Dead skin or unwanted material that falls off. To shed, peel off, or slide away. To neglect, avoid, or skip duties (informal).
example_sentence: A large sluff of snow came down after the storm. The old skin began to sluff off as the wound healed. Loose rocks sluffed down the hillside during the rain. He tried to sluff his responsibilities and let others finish the project.

english_meaning: To avoid responsibilities. To skip school or work without a good reason. To neglect assigned duties. To waste time instead of working. To evade obligations. To shirk one's responsibilities. To procrastinate on important tasks. To dodge work intentionally.
synonyms: ["Shirk","Avoid","Neglect","Skip","Dodge","Evade","Bypass","Ignore","Procrastinate","Play truant","Slack off","Duck out of","Weasel out of","Skive off (British)"]
example_sentence: He tried to sluff off his homework by pretending to be sick. Some students sluff off classes before the holidays. You should not sluff off your responsibilities if you want to succeed. She was warned not to sluff off work during office hours.

english_meaning: A soft-bodied land animal that resembles a snail but has no shell. A strong blow delivered with the fist. To strike someone forcefully with the fist or another object. A solid metal bullet fired from a firearm. To proceed at a slow pace or work without much energy.
example_sentence: A slug crawled across the garden after the rain. The boxer slugged his opponent with a powerful punch. The hunter loaded a slug into the shotgun. We slugged through the difficult project until it was finished.

english_meaning: A lazy person who stays in bed too long. A person who avoids getting up early and prefers sleeping or lying in bed instead of working or being active. It often carries a mildly negative tone, suggesting laziness or lack of discipline.
example_sentence: He was called a slugabed because he never woke up before noon. The teacher warned the slugabed to change his habits. Stop being a slugabed and get ready for work. His success came only after he stopped living like a slugabed.

english_meaning: A lazy person who avoids work or effort and prefers idleness. A person who is habitually lazy, inactive, or unwilling to work. The word describes someone who wastes time, avoids responsibility, and lacks motivation to complete tasks. It often carries a negative meaning and is commonly used in literature, moral teachings, and everyday conversations.
example_sentence: The sluggard missed many opportunities because he refused to work hard. No employer wants to hire a sluggard who avoids responsibility. Instead of behaving like a sluggard, she decided to become disciplined and productive. The teacher encouraged every student not to become a sluggard but to value hard work.

english_meaning: Aperson who hits very hard, especially in baseball, boxing, or fighting. It can also refer to someone who works or competes with great strength and determination.
example_sentence: The slugger smashed the ball over the fence. Everyone admired the slugger for his incredible strength. Our team's slugger changed the game with one powerful hit. She worked like a slugger to finish the project on time.

english_meaning: Moving, reacting or working more slowly than normal. Moving or operating more slowly than usual and with less energy or power. Moving or operating more slowly than usual.
example_sentence:
He felt very heavy and sluggish after the meal. The growth of the export market has helped to compensate for sluggish demand at home.
Sales were sluggish. Something is wrong with the car - the engine feels sluggish.
The housing market has been very sluggish these past few years.

english_meaning: The state of moving or working slowly and without energy. Lack of activity, alertness or responsiveness. Slowness of growth or progress, especially in business or the economy.
example_sentence: He complained of tiredness and general sluggishness. The sluggishness of the economy worried the government. Cold weather causes sluggishness in many reptiles. There was a noticeable sluggishness in the computer's response.

english_meaning: To sleep, especially in a light or peaceful way. It refers to a state of rest or inactivity resembling sleep. This term is often used poetically to describe a deep or quiet period of repose.
example_sentence: The child fell into a deep slumber after a long day of playing. The forest seemed to slumber under the blanket of freshly fallen snow. Nothing could disturb her peaceful slumber during the quiet night. Some animals slumber through the entire winter season in burrows.

english_meaning: A sudden or severe fall in prices, values, or sales. It also means to sit, lean, or fall heavily and limply, often due to exhaustion or despair. It denotes a rapid deterioration in economic conditions or personal posture.
example_sentence: The company experienced a severe financial slump during the last business quarter. He dragged himself to the couch and allowed his tired body to slump heavily. The sudden slump in housing prices worried many independent real estate investors. Players often experience a massive slump in performance during a long, grueling season. She tends to slump her shoulders forward whenever she feels sad or defeated.

english_meaning: To speak unclearly, often because of tiredness, illness, or intoxication. To make a false or insulting statement about someone. An insulting or disrespectful remark; a false accusation meant to damage reputation.
example_sentence: He began to slur his words after drinking too much. She slurred her colleague in the meeting. The drunk man slurred while trying to explain himself. Using racial slurs is unacceptable in any society. The article was written to slur the reputation of the leader. Alcohol can cause a person to slur their words.

english_meaning: To insult or speak offensively about someone or a group. To make a disrespectful or harmful remark that damages the reputation, dignity, or identity of a person, community, or group, often based on race, religion, gender, or background
example_sentence: He slurred against his colleague in the meeting. Politicians should not slur against each other. The article slurs against the company unfairly. She slurred against him during the argument.

english_meaning: To avoid details. To treat a subject quickly or carelessly so that important facts, mistakes, or truths are hidden or not properly explained
example_sentence: The report slurred over the main causes of the accident. He slurred over his mistakes during the meeting. The speaker slurred over sensitive issues to avoid criticism. The article slurred over key facts that readers needed to know.

english_meaning: To avoid details. To treat a subject quickly or carelessly so that important facts, mistakes, or truths are hidden or not properly explained
example_sentence: He slurred through the report without explaining the key points. The student slurred through his presentation because he was nervous. She slurred through the instructions, which confused everyone. Do not slur through important documents if accuracy matters.

english_meaning: To eat or drink something noisily and quickly, usually liquid or semi liquid food. It can also imply careless or rude manner while drinking or eating.
example_sentence: He slurped up the soup without waiting for it to cool. The child slurped up the milk happily. She slurped up the noodles in a rush. After the match, he slurped up water from the bottle.

english_meaning: To eat or drink something with a loud sucking noise. It typically happens when someone inhales air along with liquid from a spoon or glass. The term can also refer to the sound made while consuming food in this manner.
example_sentence: He began to slurp his soup loudly, much to the annoyance of his dinner guests. The children love to slurp their milkshakes through colorful straws. Try not to slurp your tea while we are at the formal meeting. He took a long slurp of the cold water after running the race.

english_meaning: Partially melted snow or ice, especially on the ground. Watery mud or wet soft mass. A sweet drink made from crushed ice and flavored syrup. Overly sentimental language or writing. Wet, soft material that is unpleasant to walk in.
example_sentence: The streets were covered with dirty slush after the snow melted. He slipped on the slush near the door. She ordered a strawberry slush at the café. The novel was dismissed as sentimental slush.

english_meaning: To hit somebody with your open hand or an object, especially as a punishment. To put something somewhere with a lot of force so that it makes a loud noise. To hit against something with a lot of force. To move your lips, apart noisily, especially before eating something good. A sharp hit given with your open hand, especially to a child as a punishment. A hard hit given with a closed hand. A short loud sound. A loud kiss. The drug heroin. A small fishing boat. Exactly or directly in a place. With sudden, violent force, often making a loud noise.
example_sentence: I think it's wrong to smack children. Do that again and you’ll get your bottom smacked. She smacked her hand down on the table. He smacked a fist into the palm of his hand. Two players accidentally smacked into each other. He turned around and smacked into a wall. They were smacking their lips at the thought of clinching the deal. You'll get a smack on your backside if you're not careful. He longed to land her a good smack in the face. A smack on the jaw. She brought her hand down on the water with a smack. A smack on the lips cheek. Smack addicts. It landed smack in the middle of the carpet. She kissed me smack on the lips. The car drove smack into a brick wall. He hit me smack in the mouth.

english_meaning: To seem to have a taste, trace, or suggestion of something (usually disapproval). To show signs or characteristics of something (often negative, like dishonesty, arrogance, unfairness).
example_sentence: Her behaviour smacks of hypocrisy. Today's announcement smacks of a government cover-up. The whole situation smacks of mismanagement and incompetence. Their behavior smacks of very bad judgment. That joke smacks of bad taste. His speech smacks of arrogance.

english_meaning: To hit or crash badly, causing damage. To beat up / strike. To mess something up very badly. Under influence of drugs.
example_sentence: He smacked up his car in the accident last night. The gang smacked him up for lying to them. She really smacked up the presentation by forgetting her slides. He looked all smacked up after the party.

english_meaning: A decisive defeat or a crushing blow. A physical confrontation or a wrestling match. A public or highly publicized thrashing or humiliation. A total defeat of an opponent in an argument or competition. A wrestling event where a winner is determined by pinning the opponent.
example_sentence: The debate turned into a total smackdown for the incumbent candidate. The final match was a brutal smackdown between two giants. The company faced a legal smackdown in the supreme court. Fans were excited to see the heavyweights in a wrestling smackdown. She delivered a verbal smackdown to the person who insulted her.

english_meaning: The long narrow part of the digestive tract where most digestion and absorption take place. The tube between the stomach and the large intestine. The organ made up of the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
example_sentence: Most nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine. The small intestine is several metres long. Food from the stomach passes into the small intestine. Damage to the small intestine can cause poor nutrition.

english_meaning: A truly intelligent or capable person does not need to boast, their work speaks for itself. But those with “small wits” (little intelligence) often exaggerate their talents to impress others.
synonyms: ["Empty vessels make the most noise","All talk and no action","Empty bragging","Self-praise is no recommendation"]
antonyms: ["Actions speak louder than words","True wisdom is humble","Silent strength","Humble confidence"]
example_sentence: He always exaggerates; small wits great boast. He always talks about how clever he is, but his actions show otherwise, small wits, great boast. People who keep bragging about their knowledge usually know the least, small wits, great boast. She keeps boasting about her cooking, but no one likes her food, small wits, great boast. A wise man stays humble; a fool talks loudly, small wits, great boast.

english_meaning: To behave in an ingratiating, oily, or unctuously flattering way. Excessive or insincere politeness used to gain favor. An unpleasantly suave or oily manner.
example_sentence: The salesman’s oily smarm made the customers feel very uncomfortable. He tried to smarm his way into the executive's good graces. There was a certain level of smarm in his overly enthusiastic greeting. She couldn't stand the way he used smarm to get what he wanted. His speech was filled with insincere smarm that failed to impress the crowd.

english_meaning: Too polite in a way that is not sincere. Extremely polite or helpful or showing a lot of respect in a way that is annoying or does not seem sincere. Unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech.
example_sentence: She was trying to be friendly, but she just seemed smarmy and insincere. To be honest I found the hotel staff rather smarmy. He's very smarmy, and usually refers to his students as children. The character is self-centered, smarmy, quick tempered, and overbearingly insincere.

english_meaning: A person who behaves as if they know everything. Someone who makes sarcastic or mocking remarks to show off their cleverness. An individual who is irritatingly cocky and overconfident. A smugly conceited and obnoxious person.

Don't be a smart alec when the police officer asks you a serious question. He lost his job because he acted like a smart alec during the client meeting.

english_meaning: A highly intelligent and clever person. Someone who is astute and capable of making good decisions quickly. A sharp-minded individual who is not easily fooled. A bright person who can solve complex problems with ease.

My daughter is a smart cookie and always gets top grades in her class. He proved to be a smart cookie by investing his money at exactly the right time.

english_meaning: To break, crush, or destroy something with great force. Hitting something very hard, such as in sports. A powerful hit, a serious collision, or a big success such as a popular movie or song.

english_meaning: To break, destroy, or demolish something with great force. To bring something down violently.
example_sentence: The police smashed down the door to rescue the hostages. The workers used hammers to smash down the old wall. He got so angry that he smashed down his phone on the floor.

example_sentence: Vandals had smashed the door in. Vandals had smashed the door in. The police smashed in the door during the raid. The strong wind smashed in the windows of the old house. He smashed in the wall with a hammer to get to the pipes. The thieves smashed in the car window to steal the bag.

english_meaning: To destroy badly by breaking into pieces. To cause a serious accident or damage. To attack violently. To suffer a breakdown (physical or emotional, less common).

He hasn't driven since his smash-up two years ago. She took revenge on her ex-boyfriend by smashing up his home

They smelled a rat after noticing the missing files from the office. I smell a rat in his story; it doesn’t sound true.

english_meaning: To discover something by smelling it, as a dog finds prey. To detect or find out something hidden, especially wrongdoing. To make a place smell unpleasant. To sense instinctively that something is wrong.

english_meaning: A tiny amount. A little bit. A minuscule quantity of something, often used informally to indicate a little more than nothing. It can describe tiny amounts of food, time, or any measurable thing.
example_sentence: Add a smidge of salt. He’s a smidge late. I want a smidge of chocolate. She moved a smidge closer. He moved the chair a smidge to the left. Can you give me a smidge of your advice?

english_meaning: A brief statement or account of the main points of a text or event. A comprehensive and usually concise abstract of previously stated facts. Done or executed quickly without the customary details or formalities. Dispensing with needless delay or legal procedures in making a decision. Acting or done without prior notice or lengthy discussion.
example_sentence: Please provide a summary of the report by tomorrow morning. The teacher asked the students to write a brief summary of the novel. The judge made a summary decision based on the overwhelmingly clear evidence. We only have time for a summary account of the meeting's proceedings.

word: Smoke oneself into an early grave
english_meaning: To damage one's health by smoking so heavily that it causes death before the normal lifespan. To shorten one's life through continuous heavy smoking. To ruin one's health steadily by refusing to stop smoking.
synonyms: ["Kill oneself slowly","Ruin one's health","Shorten one's life","Court death","Self-destruct"]
example_sentence: If he keeps this up, he will smoke himself into an early grave. The doctor warned him that he was smoking himself into an early grave. Her father smoked himself into an early grave at just fifty. Many young people are smoking themselves into an early grave without realising it.

english_meaning: Filled with or producing a lot of smoke. Having the taste, smell, or appearance of smoke. Dark, hazy, or greyish in colour. Of a voice, low, husky, and attractive.

english_meaning: To burn slowly without a flame. To be filled with a strong emotion that you do not fully express. A fire that burns with thick smoke but no flame. To show suppressed anger, hate, or jealousy.

english_meaning: A person who is very polite, flattering, and charming, sometimes in a way that seems dishonest or manipulative. A thick beverage prepared by blending fresh or frozen fruits with milk, yogurt, juice, or ice. It is usually creamy in texture and served cold. example_sentence: She made a mango smoothie for breakfast. I prefer a banana and strawberry smoothie after exercise. The café serves healthy green smoothies. He is such a smoothie that everyone believes his sweet words.

english_meaning: To burn slowly without a flame. To be filled with a strong emotion that you do not fully express. A fire that burns with thick smoke but no flame. To show suppressed anger, hate, or jealousy.
example_sentence: Melanie Griffith seems to smoulder with sexuality. The smoulder suddenly became a blaze. The fire was started by a smouldering cigarette. She was smouldering with rage as she explained how her son had been killed. He gazed at her with smouldering eyes, wishing she wasn't married. The dispute is still smouldering, five years after the negotiations began.

english_meaning: A blurred or smeared mark on the surface of something. To cause a mark or blur by rubbing against something. To become smeared or blurred. A traditional method of using smoke to purify or protect a space.
example_sentence: The child left a greasy smudge on the clean window pane. Be careful not to smudge the ink before it is completely dry. Her mascara began to smudge after she walked through the rain. He used a piece of charcoal to smudge the edges of the drawing for effect. The smoke from the smudge stick filled the room with a woody scent.

english_meaning: Covered with or full of smudges or smears. Tending to cause or result in smudges. Lacking sharp outlines or clarity.

Without my glasses, everything in the distance looks dark and smudgy. The artist preferred a smudgy charcoal style for his portraits. Her makeup looked smudgy after a long day at the office.

english_meaning: Showing excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements. Having or showing an excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements. Contented to a fault or characterized by self-satisfaction. Clean, tidy, and well-dressed.
example_sentence: He had a smug expression on his face after winning the debate. She felt quite smug about finishing the project ahead of schedule. Don't be so smug just because you got a higher grade this time. The cat looked very smug as it sat by the empty milk bowl. He walked into the room with a smug look that irritated everyone.

english_meaning: A small amount of food eaten between meals. To eat a snack or a light meal. An easy task or something easily accomplished. To consume food in a casual or hurried manner.

In British informal usage, to grab or get hold of something desirable for oneself with little effort or hesitation.

He managed to snaffle the last two tickets to the concert before they sold out. She always snaffles the best seat in the room whenever she arrives early. The children snaffled all the biscuits before the guests had a chance to taste them.

english_meaning: A small soft-bodied creature that carries a spiral shell on its back and moves very slowly. A slow-moving mollusc found in gardens and damp places. A person or thing that is extremely slow.

english_meaning: A person who pretends to be your friend but secretly tries to harm or betray you. A deceitful or treacherous person.

english_meaning: To make a sharp sound by pressing the thumb and middle finger together and releasing them quickly. To signal, call, or command someone with this gesture. To indicate that something can be done very easily or quickly. A gesture used to show impatience or to attract attention.

english_meaning: To suddenly stop being upset, distracted, emotional, or stuck in a negative mental state and return to normal thinking or behavior.  It is used when someone is overly emotional, worried, daydreaming, or acting unproductively, and the speaker wants them to quickly regain control of their thoughts or mood. It often carries a sense of urgency or mild frustration.
synonyms: ["Pull yourself together","Get a grip","Come to your senses","Wake up","Shake it off","Get over it"]
example_sentence: Snap out of it and finish your work before the deadline. She was so worried that her friend told her to snap out of it. He kept daydreaming in class, so the teacher told him to snap out of it. You need to snap out of it and focus on what really matters.

english_meaning: Quick and irritable in manner or speech. Moving or able to move with great speed. Neat and stylish in appearance. Energetic or vigorous. Weather that is cold and brisk.
example_sentence: The manager was in a snappy mood and kept cutting people off. You need to make a snappy decision if you want to catch the bus. He looked very snappy in his new tailored suit. The dancers moved to a snappy, upbeat rhythm. It's a bit snappy outside, so you might want to wear a coat.

english_meaning: A trap for catching birds or animals, typically one having a noose of wire or cord. To catch in or as if in a snare. Something that traps or deceives someone. A wire or cord stretched across the bottom of a drum to produce a rattling sound.
example_sentence: The rabbit was caught in a wire snare set by the hunter. Be careful not to fall into the snare of easy credit. The spider's web is a deadly snare for unsuspecting insects. The drummer tightened the snare to get a sharper sound. They tried to snare him into admitting his guilt during the interview.

english_meaning: To seize something quickly and often roughly. To take or grab something suddenly without permission. To rescue or remove someone quickly from danger. A short period or small amount of something. A brief piece or fragment, especially of music, song, or conversation.
example_sentence: The thief tried to snatch her handbag in the crowded market. He managed to snatch a few hours of sleep before the meeting. She snatched the burning pan off the stove just in time. I caught only a snatch of their conversation as I walked past. The rescuers snatched the child from the path of the oncoming car.

english_meaning: Stylish, smart, and attractive in an eye-catching way. Fashionable and impressively modern. Flashy and appealing in appearance. (Informal) Very smartly dressed or designed.
example_sentence: He turned up at the party in a snazzy blue suit. They have designed a snazzy new website for the shop. She bought a snazzy pair of sunglasses for the trip. The café has a snazzy interior full of bright colours.

english_meaning: To move quietly or secretly, usually to avoid being noticed. A person who moves stealthily or acts secretly to get an advantage, sometimes in a negative sense. Acting in a secretive or sly manner.
example_sentence: He tried to sneak out of the house without waking anyone. She sneaked a glance at the surprise gift. The teacher caught the sneak who copied homework. He sneaked a candy into his bag.

english_meaning: To move secretly in different places. To go from place to place quietly, often to avoid being seen
example_sentence: He was sneaking around the house last night. The kids sneaked around the garden. Reporters were sneaking around the celebrity’s house. The spy sneaked around the enemy camp.

english_meaning: To leave quietly. To leave a place secretly and quietly so that others do not notice
example_sentence: He tried to sneak away from the party early. The thief sneaked away before anyone saw him. She sneaked away while everyone was busy talking. The cat sneaked away from the dog.

english_meaning: To pass quietly or unnoticed. To go past someone or something without being detected
example_sentence: He sneaked by the guards at night. She sneaked by without anyone seeing her. The thief sneaked by the cameras. We tried to sneak by the teacher unnoticed.

english_meaning: To enter secretly. To go into a place quietly without being seen or noticed
example_sentence: The boy sneaked in through the window. She sneaked in without paying for a ticket. He sneaked in late to the meeting. They sneaked in after the movie started.

english_meaning: To enter quietly or without permission. To go into a place secretly or without authorization
example_sentence: He sneaked into the stadium without a ticket. The cat sneaked into the kitchen. The children sneaked into the teacher’s room. A reporter sneaked into the private event.

english_meaning: To go away secretly. To leave a place or group without telling anyone or without permission
example_sentence: They sneaked off during the movie. He sneaked off from work early today. The children sneaked off to play outside. She sneaked off without saying goodbye.

english_meaning: To secretly report someone’s wrongdoing. To tell authorities or someone in charge about another’s bad behavior secretly
example_sentence: He sneaked on his classmates to the teacher. No one likes someone who sneaks on others. She sneaked on her brother for breaking the vase. The spy sneaked on the enemy to his boss.

english_meaning: To go out secretly. To leave a building or area quietly so no one notices
example_sentence: He sneaked out of the house at midnight. The students sneaked out of class early. She sneaked out to meet her friends. The spy sneaked out through the back door.

english_meaning: To approach secretly. To move quietly toward someone or something without being noticed
example_sentence: The cat sneaked up on the bird. He sneaked up behind his friend to surprise him. The soldier sneaked up on the enemy. She sneaked up to listen to their talk.

english_meaning: To move secretly and surprise someone. To approach someone or something quietly and secretly, usually so they do not notice you.
example_sentence: The cat tried to sneak up on the bird. He sneaked up on his friend to give him a surprise. Old age can sneak up on you before you realize it. The police sneaked up on the thieves at night.

english_meaning: Marked by stealth, deceit, or dishonesty. Acting in a secret, sly, or underhanded manner to avoid detection.
example_sentence: It was a sneaky move to change the agreement without telling anyone. She took a sneaky glance at her phone during the meeting. The cat made a sneaky approach towards the unsuspecting bird. He has a sneaky habit of leaving the room when it is time to pay the bill.

english_meaning: To smile, speak, or look in a way that shows dislike, contempt, or superiority. A facial expression or remark showing scorn or mockery.
example_sentence: He sneered at my idea, saying it would never work. Don’t sneer at people who are trying their best. She gave a sneer of contempt before leaving the room. The critics sneered at the new artist’s work. The bully’s sneer frightened the younger children. He gave a sneer of contempt and walked away.

english_meaning: To force air suddenly out of the nose and mouth because of irritation in the nose. The act or sound of forcing air out of the nose and mouth suddenly.
example_sentence: She began to sneeze because of the strong perfume. He tried not to sneeze during the meeting. His loud sneeze surprised everyone in the room. One sudden sneeze spread dust from the table. She had to sneeze because of the dust in the room.

english_meaning: To laugh in a quiet, partly hidden, or disrespectful way. To give a smothered or sly laugh, often at someone else's misfortune, mistake, or embarrassment. To laugh secretly or rudely. It usually carries a sense of mockery or amusement at another's expense.
example_sentence: The students snickered when the teacher mispronounced the name. He snickered behind his hand at her old-fashioned dress. They snickered at his clumsy attempt to dance. Stop snickering and pay attention to the lecture. The boys snickered as the principal slipped on the wet floor.

english_meaning: To inhale through the nose, usually to smell something. To draw air audibly through the nose to detect a scent, express emotion (like sadness), or clear nasal passages. Can also mean showing disapproval or suspicion. A quick inhalation through the nose.
example_sentence: The dog sniffed the ground to find its owner. She sniffed the flowers in the garden. He sniffed in disapproval at the idea. I could hear him sniff when he was upset. She took a sniff of the fresh coffee. There was a faint sniff of perfume in the air.

english_meaning: To cut something quickly with scissors, typically in small strokes. A small cut made with scissors. A small piece cut off from something. In informal British use, a bargain or something very cheap. In informal use, a vasectomy.
example_sentence: She used the scissors to snip the coupon out of the newspaper. With one snip, he cut the ribbon to open the new store. He gave a snip of fabric to the shop to match the color for the curtains. At that price, the used car was a real snip.

english_meaning: To make small quick cutting motions toward something with scissors or shears. To criticize someone in a sharp, petty, or nagging way; to make cutting remarks.
example_sentence: The tailor snipped at the loose threads on the hem. She kept snipping at him about his messy desk. The hairdresser snipped at the stray strands to even out the fringe. He always snips at his colleagues' ideas during meetings.

english_meaning: To gradually cut something using small repeated cuts with scissors, often removing excess material bit by bit. To reduce or trim something steadily over time.
example_sentence: The barber snipped away at his overgrown hair. She snipped away the excess fabric to create a neat hem. He carefully snipped away the dead branches from the rose bush. The editor snipped away unnecessary parts of the manuscript.

english_meaning: To remove or sever a small part of something using scissors or a similar cutting tool with a quick, small cut. To detach a piece neatly from a larger whole.
example_sentence: She snipped off a loose thread from her sweater. The gardener snipped off the dead flowers from the plant. He snipped off a small piece of the ribbon for the craft project. The nurse snipped off the excess bandage before securing it.

english_meaning: To remove a piece of something by cutting it out with scissors or a similar tool. To excise a section neatly from a larger sheet or material.
example_sentence: She snipped out the article she wanted to save from the magazine. He snipped out a coupon from the newspaper. The tailor snipped out the pattern pieces before sewing them together. They snipped out the damaged section of the photograph.

english_meaning: To cut completely through something using scissors or a similar sharp tool. To pass a blade right across a material so it separates.
example_sentence: He snipped through the thick rope with a pair of heavy-duty scissors. The surgeon carefully snipped through the tissue during the procedure. She snipped through the tape to open the package quickly. The firefighters snipped through the seatbelt to free the trapped passenger.

english_meaning: A long-billed wading bird found in marshes, known for its erratic flight. To shoot at someone from a hidden position, typically with a rifle. To make a critical or cutting remark, often in a sly or indirect way. In online auctions, to place a bid at the last moment.
example_sentence: Birdwatchers spotted a snipe hiding among the reeds. The sharpshooter was trained to snipe targets from great distances. She could not resist sniping about her rival's poor performance. He waited until the last second to snipe the item at the online auction.

english_meaning: A person who shoots at people from a concealed position. One who operates from a hidden place to pick off individual targets. To shoot at someone from a hiding place. A person who criticizes or attacks others from a position of safety.
example_sentence: The military deployed a sniper to watch the perimeter of the camp. Police snipers were positioned on the rooftops during the standoff. He was injured by a lone sniper hiding in the derelict building. The politician faced constant attacks from anonymous snipers on social media. The sniper waited patiently for hours until the target appeared.

english_meaning: The act of shooting at people from a hidden position, typically with a long-range rifle. The practice of making sudden critical or harsh remarks. In online auctions, the practice of placing a winning bid at the last possible moment to prevent others from responding.
example_sentence: The soldiers took cover to avoid enemy sniping from the rooftops. His constant sniping at coworkers created a tense office atmosphere. Sniping in online auctions can frustrate bidders who lose out at the last second. The documentary examined the psychological toll of sniping on military marksmen.

english_meaning: A small piece or short extract of text, speech, music, video, or code. A brief piece of information or news. A reusable fragment of computer code. A very small part cut or taken from something.
example_sentence: She read a short snippet from the interview. The trailer includes snippets of the film's best scenes. I saved the code snippet for later use. He shared a snippet of news during lunch.

english_meaning: Curt, short-tempered, or irritable in manner or speech. Inclined to make sharp or rude remarks. Impatient and abrupt in tone.
example_sentence: The waiter got snippy when we asked for a refund. She was snippy with her coworkers after a stressful meeting. His snippy responses made everyone uncomfortable during the discussion. Try not to be snippy with the customers, even if they are difficult.

english_meaning: A fit of irritation, bad temper, or petulance, usually over something minor. A short-lived sulky mood.
example_sentence: He threw a snit when his order arrived late. She is in one of her snits again today. It was just a small snit, nothing to worry about. The children's snit over the toy ended in tears.

english_meaning: To inform on someone. To secretly report someone’s wrongdoing or misbehavior to authorities or another party. To tell a parent, teacher, etc about something wrong that another child has done. A person, especially a child, who tells a parent, teacher, etc about something wrong that another child has done. A person who informs on others.
example_sentence: He snitched on his friend for stealing. Don’t snitch on me to the teacher. She snitched about the office theft. He is a snitch who told the teacher about our prank. Snitches often lose their friends. The police caught the snitch in the gang.

english_meaning: A person who informs on others, especially to authorities. Someone who tells on others, usually revealing secrets or reporting misdeeds to get them in trouble or gain favor with authority. Often has a negative connotation.
example_sentence: The snitcher told the teacher about the cheating. No one trusted him because he was a known snitcher. The gang punished the snitcher for revealing their plans. She didn’t want to be a snitcher, so she stayed silent.

english_meaning: To weep or cry with snuffling and frequent sniffing. To complain or whine in a tearful, self-pitying, or annoying manner. To have a runny nose or show signs of a cold through sniffing.
example_sentence: The child began to snivel when his toy was taken away. Stop your snivelling and tell me what is actually wrong. He spent the whole afternoon snivelling about how unfair the world is. The sick boy sat on the sofa snivelling and sneezing. Don't come snivelling to me when you lose your money.

english_meaning: Crying or sniffling in a weak, whiny, or feeble way, often to gain sympathy. Cowardly, weak, or contemptibly tearful in manner. Behaving in a whining, servile fashion.
example_sentence: The snivelling child refused to stop crying over a broken toy. He gave a snivelling excuse for missing the deadline. Stop your snivelling and face the problem like an adult. The snivelling coward begged for mercy before running away.

english_meaning: A person who has an exaggerated respect for social position, wealth, or status and looks down on those considered inferior. A person who believes their taste in a particular area, such as food, music, or art, is superior to that of others.
example_sentence: He is such a snob that he refuses to shop anywhere but designer boutiques. She was labelled a snob for mocking her classmates' accents. A wine snob, he criticized every bottle that was not imported. The old aristocrat was a notorious snob who never mixed with commoners.

english_meaning: Behaviour or attitudes that reflect an exaggerated sense of superiority based on social class, wealth, taste, or status. The practice of looking down on others considered inferior.
example_sentence: The novel satirizes the snobbery of upper-class society. His snobbery about fine wine annoyed everyone at the dinner. There is a lot of snobbery surrounding which university you attended. Cultural snobbery often prevents people from appreciating popular art.

english_meaning: Showing pride and dislike for people considered inferior. A person who believes they are socially or intellectually superior and treats others with arrogance, often judging people by wealth, class, education, or status.
example_sentence: His snobbish attitude made others uncomfortable at the meeting. She sounded snobbish when she talked about people from small towns. The waiter was polite but not snobbish. Snobbish behavior often hides insecurity.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being snobbish. A tendency to judge or exclude others based on perceived social, cultural, or intellectual inferiority.
example_sentence: His snobbishness made him unpopular among his coworkers. The clique was known for its snobbishness toward new students. Her snobbishness about fashion labels was obvious at every party. Despite his wealth, he tried to hide his snobbishness in public.

english_meaning: Acting as if one is better than others, especially because of wealth, education, or social class.
example_sentence: She's too snobby to talk to people from small towns. Don't be so snobby just because you have a new car. She refused to talk to them because she thought they were not rich enough; that was very snobby of her. He became snobby after getting a promotion at work. Some people find her snobby attitude difficult to tolerate.

english_meaning: A long, slender predatory sea fish (Thyrsites atun) found in southern oceans, popular in South African cuisine, often smoked, grilled, or salted. The barracouta of southern waters.
example_sentence: We grilled fresh snoek on the beach during the braai. Snoek is a staple fish in Cape Town's fishing communities. He bought a smoked snoek from the market for dinner. Snoek pate is a popular South African appetizer.

english_meaning: In British informal use, to kiss and cuddle amorously. A session of amorous kissing and cuddling.
example_sentence: They were snogging on the park bench. She had a quick snog with her boyfriend before class. The teenagers were caught snogging behind the school. He leaned in for a snog at the end of the date.

english_meaning: A clever, dishonest, or unprincipled person, especially a politician who seeks personal gain rather than serving others. An old American slang term used to describe someone who has no moral principles and uses cleverness, manipulation, or deception to achieve personal success or power. The word is most often applied to politicians or public figures who care more about their own interests than honesty or public service. It is usually used in a humorous or critical way.
antonyms: ["Honest person","Principled person","Integrity driven leader","Truthful individual","Ethical politician","Upright citizen","Sincere person","Trustworthy individual","Honorable leader","Conscientious person"]
example_sentence: Many voters believed the candidate was nothing more than a snollygoster seeking power. The newspaper accused the corrupt official of being a snollygoster who ignored public welfare. Despite his charming speeches, critics described him as a snollygoster with no real values. History has recorded several snollygosters who manipulated people for personal gain.

english_meaning: A small ornamental fabric or net bag worn to hold a woman's hair in place, usually at the back of the head. A tubular scarf or headband worn around the neck or head. A fold of loose skin hanging over the beak of a turkey. Historically, a hair ribbon worn by unmarried women in Scotland.
example_sentence: She wore a black snood to keep her hair neat during the ballet class. The turkey's snood turned bright red when it was excited. Victorian women often wore decorative snoods at social gatherings. The chef wore a snood while working in the kitchen.

english_meaning: A gesture of contempt made by placing the thumb on the nose and spreading the fingers, as in the phrase 'cock a snook'. An act of open mockery or defiance. A large edible game fish found in warm coastal waters, especially off Florida and the Caribbean.
example_sentence: He cocked a snook at his rivals by winning the race effortlessly. The comedian cocked a snook at the government's new policy. Anglers love catching snook along the Florida coast. The snook put up a tough fight before he reeled it in.

english_meaning: A cue sport played on a large baize-covered table with twenty-two balls, in which players pot balls in a set order to score points. To leave an opponent's cue ball in a position where a direct shot is blocked. To place someone in a difficult or impossible situation; to thwart or trick.
example_sentence: He plays snooker every weekend at the local club. The champion snookered his opponent with a brilliant safety shot. The sudden change in the contract terms left the company completely snookered. She felt snookered by a deal she could not refuse or accept.

english_meaning: To secretly investigate or look around a place in order to find out private information about someone. To pry into the personal affairs or business of others. As a noun, it refers to a person who secretly investigates, pries, or overly involves themselves in other people's business.
example_sentence: She caught him snooping around her private office. Reporters are always snooping into the personal lives of famous politicians. I do not mean to snoop, but I could not help noticing the letter on your desk. He installed security cameras to stop his curious neighbors from snooping. My little brother is a terrible snoop who tries to read my diary.

english_meaning: To sleep lightly for a short period, especially during the day. It is often used to describe a brief nap or the act of delaying waking up by using a timer. This term carries a connotation of a casual or unplanned rest.
example_sentence: I usually like to snooze for ten more minutes after my alarm goes off. He took a quick snooze on the sofa before starting his evening shift. The cat found a sunny spot on the rug to snooze in peace. Don't snooze during the lecture or you will miss important information.

english_meaning: To breathe noisily during sleep due to vibration of the soft palate, usually when air cannot move freely through the nose and throat. A sound made when someone breathes noisily while sleeping.
example_sentence: He started to snore loudly after falling asleep on the sofa. Some people snore when they are extremely tired. Her husband’s snoring kept her awake all night. You may snore if you sleep on your back.

english_meaning: To force air violently and noisily through the nostrils. To express contempt, indignation, or impatience by making a sudden explosive sound with the nose. To inhale a substance, typically a drug, through the nose. To make a sound like a grunt.
example_sentence: The horse gave a loud snort as it galloped across the field. She let out a snort of derision at his ridiculous suggestion. He was caught trying to snort an illegal substance. The engine started with a sudden snort and a puff of smoke. They couldn't help but snort with laughter during the serious speech.

english_meaning: Rude, arrogant, or disrespectful. A person who behaves in a proud, insulting, or superior way toward others. It often refers to someone who looks down on people and speaks or acts with disrespect.
example_sentence: He gave a snotty reply when asked a simple question. The snotty attitude of the waiter annoyed the customers. She sounded snotty during the meeting and offended her colleagues. No one likes working with a snotty person who looks down on others.

english_meaning: The sport or activity of skiing on very short, wide skis that do not require poles. Also known as skiboarding, it combines elements of skiing and inline skating. It is typically practiced on groomed slopes for tricks or easy maneuvering.
example_sentence: Snowblading is a fun alternative for those who find traditional skis too long. He spent the weekend snowblading on the beginners' slopes. You don't need poles when you go snowblading. Many teenagers prefer snowblading because it feels like skating on snow. The resort offers lessons specifically for snowblading enthusiasts.

english_meaning: A bank of deep snow heaped up by the wind. A pile of snow formed against an object or in a hollow. A large mound of wind-blown snow. An accumulation of snow driven together by wind. A hazardous heap of snow across a road or path.
example_sentence: The car was buried under a huge snowdrift. Villagers had to dig through snowdrifts to reach the road. A tall snowdrift blocked the front door. Sheep can shelter behind a snowdrift during storms.

english_meaning: Extremely busy because you have too much work or too many tasks. To be overwhelmed with a large amount of work, tasks, or responsibilities. A person feels they cannot handle everything at the same time because the workload is too heavy.
synonyms: ["Overwhelmed","Swamped","Buried in work","Overloaded","Inundated","Up to ears in work"]
example_sentence: I am snowed under with office work this week. She was snowed under after the holiday season sales reports. The teacher is snowed under with exam papers to check. We are snowed under with assignments before the deadline.

english_meaning: The fall of snow from the sky. A quantity of snow that falls in a particular place or period. An instance or occurrence of snowing. The amount of snow measured over a given time. A period during which snow falls.
example_sentence: Heavy snowfall closed the mountain road overnight. The region receives its first snowfall in November. Children played happily in the fresh snowfall. This year's snowfall was heavier than usual.

english_meaning: A single flake or crystal of falling snow. A person considered overly sensitive or easily offended, used in an insulting way. Someone who believes they are uniquely special and deserving of attention. A shape or decorative pattern resembling a crystal of snow.
example_sentence: Each snowflake that fell had a perfect six-sided pattern. Children pressed their faces to the glass to watch the snowflakes. He accused his critics of being snowflakes who cannot take a joke. She cut paper snowflakes to decorate the classroom windows.

english_meaning: A motor vehicle, typically with runners at the front and caterpillar tracks at the rear, used for traveling over snow. A motorized sled designed for winter recreation and travel. A vehicle used for transport in arctic or snowy regions.
example_sentence: We took the snowmobile out to explore the frozen lake. Driving a snowmobile requires a good sense of balance. The rescue team arrived at the cabin on a high-speed snowmobile. He maintains his snowmobile every winter to ensure it stays reliable. Many people in rural Alaska rely on a snowmobile for transportation.

english_meaning: To insult by ignoring. To treat someone coldly, ignore them, or show disrespect by deliberately underestimating or rejecting them.
example_sentence: She felt hurt when her friend snubbed her at the party by not even saying hello. The actor was snubbed by the award committee despite his excellent performance. The company snubbed the proposal without giving it proper consideration.

english_meaning: To extinguish a candle or a flame. To inhale through the nose, specifically tobacco or medicine. To sniff or smell something. To kill or put an end to something suddenly. A charred part of a candle wick.
example_sentence: She used a small metal tool to snuff the candle. He reached for his tin of snuff to take a quick pinch. The dog began to snuff around the base of the tree. The rebellion was snuffed out before it could even begin. He let out a loud snuff as he inhaled the cool morning air.

english_meaning: To breathe noisily through a partially blocked nose. To sniff repeatedly, especially when crying or having a cold. To make a soft snorting sound while smelling something. A snuffling sound or breath.
example_sentence: The child snuffled quietly after crying. The dog snuffled around the bushes looking for its toy. She had a bad cold and snuffled all night. He snuffled through the pages of his old diary.

english_meaning: Providing a sense of warmth, comfort, and safety. Fitting closely or tightly but comfortably. To settle oneself comfortably and warmly. Well-protected from the weather or intruders. Small but cozy.
example_sentence: The children looked very snug and warm in their beds. These gloves have a snug fit to keep out the cold air. The cabin was snug against the winter storm outside. We found a snug little corner in the library to study. She made sure her scarf was snug around her neck.

english_meaning: Used to refer to a person whose name is unknown, forgotten, or not important. Used to avoid saying a name directly. Sometimes used when speaking negatively about someone in an informal way.
example_sentence: I met so and so at the meeting yesterday. So and so told me about the event. If so and so calls, please give them this message. He is always complaining like so and so.

english_meaning: Up to the present moment or point in time. To the extent or degree reached until now. Up to a certain distance or limit. Used to say that something has been true until now but may change.
synonyms: ["Until now","Up to now","Thus far","Hitherto","To date","Yet","As yet","Currently"]
example_sentence: So far, we have collected half of the required funds. The weather has been pleasant so far this week. He has made no mistakes so far in the tournament. So far, nobody has been able to answer the question.

word: So far as I am concerned
english_meaning: Used to give your personal opinion on something. In my opinion. According to my view. From my perspective. In my opinion.
synonyms: ["In my opinion","From my perspective","To my mind","As I see it"]
antonyms: ["Regardless of my opinion","Officially decided","It does not matter to me","Independent of my view"]
example_sentence: So far as I am concerned, the project is a success. So far as I am concerned, honesty is the most important quality. So far as I am concerned, we should finish the project before Friday. So far as I am concerned, he did nothing wrong. So far as I am concerned, everyone deserves a second chance.

english_meaning: Used to indicate that what is being said is not literal but figurative or an expression. To signal that the speaker is using a figurative, metaphorical, or non-literal expression. It often softens a statement, making it more of a comparison or illustrative example rather than a strict fact.
synonyms: ["As it were","In a manner of speaking","Figuratively speaking","Metaphorically speaking"]
example_sentence: He was, so to speak, the backbone of the team. She’s a night owl, so to speak, always awake when others sleep. The city was a melting pot of cultures, so to speak. He gave her the cold shoulder, so to speak.

english_meaning: To place something in liquid so it absorbs moisture or becomes soft. To absorb information slowly and fully. To charge someone a high price informally. To stay in a bath for relaxation. Also used when someone or something becomes very wet. A period of time when something stays in liquid. The act or state of being in liquid for some time so it absorbs water or becomes soft.
example_sentence: Put the beans in water and let them soak overnight. The rain soaked my clothes. She soaked the cloth in warm water to clean the stain. The ground was soaked after the storm.

english_meaning: To fly or rise high in the air. To increase rapidly in amount, value, or intensity. To maintain height in the air without flapping wings. To reach a great height or level of excellence. To glide effortlessly.
example_sentence: The eagle began to soar above the mountain peaks. Gas prices continue to soar as the summer approaches. Her spirits began to soar when she heard the good news. The skyscraper seemed to soar into the clouds. The melody started to soar, filling the entire concert hall.

english_meaning: To cry noisily, taking sudden, sharp breaths. To say something while you are crying. Sorrowful cry or sound. To shed tears often while making meaningless sounds as a sign of pain or distress.
example_sentence:
I heard a child sobbing loudly.
He started to sob uncontrollably. ‘I hate him,’ she sobbed. He sobbed out his troubles. He gave a deep sob. I could hear her sobs from the next room.

english_meaning: To cause someone to become free from the effects of alcohol or to become more serious and thoughtful. Not drunk or affected by alcohol. Serious, calm, and sensible. Plain and simple in appearance or style.
example_sentence: After drinking only water for the rest of the evening, he was completely sober before driving home. She gave a sober explanation of the risks before everyone made a decision. The lawyer wore a sober gray suit during the court hearing. The tragic news quickly sobered the joyful crowd.

english_meaning: To regain self control after feeling excited, angry, emotional, or overly happy. To stop joking or behaving carelessly and start thinking or acting responsibly. To become sober after drinking alcohol, with clear thinking and normal behavior returning. To reduce unrealistic excitement after realizing the true situation.
synonyms: ["Calm down","Settle down","Compose oneself","Regain composure","Become serious","Cool off","Come to one's senses","Recover","Straighten up","Collect oneself","Relax","Regain self control"]
antonyms: ["Get excited","Lose control","Become emotional","Panic","Overreact","Get carried away","Act foolishly","Become intoxicated","Stay drunk","Behave recklessly"]
example_sentence: She took a short walk to sober down after hearing the shocking news. The children quickly sobered down when the teacher entered the classroom. It took him several hours to sober down after the party. The disappointing results helped the team sober down and prepare more carefully for the next competition.

english_meaning: To become less affected by alcohol and return to a normal state. To start thinking more seriously and realistically. To recover from excitement, emotion, or poor judgment.
synonyms: ["Become sober","Recover","Regain consciousness","Clear one's head","Sleep it off","Dry out","Come around"]
antonyms: ["Wise up","Come to one's senses","Face reality","Think clearly","Become sensible","Get serious","Wake up","Realize the truth"]
example_sentence: After drinking coffee and resting for a while, he finally sobered up. The accident made him sober up and change his reckless lifestyle. We should all sober up and face the reality of the situation. She sobered up before making an important decision.

english_meaning: The state of being sober; not under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The condition of living without intoxication, showing self-control and seriousness in behavior, thought, or lifestyle. It can also imply moderation and seriousness in conduct.
example_sentence: After years of struggling with alcohol, he finally achieved sobriety. Her sobriety and calm demeanor made her a trusted leader. Sobriety is important for making clear and rational decisions. The program helps individuals maintain long-term sobriety.

english_meaning: A person's nickname or an informal name for someone or something. A descriptive name given instead of or as well as the actual name. A familiar or humorous name. An epithet or alternative name.
example_sentence: Alexander the Great was a sobriquet for Alexander III of Macedon. The city earned the sobriquet of the Big Apple. His friends gave him the sobriquet Tiny despite his large size. The sobriquet stuck with him throughout his career.

english_meaning: Friendly and enjoying the company of other people. A person who likes to meet and spend time with others. A sociable person feels comfortable in social situations, enjoys conversation, and easily makes friends.
example_sentence: She is very sociable and makes friends wherever she goes. The new teacher is sociable and easy to talk to. He became more sociable after joining the sports club. A sociable gathering was arranged for the new employees.

english_meaning: Relating to society or its organization. Needing companionship and best suited to living in communities. Relating to activities in which people spend time talking to each other or doing enjoyable things with each other. Ranking high in a social hierarchy.
example_sentence: Humans are naturally social creatures who thrive in groups. We need to address various social issues like poverty and education. They spent the entire evening in a social gathering at the club. Bees and ants are known as social insects because of their colony structure. The government is planning new social policies to help the elderly.

english_meaning: Fear of social situations. An anxiety disorder where a person experiences intense fear or self-consciousness in social interactions or situations, worrying about being judged, embarrassed, or humiliated.
example_sentence: She avoided parties because of her social phobia. Social phobia can make public speaking extremely difficult. He developed social phobia after being teased in school. Therapy helped him manage his social phobia.

english_meaning: A person who attempts to gain a higher social position or status, often by using other people. Someone who seeks to befriend wealthy, famous, or influential individuals to improve their own standing. An ambitious person whose primary goal is to move up in high society, sometimes seen in a negative light. The act or characteristic of pursuing social advancement aggressively.
example_sentence: She was dismissed by her peers as merely a social climber trying to marry into money. The novel tells the story of a ruthless social climber in nineteenth-century London. He attended every exclusive party, proving himself to be a dedicated social climber. Many people view social climbers with suspicion because their friendships often seem insincere.

english_meaning: An implicit agreement among members of a society to cooperate for social benefits. A theory in political philosophy about the legitimacy of authority and the origins of society. The idea that individuals consent to surrender some freedoms to authority in exchange for protection and order. An unwritten agreement between citizens and their government defining mutual rights and responsibilities.
example_sentence: Rousseau wrote extensively about the social contract. The social contract theory explains how governments derive their authority. Citizens uphold the social contract by obeying laws. Breaking the social contract can lead to social disorder.

english_meaning: A political and economic system in which the means of production and distribution are owned or regulated by the community as a whole. An ideology that promotes equality, social welfare, and public ownership. A system that seeks to reduce economic inequality through collective action.
example_sentence: Socialism aims to reduce inequality among people. Many European countries follow forms of democratic socialism. Socialism became influential in the twentieth century. Critics and supporters of socialism often debate its economic effects.

english_meaning: People living together in an organized community with shared laws and customs. An organization or club formed for a particular purpose. The people of a country or region considered as a whole. The rich and fashionable class of people.
example_sentence: Education plays an important role in society. He joined a literary society at college. Modern society depends heavily on technology. The charity works for the welfare of the whole society.

english_meaning: Relating to both social and economic conditions or factors. Connected with the way society and the economy influence one another.
example_sentence: The study examined the socio-economic effects of unemployment. Education can improve a family’s socio-economic position. The policy targets socio-economic inequality. Researchers collected socio-economic data from rural households.

english_meaning: The scientific study of human society and social behaviour. The academic discipline that examines social institutions, groups, and relationships. The study of how societies develop, function, and change over time. An area of knowledge concerned with social problems such as crime, poverty, and inequality.
synonyms: ["Social science","Social studies","Social theory","Anthropology","Social research","Study of society"]
example_sentence: She is studying sociology at the university this year. Sociology helps us understand why crime rates differ between cities. His research in sociology focused on rural families. The department of sociology published a report on urban poverty.

english_meaning: An intense fear of social situations or of being judged, embarrassed, or humiliated in public. It is another term for social anxiety disorder.
example_sentence: Her sociophobia prevented her from attending parties. He struggled with sociophobia throughout his school years. Sociophobia can make everyday conversations feel overwhelming. Therapy helped her manage her sociophobia effectively.

english_meaning: A surface layer of ground consisting of grass and roots bound together. Turf. An informal British term for an unpleasant, annoying, or unfortunate person. Used as a mild swear word to express anger, frustration, or dismissal.
example_sentence: He cut a piece of sod to patch up the damaged lawn. Poor sod, he lost his job right before the holidays. Sod it, I left my wallet at home again. The gardener laid fresh sod in the front yard.

english_meaning: Saturated with liquid, especially water. Thoroughly soaked or waterlogged. Dull or expressionless as if from excessive drinking.
example_sentence: His boots were sodden after walking through the muddy marsh. The rain left the picnic blanket completely sodden. They huddled together in their sodden clothes waiting for the bus. The sodden ground made it difficult to pitch the tent.

english_meaning: The programs and instructions that tell a computer how to work. Applications and systems used on computers, phones, and other digital devices. The non-physical part of a computer system, in contrast to hardware. A written set of coded instructions designed to perform particular tasks.
example_sentence: The company develops software for small businesses. Please update the software before running the report. Free software is available for editing photographs. Their new accounting software saved hours of work each week.

english_meaning: A temporary stay at a place away from one's home. It refers to a brief period of living or residing in a specific location for travel, work, or resting. It marks a short-term visit rather than a permanent settlement.
example_sentence: My brief sojourn in the picturesque village completely refreshed my weary spirit. After a short sojourn in Japan, he vividly wrote a famous travel book. Their lovely summer sojourn at the lake house was filled with pure joy. Her delightful Parisian sojourn ended quite abruptly due to a family emergency. He took a restful sojourn to the mountains to write his deeply emotional novel.

english_meaning: Comfort or consolation in a time of great distress or sadness. It refers to something that provides a source of relief or emotional support during hardships. Finding peace in a difficult situation is the essence of this word.
example_sentence: She found solace in listening to her favorite classical music during the crisis. After the loss of his pet, he sought solace in the company of friends. The quiet garden offered a sense of solace from the busy city life. His kind words provided great solace to the grieving family members.

english_meaning: A hot, dust-laden easterly wind that blows on the Mediterranean coast of Spain, especially during summer. A dry, oppressive wind causing discomfort and health problems. A local Spanish term for a specific seasonal wind.
example_sentence: The solano made the afternoon unbearably hot. Farmers dread the solano during harvest time. Many people suffer headaches when the solano blows. The solano brought clouds of dust into the town.

english_meaning: Being the only one of its kind; belonging or restricted to one person or group. It can also refer to the undersurface of a person's foot or the bottom of a shoe. It emphasizes exclusivity or singularity.
example_sentence: She was the sole survivor of the tragic airplane accident. The company has the sole right to market this innovative product. He needs to replace the worn-out sole of his favorite leather boots. Protecting the environment is not her sole responsibility but everyone's duty.

english_meaning: Only, exclusively, entirely by itself or without anyone or anything else involved. Something is done only for one reason, by one person, or involving one thing and nothing else. It emphasizes exclusiveness and absence of additional factors.
example_sentence: She was motivated solely by self-interest. Selection is based solely on merit. He became solely responsible for the firm. She wanted solely to get out of the house for a while. His rank was based solely on merit. You will be held solely responsible for any damage. She did not write solely for money.

english_meaning: Very serious or formal in manner, behavior, or expression. Looking very serious, Sad, Not smiling, Not happy.
example_sentence: She solemnly promised not to say a word to anyone about it. Her face grew solemn. A solemn experience.

english_meaning: A serious moral or legal obligation that must be fulfilled. A responsibility that is treated with deep respect and commitment. A task assigned by a higher authority or conscience that cannot be ignored. An act of service performed with great gravity.
example_sentence: It is our solemn duty to protect the environment for future generations. The judge felt a solemn duty to uphold the law fairly. Soldiers consider the defense of their country a solemn duty. Attending the funeral was seen as a solemn duty by the community.

english_meaning: To perform a religious ceremony, especially a marriage. Formal to mark (something) officially or formally especially with a religious ceremony. To perform with pomp or ceremony. To make solemn.
example_sentence: Marriage is solemnized mainly through negotiation. That was a church from which a licence to solemnize marriages had been withdrawn. The priest solemnized their marriage.

english_meaning: A person who officially performs or conducts a marriage ceremony or another formal ceremony according to legal or religious authority. An individual who has the legal, religious, or official authority to conduct and certify a marriage ceremony. The word may also refer to someone who presides over or performs other formal or ceremonial events. Depending on the country, a solemnizer may be a judge, religious leader, registrar, or another person authorized by law.
example_sentence: The solemniser ensured that the marriage ceremony followed all legal requirements. The couple thanked the solemniser for making their wedding memorable. The solemniser signed the marriage certificate after the ceremony. Every solemniser must follow the laws governing marriage registration.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being serious and dignified. A formal, dignified rite or ceremony. A trait of dignified seriousness. A high degree of earnestness.
example_sentence: The judge spoke with great solemnity when delivering the final verdict. The coronation was a ceremony of grand solemnity and ancient tradition. We were struck by the solemnity of the occasion as the memorial began. He maintained his solemnity despite the chaotic environment around him. The solemnity of the oath made everyone in the room fall silent.

english_meaning: The act of performing a ceremony with formal rites, especially a marriage. The process of making something official or legal through a formal procedure. The performance of a religious or state ritual.
example_sentence: The solemnization of their marriage took place in a historic chapel. Legal solemnization is required for the contract to be binding. Relatives traveled from afar to witness the solemnization of the vows. The office handles the solemnization of civil unions every Friday. We are gathered here for the solemnization of this holy union.

english_meaning: To perform a religious ceremony, especially a marriage. Formal to mark (something) officially or formally especially with a religious ceremony. To perform with pomp or ceremony. To make solemn.
example_sentence: Marriage is solemnized mainly through negotiation. That was a church from which a licence to solemnize marriages had been withdrawn. The priest solemnized their marriage.

english_meaning: A person who officially performs or conducts a marriage ceremony or another formal ceremony according to legal or religious authority. An individual who has the legal, religious, or official authority to conduct and certify a marriage ceremony. The word may also refer to someone who presides over or performs other formal or ceremonial events. Depending on the country, a solemnizer may be a judge, religious leader, registrar, or another person authorized by law.
example_sentence: The solemnizer verified the couple's documents before conducting the wedding ceremony. Every solemnizer must follow the legal requirements of the country. The family thanked the solemnizer for making the wedding memorable. The solemnizer signed the marriage certificate after the ceremony.

english_meaning: In a formal and dignified manner. With deep sincerity and seriousness. In a way that shows a person is not joking. With a religious or sacred character.
example_sentence: He solemnly promised to tell the truth in court. The monks walked solemnly through the ancient halls. She solemnly swore her allegiance to the new leader. The treaty was signed solemnly by both representatives.

english_meaning: A cylindrical coil of wire acting as a magnet when carrying electric current. A device used to convert electrical energy into mechanical movement. A type of electromagnet often used in automotive starters and valves.
example_sentence: The starter motor uses a solenoid to engage the engine's flywheel. When the switch is flipped, the solenoid pulls the metal rod forward. Technicians replaced the faulty solenoid in the transmission system. A solenoid valve controls the flow of water in the irrigation pipe. The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is remarkably uniform.

english_meaning: A broad, flat muscle lying underneath the gastrocnemius in the back of the lower leg. A deep calf muscle that joins the gastrocnemius to form the Achilles tendon. The muscle that keeps the body upright and steady while standing and helps push the foot downward during slow walking.
synonyms: ["Deep calf muscle","Triceps surae (part)","Lower leg muscle","Postural calf muscle"]
example_sentence: The soleus lies deep beneath the gastrocnemius muscle. A strong soleus helps you stand for long hours without fatigue. The therapist showed him an exercise to strengthen the soleus. Swimming and cycling can both work the soleus muscle.

english_meaning: To ask for something earnestly or formally, often help, support, or money. To make a request or petition for something, typically in a persuasive or earnest manner. It can also mean seeking to obtain something from someone, often in a formal or professional context. In law, it can mean to entice someone to commit an unlawful act.
example_sentence: The charity organization solicited donations from local businesses. She was soliciting advice from experienced colleagues. The lawyer was accused of soliciting a bribe. The company solicited feedback from its customers to improve service.

english_meaning: A formal or polite request for something. The act of asking someone for help, money, support, or information. An attempt to gain business, customers, or donations. Persuading or encouraging someone to do something. In legal usage, encouraging someone to commit an unlawful act.
example_sentence: The charity sent a solicitation for donations after the flood. His solicitation for financial support was accepted by the company. The sales team made phone calls for customer solicitation. The lawyer was accused of solicitation in the legal case.

english_meaning: A lawyer who gives legal advice, prepares legal documents, and helps clients in legal matters. A legal professional who advises people or companies about laws, legal rights, contracts, property matters, court cases, and official documents. In some countries such as the United Kingdom, a solicitor mainly deals directly with clients and prepares cases, while barristers appear in higher courts. A person who requests, seeks, or tries to obtain something such as donations, support, or business.
example_sentence: The solicitor prepared all the legal documents for the property transfer. She consulted a solicitor before signing the business agreement. The company hired a solicitor to handle the court case. A charity solicitor visited the market to request donations for flood victims.

english_meaning: Firm and stable in shape, not liquid or gaseous. Strong, well made, and unlikely to break or fail. Having no holes or spaces inside; not hollow. Reliable, dependable, and based on good evidence. Continuous and without interruption. An object or substance that keeps a fixed shape and volume.
