example_sentence: Ice is water in its solid state. The table is made of solid wood. She gave a solid performance in the final match. He worked for three solid hours without a break.

english_meaning: Unity or agreement among people with a shared interest. A strong feeling of unity, support, and loyalty among individuals or groups, especially when they share common goals, interests, or challenges. It often appears in social, political, or community contexts where people stand together to support each other.
example_sentence: The workers showed solidarity by protesting together. In times of crisis, communities often act with solidarity. The country expressed solidarity with the victims of the disaster. Students formed a group in solidarity to support their classmates.

english_meaning: To change from a liquid or gas into a solid. To become hard or firm. To make an idea, plan, or agreement stronger or more certain. To unite or strengthen something firmly.
example_sentence: Water solidifies into ice at zero degrees Celsius. The cement will solidify within a few hours. The victory solidified their position at the top of the league. They signed the contract to solidify the partnership.

english_meaning: To speak one's thoughts aloud when alone. To deliver a soliloquy, especially in a play. To talk at length without expecting a reply from anyone.
example_sentence: He often soliloquizes while pacing around his study. The character soliloquizes about death in the final act. She soliloquized quietly as she tidied the empty house. Grandfather liked to soliloquize over his morning tea.

english_meaning: A speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud while alone. The act of talking to oneself without addressing anyone else. A long monologue delivered in the presence of others but not directed at them.
example_sentence: Hamlet's soliloquy is one of the most famous speeches in English literature. The actor delivered the soliloquy with quiet intensity. She sat by the window in a soliloquy of regret. His long soliloquy at dinner left the guests silent.

english_meaning: The philosophical view that only one's own mind is certain to exist. The belief that nothing outside one's own experience can be truly known. Extreme self-absorption or preoccupation with one's own feelings and interests.
example_sentence: The novel explores solipsism through a narrator who doubts everything around him. Critics accused the poet of a comfortable solipsism. Solipsism is difficult to refute but almost impossible to live by. His solipsism made genuine friendship impossible.

english_meaning: Relating to the belief that only one's own mind certainly exists. Excessively concerned with oneself and indifferent to others. Showing a narrow view of the world limited to personal experience.
example_sentence: The diary has a solipsistic tone that ignores everyone else. His solipsistic worldview left no room for other opinions. Critics called the film beautiful but solipsistic. She writes in a solipsistic style that rarely looks outward.

english_meaning: A card game played alone by a single player. A single gemstone, especially a diamond, set on its own in a ring. A board game for one person played by moving pegs or marbles. A person who lives alone in isolation.
example_sentence: He plays solitaire on his phone during the train ride. She wore a simple gold ring with a small solitaire. The old wooden solitaire board belonged to his grandmother. After his retirement he lived like a solitaire in the hills.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being alone. The condition of living apart from other people. A sense of separateness or isolation from company. The quality of a place that is remote and rarely visited.
example_sentence: He found peace in the solitariness of the mountains. The solitariness of her later years shaped her writing. There is a deep solitariness about that old farmhouse. Long voyages taught the sailor to accept solitariness.

english_meaning: Alone; without others; single. Refers to being by oneself, without company, or existing alone. Can describe a person, animal, or thing that prefers or exists in isolation.
example_sentence: He enjoyed a solitary walk in the forest. The prisoner spent ten years in solitary confinement. She lived a solitary life after moving to the countryside. A solitary tree stood on the hill.

english_meaning: A lonely or deserted place. The state of being alone or kept apart from others. The state or situation of being alone.
example_sentence:
After months of solitude at sea it felt strange to be in company.
It provides one with a chance to reflect on spiritual matters in solitude. He prefers the solitude of the country to the chaos of the city.

english_meaning: Doing something alone without any assistance. It is often used in music, travel, performance, or any activity done independently. It can also mean a single performance or act by one person.
example_sentence: She decided to travel solo across the country. He performed a beautiful guitar solo at the concert. I prefer working solo because I can focus better. The pilot had to fly solo after the instructor stepped out.

english_meaning: On one’s own initiative, without being asked or instructed. It is a Latin phrase meaning “of one’s own motion.” It is used when someone takes action independently, without external prompting. In legal or formal contexts, it refers to a judge or authority acting on their own initiative.
example_sentence: The manager acted solo moto to resolve the issue before it escalated. She submitted her application solo moto without waiting for an announcement. The court took notice of the matter solo moto due to its importance. He started the project solo moto, showing strong initiative.

english_meaning: The ability of a person or organization to pay its debts. A financial condition in which assets exceed liabilities. The state of being able to meet long-term financial obligations. Financial soundness and stability. The capacity to discharge all monetary commitments when they become due.
example_sentence: The bank's solvency was confirmed by the latest audit report. Maintaining solvency is essential for any successful business. The government took steps to ensure the solvency of the company. Investors are worried about the solvency of the firm. Solvency ratios help measure a company's long-term financial health.

english_meaning: A liquid in which another substance can be dissolved to form a solution. Having enough money to pay all debts and financial obligations. Something that dissolves or breaks down a solid, liquid, or gas.
example_sentence: Water is often described as the universal solvent because it dissolves more substances than any other liquid. The company remained solvent despite the difficult economic conditions of the past two years. She used a chemical solvent to remove the old paint from the wooden door. Without investment, the business will struggle to remain solvent for more than a few months. A powerful solvent was required to break down the adhesive used in the manufacturing process.

english_meaning: Relating to the physical body, Concerning bodily sensations or movements. Associated with body tissues and organs, Pertaining to non reproductive cells of the body, Physical rather than psychological. Anything connected with the body's physical structure, functions, sensations, or cells. It is often used in medicine, psychology, biology, and health sciences to distinguish physical conditions from mental or emotional ones.
example_sentence: The patient complained of several somatic symptoms, including headaches and fatigue. Somatic exercises can improve posture and body awareness. The doctor found no somatic cause for the pain. Stress sometimes appears as somatic problems such as stomach pain.

english_meaning: Dark or dull in color or tone; gloomy. Oppressively solemn or sober in mood; grave. Lacking light or brightness. Extremely serious or sad.
example_sentence: The funeral took place on a somber, rainy afternoon in London. He was in a somber mood after hearing the disappointing news. Most of the guests were dressed in somber colors like grey and black. The hall was filled with a somber silence as the names were read. Her facial expression became somber when she started discussing the budget.

english_meaning: Dark, dull, or gloomy in colour or appearance. Serious, sad, or solemn in mood or manner. Suggesting seriousness or grief, as of a place or occasion.
example_sentence: The mourners were dressed in sombre colours. A sombre mood settled over the room after the news. The painting is dominated by sombre browns and greys. He spoke in a sombre tone about the accident.

english_meaning: To become very angry suddenly. A situation where a person loses their temper quickly or reacts with strong anger, often without thinking rationally. It suggests an intense emotional reaction, usually due to frustration, insult, or provocation.
synonyms: ["Fly into a rage","Lose one’s temper","Go ballistic","Blow up","Get furious"]
example_sentence: When he heard the insult, he saw red and stormed out of the room. She saw red when someone scratched her car. He saw red after learning about the unfair decision. They saw red during the heated argument.

english_meaning: To become very angry quickly. A situation where a person suddenly becomes extremely angry or loses control due to anger. It often implies an immediate, intense emotional reaction.
synonyms: ["Fly off the handle","Lose one’s temper","Get furious","Go ballistic","Get enraged"]
example_sentence: He sees red whenever someone lies to him. She sees red if her work is criticized unfairly. My father sees red when people waste food. The teacher sees red when students are disruptive in class.

english_meaning: To turn the body completely over in the air or on the ground. A complete turning of the body in the air or on the ground, where the feet pass over the head. A sudden change in ideas, plans, or direction. A sudden reversal of opinion, policy, or situation.
example_sentence: The child somersaulted across the soft grass. He somersaulted off the diving board into the pool. She somersaulted to impress the judges. She did a somersault on the trampoline. The gymnast landed her first somersault perfectly. He fell but managed to turn it into a funny somersault. The company's strategy made a sudden somersault after the new manager arrived.

english_meaning: Somersault. An acrobatic feat in which the feet roll over the head (either forward or backward) and return. A county in southwestern England on the Bristol Channel.
example_sentence: I plan to visit Somerset this summer to see its countryside. The cider in Somerset is considered some of the best in England. She studied the history of Somerset for her research project. Flooding is common in the Somerset Levels during winter.

english_meaning: The consequences, especially harmful ones, of a person's past actions eventually return to affect that person. A mistake or wrongdoing finally produces the result it deserves.
synonyms: ["Reap What You Sow","Pay The Price","Face The Consequences","Catch Up With"]
example_sentence: Years of ignored maintenance came home to roost when the roof collapsed. His reckless spending came home to roost when the debts piled up. The company's poor labor practices eventually came home to roost in a public scandal. Her habit of missing deadlines came home to roost during the annual review.

english_meaning: At some point in the future or later time. Eventually, after a certain period. Refers to a time that will come, but not specifically known. An unspecified time in the future not exact, but expected.
example_sentence: Somewhere down the line, you’ll realize that everything happens for a reason. They plan to buy a house somewhere down the line when they have enough savings. Somewhere down the line, we lost our connection with nature. He may apologize somewhere down the line, but it might be too late.

english_meaning: Feeling sleepy, drowsy, or inclined to sleep. Causing or tending to cause sleep. Half-asleep or in a state of dullness and inactivity. Lacking energy or alertness, as if about to fall asleep. Often used to describe places, sounds, or atmospheres that have a quiet, sleep-inducing quality.
example_sentence: The warm afternoon sun made the entire class feel somnolent. He spoke in a low, somnolent voice that nearly put the children to sleep. The small village wore a somnolent look in the heat of summer. After the heavy lunch, a somnolent silence settled over the room. She felt somnolent after taking the strong cold medicine.

english_meaning: A subjective unit of loudness, as perceived by a person with normal hearing. The loudness of a sound that is judged by a listener to be equal to a 40-decibel tone of 1,000 Hertz. A measure used in psychoacoustics to describe how intense a sound feels rather than its physical power. A unit that follows a power law relationship with sound pressure. A scale where doubling the value represents a perceived doubling of loudness.
synonyms: ["Loudness Unit","Auditory Magnitude","Sound Intensity Measure","Acoustic Scale","Phon Equivalent","Hearing Level","Sound Perception Unit","Sonic Level","Volume Measure","Audio Unit","Intensity Value","Perception Metric"]
example_sentence: The engineer calculated the noise level of the engine in sones to ensure passenger comfort. A sound of two sones is perceived as twice as loud as a sound of one sone. Psychoacoustic experiments often use the sone scale to map human hearing response. Because decibels are logarithmic, the sone provides a more intuitive linear measure of loudness.

english_meaning: A poem of fourteen lines using any of a number of formal rhyme schemes, typically having ten syllables per line. A short poem with a fixed structure and specific rhythmic pattern. To compose or praise something in a poetic form.
example_sentence: Shakespeare is famous for writing a sequence of a hundred and fifty-four sonnets. The poet dedicated a beautiful sonnet to his beloved. A traditional sonnet usually concludes with a rhyming couplet. She struggled to fit her complex emotions into the rigid fourteen-line structure of a sonnet. Reading a sonnet requires attention to both the meter and the rhyme.

english_meaning: To dive or swim under water, often used in older or dialectal English. To sink down or submerge into a liquid. To move through water with a plunging motion. To disappear beneath a surface.
example_sentence: The children watched the ducks soom under the surface of the pond. He decided to soom deep into the lake to find the lost anchor. It is dangerous to soom in areas where the water current is too strong. The fish would soom whenever they heard a loud noise nearby. As the sun set, the boat seemed to soom into the dark horizon.

english_meaning: To calm or reduce pain, stress, or discomfort. To make someone or something feel calmer, less painful, or less worried. To comfort someone emotionally. To relieve irritation or inflammation. To calm anger or fear. To make something less intense or severe. To gently calm a person, feeling, or physical pain. It can be used for emotions like anger or anxiety, or physical conditions like pain or irritation.
example_sentence: The mother soothed her crying baby with a soft lullaby. Hot tea helped to soothe his sore throat. She tried to soothe his anger after the argument. The music soothed her nerves after a stressful day.

english_meaning: Covered with or full of soot. Black or dark grey like soot in colour. Producing or giving off soot.
example_sentence: The chimney sweep came down with sooty hands and face. A sooty film covered the windows of the old factory. Sooty smoke rose from the burning tyres. The bird had sooty black feathers.

english_meaning: A person who uses clever but misleading arguments to deceive or impress others. Someone skilled in argument, especially one who uses reasoning that appears logical but is actually false or deceptive. The term originally referred to teachers of rhetoric in ancient Greece, but now it often has a negative sense, implying dishonesty in reasoning.
example_sentence: The politician was accused of being a sophist who twisted facts to win debates. Do not trust every confident speaker, some may be sophists using clever tricks. His argument sounded strong, but it was the reasoning of a sophist. The teacher warned students not to become sophists but seekers of truth.

english_meaning: To make someone or something more worldly-wise or cultured. A person who has a high degree of refinement and experience in matters of culture and fashion. To make a system or machine more complex or advanced. To alter or pervert the simplicity or purity of something.
example_sentence: Travel and education helped to legislate and sophisticate his outlook on life. She is a true sophisticate who feels at home in any major worldly capital. The engineers worked to sophisticate the software for better performance. It is hard to sophisticate a child's mind without losing their innocence. The new boutique aims to attract the urban sophisticate.

english_meaning: Having or showing refined knowledge, taste, or culture. Highly developed, complex, or advanced in nature. Experienced in worldly affairs.
example_sentence: She wore a sophisticated dress to the formal dinner. Modern fighter jets use highly sophisticated radar systems. He has a sophisticated understanding of international politics. The restaurant offers a sophisticated dining experience.

english_meaning: The quality of being sophisticated, cultured, or refined. High complexity or advanced development in a system, design, or technique. The state of having worldly experience and refined knowledge.
example_sentence: Her elegance and sophistication impressed everyone at the banquet. The technological sophistication of modern smartphones is incredible. He lacks the social sophistication required for diplomatic roles. The restaurant is famous for its culinary sophistication.

english_meaning: The use of fallacious arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving. A subtle, tricky, superficially plausible, but generally fallacious method of reasoning. False reasoning or argumentation that looks true but is actually misleading. A clever but false statement.
example_sentence: The politician relied on sophistry to avoid answering the direct question. Do not be fooled by his elegant sophistry; his facts are entirely wrong. Her argument was pure sophistry, designed to confuse the jury. Trying to justify a crime through philosophical sophistry is morally wrong. The professor exposed the sophistry behind the popular economic theory.

english_meaning: A drug, medicine, or substance that induces sleep or drowsiness. Causing or tending to cause sleep, drowsiness, or lack of alertness.
example_sentence: The medicine had a soporific effect on the patient. The professor’s long and dull lecture was almost soporific. Warm milk at night can be soporific. The rhythmic sound of rain proved to be soporific.

english_meaning: Causing emotional pain or distress. Painful and uncomfortable because of injury, infection, or too much use. Painful, and often red, especially because of infection or because a muscle has been used too much
example_sentence:
All the dust has made my eyes sore.
I've got a sore back.
My feet were sore with all the walking.

english_meaning: Comparative form of sore. Experiencing or causing a greater degree of physical pain or tenderness. Suffering from more physical injury or distress. More upset, angry, or resentful.
example_sentence: My legs were sorer today than they were yesterday. His throat felt sorer after prolonged public speaking. She was even sorer about the unexpected rejection than she admitted. I have a sorer blister on this heel compared to the other. The tense muscles in my back are sorer than ever after the heavy lifting.

english_meaning: A women’s student organization, usually in a college or university. An organized group of female students in a college or university. Members usually share common values, social activities, leadership training, and community service. Sororities often use Greek letters as names and focus on friendship, support, and personal development.
example_sentence: She joined a sorority to make new friends at university. The sorority organized a charity event for local schools. Life in a sorority helped her build leadership skills. Each sorority on campus has its own traditions and values.

english_meaning: Feeling or showing deep sadness or grief. Causing sadness in others. Expressing sorrow through appearance or words. Full of regret and unhappiness.
example_sentence: She gave a sorrowful look as the train pulled away. It was a sorrowful day for the whole village. His sorrowful song moved everyone in the hall. They received the sorrowful news early in the morning.

english_meaning: An apology is not enough. This phrase is used when someone feels that saying sorry alone is insufficient to fix a serious mistake, damage, or harm. It shows dissatisfaction and a demand for stronger action or responsibility.
synonyms: ["That is not sufficient","Words are not enough","More than sorry is needed"]
antonyms: ["Sorry is enough","Apology accepted","That will do","It is forgiven"]
example_sentence: You missed the deadline again. Sorry doesn’t cut it this time. After the damage he caused, sorry doesn’t cut it anymore. She said sorry, but for the team, sorry doesn’t cut it. When people are hurt, sorry doesn’t cut it without action.

english_meaning: The place, person, or thing from which something comes or begins. The point at which a river or stream starts. A person, book, or document that provides information or evidence. A cause or origin of a situation, problem, or feeling. To obtain materials, goods, or information from a particular place.
example_sentence: The Indus has its source high in the mountains. Sunlight is our main source of vitamin D. The journalist refused to reveal her source. The company sources its cotton from local farmers.

english_meaning: Somewhat sour. Slightly acidic or tart in taste or smell. Having a slight disposition to be sour or resentful.
example_sentence: The sauce had a pleasant sourish tang to it. The milk developed a sourish smell after being left out on the counter. He took a bite of the sourish plum and squinted his eyes. The old wine had a distinctively sourish flavor. She gave me a sourish look when I mentioned the extra work.

english_meaning: A small item kept to remember a place, person, or event. An object that someone buys or keeps as a reminder of a trip, experience, celebration, or special moment. It often represents the culture or identity of a place. Souvenirs can be simple items like keychains, postcards, or traditional handicrafts. A commemorative gift given at events such as weddings, conferences, or official ceremonies. A memory object kept for emotional attachment. A printed item such as a souvenir program or booklet prepared for a special occasion.
example_sentence: I bought the ring as a souvenir of Greece. We brought back a few souvenirs from our holiday in Mexico. He bought a model of a red London bus as a souvenir of his trip to London.

english_meaning: A king or queen. An old British gold coin worth one pound. A nation's ruler or head of state usually by hereditary right. Greatest in status or authority or power.
example_sentence:
The Tongan sovereign is head of state and exercises executive power. 
The islands are ruled by a governor, representing the British sovereign.

english_meaning: Complete power to govern a country. Unlimited power over a country. The power or authority to rule. The power of a country to control its own government. Government free from external control.
example_sentence:
The country claimed sovereignty over the island.
This constitutes an attack on the sovereignty of Parliament. Vietnam has recently conducted consolidation on the islands under Vietnam's sovereignty.

english_meaning: Having plenty of space or room; roomy and comfortable. Large in area or extent. Providing ample room to move freely. Open and airy in feel.
example_sentence: They moved into a spacious new apartment. The hotel offers spacious rooms with a view. The car has a spacious interior for long trips. We enjoyed dinner in a spacious dining hall.

english_meaning: To dig or turn over soil. A tool for digging soil. A tool with a flat metal blade and a handle, used for digging, cutting soil, or lifting earth. It can also refer to one of the four suits in playing cards.
example_sentence: He used a spade to dig a hole in the garden. The farmer cleaned his spade after work. She drew the ace of spades during the game. They spaded the soil before planting crops. He bought a new spade for gardening. The spade is kept in the shed. She used the spade to plant flowers.

english_meaning: To send large numbers of unwanted messages, advertisements, or links to people through email, social media, forums, or messaging platforms. It can also mean repeatedly posting the same message or content to attract attention or promote something. Unwanted or irrelevant messages sent in large numbers, usually online. A type of canned meat produced by Spam.
example_sentence: He always deletes spam emails. My email inbox is full of spam messages today. The forum banned the user for spamming links. Please check your spam folder if you cannot find the email. Many companies use filters to block spam.

english_meaning: To stretch across or cover something from one side to another. To extend across a space, distance, or period of time. The distance, width, or period between two points. It is often used for bridges, structures, time periods, or activities that cover a wide range.
example_sentence: I worked with him over a span of 6 years. His acting career spanned 55 years. Family photos spanning five generations were stolen. The project must be completed with a specified time span. The bridge spans the valley. Her research spans several scientific fields. The bridge has a long span over the river. The average human life span is increasing.

english_meaning: A metal hand tool used for gripping and turning nuts and bolts. A wrench, especially in British English. Something or someone that causes a sudden problem, as used in idioms. A tool of various shapes and sizes used in mechanical repair work.
example_sentence: He tightened the bolt with a large spanner. Please pass me the spanner from the toolbox. The mechanic kept a full set of spanners in his van. A loose spanner was left lying under the car.

english_meaning: To make the motions of boxing without landing heavy blows as a form of training. To engage in a minor argument or dispute. A stout pole such as a mast, boom, or yard used to support the rigging of a sailing ship.
example_sentence: The two boxers began to spar in the ring to prepare for the upcoming match. Politicians often spar with each other during live television debates. Even though they are best friends, they frequently spar over minor issues. The wooden spar of the old ship was damaged during the heavy storm.

english_meaning: To separate by striking. To remove, separate, or push away lightly by hitting or fencing
example_sentence: He sparred off the weeds from the garden. The fencer sparred off his opponent's attack. They sparred off the branches carefully. The waves sparred off the rocks.

english_meaning: To argue or fight in a friendly or not serious way. To engage in a verbal or physical argument, debate, or contest, usually not hostile but rather a discussion with some conflict or disagreement.
example_sentence: The teammates sparred over the best strategy for the game. The politicians sparred over the new tax policy. The siblings sparred over who would do the chores. Scientists often spar over interpretations of data.

english_meaning: To argue or fight lightly. To engage in a practice fight, debate, or argument, usually friendly or for training purposes.
example_sentence: They sparred with each other during boxing practice. The politicians sparred over tax reforms. We like to spar with ideas before making a decision. The kids sparred playfully in the park.

english_meaning: To have left over or as margin. Not being used. A duplicate (such as a key or a machine part) kept in reserve. To forbear to destroy, punish, or harm. Available to do what you want with rather than work
example_sentence:
I've lost my key and I haven't got a spare. I keep a spare tyre in the back of the car. Could you spare one of your staff to help us out? He's studying music in his spare time.
I haven't had a spare moment this morning.

english_meaning: To cause a sudden beginning of an action, idea, emotion, or event. It often implies triggering change or reaction. A tiny flash of light or fire caused by electricity, friction, or burning. It also refers to the beginning or sign of an idea, emotion, hope, or conflict.
example_sentence: The news sparked public anger. One comment sparked a long discussion. A spark flew from the electric switch. There was a spark of excitement in the room.

english_meaning: Thinly scattered or not dense. Something that exists in small numbers, widely spaced, or lacking fullness. It describes low density, minimal quantity, or limited occurrence.
example_sentence: The information available on the subject is sparse. The forest became sparse as we climbed higher. Sparse rainfall affected the crops this year. The population in the desert is sparse. His notes were sparse but meaningful.

english_meaning: To flood with a large amount. To overwhelm suddenly. To increase rapidly in quantity. A sudden large number or amount of something. A sudden flood of water. A series of events happening quickly.
example_sentence: After the storm, the river was in spate. There has been a spate of new applications this week. The news channel reported a spate of accidents on the highway. Social media saw a spate of reactions after the announcement. The company received a spate of orders. Messages spatted the inbox after the announcement. Requests spatted the office within minutes.

english_meaning: Relating to space, position, location, distance, direction, arrangement, or the physical relationship between objects in an area. Anything connected with physical space and how objects, places, or people are arranged, located, or organized. It is often used in geography, architecture, mathematics, psychology, computer science, and everyday descriptions of location and arrangement.
example_sentence: Good spatial awareness helps drivers judge distances accurately. The architect created a spatial design that maximized the available area. Spatial data is used to create accurate maps. Children develop spatial skills through puzzles and building blocks.

english_meaning: Said when a person being talked about appears unexpectedly. Someone you were just talking about arrives or is mentioned, implying coincidence between talking about them and their appearance. It often carries a lighthearted tone.
example_sentence: Speak of the devil, here he comes. Speak of the devil! "We were just talking about you”. I hadn’t seen John in months, and then, speak of the devil, he walked in. Speak of the devil, there’s Sarah calling you now!. We were discussing the new manager, and speak of the devil, he entered the room.

english_meaning: To say openly and honestly what you think or feel, without hiding your opinions. To express thoughts or feelings directly, even if others may not like it.
example_sentence: She always speaks her mind, even in front of her boss. He always speaks his mind, even if people get upset.

english_meaning: To clearly convey a lot of information or reveal strong feelings without using many words; to be very expressive.
example_sentence: His silence spoke volumes. Her smile spoke volumes about her happiness. The empty room spoke volumes about the recent departure of the family. His actions speak volumes more than his words ever could. The teacher’s praise spoke volumes about the student’s dedication.

english_meaning: A weapon with a long shaft and a pointed tip, typically of metal, used for thrusting or throwing. To pierce or strike with a spear or other pointed object.
example_sentence: The ancient hunter threw his spear at the wild boar. He managed to spear a large fish in the shallow river. The guards stood tall with their spears pointing towards the sky. She expertly used a fork to spear a piece of meat from the bowl. The museum exhibits a grand collection of historical spears.

english_meaning: A detailed description of the design, requirements, and materials of a product or system, usually short for specification. A speculative venture or investment, usually short for speculation. A pair of glasses, usually short for spectacles.
example_sentence: The engineers are reviewing the final spec before starting production. She wrote the screenplay on spec, hoping a studio would buy it later. Please ensure that the building materials meet the required spec exactly. We need a higher spec computer to run this advanced software smoothly.

english_meaning: A continuous area or expanse which is free, available, or unoccupied. The dimensions of height, depth, and width within which all things exist and move. The physical universe beyond the earth's atmosphere.
example_sentence: There is an empty space on the bookshelf. The rocket was launched into outer space. Please leave a space between each word. We need more space to accommodate everyone. He was staring blindly into empty space.

english_meaning: Better, greater, or different from what is usual. Designed or intended for a particular purpose or occasion. Held in particular affection or regard. An event, offer, item, or broadcast that is not part of the regular routine.
example_sentence: Today is a special day for our family. The chef prepared a special dish for the guests. This restaurant has a lunch special every Friday. She holds a special place in his heart.

english_meaning: A particular subject or area of work in which a person has expert knowledge. The practice of concentrating on one narrow field of study or activity. A special skill or subject that someone has chosen to focus on. The state of being a specialist in a limited branch of knowledge.
example_sentence: Her specialism is child psychology. The university is famous for its specialism in marine biology. He chose surgery as his main specialism after graduation. Modern medicine has moved steadily towards greater specialism.

english_meaning: A person who has expert knowledge, skill, or training in a particular field or subject. A doctor who is highly trained in a specific branch of medicine. Someone whose work or study is limited to one narrow area. Relating to or involving a particular area of expertise. Designed or intended for a specific purpose or group.
example_sentence: Her doctor referred her to a heart specialist for further tests. He is a specialist in ancient Greek literature. The hospital has opened a new specialist clinic for children. You will need specialist advice before signing the contract.

english_meaning: A subject or skill in which someone is expert. A product or dish for which a person, place, or restaurant is well known. A special feature or distinctive quality of something.
example_sentence: Grilled fish is the speciality of this restaurant. Medieval history is her academic speciality. The region is famous for its speciality cheeses. Repairing antique clocks is his speciality.

english_meaning: The process of concentrating on and becoming expert in a particular subject or skill. A particular field or branch in which someone specialises. The division of work into specific tasks in an organisation or economy. Adaptation of an organ or organism to a specific function.
example_sentence: Her specialization is paediatric surgery. Increasing specialization has changed modern medicine. Specialization of labour improved the factory's output. He chose specialization in renewable energy.

english_meaning: To concentrate on and become an expert in a particular subject, skill, or area of work. To offer or provide one particular product or service above others. To adapt to a specific function or environment, as an organ or organism does.
example_sentence: She decided to specialize in criminal law. This shop specializes in handmade leather goods. Some birds specialize in feeding on insects. He plans to specialize after completing his degree.

english_meaning: Designed, trained, or developed for one particular purpose or field. Having expert knowledge or skill in a narrow subject. Concentrated on a limited area of work or study. Adapted to perform a specific function, as in cells or organs.
example_sentence: The surgery requires highly specialized equipment. She works in a specialized branch of environmental law. Our staff have received specialized training in first aid. Nerve cells are specialized to carry electrical signals.

english_meaning: For a particular purpose and no other. In a way that is different from the usual. To an unusual or exceptional degree. With a specific person or occasion in mind.
example_sentence: This cake was made specially for your birthday. The room is specially designed for young children. He came specially to see you. The tools are specially adapted for left-handed users.

english_meaning: A group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding. A kind, sort, or variety of something.
example_sentence: The giant panda is an endangered species. There are many species of birds in this forest. This particular plant species requires a lot of sunlight. We need to protect all living species on Earth. The biologist discovered a new species of beetle in the Amazon.

english_meaning: Clearly defined or identified. Relating to a particular subject. Precise or exact.
example_sentence: He gave specific instructions on how to use the machine. The money was collected for a specific purpose. She bought a dress for that specific occasion. I have no specific plan for the weekend. They are looking for people with specific skills.

english_meaning: In a precise, definite, or explicit manner. For one particular person, thing, purpose, or reason. Used to identify a more exact example or detail.
example_sentence: The rule specifically mentions mobile phones. This tool was designed specifically for small spaces. She asked specifically for the blue folder. Several fruits, specifically oranges and lemons, contain vitamin C.

english_meaning: A detailed description of the design and materials used to make something. An act of identifying something precisely or stating a precise requirement.
example_sentence: The engineers drew up the specification for the new bridge. We need a detailed specification of the project requirements. The computer meets my hardware specification. They bought the software according to the exact specification. The specification states that the material must be waterproof.

english_meaning: To identify clearly and definitely. To state a fact or requirement clearly and precisely. To include as an item in a specification
example_sentence: Please specify your preferred time for the meeting. The contract does not specify a completion date. You must specify which item you want to order. The recipe specifies using unsalted butter. She did not specify the exact amount of money needed.

english_meaning: A sample used for scientific examination. An example representing a particular type or class. A sample collected for laboratory testing. A model or example used for demonstration. A particular individual of a species used for study.
example_sentence: The scientist examined a plant specimen under the microscope. A blood specimen was collected for laboratory testing. This butterfly specimen is preserved in the museum. The teacher showed a specimen of the mineral to the students.

english_meaning: A visually impressive scene or event. A public display that attracts a lot of attention. Something that causes amazement or strong interest. Something that is very impressive, unusual, or exciting to look at. It can also mean a public display or event that attracts attention.
example_sentence: The fireworks created a beautiful spectacle in the sky. The festival was a grand spectacle. The parade was a colorful spectacle. The sunset was a natural spectacle.

english_meaning: Extremely impressive, striking, or dramatic. Very beautiful or exciting to look at. Remarkably great in degree or effect. An elaborate and impressive show or performance.
example_sentence: The view from the mountain was absolutely spectacular. She made a spectacular recovery after the surgery. The festival ended with a spectacular fireworks display. The theatre staged a musical spectacular last night.

english_meaning: A person who watches an event, show, or activity without participating in it. An onlooker or observer at a public event. One who is present at a performance or game but is not involved directly.
example_sentence: Thousands of spectators lined the streets to watch the annual parade pass by. The stadium was packed with spectators who had come from across the country for the final. She was merely a spectator at the political meeting rather than an active participant. Spectators were asked to remain behind the barriers at all times for their own safety. His approach to life was that of a spectator rather than someone who actively engaged with the world.

english_meaning: To guess or form an opinion without having all the facts. To think about something and form a theory or opinion when you are not sure of the facts. It can also mean investing money in risky business hoping to make a profit.
example_sentence: Scientists speculate about the cause of the disease. People speculate that the company will launch a new phone soon. He speculated in real estate and made a lot of money. We can only speculate about what really happened.

english_meaning: A guess about something without enough evidence or clear knowledge. It means forming ideas, opinions, or theories about something that is uncertain or not fully known. It is often based on limited facts, assumptions, or imagination rather than solid proof. It can also refer to financial investment made with risk in hopes of profit.
example_sentence: There is a lot of speculation about the new policy changes. His resignation led to speculation in the media. People are speculating about the outcome of the election. He made money through real estate speculation.

english_meaning: An instrument used by medical professionals to dilate and examine the inside of a hollow part of the body. A mirror or reflector of polished metal used in optical instruments like telescopes. A bright, distinct patch of color on the wings of certain birds, especially ducks.
example_sentence: The doctor used a speculum to carefully examine the patient's ear canal. The antique reflecting telescope relies on a finely polished metal speculum. You can identify the duck species by looking at the vibrant blue speculum on its wings. The gynecologist ensured that the speculum was properly sterilized and warmed before the procedure. He shone a light through the nasal speculum to check for any obstructions.

english_meaning: To say or write the letters of a word in correct order. To form a word with letters in proper sequence. To signify or indicate something, especially something bad. To bring about a particular result. To be a sign of something that is going to happen. A short period of time during which something lasts. A continuous course or period of an activity. A state of being under a magical influence. Words supposed to have magical power. A strong attraction or fascination that someone or something has.
example_sentence: Can you spell your full name for the registration form? The dark clouds spell trouble for our picnic plans. She had a brief spell of dizziness after standing up too quickly. The wizard cast a spell to protect the village from harm. He worked at the company for a long spell before moving abroad.

english_meaning: To explain something clearly and in detail so that there is no doubt about the meaning. To say or write the letters of a word one by one. To make something completely clear and easy to understand. To state precisely what is required or expected. To describe in a thorough and step-by-step manner.
example_sentence: The teacher asked the student to spell out the difficult word slowly. The manager spelled out the new policy in detail during the meeting. I had to spell out exactly what I expected from the team. The contract spells out the duties of both parties. She spelled out the reasons behind her decision in a long letter.

english_meaning: To hold the complete attention of someone as though by magic. To fascinate or captivate.
example_sentence: The breathtaking performance managed to spellbind the entire audience. He was known for his ability to spellbind listeners with his incredible stories. The intricate details of the ancient ruins spellbind every visitor. A great orator can spellbind a crowd for hours. Her magical voice never fails to spellbind those who hear it.

english_meaning: Forms of words used as a magical charm or incantation. A short or continuous period of time or weather. Writes or names the letters that form a word in correct sequence.
example_sentence: The old witch cast several dark spells on the innocent villagers. He experiences brief spells of dizziness after taking the medication. She always spells her name with a double consonant. The prolonged dry spells completely ruined the crops this year. The ancient book contains powerful spells used by wizards.

english_meaning: A person who spends money carelessly, wastefully, or excessively without thinking about saving or future needs. Someone who has a habit of spending money freely and extravagantly. Such a person often wastes money on unnecessary things and may face financial difficulties because of poor money management. The word can describe a person who is generous beyond reason or someone who lacks self control in spending.
example_sentence: John is a spendthrift who spends most of his salary on luxury items. Her spendthrift habits left her with very little money for emergencies. The family advised the young spendthrift to start saving for the future. Being a spendthrift can lead to serious financial problems over time.

english_meaning: A verse form of nine lines invented by Edmund Spenser. A stanza of eight iambic pentameter lines followed by a longer alexandrine line. A nine-line stanza rhyming ababbcbcc, used in The Faerie Queene.
example_sentence: The poem is written entirely in Spenserian stanzas. Keats used the Spenserian stanza in The Eve of St Agnes. A Spenserian stanza always closes with a longer ninth line. Students analysed the rhyme scheme of the Spenserian stanza.

english_meaning: To forcefully throw out liquid, gas, or words. To eject something in large amounts and with force. It is often used for Liquids like vomit or lava/ Smoke or pollution from factories/ Words or emotions expressed angrily or uncontrollably. It can also be used figuratively for expressing opinions rapidly and without control.
example_sentence: Flames spewed from the aircraft's engine. Massive chimneys were spewing out smoke & flames. He spewed up on the pavement. She spewed up the entire meal.

english_meaning: The butterfly shaped bone at the base of the skull behind the eyes. The bone that joins with almost all the other bones of the skull. A central skull bone that forms part of the eye sockets. The bone that supports the base of the brain and holds the pituitary gland.
example_sentence: The sphenoid bone lies deep within the base of the skull. Its butterfly shape makes the sphenoid bone easy to recognise. The pituitary gland rests in a hollow of the sphenoid bone. Surgeons reach the pituitary gland through the sphenoid bone.

english_meaning: A perfectly round three-dimensional object where every point on the surface is equidistant from the center. A ball-shaped solid figure. An area of activity, interest, or influence. The apparent surface of the heavens.
example_sentence: The Earth is approximately a sphere. A basketball is a perfect sphere. His sphere of influence extends across the region. The planets move in celestial spheres.

english_meaning: Having the form or shape of a sphere or globe. Relating to, or involving a sphere or its properties. Measured or calculated on the surface of a sphere, such as in geometry or astronomy. Appearing perfectly round and symmetrical from all directions. Having a three-dimensional curved surface where all points are equidistant from the center.
example_sentence: The planet Earth is not a perfect cube but is roughly spherical in shape. The bubbles formed a delicate spherical structure as they rose to the surface. Spherical geometry is essential for calculating flight paths over long distances. The crystal ball had a smooth spherical surface that reflected the light.

english_meaning: In a manner that is shaped like a sphere or ball. Relating to or concerning the properties of spheres or geometry on a curved surface. Measured or calculated with respect to a sphere as a frame of reference. Uniformly in all directions originating from a central point. Having a three-dimensional rounded form that is symmetrical.
example_sentence: The planet was described as being spherically symmetrical in its gravitational pull. Light radiated spherically from the explosion, illuminating the entire chamber at once. The particles were arranged spherically around the nucleus to maintain equilibrium. The artist painted the highlights spherically to give the object a three-dimensional appearance.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional object that resembles a sphere but is not perfectly round. A surface of revolution formed by rotating an ellipse about one of its axes. A body that is approximately spherical in shape such as a planet or a grape. A geometric solid having a nearly circular form but slightly flattened or elongated.
example_sentence: The Earth is not a perfect sphere but rather an oblate spheroid due to its rotation. The designer chose a spheroid shape for the new futuristic lamp base. The athlete kicked the leather spheroid down the field towards the goal. High-speed rotation can cause a fluid mass to take the form of a prolate spheroid.

english_meaning: A ring-shaped muscle that surrounds and serves to guard or close an opening or tube. A biological valve that contracts or relaxes to control the passage of substances through a body orifice. A muscular band that maintains constriction of a natural passage. Any circular muscle which maintains the constriction of a body passage or orifice and which relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.
example_sentence: The pyloric sphincter controls the flow of partially digested food from the stomach to the small intestine. Damage to the anal sphincter can result in bowel incontinence issues. When the lower esophageal sphincter fails to close properly, it causes acid reflux. This specific ring of muscle acts as a gatekeeper for various bodily fluids.

english_meaning: A creature from ancient mythology featuring a lion's body and a human head. A colossal stone statue located at Giza in Egypt representing this mythical being. A person who is mysterious or enigmatic and remains difficult to understand or interpret. An insect, specifically a hawk moth, known for its large size and distinctive appearance. Something that is puzzling or acts as a riddle to be solved.
example_sentence: The Great Sphinx of Giza stands as a silent sentinel over the desert sands. He remained a sphinx during the entire negotiation, never revealing his true intentions. Ancient Greek legends describe the sphinx as a treacherous creature that strangled those who could not solve her riddle. The biologist studied the unique markings on the wings of the local sphinx moth.

english_meaning: A vegetable substance used to season food for flavor or aroma. The quality of being exciting, provocative, or interesting. To add a pungent or piquant flavor to something using aromatic substances. To enhance or add variety to something to make it more appealing. A small amount of something that adds a particular character.
example_sentence: She added a pinch of spice to the curry to enhance its aroma. Travel adds a lot of spice to an otherwise dull life. The chef knows exactly how to spice the meat before grilling. They decided to spice up the performance with some energetic music.

english_meaning: To make something more interesting, exciting, or lively. To add excitement, variety, or energy to a situation, relationship, activity, or event that feels dull or routine.
example_sentence: Let’s spice things up at the party with some fun games. She tried to spice things up in her daily routine by learning a new hobby. Adding colorful decorations will really spice things up in the room. They decided to spice things up in their relationship with a weekend getaway.

english_meaning: Extremely clean, neat, and tidy. Fresh, new, and in perfect order. Spotlessly clean and well-organized. Completely free from dirt, dust, or untidiness.
example_sentence: She keeps her kitchen spick and span at all times. The hotel room was spick and span when we arrived. After a whole day of cleaning, the house looked spick and span. His car is always spick and span, inside and out.

english_meaning: Having a piquant, sharp, or pungent taste derived from spices. Containing a large amount of spices or hot peppers that cause a burning sensation. Exciting or intense in flavor or character. Slightly scandalous, risqué, or suggestive in a way that is provocative. Full of spirit, liveliness, or sassiness.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a spicy curry that left everyone reaching for their water glasses. She enjoys reading spicy novels that feature intense romantic subplots. The debate became quite spicy when the candidates started addressing personal grievances. He added a spicy kick to the soup by throwing in some extra chili flakes.

english_meaning: An eight-legged arachnid that spins silk webs to catch its prey. A small predatory creature with two body sections and no wings or antennae. Any member of the order Araneae, most of which produce venom to subdue insects. Figuratively, something that spreads out in a web-like pattern.
example_sentence: A spider had spun its web across the corner of the window. She is afraid of every spider she sees in the house. The spider waited patiently for an insect to touch the web. Most spiders are harmless and help control household pests.

english_meaning: To make something or someone look neat, smart, or attractive. To improve appearance by cleaning, dressing well, or making something look stylish. A small bonus or commission paid to a salesperson for selling a particular product. A financial reward or extra payment given for selling goods, often used in sales jobs.
example_sentence: The store offered a spiff for every phone sold. He earned a spiff after selling the new product line. She spiffed up the room before the guests arrived. He spiffed himself up for the job interview.

english_meaning: To make something or someone look cleaner, neater, or more attractive. To improve appearance by cleaning, decorating, or making something look smarter or more presentable. It is often used for clothes, rooms, or overall appearance before an event or occasion.
example_sentence: She spiffed up her room before the guests arrived. He spiffed up his old car and sold it at a good price. They spiffed up the office for the new manager. I need to spiff up my outfit for the wedding.

english_meaning: Something that is very pleasant, excellent, or enjoyable. It is often used to express approval or satisfaction in a cheerful way. It can describe an event, idea, object, or situation that feels outstanding. Common in British English, especially in older or humorous speech.
example_sentence: That was a spiffing meal at the new restaurant. You’ve done a spiffing job with this project. We had a spiffing time at the beach yesterday. What a spiffing idea for the school event!.

english_meaning: Stylish, neat, and attractive. Something or someone that looks very clean, smart, fashionable, and well-presented. It is often used informally to praise appearance or style.
example_sentence: He wore a spiffy new suit to the wedding. Your car looks really spiffy after the wash. She arrived in a spiffy dress that caught everyone’s attention. The office looks spiffy after renovation.

english_meaning: A thin and pointed piece of metal or wood. A sharp and sudden increase in the magnitude or concentration of something. To pierce or fasten with a sharp point. To secretly add alcohol or drugs to a drink or food.
example_sentence: There was a sudden spike in the number of flu cases this winter. He drove a large metal spike into the wooden board. Be careful that someone does not spike your drink at the club. The athlete wore shoes with spikes for a better grip on the track. Gas prices are expected to spike again before the summer holidays.

english_meaning: A demand for someone to tell the truth or reveal a secret. An informal request to share gossip or hidden information immediately.
synonyms: ["Tell Me","Spill The Beans","Out With It","Confess","Let It Out","Reveal The Secret","Disclose It","Spit It Out","Come Clean","Share The Gossip","Talk"]
antonyms: ["Keep It Secret","Stay Silent","Cover It Up","Hide It","Keep It To Yourself","Keep Mum","Button Your Lip","Conceal It","Suppress It","Keep Quiet"]
example_sentence: I know you have some news about the promotion, so spill it! Come on, spill it, what did she say to you yesterday? You have been acting suspiciously all day, so just spill it. They cornered him and demanded that he finally spill it.

english_meaning: To reveal a secret or disclose confidential information, often unintentionally. To let out information that was supposed to be hidden.
example_sentence: She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party. Don’t spill the beans before the announcement!. He finally spilled the beans about why he was late. If you spill the beans, the whole plan will be ruined.

english_meaning: To share interesting gossip or private information. To reveal the details of a secret or scandal. To tell someone the latest news about people they know. An informal invitation to disclose everything one knows about a situation.
example_sentence: Come on, spill the tea about last night's party. She finally spilled the tea about her new job. Everyone gathered around her to hear her spill the tea. He refused to spill the tea about his friend's engagement.

english_meaning: To tell a long and far-fetched story or tale. To recount a narrative that is often exaggerated or improvised for entertainment. To engage in a lengthy explanation that may be untruthful or elaborate. To weave a complex series of events into an engaging oral account.
example_sentence: The old sailor would often spin a yarn about his adventures on the high seas. Don't let him spin a yarn just to get out of doing his homework. She can spin a yarn so convincing that everyone believes her lies. Grandfather loved to spin a yarn for the children every winter evening.

english_meaning: A vegetable with large dark green leaves. A green, leafy vegetable that is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. It can be eaten raw in salads, cooked as a side dish, or blended into soups and smoothies.
example_sentence: Spinach, corn salad, radishes and carrots are the favourite crops for sowing between others such as lettuces and cauliflowers. I added fresh spinach to my salad. Spinach soup is very healthy. She sautéed spinach with garlic. Spinach is rich in iron and vitamins.

english_meaning: Relating to the spine or backbone. Connected with the spinal cord. Located near or affecting the vertebral column. A shortened form for a spinal anesthetic or spinal injection.
example_sentence: The patient needed a spinal examination after the accident. A spinal injury can affect movement and feeling. The surgeon discussed the risks of spinal anesthesia. The hospital ordered a scan of the spinal column.

english_meaning: The long, thin bundle of nerve tissue that runs down the back inside the vertebral column. The main pathway that carries messages between the brain and the rest of the body. The structure responsible for reflex actions that occur without involving the brain.
example_sentence: The spinal cord runs from the brainstem to the lower back. An injury to the spinal cord may cause paralysis. Reflex actions are handled directly by the spinal cord. The spinal cord is protected by the bones of the backbone.

english_meaning: Any of the thirty-one pairs of nerves that branch out from the spinal cord. A mixed nerve that carries both sensory messages towards the cord and motor commands away from it. A nerve that leaves the backbone through a gap between two vertebrae to supply the trunk and limbs.
example_sentence: Thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves leave the spinal cord. A slipped disc can press on a spinal nerve. Each spinal nerve serves a particular area of skin. Pain in the leg may come from an irritated spinal nerve.

english_meaning: Long, thin, and appearing weak or fragile. Having slender limbs or stems that look unable to give support. Tall and thin in an unhealthy or awkward way.
example_sentence: The newborn calf stood on spindly legs. Spindly plants grew in the shaded corner of the garden. He was a spindly boy who later grew strong. The old table rested on four spindly wooden legs.

english_meaning: The row of bones running down the back of the body. The backbone or vertebral column. The central supporting structure of something such as a book or leaf. A sharp pointed projection on a plant or animal. Courage, firmness, or moral strength.
example_sentence: The injury affected several bones in his spine. The title was printed on the spine of the book. Some desert plants have sharp spines instead of leaves. She showed real spine during the difficult negotiations.

english_meaning: A large, three-cornered sail set forward of the mainsail of a yacht when running before the wind. A bulging front sail used specifically to catch a favorable wind and increase speed.
example_sentence: The crew hoisted the spinnaker as the yacht turned downwind. A brightly colored spinnaker caught the wind, propelling the boat forward. Handling a large spinnaker requires skill and coordination from the sailors. When the wind dropped, the spinnaker collapsed and lost its shape. They deployed the spinnaker to maximize their speed during the sailing race.

english_meaning: A person who spins fibre into thread or yarn. A machine or part that rotates or spins. In cricket, a bowler who makes the ball turn sharply off the pitch. A small revolving lure used in fishing, or a spinning toy.
example_sentence: The village spinner produced fine woollen thread. Their leg spinner took four wickets today. He attached a bright spinner to his fishing line. The child kept the spinner turning on the table.

english_meaning: A small wood or a small group of trees growing close together. A small area of woodland, usually consisting of trees and bushes growing together. It is smaller than a forest or a wood and is often found in rural areas, parks, farmland, or countryside landscapes. Spinneys can provide shelter for birds and wildlife.
example_sentence: The deer disappeared into a small spinney beside the field. Birds were nesting safely in the spinney behind the farmhouse. We stopped for a picnic near a spinney of oak trees. The fox emerged from the spinney just before sunset.

english_meaning: An unmarried woman. An older woman beyond the usual age for marriage. A woman whose occupation is to spin thread.
example_sentence: She remained a spinster all her life and dedicated her time to charity. In old novels, a spinster was often depicted as a lonely and bitter woman. The proud spinster refused to marry just for the sake of social conventions. My aunt is a wealthy spinster who travels the world alone. The term spinster originally referred to a woman who spun thread for a living.

english_meaning: A curve that winds around a central point while moving continuously away from or towards it. Shaped like a coil or winding curve. To move in a continuous curve around a central point, especially while rising or falling. To increase or decrease rapidly and in an uncontrolled way. A continuous harmful rise or fall in prices, wages, or a situation.
example_sentence: The smoke rose in a slow spiral above the fire. The staircase has a beautiful spiral design. Prices continued to spiral out of control. His health began to spiral downwards after the accident.

english_meaning: The non-physical part of a person which is the seat of emotions and character. A supernatural being such as a ghost or an entity without a physical body. The prevailing mood, attitude, or quality that characterizes a group or a period of time. The true intention or meaning of something as opposed to its literal interpretation. A strong distilled alcoholic drink such as whiskey or gin. Courage, energy, and determination displayed by a person.
example_sentence: The team played with great spirit despite losing the match. Many cultures believe that the spirit lives on after the body dies. We must follow the spirit of the law, not just its literal words. She felt a presence in the room as if a restless spirit were watching her.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things. Having a relationship based on a profound sense of aspects of life that are not physical. Relating to religion or religious belief. Showing great refinement and high mindedness. Deeply religious or highly dedicated to a way of life that focuses on the soul. Having a mind or soul that is elevated above worldly interests.
example_sentence: Many people turn to yoga for their spiritual well-being. The monastery provides a quiet space for spiritual reflection. He claims to have a spiritual connection with the natural world. The priest offered spiritual guidance to the grieving family.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the human spirit or soul rather than the body. With regard to religious faith and inner belief. In a manner concerned with deeper meaning and inner peace. In terms of moral and emotional wellbeing rather than material things. From a non-physical or sacred point of view.
example_sentence: The journey changed him spiritually as well as physically. She feels spiritually connected to the mountains. Fasting is spiritually rewarding for many believers. The two friends grew spiritually closer over the years.

english_meaning: To eject saliva from the mouth. To force liquid, especially saliva, from the mouth. To express strong dislike or anger by ejecting saliva. The substance (saliva) ejected from the mouth. A narrow point of land projecting into water (less common). To speak angrily or harshly, A long thin metal rod used to roast meat over fire. Small drops of rain or spray. A slight quarrel or short argument
example_sentence: She took a mouthful of food & then suddenly spat it out. He was spitting blood from a badly cut lip. She spat in his face & went out. He was dragged out of the court spitting abuse at the judge & jury. The angry boy spat at the wall. She spat out the sour fruit. The fire began to spit sparks. It started to spit rain in the evening.

english_meaning: A small ball of chewed paper, often thrown or shot through a tube as a prank, especially by schoolchildren. In baseball, an illegal pitch made by applying saliva or another substance to the ball to alter its movement. Informally, to suggest or brainstorm ideas casually, without commitment, especially in a meeting or discussion.
example_sentence: The students got in trouble for throwing spitballs across the classroom.  The pitcher was suspended for throwing an illegal spitball.  Let's spitball some ideas before we settle on a final plan.  He flicked a spitball at his friend when the teacher wasn't looking.  The team spent the morning spitballing creative solutions to the problem.

english_meaning: Having or showing a desire to harm, anger, or defeat someone. Full of spite or malice. Showing or caused by malicious intent to hurt another person.
example_sentence: She was a spiteful child who loved causing trouble. His spiteful remarks hurt her deeply. I do not want to sound spiteful, but I am glad he failed. The sisters remained spiteful toward each other for years. He took a spiteful revenge on his former boss.

english_meaning: Saliva that comes out of the mouth, often when someone spits. The watery fluid produced in the mouth by salivary glands. It may come out while speaking, coughing, or intentionally spitting. It can also refer to drops of saliva that accidentally spray while talking.
example_sentence: The angry man shouted and spittle flew from his mouth. A drop of spittle landed on the ground as he spoke loudly. The boxer wiped the spittle from his lips between rounds. The child accidentally sprayed spittle while laughing.

english_meaning: The sound or movement of liquid striking or being scattered. A small quantity of liquid that falls or is thrown onto something. A striking, noticeable display or effect. To scatter liquid on a surface. To move through water noisily.
example_sentence: The stone fell into the river with a loud splash. She added a splash of milk to her coffee. The new product made a splash in the tech market. Children love to splash water at each other in the pool. Rain splashed against the window all night.

english_meaning: To spend a lot of money on something expensive or enjoyable.
example_sentence: They splashed out on a luxury car. I splashed out for my birthday dinner. She splashed out on a designer dress. We decided to splash out on a holiday abroad.

english_meaning: To spread out, expand, or move apart, especially outward from a center. A slope, spread, or widening. Spread or turned outward.
example_sentence: He splayed his fingers on the table while thinking deeply. The branches of the tree splayed out in all directions She slipped, and her legs splayed awkwardly on the floor. The carpenter made a splay in the window frame to let in more light.

english_meaning: A small organ near the stomach that controls the quality of the blood cells. An intense emotional state of displeasure with someone or something.
example_sentence: He vented his spleen (= shouted in an angry way) on the assembled crowd. Symptoms of the disease include an enlarged spleen or liver. I feel much better now I've vented my spleen on this subject.

english_meaning: Very good, excellent, very impressive, very beautiful
example_sentence: The hotel stands in splendid isolation surrounded by moorland.

english_meaning: A small, thin, sharp piece of wood, glass, metal, or similar material broken off from a larger object. To break or split into small, thin, sharp pieces. To cause something to break into fragments. A small fragment that has separated from a whole. To divide or separate into smaller hostile groups, especially of a political or social organisation. A splinter is a tiny, sharp piece that breaks off from a hard material such as wood, bone, or stone, often becoming stuck in the skin and causing pain.
example_sentence: He got a tiny splinter of wood stuck in his finger while moving the old furniture. The vase shattered into countless splinters when it fell on the marble floor. The old wooden bench has begun to splinter and needs to be replaced. A small splinter group broke away from the main political party last year. She used tweezers to carefully remove the splinter from her child's foot.

english_meaning: To insert a word between to and the base form of a verb. To separate the two parts of a to-infinitive with an adverb or another word. A grammatical construction in which the infinitive marker to is separated from its following verb. To interrupt an infinitive phrase by placing a modifier between to and the verb. A structure commonly used to make the meaning of a sentence clearer, stronger, or more natural. A construction traditionally criticized by some grammar authorities, although it is widely accepted in modern English. A way of placing an adverb exactly where its meaning is most clearly connected to the verb. A grammatical choice in which an infinitive such as to go becomes to quickly go. A construction that can sometimes be avoided by moving the adverb elsewhere, although the resulting sentence may sound less natural. The term does not mean that the verb itself is divided; it means that to and the verb are separated by another word.
synonyms: ["Split infinitive","Insert an adverb","Separate an infinitive","Grammar construction","Infinitive separation"]
antonyms: ["Keep an infinitive together","Unsplit infinitive","Join the infinitive","Avoid separation"]
example_sentence: In the phrase to clearly explain, clearly splits the infinitive. Some teachers once told students not to split an infinitive. Modern English often accepts split infinitives when they sound natural. She chose to carefully review the contract. It is not always wrong to split an infinitive.

english_meaning: To break something into parts or to end a relationship or partnership. It can refer to people going their separate ways or dividing something into smaller sections.
example_sentence: The band split up after ten years. They split up because of differences. Let’s split up into groups for the project. The couple decided to split up last month.

english_meaning: To spend a lot of money freely. To indulge oneself by spending extravagantly or luxuriously, often on something non-essential or for pleasure. An act of spending a lot freely.
example_sentence: She decided to splurge on a designer handbag. He splurged on a weekend trip to the mountains. They splurged at the new restaurant downtown. After getting his bonus, he splurged on a new watch. That vacation was quite a splurge. Her shopping splurge lasted the whole day.

english_meaning: To damage or ruin something. To ruin plans or opportunities. To make an experience unpleasant. To become stale or rotten. To overindulge a child or pet. To take valuable goods by force after war or victory (an older or literary meaning). To weaken the quality or appearance of something.
example_sentence: Too much sunlight can spoil fresh vegetables. The surprise party was spoiled when someone revealed the secret. Parents should avoid spoiling their children with expensive toys. The meat spoiled because it was not refrigerated properly.

english_meaning: The process by which food, goods, or materials become damaged, rotten, or unfit for use due to the action of bacteria, mold, time, or improper storage. The loss or waste resulting from decay or damage. It can also refer to the amount of material wasted or rendered unusable during a production or storage process.
example_sentence: Proper refrigeration helps reduce food spoilage significantly. The supermarket suffered heavy losses due to spoilage of fresh produce. Spoilage of the cargo during transportation caused major financial damage. Farmers in hot climates face the constant problem of spoilage. The company introduced better packaging to minimise spoilage during shipping.

english_meaning: Damaged, decayed, or no longer fit for use. Used to describe food that has gone bad and is no longer safe to eat. Also used to describe a child who has been excessively indulged and has become selfish or demanding as a result. In American English, it is the preferred past tense and past participle of spoil.
example_sentence: The spoiled meat had a foul smell and had to be discarded. Growing up as the only child, he was somewhat spoiled by his parents. The fresh vegetables we bought yesterday are already spoiled. She realised the trip had been spoiled by the constant arguments. A spoiled child often struggles to adapt to the demands of adult life.

english_meaning: A person or thing that spoils or ruins something. Someone who reveals important plot details of a film, book, or show before others have had the chance to experience it. A device fitted to a vehicle, especially a racing car or aircraft, to improve aerodynamic performance by reducing drag or increasing stability. It can also refer to a candidate in an election who has little chance of winning but takes votes away from a stronger candidate.
example_sentence: He posted a spoiler about the film's ending before most people had seen it. The aerodynamic spoiler on the racing car helps keep it stable at high speeds. Please do not post any spoilers in the comment section. The third-party candidate acted as a spoiler in the election by drawing votes away from both major parties. She was furious when her friend revealed a major spoiler about the series finale.

english_meaning: Damaged, ruined, or made unfit for use or enjoyment. Used to describe a child who has been given too much by parents and has developed selfish or demanding behaviour. Also used in British English as the past tense and past participle of the verb spoil. Something that has been harmed, wasted, or impaired in quality or condition.
example_sentence: The milk was spoilt because it had been left out of the fridge overnight. He was a spoilt child who always demanded whatever he wanted. The heavy rain spoilt our picnic completely. The spoilt food had to be thrown away immediately. Her spoilt behaviour made it difficult for others to get along with her.

english_meaning: To absorb liquid. To depend on others unfairly for support. A soft, porous material that absorbs water or liquid. A sea animal with a soft body and many tiny holes. A person who depends on others for money, food, or support. A cleaning item used for washing dishes, walls, or surfaces. To clean something with a sponge.
example_sentence: She used a sponge to clean the table. The sponge absorbed all the spilled water quickly. Sea sponges live deep in the ocean. She sponged the wall carefully. The cloth sponged up the milk. He always sponges off his relatives.

english_meaning: A person who lives by depending on others for money, food, help, or support without giving anything in return. Someone who unfairly takes advantage of the kindness, money, food, or support of other people. Such a person usually avoids responsibility and depends on others for personal benefit. The word is often used negatively to describe a lazy or selfish person.
example_sentence: He became a sponger after losing interest in work. Nobody liked the sponger who always borrowed money and never returned it. Her family asked the sponger to become responsible and earn a living. A true friend helps others, not a sponger who only takes advantage.

english_meaning: Resembling a sponge in being soft, porous, and easily compressed. Capable of absorbing liquid readily. Having a light, airy, or yielding physical texture. Soft and full of cavities or microscopic holes. Lacking firmness or solid structural density.
example_sentence: The ground became spongy after the heavy rain. She baked a delicious cake with a light and spongy texture. The doctor examined the spongy bone tissue under a microscope. He stepped on a spongy moss covered log in the damp forest.
