english_meaning: A person or organization that provides funds for a project or activity carried out by another. A person who introduces and supports a proposal for legislation. A godparent at a child's baptism. To provide financial or material support for an event, activity, or person. To propose and advocate for a new legislative bill or initiative.
example_sentence: The local bank agreed to sponsor the upcoming charity marathon. She needed to find a sponsor to fund her research project. Several senators will sponsor the new environmental protection bill. The company serves as a proud sponsor of the national football team.

english_meaning: The financial support or funding provided by a sponsor for an event, person, or organization. The act of endorsing, supporting, or underwriting a project or activity. The position or responsibility assumed by a person who acts as a sponsor. The official backing given to an individual, especially for immigration or legal purposes. The provision of resources in exchange for advertising or promotional benefits.
example_sentence: The local football team relies heavily on corporate sponsorship to buy equipment. She moved to the country under the sponsorship of her current employer. The festival was organized with the generous sponsorship of several local businesses. Seeking sponsorship for the charity event proved to be a difficult task this year.

english_meaning: Done or occurring naturally without planning or external cause. Something that happens on its own, unplanned, impulsive, or arising from natural feelings rather than thought or premeditation.
example_sentence: She made a spontaneous decision to travel abroad. The children broke into spontaneous laughter. His spontaneous reaction surprised everyone. The audience gave a spontaneous standing ovation.

english_meaning: Occurring as a result of a sudden impulse and without premeditation or external stimulus. Happening or done in a natural, often sudden way, without any planning or without being forced. Voluntarily and without prompting.
example_sentence: They spontaneously started dancing when the music played. The audience erupted spontaneously into loud applause. He spontaneously offered to pay for everyone's dinner. The chemical reaction occurs spontaneously at room temperature. The bleeding stopped spontaneously after a few minutes.

english_meaning: To imitate something humorously or to trick someone by creating a fake message, call, or signal. The action can be playful or deceptive depending on context. A humorous imitation or a fake message made to trick someone. A playful imitation created to make people laugh or to poke fun at something.
example_sentence: The comedian spoofed the president’s speech on live television. The show spoofed the latest blockbuster movie. They made a spoof of the movie. The show spoofed political ads. He created a spoof video. That clip was a spoof of a news report.

english_meaning: The act of imitating something in a humorous or mocking way. The practice of disguising a communication so that it appears to come from a trusted source. Deceiving a system or person by faking an identity, address, or signal.
example_sentence: Email spoofing tricks users into sharing passwords. The show is famous for spoofing popular films. Caller ID spoofing has become a common scam. Banks warn customers about website spoofing.

english_meaning: Happening occasionally, not regularly. Occurring at irregular intervals, scattered or isolated in time or space. It describes events or actions that are unpredictable and infrequent rather than continuous.
example_sentence: He has sporadic attendance at the gym, going only when he feels motivated. The region experiences sporadic rainfall throughout the year. There were sporadic power outages in the city last week. Her involvement in the project has been sporadic, showing up only for key meetings.

english_meaning: Occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places. Scattered or isolated in occurrence. Happening occasionally rather than continuously.
example_sentence: It rains sporadically in this part of the country. She attended the meetings sporadically. Gunfire could be heard sporadically throughout the night. The disease occurs sporadically but is rarely fatal. He has worked sporadically since he graduated.

english_meaning: A tiny reproductive unit produced by fungi, algae, mosses, ferns, and some other organisms, capable of developing without fusion with another cell. A resistant dormant body formed by certain bacteria or other organisms to survive harsh conditions. To produce or release spores.
example_sentence: The fungus releases spores into the air. Bacterial spores can survive extreme heat. Fern spores spread on the wind. The mould began to spore in the damp room.

english_meaning: Having or bearing spores. Characterized by the production of spores. Produced or yielded spores as a method of reproduction.
example_sentence: The spored ferns survived the harsh winter conditions. Certain spored bacteria can remain dormant for years. The fungus spored profusely and spread across the damp wood. Airborne spored organisms are responsible for spreading the plant disease. The biologist examined the spored leaves under a high-powered microscope.

english_meaning: A handheld eating utensil combining features of a spoon and a fork. A spoon-shaped implement with short fork-like points at its tip. An informal verb meaning to eat, serve, or handle food with a spork.
example_sentence: I used a spork to eat the rice and vegetables. The camping set includes a metal spork. She packed a reusable spork in her lunch bag. He sporked the soft noodles straight from the bowl.

english_meaning: A pouch worn in front of a Scottish kilt. A traditional part of Scottish Highland dress used because a kilt has no pockets. A decorative or practical leather or fur pouch suspended from a belt or chain around the waist.
example_sentence: He wore a leather sporran with his kilt. The ceremonial sporran was decorated with silver. She placed the small key inside the sporran. A chain held the sporran securely at the front of his waist.

english_meaning: Marked with spots. Having blotches of two or more colors. To mark with small spots especially unevenly. To make note of (something) through the use of one's eyes. To cover by or as if by scattering something over or on.
example_sentence: They spotted niche in the market. She glanced out the window and spotted the Arch.

english_meaning: To pour out or gush. To eject liquid, words, or other things forcefully in a stream. Often used for liquid, speech, or ideas. A tube or lip through which liquid flows. The projecting part of a container like a teapot, jug, or kettle from which liquid can pour.
example_sentence: The river spouted from the mountain spring. He spouted his opinions without thinking. Water spouted from the broken pipe. The kettle has a long spout for easy pouring. Fill water into the pot and pour through the spout carefully. The fountain’s spout sprays water high into the air.

english_meaning: An injury to a ligament caused by sudden twisting, stretching, or tearing, usually affecting joints such as the ankle, wrist, or knee, without breaking any bone. To injure a joint in this way. A common joint injury in which the ligaments connecting bones are overstretched or partially torn, causing pain, swelling, bruising, and temporary loss of normal movement in the affected area.
example_sentence: She suffered a painful sprain in her ankle after slipping on the wet floor. The doctor told him that it was only a mild sprain and would heal within a week. A sprain should be treated with rest, ice, compression, and elevation. He had to miss the match because of a sprain in his right wrist. Be careful while running on rough ground, as you can easily sprain your ankle.

english_meaning: The act of injuring a joint, especially the ankle, wrist, or knee, by suddenly twisting or stretching its ligaments beyond their normal range without causing a bone fracture. The process of causing a painful injury to a joint through sudden movement. Spraining refers to the action of damaging the ligaments around a joint by twisting or wrenching it sharply, which often results in swelling, pain, and difficulty in moving the affected part.
example_sentence: He kept spraining his ankle every time he tried to play football on uneven ground. Spraining a wrist while skating is a very common injury among beginners. The doctor warned her against spraining the same knee again so soon after the first injury. She fell from the staircase, spraining her ankle quite badly in the process. Spraining your joints repeatedly can lead to long-term weakness if not treated properly.

english_meaning: The past tense of the spring. It describes a sudden movement upward or forward, or the act of appearing or developing quickly. It can also refer to something that arose or originated from a specific source.
example_sentence: The cat suddenly sprang from the bushes to catch the toy. A leak sprang in the pipe during the middle of the night. New businesses sprang up all over the city after the economic boom. He sprang to his feet when he heard the national anthem.

english_meaning: To spread the arms and legs out carelessly and untidily while sitting or lying down. To sit, lie or fall with your arms and legs spread out in a relaxed or careless way. To spread out  awkwardly over a large area. To spread in an untidy way, to cover a large area. A large area covered with buildings that spreads from the city into the countryside in an ugly way.
example_sentence:
He was sprawling in an armchair in front of the TV.
Something hit her and sent her sprawling to the ground. I tripped and went sprawling. The town sprawled along the side of the lake. I knocked into her in the corridor and sent her sprawling (= knocked her over). The refugee camps sprawl across the landscape. The urban sprawl of South Florida. Jamie came home from school and sprawled on the couch.

english_meaning: Spreading out over a large area in an untidy or irregular way. (Of a city) covered with buildings across a large area, often ones that have been added gradually over a period of time. Existing or reaching over a large area.
example_sentence: Bushes Sprawling along the road. Somewhere in this sprawling metropolis, there is a secret military laboratory. The sprawling medical school campus is on the grounds of a former naval academy. She moves into Manuela's tiny shack in one of the city's sprawling slums. There were weeds sprawling in the yard.

english_meaning: To open something out so it covers a larger area. To move or extend over a wider area or among more people. To distribute a substance in a thin layer over a surface. To make information, news, or feelings known to many people. A soft food that can be applied in a layer to bread or crackers.
example_sentence: She spread a warm blanket over the sleeping child. The fire spread quickly through the dry forest. News of his success spread throughout the town. He spread butter evenly on his toast.

english_meaning: A short period of uncontrolled or excessive activity, spending, or enjoyment. A short but intense period when someone does something excessively, often without control or concern for consequences. It is commonly used for spending money, shopping, partying, eating, or even crime.
example_sentence: She went on a shopping spree after receiving her bonus. The children enjoyed a weekend ice cream spree. He admitted to a spending spree that emptied his savings. The police stopped a crime spree in the city.

english_meaning: A small stem with leaves or flowers cut from a plant. A small shoot or twig used for decoration or garnish. A young person, humorously.
example_sentence: Add a sprig of mint to the lemonade. The plate was decorated with a sprig of parsley. She wore a sprig of jasmine in her hair. Garnish the soup with a sprig of coriander.

english_meaning: The season of the year between winter and summer when plants begin to grow. It also refers to a resilient metal coil that returns to its shape after being compressed. To move suddenly or rapidly upward or forward.
example_sentence: Flowers begin to bloom beautifully during the early days of spring. The mattress was old and one of the metal springs was poking through. If you press the button, the hidden compartment will spring open. A cool mountain spring provided fresh water for the hikers.

english_meaning: To develop a hole or crack that lets liquid or gas escape. To make a trap for catching animals close suddenly. To try to trick somebody into doing or saying something.
example_sentence: The boat sprang a leak during the storm. ⚙️ The old water tank sprang a leak, and the whole floor was flooded. The boat sprang a leak during the storm and began to sink. The company’s finances sprang a leak after poor management.

english_meaning: To suddenly set off a trap or to deceive or catch someone unexpectedly, especially by trick or plan. It means you create a situation to trap someone, physically or mentally, when they least expect it.
example_sentence: The hunters sprang a trap for the fox. The police sprang a trap to catch the smugglers at midnight. He sprang a trap for his enemies by pretending to be weak. The company sprang a trap on the thief with hidden cameras. They sprang a trap to expose the corrupt officer taking bribes.

english_meaning: A young person, especially someone full of energy and vitality. It is often used in a negative way to say that someone is no longer young. Refers to a young and energetic person. The phrase is commonly used humorously or politely to describe someone who is getting older and is not as young as before.
example_sentence: My grandfather still works every day, but he admits he is no spring chicken. She may not be a spring chicken, yet she dances beautifully. The coach is no spring chicken, but he remains very active. At fifty, he is not exactly a spring chicken anymore.

english_meaning: To pay for something for somebody else. To pay for or buy something, often for someone else. To pay for; treat someone to.
example_sentence: I'll spring for the drinks tonight. They offered to spring for the tickets. To increase the radio's performance, spring for a powered antenna.

english_meaning: To be caused by something; to start from something. To appear suddenly and unexpectedly from a particular place. To come from or be a result of something.
example_sentence: The idea for the novel sprang from a trip to India. Where on earth did you spring from? His need to be liked obviously springs from a deep-rooted insecurity.

english_meaning:
o suddenly begin doing something actively or with energy, especially after being inactive or waiting.
It means to start working quickly and energetically when the time comes.
example_sentence: The firefighters sprang into action when the alarm rang. Let's go!’ he said, springing into action. The town springs to life (= becomes busy) during the carnival. The rescue workers sprang into action after hearing about the flood. When the opportunity came, he sprang into action to prove his abilities.

english_meaning: To suddenly become active, energetic, or full of movement after being quiet or inactive. A situation, place, or person that quickly becomes lively or starts working energetically.
example_sentence: The market sprang into life after the festival. The town springs into life (= becomes busy) during the carnival. The quiet village sprang into life when the festival began. The crowd sprang into life as soon as the singer stepped onto the stage.

english_meaning: A young onion with a small white bulb and long green stalks. A vegetable eaten raw in salads or used as a garnish. The plant harvested before the bulb fully develops. A mild flavouring used in soups, stir-fries, and salads.
example_sentence: He sprinkled chopped spring onion over the soup. Spring onions grow easily in a small pot. The salad was garnished with spring onion rings. She used both the white and green parts.

english_meaning: To suddenly become lively, active, or energetic after being quiet or inactive. To come alive. To show energy, excitement, or movement.
example_sentence:
The crowd sprang to life when the singer arrived. 
The town springs to life (= becomes busy) during the carnival. The park sprang to life when the children started playing and laughing. The city sprang to life as soon as the festival began. After the power was restored, the whole house sprang to life again.

english_meaning: To come quickly into your thoughts or memory. Suddenly remember or think of it. To be remembered suddenly, or to occur in someone’s thoughts.
synonyms: ["Come to mind","Occur to (someone)","Remember suddenly","Recall quickly","Pop up in mind"]
example_sentence: I'm sure someone can help you, but no one immediately springs to mind. When you mention honesty, my grandfather immediately springs to mind.

english_meaning: To appear or develop quickly and/or suddenly. To suddenly appear or begin to exist. To start to exist suddenly.
example_sentence: Play areas for children are springing up all over the place. Opposition groups are springing up like mushrooms. New theatres and arts centres sprang up all over the country.

english_meaning: A flexible board used for jumping high in diving or gymnastics. Something that helps someone start or advance a career or activity. A base or opportunity for further success. A source of inspiration or motivation to begin something. A launching point for progress or achievement.
example_sentence: The diver leapt from the springboard into the pool. The scholarship became a springboard for her career. His first novel served as a springboard for greater success. Volunteering can be a springboard to full-time employment.

english_meaning: To scatter small drops or particles of a substance over an object or surface. A small quantity of something gently scattered. A brief and light rain. To distribute something in small amounts
example_sentence: She decided to sprinkle some powdered sugar on the freshly baked cake. A light sprinkle began to fall as we walked towards the park. The gardener will sprinkle water on the newly planted vegetable seeds. He always likes to sprinkle his long speeches with a few jokes. Be sure to sprinkle a little salt over the dish before serving.

english_meaning: To run very fast for a short distance or short period of time. Used when someone runs at maximum speed for a short distance. It can also describe any quick burst of effort or speed in work, sports, studies, or activities.
example_sentence: The athlete sprinted toward the finish line with great energy. She had to sprint to catch the school bus. The football player made a quick sprint across the field. We finished the project in a final sprint before the deadline.

english_meaning: An athlete who races over short distances. A person who runs at full speed over a short distance.
example_sentence: Usain Bolt is considered the greatest sprinter of all time. The young sprinter broke the national record for the 100-meter dash. She trained hard every day to become a professional sprinter. The sprinter pulled a muscle right before the finish line. A good sprinter needs immense explosive power and speed.

english_meaning: To put forth shoots. To begin to grow or develop rapidly. A newly grown shoot or bud of a plant.
example_sentence: The seeds began to sprout after a few days of rain. New businesses are starting to sprout up all over the city. A few grey hairs had begun to sprout on his chin. We ate fresh bean sprouts with our dinner.

english_meaning: To make neat or attractive. To improve appearance, especially by cleaning or decorating. A type of tree. An evergreen tree with needle-like leaves and cones, commonly found in cold regions Someone or something that is well-groomed, tidy, and stylish in appearance
example_sentence: He spruced up the living room before guests arrived. She spruced her resume before the interview. A spruce tree stood tall in the garden. Spruces are common in northern forests. He looked very spruce in his new suit. She kept her office spruce and organized.

english_meaning: Courage and determination, especially in a small or weak person. Spirit, pluck, and liveliness of character. The willingness to face difficulty without fear. A spark or piece of tinder used to light a fire.
example_sentence: The little girl showed real spunk in the final race. It takes spunk to speak up against your own team. I admire her spunk and honesty. He lost his spunk after the long illness.

english_meaning: Something that encourages or motivates action. A sharp pointed device worn on boots by riders. A small branch or extension of something such as road or railway. To encourage someone to do something faster or better.
example_sentence: His success was a spur to work harder. The rider used his spur to guide the horse. A spur road connects the village to the highway. The coach tried to spur the team to victory.

english_meaning: False or fake. Something that looks real or true but is actually false, not genuine, or based on wrong information. Often used for claims, arguments, reports, or products.
example_sentence: The report was based on spurious data. He made a spurious claim to gain public support. The police dismissed the spurious accusations. Scientists rejected the theory as spurious and unreliable.

english_meaning: To reject something or someone with contempt, scorn, or disdain. To refuse to accept an offer, advice, gift, or person in a proud or disrespectful manner. To push or kick away with the foot. To turn down a proposal or chance in a way that shows disrespect or strong dislike.
example_sentence: She spurned his offer of friendship without a second thought. He spurned the bribe and reported the matter to the police. The proud queen spurned every suitor who approached her. They spurned all attempts at reconciliation. The critics spurned the new film as shallow and predictable.

english_meaning: To secretly watch someone. To notice something suddenly. To observe carefully without being seen. A person who secretly collects information about others. Someone who works for a government to obtain secret information. A person who watches others secretly
example_sentence: The spy collected secret information about the enemy. She felt someone was spying on her. He spied a bird sitting on the tree. The government sent a spy to investigate the case.

english_meaning: To secretly watch or observe someone or something. To gather information about someone without their knowledge. To keep someone under surveillance. To monitor a person’s activities secretly. To act as a spy against another person or group.
example_sentence: He was accused of spying on his neighbors. The government was spying on political activists. She caught her brother spying on her through the window. Companies sometimes spy on their competitors to gain an advantage.

english_meaning: To secretly discover information about a place, person, or situation. To explore or examine somewhere in a hidden manner. To gather intelligence by careful observation. To scout out details for a particular purpose. To find out something by covert investigation.
example_sentence: The soldiers were sent to spy out the enemy’s position. He tried to spy out the plans of his rivals. They spied out the land before setting up camp. She managed to spy out the weaknesses in their strategy.

english_meaning: A person who directs or controls a network of spies. The head or leader of an intelligence organization. Someone in charge of espionage activities. A senior officer who manages secret agents. A chief who plans and oversees spy operations.
example_sentence: He served as the country’s spymaster during the war. The spymaster carefully planned every mission. A skilled spymaster must be intelligent and cautious. She was appointed as the new spymaster of the intelligence agency.

english_meaning: Software installed on a computer secretly to collect information about the user. A type of malicious program designed to spy on user activity. A program that transmits data from a device without the user’s knowledge. Software used for unauthorized surveillance of digital activities. A hidden application that tracks online behavior.
example_sentence: He installed antivirus software to protect his laptop from spyware. Spyware can steal passwords and personal information. The company was fined for distributing spyware to its customers. Always scan downloaded files to check for spyware.

english_meaning: A young unfledged pigeon or other similar bird especially one used as food. A short fat or thickset person. A stuffed cushion or a thickly padded back of a car or sofa. Short, fat, or bulky in physical appearance. To fall or strike with a heavy dull sound.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a roasted squab served with seasonal root vegetables. She rested her head against the comfortable leather squab of the armchair. The squab toddler waddled across the floor to reach his toy. A heavy sack of grain fell squab onto the wooden porch.

english_meaning: A small, noisy argument over something unimportant. A petty argument or fight, usually loud but not serious, often about trivial issues. It can happen between children, friends, family members, or even groups. To argue noisily about something small or unimportant.
example_sentence: The children had a squabble over who would use the computer first. A minor squabble broke out between the neighbors about parking space. The meeting was delayed because of a squabble among team members. The children squabbled over a broken toy. Colleagues should not squabble during important meetings.

english_meaning: A small group of people having a particular task. A tactical subdivision of a military platoon. A sports team or a section of a police force. A group of close friends who spend time together. A specialized unit of personnel assembled for a specific purpose.
example_sentence: The bomb disposal squad arrived quickly at the scene. The coach announced the starting squad for the championship match. A military squad was sent to patrol the borders. She went to the mall to hang out with her squad.

english_meaning: An informal British word for an ordinary soldier of low rank. A private in the army rather than an officer. A member of a squad, especially a new or junior recruit. Slang used affectionately or humorously for a common foot soldier.
example_sentence: The young squaddie had only been in the army for six months. Squaddies were seen loading supplies onto the trucks. He joined up at eighteen and served as an ordinary squaddie. The film shows the daily life of a British squaddie.

english_meaning: A large organized unit of military forces, often used for aircraft, ships or cavalry. In detail, it is a tactical group made up of several smaller units that operate together under one commander, usually in air forces and naval forces.
example_sentence: The squadron took off at sunrise for the training mission. A squadron of ships moved toward the coastline. The commander inspected the entire squadron before the operation. The rescue squadron responded quickly during the emergency.

english_meaning: Extremely dirty, unpleasant, and neglected, especially because of poverty. Describing living conditions that are filthy and run-down. Morally low, shameful, or lacking in decency. Sordid and unworthy of respect.
example_sentence: Thousands of families live in squalid conditions near the canal. The room was small, dark, and squalid. He was ashamed of his squalid behaviour towards his friends. Reporters described the squalid state of the old prison.

english_meaning: A sudden violent gust of wind, often with rain, snow, or sleet. A short, fierce storm that arrives without warning. A loud harsh cry, especially by a baby or young child. To cry out loudly and harshly.
example_sentence: A sudden squall overturned two small boats in the harbour. The picnic was ruined by a squall of wind and rain. The baby let out a loud squall in the middle of the night. Sailors watched the horizon for approaching squalls.

english_meaning: Marked by sudden strong gusts of wind and rain. Describing weather that is stormy and changeable. Rough and unsettled, especially at sea. Occasionally used for a situation that is turbulent or difficult.
example_sentence: The forecast warns of squally showers along the coast. It was a squally night and the boats stayed in harbour. Squally weather delayed the start of the match. They sailed through squally seas for two days.

english_meaning: To waste money, time, etc in a stupid or careless way. To spend extravagantly or foolishly. To lose (something, such as an advantage or opportunity) through negligence or inaction.
example_sentence: My uncle squandered all his money on gambling. She squandered her chance of winning.

english_meaning: A flat shape with four equal straight sides and four right angles. An open public area in a town surrounded by buildings. The result of multiplying a number by itself. To make something straight, even, or settled, such as an account or a dispute.
example_sentence: Draw a square with sides of five centimetres. Thousands gathered in the city square. The square of seven is forty-nine. Let me square the bill before we leave.

english_meaning: A metric unit of area equal to the area of a square with sides of one centimeter. A small measure of surface, written as cm². A unit used for measuring small flat areas in geometry, printing, and everyday work.
example_sentence: The stamp covers about six square centimeters. Calculate the area of the rectangle in square centimeters. A square meter has ten thousand square centimeters. The burn on his hand was only a few square centimeters wide.

english_meaning: A unit of area equal to the area of a square whose sides are one foot long. A measurement commonly used in the United States and the United Kingdom to specify the area of real estate or rooms. An imperial and US customary unit of area equivalent to 144 square inches. A metric equivalent approximately equal to 0·092903 square meters. A planar measure used for flat surfaces such as flooring, tiles, or land. A physical extent of 1/9th of a square yard.
synonyms: ["Square Ft","Sq Ft","144 Square Inches","0.0929 Square Meters","1/9 Square Yard","Superficial Foot","Area Measurement","Planar Unit","Surface Measure","Real Estate Unit","Imperial Area Unit","Customary Unit","Space Unit","Dimensional Foot"]
example_sentence: The total area of the living room is approximately three hundred square foot. You need to calculate the square foot of the wall before buying the wallpaper. The price of the apartment is determined by its total square foot measurement. The kitchen renovation cost fifty dollars per square foot for the new tiling.

english_meaning: A unit of area in the imperial and United States customary systems. It is equal to the area of a square with sides that are exactly one inch long. A measurement equivalent to 6·4516 square centimeters. A square surface measure used for small-scale spatial calculations. One 144th part of a square foot. A standard metric for measuring pressure when combined with force as in psi. The smallest common unit of area in the British system.
synonyms: ["Area Unit","6.45 Square Centimeters","0.0069 Square Feet","Imperial Area Measure","Surface Unit","Square Measurement","645 Square Millimeters","Tiny Plot","Spatial Unit","Planar Measurement","Dimension Unit","Grid Square","Sectional Area","Mapping Unit"]

You need to calculate the total square inches before ordering the custom tiles. The small electronic chip occupies less than half a square inch on the circuit board.

english_meaning: A metric unit of area equal to the area of a square with sides of one kilometer. A measure equal to one million square meters, written as km². A large unit used for measuring land, cities, forests, and countries.
synonyms: ["km²","Metric area unit","Large area measure","Land area unit"]
example_sentence: The national park covers three hundred square kilometers. Population density is measured per square kilometer. Wildfires destroyed twenty square kilometers of forest. The city has expanded by several square kilometers.

english_meaning: A metric unit of area equal to the area of a square with sides of one meter. The standard unit for measuring floor space, land, and surfaces, written as m². A measure widely used in building, property, and interior work.
example_sentence: The apartment covers ninety square meters. Carpet is sold by the square meter. They painted forty square meters of wall in one day. The office space measures two hundred square meters.

english_meaning: A unit of area measurement in the Imperial and US customary systems equal to a square with sides of one mile. A surface area equivalent to 640 acres or 2·589 square kilometers. A measurement commonly used to describe the land size of large geographical regions or cities. A two-dimensional representation of land coverage calculated by multiplying one mile in length by one mile in width. A spatial metric equivalent to 27,878,400 square feet.
synonyms: ["Section of land","640 acres","2.589 square kilometers","27.8 million square feet","Land area unit","Surface measure","Geographic unit","Spatial extent","Square mileage","Territorial measure","Grid square","Plot size"]
antonyms: ["Square inch","Linear mile","Point","Micron","Cubic mile","Millimeter","Single dimension","Zero area","Infinity","Minute fraction"]
example_sentence: The national park spans over one hundred square mile of pristine wilderness. The population density is calculated based on the number of people living per square mile. Each square mile of the estate is dedicated to a different type of agriculture. The total land area of the small island is less than a single square mile.

english_meaning: A metric unit of area equal to the area of a square with sides of one millimeter. A very small measure of surface, written as mm². A unit commonly used for the cross section of wires, components, and fine engineering parts.
example_sentence: The wire has a cross section of two square millimeters. Area on the microscope slide is measured in square millimeters. A square centimeter contains one hundred square millimeters. The chip's surface is only a few square millimeters.

english_meaning: A person who is considered old-fashioned, conventional, or out of touch with modern trends. Someone who strictly adheres to rules and social norms. A boring or unimaginative person who lacks sophistication or 'coolness'.
example_sentence: He felt like a square person at the underground jazz club because he was wearing a formal suit. The teenagers called their teacher a square person because she didn't understand their slang. Don't be such a square person and come out to the party with us tonight. Although he was a brilliant scientist, his peers viewed him as a square person due to his rigid adherence to tradition.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with a square base and four triangular faces meeting at a point. A pyramid with a square-shaped bottom and apex at the top. A polyhedron with five faces, one square and four triangular.
example_sentence: The Great Pyramid of Giza is a square pyramid. A square pyramid has five vertices. The monument is shaped like a square pyramid. Calculate the volume of the square pyramid.

english_meaning: A unit of area in the imperial and US customary systems equivalent to the area of a square with sides of one yard. A measurement equal to nine square feet or approximately 0·836 square meters. A standard unit often used in construction and landscaping for flooring or turf calculations. A two-dimensional measure of surface area defined as a yard multiplied by a yard. A specific quantity of material or land occupying a three-foot by three-foot square space. The surface area represented by the product of three feet by three feet.
synonyms: ["Area Unit","Nine Square Feet","0.836 Square Meters","1296 Square Inches","Yard Squared","Surface Measure","Land Unit","Plot Measure","Dimensional Unit","Spatial Extent","Imperial Area","Standard Measurement","Quadrature","Surface Area"]
example_sentence: The contractor quoted the price for the new carpet per square yard. We need to order fifty square yards of sod to cover the backyard. A single square yard is exactly equal to nine square feet. The area of the room was measured in square yards to calculate the total flooring cost.

english_meaning: To crush or squeeze something so that it becomes flat or shapeless. To suppress or put an end to something forcefully. A soft drink made from fruit juice, sugar, and water. A type of vegetable belonging to the gourd family. A racket sport played by two players in an enclosed court.
example_sentence: Be careful not to squash the tomatoes in your bag. The government squashed the rebellion quickly. He drank a glass of lemon squash after the match. She loves cooking butter squash soup in winter. My brother plays squash every weekend.

english_meaning: To crouch down with the knees fully bent and the weight on the feet. To occupy a building or piece of land without legal permission. An exercise in which a person lowers the hips from a standing position and stands up again. Short and thick in shape, or low and broad in appearance.
example_sentence: He squatted beside the fire to warm his hands. Several families squat in the abandoned building. She does twenty squats every morning. The cottage was a squat stone building near the river.

english_meaning: Short and thick in shape. A person, animal, or object that is low in height but wide or sturdy in build. It may also describe something compact, chunky, or stocky rather than tall or slender.
example_sentence: He was a squatty little man, not attractive like his son was to become. Each table had a squatty, round, red candle for a centrepiece.

english_meaning: Uttered a loud, harsh cry, typically resembling that of a bird. Complained or protested loudly or vehemently
example_sentence: The parrot squawked loudly when the stranger approached its cage. The seagulls squawked as they fought over the leftover breadcrumbs. She squawked in surprise when the cold water suddenly hit her back. Dissatisfied customers squawked about the recent increase in subscription fees. The old radio squawked for a moment before breaking completely.

english_meaning: To firmly press something, typically with one's fingers. To extract liquid from something by crushing or pressing it. To manage to get into or through a narrow or restricted space.
example_sentence: She squeezed the fresh lemons to make delicious juice. He gently squeezed her hand to comfort her during the movie. We barely managed to squeeze into the packed elevator. He squeezed the toothpaste from the bottom of the tube. The giant snake squeezed its prey tightly.

english_meaning: To push or force someone or something backward. To apply pressure or effort in order to make someone retreat or to regain space previously occupied.
example_sentence: He tried to squeeze back into the crowded train. The player squeezed back to defend his goal. She squeezed back through the narrow doorway. They squeezed back the opposition in the debate.

english_meaning: To pass through a narrow space or manage to get past something with difficulty. To move through a tight or crowded space, often carefully or with effort. It can also mean to manage to achieve or attend something despite obstacles or limited time.
example_sentence: I had to squeeze by the crowd to reach the stage. She squeezed by the narrow gap between the walls. He squeezed by in the traffic to make it on time. We managed to squeeze by and get tickets at the last minute.

english_meaning: Fit in a small space. To make time for something. To find a small opportunity to do or include something despite a busy schedule or limited space.
example_sentence: He squeezed in between them. I will try to squeeze in a meeting before lunch. She squeezed in a quick workout despite her busy day. Can we squeeze in a short call this afternoon? He squeezed in some extra practice before the exam.

english_meaning: To fit something or someone into a tight space. To push or force oneself or something into a space that is small or crowded, often with difficulty
example_sentence: She tried to squeeze into the crowded elevator. He squeezed into his old shoes. I need to squeeze into this meeting before it starts. They squeezed into the tiny car.

english_meaning: To press something to remove liquid or force something out. To exert pressure on something to make liquid come out or to extract something with effort.
example_sentence: She squeezed out the juice from the orange. The company squeezed out the last bit of profit from the project. He managed to squeeze out a few words despite being nervous. They were squeezed out of the market by bigger competitors.

english_meaning: To pass with difficulty through a narrow space or tight situation. To move carefully or forcefully through a narrow or tight area, often requiring bending, compressing, or maneuvering to fit through. It can also be used metaphorically for achieving something with difficulty.
example_sentence: He managed to squeeze through the crowded doorway. The children squeezed through the small gap in the fence. he squeezed through her exams with great effort. The car barely squeezed through the narrow alley.

english_meaning: To move closer to make space. To compress, move, or adjust position in order to create room for oneself or others, often in a confined space.
example_sentence: Everyone on the bench had to squeeze up to make room for her. Please squeeze up so the kids can sit too. They squeezed up in the car to fit one more passenger. At the crowded table, we had to squeeze up.

english_meaning: To look at someone or something with one or both eyes partly closed in an attempt to see more clearly or as a reaction to strong light. A permanent deviation in the direction of the gaze of one eye.
example_sentence: She had to squint against the glaring sunlight. He squinted through the keyhole to see what was happening inside. The bright screen made him squint. The baby has a slight squint in her left eye. He squinted at the small print on the back of the medicine bottle.

english_meaning: To look with eyes partly closed, often to see better. To look at something in a suspicious or critical way.
example_sentence: I had to squint at the screen to read the tiny text. He squinted at the paper to read the small print. She squinted at the sun as she walked outside. The old man squinted at me as if trying to remember my face. He squinted at the painting to see the details better.

english_meaning: To look at something with eyes partly closed, often because of bright light, difficulty seeing clearly, or to observe carefully.
example_sentence: She squinted through the fog to see the approaching car. He squinted through his glasses to read the small print. The sailor squinted through the rain to spot the lighthouse. They squinted through the crowd to find their friends.

english_meaning: To twist and turn the body with small quick movements, especially due to nervousness, discomfort, or embarrassment. To feel or show mental discomfort or awkwardness. To wriggle like a worm. A wriggling movement.
example_sentence: The child squirmed in his seat during the boring lesson. She squirmed with embarrassment when her secret was revealed. The worm squirmed on the wet ground. He tried to squirm out of answering the difficult question.

english_meaning: To squeeze or press something with force until it becomes flat, soft, or damaged. To crush something gently rather than breaking it completely. To press people or objects closely together in a small space. To move while being squeezed through a narrow opening. To make a soft, wet, or squashy sound by pressing something. A soft squeezing or crushing action. A squelching or soft sound produced by wet or soft objects. A tightly packed or crowded situation.
example_sentence: She accidentally squished the tomato while putting groceries into the bag. The children squished through the narrow gate to reach the playground. I heard my shoes squish as I walked across the muddy field. He squished the pillow to make it more comfortable.

english_meaning: Something that is soft, spongy, or yielding when pressed with your fingers. Describes food or objects that have become overly soft because of moisture. Used to describe someone or something that expresses a lot of love, kindness, or emotion.
example_sentence: He wrote a squishy birthday message to his wife. Their anniversary speech was sweet and squishy. She loves watching squishy romantic movies. His letter was full of squishy emotions.

english_meaning: To thrust a knife or other pointed object into a person, animal, or thing. To pierce or wound with a sharp object. To hurt someone emotionally through words or actions. To make a quick attempt at doing something. A wound made by a sharp object. A thrust with a knife or pointed weapon. An attempt to do something.
example_sentence: The attacker tried to stab the victim with a knife. Sharp thorns can stab your skin if you are not careful. His rude comments seemed to stab her feelings. I will take a stab at solving this difficult problem.

english_meaning: To make an attempt or thrust often without accuracy. To make an attempt to strike, pierce, or attack, often without precision or full force. It can also mean trying to do something uncertainly or experimentally.
example_sentence: He stabbed at the target. She stabbed at the box with scissors. He stabbed at the dark shape. They stabbed at the ice to break it.

english_meaning: To attack or hurt someone in return, usually after being attacked or betrayed. It can be physical, like with a knife, or metaphorical, like revenge in words or actions.
example_sentence: He stabbed back after being hit. She stabbed back instantly. They stabbed back in self defense. He stabbed back to escape.

english_meaning: To attack or pierce someone with a knife or sharp object, often implying betrayal or sudden harm. It can also mean metaphorically to betray someone’s trust.
example_sentence: He stabbed in with full force. She stabbed in before he reacted. The attacker stabbed in quickly. He stabbed in and ran.

english_meaning: To push a sharp object inside something. To thrust a knife or sharp object into something or someone, usually forcefully. Can also mean to pierce or penetrate physically or figuratively.
example_sentence: He stabbed into the wood. She stabbed into the fruit. The knife stabbed into the ground. They stabbed into the package to open it.

english_meaning: To strike, push, or pierce something aggressively, often to remove, expel, or destroy. It can also mean to extinguish or eliminate forcefully.
example_sentence: He stabbed out in panic. She stabbed out to protect herself. The guard stabbed out at the intruder. He stabbed out to break the barrier.

english_meaning: To pierce or go completely through an object or person with a sharp object. It implies the action of pushing a knife, blade, or sharp tool so that it passes entirely through.
example_sentence: He stabbed through the cloth. The spear stabbed through the shield. She stabbed through the paper. The blade stabbed through the bag.

english_meaning: To injure or attack someone with a knife or sharp object, typically multiple times or intensely.
example_sentence: He stabbed up in defense. The attacker stabbed up suddenly. She stabbed up to break free. The figure stabbed up through the dark.

english_meaning: Pierced or wounded with a pointed tool or weapon. Betrayed or hurt emotionally. Thrust a knife or other pointed weapon into someone or something.
example_sentence: He was stabbed in the chest during the sudden altercation. She felt stabbed in the back by her closest friend. The victim was stabbed multiple times with a pointed object. He stabbed the piece of meat violently with his fork. The tragic news stabbed her heart with unimaginable grief.

english_meaning: A person who stabs someone with a sharp weapon. A pointed tool or instrument used for piercing or making holes. Informally, someone who betrays another person treacherously.
example_sentence: The police arrested the stabber within an hour of the attack. A leather worker keeps a small stabber for punching holes. Witnesses described the stabber as a young man in a grey coat. He called his former partner a stabber after the betrayal.

english_meaning: The act of wounding or killing someone with a knife or other sharp object. An attack in which a person is pierced with a pointed weapon. Describing a pain that is sudden, sharp, and severe. Making a quick thrusting movement with something pointed. Causing a sudden sharp feeling of emotional hurt.
example_sentence: The police are investigating a stabbing that occurred late last night. She felt a stabbing pain in her chest and called for help. He kept stabbing the ground with a sharp stick. A stabbing sense of guilt kept him awake all night.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being stable, firm, or not easily moved. Resistance to sudden change, deterioration, or displacement. Constancy of character or purpose in a person's behavior. The capacity of an object or system to return to equilibrium after being disturbed. Economic or political reliability without experiencing major fluctuations.
example_sentence: The country enjoyed a long period of economic stability. They are looking to bring stability to the volatile region. Emotional stability is essential for making sound decisions under pressure. The structural stability of the bridge was tested before it opened to the public.

english_meaning: The process of making something steady, firm, and unlikely to change or fail. The act of bringing a situation under control so that it stops getting worse. The condition of becoming balanced or settled after a period of disturbance. Medical treatment given to keep a patient's condition from deteriorating. Economic or political measures taken to keep prices, currency, or a system steady.
example_sentence: The stabilization of the economy took several years of careful planning. Doctors focused on the stabilization of the patient before surgery. Foreign aid helped in the stabilization of the war-torn region. The company introduced new policies for the stabilization of its share price.

english_meaning: To make something steady, firm, or unlikely to change suddenly. To become settled and stop rising or falling. To keep prices, a currency, or a situation under control. In medicine, to bring a patient's condition to a safe and steady state. To fit a device that prevents movement or tipping.
example_sentence: The government took steps to stabilize the economy. Prices began to stabilize after a difficult year. Doctors worked quickly to stabilize the patient. Extra supports were added to stabilize the old wall.

english_meaning: A device or substance that keeps something steady, balanced, or unchanged. A fin, gyroscope, or support fitted to a ship, aircraft, or vehicle to reduce unwanted movement. A chemical added to food, paint, or plastic to prevent it from breaking down or separating. A small extra wheel fitted to a child's bicycle for balance. A person or policy that keeps a situation calm and steady.
example_sentence: The ship's stabilizers reduce rolling in rough seas. A stabilizer is added to keep the sauce from separating. He removed the stabilizers once his son learned to balance. Voltage stabilizers protect appliances from sudden surges.

english_meaning: Firmly fixed, not likely to move, change, or fail. Not easily upset or disturbed emotionally. A building in which horses or other livestock are kept. To keep or put a horse in a stable.
example_sentence: The patient's condition is now stable. The country needs a stable government. He keeps three horses in the stable. Prices have remained stable for the past year.

english_meaning: To arrange cards dishonestly so that a particular player gains an advantage. To arrange circumstances secretly or unfairly to produce a desired outcome. To create conditions that strongly favor or disadvantage someone.
example_sentence: The dealer was caught trying to stack the deck. Critics accused the committee of stacking the deck in favor of one candidate. The rules stack the deck against small businesses. Choosing only friendly judges would stack the deck unfairly.

english_meaning: Members of a staff or organization. People employed by a company, political campaign, publication, or government department.
example_sentence: The political campaign hired new staffers to manage their social media. Experienced staffers helped train the newly hired interns. Several staffers complained about the long working hours. The newspaper employs dozens of full-time staffers. Management decided to give all the staffers a holiday bonus.

english_meaning: A large beetle whose males have enlarged, antler-like jaws; commonly written as stag beetle. A woodland beetle of the family Lucanidae whose larvae feed on decaying wood. An insect known for the striking mandibles that males use to fight rivals. A protected species in many countries because of habitat loss.
example_sentence: A male stage beetle displayed its huge jaws on the tree trunk. The stage beetle is one of the largest beetles in Europe. Rotting logs provide a safe home for stage beetle larvae. Conservation groups are working to protect the stage beetle.

english_meaning: To organize and direct a performance or event, especially behind the scenes. To arrange or manipulate an event or situation to achieve a desired result or impression. To control the public appearance of a situation so that it looks spontaneous but is actually planned. To supervise the technical aspects of a theatrical production. To handle a complex situation with careful coordination and planning.
example_sentence: The political rally was carefully stage-managed to ensure maximum media impact. She had to stage-manage the entire wedding ceremony to prevent any potential family conflicts. The director tried to stage-manage the press conference so that only favorable questions were asked. It is difficult to stage-manage a live broadcast where anything can happen unexpectedly.

english_meaning: To walk or move unsteadily as if about to fall. To astonish or deeply shock someone. To arrange events or objects so that they do not occur at exactly the same time.
example_sentence: The injured man managed to stagger to his feet. The sheer size of the financial loss will stagger you. The company decided to stagger the working hours to reduce traffic. He received a heavy blow to the head but did not stagger. Her sudden resignation managed to stagger the entire office.

english_meaning: Not moving, not growing or not developing. Used for water, air, activity, progress or situations that stay still, show no improvement, feel lifeless or lack change. It often suggests dullness or an unhealthy state due to no movement.
example_sentence: Few fish survive in the stagnant waters of the lake. The housing market has been largely stagnant over the past few months. There is a stagnant pool at the bottom of the garden. Business was stagnant last month. Mosquitoes breed in stagnant pools of water. The economy has been stagnant for years, with no real growth.

english_meaning: To stop moving or developing. To become inactive or dull. To lose activity, progress or flow. It is used when something stays still, stops improving or becomes stale. It can refer to water, ideas, work, economy, motivation or growth.
example_sentence: My music career had stagnated. The electronics industry is showing signs of stagnating after 15 years of growth. Their economy was stagnating, while Japan and Asia's "tiger economies" were booming. Profits have stagnated. I feel I'm stagnating in this job. Businesses must adapt to change or stagnate. The water in the pond was stagnating. Valleys where air tends to stagnate often have high levels of pollutants. The local economy stagnated when the factories closed.

english_meaning: A mark or patch of dirt or discolouration that is difficult to remove. To mark or discolour something with a substance that leaves a lasting mark. A coloured liquid used to change the colour of wood or fabric. To damage someone's reputation or honour. A dye used to make biological specimens visible under a microscope.
example_sentence: There is a coffee stain on the tablecloth. Red wine can stain a carpet permanently. He applied a dark stain to the wooden shelves. The scandal left a lasting stain on his reputation.

english_meaning: Not marked or discoloured by stains. Of steel, treated so that it resists rust and corrosion. Free from fault, guilt, or dishonour.
example_sentence: The kitchen is fitted with stainless steel appliances. She kept the sink stainless and gleaming. He had a stainless record of public service. Stainless cutlery is easier to maintain.

english_meaning: To mark or support something with a stake. To risk money or assets on an outcome. A pointed stick or post used for marking a position or supporting something. A share or interest in a business or activity. Money risked or wagered in gambling or betting. Something that is at risk of being lost or gained.
example_sentence: He planted a wooden stake in the ground to mark the boundary. She has a financial stake in the company. They decided to stake money on the football match. The farmer staked the young plants to protect them from wind.

english_meaning: The act of secretly watching a place by police or detectives. Surveillance of a location over a period of time to gather evidence or catch a suspect. A period of continuous observation, often from a hidden position, usually conducted by law enforcement to monitor the activities of a person or building suspected of criminal involvement.
example_sentence: The detectives organized a stakeout outside the suspect's apartment. The police were on a stakeout for three nights before making the arrest. Officers conducted a stakeout to monitor the drug dealers' activities. The stakeout finally produced enough evidence to charge the gang. They sat in an unmarked van during the long stakeout.

english_meaning: No longer fresh. Dull or lacking newness. Not fresh or pleasant. Not interesting or original. Losing energy or enthusiasm. Air that feels heavy or not clean. Used for food that has lost freshness or taste. Also used for ideas, styles or feelings that have become dull, boring or no longer effective.
example_sentence: This bread's going stale. There was one piece of stale chocolate cake left in the tin. The atmosphere was stale with cigarette smoke. The room smelt of stale sweat. The room smelled musty and stale. Their marriage had gone stale. After ten years in the job, she felt stale and needed a change. The cast is changed regularly to stop the actors from getting stale. They had been working together for over five years and they had both become a little stale. He had grown stale on the job and needed a long vacation.

english_meaning: A situation where no progress is possible. To bring progress to a stop. To cause a situation in which neither side can move forward, act, or reach a decision, often due to equal resistance or opposing positions.
example_sentence: The peace talks ended in a stalemate after hours of discussion. The game reached a stalemate when neither player could make a legal move. Their argument resulted in a stalemate, with neither side willing to compromise. The disagreement stalemated the negotiations. Legal objections have stalemated the project.

english_meaning: A person who repeatedly follows or watches someone in an unwanted and obsessive way. An individual who persistently follows, monitors, or contacts another person without consent, often causing fear, discomfort, or emotional distress. Stalking behavior may include repeated calls, messages, following someone physically, or monitoring their activities online.
example_sentence: The police arrested the stalker after multiple complaints from the victim. She realized someone was a stalker when he kept following her every day. Online platforms take action to block a stalker who sends repeated unwanted messages. Living in fear, the victim changed her routine to avoid the stalker.

english_meaning: To deliberately delay action, stop progress, or cause something like a vehicle or machine to stop working temporarily. A small shop or booth where goods are sold, or a fixed space such as an animal shelter or seating area.
example_sentence: The driver stalled the car in heavy traffic. The manager tried to stall the meeting to gain more time. She bought vegetables from a roadside stall. The engine may stall if it overheats.

english_meaning: To delay intentionally. To create delays in order to gain time or avoid an immediate decision.
example_sentence: He tried to stall off criticism. The government stalled off protests for weeks. She stalled off the decision until Monday. They stalled off the issue with excuses.

english_meaning: To prevent or delay something unwanted. To keep something from happening for a period of time, often temporarily.
example_sentence: He tried to stall off criticism. The government stalled off protests for weeks. She stalled off the decision until Monday. They stalled off the issue with excuses.

english_meaning: To stop suddenly or fail to continue. Used when a machine, vehicle, process, or plan suddenly stops working or loses momentum.
example_sentence: The car stalled out in heavy traffic. The project stalled out due to lack of funds. Negotiations stalled out after disagreements. The engine stalled out on the highway.

english_meaning: To delay a decision or action intentionally. To avoid moving forward by wasting time, making excuses, or postponing action until a later moment
example_sentence: He stalled over signing the contract because he was unsure. The manager stalled over the issue until more information arrived. She stalled over answering the question to gain time. They stalled over the plan hoping the problem would resolve itself.

english_meaning: Very loyal, strong, and dependable. A person or quality that shows firm loyalty, strength of character, and reliability, especially in difficult situations
example_sentence: She is a stalwart supporter of community education. The doctor remained stalwart during the health crisis. He proved to be a stalwart friend in times of trouble. The team relied on its stalwart members to stay focused.

english_meaning: The male fertilizing organ of a flower, typically consisting of a pollen-containing anther and a slender filament. The pollen-producing reproductive part of a blossom.
example_sentence: The bee collected nectar while brushing against the stamen. A typical flower has several stamens surrounding the central pistil. The stamen consists of a stalk called the filament and an anther. During pollination, pollen is transferred from the stamen to the stigma. We examined the stamen under the microscope to see the tiny pollen grains.

english_meaning: To speak with sudden involuntary pauses and a tendency to repeat the initial letters of words. A speech disorder characterized by involuntary pauses, hesitations, and repetitions.
example_sentence: He tends to stammer when he is nervous in front of a crowd. The little boy had a severe stammer that lasted until adulthood. She managed to stammer out an apology before running away in tears. Stress and anxiety can make a person stammer much more frequently. He spoke with a slight stammer, making him feel self-conscious during public presentations.

english_meaning: A tax levied on the legal recognition of documents. A fee paid to the government for the transfer of property or assets. A tax imposed on specific instruments like checks, receipts, and land transactions. Revenue collected through the use of physical or digital stamps on official papers.
example_sentence: The buyer is responsible for paying the stamp duty on the new house. Stamp duty rates vary depending on the total value of the property. Make sure to calculate the stamp duty before finalizing the contract. The government increased stamp duty to boost national revenue.

english_meaning: A sudden panicked rush of a mass of people or animals. An unreasoning and general flight of a herd of animals. To suddenly run away or make a rapid movement due to mass panic.
example_sentence: The loud explosion caused a stampede among the terrified crowd. Hundreds of cattle were injured in the stampede after being spooked by thunder. Shoppers stampeded into the mall as soon as the doors opened for the holiday sale. The local police struggled to control the stampede at the crowded music concert. It is extremely dangerous to be caught in a stampede of frightened animals.

english_meaning: The action of pressing a mark or design onto a surface. Bringing down one's foot heavily on the ground. The process of cutting or shaping metal with a die.
example_sentence: The machine is used for stamping metal parts. He was stamping his cold feet to get warm. She is stamping the approved documents with an official seal. The angry crowd started stamping their feet. Stamping the envelopes took longer than we expected.

english_meaning: Position or opinion about an issue. Way of standing or posture. Attitude toward something. Stand taken in debate or politics.
example_sentence: What is newspaper stance on war. He is known for his anti-abortion stance. The government clarified its stance on climate policy. Her stance on education reform gained public support. The boxer adjusted his stance before the fight started. The teacher appreciated the student's clear stance during the debate.

english_meaning: To support someone. To stay ready. To do nothing while something happens. To remain loyal in difficult times.
example_sentence: I will stand by you no matter what happens. The team is standing by for further instructions. She stood by her friend during the entire crisis. We cannot stand by and watch this injustice continue.

english_meaning: To withdraw, relax, or step aside from a position or action. To stop an action, withdraw from a position of responsibility, or relax after a period of tension or readiness. It is often used in military, official, or conflict-related contexts but can apply generally.
example_sentence: The police were told to stand down after the situation was under control. The CEO decided to stand down after ten years in charge. Soldiers were ordered to stand down when the threat ended. The manager asked his team to stand down and wait for further instructions.

english_meaning: To behave in a very formal way. To insist on strict observance of manners and etiquette. To act stiffly instead of being relaxed and friendly.
antonyms: ["Be casual","Be informal","Relax","Be at ease","Be friendly","Loosen up"]
example_sentence: Please do not stand on ceremony; help yourself to the food. He never stands on ceremony with old friends. The host stood on ceremony throughout the dinner. In this office we do not stand on ceremony.

english_meaning: To become independent and self-reliant without depending on others for financial, emotional, or practical support.
antonyms: ["Depend on others","Rely on others","Be dependent","Lean on others"]
example_sentence: After finishing his studies, he decided to stand on his own feet and find a job. She works hard to stand on her own feet without asking her parents for money. Many young people want to stand on their own feet as soon as possible. Losing his job forced him to learn how to stand on his own feet quickly.

english_meaning: To be easily noticed. To appear different, impressive or more noticeable than others in a way that draws attention.
example_sentence: Her bright outfit made her stand out in the crowd. His creative ideas always stand out during meetings. The tall building stands out among the small houses. Your hard work will help you stand out from others.

english_meaning: To be noticeably different and better or more interesting than others. To be unique among others. To attract attention because of difference. To be more impressive than the rest. To not blend in with the group. To be exceptional in a competitive situation.
synonyms: ["Be unique","Be outstanding","Be exceptional","Shine out","Rise above others","Be noticeable","Be different from the rest"]
antonyms: ["Blend in","Fit in","Conform","Be ordinary","Go unnoticed","Be average","Follow the crowd"]
example_sentence: Her creative ideas always make her stand out from the crowd in meetings. He worked hard to stand out from the crowd in his class. The bright red dress helped her stand out from the crowd at the event. Good communication skills help a candidate stand out from the crowd in interviews.

word: Stand out like a sore thumb
english_meaning: To be easily seen because of being different. To attract immediate attention. To appear out of place. To be highly visible among similar things. To be unusually noticeable. When a person, object, or situation is extremely conspicuous and attracts attention because it does not fit in with its surroundings. The difference is usually obvious and sometimes embarrassing or undesirable.
synonyms: ["Be conspicuous","Be noticeable","Be obvious","Attract attention","Be prominent","Stick out","Be striking","Be eye-catching"]
antonyms: ["Blend in","Fit in","Go unnoticed","Be inconspicuous","Be hidden","Be unremarkable","Merge with surroundings"]
example_sentence: His bright yellow jacket stood out like a sore thumb at the formal business meeting. The modern glass building stands out like a sore thumb among the old houses in the village. Everyone wore black at the event, so my white shirt stood out like a sore thumb. The spelling mistake stood out like a sore thumb in the final report.

english_meaning: To remain confident and dignified, especially in difficult situations. To face challenges, criticism, or hardship with self respect, courage, and moral strength without feeling ashamed or defeated.
synonyms: ["Remain confident","Hold one’s head high","Be resilient","Stay strong"]
example_sentence: Even after losing the case, she stood tall and accepted the outcome with dignity. He was criticized unfairly, but he stood tall and defended the truth. Nations must stand tall when their values are challenged. Despite repeated failures, she continued to stand tall and pursue her goals.

english_meaning: To rise to a standing position. To rise to your feet. Also to defend someone or fail to meet someone as promised. To physically get up from a sitting or lying position. It can also mean supporting someone or something in a situation that requires courage. Another meaning is when someone does not arrive for a planned meeting or appointment.
example_sentence: She asked him to stand up when the judge entered the room. You should stand up for your friend when he is treated unfairly. He stood up after sitting for a long time. She felt hurt because he stood her up on their meeting.

english_meaning: To confront someone powerful or threatening without fear. To defend yourself or others against pressure or attack. To resist something such as criticism, force, or difficulty. To remain strong and not give in to intimidation. To tolerate or endure something difficult or unpleasant. To be strong enough to deal with a situation or challenge
example_sentence: She stood up to the bully and refused to be afraid. He finally stood up to his boss about the unfair treatment. This material can stand up to extreme weather conditions. You must stand up to pressure if you want to succeed.

english_meaning: To refuse to change your opinion or position, to defend your stance. To maintain your position, opinion, or rights firmly, even when facing opposition, criticism, or threat. It implies courage, determination, and assertiveness.
example_sentence: Despite the criticism, she stood her ground on the project. The soldier stood his ground during the attack. He stood his ground when everyone doubted his decision. Parents sometimes need to stand their ground with teenagers.

english_meaning: A situation in which neither side in a dispute can gain an advantage. A tense pause in a conflict where both sides refuse to move or give in. A deadlock or draw in a contest or negotiation. A confrontation, especially an armed one, that has reached a halt.
example_sentence: The two sides remained locked in a tense stand-off for hours. Police ended the armed stand-off without any casualties. The negotiations ended in a complete stand-off. A political stand-off delayed the passing of the budget.

english_meaning: A level of quality or achievement used as a measure of comparison. An accepted rule, principle, or requirement that must be followed. Normal, usual, or accepted rather than special or unusual. A flag or banner, especially one carried in a ceremony. A song or tune that has remained popular over many years.
example_sentence: The school maintains a very high standard of teaching. This model comes with air conditioning as standard. Their work fell below the required standard. The soldiers marched behind the regimental standard.

english_meaning: The process of making things conform to a single agreed standard. The establishment of common rules, sizes, or procedures. The act of removing variation so that products or methods are uniform. The condition of being standardized.
example_sentence: Standardization of parts reduced production costs. The company is working on the standardization of its services. Standardization helps students to be assessed fairly. International standardization makes trade much easier.

english_meaning: To make things of the same type conform to one fixed standard or pattern. To bring different items, methods, or processes into line with a common rule. To decide on and apply an official standard for something. To remove unnecessary variation so that results are consistent.
example_sentence: The board decided to standardize the examination format. We must standardize our reporting procedures. The industry has standardized the size of shipping containers. Standardizing the software helped reduce errors.

english_meaning: A complete stop or situation where no progress happens. Complete halt of movement. A situation where trade or business activity stops. Talks stop because no agreement is reached. Progress in a plan or project stops. A condition in which movement, activity, discussion, or progress stops completely. It can describe physical stopping, such as traffic, or non physical situations like business, negotiations, or development coming to a halt.
example_sentence: The heavy rain brought traffic to a standstill. The factory came to a standstill during the strike. Negotiations reached a standstill after hours of discussion. The project is at a standstill due to lack of funds.

english_meaning: A group of lines forming a division of a poem. A verse of a poem separated from others by a space. A set of lines arranged with a fixed pattern of rhyme and rhythm. In Italian architecture, a room or chamber.
example_sentence: The poem is divided into six stanzas. Each stanza ends with the same refrain. She read the opening stanza aloud. The final stanza carries the poet's main message.

english_meaning: The innermost and smallest of the three bones of the middle ear, shaped like a stirrup. The bone that transfers sound vibrations from the incus to the inner ear. The smallest bone in the human body.
example_sentence: The stapes is the smallest bone in the human body. Vibrations pass from the incus to the stapes. The stapes pushes against the oval window of the inner ear. Surgery on the stapes can restore some types of hearing.

english_meaning: A main or important element of something, especially of a diet. A piece of thin wire used to fasten sheets of paper together. To attach or secure with a staple. Main or principal.
example_sentence: Rice is a staple food in many Asian countries. Can you staple these documents together for me? Romance is a staple of her novels. He bought a new stapler and a box of staples. Cotton was the staple crop of the region.

english_meaning: Featuring or including many famous actors, performers, or celebrities. Consisting of a large gathering of distinguished or celebrated individuals.
example_sentence: The red carpet premiere was a star-studded affair with famous actors everywhere. The movie boasts a star-studded cast including several Oscar winners. We attended a star-studded gala raising funds for charity. The musical lineup for the festival is truly star-studded this year.

english_meaning: The state of being a famous performer or celebrity. The position or status of a star in films, music, or sport. The world of celebrities and public admiration.
example_sentence: The young actress rose to stardom in just two years. Stardom brought him wealth but very little privacy. He never adjusted comfortably to sudden stardom. Her voice carried her all the way to international stardom.

english_meaning: A magical or dreamlike quality attached to fame and glamour. Fine dust or matter from stars, especially cosmic particles. A romantic or enchanting feeling that makes something seem special. The glamour associated with celebrities.
example_sentence: Every atom in our bodies is made of ancient stardust. The film sprinkled a little stardust over the small town. Her presence brought stardust to the charity event. Astronomers study stardust to learn how planets formed.

english_meaning: To look fixedly or vacantly at someone or something with one's eyes wide open. A long fixed or vacant look.
example_sentence: He continued to stare at the painting for a long time. It is rude to stare at strangers. She gave him a cold stare. Don't stare at me like that. The child could only stare in amazement at the magic trick.

english_meaning: To look steadily at someone until they are forced to look away. To defeat a person in a contest of staring. To gaze fixedly out of a window or into the distance.
example_sentence: He tried to stare out his opponent across the table. She stared out of the window at the falling rain. The boys competed to stare each other out. He sat quietly and stared out over the empty fields.

english_meaning: To be very obvious or clearly visible to someone. To be right in front of a person, though not always noticed. To be an unavoidable fact or outcome that someone must confront.
synonyms: ["Be obvious","Be evident","Be apparent","Loom","Confront","Be unmistakable","Be right there","Face someone"]
antonyms: ["Be hidden","Be obscure","Be concealed","Escape notice","Be unclear","Be doubtful","Be distant"]
example_sentence: The answer was staring me in the face all along. Defeat was staring the team in the face at half-time. Bankruptcy is staring the company in the face. The solution stared him in the face once he calmed down.

english_meaning: To begin doing something immediately or enthusiastically. To commence eating, working, or arguing without delay.
example_sentence: As soon as the food arrived, everyone started in on their lunch. We should start in cleaning the kitchen before it gets too late. The teacher asked the students to start in on their reading assignment. Don't wait for me, just start in without my help.

english_meaning: To begin a journey, event, or activity in a specified manner or direction. To cause someone or something to begin a process.
