example_sentence: We decided to start off early in the morning to avoid heavy traffic. She started off her speech with an amusing joke. The warm weather started off a surge in ice cream sales. Let us start off the meeting by reviewing last week's action items.

word: Start off on the right foot
english_meaning: To begin well or correctly. To begin something in a good, positive, or successful way, especially when starting a relationship, job, project, or activity.
example_sentence: We started off on the right foot by planning everything carefully. Try to start off on the right foot with your new colleagues. The meeting started off on the right foot with a warm welcome from the manager. Their friendship started off on the right foot and grew stronger over time.

word: Start off on the wrong foot
english_meaning: To have a bad beginning. To begin something in a bad, unpleasant, or unsuccessful way, especially a relationship, job, or situation that starts with misunderstanding, mistake, or tension.
antonyms: ["Start off on the right foot","Start smoothly"]
example_sentence: They started off on the wrong foot in business. I started off on the wrong foot with my new boss by arriving late on my first day. Their friendship started off on the wrong foot because of a silly argument. The project started off on the wrong foot due to poor planning. She felt they started off on the wrong foot when she forgot his name.

english_meaning: To begin a career, venture, or life journey in a particular state or with a particular goal. To set off on a journey.
example_sentence: He started out as a humble intern before becoming the chief executive officer. They started out on their road trip across the country early Monday. She started out with great enthusiasm but faced many unforeseen obstacles. The major software project started out as a simple personal hobby.

english_meaning: To begin again from the very beginning. To wipe the slate clean and make a fresh start, especially after a failure or mistake.
example_sentence: After making several critical errors in the painting, she decided to start over. It is never too late to start over and pursue a completely new career. The software crashed suddenly, forcing him to start over on the report. They resolved their differences and agreed to start over as friends.

english_meaning: To begin operating or cause a machine or system to begin operating. To found or establish a new business venture. A newly established business or enterprise.
example_sentence: They decided to start up a small tech firm in their garage. It took a few minutes for the computer to start up properly. The government offers grants for innovative tech start ups. She wants to start up a local bakery after finishing her culinary course.

english_meaning: A newly established business, especially one that is small, innovative, and designed for rapid growth. The action or process of starting a new enterprise or operation.
example_sentence: They launched a tech start-up that specializes in artificial intelligence. Securing venture capital funding is crucial for many early-stage start-ups. Working at a fast-paced start-up requires adaptability and creative problem-solving. The government offers special grants to foster local innovation and start-ups.

english_meaning: A person, animal, or team that takes part at the beginning of a race or competition. The first course of a meal, served before the main dish. A device used to start an engine or motor. A person who gives the signal for a race to begin. A substance such as yeast or fermented dough used to begin a process. A beginner or someone at the start of an activity.
example_sentence: Only ten starters lined up for the marathon. We ordered soup as a starter. The car would not move because the starter had failed. This book is a good starter for anyone learning Arabic.

english_meaning: To cause a person or animal to feel sudden shock, surprise, or fright. To make someone jump or react quickly because of an unexpected event, sound, or sight. To be alarmed or astonished suddenly. The effect is usually short, sharp, and unexpected rather than deeply frightening.
example_sentence: The loud thunderclap startled the children in the garden. She was startled by the sudden ring of the telephone at midnight. A deer can be easily startled by any movement in the bushes. His sudden appearance at the door startled everyone in the room. The news of his promotion startled even his closest friends.

english_meaning: Suffering or death caused by severe lack of food. The state of being extremely hungry over a long period. A condition in which the body does not get the nutrition it needs to survive. By extension, a severe lack of something essential, such as attention, affection, or resources.
example_sentence: Thousands of people died of starvation during the long drought. The prisoners were kept on the edge of starvation for months. War and conflict have pushed millions to the brink of starvation. Children in the camp showed clear signs of starvation. He spoke of his emotional starvation after years of loneliness.

english_meaning: To suffer or die from lack of food. To go without enough food for a long time, to be extremely hungry, or to deprive someone of food. It can also mean to lack something essential, such as love, attention or resources.
example_sentence: The animals were left to starve to death. Pictures of starving children. The new job doesn't pay as much but we won't starve!. She's starving herself to try to lose weight. Many of the prisoners looked half starved. Whole communities starved to death during the long drought.

english_meaning: To force someone (or a group) to do something by depriving them of food or basic needs. It’s often used in war, sieges, or extreme hardship, meaning compelling by hunger.
example_sentence: The enemy tried to starve the city into surrender by blocking all food supplies. The workers refused to be starved into submission by the unfair company policies. During the war, thousands were starved into leaving their homes. The government cannot allow its citizens to be starved into desperation.

english_meaning: To suffer because of a lack of something necessary (not only food). To be deprived of something essential, such as love, attention, money, or opportunities.
example_sentence: The area is starved of water. The students are starved of opportunities. The students were starved of proper facilities in their school. Children starved of love often struggle with relationships later in life. The village was starved of clean drinking water during the drought. He felt starved of opportunities to prove his talent.

english_meaning: To force someone to surrender, leave, or give up by cutting off their food supply. To weaken someone by deliberately depriving them of necessities (especially food).
example_sentence: The army tried to starve out the rebels. They were starved out of the town. The army tried to starve out the rebels by blocking all food supplies to the valley. The landlord cut off water and electricity to starve out the tenants. During the war, the city was besieged in an attempt to starve out its people. The company reduced resources to starve out the workers on strike.

english_meaning: The particular condition that someone or something is in at a given time. A country or a political division within a federal country. The government and its official machinery. To express something clearly in speech or writing.
example_sentence: The building is in a poor state of repair. Sindh is one of the four provinces of the state. The state provides free education to all children. Please state your name and address clearly.

english_meaning: Describing a system or program that remembers information from previous interactions. Keeping a record of earlier events, inputs, or sessions. Depending on stored data to decide how to respond. Having a condition or status that persists over time.
example_sentence: A stateful application stores the user's session data. The firewall is stateful and tracks active connections. Stateful components can be harder to scale. This form is stateful, so your answers are preserved.

english_meaning: Describing a system that keeps no record of previous interactions. Treating every request as completely independent. Not storing session data between operations. Having no nationality or legal citizenship of any country.
example_sentence: HTTP is a stateless protocol by design. A stateless service is easier to scale across servers. The component is stateless and simply displays the data. Millions of stateless people live without any citizenship.

english_meaning: Not moving or not changing. Something that does not move, grow, or develop. It stays the same over time. A situation where there is no progress, improvement, or decline. A state where a person feels stuck and does not grow or improve.
example_sentence: The old system has remained static for years. The picture on the screen looked static and lifeless. Static electricity made the clothes stick together. His career became static after he stopped learning new skills. The economy stayed static despite new policies.

english_meaning: In a static, motionless, or unchanging manner. Without movement, action, or change. In terms of stationary forces or bodies in equilibrium.
example_sentence: The system was tested statically before dynamic loads were applied. The variables are statically typed to avoid runtime errors. The old rusted car sat statically in the driveway for over a decade. The statue was statically positioned to create a sense of eternal calm. He analyzed the bridge statically to ensure it could hold the required weight.

english_meaning: Not moving, fixed in one place. It describes something that doesn't change position and remains still.
example_sentence: The car remained stationary at the light. She kept the vase stationary. Stationary objects are easier to paint. The train stayed stationary for hours.

english_meaning: Materials used for writing, such as paper, envelopes, pens, notebooks, files, and other office or school supplies. It includes all items used for writing, printing, and organizing documents.
example_sentence: She bought new stationery. Office stationery includes pens and files. The shop sells stationery items. I need stationery for school.

english_meaning: A person who supports a strong role for the state in controlling the economy or society. A person who advocates extensive government authority.
example_sentence: The writer was criticized as a statist for favoring extensive regulation. A statist approach gives the government a central role. He is not a statist and prefers local decision-making. The debate compared statist and market-based policies.

english_meaning: A numerical fact or measurement that describes a group, event, or situation. A quantity calculated from sample data in statistics.
example_sentence: The unemployment statistic fell slightly this month. One statistic cannot explain the whole situation. The researcher calculated a statistic from the sample. The report includes a statistic on school attendance.

english_meaning: Relating to the use of statistics. Pertaining to data containing numerical information. Concerning the collection and analysis of quantitative data.
example_sentence: The report provides statistical evidence to support the claim. There is a significant statistical difference between the two groups. We need to conduct a thorough statistical analysis of the survey data. Statistical methods play a crucial role in scientific research. She works as a statistical consultant for the government.

english_meaning: According to statistical analysis or numerical data. In a way that relates to the collection, study, or interpretation of statistics.
example_sentence: The difference was statistically significant. Statistically, the treatment improved recovery rates. The result is statistically unlikely to be due to chance. Statistically speaking, most customers prefer the simpler design.

english_meaning: The science of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting numerical data. Numerical facts or figures about a group, activity, or situation.
example_sentence: She studied statistics at university. The latest statistics show a rise in online sales. Statistics help researchers understand patterns in data. The coach reviewed the players’ statistics before the match.

english_meaning: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal, usually life-size or larger. A sculpted representation made of stone, metal, wood, or plaster. A monument erected in honour of a person or event. A person who stands completely still, described figuratively.
example_sentence: A bronze statue of the poet stands in the city square. The statue was unveiled by the mayor last week. Tourists photograph the marble statue every day. He stood as still as a statue during the ceremony.

english_meaning: Tall, graceful, and dignified in appearance, like a statue. Having an attractively formal and imposing physical presence. Still and motionless in a way that resembles a sculpture.
example_sentence: She was a statuesque woman with a calm, steady gaze. The dancer stood statuesque under the stage lights. He admired her statuesque beauty from across the hall. The guards remained statuesque throughout the ceremony.

english_meaning: The relative social, professional, or legal standing of someone or something. The situation at a particular time during a process.
example_sentence: He is very concerned about his social status. The current status of the project is on track for completion. The legal status of the document is still being debated. Marriage changed her legal status in the eyes of the state.

english_meaning: The existing state or condition of affairs, especially regarding social, political, or economic situations. It refers to keeping things as they currently are, without change.
example_sentence: The government decided to maintain the status quo instead of introducing new laws. Many people resist change because they prefer the status quo. The peace agreement was designed to preserve the status quo between the two countries. The company’s management wanted to challenge the status quo and bring innovation.

english_meaning: To stop the flow of blood, tears, or something spreading. Very loyal, firm, strong, and dependable. A person who strongly supports someone, an idea, belief, or organization. It also describes something strong, solid, and reliable. A staunch person never easily changes loyalty or beliefs.
example_sentence: She is a staunch supporter of education for girls. My grandfather remained staunch in his beliefs throughout his life. The old bridge was built with staunch materials. Doctors worked quickly to staunch the bleeding after the accident.

english_meaning: In a very loyal, firm, determined, and strong way. Used when a person strongly supports, defends, believes in, or opposes something with firmness and loyalty. It describes unwavering commitment, courage, and determination.
example_sentence: She staunchly defended the new policy. The family was staunchly Protestant. Economic advisers remain staunchly opposed to a government-financed bailout for the holders of failed mortgages. The editorial slant of the newspaper remained staunchly conservative.

english_meaning: To avoid stepping on, touching, using, or getting involved with something. It is often used as a warning or instruction.
example_sentence: Stay off the grass because it has just been planted and needs time to grow. The doctor advised him to stay off junk food to improve his health. Please stay off social media until the issue is resolved. He was told to stay off the construction site for his own safety.

english_meaning: Remain in the same place. Do not move. To remain where you are, especially when you are told or expected not to move. It is often used in situations involving safety, instructions, or waiting.
example_sentence: Stay put until I come back. The doctor told him to stay put after the surgery. During the storm, residents were advised to stay put indoors. If you get lost, stay put and wait for help.

english_meaning: To continue doing something until it is finished, even when it is difficult or challenging. To remain committed to a plan, decision, or goal without giving up, even when there are obstacles, delays, criticism, or difficulties. It emphasizes persistence, patience, and long-term determination.
synonyms: ["Persevere","Keep going","Persist","Remain committed","Hang in there","Stick with it"]
example_sentence: Despite all the criticism, she decided to stay the course and complete her research. The project is difficult, but we must stay the course until it is finished. If you want success, you need to stay the course even during hard times. The team stayed the course and finally achieved their yearly target.

english_meaning: To keep watching or listening for more information. To remain attentive for upcoming news or updates. Used to tell the audience to wait for what comes next. To stay connected to a channel or source. A phrase meaning to be ready for something coming soon.
example_sentence: Stay tuned for our next big announcement. Stay tuned to this channel for live updates. We have exciting news coming up, so stay tuned. Stay tuned after the break for the final results.

english_meaning: Not changing in your attitudes or aims. Staying the same for a long time and not changing quickly or unexpectedly. Firmly fixed in place. Not subject to change.
example_sentence: The group remained steadfast in its support for the new system, even when it was criticized in the newspapers. He remained steadfast in his determination to bring the killers to justice.

english_meaning: In a continuous and regular manner. At a consistent rate or pace. Without variation, fluctuation, or interruption.
example_sentence: The rain fell steadily throughout the night. Her health has been improving steadily since the surgery. The company has grown steadily over the past decade. He walked steadily towards the finish line despite his injury. The temperature will rise steadily during the day.

english_meaning: Firm, stable, constant, regular, calm, or not changing suddenly. Not likely to move, shake, or fall. Continuing at the same rate without sudden changes. Remaining calm without becoming nervous or emotional. Someone who can always be trusted. Happening without interruption. To make someone or something stable or less likely to move. In a regular and controlled manner.
example_sentence: She made steady progress in learning English. Keep your hands steady while taking the photograph. His steady support helped the team succeed. The rain continued at a steady pace throughout the afternoon.

english_meaning: To take attention, credit, or praise away from someone by doing or saying something similar before they do. To spoil or reduce the effect of another person’s success, idea, announcement, or performance by introducing it first or by attracting attention away from them. It often implies taking credit or recognition that was meant for someone else, sometimes unintentionally and sometimes deliberately.
synonyms: ["Upstage someone","Overshadow someone","Outshine someone","Take credit","Draw attention away"]
example_sentence: She stole my thunder by announcing the project before I could. He stole the manager’s thunder by presenting the idea first. Don’t steal her thunder; let her share the news herself. The guest speaker stole the host’s thunder with his surprise speech.

english_meaning: Resembling steel in colour, being a hard bluish grey. Cold, hard, and unyielding in manner or expression. Showing great strength, determination, or resolve.
example_sentence: He gave her a steely look and said nothing. Her steely determination carried the team to victory. The lake lay steely grey under the winter sky. There was a steely edge to his quiet voice.

english_meaning: Very high and difficult to climb. Sudden and large in amount. To soak something in liquid so that its flavor or softness develops. Something sharply rising or falling. It can also describe a large increase in price, amount, or difficulty.
example_sentence: The hikers climbed a steep mountain road. There was a steep increase in fuel prices last month. This hill is too steep for children to ride bicycles on. Steep the tea leaves in hot water for five minutes.

english_meaning: A tall pointed tower on a church, mosque, temple, or other building. A tall, narrow tower that rises from the roof of a building, especially a church. It usually ends in a pointed top or spire and is often used as a landmark or for holding bells.
example_sentence: The church steeple could be seen from miles away. Birds were sitting on the top of the old steeple. The village is famous for its beautiful white steeple. Workers repaired the damaged steeple after the storm.

english_meaning: To control direction of car, boat, To move in a particular direction, To control situation & influence
example_sentence: Musharaf was keen on ensuring free & transparent election to steer country out of crises.

english_meaning: To guide or direct someone or something to avoid or go around an obstacle, problem, or sensitive topic. To navigate carefully to bypass something undesirable or difficult. To maneuver to evade or circumvent an issue.
example_sentence: The driver carefully steered around the pothole. He steered the conversation around the controversial topic. The diplomat steered around the sensitive political issues. They steered around the obstacles in their path.

english_meaning: To guide or direct oneself or others in a different direction. To avoid or move away from something. To deliberately choose not to approach or engage with. To redirect attention or movement from something.
example_sentence: You should steer away from risky investments. The teacher steered the discussion away from politics. He tried to steer away from controversial topics. Steer away from unhealthy foods.

english_meaning: To guide or direct someone or something to return to a previous position, topic, or course. To redirect attention or focus to an earlier point or subject. To bring someone or something back on track after a deviation.
synonyms: ["Guide back","Direct back","Return to","Bring back","Redirect to","Lead back","Turn back to","Refocus on"]
antonyms: ["Lead away","Divert from","Stray from","Deviate from","Wander from","Continue away"]
example_sentence: The moderator steered the discussion back to the original question. She steered her thoughts back to the present moment. The manager steered the meeting back to the main agenda. He steered the car back onto the road.

english_meaning: To guide or navigate using something as a reference point, principle, or standard. To make decisions or take actions based on certain guidelines or values. To use something as a guide for direction or behavior.
synonyms: ["Navigate by","Guide by","Follow","Use as guide","Orient by","Direct by","Go by","Be guided by"]
example_sentence: Sailors used to steer by the stars at night. She steers by her moral principles in difficult situations. The company steers by its core values. He steers by his intuition when making important decisions.

english_meaning: To avoid someone or something completely. To stay away from a person, place, or situation. To keep a safe distance from possible trouble. To not get involved in a certain matter. To purposely avoid contact or interaction.
example_sentence: Steer clear of that dangerous neighborhood at night. I always steer clear of arguments at work. Doctors advise us to steer clear of fatty foods. She learned to steer clear of toxic people.

english_meaning: To avoid completely or keep at a distance from. To deliberately stay away from something or someone. To not get involved with or approach. To maintain distance from potential problems or dangers.
synonyms: ["Avoid","Keep away from","Stay away from","Shun","Evade","Bypass","Give a wide berth"]
example_sentence: Steer clear of that dangerous neighborhood. You should steer clear of gossip at work. The doctor advised him to steer clear of alcohol. Steer clear of trouble.

english_meaning: To direct or guide something or someone toward a place or situation. To deliberately move or turn in a particular direction. To navigate into a position or condition. To cause to enter or approach.
synonyms: ["Direct toward","Guide into","Navigate into","Turn into","Drive toward","Maneuver into"]
antonyms: ["Steer away from","Avoid","Direct away","Navigate out","Move away from"]
example_sentence: He steered the car into the driveway. She steered the company into profitability. The captain steered the ship into port. They steered the project into new territory.

english_meaning: To guide or direct someone or something away from a particular course, topic, or direction. To divert or redirect from an original path or subject. To move away from something deliberately.
synonyms: ["Divert from","Turn away from","Redirect from","Move away from","Lead off","Veer off","Deviate from","Shift from"]
antonyms: ["Stay on","Keep to","Stick with","Maintain course","Continue on","Follow","Adhere to"]
example_sentence: She steered the conversation off the uncomfortable topic. The driver steered off the main highway. He tried to steer his mind off his worries. They steered off the beaten path to explore new areas.

english_meaning: To guide or direct something or someone outward or away from a place. To navigate out of a situation or location. To maneuver something out of a position. To drive or pilot out of an area.
example_sentence: He steered the boat out of the harbor. She steered the conversation out of difficult territory. The driver carefully steered out of the tight parking spot. They managed to steer out of the crisis.

english_meaning: To guide or navigate someone or something through a difficult situation, process, or period. To successfully manage or handle challenges, obstacles, or complex circumstances. To help someone get through a problematic or challenging experience.
synonyms: ["Guide through","Navigate through","Lead through","Pilot through","Direct through","Manage through","See through","Shepherd through"]
example_sentence: The experienced captain steered the ship through the storm. The consultant helped steer the company through financial difficulties. She steered her family through a very challenging year. The lawyer steered his client through the complex legal process.

english_meaning: To guide or direct someone or something in the direction of a particular goal, topic, or destination. To influence a conversation, decision, or action toward a specific outcome. To gradually move or redirect attention, effort, or focus toward something.
synonyms: ["Direct toward","Guide toward","Lead toward","Channel toward","Point toward","Aim toward","Orient toward","Move toward","Shift toward"]
antonyms: ["Steer away from","Divert from","Lead away","Redirect from","Turn from","Avoid","Discourage from"]
example_sentence: The teacher tried to steer the discussion towards the main topic. She steered the conversation towards her recent achievements. The manager steered the team towards a more collaborative approach. Parents should steer their children towards healthy habits.

english_meaning: The main upright part of a plant that supports leaves, flowers, and fruit. The long thin supporting part of an object such as a glass or a pipe. The base form of a word to which endings are added. To stop or restrict the flow or spread of something. To originate from or be caused by something.
example_sentence: The stem of the sunflower is thick and strong. She held the glass carefully by its stem. The stem of the word walking is walk. The government took steps to stem the spread of the disease.

english_meaning: A family tree or lineage. A recorded genealogy or pedigree. A tree diagram showing the evolutionary descent and relationship of different manuscript versions of a text
example_sentence: The historian spent years reconstructing the royal stema. A detailed stema was drawn to show the relationships between the medieval manuscripts. The noble family proudly displayed their ancient stema in the great hall. By analyzing the stema, researchers could identify the original source text. The ancient stema revealed a long line of courageous warriors.

english_meaning: A person, tool, or machine that removes stems from plants, fruits, or tobacco leaves. A linguistic algorithm or computer program that reduces words to their base or root form by stripping suffixes and prefixes.
example_sentence: The factory uses a large mechanical stemmer to prepare the freshly picked cherries for canning. In natural language processing, a stemmer reduces variations of words like 'running' down to the root 'run'. She worked long hours as a tobacco stemmer during the busy harvest season. This search engine applies an aggressive stemmer to match diverse keyword combinations accurately.

english_meaning: The process of reducing a word to its root or base form by removing endings. A technique in language processing used to group related word forms together. The act of stopping or checking the flow of something. Present participle of the verb stem, meaning to originate from a particular source.
example_sentence: Stemming reduces the words running and runs to the form run. Search engines often use stemming to improve results. The nurse succeeded in stemming the bleeding. Many of these problems are stemming from poor planning.

english_meaning: A strong unpleasant smell. A bad effect that follows an unpleasant event or situation and is noticeable for a long time.
example_sentence: I caught the stench of fear from the duke and his men. The stench of rotting fish filled the hut. We finally discovered the dead rat that was causing the stench in the basement

english_meaning: Physically move sideways to allow passage. Give up a position, role, or responsibility temporarily or permanently to let someone else take over. To allow someone else to take the lead or handle a situation.
example_sentence: Please step aside so others can pass. The manager stepped aside to let his deputy take charge. She stepped aside from the project temporarily. When the argument heated up, he stepped aside to avoid conflict.

english_meaning: To physically moving a step backward, creating space or distance. Figuratively, it can mean taking a pause to reflect, reassess, or gain perspective before acting.
example_sentence: She stepped back to get a better view of the painting. I need to step back and think before making a decision. He stepped back when he saw the dog growling. Sometimes it helps to step back from your work and rest your mind.

english_meaning: To leave a position of authority voluntarily. To decrease in power, importance, or intensity.
example_sentence: The CEO decided to step down after ten years in the company. He stepped down from the committee due to health issues. The government stepped down some regulations to ease business. She stepped down to let a younger manager take charge.

english_meaning: To intervene in a situation to help, control, or stop something. To enter a place suddenly or briefly. To take over someone’s role or responsibility temporarily. To become involved when action is needed.
example_sentence: The teacher had to step in when the students started arguing. She stepped in to manage the office while her boss was on leave. The police stepped in to control the crowd. He stepped in quickly to prevent a serious mistake.

english_meaning: To physically enter a space or area. To take on a role, responsibility, or situation, often replacing someone else.
example_sentence: She stepped into the room quietly. After the manager resigned, he stepped into the leadership role. I stepped into the shoes of my predecessor to continue the project. The firefighter stepped into the burning building without hesitation.

english_meaning: To leave or depart from a place. To measure distance by steps. To begin moving in an organized way. Informal command meaning go away.
example_sentence: The children stepped off the bus and ran toward their parents. He stepped off the stage after finishing his speech. The officer asked the soldiers to step off at dawn. She stepped off the distance between the two trees to estimate the length.

english_meaning: To place your foot onto or over something, often accidentally or intentionally. To tread on someone’s feelings or rights, to act in a domineering or aggressive way. To accelerate, especially a vehicle, by pressing the pedal.
example_sentence: She stepped on a nail in the backyard. Don’t step on his pride by criticizing him publicly. Step on the accelerator to reach on time. The government stepped on protests to maintain order. Step on it! We are late for the meeting.

english_meaning: To leave a room, building, or place for a short period. To go outside. To attend an event or social gathering. To act boldly or assertively in a situation.
example_sentence: I need to step out for a moment to take a call. She stepped out to get some fresh air. He stepped out to attend the meeting downtown. The young manager stepped out confidently to present his ideas.

english_meaning: Physically raising your foot to move past an object without stepping on it. Ignoring rules, problems, or obstacles; to bypass or disregard something.
example_sentence: She carefully stepped over the puddle. The soldier stepped over the barrier. He stepped over the rules to finish the project faster. Don’t step over people’s feelings.

english_meaning: To increase the level, amount, or intensity of something. To take action or responsibility, especially when needed. To move closer or forward physically.
example_sentence: The company decided to step up production to meet demand. She stepped up and took responsibility for the project. Volunteers stepped up during the flood crisis. He stepped up to the microphone and gave his speech.

english_meaning: To accept responsibility and take action. To willingly take responsibility in a difficult or important situation and act with courage or initiative
synonyms: ["Take responsibility","Rise to the occasion","Take charge","Accept the challenge"]
antonyms: ["Avoid responsibility","Back away","Shrink from duty","Refuse to act"]
example_sentence: When the team leader resigned, she stepped up to the plate and managed the project. It is time for the government to step up to the plate and address climate risks. He stepped up to the plate during the crisis and helped the community. A good manager knows when to step up to the plate and make tough decisions.

english_meaning: To improve your performance, effort, or skills in order to do better than before or compete at a higher level. To start performing better than you currently are. It is used when someone needs to increase effort, improve skills, or raise the quality of work or behavior in order to succeed or compete.
synonyms: ["Improve performance","Raise your standards","Work harder","Upgrade your skills","Level up"]
example_sentence: If you want to get promoted, you need to step up your game. The team must step up their game to win the final match. She stepped up her game and passed the exam with top marks. You need to step up your game if you want to compete in this industry.

english_meaning: A short folding ladder with flat steps and a small platform. A portable piece of equipment with a supporting frame used for reaching high places.
example_sentence: He used a stepladder to change the light bulb in the living room. The painter stood on a tall stepladder to reach the ceiling. We keep a small stepladder in the kitchen for reaching high shelves. She carefully climbed the stepladder to paint the window frames. Please make sure the stepladder is stable before climbing on it.

english_meaning: To form a fixed idea about a person or thing which may not really be true. A  fixed idea or image that many people have of a particular type of person or thing, but which is often not true in reality and may cause hurt and offence. A generalized belief or assumption about a group of people or things that may not accurately reflect reality. It can be based on race, gender, age, profession, or other characteristics and often leads to unfair judgments.
example_sentence: You shouldn’t stereotype people based on their accent. Teachers often stereotype students by their grades. Media tends to stereotype minorities. She was stereotyped as a shy person just because she was quiet.

english_meaning: Unable to produce offspring or lacking the ability to grow or develop. Not producing anything of value; unproductive, barren. Completely clean, free from bacteria or germs.
example_sentence: The couple discovered they were sterile and could not have children. The desert soil is sterile and cannot support crops. The surgeon used sterile gloves during the operation. His arguments were sterile and did not convince anyone.

english_meaning: The process of destroying or removing all microorganisms, including resistant spores, from an object or environment. A medical or surgical procedure that permanently prevents reproduction. The act of making something sterile or unproductive.
example_sentence: Sterilization of surgical instruments prevents infection. The laboratory follows strict sterilization procedures. She asked the doctor about permanent sterilization. Steam sterilization can destroy resistant spores.

english_meaning: Make something free from bacteria or other living microorganisms. Deprive a person or animal of the ability to produce offspring.
example_sentence: The medical staff must sterilize all surgical instruments before the operation. We always boil the baby's feeding bottles to sterilize them properly. The local government launched a campaign to sterilize stray dogs in the city. Radiation is often used to sterilize medical equipment packed in plastic. It is crucial to sterilize the wound to prevent any severe infection.

english_meaning: A device, machine, chemical, or person used to make something free of microorganisms. An appliance used to disinfect feeding bottles or medical instruments. An agent or procedure that makes a person or animal infertile.
example_sentence: The hospital installed a new steam sterilizer. Place the instruments in the sterilizer after use. Parents often use a bottle sterilizer. The technician checked that the sterilizer reached the correct temperature.

english_meaning: Of a person's work, efforts, or qualities being excellent or valuable. Being of the highest standard or quality. British money or currency. Made of standard silver
example_sentence: He has done a sterling job in organizing the charity event. She possesses a sterling reputation for honesty and integrity in her field. The antique bracelet is beautifully crafted from solid sterling silver. The value of sterling fell sharply against the dollar today. They showed sterling qualities during the unexpected crisis.

english_meaning: Serious, strict and firm in manner. Showing severe disapproval or demanding obedience. Unyielding, harsh or uncompromising in attitude. The rear or back part of a ship or boat.
example_sentence: The teacher gave the noisy student a stern look. The judge issued a stern warning to the accused. His father was a stern but loving man. The sailor stood at the stern of the ship. She spoke in a stern voice to maintain discipline.

english_meaning: The long, flat bone located in the centre of the chest to which most of the ribs are attached. Commonly known as the breastbone. A bone that forms the front wall of the chest and protects the heart and lungs. The central chest bone used as a landmark for chest compressions during CPR.
example_sentence: The surgeon made a careful incision along the sternum. He felt a sharp pain behind his sternum after the accident. The ribs are joined to the sternum by strips of cartilage. Chest compressions should be given over the lower half of the sternum.

english_meaning: Any of a large class of organic compounds with a characteristic molecular structure. A synthetic hormone or drug used in medicine to reduce inflammation. A performance-enhancing substance or anabolic drug used to artificially promote muscle growth.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed a steroid cream to treat her skin rash. Many bodybuilders were accused of using steroids to increase their muscle mass. Prolonged use of an artificial steroid can cause severe health complications. The anti-inflammatory steroid helped reduce the swelling in his injured knee. She is currently taking a steroid to manage her severe asthma.

english_meaning: A medical instrument used for listening to sounds inside the body, especially the heart and lungs. A device with earpieces and a chest piece used by doctors during examination.
example_sentence: The doctor placed the stethoscope on the patient's chest. She checked his heartbeat with a stethoscope. Every medical student carries a stethoscope. The nurse warmed the stethoscope before using it.

english_meaning: A person who looks after passengers on a ship, plane, or train. Someone employed to manage another's property or affairs. A person responsible for supplies of food to a college or club. Any person who takes care of something on behalf of others. In modern use, a caretaker or guardian of resources.
example_sentence: The steward brought us drinks during the flight. He worked as a steward on a luxury cruise ship. The estate steward managed all financial matters. Every citizen should act as a steward of the environment.

english_meaning: A female flight attendant. A woman who serves passengers on a ship, train, or plane. A woman employed to manage a household or estate. A female who takes care of guests or resources. The feminine form of steward.
example_sentence: The stewardess welcomed the passengers with a smile. She worked as a stewardess for a major airline. The stewardess helped the elderly passenger to her seat. Every stewardess is trained in emergency procedures.

english_meaning: To stay in a place for some time, usually longer than expected. To remain somewhere instead of leaving. It is often used when someone waits to see what happens next, stays to help, or does not leave immediately. It can sound casual and friendly and is common in spoken English.
example_sentence: I will stick around after the meeting in case you need help. She decided to stick around and see how things turn out. Stick around for a while, the show is not over yet. He stuck around even though most people had left.

english_meaning: To continue doing something with effort, even when it is difficult. To keep working on a task or activity without giving up, especially when it becomes hard or frustrating. It shows determination and persistence.
example_sentence: If you stick at your studies, you will improve your results. She stuck at the project despite many problems. Learning a new language is hard, but you must stick at it. He advised his team to stick at the plan until the end.

english_meaning: To remain faithful, loyal, or supportive, especially during difficult times. It is often used when someone does not abandon a person, opinion, or promise even when there is pressure to change or leave. To support someone or something consistently and not leave or abandon them.
example_sentence: She promised to stick by her friend during tough times. The lawyer decided to stick by his original argument. Good leaders stick by their teams even under pressure. He stuck by his values despite criticism.

english_meaning: To attach or fasten something firmly to a surface so it stays in place. To press or fix something onto a surface using glue, tape, or pressure so that it does not move or lift. It is commonly used for paper, labels, posters, stickers, or any flat object that needs to stay firmly attached.
example_sentence: Please stick down the label properly so it does not fall off. She stuck down the poster on the wall using tape. Make sure you stick down all the corners of the paper. The child carefully stuck down the picture in his notebook.

english_meaning: To extend beyond the surface or edge of something physically. To be easily noticed because it is different or unusual. To endure or persist in a situation, especially a difficult one.
example_sentence: His ears stick out a little, making him look funny. That bright red bag really sticks out in the crowd. She decided to stick out the tough times at her new job. The nail sticks out from the wall and could hurt someone.

english_meaning: To insist on having or getting something and refuse to accept less. To firmly demand a specific condition, amount, right, or benefit. A person who sticks out for something does not compromise easily and continues to insist until their demand is met. It is often used in negotiations, requests, or disagreements.
example_sentence: He stuck out for a higher salary despite pressure from the company. The workers are sticking out for better safety conditions. She stuck out for her original plan and refused to change it. They decided to stick out for a written agreement before signing anything.

english_meaning: To continue doing something, to follow or remain with something. To stay with a particular plan, task, rule, or person without changing or giving up. It emphasizes persistence, loyalty, or adherence.
example_sentence: She decided to stick to her diet despite the party. If you stick to the plan, you will finish on time. He sticks to his principles no matter what. I will stick to this book until I finish reading it.

english_meaning: To firmly maintain one’s position or opinion despite opposition or pressure. To continue defending your decision, belief, or opinion even when others disagree, criticize, or try to persuade you to change it. It shows determination and confidence in one’s judgment.
synonyms: ["Stand firm","Hold one’s ground","Stand one’s ground","Be resolute","Stand fast","Keep one’s position"]
example_sentence: She decided to stick to her guns even when her friends disagreed with her choice. The manager stuck to his guns and refused to change the project deadline. Despite criticism, he stuck to his guns and followed his original plan. You should stick to your guns if you are confident about your decision.

english_meaning: To say exactly what has been prepared or written. To follow an agreed plan, message, or procedure without deviation. To behave according to expectations rather than improvise or act independently.
synonyms: ["Follow the Plan","Stay on Message","Follow Instructions","Toe the Line"]
example_sentence: The spokesperson was told to stick to the script during the interview. He stuck to the script instead of improvising his speech. Despite difficult questions, she stuck to the script and avoided controversy. The actors must stick to the script during the live broadcast.

english_meaning: To rise or project upward. To rob someone using force or threat. To support or defend someone
example_sentence: A nail was sticking up from the wooden floor. The robber tried to stick up the shop late at night. She always sticks up for her younger brother. His hair sticks up no matter how much he combs it.

english_meaning: To defend or support someone or something, especially when they are criticized or treated unfairly. To protect, defend, or speak in favor of a person, idea, or right when others oppose it or treat it unjustly.
example_sentence: She stuck up for her colleague when he was blamed unfairly. A good teacher should always stick up for their students. He decided to stick up for his beliefs despite strong opposition. Friends are expected to stick up for each other in difficult times.

english_meaning: To continue with someone or something; to remain loyal or committed. To stay involved with a person, plan, activity, or idea despite difficulties or challenges. It implies persistence, loyalty, or ongoing support. It can be used in professional, personal, or casual contexts.
example_sentence: I will stick with this project until it’s finished. Stick with me, and I’ll show you the best route. She decided to stick with her old team despite the offers from others. If you stick with a healthy routine, you will feel better soon.

english_meaning: A specific issue or detail that prevents agreement or progress in a negotiation or discussion. The main obstacle or source of difficulty in reaching a solution.
example_sentence: The salary package became the main sticking point in negotiations. The sticking point in the deal was the ownership of intellectual property. Every other issue was resolved except for one sticking point. The peace talks collapsed over a single sticking point.

english_meaning: A bad or unpleasant outcome, often referring to death or serious trouble. A situation where someone meets a disastrous, harmful, or fatal outcome. It is often used in contexts of danger, crime, or risky situations.
example_sentence: He'll come to a sticky end one of these days if he carries on like that. He met a sticky end after getting involved with the gang. Ignoring safety rules can lead to a sticky end. The villain in the story faced a sticky end. Many pirates in history met a sticky end at sea.

english_meaning: Difficult to bend or move. The body of a dead person. To cheat somebody or not pay them what you owe them, especially by not leaving any money as a tip. Very much, to an extreme degree. Incapable of or highly resistant to bending.
example_sentence: The windows were stiff & she couldn’t get them open. The company faces stiff competition from its rivals.

english_meaning: Proud & refusing to change. Stubborn. Having a feeling of superiority that shows itself in an overbearing attitude. Sticking to an opinion, purpose, or course of action in spite of reason, arguments, or persuasion.
example_sentence: Four of his friends are stiff necked. He was too stiff-necked to admit that "underlings" might have useful ideas

english_meaning: The quality of being hard to bend, move, or stretch. Soreness and tightness in muscles or joints. A formal, unfriendly manner of behaving. Lack of ease or flexibility in movement or style.
example_sentence: He felt stiffness in his back after the long drive. The stiffness of the new shoes made walking painful. Morning stiffness is a common symptom of arthritis. There was a certain stiffness in her greeting.

english_meaning: To prevent something from happening, to prevent a feeling from being expressed. To withhold from circulation or expression. To cut off (the voice, the breath, etc). To kill by depriving of oxygen.
example_sentence: She managed to stifle a yawn. They hope the new rules will not stifle creativity. The government failed to stifle the unrest. The army stifled the rebellion. Stifling her impatience, she waited another half an hour. I felt I was stifling in the airless room.

english_meaning: So hot and airless that it is difficult to breathe. Preventing someone from expressing themselves freely. Suppressing or holding something back. Oppressive and uncomfortable in atmosphere.
example_sentence: The stifling heat kept everyone indoors. She found the rules of the school stifling. He struggled with a stifling sense of pressure. The stifling silence made the room feel tense.

english_meaning: In a way that makes breathing difficult. So hot or airless that it feels oppressive. In a manner that prevents free expression or development. Extremely uncomfortably.
example_sentence: The room was stiflingly hot all afternoon. It grew stiflingly humid before the storm. The atmosphere at home felt stiflingly strict. The bus was stiflingly crowded during rush hour.

english_meaning: A mark of disgrace associated with a particular circumstance, quality, or person. A negative label or social disapproval. In botany, the part of a pistil that receives pollen. A visible sign or characteristic of a disease. A mark of shame or discredit.
example_sentence: There is still a social stigma attached to mental illness. She fought to remove the stigma of failure. The stigma of the flower attracts pollinators. Divorce no longer carries the stigma it once did. He carried the stigma of the scandal for years.

english_meaning: A person who is strongly attracted to or fascinated by tattoos, body piercings, or branding. Someone who takes great aesthetic or romantic pleasure in body modifications. An individual who decorates their own body extensively with permanent marks or deeply admires it in others.
synonyms: ["Tattoo Lover","Piercing Enthusiast","Body Art Fan","Ink Lover","Body Modification Admirer","Modification Enthusiast","Tattoo Admirer","Ink Enthusiast","Body Art Admirer"]
example_sentence: As a dedicated stigmatophile, his body was completely covered in intricate ink designs. She opened a body art convention to bring together artists and fellow stigmatophiles. A stigmatophile appreciates the artistry and symbolism behind every tattoo and piercing. Dating a stigmatophile often involves visiting tattoo parlors together on weekends.

english_meaning: Quiet or calm people often have deep thoughts, strong feelings, great intelligence, or hidden abilities. A person who does not talk much or show off may actually be very wise, emotional, intelligent, or powerful inside. Just like calm water may be very deep, quiet people may have deep knowledge, strong character, or hidden talents.
synonyms: ["Quiet people often think deeply","Silent people may be wise","Depth beneath calmness","Actions speak louder than words","Wise men speak little"]
antonyms: ["Empty vessels make the most noise","Loud people are not always wise","Shallow minds talk too much","All bark and no bite"]
example_sentence: Ahmed rarely speaks in meetings, but his ideas are always brilliant, Still waters run deep. She looks quiet and shy, yet she writes amazing poetry, Still waters run deep. Many students ignored the silent boy in class, but he became the top scorer, Still waters run deep. My grandfather speaks very little, but his advice is always wise, Still waters run deep.

english_meaning: A long pole used to raise a person or structure above the ground. Also refers to stiff or unnatural style in speech or writing. Support post that lifts buildings above ground. Long poles used by performers or workers. Figurative use for artificial language or behavior.
example_sentence: A circus performance on stilts. The workers walked on stilts to paint the tall wall. Many houses near rivers are built on stilts to avoid flood water. The festival performer entertained the crowd while walking on stilts. His speech sounded formal and stilted, which made the conversation uncomfortable.

english_meaning: To encourage something to grow, develop, or become more active. To make someone feel interested and excited. To cause a part of the body or a system to become active or function more efficiently. To increase activity in an economy, market, or organisation. To rouse or excite to action or feeling.
example_sentence: The government introduced tax cuts to stimulate the economy. A good teacher can stimulate the curiosity of even the dullest student. Caffeine is known to stimulate the central nervous system. The article was written to stimulate public discussion on the issue. Bright colours and music can stimulate young children's learning.

english_meaning: The action of arousing interest, enthusiasm, or activity. The act of encouraging something to grow or develop. Physical or mental excitement. The application of a stimulus to a nerve or tissue.
example_sentence: Reading books provides great mental stimulation. The medicine causes stimulation of the nerves. Children need stimulation for healthy development. The debate offered intellectual stimulation. Bright colors provide visual stimulation for babies.

english_meaning: To touch skin or make a small hole to feel sharp pain, To make feel angry, upset, The sharp pointed part of insect that goes into skin leaving poisonous wound.
example_sentence: The scorpion has a sting in its tail. A wasp or bee sting is painful but not necessarily serious. Be careful of nettles they sting.

english_meaning: The quality of being unwilling to spend or give money. The habit or attitude of being extremely careful with money or resources, often to the point of not wanting to share or spend even when it is reasonable or necessary. A stingy person avoids generosity and prefers to keep everything for themselves.
example_sentence: His stinginess made it difficult for him to maintain friendships. She was criticized for her stinginess despite having a high income. Stinginess can sometimes lead to missed opportunities in life. The old man's stinginess became a topic of discussion in the village.

english_meaning: Not willing to spend money; very miserly. A person who is unwilling to spend money, share resources, or give help, even when it is reasonable or necessary. Such a person is excessively careful about spending and avoids generosity.
example_sentence: He is too stingy to buy gifts even for his family. The boss is stingy and never gives bonuses to employees. She saved money, but she was not stingy with her friends. Being stingy can damage relationships over time.

english_meaning: To produce a very bad smell. A strong and unpleasant smell. It is often used for rotten food, dirty places, or anything that smells extremely bad. To have a very bad reputation (informal use): The deal stinks (means it is suspicious or bad).
example_sentence: The garbage in the street began to stink after two days. His socks really stink after football practice. The fish started to stink in the hot weather. The whole room stinks because of the rotten eggs.

english_meaning: A shield-shaped insect that releases a strong unpleasant smell when disturbed. A sap-sucking pest that damages fruit, vegetables, and grain crops. A true bug of the family Pentatomidae with a broad flattened body. An insect that often enters houses in autumn looking for shelter.
example_sentence: The stink bug released a foul odour when I touched it. Stink bugs damaged much of the tomato crop this year. Several stink bugs crawled inside through the open window. He carefully swept the stink bug out of the kitchen.

english_meaning: A fixed or limited period of time spent doing a particular job, activity, or duty. A specific assignment or position held for a set duration. To limit, restrict, or be sparing with something, especially money, food, or effort. To give or use only a small amount of something. A small wading bird of the sandpiper family.
example_sentence: He completed a two-year stint as a volunteer teacher in Africa. After a short stint in journalism, she joined a law firm. Don't stint on quality when buying tools for daily use. The host did not stint on food and drinks at the party. He had a brief stint as the team captain last season.

english_meaning: A fixed amount of money paid regularly for services, study, or support. A set payment given at regular intervals to support someone, often a student, trainee, intern, researcher, religious worker, or employee in a training position. It is usually smaller than a salary and is meant to cover basic living or study expenses rather than full employment compensation.
example_sentence: The university gives a monthly stipend to research students. She received a stipend during her internship. The organization provided a small stipend to volunteers. His scholarship includes a living stipend.

english_meaning: To clearly state a condition or requirement. To insist on a specific condition. To make something necessary in an agreement. To require something formally. To specify or demand something as a condition in an agreement, law, or arrangement. It is often used in formal or legal contexts where rules or requirements must be clearly defined.
example_sentence: The contract stipulates that payment must be made within 30 days. She stipulated that no one should enter the room without permission. The rules stipulate wearing a uniform at all times. He stipulated several conditions before accepting the job.

english_meaning: Specified or demanded as part of an agreement or contract. Laid down as a condition. Explicitly stated as a requirement. Past tense of stipulate.
example_sentence: The contract stipulated a strict delivery date. She stipulated that the payment must be made in advance. The law stipulated equal rights for all workers. They stipulated the terms clearly in writing. The judge stipulated additional conditions.

english_meaning: To mix a liquid or other substance by moving an object in a circular pattern. To move or cause something to move slightly. To awaken or arouse strong feelings. A state of excitement, commotion, or disturbance.
example_sentence: She began to stir the soup with a wooden spoon. A gentle breeze stirred the leaves of the trees. The shocking news caused quite a stir in the small town. He has not stirred from his room all day. The inspiring speech stirred a deep sense of patriotism among the crowd.

english_meaning: To move or mix something around. To use a spoon or tool to move contents of a container in circles or random motion.
example_sentence: She stirred around the soup. Stir around the mixture. He stirred around the paint. Stir around the ingredients gently.

english_meaning: To mix an ingredient into something. To add something to food and gently mix until blended.
example_sentence: Stir in the sugar. She stirred in the spices. Stir in the milk slowly. Stir in the butter at the end.

english_meaning: To mix one thing into another. To incorporate something fully into a substance through mixing.
example_sentence: Stir the cocoa into the milk. Stir the oats into the yogurt. Stir the nuts into the batter. Stir the vegetables into the sauce.

english_meaning: To cause something, often trouble or emotions, to begin or increase. To create, provoke, or intensify feelings, reactions, or unrest.
example_sentence: His words stirred up anger. Rumors stirred up trouble. She stirred up interest in the plan. The speech stirred up excitement. The news stirred up fear in the town. His speech stirred up anger among the workers.

english_meaning: To deliberately cause problems, arguments, or unrest. To provoke conflict or difficulty among people.
example_sentence: He always tries to stir up trouble in the office. Don't stir up trouble by spreading rumors. Some politicians stir up trouble for personal gain. Her comments only stirred up trouble in the family.

english_meaning: Restless or crazed from a long confinement. Feeling trapped or mentally distressed from being kept indoors or in a confined space for too long.
example_sentence: After being stuck in the house for a week due to the heavy snow, I started feeling completely stir-crazy. The long flight made the energetic children go stir-crazy. If I don't get out of this hospital room soon, I'm going to go stir-crazy. We spent the whole weekend indoors and by Sunday evening we were all a bit stir-crazy. It is perfectly normal to feel stir-crazy during a strict lockdown.

english_meaning: Involving randomness or probability. Describes processes, systems, or events that are random and cannot be predicted exactly, but can be analyzed using probability
example_sentence: The weather follows a stochastic pattern during the monsoon Stock market prices are often modeled using stochastic processes The scientist used a stochastic method to simulate population growth Random noise in the signal created a stochastic variation

english_meaning: A barrier formed from upright wooden posts or stakes. A defense against attack or a means of confining animals. A military prison. To surround or protect with a stockade.
example_sentence: The settlers built a wooden stockade to protect their village. The soldiers were confined in the stockade for their disobedience. We need to reinforce the stockade before the attack. The captured animals were kept inside the sturdy stockade. They decided to stockade the perimeter of the newly established camp.

english_meaning: A large supply of goods, materials, or weapons kept for future use. A reserve stored for emergencies or shortages. To collect and store a large amount of something. To accumulate supplies over time.
example_sentence: The government kept a stockpile of medical supplies. Families began to stockpile food before the storm. The factory used its stockpile of spare parts during the shortage. Officials inspected the old stockpile of weapons.

english_meaning: A person who can endure pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining. Enduring difficulty calmly and patiently. A follower of the ancient Greek philosophy of Stoicism, teaching self-control and calmness. Unemotional and indifferent to pleasure or pain.
example_sentence: He remained stoic even after losing everything. Her stoic attitude helped her survive the crisis. The soldier faced the pain with stoic silence. She listened to the bad news with a stoic expression.

english_meaning: The endurance of pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining. Calm acceptance of whatever happens, whether good or bad. An ancient Greek school of philosophy teaching virtue, reason, and self-control. A composed and unemotional attitude towards difficulty.
example_sentence: She bore the long illness with remarkable stoicism. His stoicism during the crisis impressed everyone. Stoicism teaches that virtue is the only true good. The soldiers accepted their hardships with quiet stoicism.

english_meaning: A long draped robe or garment worn by women in ancient Rome. It served as the traditional woman's long dress, equivalent to the male toga.
example_sentence: The aristocratic Roman woman wore an elegant stola made of fine silk. In ancient times, the stola was a symbol of a woman's marital status. She draped the stola carefully over her shoulders to complete the historical costume. Unlike men who wore the toga, Roman citizens who were female traditionally wore a stola.

english_meaning: A long, narrow scarf worn around the shoulders. A long piece of cloth, often made of silk or fur, worn around the shoulders especially during formal events or religious ceremonies.
example_sentence: She wore a silk stole with her evening gown. The bride carried a white stole. The priest placed a stole around his neck. Her fur stole kept her warm in winter.

english_meaning: Showing little emotion or interest. Calm and unexcitable. Impassive. Unemotional. Not easily moved by feelings or surprises. Used to describe a person whose face or behaviour does not reveal their thoughts or reactions, sometimes appearing dull or indifferent.
example_sentence: He remained stolid even after hearing the shocking news. The guard stood at the gate with a stolid expression. Her stolid face revealed nothing about her true feelings. The accused listened to the verdict with stolid silence. Despite the chaos around him, the old farmer remained stolid and calm.

english_meaning: The organ in the body where food is stored and partly digested. The front part of the body around the abdomen. A person's appetite or desire for food. The courage or willingness to face something unpleasant. To tolerate or endure something difficult.
example_sentence: My stomach hurt after the heavy meal. She had no stomach for another argument. The medicine should be taken on an empty stomach. He could not stomach the unfair treatment of his friends.

english_meaning: A British unit of mass equal to fourteen pounds or about 6·35 kilograms. A hard solid mineral material found in the ground. A small piece of rock. A precious gem used in jewellery. The hard seed inside some fruits. To throw stones at someone.
example_sentence: He lost two stone after months of exercise. The old bridge is built of stone. She wears a ring with a bright blue stone. Remove the stone before eating the mango.

english_meaning: Something that has become fully cold and has no warmth left. A person who shows no feelings, kindness, or mercy. Used informally to show complete certainty. Used informally to describe sudden fear or shock. Describes complete silence or lack of movement.
example_sentence: The tea was stone cold when I returned. The criminal gave a stone cold reply without any regret. It is a stone cold fact that practice improves skill. I was stone cold after hearing the loud explosion. The street became stone cold quiet at midnight.

english_meaning: An aquatic insect whose larvae develop in clean, fast-flowing streams. A soft-bodied flying insect with two pairs of thin wings folded over the back. An insect used by scientists as an indicator of good water quality. A common natural model for artificial flies used in fishing.
example_sentence: The presence of stonefly larvae shows that the river is clean. A stonefly rested on the wet rock beside the stream. Anglers often tie flies that imitate the stonefly. Pollution has reduced the stonefly population in this valley.

english_meaning: A very short distance between two places. It refers to something that is nearby and can be reached quickly or easily. When a place or object is extremely close. The idea comes from the distance a person can throw a stone. If something is within that distance, it is considered very near.
synonyms: ["Nearby","Close","Near at hand","Within reach","Adjacent","Around the corner","Walking distance"]
example_sentence: The supermarket is only a stone’s throw from my house. Our office is a stone’s throw away from the railway station. They rented a hotel room just a stone’s throw from the beach. The school is a stone’s throw away, so the children walk there every day.

english_meaning: Having absolutely no money. Completely penniless, especially for a temporary period.
example_sentence: After paying the rent, I was stony broke. He was stony broke until payday. They came home from the festival stony broke. She admitted that she was stony broke and needed help.

english_meaning: A person who serves merely to support or assist others, particularly in doing unpleasant routine work. A subordinate used by another to do dirty work or act as a puppet. A straight man or foil to a comedian.
example_sentence: He was accused of being a political stooge for the corrupt mayor. The comedian used a stooge planted in the audience to deliver the punchline. She refused to act as a stooge for the management and stood up for her colleagues. The dictator relied on his willing stooges to carry out the oppressive laws. They viewed him merely as a corporate stooge who lacked his own opinions.

english_meaning: A seat without a back or arms, usually for one person. A small support for the feet. Solid waste from the bowels; feces. A footstool. A base of a plant from which shoots grow.
example_sentence: He sat on a wooden stool at the counter. The doctor asked for a stool sample. She placed her feet on a small stool. Children often use a stool to reach the sink. The stool of the tree produced new shoots.

english_meaning: To bend the upper body forward and downward. To lower oneself in dignity by doing something unworthy. To lean over. To carry oneself with the head and shoulders habitually bent forward. Used both physically for bending down and figuratively for lowering one's moral standards to do something dishonourable.
example_sentence: He had to stoop to enter the small wooden door. She would never stoop to telling lies, no matter what the reason. The old man walks with a noticeable stoop. I cannot believe he would stoop so low just to win the election. Please stoop down and pick up the toys from the floor.

english_meaning: To stop walking or moving all at once, usually from shock or surprise. To become motionless because something has caught your attention. To be halted immediately by an unexpected event. To make someone stop instantly. To bring an ongoing action to a sudden and complete stop.
example_sentence: She stopped in her tracks when she saw the old photograph. The loud bang stopped everyone in their tracks. He stopped in his tracks at the edge of the cliff. The announcement stopped the negotiations in their tracks.

english_meaning: To stop treating someone unfairly by wasting their time. To stop deceiving or misleading a person with false promises. To stop causing someone unnecessary trouble or confusion. A demand that a person be dealt with honestly and directly.
example_sentence: Stop jerking me around and tell me the truth. The company kept jerking the customers around for weeks. He asked them to stop jerking him around about the payment. She realised they were jerking her around with vague answers.

english_meaning: To stay somewhere for a short time during a journey. To stay somewhere temporarily while traveling to another place, usually for rest, transit, or a short visit.
example_sentence: We stopped over in Doha on our way to London. The flight stopped over in Istanbul for refueling. I decided to stop over at my friend’s house on my way home. They plan to stop over in Karachi to meet relatives.

english_meaning: A violent weather event with strong wind, rain, thunder, snow, or dust. A sudden outburst of emotion, protest, or attack. To move or attack forcefully.
example_sentence: A storm damaged the roof. The decision caused a storm of criticism. Soldiers tried to storm the gate. She stormed out of the room angrily.

english_meaning: A lot of unnecessary anger, excitement, or worry about something small and unimportant. Making a big issue out of a minor problem.
example_sentence: Their fight was a storm in a teacup. The argument between the two coworkers was just a storm in a teacup; they solved it within minutes. People are making a storm in a teacup over a small typing mistake in the report. Don’t create a storm in a teacup; it’s not such a serious issue.

english_meaning: A great deal of anger or excitement about a very small or unimportant matter. An unnecessary fuss over a trivial issue. A minor problem that has been exaggerated out of proportion.
synonyms: ["Much ado about nothing","Fuss","Tempest in a teapot","Overreaction","Commotion"]
example_sentence: Their argument was just a storm in the tea cup and ended quickly. The media turned a small mistake into a storm in the tea cup. Do not worry; this dispute is nothing but a storm in the tea cup. What seemed a serious crisis proved to be a storm in the tea cup.

english_meaning: Affected by storms. Full of strong wind, rain, thunder, or rough weather. Marked by conflict, emotion, or disturbance.
example_sentence: We stayed indoors during the stormy night. Their marriage had a stormy period. The sea looked dark and stormy. A stormy debate followed the announcement.

english_meaning: A sequence of drawings or panels showing the planned scenes of a film, animation, advertisement, or presentation. To plan a story or project visually in panels.
example_sentence: The director reviewed the storyboard before filming. Students created a storyboard for their video. We need to storyboard the opening scene. The storyboard helped everyone understand the sequence.

english_meaning: A conclusion to an event that is perfect or ideal, much like a fairy tale. A happy and successful resolution to a difficult situation. A sequence of events that finishes in a highly satisfying or magical way. An outcome that seems almost too good to be true based on the circumstances.
synonyms: ["Happy ending","Perfect finish","Fairy-tale conclusion","Ideal outcome","Dream finish","Success","Triumph","Satisfying conclusion","Magical ending","Culmination","Climax","Perfection"]
example_sentence: Winning the championship in his final game was a true storybook ending. The couple's reunion after twenty years was the perfect storybook ending. Every athlete dreams of a storybook ending to their professional career. Despite the early struggles, the project had a storybook ending for the team.

english_meaning: Strong & thick person, Brave & determined
example_sentence: I am afraid of a stout man standing out side.

english_meaning: An apparatus for cooking or heating that operates by burning fuel or using electricity. A kitchen appliance for cooking food. A closed heating device. Past tense of stave, meaning broken or crushed inward.
example_sentence: She boiled water on the gas stove. The old iron stove kept the room warm. Do not touch the hot stove. He cooked breakfast on the electric stove. The stove needed cleaning after the meal.

english_meaning: A condition in which the eyes do not properly align with each other when looking at an object. A visual defect where one eye deviates. Commonly called crossed eyes or squint.
example_sentence: The child was diagnosed with mild strabismus. Doctors treated her strabismus with special glasses. Surgery can correct severe cases of strabismus. Strabismus can affect depth perception. Early treatment of strabismus improves vision.

english_meaning: To attack with continuous gunfire, especially from aircraft. To attack a ground target with repeated gunfire from low-flying aircraft or to attack someone or something with rapid sustained gunfire. It is mostly used in military and combat contexts. A military attack in which an aircraft flies low over a target and fires machine guns or drops small weapons repeatedly on ground targets.
example_sentence: The fighter jet began to strafe the enemy camp at dawn. Soldiers were ordered to strafe the battlefield from the air. The aircraft strafed the convoy moving through the desert. Enemy positions were strafed repeatedly during the operation. The pilot carried out a strafe on the enemy base. A sudden strafe damaged several vehicles in the convoy.

english_meaning: An angle that measures exactly 180 degrees. The angle formed by two opposite rays lying on a straight line. Half of a complete turn. The angle that separates obtuse angles from reflex angles.
example_sentence: A straight angle measures one hundred and eighty degrees. Two right angles together form a straight angle. The hands of the clock formed a straight angle at six o'clock. He drew a straight angle on the board.

english_meaning: To make something straight or remove bends and curves from it. To become straight. To arrange or tidy something into proper order. To stand up straight after bending. To resolve or settle a problem, confusion, or misunderstanding.
example_sentence: He straightened the bent wire with a pair of pliers. She straightened her desk before leaving the office. The road straightens after the sharp bend near the river. They met to straighten out the misunderstanding between them.

english_meaning: Easy to understand or do; uncomplicated. Honest and direct in manner or speech. Going in a straight course without turns.
example_sentence: The instructions are straightforward and easy to follow. She gave a straightforward answer to a difficult question. It was a straightforward journey along the main road. His straightforward manner won everyone's trust.

english_meaning:
Pressure on a system or relationship because great demands are being placed on it. 
Mental pressure or worry felt by somebody because they have too much to do or manage, something that causes this pressure. To injure yourself or part of your body by making it work too hard. To try to make something do more than it is able to do. To pour food, etc through something with very small holes in it, for example a sieve, in order to separate the solid part from the liquid part.
example_sentence: These payments are putting a strain on finances. The rope broke under the strain. He had a definite strain of snobbery in him
