english_meaning: To use all one's energy and determination to do something. To make a supreme effort to achieve a goal. To push oneself mentally and physically to the limit.
synonyms: ["Do one's best","Strain every sinew","Exert oneself","Strive","Endeavour","Go all out"]
example_sentence: She strained every nerve to pass the entrance examination. The rescue workers strained every nerve to reach the trapped miners. He strained every nerve to keep the business alive. They strained every nerve to meet the deadline.

english_meaning: To make the greatest possible effort to achieve something. To try extremely hard, using all one's strength and resources. To work to the very limit of one's ability.
synonyms: ["Do one's utmost","Go all out","Try one's hardest","Make every effort","Pull out all the stops","Struggle hard"]
example_sentence: The team strained every sinew to win the final match. Doctors strained every sinew to save the patient. We will strain every sinew to finish the project on time. He strained every sinew to support his family.

english_meaning: To make someone feel tense, anxious, or mentally exhausted. To put great mental or emotional pressure on a person. It describes a situation where someone’s nerves are stretched to their limit because of stress, fear, or continuous effort.
example_sentence: The constant noise of the traffic strained my nerves all day. Waiting for the exam results really strained her nerves The tense atmosphere during the meeting strained everyone’s nerves. Watching the horror movie late at night strained his nerves badly.

english_meaning: A device used to separate solid particles from liquids. A utensil or tool, usually with tiny holes or a mesh, used for removing solids from liquids, such as when draining pasta, washing vegetables, or filtering tea. It can also refer to a person or thing that filters or separates.
example_sentence: I used a strainer to drain the pasta. Pour the soup through a strainer to remove any lumps. She washed the rice using a fine strainer. The gardener acted as a strainer, keeping only healthy seeds for planting.

english_meaning: A narrow passage of water connecting two large areas of sea. A difficult or troubling situation, usually used in the plural. Narrow or tight in space. Strict or severe in nature.
example_sentence: Ships pass through the strait every day. The family was in desperate financial straits. The strait between the two islands is very narrow. He found himself in dire straits after losing his job.

english_meaning: Very strict or conservative in manners, morals, or opinion. A person or attitude that is extremely conventional, formal, or rigid in following rules, social norms, or moral principles. Such a person tends to avoid anything considered improper, immoral, or unconventional.
example_sentence: Her strait-laced attitude annoyed the group. The teacher is strait-laced. He has a strait-laced view of behavior. Strait-laced policies can feel restrictive.

english_meaning: A single thin length of thread, hair, wire, or similar. A shore or beach. To leave someone in a difficult position without means of transport or resources. To run aground. One part of a rope or cable. An element or component of a whole.
example_sentence: A strand of hair fell on her face. The storm stranded travelers at the airport. They walked along the sandy strand. He picked up a strand of gold thread. Two strands of the rope had frayed.

english_meaning: Left in a difficult or helpless position without the means to move or escape. Unable to leave a place because of lack of transport, money, or assistance. Left alone in an unfamiliar or unsafe location. Of a ship: run aground on a shore. Abandoned or left behind without support.
example_sentence: Hundreds of passengers were stranded at the airport due to the snowstorm. The car broke down and we were stranded on a deserted road. Many tourists got stranded in the city after the floods. The ship was stranded on a sandbank near the coast. She was stranded abroad without money or documents.

english_meaning: To kill someone by squeezing their throat so they cannot breathe. To suppress or restrict something. To choke. To hinder growth or development.
example_sentence: The killer tried to strangle his victim. Weeds can strangle young plants. High taxes strangle small businesses. She felt her fear was strangling her voice. He loosened his tie which was strangling him.

english_meaning: To kill or injure by compressing the throat. To stop the flow of something such as air, blood, or supply. To suppress or restrict growth, activity, or development. To choke emotionally or mentally by pressure or stress. In medical context, to cut off blood supply to an organ or tissue
example_sentence: The attacker tried to strangulate the victim with a rope. Tight clothing can strangulate blood circulation if worn too long. Excessive rules can strangulate creativity in a workplace. The growing tumor may strangulate nearby tissues and organs.

english_meaning: Relating to the identification of long-term aims and the means of achieving them. Carefully planned to serve a particular purpose or advantage. Of great importance within a plan of action, especially in war or business. Placed or done in a way that gives the greatest benefit.
example_sentence: The company made a strategic decision to enter the Asian market. The port holds great strategic importance for trade. They formed a strategic partnership with a local firm. Troops were placed at strategic points along the border.

english_meaning: Relating to strategy; an older and less common form of the word strategic. Concerned with overall planning rather than immediate details. Important for carrying out a long-term plan. Done according to a carefully prepared method.
example_sentence: The general explained the strategical value of the hills. Their strategical planning gave them a clear advantage. He wrote a book on strategical thinking in business. The move had strategical as well as political significance.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to a carefully prepared plan for achieving an aim. In a position or manner that offers the greatest advantage. With careful thought about long-term results. In terms of military or business strategy.
example_sentence: The cameras are strategically placed around the building. She strategically avoided answering the difficult question. The country is strategically located between two major markets. The firm strategically invested in renewable energy.

english_meaning: A plan that is intended to achieve a particular purpose. A careful plan or method for achieving a particular goal usually over a long period of time. The skill of planning the movements of armies in a battle or war, an example of doing this.
example_sentence: To develop a strategy for dealing with unemployment. Its all part of an over all strategy to gain promotion. We need to devise an effective long-term strategy. Poor marketing strategy was blamed for the failure of the service to catch on. The president held an emergency meeting to discuss military strategy with the Pentagon yesterday.

english_meaning: A soft red heart-shaped fruit with small seeds on its surface. A sweet berry eaten fresh or used in desserts and jams. The low plant that produces this fruit. A reddish-pink colour like that of the ripe fruit.
example_sentence: The children picked strawberries in the field. Strawberries with cream are a summer favourite. She made strawberry jam from the fresh crop. He ordered a strawberry milkshake after school.

english_meaning: To move away from the correct course or place; wander. Not in the right place. A domestic animal wandering without an owner. Occurring occasionally or at random. To deviate from a subject or moral path.
example_sentence: The child strayed from his mother in the market. A stray dog followed her home. Try not to stray from the main topic. He was hit by a stray bullet. The sheep strayed into the neighbor's field.

english_meaning: A long thin line or mark of a different substance or color from its surroundings. A continuous period of specified success or luck. An element of a specified kind in someone's character. To move very fast in a specified direction.
example_sentence: She has a stubborn streak in her personality. The basketball team is currently on a five-game winning streak. A fiery meteor left a bright streak across the dark night sky. The frightened cat streaked across the lawn to avoid the dog. He washed the window but left a dirty streak on the glass.

english_meaning: A small, narrow river or flow of running water. A continuous flow of liquid, air, gas, people, or things. To move or flow continuously in one direction. To transmit or receive audio and video over the internet in real time. A continuous series of events, words, or ideas.
example_sentence: A clear stream runs behind the village school. Sunlight streamed through the open window. A steady stream of visitors arrived all morning. Millions of people streamed the match live online.

english_meaning: To make an organization or system more efficient and effective by employing faster or simpler working methods. To design or provide something with a form that presents very little resistance to a flow of air or water, increasing speed and ease of movement. This often involves removing unnecessary steps or parts.
example_sentence: The company decided to streamline its production process to reduce waste. Modern locomotives are built with a streamlined design to cut through the air. You need to streamline your digital workspace to focus better on your tasks. The new software was developed to streamline administrative duties in the hospital.

english_meaning: Trying to hide something can sometimes make more people interested in it. A situation in which an attempt to hide, remove, censor, or suppress information unintentionally makes that information more popular and widely known. The Streisand effect happens when: (1) Someone tries to stop people from seeing or discussing something (2) The attempt attracts public curiosity and media attention  (3) As a result, the information spreads even more rapidly. It commonly occurs on: Social media, News platforms, Politics, Celebrity controversies, Corporate censorship, Internet culture.
example_sentence: The company tried to delete negative comments online, but the Streisand effect caused the issue to become viral. When the celebrity sued a blogger for posting photos, the Streisand effect made millions of people search for them. Government censorship sometimes creates a Streisand effect on social media. Attempting to ban the video only increased public curiosity because of the Streisand effect.

english_meaning: The quality of being physically strong. The power to resist force, pressure, or hardship. A good quality or attribute that makes someone effective. The number or size of a group that gives it power. The intensity or concentration of something.
example_sentence: He lifted the box with all his strength. Her greatest strength is her patience. The army marched in full strength. Test the strength of the solution before using it.

english_meaning: To make or become stronger, more powerful, or more durable. To reinforce or give additional support to something. To increase the intensity, effectiveness, or soundness of something.
example_sentence: Regular exercise will gradually strengthen the muscles of the back and core. The new treaty was designed to strengthen the alliance between the two nations. She worked to strengthen her argument by gathering additional supporting evidence. The government announced plans to strengthen the national health system. The community event helped to strengthen the bonds between neighbours who rarely spoke.

english_meaning: Marked by or calling for energy or stamina. Needing great efforts & energy. Needing or using a lot of physical or mental effort or energy. Determined and showing great energy.
example_sentence:
The ship went down although strenuous efforts were made to save it. He rarely does anything more strenuous than changing the channels on the television.
His doctor advised him not to do any strenuous exercise.
Strenuous efforts were made throughout the war to disguise the scale of civilian casualties.

english_meaning: A state of mental tension and worry caused by problems in your life, work, etc. Something that causes strong feelings of worry or anxiety. Physical force or pressure. Pressure or worry caused by the problems in somebody’s life. To give extra force to a word or syllable when saying it.
example_sentence: Thing can easily go wrong when people are under stress. She failed to withstand stress & strains of public life. She stressed the need for cooperation with the authorities.

english_meaning: To make something longer, wider, or tighter by pulling it. To extend one's body or limbs to full length. To spread out over an area or period of time. A continuous area of land or water, or a period of time.
example_sentence: Do not stretch the fabric or it will lose its shape. He stood up and stretched his arms. The desert stretches for hundreds of miles. She worked for a long stretch without a break.

english_meaning: To extend continuously into the distance. To spread from a point across a wide area. To appear long and uninterrupted as it recedes from view.
example_sentence: Green fields stretch away toward the mountains. The empty road stretched away into the mist. Sand dunes stretch away in every direction. From the tower, the city seemed to stretch away forever.

english_meaning: To reach out toward something one wants to take or touch. To extend the body or a limb in an attempt to obtain something. To strive for a goal that is difficult to achieve.
example_sentence: The baby stretched for the bright toy. She stretched for the handle above the door. He stretched for the final note but missed it. The young athlete continues to stretch for excellence.

english_meaning: An extra-long limousine created by extending the body of a standard car. A chauffeur-driven luxury vehicle with additional passenger space. A long vehicle commonly hired for celebrations and formal events.
example_sentence: The wedding party arrived in a stretch limo. They rented a stretch limo for the school dance. A white stretch limo was parked outside the venue. The stretch limo had enough room for ten passengers.

english_meaning: Long narrow lines that form on the skin when it stretches or shrinks quickly. Scar-like streaks commonly associated with pregnancy, growth, weight change, or muscle gain. Marks caused by changes in the skin’s supportive tissue.
example_sentence: She developed stretch marks during pregnancy. Rapid growth can cause stretch marks in teenagers. The lotion may soften the appearance of stretch marks. Stretch marks often fade gradually over time.

english_meaning: To extend the body or limbs fully, often to relax or exercise. To lie down comfortably at full length. To make something longer or wider by pulling it. To continue or spread over a longer distance or period. To extend a hand or arm toward something.
example_sentence: Stretch out your legs after the long journey. She stretched out on the sofa and fell asleep. The road stretches out across the desert. He stretched out his hand to catch the ball.

english_meaning: To extend as far as a particular place, point, amount, or time. To be sufficient for a specified purpose or quantity. To make an effort to reach or achieve a demanding level. To broaden a rule, meaning, or resource to include something.
example_sentence: The forest stretches to the edge of the lake. Our budget will not stretch to a luxury hotel. She had to stretch to reach the top shelf. That interpretation stretches the rule to its limit.

english_meaning: Able to be made longer or wider without breaking. Made of material that can stretch and return to its shape. Flexible and easy to extend. Capable of being expanded to fit different sizes.
example_sentence: These trousers are made from a stretchable fabric. The band is stretchable and fits any wrist. Choose a stretchable cover for the sofa. Stretchable materials are comfortable for sportswear.

english_meaning: A portable frame used to carry a sick, injured, or unconscious person. A device or frame used to stretch, support, or shape something. A wooden frame over which an artist’s canvas is stretched. A brick laid with its long side visible in a wall.
example_sentence: Paramedics placed the injured cyclist on a stretcher. The canvas was secured to a wooden stretcher. The rescue team carried a folding stretcher. Each stretcher in the brick wall was carefully aligned.

english_meaning: A person who carries one end of a stretcher, usually as part of a pair or team. A medical or military worker who transports injured or sick people on a stretcher. A rescuer assigned to move casualties safely.
example_sentence: Two stretcher-bearers carried the injured player off the field. He served as a stretcher-bearer during the war. The stretcher-bearers moved carefully through the narrow passage. A trained stretcher-bearer checked the straps before lifting.

english_meaning: Able to stretch easily and return toward its original shape. Made from flexible or elastic material. Informally, capable of being interpreted or extended beyond usual limits.
example_sentence: These stretchy trousers are comfortable for traveling. The bandage is soft and stretchy. Choose a stretchy fabric for the costume. That is a rather stretchy interpretation of the rule.

english_meaning: To scatter things loosely over a surface or area. To cover a place by spreading objects untidily across it. To lie scattered here and there over a wide area. To sprinkle or spread something such as flowers, leaves, or papers.
example_sentence: They strewed rose petals along the path. Papers were strewn across the office floor. Autumn leaves strew the garden every evening. Broken glass was strewn all over the road.

english_meaning: Demanding that rules and standards be obeyed exactly. Firm in discipline and not allowing freedom or excuses. Exact, precise, and complete in meaning or application. Severe in controlling behaviour, especially of children or students.
example_sentence: Our school has strict rules about uniforms. His parents were very strict about bedtime. The word is not a translation in the strict sense. Strict security checks were carried out at the airport.

english_meaning: To walk with long, decisive steps in a specified direction. A long step or a stage of progress in a particular activity. It often implies confidence, purpose, or speed.
example_sentence: She took a long stride across the puddle to keep her shoes dry. The team is making great strides in cancer research this year. He strode confidently into the boardroom to present his new proposal. With every stride, the athlete felt a step closer to the finish line.

english_meaning: To keep doing something as well as somebody else, even though they keep making it harder for you. Keeping up exactly with someone (in speed, progress, or ability). To move or perform in equal measure, showing no weakness or falling behind.
synonyms: ["Step by step","Pace for pace","Side by side","Shoulder to shoulder","Equally matched"]
example_sentence: We’ve managed to match our closest competitors stride for stride as regards prices. The younger runner went stride for stride with the champion until the final lap (= He kept pace equally, showing equal strength and ability).

english_meaning: Loud and harsh; grating. Presenting a point of view, especially a controversial one, in an excessively forceful or unpleasant way. It describes sound or behavior that is piercing and insistent.
example_sentence: The strident sound of the fire alarm woke everyone in the building. Her strident political views often lead to heated debates during dinner. The bird's strident calls could be heard from the other side of the valley. Critics were strident in their condemnation of the new government policy.

english_meaning: In a loud, harsh, and unpleasant tone of voice. In a forceful and aggressively insistent manner. In a way that expresses opinions very strongly and often offensively. Sharply and shrilly, in a manner that grates on the ear.
example_sentence: She stridently opposed the new policy at the meeting. The speaker argued stridently against the proposal. He stridently demanded an immediate apology. The alarm rang stridently through the empty hall.

english_meaning: Bitter conflict. Serious disagreement. Angry or violent struggle. Fighting or quarrelling. A state of hostility or rivalry between people or groups. Strife refers to intense conflict, discord, or contention that may be verbal, emotional, or physical, often arising from opposing interests, beliefs, or ambitions.
example_sentence: Years of political strife left the country weak and divided. The two brothers lived in constant strife over their father's property. Religious strife tore the region apart for decades. The company was full of internal strife between managers. Peace talks were held to end the long civil strife.

word: Strike while the iron is hot
english_meaning: Act at the right time before the opportunity is lost. This proverb comes from blacksmith work. Iron can only be shaped when it is hot. If you wait, it cools down and becomes hard. The saying advises people to take action when conditions are favorable instead of delaying.
example_sentence: Strike while the iron is hot and apply now. You must strike while the iron is hot in business. They struck while the iron was hot and succeeded. Strike while the iron is hot before it’s too late.

english_meaning: A thin cord made of twisted threads used for tying or fastening. A piece of thin rope or twine. A series of similar things or events coming one after another. A stretched wire on a musical instrument that produces sound. To thread objects together on a cord. To arrange in a line or sequence. In computing, a sequence of characters treated as one unit.
example_sentence: She tied the parcel with a piece of string. The guitar has six strings. He pulled a string of colourful beads from his pocket. A string of accidents happened on that road last week. The children strung the flowers together to make a garland.

english_meaning: Having strings. Fitted with strings. Used to describe musical instruments that produce sound by means of stretched strings, such as the guitar, violin, sitar, or harp. Anything that has been threaded or tied with a string.
example_sentence: The violin is a beautiful stringed instrument. He plays several stringed instruments including the sitar and guitar. The orchestra has a large section of stringed instruments. She hung a stringed lamp above the doorway. The museum displayed ancient stringed instruments from Asia.

english_meaning: Very strict, severe, or demanding. Used for very tight control, firm discipline, or uncompromising authority. Describes difficult economic conditions, tight budgets, or limited resources. Very high and demanding standards that require careful compliance.
example_sentence: The government introduced stringent safety regulations. The company follows stringent quality standards. Due to stringent visa requirements, many applicants were rejected. The school has stringent rules about discipline.

english_meaning: A long narrow piece of something. A thin flat band of material such as cloth, paper, metal, or land. To remove clothes or a covering completely. To take away possessions, rights, or titles from someone. To peel off an outer layer. To empty or clear something of its contents.
example_sentence: He cut the paper into thin strips. The soldiers had to strip and change into new uniforms. Workers stripped the old paint from the walls. The judge stripped him of his title after the scandal. She placed a strip of tape over the torn page.

english_meaning: A young person, especially an adolescent boy who is tall, thin, and not yet fully developed physically. A youth in the early stages of manhood. The term is mostly used in literary or old-fashioned English to describe a slim teenage boy who has not yet reached full physical maturity.
example_sentence: He was only a stripling when he first joined his father's small workshop. The strippling stood nervously before the village elders. In the old story, a stripling defeats a mighty warrior with nothing but a sling. She remembered him as a thin stripling and was surprised to see him grown so tall. The army would not accept him because he was still a mere stripling.

english_meaning: A person who strips, removes, peels, or takes off an outer layer from something. The word is rare and uncommon in modern English. In some contexts, it may refer to a worker who removes bark, skin, covering, or similar material from an object.
example_sentence: The strippler carefully removed the bark from the tree trunk. A skilled strippler can clean old paint from wooden surfaces efficiently. The factory hired a strippler to remove the protective coating from the metal sheets. The strippler worked patiently to peel away the damaged outer layer.

english_meaning: To try very hard to achieve something. To make great effort, to struggle or work persistently toward a goal despite difficulties. It often shows determination and strong intention.
example_sentence: She strives to improve her skills every day. They strive for success in their business. He always strives to help others in need. We must strive to protect our environment.

english_meaning: A single movement of the hand, arm, or an object such as a brush or pen. A sudden serious medical condition caused by an interruption of blood flow to the brain. A gentle touch or caress. A hit or blow, especially in games like cricket, tennis, or golf. To move the hand gently over a surface. An act of skill or luck. A single mark made by a pen or brush.
example_sentence: He suffered a stroke and was taken to hospital immediately. She played a beautiful cover stroke to the boundary. The child stroked the kitten gently. With a single stroke of his pen, the president signed the new law. Winning the lottery was a real stroke of luck.

english_meaning: To walk in a slow, relaxed manner for pleasure. A leisurely walk. To wander without hurry. A calm and unhurried walk taken for enjoyment, exercise, or fresh air rather than for reaching a destination quickly.
example_sentence: They went for a stroll along the beach after dinner. She likes to stroll through the park every evening. The couple strolled hand in hand under the trees. Let's take a short stroll before the meeting starts. He was strolling casually when the accident happened.

english_meaning: Past tense and past participle of the verb strike. Hit forcefully. Deeply impressed or affected by something. Suddenly attacked by an illness, disaster, or feeling. Refused to work as a protest. Discovered something valuable such as oil or gold.
example_sentence: The bell struck twelve at midnight. I was struck by her intelligence and kindness. The village was struck by a powerful earthquake. Workers struck for higher wages last month. They struck oil after months of drilling.

english_meaning: To walk with a stiff, erect, and apparently arrogant or conceited gait. A rod or bar forming part of a framework and designed to resist compression. To show off one's ability or appearance in a proud way.
example_sentence: The peacock began to strut around the yard, displaying its feathers. He would often strut across the stage during his musical performances. Engineers added a steel strut to provide extra support to the bridge. She watched the models strut down the runway in the latest fashions.

english_meaning: To proudly show your ability, especially at dancing or performing. To show off your skills, talents, or style confidently in front of others.
example_sentence: Strutting your stuff to the latest chart hits. At the party, she really strutted her stuff on the dance floor. The players strutted their stuff in front of the selectors to get into the team.

english_meaning: Short, rough hair that appears on a man’s face a day or two after shaving. Short stems or stalks that remain in the ground after crops like wheat or rice have been harvested. It may symbolize neglect or a casual appearance in literature.
example_sentence: His face was covered with stubble after two days without shaving. The farmer walked across the stubble left after harvesting the wheat. She liked the look of light stubble on his chin. The stubble scratched his skin when he rubbed his face. In farming, stubble fields are sometimes burned or ploughed before planting again.

english_meaning: A person who refuses to change their mind or attitude even when reasons are given. Someone who holds firmly to their opinions, decisions, or habits, even when it is unhelpful or unreasonable. Such a person resists advice, arguments, or new information and keeps insisting on their own way.
example_sentence: She is too stubborn to admit that she made a mistake. His stubborn attitude made the discussion difficult. The child remained stubborn and refused to eat anything. He was stubborn about following his own plan. He was too stubborn to admit that he was wrong.

english_meaning: Unable to move, Unpleasant situation, place to escape, Unable to get rid of sb, Unable to answer or understand. Firmly positioned in place and difficult to dislodge. To hold to something firmly as if by adhesion.
example_sentence: The wheels were tuck in the mud. I can't get out I am stuck. We were stuck in traffic for over an hour. I was stuck with him for the whole journey. I hate being stuck at home all the day.

english_meaning: A large-headed piece of metal or plastic used for decoration or fastening. An animal, especially a stallion, kept for breeding. A vertical framing member in a building wall. Informal term for a sexually attractive or virile man.
example_sentence: He bought a fine stallion to serve as a stud on his farm. She wore a leather jacket adorned with silver studs along the collar. The carpenter secured the wooden stud to frame the interior wall. Everyone considered him a stud because of his confidence and charm.

english_meaning: Decorated or covered with studs, such as small metal knobs, jewels, or buttons. Possessing a surface densely set with decorative or functional items.
example_sentence: Her leather jacket was studded with silver spikes. The night sky was studded with countless twinkling stars. He wore a studded belt to the rock concert. The antique box was studded with precious gems.

english_meaning: Devoted to careful study and learning, especially showing diligence in reading and academic work. Marked by deliberate effort, attention to detail, and a serious attitude toward tasks. Spending much time and effort on acquiring knowledge through books and reading. Careful and painstaking in carrying out a task or duty.
example_sentence: She has always been a studious child who spends hours reading in the library.  His studious habits helped him secure top grades throughout university.  The studious student carefully reviewed every chapter before the exam.  Being studious does not always mean being naturally gifted, but rather consistently putting in effort.  The teacher praised his studious approach to even the most difficult assignments.

english_meaning: In a manner showing great care, deliberate effort, and attention to detail. Done with conscious and persistent effort, often to avoid something or to ensure correctness. With the diligence and seriousness typical of a dedicated student or scholar. Done very carefully and purposefully, sometimes implying an effort to be precise or to avoid a particular outcome.
example_sentence: He studiously avoided making eye contact with his former colleague at the conference.  She studiously prepared for the interview by researching the company in detail.  The committee studiously reviewed each application before making a decision.  He studiously ignored the rumors circulating around the office.  The artist studiously copied every detail of the original painting.

english_meaning: Matter, material, belongings, or things of an unspecified kind. A particular substance, activity, subject, or quality. To fill, pack, or force something tightly into a space. To fill food with a seasoned mixture before cooking. To overeat or feed someone excessively. To block a passage or defeat someone decisively in informal use.
example_sentence: I have too much stuff in my bedroom. What is this sticky stuff on the table? We need to stuff the turkey for Thanksgiving dinner. She tried to stuff all her clothes into one small suitcase.

english_meaning: Having poor ventilation, causing discomfort due to lack of fresh air. Being overly formal, rigid, or old-fashioned in behavior or style. Feeling congested or blocked, especially referring to the nose.
example_sentence: The room is stuffy. Don’t be stuffy in conversations. The room felt stuffy after everyone entered. He has a stuffy attitude towards modern fashion. My nose feels stuffy because of the cold. The office was stuffy and needed better ventilation.

english_meaning: To make useless or ineffective. To make someone or something appear foolish or absurd. To cause something to lose enthusiasm, energy, or effectiveness. To hinder, weaken, or limit someone’s abilities.
example_sentence: Repetitive office work can stultify even the brightest minds. The strict rules stultified all attempts at creativity. He felt that years of bureaucracy had stultified his career. Excessive regulation may stultify innovation in small businesses. The boring lecture seemed to stultify the entire audience.

english_meaning: To hit your foot against something while walking and almost fall. It is also used for making mistakes while speaking, thinking, or progressing in a task. An error, a false step, or a problem that slows progress or causes embarrassment.
example_sentence: He stumbled on a stone while walking. The company stumbled during rapid expansion. She stumbled while answering the question. His stumble cost him the race. The project recovered after an initial stumble. The speech had only one small stumble.

english_meaning: A problem or obstacle that stops progress. Something that makes it difficult to move forward, succeed, or understand. It can be a physical barrier, a rule, a mistake, or a situation that blocks achievement or development.
example_sentence: Lack of funding became a major stumbling block for the project. Poor communication is often a stumbling block in teamwork. Fear of failure can be a stumbling block to success. Complex rules turned into a stumbling block for new employees.

english_meaning: To shock or amaze someone so much that they cannot react. To make a person or animal unconscious with a blow. To surprise greatly. To leave someone speechless due to astonishment, shock, or admiration. To temporarily disable through a sudden powerful action.
example_sentence: The news of his death stunned the entire community. A heavy blow to the head stunned the boxer. Her beauty stunned everyone in the room. The audience was stunned into silence by the performance. The hunter used a special gun to stun the animal.

english_meaning: Extremely surprised or shocked. Rendered unconscious or dazed by a blow. Left speechless due to astonishment. Feeling temporarily unable to think or react clearly because of a sudden strong emotion or event.
example_sentence: She stood there stunned after hearing the shocking news. The stunned crowd could not believe what had just happened. He looked stunned when his name was announced as the winner. The stunned bird lay motionless on the ground for a few minutes. Everyone was stunned by the sudden announcement of his resignation.

english_meaning: Extremely attractive or impressive, extremely surprising or shocking. Causing a strong emotional reaction because of unexpectedness.
example_sentence: He suffered a stunning defeat in the election. His performance was simply stunning.

english_meaning: A dangerous and difficult action that somebody does to entertain people, especially as part of a film. Something that is done in order to attract people’s attention. To prevent somebody, something from growing or developing as much as they, it should.
example_sentence: He did all his own stunts. They jumped off London Bridge as a publicity stunt. you will stunt your growth by building all these muscles.

english_meaning: Prevented from growing or developing normally. Abnormally short, small, weak, or underdeveloped. Limited in intellectual, emotional, social, or economic development. The past tense and past participle of stunt, meaning to hinder growth or progress.
example_sentence: Poor nutrition left many of the plants stunted. The disease had stunted his physical growth. Lack of investment resulted in stunted economic development. The stunted tree produced very little fruit. Constant criticism can lead to stunted emotional growth.

english_meaning: A state of being stunned or amazed. Great shock or astonishment. The condition of being unable to think clearly because of surprise. A state of mental numbness or wonder.
example_sentence: She stared at him in stupefaction. The news left the audience in stupefaction. He looked at the wreckage in utter stupefaction. They watched the magic show in stupefaction.

english_meaning: To astonish or shock someone so much that they cannot think clearly. To make a person unable to think or feel properly, especially because of tiredness, drugs, or alcohol. To dull the senses or mind. To bewilder or stun with amazement or confusion.
example_sentence: The magician's tricks stupefied the young audience. Heavy drinking had stupefied his mind completely. The sheer beauty of the mountains stupefied the travellers. The bad news stupefied her for several minutes. Long hours of work stupefied his brain.

english_meaning: Causing great surprise, amazement, or shock. Extremely impressive or astonishing. So surprising that it leaves a person unable to think clearly.
example_sentence: The magician performed a stupefying trick. The stupefying news left everyone speechless. The view from the mountain was stupefying. He gave a stupefying performance on stage.

english_meaning: In a way that causes amazement or shock. To a degree that leaves one unable to think. In an astonishingly impressive manner.
example_sentence: The exam was stupefyingly difficult. The movie was stupefyingly boring. The prices in the city are stupefyingly high. The weather changed stupefyingly fast.

english_meaning: Extremely impressive or amazing. So large or great that it creates a sense of wonder or shock. It is often used to describe achievements, sizes, or beauties of a high degree.
example_sentence: The view from the top of the mountain was absolutely stupendous. The team put in a stupendous effort to win the final match. He earned a stupendous amount of money through his latest business venture. The construction of the ancient pyramids was a stupendous feat of engineering.

english_meaning: In an extremely impressive or amazing way. To an astonishingly great degree. In a manner that causes wonder or amazement.
example_sentence: The team performed stupendously well in the final. The concert was stupendously successful. She is stupendously talented at playing the piano. The project turned out to be stupendously expensive.

english_meaning: Having or showing a great lack of intelligence or common sense. Silly and badly thought out. Used informally to express annoyance with something.
example_sentence: That was a stupid mistake to make. Do not ask such stupid questions. This stupid door will not open. He felt stupid for forgetting the date.

english_meaning: The quality of having or showing a lack of intelligence or common sense. Behaviour that is extremely unwise. An action or idea that shows very poor judgement.
example_sentence: His stupidity in ignoring the warning caused the accident. I could not believe the stupidity of the plan. Sheer stupidity led to the loss of the file. She apologised for her stupidity.

english_meaning: A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility. It is a condition in which the senses and mind are dulled, often due to drugs, alcohol, or shock. A person in this state is unable to think or act normally.
example_sentence: He lay in a drunken stupor on the sofa after the party. The survivor was found in a state of stupor following the traumatic accident. The extreme heat of the desert induced a lethargic stupor in the travelers. It took several hours for him to emerge from his medication-induced stupor.

english_meaning: A state of being in or related to stupor, characterized by great diminished sensibility or partial unconsciousness. It refers to a person who is barely conscious and responds only to base physical stimuli. It is often used in medical contexts to describe lethargy or extreme numbness.
example_sentence: The patient remained in a stuporous state for several hours after the accident. The nurse noticed the patient was stuporous and unresponsive to verbal commands. Heavy medication left him feeling stuporous and confused. After the long surgery, the animal was still in a stuporous condition.

english_meaning: Strong and solidly built. Physically powerful and healthy. Firmly constructed and durable. Determined and not easily influenced or defeated. Robust in body, character, or design.
example_sentence: He was a sturdy young man who could lift heavy weights easily. The farmers built sturdy houses that could withstand storms. She showed sturdy resistance against injustice. Buy sturdy shoes for the long trek in the mountains. The bridge is made of sturdy steel and concrete.

english_meaning: A small dirty place where pigs are kept (pigpen). A dirty or untidy place where a person lives. A small painful swelling on the edge of the eyelid (also spelled stye in medical use).
example_sentence: The pigs were sleeping in the sty near the farm. His bedroom looks like a sty; it’s so messy. She has a painful sty on her left eyelid. Please clean your desk, it looks like a sty!.

english_meaning: Extremely dark, gloomy, or forbidding. Something dark, shadowy, or hellish, often invoking the darkness of the River Styx from Greek mythology. It describes places, atmospheres, or moods that are very gloomy, sinister, or oppressive.
example_sentence: The cave had a Stygian darkness that made it impossible to see. He entered the abandoned house, feeling a Stygian chill in the air. Her thoughts were filled with a Stygian despair after the loss. The novel described a Stygian underworld where hope was absent.

english_meaning: To prevent or hinder the progress of an action or intention. It specifically refers to placing an obstacle in the way of someone's plans or ambitions. This term is often used in both casual contexts and formal competitions like golf.
example_sentence: The unexpected blizzard threatened to stymie our travel plans for the weekend. Financial difficulties can often stymie the growth of a small business. The opposing team sought to stymie every move our captain made. A lack of proper documentation will stymie your application process.

english_meaning: Voluntarily. On one’s own initiative, without being asked or forced. A Latin legal phrase meaning that a court or authority acts on its own motion.
example_sentence: The judge raised the issue sua sponte. The committee acted sua sponte to protect the students. She sua sponte offered to organize the event. The court dismissed the case sua sponte after reviewing the record.

english_meaning: Charming, confident, and elegant, especially in manner. Smooth and polished in behavior or speech. Sophisticated and courteous in social situations. Displaying refined and gracious manners. Pleasingly polite and worldly.
example_sentence: He was a suave gentleman with a charming smile. The suave diplomat handled the difficult meeting perfectly. She admired his suave and confident manner. He gave a suave reply that impressed everyone.

english_meaning: Under judicial consideration and therefore not open to public discussion. Describing a case that is currently before a court. A legal rule preventing comment on ongoing proceedings.
example_sentence: The minister refused to comment because the matter is sub judice. Journalists must be careful when a case is sub judice. The judge reminded the panel that the issue remained sub judice. Publishing details of a sub judice trial can amount to contempt.

english_meaning: Completed in less than two hours. Very fast performance, short time completion, efficient timing, rapid achievement, compact duration. The term sub two hour is used for something that takes, finishes, or is achieved in under two hours. It is commonly used in sports, travel, movies, meetings, examinations, and performance records.
synonyms: ["Under two hour","Less than two hour","Short duration","Quick","Brief"]
example_sentence: The athlete achieved a sub two hour marathon record. We prefer sub two hour flights for business trips. The movie is a sub two hour thriller with fast pacing. The team completed the project in a sub two hour session.

english_meaning: Below zero degrees on a temperature scale, especially Celsius. Extremely cold, as in freezing weather conditions. Designed to work in or withstand freezing temperatures.
example_sentence: The climbers faced sub-zero temperatures on the summit. Sub-zero conditions damaged the water pipes. He wore a sub-zero sleeping bag during the expedition. The city recorded sub-zero readings for a week.

english_meaning: The part of the mind that we are not fully aware of but which influences our thoughts, feelings, and behaviour. Existing or operating in the mind without one's awareness. Related to mental activities that happen below the level of conscious thought.
example_sentence: Many of our fears come from the subconscious mind. Dreams often reveal our subconscious thoughts and desires. He had a subconscious fear of failure. Advertisements try to influence the subconscious of viewers. Her subconscious was troubled by the accident she had witnessed.

english_meaning: In a way that is not fully conscious. Without being aware of it. Done or felt in the deeper part of the mind that we do not fully notice. Acting from inner feelings, memories, or instincts without deliberate thought.
example_sentence: She subconsciously touched her hair whenever she felt nervous. He subconsciously copied his father's way of talking. People subconsciously judge others by their appearance. She was subconsciously afraid of the dark. He subconsciously chose the same restaurant every time.

english_meaning: The layer of tissue lying directly beneath the dermis. A layer made of fat and connective tissue that cushions the body. The tissue that insulates the body and stores energy as fat. The layer that attaches the skin to the muscles and bones underneath.
example_sentence: Subcutaneous tissue stores fat and keeps the body warm. Some injections are given into the subcutaneous tissue. The subcutaneous tissue cushions the body against knocks. Its thickness varies from one part of the body to another.

english_meaning: To overcome or bring someone or something under control by force or effort. It can also mean to calm strong feelings, reduce intensity, or make something less powerful. To conquer or defeat an enemy. To suppress emotions such as anger or fear. To quiet or soften sound, light, or color. To reduce strength or intensity.
example_sentence: The police managed to subdue the angry crowd peacefully. She tried to subdue her emotions during the meeting. The army subdued the rebels after a long battle. He subdued his excitement when he received the good news.

english_meaning: In astronomy, a star that is brighter than a normal main-sequence star of the same temperature but not as bright as a true giant star. A star in the stage of evolution between the main sequence and the giant phase, larger and more luminous than the Sun but smaller than a giant.
example_sentence: Procyon is a well-known example of a subgiant star. Astronomers study subgiants to understand how stars evolve. A subgiant is larger than the Sun but smaller than a giant. The telescope helped scientists identify a new subgiant in the galaxy. Our own Sun will one day become a subgiant.

english_meaning: Below the level of human beings in behaviour, ability, or living conditions. Relating to creatures that resemble humans but are not fully human. Sometimes used unkindly or offensively to describe cruel, brutal, or degraded behaviour. In science, referring to primates and animals close to humans in development.
example_sentence: The prisoners were forced to live in subhuman conditions. Scientists study subhuman primates to understand evolution. His subhuman treatment of the workers shocked everyone. Slavery reduced people to a subhuman status. The story described the villain as a subhuman monster.

english_meaning: A topic, issue, or matter that is discussed, studied, written about, or thought about. A branch of knowledge studied in school, college, or university. A person who owes loyalty to a king, queen, or government. A person or thing that is being observed, tested, painted, photographed, or talked about. Likely to experience something or controlled by something. To force someone or something to experience something, especially something unpleasant.
example_sentence: English is my favorite subject at school. The scientist carefully examined the subject during the experiment. The documentary covered an interesting subject about space exploration. All citizens should respect the laws of the country, whether they are subjects of a monarch or members of a republic.

english_meaning: To bring someone or something under control by force or power. To defeat, control, or dominate a person, group, or country so that they must obey and lose freedom.
example_sentence: The empire tried to subjugate neighboring regions through military force. History shows that no nation can subjugate people forever. The ruler used fear to subjugate the population. Many movements rose to resist attempts to subjugate their culture and identity.

english_meaning: The act of bringing someone or something under control. The process of forcing people, groups, or nations to submit to authority, power, or domination, often through political, military, or social control.
example_sentence: The subjugation of local communities led to long lasting social injustice. History records many cases of political subjugation through military force. The novel highlights the emotional effects of subjugation on ordinary people. Resistance movements often arise in response to subjugation and oppression.

english_meaning: A grammatical mood used to express wishes, doubts, suggestions or situations that are not real. Relating to verb forms that show possibility rather than fact. A verb form belonging to this mood.
example_sentence: In the sentence 'I wish I were rich', the verb is subjunctive. English uses the subjunctive far less than French does. The teacher explained the subjunctive mood with clear examples. 'It is essential that he be present' is a subjunctive form.

english_meaning: A lease given by a tenant to another person for part or all of the rented property. To rent out a property that you yourself are renting from someone else. An agreement in which the original tenant rents the property to a third party.
example_sentence: She took a sublease on a small apartment near the university. The contract does not allow tenants to sublease the property. He arranged a sublease for the summer while he was abroad. Under the sublease, the new tenant pays rent directly to him.

english_meaning: To rent to somebody else all or part of a property that you rent from the owner. To allow someone to rent all or part of a house or other building that you are renting from someone else. To rent property to another person while you are still renting it from the owner while still keeping the original rental agreement with the landlord.
example_sentence: Our rental contract states that we are not allowed to sublet the house. We have to inform the housing association if we sub-let a room. I have sublet a flat to my friend for the summer. We sublet our apartment over the summer.

english_meaning: To divert an impulse from its immediate goal to one of a more acceptable social, moral, or aesthetic nature. In chemistry, it refers to the process of changing a substance directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state. It can also mean to exalt or refine something to a higher state.
example_sentence: He tried to sublimate his anger into hard work at the gym. Many artists sublimate their emotional pain into beautiful paintings. Dry ice will sublimate at room temperature. Use your creative energy to sublimate any negative thoughts you have.

english_meaning: The transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase without passing through the intermediate liquid phase. In psychology, it is a mature type of defense mechanism where socially unacceptable impulses are transformed into socially acceptable actions. It represents the process of refining or purifying something.
example_sentence: The sublimation of dry ice creates a thick fog effect on stage. Sublimation is often seen as a healthy way to deal with internal conflict. Snow can disappear through sublimation during very cold, dry days. She found that the sublimation of her grief into poetry helped her heal.

english_meaning: Of such excellence, grandeur, or beauty as to inspire great admiration and awe. It refers to something that is supreme, outstanding, or elevated in thought and style. It can also describe a person's behavior that is haughtily aloof or extreme.
example_sentence: The view from the top of the mountain was absolutely sublime. She sang the aria with sublime grace and technical perfection. The dessert was a sublime blend of chocolate and orange. There is a sublime beauty in the simplicity of the desert landscape.

english_meaning: Affecting your mind even though you are not aware of it. Below the threshold of conscious awareness. Something that influences the mind without the person being fully aware of it. Not directly perceived but capable of affecting emotions, decisions, or behavior.
example_sentence: The advertisement used subliminal messages to influence buyers. He wasn’t aware, but the music had a subliminal calming effect. Subliminal cues in the film suggested the character was guilty. Some studies claim that subliminal exposure can change behavior subtly. The painter added subliminal symbols in the background that hinted at a hidden story. Subliminal fears from childhood can influence adult decisions without conscious awareness.

english_meaning: In a way that affects the mind without a person being aware of it. Below the level of conscious perception. Influencing thoughts, feelings, or behavior unconsciously. In a manner not directly noticed by the senses. Through hidden or indirect signals to the subconscious mind.
example_sentence: Advertisements often influence people subliminally. The music subliminally created a calm mood in the room. He was subliminally affected by the words he heard as a child. Colors can subliminally change how we feel.

english_meaning: To put under water or cover completely. To cause something to go below the surface of water or any liquid. To overwhelm or cover completely in a figurative sense, like emotions or tasks. To suppress or put aside temporarily (for example feelings or  memories). To be completely absorbed or involved in something (for example work or thoughts). To hide or obscure from view.
example_sentence: The submarine will submerge beneath the ocean surface. He submerged his hands in the cold water. The town was submerged after heavy rains. She was submerged in thought and did not hear the phone. He tried to submerge his anger to keep peace at home. She submerged herself in her studies before exams. The street was submerged under floodwater after the storm. His past memories were submerged deep in his mind.

english_meaning: The action of accepting or yielding to a superior force, authority, or will. The act of presenting a proposal, application, or document for consideration or judgment. A state of obedience or compliance. Something submitted, such as a manuscript or entry in a competition.
example_sentence: The rebels finally agreed to submission to the government. The deadline for submission of applications is next Friday. His submission to authority was complete and unquestioning. She prepared her submission for the writing contest.

english_meaning: Ready to obey or yield to others without resistance. Willing to accept the authority or control of another. Meek, humble, and unassertive. Showing a tendency to give in to the wishes or demands of others rather than to assert one's own.
example_sentence: She was too submissive to argue with her strict father. A good soldier must be submissive to the orders of his officers. His submissive nature made others take advantage of him. The dog rolled over in a submissive pose. She had a quiet and submissive manner in front of the elders.

english_meaning: In a manner showing obedience, compliance, or yielding to authority or control. Acting in a humble, meek, or passive way. With acceptance of another's will or dominance. In a way that shows readiness to submit or defer.
example_sentence: The dog approached submissively with its tail between its legs. She submissively accepted all the new rules. He submissively followed orders without question. The prisoner stood submissively before the judge.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being submissive, obedient, or yielding to authority. A tendency to comply with the wishes or orders of others. The characteristic of being humble, meek, or passive in behavior. Readiness to submit or defer to another's will or control.
example_sentence: Her submissiveness made her vulnerable to manipulation. The culture emphasized submissiveness to elders. His submissiveness was mistaken for weakness. They questioned the traditional expectation of submissiveness.

english_meaning: To present something for consideration, judgment, or decision. To yield or surrender to the authority, will, or control of another. To accept or comply with a condition, requirement, or process. To propose or suggest something formally. To give in or stop resisting.
example_sentence: Please submit your application by the deadline. The army was forced to submit after the siege. Students must submit their essays online. He refused to submit to their demands. The defendant agreed to submit to DNA testing.

english_meaning: Below the normal or average level, especially in terms of intelligence or development. Less than normal in quality, quantity, or degree. Not meeting standard expectations or requirements. Characterized by being inferior to typical standards.
example_sentence: The child was diagnosed with subnormal cognitive development. Temperatures were subnormal for this time of year. The test results showed subnormal levels of certain nutrients. Production rates have been subnormal this quarter.

english_meaning: Below the optimal or best possible level or standard. Not as good or effective as it could or should be. Falling short of ideal or maximum performance. Less than satisfactory or desirable.
example_sentence: The results were suboptimal and need improvement. Working conditions in the factory are suboptimal. The treatment plan was suboptimal for his condition. Current strategies are producing suboptimal outcomes.

english_meaning: In a manner that is below the optimal or best possible level. Not as well or effectively as could or should be done. In a way that falls short of ideal performance or results. Less than satisfactorily or desirably.
example_sentence: The system is performing suboptimally and needs adjustment. Resources were allocated suboptimally across departments. The project was managed suboptimally from the start. The team functioned suboptimally without clear leadership.

english_meaning: Lower in rank, position, or importance. Working under the authority of someone else. Less important than another thing. A person who is lower in rank. To treat something as less important than something else.
example_sentence: Every subordinate must understand the new safety rules. The manager listened carefully to her subordinate's concerns. In this plan, personal interest is subordinate to public duty. The committee decided to subordinate minor issues to the main goal.

english_meaning: To secretly persuade someone to do something illegal or dishonest, especially to give false testimony. To bribe someone to lie or give false evidence. To secretly influence a person to commit wrongdoing. To corrupt a witness or official for dishonest purposes. To persuade someone to break the law for personal benefit.
example_sentence: The lawyer was accused of suborning a witness to lie in court. He tried to suborn the official with money to change the report. The investigation revealed that several people were suborned to give false statements. Attempting to suborn a juror is a serious criminal offense.

english_meaning: To pay regularly in order to receive a service, magazine, or newspaper. To sign up to follow a channel, newsletter, or online content. To agree with or support an opinion, belief, or theory. To sign one's name at the end of a document as a formal agreement.
example_sentence: We subscribe to two daily newspapers at home. Thousands of people subscribe to her cooking channel. I do not subscribe to the view that money brings happiness. Both partners subscribed to the agreement in front of a witness.

english_meaning: An arrangement to receive a service, magazine, or product regularly by paying in advance. A sum of money paid regularly to be a member of a club or organisation. Money promised or given to support a cause or fund. A signature or formal agreement to something written.
example_sentence: I have taken out a yearly subscription to the magazine. Club members must pay their subscription before March. The library was built with public subscriptions. He cancelled his subscription after the price increase.

english_meaning: Coming after something in time or order. Following something else. Happening or existing later. Used to describe events, actions, or things that occur after a particular point or event.
example_sentence: Subsequent events proved that his warning was correct. The first meeting went well, but subsequent ones were less successful. Details will be shared in a subsequent email. Her subsequent behaviour showed she had learnt her lesson. All subsequent editions of the book include new photographs.

english_meaning: Afterwards. At a later time. In the period following something. Used to indicate that something happened after another event or action.
example_sentence: He was arrested and subsequently released on bail. The report was drafted first and subsequently approved by the committee. She joined the team in January and subsequently became its captain. The building was damaged in the earthquake and subsequently rebuilt. He fell ill and subsequently had to leave the job.

english_meaning: Too willing to obey other people. Serving as a means to help achieve a purpose. Ready to do what other people want without questioning. Excessively obedient, often in a way that lacks dignity or self-respect.
example_sentence: He refused to be subservient to his rude boss. Personal interests should be subservient to the good of the nation. Her subservient attitude annoyed her friends. The old system kept the peasants subservient to the landlords. In the film, the servant is shown as always subservient to the family.

english_meaning: To become less intense, violent, or severe. To sink to a lower level or settle down. To cease or diminish gradually. To sink into a chair, seat, or bed. To decrease in activity or strength.
example_sentence: The storm began to subside by early morning. The pain in his leg finally subsided after treatment. She subsided into the sofa exhausted after work. The crowd's noise gradually subsided.

english_meaning: To support an organization or activity financially. To pay part of the cost of something to keep the price low. To aid or promote with public money or a government grant. To provide financial assistance to reduce the burden on the consumer. To supplement the cost of a service or product through external funding. To maintain a particular activity by providing economic help.
example_sentence: The government decided to subsidise public transport to reduce traffic congestion. Many local councils subsidise arts programs to ensure they remain accessible to everyone. Farmers are often able to subsidise their income with government grants during droughts. The company agreed to subsidise the employees' gym memberships as part of a wellness initiative.

english_meaning: To support an organization or activity financially. To pay part of the cost of producing something to keep the selling price low. To provide a grant or contribution of money to help another person or entity. To reduce the cost of a service or product for the consumer through government or external funding. To promote the growth of an industry through financial incentives.
example_sentence: The government decided to subsidize public transportation to encourage people to leave their cars at home. Many local farms would go out of business if the state did not subsidize their crop production. Large corporations often subsidize child care costs for their employees as a benefit. The housing program is designed to subsidize rent for low-income families in the city.

english_meaning: Financial help given by a government or organization to reduce cost. Money or support provided by a government or institution to individuals, businesses, or sectors to make goods, services, or activities more affordable or to encourage certain economic or social policies. It is commonly used in agriculture, energy, education, and transport.
example_sentence: The government provides a subsidy to farmers to support crop production. Fuel subsidies help keep transportation costs low. Many students receive a subsidy for higher education. The company survived because of a government subsidy during the crisis.

english_meaning: The state of having what one needs to stay alive, especially food and shelter. The means of supporting life. A minimum level of existence. The ability to continue living on very little. Basic livelihood.
example_sentence: Many farmers in the area live at a subsistence level. Fishing provides the main means of subsistence for the villagers. The government promised support for those who could not earn their subsistence. The poor family struggled for daily subsistence. Subsistence farming is common in remote hilly regions.

english_meaning: Relating to speeds that are less than the speed of sound in a given medium. Traveling at a speed slower than Mach 1. Designating an aircraft or vehicle capable of maintaining flight at speeds below approximately 760 miles per hour at sea level. Involving or producing sound waves with frequencies below the range of human hearing, though this is more accurately termed infrasonic. Characteristic of or occurring in a flow of fluid where the velocity is everywhere less than the local speed of sound.
example_sentence: The passenger jet was designed for subsonic travel to maximize fuel efficiency. Subsonic speeds are generally safer for commercial aviation than supersonic ones. The laboratory conducted a study on subsonic airflow around the new wing design. Engineers measured the pressure distribution during the subsonic phase of the flight.

english_meaning: Not a standard English word. Interpreted as a compound of sub meaning under or lesser, and tail meaning the rear end. Could refer to something located beneath the tail or a subordinate tail like part. Uncommon in usage.
example_sentence: The vet examined the substail area of the dog. Feathers grew even in the substail region. The substail region requires regular cleaning. He noticed a small mark on the substail of the horse. Some birds have distinct substail markings.

english_meaning: A particular kind of matter with uniform properties. The real physical matter of which a person or thing consists and which has a tangible presence. The most important or essential part of something, such as the gist of an argument. Solid quality or character, often implying wealth, importance, or reliable stability. A drug or chemical that has certain effects on the body, especially one that is illegal or addictive.
example_sentence: The scientists analyzed the chemical composition of the unknown substance. His argument was eloquent but lacked any real substance or evidence. After years of hard work, she became a woman of considerable substance in the community. The treaty was criticized for being symbolic rather than having actual substance.

english_meaning: Below the usual or required standard. Not as good as it should be. Of lower quality than expected. Failing to meet accepted norms in quality, condition, or performance.
example_sentence: The building was demolished because of substandard construction. Many people live in substandard housing in the city outskirts. The company was fined for selling substandard products. His work has been substandard for the past few months. Substandard food was found in the storeroom during the inspection.

english_meaning: Large in amount, size, value, importance, or strength; considerable and significant. Something that is large, significant, solid, meaningful, or considerable in quantity, quality, value, or importance. It can describe money, evidence, support, improvement, buildings, meals, and achievements.
example_sentence: The company made a substantial profit last year. There has been a substantial improvement in her English skills. The police found substantial evidence against the suspect. He donated a substantial amount of money to charity.

english_meaning: To provide evidence that proves something is true. To support a claim with facts or proof. To confirm the validity of a statement. To give solid form or reality to an idea.
example_sentence: He could not substantiate his allegations against the officer. The research substantiates earlier findings. You must substantiate every claim with documents. New evidence substantiated her version of events.

english_meaning: Important, meaningful, or real. Having a firm basis in reality or fact; essential, significant, or meaningful. It can refer to a noun itself in grammar.
example_sentence: The committee made substantive changes to the proposal. She raised substantive questions during the meeting. The report contains substantive evidence supporting the claim. In grammar, “dog” is a substantive because it is a noun.

english_meaning: A person or thing that takes the place of another. To use one thing in place of another. To replace someone or something with a different one. A player who takes another's place in a game. Something used instead of what is usually used.
example_sentence: You can substitute honey for sugar in this recipe. The teacher was absent, so a substitute took the class. Butter is a good substitute for oil in baking. He came on as a substitute in the second half. There is no substitute for hard work.

english_meaning: The act of using one person or thing in place of another. The replacement of one item by another that serves the same purpose. In sport, the act of bringing a fresh player on for another. A word, value, or symbol used instead of the original one.
example_sentence: The coach made a late substitution in the second half. Substitution of butter with oil changed the taste slightly. The teacher explained substitution in simple algebra. Careful substitution of ingredients can make the dish healthier.

english_meaning: A trick or dishonest way used to achieve a goal or to escape a difficult situation. Deception used to hide the truth or to gain an advantage. A clever plan or action designed to deceive.
example_sentence: He used subterfuge to enter the meeting without an invitation. The spy relied on subterfuge to gather secret information. She obtained the money through subterfuge. Politicians sometimes use subterfuge to hide the truth. The children invented a subterfuge to skip school.

english_meaning: Referring to a region or space located underground or beneath the surface of the earth. It is often used to describe geological formations or hidden structures. It indicates something that exists out of sight below the ground level.
example_sentence: The explorers ventured into the dark subterrain of the ancient cave system. Engineers mapped the subterrain to plan the new subway tunnel. Ancient civilizations often used the subterrain for storage and protection. Deep in the subterrain, unique minerals were discovered.

english_meaning: An underground room, habitat, or area of ground. It is a variant of subterrain, specifically referring to the physical space or cave found beneath the earth. It can also denote a person or thing that exists underground.
example_sentence: The coal mine was a vast and dangerous subterrane. They discovered a hidden subterrane filled with prehistoric fossils. Living in a subterrane provides natural insulation from extreme weather. The secret meeting took place in a damp and quiet subterrane.

english_meaning: Relating to something existing, occurring, or done under the earth's surface. It can describe physical things like geological structures or metaphorical things like secret social activities. It often implies being hidden or out of sight.
example_sentence: The city has a vast subterranean network of tunnels and pipes. Some animals spend their entire lives in a subterranean environment. The resistance movement operated through subterranean channels to avoid detection. Geologists are studying the subterranean flow of water in the desert.

english_meaning: Having a comparatively fine, delicate, or thin physical layer or structure. Difficult to perceive or grasp completely due to extreme delicacy, faintness, or elusiveness. Characterized by intellectual cleverness, shrewdness, or cunning in a way that is not immediately obvious. Manifesting fine distinctions or delicate sensitivity in thought, argument, or analysis. Operating in a hidden, insidious, or highly refined manner without drawing attention. Known historically to describe something thinly composed or rarefied, such as a subtile gas or ether.
example_sentence: The ancient alchemical texts often refer to a subtile essence that pervades all matter. She possessed a subtile mind that could easily dismantle the most complex philosophical ideas. The chef used a subtile blend of spices that enhanced rather than overpowered the meat. He employed a subtile strategy to outmaneuver his opponents without them noticing. There was a subtile difference in the texture of the two fabrics that only an expert could detect.

english_meaning: Something that is gentle, not obvious, or hard to notice. Describes something that is delicate, indirect, or refined, and not easily seen, heard, or understood at first glance.
example_sentence: There was a subtle change in her voice when she spoke. The perfume has a subtle fragrance that is pleasant. His smile carried a subtle message of confidence. The artist used subtle colors to create a calm effect.

english_meaning: The quality of being delicate, precise, or difficult to notice. The ability to notice or express fine distinctions, nuances, or details that are not obvious. It can describe cleverness, delicacy, or indirectness in thought, action, or expression.
example_sentence: She appreciated the subtlety in his argument, noticing points others missed. The painter used subtlety in shading to create a lifelike portrait. His humor relies on subtlety rather than loud jokes. The diplomat handled the negotiation with great subtlety.

english_meaning: A residential area or district on the outer edge of a city or large town. A place where people live outside the busy city centre. An outlying part of a town that is mainly residential and quieter than the centre.
example_sentence: They moved to a quiet suburb of Karachi last year. Property prices in the suburb are lower than in the city centre. Many people commute daily from the suburbs to work in the city. The new school was built in a growing suburb. Life in the suburb is peaceful and family friendly.

english_meaning: Related to areas just outside a city. Describes places, lifestyles, or characteristics of residential areas located on the edge of a city, usually quieter and less crowded than the city center.
example_sentence: They moved to a suburban neighborhood for a quieter life. Suburban areas often have more parks and schools. He grew up in a suburban town near the capital. Traffic increases as suburban commuters travel to the city.

english_meaning: The act of trying to destroy or weaken a government, system, or authority, often from within. Secret action to overthrow or damage an established order. The undermining of the power, authority, or principles of an institution.
example_sentence: He was arrested on charges of subversion against the state. The government took strict action against acts of subversion. Foreign powers were accused of subversion of the peaceful nation. The book was banned for promoting subversion of religious values. Subversion of the rules cannot be allowed in any organisation.

english_meaning: Seeking or intended to undermine or overthrow an established system or authority. Tending to destabilise or challenge an existing order. A person who engages in subversive activities.
example_sentence: The pamphlets were considered subversive by the government and immediately banned. She was accused of distributing subversive material through her online platform. The novel was banned in several countries for its subversive portrayal of authority. He was placed under surveillance as a suspected subversive during the period of political unrest. A subversive element within the organisation was systematically working to undermine the leadership.

english_meaning: To try to destroy or damage a government, system, or set of beliefs. To secretly weaken the authority or power of something. To overturn or overthrow. To undermine the principles or effectiveness of an established institution.
example_sentence: They tried to subvert the government through false propaganda. Corruption can subvert the entire justice system. His writings were said to subvert the moral values of the youth. The general was accused of trying to subvert democracy. Small lies can slowly subvert trust in a relationship.

english_meaning: To achieve the desired result. To be successful. To come after someone or something in order, position, rank, or time. To inherit or take over an office, title, or role.
example_sentence: You can succeed if you work with patience. She succeeded in passing the final exam. The prince succeeded his father as king. One event may succeed another very quickly. The plan will succeed only with teamwork.

english_meaning: Coming after another person or thing in time, order, or position. Following. Taking over a role or office. Achieving success when used as the present participle of succeed.
