example_sentence: The succeeding chapters explain the theory in detail. Each succeeding year brought new challenges. The succeeding manager changed the policy. She is succeeding in her new business. The law affected succeeding generations.

english_meaning: The achievement of a desired aim, purpose, or result. The attainment of fame, wealth, or high social status. A person or thing that achieves the desired result. Favourable outcome of an attempt or effort.
example_sentence: Her hard work finally brought her success. The play was a great success with audiences. He owes his success to years of discipline. They had little success in finding the missing file.

english_meaning: Achieving the aim or result that was wanted. Having gained wealth, fame, or a high position. Producing a good outcome or working effectively.
example_sentence: The operation was completely successful. She is a successful businesswoman in the city. Their campaign was successful in raising funds. He made a successful attempt to break the record.

english_meaning: In a way that achieves the desired aim or result. With a good and favourable outcome. In a manner marked by achievement or prosperity.
example_sentence: She successfully completed her degree in three years. The team successfully defended their title. The medicine was used successfully in many patients. He successfully persuaded them to change the plan.

english_meaning: The act or order of following one after another. A sequence or series. The process of inheriting a position, title, property, or right. In ecology, the gradual replacement of one plant or animal community by another.
example_sentence: The company had a clear succession plan. A succession of storms damaged the coast. The king's death caused a dispute over succession. Forest succession can take many years. She answered a succession of difficult questions.

english_meaning: A person or thing that comes after another and takes their position, job, or role. Someone who inherits a title, office, or property. Something that replaces an earlier version of the same kind.
example_sentence: His son was named as his successor in the family business. The king had no successor to inherit the throne. The new model is a worthy successor to the previous one. She was appointed successor to the retiring principal. Every leader must prepare a capable successor.

english_meaning: The quality of expressing something in a clear, short, and direct way. Communicating ideas in a very clear and concise form without unnecessary words. It focuses on precision, clarity, and brevity so that the message is easy to understand and direct. It often valued in communication, especially in writing, presentations, journalism, and professional reports where time and clarity matter.
example_sentence: The teacher praised the student for the succinctness of his answer. Her speech was appreciated for its clarity and succinctness. Good writing requires both depth and succinctness. The report’s succinctness made it easy to read and understand.

english_meaning: To provide help, relief, or support to someone in distress or difficulty. Assistance, support, or relief given to someone in difficulty, danger, or distress.
example_sentence: The organization succored the families affected by the cyclone. Soldiers succored the villagers trapped in the valley. Volunteers brought succor to the earthquake-stricken areas. His words gave succor to those grieving.

english_meaning: Juicy, tender, and full of flavour, especially of food. Rich in moisture and pleasing to eat. Of a plant, having thick fleshy leaves or stems that store water. A plant such as a cactus that is adapted to dry conditions.
example_sentence: We enjoyed a succulent roast chicken for dinner. The mangoes were sweet and succulent. Succulent plants need very little water. She keeps a shelf of small succulents by the window.

english_meaning: To give in, fail to resist, or be overcome by something.  To die from an illness or injury. To be defeated by a stronger force. To lose control due to temptation. It refers to yielding to pressure, force, temptation, illness or any overpowering influence. It can mean surrendering emotionally, mentally or physically. It is often used when someone finally gives up after trying to resist.
example_sentence: The major has succumbed to his injuries and passed away. The town succumbed after a short siege. Thousands of cows have succumbed to the disease in the past few months. After a long battle, he finally succumbed to his illness. She tried to stay calm but eventually succumbed to fear. Many people succumb to peer pressure at a young age. The soldiers refused to succumb despite the difficult conditions.

english_meaning: Used to refer to a person, thing, or number without naming it exactly. It is used when the speaker does not want to specify details. Used to replace a specific name, amount, or detail. It shows that the speaker is not giving exact information. It can also be used when talking about an example in a general way.
example_sentence: He said that such and such happened yesterday. You must complete such and such tasks before leaving. She met such and such a person at the event. The teacher explained such and such rules in class.

english_meaning: To draw something into the mouth. To draw in liquid, air, or other substances through the mouth by creating a vacuum. Can also mean to perform poorly or cause annoyance in informal English. Act of drawing in liquid or air.
example_sentence: The baby sucks milk from the bottle. He sucks the candy slowly. This movie really sucks. She gave the straw a strong suck to get the juice.

english_meaning: To drink or swallow something quickly and eagerly. To drink something fast, often in large amounts or with enjoyment. It can also be used casually for food that is eaten very quickly. The phrase often suggests speed rather than politeness or manners.
example_sentence: He sucked down a glass of water after the long run. She sucked down her juice before leaving for work. The kids sucked down their milk in a hurry. He sat quietly and sucked down his coffee.

english_meaning: To pull something inside. To make something smaller or tighter, or to deceive someone into involvement. Become involved in something unpleasant.
example_sentence: The vacuum cleaner sucked in all the dust from the carpet. He sucked in his stomach before taking the photo. The tailor sucked in the waist of the trousers. She was sucked in by a fake online job offer.

english_meaning: To pull something in with force or attraction. To draw someone or something inside suddenly or strongly, either physically like air or water, or mentally by involving someone deeply in an activity or situation. Expel, throw out.
example_sentence: The powerful machine sucked the dust into its filter. She was sucked into the online debate and forgot about time. The whirlpool sucked the boat into the center. He got sucked into unnecessary office politics.

english_meaning: To remove something by sucking, often liquid, air, poison, or strength. To pull or remove something from inside another thing using suction or strong pulling force. It is commonly used for liquids, air, toxins, venom, or even energy in a figurative sense. It can describe physical removal as well as emotional or financial draining.
example_sentence: The doctor used a pump to suck out the poison. The machine can suck out excess water from the ground. He tried to suck out the venom from the wound. Long working hours suck out all his energy.

english_meaning: To flatter someone in order to gain favor or advantage. To behave in an overly polite or flattering way toward someone, especially a person in authority, with the intention of gaining approval, benefits, or special treatment. It usually carries a negative sense because the behavior is seen as insincere.
example_sentence: He keeps sucking up to the boss to get a promotion. She hates people who suck up instead of working honestly. You will not succeed by sucking up to teachers. He tried to suck up by praising every decision the manager made.

english_meaning: To try to gain favor by flattering or pleasing someone, often insincerely. To behave in an overly flattering way toward someone, usually a person in authority, in order to get something you want. It implies insincerity and self-interest. Ingratiate yourself with someone.
example_sentence: He is always sucking up to the boss to get a promotion. Stop sucking up to your teacher; it won’t help you cheat on the exam. She’s really good at sucking up to influential people to get contracts. Employees disliked him because he constantly sucked up to the manager.

english_meaning: Happening or coming quickly and without warning. Occurring unexpectedly. Done, made, or occurring without prior notice or preparation. Abrupt in nature.
example_sentence: His sudden departure surprised everyone at the office. A sudden storm ruined our picnic plans. She felt a sudden pain in her chest. There was a sudden silence in the room. The sudden change in weather caught the farmers off guard.

english_meaning: To make a claim against a person or an organization in court about something that they have said or done to harm you. To take legal proceedings in court. To make a request or application.
example_sentence: To sue damages. They threatened to sue if the work was not completed. To sue for divorce. The rebels were forced to sue for peace. George sues for peace after Russian blitz.

english_meaning: A type of soft leather made from the inner side of an animal's skin. It has a smooth, velvety surface and is commonly used for shoes, jackets, bags, gloves, and furniture.  A luxurious type of leather produced from the underside of animal hides, usually from lamb, goat, calf, or deer. It has a soft, fuzzy texture instead of the shiny finish found on regular leather. Suede is valued for its comfort, elegant appearance, and flexibility, but it requires careful maintenance because it stains and absorbs water easily.
synonyms: ["Soft leather","Nubuck (similar but not identical)","Velvety leather","Leather","Fine leather"]
example_sentence: She bought a pair of brown suede shoes for the winter. His suede jacket looked stylish and comfortable. Clean your suede bag carefully to avoid damaging the material. The sofa was covered with soft suede, making it feel luxurious.

english_meaning: Enough; adequate for a particular purpose or need. Having the right amount, neither too much nor too little.
example_sentence: We have sufficient food to last a week. Is your income sufficient to cover all your expenses? A sufficient amount of sleep is crucial for good health. The evidence was not sufficient to convict him.

english_meaning: To die or cause to die from lack of air or inability to breathe. To feel or make someone feel trapped, oppressed, or restricted. To smother or stifle emotions, ideas, or growth. To prevent something from developing freely.
example_sentence: He nearly suffocated in the smoke-filled room. The victim was suffocated with a pillow. She felt suffocated by her strict parents. Too many rules can suffocate creativity.

english_meaning: The act or state of being unable to breathe, often leading to death. Death or distress caused by lack of oxygen. A feeling of being oppressed or overwhelmed. The prevention of normal growth or expression.
example_sentence: The cause of death was suffocation. He felt a sense of suffocation in the crowded hall. Suffocation can occur if the airway is blocked. Rescue workers saved many people from suffocation.

english_meaning: The right to vote in political elections. The exercise of such a right. In older usage, a short prayer or plea, especially one offered in a religious service. The system by which people choose their representatives through voting.
example_sentence: Women had to fight for many years to win suffrage. Universal suffrage means that all adult citizens have the right to vote. The reform gave suffrage to millions of new voters. He wrote a famous book on the history of women's suffrage. Suffrage is a basic feature of democracy.

english_meaning: A sweet tropical fruit similar to custard apple with soft segmented flesh. A fruit with a lumpy green skin and sugary pulp inside. A member of the Annona family known for its sweetness. A fruit rich in vitamin C and natural fibers. A dessert-like fruit popular in Asian and tropical countries.
example_sentence: The sugar apple is one of the sweetest tropical fruits. She enjoyed a fresh sugar apple in the garden. Sugar apple pulp is often used in ice creams. Farmers in tropical regions grow sugar apples widely.

english_meaning: A wealthy older man who gives money or gifts to a much younger partner. A rich man who supports someone financially in return for companionship. Informally, any generous financial backer of a person or project.
example_sentence: The tabloids claimed she had found a sugar daddy. He jokes that the company's investor is its sugar daddy. She refused to be seen as anyone's sugar daddy arrangement. Gossip about a sugar daddy followed the young actor everywhere.

english_meaning: A tall tropical grass with thick jointed stems from which sugar is extracted. A crop grown mainly for producing sugar, molasses, and juice. The stems of this plant, chewed or crushed for their sweet juice. An important cash crop in many warm countries.
example_sentence: Sugarcane is grown widely in Sindh. He drank a glass of fresh sugarcane juice. The farmers harvested the sugarcane in December. Most of the country's sugar comes from sugarcane.

english_meaning: A set of matching clothes, usually a jacket with trousers or a skirt. A set of clothing worn for a special purpose or activity. A legal case brought before a court. Any of the four sets of playing cards such as hearts or spades. To be convenient or acceptable to someone. To look attractive on a particular person.
example_sentence: He wore a dark blue suit to the interview. The company filed a suit against its former supplier. Does Friday evening suit you for the meeting? That colour really suits your complexion.

english_meaning: The quality of being right or appropriate for a particular purpose. The degree to which someone or something meets the required needs. Fitness or appropriateness for a role, task, or situation.
example_sentence: The committee discussed his suitability for the position. We must assess the suitability of the land for farming. Her suitability as a team leader is beyond doubt. Doctors questioned the suitability of the treatment for young patients.

english_meaning: Right or appropriate for a particular person, purpose, or situation. Meeting the requirements or standards of something. Acceptable or fitting in a given context. Well matched to the needs or conditions at hand.
example_sentence: This film is not suitable for young children. We are still looking for a suitable candidate for the post. Please wear clothes suitable for cold weather. The hall is suitable for both weddings and conferences.

english_meaning: In a way that is right or appropriate for the occasion. In a manner that meets the required standard. Properly, correctly, or fittingly. To an appropriate degree or extent.
example_sentence: Everyone arrived suitably dressed for the formal dinner. The room was suitably furnished for guests. She was suitably impressed by his performance. The staff are suitably qualified for the job.

english_meaning: A rectangular case with a handle used for carrying clothes and belongings while travelling. A piece of luggage that can be locked and carried by hand. A travel bag, often with wheels, used on journeys.
example_sentence: She packed her suitcase the night before the flight. My suitcase was damaged during the journey. He lifted the heavy suitcase into the car. Please keep your suitcase with you at all times.

english_meaning: To be silently moody or gloomy, often because of being upset or disappointed. To remain silent, withdrawn, or silently resentful due to anger, disappointment, or unhappiness. Can refer to a temporary mood or a pattern of behavior.
example_sentence: He went to his room to sulk after losing the game. She is still sulking because her friends didn’t invite her. Children often sulk when they don’t get what they want. Instead of sulking, talk about what’s bothering you.

english_meaning: Someone who, instead of expressing anger or disappointment openly, stays quiet and moody, often to get sympathy or attention. A person who often sulks, pouts, or becomes silent and unhappy when things don’t go their way. It describes someone who easily gets offended and shows it by withdrawing or refusing to talk.
example_sentence: Don’t be such a sulk-pot; it was only a joke!. He’s a real sulk-pot when things don’t go his way. She turned into a sulk-pot after losing the game. Nobody likes a sulk-pot; it’s better to talk about your feelings.

english_meaning: Bad-tempered and sulky. Silent and gloomy in mood. Showing displeasure by refusing to talk. Dark and dismal in appearance. Persistently gloomy or morose.
example_sentence: The boy gave a sullen reply to his father. She sat in a sullen silence throughout the meeting. The sky looked sullen before the storm. He remained sullen after losing the game.

english_meaning: To damage or spoil the good condition of something, especially a reputation. To make dirty or stained. To tarnish. To reduce the purity or quality of something by wrong actions.
example_sentence: He refused to do anything that might sully his family's good name. One careless act can sully years of hard-earned reputation. Do not sully your character with such petty behaviour. The scandal sullied the image of the entire party. She would never sully her hands with dishonest work.

english_meaning: With the highest praise, an academic distinction awarded for the very highest level of achievement. The highest of the commonly used Latin honors granted at graduation.
synonyms: ["With highest honors","With the highest distinction","With highest praise"]
example_sentence: She graduated summa cum laude from the university. Only a few students earned summa cum laude that year. His diploma states that he completed the program summa cum laude. Years of disciplined study helped her finish summa cum laude.

english_meaning: To provide a brief statement of the main points of something. To reduce a long text or speech to its essential elements. To present a concise overview of a complex subject. To recap the primary arguments or facts of a discussion. To condense information into a shorter form without losing the core meaning.
example_sentence: At the end of the meeting, she will summarize the key decisions made. Please summarize the main events of the novel in one paragraph. The executive was asked to summarize the lengthy report for the board members. It is difficult to summarize such a complex scientific theory in just five minutes.

english_meaning: A short account that gives the main points of something without the details. A brief statement covering the essential facts of a longer text, speech, or event. A condensed version of a report, story, or discussion. Done quickly and without the usual formalities or attention to detail. Immediate and without delay, especially in legal or official matters.
example_sentence: Please write a short summary of the report before Friday. The teacher asked each student to give a summary of the story. He gave a summary of the meeting to those who could not attend. The judge ordered a summary hearing of the case.

english_meaning: A dialectal British word meaning something. An unspecified thing, matter, amount, or event. It is informal and is especially associated with northern English speech.
example_sentence: There is summat strange about that noise. I need summat warm to drink. He said summat that made everyone laugh. If summat is wrong, you should tell me.

english_meaning: The act or process of adding numbers or quantities to find a total. A final summary of the main points or evidence. A concluding statement by a lawyer at the end of a trial. The combined result or total effect of several things.
example_sentence: The spreadsheet performs the summation automatically. Her final paragraph offers a clear summation of the argument. The defense lawyer began his summation to the jury. The exhibition is a summation of the artist’s life work.

english_meaning: The highest point of something, especially the top of a mountain. An official meeting or series of meetings between the leaders of two or more governments at which they discuss important matters. The highest, most successful, or most important point in something.
example_sentence:
I intend to work hard to reach the summit of my career. We reached the summit at noon.
This path leads to the summit World leaders will meet next week for their annual economic summit.

english_meaning: To order somebody to appear in court. To order someone to come to or be present at a particular place, or to officially arrange a meeting of people. To call upon for specified action. To notify to come to appear.
example_sentence:
He was summoned to appear before the magistrates. She summoned the waiter.
He was summoned before the board of directors. The president summoned an emergency meeting of his advisers.
I have been summoned to appear in court.

english_meaning: Splendid and expensive-looking. Very rich, luxurious, and impressive. Involving great expense or grandeur. Extremely comfortable and pleasing, especially in food, clothes, or surroundings.
example_sentence: The king served a sumptuous feast to his guests. They stayed in a sumptuous hotel by the sea. The bride wore a sumptuous silk dress covered in embroidery. The palace was decorated in a sumptuous style. A sumptuous meal was prepared for the wedding guests.

english_meaning: The star at the center of our solar system that gives light and heat to the Earth. A huge, hot ball of gases located at the center of our solar system. It provides light, heat, and energy that make life possible on Earth. The Earth and other planets move around it. The word sun can also mean sunlight or a place that receives strong sunlight.
example_sentence: She closed her eyes and felt the sun on her face. The sun gives us natural light during the day. They enjoyed a warm day under the summer sun. The snow sparkled in the sun. Without the sun, life on Earth would not exist.

english_meaning: An astronomical event that occurs when the moon passes between the Earth and the sun, blocking all or part of the sun's light. A phenomenon where the sun appears darkened or obscured by the moon's shadow. The temporary blocking of sunlight as the moon crosses in front of the sun.
example_sentence: The sun eclipse darkened the sky at midday. Scientists traveled to observe the total sun eclipse. Never look directly at a sun eclipse without protection. The sun eclipse lasted for three minutes.

english_meaning: Having gone down below a normal level. Fallen inwards, especially of eyes or cheeks. Lying at the bottom of the sea or other water. Placed at a lower level than the surrounding area, as in a sunken garden or sunken bath.
example_sentence: Divers explored the sunken ship near the coast. His sunken eyes showed how tired he was. The house had a beautiful sunken garden. After the illness, her cheeks looked pale and sunken. Treasure was found inside the sunken vessel.

english_meaning: The ​light that comes from the ​sun:
example_sentence: The ​morning,​afternoon,​evening sunlight ​shone through the ​curtains

english_meaning: A brown colour that skin develops after being in the sun. The result of exposure of the skin to sunlight over some time. A darkening of the skin caused by ultraviolet rays.
example_sentence: She got a lovely suntan on her holiday at the beach. Use sunscreen if you don't want a heavy suntan. His suntan proved that he had been travelling in hot countries. Many tourists come to this island just for a suntan. A light suntan looked good on her fair skin.

english_meaning: On its own initiative. Without a formal request from the parties, especially when a court or authority begins action independently. Often written suo motu.
antonyms: ["On request","Under instruction","Compulsorily","In response to a petition"]
example_sentence: The court took suo motu notice of the matter. The regulator opened an inquiry suo motu. The judge issued a suo motu order to protect the witness. The authority acted suo motu after seeing the public report.

english_meaning: On its own motion or initiative, especially by a court or authority without a formal request. An action taken by a court or authority on its own initiative, without a formal request or petition from any party. Commonly used when a judge starts proceedings independently.
example_sentence: The court took suo motu notice of the environmental issue. The judge acted suo motu to prevent further injustice. The Supreme Court initiated a suo motu case on public safety. Authorities started an investigation suo motu after the incident.

english_meaning: Very good or excellent. Used to strongly emphasize that something is extremely good, impressive, or enjoyable. It is often used in casual speech and writing to show excitement or approval.
example_sentence: She did a super-duper job on the presentation. We had a super-duper time at the picnic. This phone has super-duper features for its price. The movie was super-duper fun to watch.

english_meaning: A playful, made-up word used to describe something that is extremely good, wonderful, amazing, or extraordinary. It is often used humorously when you cannot find a real word strong enough to express excitement or admiration. This word is not found in normal dictionaries as a real word. It is a coined, humorous term that expresses extreme delight, excellence, or amazement. It is often used in songs, movies, or casual speech to sound fun and dramatic rather than serious.
example_sentence: The view from the mountain was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious. Her performance in the play was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious. We had a supercalifragilisticexpialidocious day at the beach. The celebration was supercalifragilisticexpialidocious and full of joy.

english_meaning: Behaving as if one is better than other people. Showing proud contempt through looks, tone, or manner. Arrogantly dismissive of others' opinions or feelings. Full of haughty pride and disdain. Treating others as unimportant or inferior.
example_sentence: He gave the waiter a supercilious look. Her supercilious manner annoyed the whole team. The critic wrote a supercilious review of the novel. He spoke in a supercilious tone about village life.

english_meaning: Concerned only with the surface or appearance. Lacking depth or thoroughness; relating to the obvious or external aspects rather than underlying realities or details.
example_sentence: His knowledge of history is superficial. She gave a superficial glance at the report. The doctor noted only superficial cuts. Their friendship seemed superficial, lacking real trust.

english_meaning: More than is needed or wanted. Unnecessary because it adds nothing useful. Extra and therefore serving no real purpose. Redundant in a piece of writing, work, or arrangement.
example_sentence: The editor removed several superfluous paragraphs. Any further explanation would be superfluous. He packed a few superfluous items he never used. Superfluous detail can weaken a good argument.

english_meaning: The large vein that carries oxygen-poor blood from the upper body into the right atrium. The main vein draining the head, neck, chest, and arms. One of the two great veins that return blood to the heart.
example_sentence: The superior vena cava drains blood from the head and arms. Blood from the superior vena cava enters the right atrium. A tumour was pressing on the superior vena cava. The superior vena cava lies to the right of the aorta.

english_meaning: The state of being better, greater, or higher in quality, rank, or ability than others. An attitude of believing oneself to be better than other people. Advantage in strength, position, or numbers over a rival.
example_sentence: The team proved its superiority in the final match. She spoke with an air of superiority that annoyed everyone. The army had clear superiority in numbers. Nobody doubts the superiority of this new design.

english_meaning: An exaggerated belief that one is better, cleverer, or more important than other people. A psychological attitude in which a person constantly shows off their supposed greatness. Behaviour that hides insecurity behind an outward display of arrogance.
example_sentence: His superiority complex makes teamwork very difficult. She treats her colleagues badly because of a superiority complex. A superiority complex often hides deep insecurity. Wealth gave him an unpleasant superiority complex.

english_meaning: Of the highest quality or degree; excellent beyond comparison. In grammar, the form of an adjective or adverb expressing the highest degree, such as 'best' or 'largest'. An expression of the highest praise or admiration.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a superlative meal for the guests. 'Best' is the superlative form of 'good'. Critics used superlatives to describe her performance. His superlative skill impressed the whole audience.

english_meaning: To the highest degree; extremely well or excellently. In a manner that cannot be surpassed. Using words of the highest praise.
example_sentence: She performed superlatively in the final examination. The house was superlatively decorated for the wedding. He spoke superlatively of his former teacher. The orchestra played superlatively last night.

english_meaning: A prison, or part of a prison, with the highest level of security, used for the most dangerous criminals. Relating to a maximum-security facility where prisoners are kept in strict isolation.
example_sentence: He was transferred to a supermax prison after the escape attempt. Life in a supermax facility is extremely restricted. The state built a new supermax for violent offenders. Visitors are rarely allowed inside the supermax.

english_meaning: Beyond the laws of nature and science. Relating to things that cannot be explained by natural or physical causes. Connected with ghosts, spirits, magic, or other powers beyond human understanding. Belonging to a world other than the ordinary physical one.
example_sentence: Many people believe in supernatural powers and ghosts. The old house was said to have supernatural creatures inside. The novel describes several supernatural events. He claimed to have supernatural abilities to read minds. Films about supernatural beings are very popular today.

english_meaning: Pertaining to or denoting a speed greater than that of sound in the same medium. Moving, operating, or capable of flying at speeds exceeding Mach 1. Relating to waves of frequency above the range of human hearing, though this is more commonly termed ultrasonic. Involving or characteristic of speeds where the flow of air around an object is faster than the local speed of sound.
example_sentence: The new fighter jet is capable of reaching supersonic speeds within seconds. Many scientists are researching supersonic travel to reduce international flight times. The loud sonic boom was a direct result of the aircraft going supersonic. Supersonic aerodynamics requires a different wing design compared to subsonic flight.

english_meaning: A widely held but irrational belief in supernatural influence, luck, or omens, beliefs that have no scientific basis but affect behavior or decisions. A belief in supernatural causes of good or bad luck. A custom or belief passed from one generation to another without scientific proof. A belief that performing or avoiding a particular action can change the outcome of an event. A belief that certain signs or omens predict something good or bad.
example_sentence: Breaking a mirror is considered bad luck in superstition. Superstition guided their rituals. Many avoid walking under ladders due to superstition. Superstitions can affect behavior.

english_meaning: Believing in luck, omens, or supernatural influences, having strong irrational beliefs that events can be caused by magical or unexplained forces. Someone who is superstitious may avoid certain actions, objects, or days due to fear of bad luck.
example_sentence: She is very superstitious about Friday the 13th. Superstitious practices exist worldwide. He avoided black cats due to superstition. Superstitious beliefs influenced his decisions.

english_meaning: A supposed cure or preventive practice based on superstition rather than reliable evidence. A traditional ritual, charm, or folk treatment believed to remove illness, bad luck, or supernatural harm. A remedy whose effectiveness is attributed to magical or irrational belief rather than medicine.
example_sentence: He wore a red thread as a superstitious remedy for bad luck. The family tried a superstitious remedy before seeking medical advice. Researchers found no evidence that the superstitious remedy could cure the illness. The story describes salt placed at the doorway as a superstitious remedy against evil.

english_meaning: A person who watches over and directs the work of others. Someone responsible for making sure a task is done correctly. A senior worker who guides and checks employees. An academic who guides a student's research.
example_sentence: The supervisor checked every report before submission. She was promoted to supervisor after five years. My research supervisor gave me valuable feedback. Speak to your supervisor if you face any problem.

english_meaning: Lying flat on one's back with the face upward. Failing to act because of weakness or laziness. Showing no interest, energy, or resistance. Inactive or passive when action is needed.
example_sentence: He lay supine on the grass and watched the sky. The patient was asked to remain supine during the examination. The government has been supine in dealing with the crisis. His supine attitude towards injustice disappointed his friends. She was supine on the bed, staring at the ceiling.

english_meaning: Something added to complete a thing or make up for a deficiency. A separate section added to a book or newspaper to provide extra information. A substance taken to improve dietary intake or health. To add something extra to enhance or extend something else. To fill up or supply what is lacking in a system or budget.
example_sentence: She takes a vitamin supplement every morning to boost her immune system. The Sunday newspaper comes with a colorful travel supplement. He works a second job to supplement his monthly income. The textbook includes a digital supplement with practice quizzes.

english_meaning: The final meal of the day eaten in the evening, often a light or informal snack before bedtime. An evening meal served when the main meal of the day was taken at midday. A social gathering or event centered around a communal evening meal, often for a church or club. A formal banquet or late-night feast served after an evening performance or party. The food or sustenance consumed during these evening sessions.
example_sentence: After a long day of hiking, we enjoyed a simple supper of soup and bread. The church is hosting a spaghetti supper to raise funds for the new library. They invited us over for a late supper after the theater performance ended. Children in the village usually have a light supper before going to bed at eight.

english_meaning: To replace a person or thing, especially by force, competition, or better performance. To take the position or role previously held by another. To cause an older method or system to become obsolete.
example_sentence: Digital payments may eventually supplant cash. The younger player supplanted the veteran in the starting lineup. New evidence supplanted the earlier theory. The imported crop gradually supplanted local varieties.

english_meaning: Flexible and able to bend or move easily without stiffness. Graceful and smoothly moving. Able to adapt readily to changing conditions or ideas. Soft and pliable in texture.
example_sentence: Regular stretching keeps the body supple. The dancer moved with a supple grace. This cream helps keep the leather soft and supple. A supple mind adapts quickly to new ideas.

english_meaning: Something added to complete a thing or make up for a deficiency. An additional part of a book or publication. A vitamin or dietary product taken to enhance health. To add to something in order to improve or complete it. Extra material or income.
example_sentence: The magazine included a special supplement on health. He takes a vitamin supplement every morning. She supplements her income by teaching in the evenings. The teacher gave students a supplement to the textbook.

english_meaning: Added to complete or enhance something else. Serving as an extra or additional part. Provided in addition to what is already present. Relating to an angle that completes another to 180 degrees. Functioning as a secondary or auxiliary element to fill a deficiency.
example_sentence: The student took supplementary classes to improve her grades. You can find more details in the supplementary material at the end of the book. The government provided supplementary funding for the new housing project. In geometry, two supplementary angles add up to exactly one hundred and eighty degrees.

english_meaning: The phenomenon in language where a regular word form is replaced by a completely different word from another root. The use of unrelated forms to fill gaps in a paradigm, such as "go" and "went" or "good" and "better". The act of supplying something to fill a lack.
example_sentence: The pair "go" and "went" is a classic example of suppletion. Suppletion makes some verb paradigms irregular in English. Linguists study suppletion to understand how languages evolve. There is suppletion between "good," "better," and "best".

english_meaning: Serving to supply or make up for a deficiency. In linguistics, describing forms that come from a different root than the base word, such as "went" as the past tense of "go". Related to or functioning as a supplement.
example_sentence: The language uses suppletive forms for several common verbs. "Worse" is a suppletive comparative form of "bad". Suppletive allomorphs cannot be derived by regular rules. The committee played a suppletive role in funding the project.

english_meaning: A person who asks for something in a humble and earnest way, especially from someone in authority or from God. Making a humble or earnest request. Expressing a plea or entreaty.
example_sentence: The suppliant stood at the king's door begging for mercy. She raised her suppliant hands towards the sky in prayer. The suppliant villagers requested help from the officer. He fell to his knees in a suppliant posture. The letter was written in a suppliant tone.

english_meaning: A person who makes a humble and earnest request, especially in prayer. One who pleads or begs for help, mercy, or favor from a higher authority. A petitioner who approaches with deep humility.
example_sentence: The supplicants knelt before the temple altar. A long line of supplicants waited outside the governor's office. The king listened patiently to every supplicant. She approached the committee as a humble supplicant, not a demander.

english_meaning: To ask for something humbly and earnestly, especially from a person in authority or from God. To pray or beg with deep sincerity and humility. To make a humble request or petition.
example_sentence: The villagers supplicated the king for mercy during the famine. She supplicated to God for her father's recovery. He fell to his knees and supplicated for forgiveness. The followers supplicated their leader to reconsider the decision.

english_meaning: The act of asking for something humbly or earnestly, especially from God or a person in power. A humble prayer, entreaty, or petition. An earnest request made with respect and humility.
example_sentence: The old man raised his hands in supplication to God. Her supplications to the judge finally softened his heart. He offered a long supplication for the health of his sick child. The temple was filled with the sound of prayer and supplication. Despite repeated supplication, his request was refused.

english_meaning: Expressing or containing a humble request or prayer. Having the character of a plea or entreaty. Used to describe words, tones, or gestures that show respectful and earnest asking.
example_sentence: He wrote a supplicatory letter to the minister asking for help. She spoke in a supplicatory tone that touched everyone's heart. The old man's supplicatory eyes moved the officer to pity. A supplicatory prayer was recited before the meal. His supplicatory manner won the sympathy of the audience.

english_meaning: Providing encouragement, help, or emotional assistance. Willing to give aid or approval in difficult times. Serving to hold or strengthen something. Showing kindness and understanding to others.
example_sentence: Her parents were very supportive of her career. He wore a supportive brace for his knee. Friends should always be supportive of one another. The manager was supportive during the difficult project.

english_meaning: Capable of being supposed. In a way that can be assumed or imagined to be possible. Often confused with 'supposedly' which means 'according to what is believed or claimed'. In careful usage, 'supposably' relates to what could conceivably happen.
example_sentence: Supposably, this method could work if we had more time. It is supposably possible to reach the top in one day. The plan will supposably solve half of our problems. Supposably, one could learn the language in six months. Supposably, such a mistake can happen to anyone.

english_meaning: An idea or statement that is assumed to be true without proof. A belief or opinion based on guesswork. An assumption used as the basis of an argument. A hypothesis or theory not yet confirmed. A conjecture about a fact or situation.
example_sentence: His supposition proved to be correct. The theory rests on a false supposition. On the supposition that he will come, we prepared dinner. That is only a supposition, not a fact.

english_meaning: To stop, control, or put an end to something, especially a feeling, action, or expression. To prevent something from being seen, known, or expressed.
example_sentence: He tried to suppress his anger during the meeting. The government suppressed the protest before it could spread. She couldn’t suppress her laughter when she heard the joke. The doctor gave medicine to suppress the patient’s cough.

english_meaning: The white foamy waves that form when the sea breaks on the shore. The activity of riding on top of a wave, usually on a special board. To ride on waves. To move quickly from one page to another on the internet.
example_sentence: Children were playing in the surf on the beach. He learnt to surf while on holiday in Australia. The surf was too rough for swimming that day. She loves to surf the internet in her free time. The surfers waited patiently for the perfect wave to surf.

english_meaning: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink. Too much of anything to the point of causing discomfort. To supply or eat and drink too much. Overindulgence that leads to weariness or distaste.
example_sentence: There is a surfeit of information on the internet these days. He fell ill because of a surfeit of rich food at the wedding. The market has a surfeit of cheap goods this season. She was tired by a surfeit of praise from her admirers. Do not surfeit yourself on sweets during Eid.

english_meaning: To rise suddenly and powerfully. A sudden increase or forward movement. To fill somebody with strong feeling. To suddenly increase in value.
example_sentence: The crowd surged forward when the gates opened. There was a surge in demand for water during summer. A surge of anger filled his mind. Electricity surged after the storm.

english_meaning: A doctor who is trained to perform operations on the body. A medical specialist who treats injury and disease through surgery. A person qualified to carry out procedures in an operating theatre. In some contexts, a chief medical officer in the armed forces.
example_sentence: The surgeon performed the operation successfully. A skilled surgeon repaired the damaged artery. The surgeon explained the procedure to the family. She trained for years to become a heart surgeon.

english_meaning: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments to treat a disease or injury. The specialized branch of medicine concerned with manual or operative procedures. A room or establishment where a doctor, dentist, or veterinarian performs operations or sees patients. The period of time during which a medical professional is available to consult with patients. An intensive period of work or session aimed at solving a specific problem.
example_sentence: The patient underwent complex cardiac surgery to repair a damaged valve. The surgeon explained that modern laser surgery is much less invasive than traditional methods. After the accident, he spent several hours in surgery being treated for multiple fractures. The local doctor holds his daily surgery between nine and eleven in the morning.

english_meaning: Relating to or used in the practice of surgery for treating injuries or diseases. Done with great precision or extreme accuracy similar to a medical operation. Pertaining to the branch of medicine that involves manual or instrumental intervention. Characterized by the use of surgical instruments or techniques to repair or remove body parts. Applied with meticulous care to achieve a specific and clean result.
example_sentence: The patient required surgical intervention to repair the damaged heart valve. The pilot executed a surgical strike on the enemy base with incredible precision. A surgical mask is essential for maintaining a sterile environment in the operating room. She approached the complex problem with surgical accuracy and calm focus.

english_meaning: A highly targeted military attack aimed at a specific location or objective while avoiding damage to nearby areas. It is planned with precision and carried out quickly to neutralize a threat without broad destruction.
antonyms: ["Large scale attack","Indiscriminate attack","Full scale invasion","Widespread assault"]
example_sentence: The army carried out a surgical strike to eliminate the militant hideout. A surgical strike was chosen to avoid civilian casualties. The government confirmed that the operation was a precise surgical strike. Modern technology has made surgical strikes more accurate.

english_meaning: In a manner that involves or relates to medical surgery. With the extreme precision or clinical accuracy associated with a surgeon. In a way that targets a specific area for removal or alteration with minimal impact on surroundings. Through the use of operative procedures to treat a condition or injury. With a high degree of technical skill and careful deliberation.
example_sentence: The tumor was surgically removed to prevent it from spreading to other organs. The pilot surgically guided the aircraft through the narrow mountain pass. Modern technology allows doctors to repair heart valves surgically with tiny incisions. The team surgically dismantled the opponent's defense with precise passes.

english_meaning: To guess or suppose something without strong evidence. To form an opinion based on incomplete information. To infer or conclude from limited facts. A supposition or conjecture. An idea formed by guessing.
example_sentence: I surmise that he already knew about the plan. From her expression, I surmised she was upset. His surmise turned out to be correct. She could only surmise the reason for his silence.

english_meaning: Capable of being overcome or dealt with successfully. Able to be climbed over or crossed such as a physical barrier. Capable of being solved or managed despite initial difficulty.
example_sentence: With proper planning and teamwork, every obstacle in our path proved surmountable. They faced severe financial difficulties at first, but all of them were eventually surmountable. The steep hill looked daunting from afar, but it turned out to be easily surmountable. Though the project seemed overwhelming, her determination made the challenges surmountable.

english_meaning: To go beyond or do better than something or someone else. To be greater, higher, or more excellent than another in quality, degree, or performance. To exceed expectations or limits. To outdo or excel in a particular area.
example_sentence: Her performance surpassed all our expectations. He has surpassed his elder brother in academic achievements. This year's profits surpassed those of last year. The new model surpasses the older one in speed and efficiency. No other player in the team can surpass his record.

english_meaning: Having the qualities of surrealism, characterized by dreamlike, fantastical, or bizarre imagery and ideas. Strange and unsettling in a way that does not seem real, often resembling the imagery of a dream. Used to describe an experience that feels so unusual or unexpected that it seems unreal. Marked by strikingly distorted or unusual juxtapositions of imagery, as in surrealist art.
example_sentence: Standing on the empty street at dawn felt completely surreal.  The painter was famous for his surreal depictions of melting clocks and floating objects.  Watching the entire city evacuate felt like a surreal dream.  The surreal landscape of the desert seemed almost otherworldly at sunset.  Meeting her childhood idol in person was a surreal experience for her.

english_meaning: To stop resisting an enemy and submit to their authority. To give up possession of something to another person. To yield to a strong emotion, influence, or temptation. The act of ceasing resistance and accepting defeat. To hand over a right, privilege, or claim.
example_sentence: The soldiers were forced to surrender after a long battle. He refused to surrender to his fears and kept fighting. She had to surrender her passport at the airport. The rebels finally agreed to surrender to the authorities.

english_meaning: Kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of. It describes actions characterized by stealth or a desire to avoid observation. It is often used for behavior that is clandestine or unauthorized.
example_sentence: They shared a surreptitious glance across the crowded room. She took a surreptitious look at her watch during the boring lecture. The spy conducted a surreptitious entry into the high-security building. He made a surreptitious recording of the private conversation.

english_meaning: In a secret, stealthy, or hidden manner. Done quietly and carefully to avoid being noticed or caught. In a way that is kept secret because it would not be approved of. Acting in a sly or clandestine way to conceal one's actions from others. Often implies dishonesty, sneakiness, or an intention to deceive.
example_sentence: He surreptitiously slipped the note into her bag without anyone noticing. The student surreptitiously copied answers from his neighbour during the exam. She surreptitiously glanced at her phone while the teacher was speaking. The cat surreptitiously approached the bird in the garden. He surreptitiously recorded the conversation on his mobile.

english_meaning: The quality, state, or characteristic of being secret, stealthy, or hidden. The act or habit of doing things in a sly, sneaky, or concealed manner to avoid detection. The trait of behaving in a clandestine way, often with the intention of hiding one's true motives or actions. It refers to the noun form describing secret or furtive behaviour.
example_sentence: The surreptitiousness of his behaviour made his colleagues suspicious. There was a clear surreptitiousness in the way the deal was carried out. Her surreptitiousness during the meeting did not go unnoticed. The surreptitiousness of the operation kept it hidden from the authorities for years. His habitual surreptitiousness damaged the trust of his friends.

english_meaning: A person or thing that takes the place of another. Someone who is appointed, chosen, or used to act in place of another person. It can also refer to something that serves as a substitute when the original is not available. A judge in some US states who handles wills and estates. A person who carries and delivers a baby for another couple. Something used temporarily when the actual thing is missing. A representative who acts on behalf of another in official duties.
example_sentence: She saw him as a sort of surrogate father. For these people, television is a surrogate for real life. As Tolkien noted some time ago, magic is often a surrogate for technology. Because she had no children of her own, her friend's son became a kind of surrogate child to her. Martin had become Howard Cosell's surrogate son. The committee appointed a surrogate to sign the documents. She acted as a surrogate mother for her friend. Online learning became a surrogate for traditional classrooms during the crisis. The company used a surrogate spokesperson until the CEO returned.

english_meaning: A woman who gives birth to a baby for another person or couple, usually because they are unable to have babies themselves. A woman who has agreed to give birth to a baby on behalf of someone else. A woman who becomes pregnant by artificial insemination or by implantation of a fertilized egg created by in vitro fertilization for the purpose of carrying the fetus to term for another person or persons. One who acts or serves as a substitute mother. A woman temporarily acting as a mother figure for emotional or practical support. Someone who steps in to perform a mothering role when the actual mother is absent.
example_sentence: She has agreed to act as a surrogate mother for her sister. A surrogate mother is artificially inseminated with the father's semen and carries the fetus to term. They chose a surrogate mother because they were unable to conceive naturally. The surrogate mother received full medical support throughout the pregnancy. Many couples turn to a surrogate mother after several failed fertility treatments. The surrogate mother and the intended parents stayed in close contact during the process.

english_meaning: An additional tax charged on top of an existing tax. An extra levy imposed on income or goods above a certain level. To impose such an additional tax on a person, company, or product.
example_sentence: The government introduced a surtax on very high incomes. A small surtax was added to imported luxury goods. Businesses protested against the new surtax. The council decided to surtax second properties in the city.

english_meaning: Translated words or captions projected above a stage during an opera or foreign-language play. On-screen text that helps an audience follow dialogue or lyrics in another language. A theatrical device used to make performances accessible to wider audiences.
example_sentence: The opera was performed in Italian with English surtitles. Surtitles helped the audience follow the complex plot. The theatre installed a new screen for surtitles. Without surtitles, many visitors would have missed the jokes.

english_meaning: The act of carefully watching a person suspected of a crime or a place where a crime may be committed. Close watch kept over someone or something (as by a detective).
example_sentence: The police placed the building under surveillance after the robbery. Surveillance cameras help reduce crime in public areas. The suspect was kept under close surveillance for several weeks. Health surveillance is important to control the spread of diseases.

english_meaning: To examine and record the measurements, features, or condition of an area or building. To look carefully at something as a whole in order to form an opinion. A detailed study of people's opinions collected through questions. A general view, inspection, or written report of a subject.
example_sentence: The company carried out a survey of customer satisfaction. Engineers will survey the site before construction begins. He stood on the hill and surveyed the valley below. According to the survey, most residents support the new park.

english_meaning: A person whose job is to measure and record the features and boundaries of land. A professional who examines the condition and value of buildings and property. An official who inspects and reports on structures, roads, or equipment.
example_sentence: The surveyor marked the boundary of the new plot. A qualified surveyor inspected the house before the sale. The surveyor's report delayed the construction work. She works as a land surveyor for the city council.

english_meaning: Able to be survived or lived through. Describing an accident, illness, or condition that a person can come out of alive. Capable of being endured without causing death or total destruction.
example_sentence: Doctors said the injury was serious but survivable. Modern car design makes many crashes survivable. The disease is survivable if it is detected early. Engineers work to make aircraft accidents more survivable.

english_meaning: The state or fact of continuing to live or exist, especially in difficult conditions. The act of remaining alive after an accident, disaster, or dangerous situation. Something that has continued to exist from an earlier time. The ability to endure hardship or adversity. The process of surviving in nature or challenging environments.
example_sentence: Food and water are essential for human survival. His survival after the accident amazed the doctors. This old tradition is a survival from ancient times. The soldiers were trained in wilderness survival.

english_meaning: The belief in and practice of preparing to survive a serious disaster or breakdown of society. A way of life focused on stockpiling supplies and learning skills needed to stay alive in emergencies. The philosophy that individuals must be ready to protect themselves when normal systems fail.
example_sentence: Survivalism became popular after the widespread power failures. His interest in survivalism began with a wilderness course. Books on survivalism fill an entire shelf in his study. Critics argue that survivalism encourages unnecessary fear.

english_meaning: A person who prepares in advance to survive a natural disaster, war, or collapse of society. Someone who stores food, water, and equipment and learns skills for emergencies. Relating to the beliefs or practices of such a person.
example_sentence: The survivalist kept a year's supply of food in his cellar. She joined a survivalist group to learn first aid and navigation. His survivalist habits surprised his neighbours. The documentary followed a family living a survivalist lifestyle.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being easily affected, influenced, or harmed by something. A tendency to be affected by a particular disease, emotion, or influence. Sensitivity to feelings or external forces.
example_sentence: Children have a higher susceptibility to certain infections. His susceptibility to flattery often lands him in trouble. She has a natural susceptibility to cold weather. The doctor asked about the patient's susceptibility to allergies. He hides his emotional susceptibility behind a strong face.

english_meaning: Easily affected, influenced, harmed, or infected by something. Open to a particular influence or impression.
example_sentence: Young plants are susceptible to frost. He is susceptible to persuasive advertising. People with weak immune systems may be susceptible to infection. The old bridge is susceptible to damage during storms.

english_meaning: To believe that something is likely or probable, usually something bad, without having full proof. To doubt the truth or honesty of someone. A person who is thought to have committed a crime. Feeling doubtful about something.
example_sentence: The police arrested three suspects after the robbery. I suspect he is not telling the whole truth. She began to suspect her friend of dishonesty. The main suspect denied all the charges in court. Doctors suspect that the disease is caused by a virus.

english_meaning: The act of officially stopping something for a period of time. The state of being temporarily removed from a job, school, or team as a punishment. A system of springs and shock absorbers that supports a vehicle on its wheels. A mixture in which solid particles float in a liquid without dissolving. The act of hanging something from a fixed point above.
example_sentence: The player received a two-match suspension for misconduct. The suspension of the bus service caused problems for commuters. This car has a soft suspension that handles rough roads well. The medicine is a suspension and must be shaken before use.

english_meaning: A feeling or belief that something is wrong without having proof. Doubt about the honesty or intentions of a person. A slight belief that something may be true. A very small trace or hint of something. The state of being distrusted or considered guilty by others.
example_sentence: The police arrested him on suspicion of fraud. She looked at the stranger with suspicion. I have a suspicion that he already knows the truth. There was just a suspicion of lemon in the sauce.

english_meaning: Feeling that something is wrong or that someone cannot be trusted. Causing a feeling of doubt or distrust. Behaving in a way that makes people think something is dishonest. Cautious and unwilling to believe easily.
example_sentence: The police found a suspicious bag near the gate. She became suspicious when he changed his story. His suspicious behaviour attracted the guard's attention. I am suspicious of offers that sound too good.

english_meaning: To provide enough of what somebody, something needs in order to live or exist. To experience something bad. To provide what is needed for (something or someone) to exist, continue, etc.
example_sentence: This thought had sustained him throughout the years. He sustained severe head injuries. He cannot sustain a normal conversation

english_meaning: Able to continue over a long period without harming the environment or depleting resources. Something that can be maintained or continued for a long time without causing damage to natural resources, the environment, or future needs. It is often used in relation to energy, development, farming, business, and living practices that do not harm future generations.
example_sentence: The city is investing in sustainable energy sources like solar power. Farmers are encouraged to use sustainable farming methods. Sustainable development helps protect natural resources for future generations. We need a sustainable plan to reduce pollution in urban areas.

english_meaning: Food and drink that is needed to live and stay healthy. Nourishment that keeps a person, animal, or plant alive. The act of supporting, maintaining, or keeping something going. Something that gives strength, support, or encouragement.
example_sentence: The poor villagers depend on simple food for their daily sustenance. Water is essential for the sustenance of all living beings. Her faith provided her with spiritual sustenance during hard times. The charity provides sustenance to hundreds of homeless people. Farming is the main source of sustenance in this region.

english_meaning: A bold and confident way of walking, speaking, or behaving that shows pride and self importance. To walk or behave with exaggerated confidence or pride.
example_sentence: He walked into the room with a swagger that showed his confidence. The actor’s swagger made him stand out on stage. She tried to hide her nerves behind a confident swagger. He swaggered down the street after winning the match. The young officer swaggered into the hall with pride.

english_meaning: To cause food or drink to pass from the mouth into the stomach. To make a movement in the throat as if doing this, especially because of nervousness or strong emotion. To accept or believe something without questioning, especially something untrue or unpleasant. To suppress or hold back feelings. A small migratory bird with a forked tail and long pointed wings.
example_sentence: He swallowed the medicine with a glass of water. She swallowed hard before answering the difficult question. I cannot swallow such an obvious lie. He had to swallow his pride and apologize to her. A swallow built its nest under the roof of our old house.

english_meaning: To overwhelm someone with a large amount of work, tasks, or problems, making it difficult to cope. A low-lying area saturated with water, often with muddy soil and abundant plant life like reeds and mosses.
example_sentence: The hikers got lost in the swamp and had to be rescued. The swamp was full of mosquitoes and thick mud. She was swamped with emails and could not respond on time. The company was swamped by customer complaints after the product recall.

english_meaning: A large waterbird with a long neck, usually white, known for its grace. A symbol of beauty, elegance, or purity. To move around in a relaxed and carefree manner, often in a way that annoys others.
example_sentence: A pair of swans glided across the quiet lake. The dancer moved with the grace of a swan. He swanned into the office an hour late. Swans are protected birds in many countries.

english_meaning: The final performance or achievement of a person before retirement or death. A last work, appearance, or effort in a career. A farewell gesture marking the end of something.
example_sentence: That concert proved to be the singer's swan song. He wrote the novel as a swan song to his long career. The match was the veteran captain's swan song. Her final lecture was a memorable swan song.

english_meaning: Stylish, luxurious, or impressive in appearance. something that is fashionable, elegant, or high-class, often giving an impression of wealth or sophistication.
example_sentence: They stayed in a swanky hotel by the beach. He arrived in a swanky sports car. She wore a swanky dress to the party. The restaurant had a swanky interior with chandeliers.

english_meaning: To exchange one thing for another. To give one item and receive another item in return. It is used when two people exchange things, positions, roles, or information. An act of exchanging one thing for another.
example_sentence: We decided to swap seats so she could sit near the window. The children swapped toys during the playtime. He swapped his old phone for a newer model. They swapped ideas to solve the problem. They made a swap of their old books. The companies agreed on a swap of resources. Currency swaps are common in international finance.

english_meaning: To move in large numbers. To gather, rush, or move together in large numbers, often suddenly or energetically. A large number of people, insects, or things moving together.
example_sentence: Bees swarmed around the flowers. Shoppers swarmed into the mall on sale day. Fans swarmed the actor after the show. A swarm of locusts destroyed the crops. A swarm of reporters waited outside the building. The garden was full of a swarm of butterflies.

english_meaning: Having a dark complexion. Dark-skinned. Tanned. Having a dark or sun-browned face. Used to describe a person, especially their skin or complexion, that is dark in colour, often as a natural feature or because of exposure to the sun. It is usually applied to the face and is mostly used in literary or descriptive writing.
example_sentence: A tall, swarthy man stood at the door. His swarthy complexion showed years of working in the sun. The painting depicted a swarthy fisherman mending his nets. She noticed a swarthy stranger watching from across the street. The sailors had swarthy faces from the long voyage.

english_meaning: To strike quickly and sharply, often with the hand or a flat object, usually targeting something small like a fly or mosquito. The act of smacking or slapping. To study very hard or be very diligent. Someone who is very studious. SWAT = Special Weapons And Tactics (police/military unit).
example_sentence: He swatted a fly that was annoying him. He swatted the mosquito buzzing near his ear. She tried to swat the fly with a newspaper. The teacher swatted the desk lightly to get the students’ attention. A sudden swat on the ball sent it flying across the field. She’s a real swat, she spends hours on her homework. The SWAT team was called in to handle the hostage situation.

english_meaning: To wrap or cover something completely. To surround or envelop something (physically or figuratively). A band or strip of fabric used for wrapping. A broad strip or area of land, especially one covered by something (like grass, crops, etc).
example_sentence: The nurse swathed the wound in a clean bandage. The mountains were swathed in thick fog. The baby was gently swathed in a warm blanket. The storm left a wide swathe of destruction across the valley

english_meaning: To swing or move rhythmically from side to side, or to influence or persuade someone. It refers to control, influence, or a physical movement in a rocking motion. Move slowly back and forth, influence or control someone’s opinion or behavior.
example_sentence: The trees swayed gently in the wind. His speech swayed the audience’s opinion. The boat swayed as the waves hit it. She has a lot of sway in company decisions.

english_meaning: Moved slowly back and forth or side to side. Was influenced or persuaded by someone or something. Changed opinion because of an argument or emotion. Rocked gently by wind or motion. Controlled or dominated by a feeling or force.
example_sentence: The tall trees swayed in the strong wind. She was swayed by his emotional speech. The dancers swayed gracefully to the music. Voters were not swayed by the false promises.

english_meaning: A rude or offensive word, usually considered impolite in public. A curse word used to express anger or strong emotion. Vulgar language regarded as socially unacceptable. A word that is considered taboo or inappropriate. Foul language used in speech.
example_sentence: He used a swearword when he stubbed his toe. Using a swearword in front of elders is disrespectful. The teacher warned students not to use any swearword. She apologized for saying a swearword out loud.

english_meaning: Moisture released through the skin to cool the body. A state of anxiety, strain, or hard work. Physical effort or labor. To produce perspiration. To work very hard or worry intensely. To cause moisture to form on a surface or extract moisture by gentle heating.
example_sentence: His shirt was soaked with sweat after the run. Success takes a lot of hard work and sweat. Don't sweat the small stuff in life. The cold bottle began to sweat in the warm room.

english_meaning: A small gland in the skin that produces and releases sweat. A tubular skin structure that helps the body control its temperature by secreting watery fluid. A gland that removes water, salts, and small amounts of waste from the body through the skin. One of the two main types of skin glands, found as eccrine and apocrine glands.
example_sentence: The sweat glands help cool the body during exercise. Human skin contains millions of tiny sweat glands. Overactive sweat glands can cause excessive sweating. The palms and soles have a high number of sweat glands.

english_meaning: To make someone fall in love very quickly and completely. To impress or charm a person so much that they lose all resistance. To overwhelm someone with excitement or admiration. To lift someone physically off the ground in a sudden movement.
example_sentence: He swept her off her feet within a few weeks of meeting. Her performance swept the audience off their feet. The charming guide swept the tourists off their feet. He lifted the child and swept her off her feet playfully.

english_meaning: To win everything in a competition. To win all the prizes, etc in a competition. To win everything that is available. (in gambling) To win all the cards or money. To win every event or prize in a contest.
example_sentence: She swept the board at the awards ceremony. Australia swept the board in the swimming, with gold medals in every race. The government swept the board in yesterday's first contested National Assembly elections. Spain swept the board in boys' team competitions. Our team swept the board in the sports games.

english_meaning: A citrus fruit similar to a lemon but sweeter and less sour. A juicy green or yellowish fruit rich in vitamin C. A tropical fruit used to make refreshing drinks. A fruit known for its digestive and cooling properties. A common citrus fruit in South Asia and the Middle East.
example_sentence: A glass of fresh sweet lime juice is very refreshing. Doctors often recommend sweet lime for good digestion. She peeled a sweet lime and ate it slowly. Sweet limes are widely grown in Pakistan and India.

english_meaning: A starchy root vegetable with sweet orange or white flesh. An edible tuber that is roasted, boiled, or mashed. The trailing plant that produces these tubers. A nutritious food rich in fibre and vitamin A.
example_sentence: Roasted sweet potatoes are sold on street corners in winter. She mashed the sweet potato with a little butter. Sweet potato is healthier than an ordinary potato. The farmer harvested sweet potatoes before the frost.

english_meaning: To persuade someone using pleasant, flattering, or charming words, often to get what you want. To influence or convince someone by speaking in a very polite, friendly, or flattering way. Sometimes it is used when the intention is not fully honest, but aimed at gaining favor or advantage. Pleasant, flattering, or charming speech used to persuade or influence someone.
example_sentence: She tried to sweet-talk her boss into giving her a day off. He sweet-talked the guard into letting him enter without a ticket. Don’t try to sweet-talk me, I know what really happened. The salesman sweet-talked the customers into buying the expensive product.

english_meaning: To change direction suddenly, especially to avoid something. A sudden change of direction while moving. To move away from a planned course, aim, or principle. To cause a vehicle or object to turn sharply aside.
example_sentence: The driver swerved to avoid a stray dog. His car swerved sharply on the wet road. She never swerved from her principles. A sudden swerve saved them from a serious accident.

english_meaning: Moving or able to move very fast. Happening quickly or without delay. Done promptly and with little hesitation. A small fast-flying bird with long narrow wings.
example_sentence: The runner is known for his swift start. The government promised swift action on the complaint. She gave a swift reply without thinking twice. A swift darted across the evening sky.

english_meaning: To drink something in large gulps or in a greedy fashion. It also refers to the act of taking a long draft of a liquid, often directly from a bottle. It implies a quick and hearty consumption of a beverage.
example_sentence: He took a long swig of cold water after the race. She watched him swig his soda while leaning against the wall. The tired hiker took a swig from his canteen. Don't swig your juice so fast or you might choke.

english_meaning: To use deception to deprive someone of money or possessions. It involves a fraudulent scheme or a dishonest trick intended to cheat another person. Often, it refers to obtaining money through small-scale or calculated scams.
example_sentence: The silver-tongued salesman tried to swindle the elderly couple out of their savings. They uncovered a massive plot to swindle the insurance company using fake claims. He was arrested for attempting to swindle investors with a non-existent real estate project. Be careful not to let online scammers swindle you during the holiday shopping season.

english_meaning: A person who cheats others in order to get their money or property. A dishonest person who uses tricks and false promises to deceive people. A fraudster who obtains something by deception.
example_sentence: The swindler tricked several villagers out of their savings. Police finally arrested the swindler last week. He turned out to be a clever swindler. Never trust a swindler who promises quick profits.

english_meaning: A pig or a group of pigs. Used offensively to describe a person considered greedy, dirty, or unpleasant. In agriculture, refers to domestic pigs kept for meat or breeding.
example_sentence: The farmer kept a number of swine on his farm. Swine flu once spread rapidly across many countries. He behaved like a swine at the dinner table. Swine are known to eat almost anything they find. The angry teacher called the bullies a bunch of swine.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being like a swine. Greedy, coarse, or unpleasant behaviour. Piggish, selfish, or unrefined conduct. Extreme rudeness, gluttony, or dirtiness in a person's habits.
example_sentence: His swinishness at the dinner table shocked all the guests. The book criticised the swinishness of corrupt officials. Nothing can excuse such swinishness in a public place. She was disgusted by the swinishness of his manners. Swinishness has no place among educated people.

english_meaning: A leafy vegetable with large green leaves and colourful stalks. A vegetable eaten cooked like spinach or added to soups. The plant grown for these leaves and stems. A nutritious green rich in iron and vitamins.
example_sentence: Swiss chard has bright red and yellow stalks. She sauteed the Swiss chard with garlic. Swiss chard can be cooked like spinach. The garden bed is full of Swiss chard.

english_meaning: To rearrange or exchange the position of two or more things. To exchange roles, tasks, or opinions between people or objects.
example_sentence: The teacher switched around the seating plan. Can we switch around the meeting times? They switched around their travel schedule. I switched around the wires to fix the issue.

english_meaning: To return to a previous method, idea, or condition. To change direction suddenly or repeatedly.(In transportation or roads) A sharp bend or zigzag on a mountain road or railway.
example_sentence: After trying the new app, I switched back to the old one. She switched back to her original major. Let’s switch back to English for clarity. They switched back after realizing the change was unhelpful.

english_meaning: To alternate or move back and forth between two or more things.
example_sentence: I often switch between English and Sindhi while talking. She switches between tasks to stay focused. You can switch between windows using this shortcut. The TV allows you to switch between channels easily.

english_meaning: To turn off or deactivate a device. To lose interest or concentration.
example_sentence: Please switch off the lights. He switched off during the lecture. Don’t forget to switch off your phone. She switched off from work after 6 PM.

english_meaning: To activate or turn on a machine. To become alert or start focusing.
example_sentence: Switch on the computer before class. He switches on when there’s an emergency. She switched on the light. The machine switches on automatically.

english_meaning: To replace something or someone with another, to change one item for another.
