example_sentence: He switched out the old batteries for new ones. We switched out the broken chairs. The manager switched out two players during halftime. You can switch out ingredients in this recipe.

english_meaning: To change from one system, method, or device to another. To move from one thing to another, like changing channels, systems, or plans.
example_sentence: The company switched over to solar energy. Please switch over to Channel 5. We’ll switch over to digital next month. He switched over from banking to teaching.

english_meaning: To change or modify something to make it different or more interesting.
example_sentence: Let’s switch up the design for something fresher. He switched up his routine to stay motivated. You should switch up your workout once in a while. They switched up the menu for the new season.

english_meaning: In baseball, a batter who can hit from either the right or the left side of the plate. A person who is skilled at doing two different things or working in two different roles. Informally, someone who can adapt easily to either of two options.
example_sentence: The team signed a talented switch-hitter last season. As a switch-hitter, he confuses opposing pitchers. In our office she is a switch-hitter who handles sales and design. Good switch-hitters are rare in professional baseball.

english_meaning: A road, path or railway that climbs steeply by a series of sharp bends. A sudden reversal of direction or fortune. In British usage, a roller coaster. To turn sharply back in the opposite direction while climbing or descending.
example_sentence: The bus climbed the mountain by a series of switchbacks. The trail switchbacks up the steep hillside. The season was a switchback of wins and losses. Children queued for the switchback at the fair.

english_meaning: A pocket knife with a blade that springs out when a button is pressed. A flick knife, often associated with street crime. Anything with a folding blade that opens automatically.
example_sentence: The police found a switchblade in his jacket pocket. Carrying a switchblade is illegal in many countries. He opened the parcel with a small switchblade. The film shows gangs fighting with switchblades.

english_meaning: A panel or system used to connect and direct telephone calls within an organisation. A board with switches and instruments for controlling electric circuits. The department or staff that operates such a system.
example_sentence: Please call the switchboard and ask for extension four. The hospital switchboard was flooded with calls. An engineer checked the switchboard in the basement. She worked on the switchboard for many years.

english_meaning: Turned on so that electricity flows and a device works. Informally, alert, well informed and up to date. Aware of modern trends and quick to understand things. Mentally attentive and fully engaged.
example_sentence: The heater was already switched on when we arrived. She is a very switched on young manager. Make sure the machine is switched on before you begin. Our new teacher is switched on and full of ideas.

english_meaning: A sudden and unexpected change or reversal. A trick in which one thing is secretly swapped for another. An informal term for a surprising turnaround in a situation.
example_sentence: The magician pulled a clever switcheroo with the two boxes. In a surprise switcheroo, the underdog became team captain. They did a switcheroo and sent the other candidate instead. The ending of the film is a complete switcheroo.

english_meaning: Having very well-developed and muscular body due to exercise. Extremely muscular or bulked up, especially from weightlifting. In slang, physically strong and impressive-looking. Enlarged or puffed up in appearance. Informally used to praise a fit, powerful physique.
example_sentence: After a year at the gym, he looked totally swole. She admired his swole arms. The bodybuilder posted swole selfies online. Everyone in the team is getting swole for the competition.

english_meaning: To move rapidly downwards through the air, especially in an attack. To make a sudden and quick attack or arrival. A sudden diving movement, especially by a bird. A sudden raid or action, especially by police or officials.
example_sentence: The eagle made a swift swoop and caught the small rabbit. Police swooped on the hideout early in the morning. The plane made a low swoop over the field. Robbers swooped down on the shop and grabbed the cash. The hawk was ready to swoop on its prey.

english_meaning: Having taken an oath or made a solemn promise. Committed by an oath to a particular position, belief, or duty. Used to describe declared enemies, allies, or officials who have made a formal promise. Past participle of the verb swear.
example_sentence: The judge and the lawyers were sworn to tell the truth. They have been sworn enemies since childhood. He gave a sworn statement in the court. She is a sworn defender of women's rights. The two families used to be sworn friends of each other.

english_meaning: To study something very hard and carefully, especially for an exam. A person who studies very hard all the time, especially someone who spends too much time studying.
example_sentence: Ahmed is such a swot because he spends all evening doing homework. She swotted for her final exams all weekend. The teacher praised the swot for always being prepared. I need to swot up on mathematics before the test.

english_meaning: To revise or review subject material thoroughly. To memorize facts by repeated study. To prepare intensively for an exam or assessment. To gain knowledge about something in a short time with focused effort
example_sentence: I had to swot up on history before the final exam. She swotted up all night for the science test. He swotted up on computer programming before the interview. We need to swot up on grammar rules for the quiz.

english_meaning: A person who is self-indulgent and devoted to luxury and pleasure; someone who lives only for comfort and sensual enjoyment.
example_sentence: The sybarite spent his fortune on fine dining and travel. She was a sybarite who only wore the finest silk. The sybarite refused to stay anywhere without five-star amenities. His sybarite lifestyle left him bankrupt by forty.

english_meaning: Behavior that praises important or powerful people too much and in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get something from them.
example_sentence: The cosy sycophancy toward Smith was unbearable. I have never seen such sycophancy as at the Cannes press conferences. I hope that from me he will get neither unfair attack nor sycophancy.

english_meaning: A person who praises important or powerful people too much and in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get something from them. One who uses compliments to gain self-serving favor or advantage from another.
example_sentence: The prime minister is surrounded by sycophants. He is enabled by low-life sycophants who thrill in being around his celebrity.

english_meaning: Praising important or powerful people too much and in a way that is not sincere, especially in order to get something from them. Attempting to win favor from influential people by flattery.
example_sentence: There was sycophantic laughter from the audience at every one of his terrible jokes.

english_meaning: In a flattering or obsequious way to gain favor. Acting in an excessively flattering or submissive manner toward someone important or powerful, usually to gain personal advantage. It often implies insincerity or manipulation.
example_sentence: He smiled sycophantically at his boss to avoid being scolded. She nodded sycophantically during the meeting to gain favor. The student laughed sycophantically at the teacher’s jokes. He complimented sycophantically to secure a promotion.

english_meaning: The plural form of syllabus, meaning outlines of the topics covered in a course of study. Official documents listing the subjects, texts, and requirements of academic courses. Detailed plans showing what students are expected to learn during a term or year. Course guides issued by schools, colleges, or examination boards.
synonyms: ["Curricula","Course outlines","Programmes of study","Schemes of work","Study plans","Prospectuses"]
example_sentence: The new syllabi will be introduced from next session. Teachers were asked to review the syllabi of all science subjects. The university publishes its syllabi on the official website. Both syllabi cover similar topics but differ in assessment.

english_meaning: A single sound unit in a word. A unit of pronunciation that contains a vowel sound and may include surrounding consonants. Words can have one or more syllables, and syllables help in correct pronunciation, stress, and rhythm of speech.
example_sentence: The word cat has one syllable. Happy has two syllables. Teachers help students break words into syllables. Correct stress on each syllable improves pronunciation.

english_meaning: A form of logical argument in which a conclusion is drawn from two given statements called premises. A method of reasoning in which two statements lead to a logical conclusion. Any clever or formal piece of reasoning.
example_sentence: A classic syllogism is: All men are mortal, Socrates is a man, therefore Socrates is mortal. The teacher explained the rules of syllogism to the students. His argument was based on a faulty syllogism. Philosophers use the syllogism to test reasoning. The lecture began with a simple syllogism.

english_meaning: Relating to a syllogism, a form of logical reasoning in which a conclusion is drawn from two given statements. Based on strict, formal logic rather than experience or emotion. Describing an argument that moves from general premises to a specific conclusion. Sometimes used critically to mean overly formal or mechanical reasoning.
example_sentence: The philosopher explained the argument in syllogistic form. His syllogistic reasoning impressed the examiners. The essay follows a strictly syllogistic structure. Not every problem can be solved by syllogistic logic alone.

english_meaning: Use of symbols to represent ideas or qualities. The practice of using symbols, objects, figures, or colors, to represent abstract ideas, concepts, or deeper meanings beyond their literal sense. It is often used in literature, art, and religion.
example_sentence: The dove is a common symbolism of peace. In the novel, darkness is used as symbolism for fear and evil. Red color often carries symbolism of love or danger. The broken chain in the painting shows symbolism of freedom.

english_meaning: Something that is the same in shape, size, and position on both sides of a dividing line or around a central point. Often used in mathematics, geometry, nature, and design.
example_sentence: The butterfly’s wings are perfectly symmetric. The architect designed a symmetric building with identical facades. Snowflakes often have symmetric patterns. The mathematician studied symmetric equations.

english_meaning: Something that is evenly balanced or proportioned, where one side mirrors the other, giving a sense of harmony or regularity.
example_sentence: The human face is often considered symmetrical. The building has a symmetrical design. The butterfly’s wings are perfectly symmetrical. The garden layout is symmetrical along the central path.

english_meaning: In a balanced or proportionate way. Something done in a way that has symmetry, meaning both sides correspond in size, shape, or arrangement. Often used in geometry, design, or general contexts to indicate balance or proportion.
example_sentence: The windows were arranged symmetrically on both sides of the hall. The painting was composed symmetrically, giving it a sense of balance. The garden paths mirror each other symmetrically. The architect designed the building symmetrically for aesthetic appeal.

english_meaning: Balanced and proportional arrangement of parts. A state where parts of something correspond in size, shape, or position on opposite sides of a dividing line or around a center. It is often used in mathematics, art, architecture, and nature to describe harmony and balance.
example_sentence: The symmetry of the butterfly's wings is perfect. The architect designed the building with symmetry in mind. Symmetry in facial features often contributes to perceived beauty. The snowflake shows natural symmetry in its structure.

english_meaning: A feeling of pity or sorrow for someone else's suffering. Understanding and sharing another person's emotions. Support or agreement with someone's opinion or cause. A show of kindness during difficult times. A natural connection or harmony between people.
example_sentence: She showed great sympathy for the earthquake victims. He wrote a letter to express his sympathy. Many people felt deep sympathy for the poor family. Her kind words gave him much needed sympathy.

english_meaning: A long musical composition for a full orchestra, usually in several movements. A pleasing combination of sounds, colours, or things that go well together. A group of instruments playing together in harmony.
example_sentence: Beethoven's ninth symphony is world-famous. The concert ended with a beautiful classical symphony. The garden was a symphony of colours in spring. Their voices blended into a soft symphony of sound. She spent years learning to conduct a symphony orchestra.

english_meaning: A formal meeting or conference for discussion of a subject. An academic gathering to present and exchange research or ideas.
example_sentence: The university organized a symposium on climate change and sustainable development. During the symposium, several doctors presented their latest medical research. The annual literature symposium attracted writers, poets, and critics from all over the country. A symposium on disaster risk reduction provided valuable recommendations for policymakers.

english_meaning: A sign or indication of a disease, problem, or condition. An observable or felt sign that indicates the presence of a particular condition, illness, or problem. It may be physical, emotional, or behavioral. Symptoms help identify underlying causes but are not the cause themselves.
example_sentence: Coughing and fever are common symptoms of the flu. Headache can be a symptom of dehydration. Anxiety is often a symptom of stress. Rash is a symptom that may indicate an allergic reaction.

english_meaning: A Jewish place of worship. A building where Jewish people gather for prayer, religious study, community meetings, and reading of sacred texts such as the Torah. It also functions as a cultural and social center for the Jewish community.
example_sentence: The Jewish community gathered at the synagogue for their weekly prayers. The synagogue also serves as a center for education and cultural events. Tourists visited the historic synagogue to learn about Jewish heritage. The rabbi delivered a meaningful sermon in the synagogue on Saturday morning.

english_meaning: To happen at the same time or to move at the same speed as something, to make something do this. To link data files between one computer or mobile device and another so that the information in the files on both machines is the same. A state in which things happen at the same time or in the same way, or are suited to each other.
example_sentence: The live music isn't synced to the visuals. Bluetooth technology will enable a cell phone to sync with a car's stereo speaker. His opinions were in sync with those of his colleagues. He's putting himself forward as a president whose ideas are in sync with (= are suited to and show an understanding of) a nation demanding change.

english_meaning: To happen at the same time or to move at the same speed as something, to make something do this. To link data files between one computer or mobile device and another so that the information in the files on both machines is the same. A state in which things happen at the same time or in the same way, or are suited to each other.
example_sentence: Wait for the computer to synch up with your command.

english_meaning: Occurring at the same time. Happening together in time. Existing or taking place simultaneously. A less common form of the word synchronous, used mainly in older or technical writing.
example_sentence: The two events were synchronal, taking place in different cities at the same hour. The clocks in the school were kept perfectly synchronal. Their steps were synchronal as they marched down the road. The synchronal firing of the guns marked the beginning of the ceremony. In an orchestra the movements of the players must be synchronal.

english_meaning: Relating to events, phenomena, or analysis occurring at the same time. Refers to looking at something as it exists at one particular point in time rather than its historical development. Often used in linguistics or social sciences to describe structures or events that are observed simultaneously.
example_sentence: The linguist conducted a synchronic study of the language as it is spoken today. The museum displayed a synchronic collection of artworks from different countries. Her research focused on a synchronic analysis of social media trends. The conference examined the synchronic impact of climate change in various regions.

english_meaning: To happen at the same time or to move at the same speed as something, to make something do this. To (cause to) happen at the same time. To represent or arrange (events) to indicate coincidence or coexistence.
example_sentence: The sound track did not synchronise with the action. The show was designed so that the lights synchronised with the music. We'd better synchronise our watches if we all want to be there at the same time.

english_meaning: The condition of occurring at the same time. The state of being synchronous. Coincidence in time of events or actions. In art, a movement that uses colour rhythmically like music.
example_sentence: The synchronism of the drums and dancers impressed the audience. Historians study the synchronism between important events of different countries. Perfect synchronism was needed for the fireworks display. The film was praised for the synchronism of its sound and picture. Artists in the Synchronism movement used colours in a musical way.

english_meaning: The process of causing things to happen at the same time or operate together. Coordinating events, actions, or processes so that they occur at the same time or in a proper sequence. It is often used in technology, communication, music, and daily activities where timing is essential.
example_sentence: The team practiced daily to achieve perfect synchronization in their dance routine. The clocks in the building were synchronized to show the exact same time. Video and audio need proper synchronization for a smooth presentation. The athletes’ movements were in perfect synchronization during the performance.

english_meaning: To happen at the same time or to move at the same speed as something, to make something do this. To (cause to) happen at the same time. To represent or arrange (events) to indicate coincidence or coexistence.
example_sentence: The sound track did not synchronize with the action. The show was designed so that the lights synchronized with the music. We'd better synchronize our watches if we all want to be there at the same time.

english_meaning: A person or device that makes two or more things happen at the same time. A mechanism used in machines, films, or communication systems to keep separate parts working together in time. Something that synchronises signals, movements, or actions.
example_sentence: A synchronizer is used to match the sound with the picture in films. The engineer replaced the faulty synchronizer in the machine. Modern cameras have a built-in synchronizer for the flash. A signal synchronizer keeps data lines aligned. The music mixer worked as a synchronizer for the whole band.

english_meaning: Happening or existing at the same time. At the same time, at the same frequency. Happening, existing, or arising at precisely the same time. Existing or occurring at the same period of time.
example_sentence: Thus, tidal forces can lead to synchronous rotation. The software supports most synchronous communications cards. The synchronous arrival of a baby sister and loss of a beloved grandmother strongly affected the child.

english_meaning: A group of individuals or organizations combined to promote a common interest. An association of businesses working together, often for profit. An agency that sells material like articles or comics for simultaneous publication. A network of criminals engaged in organized illegal activity. To publish or broadcast content through several outlets at once.
example_sentence: A crime syndicate was busted by the police. The article was syndicated in many newspapers. A syndicate of investors bought the property. The drug syndicate operated across borders.

english_meaning: The sale or distribution of articles, columns, television programs, radio shows, or other content to multiple outlets. The continued broadcast of a television program by different stations after its original run. The formation or operation of a group that jointly undertakes a business, loan, or investment. The automatic distribution of online content through feeds.
example_sentence: The comedy became more popular after entering syndication. Her weekly column is distributed through newspaper syndication. Several banks joined the loan syndication to share the risk. The website uses content syndication to reach new readers.

english_meaning: A group of symptoms which consistently occur together, or a condition characterized by a set of associated symptoms. It can also refer to a characteristic pattern of behavior or a specific social problem. In medicine, it identifies a specific disease or disorder.
example_sentence: The patient was diagnosed with a rare genetic syndrome. Doctors are looking for a common link between these syndrome symptoms. Irritable bowel syndrome can cause significant discomfort and stress. The metabolic syndrome increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.

english_meaning: A figure of speech in which a part is used to represent the whole. A figure of speech in which the whole represents a part. An expression in which a specific term represents a broader class or a broad term represents something specific.
example_sentence: Using wheels to mean a car is an example of synecdoche. The teacher explained synecdoche with the phrase all hands on deck. Poets often use synecdoche to create vivid imagery. Calling workers hired hands is a familiar synecdoche.

english_meaning: Working together to produce an effect greater than the sum of the individual efforts. Involving cooperation between things or people so that the combined result is better. Relating to the process where two or more things enhance each other's action.
example_sentence: The two medicines have a synergistic effect when taken together. A synergistic relationship between the two departments improved the company's performance. Teamwork creates a synergistic energy that benefits everyone. The trainer explained the synergistic action of diet and exercise. The synergistic partnership boosted both brands.

english_meaning: In a way that combines different elements so their total effect is greater than their separate effects. Through cooperative interaction. In a mutually reinforcing or complementary manner.
example_sentence: The two medicines work synergistically to control the infection. The departments collaborated synergistically on the new project. These ingredients act synergistically to deepen the flavor. Exercise and a balanced diet can work synergistically to improve health.

english_meaning: The interaction or cooperation of two or more organizations, substances, or other agents to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their separate effects. It describes a beneficial harmony where teamwork yields superior results. It is frequently used in business and biological contexts.
example_sentence: The synergy between the two companies led to a massive increase in profits. Teamwork creates a synergy that helps solve complex problems faster. There is a natural synergy between the marketing and sales departments. The drug combination showed a positive synergy in treating the infection.

english_meaning: A word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language. A word that can be used interchangeably with another in certain contexts. One of two or more expressions with the same or very similar meaning.
example_sentence: Happy and joyful are synonyms, as both describe a feeling of pleasure. A good thesaurus will provide several synonyms for any word you search. She looked for a synonym of the word begin to avoid repetition in her essay. Brave and courageous are near synonyms, though they carry slightly different connotations. Using a variety of synonyms makes writing more engaging and less repetitive.

english_meaning: A brief summary or general survey of something. It provides a condensed version of a book, play, or movie plot to give the reader the main points. It is designed to provide a quick overview without exhaustive detail.
example_sentence: The editor asked for a one-page synopsis of the new novel. Can you give me a quick synopsis of what happened in the meeting? The program included a brief synopsis of the opera's plot. I read the synopsis on the back of the DVD case before renting it.

english_meaning: Related to syntax, the arrangement of words and phrases to form correct sentences in a language. It refers to the rules and structure governing how words are arranged in a sentence. It deals with sentence formation, word order, and grammatical relationships between words.
example_sentence: The sentence contains several syntactic errors. Linguists study syntactic patterns in different languages. The software can identify syntactic mistakes in writing. Word order is an important syntactic feature of English.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the arrangement of words and phrases according to the rules of grammar. The structure and arrangement of words, phrases, and clauses in a sentence according to grammatical rules. It focuses on whether a sentence is correctly formed, regardless of its meaning.
example_sentence: The sentence is syntactically correct but semantically confusing. The linguist analyzed the text syntactically to identify its grammatical structure. Although the words were familiar, they were not arranged syntactically. The software checks documents syntactically before processing them.

english_meaning: In linguistics, an orderly combination of linguistic units, such as words in a sentence, that form a meaningful whole. A sequence of elements arranged according to grammatical rules. A structured chain of related items in language or thought.
example_sentence: A syntagm is formed when words are placed together to make a phrase. Every language has its own rules for building a syntagm. The teacher analysed the sentence as a syntagm of subject, verb, and object. Poets sometimes break the normal syntagm for effect. Linguists study how meaning is built through syntagms.

english_meaning:
Sentence structure. Grammatical arrangement. Word order
Language rules. Structural organization of expressions. Programming code rules. Set of rules that governs how words, phrases, clauses, or symbols are arranged to form correct sentences in a language or valid statements in a computer programming language.
example_sentence: The teacher explained the syntax of English sentences to the students. Incorrect syntax can make a sentence difficult to understand. The programmer received an error because of a syntax mistake in the code. Learning syntax is essential for writing clear and correct language.

english_meaning: An electronic musical instrument, typically operated by a keyboard, producing a wide variety of sounds by generating and combining signals of different frequencies. It is a shortened form of the word synthesizer. These instruments are fundamental in modern electronic music production.
example_sentence: The musician used a vintage synth to create a unique atmosphere for the track. Many modern pop songs rely heavily on layers of electronic synth pads. He spent hours tweaking the settings on his analog synth. Digital synth technology has advanced significantly over the last decade.

english_meaning: The combination of ideas, components, or elements to form a connected whole. In chemistry, it refers to the production of chemical compounds by reaction from simpler materials. It describes the process of merging different parts into a unified entity.
example_sentence: The final report was a brilliant synthesis of various research findings. Photosynthesis is the synthesis of chemical compounds with the aid of radiant energy. Her ideology represents a synthesis of traditional values and modern logic. The professor asked for a synthesis of the two opposing theories.

english_meaning: To combine a number of things into a coherent whole. In a technical sense, it means to produce a substance or sound biologically or electronically. It involves the act of integrating various diverse elements to form a single system.
example_sentence: It is difficult to synthesise so many different styles into one cohesive artwork. The laboratory was able to synthesise the new drug in just three weeks. Modern computers can synthesise human speech with remarkable accuracy. We need to synthesise the data collected from all the various departments.

english_meaning: To combine different ideas, substances, or elements into a whole. To produce a substance artificially. To combine information from different sources. To create something new from existing elements. To form a coherent idea or theory. To bring together separate parts such as ideas, information, or materials and combine them into a new, unified whole. It is commonly used in science, writing, and thinking processes.
example_sentence: The scientist synthesized a new chemical compound in the lab. She synthesized information from several books to write her report. Good writers synthesize ideas to create strong arguments. The machine can synthesize human speech very clearly.

english_meaning: Made by chemical synthesis, especially to imitate a natural product. Artificially produced rather than occurring naturally. Not genuine or authentic; contrived.
example_sentence: The fabric was made from synthetic fibres that were cheaper and more durable than natural alternatives. Many perfumes contain synthetic compounds that mimic the smell of rare natural ingredients. Her smile appeared synthetic and did not quite reach her eyes. The synthetic rubber used in the tyres performed just as well as the natural variety. Scientists developed a synthetic substitute for the endangered plant compound used in the medication.

english_meaning: A straight-line configuration of three celestial bodies in a gravitational system. The alignment of the sun, earth, and moon during an eclipse or full/new moon. Any pair or union of related or connected things. A conjunction or opposition of heavenly bodies as viewed from earth.
example_sentence: A solar eclipse occurs during the syzygy of the sun, moon, and earth. Astronomers gathered to observe the rare syzygy last night. The tides are strongest during a syzygy of the moon and sun. Ancient cultures often held ceremonies during a syzygy.

english_meaning: A small flap or strip of material attached to something for pulling or identifying it. A running bill or account for goods or services especially at a restaurant or bar. A small loop or tag used to open a can. To keep a record or watch on someone or something.
example_sentence: Pull the tab to open the packaging. He generously offered to pick up the tab for our dinner. The soda can's tab broke off before I could open it. The manager asked us to tab the expenses for the monthly report.

english_meaning: To observe or monitor someone's activities carefully. To keep a record of someone's actions or expenses.
synonyms: ["Keep Tabs On","Monitor Closely","Keep Track Of","Observe Carefully","Watch Over","Keep An Eye On","Surveil","Track Activities","Shadow Someone"]
antonyms: ["Ignore Completely","Lose Track Of","Neglect","Disregard","Turn A Blind Eye","Look The Other Way","Forget About","Pay No Attention To"]
example_sentence: The manager decided to keep a tab on someone who was suspected of leaking information. She keeps a close tab on someone whenever they act suspiciously. It is difficult to keep a tab on someone who is constantly traveling. The detectives put a tab on someone to track their daily movements.

english_meaning: A large spoon used for serving food at the table. A cooking measurement equal to three teaspoons, or about fifteen milliliters. The amount of food or liquid that such a spoon holds. A standard measure written as tbsp in recipes.
example_sentence: Add two tablespoons of olive oil to the pan. She served the rice with a large wooden tablespoon. One tablespoon of honey makes the tea sweet enough. The recipe needs three tablespoons of tomato paste.

english_meaning: A newspaper with small pages, usually containing short articles and many pictures. A popular newspaper that focuses on sensational news, gossip, and celebrities. Relating to a style of journalism that is dramatic rather than serious. Something presented in a condensed or simplified form.
example_sentence: The story appeared on the front page of every tabloid. Tabloid newspapers often exaggerate celebrity scandals. He was criticized for his tabloid style of reporting. She refuses to give interviews to the tabloid press.

english_meaning: A social or religious custom forbidding a particular practice or behaviour. Something that is not allowed to be done or talked about. Forbidden or restricted by social agreement. To place a ban or restriction on something.
example_sentence: Discussing certain personal matters is still a taboo in many families. Some cultures consider it a taboo to eat certain foods. It was once taboo for women to work in that field. The book breaks many social taboos of its time. People rarely spoke of such things because they were taboo.

english_meaning: Understood or implied without being directly stated. Expressed silently or by actions rather than words. Suggested through behaviour, attitude, or context. Used for agreements, approvals, or understandings that are accepted by everyone involved even though nothing has been formally said or written.
example_sentence: There was a tacit agreement between the two leaders not to discuss the issue. His silence was taken as tacit approval of the plan. The team had a tacit understanding about their roles. Many cultural rules are tacit rather than written. By staying quiet, she gave her tacit consent to the proposal.

english_meaning: Reserved or uncommunicative in speech. Saying little. Preferring silence over conversation. Habitually quiet and not inclined to talk much. Used to describe a person whose nature is to remain silent, speak briefly, or avoid sharing thoughts and feelings openly with others.
example_sentence: He is a taciturn man who rarely shares his feelings. The taciturn old farmer answered only with a nod. She felt uneasy with his taciturn behavior during dinner. Despite being taciturn, he was deeply respected by everyone. The new officer was taciturn but very observant.

english_meaning: To add something extra to what already exists, often in a careless or hurried way. To attach an additional part, cost, or clause at the end of something. To include an item that was not part of the original plan. To fasten one thing lightly to another.
example_sentence: The hotel tacked on a service charge without telling us. He tacked on a short apology at the end of the letter. They tacked on two extra days to the training course. She tacked on a note to remind him about the meeting.

english_meaning: To attach or add something to a particular thing. To join an extra part, condition, or amount to something already complete. To append a remark, clause, or item to the end of a text or plan. To fix one object loosely onto another.
synonyms: ["Attach to","Add to","Append to","Affix to","Annex to","Fasten to","Join to","Connect to","Stick to"]
antonyms: ["Detach from","Remove from","Separate from","Delete from","Take off","Exclude from","Disconnect from"]
example_sentence: They tacked an extra fee onto the final bill. She tacked a personal message onto the official report. The builder tacked a small porch onto the front of the house. Do not tack new rules onto an agreement people have already signed.

english_meaning: The quality of being slightly sticky to the touch. The condition of a surface, such as paint or glue, that has not dried completely. The quality of being cheap, showy, or in poor taste. Behaviour or style that is considered vulgar and lacking elegance.
example_sentence: Test the tackiness of the paint before adding a second coat. The tackiness of the glue makes it easy to position the paper. Critics complained about the tackiness of the stage decorations. There was a certain tackiness in the way he boasted about money.

english_meaning: To deal with a difficult problem or task in a determined way. To stop an opposing player who has the ball in sports such as football or rugby. To speak to someone directly about a difficult or awkward matter. The equipment used for a particular activity, especially fishing. A system of ropes and pulleys used for lifting heavy objects.
example_sentence: The government must tackle unemployment as soon as possible. He tackled the striker just before he reached the goal. She finally tackled her brother about the missing money. My uncle keeps all his fishing tackle in the garage.

english_meaning: A player who stops an opponent carrying the ball in sports such as rugby or football. A person who brings down or seizes another to stop their movement. Someone who deals with a problem or difficult task with determination. A person who confronts or challenges another directly.
example_sentence: He is the strongest tackler in the entire team. The tackler brought the runner down near the goal line. Two tacklers failed to stop the fast winger. She is a fearless tackler of social problems in her community.

english_meaning: Showing poor taste, especially in a cheap, gaudy, or vulgar way. Slightly sticky to the touch, especially referring to paint, glue, or varnish that has not fully dried. Used informally to describe behavior, decorations, or clothing considered tasteless or low quality. Lacking elegance or sophistication, often in an embarrassing way.
example_sentence: The decorations at the party looked tacky and cheaply made.  Be careful, the paint on the wall is still tacky.  Her outfit was considered tacky for such a formal occasion.  The souvenir shop was full of tacky plastic trinkets.  His tacky jokes embarrassed everyone at the dinner table.

english_meaning: A planned method used to achieve a goal or deal with a situation. A specific action, method, or strategy used carefully to reach a desired result, especially in politics, business, debate, sports, or military activities. It usually focuses on short term steps that support a larger plan.
example_sentence: The coach used a new tactic to defeat the stronger team. Negotiators adopted a calm tactic to reduce tension during the meeting. Delaying the decision was a clever tactic to gain more time. The general changed his tactic when the battle situation became difficult.

english_meaning: Relating to or connected with the sense of touch. Perceived by touch or designed to be touched. Tangible; able to be felt physically. Having a pleasant texture or surface that invites touching. Of a person, fond of touching others in a friendly way.
example_sentence: Babies learn about the world mainly through tactile experiences. The artist designs sculptures that are deeply tactile and meant to be touched. The phone has a soft, tactile surface that feels good in the hand. Blind readers rely on the tactile patterns of Braille. He is a very tactile person who often hugs his friends.

english_meaning: A Korean martial art. A combat sport practiced worldwide. A method of self defense. A system of physical and mental training. An Olympic sport emphasizing kicking skills.
synonyms: ["Martial art","Combat sport","Self defense system","Korean martial art","Fighting discipline"]
example_sentence: She practices taekwondo three times a week to improve her fitness. Taekwondo teaches students discipline, respect, and self confidence. My brother won a gold medal in a taekwondo competition. Learning taekwondo helped him develop quick reflexes and self defense skills.

english_meaning: A variant spelling of TEDIUM means a feeling of weariness, boredom, mental fatigue, dissatisfaction, or lack of interest caused by something that is repetitive, dull, or uninteresting.
example_sentence: After months of performing the same task, he experienced a sense of taedium and wanted a new challenge. The long and repetitive lectures filled the students with taedium. She escaped the taedium of daily life by traveling to new places and meeting different people. The writer struggled with taedium while working on the manuscript for many years.

english_meaning: A deep weariness of life, boredom with existence, or loss of interest in living and everyday activities. A state in which a person feels tired of life, emotionally exhausted, uninterested in daily activities, and unable to find joy or purpose. It can refer to profound boredom, dissatisfaction, disillusionment, or existential fatigue.
example_sentence: After years of disappointment, he experienced a profound taedium vitae and lost interest in many activities. The novel explores the taedium vitae felt by a man who sees no purpose in his routine existence. Her taedium vitae disappeared when she found meaningful work and supportive friends. Philosophers have often discussed taedium vitae as a form of existential dissatisfaction.

english_meaning: A Korean martial art. A combat sport practiced worldwide. A method of self defense. A system of physical and mental training. An Olympic sport emphasizing kicking skills.
synonyms: ["Martial art","Combat sport","Self defense system","Korean martial art","Fighting discipline"]
example_sentence: She practices taekwondo three times a week to improve her fitness. Taekwondo teaches students discipline, respect, and self confidence. My brother won a gold medal in a taekwondo competition. Learning taekwondo helped him develop quick reflexes and self defense skills.

english_meaning: To go somewhere with someone, especially without being invited. To accompany another person as a companion or follower. To follow closely behind a group or individual. A person who habitually follows others around.
example_sentence: Do you mind if I tag along to the market? My younger brother always tags along when I meet my friends. She tagged along with the team to the tournament. He was happy to tag along rather than stay at home.

english_meaning: The small triangular bone at the base of the spine, also known as the coccyx. The lowest part of the backbone formed by fused vertebrae. The bone at the very bottom of the spine that can be injured by falling.
example_sentence: She bruised her tailbone when she slipped on the stairs. Sitting on a hard chair hurts my tailbone. The doctor took an X-ray of his tailbone. A cushion can reduce pressure on the tailbone.

english_meaning: A person who makes or alters clothes, especially for men. To make or adapt something for a particular purpose or person. To sew clothes to fit an individual's measurements. To adjust a plan or service to specific needs.
example_sentence: The tailor finished the suit two days before the wedding. We can tailor the course to suit your requirements. She asked the tailor to shorten the sleeves. The company tailors its services for small businesses.

english_meaning: Made or adapted for a particular person or purpose. Cut and sewn to fit closely and neatly. Specially designed to meet specific needs. Smart and well-fitted in appearance.
example_sentence: He wore a beautifully tailored grey jacket. The bank offers tailored loans for farmers. She received a tailored training plan from her coach. The tailored curtains fitted the windows perfectly.

english_meaning: To spoil or damage purity or reputation. To contaminate something physically or morally, or to damage someone’s reputation by association with something bad. The mark or influence of corruption or impurity. The presence or influence of something bad, impure, or corrupt.
example_sentence: The water was tainted by industrial waste. His reputation was tainted by false allegations. Corruption can taint an entire organization. Even a small lie can taint trust permanently. There was no taint of corruption in the report. The product carried a taint of poor quality. He worked hard to remove the taint from his name.

english_meaning: To go for a walk, usually in nature (mountains, forest, countryside). To tell someone rudely to go away,  leave or get lost.
example_sentence: This is my property, take a hike!. They paid Miss Beane to take a hike. She came back when the money ran out. We decided to take a hike in the hills this weekend. He was bothering me, so I told him to take a hike”.

word: Take a leaf out of someone's book
english_meaning: To follow someone's example or behavior. To learn from another person's actions. To imitate a good habit or method. To use someone else's approach as a model. To copy a successful person's way of doing things.
example_sentence: You should take a leaf out of your sister's book. I decided to take a leaf out of his book and start exercising. Teachers should take a leaf out of her book on patience. Let us take a leaf out of their book on teamwork.

english_meaning: To politely decline an invitation while suggesting that it be rescheduled for a later time. To postpone an offer or acceptance of a proposal. To delay a social engagement or appointment to a future date. To signify that one cannot participate now but wishes to do so later.
example_sentence: I would love to go to dinner, but I have to take a rain check. Can I take a rain check on our movie night until next Friday? He was too busy to attend the party and asked to take a rain check. She decided to take a rain check on the shopping trip because she felt ill.

english_meaning: To cause damage, suffering, loss, or a negative effect on someone or something over time. To have a harmful physical, emotional, mental, financial, or environmental effect. It usually describes something that gradually causes damage, stress, exhaustion, illness, or loss. The expression can also refer to disasters, accidents, wars, diseases, or difficult situations causing deaths or serious harm.
example_sentence: Years of hard work finally took a toll on his health. The long drought took a toll on local farmers and their crops. Constant stress can take a toll on your mental well-being. The economic crisis took a toll on many small businesses.

word: Take a turn for the worse
english_meaning: To become worse or more serious after a period of stability or improvement. This phrase is used when a situation, health condition, or event suddenly becomes more negative, serious, or difficult than before. It often refers to illness, problems, or general conditions that decline after seeming stable or slightly better.
example_sentence: His health took a turn for the worse during the night. The weather suddenly took a turn for the worse, and heavy rain started. After the argument, their relationship took a turn for the worse. The patient seemed stable, but his condition took a turn for the worse in the evening.

english_meaning: To make someone feel sudden surprise or confusion, often because something unexpected happened. It usually describes an emotional reaction to a surprising event, statement, or action.
example_sentence: I was completely taken aback by her sudden announcement. The news of his resignation took everyone aback. He was taken aback when he saw the unexpected gift. The teacher was taken aback by the students’ knowledge of the topic.

english_meaning: To resemble someone in appearance, behavior, or character, especially a parent or relative.
example_sentence: She takes after her mother. Ali takes after his father in being very patient and calm. She takes after her mother in looks and voice. You take after your uncle, always telling jokes and making people laugh. My sister takes after our grandmother; they both love cooking.

english_meaning: To disassemble or separate something into its component parts. To analyse or examine something in great detail, often critically. To defeat or criticise someone or something thoroughly.
example_sentence: He took apart the old clock to see how its mechanism worked. The expert was able to take apart the argument and expose each of its fundamental flaws. She took apart the toy to fix the broken wheel inside. The coach took apart the team's performance in the post-match analysis session. The journalist methodically took apart the official explanation piece by piece.

english_meaning: To return something to the place or person it came from. To admit that a statement or opinion was wrong (to withdraw words). To accept someone again after separation or disagreement. To make someone remember something from the past.
example_sentence: He took back his statement. I need to take back the book I borrowed from the library. He took back his rude comment after realizing it hurt her feelings. She finally took him back after he apologized. That old song takes me back to my childhood.

english_meaning: To write down or record information. To remove something that is hanging or fixed. To defeat or bring down someone (especially in competition or fight). To dismantle or disassemble something.
example_sentence: Please take down the notes during the meeting. He took down the old pictures from the wall. The police took down the criminal after a long chase. Workers took down the stage after the event ended.

english_meaning: To wrongly believe that someone or something is a particular person or thing. To regard or consider in a certain way. To mistake one person for another. To assume something without checking.
example_sentence: I took him for the manager of the shop. Do not take me for a fool. She was often taken for her elder sister. They took his silence for agreement.

english_meaning: To become sick or unwell suddenly. To fall into illness. To be offended by something said or done. To receive a remark badly.
synonyms: ["Fall sick","Become ill","Sicken","Be taken unwell","Resent","Be offended","Take offence"]
example_sentence: He took ill during the journey and had to return. She took ill soon after the wedding. Do not take it ill if I speak frankly. He took my advice ill and stopped talking to me.

english_meaning: To understand or absorb information. To allow someone to stay in your home. To include or cover something. To deceive someone.
example_sentence: I was taken in by his story. I couldn’t take in everything the teacher said. They took in the homeless man for a night. The trip takes in all the main sights of the city. She was taken in by his charm and lies. It was hard to take in all the details at once. They took in a stray cat. The tour takes in several historical places Don’t be taken in by his lies.

english_meaning: To consider or include something (such as facts, feelings, or circumstances) when making a decision or forming an opinion.
synonyms: ["Consider","Bear in mind","Regard","Keep in mind","Factor in","Take into consideration"]
example_sentence: Take his age into account before judging. You must take into account the weather before planning the event. The teacher took into account the student’s personal problems while grading. When building a house, engineers take into account the strength of the soil. We should take into account everyone’s opinion before making the final decision.

word: Take it with a grain of salt
english_meaning: Listen carefully but do not believe fully. Not to believe something completely or to treat it with doubt or caution.
example_sentence: I heard the news, but I took it with a grain of salt because the source is not reliable. You should take his promises with a grain of salt; he often exaggerates. She said she would finish the work today, but I took it with a grain of salt. Take online reviews with a grain of salt; not all of them are genuine.

english_meaning: To rise into the air (for an aircraft). To remove something, especially clothing. To become successful or popular quickly. To leave a place suddenly.
example_sentence: The plane took off on time. The plane will take off in two hours. Please take off your shoes before entering the room. Her business really took off after she started online marketing. He saw the police and took off immediately.

english_meaning: To accept a task or responsibility. To fight or compete against someone. To employ or hire someone. To develop or assume a particular quality or appearance.
example_sentence: She took on extra work. She decided to take on a new project at work. The small company can’t take on such a big competitor. The organization is taking on new employees this month. His voice took on a serious tone during the meeting.

english_meaning: To accept, understand, or consider someone’s idea, opinion, or advice seriously or to include someone in a process or decision-making.
example_sentence: The manager took on board the team’s suggestions before finalizing the plan. We should take on board the feedback from the community. She didn’t take on board my advice and made a mistake. The company took on board new staff to improve services.

english_meaning: To remove something from a place. To bring something outside. To invite someone out (especially for a meal or date). To obtain something officially (like insurance, loan). To destroy or kill (in action context).
example_sentence: Please take out the trash before you go to bed. He took her out to dinner last night. She took out an insurance policy for her car. The dentist will take out your bad tooth tomorrow.

english_meaning: To gain control of something (such as a business, organization, or responsibility). To replace someone and start doing their job or duties. To assume authority or possession of something. To dominate or occupy a position or role previously held by someone else.
example_sentence: The company was taken over by a rival. The new manager took over the department last week. A multinational company took over the local business. She will take over as team leader after the current leader retires. Robots are taking over many jobs in factories.

english_meaning: To reprimand or criticize someone for something they have done wrong. To hold a person accountable, usually by pointing out mistakes, misbehavior, or failures, often in a serious or formal way. It implies correction or disapproval rather than casual advice.
example_sentence: The manager took him to task for being late. She took her son to task for lying. The teacher took the students to task for cheating. Journalists took the minister to task over corruption.

english_meaning: To take all or most of someone's money, often unfairly. To cheat or swindle a person out of a large sum. To defeat someone completely in a game, contest, or lawsuit. To cause someone heavy financial loss.
example_sentence: The divorce settlement took him to the cleaners. Those online scammers took her to the cleaners. Our team was taken to the cleaners in the final. Be careful with that contract or they will take you to the cleaners.

english_meaning: To check a person’s heartbeat by feeling the pulse, usually at the wrist or neck, to assess their health condition. To understand someone’s feelings, opinions, or mood about something. To assess public opinion or general mood. To evaluate a situation before making a decision. To understand trends in a group or community.
synonyms: ["Check heartbeat","Measure pulse","Examine pulse","Assess feelings","Gauge opinion","Understand mood","Read the situation"]
example_sentence: The doctor took the patient’s pulse to check his condition. Before launching the campaign, the team took the public’s pulse. She tried to take his pulse to see how he felt about the idea. The manager regularly takes employees’ pulse to understand workplace morale.

english_meaning: To accept and deal with something difficult without letting it worry you too much. To deal with something calmly and without letting it upset you, even if it’s difficult or unpleasant. It shows patience, acceptance, and resilience in handling challenges.
synonyms: ["Accept calmly","Deal with","Handle with patience","Endure","Face without fear"]
example_sentence: It’s going to be tough, but I’m sure you’ll take it all in your stride. She took the criticism in her stride and kept working hard (= She accepted the criticism calmly and didn’t let it discourage her.).

word: Take the bitter with the sweet
english_meaning: To accept both the good and the bad aspects of a situation. To face life's difficulties along with its joys without complaint. To endure hardships as part of enjoying pleasant times. To recognize that life includes pain as well as happiness.
synonyms: ["Accept the good and bad","Roll with the punches","Take life as it comes","Endure","Bear with fortitude"]
example_sentence: In marriage you must learn to take the bitter with the sweet. A good leader takes the bitter with the sweet. Running a business means taking the bitter with the sweet. She smiled and said she had learned to take the bitter with the sweet.

word: Take the bull by the horns
english_meaning: To face a difficult situation with courage and take direct action. Dealing with a tough problem without hesitation. It highlights bravery, confidence and a willingness to act even when the situation feels risky or uncomfortable.
example_sentence: She took the bull by the horns and confronted the issue. It’s time to take the bull by the horns. He took the bull by the horns in the meeting. Taking the bull by the horns shows leadership.

english_meaning: To accept blame, criticism, or pressure for something. To endure a difficult or hostile situation without giving in. To face the consequences of a decision on behalf of oneself or others.
synonyms: ["Accept blame","Face criticism","Bear responsibility","Withstand pressure","Endure","Take the blame","Answer for","Shoulder","Absorb","Stand firm"]
example_sentence: As the captain, he had to take the heat for the defeat. She took the heat so her team would not be blamed. Managers must be ready to take the heat when plans fail. He took the heat calmly and answered every question.

english_meaning: To behave in a morally right and dignified way, especially during conflict. To refuse to argue back even when provoked. To avoid gossip or  negative talk. To act fairly when treated unfairly. To forgive instead of seeking revenge. To maintain integrity in professional or personal matters.
synonyms: ["Act with dignity","Show integrity","Rise above","Behave honorably","Keep moral standards"]
antonyms: ["Take the low road","Seek revenge","Act unfairly","Lose self control","Behave dishonorably"]
example_sentence: Even after being insulted publicly, she decided to take the high road and stayed silent. During the argument, he took the high road and spoke politely. Instead of spreading rumors, they chose to take the high road. When his colleague blamed him unfairly, he took the high road and continued his work calmly.

english_meaning: To accept blame, criticism, or loss without complaining. To calmly accept damage, failure, criticism, or responsibility for something difficult or negative, especially instead of blaming others.
synonyms: ["Accept the blame","Bear the loss","Face the consequences","Shoulder responsibility","take the hit"]
antonyms: ["Shift the blame","Avoid responsibility","Deny fault","Pass the buck"]
example_sentence: The manager decided to take the knock for the team’s failure. Small businesses took the knock during the economic slowdown. He took the knock and apologized instead of arguing. The company will take the knock if the project does not succeed.

english_meaning: To behave in a way that makes you appear morally better than others. To claim that your position or opinion is more ethical or justified than someone else's. To act on principle rather than on self-interest in a dispute. To adopt a superior moral attitude, sometimes in order to win an argument.
synonyms: ["Claim moral superiority","Act righteously","Stand on principle","Moralise","Take a principled stand","Preach"]
antonyms: ["Stoop low","Act unethically","Compromise principles","Behave dishonourably","Sink to their level"]
example_sentence: The minister tried to take the moral high ground during the debate. It is easy to take the moral high ground when you are not affected. She took the moral high ground and refused the bribe. Both parties took the moral high ground and blamed each other.

english_meaning: To take control or leadership of something. To assume authority or responsibility. To become the person in charge. To start managing a group or task. To take over from another leader.
example_sentence: After his father retired, he took the reins of the business. She took the reins of the team when the captain was injured. The new president will take the reins next month. He is ready to take the reins of leadership.

english_meaning: To begin to like someone or something. To start doing something as a habit. To go to a place for safety or escape. To adopt a new practice or way of life.
synonyms: ["Like","Grow fond of","Adopt","Begin","Resort to","Turn to","Take up","Warm to"]
example_sentence: The children took to their new teacher at once. After his retirement he took to gardening. The villagers took to the hills when the flood came. She has taken to walking every morning before work.

english_meaning: To run away quickly, especially to escape danger. To flee in a hurry. To escape by running rather than facing a situation.
example_sentence: The thief took to his heels when the alarm rang. Seeing the police, the boys took to their heels. He took to his heels and disappeared into the crowd. The dog barked and the stranger took to his heels.

english_meaning: To criticise or scold someone for a fault. To call a person to account for wrongdoing. To reprimand firmly for careless or improper behaviour.
example_sentence: The manager took him to task for arriving late. She was taken to task for the errors in the report. Parents should take their children to task politely. The editor took the writer to task over false figures.

english_meaning: To start doing a new activity, hobby, or job. To occupy space or time. To accept or deal with a matter or challenge. To continue something after a break.
example_sentence: He took up painting during the summer vacation. This project will take up a lot of your time. The committee will take up the issue in the next meeting. Let’s take up where we left off yesterday.

word: Take with a grain or pinch of salt
english_meaning: To accept a statement with doubt or reserve. To believe something only partly, allowing for exaggeration. To treat information cautiously rather than as full truth.
antonyms: ["Believe fully","Trust completely","Accept","Rely on","Take at face value"]
example_sentence: Take his account of the accident with a grain of salt. Online reviews should be taken with a pinch of salt. I take her promises with a grain of salt now. Take those figures with a pinch of salt until they are checked.

english_meaning: A natural ability or aptitude to do something well. A special skill or capability that a person is born with or develops. A person who possesses such a natural ability. A group of people with notable skills, especially in entertainment or sports.
example_sentence: She has a remarkable talent for playing the piano. The company is always searching for young talent. His talent as a writer was recognized at an early age. The football team is full of local talent. Not everyone is born with the same talent for mathematics.

english_meaning: Having a natural ability or aptitude for something. Showing great skill or cleverness in a particular field. Gifted with special abilities. Possessing remarkable talent that stands out from others.
example_sentence: She is a talented singer with a beautiful voice. Our school has many talented students in science. He is one of the most talented players in the team. The talented young artist won the national prize. Only truly talented writers can express such deep emotions.

english_meaning: An object believed to bring good luck or protect from harm. An object, often small, that people believe has magical powers to protect them from danger, evil, or illness, or to bring good fortune, success, or strength.
example_sentence: She always wore a small talisman around her neck for protection. The old ring was considered a talisman that brought good luck. He kept a coin as a talisman during difficult times. For many athletes, a lucky charm acts like a talisman before a game.

english_meaning: To speak or communicate with someone using words. To have a conversation or discussion. To give a formal speech or lecture. To discuss a particular subject. A conversation or discussion between two or more people. A formal address or lecture given to an audience. Rumor or gossip that spreads among people.
example_sentence: We need to talk about your future plans. She likes to talk to her friends on the phone every evening. The professor gave an interesting talk on climate change. Let us sit and talk this matter over calmly. There is a lot of talk about the new government policy.

english_meaning: To refer to something in conversation. To express opinions or thoughts on a topic. To explain or describe something verbally
example_sentence: We talked about the new project in the meeting. She is talking about her childhood memories. They talked about the weather during lunch. Let’s talk about your future plans.

english_meaning: To avoid speaking about the main point directly. To discuss a topic in an indirect or unclear way. To persuade someone by discussing other related points instead of the main issue.
synonyms: ["Evade","Beat around the bush","Dodge the issue","Speak indirectly","Circumvent"]
antonyms: ["Be direct","Address clearly","Speak plainly","Confront the issue","State openly"]
example_sentence: He kept talking around the issue instead of giving a clear answer. Stop talking around the problem and tell me what really happened. The manager talked around the complaint without addressing it directly. She tried to talk around the decision to avoid an argument.

english_meaning: To respond to someone, especially an authority figure, in a rude, disrespectful, or impolite manner. It often shows lack of respect or discipline.
example_sentence: The teacher warned the student not to talk back in class. Children should not talk back to their parents. He got punished for talking back to his boss. It is rude to talk back when someone is giving instructions.

english_meaning: To talk to someone as if they are inferior or not intelligent. To persuade someone not to do something dangerous or emotional. To guide an aircraft to land using radio communication. To speak to someone in a way that shows you think they are less intelligent or less important, or to calm someone and stop them from doing something harmful.
example_sentence: Don’t talk down to me, I understand the situation clearly. She always talks down to her colleagues, which makes them uncomfortable. The negotiator talked him down from jumping off the bridge. Air traffic control talked the pilot down safely during the storm.

english_meaning: To speak in a condescending, patronizing, or superior manner, making the listener feel inferior or less capable. To speak in an overly simple way assuming the listener cannot understand. To dominate a conversation with superiority.
example_sentence: The teacher should not talk down to students, even if they are beginners. She felt upset when her manager talked down to her in the meeting. He often talks down to people who don’t share his knowledge. Don’t talk down to me, I understand the situation clearly.

english_meaning: To speak repetitively, indirectly, or confusingly without reaching a clear point or conclusion. To avoid giving a direct answer by repeatedly returning to the same ideas.
example_sentence: The politician kept talking in circles instead of answering the question. We spent an hour talking in circles and made no decision. Stop talking in circles and tell me what happened. The discussion went nowhere because everyone talked in circles.

english_meaning: To convince someone to accept a plan or idea. To persuade someone emotionally or logically. To influence someone’s decision through conversation. To bring someone around to your point of view.
example_sentence: I tried to talk him into joining the trip. She talked her parents into letting her study abroad. They talked me into buying a new phone. He was talked into signing the agreement.

english_meaning: Said when a person being talked about appears unexpectedly. Someone you were just talking about arrives or is mentioned, implying coincidence between talking about them and their appearance. It often carries a lighthearted tone.
example_sentence: Talk of the devil! We were just discussing your promotion, and here you are. I was talking about Sarah, and talk of the devil, she walked into the room. Talk of the devil, I mentioned John, and he called me right after. We were just complaining about the weather, and talk of the devil, it started raining.

english_meaning: A person or subject that everyone is currently discussing or interested in. To be the focus of intense local gossip or public attention. A trending topic or event that has captured the collective imagination of a community. Something that is frequently mentioned or debated by a large group of people.
example_sentence: The new luxury restaurant has become the talk of the town since its grand opening last week. Her unexpected decision to resign so suddenly was the talk of the town for several months. That innovative architectural design is truly the talk of the town among local artists. After winning the national championship, the young athlete became the talk of the town.

english_meaning: To discuss something thoroughly in order to solve a problem or disagreement. To express all feelings or thoughts about something. To persuade someone not to do something.
example_sentence: They talked out their misunderstanding and became friends again. She needed someone to talk out her feelings after the argument. I tried to talk him out of quitting his job. The team talked out the problem before making a final decision.

english_meaning: To prevent someone from doing something by persuasion. To discourage someone through conversation. To convince someone to change their decision. To dissuade someone from an action or plan.
example_sentence: I tried to talk him out of quitting his job. She talked her friend out of buying an expensive phone. His parents talked him out of going abroad alone. We managed to talk her out of making a quick decision.

english_meaning: To discuss before making a decision. To consult someone about a matter. To negotiate or exchange views. To explain something by discussion
example_sentence: We should talk over the plan before starting the project. They talked over the issue with their manager. Let’s talk over the details of the contract tomorrow. The family talked over where to go for vacation.

english_meaning: To talk to someone for a very long time, often tiring or boring them. To speak at excessive length without letting the other person contribute.
example_sentence: My neighbour talked my ear off about his garden. She will talk your ear off if you let her start. He talked the poor clerk's ear off over one form. Be ready; that driver talks everyone's ear off.

english_meaning: To speak confidently, proudly, or boastfully, often about oneself or one’s achievements. It can have both positive and negative meanings depending on context:
example_sentence: He always talks tall about his achievements at work. Don’t talk tall unless you can prove what you say. She talked tall about helping the poor, but never did anything herself. He may talk tall, but his actions don’t match his words.

english_meaning: To explain something carefully step by step. To discuss a problem in detail. To guide someone through a process verbally. To review something by discussing it fully
synonyms: ["Explain in detail","Walk through","Discuss thoroughly","Go over","Break down","Clarify"]
example_sentence: The teacher talked through the math problem step by step. We talked through the plan before starting the project. She talked me through the application process. Let’s talk through the issue before making a decision.

english_meaning: To speak with someone or communicate verbally with someone. To communicate with someone by speaking. It can also mean to address someone about a matter, to give advice, or sometimes to express concern, warning, or instruction.
example_sentence: I need to talk to you about your homework. She wants to talk to her teacher after class. The manager will talk to the staff about the new rules. Can I talk to you for a few minutes?.

english_meaning: To praise someone or something, often in a way that makes them seem better or more important than they really are. To speak positively about someone or something in order to promote, support, or increase interest in it. It is often used in marketing, politics, or personal recommendations where someone highlights strengths to create a better impression.
example_sentence: The manager talked up the new project to attract investors. He always talks up his achievements in front of others. The company is talking up its latest product before the launch. She talked up the city, saying it is the best place to live.

english_meaning: To have a conversation with someone where both people exchange ideas, thoughts, or information. Engaging in a two-way conversation where both participants speak and listen. It emphasizes interaction rather than one-sided speaking.
antonyms: ["Ignore","Avoid conversation with","Stay silent toward","Refuse to speak with"]
example_sentence: I will talk with my teacher about my exam results. She likes to talk with her friends every evening. He talked with the manager about the project delay. We need to talk with the team before making a decision.

english_meaning: Fond of talking a great deal. Inclined to speak more than is necessary. Chatty and communicative by nature.
example_sentence: He becomes very talkative after a cup of tea. The talkative passenger kept everyone entertained. She is shy at first but soon grows talkative. A talkative child can be tiring at bedtime.

english_meaning: A feature that allows a person (like a director or producer) to speak directly to presenters through headphones or a communication system. Return communication, feedback system, or an audio reply channel.
example_sentence: The director used the talkback system to guide the anchor during the live show. The studio engineer checked the talkback communication before recording started. The talkback system failed, so the team had difficulty communicating on air. The talkback facility helps the control room guide reporters in real time.

english_meaning: To speak in a way that goes round and round without making a clear or direct point. To discuss something endlessly without reaching any conclusion or resolution. To use words that avoid the central issue while appearing to address it.
synonyms: ["Ramble","Beat around the bush","Waffle","Go around in circles","Evade"]
example_sentence: He was accused of talking in circles during the negotiation rather than stating his position clearly. After an hour of talking in circles, the committee had still not agreed on a single point. She grew frustrated with his tendency to talk in circles whenever a direct answer was required. The politician was skilled at talking in circles in a way that sounded impressive but said very little. Stop talking in circles and tell me exactly what it is that you want.

english_meaning: A tall drink of water refers to a person who is notably tall and often quite slender or lanky. It is commonly used as a colloquial phrase to describe an exceptionally tall individual in a somewhat admiring or humorous way. It can also refer to a visually appealing, attractive, and tall person who is refreshing to look at. It describes someone whose physical height stands out prominently in a group. It historically implies someone who brings a sense of refreshing satisfaction, much like a cool drink.
example_sentence: Her new boyfriend is a tall drink of water who towers over everyone else in the room. The basketball coach recruited a tall drink of water to play center for the upcoming season. He walked into the diner looking like a tall drink of water in his cowboy boots and hat. I didn't expect my blind date to be such a tall drink of water, but I was pleasantly surprised.

english_meaning: An unusually exaggerated story or highly improbable account. A narrative that features unbelievable elements, related as if it were true and factual. A boastful or deceitful story often meant to entertain rather than deceive. An anecdote that stretches the truth beyond reasonable limits.
example_sentence: He told us a tall tale about catching a fish the size of a boat. No one believed his tall tale regarding how he lost his homework. The old sailor was famous for spinning a tall tale whenever anyone would listen. That sounds like a tall tale, but I am willing to hear you out.

english_meaning: A record or count of a number of items, points, or scores. A mark used in counting, usually a stroke in groups of five. To count or calculate a total. To match or correspond with something else exactly.
example_sentence: He kept a tally of the runs scored in the match. Please tally the votes and announce the result. Her account of the incident does not tally with his. The final tally showed a clear victory for the team.

english_meaning: A brown pod-like fruit with sour sticky pulp used as a flavouring. A tropical fruit widely used in chutneys, curries, and drinks. The tall tree that produces these pods. The sour paste made from the pulp of this fruit.
example_sentence: Tamarind gives the chutney its sharp, sour taste. Children love to eat raw tamarind with salt. The tamarind tree provides wide, cool shade. She soaked the tamarind in warm water before cooking.

english_meaning: To train, domesticate, or subdue an animal, emotion, or situation. Occasionally, it refers metaphorically to something made less intense or more manageable. Something that is not wild, is gentle, or easily controlled. The act of taming, something that is tamed
example_sentence: Farmers tame wild horses for riding. She tamed her fear before the presentation. The tame cat slept on the sofa. His tame reaction surprised everyone. The lion’s tame is the result of years of training. His patience in taming the horse impressed everyone.
