english_meaning: To interfere with something secretly or improperly, often causing damage or change. To meddle or handle something without permission. To alter, damage, or interfere something in a harmful or dishonest way.
example_sentence: Someone tampered with the documents to hide the truth. Never tamper with electrical wires; it’s dangerous. The evidence was tampered with before the trial. He was caught tampering with the car’s engine.

english_meaning: Interfered with something in order to cause damage or make unauthorized changes. Meddled with something without permission, often in a harmful way. Altered or modified something illegally or improperly, especially to deceive.
example_sentence: Someone had tampered with the lock on the door. The evidence was found to have been tampered with before the trial. He was accused of having tampered with the official records. The seal on the bottle showed that it had been tampered with. Investigators believed the brakes had been tampered with deliberately.

english_meaning: Packing down a material tightly by repeated light blows. Pressing or ramming something firmly into place. Compacting loose material such as soil, tobacco, or explosives into a small space.
example_sentence: The worker was tamping the soil around the newly planted tree. Tamping the tobacco into the pipe is an art in itself. He continued tamping the gravel until the surface was level. The engineer explained the tamping process used in railway tracks. She was carefully tamping the coffee grounds before brewing.

english_meaning: A strong, sharp, or pungent taste or smell. It often refers to the sharp flavor associated with citrus or fermented foods. It can also figuratively mean a trace or touch of something specific.
example_sentence: The salad dressing had a delightful citrus tang that refreshed the palate. There was a salty tang in the air as we approached the ocean. The metal had a strange copper tang when I touched it with my tongue. His voice had a slight tang of an accent that I couldn't place.

english_meaning: A straight line that touches a curve at a single point without crossing it. A completely different line of thought or action. The trigonometric function equal to the ratio of opposite to adjacent sides. Touching but not intersecting.
example_sentence: Draw a tangent to the circle at point P. The professor went off on a tangent during the lecture. Calculate the tangent of 45 degrees. The two circles are tangent to each other.

english_meaning: Two or more circles that touch each other at exactly one point without crossing. Circles that have a single common point of contact. Circles that are externally or internally tangent to each other.
synonyms: ["Touching circles","Kissing circles","Osculating circles","Circles with single contact point"]
example_sentence: Two tangent circles share only one point. The gears are designed as tangent circles. Tangent circles do not overlap or intersect. The diagram shows externally tangent circles.

english_meaning: Relating to or along a tangent. Touching a curve or surface at a single point without crossing it. Only slightly connected or related to the main subject. Diverging from a main point or course.
example_sentence: The line is tangential to the circle at point A. His remarks were tangential to the main discussion. The professor made a tangential comment about history. The tangential velocity increases with distance from the center.

english_meaning: A quadrilateral whose four sides are all tangent to one inscribed circle. A four-sided figure that circumscribes a circle. A quadrilateral in which the sums of the two pairs of opposite sides are equal. Also known as a circumscribed or tangent quadrilateral.
example_sentence: In a tangential quadrilateral the sums of opposite sides are equal. A rhombus is always a tangential quadrilateral. The circle inside a tangential quadrilateral is called the incircle. He constructed a tangential quadrilateral around a given circle.

english_meaning: A small citrus fruit with loose orange skin that peels easily and sweet segments. A type of mandarin orange eaten fresh. The tree that produces this fruit. A bright reddish-orange colour.
example_sentence: Tangerines are easy to peel and share. He packed a few tangerines for the children. The tangerine segments were juicy and sweet. She wore a bright tangerine scarf.

english_meaning: Something that can be touched or clearly understood. Able to be physically touched. Real and concrete, not imaginary. Clear and definite, easy to notice or understand. Producing a noticeable result or effect.
example_sentence: We cannot accept his findings without tangible evidence. The tension between them was almost tangible. Drivers will see tangible improvements on major roadways. We need tangible evidence if we're going to take legal action. A firm belief in the existence of the soul, even though it is not at all tangible.

english_meaning: A confused mass of threads, hair, or branches that are intertwined. To become twisted together in a confused or complicated way. It can also refer to getting involved in a complicated or difficult situation.
example_sentence: The kitten managed to tangle the entire ball of yarn in minutes. My hair gets into a terrible tangle if I walk in the wind. Don't tangle with that group if you want to stay out of trouble. The fishing line was such a tangle that I had to cut it.

english_meaning: Something that is twisted together in an untidy or complicated way. It is often used to describe hair, wires, or complicated emotional situations. It implies a state of being snarled or knotted.
example_sentence: She spent an hour trying to comb through her tangled hair. The back of the television was a mess of tangled cables and wires. They became trapped in a tangled web of lies and deceit. The hikers struggled to move through the tangled thicket of vines.

english_meaning: A passionate ballroom dance of Latin American origin. The music composed for or associated with this dance. To dance the tango. To engage in intricate or difficult interaction with another. Used figuratively to describe cooperation or conflict requiring two people.
example_sentence: They learned to tango during their trip to Argentina. The couple performed a beautiful tango at the show. It takes two to tango, so both parties are responsible. Politicians often tango with the media.

english_meaning: Having a sharp, pungent, or refreshing taste. It usually refers to flavors that are pleasantly acidic or tart, like lemon or vinegar. It can also describe a smell that is sharp and stimulating.
example_sentence: The yogurt has a tangy flavor that goes well with sweet honey. We enjoyed a tangy lemon tart after the heavy dinner. The air was filled with the tangy scent of pine needles. I love using tangy barbecue sauce on grilled chicken.

english_meaning: To torment or tease someone with the sight or promise of something that is unobtainable. It involves exciting someone's desire or curiosity while keeping the desired object just out of reach.
example_sentence: The delicious smell of baking bread began to tantalise the hungry travelers. She used her secret knowledge to tantalise him during the negotiation. The prospect of a promotion continued to tantalise the ambitious employee. The lush oasis seemed to tantalise the thirsty nomads from a distance.

english_meaning: An alternative spelling of tantalise, referring to the act of teasing by showing something desirable but remaining out of reach. It originates from the Greek mythological figure Tantalus.
example_sentence: The bright colors of the fruit tantalize the visitors at the market. Advertisements often tantalize consumers with products they cannot afford. He would tantalize his cat by waving a laser pointer on the floor. The mystery of the locked room served to tantalize the young detective.

english_meaning: Equivalent in seriousness to or virtually the same as something else. It is used to describe something that has the same effect or value as another often negative thing.
example_sentence: Her silence was considered tantamount to an admission of guilt. For many people, losing their job is tantamount to a personal disaster. The government's new policy is tantamount to a complete reversal of their promise. Refusing to help in such a crisis is tantamount to betrayal.

english_meaning: An uncontrolled outburst of anger and frustration, typically in a young child. It can also refer to a display of bad temper by an adult.
example_sentence: The toddler threw a massive tantrum in the middle of the toy store. He is known for his workplace tantrums whenever things go wrong. She struggled to keep her composure while her son had a tantrum. A sudden tantrum from the player resulted in a technical foul.

english_meaning: To strike or touch something lightly and quickly, once or repeatedly. To touch a screen or control briefly to select or activate it. To draw liquid from a container or resource from a supply. To make use of a source of information, talent, money, or energy. To connect secretly to a telephone or communication line to monitor it. To choose or appoint someone for a role. A light blow or touch. A faucet or valve controlling liquid or gas. A device or connection used to draw from a supply. A secretly monitored telephone connection. A tool for cutting an internal screw thread.
example_sentence: She tapped gently on the door before entering. Turn off the tap so the sink does not overflow. The charity hopes to tap local expertise for the project. Police obtained a warrant to tap the suspect's phone.

english_meaning: To tap different places on a surface or device while searching or experimenting. To explore an interface or area casually through repeated touches.
example_sentence: He tapped around the app looking for the settings menu. She tapped around the wall to locate a hollow space. The child tapped around the tablet screen out of curiosity. I tapped around the interface until I found the right button.

english_meaning: To continue tapping, typing, or striking lightly and repeatedly, often for some time. To keep working at a keyboard or device with repeated touches.
example_sentence: He sat in the corner, tapping away at his laptop for hours. She tapped away on her phone, replying to messages one by one. The writer tapped away at the keyboard late into the night. Rain tapped away steadily on the windowpane.

english_meaning: To tap something in return or send it back with a light touch. To reply quickly by tapping or typing on a device. In some contexts, to reconnect with or draw again on a previous contact or resource.
example_sentence: The midfielder tapped the ball back to the goalkeeper. She tapped back a quick reply as soon as she saw the message. He tapped back on the wall after hearing a faint knock. We tapped back into our former supplier when stock ran low.

english_meaning: To connect to a supply, system, or network and draw from it. To gain access to and make use of a source of information, money, talent, energy, demand, or emotion.
example_sentence: The speaker knew how to tap into the audience's emotions. Engineers found a way to tap into the underground water supply. The startup wants to tap into growing demand for electric vehicles. She tapped into her creativity to solve the design problem.

english_meaning: To draw, drain, or divert part of a liquid, electric current, signal, or other supply from its main source. To touch a travel card or device when leaving a transport system to record the end of a journey.
example_sentence: Engineers tapped off some power from the main line to run the sensors. The brewer tapped off a small sample from the barrel. Remember to tap off when you leave the tram. The technician tapped off a signal to monitor the circuit.

english_meaning: To touch or strike a surface lightly, often to attract attention. To press an icon, link, button, or area of a touchscreen briefly. In some transit systems, to touch a card or device to a reader when beginning a journey.
example_sentence: Tap on the icon to open the application. She tapped on the window to get her friend's attention. Tap on at the station before boarding the train. He tapped on the table impatiently while waiting.

english_meaning: To signal surrender, especially in combat sports, by tapping an opponent or the floor. To quit or withdraw because of exhaustion, defeat, or inability to continue. To use up or exhaust money, energy, or another resource. To type or beat out words, a rhythm, or a signal by tapping.
example_sentence: The fighter tapped out when the hold became too painful. After ten miles, I was exhausted and had to tap out. The emergency repairs tapped out our savings. She tapped out a quick reply on her phone.

english_meaning: To move through screens, images, options, or steps by tapping repeatedly on a device. To browse or navigate a digital sequence with successive touches.
example_sentence: He tapped through the photo gallery to find the right image. She tapped through several menus before finding the settings. The user quickly tapped through the tutorial screens. I tapped through the slideshow to review every image.

english_meaning: A four-sided plane figure with one pair of parallel sides. A quadrilateral whose two opposite sides are parallel. A shape with four sides and four angles, in which the parallel sides are called bases. A quadrilateral in which the non-parallel sides are called legs. A trapezoid in American English. In anatomy, the trapezium is one of the eight small bones in the wrist. The anatomical trapezium is located at the base of the thumb and connects with the first metacarpal bone. In astronomy, the Trapezium is a group of stars in the Orion Nebula.
example_sentence: A trapezium has four sides and four angles. The teacher asked the students to calculate the area of the trapezium. The two parallel sides of the trapezium are called its bases. The trapezium is an important shape in elementary geometry.

english_meaning: A petty or trivial lie. A silly, unimportant falsehood. A small fib or pretentious nonsense. A trifling exaggeration told for fun.
example_sentence: He told a taradiddle about meeting a famous actor. Her excuse was nothing but a taradiddle. The child made up a taradiddle to avoid trouble. Nobody believed his little taradiddle.

english_meaning: Late in arriving, happening, or being done. Slow to act or respond. Delayed beyond the expected time. Sluggish or moving without haste.
example_sentence: The teacher marked him tardy for arriving after the bell. She apologized for her tardy response to the email. His tardy arrival delayed the entire meeting. The company was fined for the tardy delivery of goods. Students who are frequently tardy will lose participation marks.

english_meaning: To make the surface of a metal dull or discolored through oxidation or chemical reaction. To damage someone’s reputation. A dullness, stain, or loss of luster; damage to reputation or quality.
example_sentence: The mirrors had tarnished with age. The silver candlesticks were tarnished and dusty. He hopes to improve the newspaper's somewhat tarnished public image. Rumors can tarnish a person’s reputation. There was a tarnish on the old silver tray. The scandal left a tarnish on his career.

english_meaning: Small mountain lakes or pools, usually formed by glacial action in a hollow on a mountainside. Bodies of still water found high in the mountains, often surrounded by rocks. Plural of 'tarn'.
example_sentence: The hikers stopped to rest beside one of the peaceful tarns. Several tarns lie hidden among the rocky peaks of the region. The photographer captured the reflections in the mountain tarns at sunrise. Cold, clear water filled the tarns high above the valley. In summer, wildflowers bloom around the small tarns.

english_meaning: A starchy root vegetable with brown fibrous skin and white or purple flesh. A tropical tuber that must be cooked before eating. The broad-leaved plant that produces this root. A staple food in many island and Asian cuisines.
example_sentence: Taro must always be cooked thoroughly. She boiled taro and mashed it with salt. Taro leaves are also used in cooking. Taro chips are sold in many local shops.

english_meaning: A starchy underground root vegetable with brown rough skin and white flesh. A tropical plant whose roots and leaves are both edible. A root commonly used in curries, soups, and fried dishes. A vegetable known for its slightly sweet and nutty flavor. A staple food in many parts of Asia, Africa, and the Pacific.
example_sentence: Taro root curry is served with rice in many Asian households. She peeled the taro root before boiling it. Taro root is often deep-fried and sprinkled with spices. My grandmother makes a delicious taro root dish every winter.

english_meaning: A petty or trivial lie. A silly, unimportant falsehood. A small fib or pretentious nonsense. A trifling exaggeration told for fun.
example_sentence: She dismissed his story as a tarradiddle. He spiced up his tale with a harmless tarradiddle. The rumor turned out to be a tarradiddle. Grandmother always knew when he told a tarradiddle.

english_meaning: The seven short bones that form the ankle and the back part of the foot. A group of bones that connect the leg bones to the long bones of the foot. Bones that absorb shock and help transfer body weight while walking. The bony structure that forms the heel and the arch of the foot.
example_sentence: The heel is formed by the largest of the tarsal bones. Landing awkwardly from a jump can fracture a tarsal bone. The tarsal bones help spread body weight across the foot. An X-ray of the tarsal bones showed no serious damage.

english_meaning: A bunch of threads or cords hanging from something for decoration. A decorative hanging ornament made of threads, cords, or strips of material, often attached to clothing, curtains, graduation caps, or furnishings to add a decorative touch.
example_sentence: The graduation cap had a gold tassel hanging from it. She added a tassel to the end of her scarf. The curtains were decorated with red tassels. He bought a bag with tassels for a stylish look.

english_meaning: The act of turning a tassel, especially during a graduation ceremony. The symbolic act during a graduation ceremony when students move the tassel on their cap from one side to the other, showing they have completed their studies. Twisting or rotating a decorative tassel on clothing or objects.
antonyms: ["Beginning of study (admission)","Starting line (rather than finishing)","Status before graduation (student status)"]
example_sentence: After four years of study, she finally experienced the tassel turn at her graduation ceremony. With the tassel turn, he felt proud, his student days were over, and a new chapter in his life had begun. They all cheered as the class performed the tassel turn together. The tassel turn at the end of college felt like closing one door and opening another.

english_meaning: To report a person's minor wrongdoing to someone in authority. To engage in idle chatter or gossip. Information or news shared through gossip. The act of telling on someone. To reveal secrets or private matters. To talk idly or incessantly.
example_sentence: The little boy decided to tattle on his sister for breaking the vase. She promised not to tattle to the teacher about the missing homework. The neighbors spend their afternoons engaged in harmless tattle over tea. He is known to tattle about everyone's private business to the boss.

english_meaning: A remark made in order to anger, wound, or provoke someone. To provoke or challenge someone with insulting remarks.
example_sentence: The school bullies would often taunt the younger students during recess. He tried to ignore the cruel taunt from his opponent. The fans began to taunt the visiting team after the final whistle. It is never wise to taunt a wild animal behind a fence.

english_meaning: A dark greyish brown colour. A neutral shade between grey and brown, often used in fashion and interiors. Of or having this muted brownish grey colour.
example_sentence: She chose taupe paint for the hallway. The sofa was upholstered in a soft taupe fabric. Taupe shoes go well with almost any outfit. The room's taupe walls created a calm atmosphere.

english_meaning: Stretched or pulled tight, not slack. Showing tension, strain, or anxiety. Kept in good order and under firm control. Written or expressed concisely with no wasted words.
example_sentence: Make sure the rope is taut before you climb. His face was taut with worry as he waited for the news. The captain runs a taut ship and expects discipline. The novel has a taut plot that never loses pace.

english_meaning: A place where alcoholic drinks are sold and people can sit and drink. An inn or public house that may also provide food or lodging. A small traditional bar or drinking house. A social meeting place where travelers or local people gather.
example_sentence: The travelers stopped at a tavern before nightfall. The old tavern served hot food to weary guests. Local musicians played every Friday at the village tavern. He heard the news while sitting in a crowded tavern.

english_meaning: Of a warm sandy or orange-brown colour. Having the golden brown shade seen in lions, autumn grass, or certain owls. A light brown colour with a yellowish tinge.
example_sentence: The lion's tawny coat blended with the dry grass. She had tawny eyes that caught the light. A tawny owl called from the woods at dusk. The fields turned tawny in late summer.

english_meaning: Relating to the scientific classification of living things. Concerned with arranging items into ordered groups or categories. Based on or following a system of classification. Describing the methods and rules used in taxonomy.
example_sentence: The museum follows a strict taxonomic order in its displays. Taxonomic studies help scientists understand evolution. There is a taxonomic difference between these two plants. The paper proposed a new taxonomic arrangement for the group.

english_meaning: A scientist who specialises in classifying and naming living organisms. An expert in the theory and practice of classification. A person who identifies and describes new species. Someone who organises information into structured categories.
example_sentence: The taxonomist identified a new species of beetle. She works as a plant taxonomist at the university. A taxonomist must study anatomy in great detail. The museum employed a taxonomist to review its collection.

english_meaning: The branch of science concerned with classifying living organisms into groups. The practice and principles of arranging things into ordered categories. A particular scheme or system of classification. In information science, a structured set of labels used to organise content.
example_sentence: Modern taxonomy places humans in the family Hominidae. The team developed a taxonomy for organising research papers. Taxonomy helps scientists identify and name new species. The website uses a simple taxonomy of categories and tags.

english_meaning: A group of players forming one side in a competitive game or sport. Two or more people working together to achieve a common goal. A group of animals harnessed together to draw a vehicle. To come together as a group in order to accomplish a task. To match or coordinate two things together.
example_sentence: The national team won the championship after a very difficult match. Our research team has finally published its latest scientific findings. They decided to team up to finish the project ahead of schedule. The farmer used a strong team of horses to pull the heavy plow.

english_meaning: A fellow member of a team, especially in sports or a work group. A person who plays or works together with others on the same side. Someone who shares a common goal with others as part of a group.
example_sentence: He passed the ball quickly to his teammate. My teammates always support me during difficult matches. She thanked her teammates after winning the championship. A good teammate encourages others and celebrates their success. He is not just my colleague but a true teammate at work.

english_meaning: Working together as a team helps achieve goals successfully. Collaboration and cooperation among team members lead to the successful realization of shared goals or dreams. Individual effort alone may not achieve the same results.
synonyms: ["Collaboration leads to success","United effort achieves goals","Many hands make light work","Working together brings results"]
antonyms: ["Individual effort alone fails","Lone work struggles to succeed","Working in isolation prevents success","Disunity blocks goals"]
example_sentence: Our project succeeded because teamwork makes the dream work. The football team won the championship; it proves that teamwork makes the dream work. In any office, teamwork makes the dream work when deadlines are tight. Building a community garden was possible because teamwork makes the dream work.

english_meaning: To pull something into pieces or to strongly criticize. To separate something by force into many pieces or to destroy something emotionally or mentally through harsh criticism or conflict
example_sentence: The dog tore apart the cushion in a few minutes. The critics tore apart the movie for its weak story. War can tear apart families and communities. She felt torn apart by guilt and regret.

english_meaning: To destroy or remove something. To pull something apart or demolish it physically such as a building. It is also used figuratively to mean criticizing someone harshly, weakening their confidence, or dismantling ideas, systems, or reputations.
example_sentence: The old school building was torn down to make space for a new hospital. The article tore down the government’s policies with strong arguments. They plan to tear down the wall separating the two rooms. Constant criticism can tear down a person’s confidence.

english_meaning: To remove something quickly by pulling. To pull something away from a surface or whole with force. It can also mean to leave suddenly or to produce something rapidly such as copies from a machine.
example_sentence: He tore off the old poster from the wall. Please tear off this page and submit it. She tore off a piece of paper to write a note. The car tore off down the street after the signal turned green.

english_meaning: To tear something into pieces, to destroy a document, or to become emotional so that tears come into the eyes. It can also mean to suddenly move very fast, especially a vehicle.
example_sentence: He tore up the old contract after signing the new one. She teared up when she heard the sad news. The driver tore up the road to reach the hospital quickly. I watched him tear up the letter and throw it away.

english_meaning: To make fun of someone playfully or unkindly. To provoke or annoy someone in a light-hearted or malicious way. To gently pull apart fibers or hair to make them fluffy. A person who playfully mocks others. An act of teasing.
example_sentence: The children love to tease their little brother about his new haircut. He was just teasing you; don't take it seriously. Please stop teasing the cat before it scratches you. She used a comb to tease her hair into a fuller shape. He is such a tease at family gatherings.

english_meaning: A small spoon used for stirring tea, coffee, and other drinks. A unit of measurement in cooking equal to about five milliliters. The amount that such a spoon can hold. A standard small measure used in recipes and for giving liquid medicine.
example_sentence: Add one teaspoon of salt to the boiling water. He stirred his tea with a silver teaspoon. The doctor told her to take a teaspoon of syrup twice a day. Mix half a teaspoon of baking powder into the flour.

english_meaning: A particular way of carrying out a task, especially skillfully. A method of performance in an art, sport, or science. Skill or ability developed through practice. A systematic procedure for accomplishing something. The manner in which a person handles technical details.
example_sentence: She has mastered the technique of oil painting. The coach taught them a new technique. His writing technique is very refined. Modern surgical techniques save many lives.

english_meaning: A system of government or management in which decisions are made by technical experts rather than elected politicians. Rule by scientists, engineers, or specialists in a particular field. A society controlled by people with technical or scientific knowledge. The body of technical experts who hold such power.
example_sentence: Critics argued that the reforms were pushing the country towards a technocracy. In a technocracy, policy is shaped by data rather than public opinion. The new cabinet was described as a technocracy of economists and engineers. Supporters of technocracy believe expertise produces better decisions.

english_meaning: A technical expert who exercises power or influence within a government or hierarchy. An official who is a trained expert in a particular field, such as economics or science. A member of a technically skilled elite. A person who advocates for or practices governance based on scientific and technical knowledge. A managerial professional who prioritizes technical efficiency over political or social considerations.
example_sentence: The government appointed a technocrat to manage the national central bank during the economic crisis. Many voters prefer a seasoned politician over a cold, calculating technocrat. As a leading technocrat in the energy sector, she redesigned the entire power grid. The transition to a digital economy requires a cabinet filled with technocrats rather than just career diplomats.

english_meaning: Relating to government or management by technical experts. Based on scientific or specialised knowledge rather than political ideology. Characterised by a cool, data-driven approach to decision-making. Belonging to or typical of a technocracy.
example_sentence: The minister took a technocratic approach to solving the energy crisis. His speech was technocratic and full of statistics. A technocratic government was appointed to stabilise the economy. Voters often find technocratic language cold and difficult to follow.

english_meaning: Relating to or involving technology, especially new and advanced methods or machines. Resulting from developments in science and engineering. Concerned with the practical use of scientific knowledge.
example_sentence: Technological progress has transformed the health sector. The company invested heavily in technological research. Technological change often creates new kinds of jobs. Farmers are benefiting from technological improvements in irrigation.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to technology or the use of technology. From the point of view of technology or technical development. By means of scientific and technical methods or equipment.
example_sentence: The country is technologically far ahead of its neighbours. This hospital is technologically well equipped. Technologically, the new model is a huge improvement. Rural areas remain technologically underdeveloped.

english_meaning: A person who is an expert in a particular branch of technology. A trained specialist who applies scientific and technical knowledge in a practical field. A skilled worker who operates and maintains technical or laboratory equipment, especially in medicine or industry.
example_sentence: The hospital hired a new laboratory technologist last month. A skilled technologist checked the machine before the test began. She works as a radiology technologist at the city clinic. The technologist explained how the new system would save time.

english_meaning: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry. Machinery, tools, and systems developed from scientific knowledge. The branch of knowledge that deals with engineering and applied sciences. The particular methods and equipment used in a specific field of work.
example_sentence: Modern technology has changed the way we communicate. The factory invested in new technology to increase production. Medical technology has saved countless lives in recent years. Many older people struggle to keep up with new technology.

english_meaning: A person who loves and enthusiastically uses new technology. Someone strongly attracted to modern gadgets and digital devices. An admirer of technological progress and innovation.
example_sentence: As a technophile, he buys every new phone that appears. Technophiles were excited by the company's latest launch. My brother is a complete technophile. The magazine is written mainly for technophiles.

english_meaning: A person who fears, dislikes, or avoids modern technology. Someone uncomfortable with computers and digital devices. A person who resists technological change.
example_sentence: My grandfather is a technophobe who refuses to use a smartphone. Technophobes often struggle with online banking. She admits to being something of a technophobe. Training sessions were arranged to help technophobes at work.

english_meaning: Too long, slow, or dull; causing boredom by being repetitive, uninteresting, or overly detailed. Lacking in excitement or variety.
example_sentence: The meeting was so tedious that several people fell asleep. Data entry is one of the most tedious tasks in the office. She found the long lecture tedious and difficult to follow. The journey was tedious but the destination was worth it.

english_meaning: In a way that is too long, slow, or dull, causing boredom or weariness. In a manner that is tiresome and lacking interest. Done in an extremely detailed and repetitive fashion.
example_sentence: He spoke tediously about his childhood for over an hour. The report explained the process tediously in every small detail. She tediously copied each name from the old register. The lecturer went through the slides tediously, one by one. The meeting dragged on tediously until late in the evening.

english_meaning: The feeling of being bored, tired, or uninterested because something is repetitive, dull, or continues for a long time. A state of boredom caused by repetitive or monotonous activities. Mental weariness resulting from lack of excitement or variety. The quality of being dull, tiresome, or uninteresting. A feeling of impatience caused by a long and tedious task. The condition of being exhausted by routine work or prolonged waiting.
example_sentence: The tedium of entering data for hours made him lose concentration. She listened to music to escape the tedium of the long journey. The workers complained about the tedium of performing the same task every day. Reading an interesting book helped him overcome the tedium of waiting at the airport.

english_meaning: To be full of or swarming with living things. To be present in large numbers. To pour down heavily, as of rain. To produce or contain something in great abundance.
example_sentence: The river teems with fish during the rainy season. The market teems with people every Sunday morning. It was teeming with rain when we left the house. The old forest teems with rare species of birds. Her mind teems with new ideas for the project.

english_meaning: Meanings that are present in great abundance. Senses of a word that are numerous and overflowing. A wealth of interpretations carried by a single expression.
example_sentence: The poem is rich with teeming meanings. Sacred texts often carry teeming meanings for scholars. His short remark had teeming meanings for the family. Students explored the teeming meanings of the metaphor.

english_meaning: Relating to a person between thirteen and nineteen years of age. Belonging to or characteristic of teenagers. Suitable for or aimed at young people in their teens. The period of life between childhood and adulthood.
example_sentence: Teenage years are often full of emotional ups and downs. The magazine focuses on teenage fashion and lifestyle. Many teenage students take part in sports activities. Parents should guide their teenage children with patience.

english_meaning: A young person aged between thirteen and nineteen years. A person in the stage of life known as adolescence. A boy or girl between childhood and adulthood.
example_sentence: As a teenager, he was very passionate about music. Most teenagers spend hours on social media every day. She was still a teenager when she published her first book. Parents should try to understand the feelings of teenagers. The program is specially designed for teenagers.

english_meaning: Extremely small, tiny, or minute in size. Informal or affectionate term used to describe something very little. Very minor or insignificant in degree or quantity.
example_sentence: She found a teeny weeny spider crawling on the windowsill. He only wanted a teeny weeny slice of the birthday cake. There was a teeny weeny mistake in the financial calculation. The baby wore a teeny weeny pair of yellow socks.

word: Teeter on the brink of something
english_meaning: To be in a situation that is very close to something bad or extreme happening. To be on the edge or verge of a critical or dangerous state. It means being unstable, uncertain, or about to experience something serious, often negative (like disaster, collapse, war, or success).
example_sentence: The company was teetering on the brink of collapse. The country is teetering on the brink of civil war. The company is teetering on the brink of bankruptcy. After months of drought, the country is teetering on the brink of famine. The two nations are teetering on the brink of war.

word: Teeter on the edge of something
english_meaning: To be in a situation where something is very likely to happen soon, often something dangerous, serious, or uncertain. It means being very close to a particular state or condition (good or bad).
example_sentence: He was teetering on the edge of madness. The country is teetering on the edge of civil war. The company is teetering on the edge of bankruptcy. The peace talks are teetering on the edge of collapse. She’s teetering on the edge of a nervous breakdown.

english_meaning: Minor difficulties that arise while a new product, system, organization, or project is being developed or introduced. Temporary early-stage faults that are expected to improve with experience and adjustment.
example_sentence: The new software had a few teething problems before it stabilized. Every startup faces teething problems in its early months. The airline quickly resolved the teething problems in its booking system. Customers were patient while the service overcame its teething problems.

english_meaning: A person who completely abstains from alcoholic drinks. Someone who chooses not to drink any alcohol at all, often for personal, religious, or health reasons.
example_sentence: John is a teetotaler and never touches wine or beer. She became a teetotaler after seeing the effects of alcoholism on her family. The company prefers hiring teetotalers for positions that require clear judgment. Even at parties, he remains a teetotaler and only drinks water.

english_meaning: A person who completely abstains from alcoholic drinks. Someone who chooses not to drink any alcohol at all, often for personal, religious, or health reasons.
example_sentence: He is a teetotaller and never touches alcohol at social events. As a teetotaller, she prefers juice or water instead of wine. Many teetotallers choose a healthy lifestyle free from alcohol. Despite peer pressure, he remained a teetotaller throughout college.

english_meaning: To reveal a secret to anyone at all. To share confidential information with another person. To let someone else know about something private. To disclose a hidden truth to another individual.
synonyms: ["Reveal a secret","Spill the beans","Disclose","Divulge","Let the cat out of the bag","Share a secret","Blab","Give away","Uncover","Make known"]
antonyms: ["Keep a secret","Keep quiet","Stay tight-lipped","Conceal","Hide","Keep under wraps","Suppress","Bite one's tongue","Withhold"]
example_sentence: I promise I will not tell a soul about your new job offer. Please do not tell a soul what happened here tonight. She did not tell a soul that she was planning to leave the country. He swore he would never tell a soul her darkest secret.

english_meaning: A prescription medicine belonging to the benzodiazepine group. A drug used mainly for the short-term treatment of insomnia. A sedative that helps a person fall asleep and stay asleep. A controlled substance that can cause dependence if misused.
example_sentence: The doctor prescribed temazepam for a few nights only. Temazepam should never be taken without medical advice. Long-term use of temazepam can lead to dependence. The patient was slowly taken off temazepam under supervision.

english_meaning: An earthquake, especially a strong one. A shaking of the ground caused by movement of the earth's crust. A word used mainly in American English for a seismic tremor. Any sudden trembling of the earth's surface.
example_sentence: A powerful temblor struck the coastal region before dawn. The temblor damaged several old buildings in the town. Residents felt a mild temblor lasting a few seconds. Scientists recorded the temblor at a depth of ten kilometres.

english_meaning: Excessive boldness or confidence that shows a lack of respect. The nerve to do or say something risky or rude. Reckless daring without proper thought for the consequences. Audacity that surprises or offends other people.
example_sentence: He had the temerity to question the judge's decision. She showed great temerity in challenging her own manager. I could not believe his temerity in asking for another loan. The young writer had the temerity to criticise a famous poet.

english_meaning: A person employed for a short period to cover extra work or absence. Short for temporary worker, especially in an office. To work in such a temporary job. Informally short for temperature.
example_sentence: The office hired a temp while the secretary was on leave. She worked as a temp for several months after graduating. He is temping at a law firm until he finds a permanent job. The nurse recorded the patient's temp every two hours.

english_meaning: A person’s natural character, mindset, or emotional nature. The usual way someone thinks, feels, and behaves. In older usage: the balance of a person’s bodily humors, believed to affect personality.
example_sentence: He has a calm temperament, even under stress. Children often show a playful temperament. His artistic temperament makes him very creative but also sensitive. A good teacher needs a patient temperament. She has a fiery temperament and speaks her mind without fear. Despite his success, his humble temperament never changed.

english_meaning: Likely to change mood suddenly and become upset or angry. Having an unpredictable and sensitive nature. Relating to a person's natural character or temperament. Working unreliably or not always as expected, used of machines.
example_sentence: The actor is famous for being temperamental on set. She has a temperamental nature and gets upset easily. Our old printer is rather temperamental in cold weather. Their temperamental differences made teamwork difficult.

english_meaning: Showing moderation and self-restraint, especially in behavior or the use of alcohol. Not extreme in any way. Relating to a climate or region that is mild, without extremes of heat or cold. Balanced and reasonable in speech or conduct.
example_sentence: Britain has a temperate climate throughout most of the year. He is a temperate man who never drinks or smokes. She gave a temperate response to the harsh criticism. Temperate regions are ideal for growing wheat and apples. A good leader must be temperate in both speech and action.

english_meaning: In a moderate and self-controlled manner. Without going to extremes in behaviour, speech, or habits. In a mild and balanced way, especially regarding climate. Calmly and with restraint.
example_sentence: He always speaks temperately, even when provoked. She eats and drinks temperately as a matter of habit. The chairman responded temperately to the harsh criticism. The region is temperately warm throughout the year.

english_meaning: The degree of heat or cold measured on a definite scale. A measure of how hot or cold a place, object, or body is. A body heat higher than normal, indicating fever. In science, a quantity showing the average energy of particles in a substance.
example_sentence: The temperature dropped sharply after sunset. Keep the medicine at room temperature. The child has a temperature and should stay in bed. Water boils at a temperature of one hundred degrees Celsius.

english_meaning: Characterized by strong and turbulent emotions. Extremely stormy or violent, as of weather. Full of anger, excitement, or intense conflict. Very heated and unpredictable in nature or behavior.
example_sentence: Their marriage was tempestuous from the very beginning. A tempestuous wind blew across the coast all night. She had a tempestuous relationship with her business partner. The meeting turned into a tempestuous debate over the new policy. He is known for his tempestuous temper and sudden outbursts.

english_meaning: A shaped piece of metal, plastic, paper, or other material used as a pattern or guide for making something accurately. A ready-made model, design, or document that can be used as a starting point and filled in or modified for a particular purpose. (In computing) A pre-designed file or layout that helps create documents, web pages, or presentations quickly.
example_sentence: The carpenter used a metal template to cut identical pieces of wood. Please use this template to design the new brochure. He created a template for the monthly progress report. The website offers free templates for resumes and cover letters. Teachers were given a template to prepare the question papers.

english_meaning: A building used for religious worship, especially in non-Christian faiths such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism. A place regarded as being occupied by a god or gods. The flat area on each side of the forehead. The side piece of a pair of spectacles.
synonyms: ["Shrine","Sanctuary","Place of worship","Church","Mosque","House of God","(Anatomy) Side of forehead"]
example_sentence: The ancient temple attracts thousands of pilgrims every year. He bowed his head as he entered the temple. She felt a sudden pain in her temple. The old temple was built more than a thousand years ago. He gently rubbed his temples to ease the headache.

english_meaning: The speed or pace at which a piece of music is played. The rate or speed of motion or activity. The characteristic rhythm or pattern of an activity. The general pace or timing of something.
example_sentence: The conductor increased the tempo in the final movement. The tempo of city life can be exhausting. They played the song at a faster tempo. The team needs to pick up the tempo in the second half.

english_meaning: Relating to worldly rather than spiritual matters. Connected with or limited by time. Relating to the temples of the head. Lasting for a limited time rather than eternal. Secular or non-religious in nature.
example_sentence: They were more concerned with temporal power than spiritual enlightenment. The temporal lobe of the brain processes auditory information. All temporal things must eventually pass away. Kings focused on temporal authority over their kingdoms.

english_meaning: Either of the two bones at the sides and base of the skull near the ears. The bone that houses the structures of the middle and inner ear. The skull bone located below and behind the parietal bone. A hard bone that protects the hearing and balance organs.
example_sentence: The temporal bone encloses the delicate inner ear. A fracture of the temporal bone can affect hearing. Surgeons operate carefully near the temporal bone. The temporal bone lies just above the ear canal.

english_meaning: A broad, fan-shaped muscle at the side of the head above and around the ear. A major muscle of chewing that lifts the lower jaw and pulls it backwards. The muscle that fills the hollow area of the temple on each side of the skull.
example_sentence: Place your fingers on your temple and feel the temporalis move. The temporalis works together with the masseter during chewing. Headaches are sometimes caused by tension in the temporalis. The surgeon carefully avoided damaging the temporalis muscle.

english_meaning: For a limited period of time, not permanently. In a way that lasts for only a short time. For the time being or in the meantime. Until something more permanent is arranged. Not lasting or intended to last indefinitely.
example_sentence: The road is temporarily closed for repairs. She is temporarily staying with her parents. The office will be temporarily relocated during renovations. His vision was temporarily blurred after the accident.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being temporary or lasting for only a limited time. The characteristic of not being permanent. The condition of being transient or short-lived. The nature of existing for a brief period.
example_sentence: The temporariness of life makes every moment precious. She accepted the temporariness of her living situation. The temporariness of the job made him keep searching for something permanent. We must embrace the temporariness of all worldly things.

english_meaning: Lasting for only a limited period of time and not permanent. Serving as a provisional substitute or arrangement. Subject to change or replacement in the near future. Transitory in nature rather than enduring over a long span.
example_sentence: They found a temporary solution to the power outage. The bridge was rebuilt as a temporary structure after the storm. She took a temporary job during the summer vacation. Rain caused temporary delays in the flight schedules.

english_meaning: To delay or avoid making a decision to gain time. To act evasively in order to gain time, avoid confrontation, or postpone a decision. Often implies being indecisive or stalling strategically.
example_sentence: The manager decided to temporise until he had more information. Politicians often temporise to avoid taking a controversial stand. She temporised during the meeting to gather support for her idea. Instead of answering immediately, he temporised to think carefully.

english_meaning: To delay or avoid making a decision to gain time. To act evasively in order to gain time, avoid confrontation, or postpone a decision. Often implies being indecisive or stalling strategically.
example_sentence: The manager temporized instead of giving a clear answer. Politicians often temporize to avoid controversy. She temporized before agreeing to sign the contract. He temporized during the negotiations to gather more information.

english_meaning: To try to persuade someone to do something, especially something wrong or unwise. To attract someone by offering something desirable. To arouse a desire in someone. To risk provoking, as in 'tempt fate'.
example_sentence: The offer of a free trip tempted her to sign the contract. Do not tempt him with sweets before dinner. The delicious smell of food tempted us to enter the restaurant. He was tempted to accept the bribe but refused. Don't tempt fate by driving in this storm.

english_meaning: A person or thing that tempts, especially to do wrong. One who entices someone into evil or unwise action. In religious texts, often used as a name for the Devil or Satan.
example_sentence: He proved to be a dangerous tempter for the young boys. The tempter offered him money in exchange for silence. In the story, the tempter appears as a friendly stranger. She refused to listen to the tempter's promises. According to the Bible, the Tempter deceived Adam and Eve.

english_meaning: A woman who tempts or attracts someone, especially into sexual or immoral behavior. A seductive or alluring female. A woman who deliberately entices others.
example_sentence: In the film, she plays the role of a mysterious temptress. He described her as a dangerous temptress with a charming smile. The novel's temptress leads the hero into serious trouble. She was often unfairly labeled as a temptress by her critics. The painting shows a temptress in a red gown.

english_meaning: Capable of being defended, maintained, or justified. Something that can be supported with reasoning or argument; able to be held or defended against criticism or attack. Often used for ideas, positions, or situations that are reasonable and defensible.
example_sentence: The scientist presented a tenable theory based on years of research. Her argument for extending the deadline was tenable and convinced the committee. The company’s plan is tenable if the budget is approved. He tried to defend his actions, but they were not tenable under scrutiny.

english_meaning: Tending to keep a firm hold of something or clinging closely. It describes a person who is very determined, persistent, and unwilling to give up despite difficulties. It illustrates a strong will and unyielding nature.
example_sentence: The tenacious athlete refused to let her injury stop her from competing. You must be tenacious to succeed in this highly competitive industry. He holds a tenacious belief in the power of free speech. The lawyer made a tenacious defense of her client in court. We admired his tenacious grip on the slippery rope.

english_meaning: In a way that is very determined and persistent; holding firmly to a purpose, position, or belief despite obstacles or opposition. Doing something with great determination, persistence, and strong resolve. A person who acts tenaciously continues working toward a goal despite difficulties, obstacles, failures, or opposition.
example_sentence: She tenaciously pursued her dream of becoming a doctor. He tenaciously defended his position in the debate. The climber tenaciously gripped the rock face despite the storm. She tenaciously negotiated until a fair deal was reached.

english_meaning: The quality of being very determined and persistent; the ability to hold firmly to a purpose or belief despite difficulties or opposition. It refers to strong determination, perseverance, endurance, and firmness of purpose. A person with tenacity continues working toward a goal even when facing challenges, failures, or opposition. It can also refer to the ability to hold firmly to something, either physically or figuratively.
example_sentence: Her tenacity helped her overcome every obstacle in her career. He showed great tenacity in completing the marathon despite injury. Tenacity is the key ingredient of long-term success. The tenacity of the researchers led to a breakthrough vaccine.

english_meaning: The possession or occupancy of land or property as a tenant under a lease or rental agreement. The period of time during which someone rents a property.
example_sentence: Her tenancy began on the first of the month. The tenancy agreement was signed for one year. He ended his tenancy early and moved to another city. The landlord refused to renew the tenancy due to repeated late payments.

english_meaning: A person who pays rent for the use of a room, building, land, etc to the person who owns it. One who rents or leases a dwelling (such as a house) from a landlord. To live or work in a place as a tenant. One who rents a room or apartment in another's house.
example_sentence: They had evicted their tenants for non-payment of rent. The decorating was done by a previous tenant. The laundry in the basement is for tenants only.

english_meaning: To be likely to behave in a particular way or to happen often. To take care of, look after, or attend to someone or something. To move or lean in a particular direction. To manage or work on land, animals, or a business. To serve customers, especially at a bar or shop.
example_sentence: Prices tend to rise sharply just before the festival. She stayed up all night tending to her sick child. The discussion tended towards politics as the evening went on. He spent the morning tending the garden behind the house.

english_meaning: To usually or naturally seek protection or cover (especially during danger, bad weather, or fear). It shows a habit or natural tendency to find safety.
example_sentence: Birds tend to take shelter during storms. He tends to take shelter behind excuses when challenged. During heavy rains, people tend to take shelter under trees or roofs. Animals tend to take shelter when they sense a storm coming. Children tend to take shelter behind their parents when they feel afraid. Nomads tend to take shelter in caves during extreme weather.

english_meaning: A natural inclination or habit of behaving in a certain way. A general direction in which something is developing or a natural habit or inclination of a person or thing. Behavior, thinking patterns, or trends over time.
example_sentence: She has a tendency to wake up early every morning. There is a growing tendency toward online learning. He has a tendency to forget important dates. Children have a natural tendency to be curious.

english_meaning: Expressing or promoting a particular opinion, cause, or point of view, especially in a biased way. Not neutral or objective; deliberately favoring one side. Written or spoken in a manner intended to persuade rather than inform. Marked by a strong intentional bias.
example_sentence: The article was tendentious and lacked balanced reporting. His speech was clearly tendentious in favor of the ruling party. She wrote a tendentious book on the war. Their tendentious views made the debate unfair.

english_meaning: Soft, delicate, or easily damaged. Showing gentleness, kindness, or affection. Painful or sore to the touch. Young and vulnerable, especially in age. To formally offer or present something, such as a resignation or payment. A formal written offer to carry out work or supply goods at a stated price.
example_sentence: The meat was so tender that it melted in the mouth. She gave him a tender kiss on the forehead. His injured ankle was still tender to the touch. The company tendered a bid for the construction project.

english_meaning: In a gentle, loving, caring, or affectionate manner. With physical softness or delicacy. In a way that avoids causing pain or damage. With emotional sensitivity.
example_sentence: She tenderly wrapped the injured bird in a soft cloth. He kissed his daughter tenderly before leaving. The nurse tenderly cared for the elderly patient. She spoke tenderly to comfort the crying child.

english_meaning: Gentle affection, warmth, and care shown toward someone. A soft or delicate quality in touch, voice, or feeling. Sensitivity to pain, especially in a part of the body when touched. Kindness and sympathy expressed toward others. The state of being easily damaged or affected due to softness.
example_sentence: She looked at her baby with great tenderness. He spoke to his grandmother with love and tenderness. The doctor noticed some tenderness in her lower back. Their tenderness toward each other was clear to everyone.

english_meaning: A tough, fibrous cord of tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone. A strong band that transmits the pull of a muscle so that the bone moves. A part of the body that gives strength and stability to a joint during movement. A structure made mainly of collagen that can withstand great tension but stretches very little.
example_sentence: The athlete tore a tendon in his right ankle. A tendon connects muscle to bone and transmits its pull. Gentle stretching can reduce the risk of tendon injuries. Surgery was needed to repair the ruptured tendon.

english_meaning: enderness, affection, gentle love, warmth of feeling. A feeling of deep affection, kindness, gentleness, and emotional warmth towards someone. It is often used to describe loving care between family members, friends, or romantic partners.
example_sentence: Her voice was filled with tendresse when she spoke to her grandmother. The mother held her baby with great tendresse. His letter expressed deep tendresse and gratitude. The painting captured the tendresse between the old couple.

english_meaning: A principle, belief, or doctrine that is firmly held to be true. A core idea or rule that forms the foundation of a religion, philosophy, ideology, or system of thought. An accepted opinion or guiding conviction shared by the members of a group, profession, or organization. A fundamental assumption upon which a theory, policy, or way of life is based.
example_sentence: Non-violence is a central tenet of his philosophy. Honesty and hard work are the basic tenets of our company. The tenets of democracy include equality, freedom, and justice. She refused to abandon the tenets of her faith. Respect for elders is a core tenet of our culture.

english_meaning: A muscle that tightens or stretches a part of the body. In mathematics, a quantity that generalises scalars, vectors, and matrices. An array of numbers that changes in a fixed way under a change of coordinates. In physics, a mathematical object used to describe stress, strain, and fields. In computing, a multi-dimensional array used in machine learning.
example_sentence: The tensor muscle helps keep the eardrum tight. Einstein's equations are written in terms of a curvature tensor. Each image is stored as a tensor before training the model. Engineers use a stress tensor to study forces inside the beam.

english_meaning: A shelter made of cloth or canvas stretched over poles. A portable structure used for camping or temporary living. A large covered space used for events such as weddings or fairs. To cover something so that it forms a tent-like shape. To camp or live in a tent for a period of time.
example_sentence: We pitched our tent beside the river before sunset. A huge tent was set up for the wedding guests. He tented the injured hand with a light cloth. The family tented in the mountains for three nights.

english_meaning: A long, flexible arm-like part of an animal such as an octopus or jellyfish. A slender growth on a plant used for feeling or catching. A limb used for touching, holding, or moving. Something that spreads out and takes control, like the branches of an organisation. A far-reaching influence often seen as harmful.
example_sentence: The octopus wrapped a tentacle around the rock. A jellyfish can sting with its long tentacles. The organisation extended its tentacles into every district. One tentacle of the plant curled around the wooden stick.

english_meaning: The act of trying or testing something. An experimental method of finding a result by repeated trial. In engineering, adjustment made by trial and error. An older word for temptation or enticement. An attempt or trial made to reach a solution.
example_sentence: The mechanic solved the problem by simple tentation. Tentation is often used when no exact formula is available. Through patient tentation, the engineers found the right setting. Old texts use tentation where we would now say temptation.

english_meaning: Something that is done as a trial, experiment, or in a cautious way because it may change later. It can refer to plans, ideas, or actions that are not final or are subject to confirmation.
example_sentence: We made a tentative arrangement to meet on Friday. Her English is correct but tentative. We have tentatively agreed to buy that house. He reached some tentative conclusions about the possible cause of the accident.

english_meaning: In a way that is not certain or definite. Hesitantly and with caution. As a first attempt that may be changed later. Provisionally, subject to confirmation.
example_sentence: The meeting has been tentatively scheduled for next Monday. She tentatively agreed to join the project team. He tentatively stepped forward to speak. The date of the wedding was fixed tentatively for December. They tentatively suggested a new price for the product.

english_meaning: The quality of being uncertain or not final. Hesitation or lack of confidence in speech or action. The state of being provisional and open to change. Cautious behaviour that shows doubt. A careful, unsure manner of doing something.
example_sentence: There was a clear tentativeness in his voice during the interview. The tentativeness of the plan was obvious to everyone present. She spoke with a tentativeness that revealed her doubts. Scientists stressed the tentativeness of their early findings.

english_meaning: Very weak, slight, or insubstantial. Lacking a sound basis, as in reasoning or evidence. Thin in form or consistency. Not strongly held or supported. Barely holding together or existing.
example_sentence: He has only a tenuous connection to the company. Their evidence for the theory is very tenuous. The rope had a tenuous grip on the rock. She held on to a tenuous hope of recovery.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being tepid, that is, only slightly warm. A lack of warmth, enthusiasm, or strong feeling. A rare word often confused with trepidation, which means fear or nervous anxiety.
example_sentence: The tepidation of the bath water made it unpleasant. Her tepidation towards the proposal was obvious to everyone. Critics noted the tepidation of the audience's applause. Do not confuse tepidation with trepidation in formal writing.

english_meaning: A metric prefix denoting a factor of one trillion (1012) of the base unit. Used before units such as byte, watt, or hertz to express extremely large quantities. Represented by the symbol T in the International System of Units.
example_sentence: One terabyte of storage can hold hundreds of hours of video. The new supercomputer performs calculations at terascale speed. Scientists measure the explosion in terajoules of energy. Modern data centers routinely manage several terabytes of information.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to about one trillion bytes. A measure of computer storage equal to 1,024 gigabytes. A very large amount of digital data.
example_sentence: The new laptop has a one terabyte hard drive. Our servers process several terabytes of data each day. A single terabyte can hold thousands of films. Storage prices per terabyte keep falling.

english_meaning: A soft, silvery-white metallic chemical element of the lanthanide series. A rare-earth metal with the symbol Tb and atomic number 65. A metal used in phosphors, solid-state devices, and magnetic alloys.
example_sentence: Terbium is used in green phosphors for display screens. The alloy contains a small amount of terbium. Terbium was first identified in a Swedish mineral. Demand for terbium has risen with new technologies.

english_meaning: The three-hundredth anniversary of an important event. A celebration marking three hundred years since something happened. Relating to or marking a period of three hundred years.
example_sentence: The city is celebrating the tercentenary of its founding. A special stamp was issued for the tercentenary. Tercentenary celebrations will last a whole week. The library published a tercentenary history of the college.

english_meaning: A group of three lines of verse in a poem. A set of three rhyming lines forming a unit. In music, a triplet of three notes.
example_sentence: The sonnet ends with two tercets. Dante wrote his epic in linked tercets. Each tercet develops a single image. The poet arranged the lines into neat tercets.

english_meaning: To bring something to an end or stop it completely. To end an agreement, contract, or employment. To finish or come to a conclusion. To stop at a particular point, as a road or route does.
example_sentence: The company decided to terminate the contract early. The bus route terminates at the central station. His employment was terminated without notice. They agreed to terminate the discussion.

english_meaning: The act of ending something completely. The end of a contract, agreement, or period of employment. The point at which something stops or finishes. The process of bringing something to a close.
example_sentence: He received a letter confirming the termination of his contract. The termination of the project disappointed the staff. Either side may request termination with one month's notice. The termination of the line is at the harbour.

english_meaning: The body of terms used in a particular subject, profession, or field of study. The special language and vocabulary of a specialized area. The system of technical terms and their usage.
example_sentence: Medical terminology can be very difficult for beginners. He is well-versed in legal terminology. The book explains scientific terminology in simple language. Different fields have their own specific terminology. Students should learn the correct terminology of their subject.

english_meaning: A social insect belonging to the order Blattodea. It lives in organized colonies with workers, soldiers, and reproductive members. Termites play an important role in nature by breaking down dead wood and recycling nutrients. However, when they infest homes or wooden structures, they can silently destroy timber, flooring, furniture, doors, books, and other wooden items, leading to significant financial loss.
synonyms: ["White ant (common but technically incorrect)","Wood eating insect","Wood pest","Cellulose eating insect"]
antonyms: ["There is no direct antonym for termite"]
example_sentence: The old wooden table was badly damaged by termites. We hired a pest control company after discovering termites in the house. Termites can destroy wooden structures if they are not treated early. The scientist studied how termites build strong underground colonies.

english_meaning: A stretch of land, especially with regard to its physical features. It describes the topography and natural characteristics of a specific geographic area.
example_sentence: The rugged terrain made the hiking trip very challenging for the beginners. Soldiers are trained to navigate through difficult desert terrain. The mountain bike is specially designed for rocky and uneven terrain. They used satellite imagery to map the unknown forest terrain.

english_meaning: A fault-bounded area or region with a distinct stratigraphy, structure, and geological history. It is a crustal block or fragment that differs significantly from surrounding areas. In geology, these are often considered building blocks of continents.
example_sentence: The geologist identified a new terrane in the mountain range. This terrane originated as an island arc millions of years ago. Several exotic terranes collided to form the western edge of the continent. The boundary between the two terranes is marked by a deep fault.

english_meaning: Relating to or existing on the earth or land. Living on or in the ground, as opposed to in water, air, or trees. Of or belonging to this world rather than heaven or outer space. Broadcasting from stations on the ground rather than by satellite.
example_sentence: Frogs are amphibious, while lizards are largely terrestrial animals. The book compares terrestrial and marine ecosystems. Most terrestrial channels are still popular in rural areas. Scientists have long searched for extra-terrestrial life. The terrestrial climate varies greatly from region to region.

english_meaning: In a very bad, severe, or unpleasant way. To a great extent; extremely. In a way that causes fear or distress. Very much; excessively. Poorly or unsuccessfully.
example_sentence: I am terribly sorry for the delay. The weather turned terribly cold overnight. He played terribly in yesterday's match. She missed her family terribly while abroad.

english_meaning: A small, active breed of dog originally bred to hunt small animals in burrows. A brave and energetic dog of various small breeds. Figuratively, a person who is persistent and tenacious.
example_sentence: He keeps a small terrier as a pet at home. The terrier chased the rat into the field. Yorkshire terriers are very popular family dogs. She is a real terrier when it comes to finishing her work. The farmer's terrier barked all night at the intruders.

english_meaning: To cause someone to feel extreme fear. To frighten severely. To fill with terror or dread. To scare intensely.
example_sentence: The loud thunder began to terrify the little children. The idea of speaking in public terrifies her. Horror movies used to terrify me as a child. The sudden fire terrified everyone in the building. Do not terrify the poor animal by shouting at it.

english_meaning: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea. Showing strong defensive attitudes toward one's area, possessions, or rights. Belonging to a particular territory. Relating to a country's land or waters.
example_sentence: The country protects its territorial waters with a strong navy. Dogs can become very territorial when strangers enter the house. There is an old territorial dispute between the two nations. He is quite territorial about his desk at the office. Many animals are naturally territorial by instinct.

english_meaning: Land under control of country, ruler, Particular type of land, An area that one person, group, animal etc considers as their own.
example_sentence: They have refused to allow UN troops to be stationed in their territory. Our representative cover a large territory.

english_meaning: Extreme fear or dread. A person or thing that causes great fear. Violence used to frighten people for political purposes. A troublesome or annoying person, especially a child, used informally.
example_sentence: She screamed in terror when the lights went out. The children fled in terror from the burning house. The region lived under the terror of armed groups. That little boy is a real terror at school.

english_meaning: The use of violence and intimidation, especially against civilians, to achieve political aims. Acts intended to create widespread fear in a population. Organized violent activity carried out by groups or individuals for ideological reasons. A criminal practice condemned under national and international law.
example_sentence: Terrorism remains a serious threat to global peace. The country has suffered greatly from terrorism. World leaders pledged to fight terrorism together. Acts of terrorism are punishable under strict laws.

english_meaning: A person who uses violence and fear to achieve political aims. Someone involved in acts of terrorism. Relating to terrorism or those who carry it out. Describing an attack, group, or activity connected with terror.
example_sentence: The police arrested two suspected terrorists yesterday. A terrorist attack shook the capital last night. Security forces destroyed a terrorist hideout. He was convicted of belonging to a terrorist group.

english_meaning: To fill someone with intense fear over a period of time. To threaten or frighten people in order to control them. To carry out acts of violence that keep a community in fear. To bully or harass someone persistently.
example_sentence: Armed gangs terrorized the villagers for months. He was terrorized by threatening phone calls. The bullies terrorized younger students at the school. Rebels terrorized the region until the army arrived.

english_meaning: Using very few words; brief and to the point. Short in a way that seems rude or unfriendly. Expressed in a compact and economical style. Abrupt and lacking warmth in speech or writing.
example_sentence: His reply was terse and left no room for discussion. She sent a terse message saying only that she was busy. The manager gave a terse account of the incident. I was surprised by his terse manner on the phone.

english_meaning: In a brief and direct manner using few words. In a short way that may sound abrupt or unfriendly. Concisely and without unnecessary detail. Curtly, with little politeness or explanation.
example_sentence: He answered tersely and returned to his work. The spokesman tersely denied the allegations. She tersely told them the meeting was over. The note was written tersely, without any greeting.

english_meaning: The quality of using very few words. Brevity of expression in speech or writing. Abruptness that can seem unfriendly. Economy of language that leaves out all unnecessary detail.
example_sentence: The terseness of his reply surprised everyone. Her writing is admired for its terseness and clarity. There was a certain terseness in the official statement. He apologised for the terseness of his earlier email.

english_meaning: To try something carefully before fully committing to it. To find out people's opinions before taking action. To check a situation before making a decision. To make a small effort to see how something will be received. To gather information before proceeding.
example_sentence: He asked a few questions to test the water before proposing the idea. Let's test the water before launching the product. She tested the water by discussing the plan with her manager first. Before investing, test the water carefully.

english_meaning: A person's will, especially the part dealing with personal property. Something that serves as clear evidence or proof of a specified fact or quality. Either of the two main divisions of the Christian Bible (Old Testament and New Testament).
example_sentence: His success is a testament to his hard work and dedication. She wrote her last will and testament before the operation. The building stands as a testament to fine craftsmanship. He often read the New Testament in the evenings. Her calm behavior is a testament to her strong character.

english_meaning: To give evidence as a witness in a law court. It also means to serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or truth. To make a solemn declaration under oath.
example_sentence: The witness was called to testify during the trial. Her success will testify to her hard work and dedication. He refused to testify against his best friend in court. The ancient ruins testify to the grandeur of the lost civilization.

english_meaning: A formal statement testifying to someone's character and qualifications. A public expression of appreciation or admiration. A written or spoken recommendation given by a customer or user. An event held to honor someone.
example_sentence: The company website is full of customer testimonials. His former boss wrote him an excellent testimonial. The team organized a testimonial match in honor of the retiring player. She read the testimonial aloud at the farewell party. The book contains testimonials from famous scientists.

english_meaning: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law. Evidence or proof provided by the existence or appearance of something. A public declaration of a personal experience or belief, especially in a religious context.
example_sentence: The witness gave her testimony before the judge. His life is a living testimony to the power of faith. The lawyer challenged the testimony of the main witness. Her achievements are a testimony to years of hard work. Several people offered testimony in support of the accused.

english_meaning: One of the two male reproductive organs contained in the scrotum. The male gonad that produces sperm cells. The organ that secretes the male hormone testosterone. An oval-shaped gland responsible for male fertility and sexual characteristics.
