example_sentence: Each testis produces millions of sperm every day. The testis also secretes the hormone testosterone. An injury to the testis requires immediate medical attention. The doctor examined the left testis for swelling.

english_meaning: The main male sex hormone responsible for male physical traits and reproductive functions. A hormone mainly produced in the testes of males and in smaller amounts in the ovaries of females and adrenal glands. It plays a key role in the development of male reproductive organs, muscle mass, bone density, body hair growth, deep voice, and sexual drive. In females it supports bone strength, mood balance, and overall hormonal regulation.
example_sentence: Testosterone levels increase during puberty in boys. Regular exercise can help maintain healthy testosterone levels. Doctors sometimes test testosterone to check hormonal balance. Low testosterone may cause fatigue and reduced muscle strength.

english_meaning: Easily annoyed or quick to get angry. A person who becomes irritated or impatient very quickly, often over small or unimportant matters. A testy person may respond sharply or rudely even without a strong reason.
example_sentence: He became testy when people asked too many questions. The manager sounded testy after a long and stressful day. She gets testy if her routine is disturbed. His testy reply showed he was already irritated.

english_meaning: A fourteen-sided polygon with fourteen angles. A geometric shape with fourteen straight sides and fourteen vertices. Any flat shape with fourteen corners and fourteen edges.
example_sentence: A regular tetradecagon has fourteen equal sides and angles. The decorative plate featured a tetradecagonal border. Mathematicians study the symmetry properties of tetradecagons. The pavilion was built with a tetradecagonal base.

english_meaning: A three-dimensional solid with four triangular faces. A polyhedron with four vertices, six edges, and four faces. The simplest form of pyramid with a triangular base. A regular tetrahedron has all faces as equilateral triangles.
example_sentence: A tetrahedron is the simplest polyhedron. A regular tetrahedron has four identical faces. The molecular structure forms a tetrahedron. Calculate the volume of the tetrahedron.

english_meaning: An inherited blood disorder characterized by abnormal hemoglobin production. A genetic condition causing reduced oxygen-carrying capacity in blood. A disease resulting in anemia of varying severity. A hereditary disorder common in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian populations.
example_sentence: Thalassemia is an inherited genetic disorder. She requires regular blood transfusions due to thalassemia. Thalassemia carriers may have mild anemia. Genetic counseling is recommended for thalassemia families.

english_meaning: Fear of death or dying. An intense, persistent fear of one’s own death or the process of dying. It can cause anxiety, avoidance behaviors, and sometimes panic attacks when thinking about death.
antonyms: ["Fearlessness of death","Acceptance of mortality","Calmness about dying"]
example_sentence: His thanatophobia made him avoid hospitals at all costs. People with thanatophobia may struggle with thoughts about their own mortality. Counseling helped her manage her thanatophobia. Thanatophobia can affect daily life if it becomes severe.

word: That was your shot and you blew it
english_meaning: You had a good chance or opportunity to succeed, but you failed or wasted it.
antonyms: ["You nailed it","You made it work","You seized the opportunity","You succeeded","You took your chance well"]
example_sentence: That was your shot to impress the boss, and you blew it. That was your shot to win the match, and you blew it by missing the last goal. He had an interview with his dream company, but he blew it by showing up late. That was your shot to apologize and make things right, but you blew it.

english_meaning: A person whose job is to cover roofs with thatch (straw, reeds, or similar plant material). A worker skilled in the traditional craft of thatching.
example_sentence: The thatcher climbed onto the roof to begin his work. Only a skilled thatcher can produce such a neat finish. The village thatcher has been working for over forty years. She hired a thatcher to repair the old cottage roof. The thatcher explained how long the new roof would last.

english_meaning: Third person singular present tense of thatch. To cover a roof with straw, reeds, or similar natural material. The covering made of such material. Plural of thatch, referring to various coverings of this type.
example_sentence: The craftsman thatches roofs with rye straw using traditional techniques handed down through generations. The village still thatches its oldest cottages in the original manner to preserve their character. Each year the roofer thatches several properties in the surrounding area. The old farmhouse thatches its outbuildings with reed from the nearby marshland.

word: That’s the way the cookie crumbles
english_meaning: That is how things happen, even if it is disappointing or unfair. This idiom is used when accepting a situation that did not turn out as expected. It shows resignation and acceptance of reality, especially when nothing can be done to change the outcome.
synonyms: ["That is life","Things happen","It cannot be helped","That is how it goes","Such is life"]
antonyms: ["Everything worked perfectly","As planned","Fair and just outcome","Things went smoothly"]
example_sentence: I did not get the job, but that’s the way the cookie crumbles. We lost the match in the last minute, that’s the way the cookie crumbles. Sometimes plans fail, and that’s just the way the cookie crumbles. He worked hard but still failed the exam, well, that’s the way the cookie crumbles.

english_meaning: To melt or become soft after being frozen. To make frozen food ready for cooking by letting it warm up. To become warmer so that ice and snow begin to melt. To become friendlier and less formal after a period of coldness. A period of warmer weather when ice melts, or an improvement in relations.
example_sentence: The snow began to thaw as soon as the sun came out. Remember to thaw the chicken before you cook it. Relations between the two countries slowly thawed after the talks. An early thaw turned the mountain paths into mud.

english_meaning: A decisive trial that proves the true value or quality of something. A situation that shows whether a person or thing is genuine. The final proof of worth or ability. A conclusive test of success.
example_sentence: The next election will be the acid test for the new party. The acid test of a teacher is how weak students improve. This match is the acid test of their training. Real friendship faces its acid test in bad times.

english_meaning: Someone who is deeply loved, cherished, or highly valued by another person, usually more than anyone else. It refers to a person who is most precious or dear to someone.
example_sentence: His daughter is the apple of his eye. The little boy is the apple of his grandmother’s eye. The teacher said that Ali was the apple of her eye because he was so kind and hardworking. Ever since his grandson was born, he’s been the apple of his eye. My pet cat is the apple of my eye, I can’t imagine a day without her.

english_meaning: The overall weight of the available evidence when both sides are compared. A judgment about which side of an argument is supported by stronger evidence. The greater probability suggested by considering all the facts together.
synonyms: ["Weight of evidence","Preponderance of evidence","Overall proof","Body of evidence"]
example_sentence: The balance of evidence suggests that the treatment is effective. On the balance of evidence, the committee accepted the researcher's conclusions. Scientists weighed the balance of evidence before issuing their report. The balance of evidence points to human activity as the main cause of climate change.

english_meaning: The likelihood that something is more probably true than not. A legal standard of proof used in civil cases, meaning more likely than not. The greater chance of one explanation being correct when compared with another.
synonyms: ["Likelihood","Greater probability","Preponderance of probability","More likely than not"]
example_sentence: On the balance of probability, the court found the company responsible. The judge ruled that, on the balance of probability, the accident was caused by negligence. In civil cases, claims are decided on the balance of probability. The balance of probability suggests the missing documents were destroyed.

word: The ball is in one's court
english_meaning: It means it is someone’s turn or responsibility to take action, make a decision, or respond. Comes from tennis: when the ball is in your court, it’s your turn to hit it.
example_sentence: I’ve done my part, now the ball is in your court. I’ve done everything I could to help; now the ball is in your court. They offered you the job, so the ball is in your court whether to accept or not. She apologized, so the ball is in his court to forgive her or not.

english_meaning: The most basic or essential parts of something. The simplest outline without details. The minimum required elements. The core structure or framework. The fundamental facts of a matter.
example_sentence: He gave me the bare bones of the story. The report contains only the bare bones of the investigation. Let me explain the bare bones of the plan. She learned the bare bones of French before her trip.

english_meaning: The most important fact or point of a matter. The final result or conclusion of something. The essential truth after everything is considered. A summary of the key issue. The main financial result of a business.
example_sentence: The bottom line is that we must reduce expenses. She explained the bottom line of the report clearly. The bottom line for any company is profit. Ignore the details and focus on the bottom line.

english_meaning: An informal expression for an excellent person or thing. Used of someone who thinks very highly of themselves.
example_sentence: He thinks he is the cat's whiskers since his promotion. That new camera is the cat's whiskers. In her red dress she felt like the cat's whiskers. Their new stadium is the cat's whiskers.

english_meaning: There is no danger of being seen or caught. The way is safe and unobstructed. No one is watching or present to interfere with a planned action. The situation is secure enough to proceed.
example_sentence: We can sneak out the back door now that the coast is clear. I waited until the security guard left before telling my friends the coast is clear. You can come out of hiding now; the coast is clear. Don't move until I give the signal that the coast is clear.

english_meaning: A time very long ago that is hard to remember clearly. A period in the far past that now seems vague. Long-ago times that are only faintly recalled. Used humorously to talk about something that happened many years ago.
example_sentence: Those events belong to the dim and distant past. In the dim and distant past, people travelled by horse. He talked about his school days as if they were the dim and distant past. Such customs faded away in the dim and distant past.

word: The dogs bark but the caravan moves on
english_meaning: A saying meaning that important work continues despite criticism or opposition. Critics may complain, but progress is not stopped by their words. Used to encourage people to ignore useless noise or gossip. A reminder that determined people move forward regardless of obstacles. Real work is not affected by the objections of others.
synonyms: ["Ignore critics","Stay focused","Keep going","Move forward","Persevere","Push on","Rise above"]
example_sentence: He ignored the criticism and said, 'The dogs bark but the caravan moves on'. Despite gossip, the project continued because the dogs bark but the caravan moves on. She reminded her team that the dogs bark but the caravan moves on. Great leaders know that the dogs bark but the caravan moves on.

word: The early bird gets the worm
english_meaning: People who act early or arrive first have a better chance of success. It teaches the value of being punctual, active, and prepared before others. Success comes to those who start early.
synonyms: ["Be proactive","Act promptly","Punctual effort brings reward","Time waits for no one"]
antonyms: ["Latecomers lose opportunities","Laziness brings failure","Delay leads to loss"]
example_sentence: The early bird gets the worm, so she wakes up before sunrise to study. If you reach the market early, you will find the best fruits. The early bird gets the worm. He submitted his proposal first and got the project Truly, the early bird gets the worm. The early bird gets the worm, so I always go to work before others.

english_meaning: A very obvious problem or issue that everyone is aware of but no one wants to talk about because it is uncomfortable, sensitive, or embarrassing.
example_sentence: They avoided discussing the elephant in the room. Everyone knew the company was losing money, but no one wanted to discuss the elephant in the room. Their failing marriage was the elephant in the room during family gatherings. During the meeting, climate change was the elephant in the room that nobody mentioned. His addiction was the elephant in the room that the family chose to ignore.

english_meaning: Bad or unfair methods of doing something are acceptable if the result of that action is good or positive.
synonyms: ["Results excuse actions","Purpose excuses wrongdoing","Outcome matters more than method"]
antonyms: ["Means matter as much as the end","Do the right thing regardless of outcome","Ethics before results"]
example_sentence: He lied to get the job, believing that the end justifies the means. The leader defended corruption by saying the end justifies the means. She refused to cheat because she does not believe the end justifies the means. In politics, some people argue that the end justifies the means. He defended a morality in which the end justifies the means. That's only OK if you believe that the end justifies the means.

english_meaning: The powerful natural elements such as wind, rain, fire, and earthquakes. The physical powers that operate in the natural world. Natural events that human beings cannot control. In science, the fundamental interactions such as gravity and electromagnetism. The combined strength of the natural environment.
example_sentence: The village was left helpless before the forces of nature. Scientists study the forces of nature to predict disasters. No wall can hold back the forces of nature forever. Ancient peoples worshipped the forces of nature.

english_meaning: The whole thing or the full amount of something. Complete and total involvement without holding anything back. Going all the way, especially in the context of stripping or nudity. A comprehensive selection or set of options.
example_sentence: When he ordered the breakfast, he asked for the full monty with extra beans. The new car comes with the full monty of safety features and leather seats. They decided to give the performance the full monty, including costumes and lighting. If you are going to renovate the house, you might as well go the full monty.

english_meaning: Pretending something is bad after failing to get it. A person pretends to dislike or criticize something because they cannot get or achieve it. It refers to hiding disappointment by acting as if the thing was not valuable or desirable.
example_sentence: Ali failed to win the scholarship and then said foreign education is useless, The grapes are sour. Sana could not buy the expensive phone, so she started saying it has many problems, The grapes are sour. He was rejected for the job and later claimed the company was not good enough for him, The grapes are sour. The team lost the match and their supporters began calling the tournament unfair, The grapes are sour.

word: The grass is greener on the other side
english_meaning: People often think that other people’s situations, possessions, or circumstances are better than their own, even if that is not true. It expresses envy or the tendency to be dissatisfied with one’s own situation while admiring others.
example_sentence: He always wants to change jobs because he believes the grass is greener on the other side. She envies her friend’s life, forgetting her own blessings, the grass isn’t always greener on the other side. Don’t move to another city just because it seems exciting; sometimes the grass is greener on the other side, but challenges exist everywhere. People think the new house will solve their problems, but the grass is not always greener on the other side.

word: The harder the battle, the sweeter the victory
english_meaning: The greater the struggle to achieve something, the more satisfying the success becomes. Difficult challenges make eventual triumphs more rewarding. Success earned through hardship feels more meaningful. Victories after fierce effort bring deeper joy than easy wins. The value of achievement is measured by the difficulty overcome.
synonyms: ["No pain no gain","Struggle brings reward","Effort pays off","Perseverance wins","Hard work rewards","Toil breeds triumph","Sweet success","Earned victory","Well-fought win","Deserved triumph"]
antonyms: ["Easy come easy go","Effortless win","Cheap victory","Hollow success","Undeserved reward","Unearned triumph","Empty win","Meaningless success","Flat victory","Instant gain"]
example_sentence: After years of study she finally graduated  the harder the battle, the sweeter the victory. He won the championship after many losses; the harder the battle, the sweeter the victory. Building the business was tough, but the harder the battle, the sweeter the victory. Recovering from illness taught her that the harder the battle, the sweeter the victory.

english_meaning: The largest portion of something. The biggest and best part of a total. A major share compared to what others get. The greatest amount taken from a whole. The dominant part in a distribution.
example_sentence: The eldest son received the lion's share of the property. Marketing takes the lion's share of the company's budget. She did the lion's share of the work on the project. The lion's share of the prize went to the winning team.

english_meaning: Natural human sympathy, care, and compassion for others. A kind and gentle nature that shows itself in generosity. The instinctive tenderness that people feel towards one another. Warm-heartedness and goodwill towards fellow human beings.
example_sentence: She is full of the milk of human kindness and never refuses to help. The disaster brought out the milk of human kindness in the whole city. He seems harsh, but there is the milk of human kindness in him. Their charity work shows the milk of human kindness.

english_meaning: Having more people makes a situation happier or more enjoyable. This means that when more people join an event, gathering, or activity, it becomes more fun, lively, and enjoyable. It shows that extra people improve the situation.
synonyms: ["More people make it better","The bigger the group","The better","Everyone is welcome","The more","The better"]
antonyms: ["Less is better","Too many cooks spoil the broth","Small group is better","Keep it limited"]
example_sentence: We are planning a picnic, and everyone is invited; The more, the merrier. If your friends want to come to the party, bring them along; The more, the merrier. Our family dinner will be better with guests; The more, the merrier. Join our group project if you are interested; The more, the merrier.

word: The nuts and bolts of something
english_meaning: The practical details and basic elements of how something works. The fundamental or essential aspects of a subject or activity. The core technical components or working details of a plan or process.
example_sentence: She spent the first week learning the nuts and bolts of her new role. The training course covers the nuts and bolts of running a small business. He was good at strategy but struggled with the nuts and bolts of implementation. The report explains the nuts and bolts of the new policy in clear language.

word: The pen is mightier than the sword
english_meaning: Writing can defeat violence. Education is stronger than war. Ideas influence people more deeply than weapons. Peaceful communication creates lasting change. Knowledge and wisdom can win battles without fighting.
example_sentence: Journalists proved that the pen is mightier than the sword by exposing corruption through writing. Peaceful speeches and books changed the nation because the pen is mightier than the sword. Teachers believe that the pen is mightier than the sword in building a better society. The leader used dialogue instead of war because he knew the pen is mightier than the sword.

word: The pot is calling the kettle black
english_meaning: To accuse someone of something you are guilty of yourself. (This idiom means that someone is criticizing another person for a fault or mistake that they themselves also have.)
example_sentence: John said Peter was lazy, but John never works either. The pot is calling the kettle black. She blamed her friend for being rude, but she is equally rude herself. The pot is calling the kettle black. When politicians call each other corrupt, it is often a case of the pot calling the kettle black. You laughed at his mistake, but you made the same one yesterday. The pot is calling the kettle black.

word: The shoe is on the other foot
english_meaning: The situation has reversed, roles or conditions are now opposite from what they were before.
example_sentence: I used to boss him around at work, but now the shoe is on the other foot since he became my manager. She laughed at me for being nervous during the presentation, but the shoe is on the other foot today. The company used to delay payments to freelancers, but now the shoe is on the other foot with them waiting for clients. He used to tease me for forgetting things, and now the shoe is on the other foot.

word: The straw that broke the camel’s back
english_meaning: A small or final problem that causes a big reaction or breakdown, because it adds to many previous problems. After enduring many difficulties, one last small issue causes someone to lose patience or collapse under pressure.
synonyms: ["The last straw","Final blow","Breaking point","Tipping point","Last nail in the coffin"]
antonyms: ["Relief point","Turning point for improvement","First step toward solution","Fresh start","Calm after the storm"]
example_sentence: He had been facing many issues at work, but being blamed for something he didn’t do was the straw that broke the camel’s back. The final insult was the straw that broke the camel’s back, and she decided to quit her job. After months of delays, the cancellation of the project was the straw that broke the camel’s back for the team. Constant noise was irritating, but when the neighbor started drilling at midnight, it was the straw that broke the camel’s back.

english_meaning: The pleasant feeling and rewards that come with achieving success. The enjoyment of fame, wealth, or recognition after hard work. The attractive sense of triumph experienced after winning.
example_sentence: After years of struggle, she finally enjoyed the sweet smell of success. The team savoured the sweet smell of success in the dressing room. He wrote about the sweet smell of success in his memoir. Winning the contract gave them the sweet smell of success.

word: The thin end of the wedge
english_meaning: An event or action that is the beginning of something more serious and/or unpleasant. A minor action or decision that seems harmless at first but is likely to lead to serious, unwanted, or difficult consequences later. It warns that allowing something small can open the door to much larger problems.
synonyms: ["Slippery slope","First step toward trouble","Opening the door"]
example_sentence: The introduction of a tax on workplace parking is seen by many as the thin end of the wedge. Allowing one exception to the rule could be the thin end of the wedge. Many critics believe this policy change is the thin end of the wedge toward more restrictions. He warned that accepting the proposal would be the thin end of the wedge for future demands. What looks like a small compromise may turn out to be the thin end of the wedge.

english_meaning: A small, visible part of a much larger hidden problem or situation. What you can see is only a fraction, the real issue is much deeper or bigger.
example_sentence: These complaints are just the tip of the iceberg. The corruption scandal was only the tip of the iceberg. What we see now is just the tip of the iceberg. The visible cracks were the tip of the iceberg of damage.

english_meaning: The time when one century ends and the next begins. The years just before and after a change of century. A period marking the transition between two centuries. Around the year that closes or opens a century.
synonyms: ["Century's end","Century's beginning","Transitional period","Turning point of an era"]
example_sentence: The factory was built at the turn of the century. At the turn of the century, travel by ship was common. Fashion changed greatly at the turn of the century. The novel is set at the turn of the century in Lahore.

english_meaning: The time when one year ends and the next begins. The period around New Year. The changeover between two calendar years. Late December and early January.
example_sentence: The project will begin at the turn of the year. Sales usually rise at the turn of the year. They returned home at the turn of the year. Prices are expected to change at the turn of the year.

english_meaning: To do something completely or with maximum effort, to include everything possible.
example_sentence: He went the whole nine yards for the wedding. He gave the whole nine yards during the game. She prepared the report with the whole nine yards. They did the whole nine yards to impress the client.

english_meaning: Full of opportunity. One has the ability or freedom to achieve anything. You have opportunities available and can achieve what you want.
example_sentence: Now I have a degree, the world is my oyster. With talent, the world is your oyster. He believes the world is his oyster. She feels the world is her oyster.

english_meaning: Full of opportunity. One has the ability or freedom to achieve anything. You have opportunities available and can achieve what you want.
example_sentence: After finishing her degree, she felt the world was her oyster. With his talent and confidence, the world is truly his oyster. Once they saved enough money, they realized the world was their oyster. When you believe in yourself, the world becomes your oyster.

english_meaning: You have the ability and freedom to do exactly what you want. Every opportunity is available to you in life. You can achieve anything you desire if you take the chance. It signifies that the world contains treasures waiting to be discovered by you. It encourages someone to explore limitless possibilities without fear.
synonyms: ["Limitless opportunities","Infinite possibilities","Complete freedom","Open doors","Unbounded potential","Advantageous position","Boundless horizons","Free rein","World at your feet","Endless chances"]
example_sentence: After graduating from university with top honours, the world is your oyster. He reminded his daughter that the world is her oyster if she works hard. With a substantial inheritance and boundless talent, the world is your oyster. Don't be afraid to travel because the world is your oyster right now.

english_meaning: In a way that is exaggerated for dramatic effect. In a manner suited to the theatre. In a showy, expressive, or overly dramatic style.
example_sentence: He theatrically threw his hands into the air in disbelief. She sighed theatrically before answering the question. The child theatrically pretended to faint on the floor. He announced the news theatrically to catch everyone's attention. The politician spoke theatrically to move the crowd.

english_meaning: A person who believes in the existence of a god or gods. Someone who believes in a personal, active, and creator God. A believer in the divine as opposed to an atheist. An adherent of theism as a philosophical or religious belief.
example_sentence: A theist believes that God created the universe. Many philosophers are theists in their outlook. She was raised as a theist in a religious family. Theists and atheists often engage in deep debates.

english_meaning: The main subject or central idea of a book, speech, or discussion. A recurring topic in a work of art or literature. A particular style of decoration or design used consistently. A short melody that is repeated in a piece of music.
example_sentence: The theme of the novel is forgiveness. Loneliness is a recurring theme in his poetry. The party had a simple garden theme. The film's theme music became very popular.

english_meaning: A system of government in which religious leaders rule in the name of God or a deity. A state governed according to religious law and the guidance of clerics. A country or society where political authority and religious authority are combined in the same institution.
example_sentence: The country was ruled as a theocracy for several centuries. In a theocracy, religious law shapes every state policy. Historians compared the ancient theocracy with modern democracies. Critics warned that the reforms could turn the state into a theocracy.

english_meaning: A ruler or leader who governs in the name of God or a religion. A person who supports or belongs to a system of religious government. A member of a ruling class made up of priests or clerics.
example_sentence: The theocrat justified every law by quoting scripture. Power in that era rested with a small circle of theocrats. He was accused of behaving like a theocrat rather than a statesman. The theocrats resisted every attempt at secular reform.

english_meaning: Relating to a government ruled by religious leaders or religious law. Describing a state in which political power is exercised in the name of a deity. Having the characteristics of a theocracy.
example_sentence: The country adopted a theocratic constitution after the revolution. Theocratic rule left little space for political opposition. Historians studied the theocratic structure of the ancient kingdom. Critics called the proposed law theocratic in spirit.

english_meaning: A precision surveying instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical angles. An optical device mounted on a tripod and used by surveyors and engineers to map land and set out construction work. A telescope-based tool essential in civil engineering and geodesy.
example_sentence: The surveyor set up his theodolite at the corner of the plot. A theodolite gives far more accurate readings than a simple compass. Students learned to level a theodolite during the field class. The engineer used a theodolite to mark the road alignment.

english_meaning: Relating to the study of religious faith, practice, and experience. It pertains to the nature of God and religious belief. Often used to describe works or education focused on divinity.
example_sentence: The university offers several theological degrees for aspiring ministers. They engaged in a complex theological debate about the afterlife. He spent years reading theological texts from various religions. The priest provided a theological explanation for the ritual.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to the study of ideas about God and religion. This describes actions or perspectives rooted in religious doctrine. It refers to reasoning or interpreting something from a divine or spiritual standpoint.
example_sentence: He argued his point theologically rather than politically. The text was interpreted theologically by the scholars. Theologically speaking, the concept of grace is central to their faith. They examined the nature of suffering theologically.

english_meaning: A person who specializes in the study of religious faith, practice, and experience. They examine the nature of the divine and religious truths. This person often interprets sacred scriptures and doctrines.
example_sentence: The famous theologist preached a sermon on compassion. Every theologist has a different interpretation of the ancient text. She decided to become a theologist to understand her faith better. The theologist published a book on the history of monotheism.

english_meaning: The study of the nature of God and religious belief. It involves the systematic study of the existence and attributes of the divine. This field often includes the study of religious texts and traditions.
example_sentence: He decided to study theology at a prestigious seminary. Christian theology has evolved significantly over the centuries. The library has a massive collection of books on Islamic theology. Comparative theology examines the similarities between different religions.

english_meaning: A mathematical statement that has been proven based on previously established statements. A general proposition not self-evident but proved by reasoning. A rule or principle in mathematics or logic. A formula or result that can be demonstrated as true.
example_sentence: The Pythagorean theorem relates to right triangles. We studied several theorems in geometry class. The theorem was proven using algebraic methods. Mathematicians develop new theorems through rigorous proof.

english_meaning: Related to ideas, concepts, or principles rather than practical application. Concerned with the theory of a subject rather than its practical aspects. It involves abstract reasoning, concepts, or hypotheses rather than hands-on experience.
example_sentence: The scientist presented a theoretical model for climate change. His arguments are purely theoretical and lack practical evidence. She has a theoretical understanding of economics but has never worked in the field. The professor discussed theoretical aspects of quantum physics in class.

english_meaning: To form a theory or set of theories about something. To speculate or suggest a possible explanation for a particular event or phenomenon without necessarily having proof yet. It involves using logical reasoning to understand how something works.
example_sentence: Scientists theorize that a giant asteroid caused the extinction of dinosaurs. Many experts theorize that the economy will recover by next year. It is easy to theorize about success, but much harder to achieve it. Researchers continue to theorize about the origins of the ancient ruins found underwater.

english_meaning: A system of ideas intended to explain something, especially one based on general principles independent of the thing to be explained. A set of principles on which the practice of an activity is based. It can also refer to an idea or opinion that has not yet been proven true.
example_sentence: In theory, the new law should improve public safety significantly. The Big Bang theory explains the origin of the universe according to physics. Darwin's theory of evolution changed the way we look at biology. The professor presented a new theory regarding the behavior of light.

english_meaning: A system of esoteric philosophy or religious thought based on direct intuition of the divine essence. The belief that one can achieve knowledge of the nature of God through mystical insight or spiritual ecstasy. A specific movement founded by Helena Blavatsky in the late 19th century seeking universal brotherhood and the study of ancient wisdom. A philosophical approach that attempts to reconcile all religions and philosophies under a singular truth. The study of the underlying laws of the universe through spiritual rather than empirical means.
example_sentence: Theosophy emphasizes the search for truth through meditation and the study of sacred texts. Blavatsky's writings remain the cornerstone of modern theosophy and esoteric research. Many scholars view theosophy as a bridge between Eastern and Western spiritual traditions. The student spent years investigating theosophy to understand the hidden mysteries of the soul.

english_meaning: Related to the healing of disease or the restoration of health. Providing a sense of relaxation or psychological well-being. Serving a medicinal purpose or curing an illness. Having a positive effect on the body or mind through treatment. Beneficial to the physical or mental state of a person.
example_sentence: Gardening can be a highly therapeutic activity for those suffering from stress. The doctor recommended a therapeutic diet to help manage the patient's condition. Many people find the sound of ocean waves to be deeply therapeutic and calming. The new drug has shown significant therapeutic benefits in clinical trials.

english_meaning: In a manner that relates to the healing of disease or the treatment of illness. Specifically designed to provide a curative or restorative effect on the body or mind. Used to describe an action taken to improve health or alleviate symptoms. Serving to maintain health or prevent the worsening of a medical condition. In a way that is beneficial to physical or mental well-being through professional treatment.
example_sentence: The new drug was administered therapeutically to stabilize the patient's condition. Swimming can be used therapeutically to help recover from muscle injuries. The counselor interacted with the client therapeutically to address deep-seated trauma. The diet was modified therapeutically to manage the symptoms of the chronic illness.

english_meaning: The branch of medicine specifically concerned with the remedial treatment of disease. A particular method, system, or series of treatments used to promote healing. The medicinal action of various drugs and therapies on the human body. The practical application of medical knowledge to restore health and alleviate suffering. A systematic approach to caring for patients through clinical interventions.
example_sentence: Modern therapeutics has advanced significantly with the introduction of gene therapy. The doctor discussed various therapeutics available for managing chronic pain. Understanding the therapeutics of a drug is essential for every pharmacist. Clinical trials are necessary to prove the efficacy of new therapeutics.

word: There is no smoke without fire
english_meaning: A rumor or sign of trouble may have some truth behind it. Suspicious reports should not always be dismissed without investigation.
antonyms: ["Baselessness","Certainty of innocence","Clear evidence of no wrongdoing"]
example_sentence: People say there is no smoke without fire, so the manager investigated the complaint. Although the rumor may be exaggerated, there is no smoke without fire. Her sudden resignation made colleagues wonder whether there was no smoke without fire. The police took the allegation seriously because there is no smoke without fire.

word: There is something wrong at the bottom
english_meaning: There is a hidden problem or dishonest cause behind a situation. Something suspicious lies at the root of the matter. The real reason for a difficulty is concealed and questionable.
synonyms: ["Something fishy","A hidden catch","Foul play","A rat to smell","An underlying problem","Suspicious circumstances","A concealed motive"]
antonyms: ["Everything is fine","All above board","Perfectly clear","Transparent","Honest dealing","No cause for concern","Straightforward"]
example_sentence: The accounts keep changing, so there is something wrong at the bottom. He avoids every question, which shows there is something wrong at the bottom. Investigators felt there was something wrong at the bottom of the deal. The sudden resignation suggested there was something wrong at the bottom.

english_meaning: It refers to a place near or in the vicinity of a specified location. It indicates an approximate time, amount, or quantity relative to a given figure. It describes a general condition or degree close to a mentioned standard.
synonyms: ["Approximately","Around","Roughly","Near","Near That Place","Near That Time","More Or Less","Give Or Take","Thereabout","Nearby","In That Vicinity","Close To"]
example_sentence: He lives in London or thereabouts. The total cost will be one hundred dollars or thereabouts. We plan to arrive around midnight or thereabouts. The temperature remained thirty degrees or thereabouts all afternoon.

english_meaning: For that reason. As a consequence of what has been said. Used to introduce a logical conclusion drawn from evidence or reasoning.
example_sentence: The evidence was weak; therefore, the case was dismissed. He was ill and therefore could not attend the meeting. Prices have risen, and therefore sales have slowed. She trained hard and therefore deserved the win.

english_meaning: Producing or relating to the production of heat. Causing the body to generate heat, especially through metabolism. Capable of increasing the rate of metabolism and burning calories. Relating to substances that boost heat production in living organisms.
example_sentence: Green tea is often described as a thermogenic drink that helps burn fat. Thermogenic foods increase the body's metabolic rate. The supplement contains thermogenic ingredients to support weight loss. Exercise has a strong thermogenic effect on the body. Some spices are known for their thermogenic properties.

english_meaning: A type of microorganism such as certain bacteria and archaea that thrives at high temperatures, often between 45°C and 80°C or even higher. These organisms are commonly found in hot springs, volcanic soils, geothermal vents, and other heated environments.
example_sentence: Scientists discovered a thermophile living in a hot spring near a volcanic region. The enzyme from a thermophile can survive extremely high temperatures. Many thermophiles are found around deep sea hydrothermal vents. Researchers study thermophiles to develop heat resistant industrial enzymes.

english_meaning: A book or electronic database that lists words in groups of synonyms and related concepts. A dictionary of synonyms and antonyms. A treasury or storehouse of knowledge or information. A categorized collection of terminology used for information retrieval. A reference work used to find the most appropriate word for a particular context.
example_sentence: If you want to avoid repeating the same word, you should consult a thesaurus. Most modern word processors include a built-in digital thesaurus for writers. The researcher used a specialized thesaurus to categorize the library's vast collection. She found the perfect adjective for her poem by browsing through an old leather-bound thesaurus.

english_meaning: A statement or theory that is put forward as a premise to be maintained or proved. A long essay or dissertation involving personal research, written by a candidate for a university degree. It serves as the central argument of a scholarly work.
example_sentence: The student spent months researching and writing her senior thesis. His main thesis is that climate change is driven by human activity. You must defend your thesis before a panel of expert professors. She formulated a strong thesis for her historical analysis of the war.

english_meaning: Good times and bad times alike. Under all circumstances, whatever difficulties arise. Used to describe unwavering loyalty or support. Every kind of condition, favourable or unfavourable.
synonyms: ["Through everything","In good times and bad","Come what may","Rain or shine","Steadfastly"]
example_sentence: She stood by her brother through thick and thin. Good friends stay together through thick and thin. The team supported their captain through thick and thin. They have shared thick and thin for thirty years.

english_meaning: An informal British expression meaning extremely stupid or slow to understand. Used humorously or critically about someone's lack of intelligence.
example_sentence: He is a kind man, but thick as two short planks. Don't ask him to fix the wiring; he's thick as two short planks. She joked that her cousin was thick as two short planks. Anyone who believed that rumour is thick as two short planks.

english_meaning: A thick growth of bushes, shrubs, small trees, or other plants that grow so closely together that it is difficult to walk through them. The word can also be used figuratively to describe a complicated or confusing situation.
example_sentence: The rabbit disappeared into a thick thicket beside the river. We struggled to walk through the thorny thicket. Birds built their nests safely inside the dense thicket. The explorers cut a path through the thicket to continue their journey.

english_meaning: The upper part of the leg between the hip and the knee. It contains major muscles like the quadriceps and hamstrings and is important for movement, support, and strength. In anatomy, it also refers to the region between the hip joint and the knee joint.
example_sentence: She injured her thigh while playing soccer. The doctor massaged his sore thigh. Birds have strong thighs for jumping and flying. He felt a sharp pain in his left thigh.

english_meaning: A small hard covering usually made of metal plastic or rubber. It is worn on the fingertip to protect the finger from being pricked by a needle while sewing or stitching fabric
example_sentence: She wore a thimble to protect her finger while sewing clothes. The tailor keeps a thimble in his sewing kit. Using a thimble makes hand stitching safer and easier. My grandmother gave me her old silver thimble.

english_meaning: To dismiss or remove an obstacle or problem from one's mind by mental effort. To imagine something as no longer existing or as having never happened. To use logic or reasoning to eliminate a perceived difficulty. To disregard a negative circumstance by focusing on other thoughts. To mentally transcend one's current physical environment or surroundings. To resolve a cognitive dissonance through rationalization or creative visualization. To treat a tangible worry as though it were nonexistent through psychological repression or abstraction. To clear the mind of specific thoughts to reach a state of detachment. To intellectually explain away a fault or error until it no longer seems relevant. To conceptualize the absence of a particular entity or condition.
example_sentence: She tried to think away the pain by focusing on a peaceful beach. You cannot simply think away your financial problems without taking actual action. He attempted to think away the walls of his prison cell through deep meditation. The philosopher argued that one could think away the material world to reach pure essence.

english_meaning: To think creatively or differently. To approach a problem or situation in an original, imaginative way instead of following usual or traditional methods. It encourages innovation and fresh ideas.
synonyms: ["Think creatively","Be innovative","Be imaginative","Break new ground","Think differently"]
example_sentence: We need to think outside the box to solve this complex problem. The company succeeded because its team always thinks outside the box. Teachers should encourage students to think outside the box. He impressed everyone by thinking outside the box during the project.

english_meaning: To consider something carefully before making a decision. To reflect on a matter thoughtfully. To ponder or weigh options before acting. To review a situation mentally.
example_sentence: Please think over my offer before you reply. He needs time to think over the proposal. I'll think it over and let you know tomorrow. She thought over her options carefully before deciding.

english_meaning: To consider all the aspects and possible consequences of a situation or plan. To mentally examine a problem from beginning to end to find a solution. To evaluate the logical progression of an idea to ensure it is viable. To reflect deeply on a matter before making a final decision. To work through a complex thought process to achieve full understanding. To anticipate potential obstacles by visualizing a sequence of events. To deliberate extensively on the implications of a specific action. To scrutinize a theory or argument for any internal inconsistencies. To process information thoroughly until a clear conclusion is reached. To rehearse a scenario mentally to prepare for actual execution.
example_sentence: You need to think through the consequences before you quit your job so abruptly. The engineers had to think through every possible failure point in the new design. She sat quietly for an hour to think through the proposal her boss had made. If we don't think through this strategy now, we might face unforeseen problems later.

english_meaning: The area of the body between the neck and the abdomen, commonly called the chest. The part of the trunk enclosed by the ribs, sternum, and thoracic vertebrae. The region containing the heart, lungs, and major blood vessels. The middle section of the spine made up of twelve thoracic vertebrae.
example_sentence: The heart and lungs lie within the thoracic region. He felt a sharp pain in the thoracic region while breathing. The thoracic region of the spine has twelve vertebrae. X-rays of the thoracic region showed no fracture.

english_meaning: Any one of the twelve bones of the spine that lie in the chest region and connect with the ribs. A vertebra of the upper and middle back that helps form the rib cage. A spinal bone that supports the chest wall and limits excessive bending of the trunk. One of the vertebrae situated between the neck and the lower back.
example_sentence: Each thoracic vertebra is attached to a pair of ribs. The patient fractured a thoracic vertebra in the fall. Stiffness in the thoracic vertebrae can limit twisting movements. The surgeon operated on the eighth thoracic vertebra.

english_meaning: A sharp pointed woody projection on the stem of a plant. A source of continual annoyance or difficulty. A cause of irritation or trouble. A prickly plant. A person or thing that causes persistent problems.
example_sentence: A thorn from the rose bush pricked her finger. He has been a thorn in my side for years. The path was full of thorns and stones. Thorn bushes protected the garden from animals. His unruly behavior is a thorn in the teacher's side.

english_meaning: Complete with regard to every detail. Careful and accurate in performing a task. Absolute and unmitigated in nature. Painstaking and methodical in approach. Not superficial or partial.
example_sentence: The police conducted a thorough investigation of the case. She is a thorough professional in her field. He gave the room a thorough cleaning before guests arrived. Our teacher provided a thorough explanation of the topic.

english_meaning: Main roads or public highways connecting one place to another. Busy public streets used for travelling through a town or city. Passages or routes that are open at both ends allowing free movement.
example_sentence: The city's main thoroughfares were closed for the parade. Heavy traffic clogged the thoroughfares during rush hour. Vendors are not allowed to sell goods on public thoroughfares. Ambulances need clear thoroughfares to reach patients quickly.

english_meaning: Very complete, detailed, and careful. Done or carried out with great attention to every part. Absolute or total in nature. Used for actions, examinations, or reforms that are exhaustive, as well as for people who are completely committed to something.
example_sentence: The police conducted a thoroughgoing investigation into the case. The reform required a thoroughgoing change in the system. He is a thoroughgoing professional. The book offers a thoroughgoing analysis of the topic. The committee carried out a thoroughgoing review of the policy.

english_meaning: In a complete and careful way; leaving nothing undone. Very much; to a great degree. In every respect; entirely. With attention to every detail.
example_sentence: Please read the instructions thoroughly before starting the exam. She thoroughly enjoyed her holiday in the mountains. The room was thoroughly cleaned before the guests arrived. He thoroughly investigated every detail of the case. I am thoroughly convinced of his honesty.

english_meaning: In spite of the fact that; although. Used to introduce a contrast or unexpected element. However; nevertheless. Even if; whether or not. Used to soften a statement or add a qualifying remark.
example_sentence: Though it was raining, we went for a walk. She smiled, though her heart was heavy. He is very talented, though a bit shy. I will try to attend, though I cannot promise.

english_meaning: Something that makes you think deeply or reconsider ideas. An idea, question, book, speech, or situation that stimulates deep thinking. It encourages reflection, analysis, or discussion rather than passive acceptance. Such things often challenge beliefs, raise new questions, or offer a fresh perspective.
example_sentence: The documentary was thought-provoking and changed how people viewed climate issues. She asked a thought-provoking question during the meeting. The novel offers a thought-provoking look at modern society. His speech was short but deeply thought-provoking.

english_meaning: To beat someone or something violently, especially with a stick or whip. To defeat someone thoroughly in a game or contest. To move wildly or violently, especially arms and legs. To discuss a problem in detail until a solution is reached. A violent movement or beating.
example_sentence: The farmer thrashed the wheat to separate the grain. Our team thrashed the opponents by a huge margin. The fish thrashed about in the net. The committee thrashed out the details of the new policy.

english_meaning: A sign or statement showing danger or harm may come. An expression, indication, or situation that suggests possible danger, harm, loss, or trouble. It can be spoken, written, implied, or shown through actions. It  can be physical, emotional, or even environmental.
example_sentence: He received death threats from right-wing groups. The storm is a serious threat to coastal villages. He received a threat warning him to stay silent. Pollution is a major threat to marine life. Her angry tone sounded like a threat to everyone in the room.

english_meaning: To warn of harm, danger, or negative action. To express an intention to cause harm, punishment, or trouble. To be likely to cause damage or difficulty. To put someone under pressure or fear. To show a sign of an approaching danger. It can also mean showing signs that something bad is likely to happen.
example_sentence: The dark clouds threaten heavy rain. He threatened to call the police if the noise continued. The company is threatening legal action. His tone threatened serious consequences. The rising river threatened the nearby villages.

english_meaning: Three times as great or as numerous. Consisting of three parts, elements, or aspects. Multiplied by three. Having three components.
example_sentence: The population of the city has increased threefold in twenty years. His plan has a threefold purpose: education, health, and jobs. Profits grew threefold after the new product was launched. The threefold benefits of exercise include strength, stamina, and health. She achieved a threefold rise in her business income.

english_meaning: A song, hymn, or poem of mourning composed or performed as a memorial to a dead person. A lament or elegy expressing grief and sorrow.
antonyms: ["Ode of joy","Celebration","Hymn of praise","Anthem","Song of joy"]
example_sentence: The poet wrote a moving threnody for his late friend. A soft threnody was played at the funeral service. Her novel ends with a threnody for the lost city. The composer's most famous work is a threnody for the war dead. He recited a heartfelt threnody in memory of his mother.

english_meaning: The point at which something begins or changes. The starting point of an event, a limit that must be reached before something happens, or the strip at the bottom of a doorway. It can also refer to a level such as pain threshold or tolerance level.
example_sentence: She is on the threshold of a new career. The noise crossed the pain threshold. He paused at the threshold before entering the room. The country is on the threshold of major change.

english_meaning: The quality of using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully. It signifies the practice of economy and good management of financial means. It is often associated with saving and avoiding unnecessary expenses.
example_sentence: Through hard work and thrift, the family was able to buy their own home. He learned the value of thrift from his parents during the recession. Thrift is an essential habit for anyone who wants to build long-term wealth. The organization encourages thrift by teaching people how to budget properly.

english_meaning: Using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully. It describes a person who is cautious with their spending and avoids luxury. Being thrifty involves making wise choices to save resources for future use.
example_sentence: A thrifty shopper always looks for sales and uses discount coupons. She is very thrifty and manages to save half of her salary every month. They lived a thrifty life in a small apartment to pay off their debts. Being thrifty allowed them to travel the world without breaking the bank.

english_meaning: To cause someone to feel a sudden surge of excitement, pleasure, or fear. A sharp, intense feeling of excitement or pleasure. Can also refer to a sudden shiver caused by fear, cold, or anticipation. A sudden sharp feeling of fear or cold (a shiver or quiver). A vibrating sensation or tremor. Intense pleasure or joy from an experience
example_sentence: The roller coaster ride gave me a real thrill. She felt a thrill of excitement when she opened the letter. The suspenseful movie thrilled the audience. Skydiving is an activity that thrills many adventure seekers.

english_meaning: Extremely pleased, excited, or delighted about something. Filled with a sudden feeling of intense joy or excitement. Very happy because of a pleasant surprise or achievement.
example_sentence: She was thrilled to receive the award for best student. We are thrilled with the results of our team's hard work. He was absolutely thrilled to meet his favorite writer. The children were thrilled by the magic show. I am thrilled to hear that you got the job.

english_meaning: A very small slender insect with fringed wings that feeds on plant tissue. A tiny pest that causes silvering, scarring, and distortion of leaves and flowers. An insect capable of spreading plant viruses in greenhouses and fields. The word is used for both the singular and plural form of the insect.
example_sentence: Thrips have damaged the young onion leaves. The greenhouse manager used sticky traps to monitor thrips. A single thrips is barely visible to the naked eye. Heavy thrips infestation reduced the yield of the chilli crop.

english_meaning: To become, and continue to be, successful, strong, healthy, etc. To grow or develop successfully. Make steady progress, be at the high point in one's career or reach a high point in historical significance or importance.
example_sentence: New businesses thrive in this area. These animals rarely thrive in captivity. These plants thrive with relatively little sunlight. His business thrived in the years before the war.

english_meaning: The passage at the back of the mouth that leads to the stomach and lungs. The front part of the neck. A narrow passage or opening resembling a throat. The ability or quality of the voice, as in a sore throat affecting speech.
example_sentence: He has a sore throat and cannot speak loudly. She swallowed hard, feeling a lump in her throat. The fish bone got stuck in his throat. The narrow throat of the valley made travel difficult.

english_meaning: To beat with a strong, regular rhythm, especially in a painful or excited way. To feel or produce a strong, steady pulse or pain. A strong, regular beat or pulse.
example_sentence: Her heart began to throb with excitement. His head throbbed painfully after the long journey. The wound on his hand throbbed all night. She could feel the throb of the drums during the parade. A dull throb of pain returned to his back.

english_meaning: The stoppage or slowing of blood flow due to blood clot formation. A medical condition involving stasis of blood related to thrombosis. The state where blood clots impede circulation.
example_sentence: The doctor diagnosed the patient with thrombostasis. Thrombostasis can lead to serious complications. Medication was used to prevent thrombostasis. Blood tests confirmed a case of thrombostasis. Understanding thrombostasis helps in treating heart conditions.

english_meaning: Royal seat of a king or queen. A ceremonial chair used by a monarch as a symbol of authority and power. The position of being a king or queen. A position of high authority or leadership. To place someone on a throne or give power.
example_sentence: The king sat proudly on the throne. She inherited the throne after her father died. The throne symbolizes royal authority. The people crowned him and placed him on the throne. The council decided to throne the young prince. They throned him after the victory.

english_meaning: A large, densely packed crowd of people or animals. To gather in large numbers in a particular place. To crowd or press together. A great multitude assembled in one place.
example_sentence: A huge throng gathered outside the palace to see the king. Fans thronged the stadium hours before the match. The market was thronging with shoppers on the eve of Eid. A throng of children surrounded the ice-cream vendor. Pilgrims throng to the holy city every year.

english_meaning: To control the speed or power of an engine. To choke or strangle someone by gripping the throat. To restrict, limit, or reduce the flow, speed, or performance of something. A device or control that regulates the fuel, air, or power supplied to an engine. The control lever or pedal used to increase or decrease speed.
example_sentence: The driver throttled the motorcycle as he entered the highway. The internet provider may throttle your connection after excessive usage. The pilot throttled down the aircraft's engines during descent. The furious man threatened to throttle the thief.

english_meaning: Passing through dense mist. Seeing despite poor visibility. Moving toward safety in difficult conditions. Finding clarity after confusion. Understanding a complex situation. Overcoming uncertainty. Discovering the truth despite obstacles. Progressing through challenging circumstances.
synonyms: ["Through the mist","Through the haze","Across the fog","Amid the fog","In the mist","Through uncertainty (figurative)","Toward clarity (figurative)"]
antonyms: ["In clear weather","In clear visibility","Out of the fog","Clearly","Without confusion"]
example_sentence: The hikers slowly walked through the fog until they reached the mountain cabin. The lighthouse guided the ships through the fog during the early morning. She finally saw the truth through the fog of rumors and misunderstandings. With patience and experience, the manager led the team through the fog of uncertainty.

english_meaning: To stay loyal and supportive in both good and bad times. To remain constant, faithful, or committed despite difficulties, hardships, or challenges.
example_sentence: She stood by her husband through thick and thin. True friends remain together through thick and thin. Our team supported each other through thick and thin to reach the final. He proved his loyalty by helping his friend through thick and thin.

word: Throw a spanner in the works
english_meaning: To do something that spoils a plan or stops progress. To cause an unexpected problem or delay. To interfere with a process so that it cannot continue smoothly. To disrupt arrangements that were going well.
example_sentence: The sudden strike threw a spanner in the works of our schedule. Bad weather threw a spanner in the works on the wedding day. His resignation threw a spanner in the works for the whole team. I hate to throw a spanner in the works, but the budget is wrong.

english_meaning: To suddenly lose one's temper and behave in an uncontrolled way. To have a tantrum or emotional outburst, often over something minor. To become extremely upset or agitated in public. An informal British expression for making a fuss.
synonyms: ["Lose temper","Have a tantrum","Blow up","Flip out","Erupt","Rage","Fume","Explode","Make a scene","Storm"]
example_sentence: He threw a wobbly when he heard his flight had been cancelled. The child threw a wobbly in the middle of the supermarket. Try to explain calmly instead of throwing a wobbly. She threw a wobbly over a tiny mistake in the report.

english_meaning: To behave recklessly without worrying about the risks. To stop being careful and act boldly. To take a chance despite possible danger or loss. To abandon prudence in favour of daring action.
synonyms: ["Take a risk","Gamble","Chance it","Be reckless","Plunge in","Dare","Venture","Act boldly","Go for broke","Abandon restraint"]
example_sentence: He threw caution to the wind and invested all his savings in the venture. They threw caution to the wind and set off without a map. She threw caution to the wind and told her boss exactly what she thought. For once, let us throw caution to the wind and enjoy the evening.

english_meaning: To discourage an idea or plan by criticising it. To reduce someone's enthusiasm or hope. To express doubt that spoils a proposal. To dampen excitement about a suggestion.
example_sentence: The finance director threw cold water on the expansion plan. Please do not throw cold water on their enthusiasm so early. His remarks threw cold water on the whole celebration. The survey results threw cold water on the company's optimistic forecast.

english_meaning: To issue a bold challenge to someone. To invite a person or group into a contest or confrontation. To openly declare opposition and dare an opponent to respond. Originally, to throw down a glove as a formal challenge to a duel.
example_sentence: The opposition leader threw down the gauntlet by demanding an early election. She threw down the gauntlet and challenged the champion to a rematch. By publishing the report, the newspaper threw down the gauntlet to the regulators. He threw down the gauntlet, daring his rivals to match his offer.

english_meaning: To waste more money, time, or effort trying to fix a situation that has already failed or is beyond repair. To continuing to invest in something unsuccessful, hoping it will improve, but only making the loss worse.
example_sentence: Investing more in that failed project would be like throwing good money after bad. He already lost thousands on that car. fixing it again is just throwing good money after bad.  Buying more shares of a failing company is throwing good money after bad.

english_meaning: To fight someone physically, especially with the fists. To engage in a brawl or exchange punches. An informal expression meaning to be ready to fight. To settle a dispute through a physical fight.
example_sentence: The two men were ready to throw hands outside the stadium. Instead of throwing hands, they finally sat down and talked. Security guards separated the fans before they could throw hands. He warned that anyone throwing hands would be removed from the club.

english_meaning: To give up or admit defeat in a difficult situation. To stop trying because success seems impossible.
example_sentence: After failing the exam three times, he finally threw in the towel. The company threw in the towel after years of unprofitable business. She didn’t want to throw in the towel even when everyone doubted her. He threw in the towel when the project became too complicated.

english_meaning: To make something clearer or easier to understand. To provide new information that explains a situation. To reveal facts that were previously hidden or confusing. To help explain the cause or meaning of an event.
example_sentence: The new documents throw light on the causes of the accident. Can you throw light on why the meeting was cancelled? Her research throws light on an ignored period of history. The witness threw light on what happened that night.

english_meaning: To spend money freely and lavishly in a way that is often intended to impress others. To waste financial resources carelessly.
synonyms: ["Spend Lavishly","Splurge","Squander","Flash Cash","Spend Like Water","Be Extravagant","Waste Money","Fritter Away","Scatter Wealth"]
antonyms: ["Save Carefully","Be Frugal","Hoard Money","Scrimp And Save","Economize","Pinch Pennies","Budget Strictly","Be Thrifty","Conserve Wealth"]
example_sentence: He tends to throw money around whenever he goes to a high-end restaurant. You cannot just throw money around and expect to buy genuine friendship. The young heir started to throw money around as soon as he inherited the estate. They throw money around on luxury cars despite their company facing a major deficit.

english_meaning: To try to solve a problem simply by spending large amounts of money on it. To fund something heavily without proper planning. To use money as a substitute for real thought or effort. To invest generously in the hope of a quick fix.
example_sentence: You cannot fix a broken system just by throwing money at it. The government has thrown money at the problem for years with little result. Instead of throwing money at the issue, they hired better managers. Critics say the ministry throws money at projects without measuring outcomes.

english_meaning:
To waste money on something useless or unprofitable.
It means spending money carelessly on things that give no real benefit, return, or value.
example_sentence: Buying fake products is like throwing money down the drain. He threw money down the drain by buying a car he never drives. Investing in that fake company was just throwing money down the drain. If you keep repairing that old phone, you are throwing money down the drain. She realized that paying for that expensive diet plan was throwing money down the drain.

english_meaning: To strongly support someone or something. To use one’s influence, power, or authority to help a person, idea, project, or cause succeed.
example_sentence: The senator threw his weight behind the new law. She threw her weight behind the project to ensure success. The mayor threw his weight behind the new education reform. The company’s CEO threw her weight behind the charity project. If the government throws its weight behind renewable energy, progress will be faster. Several famous actors threw their weight behind the environmental campaign.

english_meaning: To force to leave or move out. To get rid of something that you no longer want. To confuse something or make it wrong. To say something in a way that suggests you have not given it a lot of thought. To decide not to accept a proposal, an idea, etc.
example_sentence: You'll be thrown out if you don't pay the rent. Our calculations of the cost of our trip were thrown out by changes in the exchange rate. The disciplinary committee threw out his appeal. Much of the food that stores throw out is still edible. She threw out the old clothes.

english_meaning: To make someone feel confused, surprised, or uncertain. To disturb someone's physical balance so that they nearly fall. To upset someone's composure or plans unexpectedly.
example_sentence: The sudden change in schedule threw the whole team off balance. His unexpected arrival threw her off balance for a moment. The strong wave threw the surfer off balance. Difficult questions from the audience threw the speaker off balance.

english_meaning: To offer a small favor or reward to please someone. To give a minor concession to keep someone satisfied. To provide a small piece of help or attention. To grant a small kindness. To pacify someone with a small gesture.
example_sentence: The boss threw him a bone by giving him a small raise. Throw the kids a bone and let them stay up late tonight. The company threw the workers a bone with a tiny bonus. She threw me a bone by including me in the meeting.

english_meaning: To shock, confuse, or surprise someone completely. To upset a person's plans or expectations suddenly. To leave someone unable to react because of astonishment. To disturb someone's composure with unexpected news or events.
example_sentence: The sudden resignation threw the whole team for a loop. Her question really threw me for a loop. The change in schedule threw us for a loop. News of the merger threw investors for a loop.

english_meaning: To betray or sacrifice someone for one's own benefit. To blame or criticize a colleague to protect oneself. To abandon someone in a difficult situation. To let someone else take the blame. To betray a friend or ally for personal gain.
example_sentence: The manager threw his assistant under the bus to save his own job. Don't throw your teammates under the bus during the meeting. She threw her friend under the bus to please the boss. Politicians often throw allies under the bus when things go wrong.

english_meaning: To punish someone as severely as possible for an offense. To charge someone with every possible related crime or violation. To impose the maximum penalty allowed by law. To scold or penalize an offender without showing any leniency.
synonyms: ["Punish Severely","Penalize Heavily","Give The Maximum Sentence","Come Down Hard On","Chastise","Reprimand","Condemn","Discipline","Sentence Harshly"]
example_sentence: The judge decided to throw the book at the repeat offender. If you get caught stealing again, the principal will definitely throw the book at you. The prosecutor wanted to throw the book at him to set an example for others. They decided to throw the book at the corrupt official for his numerous crimes.

english_meaning: To leave someone unprotected in a difficult or hostile situation. To sacrifice a person to save others or oneself. To expose someone to harsh criticism or attack. To abandon someone in danger without help. To let someone face severe consequences alone.
example_sentence: The manager threw the intern to the lions during the meeting. Do not throw your friend to the lions to save yourself. Journalists threw the minister to the lions after the scandal. He felt his own party had thrown him to the lions.

english_meaning: To vomit or expel the contents of the stomach through the mouth. To raise or lift something quickly. To construct or build hastily. To abandon or give up something, such as a job.
example_sentence: The child threw up after eating too much cake. He threw up his hands in frustration. Builders threw up new houses within weeks. She threw up her job to start a business.

english_meaning: To get rid of something that is no longer useful or wanted. To waste an opportunity, chance, or resource.
example_sentence: Consumers throw away around 50 billion plastic bags annually. Don’t throw away that old book; it might be useful. He threw away the letter without reading it. She doesn’t want to throw away her career because of one mistake. They threw away their chance to win by not preparing properly.

english_meaning: To push forcefully into or toward something. To force something into a particular position. To impose something unwillingly on someone. To move suddenly and powerfully forward. A forceful push. The main purpose or central idea of something. Driving force produced by an engine, rocket, or aircraft. Strong effort toward achieving a goal.
example_sentence: He thrust the door open and entered the room. The soldier thrust his spear toward the enemy. She was thrust into a leadership role unexpectedly. The rocket generated enough thrust to leave the Earth.

english_meaning: To push someone or something away with force or with a firm decision. It can describe a physical action or a strong rejection of an idea, request, or feeling.
example_sentence: He thrust aside the papers. She thrust aside her doubts. He thrust aside the curtain. I thrust aside my fears.

english_meaning: To push or move something or someone forcefully in a forward direction. Also used figuratively to mean to promote someone or something into prominence.
example_sentence: He thrust forward his hand for a handshake. The crisis thrust forward a new generation of leaders. She was thrust forward as the spokesperson without notice. The soldier thrust forward his bayonet in the training drill.

english_meaning: Force into something. To be pushed suddenly into a situation. Used when someone is placed unexpectedly or forcefully into a role, responsibility, or difficult circumstance without preparation.
example_sentence: He thrust into the crowd. She thrust into the argument. I thrust into the fray. He thrust into the conversation.

english_meaning: To push someone or something out with force. To force a person or an object out of a place, group, or position. The action is quick and strong, often showing rejection or disapproval.
example_sentence: He thrust out the intruder. She thrust out her hand. I thrust out the debris. He thrust out his chest.

english_meaning: To force something on someone, usually a responsibility or task they did not ask for. It is used when something is pushed onto a person without choice, leaving them no option to refuse.
example_sentence: He thrust his opinion upon them. She thrust responsibility upon me. He thrust the book upon his friend. They thrust the task upon her.

english_meaning: To force something onto someone without their choice or agreement; to impose something on a person.
example_sentence: Leadership was thrust upon her when the director resigned. Responsibility was thrust upon him at a very young age. Fame was thrust upon the young actor overnight. The role of caretaker was thrust upon her without preparation.

english_meaning: A violent person, especially a criminal. A person who commits crimes such as robbery or assault, often as part of a gang. Historically, a member of an organized band of robbers and assassins in India.
example_sentence: The shopkeeper was attacked by a group of thugs at night. Police arrested the thug who had been terrorizing the neighborhood. He behaves like a thug whenever he loses his temper. A gang of thugs robbed the passengers on the highway. The film is based on the story of an old-time thug.

english_meaning: Violent, brutal, or criminal behaviour, especially by gangs or organised groups. The use of physical force and intimidation to frighten or control other people. Rough, lawless conduct that shows no respect for order or human dignity. Acts of bullying and street violence carried out openly and repeatedly.
example_sentence: The police promised to end the thuggery on the city streets. Local shopkeepers complained about the thuggery of a small gang. Such thuggery has no place in a peaceful society. The report described years of political thuggery in the region.

english_meaning: The short, thick first digit of the hand, set apart from the other fingers. The digit that allows humans to grip and hold objects firmly. The part of a glove that covers the thumb. To turn over pages quickly with the thumb. To ask for a lift from passing vehicles by signalling with the thumb.
