The government serves a tutelary role for citizens who cannot advocate for themselves. He looked upon his mentor as a tutelary figure in his academic life. Tutelary spirits were often honored with small altars in many ancient cultures.

english_meaning: A lesson or period of teaching given to one student or a small group. A printed or online guide that explains how to do something step by step. A short practical class in which a subject is explained in detail. Relating to a tutor or to the teaching done by a tutor.
example_sentence: I watched a short tutorial before assembling the furniture. The teacher holds a weekly tutorial for first-year students. This tutorial explains how to install the software step by step. She learned photo editing from a free online tutorial.

english_meaning: A formal evening suit, usually black or dark, worn with a dress shirt and bow tie. Formal clothing for men, especially at weddings or ceremonies.
example_sentence: He wore a black tuxedo to the wedding. The invitation said that tuxedos were optional. She helped her brother choose a tuxedo. Everyone looked elegant in formal tuxedos at the ceremony.

english_meaning: Silly or trivial talk or writing. Nonsense or foolish speech. Meaningless chatter. To talk in a foolish or empty manner.
example_sentence: Stop that twaddle and get back to work. The article was full of political twaddle. He twaddled on for hours about nothing important. I have no time to listen to such twaddle.

english_meaning: To make a small adjustment or change to something in order to improve it or make it work better. It usually involves fine-tuning a system or a device. It refers to the act of making such an adjustment.
example_sentence: He had to tweak the engine to get the car running smoothly. The designer made a few slight tweaks to the website layout. Just a small tweak to the recipe made the cake much better. Scientists continue to tweak the formula for maximum efficiency.

english_meaning: Two people or things that are practically identical and hard to tell apart. A pair that differ only in trivial ways despite appearing to be opposites. Used to mock a choice between two options that are essentially the same.
example_sentence: The two parties are Tweedledum and Tweedledee to most voters. Choosing between the offers felt like Tweedledum and Tweedledee. Critics called the rival plans Tweedledum and Tweedledee. The twins behaved like Tweedledum and Tweedledee all evening.

english_meaning: To play with something idly using the fingers. To turn or adjust something aimlessly or nervously. To fiddle with a device without a clear purpose. To handle small objects restlessly.
synonyms: ["Fiddle with","Play with","Toy with","Fidget with","Tinker with","Mess with","Finger"]
example_sentence: Stop twiddling with the remote control. He twiddled with his pen throughout the interview. She twiddled with her ring while waiting for the results. Don't twiddle with those switches unless you know what they do.

english_meaning: A slender woody shoot growing from a branch or stem of a tree or shrub. To understand or realize something suddenly. It represents a small part of a larger plant structure.
example_sentence: She picked up a dry twig from the ground to help start the fire. The bird carefully wove the twig into its new nest. It took him a moment to twig that she was joking. We heard a twig snap in the dark woods behind us.

english_meaning: One of two children or animals born at the same birth. It can also mean two things that are very similar or identical. One of two babies, children, or animals born from the same pregnancy. Very similar, matching, or identical in appearance, structure, or function. To match or pair something with another similar thing.
example_sentence: My twin sister and I celebrate our birthday on the same day. The hotel has twin rooms with two separate beds. The two towers looked like twin structures from a distance. The company twinned its new project with an existing successful program.

english_meaning: A strong thread or string composed of two or more strands twisted together. The act of twisting or interweaving strands or fibers to form a cord. To wind or spiral around something closely, such as a vine growing up a pole. It can also describe the physical action of two things becoming entangled or intricately connected. The term is commonly used in both physical contexts, like rope making, and metaphorical contexts, like lives becoming intertwined.
example_sentence: The gardener used a piece of sturdy twine to tie back the rose bushes. The ivy began to twine itself tightly around the old oak tree. She watched the smoke twine upward from the chimney into the cold sky. He bought a ball of hemp twine to wrap the heavy parcels. Their destinies began to twine together after that chance meeting.

english_meaning: To shine with a flickering or sparkling light. This word describes a light that changes rapidly in intensity or brightness, often seen in stars or distant city lights. It can also refer to a quick, bright expression in a person's eyes, usually indicating amusement, mischief, or joy. The act of sparkling or a brief moment of brightness. The term conveys a sense of lightness, magic, and fleeting beauty.
example_sentence: The stars began to twinkle in the clear night sky as the sun set. There was a mischievous twinkle in her eyes when she told the joke. The distant city lights twinkle like diamonds on the dark horizon. He watched the Christmas lights twinkle rhythmically on the tree. The dew drops on the grass twinkle in the early morning sunlight.

english_meaning: To spin or rotate quickly and lightly. To turn something round and round with the fingers. To dance with quick turning movements. An act of spinning or a quick circular movement. Something with a twisted or spiral shape.
example_sentence: She twirled around happily in her new dress. He twirled his pen while thinking about the answer. The dancers twirled gracefully across the stage. With one quick twirl, the child made her skirt spread out.

english_meaning: To bend, turn, or rotate something into a different shape or direction. To wind two or more things together. To distort the meaning of words or facts. An act of twisting or a twisted shape. An unexpected change or development in a story or situation.
example_sentence: She twisted the wire around the pole. He twisted his ankle while playing football. The reporter twisted his words to create a scandal. The story had an unexpected twist at the end.

english_meaning: To turn something or oneself in a circular or opposite direction, can also mean to manipulate facts or words.
example_sentence: She twisted around to see who called her. He twisted the story around to make himself look better. The snake twisted around the branch. The child twisted around in the chair.

english_meaning: To control or manipulate someone easily through charm or persuasion.
example_sentence: She can twist him around her little finger. He’s so charming he can twist anyone around his little finger. The boss twists his team around his little finger. The child twists his parents around his little finger every time.

english_meaning: A sudden and unexpected change of events in a story. An unforeseen developments that alters the anticipated outcome. A narrative technique used to surprise the audience. An abrupt shift in the plot that changes the viewer's perspective. The point where the direction of a sequence of events changes dramatically.
example_sentence: The final chapter provided a shocking twist in the tale that no one saw coming. Every good thriller needs a clever twist in the tale to keep the audience engaged. Just when we thought the hero would win, a twist in the tale changed everything. The documentary ended with a dark twist in the tale regarding the protagonist's past.

english_meaning: To remove something by turning or rotating it, often used for caps, lids, or small parts that come loose by twisting.
example_sentence: He twisted off the bottle cap. Twist off the lid before pouring. She twisted off the handle accidentally. The mechanic twisted off the pipe connection.

english_meaning: To manipulate, deceive, or cleverly persuade someone to give something or agree to something, often by avoiding the full truth or applying pressure.
example_sentence: He twisted out of her grasp. She twisted out of answering the question. The thief twisted out of the policeman’s hold. He always twists out of responsibility.

english_meaning: To make something become tightly coiled, tangled, or contorted, can also mean to become emotionally tense or anxious. Tangle, coil, or become emotionally tense.
example_sentence: The wires got twisted up behind the desk. Don’t twist up the ropes. Her emotions were all twisted up after the fight. The wind twisted up the flag.

english_meaning: To become emotionally or physically involved in a complicated or harmful situation or person. To become emotionally or mentally entangled with someone or something, often causing stress, confusion, or complications.
example_sentence: He got twisted up with the wrong crowd. She’s twisted up with too many problems. Don’t get twisted up with their drama. The business got twisted up with legal troubles.

english_meaning: To tease, mock, or make fun of them, often about a small mistake or habit. A mildly insulting word for a silly, foolish, or annoying person. It is usually informal and often used in a joking or light way.
example_sentence: He called himself a twit for forgetting the meeting. Stop acting like a twit and focus on your work. She twitted her brother about his strange haircut. They often twit each other during friendly conversations.

english_meaning: A short, sudden jerking or convulsive movement. This can refer to a physical muscle spasm that happens involuntarily. It can also mean to pull or move something with a quick, sharp tug. Emotionally, it can describe a sudden feeling of regret or anxiety, such as a 'twitch of conscience'. Usage often centers around involuntary physical reactions or sudden, rapid motions of objects or body parts.
example_sentence: A nervous twitch developed in his eyelid during the stressful exam. The cat's tail began to twitch as it watched the bird intently. He felt a sudden twitch of pain in his lower back. She gave the fishing line a quick twitch to attract the fish. The curtains would twitch whenever someone walked past the old house.

english_meaning: Very similar to each other in looks, behavior, or nature.
example_sentence: The twins are like two peas in a pod; they even dress the same. My best friend and I are two peas in a pod because we think alike. Those brothers are two peas in a pod; you can hardly tell them apart. Our teachers say we are two peas in a pod because we always work together.

english_meaning: A situation where two people enjoy each other’s company, but a third person makes it uncomfortable or less private. Used for romantic couples wanting privacy. Used when a third person feels unnecessary. Indicates discomfort in small social settings. Suggests polite withdrawal from a private moment. The presence of a third person can interrupt intimacy, comfort, or natural interaction. It is often used politely to suggest that someone may be intruding.
example_sentence: I think I should leave now, two's company, three's crowd. They wanted to spend time alone, after all, two's company, three's crowd. When I joined them, I felt like I was intruding because two's company, three's crowd. He smiled and said two's company, three's crowd, hinting that I should give them space.

english_meaning: Being romantically involved with two people at the same time while deceiving them. Cheating on a partner by dating another person. Being unfaithful in a relationship. Betraying the trust of one's partner. Engaging in a secret second relationship.
example_sentence: She ended the relationship after discovering his two-timing. His two-timing hurt everyone involved. Everyone was shocked when they learned about her two-timing. Trust is difficult to rebuild after two-timing in a relationship.

english_meaning: A person of great wealth, influence, or power who is prominent in a particular industry. They are typically leaders in the business world who have built vast empires. This term often refers to individuals who have achieved great success through entrepreneurship.
example_sentence: He became a real estate tycoon by the age of thirty. The movie follows the lives of industrial tycoons in the nineteenth century. The shipping tycoon donated millions of dollars to local charities. A media tycoon bought several television stations last year.

english_meaning: A powerful tropical cyclone that develops over warm ocean water in the western Pacific region, especially near East and Southeast Asia. It brings extremely strong winds, intense rainfall, storm surges, and can cause flooding and serious damage to coastal and inland areas. It is the same type of storm that is called a hurricane in the Atlantic Ocean and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean.
example_sentence: The typhoon destroyed many houses along the coast. Fishermen returned early because a typhoon was approaching the island. Heavy rain from the typhoon caused flooding in several villages. The government prepared emergency shelters before the typhoon arrived.

english_meaning: The art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and appealing when displayed. This involves the selection of typefaces, point sizes, line lengths, line-spacing, and letter-spacing. It is an essential component of graphic design and printing. Typography affects how a reader perceives information and the overall aesthetic of a document or website. It encompasses both the functional and artistic aspects of creating printed or digital text.
example_sentence: The book's elegant typography made it very easy and pleasant to read. Modern typography often experiments with bold colors and unconventional layouts. He studied the history of typography to understand how fonts have evolved. Good typography is essential for creating a professional brand identity. The website's clean typography improved the user experience significantly.

english_meaning: Exercising power in a cruel, unfair, or oppressive way. Someone or a government that rules or behaves with absolute authority, often oppressing others, showing harshness, and not allowing freedom or fairness.
example_sentence: The king’s tyrannical rule caused widespread fear. Employees suffered under a tyrannical manager. The dictator was known for his tyrannical policies. They protested against the tyrannical laws that limited freedom.

english_meaning: Cruel, oppressive, or unjust use of power. A government, ruler, or authority that exercises power in an oppressive, harsh, or unjust manner, often ignoring the rights of the people. It can also mean any situation where someone experiences severe and unfair control or domination.
example_sentence: The citizens revolted against the king's tyranny. Tyranny can take many forms, from political oppression to workplace abuse. People suffered under the tyranny of the dictator for decades. Education helps fight the tyranny of ignorance.

english_meaning: A cruel and oppressive ruler who exercises power in an arbitrary and often brutal manner. A person exercising power or control in a cruel, unreasonable, or arbitrary way. Historical usage refers to an absolute ruler unrestrained by law or constitution. In modern contexts, it can describe anyone who is bossy and domineering in personal or professional relationships. It often implies a lack of regard for the rights and feelings of others.
example_sentence: The citizens finally rose up to overthrow the cruel tyrant. My boss is a real tyrant who demands we work every weekend. Historically, the term tyrant was used for any ruler who seized power unconstitutionally. She felt like a tyrant for making her children clean their rooms for three hours. The young prince grew into a cold-hearted tyrant who ignored the suffering of his people.

english_meaning: The archaic or British English spelling of 'tire', referring to a rubber covering for a wheel. A thick, circular piece of rubber or metal placed around a wheel to provide traction and absorb shock. It typically consists of a casing reinforced with cords and filled with compressed air. The term also historically refers to the ancient Phoenician city of Tyre, a major seafaring and commercial center. In the context of vehicles, it is the essential component that makes contact with the road surface.
antonyms: ["Interior","Core","Center (Note: As a physical object","it lacks direct antonyms)"]
example_sentence: I need to replace the rear tyre because the tread is worn down. The mechanic checked the tyre pressure before the long journey. British English usually uses the spelling 'tyre' while American English uses 'tire'. The ancient city of Tyre was famous for its purple dye and maritime trade. A puncture in the tyre caused the car to swerve off the road.

english_meaning: A beginner or novice in learning any art, craft, or field of study. Someone who has just started to learn a particular skill and lacks experience. It implies a state of being at the very beginning of a journey toward proficiency. The word often carries a sense of enthusiasm but highlights a lack of seasoned judgment. It is used to describe students, apprentices, or hobbyists in their earliest stages.
example_sentence: As a tyro in the kitchen, he struggled even to boil an egg. Even a tyro can learn the basics of this software in a few hours. The music program is designed for everyone from the tyro to the seasoned professional. She approached her new job with the eagerness of a tyro. He was a mere tyro in the world of politics when he first ran for office.

english_meaning: A unit of weight used in the United States, equal to two thousand pounds or about 907 kilograms. Also called the short ton. A standard measure for heavy goods, freight, and industrial materials in America.
synonyms: ["Short ton","Two thousand pounds","Imperial weight unit","Net ton"]
example_sentence: The truck carried five US tons of steel. One US ton equals two thousand pounds. Freight charges are calculated per US ton. The factory produces thirty US tons of paper each week.

english_meaning: Present, appearing, or found everywhere. Present everywhere, seeming to appear in all places at the same time. Existing or being everywhere at the same time. Seeming to be everywhere or in several places at the same time.
example_sentence: The ubiquitous denim never goes out of fashion. Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society. Social media has become ubiquitous in daily life. The company’s logo is ubiquitous across the city.

english_meaning: One of the two long bones of the forearm, lying on the little-finger side. The forearm bone that forms the main hinge of the elbow joint. The bone whose upper end creates the bony point of the elbow. A long bone that runs parallel to the radius from the elbow to the wrist.
example_sentence: The blow to his arm fractured the shaft of the ulna. The pointed tip of the elbow is the upper end of the ulna. The ulna and radius work together to rotate the forearm. Doctors placed a metal plate along the broken ulna.

english_meaning: Of a reason for doing something hidden without admitting. (of a reason for doing something) that somebody keeps hidden and does not admit. A secret purpose or reason for doing something.
example_sentence: She must have some ulterior motive for being nice to me. Darkyn was always right; the sense he gave her to gauge when someone around her had an ulterior motive was tingling.

english_meaning: A hidden reason for doing something, often secret or dishonest. A purpose or reason behind an action that is not openly revealed. It often implies that someone has a secret agenda or personal interest that influences their behavior.
example_sentence: I can sense that you have an ulterior motive of some sort, she explained. He has submitted several applications everywhere with ulterior motive to defame me. He offered to help, but I suspected an ulterior motive. Her praise had an ulterior motive; she wanted a favor in return. Politicians sometimes have an ulterior motive behind charitable acts. Don’t assume everyone’s kindness is free of an ulterior motive

english_meaning: Being or happening at the end of a process. Final or conclusive. The best or most extreme instance of its kind. Fundamental or elemental.
example_sentence: Her ultimate goal is to become a chief surgeon. Winning the championship was the ultimate triumph for the team. Physics seeks to understand the ultimate constituents of matter. This luxury resort offers the ultimate vacation experience.

english_meaning: In the end or finally, after a long process or series of events. At the most basic or fundamental level.
example_sentence: Ultimately, the decision rests in the hands of the voters. Although there were delays, the project was ultimately successful. All these complex economic theories are ultimately about human behavior. She ultimately decided to study law instead of medicine.

english_meaning: A final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.
example_sentence: The management issued an ultimatum to the striking workers to return by Monday. She gave her landlord an ultimatum to fix the heater or she would move out. The government rejected the foreign power's aggressive ultimatum. Failing to comply with the ultimatum could lead to war.

english_meaning: Extremely or excessively. Beyond a usual limit or range. A person holding extreme political or social views. An extremist or radical. Of the most extreme kind or degree.
example_sentence: The new screen displays images in ultra-high definition. She completed an ultra-fast training session before work. Political ultras rejected the proposed compromise. The fabric is ultra soft and comfortable.

english_meaning: A person who gives opinions about subjects they do not properly understand. Someone who speaks confidently about matters outside their expertise or knowledge. It can describe a person who gives unnecessary advice or opinions on topics they do not fully understand. Comments, behavior, or opinions that go beyond one’s knowledge.
example_sentence: The television panel was full of ultracrepidarians discussing medical science without expertise. He sounded ultracrepidarian when he started giving legal advice despite never studying law. Social media often encourages ultracrepidarian opinions on complex global issues. The professor warned students not to become ultracredipitarian commentators on subjects they barely understood.

english_meaning: Extremely short in length, distance, duration, or wording. Relating to electromagnetic or radio waves with exceptionally short wavelengths. Designed to be completed in a very brief time.
example_sentence: The competition accepts ultrashort stories of fewer than one hundred words. Researchers generated an ultrashort pulse of laser light. The station once broadcast on an ultrashort radio frequency. She chose an ultrashort haircut for the summer.

english_meaning: Relating to sound waves with frequencies above the upper limit of human hearing, usually above 20,000 hertz. Producing, using, or detecting high-frequency sound. Operating by means of ultrasound.
example_sentence: Bats navigate by producing ultrasonic sounds. The technician used an ultrasonic device to find the hidden crack. Ultrasonic cleaning removed dirt from the delicate jewelry. Dogs can hear some ultrasonic frequencies that humans cannot.

english_meaning: Sound with a frequency above the range of human hearing. A medical imaging technique that uses high-frequency sound waves to create pictures inside the body. An image, scan, or examination produced by this technique. The use of ultrasonic waves for cleaning, testing, or treatment.
example_sentence: The doctor ordered an ultrasound to examine her abdomen. The ultrasound showed that the baby was developing normally. Engineers used ultrasound to detect faults inside the metal. Some dental instruments use ultrasound for cleaning.

english_meaning: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible violet light but longer than X-rays. Relating to or using this invisible radiation. A lamp, image, detector, or region of the spectrum involving ultraviolet radiation.
example_sentence: Ultraviolet radiation from the sun can damage unprotected skin. The bank uses ultraviolet light to check security markings. Bees can see patterns in the ultraviolet range. She wore sunglasses that block ultraviolet rays.

english_meaning: Clear in meaning and open to only one interpretation. Expressed so plainly that no confusion is possible. Free from doubt, vagueness, or double meaning. Definite and easy to understand. Leaving no room for misunderstanding.
example_sentence: The instructions were short and unambiguous. We need an unambiguous answer before we proceed. The contract uses unambiguous language about payment. Her refusal was polite but unambiguous.

english_meaning: In a way that is completely clear and open to only one meaning. Plainly and without any possibility of confusion. Definitely and without vagueness. In a manner that leaves no doubt for the listener or reader. Directly and precisely stated.
example_sentence: The minister unambiguously rejected the proposal. She stated her position unambiguously at the meeting. The rules unambiguously forbid late entries. He unambiguously denied any involvement in the deal.

english_meaning: Relating to or affecting the navel or the umbilical cord. It describes the vital connection point between a fetus and its mother during pregnancy. In a broader sense, it can refer to something that is central or fundamental to a connection.
example_sentence: The doctor checked the umbilical area for any signs of infection. The umbilical link between the mother and child is vital for nutrient exchange. Genetic material can be extracted from umbilical cells. The spaceship was connected to the station by an umbilical line.

english_meaning: A flexible cord-like structure containing blood vessels and attaching a human or other mammal fetus to the placenta during gestation. It is essential for providing nutrients and oxygen to the developing fetus. After birth, this structure is cut and eventually falls off to leave the navel.
example_sentence: The doctor carefully cut the umbilical cord after the baby was born. Nutrients are passed from the mother to the fetus through the umbilical cord. Stem cells can be harvested from the blood within the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord carries oxygenated blood to the developing infant.

english_meaning: A rounded knot or depression in the center of the abdomen which marks the site of attachment of the umbilical cord. In humans, it is more commonly known as the navel or belly button. It serves as a permanent scar representing the physical connection to the mother before birth.
example_sentence: The medical student identified the umbilicus during the anatomy lesson. The pain was centered right around the patient's umbilicus. After birth, the site where the cord was attached becomes the umbilicus. He noticed a small rash spreading from his umbilicus.

english_meaning: The fully shaded inner region of a shadow cast by an opaque object. The darkest part of a sunspot. A phantom or shadowy apparition. An uninvited guest accompanying a person who was invited. An overshadowing influence or presence.
example_sentence: During a total solar eclipse, observers must be within the umbra to see the sun completely covered. The telescope captured the intricate details of the dark umbra at the center of the sunspot. She felt as though she was living in the umbra of her famous sister's achievements. The ghost appeared as a faint umbra against the cold stone walls of the castle.

english_meaning: Offense, annoyance, or resentment caused by something someone has said or done. A feeling of being insulted or slighted. Displeasure taken at a remark or action perceived as disrespectful. Shade or shadow cast by trees (literary and old use).
example_sentence: He took umbrage at her comment about his work. She spoke carefully to avoid causing umbrage. Some members took umbrage when their names were left out. There was clear umbrage in his tone during the meeting.

english_meaning: Giving or providing shade; shady. Full of shade because of thick trees or foliage. Easily offended or quick to take offense; touchy (literary use).
example_sentence: We rested under an umbrageous old tree beside the river. The garden path was cool and umbrageous all afternoon. They chose an umbrageous corner of the park for the picnic. His umbrageous nature made honest discussion difficult.

english_meaning: A very large but indefinite number, countless or many. Used to describe something that happens or exists in a great number but is not specified exactly. It emphasizes abundance or repetition.
example_sentence: I have told you umpteen times to be careful. She received umpteen messages on her birthday. They have visited that place umpteen times this year. There are umpteen reasons why you should trust him. He made umpteen attempts to fix the machine, but it still didn’t work. There are umpteen reasons why I enjoy working here.

english_meaning: Not embarrassed, ashamed, or apologetic about something. Openly confident without shame. Showing no regret or hesitation about one's actions or beliefs.
example_sentence: She was unabashed about her ambition to become a leader. He gave an unabashed apology to no one. The unabashed fans cheered loudly for their team. He expressed his unabashed admiration for her work.

english_meaning: In a way that shows no embarrassment or shame. Doing something openly, confidently, and without feeling ashamed or embarrassed, even if others might judge it. It often shows boldness or complete self acceptance.
example_sentence: She unabashedly expressed her opinion in the meeting. He unabashedly asked for help when he needed it. The child laughed unabashedly at the funny scene. She unabashedly celebrated her success on social media.

english_meaning: Without becoming weaker or less intense. Continuing at full strength without reduction. Not decreasing in force or intensity.
example_sentence: The storm continued unabated throughout the night. His enthusiasm for work remained unabated. The rain fell unabated for three days. Public anger continued unabated after the scandal.

english_meaning: Not open to more than one interpretation. Having a clear and precise meaning that leaves no room for doubt or confusion. It describes communication, evidence, or instructions that are straightforward and certain. When a statement is unambiguous, its intent is perfectly transparent to any observer. It is a critical quality in legal documents, scientific data, and daily instructions.
example_sentence: The contract was written in unambiguous language to avoid any future disputes. Her answer was an unambiguous 'no' that left no room for negotiation. We need unambiguous evidence before we can make a final decision. The instructions for the exam were clear and unambiguous. His success was an unambiguous triumph for the entire community.

english_meaning: Formed from or characterized by the complete agreement of all parties involved. When a decision is unanimous, it means everyone has voted the same way or shares the same opinion. There are no dissenting voices or disagreements in such a situation.
example_sentence: The committee reached a unanimous decision to approve the proposal. The jury returned a unanimous verdict of not guilty. There was unanimous support for the new environmental policy. The school board was unanimous in its choice for the new principal.

english_meaning: In a way that is agreed upon by everyone involved without exception. This describes actions or decisions taken with the full consent of all members of a group. It implies total harmony and lack of opposition in the process.
example_sentence: The board members voted unanimously to increase the budget. The motion was passed unanimously by the city council. The critics unanimously praised the actress for her performance. The community unanimously agreed that the old park should be renovated.

english_meaning: To be impossible to dispute or disprove. Describing a position or argument that is so strong it cannot be defeated. Being protected or fortified enough to be secure from attack. Incapable of being doubted or questioned due to its clear truth. Solidly established and beyond any form of successful criticism.
example_sentence: The prosecutor built an unassailable case against the defendant with DNA evidence. After years of dominance, the champion's reputation remained unassailable in the ring. The fortress was built on a high cliff, making it practically unassailable by land. Her logic was so clear that her conclusions were deemed unassailable by the committee.

english_meaning: Lacking in confidence or the desire to express one's opinions or needs strongly. Describing a person who is modest, shy, or reluctant to put themselves forward. It often suggests a tendency to avoid conflict or to let others take the lead in social and professional situations. Being unassertive can be seen as either a sign of humility or a lack of self-assurance. It characteristically involves a quiet or submissive demeanor.
example_sentence: The unassertive student rarely raised her hand even when she knew the answer. He was so unassertive that his colleagues often took credit for his hard work. Being unassertive in a high-pressure sales job can be a major disadvantage. She is a talented artist but too unassertive to promote her own paintings. He gave an unassertive reply, hoping to avoid any further argument.

english_meaning: Showing no prejudice for or against something. Impartial and fair. Not influenced by personal feelings, interpretations, or prejudice. Based on objective facts rather than opinions.
example_sentence: The judge was praised for giving an unbiased opinion on the case. It is essential to conduct an unbiased study to get accurate results. A journalist should always provide unbiased news to the public. We need an unbiased witness to explain what actually happened.

english_meaning: Not in accordance with the teachings or principles of the Bible. Contrary to the scriptures or religious doctrine found in Christianity. Behavior or beliefs that are considered unholy or scripturally unsound.
example_sentence: The elders argued that the new policy was unbiblical and should be rejected. Many theologians criticized the book for its unbiblical stance on morality. Some people find certain modern traditions to be entirely unbiblical. He was accused of spreading unbiblical teachings among the congregation.

english_meaning: A person who arrives without being invited. Someone who comes uninvited and is often unwelcome. An unexpected visitor who appears without warning.
example_sentence: An unbidden guest arrived just as dinner was served. Nobody enjoys an unbidden guest at a private function. He felt like an unbidden guest at the family gathering. The manager politely asked the unbidden guest to leave.

english_meaning: To remove a flaw, stain, or mark from something. To clear something of fault or imperfection. To restore a clean and spotless condition. Rarely used form; the adjective 'unblemished' is far more common in modern English.
example_sentence: The polish helped to unblemish the old wooden table. Nothing could unblemish his damaged reputation. She tried to unblemish the surface of the painting. Time alone cannot unblemish such a serious mistake.

english_meaning: Having no marks, spots, or stains. Perfect and without any fault or damage. Free from moral fault, guilt, or criticism. Describing a record or reputation with nothing negative in it.
example_sentence: He retired after an unblemished career of thirty years. The apple looked fresh and unblemished. Her unblemished record helped her win the promotion. The old car has an unblemished paint finish.

english_meaning: Not controlled or restrained in any way. Unconstrained or uncontrolled especially in terms of emotions or passions. Lacking a bridle or harness, as in a horse. Given free rein without any limitations or boundaries.
example_sentence: Her unbridled enthusiasm for the project inspired the entire team. The unbridled horse galloped across the open fields with sudden speed. Years of unbridled competition eventually led to a collapse in market prices. He spoke with unbridled honesty about the challenges he faced during the war.

english_meaning: Strange and mysterious in a way that is hard to explain. So remarkable that it seems beyond normal ability. Causing an unsettling feeling of the supernatural. Surprisingly accurate or precise. Weirdly familiar yet unnatural at the same time.
example_sentence: She has an uncanny ability to remember names. There was an uncanny silence in the empty hall. His resemblance to his grandfather is uncanny. The old house had an uncanny atmosphere at night.

english_meaning: To sell goods or services at a lower price than a competitor. To weaken or damage something, especially another person's position or efforts. To cut away material from the underside of something. In sport, to strike a ball with a backward spin, or to deliver an upward blow.
example_sentence: Local shops cannot survive if big stores keep undercutting them. His public remarks undercut the minister's authority. The carpenter undercut the edge to create a shadow line. The river has undercut the bank over many years.

english_meaning: Not able to be relied on or known for sure. Feeling doubt or showing a lack of confidence. Subject to change or likely to vary. Not clearly or precisely determined. Having an unknown outcome or consequence.
example_sentence: The weather forecast remains uncertain for the upcoming weekend. She was uncertain about which path to take in her career. The economic situation has left many investors feeling uncertain. The future of the old building is still uncertain due to legal issues.

english_meaning: In a way that shows doubt or lack of confidence. Hesitantly, without being sure about what to do. In an unsteady or wavering manner. Without a clear or firm decision. In a way that suggests something is not fixed or reliable.
example_sentence: He smiled uncertainly when asked about his plans. She stepped uncertainly onto the icy path. The child looked uncertainly at the crowd of strangers. They waited uncertainly for the manager's decision.

english_meaning: Not able to compete successfully with others, especially in business. Too expensive or of too poor quality to compete in the market. Not interested in competing or lacking a desire to win.
example_sentence: High wages made the factory uncompetitive in export markets. Their prices are uncompetitive compared with online stores. He is a talented but uncompetitive player. The old technology left the firm uncompetitive.

english_meaning: Unwilling to make concessions or to change one's principles or viewpoints. Showing an inflexible and determined attitude even in the face of pressure. This term describes a person or a stance that refuses to meet halfway or enter into a bargain that sacrifices core beliefs. It is often used to characterize high standards, strict morality, or intense political resolve. In an artistic context, it refers to work that does not cater to popular tastes or commercial interests.
example_sentence: She is known for her uncompromising stance on human rights issues. The architect had an uncompromising vision for the new skyscraper. Their uncompromising attitude made it impossible to reach a settlement. Despite the criticism, the director maintained his uncompromising artistic style. The company has an uncompromising commitment to quality and safety.

english_meaning: A lack of worry, anxiety, or interest in something. The state of being indifferent to or untroubled by something. A casual disregard for something that others would consider important.
example_sentence: His unconcern for the opinions of others allowed him to live freely and authentically. She masked her anxiety with an air of studied unconcern. The child played with apparent unconcern while the adults argued loudly nearby. His unconcern about the deadline alarmed his supervisor considerably. Her unconcern for material possessions gave her a remarkable freedom from financial anxiety.

english_meaning: Not in accordance with the constitution of a country or organisation. Violating the fundamental principles or rules laid down by a constitution. Contrary to established legal or governing principles.
example_sentence: The court declared the new law unconstitutional. Detaining a citizen without charge is unconstitutional. Many experts described the order as unconstitutional. The judges struck down the amendment as unconstitutional.

english_meaning: Freedom from limits, rules, or restrictions. A state of being unrestrained or free to act. Absence of self-control or reserve. Liberty of thought or action without any restraint. A relaxed and open manner of behavior.
example_sentence: The children played with complete unconstraint in the park. She spoke with unconstraint about her personal life. The artist worked with unconstraint and passion. His unconstraint made everyone feel comfortable around him.

english_meaning: Not cause for dispute or disagreement. Generally accepted and unlikely to provoke conflict or debate. Safe, mild, and accepted by most people without opposition.
example_sentence: The proposal was accepted quickly because it was largely uncontroversial. She chose an uncontroversial topic for her presentation to avoid arguments. The candidate kept his public statements safe and uncontroversial. Park safety is an uncontroversial issue that all residents support.

english_meaning: Not based on or conforming to what is generally done or accepted. Original, unorthodox, or out of the ordinary. Departing from established rules, traditions, or social standards.
example_sentence: She had an unconventional teaching style that resonated well with the students. His unconventional approach to business led to remarkable success. They decided to hold an unconventional wedding on a secluded beach. The artist was famous for using unconventional materials in her sculptures.

english_meaning: The quality or state of being unconventional. Behavior, style, or opinion that does not conform to established rules, traditions, or social standards. An instance of unique or original conduct.
example_sentence: Her unconventionality in dress made her stand out in the crowd. The artist was famous for the unconventionality of his techniques. Despite the unconventionality of their approach, they achieved great success. She embraced her unconventionality and refused to conform to social expectations.

english_meaning: Not persuaded or certain about something. Having doubts or reservations regarding a claim, statement, or idea.
example_sentence: Despite his detailed explanation, she remained unconvinced. The jury was unconvinced by the defendant's weak alibi. He listened to the pitch but walked away unconvinced. Skeptical scientists are still unconvinced by the preliminary findings.

english_meaning: Free from dishonesty, bribery, or moral wrongdoing. Honest and morally upright in conduct. Not spoiled, altered, or damaged from its original state. Pure and untainted by harmful influence.
example_sentence: The city needs an uncorrupt and efficient administration. He was known as an uncorrupt judge throughout his career. The backup files remained uncorrupt after the crash. Her uncorrupt character earned wide respect.

english_meaning: Rude or lacking good manners. A person, behavior or speech that is socially awkward, rude or not polished. It often refers to a lack of refinement, cultural awareness or basic etiquette in public or social settings.
example_sentence: His uncouth behavior embarrassed everyone at the dinner table. She found his uncouth remarks offensive and unnecessary. The manager warned him to stop his uncouth language at work. Despite his intelligence, his uncouth manners hurt his reputation.

english_meaning: In a rude or awkward way. In a manner that shows poor manners, lack of social grace, or ignorance of accepted behavior
example_sentence: He spoke uncouthly at the formal meeting and embarrassed his team. The guest behaved uncouthly during dinner. She laughed uncouthly without caring about others. Acting uncouthly can damage your professional image.

english_meaning: Not discouraged by difficulty, danger, or failure. Remaining brave and determined despite problems. Showing courage that is not weakened by fear. Continuing with confidence in the face of opposition. Firm in purpose even after setbacks.
example_sentence: Undaunted by the rain, they continued the march. She remained undaunted after her first rejection. The team was undaunted by the stronger opponents. He carried on undaunted despite many warnings.

english_meaning: An eleven-sided polygon with eleven angles. A geometric shape with eleven straight sides and eleven vertices. Any flat shape with eleven corners and eleven edges.
example_sentence: A regular undecagon has eleven equal sides and angles. The rare coin featured an undecagonal shape. Constructing an undecagon requires advanced geometric knowledge. The sum of interior angles in an undecagon is 1620 degrees.

english_meaning: Being shot at with weapons. Facing strong criticism or attack from others. In a situation of great pressure or scrutiny. Being blamed publicly for something. Exposed to hostile action or comment.
example_sentence: The soldiers came under fire near the border. The minister has come under fire for his recent remarks. Her decisions are under fire from the media. The company is under fire over pollution complaints.

english_meaning: With official permission granted by an authority or rights holder. Subject to the terms and conditions of a legal license. Produced, sold, used, or operated with authorized consent.
example_sentence: The medicine is manufactured under license in several countries. This software may be used only under license. The café sells the branded products under license. Local firms operate the service under license from the government.

english_meaning: Something happening very close to someone or in a very obvious way, yet the person does not notice it. Clearly visible but unnoticed. Happening openly. Extremely close. Easy to find but overlooked.
synonyms: ["In plain sight","Right in front of someone","Nearby","Obvious","Within sight"]
example_sentence: The keys were lying under my nose the whole time. The thief worked right under the police officer's nose. She searched everywhere for her glasses, but they were under her nose on the table. Important clues were hidden under our noses from the beginning.

english_meaning: With the support, protection, or sponsorship of a person or organisation. Being organised or carried out with official backing. Under the guidance and authority of someone.
synonyms: ["Under the patronage of","Sponsored by","Supported by","Backed by","Under the aegis of"]
example_sentence: The seminar was arranged under the auspices of the health ministry. Relief work continued under the auspices of the United Nations. The tournament is held under the auspices of the sports board. Research was carried out under the auspices of a private foundation.

english_meaning: Under suspicion, disapproval, or difficulty. In a state of trouble or disgrace. Facing suspicion or bad reputation. Being viewed with doubt by others. In an unfavorable situation.
example_sentence: He left the company under a cloud of suspicion. She has been under a cloud since the incident last month. The politician resigned under a cloud. The team is playing under the cloud of last year's scandal.

english_meaning: In a state of great distress, hardship, or suffering. Being subjected to constant pressure, torment, or persecution. Undergoing painful trials or severe difficulties. Living under oppressive circumstances that give no relief.
example_sentence: Ever since he lost his job, the family has been under the harrow. Small farmers were under the harrow during the long drought. She has been under the harrow of debt for years. The prisoners lived under the harrow of daily cruelty.

english_meaning: Secretly, illegally, or without others knowing, especially about money or deals. Often used to describe bribes, illegal payments, or actions done without official record.
example_sentence: They paid him under the table to avoid taxes. He was paid under the table to keep quiet. The manager was caught taking money under the table from suppliers. He made a deal under the table to get the contract approved. They bought the land under the table, without any official paperwork.

english_meaning: To feel unwell, sick, or not in a normal healthy state. Sometimes also used when someone feels sad, tired, or not at their best.
example_sentence: I didn’t go to work today because I was feeling under the weather. She looked a bit under the weather, so I asked her to rest at home. After eating too much junk food, he felt under the weather all night. I think he’s under the weather; he seems very tired and quiet today.

english_meaning: Kept secret or concealed from the public. Held in a state of strict privacy or confidentiality. Hidden away to prevent discovery or premature disclosure. Maintained in a suppressed or unrevealed condition.
example_sentence: The company kept its new product under wrap until the official launch day. They managed to keep the details of the surprise party completely under wrap. The military project was kept strictly under wrap for national security reasons. Please keep this information under wrap until we are ready to announce it.

english_meaning: To estimate something to be smaller or less important than it actually is. To fail to guess or understand the real cost, size, or difficulty of something. To consider someone to be less capable or intelligent than they really are. An estimate that is less than the true or actual value. A judgment that is too low regarding the ability or worth of someone or something.
example_sentence: Never underestimate the power of a dedicated team. The government underestimated the cost of the new healthcare project. She tends to underestimate her own abilities when applying for jobs. His initial underestimate of the required materials caused a major delay.

english_meaning: To erode the base or foundation of a structure, often literally by digging beneath it. Figuratively, it means to lessen the effectiveness, power, or ability of someone or something, especially gradually or insidiously. It is frequently used in the context of authority, confidence, or reputations where subtle actions cause slow damage. To subvert or weaken someone's position through secret or underhanded means. It can also refer to physical wearing away, such as water undermining a river bank.
example_sentence: Frequent scandals began to undermine the public's trust in the government. The heavy rain started to undermine the stability of the cliffside. Constant criticism can undermine a student's self-confidence. Secret leaks were intended to undermine the senator's re-election campaign. Small errors in the report eventually undermine the credibility of the entire study.

english_meaning: The act of eroding, weakening, or damaging something gradually and secretly. To weaken or destabilise something or someone in an insidious or subtle way. Digging beneath a structure to cause it to collapse.
example_sentence: His constant criticism was undermining her confidence in her own abilities. The flooding had been steadily undermining the foundations of the old building for years. She accused her colleague of deliberately undermining her efforts in front of management. The campaign focused on undermining public trust in the institution rather than offering solutions.

english_meaning: Not enjoying the same standard of living or rights as the majority of people in a society. Lacking the fundamental resources, advantages, or opportunities available to others. Often refers to those living in poverty or social disadvantage.
example_sentence: The charity focuses on providing education to underprivileged children in rural areas. Many underprivileged families struggle to access basic healthcare services. She dedicated her life to improving the living conditions of the underprivileged. The government has launched a new scheme to support underprivileged students.

english_meaning: To describe something as smaller, less important, or less serious than it actually is. To express something with less emphasis or force than the facts warrant. To deliberately minimise or downplay something.
example_sentence: To say the project was a challenge would be to massively understate the difficulty involved. The report seemed to understate the severity of the environmental damage caused. He has a habit of understating his own achievements out of modesty. She understated the cost of the renovation, which led to budget problems later.

english_meaning: A statement that describes something as less important, serious, or impressive than it really is. The act of presenting something in a restrained or modest way. A style of expression marked by deliberate restraint.
example_sentence: Calling the storm a little wind was a huge understatement. He described the loss as unfortunate, which was an understatement. British humour often relies on understatement. To say she was pleased is an understatement.

english_meaning: A person whose profession is to prepare dead bodies for burial or cremation and to manage funerals. While the term 'funeral director' is now more common in professional settings, 'undertaker' remains the traditional term for this role. It historically referred to anyone who 'undertakes' a task, but the specialized sense of funeral arrangements became dominant in the 17th century. An undertaker's duties include embalming, arranging the service, and providing transportation for the deceased. Modern usage is almost exclusively limited to the mortuary profession.
example_sentence: The undertaker arrived quietly to transport the body to the funeral home. He spoke to the undertaker about the specific arrangements for his father's burial. The old building on the corner had been the town's primary undertaker for decades. An undertaker must possess great empathy and organizational skills. They requested the undertaker to provide a simple, wooden casket for the ceremony.

english_meaning: To fail to impress or excite someone who expected more. To leave someone feeling disappointed or indifferent because a performance or object was lackluster. It is a humorous or sarcastic back-formation from 'overwhelm,' suggesting a lack of impact where impact was anticipated. The term is used when something is competent but thoroughly ordinary and yields no enthusiasm. It describes a feeling of being 'meh' or unimpressed by a hyped experience.
example_sentence: The fancy new restaurant's food was decent, but the tiny portions tended to underwhelm the diners. I was really looking forward to the movie, but the predictable plot managed to underwhelm me. Despite the high price tag, the latest smartphone model seemed to underwhelm tech critics. The team's performance last night did nothing but underwhelm the home fans. His speech was so generic that it left the entire audience feeling quite underwhelmed.

english_meaning: A secret or hidden world of criminal activity or organized crime. A society or community that exists outside the law. The world of the dead or the criminal world. The world beneath the surface of the earth, especially imagined as the place of the dead (in mythology or religion).
example_sentence: The police are trying to control the city’s underworld. He has connections with the criminal underworld. Legends say the hero traveled to the underworld and returned alive. In Greek mythology, Hades ruled the underworld where souls of the dead lived.

english_meaning: Not causing great damage, destruction, or ruin. Not causing severe shock, distress, or grief. Describes an event, force, or piece of news that lacks overwhelming or catastrophic impact, being manageable or minor in its effect.
example_sentence: The storm, though predicted to be a hurricane, was ultimately undevastating to the coastal town. For a seasoned investor, a small dip in the market is an undevastating event. The news of the project's delay was disappointing but undevastating to their overall plans. He found the critique of his work surprisingly undevastating; it was actually quite helpful.

english_meaning: To cancel or reverse something that has already been done. To loosen, untie, or open something that is tied, fastened, or closed. To cause someone or something to fail, collapse, or be ruined. To open buttons, zippers, belts, or other fastenings on clothes. To free someone or something from a tie, restraint, or restriction. To make something ineffective or cancel its effect.
example_sentence: Please undo the changes before saving the document. She carefully undid the ribbon around the gift. One careless mistake could undo years of hard work. He undid his seat belt after the car stopped.

english_meaning: Having a wavelike motion or form. It describes something that moves, or is shaped, in a smooth, rising and falling pattern, much like waves on water. The term can apply to physical movement, visual patterns, or even sound, such as the undulant terrain of rolling hills.
example_sentence: The snake moved with an undulant motion through the tall grass. We drove through an undulant landscape of rolling green hills. The dancer's arms created an undulant pattern in the air. A gentle, undulant breeze stirred the surface of the lake.

english_meaning: To dig something up from the ground, especially by excavation. To discover something that was hidden, secret, or lost, often after a careful search. It can refer to physically finding an object in the earth or to uncovering new information or facts.
example_sentence: Archaeologists managed to unearth an ancient temple. A reporter unearthed evidence of widespread corruption. While cleaning the attic, she unearthed a box of her grandmother's old letters. Further research might unearth the real reason for his disappearance.

english_meaning: A very inconvenient time, usually very early or very late. An hour at which people are not normally awake. An unreasonably odd time of day or night. A time considered unsuitable for activity.
example_sentence: The phone rang at some unearthly hour of the night. We had to leave at an unearthly hour to catch the flight. Why are you studying at this unearthly hour? He came home at an unearthly hour again.

english_meaning: A very early or very late hour that seems inconvenient or unnatural. An extremely inconvenient time to be awake. A time considered too early or too late for normal activity. A strange or unusual time of day. An hour when most people are asleep.
example_sentence: He called me at some unearthly hour of the night. The flight was scheduled at an unearthly hour. She wakes up at an unearthly hour to exercise. Who would visit at such an unearthly hour?

english_meaning: Clear, definite, leaving no doubt. Something that is completely clear and unambiguous. It expresses a meaning or opinion in a way that cannot be misunderstood or doubted.
example_sentence: The manager gave an unequivocal answer about the company policy. Her support for the project was unequivocal. The evidence provided an unequivocal proof of his innocence. He made an unequivocal statement that he would not resign.

english_meaning: Always right and accurate in every detail. Incapable of making a mistake or being wrong. Characterized by a constant reliability and lack of error. Consistently precise in judgement, action, or prediction. Perfectly suited to its purpose without fail. Faultless and unfailing in performance.
example_sentence: She has an unerring instinct for finding the best bargains in any store. His unerring aim allowed him to hit the target from a great distance every single time. The detective followed the clues with an unerring sense of logic. Despite the chaos, the pilot maintained unerring focus on the landing strip.

english_meaning: Not morally right or acceptable. Against the accepted rules of a profession or society. Dishonest or unfair in behavior. Involving practices that violate moral standards. Contrary to principles of good conduct.
example_sentence: It is unethical to cheat during examinations. The doctor was punished for his unethical behavior. Spreading false news is completely unethical. Many companies avoid unethical business practices.

english_meaning: Not smooth, level, or flat in surface. Not equal or fairly balanced in amount or quality. Varying in standard, with good and bad parts. Not regular in pattern or arrangement.
example_sentence: The road to the village is rough and uneven. It was an uneven contest between the two teams. The film received mixed reviews because of its uneven script. The bricks were laid on uneven ground.

english_meaning: In a way that is not smooth, level, or flat. Not equally or fairly distributed. In an inconsistent manner, with varying quality. At irregular intervals or amounts.
example_sentence: The paint was spread unevenly across the wall. Wealth is unevenly distributed in many countries. The cake baked unevenly in the old oven. His performance has been rather unevenly judged.

english_meaning: Not expected or regarded as likely to happen. Coming without warning or prior notice. Surprising because it was not anticipated. Something that occurs suddenly or out of the blue. Not looked for or foreseen.
example_sentence: The sudden rainstorm was completely unexpected by the hikers. She received an unexpected phone call from an old friend. The news of his resignation was totally unexpected by the board members. We had to deal with several unexpected expenses this month.

english_meaning: Impossible to understand. Too deep to be measured. Incapable of being fully comprehended by the human mind. Beyond the reach of thought, reason, or knowledge. Used for mysteries, emotions, or depths that cannot be grasped.
example_sentence: The universe is vast and unfathomable to the human mind. Her grief at losing her child was unfathomable. The ocean's deepest trenches remain unfathomable even today. His sudden change of behaviour was unfathomable to his friends. There is an unfathomable mystery surrounding the ancient ruins.

english_meaning: Not disconcerted or distressed. Remaining calm and composed despite unexpected or unpleasant developments. Showing no sign of worry or nervousness in a difficult situation.
example_sentence: Despite the loud boos from the crowd, the athlete remained unfazed. She seemed completely unfazed by the sudden change in plans. He remained unfazed even when he was told the project had been canceled. The experienced pilot was unfazed by the severe turbulence during the flight.

english_meaning: To not pretend or fake; to be sincere and truthful in feelings or actions. To act without deception or false appearance. To show genuine emotion rather than a false one.
example_sentence: He tried to unfeign his true feelings toward her. She could not unfeign her disappointment any longer. They urged him to unfeign and speak honestly. It is hard to unfeign joy when you feel sad.

english_meaning: Genuine, sincere, and not pretended. Real and heartfelt in emotion or expression. Truthful and without any false show. Coming honestly from the heart.
example_sentence: She thanked him with unfeigned gratitude. His unfeigned surprise made everyone laugh. The children showed unfeigned joy at the gift. He spoke with unfeigned admiration for his teacher.

english_meaning: Remaining calm and composed even under great pressure. Not easily upset or confused. Showing a persistent coolness of spirit in difficult situations. Characterized by steadiness and an inability to be rattled. Possessing an even-tempered nature that resists emotional outbursts.
example_sentence: Despite the chaotic surroundings of the emergency room, the head nurse remained entirely unflappable. His unflappable demeanor during the intense interrogation impressed the detectives. She proved to be an unflappable pilot when the engine malfunctioned mid-flight. Even when the crowd began to jeer, the speaker stayed unflappable and finished his address.

english_meaning: Not to show fear, hesitation, or weakness in the face of danger, difficulty, or pain. To remain firm, brave, and steady when others might shrink. To describe courageous and unwavering behaviour.
example_sentence: He stood unflinching in the face of harsh criticism. The soldiers remained unflinching under heavy fire. She gave an unflinching reply to the difficult question. His unflinching loyalty impressed everyone. The reporter delivered an unflinching account of the war.

english_meaning: To open or spread out something that has been folded. To make information, plans, or feelings known. To happen or become clear step by step. To stretch or expand into full form. To present information clearly and completely. To occur as a series of events.
example_sentence: She unfolded the letter and began to read it carefully. As the meeting unfolded, everyone understood the real problem. The flowers unfolded their petals in the morning sunlight. He unfolded his future plans during the presentation.

english_meaning: Something that happens unexpectedly or without being predicted. An event, situation or outcome that was not expected, planned or imagined. It describes something that appears suddenly and takes people by surprise because there was no prior indication that it would happen.
example_sentence: The project was running late owing to unforeseen circumstances. There are almost always unforeseen consequences for any major endeavor. Unforeseen problems delayed the project beyond its deadline. This was a sudden and unforeseen blow. Due to unforeseen circumstances the cost of the improvements has risen by twenty per cent.

english_meaning: Not willing or inclined to forgive or show mercy to someone who has done wrong. Harsh or hostile in nature, particularly in terms of environment or conditions. Allowing very little margin for error or weakness. Not yielding or easily softened in judgment or physical properties.
example_sentence: The desert is an unforgiving environment for those who are unprepared. She found the teacher to be unforgiving when it came to late assignments. The high-speed race track is known for its unforgiving curves. His unforgiving attitude toward his former business partner lasted for decades.

english_meaning: Awkward; clumsy. Describes a person or animal that moves in a way that is not graceful or controlled. It can also describe an object that is difficult to handle or manage because of its size, shape, or weight.
example_sentence: The newborn giraffe was ungainly, with its long legs stumbling at every step. He moved with an ungainly gait, as if his limbs didn't quite belong to him. She tried to carry the large, ungainly box up the stairs by herself. Penguins look rather ungainly when they waddle on land.

english_meaning: To ignore or pay no attention to something or someone. To deliberately disregard advice, warnings, rules, or any form of guidance. It implies a conscious choice to not notice or act on something that deserves attention.
example_sentence: Her warning went unheeded. He unheeded the safety warnings and climbed the mountain anyway. The students unheeded the teacher’s instructions and submitted the wrong assignment. She unheeded the advice of her friends and made a risky investment. Many drivers unheeded the traffic signals, causing a minor accident.

english_meaning: Impossible to recognize, name, or identify. Not able to be distinguished or known for what it is. So damaged, changed, or unclear that its identity cannot be determined. Lacking any distinctive features that would allow recognition. Unknown in origin, source, or nature.
example_sentence: The body was so badly burned that it was unidentifiable. A strange, unidentifiable smell drifted from the kitchen. The old photograph had faded until the faces were unidentifiable. Investigators found several unidentifiable objects at the crash site.

english_meaning: Made into a single entity; combined. It signifies the process of bringing together separate parts to form a coherent and single whole. This can refer to the integration of people, countries, systems, or ideas into a harmonious unit.
example_sentence: The separate kingdoms were eventually brought together into a single, unified empire. The company presented a unified brand identity across all its products. Our goal is to create a unified system that is easy for everyone to use. Despite their differences, the members were unified in their desire for change.

english_meaning: To make or become a single unit. To bring together different parts or elements to form a cohesive whole. This action often involves creating harmony, agreement, or a single entity from previously separate components. For example, a shared vision can unify a group of people.
example_sentence: The new president's first task was to unify the divided nation. A common language can unify people from different cultural backgrounds. The goal of the treaty is to unify the two economies. Their shared experience of hardship helped to unify the community. The director used a consistent visual style to unify the film's disparate scenes.

english_meaning: Involving or affecting only one side or party. Something that is done, decided, or performed by one person, group, or country without the agreement, cooperation, or consultation of others. Often refers to decisions, actions, or agreements that do not consider other parties’ input.
example_sentence: The company made a unilateral decision to cut costs without consulting employees. A unilateral declaration of independence shocked the international community. He took unilateral action to resolve the dispute. Unilateral sanctions were imposed by the government.

english_meaning: A policy or action taken by a single country, group, or person without seeking the agreement or support of others. Acting independently, especially in international relations, without consulting or cooperating with allies or other parties.
example_sentence: The government’s decision to impose sanctions was an act of unilateralism. Unilateralism often creates tension in international relations. Critics argue that unilateralism ignores the importance of global cooperation. The leader’s unilateralism damaged the trust of neighboring countries.

english_meaning: Not causing admiration or respect. Failing to make a strong or favourable impression. Ordinary, dull, or disappointing in quality. Lacking any remarkable feature.
example_sentence: His performance in the interview was unimpressive. The hotel looked small and unimpressive from outside. Critics found the film unimpressive and slow. The results were unimpressive despite months of work.

english_meaning: Expressing one's feelings or thoughts frankly without restraint. Describing behavior that is natural, open, and not restricted by social conventions. Lacking a sense of self-consciousness or embarrassment in public. Not restricted, blocked, or held back by physical or psychological barriers. Characterized by a spontaneous and carefree manner of acting.
example_sentence: She gave an uninhibited laugh that echoed through the quiet hallway. The artist's uninhibited style was evident in his bold and messy brushstrokes. Children are often uninhibited in their curiosity about the world around them. They danced with an uninhibited joy that inspired everyone at the party.

english_meaning: Not able to be understood. Unclear, confused, garbled, or impossible to make sense of. Difficult to hear, read, interpret, or explain.
example_sentence: The message was unintelligible after the signal failed. His handwriting is almost unintelligible. The lecture became unintelligible when the microphone stopped working. She spoke too quickly, and her words were unintelligible. Technical reports can be unintelligible without definitions.

english_meaning: Not planned, meant, or desired. Occurring accidentally or as an unforeseen result. Designed for someone or something else. Conveying a meaning that the speaker did not mean to express.
example_sentence: The tax produced unintended consequences. She was the unintended recipient of the email. His words caused unintended offense. The medicine may have unintended side effects.

english_meaning: Not done deliberately or by conscious choice. Happening accidentally, inadvertently, or without a planned purpose. Causing an effect that the person did not mean to cause.
example_sentence: The omission was unintentional. His unintentional joke made everyone laugh. An unintentional error changed the final total. The new rule had unintentional effects on small businesses.

english_meaning: Without intending or planning to do something. Accidentally or inadvertently. In a way that produces an unforeseen or unwanted result.
example_sentence: I unintentionally deleted the message. Her comment unintentionally embarrassed him. The policy unintentionally excluded some applicants. He unintentionally revealed the surprise.

english_meaning: Not interested in or concerned about something. Showing no curiosity, attention, enthusiasm, or desire to participate. Impartial or free from personal interest, though disinterested is often preferred for this meaning.
example_sentence: She seemed uninterested in the discussion. The children were uninterested in sitting indoors. He gave an uninterested shrug and walked away. We need an uninterested observer to judge the dispute fairly.

english_meaning: The quality or state of not being interested or curious; a lack of concern or engagement. Uninterestedness refers to an absence of personal involvement, enthusiasm, or attraction towards a subject, person, or activity. It is often characterized by apathy or a sense of detachment.
example_sentence: His uninterestedness in the family business was a great disappointment to his father. The teacher noticed the student's uninterestedness and tried a new way to explain the lesson. She feigned uninterestedness, but her eyes gave away her deep curiosity. The politician's speech was met with a wave of public uninterestedness. Her air of calm uninterestedness was just a mask for her anxiety.

english_meaning: Not attracting or holding attention. Dull, boring, ordinary, or lacking appeal. Offering little novelty, importance, variety, or stimulation.
example_sentence: The lecture became uninteresting after an hour. He found the plot predictable and uninteresting. An uninteresting title can discourage readers. The plain room looked clean but uninteresting.

english_meaning: The act of joining two or more things or people together to form a single whole. An organized group of workers formed to protect their rights and interests. A group of states or countries joined together under one government or agreement. The state of being married or the relationship between two people living together. A club or association formed by people with a shared purpose, especially in a college or university.
example_sentence: The workers joined a union to demand better wages. Their marriage was a happy union of two very different families. The union of the two companies created a global business. He was elected president of the students' union.

english_meaning: Suitable for both sexes; not gender-specific. The term refers to things like clothing, hairstyles, or facilities that are designed to be used or worn by both males and females. This approach promotes inclusivity and breaks away from traditional gender roles in fashion and design.
example_sentence: The new salon on the corner is a unisex establishment. Many modern fragrances are unisex, appealing to both men and women. He prefers to shop for unisex clothing because he likes the looser fit. The university is installing more unisex restrooms in its new buildings.

english_meaning: Having only one sex, relating to or characteristic of one sex only. Refers to organisms, plants, or animals that are either male or female, but not both. In biology, unisexual species produce gametes of a single sex only. It can also describe flowers or plants that have either male or female reproductive organs, not both.
example_sentence: Some plants are unisexual, producing only male or female flowers. Humans are typically unisexual, with distinct male and female sexes. The study focused on unisexual species of fish. Certain unisexual flowers rely on insects for pollination.

english_meaning: The state of being joined together or in agreement as one whole. Harmony and agreement between people, groups, or nations. The quality of being united in purpose, feeling, or action. A single, complete thing formed from separate parts. Consistency and balance among the different parts of a work of art or piece of writing.
example_sentence: The leader called for national unity in a time of crisis. There was a strong sense of unity among the team members. Unity in the family helped them survive difficult years. The painting has a remarkable unity of colour and form.

english_meaning: Relating to, affecting, or done by all people or things in the world or in a particular group. True or valid in all cases, places, and times. Existing everywhere or covering all situations without exception. Suitable for or able to be used in many different situations or with many different devices. A general principle, idea, or characteristic that applies to everyone or everything.
example_sentence: Access to clean drinking water should be a universal right. Music is often described as a universal language. The charger comes with a universal adapter for all devices. Kindness is a universal value found in every culture.

english_meaning: By everyone or in every case, without exception. In all places and at all times. In a way that applies to all people, groups, or situations. Widely and generally, as accepted by all concerned.
example_sentence: The proposal was universally welcomed by the members. His novels are universally admired by critics. This symbol is universally recognised as a sign of danger. The rule is not universally applied in every branch.

english_meaning: Impossible to defend or explain as reasonable, fair, or acceptable. Not supported by a valid reason.
example_sentence: The violence was cruel and unjustifiable. The company called the price increase unjustifiable. His absence without notice was unjustifiable. There is no unjustifiable reason for treating staff unfairly.

english_meaning: To untie a knot. To loosen or undo something that is knotted or tangled. To remove the knots from something such as rope, hair, thread, or muscles. To relax or ease something that feels tight or tense, including emotional tension. Unknot means to free something from being twisted, tied, or tangled, whether it refers to a physical knot in a string or a figurative tightness in the body or feelings.
