example_sentence: A white vapour trail stretched across the blue sky. The jet left a long vapour trail behind it. Cold air helped the vapour trail remain visible for several minutes. We watched two vapour trails cross above the airport.

english_meaning: Software or hardware announced publicly but never released. A technology product promoted long before it becomes available. A promised product that remains unfinished, delayed, or imaginary.
example_sentence: The much-advertised game became vapourware after years of delays. Customers were skeptical that the device was more than vapourware. The company denied that its new operating system was vapourware. Investors lost interest when the promised product remained vapourware.

english_meaning: Wanting or devouring great quantities of food. It also refers to having a very eager approach to an activity, such as reading or learning. It denotes an insatiable appetite or enthusiasm for something.
example_sentence: The boy had a voracious appetite after playing soccer all afternoon. She is a voracious reader who finishes three books every week. The voracious reader devoured the entire fantasy series in less than a month. His voracious desire for knowledge drove him to study late into the night.

english_meaning: The quality or degree of being likely to change. The amount of difference among values, people, objects, or conditions. In statistics, the extent to which data points differ from one another. The capacity to vary over time or across situations.
example_sentence: Weather variability makes long-term planning difficult. The study measured variability in students' test scores. Genetic variability helps a species adapt to change. There is considerable variability in the quality of these materials.

english_meaning: Not consistent or having a fixed pattern. Able to be changed or adapted. A quantity that may assume different values. Changing frequently or unpredictably. Something that varies or is capable of varying.
example_sentence: The weather has been very variable this week. Prices are variable and depend on demand. In this equation, x is the variable. His mood is highly variable.

english_meaning: The fact or quality of being different, divergent, or inconsistent. The degree to which something differs from a standard, expectation, or agreed norm. In statistics, a measure of the spread or dispersion of a set of data values around their mean. In legal and planning contexts, an exception or deviation from a rule or regulation that is officially permitted.
example_sentence: There was a significant variance between the estimated and actual costs of the project. The two reports showed a disturbing variance in the recorded figures. In statistics, variance helps to measure how spread out the data is. The builder applied for a variance to exceed the standard building height limit. The committee noted a variance in the way the two departments handled complaints.

english_meaning: A different form or version of the same thing. A form that differs in appearance, structure, spelling, or characteristics. A modified type produced naturally or intentionally. In biology, an organism or virus that has changed slightly from the original. In language, an alternative spelling, pronunciation, or expression. Different in form or appearance. Showing slight differences from the usual or original version.
example_sentence: This software has a free variant for students. Scientists discovered a new variant of the virus. The museum displayed several variants of the ancient coin. The recipe has a vegetarian variant that tastes just as good.

word: Variety is the spice of life
english_meaning: A proverbial expression suggesting that changes and new experiences make existence more interesting and enjoyable. The idea that diversity in one's activities or surroundings prevents boredom and stagnation. A philosophy advocating for a wide range of different things instead of a repetitive routine. The belief that having many options or variations enhances the quality of a person's life.
example_sentence: She decided to travel to a new country every year because variety is the spice of life. I enjoy trying different cuisines since variety is the spice of life. He changed his career path several times, firmly believing that variety is the spice of life. Our teacher encourages us to read books from various genres, reminding us that variety is the spice of life.

english_meaning: A resin dissolved in a liquid that dries to form a hard, clear, shiny coating on wood or metal. To apply a coat of varnish to something. To give a superficially attractive appearance to something unpleasant.
example_sentence: She applied two coats of varnish to the wooden floor to give it a durable, glossy finish. The old picture frame had been varnished many years ago and still retained its shine. He tried to varnish over the problems in the company by releasing a misleadingly positive press statement. The craftsman varnished the surface of the cabinet carefully before adding the brass fittings. The truth had been varnished with so many layers of deception that it was difficult to find.

english_meaning: The principal team representing a university, college, or school in a particular sport. A level of athletic competition specifically involving the primary team of an educational institution. A British informal abbreviation or archaic term for a university. The most senior or highest-ranking level of competition in school-based extracurricular activities. Pertaining to or relating to a university or its sports teams.
example_sentence: He finally earned his spot on the varsity basketball team after three years of practice. The varsity debate squad travelled across the country for the national championships. She wore her varsity jacket with pride during the homecoming parade. The coach decided to move several promising sophomores up to the varsity level.

english_meaning: To make changes to something so that it is not always the same. To be different from each other in size, amount, or degree. To alter something according to circumstances or requirements. To introduce variety or diversity into a routine or sequence. To show modification or deviation from a standard or norm.
example_sentence: The menu items vary depending on what fresh produce is available each season. You should vary your workout routine to target different muscle groups. Individual results may vary based on the user's skin type and age. The temperatures in the desert vary significantly between day and night.

english_meaning: The muscular tube that carries sperm from the epididymis towards the urethra. A duct of the male reproductive system that transports mature sperm. A tube cut or tied during a vasectomy. A passage that joins the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct.
example_sentence: The vas deferens carries sperm away from the testis. During a vasectomy the vas deferens is cut and sealed. Muscles in the wall of the vas deferens push the sperm forward. Each vas deferens is about forty-five centimetres long.

english_meaning: Relating to, affecting, or consisting of a vessel or vessels, especially those which carry blood. Denoting the tissue in higher plants that constitutes the vascular system, consisting of phloem and xylem. Being well supplied with blood vessels. Relating to the channels that carry fluids, such as sap in plants or blood in animals. Characterized by the presence of a complex system of conducting tissue.
example_sentence: The doctor examined the patient's vascular system to check for blockages. Vascular plants are able to grow much taller than mosses because they can transport water efficiently. Regular exercise helps improve your overall vascular health and circulation. A vascular headache is often caused by the swelling of blood vessels in the brain.

english_meaning: A decorative container without handles, typically made of glass or ceramics, used for displaying cut flowers. An open vessel used as an ornament in interior design. A historical urn used by ancient civilizations for storage or ritualistic purposes. A functional piece of pottery designed to hold water for plant life. A vessel that varies in shape and size, often serving as a focal point on a mantel or table.
example_sentence: She placed the fresh roses in a tall crystal vase on the dining table. The antique vase cracked slightly when it was moved during the renovation. Artists often use a simple ceramic vase as a subject for their still-life paintings. He bought a hand-painted porcelain vase as a souvenir from his trip to China.

english_meaning: A surgical procedure for male sterilization involving the cutting and sealing of the vasa deferentia. A permanent method of birth control to prevent sperm from entering the seminal stream. The anatomical interruption of the tubes that carry sperm from the testicles. A minor operation that renders a male unable to father a child. A common form of long-term contraception for men.
example_sentence: The couple decided that a vasectomy was the best long-term solution for their family planning needs. He felt a bit nervous before the vasectomy, but the surgeon assured him it was a routine outpatient procedure. A vasectomy is considered a permanent form of sterilization and is difficult to reverse effectively. After his vasectomy, he was advised to rest for a few days to ensure proper healing.

english_meaning: The physiological narrowing of the blood vessels resulting from contraction of the muscular wall of the vessels. A reduction in the lumen size of an artery or vein that limits blood flow to a specific area. A biological mechanism used by the body to regulate blood pressure and body temperature. The opposite process of vasodilation which increases vascular resistance. A clinical condition or response to certain drugs that causes the circulatory channels to tighten.
example_sentence: Cold temperatures often trigger peripheral vasoconstriction to conserve core body heat. Certain medications are designed to induce vasoconstriction to treat low blood pressure. Excessive vasoconstriction can lead to hypertension or localized tissue damage due to lack of oxygen. Smoking causes immediate vasoconstriction which significantly increases the strain on the heart.

english_meaning: The widening or dilation of blood vessels that results from relaxation of the muscular walls of the vessels. A physiological process that decreases vascular resistance and increases blood flow to specific tissues. A mechanism used by the body to regulate temperature by allowing more heat to escape through the skin. The physical enlargement of the interior space or lumen of an artery or vein. A response triggered by various chemical signals, exercise, or environmental heat to improve circulation.
example_sentence: Alcohol consumption can cause vasodilation, leading to a temporary feeling of warmth and a flushed face. During intense exercise, vasodilation occurs in the skeletal muscles to ensure adequate oxygen delivery. Certain medications are designed to induce vasodilation to help lower high blood pressure in patients. The body utilizes vasodilation in the skin as a primary cooling mechanism when the core temperature rises.

english_meaning: In the feudal system, a person who received land from a lord and in return pledged loyalty and military service to that lord. More broadly, a person, country, or organisation that is dependent on and subordinate to a more powerful one. Someone who is completely under the control or influence of another.
example_sentence: In medieval Europe, a knight often served as a vassal to a powerful lord. The small nation functioned as a vassal state of the empire for centuries. He felt like a vassal in his own company, completely controlled by the board. The vassal pledged his loyalty to the king in exchange for land and protection. Many smaller kingdoms were forced to become vassals after their military defeat.

english_meaning: Arched structures of brick or stone forming a roof or ceiling, often found in buildings such as churches, castles, or underground spaces. Secure rooms or compartments, often underground or made of reinforced steel, used for storing valuables, money, or important documents. The act of jumping over something using one's hands or a pole for support. It can also refer to underground burial chambers.
example_sentence: The bank vaults were sealed with heavy steel doors and a combination lock. The athlete vaulted over the fence with remarkable ease. The cathedral's vaults were beautifully decorated with painted ceilings. Ancient kings were buried in vaults beneath the palace floors. The gymnast vaulted over the apparatus during her performance.

english_meaning: The meat of a young calf, used as food. Tender pale-coloured meat obtained from calves, usually less than a few months old. A type of red meat often used in European and continental dishes.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a delicious veal cutlet for the guests. Veal is considered a delicacy in many European countries. She ordered roasted veal with mushroom sauce at the restaurant. The recipe calls for thin slices of tender veal. Some people avoid eating veal for ethical reasons.

english_meaning: A plant or part of a plant used as food, such as a cabbage, potato, or bean. A person who is incapable of normal physical or mental activity, often due to brain damage. Relating to plants or plant life.
example_sentence: We need to buy some fresh fruit and every kind of vegetable from the market. She chopped the vegetable finely before adding it to the soup. The accident left him in a vegetable state for months. The garden is full of different vegetable plants ready to be harvested.

english_meaning: Showing strong feeling. Forceful, passionate, or intense in expression. Marked by great energy or exertion. Used for emotions, opinions, denials, or actions performed with powerful intensity.
example_sentence: He gave a vehement denial of all the charges against him. She is a vehement supporter of women's education. The protesters expressed vehement opposition to the new law. His vehement speech moved the entire audience. There was vehement criticism of the government's decision.

english_meaning: In a forceful, passionate, or intense way. Expressing strong feelings, opinions, or emotions with intensity and determination; done with great energy or force.
example_sentence: She vehemently denied the allegations. He argued vehemently against the proposal. The protesters spoke vehemently for their rights. They vehemently opposed the unfair policy.

english_meaning: To cover something with something that hides it partly or completely. To hide or cover something so that you cannot see it clearly or understand It. a piece of thin material worn to protect or hide the face or head.
example_sentence: A fine drizzle began to veil the hills. In that country, women are veiled when they go out in public. The bride wore a veil made of French lace. A veil of secrecy surrounded the appointment of the new college president.

english_meaning: A blood vessel that carries blood back towards the heart. A thin-walled vessel that usually contains valves. A narrow line or streak of a different color or material, as in marble or a leaf. A particular style, mood, or quality in speech or writing.
example_sentence: A vein carries blood back to the heart. The nurse inserted the needle into a vein in his arm. Green veins run through the marble floor. She continued the story in a humorous vein.

english_meaning: Open, uncultivated grassland in southern Africa. Wide, flat countryside covered with grass and few trees, used for grazing. Open pasture land characteristic of South Africa.
example_sentence: Herds of antelope grazed peacefully on the veld. The farmers drove their cattle across the open veld. Fires spread quickly through the dry veld in summer. The sun set over the golden expanse of the veld.

english_meaning: A quiet emotional feeling experienced in old bookstores, combining nostalgia, mystery, and a sense of the past.
example_sentence: Walking through the dusty bookstore filled her with vellichor. The library’s silence and old pages created a strong sense of vellichor. He felt vellichor while browsing forgotten novels from another century. Vellichor settled in her heart as she touched books once read by strangers.

english_meaning: A soft fabric with a thick, short pile on one side. Cloth made of silk, cotton, or nylon with a smooth, rich surface. The soft skin covering the growing antlers of a deer. Something extremely smooth, soft, or luxurious to touch. Made of or resembling this fabric.
example_sentence: She wore a dark green velvet dress to the party. The chairs were covered in soft red velvet. His voice was as smooth as velvet. The deer's antlers were still covered in velvet.

english_meaning: Willing to act dishonestly or corruptly in exchange for money or personal gain. Open to bribery. Showing or motivated by a willingness to do wrong or dishonest things in return for payment. Used to describe a person, institution, or act that is corrupt, mercenary, or morally compromised by greed.
example_sentence: The venal judge accepted bribes in exchange for favourable verdicts. Many citizens were disgusted by the venal behaviour of the politicians. The company's venal practices were eventually exposed by investigative journalists. A venal bureaucracy makes it impossible to run an honest business. His venal nature made him willing to betray anyone for the right price.

english_meaning: The quality of being open to bribery or corruption. It refers to the condition of being willing to sell one's influence or principles for money. This trait is often associated with dishonest officials or politicians.
example_sentence: The venality of the local officials led to the collapse of the project. Critics often point to the venality of the political system as a major flaw. Corruption and venality have plagued the administration for years. He was shocked by the sheer venality of the contract negotiations.

english_meaning: A blood feud in which the family of a murdered person seeks vengeance on the murderer or the murderer's family. A prolonged and bitter quarrel or campaign against someone.
example_sentence: The two rival families engaged in a bloody vendetta for generations. He accused the media of pursuing a personal vendetta against him. The political vendetta ruined both of their careers. She waged a lifelong vendetta against the corporation that wronged her.

english_meaning: A person or company offering something for sale, especially a trader in the street. A business that provides goods or services to another entity. A seller of property or real estate. Any person who sells anything.
example_sentence: The street vendor sold delicious roasted chestnuts to the tourists. We need to find a reliable software vendor for our new project. The vendor of the house agreed to lower the price after the inspection. Several food vendors set up their stalls in the park for the festival.

english_meaning: To cover or disguise something’s real appearance. A thin covering or outward show that hides the real thing underneath.
example_sentence: The veneer of false love has gone. The veneer of civility has gone. The company veneered its poor service with flashy advertising. He veneered his selfishness with kind words. The table was made of cheap wood covered with a veneer of oak. His kindness was only a veneer hiding his selfish motives.

english_meaning: Deserving of a great deal of respect, especially because of age, wisdom, or character. Used as a title for an Anglican archdeacon or a person in the Roman Catholic Church who has attained the first degree of sanctity. Worthy of being venerated or revered. Ancient and impressive by reason of age. Respectable and hallowed by religious or historical association.
example_sentence: The venerable statesman was greeted with a standing ovation as he entered the hall. The institution was housed in a venerable building that had stood for three centuries. Students listened in silence to the venerable professor's final lecture. The church bestowed the title of venerable upon the monk for his life of service.

english_meaning: To regard with great respect, reverence, or awe, especially because of age, wisdom, or sacred status. To honour something or someone as holy or deeply worthy of admiration. To treat with the highest level of respect and devotion, often in a religious or cultural context.
example_sentence: The villagers have venerated this ancient temple for hundreds of years. Students still venerate the memory of the great philosopher. In many cultures, elderly people are venerated for their wisdom and experience. The faithful venerate the relics of the saints with deep devotion. He was venerated throughout the country as a founding father of the nation.

english_meaning: A feeling of profound respect and reverence. The act of honoring or adoring someone or something as holy or sacred. A state of being highly esteemed or deeply admired. A religious devotion or act of worship directed towards a saint or relic.
example_sentence: The elderly professor was treated with great veneration by his former students. The ancient temple remains a site of religious veneration for thousands of pilgrims each year. In many cultures, the veneration of ancestors is a central part of spiritual life. The artist's work is held in such high veneration that it is rarely displayed outside of the national gallery.

english_meaning: Relating to sexual desire or sexual intercourse. Resulting from or contracted through sexual intercourse. Pertaining to diseases that are transmitted by sexual contact. Of or relating to Venus, especially in a biological or historical context.
example_sentence: Medical students learn how to diagnose various venereal infections during their clinical rotations. Public health campaigns often focus on reducing the spread of venereal diseases in urban areas. The ancient text discussed the venereal appetites of the Roman gods in great detail. Clinics provide confidential testing for patients concerned about venereal symptoms.

english_meaning: Punishment inflicted in return for an injury or offense. The act of taking revenge or seeking retribution against someone who has caused harm, injury, or insult. It often implies a strong emotional desire to punish the wrongdoer.
example_sentence: He sought vengeance for the betrayal of his friend. The villain planned his vengeance carefully. She vowed vengeance after the injustice she suffered. History shows that acts of vengeance often escalate conflicts.

english_meaning: Describing a fault or sin that is minor and easily forgiven. Pardonable and not seriously wrong. In Christian teaching, a lesser sin that does not cut one off from grace.
example_sentence: Arriving a few minutes late was a venial offence. The teacher treated the error as venial and moved on. He drew a clear line between venial and serious faults. Such a venial lapse should not ruin his record.

english_meaning: A poisonous fluid secreted by animals such as snakes, spiders, or scorpions. A toxic substance injected through a bite or sting. Extreme bitterness, malice, or hatred in speech or feelings. Harmful or spiteful sentiment expressed toward someone.
example_sentence: The snake's venom can be fatal without treatment. He spoke about his rival with pure venom. Her words were full of venom and anger. Scientists study venom to develop new medicines.

english_meaning: Producing or containing venom capable of causing injury or death. Full of malice, spite, or extreme hostility. Expressing intense bitterness or hatred. Dangerous and harmful in a poisonous manner.
example_sentence: The cobra is one of the most venomous snakes in the world. He gave her a venomous look before leaving. Her venomous remarks shocked everyone. Be careful of venomous spiders in this region.

english_meaning: The flesh of a deer used as food. This term specifically refers to the meat of animals such as deer, elk, or moose. Historically, the word referred to any game animal killed by hunting. It is often considered a lean and nutrient-rich alternative to beef. It is typically consumed as steaks, roasts, or ground meat.
example_sentence: The chef prepared a succulent venison steak seasoned with rosemary and juniper. Historically, venison referred to any animal killed during a hunt. We decided to substitute the ground beef with venison for a healthier stew. The local market sells fresh venison during the autumn hunting season.

english_meaning: To release feelings, emotions, or pressure. To express emotions, frustrations, or thoughts openly, especially to relieve stress or tension. A passage, hole, or outlet through which something flows or escapes. Used in physical contexts like vents in walls, pipes, or machines.
example_sentence: She found it helpful to vent her anger in a journal. The mechanic checked the vent to see why the gas was escaping. He needed someone to vent his frustrations to after a tough day. The bathroom has a small vent to let out steam.

english_meaning: Relating to or situated on the underside or lower surface of an animal, organ, or structure. The opposite of dorsal. In anatomy, it refers to the front or belly side of the body. In plants, it refers to the surface facing inward or toward the axis.
example_sentence: The fish has a series of scales along its ventral surface. The ventral fin of the shark helps it to steer through the water. Surgeons made the incision on the ventral side of the patient. The ventral root of the spinal nerve carries motor signals to the muscles. The caterpillar used its ventral legs to grip the leaf firmly.

english_meaning: To take a risky step or action. To express something carefully or cautiously. To travel into unknown areas. A speculative investment. A joint business or partnership (as in joint venture). A business project that involves risk. To move forward or do something that involves risk, uncertainty or possible loss. A risky journey, activity or business investment started with the hope of gain.
example_sentence: They decided to venture into online business despite the risks. No one wanted to venture out after the storm warnings. His new venture in software development turned out to be successful. She ventured a guess about the results even though she was not sure. They ventured nervously into the water. The project is joint venture between public & private sectors.

english_meaning: The place where an event, meeting, performance, or activity is held or is to take place. In legal terms, the jurisdiction or location in which a case is heard or tried. A location chosen for a particular purpose, especially a public gathering or performance.
example_sentence: The wedding venue was a beautiful garden overlooking the sea. The music festival changed its venue at the last minute due to bad weather. The conference venue was equipped with state-of-the-art technology. Finding a suitable venue for the large event proved to be quite a challenge. The court agreed to change the venue of the trial to ensure a fair hearing.

english_meaning: Speaking or representing the truth. Habitually truthful and honest. Accurate and true in content or description.
example_sentence: He is known as a veracious and reliable witness. The historian gave a veracious account of the war. Her veracious reporting earned public trust. We need a veracious record of what happened.

english_meaning: The quality of being truthful, accurate, and honest. Conformity to facts or truth. Used to describe the reliability and truthfulness of a person, statement, or source of information. When someone or something has veracity, it can be trusted to be correct and honest.
example_sentence: The journalist was known for the veracity of her reporting. There are serious doubts about the veracity of the witness's statement. The court questioned the veracity of the evidence presented by the defence. His veracity had never been questioned during his long years of public service. The veracity of the ancient historical records has been confirmed by recent archaeological findings.

english_meaning: Relating to or consisting of words, whether spoken or written. Spoken rather than written, as in a verbal agreement. In grammar, relating to a verb or derived from a verb. A word or phrase formed from a verb, such as a gerund, participle, or infinitive. Informal insults or abuse directed at someone.
example_sentence: They had only a verbal agreement, with nothing in writing. Her verbal skills are excellent for a child of her age. The teacher explained the verbal forms of the sentence. He received a verbal warning from his manager.

english_meaning: Word for word; exactly as spoken or written. Repeating or copying something in exactly the same words without any change, omission, or interpretation. It is commonly used in writing, reporting, legal documents, and academic work when accuracy is essential.
example_sentence: The witness repeated the statement verbatim in court. Please copy the paragraph verbatim from the book. The teacher asked students to write the definition verbatim. His speech was recorded verbatim for accuracy.

english_meaning: An excessive, unnecessary, or unnecessarily complicated use of words. Language that is wordy, vague, or difficult to understand because it uses more words than are needed. Used to criticise writing or speech that is padded with too many words and lacks clarity or precision.
example_sentence: The legal document was full of unnecessary verbiage that made it hard to understand. The politician's speech was criticised for being full of verbiage and empty of real content. A good writer knows how to avoid verbiage and express ideas clearly and concisely. The report was so full of verbiage that its main point was completely buried. His emails are always packed with verbiage when a single sentence would do.

english_meaning: Using or containing more words than are needed. Containing more words than necessary. Characterized by the use of many or too many words.
example_sentence: Much academic language is obscure and verbose. The editors received streams of verbose articles from young hopeful journalists. The man was smartly dressed, verbose, and seriously agitated. He was a notoriously verbose after-dinner speaker. Not that he was verbose: most often when he made any comments on such matters he addressed them to himself. For once, his usually verbose wife was content to listen. His writing is difficult and often verbose.

english_meaning: Using more words than necessary. A style of speaking or writing that uses too many words, often making the message unclear or unnecessarily long. It usually has a negative sense, suggesting lack of clarity or conciseness.
example_sentence: His verbosity made the presentation difficult to follow. The teacher advised students to avoid verbosity in their essays. Due to her verbosity, the meeting lasted longer than expected. Clear writing requires reducing verbosity and focusing on key points.

english_meaning: Covered with green vegetation or grass that is fresh and flourishing. Bright and lush green in appearance. Used to describe landscapes, gardens, or areas that are richly covered with growing plants. Also used figuratively to describe someone who is young, inexperienced, or innocent.
example_sentence: The verdant hills of the countryside were a welcome sight after the grey city. Spring transformed the dry land into a verdant paradise. The castle was surrounded by verdant gardens full of flowering plants. From the plane, the island appeared as a small verdant jewel in the sea. The verdant valleys of the region attract tourists from around the world.

english_meaning: Final decision or judgment, especially by a court. The official decision made by a judge or jury after hearing all the facts in a case. It can also mean a final opinion or conclusion about something.
example_sentence: The jury reached a guilty verdict after two hours of discussion. The doctor’s verdict was that he needed more rest. The final verdict surprised everyone in the courtroom. Public verdict on the new policy was mostly positive.

english_meaning: A bright bluish-green encrustation or patina that forms on copper, brass, or bronze surfaces when they are exposed to air, moisture, or acidic substances over time. It is a form of copper corrosion that occurs through a chemical reaction. The colour resembling this bluish-green pigment, which was historically used as a paint or dye.
example_sentence: The old copper roof of the church was covered in verdigris after centuries of exposure to the weather. The artist used verdigris as a pigment to create the distinctive green tones in the painting. The bronze statue in the square had developed a thick layer of verdigris over the years. The antique candlesticks were coated in verdigris, giving them an aged and weathered look. Restoration experts carefully removed the verdigris from the ancient copper artefacts.

english_meaning: The edge or border of something. It can also refer to a point very close to a particular state or condition, often an extreme one. In botany, it refers to a particular type of grass or a rod used in hedging.
example_sentence: The company was on the verge of bankruptcy before the new investment. They sat on the grassy verge of the quiet country road. She was on the verge of tears after hearing the tragic news. We are on the verge of a major scientific breakthrough.

english_meaning: To be very close to an extreme state or condition. To come near to being (something). To be almost a particular state, quality, or feeling, especially one that is very bad or very good. Be on the edge or border of.
example_sentence:
Some of his suggestions verged on the outrageous. a dislike verging on contempt
The fabric is very dark blue, verging on black. His accusations were verging on slander. At times, his performance verged on brilliance, but at others it was nothing special. Her ability verges on genius. Our property verges on conservation land.

english_meaning: An ancient city in northern Greece, historically known as Aigai, which served as the first capital of the Kingdom of Macedonia. The site is famous for the royal tombs, including that believed to be of King Philip II, father of Alexander the Great. A UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its archaeological treasures and the symbol known as the Vergina Sun.
example_sentence: Vergina is famous for the royal tombs of ancient Macedonian kings. The Vergina Sun is an important symbol of ancient Greek culture. Tourists visit Vergina to see the museum built around the royal tombs. The discovery of the tomb at Vergina was a major archaeological breakthrough. Vergina was once the capital of the Macedonian kingdom.

english_meaning: Truly: In a way that is true or genuine. Indeed: Used to emphasize the truth of a statement. Certainly: Used to express strong certainty about something. In truth: Used to introduce or emphasize a fact. Without doubt: Used when the speaker is completely sure about something. Really: Used to emphasize that something is genuinely the case. Undoubtedly: Used to indicate that something is unquestionably true. Actually: Used to emphasize the reality of a situation. Surely: Used to express strong confidence in a statement. In all truth: Used in formal, literary, religious, or archaic language to affirm the truth of something.
example_sentence: Verily, this is one of the greatest achievements of our time. Verily, he was a man of great courage and wisdom. Verily, the truth will eventually be revealed. Verily, I tell you that kindness can change a person's life.

english_meaning: The appearance of being true or real. The quality of seeming to be true or lifelike. Realism or authenticity in art or literature. The extent to which something seems believable or plausible.
example_sentence: The novel's verisimilitude made it compelling. The artist sought verisimilitude in every detail. The story lacked verisimilitude and seemed fantastical. Verisimilitude is important in realistic fiction.

english_meaning: Used as an intensifier, often to qualify a metaphor. It implies that something is being described accurately as being truly the thing it is named. It stresses the authenticity or truth of a situation.
example_sentence: The garden was a veritable paradise of exotic flowers and birds. He has become a veritable legend in the world of professional cycling. The heavy rainfall turned the small stream into a veritable torrent. The antique shop was a veritable treasure trove of hidden gems.

english_meaning: The quality of being true; accordance with fact or reality. A true principle or belief, especially one of fundamental importance. It refers to something that is universally or lastingly true.
example_sentence: The verity of his statement was never in doubt. She clung to the eternal verities of love and kindness in a changing world. The novel questions the verity of historical accounts written by the victors. He spoke with an air of absolute verity that convinced everyone.

english_meaning: A type of thin pasta, similar to spaghetti but finer. It is often used in soups, desserts, or sweet dishes.
synonyms: ["Thin noodles","Pasta strands","Rice noodles (in Asian context)","Seviyan (South Asian term)"]
example_sentence: I cooked vermicelli pudding for Eid. She added some vermicelli to the chicken soup. The dessert was made of milk, sugar, and roasted vermicelli. Vermicelli can also be served as a light breakfast with nuts and raisins.

english_meaning: A bright red or scarlet color. A vivid reddish-orange pigment traditionally made from powdered cinnabar or artificially synthesized. It is often used in painting, decoration, and ceremonial markings.
example_sentence: The bride applied vermilion on her forehead as a symbol of marriage. The artist mixed vermilion with white to create a soft pink hue. Autumn leaves glowed like vermilion under the evening sun. The temple walls were painted in bright vermilion.

english_meaning: A bright red pigment or color with an orange tint. Having the color of bright red or scarlet.
example_sentence: The artist mixed vermilion with gold to create a royal shade. A streak of vermilion adorned her forehead. She wore a vermilion sari during the ceremony. The sunset bathed the sky in vermilion light. He painted the door in a vermilion shade.

english_meaning: Animals or insects that are harmful, dirty, or destructive, especially those that spread disease or damage crops or property. The word is often used for rats, mice, cockroaches, lice, and similar pests. It can also be used insultingly for people considered harmful or morally bad.
example_sentence: The warehouse was infested with vermin such as rats and cockroaches. Farmers try to protect their crops from vermin. The city launched a campaign to control vermin in crowded areas. He used the word vermin to insult his enemies.

english_meaning: The language or dialect spoken by ordinary people in a particular region or country. The native language or dialect that is commonly spoken by people in a specific area. It is different from formal or official language used in writing, education, or government. It can also describe something expressed in a plain, everyday style.
example_sentence: The teacher explained the lesson in the vernacular so students could understand easily. Many ancient texts were written in Latin, not in the local vernacular. The novel uses the vernacular of rural communities. He prefers writing speeches in the vernacular instead of formal English.

english_meaning: Able to do many different things or serve many functions. Someone or something that is versatile has many skills or can adapt to different tasks, situations, or purposes easily. It implies flexibility, adaptability, and usefulness in multiple contexts.
example_sentence: She is a versatile artist who can paint, sculpt, and design clothes. This smartphone is versatile; it works as a camera, gaming device, and personal assistant. His versatile skills make him valuable to any team. The versatile actor can play both comedy and serious roles convincingly.

english_meaning: Writing arranged in lines with a regular rhythm, especially poetry. A single line or a group of lines forming a section of a poem or song. A short numbered division of a chapter in a religious book. To compose poetry or express something in poetic form.
example_sentence: She wrote the whole story in verse. The choir sang the first verse of the hymn. He quoted a verse from the holy book. The poet is famous for his simple yet powerful verse.

english_meaning: Having a lot of knowledge about something, or skill at something. Having knowledge gained by close association, study, or experience.
example_sentence: He was well versed in employment law. I'm not sufficiently versed in XML to understand what you're saying. He was well versed in all branches of the field and published extensively. He is well versed in history. She was so poorly versed in the emotions that she failed to comprehend its true nature.

english_meaning: A particular form of something that differs from other forms of the same thing. An account of an event as described by one person. A translation of a text from one language into another. A particular edition or release of a product, book, or software.
example_sentence: The latest version of the app fixes several bugs. Her version of the incident differs from his. This is a shorter version of the original novel. He read an English version of the Arabic text.

english_meaning: Any one of the small bones that are stacked on top of one another to form the spinal column. A single bone of the backbone that surrounds and protects the spinal cord. One of the thirty-three bones that give the spine its strength and flexibility. A segment of the spine separated from the next by a cushioning disc.
example_sentence: The X-ray showed a crack in the lowest vertebra of his back. Each vertebra is separated from the next by a soft disc. A damaged vertebra can press painfully on the spinal cord. Surgeons fused two vertebrae to stabilise her spine.

english_meaning: An animal possessing a backbone or spinal column. Vertebrates are a major group of animals that includes mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish. They are defined by the presence of a vertebral column, which encloses and protects the spinal cord. This internal skeleton provides structural support for the body.
example_sentence: Humans, like all mammals, are vertebrates. The fossil belonged to a large vertebrate that lived millions of years ago. Scientists classify animals as either vertebrate or invertebrate. A key characteristic of a vertebrate is its internal skeleton of bone or cartilage. Birds, fish, and reptiles are all examples of vertebrate animals.

english_meaning: Standing or pointing straight up and down. At a right angle to the horizon or to a flat surface. Relating to levels of a hierarchy from top to bottom. An upright line, position, or structure.
example_sentence: Draw a vertical line down the centre of the page. The cliff rose in an almost vertical wall of rock. The company follows a strict vertical management structure. Move the pole until it is exactly vertical.

english_meaning: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, associated particularly with looking down from a great height. It can also be caused by disease affecting the inner ear or the vestibular nerve. It feels as though the surroundings are spinning.
example_sentence: Standing on the edge of the cliff, she was overcome by a sudden bout of vertigo. The medication helped to alleviate the dizziness and vertigo he experienced daily. Architects must design skyscrapers carefully to prevent vertigo in the occupants. Meniere's disease is a common cause of chronic vertigo episodes.

english_meaning:
A container used to hold liquids such as water, oil, or medicine. A ship or large boat used for transport on water. In biology, a tube that carries blood or fluid in the body such as blood vessels
A person seen as a carrier of qualities, emotions, or ideas. Sacred container used in religious practices. Any hollow structure designed to contain something.
example_sentence: She poured water into a clay vessel. The fishing vessel returned safely after the storm. Blood vessels carry oxygen throughout the body. He became a vessel of hope for his community.

english_meaning: To give someone legal rights, power, or authority. A sleeveless garment worn on the upper body.
example_sentence: He wore a black vest with his formal suit. The safety vest made the workers visible at night. The constitution vests power in the parliament. Ownership of the land will vest in the heirs next year.

english_meaning: Secured in the possession of or assigned to a person as an absolute right. Having a personal stake or interest in something, often for personal gain. Fully and unconditionally guaranteed as a right, benefit, or privilege, such as a pension, which cannot be taken away.
example_sentence: He has a vested interest in the project's success. After five years with the company, her retirement benefits became fully vested. The constitution vested judicial power in the Supreme Court. She felt she had a vested right to an opinion on the matter. Local shopkeepers have a vested interest in the town's prosperity.

english_meaning: The central cavity of the bony labyrinth of the inner ear that helps control balance. A small chamber or hall just inside the entrance of a building. An entrance space that leads into a larger area. Any small cavity or space at the opening of a body canal.
example_sentence: The vestibule of the inner ear helps us keep our balance. They waited in the vestibule before entering the hall. A problem in the vestibule can make a person feel unsteady. The old building has a marble vestibule at its entrance.

english_meaning: A trace or remnant of something that is disappearing or no longer exists. A vestige is the last small part that remains of something that was once much larger or more important. These remaining traces can be physical, like ruins, or abstract, like a lingering feeling or tradition.
example_sentence: The old stone wall was the last vestige of the fort. There was not a vestige of truth in his story. These traditions are the last vestiges of a bygone era. After the storm, not a vestige of their garden was left. He clung to the last vestige of hope.

english_meaning: Clothing or the act of dressing. Garments or clothing, especially ceremonial or formal dress. It can also mean the act of putting on clothes or being clothed. In legal or formal contexts, it may describe the granting or endowment of rights or authority.
example_sentence: The priest’s vestiture reflected centuries old traditions. Royal vestiture was prepared for the coronation ceremony. The document discussed the vestiture of authority to the new council. His academic vestiture marked his graduation day.

english_meaning: The special garments worn by clergy, acolytes, and other ministers during religious ceremonies. Vestments are often of a specific color and style that denotes a particular liturgical season, rank, or occasion. These ceremonial robes and articles of clothing are distinct from ordinary daily wear.
example_sentence: The priest carefully put on his vestments before Mass. A collection of ancient silk vestments was on display at the cathedral museum. The color of the liturgical vestments changes with the seasons of the church year. The intricate gold embroidery on the bishop's vestments was stunning. He was responsible for cleaning and storing the sacred vestments.

english_meaning: To carefully examine something for accuracy, quality, or suitability, often before approval. To evaluate someone’s background or credentials thoroughly, often for employment or security. A veterinarian, a medical professional who treats animals.
example_sentence: The committee will vet all applicants before hiring. We need to vet the report for any errors. She took her dog to the vet for a check-up. The politician’s past was thoroughly vetted by the media.

english_meaning: Someone who has had long experience in a profession, sport, or other activity. A person who has served in the military, especially one who has seen active service.
example_sentence: She is a veteran journalist with over 30 years of reporting experience. The veteran soldiers were honored at the parade. He is a veteran of many international chess tournaments. The company hired a veteran engineer to lead the project.

english_meaning: A medical professional who diagnoses, treats, and helps prevent diseases and injuries in animals. They care for pets, livestock, wildlife, and other animals and may also advise on animal health, food safety, and breeding.
example_sentence: The veterinarian treated the injured horse on the farm. Our cat recovered quickly after the veterinarian gave it proper medicine. A skilled veterinarian can identify animal diseases early. Farmers often consult a veterinarian to keep their livestock healthy.

english_meaning: A professional who treats animal diseases. Services or facilities that provide medical care to animals. Academic fields related to animal health. Medical treatment for livestock, pets and wildlife. Concerned with the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and injuries in animals, especially domesticated ones like pets and livestock.
example_sentence: She decided to pursue a veterinary career to help sick animals. The veterinary hospital treated injured horses. He attended a veterinary conference in London. The government hired a veterinary expert to inspect livestock.

english_meaning: Carefully examined or investigated for accuracy, quality, or suitability. Made a careful and critical examination of something or someone. This process is often done to ensure that a candidate is suitable for a job, a piece of information is accurate, or a plan is sound.
example_sentence: All candidates for the position were thoroughly vetted. The information in the report was vetted by three independent experts. We only work with vetted suppliers to ensure quality. The news agency ensures all its sources are properly vetted before publishing a story.

english_meaning: To annoy or worry someone. It means to make someone feel frustrated, irritated, or worried, especially with trivial matters. This feeling is often persistent but less intense than strong anger. It can also describe a problem or issue that is difficult, much debated, and without a simple solution.
example_sentence: His constant tapping on the desk began to vex me. She was vexed by the unexpected delay in her travel plans. Do not vex your father with such trivial questions while he is working. The complicated instructions for the new software would vex even a computer expert. This is a vexed question which has puzzled philosophers for centuries.

english_meaning: The state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried. It is the feeling of distress caused by a minor but persistent annoyance. Vexation can also refer to the source or cause of this irritation.
example_sentence: After the fifth phone call from the telemarketer, he threw his hands up in vexation. To her great vexation, the children had drawn all over the new wallpaper. He sighed in vexation when he realized he had missed the last train. The constant delays were a major source of vexation for all the passengers.

english_meaning: Causing or tending to cause annoyance, frustration, or worry. Full of petty irritations and annoyances. In a legal context, it describes a lawsuit or legal action brought without sufficient grounds, purely to harass or trouble the defendant.
example_sentence: The court dismissed the vexatious lawsuit filed by the rival company. He sighed, tired of the constant, vexatious demands from his manager. Her neighbors made a series of vexatious complaints about the noise. It was a vexatious delay that cost the team several hours. Filing a vexatious claim can result in penalties.

english_meaning: Travelling through a particular place on the way to a destination. By means of a specified method, person, or channel. Using a certain route, system, or medium of communication. Through the agency of something or someone.
synonyms: ["Through","By way of","By means of","Using","Over","Through the medium of","Per"]
example_sentence: We travelled to Lahore via Multan. She sent the documents via email. The news reached us via a mutual friend. You can pay via credit card or bank transfer.

english_meaning: The ability of something to work successfully or continue to exist. The capacity of a plan or business to succeed in practical terms. In biology, the ability of a seed, cell, or organism to live and develop. The state of being strong enough to survive independently.
example_sentence: The committee questioned the financial viability of the project. Doctors tested the viability of the transplanted cells. Long-term viability depends on steady funding. The report examines the viability of solar power in rural areas.

english_meaning: Capable of working successfully or being feasible. In a biological context, it refers to something capable of surviving or living successfully, especially under particular environmental conditions. It suggests a high probability of success or sustainability.
example_sentence: The committee is looking for a viable alternative to the current transport plan. Without significant investment, the small business was no longer financially viable. Scientists are testing whether the seeds remain viable after being frozen for decades. Solar energy has become a more viable option for many households recently.

english_meaning: A long bridge-like structure carrying a road or railway across a valley or other low ground. A series of arches supporting an elevated pathway. An engineering structure designed to span geographical obstacles.
example_sentence: The train slowly crossed the stone viaduct that spanned the deep valley. Ancient Romans built the aqueduct and viaduct to connect their sprawling empire. Traffic moved smoothly across the concrete viaduct connecting the two mountain ridges. The historical viaduct remains a major tourist attraction due to its architectural beauty.

english_meaning: A trade name for a prescription medicine used to treat erectile dysfunction in men. A drug containing sildenafil that improves blood flow to certain tissues. Sometimes used figuratively for anything that gives new energy or strength to something. A well-known pharmaceutical brand introduced in the late twentieth century.
example_sentence: Viagra should only be taken on a doctor's prescription. The company's profits rose sharply after Viagra was launched. Doctors warn against buying Viagra from unverified sellers. Critics called the funding a shot of Viagra for the ailing industry.

english_meaning: A person's emotional state or the atmosphere of a place as communicated to and felt by others. It is often used to describe a feeling or intuition about someone or something. In physics, it can refer to a vibration or oscillation.
example_sentence: The cafe has a very relaxing vibe that attracts local artists. I didn't get a good vibe from the new neighbor when we first met. The singer's music carries a nostalgic vibe from the 1980s. You could feel the positive vibe in the room during the celebration.

english_meaning: The plural form of vibe, referring to the collective sensations or emotional signals emitted by a person, group, or environment. It is frequently used in informal English to describe general feelings. It highlights the overall mood or energy perceived.
example_sentence: The beach party gave off some really good vibes to everyone who attended. I am getting bad vibes about this business deal and think we should back out. The city is known for its vibrant and energetic cultural vibes. They stayed late because the vibes at the concert were so incredible.

english_meaning: The quality of being full of energy, life, and enthusiasm. Brightness and intensity of colour. The quality of a sound being strong and resonant. Liveliness that makes a place or thing exciting.
example_sentence: The vibrancy of the market impressed every visitor. She loved the vibrancy of the colours in his paintings. There is a real vibrancy to the city's music scene. Age had not dulled the vibrancy of her personality.

english_meaning: Full of energy, life, and enthusiasm. Bright and striking in color. Producing a strong or resonant sound. Exciting and stimulating in atmosphere. Pulsating with activity or emotion.
example_sentence: The city has a vibrant nightlife. She wore a vibrant red dress to the event. His vibrant voice filled the room. The painting was full of vibrant colors.

english_meaning: A representative of a church, often a priest in charge of a parish. A member of the clergy who performs religious duties and leads services in a church, particularly in the Anglican or Church of England tradition. The vicar may act as a spiritual leader for the community and is responsible for the care of parishioners.
example_sentence: The vicar delivered a moving sermon on forgiveness. Our local vicar visits the sick and elderly every week. The vicar organized a charity event for the community. She spoke to the vicar about her doubts regarding faith.

english_meaning: Experienced through another person rather than directly. Describes feelings, experiences, or actions that are felt or enjoyed by watching or hearing about someone else’s experience, instead of experiencing them personally.
example_sentence: She felt vicarious joy watching her son graduate. He lives a vicarious life through adventure movies. The fans experienced vicarious excitement during the match. Parents often feel vicarious pride in their children’s success.

english_meaning: A bad habit, immoral behavior, or moral weakness. A criminal activity involving prostitution, gambling, or drugs. A tool used to hold something firmly while working on it. A serious fault or defect in someone's character. Something considered wrong according to social or religious values.
example_sentence: Gambling is considered a serious vice in many societies. Smoking is a vice he is trying hard to give up. The police are working to reduce vice in the city. He held the metal tightly in the vice while sawing it.

english_meaning: A term referring to the contrast between bad and good qualities. The comparison of moral weaknesses with moral strengths. A concept used in ethics to weigh wrongdoing against righteousness. A phrase used to describe the balance of evil and good in human nature. A theme often discussed in philosophy, religion, and literature.
synonyms: ["Good and evil","Right and wrong","Morality","Ethics","Virtue and sin"]
example_sentence: The novel explores the eternal struggle between vice and virtue. Every religion teaches us to choose virtue over vice. His life became a lesson in the balance of vice and virtue. Philosophers have long debated the nature of vice and virtue.

english_meaning: The area near or surrounding a particular place. The region or area close to a specific location. It emphasizes proximity rather than exact boundaries.
example_sentence: Crowds gathered in the vicinity of Trafalgar square. There is no hospital in the immediate vicinity. There are several restaurants in the vicinity of the hotel. The police searched the vicinity for clues. Schools in the vicinity were closed due to heavy rain. She lives in the vicinity of the city center.

english_meaning: Deliberately cruel or violent. It can also describe something that is severe, intense, or characterized by vice and immorality. Often used to describe an attack, cycles of behavior, or weather conditions.
example_sentence: The stray dog was prone to vicious attacks when it felt cornered. A vicious cycle of poverty and debt is difficult for many families to break. The city was hit by a vicious storm that caused widespread power outages. He was known for spreading vicious rumors about his political rivals.

english_meaning: It describes a situation in which one problem causes another problem, which in turn makes the first problem worse or causes it to happen again. It also refers to a logical fallacy where a premise is used to prove a conclusion, and that same conclusion is used to prove the initial premise.
synonyms: ["Vicious Cycle","Circular Reasoning","Downward Spiral","Catch-22","Endless Loop","Self-Perpetuating Problem","Chain Reaction","Paradox","Trap"]
example_sentence: The economy was stuck in a vicious circle of inflation and wage increases. By avoiding her fears, she created a vicious circle of anxiety and isolation. The debater fell into a vicious circle of reasoning that convinced nobody. Breaking a vicious circle requires a significant disruption of the standard routine.

english_meaning: It is a sequence of reciprocal cause and effect in which two or more elements continually intensify and aggravate each other. It also means a situation where an attempt to resolve a problem creates new problems that eventually lead back to the original negative situation.
synonyms: ["Vicious Circle","Downward Spiral","Catch-22","Endless Loop","Chain Reaction","Self-Perpetuating Problem","No-Win Situation","Unending Sequence","Destructive Pattern"]
example_sentence: Poverty and poor health often form a vicious cycle that is hard to break. They were trapped in a vicious cycle of borrowing money to pay off previous debts. The escalating violence created a vicious cycle of revenge in the region. To escape this vicious cycle, one must radically change their daily habits.

english_meaning: A change or variation occurring in the course of something. The ups and downs or unexpected changes in life, fortune, or circumstances. A shift from one state or condition to another, often unpredictable.
example_sentence: She remained calm despite the vicissitudes of fortune. Life is full of vicissitudes that test our strength and patience. He faced the vicissitudes of business with courage and optimism. Through all the vicissitudes of time, their friendship remained strong.

english_meaning: A person harmed, injured, or suffering from a misfortune, crime, or accident. Someone who experiences adverse effects due to an accident, crime, disaster, or other harmful events. It can also refer to a person who is tricked or exploited.
example_sentence: She was the innocent victim of an arson attack. They were the victims of a cruel hoax. She was the victim of a robbery last night. Many people were victims of the flood. He felt like a victim of unfair treatment. The scam left several victims financially ruined.

english_meaning: To treat someone unfairly or cruelly. To make someone a victim of harm, fraud, or injustice. To single someone out for cruel, unjust, or harmful treatment, often repeatedly. It can involve bullying, harassment, discrimination, or being exploited. It also includes causing someone emotional or physical suffering intentionally.
example_sentence: For years the family had been victimized by racist neighbours. The union claimed that some of the members had been victimized for taking part in strike. The school rules were designed to prevent teachers from victimizing students. She felt victimized by the unfair treatment at work. Many minorities have historically been victimized in that region. Cyberbullying can victimize people emotionally.

english_meaning: Success in a battle, war, competition, election, or contest. The act of defeating an opponent or overcoming a difficulty. Achievement of a desired goal after effort or struggle. A result that gives one side a clear advantage. A moral or personal triumph over fear, illness, temptation, or adversity.
example_sentence: The team celebrated its victory with thousands of supporters. Her recovery was a victory over a serious illness. The election victory gave the party a clear majority. Finishing the course felt like a personal victory.

english_meaning: Food or provisions, especially those prepared for consumption. To provide with food or provisions. A particular item of food or a meal.
example_sentence: The expedition set out with enough victual to last three weeks in the wilderness. The ship was victualised at the port before heading out into open waters. The innkeeper provided simple victual for the weary travellers who arrived late at night. Victual in the form of dried meat and hardtack was the staple diet of the soldiers on the march.

english_meaning: To compete eagerly with someone in order to achieve something. To strive in competition or rivalry with another for superiority. It implies a spirited struggle for a prize, position, or some other advantage.
example_sentence: The two companies are vying for control of the market. Several candidates are vying for the same leadership position. The athletes vied with each other for the gold medal. In the story, the two brothers vie for their father's affection. Different architectural firms vied to win the contract for the new museum.

english_meaning: Staying awake during normal sleeping hours, often for a purpose such as observing, guarding, praying, or showing respect. It can be used in contexts of solemnity, alertness, or watchfulness.
example_sentence: His parents kept a round the clock vigil at his bedside. The community held a candlelight vigil for the victims. The monks kept a night vigil before the festival. Soldiers stood vigil at the border. She kept a quiet vigil beside her sick mother.

english_meaning: The state of being watchful and alert to avoid danger or problems. Careful observation and attention to potential risks, threats, or unusual behavior. It involves staying alert, noticing details, and taking timely action to prevent harm or mistakes.
example_sentence: Airport security requires constant vigilance to prevent threats. The teacher praised the students’ vigilance during the science experiment. Drivers must maintain vigilance while driving in foggy conditions. Vigilance in monitoring the financial accounts helped detect fraud early.

english_meaning: Being careful, attentive, and aware of potential threats or difficulties. A vigilant person notices small details and is ready to act quickly to prevent harm or mistakes.
example_sentence: The security guard remained vigilant throughout the night. Parents should be vigilant about their children’s online activities. The soldiers were vigilant at the border to prevent any unauthorized entry. She was vigilant in noticing any errors in the report.

english_meaning: A short, evocative description, account, or episode. A small, pleasing picture or view. It can also refer to a style of photograph in which the picture fades into its background without a definite border. In literature, it is a brief scene that focuses on a single moment or gives a particular insight into a character or setting.
example_sentence: The book is a collection of vignettes about life in a small town. Each chapter was a self-contained vignette that added depth to the main character. He created a beautiful vignette of the old couple sitting on a park bench. The director used short, powerful vignettes to tell the soldier's story.

english_meaning: Physical strength and good health. It refers to the effort, energy, or enthusiasm with which something is done. It conveys a sense of active strength or force.
example_sentence: The veteran still has the vigor of a much younger man. They pursued the new project with renewed vigor and passion. Regular exercise can help maintain your physical vigor. The plants showed great vigor despite the harsh winter conditions.

english_meaning: Characterized by or involving great physical or mental energy and force. It describes something that is strong, healthy, and full of energy. It can also refer to actions carried out with great force or determination.
example_sentence: The government has launched a vigorous campaign against corruption. He remains a vigorous advocate for human rights at the age of eighty. A vigorous walk every morning is beneficial for cardiovascular health. The puppy was vigorous and playful despite its small size.

english_meaning: In a way that involves great physical or mental effort, energy, or force. It describes performing an action with intense strength or enthusiasm. It implies doing something in a determined and active manner.
example_sentence: She shook her head vigorously to express her complete disagreement. The coach instructed the players to warm up vigorously before the match. The local community vigorously opposed the construction of the new highway. He rubbed his hands together vigorously to keep them warm in the cold.

english_meaning: This is the British English spelling of 'vigor'. It refers to physical strength, energy, and the capacity for survival or growth. It also denotes the intensity and enthusiasm applied to a task.
example_sentence: The young athlete trained with immense vigour for the upcoming Olympics. The reforms were implemented with great vigour by the administration. Her writing lacks its former vigour and seems a bit repetitive now. He regained his natural vigour after a long vacation in the mountains.

english_meaning: Extremely unpleasant or disgusting. Morally bad, wicked or shameful. Very poor in quality or condition. Causing strong feelings of dislike.
example_sentence: There was a vile smell coming from the drain. He was punished for his vile behaviour towards the staff. The weather has been vile all week. She refused to repeat his vile remarks.

english_meaning: To speak or write about someone in a very negative and unfair way. To deliberately damage someone’s reputation by making harsh, false, or exaggerated statements. It is often used when criticism goes beyond facts and becomes personal or malicious.
example_sentence: The journalist was accused of trying to vilificate the minister without solid evidence. Online trolls often vilificate public figures to gain attention. It is wrong to vilificate someone based on rumors. The campaign aimed to vilificate the opposing candidate instead of discussing policies.

english_meaning: Unfairly saying or writing bad things about someone to damage their reputation. The act of deliberately spreading false, harsh, or exaggerated statements about a person, group, or idea with the intention of harming their image or credibility. It often involves insults, accusations, or character attacks rather than facts. Vilification is common in politics, media debates, and personal conflicts.
example_sentence: The politician faced public vilification after false allegations spread online. Media vilification can destroy a person’s career even before the truth is known. She spoke out against the vilification of scientists during the crisis. Vilification of minority groups often leads to social division and fear.

english_meaning: To speak or write about someone in an abusively disparaging way. It involves making malicious and often untrue statements to damage a person's reputation. This is done to make the subject appear wicked, vile, or contemptible.
example_sentence: The media campaign was designed to vilify the politician before the election. He was vilified by the press for his controversial new policy. Why do you always try to vilify people you disagree with? She felt that her ex-husband was vilifying her to their children.

english_meaning: To treat or regard someone with contempt or disrespect. To speak disparagingly or slightingly of someone or something. To regard as worthless or of little value.
example_sentence: It is wrong to vilipend those who hold different beliefs from your own. The critic seemed to take pleasure in vilipending the work of younger and less established artists. She refused to vilipend her opponents and instead engaged with their arguments respectfully. He was known to vilipend anything modern, preferring always to praise the methods of earlier generations.

english_meaning: A wicked or evil character in a story, play, or movie. A person guilty or capable of a crime or wickedness. The person or thing responsible for a specified trouble or harm. A scoundrel or rascal who lacks moral principles. A character whose evil actions or motives are important to the plot. An antagonist who opposes the hero.
example_sentence: The actor played the role of the villain so well that the audience hissed at him. In the movie, the main villain plans to take over the city using high-tech weapons. High-calorie snacks are often seen as the villain in the struggle against obesity. Every great hero needs a formidable villain to make the story truly engaging.

english_meaning: Behaving like or characteristic of a villain, especially evil, wicked, or morally corrupt. Showing extreme cruelty or malice in actions or intentions. Used to describe characters, plots, or actions associated with deliberate wrongdoing. Often used in fiction to describe the antagonist of a story.
example_sentence: The villainous antagonist plotted to take over the entire kingdom.  His villainous laugh sent chills down everyone's spine.  The film portrayed the dictator as a thoroughly villainous figure.  The villainous scheme was uncovered just in time to save the city.  Her villainous behavior shocked everyone who once trusted her.

english_meaning: A bad person who harms other people or breaks the law. A character in a book, play, or film who opposes the hero and commits evil actions. The main cause of a particular problem or difficulty.
example_sentence: The movie villain was defeated by the hero at the end. She played the villain in the school play with great enthusiasm. Pollution is the main villain behind global climate change. He was portrayed as a villain in the newspaper reports.

english_meaning: To prove that something is true or that you were right to do something, especially when other people had a different opinion. To prove that somebody is not guilty when they have been accused of doing something wrong or illegal; to prove that somebody is right about something. To free from a charge of wrongdoing.
example_sentence: I have every confidence that this decision will be fully vindicated. New evidence emerged, vindicating him completely. The witness completely vindicated him. He was vindicated in court and damages were awarded.

english_meaning: Proof that something is true or that you were right, especially when other people had a different opinion. A setting free from a charge of wrongdoing.
example_sentence: Anti-nuclear protesters regarded the Chernobyl accident as a clear vindication of their campaign. The army's victory is being seen as vindication of their tactics. It is also a vindication of his political instincts.

english_meaning: Showing a strong and unreasonable desire to harm or upset somebody because you think that they have harmed you. Likely to seek revenge.
example_sentence: He accused her of being vindictive. A vindictive comment. She liked to believe that she wasn’t vindictive by nature. They are just jealous, vindictive people.

english_meaning: The fact of trying or wanting to harm or upset somebody because you think that they have harmed you.
example_sentence: He withheld the letter out of sheer vindictiveness. A true gentleman is above envy, jealousy or vindictiveness. His generosity to his friends was matched by vindictiveness to those who fell out of his favour.

english_meaning: A plantation of grapevines. An area of land where grapevines are cultivated, usually for making wine. The term can also refer to the entire establishment, including the fields, buildings, and business of a winegrower.
example_sentence: The family has owned the vineyard for over a century. We went for a wine tasting tour at a local vineyard. The rolling hills were covered with neat rows of grapevines in the beautiful vineyard. A severe frost damaged many of the young grapes in the vineyard this spring.

english_meaning: The year or place in which wine, especially wine of high quality, was produced. A period considered typical of the best. Something of high quality from the past, classic, or old-fashioned but valuable. Of the best quality from a particular period. Typical or characteristic of a certain era. Related to wine production, especially grapes of a specific year. Used figuratively to describe excellence in any category (for example vintage performance).
example_sentence: She wore a vintage dress from the 1960s. This car is a vintage model in excellent condition. The wine is from the 2015 vintage and tastes exquisite. He collects vintage posters and old comic books. She drives a vintage convertible that turns heads everywhere. That guitar is a vintage Fender from the 1950s.

english_meaning: Able to be violated. Something that can be broken, breached, or not fully protected, especially a law, rule, agreement, or right.
example_sentence: Privacy laws are violable if enforcement is weak. The treaty proved violable under political pressure. Human rights should never be treated as violable. The agreement was written in a way that made it easily violable.

english_meaning: To break a rule, law, promise, agreement, boundary or moral principle. To disturb or interrupt something that should be kept safe or private. To fail to respect rights or freedom. To commit an act that harms or damages something valued. It also means to disrespect something sacred or private.
example_sentence: The company violated environmental laws by dumping waste in the river. He violated the privacy of his friend by sharing personal messages. The agreement was violated when one side refused to deliver the promised goods. She felt that her rights were violated during the investigation.

english_meaning: Breaking a rule, law, agreement or moral boundary. Any act that goes against a legal requirement, written guideline, social norm, personal right or ethical standard. It can involve misuse, abuse or disrespect of something that must be protected
example_sentence: The company was fined for a violation of safety rules. Entering the restricted area was a serious violation of security protocols. The journalist claimed that the new policy was a violation of free speech. Sharing private photos without permission is a violation of privacy. They were in open violation of the treaty.

english_meaning: The use of physical force that hurts or harms people or property. Any action or behavior involving force, aggression, or harm. It includes physical attacks, emotional abuse, destruction of property, or any act meant to control, dominate, or injure others.
example_sentence: The protesters demanded justice after the outbreak of violence in the city. Violence in schools affects students emotional well being. The film was criticized for showing too much violence. He believed that problems should be solved through dialogue, not violence.

english_meaning: Using or involving physical force intended to hurt, damage, or kill someone or something. It describes actions, events, or people characterized by extreme, destructive force. The term can also refer to something very strong, intense, or powerful, like a violent storm or a violent disagreement.
example_sentence: The movie was too violent for the children to watch. He has a very violent temper and gets angry easily. A violent storm knocked down trees and power lines. The peaceful demonstration suddenly turned violent. She suffered a violent allergic reaction to the medicine.
