english_meaning: Caused by or relating to a virus. Spreading quickly and widely, especially through the internet and social media. Describing content that becomes extremely popular in a short time. Of an illness, transmitted by a virus rather than bacteria.
example_sentence: The doctor said it was a viral infection, not bacterial. Her short video went viral within hours. Viral marketing can reach millions at very little cost. A viral fever spread through the whole school.

english_meaning: A person who has not had sexual intercourse. Also used to describe something that is pure, untouched, or used for the first time.
example_sentence: The expedition entered virgin territory never explored before. She poured virgin olive oil on the salad. The forest remained virgin, untouched by civilisation. The product was made from virgin materials for better quality.

english_meaning: The state of never having had sexual intercourse. Also used figuratively to mean the quality of being pure, unspoiled, or unused.
example_sentence: In many cultures, virginity is considered a matter of honour. The concept of virginity is complex and culturally defined. The mountain's virginity was lost once tourists arrived. She wrote about virginity as a social construct in her essay.

english_meaning: A bluish green pigment made from chromium oxide. A deep blue-green colour. Of or having this rich green shade.
example_sentence: The artist mixed viridian with white for the foliage. Deep viridian shadows filled the forest scene. She bought a tube of viridian oil paint. The sea shone a cool viridian in the morning light.

english_meaning: Having the power of acting or of invisible efficacy without the agency of the material or sensible part, potential, energizing. Being in essence or effect, not in fact. Existing in essence or effect though not in actual fact.
example_sentence:
Students will have more access to resources and support, both virtual and physical. The company has a virtual monopoly in this area of trade. He married a virtual stranger.
The country was sliding into a state of virtual civil war.

english_meaning: Behavior or attitudes that show high moral standards. A good moral quality in a person, or the general quality of goodness in a person. An attractive or useful quality. A quality that gives something special worth. As a result of.
example_sentence:
She succeeded by virtue of her tenacity rather than her talent. Her virtue would be proof against his charms.
Discretion is a virtue worth cultivating.
Tact is not one of his virtues. The virtue of wool as a clothing material is that it can provide insulation from the cold even when wet.

english_meaning: A person who is extremely skilled at playing a musical instrument. Someone who shows outstanding technical ability in any art or field. Showing exceptional skill and mastery. A highly accomplished performer or expert.
example_sentence: The young pianist is already a recognised virtuoso. He gave a virtuoso performance on the violin. She is a virtuoso of traditional folk music. The chef is a virtuoso when it comes to desserts.

english_meaning: Having or showing high moral standards. Behaving in a way that is morally good and right. Free from wrongdoing, sin, or corruption. Chaste and pure in conduct, especially in older usage. Showing qualities such as honesty, kindness, and integrity.
example_sentence: She led a virtuous life devoted to helping the poor. He was known as a virtuous and honest judge. Their virtuous behaviour earned the respect of the whole village. A virtuous leader inspires trust among the people.

english_meaning: In a morally good and upright manner. In a way that shows high ethical standards. Righteously and honourably. In a pure or blameless manner. With honesty and moral correctness.
example_sentence: He behaved virtuously even when no one was watching. She virtuously refused the bribe offered to her. The monks lived virtuously in the quiet monastery. They acted virtuously throughout the difficult negotiations.

english_meaning: The quality of being extremely harmful, poisonous, or damaging. The ability of a germ or virus to cause severe disease. Extreme bitterness or hostility in speech or feeling. The severity or destructive power of an illness. Intense hatred expressed in words or actions.
example_sentence: Scientists studied the virulence of the new strain of the virus. The virulence of the disease alarmed health officials. He was shocked by the virulence of her criticism. The virulence of the debate surprised everyone in the hall.

english_meaning: Extremely severe, harmful, or poisonous. Describing a disease or poison that spreads quickly and causes serious harm. Full of bitter hatred or hostility. Expressed with strong and cruel feeling. Highly infectious and dangerous.
example_sentence: A virulent form of the flu spread across the region. The plant contains a virulent poison that can kill within hours. He launched a virulent attack on his political opponents. The newspaper published a virulent criticism of the new policy.

english_meaning: In an extremely harmful or poisonous manner. In a way that spreads disease quickly and severely. With intense bitterness or hostility. In a fiercely hateful manner. Very aggressively and destructively.
example_sentence: The infection spread virulently through the crowded camp. He virulently opposed every suggestion made at the meeting. She spoke virulently about the injustice she had suffered. The article virulently attacked the government's decision.

english_meaning: A person's face. A person's facial expression. It refers to the face or countenance, especially with reference to the form, features, and expression. The term often carries a literary or formal tone, describing the overall appearance or look of a person's face.
example_sentence: The grim visage of the king struck fear into his enemies. Her smiling visage was a welcome sight after a long journey. He tried to maintain a calm visage despite the inner turmoil. A large hat shadowed his visage, making him hard to recognize. The mountain's rocky visage changed with the shifting light.

english_meaning: Having a glutinous or sticky nature or consistency. A viscid substance has a thick, syrupy quality and does not flow easily. It is a term often used in chemistry and cooking to describe liquids that resist pouring.
example_sentence: The honey was so viscid that it poured slowly from the jar. He had to clean the viscid grease off the engine parts. The sap oozing from the pine tree was a viscid, amber-colored liquid. Some cough syrups have a viscid consistency to coat the throat.

english_meaning: A chemical made from cellulose, used to make fibers that can be used to make clothes, etc. A smooth material similar to silk but made from cellulose. A cellulose ester obtained by treating cellulose with caustic soda
example_sentence: Made mainly of man-made fibers such as viscose, acetate or blends. Double-width organzas in viscose and acetate are used as sheer curtains. The fibers may be chemically modified, like in viscose (used to make rayon and cellophane). A viscous orange-brown liquid obtained by chemical treatment of cellulose and used as the basis of manufacturing rayon and cellulose film.

english_meaning: The state of being thick, sticky, and semi-fluid in consistency due to internal friction. It measures a fluid's resistance to flow. This property is common in substances like honey, syrup, or heavy oil.
example_sentence: The viscosity of the engine oil increases as the temperature drops. Honey has a much higher viscosity than water or alcohol. Scientists measured the viscosity of the molten lava flowing down the volcano. Adding extra flour will increase the viscosity of the sauce.

english_meaning: A British nobleman ranking below an earl and above a baron. A member of the European nobility holding a rank corresponding to that title. Historically, an official who acted as a deputy to a count.
example_sentence: The viscount inherited the title from his father. A viscount ranks above a baron in the British peerage. The novel tells the story of a young viscount. The viscount attended the ceremony with other members of the nobility. Historically, the viscount administered land on behalf of the count.

english_meaning: Having a thick, sticky consistency between solid and liquid. It refers to substances that do not flow easily. It is often used to describe liquids that have high internal friction.
example_sentence: The viscous syrup was difficult to pour out of the cold bottle. Tar is a highly viscous substance used in road construction. The chef prepared a viscous gravy that coated the back of the spoon. Certain types of bacteria produce a viscous slime for protection.

english_meaning: Thinking about or planning the future with imagination or wisdom. A person with original, forward-thinking ideas about what the future will or could be like. Describes a quality or plan that shows great foresight. It can also refer to something seen in a dream or trance, or someone who experiences such visions.
example_sentence: The company was led by a visionary who transformed the industry. Her visionary designs were years ahead of their time. As a visionary, he could see possibilities that others missed. The architect's visionary plan for the city was both bold and practical. Some considered the medieval saint a true visionary.

english_meaning: A pleasing view, especially one seen through a long, narrow opening like a row of trees. It refers to a mental view of a succession of remembered or anticipated events. This term often describes a panoramic prospect or a distant outlook.
example_sentence: The window offered a beautiful vista of the rolling green hills. Scientists are opening up a new vista in the field of genetic research. From the mountain peak, a grand vista of the valley unfolded before them. The garden was designed to create a long vista leading to the marble fountain.

english_meaning: Relating to seeing or sight. Able to be seen; perceived by the eyes. Relating to images, pictures, or the appearance of something. A picture, film, chart, or display used to illustrate or accompany something. Done or understood by looking rather than reading or listening.
example_sentence: The film is a visual masterpiece. Children often learn best through visual examples. The presenter used several visuals to explain the data. He suffered a temporary visual impairment after the accident.

english_meaning: To form a clear picture of something in your mind. To imagine how something will look or happen in the future. To make something visible or easier to understand through images, charts, or diagrams. To represent data or ideas in a visual form. To picture a goal clearly in order to work towards it.
example_sentence: Try to visualise the room before you buy the furniture. Athletes often visualise winning before a big race. The software helps us visualise complex data. I can clearly visualise the day we first met.

english_meaning: In a way that relates to seeing or sight. With regard to appearance. In terms of how something looks. By means of the eyes or visible signs. In a manner that can be perceived through vision.
example_sentence: The presentation was visually impressive and easy to follow. Visually, the two products look exactly the same. The website has been redesigned to be more visually appealing. Children learn better when information is presented visually. The film is stunning visually but weak in story.

english_meaning: A brief biographical sketch or a summary of one's life. It is often used as a short form for Curriculum Vitae or to denote life in a general sense. The term originates from the Latin word for life.
example_sentence: The professor asked for a short vita to include in the conference program. Her vita highlights twenty years of experience in international law. You should update your vita whenever you acquire a new professional skill. The artist's vita was displayed on the wall next to her paintings.

english_meaning: The plural form of vita, referring to multiple biographical sketches. It is most commonly encountered in the phrase 'curriculum vitae', referring to the course of one's life and professional career. It signifies the collective records of training and experiences.
example_sentence: The search committee reviewed over fifty vitae for the teaching position. Please ensure that all vitae are formatted according to the departmental guidelines. The vitae of the founding members show a diverse range of expertise. They compared the vitae of the two candidates to see who had more research experience.

english_meaning: Absolutely necessary or important to the existence or success of something. It also refers to something that is full of energy and lively. In biological terms, it relates to the body's functions that are essential for maintaining life.
example_sentence: Clean water is vital for the survival of all living organisms. The heart is a vital organ that pumps blood throughout the body. It is vital that you arrive at the meeting on time today. Her vital personality made her a popular leader among the students.

english_meaning: The state of being strong, active, and full of energy. It is the power that gives continuance to life and is present in all living things. Vitality also refers to the capacity for survival or the continuation of a meaningful existence.
example_sentence: Despite her age, she has the vitality of a person half her years. The city's economic vitality depends on new businesses. He was a man of great intellectual vitality. A good diet and regular exercise can increase your vitality. The cultural vitality of the community is one of its greatest assets.

english_meaning: To spoil or impair the quality or efficiency of something. To destroy or impair the legal validity of a contract or other document. It means to corrupt something morally or aesthetically, or to make it ineffective.
example_sentence: The discovery of fraud was enough to vitiate the entire contract. His pessimistic attitude threatened to vitiate the team's morale before the big game. Any conflict of interest will vitiate the legal proceedings. Adding too much salt will vitiate the delicate flavors of the dish.

english_meaning: A skin condition causing loss of pigment. Vitiligo is a long-term autoimmune disorder characterized by patches of the skin losing their pigment. The patches of skin become white and usually have sharp margins. The condition is not contagious or life-threatening.
example_sentence: She first noticed signs of vitiligo on her hands. Vitiligo is a non-contagious autoimmune disorder that affects the skin's pigment. Treatments for vitiligo aim to restore color to the white patches of skin. Many support groups exist for people living with vitiligo. Public awareness can help reduce the social stigma associated with vitiligo.

english_meaning: The clear, jelly-like substance that fills the large space between the lens and the retina. The transparent gel that keeps the eyeball firm and holds the retina in place. The structure through which light passes on its way to the back of the eye.
example_sentence: The vitreous body fills most of the inside of the eye. Light passes through the vitreous body to reach the retina. Small floaters may appear within the vitreous body as we age. Shrinkage of the vitreous body can pull on the retina.

english_meaning: Filled with bitter criticism or cruel hostility. Extremely harsh, cutting, and full of hatred, especially in speech or writing. Savagely abusive in tone. Relating to or resembling vitriol, a corrosive acid.
example_sentence: He launched a vitriolic attack on his former colleagues. The newspaper published a vitriolic review of the play. Their argument turned vitriolic within minutes. She received vitriolic messages after posting her opinion online.

english_meaning: To criticize or abuse someone harshly and angrily. To use bitter and insulting language against someone. To scold or condemn someone severely. To attack someone verbally with strong contempt. To rail against a person or thing in a violent manner.
example_sentence: The coach vituperated the players after their careless defeat. Critics vituperated the film as a complete waste of money. He vituperated against the corrupt officials in his speech. There is no need to vituperate; let us discuss this calmly.

english_meaning: Bitter and abusive language used against someone. Harsh and angry criticism or condemnation. The act of insulting or scolding someone severely. Verbal abuse full of contempt and hostility. A violent outburst of blame or censure.
example_sentence: The politician faced a storm of vituperation after the scandal. Her speech was filled with vituperation against her rivals. He endured years of vituperation from his critics. Calm reasoning is more persuasive than vituperation.

english_meaning: Full of bitter, harsh, and abusive language. Bitterly critical and insulting. Expressing strong anger and contempt in words. Severely scolding or condemning. Characterized by verbal attacks and harsh blame.
example_sentence: The debate turned into a vituperative exchange of insults. She received a vituperative letter from an angry customer. His vituperative remarks offended everyone in the meeting. Social media is often filled with vituperative comments.

english_meaning: In a lively, brisk, and spirited manner, used as a musical direction. A musical tempo marking instructing performers to play in a quick, lively, and animated style, faster than allegro in some interpretations. A passage or movement of music played in this lively manner.
example_sentence: The pianist played the final movement vivace, filling the hall with energy. The composer marked the section vivace to give it a joyful character. The orchestra performed the vivace with remarkable precision. She practiced the vivace passage until her fingers ached. The conductor signaled the musicians to take the next part vivace.

english_meaning: Full of life, energy, and high spirits. Attractively lively, animated, and cheerful in manner. Having a bright, sparkling personality that is engaging and pleasant to be around. Showing enthusiasm and liveliness, especially in conversation and behavior, particularly used of a woman.
example_sentence: Her vivacious personality made her the center of every gathering. The vivacious young actress charmed the entire audience. He fell in love with her warm smile and vivacious nature. The vivacious child kept everyone entertained at the party. She was as vivacious in old age as she had been in her youth.

english_meaning: In a lively, energetic, and high-spirited manner. With cheerful liveliness and animation. In a way that shows enthusiasm, charm, and a bright personality. Acting or speaking in an engaging and spirited way that attracts the attention of others.
example_sentence: She vivaciously greeted every guest who entered the hall. The children laughed vivaciously as they ran through the garden. He spoke vivaciously about his recent travels abroad. The host welcomed the audience vivaciously and began the show. She danced vivaciously to the rhythm of the music.

english_meaning: The quality of being attractively lively and animated. It describes a high spiritedness or a person who is full of energy and enthusiasm. This trait suggests a bubbly and cheerful disposition.
example_sentence: The young actress was admired for her natural vivacity on screen. Her vivacity and wit made her the life of every social gathering. Even at eighty, the old man had not lost his youthful vivacity. The music filled the room with a sense of joy and vivacity.

english_meaning: Clear, bright or full of life. Easy to imagine because it feels real. Something described in a way that is lively, bright or strongly expressive. It creates a strong picture in the mind. It can refer to colors, memories, imagination, descriptions or images that appear full of clarity and energy.
example_sentence: She has a vivid memory of her first day at school. The artist used vivid colors to paint the sunset. He gave a vivid description of the storm. The story was so vivid that I felt like I was there.

english_meaning: In a very clear and detailed way. So as to produce strong and lasting images in the mind. In bright and striking colours. With great intensity of feeling or description.
example_sentence: I vividly remember my first day at school. The writer vividly describes life in the village. The sunset lit the sky vividly with orange. She vividly recalled the sound of the rain.

english_meaning: The quality of being bright, clear, and striking. The power to create strong mental images. Intensity of colour, memory, or description.
example_sentence: The vividness of her memory surprised everyone. The painting is admired for its vividness of colour. He described the accident with startling vividness. The vividness of the dream stayed with him all day.

english_meaning: To give life, vitality, or energy to someone or something. To make something more lively, vivid, interesting, or attractive. To animate or enliven an idea, description, scene, or work of art.
example_sentence: Fresh flowers vivified the quiet room. Her humor vivified an otherwise dull meeting. The illustrator used bright details to vivify the story. A cool shower seemed to vivify the tired hikers.

english_meaning: Giving birth to live young rather than laying eggs. Describing animals whose young develop inside the mother's body. Producing offspring that are born alive.
example_sentence: Most mammals are viviparous animals. Whales are viviparous despite living in the sea. The lesson compared viviparous and oviparous reproduction. Some snakes are surprisingly viviparous.

english_meaning: The practice of performing operations on live animals for scientific research. Experimental surgery carried out on living creatures. Harsh and detailed criticism of something.
example_sentence: Many activists campaign against vivisection. Vivisection raises serious ethical questions. The law restricts vivisection in university laboratories. His article was a vivisection of the government's policy.

english_meaning: A female fox. A woman regarded as bad-tempered or quarrelsome. A spirited and fierce woman, often used disapprovingly.
example_sentence: The vixen led her cubs across the field. A vixen usually raises her young in a den. He unfairly called her a vixen during the argument. The old story describes a clever vixen in the forest.

english_meaning: A personal video log or journal posted on the internet for public viewing. A form of blog for which the medium is video, often featuring a person talking to the camera about their life or a specific topic. The act of creating and uploading video content to a platform like YouTube or TikTok. A digital record of events, experiences, or thoughts captured through video footage rather than text.
example_sentence: She decided to start a daily vlog to document her travels across Europe. Many influencers spend hours editing a single vlog to ensure it engages their audience. He uploaded a vlog explaining the technical specifications of his new camera gear. Watching a travel vlog is a great way to explore a new city from your own home.

english_meaning: A person who regularly creates and posts video logs on the internet. An individual who documents their daily life or specific interests through the medium of video for an online audience. A content creator who uses platforms like YouTube or TikTok to share personal experiences or expertise via video format. A digital storyteller who replaces written journal entries with filmed segments to engage with followers.
example_sentence: The travel vlogger shared stunning footage of the mountain ranges in their latest upload. She decided to become a full-time vlogger after her makeup tutorials gained millions of views. Many vloggers use high-quality cameras and microphones to ensure their production value remains professional. The lifestyle vlogger interacts with her community through the comments section of every video.

english_meaning: The body of words used in a particular language. The words known and used by a person. A list of words with their meanings. The range of words available for a specific subject. A dictionary or wordbook.
example_sentence: Reading books helps to build vocabulary. His English vocabulary is very impressive. The teacher gave us a list of new vocabulary. Legal vocabulary can be difficult to understand.

english_meaning: Relating to the voice. Spoken or expressed aloud. Willing to express opinions strongly. Produced by or used for singing.
example_sentence: She has strong vocal ability. The group was vocal in its criticism. Vocal exercises helped the singer. The poem has a clear vocal rhythm.

english_meaning: To shout loudly or speak in a noisy and forceful way. To cry out. To express opinions or complaints with loud and strong voice. To make a loud outcry. Used when someone speaks or protests in an aggressive, angry, or excited manner so that everyone can hear.
example_sentence: The protesters began to vociferate against the new government policy. He vociferated his complaints in front of the entire office. The crowd vociferated loudly when the referee made an unfair decision. She vociferated her support for the cause at the public meeting. The angry customer vociferated until the manager came to listen.

english_meaning: Expressing opinions or feelings in a loud and forceful way. Speaking out strongly and insistently, especially in protest or complaint. Noisy and clamorous, especially when many people speak at once. Marked by outspoken and often angry demands.
example_sentence: The workers were vociferous in their demand for better wages. A vociferous crowd gathered outside the parliament building. She became the most vociferous critic of the new policy. Vociferous protests forced the committee to reconsider its decision.

english_meaning: A fashion for something. A fashion or general liking, especially one that is temporary. A practice or interest that is very popular for a short time. A current state of general acceptance and use.
example_sentence: In the 1920s, short hair for women became the vogue. "Community" is one of the vogue words of the new government. Sixties music has come back into vogue. This novel had a great vogue ten years ago.

english_meaning: To cancel or make legally null. To remove contents or make empty. Empty space or vacuum. Feeling of emptiness or loss. Something invalid or legally null. Completely empty or lacking. Invalid or null.
example_sentence: Please void this check; it has an error. The company voided the previous agreement. he vault was void of any valuables. His words felt void and meaningless. The black hole created a void in space. After his friend left, he felt a void inside.

english_meaning: Likely to change quickly or unpredictably. Describing someone with sudden emotional shifts. Easily evaporating at normal temperatures in chemistry. Financial markets that swing sharply in value. A tense or sensitive situation that can escalate quickly. Something unstable or prone to rapid and unexpected change. It can refer to situations, emotions, markets, chemicals or people who react suddenly.
example_sentence: The political situation in the region is becoming more volatile. Her mood is so volatile that no one knows how she will react. Oil prices have been volatile throughout the year. The chemical is highly volatile and must be stored carefully.

english_meaning: The tendency of a substance to evaporate rapidly or the quality of being subject to frequent and unpredictable change. In finance, it refers to the rate at which the price of an asset increases or decreases. It also describes a person's temperament that is liable to change suddenly.
example_sentence: The volatility of the stock market makes it a risky place for small investors. Gasoline is known for its high volatility and must be stored carefully. The political volatility in the region has led to widespread protests. His emotional volatility made it difficult for him to maintain steady relationships.

english_meaning: Relating to, produced by, or involving a volcano. Formed from lava, ash, or other erupted material. Characterized by volcanic activity or eruptions. Extremely explosive, violent, or emotionally intense. Resembling a volcano in shape, force, or behavior.
example_sentence: Volcanic ash covered the roads after the eruption. The island has rich soil of volcanic origin. Researchers recorded an increase in volcanic activity. Their calm discussion suddenly turned into a volcanic argument.

english_meaning: A mountain or hill with an opening through which lava, ash, and gases may escape. A vent in Earth’s crust connected to molten rock below. The geological structure formed by repeated eruptions. An active, dormant, or extinct source of volcanic material. A situation or person likely to erupt suddenly with powerful emotion or conflict.
example_sentence: The volcano sent a column of ash high into the sky. Villages near the active volcano were evacuated. Scientists placed sensors around the volcano to detect movement. His anger felt like a volcano ready to erupt.

english_meaning: The scientific study of volcanoes and volcanic activity. The branch of geology concerned with magma, lava, and eruptions. The investigation of volcanic landforms, rocks, gases, and hazards. The study of how volcanoes form and change over time. The science used to monitor eruptions and assess volcanic risk.
example_sentence: She studied volcanology before joining the island observatory. Volcanology helps scientists identify signs of an approaching eruption. The university offers a field course in volcanology. Modern volcanology combines satellite data with rock analysis.

english_meaning: A small, short-tailed rodent that resembles a mouse. A burrowing animal commonly found in fields, grasslands, and gardens. A plant-eating mammal that feeds on roots, seeds, grass, and bark. A member of several genera in the subfamily Arvicolinae. An animal sometimes called a field mouse, although it is not a true mouse.
example_sentence: A vole disappeared into a tunnel beneath the grass. The gardener found vole tracks beside the damaged roots. Owls help control the vole population in open fields. This species of vole stores seeds for the winter.

english_meaning: The power or faculty of choosing and deciding. A conscious decision made by one’s own free will. The act of willing or intending something. Independent choice without force or compulsion. Mental control used to initiate an action. A deliberate preference that leads to behavior.
example_sentence: She left the organization of her own volition. Every participant joined the study by free volition. The movement began as an act of conscious volition. His decision reflected personal volition rather than family pressure.

english_meaning: A number of bullets, arrows, or missiles discharged at the same time. A rapid series of remarks, questions, criticisms, or blows. In ball games, a shot made before the ball touches the ground. The exchange of a ball over a net. To strike or kick a ball before it bounces. To fire or send many things together in quick succession.
example_sentence: The soldiers fired a volley into the air. Reporters greeted the minister with a volley of questions. She won the point with a powerful backhand volley. The players volleyed the ball across the net for nearly a minute.

english_meaning: A complete reversal of one's opinion, position, or policy. A sudden and unexpected change of attitude or direction, typically on a significant issue.
example_sentence: The government performed a volte face on its tax policy. His sudden volte face on the issue shocked his supporters. She executed a complete volte face after reading the new report. The prime minister's volte face on Brexit confused many voters.

english_meaning: Talkative; garrulous. Characterized by a ready and continuous flow of words; fluent. Describes someone who talks a lot in an energetic and rapid way, speaking easily and at length without much pause.
example_sentence: She was a voluble and excitable person who loved being the center of attention. After a couple of drinks, he became very voluble and couldn't stop telling stories. The voluble politician could speak for hours without a script. My voluble aunt can talk on the phone for hours on end about anything and everything.

english_meaning: By one’s own choice, without force. Doing something freely, willingly, and without pressure, obligation, or compulsion. It shows personal decision and readiness.
example_sentence: She voluntarily helped the poor during the flood. He voluntarily admitted his mistake. They voluntarily joined the training program. The worker voluntarily worked extra hours to finish the task.

english_meaning: The principle of relying on voluntary action rather than force or obligation. Giving time and effort freely for community service without expecting payment. The idea that actions, decisions, or social systems should be based on free will and voluntary choice instead of compulsion, law, or external pressure. It is often used in philosophy, sociology, and politics to emphasize individual freedom and willingness.
example_sentence: Voluntarism plays a key role in community development projects. The organization depends on voluntarism rather than paid staff. His belief in voluntarism led him to reject forced policies. Many charities survive because of voluntarism.

english_meaning: Done by choice, not forced. Something that is done willingly, without pressure, force, or obligation. It can also refer to actions done freely for others without payment, or activities controlled by one’s own will.
example_sentence: She does voluntary work at a local hospital. His apology was voluntary and sincere. Participation in the program is voluntary. He made a voluntary donation to the charity.

english_meaning: A person who offers help willingly without payment. A person who freely offers to do something without being forced or paid. To offer oneself for a task or service willingly. To offer help freely. To join a service willingly. To give information without being asked.
example_sentence: She works as a volunteer at a local hospital. He volunteered to teach children in the village. Many students volunteer during natural disasters. I volunteered my time to support the charity event.

english_meaning: The practice of offering time and services freely without payment. A system or culture where people actively engage in unpaid community service. A spirit of helping others without obligation. Organized or informal participation in social, humanitarian, or environmental causes.
example_sentence: Volunteerism plays a vital role in disaster relief efforts. Many students participate in volunteerism to support their communities. Her dedication to volunteerism inspired others to join the cause. Volunteerism helps build stronger and more connected societies.

english_meaning: The thin flat bone that forms the lower part of the nasal septum. The single bone dividing the two nasal passages. A plough shaped bone in the middle of the nasal cavity. The facial bone that joins the ethmoid bone above and the maxilla below.
example_sentence: The vomer forms part of the nasal septum. A deviated vomer can make breathing difficult. The vomer is a single unpaired bone of the face. Surgeons straightened the vomer to improve his breathing.

english_meaning: Wanting or eating large quantities of food. Having a very strong desire or appetite for something. Extremely eager or greedy. Used both literally for people or animals that eat a lot and figuratively for someone with an insatiable hunger for knowledge, reading, learning, or other activities.
example_sentence: He has a voracious appetite and can finish a large pizza alone. She is a voracious reader who finishes several books every week. The lion is a voracious predator of the African plains. Children at that age often show a voracious curiosity about the world. The company has a voracious demand for skilled engineers.

english_meaning: Extreme greed or eagerness in eating. A very strong desire or appetite for something. Insatiable hunger or craving. Excessive enthusiasm for acquiring or consuming.
example_sentence: He ate the meal with surprising voracity. Her voracity for books kept her in the library all day. The voracity of the market for new gadgets is endless. The animals fed with such voracity that nothing was left.

english_meaning: In trouble, difficulty, or a bad situation, especially when there is no easy way out.
synonyms: ["Walk away","Leave in protest","Show disapproval by leaving"]
example_sentence: Customers voted with their feet and left the store. Many employees voted with their feet by leaving the company after the new policy was introduced. When the concert was delayed for hours, the audience voted with their feet and went home. Customers voted with their feet by choosing another store with better service. Students voted with their feet by boycotting the boring lecture.

english_meaning: Something offered or dedicated in fulfillment of a vow, promise, or prayer, often given to a deity, shrine, or sacred place as an expression of gratitude, devotion, or request for blessing. It can refer to objects such as candles, offerings, or gifts placed in religious places.
example_sentence: She lit a votive candle in the church to pray for her family. The temple was filled with votive offerings left by grateful visitors. Pilgrims often bring votive gifts after their wishes are fulfilled. A small votive lamp burned quietly near the shrine.

english_meaning: To assert or confirm as a result of one's own experience that something is true or accurately described. To give a personal guarantee or become a surety for another person's character or actions. To serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or quality. To support or back up a claim with testimony. To answer for the reliability or integrity of a person.
example_sentence: I can personally vouch for his integrity and work ethic. Several witnesses were called to vouch for the defendant's whereabouts on that night. Her long list of achievements vouches for her professional competence. Can anyone here vouch for the truth of these statements?

english_meaning: To confirm the truth, accuracy, or reliability of someone or something.
example_sentence: I can vouch for his honesty. Can anyone vouch for your whereabouts last night? She vouched for his skills in the interview. He vouched for the safety of the product.

english_meaning: A solemn promise or strong commitment to do something. A serious and formal promise, often made publicly or in a sacred or emotional context. It shows strong intention and commitment to perform or avoid something.
example_sentence: She took a vow to always help the poor. The monk lives under a vow of silence. They exchanged wedding vows during the ceremony. He made a vow to stop smoking forever.

english_meaning: A long journey, especially by sea or in space. A voyage is a long journey from one place to another, usually by ship or spacecraft. To travel or move on a long journey, especially by sea. It can also be used in a broader sense for any long or meaningful journey.
example_sentence: They voyaged across the ocean for several months. The explorers voyaged to unknown lands. Early sailors voyaged without modern instruments. The crew voyaged through dangerous waters.

english_meaning: A person who derives gratification from observing unsuspecting people engaged in intimate acts or undressing. A person who enjoys observing the private lives, problems, or personal affairs of others from a distance. An obsessive viewer who prefers watching events unfold rather than participating directly.
example_sentence: The police arrested a voyeur who was caught hiding outside the building. Watching reality television allows audiences to act as a voyeur in strangers' lives. He felt like a voyeur when he accidentally overheard their intimate discussion. The photojournalist insisted she was an artist rather than a voyeur.

english_meaning: Seaweed, especially that used as fertilizer. Vraic is a term used in the Channel Islands for seaweed collected from the shore. It is traditionally gathered and spread on agricultural land to act as a natural manure, enriching the soil with minerals.
example_sentence: The farmer spread a thick layer of vraic over his potato fields to enrich the soil. For centuries, islanders have harvested vraic after the high tide recedes. The pungent, salty smell of drying vraic filled the air near the coast. They went down to the beach with carts to collect the vraic washed ashore by the storm.

english_meaning: To treat rubber with sulfur and heat to improve its strength and elasticity. This chemical process makes the rubber harder, more durable, and resistant to temperature changes. It cross-links the polymer chains in the rubber, transforming it from a sticky, weak material into a firm, flexible, and useful product.
example_sentence: Charles Goodyear discovered how to vulcanize rubber, revolutionizing many industries. They vulcanize the raw rubber to make it suitable for creating durable car tires. Without the process to vulcanize it, natural rubber is sticky and not very useful. The factory's main purpose is to vulcanize large sheets of synthetic material.

english_meaning: Lacking sophistication, taste, or good manners. Making explicit reference to sex or bodily functions in a coarse way. Rude, offensive, or crude in speech or behaviour. Belonging to the ordinary people or common language rather than the educated classes.
example_sentence: His vulgar jokes embarrassed everyone at the table. The room was decorated in a loud and vulgar style. She refused to tolerate such vulgar language. Vulgar Latin gradually developed into the Romance languages.

english_meaning: The state or quality of being coarse or unrefined. An offensive or indecent act or expression. Lack of good taste or social grace. The behavior or language of the common people as perceived by the elite. An instance of crudeness or obscenity.
example_sentence: He was shocked by the sheer vulgarity of the comedian's performance. The room was decorated with a gaudy vulgarity that hurt the eyes. Her speech was peppered with unnecessary vulgarity and insults. There is a certain vulgarity in displaying one's wealth so ostentatiously.

english_meaning: The state of being open to physical or emotional harm. Susceptibility to attack, damage, criticism, temptation, or disease. A weakness or flaw that can be exploited, especially in a computer system. The condition of needing special care or protection because of age, poverty, illness, or difficult circumstances. Willingness to show honest feelings despite the risk of being hurt.
example_sentence: The report highlights the vulnerability of coastal towns to flooding. Sharing her fears required courage and vulnerability. The update fixes a serious security vulnerability in the software. Social workers assessed each family’s level of vulnerability.

english_meaning: Open to harm, attack, or damage. Physically weak or unprotected. Emotionally sensitive or easily hurt. Exposed to criticism or attack. At risk due to lack of support or resources
example_sentence: Children are more vulnerable to online scams. The old building is vulnerable to earthquakes. She felt emotionally vulnerable after the breakup. Without insurance, the workers are vulnerable to financial loss.

english_meaning: A large bird of prey with a naked or sparsely feathered head, which feeds on the flesh of dead animals (carrion). Figuratively, a contemptible or rapacious person who preys on or exploits the misfortunes of others. These birds play a crucial role in ecosystems by cleaning up carcasses.
example_sentence: A flock of vultures descended on the carcass. The media were portrayed as vultures feeding on the scandal. He's a corporate vulture, buying up struggling companies just to sell off their assets. Vultures have excellent eyesight for spotting their next meal from high in the air.

english_meaning: The external genital organs of a female. The area that includes the labia, clitoris, and vaginal opening. The outer part of the female reproductive system that protects internal organs. The visible external region surrounding the entrance to the vagina.
example_sentence: The vulva includes all the external female genital parts. Gentle washing keeps the vulva clean and healthy. Irritation of the vulva can be caused by soaps and perfumes. The textbook contained a clear diagram of the vulva.

english_meaning: Something that is bad, weak, strange, or of poor quality. It is informal and often used to criticize ideas, behavior, performance, or objects that feel disappointing, unfair, or illogical
example_sentence: That excuse sounds wack and does not make sense. The movie had a good idea but the ending was wack. His explanation for being late was completely wack. The rules of the game feel wack and unfair.

english_meaning: To walk with short steps and a swaying motion like a duck. To move awkwardly from side to side while walking. A rolling, unbalanced gait, often due to short legs or heavy body. The manner in which ducks, penguins, or toddlers walk. To rock slightly while stepping forward.
example_sentence: Ducks waddle across the yard every morning. The little girl learned to waddle before she could run. Penguins waddle beautifully on the snow. He waddled slowly toward the sofa after dinner.

english_meaning: To move forward with short, swaying steps. To walk in a slow, rocking manner while continuing on. To progress with a duck-like gait. To keep walking clumsily from side to side. To advance slowly with a heavy, unbalanced motion.
synonyms: ["Toddle along","Amble along","Sway along","Wobble along","Shuffle along","Move along","Proceed slowly","Roll along","Trundle along","Stroll along"]
antonyms: ["Sprint along","Race along","Dash along","March along","Speed along","Stride along","Run along","Stand still","Stop","Halt"]
example_sentence: The ducklings waddled along behind their mother. The old man waddled along the sidewalk with his cane. The penguins waddled along the icy shore. The baby waddled along, laughing at every step.

english_meaning: To move about in a place with short, swaying steps. To wander here and there with a duck-like walk. To go around clumsily on unsteady legs. To move in various directions with a rocking gait. To roam a small area walking heavily.
synonyms: ["Wander around","Amble around","Toddle around","Move around","Roam around","Sway around","Wobble around","Stroll around","Meander","Loiter"]
example_sentence: The ducks waddled around the garden all afternoon. The toddler waddled around the living room excitedly. Penguins waddle around on the icy rocks. My uncle waddled around the market looking for fruit.

english_meaning: To move away with short, swaying steps. To leave a spot by walking in a rocking manner. To retreat clumsily like a duck. To depart with a heavy, unbalanced gait. To go away slowly on short legs.
synonyms: ["Toddle away","Move away","Retreat","Sway away","Wobble away","Depart","Amble away","Wander off","Withdraw","Leave"]
example_sentence: The duck waddled away when we approached. The baby waddled away from her toys. The frightened penguin waddled away quickly. He waddled away after finishing his huge meal.

english_meaning: To enter a place with short, swaying steps. To walk into somewhere with a duck-like gait. To move inside clumsily and heavily. To come into a room with a rocking motion. To step into a spot in an unbalanced manner.
synonyms: ["Enter","Walk into","Step into","Toddle into","Sway into","Move into","Come into","Wobble into","Amble into","Trundle into"]
example_sentence: The duck waddled into the pond happily. The child waddled into the kitchen looking for snacks. The penguin waddled into its burrow. He waddled into the office carrying a huge box.

english_meaning: To walk away with short swaying steps like a duck. To leave a place with a slow, rocking gait. To depart clumsily from side to side. To move off awkwardly on short legs. To go away with a heavy, rolling walk.
synonyms: ["Toddle off","Waddle away","Amble off","Wobble off","Sway off","Roll off","Stroll off","Move off","Depart","Leave"]
antonyms: ["March off","Sprint away","Stride off","Rush off","Dash away","Run off","Stand still","Stay","Arrive","Approach"]
example_sentence: The duck waddled off toward the pond. The toddler waddled off after his mother. The penguin waddled off across the ice. After lunch, he waddled off to his room for a nap.

english_meaning: To leave a place by walking with short, swaying steps. To exit somewhere in a duck-like manner. To move out clumsily and slowly. To come out of a spot with a rocking gait. To depart from an area with heavy, unbalanced steps.
synonyms: ["Exit","Leave","Walk out of","Step out of","Move out of","Emerge","Toddle out of","Depart","Come out","Withdraw"]
example_sentence: The duck waddled out of the water and shook itself dry. The toddler waddled out of the room laughing. The penguin waddled out of its nest. He waddled out of the restaurant after the enormous meal.

english_meaning: To move toward a place with short, swaying steps. To approach someone with a duck-like walk. To come across a distance with a rocking gait. To cross to another spot slowly and clumsily. To go over to a person or object walking heavily.
synonyms: ["Come over","Approach","Amble over","Move over","Walk over","Cross over","Sway over","Wobble over","Toddle over","Go over"]
example_sentence: The duck waddled over to grab the bread. My baby brother waddled over to hug me. He waddled over to the counter to order coffee. The chubby puppy waddled over to greet the guests.

english_meaning:
To walk through water, mud, or any difficult substance that slows movement. To walk through water that is not deep, such as a river or stream, usually with effort.
To move slowly and with difficulty through something that restricts movement, like snow, mud, or crowds.
Figuratively, to deal with or go through a difficult situation step by step. A shallow place in a river or stream where people can walk across.
example_sentence: The soldiers had to wade across the river during the mission. We waded through the flooded streets after the heavy rain. She waded through a pile of paperwork all afternoon. Tourists waded into the shallow sea to take photos. I spent the whole day wading through the paper work on my desk.

english_meaning: To talk or write too much without being clear or direct. It often suggests hesitation, confusion, or avoidance of the main point. A cooked food made from batter, pressed into a square or grid pattern, usually eaten sweet.
synonyms: ["Ramble","Babble","Beat around the bush","Go on and on"]
antonyms: ["Be clear","Get to the point","Be direct","Speak concisely"]
example_sentence: The speaker kept waffling and never answered the question clearly. Please do not waffle in your report and stay focused on facts. He tends to waffle when he is unsure about his decision. The essay was rejected because it waffled instead of presenting strong arguments.

english_meaning: To pass gently through the air, like a scent or sound carried on a breeze. A light object can also waft. It refers to a puff of air or a scent that is carried gently by the air. The smell of cooking often wafts from an open kitchen window.
example_sentence: The smell of baking bread began to waft from the kitchen. A cool breeze wafted in through the open window. We could hear the sound of music waft across the lake. She caught a faint waft of his cologne as he passed by. Smoke from the dying fire wafted lazily into the air.

english_meaning: To move something quickly from side to side, especially a tail or finger. To move back and forth rapidly, often to show emotion or signal something. A single movement from side to side or a person who jokes a lot.
example_sentence: The dog wagged its tail when it saw its owner. She wagged her finger to warn the child. He wagged his head in disagreement. My grandfather is known as a wag because he always tells funny stories.

english_meaning: Money paid to a worker for work done, usually daily or weekly. A fixed regular payment earned by a worker, especially for manual or hourly work. Wages are often paid daily, weekly, or based on hours worked. To carry on or engage in something such as a war, struggle, or campaign.
example_sentence: The workers demanded higher wages due to rising prices. He earns his wage by working at a construction site. The country decided to wage a war against corruption. They are waging a campaign to protect the environment.

english_meaning: A bet placed on the outcome of an uncertain event. The act of risking something on the result of a contest or chance. To gamble money or valuables. To promise or assert with confidence. Something staked as a pledge.
example_sentence: He placed a small wager on the horse race. I would wager that she will win the election. They wagered a large sum on the match. She was ready to wager her savings on the deal.

english_meaning: Playfully mischievous or humorous. Characterized by jokes and pranks. A waggish remark is meant to be funny but can also be slightly teasing or roguish, delivered with a clever twinkle in the eye.
example_sentence: He gave a waggish grin after hiding his friend's keys. The professor was known for his waggish sense of humor, often making dry jokes during lectures. Her waggish comments kept the mood light during the otherwise tedious meeting. With a waggish wink, she slipped him the answer.

english_meaning: To make a long, loud, high noise because you are sad or in pain. To cry or complain about something in a loud high voice. A long, loud, high cry expressing pain or very sad feelings.
example_sentence:
The little girl was wailing miserably. The child let out a high-pitched wail. A crowd of women followed the coffin, weeping and wailing.
He wailed with despair.
She wailed for her dead husband.

english_meaning: The narrow part of the human body between the ribs and the hips. The middle section of the body where a belt is usually worn. The part of a garment that covers or fits the middle of the body. A narrow middle part of an object such as a violin or an hourglass.
example_sentence: She tied a scarf around her waist. He has lost several inches from his waist this year. The water came up to my waist. The dress is fitted at the waist and loose below.

english_meaning: Ready and available to take over or step in when needed. Waiting quietly nearby for the right chance to act. Prepared to replace someone in a role or position at short notice. About to become important or come into use very soon.
example_sentence: A younger player is waiting in the wings to replace the injured captain. Several buyers are waiting in the wings if this deal falls through. She has been waiting in the wings for a promotion for two years. New technology is waiting in the wings to change the whole industry.

english_meaning: To voluntarily give up a right, claim, or privilege. To choose not to insist on something one is entitled to. To officially decide not to apply a rule or charge. To refrain from enforcing a regulation. To set aside or postpone the use of a right.
example_sentence: The judge agreed to waive the court fee for the poor applicant. The company decided to waive the joining fee for new members. He waived his right to remain silent and answered every question. The university waived the entrance test for top students. The hotel waived the cancellation charges as a gesture of goodwill.

english_meaning: An official statement saying that a right or claim has been given up. A document showing that someone has agreed to give up a legal right. The act of giving up a right, claim, or privilege voluntarily. A formal written agreement of surrender of a right. Permission to ignore or break a rule in a particular case.
example_sentence: All players had to sign a waiver before participating in the tournament. The university granted him a tuition fee waiver due to his financial situation. She signed a waiver giving up her right to sue the company. The bank offered a waiver of late payment charges this month. Visitors must sign a waiver before entering the adventure park.

word: Wake up and smell the coffee
english_meaning: Realize the truth or become aware of reality. Used to tell someone to stop ignoring what is happening and understand the real situation. It often means a person should become more practical, alert, or realistic about facts and problems around them.
synonyms: ["Face reality","Open your eyes","Get real","Become aware","Realize the truth","Wise up","Be realistic"]
antonyms: ["Ignore reality","Stay unaware","Live in fantasy","Be unrealistic","Remain ignorant"]
example_sentence: You still think the company will never change. Wake up and smell the coffee. He believes he can pass the exam without studying, but he needs to wake up and smell the coffee. The team keeps losing matches, so the coach told them to wake up and smell the coffee. She ignored the rising prices for months before finally waking up and smelling the coffee.

english_meaning: To stop sleeping and become awake. To make someone realize or become alert or aware.
example_sentence: They often wake up at 7 am. Please wake up your brother; it’s time for school. She finally woke up to the truth. Wake up! You’re dreaming!.

word: Walk a mile in one's shoe
english_meaning: To understand someone’s feelings, experiences, or situation by imagining yourself in their position. It teaches empathy and compassion.
example_sentence: You cannot judge others until you walk a mile in their shoes. Before criticizing your friend, try to walk a mile in his shoes. Teachers should walk a mile in their students’ shoes to understand their struggles. Walking a mile in her shoes made me realize how strong she is.

english_meaning: To stroll or move about an area without a specific destination. To explore a place by walking through it. To bypass an obstacle or problem instead of dealing with it directly. To appear in public or go about daily life in a particular state or condition.
example_sentence: We had some free time, so we decided to walk around the city. The security guard has to walk around the building every hour. You cannot just walk around the issue without addressing it. He walks around thinking he owns the entire company.

english_meaning: To carry something with you as you move from place to place. To constantly hold onto a particular feeling, idea, or burden in your daily life. To be seen in public constantly accompanied by a specific person or thing. To suffer from an untreated medical condition while continuing normal activities.
example_sentence: He always walks around with a heavy backpack. She shouldn't walk around with so much guilt over something she couldn't control. You cannot walk around with a broken finger without seeing a doctor. They always walk around with their new puppy in the park.

english_meaning: To leave a situation or a person, often because it is difficult, dangerous, or unrewarding. To escape from a severe accident or dangerous event without serious injury. To easily win a competition or contest. To refuse to get involved in an argument or conflict.
example_sentence: Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is walk away from a toxic relationship. It was a miracle that the driver managed to walk away from such a horrific car crash. Our team was so well-prepared that we were able to walk away with the championship trophy. He decided to just walk away rather than get into a fistfight with the angry customer.

english_meaning: To leave a difficult or unpleasant situation instead of dealing with it. To abandon a responsibility, relationship, or commitment. To survive a serious accident or dangerous event without major injuries. To refuse an offer or decline a deal that does not meet your expectations.
example_sentence: Sometimes it is better to walk away from an argument than to say something hurtful. He decided to walk away from the business when it started losing money. It is a miracle that they managed to walk away from that terrible car crash. You should be prepared to walk away from the negotiation if they do not offer a fair price.

english_meaning: To return to a previous place on foot. To retreat or move backward from a situation or physical position. To guide someone back to a specific location by walking alongside them. To reverse or modify a previously stated opinion or policy.
example_sentence: We decided to walk back to the hotel after dinner. The soldiers were ordered to walk back slowly to avoid detection. I will walk you back to your car so you are not alone. The politician tried to walk back his controversial comments during the interview.

english_meaning: To retract, reverse, or soften a previous statement, claim, or policy. To admit publicly that something said earlier was incorrect or overly harsh. To carefully reverse an action or decision that caused public controversy.
example_sentence: The CEO had to walk back his statement about firing employees. The company attempted to walk the new pricing policy back after customer complaints. He was forced to walk back the allegations when no evidence was found. You cannot simply walk back a promise that has already caused so much damage.

english_meaning: To move on foot along a street, path, or corridor. To descend a staircase or slope on foot. To escort someone ceremoniously down an aisle, especially in a wedding. To easily defeat someone or win something with very little effort.
example_sentence: We used to walk down this street every morning to catch the bus. She carefully walked down the stairs to greet her guests. The proud father walked his daughter down the aisle. The dominant team managed to walk down their opponents in the final match.

english_meaning: To enter a room or building by walking. To arrive at a place unexpectedly or without a prior appointment. To interrupt a private situation by entering a room unannounced. A person who arrives without an appointment to receive a service. A large storage space or closet that a person can step inside.
antonyms: ["Leave","Exit","Depart","Go out","Walk out","Book in advance","Make an appointment"]
example_sentence: She decided to walk in through the front door. We do not take reservations, so you can simply walk in. He did not knock and just walked in while I was changing. The medical clinic accepts walk-ins for flu shots every morning.

english_meaning: To enter a place or enclosed space on foot. To collide with someone or something accidentally while walking. To unknowingly encounter or enter a dangerous, difficult, or tricky situation. To easily obtain a job or position without much effort or competition.
synonyms: ["Enter","Step into","Bump into","Collide with","Crash into","Stumble upon","Encounter","Fall into","Blunder into"]
example_sentence: She opened the door and walked into the crowded room. I was not paying attention and walked straight into a glass door. You are walking into a trap if you trust that unreliable company. Because of his father's connections, he just walked into a well-paying job.

english_meaning: To leave a place suddenly, especially because you are angry or upset. To get rid of a bad feeling, mild pain, or the effects of a large meal by going for a walk. To depart from a job in order to go on strike. To win a contest easily and leave.
example_sentence: She got angry during the argument and decided to walk off. He ate too much at dinner and went outside to walk it off. The workers threatened to walk off the job if their demands were not met. After being fouled, the player tried to walk off the pain.

english_meaning: To steal something, usually easily or without being noticed. To win a prize, competition, or award very easily. To take something away that belongs to someone else without permission. To leave a place taking something valuable with you.
example_sentence: Someone managed to walk off with my laptop while I was getting coffee. The talented young actor walked off with the top prize at the film festival. You cannot just walk off with my ideas and claim them as your own. Our team walked off with the championship trophy after a flawless performance.

english_meaning: To continue walking without stopping or pausing. To step or tread on a particular surface or object. To join a sports team or theatrical cast without being formally recruited or auditioned. An uncredited or minor role in a play or movie.
example_sentence: Despite the heavy rain, the hikers decided to walk on. Be careful not to walk on the newly planted grass. He managed to walk on to the college basketball team during his freshman year. She ignored the distraction on the street and just walked on.

english_meaning: To feel extremely happy or joyful, to be in a state of great delight.
example_sentence:
She was walking on air after hearing the good news 
He walked on air when he got his first job. They were walking on air after their wedding ceremony. I have been walking on air since I met you.

english_meaning: To act very carefully to avoid upsetting someone. To be extremely cautious in words and actions around a sensitive person. To behave in a delicate manner to prevent conflict or trouble. To handle a fragile situation with great care. To tiptoe around someone or a topic to keep peace.
synonyms: ["Tread carefully","Tiptoe around","Be cautious","Handle with care","Beware","Mind one’s words","Be delicate","Tread lightly","Be wary","Stay alert"]
antonyms: ["Be reckless","Speak bluntly","Act carelessly","Be tactless","Offend openly","Charge in","Be indifferent","Ignore feelings","Provoke","Be rude"]
example_sentence: Since the argument, everyone has been walking on eggshells at home. Employees walk on eggshells around the strict manager. I feel like I’m walking on eggshells whenever we discuss politics. She walked on eggshells to avoid upsetting her sick mother.

english_meaning: To leave a place or event suddenly, often as an expression of disapproval or anger. To go on a strike by leaving one's workplace. To abandon a person or a responsibility abruptly. A sudden departure or strike by workers as a protest.
example_sentence: Half the audience decided to walk out of the terrible movie before it ended. The factory workers threatened to walk out if their demands for better pay were not met. It is deeply unfair to just walk out on your family when they need you the most. The sudden walk out by the teachers caused the school to close for the day.

english_meaning: To abandon someone, especially a romantic partner or family member, suddenly and irresponsibly. To leave a situation, task, or obligation before it is finished. To abruptly exit a performance or meeting as a sign of strong disapproval. To walk away from a commitment, leaving others in a difficult position.
example_sentence: He walked out on his wife and children without giving any explanation. You cannot just walk out on your contractual obligations when things get difficult. Several angry spectators walked out on the play during the second act. She promised never to walk out on her friends in their time of need.

english_meaning: To leave someone suddenly, ending a relationship or commitment. To abandon a partner, family member or friend who depends on you. To leave a meeting, job or agreement in protest. To desert someone at a difficult time without proper explanation.
example_sentence: He walked out on his family without leaving a note. She walked out on the meeting when her ideas were ignored. I never imagined my best friend would walk out on me like that. The singer walked out on the band just before the tour began.

english_meaning: To treat someone poorly by ignoring their feelings, rights, or taking advantage of them. To defeat an opponent very easily in a game or competition. To move across a space or surface on foot. An easy victory or something that is very easy to accomplish.
example_sentence: You must stand up for yourself and not let people walk over you. The champion team was able to walk over their rivals in the tournament. I decided to walk over the bridge to enjoy the beautiful view. The game turned out to be a complete walkover for the home team.

english_meaning: To approach a specific person, place, or thing on foot. To cross a room or space in order to reach a particular destination. To go towards someone in order to speak with them or interact.
synonyms: ["Approach","Go Towards","Move Towards","Advance To","Step Towards","Cross To","Head To","Proceed To","Draw Near","Close In On"]
example_sentence: He decided to walk over to the window and look outside. She will walk over to her friend's house after the school ends. I watched him walk over to the manager to ask an important question. Let's walk over to the cafe across the street for a quick break.

english_meaning: To move along on foot and go beyond a specific person, place, or thing. To physically pass by something without stopping or noticing it. To deliberately ignore someone by walking away and not acknowledging them. To fail to notice an opportunity that is right in front of you.
example_sentence: I walk past the same bakery every morning on my way to work. She was so angry that she just walked past me without saying hello. You cannot simply walk past someone who is asking for emergency medical help. He walked past the obvious solution while trying to fix the engine.

english_meaning: To be forced to walk off a plank over the sea as a form of execution, once associated with pirates. Figuratively, to be dismissed from a job or forced to accept punishment.
synonyms: ["Be dismissed","Be sacked","Face punishment","Be ousted","Be forced out"]
example_sentence: In the film, the captives were made to walk the plank. After the scandal, the manager had to walk the plank. He knew he would walk the plank if the deal collapsed. Pirates in the story threatened to make him walk the plank.

english_meaning: To act according to what one says; to follow through on promises or statements. Demonstrating through actions that one’s words, commitments, or claims are genuine. It emphasizes integrity and consistency between what someone says and what they do.
synonyms: ["Practice what you preach","Back up your words","Live up to your word","Act on your promises"]
antonyms: ["Talk without action","Hypocrisy","Empty promises","Fail to follow through"]
example_sentence: If you want people to respect your leadership, you need to walk the talk. Politicians must walk the talk on climate change, not just make speeches. The manager promised a safe workplace and walked the talk by implementing strict safety measures. She talks about sustainability and truly walks the talk by using eco-friendly products daily.

english_meaning: To explain or demonstrate a process or task to someone step by step. To practice a play, presentation, or procedure from beginning to end slowly. To move on foot through a particular area, building, or space. A step-by-step demonstration or guide to help someone complete a task.
example_sentence: The technician will walk you through the installation process to ensure it is done right. The director asked the actors to walk through the final scene one more time. We decided to walk through the park on our way back home. I watched a video walk through to figure out how to beat the difficult game level.

english_meaning: To approach someone or something on foot, often confidently or unexpectedly. To climb stairs, a hill, or an incline using one's feet. An apartment, building, or service window that requires approaching on foot or climbing stairs.
example_sentence: A stranger decided to walk up and ask me for directions to the train station. You have to walk up three flights of stairs to get to his apartment. She did not hesitate to walk up to the celebrity and ask for an autograph. They live in a small walk up in the historic center of the city.

english_meaning: To approach someone or something on foot. To move closer to a person or object in a confident or deliberate manner. To confront someone directly by coming very close to them.
synonyms: ["Approach","Go up to","Advance towards","Step up to","Come up to","Draw near","Move toward","Confront"]
example_sentence: I decided to walk up to the manager and ask for a raise. A stranger walked up to me on the street and asked for directions. She walked up to the microphone and began her speech. He walked up to the counter to place his order.

english_meaning: To live a devout and righteous life. To remain in close spiritual fellowship with the Almighty. To follow religious teachings faithfully in daily conduct. To live according to divine guidance.
synonyms: ["Live piously","Be devout","Follow the faith","Live righteously","Be godly"]
example_sentence: He tried to walk with God in every decision he made. The preacher urged the congregation to walk with God. She found peace when she began to walk with God. Those who walk with God are seldom afraid.

english_meaning: To feel extremely happy, joyful, or delighted, as if floating in the air because of happiness. It’s used when someone is overjoyed due to good news or success.
example_sentence: She’s been walking on air since the wedding. After getting his dream job, he was walking on air all day. She’s been walking on air since she got engaged. They were walking on air after hearing the good news He felt like walking on air when he passed the exam with top marks.

english_meaning: A long, slender insect whose body closely resembles a twig or stick. An insect that avoids predators through remarkable camouflage and stillness. A stick or cane used for support while walking. Any object used as an aid to balance or mobility by a person on foot.
example_sentence: The walking stick sat motionless on the branch for hours. My grandfather cannot walk far without his walking stick. A walking stick is almost impossible to spot among dry twigs. She bought a wooden walking stick during the hike.

english_meaning: To enclose or confine someone or something within a particular space by building or using walls. To block an opening or space with a wall. To surround a place so as to isolate or protect it. To restrict freedom of movement or vision by surrounding with barriers.
example_sentence: The ancient city was walled in to protect the inhabitants from invading armies. We decided to wall in the patio to create a more private outdoor living space. During the renovation, they had to wall in the old doorway to create a solid surface for the new kitchen. The prisoner felt suffocated as if the very air was being walled in around him.

english_meaning: To separate or isolate a space or object by building a wall. To create a barrier that prevents access or sight. To emotionally distance oneself from others. To sequester or partition a specific area within a larger one.
example_sentence: The construction workers began to wall off the construction site for public safety. She tended to wall off her emotions after the traumatic experience. The doctors had to wall off the infected area of the lung to prevent the spread of disease. They decided to wall off the pantry to create a more organized kitchen space.

english_meaning: To enclose or seal a space completely by building a wall around or across it. To trap or imprison someone or something inside a walled structure. To close off one's emotions or isolate oneself from other people.
example_sentence: The workers decided to wall up the old fireplace to stop the draft. Legend says the cruel king would wall up his enemies alive in the dungeon. After his wife died, he started to wall up his feelings and stopped talking to his friends. They had to wall up the tunnel entrance to prevent anyone from entering.

english_meaning: A small, flat case, usually made of leather or plastic, used for carrying paper money, credit cards, and identification. A pocketbook or folder-like container for personal documents. A software application or hardware device that stores digital currency and private keys for cryptocurrency transactions. An old-fashioned term for a bag or knapsack used by travelers for food or belongings.
example_sentence: He pulled a ten-dollar bill out of his leather wallet to pay for the coffee. She realized she had left her wallet on the bus and immediately called the transit office. I need to back up my digital wallet to ensure my Bitcoin remains secure. The hiker carried a small canvas wallet containing his maps and emergency supplies.

english_meaning: A person who has no one to dance with or who feels shy, awkward, or excluded at a party. Someone who remains on the sidelines of a social activity. A type of garden plant (Erysimum) known for its fragrant yellow, orange, or red flowers. A person who remains unnoticed or avoids attention in social settings.
antonyms: ["Extrovert","Exhibitionist","Socialite","Life of the party","Show-off","Mingler","Social butterfly","Confident person","Communicator","Outgoing person"]
example_sentence: She was a self-described wallflower who preferred books to loud parties. At the wedding, he felt like a total wallflower because he didn't know how to dance. The garden was filled with the sweet scent of the blooming wallflower. Being a wallflower allowed him to observe people without the pressure of interacting.

english_meaning: The act of constructing a wall or walls. Material used for the making of walls. An enclosure or partition made of brick, stone, or similar materials. The process of dividing an area with vertical structures. The act of surrounding or fortifying a place with walls.
example_sentence: The ancient city was protected by extensive stone walling. They spent the entire summer walling the garden to keep out the deer. The contractor provided an estimate for the decorative brick walling. Proper walling is essential for the structural integrity of the basement.

english_meaning: It means creating emotional barriers to protect oneself from being hurt. It refers to isolating oneself from social connections or intimate relationships. It describes a state of extreme defensiveness and unwillingness to trust others. It indicates an intentional withdrawal from the outside world.
example_sentence: After the breakup, he built thick walls around himself to avoid further pain. You cannot form deep relationships if you keep putting walls around you. She finally started breaking down the walls around her and letting people in. Therapy helped him recognize the invisible walls around him.

english_meaning: A slender stick or rod held in the hand. It is often used for pointing, measuring, or as a symbol of authority. In fiction and folklore, a wand is an instrument used by a magician, sorcerer, or fairy to perform magic spells and channel magical energy.
example_sentence: The fairy godmother waved her wand and turned the pumpkin into a carriage. With a flick of his wand, the magician made the rabbit disappear. The conductor used a thin wand to direct the orchestra. Harry Potter is famous for his powerful wizarding wand.

english_meaning: To move about from place to place aimlessly. To move without purpose, often in search of livelihood. Of the mind, to lose focus or clarity of argument or attention.
example_sentence:
We spent the morning wandering around the old part of the city.
