She was found several hours later, wandering the streets, lost. They had wandered from the path into the woods.

english_meaning: A strong desire to travel and explore the world. An intense longing to wander or see new places. A passion for exploring unfamiliar lands. The urge to leave home and experience adventure. A deep-seated love of travel.
example_sentence: Her wanderlust took her to more than thirty countries. He felt a strong wanderlust after graduating from college. The photos on the wall reflected her endless wanderlust. Wanderlust runs deep in his family.

english_meaning: To decrease gradually in size, strength, importance, or intensity. To diminish or fade over a period of time. To approach an end or become weaker. Specifically, of the moon: to show a progressively smaller illuminated area, as after being full. Broadly, it refers to any gradual decline in power, popularity, influence, brightness, or vigor.
example_sentence: His influence in the party began to wane after the election defeat. As the fire started to wane, the room grew cold and dark. Public interest in the old singer's music has waned over the past decade. The moon will wane over the coming nights until it disappears from view. Her enthusiasm for the project waned as the difficulties increased.

english_meaning: To manage to obtain or achieve something by clever or tricky means. To manipulate a situation cleverly or deceitfully to get what you want, often by persuasion, negotiation, or cunning methods.
example_sentence: She managed to wangle an invitation to the exclusive party. He wangled his way out of trouble by lying. I wangle a few extra days off work every year. They wangle the best seats at the theater through connections.

english_meaning: To wish to leave one's current club, team, or employer, especially in sport. To desire a transfer or move elsewhere.
example_sentence: The striker wants away before the transfer window closes. Two senior players are said to want away this season. He made it clear in the interview that he wanted away. The manager refused to sell the midfielder even though he wanted away.

english_meaning: To wish to have something returned that was lost, lent, or taken away. To wish to return to a former place, job, or relationship. To desire the restoration of a previous situation.
example_sentence: I lent him my camera and now I want it back. She wants her old job back at the hospital. After the argument, he wanted her back in his life. The village wants back the land it lost years ago.

english_meaning: To lack or be without something that is needed. To be in need of a basic necessity. Used mainly in negative sentences to say that someone has everything they need.
example_sentence: The children never wanted for anything while their grandfather was alive. He works hard so that his family will not want for food or shelter. Despite their simple life, they wanted for nothing. Many families in the region want for clean drinking water.

english_meaning: To wish to come inside a place. To wish to be included in a plan, deal, group, or activity. To express eagerness to participate.
example_sentence: The children are at the gate and want in. If the plan is really that profitable, I want in. He heard about the startup and immediately wanted in. She knocked twice to show that she wanted in.

english_meaning: To wish to enter a place, room, or building. To wish to join or become part of a group, organization, or activity. To desire involvement in a particular situation or deal.
synonyms: ["Wish to enter","Seek entry","Desire to join","Want in","Apply for","Seek admission"]
example_sentence: The cat is scratching at the door because it wants into the house. He wants into the family business next year. Several investors want into the project before it launches. She knocked loudly, clearly wanting into the office.

english_meaning: To try to enjoy the benefits of two opposing situations or attitudes at the same time. To refuse to accept the drawbacks that come with a chosen position. To behave inconsistently in order to gain advantage from both sides.
synonyms: ["Have it both ways","Play both sides","Blow hot and cold","Sit on the fence","Hedge"]
antonyms: ["Choose one side","Take a stand","Commit","Accept the consequences","Be consistent"]
example_sentence: You cannot want it both ways by demanding freedom and protection at once. The government wants it both ways on taxes and public spending. He wants it both ways, complaining about the rules while enjoying their benefits. Voters accused the party of wanting it both ways.

english_meaning: To wish to have no dealings, contact, or association with a person. To refuse to be involved with someone or something considered undesirable.
synonyms: ["Have no truck with","Avoid","Shun","Boycott","Steer clear of","Keep away from","Reject"]
example_sentence: The old shopkeeper wants no truck with the new landlord. She wants no truck with people who spread rumours. Our team wants no truck with dishonest suppliers. He made it clear he wanted no truck with the scheme.

english_meaning: To refuse to accept or take part in something. To reject an offer, idea, or behaviour completely. To make clear that one will not tolerate something.
example_sentence: She wants none of their excuses this time. I want none of the money you made that way. The teacher wants none of that behaviour in her classroom. He wanted none of the credit for the success.

english_meaning: Do not suffer from shortage or need. The closing part of the proverb 'Waste not, want not', meaning that avoiding waste protects one from future need.
synonyms: ["Lack nothing","Be provided for","Have enough","Be secure","Be self-sufficient"]
example_sentence: Waste not, want not, as my mother always reminded us. Those who save carefully will want not in old age. The saying ends with the promise that you will want not. Live simply and you will want not.

english_meaning: To wish to leave a place, room, or enclosed space. To wish to end one's involvement in a relationship, agreement, job, or situation. To desire release or escape from something unpleasant.
example_sentence: The dog is barking at the door and wants out. After two difficult years, he simply wanted out of the marriage. Two partners want out of the deal before the deadline. She wanted out of the meeting as soon as it began.

english_meaning: To wish to withdraw from an agreement, arrangement, relationship, or commitment. To wish to leave a place or situation. To seek release from an obligation.
synonyms: ["Withdraw from","Back out of","Pull out of","Quit","Escape from","Opt out of","Exit"]
example_sentence: He wants out of the contract before the next payment is due. She wanted out of the argument as quickly as possible. Two members want out of the partnership. The player wants out of his current club.

english_meaning: To wish to get free from a person one finds troublesome or unwanted. To desire that someone leave, be dismissed, or be removed. To wish to end a connection with someone.
synonyms: ["Want shot of","Wish to remove","Get rid of","Dismiss","Expel","Oust","Be free of"]
example_sentence: The manager clearly wants rid of the new supervisor. They wanted rid of him long before he finally resigned. She wants rid of the tenant who never pays on time. Some board members want rid of the chairman.

word: Want the ground to swallow you up
english_meaning: To feel extremely embarrassed or ashamed and wish to disappear. A strong feeling of embarrassment, shame, or humiliation. A person feels so uncomfortable in a situation that they wish they could vanish from that place instantly, as if the ground would open and hide them.
synonyms: ["Feel extremely embarrassed","Want to disappear","Feel ashamed","Be mortified","Feel humiliated"]
antonyms: ["Feel confident","Feel proud","Feel comfortable","Be at ease","Feel bold"]
example_sentence: When I slipped and fell in front of everyone, I wanted the ground to swallow me up. He forgot his speech on stage and wished the ground would swallow him up. She felt so embarrassed by her mistake that she wanted the ground to swallow her up. I called my teacher “mom” by accident and wanted the ground to swallow me up.

english_meaning: Lacking or absent; not present when needed. Not good enough; falling short of a required standard. Feeling or expressing a desire for something. Deficient in a particular quality.
example_sentence: The report was found wanting in several important details. Courage was the one quality he was never wanting in. She left the meeting wanting a clearer answer. Their hospitality left nothing wanting.

english_meaning: Deliberate and unprovoked, especially of cruelty or damage. Sexually immodest or promiscuous. Growing or spreading in an uncontrolled way. A person who behaves in a sexually immoral manner.
example_sentence: The report condemned the wanton destruction of forests. He was charged with the wanton killing of animals. Wanton weeds had taken over the garden. Her wanton disregard for the rules shocked the committee.

english_meaning: In a deliberately cruel or unjustified manner. Without any reason, restraint, or concern for the consequences. In a reckless or careless way. In a sexually immodest or promiscuous manner.
example_sentence: The soldiers wantonly destroyed the village crops. He wantonly ignored every warning he was given. Public property was wantonly damaged during the riot. She spent money wantonly and soon had nothing left.

english_meaning: The quality of being deliberately cruel, violent, or destructive without reason. Lack of restraint, discipline, or moral control. Reckless extravagance or carelessness. Sexual immodesty or promiscuous behaviour.
example_sentence: The report condemned the wantonness of the attack on civilians. His wantonness with money left the family in debt. She was shocked by the wantonness of the destruction. Critics accused the film of glorifying wantonness.

english_meaning: To protect or guard yourself (or someone) from danger, harm, disease, evil, or any negative influence.
example_sentence: People used herbs to ward against evil spirits in ancient times. Vaccinations help ward against infectious diseases. He carried an umbrella to ward against the rain. Education can ward against ignorance and intolerance.

english_meaning: To keep something harmful, evil, or unpleasant away. To protect or defend oneself from danger, illness, bad luck, or evil influences.
example_sentence: The villagers lit candles to ward away evil spirits She wore a charm to ward away bad luck. Strong immunity can ward away many diseases. He used humor to ward away his fears.

english_meaning: To prevent or protect against something unpleasant, harmful, or dangerous. To keep something or someone away.
example_sentence: He wore a lucky charm to ward off bad luck. They used mosquito nets to ward off insects. The villagers lit fires to ward off wild animals. Drinking warm water can help ward off a cold.

english_meaning: The act of guarding or protecting against something. The action of repelling, averting, or deflecting a danger or an evil influence. It refers to a defensive action or stance taken to protect oneself or others from harm.
example_sentence: The knight was focused on warding off the dragon's fiery breath. They used special charms for warding away evil spirits. Her quick reflexes were perfect for warding the sudden blows. Warding against diseases requires a strong immune system. The government is warding off a potential economic crisis.

english_meaning: A large building where goods, raw materials, or products are stored before they are sold, distributed, or used. It is often used by manufacturers, importers, exporters, wholesalers, and transport companies for storage purposes.
example_sentence: The company built a new warehouse near the port to store imported goods. All the relief supplies are kept in a central warehouse before distribution. The warehouse was filled with boxes of clothes and food items. Our warehouse manager ensures every product is properly labeled and recorded.

english_meaning: Careful caution when facing possible danger or problems. A watchful attitude that avoids risk. Reluctance to trust someone or something too quickly. Alertness combined with a degree of suspicion. The habit of acting carefully to avoid being deceived.
example_sentence: He treated the offer with a natural wariness. Her wariness of strangers came from past experience. There is growing wariness about online payments. The dog approached the visitor with obvious wariness.

english_meaning: Having or giving out a moderate degree of heat. Showing kindness, enthusiasm, or affection towards others. To make someone or something comfortably hot. To begin to feel more friendly or affectionate towards someone. A moderately hot temperature or environment.
example_sentence: We sat by the fire to keep warm during the winter night. She gave us a very warm and friendly welcome. Please warm the soup in the microwave before eating it. It took a while for the stray cat to warm to us.

english_meaning: Having a relatively high and constant body temperature largely independent of the surroundings. It also metaphorically means being passionate, emotional, or enthusiastically affectionate. This biological trait is characteristic of mammals and birds, requiring them to constantly consume energy.
example_sentence: Mammals and birds are generally warm blooded creatures. As a warm blooded individual, he showed his feelings openly and passionately. The discovery showed that some dinosaurs might have been warm blooded. Warm blooded animals must eat frequently to maintain their metabolism. Being a warm blooded species requires a lot of energy expenditure.

english_meaning: To perform light exercises at the end of a period of vigorous physical activity to allow the body to recover. To gradually lower the heart rate and stretch muscles after a workout. A period of gentle exercise and stretching after sports.
example_sentence: Make sure you warm down properly after your run to prevent muscle stiffness. The team spent ten minutes warming down on the pitch. If you don't warm down after heavy lifting, you will feel sore tomorrow. A good warm down is just as important as the initial stretch.

english_meaning: To heat cooked food again so that it can be eaten later. To present old ideas, stories, or arguments again without adding anything fresh or original.
example_sentence: She warmed over last night’s dinner. The editor warmed over an old article. They warmed over last year’s plan. He warmed over the same argument.

english_meaning: To become warm all the way inside, or to make something warm completely. To heat something until the warmth reaches its center, not just the surface.
example_sentence: Heat the soup slowly so it warms through evenly. After sitting by the fire, she finally warmed through. Make sure the bread is warmed through before serving it. He drank hot tea to warm himself through after the rain.

english_meaning: To heat something completely so that warmth reaches the inside. To heat food, a room, or any object thoroughly so that the warmth spreads evenly from the outside to the inside.
example_sentence: The message warmed through to the team. Her kindness warmed through to everyone. The food warmed through to the center. The story warmed through to listeners.

english_meaning: To slowly develop a feeling of liking, approval, or friendliness toward someone or something.
example_sentence: She warmed to the idea. The class warmed to the new teacher. He warmed to his coworkers. They warmed to the proposal.

english_meaning: To begin to like someone or something gradually. To slowly develop friendly feelings, affection, or approval for a person, idea, or situation after initially feeling unsure, distant, or neutral. It suggests a gradual emotional change rather than sudden liking.
example_sentence: She warmed towards him over time. The audience warmed towards the speaker. They warmed towards the idea. He warmed towards his colleagues.

english_meaning: To begin to like or enjoy a person, idea, or situation after initially disliking or being unsure about them. To become more friendly or comfortable with someone over time. To gradually accept an idea or proposal. To become enthusiastic about a new task or environment.
synonyms: ["Accept","Like","Embrace","Become friendly with","Get used to","Adapt to","Favor","Be won over by","Soften towards"]
example_sentence: The stray cat took a few days to warm up to her new owners. I was hesitant about the new software at first, but I am starting to warm up to it. It took the board members a long time to warm up to the controversial marketing strategy. As the evening progressed, the shy child began to warm up to the other kids at the party.

english_meaning: A warm-blooded animal maintains a relatively constant body temperature regardless of the surrounding environment. Animals, such as mammals and birds, that can regulate and maintain their internal body temperature through metabolic processes, even when external temperatures change. The term is also used figuratively to describe a person who is passionate, emotional, energetic, affectionate, or full of strong feelings.
example_sentence: Humans are warm-blooded animals that maintain a constant body temperature. Birds remain active in winter because they are warm-blooded. She is a warm-blooded person who cares deeply about others. The warm-blooded athlete showed great passion during the competition.

english_meaning: A person who encourages or tries to start war or conflict, often for political power, profit, or influence. A warmonger promotes hostility between nations or groups instead of peaceful solutions.
example_sentence: Many citizens protested against the leader because they believed he was a warmonger. Historians often debate whether certain rulers were defenders of their country or warmongers. The journalist criticized politicians who acted like warmongers during the crisis. Peace activists try to challenge the ideas spread by warmongers.

english_meaning: The quality, state, or sensation of being warm or having a moderate degree of heat. It also signifies the quality of being affectionate, kind, or emotionally resonant in relationships and interactions. Having a feeling of coziness and friendliness that puts others at ease.
example_sentence: We gathered around the fire to enjoy its comforting warmth. I could feel the warmth of her smile from across the room. He thanked his hosts for the warmth and hospitality they showed him. The morning sun provided a gentle warmth that melted the frost. There was a noticeable warmth in his voice when he spoke about his childhood.

english_meaning: To prepare the body for physical activity by doing light exercise. To prepare oneself mentally or physically for an activity. To make something warmer. To become more active, interested, or enthusiastic.
example_sentence: I’II warm up some meat for dinner. She warmed up before running. The speaker took a few minutes to warm up before the presentation. She warmed up the soup before serving it. The audience began to warm up as the concert continued.

english_meaning: A legal document authorizing police or another official to arrest someone, search a place, seize property, or perform another action. An official certificate, authorization, or written order. A reason or justification for an action, belief, or statement. Evidence or circumstances sufficient to make something necessary or appropriate. To justify or provide good reason for something. To guarantee or officially assure a result, quality, or condition. To call for or deserve a particular response.
example_sentence: The police obtained a warrant before searching the house. There is no warrant for such a serious accusation. The evidence warrants a full investigation. This minor mistake does not warrant dismissal.

english_meaning: A written promise from a manufacturer or seller to repair, replace, or refund a product if specified problems arise within a stated period. The period or conditions covered by such a promise. A formal assurance that facts, quality, ownership, or performance meet stated requirements. In law, a contractual promise whose breach may give a right to damages.
example_sentence: The laptop comes with a two-year warranty. The store repaired the faulty appliance under warranty. Read the warranty carefully before buying the machine. The contract includes a warranty that the seller owns the property.

english_meaning: A brave and experienced fighter, especially in past times. A soldier engaged in war or battle. A person who fights determinedly for a cause or belief. Someone who shows great courage in facing hardship.
example_sentence: The ancient warrior was buried with his sword and shield. She is a tireless warrior for children's education. The old warrior told stories of long-forgotten battles. Cancer patients are often called warriors for their courage.

english_meaning: Covered with or having warts or wart-like growths. Resembling a wart in texture or appearance. It describes skin or surfaces that are rough, bumpy, and uneven due to small, hard excrescences.
example_sentence: The toad had a bumpy and warty skin that blended with the rocks. The old tree trunk possessed a warty texture that felt rough to the touch. A warty growth appeared on the back of his hand. Many species of pumpkins have a uniquely warty rind. The witch in the fairy tale was depicted with a scary warty face.

english_meaning: Feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems. It describes a state of being watchful or on one's guard against deception or trickery. One is often alert and suspicious in situations that seem uncertain.
example_sentence: She gave the stranger a wary look before answering the door. The cat kept a wary eye on the dog across the room. Investors are increasingly wary of the volatile stock market. You should be wary of any deal that seems too good to be true.

english_meaning: Careful or cautious about someone or something. Feeling suspicion because there may be danger, risk, or deception. Reluctant to trust or accept something quickly. Alert and watchful in a particular situation.
example_sentence: Investors are wary of sudden market promises. She was wary of strangers after the incident. The doctor remained wary of giving a quick diagnosis. We should be wary of information that has no source.

english_meaning: To remove dirt, stains, or something unwanted with water. To carry something away by the force of water. To make feelings such as guilt, pain, or sadness disappear.
example_sentence: The flood washed away the bridge. The heavy rain washed away the footprints on the ground. She tried to wash away her worries by listening to music. Floods can wash away entire villages. He used soap to wash away the stains from his shirt.

english_meaning: To clean something thoroughly with water or another liquid To help swallow food or medicine by drinking liquid.
example_sentence: He washed down the car after the trip. After painting the walls, we washed down the brushes with water. The workers washed down the dusty floor before starting their shift. He took a pill and washed it down with a glass of water. We had spicy food, so I washed it down with a cold drink.

english_meaning: To remove dirt, stains, or unwanted substances from something by washing. To be removed or cleaned away by the action of water.
example_sentence: The mud washed off easily. he tried to wash off the paint from her hands. The rain will wash off the dust from the leaves. I need to wash off the mud before entering the house. The ink stain is hard to wash off from the fabric.

english_meaning: To be removed or carried away by water. To cancel or spoil an event because of rain or bad weather. To fade in color (due to repeated washing or sunlight). To fail or be dismissed (especially from training or a program).
example_sentence: The cricket match was washed out by rain. The heavy rain washed out the cricket match. (canceled). The flood washed out the bridge. (carried away). His old jeans are completely washed out. (faded). He tried to become a pilot, but he washed out during training. (failed)

english_meaning: To affect someone suddenly and strongly, like a feeling or emotion. To spread across or cover something, like water or waves. To pass over without leaving much effect.
example_sentence: A sense of relief washed over her. The tide washed over the rocks. His words just washed over the audience. A wave of happiness washed over me when I heard the good news. Fear washed over the crowd as the storm grew stronger.

english_meaning: To flow through something, often cleaning or carrying things away. To pass completely through a system, process, or group. To overwhelm or strongly affect someone (for example emotions “wash through” a person).
example_sentence: The medicine washed through his system quickly. A feeling of relief washed through her after hearing the good news. The floodwaters washed through the village, destroying many houses. Fresh air washed through the room when we opened the windows. Joy washed through him as he received the award.

english_meaning: To clean one’s hands and face, especially before eating. To clean dishes after a meal. To become covered in water or carried to shore by water. To finish or conclude something.
example_sentence: He washed up after dinner. Please wash up before dinner. I’ll wash up the dishes after lunch. After the storm, a lot of debris washed up on the beach. Let’s wash up this work before we leave.

english_meaning: A flying insect with a slender body and a powerful sting, typically known for building paper nests. Unlike bees, it usually has a smooth body and can sting repeatedly. Metaphorically, it refers to a person who is irritable, snappish, or spiteful.
example_sentence: A furious wasp flew through the open window and terrorized the room. He bravely removed the wasp nest from the upper corner of the porch. A wasp sting can cause a severe allergic reaction in some individuals. Unlike honeybees, a wasp can sting multiple times without dying. She delivered a waspish response to the reporter's intrusive question.

english_meaning: To use something carelessly, extravagantly, or without a good purpose. Material that is no longer needed and is thrown away. A wide, empty, and often barren area of land. To gradually lose strength, health, or vitality. An action or use of something that does not produce a useful result.
example_sentence: Do not waste your time on useless arguments. The factory dumps its waste into the river. The desert is a vast waste of sand and rock. His health began to waste after the long illness.

english_meaning: Do not waste anything. The opening part of the proverb 'Waste not, want not', meaning that careful use of resources prevents future shortage. Used as advice to avoid extravagance.
example_sentence: Waste not, and you will always have enough for tomorrow. My grandmother lived by the rule of waste not. Waste not the water you draw from the well. In hard times people learn to waste not.

english_meaning: Using more of something than is needed, especially money, time, or resources. Causing loss or unnecessary use of things. Extravagant and careless in spending. Producing much waste or unused material. Not economical or efficient in habits.
example_sentence: Leaving lights on all day is very wasteful. Their wasteful lifestyle put them into serious debt. It is wasteful to throw away food that can still be eaten. The old machine was wasteful of both fuel and time.

english_meaning: To look carefully in order to notice someone or something. To wait and stay alert for a particular event or sign. To be careful about a possible problem or danger. To keep looking until something appears.
synonyms: ["Look out for","Keep an eye out for","Await","Anticipate","Be alert to","Monitor"]
example_sentence: Watch for the postman; the parcel should arrive today. Drivers should watch for children near the school gate. Watch for any sudden change in the patient's condition. We watched for the signal before starting the engine.

english_meaning: To be careful about one’s behavior or actions. To pay attention to what one does or says to avoid mistakes, danger, or offense. Often used as a warning to proceed cautiously.
example_sentence: Watch your step when walking on the icy pavement. He was warned to watch his step at work after the last incident. If you want to keep your job, you need to watch your step around the boss. Watch your step in negotiations, one wrong move could cost you a deal.

english_meaning: To be careful or alert, especially to avoid danger. To keep an eye out for something or someone. To be on guard against a possible threat. Used as a warning to someone to be cautious.
example_sentence: Watch out! There's a car coming. You should watch out for pickpockets in crowded markets. Watch out for slippery floors after mopping. Parents told the children to watch out while crossing the road.

english_meaning: Paying careful attention to what is happening. Alert to possible danger or problems. Observing closely in order to notice any change. Vigilant and ready to act if needed.
example_sentence: The watchful guard noticed the movement near the gate. She kept a watchful eye on the children by the pool. Under the watchful gaze of the coach, the team practised hard. Farmers must be watchful during the storm season.

english_meaning: In an alert and attentive manner. While paying close attention to what is happening. In a way that shows caution about possible danger. Observantly and carefully.
example_sentence: The dog sat watchfully beside the sleeping child. She waited watchfully near the entrance of the hall. The nurse watchfully monitored the patient all night. He watchfully checked the road before crossing.

english_meaning: The quality of being alert and attentive. Careful attention paid to what is happening around one. Readiness to notice danger or change. A state of constant vigilance.
example_sentence: His watchfulness prevented a serious accident at the site. Constant watchfulness is essential for a night guard. The success of the mission depended on their watchfulness. Parents' watchfulness keeps young children safe.

english_meaning: A large barrel for collecting rain as it flows off a roof. A large container for collecting rain that can then be used to water plants.
example_sentence: We installed a water butt in the garden to collect rainwater. The water butt was full after the heavy rain. She uses water from the water butt to water her plants. Make sure the water butt is covered to keep insects out.

english_meaning: An aquatic vegetable with a crisp white flesh, grown in marshy areas. A tuber commonly used in Asian cooking. A fruit of a floating water plant with a hard, dark shell. A crunchy edible bulb used in stir-fries, soups, and desserts. A nutritious food often eaten fresh or ground into flour.
example_sentence: Water chestnuts add a nice crunch to stir-fried vegetables. In winter, roasted water chestnuts are a popular snack. She used water chestnut flour to prepare traditional sweets. Farmers grow water chestnuts in shallow ponds.

english_meaning: A phrase used to describe an obvious or undeniable fact. Something so clear that it does not need to be explained. Used sarcastically to comment on stating the obvious. A truth known to everyone. Refers to universally accepted knowledge.
example_sentence: Saying he is smart is like saying water is wet. Of course she got the job; water is wet. Telling me that the sun is hot is like saying water is wet. Everyone knows he studies hard; water is wet.

english_meaning: A leafy green plant with small round leaves and a sharp peppery taste. An aquatic vegetable eaten raw in salads and sandwiches. The plant that grows in or beside running water. A nutritious green rich in vitamins and minerals.
example_sentence: Watercress adds a peppery bite to the salad. She grows watercress near the small stream. The sandwich was filled with cheese and watercress. Watercress soup is light and healthy.

english_meaning: Doing something useless or pointless that gives no real result. Effort that is wasted because the activity cannot produce any real benefit. Just like a plastic plant does not need water, some actions look productive but have no meaningful impact. It is often used for inefficient work, empty routines, or symbolic actions done only for appearance.
synonyms: ["Wasting effort","Futile effort","Pointless activity","Beating a dead horse","Going through the motions"]
example_sentence: Spending hours on a report that no one will read is like watering a plastic plant. Fixing a system without addressing the real issue is just watering a plastic plant. He keeps attending meetings that achieve nothing, basically watering a plastic plant. Promising change without action is like watering a plastic plant.

english_meaning: Doing something useless or ineffective. Making effort where no result is possible. An action that is pointless because it cannot produce any benefit. Just like pouring water on a stone will not help anything grow, the phrase is used when effort is wasted on something that cannot change or improve.
synonyms: ["Waste of time","Futile effort","Pointless attempt","Beating a dead horse"]
example_sentence: Trying to convince him is like watering a stone. Spending money on that broken machine is watering a stone. Teaching without student interest feels like watering a stone. Arguing with someone who never listens is just watering a stone.

english_meaning: A very large fruit with a hard green rind and sweet, watery red flesh. A summer fruit eaten chilled to cool the body. The trailing vine that produces this fruit. The refreshing juice made from this fruit.
example_sentence: Nothing beats cold watermelon on a hot afternoon. The watermelon fields lie along the riverbed. He cut the watermelon into thick red slices. She blended watermelon into a chilled juice.

english_meaning: A unit of energy equivalent to one watt of power expended for one hour. A measure representing the capacity of a battery or the energy consumed by an electrical appliance over time. A derived unit equal to 3,600 joules or 3·6 kilojoules. A practical unit used to quantify relatively small amounts of electrical energy. The product of power in watts and time in hours used to calculate electricity usage.
synonyms: ["Energy Unit","Electrical Energy","3600 Joules","Wh","Battery Capacity","Power Over Time","Kilowatt-hour Fraction","Unit Of Work","Consumption Metric","Energy Measurement","Storage Capacity","Power Usage","Quantitative Energy"]
example_sentence: The capacity of this lithium-ion battery is approximately fifty watt-hours. Each LED bulb consumes about ten watt-hours of electricity every hour it remains on. You can calculate the total energy usage by multiplying the wattage by the duration in watt-hours. The meter tracks every watt-hour used to ensure accurate billing for the household.

english_meaning: A moving ridge of water on the surface of the sea or a lake. To move your hand back and forth as a greeting or signal. A sudden increase or spread of a feeling, activity, or condition. A curving movement or shape, as in hair. A disturbance that transfers energy, such as sound or light.
example_sentence: A large wave knocked the child off his feet. She waved goodbye from the window of the train. A wave of relief passed through the waiting families. Heat waves are becoming more frequent every summer.

english_meaning: The shape of a wave when it is drawn as a graph of its value against time. A visual representation showing how a signal such as sound, light, or electricity varies over time. In electronics, the pattern traced by a varying voltage or current on an oscilloscope. In audio work, the graphical display of a recorded sound used for editing and analysis.
example_sentence: The engineer studied the waveform displayed on the oscilloscope. A pure tone produces a smooth sine waveform. The software lets you zoom into the waveform to edit the recording. Any distortion in the signal changes the shape of its waveform.

english_meaning: The distance between two successive corresponding points of a wave, such as crest to crest. A measure used to describe light, sound, radio, and other electromagnetic or mechanical waves. The specific band of radio frequency on which a station broadcasts. Informally, a person's way of thinking or point of view, especially when compared with someone else's.
example_sentence: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue light. The station broadcasts on a shortwave wavelength. Scientists measured the wavelength of the emitted radiation. The two colleagues simply were not on the same wavelength.

english_meaning: A small wave or ripple on the surface of water. A brief oscillation used in mathematics to analyse signals and images. A short wave-like function with limited duration used in data processing.
example_sentence: A gentle breeze created wavelets across the pond. Wavelets lapped softly against the side of the boat. Engineers use wavelet analysis to compress images. The wavelet transform is common in signal processing.

english_meaning: A mathematical technique that breaks a signal into small wave-like components called wavelets. A method of analysing a signal in both time and frequency at the same time. A tool widely used in image compression, noise removal, and feature detection. An alternative to the Fourier transform that works well for signals whose properties change over time.
example_sentence: The wavelet transform is often used to compress digital images. Engineers applied a wavelet transform to remove noise from the recording. Unlike the Fourier transform, the wavelet transform preserves time information. Her thesis explains the wavelet transform in simple terms.

english_meaning: To increase and decrease. To grow and then decline. To rise and fall in strength, intensity, or importance over time.
example_sentence: His confidence waxed and waned throughout the competition. Public interest in the issue waxes and wanes over time. The company’s profits wax and wane with the state of the economy. Friendships often wax and wane as people move through different stages of life. Waxing and waning is a part of life.

english_meaning: The act of traveling, especially on foot. A journey or trip made by an ordinary traveler. Passage from one place to another. The experience or process of traveling along a road. Movement across a distance as part of a journey.
example_sentence: His life of wayfare took him across many lands. The old man spoke of his years of wayfare with joy. Wayfare in ancient times was full of dangers. She loved the simple joy of wayfare on country roads.

english_meaning: A person who travels, especially on foot. A traveler or wanderer. Someone who is on a journey through unfamiliar places. A pilgrim or roamer moving from place to place. A person who spends much of their life traveling.
example_sentence: An old wayfarer stopped at the inn to rest for the night. The wayfarer walked with a small bag on his back. Many wayfarers cross this mountain pass every year. She felt like a lonely wayfarer in a strange city.

english_meaning: To stop or interrupt someone and detain them in conversation or trouble them in some other way. To lie in wait for and attack from ambush. It often implies a surprise attack or interception along a path.
example_sentence: The robbers planned to waylay the carriage as it passed through the dark forest. News reporters tried to waylay the politician outside the courthouse. I meant to leave early, but I was waylaid by a chatty neighbor. They waylaid the messenger to steal the confidential documents. Do not let anyone waylay you on your journey home tonight.

english_meaning: A foolish or stupid person. Someone who acts in a very silly, clumsy, or thoughtless way. It is usually lighthearted or mildly insulting.
example_sentence: He forgot his keys again; what a wazzock. Only a wazzock would attempt to climb that wall without safety gear. Stop acting like a wazzock and think before you speak. That wazzock nearly spilled coffee all over the new carpet.

english_meaning: A state of being happy, healthy, well-being and successful. A red, swollen mark on the skin caused by a hit, whip, or other impact.
example_sentence: The government works for the weal of its citizens. He dedicated his life to the public weal. After the accident, he had a painful weal on his arm. The horse left a long weal on the fence when it kicked.

english_meaning: Good times and bad times. Happiness and sorrow. Prosperity and adversity. The ups and downs of life.
example_sentence: True friends stand by you in weal and woe. Marriage is a bond where partners share weal and woe together. The leader promised to support his people through weal and woe. Parents remain with their children in weal and woe throughout life.

english_meaning: A large amount of money, property, or valuable possessions. The state of being rich and prosperous. A plentiful supply or abundance of something. Valuable resources of a country or community.
example_sentence: He inherited great wealth from his grandfather. The region's wealth comes mainly from oil. She has a wealth of experience in teaching. National wealth should be spent on health and education.

english_meaning: Having a large amount of money, property, resources, or valuable possessions. Rich, prosperous, and financially comfortable. Abundant in something valuable or desirable.
example_sentence: The wealthy businessman donated money to the hospital. She comes from a wealthy family but lives simply. A wealthy country can still have poor communities. The soil is wealthy in minerals. They became wealthy through years of hard work.

english_meaning: Pretending to be bad at something, or acting helpless on purpose, so that another person will do the task instead.  A behavior where a person acts incapable, careless, or unskilled deliberately to avoid responsibility, effort, or work. The person may know how to do the task, or could learn it, but chooses to perform badly so others stop asking them and take over. It is often discussed in homes, workplaces, and relationships. It means using fake inability as a tool to escape duty.
synonyms: ["Deliberate incompetence","Pretended helplessness","Feigned inability","Strategic incompetence","Manipulative helplessness","Passive avoidance","Intentional inefficiency","Avoidance behavior"]
example_sentence: He kept shrinking his clothes in the wash, and his wife felt it was weaponised incompetence so she would do all the laundry. At work, some employees use weaponised incompetence by doing tasks so poorly that the manager stops assigning them those duties. She accused her brother of weaponised incompetence when he claimed he did not know how to wash dishes properly. Weaponised incompetence can damage relationships because one person ends up carrying all the responsibility.

english_meaning: To slowly disappear or be removed through constant rubbing or use. To gradually erode. To be reduced little by little over a long period. To fade through time. It is mostly used about surfaces, materials or written marks that lose their original form because of water, wind, friction or long use.
example_sentence: The inscriptions on the old stones have worn away with time. The river has slowly worn the rocks away. The paint on the gate has worn away due to rain. The pattern on the carpet has worn away in the middle. Footsteps over centuries have worn the marble steps away.

english_meaning: To ignore things that are happening around you and focus only on one thing.
example_sentence: He wore blinkers to avoid feeling guilty. Don’t wear blinkers about your child’s behavior. The manager wore blinkers regarding corruption. You can’t wear blinkers forever.

english_meaning: To make something smaller, thinner or weaker by constant use. To gradually reduce a person's strength, energy, or resistance. To overcome opposition through persistent pressure. To exhaust by continuous effort. It is used both for physical objects that lose shape and for people whose patience, will or health is slowly broken down by ongoing demands.
example_sentence: The heels of his shoes have worn down completely. Years of stress slowly wore her down. The lawyer wore down the witness with constant questioning. Constant rain has worn down the surface of the rock. He kept asking until he wore his parents down and they agreed.

english_meaning: To gradually disappear or fade away. To lose effect over time. To slowly reduce in strength. To stop having an influence. It is most often used about feelings, sensations, pain, medicines or novelty that lessen little by little until they are no longer felt.
example_sentence: The effect of the painkiller will wear off in a few hours. His initial excitement about the new job soon wore off. The numbness from the injection slowly wore off. The novelty of the toy wore off within a week. The shine on the table has worn off over the years.

english_meaning: To pass slowly. To continue for a long time. To go by in a way that feels long or tiring. To progress gradually. It is generally used for time, evenings, hours, days or years, suggesting that the period feels slow, long or somewhat tedious as it continues.
example_sentence: As the night wore on, the guests began to leave. The meeting wore on for several hours without any decision. As the years wore on, she became more confident. The lecture wore on and the students grew restless. As winter wore on, the days became even colder.

english_meaning: To become unusable through long use. To make someone extremely tired. To exhaust completely. To use something until it is no longer effective. It refers either to objects that lose their strength and quality after long use, or to people who become physically and mentally drained because of hard work, stress or constant activity.
example_sentence: My old shoes have finally worn out after years of use. Looking after three small children wears her out by the evening. The long journey wore the travellers out completely. The carpet in the hallway has worn out in several places. Constant night shifts can wear a person out very quickly.

word: Wear the pants in the family
english_meaning: To be the person who makes the decisions and holds authority in a household. To be the dominant partner in a marriage or family. To control family matters and have the final say. An informal expression describing who is really in charge at home.
synonyms: ["Be the boss","Rule the roost","Call the shots","Be in charge","Hold the reins","Run the show","Dominate"]
example_sentence: Everyone knows his wife wears the pants in the family. He jokes that his mother wore the pants in the family. If you want a quick answer, ask whoever wears the pants in the family. She quietly wears the pants in the family without ever raising her voice.

english_meaning: To make a hole in something or become a hole through long use or friction. To use a material until it is completely worn out and pierced. To rub through the surface. It refers to cloth, leather, metal or any surface that becomes so thin from constant use that it finally breaks open.
example_sentence: The elbows of his old jacket have finally worn through. The soles of my shoes wore through after the long hike. The carpet near the door has worn through. After years of use, the bottom of the pot wore through. The knees of his trousers have almost worn through.

word: Wear your heart on your sleeve
english_meaning: To openly show your emotions without hiding them. It describes a person who expresses feelings honestly and clearly. Such a person does not conceal emotions like love, sadness, or anger, and others can easily understand how they feel. It can suggest sincerity and openness, but sometimes also emotional vulnerability.
synonyms: ["Be open about feelings","Be emotionally expressive","Show your emotions","Be transparent","Be sincere"]
antonyms: ["Hide your feelings","Be reserved","Be emotionally guarded","Keep emotions inside","Be secretive"]
example_sentence: She wears her heart on her sleeve, so everyone knows when she is upset. He is not afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve and express his love. Unlike others, she wears her heart on her sleeve and speaks honestly. Wearing your heart on your sleeve can make you vulnerable in tough situations.

english_meaning: The condition or quality of being tiring, tedious, or exhausting. A state that causes mental or physical fatigue due to dullness, length, or repetitiveness.
example_sentence: The wearisomeness of the long lecture made half the audience fall asleep. She could not bear the wearisomeness of her daily commute anymore. He complained about the wearisomeness of doing the same repetitive task every day. The sheer wearisomeness of the journey left them completely exhausted. In spite of the wearisomeness of the process, they managed to complete the project on time.

english_meaning: Feeling or showing extreme tiredness, especially as a result of excessive effort or endurance. Reluctant to see, experience, or accept any more of something. To make someone feel tired and lacking enthusiasm.
example_sentence: After walking all day, we were too weary to continue. She looked weary after working late every night. The travelers felt weary but happy when they reached home. He grew weary of hearing the same excuse again and again.

english_meaning: A small, slender carnivorous mammal related to stoats, known for its active and stealthy hunting. To achieve something by use of cunning or deceit. To evade an obligation or avoid a difficult situation.
example_sentence: The farmer saw a weasel sneaking around the chicken coop at dawn. He always tries to weasel his way out of helping with household chores. The politician managed to weasel out of the difficult question during the interview. As a sly businessman, he acts like a weasel when negotiating contracts. A weasel can squeeze through incredibly small gaps to catch its prey.

english_meaning: To survive a difficult period without serious harm. To endure a crisis successfully. To hold out until conditions improve.
example_sentence: The company managed to weather the storm of the recession. With family support, she weathered the storm of her illness. Small businesses struggled to weather the storm last year. He weathered the storm of criticism with great patience.

english_meaning: A mechanical device typically attached to an elevated structure that shows the direction of the wind. A person or thing that frequently changes their opinions or loyalties according to prevailing trends.
example_sentence: The old barn had a rusty iron weathervane shaped like a rooster on its roof. You can check the weathervane to see which way the storm is blowing. People called the local representative a weathervane because he constantly changed his stance on major issues. The wind spun the weathervane wildly during the strong hurricane. A golden weathervane sits at the very top of the church spire.

english_meaning: To make fabric carpet & basket by crossing threads or strips across over & under each other by hands or machine
example_sentence: The baskets are woven from strips of willow.

english_meaning: A customary service of reaping owed by a tenant to his lord during the Middle Ages. A historical feudal obligation involving agricultural labor. It refers to a specific type of forced or customary harvest work.
example_sentence: The peasants were summoned for the wedbedrip before the autumn rains began. Failure to attend the wedbedrip resulted in severe fines for the villagers. During the wedbedrip, tenants worked entirely for the lord's benefit. Historical records show exactly how many days of wedbedrip each family owed. The custom of wedbedrip faded as feudalism declined in England.

english_meaning: To push something into a tight space or force apart. An object shaped with one thick side and one thin side, used to split objects, lift something, or keep things tightly fixed. It also refers to anything that creates separation between people, ideas, or groups.
example_sentence: He used a wedge to split the log into two pieces. A misunderstanding drove a wedge between the friends. She placed a wedge under the door to keep it open. He wedged the box into a small corner of the room.

english_meaning: The state of being married. The condition of being legally joined in marriage. It emphasizes the formal or recognized union of two people as husband and wife.
example_sentence: They lived together in wedlock for over fifty years. Children born in wedlock have certain legal rights. She was proud to remain faithful throughout their wedlock. Many cultures have specific customs surrounding wedlock.

english_meaning: A wild plant growing where it is not wanted, especially among cultivated plants or crops. To remove unwanted plants from a garden or field. Used informally to describe the cannabis plant or marijuana. To eliminate or remove something considered undesirable from a group or situation.
example_sentence: The gardener spent the morning pulling weeds from the vegetable patch.  Without regular care, weeds can quickly overtake an entire garden.  The committee decided to weed out unqualified applicants before the final interviews.  Police found a small amount of weed during the search.  Farmers use various methods to weed their fields efficiently.

english_meaning: A period of seven consecutive days. The seven days from Monday to Sunday. The part of the week when people normally work, excluding the weekend. A period of seven days marked for a special purpose or event.
example_sentence: I will visit my grandparents next week. She works forty hours a week. The exams will continue for two weeks. The school is celebrating Reading Week this month.

english_meaning: To find out how heavy someone or something is, typically using scales. To carefully assess the nature, importance, or consequences of a decision or situation. To have a specified weight or exert a specific physical or mental pressure.
example_sentence: The merchant needs to weigh the spices before calculating the total price. I always weigh my luggage before heading to the airport. You must carefully weigh the pros and cons before accepting the new job offer. The heavy responsibility began to weigh on the young manager's mind. The champion boxer will weigh in exactly at the limit of his division.

english_meaning: Strange or unusual. Something that is not normal, expected, or easy to understand. It may feel odd, surprising, or even slightly unsettling. Something feels off or not right. Connected with magic or fate. Acting differently from others
example_sentence: That was a weird dream I had last night. He made a weird sound when he saw the surprise. The weather has been really weird this week. She has a weird way of solving problems, but it works. I felt weird after taking that medicine. In old stories, weird sisters could predict the future. People thought his habits were weird.

english_meaning: To make someone feel uncomfortable, uneasy, or surprised by strange behavior. To induce a sense of creepiness.
example_sentence: That guy really weirds me out with his staring. It weirded her out when the cat started talking in the movie. I didn't mean to weird you out by showing up unannounced. The strange noises in the basement weirded out the kids.

english_meaning: In a strange or bizarre manner. Uncannily or mysteriously.
example_sentence: She was acting weirdly all afternoon. The lights flickered weirdly in the empty hallway. Weirdly enough, I actually enjoyed the movie. The trees were shaped weirdly by the strong winds.

english_meaning: The quality of being very strange or bizarre. The state of being supernatural or uncanny.
example_sentence: There was a certain weirdness about the abandoned house. I couldn't explain the weirdness of the dream. The movie captures the weirdness of small-town life. We laughed at the weirdness of the whole situation.

english_meaning: A person whose dress or behavior seems strange or eccentric. An oddball.
example_sentence: I felt like a bit of a weirdo standing there all by myself. Some people think he's a weirdo because of his clothes. Don't be such a weirdo and just talk to them. The movie is full of weirdos and eccentric characters.

english_meaning: A person who is polite, well-mannered, and shows good upbringing.
example_sentence: She is a well-bred young woman. His well-bred manners impressed everyone. They are from a well-bred family. A well-bred person never behaves rudely.

english_meaning: Having a lot of money, In a good situation. Being in good condition or favorable circumstance
example_sentence: His family is not very well-off. Some people don’t know when they are well off.

english_meaning: The state of being comfortable, healthy, and happy. A condition of good physical and mental health. The overall quality of life and satisfaction. Welfare and prosperity of a person or group.
example_sentence: Regular exercise contributes to overall well-being. The company cares about employee well-being. Mental well-being is as important as physical health. Meditation can improve your sense of well-being.

english_meaning: Having a lot of money, In a good situation. Being in good condition or favorable circumstance
example_sentence: His family is not very well-off. Some people don’t know when they are well off.

english_meaning: An organisation or system that works very smoothly and efficiently. A group of people who cooperate perfectly with no wasted effort. A process in which every part functions exactly as it should. Something running without problems, delays or friction.
example_sentence: The kitchen runs like a well-oiled machine during the dinner rush. After months of practice, the choir became a well-oiled machine. Their election campaign was a well-oiled machine from start to finish. With clear instructions, the warehouse works like a well-oiled machine.

english_meaning: A man who habitually associates with promiscuous women or prostitutes. A womanizer, philanderer, or lecher who frequently engages in casual sexual relationships. It describes an individual known for his lustful and immoral behavior towards women.
example_sentence: The notorious wencher was banned from joining polite society gatherings. Throughout the novel, the protagonist struggles to overcome his past as a careless wencher. Everyone warned her that the charming prince was actually a deceitful wencher. The old tavern was famous for hosting drunks, gamblers, and an occasional wencher. He lived his life as a drunkard and a wencher until his final days.

english_meaning: To go in a specified direction, typically slowly or by an indirect route. To direct one's course or travel steadily toward a destination. It often implies a leisurely, winding, or unhurried journey.
example_sentence: The tired hikers began to wend their way down the mountain as the sun set. A stream continues to wend through the quiet and peaceful valley. We watched the glowing lantern wend its way through the dense forest. People slowly wend their way home after the long festival concludes. She likes to wend her way through the crowded market on Sunday mornings.

english_meaning: Covered or soaked with water or another liquid. Not yet dry, as of paint or ink. Rainy in terms of weather. To make something damp or soaked. Feeble or lacking in strength of character (informal British use).
example_sentence: My shoes are completely wet from the rain. Careful, the paint is still wet. It has been a very wet summer this year. She wet a cloth and cleaned the wound.

english_meaning: A person who spoils other people's fun by failing to join in or by disapproving of their activities. Someone who brings down the mood of a group. A negative person who discourages enjoyment or enthusiasm. An individual who acts as a constant source of pessimism.
example_sentence: Nobody invited him to the party because he is such a wet blanket. Don't be a wet blanket and come dance with us. She acted like a wet blanket when we suggested going to the amusement park. His constant complaining makes him a real wet blanket on road trips.

english_meaning: A very enjoyable and exciting experience. A period of great fun and amusement. An occasion on which someone enjoys themselves enormously. Used to describe having far more fun than expected.
example_sentence: The children had a whale of a time at the beach. We had a whale of a time at your wedding, thank you. Everyone had a whale of a time at the office party. Despite the rain, they had a whale of a time camping.

english_meaning: A structure built on the shore of a harbour or on the bank of a river where ships may dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
example_sentence: The cargo ship was anchored at the wharf. Workers loaded goods onto the wharf. The old wharf is a popular tourist spot. Fish were brought to the wharf every morning. The wharf was busy with activity all day.

english_meaning: Anything or everything that; no matter what. Used to say that something does not matter or that any choice is acceptable. Used to show indifference, annoyance, or lack of interest in a casual reply.
example_sentence: Take whatever you need from the shelf. Whatever happens, I will support your decision. She said 'whatever' and walked away. Whatever the reason, his behaviour was unacceptable.

english_meaning: What is the information?. What is happening?. What is the latest news or update?. Tell me the details. What is going on?.What is the situation?. Any new gossip or news?. What do you know about it?. The phrase comes from “411,” which was once the telephone number for directory assistance in North America. Later, it became slang for “information”.
synonyms: ["What’s up?","What’s going on?","What’s new?","Fill me in","Give me the details","Any news?","What’s happening?","Tell me the update"]
antonyms: ["I already know everything","No news","Nothing is happening","Keep it secret","Don’t tell me anything"]
example_sentence: Hey Ali, what’s the 411 about the new office manager?. I have been away for a week, so what’s the 411 at school?. Sara called me last night asking what’s the 411 with our project. Everyone is excited today. What’s the 411?.

english_meaning: At all; used after a negative statement to make it stronger. Of any kind at all, used for emphasis with words like no, none, or nothing. Whatever the case may be; no matter what. Used to stress that something is completely absent or entirely unimportant. Anything at all, regardless of type or amount.
synonyms: ["At all","Of any kind","Whatever","Anything at all","In any way","Under any circumstances"]
example_sentence: There is no evidence whatsoever to support that claim. He showed no interest whatsoever in the offer. She had nothing whatsoever to do with the accident. They gave no reason whatsoever for the delay.

english_meaning: To persuade someone gently or cleverly, often by flattering or coaxing, especially to get what you want. To influence or convince someone to do something by using soft talk, charm, praise, or emotional appeal. It is often used when someone is trying to get a favor, money, or permission in a subtle or indirect way.
example_sentence: She tried to wheedle her parents into buying her a new phone. The child wheedled his teacher for extra marks. He wheedled information out of his friend. They wheedled their way into getting free tickets.

english_meaning: To submerge, engulf, or cover completely, especially with water or some overwhelming force. To overpower, overcome, or bury beneath something. Figuratively, to overwhelm someone emotionally or mentally with feelings, work, or pressure. An older or literary word now often replaced by 'overwhelm'.
example_sentence: The huge waves whelmed the small fishing boat in seconds. A sudden wave of grief whelmed her after hearing the news. The flood whelmed the village within hours. He felt whelmed by the responsibilities placed upon him. Dark clouds whelmed the sky before the storm.

english_meaning: To turn an object upside down or cause it to fall over. To completely cover something with water, earth, snow, or another substance. To surround or overpower completely, often by force or emotion. To sink or place something beneath the surface of water.
example_sentence: The storm whelved several fishing boats along the coast. Heavy snow whelved the mountain path overnight. A sudden wave whelved the canoe in seconds. Sad memories whelved her after she read the old letter.

word: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
english_meaning: Adapt yourself to the customs, habits, and behavior of the people or place you are visiting. Behave according to the environment. Respect the culture of others. Adjust to different situations, Follow local traditions and manners. Blend with the people around you.
example_sentence: Ahmed removed his shoes before entering the house in Japan because when in Rome, do as the Romans do. Sara learned a few Turkish greetings before visiting Istanbul because she believes that when in Rome, do as the Romans do. While working in another company, Ali followed their office rules because when in Rome, do as the Romans do. The tourists tried local food and respected local traditions because when in Rome, do as the Romans do.

english_meaning: Problems or good events often happen all at once. When one thing goes wrong or right, many similar things tend to happen at the same time. It is often used for difficulties, but it can also describe sudden success or good luck occurring together
synonyms: ["Misfortunes Never Come alone","One thing after another","Trouble comes in waves"]
example_sentence: He lost his job and his car broke down the same week. When it rains, it pours. First she failed the exam and then she fell sick. When it rains, it pours. After years of struggle, he got promoted and won an award. When it rains, it pours. The team faced injuries, bad weather, and budget cuts. When it rains, it pours.

english_meaning: Something that will never happen or something very impossible or unrealistic.
synonyms: ["Not a chance","Out of the question","In your dreams"]
example_sentence: That will happen when pigs fly. He said he would stop lying when pigs fly. She will apologize to him when pigs fly. I will buy that expensive car when pigs fly. They will finish the project on time when pigs fly.

english_meaning: At whatever time; on any occasion that. Every time that something happens. Used to express surprise when asking about a time.
synonyms: ["Any time","Each time","Every time","At any moment","No matter when"]
antonyms: ["Never","At no time","Only once","At a fixed time"]
example_sentence: Call me whenever you need any help. Whenever it rains, the street floods quickly. You may visit us whenever you are free. Whenever did he learn to speak French so well?

english_meaning: The real source of a problem or difficulty. The point at which trouble or hardship is actually felt. The hidden cause of distress known best to the person suffering it.
example_sentence: Only the manager knows where the shoe pinches in this department. High rent is where the shoe pinches for most young families. He explained where the shoe pinches in the current system. Everyone praises the plan, but few see where the shoe pinches.

english_meaning: Used to compare or contrast two facts, ideas, or situations. While on the contrary; although. In legal language, used at the beginning of a document to introduce a statement of fact.
example_sentence: She loves spicy food, whereas her husband prefers mild dishes. The north receives heavy rainfall, whereas the south remains dry. Whereas the first plan was expensive, the second is quite affordable. He is calm and patient, whereas his brother is quick-tempered.

english_meaning: For what reason or purpose. As a result of which. A reason or cause for something. It is often used in archaic or formal contexts to ask why or to state a conclusion.
example_sentence: Wherefore do you weep, my child?. He explained the why and wherefore of his decision. The contract was breached, wherefore we claim damages. I know not wherefore she left so suddenly. Let us examine the wherefore of this strange occurrence.

english_meaning: In or to whatever place; in any place that. In every case or situation where. Used to express surprise when asking about a place.
example_sentence: You can sit wherever you feel comfortable. Wherever she goes, her dog follows her. We will help wherever help is needed. Wherever did you find that old photograph?

english_meaning: The money or other means needed for a particular purpose. The resources or capabilities required to accomplish a task. It generally refers to financial resources but can also mean physical or mental ability.
example_sentence: They lacked the wherewithal to pay for the repairs. She has the intellectual wherewithal to succeed in this difficult course. I would like to buy that house, but I just do not have the wherewithal. The government must provide the wherewithal to rebuild the infrastructure. Finding the wherewithal to fund the project took several months.

english_meaning: To sharpen the blade of a knife or tool. To stimulate or increase a desire, appetite, or interest. To make someone eager for more of something.
example_sentence: He whetted the blade on a smooth stone. The aroma from the kitchen whetted our appetite. The trailer whetted my interest in the film. A short visit only whetted her desire to travel more.

english_meaning: Used to introduce alternatives or express a doubt or choice between possibilities. Expressing an inquiry or investigation into two alternatives. Used before or between choices. Regardless of which of two possibilities.
example_sentence: I don't know whether he will come or not. She asked whether the shop was open. Whether you agree or not, the decision stands. He couldn't decide whether to stay or leave.

english_meaning: The watery part of milk that remains after the formation of curds. It is a byproduct of cheese production and contains protein, vitamins, and minerals. It is often used in health supplements and baking.
example_sentence: The liquid part seen floating on yogurt is often just whey. The little miss muffet poem mentions eating curds and whey. Bakers sometimes use whey instead of water to improve the texture of bread. Whey protein is highly popular among athletes for muscle recovery.

english_meaning: Used to ask about a choice between a limited number of things. Used to introduce a clause giving more information about something already mentioned. Referring to a particular thing among others. Used in questions about identity or selection.
example_sentence: Which book do you want to borrow from the library? He bought a laptop which has a very fast processor. Which of these two roads leads to the station? She could not decide which colour suited her best.

english_meaning: Any one out of a group, no matter which is chosen. Used to say that the result is the same no matter which option is selected. The particular one of a limited set that is chosen or preferred. Whatever one or ones of a given number of choices. Used to refer to the option that suits best.
example_sentence: Choose whichever book you like from the shelf. Take whichever route is faster at this hour. Whichever team wins will play in the final. You may pay by card or cash, whichever is easier for you.

english_meaning: A brief or faint smell carried in the air. A quick puff or breath of air, smoke, or vapor. A slight trace or hint of something. To catch a slight smell of something.
example_sentence: I caught a whiff of fresh bread as I passed the bakery. There was a whiff of smoke coming from the kitchen. She sensed a whiff of trouble in his voice. He whiffed the perfume and smiled.

english_meaning: During the time that something else is happening. A period or interval of time. Although or whereas, used to contrast two facts. To pass time in a relaxed or unhurried way, usually as 'while away'.
example_sentence: She read a book while the children were sleeping. We waited a while before the train finally arrived. While I agree with your idea, I think the cost is too high. They whiled away the afternoon playing cards in the garden.

english_meaning: Formerly. Once. At an earlier time, usually in literary or old-fashioned language.
example_sentence: Whilom, the village stood beside a much smaller river. The whilom champion now coaches young athletes. This was whilom a busy market, but it is quiet today. In the poem, the knight recalls his whilom glory.

english_meaning: During the time that something is happening. At the same time as something else is happening. In spite of the fact that.
example_sentence:
In the UK it is illegal to drive whilst holding a mobile phone.
Harrison's clock allowed seamen to keep time accurately whilst at sea. whilst a good worker, he's not a very good manager.

english_meaning: A sudden and unpredictable thought, wish, or decision that arises without careful planning or logical reason. It often reflects a temporary mood or personal fancy rather than serious consideration.
example_sentence: On a whim, she decided to travel to the mountains without telling anyone. He bought the expensive watch on a whim. The plan was not serious, it was just a whim. Children often act on a whim.

english_meaning: To make a series of low, feeble sounds expressive of fear, pain, or discontent. A low, feeble sound of this kind. To complain in a weak or whining manner.
example_sentence: The injured dog began to whimper in pain. He heard a faint whimper coming from the dark corner of the room. Stop whimpering and tell me exactly what happened. The child gave a little whimper when the nurse administered the injection. The rebellion ended with a whimper rather than a bang.

english_meaning: Playfully unusual or imaginative, sometimes unpredictable. Acting in a playful or imaginative way. Unpredictable and changeable in behavior. Odd or fanciful in a charming manner. Following sudden ideas rather than logic.
example_sentence: Her whimsical drawings made everyone smile. He made a whimsical decision to travel without a plan. The garden had whimsical decorations in bright colors. She has a whimsical sense of humor that surprises people.

english_meaning: In a partly unusual and playful or fanciful manner. In a way that is subject to erratic behavior or unpredictable change. Acting in a quirky or capriciously eccentric way.
example_sentence: She smiled whimsically as she remembered her childhood adventures. The cafe was whimsically decorated with mismatched furniture and bright colors. He whimsically decided to take a spontaneous road trip across the country. The author writes whimsically about the mundane details of everyday life. The song ends whimsically with an unexpected kazoo solo.

english_meaning: To complain in a weak, annoying, and high-pitched voice. To make a long, high, unpleasant sound, as a dog or machine does. To grumble persistently about small problems. A complaining cry or a continuous high-pitched sound.
example_sentence: The child began to whine for another sweet. Stop whining and finish your homework. The dog whined at the door all night. We could hear the whine of the engine from far away.

english_meaning: A strip of leather or length of cord fastened to a handle, used for beating a person or for urging on an animal. To beat someone or something with a whip or similar instrument. To move fast or suddenly in a specified direction. To beat cream, eggs, or other food into a froth.
example_sentence: The jockey used his whip to urge the horse toward the finish line. You need to whip the eggs until they are light and fluffy. The harsh wind whipped through the narrow streets of the city. He was accused of using a whip to threaten the workers. She quickly whipped out her phone to record the incident.

english_meaning: To turn or cause to turn or spin around rapidly. A rapid dizzying motion or succession of events. To move or be moved quickly with a circular motion.
example_sentence: The dancers began to whirl around the room. Her mind was in a whirl after the shocking news. Leaves whirl in the autumn wind. He decided to give the new software a whirl. The helicopter blades began to whirl rapidly.

english_meaning: A column of air moving rapidly around and around in a cylindrical or funnel shape. A very rapid and confusing sequence of events or actions. Proceeding with great speed or energy.
example_sentence: The town was hit by a destructive whirlwind. They had a whirlwind romance and married within a month. The president's whirlwind tour covered five countries in four days. A whirlwind of dust rose from the dry field. The next few weeks were a whirlwind of activity.

english_meaning: To take or move someone or something somewhere suddenly and quickly. To beat or stir a substance, especially cream or eggs, with a light rapid movement. A utensil for whipping eggs or cream.
example_sentence: The waiter proceeded to whisk our plates away. She used a wire whisk to beat the eggs. The celebrity was whisked off to a secret location. Whisk the cream until it forms soft peaks. With a quick whisk of his tail, the horse trotted away.

english_meaning: A long projecting hair or bristle growing from the face or snout of many mammals. The hair growing on a man's face, especially on the cheeks. A very small distance or amount.
example_sentence: The cat twitched an ear and a whisker. He won the race by a mere whisker. The old man stroked his silver whiskers. My grandfather used to trim his whiskers every morning. The car missed the pedestrian by a whisker.

english_meaning: To speak very softly using the breath rather than the voice. A very quiet remark meant to be heard by only a few. A soft rustling sound, as of leaves or wind. A rumour or hint circulating quietly.
example_sentence: She whispered the answer into his ear. He spoke in a whisper so the baby would not wake. There was a whisper of wind through the trees. Whispers of a merger spread through the office.

english_meaning: Extremely pale in the face, usually because of fear, shock or illness. Having lost all colour from the face suddenly. Looking frightened or unwell to a noticeable degree. Very pale in appearance, like white cloth.
example_sentence: She went white as a sheet when she heard the news. He came out of the hospital room white as a sheet. You are white as a sheet, please sit down and drink some water. The boy turned white as a sheet after the loud crash.

english_meaning: A colourless blood cell that helps the body fight infection and disease. A cell of the immune system that destroys harmful bacteria, viruses, and foreign particles. Any of several types of blood cells such as lymphocytes, neutrophils, and monocytes. A cell whose number in the blood rises during infection or inflammation.
example_sentence: White blood cells defend the body against infection. The test showed a high number of white blood cells. White blood cells are produced mainly in the bone marrow. Chemotherapy can lower a patient's white blood cell count.

english_meaning: Relating to office, professional or administrative work rather than manual labour. Describing employees who work in offices, usually in salaried positions.
