Referring to crimes committed by professionals for financial gain, such as fraud. A worker whose job requires education and clerical or managerial skills.
example_sentence: He left a factory job for a white collar position in the city. White collar crime often goes unreported for years. The company employs both white collar and blue collar staff. Many white collar workers now do their jobs from home.

english_meaning: A possession that is costly to keep but of little or no use. A project or building that costs a great deal and gives little benefit. An unwanted item that is difficult to dispose of. Something impressive in size but a burden to its owner.
example_sentence: The new stadium turned out to be a white elephant for the city. That old boat is a white elephant we can neither use nor sell. Critics called the airport a costly white elephant. The mansion became a white elephant after the family lost its income.

english_meaning: A tiny white sap-sucking insect that gathers on the underside of leaves. A greenhouse and field pest that weakens plants and secretes sticky honeydew. An insect that spreads plant viruses and encourages the growth of sooty mould. A small moth-like pest, usually written as whitefly.
example_sentence: Clouds of white fly rose when we shook the tomato plants. White fly infestation has weakened the cotton crop. Yellow sticky traps are effective against white fly. The gardener sprayed neem oil to control white fly.

english_meaning: A small or harmless lie told to avoid hurting someone or to keep peace. A minor lie that is not meant to harm anyone. It is often used in social situations to be polite, avoid conflict, or protect someone’s feelings. Though it is still untrue, it is usually considered acceptable in many cultures.
example_sentence: She told a white lie about liking the gift to make her friend happy. He said he was busy, but it was just a white lie to avoid the meeting. Parents sometimes tell white lies to protect their children’s feelings. Saying the food tastes good, even when it doesn’t, is a common white lie.

english_meaning: To deliberately hide unpleasant facts or wrongdoing. To present a false, favourable account in order to protect someone's reputation. To cover a surface with a white lime-based paint. In sport, to defeat an opponent in every game or match of a series.
example_sentence: The report was criticised as a whitewash of official failures. They tried to whitewash the scandal with a short apology. He spent the weekend whitewashing the garden wall. The team suffered a five-nil whitewash in the series.

english_meaning: To carve or shape wood by cutting small pieces from it with a knife. To cut thin slices from a piece of wood as a pastime. To reduce something gradually in size, amount, or number. To pare down step by step.
example_sentence: He sat on the porch whittling a small wooden bird. The old man whittled a walking stick from a branch. They whittled the shortlist to five candidates. Rising costs have whittled our savings.

english_meaning: To reduce something slowly and steadily until little remains. To wear down a quantity, right, or advantage bit by bit. To gradually destroy or erode something over time. To spend time idly cutting wood.
example_sentence: Inflation has whittled away the value of their pension. New rules slowly whittled away workers' rights. His confidence was whittled away by constant criticism. The lead was whittled away in the final minutes.

english_meaning: To move very quickly, often with a rushing sound. A person who is exceptionally skilled at something. To make a hissing or humming sound while moving fast. A quick or impressive achievement.
example_sentence: Cars whizzed past on the highway. He is a whiz at solving math problems. The arrow whizzed through the air. She finished the puzzle in a whiz.

english_meaning: Used to ask about the identity of a person or people. Used to introduce a clause that gives more information about a person. Referring to the person or people mentioned earlier. The subject form used for people in questions and clauses.
example_sentence: Who is standing at the door right now? The man who helped us was a retired teacher. Nobody knew who had left the message. Who wants to join the trip on Sunday?

english_meaning: A novel, play, or film about a murder or other crime in which the identity of the perpetrator is not revealed until the end. A suspenseful detective story or mystery narrative focusing on unraveling a crime.
example_sentence: I spent the weekend reading a classic Agatha Christie whodunit. The movie was a brilliant whodunit that kept everyone guessing until the final minute. She loves writing whodunits with complex plot twists. The play is a comedy wrapped inside a gripping whodunit.

english_meaning: An alternative spelling of whodunit. A story, movie, or play about a crime where the culprit's identity remains hidden until the final reveal.
example_sentence: The theatre group is staging a traditional murder whodunnit this week. Everyone enjoys a good whodunnit on a rainy evening. The author established her reputation with a series of clever whodunnits. The detective revealed the killer's identity in classic whodunnit fashion.

english_meaning: The person or people who; anyone who. No matter who; used to say that the identity of the person does not matter. Used in questions to express surprise about who did something.
example_sentence: Whoever finishes first will receive a prize. Whoever told you that was mistaken. Give the letter to whoever answers the door. Whoever could have left the gate open?

english_meaning: A number without fractions or decimals, including zero and all positive integers. Any of the numbers zero, one, two, three and so on. A complete number that represents an exact quantity. An integer used in counting that has no fractional part.
example_sentence: Five is a whole number, but five and a half is not. Whole numbers include zero as well as the counting numbers. Round the answer to the nearest whole number. The recipe requires a whole number of cups, not fractions.

english_meaning: Everything possible; the complete amount or the full extent. All of something, with nothing left out. The entire range of items, services or effort involved. Used to stress that nothing was held back.
synonyms: ["Everything","The lot","The full works","All of it","Entirety","Whole shebang","Soup to nuts"]
example_sentence: They gave us the whole nine yards for the wedding dinner. If you want the deluxe package, you get the whole nine yards. He explained the plan, the budget, the risks, the whole nine yards. She went the whole nine yards to make her son's birthday special.

english_meaning: The object form of 'who', used to refer to the person receiving the action. Used in formal English after verbs and prepositions. Used to ask which person is affected by an action. Introducing a clause about a person as the object.
example_sentence: To whom should I address this letter? The candidate whom we interviewed was very impressive. She is the person with whom I shared the office. Whom did they finally select for the position?

english_meaning: An exclamation used when a small mistake or accident happens. A word said to show mild surprise or apology. A cry of excitement or joy.
example_sentence: Whoops, I dropped the glass! Whoops, I think I sent that message to the wrong person. She said whoops and quickly picked up the papers. Whoops of joy rose from the crowd after the goal.

english_meaning: A soft rushing sound made by something moving quickly through the air. To move rapidly with such a sound. An exclamation imitating fast movement.
example_sentence: We heard the whoosh of the train as it passed. The car whooshed past us on the highway. With a soft whoosh, the door slid open. The rocket rose with a great whoosh of flame.

english_meaning: A person, typically a woman, who engages in sexual intercourse for money. A prostitute. To debase oneself by doing something for money. A deeply derogatory term for a sexually promiscuous person.
example_sentence: The historical novel deals with the troubled life of a nineteenth-century whore. He was accused of whoring after fame and fortune. The term is highly offensive and degrading when directed at someone. The charity aims to help desperate individuals forced to act as a whore. He felt that the author was willing to whore his talents for a quick buck.

english_meaning: A brothel or an establishment where prostitutes are available. A building in which sex workers operate. It refers to a place where people pay to engage in sexual activities.
example_sentence: The detective raided the notorious whorehouse located at the edge of the town. She wrote a novel about a woman who escaped a 19th-century whorehouse. The abandoned building was once rumored to be a thriving whorehouse. They campaigned to shut down every illegal whorehouse in the district. The film depicts the harsh realities of living in a rural whorehouse.

english_meaning: Used to ask who something belongs to. Showing possession or ownership by a person. Used to introduce a clause describing something belonging to someone. The possessive form of 'who' and sometimes of 'which'.
example_sentence: Whose bag has been left on the table? The writer whose novel won the prize will speak tonight. She met a family whose children study abroad. Whose turn is it to present the report?

english_meaning: Evil or morally wrong in principle or practice. Playfully mischievous. In slang, it means excellent, wonderful, or extremely. It describes something that is highly malicious or, conversely, extremely impressive.
example_sentence: The wicked witch cast a dark spell over the sleeping kingdom. He gave a wicked grin before pulling the prank on his sister. The band played a wicked solo that left the audience cheering wildly. It was a wicked storm that tore the roof off the old barn. She has a wicked sense of humor that catches people off guard.

english_meaning: The quality of being evil or morally wrong. Cruel or harmful behavior toward others. An act that is deeply immoral. Sinful or unjust conduct. A state of being full of bad intentions.
example_sentence: The wickedness of his crimes shocked the whole nation. She could not tolerate the wickedness around her. Stories often teach children to reject wickedness. His wickedness finally brought him to ruin.

english_meaning: Measuring a large distance from one side to the other. Covering a large area or range. Including a great variety of things or people. Fully open, as of eyes. Missing the target, especially in sport.
example_sentence: The river is very wide at this point. The store offers a wide range of products. Her eyes were wide with surprise. The shot went wide of the goal.

english_meaning: Over a large area or among many people. To a great extent or degree. In many different places or by many different groups. With a large space between two points.
example_sentence: His books are widely read in many countries. Opinions on the matter differ widely. The disease spread widely during the rainy season. She is widely respected as a teacher.

english_meaning: An opinion or idea accepted by a large number of people. A view that is common within a society or group. A popular assumption that may or may not be true. Conventional wisdom shared by the majority.
synonyms: ["Common belief","Popular opinion","Conventional wisdom","General view","Received wisdom","Consensus","Prevailing notion"]
example_sentence: It is a widely held belief that breakfast is the most important meal. The study challenged a widely held belief about memory. That widely held belief has little scientific support. Many widely held beliefs change as knowledge grows.

english_meaning: Existing or happening in many places and among many people. Distant and widely extended in space or breadth. Prevalent or occurring over a large area or among many individuals. Distributed over a considerable extent. Generally accepted or used across a broad range of contexts. Having a great range or scope.
example_sentence: There is a widespread belief that the economy will improve by next year. The virus caused widespread panic throughout the entire region. The storm resulted in widespread damage to the coastal infrastructure. The artist's work received widespread acclaim from critics and the public alike.

english_meaning: A small device or gadget whose name is unknown or unimportant. A simple element of a computer interface, such as a button or slider. A small application that displays information on a screen. An imaginary product used as an example in business and economics.
example_sentence: The factory produces thousands of widgets every day. Drag the weather widget onto your home screen. The designer added a new widget to the dashboard. Economists often explain supply and demand using widgets.

english_meaning: A woman whose husband has died and who has not remarried. A female left alone after the death of her spouse. A woman mourning the loss of her husband. A term used in legal or social records for such a woman. A female bereaved of her partner.
synonyms: ["Bereaved wife","Surviving wife","Dowager","Relict","Lone woman","Grieving spouse","Mourner","Bereft","Solo wife","Widowed woman"]
example_sentence: She became a widow at a young age. The widow raised her children with great courage. The war left many widows in the village. The widow inherited her husband's property.

english_meaning: A man whose wife has died and who has not remarried. A male person left alone after the death of his spouse. A man mourning the loss of his wife. A husband who has become single due to bereavement. A term used in legal or social records for such a man.
synonyms: ["Bereaved husband","Surviving husband","Lone man","Grieving spouse","Solitary husband","Unmarried again","Bereft","Widow's counterpart","Single man","Mourner"]
example_sentence: He became a widower after thirty years of marriage. The old widower lived alone with his dog. As a widower, he raised his children by himself. The widower slowly recovered from his grief.

english_meaning: The measurement of something from one side to the other. The distance across an object, opposite to its length. The extent or range of something. A piece of material measured across from edge to edge.
example_sentence: Measure the width of the door before buying the frame. The river is about ten metres in width. The table's length is twice its width. The road was narrow, with barely enough width for two cars.

english_meaning: To hold and use a weapon or tool. To have and be able to use power or influence. It describes the act of exercising authority or physically brandishing an instrument effectively.
example_sentence: The warrior was known to wield a massive broadsword in battle. The CEO continues to wield enormous influence over the company's decisions. You must learn how to wield this machinery safely before starting the job. The union leaders wield considerable power in the upcoming negotiations. She can wield a paintbrush like a true master of the Renaissance.

english_meaning: In a state of extreme agitation, excitement, or panic. Having lost emotional control, often due to drug use or severe stress. It describes a person who is freaked out or acting irrationally.
example_sentence: He was completely wigged-out after drinking too many energy drinks. The sudden loud noise left the poor dog totally wigged-out. She got completely wigged-out when she saw the massive spider holding on to the wall. I felt a bit wigged-out before walking onto the stage to give my speech. They were wigged-out by the creepy atmosphere in the abandoned hospital.

english_meaning: Lacking discipline or control, In natural condition, Strong feelings. Not kept in a house or on a farm. A natural environment that is not controlled by people. Extreme or violent and not controlled
example_sentence: The boy is wild & completely out of control. He has a wild look in his eyes. The plants grow wild along banks of liver. The island is wild & lonely place. It makes me wild (angry) to see such waste.

english_meaning: A useless or hopeless search or pursuit that wastes time and effort. A situation where someone is sent on a search or task that is pointless, misleading, or impossible to achieve. It often involves chasing something that does not exist or cannot be found, leading to frustration and wasted time.
example_sentence: We went on a wild goose chase looking for a shop that had already closed years ago. Trying to find that rare book without any details turned into a wild goose chase. The clues in the puzzle led us on a wild goose chase across the city. Don’t send me on a wild goose chase just to avoid answering my question.

english_meaning: Comparative form of wild, meaning more untamed, fiercely active, or violent. To cause someone to lose their way or become bewildered. It describes a state of being more uncontrolled or closer to a natural, uncivilized condition.
example_sentence: The river grew wilder as we traveled further downstream away from the city. His imagination ran wilder than ever after reading the fantasy novel. The party became wilder once the live band started playing their hit songs. There is no wilder frontier than the deepest trenches of the ocean. The storms this winter are much wilder compared to the previous years.

english_meaning: A clever or deceitful trick used to persuade or trap someone. Cunning behaviour intended to deceive. To lure or entice someone by cleverness or charm. To pass time pleasantly, often in the form 'wile away'.
example_sentence: He used every wile he knew to get out of the punishment. The old trader was famous for his wiles in the marketplace. She wiled him into signing the papers without reading them. The feminine wiles of the character drive the whole play.

english_meaning: Deliberate and intentional, especially in doing something wrong. Stubbornly determined to have one’s own way. Refusing to listen to advice or instruction. Done knowingly with full awareness of consequences.
example_sentence: The court called it a wilful violation of the law. He is a wilful child who never listens to his parents. Her wilful neglect of duty led to dismissal. The damage was found to be wilful rather than accidental.

english_meaning: Ready and happy to do something without objection. Prepared to agree or cooperate readily. Done or given by choice rather than by force. Showing eagerness to help or take part.
example_sentence: She is always willing to help her classmates. He was willing to accept the new terms of the contract. They gave their willing support to the campaign. Are you willing to work on Sunday?

english_meaning: A sudden and violent squall blowing offshore from a mountainous coast. A sudden burst of wind or commotion. It often refers specifically to cold, dense air sweeping down from snow-capped mountain peaks toward the sea resulting in a fierce and dangerous storm.
example_sentence: The small fishing boat was nearly capsized by a sudden williwaw. Experienced sailors know to watch out for a williwaw when anchoring near steep coastal mountains. Their peaceful afternoon was disrupted by a williwaw that tore through the harbor. The expedition was delayed when a fierce williwaw battered their camp.

english_meaning: Doing something whether you want to or not, or doing it in a careless or unplanned way. It can describe being forced into something or acting without proper thought. In careless way without planning, Without direction or planning, Whether desired or not, Something happens whether one wishes it or no
example_sentence: He would be forced to collaborate willy-nilly. Don’t use your credit card willy-nilly. The project moved forward willy nilly because the deadline was too close. She packed her bags willy nilly and rushed to catch the bus. If you avoid planning, you end up making decisions willy nilly. The rules were changed willy nilly without asking anyone.

english_meaning: Skilled at gaining an advantage, especially deceitfully. Marked by skill in deception or cunning. It describes someone who is crafty and uses clever tricks to outwit others in competitive or adversarial situations.
example_sentence: The wily fox managed to evade the hunters once again. He is a wily politician who knows exactly how to manipulate the media. She used a wily strategy to win the negotiation without making any real compromises. It takes a wily opponent to challenge a reigning champion successfully. The wily old cat always found a way to steal food from the counter.

english_meaning: A person who is physically weak and lacks confidence or courage. Someone who is easily intimidated or afraid of minor challenges. To fail to do something because of fear or lack of conviction. A spineless individual who avoids conflict at any cost. Used informally to describe a person who is overly sensitive or fragile.
example_sentence: Don't be such a wimp and jump into the pool. He was too much of a wimp to tell his boss the truth. I wanted to go bungee jumping but I wimped out at the last second. She called him a wimp when he refused to watch the horror movie.

english_meaning: To withdraw from doing something due to fear, nervousness, or lack of courage. To decide not to do something at the last minute because you are frightened.
example_sentence: He promised to go skydiving with us, but he wimped out at the last minute. Don't wimp out now after all the preparation we have done. She was going to confront her boss, but she wimped out when she entered his office. If you wimp out on this deal, you might lose a great opportunity.

english_meaning: Lacking strength, courage, or confidence. Weak and timid in character or appearance.
example_sentence: He made a wimpish attempt to argue his point. Nobody listened to his wimpish complaint. Her brother had a wimpish personality and avoided all confrontation. He was tired of being perceived as a wimpish person by his peers.

english_meaning: A traditional cloth head covering worn by women that covers the neck and sides of the face, historically worn by medieval women and still worn by some modern nuns. To cover or fold in ripples or waves.
example_sentence: The nun adjusted her white wimple before entering the chapel. Medieval noblewomen often wore elaborate wimples woven from fine linen. The gentle breeze caused the water to wimple slightly. Her face was framed neatly inside the crisp white wimple.

english_meaning: To succeed in a contest, battle, election, or competition. To obtain something through effort, skill, or merit. To gain someone’s support, affection, or approval. To reach a desired place or condition. A victory or successful result.
example_sentence: Our team hopes to win the final tonight. Her honest answer won the judges’ respect. They celebrated a narrow win after the match. Patience will help you win people’s trust.

english_meaning: To gain someone’s support, approval, affection, or agreement. To persuade someone who was initially doubtful or opposed. To make someone like or trust you through words or actions.
example_sentence: Her honesty helped her win over the skeptical audience. The coach gradually won over the unhappy players. A free trial may win over new customers. He used patience and humor to win his neighbors over.

english_meaning: To persuade someone to support, agree with, or approve of you. To change a person’s initially negative or doubtful opinion. To gain someone’s affection or cooperation through patient effort.
example_sentence: We finally won the manager round to our proposal. Her practical arguments won round the doubtful committee members. He hopes to win his critics round with better results. A friendly conversation may win her round.

english_meaning: To suddenly react with pain or discomfort. To make a quick facial or body movement because of physical pain, emotional hurt, or embarrassment. It often happens without thinking, such as when hearing bad news or feeling sudden pain.
example_sentence: He winced when the doctor touched the injured arm. She winced at the sound of nails scratching the wall. The child winced after falling on the ground. He winced when he heard the harsh criticism.

english_meaning: In all conditions. Facing all hardships and changes. Refers to all kinds of weather conditions that is rain, sun, storm, heat, etc. In all situations or no matter what happens. Difficulties, challenges, or changing circumstances.
synonyms: ["Through thick and thin","In all circumstances","In every condition","Despite difficulties"]
antonyms: ["Only in comfort","In fair weather only","During easy times","When convenient"]
example_sentence: The sailors continued their journey through wind and weather. True friendship lasts through wind and weather. Farmers work hard in all wind and weather to feed the nation. The old lighthouse has stood strong against wind and weather for centuries.

english_meaning: Move in curves. To twist or curve around something or along a path.
example_sentence: The path winds around the hill. Vines wind around the fence. The river winds around the valley. Cables wind around the desk.

english_meaning: Reverse or return. To turn something backward or return to an earlier position or time.
example_sentence: Wind back the clock to see the start of the game. He wound back the tape. Let’s wind back to where we started. Wind back the curtains to let in light.

english_meaning: Relax or decrease gradually. To gradually reduce activity or come to a relaxed state.
example_sentence: He wound down after work. The party wound down at midnight. Sales wound down after the holiday season. I need to wind down before bed.

english_meaning: Finish gradually. To bring to an end or conclude something slowly or carefully.
example_sentence: The meeting wound off after an hour. He wound off the tape. The lecture wound off with questions. They wound off the festival with fireworks.

english_meaning: Continue moving. To continue or extend along a twisting course.
example_sentence: The path winds on for miles. The story winds on through chapters. The road winds on toward the city. His explanation winds on endlessly.

english_meaning: Pass in a winding way. To move through an area following a curved or twisting path.
example_sentence: The road winds through the forest. Streams wind through the meadow. He wound through the crowd. The trail winds through the mountains.

english_meaning: Conclude or finish. To bring to an end or finish, often by force or intentionally
example_sentence: We need to wind up the meeting. He wound up his speech. The company wound up operations. Let's wind up this project today.

english_meaning: Following a twisting or spiral course rather than a straight line. It can also refer to the act of tightening the spring of a clock or mechanism. Frequently used to describe paths, rivers, or stairs that curve repeatedly.
example_sentence: The car slowly climbed the winding road up the mountain. We followed a winding path through the thick forest. The hikers were exhausted by the winding staircase inside the tower. A winding river flowed gracefully through the center of the valley.

english_meaning: To close and open one eye quickly, often as a signal or a hint. It can express a shared secret, humor, or affection between two people. In a broader sense, it can mean a quick flash or sparkle of light.
example_sentence: He gave me a playful wink to show he was joking. I saw the star wink in the clear night sky. She didn't say a word, she just gave a knowing wink. The bright light began to wink through the trees as we drove by.

english_meaning: To deliberately ignore or pretend not to notice something wrong. To pretend that you have not noticed something, especially something bad or illegal. To connive at; disregard. To pretend not to see, as in connivance. To ignore deliberately, as to avoid the necessity of taking action.
example_sentence: The authorities winked at corruption. To wink at minor offenses. During the holiday, parking violations were winked at. The teacher winked at his mischief. They winked at corruption.

english_meaning: To extract or remove something with difficulty or by using a small tool. It can also refer to a small edible sea snail often found on rocky shores. In a figurative sense, it means to pry information or secrets from someone.
example_sentence: It took a long time to winkle the truth out of the reluctant witness. We used a small pin to winkle the meat out of the shell. They spent the afternoon collecting winkles on the beach. She managed to winkle the secret out of her younger brother.

english_meaning: To manage to remove or obtain with difficulty. To get something/somebody out of a place or position, especially when this is not easy to do. To resolve something by fighting until the end.
example_sentence: He winkled out the truth. She winkled out the old documents. The journalist managed to winkle out the truth after weeks of interviews. Police tried to winkle out information from reluctant witnesses. She winkled out old records from dusty archives. It took time to winkle out who was responsible for the mistake.

english_meaning: To get information from somebody, especially with difficulty. To persuade or trick someone into giving something.
example_sentence: They winkled money out of him. She winkled out of doing the task. The journalist managed to winkle the truth out of the official after several interviews. Police tried to winkle the suspect out of the abandoned house. It took time to winkle useful data out of old government records. She finally winkled an apology out of him after a long discussion.

english_meaning: To blow a current of air through grain in order to remove the chaff. To remove people or things from a group until only the best ones are left. It broadly refers to the process of separating the valuable parts from the useless or unwanted elements.
example_sentence: The farmers winnow the grain by throwing it into the air and letting the wind carry away the lighter chaff. It took him hours to winnow the truth from the mass of conflicting rumors. The committee must winnow through hundreds of applications to find the ideal candidate. Only the strongest contestants remained after the judges decided to winnow the competition. They use traditional methods to winnow the harvested rice.

english_meaning: A flat, woven basket or implement used in traditional agriculture for winnowing grain. A tool that aids in separating the chaff from the grain by tossing the mixture into the air. It is usually made of bamboo or cane and relies on wind to blow away the lighter unwanted particles.
example_sentence: The villagers expertly used a winnowing fan to clean the freshly harvested wheat. She held the winnowing fan high above her head to catch the afternoon breeze. Each family in the rural community owned a handmade winnowing fan for their crops. The museum displayed an ancient winnowing fan used by early farmers in the region. Using a winnowing fan requires a steady rhythm and good coordination.

english_meaning: Attractive or appealing in a charming, delightful way. Pleasing and engaging, having a cheerful or sweet personality. Pleasing to the eye or mind. Cheerful or engaging personality.
example_sentence: She had a winsome smile that lit up the room. His winsome personality made everyone feel at ease. The puppy’s winsome antics brought joy to the children. Her winsome laughter was infectious at the party.

english_meaning: In an attractive, charming, or appealing manner. In a sweetly innocent and engaging way. With a pleasant manner that naturally wins affection or approval.
example_sentence: She smiled winsomely at the nervous child. The actor delivered the playful line winsomely. He winsomely persuaded the guests to stay for dinner. The little girl waved winsomely from the stage.

english_meaning: The coldest season of the year, occurring between autumn and spring. A period of cold weather characteristic of this season. A year or period counted by the winters experienced. To spend the winter in a particular place. To keep animals, plants, or supplies through the winter.
example_sentence: Winter brings heavy snow to the mountain villages. Many birds fly south before winter begins. We plan to winter in a warmer part of the country. The farmer prepared enough feed to winter the cattle safely.

english_meaning: To destroy or remove somebody/something completely. To fall over, especially when you are doing a sport such as skiing or surfing. To make somebody extremely tired. To remove data or records completely. To kill a whole group of people or animals. To suffer total financial loss.
example_sentence:
She wiped out at the third gate in the slalom race. All that travelling has wiped her out. Whole villages were wiped out by the earthquake.
Last year's profits were virtually wiped out. People worry that climate change will wipe out coffee crops in certain countries.

english_meaning: Cleaned or dried by rubbing a surface with a cloth, paper, or hand. Erased, removed, or completely obliterated from a physical or digital space. It can also describe the state of being physically exhausted or completely destroyed when used as part of idiomatic expressions.
example_sentence: He carefully wiped the kitchen counter with a damp sponge. All the data on the hard drive was completely wiped before the computer was sold. She wiped the tears from her face and tried to smile. After running the marathon, the athlete looked completely wiped and collapsed on the grass. The sudden stock market crash wiped billions of dollars from investors' portfolios.

english_meaning: Thin but strong and muscular in build. Stiff and coarse in texture, like wire, especially of hair. Tough and able to endure hard physical effort. Resembling wire in appearance or feel.
example_sentence: He was short and wiry but surprisingly strong. Her wiry hair refused to stay in place. The wiry athlete finished the race without effort. A wiry old farmer worked in the field all day.

english_meaning: The quality of having good judgement based on knowledge and experience. Deep understanding of what is true, right, or lasting. Accumulated learning and knowledge of a society or tradition. The soundness or sensibleness of an action or decision.
example_sentence: With age came patience and wisdom. He questioned the wisdom of selling the land now. The book collects the wisdom of village elders. She showed great wisdom in handling the dispute.

english_meaning: One of the four large molars at the very back of the jaw, appearing in adulthood. The last tooth to grow, usually between the ages of seventeen and twenty-five. A third molar that often causes pain or requires removal. A late-growing back tooth named for the maturity at which it appears.
example_sentence: His wisdom tooth had to be removed by a specialist. Many people feel pain when a wisdom tooth appears. She was told her wisdom teeth were growing sideways. A swollen gum is often a sign of a wisdom tooth.

english_meaning: Lacking strength, decisiveness, or firm conviction. Weak, feeble, or indecisive in character, opinion, or action. Used to describe something thin, watery, or lacking flavor when referring to food or drink. Vague or unclear, failing to take a clear stance on an issue.
example_sentence: His wishy-washy response failed to satisfy anyone on either side of the debate.  The soup tasted wishy-washy and clearly needed more seasoning.  She gave a wishy-washy answer instead of stating her opinion clearly.  Voters were frustrated by the candidate's wishy-washy stance on important issues.  The committee's wishy-washy leadership left the project without clear direction.

english_meaning: The ability to say or write things that are both clever and humorous. Your ability to think quickly and clearly and to make good decisions.
example_sentence: Brevity is the soul of wit He needed all his wits to find his way out. The game was a long battle of wits. It should not be beyond the wit of man to resolve this dispute.

english_meaning: A woman thought to have magical powers, especially evil ones. A female sorcerer or practitioner of witchcraft. In folklore, a woman who uses spells and charms. A term sometimes used disapprovingly for an unpleasant woman.
example_sentence: The story is about a witch who lives in the forest. She dressed up as a witch for Halloween. In old times, women accused of being witches were punished. The witch cast a spell on the prince.

english_meaning: The practice of magic, especially black magic, using supernatural powers. The use of spells and charms often associated with evil spirits. The art or exercise of magical powers by a witch. Supernatural or mystical influence attributed to sorcerers.
example_sentence: In ancient times, many innocent women were accused of witchcraft. She was fascinated by stories about witchcraft. The novel explores the mysterious world of witchcraft. Some cultures still believe in the power of witchcraft.

english_meaning: The time late at night when supernatural events are said to occur, traditionally midnight. A time associated with witches, ghosts, and magic. A period considered dark, mysterious, or eerie. Figuratively, a critical or difficult time of day, especially late at night. A moment when things feel strange or unsettling.
example_sentence: Ghost stories always come alive during the witching hour. She woke up at the witching hour to a strange noise. Legends say spirits roam freely at the witching hour. The old house feels haunted around the witching hour.

english_meaning: Eagerly and enthusiastically, especially about attending an event. Very willing to be somewhere and looking forward to it. In a lively, cheerful and fully prepared manner. Used to confirm an invitation with strong enthusiasm.
example_sentence: Of course I will come to your party, with bells on. She said she would be there with bells on. We arrived at the reunion with bells on. If you invite him, he will turn up with bells on.

english_meaning: To be unaware of or ignore everything except one focus, narrow-minded or not considering the bigger picture.
example_sentence: He rushed into the deal with blinkers on. She trusted him with blinkers on. The company invested with blinkers on. Many entered the market with blinkers on.

english_meaning: To succeed brilliantly or achieve something with great success. To achieve distinction. To perform exceptionally well. To win honorably. To succeed beyond expectations.
example_sentence: She passed the final exam with flying colours. The team completed the project with flying colours. He came through the interview with flying colours. The students performed with flying colours in the science competition.

english_meaning: In a forceful, arrogant, strict, or oppressive manner. It is used when someone acts with too much authority, power, or harshness.
example_sentence: The officer dealt with the workers with high hand. The manager ruled the office with high hand and nobody could question him. The landlord treated the poor tenants with high hand. The principal handled the matter with high hand instead of listening calmly.

english_meaning: With extra emphasis or something additional added. Even more so, with something extra on top. Used to say that something is better or bigger than expected.
example_sentence: He told the story with knobs on, adding many extra details. The party was a success, with knobs on. She described the event with knobs on for her friends. They celebrated their victory with knobs on.

word: With one’s tongue in one’s cheek
english_meaning: In a way that is not meant to be taken seriously. Speaking with humorous or ironic insincerity. Saying something jokingly while appearing serious.
example_sentence: He praised the plan with his tongue in his cheek. Her compliment was clearly made with tongue in cheek. The article was written with tongue in cheek and should not be taken literally. He said it with his tongue in his cheek, and everyone laughed.

english_meaning: To dry up and shrink, especially of plants. To lose freshness, strength, or vitality. To gradually decline or fade away. To make someone feel ashamed with a severe look or remark.
example_sentence: The flowers withered in the summer heat. His hopes withered as the days passed. Support for the plan withered after the scandal. She withered him with a single disapproving glance.

english_meaning: Dried, shriveled, or faded because of age, heat, or lack of water. Weakened, diminished, or lost in strength and vitality. Having become old, wrinkled, or physically frail. Past tense and past participle of wither, meaning became dry or caused to decline.
example_sentence: The withered leaves fell from the tree. Years of drought had withered the crops. His enthusiasm withered after repeated failures. She removed the withered flowers from the vase.

english_meaning: Intended to make someone feel completely crushed, mortified, or humiliated. It also refers to the action of decaying, shriveling, fading, or losing vitality.
example_sentence: She gave him a withering look that silenced the entire room. The crops were suffering under the withering heat of the summer sun. His withering criticism destroyed the young artist's confidence. The withering leaves fell gently to the dry ground. The general delivered a withering assessment of the troops' performance.

english_meaning: In a severely critical, scornful, or humiliating manner. In a way that makes someone feel small, embarrassed, or powerless. With devastating sharpness or contempt. In a manner that causes something to dry, fade, or weaken.
example_sentence: She spoke witheringly about the poorly managed project. The critic dismissed the performance witheringly. He looked witheringly at the person who interrupted him. The hot wind blew witheringly across the unwatered fields.

english_meaning: The highest part of a horse or similar animal’s back, located between the shoulder blades. A point used for measuring an animal’s height. Third-person singular of wither, meaning dries up, shrivels, fades, or loses strength.
example_sentence: The saddle rested just behind the horse’s withers. The veterinarian measured the pony at the withers. This plant withers quickly without water. Public trust withers when leaders hide the truth.

english_meaning: To refuse to give, provide, or allow something that is expected or requested. To keep back information, money, permission, or support. To deduct an amount from wages or payments, especially for tax. To restrain an action, feeling, or judgment.
example_sentence: The witness was accused of withholding important evidence. Employers withhold tax from each monthly salary. The committee decided to withhold its approval. She could not withhold a smile when she saw the surprise.

english_meaning: Inside a place, area, object, group, or boundary. Before a specified period of time has passed. Not beyond a particular distance, range, limit, or rule. Inwardly or internally. The inside or inner part of something.
example_sentence: Please remain within the marked area. We expect a reply within three days. The project stayed within its budget. Real confidence must come from within.

english_meaning: Extremely close to achieving or experiencing something. By a very small margin.
synonyms: ["On the verge of","Close to","Nearly","Almost","A hair's breadth from"]
example_sentence: They came within a whisker of winning the title. The car passed within a whisker of the wall. She was within a whisker of breaking the record. We were within a whisker of missing the flight.

english_meaning: Something that is achievable, attainable, or possible for someone. Refers to an opportunity, goal, or success that is close enough for a person to reach with effort.
example_sentence: Success is within your grasp if you work hard. Success is within her grasp if she continues to work hard. With this promotion, financial stability is finally within his grasp. Victory was within the team’s grasp, but they lost focus at the last minute. Education should be within the grasp of every child.

english_meaning: Without stopping what you are doing. Continuing to move, act, or progress smoothly without stopping, slowing down, or losing momentum.
example_sentence: Marta scored from 20 metres without breaking stride. She picked up the phone without breaking stride on her morning walk. He answered the tough question without breaking stride, showing his confidence.

english_meaning: To resist successfully. To endure. To remain undamaged or unaffected by something. To stand up against attack, pressure, or force without giving way. To bear or tolerate difficult conditions. Used for people, materials, or structures that are strong enough not to be defeated, broken, or harmed by the opposing force, pressure, weather, or hardship they face.
example_sentence: These houses are built to withstand strong earthquakes. The soldiers withstood the enemy attack for many hours. She had to withstand a lot of criticism for her decision. This material can withstand very high temperatures. He could not withstand the pressure and finally resigned.

english_meaning: Attestation of a fact or event. One that gives evidence. One who has personal knowledge of something. Something serving as evidence or proof. To testify to. To furnish proof of.
example_sentence: Police have appealed for anyone who witnessed the incident to contact them. We had witnessed one of the most outstanding theatrical performances of the decade. We have a witness to the killing. She gave a witness statement to the police.

english_meaning: Done in full awareness or consciousness; deliberate and knowing. It refers to someone who is fully conscious of the nature and consequences of their actions.
example_sentence: He was a witting accomplice in the elaborate financial fraud. The witness denied having any witting knowledge of the criminal conspiracy. She made a witting choice to abandon her promising career for art. Witting participants in the medical study were briefed about all possible risks. It was a witting violation of the established security protocols.

english_meaning: Wise, having good judgement. Possessing a strong intellect or intellectual capacity, intelligent, skillful, ingenious. Clever and humorous.
example_sentence: He was much in demand as a witty public speaker. She may have grown older, but she has grown no less witty. His speech was both witty and informative. Somebody made a witty remark about needing a forklift truck.

english_meaning: A man believed to have magical powers. A person who is exceptionally skilled in a particular field. A software feature that guides users through steps of a task. A sorcerer or magician in myth and fairy tales. Someone who does something remarkably well.
example_sentence: The wizard cast a spell to protect the kingdom. He is a wizard when it comes to solving math problems. Follow the setup wizard to install the program. Children love reading stories about a friendly wizard.

english_meaning: Old, shrunken, and wrinkled because of age, hardship, or exposure to the weather. A person, face, or object that has become dry, shrivelled, wrinkled, or thin because of old age, difficult experiences, illness, or long exposure to the sun and wind. It can also describe fruits or plants that have dried up.
example_sentence: The wizened old farmer smiled kindly despite his weathered face. She picked up a wizened apple that had been left in the basket for weeks. The traveller met a wizened man who shared stories of the ancient village. Years of working under the hot sun had left his hands wizened and rough.

english_meaning: To move from side to side in an unsteady way, to make something do this. To move or proceed with an irregular rocking or staggering motion or unsteadily and clumsily from side to side. An uncertainly directed movement. A slight unsteady movement from side to side. A moment when you hesitate or lose confidence about something.
example_sentence: Her voice wobbled with emotion. Yesterday the president showed the first signs of wobbling over the issue. This chair wobbles. The handlebars developed a wobble. The team is experiencing a mid-season wobble.

english_meaning: Unsteady, shaky, or moving from side to side in an unstable manner. Lacking firmness or stability, often used to describe furniture, structures, or physical balance. Used figuratively to describe a plan, situation, or argument that is weak or likely to fail. Trembling or shaking, especially due to nervousness, weakness, or fear.
example_sentence: The old chair was so wobbly that nobody dared sit on it.  Her legs felt wobbly after standing for hours in the heat.  The plan seemed wobbly from the very beginning and eventually fell apart.  The table wobbled because one of its legs was shorter than the others.  He took a few wobbly steps before regaining his balance.

english_meaning: Great sorrow, distress, or trouble. A deep sense of sadness, misery, or misfortune. It can describe personal suffering or broader troubles affecting people or situations.
example_sentence: She was full of woe after hearing the bad news. The villagers faced woe during the long drought. His woe was visible in the tears streaming down his face. Financial woe forced them to sell their house.

english_meaning: In a manner expressing profound sorrow, misery, or grief. It is frequently used to emphasize that something is very bad, inadequate, or entirely deplorable.
example_sentence: The school's science laboratory was woefully underequipped for modern scientific experiments. He shook his head woefully as he surveyed the severely ruined garden. Her defensive skills were woefully inadequate against the international champion. The construction project was woefully behind schedule due to constant interruptions. We remain woefully ignorant about the vast mysteries of the deep ocean.

english_meaning: An archaic legal or historical term originating from Anglo-Norman, meaning to empty, clear out, depart, or render void. It is typically encountered in historical texts concerning the vacation of property or nullification of rights.
example_sentence: The medieval writ required the current tenants to woidre the estate before the next harvest. Scholars translating the Anglo-Norman manuscript debated the exact historical meaning of woidre. To woidre the property meant leaving behind all permanent fixtures and crops. The king issued a formal order to woidre the borderlands of all known rebels. The contract included an ancient clause to woidre the agreement under extreme duress.

english_meaning: To pursue someone eagerly, often with selfish or aggressive intent.
example_sentence: Investors were wolfing after the new tech startup before it even launched. He spent years wolfing after fame and recognition in the film industry. Some journalists are constantly wolfing after sensational stories to sell papers. The company’s competitors were wolfing after its latest innovation.

english_meaning: To eat something very quickly and eagerly.
example_sentence: He wolfed down his breakfast before leaving for work. The kids wolfed down the pizza in just a few minutes. She was so hungry that she wolfed down the sandwich without chewing properly. They wolfed down the snacks while waiting for the movie to start.

english_meaning: A dangerous person who pretends to be harmless or friendly. Someone who hides evil intentions behind a kind appearance. A deceiver who disguises their true nature. A person whose outward behavior is misleading. Anyone who seems trustworthy but is secretly a threat.
example_sentence: Beware of him, he is a wolf in sheep's clothing. The kind stranger turned out to be a wolf in sheep's clothing. Many con artists are wolves in sheep's clothing. She did not know her new friend was a wolf in sheep's clothing.

english_meaning: To eat something quickly and greedily, as if one were a wolf. It conveys the idea of devouring food with great speed and appetite.
example_sentence: He wolfed out the pizza before anyone else could take a slice. After the long hike, they all wolfed out on sandwiches. Don’t wolf out your dinner so fast, you might get a stomachache. The kids wolfed out the birthday cake in minutes.

english_meaning: Having qualities traditionally associated with women, often implying weakness or softness.
example_sentence: His womanish behavior made him avoid confrontation. She criticized his womanish approach to handling problems. The villain mocked him for his womanish gestures. People often unfairly label sensitive men as womanish.

english_meaning: To habitually engage in relationships with multiple women, often in a flirtatious or exploitative way. It refers to a man who is fond of women in a way that is often considered morally questionable.
example_sentence: He tends to womanize whenever he travels to new cities. The movie portrays a man who womanizes but never commits to anyone. People criticized him for trying to womanize his colleague. Despite being married, he continued to womanize.

english_meaning: A man who habitually seeks out and engages in romantic or sexual relationships with multiple women, often showing little regard for their feelings.
example_sentence: He was known as a womanizer and never stayed in one relationship for long. The actor gained a reputation as a womanizer in Hollywood. Despite his charm, many considered him a womanizer. She avoided dating him because he had a history of being a womanizer

english_meaning: The organ in a woman’s body where a baby develops before birth. The uterus, a hollow muscular organ in female mammals where the embryo develops and grows until birth. It also metaphorically refers to a place where something originates or is nurtured.
example_sentence: The baby grew safely in her mother’s womb. The artist said his studio was like the womb of creativity. Scientists study how cells develop in the womb. The story was born in the womb of history.

english_meaning: A feeling of surprise and admiration caused by something beautiful or unexpected. Something that causes such a feeling. To think about something with curiosity or doubt. To want to know or be curious about something.
example_sentence: The children looked at the fireworks in wonder. The pyramids are among the wonders of the world. I wonder why he left so early. She wondered whether the news was true.

english_meaning: Extremely good, pleasing, or enjoyable. Causing feelings of surprise, admiration, or delight. Excellent in quality or performance. Remarkable and hard to believe because of its beauty or greatness.
example_sentence: We had a wonderful time at the beach. She is a wonderful teacher who inspires her students. The view from the mountain was simply wonderful. Thank you for the wonderful gift.

english_meaning: To try to win someone's love or affection, especially for marriage. To seek support, favor, approval, or cooperation from someone. To attract or persuade someone through effort, charm, or promises. The act of courting or seeking someone's love. Efforts made to gain support or approval.
example_sentence: He tried to woo her with flowers and thoughtful gifts. The company worked hard to woo new customers. The politician traveled across the country to woo voters. The university is trying to woo talented students with scholarships.

english_meaning: A hard-shelled tropical fruit with a strong aroma and tangy pulp. A fruit used to make chutneys, jams, and drinks. A fruit widely used in Ayurvedic medicine for digestion. A round brown fruit with sticky brown flesh inside. A native fruit of South Asia known for its medicinal value.
example_sentence: Wood apple chutney is a traditional dish in South Asia. He drank a glass of wood apple juice for digestion. The wood apple has a very hard outer shell. My mother often prepared wood apple sherbet in summer.

english_meaning: An imaginary prize given to the person or team that finishes last. The lowest place in a competition or league. A booby prize awarded in fun to the worst performer. Literally, a spoon made of wood used for cooking.
example_sentence: Our team finished last and took the wooden spoon again. Nobody wants to win the wooden spoon this season. He joked that he deserved the wooden spoon for his cooking. She stirred the sauce with a wooden spoon.

english_meaning: A small area covered with trees, smaller than a forest but larger than a few individual trees. It may be a small grove, copse, or patch of woodland found in rural or natural landscapes.
example_sentence: The children played near a quiet woodlet behind the village. Birds built their nests in the woodlet beside the river. A narrow path led through the woodlet to the old farmhouse. The deer disappeared into the dense woodlet at sunset.

english_meaning: A bird with a strong beak that pecks holes in tree trunks to find insects. Any bird of the family Picidae, known for drumming on wood. A bird that makes a rapid tapping sound on trees. Figuratively, a person who works persistently at the same task.
example_sentence: A woodpecker was tapping loudly on the old oak tree. We watched a woodpecker searching for insects in the bark. The forest echoed with the drumming of a woodpecker. Children were excited to spot a woodpecker near the path.

english_meaning: Absent-minded daydreaming or aimless thinking instead of paying attention. Indulgence in idle fancies or unrealistic imagination. The state of being lost in thought and unaware of one's surroundings. Foolish or impractical planning that leads nowhere.
example_sentence: The teacher noticed that half the class was wool gathering during the lecture. Stop wool gathering and finish your homework. His wool gathering cost him a promotion at work. She spent the whole afternoon wool gathering by the window.

english_meaning: In a way that shows you feel weak or ill and unable to think clearly. In a dizzy, unsteady, or slightly faint manner.
example_sentence: His eyes opened woozily. She emerged from the rollercoaster somewhat woozily. He lay motionless for about 30 seconds before standing up and woozily walking off the field. Michelle stumbles woozily out of bed to be sick in the bathroom. I looked woozily around for Mr and Mrs Gould.

english_meaning: A state of feeling unsteady, dizzy, or lightheaded. It is often accompanied by a sense of confusion or lack of balance. This condition can be caused by illness, exhaustion, or medication.
example_sentence: The medication caused a strange wooziness that lasted for hours. He woke up with a feeling of wooziness after the surgery. The heat and dehydration led to a sudden wooziness. She tried to shake off her wooziness before standing up.

english_meaning: Feeling unsteady, dizzy, or dazed, often as a result of illness, injury, or lack of sleep. It describes a sensation of being physically lightheaded or mentally clouded. It is frequently used to describe the side effects of medication or the feeling after a head concussion.
example_sentence: The medication made him feel slightly woozy and lightheaded. After spinning around in circles, the child felt incredibly woozy. She felt woozy after standing up too quickly from her seat. The athlete felt woozy after the collision and had to leave the field.

english_meaning: The general opinion, rumor, or gossip circulating among people. What people are saying informally, often in public.
example_sentence: Word on the street is that the company is planning to hire more staff soon. Word on the street says that the new cafe in town is amazing. I haven’t confirmed it, but word on the street is that she’s moving abroad. Word on the street is that the football team will win the championship this year.

english_meaning: A skilled writer or expert in words. A person who is skilled in using words, especially in writing. Someone who crafts language with precision and artistry.
example_sentence: She is a true wordsmith, crafting stories that captivate readers. The poet proved to be a wordsmith, blending emotion and rhythm seamlessly. As a wordsmith, he could turn simple sentences into powerful messages. Every article she writes shows her skill as a wordsmith.

english_meaning: Using or containing too many words. Verbose. Expressed in more words than necessary. Long-winded in speech or writing.
example_sentence: His essays are often too wordy and hard to follow. She gave a wordy explanation instead of a simple answer. The report is wordy but lacks substance. Editors dislike wordy writing.

english_meaning: Deserving respect, attention, or admiration. Having qualities that make someone or something good enough for a particular purpose. Suitable for a specified role, action, or reward. A person of great merit or importance.
example_sentence: He is a worthy candidate for the leadership role. This cause is worthy of our full support. She proved herself a worthy opponent in the debate. The village elders are considered worthies of the community.

english_meaning: To have a negative effect on something or to oppose someone or something. To create difficulties, reduce chances of success, or act in opposition to a goal, plan, person, or idea.
example_sentence: His lack of experience worked against him in the interview. Poor weather conditions worked against the rescue efforts. Her own fear started to work against her progress. Rising prices are working against small businesses.

english_meaning: To find a way to deal with a problem or obstacle without directly confronting it. To handle an issue, limitation, or obstacle by finding an alternative method, solution, or route instead of trying to remove or solve the problem directly.
example_sentence: We had to work around the broken printer by sending documents digitally. She worked around her tight schedule to attend the meeting. The developers found a way to work around the software bug. They worked around the traffic by leaving earlier than usual.

english_meaning: To include or introduce something gradually. To develop something slowly through effort. To gradually add something into a plan, system, conversation, or physical object.
example_sentence: She worked the idea into her proposal. He worked jokes into the presentation. They worked new data into the report. I worked your suggestion into the plan.

english_meaning: To be extremely effective and produce exactly the desired result. To succeed easily and immediately. To function perfectly without any trouble. To achieve the intended effect better than expected.
synonyms: ["Succeed","Do the trick","Work perfectly","Be effective","Go smoothly","Deliver results"]
example_sentence: The new medicine worked like a charm and the pain disappeared. Her polite approach worked like a charm with the angry customer. This cleaning trick works like a charm on old stains. The updated software works like a charm on older phones.

english_meaning: To work extremely hard and for long hours. To labour continuously with great effort and little rest. To exhaust oneself through heavy or tiring work. To toil constantly in order to achieve something.
example_sentence: He works like a dog to support his large family. During harvest season the farmers work like dogs. She worked like a dog to finish the project on time. They worked like dogs all summer to build the house.

english_meaning: To eliminate or reduce something by physical or mental effort, effort at work, or other activity. To get rid of something, often a feeling, energy, or debt, through action.
example_sentence: She went for a long run to work off her stress. He worked off his debt by doing extra shifts at the office. I need to work off the calories I ate at lunch. They worked off their frustration by cleaning the house.

english_meaning: To spend time and effort to improve, develop, fix, or complete something. To actively deal with a task, problem, project, skill, or situation in order to make progress or bring improvement. It can refer to physical work, mental effort, planning, learning, or repairing.
example_sentence: I am working on my report. She is working on her skills. We are working on the plan. He needs to work on communication.

english_meaning: To gradually achieve higher status, position, or success through effort and time. To start from a lower level and progress step by step to a higher level through hard work, experience, and persistence. It often refers to career growth, social status, or skill development.
example_sentence: She started as an intern and worked her way up to manager. He worked his way up in the company through dedication and honesty. They worked their way up from a small business to a large enterprise. She worked her way up to the top of her profession.

english_meaning: To exercise physically, to find a solution, or to develop successfully. Exercise or solve a problem. Work out means doing physical exercise to stay fit. It also means thinking carefully to find an answer or solution to a problem. In relationships or plans, it can mean ending successfully or being resolved in a good way.
example_sentence: I work out at the gym every morning. We need to work out a solution to this issue. She worked out the answer after some thinking. Their plan worked out better than expected.

english_meaning: To treat someone roughly or criticize strongly, to revise or improve something. To physically assault or hit someone. To examine, revise, or improve something carefully.
example_sentence: The gang worked him over after the argument. She worked over the report before submitting it. The mechanic worked over the engine to fix the problem. He got worked over by the critics for his controversial statement.

english_meaning: To deal with a problem or task step by step until it is finished or understood. To carefully handle, solve, or process something by giving it time and effort.
example_sentence: We need to work through these calculations carefully. She worked through her fear with the help of a counselor. The team worked through the report before submitting it. He stayed calm and worked through the problem step by step.

english_meaning: To make efforts to achieve a goal or result. To take planned and continuous actions in order to reach a particular aim, objective, or outcome.
example_sentence: The team is working towards improving disaster preparedness. She is working towards a master’s degree in climate studies. The government is working towards reducing poverty. We must work towards long term solutions for climate risks.

english_meaning: To gradually develop or produce something such as emotion, energy, courage, or effort. To build something slowly through effort or time. It can also mean preparing something step by step.
example_sentence: He worked up the courage to speak in the meeting. She worked up a sweat during her morning exercise. The story worked up excitement among the audience. It took him time to work up an appetite after the illness.

english_meaning: To cooperate, collaborate, or engage jointly with a person, group, organization, or system to achieve a shared goal.
synonyms: ["Collaborate with","Cooperate with","Team up with","Partner with","Coordinate with"]
example_sentence: She works with local communities to improve education. I enjoy working with people who are honest and skilled. The engineer is working with new software tools. Our team worked with the government on disaster planning.

word: Work your fingers to the bone
english_meaning: To work extremely hard for a long time. To labor exhaustively until physically tired. To toil relentlessly, often for little reward. To exert oneself to the point of exhaustion. To put in enormous effort in one's work.
example_sentence: She worked her fingers to the bone to feed her children. The farmers work their fingers to the bone during harvest season. He worked his fingers to the bone to build his business. My parents worked their fingers to the bone for our education.

english_meaning: Able to be used or done successfully. Practical and likely to succeed. Of material or land, capable of being shaped, worked or cultivated.
example_sentence: They finally reached a workable compromise. Is this a workable solution for the whole team? The clay must be soft and workable. We need a workable timetable before Monday.

english_meaning: Ordinary and everyday, without anything special. Relating to routine daily work. Plain and practical rather than exciting.
example_sentence: He longed to escape his workaday routine. The film shows the workaday life of a fisherman. She wore plain, workaday clothes. Behind the glamour lies a workaday business.

english_meaning: Someone who works too much. A person who is excessively devoted to work and finds it difficult to relax or stop working. Often prioritizes work over personal life, relationships, or health. Someone with an obsessive need to work. A person who derives identity and self-worth from working. Can have negative connotations due to work-life imbalance.
example_sentence: Sarah is a workaholic and often misses family gatherings because of her job. He became a workaholic after getting promoted to manager. Despite being exhausted, the workaholic stayed late at the office to finish the project. John’s friends worry about him because he is turning into a workaholic.

english_meaning: Concerned with or relating to material things, practical matters, or everyday life rather than spiritual or intellectual matters. Experienced and sophisticated as a result of extensive knowledge of life and human affairs. Pertaining to the physical world rather than a spiritual or heavenly realm. Used to describe a person who is knowledgeable about practical matters such as money, fashion, and social customs.
example_sentence: He gave up his worldly possessions to live a simple, monastic life.  Years of travel had made her remarkably worldly and culturally aware.  The monk renounced all worldly pleasures in pursuit of spiritual peace.  Her worldly wisdom helped her navigate difficult business negotiations with ease.  The novel explores the conflict between worldly ambition and spiritual fulfillment.

english_meaning: Extending or spread throughout the entire world. Existing or happening in all parts of the globe. On a global scale; everywhere in the world.
example_sentence: The company sells its products worldwide. The news of the discovery spread worldwide within hours. Climate change is a worldwide concern. The concert was broadcast live to a worldwide audience.

english_meaning: Something that causes worry or concern. A situation, behavior, or condition that makes people feel anxious, uneasy, or concerned about possible problems or danger.
example_sentence: The dark clouds were worrisome before the flight. His sudden silence is worrisome to his family. The doctor said the test results looked worrisome. Rising prices are becoming worrisome for many people.

english_meaning: To feel anxious or troubled about possible problems. A state of mental unease caused by fear of something bad. To cause someone to feel anxious or upset. A problem or situation that causes anxiety. To keep thinking about something unpleasant that may happen.
example_sentence: Try not to worry about things you cannot control. Her long silence began to worry the family. Money is his biggest worry at the moment. He worries that he may fail the interview.

english_meaning: A person who worries excessively about small or unlikely problems. Someone who is habitually anxious. A person who frets over minor issues. An individual prone to overthinking. A chronic worrier.
example_sentence: Don’t be such a worrywart; everything will be fine. My mother is a worrywart about our safety. He is a worrywart who checks the door lock ten times. She calls herself a worrywart about small things.

english_meaning: To become worse or make something worse. To deteriorate in condition, quality, or state. To cause a situation to become more serious. To decline in health or well-being. To aggravate an existing problem.
example_sentence: The weather is expected to worsen by evening. His condition worsened after the accident. Ignoring the problem will only worsen it. Their relationship began to worsen after the argument.

english_meaning: The feeling or expression of reverence and adoration for a deity. To show religious devotion or love, often through ceremonies or prayers. Great admiration or devotion shown towards a person, principle, or object.
example_sentence: People gather in the temple every Sunday for worship. He worshipped his older brother and followed him everywhere. The worship of ancient gods involved many fascinating rituals. She led the congregation in a powerful song of worship. Many cultures have unique forms of ancestor worship.

english_meaning: Deserving of respect because one is good at one's work. Competent and effective in a role or profession. Living up to the standard expected of a person in that position.
example_sentence: Any teacher worth her salt would notice that mistake. No journalist worth his salt would print an unverified story. If he is worth his salt, he will finish the job on time. Every engineer worth their salt double-checks the calculations.

english_meaning: Having or showing the qualities or abilities that merit recognition or reward. Deserving of effort, attention, or respect. A person notable or important in a particular sphere.
example_sentence: The charity is a worthy cause that deserves our support. He proved himself to be a worthy opponent during the chess match. She is a worthy successor to the previous team captain. They felt the project was not worthy of their time and resources. The town's worthies gathered at the hall for the annual meeting.

english_meaning: To seriously damage something or to cause intense mental or physical suffering. Great destruction, collapse, or extreme physical or mental suffering.
example_sentence: The storm wracked the coastline. The illness wracked his body for years. She was wracked with anxiety before the exam. The war left the city in utter wrack. The building was reduced to wrack after the earthquake. The floods caused widespread wrack across the region.

english_meaning: The spirit or ghost of a dead person that appears as a faint shadowy figure. In literature and folklore it is often seen as a supernatural appearance connected with death. The word is also used metaphorically for a person who looks extremely thin, weak, pale, or ghost like. Sometimes it describes something that seems unreal, fleeting, or barely visible.
example_sentence: The old castle was said to be haunted by the wraith of a forgotten king. After weeks of illness, he looked like a wraith, pale and weak. A pale wraith seemed to move silently through the dark hallway. In the mist, the distant figure appeared like a wraith floating above the ground.

english_meaning: A dispute or argument, typically one that is long and complicated. To engage in a lengthy and noisy quarrel. To round up, herd, or take charge of livestock, especially horses.
example_sentence: The politicians had a long wrangle over the new budget policy. He wrangled with his landlord for months about the broken heater. Our guide had to wrangle the scattered horses back to the camp. After a lengthy legal wrangle, the company finally won the lawsuit. It took hours to wrangle the children into their costumes for the play.

english_meaning: To cover an object by folding or winding a material around it. To finish or conclude something. Something used to cover or enclose, a covering layer. Completion of an event or task.
example_sentence: Wrap the bandage firmly around the injured limb. He spent the evening wrapping up the Christmas presents. Each apple was wrapped in paper. She wrapped the present and tied it with ribbon. She wrapped the baby in a blanket. We stock a wide range of cards and gift wrap.

english_meaning: To finish something. To bring something to an end or complete it. It can refer to finishing a meeting, concluding a task, dressing warmly, or covering something.
example_sentence: We need to wrap up this meeting quickly. She wrapped up the baby in a warm blanket. Let’s wrap up the project by tomorrow. He wrapped up his speech with a strong message.

english_meaning: Extreme anger, especially the strong anger of a powerful person or of God in religious texts. Severe punishment or vengeance carried out as a result of such anger. A literary and formal word for intense rage. Fury that is righteous, fearsome, or destructive in nature.
example_sentence: The king's wrath fell upon those who had betrayed him. He feared the wrath of his father after the broken window. Religious texts often speak of the wrath of God against injustice. The minister faced the wrath of the public after the scandal. Nothing could calm her wrath once the truth was revealed.

english_meaning: To cause something harmful or damaging to happen, especially destruction, chaos, or punishment. To inflict or carry out an action with significant negative consequences. Often used in the phrase wreak havoc, meaning to cause widespread disorder or damage. To bring about a forceful and often violent effect on a person, place, or situation.
example_sentence: The storm wreaked havoc on coastal towns, destroying homes and roads.  The scandal wreaked serious damage on the company's reputation.  The invading army wreaked destruction across the countryside.  Economic instability can wreak chaos on global markets.  The virus wreaked devastation on the local farming community.

english_meaning: An arrangement of flowers, leaves, or stems fastened in a ring and used for decoration or for laying on a grave. A circular band of foliage. A curl or ring of smoke or soft cloud.
example_sentence: We hung a beautiful pine wreath on our front door for the holidays. The mayor laid a wreath at the war memorial to honor the fallen soldiers. A wreath of thick smoke rose slowly from the old chimney. She wore a delicate floral wreath in her hair during the spring festival. Making a homemade wreath requires patience and fresh greenery.

english_meaning: To cause serious damage or destruction physically or emotionally. Something that is badly damaged or destroyed. The remains of something ruined such as a vehicle or building. Severe damage, destruction, or ruined condition.
example_sentence: The storm left the village in complete wreck. The accident wrecked his car beyond repair. Stress can wreck your health if ignored. Divers explored the wreck at the bottom of the sea.

english_meaning: A tool with adjustable jaws used for gripping and turning nuts, bolts, or pipes. To pull or twist something suddenly and violently. A sudden, violent twist or pull. A feeling of intense sadness or emotional pain caused by parting from someone or something. To injure a part of the body by twisting it sharply. A wrench can refer to a metallic hand tool used by mechanics, the act of pulling something forcefully, or the emotional pain felt when leaving a beloved person, place, or situation.
example_sentence: He used a heavy wrench to loosen the rusted bolts on the old engine. She wrenched the door open and rushed out of the room in anger. Leaving his childhood home was a real wrench for him. He wrenched his back while lifting the heavy box without help. The mechanic always keeps several different sizes of wrench in his toolbox.

english_meaning: To pull or force something away from someone's grasp with a violent or sudden twist. To obtain something from someone with great effort or difficulty.
