To take control or power away from someone, often against their will. To extract information or a confession through intense pressure or force. To seize an opportunity or advantage from a competitive situation.
example_sentence: The guard managed to wrest the weapon from the intruder after a brief struggle. She had to wrest the truth from him through hours of interrogation. The small party managed to wrest control of the local council in the recent election. He tried to wrest the heavy trophy from his teammate's hands during the celebration.

english_meaning: To engage in a physical struggle with someone by trying to throw or force them to the ground. To struggle or contend with a difficult problem, situation, or emotion. To force or move something with difficulty or strenuous effort. To take part in the sport of wrestling as a professional or amateur. To grapple mentally or spiritually with a decision or belief.
example_sentence: The two brothers would often wrestle in the backyard for hours. Scientists continue to wrestle with the complexities of the new virus. He managed to wrestle the heavy suitcase into the overhead compartment. She had to wrestle with her conscience before making the final choice.

english_meaning: To take something from someone by force or struggle. To gain control of something after a hard fight or contest. To pull an object out of another's grip.
example_sentence: The officer wrestled the knife away from him. The opposition wrestled power away from the ruling party. She wrestled the bag away from the thief. He wrestled the ball away in the last minute.

english_meaning: To force someone or something to the ground by struggling. To bring under control after a hard effort. To reduce or overcome a problem through persistent effort.
example_sentence: Two guards wrestled the intruder down. He wrestled the frightened calf down gently. The government is trying to wrestle inflation down. She wrestled her fears down and spoke.

english_meaning: To push or force something away from oneself with effort. To remove something with a struggle. To fight off an attacker or a difficulty.
example_sentence: He wrestled the heavy lid off the tank. She wrestled off the wet coat in a hurry. The player wrestled off two defenders. They wrestled off the challenge and won.

english_meaning: To free oneself from something by struggling. To escape from a difficult situation with great effort. To get out of an obligation or agreement by argument or struggle.
synonyms: ["Escape from","Break free of","Extricate oneself","Get out of","Wriggle out of","Free oneself"]
example_sentence: He wrestled out of the tight jacket. She wrestled out of the ropes and ran. The firm tried to wrestle out of the contract. They wrestled out of a difficult position.

english_meaning: A person who takes part in the sport of wrestling as a professional or amateur. An athlete who engages in hand-to-hand combat by grappling and throwing opponents. One who struggles or grapples with a difficult problem or situation. A competitor in various traditional forms of physical combat like sumo or catch-style wrestling. A performer in televised professional wrestling entertainment. A person characterized by their physical strength and skill in close-quarters struggle.
example_sentence: The champion wrestler pinned his opponent to the mat in the final round. He is a retired professional wrestler who now trains young athletes. The philosopher was a mental wrestler who tackled complex ethical dilemmas. Local villagers gathered at the fair to watch the traditional wrestler compete in the sand pit.

english_meaning: A physical competition involving grappling and combat maneuvers. The act of struggling or contending with a difficult problem or situation. A professional entertainment sport featuring scripted combat and theatrical elements. The practice of throwing or pinning an opponent to the ground using physical force. Engaging in a vigorous effort to master or overcome something.
example_sentence: The high school team is practicing wrestling techniques for the upcoming state championship. She spent all night wrestling with the complex mathematical equations in her thesis. Professional wrestling attracts millions of viewers with its blend of athletics and drama. Ancient cultures developed various styles of wrestling as a fundamental form of combat training.

english_meaning: An unfortunate or miserable person deserving pity. A person regarded as despicable, mean, or contemptible. Someone in a very unhappy or unlucky condition. A used as a term of mild disapproval or playful insult. A person of low character or poor moral standing.
example_sentence: The poor wretch had not eaten for three days. The cruel wretch hurt his own brother for the sake of money. She felt sorry for the homeless wretch sleeping on the bench. You little wretch, where have you hidden my keys? Many a wretch has been transformed by a single act of kindness.

english_meaning: Being in a very unhappy or unfortunate state. Of poor quality or very bad. Used to express anger or annoyance. Deserving of pity or contempt. Being in a state of great distress or misfortune. Extremely unsatisfactory or miserable in appearance or character.
example_sentence: The family lived in a wretched shack that barely protected them from the rain. He felt wretched after realizing he had offended his best friend. The wretched weather ruined our plans for a picnic in the park. She looked at the wretched beggar with a mixture of pity and sadness.

english_meaning: In a very unhappy or unfortunate state. To a very poor or inadequate degree. In a way that expresses misery or sorrow. Being of very low quality or value. In a manner that is despicable or contemptible.
example_sentence: The refugees lived wretchedly in the overcrowded camps during the winter. She felt wretchedly guilty about the accident even years later. The play was wretchedly performed by the amateur cast. The old man lived wretchedly in a small, damp basement room.

english_meaning: A state of extreme misery, unhappiness, or misfortune. The quality of being very poor in condition or quality. A feeling of deep distress or mental anguish. The state of being despicable, contemptible, or worthless. Physical suffering or severe lack of comfort.
example_sentence: The sheer wretchedness of the refugees' living conditions was heartbreaking to witness. He couldn't hide the wretchedness in his eyes after losing his entire family. The old house had fallen into a state of absolute wretchedness and decay. Despite his immense wealth, he lived a life of inner wretchedness and isolation.

english_meaning: To twist or move with small quick movements often because of discomfort or excitement. To move by twisting, turning, or squirming in a small and repeated way.
example_sentence: The child wriggled in his chair. The fish wriggled out of my hand. She wriggled through the narrow gap. He tried to wriggle free.

english_meaning: A person who builds, makes or repairs something, usually by hand. It is used for traditional craft workers such as a shipwright, wheelwright or playwright. The word comes from an old term meaning maker or builder.
example_sentence: The village wright repaired wooden wheels for the old carts. A skilled shipwright worked on the new fishing boat. Her grandfather was known as the best wright in the region. The playwright spent months perfecting his new drama.

english_meaning: To twist or squeeze something forcibly, especially to extract liquid. To distort or contort in emotion or expression, such as grief or frustration. To obtain something with difficulty.
example_sentence: She wrung the wet towel before hanging it to dry. He wrung his hands in anxiety. They managed to wring a confession from the suspect. The artist wrung every emotion out of the story.

english_meaning: A slight line or fold in something, especially fabric or the skin of the face. To make or cause lines or folds in something. A minor difficulty or snag.
example_sentence: The old man had deep wrinkles on his forehead. Be careful not to wrinkle the silk dress. She tried to iron out the wrinkles from the shirt. The new plan has a few wrinkles that need to be ironed out. He wrinkled his nose in disgust at the smell.

english_meaning: Having small lines or folds in the skin or fabric. Marked by wrinkles. Showing signs of aging or lack of ironing.
example_sentence: The baby held onto his grandmother's wrinkled hand. I cannot wear this wrinkled shirt to the interview. He had a wrinkled face from years of working in the sun. The washed clothes were left wrinkled in the basket. She applied a cream to soothe her wrinkled skin.

english_meaning: The joint connecting the hand to the forearm. The narrow flexible part of the arm just above the hand. The part of a garment or watch strap that fits around this joint.
example_sentence: She wears a silver bracelet on her wrist. He sprained his wrist while playing badminton. The watch felt loose on his thin wrist. Typing for hours can cause wrist pain.

english_meaning: A formal written order issued by a court or legal authority. A document commanding a person to do or stop doing something. Legal authority or power to act. An official command in written form.
example_sentence: The court issued a writ against the company. He challenged the order through a writ petition. A writ of habeas corpus was filed the same day. The writ was served on the defendant yesterday.

english_meaning: To record something on paper or in writing. To make a written note of information. To put thoughts, ideas, or details into written form. To officially reduce the value of an asset in accounting.
example_sentence: Please write down your address here. She wrote down every word the professor said. Don't forget to write down the phone number. The company had to write down the value of its old equipment.

english_meaning: Something worth or not worth mentioning because of its quality or importance. To be unusually good, impressive, or exciting.
example_sentence: The food was nothing to write home about. The movie was fine, but nothing to write home about. The meal was not bad, yet nothing to write home about. His performance was something to write home about; everyone praised him. The hotel was clean but not worth writing home about.

english_meaning: To cancel a debt or record it as a loss in accounts. To dismiss someone or something as unimportant or a failure. To damage a vehicle beyond repair. To acknowledge that money owed cannot be recovered. To regard as hopeless or worthless.
example_sentence: The bank agreed to write off the loan. Critics wrote off the film as a failure. Do not write him off; he can still succeed. Her car was written off after the accident.

english_meaning: Make continual twisting, squirming movements or contortions of the body. Respond with great emotional or physical discomfort to. To twist the body about, or squirm, as in pain, violent effort, etc.
example_sentence: The injured snake writhed on the ground. He lay writhing in pain after the nasty fall. She writhed in embarrassment when her mistake was pointed out. The patient was writhing on the hospital bed. The sudden cramp caused him to writhe in agony.

english_meaning: Something believed to be destined or predetermined by fate. An event that seems to be meant to happen. A romantic idea of a predestined relationship. A situation that appears to be arranged by destiny. Fate that cannot be avoided or changed.
example_sentence: Their meeting felt as if it was written in the stars. She believed their marriage was written in the stars. Success in this project seems written in the stars. Some say our friendship was written in the stars.

english_meaning: A person who behaves illegally or dishonestly. An individual who commits a sin or a moral transgression. A lawbreaker who violates established rules or statutes. One who commits an offense or a crime. Someone who acts in a way that is unfair or harmful to others.
example_sentence: The police are determined to bring every wrongdoer to justice. She forgave the wrongdoer despite the harm they had caused her. The company launched an investigation to identify the wrongdoer behind the fraud. Religious texts often speak about the eventual redemption of a sincere wrongdoer.

english_meaning: Illegal or dishonest behavior. An act that is morally wrong or against the law. Misconduct or bad actions. Any act that violates ethical or legal standards.
example_sentence: The company was cleared of any wrongdoing after the inquiry. He denied all charges of wrongdoing. Any wrongdoing will be strictly punished. The investigation revealed serious wrongdoing.

english_meaning: Beaten out or shaped by hammering. Worked into shape by artistry or effort. Worked, elaborated, or created.
example_sentence: The gate was made of solid wrought iron. The storm wrought havoc on the coastal towns. Her dress was intricately wrought with silver threads. A well-wrought plan is essential for the project's success. The poetry is carefully wrought to evoke emotion.

english_meaning: Showing that you find a bad or difficult situation slightly funny. Bent to one side. Bent, twisted, or turned usually abnormally to one side.
example_sentence: He pulled a wry face when I asked him how it had gone. At least we got one vote,’ she said with a wry smile. With wry humour, they laugh at their misfortunes. Jim permitted himself a wry smile.

english_meaning: Doing or saying something with a dry, ironic, or slightly mocking humor, often showing that you find something strange, awkward, or mildly amusing in a thoughtful or restrained way. It can also suggest a twisted or skewed expression, especially of the face, reflecting irony or discomfort.
example_sentence: She smiled wryly when she realized she had forgotten her own birthday. He wryly admitted that his plan had failed from the beginning. “That went better than expected,” she said wryly after the disaster. The teacher wryly noted that no one had done the homework again.

english_meaning: Showing hospitality and kindness to guests, strangers, or foreigners. Being friendly and generous to visitors.
example_sentence: The villagers were xenial, welcoming every traveler with food and shelter. She has a xenial nature and always makes visitors feel at home. Their xenial traditions are rooted in their culture of hospitality. Being xenial is an important trait for anyone working in tourism.

english_meaning: A gift given to a guest or a present exchanged between host and guest, especially in ancient times. A traditional or formal gift presented to a guest as a gesture of hospitality, goodwill, or respect. Historically, it was used in ancient Greek and Roman cultures where hosts would offer gifts to visitors or guests as a sign of honor and friendship.
example_sentence: The host presented a beautiful xenium to honor his guest. In ancient cultures, offering a xenium was a sign of respect. She brought a small xenium when visiting her friend’s home. The tradition of giving a xenium still exists in some societies.

english_meaning: Friendly and welcoming to strangers or guests. A person who is warm, hospitable, and kind toward strangers. It is often used to highlight generosity and openness in social behavior.
example_sentence: The village is known for its xenodochial people who warmly greet visitors. She has a xenodochial nature, always making newcomers feel comfortable. The host was extremely xenodochial, offering food and shelter to everyone. His xenodochial attitude helped him make friends wherever he traveled.

english_meaning: A place or institution that provides lodging for strangers, especially pilgrims or travelers. A charitable shelter for strangers,  A religious guesthouse in early Christian times, A hospice-like place for travelers. An ancient or historical type of guest house, often run by religious communities, where strangers, travelers, or pilgrims were welcomed and given shelter, food, and care. It reflects the idea of hospitality toward unknown guests.
example_sentence: The ancient xenodochium offered refuge to weary travelers crossing the desert. Monks managed the xenodochium and ensured every guest received food and rest. In medieval times, a xenodochium served both pilgrims and the poor. The ruins of the old xenodochium still stand near the historic church.

english_meaning: An intense enthusiasm for foreign people, customs, or products. An excessive admiration for anything that comes from abroad. A strong preference for foreign culture over one's own. Obsessive fondness for foreign languages, fashion, or lifestyles. A mania for all things strange or foreign.
example_sentence: His xenomania showed in every corner of his imported furniture. Critics blamed xenomania for the decline of local crafts. Her xenomania began after a long trip through Europe. Xenomania is often mistaken for simple curiosity about the world.

english_meaning: A person who loves or is strongly attracted to foreign cultures, people, or things. One who admires that which is unfamiliar or from other lands. An individual fascinated by foreign customs, languages, or lifestyles. A lover of the exotic and the foreign.
example_sentence: As a xenophile, she loves traveling to remote countries. He is a true xenophile who collects art from around the world. Xenophiles often learn several foreign languages. The city attracts xenophiles with its diverse culture.

english_meaning:
Fear or hatred of strangers or foreigners.
Xenophobia is an intense or irrational dislike or fear of people from other countries or cultures. It often leads to prejudice, discrimination, or hostility toward foreigners.
example_sentence: The rise of xenophobia has affected immigration policies worldwide. She experienced xenophobia when moving to a new country. Xenophobia can result in social tension and conflict. Educating people about cultural diversity helps reduce xenophobia.

english_meaning: A musical instrument made of wooden bars that are struck with mallets to produce sound. A teaching tool used in early music education. A melodic percussion instrument. Sometimes used in children’s toys for learning sound and rhythm. A percussion instrument consisting of a series of wooden bars of different lengths. Each bar produces a different pitch when struck with a mallet. It is commonly used in orchestras, bands, and music education.
example_sentence: She played a cheerful tune on the xylophone. The child learned basic music using a colorful xylophone. The xylophone added a bright sound to the orchestra. He tapped the xylophone gently with two mallets.

english_meaning: A medium-sized sailing boat equipped for cruising or racing. A luxurious recreational boat or ship. To sail or cruise in a yacht.
example_sentence: The billionaire hosted a lavish party on his private yacht. They spent the weekend sailing the yacht along the coast. He moored his luxury yacht in the marina. The yacht club organized a sailing competition for the summer. Owning a yacht requires significant maintenance and expense.

english_meaning: A large starchy tuber with rough brown skin and firm white or yellow flesh. A root vegetable eaten boiled, roasted, or pounded. The climbing plant that produces these tubers. A staple food in parts of Africa and Asia.
example_sentence: Pounded yam is served with rich soup. Yams are heavier and starchier than potatoes. She stored the yams in a cool, dry place. The yam vine climbs along the wooden pole.

english_meaning: A sudden, hard pull. To pull or remove abruptly and vigorously. A quick and forceful jerk.
example_sentence: He gave the door a hard yank, but it wouldn't open. She tried to yank the weeds out of the garden. The dentist had to yank the bad tooth out. I felt a sudden yank on my fishing line. Don't yank the dog's leash so violently.

english_meaning: An imperial unit of length equal to three feet or 0·9144 metres. An enclosed area of ground next to a building. A place used for a particular kind of work, such as a shipyard or railway yard. A garden area around a house.
example_sentence: He bought three yards of cloth for the curtains. The children were playing in the back yard. One yard is equal to three feet. The old trains are kept in the railway yard.

english_meaning: A measuring rod a yard long. A standard used for comparison. A criterion or metric for evaluating performance or quality.
example_sentence: Profitability is not the only yardstick of a company's success. He used a wooden yardstick to measure the fabric. Test scores are often used as a yardstick for educational quality. We need a reliable yardstick to evaluate the outcome properly. Her performance set a new yardstick for future athletes.

english_meaning: To open your mouth wide and breathe in deeply through it, usually because you are tired or bored. An involuntary intake of breath through a wide open mouth, usually triggered by fatigue or boredom. Something or someone that is very boring.
example_sentence: He stood up, stretched and yawned. I can't stop yawning - I must be tired. She managed to stifle a yawn. He covered his mouth to hide his yawn. The film was a total yawn.

english_meaning: A period of twelve months, or three hundred and sixty five days. The time the earth takes to travel once around the sun. A period used for keeping records, such as a school year or a financial year. A long time, often used in the plural for emphasis.
example_sentence: She turned eighteen years old last month. The academic year begins in September. He has worked at this company for ten years. I have not seen him in years.

english_meaning: Continuously, over many years without change. Happening in the same way every single year. Repeatedly and regularly for a long period. Used to stress a long, unchanging routine.
example_sentence: They visit the same seaside town year in, year out. Year in, year out, he walked to the same office at seven o'clock. The festival is held on the first Sunday of May, year in, year out. Farmers here plant the same crops year in, year out.

english_meaning: To have an intense feeling of longing or desire for something, typically something that one has lost or been separated from. It implies a deep emotional ache or a persistent craving for a person, place, or state of being. Often used in literary or poetic contexts to describe soulful longing.
example_sentence: She began to yearn for the comfort of her childhood home. Many refugees yearn for the day they can safely return to their country. He would often yearn for a life of adventure and travel. They yearn to see justice served after years of legal battles.

english_meaning: A feeling of intense longing for something. A deep desire or craving, especially for something lost or unattainable. A strong feeling of wishing for something.
example_sentence: She felt a deep yearning to return to her homeland. The boy looked at the expensive toys with yearning. After months of travel, he had a strong yearning for a home-cooked meal. Her poetry reflects a yearning for peace and simplicity. There is a universal yearning among humans for love and connection.

english_meaning: A loud, sharp cry, especially of pain, surprise, or delight. To shout in a loud, piercing voice. To communicate something with high volume.
example_sentence: He heard a loud yell coming from the dark alley. Please do not yell at the children when they make mistakes. The fans began to yell with excitement as the team scored. She had to yell over the loud music to be heard. Give me a yell when dinner is completely ready.

english_meaning: Lacking courage; easily frightened. Cowardly and unwilling to face danger. Describing someone who avoids confrontation out of fear. Used as an insult for a person who runs away from trouble.
example_sentence: He was too yellow-bellied to admit his mistake. The villagers called him a yellow-bellied coward. Don't be yellow-bellied; speak up for what is right. Her yellow-bellied brother refused to join the rescue party.

english_meaning: A short, sharp cry, especially of pain or alarm. To utter a quick, shrill cry. A sudden vocalization often made by animals or humans in distress.
example_sentence: The puppy let out a yelp when someone stepped on its paw. She gave a little yelp of surprise when the balloon popped. We heard the sudden yelp of a fox in the distance. He backed away with a yelp of pure terror. The sudden sting made him yelp in pain.

english_meaning: A strong desire or craving. The basic unit of money in Japan. It refers to a sudden or intense yearning to do or have something.
example_sentence: I have a sudden yen for chocolate. She has always had a yen to travel the world. The exchange rate for the yen is very favorable right now. He felt a deep yen to return to his hometown. It is hard to resist such a strong yen.

english_meaning: Excellent, loyal and useful help given in time of need. Faithful and valuable service rendered with sincerity. Hard, honest work done reliably for a cause or person. Timely assistance that proves genuinely effective.
example_sentence: The volunteers did yeoman’s service during the floods. He rendered yeoman’s service to the school for thirty years. The nurses performed yeoman’s service throughout the crisis. Our neighbours did yeoman’s service when my father fell ill.

english_meaning: Last night. Yestreen is a Scottish and literary word meaning the night just before today. It refers specifically to yesterday night and is mostly used in poetry, old literature, or formal writing.
example_sentence: He arrived home late yestreen after a long journey. The storm that began yestreen damaged several houses. She spoke of events that happened yestreen with sadness. Yestreen was colder than any night this week.

english_meaning: To produce or provide a natural, agricultural, or industrial product. To give way to arguments, demands, or pressure. It describes the act of surrendering or the quantity of something produced.

english_meaning: A rude, aggressive, or hooligan-like young person. A young man who behaves in a noisy, violent, or antisocial way, often involved in petty crime or troublemaking. The term is mostly British slang.
example_sentence: The yob smashed the shop window during the protest. Local authorities are trying to stop yobs from vandalizing the park. A group of yobs were causing trouble outside the stadium. The police caught a yob trying to steal a bicycle.

english_meaning: A semi-solid sourish food prepared from milk fermented by added bacteria, often sweetened or flavored with fruit. It is a dairy product known for its probiotic benefits and creamy texture. It is a staple in many cultures around the world for both cooking and direct consumption.
example_sentence: She enjoys eating plain yogurt with a drizzle of honey in the morning. Yogurt is a great source of calcium and healthy bacteria for the gut. You can use yogurt as a healthy substitute for sour cream in many recipes. The local shop sells a variety of frozen yogurt flavors.

english_meaning: A wooden frame placed over the necks of animals so they can pull together. A device or harness that joins animals for work. A burden, control, or oppressive authority. To join, link, or harness together. To force someone into service or control.
example_sentence: The oxen pulled the cart under a heavy yoke. The people struggled to throw off the yoke of tyranny. The farmer yoked two animals before sunrise. The plan would yoke local schools to a national testing system.

english_meaning: An uneducated and unsophisticated person from the countryside. It refers to a person who is often perceived as not very intelligent or uninformed about modern urban culture. It is frequently used in a slightly derogatory, stereotypical, or humorous way to describe a naive country bumpkin.
example_sentence: The arrogant tourists treated the locals as if they were uneducated yokels. He played the part of a naive country yokel in the new comedy movie. A group of local yokels gathered outside the village store to stare at the expensive car. She felt like a complete yokel when she couldn't figure out the subway system in the big city.

english_meaning: A metric prefix meaning one septillion (1024) times the base unit. The largest prefix in the International System of Units, used for describing astronomical or planetary-scale measurements. Represented by the symbol Y.
example_sentence: A yottabyte could store the entire contents of millions of data centers. The prefix yotta was added to the SI system in 1991. Astronomers sometimes describe enormous energies in yottajoules. One yottabyte equals one thousand zettabytes.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,024 zettabytes. One of the largest standard units of data storage. A theoretical measure used for extremely vast amounts of digital information.
example_sentence: A yottabyte is larger than any storage system built today. One yottabyte equals 1,024 zettabytes. Engineers rarely use the term yottabyte in daily work. Future networks may handle yottabytes of data.

english_meaning: You failed or you missed your chance to do something important.
example_sentence: You blew it when you forgot to submit your job application on time. She blew it by arguing with the manager during the interview. We had a great chance to win the match, but we blew it. He knows he blew it when he lied to his best friend.

word: You look like a million bucks
english_meaning: You look extremely attractive, elegant, stylish, or impressive. This idiom is used to compliment someone’s appearance, meaning.
example_sentence: Wow, you look like a million bucks in that dress!. After his makeover, he looked like a million bucks. You must be going to a party, you look like a million bucks today!. She felt like a million bucks after winning the award.

word: You look like a million dollars
english_meaning: You look amazing, stunning, or exceptionally good. It expresses strong admiration, often when someone is dressed up or looking their best.
example_sentence: Wow! You look like a million dollars in that wedding dress!. After the makeover, she looked like a million dollars. He came to the party in a new suit and looked like a million dollars. Even after a long flight, she still looked like a million dollars.

english_meaning: Having the qualities, freshness, or energy of a young person. Looking or appearing young. Characteristic of youth or the early stage of life. Vigorous and lively in nature.
example_sentence: She has a youthful appearance despite her age. His youthful enthusiasm inspired the whole team. The painting captured her youthful beauty. He remained youthful in spirit throughout his life.

english_meaning: A youthful mistake. An immature decision. A reckless act committed in youth. A foolish action caused by inexperience. A lapse in judgment during adolescence or early adulthood. An impulsive act later regretted. A minor offense committed while growing up. An error made before reaching maturity.
example_sentence: He put his conviction down to a youthful indiscretion that he deeply regretted. The politician was forgiven for what many called a youthful indiscretion. She laughed off the embarrassing photograph as a youthful indiscretion. A single youthful indiscretion should not define a person's entire future.

english_meaning: A woman who is plump, full-figured, or shapely in an attractive way. A woman slightly fat, in a way that is attractive. A woman having large breasts and hips and not thin, but in a way that is attractive. Of a woman, having a plump and sexually attractive figure, voluptuous, well-proportioned.
example_sentence: Marilyn Monroe was sometimes called full-figured or zaftig. She was rather buxom. I would call her zaftig.

english_meaning: A decorative holder for a hot coffee cup without a handle, used in the Middle East. A metal or ornamental cup sleeve.
example_sentence: The waiter served coffee in a silver zarf. Traditional zarfs are often beautifully engraved. She bought a brass zarf from the market. The hot cup sat safely inside the zarf.

english_meaning: A person who is fanatically devoted to a cause, belief, religion, or political ideal. An extreme enthusiast. Someone who supports a viewpoint with uncompromising and often intolerant passion. The term is often used in a negative sense for excessive or aggressive devotion.
example_sentence: He was a political zealot who never accepted other views. Religious zealots often misinterpret the true message of faith. The reformer was called a zealot by his opponents. A zealot can sometimes do more harm than good to a cause. She is a zealot when it comes to environmental protection.

english_meaning: Showing great energy and enthusiasm for something, especially because you feel strongly about it. Enthusiastic and eager
example_sentence: I was zealous in my demands on my sisters for promptness in rehearsals.

english_meaning: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history as shown by the ideas and beliefs of the time. It encapsulates the cultural, intellectual, and moral climate of a specific era.
example_sentence: His new novel perfectly captures the zeitgeist of the late twentieth century. The film was praised for reflecting the cultural zeitgeist. As the generation changed, so did the political zeitgeist. Fashion is often a good indicator of the current zeitgeist. Understanding the zeitgeist helps historians interpret past events.

english_meaning: The highest point reached by a celestial or other object. The peak or culmination of success, power, or development. The point in the sky directly above an observer. Used figuratively to describe the most successful or glorious moment in someone’s life or career.

english_meaning: A soft, gentle breeze. A light wind, especially one coming from the west. Something very light and airy, such as delicate fabric. In poetry, a personification of the west wind.
example_sentence: A pleasant zephyr cooled the evening air. The curtains moved gently in the zephyr. Her dress was made of a fabric as light as a zephyr. Poets often describe the zephyr as a messenger of spring.

english_meaning: An angle that measures exactly 0 degrees. The angle formed when two rays lie exactly on top of each other. An angle showing no rotation between two lines. The smallest possible angle in geometry.
example_sentence: A zero angle is formed when the two arms coincide. The protractor reading showed a zero angle. A zero angle has no measurable opening. He explained the zero angle before moving to acute angles.

english_meaning: To focus attention closely on one particular thing. To aim carefully at a target. To identify and concentrate on the main issue or cause. To move directly towards something.
synonyms: ["Focus on","Concentrate on","Target","Home in on","Pinpoint","Aim at","Single out"]
example_sentence: Investigators zeroed in on a single suspect. Let's zero in on the main cause of the delay. The camera zeroed in on the winner's face. She zeroed in on the errors in the report immediately.

english_meaning: To reduce something to zero. To cancel or eliminate a budget, balance, or allocation completely. To set a value or counter back to zero. To remove funding entirely.
example_sentence: The committee voted to zero out the travel budget. Please zero out the counter before the next test. Lawmakers zeroed out funding for the old programme. He zeroed out his credit card balance last month.

english_meaning: A policy of punishing all instances of a specific prohibited behavior, no matter how minor, without any exceptions. It leaves no room for discretion or excuses when rules are broken. This approach is often used by schools, workplaces, or police forces to deter misconduct.
example_sentence: The school has a policy of zero tolerance for bullying or harassment. The company maintains zero tolerance toward any form of discrimination. The city announced zero tolerance for illegal parking during the festival. Athletes are aware of the zero tolerance policy regarding performance-enhancing drugs.

english_meaning: To direct one's attention, efforts, or resources precisely toward a specific target or goal. To adjust a device or weapon so that it aims accurately. To move steadily closer to a target or objective. Often written as a compound or brand-style spelling of the phrase "zero in".
example_sentence: The team needs to zero in on the most urgent issues first. The app helps users zero in on the best deals nearby. After calibrating, the telescope zeroed in on the distant star. We should zero in our marketing on younger audiences.

english_meaning: Past tense and past participle of zero: set or adjusted to zero. Brought a value or reading to zero. Aimed or directed precisely at a target.
example_sentence: The technician zeroed all the gauges before the experiment started. Once the meter was zeroed, the measurements matched perfectly. The account was zeroed after the final payment. The gun was zeroed at a distance of one hundred meters.

english_meaning: Focused attention or aim precisely on a target. Having narrowed down to the exact person, thing, or answer. Adjusted sights or instruments so they point accurately.
synonyms: ["Focused on","Targeted","Pinpointed","Homed in on","Locked onto","Narrowed down to"]
example_sentence: The police have zeroed in on two possible suspects. Once she zeroed in on the problem, the fix was easy. The camera zeroed in on the speaker's face. Scientists have zeroed in on the gene responsible for the condition.

english_meaning: The act of adjusting or setting something to a zero point or baseline. Resetting a counter, gauge, or scale to zero before measuring. Adjusting a firearm's sight so that it aims accurately at a target.
example_sentence: Zeroing the scale before weighing ensures accurate measurements. The technician spent an hour zeroing the instruments in the lab. Zeroing the rifle sight took several practice shots. After zeroing the meter, the readings became stable.

english_meaning: Moving or aiming steadily closer toward a target. Focusing attention or effort increasingly on something specific. Gradually narrowing down possibilities to reach the exact answer or location.
example_sentence: The pilot began zeroing in on the landing strip. Detectives are zeroing in on the main suspect. Researchers are zeroing in on the cause of the disease. The company is zeroing in on a younger customer base.

english_meaning: The process of focusing steadily and closely on a specific target, goal, or detail. Concentrating resources or attention on one particular thing. Progressively narrowing a search or investigation toward the exact answer.
synonyms: ["Focusing on","Concentrating on","Homing in on","Closing in on","Targeting","Pinpointing"]
example_sentence: Investigators are zeroing in on the source of the leak. The company is zeroing in on quality instead of quantity. She kept zeroing in on the smallest details of the design. The missile is zeroing in on its target.

english_meaning: Bringing a value, balance, or figure down to exactly zero. Canceling out a debt, score, or difference so that nothing remains. Resetting something completely to a neutral state.
example_sentence: The accountant recommended zeroing out the balance before closing the account. After the refund, the invoice was zeroed out. The team focused on zeroing out the remaining errors in the code. By the end of the quarter, the debt was zeroed out completely.

english_meaning: Enjoyment, Quality of being exciting, interesting & enjoyable
example_sentence: She danced with zest of twenty year old. The slight risk added zest to the experience.

english_meaning: A metric prefix denoting a factor of one sextillion (1021) of the base unit. Applied to units like byte to measure planetary-scale amounts of digital information. Represented by the symbol Z in the International System of Units.
example_sentence: By 2030, global data may exceed several zettabytes annually. A zettabyte equals one trillion gigabytes. Storage engineers plan for zettabyte-scale archives. The network can handle zettabytes of traffic over its lifetime.

english_meaning: A unit of digital information equal to 1,024 exabytes. An enormous measure of data, roughly a sextillion bytes. A unit normally used to describe the total amount of data created worldwide.
example_sentence: The world now produces many zettabytes of data each year. One zettabyte equals 1,024 exabytes. Cloud services deal with zettabyte-scale information. Experts say global storage will soon reach hundreds of zettabytes.

english_meaning: To move from side to side in sharp, quick turns instead of going straight. It describes a repeated change of direction. A shape or line made of sharp turns going left and right. It is a pattern that repeats in an uneven path. Describes something that has a pattern of sharp, repeated turns. Not straight but uneven and turning left and right.
example_sentence: The cyclist had to zig zag through the crowd. The snake left a zig zag on the sand. The zig zag road slowed the cars. We watched the kite move in a zig zag across the sky.

example_sentence: Archaeologists discovered the ruins of a massive ziggurat in the ancient city of Ur. The ziggurat was a symbol of bridging heaven and earth. People would gather at the base of the ziggurat for religious festivals. Building a ziggurat required immense labor and architectural skill. The terraced steps of the ziggurat are quite well-preserved today.

english_meaning: A line or course with sharp alternating turns to left and right. Having the form of a series of sharp angular turns. To move forward with repeated sharp turns from side to side. Marked by a pattern of angled lines.
example_sentence: The path zigzags up the steep hillside. Lightning made a bright zigzag across the sky. She wore a jumper with a bold zigzag pattern. The rabbit zigzagged across the field to escape.

english_meaning: To move about quickly from place to place. To travel briskly around an area. To be busy going here and there in a hurry.
example_sentence: She zips around the city on her scooter. The children zipped around the garden all afternoon. He zipped around town collecting supplies. Delivery riders zip around the neighbourhood every evening.

english_meaning: To move through something very quickly. To complete a task or read material rapidly. To pass swiftly from one place to another.
example_sentence: She zipped through the report in twenty minutes. The train zipped through the tunnel without stopping. He zipped through his homework before dinner. Visitors zipped through the exhibition in half an hour.

example_sentence: Zip up your jacket; it is cold outside. He zipped up the suitcase and headed for the airport. Just zip up and listen for a moment. The editor zipped up the article with sharper headings.

The motile zoid swam toward its target using tiny flagella. Observing a zoid helps scientists understand basic cellular movement. The formation of the zoid is a crucial step in the life cycle of the algae.

english_meaning: An informal, shortened slang form of the word zombie, sometimes used in casual digital communication, gaming, or social media. Refers to a fictional reanimated corpse that moves and behaves in a mindless, often aggressive manner. Used figuratively to describe a person who appears tired, sluggish, or unresponsive, as if not fully conscious.

After the exam, all the students looked like zombs walking through the hallways.  The movie was packed with cheesy zomb costumes and special effects.  I felt like a zomb this morning after barely sleeping.

english_meaning: An area or stretch of land having a particular characteristic, purpose, or use, or subject to particular restrictions. A specified region or sector distinguished from adjacent areas by a distinctive feature. A state of intense focus or optimal performance, often referred to as being in the zone. To divide a city or area into sections subject to different restrictions or meant for different purposes.
example_sentence: The city is divided into several commercial and residential zones. The government declared the disaster-stricken region a no-fly zone. Please do not park your car in the loading zone. The local authorities have zoned this land for industrial development. She was completely in the zone while writing her final research paper.

synonyms: ["Focus on","Concentrate on","Pay attention to","Direct attention","Fixate on"]
example_sentence: During the exam, I zoned in on the most difficult questions first. He zoned in on her voice even in the noisy room. You need to zone in on your goals if you want to succeed. The teacher asked the students to zone in on the main idea of the passage.

synonyms: ["Focus on","Zero in on","Concentrate on","Home in on","Fix on","Target"]
example_sentence: The coach told the players to zone in on defence. She zoned in on the one figure that looked wrong. Readers quickly zone in on the headline. He zoned in on the task and finished it early.

english_meaning: A place where wild or rare animals are kept, cared for, studied, and shown to the public. Informally, a crowded, noisy, or disorderly place.

english_meaning: A strong love or affection for animals. The belief that animals should be protected and treated kindly. In psychiatry, an abnormal sexual attraction to animals.
